She is willing and able to follow instructions, provide informed consent, make the required study visits, and use an electronic patient diary during the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian male scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with lisinopril. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no history of drug addiction or liver or kidney disease. He reports no allergies to any medications. He has no significant medical history and does not take any regular medications. His physical examination is unremarkable. He weighs 82 kg and is 180 cm tall. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25.3 kg/m². He has fasted for 8 hours and has been cleared for surgery by his anesthesiologist. He has been informed of the study and has provided written consent to participate.

The patient is a 6-year-old female child diagnosed with Rett syndrome. She is in disease stage 1-2 and has abnormality of at least two disease biomarker levels. The patient has a confirmed MeCP2 mutation. She presents with impaired motor and cognitive development, with the inability to communicate verbally. She is under the care of a guardian who is able to consent and comply with protocol requirements. The patient has not used Coenzyme Q10, vitamin E and Idebenone for at least two weeks prior to enrollment into the study. The patient has no known conditions that could compromise her safety or adherence to treatment with EPI-743. The patient does not have any clinically significant allergy or hypersensitivity to EPI-743 or Vitamin E. There is no clinical history of bleeding or abnormal baseline PT/PTT. The patient does not have any other concurrent inborn error of metabolism, hepatic or renal insufficiency, end stage cardiac failure or fat malabsorption syndromes precluding drug absorption.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with essential hypertension for the past 5 years. She has been taking amlodipine for the past 2 months but her blood pressure is still not well controlled. At her last visit to the clinic, her sitting diastolic blood pressure was measured at 92 mmHg. She has no history of secondary hypertension or any other significant medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications that may affect her blood pressure. She has voluntarily agreed to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using medically acceptable contraception. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse and has not participated in any other clinical trials with investigational drugs in the past 4 weeks.

A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a history of recurrent episodes of anterior epistaxis over the past year. He has no known bleeding disorder and is not taking any anticoagulation therapy. The patient gives informed consent to participate in the study. He reports a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient is hemodynamically stable and is not experiencing any active bleeding at the time of presentation.

This is a 58-year-old male veteran with a history of chronic migraines for the past 5 years, with a confirmed frequency of more than 10 headache days per month. He has tried various medications without much relief and has found that his migraines are impacting his daily life and work. He has been diagnosed with hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes daily medication for both conditions. He has no history of traumatic brain injury or severe cognitive impairment, and his primary complaint is headache. He is fluent in English and is able to use the VA Annie App and MyHealtheVet secure messaging. He is interested in participating in the Telemedicine-based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) program (TENACITY) for migraines to explore additional treatment options and improve his quality of life.

Patient is a 35-year-old male who has previously been treated for HCV infection with direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy with a sustained virologic response at 12 weeks. He has a fibroscan score of less than 12.5kPa within the past 6 months. The patient is willing to practice continuous effective contraception from screening until 4 months after the last vaccination. He is available for follow-up for the planned duration of the study and is willing to undergo HCV and HIV testing, counseling, and receive test results. The patient has no history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine, and has not received any investigational HCV vaccine within the last 6 years. He has not participated in another research study involving an investigational product in the 30 days preceding enrollment or planned use during the study period. The patient is not currently using immunosuppressive medication and has no history of major autoimmune disease. He has no history of cancer or serious psychiatric conditions, and does not have any other serious chronic illnesses requiring hospital specialist supervision. The patient is not seropositive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and has no clinically significant acute or chronic medical condition that is considered unstable/progressive. Overall, this patient meets the inclusion criteria for the Class II Invariant Chain HCV Vaccine Study and is a suitable candidate for participation in the clinical trial.

A 57-year-old male smoker presents with persistent cough and shortness of breath that have been worsening for the past 2 months. He reports occasional chest pain and weight loss of 5 kg in the past month. He denies any history of lung disease or cancer in his family. Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and crackles on lung auscultation. Vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory results are as follows: CBC within normal limits, liver and renal function tests within normal limits. A chest X-ray shows a large mass in the right lung with multiple nodules in both lungs. A biopsy confirms small cell lung cancer. The cancer is extensive stage and the patient has not received any prior treatment. The patient is deemed eligible for the clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of irinotecan and carboplatin in treating newly diagnosed extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who presented with left knee pain and swelling for the past 3 months. He has no significant past medical history and denies any history of trauma or infection. Physical examination revealed a tender and swollen left knee with limited range of motion. X-ray and MRI showed a lytic lesion in the distal femur with surrounding soft tissue edema. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of osteosarcoma. The patient has normal organ function with CCr of 80 mL/min/1.73 m2, AST/ALT of 20/25 IU/L, total bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, shortening fraction of 28%, and SpO2 of 98% on room air. His ANC is 1500/uL and platelet count is 100,000/uL. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent.

A 58-year-old male patient presents with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 10 years. He has experienced increasing dyspnea, chronic cough, and sputum production over the past year. He is a current smoker with a 30 pack-year history of smoking. His vital signs are stable and within normal limits. The physical examination reveals bilateral expiratory wheezing, prolonged expiratory phase, and decreased breath sounds in both lungs. The patient's forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) is 45% of predicted, and his FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio is 0.58. His oxygen saturation on room air is 92%. He is not currently receiving any inspiratory muscle training (IMT). He has not had any acute exacerbation of COPD in the past 4 weeks. He is willing and able to cooperate with the measurements of this study.

A 22-year-old physically active male is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining the effects of L-arginine on endothelial, cardiovascular, and performance responses to resistance exercise. He is currently not taking any medications or supplements containing L-arginine or other nitrate precursors. He has not participated in another clinical trial or consumed another study related investigation product within the last 30 days. He exercises regularly by lifting weights and doing cardio for 60 minutes at least 4 days a week. He has no known allergies and has not been pregnant.

This study is not recruiting patients as it is a retrospective data analysis study. Therefore, a patient description cannot be generated. However, the study is aimed at healthy individuals who received a health check-up colonoscopy screening at Far Eastern Memorial Hospital in Taiwan between March 2013 and August 2014, and the study is analyzing the efficacy of a medical team resource management (TRM) method on the adequacy of bowel preparation. The study is collecting demographic information such as age and gender, as well as information on the types of purgative treatments used and the results of bowel preparation. The study is excluding gastroenterology outpatients/inpatients, missing data subjects, and those outside of the age limit and time period.

The patient is a 50 year old man who was admitted to the medical intensive care unit due to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) caused by pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently well controlled with medication. He is intubated and receiving mechanical ventilation support. His predicted ICU stay is longer than 72 hours. He has not been able to eat orally since his admission. He does not have any contraindications for enteral feeding and has not experienced any upper or lower GI bleeding. He does not have any history of metoclopramide-related EPS or Torsades de pointes. His family reports that he has always had a healthy appetite and enjoys a wide variety of foods. He is currently classified as being at moderate nutritional risk by the modified NUTRIC scoring system.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 10 years. Despite taking various antidepressants, she has been experiencing major depressive symptoms that have not responded to treatment. The patient has a history of gut issues and has undergone a colonoscopy in the past. She has not undergone fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) before. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness, safety, and acceptability of FMT on depressive symptoms. She is currently not taking any other medications or undergoing any other treatments for her depression.

This is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. She has been receiving treatment for her condition, but continues to experience negative symptoms, such as social withdrawal and reduced motivation. She has not experienced any significant improvement in her symptoms despite taking antipsychotic medications as prescribed. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of sulforaphane on her negative symptoms and cognitive function. She has no history of substance abuse, traumatic brain injury, or other neurological or organic diseases of the central nervous system. She is not currently taking any antidepressants, stimulants, or mood stabilizers. She is willing to sign the study consent for participation and is committed to attending all study visits. She understands that she may receive a placebo during the trial but hopes that her participation may contribute to advancements in treating schizophrenia.

This clinical trial is seeking children who previously participated in the Infant Brain Study, which took place from birth to 24 months of age. The study will assess the effects of cord clamping time on the structure and function of the developing brain at three and four years of age. Children who are eligible for this study must have been born healthy at term and enrolled in the previous trial. The assessments will include MRIs and neurodevelopmental testing to examine cognitive, motor, visual, and behavioral outcomes. The purpose of this study is to measure the effects of cord clamping time on the structure and function of the developing brain at three and four years of age. If you have a child who previously participated in the Infant Brain Study and meets the inclusion criteria, please contact us to learn more about participating in this important follow-up study.

A 35-year-old male who has been using injection drugs for the past 5 years is seeking treatment for his addiction. He has been participating in the Baltimore Needle Exchange Program (BNEP) and has expressed interest in methadone maintenance treatment. He is not currently enrolled in any treatment program using methadone or other agonist medications. He meets the DSM-IV criteria for opioid physical dependence and CSAT guidelines for long-term use of opioid agonist medications. He does not have any acute medical problems that require immediate and intense medical management, nor does he have a formal thought disorder, delusions, hallucinations, or imminent risk of harm to self or others. He is willing to participate in a 6-month study that will randomly assign him to one of three 3-month induction conditions: Low Threshold Stepped Care induction (LTSC), Voucher-Based Stepped Care induction (VBSC), or Routine Stepped-Care induction (RSC). He understands that he will be followed for 6 months, during which time his retention, drug use (via urinalysis and self-report), and other infectious disease risk behaviors (e.g., syringe sharing; number of injections) will be measured. He is also aware that the study will evaluate the cost of each induction strategy.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman with moderate persistent bronchial asthma according to GINA guidelines. She has no history of smoking or associated respiratory diseases. She has not been on oral corticosteroids in the previous six months and is not currently pregnant. She experiences symptoms such as wheezing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness on a regular basis. She has been using a rescue inhaler as needed but has not found it to be effective in controlling her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of two different LABA+ICS combinations on small airways obstruction in asthma. She is willing to adhere to the treatment plan and attend all required appointments for the duration of the study.

70-year-old male with a history of forgetfulness and difficulty in remembering things for the last 6 months presents to the clinic. He has also experienced difficulty in performing routine activities such as cooking, managing finances, and keeping track of appointments. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any history of substance abuse or recent infections. The patient has undergone a brain MRI that showed mild cerebral atrophy. The clinical diagnosis of MCI due to AD was made according to the National Institute of Aging and Alzheimer's Disease Association (NIA-AA) diagnostic criteria in 2011. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the reliability and validity of plasma miRNAs for early diagnosis of MCI due to AD and other dementia such as DLB and FTLD.

A 60-year-old retired NFL player presents with a history of multiple concussions during his career. He complains of forgetfulness, difficulty concentrating, and occasional headaches. The patient is concerned about his memory issues and how they may affect his daily life. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well controlled with medication. He has no history of diabetes or any other medical conditions. The patient underwent a neurological evaluation, and a diagnosis of growth hormone deficiency was made based on clinical grounds. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. He retired from professional football over five years ago and has not played since. He is currently not taking any medications other than his hypertension medication. The patient is motivated to improve his cognitive function and overall quality of life.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who reports sporadic use of nicotine in the form of e-cigarettes. He has no history of cardiovascular or respiratory disease and his clinical examination, EKG, blood tests and lung function are all within normal limits. He has no history of systemic or chronic disorders such as rheumatologic or metabolic disease. He has not experienced any symptoms of infection or inflammation within the last 2 weeks. His BMI is below 30. He is interested in participating in a study investigating the acute vascular effects of e-cigarette use.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with non-del(5q) low to intermediate-1 risk MDS. He has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising for the past few months. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks of the study. He is able to comply with the requirements of RevAssist® and is willing to undergo regular blood tests and follow-up visits. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to Telintra™ or prior therapy with thalidomide or lenalidomide. He has not undergone prior allogenic bone marrow transplant for MDS and has no history of prior malignancy except for treated carcinoma of prostate for which he has been disease-free for more than 3 years. The patient has a performance status of 1 and documented significant cytopenia for at least 2 months. He has discontinued growth factors for at least 21 days prior to study entry. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to undergo two negative serum pregnancy tests before taking lenalidomide.

A 54 year old man was admitted to the neurology department with a sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but has never had a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) before. He is a smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and has a high stress job. His wife reports that he has not been taking his medications regularly and has not been following a healthy diet. The patient is fluent in French and is able to answer the questionnaire.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is generally healthy and takes no regular medications. She has no history of hematologic diseases and has never been on anticoagulant medications. She weighs 60 kg and her age falls within the eligible range for the study. She is interested in participating in the study after being provided with all the necessary information about the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male smoker with a history of COPD and asbestos exposure. He has been referred for a non-enhanced chest CT for lung nodule search and control. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and occasional coughing for the past few months. His vital signs are stable, and physical examination is unremarkable. His chest X-ray showed a suspicious nodule, and a CT scan was ordered to further investigate its nature. The patient has a body mass index of 28 kg/m² and is able to lie down and hold his breath for more than 5 seconds. He is affiliated with the French social security and has signed the consent form to participate in the study. The patient has not had pneumonia in the last 3 months and is not currently participating in any interventional studies. He is not a pregnant or breastfeeding woman.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of penile squamous cell carcinoma. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past, but the disease has progressed and is now considered unresectable and metastatic. He is experiencing symptoms such as pain, fatigue, and weight loss. The patient has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group) Performance Scale. He has adequate organ function with all screening labs being performed within 14 days of treatment initiation. The patient agrees to use an adequate method of contraception starting with the first dose of study therapy through 120 days after the last dose of study therapy. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial. The patient has not participated in a study of an investigational agent and received study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of treatment. He does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of trial treatment. The patient does not have a known history of active TB (Bacillus Tuberculosis) or hypersensitivity to Pembrolizumab or any of its excipients. He has not had a prior anti-cancer monoclonal antibody (mAb) within 4 weeks prior to study Day 1 or who has not recovered (i.e., ≤ Grade 1 or at baseline) from adverse events due to agents administered more than 4 weeks earlier. The patient has not had prior chemotherapy, targeted small molecule therapy, or radiation therapy within 2 weeks prior to study Day 1 or who has not recovered (i.e., ≤ Grade 1 or at baseline) from adverse events due to a previously administered agent. The patient does not have a known additional malignancy that is progressing or requires active treatment, known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis, active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years, known history of, or any evidence of active, non-infectious pneumonitis, active infection requiring systemic therapy, known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the trial. The patient is not pregnant or expecting to father children within the projected duration of the trial, starting with the pre-screening or screening visit through 120 days after the last dose of trial treatment. The patient has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent. The patient does not have a known history of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) (HIV 1/2 antibodies), known active Hepatitis B (e.g., HBsAg reactive) or Hepatitis C (e.g., HCV RNA [qualitative] is detected), known active Tuberculosis infection, and has not received a live vaccine within 30 days of planned start of study therapy.

The patient is a 70 year old woman who recently fell while walking on a flat surface and sustained a hip fracture. She has no history of dementia and is able to provide informed consent. Her medical history is significant for osteoporosis, which was diagnosed by DEXA scan and has been treated with bisphosphonates for several years. She has no history of high energy fractures or any other major medical conditions. She is willing to participate in genetic testing to determine if she has any gene-polymorphies in the P2X7 gene that may be associated with osteoporotic fractures.

The patient is a 2-year-old boy who has been admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit due to respiratory distress. He has been intubated and is currently receiving mechanical ventilation. The patient has been diagnosed with pneumonia, and his condition is being closely monitored by the medical team. The physician has recommended chest physiotherapy as part of his treatment plan. The patient has no other medical conditions and is in stable condition. The patient's parents have been informed about the research study, and they have given their consent for their child to participate. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he is intubated, mechanically ventilated, receiving chest physiotherapy, and is within the age range of 0-4 years.

The patient is a 46-year-old male who has been referred for an elective hand surgery procedure to treat carpal tunnel syndrome. He is in good health with no significant medical history, and his physical status is classified as ASA I. The patient is not currently taking any medications, and he has no known allergies. The surgery is expected to take no longer than 30 minutes, and it will involve the median nerve. The patient speaks French fluently and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing headaches and seizures for the past few months. She underwent an MRI which revealed a brain tumor. The biopsy confirmed that it is a malignant neuroectodermal tumor. She has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is currently on leave due to her health concerns. She is physically active and enjoys hiking and yoga. Her performance status is good. She has not undergone any previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Her blood tests show normal levels of white blood cells, neutrophils, platelets, and liver function. She has a negative pregnancy test. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options and improve her quality of life.

Patient is a 40-year-old male from India who presents with pain in the perianal region and discharge from the anal opening. He reports having these symptoms for the past 3 months. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. On examination, the patient is found to have a high perianal fistula. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of Prolene Thread Seton vs Silk Thread Seton for the treatment of perianal fistula. He meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and mild renal impairment, with a CLcr of 65 mL/min. He has been on antihypertensive medication for the past 5 years, but his blood pressure has remained elevated with a mean sitting BP of 150/95 mmHg. He reports occasional headaches and dizziness but denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or transient ischemic attack. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant gastrointestinal, respiratory, hematological, metabolic, immunological, or other underlying disease. He is not allergic to ARBs or ACE inhibitors and is not taking any disallowed medication. He is not a drug or alcohol abuser. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he agrees to use adequate contraception during the study.

As this study is a registry study, there is not a specific patient description. Instead, the study aims to collect data from patients who have used Shuxuening injection during their inpatient time from December 2012 to December 2014 in Chinese hospitals. There are no specific eligibility criteria or exclusion criteria for individual patients as the study will collect data from a large cohort of patients. The study will focus on collecting demographic information and adverse drug events/reactions related to the use of Shuxuening injection.

85-year-old F with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and a history of mild cognitive impairment. The patient has been experiencing sleep disruption, unsatisfactory sleep, early morning awakening, early bedtime, and excessive daytime sleepiness. These symptoms have been reported by both the patient and their caregiver. The patient has no history of liver or coronary disease but is currently not participating in any other clinical drug trial. The patient is willing and able to follow the protocol for the clinical trial.

A 45-year old female office worker was diagnosed with severe hypertriglyceridemia six months ago. She reports no symptoms but was incidentally found to have a high level of triglycerides during a routine check-up. She is currently on a low-fat, low-cholesterol diet, and takes atorvastatin and ezetimibe to manage her cholesterol levels. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any illicit drugs. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses an intrauterine device for contraception. She has regular menstrual periods. Her body mass index is 23 kg/m². She has no history of pancreatitis, liver or kidney disease. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is interested in participating in clinical trials to help find new treatments for her condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with malignant colonic obstruction localized between the splenic flexure and 15cm from the anal margin. She is experiencing clinical occlusion to gas and feces and is scheduled for endoscopy and stent location within the next 24 hours after diagnosis. She has no associated pathologies that contraindicate general anesthesia and is considered stable for the procedure. She has given her informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient has no history of bowel perforation and has not been diagnosed with multiple liver metastases. She is interested in exploring all treatment options available to her and hopes to improve her postoperative outcome and reduce hospital stay time.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is admitted to the medical ICU with severe pneumonia. He is intubated and mechanically ventilated due to respiratory failure. The patient is expected to stay in the ICU for more than 72 hours. The family history is negative for psychiatric disorders. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has not received any antipsychotic drug before attending the study. The patient's renal and hepatic functions are within normal limits. The patient's legal representatives have provided written consent to participate in the study. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of low dose quetiapine in preventing delirium in critically ill patients.

14-year-old boy diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 6 months ago. He is currently on insulin therapy and has a good understanding of his condition. He has had no episodes of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and his hemoglobin A1c is 7.2%. He is active in sports and is otherwise healthy. He meets the inclusion criteria for this study and is interested in participating to potentially prevent the loss of insulin secretory capacity. He has no history of asthma, hepatitis C, hepatitis B, or HIV. His weight is 65 kg.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with diabetes mellitus type 2 for the past 10 years. He complains of blurred vision and difficulty reading, especially in low light. The patient has received two consecutive intravitreal bevacizumab injections for the treatment of diabetic macular edema but has not experienced complete resolution of central subfield thickening by OCT. His central 1mm subfield thickness is greater than 300 microns as measured on SD-OCT. His visual acuity score is less than or equal to 73 letters (20/40) by the ETDRS visual acuity protocol. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, and his blood pressure is well controlled with medication. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ranibizumab in treating diabetic macular edema in patients with poor response to bevacizumab.

A 65 year old postmenopausal woman with a diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer that is negative for estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor while positive for androgen receptor. The patient has completed prior chemotherapy, biologic therapy and radiotherapy at least 4 weeks before the trial. The patient has normal leukocyte, absolute neutrophil and platelet counts, as well as normal bilirubin, AST, ALT and creatinine levels or creatinine clearance above 60mL/min. The patient is not currently taking any dehydroepiandrosterone or androstenedione supplements and is not receiving chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormone therapy or immunotherapy.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been leading a sedentary lifestyle for the past few years. He has no history of hypertension, diabetes, neurological diseases or stroke. He is currently not taking any medications. The patient has agreed to participate in a study investigating the effects of age, exercise, and cardiovascular disease on blood pressure regulation. He will undergo screening tests, including history, questionnaires, physical exam, lab tests, treadmill exercise tolerance test, and maximal exercise test. These screening tests will be repeated at 3 months and 6 months. The patient will be assigned to the Sedentary Older Individuals Group and will undergo an exercise-training program designed for his fitness level. During the first month, he will be supervised while exercising at Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital, but after that may choose to exercise at home or in a fitness center. These exercise sessions will take place 3-5 times per week for 15-40 minutes per session based on the individual's exercise program, increasing to 4-6 times per week for 30-60 minutes per session after the first month. The patient will be required to visit Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital a minimum of once every two weeks so that information can be collected from a heart rate monitor. Testing is done at the beginning and end of the exercise-training intervention period to determine what effect the intervention has had on the individual's blood pressure regulation. This testing consists of 2 sequential study days. Differences in blood pressure regulation pre- and post-training will be studied.

This clinical trial is seeking patients who have been diagnosed with breast cancer, germ cell tumor, colon cancer, leukemia, lymphoma, or sarcoma and have completed treatment within the past 1-2 years. The patient must have an ECOG performance status of 0-1 and must be able to read and self-complete study questionnaires. Patients with psychological conditions that may prevent participation in the study are not eligible. Hormonal treatment for breast cancer is allowed, but no concurrent treatment is allowed. The study aims to determine the amount of information received on aspects of fertility and infertility before cancer treatment in a comprehensive cancer center, as well as to analyze whether the information received by patients is related to the desire to be parents or desire to be informed. Demographic data, diagnosis, quality of life, and associated psychosocial information received by patients will also be evaluated.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing discomfort and pain in her left leg due to varicose veins. She has noticed that her left leg is swollen and feels heavy, especially after prolonged periods of standing or sitting. She also reports occasional itching and burning sensations in the affected area. Upon examination, it is found that she has insufficiency of the great saphenous vein, with reflux greater than 0.5 seconds and a diameter of the vein greater than 0.5 centimeters. The patient has not received any prior treatment for her condition. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different endovenous laser ablation techniques for treating her varicose veins. She understands that the trial will involve using either a 940 nm diode laser or a 1470 nm Nd:Yag laser to occlude the great saphenous vein. She is willing to be randomized to either treatment arm and understands that the study will involve follow-up visits at 1 week, 3 months, and 1 year post-treatment to assess her pain scores, satisfaction, and quality of life. She understands that there may be potential risks associated with the treatment, including the possibility of deep or superficial vein thrombosis, nerve injury, skin burns, and (sub)cutaneous infections. However, she also understands that the study has been designed to minimize these risks and that the primary focus of the study is on patient-reported outcomes. The patient is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that her involvement will help to improve the treatment options available for individuals with varicose veins.

A 54-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer and has been recommended chemotherapy by her oncologist. She has no history of heart disease, stroke, or other chronic illnesses. She is currently working as an administrative assistant and has been sedentary for most of her adult life. She is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol in moderation. She lives alone in an apartment and has a supportive family. She has no problem with mobility and can walk without assistance. She is fluent in English and is able to read and write. She is interested in joining a clinical trial that can help her improve her physical activity level and potentially reduce the side effects of chemotherapy.

This is a 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and smoking. He presented with chest pain and was diagnosed with a first episode of myocardial infarction three weeks ago. He underwent balloon angioplasty and stenting of the right coronary artery. His ejection fraction on echocardiogram was 45%. He has been compliant with his medications including aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. He is interested in participating in exercise training to improve his cardiac function and is able to commit to a 4-month follow-up period. He has no history of pacemaker or heart transplant and is currently in sinus rhythm.

The patient is a 32-year-old active duty service member in the United States military who has recently returned from deployment. He is experiencing symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) including nightmares, flashbacks, and hypervigilance. The patient has scored 60 on the Clinician Administered PTSD Score for DSM-5 (CAPS-5). He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is open to participating in a clinical trial that involves a combination of eye movement desensitization reprocessing (EMDR) and venlafaxine XR to treat his PTSD symptoms. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to adhere to the study protocol for the entire 24-week duration. The patient is not currently experiencing suicidal or homicidal ideation, and is not pregnant. He does not have profound hearing loss, HIV and AIDS, or current chemotherapy. The patient has no history of bipolar disorder or cyclothymia, substance dependence (excluding nicotine), or use of bupropion above 150mg daily, mirtazapine above 15mg daily, an SSRI, another SNRI, tricyclic antidepressants in doses above 50mg, an MAO-I, a stimulant, a mood stabilizer/anti-epileptic for an indication of mood stability or reduction in anger, an anti-psychotic, lithium, chronic daily use of steroids, tapentadol, dronabinol, or ketamine.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (SPMS) two years ago. She has experienced a gradual worsening of symptoms, including difficulty with walking, balance, and coordination. She has been treated with interferon beta-1a and corticosteroids in the past, but her disease has progressed despite these treatments. She has an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 6.0, indicating that she is still able to walk without assistance but requires a cane or other mobility aid for longer distances. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is married with two children and works part-time as a teacher. She understands the risks and benefits of siponimod and is willing to provide written informed consent for participation in the Managed Access Program (MAP). She has no history of chickenpox or varicella vaccination and will need to undergo antibody testing prior to starting treatment with siponimod. She is committed to using a highly effective method of birth control for the duration of treatment with siponimod and for at least ten days after stopping treatment. She is able to comply with treatment instructions and requirements and is willing to follow the suggested treatment guidelines provided by her Treating Physician.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking for 40 years was diagnosed with moderate COPD. He experiences shortness of breath during physical activity and has been using bronchodilators regularly. He is otherwise healthy and has no other chronic conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effects of different gas mixtures on his pulmonary function. He is able to perform pulmonary function tests and light cycling exercise. He is willing to complete the study in 5 working days or less and is able to provide written informed consent. He has not participated in any other interventional clinical trials in the last 30 days.

A 68-year-old woman with bilateral knee osteoarthritis comes to the clinic seeking treatment options. She has been experiencing pain and stiffness in both knees for several years and has tried various conservative treatments including medication, physical therapy, and weight loss with no significant improvement. She has no history of malignancy or severe extra-articular deformities and has not been diagnosed with any systemic inflammatory diseases. She is not morbidly obese and has no severe cardiac insufficiency. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for bilateral TKA under single anesthesia and is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

A 42-year-old woman presents with persistent heartburn and regurgitation for the past 3 months. She describes the heartburn as a burning sensation in her chest that occurs after meals and is relieved by antacids. She denies any difficulty swallowing, nausea, vomiting or abdominal pain. She has tried over-the-counter antacids and proton pump inhibitors with no relief. She is a non-smoker and has no significant past medical history. She is not taking any medications. Physical examination is unremarkable with no signs of distress. Blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 75 beats/minute, and BMI is 24. She reports that her symptoms have negatively impacted her quality of life and ability to sleep. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of TAK-438 compared to placebo in the treatment of non-erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) and end-stage renal disease. He is scheduled to undergo elective kidney transplantation in the next few weeks. His DM is well-controlled with oral hypoglycemic agents and he has no other significant medical history. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He has been compliant with his medications and has not experienced any recent hypoglycemic or hyperglycemic episodes. He has not had any recent infections or inflammation at the puncture site for cannulation. He has no history of coagulopathy and the modified Allen's test was negative. He is willing to participate in this study and has provided written informed consent.

2-year-old male child weighing 8kg presents with a history of fever within the last 24 hours and an axillary temperature of 38.2Cº. The child has no general danger signs or severe malaria present, and there is no other cause of fever detectable. The guardian/patient has understood the procedures of the study and is willing to participate. The patient is able to come for stipulated follow-up visits and has easy access to the Study Site. The child has no history of allergy to test drugs and has not taken any drugs other than paracetamol and aspirin within the last 3 days.

63-year-old F with Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease and on hemodialysis for the past 2 years due to diabetic nephropathy. She has been on the kidney transplant waitlist at Johns Hopkins Hospital for the past 10 months and has not been able to find a living kidney donor. She has no history of hepatitis C infection and has not engaged in any behavioral risk factors for contracting HCV other than being on hemodialysis. Her calculated panel reactive anti-human leukocyte antigens (anti-HLA) antibody (flow cPRA) is below 80%. She has been informed about the option of receiving a kidney from a deceased donor with hepatitis C infection and participating in a clinical trial that would involve prophylactic treatment with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir before and after transplant to prevent the establishment of HCV infection. She has expressed interest in participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

53 yo male with history of stage D heart failure secondary to ischemic cardiomyopathy, status post LVAD placement as bridge to transplant. Patient has been on the transplant list for 6 months but has not yet received a donor heart. Patient will be enrolled in a study examining the effect of Anginera on cardiac tissue obtained during heart transplant. Inclusion criteria for the study have been met as patient is in stage D heart failure and has an LVAD as a bridge to transplant. Exclusion criteria have been ruled out as patient does not have biopsy proven acute myocarditis, giant cell myocarditis, or known infiltrative disease. Patient has provided informed consent and will be randomized to receive Anginera treatment prior to heart transplant. Patient will be followed up for one year post-transplant to assess heart function and any adverse effects of the treatment.

A 35-year-old female patient was diagnosed with papillary thyroid microcarcinoma of 2.5 cm. She underwent a thyroid ultrasound and a CT scan, which showed no evidence of lymph node metastasis or extrathyroidal extension. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no other significant medical history. She has no known allergies and does not take any medications regularly. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 58-year-old female patient was diagnosed with stage III breast cancer and underwent surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. After completing the conventional treatment, the patient's imaging examinations and laboratory tests showed no evidence of cancer recurrence. However, the patient still experienced fatigue, occasional headaches, and decreased appetite. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial of DC-CIK immunotherapy to potentially improve her quality of life and overall survival. The patient has no history of other tumors and her ECOG score is 1. The patient is in good physical condition and is expected to survive for more than 6 months. Her blood routine, liver and kidney function, and hemagglutination laboratory examination results meet the eligibility criteria. The patient has signed an informed consent and is willing to comply with the prohibitions and restrictions stipulated in the research plan.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma three years ago. She underwent three chemotherapy regimens and achieved partial remission. Her latest bone marrow biopsy showed less than 20% involvement. The patient has CD20-positive disease and is generally in good health with the exception of mild hypertension. She has no history of myelodysplastic syndrome/acute myeloid leukemia or abnormal cytogenetic analysis indicative of MDS on the pre-transplant bone marrow examination. The patient is willing to undergo autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation with BEAM conditioning. The patient has no history of severe reaction to Rituxan or Filgrastim (G-CSF). The patient has not received prior radioimmunotherapy and is not known to be hypersensitive to murine proteins.

This is a 42-year-old female diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in the chronic phase. She has been previously treated with a BCR-ABL targeting TKI, but has developed resistance to the therapy. She is currently experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. The patient has adequate organ function and has tested negative for pregnancy. She is willing to use highly effective methods of contraception during the study. She has no history of acute or chronic pancreatitis or impaired cardiac function. She is not currently receiving treatment with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or medications that have the potential to prolong the QT interval. The patient has not been previously documented to have the BCR-ABL Y253H, E255K/V, T315I or F359C/V mutation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the feasibility of administering the combination of nilotinib and LDE225 for the treatment of chronic or accelerated phase of CML.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been on buprenorphine maintenance treatment for the past year due to opioid dependency. She is seeking at least a 4 mg reduction in her buprenorphine maintenance dose. Her urine toxicology screen is positive for buprenorphine at the time of screening. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications that are known to interact with the study drug. She has agreed to collection of blood samples for genotyping of CYP2D6 metabolizer status. As a female of childbearing potential, she has been using birth control for at least 30 days and has agreed to use an acceptable form of birth control through at least 30 days after the last dose of study drug. She has no known abnormalities in her cardiovascular exam.

Pt is a 17yo M with a confirmed diagnosis of Cystic Fibrosis. He has a FEV1 of 50% predicted and is able to exercise, but struggles with motivation and adherence to exercise regimens. He currently participates in some physical activities, such as hiking and swimming, but reports difficulty in maintaining a consistent exercise routine. He has access to the internet and is interested in participating in a partially supervised exercise program to improve his lung function and quality of life. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 4 weeks and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He does not have any unstable medical conditions or recent injuries that would preclude him from exercise. He is currently taking inhaled antibiotics and DNAse, but has not had any recent medication changes. He is not colonized with Burkholderia cenocepacia.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital after experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. He was diagnosed with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. The patient has been on mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours and is eligible for the study. The patient has a medical history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been hospitalized several times in the past for exacerbations. The patient is alert and oriented and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has an arterial catheter in place for blood sampling at study start. The patient is not pregnant and does not have a history of home mechanical ventilation or end-stage liver disease. The patient has not been on mechanical ventilation for more than 48 hours and is not likely to require extracorporeal support. The patient does not have severe cardiogenic shock or isolated right heart failure. The patient is not suffering from head trauma or other conditions where intra-cranial pressure may be elevated and tight regulation of arterial CO2 level is paramount. The patient is not a primary neurological patient with limited prognosis or stroke hemiplegia. The patient is able to participate in the study and provide consent or have advice from the next of kin or treating physician following understanding and acceptance of oral and written information describing the study.

A 55 year old woman who underwent surgery for breast cancer at the University of Campinas is experiencing restricted shoulder range of motion due to axillary lymph node dissection. She is currently experiencing difficulty in performing daily activities and feels that her quality of life has been affected. She has not received any previous radiotherapy and does not have any bone metastasis in the homolateral upper limb. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is interested in receiving manual therapy and kinesiotherapy to improve her shoulder range of motion and upper limb functionality.

Pt is a 55yo M with a recently diagnosed locally advanced lung cancer who is scheduled for locoregional radiation therapy. He presents with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 10-pack year smoking history, with no prior history of cardiac disease. He is classified as having an intermediate to high future cardiovascular risk based on Framingham Risk Score assessment. The patient agrees to participate in a prospective study that will investigate the correlation of post-tomotherapy cardiovascular effects with myocardial perfusion and cardiac functional studies. Before initiating radiation therapy, the patient will undergo myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) with Tl-201 and a Cadimium-Zinc-Telluride (CZT) cardiac camera to complete baseline evaluation. The patient will then receive scheduled treatment, including radiation therapy. The patient will be followed-up regularly in the cardiovascular outpatient department, and further work-up will be indicated if there is functional status deterioration or aggravated symptoms. Post-therapeutic myocardial perfusion study will be performed 12 months after the initial cardiovascular outpatient department visit. Blood samples will be drawn for measurements of blood glucose, lipid profile, and circulating biomarker of CRP. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he has a thoracic malignancy and is classified as having an intermediate to high future cardiovascular risk clinically. The patient does not meet the exclusion criteria as he has no pre-existing cardiac disease, is not pregnant, and does not have any medical contraindication of stress cardiac SPECT.

As this is a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of the Incredible Years (IY) Teacher Classroom Management (TCM) program in reducing behavior problems and promoting social competence in students aged 6-8 years (school) and in children aged 3-6 year (day-care), there is no specific patient description required. Instead, the trial will involve recruiting schools, students/children aged 3-8 years, and teachers and staff who work with students/children aged 3-8 years. The inclusion criteria for the trial are schools who meet predefined criteria for program implementation of IY TCM (intervention) and schools who have not implemented any IY program (comparison), students/children aged 3-8 year with parents who speak Norwegian, and teachers and staff who work with students/children aged 3-8 years. The exclusion criteria are schools who did not meet predefined criteria for program implementation of IY TCM, students/children aged 3-8 year with parents who do not speak Norwegian, and teachers and staff who do not work with students/children aged 3-8 years, and who have known the students/children for fewer than 3 weeks.

A 25-year-old male with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weight of 70 kg presented to the clinic for the study. He has no significant medical history, and all laboratory values were within normal limits. He has not participated in any clinical study or taken any investigational drug in the past 12 weeks. He has no claustrophobia and is able to undergo both MRI and PET scanning. He is interested in participating in the study and would like to learn more about the potential benefits of AZD7325.

A 30-year-old female came to the clinic complaining of severe itching and burning sensation in her genital area. She reported having thick, white, and odorless vaginal discharge. She noticed these symptoms after taking antibiotics for a urinary tract infection. The patient reported that she has never had a vaginal infection before. She denied any history of sexually transmitted infections. She had regular menstrual cycles and was not pregnant. The physical examination revealed erythema and swelling of the vulva and vaginal walls. The gynecological exam confirmed the diagnosis of severe vulvovaginal candidiasis. The patient provided written informed consent and agreed to participate in the clinical trial.

40-year-old male, who underwent a cadaveric kidney transplant 6 months ago, is currently on immunosuppressive therapy of tacrolimus and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF). His graft function is stable with a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gout. He has no history of malignancy or recent infections. He is compliant with his medications and has not taken any investigational drugs in the past four weeks. He has no known thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, or leukopenia. He has no evidence of severe liver disease or HIV/Hepatitis B surface antigen positivity. He is interested in participating in the study to investigate the tolerability and safety of converting from MMF to enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium (EC-MPS).

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been diagnosed with a small umbilical hernia. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He has never undergone surgery before and is nervous about the procedure. However, he is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help improve surgical techniques and outcomes for future patients. He understands the study requirements and is able to read and understand Danish. He has no known allergies to the medications used in the study and has normal renal function. He is not pregnant or lactating, and there is no indication for a rapid sequence induction.

Patient is a 46-year-old man from Brazil who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is about to begin chemotherapy treatment. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. He reports feeling fatigued and experiencing occasional night sweats. His physical exam is unremarkable, except for mild splenomegaly. His blood work shows a white blood cell count of 45,000/μL, hemoglobin of 9.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 30,000/μL. He has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 55-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy, which revealed a 2.5 cm infiltrating ductal carcinoma with involvement of one lymph node. The patient has no significant past medical history and no history of prior radiation therapy. She underwent genetic testing, which showed no mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2. Her oncologist has recommended proton beam therapy as part of her treatment plan. The patient is interested in participating in the Proton Therapy Patient Registry study to help contribute to the research on this relatively rare radiation modality. She is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who suffered a tibial fracture 9 months ago and has not achieved bone union despite prior surgical interventions. The patient has undergone major surgeries including bone grafting and internal fixation. The patient is in good health and has an ASA 1 classification. The largest cortical gap in any radiographic incidence is between 1-5 cm. The patient is willing and able to participate in post-operative evaluations and required rehabilitation regimen. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the active substance or collagen. The patient does not have any known auto-immune disease, active infection, or any systemic illness that could impair bone healing. The patient is not currently receiving chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunosuppressant treatment. The patient does not have severely compromised soft tissue coverage or vascularization at the non-union site. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is not suffering from neuromuscular diseases or conditions interfering with normal weight bearing. The patient is a suitable candidate for the trial.

The patient is a 5-year-old girl who will be undergoing routine blood work to monitor her chronic condition. She has a history of anxiety and fear related to medical procedures, often requiring her parents to restrain her during blood draws. She has no allergies and is not currently taking any medications. Her parents will be present during the procedure. The procedure is expected to take approximately 10-15 minutes. The patient has no known developmental abnormalities.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications or supplements. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol in moderation, with an average of 1-2 drinks per week. The patient is sexually active and willing to use a medically acceptable method of contraception during the study. He has signed and dated a written informed consent form prior to admission to the study in accordance with GCP and local legislation. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, or hormonal disorders. He has not undergone cholecystectomy or surgery of the gastrointestinal tract that could interfere with the pharmacokinetics of the trial medication. The patient has no history of seizures, stroke, or other relevant neurological or psychiatric disorders. He has not experienced relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts. The patient has not had any chronic or relevant acute infections and has no history of relevant allergy or hypersensitivity. He has not taken any drugs with a long half-life within 30 days or less than 10 half-lives of the respective drug prior to administration of trial medication. The patient has not used any drugs that might reasonably influence the results of the trial within 10 days prior to administration of trial medication. He has not participated in another trial where an investigational drug has been administered within 60 days prior to planned administration of trial medication. The patient is willing to refrain from smoking on specified trial days and is able to comply with dietary regimen of trial site. His laboratory parameters are within the reference range.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and is currently receiving treatment through outpatient dialysis at a specified clinic. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. He reports occasional blurry vision and has not had a retinal evaluation in over a year due to difficulty accessing medical care outside of his dialysis appointments. He is willing to participate in the study and is over 18 years of age.

Patient is a 62-year-old male from the United States who has been experiencing symptoms of congestive heart failure for the past 6 months, including shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in the legs. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 10 years. He is retired and lives with his wife. His past medical and drug history are notable for hyperlipidemia and he is currently taking atorvastatin. His BMI is 30, BP: 140/90, HR: 80/min. Laboratory studies are within normal limits. The patient is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 15 year old boy who was recently diagnosed with an advanced stage of pediatric cancer. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but there is no curative option available for him. He is experiencing severe symptoms including pain, digestive disorders, asthenia, and anxiety. He is able to walk 100 meters without help and perform muscular strengthening exercises. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the feasibility and toxicity of adapted physical activity (APA) for patients with advanced pediatric malignancies. He and his parents have provided written informed consent for his participation. He has not participated in any Phase I trial, does not have dyspnea at rest or exertion, and does not have any cardiovascular pathology. His life expectancy is expected to be more than three months and his disease is currently stable. He is willing to comply with medical follow up.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and requires maintenance hemodialysis. He is scheduled to have a radio-cephalic arteriovenous fistula (AVF) created for vascular access. He has no history of psychosis or osteonecrosis. He has no previous AVF in the ipsilateral arm or current central venous catheter in the ipsilateral side. He is not currently taking any oral, rectal or injectable glucocorticoids (CS) or immunosuppressant drugs. Inhaled glucocorticoids are allowed. He is not currently taking NSAIDs. He is willing to comply with the study's procedures and will use reliable and acceptable contraceptive methods throughout the study and until three months after the last study medication. He has no history of malignancy or uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. He has no signs of active infection requiring systemic treatment. He is negative for Quantiferon test and hepatitis panel. He has no history of anaphylaxis or severe allergic responses. He has no planned live-virus vaccinations or surgical interventions within six weeks after AVF surgery. His hepatic function and hematology panel are within normal range.

68-year-old female patient who has been experiencing memory problems for the past year. She has been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) by her primary care physician. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of hypertension, diabetes, or heart disease. She is postmenopausal, and not taking any hormonal therapy. She is fluent in English and has good cognitive abilities to be able to follow instructions and complete all study procedures as per the protocol. She has no history of glaucoma, arrhythmias, severe lower extremity vaso-occlusive disease, or clinically significant valvular disease. She is not pregnant and is willing to comply with study-specific instructions. The patient has read and understood the study rationale and is willing to sign informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver. He is experiencing hypersplenism, which has led to a platelet count of less than 50*10^9/L. He has no evidence of portal vein thrombosis or spleno-mesenteric thrombosis according to his ultrasound evaluations and angio-CT. He has not been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma or any other malignancy, and does not have a hypercoagulable state other than his liver disease. He is not taking any oral contraceptives, anticoagulation, or anti-platelet drugs. His baseline INR is below 2, and he is not classified as Child-Pugh grade C. He has no history of hemorrhagic stroke, and is not currently pregnant. He does not have uncontrolled hypertension, and is under the age of 75. He has not been diagnosed with F2 varices with red whale marks or F3 varices, nor does he have bleeding portal hypertension. He is not infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old Chinese male who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) due to coronary heart disease. He is currently taking dual antiplatelet therapy consisting of 100mg of aspirin daily and 75mg of clopidogrel for at least 1 year after the procedure. He has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit 3 years ago. His medical records show that he had genetic testing done at Peking University First Hospital as part of a previous study. He has completed 18 months of follow-up after the PCI procedure and is eligible for this study. His platelet function was assessed using VerifyNow® P2Y12 (VN-P2Y12) assay (Accumetrics, San Diego, California, USA) during the previous study. The investigators will use this data along with his genetic test results to explore the effect of smoking and genetic risk factors on restenosis and efficacy of clopidogrel after de novo PCI. The patient has no history of cancer, viral hepatitis, or any other related diseases, and his clinical data is complete.

The patient is a 30 year old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia. She has been receiving blood transfusions every 3-4 weeks for the past 10 years, which has greatly affected her quality of life. She is now interested in participating in a clinical trial for gene correction of HBB in patient-specific iHSCs using CRISPR/Cas9. She has no history of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or other organ transplantation. Her organ function is adequate, including a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dl, ALT/AST level of 1.5×ULN, and total bilirubin level of 0.9x ULN. Her chest X-ray and ECG results are normal and she has no history of serious cardiopulmonary diseases. She is willing to use reliable contraceptives during the study period and within three months of discharge. She understands the post-physical therapy/rehabilitation process and is willing to undergo it if needed. She has no known allergies to macromolecular biological agents such as antibodies or cytokines and has not received any investigational clinical trials within the past 3 months. She has no active hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection and no infectious diseases that cannot be controlled within 4 weeks. She does not have severe central nervous system disease or epilepsy and is not suffering from mental illness or alcohol/drug dependence. She is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any other medical conditions that would make her ineligible for the study.

A 31-year-old woman was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) a year ago. She has had at least one documented relapse in the last year and has an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 4.0. She is currently not experiencing any relapse and has not had any in the last 30 days. She is not pregnant or nursing and has no other chronic disease of the immune system. She takes daily vitamin supplements and has no allergies to any food or drugs. She has never had any suicidal ideation or behavior in the past. Her CBC laboratory values are within normal range. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effects of a single infusion of VAY736 on disease activity in patients with RRMS.

The patient is a 40 year old woman who has been diagnosed with severe asthma for the past 24 months. She has been experiencing frequent exacerbations with symptoms including wheezing, shortness of breath, and coughing. She has tried several medications including inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators, but her symptoms have not been well-controlled. She has not participated in any therapeutic clinical trials and is willing to participate in this study. She is insured and able to read and comprehend the questionnaires.

A 60-year-old man who suffered a stroke 6 months ago presents with complaints of difficulty in sleeping. He has no history of psychiatric illness or sleep disorder prior to his stroke. He is currently on medications for hypertension and dyslipidemia. He is interested in improving his sleep quality as he feels that it is affecting his daily activities. The patient is fluent in English and has reliable access to the internet. He is currently residing in the United Kingdom and is in stable health. The patient does not have any upcoming surgeries scheduled in the next 5 months and is not currently undergoing treatment for insomnia. The patient does not have any history of seizures or untreated obstructive sleep apnea. He is not a habitual night shift or evening shift worker, and has no other serious clinical conditions that may affect his participation in the study.

42-year-old male with a history of chronic sinusitis and maxillary sinus disease presents with persistent nasal congestion, facial pain, and pressure despite maximal medical management. He has never undergone sinus surgery before and is interested in exploring surgical options. He does not have a history of fungal disease, Samter's triad, hemophilia or prior sinus surgery. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of balloon sinus dilation with traditional endoscopic sinus surgery, and is able to commit to the required follow-up visits for a minimum of 12 months.

Patient is a 9-year-old boy from the United States who was diagnosed with cancer in his left leg. He has undergone chemotherapy that includes vincristine and has developed damage to his peripheral nervous system affecting the strength, sensation, and flexibility in his foot and ankle. This has led to a change in his walking pattern and ankle flexibility and has contributed to decreased physical activity level and fatigue. His Ped-mTNS score is 6, and his step length is more than 1 standard deviation below mean for his age. His ankle dorsiflexion passive range of motion is less than 10 degrees. He is able to give assent according to institutional guidelines, and his parents have given their consent for him to participate in the study. He has no history of neurological, developmental, or genetic disorders and does not have osteonecrosis. His lower extremity sarcomas have been ruled out, and he has antigravity dorsiflexion strength.

Patient is a Hispanic woman who is HIV-positive and between the ages of 21 and 50. She has a CD4 cell count of 500 cells/mm3 or less, or a viral load of 1000 copies/mL or higher despite being on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART). The patient has a minimum education level of 9th grade and is a non-drug abuser, with no history of diabetes or use of hypoglycemic agents. She has not had any opportunistic infections of the central nervous system and does not have any underlying neurologic or neuropsychiatric disorders. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has not given birth within the last 60 days. She is willing to give informed consent and is capable of understanding the informed consent process. The patient is physically untrained and normally active, and is interested in participating in a 6-week exercise program to improve her cardiorespiratory fitness, insulin resistance, and cognitive function.

This clinical trial is only open to participants who have previously taken part in an Astellas sponsored single agent ASP2215 trial and have not met any discontinuation criteria. The eligible subject should not have any persistent intolerable toxicity from continued treatment of ASP2215 and should be deriving benefit from its continued use. Female subjects must agree not to try to become pregnant during the study and for 180 days after the final study drug administration, and must not donate ova, and must not breastfeed throughout the study period. Male subjects and their female spouse/partners who are of childbearing potential must be using highly effective contraception starting at Screening and continue throughout the study period, and for 120 days after the final study drug administration. The subject must agree not to participate in another interventional study while on treatment. The clinical trial excludes subjects who require treatment with concomitant drugs that are strong inducers of cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A or require treatment with concomitant drugs that target serotonin 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1 (5HT1R) or 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2B (5HT2BR) or sigma nonspecific receptor.

A 6-year-old male child is admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with severe respiratory distress. The child is diagnosed with pneumonia and requires immediate mechanical ventilation support. The child is receiving supplemental oxygen for abnormal gas exchange with an oxygen saturation of 90%. The child is an emergency admission accepted to the participating PICU within the first 6 hours of face-to-face contact with PICU staff. The child is not previously recruited to the Oxy-PICU study and has no known brain pathology or injury as the primary reason for admission. The child has no known pulmonary hypertension, sickle cell disease, or uncorrected congenital cardiac disease. There is no end-of-life care plan in place with limitation of resuscitation, and the child is expected to survive PICU admission. This is the child's first admission requiring mechanical ventilation support.

A 42-year-old woman called the emergency number (1-1-2) from her smartphone when she saw her husband lying unconscious on the floor. She is at home with her two children (age 8 and 10) who are also present in the room. She has a video-capable smartphone and is willing to livestream the situation. She is able to provide basic information about her husband's condition, and she is willing to follow the medical dispatcher's instructions. She has no history of medical problems and is not taking any medication. She has basic knowledge of CPR, but has not received formal training. She is currently feeling anxious and worried about her husband's condition.

A 56 yo F with newly diagnosed T2DM and HbA1c of 8.5%. She has no history of cardiovascular complications and is not currently taking any antihyperglycemic drugs. She takes a daily low-dose aspirin for primary prevention. She has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril 10mg daily. She does not smoke and does not have any liver or kidney disease. She has never been pregnant. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of sitagliptin on endothelial function.

A 55-year-old male patient is admitted to the ICU with a history of hypertension and diabetes. He is currently on medications for both conditions. He is scheduled for a surgery to repair an abdominal aortic aneurysm. The patient is cooperative and able to provide informed consent. He has no history of cardiac disease and no known allergies. He has a BMI of 28 and is a non-smoker. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the procedures involved.

A 25-year-old man diagnosed with Gilles de la Tourette's syndrome is interested in participating in a clinical trial to gain a better understanding of his condition. He experiences multiple motor tics and vocal tics on a daily basis and has been on stable medication for over a year. He has a high school education and works part-time in retail. He has no history of cognitive disorders, mental retardation, or serious neurological pathologies. He has 20/20 vision and does not wear glasses or contacts. He is comfortable with the English language and able to understand words associated with emotions. He is not currently participating in any other studies and is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up. He is excited to potentially contribute to research that may benefit others with Gilles de la Tourette's syndrome.

Pt is a 14yo F with a long history of kidney stones and calcium oxalate crystals in her urine, who was recently diagnosed with primary hyperoxaluria type 3 (PH3) after genetic testing.
