She is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history. Her symptoms include recurrent flank pain, nausea, vomiting, and painful urination. Her most recent stone event occurred 6 months ago, with a 4mm stone that required surgical removal. Her 24-hour urine collection showed a Uox level of 1.2 mmol/24 hours normalized to 1.73 m2 BSA. She has no history of liver disease and her eGFR at screening was 65 mL/min. She is willing and able to comply with study procedures, including 24-hour urine collections and follow-up visits every 6 months for up to 2 years.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has a body mass index (BMI) between 18 and 30 kg/m² and has not smoked cigarettes or used nicotine-based products in the past 3 months. He has no history of liver or renal insufficiency, allergies, hypersensitivity or intolerance to JNJ-54861911 or its excipients, sulfonamides, midazolam, caffeine or tolbutamide. He is not HIV positive and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has undergone a physical examination, medical history, vital signs and 12-lead ECG performed at Screening, and all results were normal. He is sexually active with a woman of child-bearing potential and agrees to use adequate contraception methods throughout the study. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent document indicating that he understands the purpose and procedures required for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with gynecologic cancer. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and pelvic pain for the past few months, which led her to seek medical attention. She underwent several diagnostic tests, including a pelvic ultrasound and biopsy, which confirmed the presence of gynecologic cancer. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She does not have any known allergies. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo conformal radiotherapy for her cancer. She has no evidence of metastases.

A 68-year old retired teacher has been scheduled for an elective coronary artery bypass surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been on medication for these conditions for the last five years. She lives with her husband and is independent with activities of daily living. She has two children and three grandchildren who she enjoys spending time with. She reports occasional forgetfulness but denies any other cognitive impairment. She is fluent in English and has no history of psychiatric illness or use of tranquilizers or antidepressants. She wears glasses and hearing aids but her vision and hearing are adequate for communication. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

45 y/o female with metastatic breast cancer, diagnosed [**2132-5-14**]. Patient has received anthracycline and taxane based chemotherapy as well as endocrine therapy, with progression of disease. Imaging studies have shown multiple liver metastases and a solitary brain metastasis. The patient has previously undergone radiation therapy to the brain. The patient is otherwise generally healthy with no significant comorbidities, and has a performance status of 1. The patient is not pregnant and uses effective contraception. The patient is willing and able to undergo autologous bone marrow or peripheral blood stem cell transplantation. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to E. coli derived proteins.

A 52-year-old female patient has been diagnosed with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) for 5 years. She has participated in a previous PBC study that involved seladelpar treatment and is interested in continuing the treatment. She has no history of allergies or intolerances to medications and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. Her liver function tests (AST, ALT, and total bilirubin) are within normal range. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use appropriate birth control methods during the study period. She has not received any systemic steroids, fibrates or obeticholic acid within the last 2-3 months. She does not have any other medical condition that would preclude full participation in the study or confound its results. She is willing to give written informed consent and is interested in contributing to the advancement of PBC treatment.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who lives alone in her own home. She was diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment about 2 years ago. Her symptoms include difficulty remembering appointments, losing track of time, and misplacing items. She has no prior history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has no history of psychiatric illness. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. She is able to perform activities of daily living independently, but has some difficulty with complex tasks such as paying bills and managing her medications. She has no history of falls or other injuries. She is interested in participating in this study to better understand the experience of living alone with cognitive impairment and to help inform the development of programs that could benefit others in similar situations. The participant is available for interviews and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 56-year-old male diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) after experiencing several episodes of headaches, dizziness, and confusion. The patient has no history of cancer and has previously been in good health. The patient underwent biopsy and was diagnosed with GBM. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is currently taking 8mg of dexamethasone per day for symptom management. The patient has no history of immunodeficiency, active TB, or active autoimmune disease. The patient is negative for HIV and has not received any anti-cancer monoclonal antibody within the past 4 weeks. The patient has no known significant drug allergies or contraindications for 3T MRI. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial and has

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia 3 years ago. He experiences auditory hallucinations and delusions, and has a history of medication non-adherence. He currently takes risperidone and has been stable for the past 6 months with no significant exacerbations. He has completed high school and has an IQ of 85. He reports difficulty with working memory and processing speed, which has impacted his ability to maintain employment and social relationships. He is interested in participating in a cognitive training program to improve his cognitive function and daily functioning. He has no history of substance abuse or medical conditions that affect cognition. He is willing and able to provide informed consent.

A 38-year-old female patient came to the clinic seeking treatment for moderate-to-severe crow's feet lines and glabellar lines. She reported that these lines have been bothering her for the past few years, and despite trying various creams and serums, she has not seen any significant improvement. She has previously participated in the phase 3 study for crow's feet lines and is interested in participating in the extension study that explores the efficacy and safety of DWP450 for treating both crow's feet lines and glabellar lines. She is generally in good health and has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in this clinical trial.

Patient is a 60-year-old Japanese man who has been diagnosed with relapsed multiple myeloma. He has received at least one prior line of therapy for MM and has achieved a partial response to at least one prior regimen. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1. The patient has not received daratumumab or other anti-CD38 therapies previously. He is not refractory to bortezomib or other proteasome inhibitors and is not intolerant to bortezomib. The patient has not received anti-myeloma treatment within 2 weeks or 5 pharmacokinetic half-lives of the treatment, whichever is longer, before the date of daratumumab first administration. The only exception is emergency use of a short course of corticosteroids (equivalent of dexamethasone 40 milligram per day [mg/day] for a maximum of 4 days) before treatment. The patient has no history of malignancy (other than multiple myeloma) within 3 years before the date of daratumumab first administration. The patient has no concurrent medical condition or disease (eg, active systemic infection, pulmonary impairment) that is likely to interfere with study procedures.

A 35-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with acute abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She has a history of endometriosis and had a laparoscopic surgery a year ago. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease and anemia. He has been on dialysis for the past 6 months and has been receiving short-acting epoetin (EPO) treatment. His current hemoglobin level is 9.5 g/dL. Serum ferritin level and transferrin saturation (TSAT) are 150 ng/mL and 25%, respectively. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has never received a blood transfusion and has no history of bleeding disorders or hemoglobinopathies. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

5-year-old child with Prader-Willi syndrome, diagnosed with genetic testing and treated with growth hormone for the past year. Child has no history of oxytocin use for at least 5 years. No significant medical history except for behavioral troubles related to Prader-Willi syndrome. No hepatic or renal insufficiency, abnormal electrocardiogram, arterial hypertension or hypotension, or diabetes. Child is able to accept intranasal administrations.

50 yo M with a history of degenerative disc disease and chronic back pain presents for elective lumbar laminectomy with instrumentation. Pre-op evaluation reveals no contraindications to anesthesia. Patient consents to participate in a clinical trial studying the duration of blockade of peripheral nerves with bupivacaine depending on the adjuvants. Patient is randomly assigned to receive a solution of bupivacaine 0.375% together with dexamethasone 0.02% as the adjuvant. Blockade is performed successfully with no complications. The duration of the blockade is estimated by puncturing the skin with a needle. The intensity of pain is assessed at 6, 12, 24, and 36 hours after the blockade using a Visual analog scale (VAS). The amount of narcotic anesthetic used in the postoperative period is also recorded. In addition, patient undergoes electromyography of the innervation area of the blocked nerve before the surgery and 24 and 36 hours after surgery. The trial is designed to determine the duration of the blockade and the amount of narcotic anesthetic used in the postoperative period between patients receiving different adjuvants to bupivacaine. The patient is closely monitored throughout the study period for any adverse events.

63-year-old female patient, living in Scotland, has been registered with her GP practice for over 10 years. She has a history of high blood pressure and has been taking medication for it for the last 5 years. She has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has a family history of bowel cancer, with both her mother and father having been diagnosed with the disease in their 70s. The patient received a bowel cancer screening kit by mail from the National Bowel Cancer Screening Programme 3 months ago but has not yet returned the sample for testing. The patient has previously given consent to receive phone text/SMS messages for reminders from her GP practice. The patient has no previous experience of bowel cancer screening or knowledge of its benefits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with Autistic Disorder according to DSM-IV-TR. He has completed the 031-11-002 study and visited the hospital during week 8. He is currently receiving outpatient treatment for his condition. He has no other known disorders on the autism spectrum, such as Asperger's or Rett's Disorder. The patient has not been diagnosed with Fragile-X Syndrome or Childhood Disintegrative Disorder. The patient is currently not taking any medications that are listed as a contraindication in the ABILIFY package insert.

A 25-year-old male, who works as a teacher, presented with no significant medical history, except for a mild allergy to eggs. He denied any recent use of anti-allergic medications, blood products or immunoglobulins. He was in good physical and mental health, without any diagnosis of chronic diseases, such as diabetes, heart disease, or hypertension. He reported no use of any vaccine in the past 30 days or any medication under investigation in the past year. He had no history of convulsions, psychiatric disorders, or alcoholism. He denied any illicit drug abuse. He was willing to strictly follow the study protocol and had the capacity to understand and sign the informed consent form. His intellectual level allowed him to fill in the diaries for registering of symptoms at home. He was willing to undergo serological testing for HIV, HBV, and HCV. His physical examination at screening period showed no clinically significant changes, and lab examination at screening period showed normal ranges, determined by the laboratory. He was eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female from the United States, diagnosed with systemic sclerosis (SSc) and presenting with digital ulcerations on her fingers. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and has tried various treatments with limited success. She has a history of hypertension and has been taking lisinopril for the past 2 years. The patient is a non-smoker and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options for her condition.

A 25-year-old male diagnosed with X-linked retinitis pigmentosa (XLRP) caused by mutations in RPGR gene. The patient has a history of night blindness, visual field loss, and difficulty seeing in low light conditions. He has undergone genetic testing and has been confirmed to have RPGR mutations. The patient has previously participated in the MGT009 study and received AAV2-RPGR gene therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the Long-Term Follow-Up study and able to meet the study requirements. He is in good general health and has not experienced any adverse effects related to the gene therapy.

The patient is a newborn infant weighing 700 grams who required mechanical ventilation within the first 48 hours of delivery due to premature pulmonary disease. The infant has received exogenous surfactant during mechanical ventilation. The study aims to compare the effectiveness of two Bubble CPAP devices, BabiPlus and B&B, in improving oxygenation and decreasing the need for re-intubation or non-invasive positive pressure ventilation in infants with extremely low birth weight. Infants with birth weight between 500 and 1250 grams and who meet the study inclusion criteria will be considered for enrollment in the trial. The study will not include infants with congenital conditions that preclude the use of CPAP, birth weight >1250 grams or <500 grams or infants whose parents do not speak English.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who suffered a first-ever stroke 4 months ago, resulting in moderate to severe movement impairment of her left upper limb. She has no balance problems and does not experience excessive spasticity in any of the joints of her affected limb. She is currently receiving physical therapy twice a week and has been making some progress in her recovery. However, she is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer additional innovative and effective interventions for individualized stroke rehabilitation. The patient is motivated and willing to follow study instructions and perform study tasks. Her Mini Mental State Examination score is 28, indicating no cognitive impairment. The patient has no upper limb fracture within the past 3 months and does not exhibit any physician-determined major medical problems or poor physical conditions that would interfere with participation. She does not experience excessive pain in any joint that might limit participation.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been missing her upper front teeth for several years due to trauma. She has been wearing a removable denture that has been causing her discomfort and difficulty eating. The patient has a partially edentulous anterior maxilla with a residual ridge length of ≤11.5 mm. She is a non-smoker with no intraoral soft and hard tissue pathology. The patient has no systemic conditions that contraindicate implant placement and does not have a history of radiation therapy to the head and neck. She has no immunodeficiency pathology, bruxism, stress situation, or emotional instability. Her aesthetic demands are realistic and she is willing to undergo vertical and horizontal alveolar ridge augmentation using autogenous onlay blocks combined with guided bone regeneration using native collagen membrane.

This is a 65 year-old female with a history of missing teeth and difficulty chewing due to poor fitting dentures. She has been wearing double complete dentures for the past 10 years and has noticed occasional clicking and discomfort in her jaw joint. She has no history of orthodontic treatment and is not currently undergoing any dental procedures. She is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the prevalence of temporomandibular disorder (TMD) in individuals wearing double complete dentures.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing feelings of sadness and hopelessness for the past 6 months. She reports a loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed, difficulty sleeping and concentrating, and significant weight loss. She denies any history of manic or hypomanic episodes or any psychotic symptoms. She has never been hospitalized for psychiatric reasons nor has she received any previous treatment for her depression. She is currently not taking any medications and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has a supportive family and a stable job. The patient meets the criteria for Major Depressive Disorder and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her symptoms.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who recently got diagnosed with colorectal cancer with hepatic metastases. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes for which he takes medications. He has no history of allergies to iodine contrast media. His creatinine clearance is 70 ml/min. He is currently undergoing evaluation for the eligibility of systemic treatment. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the written informed consent. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has undergone contrast-enhanced spiral computed tomography, which has shown liver nodules ≥ 20 mm in diameter. He is designated for treatment with standard-of-care first-line bevacizumab-containing, fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. He is not participating in any other interventional trial with an investigational medicinal product.

The patient is a 64-year-old man diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) 2 years ago after experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. His past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medications. He has previously undergone treatment with a standard chemotherapy-containing regimen but failed to achieve at least a partial response or documented disease progression after response. His most recent CT scan shows measurable disease. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild lymphadenopathy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. Laboratory tests reveal neutrophils of 1.2 x 109/L, platelets of 80 x 109/L, creatinine clearance of 60 ml/min, AST and ALT within normal limits, and bilirubin within normal limits. The patient has not received corticosteroids in excess of prednisone 10 mg/day or its equivalent with antineoplastic intent within the past 7 days. He has not undergone major surgery within the past 4 weeks, and he has recovered from toxicity of any prior anti-cancer therapy to <Grade 1 (except for alopecia, ANC, and platelets). The patient has no history of other active malignancies within the past 2 years, and he has no active clinically significant cardiovascular disease or QTcF >480 msecs based on Fridericia's formula or other significant electrocardiogram abnormalities including second degree atrioventricular (AV) block Type II, or third degree AV block. He is able to swallow capsules, and there is no disease that significantly affects gastrointestinal function. He has no active infection or known HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection. He has not received allogenic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation prior to enrollment, and he has no life-threatening illness, medical condition or organ system dysfunction which could compromise his safety or put the study at risk. He is not currently taking any medication which is a strong cytochrome P450, family 3, subfamily A (CYP3A) inhibitor or strong CYP3A inducer.

A 28-year-old woman who is fluent in German presents with no history of chronic or mental illness. She does not regularly consume caffeine, alcohol, or engage in intensive physical exercise. She is not currently taking any psychotropic medications. The patient does not have acute hay fever. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to examine the effects of interventions that optimize expectations and induce positive emotions after an acute stressor.

This is a 67-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion for the past six months. His echocardiogram showed severe aortic stenosis and he was referred for surgical intervention. He has opted for aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting. He has no other significant medical history and all his preoperative labs and tests were within normal limits. He is eager to participate in this clinical trial to help improve outcomes for future cardiac surgery patients.

47 yo F with a history of metastatic breast cancer (MBC) with ER+, PR+, HER2-, and AR+ tumors who has received 2 prior hormonal therapies and 1 prior chemotherapy treatment in the advanced setting. Patient presents with worsening symptoms including fatigue, bone pain, and decreased appetite despite treatment with bisphosphonate therapy. CT scan reveals progression of bone metastases. Patient has a past medical history of hypertension and type II diabetes mellitus, which is well-controlled with oral hypoglycemic agents. Patient has an ECOG performance status score of 1, with adequate hematological, liver, and renal function. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 3 months and is willing and able to comply with the study and follow-up procedures. Archival tumor tissue from a primary biopsy or metastatic lesion has been confirmed to express AR≥10% staining by immunohisto-chemistry. The patient has not received prior anti-androgen therapy and does not have active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease. The patient is not receiving treatment for any other malignancy and has not received any investigational drugs ≤21 days or 5 half-lives prior to the first dose of orteronel. The patient is willing to use adequate contraceptive measures during the entire study treatment period and for 4 months after the last dose of study drug.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with colon cancer and has scheduled a surgical procedure under general anesthesia. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control his blood pressure. He has no history of renal disease and does not require dialysis. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He lives with his wife and two adult children. He is physically active and enjoys taking long walks in the park. His BMI is 26 and his blood pressure at the time of the screening is 130/80 mmHg. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or any other significant medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is able to understand and consent to participate in this clinical study, expressed by signing the Informed Consent (IC).

A 57-year-old male with type 2 diabetes has been experiencing chronic pain in his feet for the past 3 years. His diabetes is well controlled with medication and lifestyle modifications. He reports that his pain has been interfering with his sleep and daily activities. He has no other chronic pain conditions, and his medical and psychiatric history is unremarkable. He has not taken any medications for his neuropathic pain before. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of SPM 927 for the treatment of painful distal diabetic neuropathy.

A 29-year-old African American female presents to the hospital with regular contractions and pelvic pressure. She is currently 28 weeks pregnant with her first child and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far. She denies any history of preterm labor or delivery. Her medical history is unremarkable and she does not have any known allergies. Her vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 90 beats/min, and respiratory rate of 16 breaths/min. Her physical examination reveals a gravid uterus consistent with 28 weeks of gestation, with regular uterine contractions and a cervical dilation of 2 centimeters. There is no evidence of fever or fetal distress. Laboratory tests are ordered and show no significant abnormalities. She is diagnosed with spontaneous preterm labor and is offered participation in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of retosiban versus atosiban for women in spontaneous preterm labor. She gives written informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 56-year-old male diagnosed with colon cancer and currently admitted to the Long Term Care (LTC) unit. He has been receiving chemotherapy treatment for the past 6 months and has a history of thrombocytopenia. The patient has read and signed the informed consent form, including the specific consent for genotyping of clotting factors. He has social insurance and weighs more than 50kg with a hemoglobin level of 8.5 g/dl. The patient has not been previously included in the study and does not fall under the category of vulnerable persons.

A 35-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia based on a SCID-P interview who is fluent in English and able to understand the study requirements. The patient has no past or present Axis I diagnosis, no significant medical or neurological disease, and no history of head injury with a loss of consciousness greater than 15 minutes. The patient does not have a hearing deficit greater than 40dB in both ears and is not substance dependent, except for caffeine and nicotine. The patient does not have any first-degree relative with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. The patient is willing to participate in EEG and MRI sessions, as well as behavioral testing, and is comfortable with the vibratory sensation produced with the electrical current during the tasks. The patient is willing to sign a separate permission form for the study team to contact their current or former doctor(s) for mental health information if needed.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is concerned about her family history of liver disease and dyslipidemia. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is motivated to participate in this study to gain a better understanding of her risk for developing fatty liver and atherogenic dyslipidemia. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m² and her glomerular filtration rate is estimated to be above 60 ml/min/1.73 m². She does not have diabetes and her HbA1c value is less than 6.5%. She has normal thyroid function and blood pressure. She has not been diagnosed with any liver disease and her liver function tests are within the normal range. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has provided written consent and carries one of the following genetic variants: apo-CIII loss-of-function mutation, apo-CIII gain-of-function mutation, TM6SF2 E167K mutation, PNLPLA3 I148M mutation, apoE, LIPG, ANGPTL3, or ANGPTL8 LOF or GOF variants. She is eligible to participate in the study as a candidate for further evaluation of liver fat metabolism, lipid and apolipoprotein metabolism, and lipid phenotypes.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 5 years. He is a former smoker, having quit smoking 2 years ago after smoking for 40 years. He is currently taking a daily maintenance dose of inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes medication, and has no reported allergies. He is otherwise in good health and leads an active lifestyle, walking 30 minutes a day and engaging in light exercise. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past year.

The patient is a 15-year-old female who was diagnosed with insulin-dependent diabetes 3 years ago. She is currently on a multiple daily injection regimen and has had difficulty controlling her blood glucose levels. Her HbA1c level is consistently above 8%. She lives in a rural area outside of Lubbock and has limited access to specialized diabetes care. Her family is supportive of her diabetes management and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any psychiatric illness or developmental delay, and her educational level is above the 4th grade. She is not pregnant and does not have a known seizure disorder.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis (CRS) that has not responded to standard treatment with topical nasal corticosteroids after medical and surgical treatment. He experiences severe stuffiness, nasal discharge, facial pressure/pain, and sleep disorders, which significantly impact his quality of life. He has no known allergies or contraindications to the use of oral methylprednisolone or methotrexate. He has not received systemic oral methylprednisolone or methotrexate treatment for any other reason. He has no known malignant disease and has signed an informed consent form. He is willing to participate in an eight-week clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of low-dose methylprednisolone or low-dose methotrexate with the standard intranasal, topical corticosteroid treatment for treatment-resistant CRS with nasal polyposis.

The patient is a 65-year-old Hispanic woman who has been feeling down and anxious lately. She has a score of 6 on the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) and a score of 5 on the Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7) questionnaire. She is not currently on any medication for depression or anxiety. She has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. She has been diagnosed with high blood pressure and takes medication for it. She is retired and lives alone in Miami. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her prevent depression and anxiety. She is willing to commit to the study for the next two years and has medical clearance from her physician to participate in the health promotion intervention.

A 63-year-old man with hypertension for over 10 years. He has been taking three different anti-hypertensive drugs, including a diuretic, at maximum tolerated doses with no significant blood pressure reduction. He works as a businessman and has a history of smoking for 20 years, but he quit smoking 10 years ago. He drinks occasionally and exercises for 30 minutes a day at least 3 days a week. He has no known allergies or underlying diseases. He has not undergone any renal denervation procedure in the past. He speaks Mandarin fluently and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been struggling with Depersonalization Disorder for the past year. She reports feeling detached from herself and her surroundings, as if she is watching her life unfold from a distance. She has tried various medications and psychotherapy, but has not seen significant improvement. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any neurological disorders or contraindications for TMS. She is willing to participate in the study and is capable of providing informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been on hemodialysis for the past 2 years due to end-stage renal disease. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 8 weeks ago, confirmed by a positive PCR test. At the time of diagnosis, he had symptoms of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He was hospitalized for 3 days and received treatment with oxygen therapy and remdesivir. He has since recovered and is now stable. He has not received any COVID-19 vaccine. He has no known allergies or any other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

55 y/o postmenopausal female with a history of endometrial cancer, diagnosed with high-risk histologic type (serous) following a biopsy. She is scheduled for surgical staging which will include hysterectomy and selective lymphadenectomy. She has no significant past medical history, is not on any medications, and denies any allergies. She reports increasing vaginal bleeding over the last few months, and has also experienced pelvic pain and discomfort. She underwent a pelvic ultrasound which revealed thickening of the endometrium, prompting a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of endometrial cancer. She is motivated to participate in this study to help advance the understanding of lymph node counts in endometrial cancer staging.

The patient is a 27-year-old man who drinks alcohol socially, consuming 1-2 drinks per week. He has no history of alcohol abuse or dependence. He has a BMI of 24 and is able to read and complete study evaluations in English. He has never taken any investigational drug or participated in any other study involving excessive blood sampling or interventional measures. He does not have any medical conditions that would contraindicate the consumption of alcohol, and he does not have a history of neurological trauma or disease, delirium, hallucinations, or any significant systemic illness or unstable medical condition. He is not pregnant, nursing, or using unreliable methods of birth control. He has not donated blood within the past six weeks and is not currently using any psychoactive medications or drugs that could interact with AZD0530. His liver function tests and serum creatinine levels are within the normal range. He has no history of interstitial lung disease.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension presents with no significant symptoms. His blood pressure readings taken at home, outside of the clinic, have been consistently high, ranging from 135/85 mmHg to 145/95 mmHg. However, at the clinic, his blood pressure readings are normal, ranging from 120/80 mmHg to 130/85 mmHg. He has not been on any antihypertensive medications for the past two weeks. Laboratory results show microalbuminuria of 2.8 mg/mmol and a brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity of 1450 cm/s. His EKG shows left ventricular hypertrophy with a Cornell voltage combination of 2500 mm·ms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at investigating the target organ protection effects of antihypertensive treatment in patients with masked hypertension and at least one kind of target organ damage, as he understands the importance of controlling his blood pressure levels for his overall health.

The patient is a 30 year-old male with a history of ulcerative colitis. He was diagnosed 3 years ago based on symptoms of abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and urgency. He has been treated with mesalamine and corticosteroids with inadequate response. He has no history of asthma or autoimmune diseases. He has not had a colonoscopy in the past year but had adenomatous polyps removed during a previous colonoscopy 2 years ago. He has no history of untreated latent or active tuberculosis. He has not traveled outside the country in the past 6 months. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medication other than those prescribed for UC.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic with a history of malignant melanoma. He was previously enrolled in the GENTA-GM301 protocol and has completed 8 courses of oblimersen (G3139) and dacarbazine, which resulted in a complete objective response. He has unresectable and metastatic melanoma. The patient has measurable disease, and there is no uncontrolled brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no significant medical disease except for malignant melanoma. His hemoglobin level is 11 g/dL, and his platelet count is 150,000/mm^3. Other laboratory test results are within normal limits. He is HIV negative and has no active infection or autoimmune disease. He has no known hypersensitivity to phosphorothioate-containing oligonucleotides or dacarbazine. He is not currently receiving any other anticancer therapy.

55-year-old male with a history of chronic low back pain that radiates to both legs. He reports no history of trauma or neurological deficits. CT and MRI imaging show disc degeneration and stenosis at L4-L5 and L5-S1. The patient has failed conservative therapies including physical therapy, medication, and epidural steroid injections. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the CarboFix Pedicle Screw System. The patient has no history of metabolic bone disease or immune deficiency disease. He is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with bone metabolism. The patient has no metal allergies and is willing to make a commitment to return for required follow-up visits. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and has given informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman with a 5-year history of widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and insomnia was diagnosed with fibromyalgia. She has tried multiple treatments in the past, including physical therapy and various medications, but none have provided significant symptom relief. She reports that her pain is constant and widespread, affecting her back, neck, shoulders, hips, and legs. She also experiences frequent headaches and has difficulty concentrating. The patient has no history of rheumatologic diseases, bipolar disease, OCD, severe anxiety, or schizophrenia. She does not have any systemic infections, severe cardiac disease, or chronic steroid usage. She has been taking low-dose opioids intermittently for pain management. The patient is an English speaker and is interested in exploring new treatment options for fibromyalgia symptoms.

38 yo M with a recent history of non-penetrating traumatic brain injury (TBI) following a motor vehicle accident resulting in mild TBI symptoms such as headache, dizziness, and confusion. The patient was evaluated in the emergency department and received standard treatment for TBI. The patient has now been referred to a clinical trial to investigate the long-term effects of TBI. The patient is interested in participating in the study

A 34-year-old man, who has been convicted of robbery and sentenced to parole, is eligible for this study. He has access to a mobile phone and has been assigned a probation officer. The patient is fluent in spoken Swedish and has no additional interventions such as intensive supervision with electronic monitoring or in-patient care at a health and rehabilitation clinic. The patient is interested in participating in this study to help reduce his risk of recidivism and improve his chances of successful reintegration into society.

52 yo F diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer and underwent lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy. Though her treatment was successful, she was left with limited range of motion and pain in her affected arm. She has been experiencing difficulty performing daily activities and has been unable to return to her normal routine. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effect of domiciliary physiotherapy on upper limb function during the period of radiotherapy in women who have undergone surgical and radiation treatment for breast cancer. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Migraines - No history of neurological or orthopedic diseases that could impair the movements of the upper limbs.

A 65-year-old African American man with a history of hypertension and Type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with a decline in cognitive function over the past year. He reports difficulty remembering names, dates, and appointments. He also has trouble with everyday tasks such as paying bills, cooking, and cleaning. He has a history of a transient ischemic attack (TIA) 2 years ago. He is a former smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He has gained weight over the past year and reports a decrease in physical activity. His medications include lisinopril and metformin. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. He is married and has two adult children who live nearby. He reports that his wife has been helping him with some of his daily tasks. He is fluent in English and is able to use a smartphone. His MMSE score is 24.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who presents to a primary care outpatient center with a persistent cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing for the past week. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She reports no fever or chills, but has been feeling fatigued and has lost her appetite. She is a non-smoker and works in an office environment. Upon examination, the doctor notes rales and rhonchi in the lungs with decreased breath sounds in the lower lobes. The doctor diagnoses her with a lower respiratory tract infection and prescribes her antibiotics. She consents to participate in the Antibiotic Observatory for Respiratory Diseases study and allows the investigating doctor to collect her demographic data, medical history, and symptomatology. She completes a medication appropriateness index (MAI) score to evaluate the appropriateness of her antibiotic prescription.

A 2-week-old healthy term infant is brought in by their mother for enrollment in a clinical trial. The baby's mother reports a history of atopic disease in the family, including physician-diagnosed atopic dermatitis (AD), allergic rhinitis, and asthma. The baby is exclusively breastfed, and the mother intends to maintain breastfeeding for at least 12 weeks. The baby has not been admitted to the neonatal unit and has no baseline illness or condition that would introduce significant safety concerns. The mother is over 18 years old, the legal guardian of the infant, fluent in English, and willing to comply with the study protocol requirements. The infant has not consumed more than 100 mL of formula per day within the 48 hours prior to enrollment. The baby is a singleton and has no significant birth defects or complications that would create a safety concern or confound the study.

The patient is a 15 year old Chinese male with a history of hemophilia B. He has been previously treated with FIX replacement therapy and has a FIX activity level of less than 1%. He has no history of FIX inhibitor and has not been treated with immunomodulatory therapy in the past 30 days. He has no bleeding disorder in addition to hemophilia B and is not currently using primary FIX prophylaxis. He has not participated in any other investigational drug or device studies within the past 30 days and has no known hypersensitivity to hamster protein. He has no significant hepatic or renal impairment, with normal ALT and AST levels, bilirubin levels and serum creatinine levels. He has not undergone any recent surgeries and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing and able to follow the terms of the protocol and participate in study-related activities.

Premature male infant born at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 800g diagnosed with severe respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) shortly after birth requiring mechanical ventilation. The infant has no known congenital anomalies and has not had prenatal infections. The infant meets the eligibility criteria for the study and the parents have provided informed consent for participation.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who had an abnormal Pap smear showing ASC-US, ASC-H or LSIL. She has a confirmed HPV16 infection through the Aptima HPV 16 18/45 Genotype Assay. She has no history of HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection. Her body mass index is below 32 kg/m2. She has normal organ function parameters, including white blood cell count, lymphocyte number, absolute neutrophil count, platelets, hemoglobin, total bilirubin, AST, ALT and creatinine. She has had a colposcopic examination with mandatory ECC and cervical biopsy, which showed <CIN2 histologic diagnosis. She is not trying to conceive and agrees to use contraception or remain sexually abstinent through 6 months of the study. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and has signed an informed consent form. She has not had chemotherapy, radiation, biological cancer therapy or other investigational agents within 28 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She has not undergone cervical conization or LEEP procedure, or previous total hysterectomy due to cervical lesions at enrollment.

42-year-old male with a history of hypertension and obesity, scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient's weight is 120 kg, and he has a BMI of 36. The patient has no significant medical or surgical history other than his hypertension and obesity. The patient is not taking any medications and has no known drug allergies. The patient has no history of liver, heart, or kidney failure and does not have a pacemaker. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 10-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his mother after falling off his bike and injuring his right arm. The boy is in significant pain and holding his arm close to his body. The mother reports that he is unable to move his arm and is crying. The patient is otherwise healthy, and there is no significant past medical history. The mother is a 36-year-old woman who is worried about her son's injury and is anxious about the upcoming procedure. She speaks fluent English and has no history of mental illness. The patient is eligible for the study as he requires fracture reduction under conscious sedation by the emergency department attending physician, and he is able to understand basic spoken English. The mother is also eligible for the study as she is able to understand basic spoken English and does not present any exclusion criteria.

A 28-year-old healthy male, non-smoker, with a body weight of 67 kg and BMI of 22.5 kg/m^2 presents for a bioavailability study of candesartan cilexetil under fasting conditions. The patient has no known allergies or sensitivities to any medications or components thereof. He has no history of liver disease or gastrointestinal disease or surgical history that can affect the absorption of the investigational drug. The patient is not a regular alcohol consumer and has not used any tobacco or nicotine-containing products in the past 6 months. The patient has not participated in any clinical trial or received any investigational product within the last 90 days or five half-lives or twice the duration of the biological effect of the investigational product (whichever is longer). The patient has negative serum and urine hCG test results, indicating no current pregnancy. The patient has no current or chronic history of any medical conditions or abnormalities and has normal liver function tests and corrected QT interval. The patient has agreed to use one of the contraception methods listed in the protocol for an appropriate period of time prior to the start of dosing to minimize the risk of pregnancy. The patient has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of intense fear and anxiety in social situations. She feels constantly scrutinized and judged by others, leading to avoidance of social interactions. She has difficulty making friends and often feels isolated. She reports physical symptoms such as sweating, trembling, and heart palpitations during social situations. She has been diagnosed with social phobia according to DSM-IV criteria. She has no history of severe depression or suicidal behavior, addiction, or abuse. She is not currently undergoing any other psychological treatment. She is stable on medication for anxiety. She has access to a computer with internet connection and a printer. She is interested in participating in the study to help manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

A 35-year old woman was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) three years ago. She experiences difficulty with walking and balance, and has had one relapse in the past year. Her past medical history is significant for asthma and seasonal allergies. She lives with her husband and two children. She works part-time as a teacher's aide. The patient complains of stiffness and tightness in her legs, particularly in the calf muscles. She also has difficulty lifting her toes when walking, causing her to trip and stumble occasionally. She is currently taking interferon beta-1a to manage her MS symptoms. She is motivated to participate in the study to improve her walking ability and quality of life.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with coronary heart disease. He has been experiencing feelings of sadness and hopelessness for the past few weeks and has lost interest in activities he once enjoyed. He reports difficulty sleeping and has noticed a decrease in his appetite. The patient speaks both English and Spanish fluently. He scores a 12 on the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ9), indicating elevated depressive symptoms. He has no history of psychosis, schizophrenia, or bipolar disorder, and has not attempted suicide. The patient does not have a history of alcohol or substance abuse.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy who has been experiencing a fever for the past 24 hours. His parents noticed that he also has a cough and runny nose. They consulted with their family doctor who advised them to take their child to the pediatric emergency department at Strasbourg University Hospital. They have agreed to participate in the study. The boy has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medication. He is accompanied by both of his parents and they all speak French.

A 30 year old woman who works as a graphic designer and enjoys drinking coffee comes to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial. She has never been diagnosed with any neurological or psychiatric disorders and has no family history of alcoholism. She reports occasional social drinking but denies any drug use. She is not taking any prescription medications and is not a smoker. She is interested in the study and has read the informed consent form carefully. She is right-handed and meets all eligibility criteria. She consents to participate and is excited to learn more about how different drugs affect brain activity.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who recently suffered from an acute myocardial infarction. He has no history of drug abuse and is not pregnant. The patient has no other critical illness and has not previously undergone CABG or PCI. He is concerned about his health and is interested in participating in the study to reduce his risk of further coronary heart disease and death. The patient is well-groomed and appears to be in good physical health. He is motivated to make lifestyle changes and follow the multifactorial risk reduction plan as outlined in the study.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with primary Sjögren's syndrome a few years ago. She complains of a dry mouth condition, which is affecting her ability to speak and swallow. She has tried using oral comfort agents, but they have not provided much relief. She is otherwise healthy and does not smoke or consume alcohol. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Her past surgical history is significant for a hysterectomy, and she is currently taking medication for high blood pressure. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of daily administration of an oromucosal formulation of 552-02.

A 38-year-old woman visited the clinic for a routine gynecologic exam. She has been taking oral contraceptives with 30ʯg ethinyl estradiol (EE) plus 125ʯg levonorgestrel (LNG) for the past year and has been compliant with its use. She is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 25.4 kg/m2, and her vital signs are normal. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no known allergies to any medications. She has not used any drugs of abuse in the past 3 months and does not smoke or drink heavily. She is willing to use a barrier contraceptive method during the study and one month after the end of the study visit. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 55-year-old female patient diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis of the knee and scheduled for knee replacement surgery is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2 and has never smoked. She has not been regularly taking any NSAID, corticoid-steroids, DMARD, cytostatic, immune suppressive medicine or any other medication. The patient is physically active and able to perform exercise. She has not had any recent trauma to the knee, knee surgery or exposure to tracers. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help improve the understanding of cartilage development and function in relation to osteoarthritis prevention.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is pregnant and scheduled for a cesarean section delivery. She has no history of mental disorders and has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions such as hypertension, diabetes or cardiac diseases. She is in good general health and has had a healthy pregnancy with no complications. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to undergo either general or spinal anesthesia for the procedure. She will be monitored for early cognitive dysfunction in the postoperative period. The patient is expected to be cooperative and comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 30 year old woman who has been experiencing eczema for the past year. She has tried various topical treatments but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She has no other systemic illness and has not taken oral steroids in the past month. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to observe the safety and efficacy of Ganoderma tea on her eczema symptoms. She is willing to comply with the study protocol, which involves taking the tea twice a day initially, with the dosage increasing to three times a day within two weeks. She understands that she may need to use short-term steroids or other topical medication to relieve her symptoms during the control or intervention period.

A 14-year-old male patient with X-linked Chronic Granulomatous Disease (X-CGD) was referred to the clinic with a history of recurrent infections, including pneumonia, skin abscesses, and osteomyelitis. Despite being on prophylactic antibiotics, he has been hospitalized multiple times in the last 2 years. Blood tests showed significantly reduced biochemical activities of the NADPH-oxidase, confirming the molecular diagnosis of X-CGD. The patient has been on high doses of steroids for the last 6 months due to severe colitis. His parents are willing to participate in the study and have signed the informed consent. The patient's HLA typing is not matched with any available donor, and therefore bone marrow transplant is not an option. The patient is otherwise in good health, with no contraindications for leukapheresis or administration of conditioning medication.

A 64-year-old postmenopausal woman with a BMI of 28 kg/m^2 presents to the clinic with a desire to increase her physical activity levels to reduce her risk of breast cancer. She has a history of hypertension, well controlled with medication, and osteoarthritis of the knees. She is not currently enrolled in any weight management program and has not engaged in regular, planned walking for at least 30 minutes a day. She has access to a cell phone and is fluent in English. Her primary care physician has provided a letter stating that she is able to participate in a physical activity program that involves walking up to 10,000 steps per day.

Patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of poor oral hygiene and gingivitis. He has been experiencing bleeding gums and bad breath for the past few months. He has tried different toothbrushes and toothpaste but has failed to achieve significant improvement. The patient has a plaque score of 2.5 (Turesky Modification of the Quigley-Hein index) on his last dental visit. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy of using a 3D motion tracking toothbrush in dental plaque control. The patient does not have any gross dental caries or orthodontic appliances, and he is not medically compromised.

A 45-year old male presents with headaches, dizziness, and occasional seizures for the past few months. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He works as a sales representative and travels frequently. He is married with two children. His family has no history of brain tumors. The patient reports that his symptoms have been worsening over time, and he is seeking medical attention. A brain MRI reveals a 3 cm mass in the left frontal lobe consistent with a glioma. He is referred for surgery and is informed about the clinical trial for fluorescence-guided surgery for low- and high-grade gliomas. The patient is interested in participating and meets the eligibility criteria. He is randomized to the study drug group and takes the 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) before his surgery. During the surgery, the surgeon uses a special microscope fitted with a blue light that allows him to see the tumor margins more clearly. The patient undergoes a successful surgery and is followed up with MRI scans and NIHSS assessments. He will be monitored for overall survival and progression-free survival.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who lives in a rural community in a sub-Saharan African country. She has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and blood in her urine for several months. Her family has limited access to healthcare and cannot afford to pay for medical treatment. The patient has never been diagnosed with any serious medical conditions and has no history of hospitalization. She has not received any vaccinations or preventive health measures. She has not been tested for malaria or other infectious diseases. The patient and her family are willing to participate in the study and have provided written informed consent. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study, and the investigators plan to test her for Schistosoma haematobium infection and assess the effect of this neglected tropical disease on Plasmodium falciparum transmission in the area of co-endemicity. The investigators will also evaluate whether the patient's immune response to P. falciparum is impaired due to helminth infection and whether this leads to an increase in gametocyte carriage and transmission of the parasite to mosquitoes.

A 35 year old woman with a history of widespread pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances came to the clinic with a diagnosis of fibromyalgia. She has been experiencing these symptoms for at least 6 months with no significant improvement despite previous treatments. She is a full-time working mother of two and has limited time for self-care due to her busy schedule. She reported feeling frustrated and overwhelmed with managing her symptoms and is interested in exploring new self-management strategies. She has access to a computer and the internet at home and is willing to participate in a web-based program for symptom management.

This is a 42 year-old male with a diagnosis of Schizophrenia. He has been on antipsychotic medication for several years and is considered stable. He currently experiences persistent cognitive deficits that impact his daily functioning, including difficulty with attention and memory. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially improve his cognitive function. He does not have any significant medical issues or ECG abnormalities and has not donated blood in the past eight weeks. He is not currently being treated with Clozapine.

The patient is a 42 year old woman who has been experiencing urinary urgency and occasional incontinence for the past year. These symptoms have been impacting her quality of life, causing her to avoid social situations and feel embarrassed. She has tried behavioral modifications such as timed voiding and pelvic floor exercises, but has not seen significant improvement. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is sexually active and has noticed a decrease in sexual desire and satisfaction since developing these symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of Mirabegron on her overactive bladder symptoms and potential improvement in sexual function.

A 4-month-old male infant was diagnosed with Tetralogy of Fallot and was scheduled for corrective surgery. The infant has been experiencing episodes of cyanosis and shortness of breath. He is otherwise healthy, with no other significant medical history, and is on no medications. The surgery was planned, and the infant was admitted to the hospital the day before the surgery. The surgery was performed, and the infant was randomized to the experimental group. The surgery lasted 4 hours, and the infant was cooled down to 32°C. The infant was then placed on the temperature-regulating blanket and incrementally rewarmed. The infant received a single weight-based 15 mg/kg dose of intravenous Tylenol in the operating room. The infant remained stable, and EEG was performed for 48 hours to screen for seizures. The PI interpreted the EEG every 6-8 hours. The infant remained on the blanket at 36.5°C for another 12 hours. The blanket and esophageal temperature probe were then removed a total of 24 hours after the surgery was completed. The infant was transferred to the general floor for further observation and recovery.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with entropion and recommended for surgery. She is generally healthy and has no known medical conditions. She has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to anesthesia. Her parents have agreed to participate in the clinical trial and have given their informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who suffered a complete spinal cord injury at the level of T6 due to a motor vehicle accident two years ago. He has been experiencing severe bowel and bladder dysfunction, which has significantly impacted his quality of life. He currently uses clean intermittent catheterization and digital rectal stimulation to manage his bladder and bowel dysfunction, respectively. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effect of a surgically created somato-sensory reflex arch on bladder and bowel symptoms in spinal cord injury patients. He meets the inclusion criteria of the trial as he is above 18 years of age, has a motoric complete spinal cord injury at the level of T6, and has preserved hamstring reflex (L5). He is willing to participate in the study and has no contraindications such as respiratory dependence, malignancy in the urinary tract, urethral strictures, ileostomy or colostomy, radiation towards the area, or pregnancy (for men planning a pregnancy with their partner).

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who was playing on the playground when he fell from a height of about 5 feet and landed on his outstretched arm. He immediately felt severe pain and swelling in his right arm, and his parents took him to the emergency room. X-rays revealed a Gartland Type 3 supracondylar humeral fracture (SCHF). The orthopedic surgeon recommended surgery to fix the fracture. The patient has no known medical conditions or allergies and has never had surgery before. He is currently taking no medications. The patient's parents have agreed to participate in this clinical trial to compare pin configuration effects on early secondary displacement in the surgical treatment of pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures. They understand that their child will be randomly assigned to one of the five groups according to the top in configurations (crossed 1 lateral 1 medial, crossed 2 lateral 1 medial, crossed 1 lateral 2 medial, 2 lateral divergent, and 3 lateral divergent). The parents also understand that their child will be followed up for a year after the surgery to compare Bauman angle (BA), Humerocapital angle (HCA), Anterior humeral line (AHL), flexion range, extension range, and Carrying angle (CA) at preoperative, postoperative 1st-day, postoperative last control, and non-operated side.

42-year-old female with a 4-year history of Crohn's disease. The patient was diagnosed with CD in the colon and ileum based on imaging studies and endoscopic findings. The patient has been previously treated with a combination of prednisone and immunosuppressants, but failed to achieve remission. The patient has also received infliximab treatment, but had to discontinue due to an allergic reaction. Currently, the patient is experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. The CDAI score is 400. The patient has normal renal function and weighs 60 kg. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial involving the use of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) for the treatment of refractory Crohn's disease. The patient has no history of HIV, hepatitis, or any allergic reaction to contrast agents, cattle or pig products. The patient does not have a stricture or perforation type CD and has not received permanent colostomy. The patient has not used any biological preparation in the past 3 months and has not used prednisone > 20 mg/day within the past month. The patient does not have short bowel syndrome and does not require total parenteral nutrition. The patient's liver function is within normal range and they have not had any malignant tumors within the last 5 years. The patient does not have combined bacterial or viral enteritis, intestinal typicality thickening of the living, or tuberculosis. The patient has signed informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 42-year-old woman with a body mass index of 38 kg/m2 presents for an elective laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy surgery. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of chronic pain or drug addiction. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle, but has struggled with maintaining a healthy weight. She has never undergone any type of bariatric surgery before. She reports occasional back pain and difficulty sleeping due to her weight. She is excited about the surgery and hopes it will improve her quality of life. She has no known allergies to any medications.

A 7-year-old female with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) requiring central venous access for chemotherapy administration. The patient has a history of multiple hospitalizations and has previously undergone several attempts for central venous access, including placement of a tunneled central venous catheter (CVC) and peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC), both of which were complicated by infections. The patient's physician has recommended subclavian vein catheterization as the preferred method of central venous access.

A 42-year-old female presents with a BMI of 29.8 kg/m2 and a history of hypertension. She reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet that is high in processed and fast food. Her waist circumference is 93 cm, and her blood pressure is 135/90 mmHg. She has no history of diabetes or cardiovascular events. Her fasting glucose level is 110 mg/dL, and her triglyceride level is 160 mg/dL. Her HDL cholesterol is 48 mg/dL. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to study the effect of a combination of functional foods on gut microbiota in subjects with metabolic syndrome. The study includes a double-blind, parallel-arm, placebo-control design and involves dietary interventions for 2 months. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She is informed about the exclusion criteria, and none of them applies to her. She signs the informed consent and is enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who presents to the Emergency Department with a red, swollen, and painful area on her leg. She reports that the area has been gradually getting worse over the past few days and is now causing her significant discomfort. She denies any recent injuries, but reports that she has had cellulitis in the past. She is generally healthy and takes no medications. She has no known allergies to medications. Upon examination, there is a 10 cm area of erythema and edema on her lower leg, with associated warmth and tenderness to touch. Her vital signs are within normal limits. The attending physician diagnoses her with uncomplicated cellulitis and prescribes cephalexin. The physician also offers her the option to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of adding trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) to her treatment regimen. The patient agrees to participate and signs the informed consent form. She is randomized to receive either Bactrim or placebo in addition to cephalexin and agrees to attend all follow-up appointments.

A 54-year-old male non-smoker presented to the oncology clinic with complaints of persistent cough, chest pain and shortness of breath. His medical history revealed that he had been diagnosed with stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) six months ago, and had undergone chemotherapy with no significant improvement in his symptoms. He had unintentionally lost 8% of his body weight over the past 6 months and was experiencing anorexia. His BMI was 19 kg/m2 at the time of screening. He had no history of alcohol or illicit drug abuse. His ECOG performance status was 1. His laboratory results showed AST (SGOT) and ALT (SGPT) levels within normal range, and creatinine clearance >30 ml/minute. His blood pressure was well controlled with medication. He provided written informed consent to participate in the study and was randomized to receive anamorelin HCl 100 mg or placebo once daily for 24 weeks.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment and has a sedentary lifestyle, with a physical activity score of Dijon less than or equal to 20. She works as a freelance graphic designer and spends most of her day sitting in front of a computer. She has never been an active person and finds it challenging to engage in physical activity. She lives with her husband and two children, aged 9 and 12. She has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother and grandmother both being diagnosed with the disease in their 50s. She has been experiencing fatigue and weakness since beginning her chemotherapy treatment. She is motivated to improve her overall health and is interested in learning more about the benefits of physical activity, but feels unsure about how to get started. She is willing to participate in the study and hopes that it will provide her with the motivation and support she needs to become more active.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been struggling with alcohol use disorder for the past 10 years. He has tried to quit on his own, but has been unsuccessful. He has sought treatment at a local addiction treatment center and has been enrolled in Aware Recovery Care's In-Home Addiction Treatment program for the past 3 months. He has had multiple relapses in the past and is willing to use the Soberlink device to provide blood alcohol content (BAC) readings as a part of his routine treatment. He has no history of taking anti-alcohol/craving medications (Antabuse, Campral, Vivitrol) and is willing to discuss test results with his care team. He is an English speaker and reader and is willing to sign the Soberlink Client Agreement. He is currently unemployed, lives alone and has no children.

A 28-year-old Hispanic male was diagnosed with schizophrenia 4 years ago after experiencing auditory and visual hallucinations, delusions of persecution, and disorganized speech. He has been stabilized on Lurasidone for the past year and has not experienced any psychotic episodes during this time. However, he reports significant difficulty with memory, attention, and problem-solving, which has impacted his ability to maintain employment and manage daily tasks. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his cognitive functioning. He has a high school education and has worked in manual labor jobs since dropping out of college due to his illness. He lives with his parents who provide support but he is motivated to improve his independence. He has no history of substance abuse or dependence and is compliant with his medication regimen. He is fluent in English and has no hearing or visual impairment. He is willing to attend twice weekly sessions for cognitive remediation or active control sessions for the ~6 month duration of the cognitive remediation phase of the study.

A 63-year old retired teacher was diagnosed with endometrial cancer six months ago. She had a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and omentectomy. The pathology report indicated endometrioid adenocarcinoma, stage IIIC. The patient has completed six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She is married and has two adult children. The patient complains of persistent abdominal pain and bloating. She says that her energy level has decreased and she is having difficulty with daily activities. She denies any recent weight loss or changes in appetite. Her most recent CA-125 level was 150 U/mL. She is not on any other medications or supplements. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in clinical trials to explore other treatment options.

A 25-year-old female diagnosed with relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis and currently receiving treatment with Rebif. She has been using the Rebiject II injection device for the past 6 months and has received training on its use. She visits her MS nurse regularly for review and has been compliant with her medication regimen. She is able and willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent. She is not receiving any other disease modifying therapy and is able to self-inject.

A 27-year-old female working as a graphic designer in an advertising company comes to the clinic complaining of neck and back pain. She spends most of her workday sitting in front of a computer working on design projects. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past six months. She has tried different chairs and desks but still feels pain. She has no history of chronic illness or surgeries. She is not taking any medications. She exercises 3-4 times a week, mostly jogging and yoga. She has no known allergies. She is interested in participating in a study that investigates the effect of ergonomic workstation intervention on improving her knowledge, self-efficacy, and habit formation. She is willing to spend some time outside of work hours. She is familiar with using computers and is confident in her ability to learn new skills.

A 54-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of severe pneumonia. He has no history of chronic illness and does not smoke. He is married and has two children. He works as a construction worker. He has been on antibiotics for the past 12 hours. He is covered by medical insurance. Rectal screening revealed colonization with Enterobacteria. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing progressive weakness in his limbs for the past 6 months. He has difficulty walking and has noticed a decrease in grip strength. He has no significant medical history and does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has undergone electromyography (EMG) and has been diagnosed with neuropathy with anti-MAG antibody. He has been referred to the Nice University Hospital Pasteur Hospital 2 to participate in a clinical trial to assess the use of ultra-high frequency ultrasound in the diagnosis and monitoring of neuropathies. He will undergo an ultrasound study of the nerves using an ultra-high frequency ultrasound system, which will allow for the assessment of anatomical structures of the nerve, including size, structure, vascularization, and assessment of booklets. The ultrasound data will be compared with the data obtained from the EMG and clinical scores obtained using clinical rating scales. Patient A will be one of 10 patients with neuropathy with anti-MAG antibody included in the study, which also includes 10 patients with polyradiculoneuritis Inflammatory Demyelinating Chronicles (IPDC), 10 patients with Neuropathies Motrices in Multifocal Conduction Blocks (NMMBC), and 10 control subjects with no signs of neuropathy at the EMG examination. Patient A must be affiliated with a social security scheme, sign informed consent, and not have any risk factors associated with neuropathic disease.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been experiencing hip pain for several months. He has been diagnosed with a labral tear and femoroacetabular impingement, and has been scheduled for hip arthroscopic surgery. He has no history of other joint problems or surgeries.
