He is physically active and enjoys hiking and playing basketball. He currently works as a construction worker and is concerned about his ability to return to work quickly after surgery. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements for crutch use for either 2 or 4 weeks post-surgery. He has no other medical conditions or allergies.

25F presents to the clinic with complaints of itching and burning in the vaginal area. She reports a foul-smelling discharge and discomfort during urination. She denies any recent sexual activity, but is sexually active and uses condoms inconsistently. She has no known medical history and is not taking any medications. On physical examination, there is erythema and tenderness in the vulvar area and the vaginal discharge is noted to be malodorous. A wet mount assessment is performed and T. vaginalis is identified. She is diagnosed with trichomoniasis and is offered enrollment in a clinical trial testing the effectiveness and safety of a single, oral dose of Solosec® for the treatment of trichomoniasis. She agrees to participate in the study and meets the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 32-year-old female athlete who has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain during exercise. She has a history of exercise-induced asthma and has been using albuterol inhaler as needed. She has no known cardiac or pulmonary diseases and has not had any recent surgeries. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is currently taking birth control pills and has no known allergies. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the accuracy of cardiac output measurement during exercise.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease. He is scheduled to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting surgery due to severe blockages in his coronary arteries. He has never had any kidney problems in the past, but his doctor has informed him that the surgery carries a high risk of developing acute kidney injury (AKI). He is not currently experiencing any symptoms of sepsis and has not had any recent episodes of AKI. The patient has two functioning kidneys and is not scheduled for any nephrectomies.

A 40-year-old woman presents to the clinic for evaluation of her risk of gastric cancer. Her father was recently diagnosed with gastric cancer and she is concerned about her own risk. She reports no history of gastric symptoms, but does have a history of heartburn and occasional indigestion. She has no history of peptic ulcer disease or other gastrointestinal issues. She has never been tested for Helicobacter pylori infection. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol excessively. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of H. pylori eradication in reducing the risk of gastric cancer in family members of gastric cancer patients. She provides informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old Chinese woman with a BMI of 25.5 kg/m2 who has no history of serious clinical diseases. She is not currently taking any prescription, non-prescription medicine, Chinese herbal medicine or health products. She has not been vaccinated within the past 4 weeks and has no history of drug abuse, smoking, or alcoholism. She has no known allergies to monoclonal antibodies and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and understands the purpose, nature, methods, and possible adverse reactions of the trial. She has no abnormal vital signs or ECG results and has passed the physical examination, laboratory examination, and abdominal ultrasound examination.

A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast with a palpable lump measuring 3.2 cm. The ER/PR status was positive, and HER2 was negative. A biopsy of the axillary lymph node was negative for malignancy. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She is a former smoker, quit 10 years ago, and has a pack-year history of 10. She drinks alcohol socially, 2-3 drinks per week. Her BMI is 28. She is employed full-time as a librarian and lives with her husband. She reports no difficulty with activities of daily living or any limitations in mobility. She expresses concern about her cancer diagnosis and is willing to participate in any study that may improve her outcome.

50 yo woman with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a family history of coronary artery disease presented to the emergency department with chest pain. An ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3, and she was diagnosed with an acute myocardial infarction. The patient was taken to the catheterization lab for a coronary angiogram and intervention. During the procedure, the patient received Iopromide intra-arterially as a contrast agent. The patient experienced a mild allergic reaction, including hives and itching, which was treated with antihistamines and resolved quickly. The patient was discharged after a successful intervention and was scheduled for follow-up appointments with her cardiologist.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with precursor B-acute lymphoblastic leukemia. He is positive for the CD19 protein marker, which is found on the surface of B cells. The patient has no history of chemotherapy treatment for this disease (maximum 5 days of steroid treatment is allowed). He has a WHO (World Health Organization) performance status of 1, meaning he is able to carry out light work and normal activities with some difficulty. The patient is willing and capable of giving informed consent. He has no history of severe cardiovascular or pulmonary disease, neurological or psychiatric disease, or active malignancies. He is not known to be HIV-positive and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing and capable of using effective means of birth control during the trial.

A 35-year-old female, who is 5'4" and weighs 180 pounds, is interested in participating in a clinical trial related to weight loss. She has been struggling with weight loss for several years and has tried various diets and exercises without success. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. She is currently not taking any medications and has no known medical conditions. Her physical exam reveals a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, a pulse rate of 80 beats per minute, and a body mass index (BMI) of 31. She has no limitations in her daily activities, but she wants to lose weight to improve her overall health and quality of life. She is willing to follow a liquid formula diet and undergo testing of neuroendocrine, autonomic, and metabolic function as part of the clinical trial. She is not pregnant and is willing to stay in the hospital for a prolonged period to participate in this study.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with an aorto-iliac aneurysm with involvement of the iliac bifurcation. He has no other medical condition and takes no medications. He has been experiencing occasional discomfort in his lower abdomen and back pain. His physical examination reveals a pulsatile mass in his abdomen. The patient is well-groomed and well-nourished, with a normal gait and no difficulty in breathing. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to treat his aneurysm and is willing to undergo the implantation of the devices under study. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to sign the informed consent form. The patient has no contraindications for the study and meets the inclusion criteria.

Wang is a 28 year old Chinese male who works as a software engineer. He is 175 cm tall and weighs 70 kg, with a BMI of 22.9 kg/m^2. He has no history of any chronic illness or medical abnormality, and his physical examination and laboratory values are normal. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any drugs, prescription or non-prescription. He does not take any Chinese herbal medicines or food supplements. He has not participated in any drug clinical trials in the past 3 months nor had any blood donation or loss over 400 mL in the past 3 months. He has no family history of diabetes, thyroid cancer, or submandibular gland cancer, nor has he had a history of pancreatitis, cholelithiasis, drug allergy, or serious unconscious hypoglycemia. He is not a carrier of Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibodies, or HIV antibodies. He is willing to refrain from smoking, eating and/or drinking containing xanthine/caffeine, or strenuous exercise, or others that affect drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion within 2 days before the study drug administration. He is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control if he is a female subject of childbearing potential, is pregnant or planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding, or a male subject who does not use an acceptable method of birth control, within six months before randomization.

A 25-year-old non-smoking female with no significant medical history, normal renal function, and intact ovarian function is sought for a clinical trial. She should weigh between 18.0 and 32.0 kg and should have a body mass index (BMI) within that range. The participant must be willing to use Loestrin and must not have any clinically significant active or ongoing medical condition. She must have a negative QuantiFeron- TB Gold test at screening and have had a normal pap smear result within 3 years. The participant must not have a significant chronic medical illness or a history of relevant drug allergy to immunologic or related compounds. She should not have had any serious bacterial, fungal, or viral infection within 3 months or a history of recurrent or chronic infection or risk for TB. Additionally, she should not have a history of any medical condition related to the use of hormonal contraceptives and should have an average alcohol intake of fewer than 21 units per week.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of melanoma that was diagnosed 6 months ago. She underwent surgery for the melanoma and has since been receiving regular follow-up care to monitor her condition. Recent imaging studies have shown that the melanoma has metastasized to other parts of her body, making it unresectable (stage IV). She has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate is 80 beats per minute, and her BMI is 24. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications currently. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help researchers better understand melanoma and improve treatment options for people with the disease. She is willing to provide blood samples as part of the study and understands that there will be no extra clinic visits required.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has a history of exercise-induced asthma. He experiences shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness during and after exercise. He has been using a short-acting bronchodilator to manage his symptoms. He has not had any asthma exacerbations within the last 4 weeks and has a baseline FEV1 of 80% predicted. He is not currently taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the protective effect of a fixed drug combination of disodium cromoglycate plus reproterol compared to single component reproterol for exercise-induced asthma. He understands the study procedures and is willing to give informed consent.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, so there is no need for a patient description. It involves the heads of all psychosomatic, psychiatric and psychological consultation and liaison (C&L) services in acute care hospitals across all participating countries.

64-year-old male smoker with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with symptoms of cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. A chest x-ray was performed and showed a large mass in the left lung. A biopsy was obtained and confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The patient has previously undergone chemotherapy and immunotherapy for the treatment of NSCLC, but the disease has progressed, and he is not a candidate for surgery. He is currently on warfarin for a history of deep venous thrombosis. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and meets all of the inclusion criteria, including having measurable or evaluable disease, an ECOG performance score of 1, and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. However, the patient has a history of cerebrovascular accident and peripheral vascular disease with claudication on walking less than 1 block, which are exclusion criteria for the trial.

A 45-year-old female was diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and started on ponatinib therapy. She has no significant medical history and takes no other medications. She denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, or edema. Physical examination revealed no significant abnormalities. Baseline echocardiogram showed normal left ventricular systolic function with an ejection fraction of 60% and no significant valvular abnormalities. She has no history of pregnancy, lactation, or allergies to ultrasound contrast agents. She does not have any major medical illness involving the heart or vasculature such as coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, or dilated cardiomyopathy. She is hemodynamically stable and has no contraindications to the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a BMI of 33 kg/m2 who has struggled with weight gain for several years. He has a family history of obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. Despite multiple attempts to lose weight through diet and exercise, he has not been successful. He does not engage in structured exercise and reports consuming more than one cup of coffee per day. He has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders, and is not currently taking any antidepressants or antipsychotics. He has no significant co-morbidities, and has not had any abnormal findings on MRI or PET studies. He is willing to abstain from alcohol, physical exercise, and excessive caffeine for the 3 days prior to imaging studies. He is interested in participating in the study to better understand the relationship between dopamine receptors and insulin resistance, and hopes that the results of the study may help him with weight loss efforts.

A 35-year-old non-smoking female with no history of cardiovascular disease and ASA 1 is eligible for this clinical trial. She is scheduled for an elective surgery and has reported experiencing moderate to severe pain after previous surgeries. She is not pregnant or nursing and does not have asthma. She is willing to participate in this study to find an effective analgesic adjunct for postoperative pain management.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing joint pain and swelling, fatigue, and a butterfly rash on her face for the past 6 months. She has been to several doctors who have been unable to provide a diagnosis. She has a family history of autoimmune disorders, including lupus. Further evaluation shows that she meets at least 4 of the 11 items of the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria 1997 for SLE and her SELENA-SLEDAI score is 12. She has been on a stable treatment regimen consisting of hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and mycophenolate for the past 2 months. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with all required study evaluations and procedures. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of allergic reactions to human biological medicines.

The patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years. He has been on stable antiparkinsonian medications for the past 4 weeks. The patient complains of excessive daytime sleepiness, with an Epworth Scale Score of 14, which is affecting his daily activities and quality of life. The patient does not have any other known degenerative parkinsonian syndromes, shift work, chronic or occasional sleep deprivation, or circadian rhythm disorders. The patient does not have a severe depression indicated by (BDI>= 16)or at suicidal risk (BDI item G>0) or depression treated for less than 8 weeks. The patient does not have a cognitive impairment. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with melanoma on his left arm. He has already undergone a skin biopsy and is awaiting further treatment. He does not have any other significant medical history and is generally healthy. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He has fair skin and has had a few sunburns in the past. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance research on non-invasive skin testing. His skin is free of ulceration or any other infectious diseases.

A 50-year-old man with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of a non-invasive wellness device called the Gentle Jogger®. He has been diagnosed with diabetes for the last 10 years and is currently on oral diabetic medications. He is relatively sedentary and spends most of his day sitting due to his job as a computer programmer. He has noticed that his blood sugar levels are not well controlled despite taking his medications and following a diabetic diet. He is interested in trying the Gentle Jogger® to see if it can help improve his glycemic control and increase his muscle strength and endurance. He is able to provide informed consent and is within the age range of 25-80 years old.

As this is an observational study, patient descriptions are not applicable. The study utilizes endometrial biopsy samples collected from subjects that participated in a previous clinical trial. The inclusion and exclusion criteria for this study are related to the previous trial and the quality of the biopsy samples collected.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who smokes two packs of cigarettes a day for the last 30 years. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and cough with sputum production for the past few months. He has not sought medical attention for these symptoms yet. He has no history of respiratory diseases or allergies. He is generally healthy and takes no medications. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to detect chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in high-risk patients attending primary care centers. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old man diagnosed with colorectal cancer and scheduled for surgery in two weeks. He has been feeling anxious and depressed since his diagnosis and is looking for ways to manage his stress. He has a primary caregiver, his wife, who is also feeling overwhelmed and stressed about his diagnosis and upcoming surgery. The patient has no history of mental disorders, alcohol or substance abuse, and has not participated in any other clinical trials. He is willing and able to complete all assessments related to the study.

An 68 year old woman presents to the hospital for a scheduled surgery to remove a benign tumor in her abdomen. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She is alert and oriented, and able to communicate fluently in Thai. Her visual and auditory faculties are intact, and she has given informed consent to participate in the study. She has an ASA physical status of 2. She is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV within the past 5 years. He has been receiving ART for the past year and has experienced depressive symptoms and high levels of stress. He has also reported occasional substance use. He lives in a rural area in Nepal and has limited access to healthcare services. He has not enrolled in a community home-based care program before and is open to receiving psychosocial support and basic healthcare services at his home. He is willing to participate in an intervention study to assess the impact of community home-based care on his mental health, substance use, and ART adherence.

The patient is a 9-year-old female who was involved in a car accident with her family three months ago. Since then, she has been experiencing nightmares, flashbacks, and avoidance behaviors related to the accident. Her symptoms have been affecting her daily life and causing her distress. She has been diagnosed with Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) by a qualified clinician and scores ≥35 on the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for Children and Adolescents (CAPS-CA) total symptom severity score. She has at least one symptom per PTSD cluster related to the index trauma according to DSM IV diagnostic criteria. She lives within a reasonable distance (maximum 1 hour of travel) to the treatment center and has the cooperation of at least one non-offending primary caregiver. She does not have a history of psychosis or acute suicidality and has not started or changed psychopharmacological medication in the past 6 weeks. She is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial comparing the effectiveness of Trauma-Focused Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT) with a wait-list condition.

The patient is a 68-year-old male retiree who has been using hearing aids for the past 5 years. He has moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss and has difficulty following conversations in noisy environments. He lives with his wife in a quiet suburban community and enjoys playing golf with friends. He is willing to participate in the study and travel to study appointments. He is in good overall health and takes medication for high blood pressure. He is excited to try new hearing aids that may improve his ability to hear in challenging listening situations.

The patient is a 25-year-old Thai transgender woman who is sexually active with men. She has tested negative for HIV in the past and is interested in exploring options for HIV prevention. She is able to read and write effectively in Thai language and is willing to comply with study requirements. She has no physical or mental conditions that may complicate interpretation of study outcome data. She has a creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min and a negative urine protein result. The patient is available to return for study visits and is willing to provide reachable contact numbers and address. She is not currently participating in any interventional HIV research.

A 60-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with primary open angle glaucoma and has been on topical hypotensive medications for over a year. However, his glaucoma is not adequately controlled with these medications. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking antihypertensive medication to manage it. He has never had any ocular surgeries or treatments before. He wears glasses for reading and driving. He has no known allergies to any medications or foods. He is a retired engineer and spends his time reading and watching TV. His vision is otherwise good and he is able to perform his daily activities without difficulty. He has not experienced any adverse events related to his glaucoma medications.

A 57-year-old male presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of weakness on the right side of his body, difficulty speaking, and confusion. His wife reported that the symptoms started only 2 hours ago. The patient has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia and is currently taking medications for both. He has no history of smoking, alcohol consumption, or drug use. The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time, but his speech is slurred, and he has mild facial droop. His blood pressure is 160/95 mmHg, and his heart rate is 80 bpm. The patient undergoes a non-contrast CT scan, which shows an acute ischemic stroke in the left middle cerebral artery territory. The National Institute of Health Stroke Scale score is 12. The patient fulfills all inclusion and exclusion criteria for the clinical trial involving the administration of allogenic mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes. He consents to participate in the trial and is randomized to receive the exosome treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has undergone a mastectomy due to breast cancer. She is currently cancer-free and has been cleared by her oncologist to undergo breast reconstruction using silicone-filled breast implants. She has no history of autoimmune diseases or any infection at the time of enrollment. The patient has adequate tissue available to cover the implants and saline-filled implants are not an appropriate choice for her. She is committed to following all study requirements, including agreeing to all follow-up visits and accepting the risks involved with the procedure. The patient has a supportive network of family and friends who will help her with the recovery process. She has realistic expectations about the outcomes of the procedure and is willing to undergo further surgery if medically required.

The patient is a 63-year-old man who has been experiencing blood in his urine and frequent urination. He also reports pain or discomfort during urination. He has no significant past medical history and is not on any medication. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a family history of prostate cancer, but no history of bladder cancer. He underwent a cystoscopy and a biopsy that confirmed muscle-invasive bladder cancer. He has completed a maximal transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) and is now eligible for the trial. His performance status is good (ECOG 0). His laboratory results show an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1900/mm^3, platelets (PLT) of 110,000/mm^3, total bilirubin of 1.1 upper limit of normal (ULN), aspartate

A 52-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 5 years. He has been taking metformin (2000 mg/day) for the past 6 months but has not achieved adequate glycemic control. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² and a waist circumference of 105 cm. He has a sedentary lifestyle and consumes a high-calorie diet with frequent alcohol intake. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or other significant medical conditions. He is willing to use acceptable contraception to prevent pregnancy during the study and for 21 days after the last dose of study drug.

80F retired teacher with a history of depression and anxiety for the past 10 years. She has been treated with various antidepressant medications and psychotherapy in the past and is currently on sertraline 100mg daily for the past 6 months. She has been experiencing worsening symptoms of depression and anxiety including feelings of hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, and social withdrawal. She has difficulty sleeping and has lost weight unintentionally. She was referred to the VA Mental Health Clinic for evaluation and treatment. Upon evaluation, she was diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID). She was approached by the research team about participating in a study that evaluates the effectiveness of telepsychology for treating depression in elderly veterans. She was provided information about the study and agreed to participate. She was randomized to the telepsychology group and will receive care in her own home via videophone contact with a therapist at the Charleston VA Medical Center. She will receive treatment over an 8-week period and will be followed up for an additional 12 months to ascertain longer-term effects of treatment on three outcome domains: clinical outcomes, process outcomes, and cost-effectiveness. She is looking forward to participating in the study and hopes that the new mode of service delivery will help her manage her depression symptoms.

This is a 29 year old male with a BMI of 26.5 kg/m2 who is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of NnEx ingestion in patients with overweight or obesity. He has no history of using antidiabetic medication and has no known liver, kidney, or heart disease. He does not have any food allergies and consumes less than 2 L of tea daily. He is willing and able to follow the instructions given during the study.

A 44-year old female was diagnosed with stage 3a chronic kidney disease 3 years ago. She has a medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been on Metformin and Lisinopril for the past 5 years. She is married and has two children. She works as a full-time accountant. Her current symptoms include occasional headaches, fatigue, and mild edema in her ankles. She otherwise feels well and is able to perform her daily activities without any difficulty. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy female with a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2 and a total body weight of 60 kg. She has no history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, or neurologic diseases. She is not allergic to any medications, but reports seasonal allergies that are asymptomatic at the time of screening. She is willing to participate in the trial and provide informed consent.

A 25-year-old male who smokes both cannabis and tobacco cigarettes is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial. He has been smoking cannabis for the past 5 years, and tobacco cigarettes for the past 7 years. He reports that he smokes approximately one pack of cigarettes per day and uses cannabis several times per week. He has attempted to quit smoking cigarettes multiple times in the past, but has been unsuccessful. He is in good physical health and has no significant medical or psychiatric history. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. He is interested in participating in the study to try to quit smoking cigarettes and reduce his cannabis use.

7-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Niemann-Pick disease Type C1 (NPC-1) with two NPC-1 mutations on genotyping and a NIH NPC Severity Score <30. The patient experiences progressive neurological symptoms, including ataxia and saccadic eye movements. The patient has not received cyclodextrin therapy in the past and does not currently take any cholesterol-lowering agents such as statins, fibrates, or ezetimibe. The patient's renal function is normal, but the patient has a Karnofsky score of 35 due to the neurological symptoms. The patient's parents have been informed about the study and are willing to provide written, informed consent. The patient is not currently involved in any other interventional clinical trials and is not breastfeeding.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) at the age of 6. She underwent chemotherapy treatment for 2 years and has been in remission for 4 years. She complains of occasional chest pain and shortness of breath during exercise. She has a family history of heart disease, with her mother having had a heart attack at the age of 45. She is otherwise healthy, with no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help researchers understand the long-term effects of cancer treatment on cardiovascular health.

A 42-year-old female diagnosed with bipolar disorder type II presents with recurrent depressive episodes, which have been resistant to multiple pharmacological treatments over the past year. She has a history of multiple suicide attempts and hospitalizations. The patient's family history is significant for bipolar disorder in her mother and grandmother. The patient is currently not taking any psychotropics and has not taken lithium in the past 6 months. She is able to give voluntary informed consent and satisfies the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient has no metallic implants or other contraindications to MRI.

A couple gave birth to a healthy baby boy at the University of Virginia Medical Center. They are first-time parents and are looking forward to raising their child in the best possible way. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help them better understand the impact of bathing practices on their baby's skin health. The baby was born at term, and the mother is over 18 years of age and capable of providing informed consent. They do not have any other medical conditions that would prevent them from participating in the study. The family speaks English and is willing to comply with study procedures. They are excited to contribute to research that could improve the health of newborns in the future.

A 45-year-old male patient presented with a history of hypertension, which has been well controlled with medication for the last 4 years. He also complains of occasional lower back pain, but it is not severe and can be managed with over-the-counter painkillers. His urine tests have shown proteinuria of 1.2 g/day for the last 3 months despite treatment with an ACE inhibitor. His estimated glomerular filtration rate is 50 ml/min/1.73m2. His serum calcium level is within normal range. He has no history of malignancy, systemic infection, or severe coexisting disease. He is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 2 years. He is willing to give written consent and comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 35 year-old HIV-positive male who has been on a Saquinavir-based HAART regimen for the past 6 months. He has been adherent to his medication and has achieved an undetectable viral load for the last 3 months. He has a history of intravenous drug use but has been clean for the past year. He is a current smoker, smoking approximately 1 pack per day. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would interfere with drug absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion. He is willing to provide written informed consent and is able to understand the nature and extent of the study and the procedures required.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been struggling with alcohol addiction for the past five years. She has a history of childhood sexual abuse and has been diagnosed with PTSD. She experiences flashbacks, nightmares, and hypervigilance on a daily basis. She has tried to quit drinking on her own but has been unsuccessful. She is currently seeking treatment at an outpatient clinic and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She is fluent in English and is not currently taking any medications for her PTSD symptoms. She is motivated to get better and is committed to attending therapy sessions regularly.

The patient is a 10-year-old male who sustained a laceration on his right forearm while playing outside. The wound is approximately 3 cm long and 1 cm deep, with clean edges. The patient was brought to the Pediatric Emergency Department of the Geneva's University Hospital within 2 hours of the injury. The patient has no known medical history and is not taking any medications. Upon examination, the wound is determined to require suturing. The patient and his parent have consented to participate in the study and have been randomized to receive either absorbable or non-absorbable suture material. The size of the thread used is 4-0. The first follow-up appointment is scheduled for 7-10 days after the suturing. The patient is deemed eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis two years ago. She has been experiencing recurrent abdominal pain, blood-streaked stool, and diarrhea for the past six months. She has been on a full dose of 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) for four weeks, but her clinical symptoms have not improved. Endoscopy showed Mayo endoscopic score ≥2, and complete Mayo score ranged from 4 to 10, indicating mild-moderate activity. She is in good general health and has no history of severe allergies, HIV/AIDS, or any other immunodeficiency. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45 year old male who presented to the ED with complaints of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. He reported using multiple medications, including over-the-counter pain relievers and prescription medications for hypertension and high cholesterol. He is a smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He works as a construction worker and has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 days. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol for which he is currently taking medication. He is divorced and lives alone. He speaks fluent English and has no known allergies. He has never participated in a clinical trial before.

A 45-year-old non-smoking female who has no history of cardiovascular disease, psychiatric disorders or any other chronic illnesses presents for a clinical trial investigating the effects of beta-blockers and aspirin on hemostasis and endothelial function after acute mental stress. She has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She reports to drink only one cup of brewed coffee per day and no more than one glass of wine per week. She speaks Swiss-German as her native language. She is willing to discontinue any regular medication, including aspirin, for the duration of the study. She will be randomized to receive either placebo, inderal, aspirin, or a combination of inderal and aspirin for five days prior to the acute mental stress test. She understands and agrees to the study protocol and procedures and is willing to attend all scheduled visits.

A 35-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident and was diagnosed with a concussion/mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) by the ER physician. He reports difficulty with memory, difficulty completing tasks quickly, and a slower ability to multitask. He also reports struggling with communication, both verbally and nonverbally. He speaks English as his primary language and has no prior history of TBI requiring hospitalization or rehabilitation. He has no known neurological or psychological diagnoses that would prevent the completion of the screening measures. He does not live in Flagstaff, AZ or the surrounding area, but is willing to travel for follow-up screening and therapy. He wears reading glasses to correct his vision.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male who is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He has a BMI of 22 kg/m^2 and has no significant medical history. He has never participated in a clinical trial before and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study. He is sexually active but has undergone surgical sterilization. He is willing to use two different forms of effective contraception, including a barrier method, for the duration of the trial and for 3 months following the last dose of trial medication. His screening visit shows normal medical history, physical examination including 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), vital signs, and blood and urinary laboratory assessments. He does not have a history of or presence of cancer, diabetes, or any clinically significant cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, endocrinological, haematological, dermatological, venereal, neurological, psychiatric diseases or other major disorders that might have an impact on the current trial, as judged by the investigator. The patient does not have hepatitis or is not a carrier of the Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) or Hepatitis C antibodies, and has a negative result to the test for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) antibodies. His amylase and lipase values are within normal range.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hypertension and is currently taking medication to control his blood pressure. He is a moderate drinker who consumes approximately 2-3 drinks per day, which is above the recommended limit for alcohol consumption. He is interested in participating in a study that aims to evaluate the long-term effect of reducing alcohol intake on blood pressure levels. The patient has no other significant medical history and is willing to commit to the cognitive-behavioral program aimed at reducing his alcohol intake. The patient is willing to undergo echocardiograms and provide biochemical markers to validate changes in his alcohol consumption. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study with a diastolic blood pressure of 80-89 mm Hg and an alcohol intake of 21 drinks or more per week. The patient is motivated to improve his health and is willing to participate in the trial to potentially benefit himself and others.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent cough and shortness of breath. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. She received chemotherapy as the first-line treatment but unfortunately, the disease progressed after completing the treatment. The patient is now eligible to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of a sequential treatment of erlotinib and docetaxel. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, and adequate hematological, liver, and renal function. She has no contraindications for the use of erlotinib or docetaxel. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is accessible for follow-up. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other drugs under investigation. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old African American woman who has a family history of cardiovascular disease. She is concerned about her health and wants to take preventative measures. She is not currently taking any vitamins or supplements but is willing to participate in the study. She has no significant medical history or current health issues. Her blood pressure and cholesterol levels are normal. She has never smoked and does not drink alcohol. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She is interested in taking vitamin E and C to potentially slow the progression of common carotid artery plaque build-up. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all follow-up appointments.

A 75 yo F with a history of sarcopenia, complaining of weakness and difficulty performing daily activities such as dressing and walking. She is postmenopausal and is able to follow a walking program. She does not have any significant health issues or conditions that would prevent her from completing the study per protocol. She is willing and able to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures, and has provided signed informed consent. She is not currently participating in resistance training more than 3 times per week and regular exercise consisting of an average of 30 minutes per day or more of at least moderate physical activity. She does not have any respiratory disease that requires oxygen treatment, cancer requiring treatment currently or in the past 3 years (except primary nonmelanoma skin cancer or in situ cervical cancer), neurological conditions that are causing impaired muscle function or mobility, certain cardiovascular conditions, or uncontrolled diabetes.

This is a 62-year-old female with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and heart failure. She has been on optimal medical therapy for the past 6 months, but her symptoms have not significantly improved. She has a pacemaker implanted with a right ventricular mid-septal lead, but her QRS duration on EKG is >120 msec due to right bundle branch block. She has a normal sinus rhythm and a PR interval <250 msec. The cardiologist has turned off her LV lead pacing function for the past 3 months due to lead malfunction. She is interested in participating in the SPARK trial to potentially improve her heart function, symptoms, and quality of life.

A 40-year-old female with a history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) for the past 5 years. She has tried various diets and medications but has not experienced significant relief from her symptoms. She experiences bloating, abdominal pain, and bouts of diarrhea and constipation. Her symptoms significantly affect her daily life and work. She is interested in participating in a group therapy program that could help her better manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She has no history of severe psychiatric conditions and is willing and able to participate in group therapy.

A 6-year-old child with short bowel syndrome is experiencing difficulty digesting sugars and is dependent on parenteral nutrition to meet at least 50% of their fluid and caloric needs. The child is currently on a diet that contains sucrose but is experiencing symptoms such as abdominal distension, pain, vomiting, and diarrhea. The child's parents are willing to enroll their child in a clinical trial that aims to improve sucrose digestion through the administration of exogenous sucrase. The child has not received IV antibiotics for a confirmed bout of bacteremia, and is receiving enteral nutrition. The child is otherwise in good health and able to provide informed consent.

A 35-year-old female office worker presenting with mechanical neck pain for the last 6 weeks. Pain is described as dull and achy, radiating to the right shoulder and occasionally to the right arm. No numbness, tingling, or weakness reported. Pain intensity rated 6/10 on the Numerical Pain Rating Scale. No history of trauma or surgery in the cervical spine. No signs of cervical radiculopathy. Physical examination revealed palpable pain on active trigger points in the upper trapezius muscle. No signs of serious pathology or vascular syndromes. No history of inflammatory disorders or infections. Willing to participate in the study and meet the age criteria (18-50 years).

A 3-year-old male with chronic kidney disease and secondary hyperparathyroidism presents with elevated plasma iPTH levels. The patient has not received any cinacalcet therapy for at least 30 days prior to the start of dosing. The patient's corrected calcium levels are ≥ 8.8 (2.2 mmol/L) and serum phosphorus levels are within the normal range. The patient weighs 10 kg at the time of screening. The patient has no history of congenital long QT syndrome, second or third degree heart block, ventricular tachyarrhythmias or other conditions associated with prolonged QT interval. The corrected QT interval (QTc) is within normal limits. The patient is not taking grapefruit juice, herbal medications or potent CYP 3A4 inhibitors. No concomitant medications that may prolong the QTc interval are being taken. The patient is eligible for the study.

A 35-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a large, painful abscess on her left thigh. She has a history of diabetes and is currently on insulin therapy. Upon examination, there is a 10 cm area of erythema with central fluctuance and tenderness. The patient is febrile with a temperature of 38.5°C and has a white blood cell count of 15,000/mm^3. A culture of the abscess is obtained, which grows methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). The patient is admitted to the hospital for intravenous antibiotic therapy and surgical drainage of the abscess. She is approached for enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of GSK2140944 in the treatment of Gram-positive acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. She provides written, dated, informed consent and is willing and able to comply with the study protocol.

A 40-year-old healthy woman with a BMI of 24 and a body fat percentage of 25% is interested in participating in a clinical trial on the effects of protein ingestion and exercise training on muscular performance. She engages in structured physical activity for more than 30 minutes, 4 days a week, and has been weight stable for the past 6 months. She has no history of cardiovascular or metabolic diseases and has never smoked. She has no orthopedic conditions that would limit her participation in exercise training. She is not pregnant and has no allergies to milk products. She is excited to participate in this study to improve her muscular strength and performance, and is willing to follow a meal plan and participate in a program of progressive exercise training for 12 weeks.

A 52-year-old man is admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on medication for both conditions. He was intubated on admission and is being mechanically ventilated. The size of the endotracheal tube is 8mm. The patient's SpO2 is currently at 95% on a FiO2 of 0.6. The attending physician has requested a diagnostic bronchoscopy to assess the extent of lung damage. The patient is conscious and able to follow commands. He has no history of pneumothorax or acute cardiovascular disease. His blood pressure is stable and he is not on any inotropic support. He has no history of cerebrovascular disease or any other condition that requires stable blood pressure and saturation.

35-year-old male with a history of asthma diagnosed by a healthcare provider. He experiences symptoms such as wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, particularly during seasonal changes and when exposed to allergens. His forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) is greater than 1.0 liter, and his fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) level is greater than 50 ppb. He has not been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or bronchiectasis. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide sputum samples for biomarker testing.

A 54-year-old man was diagnosed with colon cancer 3 years ago. He underwent surgery and received standard chemotherapy, but the cancer has come back and spread to his liver and lungs. He has been receiving palliative radiation therapy to control symptoms of pain and dyspnea. He has no other significant medical history, and he is a non-smoker. He reports feeling tired and having difficulty with his daily activities. He has lost approximately 10 pounds in the last month. Laboratory findings are remarkable for mild anemia and elevated liver enzymes. A CT scan confirms multiple liver and lung metastases. The patient and his family are interested in further treatment options and are willing to participate in a clinical trial.

An 11-year-old female presents to the clinic with a history of migraine headaches for the past year. She reports experiencing an average of 8 migraine days per month, accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. The headaches typically last for a few hours and respond partially to ibuprofen. She has no known triggers for her migraines. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant past medical history. Her parents report that she has been compliant in completing the eDiary for the past 3 months and they have noticed a significant impact on her quality of life due to her migraines. They are interested in exploring potential preventive treatments for her migraines and are willing to participate in a clinical trial. The patient is developmentally appropriate to provide formal assent and her parents have provided written informed consent for her participation. She is not currently taking any medications for migraine prevention.

A 14-year-old girl presented to the clinic with headaches, nausea, and blurred vision. She had a history of delayed growth and was found to have a craniopharyngioma brain tumor after a CT scan and MRI. The tumor was partially removed during surgery, leaving behind some residual tumor. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial of intensity-modulated proton therapy for incompletely resected craniopharyngioma. She meets the inclusion criteria of being diagnosed with craniopharyngioma, being between 0-21 years of age, and not having prior history of fractionated radiation therapy or treatment with intracystic P-32 or intracystic bleomycin. She is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that this new form of radiation therapy will effectively treat her tumor and reduce side effects compared to traditional forms of radiation therapy.

The patient is a 53-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of ARDS. He was previously healthy with no significant medical history. He developed respiratory distress and was intubated in the emergency department. He has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit 5 years ago. He has a BMI of 28 and is currently on mechanical ventilation. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 92% on 100% FiO2. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. His physical exam is significant for bilateral crackles on lung auscultation. Chest x-ray shows bilateral infiltrates consistent with ARDS. He has no contraindications for nasogastric tube placement and is willing to participate in the study. He has provided informed consent and is willing to undergo the esophageal pressure measurement and diaphragm ultrasound.

A 25-year-old woman who is HIV positive and has been on a stable regimen of atazanavir and ritonavir for the past few months comes to the clinic for a contraception consultation. She has been sexually active with her partner and is looking for an effective birth control method. She is interested in taking the progestin-only pill (POP) as it does not contain estrogen, which she has been advised to avoid due to her HIV medications. She is currently not taking any other medications and has no history of ovarian dysfunction or irregular periods. She has a CD4+ cell count of 350 cells/mm3 and is in good overall health with a BMI of 25 kg/m^2. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of atazanavir and ritonavir on the pharmacokinetics of oral norethindrone contraception.

A 25-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in a study investigating the adhesion of new adhesives to the skin. She has intact skin on the area to be used in the investigation and is not currently receiving or has received radio- and/or chemotherapy in the past 2 months. She has not received topical steroid treatment in the abdominal skin area or systemic steroid (tablet/injection) treatment in the past months. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and does not have any dermatological problems in the abdominal area as assessed by the investigator. She has given written informed consent and is at least 18 years of age with full legal capacity.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) presenting with visual impairment and macular edema in the right eye. His best corrected visual acuity in the affected eye is approximately 20/60. He has not received any intra-vitreal anti-VEGF injections or pan-retinal laser photocoagulation in the past 3 months. He has not been using any topical ocular or systemic corticosteroids for the past 30 consecutive days. He has not received any intraocular or periocular corticosteroid injections in the past 3 months. He does not have iris neovascularization or neo-vascular glaucoma. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of ranibizumab and combination of ranibizumab and triamcinolone for the treatment of macular edema secondary to CRVO.

A 35-year-old Chinese man who has been smoking a pack of cigarettes per day for the last 10 years is seeking help to quit smoking. He is married with no children and works as an accountant. He has a history of high blood pressure, which is well-controlled with medication. He has also been diagnosed with erectile dysfunction for the past year and has been taking medication for this condition. He is interested in participating in a smoking cessation program that includes counseling and nicotine replacement therapy. He is willing to use NRT and is committed to quitting smoking within the next 7 days. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. He exercises regularly and does not have any other underlying health conditions that would contraindicate the use of NRT. He is willing to sign an informed consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year old man who recently experienced a transient ischemic attack (TIA) and has been diagnosed with carotid artery atherosclerosis. He does not have any other medical conditions and is currently taking medication to manage his blood pressure. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is interested in participating in the VISION study. He does not have any significant renal impairment or history of contrast nephropathy. He has not been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation and is able to lie flat during scanning. The patient is not a woman of childbearing potential. The patient has not had a hemorrhagic stroke within the past 3 months and does not have total occlusion of a culprit carotid artery. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the VISION study and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has a visual acuity impairment caused by macular edema in his left eye. He has been on stable medication for his diabetes for the past three months. The patient has not received any laser photocoagulation treatment in his left eye for the last three months, and he has no history of intraocular surgery in his left eye within the past three months. The patient's blood pressure is within the normal range.

65-year-old male with a history of primary open-angle glaucoma diagnosed 10 years ago, with persistent elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) despite being on maximum tolerated medical therapy. He has had progressive visual field loss, with a mean deviation of -9 dB in the right eye and -10 dB in the left eye. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes, and he has no history of cataracts or refractive error. He has previously participated in the Assessment of Ability Related to Vision (AARV) study, where his performance-based measure score was 35, despite having a midrange visual field score. He has no history of neurological disease or cognitive deficits, and his mini-mental status examination score is 28. He is not on any neuroprotective agents. He is a retired accountant, married with two children, and lives an active lifestyle with regular exercise and a healthy diet. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo T-1 weighted MRI brain scan and AARV testing.

A 45-year-old female with a diagnosis of simple stress urinary incontinence is being recruited for a clinical trial of electroacupuncture (EA) for this condition. She is experiencing involuntary urine leakage during physical activities such as coughing, laughing, or sneezing. The patient is interested in participating in the study after being informed of the potential benefits of EA treatment. She has not undergone any previous surgery for urinary incontinence or pelvic floor operations. Her edeoptosis is less than degree 2, and she does not have any symptomatic urinary tract infections. Her RUV and Qmax are within the acceptable range. She is able to walk, climb stairs, and run without constraint. The patient has not been continuously treated for urinary incontinence or bladder function, and does not have any serious cardiovascular, cerebral, liver, kidney, or psychiatric diseases, diabetes, MSA, injury of cauda equine or myeleterosis. She is not currently pregnant or lactating, and does not have a cardiac pacemaker, metal allergy, or severe needle phobia. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and signs the informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 40-year-old male of Asian ethnicity who presented with a history of cough, fever, and hemoptysis for the past 4 weeks. There is also a history of joint pain and swelling in the wrists, ankles, and knees. The patient has lost 3 kg of weight in the past month. The chest X-ray showed multiple nodules in both lungs. The renal function tests were within normal range. The anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) test was positive, and the biopsy of lung nodules showed granulomatous inflammation. The patient was diagnosed with Wegener's granulomatosis. The patient has no history of any chronic medical illnesses or allergies. The patient has not received any immunosuppressive therapy in the past. The vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mm Hg, a heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute. The patient has no contraindications to corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 13 yo F with a diagnosis of asthma for the past 5 years. She experiences recurrent episodes of wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, which affects her daily activities including school attendance. The symptoms are usually well controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and short-acting beta-agonists. She has not been hospitalized for asthma exacerbation in the past year. She has regular follow-up visits with her pediatric pulmonologist at the Department of Pediatrics and Pediatric Health Care Center of the University of Szeged. The patient and her parents are open to participate in the telespirometric measurements at home for a period of 12 months, as recommended by her pulmonologist. They understand that the remote monitoring of her lung function will help predict the occurrence of asthma exacerbations, and may lead to a modification of her treatment plan. They have signed the informed consent and are willing to come for personal visits every three months.

The patient is a 64-year-old male who presents with a persistent cough and shortness of breath. He reports a history of smoking for 45 years and has quit for 2 years. The patient's chest X-ray showed enlarged intrathoracic lymph nodes, and a CT scan was performed to further evaluate the lymphadenopathy. The CT scan reveals multiple enlarged mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes with a short diameter more than 1 cm. The patient is referred for EBUS-TBNA to obtain a pathological diagnosis. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. The patient is compliant with his medications and reports no adverse effects. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent. The patient has no contraindications for EBUS-TBNA and is considered a suitable candidate for the study.

A 40-year-old woman presents to her dermatologist with a circular rash on her thigh that has been gradually expanding over the past week. The rash is approximately 6 inches in diameter, with a red outer ring and a clear center. She also reports feeling fatigued and having a headache. The dermatologist suspects erythema migrans, a common manifestation of Lyme borreliosis, and informs the patient about the study investigating the species of Borrelia involved in the disease in France. The patient agrees to participate and signs the written consent. A cutaneous biopsy is performed to isolate Borrelia by means of culture and PCR. The patient has no allergies to local anesthesia and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 45-year-old male veteran who served in the military for 20 years. He has been experiencing tingling sensations and numbness in his upper and lower extremities, as well as difficulty with balance and coordination. The patient was diagnosed with cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) after an MRI revealed stenosis in his cervical spine. He has a lower extremity muscle strength of 4 as quantified by manual muscle test (MMT) 36 or above, and is able to stand without support with eyes closed for 30 seconds or more. The patient has no history of lower extremity or lumbar spine disease, peripheral neuropathy, or other neurological disorders. He has no difficulty standing in an upright position with both feet together and eyes closed. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the diagnosis and treatment of CSM for veterans like himself.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has a long history of seasonal allergies to birch pollen. She experiences symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy and watery eyes every year during the birch pollen season. The patient has a positive skin prick test and conjunctival test to birch, and a positive specific Immunoglobulin E (IgE) to birch. She has never been hospitalized for asthma, and her forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) is within the normal range. The patient is currently not taking any medication for her allergies, and she is willing to participate in the study to assess the efficacy and safety of SLIT One birch for the treatment of her birch pollen induced allergy.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past six months. He has feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities he used to enjoy. He has difficulty sleeping and often feels fatigued during the day. He does not have any history of suicidal attempts and is not currently experiencing any suicidal or homicidal thoughts. He has not received any treatment for depression in the past. He is not currently using any medications, but he is interested in participating in a clinical trial for depression treatment. He does not have any medical history of liver disease or seizure disorder. He is willing to use medically acceptable means of contraception throughout the study. He does not have any history of alcohol or substance abuse, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, panic disorder, or obsessive-compulsive disorder. He has not used any form of hypericum or sertraline during his current episode of depression. He is not currently in psychotherapy, but he is willing to participate in regular follow-up visits to monitor his symptoms and any side effects he experiences. He has the capacity to give informed consent and is willing to follow study procedures.

A 55-year-old man presents with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3, confirmed by two separate GFR measurements using CKD-EPI equation between 15 and 59 ml/min per 1.73 m2, with no other underlying medical conditions. He has been on blood pressure medication for the last 6 months with the systolic blood pressure ranging from 130-140 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure ranging from 80-90 mmHg. He is not on any TCM treatments for the last 2 weeks. He has no history of diabetes or any other chronic diseases. He is currently married and has two children. He is willing to participate in a 12-month clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of Fu-zheng-qu-zhuo oral liquid in improving renal function in patients with CKD stage 3 and 4. He has no history of psychiatric illness or tuberculosis and has not been enrolled in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma in her oropharynx. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis and has no history of any other malignancy. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which she manages with lisinopril. She reports no allergies to any medication. She has no history of salivary gland disease, Sjögren's syndrome, or any other medical issues. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her performance status is Zubrod 1. Her lab results show a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL. She has not undergone any chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the past 3 years. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study and is not pregnant or nursing. She has not received any neoadjuvant chemotherapy and is not on any concurrent cholinergic, anti-cholinergic, or tricyclic drugs.

A 58 year old man who has undergone heart transplantation 8 months ago is experiencing stable cardiovascular health. He is currently taking immunosuppressive medications and has no history of cardiac allograft rejection. His most recent hemodynamic assessment shows no evidence of restrictive physiology or cardiac allograft dysfunction. He has not been using any omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid supplements and does not have alcoholism or drug abuse problems. His Hb A1C is within normal range and fasting triglycerides are below 250 mg/dl. He is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old Chinese male who is generally healthy and has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18.5 to 25.0 kg/m2. He does not smoke, and has no known food allergies or intentional food restrictions. He does not have any metabolic or cardiovascular diseases, nor does he have any liver or kidney disorders. He is not taking any prescribed medication or dietary supplements that may interfere with the study measurements. He consumes less than 6 alcoholic drinks per week and does not engage in sports at the competitive or endurance levels. He is interested in participating in a study investigating the effects of different forms of fat on glycaemia, lipaemia, and insulinaemia. The study requires him to attend four testing sessions, each lasting 6.5 hours, and to follow specific dietary instructions prior to each session. He will be asked to provide a blood sample at various time points during each testing session. He has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to sign it if he meets the eligibility criteria.

A 25-year-old woman who is a student and works part-time as a sales assistant comes to the clinic for a contact lens fitting. She has been wearing contact lenses for daily wear for the past 2 years and is comfortable with her current lenses. She reports no history of ocular disease or infection and has no known allergies. Her visual acuity is 20/20 in each eye and she has an astigmatism of less than 1.00 D. She is willing to wear contact lenses for at least 12 hours a day during the study period and is available for follow-up appointments. She is interested in participating in the study and has read and signed the information consent letter.

A 45 year old female patient has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) according to the 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for RA. She has been taking at least one conventional synthetic (cs)DMARD (methotrexate (MTX), leflunomide, sulfasalazine (SSZ)) regularly for at least the preceding 12 weeks, with stable doses for at least the preceding 8 weeks. However, she has not responded to at least one TNF-inhibitor (TNFi) and has discontinued treatment after at least 3 months. She has moderately to severely active RA with at least 4 tender joints of 28 joints examined, at least 4 swollen joints of 28 joints examined and an elevated serum C-reactive protein level (CRP). She is seronegative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and negative for hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibodies. She has a high type I IFN gene signature test. She is not lactating or pregnant, and is using two effective methods of avoiding pregnancy, only one of which is a barrier method. She does not have any other condition that would interfere with evaluation of the investigational product or interpretation of patient safety or study results. She is willing to give written informed consent and commit to the study protocol.

This is a 42 year old female who has been experiencing chronic cough and non-cardiac chest pain for the past 3 months. She reports occasional heartburn and regurgitation but her symptoms are mainly extra-esophageal in nature. She has tried over-the-counter antacids with minimal relief. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism and anxiety. She is currently taking levothyroxine and sertraline. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if high-dose rabeprazole will provide better relief for her extra-esophageal symptoms.

Pt is a 45yo F recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer of the basal like subtype with EGFR expression confirmed by biopsy. She has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She presents with a breast mass and multiple lung nodules on imaging. The biopsy of the breast mass confirmed triple negative breast cancer with a Ki-67 of 70%. The ECOG performance status is 1. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for this metastatic disease. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for the past 10 years. She uses insulin injections to control her blood glucose levels. She reports feeling short of breath and having difficulty with physical activity, especially when climbing stairs or walking uphill. She also reports occasional episodes of dizziness and lightheadedness during exercise. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m² and is a non-smoker. Her past medical history is not significant for any other medical issues. Her family history is negative for diabetes and any other chronic illnesses. She is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about how her diabetes may be affecting her lung function and exercise capacity.

A 7-year-old male child with a recent diagnosis of diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) presents for enrollment in a clinical trial. The patient has not received any prior therapy other than steroids. The patient is able to swallow oral medications and has a Karnofsky score of 80%. The patient has a total bilirubin level within normal limits, and normal liver and kidney function. The patient has no history of seizures but has a history of febrile seizures. The patient's parents are willing to use a medically acceptable form of birth control during the study period. The patient's treating physician has ruled out disseminated disease, and the patient has undergone MRI of the spine. The patient and their parents have been informed of the nature of the study, agreed to its provisions, and signed and dated the informed consent form approved by the appropriate IRB/IEC.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who lives in a retirement community and has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and osteoporosis. She has noticed a decline in her physical abilities, including difficulty with balance and lifting objects. She is interested in participating in an exercise and nutrition program to improve her overall health and quality of life. She is able to speak English and is willing to attend the program with the help of a translator if needed. She currently does not engage in regular resistance exercise and is not in palliative care. She is able to perform basic activities of daily living and does not have cognitive impairment. She has no absolute exercise contraindications but will seek physician approval before exercising if necessary.

The patient is a 21-year-old man diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). He has a history of difficulty with social interactions and communication, as well as repetitive behaviors and routines. He is currently experiencing symptoms of ASD and is undergoing treatment for this condition. The patient has an IQ score above 70 and is medication-free for the month preceding participation in the study. He is willing to provide urine samples to screen for use of illicit substances prior to each scan. The patient does not have a history of psychosis, co-morbid major mental illness, or significant physical illness such as heart disease or high blood pressure. He does not have a known allergy to cannabis and has not undergone treatment for epilepsy. The patient is a male and is within the age range of 18-50 years. He is willing to give informed consent to participate in the study and is available to attend all the required sessions.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl with chronic pain related to sickle cell disease. She has been on oral morphine for the past 5 days but is still experiencing severe pain. She is expected to require pain medication for at least the next 4 months. She is able to swallow medication and has no known allergy to oxymorphone or other opioids. Her parent or legal guardian has provided informed consent for her participation in the study.

45yo man with symptomatic saphenous vein insufficiency, presenting with discomfort, swelling, and discoloration of both legs. He has no history of DVT or previous varicose vein surgery or injection sclerotherapy. The patient is seeking treatment for his symptoms and has been recommended for endovenous laser ablation of the saphenous veins. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the fate of calf perforators after the procedure.

The patient is a 6-week-old infant from South Africa who is in good health as confirmed by medical history and clinical examination. The infant was born full-term and has no history of premature birth, congenital abdominal disorders, intussusception, or abdominal surgery. The infant's parents have provided informed consent and intend to remain in the area with the child during the study period. The infant has not received any rotavirus vaccine in the past and is not currently receiving any immunoglobulin therapy or blood products. The infant has not been diagnosed with any systemic disorder, immunological impairment, or major congenital or genetic defect. The infant's parents have no medical condition that would interfere with protocol adherence or their ability to give informed consent. The infant has not been exposed to HIV and a PCR test has been done to confirm the same. The infant meets all inclusion criteria for the infant cohort of the Phase I/II Descending Age Study of P2VP8 Subunit Parenteral Rotavirus Vaccine in Healthy Toddlers and Infants.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who lives independently and walks without assistive devices. She has a medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or neurological disorders that affect lower extremity function, and has never received a cortico-steroid injection to the quadriceps or patellar tendon. She reports occasional knee pain but no pain in the thigh muscles. She does not have a diagnosis of inflammatory arthritis or muscle diseases such as muscular dystrophy. She currently participates in a regular exercise program once a week. She does not take anticoagulants or platelet inhibitors.
