She does not have any chronic and significant respiratory disease or shortness of breath. Her vision is good and she is able to accurately see the monitor screen during training program.

A 42-year-old man came to the clinic with a history of Parkinson's Disease (PD) diagnosed by a movement disorder neurologist. He has been taking PD medications for the past 3 years but still experiences disabling motor clinical features that are not optimally controlled. He has a predominant disability on the right side of his body. His motor assessment while OFF medications on the MDS-UPDRS is 40. He has been stable on his medications for 30 days prior to study entry. The subthalamic nucleus is visible on his MRI, which makes him eligible for the study. He is able and willing to give informed consent and attend all study visits. He is able to communicate sensations during the ExAblate Transcranial procedure. He meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with pseudohypoparathyroidism, a rare genetic disorder that causes hormone resistance, short stature, early-onset obesity, and cognitive impairment. He has participated in a previous randomized clinical trial for pseudohypoparathyroidism and has been deemed eligible for the open label extension study of theophylline treatment. The patient has no history of seizure disorders, cardiac arrhythmia, or hepatic insufficiency. He does not smoke or abuse alcohol, and is not pregnant nor planning to become pregnant in the next year. The patient has no active peptic ulcer disease and is not currently taking any medication that may affect theophylline levels. He is compliant with study procedures and is willing to participate in the 24-month clinical trial.

A 18-year-old female with moderate to severe acne vulgaris presents with concerns about the appearance of her skin. She has tried multiple over-the-counter acne treatments with minimal improvement. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of dapsone in treating acne vulgaris. She has not participated in any previous Allergan study. She does not anticipate the need for surgery or hospitalization during the study.

25 year old female with type 1 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at age 13. Currently on a basal-bolus regimen with human rapid and intermediate (NPH) insulin with an HbA1c of 8.5%. Has a history of hypoglycemia unawareness and has experienced multiple episodes of severe hypoglycemia requiring assistance in the past year. No history of diabetes-related complications or comorbidities. Compliant with insulin regimen and blood glucose monitoring. Not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the next 6 months. Lives in Romania.

A 65-year-old man with a history of metastatic prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel-based therapy is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial. He has experienced two rising PSA levels of 3 ng/mL and 4 ng/mL, respectively, measured one week apart. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and adequate hematologic and organ function. The patient has no history of diabetes or significant heart disease. He has not previously been treated with abiraterone, ipatasertib or GDC-0980. She is informed that the study will involve taking hydroxychloroquine and prednisone or placebo, and she is willing to take the study medication as directed. She understands that the study is double-blinded, and she may receive either hydroxychloroquine and prednisone or prednisone alone.

A 25-year-old non-smoking woman who is not breastfeeding and has a BMI of 23.5 is eligible for this clinical trial. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has not taken vitamin supplements in the past 7 days prior to the administration of the medications under study. She does not have any significant cardiovascular disease and has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgery that could affect drug absorption. She has not donated or lost a significant volume of blood or plasma or platelets during the 3 months prior to the start of the study. She has not participated in any type of clinical study during the 3 months prior to the start of the study. She has no fear of blood collection and is willing to participate in the study.

A 70-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with decreased vision in his left eye. On examination, the patient is found to have subfoveal choroidal neovascularization (CNV) secondary to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) with a lesion greatest linear dimension (GLD) of 4000 microns (approximately 6.7 disc areas [DA]). The patient's best-corrected Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) visual acuity (VA score) is 60 letters (approximate Snellen equivalent of 20/60). The patient has not received any prior treatment for CNV in the study eye except for laser treatment outside the subfoveal area. The patient is willing and able to attend the protocol-required visits and does not have any known allergies or hypersensitivities to the study treatments. The patient does not have subfoveal geographic atrophy or subfoveal fibrosis in the study eye and has not had intraocular surgery within the past 3 months. The patient does not have any other systemic diseases or active uncontrolled infections that would make them a poor medical risk, and does not have uncontrolled glaucoma or a history of stroke within the past year.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese man who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus infection. He has been experiencing mild fatigue, occasional joint pain, and loss of appetite for the past few months. His medical history includes hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are being managed with medications. He has never received any treatment for his hepatitis C infection. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he has no other significant medical or surgical history. He is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder. She has been diagnosed with bipolar II disorder for the past 3 years and has been on medication treatment for the past year. She has been taking mood stabilizers regularly but has been experiencing episodes of depression and hypomania. She is currently unemployed and living with her parents. She has been feeling hopeless, and has had difficulty concentrating and sleeping. She reports a history of non-adherence to medications due to forgetfulness and being busy with her daily activities. She has no history of substance abuse or psychotic symptoms. She is currently not suicidal or homicidal. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her adherence to medication treatment and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman with a history of opioid addiction who is currently on buprenorphine maintenance therapy. She is at the end of her third trimester and has scheduled an elective cesarean delivery via a Pfannenstiel incision under regional anesthesia due to her previous history of a cesarean section. Her BMI is 28, and she has no known allergies to any of the study medications. She is currently in good health and has not experienced any complications during her pregnancy. She has consented to participate in the study and is willing to undergo either a TAP block or a patient-controlled epidural for pain control after her surgery. She has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of participation in the study and understands the use of a patient-controlled epidural analgesia.

45-year-old male with a history of knee pain and discomfort for the past year presents for knee arthroscopy. He has no known medical conditions and is classified as ASA 1. He is informed about the study and is willing to participate. The patient has not taken any pain medication in the past 12 hours and has no known allergies to medications. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient has not been diagnosed with osteoarthritis or synovitis. He has not had any recent infectious diseases or immunodeficiency. The patient does not have kidney failure, heart failure, or a history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. The patient has not received perioperative steroid treatment, paracetamol, NSAIDs, or COX2-inhibitors. The use of a tourniquet for bloodless field is not necessary for his surgery. The patient reports moderate pain (VRS=2) at rest, and is eligible for inclusion in the study.

44-year-old male, BMI of 27 kg/m2, with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presents to the clinic for routine follow-up. He reports occasional shortness of breath on exertion and fatigue. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. He is currently taking amlodipine and atorvastatin as prescribed by his primary care physician. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in processed foods and saturated fats. He expresses interest in making lifestyle changes to improve his health. He has a smartphone and is willing to use a wearable device and mobile application to track his progress and receive feedback coaching. He has no history of severe cardiopulmonary disease, cancer, or other acute diseases, and is not currently pregnant.

An 18 year old female who is a full-time college student with no significant past medical history. She is fluent in English and is able to read and understand study materials. She has no history of participating in contact sports or any chronic diseases. She has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, neuropsychological disorders or special education. She is not currently taking any medications or substances that affect the central nervous system. She has no significant sensory deficits, and no history of clinically significant brain trauma.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who underwent a first metatarsal bunionectomy surgery. She has a history of moderate to severe pain and has been experiencing pain within 9 hours after the discontinuation of the postoperative analgesia. The patient has not used any antiparkinsonian drugs, neuroleptics, anticonvulsants, MAOIs, TCAs, SSRIs, or SNRIs within 30 days of surgery and throughout the study period. She has no history of seizure, febrile seizure, or loss of consciousness due to head trauma. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide written informed consent. Her vital signs are stable, and her physical examination is unremarkable. The patient's pain intensity is moderate to severe and her pain intensity VAS score is equal to or greater than 40 mm. She is permitted to use supplemental systemic analgesics during the postoperative surgical period.

The patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with locally advanced thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. He presented with dysphagia, weight loss, and occasional chest pain. He underwent an endoscopy, and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. He has no significant past medical history, and he does not smoke or drink alcohol. His physical examination was unremarkable except for mild dehydration. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score is 0. His lab work showed normal hematopoietic, liver, and renal function. His chest CT and PET/CT scans showed T3N1M0 esophageal cancer. He has not received any previous treatment for his cancer, including chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and can be followed up for a long time. He signed the informed consent form and is willing to cooperate with the treatment.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and cirrhosis. He presented to the emergency department with symptoms of upper gastrointestinal bleeding, including melena and hematemesis. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) revealed bleeding esophageal varices, which were managed with endoscopic band ligation (EBL). The patient is currently receiving standard of care therapy, which includes 72-hour octreotide infusion. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all of which are well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no known allergies, and is willing and able to provide informed consent for study.

A 28-year-old Caucasian male with type 1 diabetes for 5 years presents with frequent episodes of hypoglycemia despite following the recommended treatment of ingesting 15-20g of carbohydrates. He is on multiple daily insulin injections and uses rapid-acting and basal insulin analogs. His HbA1c is 8.5%. He reports symptoms of sweating, shaking, and confusion during hypoglycemic episodes. He has no history of microvascular complications and his renal function is normal. He has no history of macrovascular events or abnormal cardiac rhythm. His blood panel and hemoglobin levels are within normal limits. He is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. He has not experienced a severe hypoglycemic episode in the past month and does not have hypokalemia. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of the recommended treatment for hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes patients using modern insulin analogs.

A 67-year-old male presents with night sweats, fatigue, and weight loss of 10 pounds over the past 3 months. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and benign prostatic hyperplasia. He is a former smoker with a 30 pack-year history and quit smoking 6 years ago. Physical exam reveals cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. His laboratory results show an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and lactate dehydrogenase. A biopsy of a cervical lymph node confirms classical Hodgkin lymphoma. He has not received any treatment for his condition and is mentally and physically fit to withstand the proposed treatment regimen. He provides written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of frequency, urgency, and bladder pain for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with interstitial cystitis (IC) and has undergone cystoscopic hydrodistention under anesthesia within the past year, which revealed grade 2 diffused glomerulations but no Hunner's lesion. She has not had a

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of peripheral arterial disease and has been experiencing pain in his legs while walking for the past few months. He has been diagnosed with Rutherford category 4, indicating moderate to severe claudication or pain in his legs. He has already undergone a few endovascular interventions in the past to open the blocked vessels, but the symptoms keep recurring. He is scheduled for another intervention to treat the occlusion or stenosis in the infrainguinal vessels. He is able to provide informed consent and meets the age criteria for the study. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is not pregnant or lactating, and the specific limb to be treated has previously undergone endovascular intervention.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was recently hospitalized for an acute myocardial infarction. He resides in Pierce County, Washington with his spouse who is physically and mentally capable of operating an AED. He has a history of coronary artery disease and has undergone a cardiac procedure. He is able to provide written informed consent and has a telephone. He does not have a DNR order checked on his chart and does not have an implantable cardioverter defibrillator. He speaks fluent English.

As this is a study involving medical professionals, there is no patient description required. Instead, eligible participants are surgeons and anesthesiologists who are accredited to practice at HSS, as well as all anesthesia and orthopedic surgery fellows and residents. The inclusion criteria specify that these individuals must be willing to participate in the study, while there are no specific exclusion criteria listed other than refusing to participate.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her 16th week of gestation. She is of average weight with a BMI of 22. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or drugs. She has no history of serious systemic infections, cancer, major organ disease, or systemic lupus erythematosus. She does not have multiple infants, and there are no fetal diagnoses of congenital cardiac structural or conduction defects or brain malformations. She has not been diagnosed with Type I diabetes, and her blood pressure is within normal range. The patient understands English and is willing to take the study capsules and be contacted by phone.

The patient is a premature infant born at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1200 grams. The infant required intubation and mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress syndrome. The infant received surfactant therapy and mechanical ventilation was discontinued after 3 days. The infant required multiple blood transfusions due to anemia of prematurity with low hemoglobin levels. The infant is currently stable and receiving enteral feedings with human milk fortifier. The infant is being considered for enrollment in the clinical trial to measure anemia and physiologic tissue response to blood transfusions using quantitative NIRS.

A 58-year-old woman with a diagnosis of metastatic lung cancer presented with a complaint of fatigue, loss of appetite and weight loss. She reported difficulty completing her activities of daily living and had a WHO performance status of 2. She denied any history of enteral or parenteral nutrition within the last month or any psychiatric disorder that could impair her ability to participate in the trial. She was currently receiving palliative treatment for her cancer. The patient was able to walk at least 100 meters independently without crutches or walking frame, as assessed by her treating physician based on her history and physical condition. She had no known brain metastases or symptomatic bone metastases. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she was taking Lisinopril and Atorvastatin. She reported no known allergies. Her vital signs were within normal limits. The patient provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old male ex-smoker with a smoking history of 20 pack-years presents with a chronic cough and difficulty breathing. He reports that his symptoms have been present for the past 5 years and have progressively worsened. He has been diagnosed with COPD and has been using a combination inhaler containing salmeterol and fluticasone for the past 3 months. However, he has experienced several exacerbations of his symptoms in the past year, requiring antibiotics and oral steroids. His FEV1 is 45% predicted. He has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. He denies any history of cardiac problems or allergies. He works as a truck driver and is married with two adult children. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of tiotropium delivered by the Respimat inhaler in patients with COPD.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been diagnosed with HIV infection for the past 6 years. He has a CD4 count of 120 cells/mm3 and has been on antiretroviral therapy for the past 4 years. For the past week, he has been experiencing shortness of breath, dry cough and fever. He has lost some weight and has been feeling weak. A chest X-ray revealed interstitial infiltrates in the lungs. His physician suspects Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) and has recommended a bronchial fibroscopy with broncho-alveolar lavage (BAL) for a definitive diagnosis. However, due to his weakened immune system, the physician is also interested in the potential of non-invasive diagnostic methods for PCP. The patient is being admitted to the Grenoble Alpes University Hospital for further evaluation and treatment. He has medical insurance and is willing to participate in the clinical trial after being informed about the study and providing written consent.

The patient is a 10-year-old Caucasian girl who has been diagnosed with myopia with a refractive error of -2 diopters in both eyes. She has experienced myopia progression of -0.75 diopters per year over the past year. The patient has no history of astigmatism or anisometropia beyond 1.5 diopters. She has no history of glaucoma, amblyopia, strabismus, or any other ocular disease. The patient has no developmental delays and can respond to subjective testing. She has never worn contact lenses before and is willing to comply with wearing the experimental lenses daily for 18 months. The patient has normal color vision and has no history of wearing bifocal lenses. She has never had any type of eye surgery. The patient is able to have axial length measurements accurately on the Zeiss Intraocular Lens Master and can be refracted to 20/20 or 20/15. The patient is willing to donate a blood sample or a buccal swab for genetic analysis.

The patient is a 35-year-old male OEF/OIF veteran who has recently experienced combat-related trauma. He reports recurrent nightmares, flashbacks, and avoidance of trauma-related cues, which have been affecting his daily life for the past year. He has not been diagnosed with PTSD but meets the criteria for sub-threshold PTSD as defined by Blanchard et al. (1994). He is fluent in English, has the ability to read and write, and is willing to attend on-site appointments and be contacted by phone with study reminders. He has no history of primary psychotic disorder, impaired cognitive functioning, or suicidal or homicidal intent. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about forgiveness-based writing and potentially prevent the progression of his symptoms to full PTSD.

27-year-old male with a history of recreational cannabis use for the past 2 years, smoking cannabis 2 days a week. He is in good health, with no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. He has a BMI of 24 and weighs 70 kg. The patient has abstained from cannabis use for the past week and has negative urine drug tests for all substances except cannabis. The patient is able to read and speak Spanish fluently and is willing to comply with study requirements. The patient is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications, except for occasional use of paracetamol. The patient has not participated in any other clinical studies in the last three months and does not have any clinically significant findings in physical examination or safety laboratory parameters.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with stage I hypertension based on her routine blood pressure measurements at her primary care physician's office. She has never been on any medication for hypertension and has no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes. She works as a teacher and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She occasionally drinks alcohol and does not smoke. Her blood pressure readings at the clinic are consistently above 140/90 mmHg. She has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to undergo acupuncture treatment. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She has been informed that she may receive either true acupuncture or sham acupuncture and that the results will be compared at the end of the study. She has agreed to follow the study protocol and attend all scheduled appointments.

55 yo M with a history of metastatic prostate cancer with bone involvement and persistent severe pain despite optimized analgesic therapy including opioids and bisphosphonates. Imaging reveals a painful musculoskeletal metastasis in the left proximal femur. The patient has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months and an ECOG performance status of 1. Neutrophil count is 2.6 Gi/l within the past 14 days and coagulation panel is adequate. The patient has medical insurance coverage and has signed and dated informed consent document indicating that he has been informed of all the pertinent aspects of the trial prior to enrollment. Past Medical History: - Metastatic prostate cancer with bone involvement - Hypertension - Gout - Hyperlipidemia - Benign prostatic hyperplasia - S/p left inguinal hernia repair with mesh placement [**10-24**] - Allergic to penicillin - Current medications: oxycodone, acetaminophen, allopurinol, atorvastatin, tamsulosin.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. She is currently being treated with insulin therapy and metformin, and her HbA1c level is between 7% and 9%. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has no history of chronic liver disease, neoplasia treatment, or use of glucocorticoids within the past 3 months. Her eGFR is above 30 (calculated CKD EPI) and her hemoglobin level is above 11 grams. She has no history of type 1 diabetes or use of GLP1 agonists. She has been experiencing occasional episodes of hypoglycemia and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of insulin therapy in elderly patients with T2DM. She is able to commit to the protocol instructions and visit schedule and is willing to wear a FreeStyle Libre Flash CGM for a 6-week study period. She is able to travel to the research center for sensor changes and is interested in learning more about her glycemic control and adherence to therapy.

A 55-year-old male patient was referred by his primary care physician to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the impact of a 12-week yoga-mindfulness intervention on cognition in older adults with HIV. The patient was diagnosed with HIV 7 years ago and has been taking anti-retroviral drugs since then. He reports experiencing difficulties with memory and thinking, which affect his daily activities and quality of life. He currently resides in the Halifax area and has the capacity to provide informed consent. He is interested in participating in the study and willing to attend yoga classes twice a week for the duration of the intervention. He has no contraindications to exercise and has not participated in a yoga program within the past 6 months.

A 20-year-old female patient with a history of fibroadenoma was referred to participate in a clinical trial investigating the link between prolactin receptor gene mutations and breast diseases. She has been diagnosed with multiple fibroadenomas and has not received any hormonal treatment for the past 3 months. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. The patient will be asked to provide tumoral and peri-tumoral tissue samples for in vivo analysis of PRLR mutants.

The patient is a 35 year-old male who presented to the hospital with severe abdominal pain. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication regularly. He works in construction and smokes half a pack of cigarettes every day. He has no known allergies. The pain started suddenly 2 hours ago and is located in the lower right side of his abdomen. He rates the pain as 8 out of 10 on a pain scale. He has no vomiting or diarrhea but feels nauseous. He denies any recent travel or illness. His vital signs are stable and within normal limits. He has a normal physical exam except for tenderness in the right lower quadrant. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman presents with a history of recurrent infections, including pneumonia, sinusitis, and urinary tract infections. She has also experienced several episodes of joint pain and swelling, which have been attributed to rheumatoid arthritis. She has a family history of autoimmune disorders, with her mother having been diagnosed with lupus. The patient is interested in participating in a study that may help identify the underlying genetic cause of her immune disorder. She has no known allergies, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient is willing to provide a blood sample for whole exome sequencing and is open to receiving secondary findings from the study. She is willing to allow her genetic information to be shared in controlled access databases.

A 48-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with early breast cancer. The tumor size is 2.5 cm and there is no palpable lymph node involvement. She is otherwise healthy with no underlying medical conditions. She has no history of breast cancer in her family. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no allergies to any food or drugs. She has not undergone any breast surgeries in the past. She is willing to undergo PET/MRI prior to her surgery and has provided informed consent for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing persistent lower back pain for over 6 months. He describes the pain as radiating to his buttocks and lower limbs, and it is aggravated by walking. He also experiences fatigue and loss of sensation in his lower limbs. The patient has been diagnosed with Lumbar Spinal Stenosis (LSS) and has been informed that he is eligible to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficiency of surgical treatment for degenerated LSS. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands that he may be randomly assigned to either a surgical group or a nonoperative group. He has been informed that he will be assessed at regular intervals over a period of 2 years and that the primary outcome will be pain relief as measured by Oswestry disability index. The patient does not have any neurologic disease that causes impaired function of the lower limbs.

The patient is a 20-year-old university student who wears daily, soft, frequent replacement lenses licensed in Canada (monthly disposable lenses) for at least 3 days a week and 6 hours a day during the past 2 months. She has been experiencing discomfort while wearing her contact lenses, with a difference of at least 3 hours between her average and comfortable wear time with habitual lenses. She falls into the symptomatic group as per Young's criteria. She is able to remove and insert the lenses by herself and owns a wearable pair of spectacles. She has correctable visual acuity (VA) to logMAR 0.20 or better in each eye and shows an acceptable lens fit with her habitual lenses. The patient has no known active ocular disease or infection, no ocular abnormality that would contraindicate contact lens wear, and does not use any systemic or topical medications that may affect the study measures. She is willing to follow the study instructions and maintain the appointment schedule, and is willing to wear the study lenses for 10 hours.

56-year-old male patient, currently admitted to the VA hospital for complications related to his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has a history of smoking for the past 30 years and has tried to quit smoking on several occasions, but has not been successful. He reports smoking at least a pack of cigarettes a day before his hospital admission. On review of his medical records, it was noted that he had a previous history of depression, but it was well-controlled with medication. He is currently on albuterol inhaler and oxygen therapy for his COPD. Upon screening, he reported that he had smoked at least 5 cigarettes/day for the past year and has used tobacco products during the week prior to admission. He was given a Beck Depression Inventory, and his score was within the acceptable range for the study. He expressed his willingness to participate in the study and provided informed consent. He did not report any contraindications to the use of bupropion, and his physician was contacted to verify his eligibility. The research associate put in the prescription for the study drug, and he was randomized to Study Arm 1. He will receive a standard 7-week course of sustained release bupropion, a self-help booklet, counseling on smoking cessation strategies, and follow-up phone counseling during the first 3 months after randomization. He will complete study questionnaires regarding his medical and smoking history and will be followed one week after his hospital discharge to record his blood pressure and to monitor possible side effects. He will be trained to resist and cope with the temptations and stresses likely to be encountered after discharge from the hospital. Behavioral self-management techniques to counter known relapse-triggers such as stress, the presence of other smokers, alcohol use, and depression will be discussed during follow-up counseling calls. Saliva cotinine levels will be measured in all participants who give a history of smoking abstinence at the end of treatment and at 6 months.

The patient is an 82-year-old male who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and a persistent sore throat for the past 3 months. Examination reveals a mass in the hypopharynx and further evaluation confirms a diagnosis of locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy and has not participated in any other interventional clinical trials within the past month. The patient's Karnofsky Performance Scale score is above 60 and his life expectancy is estimated to be more than 6 months. Laboratory tests show that the patient's hemoglobin, white blood cell count, and platelet count are within normal limits, and his liver and renal function are also normal. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and is eligible to participate in the study as an Arm A participant in the "Prospective, Randomized, Controlled, Phase II Multiple Centered Clinical Trial of Nimotuzumab Combined with Radiotherapy for Senile Locally Advanced SCCHN".

A 42-year-old male with type 2 diabetes and a history of peripheral neuropathy in both feet has been prescribed the Podimetrics Remote Temperature Monitoring System for monitoring his foot health. He is employed as a desk worker and spends most of his day seated. He reports mild physical activity, such as walking for approximately 20 minutes a day. He has no history of foot ulcers. He is able to understand and communicate in English and has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

Pt is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B. He has been diagnosed with cirrhosis and is HBsAg positive for more than 6 months. His HBV DNA levels are detectable and he has not been treated with any nucleoside/nucleotide analogues before. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating emtricitabine plus adefovir dipivoxil in Chinese naive HBV related cirrhosis patients. He has no history of HCC and his AFP levels and imaging studies have not shown any evidence of it. His creatinine levels are within normal limits and he has no signs of kidney disease. His hemoglobin levels are normal and he has not been infected with other viruses such as HAV, HEV, HCV, HDV, or HIV. He has no history of autoimmune diseases or cancer. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressants or immunomodulators. He has not undergone liver transplantation and is not allergic to nucleoside or nucleotide analogues. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease (CAD) after a coronary angiography. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and hypertension for 10 years, which is well-controlled with medication. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 29.6 kg/m2 and complains of snoring and daytime sleepiness. He has never been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and has not undergone any pharyngeal surgery or received continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment for OSA. He is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

28-year-old pregnant woman in her first trimester, living in a rural area approximately 0.5 miles away from a glyphosate-treated field. She has no history of gestational diabetes or any other high-risk pregnancy factors. She currently consumes an exclusively conventional diet and has no intentions of switching to an organic diet. She agrees to refrain from applying residential glyphosate (Round Up) during the study. She has no occupational exposure to glyphosate and does not live with anyone who has occupational glyphosate exposure. She is willing to participate in a study that will assess her glyphosate exposure via urinary biomonitoring on a weekly basis throughout pregnancy, and to take part in a two-week dietary intervention that will involve one week of organic food and one week of conventional food in a randomized crossover design. She is also willing to provide daily spot urine samples during the dietary intervention phase. All study components will be completed with no face-to-face interaction to eliminate all coronavirus (COVID-19) related risks.

The patient is a 62-year-old Hispanic male who has been experiencing persistent cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing for the last 3 months. He has a history of smoking for over 30 years and has a family history of lung cancer. The patient was referred to a pulmonologist who performed a bronchoscopy and a biopsy. The biopsy confirmed the presence of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) with metastasis to the liver and bones. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 2 at diagnosis. He has been assigned by his treating physician to receive chemotherapy and palliative care. The patient has access to his medical chart for data collection and is willing and able to provide written informed consent and privacy authorization for the release of personal health information for the Prospective Epidemiological Study of Metastatic Non Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) in Latin America - LATINO Lung.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been struggling with opioid addiction for the past two years. She has tried various treatments including methadone and sublingual buprenorphine, but has not been able to maintain long-term sobriety. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial for Probuphine as a potential treatment option. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use a reliable form of contraception during the study. She has no significant medical or psychiatric conditions that would preclude her from participating in the trial. She is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a healthy newborn baby girl born to a 28-year-old mother without any history of chronic illnesses or medication use during pregnancy. The baby was born at 39 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 3.2 kg. The mother's serology for hepatitis B is negative. The baby was born by a normal vaginal delivery with Apgar scores of 9 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The baby has no congenital abnormalities or infections, and all routine newborn screening tests are normal. The parents have given informed consent for the baby to participate in the clinical trial, which aims to assess the immunogenicity and safety of the PENTAXIM vaccine in the Philippines. The baby will be randomized to Group A and will receive the PENTAXIM vaccine at 6, 10, and 14 weeks of age, along with the recombinant 10 µg hepatitis B vaccine at 0, 6, and 14 weeks of age. The baby will also receive a booster dose of PENTAXIM vaccine at 18-19 months of age. The baby has not received any vaccines since birth, except for BCG.

A 55-year-old Caucasian female presented to the Cardiology clinic with a history of palpitations and shortness of breath. She reported that these symptoms have been occurring on and off for the past 2 years, and have become more frequent in the last few months. She denied any chest pain or syncope. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type II diabetes, which were all well-controlled with medications. She had no known family history of cardiac diseases. She was a non-smoker and did not consume alcohol. Her physical examination was unremarkable except for irregularly irregular heart rhythm. Her electrocardiogram (EKG) showed atrial fibrillation. She was started on rate control medications and anticoagulation therapy. She was referred for ablation therapy due to unsuccessful attempts with antiarrhythmic drugs. She was evaluated for eligibility for the study, and her left atrial anteroposterior diameter was found to be 44 mm by echocardiography. She was deemed eligible for the study and provided informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is inoperable, and the patient is not willing to undergo surgery. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The patient's performance status is good, with a KPS score of 70. His blood tests show that he meets the eligibility criteria for the study, with a neutrophil count of 2.1×10^9/L, platelet count of 120×10^9/L, and hemoglobin level of 110g/L. The patient has no other serious medical conditions or complications. The patient has measurable disease, with a maximum diameter of the tumor being 3cm as measured by spiral CT. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the treatment and follow-up procedures.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and discomfort in her jaw for several months. She reports difficulty in opening her mouth fully and experiences a clicking sound upon opening or closing her jaw. She has not received any prior treatment for her symptoms. Upon evaluation, she is diagnosed with temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis of unknown etiology according to the RDC/TMD criteria. She is eligible for participation in the clinical trial and is randomly assigned to either the treatment or placebo group. The patient is able to tolerate the laser therapy and attends all scheduled sessions. She is evaluated at the start of treatment, after the 6th and 12th laser therapy sessions, and one month after the end of treatment. The patient reports a decrease in pain and tenderness in masticatory muscles as measured by the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). She also reports an improvement in the range of lateral and protrusive mandibular movements, and the difficulty in chewing food. She does not experience any sound in her joint upon opening or closing her mouth. One year after treatment, the patient undergoes a second cone beam CT of the TMJ to evaluate any changes in the morphology of the joint.

50-year-old female with a medical history of metabolic syndrome, hypertension, and high cholesterol. She is currently taking medication to control her hypertension and cholesterol levels. She reports experiencing occasional stress and anxiety due to work and family responsibilities. She is interested in participating in a study that explores the benefits of nature and forest therapy for her health. She has no mobility limitations and is able to engage in physical activity. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with thoracic idiopathic scoliosis (Lenke 1 or 2) during a routine school examination. Her condition has been monitored for the past year by a pediatric orthopedist, but her curves have progressed despite the use of a brace. The orthopedist has recommended posterior spinal fusion with instrumentation as the next step in her treatment. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She is an active teenager who enjoys playing soccer and hiking with her family. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings. She is excited to undergo surgery and hopes that it will improve her quality of life. Her parents are fully supportive of the decision to proceed with surgery and have signed the necessary consent forms.

The patient is a 16-year-old adolescent who has been experiencing halitosis for the past six months. She is a high school student and feels embarrassed and self-conscious about her breath. She brushes her teeth twice a day and uses mouthwash regularly but notices that the bad breath persists. She has no dental-facial anomalies and is not currently undergoing any orthodontic or orthopedic treatment. She has no removable appliances, implants, or dentures. She has no history of periodontal disease or carious lesions. She has not undergone any cancer treatment and has not taken any antibiotics in the past month. She is not pregnant and has no known hypersensitivity to the photosensitizing agent. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form with authorization from her legal guardian.

A 4-year-old girl was referred to the clinic by her pediatrician due to difficulty swallowing and choking episodes while eating. The parents report that the child has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 months. A modified barium swallow study revealed aspiration during oral feeding. The pediatrician also noticed that the child has a weak cry and hoarse voice. Microlaryngoscopy was performed, and the diagnosis of type I laryngeal cleft was confirmed. The child is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The parents are willing to have their child undergo general anesthesia for the injection laryngoplasty procedure. The child's weight is 15 kg, and she is up to date on all her vaccinations.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with arrhythmia and has had a pacemaker implanted over a year ago. He is experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath, and his cardiologist has recommended a transvenous lead extraction procedure. He has provided informed consent to participate in this study, which involves the use of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) imaging during the procedure. He has no history of psychiatric or medical comorbidity that would affect his ability to provide consent. The IVUS catheter will be inserted through his veins to the superior vena cava (SVC) and right atrium to assess the presence and severity of intravascular lead adherence (ILA) or scarring, which could impact the difficulty of the extraction procedure. He has at least one lead over 1 year dwell time requiring extraction, and there is no venous occlusion that would prevent the IVUS catheter from passing. He is 178 cm tall, weighs 87 kg, and has a BMI of 27.5. He has no known allergies and is not on any medications that would interfere with the IVUS imaging. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol excessively.

The patient is a 60 year old African American male who was recently discharged from the emergency department after experiencing high blood sugar levels. He has a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years and has received treatment from Jefferson Primary Care Physician. He has had multiple ED visits due to uncontrolled diabetes and is now interested in participating in a clinical trial to help prevent future ED visits. He lives alone in a low-need community and has difficulty managing his diabetes due to limited access to healthcare resources. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He has limited knowledge about diabetes management and is willing to receive education from healthcare professionals. He is willing to participate in a 12-month trial and is committed to following the intervention plan. He has no significant medical or psychiatric history that would exclude him from participating in the study.

7-year-old male, scheduled for an MRI at Children's Hospital Boston due to recurrent headaches. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient's parents have provided written consent for the study. The patient meets the established sedation criteria and has no history of allergy, intolerance, or reaction to dexmedetomidine or propofol. The patient does not have current, repaired, or risk for Moya-Moya disease, has not had a stroke within the past six months, and does not have uncontrolled hypertension. The patient is not currently using beta antagonist, alpha 2 agonist or calcium blocker. The patient does not have a known soy, Lecithin, or egg allergy.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl with a history of cystic fibrosis. She has been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has noticed that she has been feeling more tired during the day. She has also been experiencing shortness of breath during physical activity. Her lung function tests show a forced expiratory volume in one second of 55% predicted value. She has not had an acute respiratory exacerbation in the past month and has completed an antibiotic course. She has agreed to participate in a sleep study at the hospital for one night. She has no other medical conditions and has a valid health insurance.

A 35 year old man who works as a construction worker came to the clinic with complaints of low back pain that has been bothering him for the last 3 months. The pain is mostly on the lower back and buttocks area and it gets worse after long hours of standing or bending. He rates his pain at 6/10 on the numeric analog scale for pain. His Modified Oswestry Disability Index score is 25%. He has no known history of any red flags or nerve root compression. He has not undergone any surgery to his lumbar spine and he is not pregnant. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve outcomes in patients with mechanical low back pain through exercise program and stretching for the hips.

A 45-year-old female patient diagnosed with pelvic organ prolapse and scheduled for laparoscopic surgery was referred to the clinical trial. She is proficient in English and has no previous participation or randomization in the study. She has no history of abdominal wall pain and is not a chronic pain patient. She is in good general health and has no current medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study.

A 27-year-old female presents with anterior knee pain that has been present for the past 4 months. The pain is described as diffuse and located around the patella, with an intensity of 6 on the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) of pain in the last week. The pain is aggravated by activities that require knee flexion, such as stair climbing, kneeling, and prolonged sitting. The patient reports no history of trauma to the knee, surgery, or fractures in the lumbar spine, hip, knee, or ankle. She denies any history of patellar dislocation, meniscal injury, cruciate ligament injury, or collateral ligament injury. The patient also reports no history of any tendonopathy in the patellar tendon, tendons of the goose, or band leg tibial ilium. She does not have any edema in the knee joint. Upon examination, the patient presents with ankle dorsiflexion restriction, as measured by the Lunge Test. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial aimed at analyzing the effect of ankle mobilization techniques in ankle dorsiflexion range of motion in women with patellofemoral pain and with dorsiflexion restriction.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing hearing loss in her left ear for the past 5 years. She has a history of chronic otitis media and has undergone multiple ear surgeries in the past. The hearing loss has significantly impacted her quality of life and ability to communicate with others. She has tried hearing aids but has not found them to be effective. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. On examination, the patient's bone conduction thresholds with a pure tone average PTA4 are < 30 dB hearing level in her left ear. She is considered a suitable candidate for the Baha Attract System and has provided informed consent to participate in the investigation. She has not received radiation therapy in the same side of her skull where the Baha Attract System will be positioned, and her bone quality and thickness is sufficient for the implant. The patient is able to follow investigational procedures and complete quality of life scales.

A 24-year-old female presents to the emergency department with complaints of sexual assault that occurred 4 weeks ago. She reports feeling anxious, depressed, and guilty about the assault. She has been having difficulty sleeping and has occasional nightmares related to the event. She is currently living with her roommate and has no family support in the area. She reports drinking more often than usual since the assault and has been drinking more than 3 drinks on some days. She is currently unemployed and spends most of her time at home. She has a smartphone and internet access. She speaks fluent English. Her past medical history is significant for depression and anxiety. She is not on any medications currently. She denies any suicidal ideation or previous suicide attempts. Her PTSD Checklist score is 35.

The patient is a 56-year-old female who has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis in both knees. She has had pain in her knees for the past 8 months despite trying conservative therapies such as physical therapy and pain medication. She has a BMI of 32 and is in good overall health with no history of major medical conditions. She speaks and understands English fluently. She has not had any knee surgery or major injuries within the past year and has not received any injections in her knees in the past 6 months, including corticosteroids, viscosupplementation, or platelet rich plasma. She does not have gout, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus arthropathy, psoriatic arthritis, avascular necrosis, severe bone deformity, or infection of the knee joint. She is willing to stop taking prescription pain medication 7 days prior to any visit and is not allergic to lidocaine, epinephrine, or valium. She does not use any form of tobacco, including e-cigarettes. She has bilateral knee pain scores of 7 on the short-form WOMAC pain scale.

A 40-year-old man presented to the orthopedic clinic with complaints of pain and swelling in his left knee following a sports injury. He was playing soccer when he twisted his left knee while trying to change direction. He experienced immediate pain and swelling in the knee. He was unable to bear weight on his left leg and required assistance to walk. On examination, there was marked swelling and tenderness over the posterior aspect of his left knee. A posterior drawer test was positive. X-ray revealed a tibial avulsion fracture of the posterior cruciate ligament. MRI showed a complete tear of the posterior cruciate ligament. He has no history of any chronic illness and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and social drinker. He works as a construction worker and leads an active lifestyle. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new bone fixation plate for the repair of tibial avulsion fracture of posterior cruciate ligament of the knee.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing skin changes on her abdomen and back for the past year. She has noticed that the skin is becoming thicker and harder, and there are areas of discoloration. Her primary care physician referred her to a dermatologist who diagnosed her with morphea after a physical examination and skin biopsy. The patient has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in the Morphea in Adults and Children (MAC) cohort study and understands the purpose of the registry. She is able to give informed consent and is willing to provide blood samples for the DNA repository. The patient is of Hispanic descent and has no family history of morphea or systemic sclerosis.

A 25-year-old individual diagnosed with DOCK8 deficiency, LAD-1, or GATA2 Deficiency is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. The patient must have adequate venous access for peripheral apheresis or must consent to use a temporary central venous catheter for apheresis. They must have a serum creatinine level of less than 1.5 mg/dL, total bilirubin level of less than 3mg/dL, and ALT and AST levels less than 5 times the upper limit of normal. Female patients of childbearing age must have a negative urine pregnancy test within one week of beginning Filgrastim administration. They cannot have HIV infection, chronic hepatitis B or hepatitis C virus infection, active infection that is not responding to antimicrobial therapy, or active malignancy in another organ system other than the hematopoietic system. Additionally, they must not have a history of psychiatric disorder which may compromise compliance with the protocol, or which does not allow for appropriate informed consent. Individuals with severe heart disease or symptomatic angina will not be eligible. Patients cannot have any medical contraindications to stem cell donation such as severe atherosclerosis, autoimmune disease, iritis or episcleritis, deep venous thrombosis, cerebrovascular accident, or thrombocytopenia (platelets less than 50,000 per microlitre) at baseline evaluation. Finally, patients must test negative for transfusion-transmissible infectious agents, including hepatitis B (HBsAg), hepatitis C (anti-HCV), HIV (anti-HIV-1/2). The trial aims to collect stem cells from the blood of individuals with immunodeficiency diseases to develop potential gene therapy treatments. The patient will receive five days of G-Filgrastim followed by a single apheresis. CD34+ cells will be selected and frozen in aliquots by the Cell Processing Section of the Department of Transfusion Medicine. No treatments or investigational therapy will be administered on this protocol.

A 55 year old male with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 pneumonia is experiencing severe respiratory distress with a respiratory rate of 35 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation levels below 90%. The patient has been hospitalized and requires mechanical ventilation. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but no significant allergies to medications. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. The patient is not pregnant nor lactating. The patient has no known primary immunodeficiency nor HIV-infection. The patient has no immune diseases, mental illness, nor drug addiction but has been taking antiviral drugs for the treatment of COVID-19. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trial in the last 30 days.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of heart disease and hypertension. He is scheduled for a transesophageal echocardiography exam to evaluate his heart function. He has previously undergone this procedure and found the standard bite block uncomfortable and difficult to tolerate. He has experienced some discomfort in his jaw and mouth after the procedure due to the hard plastic material of the bite block. The patient is currently on medications for his heart condition and has no known allergies. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the modified bite block for improved patient comfort during the procedure. He is not currently undergoing any other medical treatments or procedures.

Patient is a 60-year-old male who presented with a persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past two months. Imaging studies revealed the presence of a small nodule in the lung, which was suspected to be malignant. The nodule is located in a suitable site for percutaneous lung puncture, and the patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the optimized pre-loaded micro-coil locating method for pulmonary small nodules. The patient has no history of pneumothorax or pleural effusion, and has a generally good health status with no severe cardiopulmonary dysfunction or cachexia. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 62-year-old woman underwent a screening colonoscopy which revealed a non-pedunculated polyp of 8 mm in the sigmoid colon. She had no history of colorectal cancer or polyps. The biopsy result showed a tubular adenoma with low-grade dysplasia. She was scheduled for a polypectomy and was offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the accuracy of the resection of non-pedunculated polyps of 5-20 mm. She met the inclusion criteria for the trial and had no exclusion criteria. She provided informed consent and was randomized to the group that will undergo polypectomy with the use of Narrow Band Imaging (NBI) to define the margins of the lesion before the procedure.

This clinical trial is not applicable to patients as it is focused on evaluating the effectiveness of a multifaceted knowledge translation intervention on pain in hospitalized infants. Therefore, the participants in this trial would be NICUs and staff members of the NICUs in Canada, and not individual patients.

A 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) has been receiving chronic intravenous Treprostenil therapy for the past 6 months. He is on hemodialysis therapy three times a week for the past year. The patient is in functional class III of PAH and has no other significant medical history. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His vital signs are stable, and he has no symptoms of acute right ventricular failure. The patient has no known allergies to Treprostenil or any other medications. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 35-year-old female patient with a recent diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) is being considered for participation in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of Tecfidera in restoring glutathione synthesis. The patient has not previously received any MS therapy and has an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 2.5. She has experienced three relapses in the past year, with symptoms including numbness and tingling in the extremities and difficulty with fine motor movements. The patient has no known allergies to fumarates and has not been treated with systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressants. She has no contraindications for MRI/MRS and is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential benefits and risks associated with it.

An 80-year-old woman presented at the hospital with a hip fracture after a fall at home. She has a medical history significant for hypertension, osteoporosis, and hypothyroidism, for which she is taking levothyroxine. She lives alone but has family members who check on her regularly. She has never undergone surgery before and is concerned about the risks associated with anesthesia. She has no known cognitive or mental health issues, and her Mini-Mental State Examination score is 27. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 26. She is classified as an ASA grade II patient. The surgeon has recommended open reduction and internal fixation.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl diagnosed with medulloblastoma. She has undergone standard therapy, including chemotherapy and radiation, but has experienced relapse. The tumor has spread to other parts of her brain and spinal cord. She is experiencing headaches, vomiting, and difficulty with movement and coordination. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. She is eager to participate in the clinical trial and hopes to find a treatment that will help her fight the cancer. Her family is supportive of her decision and is willing to provide any necessary assistance throughout the trial. The patient is well-nourished and well-dressed, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She is able to communicate clearly and understand the instructions provided by the medical team. The patient's Lansky/Karnofsky performance scale is above 50 and her ECOG is less than or equal to 2. She is eligible for the trial and is willing to undergo the required tests and treatments.

The patient is a 45-year-old non-smoking woman who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of coughing and wheezing for the past 3 months. She has no history of asthma or other respiratory conditions. Her chest x-ray is normal, but her physician suspects that she may have an underlying respiratory condition that requires further investigation. The patient consents to undergo bronchoscopy and biopsy to determine the cause of her symptoms. She has no known hemorrhage risk and no contra-indication for bronchial endoscopy. She has health insurance coverage and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50 year old woman who works full-time as a teacher and has two children. She is generally healthy but feels that she does not have enough energy to keep up with her busy schedule. She admits to eating fast food and processed snacks frequently due to lack of time to prepare meals. She reports that she eats about 2 servings of fruits and vegetables per day. Her recent blood tests were normal: Hgb: 12.5 g/dL WBC: 7500 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /mL Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL BUN: 15 mg/dL Glucose: 90 mg/dL Cholesterol: 200 mg/dL The patient is interested in learning how to eat healthier but feels overwhelmed by the many options available and is unsure of where to start. She would like to participate in a study that can help her increase her fruit and vegetable intake without having to completely change her diet.

53-year-old female, postmenopausal, with a history of stress urinary incontinence (SUI) for 5 years. She has tried conservative measures such as pelvic floor exercises and weight loss but they have been ineffective. She has no history of previous incontinence procedures, neither has she undergone any concomitant prolapse procedure. She is fluent in English and has the capacity to consent. She has been diagnosed with urodynamic stress incontinence, and her treating urogynecologist has recommended the placement of a retropubic midurethral sling as an appropriate treatment. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the low elasticity polyvinylidene fluoride (DynaMesh®-SIS soft) retropubic midurethral sling. She is willing to complete standard urinary incontinence and quality of life questionnaires prior to the procedure and at 3, 6, 12, 18 and 24 months postoperatively, and attend clinical follow-ups at 3 and 12 months postoperatively.

A 25 year old woman was diagnosed with monogenic diabetes at age 18. She has been taking sulfonylurea medication for the past 7 years to manage her blood glucose levels. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. She has a stable weight and good general health. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the mechanisms of metabolic control in monogenic diabetes patients treated with sulfonylurea medications.

A 52-year-old male was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme six months ago. He underwent surgical resection followed by radiotherapy and temozolomide chemotherapy. However, his follow-up MRI showed recurrence of the tumor with a single focus of measurable Central Nervous System (CNS) neoplasm measuring 3 cm in diameter. He has no history of other primary malignancy or HIV positivity. He is currently taking prescribed corticosteroids for neurological symptoms. His Karnofsky performance status is 80% and his blood work shows an absolute neutrophil count of 1,500/mm³, platelet count of 110,000/mm³, total serum bilirubin of 1.5 times upper limit of normal (ULN), SGOT of 2 times ULN, BUN of 1.2 times ULN, and creatinine of 1.3 times ULN. He has no acute infection and is neurologically stable for the past two weeks.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a BMI of 27. She has no history of sleep-related breathing disorders or psychiatric disorders. She has not been diagnosed with any neurological or medical disease that might affect sleep. She does not take any medication that may affect sleep or sleep-related movement disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to study infra-slow EEG oscillations during sleep. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is available to participate in the study for the required duration.

A 28-year-old expectant mother is scheduled for an elective Cesarean section in two weeks. She has a history of mild asthma and seasonal allergies, but they are well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has no history of drug abuse. Her height is 165 cm, and she weighs 70 kg. Her obstetrician has advised her to breastfeed her newborn after delivery. She has agreed to provide breast milk samples for the clinical trial. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study as she is healthy, has normal cardiac and pulmonary function, and has no complications during pregnancy. She understands the study procedures and is willing to comply with them.

A 35-year-old female patient came to the clinic with a history of asthma symptoms since childhood. She has been using a non-corticosteroid controller medication for the past 6 months without any significant improvement in her symptoms. She complains of wheezing, coughing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness, particularly at night and early in the morning. She is a non-smoker and has no history of respiratory infections. Her pre-bronchodilator FEV1 is 70% of predicted normal value at screening, and she has demonstrated reversibility of disease with a 15% increase in FEV1 with the use of a short-acting beta-2 agonist. She agrees to replace her current short-acting beta-2 agonist with albuterol for the duration of the study. She is judged capable of withholding albuterol for at least 4 hours prior to study visits. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is not affiliated with the investigator or site staff. She has no history of severe milk protein allergy or sensitivity to the constituents of the novel DPI. She has no other clinically significant, uncontrolled condition or disease that would pose a safety risk to her or confound interpretation of study results.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman diagnosed with Takayasu arteritis (TAK) 2 years ago. She has experienced moderate symptoms, including hypertension (systolic blood pressure of 165 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 100 mmHg), with aortic arch and carotid artery involvement, causing dizziness during light physical activity. She has not experienced any pulmonary artery or renal artery involvement, and her eGFR (MRDR) is 70

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with a regular sleep schedule. She works as a graphic designer and is typically in bed by 11 pm and wakes up at 7 am. Her BMI is 24. She has no history of any major illnesses or psychiatric disorders. She is not taking any medications currently or in the past month. She does not consume more than one cup of coffee per day. She has never smoked or used any drugs. She is sexually active and uses a hormonal contraceptive method. She is willing to abstain from sexual activity or use double-barrier contraception during the study period. She is able to read and communicate in English and has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 14-year-old girl with a history of elevated blood pressure presents for evaluation. She has no symptoms and is physically active. Her blood pressure is consistently above the 95th percentile for her age and sex, and her BMI is within the normal range. She has no family history of hypertension or cardiovascular disease. Laboratory tests revealed normal fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin, and renal function. The patient has not been on any antihypertensive medication. The echocardiogram showed increased left ventricular mass, and the fundoscopic examination revealed retinal vascular abnormalities. The patient is enrolled in the clinical trial to evaluate the potential risk factors and the time sequence for the development of these end-organ complications in children with essential hypertension. The patient will undergo longitudinal evaluation to monitor the development of left ventricular hypertrophy and retinal vascular disease and to determine the relationship of these complications to the risk factors found in the first phase of the study. The study will help to identify the risk factors associated with end-organ complications in children and adolescents with essential hypertension and to develop strategies for their prevention and treatment.

Patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been on a stable regimen of Ortho Cyclen for the past 3 months. She has regular menstrual cycles and has not experienced any breakthrough bleeding or spotting. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 55 kg. She has no significant medical history and has not undergone any major surgeries in the past. She does not smoke and has not had any recent drug or alcohol abuse. She is willing to switch to Ortho Cyclen for the duration of the study, which is approximately 78 days. She is not currently breastfeeding and has a negative pregnancy test within 24 hours prior to dosing on Day 1 of Cycle 1. She has no history of biliary disorders, gastrointestinal diseases, or any other sound medical, psychiatric, and/or social reasons that would prevent her from participating in the study.

56-year-old female with a history of smoking and a current diagnosis of lung cancer. The patient presents with a non-visible lung lesion up to 3cm in size in the largest diameter. She is a candidate for a non-emergency bronchoscopy procedure and is willing to provide signed informed consent. She has not undergone a CT scan over a month before the bronchoscopy procedure. The patient is otherwise in good health and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic Stage D/ New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class IIIB/IV left ventricular failure. He has been on optimal medical therapy, including dietary salt restriction and diuretics, for the last 60 days but is failing to respond to treatment. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is overweight with a BMI of 35 and has a history of smoking but has quit for the last 5 years. He works as a mechanic and has had to reduce his working hours due to his condition. He has been on an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) for the last 7 days and inotropes for the last 14 days. His left ventricular ejection fraction is ≤ 25%. He is ineligible for cardiac transplantation due to his medical history. He has no history of mechanical circulatory support (MCS) other than an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP). He is willing to receive either the HeartWare® VAS or control LVAD. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 22 weeks pregnant. She has been smoking for the last 6 years and is currently smoking around 10 cigarettes per day. She has tried to quit smoking on several occasions but has been unsuccessful. She is experiencing a low mood and feels anxious about her pregnancy. The patient is an English speaker and has access to a telephone. She is willing to attend all the counseling sessions and is open to all the study procedures. There are no known complications that would adversely affect her attendance. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in all assessments and study procedures. The patient is not currently undergoing psychotherapy, and there is no history of any medical condition that would preclude her from completing the study requirements.

A 15-year-old female was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) six months ago. She completed induction chemotherapy and achieved complete remission with no evidence of disease. However, she has not yet undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation due to concerns about toxicity of the conditioning regimen. Her medical history is significant for anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia related to her leukemia. She has no history of allergies or autoimmune diseases. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for a visible port-a-cath in place. Her laboratory values are as follows: WBC count 4.5 x 10^9/L, Hgb 9.5 g/dL, platelets 80 x 10^9/L, and ANC 1.2 x 10^9/L. She has no other medical problems and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and feasibility of extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) as part of a reduced intensity preparative regimen for stem cell transplantation in children and young adults with leukemia.

75-year-old female with a history of osteoporosis and mild cognitive impairment presents to the hospital with a fall from standing height. X-rays reveal a displaced, comminuted distal femur fracture. She was ambulatory with the use of a cane prior to the injury. She has no history of previous fractures and has not undergone any surgical fixation or joint replacement in the affected area. She has no active or previous infections around the fracture site, no major vascular injuries, and no associated major injuries of the lower extremities. The patient speaks English and has a substitute decision maker who can provide written informed consent.

45-year-old female diagnosed with ovarian cancer, underwent first line primary surgery and chemotherapy, followed by second line chemotherapy that failed to produce any improvement. She underwent secondary cytoreductive surgeries, but the cancer continued to progress, and she is now considered incurable. She is expected to receive third line chemotherapy for palliation, but she meets the entry requirements for this study. The patient has a Karnofsky score greater than 80 and has not been treated with any chemotherapy or biologic therapy within the previous 21 days. The patient has no CNS metastases, no lung disease, and a pulmonary function test (PFT) with FEV1 >50% expected. The patient has no uncontrolled hypertension, myocardial infarction, or unstable angina in the past 6 months, no NYHA class II-IV congestive heart failure, no atrial fibrillation (AF) or Supra Ventricular Tachycardia (SVT) requiring medication to control, and no peripheral vascular disease ≥ CTCAE grade 2. The patient has normal electrolyte, renal and liver function parameters, and hematologic parameters. The patient is aware of the investigational nature of this treatment and has indicated informed consent by the IRB-approved written process.

Pt is a 35yo M who works in a petrochemical plant as a technician. He has been working there for the past 5 years and has been exposed to butadiene on a daily basis. He has not been diagnosed with any metabolic disorders and is in overall good health. He is interested in participating in a study to better understand the relationship between butadiene exposure and biomarkers in the blood and urine.

Pt is a 45yo male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to diabetes who has been on dialysis for the past 3 years.
