He is currently listed for kidney transplant and has been informed that he is at high risk for delayed graft function (DGF) due to his donor's Irish scale risk score being ≥25%. The patient has no history of prior transplantation and is not highly sensitized to the donor. He has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and is compliant with all medications. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. He is not pregnant nor breastfeeding, and he has agreed to use medically approved contraception during the study. There is no history of HIV or active hepatitis B or C infection. The patient has a history of well-controlled hypertension and his most recent labs are within normal limits. He is able to comply with the requirements of the study protocol and is not participating in any other investigational studies.

A 54-year-old man who has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol suffered an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and was successfully resuscitated by paramedics. He was brought to the hospital where he received intensive care and had a sustained return of spontaneous circulation. He is currently unconscious and unable to obey verbal commands or respond to pain. He has no history of dementia or substance abuse. He speaks the local language fluently and is able to participate in the neuropsychological assessment without the need for an interpreter. He is not on oxygen therapy and has not been diagnosed with COPD. He has no obvious or suspected pregnancy. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with all aspects of the assessment.

A 38-year-old woman who has undergone IVF in the past with no success due to low embryo quality is eligible for this clinical trial. She has signed the informed consent form and has an AMH level of 6 pM/L. She has a BMI of 25 and is planning to undergo an IVF cycle with arrays in Preimplantation Genetic Screening. Her partner has a semen sample with a concentration exceeding 3 million/mL progressive motile sperm. In her previous IVF cycle, she had 7 metaphase II oocytes retrieved. However, all of the embryos obtained were included in the worst prognosis category according to morphological criteria established by ASEBIR. She has no formal contraindications for ovarian cortex biopsy or follicle puncture, and her male partner does not have severe male factor infertility. She is interested in participating in this pilot study to improve embryo quality through autologous mitochondrial transfer.

The patient is a 65 year old man who was previously diagnosed with polycythemia vera, a type of myeloproliferative neoplasm. He has been experiencing unexplained weight loss, fatigue, and shortness of breath for the past few months. Further evaluation reveals that he has developed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) secondary to his previous condition. He is being considered for participation in a clinical trial investigating the use of ruxolitinib in combination with chemotherapy for post-MPN AML. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 2 or better and is deemed physically fit enough to tolerate induction chemotherapy. He has no history of serious secondary malignancies within the past 2 years and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not previously received treatment with ruxolitinib and has not participated in any other clinical trials at the time of registration.

A 45 year old man is brought to the emergency department after collapsing on the street. Bystanders performed CPR until the arrival of the ambulance. The patient was found to have an extra-hospital cardiac arrest and was resuscitated successfully. He has no significant past medical history and was not taking any medications. The patient is currently unconscious and intubated. The team decides to initiate therapeutic hypothermia using the CoolGard 3000® system to improve his outcome. He will be included in a clinical trial to evaluate the cerebral oximetry value in patients subjected to two different levels of therapeutic hypothermia after an extra-hospital cardiac arrest. The patient is between 18 and 80 years old, and has no neurological or traumatic cause of cardiac arrest.

A 32-year-old woman came to the fertility clinic with a history of infertility for the past 2 years. She has been trying to conceive with her partner for over a year without success. She has regular menstrual cycles and has never been pregnant before. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she does not smoke or drink alcohol. Upon evaluation, she was diagnosed with unexplained infertility. She has agreed to undergo ovarian stimulation with MENOPUR as part of her infertility treatment plan.

A 68-year-old man was recently diagnosed with mantle cell lymphoma after experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His biopsy results confirmed MCL according to the WHO classification. He has not received any prior treatment for MCL and is ineligible for autologous transplant. His ECOG performance status is 1. His laboratory results show a platelet count of 130,000/mm3, an absolute neutrophil count of 1,500/mm3, and a calculated creatinine clearance of 55 mL/min. He has no history of allergies or hypersensitivity to thalidomide or murine antibodies. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is willing to abstain from donating blood while taking lenalidomide therapy. He understands the potential teratogenic risk of lenalidomide and agrees to follow proper pregnancy precautions. He is aware of the risks of foetal exposure and will not share study medication with another person.

This is a 62 year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes and diabetic retinopathy. He has been experiencing visual impairment due to diabetic macular edema (DME) for the past 6 months. He has not received any prior treatment for his DME. His visual acuity in his left eye is 20/80 and in his right eye is 20/40. He has signed informed consent to participate in the AURIGA observational study to evaluate the effectiveness of intravitreal aflibercept in the treatment of DME. He has no contraindications as listed in the local intravitreal aflibercept SmPC (summary of product characteristics) and is not currently participating in any other clinical (interventional) study or any other anti-VEGF study. He has not received systemic anti-VEGF and pro-VEGF treatment and has no structural damage to the center of the macula that is likely to preclude improvement in VA following the resolution of macular edema. He has not had prior retinal surgery and has not received prior treatment with aflibercept. He has not had a history of stroke or transient ischemic attacks within the last 6 months, and has not had laser photocoagulation (panretinal or macular) in the study eye within 90 days of Day 1. He is eligible for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old Asian male who presents to the clinic with symptoms of jaundice, fatigue, and abdominal pain. He reports that he has been feeling unwell for the past two weeks and that his symptoms have been progressively worsening. He has a history of chronic hepatitis B and was diagnosed 5 years ago. He was not previously treated with antiviral therapy. On physical examination, he has a yellowish discoloration of the skin and sclerae. His abdomen is tender to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory tests reveal elevated levels of AST and ALT, as well as total bilirubin. His prothrombin time is also prolonged. His HBV DNA level is above 2,000 IU/mL. His serum creatinine is within normal limits. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any known allergies. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and signs the informed consent form.

A 25-year-old woman, with a BMI of 22 kg/m2, has been using oral contraceptives containing norgestimate and ethinyl estradiol for the past 6 months. She has no history of thromboembolic disease, liver disease, migraines, or any other medical conditions. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. She does not use any other forms of contraception. She has never been exposed to sotagliflozin (LX4211) and has not taken any injectable contraceptives or hormonal intrauterine devices in the past 12 months or a topical controlled delivery contraceptive (patch) in the past 3 months. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and able to provide written informed consent.

There is no need to generate a patient description for this clinical trial as it does not involve direct patient participation or intervention. The study is focused on evaluating the impact of work schedules on healthcare continuity, fatigue, and adverse events in ICUs, and involves the participation of residents, staff members, and patients/family members under the care of the participating residents. Therefore, patient descriptions are not applicable in this context.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 5 years ago. She has been treated with Enbrel for the past 6 months with a stable disease. Her rheumatologist has decided to transition her to Benepali due to cost-saving measures. She has had no major episodes of infection requiring hospitalization or treatment with parenteral anti-infectives within the past 2 months. She has not received any live or live-attenuated vaccines within the last 6 months and has not been treated with any investigational agents within the last 6 months. She is not receiving any other biologic agent for RA. She is advised to use appropriate contraception to avoid becoming pregnant during Benepali therapy and for three weeks after discontinuation of therapy.

A 30-year-old woman is pregnant with twins and currently in her 20th week of gestation. She has a history of one previous pregnancy resulting in a term delivery of a healthy singleton. She has been experiencing a smooth pregnancy with no complications so far. Her current prenatal ultrasound shows twin gestation with a documented first trimester ultrasound, confirming her reliable menstrual date. However, her cervical length is less than 25mm. She has no history of major malformation or chromosomal abnormality to her fetuses. She has no history of seizures, psychiatric disorders, uncontrolled chronic hypertension, congestive heart failure, chronic renal failure, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus with end-organ dysfunction, active thrombophlebitis or thromboembolic disorder, history of hormone-associated thrombophlebitis or thromboembolic disorders, active liver dysfunction or disease, or known or suspected malignancy of the breast or genital organs. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

32 yo male with a history of external genital warts for the past 3 months. Lesions are flat and papular, not pediculated, and have not been treated with any previous condyloma treatment in the last 2 months. Total wart area is approximately 200mm2 and individual wart area measures no more than 50mm2 with a major perpendicular diameter of 10mm or less. The patient has not received any genital wart treatment for previous condylomas (other than the prior treatment for current condylomas referred at inclusion criteria) in the last 12 months before enrollment. The patient has no history or presence of cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastro-intestinal, hepatic, renal, metabolic, hematological, neurologic, psychiatric, systemic or infectious disease, and is not transplanted or immunosuppressed. The patient has no clinically significant abnormality following review of screening laboratory tests, vital signs, full physical examination and ECG. The patient has not used any dermatological drug therapy in the treatment area during the last month prior to the first application of the study drug. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a history of occasional anxiety and no significant medical conditions. He is scheduled to undergo elective lumbar surgery under general anesthesia and has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. He has no known allergies to narcotics and has a heart function rating of Ⅰ. The surgery is expected to last between 2 to 4 hours. The patient has never been diagnosed with depression or brain trauma, nor has a history of narcotics or drug addiction. The patient has not been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome. The patient is able to sign informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 9-year-old male patient is diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and is scheduled for renal transplant surgery. The patient weighs 26 kg and has no history of any major medical conditions. The patient has no known allergies to medications or anesthesia. The family history is unremarkable. The patient has no current infection or any other contraindications for surgery. The patient will be eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of weight and end-stage renal disease.

50-year-old woman with newly diagnosed metastatic breast cancer. She has a history of hypertension and has been on medication for the past 5 years. She is postmenopausal and has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She has a good performance status (ECOG 0) and has not received any prior chemotherapy for advanced or metastatic disease. Her HER2/neu status is positive by immunohistochemistry (3+ by HercepTest^™), and she meets all other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study. She has measurable disease with multiple lesions in the liver and lungs on CT scan. She has not undergone any major surgery or radiotherapy in the past 4 weeks, and she is willing to use effective contraception during and for 30 days after study participation.

27-year-old Muslim male with no significant medical history and a BMI of 25 kg/m². He has been practicing Ramadan fasting for the past 5 years and is interested in participating in a study that investigates the benefits of a modified Ramadan fasting regimen on health and well-being. He reports no history of eating disorders or psychological disorders and is not currently on a diet. The patient is willing to adhere to the educational components and nutritional modifications provided by the study protocol. He is not currently pregnant nor breastfeeding.

A 28-year-old woman presents with irregular menstrual cycles, acne, and excessive hair growth on her face, chest, and abdomen. She has been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She reports a history of being overweight and insulin-resistant. Her blood tests show elevated levels of androgens and insulin. An ultrasound of her ovaries reveals multiple small follicles. She is diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) according to the Rotterdam diagnostic criteria. The patient is interested in participating in a prospective cohort study to investigate the short- and long-term health consequences of PCOS. She is willing to provide biological samples, complete questionnaires, and share her health data to help provide evidence for PCOS prognosis.

A 28-year-old non-smoking male presented to the hospital within 14 days of sustaining a complete mid-substance Achilles tendon rupture. He has no other injuries affecting his lower limb functions and is not taking any immunosuppressive or anticoagulation treatment. He is able to attend all follow-up appointments and can manage transport to and from the hospital on his own. He understands Danish and is willing to participate in the study investigating the effect of delayed loading following surgical repair of a ruptured Achilles tendon on clinical outcome and muscle and tendon structure after one year.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m^2 and has been trying to control her blood sugar levels with diet and exercise. However, her HbA1c levels have been consistently high at 8.5% (69 mmol/mol) despite her efforts. She has never taken any medication for diabetes before, but has been on metformin for the past 30 days. She has no history of chronic pancreatitis or inflammatory bowel disease. She is not taking any medication with a narrow therapeutic window. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her diabetes.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his left knee for the past year. He is diagnosed with degenerative arthritis of the knee, with an IKDC score of 55 and Grade 2 osteoarthritis as determined by the radiographic criteria of Kellgren and Lawrence. The patient has tried non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications, but they have not provided adequate relief. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history and no major findings from the physical examination, hematology, serum chemistry, and urine tests. The patient has not taken glucosamine, chondroitin, or any natural medicine within 14 days before the injection of the investigational product. He has not taken anti-inflammatory drugs within 14 days before the injection of the investigational product. He has not taken immunosuppressive agents within 3 months before enrollment in this study. He is not pregnant, and he has not participated in another clinical trial within 30 days before enrollment in this study. The patient is willing to use an effective contraceptive method during the study period and has voluntarily agreed to participate in this study, and signed the informed consent form.

A 15-year-old female student presents with recurrent headaches for the past year. The headaches are throbbing in nature, usually on the right side of the head, and are associated with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. She experiences these symptoms about 2-3 times a week, which last for 4-6 hours. She reports that the headaches often interfere with her school attendance and extracurricular activities. She has tried various over-the-counter medications like ibuprofen and paracetamol, but the relief is only temporary. She has no history of head injury, seizures, or other neurological disorders. She denies smoking, alcohol, or drug use. Her physical examination and neurological examination are normal. Her family history is positive for migraine headaches, with her mother and grandmother experiencing similar symptoms. She is fluent in Norwegian and is willing to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old man presents with chronic low back and hip pain that has been affecting his daily activities for the past 6 months. The pain started after he lifted a heavy object at work. The pain is localized to the lower back and right hip and is described as a dull ache. The pain is aggravated by prolonged sitting or standing and improves with rest. He denies any radiation of pain or numbness/tingling in the legs. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications, physical therapy, and massages with no significant improvement. He has no significant past medical history, allergies, or surgeries. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. On physical examination, he has tenderness in the lumbopelvic region and restricted hip motion. His neurological examination is normal with no sensory or motor deficits. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

Maria is a 42-year-old woman who presented with a history of chronic constipation and difficulty defecating. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past year and they have significantly impacted her quality of life. Maria has tried various laxatives and enemas with little relief. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities. Further diagnostic tests, including a defecography and anorectal manometry, confirmed a diagnosis of obstructed defecation syndrome with an ODS score of 12 and CCS score of 6. She was advised to undergo stapled transanal rectal resection (STARR) surgery. After obtaining written informed consent, she was enrolled in a randomized controlled trial to assess the efficacy of psyllium fiber in improving postoperative progress and functional outcome after STARR.

A 62-year-old male patient is scheduled for elective coronary artery bypass grafting surgery due to angina and triple vessel coronary artery disease. He has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes which are well-controlled with medications. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath at rest but reports experiencing chest pain with exertion. His physical examination is unremarkable except for a blood pressure of 145/90 mmHg and a heart rate of 80 beats per minute in sinus rhythm. Laboratory tests are within normal limits. The patient does not have a history of atrial fibrillation or frequent and coupled extra systoles. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 40-year-old male patient with a history of Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome and idiopathic high levels of gastric acid secretion is being considered for this clinical trial. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of severe peptic ulcer disease due to uncontrolled gastric acid secretion. The patient is not currently taking any medication for the condition. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is available for follow-up visits. The patient does not have a history of adverse reactions or allergic responses to Omeprazole. The patient understands the importance of practicing effective birth control if female and of childbearing age.

A 55-year-old male came to the clinic complaining of rectal bleeding and abdominal pain. He has a history of colon cancer in his family, and he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few months. A colonoscopy revealed a tumor less than 6 cm from the anal verge, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of rectal cancer. An MRI showed that the tumor was advanced (T3-T4) and very low in the rectum. The patient has not experienced any distant metastases, nor does he have intestinal obstruction. He is otherwise healthy, with no allergies or mental disorders. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to undergo the cylindrical abdominoperineal resection surgery.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing a decline in her cognitive abilities over the past few years. She has noticed difficulties in remembering recent events and has been struggling with completing tasks that were once easy for her. She has a family history of Alzheimer's disease, with her mother having been diagnosed with the disease in her later years. The patient has undergone standard diagnostic procedures and has been diagnosed with prodromal dementia according to the Dubois criteria. Her clinical dementia rating (CDR) is 0.5, which suggests a very mild stage of dementia. Her memory impairment is defined as delayed recall on Verbal Learning Test (15 WLT) < 1.5 SD. Her MMSE score is 23, indicating mild cognitive impairment. She is mentally competent and has given informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of major vascular disorders or psychiatric or neurological disorders. She has no contraindications for scanning and no structural abnormalities of the brain. She has a reliable informant who can provide information about her cognitive abilities.

A 38-year-old female with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) presents with a platelet count of 8,000/µL. She has not experienced any bleeding episodes, but her physician has recommended prophylactic platelet transfusion due to her low platelet count. The patient is hesitant about receiving unnecessary transfusions and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares a prophylactic with a therapeutic platelet transfusion strategy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the AML project and has given written informed consent. She does not have known refractoriness to platelet transfusion or any plasmatic coagulation disorder.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing some urinary symptoms, such as hesitancy, weak stream, and nocturia. He went to see his primary care physician, who ordered a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) blood test and a digital rectal exam (DRE). The PSA level was slightly elevated (6 ng/ml), and the DRE revealed a suspicious area on the prostate gland. The patient was referred to a urologist, who recommended a dedicated MRI of the prostate to evaluate the suspicious area. The MRI showed a PI-RADS 4 lesion. The urologist discussed with the patient the possibility of a biopsy to determine if the lesion is cancerous. The urologist explained that there are two biopsy techniques available, one using software registration and the other using visual registration. The patient was informed that he would receive both types of biopsy, but the order would be randomized. The urologist also explained that traditional systematic biopsies would also be performed. The patient agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent. He was in good health, with no prior history of prostate cancer or prostate biopsy. He was willing to comply with the study protocol and further follow-up.

Patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with trichotillomania for the past 5 years. She reports having recurrent and persistent urges to pull her hair out, resulting in noticeable hair loss and bald patches. The patient has tried multiple treatments including behavioral therapy and various medications, but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. She is currently not taking any medications for her trichotillomania. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the medication. She has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or dementia, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to use medically accepted forms of contraception during the course of the study. The patient has no significant medical history or abnormalities on physical examination or laboratory tests. She is excited to try a new treatment option and hopes to see improvement in her symptoms.

A 58-year-old man was diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis (PMF) two years ago. He has been receiving treatment with ruxolitinib for the past 20 weeks, but has not had an optimal response. His spleen is enlarged and palpable, and he experiences significant fatigue and night sweats. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not undergone splenectomy or received prior MDM2 inhibitor or p53-directed therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his condition.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who sustained a right tibial fracture in a motor vehicle accident. The fracture is closed and requires surgical repair with internal fixation. The patient has no significant medical history, does not smoke, and does not take any medications. He has no known allergies to medication. He is able to comply with the study requirements and is willing to undergo randomization to receive either low molecular weight heparin or a placebo injection for up to 14 days after surgery. He has no contraindications to anticoagulation therapy and is able to receive contrast dye for ultrasound examinations.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo an elective surgery. She has a BMI of 32 and has been diagnosed with obesity. She has no other comorbidities and her American society of anesthesiologists physical status is II. She has no history of upper gastrointestinal tract morbidity or upper abdominal surgery. She is not pregnant and does not have renal or liver cell failure. She has fasted for 8 hours after a light meal of 200 ml milk, 50 g white cheese, and 120 g bread. She has signed a detailed informed consent form before enrollment in the study. She is willing to undergo focused gastric ultrasound by a trained physician in the semi-sitting position and right lateral position. She is willing to have a nasogastric tube (18-french) inserted after induction of anesthesia and endotracheal intubation, to perform aspiration of gastric contents through gentle suction using a 50 ml syringe with synchronous epigastric massage and gentle movement of nasogastric tube in and out for 10 minutes after confirmation of nasogastric tube position.

54-year-old female breast cancer survivor who underwent lumpectomy followed by radiation and chemotherapy. She developed mild to moderate lymphedema in her right arm after the treatment. She is currently in the maintenance phase of lymphedema treatment and is wearing a properly fitted daytime compression sleeve for 12 hours per day as per standard care. She is not currently using any nighttime compression. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study whether adding night-time compression to standard care will improve control of lymphedema and overall quality of life. She is willing and able to comply with the protocol, measurement, and follow-up schedule. She has no current active disease, skin irritations/rash, or thrombosis of the affected arm.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that has come back after previous treatments or has not gone away after treatment. The patient has no history of significant arrhythmias and her Karnofsky score is greater than 60%. The patient has had prior chemotherapy and has recovered from all acute non-hematologic toxic effects of all prior chemotherapy. The patient's tumor is CD30-positive and there is available allogeneic T cells with ≥15% expression of CD30CAR determined by flow-cytometry. The patient is not currently receiving any investigational agents or received any tumor vaccines within the previous six weeks. The patient has not received CD30 antibody-based therapy within the previous 4 weeks. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, has no history of hypersensitivity reactions to murine protein-containing products, and is not currently using systemic corticosteroids at a dose equivalent to higher than 10 mg/day of prednisone. The patient has no active significant, uncontrolled bacterial, viral or fungal infection and is not experiencing any symptomatic cardiac disease (NYHA class III or IV disease). The patient is willing to utilize one of the more effective birth control methods during the study and for 6 months after the study is concluded, if sexually active. The patient has been informed about the trial and has given her informed consent, and is willing to adhere to the study visits and procedures, including the standard medical screening tests, lymphodepletion chemotherapy with cyclophosphamide and fludarabine, infusion with CD30.CAR-EBVST cell treatment and follow-up visits.

32 y/o non-smoker with asymptomatic bilateral mesioangular impacted mandibular third molar (Pell and Gregory class II, position B). No history of alcohol abuse or allergy. No signs of acute severe periodontitis. Willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effects of surgical drain and kinesiologic tape applications on postoperative morbidity after mandibular third molar surgery. Willing to attend follow-up visits on days 2, 7, and 14 after surgery for pain, swelling, and maximum mouth opening assessments.

A 56-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with complaints of shortness of breath, cough, and fever for the past two days. He has a history of smoking and hypertension, but no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or heart failure. On examination, the patient is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 35 breaths per minute, and his oxygen saturation is 88% on room air. Arterial blood gas analysis reveals a PaCO2 of 50 mmHg and pH of 7.31. Chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates consistent with pneumonia. The patient is diagnosed with acute respiratory failure and started on non-invasive ventilation (NIV) using a face mask. Despite initial improvement, the patient continues to have difficulty synchronizing his breathing with the ventilator, leading to increased work of breathing and dyspnea. The patient is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial comparing pressure support ventilation (PSV) versus neurally adjusted ventilator assist (NAVA) during acute respiratory failure (ARF). He meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and has provided informed consent for participation.

35 yo F with a history of HIV infection diagnosed 4 years ago. Currently, the patient is on a stable HAART regimen for the past 8 weeks and has a CD4+ T-cell count of 300/mm(3). The patient's plasma HIV viral load has been less than 10,000 copies/ml on at least two occasions within 8 weeks prior to study entry. The patient has a Karnofsky Score greater than or equal to 80. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the safety and efficacy of the experimental drug Bay 50-4798. The patient has not received IL-2 or an IL-2 analogue in the past. The patient has not received any immunomodulators, cytokines, growth factors, or systemic corticosteroids in the past 4 weeks. The patient has not had an AIDS defining illness by the Centers for Disease Control definition within 8 weeks prior to study entry. The patient has not had any acute bacterial or viral infection within 4 weeks prior to enrollment. The patient has not received any immunization within 4 weeks prior to enrollment. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease, transplantation, or bone marrow suppression. The patient has no evidence of hepatic disease or significant cardiac insufficiency. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who resides in a noninstitutional group quarter, a YMCA. He is fluent in English and is interested in participating in the National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions-III (NESARC-III). He has a history of alcohol use disorder and wants to contribute to research in order to develop better treatment methods for people struggling with similar conditions. He is willing to complete an automated computer-assisted interview, an automated questionnaire, and provide a saliva sample for genetic study. He has no history of institutionalization, is not currently in prison, and is not living on a military base.

This is a 44-year-old woman who was diagnosed with lung cancer last year. Molecular testing completed on her tumour identified rare molecular alterations in the ALK gene. She is a Canadian resident and has been receiving follow-up for cancer care in Canada. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but has not had a significant response to treatment. She is interested in participating in the CARMA-BROS study to explore different treatment options and understand the natural history of her disease. Despite her condition, she maintains a positive outlook and is committed to finding the best possible treatment options.

32 yo F presents with a positive HIV test after routine screening. She has no prior history of HIV treatment and a CD4 count of 250 cells per microliter. She is currently asymptomatic and has no significant medical history. She is of child-bearing potential and agrees to use a proven barrier method of contraception during the study period. She is able to understand and provide written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She is not currently using any illicit drugs or alcohol. Her estimated creatinine clearance is greater than 40 ml per minute, and her serum aminotransferase levels are within normal limits. She does not have any history of pancreatitis or hepatitis. She has no other significant medical conditions that may affect the safety of the trial. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 35 year old male diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), which was discovered during routine medical check-up. He has no family history of HCM and has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain for the past three months. He has been prescribed medications to control his symptoms, but they have not been effective. He has been advised to undergo septal myectomy, a surgical procedure to remove a portion of the thickened heart muscle, to relieve his symptoms. He has been approached by researchers to participate in a genomic sequencing study to identify the potential genetic cause of his HCM. He is willing to provide informed consent and is interested in receiving the results of the secondary variant screen. He is not pregnant and does not have any other medical condition that would interfere with his participation in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with type 1 diabetes diagnosed at the age of 18. She has been treated with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion for the past 5 years and her HbA1c level is 7.2% (55 mmol/mol). She has no other chronic or acute diseases, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She lives a sedentary lifestyle, works as a graphic designer and consumes a Western-style diet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of polyphenol enriched extra-virgin olive oil on postprandial glycemia in patients with type 1 diabetes. She understands the study requirements and is willing to optimize her insulin therapy during the run-in period.

45 yo F with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, diagnosed 5 years ago, and BMI of 28, referred for a new study to optimize interval training in patients with Type 2 Diabetes. She has no history of smoking, eating disorder, or insulin dependence. The patient is currently treated with Metformin 500 mg BID and has good glycemic control with HbA1c of 6.5%. She reports moderate physical activity, including walking for 30 minutes most days of the week. She has no contraindication to increased physical activity. The patient is interested in participating in the study to learn about new strategies to optimize her physical activity and glycemic control. The patient is willing to undergo a mixed meal tolerance test after the interventions are completed.

The patient is a 35-year-old overweight Korean woman with a BMI of 26. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications or supplements. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the effect of Korean Red Ginseng on insulin sensitivity. She reports consuming a typical Korean diet high in rice, vegetables, and meat. She does not smoke or drink excessive amounts of alcohol. She works in an office and reports engaging in moderate physical activity such as walking and yoga for at least 30 minutes a day. She is willing to adhere to the study protocol, including taking the assigned capsules three times a day for 12 weeks, completing dietary and physical activity assessments, and attending all study visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of severe cardiomyopathy (EF <35%) diagnosed 4 years ago. He was implanted with a single-chamber ICD for primary prevention and has been following up regularly with his cardiologist. He has been experiencing palpitations and shortness of breath on exertion, which have been increasing in frequency and duration over the past year. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of syncope or sustained ventricular arrhythmias. The patient has given his informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to provide blood samples for genetic analysis.

56 yo M with a 40 pack-year smoking history and a diagnosis of stage II lung cancer being scheduled for a right thoracotomy. The patient has a history of mild hypertension controlled with lisinopril, and is otherwise healthy. Preoperative workup was unremarkable. The patient is a candidate for either an Erector Spinae Plane Block or Perioperative Intravenous Lidocaine for pain control following the procedure, and is willing to participate in the study. Past Medical History: - Hypertension, controlled with lisinopril - Stage II lung cancer

A 35-year-old male who received a 2-dose schedule of GSK Biologicals' hepatitis A vaccine 11 years ago is eligible for this study. He has no significant medical history and has not received any other hepatitis A vaccine since the primary vaccination. He is willing to donate blood samples at Years 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20 after the first vaccine dose of the primary vaccination course to determine his anti-hepatitis A (anti-HAV) antibody concentrations. He understands that if he becomes seronegative for anti-HAV antibodies during any of the long-term blood sampling time points, he will be offered an additional vaccine dose. He is willing to receive an additional vaccine dose and allow for blood samples to be taken to evaluate the immune response following this vaccination. He has signed the written informed consent before the blood sampling visit of each year.

65-year-old male who suffered a first unilateral ischemic brain injury 3 years ago and completed rehabilitation services 6 months ago. The patient can walk independently for at least 10 meters with a cane, but has low balance self-efficacy with an Activities-specific Balance Confidence scale score of 70. The patient is able to follow instructions and provide written informed consent. The patient has no additional medical, cardiovascular, orthopedic, or psychiatric conditions that would hinder proper treatment or assessment. The patient does not have receptive dysphasia or significant lower peripheral neuropathy. The patient is not involved in any other drug studies or clinical trials.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with asthma at the age of 12. She has a history of moderate to severe asthma and has been followed closely by a specialist clinic for the past 10 years. She is currently using a combination of inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists as her maintenance therapy. She has a history of multiple hospitalizations due to asthma exacerbations and has required oral corticosteroids multiple times in the past year. She works full time as a nurse in a hospital and has had to take time off work due to her asthma symptoms. She reports experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and coughing during asthma exacerbations. She has never smoked and has no other significant medical history. Her past medical history and family history are non-contributory. She has signed the consent form for research with the BD-Asthma registry and has agreed to participate in the indirect cost study.

The patient is a 16-year-old girl with a history of enteric hyperoxaluria and hyperoxalemia associated with Crohn's disease. She was diagnosed with Crohn's disease at the age of 11 and has been on medication for it since then. She has been experiencing recurrent episodes of kidney stones and has been on a low oxalate diet for the past 2 years. Despite the diet, she has urinary oxalate levels of 60mg/24h (normalized for body surface area). Her eGFR is 20 mL/min/1.73m2 and plasma oxalate is 8 µmol/L. She has been stable on her current medication regimen for the past 6 months. She is willing to discontinue Vitamin C supplementation for the duration of the study. She weighs 50 kg and is willing to administer ALLN-177 with each meal/snack 5 times per day for 12 consecutive weeks.

The patient is a 7-year-old child who lives in a rural area of a malaria-endemic country. The child has been experiencing fever, headache, and fatigue for the past 2 days. The child's parents report that the child has not been eating or drinking well, and has been increasingly lethargic. The child has no significant past medical history and has not received any treatment for malaria in the past. The child's temperature is 39.2°C (102.6°F). The physical exam is notable for mild splenomegaly, and no other abnormalities are noted. A blood smear is obtained, which confirms the diagnosis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria. The child is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history.

75 year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis and scheduled for elective hip replacement surgery in 5 days. He has reported occasional snoring and daytime sleepiness but has never sought medical attention for it. He denies any history of psychiatric disorders, drug or alcohol dependence, or neurological disorders. He is proficient in English and has a reading level of Grade 7. He is able to comprehend and complete study questionnaires. He has not had any prior diagnosis of sleep-related breathing disorder or CPAP treatment. He has no contraindications to CPAP face-mask and does not have significant cardiac disease. He has not had any myocardial infarction or cardiac surgery or percutaneous coronary interventions within the last 3 months. He is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent.

Patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) and anemia. The patient is currently undergoing treatment with an erythropoiesis stimulating agent (ESA) using a self-application system. The patient has been on the ESA treatment for at least 3 months and has a life expectancy of more than 9 months in the judgment of the attending physician. The patient's ferritin levels are greater than 200 mcg/L in accordance with the relevant guidelines. The patient is interested in participating in an observational study of MIRCERA to evaluate its efficiency, safety, and acceptance.

The patient is a 23-year-old male undergraduate student at the University of Houston. He has a history of binge drinking at least once a week for the past month. He identifies as a religious person and is interested in incorporating his religious beliefs into his efforts to reduce his alcohol consumption. He has not been diagnosed with any learning disabilities and is not currently enrolled in any treatment for alcohol or other substances.

The patient is a 58-year-old Caucasian woman who has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She has had a history of smoking for 25 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. She has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and coughing for the past 2 months. She underwent a CT scan, which revealed a mass in her right lung. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. She has already received one round of platinum-based chemotherapy, which did not show any significant improvement in her condition. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1. The laboratory tests show that she meets the criteria for the study. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent. She is a postmenopausal woman with no history of other cancers or significant weight loss

The patient is a 13-year-old male diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis. He has been experiencing persistent knee arthritis for the past six months, which has caused him significant pain and discomfort. The pain has been affecting his daily activities, and he has been unable to participate in physical activities, such as sports and running. The patient has no prior history of knee injections or allergies to Bupivacaine. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of genicular nerve block in treating juvenile idiopathic arthritis. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

A 28-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history presents for the Single and Multiple Ascending Dose Study of NGM120. He reports no history of allergies, dermatological, hepatic, renal, hematological, pulmonary, metabolic, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, neurological, or psychiatric disorders. His ECG findings are normal. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is currently not taking any medications.

A 45-year-old male with a BMI of 25 presents to the clinical trial site for participation in a Phase I open interaction study. He has no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug abuse. He reports no significant medical history and is currently not on any medications. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and provides written informed consent. The subject is in good general health, with no significant abnormalities noted on physical examination or laboratory tests. He is willing to abstain from any medication throughout the study and is willing to fast before the administration of midazolam. The subject is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the development of new drugs and to gain more knowledge about his own health.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) 3 years ago. She has been receiving treatment with rituximab and chlorambucil, but her disease has progressed to Binet stage C. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications besides those for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She reports feeling fatigued and experiencing night sweats. On physical examination, she has palpable lymph nodes in her neck and axillae. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2. Her laboratory results show elevated white blood cell count (150,000/mm3) and elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could offer her a potential treatment option for her CLL.

58 year old woman with a history of localized neuropathic pain in the lower back and right leg following a lumbar disc herniation five years ago. Pain is described as burning, shooting, and stabbing, with a score of 6 on the Neuropathic Pain Scale. She has failed first-line treatment with gabapentin and amitriptyline. The patient has not received any prior Qutenza® patch installations. She does not have any known allergies to Qutenza® components and has stable blood pressure. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is able to understand the proposed study. She is interested in participating in the study and does not have any legal protection measures in place. She is affiliated with a social security scheme and is willing to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old female with a 7-year history of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis who has experienced recurrent flare-ups despite treatment with mesalamine and corticosteroids. She experiences frequent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding, which significantly impact her quality of life. She is willing to learn and able to self-administer study drug and is aware of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial. She agrees to practice effective methods of contraception and has no history of colonic or rectal surgery other than hemorrhoid surgery or appendectomy. She has not been diagnosed with Crohn's disease, indeterminate colitis, microscopic colitis, or any other relevant conditions. She is not currently receiving total parenteral nutrition and has no history of malignancy.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who recently had a heart attack and was diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He is being evaluated for possible revascularization with a drug-eluting stent (DES). The patient has a stenosis of at least 50% in his major epicardial coronary arteries, including the left anterior descending artery (LAD), left circumflex artery (LCX), and/or right coronary artery (RCA). His target vessel size is greater than or equal to 2.5mm in visual estimation. The patient is able to verbally confirm his understanding of the risks, benefits, and treatment alternatives of receiving invasive physiologic or imaging evaluation and PCI with a DES, and he provides written informed consent prior to any study-related procedure. The patient does not have a known hypersensitivity or contraindication to Heparin, Aspirin, Clopidogrel, Prasugrel, Ticagrelor, or Contrast media. He does not have active pathologic bleeding, gastrointestinal or genitourinary major bleeding within the prior 3 months, or a history of bleeding diathesis, known coagulopathy, or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. The patient has no non-cardiac co-morbid conditions with a life expectancy of less than 1 year. The patient's target vessel is not totally occluded, and his target lesion is not located in a coronary arterial bypass graft or left main coronary artery stenosis greater than or equal to 50%. The patient is eligible for angiography-derived FFR and does not have ostial RCA greater than or equal to 50% stenosis, myocardial bridging, severe tortuosity, severe overlap, or poor image quality.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and stable angina. He complains of chest pain on exertion that resolves with rest. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He is referred for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for the treatment of his coronary artery disease. He has no history of bleeding disorders or internal bleeding. His platelet count is normal. He has no history of allergies to aspirin, clopidogrel bisulfate, and/or heparin. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with the specified follow-up evaluation. He provides written informed consent prior to the procedure using a form that is approved by the local Institutional Review Board.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who underwent a primary total knee arthroplasty due to severe osteoarthritis. She has a history of controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both well-managed with medication. She does not have any peripheral nerve neuropathy or psychiatric illness. She has no known allergies to lidocaine or ropivacaine. Her ASA score is 2. She has no known renal or hepatic dysfunction. She has not received chronic opioid therapy or NSAIDs in the last three months. She is able to use a patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) device. She has no evidence of genu valgum or infection at the injection site. She has given informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been on chronic hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to end stage renal disease. He has a history of hypertension and has been on long term antihypertensive medication. He has a good fistula flow rate and is currently undergoing hemodialysis thrice a week. He has been experiencing some minor bleeding during hemodialysis sessions and hence, his heparin dose has been reduced. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is able to understand the study design and follow the instructions provided. He is affiliated with the French social security system. His systolic blood pressure is consistently above 110 mmHg and his hemoglobin levels are within normal range. He does not have any documented thrombophilia and is not under anti-vitamin K medication. He does not have any severe diseases or ongoing research protocols. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has provided consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 29 year old man from a Somali community who frequently chews khat, with the intention to reduce or stop using it. He has no significant past medical history and no history of severe psychiatric disorders. He is currently employed and lives with his family in the community. He is motivated to participate in the study and willing to make changes to his khat use. He is able to understand and speak English fluently. He reports chewing khat several times a week for several hours at a time and is concerned about the negative effects on his health and relationships.

A 35-year-old male was diagnosed with HIV infection 2 months ago. He is currently asymptomatic and has no prior history of antiretroviral therapy. His CD4 count is 230 cells/mm3, and his viral load is 20,000 copies/ml. He is a college graduate who works as an accountant. He is single and lives alone. He is a non-smoker and doesn't use any illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol socially. The patient has no other medical problems or allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with the treatment. He is compliant and able to attend regular follow-up visits.

42-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild obesity. He was recently diagnosed with severe mitral regurgitation during a routine echocardiogram. He is currently asymptomatic and has no history of heart disease or heart surgery. He has good exercise tolerance and regularly engages in moderate physical activity. His left ventricular ejection fraction is 65% and his left ventricular end-systolic dimension is 40mm. He has no history of atrial fibrillation or pulmonary hypertension. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing early mitral valve repair versus watchful waiting.

The patient is a 60-year-old Chinese man who has a history of stable angina and has been experiencing chest pain for the past two months. He has a medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient has been on multiple medications for the management of his conditions, including aspirin, beta-blockers, statins and antidiabetic agents. The patient has undergone a coronary angiography which revealed a long lesion in his left anterior descending artery with a diameter stenosis of 80%. The patient is a suitable candidate for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) but he prefers a less invasive treatment option. The patient has been informed of the nature of the study, agrees to its provisions and has been provided written Notice of Informed Consent. The patient is willing to comply with specified follow-up evaluations. The patient has not participated in any other investigational drug or device study and does not have any medical condition that may interfere with his participation in the study. However, the patient has a history of contrast sensitivity, which can be adequately premedicated.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with lymphoma 6 months ago. He has undergone chemotherapy and is scheduled for a follow-up thoracic CT scan as part of his routine surveillance. He has no significant medical history and has not had any recent radiological exams. He has been informed about the clinical trial investigating dose reduction in thoracic CT and has given his consent to participate.

A 55-year-old female presented with pain and swelling at the base of her left thumb, which has been progressively worsening over the last year. She has a history of osteoarthritis and mild hypertension. She denied any history of alcohol or drug abuse. She reported no allergies to medications and denied any previous surgeries or serious medical conditions. Physical examination revealed tenderness and swelling at the base of the left thumb with a positive grind test. X-ray confirmed the diagnosis of trapeziometacarpal osteoarthritis of the thumb. The patient was scheduled for trapeziectomy surgery and was informed about the study aiming to assess the efficacy of non-opioid medication for pain control after surgery. She expressed interest in participating in the study and was pre-screened for eligibility. She meets the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. She was provided with a detailed explanation of the study and consented to participate. She was randomized to receive the combination of ibuprofen and acetaminophen for pain control after surgery. She is able to complete study forms and is scheduled for follow-up appointments to evaluate her pain levels and hand function.

A 51-year-old male patient presents with a complaint of shortness of breath and chest pain for the past 2 months. He has a history of asbestos exposure for 15 years while working as a construction worker. A chest X-ray showed pleural effusion, and a CT scan revealed diffuse pleural thickening and nodularity. A biopsy of the pleura confirmed the diagnosis of malignant pleural mesothelioma. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy, and his ECOG performance status is 1. His physical examination is significant for decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. Laboratory tests show adequate bone marrow reserve, with white blood cells of 5.5 × 10^9/L, neutrophils of 2.9 × 10^9/L, platelets of 180 × 10^9/L, and hemoglobin of 12.5 g/dL. His liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the study, and paraffin blocks of his biopsy sample will be tested for CD74 and VEGF expression before starting treatment with Pemetrexed/Platinum protocol.

A 55-year-old male presents with a painful rash on the right side of his chest. He reports that the pain started a few days before the rash appeared and has been progressively getting worse. He describes the pain as sharp, burning, and constant. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He takes metoprolol, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. Vital signs are reported as: blood pressure: 138/82 mm Hg, heart rate: 78 beats/min, respiratory rate: 16 breaths/min, and temperature: 37°C. The patient appears uncomfortable and is guarding his right side. On examination, there are grouped vesicles on an erythematous base located on the right side of his chest. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. The patient is diagnosed with shingles and is offered participation in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of pregabalin in reducing pain during shingles. The patient meets the eligibility criteria, except he is currently taking anticonvulsants for his diabetic neuropathy.

A 45-year-old woman who works in an office and spends long hours in front of a computer screen. She has been wearing soft contact lenses for over 10 years, and currently wears them 6 days a week. She has a spectacle add of +1.25D and a best-corrected distance visual acuity of 20/20 in each eye. She has no history of eye injury or surgery in the past 12 weeks, and is not currently enrolled in any other ophthalmic clinical trial. Her ocular and systemic health is normal, with no evidence of any abnormality or disease that might affect successful contact lens wear. She does not wear any lenses that are similar to the study products, and is willing to be fit into available study sphere powers (-1.00 to -5.00D). Her astigmatism is less than 1.00D. She is interested in trying new multifocal contact lenses that might improve her visual performance and comfort during long hours of computer work.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of joint pain, redness, and swelling for the past two years. He was previously diagnosed with gout based on his symptoms and high serum uric acid levels (9.5 mg/dL). He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He drinks alcohol occasionally, but not more than 2-3 drinks per week. He has no allergies and is not taking any other medications. He has no history of liver or kidney disease. His body mass index is 32 kg/m². He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of a new medication for gout treatment.

A 54-year-old Hispanic woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) for the past 10 years presented with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and was scheduled to undergo a deceased donor renal transplantation. Her medical history included hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetic retinopathy. She was also taking metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. Her blood glucose levels were not well-controlled despite treatment with metformin and insulin. Her hemoglobin A1c was 8.5%. On physical examination, she had no significant findings except for mild peripheral neuropathy. Her baseline serum creatinine was 4.2 mg/dL. She was deemed a suitable candidate for transplant and was enrolled in the clinical trial to test the impact of tight peri-operative glucose control on short term graft function. She provided informed consent and met all the inclusion criteria for the study. She was randomized to the study group and received an insulin infusion to achieve tight glycemic control during the peri-operative period. Post-transplant, her glucose control was left to the discretion of the primary team. The study aimed to evaluate the impact of tight glycemic control on poor initial graft function, wound infection, length of hospital stay, 30-day mortality, hypoglycemic episodes, and stroke. The primary endpoint was acute rejection at 90 days and graft survival/renal function at 3 months, 6 months, and then yearly.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with leukemia and is receiving chemotherapy treatment. She has been experiencing frequent nausea and vomiting after each chemotherapy session. Her parents are concerned about her quality of life and want to explore alternative methods to alleviate her discomfort. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. She is currently attending school and participating in extracurricular activities. She is excited to participate in a research study that could potentially help her and other children with cancer. The patient and her parents are fluent in English and are willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with moderate obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of 20. He has not received any treatment for OSA yet but is planned for continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment in the next few weeks. The patient has a history of hypertension but is currently well-controlled with medication and has not had any changes in his medication in the last 3 months. He is a non-smoker with no other significant medical history. The patient's BMI is 32, which falls within the eligibility criteria for the study. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about the effect of rocuronium on his hypoxic ventilatory response.

A 50-year-old male patient visited the clinic with chest pain that occurred at rest and lasted for more than 10 minutes. He has type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure that is well controlled with medication. He has never had a heart attack before. He is a smoker and has been smoking for the past 20 years. He has also had elevated cardiac proteins in his blood indicating acute coronary syndrome. He is willing and able to give informed consent. He has not had any prior heart surgery (PCI) within the previous 2 weeks before randomizing in the trial. He has no ECG findings that make the Holter monitor for ischemia unable to read.

A 30-year-old female, who works as a software engineer, has been experiencing moderate stress at work due to a tight deadline for a project. She finds herself feeling anxious and overwhelmed with her workload. She has a BMI of 24 and no medical history of significant hypertensive, hepatic, renal, pulmonary, gastro-intestinal, endocrinological, neurologic, haematological, or psychiatric disease. She does not smoke, and she drinks alcohol occasionally. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is using effective contraception. She has normal vision and is not on any regular medication/supplements. She is interested in participating in the study and has not previously participated in a stress study involving the Trier Social Stress Test.

A 55 year old male with a history of smoking and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) Gold stage III is being considered for pulmonary rehabilitation. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but is currently well controlled on medications. He reports dyspnea with minimal exertion and has difficulty performing daily activities. He has never used electrical stimulation before and has no history of recent lumbar surgery or skin lesions. He is not currently experiencing an acute exacerbation of COPD. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at improving his exercise capacity and reducing his dyspnea during exercise.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy who is scheduled for elective tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy due to recurrent tonsillitis and sleep apnea. He has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA I. His parents have given their informed written consent for his participation in the clinical trial. He has no known cognitive impairment, chronic pain, or use of analgesic drugs, and there is no family history of malignant hyperthermia. He is currently not taking any medications and has no history of kidney, liver, pulmonary, or cardiac disease. The boy is accompanied by his parents, who are both supportive of his participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a diagnosis of severe hemophilia A. He has a history of frequent spontaneous joint bleeds, and has been receiving prophylactic treatment with a factor replacement product not designed to have a prolonged half-life. He has had at least 100 prior exposure days (EDs) to factor replacement products. His most recent factor level was 5%, and he has not developed any inhibitors to date. The patient reports that he experiences significant pain and discomfort during joint bleeds, which negatively impacts his ability to work and participate in activities of daily living. He has also incurred significant medical costs related to his hemophilia treatment, including factor replacement products, medical appointments, and imaging studies. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of prophylactic treatment with rFVIIIFc and rFIXFc therapy in reducing his treatment burden and improving his health economic outcomes while maintaining disease control.

A 67-year-old woman presented to the clinic with decreased vision in her right eye, which she noticed a week ago. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and underwent cataract surgery in both eyes 2 years ago. On examination, her visual acuity was 20/20 in the left eye and 20/200 in the right eye. Fundus examination showed retinal detachment with proliferative vitreoretinopathy in the right eye. She underwent pars plana vitrectomy with Brilliant Blue G-Assisted internal limiting membrane peeling using a 3D visualization system at the Department of Retina of Centro Oftalmologico Dr Charles, Buenos Aires-Argentina. The surgery was performed by a single experienced vitreoretinal surgeon. Her follow-up period was 14 months, during which her visual acuity improved to 20/40 in the right eye. She did not experience any complications related to the surgery. She is eligible for the clinical trial as she is older than 18 years of age and suffered from retinal detachment with proliferative vitreoretinopathy and underwent primary PPV at the Department of Retina of Centro Oftalmologico Dr Charles, Buenos Aires-Argentina between January 1, 2016 and August 1, 2020.

This clinical trial does not involve patients and is focused on implementing strategies to increase the utilization of medications for alcohol use disorder among health professionals working on the general medicine services at Yale New Haven Hospital. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this trial.

A 32-year-old woman has been trying to conceive with her husband for over a year without success. She has regular menstrual cycles and has confirmed ovulation with home ovulation kits. Her husband has no known fertility issues. She has not been diagnosed with any endocrine diseases and is not taking any NSAIDs or corticosteroids. She has not experienced any uterine bleeding. HSG results confirmed that she does not have tubal occlusion.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who has been trying to conceive with his partner for over a year with no success. He has been previously diagnosed with azoospermia, and his doctor has recommended him for a clinical trial to examine the possible connection between HPV and reduced sperm production. The patient has no previous history of genital warts or other sexually transmitted infections. He is in good health, with no history of testicular abnormalities or medical conditions that may affect fertility. The patient understands the purpose and possible consequences of the study and is willing to participate.

A 56-year-old female patient was diagnosed with locally advanced pancreatic cancer after experiencing abdominal pain and weight loss for several months. A CT scan confirmed the diagnosis and multidisciplinary team discussion led to the patient being deemed ineligible for surgery. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80 and is otherwise healthy. The tumor size is 3.5 cm in maximum diameter, and there is no evidence of lymph node metastasis. The patient has received 4 months of FOLFIRINOX chemotherapy and has responded well to treatment. A baseline CT scan was performed 1 month ago. The patient is able to maintain the set-up position during RT and is willing to participate in the clinical trial after being informed of the study-specific informed consent form.

65-year-old female with a diagnosis of refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts and anemia with hemoglobin <110g/L. She requires at least 1 unit packed red blood cell transfusions every 28 days. She has a life expectancy of >7 months and is unlikely to proceed to bone marrow or stem cell transplantation therapy following remission. She has serum bilirubin levels less than or equal to 1.5 times the upper limit of the normal range for the laboratory, serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase (aspartate aminotransferase) and serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (alanine aminotransferase) levels less than or equal to 2 x ULN, and serum creatinine levels less than or equal to 1.5 x ULN. She has not received prior treatment with azacitidine or had any prior history of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). She has no history of malignant or metastatic disease within the previous 12 months or uncorrected red cell folate deficiency or vitamin B12 deficiency. She has not been treated with radiation, chemotherapy, or cytotoxic therapy for non-MDS conditions in the previous 12 months. She has no known or suspected hypersensitivity to azacitidine or mannitol, no prior transplantation or cytotoxic therapy to treat MDS, and no serious medical illness likely to limit survival to less than or equal to 7 months. She has not been treated with androgenic hormones during the previous 14 days and has no active viral infection with known human immunodeficiency virus or viral hepatitis Type B or C. She has not been treated with other investigational drugs with the previous 30 days.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy female with a normal body weight and height (BMI < 30). She has no history of metabolic or gastrointestinal disease and is not allergic to soy. She does not use vitamin supplements containing vitamin K and is not receiving any systemic or topical treatment likely to interfere with the study parameters. She is not receiving corticoϊd treatment or using oral anticoagulants. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the optimal dose of vitamin K2 for improved bone and vascular health. She is willing to consume the indicated amount of capsules once daily with either breakfast or dinner for a period of 12 weeks. The patient is available for blood sample collections at the indicated time points during the study.

A 32-year-old female office worker has been experiencing recurrent vaginal itching and burning for the past six months. She has been diagnosed with vulvo-vaginal candidiasis by her gynecologist and has been treated with fluconazole multiple times. She reports that her symptoms alleviate after treatment but recur within a few weeks. She is sexually active with her partner who has no history of genital infections. She is not pregnant or nursing and does not plan to conceive in the near future. She is in good health with no significant medical history. She is not taking any medication or dietary supplements. She is aware of the study requirements and is willing to comply with the protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who reports a history of knee pain and stiffness which has been ongoing for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with grade 2 osteoarthritis of the knee based on a prior radiograph. She has tried non-pharmacological interventions such as weight loss, physical therapy, and using knee braces, but these have not provided significant relief. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. She has no known allergies to any medications, including lidocaine or hyaluronate. She has not had any recent knee injections, and her skin is free of any localized infections at the planned site of injection. She is willing and able to complete a follow-up phone call three months after the injection.

A 25-year-old woman in her first pregnancy is seeking analgesia for labor pain. She is currently at 39 weeks of gestation and has a singleton pregnancy. The patient has spontaneous onset of labor with cervical dilatation of 3cm. She has no history of medical disorders or allergies to paracetamol. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of drug abuse. She has not received any other kind of analgesia before recruitment in the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

A 50-year-old female patient with a history of aneurysm in the middle cerebral artery presents with recurrent headaches and dizziness. She has a past medical history of hypertension and dyslipidemia. The patient is currently on multiple medications including aspirin, lisinopril and atorvastatin. She has been referred to the neuro-angiography suite for endovascular treatment. The patient is able to provide informed consent or has a legally authorized representative who can provide informed consent. She has no significant allergies or contraindications to intra-arterial contrast medium. The patient will be asked to participate in the study and undergo an extra C-arm computed tomography (CACT) scan in addition to the standard-of-care CACT scans while receiving standard treatment.

The patient is a 35 year old Hispanic male who presented to the clinic with fatigue, bruising, and bleeding gums. He reported a history of recurrent infections in the past few months. A complete blood count (CBC) was ordered and showed a low platelet count and high white blood cell count. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). He has no significant past medical history, and he is currently working as an accountant. He is married with two children and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is in good physical condition, and his performance status is 90%. His echocardiogram showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 55%, and his baseline ECG showed a QTc of 480 msec.
