His creatinine clearance is 80 mL/min, his bilirubin level is within normal limits, and his AST and ALT levels are slightly elevated. He is not pregnant or nursing, and his wife is using contraception. He has not received any prior treatment for APL, and he has no other concurrent active malignancy or serious medical condition that would exclude him from the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with inoperable pancreatic cancer with obstructive jaundice. He has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice for several weeks. Imaging studies confirmed the diagnosis, and he has been deemed ineligible for surgery by the multidisciplinary team. He has not undergone any previous treatment for pancreatic cancer. He has no significant medical history, and his physical exam is unremarkable except for the jaundice. His lab tests show platelets at 120 x 109 mm3, INR at 1.2, and no evidence of portal vein thrombosis. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and undergo ERCP.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia in the chronic phase. He was initially diagnosed with the disease after experiencing fatigue, unexplained weight loss, and shortness of breath. His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. He has no history of cardiac insufficiency or coronary artery disease. The patient has an HLA-matched unrelated donor available for stem cell transplantation. He is willing to undergo treatment with fludarabine and busulfan followed by peripheral stem cell transplant and GVHD prophylaxis comprising antithymocyte globulin, tacrolimus, and methotrexate. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is using effective contraception.

This is a 42-year-old male with a history of total deafness. He has been using sign language and lip reading as his primary means of communication for most of his life. He has been considering a cochlear implant for some time now and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves local anesthesia with sedation during the surgery. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is excited about the possibility of being able to hear again and is looking forward to the procedure. He understands the risks and benefits of the local anesthesia with sedation approach and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 15-year-old girl who has been experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of hopelessness, loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy, and difficulty sleeping. She has been referred to a therapist by her school counselor and has agreed to undergo psychotherapy. The patient has no history of psychiatric hospitalization or self-harm behaviors. She is currently not taking any psychiatric medications and has no known medical conditions that would interfere with therapy. The patient speaks English fluently and can provide informed consent.

The patient is a 56 year old man diagnosed with chronic kidney disease who has been on hemodialysis for the past 8 months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but his blood pressure and lipid levels are currently well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His recent laboratory results show a hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, serum creatinine level of 8.9 mg/dL, serum calcium level of 9.2 mg/dL, and serum phosphate level of 6.5 mg/dL. He has been experiencing occasional chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity for the past few weeks. His electrocardiogram (ECG) shows no signs of acute myocardial infarction, but a coronary tomography reveals a coronary calcium score of 20 Agatston units. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of phytomenadione on coronary artery calcification in hemodialysis patients, and is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits. He has no known allergies to vitamin K and has not received any previous or current treatment with phytomenadione.

A 15 year old girl comes to the clinic with her mother for a routine check-up. She is overweight and her mother is concerned about her health. The girl has been struggling with her weight for some time and has tried various diets, but nothing seems to work. She is otherwise healthy and has no medical history to indicate any underlying conditions that may affect her growth hormone or insulin secretion. She is not on any medications that could interfere with the study. The girl is willing to participate in the study and undergo the necessary procedures. She understands that the study aims to understand the relationship between hormonal changes, body composition, and insulin resistance in overweight and normal weight adolescent girls. She is also willing to comply with the dietary restrictions and test meals to be provided during the study.

A 25-year-old woman presents for enrollment in a clinical trial to assess the bioavailability of a new oral disintegrating tablet formulation of sildenafil. She is in good health with no significant medical history. Her physical examination is unremarkable and her weight is within the eligible range for the trial. She has no history of drug allergies or any other clinically significant hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease. She has no evidence of substance abuse or dependence, with a negative urine drug screen. She is currently not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications. She is interested in potentially participating in the trial and is willing to comply with all study procedures and requirements.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC) that has progressed after first-line standard therapy that was not irinotecan-based. He is currently experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication, and a smoking history of 20 pack-years. He has no history of other significant medical conditions. His lab results show adequate organ and bone marrow function, with a hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL, a WBC count of 4.5 x 10^9/L, an ANC of 2.0 x 10^9/L, and a platelet count of 130 x 10^9/L. His serum creatinine, AST and alkaline phosphatase, and total bilirubin levels are within normal limits. He is willing to use effective contraception while on treatment and for 3 months after the end of treatment. He has signed an informed consent form and an IRB-approved ICF before undergoing any study-specific procedures or tests. He has not received chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, RT, minor surgery, or any investigational agent within 4 weeks before study enrollment. He has not received nitrosoureas, mitomycin C, immunotherapy, biological therapy, or major surgery within 6 weeks before study enrollment. He has never received first-line therapy for CRC that was irinotecan-based. He does not have a history of myocardial infarction, severe/unstable angina pectoris, coronary/peripheral artery bypass graft, NYHA class III or IV congestive heart failure, cerebrovascular accident or transient ischemic attack, pulmonary embolism or other clinically significant thromboembolic event, or clinically significant pulmonary disease. He does not have clinically active brain metastasis, an uncontrolled seizure disorder, spinal cord compression, or carcinomatous meningitis. He has not been diagnosed with any malignancy other than CRC within the past 5 years. He has no clinically significant active infection that requires antibiotic therapy or HIV-positive status receiving antiretroviral therapy. He has never received previous treatment with CS-1008, other agonistic DRSantibodies, or with TRAIL agonists. He is not known to be homozygous for the UGT1A1*28 allele, and his Kras allele status is not wild type. He does not have Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) deficiency.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy with a history of severe chronic plaque psoriasis for the past 2 years. He has tried several topical treatments, including corticosteroids, with limited success. He currently has a PASI score of 25, an IGA score of 4, and total body surface area affected of 20%. He has not received any systemic or UV therapy to treat his psoriasis. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He is not currently taking any medications. His parents are supportive of his participation in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his psoriasis.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing dyspnea and dry cough for the past year. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. Chest imaging revealed interstitial lung disease, and further evaluation led to the diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). His current treatment includes oxygen therapy and pulmonary rehabilitation. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who works as an accountant. She is married and has two children, ages 6 and 8. She is generally in good health and has no significant medical history. She exercises regularly and has a healthy diet, but has been struggling to lose the last few pounds of weight. She does not smoke or use any drugs, and does not consume more than two cups of coffee or tea per day. She is interested in participating in the study as she is curious about the potential effects of tea extract on her lipid metabolism. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is practicing a reliable method of contraception. She has not participated in any other clinical studies or received any investigational drugs in the past 90 days. Her BMI is 25.5 kg/m^2, which falls within the study's eligibility range.

A 45-year-old male patient who was recently diagnosed with pheochromocytoma and is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic adrenalectomy. The patient has a history of hypertension and occasional episodes of palpitations and headaches. He is currently taking medication for his blood pressure but has reported no significant improvement in his symptoms. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no major comorbidities. The patient has provided informed consent and has agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old female with a diagnosis of noninfectious intermediate uveitis of at least 3 months duration. She is currently taking greater than or equal to 20 mg/day of Prednisone as well as other immunosuppressive drugs. Despite the treatment, she still experiences occasional flare-ups of her uveitis symptoms including blurred vision, eye pain and redness. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) by ETDRS protocol is better than or equal to 20/200. She has an intraocular pressure of 24 mmHg or less and anterior chamber cells and vitreous haze of less than or equal to 1. She has no history of Retisert treatment and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not increased her systemic immunosuppressive treatment regimen within 6 weeks before baseline.

The patient is a 60-year-old female who was diagnosed with locally advanced adenocarcinoma of NSCLC. She has no history of smoking or any other significant medical history. The patient has signed and dated written informed consent and is eligible for treatment with Vargatef®. The patient has undergone diagnosis and/or re-biopsy before the initiation of the first line treatment and has available fixed and paraffin embedded (FPE) tumor tissue (minimum of 10 slides and up to 20 slides if possible at 5µm thickness). The patient has no contraindication to Vargatef® or docetaxel as specified in their respective labels. The patient has not initiated Vargatef® more than 7 days prior to inclusion in this NIS and is not participating simultaneously in a clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of hypercholesterolemia and documented coronary artery disease (CAD). He has been undergoing chronic fortnightly LDL-apheresis treatment for the past year. He is a non-smoker and has no history of diabetes or hypertension. His current medications include atorvastatin and aspirin. He has a family history of heart disease with his father having had a myocardial infarction at the age of 60. He is currently asymptomatic and has no complaints. His most recent lipid panel revealed a total cholesterol level of 275 mg/dL and an LDL cholesterol level of 190 mg/dL. He has given his informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 30-year-old male diagnosed with bipolar disorder has been taking aripiprazole for the past 1 year. He has a history of two manic episodes in the past, the last one being 18 months ago. He is currently stable on aripiprazole 15mg per day. He has no history of cardiac disease or any other major medical illnesses. He smokes 5-6 cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no family history of cardiac disease. He has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the heart rate changes in bipolar patients under the medication of aripiprazole and quetiapine. He understands the procedure of the study and is willing to cooperate for evaluating heart rate changes. He has no intention of quitting the study without any conditions.

A 6-year-old girl presents to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital with a cough, runny nose, and fever for the past 3 days. She reports feeling tired and having mild difficulty breathing. Her mother reports that her symptoms started with a sore throat and have progressed to include coughing and nasal congestion. She has no significant past medical history and is up to date on her vaccinations. She lives with her parents and younger sister, who have not had any recent illnesses. Upon examination, she has a temperature of 101.5°F, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 96% on room air. Lung auscultation is notable for mild wheezing bilaterally. The treating physician orders a nasopharyngeal swab for respiratory virus testing. The patient is eligible for inclusion in the study and provided informed consent is obtained from the parents.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing seasonal allergic rhinitis symptoms for the past few years. She reports nasal congestion, sneezing, and itchy and watery eyes during the pollen season. She is otherwise healthy and has a BMI of 22. She has a positive skin prick test for timothy and birch allergens and a sufficient reaction to nasally administered allergen at screening. She has not received anti-allergy immunotherapy in the past two years and does not have a history of asthma. She occasionally uses over-the-counter analgesics and has not ingested grapefruit or herbal remedies that may affect the enzyme CYP3A4. She does not smoke and has no significant laboratory findings. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using adequate birth control. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

52 y/o male with a recent diagnosis of follicular lymphoma, Grade II, who has previously received one regimen of chemotherapy with partial response but developed recurrent lymphoma. Patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. Lab results show an absolute neutrophil count of 1800 cells/mm3 and a platelet count of 120,000 cells/mm3. Patient has adequate renal and hepatic function. CT scan shows a bi-dimensionally measurable disease with one lesion measuring 2.5 x 2.5 cm. Patient is negative for HAMA. Patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is 18 years of age or older. The patient has not received more than one course of rituximab and does not have involvement of more than 25% of intratrabecular marrow. The patient has not received prior radioimmunotherapy, has no history of another malignancy, is not pregnant or nursing, and does not have ascites or hydronephrosis. The patient has not received previous non-human monoclonal antibody therapy and has not failed stem cell harvest.

The patient is a 45-year-old African American male who is currently admitted to the hospital due to chest pain. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He complains of sharp chest pain that started suddenly about 3 hours ago. The pain is located in the center of his chest and radiates to his left arm. He rates the pain as 8 out of 10 in severity. He denies any shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting or dizziness. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, temperature of 98.6°F, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. His electrocardiogram shows no significant changes. He is not taking any medication for his hypertension or high cholesterol. His medical history is also positive for smoking for the past 20 years. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in this study and agrees to remain under observation until all study procedures are completed.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease. She has a history of hypertension, osteoarthritis, and hypercholesterolemia. She lives with her husband and their adult son who provides most of her care. She has completed Study BN29552 or BN29553 and has completed the Week 105 visit. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and complete all aspects of the study, including MRI, lumbar puncture (if applicable), and PET imaging (if applicable). She has adequate visual and auditory acuity to perform neuropsychological testing. She is using a protocol-approved contraceptive method and is willing to remain abstinent from heterosexual intercourse for at least 8 weeks after the last dose. She has not had any recurrent symptomatic ARIA-E events or exacerbations of previous events. She does not have any intracranial lesions that could potentially increase the risk of CNS bleeding. She is not at risk of suicide in the opinion of the investigator. She has not had alcohol and/or substance abuse or dependence within the past 2 years and during the study. She is not pregnant or lactating, or intending to become pregnant during the study. She does not have any other severe or unstable medical condition that could put her at special risk, bias the assessment of her clinical or mental status to a significant degree, or interfere with her ability to complete the study assessments. She is not using chronic anticoagulants or participating in any other investigational drug treatment trial.

The patient is a 64-year-old man who has been diagnosed with muscle-invasive bladder cancer. The patient's past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. The patient has undergone several imaging studies, including CT scans and MRIs, which have confirmed the presence of a bladder tumor. The patient has been advised to undergo radical cystectomy with urinary diversion (ileal conduit). The patient has been referred to the Department of Urology at Bern University Hospital for the surgery. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the optimal duration of perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis (PAP) in radical cystectomy. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with major depressive disorder two years ago. She has been on medication, but has not experienced significant relief from her symptoms. She reports feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and lack of motivation. She also has difficulty sleeping and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore potential alternative treatments for her depression. She has no metal in her eyes or head and is not claustrophobic. She is able to lie flat and has no history of brain injury. She is not pregnant.

A 52-year-old man with a history of HIV infection, currently on antiretroviral therapy, presents with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of smoking, but quit 10 years ago. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or prior cardiac events. His most recent CD4 count was 350 cells/mm3. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of an imaging agent, 99mTc-tilmanocept, to assess macrophage-specific inflammation in individuals with HIV compared to those without HIV. He is willing to undergo SPECT/CT scanning and other necessary tests to evaluate immune activation and cardiovascular disease parameters. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no history of severe allergies or contraindications to the study procedures.

Pt is a 25yo South Asian F with no significant past medical history, no allergies, and a non-smoker. Her BMI is 23. She is physically active and able to walk continuously for one hour. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effect of prior walking on postprandial metabolism and endothelial function in healthy South Asian and White European women. She is able to attend the laboratory for preliminary assessments and familiarisation with the study procedures. She is able to fast overnight for 10 hours before attending the laboratory on day 2 of the trial. She is not taking any medication that might influence fat metabolism or blood glucose. She has no history of muscle or bone injuries that would prevent her from walking on a treadmill. She is willing to consume a high-fat breakfast and lunch on day 2 of the trial and to have venous blood samples and endothelial function measurements taken throughout the day.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (stage II Hoehn and Yahr). He is currently taking levodopa and carbidopa, with only partial improvement in his motor symptoms. His daily caffeine intake is estimated to be less than 100 mg per day. He is able to understand the consent process and is willing to participate in the study. The patient does not have dementia, with an MMSE score of 29/30. He has no history of uncontrolled hypertension, lithium or clozapine use, active peptic ulcer disease, or supraventricular cardiac arrhythmia. The patient has not previously experienced adverse reactions to caffeine.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with intracranial hemorrhage (ICH). He is currently hospitalized and receiving treatment for his condition. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is alert and oriented, with no signs of dementia. He is interested in participating in this study to help advance the understanding and diagnosis of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), which is a common cause of ICH in the elderly. He is willing to undergo neuro-psychological examinations, genetic and biochemical markers test, MRI and PET imaging. He has no allergies to contrast mediums or previous history of aneurysm clipping. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is married and has two adult children. He is a retired engineer who enjoys reading and gardening. He is willing to participate in the study to help improve the diagnosis and prognosis for patients with CAA.

A 32-year-old male who fell off his bike and landed on his shoulder resulting in a clavicle fracture. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He is scheduled for clavicle surgery under general anesthesia. He has no history of bleeding diathesis, is not receiving anticoagulant treatment, and has no known allergies to local anesthetics or opioids. He does not have any skin infections at the site of the needle puncture. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has been informed about the study and has provided consent to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort, bloating, and irregular periods for the past few months. She has no significant medical history but has a family history of breast cancer. She underwent a pelvic ultrasound which revealed a mass in her ovary. Her doctor has recommended further imaging to determine the nature of the mass. The patient is alert and oriented with no significant physical exam findings. She is otherwise healthy and well-nourished. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the most accurate imaging modality for locating ovarian cancer tumors. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate is >30, and she has no known allergies to gadolinium. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is eligible to undergo laparoscopic evaluation for resectability.

This is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (including nasopharynx) that is considered incurable with surgery or radiation therapy. She has bidimensionally measurable disease and no uncontrolled CNS metastases. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and her absolute neutrophil count is at least 1,500/mm3 and platelet count is at least 100,000/mm3. Her bilirubin is no greater than 1.5 mg/dL, creatinine is no greater than 1.5 mg/dL, and creatinine clearance is at least 60 mL/min. She has no history of hypercalcemia or ventricular arrhythmias or symptomatic bradyarrhythmia. She has no significant detectable infection and no other active malignancies. She has recovered from any prior major surgery, prior interleukin-2, interferons, and monoclonal antibodies. She had prior paclitaxel infusion no greater than 24 hours for recurrent or metastatic disease. She is not pregnant or nursing and uses effective contraception. She is eligible to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of paclitaxel in treating patients with recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck.

12-year-old male with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, diagnosed at the age of 6. He has been treated with glucocorticoids for the past 9 months due to high disease activity. His growth velocity is below the 25th percentile and he has short stature. He has not been treated with growth hormone before and has no endocrinopathy or other chronic diseases. His bone age is 9 and his growth hormone levels after stimulation with clonidine were above 10 ng/ml. He is prepubertal and has no history of malignancy, chromosomal aberration or syndromal disease. He has not been previously treated with Oxandrolone and was not small for gestational age. His fasting glucose level is within normal limits.

A 27 year old woman with type 1 diabetes mellitus comes to the clinic for a routine check-up. She has been receiving insulin therapy for the last 5 years with no prior history of switching between insulin products or between CSII and MDI. Her recent HbA1c value is 8.5% with a fasting blood C-peptide level of 0.5 ng/mL. Her body mass index is 25.5 kg/m2. She has no history of proliferative retinopathy, severe hypoglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis, or any other chronic disease requiring the continuous use of corticosteroids, immunosuppressants, etc. She has never participated in a clinical study or post marketing study of ASP1941 (ipragliflozin) or any other SGLT2 inhibitor. She has no history of drug addiction, alcohol abuse, or psychiatric disorder that would make her inappropriate for participation in the study. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ASP1941 in combination with insulin for the treatment of type 1 diabetes mellitus.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who recently fell while walking her dog and sustained a distal radius fracture in her right wrist. She is right-hand dominant and is experiencing pain and difficulty using her hand for daily activities such as writing, cooking, and dressing. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is able to communicate fluently in Dutch and has no known difficulties with motor imagery. She lives alone in her own apartment and is able to perform all activities of daily living independently. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve her wrist function and reduce pain.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing irregular menstrual cycles and weight gain. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) based on the Rotterdam criteria. She has a history of acne and excess facial hair growth. She has not been taking any antidiabetic medication in the past one month. She does not have any history of thyroid diseases or other endocrine diseases. She has no history of acute or chronic infection, severe cardio-cerebrovascular diseases, or acute/chronic pancreatitis. She is not taking any letrozole, clomiphene, oral contraceptive, glucocorticoid, gonadotropin, gonadotropin releasing hormone agonist, anti-androgen drug or other drugs for PCOS in the past three months. She does not have a history of recurrent urinary tract infection or malignant tumor. She has not participated in any weight loss programs or undergone any gastrointestinal surgery in the past three months. She has normal liver and kidney function. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant within the next six months. She is willing to give informed consent and comply with the protocol.

The patient is a 27-year-old Chinese woman who is in a stable relationship and wishes to use a contraceptive method to prevent pregnancy. She has no history of any significant medical conditions, and her menstrual cycle is regular. She has never used hormonal contraception before and is interested in trying either Yasmin or Marvelon. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements and has no known allergies. She has a BMI within the normal range and does not smoke or consume alcohol excessively. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to attend all scheduled visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia one year ago. He has been on antipsychotic medications for the past 8 months with no significant improvement in his negative symptoms. He is right-handed and has no history of seizures, epilepsy, severe head injury, or implantation of a cardiac pacemaker or any other electronic devices. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent.

A 45 year old female presents with a large mass on her thigh that has been growing for the past 6 months. She reports significant pain and difficulty walking due to the size of the mass. Imaging studies reveal a soft tissue sarcoma, and a biopsy confirms the diagnosis. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and weighs 68 kg. She has no previous history of anthracycline treatment or participation in another clinical study with an investigational product in the past 2 weeks. She has not received any anticancer therapy in the past 14 days and has no concurrent chemotherapy, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment within 14 days prior to entering the study. She has no history of allogenic organ transplantation and no active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to employ effective birth control during the study period. She agrees to participate in the study and is able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study including undergoing treatment and scheduled visits and examinations including follow up.

32-year-old female patient presents with a non-vital mandibular premolar with no significant past medical history. The tooth has been asymptomatic but has a small periapical radiolucency on an X-ray. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any allergies to penicillin. She has not taken any antibiotics during the past two weeks preoperatively. The patient reports no history of bruxism or clenching. The tooth has possible restorability and has not undergone any previous endodontic treatment. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial and is randomized into the experimental group. She is provided with a pain scale chart to record her pain level before any intervention. The tooth is anesthetized, accessed and mechanical instrumentation is performed. The canals are thoroughly irrigated using a 3 ml syringe of 2.5% Sodium hypochlorite between every subsequent instrument. XP Endo finisher is used after the last instrument in preparation. Obturation is done, and postoperative instructions are given to the patient. The patient will be followed up to assess postoperative pain and flare-ups.

A 35-year-old male with a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis for the past 4 years with an Expanded Disability Status Scale of 4.5. He is currently able to walk independently without assistance for 200 meters. He had no relapse within the last three months and has not received intensive rehabilitation in the last six months. He is on a stable dose of medication for the past six months. He has no complicating medical condition or orthopedic diagnosis that limits rehabilitation. He has no cardiac or respiratory disease that may interfere with endurance training. He has signed the information and informed consent and is affiliated with social security. He is working full time as a data analyst and has a supportive family.

The patient is a 28-year-old, right-handed male with no history of neurological disorders or traumatic brain injury. He has never been diagnosed with any DSM-V disorder and is not currently taking any psychoactive medications. The patient has normal cognition and is fluent in English. He is willing and able to give informed consent and follow study procedures. The patient has never had an MRI scan before and does not have any implanted devices, such as an aneurysm clip or cardiac pacemaker. He has not had a history of stroke, epilepsy, or brain scarring. Additionally, the patient has not used any psychoactive medications recently and is willing and able to abstain from medications that could reduce the seizure threshold to TMS as determined by the principal investigator. Overall, the patient is in good health and an optimal candidate for this study.

He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for six months. He is willing to use a medically acceptable method of contraception during the trial. He has given written informed consent and is eager to participate in the study.

35 yo male veteran with a history of multiple deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan presents with symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) including flashbacks, nightmares, and hypervigilance. The patient has tried multiple antidepressant medications without significant improvement in symptoms. The patient reports feeling hopeless and is concerned about the impact of PTSD on his daily life and relationships. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options and improve his quality of life. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and does not have a history of severe head injury or current high risk for suicide.

The patient is a 55-year-old African American woman who has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She presents with chest pain that started about 2 weeks ago. The pain is located in the mid-chest and radiates to her left arm. She describes the pain as a pressure sensation, which is worse with exertion and relieved with rest. She denies any shortness of breath, palpitations, or diaphoresis. The patient has been taking amlodipine and atorvastatin for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia, respectively, for about 2 years with no significant side effects. She has a family history of coronary artery disease in her father and brother. The physical exam is unremarkable except for a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg. The ECG shows ST depression in leads V1-V4. The patient is referred to Kettering Medical Center for PET myocardial perfusion imaging with or without CTA and/or coronary flow reserve measurement as part of her workup.

36 yo female with a BMI of 45 who has struggled with obesity for several years. She has tried multiple diets and exercise routines but has not been successful in losing weight. She has recently been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, which has further motivated her to seek bariatric surgery. She is able to provide written informed consent and has a good understanding of the purpose of the study. She does not have any cognitive impairment. She is scheduled to undergo an elective bariatric surgery and is willing to participate in the study to help improve patient outcomes after bariatric surgery.

A 56-year-old female patient with multiple myeloma after primary treatment is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She speaks fluent German and has no language barriers to follow the study procedures. She has been cleared by her cardiologist and internal medicine specialist for exercise. She has no musculoskeletal issues that would hinder her physical trainability. She is mentally stable and has no severe mental illness. She is interested in maintaining her independence and quality of life and hopes that regular physical training will help her achieve this goal. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the individualized training program. She is open to bringing her training partner along to ensure her safety during training sessions.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with advanced non-uveal melanoma, diagnosed six months ago. He has unresectable stage III disease and has previously received an approved PD-1 inhibitor for treatment, but experienced disease progression. He has BRAF mutations and is refractory to approved BRAF-based therapy. He presents with fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss. He has no history of autoimmune disease, active infections, or cardiac disease. His past medical history is non-significant. His family history is significant for melanoma in his paternal grandfather. He is currently not receiving any systemic steroids or other immunosuppressive therapies. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend specified treatment schedules.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) three years ago. He has been treated with imatinib and dasatinib in the past but has not responded well to either of the medications. His most recent bone marrow biopsy showed that he still has a high level of leukemic cells. He is now being considered for treatment with bosutinib as a last resort. The patient has no known history of hypersensitivity to any medications. He has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of the drug and has provided informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits. The patient is not currently pregnant, and he will use contraception during the study period as advised by the study team.

25 year old healthy male who is fluent in Danish and has no history of neurological, psychiatric or severe somatic diseases. He is not taking any medications that can influence the results of the study and has no contraindications for magnetic resonance scanning. He does not have any allergies to the medications used in the study and has not participated in any studies with radioactivity over the past year. He is willing to undergo PET scans and is available for the duration of the study.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes presents to the clinic complaining of difficulty controlling her blood sugar levels despite being compliant with her medication regimen that includes exenatide, metformin, and a sulfonylurea. Her most recent hemoglobin A1C level was 8.5%. She has not used insulin on a regular basis for the past 2 years and has not had any episodes of severe hypoglycemia in the past 6 months. She has no history of hematologic, oncologic, renal, cardiac, hepatic, or gastrointestinal disease. The patient is not pregnant nor intends to become pregnant during the course of the study.

Patient is a 55-year-old Latino man living in Miami who has been diagnosed with HIV and is currently on antiretroviral therapy. He reports occasional memory lapses and is concerned about cognitive decline. He has no history of neurodegenerative disorders or dementia, and is able to complete a Mini Mental Status Exam with a score of 28. He is capable of participating in physical activity and has no contraindications to exercise as outlined by the American College of Sports Medicine. He has stable housing and no plans to move outside of the Miami metropolitan area within the next 6 months. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

56 year old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and poorly controlled blood sugar levels despite multiple medications. She lives in rural Pennsylvania and reports difficulty accessing healthy food due to limited availability of fresh produce in her area. She has been struggling to manage her diabetes and has had multiple hospitalizations for hyperglycemia and complications related to her disease. She reports feeling overwhelmed by the demands of managing her illness and is interested in participating in the Fresh Food Farmacy program to improve her health and quality of life. She speaks English fluently and lives within the geographic reach of the program. She has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions that would exclude her from participation in the program. She is motivated to make positive changes in her diet and lifestyle and is excited to learn more about healthy eating and diabetes self-management through the program.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer 3 years ago. She has received several rounds of chemotherapy including anthracycline and taxane, but her cancer is now refractory to these treatments. The patient reports feeling fatigued and has noticed an increase in the size of her breast mass. She has a WHO performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal pathology and is not currently taking any medications that could affect the bioavailability of ZD6474. She has no significant cardiac events within the past 3 months and no history of clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia or congenital long QT syndrome. The patient has not received any systemic anti-cancer therapy or investigational agents within the last 4 weeks and is not currently taking any drugs with known significant 3A4 inhibitory or stimulatory effects. She is not currently receiving therapeutic doses of warfarin. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits.

A 24-year-old woman in her 39th week of pregnancy with her first child is being considered for a clinical trial. She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy with no medical history of note. She has not had any previous pregnancies or deliveries. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has been attending regular antenatal appointments and all her test results have been normal. She has not experienced any contractions or other signs of labor. Her obstetrician is considering inducing labor at 39 weeks instead of waiting until she goes into labor naturally. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will investigate whether early induction of labor in low-risk primiparous women increases the rate of cesarean section.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of colorectal adenocarcinoma RAS/BRAF wild type on primary and/or related metastasis. The metastatic disease is initially unresectable and the patient has not received any prior chemotherapy treatment for metastatic disease. The cancer is located in the left colon. The patient is suitable for first-line chemotherapy and has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has at least one site of measurable disease per RECIST criteria ver. 1.1. The patient has an ECOG Performance status of 2 and adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function assessed before starting study treatment. The patient's DPD status is wild type. The patient has a negative blood pregnancy test within 24 hours prior to the start of study treatment. The patient is willing to avoid pregnancy during the trial and until 5 months for WOCBP (Women of Childbearing Potential) and 7 months for male subjects with female partners of WOCBP after the last trial treatment. The patient has no contraindication to the use of Cetuximab, Bevacizumab, Irinotecan, 5FU, or folinic acid. The patient has not received radiotherapy to any site within 4 weeks before the randomization. The patient has no serious, non-healing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture. The patient has no evidence of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. The patient has controlled hypertension and has no prior history of hypertensive crisis or hypertensive encephalopathy. The patient has no additional malignancy in the last 5 years, active and untreated brain (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis, active infection requiring systemic therapy or active disseminated intravascular coagulation, history of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) (HIV 1/2 antibodies), or any positive test for hepatitis B or hepatitis C virus indicating acute or chronic infection. The patient is not on chronic, daily treatment with high-dose aspirin (>325 mg/day) and has no history of venous thromboembolism > NCI CTCAE Grade 3. The patient has no history of abdominal fistula, GI perforation, intra-abdominal abscess or active GI bleeding within 6 months prior to the first study treatment. The patient has no history of acute or subacute intestinal occlusion or chronic inflammatory bowel disease or chronic diarrhea. The patient is not on current, recent (within 10 days prior to study treatment start) or ongoing treatment with anticoagulants for therapeutic purposes. The patient has not had any major surgical procedure, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days prior to study treatment start, or anticipation of the need for major surgical procedure during the course of the study. The patient has no history of any severe hypersensitivity reactions to any monoclonal antibody. The patient has no significant concomitant disease which, in the investigating physician's opinion, rules out the patient's participation in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with asthma by her physician and has been using asthma medication within the last 2 weeks. She is also severely obese with a BMI of 42 and has decided to undergo weight-reduction surgery. She has never smoked and has not used tobacco within the past month. She does not have any other chronic lung diseases or connective-tissue diseases but has been diagnosed with hypertension and is receiving treatment for it. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of weight loss on lung functioning and asthma symptoms.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has recently given birth to her first child. She developed high blood pressure during her pregnancy and was diagnosed with preeclampsia. Her blood pressure has been stabilized with medication, but she still experiences occasional fluctuations. She is breastfeeding her baby and has some postpartum pain, which is managed with acetaminophen. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the use of NSAIDs for postpartum pain relief, but wants to ensure that it will not negatively affect her blood pressure. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no known sensitivities to ibuprofen or acetaminophen. She is willing to be randomized to receive either an analgesic regimen with or without NSAIDs.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis in her right knee. She has been experiencing persistent pain and stiffness, which has been affecting her daily activities. She is otherwise healthy with no history of any allergies or chronic illnesses. She doesn't smoke and drinks occasionally. She is currently not taking any medications. She has been referred to a surgeon for a unilateral total knee arthroplasty (TKA). The surgeon has planned the use of regional anesthetic techniques, including infiltration between the popliteal artery and the capsule of the posterior knee (IPACK), adductor canal block (ACB), and periarticular injection (PAI) during the surgery. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the potential therapeutic benefit of perioperative dronabinol use in TKA patients. She understands the study protocol and is willing to follow it. She has a BMI of 30.

A 45-year-old woman has experienced severe hearing loss in both ears for several years. She has tried hearing aids but found them ineffective. She has been evaluated by a cochlear implant team at Vanderbilt University Medical Center and determined to be a good candidate for a cochlear implant. She is scheduled to undergo cochlear implant surgery using the Advanced Bionics SlimJ/L23 device. She is fluent in English and able to read and sign a written informed consent form. She has no history of pregnancy, and a pregnancy test will be performed before the procedure. She weighs 150 lbs, which is within the weight limit for the Xoran xCAT headboard. She will be able to undergo adequate audiology follow-up after the procedure. She has not had a fine resolution CT or fpVCT of the head before, and is willing to participate in this research study.

A 62-year-old woman was referred to the outpatient clinic by her primary care physician due to suspected heart failure. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and occasional chest discomfort for the past 6 months. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. She denies smoking, alcohol or drug use. She has no known allergies to medications. She has not had any previous cardiac surgeries or interventions. She is willing to comply with the clinical investigational plan and has signed the informed consent form. She has no known implanted electronic equipment or significant operation scars in the seismocardiographic recording area. She is not pregnant.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital 48 hours ago due to sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. She was diagnosed with an ischemic stroke affecting the M1-segment of the middle cerebral artery and has cortical involvement. She was previously healthy and independent with no prior history of major cardiac, psychiatric, or neurological diseases. She is currently alert and oriented but has residual weakness in her left arm and leg, as well as difficulty with speech. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. She has no contraindications for Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation.

A 7-year-old girl was diagnosed with Fanconi Anemia (FA) based on chromosome breakage test after exposure to an alkylating agent (mitomycin) on peripheral blood lymphocytes. She has not undergone any bone marrow transplant or other treatments. She has a history of microcephaly, a reduction in brain volume, and has been experiencing difficulties with fine motor skills and handwriting. She is easily fatigued due to the energy expended trying to execute fine motor movements correctly. She has no skeletal malformations of the upper limbs that could explain her difficulties. She does not have any other significant medical conditions and does not take any medications. Her parents have agreed to participate in the research and she is eligible for neuropsychological tests and MRI without sedation.

The patient is a 56 year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He takes metformin 1000mg twice daily, lisinopril 20mg daily and atorvastatin 40mg daily. He was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with unstable angina. Coronary angiography revealed significant stenosis in the left anterior descending artery, which was successfully treated with PCI. He is currently stable and will be discharged soon. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 26-year-old nulligest woman of Burkinabe origin who is currently residing in France. She has no history of malaria infection and has not traveled to any malaria endemic region for the last six months. She is in good health and has no chronic illness. She has no history of allergic reactions to any vaccine or any of the vaccine components. She is willing to use reliable contraceptive methods throughout the study period. She has not participated in any clinical trial involving an investigational product for the last 28 days and does not plan to participate in any other clinical study during the conduct of this study. She is registered in the French Health ministry computerized file and authorized to participate in a clinical trial. She understands and can follow all the required study procedures for the entire study duration. She has no psychiatric condition that may affect participation in the study. She has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products within the last three months. Her screening biochemistry, hematology blood tests, and urinalysis results are all within normal limits, with no clinically significant abnormal findings. She has not had any symptoms, physical signs, or laboratory values suggestive of systemic disorders that could interfere with the interpretation of the trial results or compromise her health. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 32-year-old woman with a BMI of 45 has struggled with obesity for most of her life. She has tried several diets and exercise programs without any success. She has no underlying medical conditions and takes no medications. She has never had surgery before, but is interested in laparoscopic gastric-bypass surgery as a last resort to achieve significant weight loss. She exercises moderately for 30 minutes a day, three times a week. She has no history of alcohol or drug dependence/abuse, chronic pain disorder, or significant psychiatric conditions. She is able to understand and comply with the demands of the study. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her post-operative analgesia experience.

A 32-year-old male came to the clinic seeking help for his recreational use of opiates. He admitted to using heroin occasionally for the past six months, but denied any dependence or withdrawal symptoms. He is currently employed as a construction worker and has not experienced any negative impact on his work performance or personal relationships. He is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He has never participated in a clinical trial before, but is interested in exploring non-addictive treatment options for his opiate use. He meets the eligibility criteria for this study as a non-dependent opiate user and is willing to participate in the randomized controlled trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with no significant medical history. She is currently working as a teacher and has no family history of colon cancer. She has never undergone a colonoscopy before but is interested in getting screened for colorectal cancer. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or any other gastrointestinal issues. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She has not undergone any partial or complete colectomy and has no history of familial polyposis syndromes. She is compliant with the split bowel preparation and is willing to undergo scheduled sedation during the procedure.

A 30-year-old woman with a BMI of 25 is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has no history of hypercalcemia, gastrointestinal malabsorption, kidney disease, or liver disease. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements, including vitamin D supplements. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no known allergies or medical conditions. She works as an office administrator and exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week. She has no upcoming vacations to sunny climates.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with systolic heart failure. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is <=35%. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He takes medication for these conditions but has not had any recent hospitalizations or surgeries. He has an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) in place, which allows regular evaluation of heart rhythm. He has no history of rheumatologic disease. The patient is married and lives with his wife. He is retired and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren. He has never smoked and does not use any illicit drugs. He is willing to come into the EP device clinic every three months for one year to have his device interrogated and will complete an EKG. He is open to having labs drawn to measure levels of certain markers of inflammation in the body to help identify new ways to test for risk of abnormal heart rhythms and other heart disease.

17yo female with a history of sickle cell disease and a recent hospitalization for a vaso-occlusive pain crisis. She is currently admitted to Golisano Children's Hospital and has been informed that she will need to transition to an adult-oriented health care provider soon. She has expressed concerns about the transition and is unsure of what to expect. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to assess adolescent patients' knowledge, attitudes and participation in transition planning to adult oriented health care. She is comfortable with completing electronic surveys via SurveyMonkey© and is interested in viewing an educational video on the topic. The patient speaks English and has no intellectual disabilities.

58F with a recent diagnosis of stage II breast cancer started treatment with chemotherapy. She reports significant fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and occasional nausea since starting chemotherapy. She has no history of psychiatric illness or mental health problems. She is able to understand and communicate effectively in English. She has no history of cognitive impairment or difficulty understanding medical terminology. She is interested in participating in clinical trials that help improve the quality of life of cancer patients. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in this trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has never had a Pap test before. She has been a member of her family physician's practice for the past 5 years, but has never felt comfortable with the idea of a pelvic exam. She has received one reminder letter in the past for Pap smear testing, but didn't respond to it. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial as she feels more comfortable with the idea of vaginal self-sampling. She is sexually active with her husband and has two children. She works as a full-time teacher and spends most of her free time with her family. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Her BMI is 24 and her blood pressure is normal. She is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that the self-sampling option will increase her participation in cervical cancer screening.

A 50-year-old male with a history of heart failure presents with fatigue, shortness of breath, and reduced exercise tolerance. He is currently classified as NYHA class III. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He has been on various medications for heart failure management, including beta-blockers and ACE inhibitors. His total testosterone level was found to be less than 5 ng/mL on lab work. He has no history of prostate cancer or prostatism. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the benefits of topical testosterone therapy on HF symptoms and function, as well as its effects on rehospitalization rates and quality of life.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with a high fever, chills, and rapid breathing. She reports feeling generally unwell for the past few days with a cough and body aches. On examination, she has a temperature of 39.5°C, a heart rate of 110 beats per minute, a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, and low blood pressure. Blood tests show elevated white blood cell count and CRP levels. Blood cultures are taken, and she is started on intravenous antibiotics for suspected sepsis. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria for suspected sepsis and fulfills the sepsis-3 definition of sepsis with a sequential organ failure assessment score of 2 or more.

The patient is a 72-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He is retired and lives with his wife in a suburban home. He has a history of hypertension and well-controlled type 2 diabetes. He takes lisinopril and metformin daily. He enjoys gardening and playing golf, but he has been feeling weak and easily exhausted in recent weeks. He has lost 5 pounds unintentionally and has noticed a decline in his overall physical ability. He has never had cancer before and is concerned about the best treatment options for him, given his age and general health status. He is interested in participating in a study that could help determine the best treatment options for elderly patients with cancer. He is willing to provide informed consent and biological samples for the study.

This is a 35-year-old male who is generally healthy but has a history of high plasma uric acid levels, with a reading of 320 micro moles/L during a recent routine medical check-up. He has no history of treated hyperuricemia, gout, or kidney stones. He is a non-smoker, does not consume more than 3 units of alcohol daily, and has a BMI of 25 kg/m². He exercises regularly but is not involved in any vigorous sports competitions. He has no history of intestinal disorders. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effect of quercetin supplements on blood uric acid and other biomarkers. He is willing to comply with the protocol and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her 37th week of pregnancy. She is a primigravida and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy so far. She has a regular menstrual cycle and her last menstrual period was 40 weeks ago. She has been attending regular antenatal checkups and has been advised to have a vaginal birth. The baby is in the vertex presentation and the estimated fetal weight is within the normal range. She has no history of collagen disorders, vaginal surgeries, pelvic floor operations or infibulations. She has no known allergies to any of the components of the BabySlide® device. She has agreed to participate in the study and has given her written informed consent. The plan is to deliver the baby by vacuum extraction and to use the BabySlide® device during the delivery to evaluate its effectiveness in reducing birth tears.

35-year-old female with a history of relapsed Hodgkin's Lymphoma who has failed multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation. She is currently in remission but is expected to require an autologous stem cell transplant in the near future. She has no significant comorbidities and has a Karnofsky performance status of 90%. She is currently not on any medications and has not received chemotherapy in the past 2 weeks. Her blood counts are within normal limits, and her pulmonary function tests show a DLCO of 70% predicted. Her cardiac function is normal with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. Her liver function tests are normal, and she has no evidence of renal insufficiency. She has no significant co-morbid medical or psychiatric illness that would significantly compromise her clinical care and chances of survival in the transplant setting. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed written consent.

I apologize, but there seems to be a mistake in your request. This is a clinical trial for mental health intervention in college students, and there is no need for a patient description. Could you please clarify your request?

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with heart failure. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs for the past few months. His ejection fraction is less than 40%, and he has not undergone any revascularization procedures in the last six months. He has been taking his medications regularly for the past four weeks, and his NewYork Heart Association (NYHA) class is II-III. He can walk without support or assistive devices. The patient does not have any neurological, cognitive, or orthopedic diseases that may affect the measurements. His respiratory function test results show an FEV1 of greater than 35%. His BNP level is less than 100pg/ml, and he does not have an acute infection. His resting heart rate is less than 140 beats/min, and he does not have dementia. His BMI is less than 35, and he does not have any other chronic diseases that may affect his balance and walking. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to cooperate with the study requirements.

The patient is a 30 year old man with a history of congenital heart disease who is scheduled to undergo a medically necessary heart catheterization procedure. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain during physical activity. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the safety and feasibility of using MRI-guided catheters for right-heart catheterization. He is able to undergo magnetic resonance imaging and does not have any implanted devices that are contraindicated for MRI. He has normal renal function and is not allergic to gadolinium-based contrast agents. He is willing to undergo the research MRI procedure either before or after the standard X-ray guided heart catheterization.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (WM) two years ago. He initially presented with fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. His laboratory tests revealed anemia and elevated serum immunoglobulin M (IgM) levels. He was started on treatment with rituximab and bendamustine which resulted in partial remission. However, during his regular follow-up visits, he complained of worsening fatigue, fever, and night sweats. His laboratory tests showed increased serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels and a progressive rise in serum IgM levels. A biopsy was conducted, and he was diagnosed with transformed WM to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). He is now being considered for inclusion in a clinical trial investigating the clinico-biological features, therapy, outcomes, and prognostic factors in WM patients with biopsy-proven transformation to DLBCL. He has no history of other cancers or significant comorbidities. He is retired and has a supportive family. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of participation.

65 yo male with a history of lung cancer presented to the anti-cancer center with complaints of worsening shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. He was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer with metastases to the liver and bones 6 months ago and has been receiving chemotherapy since then. During this hospitalization, he has been experiencing increased pain in his right hip and is unable to ambulate without assistance. He also reports decreased appetite and unintentional weight loss. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking for over 30 years, but he quit smoking after his cancer diagnosis. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and oxycodone. He is married and lives with his wife who has been his primary caregiver throughout his cancer treatment. He has two sons who live out of state but have been in contact with him regularly. On the PALLIA-10 questionnaire, he scored 8/10, indicating a need for palliative care. He is currently being evaluated by the mobile palliative care team.

A 28-year-old woman gave birth to a premature baby boy at 30 weeks gestational age. The baby was born with a 5 mm diameter hemangioma on the forehead. The baby has been in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) for the past 4 weeks and has been doing well. The mother has no history of hemangioma in her family. She has a history of asthma and takes an inhaler as needed. She denies smoking or drinking alcohol during her pregnancy. She delivered via C-section due to fetal distress. She has been visiting her baby in the NICU daily and is interested in enrolling her baby in the cryocontact therapy study to treat the hemangioma. She has been informed about the study and has given her written informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma two years ago. He has received one or more standard treatment regimens but has experienced a relapse. He has no history of proteasome inhibitor therapy, including bortezomib or carfilzomib. He has a performance status of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work, such as office work or light housework. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He complains of fatigue and bone pain, but otherwise does not have any other significant symptoms. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all follow-up visits. He understands that he will be randomized to one of the treatment arms, which will involve taking ixazomib citrate and/or dexamethasone and/or cyclophosphamide. He has agreed to use two effective methods of contraception during the study period, as he is sexually active and his partner is of childbearing potential.

A 63-year-old male diagnosed with mild to moderate open-angle glaucoma is currently taking two ocular hypotensive medications to manage his intraocular pressure (IOP). He has a history of Schaffer grade III in all four quadrants. The patient has never undergone any glaucoma surgery or laser trabeculoplasty other than selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT). The patient had cataract surgery six months ago, and his visual field test (Humphrey SITA standard 24-2) showed a mean deviation better than or equal to -12.0 dB. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol and follow-up visits for 12 months. The patient has no history of acute angle-closure, traumatic, congenital, malignant, uveitic or neovascular glaucoma, pigmentary or pseudoexfoliative glaucoma.

65-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to his primary care physician with complaints of fatigue and ankle swelling. Physical examination revealed bilateral pitting edema and hypertension with a blood pressure of 160/100 mmHg. Laboratory tests showed an elevated serum creatinine level of 2.5 mg/dL and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 25 mL/min/1.73m2. Urinalysis showed proteinuria with a protein-to-creatinine ratio of 1.5 g/g. The patient was referred to a multidisciplinary CKD clinic for further evaluation and management. The nephrologist at the CKD clinic confirmed the diagnosis of stage 4 chronic kidney disease (CKD) and recommended dietary modifications, blood pressure control, and close monitoring of renal function. The nephrologist also discussed the option of starting dialysis in the future if the patient's kidney function continued to deteriorate. The patient expressed concerns regarding the potential risks and side effects of early dialysis initiation and the nephrologist informed the patient about the ongoing clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of a knowledge translation strategy to defer dialysis initiation. The patient agreed to participate in the trial and was randomized to the active knowledge translation strategy group. The patient received patient- and provider-directed educational tools based on the recent published clinical practice guidelines, including visual aids and in-person medical detailing. The patient's renal function was closely monitored, and the nephrologist worked with the patient to optimize blood pressure control and manage other comorbidities. The patient's eGFR remained stable, and dialysis initiation was deferred. The patient's participation in the trial contributed to the knowledge regarding the effectiveness of the active knowledge translation strategy to defer dialysis initiation and may lead to improved patient outcomes and reduced health care costs in the future.

A 42-year-old Hispanic woman has been scheduled for laparoscopic cholecystectomy surgery due to gallstones. She has a BMI of 35 m2/kg and is fluent in English and Spanish. She has no history of psychiatric, neurological or neuromuscular disorders, and no known thyroid disease. Her alcohol consumption is limited to one drink per week and she has no history of drug abuse. She is not currently taking opioids or any other medications affecting the central nervous system. She has no known allergies to study medications or soy/egg proteins. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing heartburn and regurgitation for the past 6 months. He describes the heartburn as a burning sensation in his chest that occurs after eating and worsens when lying down. He also experiences regurgitation of food and stomach acid into his throat, which causes him to cough and occasionally choke. He has tried over-the-counter antacids, but they only provide temporary relief. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription medications. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He drinks alcohol occasionally and smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day. His BMI is 25 and his blood pressure is normal. He is willing to participate in the study and is excited to learn more about his reflux symptoms.

54-year-old Caucasian male with a history of papillary thyroid cancer diagnosed 2 years ago. He underwent total thyroidectomy and bilateral central neck dissection followed by radioiodine ablation. A recent follow-up neck sonogram showed several suspicious lymph nodes in the left cervical chain and a biopsy confirmed metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma. The patient is now scheduled for 131I ablation therapy and will have a clinical FDG PET/CT scan prior to the therapy. He reports no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He denies any fever, weight loss or night sweats. He has no history of claustrophobia or difficulty sitting still. Physical exam is unremarkable, with no palpable lymph nodes or other masses. The patient is eager to participate in the study and provide valuable information to help improve cancer imaging and treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He has been experiencing pain in his heels for the past month and it has been affecting his work performance. He describes the pain as sharp and unbearable, especially in the first steps after a prolonged period of rest. He has tried resting and using over-the-counter painkillers, but they have not been effective. He does not have any medical history of peripheral neuropathies, tarsus tunnel syndrome, or rheumatic diseases. He has not received acupuncture or dry needling as a treatment. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the exercise program. His VAS score is 4 out of 10 in the first steps of the morning. His medical history indicates that he does not have any clotting disorders, fractures, infections, or tumor processes. He has not undergone any previous surgeries on the foot. He is not pregnant and does not have any communication disorders. He does not have any pacemakers or electrostimulators.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with compensated cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C infection. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. He presents with a history of hematemesis and melena for the past 2 days. He denies any history of alcohol abuse or illicit drug use. On physical examination, his vital signs are stable with no fever or tachycardia. Abdominal examination reveals mild hepatomegaly with no ascites or tenderness. He undergoes an upper GI endoscopy and is found to have bleeding esophageal varices, which are successfully treated with band ligation. The patient is eligible for the study as he has a Child score "A" and has no signs of infection or a previous history of antibiotic use.

A 57 year old woman was admitted to the hospital with a stroke. She has been diagnosed with moderate to severe upper limb functional limitation due to the stroke, and her Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) score is 20. She has shoulder subluxation, but it is less than grade 3. This is her first stroke, and she is admitted to the rehabilitation unit. She is able to sit in a chair or bed and use a computer or tablet with or without the help of carers. She is able to understand and speak English and provide informed consent. She does not have any significant cardiorespiratory, orthopaedic, neurological, or other conditions that would preclude her from taking part in an exercise programme. Her Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 30, indicating no cognitive impairment. She is not currently participating in another project.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was involved in a motor vehicle collision resulting in a severe traumatic brain injury. He was immediately intubated and mechanically ventilated upon arrival at the emergency department. A CT scan showed multiple skull fractures and intracranial hemorrhage. The patient was admitted to the ICU and received continuous infusions of opioids, benzodiazepines, and neuromuscular blocking agents for more than 72 hours. He has been experiencing fever and agitation, which has prolonged his ICU stay. The patient has no history of chronic alcohol abuse or regular use of heroin, cocaine, or amphetamines. He has never used opioids chronically before. The patient has not been admitted to any other ICUs or moved to other ICUs with ongoing infusions.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of smoking and a chronic cough for over a year. He has been diagnosed with Chronic Idiopathic Cough (CIC) and has not responded to targeted treatment for identified underlying triggers. He reports that his cough is worse during the day and frequently disrupts his work and sleep. He also mentions that he has tried various over-the-counter cough remedies without relief.
