He is currently not taking any medication for his cough. His physical examination is unremarkable, and his baseline cough count is 20 per hour. He has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in the study.

Pt is a 45yo M with a history of mild hepatic impairment due to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. He has been managing his condition with diet and exercise but has been experiencing occasional abdominal discomfort and fatigue. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He has a BMI of 26.5 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker. He is not taking any prescription or OTC drugs except for occasional use of paracetamol for mild headaches. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the effect of Mirabegron on subjects with mild hepatic impairment.

23F with a history of recurrent sacrococcygeal pilonidal disease presents with complaints of painful swelling and drainage in the region for the past 6 months. She has previously undergone multiple surgical procedures for the same issue, including incision and drainage, excision and primary closure, and open wound healing. She reports difficulty sitting and performing daily activities due to the discomfort and discharge. On examination, a single pit with inflammation and tenderness is noted in the sacrococcygeal region. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent recurrence of the condition and improve her quality of life.

A 23-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes and hypertension presents with difficulty in controlling her blood pressure despite being on multiple medications including lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. She reports a sedentary lifestyle due to her busy work schedule and lack of motivation. Physical examination was unremarkable except for elevated blood pressure at 148/92 mmHg. She is currently using an iPhone and is compatible with wireless devices, including FitBits©. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve her physical activity levels and blood pressure control.

A 45-year-old female diagnosed with diabetes mellitus based on her blood glucose and hemoglobin A1C levels. She has been managing her diabetes with insulin injections for the past 5 years. She has no history of bariatric surgery, total colectomy, or proctocolectomy. She has not participated in any experimental drug protocols within the past 12 weeks and is not currently receiving total parenteral nutrition. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has been struggling with borderline personality disorder (BPD) for several years. She has a history of multiple suicide attempts and non-suicidal self-injury episodes. She has received some therapy in the past but has not had access to Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT) due to long waitlists and high costs. She is currently experiencing difficulty in her personal relationships, with frequent arguments and feelings of intense anger and abandonment. She has a history of alcohol and drug abuse, but is currently in recovery. She is fluent in English, living in the Greater Toronto Area, and has had Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) coverage for over a year. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive DBT treatment but is concerned about the length of treatment and the potential cost.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer after a biopsy. The biopsy revealed a high-risk prostate cancer according to D'Amico classification with a Gleason score of 8. The patient has not received any treatment for the cancer yet. The patient is scheduled for radical prostatectomy and extended pelvic lymph node resection up to 6 weeks after the investigational PET/CT scan followed by histopathology assessment. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to [18F]CTT1057. The patient has not undergone any PSMA targeted therapies, Luteinizing Hormone-Releasing Hormone (LHRH) analogues, or Androgen Deprivation Therapy (ADT) within the specified time periods. The patient has not used 5-alpha reductase inhibitors within 30 days before screening. The patient does not have small cell or neuroendocrine PCa in more than 50% of biopsy tissue and does not have incidental PCa after transurethral resection. The patient has not used any other investigational drugs within 30 days before screening.

A 32-year-old man who is generally healthy and takes no medications came to the clinic to participate in the clinical trial. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, hormonal, neurological, or psychiatric disorders. He has a BMI of 24.5 and has never smoked or used drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally but doesn't exceed 60 g/day. He has no history of blood donation or excessive physical activities. He is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the study center. He signed and dated written informed consent prior to admission to the study in accordance with GCP and the local legislation.

This clinical trial is not seeking patients specifically, but rather is being conducted on all surgical admissions to wards E4 and F4 at the Juravinski Hospital in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. Therefore, there is no specific patient description required for this trial.

Maria is a 28-year-old woman who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has a healthy weight and exercises regularly. She has never taken Prasugrel or any related compounds before. She does not have any known allergies to medications. Maria does not regularly drink alcohol and does not exceed the recommended alcohol intake. She has no current medical conditions and is not taking any medications. Maria is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with chronic constipation. She has been experiencing this condition for several years and has tried various treatments including fiber supplements, laxatives, and enemas. She has completed the entire treatment period of one of the previous studies mentioned and did not experience any severe side effects. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding and has adequate contraceptive protection. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes medication daily. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is a working mother of two children and has a busy daily schedule. She struggles with constipation and often feels bloated and uncomfortable. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of prucalopride in treating her chronic constipation.

A 32-year-old male patient is scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy for chronic cholecystitis. He has no significant medical history other than occasional episodes of acid reflux. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently not taking any medication. The patient has expressed a high level of thirst during the preoperative assessment and has been approved for the study of the efficacy of ice popsicles compared with water at room temperature in relieving thirst in the immediate postoperative period. He has agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent form.

A 38-year-old Hispanic female patient presents with moderate to severe melasma on her forehead, cheeks and upper lip. She has had this condition for the past 5 years and has tried various over-the-counter creams with no significant improvement. She has Fitzpatrick skin type IV and has no known allergies. She is not currently receiving any other dermatologic treatments. She reports no history of skin cancer or any other dermatologic condition that may interfere with the safe evaluation of the study combination. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for treatment of her melasma and willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for 4 years. He is taking oral medication, metformin, to control his blood sugar levels. He has been leading a sedentary lifestyle and is currently not engaged in any regular exercise routine. His BMI is 29. He has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He had a single episode of atrial fibrillation 3 years ago which resolved spontaneously and did not require any treatment. He has mild diabetic retinopathy which is monitored by his ophthalmologist on a regular basis. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a project manager in a construction company and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He is interested in improving his physical fitness level and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the effects of exercise on metabolic parameters in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

25-year-old female with a BMI of 25 kg/m² interested in exploring dietary interventions to improve overall health and well-being. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription or non-prescription medications that could impact systemic inflammation, blood sugar control, or the human microbiome. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study, including completing questionnaires and keeping a diet diary. She is available for all scheduled visits at the investigational site. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, immunodeficiency disorder, illegal drug use, or chronic alcoholism. She does not have any difficulties or major inconvenience in changing her dietary habits, and does not have any food allergies or restrictions due to medical, religious, or other concerns. She is not diagnosed with allergic rhinitis, eczema, asthma, or inflammatory bowel disease. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the effects of a juice fast on her gut health, epigenetic markers, and overall well-being.

32 yo F with primary infertility of unknown cause, previously underwent IVF cycle with controlled ovarian stimulation using REKOVELLE® resulting in 2 blastocysts, one transferred and one cryopreserved. Patient presents for FET with the cryopreserved blastocyst. BMI 24.1, AMH 2.9 ng/ml (measured 8 months prior to IVF cycle). No significant medical history. Past surgical history includes appendectomy and cholecystectomy. No history of smoking or alcohol use. Willing and able to understand English patient information and provide written informed consent.

This is a 32-year-old male who suffered a tibial fracture in a motor vehicle accident six months ago. Despite undergoing surgical intervention and bone grafting, he has shown no signs of radiographic healing for at least three months. He has been experiencing pain and discomfort at the injury site, with an intensity of 7 out of 10. He has adequate soft tissue coverage at the delayed healing site and a sufficient amount of iliac crest autograft available for a bone grafting procedure. He is at least 21 years of age and skeletally mature at the time of surgery. He is willing and able to comply with the study plan and able to understand and sign the Patient Informed Consent Form. He has no history of congenital pseudarthrosis or pathological fracture nonunion, articular involvement, hypertrophic tibial delayed healing, inadequate neurovascular status in the involved limb, active or known prior infection at the delayed healing site, and existing stable hardware that will not be removed. He has had no prior exposure to any recombinant BMPs of either human or animal extraction, and has no documented allergy or intolerance to metal or metal alloys, such as stainless steel or titanium. He has not received treatment with an investigational therapy (drug, device, and/or biologic) within 28 days prior to implantation surgery or such treatment is planned during the 12-month period following the study surgery.

Pt is a 28yo F with a history of taking birth control pills for the past 3 years. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of vitamin B6 on women taking birth control pills. The patient is in good health, with normal screening labs and body weight. She is not pregnant and has never had gastrointestinal surgery. The patient does not have any chronic diseases and is a non-smoker. She does not consume alcohol excessively or use any chronic drugs. The patient reports that she does not take any vitamin supplements. Plasma PLP levels have not been measured yet, but the patient is interested in finding out if she meets the inclusion criteria for the trial.

A 65-year-old woman has been experiencing severe knee pain for the past few years, limiting her mobility and affecting her quality of life. After discussing with her doctor, she has decided to undergo elective primary knee replacement surgery under spinal anaesthesia. She is willing to receive patient controlled midazolam sedation during the surgery. The patient is not deaf and is willing to use noise cancelling headphones during the procedure. She is able to provide informed consent for participation in the trial.

A 56 year old female is admitted to the surgical intensive care unit (SICU) with a history of hypertension and diabetes. She had undergone a laparotomy for a ruptured ovarian cyst and had excessive bleeding during the surgery. The patient has been receiving blood transfusions since then, but her hemoglobin levels have not been stable. Her current hemoglobin level is 8.5 g/dL and the physician is concerned about ongoing bleeding. The patient is alert and oriented, and her vital signs are stable. She has no history of previous surgeries or other major medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and to have her hemoglobin levels monitored non-invasively.

57 yo F with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech. CT scan revealed an acute ischemic stroke and MRI confirmed an intracranial large artery occlusion in the middle cerebral artery (MCA M1). The patient was immediately initiated on IV tPA and transferred to a comprehensive stroke center for further treatment. Endovascular treatment (EVT) was initiated with the use of Reco ® thrombectomy device. The procedure was successful in removing the clot and the patient's neurological deficits improved significantly. The patient was discharged to a rehabilitation facility for further recovery. The patient or their legal representative has provided informed consent to participate in this registry study to evaluate the utilization and outcomes of EVT treated AIS patients using Reco ® as the primary therapy in the real-world setting.

The patient is a 54-year-old female who has been experiencing severe knee pain for the past few years. She has a BMI of 32 and has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee. She has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy, weight loss, and pain medications, but the pain has continued to worsen. She has no history of knee surgery and has not participated in any clinical trials before. She is currently taking medication for hypertension and high cholesterol, but is otherwise healthy. She is able to understand the study procedures and is willing to give informed consent. She is willing to undergo preoperative full-leg standing radiographs and return for all follow-up evaluations. She has no conditions that would pose excessive operative risk and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 45-year-old office worker complains of numbness and tingling sensation in both hands, especially at night. She reports difficulty gripping objects and feels weakness in her hands. She has no significant past medical history except for hypothyroidism, which is well controlled on medication. She never had any surgeries or injections on her wrists. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She works at a desk job where she needs to use a computer and a mouse for an extended period. Her symptoms have been present for the last 6 months and she is currently taking over-the-counter pain medication for relief. She was diagnosed with CTS through an electrophysiological study. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive treatment for her condition.

The patient is a 27-year-old male with a mild to severe intellectual disability, who exhibits challenging behavior including verbal and physical aggression, hyperactivity, refusal to attend activities, and non-responsiveness, that requires professional input. He is currently receiving care from community intellectual disability services and is eligible to participate in the study. The patient's behavior has caused disruption in his daily activities and has led to prescription of long-term medication. The patient's mental health and quality of life have been impacted due to his challenging behavior. The patient's clinical team has determined that he meets the inclusion criteria for the study and he has agreed to participate. The patient's service has agreed to participate in the study and has at least two staff members willing to receive training in Positive Behavior Support (PBS). The service manager has provided written agreement for the service's participation in the study. The patient does not have a primary clinical diagnosis of personality disorder or substance misuse, and there are no ongoing investigations or complaints that would make him ineligible for the study.

Patient is a 32-year-old female who has been scheduled to undergo an abdominal hysterectomy. She has a history of endometriosis and fibroids, and her gynecologist has recommended surgery as the best treatment option. The patient has given informed consent for the surgery and also to participate in this study. She has been experiencing moderate to severe pain related to her condition and is concerned about the possibility of chronic postsurgical pain. The patient does not have any other significant medical history and is not taking any medications that could potentially affect the study outcomes. She has been advised to follow the postoperative pain management plan provided by the hospital and to report any pain or discomfort experienced during the follow-up visits.

The patient is a 10-year-old Chinese boy who was referred to the ophthalmology department for a routine eye examination. He has no history of ocular trauma or surgery and has no known ocular or systemic diseases. His parents provided their consent for him to participate in the study and he is able to follow the experimental rules. The patient has a spectacle corrected visual acuity of 1.0 in each eye and can fixate on a target without difficulty. His equivalent spherical lens range is -2.50D in both eyes, with no significant anisometropia. The patient has not used atropine eye drops or other medications for the past month. His intraocular pressure is within the normal range. The patient is cooperative and able to provide high-quality image results.

A 58-year-old Caucasian man presents with complaints of frequent urination, difficulty starting and maintaining a steady stream, and feeling like he has to go again shortly after finishing. He reports waking up at night to urinate at least once. He also reports occasional mild pain during urination. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. He has no history of urinary tract infections. He has no history of prostate cancer or other genitourinary cancer. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and mild hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has no known drug allergies. He drinks alcohol socially and smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day. He works as a construction worker and exercises regularly. His PSA level is 7.2 ng/mL. A digital rectal exam reveals a smooth, enlarged prostate gland. His uroflowmetry reveals a maximum flow rate of 9 mL/sec, post-void residual volume of 60 mL, and voided volume of 150 mL. His IPSS score is 18.

The patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with hormone-resistant prostate cancer with metastasis to the bones. He has been treated with androgen suppression therapy for the past 10 months. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not have any history of autoimmune diseases, inflammatory bowel disease, or any other active malignancies. His latest PSA test showed a level of 20 ng/ml. The patient's ECOG performance status is 0-1, and his hemoglobin, platelets, and white blood cell counts are all within normal limits. His creatinine and liver function tests are also normal. The patient has not received any herbal product or systemic corticosteroids in the past 2 weeks. He is sexually active and uses condoms as a form of contraception. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 70-year-old Hispanic woman came to her primary care physician with complaints of forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating. Her daughter, who accompanies her to the appointment, reports that her mother has been forgetting important appointments and recently misplaced her wallet. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, all well-controlled with medication. She is an active member of her community and participates in social activities. On physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Her blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and her heart rate is 70 beats per minute. The neurological examination is unremarkable. The patient speaks fluent Spanish and has no hearing or vision problems. She is not a permanent resident of a nursing facility and is seeing her primary care physician for a routine check-up. The patient

35-year-old female with a BMI of 39.2, who has been struggling with food addiction and obesity for several years. The patient has attempted various conventional weight loss methods in the past without success. She has no prior experience with TMS or any other brain stimulation treatments. The patient does not have any significant medical history other than obesity, and has not been diagnosed with any neurological or psychiatric disorders. She is not currently on any psychotropic medication or undergoing any other treatment for obesity or food addiction. The patient is a nonsmoker and does not consume alcohol or use drugs. She is willing to participate in the study and able to communicate effectively with the investigator.

The patient is a 59-year-old Caucasian male who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has no symptoms related to the cancer and his PSA level is 42 ng/ml. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril 20 mg daily, and he has a family history of prostate cancer in his father. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His Karnofsky Performance Status is 90. He has not undergone any previous treatment for prostate cancer and has no history of pelvic irradiation. He does not take anticoagulants. His prostate biopsy showed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 7 (4+3). His T-stage is T2c. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness and side effects of conventional dose radiotherapy to high dose radiotherapy.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a history of TTP-HUS, which has relapsed despite standard therapy. She presents with symptoms of anemia, thrombocytopenia, and renal failure. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes lisinopril. Her physical examination is significant for pallor and petechiae on her arms and legs. Laboratory evaluation reveals hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, platelets 45,000/mm3, creatinine 2.5 mg/dL, and LDH 1500 U/L. Her ADAMTS13 activity is less than 10%. She has no evidence of DIC, malignant hypertension, vasculitis, or anti-phospholipid antibody syndrome. She has not undergone stem cell, bone marrow, or solid organ transplant. She has not been previously treated with rituximab. She is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

A 21-year-old female college student with a body mass index of 22 presented for screening in a study investigating the effect of forward head and rounded shoulder posture on hand grip strength in asymptomatic young adults. She is right-handed and has no history of neck or shoulder symptoms, fractures, dislocations, radiculopathy, recent shoulder surgery, or musculoskeletal abnormalities. She leads a sedentary lifestyle and is not an athlete. During the screening, the distance between the table and the posterior aspect of the lateral part of her acromion process was measured and found to be ≥ 2.5 cm. Her posture was also assessed using the craniovertebral angle, which was found to be ≤ 50, indicating forward head posture. She was included in the study as a subject with forward head rounded shoulder posture. She gave informed consent and agreed to participate in the study.

52-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of primary hypertension based on ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) with a mean 24-h systolic BP ≥130 mmHg or mean 24-h diastolic BP ≥80 mmHg. He has not taken any antihypertensive medications before. He has a history of smoking and a family history of hypertension. His physical examination is unremarkable. His blood tests show normal renal function (creatinine 1.0 mg/dL), serum potassium of 4.2 mEq/L, and uric acid of 5.5 mg/dL. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes or gout. He is not pregnant nor lactating. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the efficacy of different doses of two thiazide diuretics, chlorthalidone (25 mg/day) and hydrochlorothiazide (50 mg/day), combined with a potassium-sparing diuretic, amiloride, in different doses (10 mg/day or 20 mg/day), to control his blood pressure. He understands that the study will be randomized, double-blinded, and last for 12 weeks. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and to visit the clinic regularly for follow-up.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl who attends a public school in the municipality of Aarhus, Denmark. She is generally healthy and does not have any significant medical history. She has had regular dental check-ups and has been diagnosed with no dental problems. She complains of mild anxiety and discomfort during dental treatments, especially when the procedure involves the use of needles. She is willing to participate in the study to help improve her dental experience and possibly reduce her anxiety during dental treatments. She does not have any difficulties breathing through her nose and is not pregnant. The upper central incisors are sound, and there is no evidence of trauma to these teeth. She is classified as an ASA group I.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was diagnosed with colorectal cancer 2 months ago. The cancer has metastasized to her liver, with multiple liver metastases, making her ineligible for liver resection or RFA. She has no history of other cancers, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. Her current medication includes over-the-counter pain medication. On physical examination, the patient appears to be in general good health, with no acute distress. Her vital signs are within normal limits. There is no evidence of extrahepatic disease, and her liver tissue is involved under 70%. She has measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1, and her performance status is 1. Her ANC and platelet counts are within normal limits, and her estimated creatinine clearance is above the required level. Her INR and bilirubin levels are also within normal limits. Her physician has recommended this clinical trial to her as a potential option for treatment.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who suffered a stroke in the last 8 weeks, affecting his left hemisphere. He is currently admitted to the Hof Ter Schelde rehabilitation hospital for post-stroke rehabilitation. The patient has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are currently under control with medication. He is married and has two adult children. The patient is retired and used to work as a carpenter before the stroke. He is currently experiencing difficulties with postural control and balance, which impairs his ability to perform daily activities. The patient is able to follow instructions and has given informed consent to participate in the study. He has no history of substance abuse, psychiatric disorders or epilepsy. He does not have a pacemaker or internal defibrillator, and he is not pregnant.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who sustained a severe burn injury less than 24 hours ago. The burn is 2nd degree and covers 15% of his total body surface area (TBSA). He was involved in a workplace accident and was transported to the hospital by ambulance. He is currently conscious and alert but in significant pain. He has no significant past medical history, and he is not taking any regular medications. He does not have any known allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He is married and has two children. He works as a mechanic and enjoys playing basketball in his free time. He has no history of significant medical problems or hospitalizations in the past.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been experiencing painful and itchy pustules on the palms and soles of her feet for the past six months. She has tried using topical steroid and vitamin D3 derivative preparations, as well as phototherapy and systemic etretinate, but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She has been diagnosed with palmoplantar pustulosis and has a score of 15 on the Palmo-Plantar Pustular Area and Severity Index (PPPASI). She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of guselkumab for this condition. She has no history of plaque-type psoriasis or malignancy, and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. She is of childbearing potential and is practicing a highly effective method of birth control.

The patient is a healthy 25 year old female with no significant medical history. She has a body weight of 55kg and BMI of 22kg/m2. She does not smoke, drink alcohol excessively or take any medications. She has not participated in any clinical investigation within the last 6 months and has not donated blood within the last 60 days. She is willing to use contraceptives during the study period and is willing to sign an informed consent form. She meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 60-year-old Caucasian man with a long history of smoking presents with difficulty breathing for the past 3 years. He has a productive cough and wheezing. He was diagnosed with COPD and prescribed two different inhalers by his primary care physician. He has been using them for the past year but still experiences symptoms. He works as a construction worker and is exposed to dust and fumes on a daily basis. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently on medications for these conditions. He has a BMI of 31 and does not exercise regularly. He is married with two grown-up children. His family history is negative for any respiratory problems. He has not been hospitalized for COPD exacerbation in the past year. His FEV1 is 55% of predicted. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if there is a better inhaler option for him.

75-year-old female with no history of neurological problems or head injury, normal Mini Mental State Examination of 26, and Montreal Cognitive Assessment score of 28. The patient is not taking any psychoactive medication and has no metal implants in her head or implanted electronic devices. She has normal or corrected-to-normal vision, color vision, and no skin sensitivity. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her memory and cognitive function.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with a history of rectal bleeding and abdominal pain for the past 3 months. He underwent colonoscopy and biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic colorectal cancer. A CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed multiple liver and lung metastases. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has no history of lipid-lowering therapy with statins in the past year, and his liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has no active infection requiring antibiotics therapy, and he has not received radiotherapy in the past 2 weeks. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy for metastatic CRC. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 70-year-old male patient has been newly diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He has not received any prior standard or investigational chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplasia. He has no history of heart disease, hepatitis B or C, or HIV positivity. He has a WHO performance status of 1 and his serum creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. He has no known hypersensitivity to everolimus or other rapamycins. The patient has not been enrolled in this trial before and is not receiving any other concurrent anti-leukemia agents, investigational agents, or biological agents.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) six months ago. He has a history of chronic hepatitis B and cirrhosis. He underwent transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) as first-line therapy with sorafenib, but showed disease progression after 4 months of TACE. He has discontinued sorafenib treatment 14 days prior to randomization. His Child-Pugh score is 6 (Class A). His ECOG performance status is 1. His recent lab results show: Total bilirubin 2.2 mg/dL, AST 70 U/L, ALT 90 U/L, serum creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, INR 1.3, platelet count 100,000/mm3, and AFP 500 ng/mL. His liver mass is 5 cm in diameter with characteristic vascularization seen on triphasic CT scan. There is no evidence of extrahepatic metastases or vascular invasion. He is currently not taking any medication or undergoing any other therapy for HCC. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who is scheduled for emergency surgery due to a bowel obstruction. He has a history of gastroesophageal reflux and has been fasting for over 8 hours. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies to medications. The surgery will require general anesthesia with tracheal intubation, and the patient is at high risk for aspiration of gastric contents during the procedure. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of Remifentanil to a muscle relaxant for rapid sequence intubation.

A 30-year-old Chinese male with a history of recreational ketamine use for the past 2 years presented to Taipei City Hospital and Psychiatric Center seeking treatment for ketamine dependence. He reported using ketamine on a weekly basis and had recently increased his usage to twice a week. He denied any other drug use or psychiatric disorders. He reported occasional difficulty falling asleep and feeling anxious during periods of abstinence from ketamine. He had no significant medical history and was not taking any medications. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory tests revealed no significant findings except a positive urine screen for ketamine. He provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial for lamotrigine for ketamine dependence. He agreed to monthly pregnancy testing and agreed to use appropriate forms of birth control for the duration of the study. He was randomized to the lamotrigine group and started on a dose of 25mg before bed. He will be monitored for 12 weeks and will undergo urinary toxicology and visual analogue scales at each visit. He will also be monitored for any adverse events related to the study medication.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of a myocardial infarction and peripheral arterial disease. He is currently taking aspirin, beta-blockers, and a statin medication. He has never been diagnosed with Type II Diabetes or used hypoglycemic drugs in the past. His blood pressure is well controlled with his current medication regimen, and his LDL cholesterol level is below 130mg/dL. He has never had an MRI and is not aware of any contraindications to the exam. He has no history of claustrophobia. He has never been diagnosed with renal insufficiency or required renal dialysis. He has never taken ACEI/ARBs, anti-oxidants, calcium channel blockers, or diuretics. He has not experienced a transient ischemic cerebral attack in the past 6 months. He has no known allergies to renin inhibitors. He has no history of malignancy, including leukemia and lymphoma. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and able to attend scheduled clinic visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a cardiac tumor located in the ventricular chamber of the heart. Surgical removal is not an option for her due to the high risk of complications, and she is experiencing significant symptoms including shortness of breath and chest pain. She has undergone imaging tests that have confirmed the presence of the tumor and the obstruction caused by it. She has a history of hypertension but is otherwise healthy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to explore minimally invasive treatment options and avoid the risks associated with traditional surgery. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the intervention treatment and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old male with a history of transfemoral amputation due to a traumatic injury. He has been using a prosthesis for several years but experiences phantom limb pain and discomfort while using it for extended periods. He is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions. He is currently employed as a construction worker and enjoys hiking and outdoor activities. He is interested in participating in this study to improve his functional abilities and alleviate his phantom limb pain.

The patient is a 57 year old male diagnosed with stage IV squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He has a history of heavy tobacco and alcohol use. He has undergone surgery to remove the tumor and has been recommended to undergo radiation therapy and chemotherapy for further treatment. He is currently experiencing discomfort in his mouth due to the thick saliva caused by radiation therapy and chemotherapy. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and is otherwise healthy without any active infection or severe medical illness. He is married and has two children. He is a retired teacher and enjoys reading books and watching movies in his free time. He has never been allergic to any medication and is not currently on any medication. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man living in a rural area of Bangladesh. He has been drinking arsenic contaminated water for the past 10 years. He noticed the development of hard, wart-like growths on his palms and soles which makes it difficult for him to work. He also has a reddened scaly patch on his leg that has been persistent for the past 6 months. He has never received any treatment for these conditions before. He has no known allergies or medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his informed consent.

A 10-year-old girl has been experiencing recurrent abdominal pain for the past 6 months, occurring at least weekly or 5 days per month. The pain is described as a dull ache, sometimes sharp, and occurs in the periumbilical region. The episodes usually last for a few hours and are sometimes accompanied by nausea and vomiting. The pain interferes with her school attendance and social interactions with her peers. Her parents have consulted with her pediatrician, who has ruled out any medical causes for the pain. The pediatrician has referred her to this clinical trial to evaluate a new biobehavioral model for assessing and treating migraine and recurrent abdominal pain in children. The parents have given their consent for her to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male presents with a history of glioblastoma that was initially diagnosed 18 months ago. He underwent surgical resection followed by radiation therapy with concurrent chemotherapy with temozolomide. MRI scans showed no evidence of disease recurrence until 4 months ago when he developed progressive headaches, focal seizures, and impaired balance. Brain MRI demonstrated a new enhancing lesion consistent with recurrent glioblastoma. The patient underwent repeat surgical resection and pathology confirmed recurrent glioblastoma. He received adjuvant treatment with bevacizumab and temozolomide chemotherapy for 6 months with a partial response but subsequently developed disease progression. His Karnofsky performance status is 80%. Laboratory results are as follows: ANC: 2.3 x 109/L, Platelets: 201 x 109/L, Hgb: 12.5 g/dL, serum total bilirubin: 0.9 x ULN, ALT: 20 U/L, AST: 25 U/L, BUN: 14 mg/dL, Cr: 1.1 mg/dL, INR: 1.2. The patient is not on anticoagulant therapy. He has no history of significant cardiac diseases, hepatitis, or other severe medical conditions. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who has been diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma. He has a family history of the disease and has been experiencing gradual loss of peripheral vision over the past year. He underwent a comprehensive eye exam, which included visual acuity, intraocular pressure measurement, gonioscopy and fundus photography. The fundus photography showed signs of optic disc damage, which is consistent with the diagnosis of open-angle glaucoma. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that will compare the manual and automatic segmentation of the optic disc to evaluate which method is more accurate in determining the parameters of the optic disc, including cup size, size of excavation, cup-to-disc ratio, and rim area.

A 35-year-old female office worker has been experiencing severe abdominal pain for the past few months. She has consulted with her primary care physician and underwent several diagnostic tests, which revealed the presence of gallstones. The patient has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any illicit drugs. She is married and has two children. She is scheduled for laparoscopic cholecystectomy to remove the gallstones. She is currently taking over-the-counter pain medications to alleviate her symptoms. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is an alert and cooperative patient who is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with a body mass index of 22 kg/m2. He does not have any history of heart, lung, liver, kidney, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, musculoskeletal or endocrine disorders or other systemic illness. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is not taking any regular medications or herbal supplements/remedies. His blood pressure and pulse rate are within normal limits. The patient is willing to use highly effective methods of birth control during the study period.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing sensitivity in his teeth for the past 8 months. He reports the pain being triggered by hot, cold, sweet, and sour foods and drinks, and when brushing his teeth. He has 28 natural teeth, with no history of periodontal disease and no dental implants. He has never received any professional desensitizing treatments, teeth whitening, or orthodontic bands, and does not have any dental restorations. He uses a regular toothpaste and has not used any desensitizing toothpaste for at least six weeks. He is in good general health and has no history of substance abuse or chronic debilitating diseases. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and restrictions, and understands the study. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and none of the exclusion criteria.

John is a 47 year old male who was recently diagnosed with a type B aortic dissection. He presented to the hospital with sudden onset of severe chest pain that radiated to his back. CT scan revealed a tear in the inner layer of his aorta, which is the main artery that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body. His aortic diameter is 5.8cm and he has no thrombosis in the false lumen. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medications to control it. He has no known allergies or comorbidities. His family history is significant for hypertension in his father and grandfather. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the nature of the procedure. He is available for the appropriate follow-up visits during the follow-up period and is capable of following all study requirements. He has provided a written informed consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at the age of 5. She has been attending the Paris Cochin adult CF centre for the last 10 years. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Her medical history includes frequent respiratory infections, sinusitis and bronchitis. She is currently taking Ivacaftor/Lumacaftor as a CFTR modulator therapy. Her last pulmonary function test showed a forced expiratory volume (FEV1) of 70% predicted. Her bone mineral density test revealed osteopenia in her lumbar spine and femoral neck. She has no history of fractures or bone pain. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has a stable body weight and does not have any significant gastrointestinal symptoms. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with operable breast cancer. She has no significant medical history, and all her organ functions are adequate. She is not currently receiving any other treatments for her breast cancer and is not taking any medications, including herbal remedies and non-prescription drugs. She has no known allergies to Vitamin E and TRF. She has a life expectancy of at least 3 months and has agreed to participate in the trial and adhere to the study protocol.

Patient is an 11-year-old boy who recently sustained a fracture to his distal radius. The fracture was classified as Salter-Harris type III and occurred during a basketball game. The patient's growth plates are open, and he is able to provide informed consent in English. The patient does not have any prior injuries to the distal radius or any known diseases that could alter bone healing or growth. There are no contraindications to undergoing an MRI scan. The patient and his parents have expressed interest in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of growth plate injuries and potentially improve the care of children with similar injuries in the future.

58 year old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and recent onset of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. The patient tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 by RT-PCR and requires urgent neurosurgical intervention for a spinal cord compression. The patient will be undergoing the surgery while in isolation with full personal protective equipment.

45-year-old female with a 7-year history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), currently receiving treatment with TNF inhibitors for the past 12 weeks with stable dosages, and methotrexate for the past 6 weeks at a stable dose. Patient reports having active RA despite the current treatment regimen. She presents with a DAS-28 score of 4.2, indicating active disease. She is compliant with her current medications and has no history of uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes, or liver disease. She has never been pregnant nor is currently breastfeeding. She is sexually active and agrees to use two forms of adequate contraception while on study medication. Her laboratory tests including hemoglobin, WBC count, platelets, serum creatinine, total bilirubin, AST, and ALT are within normal limits. The patient has no history of tuberculosis, fungal infections, or recurrent bacterial infections. Chest x-ray performed within the past 3 months is normal. She has not taken any investigational medication in the last 4 weeks. The patient is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. She has signed the informed consent form and is able to provide voluntary consent.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with symptomatic hemiparetic cerebral palsy, with right side hemiplegia since birth. He experiences difficulty with manual dexterity and has limitations in activities of daily living, such as dressing and personal hygiene. The patient underwent a clinical and MRI examination that confirmed perinatal stroke syndrome. He is able to extend his wrist and fingers to some degree, but has limited hand grip strength and cannot lift heavy objects. The patient was born at term and is currently between 6-18 years of age. The patient and their parents have provided informed consent to participate in the study. There are no neurological disorders unrelated to perinatal stroke, and the patient has no severe spasticity in the affected limb or severe developmental delays. The patient has not undergone any previous constraint, brain stimulation, or other modulatory therapy in the past 6 months.

The patient is a 32-year-old Chinese female who has recently been diagnosed with Takayasu arteritis. She has experienced claudication of the extremities, decreased brachial artery pulse, and a difference in blood pressure of over 10 mm Hg between her arms. An arterial bruit was audible on auscultation over one subclavian artery. Her arteriogram revealed narrowing of the aorta and its primary branches, indicating a segmental arterial abnormality. The patient has no history of atherosclerosis or any other infectious forms of large vessel vasculitis. She has not been treated for Takayasu arteritis previously and is willing to participate in the China Takayasu Arteritis Registry (CTA Registry) to contribute to the understanding of the disease and its treatment strategies.

A 36 year old Amish woman who is a part of the NIMH AMBiGen study for bipolar disorder is concerned about the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on her mental health. She lives in a close-knit community with limited access to healthcare and relies on her family for support. She has been feeling anxious and stressed due to the pandemic and is interested in participating in a study that examines the impact of COVID-19 on the mental health of Amish and Mennonite communities. She is willing to fill out anonymous surveys four times over 24 months and will call the research team if she has any questions or concerns. She hopes that her participation will help researchers understand the unique challenges faced by her community during the pandemic and lead to better mental health services.

A 30-year-old male athlete who regularly participates in basketball and football is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the influence of a brief application of cooling ice spray on the time to stabilization after a forward jump. He has no history of cognitive deficits or physical disability. He is currently not experiencing any pain or injuries in the previous 6 weeks. His Tegner-Activity-Scale score is 7, indicating that he regularly participates in sports at a competitive level. He has no known allergies to cooling ice spray. He is willing to follow the protocol and attend all scheduled visits required for the study.

A 72-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory problems for the past year comes to the clinic. She has been finding it difficult to remember names, appointments, and everyday tasks. She forgets where she has kept her belongings and has trouble following conversations. The patient has a family history of Alzheimer's disease, as her mother and grandfather both had the condition. The patient has been diagnosed with mild Alzheimer's disease by the physician, with a score of 24 on the Folstein Mini Mental State exam. She has a clinical dementia rating score of 1, indicating mild dementia. She has a family member who is willing to serve as an informant during the study. She has tested positive for serum antibodies to HSV1 or HSV2. She has been taking cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine, and concomitant psychotropic medications for the past year. She has no major neurological disorders and has not had a stroke with residual neurological deficits. She has no acute, severe, unstable medical illness or recent alcohol or substance use disorder. She has had a successful treatment for cancer in the past. She has a sitting blood pressure of 140/90 mm Hg and an estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate of 60 ml/min/1.73m2. She has no metal implants or pacemaker, and does not suffer from claustrophobia. She has no vision or hearing impairments that would prevent her from performing psychometric tests accurately. She has a positive attitude towards the use of anti-viral therapy for Alzheimer's disease and is willing to participate in this randomized, double-blind, 78-week Phase II proof of concept trial.

A 26-year-old male with a large tattoo on his left upper arm is interested in undergoing laser-assisted tattoo removal. He reports that the tattoo was done impulsively during his college years and has lost its significance. He is otherwise healthy with no history of chronic pain or skin disorders. The patient reports experiencing moderate to severe pain during the previous laser session and is interested in exploring options for pain management during the procedure. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has not participated in any clinical trials involving S-Caine Peel in the past.

A 70-year-old male patient was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease five years ago. The patient's main symptom is gait impairment, with frequent freezing of gait episodes, causing significant disability in daily activities. The patient is currently taking a stable dose of anti-parkinsonian medication and has not required medication adjustments. The patient is able to perform activities of daily living independently, but experiences difficulty with walking and balance. The patient scored 28 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). The patient has no history of musculoskeletal disorders or cerebellar, vestibular, or sensory ataxia. The patient has not undergone deep brain stimulation (DBS) treatment and has no history of stroke. The patient is not currently taking or has discontinued the use of monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitor drugs. The patient is a male and is not of childbearing potential. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of Methylphenidate for the treatment of gait impairment in Parkinson's disease.

A 60-year-old postmenopausal woman who has experienced amenorrhea for 2 years presents with symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. She has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. The patient is a nonsmoker and has a body mass index (BMI) of 24. She has not used any hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in the past. Her FSH levels were measured and found to be elevated (40 mIU/mL). She has not experienced any significant medical illness or surgeries in the past year, and she is not currently taking any medication that would interfere with this study. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help researchers understand the safety and effectiveness of different dosages of BZA/CE, a new experimental drug that could potentially relieve her menopausal symptoms.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has been using oral contraceptives for the past 5 years to prevent pregnancy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a transdermal contraceptive delivery system. She reports having regular menstrual cycles that occur every 28 days and last 5 days. Her last menstrual period began 14 days ago. She has never been pregnant and has never had any gynecological surgeries. She is in good health and does not smoke. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements. She has no known allergies to medications or adhesives. She understands the requirements of the study and is willing to use a non-hormonal method of contraception during the study period. She provides informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old female with a diagnosis of relapsed multiple myeloma, who has received at least one previous treatment for the condition. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, and a Karnofsky score of 80%. Her calcium level is within normal range (≤ 10.5 mg/dL) and she has not had renal stone formation in the past 5 years. She has no history of symptomatic congestive heart failure or unstable angina pectoris. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 3 months after completion. She has not had osteonecrosis of the jaw and has no history of allergic reaction to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition of calcitriol, paricalcitol, or zoledronate. It has been more than 4 weeks since her last chemotherapy treatment and she is not receiving any other concurrent investigational agents or therapies for multiple myeloma or plasma cell disorders. She is not taking digoxin.

The patient is a 19-year-old male with Down Syndrome who has recently been diagnosed with cognitive deficits. He has a legal guardian who has given consent for him to participate in this clinical trial investigating the effects of epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) on cognitive function. The patient is not currently taking any medications or supplements and has not undergone any major surgeries in the last three months. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, or renal problems. He does not follow a vegetarian diet and does not engage in physical exercise for more than 2 hours per day or consume more than 3000 kcal per week. The patient is excited to participate in the study and hopeful for potential improvements in his cognitive abilities.

A 32-year-old female came to the clinic with a history of abdominal pain and heavy menstrual bleeding. She was diagnosed with multiple uterine fibroids, including subserosal, intramural, and submucosal fibroids, based on pelvic ultrasound and MRI scans. She experiences discomfort during sexual intercourse and has difficulty conceiving due to the size and location of the fibroids. She has no history of other medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to identify and characterize the stem cell population responsible for the formation and growth of leiomyomas. She is willing to undergo surgery for tissue collection and storage for research purposes and is willing to sign an informed consent form.

The patient is a 35 year old woman living in Copenhagen, Denmark. She has no known medical conditions and is generally in good health. She is a Danish citizen and has been living in one of the 11 municipalities in Copenhagen for the past 5 years. She has no current plans for pregnancy.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for a few months. He has also been experiencing heartburn and acid reflux. He takes antacids occasionally but the symptoms still persist. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol consumption. He has no known allergies and takes no regular medications. He has not had any previous treatment for H. pylori infection. Upon referral for upper GI endoscopy, he is found to be positive for H. pylori infection through a rapid urease test. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 35-year-old male veteran diagnosed with schizophrenia presents with complaints of difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep. He reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and has tried over-the-counter sleep aids without success. He reports that he typically falls asleep around 2-3am and wakes up several times during the night, leading to daytime fatigue and difficulty concentrating. His Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) score is 18. He also reports experiencing auditory hallucinations and delusions related to his schizophrenia, but reports that these symptoms have been stable with his current medication regimen. He is currently receiving outpatient mental health services at a designated study site and has been deemed clinically stable to participate in the study. He is willing to participate in the study and has capacity to sign informed consent. He denies any problematic drug or alcohol use and has no prior diagnosis of sleep apnea in medical records.

The patient is a 22-year-old female college student who has noticed a significant weight gain in the past year. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 28, which is classified as overweight. She has tried various diets and exercise routines with limited success. She has noticed that her eating habits have become unhealthy, as she frequently indulges in fast food and sugary snacks. She also admits to not getting enough physical activity due to her busy schedule as a full-time student. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to address her weight gain and improve her overall health. She has no history of eating disorders or sleep apnea. She is not currently taking any prescription drugs for weight loss or disordered eating behaviors. She is motivated to make lifestyle changes to improve her health and is willing to attend the weekly group sessions as part of the intervention.

A healthy non-smoking male or female between the ages of 18 to 50 with a body mass index (BMI) between 18.5 and 29.9 kg/m2 is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. The participant should not be currently taking any medication, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) or herbal remedies, within 2 weeks before the first administration of Investigational medicinal product (IMP). The participant should not have a history of hypersensitivity or allergy to diclofenac or any related medication, cayenne pepper or other capsaicinoids (paprika plants). The participant should not have a history of bronchospasm or bronchial asthma, arterial hypertension, myocardial infarction, thrombotic events, stroke, congestive heart failure, impaired renal function, or liver disease. They should not have any relevant history or laboratory or clinical findings indicative of acute or chronic disease likely to influence study outcome. The participant should not have any bruises, damaged skin, eczema, or wounds on the application site, or the application site inappropriate for applying the IMP in the opinion of the PI (Principal Investigator).

As this clinical trial is focused on neonates born to parents living in low income countries, a patient description could be:  The patient is a newborn baby boy born at a rural clinic in Ghana. His parents are both farmers and live in a small village without access to clean water or basic sanitation facilities. They have limited access to healthcare and are not familiar with the concept of clinical trials. The baby was delivered vaginally at full term with a birth weight of 2.8 kg. He is the first child of his parents and they are both excited and worried about caring for him. The baby has no known health issues at this time, but is at risk of developing severe bacterial infections due to the limited access to healthcare and sanitation in his community. His parents have been approached by the clinic staff about participation in the ChARLI program and have agreed to learn more about the study.

42-year-old female with a history of abnormal vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain presents to the gynecological oncology clinic with a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. Biopsy confirmed primary, locally advanced cervical cancer with FIGO 2008 stage 3B. PET scan showed the absence of distant metastases. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate hematologic, renal, and hepatic function. The patient has not had any prior radiation or chemotherapy for this tumor, and she has not been diagnosed with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis. She has no history of serious illness or medical conditions that would preclude the safe administration of the trial treatment. The patient has signed an informed consent form and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the survival difference between weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 and tri-weekly cisplatin 75 mg/m2 administration concurrent to radiation therapy in locally advanced cervical cancer.

This is a 20 year-old male who is a student-athlete at Brock University. He is currently participating in a varsity sport and has experienced some difficulties with his mental health in the past. He has expressed interest in learning more about mental health and how to support his own mental wellness. He is willing to participate in an online mental health in sport module and complete surveys at pre-intervention, post-intervention, 3-months and 6-month time points. He understands that he will be randomly assigned to either the mental health module or the waitlist condition. He is excited to contribute to research on mental health in student-athletes and hopes that his participation will help improve mental health literacy and reduce stigma among his peers.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with multiple chronic medical conditions, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and osteoarthritis. He has been living with his wife for over 30 years, and they have two adult children who live nearby. He works as a middle manager in a large company and enjoys spending time with his family and reading in his free time. He reports feeling overwhelmed at times by his health conditions and struggles to communicate his feelings with his wife. He has a good command of both written and spoken German. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how he and his wife can cope with their health situations together. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 4 weeks and does not have any substance abuse issues. He provides written consent for participation and his wife is also interested in participating.

The patient is a 63-year-old man admitted to Boston Medical Center for shortness of breath and cough. He has a history of smoking for over 40 years, with an average of one pack per day. He has tried to quit smoking multiple times but has been unsuccessful. His CT scan shows signs of emphysema, which is likely due to his smoking history. During his hospitalization, he is approached by a thoracic oncology nurse who informs him that he is eligible for an LDCT screening for lung cancer and provides him with a decision aid to help him make an informed decision. The nurse also provides him with smoking cessation counseling and resources to help him quit smoking. The patient is willing to participate in the study and gives his informed consent. He is randomized into the group that receives the inpatient SDM intervention. After a month, he reports that he has cut down his smoking significantly and has scheduled an LDCT screening appointment. He feels more knowledgeable about the benefits and risks of LDCT screening and is grateful for the intervention that helped him take steps towards improving his health.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a BMI of 31. He was diagnosed with metabolic syndrome characterized by a waist circumference of 100 cm and high blood pressure (145/90 mmHg) and triglyceride level (2.0 g/L). He has been on medication for the last 6 months to control his blood pressure and triglyceride levels. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any other medical conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of the dietary supplement STABLOR™ on the change of his abdominal visceral fat mass. He is willing to follow the study protocol for the duration of the study and is committed to maintaining his current medication regimen. He understands that the study may involve dietary changes and the consumption of a supplement, and he is willing to comply with these requirements.

10-year-old female diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) at age 6. She has been receiving treatment for her condition and her symptoms have been well controlled. She is currently attending school and participating in extracurricular activities. Her parents are interested in her participation in clinical research to help advance the understanding and treatment of JIA. They have read and understood the informed consent document and are willing to comply with the study procedures. The patient is in overall good health and does not have any other medical conditions.

A 21-year-old male, previously institutionalized in Bucharest, Romania during infancy, is being recruited for the Bucharest Early Intervention Project. The male was abandoned at birth and placed in an institution where he remained until the age of 22 months. At that time, he was randomly assigned to high-quality foster care as part of the BEIP study. He has been assessed at 30 months, 42 months, 54 months, 8 years and 12 years of age as part of the study. He is now being approached to participate in the final assessment at 21 years of age. He has no history of open or closed head injury or bacterial or viral meningitis within the past 12 months. He is willing and able to participate in the assessment.

42-year-old female with a history of gastroparesis, confirmed by radiologic studies, presenting with early satiety, postprandial bloating, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Patient has not undergone any surgical interventions except for an appendectomy and cholecystectomy. No history of ulcer disease. Patient has not received any prior treatment with botox. She has been prescribed various prokinetic agents with limited efficacy and bothersome side effects. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of botox injection for the treatment of gastroparesis.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who recently had a transient ischemic attack (TIA) and was diagnosed with 70-99% stenosis of a major intracranial artery (carotid artery, MCA stem (M1), vertebral artery, or basilar artery). He is currently taking aspirin and clopidogrel and has been advised to manage his blood pressure and cholesterol levels. He has no history of cardiac disease or other medical conditions that would conflict with the study. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the purpose of the trial. The patient will be available for all follow-up visits required by the protocol and is willing to use contraception for the duration of the study. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to be randomized to either intensive medical therapy alone or intracranial angioplasty and stenting using the Gateway balloon and Wingspan self-expanding nitinol stent. The patient has no history of severe calcification at the target lesion or intraluminal thrombus proximal to the target lesion. He has no progressive neurological signs within 24 hours prior to enrollment and no history of a primary intracerebral (parenchymal) hemorrhage (ICH). The patient has no history of an untreated chronic subdural hematoma of greater than 5 mm in thickness. He has not undergone stenting, angioplasty, or endarterectomy of an extracranial (carotid or vertebral artery) or intracranial artery within 30 days prior to expected enrollment date. The patient meets all eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

A 68-year-old male with a history of hypertension presents with abdominal pain and discomfort. He underwent a routine abdominal ultrasound that revealed the presence of an abdominal aortic aneurysm. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and has no known allergies.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. Her current treatment plan includes pioglitazone hydrochloride and metformin hydrochloride separately. However, her physician has recommended her to switch to Metact Combination Tablets due to her inadequate response to the current treatment plan. She has no history of cardiac insufficiency or lactic acidosis, and her renal and hepatic functions are normal. She is not pregnant or potentially pregnant. She is willing to participate in the study to investigate the safety and efficacy of long-term use of Metact Combination Tablets.

The patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man presenting to the emergency department with acute chest pain that started 6 hours ago. He describes the pain as a squeezing sensation in the center of his chest that radiates to his left arm. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but he is not currently taking any medications. He denies any shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. His vital signs are within normal limits. An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST-segment depression in leads V1-V4. The patient is a candidate for further evaluation and management for possible acute coronary syndrome. The patient is able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 23-year-old female patient with a diagnosis of neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1) presents with multiple plexiform neurofibromas. The patient reports an increase in size and discomfort of the tumors within the past year. The tumors are located in the neck/mediastinum region and are causing disfigurement and functional impairment. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. She has not received any prior or concurrent chemotherapy and is not currently enrolled in any chemotherapy clinical trial. The patient has not undergone radiotherapy in the past 6 weeks. Prior surgery for the progressive plexiform neurofibromas is allowed if incompletely resected and measurable disease remains, which is the case for this patient. She is eligible for Stratum 2 of the clinical trial and is currently enrolled in a clinical therapeutic trial at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing cluster headaches for the past 5 years. He has been diagnosed with chronic cluster headaches according to the International Headache Society criteria. His headache periods last approximately 2 months, and attacks respond to oxygen. He has tried multiple medications for his headaches, including triptans and verapamil, but has not found significant relief. He is currently not taking any preventive medication but occasionally uses oxygen to abort his attacks. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications other than occasional over-the-counter pain relief medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He understands the study procedures and risks associated with the study and is willing to adhere to the study procedures and sign the consent form. He is willing to abstain from taking preventive and abortive medication (except for oxygen) long enough before and after the LSD/placebo treatment session to avoid the possibility of a drug-drug interaction. He is willing to refrain from taking any psychiatric medications during the experimental session period. He agrees to not ingest alcohol-containing beverages for at least 1 day before each LSD treatment session. He is willing not to drive a traffic vehicle or to operate machines within 24 hours after LSD/placebo administration. He weighs 70 kg and has no contraindications for the study.

The patient is a 62 year old female diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) of subtype RAEB I. She has a history of mild iron overload with serum ferritin levels ranging from 350 µg/l to 1100 µg/l over the past 3 months. She is transfusion dependent, receiving red blood cell transfusions every 2-3 weeks due to low hemoglobin levels (Hb < 10.5 g/dl). The patient has not received any previous cytostatic drugs, thalidomide, lenalidomide, G-CSF or EPO. She has no indication for stem cell transplantation. The patient is of sound mind and has provided informed consent. She has no intolerance to deferasirox or other chelation therapy. She has no concomitant second malignant disease that may interfere with life expectancy. Her mean levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) are within normal limits. She does not have uncontrolled systemic hypertension, and her serum creatinine levels are within normal limits. She has no history of nephrotic syndrome, and her systemic diseases will not prevent her from undergoing the study treatment. She has no psychiatric or addictive disorders that may prevent her from giving informed consent or undergoing study treatment. She has not been treated with systemic investigational drugs within the past 4 weeks or topical investigational drugs within the past 7 days. She has no surgical or medical conditions that might significantly alter the absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion of any drug. She meets the eligibility criteria for the Exjade-Early-Trial and will be enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 6-week-old Pakistani infant who is healthy and free of any serious medical condition. The parents or guardians have provided written informed consent for the infant to be enrolled in a rotavirus vaccine immunogenicity clinical trial in Karachi, Pakistan. The infant has not been previously immunized against rotavirus and has not received any investigational drug or vaccine within the last 30 days. The infant has not undergone any abdominal surgery and has not received any immunosuppressive drugs. The infant's birth weight is above 2000 grams and there is no history of immunoglobulin or blood product use since birth. The infant has provided a baseline fecal sample before receiving the Rotarix vaccine. The parents or guardians have also provided written informed consent for the infant to participate in a nested case-control study to compare the fecal microbiota composition and diversity of infants who demonstrate immune seroconversion to rotavirus vaccination (control) and those who do not (case).

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was admitted to the emergency department with chest pain that started 3 hours ago.
