The ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4, and blood tests revealed elevated levels of troponin. The patient was diagnosed with ST elevation acute myocardial infarction (STEMI) and underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within the first hour of admission. The echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction (EF) of 45% and segmentary dysfunction of the infarction area. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the Cell Therapy in Myocardial Infarction clinical trial, as he has an EF ≤ 50%, measured between the 3rd and 5th day post AMI, and segmentary dysfunction of the infarction area. He is between the ages of 30 and 80 and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no history of illicit drug or alcohol abuse, nor any other co-morbidities that would exclude him from the clinical trial.

Samantha is a 25-year-old woman who has a history of seasonal allergies. She suffers from sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes every time there is a change of season. She has been diagnosed with allergic asthma by her primary care physician. Samantha is allergic to Timothy grass pollen and has been experiencing coughing and wheezing for the past few weeks due to the increased pollen count in her area. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or caffeine, and has not had any major surgeries. She is not currently pregnant nor breastfeeding. She is willing to use birth control throughout the study period. Samantha has not taken any NSAIDs for the past month and is willing to avoid them throughout the study. She is interested in participating in the study to help with the development of new treatments for her condition.

Patient is a 35-year-old male with a long-standing history of primary premature ejaculation. He has been in a stable heterosexual relationship for the past 6 years. The patient reports that he has always experienced premature ejaculation during sexual intercourse, with an intravaginal ejaculatory latency time (IELT) of less than 60 seconds. This has caused the patient significant distress and has negatively impacted his sexual relationship with his partner. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of liver disease, prostatitis, or other medical or psychiatric conditions that may affect his ability to participate in the study. The patient reports that he does not smoke and does not consume alcohol regularly. The patient is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his sexual performance and overall quality of life.

55-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and CAD. He is scheduled for an elective non-cardiac vascular surgery with a high or intermediate surgical risk. He has no history of congestive heart failure, arrhythmias, or pulmonary disease. He is not on chemotherapy or bleomycin treatment. His preoperative oxygen saturation on room air is above 95%. He has no scheduled surgery in the thoracic cavity. He has no signs of systemic inflammatory response syndrome or sepsis. He is not pregnant. His baseline hs-TnT level is below 65ng/L. He is willing to provide written informed consent for the study.

Pt is a 70yo F with no significant medical history, who is currently retired and enjoys reading and crossword puzzles. She reports some occasional forgetfulness but nothing that has significantly impacted her daily living or work. She speaks English as her primary language and has no issues with hearing or vision. She is interested in participating in a study that will help her maintain cognitive function and potentially improve her memory.

A 25 year old male patient with a history of epilepsy since the age of 15 came to the clinic seeking better control of his seizures. He has been experiencing nocturnal seizures for the past 6 months, which have been affecting his quality of life as he is unable to get a good night's sleep. He has been on anti-epileptic medication for the past 10 years but has been struggling with side effects such as drowsiness and fatigue. His latest EEG showed evidence of seizure activity during sleep. In the physical exam, he was alert and oriented to person, place, and time, with no focal neurological deficits. He has no history of diabetes or renal failure. He is not on any medication for cardiac conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and has the capacity to consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate COPD. He has a history of smoking for over 30 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. He has a family history of lung disease. He is currently taking albuterol inhaler as needed for his COPD symptoms. He has no other significant medical conditions except for occasional seasonal allergies. He is willing to comply with study restrictions and participate in all required tests. His post-bronchodilator FEV1 is above 50% of predicted value at the time of enrollment. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 30 days.

The patient is a 52 year-old man who has been struggling with obesity for the past 10 years. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and sleep apnea. His current BMI is 49 kg/m² and he has not had success with previous weight loss treatments. He is interested in undergoing a laparoscopic gastric by-pass surgery to help with his weight loss goals. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently taking medications for his hypertension and diabetes. He has health insurance and is willing to participate in a 6-month follow-up before and after the surgery. He has not had any previous gastric surgeries or complications related to gastric lap-band.

The patient is a 42-year-old man with a BMI of 42 kg/m². He has a history of severe obesity and has tried various weight loss programs in the past without much success. He complains of fatigue, shortness of breath, and difficulty with physical activities. He has no history of diabetes, heart, kidney or liver failure. His physical exam is significant for obesity, with a waist circumference of 115 cm. His lab workup shows high triglycerides, low HDL, and normal liver and kidney function. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. He is not taking any medications except for occasional over-the-counter pain relief. He is interested in participating in a study that involves a very low carbohydrate ketogenic diet for weight loss and metabolic improvement.

A 47-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, and she is finding it difficult to remain physically active due to the pain and discomfort caused by the disease. She has tried exercising on her own but has not been able to maintain a consistent routine. She is interested in participating in a physical activity programme that is delivered outside of a secondary care setting, and she has expressed a desire for more information on how to exercise without exacerbating her symptoms. She is able to speak and understand English and is willing to provide informed consent for the study. She does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

10-year-old girl with a diagnosis of Pervasive Developmental Disorder Not Otherwise Specified (PDD NOS) is being evaluated for a clinical trial studying the effectiveness and tolerability of aripiprazole in the management of maladaptive behaviors associated with PDD. The patient has a history of significant irritability as determined by a Clinical Global Impression Severity score of 4 (Moderately ill) and a score of 18 on the Aberrant Behavior Checklist Irritability Subscale. She is medication-free for at least 2 days prior to screening laboratory tests and electrocardiogram (ECG). She has no comorbid disorder with possible association to autism, nor does she have a significant medical condition such as heart, liver, renal, or pulmonary disease, or a seizure disorder. She has no history of an adequate trial of aripiprazole and is not hypersensitive to aripiprazole. Her IQ is greater than 50 based on the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). She is a suitable candidate for the study as determined by the investigator.

The patient is a 32-year-old Caucasian male complaining of gradual blurring of vision in both eyes for the past year. The blurring is worse in the right eye, which is also associated with occasional halos around light sources. He has never worn glasses or contact lenses before. He is not using any medications and has no significant past medical history. His family history is negative for any ocular or systemic diseases. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/60 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. Slit-lamp examination reveals bilateral corneal thinning, stromal haze, and a Fleischer ring in the right eye. Corneal topography confirms the diagnosis of keratoconus with a Kmax value of 53.5 in the right eye and 48.2 in the left eye. Central corneal thickness is 372 microns in the right eye and 395 microns in the left eye. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve corneal thickness and visual acuity in patients with keratoconus using fresh lenticule implantation with Relex Smile surgery.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 8 and a PSA level of 12 ng/mL. He has undergone conventional staging examinations, including a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis, and whole-body bone scintigraphy. He is a candidate for curative prostatectomy or curative radiotherapy. However, he is deemed to be at intermediate or high risk for recurrence or metastatic disease after initial curative treatment. His PSA level has not responded to previous treatment options. The patient is not claustrophobic and is willing to undergo positron emission tomography using carbon-11 acetate (AC-PET) imaging to help guide his treatment plan.

Maria is a 52-year-old woman who has been experiencing discomfort in her stomach for the past few weeks. She has a history of indigestion and heartburn and has been taking antacids to relieve her symptoms. She went to see her doctor, and after undergoing a ^13C-urea breath test, she was diagnosed with Helicobacter pylori (HP) infection. Her physician recommended her to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the efficacy and safety of bismuth-containing quadruple therapy with oral vonoprazan (TAK-438) 20 mg compared to esomeprazole 20 mg twice daily in patients with HP infection. Maria has no history of malignancy, hepatitis infection, or any other serious medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and is excited to learn more about potential treatments for her HP infection.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of relapsing-remitting MS 5 years ago. She complains of fatigue and heat sensitivity while walking. She uses a walking aid and is able to walk up to 20 meters without stopping. She has no history of relapse for the past 6 months. Her past medical history is significant for depression, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of other medical conditions. Her family history is negative for MS. Her lab study is as below: FBS: 95 mg/dL HbA1c: 5.8% Cholesterol: 165 mg/dL TG: 85 mg/dL LDL: 90 mg/dL HDL: 55 mg/dL.

A 54-year-old male with previous medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. The patient also complains of occasional shortness of breath and swollen lymph nodes in the neck. Physical examination reveals enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, axillae, and groin. Blood work showed elevated white blood cell count (WBC) with lymphocytosis. Further workup confirmed the diagnosis of untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) according to iwCLL / WHO criteria. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for CLL treatment and meets the eligibility criteria, including having a CIRS score ≤ 6, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status of 0 or 1, and adequate hematologic, renal, and liver function. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is not using warfarin and has not received any previous CLL-directed therapy. The patient is a non-smoker and has no known allergies to the study drugs, venetoclax and obinutuzumab. The patient is willing to use effective contraception during the study period as required by the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman in her third trimester of pregnancy with a singleton pregnancy. She has a history of gestational diabetes during her previous pregnancy. She is currently on a controlled diet and moderate exercise regimen to manage her blood sugar levels. She intends to breastfeed her newborn and has no prior history of breastfeeding difficulties. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and her alcohol intake is limited to occasional social drinking. She has no significant medical history or comorbidities. Her blood pressure is within normal limits, and her blood work is unremarkable. She has no family history of obesity or diabetes. She is willing to participate in the study and attend all study visits and phone call interviews.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has just been diagnosed with hypertension during a routine check-up. Her blood pressure readings have been consistently elevated, and she is currently not taking any medication for hypertension. She has no significant medical history, including no history of diabetes, renal disease, heart disease, sleep apnea, or any other chronic illnesses. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been wearing soft contact lenses for the past 5 years. She has no history of eye diseases or conditions and is currently not taking any systemic or ocular medications. She has a manifest cylinder of less than or equal to 1.50 diopter in each eye and a best-corrected visual acuity better than or equal to 20/25 Snellen in each eye. She is willing to stop wearing her habitual contact lenses for the duration of the study lens exposure and during the washout period. She has no history of dry eye and is not currently using artificial tears.

The patient is a 55 year old man with a history of hepatitis B and cirrhosis. A recent ultrasound revealed a solitary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with a diameter of 4cm. He has not received any previous treatment for HCC and his liver function is classified as Child-Pugh class A. His platelet count is 50,000/mm3 and his prothrombin time is within normal limits. He is otherwise healthy with no history of cardiac, pulmonary, cerebral or renal dysfunction. He understands the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has noticed a mole on her back changing in appearance over the past few months. She has also noticed some other smaller moles appearing on her arms and legs. She has fair skin and a history of sunburns in her youth. The patient is generally in good health and has no other medical history. She is willing to participate in the study to contribute to the advancement of skin cancer research. The patient understands the biopsy procedure and is willing to have skin biopsies done on the suspicious areas on her back, arms, and legs. She has no known allergies or contraindications to the biopsy procedure. The patient is not pregnant. She is interested in learning more about skin cancer prevention and treatment options.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past year. The pain is located in the lower back and radiates down to her legs. She has tried various conservative treatments such as physical therapy and pain medication, but none have provided long-term relief. Imaging studies have revealed degenerative disc disease at the L4-L5 level. She has a history of smoking but is willing to quit for the study. She has no allergies to titanium and has not participated in another investigational study in the past 30 days. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and meets all the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with migraines for the past 10 years. She has been experiencing severe headaches that last for hours and often accompanied by nausea, vomiting and sensitivity to light and sound. She has been taking medication to control the pain, but she still experiences migraines at least once a week, which disrupts her daily activities. She is interested in trying complementary and supportive therapies to cope with pain during a migraine attack. She has never tried aromatherapy massage before but is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She is fluent in Turkish, literate and has no communication problems. She has no history of any psychiatric disorders and her vital signs are within normal limits.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. She has never received antiretroviral treatment before and her CD4 cell count is 350 cells/mm3. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has been experiencing occasional fatigue and mild headaches. Her viral load at the time of diagnosis was 75,000 copies/mL. She has been confirmed to have CCR5-tropic-only virus and does not have any primary resistance mutations or phenotypic resistance to TDF, FTC, or EFV, nor any mutations associated with multidrug nucleoside/nucleotide resistance. She does not have any history of hepatitis B or C, cirrhosis of the liver, or any known active or chronic liver disease. She is not currently pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant during the study period. The patient is able to comply with the study protocol and is willing to take the study medications as prescribed. She speaks and understands English fluently and is available for all study visits.

24-week-old male infant, born at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 980 grams, diagnosed with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), requiring invasive mechanical ventilation since birth. The infant has had multiple episodes of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and has been treated with surfactant therapy. The most recent tracheal aspirate culture was positive for pathogenic Gram-negative bacteria. The infant has a serum creatinine level of 0.2mg/dL and no known congenital or acquired disease of the kidney or liver. The infant has not received any systemic antibiotics in the past seven days and is not on any nephrotoxic medication or neuromuscular blocker. The infant's endotracheal tube leak is <20%. The family has provided informed consent for the infant's participation in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after presenting with abdominal pain, jaundice, and unintentional weight loss. Imaging studies confirmed the HCC. He has previously undergone transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) therapy and has residual measurable tumor. His liver function tests are within normal limits, and his Child-Pugh score is A. He has no history of other malignancies or organ transplants. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. He has a performance status score of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale. His absolute neutrophil count, hemoglobin, platelet count, and blood creatinine are all within normal ranges. He has no history of significant cardiovascular disease or serious autoimmune disease. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with her partner. She has regular menstrual cycles and no known fertility issues. Her partner has normal sperm parameters, with a concentration of 20 million per ml and progressive motility of 40%. They have decided to undergo IVF with Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidies. The patient's BMI is 26 kg/m2, and she is of Arab descent. She has never undergone IVF before and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the optimal incubation time for oocytes. Her ovarian stimulation protocol will be determined by her physician. She has not been diagnosed with PCO and her progesterone levels are within normal limits. She and her partner are excited to participate in the study and hope it will increase their chances of a successful IVF cycle.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. She has been experiencing symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized thinking for the past 2 years. She has been taking antipsychotic medication for the past 6 months, including olanzapine, but has noticed that she has gained significant weight since starting the medication. She is concerned about her weight gain and how it may affect her overall health. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the underlying mechanism of antipsychotic-induced metabolic disturbances and to develop efficient treatments. She has not received any other second-generation antipsychotics prior to this study and does not have any medical conditions that may confound glucoregulatory assessment. She is willing to undergo regular assessments of her metabolic profile, including anthropometrical parameters, body composition, glucose level, insulin level, lipid profile, and leptin level, to help advance the understanding and treatment of this issue.

This is a 35 year-old female who was diagnosed with Graves' disease 6 months ago. She presents with symptoms of hyperthyroidism including palpitations, weight loss, and difficulty sleeping. She reported a history of cigarette smoking for the past 10 years, smoking half a pack per day. She was started on methimazole and propranolol, and her symptoms have improved. She has a family history of autoimmune diseases including type 1 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the genetic polymorphisms associated with cigarette smoking and Graves' disease.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been experiencing pain in her right leg for the past few months. She reports difficulty walking and numbness in the affected leg. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has never had any surgeries or interventions for her leg pain. Physical examination reveals decreased pulses in the right foot and ankle, and a cool temperature in the affected limb. There is no evidence of skin changes or ulcers. An ultrasound shows a femoral-popliteal lesion in the right leg that is classified as TASC-C. The patient has a continuous permeable leg axis and is classified as Rutherford 3. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the contribution of Optical Coherence Tomography in the endovascular treatment of femoral occlusions.

52-year-old male smoker with a 35 pack-year smoking history is scheduled for a routine primary care visit next week. The patient has tried to quit smoking multiple times in the past but has been unsuccessful. He is interested in learning more about lung cancer screening and potentially quitting smoking for good. The patient has a family history of lung cancer and is concerned about his risk. The patient is fluent in English and is willing to participate in a smoking cessation program. He has no history of lung cancer.

A 27-year-old primigravida woman presented to the labor and delivery unit at 39 weeks of gestation with regular contractions and ruptured membranes. She had an unremarkable prenatal course with no history of medical or surgical illness. She denied any drug or tobacco use and had no known allergies. Her vital signs were stable, and fetal monitoring showed a category I tracing. On examination, her cervix was 4 cm dilated and 80% effaced with a fetal station of -2. The patient consented to participate in the clinical trial assessing pelvis diameters as a predictor for the mode of delivery. She met all the inclusion criteria and had no exclusion criteria. The labor pro ultrasound measurement of her pelvic diameters was taken, and the results were recorded. The patient was managed according to the standard of care for labor management. After several hours of labor, the patient progressed to full cervical dilation with a fetal station of +2. She was encouraged to push, and within 30 minutes, she delivered a 3.2 kg healthy baby girl via normal vaginal delivery.

28yo woman in her first pregnancy, at 38 weeks gestation, with a cephalic presentation, who presents to the labor and delivery unit with regular contractions and ruptured membranes. She has no history of any chronic medical conditions and her pregnancy has been uncomplicated. The patient has received written information about the study and is willing to participate. She is randomized to the group receiving the modified Ritgen´s maneuver during delivery.

A 55-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to control his blood pressure. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and his oxygen saturation level is at 92% on room air. He has no known allergies to any medications. He has never participated in any clinical trials before and understands the procedures and requirements of the study. He is willing to provide written informed consent and authorize the disclosure of protected health information.

The patient is a 22-year-old female college student who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her foot skin hydration. She has no known medical conditions and has never had any foot-related injuries or surgeries. She is currently not using any creams or lotions on her feet at night. She is an avid runner and spends a lot of time on her feet. She describes her skin as dry and sometimes experiences cracking and irritation on her heels. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to find a cream that will help improve the hydration of her feet.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer after complaints of chronic cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath. Biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or biological therapy. He has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has no CNS metastases or other primary malignancies. He is not eligible for combined modality therapy with curative intent. He has at least one measurable lesion and is willing to participate in a clinical trial testing a combination of OGX-011, gemcitabine and cisplatin or carboplatin.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with alcohol dependence for the past 5 years. She drinks an average of 25 drinks per week and has been unable to quit on her own. She has no other psychiatric disorders besides alcohol dependence and is in good physical health as determined by a complete physical examination and laboratory screening tests. She answered an advertisement in the newspaper expressing her wish to stop drinking and is willing to participate in behavioral treatments for alcoholism. She is literate in English and able to read, understand, and complete the rating scales and questionnaires accurately. She has a stable residence and no plans to move in the next three months. She has not received inpatient or outpatient treatment for alcohol dependence within the last 30 days and is not being treated with any medication with potential for clinically significant interactions with alcohol or olanzapine and/or ondansetron. She is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to adhere to an acceptable form of contraception during the study. She has never had a seizure disorder, diabetes, or any severe or life-threatening reaction to olanzapine or ondansetron. She is not pending imprisonment.

A 6-week-old male infant who was delivered full-term via spontaneous vaginal delivery presents to the pediatric clinic with a history of excessive crying and fussiness for more than 3 hours per day, occurring for more than 3 consecutive days in a week, for the past 2 weeks. The infant is exclusively breastfed, and the mother denies any significant dietary changes. The infant has been gaining weight appropriately, and there are no other significant medical or surgical histories. The mother does not smoke or consume alcohol, and there is no history of drug abuse in the family. The infant's physical exam is unremarkable, and there are no signs of abdominal distension or tenderness. The infant's bowel movements are normal, and there is no blood in the stool. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the efficacy of Lactocare Baby Drops in infants with colic, and the mother is interested in participating in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with no known medical conditions. He has a BMI of 23 and weighs 70 kg. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or any drugs. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no known allergies and takes no medications. His blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 70 beats per minute. His physical examination, hematology, clinical chemistry, urinalysis, vital signs, and ECG at baseline are all within normal limits. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and visits and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

There is no patient required for this clinical trial as it is a study of the intestinal microbiome of human caretakers and captive great apes. However, eligible participants for the study are adult caretakers who are in good health and currently working with captive great apes. They must agree to provide a stool sample for the study and be observed during their professional activity by the researchers. They cannot be protected adults, pregnant or nursing mothers, or have gastrointestinal disorders or chronic diseases. They must not have taken antibiotics or antifungal treatment in the month preceding the collection of their stool sample.

A 32-year-old female with a history of chronic idiopathic urticaria presents with persistent symptoms despite treatment with standard-dosed H1 antihistamines. She reports experiencing hives, itching, and swelling on a daily basis for the past 6 months. She has no known allergies or other medical conditions. She currently takes cetirizine and ranitidine daily, but has not noticed any improvement in her symptoms. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of omalizumab as an add-on therapy for the treatment of her refractory chronic idiopathic urticaria. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced esophageal cancer. He presents with difficulty swallowing and chest discomfort. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. He is married with two children and works as a sales representative. His performance status is 1 and he is able to carry out most daily activities without assistance. His lab results are within normal limits, and he has no evidence of distant metastasis. He is willing to use an effective contraceptive method during the study period. He has not received previous radiotherapy or chemotherapy. He is able to provide written informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with a weakened immune system due to a history of chemotherapy for lymphoma. Recently, he has been experiencing persistent fever and shortness of breath. A CT scan of his chest revealed a possible fungal infection. His laboratory results showed elevated liver function tests (AST: 3 times ULN and alkaline phosphatase: 4 times ULN) but normal renal function (creatinine clearance: 70 mL/min). He has no known drug allergies and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. He has not received any antifungal therapy in the past 14 days and is not currently taking any of the medications listed as exclusions for this trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with esophageal cancer. He is a smoker and has a history of heavy alcohol consumption. He has been experiencing dysphagia, unintentional weight loss, and occasional chest pain. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. He underwent endoscopy and biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. The tumor is located in the lower third of the esophagus and is deemed resectable. He is scheduled to undergo esophagectomy surgery. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial to contribute to the advancement of understanding the prognostic factors related to lymph node involvement in esophageal cancer.

A 56-year-old man with a recent diagnosis of locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the esophagus is currently undergoing treatment. He has received potentially curative chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and/or surgery within the past 1-3 months. The patient has no evidence of residual tumor or metastatic disease after undergoing potentially curative therapy, and there were no positive margins at the time of prior surgery. The patient has no measurable or evaluable disease. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is expected to have a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has a platelet count of 120,000/mm^3 and an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm^3. The patient has a bilirubin level of 1.5 mg/dL and creatinine level within the upper limit of normal. The patient has no New York Heart Association class III or IV heart disease. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and a negative pregnancy test was confirmed. The patient is willing to use effective contraception and is able to swallow the study drug. The patient has not previously received gefitinib and is not taking any concurrent CYP3A4 inducing agents or antacids 4 hours before or after study drug administration.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman with a history of ovarian cancer, who received carboplatin and paclitaxel as part of her chemotherapy regimen. She is experiencing chronic, debilitating pain in her lower extremities that has been ongoing for over 3 months. Her pain is rated as a 7 out of 10 on the pain scale, and she has been taking gabapentinoids, including pregabalin, to manage her pain, but with little relief. She has undergone multiple diagnostic tests, including nerve conduction studies, which have confirmed the diagnosis of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN). The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Scrambler Therapy with the Calmare MC5-A machine in relieving her CIPN pain. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including having a life expectancy of more than 3 months, an ECOG Performance Status of 0-3, and understanding the study's requirements, risks, and discomforts. She is willing to sign an informed consent form and is not pregnant, nursing, or unwilling to employ adequate contraception.

42 yo F with a history of hypertension and a BMI of 29. She was incidentally found to have fatty liver on a recent CT scan that was done to evaluate her hypertension. She reports occasional alcohol consumption, but denies any significant alcohol intake. She takes hydrochlorothiazide for her hypertension and has no significant past medical history. She is interested in participating in a study to determine if there is a relationship between her iron status and her fatty liver disease. She is able to provide informed consent and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 15-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) type 3. She is able to walk independently for short distances but experiences fatigue and difficulty with physical activity. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial of exercise as an intervention for SMA. She enjoys bike riding and lifting weights as hobbies and is excited to potentially improve her physical function through participation in the study. She has not used any investigational medications intended for the treatment of SMA in the last 30 days and does not have any coexisting medical conditions that would contraindicate moderate intensity exercise. Her parents have provided written informed consent for her participation in the study.

A 52-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of high blood pressure despite being on antihypertensive therapy for the past year. He had a screening diagnosis of isolated systolic hypertension, with a systolic blood pressure of 155 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure of 80 mm Hg (office blood pressure measurements). His echocardiography showed no left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). His latest lab results showed a serum creatinine level of 1.4 mg/dL and an Hb A1c level of 6.8%. He has no history of congestive heart failure, stroke, or any significant ECG abnormalities. He is a nonsmoker and does not use any tobacco or nicotine-containing products, caffeine-containing beverages or food, or alcohol. He is willing to comply with the protocol and complete an informed consent.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy with a past medical history of chronic asthma. He has had at least one asthma exacerbation associated with a cold in the past year and has required treatment with asthma medication within the last 6 months. He is a non-smoker and has no other acute or chronic pulmonary disorders. He is about to start the new school year and his parents are concerned about his asthma worsening during this time. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of montelukast in reducing the number of days of worsening asthma during the first 8 weeks of school.

The patient is a 30 year old woman who has been suffering from excessive sweating in her underarms, which has been interfering with her daily activities and causing social embarrassment. She has tried various antiperspirants and home remedies, but nothing has provided long-lasting relief. She has a history of no medical conditions or allergies and is currently not taking any medication. Her pregnancy test is negative. She is willing to follow the instructions of the clinical trial and can continue until the end.

45 yo M smoker of at least 15 cigarettes/day of a brand delivering > 0.5mg nicotine according to the standard Federal Trade Commission (FTC) method with no interest in quitting smoking as measured by self-report. The patient reports generally good health with no significant health problems such as chronic hypertension, emphysema, seizure disorder, or history of significant heart problems. The patient has no current alcohol or drug abuse and does not use psychoactive medications. The patient is not using nicotine replacement therapy or any other smoking cessation treatment. The patient is right-handed as measured by a three-item scale used in the laboratory. The patient is willing and able to attend all required experimental sessions and has no contraindications for MRI. The patient is eligible to participate in this study.

A 62-year-old male smoker with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with a persistent cough for the past 4 months. He reports occasional shortness of breath on exertion and unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds over the past 2 months. He denies any hemoptysis or chest pain. A chest X-ray showed a right upper lobe mass, and further evaluation with a PET scan revealed multiple lung nodules with increased metabolic activity consistent with non-small cell lung cancer. A biopsy of the lung mass confirmed the diagnosis. The patient has no prior treatment for his cancer, and brain imaging did not show any metastases. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no history of deep vein thromboses or pulmonary embolus. His laboratory values are within normal limits, with no proteinuria detected. He is a former heavy smoker, having quit 5 years ago, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has no history of gross hemoptysis, and his hypertension is well-controlled with medications.

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with asthma since the age of 14. He has been on the same regular treatment for the past 6 months and has not smoked for over a year. He has a prebronchodilator FEV1 of 70% of the predicted value and has demonstrated reversible airway obstruction. He has no history of respiratory infection in the past 4 weeks and has no other severe chronic respiratory disease. He has no other concurrent illnesses and has normal serum potassium levels and blood pressure. He is not taking any drugs that prolong the QT-interval. He is not currently participating in another clinical drug study, and he has provided written informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He underwent surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. However, he developed recurrent disease and received second-line chemotherapy with FOLFIRINOX, which was unsuccessful. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His most recent lab results showed white blood cell count (WBC) of 5.2 x 10^6/L, neutrophil count of 2.8 x 10^9/L, platelet count (PLT) of 115 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin (HB) of 11.8 g/dL, total bilirubin (TB) of 0.9 x ULN, alanine transaminase (ALT) of 32 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) of 45 U/L, serum creatinine (Scr) of 1.1 x ULN, and albumin (ALB) of 3.8 g/dL. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form. He has not participated in any other drug clinical trials in the past 4 weeks and has no history of immune deficiency diseases or systemic steroid therapy. He has not received anti-tumor immune therapy in the past 4 weeks and has recovered from the adverse effects caused by the previous therapies. The patient has no active tuberculosis or malignant tumors (except for basal and skin squamous cell carcinoma, cervical carcinoma in situ and papillary thyroid carcinoma). He has no central nervous system metastasis or meningeal metastasis. The patient has no serious and uncontrollable internal diseases such as severe diabetes, severe hypertension, serious infection, congestive heart failure, ventricular fibrillation, coronary heart disease with obvious symptoms or myocardial infarction in the past 6 months. He has no blood precancerous diseases, such as myelodysplastic syndrome, and no clinically relevant or preexisting interstitial lung diseases.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with HIV infection. He has never taken any antiretroviral drugs before and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. He is sexually active and agrees to use a barrier method of birth control during the study. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and does not have any active/acute CDC Category C event. He has no medical condition that could affect the safety of the study. He has not received radiation or chemotherapy in the past 28 days and does not expect to receive them during the study. He has not taken any drugs that affect the immune system or have anti-HIV activity in the past 28 days. He has no allergies that could interfere with the study. He has a viral load of 10,000 copies/ml and is otherwise in good health.

The patient is a 6-month-old baby girl who was born at full term with no complications during pregnancy or delivery. She is currently in good health and meeting all developmental milestones. Her parents are willing to bring her to all study visits. She has not had any ear infections or ear-related issues to date. Her family history is non-significant for any ear-related conditions. She is currently breastfed and has not started solid foods yet. She lives in suburban Rochester, New York.

The patient is a 15 year old boy who is currently studying in high school. He is interested in sports but due to his busy schedule and lack of motivation, he is not getting enough physical activity. He feels tired most of the time and has gained some weight in the last few months. He is concerned about his health and wants to make a change. He lives with both of his parents and has a younger brother. He enjoys playing video games and watching movies in his free time. He has no medical conditions and takes no medication. His BMI is 25 and his blood pressure is 120/80. He has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He is willing to participate in a research study to increase his physical activity levels and improve his overall health.

65 yo M with a known history of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) presents with fatigue and shortness of breath. CBC reveals pancytopenia and bone marrow biopsy confirms progression to acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The patient is deemed a candidate for AML-like treatment that could potentially result in complete remission (CR). The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare treatment methods and outcomes of AML and MDS patients. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Coronary artery disease - Type 2 diabetes - Cigarette smoking (quit 10 years ago) - Asymptomatic gallstones - History of basal cell carcinoma on the right cheek - No history of prior malignancies.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has a BMI of 25. He is generally healthy and has no known metabolic diseases or conditions that may pose undue risk during the study. He has a regular sleep-wake cycle and is able to comply with study procedures. He is interested in understanding the effects of dietary carbohydrate and sugar intake on physical activity energy expenditure. He has no anticipated changes in physical activity during the study period. He is willing and able to provide informed consent and adhere to the prescribed diets for the 3-day intervention periods. The patient is available for regular check-ins with the study team and is committed to completing the study.

This is a 56-year-old woman who has tested positive for COVID-19 and has been admitted to the hospital due to respiratory distress, with an SpO2 of 94% and a respiratory rate of 22. She has no known allergies to medications and is not currently enrolled in any investigational drug trials. She will be included in an observational study to compare the effectiveness of various treatments provided to COVID-19 patients, including Hydroxychloroquine. The study will involve a retrospective/prospective chart review of cohorts of hospitalized patients across the OSF Healthcare System who have tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and exhibit signs or symptoms of respiratory distress during the course of their hospitalization. The outcomes of patients who both receive and do not receive Hydroxychloroquine will be compared, with particular attention to the timing of administration in relationship to the onset of respiratory distress. The patient's data will be kept securely on password-protected computers and analyzed by applicable research personnel listed on this study. Results of this study will be presented within OSF Healthcare at national meetings and/or published in academic journals while ensuring the privacy, health, and welfare of research subjects during and after the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old African American woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. Her pre-pregnancy BMI was 42 and she has gained approximately 25 pounds during her pregnancy. She is currently at 38 weeks gestational age and has been experiencing significant back pain and discomfort in recent weeks. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable and she has no known contraindications to neuraxial blockade. She has no history of scoliosis and her ASA score is 2. She is eager to have an epidural for pain relief during labor but is concerned about the potential difficulties in placement due to her high BMI. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help improve the experience and outcomes of labor epidural placement for other women in the future.

Patient A is a premature infant born at 30 weeks gestation. The infant has not yet received any enteral feeding and has no major congenital malformations, including congenital heart disease. The parents/legal guardians of the infant have provided written informed consent to participate in the study. The infant will be continuously monitored for cerebral and splanchnic oxygen saturation using INVOS 5100 oximeter. The monitoring will be performed from 30 minutes before to 3 hours after feeding administration. The infant will also undergo an echocardiographic evaluation before enteral feeding introduction to evaluate hemodynamics and PDA status. The study aims to evaluate whether splanchnic oxygenation patterns in response to enteral feeding introduction in preterm infants may be affected by PDA status. The infant will be enrolled in the study as long as the infant meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 32-year-old female presented to the clinic with symptoms of major depressive disorder (MDD), including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She reported experiencing these symptoms for at least a month and had not been taking any antidepressant medication for the past 10 half-lives of her previous medication. She was willing to limit the introduction of any new treatments during the study and was right-handed. Her Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (17-item HDRS) score was greater than 15 at screening and randomization. She had no major medical illnesses or ongoing pain, but had a history of generalized anxiety disorder. She was not pregnant or nursing and did not have any contraindications to PET or MRI methods. She had not previously taken duloxetine and had no active suicidal ideation. She tested negative on a urine screen for opioids and any substances of abuse.

Maria is a 25 year old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is in her 33rd week of pregnancy and is planning to have a vaginal delivery. She has no history of pelvic or vaginal surgeries and has not used any antenatal pelvic floor methods of preparation prior to study enrollment. She has not been diagnosed with pelvic organ prolapse or any vaginal infections. She is able to contract her pelvic floor muscles and is comfortable with vaginal palpation. She has no neurological or cognitive impairments that prevent her from understanding the proposed procedures. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn more about antenatal pelvic floor preparation techniques and how they can potentially prevent perineal trauma during childbirth.

This is a 32 year-old female with a long-standing history of asthma. She has been on regular inhaled therapy for the past 2 years, which has helped to manage her symptoms, but she still experiences occasional bouts of coughing, wheezing and dyspnea. She is a non-smoker and generally in good health, but feels that her asthma is limiting her ability to participate in physical activities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the efficacy of a 3-weeks asthma rehabilitation program at high altitude and low altitude on lung function and asthma control. She meets the inclusion criteria as she has a history of asthma consisting of variable symptoms and asthma variability in peak expiratory flow > 10%/day and/or a reversible airflow obstruction in spirometry. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria and is motivated to adhere to the study procedure.

A 48-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of advanced ovarian cancer presents for potential enrollment in a clinical trial. She underwent a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 2 weeks ago, which confirmed the diagnosis of stage III ovarian cancer. She has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. The patient reports no allergies to medications and no family history of cancer. She is eager to participate in a clinical trial to help advance the understanding and treatment of cancer.

A 55-year-old male patient visited the clinic with chest pain episodes for the last two months. The pain was located in the center of the chest, radiating to the left arm, and lasted for about 15 minutes. The patient has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. The physical examination was significant for a blood pressure of 160/100 mmHg, a heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and a BMI of 30. The laboratory study was significant for elevated total cholesterol levels (260 mg/dL) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (180 mg/dL). The patient was scheduled for clinically indicated coronary angiography within the next 7 days following Study Day 1. The patient does not have any known hypersensitivity or contraindication to dipyridamole or ultrasound contrast agents, and no history of heart transplant, right-to-left shunt, uncontrolled ventricular tachycardia, or current atrial fibrillation, atrial tachycardia, or atrial flutter. The patient also has no pacemaker or defibrillator and has not been exposed to PB127 Ultrasound Contrast Agent before.

The patient is a 50 year old male with paraplegia due to a spinal cord injury that occurred in a motor vehicle accident 5 years ago. He is currently residing in a long-term care facility and has developed a pressure ulcer on his sacrum. The ulcer is between 4 and 15cm in diameter and has been present for approximately 2 months. He has no history of connective tissue disorders or immunosuppression, and is not currently receiving hemodialysis or steroids. He is able to provide informed consent for participation in this clinical trial.

A 7-year-old Korean boy with no history of chronic medical conditions presented for participation in the clinical trial. The patient is generally healthy and has no known allergies to eggs, chicken, neomycin, gentamicin or any components of the study vaccine. He has not received an influenza vaccine in the past 6 months, nor does he have a family history of immune system disorders or Guillain-Barre syndrome. The patient has not been diagnosed with Down's syndrome or cytogenetic disorders. He is not being treated with an anticoagulant and has not had an acute fever with body temperature greater than 38.0 Cº in the past 72 hours. The patient has not received immunosuppressant or immune modifying drugs in the past 3 months, nor has he received immunoglobulin or blood-derived products in the past 3 months or expects to receive them during the study. The patient has not participated in another experimental study in the past 30 days prior to administration of the study vaccine. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who is a gold miner in Puerto Colombia, Atlántico, Colombia. He has been working in the gold mine for the past 7 years and has been exposed to mercury vapor and dust during the extraction process. He has noticed some symptoms such as fatigue, headaches, and muscle weakness. He is married and has two children. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of drug addiction or allergies. His blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. His BMI is 26.8. His lab results show a urinary mercury level of 15 ug/L. He has not undergone any chelation therapy in the past 3 months. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all the clinic visits. He has signed and dated the informed consent form approved by the IRB.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence for the past 2 years. She reports leakage of urine when coughing, sneezing, or during exercise. She has tried pelvic floor exercises but has not seen any improvement. She underwent mid-urethral sling placement surgery in the past but has concerns about the use of synthetic mesh. She is interested in alternative options that avoid the use of synthetic mesh. She has no active urinary infection, neurologic disorders, malignancies, or history of radiotherapy.

The patient is a 50 year old Hispanic female who presents to the clinic with chest pain that started about 3 months ago. She describes the pain as pressure-like, located in the center of her chest, and sometimes radiating to her left arm. The pain comes on with exertion, such as walking up stairs, but also occurs at rest. She has tried taking over-the-counter pain medications, but they do not provide relief. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has never had a heart attack or other heart problems before. She works as a housekeeper and is physically active at work. She is married and has two children. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She speaks Spanish as her primary language but is also fluent in English. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand her chest pain and to help researchers learn more about heart disease in women.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who works as a firefighter. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or hospitalizations in the past 2 years. He has a history of smoking but quit 6 months ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He does not use any nicotine products, herbal supplements, or caffeine. He is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription medications. He has no allergies to medications. He does not have any chronic infections or viral illnesses. He is willing to comply with the study's dietary requirements and is able to swallow medications. He has no history of seizures or other conditions that would prevent him from complying with the study protocol. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and is not planning to participate in any experimental treatment studies during the study period. He is willing to refrain from donating sperm during the study period. He meets the criteria for using an approved method of birth control.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who had a stroke 1 year ago and has been experiencing spasticity in his upper limb since then. He has been receiving traditional treatments including range of motion exercises and medication, but has not seen significant improvement. He has been deemed eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of a first-time stroke at least six months prior with chronic sequela of spasticity, demonstration of consistent resting motor evoked potential from ipsilesional and contralesional hemispheres, and sufficient ambulation or wheelchair mobility to allow him to present to treatment and testing areas with minimum assist. He is right-handed, and his stroke affected the left hemisphere. The patient is able to follow three-step directions and has demonstrated 10 degrees of active extension at the metacarpophalangeal joint and wrist of the paretic upper extremity. He does not have any co-morbidities impairing upper extremity function and does not have any indwelling metal or medical devices incompatible with TMS. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no planned vacations or travel during the study period.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with a glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) after experiencing headaches and blurry vision. She underwent a neurosurgical procedure to remove the tumor, and a post-surgical MRI showed that the tumor was totally resected. She is currently undergoing evaluation for radiation therapy and chemotherapy. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any regular medications. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is married and has two children. She is currently working as a teacher but has taken a leave of absence for the time being. She is concerned about the potential side effects of radiation therapy and chemotherapy but is willing to participate in the study to receive a potentially more effective treatment.

A 30-year-old healthy female is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a new medication called Tralokinumab. She has no known medical conditions, takes no regular medications, and her past medical history is unremarkable. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or drugs. She is of childbearing potential but is currently using a highly effective form of birth control. She has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 3 months. She is willing to comply with the study schedule, including regular visits to the study center and follow-up visits. She has agreed to undergo blood tests, physical exams, and other procedures as required by the study protocol. She is aware of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and has provided written informed consent to participate.

A 25-year-old male athlete who participates in overhead sports such as baseball and tennis has recently undergone Bankart shoulder surgery due to recurrent instability. He has been playing sports for over 10 years and dedicates more than 3 hours per week to training and competing. He has no other current pathologies that interfere with his physical activity. He is willing to participate in this study and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a history of spinal cord injury at the level of T6 due to a car accident that occurred 2 years ago. He has been non-ambulatory since the injury and relies on a wheelchair for mobility. His height is 5'11" and he weighs 220 lbs. He has been cleared by his physician for full weight-bearing and locomotor training. His passive range of motion is within functional limits for safe gait and use of an assistive device. He has intact skin where it interfaces with the robotic device. His Modified Ashworth Scale for spasticity score is 2. He does not have any lower extremity joint limitations that exceed 10 degrees at the hips, knees, or ankles. His blood pressure and heart rate are within established guidelines for locomotor training. He is able to tolerate being in an upright standing position without feeling lightheaded or having a headache.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently incarcerated in a women's prison. She has a history of alcohol use and has been classified as having hazardous drinking patterns. She reports a history of engaging in high-risk sexual behaviors and drug use. She is concerned about her risk for contracting HIV and wants to make changes to her lifestyle to reduce her risk. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to attend two motivational interview sessions during the first month of study participation. She has a positive attitude towards change and is committed to reducing her alcohol consumption and improving her overall health.

A 5-year-old male child with a history of global developmental delay and hypotonia since birth. The patient has had multiple hospital admissions for recurrent infections and has been diagnosed with failure to thrive. The patient has a history of seizures, which are controlled with medication. The patient's medical history is significant for a diagnosis of CDG Type Ia based on genetic testing. The patient has received physical therapy and occupational therapy to improve gross and fine motor skills. The patient has a restricted diet due to gastrointestinal issues and is currently taking a specialized formula. The patient and their family are interested in participating in a study to help further research and treatment options for CDG.

A 55-year-old male patient with a medical history of hypertension and dyslipidemia is scheduled for cardiac surgery under extracorporeal circulation (ECC) due to severe aortic stenosis. The patient denies any respiratory symptoms, such as cough, fever, or nasal congestion during preoperative assessment. He has not received the influenza vaccine this year. The patient has given free, informed, and written consent to participate in the study. The patient is affiliated with a social security scheme and meets all inclusion criteria. He is not admitted for heart transplantation or implantation of a left heart mechanical assist device or a total artificial heart. The patient is not participating in another clinical study that may interfere with the procedures in this study. The patient is not subject to legal protection, guardianship, trusteeship, or pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been a heavy smoker for over 30 years. He started experiencing a persistent cough, shortness of breath and chest pain. A chest x-ray showed a mass in his right lung. A biopsy confirmed the mass to be small cell lung cancer. The cancer has already spread to his liver and lymph nodes in his chest. He has not received any chemotherapy for his cancer before. His performance status is 1 and he is able to care for himself but cannot work or perform strenuous activities. His hemoglobin level is 11.5 g/dL, WBC count is 4,000/mm3, platelet count is 130,000/mm3 and neutrophil count is 2,000/mm3. His bilirubin level is 1.8 mg/dL, SGOT and SGPT levels are 50 U/L and 45 U/L respectively. His alkaline phosphatase level is 100 U/L. His creatinine level is 1.3 mg/dL and creatinine clearance is 75 mL/min. He has no history of gastrointestinal conditions, hearing impairment, or any other medical conditions that would preclude the use of the study drugs. He has not received any investigational drugs within the past 30 days, and has not received any immunotherapy, hormonal therapy or radiotherapy for his lung cancer. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for at least one month after the study.

The patient is a 14-year-old male high school student who was playing football when he collided with another player and fell onto his right shoulder. He felt immediate pain and was unable to move his arm. After being evaluated by a physician, he was diagnosed with a displaced mid-shaft clavicle fracture. The fracture measures 1.5 cm in shortening and is displaced 100% the width of the clavicle. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He has no cognitive disabilities that would inhibit the completion of questionnaires. The patient and his parents have agreed to participate in the study and have signed the informed consent form.

This is a 6 year-old female with a history of good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups. During her last visit, her dentist noticed a deep cavity on the lower left primary molar tooth. The tooth was asymptomatic with no clinical or radiographic evidence of pulp pathology. The dentist recommended a pulpotomy procedure to prevent further damage to the tooth. The parents consented to the procedure and the child was randomly assigned to receive either Mineral Trioxide Aggregate or BiodentineTM as the pulpotomy medicament. The child will be followed up at 3-month intervals for the next 36 months to record any clinical or radiographic success or failure of the treatment. The child has no other medical or dental conditions that would interfere with the study.

A 10-year-old girl diagnosed with intermediate-risk neuroblastoma and scheduled to receive chemotherapy. She has experienced unintended weight loss since her diagnosis and has struggled to maintain a healthy weight. She has no history of anorexia or bulimia, and she is not currently taking any appetite-stimulating medications. She is not currently receiving steroids for more than 7 days as part of her cancer treatment regimen. She has not been diagnosed with glaucoma, cystic fibrosis, inflammatory bowel disease, or GI/GU obstruction. She is not allergic to cyproheptadine HCl. Her parents are willing to participate in the study and comply with the requirements of the study, including completing medicine logs and attending follow-up visits.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who presents with a history of obesity for the past 10 years. Her BMI is 35 and she has tried multiple diets and exercise programs without any significant weight loss. She has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications regularly. She is a non-smoker and has no known drug allergies. The physical examination is unremarkable except for her obesity. The vital signs are within normal limits. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She is not currently taking metformin or any other medication for diabetes. She has no history of bariatric surgery or any other major surgeries. She does not have any neurological or adipose tissue pathology. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to undergo MRI and lumbar puncture for the study. She has no contraindications for these procedures or for metformin use.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of bipolar I disorder. She is currently experiencing a depressive episode and has been diagnosed with it according to the DSM-IV criteria. She has been experiencing symptoms such as persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, changes in appetite, insomnia, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. Her Young Mania Rating Scale score is 8 and her Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (17-item) score is 18. She is not currently taking lithium or quetiapine for her depression, but she has tried them in the past. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use doctor-approved birth control throughout the study. She has no history of schizophrenia, substance dependence, or organic mental disorder. She is competent to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is 35 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has no significant medical history and is in good health. She has been scheduled for an elective cesarean delivery due to previous complications during labor. She is aware of the potential postoperative pain and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no known allergies to local anesthetics, morphine, fentanyl, or ropivacaine. She has not been on chronic opioid medication and has no major medical or psychiatric problems. The patient's BMI is 28, which is within the acceptable range for the study. She has been informed of the study and has given her consent to participate.

The patient is a 72-year-old English-speaking woman who has low levels of physical activity and has experienced one or more falls in the past year. She reports feeling unsteady when standing or walking and worries about falling. She has not experienced any chest pain, tightness, or pressure during physical activity, nor has she had any current dizziness. She has not had any lower extremity injury or surgery in the past 6 weeks and is able to walk. She does not have a formal diagnosis of neurocognitive impairment or dementia. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve her physical activity levels and decrease her risk of falling.

Patient is a 30-year-old African American woman who has a history of asthma since childhood. Despite taking low-dose inhaled corticosteroids, the patient has been experiencing inadequately controlled asthma symptoms. She reports experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness, especially during physical activity. The patient has not had any major medical problems other than asthma and is a non-smoker. She is willing to provide a blood sample for DNA extraction and genetic analysis. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is practicing abstinence as a birth control method. The patient is interested in participating in the study to find the best asthma treatment for African Americans.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been receiving hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to end-stage renal disease. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking calcium carbonate as a phosphate binder and active vitamin D as prescribed. His serum phosphorus concentration at the end of the washout period was 6.2 mg/dL. He has never participated in a clinical trial before and is willing to follow the study protocol. He is able to chew the lanthanum carbonate tablets completely before swallowing and is not intubated or receiving enteral tube feedings. He does not have severe hyperparathyroidism and is not taking any calcium-, magnesium-, or aluminum-containing antacids. He has no known non-compliance with oral medications and is willing to discontinue his current phosphate binder therapy for one week before the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is currently in her 21st week of gestation and is experiencing preterm labor with intact membranes. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She is willing to undergo serial endovaginal scans to monitor her cervical morphology and volume as predictors of preterm delivery risk. The patient is aware that the study aims to identify prognostic indicators of adverse pregnancy outcome by three-dimensional ultrasound and that the results will be correlated with maternal and fetal biological markers, placental pathology, and pregnancy outcome. She is also aware that the study will compare the performance of conventional two-dimensional endovaginal ultrasound with three-dimensional ultrasound findings. The patient is willing to cooperate and participate in the study to improve our understanding of the nature and timing of cervical volume changes in relation to pregnancy outcome.

The patient is a 25-year-old male from a rural area in a developing country. He works as a farmer and has a history of frequent headaches and seizures for the past six months. The headaches are usually on one side of the head and are accompanied by nausea and vomiting. The seizures are generalized and occur about twice a month. He has never received any treatment for his symptoms and has no known allergies. His family has a history of epilepsy. He visited a doctor who ordered a CT scan which revealed multiple cysts in his brain. He was diagnosed with neurocysticercosis and was informed about the clinical trial. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the requirements of the study. He is not currently taking any medications and has no other medical conditions. His blood pressure is normal, and his BMI is 23. He has completed high school and can read and write in his native language. He is married and has two children. He is interested in learning more about his condition and wants to receive the best possible treatment.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer six months ago. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the disease has progressed. He is now experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and coughing, and has lost 10 pounds in the past two months. He has no history of smoking, but was exposed to second-hand smoke at work for many years. He has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it. He has a KPS score of 70 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. His labs show WBC: 4500c/ml, Platelets: 150×10^9/L, Hb: 12.0g/dL, LY: 1.2×10^9/L, LY%: 27%, Alb: 3.2g/dL, serum lipase and amylase: within normal limits, serum creatinine: 1.2mg/dL, AST and ALT: within normal limits, serum total bilirubin: 1.0mg/dL. He has no history of organ transplantation or waiting for organ transplantation. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 56-year-old male was diagnosed with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the effectiveness of pembrolizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. He has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG Performance Scale and is R0 resectable thoracic esophageal cancer, cT2N1M0. He has not received any systemic or local treatment for esophageal cancer in the past. He is willing to provide tissue, blood, and urine samples and has adequate organ function. He has no history of autoimmune disease or symptomatic interstitial lung disease. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is interested in exploring treatment options that may improve his chances of survival.

A 25-year-old female university student with no significant medical history and no known bleeding disorders. She is fluent in English and able to accurately read and answer questions about her past medical history. She does not currently take any medications or supplements that affect the clotting process. She has not had any significant surgeries or trauma in the past year.

This is a 65-year-old woman who was diagnosed with biliary tract cancer about 6 months ago. The diagnosis was confirmed by a biopsy of a mass located in the bile ducts. She underwent internal endoscopic drainage/stenting to relieve the treatable biliary duct obstruction. She now presents with symptoms related to her disease, including pain and discomfort, and has a Karnofsky performance status of 70%. Her analgesic consumption is at least 10 mg of morphine equivalents per day and her baseline pain intensity score is 30 mm out of a possible 100 mm. She has no prior history of chemotherapy for advanced/metastatic disease and no other significant underlying medical conditions that would preclude study participation.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl with a diagnosis of cerebral palsy. She has been experiencing difficulty with coordination and movement, as well as speech disturbances. She has also been diagnosed with low vertebral bone density, which puts her at risk for osteoporosis in the future. The patient is able to stand for 10 minutes with handheld support. She has not undergone any surgery, casting, or received botulinum toxin in the past 12 months and does not have any metal rods or plates in her tibia or lumbar spine. She does not have severe scoliosis or bowing of the tibia. She does not have any other medical condition affecting her bone or muscle, and she is not taking corticosteroids or seizure medication. The patient's parents are willing to provide informed consent for her participation in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Ewing's sarcoma in her left femur. She had a biopsy done which confirmed the diagnosis. Imaging studies showed no evidence of metastatic disease or distant node involvement. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. She has not received any prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or radiotherapy. She is not pregnant nor nursing.
