She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare different chemotherapy regimens combined with radiation therapy and/or surgery in treating patients with Ewing's sarcoma.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been experiencing bedwetting for several years. He has been diagnosed with monosymptomatic nocturnal enuresis and has tried various treatment options, including behavioral modifications, but has not seen significant improvement. He is generally healthy and has no history of chronic illness, renal failure, hypertension, congenital heart disease, diabetes mellitus, or diabetes insipidus. He has completed uroflowmetry and bladder sonography, which did not reveal any structural abnormalities in the urinary tract. He is willing to try Desmopressin® treatment and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to predict treatment response using Copeptin. He is currently in 4th grade and enjoys playing video games and soccer. He lives with his parents and younger sister and is excited to potentially find a solution to his bedwetting problem.

The patient is a 28-year-old female diagnosed with Crohn's disease for the past 5 years. She complains of frequent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue. She is currently on medication, including mesalamine and prednisone, but still experiences symptoms. She is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. She does not have any other significant medical history or family history of autoimmune diseases. She works as a desk job and does not engage in regular physical activity due to her symptoms. She reports feeling anxious and depressed due to her chronic illness. She is interested in participating in a study that explores the benefits of physical activity for patients with inflammatory bowel disease.

A 55-year old accountant was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus three years ago. He is currently on oral hypoglycemic agents and his blood sugar is well controlled. He has no history of heart disease, liver disease, or renal disease. He is a non-smoker and drinks occasionally. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He has no complaints of shortness of breath, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. He has a normal liver function and renal function. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is married and has two children. He works full-time and enjoys spending time with his family on weekends.

A 20-month-old male toddler is brought to the emergency department with symptoms of respiratory distress. The child has a history of first acute bronchiolitis and has been experiencing coughing, wheezing, and difficulty breathing for the past two days. The child's condition has worsened and he meets the criteria for hospital admission due to respiratory rate > 60/min, pulse oxymetry < 95%, and alimentary intake < 2/3 of the needs. The child has no known history of chronic lung disease or congenital heart disease. Vital signs are reported as: temperature: 37°C, heart rate: 130 beats/min, respiratory rate: 62 breaths/min, and blood pressure: 80/50 mm Hg. The child is also experiencing nasal congestion and has a productive cough with yellow sputum. The child's parents report that they have never given him any chest physiotherapy procedures before. After evaluation, the child is found eligible to participate in the BRONKINOU study, which aims to evaluate the effectiveness of chest physiotherapy with forced expiratory techniques in reducing the duration of respiratory distress in toddlers with acute bronchiolitis.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in the first trimester of her pregnancy. She is overweight with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and is concerned about the potential negative impact of excessive weight gain during pregnancy on her health and that of her developing baby. She is an English-speaking resident of the United States and is interested in participating in the Parents as Teachers (PAT) program to receive guidance on healthy eating and physical activity during pregnancy and postpartum. She is willing to participate in the HEALTH-P2 intervention and to be randomly assigned to either the intervention group or the usual care group. She plans to continue participating in the PAT program until her baby turns one year old and is able to give informed consent for participation. She is physically able to engage in a walking program but is not planning to become pregnant again before her baby turns one.

A 55-year-old male with type 2 diabetes came to the clinic with a non-healing ulcer on his left foot for the past 6 weeks. The ulcer is approximately 2 cm2 in size and located on the medial side of the left foot. The patient has tried various treatments, including regular wound dressings, antibiotics, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy, but has not seen any significant improvement. The patient has no signs of infection, and his HbA1c level was 9% at his last check-up. His serum creatinine level is within normal range, and he has adequate circulation to the affected foot. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. He has not received any biomedical or topical growth factor treatment in the past 30 days, and he is not taking any medications that are considered immune system modulators or cox-2 inhibitors.

A 55-year-old male patient presents with a history of liver cancer. He has recently undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and his oncologist has recommended a liver resection as part of his treatment plan. The patient has no history of liver disease or other relevant medical conditions. He is otherwise healthy and maintains an active lifestyle. The patient is able to provide written, informed consent and has no contra-indications to paracetamol. He is not jaundiced and his bilirubin levels are within normal range. The liver resection will be his only surgical procedure and he meets the age requirement for the study.

A 55-year-old male patient with a recent diagnosis of tuberculosis was referred to the tuberculosis clinic at London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and is on medication for it. He has been on tuberculosis treatment for 2 weeks and is experiencing some side effects from the medications. He is married and has two children. He works as a builder and exercises regularly. He smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol socially. He is 178cm tall and weighs 85kg. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He has no known allergies to any medications. He speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study if he meets the eligibility criteria.

The patient is a Chinese male or female, aged 50 years or older, with a history of dyspepsia lasting at least 4 weeks or more. The patient may also have a family history of gastric cancer, a medical condition for which an OGD is indicated, or a past history of intestinal metaplasia or dysplasia. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits and other study procedures. The patient does not have a personal history of stomach cancer or surgery, disabling illnesses, bronchial asthma, a known allergy to fluorescein, renal impairment with serum creatinine above the upper limit of normal, uncorrected coagulopathy, or severe thrombocytopenia precluding biopsy. The patient has personally signed and dated the patient informed consent form indicating that he/she has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) two years ago. She has had progressive disease on two systemic therapies and is currently experiencing persistent skin lesions that cause itching and discomfort. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications other than occasional antihistamines to alleviate the itching. She has not received any topical steroids for the past two weeks. She has a performance status of 1 according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group criteria. Her bone marrow, hepatic and renal function are normal. She has no history of major surgery in the past 3 weeks. She is willing to practice effective contraception during the study period and is able to understand and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who works in an office and leads a healthy lifestyle. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has never participated in a clinical trial before. She has a BMI of 22. Her physical examination, laboratory assessments, and vital signs are all within normal limits. She has a negative urine drug screen and ova and parasite test. She is not pregnant and uses dual methods of contraception. She has no known hypersensitivity to any constituent of the study drug. She has not received treatment with chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the preceding 6 months. She has not received treatment for a helminthic parasitic infection within 6 months of screening. She has not used omalizumab, dupilumab, systemic immunosuppressive drugs, or systemic corticosteroids in the 30 days before Screening. She has not been vaccinated with live attenuated vaccines within 30 days prior to initiation of treatment in the study, during the treatment period, or vaccination expected within 5 half-lives (4 months) of study drug administration. She has negative hepatitis serology results and HIV serology results at Screening. She has no alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse or dependence.

30 year-old sexually active female presenting with vaginal itching, burning, and discharge. She reports having unprotected sex with a new partner two weeks ago. The discharge is yellow-green, malodorous, and has a frothy consistency. Pelvic exam reveals erythema and edema of the vaginal mucosa with an abundant amount of malodorous discharge. Wet mount microscopy confirms the presence of Trichomonas vaginalis. The patient denies any history of seizures or peripheral neuropathy and is not currently pregnant or nursing. She has no known allergies to study drugs and is willing to abstain from alcohol during the treatment period and for 48 hours after. The patient is not on anticoagulation therapy and has no history of drug abuse. She is not expecting to have menses within the next 8 days.

This study is seeking individuals who have been diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and their family members as well as controls without ASD. For probands with ASD, they must meet the diagnostic criteria for ASD of the DSM-5, be at least 24 months old, and have a somatic and intellectual state compatible with a blood test. Individuals with severe intellectual deficiency, personal psychiatric or neurological history, or medical conditions that are not compatible with inclusion will be excluded. The study will involve genetic screenings and analysis of synaptic genes in order to identify genetic variation in synaptic pathways that may be targeted for therapeutic development. The investigators will also establish comprehensive genotype/phenotype correlations to better understand the range of clinical phenotypes caused by mutations in synaptic genes. Participants will need to provide informed consent and be affiliated with social insurance.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia. She received peripheral blood stem cells from an adult matched unrelated donor. The patient is currently in complete remission of her leukemia, and her transplant occurred 100 days before the start of the study drug. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to tolerate routine oral posaconazole as fungal prophylaxis therapy. The patient has not participated in any clinical trial evaluating another preventative strategy for chronic GVHD or ongoing participation in a clinical trial for therapy of acute GVHD. The patient has no evidence of relapsed hematologic malignancy based on routine restaging studies. She has no evidence of any active uncontrolled infection or evidence of natural exposure to Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, or HIV without demonstration of PCR negativity for said virus. The patient has no evidence of ongoing gastrointestinal or hepatic acute GVHD or evidence of greater than ongoing Stage I cutaneous acute GVHD at the time of enrollment. She has not received any Donor Lymphocyte Infusion (DLI) within the past 6 weeks and has no plans for a DLI in the upcoming 30 days. The patient has no major cardiovascular events within the past 6 months, including myocardial infarction, unstable angina, cerebrovascular accident, pulmonary embolism, heart failure uncontrolled by medications or New York Heart Association Class III or IV heart failure. She has no history of arterial or venous thrombosis within the past year. The patient has no liver function test abnormalities and has a neutrophil count of 2.5 x 10e9/L and a platelet count of 120 x 10e9/L. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder and recurrent major depressive episodes has been experiencing worsening symptoms of depression for the past week. She has lost interest in her hobbies and feels hopeless and helpless most of the day. She has also been experiencing insomnia and decreased appetite. She has a history of hospitalization for a manic episode and is currently being treated with lithium and quetiapine. She has a supportive family but feels more comfortable seeking help at home. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that provides home treatment and peer support during her current episode. She is able to give informed consent and has no current suicidal thoughts.

A 25-year-old healthy male who has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 is interested in participating in a study that aims to evaluate the short-term effects of structured lipids on appetite regulation. He is a non-smoker, has no history of gastrointestinal disorders, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or chronic infectious disease. He exercises regularly and has no dietary supplements. He has never donated blood in the past three months or during the study. He does not consume more than 21 alcoholic drinks per week and is not an elite athlete. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how LCF can affect appetite regulation and energy balance.

The patient is a 56-year-old American woman who presented to the hospital with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. She was diagnosed with an ischemic stroke and underwent endovascular thrombectomy to remove the clot in her middle cerebral artery. After successful clot retrieval, her blood pressure remained elevated, with two consecutive readings of systolic blood pressure greater than or equal to 150 mmHg, and she is not diabetic. She is able to provide informed consent or has a legal representative who can provide informed consent. She has no contraindications to enrolling in the DETECT trial, and will be randomized to either intensive blood pressure lowering with a target systolic blood pressure less than 140 mmHg or standard blood pressure management with a target systolic blood pressure less than 180 mmHg for the first 48 hours after randomization. She will be followed up to 90 days after her clot retrieval to assess for hemorrhagic transformation and functional outcome.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in her left knee for the past year. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) to manage her pain. However, the NSAIDs have not been providing her with adequate pain relief. She is generally healthy with no known allergies or major medical conditions. She has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. She is currently not taking any prescription medications other than the NSAIDs for her osteoarthritis. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the Extended Release Hydrocodone/Acetaminophen medication will provide better pain control for her osteoarthritis.

This is a 28-year-old male who sustained a mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) while playing recreational football. The injury resulted in a brief loss of consciousness, but he did not seek medical attention at the time. He has been experiencing post-concussive symptoms for the past 6 weeks, including headaches, dizziness, difficulty concentrating, and forgetfulness. These symptoms have been interfering with his ability to perform his job as a computer programmer. He has no history of other neurological or psychiatric conditions and is fluent in English. He has reliable transportation and is motivated to participate in the study to improve his daily life activities.

This is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and is scheduled to undergo surgery in the next few weeks. She is feeling very anxious about the surgery and is worried about the pain, recovery process, and potential complications. She has no prior history of mental health issues or anxiety disorders but is finding it challenging to manage her anxiety. She has been informed about the PREPARE clinical trial, which aims to verify whether a short psychological intervention can help patients increase their perceived self-efficacy in managing preoperative anxiety. She is interested in participating in the study and hopes that the intervention will help her feel more confident and less anxious about the upcoming surgery. She has no other significant medical history and meets all the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 4-year-old boy with a history of frequent upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) is being considered for the CLEARI study. He has had at least 10 URTIs in the past year and has been hospitalized once due to complications. He attends daycare and has a history of prematurity and low birth weight. He is otherwise healthy, with normal growth and development. He has no chronic medical conditions, is not on any regular medications, and does not have any allergies. His parents are non-smokers, and there is no history of respiratory illness in the family. The parents are interested in exploring options for preventing URTIs in their child and are open to participating in a clinical trial.

A 55-year-old man with a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and cirrhosis of the liver has been referred to the clinic for further evaluation. He was diagnosed with HCV infection 10 years ago and has been treated with direct acting antiviral (DAA) drugs. He has no history of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and is not currently experiencing any symptoms. His medical history includes hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He has no known allergies. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance research on HCC and DAA treatments.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who is experiencing pain and stiffness in his right big toe. He is an active person who enjoys hiking and gardening, but his symptoms have been limiting his activities. He works as a carpenter and spends most of his day on his feet. He has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medications, but they have not provided significant relief. His X-ray imaging reveals osteoarthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint. He has good bone stock and is physically and mentally willing to comply with post-operative rehabilitation and scheduled clinical visits. He has no history of infections, tumors, or allergies to calcium carbonate or hyaluronate. He is not pregnant and has not participated in any other clinical trials parallel to this study. He has no known systemic diseases or substance abuse. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his symptoms and return to his active lifestyle.

28-year-old male, non-smoker, with no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and no significant medical history presents to the clinic. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and tolerability of multiple doses of aerosolized and intravenous colistimethate sodium separately or in combination in healthy adult subjects. He has never participated in a clinical trial before and is interested in contributing to medical research. He has a BMI of 23.2 kg/m^2, and has not used tobacco/nicotine within the past 3 months. The patient has no history of asthma, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, endocrine, metabolic, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic, psychological or psychiatric disease, and he has never experienced seizures, ataxia, or Myasthenia Gravis. He is not immunocompromised, and has tested negative for HIV-1 and HIV-2. He has not donated blood or experienced significant blood loss within the past 56 days, and has not donated plasma within the past 28 days. The patient has no significant allergies, and has not taken medications that would exclude him from this trial within the past 30 days. He has normal laboratory values for serum creatinine, hemoglobin, platelet count, absolute neutrophil count, serum blood urea nitrogen, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and proteinuria. He has not taken NSAIDs within the past 48 hours, and has not taken any inhaled medication within the past 5 days. His FEV1 is greater than 80 percent predicted, and he has no prior evidence of vestibular problems or neuropathy. His ECG shows a normal QT interval.

56-year-old male diagnosed with stage III gastric cancer. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or surgery for gastric cancer. The patient has a performance status of 1, with no other severe concurrent diseases or psychiatric disorders that would preclude compliance. The patient has normal hematopoietic function, with a WBC count of 7,000/mm^3, a platelet count of 150,000/mm^3, and a hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL. The patient's liver function is normal, with a bilirubin level of 1 mg/dL, SGOT/SGPT levels within normal limits, and an alkaline phosphatase level of 50 U/L. The patient's renal function is also normal, with a creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL and a calculated creatinine clearance of 80 mL/min. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction or congestive heart failure within the past 3 months. The patient is HIV-negative and has no active or uncontrolled infections. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has agreed to use effective contraception during the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman at 27 weeks gestation. She has a history of preterm labor in her previous pregnancy, which was managed with tocolytics and bed rest. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her prenatal care has been unremarkable, with normal ultrasound findings and no significant pregnancy complications. During a routine ultrasound, a cervical length of 22 mm was incidentally found, and she was referred for further evaluation. Upon examination, she had no cervical changes or signs of preterm labor. She has no contraindications to vaginal progesterone use and is willing to participate in the study. She understands the study requirements and has given informed consent to participate.

58 year-old male with a history of shortness of breath and chronic cough for the past 6 months. He has recently been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and has been taking N-acetylcysteine to manage his symptoms. His baseline forced vital capacity (FVC) is 60%, and he is able to walk 300 meters in the 6-minute walk test without requiring oxygen supplementation. He has never smoked cigarettes or marijuana and has no allergies to medications. He is not currently taking losartan or any other angiotensin II receptor blocker. His current medications include N-acetylcysteine and a daily multivitamin. He is willing and able to attend clinic visits for the duration of the study.

A 42-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) for the last 6 months. She was diagnosed with ITP 3 months ago according to ASH guidelines and has completed one prior treatment for ITP. The patient reports a sharp decline in her platelet count and is currently thrombocytopenic, with a platelet count of less than 50 x 10^9/L. She is in good health otherwise with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1. Her serum creatinine concentration is 1.5 mg/dL, and serum bilirubin concentration is within normal limits. Hemoglobin is greater than 10.0 g/dL. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She has not received any treatment for ITP for the last 4 weeks and has not participated in any study evaluating PEG-rHuMGDF, rHuTPO, or related platelet products. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using adequate contraceptive precautions. She does not have any known history of bone marrow stem cell disorder or active malignancy. The patient has not experienced arterial thrombosis or venous thrombosis in the past year and is not receiving anticoagulation therapy. She has not received IV Ig or WinRho within the last 2 weeks and has not received hematopoietic growth factors, including interleukin (IL)-11 (Neumega®), within the last 4 weeks.

A 56-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy. Her cancer was estrogen receptor-positive and HER2-negative. She was started on an aromatase inhibitor after completing radiation therapy but experienced a relapse about 6 months ago. She was switched to another aromatase inhibitor but unfortunately progressed after 3 months. She was started on fulvestrant and has been on it for the past 3 months but her cancer has progressed again. Her oncologist has recommended a clinical trial to study the effectiveness of a combination of fulvestrant and AZD2014 in treating advanced or metastatic breast cancer. She has been informed that the trial involves randomization into one of four treatment arms: fulvestrant alone, fulvestrant + AZD2014 (continuous daily schedule), fulvestrant + AZD2014 (intermittent schedule - 2 days on, 5 days off), or fulvestrant + everolimus. She is postmenopausal and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study. She is willing to participate in the trial to receive a potentially more effective treatment for her cancer.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who underwent a coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) procedure at the Cardiothoracic department of the University hospital of Orebro, Sweden, due to severe coronary artery disease. During the procedure, a saphenous vein graft was harvested using the standard technique. Recently, he has been experiencing chest pain and was referred to the Angiographic unit of the University Hospital of Orebro for a post-operative coronary angiography. The angiography revealed a significant stenosis in the previously implanted saphenous vein graft. The patient is now being considered for a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) procedure to treat the stenosis. He is a potential candidate for the short and long-term results of PCI in no-touch vein-graft study, which aims to evaluate the efficacy of the no-touch technique in comparison to the conventional technique for venous graft harvesting after CABG. The study will analyze all the operated patients in the clinic who underwent a post-operative coronary angiography due to angina pectoris and received a stent during the angiography. This will help compare the occlusion grade and the rate of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) between the two techniques. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and will be considered for enrollment after a detailed evaluation by the study team.

55-year-old man diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma after experiencing disease progression despite undergoing nephrectomy. The patient has at least one measurable lesion with a diameter of 20 mm or more by conventional techniques or 10 mm or more by spiral CT scan. The patient has a performance status of CTC 0-2, with a WBC count of at least 2,000/mm^3 and a platelet count of at least 75,000/mm^3. The patient has no baseline neuropathy or cerebellar dysfunction greater than grade 1 and has not received prior carboxyamidotriazole or concurrent filgrastim (G-CSF) or sargramostim (GM-CSF). The patient has not undergone chemotherapy in at least four weeks and has not undergone radiotherapy in at least four weeks. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and fertile patients must use effective contraception. The patient is willing to participate in a randomized, double-blind, multicenter study to assess the effectiveness of carboxyamidotriazole in treating metastatic kidney cancer.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl from a low-income, ethnic minority family living in Los Angeles County. She has not received any doses or only one dose of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine. She is a patient at Northeast Valley Health Corporation, one of the largest federally qualified health centers in the county. She speaks English or Spanish and has received at least one service at the FQHC in the past two years. She is eligible to participate in a clinical trial aimed at increasing HPV vaccine uptake among low-income, ethnic minority adolescents in Los Angeles County. The trial will evaluate the effects of three different clinic-level reminder systems (mailed letter, automated/robo telephone call, text message) on HPV vaccine initiation and completion. The reminder messages will be delivered in the patient's preferred language (either English or Spanish) and will emphasize the importance of HPV vaccination and how to make an appointment. The patient will be randomized to the usual care or one of the three reminder system interventions. Data extracted from electronic medical records will be used to measure HPV vaccine initiation and completion rates at regular intervals post-intervention implementation.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic neuropathic pain for the past 2 years. He has been diagnosed with a neurologic lesion and has been using a TENS device for the past 6 months with some relief. However, he finds the device to be cumbersome and uncomfortable to use on a daily basis. His DN4 score is 7/10, indicating a significant level of pain. He is covered by national health insurance and is able to express consent for participation in the study. He has no planned surgeries or modifications to his treatment plan in the next two months, and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials. There are no medical contraindications for TENS therapy for this patient.

Patient is a 50yo Caucasian male who presents with moderate knee osteoarthritis and a BMI of 28. He reports joint discomfort and mobility impairment. He has no history of heart disease, kidney or liver disease, or any other disease that might influence the results of the study. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of non-animal chondroitin sulphate for overweight subjects with knee osteoarthritis. He is willing to be randomly assigned to either the experimental group or the control group and is committed to attending all follow-up appointments for the duration of the trial.

The patient is a 42-year-old man with epilepsy who has been diagnosed for 10 years. He has seizures once a month, which are controlled with carbamazepine 600mg/day. He works as an accountant and has a regular sleep schedule. He does not have any other medical conditions and does not take any medications other than carbamazepine. He is interested in participating in a study that could help him improve his quality of life and sleep. He does not have any cognitive or psychiatric disorders that may interfere with his participation in the study. He has never practiced yoga before but is willing to learn and participate in the program. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is married and has two children. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with them.

A 14-year-old girl with a history of a prenatal ovarian cyst diagnosed during the third trimester of her mother's pregnancy presented to the clinic for a follow-up evaluation. The cyst was identified during a routine ultrasound and was managed conservatively. The patient has not reported any complications related to the cyst but was interested in learning more about the long-term effects on her ovarian function and puberty. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She is a healthy, active teenager who has started to notice some changes in her body but has not yet started menstruating. Her parents have provided written consent for her to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with fever, chills, and confusion. He was diagnosed with sepsis due to a urinary tract infection. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He is currently taking lisinopril, metformin, and glipizide. His vital signs are: temperature 39°C, heart rate 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate 28 breaths per minute, and blood pressure 90/60 mmHg. Blood tests reveal a white blood cell count of 15,000 cells/mm3 and a lactate level of 3.5 mmol/L. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluids, but his condition continued to deteriorate. He was then considered for the clinical trial for resatorvid because of his severe sepsis with respiratory failure.

A 55-year-old male patient with confirmed COVID-19 infection presented at the hospital with respiratory distress, a respiratory rate of 35 per minute, and an oxygen saturation level of 91% at rest. He was admitted to the ICU and put on a respirator within the first 24 hours of hospitalization. His chest radiograph showed pneumonia. He has no history of malignancy or co-infection. He has been married for 30 years and has two children. He is a smoker and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He takes medications for these conditions. He has no known allergies to food or drugs. He works as a manager in a retail store and enjoys playing golf on weekends. He is interested in participating in clinical trials that can help him recover from COVID-19.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is not a medical intervention trial. It is an evaluation of an online professional development course for teachers and parents with eligibility criteria based on their profession and access to technology.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who is generally healthy and physically active. She lives in the UK and has a BMI of 24 kg/m2. She has never been on a weight loss diet and is not currently taking any medication that may affect her appetite. She is not allergic to any of the test foods and has no dietary restrictions. She does not smoke and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is interested in participating in the study to learn how different macronutrients affect her appetite and overall energy intake.

The patient is a 52-year-old female diagnosed with rectal cancer located approximately 10 cm from the anal verge. She has no history of previous intestinal surgery except for an appendectomy. She is in good general health with an ASA score of II. Her BMI is 25 and she does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is fluent in English and has no physical or psychological barriers that prevent her from providing oral and written consent. She has no signs of distant metastasis and the tumor does not involve any neighboring organs.

54-year-old male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF=25%) was referred to the cardiology department for evaluation of the candidacy for CRT-D implantation. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue upon exertion, as well as occasional palpitations. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He does not smoke, but reports occasional alcohol consumption. The patient has been on guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, including beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics. On physical examination, he has jugular venous distention, bilateral basal rales, and a displaced point of maximal impulse. An electrocardiogram shows sinus rhythm with a prolonged QRS duration of 150 ms. An echocardiogram reveals a dilated left ventricle with an EF of 25%, and moderate mitral regurgitation. After evaluation, the patient is deemed a suitable candidate for CRT-D implantation with Biotronik CRT-D and QP lead featuring MultiPole pacing mode. The patient agrees to participate in the BIO|SELECT Pilot study and provides written informed consent.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from the United States who was recently hospitalized for an acute myocardial infarction confirmed by elevated cardiac enzymes and electrocardiographic changes. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine and lisinopril. He was discharged from the hospital with a prescription for a beta-blocker. He is willing to participate in the PACE-MI (OBTAIN) registry study to help researchers evaluate the effect of beta-blocker use on post-MI survival. He is able to attend follow-up appointments and provide information about his medication use and any cardiovascular hospitalizations.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for the past 6 months. She was diagnosed with asthma at the age of 10 and has been using an albuterol inhaler as needed. Her symptoms have been worsening and she has been experiencing more frequent asthma attacks, despite using her inhaler regularly. She has a history of smoking, but quit 2 years ago. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. She has signed the informed consent form and is affiliated with a health insurance plan. Her spirometry results show an MMV of 85%, and MMV/VC of 75%. Carbon Monoxide Transfer Coefficient (KcO) is 85%. She has not had any broncho-pulmonary infectious diseases or oral/systemic corticotherapy in the past 3 months. She is willing to participate in the study to better understand her asthma and find a more effective treatment plan.

A 42-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV infection who has been receiving antiretroviral therapy for more than 4 weeks is eligible for this clinical trial. He has no history of pneumococcal infection or vaccination, no current opportunistic infections, and no known immunodeficiency other than HIV infection. He does not have any coagulation disorders. The CD4 T-cell count of the patient will determine which group he will be assigned to. If the CD4 T-cell count is ≥350 cells/µL, he will be assigned to Group 1, and if the CD4 T-cell count is <350 cells/µL, he will be assigned to Group 2. The patient will be informed about the study, and informed consent will be taken before enrolling him in the trial. Venous blood samples of 10 mL will be collected on day 0 and post-vaccination day 28 ± 7.

The patient is a 60 year old male with a history of ischemic heart disease and heart failure. He has undergone myocardial perfusion scintigraphy and has been recommended for implantation of an ICD due to a low LVEF of 25% and NYHA stage III symptoms. He has provided informed consent and is a member of a social security system. He has no history of open heart surgery, diabetes mellitus or dementia. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient has been experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain. He is currently taking medications including beta blockers and ACE inhibitors to manage his heart condition. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially avoid unnecessary implantation of an ICD, but understands that he may still require one for his condition.

A 64 year old female patient is scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to gallstones. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of diabetes or hypertension. The patient has a BMI of 28 and has no history of skin lesions or pressure injuries. She is scheduled for a 4-hour surgery and will be positioned in the supine position for over 3 hours. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and has agreed to be randomized to either the control or intervention group. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of triple-negative breast cancer presents with clinical symptoms of metastatic disease. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension treated with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. She has no history of diabetes, heart disease, or other significant medical conditions. Her menopausal status is not specified. The physical examination reveals multiple palpable masses in both breasts and right axillary lymphadenopathy. No other palpable lymph nodes or organomegaly are noted. Laboratory evaluation reveals WBC count of 4,500/mm³ and platelet count of 120,000/mm³. She has normal electrolytes, bilirubin, and renal function with a creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min. Her liver function tests reveal ALT and AST levels within the normal range, but with an alkaline phosphatase level that is slightly elevated at 2.7 times the upper limit of normal. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she agrees to use effective contraception. She has no known hypersensitivity to bendamustine hydrochloride, mannitol, or erlotinib hydrochloride. She has not received prior bendamustine or EGFR-directed therapy. She has not received any other antineoplastic treatments in the past 2 months, including radiotherapy, chemotherapy, biological therapy, hormonal therapy, immunotherapy, gene therapy, and surgery. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma. He has undergone a partial nephrectomy in the past for a benign kidney tumor. He is in overall good health with a Karnofsky performance status of 90%. He has no significant medical history, but his blood pressure is controlled with medication. The patient is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. He has not received any prior systemic therapy for advanced RCC. He does not have brain metastases or evidence of symptomatic brain or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis on screening CT or MRI scan. He has no active infection or concurrent treatment on another clinical trial. He is surgically sterile and is willing to use effective contraception during the period of therapy.

A 60-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer requiring androgen deprivation therapy for at least 3 months prior to inclusion. The patient has not been participating in any strength or cardiovascular training 2 times or more per week prior to inclusion. He has a cognitive well-functioning status to be able to answer questionnaires and train according to instructions. The patient has not been diagnosed with metastasis to other regions than bones and has a haemoglobin percentage greater than 6.1 mmol/l. He has no history of mental or physical conditions that make him unfit for participation. The patient is not at risk of getting an osteoporotic fracture due to long-term treatment with steroids or earlier fractures due to minimal trauma. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes who has been struggling to control her blood sugar levels with oral medications alone. She is interested in trying Exubera, an inhaled form of insulin, to see if it can help improve her glucose control. She has no history of lung or heart disease and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her life expectancy is not limited by any other medical conditions. She meets the eligibility criteria for receiving Exubera treatment based on the approved local label.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who has been experiencing mild memory loss and difficulty in completing daily tasks for the past 9 months. He has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication to control it. He has completed the primary education and has been retired for the past 5 years. He lives with his wife who is capable of accompanying him on all clinic visits. He has no history of neurological diseases or head trauma. He has undergone brain MRI and CT scan which confirmed the diagnosis of mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment. He has been diagnosed with kidney deficiency pattern by a Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioner. His Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 22 and his Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score is 25. He has adequate visual and auditory abilities to perform all aspects of cognitive and functional assessments. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has signed and dated written informed consent, along with his caregiver.

A 19-year-old female with acute lymphoblastic leukemia who is scheduled for an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) using a myeloablative conditioning regimen. The patient has no known allergies to rifaximin or other rifamycin antimicrobial agents. She has no ongoing bacterial, viral or fungal infections and is not currently on broad-spectrum antibiotics for the treatment of a previous infection. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has been informed about the study and has consented to participate.

52 yo F with a history of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and associated right heart failure, NYHA class III. She has been clinically stable and on optimized PAH treatment for the past 6 months. Her current medications include sildenafil, bosentan, and diuretics. Her mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) is 35 mmHg and her 6 minute walk distance (6MWD) is 150m. She has no evidence of fluid overload or volume depletion. Her past medical history includes hypothyroidism and depression, both well-controlled with medications. She has no history of reactive airways disease or adverse reactions to beta-blockers. She has a resting heart rate of 70 bpm and no heart block on ECG. Her cardiac index is 2.2 l/min/m2 and her pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is 10 mmHg. She is interested in participating in a study of carvedilol for PAH and associated right heart failure, and is willing to undergo multiple assessments including cardiac MRI, 6 minute walk distance, serum brain natriuretic peptide, echocardiogram, and functional class assessment. She provides informed consent and has no contraindications to CT or PET scanning, no coagulopathy or severe renal insufficiency, and no malignancy or co-morbidity limiting survival or ability to complete the study.

The patient is a 66-year-old female with a history of type II diabetes. She has been diagnosed with COVID-19 and has a deficient serum vitamin D level of 20 ng/ml. She has not received any cholecalciferol supplementation within the last 6 weeks. She has no known history of renal stones or hypercalcemia within the past year, and her baseline serum total calcium level is within normal limits. She has no established diagnosis associated with an increased risk of hypercalcemia, no known malignancy, no organ transplant, and no known chronic autoimmune diseases. She is not currently on systemic steroids for any cause. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of vitamin D therapy on morbidity and mortality in patients with COVID-19.

This clinical trial is seeking normal male and female subjects who are over the age of 18 years. The study will determine whether Tetrix Cream remains on the hands after gentle washing with soap and water. Participants will be required to apply Tetrix Cream to their hands and then wash their hands with soap and water. The study will assess whether the cream is removed from the hands after washing. No underlying medical conditions are required for participation in this study.

The patient is an 8-year-old girl named Lily who will soon receive her annual flu vaccination. Lily has a history of experiencing severe distress during her previous vaccinations, which led to her developing a fear of needles. She is generally healthy and has no history of allergies or chronic illnesses. Lily enjoys using technology and is familiar with computers and cell phones. She lives with her parents and younger brother, who have no significant medical history. She attends school regularly and is currently in the third grade. Her parents are concerned about her distress during vaccinations and are willing to try new methods to reduce her anxiety.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 7 years. He reports that his pain is worse with prolonged sitting and standing, and is relieved with lying down. He has tried conservative treatments including physical therapy, chiropractic care, and medication management without significant relief. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has never had surgery on his lumbar spine. His imaging studies show degenerative disc disease at the L4/L5 level with decreased disc height and facet joint degeneration. His preoperative Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score is 40 out of 100, indicating moderate disability. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for XL TDR® eXtreme Lateral Total Disc Replacement for the treatment of lumbar degenerative disc disease. He understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to comply with all protocol visits and assessments. The patient's BMI is 32, and he does not have any allergies to the device materials. He is not enrolled in any other investigational studies and does not have any waddell signs of inorganic behavior.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has been experiencing abnormal vaginal discharge, itching, and odor for the past week. She visited a gynecological clinic and tested positive for bacterial vaginosis. She has no history of sexually transmitted infections and has been sexually active with her partner for the past year. She wants to participate in a clinical trial that compares the once-daily in-situ forming metronidazole vaginal gel with the twice-daily conventional metronidazole vaginal gel. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all follow-up appointments. She is not pregnant or nursing and has no difficulty communicating in English.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with medullary thyroid cancer six months ago. She has undergone surgery and has received chemotherapy, but her condition has not improved. She experiences mild fatigue and loss of appetite but is otherwise healthy. Her calcitonin levels are greater than 16 pg/mL, and she has evidence of metastatic medullary thyroid cancer on CT scan. She has no history of autoimmune diseases, HIV, or hepatitis. She is not currently taking any systemic steroids, and her hematological and biochemical parameters are within normal limits. She is willing to travel to the NIH for follow-up visits and understands the risks and benefits of the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use effective birth control during and for six months after the last vaccination therapy. She meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

This is a 52-year-old female who has recently been diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) after experiencing headaches and seizures. She underwent surgical removal of the tumor and has completed radiation therapy. She is now being offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of a herbal supplement, Boswellia serrata, in combination with standard treatment for GBM. The trial aims to determine whether this herbal approach can reduce peritumoral brain edema and improve quality of life and survival. The patient is in good overall health with

This is a 6-month-old infant with a congenital heart defect that requires radical correction under cardiopulmonary bypass. The patient has no history of acute renal or liver failure before surgery and has not required any cardiotonic support leading up to the procedure. The patient's medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

The patient is an 80 year-old male with a medical history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. He is scheduled to undergo hip joint surgery under spinal anesthesia. He has no known allergies to any of the study drugs and is not taking any beta blockers or monoamine oxidase inhibitors. His ejection fraction is within normal limits and he has no history of heart block or arrhythmias. He has no coagulopathy or increased intracranial tension. His baseline blood pressure is stable and he is able to maintain standard calm breathing at a rate of 6-8 breaths per minute. He has not received any medication prior to the surgery except for his antihypertensive medication.

A 55 yo woman who has been experiencing menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. She is interested in Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) to alleviate these symptoms but is concerned about the potential side effects of estrogen. She has a history of high cholesterol and is currently taking a statin medication. She has also tried natural remedies such as black cohosh and soy isoflavones but has not found significant relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that combines HRT with herbal supplements such as garlic oil, rutin, and nattokinase to reduce the potential side effects of estrogen. She has never been diagnosed with breast cancer or any other estrogen-dependent malignant tumors, and has no history of venous or arterial thromboembolic disease. She is willing to undergo regular check-ups and follow the study protocol.

32 yo F, 37 weeks gestation, with a singleton pregnancy scheduled for an elective cesarean section due to a previous c-section. She is 165 cm tall and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. She has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA grade I. The patient has no known uterine abnormalities, ruptured membranes, oligohydramnios, or intrauterine growth restriction. She has not been diagnosed with hypertension, diabetes, or eclampsia during her pregnancy. She has no history of spinal deformities or infections and is willing to sign informed consent.

6 weeks old healthy full-term infant with no malformations or disorders affecting the gastrointestinal or urinary tract. The infant was born at gestational week 39+1 and has been meeting all developmental milestones. The parents are fluent in Swedish and interested in participating in the study to potentially prevent functional bowel and bladder disorders in their child. The infant has not yet started toilet training, making them eligible for the study.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who is currently residing in an institutionalized setting. He is able to walk independently without any technical aid but has experienced some difficulty with balance in recent months. He reports occasional pain in his lower back and knees, but the pain does not interfere with his daily activities. He does not have a history of depression or any other significant medical conditions. He is interested in participating in a study to improve his balance and overall physical health. He is able to understand the study aims and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 19 year old African American male college student who smokes an average of 7 cigarettes per day for the past 3 years. He is currently studying business and hopes to start his own company after graduation. He lives on campus and enjoys playing basketball with his friends in his free time. He reports no significant medical history and has never been diagnosed with any chronic illnesses. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to learn more about the potential genetic changes caused by smoking and to potentially contribute to the development of early cancer screening methods.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with a glioblastoma in her right temporal lobe. She is married with two teenage children and works as a teacher. She is right-handed and has always enjoyed reading and playing the piano. She has noticed some difficulty with her vision in her left eye and has been experiencing some mild cognitive impairment, such as forgetting appointments and difficulty with word-finding. Her overall health is good, and she is currently taking medication for hypertension. She has no history of psychiatric disease and has never had any visual problems leading to certification as sight impaired. She is willing to undergo surgery to remove the tumor and has given informed consent to participate in the SIND study. She has no contraindications for a contrast-enhanced MRI.

A 28-year-old woman was diagnosed with strabismus during her routine eye examination. She has a history of amblyopia in her right eye since childhood, which was treated with patching therapy. She wears corrective glasses but still experiences double vision in certain visual fields. She has a valid driver's license and drives regularly for work and personal errands. She reports difficulty with judging distances, especially when changing lanes or merging onto highways. She has not undergone any previous strabismus surgery. She is interested in participating in this study to improve her driving ability and hopes that the surgery will help her overcome her visual challenges while driving.

A 45-year-old man is diagnosed with active tuberculosis and is being treated at a local clinic. The patient has been in close contact with his family members and co-workers, and he is concerned about their health. The patient is approached by study staff and is asked to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the likelihood of his contacts developing active TB within 12 months. The patient agrees to participate and provides the contact information of his family members and co-workers. The study staff will follow up with these contacts and will test them for TB. The patient will also undergo blood tests to determine his levels of C-reactive protein (CRP), hemoglobin (Hb), and iron homeostasis markers, including Hepcidin, Ferritin, and Transferrin. The study staff will evaluate the correlation between these markers and the progression of TB. The patient will be followed up at 6 months and 12 months, and if he meets the presumptive TB or sputum expectorator definitions at any time during the follow-up period, he will undergo Xpert Ultra (or Xpert MTB/RIF if Ultra is unavailable) and culture testing. All positive cultures will undergo whole genome sequencing (WGS) to track index case and co-prevalent or incident case transmission. The patient's information will be kept confidential and identified only by a code. The study will also enroll other participants in South Africa, Mozambique, and Uganda who meet the eligibility criteria.

A 12-year-old male with a history of tetralogy of Fallot and a previous surgical repair of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) presents with symptoms of RVOT obstruction and insufficiency. The patient reports shortness of breath, fatigue, and exercise intolerance. An echocardiogram reveals significant stenosis and regurgitation in the RVOT. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the REVALV study, including being between the ages of 5 and 70, having a weight of at least 30kg, and having an RVOT diameter of 22mm or less. The patient does not have any exclusions, including no incompatibility with a 22Fr delivery health and no coronary anomalies near the RVOT. The patient and their legal guardians provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) three years ago. She has undergone two prior chemotherapy regimens and a stem cell transplant, but her cancer has relapsed and now requires treatment due to progressive disease. She has measurable disease according to the 2014 Lugano criteria for non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Her blood counts and renal and hepatic function are adequate. She has no history of pneumonitis, and her cardiovascular health is stable. She has not received any prior therapy with a cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK9) inhibitor. She is not on any immunosuppressive treatment, including systemic or enteric corticosteroids, except for topical use. She is willing to participate in a Phase 1 clinical trial and provide written informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman, who is a close family member of a person diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, is seeking support and assistance in caring for her loved one. She has been the primary caregiver for the past year and has noticed an increase in stress and anxiety related to the caregiving role, especially with the added concerns of COVID-19. She has access to the internet and is interested in participating in a study that will provide her with tools and resources to better manage her stress and anxiety levels. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who regularly attends the Oslo Mammography Screening Program. She has no current breast complaints, and her last mammogram was conducted 2 years ago, which showed no abnormalities. She has no family history of breast cancer, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol only occasionally. She has a pacemaker implanted due to a previous heart condition but is otherwise in good health. She is interested in participating in the Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) trial and has signed the informed consent form.

45 yo F recently diagnosed with Stage II breast cancer. The patient is scheduled to undergo neoadjuvant TC chemotherapy (docetaxel, cyclophosphamide) for 4 cycles. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. She has a WBC count of 5.0 × 109/L, hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 180 × 109/L. Liver function tests are within normal limits. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is willing to comply with the study procedures. The patient is using an oral contraceptive method of birth control. She has no history of tuberculosis or exposure to tuberculosis. She has no known hypersensitivity to E.coli derived proteins or any other components of the study drug. The patient has not received any other investigational drugs or biologics within 1 month or five half-lives of enrollment. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not undergone radiation therapy or bone marrow or stem-cell transplantation. She has no underlying medical condition that would make the administration of study drug hazardous to the patient or that would obscure the interpretation of adverse events. The patient is not seropositive for HIV or have had an AIDS-defining illness or any known immunodeficiency disorder. The patient meets all the inclusion and exclusion criteria for this study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with advanced gastric cancer that has spread to the liver and lungs. He has received first-line chemotherapy with cisplatin and fluorouracil but did not respond well to treatment. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well controlled with medication. He has a performance status of 1 and an estimated life expectancy of at least 6 months. His bone marrow function is within normal limits, and his liver and kidney function are within normal limits. He has no history of autoimmune disease and has not received live vaccines within the last 30 days. He has no symptomatic brain metastases or other active malignancies. He is willing to comply with the study plans and sign the informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been suffering from chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis for the past year. He has been experiencing nasal obstruction, congestion, and discharge for more than 12 weeks. The patient has undergone CT scans and endoscopic exams which have confirmed the presence of paranasal sinus mucosal inflammation and nasal polyps. He has not been treated with any oral or systemic IV glucocorticoids or immunomodulatory biologics in the past 2 weeks. The patient is willing to sign an IRB approved research consent form to participate in the study. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, including no history of facial trauma, sinonasal neoplasm, pregnancy, lactation or mental disability. He is excited to take part in this study to better understand the mechanism of action of omalizumab and to possibly identify specific responders for this treatment.

This is a 65-year-old female with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis for the last 10 months. She has a history of coronary artery disease, for which she underwent a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stenting three years ago. She has been on clopidogrel and aspirin since then, but her platelet reactivity has remained high despite the medication. Her recent platelet function test showed P2Y12 reaction units (PRUs) of 250. She has no known allergies to aspirin, clopidogrel, or ticagrelor. She has no concomitant use of other antithrombotic drugs, thrombocytopenia, or hematocrit <25%. Her hemoglobin A1c is 7.5%, and she has no liver disease, severe pulmonary disease, or active bleeding. She has not had any acute coronary or cerebrovascular events in the last 3 months, and she is not pregnant. She is not taking any cytochrome P450 inhibitors or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and she has not been treated with glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antagonists in the last 30 days.

Patient A is a 55-year-old woman who had a stroke 6 months ago. She has been receiving physical therapy for the past 3 months and has improved her ability to walk with an assistive device. She can walk for up to 10 minutes with a walker or cane, but experiences fatigue and difficulty maintaining her balance. Her gait speed is measured at 0.8 m/s. She is motivated to continue her rehabilitation and improve her walking ability. She has no history of significant cardiac or pulmonary disease, and is cleared for aerobic exercise by her primary care physician. She is not currently using a pacemaker or any other medical device. She is able to follow instructions and is willing to participate in a mixed exercise program involving treadmill training and resistance exercise. She is classified as American Heart Association class B and has a modified Rankin score of 2.

A 58-year-old Hispanic man with type 2 diabetes presents with a non-healing wound on his left foot. He has had diabetes for 15 years and takes metformin and insulin. He smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and has a history of hypertension. He reports that the wound has been present for 6 months and has not improved with standard wound care. He denies any loss of sensation or pain in his foot. He is able to walk without assistance and has not experienced any recent falls or trauma. His HbA1c level is 9.5% (80 mmol/mol). He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of inhibiting glucocorticoid activation on skin function and wound healing in patients with type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who underwent surgery for a type A thoracic aortic dissection (AD) or intramural hematoma (AH) at Grenoble University Hospital between 1 January 1990 and 30 June 2007. He is currently being monitored as an outpatient and is able to travel to Grenoble University Hospital for the study. He has given his written consent to participate in the study. The patient has a history of hypertension and has been taking antihypertensive medication for the past 5 years. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently participating in any other studies. The patient is covered by the French social security system. He does not have any mobility issues and is able to comply with the requirements of the protocol. The patient is not pregnant, recently gave birth or is breastfeeding. The patient is not in the terminal phase of a serious illness.

The patient is a 55-year-old non-smoking woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is currently scheduled to start treatment with Tarceva in the next few days. She has no history of skin rash or other skin toxicity. She has not received any systemic or intranasal antibiotics in the past 7 days, nor has she used any other topical formulations in the past 14 days. She has not received any other anticancer therapy in addition to Tarceva. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

55-year-old male with a history of smoking and a recent diagnosis of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has undergone one line of chemotherapy but has not responded to treatment. The patient has no history of brain metastases or symptomatic brain metastases and does not require dehydrating agents or corticosteroids to control intracranial symptoms. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has at least one measurable lesion as defined by RECIST (version 1.1), confirmed by computed tomography (CT) scan or MRI. The patient is EGFR-negative and ALK-negative and has a survival expectation of greater than 3 months. The patient's main organ function is normal, and the patient is willing and able to comply with all aspects of the protocol. The patient has provided written informed consent before participating and is a female of childbearing potential who has had a negative pregnancy test in the past 7 days.

Sophie is a 28-year-old woman who has been struggling with insomnia for the past 6 months. Despite practicing good sleep hygiene and trying over-the-counter sleep aids, she still has difficulty falling and staying asleep. She reports feeling tired and irritable during the day, which is affecting her work and social life. Sophie has a head circumference of 58 cm and owns an Android smartphone with internet access. She is not currently taking any medications and does not have a history of mental health disorders. Sophie is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve her sleep quality and is willing to commit to performing at least 3 sessions per week with the URGOnight solution for about 4 months. She understands the study requirements and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 2-year-old child from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) who is experiencing cough and fever for the past 3 days. The parents noticed that the child has been breathing faster than usual and is having difficulty breathing. They took the child to the local hospital where they suspect that the child may have pneumonia. The child has no other underlying medical conditions and has never been diagnosed with pneumonia before. The parents have given the child acetaminophen to reduce fever but have not given any other medication. The child is alert and responsive but appears to be in distress due to difficulty breathing. The vital signs are as follows: Temperature - 38.5°C, Heart rate - 120 bpm, Respiratory rate - 40 breaths per minute, Oxygen saturation - 90%. The parents have given written consent for the child to participate in the clinical trial to test the Multimometer device for measuring vital signs in children suspected of having pneumonia.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. She has had previous chemotherapy for metastatic disease and had a partial response but then discontinued the chemotherapy due to side effects. She has not received any other therapy for metastatic disease. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no known allergies. She lives alone and works as a teacher. She has no children. She has measurable disease as defined by RECIST version 1.1. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has normal organ and marrow function as defined in the eligibility criteria. She has archival tumor tissue available that is formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded. She understands the study and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. She has not received prior treatment with any CDK inhibitor. She has no known active uncontrolled or symptomatic central nervous system (CNS) metastases. She is not using any food or drugs known to be potent CYP3A4 inhibitors or drugs known to be potent CYP3A4 inducers. She has not had major surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or other anti-cancer therapy within 3 weeks before treatment. She has not had any of the following within 6 months prior to study consent: myocardial infarction, severe/unstable angina, ongoing cardiac dysrhythmias of NCI CTCAE Grade 2 or more, atrial fibrillation of any grade, coronary/peripheral artery bypass graft, symptomatic congestive heart failure, cerebrovascular accident including transient ischemic attack, or symptomatic pulmonary embolism. She has no impairment of gastro-intestinal function or GI disease that may significantly alter the absorption of palbociclib. She has not had hematopoietic stem cell or bone marrow transplantation. She has no known hypersensitivity to anastrozole. She does not have known human immunodeficiency virus infection. She has no severe acute or chronic medical or psychiatric condition that may increase the risk associated with study participation or investigational product administration or may interfere with the interpretation of study results. She is not participating in other studies involving investigational drug(s) within 4 weeks before treatment initiation in this study.

A 20-year-old male college student complains of headaches occurring 2-3 times per week, lasting for 3-4 hours each time. The headache pain is described as a band-like tightness, moderate to severe in intensity, and located bilaterally in the forehead and temples region. The patient also reports that he has been experiencing neck pain and stiffness, especially after spending long hours studying or using his laptop. He denies any visual disturbances, nausea, or vomiting. He has no significant past medical history, and he is not taking any medications. He denies smoking, alcohol use, or drug abuse. On physical examination, the patient has a forward head posture, rounded shoulders, and tightness in the cervical muscles. The neurological exam is unremarkable. The patient's vital signs are within the normal range. Laboratory investigations, including CBC, electrolytes, and liver function tests, are all normal. The diagnosis of tension-type headache is made according to the International Headache Society criteria. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of exercise and relaxation techniques on tension headache pain parameters in university students.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of cardiovascular diseases. He was diagnosed with non-ST segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) a few months ago and was hospitalized for treatment. He also has a history of hypertension, high cholesterol levels, and a family history of heart disease. The patient is currently taking medications for his conditions and has been advised to make lifestyle changes to improve his health. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. The patient is willing to participate in the Fujian Province Cardiovascular Diseases Study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 45-year-old man who works as a construction worker and complains of chronic knee pain has been referred to the clinic. He has noticed that his right leg feels shorter than his left leg and he has been experiencing discomfort in his hips as well. He has no history of previous surgeries or injuries to his legs or hips. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions. He has flat feet and has never used shoe inserts or lifts before.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of right hip replacement surgery 10 years ago due to osteoarthritis. He has been experiencing pain and stiffness in the hip joint for the past 6 months which has been progressively worsening. X-ray and MRI imaging show possible loosening of the prosthesis. The patient is scheduled for surgical evaluation and tissue sampling to determine if there is an infection or aseptic loosening. He has no known allergies and no active inflammatory or infectious processes at any other location. The patient is willing to undergo both 68Gallium-citrate and 18F-FDG PET/CT scans to aid in the evaluation of his condition.

A 48-year-old man visited the urology outpatient clinic with a history of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) for the last 6 months. He complains of a weak urine stream, hesitancy, straining, and incomplete bladder emptying. He also experienced urgency and frequency, particularly during the night. The symptoms have been progressively worsening, affecting his quality of life. He denies any pain, hematuria, or fever. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril 20mg daily. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. On examination, his abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no palpable bladder. Digital rectal exam reveals a moderately enlarged prostate gland with a smooth surface, no nodularity, and no tenderness. His prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is within the normal range. His International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) is 16. Uroflowmetry shows a maximum flow rate (Qmax) of 8 ml/sec with a voided volume of 250 ml. The residual urine volume is less than 50 ml. The urodynamic study confirms the diagnosis of bladder outlet obstruction. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the urodynamic effects of UK-369,003 in men with LUTS.

28-year-old male diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for 5 years, currently using insulin pump therapy and experiencing recurrent hypoglycemic episodes despite adjustments to insulin dosing. His HbA1C level has been consistently above 8%. The patient is interested in participating in the pilot study for the DiaPort Closed-Loop Artificial Pancreas. He has no history of cardiovascular events, retinopathy, or significant laboratory abnormalities. The patient is mentally capable and willing to perform repeated glucose checks, consume standardized meals, and take insulin as instructed. He is affiliated with a social medical insurance and has signed the informed consent form.
