The patient is not currently enrolled in another clinical trial and has an annual study income of less than 4,500€.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was admitted to Duke University NCCU with a diagnosis of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). The patient has a history of hypertension and presented to the emergency department with a sudden onset of severe headache, vomiting, and confusion. The patient's Glasgow Coma Score is 12, and her Hunt and Hess Score is 3. An intraventricular catheter was placed to manage her intracranial pressure (ICP). The patient has been in the hospital for 48 hours, and her condition remains stable. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been wearing soft contact lenses for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing difficulty reading small print and has to hold reading materials farther from his eyes. He also has a mild astigmatism in his left eye. His visual acuity is 20/20 in his right eye and 20/25 in his left eye with his current contact lenses. He has no significant ocular history and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol socially. His blood pressure is well-controlled on medication. He works as a computer programmer and spends most of his day in front of a computer screen. He uses artificial tears occasionally to relieve dryness and discomfort. He is interested in participating in a study that compares the pre-lens tear film characteristics of daily disposable contact lenses for presbyopia and astigmatism. He is willing to wear study lenses for up to 12 hours and attend all study visits. He meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with follicular non-Hodgkin's lymphoma 3 years ago. He underwent chemotherapy and achieved partial remission, but the disease relapsed 6 months ago. He has no history of allergies or other medical conditions. He is married and has two children. He works as a sales manager and leads an active lifestyle. His current symptoms include fatigue, night sweats, and occasional fever. His latest FDG-PET and CT scans showed multiple lymphoma lesions in his neck, chest, and abdomen. His physician prescribed standard radioimmunotherapy with 90-yttrium-labeled anti-CD20 antibodies as the next line of treatment. He has agreed to participate in the RIT registry and MERIT-NHL study, and his pre-treatment FDG-PET and CT images will be used to evaluate prognostic factors for his treatment outcome.

Patient A is a healthy 12-month-old toddler who is up to date on all routine vaccinations. The toddler has no documented history of serious acute or chronic disease, known or suspected impairment of immunologic function, or known hypersensitivity to any vaccine components. The parent or legal guardian has provided informed consent and is willing and able to comply with all trial procedures

This is a 45-year-old woman who has been living with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 10 years. She has been on multiple disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) and biologic agents but has not been able to achieve complete control of her symptoms. She recently completed the core study of ACZ885A2207 and did not experience any serious or severe drug-related adverse effects. Her rheumatologist has recommended that she participate in the extension study to assess the long-term safety and tolerability of ACZ885. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that it will provide her with long-term relief from her symptoms and help slow down the progression of joint damage. She understands that there may be additional inclusion and exclusion criteria that apply and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

Patient is a 3-year-old girl who is scheduled for a routine blood test at a pediatric blood drawing center. She has a history of anxiety during medical procedures and often requires multiple attempts to achieve peripheral intravenous cannulation. She has previously received topical anesthetic cream during blood draws, but this will exclude her from participating in this clinical trial.

Patient is a 25-year-old man from the United States who is generally healthy and free from any serious medical condition. He does not have any known allergies or history of neurological symptoms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an adjuvanted influenza vaccine combined with CpG7909 to help advance the development of new treatments. He has not had any recent flu shots or vaccinations and is willing to undergo laboratory safety testing as part of the study.

A 55-year-old male patient presented with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes for the past five years. He has a family history of cardiovascular disease, with his father having a heart attack in his early 50s. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and diabetes but admits to occasional smoking. He has no history of cerebrovascular or peripheral artery disease. He is concerned about the potential long-term effects of his conditions and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess his risk of developing atherosclerosis. He is willing to commit to annual follow-up testing for the next four years.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) at the age of 5. He has been on corticosteroids for the past 3 years to slow down the progression of the disease. The patient's past medical history is notable for progressive muscle weakness, difficulty with walking and standing, and frequent falls. The patient is able to walk independently for about 5 to 10 minutes at a self-selected speed, after which he requires a wheelchair. The patient's cognitive abilities are intact and he is able to understand directions for testing procedures. The patient has not undergone any recent surgeries or changes in medication. There is no family history of DMD or other muscle disorders. The patient's vital signs are normal, with a blood pressure of 120/80, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and BMI of 18. The patient has no other significant medical conditions.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with a history of partial epilepsy that has been unresponsive to medication. He has been experiencing frequent interictal spikes on standard EEG recordings. He has a normal birth history and developmental milestones. He has no significant medical history or allergies. He is currently taking levetiracetam and topiramate to control his seizures. Physical examination is unremarkable, with no neurological deficits or focal neurological signs. He has no dermatosis on his face or scalp. The patient and his parents have provided informed consent for this study.

A 58 year old man has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1 infection with compensated cirrhosis. He has not been treated with any interferon formulation, Ribavirin (RBV), or HCV Direct Acting Antivirals (DAA) (protease, polymerase inhibitor, etc.). He has no history of liver or any other organ transplant but has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. His HCV RNA is ≥ 10,000 IU/mL at screening. He has not been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and has no evidence of decompensated liver disease including, but not limited to, radiologic criteria, a history or presence of ascites, bleeding varices, or hepatic encephalopathy. The patient is interested in participating in the study to receive the investigational treatment regimen of DCV+ASV+BMS-791325 in a fixed dose combination (the DCV 3DAA (Direct Acting Antiviral) Regimen) With or Without RBV for 12 Weeks.

A 32-year-old female patient with a history of Crohn's disease and pyoderma gangrenosum is seeking participation in the open label clinical trial. She was diagnosed with Crohn's disease at the age of 25 and has been receiving treatment for the same for the past 7 years. The patient also developed pyoderma gangrenosum in the past year, which has been moderately severe and has not responded well to traditional treatments. She has never been treated with Infliximab for pyoderma gangrenosum. The patient has a good understanding of the study requirements and is willing to commit to the study visits every 2 weeks initially and then every 1-2 months later in the study. She has no history of serious infections and has not received any monoclonal antibodies other than Infliximab for the treatment of IBD. The patient is eager to participate in the clinical trial and hopes that it will provide relief from her symptoms.

Patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of recurrent diverticulitis, scheduled for hemicolectomy. She has no known history of chronic obstructive or restrictive pulmonary disease, diabetes mellitus, ischemic heart disease, or peripheral artery disease. The patient has an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status of 1, indicating she is healthy with no systemic disease. The estimated length of the surgery is less than 200 minutes and there is no anticipated need for blood transfusion or vasopressor/inotrope infusion. The patient is willing to participate in the study to help advance medical knowledge and improve patient care.

A healthy 30-year-old male with a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 23, living in Ahmedabad city, with no significant medical history or clinically abnormal findings during screening, is being recruited for the study. He has never been diagnosed with any significant disease or condition, and he does not have a history of drug addiction or recreational drug use. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or alcoholic products, and he is willing to abstain from smoking and alcohol during the study. He is able to understand and comply with the study procedures and is willing to give voluntary written informed consent to participate in the trial. He is willing to use 2 forms of effective contraception methods simultaneously during Isotretinoin study and for 1 month after the study. He is not taking any medication, including herbal medicines, within 14 days before dosing in Period I.

67 year old male with a confirmed diagnosis of CLL with p53 deletion by FISH in at least 20% of leukamia cells. Patient is currently Binet stage B with lymphocyte doubling time of less than 6 months and experiencing disease-related symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. Patient has received prior treatment with chlorambucil and prednisone but did not achieve a complete response. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is currently on amlodipine, atorvastatin, and metformin. The patient has no history of anaphylaxis or active infection.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of metastatic cancer expressing CEA. He has previously undergone standard therapy known to have a possible survival benefit, but has now progressed through that therapy or refused it. He has a Karnofsky performance score of 80% and an estimated life expectancy of more than 3 months. His blood work shows adequate hematologic function, with WBC ≥ 3000/microliter, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL, and platelets ≥ 75,000/microliter. His renal and hepatic function are adequate, with serum creatinine < 1.5 mg/dL, bilirubin < 1.5 mg/dL, and ALT and AST ≤ 2.5 x upper limit of normal. He is not currently receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He has no history of autoimmune disease or brain metastases. He has not received CEA-targeted immunotherapy for at least 3 months prior to enrollment. He is able to understand and provide signed informed consent, and is willing to return to the clinical site for adequate follow-up, as required by the protocol.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of peripheral arterial disease and presenting with claudication symptoms in the right leg. He has no other medical conditions and is on aspirin therapy. An angiogram revealed a stenotic lesion in the right external iliac artery that is suitable for stenting. The patient has a Rutherford classification score of 3. He is willing to comply with the specified follow-up evaluations and is over 18 years of age. The patient understands the nature of the procedure and provides written informed consent prior to enrolment in the study. The patient is eligible for treatment with the BeGraft Peripheral Stent Graft System (Bentley InnoMed). The target lesion is a modified TASC-II class B lesion with a single short (≤3 cm) stenosis of the external iliac artery not extending into the common femoral artery. The patient is excluded from the study if there is an aneurysm immediately adjacent to the site of stent implantation, stenosis distal to the site of stent implantation, lesions in locations subject to external compression, or heavily calcified lesions resistant to PTA. The patient is also excluded if there is a history of coagulation disorders, aspirin allergy or bleeding complications, or is unable or unwilling to tolerate anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy.

The patient is a 45 year old male with a history of bronchiectasis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has been experiencing cough with sputum production for the past 6 months and has been admitted to the hospital for exacerbation of symptoms. He is currently receiving oxygen therapy and nebulizer treatments. He has a history of smoking and quit 2 years ago after being diagnosed with COPD. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled on medications. He is currently not employed due to his health condition and spends most of his time at home. He has never undergone chest physiotherapy or Vest treatment before.

A 45-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital due to difficulty breathing and chest tightness. She has a history of asthma and has been hospitalized for exacerbations in the past. She has been on inhaled corticosteroids and beta-agonists for maintenance therapy but has still experienced frequent exacerbations. Her symptoms have been worsening over the past week, and she was unable to manage them with her usual medications. Spirometry showed evidence of airflow obstruction with a FEV1/FVC ratio of less than 70%. She has not taken any macrolide antibiotics in the past 4 weeks and does not have any contraindications to their use. Her liver function tests and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. She is fluent in English and able to provide consent for the study. She will be discharged home after completing the study.

A 30 year old woman presents to the emergency department with severe pain in her right flank that radiates towards her lower abdomen. She reports nausea and vomiting and she has not been able to tolerate any oral intake since the onset of pain. Physical examination reveals tenderness in the right costovertebral angle and lower abdomen. A urinalysis shows presence of red blood cells and leukocytes. She has no history of renal colic or any other chronic medical condition. She has not taken any pain medication prior to her visit to the emergency department. She consents to participate in the study aimed at finding the best combination of drugs for pain control in renal colic.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer that has spread to her lungs and liver. She has been undergoing chemotherapy for the past 6 months, but her symptoms have been increasing. She experiences shortness of breath, fatigue, and pain in her chest and abdomen. She has a good understanding of her illness and prognosis, but she is struggling with making decisions about her treatment options. She lives with her husband and two teenage children in a suburban area in Romania. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 2. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she has minimal symptom burden in IPOS (only three symptoms with a score of 2 or higher), and her prognosis is over 1 month according to her clinician.

A 58-year-old woman presents with a recent history of headaches and blurry vision. She underwent an MRI which showed a 4 cm mass in the right frontal lobe. Further investigations confirmed the diagnosis of glioblastoma. She has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. Her vital signs are stable and there are no neurological deficits on examination. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She speaks fluent German and is not claustrophobic. She has no artificial joints or metal parts in her body and does not have a pacemaker. She is scheduled to receive chemoradiation and adjuvant chemotherapy with temodal according to Stupp et al. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study treatment if required.

A 55 year old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis of the knees presents with complaints of persistent joint pain and discomfort. She has been taking over-the-counter NSAIDs and acetaminophen for pain relief but has not experienced significant improvement. She is interested in trying a natural supplement for her pain and discomfort. She is not currently taking glucosamine, chondroitin sulfate or MSM. She weighs 180 pounds and has no known allergies to eggs or egg products. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. She has never participated in a study to evaluate pain relief in the past 6 months and is not currently involved in any other research study.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been referred for a routine outpatient colonoscopy. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. The patient reports no history of inflammatory bowel disease or previous bowel resection. Her bowel preparation has been completed and is deemed adequate by the physician. She has no known musculoskeletal disorders or mobility issues that would limit effective patient position changes during the procedure. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who was diagnosed with schizophrenia 5 years ago. He has been taking an atypical antipsychotic medication for the past 2 years, and his symptoms have been stable. He complains of difficulty with concentration, memory, and attention. He reports that these cognitive difficulties are impacting his ability to work and engage in social activities. He lives with his parents and has a part-time job. He has a history of smoking, but he quit 6 months ago. He has no past medical history of note. He is fluent in English and has no difficulty with communication.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago. She has been on oral hypoglycemic agents for the past 3 years, but her blood sugar levels are not well-controlled. Her current HbA1c level is 9.2%. She has no history of insulin use or any other significant medical conditions. She is currently not pregnant and is using adequate contraceptive measures. She is willing to participate in the study and is cooperative in following the protocol. She lives in Africa and is seeking better management of her diabetes.

A 54-year-old male with a history of hepatitis B presents with abdominal discomfort and fatigue. Imaging studies reveal multiple hepatic masses consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient has a Child-Pugh score of A and an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is not a candidate for resection or transplantation. The estimated survival time is greater than 12 weeks. The patient has not received systemic therapy and has at least one evaluable target mass. The patient is compliant with HBV treatment and has HBV-DNA below 500IU/mL. The patient has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in the study.

58-year-old M with a history of stroke 8 months ago presenting with moderate impairment in the affected hand. The patient reports difficulty with tasks such as holding utensils, writing, and grasping objects. The patient is medically stable and has not experienced any significant changes in motor function or tone in the past month. The patient has a detectable finger flexor hypertonia with a MAS score of 2. The patient has no visual or hearing deficits, nor cognitive impairment. The patient has no history of pulmonary disease, nor are they currently on any tone-altering medications or have received any botulinum toxin or phenol injections recently. The patient does not have a pacemaker and is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve hand function and reduce spasticity.

A 13-year-old girl diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is eligible to participate in a clinical trial investigating the oxidation rates of different substrates during exercise in children and adolescents with JIA. The patient has been diagnosed with JIA for 2 years and is currently not receiving any anti-TNFα treatment. She experiences joint pain and stiffness, especially in the morning, and has difficulty performing daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs and carrying heavy objects. Her BMI is within normal range (20.2 kg/m2) and she has not received any systemic corticosteroid treatment in the past 3 months. The patient is physically inactive due to her joint pain and stiffness, and has not participated in any regular exercise program. The patient and her parent/guardian are willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty reading for several months, and his ophthalmologist has recently diagnosed him with diabetic macular edema (DME) in his left eye. His visual acuity is 20/40 in the left eye and 20/20 in the right eye. He has no history of eye surgery, but he has had cataract surgery in his left eye 5 years ago. He is currently on metformin and glipizide for his diabetes, and his HbA1c level is 7.2%. He has no other significant medical history, and he is a non-smoker. He has no known allergies to any medications.

56-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer with multiple bone metastases. The patient has previously undergone mastectomy and has failed to respond to standard therapy including chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, and radiation. The patient has no history of CNS metastasis and does not have any pre-existing sensory or motor neuropathy of grade ≥ 2 based on NCI CTCAE V3.0. The patient has not undergone any major surgery within the last 2 weeks prior to the screening/baseline visit. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has given written informed consent complying with the local regulatory requirements.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was diagnosed with high-grade carcinoma in situ (CIS) of the bladder during a routine check-up. He has no prior history of CIS or any other malignancy. He underwent transurethral resection (TUR) of all visible lesions approximately two weeks ago. Pathology results confirmed the diagnosis of CIS. His current urinary cytology shows malignant cells. He has no muscle involvement, urethral strictures, or upper urinary tract tumors. His renal and hepatic function are normal. He has no active tuberculosis or any other active infections. He is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has no psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that would preclude study participation. He has not received any prior BCG treatment or intravesical cytostatic agents within the last three months. The patient is willing to undergo anesthesia and repeated catheterization for the study.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath and coughing for several months. She has a history of chest computed tomogram or chest radiograph findings compatible with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP). Her lung biopsy clearly documented the presence of PAP of any type or degree. She has been previously diagnosed with autoimmune PAP based on a positive (abnormal) serum GMAb test. She has not received any treatment for her condition yet. She is generally healthy and has no other serious medical illnesses. She is married, has two children, and works as a teacher. She is willing to participate in a national registry for PAP to help improve the diagnosis and treatment of the disease. She is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

28-year-old female with a history of bipolar I disorder and generalized anxiety disorder presents to the clinic seeking treatment for her anxiety symptoms. She has been stable on pharmacotherapy for the past 6 months and reports no current depressive or manic symptoms. She reports moderate to severe anxiety symptoms including excessive worry, racing thoughts, restlessness, and irritability. She has tried several psychotherapies in the past but has not found them helpful. She is currently taking lithium and quetiapine as per the Texas Implementation of Medication Algorithm. She is not pregnant and has no medical conditions that would interfere with the study. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence, psychosis, or other psychiatric disorders. She is interested in participating in a study that investigates a cognitive-behavioral therapy designed specifically to target common core processes across mood and anxiety disorders.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He is a smoker and has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath when climbing stairs. He has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is at high risk for cardiovascular events. He has never taken aspirin for prevention of heart attack or stroke. He has an upcoming appointment at the Geisinger clinic and is interested in learning more about his risk of CVD and ways to prevent it. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a patient-initiated or physician-initiated model for taking aspirin to prevent heart attack and stroke.

A 32-year-old male smoker presents with a complaint of severe sore throat on the right side, difficulty swallowing, and pain in the right ear. The patient reports a fever of 38.2°C and a general feeling of malaise. Physical examination shows trismus, uvula deviation to the left, and a swollen right tonsil with a visible white-yellowish exudate. The patient's vital signs are stable, and there is no evidence of respiratory distress. The patient consents to participate in a clinical trial that aims to prospectively evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of tonsillectomy compared to drainage under local anesthesia for the treatment of tonsillar abscess. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including being over 18 years of age, having clinical suspicion of unilateral tonsillar abscess without signs of "extra-capsular" complication, and being able to provide informed consent. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria, including contraindications to injected CT or drainage in local anesthesia, associated complications found on CT, or inability to understand the different procedures.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing knee pain for the past year. He has difficulty walking, climbing stairs, and standing for prolonged periods of time. He was previously diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis by his general practitioner and has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) to manage his symptoms. However, the NSAIDs have not been effective in reducing his pain. He has no other significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He works as a carpenter and his job requires him to stand and walk for extended periods. He has not undergone any surgery or osteotomy around his knee. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the different treatment options available to him and to potentially improve his knee OA symptoms. He is fluent in Danish and is willing to answer the questionnaires at the two-year follow-up.

A 50-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with breast cancer and is scheduled to undergo mastectomy surgery. She has opted for post-mastectomy autologous breast reconstruction using the deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap reconstruction technique. She is fluent in English and has no history of cognitive impairment or mental capacity issues. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and complete quality of life questionnaires. She has no mobility issues and is able to ambulate independently. The patient is not pregnant and meets all the inclusion criteria for the pilot randomized controlled trial comparing Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) to conventional perioperative care for patients undergoing autologous DIEP breast reconstruction.

Pt is a 50-year-old male with a history of myopia and mild hypertension. He wears corrective glasses and has a history of ocular migraines. He has been experiencing some mild blurriness in his vision and is concerned about the health of his eyes. He is interested in participating in a clinical study to assess the quality of a new color fundus camera compared to a commercially available one. He is able to comply with the examination requirements and is willing to undergo the necessary exams. His current prescription for corrective lenses is -6 diopters in both eyes.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy male who has a BMI measurement result at screening visit between 18 and 27 kg/m2. He has no significant past or present medical history of hepatic, renal, immunological, respiratory, musculoskeletal, endocrine, neurological, hemato-oncological, or cardiovascular disorders. The patient has not had any significant infection or injury within the past 21 days before the randomization. He has no genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactose dehydrogenase deficiency or glucose-galactose uptake disorder. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the consent form after listening to all procedures and objects of the clinical trial. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the clinical trial and has no history of hypersensitivity reaction that is clinically significant to gemigliptin or dapagliflozin or empagliflozin ingredients, drugs that contain the same class of ingredients, or other drugs (DPP-4i, SGLT-2i). The patient has no significant abnormalities in other clinical tests and has a clinically normal ECG.

The patient is a 34-year-old Caucasian woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 3 years. She has undergone 4 unsuccessful IVF cycles in the past, despite having a good ovarian reserve and no other significant medical conditions. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility. She has a regular menstrual cycle, with a cycle length of 28 days. She has never been pregnant before. She has no history of moderate or severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). On the day of trigger, she has no more than 10 follicles of 12mm and up. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the potential of achieving a successful IVF cycle with a different ovulation trigger approach.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) brain tumor six months ago. She presented to the clinic with a headache that was aggravated by coughing and bending over. She also experienced nausea and vomiting, as well as difficulty with speech and sensation in her left arm and leg. Imaging studies revealed a large mass in the right frontal lobe of the brain, which was subsequently biopsied and confirmed as a GBM. She underwent surgical resection of the tumor followed by radiation therapy and temozolomide chemotherapy. Her current MRI shows no evidence of disease progression, and her neurological symptoms have improved. She is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the role of Notch signaling in glioma proliferation. She has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is willing to participate in the study and agrees to adhere to the study protocol.

The patient is an adult with a confirmed diagnosis of advanced malignant tumors that is unresectable or metastatic and for which standard curative or palliative measures do not exist or are no longer effective. The tumor must carry the BRAF mutation. The patient should not have received systemic chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic therapy or radiation therapy within 4 weeks of study entry. The patient must have Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status =< 2 (Karnofsky >= 60%) and life expectancy greater than 12 weeks. The patient should have ANC >= 1.5 X 10^9/L, hemoglobin >= 9 g/dL, and platelets >= 100 X 10^9/L. The patient should have a left ventricular ejection fraction >= institutional lower limit of normal. The patient must have the ability to swallow oral medication and keep a pill diary. The patient must not have symptomatic untreated brain metastases. Pregnant women are excluded from the study due to unknown teratogenicity of dabrafenib and pazopanib and because pazopanib belongs to pregnancy risk factor group D.

The patient is an adult between 30 and 86 years old who will undergo cataract surgery by phacoemulsification. They have a physical status of ASA I or II and are cooperative during the procedure. The patient does not have communication difficulties and is not allergic to any medication in the protocol. They are not currently on chronic therapy with clonidine, antihypertensive medication, or have diabetes or glaucoma. The patient has not undergone previous surgery in the same eye and does not have any abnormalities in coagulation.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with a cataract in his left eye. He has no known allergies or medical conditions and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not sexually active and has not undergone any previous eye surgery. His physical examination and lab studies are unremarkable for any abnormalities. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, his heart rate is 75 bpm, and his oxygen saturation is 98%. He is scheduled to undergo elective eye surgery under local anesthesia at UMMC.

A 35-year-old man is currently enrolled in a methadone maintenance program for opioid addiction. He has a history of substance abuse, including heroin and prescription painkillers. The patient has completed detoxification and rehabilitation programs in the past but has experienced relapses. He has expressed interest in exploring additional treatments to support his recovery. He is fluent in English and able to attend treatment sessions and complete assessment questionnaires. The patient has no indication of active psychosis and has not participated in a past mindfulness-based relapse prevention group. He has been cleared by clinic staff to participate in the study.

As this clinical trial is retrospective and focused on comparing the results of two different types of peripheral blood stem cell mobilization, there are no specific patient characteristics needed for eligibility. However, patients included in the study would likely be those with myeloma or lymphoma who have undergone or are planning to undergo an autologous stem cell transplant. The study would include patients of all ages above 8 years who have been recommended for an ABSCT. Patients under the age of 18 would be excluded.

52 yo F diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) 5 years ago, managed on Warfarin for stroke prevention. Patient was recently diagnosed with moderate mitral stenosis during an echocardiogram, with a mitral valve area of 1.2cm2. Patient has no history of stroke, transient ischemic attack or systemic embolism. Patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. Current medications include Metformin, Lisinopril, and Atorvastatin. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the safety and efficacy of Dabigatran and Warfarin in stroke prevention amongst AF patients with moderate to severe mitral stenosis. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and has an estimated creatinine clearance of 73 mL/min.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a diagnosis of haemophilia A. He has been receiving treatment with plasma-derived factor VIII (pdFVIII) for the past 5 years. He has experienced joint bleeding episodes in his left knee and right elbow, which have resulted in some joint damage. He has not undergone any joint surgery or replacements in the past year. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the upcoming clinical trial to evaluate the impact of systematic joint examination on haemophilia treatment management decisions. He has signed the informed consent form and is ready to undergo the mandated assessments, including the HEAD-US and Haemophilia Joint Health Score (HJHS).

The patient is a 55 year old Hispanic male who presents with persistent epigastric pain, nausea and vomiting, and weight loss of 10 pounds over the past 2 months. Endoscopy and biopsy reveal adenocarcinoma of the gastroesophageal junction. Imaging studies confirm the presence of metastatic disease. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not received any prior systemic treatment. Laboratory values are within normal limits, including normal liver and kidney function. The patient has no pre-existing peripheral neuropathy and has no history of HIV or Hepatitis C. The patient is married and has two adult children. He works as an accountant and is currently on medical leave. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and has no known psychiatric illness that would limit compliance. The patient has no other history of cancer within the past 3 years.

The patient is a 55-year-old Asian man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 7 years. He has a history of hypertension with systolic blood pressure ranging from 145-160 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure ranging from 90-100 mmHg, despite concurrent treatment with two antihypertensive medications. He has previously used metformin and sulfonylurea, but they did not adequately control his blood sugar levels. He is currently on a stable dose of sitagliptin and pioglitazone. He has no history of alcohol abuse or drug addiction. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has no significant past medical history, and he is not taking any prohibited medications. His current laboratory results show an HbA1C level of 8.5% and serum potassium level of 4.5 mEq/L. He has not participated in any clinical trials or used any investigational compounds within the past 30 days. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and has signed a written informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is scheduled for a laparoscopic surgery. She has no known medical history and is generally healthy. She has never had an IV catheter inserted before and is anxious about the procedure. The patient is able to understand and speak English fluently. She has no known allergies to any medications or latex. Her vital signs are within normal limits. She has no history of depression or anxiety. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in this observational study.

A 42-year-old man presents with a history of skin rash that started 2 years ago. The rash is itchy and scaly and often appears in patches. The rash has been unresponsive to topical corticosteroids and antihistamines. He has also noticed some lymph node enlargement in his neck and groin regions. He has no significant past medical history or family history. Physical examination revealed erythematous patches with some scaling over the trunk, arms and legs. There are palpable lymph nodes in the neck and inguinal regions. Biopsy of the skin lesion confirmed the diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Baseline blood workup, chest x-ray and CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis were negative for any other organ involvement. He has not received any treatment for his disease. He is married, has two children and works as an engineer.

10-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of pneumonia caused by a bacterial infection. She has been hospitalized for the past 3 days and has been receiving IV antibiotics. She has a history of asthma and has been taking daily inhaled corticosteroids for the past year. She has no known allergies to macrolide antibiotics. Her serum creatinine level is within normal limits. Her parents have given written consent for her to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics of solithromycin.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with AML three months ago. She underwent AML cell harvest and cryopreservation and has had a minimum of 5x107 cells cryopreserved. She has a haplo-identical donor and underwent allogeneic transplantation 35 days ago. She is currently in complete remission and has no evidence of ongoing grade 2 or higher acute GVHD. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Her total bilirubin, AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT), and creatinine levels are normal. Her absolute neutrophil count is 1500 and her platelet count is 80,000. She has normal organ and marrow function. She is not pregnant and has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study. She understands and has given her written informed consent to participate in the study. She has not received any other non-FDA approved study agents at the start of vaccination, and does not have any uncontrolled intercurrent illness or autoimmune or inflammatory disorders requiring active treatment with systemic steroids or immunosuppressive therapy.

The patient is a 55 year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer. The cancer has spread to his liver and lungs, and is not amenable to potentially curative treatment. He has no significant medical history and his performance status is either 0 or 1. He has not received any prior chemotherapeutic regimen for metastatic disease. His disease-free interval from end of adjuvant therapy is at least 6 months. He has no peripheral neuropathy greater than Grade 1, and is not receiving any concomitant treatments with drugs/ingredients reported to have a potential activity in preventing peripheral sensory neuropathy. He has no concurrent active cancer originating from a primary site other than colon or rectum, and has no symptoms suggesting brain metastasis. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed written informed consent prior to study entry.

32-year-old woman with a singleton pregnancy, currently in labor and admitted to the maternity department of the Inselspital Berne. She has a gestational age of 38 weeks and 2 days. She has a history of a previous uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has received regular prenatal care throughout this pregnancy. The patient has consented to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient does not have a documented refusal or any other exclusion criteria. The CTG-registrations of the patient will be used for the analysis of the AI-CDS system to determine the best fetal extraction moment during labor.

A 42-year-old woman has been dealing with varicose veins for the past few years. She has noticed that her legs have become increasingly swollen and painful, especially when standing for extended periods of time. She is physically active and exercises regularly. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she does not take any medications. She is scheduled to undergo endovascular laser treatment (EVLT) for her varicose veins in the coming weeks. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help identify patients at high risk of postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) who will benefit from prophylactic anticoagulation. She is willing to follow up for 4 weeks after the procedure and undergo examinations to check for VTE.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with a pituitary adenoma. She is scheduled to undergo an elective transsphenoidal resection surgery. During the surgery, she is expected to have an intraoperative high flow CSF leak. She has a BMI of 28, which puts her at an elevated risk of postoperative CSF leak. She has no known allergies to medications and is not currently taking any medications. She has no significant past medical history other than the pituitary adenoma. The patient has agreed to participate in the trial and is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception during the study treatment and for at least one month after stopping the treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with distal ulcerative colitis. She has been experiencing symptoms such as bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and urgency to defecate. Her Mayo Clinical Score is greater than 7, indicating moderate to severe disease activity. She has not been treated with systemic steroids or azathioprine in the past 3 months. She has no known liver or kidney disease and no history of severe heart failure. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written consent.

The patient is a 16-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Bipolar I Disorder. He has manic episodes with a YMRS score of 25. His past medical history is significant for anxiety and depression for which he has been taking sertraline for the past 6 months. He is currently not taking any other medications. His weight is 70 kg and he has no history of anorexia nervosa or any other serious medical or neurological conditions. The patient's parents are fully capable of monitoring his disease process and compliance to treatment. The patient has read and understands the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

An 82 year old woman has been experiencing unintentional weight loss and loss of appetite for the past few months. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis, and she takes medications for these conditions. Her Barthel's scale score is 70, and her MMSE score is 28. She has not received any previous enteral nutrition and does not use laxatives. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve her nutritional status.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a history of familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) confirmed by genetic testing. She has a family history of elevated cholesterol and early heart disease, and her untreated LDL-C levels were found to be above 190 mg/dL. She has been on statins for the past 6 months but is still experiencing elevated LDL-C levels, with a recent LDL-C level of 3.2 mmol/L (125 mg/dL). She has no history of heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia or severe hypertension. Her fasting triglyceride levels are within normal range. She has no active liver disease or other medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use at least two methods of highly effective contraception during the study period. She has not received any investigational products or devices within the past 30 days or monoclonal antibodies directed towards PCSK9 within the past 90 days. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effect of inclisiran treatment on her LDL-C levels.

The patient is a 45 year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer. She has a 3 cm mass in her right breast and multiple enlarged lymph nodes in her right axilla. She underwent a needle core biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of infiltrating ductal carcinoma. She has no history of breast cancer or any other malignancy. She has a past medical history of hypertension and is currently on lisinopril 10 mg daily. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is pre-menopausal and has two children. She has no family history of breast cancer. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study period and for three months after completion of the treatment. She had a negative bone scan and CAT scan of chest and abdomen for metastatic disease.

55 year old male who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after undergoing a biopsy. The tumor is in the left lung and has been staged as T3N2M0. The patient has completed chemotherapy and external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) to radiation doses of 60Gy to the primary tumor and 50Gy to mediastinal structures. The patient's Zubrod performance status is 1. The patient is deemed medically inoperable due to underlying physiological medical problems, including severe pulmonary hypertension and a history of diabetes mellitus with end organ damage. The patient has undergone pre-treatment evaluations, including spirometry, lung volumes, diffusion capacity, and arterial blood gases. The patient's labs are within normal limits, including WBC count, platelets, total bilirubin, serum creatinine, AST and ALT, and serum albumin. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has agreed to use effective contraceptive methods during the trial. The patient's primary tumor is technically resectable after chemoradiation by an experienced thoracic cancer clinician, with a reasonable possibility of obtaining a gross total resection with negative margins. The patient has not received any other concomitant antineoplastic therapy and has no evidence of regional or distant metastases after appropriate staging studies. The patient is willing to sign a study-specific consent form and is able to comply with the protocol therapy and follow-up.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 4 years ago. She has been taking disease-modifying drugs as prescribed by her neurologist but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. The patient reported experiencing frequent episodes of weakness, numbness, and tingling in her arms and legs, as well as difficulty walking and maintaining balance. Upon consultation with her neurologist, it was decided that a switch to Betaferon was necessary. The patient has been on Betaferon for 2 months and has been using the auto-injector device provided by the BetaPlus support program. The patient has reported some difficulties in adapting to the new medication and device, but the nurse support has been helpful in providing education and guidance on the proper use of the device. The patient has agreed to participate in the observational survey and is willing to fill out the FAMS questionnaire, WCQ, and CES-D questionnaire to assess her quality of life, coping processes, and depression. The patient is motivated to improve her adherence to the Betaferon therapy and is optimistic about the potential benefits it may bring to her quality of life.

This is a 52 year-old Japanese male with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for the past 7 years. He has been managing his diabetes with diet and exercise and has been on sitagliptin monotherapy for the past 6 months. Despite his efforts, his most recent hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) reading was 8.5%. He has not taken any additional oral hypoglycemic agents (AHA) in the past 8 weeks. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the addition of metformin to his current treatment regimen, as he hopes to improve his glycemic control and avoid the need for insulin therapy. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study, with an HbA1c level between 6.0% and 9.0% and a diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, who presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He is admitted to the cardiac care unit for further evaluation and management. After initial assessment, it is determined that he will need to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 0.6, and is enrolled in the study. He will have a central venous catheter and a transpulmonary thermodilution catheter inserted for hemodynamic monitoring, as well as an esophageal doppler probe for calibration of the pulse contour algorithms. The patient will undergo a passive leg raising maneuver and CO measurements will be taken before, during, and after the maneuver. CO measurements will also be taken every 10 minutes until the start of CPB, and then again 15 minutes after weaning from CPB. The patient will be closely monitored throughout the study to ensure his safety and well-being.

A 50-year-old man presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and nausea. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. His blood pressure was 160/90 mmHg, and his blood glucose was high at 300 mg/dL. He was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis and started on intravenous fluids per standard of care, receiving a minimum of 1000 ml. He met the inclusion criteria for the study and agreed to participate.

75 yo F with a clinical diagnosis of probable Alzheimer's disease, living at home with her daughter as caregiver. She has a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 20 at screening. She is fluent in English and signed the informed consent form. She has been on a stable dose of rivastigmine for 3 months and has been continuously dosing for at least 3 months. She is a non-smoker and has a ratio of total tau/Abeta42 in cerebrospinal fluid >= 0.30. Her caregiver will be responsible for administering the drug and recording the time. The patient has no history of ischemic colitis or ischemic enterocolitis, nor any history of myocardial infarction or unstable angina. She has no clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia or cardiomyopathy. She has no symptomatic hypotension or uncontrolled hypertension. She does not have a clinically significant abnormality on screening electrocardiogram. Her medical condition is stable and acceptable for participation in the study. She is not exposed to any experimental drug, experimental biologic or experimental medical device within the longer of 5 half-lives or 3 months before screening. She does not reside in a skilled nursing facility. She has no clinically significant laboratory test results. She has no clinically significant untreated hypothyroidism, nor does she have insufficiently controlled diabetes mellitus. She has no renal insufficiency, and no history of malignant tumor within 3 years before screening. There is no history of brain tumor or other clinically significant space-occupying lesion on CT or MRI. She has no history of head trauma with clinically significant loss of consciousness within 12 months before screening. She has no history of stroke within 18 months before screening, and no history of a stroke concomitant with onset of dementia. She has no specific degenerative CNS disease diagnosis other than Alzheimer's disease. She is not on donepezil 23 mg or greater quaque die currently or within 3 months prior to enrollment in the study. She has not discontinued AChEI < 30 days prior to enrollment in the study. She is not taking antipsychotics, tricyclic antidepressants and monoamine oxidase inhibitors, anxiolytics or sedative-hypnotics, peripherally acting drugs with effects on cholinergic transmission, immunosuppressants, antiepileptic medications, chronic intake of opioid-containing analgesics, sedating H1 antihistamines, nicotine therapy, varenicline or similar therapeutic agent within 30 days before screening. She has no clinically significant illness within 30 days of enrollment. She has no history of significant neurological, hepatic, renal, endocrine, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, or metabolic disease. She has negative serum hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and negative hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody test at screening, as well as negative HIV test at screening. She has not lost a significant volume of blood (> 450 mL) within 4 weeks prior to the study. She is not taking metformin or cimetidine.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of heart failure and a documented ejection fraction (EF) ≤ 35%. He has experienced firing of an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) within 6 months prior to enrollment and has been diagnosed with NYHA Class II-III heart failure. He has a body weight of 200 pounds and is able to lie flat for at least 2-hour intervals. He has undergone a SPECT or an approved PET perfusion imaging study performed within 90 days prior to, but no less than 3 days prior to enrollment. He does not have a history of diabetes, coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, heart arrhythmia (except sinus arrhythmia), cardiomyopathy (e.g. restrictive, infiltrative or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), constrictive pericarditis, myocarditis, complex congenital disease, surgically correctable valvular disease, and/or inoperable, obstructive valvular disease, pacemaker, syncope, transient ischemic attack (TIA) or cerebrovascular accident (CVA), Parkinson's disease, degenerative cerebral disease, or organ transplantation. He is not currently participating in another clinical trial of an investigational product and does not have any clinically significant laboratory abnormalities. He has not received any radiopharmaceutical within a period equal to 10 half-lives of the isotope prior to enrollment or receipt of any radiopharmaceutical containing iodine within a period of 3 months prior to enrollment. Additionally, he has not received any medications within 30 days prior to enrollment that have confounding effects to the autonomic nervous system. He does not have any metal that cannot be removed from the body located in the thorax and is not receiving Class I or III antiarrhythmic drug therapy, except for amiodarone.

There is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial as it focuses on the evaluation of the operability and usability of the SL-D301 Slit Lamp and the DC-4 digital camera attachment by an eye care professional on willing subjects. The trial does not involve any medical treatment or intervention on the subjects, but rather the evaluation of the instruments used for routine eye examinations and image capture. Thus, any willing subject can participate in this trial, and there are no specific eligibility criteria or requirements for the subjects.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who is scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to gallstones. She has a history of mild hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is not allergic to any medications, including dexketoprofen. She is 75 kg and is classified as ASA 2. She has never undergone general anesthesia before and is concerned about potential pain during the procedure.

A 31-year-old accountant who is currently pregnant with her second child has been diagnosed with gestational diabetes. She has no previous history of diabetes or any other chronic illness. She is married and lives with her husband and their 3-year-old daughter. She is currently on a healthy diet and has been advised to exercise regularly. However, despite these efforts, she requires insulin therapy to manage her glucose levels. She is concerned about the potential risks of high glucose levels to her pregnancy and the baby's health. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of continuous glucose monitoring in improving her glycemic control and reducing the risk of hypoglycemia. She is eager to learn more about the study and how she can contribute to advancing medical research.

A 55 year old woman was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago and has been managing it with a modified diet and metformin. Her BMI is 30 and she has not been exercising regularly for the past 6 months. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or stroke, liver, lung or GI diseases. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol often. She has not undergone any weight loss program or obesity surgery in the past year. Her HbA1c level is 65 and she is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her metabolic control and reduce her fat mass. She is willing to follow a modified paleolithic diet and exercise under observation for 3 sessions per week.

A 56-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents with mild to moderate renal insufficiency. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 50 ml/min/1.73m2. He requires an enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for the evaluation of a suspected pancreatic tumor. He has never received any gadolinium-based contrast agents before and has no known allergies to medications. He is currently taking lisinopril and metformin for his medical conditions. He is able and willing to comply with the necessary study requirements and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have any major mental illnesses or other conditions that would affect observation.

Patient is a 58-year-old man from Germany who has been diagnosed with chronic heart failure for the past 2 years. He has been treated with optimal pharmacological therapy including resynchronization therapy for the past 6 months but has been experiencing persistent symptoms of dyspnea and exercise intolerance. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of renal artery intervention or any other significant medical conditions. His ejection fraction is 30% and his glomerular filtration rate is 45 mL/min/1.73m2. His blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of renal denervation in chronic heart failure patients with resynchronization therapy.

The patient is a 65 year-old retired teacher who is living independently. She has no history of cognitive impairments or neurological disorders. She is in good physical health and takes medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. She is active in her community and enjoys participating in social events with her friends and family. She has noticed that her memory for recent social events is not as good as it used to be and is interested in participating in a study that may help improve her memory. She is willing to commit to the seven day training period and is open to trying new memory strategies. She is able to travel to the University of Manitoba for the pre- and post-training sessions.

The patient is a 68-year-old Caucasian woman who recently underwent a sleep study and was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea. She has no prior history of sleep apnea or treatments for it. The patient is able to read English-language newspaper text with the help of contact lenses and glasses. She is scheduled for a sleep clinic appointment with a UCLA sleep provider and is able to attend a sleep educational session prior to the appointment. The patient has no history of dementia or mild cognitive impairment, and her Mini-Cog score is 4. She has no severe physical or mental illness, and has not been hospitalized or had substance abuse issues within the past 90 days. The patient is interested in learning more about her treatment options for obstructive sleep apnea and is willing to participate in the study.

A 67-year-old Caucasian male presents with complaints of memory impairment, particularly with name recall and retaining new information. He has a history of hypertension and takes medications for the same. He reports no history of major psychiatric or neurological disorders, and denies any history of head trauma with loss of consciousness. He is a non-smoker and denies any history of substance abuse. His cognitive function score is consistent with amnestic mild cognitive impairment based on pre-screening evaluation. His Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 28 at the time of initial consent. He is interested in participating in the study to determine if exercise can improve his memory abilities and brain health.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing heartburn at least twice a week during the nighttime period over the past month. He has been taking heartburn medication, which provides some relief, but he still experiences heartburn frequently at night. He is willing to discontinue the use of heartburn treatment for 7 days prior to inclusion in the study. He does not have a history of erosive esophagitis or gastroesophageal reflux disease diagnosed by a physician and confirmed by testing (endoscopy). The patient is willing to take only the study medication and the antacid provided as a rescue medication for relief of acute heartburn during the study.

A 58-year-old male was recently diagnosed with stage III colon cancer and was admitted to the oncology ward for further management. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are currently being managed with medications. He underwent surgery to remove the cancerous tumor and is now receiving chemotherapy. He is currently experiencing some side effects of the chemotherapy, including nausea and vomiting, but is otherwise stable. He is being closely monitored by the healthcare team to ensure that he is responding well to treatment. The hospital has implemented strict screening and isolation measures to prevent the spread of VRE, which the patient is aware of and is willing to comply with. He is looking forward to completing his treatment and recovering fully.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) for 5 years. He has been taking pre-mixed insulin (12 U/day) for the past 10 weeks alone and has not achieved optimal glycemic control, with his most recent HbA1C level being 8.5%. He has been on a stable dose of metformin (1500 mg/day) for the past 6 months. He has no history of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor or glucagon-like peptide-1 mimetic or analogue use. He has no history of pre-prandial short-acting or rapid-acting insulin use. He has experienced a few episodes of hypoglycemia in the past, but they were mild and did not result in seizure, coma, or loss of consciousness. He has no known contraindication to sitagliptin, insulin, or metformin. He has no history of liver disease, coronary heart disease, congestive heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, hyperthyroidism, malignancy, hematological disorder, or drug abuse. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is not planning to conceive or donate eggs during the study. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for the study duration.

The patient is a 50 year old female who was diagnosed with bronchiectasis by CT scan. She has a moderate to severe disease with FEV1 less than 60% predicted. She is currently in a stable state and has not received oral or intravenous antibiotics in the last three weeks. She is not taking any medication such as bronchodilators, oxygen, long term prophylactic antibiotics or steroids in the last three weeks. She is a non-smoker and over 40 years of age. She is available for a repeat measure 10-14 days later. She lives within 50 miles of the hospital. There are no other co-morbid conditions that could influence muscle strength. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who is in good health and has not had a menstrual cycle for over 5 years presents for this study. She weighs within 20% of the Metropolitan Life weight table and her plasma CTx-1 levels are greater than or equal to 0.25 ng/ml. She has no history of parathyroid, thyroid, pituitary or adrenal diseases, and has never had musculoskeletal disease. She has no history of gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD) or other significant gastrointestinal disorders. She has not had cancer within the past 5 years and has never had regular use of a Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drug (NSAID). She has not had surgery within the past 60 days and has no known allergies to the active ingredients or the excipients in the study medications. She is not currently taking any concomitant medications other than acetaminophen, has not used bisphosphonates within the past 6 months or estrogen-like drugs within the past 2 months, and has not used calcitonin within the past month. She is willing and able to comply with all study requirements and is willing to sign written informed consent.

A 10-year-old boy was diagnosed with CDK13 intragenic pathogenic SNV by genetic testing. He was referred to a pediatric neurologist due to developmental delay and intellectual disability. The patient has difficulties with language and communication skills, as well as with fine and gross motor skills. He is able to walk independently but has a slightly awkward gait. The patient has also been diagnosed with a mild form of scoliosis. He is a fourth-grader and receives special education services at school. His parents report that he struggles with following multi-step instructions and has difficulty with problem-solving tasks. He is a friendly and sociable child who enjoys playing with his siblings and friends. The patient has undergone MRI scans of his brain, which showed some mild abnormalities, but his family is willing to share the data with the researchers. The family has also agreed to provide a blood sample for DNA analysis.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with stage 3 chronic kidney disease. He has a history of hypertension for which he takes lisinopril and amlodipine. His blood pressure is well controlled with these medications, and his last recorded blood pressure was 138/82 mmHg. He does not have any significant comorbidities, and he does not have a history of alcoholism or terminal illness. The patient is interested in participating in this study to better understand his condition and to contribute to medical research. He is able to understand and provide informed consent for the study. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements, including attending all study visits and adhering to any additional monitoring or study procedures.

The patient is a 60-year-old postmenopausal woman with a BMI of 24. She enjoys a glass of wine with dinner a few times a week but does not exceed the weekly alcohol use of 14 drinks. She has no history of alcohol abuse or major health problems such as ulcers, heart diseases, diabetes, or cancer. She has not had a hysterectomy and is not currently taking HRT. She does not take any prescription medication that could interfere with the study. She is a non-smoker and is not allergic to alcohol or ibuprofen. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of PPARγ2 polymorphism and NSAIDs on acute alcohol-induced changes in serum estrogens among post-menopausal women.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 5 years ago. She has been treated with methotrexate for the past 2 years but has experienced an inadequate response. She was switched to an anti-TNF agent, but after 6 months of treatment, her symptoms have not improved. She presents to the clinic with persistent joint pain, swelling, and stiffness, which are affecting her daily activities. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her family history is negative for rheumatoid arthritis or any other autoimmune disorders. Her lab study shows a high level of C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) indicating active inflammation. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive MabThera as a treatment option.

A 32-year-old female with a history of ulcerative colitis for the past 5 years, presented with moderate to severe active symptoms such as bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain and cramping, and urgency to defecate. The patient underwent colonoscopy which confirmed the diagnosis of active ulcerative colitis. The patient has been receiving mesalamine and sulfasalazine for more than 4 weeks, but her symptoms have not improved. The patient has not received any corticosteroids or immunosuppressive agents. The patient is willing to participate in the required follow-up visits and able to complete the diary. The patient has adequate peripheral venous access to allow for completion of the apheresis treatments. The patient is not pregnant, lactating or planning to become pregnant during the course of the clinical investigation. The patient has not used any investigational drug, biologic or device within the last 30 days. The patient has not previously received Adacolumn® treatments. The patient has no history of dysplasia or carcinoma of the colon.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing painful menstrual periods for at least four of the previous six menstrual cycles. She has a history of primary dysmenorrhea, which began within four years of menarche. She has regular menstrual cycles, and she has been using the same strength and type of hormonal contraception for at least the previous six months. She is a tampon user and is willing to use tampons throughout the study dosing period. She has a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m2, and she is able to understand and willing to complete the efficacy evaluations. She can speak and understand English and is capable of giving written informed consent for the study. She does not have any pelvic pain other than that thought to be associated with primary dysmenorrhea, such as chronic pelvic pain occurring at times other than exclusively during menses and/or dyspareunia. She has not experienced dysmenorrhea symptoms that are effects of or thought to be effects of (at least in part) secondary causes of dysmenorrhea, such as uterine fibroids, endometriosis, and/or currently symptomatic ovarian cysts. She has had dysmenorrhea that required, in her opinion, the use of analgesic medication during four of the previous six menstrual episodes. She is not currently using contraceptive injection, implant, or extended cycle OC (hormonal contraceptive cycles consisting of 28 days or more of active hormones). She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she has not participated in a clinical trial in the 30 days from the time of last dosing in the prior study to the time of providing consent for this study. She has no history of allergic hypersensitivity or significant intolerance related to treatment with any medications used in this study. She has no history of past or ongoing clinically significant disease, illness, or disorder that makes her unsuitable for study participation, including active vaginal, vulvar, and cervical lesions. She has no laboratory abnormalities that could contraindicate study participation, and she has no history of, within the past 4 years, or ongoing significant psychiatric illness that makes her unsuitable for study participation. She has no history of chronic analgesic or tranquilizer use or drug abuse including alcohol within the 6 months before providing consent for this study. She is not regularly using any concomitant medications that might confound efficacy and/or safety assessments, in the opinion of the Investigator. Finally, she is willing to use only those medications that are allowed in the study for the treatment of her dysmenorrhea, i.e., study drug and rescue medication.

45-year-old male with a history of idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) for over 6 months, with no apparent other causes for eosinophilia and signs and symptoms of organ involvement. The patient has no expression of any of imatinib targets (c-Kit receptor, PDGFR, bcr-abl receptor) on bone marrow cells. The patient has undergone previous chemotherapy with no recovery from the acute toxic effects. The patient has not received any investigational agent within the past 4 weeks and has not undergone any major surgeries within the past 4 weeks. The patient has adequate hepatic and renal function with a serum bilirubin and creatinine level within normal limits. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 38-year-old Caucasian man has been experiencing symptoms of acid reflux, including heartburn, regurgitation, and bloating for the past two weeks. His symptoms have been interfering with his daily activities and sleep. He has tried over-the-counter antacids but has not found relief. He is generally healthy, with no significant past medical history or medication use. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a family history of acid reflux disease. He has not experienced any alarm symptoms such as difficulty swallowing, unintentional weight loss, vomiting, or gastrointestinal bleeding. He is not pregnant and has no contraindications to Nexium. He has not taken Nexium or any other proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) in the past month.

A 55-year-old man visits the clinic with a history of sun damage due to his outdoor job. He noticed some rough, scaly patches on his forehead, cheeks, and nose. A dermatologist diagnosed them as actinic keratoses. He is otherwise healthy, doesn't smoke, and has no significant medical history. He has no allergies to any medication. He is married and has two children who are in their twenties. He works as a construction worker and spends most of his time outdoors. He wears a hat and applies sunscreen when he remembers. His skin is Fitzpatrick type III. He is interested in participating in the study to determine the most effective treatment for his skin condition.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer after experiencing urinary symptoms and undergoing a prostate biopsy. He has no history of prior chemotherapy for prostate cancer. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the safety, tolerability and efficacy of AZD5363 for prostate cancer.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of prostate adenocarcinoma. He has undergone definitive external beam radiotherapy and has a PSA level within the last 3 months. The patient is able to have gold fiducial markers placed in the prostate for the study if approved by a Cardiologist due to being on anticoagulants. The patient has no history of lymph node irradiation and does not have artificial hips. The patient's dimensions are less than 40cms and he has an ECOG score of 1. The patient is willing to understand and sign the informed consent form.

28-year-old male who sustained a crush injury to his right leg in a work-related accident. The injury resulted in a 6 cm x 8 cm abrasion on the anterior aspect of his lower leg, with surrounding erythema and edema. The patient was immediately taken to the emergency department and received wound care with sterile saline irrigation and debridement. The patient has no known allergies and is able to read and understand the informed consent form in German.
