He has provided voluntary consent to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for over a year. She has been taking methotrexate for the past 3 months with no significant improvement in her joint pain and swelling. She has a positive test for both RF and anti-CCP antibodies. She experiences pain in at least 6 out of 68 tender joints and at least 6 out of 66 swollen joints. Her DAS28-ESR score is greater than 3.2. She has not had any major infections recently and is not currently pregnant or nursing. She has a history of mild elevated liver enzymes but has been cleared by her doctor to continue taking methotrexate. She is willing to use effective contraception during the study.

A 32-year-old woman presents with chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. She reports these symptoms have been ongoing for the past 6 months and have not improved with over-the-counter medications. She has a family history of Crohn's disease. Physical examination reveals mild tenderness in the lower abdomen without other significant findings. Laboratory tests show elevated inflammatory markers and fecal calprotectin levels. The gastroenterologist recommends undergoing a colonoscopy to investigate further. The patient agrees to participate in a research study to examine the role of intestinal microbiota in chronic inflammatory bowel diseases.

A 28-year-old healthy male with no pre-existing medical conditions and no history of allergies to medication. He has no known kidney, heart, or liver disease and does not have eczema or psoriasis on the injection site. He is not currently taking any regular painkillers and does not suffer from neuropathy. He is not pregnant and does not have diabetes. He is interested in participating in this study to help improve pain management for future patients.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic abdominal pain and intermittent diarrhea for the past 6 months. He has also noticed a 10-pound weight loss during this time period. He has no history of gastrointestinal disease but has a family history of Crohn's disease. The patient is able to understand and comply with protocol requirements and signs the informed consent form. He is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who recently sustained a traumatic injury to his cervical spine resulting in paralysis from the neck down. He is currently dependent on mechanical ventilation to breathe and has been classified as an A-C on the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) Impairment Scale. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery to have diaphragm pacing electrodes implanted to help promote ventilator weaning. He has no history of progressive neuromuscular diseases, neurologic injuries, or chest wall injuries that would impact his breathing. The patient is able to understand and consent to participate in the study, and has no cognitive impairments that would limit his ability to participate.

A 4-year-old boy was recently diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder. He has difficulty in social communication and interaction, as well as repetitive behaviors and restricted interests. He is non-verbal and has difficulty in following instructions. He is receiving early intervention services from a speech therapist and a behavior analyst. He enjoys playing with puzzles and blocks and has a keen interest in trains and airplanes. His parents are looking for additional resources to help their child overcome communication and language difficulties. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial for a computerized language training program for children with ASD. The child has no other medical conditions or allergies.

A 62-year-old Caucasian male presents with chronic knee pain for the past 6 months. He describes the pain as dull and achy, with occasional sharp pain during activities such as walking and climbing stairs. He has tried over-the-counter pain relievers and topical creams, but they only provide temporary relief. He has no previous history of knee injury or surgery. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works at a desk job. He has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of inflammatory joint disease or other medical conditions affecting the knee. He is willing to maintain a stable analgesic regimen throughout the study period. He has no known allergies to medications. He speaks and understands English fluently. Knee X-rays show evidence of Kellgren and Lawrence Score two with definite osteophytes and definite joint space narrowing consistent with mild to moderate knee osteoarthritis. His white blood cell count is 6.8, hemoglobin is 13.5, and platelets are 220. His glomerular filtration rate is 85, and liver enzymes are within normal limits.

58-year-old female patient who underwent the All-on-4 concept implant-supported fixed prostheses rehabilitation due to severe periodontitis resulting in tooth loss. The patient has been wearing removable dentures for the past five years, but has experienced discomfort and difficulty in chewing. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy, and has adequate bone volume for implant placement. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the long-term outcome of implant-supported fixed prosthetic rehabilitations using peek material.

This is a 58 year-old male who has been diagnosed with heart failure with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35%. He has been hospitalized twice in the last year for heart failure exacerbations and was discharged 3 days ago. His NYHA functional class is III and he has been consistently NYHA class III or IV for the past 60 days. He is currently on optimal therapy with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta blockers. He has agreed to come to the clinic up to 2 times per week for 16 weeks of study drug infusions and to participate in all required follow-up assessments through week 24. He is willing to be contacted monthly after week 24 for follow-up, until the entire study has been completed. He is able to discontinue intermittent or continuous infusions of dopamine, dobutamine, milrinone, nitroglycerin, or open-label Natrecor beginning at the time of the screening visit. He has a systolic blood pressure consistently >90mm Hg. He has not received recent outpatient IV vasoactive (milrinone, dobutamine, dopamine, nitroglycerin, or open-label Natrecor) therapy as defined as >2 outpatient (excluding emergency room or inpatient) infusions in the last 30 days without a subsequent hospitalization. He has not had a biventricular pacemaker placed within the 45 days before randomization or a single or dual chamber pacemaker or an automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator placed within the 15 days before randomization. He does not have cardiogenic shock, volume depletion, or any other clinical condition at the time of randomization that would contraindicate the administration of Natrecor. He is not currently receiving chronic dialysis or have the expectation that dialysis will be required during the next 12 months.

The patient is a 26-year-old Caucasian male who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus 4 years ago. He has been on multiple daily injections of insulin glargine U100 for the past 3 years. He has a fasting C-peptide level of 0.20 nmol/L and a BMI of 25.2 kg/m². He has experienced difficulty in maintaining his blood sugar levels within the target range, despite regular exercise and a healthy diet. He has no known allergies to insulin analogs or pramlintide. He is not taking any medications that affect gastrointestinal motility. He has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgeries or has any symptoms suggestive of gastroparesis. His past medical history is unremarkable apart from type 1 diabetes. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is willing to participate in the trial and is able to comply with all the study requirements.

Patient A is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe health anxiety for the past 8 months. She frequently worries about having a serious illness, which interferes with her daily functioning and causes her to seek medical attention excessively. She has visited her primary care physician multiple times in the past few months, but all medical tests have come back normal. She has no previous history of mental health disorders and has never received any formal psychological treatment. She is a native Danish speaker and has access to a computer and internet at home. Her Whiteley-7 score is 30, indicating a high level of health anxiety. She is willing to participate in an internet-based treatment program and is not currently experiencing acute suicidal risk or substance abuse. She is not pregnant and is willing to provide informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

54-year-old female with a diagnosis of metastatic triple-negative breast cancer presents with increasing abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging studies reveal extensive hepatic involvement, with no evidence of brain or meningeal metastases. She has failed multiple lines of chemotherapy and has exhausted all standard therapies. The patient has an estimated life expectancy of at least 12 weeks and has a WHO performance status of 1. Her recent laboratory studies are within normal limits, and she has no history of significant gastrointestinal impairment or inadequate bone marrow reserve. The patient is willing to participate in a Phase I study to assess the effect of ketoconazole on the PK of multiple doses of cediranib, an experimental drug that may offer some benefit in the treatment of her advanced cancer.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms, including urinary urgency and frequency, for the past few months. He does not have a suprapubic catheter and has not undergone radical prostatectomy or cystoprostatectomy. He has no history of urethral stricture or prostatitis. A urine culture was negative for bacterial growth. The patient is willing to undergo cystoscopy for diagnostic purposes and is interested in participating in the study to compare the discomfort of flexible versus rigid cystoscopy.

A 40-year-old male veteran who was honorably discharged from the military three years ago. He has been struggling with alcohol dependence and has been diagnosed with PTSD. He drinks regularly and has not been abstinent for more than two weeks in the past year. He has a history of relapse and has been in and out of rehab programs. He has experienced traumatic events during his time in the military and has been experiencing nightmares, flashbacks, and anxiety as a result. He has been taking medication for his PTSD but has not seen much improvement. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates prazosin versus placebo for 12 weeks in a double-blind, controlled fashion, as he hopes it may help reduce his symptoms of PTSD and alcohol use. He is willing to participate in laboratory sessions to determine his reactivity to stress and is not currently taking medication for any other psychiatric condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic heart failure (CHF) and has a cardiac pacemaker. She experiences shortness of breath and fatigue during physical activities such as walking and climbing stairs. She has been taking medication to manage her CHF, but still struggles with exercise tolerance. Her echocardiogram showed a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF<50%). She does not have angina pectoris symptoms and has not had any changes in medical therapy in the last three months. She is willing and able to participate in a clinical trial to explore optimal programming for her pacemaker to improve her exercise tolerance and quality of life. She does not currently take calcium channel blockers.

The patient is a 5-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with high-risk neuroblastoma. He has not undergone any systemic therapy yet. The patient's diagnostic tests include a biopsy of a mass in his abdomen which confirmed the diagnosis of neuroblastoma. His current staged disease is stage M with MYCN amplification. He has no history of bone marrow failure syndromes. The patient's past medical history is significant only for a single episode of acute otitis media that was treated with antibiotics. The patient's labs show adequate renal and hepatic function. The patient has a normal ejection fraction and a shortening fraction of 30%. The patient's parents are aware of the risks of the study and have signed a written informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was found wandering in the streets, disoriented and agitated. He is not able to provide any information about himself or his medical history. Upon arrival of the paramedics, he becomes combative and violent, posing a danger to the staff. He is restrained for his safety and the safety of the staff. The paramedics suspect that he may have ingested some kind of drug, but they are not sure. He is transported to Mercy Fitzgerald Hospital for further evaluation and treatment.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) 2 months ago. She presents with fatigue, weakness, and occasional shortness of breath. She has a past medical history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. She has never received any prior therapy for MDS. Laboratory findings show a hemoglobin level of 9.8 g/dL, a platelet count of 75,000/mm³, and an absolute neutrophil count of 800/mm³. Her karyotyping performed within the past 8 weeks confirms the diagnosis of MDS. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has AST and ALT levels within the normal range and a creatinine level of 1.5 mg/dL. She has normal serum vitamin B12 and folate levels. Her ferritin level is 80 ng/mL and copper level is 60 µg/dL. She has not received any other concurrent treatment for MDS or hematopoietic growth factors.

A 56 year old woman presents with abdominal pain and jaundice for the past month. She has also experienced significant weight loss and loss of appetite. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she is currently taking medications. Diagnostic imaging reveals a mass in the head of the pancreas, and a biopsy confirms the presence of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The tumor is deemed borderline resectable per NCCN criteria. The patient is otherwise healthy, with an ECOG PS of 0, and she has no history of autoimmune disease or prior abdominal radiation therapy. She meets all other inclusion criteria for the study, including the ability to undergo a Whipple resection per surgeon assessment. She has no history of chemotherapy or invasive malignancies in the past 5 years. She is willing to employ adequate contraception if necessary and is able to provide written informed consent. She will be evaluated for pre-existing peripheral neuropathy and hearing deficits.

The patient is a 32-year-old Hispanic mother of two children, a 4-year-old boy and a 7-year-old girl. She is married and works part-time as a cashier. She reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to her husband's long work hours and her responsibilities at home. She has a history of depression and anxiety but is not currently taking any medications. Her children have no significant medical history and are up-to-date on their vaccinations. The family speaks both English and Spanish at home. The mother is presenting for a routine well visit for her children and is interested in learning more about parenting techniques to manage her stress and improve her relationship with her children. She reports experiencing verbal abuse from her own parents growing up and is concerned about her own parenting techniques. She is open to participating in the ACEs screening and intervention study.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. He has a history of injection drug use in his 20s, but has been clean for the past 10 years. He is currently on methadone maintenance therapy for opioid addiction. He has a family history of hepatitis B, with his mother and brother also having been diagnosed with the disease. His latest lab results show that he is HBeAg positive and his HBV DNA levels are greater than 10E5 IU/mL. His ALT levels are elevated at 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. He has not been diagnosed with liver cancer or liver failure, and he is not currently pregnant. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the effects of antiviral therapy on host immune function in patients with chronic HBV infection.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been hospitalized due to severe malnutrition. She has lost a significant amount of weight in the past few months and has been unable to consume solid food due to difficulty swallowing. She has a medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are currently managed with medications. She is alert and oriented, but complains of weakness and fatigue. Upon examination, the patient appears undernourished with visible loss of muscle mass and subcutaneous fat. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential benefits and risks. She has no known allergies to milk or lactose intolerance.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who had an unexplained ischemic stroke six months ago. She presents with no other identifiable cause of stroke and her Modified Rankin score is 2. She is currently taking no medications and has no significant medical history. She is 160 cm tall, weighs 60 kg, and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is a single mother of two children and works as a teacher. She is concerned about the risk of future strokes and is considering participating in a clinical trial to prevent stroke recurrence. Upon evaluation, she is found to have a PFO with a right-to-left shunt of more than 30 microbubbles. She is interested in the possibility of transcatheter closure of the PFO, but is open to other treatment options.

A 32-year-old female patient presents with a history of poor vision in her left eye since childhood. She was diagnosed with anisometropia, with a power difference of -4.5D between her left and right eye. Despite wearing corrective lenses, her left eye's visual acuity remains poor, with a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/200. The patient reports no history of eye muscle surgery or any other ocular pathology. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient reports occasional mild anxiety, but no history of depression or other mental health disorders. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the possibility of improving her amblyopia through complete light deprivation.

This is a 22 year old male of Japanese descent who is in good health with no history of any clinically important disease or disorder. He has a BMI between 18 and 30 kg/m2 and weighs between 50 and 100 kg. The subject was born in Japan to Japanese parents and has lived in Japan for the majority of his life. He has no history of drug abuse or excessive alcohol intake and is a non-smoker. He has not taken any prescribed or non-prescribed medication, including antacids, analgesics, herbal remedies, megadose vitamins, and minerals, during the 2 weeks prior to the first administration of investigational product. He has no history of plasma or blood donation within the past 1-3 months. The subject is able to communicate reliably with the study team and is willing to comply with study procedures, restrictions, and requirements. The subject does not have any medical dietary restrictions and is not a vulnerable subject.

The patient is a 30 year-old male who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection three years ago. He is currently on antiretroviral therapy which consists of two nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) and one non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI). His most recent HIV viral load was undetectable (<50 copies/ml) and his CD4 cell count was 450 cells/µl. He has no history of hepatitis or bleeding disorders. He has adequate vascular access for leukopheresis. He has never received zidovudine (AZT) and is not currently taking any drugs that interact with valproate or raltegravir (MK-0518). He is not pregnant, nursing or planning to conceive during the course of the study. He has a negative urine beta-HCG pregnancy test. He has no signs or symptoms of hepatic decompensation and his serum fasting glucose, creatinine, AST, ALT, and total bilirubin levels are all within normal limits. He is not currently using drugs or alcohol and has no history of substance abuse or dependence. He is willing to adhere to protocol therapy and can comply with time requirements for protocol-specified visits and evaluations. He is able and willing to give written informed consent for the study. He speaks English fluently.

A 60-year-old male presents with memory loss, difficulty in concentration and decision making, and difficulty in performing familiar tasks. He has a family history of Alzheimer's disease in his father. He is currently taking donepezil for the past 2 months. His medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he is taking losartan. His BMI is 30 kg/m2. He does not have any history of alcohol or drug abuse. His cognitive scores on the MMSE and RBANS DMI are 23 and 80, respectively. The Modified Hachinski Ischemia score is less than 4. He has a caregiver who is willing to ensure compliance with study medications, visits, and study procedures. He is able to understand and comply with the study procedures and has voluntarily agreed to participate in this study, and provided written informed consent prior to the start of any study-specific procedures. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 40 year old male who suffered a spinal cord injury 10 months ago resulting in incomplete thoraco-lumbar spinal cord injury. He is currently unable to walk independently and has been using a wheelchair for mobility. He has been diagnosed with AIS grade C according to the ASIA Impairment Scale. He has not responded to traditional physical therapy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of rTMS and body weight-support treadmill training to improve his sensory-motor function. He has no history of seizures or metallic implants in his head. He is not pregnant nor is he taking any neuroleptic medications.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has developed a wart on her foot that has been gradually increasing in size over the past few months. The wart is located on the plantar surface of her foot and is causing her pain when she walks. The lesion is approximately 8mm in diameter and has a rough, cauliflower-like appearance. The patient has no history of immunosuppression and is otherwise healthy. The patient and her family are interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a new, non-invasive treatment option for non-facial verruca vulgaris in pediatric patients. They are willing to adhere to the study's visit schedule and treatment requirements.

A 52-year-old woman was referred to a neurosurgeon for evaluation of persistent low back pain radiating to her right leg. She reported that the pain was interfering with her daily activities and affecting her sleep. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which she takes daily medications. She has never had any previous spine surgeries or neurological deficits. MRI showed a herniated disc at L5-S1 compressing the right S1 nerve root. The decision was made to proceed with a lumbar discectomy. She has been scheduled for elective surgery and preoperative evaluation showed that she is ASA II. She was advised about the study and consented to participate. She has no history of renal insufficiency and is within the age range of 18 to 65 years old. She was randomized to receive either neostigmine or sugammadex as the neuromuscular reversal agent after the procedure.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has recently undergone cardiac surgery and is now being treated at a postoperative cardiac rehabilitation center. During his initial Trans Thoracic cardiac Echography (TTE) evaluation, it was discovered that he has a pericardial effusion (PE) of severity >2, with a loculated effusion >10 millimeters. He has no history of cardiac transplantation and is not allergic to diclofenac. His medical history includes hypertension, and he is currently taking lisinopril 10mg daily. He has no history of gastro-intestinal ulcer or renal insufficiency. He has no known allergies to any medication. His creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL, and his hemoglobin level is 14.5 g/dL. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the written informed consent.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (PD) six months ago. She presents with bradykinesia and resting tremor that is asymmetric. She has not received any therapy, including levodopa, dopamine agonists, anticholinergics, amantadine, or selegiline to treat her symptoms. She is willing and able to give informed consent, and her age is over 30. She has not been exposed to CoQ10 or GPI 1485 within the last 90 days. She has not used minocycline or creatine within the last 90 days. She does not have any clinically significant medical condition or laboratory abnormality that would interfere with her ability to participate in the study or to be followed. She has no history of hypersensitivity or intolerability to CoQ10 or GPI 1485. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male and female participants who are not of childbearing potential, aged between 18 and 55 years old, with a body mass index (BMI) of 18.0 to 32.0 kg/m2. Participants must have normal renal function and no history of active tuberculosis, pulmonary, renal, or liver disease, or cardiac arrhythmias. They must not have smoked within the last 6 months or be current smokers, including electronic cigarettes or nicotine-containing products. Participants must also not have donated blood to a blood bank or in a clinical study (except screening or follow-up visit) within 4 weeks of study drug administration (within 2 weeks for plasma only). Women of childbearing potential or breastfeeding are excluded from this study. The study requires participants to stay at the clinical facility for the duration of the study.

A 57-year-old male patient with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is waiting for a kidney transplant. He has been on dialysis for the past 2 years and has no history of previous organ transplants. The patient has no donor-specific antibodies (DSA) and negative cross-match testing. He has received all up-to-date vaccinations as per local immunization schedules. The patient has no history of confirmed venous thromboembolism, arterial thrombosis, coagulopathy, or known platelet disorders, and does not require treatment with antithrombotic drugs. He has no contraindications to kidney biopsy. The patient is willing to follow protocol-defined contraceptive methods. The patient has not received any systemic immunosuppressive drug therapy for more than a total of 2 weeks within 24 weeks prior to informed consent form signature, nor undergone lymphodepleting therapy. He has no risk factors for venous thromboembolism or arterial thrombosis or prothrombotic status. The patient has no medical history of chronic hepatitis B infection, hepatitis C virus antibody, human immunodeficiency viruses antibody, or active tuberculosis (TB). He has no history of cancer except for cutaneous basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma treated with apparent success with curative therapy. The patient is eligible for the study, as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was found unresponsive by his wife at home and CPR was initiated by the emergency medical services (EMS) upon arrival. The patient was intubated and had IV access established. The initial rhythm was ventricular fibrillation and two shocks were delivered before ROSC was achieved. Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient remained intubated and sedated, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 3. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria for the CILICA-HS clinical trial.

42 yo F with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed 2 years ago. The patient underwent standard R-CHOP chemotherapy but relapsed 6 months later. She then received high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplant but again relapsed 4 months after the transplant. PET scan confirms multiple areas of active disease. The patient has undergone CD19 CAR-T therapy but had only a partial response. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1, and she has no other significant medical history. Her labs show good renal and liver function. The patient expresses CD20 on flow cytometry/immunohistochemistry. The patient has been referred to the clinical trial to receive CD19/CD20 dual-target CAR-T cell therapy. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to participate.

A 55 year old man presents with a small, painless, and discolored patch on his forehead that has been slowly growing over the past few months. Biopsy results confirm the presence of a thin and non-aggressive basal cell carcinoma. The patient has no history of skin cancer, is generally healthy, and is not taking any medications that could interfere with the trial. The patient is willing to abstain from extensive sunbathing and use of solarium during the observer blind part of the study. The patient has no history of porphyria and is not currently undergoing immunosuppression therapy. The patient provides written informed consent and is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception during the observer blind part of the study.

A 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 33.5 kg/m2 who is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the peripheral pharmacodynamics of Phentermine-Topiramate in obese patients. She has no significant medical history, takes no medications, and has never had any major psychiatric illness. She is not currently being treated for any cardiac, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, hematological, neurological, endocrine, or unstable psychiatric disease. She has a negative pregnancy test and is not on any appetite suppressants or orlistat. Her blood pressure is well controlled, and her fasting glucose and triglyceride levels are within normal limits. She does not have type 1 diabetes, nephrolithiasis, or a history of substance abuse or eating disorders. She is not taking any medication that could interfere with the study or cause drug interactions. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this study.

A 66-year-old male smoker with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and emphysema presented to the clinic with shortness of breath and wheezing. He has been experiencing worsening symptoms over the past 6 months and has been using his rescue inhaler more frequently. He has a history of heart disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He was diagnosed with COPD 10 years ago and was prescribed a long-acting bronchodilator and inhaled corticosteroid. His current medication regimen includes albuterol inhaler, salmeterol/fluticasone inhaler, and tiotropium inhaler. He reports difficulty walking up stairs and doing household chores due to shortness of breath. His oxygen saturation is 89% on room air. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to address his COPD symptoms and improve his quality of life.

A 30-year-old physically active male who regularly participates in weightlifting, running, and swimming is eligible for this clinical trial. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 22.5, which is within the normal range. He has been practicing these activities for the past 5 years, and has no history of overweight or obesity. He is interested in participating in this study to help researchers better understand how to estimate fat mass in physically active individuals.

A 45-year-old female with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections presented to the hospital with fever, chills, and abdominal pain. She was diagnosed with pyelonephritis and admitted for intravenous antibiotic treatment. During admission, she was screened and found to be a carrier of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli. She was offered enrollment in a clinical trial studying the impact of specific antibiotic therapies on the prevalence of human host resistant bacteria and agreed to participate. She will provide serial stool samples every 2-3 days during her hospitalization for analysis of the number of resistant organisms and resistant genes. She will also be monitored for clinical parameters, bowel movements, and presence of diarrhea. The target antibiotics for the study include commonly used agents in the hospital setting including quinolones, cephalosporins, piperacillin/tazobactam, ertapenem, imipenem, doripenem, metronidazole, clindamycin, and aminoglycosides. The effects of the antibiotic agents/classes on selection, enrichment, and spread of the target AMR organism will be examined. The patient will also be examined for the risk of developing infections as a function of various factors including time and load of carriage of resistant organisms and exposure to antibiotics.

A 40-year-old Caucasian woman presents with a small nodule on her thyroid gland, which was discovered incidentally during an ultrasound performed for an unrelated reason. The nodule was biopsied and confirmed to be papillary thyroid microcarcinoma. The patient has never had any thyroid problems in the past and has no family history of thyroid cancer. She has no symptoms related to the nodule and her thyroid function tests are within normal limits. She is otherwise healthy and active, with no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and enjoys hiking and yoga in her free time. Her ECOG performance status is 0.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy presented with progressive shortness of breath and fatigue. He had undergone coronary artery bypass grafting and received optimal medical therapy but continued to decline. He was evaluated by a heart failure specialist and found to have severe left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 20%. He was put on the waiting list for heart transplantation but due to the shortage of donor organs, he was implanted with a continuous-flow left ventricular assist device (CF-LVAD). He has been stabilized on CF-LVAD therapy for 6 months and has had no major complications. He has been compliant with his medications and follow-up visits. He reports some improvement in his symptoms but still experiences shortness of breath and fatigue with minimal exertion. He is willing to participate in the study to help advance the knowledge of biological markers associated with exercise capacity in CF-LVAD patients.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol use. He presents with clinical symptoms consistent with pancreatic cancer, which is confirmed by biopsy. Imaging studies reveal locally advanced, unresectable disease with regional nodal involvement. The patient has a baseline Karnofsky performance status of 80 and no significant comorbidities. Laboratory studies are within normal limits, including liver and renal function tests. The patient is sexually active and agrees to practice contraception during the study. He does not have a history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. The patient has no history of CNS disease or significant cardiovascular disease. He is not currently taking anticoagulants or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications.

72-year-old female with a history of hypertension, diabetes, and peripheral arterial disease who has been suffering from a chronic lower leg ulcer for the past 6 months. Despite regular wound dressing changes, the ulcer has not shown any significant signs of improvement and is covered with devitalized tissue for more than 50% of its surface. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of a new investigational product, ChloraSolv®, in debriding chronic wounds. The patient is able to read and understand the Patient Informed Consent and has provided meaningful written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient agrees to comply with the Protocol requirements and is willing to undergo weekly application of the investigational product for 6 weeks and follow-up for wound status evaluation after 12 weeks from baseline. The wound area is approximately 4 cm², meeting the eligibility criteria for the study. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and does not have any known allergies or hypersensitivity to the components of the investigational device.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who has been suffering from chronic pain in his right upper limb for the past 3 years. He was initially diagnosed with a rotator cuff injury, but despite treatment, the pain persisted and spread to his entire right arm. He has been diagnosed with Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) by a specialist after ruling out other causes of the pain. His pain is constant and rated as 8 out of 10 on the VAS scale. The patient has tried various medications, including opioids, but they have not provided significant relief. He has also undergone physical therapy, but the benefits have been limited. The patient is married and works as a software engineer. The pain has significantly impacted his daily routine and work productivity. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial as he is looking for an effective treatment that can provide long-lasting relief from the pain. He has no history of severe brain injury, epilepsy, or stroke. He is in good general health with no other significant medical conditions. His BMI is 25, and his blood pressure is within the normal range. He does not have any addictive behavior or severe psychiatric disorders. He is willing to be randomized into a treatment group and is committed to following the study protocol.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been suffering from chronic knee pain due to osteoarthritis for several years. He has tried various treatment options, including physical therapy, pain medications, and steroid injections, but none have provided long-term relief. He has been advised by his orthopedic surgeon to undergo a total knee arthroplasty procedure. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history apart from hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His weight is 75 kg, and his height is 170 cm, with a BMI of 25.95. He has no known allergies to medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his written consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman with severe osteoarthritis of the right knee. She has been experiencing chronic pain in the knee joint for the past 2 years, which has significantly impacted her ability to perform daily activities. She has tried nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and physical therapy with little relief. She does not have a history of narcotic dependence or any other medical conditions. Her surgeon recommends a total knee replacement surgery. The patient is interested in participating in the study and undergoes pharmacogenetic testing to determine the most effective pain medicine for her.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male volunteers aged between 21 and 50 years old with a BMI between 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m2. The patient should not have any clinically relevant concomitant disease, including gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders. They should not have a history of relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells or blackouts, epilepsy, psychiatric disorders or neurological disorders. The patient should not have participated in another trial with an investigational drug within two months prior to administration or during the trial. They should not be a smoker or unable to refrain from smoking on trial days and should not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient should also not have donated blood within four weeks prior to administration or during the trial or engaged in excessive physical activities within one week prior to administration or during the trial. Any laboratory value outside the reference range that is of clinical relevance will exclude the patient from participating in the trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He presented with fatigue, weight loss, and easy bruising for the past few months. His blood tests showed pancytopenia and a bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of AML with involvement of the 11q23 locus. He has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He works as an accountant and is married with no children. His physical exam was remarkable for pallor and mild hepatosplenomegaly. He has been started on chemotherapy and is being followed up at the South Lyon Hospital Center. A sample is available in the cytogenetic laboratory for this study.

A 35-year-old female patient with a clinical diagnosis of moderate to severe persistent facial erythema of rosacea came to the clinic for the study. She has been experiencing the symptoms for the past 6 months, including redness, bumps, and swelling on her face. She is married and has two children. She is currently not pregnant, and her menstrual cycle is regular. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 3 days a week. She is not on any medications. She has no history of any systemic or dermatological disorder except rosacea. She is willing to follow the instructions and complete the subject diary without assistance. She has not participated in any clinical trial or biologics study within the past 6 months. She is willing to use an acceptable form of birth control from the day of the first dose administration to 30 days after the last administration of Investigational Product (IP). She is willing to avoid the use of abrasive cleansers or washes, adhesive cleansing strips, and wax epilation on the face during the entire duration of her study participation. She is willing to minimize external factors that might trigger rosacea flare-ups such as spicy foods, thermally hot foods and drinks, hot environments, prolonged sun exposure, strong winds, and alcoholic beverages. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within 12 months prior to the Screening visit. She is not an employee or family member of the research center or Investigator.

A 45-year-old male with a history of recurrent kidney stones presents to the emergency department with severe left flank pain and nausea. The patient reports similar episodes in the past and has a previous diagnosis of ureteric stones. Physical examination reveals tenderness in the left flank region and positive CVA tenderness. Vital signs are within normal limits. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. CT scan is ordered to confirm the presence of ureteric stones.

Patient is a 40-year-old male who has been diagnosed with HIV and is receiving care at the Duke Infectious Diseases Clinic for the last 2 years. He is currently on antiretroviral therapy and has a 2013 American Heart Association 10-year ASCVD risk score of ≥ 15% with a diagnosis of hypertension. The patient is English literate and has the capacity to give legally effective consent. He has no prior diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome, stroke, peripheral vascular disease, and end-stage renal disease. The patient is willing to participate in a telephone-based CVD risk reduction curriculum delivered over 24 weeks, along with receiving a series of educational pamphlets on CVD risk reduction. The patient is interested in improving his cardiovascular health and is motivated to make necessary lifestyle changes to reduce his CVD risk.

A 54-year-old male patient with a history of smoking and drinking alcohol presented with a complaint of a lump in the throat and difficulty swallowing. He had noticed these symptoms for the last three months and had lost 8 kg of weight in the last 2 months. He denied any respiratory symptoms or pain. On examination, a 3x3 cm non-tender, firm, fixed mass was palpable in the right tonsillar area. The patient's performance status was ECOG 1. Biopsy from the mass confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. The patient has not received any prior therapy for head and neck cancer. His laboratory tests were within normal limits, including creatinine clearance, liver function tests, and blood counts. He was HIV negative and had no concurrent uncontrolled illness or active infection. He was a current smoker and had stopped alcohol consumption after the diagnosis. He was not using any other medications or experimental therapies. He was willing to use effective contraception during and for 6 months after the study treatment. He signed the informed consent for the clinical trial.

Maria is a 24-year-old Hispanic female who was diagnosed with keratoconus during a routine eye exam. She has been experiencing blurred vision, glare, and halos around lights for the past few months. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies. Maria wears soft contact lenses daily for correction of her myopia, but she is willing to discontinue wearing them for the study. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is 70 letters on the ETDRS chart. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning a pregnancy. Maria is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including follow-up visits and birth control measures. Her corneal curvature (Kmax) is 48.5 D, and her axial topography is consistent with mild keratoconus. She has not had any previous corneal crosslinking treatments or surgeries. Her corneal pachymetry is 420 microns at the thinnest point. Maria is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve her vision and potentially prevent further progression of her keratoconus.

A 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 29.5 visited the nutrition clinic to lose weight. She had no medical history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes or kidney diseases. She reported no allergies to fish or walnuts. She had no history of taking lowering blood glucose or lipid profile agents. She expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial that involves omega-3 supplementation to aid weight loss. Her economic status was stable and she could afford the cost of fish and walnuts. She was provided with an overview of the study and signed the consent form. She was randomized into one of the three groups and started a low-calorie diet to lose weight. She was advised to record her food intake and to avoid consuming plant sources of omega-3. Her dietary intake was controlled by a dietitian and she was followed for 12 weeks.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He was diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy and has been scheduled for vitrectomy surgery. The patient has been under glycemic control with insulin therapy and his HbA1c is currently 8.5%. His blood pressure is under control with antihypertensive medication, with a blood pressure reading of 130/80 mmHg. His lipid profile is within normal limits with LDL levels of 120mg/dL and triglycerides of 150mg/dL. The patient has not undergone any ocular or laser surgery in the past 6 months and has not received any intravitreal antiangiogenic agents in the last 2 months. He has no other ocular or systemic pathologies, and his vitreous hemorrhage is due to the complications of diabetic retinopathy. He has not taken any oral antioxidant supplements that exceed daily recommendations in the last 6 months and has not taken any immunomodulators, biological, or anti-inflammatory agents in the past 3 months. He is a non-smoker and has no history of neurodegenerative or carcinogenic processes. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given his signed informed consent.

A 62-year-old male presented with recurrent episodes of chest pain for the past few months. He was diagnosed with significant three-vessel coronary artery disease and was scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery at Maine Medical Center. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to medications. He is currently taking aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin, and metformin. He is physically active, performing regular exercise for 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week. The pre-operative evaluation is unremarkable except for the diagnosis of atrial fibrillation (AF) on electrocardiogram (ECG) during his preoperative workup. He has no history of AF or any other arrhythmias. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of chronic kidney disease and a creatinine clearance of 40 ml/min. She recently presented with acute proximal deep-vein thrombosis (DVT) and is planned to be treated for at least 3 months. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has a life expectancy of more than 3 months and has social security affiliation. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate reduced doses of direct oral anticoagulants (DOAs) compared to standard-of-care (SOC) anticoagulation for VTE treatment in patients with moderate or severe renal insufficiency. She has signed informed consent and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study. However, she does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including any contraindications for UFH, LMWH, VKA, or oral anticoagulants.

An 80-year-old woman named Margaret was recently discharged from the Medical Department at Sjælland University Hospital, Køge to her private home in Roskilde. She has a medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and rheumatic diseases. Margaret has been feeling weak and tired lately, and she has lost her appetite, causing her to lose weight. Her family has been concerned about her health and has been encouraging her to eat more. Margaret speaks Danish fluently and is able to give written consent. She is not receiving any tube feeding or intravenous nutrition. Margaret is not a nursing home resident and is not scheduled for any readmission. She is interested in participating in the individual nutritional intervention trial to improve her nutritional status and quality of life.

A 32-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident and was transported to the hospital via ambulance. Upon arrival, he was noted to have multiple injuries, including a severe laceration to his left leg and a suspected traumatic brain injury. His blood pressure was 70/40 mmHg and his heart

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a smoking history of 20 pack-years. He has been experiencing increasing shortness of breath and wheezing over the past few months, despite the use of his bronchodilator medication. Pulmonary function tests have shown significant airway obstruction. The patient is scheduled to undergo a bronchoscopy with possible intervention to relieve the obstruction. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent form for the Vibration Response Imaging (VRI) procedure. He has a body mass index of 25 and does not have any chest wall deformities or spine deformities. He does not have any skin lesions that would interfere with the sensor placement for the VRI procedure. The patient does not have a cardiac pacemaker or implantable defibrillator.

Pt is a 65yo M with a history of COPD diagnosed 5 years ago. He is a former smoker with a 30 pack-year history and quit smoking 2 years ago. He has been compliant with his maintenance inhalers and has had a few exacerbations in the last year requiring oral steroids and antibiotics. He denies any chest pain, palpitations or syncope. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medication. He is able to perform activities of daily living such as walking around the house and self-care, but has difficulty with exertional activities. He is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent.

42-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of stage IV HER2-positive breast cancer. The cancer has spread to her lungs and liver. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or HER2-targeted therapy for advanced or metastatic breast cancer, but did receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy for early stage breast cancer two years ago. The patient has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. She is currently experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain. Recent imaging shows progression of the disease with new lung nodules and liver metastases. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to travel to the study site. She is willing to undergo additional testing and procedures as necessary to participate in the trial.

55-year-old male with asymptomatic aortic stenosis (Doppler velocity ≥ 3.0 m/s) diagnosed during a routine physical examination. No previous history of valvular disease, coronary artery disease, or heart failure. Patient has no symptoms related to the aortic stenosis such as shortness of breath, chest pain, or fainting. The patient is able to exercise on a treadmill without difficulty and has a creatinine clearance of 75 mL/min. The patient has not undergone any previous aortic valve replacement surgery or planned valve surgery prior to enrollment. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 24. He is a non-smoker, and does not consume alcohol regularly. He has no significant medical history, and has not taken any medication, high dose vitamins, dietary supplements or herbal remedies within the past 14 days. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, or any psychiatric disorders. The patient has not participated in any clinical studies for a new chemical entity within the past 4 months or a marketed drug clinical study within the past 3 months. He has not donated blood within the past 3 months, and has not consumed more than 2 units of alcohol per day within 7 days prior to the first dose of IMP or had consumed any alcohol within the 48 hr period prior to the first dose of IMP. The patient is available to complete the study, and has provided written informed consent to participate.

This is a 42-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of fatigue, shortness of breath, and chest pain for several months. She was initially diagnosed with asthma and treated with inhaled corticosteroids, but her symptoms did not improve. Further investigation revealed a persistent blood eosinophil count of greater than 1500 cells and signs of organ system involvement, including skin rash, gastrointestinal discomfort, and elevated troponin levels indicating cardiac involvement. After ruling out parasitic or allergic causes of hypereosinophilia, she was diagnosed with Hypereosinophilic Syndrome (HES). She was started on systemic corticosteroids and other chemotherapeutic drugs, but experienced significant side effects and was not responsive to treatment. She is now being considered for a clinical trial evaluating the corticosteroid-sparing and clinical benefits of intravenous Mepolizumab in HES. She has achieved and maintained a stable prednisone dose, is not pregnant or nursing, and does not have any exclusion criteria, such as Churg-Strauss Syndrome or hematological malignancy.

Jessica is a 35-year-old woman who works as an administrative assistant. She has been diagnosed with hypertension and takes medication to control it. She has a high school diploma and reads at a 7th grade level. She sometimes struggles to understand medical information and has difficulty remembering instructions given to her by her healthcare provider. Jessica has never participated in a clinical trial before, but is interested in learning more about her medications and how to take them correctly. She speaks English fluently and has no hearing or visual impairments that would hinder her ability to participate in this study.

A 26 year old female with Maier-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome (MRKH) presents to the clinic with a strong desire to have a biological child. She has a mucosal neovagina of at least 7 cm and has been in a stable relationship for over a year. She is psychologically stable and compliant and has good renal function with both kidneys present. She has no major chronic illnesses and does not have any other risk factors or malignancies. Her BMI is within normal range. The patient has undergone IVF and has at least 8 frozen embryos which makes her eligible for uterus transplantation from a multi-organ donor. She lives in Belgium and has a good health insurance coverage. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the clinical trial.

A 58-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of sepsis and acute kidney injury. He had a fever, chills, and abdominal pain for the past few days. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, which are well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is able to take oral capsules and has no contraindications for probiotics by nasogastric tube.

Patient A is a 45-year-old female who recently received a diagnosis of uterine cancer. She has a histologically confirmed primary diagnosis of deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) or Polymerase ε mutation (POLE-EDM) uterine cancer, and is intended to be treated with a hysterectomy. She has measurable disease based on MRI and is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or a woman of childbearing potential. She has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent or with an agent directed to another stimulatory or co-inhibitory T-cell receptor. She also has not received prior systemic anti-cancer therapy including investigational agents within 4 weeks prior to allocation. She has not received prior radiotherapy within 2 weeks of start of study treatment, and has not received a live vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She is not currently participating in or has participated in a study of an investigational agent or has used an investigational device within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. She does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy (in dosing exceeding 10 mg daily of prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first dose of study drug. She also does not have a known additional malignancy that is progressing or has required active treatment within the past 3 years. She has no known active CNS metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis, and does not have severe hypersensitivity (≥Grade 3) to pembrolizumab and/or any of its excipients. She does not have active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years, and has no history of (non-infectious) pneumonitis that required steroids or has current pneumonitis. She does not have an active infection requiring systemic therapy, and does not have a known history of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) or Hepatitis B or C. Lastly, she has no history or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that might confound the results of the study, interfere with the subject's participation for the full duration of the study, or is not in the best interest of the subject to participate, in the opinion of the treating investigator.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a history of kidney stones. She has experienced recurrent kidney stones in the past 3 years and is motivated to find a solution to prevent future stones. Her most recent stone was composed of calcium oxalate. She has good renal function and no evidence of hyperparathyroidism or obstructive uropathy. Her urine analysis shows normal levels of calcium, uric acid, and citrate, but elevated levels of oxalate, consistent with hyperoxaluria. She has no significant dietary restrictions or deficiencies in calcium intake. She is not currently pregnant and has not experienced any recent significant cardiovascular events. She is interested in participating in the trial to determine if pyridoxamine can reduce her oxalate excretion and prevent future kidney stones.

The patient is a 63-year-old male who has tested positive for COVID-19. He has been experiencing symptoms such as fever, cough, and shortness of breath for the last 5 days. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes and takes medication for both conditions. He lives alone and has been self-quarantining at home since the onset of symptoms. His oxygen saturation level is 96% on room air. He has not received any medication or treatment for COVID-19 yet. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written consent.

A 56-year-old male veteran who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes has been referred to the Charleston VAMC for participation in a clinical trial aimed at studying racial/ethnic differences in trust in physicians and mistrust of the health care system among veterans with Type 2 Diabetes. The patient is a White American with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. The patient has no cognitive impairment and speaks English fluently. He has been receiving regular care for his diabetes at the VA hospital for the past three years. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient's medical history and diabetes-specific health outcomes will be obtained from the VA electronic medical records system. The patient will be asked to complete two valid and reliable survey instruments, the general trust in physician scale (GTIPS) and the Health Care System Distrust Scale. The patient will be followed up for 12 months to determine the predictive power of trust in physicians and mistrust of the health care system on personal health practices and health outcomes. The patient's eligibility for the study has been confirmed as he meets the inclusion criteria of being a White American veteran aged 18 years and older with Type 2 Diabetes and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who has been experiencing headaches and dizziness for the past few weeks. The patient had a minor fall a few weeks ago and since then, he has been experiencing these symptoms. The patient has no history of head injury or any other neurological problems. The patient is hypertensive and takes medications for high blood pressure. The physical examination showed that the patient was oriented to time, place, and person. The patient had no focal neurological deficits. The CT scan of the brain showed a chronic subdural hematoma that is causing compression of the underlying brain tissue. The patient was referred for surgical management. However, the patient is hesitant to undergo traditional surgery and is interested in a less invasive treatment option. The patient has no known allergies to medications or contrast agents. The patient's medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of middle meningeal artery (MMA) embolization compared to traditional surgical strategies for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH). The patient is fluent in English and has health insurance that covers the procedure.

A 25 year old female with a history of Hodgkin's Lymphoma, who is scheduled for a chemotherapy regimen with multiple days of treatment. She has a BMI of 24.5 and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no known allergies or conditions that could affect study conduct or laboratory assessments. She is willing to follow the restrictions and schedule of study procedures and understands the purposes and risks of the study. She is using an acceptable form of contraception and is not lactating.

A 65-year-old male with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) in his left eye, resulting in decreased visual acuity (20/80) and significant macular edema, complains of blurred vision and difficulty reading. His medical history includes hypertension, which is controlled with medication, and no history of liver or renal problems. He has no history of chronic hepatitis or liver failure. He has not had any cerebral vascular event or myocardial infarction in the past three months. He has no known allergies or hypersensitivities to minocycline or any drug in the tetracycline family. He is currently not taking any tetracycline medication. He has normal renal and liver function. He is willing to minimize exposure to sunlight or artificial UV rays and to wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen (minimum SPF 15) if he must be out in the sun. He agrees to notify the study investigator or coordinator if any of his doctors initiate a new medication during the course of this study. His best-corrected ETDRS visual acuity score in his left eye is between 78 and 34 letters (i.e., between 20/32 and 20/200). His left eye shows definite retinal thickening due to a CRVO based on clinical examination involving the center of the macula that is not refractory to further therapy as based on the investigator's clinical judgment. His left eye has retinal thickness in the central subfield on baseline OCT measurement > 350 microns, as measured by Zeiss Cirrus spectral domain OCT, or an equivalent retinal thickness on a similar OCT machine. He has no history of a recurrent RVO. He is able to cooperate during the procedure for accurate fundus photographs. He has no ocular condition (other than RVO) that might affect macular edema or alter visual acuity during the course of the study. He has not undergone major ocular surgery (including cataract extraction, scleral buckle, any intraocular surgery, etc.) within three months prior to study entry. His right eye meets all the same criteria for study eye eligibility, but the left eye was selected as the study eye by the investigator.

A 56-year old male with Type II Diabetes was diagnosed with atherosclerotic heart disease (MI) a year ago. He is currently taking Metformin, Sitagliptin and Liraglutide to control his blood sugar levels. He also takes Lisinopril to control his blood pressure. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery 5 years ago. He has a family history of heart disease with his father having had a heart attack at the age of 62. He is married and has two children. He has been able to continue his work as a mechanic without any difficulty. The patient does not have any known allergies to medications. He is not on any other experimental drug. The patient has a urine albumin/creatinine ratio of 40 mg/g. He has no history of drug abuse and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 24-year-old female who was diagnosed with chordoma at the age of 17. She was treated at the Massachusetts General Hospital Department of Radiation Oncology and is an English speaker. She is currently living in the United States and is interested in participating in a research study investigating the genetic basis of chordoma. She is willing to provide medical records relating to her chordoma and any other serious medical conditions she has had. She is also willing to provide a piece of her stored tumor tissue and collect two samples of cheek cells for genetic analysis. She has no family history of chordoma or any other cancers or tumors that started in the brain or spine. She completed high school and is currently working as a receptionist. She is single and has no children. She has no history of smoking or drug use.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of chronic liver disease presents with ascites, jaundice, and spider angiomata. The patient is admitted to the hospital, and the clinical care team plans to transfuse plasma to target a specific INR value. The patient has a biopsy-confirmed diagnosis of cirrhosis and laboratory evidence of synthetic dysfunction (INR>1.5, bilirubin> 2.0 mg/dL, albumin<2.5 mg/dL). The patient has no history of taking vitamin K antagonists and is able to provide consent for the study. The patient is not pregnant and is not a prisoner. The patient is eligible to participate in this clinical trial to validate a plasma transfusion dosing algorithm in patients with chronic liver disease.

This is a 45 year-old female who presented with jaundice, abdominal pain, and weight loss of 10 pounds in the past month. She underwent imaging studies which revealed a large mass in the common bile duct with evidence of biliary obstruction. Further workup, including biopsy, confirmed the diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma. She has a Child-Pugh classification of A and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group scoring system (ECOG) score of 1. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has been referred to a specialized center for further evaluation and treatment.

A 42-year-old office worker has been experiencing intense pain in their lower back, buttocks, and legs for the past 3 months. The pain is severe and has started to affect their daily activities. They consulted their general practitioner who diagnosed them with Sciatica. The patient was referred to a Spinal Specialist who conducted a thorough physical examination and recommended investigations to determine the underlying cause of the patient's symptoms. The patient underwent various tests, including an MRI scan and nerve conduction studies. The results of the tests were received 2 weeks ago, and the patient was informed that the cause of their Sciatica was likely due to nerve root involvement. The patient is currently experiencing a mix of emotions, including relief that they know the cause of their pain, but also frustration at the ongoing discomfort and the need for further treatment. They are interested in participating in the clinical trial to share their experience and help improve the care of patients with Sciatica. The patient is fluent in English and has no history of spinal surgery or any other serious medical conditions.

50-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes, managed with diet and exercise, presents with difficulty controlling his blood sugar levels. He has not had any medication adjustments in the past 2 months and his hemoglobin A1C has been stable between 7.0% to 8.0% with no variations of more than 10% since the prior visit. He has no history of overt cardiovascular disease, hepatic or renal insufficiency, or hemoglobinopathies. The patient is compliant with his medications and follow-up appointments. He has no known allergies and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of mulberry leaf extract in controlling his blood sugar levels. The patient is not on insulin and is not a woman of reproductive potential.

25 year-old female with a history of cystic fibrosis, who has been experiencing worsening respiratory symptoms over the past few months. She reports a productive cough with green sputum, shortness of breath, decreased exercise tolerance, and fatigue. Her lung function tests show a FEV1 of 45% predicted. Sputum cultures have grown Pseudomonas aeruginosa. She is currently on albuterol, hypertonic saline, and dornase alfa. She has never been on any antipseudomonal antibiotics by inhalation, IV, or oral routes in the past 14 days. She has never had a lung transplant and is not pregnant. She is willing to provide written informed consent prior to any study related procedures.

Samantha is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Stage IV melanoma. She has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but her cancer has progressed. She has a B-Raf V600E mutation in her tumor. Samantha has an ECOG score of 1 and her organ and marrow functions are adequate. She has no significant history of cardiovascular disease. Samantha has never received treatment with a RAF inhibitor. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to receive combination therapy with BMS-908662 and ipilimumab in hopes of improving her anti-tumor response and overall survival.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing facial wrinkles (rhytides) for some time. She has Fitzpatrick III skin type, and has been post-menopausal for the past 5 years. She does not have any uncontrolled comorbid conditions and is not a smoker, nor does she consume alcohol or use corticosteroids. She has not undergone any chemical peeling or skin filling in the face or neck in the past 12 months and does not have any keloid scars. Her Mini-Mental State Examination score is 24, indicating normal cognitive function. She has no history of psychiatric disorders and is not undergoing orthodontic treatment. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve the appearance of her facial wrinkles.

The patient is a 17-month-old boy who was born premature at 32 weeks and spent 6 weeks in NICU due to respiratory distress syndrome. He was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at 10 months of age and is currently receiving physical therapy twice a week. He has significant motor impairments that limit his ability to crawl or walk independently. He is able to sit upright with support but has difficulty maintaining balance. He has good vision and hearing, and is responsive to his environment. He enjoys playing with toys and interacting with his parents and siblings. His cognitive abilities are equivalent to a 9-month-old level. His parents are interested in exploring the use of power mobility device to improve his exploratory behaviors, cognitive, communication, and social-emotional development.

This is a 45 year-old African-American male who has been diagnosed with hypertension and has been prescribed antihypertensive medication. Despite being prescribed medication, the patient has struggled with adherence to their medication regimen. The patient has a history of smoking and a family history of hypertension. The patient is able to walk several blocks and is able to provide informed consent in English. The patient is interested in participating in a study that may help improve their adherence to their medication and ultimately improve their overall health.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with moderate to very severe COPD. He has been smoking for over 30 years and has quit smoking for the past 6 months. He experiences shortness of breath when performing daily activities, such as walking and climbing stairs. He has been using two or more inhaled maintenance therapies for the management of his COPD for the past 6 weeks. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has not been hospitalized due to poorly controlled COPD in the past 6 weeks. He is not allergic to β2-agonists, corticosteroids, or muscarinic anticholinergics. He agrees to use an acceptable contraceptive method as he is sexually active. He signs the informed consent to participate in the 12-week chronic-dosing study to assess the efficacy and safety of BGF MDI compared to BFF MDI in subjects with moderate to very severe COPD.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who works as a marketing manager. She has a missing mandibular incisor due to a sports injury two years ago. She is in good general health with no significant medical history or allergies. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has not had any major dental work done in the past two years. She is conscious of her appearance and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve the aesthetics of her smile. She is willing to attend all follow-up appointments and is committed to adhering to the study protocol.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic melanoma in the lungs and liver. She has no other history of malignancy and has not received any prior therapy with DTIC or thalidomide. The lesions are measurable and her labs show an ANC of 1800/mm3, hemoglobin of 10 mg/dl, platelets of 120,000 mm3, liver function tests within normal limits, and creatinine of 1.2 mg/dl. She has an ECOG performance status of 2. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use adequate contraception as instructed. The patient has been informed of the potential for severe birth defects with thalidomide and is able to follow instructions to avoid conception while taking thalidomide.

A 14-year-old female adolescent suffering from depression has completed 12 sessions of IPT-A and has shown a partial response to treatment with a CGI-I score of 2. She is an English-speaking individual with both parents being fluent in English. The patient is currently not on any medication for depression. She has no history of any significant medical or psychiatric conditions and has not been hospitalized in the past 6 months. The patient is not currently pregnant or planning pregnancy during the study period. She has a supportive family environment and is willing to comply with the continuation treatment plan.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with clinically localized prostate cancer. He has no history of diabetes, urinary incontinence, or erectile dysfunction, and has maintained normal sexual function. He has a regular sexual partner and has not undergone any prior treatment with hormones, anti-androgens, or androgen deprivation therapy. The patient has not used aspirin or heparin in the past two weeks and does not anticipate needing to use them for the next two weeks following the radical prostatectomy. The patient has not previously received any form of platelet-rich plasma treatment.

The patient is a premature baby boy weighing 450 grams, born at 26 weeks gestation. He was admitted to the NICU due to respiratory distress and requires oxygen greater than 30%. He has no evidence of focal lobar consolidation in his lung fields. He has been receiving continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy for the past 3 days, but his respiratory distress persists. The baby's past medical history is non-significant.
