His mother has no significant medical history, and his father has a history of seasonal allergies. The baby's feeding is being managed through a nasogastric tube. The baby's vital signs are stable, and he is tolerating the current therapy well.

A 15-year-old female presents with a BMI of 32. She is in Tanner stage III and reports regular menstrual cycles. She has no chronic medical problems and is not taking any medications. She has a family history of obesity and her older sister was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at the age of 18. She has been referred for the study because she meets the inclusion criteria for obese insulin resistant adolescents. Her adiponectin level is 5 ug/dl, triglyceride level is 150 mg/dl and WBISI is 0.8. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that it will help her understand the underlying mechanisms of obesity and insulin resistance.

A 2-year-old boy with sickle cell anemia is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy and safety of hydroxyurea for children with SCA in malaria endemic regions. He was diagnosed with sickle cell anemia at birth and has a history of recurrent episodes of vaso-occlusive crisis and acute pain episodes. He has no history of blood transfusions or other major medical conditions. His most recent laboratory results show hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL, platelet count of 200 x 10E9/L, and ANC of 2.5 x 10E9/L. He lives in a malaria endemic region and has had one episode of malaria in the past year, which was treated successfully with antimalarial medication. He weighs 12 kg and is willing to comply with all study-related treatments, evaluations, and follow-up.

9-year-old female with a history of congenital heart disease, including transposition of the great arteries and a ventricular septal defect, status post-repair in infancy. She was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit with severe acute heart failure, including pulmonary edema and low cardiac output. She had been receiving conventional inotropic treatment, but her symptoms persisted. She is able to communicate and understand the purpose of the study. Her parents have given written consent for her to participate in the study and for the transfer of material for cellular and molecular studies. She does not have hypertrophic or restrictive cardiomyopathy, aortic stenosis, or any known allergies to drugs used in the study. She is not pregnant.

A 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with type IIa hyperlipidemia. His LDL-C levels have been consistently high, ranging from 140 to 160 mg/dL. Despite his efforts to adhere to a low-cholesterol diet, his cholesterol levels remain elevated. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his cholesterol levels and reduce his risk of developing cardiovascular disease. He has no known sensitivities to ezetimibe, simvastatin, or niacin and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

47-year-old male patient diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) for the past 5 years presented to the rheumatology clinic with complaints of worsening joint pain, swelling, stiffness, and difficulty in performing daily activities. The patient also reported the presence of psoriasis on his scalp, trunk, and limbs for the past 10 years which is now flaring up more frequently. He has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief, but the symptoms are not well controlled. The patient has no significant past medical history except hypertension for which he is taking an ACE inhibitor. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Physical examination revealed multiple, tender, and swollen joints in the hands, wrists, elbows, knees, and ankles. Psoriatic skin lesions were also observed on the scalp, elbows, and knees. Radiographs showed joint space narrowing and erosions in the affected joints. Laboratory investigations showed elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). The patient has not received treatment with anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF) or other biologic agents before. He provided written informed consent allowing the use of his data for the study and providing permission for contact by the study personnel. He is currently not participating in any other prospective study including controlled clinical trials and observational studies.

A 60-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and underwent a coronary angiogram, which revealed a high thrombotic burden in the culprit lesion. The thrombus size was estimated to be at least 2 times the diameter of the vessel. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes, all well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. He has never had a heart attack before. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate thrombectomy as an adjunct to primary angioplasty.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. His diagnosis was confirmed by a biopsy of the prostate gland. A bone scan showed no evidence of bone metastases. His oncologist recommended androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with leuprolide acetate to lower the level of testosterone in his body, which can stimulate the growth of prostate cancer cells. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light physical activity. His medical history is unremarkable except for high blood pressure, which is well-controlled with medication. He has never been treated with calcitriol or bisphosphonates. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to take the study medication as prescribed.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who has been experiencing abdominal pain and unexplained weight loss for the past 2 months. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. A CT scan revealed a mass in the pancreas. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The cancer is unresectable, and the patient has not received any prior chemotherapy. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and his blood work shows normal levels of creatinine, bilirubin, ALT, and AST. He has no other significant medical conditions and is not currently being treated for any infections or illnesses. He is able to swallow pills and has no malabsorption problems or ongoing nausea or vomiting. He has agreed to use an effective contraceptive method and is not allergic to eggs. He is willing to stop taking any additional dietary/herbal supplements except Senekot.

A 28 year old woman presents with severe pelvic pain that has been going on for the past 5 years. She reports that she has tried various treatments including pain medications and hormonal therapy, but has not found any relief. She has a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and painful periods. She has no other underlying medical conditions and is not currently on any medications. She is seeking treatment for her pain and is willing to undergo surgery for the management of her endometriosis.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a history of chronic pancreatitis. She has been experiencing severe abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, and diarrhea for the past year. She has been on pain medications but the pain is not well-controlled. Her physician has recommended a total pancreatectomy and islet autotransplantation. She does not have a history of diabetes mellitus or hyperglycemia. Her baseline fasting glucose is within normal range. She has no significant medical conditions that could impact islet function. Her serum creatinine levels are normal. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She is interested in participating in the study because she wants to maximize the chances of achieving insulin independence after the procedure. She is willing to follow the study protocol, including taking sitagliptin for one year after the surgery.

This is a 59 year-old male with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy who underwent implantation of an ICD three months ago per standard of care guidelines. He has been well-controlled on his current medication regimen but has experienced occasional episodes of shortness of breath and fatigue. He has a smartphone with Bluetooth capability and internet access. He has no other identifiable reversible cause explaining his left ventricular dysfunction. He is willing to participate in a clinical study that aims to improve his management of heart failure with the use of an implanted device that will provide data on his heart rate, activity, and fluid status to a multidisciplinary team who will guide his medical care based on a pre-specified standard of care medication decision model.

A 2-day old full-term baby boy who was born via vaginal delivery with no complications is being admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to clinical suspicion of infection. The baby's birth weight was 3.5 kg and he has no known congenital malformations or syndromes. The mother's prenatal care was unremarkable and she was not administered antibiotics during pregnancy. The baby's blood cultures are pending, but due to clinical suspicion, the neonatologist has ordered the initiation of antibiotic therapy. The baby has not been exposed to probiotics before and does not have a diagnosis of cow's milk protein allergy. The baby is eligible for the study if the antibiotic treatment is expected to last for at least 5 days. The study team will randomly assign the baby to receive either the probiotic Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 or a placebo, and evaluate the effect of the probiotic on the infant's gut microbiota development, functional gastrointestinal disorders, weight gain, body composition, and bone density.

The patient is a 35 year-old male diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) by a psychiatrist. He has a history of depressive symptoms for more than 2 years, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and worthlessness. He has tried several antidepressant medications over the years, but none of them have been effective in treating his symptoms. He is currently not taking any antidepressant medication, but he is seeing a therapist regularly. He has no history of drug abuse or dependence. He is able and willing to complete study procedures, including regular completion of web surveys and telephone interviews with study personnel.

A 5-year-old boy named Jack accompanied by his parents visited the dental clinic for a routine check-up. Jack has no underlying medical conditions and is generally healthy. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Jack brushes his teeth twice a day and his parents help him floss regularly. Jack has a deep carious lesion in his primary molar, but he has no pain or tenderness to percussion. Preliminary radiographs indicate that there is no evidence of pathologic internal or external root resorption or any evidence of inter-radicular bone destruction. Jack's parents have consented to participate in the study and Jack is willing to cooperate with all the steps of the study.

Patient B is a 9-year-old female who is currently in the 4th grade. She has been struggling with her weight for the past year and her parents have become concerned. She is currently at the 89th percentile for BMI and her parents are worried that she may continue to gain weight. They are interested in enrolling her in a clinical trial to help her lose weight and develop healthier habits. The family is fluent in English and are able to attend all treatment and assessment sessions. The child does not have any medical conditions that impact weight or may affect participation in physical activity or treatment. The family is willing to be randomized to either treatment arm and is committed to completing the entire program.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has recently undergone a major surgery due to colon cancer. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His occupation is a desk job and he is relatively sedentary. He has been informed by his healthcare provider that he is at high risk for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) according to a National guideline and has a Caprini score of 11+. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of venous thromboembolism prophylaxis by the combination of graduated compression stockings (GCS), standard doses of low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWH), and sequential compression device (SCD) in surgical patients at high and extremely high risk for VTE. He is willing to provide informed consent and agrees to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study.

53-year-old female with a history of Alzheimer's disease and a previous MRI scan showing structural changes in the brain is being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial. She has been experiencing memory loss, difficulty with language, and confusion for the last 2 years. She is currently taking donepezil and memantine to manage her symptoms but has shown little improvement. She is interested in participating in this study as she hopes it will provide more information on the changes in her brain and improve her understanding of the disease. She has no known ferromagnetic objects in her body and has no history of cochlear impairment or pregnancy. She is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who had a kidney transplant 4 years ago. He is currently being treated with anticalcineurin and has stopped taking corticosteroids for over 6 months. He has experienced a weight gain of more than 3 kg in the past two years. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. His renal function is stable with a creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min/1.73m². He has not had any infections or changes in weight in the past 3 months and is HIV and HCV serology negative. He has not had any acute rejection episodes and is compliant with his immunosuppressive medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 55-year-old Korean male with a history of hypercholesterolemia. His LDL cholesterol levels have been consistently high despite adhering to a low-fat diet and exercising regularly. His physician has prescribed Rosuvastatin/Ezetimibe for the first time to help manage his cholesterol levels. Patient A has no known allergies to any medications and has not experienced any adverse reactions to previous medications. He has a normal renal function and is not currently taking any medications that may interact with Rosuvastatin/Ezetimibe. He has provided informed consent to participate in this post-marketing surveillance study.

A 6-year-old boy was referred to a geneticist by his pediatrician due to developmental delay and vision problems. The child was born at full term with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. He has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and gastroesophageal reflux disease. His parents are non-consanguineous and healthy, and there is no known family history of neurological or vision problems. The child started walking independently at the age of 2.5 years, and his speech development is delayed. On physical examination, the child has a head circumference at the 90th percentile, with no dysmorphic features noted. The neurological examination showed hypotonia, hyperreflexia, and a positive Babinski sign. The child had bilateral corneal clouding and retinal degeneration on ophthalmologic examination. The clinical suspicion for MLIV was raised based on the clinical presentation and significantly elevated blood gastrin levels. The child is eligible for the study and able to travel to the Baylor Institute of Metabolic Disease in Dallas for evaluation.

A 55-year-old non-smoking Asian male presents with persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has no significant past medical history and denies any family history of cancer. Physical exam reveals decreased breath sounds in the left lung. A chest X-ray shows a mass in the left lung. A subsequent CT scan confirms a 6 cm left upper lobe lung mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy of the mass is consistent with adenocarcinoma of the lung. Molecular testing reveals that the tumor has an EGFR activating mutation. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1. He has not received any prior systemic therapy for advanced disease. He is eligible for cohort A of a clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of the oral PanHER inhibitor, PF-00299804, as a single oral agent in patients with advanced adenocarcinoma of the lung who are either non-smokers, former light smokers, or have known EGFR activating mutation.

A 40-year-old male came to the clinic for a routine check-up. On examination, he was found to have a BMI of 30 and elevated blood pressure (SBP 140 mmHg and DBP 90 mmHg). His lipid profile showed LDL-C levels of 120 mg/dL. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, stroke, diabetes, liver, kidney or autoimmune disease. He is a non-smoker and does not take any blood pressure or cholesterol-lowering medications. However, he has been taking fish oil capsules and fiber supplements for the last 6 months. He is willing to discontinue these supplements for the duration of the study. He has no known nut allergies and is not a vegetarian. He is interested in participating in the study to reduce his risk of cardiovascular disease.

Patient is a 6-month-old male infant with a diagnosis of congenital heart disease, who is scheduled to undergo a cardiac catheterization procedure for both treatment and diagnosis. The infant weighs 6 kg and has no known skin abnormalities affecting the digits. The parents have provided written consent for the infant's participation in the study.

This is a 68-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin to manage his conditions. He has no history of neurological abnormalities, seizures, or cardiac arrhythmias. He has a BMI of 27 kg/m2 and is considered to be in good health for his age. He has no history of orthostatic hypotension or any other medical conditions that are not stably controlled. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance medical research and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the hospital with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. His EKG showed ST segment depression in the inferolateral leads. Cardiac catheterization was performed and revealed a 70% stenosis in the mid right coronary artery, consistent with a de novo coronary lesion. The patient has no previous history of coronary artery disease and is not currently taking any antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications. His hemodynamics were stable on presentation, and his estimated life expectancy is greater than 1 year. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a DCB-only approach for de novo coronary lesions.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy from a rural community in a low-income country. He was brought in by his mother who noticed that his arms and legs have become very thin and he has lost weight. He has been experiencing diarrhea for the past two weeks and has been vomiting intermittently. He is not able to eat much and has been losing his appetite. The mother reports that he has been breastfeeding but has not been consuming any other sources of nutrition. The child has no known allergies and has not been involved in any other research trials or supplemental feeding programs. The child's mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) measures at 11.6 cm and there is no bipedal edema. The child has no history of any debilitating illness.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her 20th week of pregnancy. She has a history of recurrent vaginal candidiasis, which has been confirmed by a positive vaginal yeast culture. She experiences symptoms of burning sensation in the vagina vulva, production of heavy white/yellow curd-like discharge and/or an itchy vulva, pruritus, dyspareunia, dysuria, irritation, soreness of the vulva and other discomforting symptoms. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatments to antibiotics, as she is concerned about the development of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. She is willing to commit throughout the experiment and is not currently taking any long-term medication. She does not have Type-1 diabetes nor Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency.

This is a 35-year-old male migrant farmworker who lives with his wife and two young children on a farm in the western region of North Carolina. He works long hours in the fields and is often exposed to pesticides. He and his family have limited knowledge about the potential dangers of pesticide exposure and how to reduce their risk of exposure. He is interested in learning more about how to protect his family's health and is willing to participate in a Lay Health Advisor program to receive education and training on pesticide safety in the home. His family is eligible for this study as they have at least one member employed in farmwork and at least one coresident child.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is scheduled to undergo elective surgery for a hernia repair. He works as a construction worker and is physically active on a daily basis. He is 175 cm tall and weighs 85 kg (BMI: 27.8). He has no history of cardiovascular disease or stroke, and he does not smoke or drink alcohol. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 70 beats per minute. He reports no difficulty walking or communicating. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent. The patient has not been prescribed any routine exercise regimen in the past, but he is willing to follow the prescribed walking routine before his surgery.

56-year-old male with a history of hypertension, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who was admitted to the GICU with respiratory distress and hypoxia. He was intubated and mechanically ventilated. The patient had a central venous line and urinary catheter placed for monitoring and management. He was started on empirical antibiotics for possible pneumonia. The patient remained in the GICU for 7 days and was then transferred to the regular floor with a plan for further management of his respiratory distress. He was discharged home after 3 days on the regular floor. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no known allergies to copper or iodine.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for several years. Despite being on antipsychotic medication, she continues to experience residual positive and negative symptoms, as well as cognitive impairment that affects her daily life. She has not been hospitalized for psychiatric reasons in the past 30 days and her current psychiatric medication has been stable for at least 30 days. She is not pregnant and is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study period. She has no history of liver disease or heart failure, and her kidney function is normal. Her lipid levels are slightly elevated, but she has not been diagnosed with hyperlipidemia. She is not currently taking any medications that are contraindicated with Pravastatin. She is interested in participating in the study to see if adding Pravastatin to her current medication regimen can improve her symptoms and cognitive functioning.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection for over a year. He has been treated with combination antiviral therapy (ARV) for at least a year and has achieved plasma HIV-1 RNA levels below detection for at least six months. His virus is CCR5 tropic, as determined by the Monogram assay. He is willing to undergo a gastrointestinal (GI) biopsy at study entry and agree to subsequent GI biopsies at 12 and 24 weeks. He has a normal ANC, hemoglobin, platelet count, liver function tests, and creatinine clearance. He

A 56-year-old male with metastatic urothelial carcinoma who has previously undergone cisplatin-based chemotherapy. He has measurable disease with multiple lung and liver lesions. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of significant cardiac disease or peripheral neuropathy. He has no known allergies to any of the study medications. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no history of significant gastrointestinal disease or procedure that could interfere with the oral absorption of ixazomib.

This is a 55-year-old woman with recurrent serous epithelial ovarian cancer. She was initially diagnosed in [**10/2117**] and underwent surgical debulking followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. She had an excellent response and was monitored off treatment for approximately 18 months. She then presented with a rising CA-125 and had a CT scan which showed progressive disease. She then received six cycles of carboplatin and liposomal doxorubicin with a partial response. She subsequently had disease progression with rising CA-125 and new pulmonary nodules. A biopsy confirmed recurrence of her ovarian cancer. She then received six cycles of gemcitabine and carboplatin with a partial response, which was again followed by disease progression. She is currently off treatment and is being evaluated for this clinical trial.

25 y/o female, diagnosed with schizophrenia 6 months ago, with no prior history of psychotic disorders. Currently on Olanzapine monotherapy for the past 3 months, with some improvement in delusions and hallucinations, but experiencing significant weight gain and cognitive deficits. She reports increased appetite and cravings for sugary and high-fat foods, leading to a weight gain of 10 pounds in the past month. She also reports difficulty with memory, attention, and decision-making, which is affecting her ability to work and socialize. She denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse, and is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. She has no comorbid severe physiological disease and no contraindication to rTMS.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old Korean male who has been genotyped as an extensive metabolizer of CYP2C19. He has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and does not have any clinically relevant concomitant diseases. He does not have a history of surgery or any chronic or acute infections. He does not smoke or abuse drugs, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not participated in any other clinical trial with an investigational drug within the past two months. He is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site and use acceptable methods of contraception to avoid pregnancy in his female partner.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with metastasis to the spine and liver. She has been experiencing severe pain in her lower back and right leg for the past week, which has significantly decreased her mobility and quality of life. The patient has no history of radiation therapy. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis, for which she takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and alendronate, respectively. She denies any drug allergies. The patient is currently not receiving any chemotherapy or immunotherapy. She has a performance status of 2, with a BMI of 27. She is able to understand and sign the informed consent document.

58-year-old male with end-stage liver disease secondary to alcohol abuse presents for liver transplantation evaluation. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. He has been abstinent from alcohol for the past 6 months and is compliant with his medications. His Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score is currently 28. He reports no recent illnesses or hospitalizations. Physical examination reveals jaundice, ascites, and spider angiomas on the chest and arms. Laboratory studies show elevated bilirubin, creatinine, and INR. Vitamin D level is found to be low (12 ng/mL). He is scheduled for liver transplantation and will be enrolled in the observational prospective study evaluating vitamin D levels in liver transplantation recipients.

The patient is a 63-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past week. Upon examination, the patient's blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, and heart rate is 85 beats per minute. His laboratory results show a serum creatinine level of 1.0 mg/dL. He is admitted for on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. The patient has no known allergies and has never undergone a CABG procedure before. He has not been diagnosed with end-stage kidney disease or undergoing any renal replacement therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits involved.

A 55-year-old man with a history of cirrhosis presents to the hospital with confusion, agitation and lethargy. The patient's family reports that he has been more forgetful and confused for the past few days. The patient has a history of alcohol abuse and has been noncompliant with his medication regimen. Physical examination reveals asterixis and elevated ammonia levels. The patient has no signs of infection, electrolyte disturbances, or gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient's MELD score is 15. The patient's next of keen is informed about the clinical trial and has consented for the patient's participation. The patient does not have any contraindications for albumin administration.

This is a 45-year-old woman with a long-standing history of asthma. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 32, which is classified as obese. Despite being compliant with her asthma controller medication, she has reported persistent shortness of breath and wheezing. Upon further evaluation, it was found that her blood levels of L-arginine, an amino acid that is used to make nitric oxide (NO) in the lungs, were reduced. Nitric oxide is critical for proper lung function, and reduced levels of NO can lead to increased airway resistance and asthma symptoms.   She has been invited to participate in a short open-label study to receive L-citrulline, an amino acid that can increase levels of L-arginine and thereby restore the concentration of NO in the airways. The study will involve taking 15g/day of L-citrulline for two weeks. Before and after the treatment, she will undergo lung function testing and donate blood for analysis.   To be eligible for the study, she must have a BMI of 30 or greater, be diagnosed with asthma, and have a smoking history of 10 pack years or less. She must not have had a respiratory tract infection or a corticosteroid burst within the last four weeks, and she must not have any significant concomitant medical illnesses such as heart disease, cancer, or uncontrolled diabetes. She cannot be on high dose inhaled steroids or current statin use, and she cannot have an intolerance or allergy to L-arginine or L-citrulline.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who has been evaluated for kidney transplantation at Mayo Clinic. He has been on hemodialysis for five years and has been experiencing decreasing physical function. He used to work as a chef, but now he has difficulty standing for long periods of time and lifting heavy objects. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well-controlled. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 28 kg/m2, and he weighs 200 lbs. He has no history of heart disease or other significant comorbidities. He is interested in participating in the study and has provided written consent. He completed the SPPB and Fried Frailty Phenotype testing and was found to be frail. He speaks English fluently and has access to an adequate interpreter if needed. He has a supportive family and lives in a single-story house with his wife. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/75 Hgb: 11 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 8 mg/dl BUN: 80 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy

A 35-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of migraines for the past 10 years. She experiences headaches 8-10 times a month, lasting for 2-3 days each time. She has tried different medications for migraine prophylaxis, but they did not provide sufficient relief. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) for migraine prevention. She is a non-smoker and is not allergic to fish or omega-3 fatty acids. She has read the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or nursing and has no history of bleeding diathesis or use of anticoagulation agents.

A 62-year-old man with advanced lung cancer has been referred to the Palliative Care Unit at Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet. He has been experiencing increasing fatigue, difficulty performing physical activities, and limitations in his work and daily activities. He is also experiencing pain and worry related to his diagnosis. He lives with his wife and adult son, and they provide him with most of his care at home. He is able to read and understand Danish.

55yo male with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 5 years ago. He has been managing his diabetes with diet and exercise, but his last HbA1c level was 8.5%. He has a history of hyperlipidemia and hypertension, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of pancreatitis or retinopathy. His current body weight is 95kg and he reports a weight loss of 3kg in the past 3 months. He has never had gastric surgery or other gastric procedures for weight loss. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is willing to use highly effective birth control methods during the study period.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been injecting opiates for the past 2 years. He injects at least 4 times a week and has never received any drug abuse treatment. He resides in Denver and is not transient. He is not involved in any other research activities and is willing to meet with an Addiction Research and Treatment Services (methadone clinic) counselor. He is motivated to receive treatment and is looking for ways to reduce his drug use. He is currently unemployed and lives with his girlfriend who is also an opiate user. He has no history of mental illness or any other medical problems. He is able to provide informed consent and participate in the follow-up interviews.

The patient is a 72-year-old veteran who is scheduled for a non-urgent primary care visit at the VA Ann Arbor Medical Center. The patient has no history of colorectal cancer screening and is due for screening according to the 2008 USPSTF colorectal cancer screening guideline. The patient has multiple comorbidities including hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. The patient is also a former smoker with a 20 pack-year history but has quit smoking for the past 5 years. The patient reports no symptoms related to colorectal cancer such as abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or changes in bowel habits. The patient is able to communicate effectively in English and has no cognitive impairment or visual impairment. The patient has a medical power of attorney who is not involved in the patient's care decisions. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is assigned to a primary care provider who has consented to the study.

This is a 25-year-old female who works as a graphic designer. She has been wearing glasses for the past two years and has been experiencing discomfort when wearing them for long periods of time. She is interested in trying contact lenses and is considering different options. She has a spherical distance prescription of -2.75 in both eyes and has no astigmatism. She has no history of ocular abnormalities or diseases and has never had any anterior ocular surgery. She is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with contact lens wear and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to comply with the study schedule and is excited to participate in this clinical trial to explore her options for comfortable contact lens wear.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who works in an IT company. He is physically active and exercises 3 to 4 times a week. He has no significant medical history and currently takes no medication. His BMI is 22. He enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking, camping and playing football. He has no known allergies to medications or any food. His blood pressure is normal and there is no evidence of any cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, hematological, or neurological disorders. He has not participated in any clinical trial involving an investigational product within the last 30 days. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to medical research and to gain knowledge about his health.

62-year-old male with a history of obesity and loud snoring, presented with daytime sleepiness and poor concentration. The patient reported gasping and choking episodes during the night, and his partner reported that he often stops breathing while sleeping. The Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score was 15. The patient underwent an overnight polysomnography (PSG) which confirmed a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of 42 events per hour. The patient has not been treated for OSA before and does not have any other medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and not taking any maintenance medications.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presents to the clinic with a history of pain in the ball of her left foot. The pain is described as sharp and burning, and it is exacerbated with walking and standing for prolonged periods. She reports a history of wearing high heels on a regular basis for work. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the third and fourth metatarsal heads, and the pain is reproduced with palpation of the intermetatarsal space. Magnetic resonance imaging confirms a diagnosis of Morton's neuroma. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of insole with metatarsal support on pain in patients with Morton's neuroma. She is able to walk independently and is willing to comply with the study protocol, including wearing the insoles provided for the duration of the trial. She signs the informed consent form and meets all inclusion criteria.

A 28-year-old male athlete who plays volleyball regularly for at least 6 hours per week is being sought for a clinical trial on the analysis of shoulder muscle activity during isokinetic evaluation of rotators. The study aims to assess the impact of different positions of the glenohumeral joint on the maximum muscle contraction of different shoulder muscles. To be eligible, the participant should not have any pain in the shoulder and should not have any shoulder pathologies such as gleno-humeral dislocation, tendinopathy, sub-acromial conflict, etc. Additionally, the participant should not have any history of shoulder surgery, such as prosthesis or stabilizing surgery. If you meet the above criteria and are interested in participating in the study, please contact us for further information.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with schizophrenia, according to the DSM-IV criteria. She presented with a 3-month history of auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech. She has no history of substance abuse or high risk for suicide. She was started on risperidone at a dose of 1 mg/day, which was gradually increased to 4 mg/day over the course of 4 weeks. Despite the treatment, she still reports auditory hallucinations and has difficulty concentrating. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of switching from risperidone to aripiprazole in the early stage of pharmacotherapy.

A 45 yo F with a diagnosis of moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis for the past 2 years. She has tried multiple topical treatments and phototherapy in the past, but none of them provided significant improvement. She is currently experiencing a flare-up with involvement of approximately 20% of body surface area and is looking for more effective treatment options. She has not been previously exposed to adalimumab or risankizumab. She is willing to use highly effective birth control methods during the study period, as she is of childbearing age. She has no history of major surgery or chronic infections and does not take any medication that would interfere with the safe conduct of the study. She is not currently enrolled in any other investigational study and has not been enrolled in this trial in the past.

This is a 65 year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who presents with complaints of pain and weakness in the legs. She was diagnosed with aortoiliac occlusive disease after CT angiography showed TASC B lesions. She has good distal runoff and is a suitable candidate for either iodine contrast or carbon dioxide for endovascular treatment. She has no history of allergy to contrast and her kidney function is normal. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the quality of image produced by both contrast mediums and their safety.

A 32-year-old woman is looking for a non-invasive weight loss solution. She has a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and is fluent in English. She is currently not pregnant and is not lactating. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and adhere to the study visit schedule. She has no gastrointestinal disorders and has not had any prior bariatric procedures. She has no significant multisystem disease and has a HbA1c level of 6.2. She has no significant cardiac arrhythmia or ectopy, and no significant cardiovascular disease. She has no existing implanted electrical stimulator and has no history of malignancy in the last 2 years. She has not had a weight change of +5% of her Total Body Weight in the 3 months prior to enrollment. She has no moderate/severe psychiatric disorder, no diagnosed neurological disease, and no diagnosed eating disorder. She has no skin disorder affecting the thoracic dermatomes, no abdominal surgery, and no other scars which may interfere with stimulation in the opinion of the PI. She is not currently enrolled in other potentially confounding research. She has no known allergic reaction to materials in the electrodes and/or is otherwise unable to tolerate stimulation with the wearable TENS system. She is not actively participating or unwilling to discontinue participation in another weight loss program. She is not taking weight loss control medications including but not limited to OTC medications, Metformin, and Belviq. She is able to take anti-nausea medications planned for the study. She is able to walk at least 0.8 kilometers per day (10 minutes of continuous walking). She is a non-smoker and has no history of treatment for or current abuse of drugs or alcohol. She has a score of <10 on the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), demonstrating no significant depression. She is not taking Topiramate for severe headache disorders.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) 6 months ago. He has been experiencing palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of cardiac surgery or implantable cardiac device procedures. His ECG shows atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 80 bpm. His echocardiogram shows a left atrium size of 4.5 cm, normal left ventricular function and no evidence of thrombus. He is currently taking a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) and a beta-blocker. He is willing and capable of participating in all testing associated with this clinical study at an approved clinical investigational center. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is of legal age to give informed consent specific to state and national law.

A 25-year-old non-smoker Korean male who is currently working as a software engineer with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 is eligible for this clinical trial. He has no history of any diseases and has not experienced any significant weight changes in the past 6 months. He does not consume nuts regularly and does not take any nutrient supplements. He exercises regularly and has a Korean habitual diet. He does not consume alcohol frequently. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions given by the investigators.

A 60-year-old retired teacher was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) last year. She underwent surgical resection followed by radiation therapy. Despite these treatments, her cancer has recurred and has spread to the liver and bones. She has persistent cough and shortness of breath. She is currently taking morphine for pain management. She has a past medical history of hypertension and osteoporosis. She lives with her husband and two adult children. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has no other concurrent severe underlying disease. She understands the possible risks and benefits of the treatment and is willing to sign a written informed consent.

Patient is a 32-year-old man who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 2 years ago. He has been on a combination of mesalamine and prednisone, but despite these medications, he has experienced frequent flare-ups of his disease, with significant abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and weight loss. His most recent colonoscopy showed moderate to severe inflammation with an endoscopic subscore of 3. He has been informed by his physician about the possibility of enrolling in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of infliximab in inducing histological remission, and he is interested in participating. He has never been treated with infliximab or any other anti-TNF agents. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of tuberculosis or other infections, and he is willing and able to adhere to the visit protocol schedule and procedures.

A 35-year-old male patient who has been diagnosed with Friedreich's ataxia is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of his symptoms. He has a confirmed diagnosis of FA through genetic testing and is currently stable on all his medications. He has not used any investigational product in the last 28 days, and he has no history of substance abuse. He does not have any preexisting psychiatric illness, diabetes, or clinically significant cardiac disease. His CBC, CMP, and diabetes lab results are within normal limits, and his creatinine is ≤1.5 mg/dl. He is ambulatory with assistance and is willing to provide informed consent for the study. He does not currently smoke and has not smoked within the past 12 months. He has no legal incapacity or limited legal capacity, and he has no abnormal WBC, hemoglobin, or platelet count.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma at stage IVc according to the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) edition VII. The patient has already undergone chemotherapy and radiotherapy but the cancer has recurred. The patient has no other malignancies and the major organs are functioning properly. The patient is not allergic to nedaplatin or gemcitabine. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has not received any other clinical trial drugs within the past 3 months.

A 67-year-old woman presents with a history of Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) and is currently receiving standard of care (SOC) antibiotic therapy for the infection. She has had multiple recurrences of CDI in the past, despite receiving treatment with metronidazole and vancomycin. Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of chronic diarrheal illness or planned surgery for CDI. She is a post-menopausal female and is not currently sexually active. She has no plans to donate ova, sperm or blood products during the study period. She is willing to use two acceptable methods of birth control during the study period as required. She has not participated in this study before and has not received MK-3415 or MK-6072. She has not received a C. difficile vaccine or another experimental monoclonal antibody against C. difficile toxin A or B. She is not planning to receive immune globulin during the study period. She is not on any medication that decreases gastrointestinal peristalsis or any therapies that have been demonstrated to decrease CDI recurrences. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and is expected to survive for the duration of the study.

A 52-year-old M diagnosed with advanced medullary thyroid carcinoma with elevated levels of calcitonin and a doubling time of less than 24 months after total thyroidectomy. The patient is not eligible for curative surgical therapy, and has not been on Vandetanib for the past 3 weeks. The patient has no renal or bone marrow failure, and has a calculated glomerular filtration rate of over 60 ml/min per 1.73 m2 body surface. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or allergic to Physiogel or other gelatine products. The patient has not experienced any serious side reactions in the past after the application of pentagastrin, and has not been diagnosed with an active second malignancy or in remission after a second malignancy within the last 5 years. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who does not smoke or use any tobacco products. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 and has never been pregnant or lactating. She has no history of allergy to systemic or topical corticosteroids and has not received any drugs as part of a research study within the past 30 days. She has no medical conditions requiring regular treatment with prescription drugs and has no history of drug or alcohol addiction requiring treatment in the past 12 months prior to dosing. She has no skin conditions or coloration that would interfere with the placement of test sites or the response or assessment of skin blanching. She is willing to sign and date an informed consent form that meets all criteria of current FDA regulations.

A 4-year-old boy was admitted to the pediatric ICU with a diagnosis of sepsis and respiratory failure. He was intubated and mechanically ventilated for 5 days. His medical history is significant for a congenital heart disease repaired 2 years ago. On examination, he was found to have bilateral crackles on lung auscultation, and his chest X-ray showed bilateral consolidation. He received antibiotics and supportive care, and his respiratory status improved. The team decided to initiate a weaning protocol to assess his readiness to extubate. The patient was enrolled in the clinical trial, and the team used Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) during the spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) on a T-piece to monitor his ventilation and pulmonary perfusion. The patient did not experience any complications during the weaning trial and was successfully extubated. The EIT data showed a significant increase in functional residual capacity during and after the weaning trial, suggesting his readiness for extubation.

A 55-year-old woman who is post-menopausal and experiencing thinning hair came to the clinic seeking treatment options. She has no underlying diseases and takes no medications. She is married and has two children. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day, three times a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Her past surgical history is significant for a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. She is in good general health and is willing to maintain her current diet, medications and exercise routine for the duration of the study. She is willing to take the provided oral supplement and maintain her normal hair washing routine. She is willing to have her hair cut and colored consistently throughout the 12-month study period. She is willing to undergo physical exams, digital photography, hair bundle measurements, and hair washing counts at the required visits. She is willing to answer questionnaires related to general lifestyle, quality of life related to hair loss, self-assessment, subject treatment satisfaction, and ease of use, subject hair satisfaction and the menopause rating scale at the required visits. She has no history of telogen efflu

A 56-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years is seeking treatment for his dyskinesias. He currently takes 600mg of levodopa daily and has noticed an increase in his dyskinesias in the past few months. He is married with two adult children and works as an accountant. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or substance abuse. He is able to perform activities of daily living independently and has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) score of 28. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help find better treatment options for his dyskinesias.

A 65-year-old male with a history of high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to his primary care physician with complaints of fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. On physical examination, the patient was noted to have cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Further laboratory testing confirmed a diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) with high-risk features including unmutated IgVH gene status and CD38 positivity. The patient is ECOG performance status 1 and has no other comorbid conditions. He has not received any prior treatment for CLL, including chemotherapy or monoclonal antibody therapy. The patient is willing to provide mandatory blood samples for research studies and is not pregnant or nursing. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial evaluating the combination of rituximab and alemtuzumab with sargramostim (GM-CSF) as first-line therapy for early-stage CLL with high-risk features.

This is a 52-year-old female who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 3 years ago. She has been on a stable dose of metformin for the past 2 years and her HbA1c levels have been consistently above 7%. She has tried multiple oral medications in the past but has not achieved adequate glycemic control. She has a BMI of 29 and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new medication for the treatment of type 2 diabetes. She has not been previously treated with insulin and has no history of pancreatitis. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to attend all study visits.

45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and stable angina presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He is diagnosed with triple-vessel coronary artery disease (CAD) and scheduled for elective off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB). Preoperative echocardiography shows an ejection fraction > 0.40. The patient has no history of atrial fibrillation or valve dysfunction. Peripheral vascular examination is normal, and the patient has no contraindications for the use of peripheral plethysmography. The patient has not undergone any other surgeries, and there is no indication for intraaortic balloon pump insertion.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese male who has been diagnosed with advanced solid tumours. He has previously undergone standard therapy which was unsuccessful in treating his condition. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) score of 1 and is in overall good health with no significant underlying medical conditions. His recent blood tests show no abnormalities and he has no history of cardiac disease. He is willing to use barrier contraception if needed. He is able to swallow oral medication without difficulty. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and tolerability of adavosertib in Japanese patients with advanced solid tumours.

Pt is a 47yo M with a recent diagnosis of high-grade glioma. He has undergone surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy as per the Stupp protocol. However, follow-up MRI scans have shown uncertain recurrence diagnosis due to complex MRI changes. The patient has been referred to the neurooncology MCC for further management decisions. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He has no comorbidities or allergies that would contraindicate MRI or 18F-FDOPA PET imaging.

A 45-year-old female breast cancer survivor who was diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer 3 years ago. She received adjuvant trastuzumab treatment for 12 months after completing chemotherapy. She has not experienced any symptoms of heart problems or heart failure. She has not undergone any cardiac imaging since completing treatment. She has a family history of heart disease, but she has never been diagnosed with any cardiac condition. She is willing to participate in a long-term assessment of her cardiovascular health to detect any late signs of heart damage from chemotherapy.

Patient is a 52-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with end-stage liver disease due to chronic hepatitis C infection. He has a BMI of 28 and no other significant medical history. The patient has been evaluated and deemed eligible for living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) using the right lobe (RL) graft. The patient will require anterior sector venous outflow reconstruction during the procedure. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided informed consent. The patient will be randomly assigned to receive either ePTFE or Dacron graft for anterior sector venous outflow reconstruction. The patient will be followed up for graft patency, infection rates, and outcomes with respect to graft and patient survival.

A 28 year old male who is a frequent concert-goer and has no prior training in CPR. He is curious about new technologies and is interested in participating in the Lowlands Saves Lives trial. He has no history of cardiac disease, no known allergies, and is able to perform the tandem gait test. He is willing to participate in either the face-to-face or Lifesaver VR training, and is available to attend the Lowlands music festival on August 16-18, 2019.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with bipolar II disorder who has been experiencing a depressive episode for the past 6 months. She has previously tried two different medications without any significant improvement of symptoms. She has no history of psychosis or suicidal ideation. She is currently taking 150mg of bupropion daily for her depression, which has been stable for the past 4 weeks. She has no other significant medical or neurological history. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

Meet John, a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness and loud snoring for the past few months. He has noticed that his sleep disturbances have been affecting his work performance and ability to concentrate during the day. He has not been diagnosed with any sleep disorders before but has a family history of sleep apnea. John has a stable medical history and is not currently taking any medications that could affect sleepiness. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the relationship between his sleep-disordered breathing and daytime alertness levels.

A 55-year-old male with a long-standing history of hip and knee osteoarthritis is being referred to Diakonhjemmet Hospital for follow-up treatment. He has been experiencing chronic pain and stiffness in his hips and knees for several years now, which has significantly limited his mobility and ability to engage in daily activities. He has tried various treatments in the past, including medication and physical therapy, but has not experienced significant relief from his symptoms. He is not a candidate for surgery and is looking for alternative treatment options to manage his condition. He is fluent in Norwegian and able to walk unaided for short distances. He has no history of sudden death in his family and no first-degree relatives with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. He is motivated to participate in a web-based exercise program that includes peer support to improve his physical functioning and quality of life.

A 45-year-old female with recently diagnosed invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast. She has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. A formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor block from a prior biopsy of the primary tumor or lymph node is available, and the primary tumor is measurable by imaging modality. The patient is a candidate for neoadjuvant paclitaxel chemotherapy and has no metastatic disease based on staging work-up with CBC and liver function studies. She has adequate organ and marrow function, and is willing to undergo additional biopsy of the breast tumor or lymph node. The patient is willing to use effective contraception for the duration of the study and is willing and able to sign a written informed consent document. She does not have a history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to paclitaxel and is not on non-aspirin anti-coagulation or with documented bleeding disorders. She is not HIV positive, and does not have uncontrolled intercurrent illness or other malignancies requiring therapy. The patient is not pregnant and is not breastfeeding.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She had a routine ultrasound at 20 weeks of gestation, which showed an abnormality in the corpus callosum of the fetus. The patient has no relevant medical history, and her family history is negative for any genetic disorders. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is not currently taking any medications, and her prenatal care has been unremarkable so far. The patient has agreed to undergo amniocentesis to obtain fetal DNA for genetic testing, and has given informed consent to participate in this clinical trial to determine the frequency and type of genetic abnormalities found in cases of antenatal corpus callosum malformation.

The patient is a 25-year-old white male who is a nonsmoker and has a body mass index of 22 kg/m2. He is in good health with no significant medical history. He has no excessive hair growth on the volar surface of the forearm and has no dermatological conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, or dermatitis. He has clear skin on the forearm, free of any abnormalities, including tattoos, keloids, tumors, ulcers, burns, flaps, or grafts. He is able to avoid excessive tanning and is not currently using any lotions, oils, depilatory preparations, makeup, or other topical treatments on the arms. The patient has no history of asthma, severe allergic reactions to food or drugs, or adverse experiences related to the administration of current or investigational drugs. He is not currently using any prescription or nonprescription drugs regularly and is not a habitual or heavy consumer of coffee or caffeinated beverages. The patient is not a regular user of any illicit drugs or alcohol and has not been involved in testing an investigational drug in another clinical study within the last 4 weeks or 5 half-lives. The patient has no evidence of a clinically significant active infection, fever, or any cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, or neurological disorders. He is judged to be in good health on the basis of medical history, physical examination, and vital signs. The patient has given written informed consent and understands the procedures and agrees to comply with them for the entire length of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III colon cancer. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has a family history of colon cancer, with her father being diagnosed at age 65. She is currently working as a teacher and has no mobility issues. She has not started chemotherapy yet and is willing to stop taking any herbal supplements and current Vitamin D supplementation (Multivitamin with Vitamin D component is acceptable). She has baseline serum Vitamin D level below 52 ng/ml. She is willing to travel to Legacy Health/OHSU facility if necessary and agrees to attend study visits outside of standard of care visits, if necessary. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the protocol.

The patient is a 63-year-old Caucasian male who has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has a history of smoking, having smoked 1 pack per day for 35 years. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and fatigue for the past few months. His medical history is positive for hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well controlled with medication. He has not received any prior treatment for his lung cancer. He is willing to participate in clinical trials to help advance research and treatment options for lung cancer patients. His performance status is 1. His doctor has recommended him for this particular clinical trial.

50 year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) due to hypertension who underwent renal transplantation 9 months ago. He has been compliant with his medication regimen, including immunosuppressive therapy. However, he has been experiencing persistent elevated PTH levels despite treatment with cinacalcet. His PTH level remains elevated at 25 pmol/L with serum calcium level of 2.75 mmol/L and serum phosphorus level of 0.9 mmol/L. Cervical scintigraphy revealed multiple hyperactive parathyroid glands. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of subtotal parathyroidectomy using minimally invasive surgery versus cinacalcet for the treatment of persistent secondary hyperparathyroidism post renal transplantation. He has no contraindications to surgery and has provided signed informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 60 year old male who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his right knee for the past year. He was diagnosed with osteoarthritis and underwent a total knee replacement 3 years ago. However, he recently started experiencing pain and instability in the knee joint again. He was referred to an orthopedic surgeon who recommended a revision total knee arthroplasty. The patient has a history of hypertension and is on medication for it. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is retired and lives with his wife. He is able to perform activities of daily living independently but has difficulty walking long distances due to knee pain. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a body weight of 150 pounds and a body mass index within the range of 18.0 to 30.0 kg/m2. He is a non-smoker and does not use any tobacco or nicotine-containing products. He has no history of alcoholism, drug abuse or addiction within the last 24 months. His medical history is unremarkable, and he has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medications, nor any dietary or herbal supplements in the last 7 days prior to the first dose of IP. He has no known allergies to pseudoephedrine or ozanimod. He is willing to practice a highly effective method of contraception throughout the study until completion of the 75-day Safety Follow-up. He is able to comprehend and provide written informed consent, and is able to comply with the requirements of the study, including the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

25-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia by ICD-10 criteria with a PANSS total score of 65 and an EC factor score of 20. He has no history of intolerance or lack of response to quetiapine fumarate or haloperidol. He is not pregnant, lactating, or has no diagnosis of other mental disorders. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and has provided written informed consent. He has not used any cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors or inducers in the past 14 days and is not using any long-acting antipsychotics. He has no substance or alcohol dependence and no recent history of opiate, amphetamine, barbiturate, cocaine, cannabis, or hallucinogen abuse. His medical history is stable and he does not have any medical conditions that would affect absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of study treatment. He has not participated in another drug trial within the past 28 days and has not used antipsychotics, clozapine, or ECT in the past 28 days. He has not initiated quetiapine or haloperidol treatment within the past 30 days and has not used MAOI in the past 14 days. His complete blood count (CBC) with white blood cell (WBC) differential shows a neurotrophil count of > 1.5 x 109/L at screening. He does not have Diabetes Mellitus or any other unstable medical illness.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who has been living with type 2 diabetes for 8 years. He is currently taking metformin and glipizide to manage his blood sugar levels, and his HbA1c is well-controlled at 7.2%. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril to control his blood pressure. He quit smoking 2 years ago after smoking for 25 years. He has a family history of heart disease - his father had a heart attack at the age of 60. He leads a sedentary lifestyle and has a body mass index (BMI) of 32. He has not had any chest pain or other symptoms of heart disease. He has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications or supplements. He has regular check-ups with his primary care physician and endocrinologist. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help identify his risk of developing coronary artery disease.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years with her partner, without any success. She has regular menstrual cycles and no significant medical history. Both the patient and her partner have undergone fertility testing with normal results. The patient's AMH level is 1.5 ng/mL, indicating good ovarian reserve. Hysterosalpingography confirms that her tubes are patent. The couple has not undergone any previous trials of IUI with the ANTIUI protocol. The couple meets all the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is interested in participating.

A 32 year old woman comes to the clinic with complaints of heavy and painful periods along with lower abdominal pain. She has been diagnosed with uterine leiomyoma of 12 mm in diameter detected by transvaginal ultrasound. She has no history of myomectomy, chronic systemic diseases, malignancy, or adenomyosis. She is currently not pregnant or lactating, and has not had an abortion or pregnancy loss in the last 6 months. She is not taking any vitamin D supplements or oral contraceptives/hormonal agents in the last 3 months. She is within the reproductive age range of 25-50 years. The patient's family history, daily sunshine exposure, clothing preferences, and education level will be evaluated during the study. Blood samples will be taken to analyze vitamin D, calcium, magnesium, phosphorus, thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), hemoglobin (hb), hematocrit (htc), platelet (plt), and albumin in order to compare the biochemical markers between the study groups.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been experiencing nasal obstruction for the past 3 years. He was diagnosed with nasal septal deviation by his primary care physician, and referred to the Stanford Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Clinic for further management. He reports difficulty breathing through his nose, particularly at night, and has tried various over-the-counter nasal sprays with little relief. He has never had any nasal or septal surgery, nor has he used any intranasal steroids or systemic steroids in the past. He is not pregnant or actively breastfeeding. His medical history is unremarkable, and he does not take any medications regularly. He works as a software engineer and enjoys hiking and playing basketball in his free time. His NOSE score at the initial visit was 60. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to use both drugs as instructed. He has been informed of the possibility of surgical intervention after completing the study drugs, but would prefer to avoid surgery if possible.

The patient is an 11-year-old boy who was diagnosed with type 3 Gaucher disease two years ago. He has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, anemia, and easy bruising. The patient has moderate splenomegaly and thrombocytopenia, with a platelet count of 85,000/µL. He has not received any treatment for Gaucher disease in the past 12 months. The patient is not currently undergoing splenectomy. His parents are willing to use a medically acceptable method of contraception during the study if the patient is female. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent that has been approved by the Institutional Review Board/Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC).

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago and underwent a combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy for 6 months. She reports experiencing persistent fatigue that has severely affected her ability to perform daily activities. Her fatigue score on the FACIT-Fatigue scale is 32. She does not have any pre-existing anemia. Currently, she is not receiving any cancer treatment and is not suffering from any other physical or psychological impairments. She is not pregnant and does not have any confounding underlying medical illnesses. Her family history is negative for cancer or any other chronic illnesses. She is interested in participating in the study to investigate whether systematic exposure to light can reduce her cancer-related fatigue.

The patient is a 32-year-old HIV-positive male who has been on a first-line cART regimen with three antiretroviral drugs for the past two years. His most recent viral load test showed that his HIV-RNA is less than 50 copies/mL, and he has not experienced any virological failures or blips. He is interested in switching to a NRTI-sparing regimen to minimize long-term side effects associated with ART. He has no history of chronic hepatitis B, and he is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to use highly effective contraception methods during heterosexual intercourse or practice sexual abstinence for the duration of the study and for 30 days following discontinuation of study drugs. He has no known hypersensitivity to B/F/TAF FDC tablets, DTG, and 3TC, and he is not currently taking any medications that are contraindicated for the study. He is willing to comply with protocol requirements and to participate in the study to evaluate inflammatory and immunological changes of HIV-positive patients switching to DTG dual regimen compared to those switching to a triple drugs regimen (B/F/TAF).

A 40-year-old male who sustained a moderate to severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) in a motor vehicle accident 8 months ago. He has experienced weight gain since the injury, and his BMI is 28. He has been cleared by his physician to participate in the Group Lifestyle Balance™ for Individuals with Traumatic Brain Injury (GLB-TBI) program. He is fluent in English and has a smartphone he is willing to use for the program. He has no history of diabetes or eating disorders. Due to his injury, he experiences some cognitive difficulties, but they do not affect his ability to participate in the program.

A 55 year old woman has been diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) and has had recurrent disease in remission. She has received previous chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her disease has returned. She is considered to be a high risk candidate for conventional myeloablative transplantation. She is a 5-6/6 HLA-matched sibling or 9-10/10 matched unrelated donor. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80% and she is able to perform most activities of daily living. Her pulmonary-diffusing capacity is 45% and her cardiac ejection fraction is 50%. She has no serologic evidence of infection with the human immunodeficiency virus and is able to give informed consent. She has no history of psychiatric illness or mental deficiency. Her liver function and serum creatinine are within normal limits. She has no active infection or CNS metastasis. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive RIST with fludarabine and busulfan to treat her AML.

8-year-old boy with suspected sepsis, admitted to the hospital with fever, tachycardia, and hypotension. He has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and was recently treated with antibiotics for a skin infection. Upon admission, he required mechanical ventilation and was started on vasoactive medications for cardiovascular dysfunction. He has no known bleeding disorders and has not undergone any recent surgeries. He has no known history of bone marrow transplant and does not have end-stage renal disease. His parents have consented to transfusion of blood products if necessary.

As this is a clinical trial focused on mentally fatigued soccer players, the patient is a 20-year-old male university soccer player who has been playing soccer since his senior school years. He has been experiencing mental fatigue and difficulty in decision-making skills during his recent games. He is not currently taking any medication and reports no known disease or sleep disorder. The patient has normal vision and is not color blind. He is willing to participate in the study and agrees to view nature photos as part of the intervention.

A 62-year-old Caucasian male presents with a recent diagnosis of metastatic colorectal cancer. The cancer has spread to his liver and lungs. He has no significant medical history besides this diagnosis. The patient underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the cancer to be KRAS wild-type.
