He is currently in good health, with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve his prognosis. He is willing to undergo treatment with folinic acid + fluorouracil + irinotecan (FOLFIRI) plus cetuximab or folinic acid + fluorouracil + oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) plus cetuximab as first-line therapy. The patient understands that he will be monitored every 8 weeks for efficacy and will continue treatment until progressive disease or unacceptable adverse events occur. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and meets all other eligibility criteria for the APEC-Study.

The patient is a 47-year-old male presenting to the gastroenterology clinic with a history of chronic constipation, bloating, and abdominal discomfort for the past 6 months. He has never undergone a colonoscopy before and is willing to participate in a research study for his diagnostic colonoscopy examination. His medical history is significant for high blood pressure, which is well controlled with medication. He denies any history of cardiac disease, obstructive lesions in the colon, or previous colon resection. He is not experiencing fecal obstruction and is hemodynamically stable.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 42 kg/m². She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are currently managed with medication. She has been recommended to undergo biliointestinal bypass (BIBP) surgery to help with her weight loss. She has never smoked, and her lung function tests have been normal. She does not have a history of asthma or any other respiratory conditions. She has been advised by her doctor to consider participating in a clinical trial evaluating the use of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) postoperatively to prevent acute respiratory failure.

A 9-year-old girl was brought to the emergency department with a laceration on her left leg. The wound was approximately 5 cm in length and required primary closure. She has a past medical history of asthma, but she is not currently experiencing any symptoms. She is not taking any medications regularly. Her vitals are within normal limits with a heart rate of 90 beats per minute and blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg. The patient and her parents have been informed about the study and have given consent for her participation. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is randomized to receive either atropine or placebo as an adjunct to ketamine sedation during the procedure.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman diagnosed with HER2-positive early breast cancer. She underwent surgical excision of the tumor and received neo-adjuvant chemotherapy with no evidence of residual, locally recurrent or metastatic disease after completion of surgery and chemotherapy. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. She has no history of other malignancies or serious cardiovascular disease. The patient's liver and renal function are normal. She has never received doxorubicin or epirubicin. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will be available for the planned 18 cycles of treatment.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been experiencing tinnitus for over a year. He describes his tinnitus as a high-pitched ringing sound that is present in both ears. He also reports having difficulty hearing in noisy environments and has noticed a gradual decrease in his hearing ability over time. He has not sought any treatment for his tinnitus and has no history of ear infections or trauma. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. Upon examination, his otoscopy is normal, but his audiogram shows mild-to-moderate sensorineural hearing loss in both ears. He agrees to participate in the study and fulfills the inclusion criteria.

30-year-old woman with a history of persistent asthma, currently receiving daily treatment with inhaled corticosteroids up to the maximum dose per day indicated in the product label. She has not had an acute asthma attack requiring hospitalization in the past 6 months or an emergency room visit within the past 6 weeks. The patient has an FEV1 at Visit 1 of 70% of predicted normal and demonstrates an increase of ≥12% and ≥200 mL in FEV1 over her pre-bronchodilator. She does not have a smoking history of greater than 10 pack years, seasonal allergies likely to deteriorate during the study period, or any other clinically significant conditions that may interfere with study conduct or patient safety.

Patient is a 45yo male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection of genotype 1. He has previously undergone treatment with interferon-alpha and ribavirin but was not successful. He has been advised to abstain from alcohol consumption for the duration of the study. The patient does not have cirrhosis or decompensated liver disease. The liver function tests show AST and ALT levels within the normal range. The platelet count is normal and there is no evidence of diabetes mellitus. The patient has not abused alcohol or drugs within the past year. The patient is interested in participating in the pilot study to explore the safety and anti-viral efficacy of infused ascorbic acid in HCV genotype 1 hepatitis.

The patient is a 3-year-old male child who has been coughing and experiencing difficulty in breathing for the past 2 days. His mother reports that he has had a fever for the past 3 days, which has been treated with paracetamol. The child has no history of asthma or other chronic respiratory conditions. His vital signs are as follows: temperature of 38.5°C, heart rate of 120 beats/min, respiratory rate of 32 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation of 91% on room air. On physical examination, the child has bilateral chest crackles and subcostal retractions. His weight is 12 kg, height is 95 cm, and head circumference is 48 cm. Laboratory results show a white blood cell count of 12,000/mm3 and a C-reactive protein level of 10 mg/L. The child is diagnosed with acute lower respiratory infection and admitted to the hospital. He meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of inhaled corticosteroids in addition to standard treatment for children hospitalized with ALRI.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer that has not responded to hormone therapy. He has no symptoms directly attributable to metastatic disease and no central nervous system metastases or carcinomatous meningitis. His performance status is ECOG 1 and his life expectancy is at least 12 weeks. He has no history of other malignancy within the past 5 years except basal cell skin cancer, no uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, and no other medical or psychiatric conditions that would preclude study. He has not received chemotherapy or hormonal therapy within the last 4 weeks and has not received longer-acting hormonal agents such as bicalutamide within the last 6 weeks. He has not received immunotherapy within the last 4 weeks and is not currently receiving any other concurrent investigational agents. His bilirubin levels are no greater than 1.5 mg/dL and his creatinine levels are no greater than 2 times the upper limit of normal. He has no uncontrolled high blood pressure, unstable angina, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmias, or myocardial infarction in the past 6 months.

A 15-year-old male teenager presents with a history of obesity with a body mass index (BMI) of 36. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg and his fasting glucose is 110 mg/dL. His liver function tests are within normal limits. He has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He reports feeling self-conscious about his weight and has struggled with maintaining a healthy diet and regular exercise routine. He is interested in participating in a weight management program and is open to telehealth options. He speaks fluent English and his parents are also fluent in English. He is able to stand on a scale independently without assistance.

This is a 32 year-old female who is currently 37 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has a BMI of 24 and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far. She is scheduled for a planned cesarean section due to a breech presentation of the fetus. She has no history of bleeding disorders or use of anticoagulants other than low-dose heparin. She has a preoperative hemoglobin level of 12 mg/dL. She is able to read and understand English. She has not had any formal chronic pain management within the past year. She has no history of chronic pain syndrome.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis for the past 10 years. He has experienced unpredictable recurrent attacks of neurologic dysfunction followed by partial recovery. His current EDSS score is 6.0. Despite receiving high dose prednisone, beta interferon and glatiramer acetate, his symptoms and manifestations of MS activity have not responded to conventional treatment. He has not received prior lymphoid irradiation and has no history of hypersensitivity to murine proteins or E.coli derived proteins. He has no history of lack of compliance with medical care or any medical or psychiatric conditions which would compromise his ability to comply with the protocol. He has no evidence of myelodysplasia or an active malignancy. He is not receiving concurrent beta interferon therapy or high dose prednisone. He has significant organ toxicity including a creatinine level greater than twice normal; glomerular filtration rate less than 40 ml/min. His FEV1 or FVC is less than 75% predicted; DLCO is less than 50% predicted. He has a significant cardiac dysfunction defined as a shortened ejection fraction (less than 26%). His hepatic transaminases are greater than two times normal; total bilirubin is greater than 3.0 mg/dl. He is willing to undergo collection of sufficient numbers of HSCs to meet protocol requirements, i.e. 3X10e6 CD34+ cells. He is willing to use effective contraception for a minimum of 12 months post transplant.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has no history of psychiatric disorder or suicidal behavior. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. Her labs and ECG are normal. She is currently practicing acceptable forms of birth control and is willing to continue throughout the trial. The patient has not taken any investigational product within the last 30 days and has not been exposed to more than 4 new chemical entities in the last 12 months. She is not pregnant or nursing and has tested negative for Hepatitis and HIV. She is interested in participating in the PAXIL CR Bioequivalence Study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. He is currently taking metformin to manage his blood sugar levels. Despite his medication, he has been experiencing some difficulty with his blood sugar control and has noticed some mild symptoms such as increased thirst and fatigue. He has no known allergies to medications and has not taken any PPAR-gamma agonists. The patient is otherwise in good health and has no significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of sitagliptin in managing his diabetes and improving his cardiovascular health.

Patient is a 32-year-old man from the United States who had a closed head injury of moderate severity (Glasgow coma scale score of 11) due to a car accident 6 months ago. He was discharged from the hospital after 2 weeks and has since been experiencing persistent depressive symptoms, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities. He has never had depression before the accident. He has been on sertraline 50mg daily for the last 4 weeks, but he did not observe any significant improvement in his symptoms. His family has noticed that he has also been having difficulty with memory, attention, and executive function tasks. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. He is currently employed as an accountant and lives with his wife and two children.

A 57-year-old male patient was diagnosed with esophageal cancer (adenocarcinoma). He has no significant past medical history. He underwent an endoscopic ultrasound and spiral CT scan which confirmed localized, non-metastatic disease (T2, N0). The total disease length (primary and lymph nodes) is less than 10 cm by EUS. The patient is not suitable for surgery due to his poor health condition. He has no metastatic disease. He has no significant extension of the tumor into the stomach. His WHO performance status is 1. His absolute neutrophil count, white blood cell count, platelet count, hemoglobin, serum bilirubin, ALT/AST, alkaline phosphatase, glomerular filtration rate, and cardiac ejection fraction are all within normal limits. He has no hearing impairment or sensory-motor neuropathy > grade 2. He has no major trauma within the past 4 weeks. He has not been exposed to sorivudine and analogues for the past 4 weeks. He has not received major surgery, monoclonal antibody or radiotherapy for the past 4 weeks, 4 weeks, and 3 months, respectively. He has not received any prior treatment for invasive esophageal carcinoma or gastroesophageal junction carcinoma.

This is a 55-year-old woman who underwent a screening colonoscopy at Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) within the last 9 months with removal of at least one adenoma. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of aspirin as a potential chemopreventive agent to reduce the risk of colorectal cancer. She is not currently taking aspirin or any non-aspirin non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) at any dose at least three times a week during the two months prior to randomization. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, liver or kidney disease, bleeding diathesis, or any prior diagnosis of gastrointestinal cancer. Additionally, she is not receiving any other investigational agents and has no history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to aspirin. She is willing to abstain from non-protocol use of aspirin or NSAIDs and provide blood, urine, or stool samples or colon biopsies during the study. She understands the study requirements and is able to comply with them. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and agrees to use adequate contraception if she is of child-bearing potential. She is able to swallow pills and is not taking any anticoagulant agent or antiplatelet agent.

A 22-year-old Caucasian male presents with a history of wearing soft contact lenses for the past 5 years. He reports wearing his contact lenses for at least 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. He has no history of any ocular or systemic allergies or diseases that may interfere with contact lens wear. His best corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. His vertex-corrected distance refraction allows a plano over-refraction with the available contact lens powers of -1.00 to -6.00 Diopters (D) in each eye, and his refractive astigmatism is less than or equal to 1.00 D in each eye. He has no history of ocular or interocular surgery, and no current or planned ocular infection. He has had no previous diagnosis of binocular vision abnormality or strabismus. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the short-term clinical performance of two FDA-approved contact lenses.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. The patient reports that he has been experiencing shortness of breath with exertion and fatigue for the past 6 months. He has also noticed some swelling in his legs and ankles. His physical exam is significant for jugular venous distention, bibasilar crackles, and lower extremity edema. His lab studies showed: N-terminal pro b-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP): 2100 pg/mL, Troponin I: 0.05 ng/mL, Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 60 mL/min/1.73m2. His echocardiogram showed a thickened interventricular septum measuring 16 mm and a posterior wall thickness measuring 14 mm. His ejection fraction was 50%. Based on these findings, the patient was diagnosed with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.

An 82-year-old male resident of Olmsted County, who lives alone in his own home. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has a history of falls in the past six months, with one resulting in a hip fracture that required surgery. He has difficulty getting up from a chair, walking long distances, and climbing stairs. He has no history of cognitive impairment or depression. He manages his own medications, but he often forgets to take them on time. He has a daughter who lives nearby and helps him with grocery shopping and transportation to medical appointments. He speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who presented with abdominal pain and weight loss. She has a history of smoking for 40 years and has a family history of pancreatic cancer (her mother). She denies any other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Physical examination reveals a palpable mass in the epigastric region with no other remarkable findings. Laboratory results show mild anemia and elevated liver function tests. Imaging studies reveal a mass in the pancreatic head and multiple liver lesions suspicious for metastasis. A biopsy of the pancreatic mass confirms the diagnosis of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial and has a good Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status. She is willing to undergo a core needle biopsy for biomarker analysis and has no contraindications for treatment with either modified folfirinox or gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel. She is also willing to participate in the laboratory components of the trial, including molecular profiling and drug testing sensitivity.

A 28-year-old male was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) a year ago. The patient underwent chemotherapy, which resulted in complete remission. Unfortunately, the patient relapsed after 6 months and received a second round of chemotherapy, which was also not successful. The patient is currently in a high-risk category and experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and fever. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, and there is no known family history of cancer. The patient has not undergone allogeneic stem cell transplantation or any treatment with T cell inhibitors. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Score of 80 and meets all the other inclusion criteria for the clinical trial. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided voluntary informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with HIV during her pregnancy. She is currently in her second trimester and is worried about the risk of transmitting the virus to her baby during delivery or breastfeeding. She has been referred to a specialized clinic for HIV-positive pregnant women and has been advised to start taking antiretroviral drugs to reduce the amount of virus in her body. The patient is planning to exclusively breastfeed her baby for six months and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of pregnancy on drug exposure and HIV transmission to the baby. She understands the study information and is committed to complying with the follow-up schedule. The patient has no other medical conditions or illnesses that would exclude her from participating in the study.

50-year-old male with a history of hyperlipidemia and currently on stable statin therapy for the past 6 weeks. The patient has an LDL-C of 120 mg/dL and has been struggling to achieve optimal cholesterol levels despite previous attempts to modify his diet and increase physical activity. The patient has no history of coronary heart disease or any risk factors for CHD. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine whether the addition of SLx-4090 to his current statin therapy can effectively reduce his LDL-C levels.

32yo male with newly diagnosed HIV-1 infection, presenting with fever, night sweats, and lymphadenopathy. Patient has no prior history of treatment with antiretroviral therapy or non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) and has never been exposed to Saquinavir or Nelfinavir. Patient has a viral load of 75,000 copies/ml by Amplicor assay. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares the efficacy of three different anti-HIV drug combinations containing Saquinavir Soft Gelatin Capsules. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been diagnosed with a meniscus tear in his right knee. He has been experiencing pain and swelling in the knee joint for several months, which has affected his ability to participate in sports and physical activities. MRI imaging confirmed the meniscus tear, and the orthopedic surgeon recommended a surgical procedure to repair the tear. The patient has been informed about the two techniques available for the procedure - one involving abrasion of the suture area before suturing and the other without abrasion. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to compare the outcomes of both techniques. The patient has no other significant medical history or comorbidities.

The patient is a 3-year-old child with a diagnosis of congenital heart disease who is scheduled to undergo operative repair with the use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). The child's parent/legal guardian has provided written informed consent to participate in a study investigating the presence of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) and high-mobility group-1 protein (HMG-1) in the serum and myocardium of children undergoing CPB. Prior to surgery, the child will have an assessment of cardiac function by echocardiography and blood assays for various cytokines, including TNF, interleukin-6, interleukin-8, interleukin-10, complement 3a, MIF, and HMG-1. Cardiac tissue, removed as a planned part of the procedure, will be assayed for MIF and apoptosis. The patient will be admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) post-operatively for routine care, and blood will be obtained for cytokine assays at various time points. The study aims to correlate the presence or absence of MIF and HMG-1 with clinical outcomes after CPB. The patient must be under 5 years of age and have written consent from a parent/legal guardian. The patient cannot have evidence of ongoing infection or known immunodeficiency.

63-year-old male diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's Disease (PD) for the past 8 years. The patient is currently being treated with levodopa, but has been experiencing motor fluctuations and has a minimum of 3 hours of "Off" time per day. The patient is cognitively intact and is able to safely and effectively manage the drug delivery system and the diaries. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help find new treatment options for PD. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Gastric ulcer.

A 43-year-old woman has been experiencing abnormal vaginal bleeding for several months. She has no history of cancer and is otherwise healthy. She underwent surgical curettage and pathology confirmed endometrial adenocarcinoma G1. She is premenopausal and has no children. She wishes to preserve her fertility and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that would allow her to undergo fertility-sparing surgery or ovarian preservation surgery. She is willing to be randomized into one of the three groups and is willing to be closely monitored for therapeutic efficacy, safety, and quality of life during the study.

58 y/o male with a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson Disease (PD) determined by a board-certified neurologist with specialty training in movement disorders. The patient presents with urinary urgency with or without urgency incontinence usually with increased daytime frequency and nocturia. The patient has an ICIQ-OAB Symptom Score of 8, which indicates clinically significant symptoms of OAB, defined as presence of urinary urgency with or without urgency incontinence usually with increased daytime frequency and nocturia in the absence of infection or other obvious pathology. The patient has no significant cognitive impairment, as indicated by a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score of 20, which is above the recommended diagnostic cutpoint for dementia in PD. The patient has not undergone previous intensive pelvic floor muscle exercise training and does not have clinically significant depression as measured by a Geriatric Depression Scale-Short Form score of 5. The patient is not using an indwelling urinary catheter, and the post-void residual (PVR) urine measurement by bladder ultrasound is within normal limits. The patient does not have severe uterine prolapse past the vaginal introitus and has well-controlled diabetes defined by a hemoglobin A1c (HgbA1c) of 7.5% within the last 3 months. The patient does not have chronic renal failure and is not on hemodialysis. The patient does not have genitourinary cancer with ongoing surgical or external beam radiation treatment. The patient has not undergone previous artificial urinary sphincter, sling procedure, or implanted sacral neuromodulation device, and does not have a history of bladder-injection of botulinum toxin in the last 12 months. The patient does not have any unstable health condition expected to result in hospitalization or death within the next 3 months. The patient is not hypersensitive to drug class and does not have a contraindication to the study drug (solifenacin) including narrow-angle glaucoma, history of gastric retention, or history of acute urinary retention requiring catheterization. The patient is not currently taking a bladder relaxant and has been off of alpha-blockers for at least 4 weeks. The patient is not taking dutasteride or finasteride and has been off of these medications for at least 6 months.

A 40-year-old woman was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) 6 months ago. She received standard first-line chemotherapy but unfortunately did not respond to treatment. PET/CT scan showed progressive disease with multiple lymph nodes involvement. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no known allergies. She has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past 5 years. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Her recent blood work shows an absolute neutrophil count of 1500/μL, platelet count of 70,000/μL, total bilirubin of 1.1x institutional upper limit of normal (IULN), AST of 1.5x IULN and ALT of 1.2x IULN. Her creatinine level is within normal limits. Her albumin level is 3.5 g/dL. Her prothrombin time (PT) and PTT are within normal limits. She is not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She has no history of active hepatitis B or C infections, known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or known to be positive for HCV RNA or HBsAg (HBV surface antigen). She has no history of or active central nervous system (CNS) involvement by lymphoma. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests and other study procedures and is able to understand and sign a written informed consent document.

Patient is a 30-year-old nonsmoking woman with no history of cardiovascular disease, liver or renal disease, diabetes, lung disease, or cancer in the last 5 years. She has a BMI of 24 and normal blood pressure with systolic blood pressure averaging <120 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure averaging <80 mm Hg. Her total and LDL-cholesterol levels are within normal limits for her age and sex. Her fasting triglycerides are < 150 mg/dL and her fasting blood sugar is < 100 mg/dL. She is not taking any hormones or drugs known to affect lipid metabolism or blood pressure. She is willing to abstain from alcohol and dietary supplements during the study and to consume all study foods as instructed. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with invasive breast carcinoma. After discussing her options with her healthcare provider, she has decided to undergo a mastectomy with immediate implant reconstruction. The healthcare provider has determined that the patient will need postoperative radiotherapy following the mastectomy. The patient is in good health, has a Performance Status of 1, and is geographically accessible for follow-up. She is affiliated with the French national social security system. The patient has not had any previous history of breast cancer or radiotherapy to the breast. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer and has a family history of cancer. Her mother and grandmother both had breast cancer, and her maternal aunt had ovarian cancer. She is concerned that her cancer may have a genetic component and is interested in participating in a study that may identify genetic mutations that could lead to cancer. She is willing to provide biospecimens for research and has no physical, cognitive or psychiatric conditions that would interfere with her ability to provide informed consent. She is also interested in having her family members participate in the study to see if they are at risk for developing cancer as well.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year. She has undergone several fertility tests and has been diagnosed with male factor infertility due to her partner's low sperm count. She has undergone in vitro fertilization (IVF) and has several cleavage stage embryos that are eligible for cryopreservation. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of vitrification versus slow cooling for preserving embryos for later transfers. She is a suitable candidate as she is under 35 years of age and has no other exclusions. She is willing to undergo single embryo transfer and this is her first IVF cycle.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been suffering from severe plaque type psoriasis for the past 8 months, affecting approximately 20% of her total body surface area. She has previously tried topical steroid creams but has not seen significant improvement. She is currently not on any systemic therapy for psoriasis. Her recent lab works show: WBC count: 4800/cu mm Platelet count: 120,000/microliters Serum creatinine: 1.2 mg/dl Total bilirubin: 1.5 mg/dl AST (SGOT): 30 U/L ALT (SGPT): 35 U/L Her recent chest x-ray and purified protein derivative (PPD) test were negative. She is not pregnant and is using adequate contraception.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with severe anorexia nervosa for more than 12 months. She has been experiencing low bone mineral density, which has been confirmed by a Z-Score of less than -2.5 or T-Score below -2.5 in at least one of the assessed localizations (lumbar spine L1 - L4, total hip, femoral neck), without any previous fragility fracture. She has been an inpatient or outpatient at the Centre for Eating Disorders at the Clinic for Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the University Hospital of Zurich. She has no metabolic bone diseases other than primary osteoporosis, no pre-existing hypercalcemia, no severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 ml/min), no prior external beam or implant radiation therapy to the skeleton, no skeletal malignancies or bone metastases, and no unknown elevation of serum alkaline phosphatase. She has no severe psychiatric diseases other than AN, drug addiction, HIV positive status, or open epiphyses. She is willing to participate in the study and can understand the aims of the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has no history of chemotherapy or immunotherapy for advanced or metastatic disease. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of heart disease or other significant medical conditions. He has no central nervous system or bone metastases. His renal function is normal. He has no malabsorption syndrome and is able to take oral medication. He has no other active malignancies and has not had any cancer within the last 5 years.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver due to long-term alcohol abuse. During a routine imaging test, a 2 cm hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) was discovered. The patient has no other significant medical history and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is interested in pursuing surgical resection or radiofrequency destruction for their HCC. They understand the potential risks of the procedures and are willing to participate in this clinical trial to receive transarterial radioembolization prior to surgery or radiofrequency destruction. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy from a rural area in Myanmar who presents to the local health clinic with fever and chills for the past 3 days. He complains of headache and body aches. He has a history of malaria and has been treated with chloroquine in the past. On examination, he has a temperature of 38.5°C, a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, and a pulse rate of 110 beats per minute. His spleen is palpable and enlarged. A rapid diagnostic test for malaria is positive for Plasmodium falciparum. His weight is 30 kg. The patient is accompanied by his mother who gives informed consent for him to participate in the clinical trial.

42-year-old male with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection who has been receiving lamivudine treatment for the past year. There is confirmation of the presence of the rtM204I/V mutation with or without the rtL180M mutation, which confers resistance to lamivudine. The patient's HBV DNA levels are ≥10^3 IU/mL. The patient has not received any other oral HBV therapy with approved nucleotide and/or nucleoside therapy or other investigational agents for HBV infection. The patient has not undergone interferon or pegylated interferon therapy within 6 months of the screening visit. The patient has no evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma, is negative for coinfection with hepatitis C virus, HIV, or hepatitis D virus. The patient has no significant renal, cardiovascular, pulmonary, or neurological disease. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the study drugs, the metabolites, or formulation excipients. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and is able to comply with the study requirements.

A 60-year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presents with symptoms of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has been diagnosed with sinus node dysfunction and has been recommended for a pacemaker implantation. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a past history of smoking. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has had documented episodes of AF within the last 6 months. The patient is willing to undergo a randomized, parallel, single-blinded multi-center study to compare the long term clinical outcomes of atrial pacing and the long term effect of the AF Suppression algorithm. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the prescribed follow-up tests and schedule of evaluations. The patient does not have a pacemaker or ICD and does not have a reversible etiology of AF.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who was diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) two years ago. He has been undergoing regular follow-up care at the Norris Cotton Cancer Center of DHMC. The patient has been feeling generally well, with occasional fatigue and some mild lymph node swelling. The patient has not received any cytotoxic drug, oral or intravenous steroid or targeted antibody therapy for their CLL or any other hematologic malignancy or disease process within the past 2 months. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient is willing to participate in the study and donate a blood sample for research purposes.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 2 years. She has been taking Celebrex for the past 6 months, but has been experiencing joint pain and stiffness. Her average daily pain score is 7 out of 10 on the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently well controlled with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She works as a part-time accountant and enjoys gardening as a hobby. She is willing to take part in a clinical trial to see if ULTRACET® (tramadol 37.5 mg and acetaminophen 325 mg) as add-on therapy can provide additional pain relief. She has not taken Tramadol HCl within the last 30 days and is not currently taking any other medications for pain relief.

A 13-month-old healthy baby girl is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial for an investigational measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine. She has not received any of these vaccines before and has not had any previous infections or exposure to measles, mumps, rubella, varicella, or zoster. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has not undergone any immunosuppressive therapy. She has never had a seizure and does not have any allergies to sorbitol, gelatin, or neomycin. She has not had a fever in the last 3 days. The parents are interested in enrolling their child in the study and are willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who was brought to the Assessment Center of Mulago Hospital by his mother due to cough and fast breathing. The child has no known medical conditions and has not been hospitalized before. His mother reports that he has been coughing for the last 2 days and has had fever intermittently. The child's temperature at presentation was 38.5 degrees Celsius. The mother reports that the child has not been on any antibiotics for the past 48 hours. The child's respiratory rate at presentation was 45 breaths per minute, which is above the age-specific cut-off according to the WHO criteria. The child was enrolled in the study following informed consent from the mother. The study nurse drew 5 mls of blood from the ante cubital fossa for a complete blood count and blood cultures. The child was also subjected to sputum induction to obtain a sample for gram stain, ZN stain, and culture and sensitivity. Rapid HIV antibody test was done, which turned out negative. The child was randomized to receive either oral amoxicillin (25 mg/kg/dose) or cotrimoxazole (trimethoprim 8 mg/kg and sulphamethoxazole 40 mg/kg) and was followed up on day 3 and 5 of treatment. The mother was instructed on how to give the study drugs and was asked to return to the clinic on day 3 and 5 of treatment.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer through a biopsy. He has not received any prior treatment for prostate cancer, including hormonal therapy. His cancer is deemed to be organ confined and he is scheduled to undergo radical prostatectomy. The patient has no major calcification noted during the TRUS procedure. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. The patient has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

8-year-old M who is enrolled in Colorado Access RCCO with a history of receiving some (but not all) of his recommended immunizations. He is up-to-date on his DTaP and IPV vaccines, but is missing his MMR and Varicella vaccines. His parents are concerned about the safety and efficacy of vaccines and have been hesitant to get the remaining vaccines for their child. They are interested in participating in a study that could help them make an informed decision regarding their child's immunizations. Past Medical History: - Allergic Rhinitis - Mild Eczema - No significant past medical history.

Patient is a 50-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of refractory hematologic malignancy. He has been previously treated with available therapies without success. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has adequate hepatic and renal function. The patient does not have an active CNS malignancy but has a history of prolonged QT interval. He does not have significant GI or liver disease and does not have any other serious concurrent illness or medical condition.

56 yo F with a 5-year history of rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed per the 2010 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria. She is currently being treated with methotrexate (15 mg/week) and has persistent active disease. She has no history of autoimmune disease other than RA and no comorbidities that would interfere with the study. She has never been treated with a B cell-depleting biologic agent and is not currently in ARA functional class IV disease of ACR Revised Steinbrocker Classification. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve her disease control and help advance medical research.

The patient is a healthy 28-year-old woman who has not previously received any vaccine against typhoid fever. She has no history of autoimmune disorders or any other known immune system impairment. She is currently not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. She has not participated in any clinical trials involving investigational products in the past 30 days and does not plan to participate in any other clinical trials during the study. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and has no history of substance or alcohol abuse. She has not received any vaccines within 4 weeks prior to enrollment and does not plan to receive any vaccines within 4 weeks of the study vaccine. She has no known allergies to vaccine components and is willing to use birth control measures for the entire study duration. She has given written consent to participate in the study after the nature of the study has been explained to her.

54F, married, daughter of a cancer patient. The patient's mother was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago and since then, the patient has taken on the role of primary caregiver. She is retired and lives with her husband. The patient reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed with her caregiving duties, which has led to difficulty sleeping and fatigue. She has never practiced Qigong before and is interested in learning more about mind-body exercises to help manage her stress and improve her physical and emotional health. She speaks English fluently and is able to read and write in English. She reports a distress level of 5 on the NCCN Distress Thermometer. She does not have any unstable illnesses or psychiatric disorders and is able to walk continuously for 15 minutes. She is not currently engaged in any regular exercise routine.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with severe osteoarthritis in his right knee, resulting in significant pain and disability. He has no history of trauma to the knee or any other significant medical conditions. He has tried non-surgical treatments, such as physical therapy and pain medications, but has not experienced significant improvement. He is willing to undergo total knee replacement surgery and is open to the possibility of participating in a clinical trial comparing the use of the VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution versus manual instrumentation. He is able to provide voluntary, written informed consent and is able to understand and comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits. He is fluent in English and able to complete all required patient-reported outcomes in English. He does not have any active infections or other conditions that would make the procedure unjustifiable. He has not participated in any clinical trials or investigations in the last three months and is not currently involved in any personal injury litigation.

60-year-old female referred to Westmead Hospital Endoscopy Unit for an endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) of a colonic polyp reported to be ≥20mm in size. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She is currently on lisinopril and atorvastatin for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia, respectively. She is allergic to codeine and has a history of gastrointestinal upset with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). She has given informed consent to be enrolled in the trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with SLE six years ago. She has been experiencing active SLE symptoms with a SLE Disease Activity Index (SLEDAI) score of 6 at screening. She has tried several treatments for SLE in the past, but none have been successful. She is currently experiencing joint pain, skin rashes, and fatigue. The patient has a history of smoking but has quit for the past two years. She works as a part-time receptionist at a small office and takes care of her two young children at home. Her medical history includes a previous episode of pneumonia that was treated with antibiotics. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no known history of malignancy or other serious health conditions. Her BMI is 25 and her blood pressure is normal. She is interested in participating in this study to explore new treatment options for her SLE symptoms.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few months. She visited her doctor, who diagnosed her with gallstones and recommended surgery to remove her gallbladder. She was referred to a hospital where she was informed about a clinical trial for a new surgical robot - the Chinese Micro Hand S surgical robot. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial as she is between 18 and 65 years old, has a BMI of 22 kg/m2, and has been diagnosed with cholecystitis. She has no previous relevant operation history, no mental illness, and is classified as ASA I. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is generally in good health. She has some concerns about the surgery as it is a new technology, but is willing to participate in the clinical trial as it may provide her with a better outcome than traditional surgery. She has been fully informed about the trial and has signed the informed consent.

Patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU due to severe sepsis with circulatory failure requiring norepinephrine support. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels, but no previous hospitalizations or surgeries. Upon admission, his SOFA score was 10 and his plasma albumin level was 18 g/L. He is currently receiving broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy and mechanical ventilation. Despite aggressive management, his blood pressure remains unstable and he requires increasing doses of norepinephrine to maintain target mean arterial pressure. The patient is able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) based on the McDonald criteria three years ago. She has not taken any disease-modifying therapies since the last 3 months and her current EDSS score is 3.5. She presents to the clinic with occasional episodes of numbness, tingling, and weakness in her right lower limb. She has a history of optic neuritis in the left eye that resolved without any visual impairment. Her MRI shows one gadolinium-enhancing lesion in the periventricular white matter. Her past medical history is not significant for any other medical issues. She has no known allergies to medications. Her family history is negative for MS or any other neurological diseases. Her lab studies are normal, including renal and hepatic function tests. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

Maria is a 34-year-old woman who has just given birth to her first child via vaginal delivery. She has been experiencing a persistent headache that is exacerbated by sitting or standing and is relieved when lying down. She has received a diagnosis of post-dural puncture headache and her doctor has recommended an epidural blood patch to treat the condition. Maria has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of maintaining a prone position after the blood patch. She is willing to be followed up during her hospital stay, and has signed the informed consent form. She is affiliated with a health insurance plan and has no other medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She has not participated in any other interventional studies and has not undergone a cesarean section.

A 25-year-old female with a Nexplanon implant is seeking to have it removed. She has no known allergies to lidocaine or EMLA cream and speaks English as her primary language. She is not currently pregnant and is over 18 years of age. She has no other underlying medical conditions and is not taking any medications.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been in close contact with her roommate who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. She has not experienced any symptoms of the disease and considers herself to be in good health. She has no history of chronic illnesses, allergies, or surgeries. She has a healthy lifestyle, exercises regularly, and maintains a balanced diet. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her family history is negative for any major illnesses. She is interested in participating in a study that examines the antibody response in contacts of COVID-19 patients. She has read the eligibility criteria carefully and believes that she meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. She is willing to undergo the testing and follow-up visits required for the study. She hopes that her participation can help researchers better understand the immune response to COVID-19 and contribute to the development of effective treatments or vaccines.

The patient is a 7-year-old child who participated in the original VIDI study from the age of 2 weeks until 2 years. The child was given a daily dose of 10 ug of vitamin D supplement during the study period. The child has been in good health with no history of chronic illnesses or hospitalizations. The child has been following a healthy diet and engaging in regular physical activity. The parents have given their consent for the child to participate in the 6 Years Follow-up (VIDI2) study to evaluate the long-term effects of the vitamin D intervention on bone strength, growth pattern, body composition, morbidity due to infections and allergic diseases, development of immunity, neurocognitive development, mental health, occurrence of molar-incisor hypomineralization, dental caries, and oral immunity. The child will undergo regular check-ups and tests for the next 6 years as part of the study.

Patient is a 35yo female with a presumed benign adnexal disease who has been experiencing pelvic pain and discomfort for the past 6 months. She has no prior history of pelvic surgeries or conditions. Upon evaluation, imaging studies have shown a cystic mass measuring approximately 5cm in the right ovary. The patient has been recommended to undergo laparoscopic surgery for removal of the cyst. She is fluent in French and able to read and sign the informed consent form. The patient has no contraindications to laparoscopy and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 70 year-old retired school teacher who has recently been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's Disease. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has never smoked or consumed alcohol. She has a BMI of 25 and is physically active, taking daily walks around her neighborhood. She is currently taking donepezil for her Alzheimer's Disease and has been on a stable dosage for the past 6 months. She has no history of neurosurgical intervention, cardiac disorders, or psychiatric diseases. She has not undergone cortisone treatment in the past 6 months. She has no metallic objects in her head and no microbubbles in the application area. She is able to provide written informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old Hispanic woman who recently received her results from the CANRISK tool, indicating that she is at medium to high risk of developing type 2 diabetes. She has been feeling worried about her health and is looking for ways to improve her lifestyle to reduce her risk. The patient reports that she has not engaged in regular physical activity in the past and is interested in learning more about how to increase her physical activity levels. She does not have any medical conditions that would prevent her from safely participating in physical activity. The patient is available for all sessions and testing and is willing to commit to the intervention/control sessions. She has below-average self-compassion scores and is interested in learning more about how to use self-compassion to help her self-manage and increase her physical activity. The patient has not participated in any other type 2 diabetes education groups and is not currently undergoing any other behavioral change programs.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma. He is experiencing symptoms such as rectal bleeding, changes in bowel habits, and abdominal pain. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol use. He is employed as a construction worker and has physically demanding work. His performance status is ECOG 1. His medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he is taking medication. He has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or other malignancies. His lab results demonstrate an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm^3 and a platelet count of 120,000/mm^3. His bilirubin and creatinine levels are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or nursing, and he is willing to use effective contraception. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that tests UFT associated with neoadjuvant radiotherapy versus radiotherapy alone in rectal adenocarcinoma.

50 year old male with a history of gout for 10 years, presenting with chronic tophaceous gout refractory to conventional therapy. The patient has been taking allopurinol, febuxostat, and probenecid for the last 2 years with no improvement in symptoms. Serum uric acid levels remain above 8 mg/dL with persistent joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. Patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild renal insufficiency with serum creatinine of 1.5 mg/dL. The patient has no history of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency or anaphylactic reaction to a recombinant protein. The patient is willing to use an approved method of birth control, and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements and attend all study visits.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who was diagnosed with advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) confirmed by histopathology. Her medical history is non-significant. She has HER2 insertion or amplification and failed with standard chemotherapy. She has no history of PD-1/PD-L1 antibody use. The patient has no contraindication for chemotherapy and is willing to receive chemotherapy or chemotherapy plus PD-1 antibody. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is in overall good health with no significant comorbidities. She is able to provide informed consent and willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 28-year-old woman gave birth to a healthy baby girl at The Ottawa Hospital - Civic Campus. She is a first-time mother and intends to breastfeed her baby. She had a vaginal delivery and was discharged from the hospital after 2 days. She currently lives with her partner in a house located in the suburbs of Ottawa. She has a family history of breast cancer but does not have any personal history of breast surgery. She understands and speaks English fluently. She has access to transportation and is willing to attend the breastfeeding clinic for additional support. She can be reached via phone or email after discharge. She has no psychological risk factors that may impede her ability to attend the clinic. She is interested in participating in a research program to evaluate the benefits of the post-partum clinic for breastfeeding support.

Patient is a 55-year-old female from the United States who has been diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer. She has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her disease has progressed. She has no known history of HER2 amplification or overexpression, but her tumor tissue will be screened for HER2 mutation by the Washington University GPS laboratory. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate organ function. She has not received any investigational agents or systemic cancer therapy within the past 4 weeks, but has taken some herbal supplements in the past. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use adequate contraception throughout the study period. She understands the study requirements and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced pancreatic carcinoma. He underwent CT scan and MRI, which showed a tumor measuring 4 cm in the head of the pancreas. Multidisciplinary discussion involving a radiologist and surgeon concluded that the tumor is unresectable due to its encasement of the superior mesenteric artery. He has no evidence of metastasis. His performance status is 1. He has no significant comorbidities and his vital functions are stable. His laboratory tests show normal values for AST/ALT, bilirubin, creatinine, and albumin. He is not receiving any other cancer treatment and has no history of cancer except for basal cell carcinoma. He has no history of cardiac problems or active infections. He has no pre-existing neuropathy or Gilbert's disease. He has adequate organ function, and his uracilemia is below the cut-off value. He is not pregnant nor is he at risk of pregnancy. He is willing to use contraception during the study and for 4 months after the last intake of study treatment. He has been informed about the study and signed the informed consent form. He has public health insurance coverage. He has no fructose intolerance and is not currently treated with warfarin. His psychological condition and family, sociological, or geographical situation are not expected to hamper his compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.

35yo male with a benign bone tumor located in the pelvis that is not easily accessible and is in close proximity to the joint, causing concern for joint violation during resection. The patient has had previous unsuccessful attempts at surgical removal of the tumor and is now being considered for navigation-assisted surgery. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and has consented to the use of computer-assisted navigation during the operation. The patient will also be able to withstand a longer surgical time for joint reconstruction if necessary.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago. She is currently on metformin therapy and her HbA1c level is well-controlled within the range of 7-8%. She has a history of congestive heart failure, confirmed by her doctor, and is currently in NYHA functional class III. Her ejection fraction is less than 50%. She has been receiving standard therapy for her cardiac condition for the past 6 months. She has no history of renal or liver impairment, malignant disease, or recent cardiovascular events. She has not been treated with insulin or incretin-based therapies for the past 6 months. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and is able to sustain imaging studies.

A 42-year-old male with HIV-1 infection who has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 2 years with a PI-based regimen. The patient has maintained undetectable plasma HIV-1 RNA levels (<50 copies/mL) for the past 6 months. However, he has been experiencing dyslipidemia with LDL cholesterol levels above 130 mg/dL and triglycerides above 350 mg/dL due to the current PI regimen. The patient has also been experiencing gastrointestinal disturbances associated with his current regimen's posology. The patient is highly motivated to continue ART but is seeking a regimen that is easier to take and has less toxicity. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will compare the efficacy and safety of switching from a PI to etravirine as a strategy of simplification therapy. The patient has not experienced any treatment interruptions or blips in viral load in the past year and has good adherence to his current regimen.

56-year-old female with a history of annual mammograms and a recent mammogram that identified an area of concern in her right breast. The patient was referred to the University of Alabama at Birmingham for a stereotactic biopsy. The patient has no history of breast cancer or other significant medical problems. The biopsy is scheduled and the patient is informed of the study and given the option to participate. The patient agrees to participate and is randomized to the group that will undergo clip placement with approximately a 5 mm retraction of the biopsy clip post-placement. The patient is fully informed of the study and understands that this is a voluntary decision. The patient's medical records are reviewed to ensure that she meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who experienced a spinal cord injury over a year ago. His injury is non-progressive and located above the T10 neurological level. He is able to tolerate an upright position for more than 30 minutes and has a unilateral knee extension strength of at least 1/5 on manual muscle testing. He has no open wounds at the stimulation site and is not pregnant. He does not have a cardiac pacemaker or defibrillator, and he has no evidence of uncontrolled autonomic dysreflexia. He speaks English fluently and is able to comply with procedures and follow-up.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus type 2 for the past 10 years. He has recently developed a foot ulcer and has sought medical attention for it. Upon examination, the ulcer has been classified as Grade II according to Wagner classification. The patient has a BMI of 30 and is otherwise in good general health. He has no history of nephropathy, cardiomyopathy, recent myocardial infarction, or pulmonary problems. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided written consent to participate. He will be randomized into one of two groups: Helium-Neon Laser therapy (HNLT) or Infrared Laser therapy (ILT) group. The patient will undergo treatment for 8 weeks and the ulcer surface area will be assessed using a sheet of cellophane paper at the beginning of the study, after four weeks, and after eight weeks at the end of the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, causing severe abdominal pain and difficulty managing her diabetes. She has had multiple hospitalizations for acute exacerbations of her condition and has undergone numerous procedures to manage her symptoms, including a transduodenal sphincteroplasty. Her diabetes has been difficult to manage, with frequent fluctuations in blood sugar levels despite multiple medication adjustments. She currently takes insulin injections and metformin daily. She has a BMI of 25 and normal renal function. Her liver function tests are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial as she hopes it will improve her glycemic control and reduce her pain. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 65-year-old retired accountant noticed that he has been forgetting small details, such as where he placed his keys or glasses, and having trouble recalling names of acquaintances during social events. He has never had any serious medical condition and has been generally healthy throughout his life. He does not have any history of alcohol or drug abuse, and he does not smoke. He is right-handed and of Han nationality. He is concerned about his memory loss and wants to participate in a study that will help him understand the cause of his cognitive decline. He has no physical complaints, and his physical examination is normal. His score on a standardized neuropsychological test is within normal range for his age, sex, and education. The patient has no history of cognitive decline in his family. He is willing to cooperate with the study and undergo MRI scans once a year for five years.

A 45 year old man with end stage renal disease due to uncontrolled hypertension has been on HD for the past 6 months. He is overweight and has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. His blood pressure is well controlled with medication, and his blood sugar levels are under control with insulin therapy. He reports feeling weak and lethargic most of the time and has lost 10 pounds over the past month. He is currently receiving standard nutrition care with dietary counseling and high protein diet. He has no history of hospitalization over the past 3 months. He agrees to participate in the study and provide a blood sample for NIR method for Cr determination.

A 55-year-old man with a history of knee pain and stiffness visited the clinic for a consultation. He was diagnosed with stage II degenerative knee joint disease last year and has been experiencing discomfort and difficulty with physical activity ever since. He works as a desk job and spends most of his time sitting. He does not exercise regularly and has gained some weight in the past year. He has no other major medical conditions, but he does have a history of smoking. He is currently taking over-the-counter pain relievers for his knee pain. He is interested in participating in a study to explore the benefit of functional movement control for patients with knee osteoarthritis.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who recently underwent a CT scan for evaluation of his persistent cough and shortness of breath. The CT scan revealed a suspicious mass in the lung, and his primary care physician referred him to a lung specialist for further evaluation. He has no significant past medical history and has never smoked. His physical examination is unremarkable except for decreased breath sounds over the right lung base. The patient is willing and able to undergo bronchoscopy and thoracic surgery if necessary. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 22-year-old man of color who identifies as gay and has engaged in sexual activity with men in the past 90 days. He recently tested negative for HIV within the past 90 days but has reported engaging in high-risk sexual behavior and illicit drug use. The patient has used illicit drugs for at least 5 days in the past 90 days and has engaged in at least one episode of condomless anal sex or has tested positive for a sexually transmitted infection within the past 90 days. He is currently living in the New York City area and is able to communicate in English. The patient has no history of serious cognitive or psychiatric impairments and is not currently taking Truvada as Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP). The patient is seeking access to a community-based intervention that will help him reduce his substance use and HIV risk behaviors.

A 68 year old man came to the clinic with a history of renal cancer. His medical history includes hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. His creatinine level was 29 ml/min/1.73 m2, which puts him at risk of severe renal insufficiency. The tumor is located in the native renal parenchyma and has a largest diameter of 3.8 cm. The tumor is not easily accessible for nephron-sparing surgery due to its location. A preoperative MRI revealed that the tumor is solid and there is no metastasis. The patient has no contra-indication for cryoablation treatment. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of percutaneous cryoablation for renal tumors smaller than 4 cm.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with end-stage renal disease undergoing hemodialysis three times a week. He received the complete full course of primary vaccination with either Henogen's HBV vaccine or Fendrix™ for hepatitis B prevention. He has no known allergies to any medication and has not been diagnosed with any other chronic diseases. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient has not received any immunosuppressive treatments such as parenteral steroids or chemotherapy. The patient has not been diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Blood sampling will be performed at Months 12, 24 and 36 after the first dose of primary vaccination to measure immune persistence.

A 35-year-old male smoker presents with a history of smoking five to six cigarettes per day for the past 10 years. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and has no significant medical history. He has not used any nicotine replacement therapy within the past 14 days and has not donated blood within the past 12 months. His lung function tests and vital signs are within normal limits. He denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is not trying to stop smoking but is interested in trying different nicotine delivery systems. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the bioavailability of nicotine delivered by an electronic vapour product.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is sexually active and using a reliable form of contraception. She is in good general health with a BMI of 23. She is a non-smoker and has not consumed alcohol or caffeine in the past 24 hours. She has not taken any vitamin supplements or medications within the past 7 days. She has no known allergies or history of significant cardiovascular disease, thrombophlebitis, thrombosis, or coagulopathy. She has not had any gastrointestinal surgery that could affect drug absorption. She has not fainted during blood collection or has fear of it. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the bioavailability of Desogestrel 0.075 mg tablets compared to a reference product. She is capable of understanding the informed consent form and willing to comply with the study requirements, including confining herself in the study site for approximately 36 hours during each study period.

As this is a clinical trial focused on an education program for the prevention of type two diabetes in elementary school children, there is no specific patient description needed. However, eligible participants would be those in grades 2-6 in schools with high Hispanic enrollment during the 2001-2005 school year.

50 year old man with chronic lower back pain and a history of opioid use for pain management. He is currently taking oxycodone 10mg every 6 hours for the past 6 months. He has tried other non-opioid pain medications in the past but did not find them effective. He is willing to participate in a study to evaluate a new questionnaire to assess opioid misuse and abuse among patients with chronic pain. The patient has no history of cognitive or psychiatric impairment that would interfere with participating in a one-on-one discussion. He is able to read, speak, and understand English and complete all study assessments. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese man with chronic liver disease. He has been experiencing a low platelet count with a baseline count of 35,000/mcL. He has no history of arterial or venous thrombosis, and does not have any of the risk factors associated with it. The patient has a Child-Pugh score of 7 and a baseline serum sodium level of 135 mEq/L. His hemoglobin concentration is stable at 10 g/dL for the past 4 weeks. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is not currently pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. He is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and instructions and has provided written informed consent. The patient has no history of platelet agglutination abnormality or porphyria. He has not received platelet transfusion or interferon treatment within the specified time frame. The patient is physically able to ingest and retain oral medication.

A 30-year-old male who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of dietary patterns associated with egg intake on glucose control and insulin resistance. He has no history of diabetes, and his fasting glucose level is normal. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and is generally healthy. He exercises regularly and enjoys running outdoors. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, and his blood pressure is normal. He does not have any history of eating disorders or drug abuse. He does not have any known allergies to eggs, and he consumes eggs at least twice a week. He is not attempting to lose weight, and he is not currently taking any medications that may influence his appetite, sensory functioning, or hormone signaling. He is interested in learning more about how dietary patterns may impact his health and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help advance scientific knowledge in this area.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty with her memory for the past year. She has noticed that she forgets things easily and has trouble recalling names and faces. She has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders other than Alzheimer's disease, and her family history is negative for AD. She has not received any investigational medication within the last 30 days or scheduled to receive any investigational drug. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She does not have any history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has no significant abnormalities in any clinical laboratory test. She has a Mini Mental State Score of 22. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. She is between the ages of 60 and 80 years, and her weight is above 50 kg. She has no metal objects in or around her body, and she does not have any blood donation history within the last three months.

A 35-year-old male patient was diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency at the age of 22, due to a pituitary tumor. He has been on growth hormone replacement therapy for the last 13 years and has completed the initial long-term study on the safety of growth hormone replacement in adult patients with growth hormone deficiency. He presents with no other pituitary hormone deficiencies and no history of cardiac, pulmonary, renal or hepatic impairments. He has a good history of compliance with his treatment regimen and has not experienced any significant side effects from the treatment. His blood pressure and blood glucose levels are within normal range, and he has no history of psychological disorders or malignant cancer.

The patient is a 50-year-old postmenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with stage I breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy and is scheduled to start adjuvant therapy with tamoxifen. Her mammogram revealed heterogeneously dense breast tissue (BIRADS 3). She has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother being diagnosed at the age of 60. She does not use soy-based dietary supplements and is willing to discontinue use if needed. She has no history of hyponatremia and her blood chemistry tests are normal. She is not pregnant and is practicing birth control. She is able to comply with the study requirements and is willing to take the study-provided medication and record any symptoms experienced.

This is a 6-year-old male scheduled to undergo hernia repair surgery. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. The estimated operative time is approximately 3 hours. The patient's parent has provided consent for their child to be included in the study. The purpose of the study is to determine if two different concentrations of bupivacaine delivered at a total dose of 1 mL/kg offer similar or altered analgesia, i.e., does the concentration of the anesthetic matter more than the volume of local anesthetic while performing a TAP block in children undergoing groin surgery. The solution used for the TAP block will be drawn up by an investigator who is not a participant in the patient's care in a sterile fashion. The family will be required to complete a postoperative questionnaire.

A 35-year-old male patient with burns covering 30% of his total body surface area was admitted to a Texas burn center within 4 days of his burn injury. He sustained the burns due to a fire in his home. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. He has no known history of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), AIDS-related complex (ARC), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), cancer or pregnancy. The patient has consented to participate in the study and will have approximately 11 serum samples collected throughout his hospital stay, as well as clinical data related to sepsis and infection predictors recorded. The patient is within the age range of 18-80 years old and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who works as a software engineer. He has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders and is not taking any central nervous system medication. He does not smoke or use any drugs and occasionally drinks alcohol. He has no family history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to scientific research. He has no medical conditions that would prevent him from participating and has not had significant exposure to radiation in the past year. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.
