58 y/o male with diagnosed Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) that has progressed despite prior treatment with sorafenib. Patient has a history of hypertension and is currently on antihypertensive therapy with well-controlled blood pressure. Patient is currently on antiviral therapy as per local standard of care for occult hepatitis B infection. Patient has adequate hepatic, renal, and hematologic function. Patient has a history of prior chemotherapy and small molecule kinase inhibitor systemic therapy, but has not received any such therapy for at least 3 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. Patient has not received prior regional therapy such as ablation, embolization, or radiation therapy for at least 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment. Patient has measurable disease as defined by RECIST version 1.1. Patient's liver cancer cells have been confirmed to express the androgen receptor by IHC on pretreatment HCC samples. Patient is capable of understanding and complying with the protocol requirements and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 50 year old male with end-stage renal disease, who has been undergoing maintenance hemodialysis three times a week for the past 6 months. He has a history of requiring IV iron supplementation within the last 2 months. He has not been diagnosed with absolute iron deficiency at the time of enrollment. The patient has no current malignancies and no history of drug or alcohol abuse within the last 6 months. The clinical trial involves adding soluble ferric pyrophosphate (SFP) to the dialysate to prevent the development of iron deficiency and maintain hemoglobin levels. The study will compare the effects of SFP with conventional dialysate on iron balance in hemodialysis patients. The patient will be monitored for any adverse effects during the trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old male complaining of persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. He has been a smoker for 40 years and still smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both of which are controlled with medication. He is a retired construction worker and has been feeling fatigued and weak for the past few months. He has lost about 5kg of weight in the past 2 months. He has no family history of lung cancer or any other cancers. He has never been diagnosed with cancer before. He is married and has two grown-up children. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. His ECOG performance score is 1. His chest X-ray and CT scan show a large mass in his left lung and a small lesion in his liver. His biopsy confirms the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. His brain MRI shows no metastasis. He has not received any anti-tumor treatment before.

29F with a history of myopia and successful contact lens wear for the past 5 years, referred by her optometrist to participate in a clinical trial comparing the performance of two daily disposable contact lenses. She has no known ocular conditions that would contraindicate contact lens wear and has not worn PRECISION1, Biotrue ONEday, or DAILIES TOTAL1 contact lenses before. She reports wearing her contact lenses for at least 10 hours per day, 5 days per week. The patient is willing to wear contact lenses for at least 16 hours per day and is able to understand and sign an IRB approved Informed Consent Form. She is excited to participate in the clinical trial and contribute to the advancement of contact lens technology.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who is interested in reducing the appearance of moderate to severe forehead wrinkles. She has never undergone any previous botulinum toxin injections, and is willing to participate in all procedures of the study. She is in good health with no known neurological or autoimmune disorders, and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has no history of sensitivity to the components of the formula or adverse effects from previous cosmetic procedures. The patient has positive sweating ability on the forehead, as confirmed by Minor's test. She is aware of the study objectives and has sufficient schooling to cooperate with the study requirements. The patient agrees not to undergo any other cosmetic or dermatological procedures during the study and is available throughout the duration of the study (112 days).

A 35 yo F with a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) for the past 10 years. She has had two inadequate responses to antidepressant therapy in her current Major Depressive Episode (MDE). She is currently not pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. She has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 25.0 kg/m2 and is willing to use an acceptable method of contraception for the duration of the study. She has no current primary Axis-I disorder other than MDD and has not used opioid agonists or opioid antagonists within the past 14 days. She has not received electroconvulsive therapy treatment within the last 2 years or received more than one course of electroconvulsive treatment during her lifetime. She has not attempted suicide within the past 2 years and has had no positive tests for drugs of abuse. She has no known intolerance, allergy, or hypersensitivity to buprenorphine or opioid antagonists (eg, naltrexone, naloxone). She has not experienced significant blood loss or blood donation within the last 60 days.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman, who is a first-time mother, is experiencing cervical dilation less than 5 cm and is admitted to the hospital with harbingers of labor. She reports moderate to severe labor pain with a Numeric Rate Scale of 7. She has no prior history of medical conditions and is not taking any regular medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or illicit drugs. She has a normal BMI and has been following a healthy diet and exercise regimen during pregnancy. She is currently at full-term pregnancy with a single vertex presentation fetus. She has no contraindications for epidural analgesia, and her obstetrician has recommended it for pain management during labor. The patient has been informed about the study and has given her consent to participate.

Patient A is a 20-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. She weighs 50 kg and is able to perform acceptable spirometric maneuvers as per American Thoracic Society standards. Her FEV1 is between 25-85% predicted, and she is clinically stable. She has not participated in another study with an investigational drug within the last month or six half-lives. She

A 56-year-old male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer is scheduled to receive chemotherapy through a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC). He has no history of clotting disorders or previous occlusions of a central line. The patient is currently taking aspirin daily for secondary prevention of myocardial infarction. He has no known allergies to heparin or citrate. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of heparinised saline and 4% citrate as locking agents for PICC to prevent occlusion. The patient is mentally competent and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital due to acute pancreatitis. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but otherwise he is generally healthy. He is currently on a course of antibiotics to treat a suspected infection related to his pancreatitis. He reports experiencing diarrhea since starting the antibiotics, which is causing discomfort and distress. He has not had any episodes of Clostridium difficile in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and meets the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has just given birth to a premature baby. The infant was born at 32 weeks and weighed 1.8 kg. The mother has no significant past medical history and did not have any complications during her pregnancy. The infant was delivered via cesarean section due to fetal distress. The baby was immediately transferred to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of Kanuni Sultan Suleyman Training and Research Hospital due to respiratory distress. The baby required surfactant therapy and mechanical ventilation. The mother is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the possible role of maternal/neonatal vitamin D levels on RDS development in preterm infants. Blood samples will be collected from both the mother and infant to determine their vitamin D levels. The mother is hopeful that this study will help researchers better understand how to prevent RDS and other neonatal morbidities.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with locally advanced pancreatic cancer that was deemed inoperable by her treating physician. She has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy yet. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has no known history of chronic hepatitis B or C, chronic active hepatitis or active autoimmune diseases. She has no history of acute or subacute coronary syndromes including myocardial infarction. The patient's blood pressure is well-controlled with medications. She has no history of heart insufficiency, irreversible cardiac arrhythmias, or ischemic peripheral vascular disease. She has no history of severe rheumatoid arthritis or severe diabetic retinopathy. She has not undergone allograft or stem cell transplantation. She has no known allergy to IL2, gemcitabine, or other intravenously administered human proteins/peptides/antibodies. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has agreed to use effective contraception. She has not received chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the last 4 weeks. She does not require or is taking corticosteroids or other immunosuppressant drugs on a long-term basis. She meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

57yo man with relapsed multiple myeloma who has received prior treatment with bortezomib, lenalidomide, and carfilzomib. He has also received autologous stem cell transplant 2 years ago. His disease progressed on his most recent therapy of daratumumab, pomalidomide and dexamethasone. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medications. His recent echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 60%. He currently has mild anemia and thrombocytopenia, but no signs of bleeding or infection. He is willing to undergo bone marrow aspiration per protocol.

A 21-year-old female college student presents to the dental clinic for a routine check-up. She reports good oral hygiene practices and has no history of dental caries or previous restorations. She denies having any allergies to dental materials. On examination, her teeth appear to be in good condition with no signs of decay or malocclusion. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial related to dental sealants.

Patient is a 40-year-old female from the United States who comes to the clinic with concerns about hair loss. She reports a family history of genetic hair loss and has noticed thinning hair over the past year. She has a Fitzpatrick skin phototype of II and is in overall good health with no history of major medical issues. She has not used any hair growth products or treatments in the past year. She is willing to wear a baseball cap configured with a non-heat generating, laser product for every other day for 16 weeks as part of the study. She has never been diagnosed with photosensitivity to the specific wavelength of light - 650 nanometers. She does not have any malignancy in the target treatment area and does not have any past medical history of collagen-vascular disease, thyroid disease or other cutaneous or systemic disease that seriously affects the scalp.

The patient is a 60-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and a body weight of 80 kg. He is of European ethnicity and has no history of allergies or known hypersensitivity to Neramexane/Memantine/Amantadine and their derivatives. He has not been exposed to any investigational agent within the last two months before the first drug administration and has not been exposed to any radiolabeled substance or significant radiation within the last 12 months. He is able to read, write, and fully understand Dutch language. He has no evidence of significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, endocrinological, metabolic, psychiatric, neurologic, or other acute or chronic diseases. He has no disorders or surgery of the gastrointestinal tract that may interfere with drug absorption or may otherwise influence the pharmacokinetics of the investigational medicinal products. He has no clinically relevant acute or chronic infections observed within 4 weeks before first drug administration and no history of malignancy except basal cell carcinoma. He has normal ECG, blood pressure, and pulse rate. He has no history of alcohol or drug dependence and his alcohol consumption is within the recommended limit. He has not used any prescribed medication or over-the-counter drugs within 4 weeks prior to the first administration of IMP (except paracetamol, maximum 2 g/day). He has not used any food, food supplement, or medication known to induce or inhibit CYP3A4 or other cytochrome P450 enzymes within two weeks before first drug administration. He is a non-smoker and has not donated blood more than 450 mL within 60 days before first drug administration. He has no positive results in any of the serology tests and no positive drug screen or alcohol test. He is not an employee or direct relative of an employee of the CRO or Merz Pharmaceuticals. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent after having been informed of the requirements and the restrictions of the study and is available for study visits/procedures.

A 45-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department with chest pain that had started 3 hours earlier. He described the pain as a pressure sensation on his chest that radiated to his left arm. The patient had a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, but no prior history of myocardial infarction. An electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads, and the patient was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). He was immediately taken to the catheterization laboratory for primary percutaneous revascularization (PCI). The patient has initial TIMI 0 in the infarct-related coronary artery. He does not have liver disease, thrombolytic therapy, atrial fibrillation, congestive heart failure, migraine headache, valvular heart disease, primary myocardial disease, or cardiogenic shock. The patient is not a woman of childbearing potential and has a life expectancy of at least 3 years. The patient is not currently taking konazoles, ritonavir, rifampicin, or sulfonyl-urea derivatives. He is not participating in another clinical study and does not have metal implants contraindicating CMR.

68-year-old Caucasian male who has a history of extensive sun exposure due to his outdoor job as a construction worker. He was diagnosed with multiple actinic keratosis (AK) lesions on his face, scalp, and hands during a routine skin examination. He participated in the PEP005-016 clinical study and received the study drug for 2 consecutive days. At Day 57, he achieved complete clearance of all the AK lesions. He has now been invited to participate in the long-term follow-up study to assess the recurrence of AK lesions and long-term safety in the treated areas over a 12-month period. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. He does not have any concurrent participation in another research study that would involve the selected treatment area.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who has been receiving chronic dialysis treatments for the past 5 years. He weighs 80 kg and has a blood flow rate of 300 ml/min with a recirculation of the vascular access of 3%. He is currently using not fractioned heparin in continuous infusion as anticoagulant and has stable anticoagulation dosage over the last 6 treatments. His dialysis prescription (Qb, Qd, treatment time) has been stable over the last 6 treatments. He has given informed consent to participate in the study. His hemoglobin concentration at the beginning of the treatment is 13.5 g/dl. He has no history of HIV or active Hepatitis A, B or C. He is not pregnant and is not participating in other clinical investigations during the course of this study. He has no known coagulation disorders, bleeding risk, acute infection, recent surgical intervention, cancer, or immune disease.

Pt is a 45yo F diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy with 2cm residual disease, and subsequently had a right axillary lymph node dissection with 6/10 nodes positive for metastasis. ER/PR/HER2 status was positive/positive/negative. She received adjuvant radiation therapy and completed 6 cycles of adjuvant AC chemotherapy with good tolerance. However, 6 months later, she presented with bone and liver metastasis. She was started on capecitabine chemotherapy and achieved stable disease with good tolerance. She is now presenting for enrollment into a clinical trial that will analyze genomic, proteomic, and pharmacogenomic assessments for predicting response and toxicity in patients receiving chemotherapy for advanced breast cancer. She is willing to undergo pre-treatment core or incisional biopsy with adequate tissue for histology and genomic/proteomic analysis. She has measurable disease and is currently on a chemotherapy regimen that is one of the study arms. She has no serious uncontrolled medical or surgical condition that would compromise her study participation, and has agreed to use adequate contraception while on treatment and for a period of 3 months after the final dose of chemotherapy.

A 28-year-old man who identifies as gay and has a history of sexual activity with men came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He is HIV-negative and has never been diagnosed with any sexually transmitted infections. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He exercises regularly and has a healthy diet

The patient is a 25-year-old woman with a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. She has been experiencing exercise intolerance and shortness of breath during physical activity. She is currently taking traditional CF-treatment medications and has been clinically stable for the past 2 weeks. Her FEV1 percent predicted is 40% and her resting oxygen saturation in room air is 95%. She has no diagnosis of heart disease or pulmonary artery hypertension. She is a non-smoker and not currently pregnant or nursing. She is able to swallow pills and has not been diagnosed with B. Cepacia. She is interested in participating in the study to understand the physiological mechanisms behind her exercise intolerance and potentially improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing tinnitus for the past 6 months. She is a native Hebrew speaker and has been fluent in the language since childhood. She reports that her tinnitus is constant and has been causing her significant distress, including difficulty sleeping and concentrating. She has not undergone any treatment for tinnitus and is not taking any medications that might affect her ability to perceive emotions in spoken language. She has not experienced any significant hearing loss, and her hearing is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the impact of tinnitus on her ability to perceive emotions in spoken language.

75 yo F with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, referred by her primary care physician for evaluation of mild cognitive changes. She reports difficulty with financial management and medication adherence. She has a reliable informant who corroborates these difficulties. She reports no history of psychiatric illness or substance abuse. She is able to read at the 8th grade level and has experience using a computer. Her MOCA score is 28. She meets the criteria for the diagnosis of MCI based on Jak Bondi criteria. She is fluent in English and has no sensory limitations.

A 56-year-old woman with a history of Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) and Coronary Heart Disease (CHD) visited the clinic for a routine check-up. She has been married for 25 years and has two adult children. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She brushes her teeth twice a day but has been experiencing bleeding gums and bad breath for the past few months. Her dentist diagnosed her with Chronic Periodontitis (CP) and recommended her for this clinical trial. She has no allergies to any medication or local anaesthetic. She has not taken any immunosuppressive or anti-inflammatory drugs in the last three months. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not taken any drugs that may potentially determine gingival hyperplasia. She is excited to participate in the study and contribute to research on the link between Vitamin D and SSc, CHD, and Periodontitis.

A 6-year-old boy who is slightly overweight and has a family history of obesity, diabetes, and heart disease. He enjoys playing video games and watching TV. His parents are concerned about his eating habits and want to learn how to encourage healthier behaviors. They are open to discussing goals for physical activity and nutrition during well-child visits. They have Tricare insurance and usually visit a pediatrician at a military hospital.

12 year old boy with a history of ADHD diagnosed at age 7. He has been treated with stimulant medication in the past, but his parents report that his aggressive behavior has persisted despite the medication. He has been diagnosed with oppositional defiant disorder and has a score that exceeds the study threshold on the standardized scale of aggressive behavior. He has no history of psychosis, major depression, pervasive developmental disorder, obsessive compulsive disorder, or any other anxiety disorder as a primary diagnosis. He has an IQ within the normal range and is currently in the sixth grade. His parents are willing to participate in regular study visits and behavioral counseling sessions with a therapist.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and a total body weight of 60 kg. She does not have any significant medical history and is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription drugs, vitamins, grapefruit juice, or dietary/herbal supplements. She does not smoke or use tobacco-containing products and has not consumed alcohol or drugs in the past month. She has not donated blood within the past 30 days and does not have evidence of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV infection. The patient is interested in participating in a Phase 1 clinical trial to evaluate the safety of a new investigational study drug called ARRY-300. She is of non-childbearing potential and meets all additional inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 50 year old female who has been experiencing moderate to severe eye pain, redness and blurred vision for several months. She has previously been diagnosed with superficial punctate keratitis (SPK) and/or corneal erosion in both eyes. She has been treated with various medications, but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She wears glasses and has no history of ocular surgery or trauma. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She works as a secretary and spends a lot of time in front of a computer screen. She is interested in participating in this study to potentially improve her symptoms and overall quality of life.

A 60-year-old female came to the clinic with a history of herpes zoster infection that occurred 7 months ago. She developed a rash on the left side of her chest and was treated with antiviral medication, but the rash left a persisting pain in the same area. She describes the pain as a burning sensation, and it has been affecting her ability to sleep and perform daily activities. She has tried several pain medications, including over-the-counter analgesics, but they have not provided sufficient relief. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and has agreed to use only the protocol-defined rescue medication. She is not employed by the sponsor or study staff, nor is she related to them. She has intact skin over the painful area to be treated and is able to apply the study ointment as directed. She meets the inclusion criteria of the study and is eligible to participate.

A 62-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation presents to the hospital for a scheduled radiofrequency ablation procedure. He has been experiencing palpitations and shortness of breath for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but it is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He has not been on any corticosteroids in the past week and does not have any allergies to prednisone or its components. He has no history of heart failure or cardiomyopathy, and has not been diagnosed with any immunological disorders. He is willing to provide written informed consent for the trial.

A 10 yo F with cerebral palsy and spastic diplegia who resides in a rural area of northern California. The child is currently enrolled in the CCS Medical Therapy Program and receives physiatry services from a non-pediatric specialist provider at her local school-based Medical Therapy Unit. The child's parent has expressed concern regarding the quality of care provided by the non-pediatric specialist and the difficulty in accessing in-person care from a pediatric physiatrist due to the long distance travel required. The child has been compliant with an evidence-based hip surveillance program but has experienced difficulty in attending scheduled appointments due to transportation challenges. The child's parent is interested in exploring the possibility of accessing medical direction from pediatric physiatrists through a telemedicine-based model of care to improve the quality of care and increase access to necessary services.

A 25 year old right-handed healthy individual with no history of neurological or psychiatric diseases, brain injury, cognitive handicap, speech disorder, alcohol or drug abuse, neurosurgical intervention, and chronic diseases such as asthma or diabetes mellitus. The individual should not have used any acute medication in the last 12 months and should not have received any acupuncture treatment in the last 12 months. They should not be pregnant or planning to be pregnant during the study. They should also have no contraindications for acupuncture such as anti-coagulation therapy and should be willing to undergo MRI scanning. The individual should provide informed consent and should have no medical knowledge about acupuncture.

A 56-year-old man was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the stomach that has spread to his liver, lungs, and lymph nodes. He had noticed persistent abdominal pain, bloating, and fatigue for several months, which led to the discovery of the cancer. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has no known allergies. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a Karnofsky score of 80%. He has not received any prior treatment for his metastatic disease. Blood tests show normal organ and marrow function. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that uses genetic markers to select the best chemotherapy regimen for his cancer.

The patient is a 45 year old woman scheduled to undergo a major abdominal surgery. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of cardiac dysrhythmia or vascular pathology at the punction site. The patient is generally healthy and has no other significant medical conditions. She has consented to invasive arterial measurements during the surgery and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been struggling with mild to moderate flank fat for the past few years. She is generally healthy, with no known systemic diseases or allergies to any medications. She has never undergone any cosmetic procedures in the flank area, and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials. The patient is sexually active, but has been using reliable contraception for the past month and has tested negative for pregnancy within the past 10 days. She is willing to abstain from any other treatments to the flank region during the course of the study. The patient is able to follow study instructions and is likely to complete all required visits. She is interested in participating in the study, hoping to benefit from the use of Kybella for the reduction of flank fat.

A 50-year-old male with a history of myocardial infarction (MI) is sought for a clinical trial. The patient must be managing their MI condition both physically and mentally, and own a mobile telephone with the ability to read text messages or receive voice messages. The patient must also be willing to provide informed consent. The trial aims to improve medication adherence and promote healthy lifestyles among MI patients through using a provider-facing mobile app and patient-facing text messages. The trial requires patient participation for a 12-week period and involves receiving regular text messages about consistent medication use and lifestyle modification. The patient will receive standard ongoing care as well. The study is designed to have two interventions targeting physicians and patients respectively. The study will be conducted in Shanghai and Haikou, Hainan, China. The study team will include four academic collaborating institutions. The DKU research team will play the leading role in designing the study, developing the app and messages, and overseeing the entire implementation process. The PHRI research team will primarily work with the DKU research team on the physician-facing app and patient-facing messages development. The Fudan and Hainan research team will be responsible for local implementation. The study offers participants the prospect of direct benefits such as potential improvement in medical adherence, healthy lifestyle building, guidance for physicians on evidence-based medicines prescription, and facilitation of interactions between patients and physicians. No foreseeable risks are anticipated for physicians or patients.

A 25-year-old female with a confirmed genetic diagnosis of Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome (CMS) presents with symptoms of muscle weakness, difficulty breathing, and fatigue. She has been experiencing these symptoms intermittently since childhood. She is currently not on any medications for CMS. She has no significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is currently not pregnant and is using birth control. She is willing to use 2 acceptable methods of contraception during the trial. She is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to gain access to amifampridine phosphate therapy. Her family is supportive of her decision to participate in the study. Her CMS subtype is not slow-channel syndrome, LRP4 deficiency, or acetylcholinesterase deficiency. She has not used any investigational product or investigational medical device in the last 30 days. She has not used any other form of 3,4 DAP other than the investigational product provided.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). He has been on treatment with tyrosine kinase inhibitors for the past 2 years, but his disease has progressed to blast phase. He has been evaluated for a bone marrow transplant and has no available HLA-matched donor. His performance status is good with a Karnofsky score of 80%. He has no significant cardiac, pulmonary, renal, or hepatic dysfunction. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to participate. He has identified his wife as his caregiver during the transplant process. The patient has no known allergies to dimethyl sulfoxide and is not HIV positive.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been suffering from chronic bronchitis for the past 6 years. He has been experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and recurrent episodes of chest tightness. He has been using bronchodilators and corticosteroids as prescribed by his doctor, but his symptoms have not improved. He has been advised by his physician to participate in a clinical trial that involves using Avelox to treat his condition. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are both well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and does not have any known allergies to any medications.

A 45-year-old man from Egypt has been diagnosed with chronic Hepatitis C virus infection. He has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite. He has a history of intravenous drug use in his younger years. He has not received any treatment for his condition yet. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that assesses the effects of Direct Acting Antiviral therapy on chronic Hepatitis C virus patients. He has no known allergies to any of the components of the antiviral drug. He is not a geriatric or pediatric patient and does not have primary hematological abnormalities.

The patient is a 72-year-old man with a diagnosis of colon cancer. He has not yet received radiation therapy or chemotherapy and is scheduled to undergo surgery for the treatment of his tumor. The surgery is expected to last for more than 2 hours and will be performed under general anesthesia. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed written informed consent. He has no preoperative history of schizophrenia, epilepsy, parkinsonism, or myasthenia gravis. He is able to communicate effectively and does not have any language barriers. He has been classified as American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification II. His liver and renal functions are satisfactory. He is not undergoing dialysis before surgery.

A 57-year-old male smoker presented to the clinic with complaints of persistent cough, fatigue, and shortness of breath. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the right lung and biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. He received platinum-based combination chemotherapy for metastatic disease and subsequent treatment with pembrolizumab as a candidate. However, disease progression was observed after receiving immunotherapy. Weekly paclitaxel was recommended for treatment, and the patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive napabucasin in combination with weekly paclitaxel. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate organ function. The patient is willing to submit tumor tissue for correlative analyses and understands the importance of avoiding pregnancy during treatment. He does not have any other chronic medical or psychiatric illnesses that may interfere with protocol therapy administration or compliance with required procedures.

A 56-year-old female with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who underwent an allogeneic stem cell transplantation one month ago. She presents with a fever of 39°C and a neutrophil count of 200 cells/mm³. She has no known allergies to antibiotics. She is currently taking immunosuppressive medications for the stem cell transplant. The patient is conscious and oriented, with stable vital signs. She is able to provide informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 36-year-old male with a history of diabetes who presents to the hospital with fever, chills, and severe abdominal pain. He has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and was recently hospitalized for pneumonia. The patient's urine culture shows the presence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae. The patient was initially started on broad-spectrum antibiotics but failed to respond to treatment. The patient has no known allergies to any antibiotics. The patient's blood pressure is within normal limits, and he has no signs of sepsis. The patient has a normal renal function and no concomitant medication that would interfere with the study. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has consented to participate in the clinical trial.

This is a 40 year old male who presented with symptoms of shortness of breath and fatigue. An echocardiogram showed severe left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 30%. A cardiac MRI confirmed the presence of dilated cardiomyopathy. The patient has no significant past medical history, and denies any recent viral illness, chest pain, or family history of cardiomyopathy. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in a study that aims to evaluate left ventricular recovery in patients with new onset dilated cardiomyopathy. The patient has no evidence of coronary artery disease and has not had a myocardial biopsy that reveals evidence of hemochromatosis, amyloid, sarcoidosis, or giant cell myocarditis. The patient's alcohol consumption does not exceed an average of three drinks per day, and there is no evidence of chronic liver disease or chronic renal disease. The patient is not currently enrolled in any other placebo controlled experimental trials.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He presents to the hospital with a severe headache, nausea, and vomiting. A CT scan of the head reveals a ruptured intracranial aneurysm. The patient is neurologically stable with Hunt & Hess Score of III. He is stabilized and admitted to the hospital for further management. The patient is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is a married electrician with two children and has a supportive family. The patient's MRI and angiogram confirm a wide-necked bifurcated saccular, intracranial aneurysm, which is suitable for treatment with the Contour/Contour 021 System. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has signed and dated an institutional review board (IRB)/Ethics Committee (EC)-approved written informed consent prior to initiation of any study procedures. He is able to comply with all aspects of the screening, evaluation, treatment, and the post-procedure follow-up schedule. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

A healthy 35-year-old male with no significant medical history, who does not smoke or use tobacco products, and has not taken any systemic prescription medication or donated blood or plasma in the last 14-28 days. The volunteer must be willing to abstain from donating blood for four weeks after completing the study. The volunteer should not have any history of drug or alcohol addiction, abuse, or allergies to metformin or related drugs. Female volunteers must not be currently breastfeeding, and if of childbearing potential, must be practicing an acceptable method of birth control or be postmenopausal or surgically sterile. The weight range must not exceed ± 20% for height and body frame as per Desirable Weights for Adults -1983 Metropolitan Height and Weight Table. The volunteer must be willing to undergo screening procedures, including general observations, physical examination, demographics, medical and medication history, and laboratory tests for HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, drug abuse, pregnancy (if applicable), and clinical chemistry. The volunteer must not have any clinically significant disorder involving the cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, gastrointestinal, immunologic, hematologic, endocrine, or neurologic system(s) or psychiatric disease.

A 27-year-old Somali woman who is 28 weeks pregnant with her first child attends her antenatal appointment. She is accompanied by her sister as her husband works during the day. She reports feeling anxious and nervous about being pregnant as she has never experienced it before. She understands enough English to communicate with her healthcare provider. She reports that she is experiencing some physical and emotional abuse from her husband. She reports that her husband has been physically abusive towards her in the past, and she is afraid that he may harm her or her unborn child if she tries to leave. She has never reported the abuse to anyone before. She is concerned about the safety of herself and her baby and is open to learning about ways to increase her safety. Her sister is supportive and encourages her to participate in the study. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no allergies. She is not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She lives with her husband and sister in a small apartment. She works part-time as a cleaner in a local office. She is willing to complete the questionnaire in private.

The patient is a 56 year-old male who was diagnosed with colorectal cancer two years ago. He underwent a colectomy and was found to have metastasis to the liver. The liver metastases were treated with systemic chemotherapy, which resulted in a partial response of the liver metastases. However, a follow-up CT scan showed that the largest liver metastasis had increased in size. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has been deemed medically eligible to receive RFA. His platelets count is 120×103/mm3, total bilirubin is 1.2mg/dl, and creatinine level is 1.8 mg/dl. The patient has no other serious medical conditions and is willing to participate in the study. He has been informed about the risks and benefits of the treatment options and has signed the informed consent form.

A 15-year-old high school student from Israel is experiencing difficulties in school and at home. She feels overwhelmed with school work and social pressure. She has been experiencing mood swings and has had suicidal thoughts. Her parents are concerned about her well-being and have taken her to a therapist. The therapist has prescribed medication and recommended counseling sessions. The student has missed several days of school due to her mental health issues. Her parents are supportive and have been attending counseling sessions with her. They hope that participating in the SEYLE program will help their daughter learn healthy behaviors and coping mechanisms, as well as provide them with tools to help support her mental health. The student is interested in participating in the program and is willing to comply with all requirements. She is currently not taking any other medications and has no known medical conditions that would prevent her from participating.

A 42-year-old male diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis 6 years ago is seeking a new treatment option due to recent worsening of symptoms. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He currently takes methotrexate but has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He reports joint pain and stiffness, particularly in his hands and feet, as well as fatigue and difficulty with mobility. He has not tried any biologic medications before and is open to the possibility of using a biosimilar. He is an active smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works full-time as a construction worker and is physically active on a daily basis. He is willing to participate in an observational study to assess the effectiveness and utilization of originator and biosimilar anti-TNF agents in patients with psoriatic arthritis.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing muscle weakness and difficulty swallowing for the past 6 months. She has also developed a skin rash on her face and arms, and has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism and she is currently taking levothyroxine. She has been treated with high dose corticosteroids, azathioprine and methotrexate for the past 3 months with no improvement. Her muscle strength (MRC) is grade 3/5 and her CPK level is elevated. Her pulmonary function test shows %VC < 70% predicted and DLCO < 60% predicted. She has no significant history of allergies or other medical conditions. She is married and has two children. She has a Master's degree in business administration and is working as a consultant. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has been informed about the potential risks and benefits of the stem cell transplantation and has given written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no history of malignancy and is using effective birth control. Her platelet count is normal and ANC is 1500/ul.

A 38-year-old female patient presented to the clinic with a history of depression for the past two years. She has been taking sertraline for the past six months, but her symptoms have not improved. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and has difficulty enjoying activities she used to love. She also experiences fatigue, difficulty sleeping, and decreased appetite. She has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or other psychotic disorders. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses reliable birth control. She has no history of allergic reactions to medications, alcohol, or drug abuse. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications that are not allowed in this study. She is willing to switch to duloxetine and participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 7 years presents with complaints of pain and stiffness in her hands. She has been on methotrexate and prednisone for the past 6 months, with some improvement in her symptoms. She reports difficulty with activities of daily living, such as buttoning her clothes and holding utensils while eating, due to the pain and stiffness in her hands. She has a score of 6 on a visual analog scale (VAS) for pain in her right hand, which is her more aching hand. She has no history of hand surgery or any other upper limb splint usage. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has no known allergies to the splint material and lives in an accessible area.

45-year-old woman with a documented germline pathogenic BRCA1 mutation and no personal history of pancreatic cancer or other malignancies. She has a family history of pancreatic cancer with her father being diagnosed at age 60 and her paternal grandmother at age 72. She is interested in participating in a screening program to monitor for early pancreatic lesions and potentially reduce her risk of developing pancreatic cancer. She is willing to undergo annual screening with endoscopic ultrasound or MRI, as recommended by the study protocol. She is not pregnant and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

45F diagnosed with HER-2 negative breast cancer with metastasis to the liver and lungs. She underwent a modified radical mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Patient achieved complete remission but relapsed after 2 years with metastasis to the lungs and liver. She was started on bevacizumab for maintenance treatment but progressed after 6 weeks of treatment. Upon examination, she had no signs of ascites and no evidence of jaundice. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status was 1. Her past medical history was significant for hypertension and chronic migraines. She had no history of autoimmune disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or primary immunodeficiency. Her baseline laboratory values were within normal limits. The patient was willing to comply with the protocol and scheduled visits and examinations, including tumor biopsy and blood sampling. She was not pregnant or breastfeeding and agreed to use an effective method of birth control.

This is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with metastatic malignant melanoma. She has already undergone surgery and radiation therapy, but her disease has progressed. She has no evidence of significant active infection and has adequate renal and normal hepatic function. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the study and three months following termination of treatment. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work, but is unable to perform any strenuous physical activity. She is able to give informed consent and follow the guidelines given in the study. Her hematological function is not impaired, as evidenced by her laboratory parameters: WBC > 3.0x109/L; ANC > 1.5 x 109/L; Hgb > 9.0g/dL; PLT >100x109/L. She has never been treated with more than 2 prior chemotherapy regimens, nor has she undergone any previous immunotherapy regimens. She is eligible for participation in this Phase I/II clinical trial of Valproic Acid and Karenitecin for Melanoma.

Patient A is a 45-year-old German-speaking male who is scheduled to undergo an extensive surgical intervention in orthopaedic surgery. He has a history of anxiety and depression and tends to somatize his symptoms. He is capable of giving consent and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have any history of delirium, dementia, or other mental disorders with significant cerebral dysfunction. He is not under guardianship and is not participating in any other clinical studies. The patient will be assessed using standardized and validated questionnaires prior to surgery and in follow-up visits to determine the psychological and social factors that may contribute to his postoperative outcome.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension, but otherwise healthy, is scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. He has never had any major surgery before and has no known allergies or adverse reactions to anesthesia. He is classified as ASA class II. He understands and signs the informed consent form and agrees to participate in the study.

A 50 yo F diagnosed with primary aldosteronism with biochemical hyperaldosteronism and positive suppression test. The subject is not diagnosed with type 1 or type 2 diabetes and is not taking any anti-diabetic medication. The subject is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or on anticoagulants. The subject has no history of serious neurologic disease, immunological or hematological disorders, or asthma requiring frequent use of inhaled beta agonist. The subject has no gastrointestinal impairment that could interfere with drug absorption and has normal hepatic and hematocrit levels. The subject is willing to comply with the study protocol and undergo adrenalectomy or initiate medical treatment according to routine clinical care.

The patient is a 17-year-old male who has just started orthodontic treatment for moderate crowding in the lower anterior mandibular arch. He does not have any untreated caries or gingivitis. He is not taking any medication that may affect dental movement. He has not had any previous orthodontic treatment. He will be randomized to either the heat-activated NiTi archwire group or the superelastic NiTi archwire group. He will be followed up for three months and will have cast models taken every month to measure the amount of anterior lower arch crowding resolution. The mechanical properties of the archwires will also be measured before and after three months of clinical use. He will not be eligible if he has any systemic disease, has a history of trauma or root resorption in the lower arch, or does not attend more than one appointment per month.

The patient is a 65 year old male who has been diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) during a routine check-up. He has no significant medical history and takes only mild blood pressure medication. He has been referred to a vascular surgeon for evaluation and has been advised that he is a candidate for an endovascular stent graft repair of his AAA using the Endurant Stent Graft System. He has read and understood the patient informed consent form and has agreed to participate in the ENGAGE registry study. He is able and willing to comply with the study procedures and follow-up requirements.

Patient is a 58-year-old man who suffered a hemorrhagic stroke 12 months ago. He has been experiencing muscle stiffness in his right upper limb and has limited range of motion and muscle strength. He has not received any treatment for spasticity in the past three months, nor does he have any other neurological conditions that may affect motor response. He is able to communicate in English and is willing to comply with all study protocols, including having an MRI and completing all clinical assessments. His cognitive function and depression scores are within normal range. He has no known allergies to hyaluronidase and is not claustrophobic. He does not have any pacemakers or clips that may preclude MRI. He does not have any contracture at any joint with Modified Ashworth Scale score = 4 and major disability with modified Rankin Scale score ≥4. He does not have a history of psychiatric illness, complicated medical condition, or significant injury to either upper limb.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic heart failure six months ago after experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue and swelling in his legs. His echocardiogram revealed an ejection fraction of 35%. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He has been prescribed medications including ACE inhibitors, beta blockers, and diuretics to manage his heart failure. Despite the treatment, he still experiences occasional shortness of breath and fatigue. He is interested in participating in EVITA-HF to help improve the understanding and treatment of heart failure.

A 45-year-old man who has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest tightness for the past few months. He is a smoker and has a family history of lung disease. He has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and has been prescribed medication to manage his symptoms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to better understand the genetic factors involved in the development of lung disease. He has no other significant medical history and meets the inclusion criteria for the study as a smoker with symptoms consistent with pulmonary disease. He understands that he may be asked to undergo pulmonary function tests, chest x-rays, and bronchoscopy as part of the study. He is willing to participate in the study and hopes that the research will help improve the understanding and treatment of lung disease.

The patient is a 72-year-old male who was diagnosed with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) two years ago. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy but has relapsed and is now refractory to standard treatment options. He presents with fatigue, night sweats, and enlarged lymph nodes in his neck, axillae, and groin. He reports no significant medical history or other chronic illnesses. He has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG scale. His blood work shows a low red blood cell count, low platelet count, and high white blood cell count. Imaging studies reveal extensive lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer him a new treatment option for his relapsed MCL.

The patient is a healthy male or female between the ages of 18 and 60 years old, with a body weight greater than 50 kg and a BMI within the range of 18-30kg/m2. They have normal or high normal blood pressure, and a 24-hour holter with no clinically significant findings. The patient has a QTcB or QTcF less than 450 msec at screening and pre-dose and has normal liver function tests and creatinine clearance within the normal range at screening and pre-dose. They are capable of giving written informed consent, including compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form. The patient is not a vegetarian or vegan and is willing to consume a high-fat meal. They do not have a previous disease or a current medical condition that would exclude them from the trial. They have not made a suicide attempt in the past and do not pose a significant suicide risk. The patient does not have clinically significant proteinuria or hematuria or other clinically significant findings in urinalysis. They do not have symptoms of urinary dysfunction or ECG showing PR interval is >220 msec, or presence of intraventricular conduction disturbances (complete or incomplete BBB) at screening or prior to dosing. The patient does not have clinically significant arrhythmias, a positive pre-study Hepatitis B surface antigen, or positive Hepatitis C antibody result within 3 months of screening. They do not have current or chronic liver disease or biliary abnormalities, or a history of regular alcohol consumption within 6 months of the study. The patient does not smoke more than 10 cigarettes per week and has not participated in a clinical trial and received an investigational product within the following time period prior to the first dosing day in the current study: 30 days, 5 half-lives or twice the duration of the biological effect of the investigational product (whichever is longer). They have not been exposed to more than four new chemical entities within 12 months prior to the first dosing day. They are not using prescription or non-prescription drugs, have no history of sensitivity to any of the study medications, or components thereof or a history of drug or other allergy. The patient is mentally and legally capable and willing to follow the procedures outlined in the protocol.

A 56-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer completed her treatment six months ago. She is currently living with type 2 diabetes and hypertension for over a year. She is a single mother of two children and works as a part-time cashier at a grocery store. She is struggling to manage her chronic illnesses while taking care of her children and working. She experiences fatigue level 5 out of 10 on average within the past 7 days. She is interested in improving her physical activity level and overall health but has limited time and resources to attend a gym or group exercise classes. She owns a smartphone and is willing to participate in a technology-enhanced home-based exercise program. Her annual household income is below $30,000 for a family of three. She has no active infection and is not diagnosed with any psychological disorder.

A 45-year-old Asian male with a history of chronic hepatitis B presents to the clinic with complaints of yellowing of the skin and eyes for the past two weeks. He reports a loss of appetite, fatigue, and mild abdominal discomfort. He denies any fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. He has a past medical history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril 10mg daily. He has a history of alcohol use in the past but has been abstinent for the past year. He denies any illicit drug use. On physical examination, he is jaundiced with scleral icterus. His abdomen is soft and non-tender with no hepatosplenomegaly or ascites. Laboratory studies reveal elevated levels of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) greater than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), and gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT) greater than 3 times the ULN. His total bilirubin level is 2 times the ULN. The patient is diagnosed with intrahepatic cholestasis, meeting the EASL 2009 diagnosis criteria. He is positive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and has a detectable hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA level. He is a candidate for the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of S-adenosyl-L-methionine in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B patients with cholestasis.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has a history of coronary heart disease. He has a family history of heart disease and has been diagnosed with high cholesterol levels. He has been taking medication to manage his cholesterol levels for the past year, but his LDL-C levels are still above the currently accepted minimum target level. He has experienced chest pain in the past and has undergone a coronary angiogram which showed significant narrowing of his coronary arteries. The patient is generally healthy and does not have any other major medical conditions. He is willing to participate in this study to determine if further lowering of his LDL-C levels can provide additional cardiovascular risk reduction.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has been suffering from migraines for the past 5 years. She experiences migraines with aura, characterized by visual disturbances such as flashing lights or zigzag lines, and followed by intense headaches. She has tried various medications to manage her migraines but has not found any that provide significant relief. She experiences migraines on an average of 2-3 times per month, and the attacks last for several hours. She has no history of cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the blood-brain and blood-dura barrier during migraine attacks using MRI. She understands that she will be given a phone number to call when she experiences a migraine attack and will be asked to undergo an MRI during and outside of the attack. She is interested in participating in the study to help further research on migraine and potentially find new treatments for her condition.

Sophie is a 5-year-old girl who was diagnosed with methylmalonic acidemia/aciduria (MMA) due to methylmalonyl-coenzyme A mutase (MUT) deficiency. She has elevated plasma methylmalonic acid levels and confirmed diagnosis by molecular genetic testing. Sophie has never received gene therapy for the treatment of MMA and has not undergone any organ transplantation. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is above 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, and she is not on chronic dialysis. Sophie is currently not taking any medications for her MMA condition. She is in good general health and is able to participate in physical activities. Her parents are willing to give consent for her participation in the study.

A 68-year-old healthy male with no significant past medical history, who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for influenza A/H1N1 vaccines. The patient has no known allergies to vaccines or vaccine ingredients, and is able to provide legal identification. The patient understands the informed consent and is willing to sign. They have not had contact with any cases of influenza A (H1N1) virus, and do not have any autoimmune diseases or immunodeficiencies. They have not had any serious adverse reactions to vaccines in the past, and do not have asthma, diabetes, or any bleeding disorders. The patient has not had any malignancies, seizures, or thyroid disorders that required medication in the past year. They have not received any blood products or other investigational research agents within the past 3 months, and have not received any live attenuated vaccines within the past 30 days. The patient's current axillary temperature is below 37.0 centigrade. The patient does not have any medical, psychiatric, or social conditions that would contraindicate participation in the study.

A 48-year-old woman presents with a history of renal cell carcinoma (RCC). She was diagnosed with RCC 3 years ago and underwent a partial nephrectomy for the removal of a 3.5 cm renal mass. She has been in remission since then, but a recent imaging study revealed a new 4 cm mass in the remaining kidney. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements, including regular follow-up visits for the next 5 years. The patient has been informed of the study and has provided written informed consent, including data privacy authorization. She is not participating in any other clinical trials using drugs or devices.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate plaque psoriasis. She has been experiencing red, scaly patches on her skin that are itchy and uncomfortable. She has tried various over-the-counter creams and ointments, but they have not provided much relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of a new treatment for plaque psoriasis. She is in good mental and physical health, and is not currently taking any biologics or other medications that could interfere with the study. She understands and agrees to the terms described in the informed consent, and is willing to return for follow-up visits. She is not pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes and coronary artery disease. He has been experiencing recurrent chest pain and has a diagnosis of unstable angina. He has been receiving optimal medical therapy for his condition but still experiences some symptoms. He is currently taking metformin and a statin. He has leukocytosis and his white blood cell count is 8000/μL. He is not a current smoker and has no history of liver cirrhosis or clinical cholestasis. He has normal renal function with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 70 mL/min/1.73m2. He has no history of active malignancy and is not currently taking any medications that may interact with colchicine. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III high-grade serous ovarian cancer, who has undergone cytoreductive surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. She has been on olaparib for the past 6 months, but her cancer has progressed despite treatment. The patient has a performance status of 1 and is willing to undergo tumour biopsy pre-treatment if a biopsy at the time of progression on olaparib is not available. She has adequate bone marrow, renal, and hepatic function per local laboratory reference range, with a Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 55% by echocardiograms or multigated acquisition (MUGA) scan within 28 days of registration. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She is currently using effective contraception and is willing to continue its use throughout the study treatment and for 3 months after the last dose of study treatment(s).

This clinical trial is seeking family caregivers of patients affected by major neurocognitive disorder, such as Alzheimer's disease. The ideal patient for this trial would be a family member or close friend who is currently providing care for a loved one with cognitive decline that compromises their independence. The patient should not have a diagnosis of major depression or other psychiatric conditions and should not be currently participating in another program of intervention for caregivers or TCC. The patient should be an adult who is not protected by the law and has not lost their liberty by court or administrative order. The patient must also be willing to sign an informed consent form.

A 12-year-old male patient with a past medical history of dilated cardiomyopathy and heart transplant was referred to the cardiology department for clinically-indicated cardiovascular catheterization. The patient has been on immunosuppressive medication since the transplant and was currently asymptomatic. He had no known drug allergies and no family history of heart disease. His vital signs were within normal limits. His echocardiogram showed mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction with no significant valvular abnormalities. The patient was scheduled for a diagnostic cardiac MRI before the catheterization procedure to understand cardiac function and localize the proposed catheter trajectory from the access site into the targeted cardiovascular chambers. The MRI-guided catheterization was performed with continuous recording of electrocardiogram signals and transcutaneous hemoglobin ("pulse") oximetry. Hemodynamic measurements were obtained from the targeted cardiovascular chambers using fluid-filled transducers connected to the catheters, and blood hemoglobin saturation specimens were collected. Additional research cardiac MRI imaging was performed to determine T1 and T2 values, with 6 short axis slices and one long axis slice positions identified for T1 map and T2 map acquisitions. At the conclusion of the MR imaging and MR-guided right heart catheterization procedure, the subject was returned to the X-ray suite for cardiac biopsy. The biopsy specimens were obtained using image overlay software to display the regions of abnormal T1 and T2 onto the fluoroscopy system. The patient was observed for complications in the cardiac procedure recovery unit for at least 6 hours before being discharged. A serum creatinine blood test was collected at the time the clinically indicated IV was placed. The blood samples were identified with the study ID number only and stored in a secure freezer owned and maintained by the department of cardiology located at the Sheikh Zayed campus. The patient will be assessed for early and late complications at the time of discharge and again approximately 2-6 weeks ± 7 days post-procedure.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is overweight with a BMI of 29. She has a sedentary lifestyle and has not been exercising for the past 6 months. She is generally healthy and has not been diagnosed with any chronic illnesses. She is a non-smoker and has not used antibiotics in the past 3 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of exercise on gut microbiota, CVD risk factors and appetite regulation in overweight women. The patient is available to attend 4 weekly sessions of endurance type exercise lasting for 30, 40, 50, and 60 minutes in weeks 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively. She is willing to undergo submaximal exercise tests and a 7-hour experimental trial during which blood samples will be collected and metabolic rate will be measured before and after consumption of standardized breakfast and lunch. She is also willing to record her diet for 3 days and provide fresh stool samples during these 3 days.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who participated in the previous EXESAS study to evaluate the effect of exercise on sleep apnea. He was in the control group and received only standard dietetic and physical activity counseling. He has moderate sleep apnea with an Apnea Hypopnea Index (AHI) of 23. He did not report daytime sleepiness with an ESS score of 8. He does not have any known respiratory or heart disease and no contraindication to exercise training was discovered during the stress test. He is not currently receiving treatment for sleep apnea and does not have an AHI greater than 30. He has agreed to participate in the follow-up study to evaluate the long-term effect of exercise on sleep apnea.

The patient is a 20-year-old female with Fitzpatrick skin type II, who is interested in participating in a dermatological study to help improve topical anesthesia procedures. She has no history of keloid or hypertrophic scar formation, and has normal wound healing. She has no active skin diseases, allergies to local anesthesia, or chronic pain or other alterations in pain sensation. She is not pregnant or lactating and is competent to understand the procedure. She is not currently taking any systemic analgesics or medications that can influence pain sensation. She has not had excessive sun exposure recently.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic shoulder pain for the past few years due to osteoarthritis. He has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and corticosteroid injections, but they have not provided long-lasting relief. He is scheduled for a total shoulder arthroplasty and is interested in participating in a study that examines the natural history of pain after the surgery. He is fluent in English and is capable of providing informed consent. He is not on any anticoagulant medication, and there is no evidence of infection at the injection site. He is not undergoing the surgery due to trauma or rheumatoid arthritis, and it is not a revision or conversion surgery. He is not planned to receive tranexamic acid during the surgery.

A 54-year-old woman has been experiencing persistent bone pain, fatigue, and recurrent infections. After undergoing various diagnostic tests, she was diagnosed with multiple myeloma based on the presence of elevated calcium, renal failure, anemia, and bone lesions. The patient is in good physical condition with an ECOG performance status of 0, and has no history of significant cardiovascular disease or previous malignancies. However, she has a total bilirubin level of 2.0 x ULN due to Gilbert syndrome, and her ALT and AST levels are both elevated at 2.5 x ULN. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent. She has no known allergies to humanized or murine monoclonal antibodies, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not received radiotherapy to multiple sites within the past four weeks, and does not have active infections by HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and will be considered for enrollment.

58-year-old male smoker with a history of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer that has metastasized to the liver and bones. He has previously undergone neoadjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He now presents with increasing pain in the right femur and left iliac crest. Imaging studies reveal progression of the disease with multiple new bone metastases. Biopsy confirms the presence of non-small cell lung cancer. He is otherwise in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. He has no history of allergic reactions to any of the compounds used in the trial. Lab values are within normal limits, and there is no evidence of interstitial pneumonitis or pulmonary fibrosis on imaging. He has not received any prior therapy targeting the EGFR or Insulin-like growth factor (IGFR) pathways. He has not received any prior systemic therapy, including bevacizumab for advanced stage NSCLC. He is not pregnant or nursing. He has no significant uncontrolled cardiac disease within the past 6 months. He is willing to use effective contraception during and for 3 months after the last dose of cixutumumab.

This is a 26 year-old woman who has recently given birth to a healthy baby girl. The baby is now one week old and the mother is interested in participating in a study about the epidemiology of rotavirus infection in North India community. The mother has no history of chronic gastrointestinal disease or any other illness requiring hospitalization. She is able to understand the study procedures and has provided consent for her baby to participate in the study. The family has no plans to move within the next 12 months. The mother will be responsible for bringing her baby to weekly follow-up appointments and will be instructed on the signs and symptoms of suspected intussusception, dehydration and danger signs that require hospital referral. She will also be asked to provide stool specimens in the event that her baby experiences gastroenteritis.

30-year-old female, recently diagnosed with ITP, presents with a history of easy bruising, petechiae, and gum bleeding. She has no significant past medical history, no history of bleeding disorders in the family, and is not taking any medications at present. Her platelet count at the time of diagnosis was 22 billion/L. She has no active infections and is not pregnant or nursing. She has no history of bone marrow stem cell disorder, liver disease, or malignancy. She has no history of active tuberculosis or immunodeficiency. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of blisibimod for ITP treatment.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who recently underwent surgery to remove primary liver cancer. The patient's tumour was histologically-proven to be hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The patient is generally healthy with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient's Child Pugh classification is A. There is no evidence of tumour metastasis or co-existing malignant disease. The patient has not had any prior recurrence of HCC or any liver resection prior to the most recent surgery. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if PI-88 can help prevent the recurrence of HCC after surgery.

The patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of HIV-1 infection and ongoing antiretroviral therapy. Despite the current treatment, he has evidence of HIV-1 replication and documented genotypic or phenotypic resistance to at least one ART drug within three drug classes or within two drug classes with limited treatment options. He has been diagnosed with CCR5-tropic virus, as determined by Monogram Biosciences Trofile® Assay. He has a plasma HIV-1 RNA level of ≥ 400 copies/mL and documented detectable viral load (HIV-1 RNA >50 copies/mL) within the last 3 months prior to the screening visit. He is willing to remain on treatment without any changes or additions to the OBT regimen, except for toxicity management or upon meeting criteria for treatment failure. The patient has met the laboratory values criteria and is willing to use 2 medically accepted methods of contraception during the course of the study. He is willing and able to participate in all aspects of the study, including use of SC medication, completion of subjective evaluations, attendance at scheduled clinic visits, and compliance with all protocol requirements as evidenced by providing written informed consent. He has no history of anaphylaxis to oral or parenteral drugs, bleeding disorder or anti-coagulant therapy, and has not participated in an experimental drug trial(s) within 30 days of the screening visit. The patient does not have any known allergy or antibodies to the study drug or excipients. He is not currently receiving radiation or cytotoxic chemotherapy, immunosuppressants or immunomodulating agents (e.g., interleukins, interferons), hydroxyurea or foscarnet, or oral or parenteral corticosteroids. The patient does not have any clinical condition that, in the investigator's judgment, would potentially compromise study compliance or the ability to evaluate safety/efficacy.

A 23-year-old man comes to the clinic seeking information about safe sex practices. He identifies as gay and has been sexually active with multiple partners over the past year. He has never been tested for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) and is concerned about his risk of contracting HIV.
