He reports occasional drug use, including marijuana and cocaine, but states he always uses condoms during sexual activity. He is currently not in a monogamous relationship and is not using any form of hormonal contraception. He is a full-time student and lives with roommates in an off-campus apartment. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial focused on preventing the transmission of STDs in the youth through effective intervention.

The patient is an adult aged 35 to 65 years old who has been diagnosed with high blood pressure, with a systolic blood pressure between 120-159 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure between 80-99 mmHg. They have a BMI of 18.5 kg/m2 or higher and have access to a smartphone with a data plan, valid email address, and are willing to receive daily text messages. The patient is able and willing to participate in online study videoconferencing visits (Zoom) and reads and writes in English. The patient has not had a cardiovascular disease event (e.g. stroke, myocardial infarction) in the prior 6 months, has not undergone bariatric surgery in the last 12 months or planned during the study period, does not have active cancer or recent hospitalization due to psychiatric condition or event, is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period, and does not have documented dementia. The patient is interested in improving their blood pressure through a heart-healthy eating plan and is willing to participate in a digital health program to achieve this goal.

The patient is a 34 year old woman who was diagnosed with a low-grade astrocytoma 2 years ago. She underwent surgical resection followed by radiation therapy and chemotherapy. She has recently started experiencing headaches and seizures again. An MRI scan shows evidence of disease progression. She is interested in exploring alternative therapies and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and a life expectancy of more than 2 months. Her laboratory results show WBC count of 3,200/mm^3 and platelet count of 75,000/mm^3. Her bilirubin, SGOT, and SGPT levels are all within normal limits. Her creatinine level is 1.8 mg/dL. She has no history of hypertension, heart disease, or lung disease. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She has not received any antineoplaston therapy in the past.

A 6-month-old baby girl who has been screened positive for HLA DQ2/X (X is neither DQ2 or DQ8) in the GPPAD-02 screening is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a gluten-restricted diet on the risk of developing celiac disease and IA. The baby's parents are both willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. There are no known chronic disorders affecting the baby's diet. The baby has been breastfed exclusively for the first 4 months of life and then started on solid foods, including gluten-containing foods. The baby has not exhibited any symptoms of celiac disease or other autoimmune disorders at this time.

Patient is a 32-year-old male OEF veteran who has been experiencing difficulty maintaining an active lifestyle since returning home. He has noticed a significant decrease in his physical activity levels and has gained weight since leaving the military. He is interested in starting a physical activity program to improve his overall health but prefers technology-mediated interventions. He owns a smartphone and has access to a computer with an internet connection. He is comfortable with the use of wearable devices and is willing to wear a Fitbit Charge 2 as part of the Stay Strong program. He is currently receiving care at a VA Medical Center and has a VA Health Care Provider responsible for his care in the system. He is younger than 65 years old and is competent to consent to a research study.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with relapsed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL). She has previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy for her disease, but her lymphoma has progressed. She has a confirmed diagnosis of CD20 positive NHL and has measurable disease with at least one extranodal tumor mass of more than 1.5 cm in the GTD. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she has adequate bone marrow function with ANC of 1.2 x 109/L, platelet count of 80 x 109/L, and hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL. She has no known brain metastases and has not received any systemic corticosteroids or monoclonal antibodies within the last 28 days. She has not undergone prior anti-CD137 monoclonal antibody therapy. Her serum creatinine is within normal limits, and her total serum bilirubin is less than or equal to 1.5 x ULN. She is interested in exploring new treatment options and is willing to participate in this clinical trial.

56-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma (PTCL) of the Angioimmunoblastic subtype. She has not received any prior systemic therapy for lymphoma. The patient has a measurable tumor mass of 2.5 cm in one dimension and measurable in two dimensions. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has no known central nervous system (CNS) involvement by lymphoma and no active viral infection with HIV or hepatitis type B or C. She has no prior history of malignancies other than PTCL. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the efficacy and safety of first-line CC-486 plus CHOP in patients with PTCL who have received no prior systemic therapy.

The patient is a 25-year-old female basketball player who has been training regularly for the past 4 months. She is currently studying physical therapy at a university and is in good health. She does not smoke, drink or use any drugs. Her body mass index is 24.5 which is within the normal range. She is not currently injured and has no history of any chronic disease. Her blood tests show normal levels of all relevant biomarkers. She is interested in participating in this study to gain a better understanding of the effect of exercise on serum uncoupling protein-1, irisin, interleukin 6 levels, and blood lipid and lipoprotein concentrations.

The patient is an 70-year-old American man who is experiencing age-related symptoms such as decreased energy, cognitive decline, and poor blood circulation. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol and is currently taking medications for both conditions. He has not had any cardiac or cerebrovascular ischemic events within the past year. He does not have a history of smoking, but he has a family history of lung cancer. He has no history of malignancy within the past year. His cognitive function is slightly impaired, but he is still able to perform daily activities. He has mild chronic renal failure with a GFR of 45. He does not have uncontrolled diabetes or any immunosuppressant therapy. He has no contraindications to perform MRI scans. He does not have any pulmonary diseases that would make him ineligible for the trial.

A 62-year-old man came to the clinic for a routine physical exam. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He exercises regularly, eats a healthy diet, and doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. He hasn't received any hepatitis B vaccine or had any previous exposure to hepatitis B virus. He is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. His BMI is 27 kg/m². His blood tests indicate that he is negative for HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HBc, HCV, and HIV. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the immune response to a hepatitis B vaccine in healthy older adults.

65-year-old male patient with a history of smoking for 40 years presented with cough, fatigue, and shortness of breath. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are under control with medications. He has never been diagnosed with any type of cancer before. Physical examination revealed decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. Chest X-ray and CT scan showed a mass in the right lung with mediastinal lymph nodes involvement. The patient underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. He received 4 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy and showed no signs of disease progression. He is now considered eligible for maintenance therapy with bevacizumab and/or pemetrexed. He consented to participate in the study and has no history of other cancers or medical conditions that would prevent him from undergoing PET scans or participating in the study.

A relatively healthy male veteran who is at least 50 years of age and has no major health issues such as cancer, heart disease, high blood pressure, or diabetes. The patient must be willing to participate in the study for at least five years and provide information on their medical history, lifestyle, and health status. The patient must be a mixed racial group (for example, White, African-American, and Hispanic) and be willing to attend follow-up clinic visits and complete biannual forms and telephone interviews. The patient must have a life expectancy of at least 5 years. This study is an observational cohort and does not involve any treatment or intervention. The purpose of the study is to gather information on what types of diseases male veterans develop and to determine if racial differences in lifestyle, blood test results, or genes are related to the types of diseases that are found.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has struggled with her weight for several years. Her body mass index (BMI) falls within the range of 25 to 35 kg/m², which puts her in the overweight or obese category. She has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past but has found it difficult to maintain long-term weight loss. She is a non-smoker and does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse. She exercises for less than 3 hours per week and is in good physical condition. She has not used any weight reduction treatments or products in the last 3 months prior to the screening visit. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using an efficient contraceptive method. She has not had bariatric surgery and does not have a history of eating disorders, diabetes, or other significant medical conditions. She is willing to follow diet and lifestyle instructions throughout the study and to take study capsules three times a day for 3 months and 1 week. She is registered with the French Social Security and has provided written informed consent after receiving and understanding the subject information.

67-year-old Caucasian male with mild cognitive impairment, as diagnosed by his neurologist. His primary caregiver, his wife, is also willing to give her oral consent for his participation in the study. His BMI is 27.5 kg/m², and he has no history of smoking, diabetes, or COVID-19 infection. His Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 23 out of 30. He has no neurological deficits, and his brain MRI has shown no signs of other causes of neurocognitive disorders. He is not currently taking any medications that interfere with taste. He has fasted for at least 2 hours before the study, and he is able to perform cognitive testing.

Pt is a 35yo male with a long-standing history of ulcerative colitis, diagnosed 8 years ago. The patient has been treated with aminosalicylates and corticosteroids without achieving a sustained remission. The patient has been unable to tolerate 6-mercaptopurine or azathioprine. The patient experienced a partial response to infliximab but had to discontinue due to severe infusion reactions. The patient's symptoms include bloody diarrhea, cramping abdominal pain, and urgency. The patient's last Mayo score was 8 with endoscopic subscore of 2. The patient is sexually inactive and willing to use contraception during the study. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent. The patient has not self-injected any agent in the past. The patient does not have Crohn's disease or inflammatory bowel disease type unclassified. The patient has not undergone (procto)colectomy for ulcerative colitis or has an ostomy. The patient has not received adalimumab therapy. The patient does not have acute severe IV steroid-refractory colitis. The patient is not using any concomitant biologic agents. The patient does not have active tuberculosis or any opportunistic infection within 6 months prior to the first injection. The patient does not have any history of demyelinating disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, lymphoproliferative disease, or any unknown malignancy within the prior 5 years. The patient does not have active hepatitis B infection, allergy or sensitivity to golimumab or its excipients, or latex sensitivity. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient does not have any condition that would prevent completion of the study.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman diagnosed with ALS. She has a history of progressive weakness that started in her right hand and has spread to involve her left hand and legs. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has undergone a recent lumbar puncture as part of her diagnostic workup, and an additional 3 ml of cerebrospinal fluid was collected for storage in the CSF repository. She has no history of bleeding disorders or spinal cord abnormalities, and the lumbar puncture was performed without any complications. Her neurological exam is significant for diffuse weakness and atrophy in the upper and lower extremities, and brisk reflexes. She has no sensory deficits, and her cranial nerves are intact. Her medical records show diagnostic workup including electromyography and nerve conduction studies which were consistent with the diagnosis of ALS. The patient has provided informed consent for the additional collection of CSF as part of the repository.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD. He has been taking stimulant medications for the past few months as prescribed by his physician, but he is still having trouble falling asleep at night. His parents have tried various sleep aids, but nothing seems to be working. They are interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of melatonin as a treatment for initial insomnia in children with ADHD. The boy is in good health and does not have any other psychiatric or neurological diagnoses that may affect sleep. He is not taking any other medications except for the stimulant medication for his ADHD. The boy and his parents are willing to participate in the trial and are committed to following the study protocol.

A 45-year-old male with a family history of high cholesterol and heart disease is concerned about his own cholesterol levels. He recently had a routine blood test that showed his LDL-C level is 130 mg/dL. He has never been diagnosed with heart disease, but he is aware that he is at higher risk because of his family history. He exercises regularly and eats a healthy diet, but he has not been able to lower his cholesterol through lifestyle changes alone. He does not have any history of heart failure or uncontrolled hypertension.

56-year-old male admitted to the Trauma ICU following a motor vehicle accident. The patient is intubated and on ventilator support due to multiple rib fractures and pulmonary contusions. The patient has a history of smoking and is a heavy drinker. The patient has a full set of teeth with some mild dental decay. The patient does not have any known allergies to medication or oral care products. The patient has consented to participate in the study and will be randomized to either the treatment or standard group.

A 30-year old male with healthy skin is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the potential of a gel to reduce steroid induced skin atrophy. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day indoors. He has no history of skin conditions, allergies, or sensitivity to topical products. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. The patient is willing to follow the study protocol and has hairless areas on his volar arms that are sufficient for measurements. His skin is of Fitzpatrick type II and he has no history or current evidence of infection, eczema or any relevant skin disease. He is interested in contributing to medical research and is eager to learn more about the study.

A 51-year-old woman diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has been living with PAH for 2 years with a WHO functional class III status. She experiences shortness of breath with exertion, fatigue, and occasional chest pain. She has not experienced any recent changes in medical therapy for PAH in the past 3 months. She has not enrolled in pulmonary rehab in the past 6 months. She has never participated in regular exercise and her physical activity level is very low. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any other comorbidities that limit physical activity. She has a computer and internet access. She is competent to give informed consent and is willing to be followed up at the University of Michigan Hospital Centers for at least 1 year. She is fluent in English.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He has a history of smoking and high blood pressure. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath, which are exacerbated by physical activity. He has been advised to undergo off-pump coronary artery bypass graft surgery to improve his condition. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and has no other medical conditions. The patient is alert and cooperative, and physical examination reveals no abnormalities. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) 5 years ago. She experiences bladder-sphincter dysnergia and has been managing her bladder with clean intermittent self-catheterization (CISC). She has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs), with approximately 4 episodes per year. She has no other associated neurological disorders and her Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score is 4. She has not received tibial neuro-stimulation or sacral neuro-modulation in the last 3 months. She is not currently receiving alpha-blocker treatment and has no history of benign prostatic hypertrophy. Her last ultrasound scan was 4 months ago and showed no bladder diverticula or renal abnormalities. She has normal renal function and no metallic prosthesis on her lower limbs or pacemaker. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her bladder emptying efficiency.

A 70-year-old woman with a history of dementia has been living in a nursing home for the past 6 months. She has a history of falls in the past, which led to a hip fracture and hospitalization. Currently, she is taking several medications for her dementia, hypertension, and diabetes. The patient has been identified as having a high risk for falls with injury, and she meets the inclusion criteria for the NH PRIDE study. The nursing home staff has agreed to participate in the study, and the patient's family has provided informed consent for her to participate in the study. The patient will be monitored for injurious falls, and the nursing home staff will receive training on preventing falls and managing medications to reduce falls. The study aims to develop a consistent approach to prevent falls in nursing home residents and reduce the risk of injury.

35 F with a history of obesity, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She has been feeling hopeless, sad, and has lost interest in activities she once enjoyed, such as cooking and spending time with friends. She has also been experiencing difficulty sleeping and has been feeling fatigued most of the time. Her primary care physician referred her to participate in a study aimed at evaluating the effectiveness of a one-day Acceptance and Commitment Training + Illness Management (ACT-IM) intervention for patients with comorbid vascular disease risk factors and depression or anxiety. She has agreed to participate in this study and will undergo a baseline assessment that includes a physical exam, blood draw, and non-invasive measure of blood vessel health using EndoPAT. She will then be randomized to either the ACT-IM intervention or Treatment-As-Usual (TAU). Follow-up assessments will take place at 2-, 6-, 12-, and 24-weeks to evaluate her mental health, functioning, illness self-management, blood vessel health, and blood.

A 9-year-old boy was diagnosed with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) after presenting with proteinuria and edema of the lower limbs. Despite treatment with corticosteroids and calcineurin inhibitors, the boy's condition did not improve and he developed drug-resistant FSGS. The boy's GFR is ≥ 60 ml/min/1.73 m2. His parents have given informed consent to participate in the post-approval study of Liposorber® LA-15 System for the treatment of FSGS in children. The boy is not currently taking ACE inhibitors or antihypertensive drugs other than ACE inhibitors. He has no known hypersensitivity to dextran sulfate, heparin, or ethylene oxide. He has no medical conditions or disorders that would limit his life expectancy or cause noncompliance with the study plan. He is not currently receiving extracorporeal circulation therapy and has no cardiac impairments, thyroid disease, or liver abnormalities. The boy weighs 25 kg.

A 28-year-old female, who is generally healthy, has volunteered for this study. She works as an accountant and has no underlying medical conditions. She has no allergies and takes no medications. She has a normal sense of taste and smell and no difficulties with chewing or swallowing. She exercises regularly and eats a balanced diet. She is not a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has lived in the UK for over 3 years and has no plans to travel outside the country during the study period. She has no history of blood sampling difficulties or disorders that would make blood sampling dangerous to her health. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about her selenium status and how it can be improved through diet.

The patient is a 23-year-old Active Duty service member who recently reported to Nellis Air Force Base. He has been experiencing lower back pain for the past two weeks that started after a strenuous physical training session. The pain is described as dull and achy, and radiates from the lower back to the left leg. The patient rates the pain as a 7 out of 10 on a pain scale. He has been taking over the counter NSAIDs intermittently, but the pain persists. He has no history of chronic low back pain or underlying rheumatologic conditions. He is not currently pregnant or attempting to become pregnant, and he is not taking opioid medications. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for his acute low back pain.

47-year-old male with a history of diabetes and obesity who has undergone bariatric surgery in the past. He has had a history of uncontrolled diabetes and has been on insulin for the past 5 years. He has tried multiple diets and exercise regimens but has been unable to achieve significant weight loss. He is currently on metformin and insulin, and his HbA1c is 8.2%. He is interested in participating in a study to investigate the influence of substantial weight loss due to bariatric surgery on brain functions. He has no history of claustrophobia and has no contraindications for fMRI. He is willing to undergo fMRI scans before and after the surgery.

A 27 year old pregnant woman is currently in her second trimester and has a history of preterm birth in her previous pregnancy. She delivered her first baby at 34 weeks gestation and her baby had to stay in the neonatal intensive care unit for one month. She has a mobile phone capable of downloading apps from the Apple App Store or Google Play and is fluent in English. She is interested in participating in the study to reduce the risk of preterm birth in her current pregnancy and any future pregnancies. She is willing to consent to the study and is open to using technology to improve her knowledge of healthy behaviors and adherence to recommended care. She is excited to be a co-creator of content and participate in a support network that can capture her behavior regarding her lifestyle, environment, social factors, and personal health status. She is hoping to improve her inter-pregnancy interval, avoid postpartum depression, improve infant-mother bonding, and breast milk feeding. She is committed to following the study protocol and is eager to be a part of the effort to reduce infant mortality.

The patient is a 50 year old Hispanic male who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes for the past 10 years. He was recently referred to an ophthalmologist due to complaints of blurred vision and difficulty reading. Upon examination, the ophthalmologist diagnosed him with Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) and recommended treatment. The patient has no prior history of ocular treatment and has not undergone any ocular surgery. His medical history is significant for high blood pressure, which is currently well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He works as a mechanic and spends most of his day on his feet. He is able to read and write in English and Spanish. He is eager to participate in the study as he wants to find the best treatment option for his condition.

45-year-old male with a history of chronic stable angina and hypertension presented to the hospital with chest pain. He underwent diagnostic coronary angiography, which revealed evidence of coronary pathology requiring further imaging to guide treatment. He has no history of significant renal insufficiency. The patient has a history of smoking and is currently on statin therapy. He is compliant with his medications and has no known drug allergies. He reports occasional alcohol use but no illicit drug use. He denies any recent changes in his chest pain pattern, shortness of breath, or palpitations. Physical examination is unremarkable except for mild hypertension. His laboratory studies, including complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and cardiac biomarkers, were within normal limits. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study to determine the differences between high-definition IVUS images and OCT in imaging coronary pathology.

A 50-year-old male patient presents with elevated liver enzymes and is referred for a liver biopsy to determine the underlying cause. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and is currently taking a blood thinner for a previous deep vein thrombosis. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to undergo either a percutaneous or endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy. He is not pregnant and has no known coagulopathies or hemophilia.

A 25-year-old female with Alopecia Universalis has been experiencing hair loss for the past 5 years. She has tried various treatments, including corticosteroids and topical minoxidil, but has not seen any significant improvement. She is frustrated with the lack of options for treatment and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a topical solution. She is willing and able to follow all study instructions and attend all study visits. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant during the duration of the study. She does not have any active skin disease on her scalp or any other conditions that would interfere with the study assessments. She does not wear a permanent or difficult to remove hairpiece or wig.

A 12-year-old male with a history of severe asthma presents to the pediatric pulmonology and allergy department at Necker Hospital in Paris. He has been experiencing frequent episodes of wheezing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness, despite being on high doses of inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting bronchodilators. He has a past medical history of eczema and environmental allergies. He reports that his symptoms have been affecting his daily activities and school attendance. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is significant for wheezing and diminished breath sounds in the lung fields. The patient is scheduled for bronchial endoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage, biopsy, and blood collection as part of a clinical trial investigating the role of type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) in severe pediatric asthma. The study aims to determine if ILC2 are more abundant in the bronchial mucosa, bronchoalveolar lavage, and blood of children with severe asthma compared to non-asthmatic controls. The results of the study may help improve the understanding of the mechanisms responsible for bronchial inflammation in asthma and lead to the development of new therapies to prevent its development.

Patient is a 24-year-old male athlete who is currently competing at the varsity level in track and field. He has been training in his sport for the past 5 years and has been competing at a high level for the last 3 years. He is in good health with no medical conditions that would be affected by caffeine or require avoidance of caffeine. He reports that he consumes caffeine regularly as part of his training regimen, typically in the form of coffee or energy drinks. He has no known allergies or adverse reactions to caffeine. He is able to commit to four 2-hour visits to the lab 7 days apart and is willing to abstain from caffeine for 4 weeks during the study. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his athletic performance through the use of caffeine. He will be compensated $50 for his participation in the study.

A 25-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with lupus for 3 years is interested in participating in the ANTLER pilot intervention. She meets at least 4 of the 11 ACR classification criteria for SLE and has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She is able to ambulate at least household distances and is able to provide informed consent. She has no history of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus or cardiovascular disease. Her blood pressure is within normal limits (SBP 120, DBP 80). She reports feeling fatigued and has difficulty sleeping at night. She wants to improve her physical activity level, dietary/nutritional intake, and sleep quality. She is willing to wear the Actigraph accelerometer 24 hours/day and complete a sleep log for measurement of physical activity and sleep. She is also willing to utilize a smartphone application to self-monitor changes in her behaviors and receive feedback.

The patient is a 5-year-old girl diagnosed with Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) six months ago. She has been experiencing joint pain and stiffness in both knees and wrists. Physical examination revealed joint effusion and limited range of motion in affected joints. Laboratory tests showed negative rheumatoid factor and positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA). Her previous treatment plan includes nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and methotrexate, but the symptoms are not completely controlled. She has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and occasional constipation. Her parents are interested in trying new treatment options for her JIA and are willing to participate in the study.

A 9-year-old boy is diagnosed with Biliary Atresia and is in need of a pediatric liver transplantation. He has failed Kasai procedure and his laboratory findings show elevated total bilirubin, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase. He has no significant past medical history and does not have any other comorbidities. His family history is unremarkable for any liver disease or autoimmune disorders. He has not been on any long-term medications and has no known allergies. The transplant team has explained the potential benefits and risks of the steroid-free immunosuppressive regimen to him and his parents, and they have given informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and attending her first antenatal care visit at a health facility in Cabo Delgado province, Mozambique. She has been diagnosed with HIV at the same visit and is living in the catchment area of the health facility. She is able to provide informed consent and has signed the consent form for the study. She is not currently on any antiretroviral therapy (ART) and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study. She is excited to participate in the study and contribute to the improvement of maternal and infant health in her community.

The patient is a premature newborn baby girl born at 30 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 950 grams. She was initially admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to respiratory distress syndrome and received surfactant therapy. She had a stable course until day 7 of life, where she developed abdominal distension, bilious vomiting, and bloody stool. She was diagnosed with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) stage III according to Bell's criteria and underwent surgical intervention, including laparotomy and resection of the necrotic bowel. She received antibiotics, total parenteral nutrition, and was eventually discharged from the NICU after 60 days. Her parents have no known medical history, and she has no significant medical history other than the diagnosis of NEC.

A 45-year-old female patient diagnosed with recurrent malignant glioma, who has undergone surgery and completed radiotherapy or chemotherapy. The patient is not currently using steroid hormones, has good bone marrow, liver, and kidney function, and is in good overall health with a Karnofsky score greater than 60. The patient does not have a medical history of refractory hypertension, bleeding, active vascular disease, or intestinal perforation. The patient is not frail and is expected to survive for more than 8 weeks. The patient is not HIV positive, pregnant, or lactating. The patient is willing to participate in a multi-center, prospective, observational clinical research study to evaluate the efficacy of APT magnetic resonance imaging in predicting the efficacy of bevacizumab in recurrent malignant gliomas.

This is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with hypertension 6 months ago during a routine check-up. She has been taking telmisartan 80 mg monotherapy since then, but her blood pressure is still not well controlled. She has no history of diabetes, heart disease, or other major medical conditions. She has no known allergies to any medication. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 36-year-old married woman with a history of infertility for the past 2 years is looking for ways to increase her chances of conceiving. She has tried various fertility treatments, but none have been successful. She is in good health and does not have any medical conditions such as diabetes, hypertension or thyroid issues. She has a normal BMI of 23 kg/m2 and does not smoke. She exercises regularly and follows a balanced diet. She has been trying to conceive naturally for the past year but has not been successful. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the relationship between preconception dietary patterns, especially the Mediterranean diet (MD) pattern, and in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, as well as adiponectin and follistatin concentrations in the plasma and follicular fluid of women undergoing IVF treatment. She is willing to fill out questionnaires and undergo blood tests to evaluate her dietary pattern and adherence to MD. She is open to receiving IVF treatment as part of the clinical trial and is willing to follow the exclusion criteria, which includes not having a previous IVF attempt or pregnancy, not having endometriosis or female diabetes mellitus or cardiovascular disease. She is excited about the potential benefits of participating in this clinical trial and hopes it will increase her chances of conceiving.

The patient is a 38-year-old pregnant woman who is at term (37 completed weeks of gestation). She has a history of uncomplicated pregnancies and vaginal deliveries, with no history of preterm labor or cervical insufficiency. The patient has been diagnosed with a Bishop score of less than 6 and is being considered for cervical ripening to induce labor. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would contraindicate the use of PROPESS. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the observational survey to evaluate the safety of the treatment.

A 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B for the past 5 years is currently undergoing antiviral treatment to control the virus. His viral load has been under control for the past 6 months, with a level of less than 500 IU/mL. He has no history of cirrhosis or decompensated liver disease. His liver function tests have been within normal limits, with no evidence of any abnormalities. He has not been treated with tenofovir or tenofovir plus emtricitabine in the past. He does not have any other concurrent infections, such as hepatitis C, hepatitis D, or HIV. He is willing to be followed up for at least 4 years after stopping antiviral therapy. He is willing to provide written, informed consent and is eligible to enter protocol 07-DK-0207 or be treated by his local physician should relapse or a hepatitis flare occur. He is otherwise healthy and meets all the inclusion and exclusion criteria for this study.

A 17-year-old Caucasian male with Ewing sarcoma of the left femur presented with recurrent disease that was refractory to multiple lines of chemotherapy. He underwent a reduced intensity conditioning (RIC) haploidentical bone marrow transplant (BMT) and is now post-transplant. He has fully recovered from the acute toxic effects of the BMT, with no evidence of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). His performance status is Karnofsky ≥ 50%. He has no known active infections or autoimmune diseases. His hematologic parameters are within normal limits, with a peripheral absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 950/mm3 and platelet count of 75,000/mm3. His renal function is adequate, with a creatinine clearance of 85 ml/min/1.73 m2. Liver function is normal, with bilirubin at 0.8 mg/dL and SGPT at 40 U/L. Tumor biopsy will be taken at baseline and at Cycle 2. He has previously been registered on protocol J12106 "A Phase II Trial of Reduced Intensity Conditioning and HLA-matched or Partially HLA-mismatched (HLA-haploidentical) Related Donor Bone Marrow Transplant for High-risk Solid Tumors" before enrolling on this study. The patient is eligible for this trial to receive nivolumab to prevent or delay relapse or progression of his Ewing sarcoma.

A 9 year old girl with a diagnosis of Crohn's disease presents to the clinic with complaints of poor growth and significant weight loss. The patient has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and vomiting for the past six months. The patient has lost 10 pounds over the past 2 months and her parents are concerned about her poor appetite and lack of energy. The girl has been on medication for Crohn's disease for 2 months but has not shown any significant improvement. The girl has not reached puberty yet and is Tanner stage 1. The patient is willing to participate in the longitudinal evaluation. The patient does not have any other chronic illnesses or immunological disorders.

A 45-year-old Muslim male who underwent living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) one year ago is being recruited for a clinical study on the effects of Ramadan fasting on post-LDLT patients. The patient's liver and renal functions have been normal for the past 3 months, and there have been no reported rejection episodes in the last 6 months. The patient is willing to fast during the upcoming Ramadan period and has given informed consent for the study. The patient does not have Budd Chiari syndrome and does not have any vascular stents requiring long-term anticoagulation. The patient's creatinine clearance is above 60 ml/min and serum creatinine is within normal range at the time of enrollment in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been experiencing mild cough and chest pain for the past 2 months. She was recently diagnosed with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) after a biopsy. Her CT scan and PET-CT scan revealed that she has stage IIA NSCLC with a single lesion measuring 3 cm in diameter. She has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy for NSCLC. Her FEV1 is 2.5 L, and her ECOG performance status is 1. Her blood tests show that she has a hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL, a white blood cell count of 5800/μL, and a platelet count of 150,000/μL. Her liver and renal function tests are normal, with a total bilirubin level of 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT level of 2 x ULN, serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL, and creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min. She has no history of any other malignancy, diabetes, or cardiac disease. She has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 29-year-old pregnant woman at 29 weeks of gestational age presented with premature labour. She has a history of hypothyroidism, for which she is taking Levothyroxine. The patient denied any significant medical, surgical, or family history. She smokes 5 cigarettes per day and drinks 2 cups of coffee per day. The vital signs were stable in the initial evaluation, and fetal heart rate monitoring showed a category II pattern. An obstetric ultrasound showed a single viable fetus in breech presentation with an estimated weight of 1200g. The cervix was effaced with 2cm dilation. The decision was made to perform an urgent caesarean section due to premature labour. The patient was counselled about the study, and she agreed to participate. The inclusion and exclusion criteria were met, and informed consent was obtained. The infant was delivered successfully and was immediately transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit. Cord clamping was performed according to the randomization, with the delayed cord clamping group receiving a wait time of 60 seconds before clamping, while the early cord clamping group received clamping within 10 seconds of delivery. The infant required mechanical ventilation for 24 hours and had an APGAR score of 6 and 7 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The cord pH was 7.25. The infant had no significant complications during the hospital stay and was discharged home at 37 weeks of gestational age. The mother had no significant postpartum haemorrhage, and her recovery was uneventful.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has recently undergone breast conserving surgery for early stage invasive breast cancer. She has a history of large breasts with a bra size of 42 inches and pre-surgery cup size of D. The pathology report confirms the diagnosis of breast cancer and she is recommended to undergo radiation therapy to decrease the risk of cancer recurrence. However, due to her large breast size, she is at an increased risk of developing skin reactions and breast pain during and after the radiation therapy. She is eligible to participate in the Prone Breast Radiation Therapy Trial which aims to investigate if lying on her belly ("prone") during the radiation treatment can decrease the risk of skin reactions and breast pain. The trial is looking for women who have undergone breast conserving surgery and have a bra size of 40 inches or greater, or a pre-surgery cup size of D or greater.

This is a healthy 8-week-old male infant without any significant past medical history. The infant was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery and has been growing and developing well according to his pediatrician. The infant's parents have consented to participate in the study evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of the 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (13vPnC) in healthy infants. The parents are able to understand and sign an informed consent form and complete a parent worksheet during the study participation. The infant has not received any previous vaccination with licensed or investigational pneumococcal vaccine, Hib conjugate, DTaP or IPV vaccines. The infant is not diagnosed with any significant neurological disorder or history of seizure including febrile seizure, or significant stable or evolving disorders such as cerebral palsy, encephalopathy, hydrocephalus, or other significant disorders. Additionally, the infant does not have a bleeding diathesis or condition associated with prolonged bleeding time that would contraindicate intramuscular injection. The infant has not received blood products or gamma globulin, and there is no known or suspected immune deficiency/suppression.

A 34-year old woman was diagnosed with ME/CFS a year ago after experiencing chronic fatigue, body aches, and flu-like symptoms for several months. She had to quit her job as a teacher due to her illness and now spends most of her time at home. She has tried various medications and therapies with little improvement. She lives with her partner and their two children. She describes her fatigue as a heavy, crushing feeling that never goes away. She also experiences headaches, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. She has had to cut back on her daily activities and social engagements due to her condition. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is interested in participating in the study to help with finding a more objective diagnostic marker for ME/CFS. She hopes that her participation will lead to better understanding and treatment options for this debilitating illness.

28-year-old pregnant woman, primigravida, at 37 weeks gestation presenting for a routine prenatal visit. No significant medical history or prenatal complications noted. Singleton pregnancy confirmed on ultrasound. No known congenital fetal anomalies. No history of uterine or adnexal gross pathology. The patient has a non-scared uterus. The patient has no known medical disorders such as diabetes mellitus or hypertension. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

19 yo Chinese male college student who has been smoking for 2 years. He smokes approximately 5 cigarettes per day and is interested in quitting. He reports feeling stressed and anxious frequently due to academic pressures, but has not sought treatment for these symptoms. He also reports feeling self-conscious about his smoking habit and worries about the negative impact it may have on his health. He has tried to quit smoking before but found it difficult to stay motivated. He speaks fluent Cantonese and is comfortable communicating in the language. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the psychosocial factors associated with smoking in youth and to potentially gain insight into how to quit smoking successfully.

70-year-old female with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to diabetic nephropathy who has been receiving chronic hemodialysis at the Kingston Health Sciences Center regional hemodialysis program for the past 3 years. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently taking metoprolol, amlodipine, atorvastatin, and insulin. The patient comes to the hemodialysis unit three times a week and has been receiving routine bloodwork every four weeks. The patient has been struggling to maintain her hemoglobin and phosphate levels within recommended targets despite frequent adjustments to her medication regimen. The patient has consented to participate in the study and agrees to have her routine bloodwork switched from four-week intervals to six-week intervals to help determine if this change in frequency of measurement will affect her achievement of anemia and CKD-MBD targets.

A 12-year-old female patient with a history of high risk neuroblastoma presents for a follow-up appointment. She was diagnosed with neuroblastoma at the age of 8 and underwent chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery. Her last treatment was completed 45 days ago. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes amlodipine 5mg daily. Her physical exam is unremarkable. Vital signs are stable, blood pressure is 118/70 mmHg, pulse rate is 86 beats per minute, and temperature is 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit. Blood tests, urine tests, and MRI show no evidence of disease. The patient's parents have been informed of this clinical trial and express interest in participation.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who was diagnosed with type III esophageal atresia at birth. She underwent surgery for esophageal atresia repair via right thoracotomy at the age of 1 month. She has been followed up regularly at the hospital, and her last follow-up was 6 years ago. She has not had any respiratory symptoms since the surgery. She has never smoked or been exposed to secondhand smoke. Her past medical history is not significant for any other medical issues. Her family history is negative for any respiratory diseases. Her physical exam shows no abnormalities. She is able to perform all activities of daily living without any difficulty. Her lab studies are within normal limits. She is currently enrolled in school and doing well academically.

A 42-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of severe pain in her lower back, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She had a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and was previously diagnosed with a kidney stone. She has been suffering from these symptoms for the past 3 days. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She denies any recent trauma or infection. She is currently experiencing severe pain, which is not relieved by over-the-counter pain relievers. She is an office worker and has no significant occupational exposure. She has no family history of kidney stones. She is willing to undergo a low-dose CT scan to confirm the presence of a urinary stone.

The patient is a 12-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Phenylketonuria (PKU) since birth. He has been following a low-phenylalanine diet with the intake of at least one protein substitute per day. He has been on the same amino acid based protein substitute for the past 6 months. His blood Phe levels have been stable for the past three measurements taken in the past six months. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. He attends school regularly and is in the sixth grade. He enjoys playing video games and reading books in his free time. He has no known allergies and is not taking any other medication for any other medical condition. He is willing to replace his current protein substitute with PKU Sphere and able to take at least 50% of protein requirements as PKU Sphere. His parents are supportive of his participation in the study and have given written, informed consent.

32 yo F in her first pregnancy with a gestational age of 38 weeks and a medical indication for induction of labor due to gestational hypertension. The patient is nulliparous with a cephalic presentation and an unfavorable cervix with a Bishop's score of 6. She has no known contraindications to the use of prostaglandins and there are no significant fetal or maternal concerns that would make induction necessary under continuous monitoring. The patient has not experienced rupture of membranes and is not carrying multiple gestations. She has no history of cesarean delivery and is not considered grandmultiparous.

A 45 yo F with a suspected diagnosis of leukemia and requiring a bone marrow biopsy for standard care. The patient has a history of fatigue, easy bruising, and recurrent infections. The patient has undergone previous treatment for other medical conditions, including hypertension and type 2 diabetes. The patient has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to medical treatments.

The patient is a 68-year-old Chinese woman residing in a long-term care facility for the past 4 months. She has been leading a sedentary lifestyle for the last month due to her physical limitations. She has a history of sarcopenic obesity and has gained 3 kg of weight in the last three months. She does not have any exercise restrictions and can communicate in both traditional Chinese and Taiwanese. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are both well-controlled with medications. She has no history of severe heart, lung, liver, or kidney disease, cancer or malnutrition. She has no limb weakness, but is unable to anti-gravity completely due to her obesity. Her cognitive function is intact with a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) scale score of 1. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to support herself for at least one hour sitting in a wheelchair or bed edge.

Patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been struggling with knee pain for the past 5 years, which has become more severe over time. She has difficulty walking and standing for long periods of time and has been experiencing stiffness in her knee joint. She was diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and has a BMI of 28. She has been taking over-the-counter pain relievers, such as acetaminophen, but has not found significant relief. She has never received acupuncture treatment before and is willing to try it. She has no history of renal function impairment or sensitivity to the study drug. She is not currently taking NSAIDs or antidepressants and has never been diagnosed with bipolar disorder. She is interested in participating in the trial to try a new treatment option that may provide relief from her symptoms.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with asthma since she was 5 years old. She experiences symptoms such as wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath several times a week, which disrupt her daily activities. She has been prescribed a combination of inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting bronchodilators for asthma management. Her parents report that she has been using her inhaler more frequently lately, and they are concerned about her asthma control. The patient has access to an Apple-based smartphone and is interested in using a mobile app for managing her asthma. She is able to speak and understand English. Her medical history is significant for eczema and seasonal allergies, which are well-controlled with over-the-counter medications. The patient has never been hospitalized for asthma exacerbations but has had to visit the emergency department once in the past year due to worsening asthma symptoms. Her most recent spirometry test shows a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 75% predicted. She is not taking any other medications that could interfere with asthma management.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl diagnosed with asthma by clinical suspicion and spirometry test. She presents with recurrent episodes of coughing, shortness of breath and chest tightness. Her asthma is well-controlled with daily use of inhaled corticosteroids and beta-agonists as needed. She has a history of frequent respiratory infections, which exacerbate her asthma symptoms. She has no other significant medical history and her family history is negative for asthma. Her parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial and have provided informed consent for her participation. She is eligible for the trial as she meets the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old female with a history of primary hypertension for 5 years, despite being on chronic antihypertensive treatments, is eligible for this study. She has been experiencing occasional headaches and dizziness, and her blood pressure readings have consistently been above 150/90 mmHg at each visit. She does not have any known secondary hypertension and has not been diagnosed with hypertensive retinopathy or encephalopathy. She is willing to participate in a double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of firibastat (QGC001) in treating her uncontrolled primary hypertension.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it aims to assess the knowledge, practice, and attitude of paediatricians regarding early childhood caries and infant's oral health. Therefore, the participants in this trial will be paediatricians working in hospitals who treat infants and children under the age of 6 years. The study aims to identify the areas of weakness in their knowledge, practice, and attitude towards early childhood caries and oral health of infants and children. This will help in improving their knowledge and facilitate the early assessment of oral health status and provision of preventive measures to reduce or eliminate oral diseases in infants and children.

Patient A is a 40-year-old male who has a body mass index (BMI) of 40. He has been struggling with obesity for most of his adult life and has tried various diets and exercise routines without success. He has been referred by his physician for a surgical procedure that requires intubation. He has no history of respiratory problems or any other significant medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 125/80 mmHg, heart rate of 78 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. His airway assessment reveals a Mallampati score of 3, indicating that he has a partially visible oropharynx. He has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial comparing GlideScope ® with Fastrach TM for intubation in morbidly obese patients.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids and requires a surgical intervention. She has previously undergone surgery without complications, and her past medical history is unremarkable. She has no known allergies to medications. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is physically active and follows a healthy diet. She has a normal BMI. She is currently taking oral contraceptives. She has no history of neuromuscular disease or any other medical condition that could affect neuromuscular function. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to understand and sign the consent form.

Patient is a 45yo woman who has been experiencing urinary incontinence for the past year. She reports loss of urine associated with coughing, sneezing or laughing as well as loss of urine associated with the strong urge to void. She has tried pelvic floor exercises and lifestyle modifications without improvement. She has not been pregnant and has no intention of becoming pregnant. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of surgical vs pharmacological treatment for her mixed incontinence symptoms. She has no history of urinary tract infections or interstitial cystitis. She is not currently taking any anti-cholinergic agents or diuretics. She has no contraindications for using anti-cholinergic agents. She is capable of filling out the micturition diary, visual analog scale and pathology specific quality of life questionnaire. She understands and is willing to sign an informed written consent form for participating in the trial.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She underwent first-line chemotherapy with limited success and now requires a second-line therapy. She has a history of smoking, having smoked approximately half a pack a day for 30 years, but has quit smoking for the past 5 years. She has no other significant medical history and is able to provide a sample for EGFR mutation testing. She does not have any evidence of central nervous system metastasis or active interstitial lung disease. She is motivated to participate in the study and will comply with all study requirements.

An elite male soccer player aged 26, with a BMI of 23, is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores the effects of dark chocolate on athletic performance. He does not have any known clinical signs of diabetes, hypertension, renal, hepatic, hematological disease, gastrointestinal disorders, endocrine disorders, coronary heart disease, infection, or cancer. He is not taking any medicines known to affect lipid and/or glucose metabolism, fish oils, or evening primrose oil, or fat soluble vitamin supplements within the last 4 weeks, and is not suffering from alcohol or any other substance abuse or having eating disorders. He has suitable veins for blood sampling and/or cannulation and is not allergic to cocoa or any of the ingredients contained within either of the chocolate bars. He is not taking aspirin or aspirin-containing drugs, other anti-inflammatory drugs, or any drugs or herbal medicines known to alter platelet function or the haemostatic system in general.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a long-standing history of type 2 diabetes. He is currently managed with oral hypoglycemic agents and has a recent HbA1c of 7.2%. He works as a truck driver and spends most of his day sitting in the truck. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. He was recently involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained a right ankle fracture. The ankle fracture has been diagnosed as Weber B fracture, and he is scheduled for an operative intervention within the next two weeks. He has no history of peripheral neuropathy, but has a positive monofilament test. He has no other injuries and his BMI is 28. He is married with two children and lives in a two-story home. He reports that he is able to comply with the postoperative protocol and is willing to use a brace for the required duration. He has no history of ankle deformity or Charcot arthropathy.

A 45-year-old female patient with a history of fecal incontinence for the past 2 years. She has tried using adult diapers and pads, but they have been ineffective in managing her condition. She has not undergone any invasive procedures for treatment. She is mentally capable and willing to participate in her own treatment. She has no known allergies to silicone or its components. Her colon surveillance complies with National Program/Guidelines for the Early Detection of Colorectal Cancer. She has no major neurological diagnosis or known life-threatening diseases. She is not currently participating in another clinical study and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not had rectal surgery in the past 6 months and has no pre-existing rectal pain or rectal bleeding. She is not on anti-coagulants or anti-platelets treatment, except for low-dose aspirin. She is willing to continue her current medication regimen for the duration of the study. She has had a minimum of four incontinence episodes during the 2-week baseline period and is able to self-manage insertion and removal of the device.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been experiencing chronic pain for the past year. The pain is located in his lower back and radiates down his legs. He describes the pain as sharp and burning, and it has been interfering with his daily activities and work. He has seen multiple doctors and specialists, but the cause of his pain remains unknown. He has tried various pain medications and physical therapy, but nothing has provided significant relief. The patient has a family history of heart disease and kidney problems, but he has not had any significant health issues in the past. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He occasionally drinks alcohol and does not smoke. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially find the cause of his chronic pain and receive appropriate treatment.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been struggling with cocaine use disorder for the past three years. He has been in early remission for two months and is seeking treatment to maintain his sobriety. He has a BMI of 25 and weighs 70 kg. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has no history of adverse reactions to antibiotics or beta-lactam drugs. He is willing to undergo MRI scans and can tolerate them for the required duration. He is not currently using any drugs other than cocaine and does not have HIV. He is not pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who works as a graphic designer. She wears glasses or contact lenses for myopic refractive errors, which has been causing inconvenience in her daily life. She has no other medical condition and is generally healthy. She has a history of stable refractive error, and has been using the same prescription for the past two years. She does not have any other ocular abnormalities or sensitivities to medications. The patient is willing and capable of returning for follow-up examinations for the duration of the study. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative solutions for her refractive error.

The patient is a 40-year-old Chinese immigrant who has been living in the United States for five years. She is married with two children and works as a cashier in a grocery store. She speaks Mandarin and has limited English proficiency. She reports feeling stressed and isolated since moving to the United States and has experienced discrimination based on her ethnicity. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes but has never been diagnosed with the disease herself. She has no history of cancer, autoimmune disorders, HIV, or psychiatric illness. She does not take any medications that may impact study outcomes. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a BMI of 31, classified as obese. She has no history of chronic illness, has not used antibiotics in the past month, and is not on any medication for cardiac disease, statins, or antihypertensive drugs. She has not been diagnosed with any inflammatory bowel disease, irritable bowel syndrome, and has not had any small intestinal bacterial overgrowth or intestinal surgery, excluding hernia repair and appendectomy. She is not currently undergoing immune modulatory treatments and has no known abnormal liver or kidney function as measured by routine serum chemistry testing. The patient is willing to take an oral dietary supplement and placebo daily for a total of 56 days, willing to complete gastrointestinal (GI) and dietary surveys, body composition assessment, and provide blood, urine and stool sample at 4 intervals during the pilot study (baseline, after first supplementation period (day 28), after washout period (day 49), and after second supplementation period (day 77).

The patient is a 70 year old male with no significant medical history. He is living with his spouse and is retired. He enjoys gardening and walking around his neighborhood. He has a BMI of 27 and his blood pressure and pulse rate are within normal limits. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is not taking any medications or supplements on a regular basis. He has not participated in any clinical trial in the past 90 days. He is sexually inactive and therefore does not need to use any contraception. He has never donated blood or blood products in the past 90 days. He has no known allergies to medications, including nifedipine, α adrenoceptor antagonists, or latex. He understands the purpose and risks of the study and is willing to follow the restrictions and schedule of procedures as defined in the protocol. He is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 7 year old girl was diagnosed with retinoblastoma at the age of 4 and has since undergone treatment with cisplatin. She has completed treatment and has a minimum follow-up of 3 years after stopping treatment. She has separate complete audiograms for each ear to define the Brock grade. The patient's parents have given informed and written consent for her to participate in this study. The patient is affiliated with a social security scheme. The patient has not had any brain tumor, tumor "paraméningée" or renal toxicity (≥ Grade 2) at the time of treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy. The patient has not received any cerebral or total body irradiation (Total Body Irradiation). The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the control group in this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COVID-19 and has been hospitalized due to severe respiratory distress. He is currently in Stage 2b of the disease, experiencing hypoxic pneumonia with respiratory frequency of over 30 breaths per minute and SaO2 levels below 90mmHg on room air, along with a clear biological inflammatory syndrome with CRP levels above 150mg/L. He has no history of chronic illnesses or autoimmune diseases, but has been experiencing fever, cough, and shortness of breath for the past 7 days. The patient is not currently pregnant or lactating and has no known allergies to anakinra or ruxol

This is an 80 year-old female with a history of mild cognitive impairment and frailty. She lives at home with her daughter who helps her with daily activities. She has difficulty with walking and balance, and has experienced a few falls in the past year. She has a Barthel Index score of 70, indicating some difficulty with activities of daily living. She has no significant medical history, but has been advised by her physician to engage in physical activity to improve her strength, balance, and overall functional capacity. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will provide her with a structured exercise program to help improve her physical and cognitive abilities.

A 58-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) after presenting with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medication. She is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and has a 20-pack-year smoking history. Imaging studies revealed multiple lesions in the lungs and liver. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of SCLC. She has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy, biologic therapy, or radiotherapy for SCLC. Brain metastases were ruled out by CT scan. Her performance status is Zubrod 1, indicating that she is able to carry out light work, but requires rest periods. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has no other malignancy within the past 5 years. Her blood work reveals an absolute granulocyte count of 2,200/mm^3, WBC count of 4,800/mm^3, and platelet count of 120,000/mm^3. Her bilirubin and liver enzymes are within normal limits. She is not pregnant or nursing, and uses an effective contraceptive method.

29-year-old female with a 5-year history of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) that has been treated with interferon and Copaxone. Despite treatment, she has had 2 or more steroid-treated clinical relapses within the last 12 months. She has an EDSS score of 3.5 and cognitive dysfunction that prevents gainful employment. She is willing to comply with effective means of birth control until 6 months post-transplantation. She has no history of sickle cell disease, coagulopathy, or insulin-dependent diabetes. She has no metallic objects implanted in her body that would preclude her ability to safely have MRI exams. Her platelet count is within normal limits and her white blood cell count is greater than 1,500 cells/mm3. She has no active infections and does not have any psychiatric illness or cognitive dysfunction that would make compliance with treatment or informed consent impossible. She has not received Tysabri, Gilenya, Tecfidera, Aubagio, Lemtrada/Campath, Rituxan, or Ocrevus within the specified timeframes. She has not received prior treatment with Novantrone. She meets the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study.

68 year old female who is generally healthy and actively participates in daily activities such as shopping, cleaning, and gardening. She has no history of Parkinson's disease or cognitive deficits but is interested in participating in a study that investigates balance and strength in an elderly population. She does not have any neurological or orthopedic deficits that would affect her gait and cognition. She is able to stand on a platform and complete mental tasks with her eyes open and closed. She is able to move and balance by rising from a chair, walking three feet, turning around, walking back to the chair, and sitting down. She is also able to flex and extend her legs as quickly as possible. She is excited to participate in this study to contribute to the understanding of balance and strength in the elderly population.

35 F diagnosed with high-risk acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) in first complete remission (CR1) after induction chemotherapy. Patient is not a candidate for allogeneic stem cell transplantation due to lack of appropriate donor. She has undergone successful mobilization of hematopoietic stem cells with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) and plerixafor and will be undergoing a standard autologous stem cell transplant. Patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and adequate renal and liver function. She has negative antibody serology for HIV and is not pregnant. The patient has signed informed consent to participate in this clinical trial to receive cytokine-induced killer (CIK) cells post-transplant to reduce the risk of relapse.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of alcohol abuse presents with abdominal distention and jaundice. The physical examination reveals hepatomegaly and ascites. His laboratory results indicate elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels. His MELD score is 18. He has a history of hepatic encephalopathy and has been prescribed lactulose. He has had multiple hospitalizations due to recurrent episodes of hepatic encephalopathy despite treatment with lactulose. He complains of fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and forgetfulness. He is currently not able to work due to his symptoms. He is married and has two children. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment. He has no history of neurological or gastrointestinal bleeding disorders.

A 28-year-old woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication. She is generally healthy and has never participated in a clinical trial before. She is a non-smoker and has a body mass index (BMI) of 23. She is not currently pregnant nor lactating. She has not had any history of cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, hematological, or neurological disorders. She has not been diagnosed with any psychiatric disorders. Her medical history does not include any malignancy within the past 5 years. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research. She has not had any allergic reaction to humanized monoclonal antibodies. She is willing to comply with the CRU smoking restrictions and agrees not to donate blood or plasma until after the end of her participation in the study.

Patient A is a 12-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and is currently receiving medication for the treatment of ADHD. However, both the patient and her parent/legal guardian are dissatisfied with the current medication, as measured by a VAS score of less than 50. The patient is in good health, has no current psychiatric comorbidity, and is not using other prescription medications for ADHD with psychoactive properties. She has not used monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors within the past week or an investigational drug within the past month. She has no known clinically significant drug sensitivity to modafinil or any of its inactive ingredients. The patient and her parent/legal guardian are English-speaking and willing and able to comply with study procedures and restrictions. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is postmenarche, but is not sexually active.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer 3 years ago. She underwent primary debulking surgery followed by six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy after the diagnosis. She experienced a complete response to the chemotherapy, and her CA-125 levels were normalized. However, her cancer recurred 6 months after completing the chemotherapy. She received a second-line treatment with gemcitabine and carboplatin, but her disease progressed after three cycles. She is currently experiencing abdominal pain and bloating, and her CA-125 levels are elevated. She has a performance status of 1, and she is able to perform most activities of daily living with minimal assistance. She has no history of cardiovascular or renal disease, but she has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is postmenopausal and had a total hysterectomy at the time of her initial diagnosis. She has no history of other malignancies or significant comorbidities. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She takes lisinopril and amlodipine for hypertension. Her blood counts, liver function tests, and renal function tests are within the normal range. She is willing to take oral medication and has no known allergies to any medications. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has suffered a trauma to his jaw resulting in a subcondylar fracture. He experiences pain and difficulty opening his mouth. He has no previous history of facial surgery or trauma. The patient is in good health, with no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. The patient has undergone preoperative panoramic radiographs and/or computed tomography (CT) images which confirmed the subcondylar fracture. The patient is mentally stable and can undergo an adequate neuromotor examination. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to undergo open reduction and internal fixation using titanium miniplates. The patient will be closely followed up at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months and 6 months postoperatively.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been diagnosed with gestational diabetes during her previous pregnancy. She is currently overweight with a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has a family history of type 2 diabetes. She completed lactation and is willing to participate in the study. She has dysglycemia and/or ß-cell dysfunction postpartum which requires pharmacological intervention. She has no personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2. She has no history of pancreatitis, significant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, or hepatobiliary diseases. Her serum liver enzymes are within normal limits, and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication.
