She is not currently taking metformin, thiazolidinediones, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonist medications. She is not taking any weight-loss drugs and has not been diagnosed with diabetes postpartum or before. Her creatinine clearance is above 60 ml/min, and she is not undergoing chemotherapy or radiotherapy for cancer. She has no plans for pregnancy in the next two years and is not currently breastfeeding.

A 62-year-old male with a history of prostate adenocarcinoma, who underwent radical prostatectomy 5 years ago, now presents with an increasing serum PSA level. The latest PSA value is 0.5 ng/mL, which is higher than the previous value of 0.2 ng/mL. The patient has no history of radiation therapy or chemotherapy. The patient is experiencing no symptoms and his ECOG performance status is 1. The patient has undergone a routine imaging workup including a bone scan and prostatic/pelvic MRI, which showed negative results for distant metastases. The patient has given informed consent and is willing to undergo the 68Ga-PSMA PET-CT scan to evaluate for the presence of recurrent prostate cancer.

A 25-year-old woman with a history of orthostatic intolerance, frequent lightheadedness, and occasional fainting episodes visited the clinic. She also reported experiencing nausea, vomiting, constipation, and urinary frequency. The patient's symptoms have been ongoing for several years, and she has visited multiple doctors with no clear diagnosis. The patient was referred to the Clinical Autonomic Disorders training protocol for evaluation. She will undergo a medical history and physical exam, including testing for problems thinking, and complete a symptom questionnaire. The patient may also have an intravenous line placed for blood drawing and receive an electrocardiogram. Her ability to sweat and sense of smell will be tested, and her breathing, bowel sounds, and body functions will be monitored. Her pupillary size, response to environmental temperature changes, and breathing will be measured. The patient may also have a bladder ultrasound, and small pieces of skin may be taken for study. The purpose of the protocol is to train Fellows in the evaluation of clinical disorders of the autonomic nervous system and to allow patients with autonomic disorders to be evaluated. The primary objective is to enable Fellows to sit for and pass the certifying examination in autonomic disorders administered by the United Council for Neurologic Subspecialties (UCNS) and to maintain UCNS accreditation of the Fellowship. The patient is eligible for inclusion in the study as she is suspected to have failure of one or more components of the autonomic nervous system.

The patient is a 17-year-old male diagnosed with ADHD-Predominantly Inattentive Presentation. He has a valid driver's license and drives for approximately 5 hours per week. He finds it difficult to focus on the road and frequently gets distracted by secondary tasks while driving, leading to near-misses. His parents are concerned about his driving behavior, and they are willing to participate in the study. The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with gingival recession in his maxillary and mandibular anterior teeth. The patient is a 10-month-old male infant who was born full-term and is in good health. The patient is a healthy male or female volunteer who is at least 18 years old and able to give informed consent. 65 yo F with history of breast cancer who presents with significant pain, redness, and drainage at the site of a cutaneous metastasis on her chest wall. A 55-year-old male smoker who was diagnosed with small cell lung cancer. He presents with shortness of breath, cough, and weight loss. The patient is a 45-year-old Hispanic/Latino(a) man who underwent kidney transplant at the University of New Mexico Hospital (UNMH) six months ago. A 57-year-old postmenopausal woman was diagnosed with endometrial cancer two years ago. She underwent surgery and radiation therapy and has been cancer-free for the past 18 months. She has a BMI of 28 and is otherwise healthy. She does not have a history of diabetes or any other cancer (excluding skin). She is not taking any medication that affects glucose metabolism. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her insulin resistance and overall health.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian man who has recently been diagnosed with intestinal T-cell lymphoma. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past few months. He is currently unemployed and lives with his wife and two children. He has no history of cancer or chemotherapy. His blood work shows a neutrophil count of 2200/mm3, platelet count of 120,000/mm3, and creatinine clearance of 70 ml/min. His EKG is normal. He has been referred to this clinical trial by his oncologist and has been informed about the risks and benefits of the treatment. He is willing to participate in the trial and is committed to following the treatment plan.

The patient is a 15 year old girl who has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness and hopelessness for the past 6 months. 45-year-old male with acute onset of lower back pain after lifting heavy objects at work. He has not received any prior treatment for his low back pain and is willing to refrain from taking non-study medications or non-study procedures for the management of his low back pain throughout study participation. He speaks English as his primary language and is willing to participate in the study.

This is an 75 year old male who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled to undergo an elective prostatectomy. He has a history of hypertension which is well controlled with medication. He has no known drug allergies and is fluent in German language. The expected surgery duration is approximately 2 hours and the planned anaesthesia is general. The patient has been informed of the study and has provided written informed consent to participate.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who is classified as overweight with a BMI of 28 kg/m2. She has moderately elevated LDL-C levels with a value of 168 mg/dL. A 55-year-old Chinese male with a history of type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy presents with a non-healing ulcer on his left foot. He also reports numbness in his feet and occasional tingling sensations. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a 20-pack-year history of smoking. The patient's HbA1c level is 8.2%. He is admitted to the hospital for further evaluation and treatment of the diabetic foot ulcer. The patient is able to communicate fluently in Mandarin and has no cognitive impairment. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of a discharge planning using the strategy of motivational interviewing for patients with diabetic foot ulcers.

This is a 53-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced Triple Negative Breast Cancer. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with little effect on her disease progression. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. The patient has been selected to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a combination of CORT125134, a novel glucocorticoid receptor antagonist, and nab-paclitaxel. The trial is a single-arm, non-randomized, open-label, multicenter study with no control group. The patient will be enrolled in the dose expansion portion of Segment II of the study, once the development regimen for the intermittent-dosing regimen has been determined. The study will assess the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and the preliminary efficacy of the combination treatment in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors who have disease progression after treatment with available therapies and for whom nab-paclitaxel treatment is appropriate. The patient's measurable disease will be evaluated using the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1 in at least 1 lesion. The treatment will be administered in 28-day cycles. The patient will be closely monitored throughout the trial to assess the safety and efficacy of the combination treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old individual who has been experiencing bleeding gums while brushing and flossing for the past six months. A 56-year-old man with a history of depression that has not been responding to standard treatment for over 6 months went to his primary care physician for a check-up. 55-year-old woman with a history of gastritis and dyspepsia presents to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and discomfort. Upon evaluation, she is diagnosed with H. pylori infection and is deemed eligible for enrollment in a clinical trial studying the efficacy of probiotic supplementation during H. pylori eradication therapy. She has no history of gastrectomy, gastric malignancy, or allergies to the antibiotics or PPI used in the treatment. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no severe concurrent diseases. She is willing to accept random assignment of subjects and is interested in exploring alternative options for managing the adverse effects of H. pylori eradication therapy.

The patient is a 45 year old male who works as a carpenter. He has been experiencing pain and stiffness in his right middle finger for the past 3 months. He noticed that the finger gets stuck in a bent position and he has to use his other hand to straighten it out. The pain has been interfering with his work, making it difficult to hold and grip tools. He does not have a history of diabetes, hypothyroidism, or rheumatic or connective tissue disease. He has not had any injections or surgery on his finger in the past 6 months. He is not allergic to triamcinolone or hyaluronic acid. He is not currently pregnant. Upon examination, he was diagnosed with grade 2 trigger finger on the Quinnell grading scale and confirmed by ultrasound. He is interested in participating in the study to compare the therapeutic effects of hyaluronic acid versus steroid injections under ultrasound guidance.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is scheduled for cardiac surgery via sternotomy and cardiopulmonary bypass. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He is a former smoker and has been smoke-free for 5 years. He consumes alcohol occasionally. He is generally healthy and physically active. The patient is willing to participate in post-operative swallowing evaluation testing as part of the clinical trial.

This clinical trial is looking for individuals between the ages of 18 and 40 who have previously participated in the Study Of Pharmacogenetics In Ethnically Diverse Populations (SOPHIE) study and possess a specific OCT1 genotype. Patients who are taking any medications other than vitamins, have anemia, elevated liver enzymes or creatinine concentrations, or are pregnant at the time of the study will be excluded. The study aims to determine if individuals who carry a decreased or non-functional variant of OCT1 exhibit differences in the pharmacokinetics of metformin in comparison to individuals who carry the common allele, and if they exhibit differences in the response to metformin in comparison to individuals who carry the common allele. The study will evaluate metformin pharmacokinetics and glucose metabolic effects in healthy subjects rather than in patients with type 2 diabetes. The participants will undergo an oral glucose tolerance test before and after metformin administration, with insulin levels being determined after glucose administration. The study expects to observe significant differences in post-glucose-administration insulin levels between individuals with different OCT1 genotypes. Participants will also be monitored for plasma lactate concentrations after metformin treatment, and the corresponding concentrations will be measured.

Patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of right-sided inguinal hernia. He is scheduled for elective primary unilateral open tension-free mesh inguinal hernia repair. The patient has no history of chronic pain, opioid dependency, coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, dementia, or peripheral neuropathy. The patient has a BMI of 28 and is in good general health. The patient is able to provide informed consent and understand the visual analog scale (VAS) for pain assessment. The patient has no skin infections near the injection site.

A 15-year-old male, currently in the Juvenile Drug Court program of Rhode Island Family Court, is eligible for this study. A 45-year-old male patient presents with a history of persistent hoarseness, difficulty swallowing, and a feeling of something stuck in his throat. The patient is willing to undergo transoral surgery in the oropharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx to address his symptoms. The patient is 5'11", weighs 180 lbs, and has a BMI of 25.2.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a single titanium implant in her upper right jaw. She has been experiencing bleeding on gentle probing around the implant site, indicating peri-implant mucositis. She has more than 1 mm of keratinized peri-implant mucosa, and no signs of loss of supporting bone. She has not received any systemic antibiotics or treatment for peri-implant mucositis in the past 3 months. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve the health of her implant and prevent further complications.

The patient is a 60-year-old male complaining of shortness of breath and fatigue. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. Recently, he has been experiencing difficulty climbing stairs and walking long distances. He also wakes up at night due to shortness of breath. A 45 year old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, presents to the nephrology clinic with complaints of fatigue, intermittent lower extremity edema and nocturia. The patient is a 16-year-old male who recently sustained a concussion while playing football. He experienced a hit to the head during practice and subsequently experienced symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. He was evaluated by a physician and diagnosed with a concussion. The patient has no history of ADHD or moderate to severe traumatic brain injury. He is fluent in English and able to understand instructions. He is currently experiencing symptoms and has not yet reached the 10-day mark since his injury. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in the study and understand the risks and benefits of the treatment options.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with localized rectal cancer after experiencing persistent diarrhea and rectal bleeding for several weeks. Further investigations revealed a tumor in the rectum, and biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. The patient has no significant medical history and no family history of cancer. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0. His physical examination was unremarkable with no palpable lymph nodes or hepatosplenomegaly. His laboratory results show normal liver and kidney function, and his carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level is within normal range. His CT scan revealed a 5 cm mass in the rectum with no evidence of distant metastasis. The patient is eligible for the pilot trial of pre-operative chemoradiotherapy using capecitabine, external beam radiation, and cetuximab in patients with localized (non-metastatic)

The patient is a male infant born at 27 weeks gestation and admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). He weighed 900 grams at birth and was intubated upon admission. The infant is currently on mechanical ventilation and receiving total parenteral nutrition. He has been diagnosed with respiratory distress syndrome and is receiving surfactant therapy. At this time, he has not developed any intracranial hemorrhage. The medical team is considering enrolling the infant in a clinical trial to investigate the relationship between intraventricular hemorrhage and head position in preterm infants. The trial will randomly assign infants lying on flat (zero degree) beds to be cared for either in a supine flat midline or a supine right flat lateral head position throughout the first 168 hours of life. The goal is to keep the infant's head in their assigned position unless a medical indication requires a change in position. The bedside nurse will check the correctness of the infant's head position every 4 hours. The trial will include two screening head ultrasounds within the first 168 hours of life. The medical team will be unmasked to the assigned head position to provide routine nursing care, including a change in head position every 6-12 hours as needed. The infant will be eligible for the trial if he was born at the study NICU and has a gestational age less than 30 weeks. Exclusion criteria include lethal congenital anomalies, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, need for external cardiac compression or epinephrine administration at birth, and outborns.

The patient should be a male between the ages of 18 to 45 who is currently living in Ndola, Zambia for the duration of the 10-week study. He should be willing to provide proof of residence and able to complete a consent form. The patient should be in good health with no chronic illnesses such as diabetes, asthma, hypertension or skin conditions. He should not be on any herbal or traditional medicines or immune-boosting treatments. The patient should not have received any investigational drug or herbal medicine within the past 2 months. He should not have a history of TB, excessive alcohol consumption or smoking. The patient must test negative for HIV, HBV, and HCV infection.

The patient is a 5 year old boy scheduled for a hernia repair surgery. He has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. The patient is nervous about the surgery and has experienced pain in the past. The patient will be given a detailed explanation of the expected benefits and possible risks of the study, and his parents will sign an informed consent form. The patient will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: intravenous magnesium group, caudal magnesium group, or placebo group. The patient will undergo anesthesia induction with sevoflurane, fentanyl, and atracurium, and anesthesia will be maintained with isoflurane and additional atracurium doses. The study solution will be started and caudal block will be performed. Surgery will begin 10 minutes after the block. After emergence from anesthesia, the patient will be managed in the post anesthesia care unit (PACU) by an observer blinded to group allocation. Any postoperative pain will be managed with rectal paracetamol as rescue analgesia if needed. The patient will be monitored for any adverse reactions to the magnesium or any other medications.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) a year ago. He underwent surgery and radiation therapy followed by chemotherapy with temozolomide. However, the tumor has recurred, and he has undergone a second surgery to remove the recurrent tumor. The patient has completed at least 21 days of combination therapy with radiation and temozolomide. He has no metastatic extracranial or leptomeningeal disease and his tumor target is ≤ 5 cm. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status score of 80 and has normal organ and marrow function. He has no history of major surgery in the past two weeks and is not on any medication that may interfere with the study treatment. He is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, and laboratory tests. The patient is a non-smoker and has no known allergies to any study drug components. He is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to conceive during the study treatment period. The patient has signed the informed consent and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of stereotactic radiosurgery with MBG453 and spartalizumab in treating recurrent GBM.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with a mitochondrial cytopathy. He has been experiencing fatigue, muscle weakness, and difficulty exercising for the past few months. His medical history includes recurrent episodes of vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. He has been on a usual diet consisting of 30% lipids, 60% glucides, and 10% proteins for the past month. The child's parents have given informed consent for him to participate in this clinical trial. The patient has social security coverage. The child is able to understand and follow the protocol. There is no evidence of acute infection in the past 7 days.

The patient is a 32-year-old female living in Kampala, Uganda. She was diagnosed with HIV six months ago and has been attending the Mulago Hospital's HIV care clinic regularly. She has not received any antiretroviral therapy (ART) yet. She has no known drug allergies and is not taking any medications. She has no known history of hepatitis B infection or vaccination. She works as a teacher and lives with her husband and two young children. She is generally healthy with no significant medical history. She has no current symptoms related to her HIV infection. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol, including providing informed consent.

Patient is a 26-year-old woman who gave birth to a premature baby at 32 weeks gestation. The baby was transferred to the NICU at Mansoura University Children's Hospital due to respiratory distress, requiring the use of nasal CPAP. The baby is otherwise stable, with no significant medical history. The mother is currently breastfeeding, and both she and the baby are tolerating feeds well. The baby has not received any sedation or analgesia in the preceding 72 hours and has not undergone any surgical intervention or painful procedures such as venipuncture, intubation, suctioning, blood sampling, heel-prick, or catheterization 30 minutes before assessment. The baby has no signs of nasal injuries at the time of application of nCPAP and does not have necrotizing enterocolitis.

32 yo M with a history of infertility and diagnosed with non-obstructive azoospermia. Has undergone previous testing including semen analysis and genetic testing. A 24-year-old male college student is interested in participating in a study investigating the effects of XSurge supplementation on biomarkers and performance from high-intensity resistance exercise. The patient is a 19-year-old female diagnosed with Anorexia Nervosa who has been admitted to the Intensive Structured Living Unit (ISL) at Melrose Institute for treatment. She has no history of substance or alcohol abuse or dependence, malabsorption syndrome, or Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. She has not participated in any other clinical trials and is not currently pregnant.

A 45-year-old Danish woman was diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis 2 years ago, according to the 2009 ACR/EULAR criteria. She is currently taking Methotrexate and Prednisolone to manage her symptoms. She has experienced joint pain and stiffness, particularly in her hands, making it difficult for her to perform daily activities such as dressing and cooking. She has also noticed a decrease in her physical activity level due to her condition. She is able to sit on an exercise bike and is interested in participating in a 6-week supervised exercise program to improve her cardiovascular fitness and muscle strength. Her disease activity is low, and she has not experienced any cardiovascular events in the last 6 months. She has not had a history of myocardial infarction, angina pectoris, or severe lung disease. She does not take beta-blockers and has a stable blood pressure within normal limits. She speaks and understands Danish fluently.

45 year-old African American man who has been experiencing muscle weakness in his legs for the past year. He has not sought medical attention until now due to financial constraints. He reports difficulty getting up from a seated position and climbing stairs. He also reports aching in his calf muscles and occasional cramping. He denies any weakness in his arms or neck. On examination, he has 4/5 strength in his hip flexors and knee extensors bilaterally, 5/5 strength in his upper extremities and neck muscles, and normal sensation throughout. He has an elevated creatinine kinase level of 600 U/L. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

This clinical trial is not applicable for a patient description as it does not involve the recruitment or enrollment of individual patients, but rather focuses on studying the adoption and use of improved cookstoves in a rural community in Northern Ghana. Therefore, the eligibility criteria are related to clusters of households rather than individual patients.

85 year old man residing in a nursing home who has reported difficulty falling and staying asleep for the past few months. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and arthritis. He speaks English fluently and is able to communicate and follow simple commands. He has no history of cognitive impairment and has a surrogate who can provide consent for his participation in the study. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his sleep quality and overall well-being.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing occasional heart palpitations for the past year. He underwent an electrocardiogram (ECG) which showed premature ventricular complexes (PVCs). The patient was referred for further evaluation and was diagnosed with PVC-induced cardiomyopathy. The patient was started on medication, but the symptoms persisted. The patient was then evaluated for PVC ablation, but the procedure was unsuccessful in abolishing the PVCs acutely. The patient was then referred for this clinical trial to investigate if there could be a late effect of ablation on his PVCs. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and will be enrolled for further evaluation.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who are between the ages of 23 and 50 and have a history of head and neck cancer. Specifically, they are looking for individuals who were treated with unilateral radiotherapy (RT) 5-10 years ago. The study will investigate long-term complications, specifically vascular and psychosocial complications. Participants must be able to communicate effectively in Dutch and cannot have any contraindications for MRI. The study will involve structured survivorship care, including carotid ultrasonography, MRI of the carotid arteries and brain, neuropsychological assessment, and self-reported questionnaires concerning depression, fatigue, quality of life, positive health, and employment status. If you meet these criteria and are interested in participating in this study, please contact the research team for more information.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with moderate renal impairment 2 years ago. She was previously diagnosed with hypertension and is currently taking medication to control it. She reports no significant medical history other than the hypertension and has never been hospitalized for any reason. The patient reports no current symptoms related to her renal impairment and has not experienced any significant changes in her health since her diagnosis. Her most recent lab results show an eGFR of 40 mL/min/1.73m2, which is consistent with her moderate renal impairment. The patient has a BMI of 28 kg/m2, which falls within the inclusion criteria for the study. She has been made aware of the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

A 13-year-old male diagnosed with cystic fibrosis came to the clinic for a regular check-up. He has had CF since he was a baby and has been taking multivitamins and pancreatic enzymes regularly since then. He is currently taking Tobramycin, Azithromycin, and hypertonic saline for his respiratory symptoms. He has a sweat chloride level of 72 mEq/L and pancreatic insufficiency confirmed by a stool sample with an FE-1 of 45 μg/g. His weight is 45 kg, and his FEV1 is 70% of predicted. He has no history of allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis or nontuberculous mycobacterial infection. He is willing to discontinue his current oral vitamin and antioxidant supplementation for the duration of the study. He is not a smoker and has no known hypersensitivity to oral AquADEKs®.

This is a 45-year-old obese female with a history of sleep apnea, hypertension and GERD. She is scheduled for elective surgery for a large uterine fibroid. Her preoperative evaluation reveals Mallampati class III, neck circumference of 46cm and thyromental distance of 5cm. She has no known history of difficult airway management but due to her anticipated risk factors, the anesthesiologist anticipates a potentially difficult airway. She has been consented to participate in the clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of the King Vision® Video Intubation System and Cobalt GlideScope® in patients with anticipated difficult airways.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who works in a busy office environment. He is generally healthy but complains of symptoms of the common cold, including nasal congestion, headache, muscle pain, and cough. He has had these symptoms for the past two days, and they have been interfering with his work. He has not taken any medication for these symptoms yet. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness and safety of a fixed combination of paracetamol, phenylephrine, and chlorpheniramine in treating common cold and flu-like illness.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is scheduled for nasal intubation for general anesthesia due to a dental procedure. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications on a regular basis. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is of Korean ethnicity and is fluent in Korean. She has no known nasal airway disease or cervical movement disorder. She has a Modified Mallampati score of 2 and her mouth opening is greater than 2cm. She has no facial anomalies. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the study.

A 32-year-old right-handed woman had a stroke last year that resulted in a brain lesion localized in the right hemisphere. She struggles with attention and has difficulty focusing on certain tasks, especially those involving monetary rewards. She has normal vision and is covered by social health security. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric illness and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not participated in any other brain stimulation studies in the past week and has no history of recurrent otitis media.

A 55-year-old woman with a history of borderline pancreatic adenocarcinoma presents to the clinic for further management. She has no significant past medical history and is currently experiencing abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting. She has lost 10 pounds in the last month and reports having yellowish discoloration of her skin and eyes. On examination, her abdomen is tender to palpation and an abdominal ultrasound reveals a mass in the pancreas. A CT scan confirms the presence of a locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She is eligible for this clinical trial and shows interest in participating. She is willing to comply with the protocol including all scheduled MRI studies and paired tumor biopsies. She has no history of DVT or PE and is not contraindicated for therapeutic anticoagulation or heparin. She has no contraindications for MRI and is willing to undergo all scheduled MRI exams. She has an ECOG PS of 1 and has adequate organ and hematopoietic function. She is currently not receiving any anticancer agents or radiation. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use an approved contraceptive method. She has no pre-existing peripheral neuropathy or known allergy to hyaluronidase. She is capable of giving informed consent and has signed the informed consent form.

A 25-year-old female presents with a past medical history of β-thalassemia major. She has been receiving regular blood transfusions every 4-6 weeks for the past 12 years. Her most recent cardiac MRI T2* value is 8 ms, indicating severe cardiac iron overload. She is compliant with intensive iron chelation therapy regimens including i.v DFO 24 hr infusions. Her LVEF is 62% as determined by CMR. There is no evidence of shortness of breath, orthopnea, exercise intolerance, lower extremity edema, arrhythmias or liver failure. She has no history of malignancy or psychiatric or addictive disorders. She is not pregnant and is using an effective method of birth control. Her serum creatinine and ALT levels are within normal limits. She has no history of hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or their excipients. She is willing to comply with the protocol and able to undergo all study assessments including blood sampling and MRI.

The patient is a 47-year-old male with a history of knee arthritis. He has been experiencing pain in his knee joint for several years and has tried various treatments including physical therapy, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and corticosteroid injections, but with limited success. He is generally in good health with no significant medical history and has a BMI of 28. His blood pressure is well controlled with medication and his resting heart rate is within normal limits. He is currently taking no medications for pain management. He has no known allergies to medications or latex. He is willing to use highly effective methods of birth control during the study period. During the initial training session, he reported a pain score rating of 3 out of 10 during a 5 minute heating of 45°C-47°C to the lower calf.

A 17-year-old post-pubertal female who spends long hours on her laptop and smartphone for her studies, and has noticed that her posture has worsened over time. She has no history of headache, migraine, vertebra-basilar insufficiency, TMD, neck pain, fixed or mobile spinal deformity, or any history of fracture or surgery of the upper quadrant of the body. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and is generally in good health. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to investigate the effect of forward head posture on TMJ proprioception in post-pubertal females.

63 F with stage IV ovarian cancer and a history of intractable pain despite multiple modalities of treatment including radiation and opioids. She presents with daily pain scores of 8-9/10 on a numeric rating scale despite being on oral morphine equivalent of 90mg/day. She reports difficulty in performing activities of daily living and has significant anxiety and depression related to her pain. She has no known allergies to opioids or other pain medications. She has a negative pregnancy test and is on a reliable form of birth control. Her projected survival is less than 25%. Her labs are within normal limits, including bone marrow function, IgG levels, and CD4 count. She has no history of active herpes infection or vaccination to prevent HSV infection. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative options for pain management.

8-year-old male diagnosed with neuroblastoma at age 4. Has undergone two prior standard treatment regimens, but the metastatic neuroblastoma has become refractory to conventional therapies. Currently experiencing progressive disease with metastases to the liver, bone marrow and bones. Patient has no effective treatment options available. Patient has normal bone marrow, liver, and renal function. Patient and parents/legal guardians have provided informed consent for the study.

A 68-year-old Greek man with a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis is scheduled for elective orthopedic surgery under general anesthesia. He reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty with word-finding, but denies any significant memory impairment or confusion. He has been married for 40 years and lives with his wife. He is retired and enjoys gardening and reading. He does not smoke, but drinks alcohol occasionally, with an average of 2-3 units per week. He takes medications for his hypertension and osteoarthritis. His most recent HbA1c level was 6.8%. He has never undergone neuropsychological testing before. He is fluent in Greek.

A 42-year-old female presents with a complaint of chronic pain in the upper trapezius muscle that has lasted for more than 8 weeks. The pain is described as a dull, aching sensation that radiates to the shoulder blade and down the arm, accompanied by occasional muscle spasms. The patient reports no history of trauma or recent physical activity, but she does have a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of her time sitting in front of a computer. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they provide only temporary relief. The patient has never received physiotherapy or local injections for her pain. The patient's medical history is unremarkable, with no significant past illnesses or surgeries. She is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical examination reveals tenderness and trigger points in the upper trapezius muscle. The patient meets the Simon's diagnostic criteria for myofascial pain syndrome and is eligible for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She has been recommended for Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell (CART) therapy. She is married with two children, ages 3 and 5. She has a full-time job as a teacher. She is generally healthy and active, but has concerns about the upcoming CART therapy and managing her symptoms. She has an iPhone and is comfortable using technology. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how to manage her symptoms and to be more involved in her healthcare.

This is a 62-year-old woman who recently underwent prosthetic replacement of a diseased heart valve. She is currently taking anticoagulation medicine to reduce her risk of thromboembolism due to the thrombogenic nature of mechanical heart valves. She has been experiencing some difficulty with the monitoring of her anticoagulation levels, as it requires her to visit medical laboratories or hospitals regularly. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of patient self-testing of the International Normalized Ratio (INR) compared to the usual care. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any genetic clotting disorders that would exclude her from participating. She is willing and able to learn how to perform finger stick blood sampling for self-testing and does not have any physical disabilities that would prevent her from doing so. She hopes that by participating in this study, she will have better control of her anticoagulation levels and improve her overall quality of life.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been diagnosed with type II diabetes for the past 15 years. She has a history of foot burn injury that occurred 9 months ago in a kitchen accident, resulting in a 15% total body surface area (TBSA) burn. She has been receiving physical therapy rehabilitation to improve her balance and mobility. She has no cognitive or mental dysfunctions and is not pregnant. She has no history of cancer or severe vascular complications. She is able to walk but experiences difficulty with balance and confidence due to her foot injury. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her balance and quality of life.

Pt is a 35yo M with a history of aortic coarctation repair at age 10. The patient has a family history of coronary artery disease and has been experiencing chest discomfort on exertion. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of acute or chronic inflammatory disease, malignancies, or diabetes mellitus. The patient's blood pressure is well controlled on lisinopril, and he has a normal lipid profile. The patient is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the potential cardiovascular complications associated with aortic coarctation.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) since the age of 8. She currently takes medication for her ADHD and has been stable on the same medication for the past year. She struggles with impulsivity, distraction, and difficulty focusing on tasks for extended periods of time. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores alternative forms of cognitive training for patients with ADHD. She enjoys playing video games and is excited about the prospect of using a Virtual Reality video game, "The Secret Trail of Moon (TSTM)," as a cognitive tool to improve her attention and executive functioning skills. She has no plans for mobility in the next 3 months and is willing to commit to the study visits and training sessions. Her parents are supportive of her participation and have signed the informed consent form.

A 29-year-old woman who is 38 weeks pregnant is scheduled for an elective cesarean delivery due to a previous cesarean section. She has no history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, or cardiovascular disease. Her pregnancy has been uneventful so far, with no complications. She has a normal hemoglobin level and no history of coagulopathy disease. The patient has not experienced any prolonged labor or premature rupture of membrane. She is carrying a single fetus and has no history of multiple pregnancies. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial and none of the exclusion criteria. She is willing to participate in the study and is looking forward to contributing to medical research.

Pt is a 55yo M with a long-standing history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has had difficulty managing his blood glucose levels despite efforts to adhere to a strict medication regimen and dietary changes. Recently, he has noticed some blurriness and distortion in his vision, which prompted him to visit his eye doctor. Upon evaluation, he was diagnosed with diabetic macular edema (DME), a common complication in people with diabetes where blood vessels in the eye leak fluid, resulting in swelling inside the back of the eye and progressive vision loss. He has been offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial investigating the genetic factors that may influence the development of DME. The study will require one visit to the National Institutes of Health eye clinic, where he will undergo an eye examination, optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fluorescein angiography (FA) to evaluate the severity of his DME. He will also be required to provide a blood sample for genetic testing. The study will investigate whether single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), erythropoietin (EPO), endothelin-1 (EDN1) and receptor for advanced glycation end product (RAGE) genes affect the development and progression of DME. No treatment will be provided as part of this protocol, but he will be allowed to receive standard-of-care treatment at the NEI under this protocol.

A 28-year-old woman presents with acute abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. A pregnancy test was positive, and an ultrasound reveals an ectopic pregnancy in the right fallopian tube. Her β-hCG level is 10,000 mIU/mL, and the gestational sac has a diameter of 3 cm. The patient is hemodynamically stable, and laboratory tests show no deleterious effects of methotrexate treatment on organ functions. She agrees to methotrexate treatment and follow-up.

A 55 year old male patient with a history of COPD was referred to the clinic for the study. He has a 20 pack-year smoking history and was diagnosed with COPD 5 years ago. He has a medical record of spirometry confirmed by a pulmonologist, showing an FEV1/FVC ratio of less than 0.7. He has been receiving outpatient treatment for COPD and has a history of exacerbations in the past year. He does not have a history of lung cancer or any other interventional studies. He is able to understand the study procedure and has given written informed consent for participation in the study.

A 35-year-old African American woman was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) when she was 28 years old. She has been experiencing joint pain, swelling, and stiffness, as well as fatigue and occasional fever. She has been taking hydroxychloroquine and prednisone for the past 6 years, but she still has flare-ups of her symptoms despite the medications. She participated in a previous clinical trial with CEP 33457 and completed at least visit 8 (week 24) and is interested in participating in a long-term study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of repeated administration of CEP 33457. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She agrees to use a medically accepted method of contraception for the duration of the study and for 30 days after discontinuation of study drug treatment. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has no history of positive test results for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) or hepatitis C virus antibody (HCV Ab). She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

75-year-old male with end-stage renal disease listed for kidney transplantation presents with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on dialysis for the past year and is currently receiving hemodialysis three times a week. His past medical history is significant for coronary artery disease with stents placement, peripheral vascular disease with right leg amputation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He is currently on several medications, including aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, metoprolol, and insulin. The patient has been invited to participate in a clinical trial investigating the health-related quality of life in kidney transplant candidates over the age of 65. He will be monitored using the Kidney Disease and Quality of Life (KDQOL-SF) form every 6 months until transplantation, and then at 10 weeks post-transplant, 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years. The study will also explore the patient's expectations before and after transplantation, as well as the relationship between pre-transplant comorbidity, post-operative complications, post-transplant 1-year survival, and HRQOL. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has agreed to participate.

As this is a retrospective study, no active patient participation is required. The study will review records of approximately 100 patients who have been treated with the AngioVac Venous Drainage Cannula and the Extracorporeal Circuit between February 1, 2013, and February 28, 2015, across up to 12 centers within the United States. Therefore, no patient description is necessary for this clinical trial.

Patient is a 7-year-old boy from the United States who has been diagnosed with X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency (XSCID). He has a proven mutation in the common gamma chain gene as defined by direct sequencing of patient DNA, and no available HLA matched sibling donor. He has had chronic active infections in the past 2 years, including respiratory and gastrointestinal infections, and has required treatment with systemic antibacterial, antifungal or antiviral antibiotics for 14 days. He has also been diagnosed with chronic pulmonary disease, with evidence of restrictive or obstructive disease on pulmonary function tests. He requires regular IgG supplementation due to hypogammaglobulinemia. He has not been treated with any chemotherapeutic agents in the past 3 months. He weighs 25 kg and is willing to have blood and tissue samples stored.

A 34-year-old woman, who is 39 weeks pregnant and has a history of a previous cesarean section, is scheduled for an elective cesarean section due to a breech presentation. She has no known allergies and has not had a fever or taken antibiotics in the past 14 days. Her gestational diabetes is well-controlled with diet and exercise. The patient has been informed of the study and has given her consent to participate.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who underwent bone marrow transplant (BMT) for leukemia two years ago. She has been doing well since the transplant, with no major health issues. However, her parents have noticed that she has gained some weight in the past year and is having difficulty losing it despite a healthy diet and exercise. They are concerned about the long-term effects of her BMT and want to ensure that she is not at risk for developing metabolic syndrome. The patient has no history of type 1 diabetes, HIV, chronic liver disease, cystic fibrosis, chronic renal failure or known genetic syndrome. She is not currently being treated with Megace® or anabolic steroids. She is willing to undergo testing for growth hormone deficiency, abnormal lipid metabolism, hypothyroidism and gonadal dysgenesis, as well as participate in a study to evaluate for concomitant endocrinopathy, prediabetes and impaired glucose tolerance in BMT survivors. The patient is able to comply with the study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 30. She has struggled with weight loss in the past, having tried multiple diets and exercise programs without success. She has no significant medical history, including no history of diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, or other chronic illnesses. She does not smoke or use drugs, and has no history of alcohol abuse. She is not currently taking any medications that affect body weight. The patient has moderate physical activity, but she states that she has difficulty adhering to a strict exercise regimen due to time constraints. She is interested in participating in the study to understand why she has difficulty losing weight and to potentially receive treatment with lorcaserin. The patient is aware of the risks involved in the study, including undergoing a lumbar puncture, and is willing to participate in both phase 1 and phase 2 of the study.

The patient is an adult diagnosed with a hematologic malignancy who has completed a prior idelalisib study and is currently receiving clinical benefit from the treatment. They are willing and able to comply with the study protocol and have a negative pregnancy test result (if female of childbearing potential) or agree to use specified methods of contraception (if male or female of childbearing potential) during the study. There are no other specific medical conditions or medications that would exclude the patient from participating in the trial.

Patient is a 64-year-old man from the United States with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He presents with a thoracic aortic aneurysm and impaired renal function. His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has no history of allergy or adverse reaction to nesiritide. He has not had any organ transplant or preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP). He has no signs of decompensated congestive heart failure (CHF). His creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dL (normal range: 0.7-1.3 mg/dL). He is otherwise healthy and physically active.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with acute ischemic stroke. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension that has been controlled with medication for the last 5 years. He presented to the hospital with the sudden onset of weakness on the right side of his body and difficulty speaking. A CT scan confirmed a small ischemic lesion in the left hemisphere of his brain. He was immediately started on antiplatelet therapy and is currently stable. He has good vision in both eyes and no history of eye diseases. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent. His SVD score is >1. He does not have anophthalmia.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently admitted to the hospital for an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). He underwent a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for his condition and was diagnosed with high risk of ventricular remodeling. His NT-Pro-BNP levels were found to be above 1000 ng/L. He experienced typical chest pain for more than 30 minutes and had a significant electrocardiogram (ECG) changes with ST-segment elevation in two or more contiguous leads. His peak cardiac enzyme levels were significantly elevated as well. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medications for it. He is married and lives with his wife in a 3-room flat. He has two children, both of whom are working and live in the same city as him. He is a retired civil servant and spends most of his time watching TV and reading newspapers. He has never used any telemedicine services before and is not very familiar with technology. He has some difficulty in walking and feels breathless while climbing stairs. His body mass index (BMI) is 28, and his blood pressure (BP) is 140/90 mmHg. There is no significant finding in his physical examination except for a mild pitting edema in both lower limbs.

25-year-old female with no history of foot pain, trauma, or deformities. She reports no chronic medical conditions or use of medications. She has no known allergies. Physical examination of the feet reveals no abnormalities or tenderness on palpation. She has a normal gait and no difficulty with ambulation. The patient has no history of previous foot surgery or any other interventions related to the feet. She is interested in participating in a study to help further our understanding of normal sonographic anatomy of the soft tissues of the foot.

The patient is a 65-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing intermittent pain in her legs during activities such as walking or climbing stairs. She has a history of smoking and hypertension, and her ankle/brachial index (ABI) is found to be below 0.90 at rest. She has not been prescribed medications for intermittent claudication in the past three months. She does not have any active cancer or liver or renal disease. The patient has no cognitive dysfunction and is willing to participate in a supervised exercise program.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years. He experiences severe foot dystonia on his right side, which makes walking difficult and uncomfortable. He has never been treated with botulinum toxin before. He reports that his dystonia is present for more than 1 hour a day and has a severity index of 3 (severe). He is currently on medication for his Parkinson's disease but it does not alleviate his foot dystonia. He has no contraindications to the use of botulinum toxin and is willing to participate in the study. He is affiliated with social security and has agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25 year old female who is in good health and not a smoker. She has no significant medical history, is not pregnant or lactating, and does not have a family history of long QT syndrome or sudden death possibly related to LQTS. She has no history of drug abuse or use of drugs known to inhibit or induce cytochrome P450 enzymes and/or P-glycoprotein. She weighs 60kg and is within 15% of ideal body weight. The patient has no significant EKG changes and is willing to participate in a pharmacokinetic and exploratory electrocardiogram (ECG) study to characterize the pharmacokinetics of colchicine after an oral dosing regimen of 4.8 mg over 6 hours and compare ECG changes, if any, from this dosing regimen to that of a single dose of moxifloxacin 400 mg, a positive control for the corrected QT interval (QTc) prolongation.

A 42-year-old man presented to the clinic with complaints of dysphagia and chest pain. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. He has a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and has been taking proton pump inhibitors (PPI) for 2 years. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no prior history of esophageal surgery or endoscopic treatments. He is willing to participate in the study and can tolerate pre and post-operative testing. He meets the inclusion criteria of having an esophageal motor disorder (EMD) and will receive a treatment such as POEM, neumatic dilatation, LHM, or botox injection. He does not have any exclusion criteria that would prevent him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of diffuse systemic sclerosis for the past 12 months. She has noticed tightening and hardening of her skin, as well as decreased mobility in her hands and feet. She has been diagnosed with the disease by a rheumatologist and has a Modified Rodnan Skin Score within the range specified by the study protocol. She has not been taking any protocol-specified immunosuppressants within the past 4 weeks, nor has she been on systemic corticosteroids in a dose greater than 10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and agrees to delay reproduction during the trial and up to 9 months after the final infusion. She is willing to attend follow-up assessments for a minimum of 9 months and agrees to delay elective surgery during the trial and up to 9 months after the final infusion. She is generally in good health with no severe kidney, heart, lung, or gastrointestinal disease.

A 57-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) presents with symptoms of fatigue, shortness of breath, and leg swelling. He has been on haemodialysis for the past 6 months and is currently taking phosphate-lowering medication. The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus for which he takes medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His physical examination reveals bilateral pitting oedema up to the mid-shin and a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg. Blood tests show elevated phosphate levels, but his calcium and parathyroid hormone levels are within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve his health outcomes and is able to provide informed consent. He is not scheduled for kidney transplant and does not have any major illness that may result in death in the next 6 months.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. He has a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. He has undergone biopsy and surgery to obtain tissue samples for diagnosis and treatment planning. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided consent for the use of his tissue samples for genetic mutation analysis and gene expression studies. The patient has not received any prior concurrent therapy for his cancer.

Patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of metastatic breast cancer. She has received prior chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Her current treatment plan includes taxane or ixabepilone therapy. She has at least one measurable lesion with a diameter of ≥ 2 cm by CT scan. The patient's serum calcium level is below 10.5 mg/dL, and she has an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1. Her ANC is ≥ 1,500/mm³, platelet count is ≥ 100,000/mm³, and hemoglobin is ≥ 9 g/dL. She has a life expectancy of > 3 months, and she is not currently pregnant. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 6 months, no serious medical illness that would limit survival to < 3 months, and no active, uncontrolled bacterial, viral or fungal infection. She is not currently receiving concurrent chemotherapy or biologic therapy, including trastuzumab and bevacizumab, and she is not receiving hormonal agents for breast cancer, except luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone agonists. The patient is a suitable candidate for the trial to determine the best dose and best way to give paricalcitol when added to chemotherapy for treating patients with metastatic breast cancer.

6-year-old female diagnosed with congenital heart disease requiring elective open-heart surgery with extracorporeal circulation (ECC). The patient has no known allergies or contraindications to scheduled medication. The patient's parents have provided written informed consent, and the patient has assented to participate in the study. The patient's American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification is II.

55 y/o female with recurrent leiomyosarcoma on the right thigh. She has had multiple surgeries and radiation therapy in the past to treat the disease. She is currently experiencing progressive disease with a 4 cm mass on the right thigh and a 3 cm mass on the left thigh. Past medical history is significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. She has no history of peripheral neuropathy, active or uncontrolled infection, or other malignancies. She is not pregnant or nursing. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80%. She has not received gemcitabine or docetaxel in the past. Her absolute neutrophil count is 2,200/mm^3 and platelet count is 150,000/mm^3. Her bilirubin and creatinine levels are within normal limits.

A 68-year-old man who has been experiencing symptoms of heart failure (shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in the legs) for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, but they are well-controlled with medication. He has never been diagnosed with heart disease before. He takes medication for his conditions and a daily aspirin. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is 28. He has not had a heart attack or cardiac surgery in the past. He is willing to undergo a cardiac MRI to help diagnose his heart condition.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hyperuricemia and no other significant medical history presents for screening for a clinical trial. He has not been diagnosed with gout and has no known allergies or sensitivities to tranilast or allopurinol. He is not currently pregnant or nursing.

A 60-year-old man was referred to the cardiology department for coronary angiography due to chest pain. He has a history of high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. He has a BMI of 28 and has never had any kidney problems. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a manager in a logistics company and exercises regularly, going for a 30 minute walk every day. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to any medication. He has been taking aspirin for the past year as part of his preventive medication regimen. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the understanding of CIN and reduce the risk for future patients.

A 60-year-old man with a history of Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS) has been referred for a clinical trial. He was diagnosed with MDS 6 months ago and has been receiving supportive care. He has no other underlying health issues and has a good performance status, scoring 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale. He has never received intensive combination chemotherapy or high-dose ara-C. He is currently not taking any medications except for occasional pain relievers. He is married and has two grown-up children. He has retired from his job as a teacher due to his illness. He is willing to provide written informed consent and committed to complying with study procedures and follow-up. He has no history of allergies or active infections.

Pt is a 55yo M with a past medical history significant for COPD and pneumonia, who was admitted to the hospital 30 days ago due to respiratory failure and required intubation and mechanical ventilation. The patient remains on mechanical ventilation due to persistent hypoxemia and difficulty weaning. The patient is currently stable and meets the eligibility criteria for a clinical trial examining the effects of neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) on patients with prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). The patient is able to communicate with the medical team and has no active infections or hemodynamic instability. The patient is not currently on high-dose vasopressors and has no known neuromuscular diseases or bone contractures. The patient's BMI is 27 kg/m2, and there is no evidence of severe edema. The patient is interested in participating in the trial and hopes that the NMES will help improve their muscle strength and aid in the weaning process from mechanical ventilation.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been experiencing dry, itchy and gritty eyes for the past 6 months. She has tried over-the-counter lubricant eye drops with no significant relief. Upon examination by an ophthalmologist, she was diagnosed with mild to moderate dry eye disease. She wears glasses for mild myopia and has a best corrected visual acuity of +0.4 logMAR. She has no history of ocular allergies, infections or inflammatory conditions. She is willing to comply with contraception requirements and sign informed consent for the study. She does not use contact lenses and has not had any recent ophthalmic surgeries. She is willing to suspend current treatments for dry eye disease to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman who has been experiencing blurred vision and difficulty seeing at night for the past year. She has no previous history of eye problems and wears glasses for myopia. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. Her family history is negative for eye disorders. The ophthalmologic exam revealed a diagnosis of keratoconus with a corneal thickness of less than 400 microns. She is eligible for the Corneal Cross Linking procedure and has consented to participate in the German Corneal Cross Linking Register.

A 35-year old marketing professional was referred to a methadone maintenance program by his primary care physician due to opioid addiction. He was introduced to opioids after a major surgery a few years ago. He has been on methadone maintenance treatment for the past month. He lives alone in an apartment, but he has a supportive family who visit him regularly. He has a history of depression but has been stable on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) for the past year. He reports occasional alcohol use but denies any use of illicit drugs other than opioids. He is fluent in English, and he owns a smartphone that he uses regularly throughout the day. He is interested in participating in the study to explore additional avenues for recovery and support. He is currently unemployed and is actively seeking employment. He reports occasional cravings for opioids but has not relapsed since starting methadone treatment.

45-year-old male scheduled for neuromonitoring spine surgery with a history of hypertension and well-controlled type 2 diabetes. The patient has normal renal and liver function and is not taking any medications for their medical conditions. The patient has never been diagnosed with diabetes insipidus or any other kidney or liver disease. They are not taking any medications known to cause DI and do not have a history of polyuria. The patient speaks Korean fluently and is able to understand the consent forms. The patient does not fall into the category of vulnerable subjects and is able to give informed consent for the study.

A 45-year-old female comes to the clinic complaining of a gritty sensation in her eyes, occasional blurry vision, and redness. She reports that these symptoms have been present for the past several months and have significantly affected her quality of life. She is currently using over-the-counter eye drops, but the relief is only temporary. She has a history of seasonal allergies and is currently taking antihistamines for them. She wears glasses for nearsightedness but does not use contact lenses. On examination, she has mild conjunctival injection and punctate keratitis, with no evidence of corneal ulceration or infection. The Schirmer's test confirms a low tear production (less than 5 mm in 5 minutes). Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may benefit her condition.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently hospitalized for a cryptogenic stroke. He presents to the clinic for follow-up with complaints of mild weakness on the right side of his body, difficulty with speech, and occasional headaches. The patient reports a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has a family history of stroke, with his mother having had a stroke at age 75. The patient has been taking aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily for the past 5 years. He is currently retired and lives with his wife. He denies any history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. His physical examination reveals mild right-sided weakness and mild dysarthria. His lab studies show a hemoglobin A1c level of 6.8%, a total cholesterol level of 180 mg/dL, and a low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level of 100 mg/dL. An echocardiogram shows a patent foramen ovale. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if device closure of the PFO combined with antiplatelet medical management can reduce his risk of recurrent stroke or TIA.

The patient is a 55-year-old non-smoking woman who has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer at stage IIIB. She has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy for lung cancer. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, and is able to perform most activities of daily living but is limited in strenuous activities. She has no known history of peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 1, and is not currently pregnant or nursing. The patient has no concurrent other malignancies other than basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. She is HIV-negative, and has no medical condition that will not permit treatment or follow-up according to the protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of chronic alcohol abuse for the past 5 years. He presents with jaundice, abdominal pain, and fatigue. His medical history is significant for hypertension and he is currently taking lisinopril. Blood tests reveal elevated bilirubin levels and a Maddrey score of 36. Liver biopsy confirms the diagnosis of severe alcoholic hepatitis. He has not been diagnosed with any other liver disease and is negative for hepatitis B and C. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and gives his consent. He has no history of allergies to any medications, including N-acetyl cysteine.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of schizophrenia was referred to the clinic. She has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for over 5 years and is currently on antipsychotic medication but has reported inadequate efficacy, poor tolerance, and non-acceptability of her current dosage regimen. She is an outpatient and capable of making treatment decisions. She has no history of substance or alcohol abuse, and her urine drug screen was negative. She is not pregnant, lactating, or requiring treatment for epilepsy. She has no other DSM-IV Axis I diagnosis, concomitant organic mental disorder, or mental retardation. She is fluent in English and French and has a grade 7 proficiency level in both languages. She is willing to use a reliable method of birth control during the study. She has not been on clozapine treatment within the last 4 weeks and has no known intolerance to seroquel IR. Her TSH concentration is within the normal range. She is not on any drugs that induce or inhibit the hepatic metabolizing cytochrome P450 3A4 enzymes or long-acting injectable antipsychotic drugs. She has no history of idiopathic or drug-induced agranulocytosis, and her ECG does not show any cardiac abnormality. She has no evidence of clinically relevant disease or laboratory test results outside the reference range that would interfere with the study outcome. She has no history of non-compliance or previous enrollment in the present study. She is willing to accommodate the visit schedule and is not involved in the planning and conduct of the study.

Patient is a 10-year-old child residing in Birmingham who is scheduled to undergo a chair General Anaesthetic for the extraction of at least one carious tooth at Birmingham Dental Hospital. The child has a permanent molar tooth that is 'sound and sealable'. The child is cooperative and able to undergo a clinical dental examination. The child will be accompanied by an adult with legal capacity to give informed consent. The child has no signs of a systemic illness or oral symptoms that would preclude sealant placement. The accompanying adult is able to confirm that they will be contactable and able to attend for review during the 2 years duration of the study.

A 10-year-old boy was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia and received a hematopoietic stem cell transplant at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. He has been closely monitored by the BMT-AFU clinic since then. He is currently in remission and has had no major complications post-transplant. He and his family are willing to participate in long-term data collection to assess his clinical and psychosocial outcomes. They hope that their participation will help future transplant recipients and their families.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman from Israel who is currently in her first trimester of pregnancy. She is married and this is her first pregnancy. She has a healthy lifestyle and no medical concerns. Her pre-pregnancy BMI is 22 and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She is not currently taking any medication except for prenatal vitamins. She has no history of thyroid disease or use of contrast material in the past year. She is willing to participate in the study and has no other chronic diseases. She is interested in ensuring the best possible health for her and her developing baby.

42-year-old female presents with chronic pelvic pain and discomfort for the last 6 months. The patient reports a pain score of 4 out of 10 on the visual analog scale (VAS), associated with lower urinary tract symptoms such as urgency, frequency, and nocturia. The discomfort is localized in the suprapubic and perineal area and affects her daily activities and quality of life. The patient denies any history of oncology or pelvic radiotherapy treatment, but has a history of endometriosis and pelvic inflammatory disease. She reports no systemic or neurological diseases but has been experiencing mild symptoms of depression and anxiety due to the chronic pain. The patient is interested in conservative treatment options and has consented to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effects of physiotherapeutic interventions on Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome (CPPS).

52 yo male with a recent diagnosis of active pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) and diabetes mellitus type 2 (DM2) referred to a health clinic in Orizaba, Veracruz for management of both conditions. The patient resides in a rural area and has limited access to health care services. He reports poor glucose control and difficulty adhering to treatment due to his work schedule and lack of support from family members. The patient has no history of HIV infection or pregnancy. He has been started on TB treatment and is willing to participate in the joint management strategy study. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia. Family History: - Father with history of type 2 diabetes. Social History: - Lives in a crowded household with several family members. - Works as a farm laborer with irregular hours. - Limited access to nutritious food.

50-year-old female with a BMI of 28 kg/m2 was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes three years ago. The patient is currently on metformin for glycemic control and has no history of insulin use. She has no history of chronic complications of diabetes such as kidney disease, retinopathy, neuropathy, or lower limb vascular lesions. The patient has no history of acute complications such as diabetic ketoacidosis or high permeability syndrome. She has never experienced severe hypoglycemia. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction or acute coronary syndrome, and her blood pressure is well controlled with medication with an SBP of 130 mmHg and a DBP of 80 mmHg. She has no history of cancer, blood donation, or blood transfusion. She is a non-smoker, non-alcoholic, and has no history of drug abuse. The patient is willing to accept physical contraception and sign the informed consent voluntarily. Her fasting blood glucose level is 9.7mmol/L, and her HbA1c level is 8.5%.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with a 9 cm hepatocellular carcinoma in the left lobe of the liver. He has no history of liver resection or radiotherapy. His liver function is Child-Pugh class A with a normal prothrombin time and international normalized ratio. CT scan showed no tumor thrombosis in the main trunk or right and left branch of the portal vein or major hepatic vein. He is not using any medication that can affect the coagulation system. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. He agrees to participate in the study and undergo either the "crush-clamp" technique or liver resection using the Harmonic Scalpel device.

A 45-year-old woman presents with complaints of stress urinary incontinence, which she has been experiencing for the past year. She describes leakage of urine with activities such as exercise, coughing, or sneezing. She denies any history of pelvic surgery or pelvic organ prolapse, and has not received any prior treatment for SUI such as pelvic floor physical therapy or medications. She is not currently pregnant and has no active infections. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes lisinopril. She does not smoke and consumes alcohol socially. On physical exam, a positive bladder stress test is noted. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating a novel treatment for SUI using a fractional carbon dioxide laser. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and signs the informed consent form. She meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria. She is randomized to receive either active or sham fCO2 laser treatments, and receives three treatments approximately four weeks apart. The primary efficacy endpoint is assessed four weeks after completing all treatments, and treatment durability and safety are assessed eight weeks after the primary endpoint.

The patient is a 50-year-old Hispanic man residing in Somerville, Massachusetts, within 200 meters from interstate I-93. He is overweight and has been diagnosed with pre-hypertension.
