He speaks both English and Spanish fluently and is able to answer questionnaires. He lives at home full-time with his family, but none of them smoke. He has not had a heart attack, stroke, or any other major cardiovascular outcome. He is not taking any anti-hypertensive or anti-inflammatory medications. He does not have a mechanical air handling system in his home, and he does not have any routine high exposures to traffic pollution away from home. He lives in an apartment with highway-facing windows that is no more than 3 stories tall. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of High Efficiency Particulate Air (HEPA) filtration on cardiovascular risk in individuals who live near urban highways.

A 52-year-old woman with a 15-year history of type 2 diabetes presents with recurrent episodes of nausea, vomiting, and early satiety for the past 6 months. She has been experiencing significant fluctuations in her glycemic control with HbA1c levels ranging from 8.5% to 10.2%. The patient has been on multiple medications to control her blood sugar, including metformin, glimepiride, and insulin glargine. Despite these efforts, she has been unable to maintain stable glycemic control. She underwent a wireless motility capsule study, which revealed delayed gastric emptying, and was diagnosed with gastroparesis. The patient has been referred for per-oral pyloromyotomy (POP), which she has agreed to undergo. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the impact of POP on her glycemic control. She is able to complete all study requirements and willing to wear a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) sensor.

This clinical trial is not applicable to patients as it is a study aimed at evaluating the effectiveness of an education program for pediatric residents on the diagnosis and management of disruptive behavior disorders in children. Therefore, there are no patient descriptions required for this trial.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who was previously diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He underwent surgery followed by radiation therapy for his primary tumor, but subsequently developed metastatic disease in his cervical lymph nodes. He received chemotherapy with cisplatin and cetuximab but had progressive disease after three cycles of treatment. He has not received any systemic therapy for the past 6 months. Imaging studies show multiple lymph nodes with increased metabolic activity. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and does not have any significant comorbidities. His lab studies show normal organ function and blood counts. A new biopsy was obtained and showed PD-L1 expression on at least 1% of tumor cells. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for TQB2450 and meets all of the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) for the past 5 years. She experiences shortness of breath, chest pain and dizzy spells that are not controlled with medication. She has undergone previous invasive septal reduction therapy (ethanol septal ablation/surgical myectomy), but her symptoms have not improved. Due to her increased risk and co-morbidities, she is not a candidate for further invasive treatment. She currently has a pacemaker implanted. Her ventricular septal thickness at the site of ablation is 18mm. She is able to tolerate lying flat for one hour. She has no history of chest radiotherapy and is willing to provide written informed consent. The patient is interested in participating in the Non-Invasive Radiation Ablation in Patients with Hypertrophic CardioMyopathy (NIRA-HOCM) clinical trial and hopes to find a non-invasive treatment option for her symptoms.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. She has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She presents with fatigue, night sweats, and a palpable mass in her left axilla. Her laboratory results show elevated LDH levels and uric acid levels at 10.5 mg/dL. Her white blood cell count is within normal limits. She has no known allergies and is mentally competent to sign an informed consent. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo repeated administration of SR29142 for five days.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer (MBC) in the left breast 2 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy and was started on adjuvant chemotherapy with anthracycline and taxane. However, she developed distant metastasis to the liver and bones 6 months ago. She has been treated with hormonal therapy and radiation to the bone lesions but there has been no improvement in her symptoms or disease status. Her HER2 status is negative. She has no other significant medical history and her ECOG performance status is 1. She is not currently receiving any other cancer treatments or immunotherapy. She has no history of seizures or serious infections. She has normal cardiac function with a LVEF within institutional normal limits by multiple gated acquisition (MUGA) scan. She is not pregnant or lactating and has agreed to use an acceptable method of birth control. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

A 38-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy and axillary dissection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. She has been clinically free of any identifiable disease since then but has noticed a rising level of CA 15-3 on two consecutive occasions separated by two weeks. She is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or autoimmune diseases. The patient has no other active cancer except for basal cell carcinoma on her arm, which was removed surgically last year. She is not pregnant, and her pregnancy test is negative. She is fertile but using effective contraception. The patient has never received immunotherapy or a vaccine with any of the antigens in the study. Her lymphocyte count is at least 500/mm^3 and WBC is at least 3,000/mm^3. Her liver function tests are normal, with AST and alkaline phosphatase levels not exceeding 1.5 times the upper limit of normal. Her creatinine levels are also within normal limits. The patient has no clinically significant cardiac disease, and her Karnofsky performance status is between 80-100%. She is interested in participating in the trial to potentially reduce her risk of breast cancer recurrence.

This is a 30-year-old female who has been suffering from IBS symptoms for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing frequent abdominal pain, bloating, and irregular bowel movements, which have been affecting her daily life. She has tried various dietary changes and over-the-counter medications, but none have provided significant relief. She has been diagnosed with IBS by her gastroenterologist and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore a new diet with a low-FODMAP content. She is able to read, understand, and write Swedish and meets all the eligibility criteria for the study. She has no history of severe heart, liver, neurologic, psychological, or gastrointestinal disease such as celiac disease or inflammatory bowel disease. She is eager to participate in the study and hopes to find a dietary approach that will alleviate her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

38 yo F with a history of migraine headaches with aura and a previous participation in the CAPSS-277 study, presenting with recurrent migraines despite current prophylactic medication. Patient is in generally good health, compliant with oral medications, and using birth control. Past Medical History: - Migraine headaches with aura - Anxiety - Hypothyroidism - Asthma - Allergic rhinitis - Polycystic ovary syndrome - History of DVT treated with Lovenox and Coumadin

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of high cholesterol. He has been on a diet and exercise regimen for the past 6 months but has not seen significant improvement in his cholesterol levels. He has no history of heart disease or any other significant medical conditions. He is currently taking no medications for his high cholesterol. He leads an active lifestyle and participates in regular physical activity such as jogging and cycling. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol only occasionally. His BMI is 26 and his blood pressure is within normal range. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his high cholesterol.

A 25-year-old male patient with a history of depression has been brought to the emergency department after intentionally ingesting a large quantity of sleeping pills. The patient's roommate called an ambulance after finding him unconscious in his apartment. Upon arrival, the patient was found to be somnolent and unresponsive to verbal stimuli. His vital signs are stable, and he is breathing spontaneously. The patient has no significant medical history, and he is not taking any medications. The patient's girlfriend reports that he has been struggling with depression for the past six months and has been talking about suicide for the past few weeks. The patient is not currently under the care of a mental health professional. The physician has decided to admit the patient to the hospital for observation and monitoring. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

An 80-year-old male with a history of Alzheimer's disease presents with behavioral changes including increased agitation and apathy. He currently resides in a nursing home and is dependent on assistance from caregivers for his daily activities. He has no history of seizures, deafness or blindness, and is not currently using a pacemaker. His family has provided informed consent for his participation in the study. The patient is able to participate in the LUMEEN immersive workshops and is willing to take part in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male veteran who was deployed to Afghanistan for 2 years. He reported experiencing several traumatic events during his deployment, including witnessing the death of a fellow soldier and being involved in a roadside bombing. The patient has been experiencing symptoms of PTSD for the past 6 months, including recurring flashbacks, nightmares, and hyperarousal. He has sought treatment at the VA hospital and has been diagnosed with PTSD based on a score of 55 on the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale (CAPS-5). The patient is able to read and speak English fluently and has explicitly denied any suicidal or homicidal ideation. He has no history of brain injury or major confounding psychiatric disorders, and is not currently undergoing substance abuse treatment. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help improve the diagnosis and management of PTSD for himself and other veterans.

A 55 yo non-smoking woman with a BMI of 28 who has recently been diagnosed with impaired glucose tolerance. She has no history of CAD or cerebrovascular disease that would preclude exercise and has not received any implantable defibrillator. She reports no active cancer and has no history of chronic pulmonary, thyroid, renal, liver, or hematological disease. She is not HIV positive nor prone to malnutrition and has no history of sickle cell anemia. She has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes but is not currently taking medication to treat it. Her diabetes is poorly controlled and she has poorly controlled hypertension. She is not taking any medications including beta-blockers, oral steroids, warfarin, certain statins, HRT, OCP, TZD, or chronic steroids or NSAIDS that may not be safely discontinued temporarily for specific procedures. She is not allergic to lidocaine or heparin and has not had any recent weight change. She is not currently pregnant or nursing and has no physical impairment limiting exercise. She has no history of dementia or unstable clinical depression.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who has recently been diagnosed with stage III follicular lymphoma. She has been experiencing fatigue and night sweats for the past few months. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies to drugs or food. The patient has normal renal function and her ALT levels are within normal range. She has an expected survival of 6 months or more, and her ECOG grade is 1. The patient has been informed about the trial and has given her consent to participate.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been smoking cigarettes for the past 6 years. She smokes about a pack of cigarettes a day and has tried to quit smoking multiple times without success. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and drinks alcohol only on social occasions. She works as a part-time waitress and attends college part-time. She has a history of occasional migraines and takes over the counter pain medications to manage them. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease and has never used nicotine replacement products, bupropion or varenicline to quit smoking. She has an estimated IQ score of 95. She is not currently taking any medications for depression, anxiety, or attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Her vital signs are within normal range. She has no nasal pathology that would preclude administration of nasal spray. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of nicotine on attention mechanisms in smokers.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who works as a software engineer in a private corporation in Oslo, Norway. She lives 5km away from her workplace and has a sedentary lifestyle due to her desk job. She has a family history of heart disease, and her father had a heart attack at a young age. She is interested in cycling to work to improve her physical activity and reduce her risk of heart disease. She has not cycled regularly before and feels intimidated by the distance and the hills in her area. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and use the electrically assisted bicycle provided to her for the duration of the study. She is excited to see if this intervention can improve her cardiorespiratory fitness and overall health.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing chest discomfort and shortness of breath on exertion for the past month. His primary care physician has recommended a coronary CT angiography to evaluate for possible coronary artery disease. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction or unstable angina pectoris. He has a BMI of 28kg/m2 and normal renal function with a serum creatinine of 0.9mg/dl. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity reactions to contrast agents. He is not pregnant and has no plans for pregnancy. He has not participated in any other clinical trials for cardiovascular disease and is not taking any medications that would contraindicate the use of adenosine.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has a history of hydrocephalus and has had a VP shunt placed to manage the condition. The patient has been experiencing symptoms of shunt malfunction, including headaches, nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. The patient has undergone an imaging study of the head which confirmed the malfunction. The patient is scheduled for a shunt revision and is being considered for participation in the study to test the sensitivity and specificity of a shunt tap in predicting shunt failure.

A 52-year-old Egyptian man who has been diagnosed with hepatitis C virus (HCV) related liver failure is being considered for liver transplantation. He has been on the waiting list for several months and has now been offered a living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) procedure. He is married with two children and works as a carpenter. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past year. He is currently on antiviral treatment for his HCV and takes medication for his high blood pressure. He is fluent in Arabic and has given his informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. He underwent immunotherapy treatment, but unfortunately, it was not successful. Upon further testing, it was discovered that he has a confirmed NRG1 gene fusion in his solid tumor. He will be enrolled in a multi-site retrospective chart review study in the U.S. to determine the real-world effectiveness of afatinib (Gilotrif) following immunotherapy in the treatment of metastatic, squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. The patient will be followed up for at least 3 months after initiation of afatinib treatment and will not have received any other Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)/ErbB-directed therapy other than afatinib.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been suffering from chronic low back pain for the past 10 years. She reports that the pain started after she had a car accident and has been gradually worsening over the years. She describes the pain as a dull ache in the lower back that radiates down to her buttocks and thighs. The pain is aggravated by prolonged sitting or standing and is relieved by lying down. She has tried various treatments such as painkillers, massages, and physical therapy, but none have provided significant relief. She has no history of surgery on the low back region or any structural deformities. She does not have any skin conditions that prevent the usage of electrotherapy. She does not have a pacemaker or any other types of implants on the low back, pelvis, and thoracic region. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare the effects of interferential current therapy (IF) and pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (PEMF) on her chronic low back pain, functional status, and quality of life.

A 35-year-old female with a history of chronic migraine (CM) for over a year. She experiences headaches at least 15 days per month, with the majority of them lasting for over 4 hours. The patient has tried several preventive medications with no significant improvement. She is currently not taking any preventive medication but takes analgesics as needed. She has no history of allergy or sensitivity to any component of the test medication. She is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of any significant medical condition that might interfere with neuromuscular function. She is willing to provide responses to questionnaires, complete the online diary and has email and internet access.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who is scheduled to undergo elective surgery for a gallbladder removal due to recurring gallstones. He lives in Strasbourg and has Wi-Fi connectivity at his home. He has no history of skin disease or any implantable devices. He is affiliated with the French social security system and is able to understand and give written informed consent for the study. He is physically and mentally capable of wearing the MultiSense® strip for 7 days after his surgery and understands the importance of accurate monitoring of his vital signs during the post-operative period. He is interested in participating in the study and contributing to the advancement of remote monitoring technology for post-operative patients.

A 35-year-old male presents with complaints of pain and bleeding during defecation for the past 2 months. He reports a history of occasional constipation and straining during bowel movements. Physical examination reveals grade 2 hemorrhoids with no evidence of any other perianal pathology. He has no history of malignancy or chronic colorectal diseases, and does not routinely use vasoactive medications. The patient is enrolled in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a sodium pentaborat based gel on perianal benign diseases. He is assigned to Group-3 (n:50), the group for grade 2 hemorrhoidal disease cases. The study involves the use of the gel and regular follow-up appointments for evaluation of symptoms and treatment response.

The patient is a 55 year-old woman who recently underwent hand surgery for carpal instability. She had no prior history of bone fractures or deformities, and her skeletal anatomy and function in both arms are normal. She is not currently taking any medication that could affect bone density. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no medical conditions that would exclude her from the study, such as renal or liver disease, diabetes, or epilepsy. She has not been diagnosed with osteoporosis and has not experienced any osteoporotic hip or vertebral fractures. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.

A 45-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has been referred to the ophthalmology department of Penn State College of Medicine for the evaluation of mild to moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Her hemoglobin A1c is under control with oral anti-hyperglycemia agents, and her best-corrected visual acuity in the study eye is 20/30. She has not undergone any retinal photocoagulation or treatment for diabetic retinopathy in the past three months, and the investigator does not anticipate any such treatment in the subsequent two years. Her central subfield thickness on OCT is less than 275 microns, and her pupil dilation and media clarity are sufficient for high-quality fundus photographs. Her visual field and dark adaptation testing are reliable, but her FDP function is abnormal with a foveal sensitivity of 28.2 dB. She is willing to give informed consent and is eligible for the study.

55-year-old male with a history of smoking and recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. The patient underwent lung resection surgery two months ago and has not received chemotherapy or radiotherapy. However, the patient has been experiencing shortness of breath and a decrease in exercise tolerance since the surgery. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve his physical performance and overall quality of life. The patient has no known cardiac conditions or severe joint diseases. The patient is willing to participate in an outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program or respiratory exercise training.

A 72-year-old male came to the clinic complaining of difficulty walking and climbing stairs. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. He reports having lost weight recently and feeling weaker than usual. He has a BMI of 28 and has been living independently. He is able to complete a 400-meter walk, but it takes him longer than 15 minutes. He does not have any hearing or speech problems, nor any visual impairments. He does not have any neuromuscular or psychiatric disorders. He is not currently participating in any physical activity program. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent.

25 yo F with a history of malocclusion and facial asymmetry who underwent orthognathic surgery (BSSO) to correct the skeletal differences between the upper and lower jaw. The patient is currently experiencing facial swelling after the surgery and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of manual lymphatic drainage on post-operative swelling. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the study, is not on any deviant medication, and has no facial hair. The patient is willing to undergo 5 sessions of MLD as part of the intervention group and understands the possible risks and benefits associated with the study. The patient will fill out a questionnaire to assess pain and swelling and will have 3D face scans taken at specified intervals to objectively measure the swelling. The patient is excited to participate in a study that could potentially improve the post-operative experience for others undergoing orthognathic surgery.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer presents with metastatic disease to the liver and lungs. She has previously received multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her disease has progressed despite treatment. She is currently experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and abdominal discomfort. Imaging studies reveal multiple liver lesions and bilateral lung nodules. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus, but has been diagnosed with hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia, both of which are controlled with medication. She has no malabsorption syndrome or other conditions that would interfere with enteral absorption. The patient is willing to use contraception during the trial.

35 yo M in a stable monogamous relationship with his partner for 3 years, presenting with a history of premature ejaculation during sexual activity. He reports that he typically ejaculates within 1-2 minutes of vaginal penetration, causing significant distress for both himself and his partner. He denies any history of medication withdrawal, interpersonal difficulty or distress related to his sexual function. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not currently taking any medications for the treatment of premature ejaculation. He has no history of seizures or major psychiatric disorders and denies alcohol abuse or dependence. His partner is willing to participate in the study and agrees to attempt sexual intercourse at the minimum intervals specified in the protocol. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating.

A 35-year-old male, non-smoker, with a body mass index (BMI) of 24 kg/m2, is scheduled to undergo elective surgery under general anesthesia. He has no history of cervical spine surgery or disease, esophageal operation, or gastroesophageal reflux disease. He has no risk factors for difficult intubation. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He has never undergone general anesthesia before. He is currently on no medications.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather students in 5th-6th grade (aged 10-14) from selected schools in the Los Angeles metropolitan area. There are no specific patient characteristics needed for this trial.

A 32-year-old woman and her 35-year-old husband, both carriers of the thalassemia gene, have been trying to conceive for over two years without success. They have been undergoing fertility treatment, including IVF with PGD, at a hospital in southern China since 2011. The woman has a history of irregular menstrual cycles, and her husband has a low sperm count. They have both undergone genetic testing, which revealed that the woman carries the HBA genetic defect, while her husband carries the HBB genetic defect. They have agreed to participate in a retrospective study investigating the effect of these genetic defects on early embryo development. They have undergone blastula biopsy as part of their PGD treatment, and the embryos with HBA or HBB genetic defects have been identified and documented. They have not experienced any previous abortions related to the biopsy procedure, and their diagnostic results are clear. They are willing to share their medical history and participate in this study to contribute to the advancement of reproductive health research.

The patient is a newborn baby boy who was admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) due to neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) after his mother used opiates during pregnancy. The baby was born full term at 38 weeks and is currently symptomatic with a Finnegan Neonatal Abstinence Score that meets the NICU protocol for treatment. The baby has no history of seizures or major congenital malformations. The parents are English-speaking and able to understand and consent to the study.

28-year-old female with a 3-year history of Crohn's disease presents for follow-up after undergoing ileocolonic resection and small bowel to colonic anastomosis, 3 weeks prior. She is currently on Mesalamine and has been on Infliximab in the past, but not in the last 8 weeks. She reports occasional diarrhea, abdominal pain, and nausea, but denies any rectal bleeding or weight loss. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent endoscopic recurrence following surgery for Crohn's disease. She does not have any other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures and attend study visits. She currently uses an effective method of contraception and has a negative serum pregnancy test.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has a family history of breast cancer. Her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 50 and underwent a mastectomy followed by chemotherapy. The patient is currently sedentary and does not engage in any regular physical activity. She is interested in learning more about how physical activity can reduce her risk of developing breast cancer and is willing to participate in a physical activity intervention developed for healthy men and women. She is able to speak and read English and has no known medical conditions that would make physical activity unsafe. She is not currently pregnant and has no plans to move from the area in the next 3 months.

62-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis of the right knee, currently experiencing significant pain and difficulty with ambulation. She has tried conservative management with physical therapy and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs without significant improvement. She is scheduled to undergo a total knee replacement surgery and has been approached to participate in a clinical study evaluating the effect of platelet rich plasma (PRP) on short-term patient outcomes following TKR. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has agreed to be blinded to her treatment group assignment. She is willing and able to return for follow-up over at least a six-week post-operative period. Her hemoglobin levels are within normal limits for her gender. She has no known allergies to bovine thrombin or other bovine-derived products. She has no significant medical or psychiatric history that would preclude her from participating in the study.

An 80-year-old retired teacher, Mrs. Johnson, is referred to a memory clinic by her primary care physician for memory loss and mild confusion. She has completed high school and has no history of developmental or learning disabilities. She is a native English speaker and has no psychiatric conditions, sleep disturbances, or history of heavy metal exposure. She has been diagnosed with probable Alzheimer's disease by a specialty clinic and has been taking a cholinesterase inhibitor for the past four weeks. Her resting blood pressure is 145/85 mmHg, and she has stable hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her TSH and Vitamin B12 levels are normal. Mrs. Johnson lives alone, and her adult daughter is her knowledgeable informant who can report her day-to-day activities. Mrs. Johnson is able to give assent/consent to participate in the research study. She has no orthopedic, neurologic, or behavioral limitations that may preclude exercise training and is willing to participate in a three-day/week physical activity program for up to 6 months.

A 55-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) presents with chronic pain in multiple joints, particularly in the hands and feet. She has been taking disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for the past year, but still experiences significant pain. The patient reports difficulty sleeping due to the pain and is frustrated with the lack of improvement in her quality of life despite treatment for RA. She has no other painful conditions, malignancies, or hemopathies. The patient does not have a history of psychiatric disorders or dementia but has been diagnosed with mild depression. She is able to provide written consent and is interested in participating in a study that investigates the multidimensional origin of pain in RA patients.

A 28-year-old woman is in her third trimester of pregnancy and plans to deliver at a hospital. She has had regular prenatal care and has not experienced any complications during pregnancy. She has a good understanding of the importance of vaccinations and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the best measles vaccination schedule for her newborn. The woman has a history of receiving the measles vaccine during childhood and has not had any known exposure to measles during her pregnancy. She is expecting a healthy term infant and is interested in learning more about the study. The woman is able to provide informed consent for her newborn to participate in the trial.

A 42-year-old accountant was recently diagnosed with mild to moderate hypertension during a routine check-up. She has no prior history of hypertension or any other significant medical conditions. Her blood pressure readings have been consistently high for the past three months, despite making lifestyle modifications such as reducing her salt intake and increasing her physical activity. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. Her current medications include a daily multivitamin and occasional ibuprofen for headaches. She is interested in participating in the study to help manage her blood pressure and potentially reduce her risk of developing complications associated with hypertension. She is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all required follow-up visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) with a history of oral self-biting injuries. He has difficulty controlling his oral muscles, which leads to frequent biting of his tongue and cheeks, causing considerable discomfort and pain. The patient has tried various methods to manage these injuries, including topical anesthetics and soft food diets, with limited success. He has been referred to the ALS Functional Unit at Bellvitge University Hospital to participate in a clinical trial assessing the effectiveness of two oral appliances for managing oral self-biting injuries. The patient is able to understand and consent to the study requirements and has no advanced evolution of the disease that would exclude him from treatment.

The patient is a 40-year-old female with a body mass index (BMI) of 38 kg/m2. She has a history of prediabetes and has been trying to lose weight for the past year with no success. She is currently not on any antidiabetic medications but has been advised by her physician to make lifestyle changes to prevent the onset of diabetes. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently enrolled in any weight loss or exercise programs. She is a non-smoker and is not pregnant or nursing.

A 2 year and 8 months old girl was referred to the clinic by her pediatrician due to a delayed onset of independent walking. She was born at term with a weight of 2.5 kg and no significant medical history. Her mother noticed a delay in motor development since she was 6 months old. She started crawling at 12 months of age and was able to stand with support at 20 months. She recently started walking independently for 4 months with a tendency to walk on her right toes. She was diagnosed with left hemiplegic cerebral palsy after a MRI scan at 2 years old. She has no history of musculoskeletal trauma, surgery, or botulinum toxin injections. She is currently receiving physical therapy once a week. Her mother reports no known skin allergies.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing perianal fistulas, which have caused her significant discomfort and pain. She has tried various treatments, including antibiotics and topical creams, but has not seen any improvement. The pain has affected her daily life, as it is difficult for her to sit or stand for extended periods of time. She has no known allergies or drug abuse issues, and is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the study and follow up with the gastroenterologist and colorectal surgeon. She hopes that this study will help her find relief from the perianal fistulas and improve her quality of life.

A 25 year old man who identifies as gay presented to the clinic for HIV testing. He reported having unprotected anal sex with multiple partners in the past year. He is currently not in a monogamous relationship and has not been in one for the past 2 years. He is willing to participate in a study that could help him reduce his risk of contracting HIV. He has no obvious mental disorder and is able to attend all scheduled study visits. He is currently not enrolled in any Phase III HIV vaccine trial or any HIV prevention study.

A 22-year-old female who has been dealing with vitiligo for the past 5 years. She has multiple symmetrical white patches on her face, arms, and legs. She has tried various treatments including topical corticosteroids and phototherapy, but with little success in repigmenting her skin. Her vitiligo has caused her significant distress and has impacted her quality of life. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores the use of camouflage in combination with topical application and/or NB-UVB to improve the appearance of her skin and potentially repigment her white patches. She has no history of allergies and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease for the past 4 years. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss over the past few months. Despite being on a stable dose of azathioprine and 5-ASA preparation, his Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) is above 200 and his CRP is above 10 mg/l. He is currently on a low dose of prednisolone (5mg/day). He has not been on long-term antibiotics for Crohn's disease or any other indication. He is not pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding. He has not participated in any other trials in the last 3 months. He has no known sensitivity to clarithromycin. He has not had any complications requiring surgery due to Crohn's disease.

A 45-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She has no history of breast cancer in her family, nor has she ever been pregnant. She underwent a lumpectomy and has been cleared for adjuvant chemotherapy. She is HER2 negative and has no other underlying health conditions. Her ECOG score is 0. Her blood work shows ANC of 2.5 x 10^9/L, platelets of 120 x 10^9/L and hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL. Her liver function tests show bilirubin of 0.9 x UNL, AST of 24 U/L, ALT of 26 U/L, and alkaline phosphatase of 80 U/L. Her creatinine level is 0.9 x UNL and her creatinine clearance is 85 mL/min. Her FEVI is 60% and her electrocardiogram is normal. She has not received any prior treatment for breast cancer and is not currently on any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance breast cancer treatment.

78 year old woman with a history of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer, currently admitted to the oncology service at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania for management of dyspnea and cough. She has previously received chemotherapy and radiation therapy for her cancer. The patient is able to speak and read fluently in English and has no cognitive impairment that would prevent her from giving informed consent. Vital signs are currently stable. The patient has no code status limitations noted in her electronic medical record and does not have a feeding tube or tracheostomy in place. She is experiencing shortness of breath and some pain, but it is well-controlled with medication. She has been hospitalized on the oncology service in the past year.

A 32-year-old woman presented to the neurology clinic with complaints of blurry vision and tingling sensations in her left hand and foot. These symptoms started 2 weeks ago and have been gradually worsening. She denies any fever, headaches, or recent infections. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently on any medications. She works as a graphic designer and is married with no children. On examination, the patient has decreased visual acuity in her left eye and reduced sensation in her left hand and foot. The MRI of her brain shows multiple hyperintense lesions in the periventricular white matter and corpus callosum, suggestive of multiple sclerosis. The patient is diagnosed with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) and is advised to undergo a lumbar puncture to confirm the diagnosis and to explore the possibility of future progression to multiple sclerosis (MS). The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form.

A 28-year-old female with a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days, experiencing intense cramping pain that lasts for 2 to 3 days during her menstrual period. She has been experiencing this pain for the past 8 years and has been taking analgesics persistently, which have not provided enough relief. She has to take leave from work and daily activities during her menstrual period because of the pain. She has no history of head injury, pituitary gland disease, organic pelvic disease, or psychiatric disorder. She is not pregnant, has not given birth, and does not have any metal or pacemaker implant. She has not taken any hormone agents within the past 6 months.

This clinical trial does not involve patients and does not require recruitment. It is a retrospective cohort study using routinely collected health care data to investigate the impact of smoke-free legislation on perinatal health in England.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who presented with fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes medication. Physical examination revealed enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and axilla. A biopsy of the lymph node showed the presence of non-follicular low grade B-cell lymphoma. Subsequent staging studies showed no evidence of disease involvement outside the lymph nodes. The patient has no significant family history of cancer. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at identifying factors that may predict the prognosis of her lymphoma.

50 year-old woman who underwent chemotherapy treatment for breast cancer and is experiencing cognitive changes including impairment of memory, learning, concentration, reasoning, executive function, attention and visuo visio-spatial skills. She is right handed and speaks English fluently. She has completed her cancer treatment and is considered curative with the exception of endocrine therapy after chemotherapy. She is able to attend daily intervention (Monday-Friday) for 2 weeks. She has not participated in another interventional study within the last 6 months. She does not have a history of brain metastasis or other brain tumor, stroke, traumatic brain injury, epilepsy, or other seizure disorders. She is not taking medication for seizures or that could lower seizure threshold if withdrawn. She is able to complete the neuropsychological testing, and has not been treated with rTMS before. She does not have any routine contraindications for MRI and is not pregnant or thinking of becoming pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis homozygous F508del-CFTR mutation. She has a history of chronic respiratory infections and has been on chronic therapies for CF lung disease, including hypertonic saline and azithromycin, for the past year. She has a sweat chloride level of 75 mEq/L and a weight of 50 kg. Her forced expiratory volume (FEV1) is 60% of predicted normal for her age, gender, and height. She has no acute infections or pulmonary exacerbations that require treatment or hospitalization within the past 2 weeks. Her blood hemoglobin and serum albumin levels are within normal range. She has no history of abnormal renal function or solid organ or hematological transplantation. She does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse in the past year. She does not use continuous or nocturnal supplemental oxygen.

A 60-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer and underwent surgery to remove the primary lesion. She has been confirmed to have estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer and is scheduled to receive adjuvant endocrine therapy with aromatase inhibitors (AIs) in the following year. She has been postmenopausal for 5 years and has a history of mild osteopenia. Her blood tests show leukocyte count of 4*10(9)/L and platelet count of 85*10(9)/L. Her serum glutamate oxaloacetate(AST/SGOT) and serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase(ALT/SGPT) are both within the normal range. Her serum creatinine/blood urea nitrogen(BUN) levels are also within the normal range. She has no history of pelvic fracture or bone metabolic disease and has not received any drugs that interfere with bone metabolism in the last 12 months. Her baseline Bone Mineral Density T-score is -1.5 SD. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to test the efficacy of two traditional Chinese medicine in preventing osteoporosis induced by adjuvant endocrine therapy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been suffering from hip pain for the past year. The pain has been gradually worsening and is now affecting his daily activities, such as walking and climbing stairs. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis by his physician and has been deemed a candidate for hip replacement. He has no history of severe osteoporosis, osteonecrosis, or avascular necrosis, and has adequate bone stock to support the device. The patient is mentally capable and willing to participate in the clinical study, and will be available for follow-up out to 2 years and annually thereafter until the last patient reaches the two-year evaluation. He has no known metal sensitivity, is not severely overweight, and has no known moderate or severe renal insufficiency. The patient has consented to participate in the clinical study and will undergo hip replacement surgery with the Cormet Hip Resurfacing implant system.

The patient is a 23-year-old female college student who binge drinks at least once a month and consumes energy drinks on a regular basis. She has a BMI of 22 and weighs 60 kg. She has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorders, and has never participated in a clinical trial before. The patient is a non-smoker and drinks coffee occasionally. She is currently using hormonal contraception and has no plan of becoming pregnant in the near future. The patient has no evidence of somatic or psychiatric disorders and her general blood and urine laboratory tests are within normal ranges. She has never experienced any adverse reactions to alcohol or energy drinks. She is able to understand the nature of the study and willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for the past 2 years. He is currently on insulin treatment and has a stable disease with HbA1c levels less than 8.5%. He has not experienced any severe hypoglycemic events in the past year. He weighs 80 kg and is in good health according to his medical history, physical examination, vital signs, ECG, and lab assessments. He has no history of cancer, cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, endocrinological, hematological, dermatological, venereal, neurological, or psychiatric diseases or other major diseases. He has not participated in any clinical trial or received any investigational drug in the past 3 months. He has no known or suspected allergy to trial products or related products. He is mentally capable and willing to participate in the trial.

A 45-year-old male with a history of von Willebrand disease presented to the clinic with complaints of rectal bleeding and discomfort. The bleeding started about 6 months ago and has been intermittent but has increased in frequency over time. The patient has tried dietary and behavioral measures, as well as venotropic and topical medication, without relief. Physical examination revealed internal hemorrhoids of grade II. A colonoscopy was performed and showed no other abnormalities. The patient is on anticoagulant therapy with warfarin to manage his bleeding disorder. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 42-year-old female with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery 6 years ago presents with recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging studies reveal a possible biliary obstruction. The patient is referred for an Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) to further evaluate the condition. However, due to her altered gastric anatomy, the use of an endoscopic overtube is required to facilitate the procedure. The patient is able to provide informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

45-year-old male with chronic hepatitis C infection diagnosed 3 months ago presents with elevated liver enzyme levels and fatigue. He has no prior treatment with HCV antiviral medications and has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. Liver biopsy performed 2 years ago revealed non-cirrhotic fibrosis. Fasting blood glucose and HbA1c levels are within normal limits. He has a history of hypertension but is currently managed effectively on a stable regimen of one antihypertensive medication. He has not used any herbal/natural remedies with antiviral activity in the past 30 days. He has no history of immunologically mediated disease, cardiac or pulmonary disease, seizure disorder, or anticonvulsant use. He has not undergone major organ transplantation and has not received systemic antineoplastic or immunomodulatory treatment within the past 6 months.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with unresectable pancreatic cancer. He experienced abdominal pain, jaundice, and significant weight loss over the past few months. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. A CT scan showed involvement of critical vasculature, making surgical resection unfavorable. The patient completed chemotherapy and radiation therapy four weeks ago and has adequately recovered from the side effects. His Karnofsky performance status is 80%. His lab results show normal organ and marrow functions, with a platelet count of 80,000/mm3 and total bilirubin level of 1.2 mg/dL. He has no history of autoimmune diseases and understands the study protocol. He agrees to use adequate contraception as he is married and has a child. He is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic back pain for the past 5 years. She has tried various treatment modalities, including physical therapy, acupuncture, and non-opioid medications, without significant relief. She was ultimately prescribed opioid medication for the management of her pain, which has been effective in reducing her discomfort and improving her quality of life. She has been on long-term opioid therapy (LtOT) for the past 18 months, taking oxycodone 10mg every 6 hours. The patient reports some mild side effects, such as constipation and drowsiness, which she manages with over-the-counter medications. She has no history of drug abuse or addiction, and she takes her medication as prescribed. She has a history of depression and anxiety, for which she takes medication and attends therapy sessions. The patient is currently working as a full-time administrative assistant and has no plans to change her employment status. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the understanding of the risks associated with long-term opioid therapy in chronic noncancer pain patients, and to potentially contribute to the development of national guidelines for opioid use in South Korea. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to complete the screening tools and questionnaires evaluated in the study.

A 45-year-old African-American woman came to the clinic with complaints of persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the past 6 months. She had a history of recurrent respiratory infections and was recently diagnosed with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on a chest X-ray. A subsequent CT scan of the chest revealed multiple enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes. A clinical suspicion of sarcoidosis was raised, and the patient's pulmonologist recommended a bronchoscopy with biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. The patient was randomized to undergo either a standard TBNA or EBUS-TBNA as part of a clinical trial comparing the diagnostic yield of these procedures for sarcoidosis. She provided informed consent and was deemed eligible for the study. Her coagulation profile was normal, and she was not taking any medications that could interfere with the bronchoscopy procedure.

A 52-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia presented to the clinic with symptoms of heart failure including fatigue, shortness of breath, and swelling in the lower extremities. He has been diagnosed with heart failure for the past 6 months and has been receiving optimal medical therapy. The patient underwent a 256-slices CT-scan which revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30%. The patient has no history of coronary artery bypass surgery or pacemaker implantation within the last 3 months. The patient has no atrial fibrillation and does not require intravenous positive inotropic agents or diuretics. The patient has no immunodeficiency or neutrophil count below 1000 mm3. The patient has no active neoplasia or treated cancer within the last 5 years. The patient has medical insurance and has given written informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia. He has already undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has not responded as expected. The patient is now in urgent need of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) as the disease is progressing rapidly. However, there is no fully HLA matched sibling donor available for the patient. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for this Expanded Access Protocol Using Alpha/Beta T and CD19+ Depleted PBSC. The patient's overall health condition is good, with a Karnofsky performance score of 80. The patient has no history of uncontrolled bacterial, viral, or fungal infections, and has signed informed consent to participate in the trial. The patient's family members have been evaluated as potential donors, but none of them are fully HLA matched. The patient will be matched with an unrelated donor identified through the National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) who meets the matching criteria of the program. The donor will undergo mobilization of peripheral stem cells and apheresis to provide PBSC for the transplant. The patient will be monitored closely for any adverse events during and after the transplant.

This is a 62 year-old male who has a history of stroke that resulted in right-sided hemiparesis. He has been experiencing spasticity in his right elbow flexor muscles, which has been causing difficulties in performing daily activities, such as dressing and feeding himself. He has been evaluated by his physician and diagnosed with grade 2 spasticity, as measured by the Modified Ashworth Scale. He has not received any botulinum toxin injections within the last three months and does not have a history of elbow contracture or any operations on his spastic upper extremity. He has agreed to participate in the study to assess the severity of spasticity in different forearm positions, as he hopes to improve his ability to perform daily activities.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman living in a PPR flat in Kuala Lumpur. She is able to walk without any assistance but has noticed that she is starting to feel weaker and less energetic than before. She has no history of chronic diseases but has had some minor surgeries in the past, including a hip replacement surgery six months ago. She is able to read and write and has no cognitive or sensory impairments. She has never participated in any health interventional studies before and is willing to participate in this program to learn more about how to prevent frailty and improve her overall health. She is interested in learning more about nutrition and exercise and is looking forward to participating in group sessions with other elderly individuals in her community.

A 56-year-old male patient who has undergone radical prostatectomy for adenocarcinoma of the prostate is experiencing a rising serum prostate-specific antigen level. He has a history of hypertension and takes antihypertensive medication daily. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is allergic to milk but has no known allergic reactions to soy products. He has a Zubrod performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 1 year. He has not received any chemotherapy or hormonal therapy in the past year, and he has never undergone radiotherapy. He is willing to participate in a behavior-based dietary intervention to help him maintain a low-fat, high-fiber, soy-supplemented diet.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who has no significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and phosphate binding capacity of Renazorb. She is willing to follow a controlled phosphate diet and consume the medication orally 3 times a day within 15 minutes after meals. She understands the risks involved in the trial and is willing to provide urine and feces samples for analysis. She is able to stay at the clinical research unit from Day -1 to Day 13 and attend the End-of-Study Visit on Day 20.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently hospitalized due to a hip fracture. During his hospital stay, he was found to have a positive MRSA culture from a nasal swab. He was discharged home with instructions for decolonization therapy. He has no known history of MRSA infection and he is not currently taking any antibiotics. He lives alone and is independent in his activities of daily living. He has no known allergies to medications. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with the treatment protocol. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was diagnosed with diabetes five years ago and has been managing his condition with oral medications prescribed by his primary care physician. He is married and has two teenage children. He works as an office manager and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He struggles with maintaining a healthy diet and consistent exercise routine due to his busy work schedule but is motivated to improve his glycemic control. He has never used telehealth coaching before but is open to the idea of incorporating it into his diabetes management routine. He speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in a qualitative interview to provide feedback on a telehealth coaching platform for glycemic control.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing frequent episodes of diarrhea accompanied by abdominal pain and discomfort for the past year. She has tried various over-the-counter medications but none have provided significant relief. She has not undergone any diagnostic tests for her symptoms yet. She has a family history of irritable bowel syndrome. She is interested in participating in a long-term study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a new medication, YM060, for the treatment of diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome.

The patient is a 28-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia five years ago. He has been taking medication regularly and is currently receiving outpatient treatment. He reports having difficulties with expressing and identifying his emotions, feeling unmotivated and uninterested in his usual activities, and having difficulty with social interactions. His speech is limited and he feels that he has lost his sense of purpose. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has not been involved in any violent incidents in the past year. He lives in an apartment with his family and has no plans to move in the next year. The patient's score on the NSA-16 indicates that he has clinically meaningful negative symptoms. The patient is willing to participate in the MOVE program and is comfortable with the sessions being audio and video recorded for training purposes.

A 25-year-old female with a diagnosis of Type 1 Diabetes presents for a clinical trial comparing intranasal insulin to subcutaneous insulin. She has been on multiple daily injections (MDI) for the past 5 years to manage her diabetes. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2 and her most recent HbA1c level was 7.5%. She has no history of active proliferative retinopathy or nephropathy. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits. She is motivated to find a more convenient and effective way to manage her diabetes.

A 52-year-old Asian woman, with a medical history of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Stage 4 and hypertension, presented to the nephrology clinic for a routine follow-up visit. Her current medications include losartan, amlodipine, and calcium carbonate. Her most recent lab work showed a serum albumin level of 2.9 g/dL and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 22 mL/min/1.73m2. Her body mass index (BMI) is 27.5 kg/m2. She denied any recent weight loss, decreased appetite, or gastrointestinal symptoms. She has never been prescribed an oral nutritional supplement (ONS) before. She understands the study protocol and is willing to provide informed consent. She meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. She will be stratified as a female CKD Stage 4 without T2DM and will receive the renal specific ONS supplement (1-2 servings/day) for 24 weeks in addition to standard of care and dietary counseling. The study will monitor her nutritional status (serum albumin, anthropometrics, quality of life, etc.) and the use of the ONS supplement will be evaluated for efficacy.

A 62 year old male visited the clinic with complaints of chest pain, shortness of breath, and fatigue. An echocardiogram revealed severe calcific aortic stenosis, and the patient was advised to undergo aortic valve replacement surgery. His medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia, all of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of neurological impairment as defined by a NIHSS score of 0 and an mRS score of 0. He is scheduled to undergo aortic valve replacement surgery via a full sternotomy in the next two weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and can provide informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who experienced chest pain that radiated to his left arm. He also felt shortness of breath and sweating. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes enalapril and atorvastatin. He does not smoke and has no history of allergies. He is married and works as a construction worker. He was admitted to the hospital and underwent coronary angiography, which revealed stentfailure due to stentrestenosis. The cardiologist recommended a new intervention with a stent, and the patient agreed to participate in the PROCTOR study. He signed the informed consent form and met all the inclusion criteria, including having a coronary artery diameter larger than 2.5mm and a life expectancy of more than 5 years. He will undergo high-resolution imaging with OCT to improve the diagnosis and enable a more specific or tailored treatment, and he will be followed for 5 years to assess the prevalence of stentpathology in patent or functional stents.

A 68-year-old woman with a history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and hypertension presented with decreased vision in her left eye. Her medical history included a myocardial infarction 5 years ago, for which she underwent stent placement and has been on antiplatelet therapy since then. Her current medications include aspirin, atenolol, and amlodipine. She is a former smoker who quit 15 years ago and denies alcohol consumption. Best-corrected visual acuity in her left eye was 20/100, and the right eye was 20/30. Examination of the left eye revealed hemorrhagic macular changes and a polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy lesion. A diagnosis of PCV secondary to AMD was made, and the patient was referred to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of IRay treatment for PCV. After providing informed consent and meeting the eligibility criteria, the patient received 16 Gy of IRay treatment and Lucentis, followed by Lucentis treatment as needed. The patient will be followed for 2 years to evaluate the change in the proportion of lesion activity and lesion size at 12 months.

A 25-year-old female office worker complains of pain in the upper back region between the shoulder blades. She noticed the pain after long hours of working on her laptop while sitting on a couch with poor posture. She describes it as a constant aching pain that becomes more intense with certain movements. She has no history of trauma or any major illnesses. She has not received any treatment for this pain before. The pain is affecting her ability to work and focus on her daily tasks. She has no neurological symptoms and has never been diagnosed with any degenerative process or osteoporosis. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to alleviate her pain.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic Hepatitis C genotype 1 infection. He had previously been treated with a pegylated interferon and ribavirin but relapsed after the end of treatment response. The patient does not have any non-HCV chronic liver disease and has not received any interferon therapy subsequent to the relapse with pegylated interferon-alpha and ribavirin. The patient's liver function is stable with no signs of decompensated liver disease. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) six months ago. He presented with fatigue, night sweats, and enlarged lymph nodes in his neck and armpits. A biopsy of one of the lymph nodes confirmed the diagnosis of CLL. He was started on chemotherapy with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide and has completed six cycles of treatment. His most recent CT scan showed a partial response to treatment with some residual lymph node enlargement. He has a Zubrod performance status of 1 and his blood counts are within normal limits. He has no history of autoimmune hemolytic anemia or anaphylaxis. He has not received any prior treatment with CAMPATH-1H and is willing to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old male patient was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) due to a severe head injury from a car accident. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication. He has no history of gastric ulcer or any other gastrointestinal problems. He has no known allergies to any medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is married and has two children. He works as a financial analyst and exercises regularly. He has no history of any surgery in the past. The patient or his family has consented to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old male patient came to the clinic complaining of weakness on the right side of his body and difficulty speaking. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He had a stroke 6 months ago, which resulted in weakness on the left side of his body. He takes lisinopril and atorvastatin daily. He has never smoked and does not drink alcohol. He is married and has two children. His past medical history is significant for a myocardial infarction 2 years ago, which was treated with angioplasty and stenting. He understands the purpose of the study and has provided informed consent. He is eligible for this clinical trial as he is aged between 18 and 70 years, has complaints of symptomatic ICAS, and meets all the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

Patient A is a 50-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer. He has not received any systemic therapy for his cancer yet. He works as a teacher and enjoys gardening in his free time. He reports no major medical history except for high blood pressure that is well controlled with medication. He is in overall good health with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. His laboratory values are within normal limits. He is willing to undergo Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT). He is not on any immunosuppressive treatment and has never received any immunotherapy agents. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to comply with the study schedule and understand the risks and benefits of the clinical trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old man with end-stage renal disease requiring hemodialysis. He has been on hemodialysis for the past year and has received at least 5 hemodialysis treatments with a blood flow of 250 ml/min or greater. He is able to speak and understand Danish. The patient has an AV fistula in his left arm, which was created 6 months ago. He has experienced complications with the cannulation of his AV fistula and has been using the sharp needle technique. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate a new method for creating a buttonhole tunnel track by repeated needling of the AV fistula on the same day. The patient does not have an artificial heart valve, is not in high dose immunosuppressive treatment, and does not have any infections in his buttonholes. The patient is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

A 57-year-old woman was diagnosed with locally recurrent breast cancer 6 weeks ago. She has undergone a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy for her breast cancer 3 years ago. She has a history of hypertension, which is controlled by medication. She has no other comorbidities and is otherwise healthy. She is married and has two adult children. She works as a teacher and enjoys gardening in her free time. She has no history of substance abuse or mental illness. She has not received any chemotherapy or targeted therapy for recurrent disease. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been wearing glasses since he was 10 years old. He has a prescription of -3.50 diopters in his right eye and -2.75 diopters in his left eye. He has no history of ocular diseases or surgeries. He does not wear contact lenses. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in undergoing bilateral PRK surgery to correct his refractive error. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He is generally healthy and has no known allergies.

52-year-old woman who underwent cholecystectomy 8 months ago presents with jaundice, abdominal pain, and pruritus. An ultrasound and MRCP confirm the presence of a biliary stricture. Her bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase levels are raised. She has no history of endoscopic therapy for this condition. She is able to adhere to regular follow-up and is not a living-donor liver transplant patient. She meets the inclusion criteria for this trial.

A 32-year-old male, who is a software developer, is interested in participating in the TRIM study on Vitamin B12. He has no known chronic systemic diseases and is not currently taking any vitamin B12 supplements. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol excessively. He has a balanced diet and exercises regularly. The participant is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to give informed consent. He is interested in contributing to scientific research and learning more about his own vitamin B12 levels.

A 25-year-old male presents with a history of perennial allergic rhinitis for the past 4 years. The patient reports experiencing nasal congestion, sneezing, itching, and rhinorrhea all year round. The patient reports that these symptoms are worse in the morning and at night. The patient has tried various over-the-counter antihistamines and decongestants with limited relief. The patient has not received any treatment for the condition in the past 30 days. The patient has a positive allergy skin test for house dust-mite and cat dander. The patient is willing to keep a daily record of his nasal allergies. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of asthma or recent nasal surgery. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to mometasone or other steroids. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

Pt is a 65yo female with a history of OAB symptoms of urinary frequency, urgency, and incontinence for the past 6 months. She has tried lifestyle modifications such as bladder training and pelvic floor exercises with little improvement. She is willing and able to complete the micturition diary and questionnaires correctly. She has not participated in any other interventional study from the time of screening until the final study visit. She has no ongoing symptoms suggestive of bladder outlet obstruction or history of BOO that is currently not well-controlled. Post-Void Residual Volume (PVR) is less than 150 mL. She has no neurogenic bladder or neurological dysfunction or injury which could affect the lower urinary tract or nerve supply. There is no significant stress incontinence or mixed stress/urgency incontinence where stress is the predominant factor as determined by the Investigator. She has no indwelling catheter or practices intermittent self-catheterization. There is no evidence of Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) and no chronic inflammatory condition such as interstitial cystitis, bladder stones, previous pelvic radiation therapy, or previous or current malignant disease of the pelvic organs. She does not reside in a nursing home and is not likely to enter a hospital or nursing home due to medical instability within the next 6 months in the opinion of the Investigator. She has not received intravesical injection in the past 12 months with botulinum toxin, resiniferatoxin, or capsaicin, nor received electro-stimulation therapy for OAB (e.g. sacral nerve stimulation or Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation [PTNS]). She has not begun or changed a bladder training program or pelvic floor exercises less than 30 days prior to Screening. She does not have moderate or severe hepatic impairment defined as Child-Pugh Class B or C or severe renal impairment defined as estimated creatinine clearance less than 29 mL/min determined by Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR, Cockroft-Gault, or MDRD formulae). Her sitting systolic blood pressure is less than 180 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure is less than 110 mmHg. She has no evidence of QT prolongation on electrocardiogram (ECG) defined as QTc greater than 450 msec for males, QTc greater than 470 msec for females or a known history of QT prolongation. She has no clinically significant ECG abnormality or hypersensitivity to any components of mirabegron, other β-AR agonists, or any of the inactive ingredients. She has no concurrent malignancy or history of any malignancy (within the past 5 years), except non-metastatic basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin that has been treated successfully. She has no current history of alcohol and/or drug abuse and is not using prohibited medications which cannot be stopped safely during the period. She has not stopped, started or changed the dose of a restricted medication within the last 30 days prior to Screening. She is not involved in the conduct of the study as an employee of the Astellas group, third party associated with the study, or the study site team. She has not previously received mirabegron.

45-year-old female with a history of overactive bladder is seeking treatment to improve her symptoms. She reports experiencing urgency, frequency, and occasional urge incontinence. She has tried lifestyle modifications, such as bladder training and pelvic floor exercises, but has not seen significant improvement. She is not currently taking any medication for her overactive bladder. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or on any other medication that could interact with solifenacin or oxybutynin. She has no history of chronic constipation or closed angle glaucoma. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

64-year-old male patient, retired, with a history of osteoarthritis of the knee, presented to the orthopaedic clinic complaining of persistent knee pain despite taking painkillers for several months. The pain has been worsening over the last few weeks, and he is experiencing difficulty in walking and performing activities of daily living. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and past smoking history. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 30.8, and he admits to having a sedentary lifestyle. He has never had any previous knee surgeries or injuries. The patient's X-rays show significant joint space narrowing in the medial and lateral compartments of both knees, as well as osteophytes and sclerosis. He is diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and recommended for total knee replacement (TKR) surgery. The patient is able to walk short distances with a walking stick, and his knee pain is rated 8/10. His examination reveals mild joint effusion and crepitus with active and passive range of motion limitation. His muscle strength is preserved, and he has no ligamentous instability. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial comparing bespoke vs standard instrumentation in TKR, and he meets the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been suffering from lower back pain and pain in her legs and buttocks for the past year. The pain is mainly felt when walking or standing for longer periods of time and is partially relieved when flexed. She has no history of lumbar surgery and is able to sit for about 50 minutes without pain. She is able to walk a distance of 20 meters before experiencing pain. An MRI revealed degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis at L3-L4 level. She has no significant medical history and is not on any medication for pain. She is willing to undergo all follow-up examinations for this clinical trial. The patient is well-dressed and well-nourished, and appears to be in good health overall.

This is a 32 year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis for the past 5 years. She has experienced several relapses in the past, with the most recent one occurring 10 days ago, presenting with difficulty in walking and hand tremors.
