She was started on high dose intravenous corticosteroids for 5 days and was then referred for this clinical trial. Her Expanded Disability Status Scale/Functional Systems Score (EDSS/FSS) is 4.5, indicating moderate disability due to the disease. She has not previously been treated with Acthar for MS. She is currently on a stable dose of beta-interferon treatment for the past 2 years. She is willing to participate in the 14-day study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old female from China presenting with symptoms of dysuria, frequency, urgency, and suprapubic pain for the past 2 days. She has noticed white blood cells in her urine and believes she may have a urinary tract infection. The patient has no history of complications related to urinary tract infections. She is not currently pregnant or nursing and is willing to use contraception during the study period. The patient has no history of quinolone hypersensitivity or allergic constitution. She has not taken xanthines, fenbufen, antibiotics, or antibacterials in the past 2 weeks. The patient has no history of overactive bladder or convulsion. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not currently taking any medication. The patient is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has recently noticed that her balance has become more unsteady. She is concerned about the risk of falling and injuring herself. She has no previous experience with Pilates but is interested in participating in the study to see if it can help her improve her balance and reduce her risk of falling. She has no cognitive issues that would prevent her from practicing Pilates, and she does not take any medications that would alter her balance. She is excited to try something new and hopes to see some positive results from the intervention.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of primary brain tumor. He has completed surgical removal of the tumor and is now undergoing external beam cranial radiotherapy. He complains of fatigue, difficulty in concentrating, and decreased quality of life since the initiation of radiotherapy. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. His lab work is within normal limits. He has no history of allergy to any medication, steroid psychosis, or Tourette's Syndrome. He is not on any medication for attention deficit disorder, anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, or substance abuse. He is not taking any antidepressant medication. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study if he is fertile.

25 year old female diagnosed with bulimia nervosa for the past 3 years. She has a BMI of 20 and has experienced multiple episodes of binge eating and purging each week. She has previously attempted to seek help through traditional therapy but was not able to attend regular sessions due to work and school schedules. She is currently not undergoing any psychological treatment and is interested in trying an internet-based treatment program that can be tailored to her specific needs and schedule. She has access to a computer and internet at home and is willing to participate in the study for the next 8 weeks.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman in her first pregnancy at full term. She had a spontaneous vaginal delivery with a mediolateral episiotomy performed during the second stage of labor to facilitate the delivery of her baby. The patient is experiencing moderate to severe pain in the perineal area following the episiotomy repair procedure. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare the postoperative pain following repair of episiotomy by continuous or interrupted suturing. The patient has no previous medical history of chronic diseases, and there are no indications of fetal distress or other complications during delivery. She did not receive epidural analgesia during labor and does not have any factors that could affect wound healing. The patient's BMI is within the normal range, and she has no allergies to medications.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who presented to the Emergency Department with acute onset of severe abdominal pain in the right lower quadrant. He reports that the pain started around 6 hours ago and has been getting progressively worse. He also complains of nausea and vomiting. On examination, the patient has tenderness and guarding over the right lower quadrant of the abdomen.  The patient has no previous history of appendicectomy. The doctor must enter free text describing the patient's symptoms and clinical presentation into the prediction algorithm to determine the likelihood of appendicitis.

45-year-old male with a history of colon cancer is in need of central venous access port implantation for chemotherapy. He has no known allergies or drug intolerances. He is currently on no medications except for aspirin for cardiovascular prophylaxis. His blood clotting is normal and he has no history of central venous thrombosis or septic state. He has no past history of shoulder trauma or surgery. He has no known pneumothorax or agranulocytosis. He has been informed about the study and has given his consent for the implantation of a totally implantable central venous access port under local anesthesia using either ultrasound-guided subclavian vein puncture or cephalic vein dissection.

This is a 65 year-old male with a history of smoking and presenting with non-specific chest pain. A CT scan revealed a 3cm right pulmonary nodule in the upper lobe. The patient underwent a biopsy which confirmed non-small cell lung cancer. Further imaging showed no evidence of metastasis, and the patient was deemed medically inoperable due to underlying pulmonary disease. The patient was offered stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) as an alternative to surgery. The patient has no other concurrent illnesses and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a postmenopausal woman who is at least five years after her last menstruation, or has had both ovaries surgically removed at least two years prior to the trial start. She is in good general health with no significant illnesses that could interfere with her participation in the trial as determined by her physician. She has not used any type of vaginal or vulvar preparations, such as pessaries, contraceptive sponges, douches, or vaginal moisturizers, or other non-oestrogenic medications including K-Y jelly, within the past month. She does not have hot flushes that require systemic hormone replacement treatment, and has not had a previous history of breast cancer or abnormal genital bleeding. She has a normal mammogram within the past year prior to the trial start. She is able to speak and write in the German language. She is not known or suspected to have any allergy to estradiol or related products, and is not currently using steroid hormones or drugs known to significantly influence estrogen metabolism, such as barbiturates, phenytoin, rifampicin, or carbamazepine. She has not participated in any other trial involving other investigational products within the last 30 days prior to the first planned drug administration.

There is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial as it is focused on assessing the effectiveness of an e-prescribing interface for hydroxychloroquine. However, eligible participants for this study are all providers that prescribed hydroxychloroquine in the year previous to the intervention start date in rheumatology and dermatology clinics. Inactive providers in rheumatology and dermatology clinics are excluded from the study.

The patient is a 6-year-old male child who was admitted to the Pediatric Critical Ill Unit at University Hospital in Montpellier, France, due to respiratory distress caused by pneumonia. The patient is currently stable and is not requiring any respiratory support. He is a native French speaker and his parents are present and have provided consent for him to participate in the MUSIDORE PED Study. The patient is alert and oriented, and able to follow instructions. He has no history of deafness or other hearing impairment. The investigators will randomly assign the patient to undergo a cleaning care procedure with or without music therapy, and will compare the variation of FLACC scores before and during the procedure. The patient will serve as his own control in this study. The parents have also provided consent for the procedure to be videotaped for research purposes.

The patient is a 65 year old man with metastatic hormone-resistant prostate cancer. He has been experiencing difficulty urinating, frequent urination, and blood in his urine for the past year. Biopsy results confirmed the diagnosis of prostate cancer, and he underwent surgery to remove his prostate gland. Despite treatment, his prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels continued to rise, indicating that the cancer had spread to other parts of his body. Imaging studies revealed that the cancer had metastasized to his bones, including his spine and hip. He has received anti-androgen therapy and chemotherapy in the past, but the disease has progressed despite treatment. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, is otherwise healthy, and is able to take oral medication. He meets all other eligibility criteria for the study, including having not received abiraterone or dasatinib previously. He agrees to use contraception throughout study treatment as he has fathering potential.

A 28 year old Japanese male who is in good health and has no history of any major medical issues is interested in participating in this clinical trial. He is fluent in Japanese and has a valid Japanese passport. His parents and grandparents are all Japanese. He has no known allergies and takes no medications. His laboratory parameters are within normal limits and he has a screening serum urate level of 5.2 mg/dL. He has not undergone any major surgery in the past 3 months and has not been exposed to any investigational drugs or medical devices in the past 30 days. He is willing to provide written informed consent and is able to understand the study procedures and the potential risks involved.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is focused on testing the effectiveness of electronic health record-based interventions for improving follow-up in primary care, and it involves primary care providers rather than patients.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing migraines for the past 5 years. She has been diagnosed with chronic migraine, experiencing more than 15 headache days per month, with each headache lasting for 4-72 hours. She has tried various medications for migraine prevention, but none have been completely effective. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no known cardiovascular, pulmonary, endocrine-metabolic, rheumatic or other neurologic disease or psychiatric disorder. She does not smoke or use alcohol or drugs. She has been sedentary for the past 6 months and is interested in participating in a study to determine the effect of aerobic exercise training on migraine prevention. She is willing to commit to a 20-week study and is able to attend 3 exercise sessions per week, each lasting 40 minutes. She is able to read and understand the study procedures and is able to give written informed consent.

This clinical trial is looking for women who have given birth at a term of 22 weeks or more, or to a fetus with a birth weight of 500g or more, regardless of the type of delivery, parity, or fetal presentation. The study will take place at the Clermont-Ferrand University Hospital Center in France. The objective is to assess the prevalence of depression at 2 months, 6 months, and 1 year postpartum in women who have had an immediate postpartum hemorrhage (defined as blood loss of 500mL or more within 24 hours of delivery). The study will also include a cohort of partners of the women who gave birth. The partners must also be affiliated with French CNAMTS (salaried worker) health insurance. The intervention will consist of 3 questionnaire surveys, and the participants will receive an email with a participation number and a link to the self-administered questionnaires. The study requires a total of 1542 women to be included and will be conducted in compliance with Good Clinical Practices and French public health law. Women who do not understand French, refuse to participate, or did not give birth at the Clermont-Ferrand University Hospital Center maternity unit and were secondarily transferred there postpartum are excluded. Partners who do not meet the inclusion criteria or refuse to participate are also excluded.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) based on one relapse with time dissemination on MRI. She has had symptoms for less than one year, and her disease has progressed rapidly, resulting in an EDSS score of 4. She is concerned about the potential for her condition to worsen and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options. She is currently using oral contraceptives as a method of birth control. She has no history of immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory treatments, and she has not received any corticosteroids in the past 2 weeks. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has no other medical conditions that might interfere with the study, and she is able to provide informed consent. Her cardiac function is normal, and she has no history of hematologic malignancy or liver impairment. She has not been vaccinated against yellow fever or received any attenuated vaccines. She is not currently taking phenytoin or fosphenytoin. She has no history of severe depression, suicidal thoughts, uncontrolled epilepsy, or addiction. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to any of the medications or excipients used in the study. She is able to undergo an MRI without issue.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who presented to her primary care physician with complaints of fatigue and anxiety. She drinks alcohol regularly, particularly on weekends, and sometimes feels like she is unable to control her drinking. She smokes occasionally and has no other significant medical history. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at reducing alcohol consumption. The patient is fluent in both Spanish and Catalan languages. The screening test revealed an AUDIT-C score of 6, which meets the inclusion criteria for the trial. She is interested in participating and is able to access the trial website.

A 49-year-old male stroke survivor visited the clinic for a follow-up appointment. He had a stroke 8 months ago and has been experiencing decreased sensorimotor function in his affected arm. He can use his arm to some extent in daily activities, but it's not fully functional. He has no other medical conditions and is not on any medications. He is married with two children and works as a high school teacher. He reports no history of psychiatric symptoms, fibromyalgia or arthritis. He is able to communicate and understand test instructions. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his upper extremity sensorimotor function.

A 45-year-old male who has had a documented myocardial infarction three months ago is eligible to participate in the Coronary Drug Project. He has a history of smoking and hypertension but is currently taking medications for both conditions. He has no known history of diabetes or other significant medical conditions. The patient is willing to commit to regular follow-up visits every 4 months for the duration of the study period. The patient has no known allergies to any of the medications being investigated in the trial.

60-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease presented to the cardiology clinic with complaints of fatigue, shortness of breath, and decreased exercise tolerance. He also reports feeling lightheaded and dizzy when standing up from a seated position. His physical exam revealed bilateral lower extremity edema, jugular venous distension, and crackles on lung examination. Echocardiogram revealed an ejection fraction of 40%, and a nuclear cardiolyte stress test confirmed moderate congestive heart failure (CHF) with a New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class of III. He has been on optimal heart failure therapy with ACE inhibitors and beta-blocker therapy for the past six months with a documented rationale for variation. He denies any history of COPD or reactive airway disease. There is no history of pulmonary veno-occlusive disease or non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. He is not currently taking any medications known to be a potent inhibitor of CYP3A4 or organic nitrate medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating sildenafil for the treatment of moderate CHF.

Pt is a 55yo male diagnosed with Barrett esophagus without dysplasia, indeterminate for dysplasia, or low-grade dysplasia. The patient has no history of esophageal carcinoma or other cancer(s) except for non-melanoma skin cancers. The patient is currently on proton pump inhibitor (PPI) for the past 6 months. The hemoglobin, leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, and platelets are within normal range. The patient has no contraindication to esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and is willing to provide tissue samples for research purposes. The patient has no diabetes mellitus, history of vitamin B12 deficiency or megaloblastic anemia, or history of lactic acidosis. The patient has no diseases associated with weight loss, no history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to metformin, and no uncontrolled intercurrent illness. The patient has no genetics disorders such as a family history of hereditary gastrointestinal polyp disorder (e.g., familial adenomatous polyposis [FAP], hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer [HNPCC], Peutz-Jegher disease) and no chronic alcohol use or a history of alcohol abuse. The patient has no kidney disease or renal insufficiency and is currently not on any medication(s) for weight loss. The patient has not received any other investigational agents =< 3 months prior to Pre-Registration.

The patient is a 3-week-old infant who has been diagnosed with excessive crying/infantile colic by NHS Health Visitors. The infant is healthy, full-term and has no co-morbidities. The infant's parents have been struggling with their crying baby, who cries inconsolably for prolonged periods of time and is difficult to soothe. The infant is well-fed and there are no signs of failure to thrive. The parents have not been participating in any other therapeutic clinical trials and do not currently receive manual therapy treatment. They are able to communicate effectively in English. The primary caregiver is the mother who is otherwise healthy and has no medical history of note. The infant is currently receiving usual NHS care and will be randomly assigned to either the usual NHS care group or the usual NHS care plus cranial osteopathic intervention group for the purpose of this study. The parents have consented to participate in this pilot investigation to explore the effectiveness of cranial osteopathy in addition to usual NHS care for infantile colic.

A 62-year-old male with fair skin has a history of actinic keratoses on his forehead, nose, and cheeks. He has been undergoing Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) for the last 2 years for treatment of his skin lesions. He takes a daily multivitamin but does not supplement with Vitamin D. He has never been diagnosed with skin cancer. He is willing to participate in a research study that will measure biomarkers in his blood that may predict the outcome of his PDT treatment. He is aware that he may withdraw his consent at any time.

This is a 50 year old male who suffered a fall from a height of 6 feet and sustained a wrist injury that resulted in posttraumatic radiocarpal osteoarthritis. He underwent radioscapholunate fusion as part of his treatment plan. He has a history of hypertension, controlled with medication, and no other significant medical history. He is able to read and write in English and has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He experiences occasional pain and decreased range of motion in his affected wrist and hopes to improve his wrist function with the fusion procedure. He has not undergone any other surgical intervention for his wrist injury.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been using heroin intravenously for the past 2 years. He lives in Nairobi, Kenya and has never been tested for HIV or hepatitis C. He has a history of sharing needles with other drug users and has never received any medical treatment for his addiction. He reports experiencing withdrawal symptoms when he tries to stop using heroin. He has struggled to maintain employment due to his drug use and his family relationships have been strained. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that provides testing and linkage to care for injecting drug users in Kenya. He hopes to receive counseling and treatment for his addiction and to learn more about his HIV and hepatitis C status. He is willing to attend NSP/MARP service sites and to live in Nairobi, Western region, or coastal Mombasa for the duration of the trial. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who underwent multiple spine surgeries for herniated discs in the lumbar region. Despite the surgeries, she continues to experience severe neuropathic back pain with associated leg pain. She has tried various conservative treatments, including physical therapy, medications, and injections, but they have not provided adequate relief. She reports a daily average pain score of 8 out of 10 on the visual analog scale (VAS) for both back and leg pain. She also experiences difficulty performing daily activities and has a high level of disability according to the Oswestry Disability Index. The patient does not have a history of psychosis or malignancy. She is willing to undergo a surgical implantation of a spinal cord stimulator and understands the potential risks and benefits of the procedure. She is covered by a French Health Insurance plan and has given written consent to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old man with a history of diabetes and hypertension visited the ophthalmology clinic complaining of blurry vision and floaters in his left eye. After a thorough examination, he was diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy and was scheduled for an intravitreous injection. He has not used any antibiotics in the past month.

A 68-year-old male retiree with a history of smoking and high blood pressure presents with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. He underwent a coronary angiography that revealed atherosclerosis of the coronary arteries. He is currently on medications for hypertension and high cholesterol. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the prevalence of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) in patients undergoing coronary angiography. He understands the study requirements and diagnostic procedures and is willing to sign an informed consent form prior to both procedures. He is available for ultrasonographic follow-up after the procedure. The patient has no known systemic infection or untreatable bleeding, and is not enrolled in any other study protocol.

A 45 yo man who was a first responder on September 11th, 2001. He has been smoking for the past 20 years and currently smokes 10 cigarettes a day. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and coughing for the past few months. He is also experiencing symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) such as nightmares, flashbacks, and avoidance behavior. He has tried to quit smoking before but has been unsuccessful. He is interested in smoking cessation treatment and wants to improve his overall health. He has not participated in any other smoking cessation program and does not have a history of alcohol dependence or serious mental illness. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male who leads an active lifestyle and has no history of any medical conditions. He has never participated in any studies involving ionizing radiation and has not donated blood in the past 6 months. He has no history of substance abuse and does not suffer from any kidney or pulmonary disease. He is not claustrophobic. He has been instructed to follow a standardized diet for a week prior to the study. The patient will undergo a baseline dynamic cardiac PET scan with 15O-water followed by 11C-palmitate and 18F-FDG tracers, together with baseline blood samples, muscle biopsy and subcutaneous fat biopsy to assess peripheral metabolic status. An intravenous infusion of sodium beta-hydroxybutyrate will then be initiated at a concentration and rate sufficient to achieve 1-2 mM ketonemia after 30 minutes (assessed by blood sample). A second dynamic PET scan identical to the first will then be performed under continuous ketone infusion at a constant rate. Finally, a second set of blood samples, muscle and subcutaneous fat biopsies will be taken after the scan before stopping the ketone infusion. The study aims to test whether infusion of 3-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) inhibits myocardial glucose and fatty acid uptake. The results of this research are expected to provide insights into how human heart metabolism responds to increased ketone bodies, and whether there are significant functional improvements.

52-year-old male who underwent renal transplantation 3 years ago and currently takes Prograf® and Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) for immunosuppression. The patient has been stable with the current regimen for the past 3 months, with no acute rejection episodes in the last year. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is > 50 ml/min x 1.73 m2. The patient has no history of chronic inflammatory bowel disease or psychiatric illness. The patient is not diabetic, and there is no history of leukopenia or thrombocytopenia. The patient is willing and able to comply with study requirements, including attending study visits and completing questionnaires. The patient is not planning to become pregnant, is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and will use effective contraception during the study. The patient has not received any investigational medicinal product during the last 30 days.

A 35-year-old man with a history of chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in first chronic phase was referred due to his condition being resistant to standard chemotherapy. He has been on imatinib therapy for the past 6 months, but there has been no improvement in his condition. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He exercises regularly and has no history of allergies. His blood counts are low, with a platelet count of 20,000/mm3, neutrophil count of 300/mm3 and a reticulocyte count of <1%. He is seeking alternative treatment options and is willing to participate in clinical trials.

A 45-year-old female with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hypothyroidism presented with abdominal discomfort, bloating, and occasional diarrhea. She was admitted to the hospital for evaluation and a stool culture was found positive for ESBLE. She has been on multiple courses of antibiotics in the past year for recurrent urinary tract infections. She is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, levothyroxine, and occasional ibuprofen for joint pains. She has no history of recent gastrointestinal infections or inflammatory bowel disease. She is willing to participate in the study and has agreed to consistent use of prebiotic or probiotic supplements during the study. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is not pregnant or lactating and has agreed to use contraception during the study period. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

31 year old male diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa with confirmed autosomal dominant inheritance pattern. He has a history of night blindness, loss of peripheral vision, and difficulty with color discrimination. The patient is interested in participating in the study of dietary N-3 fatty acids for patients with retinitis pigmentosa and Usher syndrome. He is willing to participate in one or more of the arms of the study. The patient has no history of seafood or fish oil supplement intake and is willing to follow a diet free of seafood and fish oil supplements during the study. He is in good general health with no other significant medical history. The patient is able to provide informed consent and comply with study requirements.

A 14-year-old boy has recently been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and has been included in the ALLTogether protocol. He is currently categorized as intermediate risk-low for the disease. He has been prescribed dexamethasone and PEG-asparaginase for his treatment. The patient has a family history of hyperlipidemia and has been experiencing elevated levels of total cholesterol and triglycerides, which have been attributed to the treatment. The patient is experiencing side effects, including nausea and abdominal discomfort, which may be related to these elevated levels. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or underlying medical conditions. The patient and his parents have been informed about the clinical trial and have expressed interest in participating to potentially reduce the risk of developing hyperlipidemia and adverse events related to the treatment.

A 3 yo F diagnosed with a primary cleft palate requiring surgical repair. The patient has no history of chronic pain or seizure disorders and is not currently taking any medications for pain management. The patient has no known contraindications to acetaminophen or morphine. The patient has no known allergies to local anesthetics or midazolam. The patient has an ASA physical status of I or II.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who had a lumpectomy for early-stage breast cancer in her right breast followed by radiation therapy. She had a sentinel lymph node biopsy and one lymph node was positive for cancer cells, she underwent axillary lymph node dissection as a result. She has been experiencing swelling, heaviness, and discomfort in her right arm for the past few months. The swelling is more pronounced after she engages in physical activity or spends a long time standing or sitting. Her arm feels tight and she has difficulty moving it. She has tried compression sleeves and massage therapy, but they did not provide long-term relief. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of chronic diseases. Her occupation involves a lot of computer work and she leads a sedentary lifestyle. She is married and has two teenage children. Her hobbies include gardening and reading.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who suffered a traumatic brain injury in a car accident 2 years ago. He experiences difficulty with attention, concentration, and memory, which has affected his ability to work and engage in daily activities. He has been receiving cognitive rehabilitation for the past 5 months, but has not seen significant improvement. His Mississippi Aphasia Screening Test score for the comprehension subtest is above 45. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his attentional skills using competitive versus non-competitive training strategies. He does not have severe cognitive impairment or any visual or auditive disorders that would limit his ability to comply with the treatment regimen. He is willing and able to give informed consent to participate in the study.

A 3-year-old girl who has no history of varicella, shingles, measles, mumps, and rubella is eligible for this clinical trial. She is in good health and has no immune impairment or deficiency. The child has not received any measles, mumps, rubella, and/or varicella vaccine either alone or in combination before. She has not been exposed to measles, mumps, rubella, varicella, or zoster in the past 4 weeks before vaccination. The child has not received any inactive vaccine in the past 14 days or any live vaccine within the past 30 days. She has not received any immune globulin or any blood product in the past 3 months. The child and her parents are willing to participate in this clinical trial to compare the safety and efficacy of ProQuad™ versus M-M-R II™ and VARIVAX™ in healthy children.

The patient is a 25-year-old female diagnosed with asthma for the past 5 years. She experiences occasional wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, which are usually triggered by exposure to dust, pollen, or pet dander. She has been using an inhaler twice daily and has had no hospitalizations or emergency department visits in the past year. She is not a smoker, does not have any other underlying lung disease, and has not used any oral steroids in the past 4 weeks. She is currently not using any hormonal contraception but is interested in starting oral contraceptives. She has regular menstrual cycles and has not noticed any significant changes in her asthma symptoms during different phases of her menstrual cycle. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. She is willing to participate in the study and provide information on her menstrual cycle, asthma symptoms, and medication use.

As this is a retrospective chart review, no patient description is necessary. However, it can be mentioned that the study includes children who were diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and had received prior treatments before being treated with either Romiplostim or Eltrombopag at Weill Medical College of Cornell University, New York, New York, or Children's Hospital Orange County, Orange, California, between 2009-2013.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with thyroid cancer and requires a thyroidectomy. He has no significant medical history and currently takes no medications. He has never smoked and has no history of respiratory infections or sore throat in the past two weeks. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has normal blood pressure and blood sugar levels. He is classified as ASA I. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of remifentanil in preventing cough during emergence from general anesthesia.

The patient is a 62-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic liver cancer. He has previously undergone chemotherapy, but the cancer has progressed. He has no history of CNS metastases or seizure disorder. His performance status is ECOG 1. His absolute neutrophil count is 1800/mm^3, platelet count is 110,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin is 11.2 g/dL. His bilirubin, AST, and creatinine levels are normal. He has no history of heart disease and is not pregnant or nursing. He is not on any antiretroviral therapy. He is not using any oral contraceptives. He has not undergone any immunotherapy or biologic therapy within the last 4 weeks. It has been more than 4 weeks since his last chemotherapy. He has not undergone any radiotherapy. He is not taking any CYP3A4 inducers. He is willing to use effective contraception during and for 3 months after study participation. His fasting cholesterol level is 280 mg/dL and fasting triglycerides level is 300 mg/dL. He has no uncontrolled infections. He understands the purpose of the study and is willing to participate.

A 56-year-old man with a history of stable angina who has been on chronic statin treatment for the past 6 months is scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and has undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the past. While his symptoms have been well-controlled with medication, his cardiologist has recommended CABG for optimal management of his coronary artery disease. The patient is willing to participate in the StaRT-CABG trial to investigate whether an additional treatment with high-dose statins before CABG surgery can reduce the incidence of major post-surgery complications including death, myocardial infarction, and stroke. The patient has signed the informed consent form and meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial.

A 55-year-old male presents with a history of chronic back pain and bilateral leg pain. The pain is primarily in the buttocks and is relieved by sitting or stooping forward. The patient has tried conservative treatment, including analgesics, NSAIDs, and physical therapy, without significant improvement. The patient underwent an MRI of the lumbar spine, which showed moderate central canal spinal stenosis at the L3-L4 level. The stenosis is consistent with the patient's symptoms of back/buttock/leg pain in a neurogenic claudicatory fashion, relieved by stooping or sitting down. The patient has chosen to receive bilateral transforaminal epidural steroid injections (BTESI) as the next treatment option. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent and can tolerate the procedure. There are no significant psychologic diagnoses or dementia. The patient is not receiving workman's compensation benefits.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic pain and swelling in her legs for the past year. She has been diagnosed with CVI grade II and has been treated with compression therapy for the past 6 months, but has not seen any significant improvement in her symptoms. She is not currently taking any venous drugs or laxatives that could affect her fluid or electrolyte balance. She has no history of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, neuropathies, hyper- or hypocalcaemia, or malignancies. She has not participated in any clinical trials within the last 90 days and is not currently pregnant or nursing. She is willing and able to give written informed consent prior to participation in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy female who has never been vaccinated against Ebola virus. She has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to any vaccine components. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has not received any vaccine in the 2 weeks prior to the trial vaccination, and does not plan to receive any vaccine in the 3 weeks following the trial vaccination. She is willing to comply with the applicable contraceptive requirements of the protocol. She has not participated in a clinical trial or used an investigational product within 30 days prior to receiving the first dose within this study. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She is willing to minimize blood and body fluid exposure of others for 7 days after vaccination. She is willing to refrain from blood donation during the course of the study. She is cooperative and available for the entire study. She has no history of immunosuppressive or immunodeficient condition, cytotoxic therapy in the previous 5 years, and/or diabetes. She is not working with livestock. She has no chronic or active neurologic disorder, including migraines, seizures, and epilepsy, excluding a single febrile seizure as a child. She has no history of Guillain-Barré Syndrome. She has no active malignancy or history of metastatic or hematologic malignancy. She does not have suspected or known alcohol and/or illicit drug abuse within the past 5 years. She has no moderate or severe illness and/or fever >38°C within 1 week prior to vaccination. She has not received immunoglobulins and/or any blood products within the 120 days preceding study entry or plans to receive them during the study period. She does not have skin lesions close to the injection site or active oral lesions. She does not have thrombocytopenia contraindicating intramuscular vaccination based on the investigator's judgment. She has no significant infection or known inflammation. She has no history of relevant cardiovascular disorders or evidence of hyper- or hypotension. She is willing to comply with the study directives.

A 38 year old male presents with chronic hepatitis C infection that has progressed to cirrhosis. The patient has been planning to commence antiviral therapy soon. The patient has no known allergies to ICG and is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the study and will be assessed using non-intrusive dynamic liver testing to evaluate the liver function pre and post-treatment. The patient may benefit from the study by obtaining a more personalized treatment plan based on the results of the dynamic liver tests.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who presents to the clinic with a persistent cough for the past 7 days. She reports having difficulty breathing and chest congestion. She denies any fever, chills, or body aches. She has no history of chronic pulmonary disease, and she takes no medications except for occasional acetaminophen for headaches. She is a non-smoker, and she has no known allergies. Her physical exam reveals mild wheezing, and her vital signs are normal. Her lab work shows no significant abnormalities. She provides a written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with a singleton gestation. She is presenting for Sequential Screen testing at HUP and is competent to provide verbal informed consent. There is no history of multiple gestations or major fetal anomalies. She is currently in her first trimester and will be undergoing measurement of placental volume and diameter at 11-14 weeks and 18-24 weeks of gestation. The purpose of the measurements is to determine if placental growth can predict adverse pregnancy outcomes. The study will also investigate the relationship between placental growth and serum levels of various biomarkers to improve detection of adverse outcomes. The patient is willing to provide blood samples for the study and is excited to contribute to improving the understanding of placental growth and its role in adverse pregnancy outcomes.

Patient 1: A 35-year-old female with a history of breast cancer who underwent mastectomy and radiation therapy. She developed a broad scar and contracture band in the chest area, making it difficult for her to perform daily activities. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions.  Patient 2: A 50-year-old male with a history of esophageal cancer who underwent esophagectomy with gastric pull-up reconstruction. He subsequently developed an esophagocutaneous fistula that has been difficult to manage. He has no other medical conditions.  Patient 3: A 20-year-old female with ambiguous genitalia who underwent previous surgical interventions with unsatisfactory results. She has no other medical conditions and is seeking reconstructive surgery for improved genital appearance and function.

27-year-old female diagnosed with anorexia nervosa 5 years ago with a BMI of 13.5 kg/m2. Despite multiple attempts at treatment, including cognitive behavioral therapy and medication management, she has not responded to any conventional treatments over the past year. She currently denies any gastrointestinal symptoms, but admits to excessive exercise and purging behaviors. She has refused artificial nutrition and has no history of drug use (except for occasional tobacco use). Her Edinburgh score is 16. She is interested in participating in this study to explore alternative treatment options for her enduring anorexia nervosa.

The patient is a 57-year-old man with a history of liver cirrhosis and recurrent ascites. He was admitted to the hospital for increasing abdominal distension and difficulty breathing. The patient has a history of alcohol abuse and has been abstinent for the past 6 months. On examination, he had tense ascites with mild abdominal tenderness, and there were no signs of hepatic encephalopathy. A diagnostic paracentesis was performed, and the ascitic fluid analysis revealed a polymorphonuclear cell count of 450/mm3. Blood cultures were positive for extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli. He was diagnosed with nosocomial spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and started on ceftazidime. However, after 48 hours of treatment, his fever persisted, and repeat ascitic fluid analysis showed an increase in polymorphonuclear cell count to 550/mm3. The patient was then enrolled in the clinical trial to receive either daptomycin + meropenem or continue on ceftazidime for the treatment of his nosocomial SBP. The patient has no history of significant heart or respiratory failure and is not allergic to ceftazidime, meropenem or daptomycin.

A 56 year old woman visits the clinic for a gastroenteroscopy scheduled for next week. She is generally healthy, with no history of drug or alcohol abuse or mental illness. She has normal hearing and vision and is able to read and write. Her vital signs are stable, and she has no signs of severe central nervous system diseases or liver or kidney dysfunction. She is willing to participate in the study and can follow up regularly. She has not undergone any intravenous or general anesthesia for other causes in the last 3 months. Her medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. She is curious to learn more about the possible effects of intravenous anesthesia on her cognitive function after the procedure.

The patient is a 45 year old Hispanic male who has been experiencing symptoms of heartburn, acid reflux, and regurgitation for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and Barrett's esophagus after undergoing an endoscopy and biopsy at a gastroenterology clinic. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally with meals. He works as a construction worker and sometimes experiences difficulty in swallowing food due to his condition. He is currently taking proton pump inhibitors for his GERD symptoms but they are not fully effective. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help find a better treatment option for his condition.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been missing her maxillary central incisors for the past 2 years due to trauma. She is a non-smoker and maintains good oral hygiene. Upon clinical examination, the patient was found to have deficient alveolar thickness with a ridge width of less than 4 mm. She has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the past 6 months and has no significant medical history. The patient is interested in undergoing implant placement in the anterior maxillary aesthetic zone and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of mineralized plasmatic matrix (MPM) with or without collagen membrane on peri-implant bone regeneration. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 17-year-old female with a BMI of 39 kg/m2 and a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 2 years. She has been under medical supervision for her diabetes and has been on insulin therapy for the past 6 months. She also has hypertension and mild obstructive sleep apnea for the past 2 years. She has undergone medically supervised lifestyle changes that have not been successful in achieving a healthy weight. She has achieved approximately 95% of adult stature and is in Tanner stage IV. She is committed to undergoing psychological evaluation and has validated the Center for Epidemiology Study Depression (CES-D) scale and Spence Children's Anxiety Scale (SCAS) surveys. She is willing to adhere to nutritional guidelines after intragastric balloon (IGB) placement provided by the weight management clinic dietitian. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and has decisional capacity and desire to provide informed assent in conjunction with parent/guardian consent. She is not pregnant and agreed to avoid pregnancy for 1 year after IGB placement through approved contraception. She has no endoscopic contraindications and has been tested negative for Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) via a fecal antigen study prior to initial endoscopic assessment. She has no history of gastrointestinal surgery, bariatric surgery, or surgery of any kind on the esophagus, stomach, or any type of hiatal hernia surgery. She has no inflammatory disease of the gastrointestinal tract, potential upper gastrointestinal bleeding conditions, gastric mass, or any structural abnormality in the esophagus or pharynx. She has no severe coagulopathy, poorly controlled diabetes, serious health conditions unrelated to her weight that would increase the risk of endoscopy, chronic abdominal pain, motility disorders of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, hepatic insufficiency or cirrhosis, serious or uncontrolled psychiatric illness or disorder that could compromise their understanding of, or compliance with, follow-up visits and removal of the device, or known to have, or suspected to have, an allergic reaction to materials contained in the system. She is not taking medications on specified hourly intervals that may be affected by changes to gastric emptying and is not taking corticosteroids, immunosuppressants, or narcotics. She has no history of an intragastric device or participated in any clinical study which could affect weight loss within the past 6 months.

A 45-year-old female patient with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that has relapsed after two lines of previous therapy came to the clinic seeking new treatment options. The patient is ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant, allogeneic stem cell transplant, or CAR T cell therapy. The patient has confirmed CD19 tumor expression and has not received subsequent therapy for the treatment of lymphoma post CAR T-cell therapy. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has at least one measurable lesion in accordance with RECIST Version 1.1. The patient must have a recent formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor biopsy specimen obtained following the conclusion of the most recent anticancer treatment and must be willing to release the specimen for exploratory tumor molecular profiling. The patient must also be willing to provide pre- and post-infusion blood samples for exploratory analyses. The patient is able to understand and provide a signed informed consent that fulfills the relevant Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) guidelines. The patient weighs more than 50 kg and does not have serious uncontrolled concomitant disease that would contraindicate the use of the investigational drug used in this study or that would put the subject at high risk for treatment-related complications. The patient has not participated in an investigational drug study or received any investigational treatment within 14 days prior to dosing for this study. The patient has not assessed by the Investigator to be unable or unwilling to comply with the requirements of the protocol. The patient is not pregnant or nursing.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the ICU with a high fever, severe abdominal pain, and low blood pressure. He was diagnosed with septic shock secondary to community-acquired peritonitis. His lactate levels were high (3.5 mmol/L) and he required norepinephrine at a dose of 0.4 µg/kg/min to maintain his blood pressure. He had a history of hypertension and was taking medications for it. His creatinine levels were elevated (2.5 mg/dL) indicating acute kidney injury. The patient is conscious and alert, but he is weak and tired. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent for the clinical trial. He has no known allergies to citrate or heparin.

62-year-old male of Chinese descent was diagnosed with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma after experiencing abdominal pain and jaundice. He underwent a partial hepatectomy and was started on sorafenib. However, after 14 days of treatment, he experienced severe side effects and had to discontinue the treatment. His Child-Pugh score is 7, indicating mild cirrhosis, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 1. His hematologic, hepatic and renal functions are adequate. He has no history of active cardiac disease and thrombotic or embolic events in the past 6 months. He is able to swallow tablets without difficulty and has not been previously treated with any investigational agents for hepatocellular carcinoma other than sorafenib. He is willing to use an acceptable method to avoid pregnancy.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with end-stage osteoarthritis in his right knee. He has been experiencing severe pain and stiffness in his knee for the past 2 years, which has severely impacted his daily activities and quality of life. He has tried various non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy and medication, but they have not been effective in relieving his pain. The orthopedic surgeon recommended a total knee arthroplasty (TKA), which the patient agreed to undergo. The patient has a history of mild hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He lives with his wife and two adult children and is currently employed full-time as an accountant. The patient is fluent in English and has a cell phone with text messaging capability. He is motivated to participate in the study and hopes that it will help him achieve better outcomes after the surgery.

32-year-old female who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis and underwent an ileal pouch anal anastomosis (IPAA) surgery 2 years ago. She has been experiencing recurrent symptoms of pouchitis despite multiple courses of antibiotics. Her Pouch Disease Activity Index (PDAI) score is greater than 7 indicating moderate to severe disease activity. She has been on oral 5-aminosalicylate (5 ASA) and immune suppressant therapy for her pouchitis, but no significant improvement has been observed. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of alicaforsen enema, a medication being investigated for the treatment of antibiotic-refractory pouchitis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and willing to use contraception during the trial. She does not have any other significant medical history or conditions that would exclude her from participating in the trial.

A 56-year-old male smoker presents with persistent cough and shortness of breath. He has a history of smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 30 years. He has lost 10 pounds in the past 2 months without any significant change in his diet or exercise routine. He has no history of lung cancer in his family. A chest X-ray shows a mass in his left lung. A biopsy confirms the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer. His Karnofsky performance status is 80%, and he has no comorbidities. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy. His bone marrow, liver, and renal function are all within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 68 year old woman who has been feeling sad and hopeless for the past few months. She has difficulty sleeping, has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy, and has been experiencing decreased appetite. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She lives alone and has been feeling isolated. She sought help from her primary care physician who recommended starting treatment for depression. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the impact of shared decision-making (SDM) nursing intervention in comparison to physician recommended Usual Care. She will be randomized to receive either SDM or UC and will be assessed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 24 to determine treatment adherence and depressive status. She meets the inclusion criteria of being 65 years and older, presenting to Lincoln Hospital, Bronx NY, screening positive for depression, and receiving primary care physician recommendation for depression treatment. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is scheduled for a hysterectomy surgery in three weeks. She has a history of chronic pain due to endometriosis and has been taking oxycodone and alprazolam daily for the past six months. She has a history of depression but is currently stable on her antidepressant medication. She is interested in participating in a study that would help her safely taper off her medication use after her surgery. She owns a smartphone and is willing to use it for video visits with the behavioral health tele-health program. She is fluent in English and is willing to sign an informed consent form. She has no history of suicidal ideations, is not on methadone or buprenorphine for treatment of opioid use disorder, and is not on palliative care.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired male who is generally in good health. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is being managed with medication. He is not currently taking any other medications. His blood glucose, hemoglobin A1c, urea, creatinine, vitamin-B6, vitamin- B12 and folate levels are within normal ranges for his age. He has a BMI of 27. He enjoys a balanced diet and exercises regularly with brisk walking for at least 30 minutes per day. He is a non-smoker with occasional alcohol consumption. He has no known allergies or intolerances to any foods. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the study requirements, including blood draws and following the provided diet. He is available for the entire duration of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old Hispanic woman diagnosed with bipolar disorder. She has a BMI of 29.9, indicating that she is overweight. She has a sedentary lifestyle and is not currently engaged in any regular exercise routine. She lives in a supportive housing agency in New York City and is interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle program to improve her physical health. She has no history of anorexia nervosa, cardiovascular events, or exercise-induced asthma. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no cognitive impairment, as determined by the Mini-Cog Examination. She is fluent in English and Spanish and is willing and able to give informed consent to participate in the study. She has received medical clearance from her primary care provider to participate in light-to-moderate physical activity.

This is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with metastatic transitional cell carcinoma of the urothelium involving the bladder. He has been treated previously with platinum-containing chemotherapy, but has experienced progression or recurrence of his disease. He now presents with measurable disease by CT or MRI and is seeking additional treatment options. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1 and he is willing to provide tumor tissue for biomarker analysis. He has not received more than 2 prior lines of chemotherapy and does not have liver metastases. He does not have a history of active cancer that has spread to the central nervous system, autoimmune disease, or positive testing for hepatitis B virus surface antigen, hepatitis C virus ribonucleic acid, human Immunodeficiency virus or acquired Immunodeficiency syndrome. He is interested in participating in the study of nivolumab to potentially reduce the size of his tumor.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with Fabry disease after experiencing recurrent episodes of burning pain in his extremities, particularly in his hands and feet. He had a family history of Fabry disease with his mother and maternal uncle being diagnosed. The patient also had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His current medications include amlodipine and atorvastatin. He is a smoker and has a history of heavy alcohol use. He agreed to participate in the Evaluation of HEArt invoLvement in Patients With FABRY Disease study and provided informed consent. The study will monitor his cardiac symptoms and evaluate risk factors for arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, and terminal heart failure. The patient will be followed closely by the Fabry Center Wuerzburg (FAZiT) to ensure optimal management of his Fabry disease.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with lung cancer and is scheduled for an elective thoracotomy. He has no history of drug abuse or coagulation disorders. The patient has agreed to participate in this study and has provided informed consent. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics and has two chest drains. The patient is willing to undergo either thoracic epidural analgesia or combined intrathecal and thoracic paravertebral analgesia to manage his postoperative pain.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with advanced small bowel cancer. She had already undergone two rounds of systemic therapy and was not eligible for further standard treatment. She experiences abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, and has lost a significant amount of weight. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She has a family history of colorectal cancer. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her condition.

A 48-year-old female with a BMI of 31.5 presented with a sedentary lifestyle and a desire to increase her physical activity. She is a daily user of an Android smartphone and is willing to participate in the study protocols, including regularly carrying a mobile phone, using the HeartSteps application, answering phone-based questionnaires, and tracking her physical activity using the Fitbit Versa activity tracker. She is able to walk one mile without significant discomfort and is not currently enrolled in a formal exercise program. She has no history of psychiatric disorder, orthopedic problems, peripheral neuropathy, severe cognitive impairment, or pregnancy. She is fluent in English and is competent to give informed consent.

Pt is a 45yo M status post allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation with newly diagnosed post-transplant constrictive bronchiolitis (PTCB). He has a history of smoking and reports shortness of breath with exertion. He has been experiencing a decline in his forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) percent predicted by at least 15% and his Total Lung Capacity (TLC) is > 85% to rule out restrictive lung disease. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and has no known hypersensitivity to corticosteroids. The patient will undergo screening tests including pulmonary function test (PFT) and will be randomly assigned to receive either inhaled fluticasone propionate or continue with standard of care. The patient will receive fluticasone propionate twice a day by oral inhalation and will be given detailed instructions by the research nurse or clinic nurse at his first study visit. The patient will also complete a diary to record how often he uses his rescue inhaler and when he takes the study drug each week. The patient will be monitored through various tests and procedures at regular intervals throughout the study.

A 28-year-old female Han Chinese resident of Hunan province has volunteered for this study. She is currently working as a nurse in a local hospital. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She does not have any history of hematological or liver diseases, immune system diseases, allergies or surgeries in the past 3 months. She has regular menstrual cycles and is not pregnant. She has a blood type of O positive. She is physically active and enjoys jogging and yoga in her free time. She is interested in participating in this study to contribute to the development of normal reference range of TEG in Hunan province.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in his first remission with high risk features, including FAB M6 classification and complex karyotype. He has undergone one cycle of induction therapy to achieve remission. The patient has a genotypically HLA-identical sister who is willing to be a donor for bone marrow transplantation. He is in good general health with no significant history of medical illness or hospitalization. The patient is willing to undergo the bone marrow transplantation procedure and to be enrolled in the clinical trial to prevent GVHD after BMT. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 47-year-old female came to the clinic with a lump in her left breast that had gradually increased in size over the past 6 months. She also reported experiencing pain in the breast and noticed a change in the skin texture. She was diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer that has spread to nearby lymph nodes. Her HER2 status was negative. She has no significant medical history other than hypertension controlled with medication. She has not received any chemotherapy before. She has a performance status of 1 according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group criteria. The patient underwent a biopsy confirming the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma, and imaging studies were performed, which showed the extent of the disease. The patient meets all the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial, including adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. She is able to swallow medication and has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 78-year-old male who has been hospitalised at the Champmaillot Geriatric Centre for a week due to a recent fall that caused a hip fracture. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are currently well-controlled with medication. He has no known food allergies or dietary restrictions. He has a good appetite and typically finishes his meals, but occasionally leaves some food on his plate. He is able to feed himself independently and does not require assistance. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 24.5 kg/m² and weighs 76 kg. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. He has given his informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 22-year-old female university student who is concerned about her weight and body composition. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 26 kg/m2, which is considered overweight. She is currently not involved in any regular physical activity due to her busy academic schedule. She is a non-smoker and does not use any drugs or alcohol. She is not pregnant and has no physical limitations that would prevent her from participating in physical activity. She owns a smartphone that can connect to a Mi Band. She is interested in participating in the "Mi Band Step Challenge" to improve her body composition and overall health.

A 50-year-old male presents with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed clinically for the past 3 years. He is currently on insulin therapy with a total insulin dose of 0.8 (I)U/kg/day. His most recent HbA1c level was 8.5%. He has a body mass index of 28 kg/m2 and a body weight of 90 kg. He has no known hypersensitivity to IMP(s) or related products. His haematology, biochemistry, coagulation, and urinalysis values are within normal limits. His supine blood pressure is currently 135/85 mmHg, and his heart rate at rest is 70 beats per minute. He is not taking any other clinical trial medication and has not participated in this trial before. He is willing to use contraceptive methods if necessary.

A 50-year-old male who suffered a myocardial infarction a month ago and has completed the standard post-infarction management is eligible for this study. The patient has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled by medication. The patient is able to exercise and has no hemodynamically significant valvular disease, moderate to severe chronic lung disease, or atrial fibrillation. The patient has not experienced exercise-induced myocardial ischemia and has a hemoglobin level of over 12 g/dl. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is committed to following the structured program of exercise training.

A 32-year-old man from Reunion Island was diagnosed with leptospirosis infection by polymerase chain reaction in 2014. He had a history of occupational exposure to water contaminated with animal urine while working in a local farm. He received appropriate antibiotic treatment and has been symptom-free since then. He has a social security issue and is not under any medication or treatment that might affect his immune system. He is interested in participating in a study to evaluate his immune response to leptospirosis infection and determine if he still requires vaccination.

This is a 45-year-old male who recently underwent a colonoscopy after experiencing rectal bleeding and abdominal pain. The colonoscopy revealed a large tumor in the sigmoid colon, which was confirmed to be colorectal cancer. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. He has no family history of colorectal cancer. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male with a history of locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has recurred despite previous treatment with EGFR-TKI therapy. He is seeking further treatment options and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and is in general good health, with an ECOG performance status of 1. Laboratory tests show normal function of main organs, with a hemoglobin level of 115 g/L, absolute neutrophil count of 2.5x10^9/L, platelet count of 90x10^9/L, total bilirubin level of 1.2xULN, ALT and AST levels of 1.8xULN and 2.2xULN respectively, BUN level of 1.2xULN, and serum creatinine level of 1.0xULN. He has completed all prior anticancer therapies over 4 weeks ago and has recovered from all related toxicities to grade ≤ 1. He has no history of interstitial lung disease related to previous EGFR-TKI treatment. He has signed and dated informed consent and is willing to use methods of contraception or total abstinence from start of dosing until 6 months after discontinuing of study treatment. He has not received any concomitant immunosuppressive agents or high-dose corticosteroids, and his INR is ≤ 1.5. He has not received any drugs recognized as being inhibitors or inducers of the liver isoenzyme in the last 4 weeks prior to registration in the current study. He has not consumed pitaya, pomelo, grapefruit, orange, mango or other fruit that may affect drug metabolizing enzymes or juice within 3 days prior to the treatment, nor coffee, tea, cola, chocolate or other caffeine-containing beverages, alcoholic beverages and / or other alcoholic products within 2 days prior to the treatment. He has not received high dose irradiation treatment or other 14C-labeled drug within 1 year, and has no known history of alcoholism or drug abuse. He has not participated in any clinical trial within 4 weeks prior to screening.

A 45-year-old female patient who recently received dental implants at the Department of periodontology, Rambam Health campus, Haifa in Israel, has been asked to participate in a clinical trial. She is in good general health and willing to provide informed consent. The patient has no history of uncontrolled diabetes or systemic infectious diseases such as hepatitis or HIV. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is not taking any medication that affects soft tissue condition and has not undergone guided bone regeneration during implant placement. The patient will undergo surgical uncovering of the implants and will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The first group will receive standard treatment with a 4mm height healing abutment without the use of Chlorohexidine gel. The second group will receive Chlorohexidine 1% gel (Corsodyl®) applied on the abutment and internal hex of the implant, followed by connection of the 4mm healing abutment. The patient will be monitored for tissue healing following the procedure.

The patient is a healthy adult between the ages of 21 and 50 years old, with a body mass index (BMI) between 18.5 and 25.0 kg/m^2. They have no visual impairment and can correct their vision with eyeglasses or contact lenses. The patient has no history of drug or food allergies, alcohol or drug dependence, or abnormal drunken behavior. They have received prior explanation about the study, and are able to understand and provide voluntary written consent for participation. The patient is interested in helping further research on driving ability and is willing to participate in a driving simulator study to collect alcohol calibration data.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with mild hypercholesterolemia. She has a family history of heart disease and is concerned about her risk of developing cardiovascular disease. She has not been taking any lipid-lowering medications for at least 3 months and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of aged garlic powder on improving her blood lipid levels. The patient is generally healthy with no history of heart disease, cancer, renal disorder, or diabetes mellitus, and is not currently taking any lipid or antihypertensive medications. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all required visits and assessments.

A 52 years old female with a history of hypertension, well-controlled with medication, and no other significant medical history, presented to the plastic surgery clinic requesting bilateral blepharoplasty. She had no history of upper respiratory tract infections, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or smoking. She has never been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea or had any issues with drug or alcohol abuse. Her BMI is 26.2, and she has no known allergies to any medications. After a thorough discussion of the risks and benefits of the procedure, she agreed to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of nasopharyngeal airway versus laryngeal mask airway in general anesthesia for blepharoplasty.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B for the past 3 years. He has been on Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for the last 2 years. His HBsAg is positive and HBV DNA level is 50 IU/mL. He has no other hepatic diseases or history of ascites, jaundice, varicoses vein bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, or other signs of liver failure. His laboratory tests are normal, except for ALT which is slightly elevated. He does not have any history of malignant tumors or organ transplantation. He is not on any immunosuppressive drugs or high dose systemic corticosteroids. He does not have any serious illnesses such as heart failure, renal failure, and pancreatitis. His blood pressure is normal and he does not have any seizure disorders. He is not infected with hepatitis C, hepatitis D or human immunodeficiency virus. He does not have any hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction to the components of the clinical trial drug or HBV vaccine components. He has not consumed alcohol for the past 6 months and is not concerned about the deterioration of daily function due to mental illness. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and can understand and sign a written informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with Type II diabetes mellitus two years ago. He has been performing self-monitoring of blood glucose regularly as per his doctor's recommendation. He reports occasional difficulty in obtaining an adequate blood sample for testing due to poor circulation in his fingers. He is otherwise in good physical and mental health and is willing to sign the informed consent. He is able to read and follow study instructions. He is not pregnant, has no history of bleeding disorders, and has not donated blood or lost 400 mL or more of blood in the past 4 weeks. He is not currently participating in another study and has not had drug or alcohol abuse within the past 12 months. He has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medication within the past two days that may affect pain perception. He has not consumed alcohol within the past 48 hours.

Mary is a 58-year-old woman who recently suffered from a stroke. She experienced a sudden onset of confusion, difficulty speaking, and weakness on the right side of her body. She was admitted to the hospital and diagnosed with an acute ischemic stroke. She was treated with tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) and has been taking aspirin to prevent future clots from forming. Her physical examination and laboratory tests were otherwise normal. She has no history of autoimmune diseases, cancer, or thrombocytopenia. She does not have HIV or any other known immunodeficiencies. She had no recent major surgery, systemic infections, or severe respiratory infections. She does not have dementia or psychiatric problems that prevent her from providing informed consent or following an outpatient program reliably. She is not pregnant, and she has no history of severe rhinopathy or sinusitis. She is not taking any other intranasal drugs. She has not been exposed to an investigational drug within the 30 days prior to screening for this study. She is willing to undergo a brain MRI prior to the start of the study drug. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if E-selectin nasal instillation can prevent secondary stroke.

A 62-year-old man presents with a history of prostate cancer for the past 5 years. He has been on hormone therapy for the past 2 years and his PSA levels have been steadily increasing over the past 3 months. The patient's most recent PSA level is 12 ng/mL. He has no history of heart disease or myocardial infarction. His medical record shows no evidence of CNS involvement, HIV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C. The patient's Karnofsky Performance Status is 80. His laboratory values are within normal limits for granulocyte, platelet count, total bilirubin, AST and ALT, serum creatinine, calculated creatinine clearance, and urinalysis. The patient has not received prior chemotherapy or treatment with Vidaza. He is willing to use acceptable methods of birth control to avoid fathering a child for the duration of the study and for a period of 2 months thereafter. He has signed the Patient Informed Consent Form and the Patient Authorization Form. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial.

Patient is a 27-year-old pregnant woman from the United States who is in her 39th week of gestation. She has a singleton pregnancy with vertex presentation and is currently experiencing active labor with cervical dilation of 4cm. She has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 and desires labor epidural analgesia. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has not had any previous surgeries on her sacral or lumbar spine.
