She has no known allergies to local anesthetics. Her platelets, International Normalized Ratio, and partial prothrombin time are within normal limits. She does not have any coagulopathy, renal failure, or hepatic failure. She is willing and able to provide her own consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy and is concerned about the potential for weight gain during treatment. She has a BMI of 28 and has struggled with weight management in the past. She is interested in learning more about lifestyle changes that may help her maintain her weight during treatment and improve her quality of life. The patient has received approval from her treating physician to participate in this study and is willing to sign the informed consent document.

A 45-year-old female office worker presented with shoulder pain that has persisted for more than four weeks. She has difficulty moving her shoulder and experiences pain when doing so. She has not received any treatment for her shoulder within the last 6 months. She has no history of frozen shoulder, acromioclavicular joint disorders, or any other relevant medical conditions. She exercises regularly, but has stopped doing overhead activities due to her shoulder pain. She takes no medications, has no allergies, and has no history of surgery.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who suffered a severe brain injury due to a car accident. He was brought to the emergency department unconscious and has been in a coma for the past week. Despite aggressive medical interventions, his condition has not improved, and the medical team has decided to withdraw life-sustaining treatment. The patient's family has been informed and has agreed to the withdrawal of treatment. The patient is covered by social security and eligible for organ donation according to the hospital's coordination. The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score is less than 5, and the patient has lost bilateral corneal reflexes. The transplant coordinator has approached the family and explained the anticipated organ donation approach. The family has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is eligible for participation in the study and will be evaluated according to the standardize selection procedure to determine if he meets the criteria for organ donation.

A 21-year-old female patient visits the clinic with complaints of blurry vision, difficulty seeing at night, and sensitivity to light. She reports that her vision in both eyes has been gradually getting worse over the past few months. On examination, the patient is found to have keratoconus with central and inferior steepening in both eyes. The patient's best-corrected visual acuity (BSCVA) is worse than 20/20 in both eyes. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial comparing the safety and effectiveness of Epi-ON CXL versus Epi-OFF CXL. The patient is willing to follow all instructions and comply with the schedule for follow-up visits. The patient is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant in the near future. The patient provides written informed consent and agrees to use a medically acceptable form of birth control for at least one week before the treatment visit and for one month following treatment. The patient has no history of corneal transplant or previous CXL in either eye. The patient has no other ocular conditions that may predispose the eye for future complications or prevent the possibility of improved vision. The patient has a corneal pachymetry of >375 microns at the thinnest point in both eyes. The patient is not allergic to any of the test articles or its components.

A 58-year-old African American woman came to the Clinic with a history of fatigue, weight loss, and abdominal discomfort. She was diagnosed with Primary Myelofibrosis based on the 2008 revised International Standard Criteria. Her JAK2 mutation status was positive. Her spleen was enlarged, and her anemia was marked (Hgb < 10g/dL). Her leukocyte count was normal, but her platelet count was low (platelet count < 50,000/µL without the assistance of growth factors, thrombopoietic factors or platelet transfusions). She had no history of malignancy in the past 3 years. She had no impairment of gastrointestinal function or GI disease that may significantly alter the absorption of oral INC424. She had no cardiac disease that may jeopardize the safety of the patient or compliance with the protocol. She had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She had not received any therapy for PMF in the past. She met the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial and was interested in participating in the study.

Patient A is a 60-year-old Indian male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer five years ago. He has undergone several treatments, including radical prostatectomy, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy. His latest PSA level showed an increase from 20 ng/ml to 50 ng/ml, indicating disease progression. The patient has developed bone pain and difficulty in urination. The biopsy of the bone lesion confirmed the presence of metastatic adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The patient has received docetaxel-based chemotherapy but showed disease progression. The patient has an estimated life expectancy of more than six months, and he is being newly initiated on Xtandi treatment (enzalutamide) as per the locally approved prescribing information. The patient agrees not to participate in any other interventional drug trials during the course of this trial. The patient has no other conditions that would make him unsuitable for study participation.

The patient is a 28 year old female with a confirmed diagnosis of congenital generalized lipodystrophy. She has not been previously treated with metreleptin and is seeking treatment for her condition. She has no known history of drug or alcohol abuse within the last year and does not have any conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She has not participated in another clinical study with an investigational product in the last 6 months. She is willing to use an acceptable method of contraception as defined by the study protocol. She has negative pregnancy test results and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is able to provide informed consent and comply with the requirements of the study.

A 55-year-old male stroke survivor came to the clinic with complaints of difficulty in swallowing and speech impairment. He had a stroke in the middle cerebral artery (MCA) 6 months ago, which affected the right side of his body. He has no history of other medical conditions or allergies. He is married, has two children, and is currently unemployed. He has completed high school and has no history of smoking or drinking. He wears a hearing aid in his left ear due to moderate hearing loss. He has no history of head and neck surgery or radiation therapy. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his speech and swallowing function.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who has been experiencing numbness and tingling in his fingers for several months. He has been diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome and has been recommended for carpal tunnel release surgery. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no known drug allergies. He is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a healthy adult between the ages of 21 and 45 with a BMI between 18.5 and 25 kg/m2. They have not consumed any cannabinoids or other substances regularly and are not currently taking any medications that could potentially interfere with pain sensation. They do not have any history of neuropathy, chronic pain, neuromuscular diseases, or psychiatric diseases. They also do not have any known or suspected kidney or liver diseases, and are not pregnant or lactating. They are able to understand the study procedures and the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) for rating pain intensity, and are able to give informed consent.

A 68-year-old man was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent cough and chest pain. Further tests showed a tumor in the lung measuring 6 cm. He underwent a biopsy and was confirmed to have NSCLC. The tumor was deemed surgically inoperable due to its size and location. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of pacemaker implantation, current infection, or anti-neoplastic chemotherapy. The patient has provided written consent to participate in the study and is willing to undergo treatment with stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) with either volumetric modulated arc therapy or intensity-modulated radiation therapy. He will receive 7.5 Gy x 10 daily fractions of radiation therapy to the tumor periphery with the option of 12 Gy x 5 daily fractions if dose constraints for organs at risk can be easily met while optimal planning target volume coverage is achieved. The patient will be followed up to 2 years post radiation therapy to assess the response to treatment.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with ovarian cancer, stage III, 7 months ago. She underwent cytoreductive surgery followed by 6 cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy. After completing the treatment, she had a negative physical examination, CA-125 levels of 25 U/ml, and no definite evidence of disease by CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and a life expectancy of more than 6 months. She has no bleeding disorders, HIV, or other malignancies within the past 3 years. She is not pregnant or nursing and uses effective contraception. She has no serious concurrent illnesses requiring hospitalization and no mental impairment that would preclude giving informed consent or complying with study requirements. She is HLA-A2 positive and her tumor expresses NY-ESO-1 by reverse transcriptase and polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) analysis or immunohistochemistry. She is willing to participate in this phase I clinical trial to study the side effects of vaccine therapy for ovarian epithelial cancer.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C. He has been receiving conservative medication for this condition. His serum alanine aminotransferase levels, measured 4 weeks prior to the initiation of treatment, were over 61 IU/mL. He is not currently receiving treatment with antiviral agents, corticosteroids, immunosuppressive drugs, glycyrrhizic acid, cholestyramine, or any other drugs that could interfere with hepatic function. He does not have decompensated cirrhosis and is not infected with any other hepatic virus. He has no history of autoimmune disease, alcohol or drug-induced hepatic disorder, neoplasia, hepato-cholangiolar disease, fulminant hepatitis or peptic ulcer. He is not currently hospitalized for any complications of the heart, kidney, or pancreas. He is not pregnant and is not an alcoholic. His alcohol intake is less than 27 ml/day. He has not been involved in any other clinical trials within the past 4 weeks. He does not have a history of sensitivity to ursodeoxycholic acid or bile acid-products.

The patient is a 72-year-old man who has been diagnosed with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Despite trying different antiarrhythmic drugs, his symptoms have not improved. He underwent a catheter ablation procedure for AF but the procedure was unsuccessful. He has a dual chamber pacemaker implanted and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He understands the nature of the study and treatment procedure and provides written informed consent. He has no history of unstable angina or any disease that is likely to shorten his life expectancy to less than a year. He has not undergone any cardiac surgery within the last three months, nor is he awaiting a cardiac transplantation or any other cardiac surgery within the next year. He has not had a myocardial infarction in the last 60 days and is not contraindicated for oral anticoagulation. He does not have active systemic infection or sepsis and has no history of a documented thromboembolic event such as stroke or transient ischemic neurological attack (TIA) in the three months prior to enrollment. He has no clinical condition that might jeopardize his safety during participation in this trial or prevent him from adhering to the trial protocol. He does not have an esophageal ulcer.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medication to manage these conditions. She experiences shortness of breath and fatigue when walking up stairs or hills, but is otherwise able to complete daily tasks without issue. She is retired and lives with her husband. They have two adult children who live nearby. She is a former smoker but quit 10 years ago. She exercises regularly by walking and doing yoga. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve her ability to exercise and increase her overall quality of life.

The patient is a 65-year-old male from Guangxi province, China. He was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) involving portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) of Cheng's type I. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both well-controlled with medications. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. His liver function is Child-Pugh A with a score of 6. He has no extrahepatic metastasis and is expected to survive for more than 6 months. His residual liver volume is more than 35%. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has not undergone any previous radiation therapy or chemotherapy for his HCC.

This is a 32-year-old female who has a history of seasonal rhinoconjunctivitis due to ragweed pollen allergy. She experiences moderate to severe symptoms during the ragweed season, which typically lasts from late summer to early fall. She has a positive skin prick test for ragweed allergen and specific IgE for ragweed. She has not received any immunotherapy for ragweed allergy in the past. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of asthma or other significant medical conditions. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and is willing to use an acceptable form of birth control during the study. She is willing and able to attend required study visits and follow study instructions. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is not taking any medications that would interfere with the study.

A 10-year-old boy with a history of recurrent ear infections and dizziness has been referred to Boston Children's Hospital for vestibular rehabilitation due to balance impairment. He has complained of difficulty walking and maintaining balance, and his parents have mentioned that he has fallen several times in the past few weeks. The patient is an English speaker and has no known developmental delays. The patient and his parents have agreed to participate in the clinical trial and understand the use of the Sensory Kinetics Balance Rehabilitation System. They are committed to completing the full 3-month course of vestibular rehabilitation.

A 28-year-old HIV-positive individual who has been on their first antiretroviral treatment regimen based on any two NRTIs plus lopinavir/ritonavir for at least 6 months. The patient's viral load is <50 copies/ml and CD4 cell count is >100 cells/mm3 at the time of baseline evaluation. The patient has not been treated for an active opportunistic infection within the last 30 days and does not exhibit any evidence of acute illness. The patient has confirmed their willingness to participate in the study and has signed the IRB/IEC approved informed consent form. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use a barrier method of birth control for the duration of the study if female. The patient does not have current uncontrolled substance abuse or psychiatric illness that could preclude compliance with the protocol.

58-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol abuse, presents with a biopsy-confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsil. The patient has no significant comorbidities and is classified as having a performance status of 1. The patient has adequate renal and hepatic function. No history of peripheral neuropathy or allergic reactions to chemotherapeutic agents. The patient has no history of HIV.

The patient is a 56 year-old African American male residing in or near the North Lawndale neighborhood. He has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension and requires at least one medication per day for each condition. His HgA1c level is above 7%, indicating poor diabetes control. He has a BMI of 30, indicating that he is overweight. He has no comorbid conditions limiting his life span, such as cancer or AIDS, and has not had any major endorgan complications of diabetes, such as kidney dialysis or amputation. He is not currently receiving treatment for a major psychiatric disorder or struggling with alcoholism. He is able to give informed consent and is over the age of 18. He has not been able to manage his diabetes and hypertension effectively and is looking for ways to improve his health and reduce his weight.

72-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus type 2, and chronic heart failure presented to the cardiology clinic for routine follow-up. His medications include metoprolol, lisinopril, furosemide, and metformin. He reports a recent hospitalization for decompensated heart failure, during which his ejection fraction was found to be 35%. His physical exam is significant for tachycardia, jugular venous distention, bilateral lower extremity edema, and bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation. His laboratory studies are notable for an elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) level of 800 pg/mL. He reports experiencing shortness of breath with minimal exertion and difficulty sleeping due to orthopnea. He also reports feeling anxious and worried about his health status. He has a spouse who is able to assist him with the use of technology at home. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve his heart failure management and reduce his need for hospitalizations.

A 55-year-old female diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) found during routine blood work. She has a history of hypertension, hypothyroidism, and osteoporosis. Her MDS is classified as refractory anemia with excess blasts (RAEB-1) and she has received 2 units of red blood cell transfusions within the past 3 months. Her platelet count is 45,000/mm3 and neutrophil count is 900/mm3 due to a recent respiratory infection requiring antibiotics. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for her MDS. She is not pregnant or nursing and uses effective contraception. She is currently taking levothyroxine and alendronate. She has a performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living.

A 25 year old healthy male, with a body mass index (BMI) of 22.5 kg/m², is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential future treatment for schizophrenia. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has not taken any prescription medication, herbal remedies or dietary supplements for the past 28 days. He has never attempted suicide or talked about it. He does not smoke more than 5 cigarettes daily. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has no objection to having his GP informed of his participation in the study. He is able to communicate with study personnel and understands the nature of the trial. He has no clinically significant disease and does not have any condition or operation that might affect the way the body absorbs medicines.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been on a low-fat diet and exercise regime for the past 6 months and has not taken any lipid-lowering medication during this period. He recently underwent a carotid ultrasound examination that showed the presence of a carotid plaque with an abnormal CIMT of 1.1mm. His lipid profile was LDL of 2.8mmol/L and TC of 4.8mmol/L. He has been referred to participate in the clinical trial investigating the antiatherogenic effect of GSPE. The patient has no history of severe cardiomyopathy, acute coronary syndrome, hepatic dysfunction, end-stage renal failure (serum creatinine <117mmol/L), prior carotid endarterectomy, or any other significant medical history. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the treatment regimen and follow-up visits.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman who is scheduled for a cesarean section procedure will be eligible for this clinical trial. She must be able to speak in Thai language, co-operate with the research, and have received general anesthesia during the procedure. However, she must not have a twin pregnancy, placenta previa, placental abruption, chorioamnionitis, bowel or bladder injury during the operation or postpartum hemorrhage. Additionally, she must not have a history of gastrointestinal surgery or neurological or neuromuscular diseases. The woman must also not have any hepatic diseases and cannot have received prior acupressure treatment. The study aims to compare the efficacy of acupressure at ST-36 Zusanli to no acupressure in helping the patient recover bowel function post cesarean section.

A 35-year-old woman was recently hospitalized for severe depression. She has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and worthlessness for the past 4 months. These feelings have been affecting her daily life, making it difficult for her to work and engage in social activities. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies to anesthetics. Her physical examination is unremarkable. The patient has been recommended for electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) as a treatment option for her depression. She has been informed about the study comparing the use of Thiopental and Propofol as anesthetic agents during ECT and has given her consent to participate. The patient will be randomized to receive either Thiopental or Propofol as anesthetic during the ECT treatment. She will be rated with Hamilton depression scale and BDI before treatment, after six treatments, and when treatment is concluded. The patient will also be rated with MMSE to evaluate her cognitive function after the treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing episodes of fainting and dizziness. He has been referred to the center for tilt testing to evaluate the possibility of vasovagal syncope. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He is willing and able to cooperate with the study procedures and is able to provide written informed consent. He has not had a prior tilt test and is not enrolled in any other device or drug study.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is focused on evaluating the effectiveness of the dissemination of the Action Schools! BC model in elementary schools, rather than testing a treatment or intervention on individual patients. The study involves the participation of schools, teachers, and students who meet the inclusion criteria and provide consent.

25 yo F with a history of wearing monthly silicone hydrogel contact lenses for 2 years, experiencing symptoms of dryness and discomfort with lens wear. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate two different contact lens solutions. She is willing to wear the study lenses on a daily basis for at least 4 hours per day and attend all study visits. She has not used hydrogen peroxide-based solutions before and does not sleep in her lenses. She has no history of ocular infections, inflammation, abnormalities, or active diseases that would prevent her from wearing contact lenses. She has no systemic diseases that may affect the eye or be exacerbated by contact lens wear or solutions, nor is she taking any medications that would contraindicate contact lens wear. She has no history of herpetic keratitis, ocular surgery, or irregular cornea. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent.

A 40-year-old mother of a 6-year-old boy with a previous diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) presents with concerns about her child's social and communication skills. The child is currently receiving special education services and speech therapy at school. The mother reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the challenges of caring for a child with ASD. She also reports experiencing feelings of sadness and helplessness at times. The physical examination of the child is unremarkable. Laboratory evaluations are normal. The mother is fluent in English and is able to consistently participate in intervention sessions. She is not taking any psychiatric medications and has no history of severe psychiatric, genetic, or medical disorders. Her baseline resilience score is below 80 on the CD-RISC. She is married and has two other children who do not have any developmental issues. She is highly motivated to participate in the resilience training program and is willing to commit to attending all sessions.

A 54-year-old man is currently intubated and ventilated in the ICU of a hospital due to COVID-19 pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, but is otherwise healthy. He has been receiving hydroxychloroquine as part of his treatment regimen, administered through a nasogastric tube. His laboratory values have been within normal limits during his hospitalization. He has not participated in any other clinical trials and is affiliated with a social security scheme.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of Stage II breast cancer. She underwent lumpectomy surgery and the margins of the resected specimen were histologically free of tumor. The tumor size is 2.5 cm and is unifocal. The patient has not undergone axillary staging yet but is scheduled to undergo sentinel node biopsy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to reduce skin toxicity during radiation therapy. The patient is eligible for the trial as she is over 50 years old, has a life expectancy of at least two years, and has stage II breast cancer. She has no history of non-ipsilateral breast malignancies and does not have any coexisting medical conditions that would preclude her from meeting the study requirements.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has previously undergone a lumpectomy, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She has no history of heart disease or organ transplant. Her ECOG status is 1. She has adequate liver, renal, and bone marrow function. She is willing and able to swallow pills. She has not been previously exposed to doxorubicin or other anthracyclines exceeding the maximum lifetime cumulative dose. She is expected to live for at least 12 weeks.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who is currently in her first trimester of pregnancy. She has a history of congenital heart disease and is planning to deliver her baby at Saint Luke's Hospital of Kansas City. She is otherwise healthy and has not been diagnosed with hypertension, diabetes, multiple gestations, preeclampsia or autoimmune disease. She has been enrolled in the study to evaluate the use of bio-reactance cardiac output monitoring using the NICOM during the second and third stages of labor and 24 hours postpartum. She has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old Caucasian woman with a family history of colon cancer. Her mother was diagnosed with colon cancer at the age of 52. The patient has never had any gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal discomfort, altered bowel habits or hematochezia. She has no personal history of iron deficiency anemia, iron deficiency without anemia, or positive fecal occult blood test within the past year. She has never undergone colonoscopy or barium enema within the past 10 years, nor has she undergone flexible sigmoidoscopy within the past 5 years. She has no personal history of adenoma, colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, HNPCC, or familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). She has not experienced any unintentional weight loss greater than 10 pounds within the past six months. The patient speaks and reads English fluently. She is referred for colorectal cancer screening due to her family history of colon cancer.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with ADHD combined presentation. He has been experiencing difficulties falling asleep and staying asleep for the past few months. His parents have reported that he takes a long time to fall asleep and often wakes up during the night. They also report that this has been affecting his behavior during the day, with increased irritability, impulsivity and difficulty focusing. The patient's medical history is significant for asthma and seasonal allergies, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of sleep disorders or other psychiatric conditions. The patient is currently not on any medication for ADHD or sleep. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in the study and comply with its requirements.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with tracheal stenosis secondary to prolonged intubation for respiratory failure. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes lisinopril and atorvastatin, respectively. She quit smoking 2 years ago after smoking 1 pack per day for 20 years. On physical examination, she has mild stridor and decreased air entry bilaterally. Pulmonary function tests show a moderate obstructive pattern. She has been scheduled for elective upper tracheal resection and reconstruction surgery. She has no known allergies to medications and is not on any opioid medication. She has been advised about the study protocol and has agreed to participate. Her American Society of Anesthesiologists physical class status is II.

A 38-year-old Caucasian male with a diagnosis of cervical dystonia presents with involuntary muscle contractions in the neck, causing abnormal head movements and postures. He reports experiencing symptoms for the past 2 years, which have gradually worsened. He has tried various treatments, including physical therapy, medications, and botulinum toxin injections. He currently takes trihexyphenidyl for symptomatic relief, but his symptoms have not improved. He complains of neck pain, stiffness, and difficulty performing daily activities. He has no history of neurological disorders or other medical conditions that may affect cervical dystonia. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. His family history is negative for any neurologic conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form. He has not received botulinum toxin injections in the past three months.

The patient is a 72 year old female who has recently experienced two falls in the past year. She has no history of chronic illnesses or neurological conditions but has been experiencing some gait instability and feels concerned about her balance. She lives independently and is able to walk without assistance for at least 10 minutes. She has normal vision and has not undergone any brain surgeries in the past 6 months. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve her balance and prevent future falls.

The patient is a newborn infant born at 38 weeks gestation with a diagnosis of hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). The infant is experiencing moderate to severe HIE symptoms, which include poor muscle tone, weak reflexes, and decreased or absent breathing. The infant has been identified as a candidate for therapeutic hypothermia, which is the single most promising intervention for HIE. The goal of this clinical trial, California Transport Cooling Trial (CTCT), is to test the efficacy of the cooling device in achieving the target temperatures in patients with moderate to severe HIE during transport when compared with current practices. The patient will be eligible for the clinical trial if they are a term or near-term infant with gestational age ≥35 weeks and in whom the decision has been made to perform cooling during transport. The patient will be excluded from the trial if they have a congenital or lethal chromosomal anomaly or if the decision has been made to not provide full intensive care or if the parents refuse to consent.

45 yo female with recently diagnosed breast cancer after a routine mammogram. Biopsy confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma with no evidence of metastasis on imaging studies. The tumor measures approximately 1.5 cm in diameter and is located in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast. The patient has no significant medical history and has a WHO performance score of 0. She has consented to breast conserving surgery and is interested in participating in the Fluorescence Guided Surgery trial. The patient has intact reproductive organs and is willing to use effective contraception during the trial and for 3 months thereafter. She has no history of breast prosthesis or infusion reactions to Bevacizumab or other monoclonal antibody therapies. She has not received any concurrent anticancer therapy within the last 6 weeks and has no significant renal or hepatic impairment. Her blood pressure is well controlled on current medications. She has no history of significant cardiac disease or arrhythmias and her ECG shows no evidence of QT prolongation. Her electrolyte levels are within normal limits.

The patient is a 25 year old male who is generally healthy and does not smoke. He has a BMI within the range of 18.0 to 28.0 kg/m2. He has no history of substance or drug abuse within the past 12 months and has no clinically significant abnormal laboratory values. He has no history of cardiac, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, metabolic, neurologic, or psychiatric disorder that may interfere with successful completion of the trial. He is willing to abstain from alcohol or caffeine containing foods or beverages or grapefruit containing foods or beverages from 48 hours prior to each intake of study medication until the end of confinement at the clinical center. He does not drink more than 5 cups or glasses of caffeinated beverages per day. He is willing to participate in the study and understand the study procedures, the risks involved and ability to be trained to use the devices correctly.

A 72-year-old patient comes to the clinic complaining of shortness of breath, fatigue, and difficulty exercising. The patient has a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and has been taking medication for the past 6 weeks. Despite taking the medication, the patient's symptoms have not improved. The patient is also experiencing difficulty with daily activities and has become increasingly dependent on others for help. The patient has been diagnosed with a skeletal muscle myopathy related to HF, which is causing significant impairment in physical function. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of oral nitrite pills to improve physical function in older patients with heart failure. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, including age ≥70 years, NYHA class II or III for the previous three months despite a minimum of 6 weeks of treatment, and optimal therapy according to AHA/ACC and HFSA guidelines. The patient does not have any of the exclusion criteria, including allergy to lidocaine or dementia. The patient is willing to modify anti-thrombin and anti-platelet therapy prior to muscle biopsies individually in coordination with the participant's primary cardiologist. The patient is excited about the potential benefits of the trial and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis. He has had several episodes of acute pancreatitis in the past and has been advised to undergo an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) procedure to evaluate the status of his pancreatic duct. He has a history of hypertension and is taking antihypertensive medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is employed as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no known allergies and is not on any other medications. He has never undergone an ERCP procedure before and is slightly anxious about the procedure. He has good oral hygiene and no significant medical history. His BMI is 25 and his blood pressure is well-controlled at 130/80 mmHg. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve the sedation techniques for future patients undergoing ERCP procedures.

A premature infant was born at 26 weeks gestational age and weighs 900 g at birth. The infant is currently 4 weeks old and has been diagnosed with stage 2 ROP without plus disease. The parents have provided written informed consent for their infant's participation in the clinical trial for prevention of threshold retinopathy of prematurity. The infant has no known congenital malformations or chromosomal anomalies. The infant has not been diagnosed with any of the exclusion criteria, including heart diseases requiring open-label propranolol treatment, atrio-ventricular block grade 2 or 3, and bronchial asthma. The infant has not been treated with medication that may interact with propranolol, such as clonidine, digoxin, or verapamil. The infant has not experienced persistent hypoglycemia, hyperkalemia, or neutropenia. The infant's liver and kidney functions are within normal limits. The attending physician has not detected any eye malformations or large hemangiomas. The infant is eligible to participate in the clinical trial for oral propranolol for prevention of threshold retinopathy of prematurity.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She has received three prior lines of therapy and has progressed on or since the last treatment. She presents with abdominal pain, bloating, and fatigue. She has a surgically unresectable tumor and has measurable disease per RECIST 1.1. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has provided a PD-L1 evaluable archival tumor tissue sample or newly obtained core or excisional biopsy of a tumor lesion not previously irradiated. She has not received prior therapy with lenvatinib, an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti PD-L2 agent or with an agent directed to another stimulatory or co-inhibitory T-cell receptor. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is not a woman of childbearing potential (WOCBP), OR she is a WOCBP that agrees to use contraception during the treatment period (or 14 days prior to the initiation of study treatment for oral contraception) and for at least 120 days post pembrolizumab, or 30 days post lenvatinib, whichever occurs last. She has adequate organ function and her Child-Pugh Score is Class A: well-compensated disease. She has not received prior therapy with at least 1 (platinum-containing regimen or gemcitabine-containing regimen) but no more than 2 prior systemic therapies for unresectable or metastatic pancreatic cancer. She is willing to use approved contraception during the treatment period for at least 7 days after the last dose of lenvatinib or refrain from heterosexual intercourse during this period. She is willing to provide written informed consent.

This is a 37 year old female who has been diagnosed with chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and completed the preceding study CLOU064A2201. She has provided written informed consent and is willing and able to complete a daily symptom eDiary and adhere to the study visit schedules. She has a UAS7 score of ≥16 at the end of the treatment period or follow-up period of CLOU064A2201 and is eligible to roll-over into CLOU064A2201E1. She does not have any clearly defined predominant or sole trigger of her chronic urticaria and does not have any skin disease associated with chronic itching that might influence the study evaluations and results. She does not have any significant bleeding risk or coagulation disorders and does not have any ongoing, chronic or recurrent infectious disease.

A 25-year-old woman came to the orthodontic clinic for a consultation regarding her malocclusion. She is a non-smoker and has no underlying health conditions. Her oral hygiene is good, and she has no history of periodontal disease or dental caries. She is fluent in Spanish and has no cognitive disorders. Her facial structure is normal with no craniofacial anomalies. She is interested in orthodontic treatment to improve her smile and overall oral health. The orthodontist determined that her malocclusion is moderate in complexity based on the Dental Aesthetics Index DAI. She is eligible for the study and will be randomly assigned to either the mini tube system or conventional ligating brackets. She will be asked to complete an online questionnaire at specific time points during the first 6 months of treatment to evaluate the impact of the treatment on her oral health-related quality of life.

A 68-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer and underwent breast surgery without adjuvant chemotherapy. She is scheduled to undergo standard fractionated radiation therapy to the breast. She is an active woman, but has noticed increased fatigue since her surgery. She speaks English and is willing to participate in moderate-intensity physical activity. She is able to walk comfortably and has no significant medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the walking intervention. She is interested in participating in the study and willing to meet all study requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old healthy woman who is interested in maintaining her overall health and quality of life. She is not currently taking any prescription medications and has no history of chronic illnesses, cardiac, pulmonary, liver, or kidney abnormalities. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 and has been consistently physically active for the past year, meeting Canada's Physical Activity Guidelines. She currently consumes a diet that meets the Canadian recommended dietary allowance (RDA) for protein of 0.8 g/kg/day, but is curious about the potential benefits of a higher protein diet. She has no allergies or dietary restrictions, and is willing to consume eggs as part of the study. She is able to safely complete the exercise program without assistive devices and has no injuries that would prevent her from participating in the study.

A 45-year-old woman presents with lower back pain and discomfort for the past 4 years. She reports progressive pain that radiates to her thighs and legs, which is more prominent after prolonged standing or walking. She denies any bowel or bladder dysfunction or numbness. She has a history of smoking but has quit 2 years ago. Her medical record shows chronic lower back pain with no history of spine surgery or prior spinal injury. X-ray and MRI imaging show non-cervical spinal stenosis and degenerative disc disease between L4-L5. She is willing and able to comply with all the requirements of the protocol, including follow-up requirements, and is willing to sign a study-specific informed consent. She is skeletally mature and 52 years old at the time of enrollment. She has no history of an osteoporotic fracture, endocrine or metabolic disorders, and is not taking medications that may interfere with bony/soft tissue healing. She has no known allergy to titanium or cobalt chrome, rheumatoid arthritis, autoimmune disease, or systemic disorders such as HIV, active hepatitis B or C. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study. She has a BMI of 31 and has no physical or mental conditions that would interfere with patient self-assessment of function, pain, or quality of life.

A 30-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of infertility. She has been trying to conceive for two years with no success. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and painful periods. Upon further examination, it was discovered that she has a Mullerian anomaly. She has no other underlying disease and takes no medication. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. She has no allergies to any food or drugs. She has been recommended for minimally invasive surgery to correct the anomaly and improve her fertility. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to gain a better understanding of her condition and to help others with similar issues.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who has recently given birth to a healthy full-term baby. She speaks fluent English and has been discharged from the hospital within the last 6 weeks. She is interested in finding a way to manage her weight after giving birth and is open to participating in a study that provides a holistic approach to weight management. She is willing to receive motivational appeals through text messages, use environmental aides such as a baby carrier and pedometer to measure exercise at home. She is also interested in receiving peer support and task-oriented professional support from nutrition and lactation experts. She is not carrying multiple births and has not given birth to a preterm infant.

The patient is a 8-year-old male who has been diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency, with peak GH levels less than 10 ng/ml in two provocative tests. He has been experiencing delayed growth and has fallen behind his peers in terms of height. He has no other known pediatric or endocrine diseases. His family history is unremarkable, with no known history of obesity or short stature. The patient is otherwise healthy and active, with a normal appetite and no significant weight changes.

A 62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents to the hospital with palpitations and shortness of breath. An ECG shows prolongation of QT interval, and the patient is admitted for initiation of antiarrhythmic therapy with sotalol. He has a family history of sudden cardiac death and coronary artery disease. He is willing to undergo genetic testing and provide blood samples for genotyping. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who underwent an autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplant for multiple myeloma 4 months ago. He presents with symptoms of a cold, including nasal congestion, cough, and sore throat. He reports that his symptoms started 2 days ago and have been worsening. The patient has had an upper respiratory tract swab taken, which has confirmed the presence of HRV infection. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of an investigational drug called vapendavir for the treatment of HRV infection in hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol, maintain adequate oral intake of medication, and use a double barrier method of birth control if necessary. The patient has no significant medical history, is not currently taking high dose systemic steroids, and is not experiencing a lower respiratory tract infection, making him eligible for the study.

A 35-year-old man was recently diagnosed with a low-grade glioma, specifically an oligodendroglioma. The tumor is located in the supratentorial area of the brain and has been confirmed through histological testing. The patient has no other low-grade histologies and no evidence of spread to other areas of the brain or spinal cord. The patient has not received any prior treatment for the tumor, including chemotherapy or radiation therapy. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 90-100% and normal hematopoietic, hepatic, renal, and pulmonary function. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception if needed. The patient has no other malignancy within the past 5 years, except for a nonmelanoma skin cancer. The patient is eligible to participate in the trial and will be randomized to either arm I or arm II/III based on their age, tumor subtype, and Karnofsky performance status.

The patient is a 35-year-old man diagnosed with HIV three years ago. He is currently being followed by a physician at one of the participating centers of the Regional Coordination of the Fight against HIV Infection (COREVIH) Pays de la Loire. He has been compliant with his antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is undetectable. He reports experiencing fatigue and pain on a daily basis, which affects his ability to carry out his daily activities. He has previously participated in sports activities such as jogging and swimming, but has reduced his level of physical activity due to his symptoms. The patient is willing to answer the self-questionnaire and is not under guardianship.

A 30-year-old male with a history of Glycogen Storage Disease type IIIa (GSDIIIa) presents with exercise-induced muscle pain and cramps. He has difficulties with prolonged exercise and requires frequent rest periods to recover. The patient is genetically and biochemically verified to have GSDIIIa. He has no clinically significant cardiac or pulmonary disease, and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is mentally competent and understands the purpose of the trial. He has no conditions of the joints or skeletal muscles that would exclude him from the trial. The patient is able to complete at least 10 minutes of cycle-ergometry exercise at 70% of VO2peak without moderate to severe muscle weakness. He does not have diabetes or blood-clotting or bleeding disorders, and has not donated blood in the last month. The patient is not taking any medications that may interfere with the results or increase the risk of bleeding.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been struggling with obesity for several years with a body mass index (BMI) of 38.5 kg/m2. She has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past but has not been successful in achieving and maintaining weight loss. She reports currently having access to a computer and the internet, and owns a compatible smart phone device that is compatible with the BodyMedia® FIT Bluetooth® System that will be examined in this study. She has no physical limitations to engaging in physical activity, but has not participated in structured aerobic exercise for ≥ 60 minutes per week over the prior ≥ 3 months. She reports not being treated for any current medical conditions that could affect body weight such as cancer, diabetes mellitus, hyperthyroidism, inadequately controlled hypothyroidism, chronic renal insufficiency, chronic liver disease, gastrointestinal disorders including ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, or malabsorption syndromes, etc. She also reports not having current congestive heart failure, angina, uncontrolled arrhythmia, symptoms indicative of increase risk of an acute cardiovascular event, coronary artery bypass grafting or angioplasty, prior myocardial infarction, and conditions requiring anticoagulation therapy (i.e. deep vein thrombosis). Her resting systolic blood pressure is 130 mmHg and resting diastolic blood pressure is 85 mmHg. She is not taking any medications to control blood pressure. She is not being treated for any psychological issues or taking psychotropic medications within the previous 12 months. She is not taking prescription or over-the-counter medications that affect body weight and metabolism. She has not lost > 5% of current body weight in the past 3 months and has not maintained any weight loss at the time of recruitment for this study. She is not currently participating in an exercise or weight control study, had not participated in an exercise or weight control study within the previous 6 months, or a current participant in a commercial weight reduction program. She has not undergone bariatric surgery (e.g., gastric bypass, lap-band) for weight loss and is not currently being treated for an eating disorder. She is not currently pregnant, pregnant in the last 6 months, breast feeding in the last 3 months, lactating, or planning on becoming pregnant in the next 3 months. She has no plans of relocating outside of the greater Pittsburgh area within the next 6 months.

Maria is a 54 year old woman who works in an office and leads a relatively sedentary lifestyle. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She also had an echocardiogram that showed mild left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) with normal ejection fraction. She has never had a heart attack or stroke. Maria sometimes experiences feelings of sadness and loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has never been diagnosed with major depression, but her primary care physician has prescribed her with an antidepressant medication. Maria is interested in participating in a clinical trial to learn more about her cardiac health and mood. She is willing and able to perform mild exercise and undergo blood draws and body measurements as part of the study. She fully understands the study and has signed the informed consent form. She lives within a reasonable distance of UCSD and VASDHS and is able to attend all scheduled appointments during the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who underwent renal transplantation three months ago. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, both of which are well-controlled with medication. His current serum creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL. He has not experienced any episodes of acute rejection so far, but a recent 2-week protocol biopsy showed borderline changes. He works as an accountant and is married with two children. He exercises regularly and does not smoke or use any drugs. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 30 days. He agrees to participate in this study and sign the consent form.

A 45 year old woman has been experiencing widespread pain and tenderness in her muscles and soft tissues for over a year. The pain has been affecting her daily life, making it difficult to perform basic tasks and reducing her overall quality of life. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia by her physician and has been prescribed several medications, including muscle relaxants and painkillers, but has not seen significant improvement. She is interested in alternative therapies and has heard about acupuncture as a potential treatment for fibromyalgia. The patient is a resident of Washington DC and is willing to travel up to 3 times per week to the acupuncture site. She is not currently taking any new medications or undergoing any other treatment for fibromyalgia symptoms. She is capable of giving informed consent and has no knowledge of acupuncture that could prevent blinding. The patient has no coagulation abnormalities and is not experiencing any other autoimmune or inflammatory diseases that cause pain. She is not currently taking narcotic analgesics and has no history of substance abuse. She is not participating in any other therapeutic trials, is not pregnant or nursing, and is not receiving disability insurance payments or involved in any ongoing litigation related to fibromyalgia. She is not contraindicated for the use of acetaminophen or ibuprofen and has no impairments or situations that would prevent her from completing the study protocol.

The patient is a 64 year old woman who has been experiencing persistent upper abdominal pain for the past 3 months. She has also noticed a significant amount of weight loss and lack of appetite. After various diagnostic tests, including CT scans and biopsies, she was diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She has no history of cancer or any significant medical conditions. Her ECOG PS is 1, and she is able to take oral medication. She has not received any prior treatment for pancreatic cancer, nor has she undergone any curative surgeries. Her major organ functions are normal, and she has no clinically significant abnormal ECG findings. She is willing to participate in the study and has voluntarily signed the written informed consent form.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypercholesterolemia for the past 10 years. He was diagnosed during a routine check-up with a total cholesterol level of 270 mg/dL and LDL-C level of 190 mg/dL. He has been taking atorvastatin 40mg daily for the past 5 years and has not reported any adverse effects. He also reports a family history of hypercholesterolemia and cardiovascular disease. His current blood lipid levels are LDL-C 80 mg/dL, HDL-C 45 mg/dL, total cholesterol 150 mg/dL, and triglycerides 120 mg/dL. He leads a sedentary lifestyle and has a BMI of 29. He has not made any significant dietary changes in the past year. He has regular check-ups with his primary care physician every 6 months.

A 25-year-old male diagnosed with Freeman-Sheldon Syndrome presents with difficulty in performing daily activities due to limb and facial deformities. He frequently experiences depression and anxiety related to his condition and has noticed a decreased quality of life. The patient's family members, who have also been affected by the condition, are interested in participating in the study to help improve the quality of life for themselves and others with similar conditions. They have a close relationship with the patient and have been actively involved in his care. All parties are willing to provide medical records and participate in surveys to confirm the diagnosis and eligibility for the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 24 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has a BMI of 27, and her pregnancy has been uneventful so far. She has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions prior to her pregnancy and is not on any medications. She reports feeling tired during the day and has difficulty sleeping at night due to frequent urination, back pain, and discomfort from her growing belly. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the impact of sleep quality during pregnancy on pregnancy outcomes. She is willing to fill out questionnaires about her sleep quality and undergo polysomnography and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring if required. She understands that the study will involve a longitudinal follow-up and will help in understanding the prevalence and impact of sleep disorders during pregnancy.

54 year old male with a recent positive RT-PCR test for COVID-19 and a history of hypertension and obesity. The patient was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, fever, and a dry cough. Upon admission, laboratory results showed increased D-dimer and fibrinogen levels, indicating possible COVID-19-associated coagulopathy. The patient will be enrolled in the clinical trial to study the detailed coagulation screen and second line coagulation parameters to better understand the coagulation abnormalities associated with COVID-19. The patient will be monitored closely for any changes in coagulation parameters and will receive standard of care treatment for COVID-19.

The patient is a 35-year-old female veteran who served in Iraq and Afghanistan. She has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression, including trouble sleeping, difficulty concentrating, and low mood for the last six months. She has been to see her primary care provider at the VA hospital, who has recommended she participate in a clinical trial for Collaborative Care for Women Veterans. The patient is interested in participating in the trial as she believes it could help her manage her symptoms and improve her overall quality of life. She is currently taking medication for her anxiety and depression but has not noticed much improvement in her symptoms. The patient has no history of cognitive impairment and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 43-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with locally recurrent breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy two years ago for early-stage breast cancer. She has no history of heart or gastrointestinal disease. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score is 1, and she has measurable disease on imaging. The biopsy confirms ErbB-2 positive locally recurrent breast cancer. She has not received any systemic anti-cancer therapy for locally recurrent or metastatic disease. She is currently working as a school teacher and has two children. She is currently not in a relationship and has no plans for future pregnancies. She is looking for a treatment option that can shrink her cancer and extend her life while maintaining her quality of life.

45-year-old female patient with a history of coronary artery disease and recent coronary revascularization presents with high cholesterol levels and an unfavorable blood fatty acid profile. She has a family history of heart disease and has been advised to make dietary changes to reduce her risk of future cardiovascular events. The patient does not have diabetes mellitus and has no known food intolerances. Her BMI is within the range of 19-33. She is not currently taking any drugs or food supplements with omega-3 fatty acids or natural or synthetic antioxidants. The patient has not previously adhered to a full Mediterranean diet but is willing to make dietary changes to improve her health.

A 42-year-old man presents with a history of heavy drinking for the past 5 years. He reports drinking an average of 30 standard drinks per week and has been unsuccessful in cutting down his alcohol consumption despite several attempts. He reports experiencing negative consequences related to his drinking, including problems at work and in his personal relationships. He has no known history of drug abuse or dependence and is currently not seeking to quit drinking altogether. The patient is fluent in English and agrees not to seek additional substance abuse treatment during the treatment period. He is willing to reduce his drinking to non-hazardous levels and shows no evidence of significant cognitive impairment. The patient has no history of severe alcoholism, seizures or severe withdrawal symptoms, and has not had an inpatient treatment episode for drinking. He is not legally mandated to receive substance abuse treatment and is socially stable enough to complete the study requirements.

A 26-year-old female came to the clinic with symptoms of runny and stuffy nose, postnasal drip, and itchy eyes for the past 2 fall seasons. She has a history of fall pollen allergy and received positive skin testing to ragweed, grass mix, and tree mix allergens. She has been using over-the-counter antihistamines and nasal decongestants for symptom relief. She is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She doesn't smoke or use illicit drugs. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not pregnant. She is willing to stop using her current medications for the duration of the study. She has never participated in an investigational study before. She is fluent in English and able to understand the study procedures and requirements.

45-year-old mother of two children aged 9 and 12 presents to the clinic with symptoms of influenza-like illness (ILI) including fever, cough, and body aches. She was diagnosed with influenza and started on appropriate treatment. Family members living with her include her husband, who is 50 years old and suffers from hypertension, and her two children. The family has no history of vaccination against influenza. The study team proposes to enroll the entire family in a randomized, controlled, unblinded, clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of non-pharmaceutical methods in preventing the spread of influenza within the family. The mother and her family will be randomly allocated to either the intervention group or the control group. Those in the intervention group will receive comprehensive guidance about sanitation and hygiene, as well as surgical masks to wear whenever in close contact (3 feet / 1 meter) with the index case, and will be asked to isolate the index case as much as possible. Those in the control group will receive only standard guidance about sanitation and hygiene relevant for reducing the transmission of influenza. The primary endpoint of the study will be secondary infection of influenza of at least one of the family members in order to assess the efficacy of the interventions. The family will be asked to comply with the interventions for the entire duration of the mother's illness, which is expected to last about 1 week.

45-year-old female with a 10-year history of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) presents with disabling tremors in the upper limbs, causing significant difficulty with daily activities such as writing, eating, and dressing. The tremors have been unresponsive to previous medical treatments including carbamazepine, clonazepam, and primidone. The patient is otherwise stable on her current MS medication regimen. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of botulinum toxin injection therapy for MS tremors. The patient is able to provide informed consent and meets all eligibility criteria including absence of botulinum toxin treatment within the past 4 months and no known contraindications to Botox injection.

The patient is a 64-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He has a family history of prostate cancer, with his father and two uncles having been diagnosed. He has undergone a biopsy, which confirmed the presence of cancerous cells in his prostate. His PSA level is 12 ng/mL. He is scheduled to undergo a gadolinium-enhanced MRI as part of his routine care, and has agreed to participate in this study. He has no electrical or ferromagnetic implants, and is not claustrophobic.

55-year-old man who recently suffered a first-ever ischemic hemispheric stroke. He presented to the hospital within 48 hours of symptom onset, with weakness in his left arm and leg. He has no significant past medical history and is currently on no medications. He has no history of dementia or previous stroke. His NIHSS score is 4, with motor deficits affecting both his upper and lower limbs. He has health insurance and has provided written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old Caucasian male who presented with symptoms of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), including thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA), and clinical evidence of organ compromise. The diagnosis of TTP was confirmed by severely reduced ADAMTS13 levels and positive antibody screen. The patient has provided consent to be included in the United Kingdom TTP Registry and for the collection, storage, and analysis of admission and remission information, as well as EDTA samples once in remission. The patient has no history of cancer or transplant-associated MAHA. Follow-up laboratory and clinical data will be collected at least yearly to identify any changes.

31-year-old male with a history of sickle cell disease (SCD) genotype HbSS or HbSB0 who has experienced vaso-occlusive crises (VOCs) requiring hospital, emergency room, or clinic visits less than 10 times within the past 12 months. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use highly effective methods of contraception or practicing abstinence from study start to 30 days after the last dose of study drug. The patient has not been hospitalized for a sickle cell crisis or other vaso-occlusive event within 30 days prior to dosing. The patient does not have active hepatitis A, B, or C or known to be human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive. The patient does not have severe renal dysfunction or on chronic dialysis. The patient does not have a history of malignancy within the past 2 years prior to treatment Day 1 requiring chemotherapy and/or radiation (with the exception of local therapy for non-melanoma skin malignancy). The patient does not have a history of unstable or deteriorating cardiac or pulmonary disease within 6 months prior to consent. The patient has not participated in another clinical trial of an investigational agent or medical device within 30 days or 5 half-lives of date of informed consent, whichever is longer, or is currently participating in another trial of an investigational agent or medical device. The patient has adequate venous access as determined by the Investigator/site staff. The patient does not have ongoing or recent (within 2 years) substance abuse. The patient is able to undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) assessments (Cohort B only), and does not have a known allergy to voxelotor.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman diagnosed with relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 2 years ago. She has not received any treatment for MS yet. Her past medical history includes asthma, which is well controlled with inhaled medications, and a previous episode of Bell's palsy, which resolved completely. She has no allergies to medications. The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Vital signs are within normal limits. Neurological examination reveals mild weakness in the left leg, with an EDSS score of 2.0. She has no cognitive impairment or mood disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of fingolimod compared to currently approved disease modifying therapy for MS. She has no plans for pregnancy and is willing to use contraception throughout the study. She understands the study requirements and consents to participate.

A 28-year-old female with a history of grinding her teeth at night complains of jawline enlargement and asymmetry on her face. She has been conscious of her appearance and has tried different treatments such as laser and thread therapy, but she did not see any improvements. She does not have any facial palsy or myasthenia. She has never received any botulinum toxin treatment before. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no plans of getting pregnant during the study period. She has no known hypersensitivity to botulinum toxin. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not participating in any other investigational study at present or 30 days prior to the screening date. She is excited to participate in the study to improve her facial appearance and gain more confidence in her daily life.

Maria is a 33-year-old woman who works as a software developer. She has been smoking for 10 years and currently smokes 8 cigarettes per day. She has tried to quit smoking several times in the past but has been unsuccessful. She has no significant medical history and takes no medication. Her physical exam and vital signs are within normal limits. She has no visible skin disorders or abnormal skin pigmentation. She is interested in participating in the study to help her quit smoking and to contribute to medical research.

50 year-old woman with a history of Overactive Bladder (OAB) symptoms, including urinary frequency, urgency, and occasional incontinence episodes. She reports consuming an average of 3 cups of coffee per day, in addition to tea and soda. She has tried several medications for OAB symptoms in the past but has not found significant relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of caffeine reduction on her symptoms. She does not have a history of stress-predominant bladder symptoms, urinary tract infections, hematuria, pregnancy within the past six months, or radiation to the pelvic floor.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis two years ago. She experiences joint pain and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and knees, which has significantly impacted her daily life. She has tried several disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs) in the past, but none of them have provided significant relief. She is currently on methotrexate and prednisone, but is still experiencing significant joint pain and inflammation. She is willing to try a new treatment and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that uses contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) to assess the degree of synovitis in patients with inflammatory arthritis and to evaluate the response to DMARD therapy. She is able to sign the study-specific informed consent and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements. She does not have any known cardiac shunt or pulmonary hypertension, and does not have any known hypersensitivity to perflutren or gadolinium contrast agents or renal insufficiency.

The patient is a 65-year-old African-American man who was recently diagnosed with non-metastatic prostate cancer and has been receiving Androgen Deprivation Therapy (ADT) for 6 months. He reports experiencing fatigue, decreased libido, and weight gain since starting treatment. His BMI is 30, and he has a sedentary lifestyle with less than 60 minutes of moderate physical activity per week. He has access to a smartphone and is willing to participate in an 8-week exercise intervention study to counteract the adverse side effects of ADT. He has no severe cardiac disease or recent myocardial infarction, and he is not being treated for any other cancer. He is willing and able to follow the study procedures and instructions of the researcher.

A 32-year-old woman named Sarah came to the Clinic with concerns about her bone health. She has a family history of osteoporosis and wants to take preventative measures. Sarah is a non-smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle due to her desk job. She has a BMI of 23 and consumes an average of 800mg of calcium per day. She has never had a bone densitometry measurement before and has no history of thyroid disease, renal failure, malignancy, or rheumatoid arthritis. Sarah has not undergone a hysterectomy, is not currently on hormone replacement therapy, and has no plans to become pregnant within the next two years. She is interested in being a part of a study that will give her personalized feedback on her bone mineral density and teach her about osteoporosis prevention.

A 27-year-old female patient with cystic fibrosis confirmed by sweat test was referred to the clinic. She had a history of chronic cough with sputum production and recurrent chest infections. Her symptoms had worsened over the past few weeks with increased cough, sputum purulence, and fever. Her spirometry test showed FEV1 of 35%. She was a chronic carrier of Pseudomonas aeruginosa with at least three successive positive ECBCs over a period of 18 months. She had received at least one IV course of antibiotics in the 18 months prior to inclusion. She did not have any severe exacerbation, and her medical history did not reveal any other significant comorbidities. She was not colonized by Burkholderia cepacia or an atypical mycobacterium. She did not have any cirrhosis, myasthenia gravis, or hearing aid use. She did not have any recent history of severe hemoptysis. She was not participating in any other clinical study on a drug.

A 28 year old male came to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial related to respiratory imaging. He is a non-smoker, with no history of respiratory diseases or surgeries. He is currently a healthy individual with a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and a height of 180 cm. He has never had any intra-oral piercings, dental brackets, or any implant that could interfere with the MRI procedure. He has no claustrophobia and is able to understand and comply with the requirements of the study. He has not taken any investigational new drug within the last 4 weeks. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with stage IV colon cancer. She has been undergoing chemotherapy and radiation treatments, but still experiences severe pain episodes that interrupt her daily routine. She is currently taking 60mg of oral morphine per day to manage her pain, but it is not always effective. She has been experiencing 1-4 breakthrough cancer pain episodes per day, which are usually controlled by rescue medication. She has tried other pain management options, but they have not been successful. She is willing to participate in a long-term safety study of Nasalfent, as the nasal delivery system would be more comfortable for her than taking medication by mouth. She is able to evaluate and record her pain relief, assess medication performance at set times after dosing, record adverse events, and record each use of the study drug or rescue medication in a diary. She is able to be up and about for more than 50% of the day. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and agrees to practice a reliable form of contraception during the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old female diagnosed with epilepsy at the age of 18. She has been on a stable dose of topiramate for the past 5 years and has experienced a reduction in the frequency and severity of seizures. She is currently taking 100 mg of topiramate twice a day. She is a full-time student and works part-time as a cashier. She is sexually active and uses an effective form of birth control. She has no history of suicidal thoughts or ideation. She has no other significant medical conditions that may affect the safety of the study. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve the effectiveness of her current treatment.

Samantha is a 48 year old female who was recently diagnosed with early stages of type 2 diabetes. She has a family history of diabetes, and has been experiencing increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue. Her fasting serum glucose level was found to be 8.9 mmol/L during her last visit to the doctor. She manages her diabetes with diet and exercise, and has not yet started any medication for it. She is interested in natural remedies to help control her blood sugar levels, and has heard about the potential benefits of pomegranate juice. She does not have any other medical conditions, and does not smoke or take any medications or supplements that would exclude her from participating in the study. She is excited to see if pomegranate juice can have a positive impact on her blood sugar levels and overall health.

A 28-year-old woman who is 31 weeks pregnant comes to the clinic with concerns about the growth of her fetus. Her obstetrician has identified a decrease in fetal growth rate during her latest ultrasound scan. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is not currently taking any vasodilator agents and has no history of cardiovascular morbidity. Her blood pressure is 122/78 mm Hg. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of sildenafil citrate in the treatment of fetal growth restriction.
