A 52-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of distal symmetric polyneuropathy, secondary to diabetes, diagnosed in accordance with the American Academy of Neurology criteria. The patient does not have a history of diabetic foot ulcers or lower extremity amputation. The patient is able to read, understand, and provide written informed consent before enrolling in the study at screening. The patient does not have any clinically significant illness which, in the opinion of the investigator, would compromise the patient's suitability to participate in the study for reasons of safety or would confound the efficacy assessments. The patient has a partner of child-bearing potential but is willing to use adequate contraception.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was diagnosed with invasive transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder that has spread to his lymph nodes and distant organs. He has previously undergone platinum-containing systemic chemotherapy for advanced or metastatic disease, but the tumor has progressed. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and an estimated minimal life expectancy of 3 months at screening. He has at least one measurable tumor lesion according to RECIST 1.1 criteria. The patient has adequate organ system function at screening and is using adequate contraception. He has not received more than one prior chemotherapy, biologic therapy, or hormonal therapy within 14 days prior to the first dose of study medication. The patient has no history or clinical evidence of central nervous system (CNS) metastases or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. He also has no clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities that may increase the risk for gastrointestinal bleeding within 28 days prior to beginning study treatment. The patient does not have a history of cardiac or cardiovascular conditions within the past 6 months before registration and his corrected QT interval (QTc) is within normal range. He also does not have a history of cerebrovascular accident including transient ischemic attack (TIA), pulmonary embolism or untreated deep venous thrombosis (DVT) within the past 6 months before registration. The patient has no peripheral neuropathy grade ≥ 2 (NCI CTC v3.0) and no unstable diabetes mellitus. He has not undergone major surgery or trauma within 28 days prior to registration and/or has no non-healing wounds, fractures, or ulcers. The patient has no evidence of active bleeding or known endobronchial lesions and/or lesions infiltrating major pulmonary vessels. He is not hemoptysis with bleeding of > 2.5 mL within 8 weeks before registration. The patient has no serious and/or unstable pre-existing medical, psychiatric/psychological, familial, sociological, geographical or other condition that could interfere with the study procedures. He has not received prior treatment with Pazopanib or Vinflunine and is not pregnant or lactating.

25 year old female with a history of irregular periods, absence of menses for the past 6 months and normal serum FSH concentrations. She has no history of other causes for cycle disturbances, including normal prolactin concentrations and thyroid stimulating hormone. She is not currently taking any medications and has no history of gonadotoxic treatment. She has no known family history of cycle irregularities or endocrinological disease. She is interested in participating in the COLA Study and Biobank to identify potential genetic factors associated with her cycle disturbance.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been diagnosed with HIV and HCV. He has been living with HIV for 10 years and HCV for 5 years. He was diagnosed with HCV after routine blood tests revealed elevated liver enzymes. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been in recovery for the past 3 years. He is currently taking antiretroviral therapy for HIV and has been adhering to his medication regimen. He works as a construction worker and is married with two children. He reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating, which he attributes to his busy work schedule. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how the HCV treatment will affect his neurocognitive abilities. He is able to read and speak English and is willing to comply with the study requirements. He has no history of psychotic spectrum disorder, learning disability, seizure disorder or any other neurological disease.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the gastrointestinal tract. He is currently being treated with oxaliplatin plus capecitabine chemotherapy regimen. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He lives with his wife and has two adult children. He works as a retired accountant and enjoys reading and gardening in his free time. He has not experienced any cardiac symptoms or history of cardiac disease, such as myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular accident. He is able to swallow medication easily and has an ECOG performance status of 1.

A 35-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with an adnexal mass during a routine gynecological examination. She is a mother of two children and works as a teacher. Since the diagnosis, she has been experiencing physical discomfort such as pain and fatigue, and has been feeling anxious and uncertain about the future. She has also been experiencing difficulties communicating with her family members and has been feeling socially isolated. The patient has been scheduled for surgery in two days and is in need of preoperative education to help her cope with the physical, psychological and social problems associated with the diagnosis and treatment process. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and does not have any psychiatric illness.

45 yo F with a diagnosis of stage IV metastatic breast cancer with known bone and liver metastases. Patient has previously failed multiple lines of systemic chemotherapy and targeted therapy, including trastuzumab, pertuzumab, and ado-trastuzumab emtansine. Within the past month, she has also received palliative radiation to a painful bone metastasis. Patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living independently. CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis shows progression of liver metastases with new lesions and increase in size of previously known lesions, as well as new bone lesions. Patient is HLA-A2 positive and has provided a tumor specimen for testing the expression of PD-L1 and infiltrating lymphocytes. She has no contraindications to separating lymphocytes and has not undergone any anticancer treatment in the past month. Hematology and biochemical indices meet the inclusion criteria. Patient is willing to practice birth control during the regimen and has provided informed consent. She is willing and able to follow the research program and follow-up process.

A 40-year-old woman with a history of three consecutive miscarriages presented to the fertility clinic seeking assisted reproductive technology. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has been married for 5 years and has been trying to conceive for 2 years. She has a regular menstrual cycle with no history of abnormal uterine bleeding. Her partner has no significant medical history and has normal semen parameters. The couple underwent in vitro fertilization (IVF) and obtained 5 blastocysts on day 5 of embryo culture. Two of the blastocysts were considered good-quality based on a morphological score of inner cell mass B or A, trophectoderm C or better, and grade 4 or better. The patient is randomized to the study group and undergoes preimplantation methylome screening (PMS). The methylation level of the blastocysts is analyzed and the embryo with methylation level closest to the optimal level of 0.30 ± 0.02 is transferred to the uterus. The remaining blastocysts are cryopreserved. The patient is monitored for pregnancy and has a successful single frozen blastocyst transfer resulting in a live birth.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who recently suffered from a ruptured intracranial aneurysm with a Hunt and Hess grade of III. He underwent endovascular treatment and is now in the recovery stage. He has no history of other neurological conditions or co-morbidities that could interfere with the study. He is currently taking dual antiplatelet medication, which he can tolerate well. A follow-up angiogram showed a wide neck bifurcation aneurysm on the right side of his brain at the MCA bifurcation. He is interested in participating in the pToWin clinical trial to potentially receive treatment for this aneurysm using the pCONus device. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the follow-up examinations and the medical regimen required for the study.

Sarah is a 30-year-old woman who works at a computer all day. She sustained a distal radius fracture after a fall while ice skating. She presented to the emergency department within 2 days of the injury. X-rays confirmed that she has a distal radius fracture type B. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She is right-hand dominant and has no fractures in the concomitant side of the upper extremities. She is able to understand the functional evaluation and is willing to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has not undergone any previous hand or wrist surgery, and she is not affected by any cognitive deficits.

A healthy newborn baby boy, weighing 3.5 kg, born at 39 weeks gestation to a mother with a pre-pregnancy BMI of 22 kg/m2. The mother had elected not to breastfeed and provided written informed consent for her infant's participation in the study. The infant's father is also of legal age and able to fulfill the requirements of the study protocol. The family is fluent in French and can be contacted directly by telephone throughout the study. The infant has no cognitive or physical developmental disorders and has not received any radiation therapy. The infant has not participated in any other clinical trials prior to enrollment.

The patient is a 68 year old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago. He has been on LHRH agonists and his testosterone levels have been maintained at castrate levels. Despite the hormonal therapy, his PSA levels have been increasing and he has developed androgen-independent prostate cancer (AIPC) or hormone-refractory prostate cancer (HRPC). He has had two consecutive rises in PSA after the last hormonal manipulation and his PSA levels are above 5mg/dL. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score of 90% and has not received any chemotherapy treatments. He has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months. He has given signed written informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have any history of bleeding diathesis, long-term anticoagulant therapy or hypersensitivity to active or inactive excipients of fulvestrant. His platelet count is above 100 x 10e9 /L and his Total bilirubin, ALT and AST levels are within normal limits.

A 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension is currently taking beta-blockers as prescribed by his primary care physician. He has no history of head, neck or esophageal cancer, stroke, or neurological disease. He is not currently taking any other medications that are listed in the exclusion criteria. He reports no problems with swallowing or any severe clinical signs of aspiration. He is interested in participating in the study to help contribute to medical research.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of moderate hepatic impairment (Child Pugh B), which was diagnosed two years ago due to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. She has been receiving treatment for the past 18 months and has been stable. Her current medications include metformin, atorvastatin, and omeprazole. She has no other significant medical history and is in otherwise good health. She has a body mass index of 28 kg/m2. She has never participated in a clinical study involving an investigational drug in the past 5 years. She has not used any mineralocorticoids or MRAs in the past 90 days. She has not used any prescription drugs in the past 30 days, except for her established therapy for hepatic disease. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help further research on the effect of hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics of KBP-5074.

A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) six months ago. He underwent treatment with 5-fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, and bevacizumab-based therapy, but the cancer has progressed. He is now experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation. His performance status is 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale, and he has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or central nervous system disease. He has not participated in any experimental drug study in the past. He is willing to use reliable means of contraception throughout the trial and for 6 months following his final exposure to study treatment. He is capable of being accessible for study follow-up.

This is a 62 year old male with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia that has become refractory to standard treatments. He has also been diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status Score of 1, indicating that he is still able to carry out some activities but is limited in strenuous activities. His left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than or equal to 50%, and he has tested negative for hepatitis B, C, and HIV within the last 3 months. The patient has adequate liver and kidney function. In the past 3 weeks, he has not received chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, or any investigative agents. However, he has been taking hydroxyurea, which will be stopped at least 24 hours before the first dose of the study drug. The patient does not have any known or suspected involvement of the central nervous system. He has not suffered from unstable angina or myocardial infarction within the preceding 12 months, nor does he have congestive heart failure. He does not have poorly controlled hypertension or diabetes, ongoing active infection, or psychiatric illness. Additionally, he is not receiving any medications known to have a risk of causing QTc prolongation.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma in her right breast. The tumor size was 2.5 cm, and the biopsy showed negative margins. The sentinel lymph node biopsy was negative, and there was no lymph invasion or hemangiosis. Her pathology report showed that the tumor was estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive, and HER2-negative. She is a nonsmoker, and her medical history is unremarkable. She has no history of breast cancer or any other malignancy. She underwent breast-conserving surgery, and the final pathology confirmed the presence of invasive ductal carcinoma with clear margins. Her Van Nuys Prognostic Index was 6. Her breast was unifocal and unicentric, and there was no evidence of any other suspicious lesions in either breast. Her age is 47 years, and she is postmenopausal. She has agreed to participate in this study, and she has signed the study-specific consent form.

A 25-year-old Caucasian woman was scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia for the removal of her gallbladder. She has no significant medical history and is in good health. She is compliant with the dose/visit schedules and is willing to use an accepted method of contraception. She has no family history of malignant hyperthermia or any allergy to general anesthesia medications. She has never participated in any previous or new trials and is not a member of the study/sponsor staff. She is able to provide informed consent and is an ASA class 2. Her neuromuscular function will be monitored during the surgery, and she is expected to receive rocuronium for neuromuscular blockade. She is born and currently residing in Europe and has never emigrated out of Europe.

Patient B is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) based on his complaints of snoring, episodes of waking up with choking, and excessive daytime sleepiness. He works as a salesman and has a sedentary lifestyle. He reports having gained weight over the last few years and has a body mass index of 33. He denies the use of any psychoactive drugs and has no history of neurological, cardiological or pulmonary diseases. He has tried using a continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machine but found it uncomfortable to use. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help him manage his OSA symptoms.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of ulcerative colitis. He has been experiencing frequent episodes of bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and cramping for the past year. The patient has previously tried mesalamine and corticosteroids, but these treatments were ineffective in controlling his symptoms. The patient has not undergone any surgeries related to his condition. He is currently not using any medication for ulcerative colitis. The patient has no history of tuberculosis or other opportunistic infections. He has no history of heart failure or any other major medical conditions. He is not currently pregnant nor planning to become pregnant. The patient has no known allergies to sorbitol, L-histidine, L-histidine monohydrochloride monohydrate, polysorbate 80, or water for injections.

45 yo F with a history of arteriovenous malformation (AVM) in the left maxillofacial area. The patient underwent surgical resection of the AVM 2 years ago and had no complications during or after the surgery. She has been followed by her craniofacial surgeon since then and has had no recurrence of the AVM. The patient has been referred to participate in a feasibility study of Phase-contrast MRI for flow in the external carotid branches arteries. She meets the inclusion criteria for group 3: antecedent of embolization of branches of the external carotid artery. The patient has provided informed consent and has no MRI contraindications, is not pregnant or lactating, and does not have guardianship or trusteeship.

35-year-old female hospital worker with a body mass index (BMI) of 30.5 kg/m², indicating obesity. The patient has a sedentary lifestyle due to her work demands and has a history of poor dietary choices, including high-calorie and high-salt meals. She has no history of major medical problems such as heart disease in the last 6 months, orthopedic or joint problems that would be a barrier to physical activity, or alcohol or substance abuse. The patient is not pregnant and has not experienced a recent weight change of ≥10% of baseline weight. She is not taking any medications that might affect body weight and has not participated in any other weight control programs. She has no uncontrolled psychiatric problems or eating disorders. The patient is motivated to lose weight and willing to comply with a low calorie low salt lunch program.

A 50-year-old woman presents with a history of a non-palpable breast lesion that was detected on mammography during her routine screening. The mammogram showed a small mass in the upper outer quadrant of her left breast. A biopsy confirmed the presence of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery to remove the lesion, but the surgeon is concerned about the difficulty in locating the lesion during the surgery. In order to improve surgical outcomes, the patient is being considered for a pilot clinical trial using radiofrequency identification technology. The patient is able to give written informed consent, can read and write English, and meets the criteria for the study. She does not have multicentric breast cancer or stage IV breast cancer and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is eager to participate in the study to improve her chances of successful surgery and reduce the risk of complications.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of stage III colon cancer. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor and has completed adjuvant chemotherapy with FOLFOX regimen. However, a follow-up CT scan showed a new lesion in his liver indicating metastasis. He has no significant medical history and has never received anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody or fusion-protein drugs. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and he has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. His hepatitis C virus (HCV) and HIV antibody tests were negative, and he does not have any evidence of serious infection. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to receive hPV19 in combination with chemotherapy to slow down the growth of his tumor. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided his informed consent.

Patient A is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with diffuse large cell lymphoma and has undergone initial chemotherapy treatment. The patient is in partial response, with residual disease in the mediastinal area. He has no history of chronic liver disease, poorly controlled diabetes or ischemic heart disease. The patient's performance status is ECOG 1, with no symptoms of cardiac disease or uncontrolled hypertension. The patient has no obstructive airway disease, resting hypoxemia, or active ischemic or degenerative CNS disease. The patient has no HIV or HTLV-1 associated lymphomas and has not received more than 3 courses of combination chemotherapy. The patient is willing to undergo peripheral stem cell transplant and is willing to receive filgrastim treatment combined with high dose chemotherapy. The patient is expected to have a life expectancy of greater than 8 weeks and has a LVEF of at least 45% by MUGA. The patient's creatinine clearance is greater than 50 mL/min, and their bilirubin, AST, and alkaline phosphatase levels are within normal range.

45 year-old woman recently diagnosed with locally advanced cervical cancer following a routine gynecological examination. The cancer has been confirmed to be in stages IB2 to IVA, squamous-cell carcinoma. The multidisciplinary board has recommended radiotherapy and cisplatin-based chemotherapy with a curative intent. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency disease, nor any active infection requiring therapy. She has no underlying medical condition that could render the administration of the study treatment hazardous, and her laboratory values are within the required criteria. The patient is affiliated with the French Social Security System and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. She has not received any prior systemic treatment or radiotherapy for cervical cancer, nor has she undergone any prior immunotherapy, including tumor vaccine, cytokine, anti-CTLA4, anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or similar agents. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who underwent Roux-en-Y Bariatric Surgery 10 months ago. She has a BMI of 32 and is in overall good health. She does not smoke or use any nicotine products and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or dependency. Her current medications include a daily multivitamin and calcium supplement. She has not been diagnosed with any neurological, hepatic, renal, or cardiovascular disease. She has no history of vomiting or diarrhea associated with bariatric surgery. She is not currently taking any antidepressant medications and has no known allergy to duloxetine or its constituents. She has a negative pregnancy test and is practicing an accepted method of birth control. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male of African American descent who underwent hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 9 months ago. He developed acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) 2 months after the transplant and was treated with systemic corticosteroids, but did not respond well to the treatment. His aGVHD progressed to grade 3 despite treatment with corticosteroids. At the time of enrollment, he is receiving second-line therapy for aGVHD, which includes extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP). He has no history of chronic GVHD or other significant medical conditions and has not received donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) for progression of the underlying disease. His Karnofsky performance status is 80% and he is able to perform his activities of daily living independently. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past year. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and has been recommended for off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG). He has been classified as NHYA II and ASA II. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no significant medical or surgical history, and his LVEF is above 35%. The patient has given his consent to participate in the study and is willing to be randomly assigned to either the RIPC group or the control group.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has a history of allergic rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis related to birch pollen with mild to moderate persistent asthma. She presents with symptoms of sneezing, runny nose, and itchy/watery eyes during the birch pollen season. She has a positive skin prick test for birch pollen and a positive serum specific anti-birch IgE-test (>0.7 U/ml) within 1 year before randomization. She has not received any specific immunotherapy (SCIT or SLIT) with birch pollen allergens within the past 5 years. She has a FEV1>70% for patients with a history of mild to moderate asthma. She has not received any systemic steroids within 4 weeks before the start of the study and during the study. She is not currently taking systemic or local β-blockers. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate contraceptive measures. She has no history of alcohol, drug, or medication abuse within the past year. She is willing to participate in the study and able to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 42-year-old man with biopsy-proven Stage IIIA melanoma in his left leg. He has two satellite metastases and advanced local disease. He has no evidence of systemic disease outside the involved extremity. He has not had any prior isolated limb perfusion. He completed chemotherapy and regional therapy of the extremity one month ago. He has no history of claudication and his platelets, bilirubin, creatinine, and coagulation profile are all within normal limits. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is HIV negative and not a pregnant or nursing woman. He is interested in participating in a randomized Phase III study with hyperthermic isolated limb perfusion for locally advanced melanoma confined to an extremity. He understands that one arm of the study will be a standard 60 minute perfusion with melphalan as a single agent, while the second arm of the study will combine melphalan, tumor necrosis factor, and interferon-gamma in the isolated limb perfusion reproducing a regimen shown to have 100% response rates in a Phase II European trial. He is aware that he will be followed for local response rates, duration of response, treatment toxicity, and disease-free survival.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who was diagnosed with bipolar disorder II four years ago. She has a history of depressive and hypomanic episodes, with at least one hypomanic episode in the past year. She has had three depressive episodes and one hypomanic episode in the past five years. She is currently taking mood stabilizers and antidepressants prescribed by her psychiatrist. She owns a smartphone and is proficient in using it. She has no history of substance abuse or personality disorders. She is generally reliable and understands the tasks required by the study protocol. She has agreed to sign the informed consent document prior to enrollment in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has spread to her spine. She has been experiencing back pain and weakness in her legs. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She lives alone and is retired. She enjoys reading and spending time with her grandchildren. She has not undergone any previous treatment for her metastatic spine cancer, and she is eligible for either surgery or radiation therapy. She has mild to moderate weakness in her legs and is able to walk with the assistance of a cane. She is alert and oriented, and she does not have any signs of dementia. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with COPD three years ago. He has a history of smoking for 30 years but quit smoking 6 months ago. He completed a pulmonary rehabilitation program 2 months ago and is currently on maintenance medications. He reports shortness of breath during daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He has no history of heart disease or other chronic conditions. He is able to walk for 6 minutes without stopping and his oxygen saturation is 92% at rest. He has no cognitive dysfunction and speaks fluent English. He has never practiced tai chi before. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to attend the study visits regularly.

A 40-year-old Asian male with a history of Hepatitis Delta Virus infection for the past 8 years presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. The patient reported that his symptoms have been gradually worsening over the past few weeks. His medical history was significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with Lisinopril, and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, controlled with Metformin. He denied any history of alcohol abuse or illicit drug use. The patient's vital signs were stable, and the physical examination revealed mild tenderness in the epigastric region of the abdomen. Laboratory results showed elevated liver enzymes, with an ALT of 120 IU/L and AST of 90 IU/L. The patient's HDV RNA level was > 5 log10 IU/mL, and his HDV antibody was positive. The patient met the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial, including being between the ages of 18-65, having a BMI of ≥ 18 kg/m2 and weighing ≥ 45 kg, having CHD infection of at least 6 months' duration documented by a positive HDV antibody (Ab) test and HDV RNA ≥ 3 log10/mL by qPCR at study entry, and having a serum ALT > upper limit of the normal range (ULN) and < 10 × ULN. The patient provided written consent and was randomized to receive either Lonafarnib (LNF) and Ritonavir (RTV) combination therapy or LNF monotherapy for a duration of 48 weeks. The patient was advised of the potential risks and benefits of the study and agreed to follow the study procedures.

Postmenopausal women who were randomized to either denosumab or placebo in the 20050179 (NCT00293813) study and completed that study (ie, attended an end of study visit) are eligible to participate in this study. They must have completed the previous study at least 12 months prior and be ambulatory. Participants who failed to receive both doses of denosumab (or SQ [subcutaneous] placebo) during the previous study or were randomized to the alendronate arm during the previous study are excluded. Additionally, subjects diagnosed with any of the following conditions following completion of the previous study are excluded: hyperthyroidism, hyperparathyroidism, malignancy within the last 5 years (except cervical carcinoma in situ or basal cell carcinoma), any condition that required chronic (greater than three months cumulative and greater than 5 mg/day) glucocorticoid therapy, other diseases which affect bone metabolism, self-reported alcohol or drug abuse within the previous 12 months, any disorder that, in the opinion of the investigator, may compromise the ability of the subject to give written informed consent and/or comply with study procedures, received any investigational product other than denosumab in two years before the screening visit, received > 3 months (or equivalent) of osteoporosis treatment since having completed the previous study, currently using the following osteoporosis agents: bisphosphonates, calcitonin, fluoride, parathyroid hormone analogue, selective estrogen receptor modulators, systemic oral or transdermal estrogen (except vaginal preparations and estrogen creams which are acceptable), strontium or tibolone, currently enrolled in or has not yet completed at least 1 month since ending other investigational device or drug trial(s) (other than Amgen trial 20080287), or subject is receiving other investigational agent(s).

Patient is a 25-year-old woman who has just given birth to a healthy baby boy. She had received the measles and meningitis C vaccines during her pregnancy. The baby is now 3 months old and will be participating in a clinical trial to monitor the levels of maternal antibodies against measles and meningitis C. The study aims to determine whether these antibodies wane in the first six months after birth. The baby will have blood drawn at 0 months (from the placenta), 3 months, 5 months, and 7 months old to measure the geometric mean titers (GMTs) of measles and meningitis C using the ELISA test. The study is looking for healthy infants to participate and will exclude those with poor scores.

The patient is a 25-year-old pregnant woman who is currently at 26 weeks and 5 days of gestation. She had a history of preterm labor in her previous pregnancy. The patient has been experiencing regular contractions and severe pain for the past hour. The cervical dilation is 4 cm. The patient has no known chronic renal or hepatic impairment before pregnancy. The patient is not on magnesium sulfate or any other medication for preterm labor. The patient has provided her written consent to participate in the study and has joined a social security scheme. The patient is willing to receive either melatonin or placebo injection in the delivery room to reduce the risk of brain damage in the white matter of her fetus. The patient is not experiencing any maternal or fetal distress that requires an emergency cesarean.

A 27-year-old married woman living in a rural area in Uganda is interested in participating in a clinical trial to facilitate early resolution of pregnancy status. She has completed high school and works as a salesperson in a local market. She is currently not attending school. She has been married for 3 years and has one child. She wants to space her pregnancies but has difficulty determining her pregnancy status due to limited access to pregnancy tests in her area. She has not undergone any sterilization procedure nor has her husband. She has a good understanding of menstrual periods and is willing to participate in this study to help improve reproductive, maternal, and child health outcomes in her community.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of benign prostatic hypertrophy (BPH) for the past 6 months. He has noticed a decrease in the urinary stream, as well as increased frequency and urgency to urinate. He has not undergone any prostate-related surgical procedures in the past month, nor has he been diagnosed with prostate or bladder cancer. He is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He has continuous eligibility for 6 months prior to and 12 months after the index prescription date. The patient has been prescribed either a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor (5ARI) or an alpha-blocker (AB) to treat his BPH symptoms. He will be monitored for one year to assess the treatment patterns and outcomes of his BPH medication.

50-year-old male patient with a history of COPD and a recent exacerbation requiring ICU admission. He is intubated and mechanically ventilated with a FiO2 of 50% and PEEP of 10 cmH2O. His ABG shows a pH of 7.32, pCO2 of 58 mmHg, and pO2 of 68 mmHg. He is being considered for a percutaneous tracheostomy procedure due to prolonged mechanical ventilation. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications other than those administered during his hospitalization. He has a BMI of 28 and is 5'10" tall. He has no history of bleeding disorders or thyroid diseases. He has given informed consent for the procedure and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been referred to the Vascular Medicine Department of Caen University Hospital for a vascular examination. He has a history of smoking and high blood pressure but is otherwise healthy. He has no prior diagnosis of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) or any other vascular condition. The patient has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate. He has social protection and is eligible for the study. The patient has no arrhythmia or any amputation. His limbs are free of extensive trophic disorder, allowing measurements to be taken. He has not undergone any subgonal bypass and does not have known bilateral sub-clavian stenoses. The patient is not deprived of liberty or under a measure of legal protection. He is not under any psychiatric or physical treatment and is legally competent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 3 years. He presents with symptoms of chronic cough, particularly worse at night, and recurrent wheezing during the past 6 months. He has also experienced difficulty breathing during exercise and when exposed to smoke or pollen. He has been receiving medical care for treatment of respiratory symptoms consistent with asthma and has had reversible (greater than or equal to 12%) airflow obstruction after an inhaled short-acting beta2-agonist. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not on any chronic medications. He is fluent in English and is able to read and understand basic instructions. His family is supportive of his participation in the study and is willing to attend all follow-up visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman of South Asian descent who has been diagnosed with diabetes for the past 5 years. Despite taking medication regularly, her HbA1c levels have consistently been above 7. She has been struggling to manage her diabetes due to cultural and language barriers, which have resulted in a lack of understanding of the disease and difficulty accessing appropriate resources. She has a family history of diabetes, with her mother and siblings also having been diagnosed with the disease. She is fluent in English and has a regular primary care physician, but has not been able to achieve adequate glycemic control. She is interested in participating in the study to gain better control of her diabetes and to learn more about culturally relevant resources available to her.

The patient is a 58-year-old male, Hispanic, who had a history of chest pain and underwent angioplasty six months ago. He is currently on medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. He works as a salesman and has a sedentary lifestyle. He is married with two children and lives in a suburban area. He is interested in participating in a cardiac rehabilitation program to improve his overall health and reduce his cardiac risk factors. He has a good cognitive level and is able to perform aerobic exercise on a treadmill or cycle ergometer. He is familiar with the use of a mobile smartphone and is willing to participate in a home-based monitoring cardiac rehabilitation program. His ejection fraction is 45% and his functional capacity is 5 METS. He is not currently experiencing any arrhythmias or other complications related to his heart condition. He is willing to sign the informed consent form and participate in the study.

The patient is a 35 years old male who is generally healthy and has no history of chronic illness. He works as a software developer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He doesn't smoke or consume alcohol. He has no significant family history of gastrointestinal diseases. He occasionally experiences heartburn after a large meal or spicy food, but it is not frequent enough to interfere with his daily activities. He is not taking any prescription drugs or over-the-counter medications, except for occasional paracetamol for headache. He is interested in participating in clinical trials to contribute to medical science. He is willing to comply with the study procedures, which may require multiple visits to the research site and a strict medication regimen. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is able to give fully-informed, written consent. He is not pregnant, lactating, or using a steroid contraceptive. He has normal blood pressure, heart rate, and laboratory values. He has no evidence of drug abuse or infectious diseases. He is cleared by his GP to participate in the trial.

Sarah is a 49 year old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer that metastasized to her liver. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not responded as expected. Sarah's oncologist informed her about the WINTHER study and its personalized therapeutic approach based on the analysis of matched tumor and normal biopsies. Sarah is interested in participating in the study and has given her informed consent. She meets the eligibility criteria as she has a metastatic cancer for which a histologic normal counterpart can be obtained. She has progressed on at least one prior regimen for advanced disease and has measurable or evaluable disease according to RECIST 1.1 criteria. Sarah is in good physical condition with an ECOG Performance status of 1. She has no organ or hematopoietic function alterations that would exclude her from participating in the study. She has not received personalized therapeutic treatment based on molecular anomaly during the treatment period prior to the WINTHER directed treatment.

68 year old female with a history of bilateral cataracts and no significant ocular or medical history. She has been experiencing decreased visual acuity and some glare and halos around lights. She has been advised by her ophthalmologist to undergo cataract extraction surgery. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially receive the aspheric ReSTOR multifocal intraocular lens (IOL). She is able to comply with scheduled visits and other study procedures. She has not undergone any ocular surgery in the past three months or intraocular laser surgery in the past month in either eye. She is not currently participating in any investigational drug or device trials and has no other ocular or medical conditions that would increase the risk associated with study participation or study device implantation.

A 50 year old woman underwent an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones. She has no history of heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes. She has not smoked cigarettes in over 10 years and reports no current alcohol or substance abuse. She has no allergies and is not taking any medications. Her Glasgow Coma Score is 15 and her American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status score is 2. She has no history of complete bowel obstruction and does not have dentures. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent post-operative ileus and is willing to chew gum as part of the trial protocol.

A 38-year-old female patient presents with recurrent chronic abdominal pain and discomfort with no detectable organic causes. She reports a change in frequency and form of stool, and relief with defecation. The patient has been diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) according to Rome IV Criteria. She has a history of anxiety and depression, but no other significant medical history. The patient is not currently taking any medications or supplements for IBS. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a novel formulation of B. longum BB536 and L. rhamnosus HN001 with vitamin B6 on the gut microbiota and intestinal permeability in IBS subjects.

A 30-year-old male with no known medical conditions came to the clinic to participate in the clinical trial for the drug Kaletra™. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol or use drugs. He has not taken any medication known to inhibit or induce cytochrome P450 isozymes or ABC-transporters in the past two months. He has been deemed in good health by the clinic's physician and has given informed consent to participate in the trial.

45-year-old man who complains of pain and tenderness in the medial aspect of the knee that has been bothering him for the past few weeks. The pain is worse with activity and relieved by rest. He denies any history of trauma, fever, chills, or night sweats. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the anserine bursa with no evidence of swelling or erythema. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. He has never been diagnosed with any intraarticular pathology that may be responsible for the pain in his knee.

A 35-year-old female pediatrician who works in a tertiary hospital complains of feeling overwhelmed and burnt out due to her heavy workload. She has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. She has no previous experience with yoga or meditation, and is not currently taking any medications. She is literate and able to provide informed consent.

A 30-year-old Chinese woman gave birth to a baby boy weighing 2.9 kg at 36 weeks gestation. The baby was delivered via vaginal delivery with no complications. Shortly after birth, the baby developed respiratory distress and was placed on nCPAP. However, the baby's respiratory distress persisted and he was considered a candidate for non-invasive respiratory support. The parents have given signed informed consent to participate in a clinical trial comparing NIPPV vs nCPAP in newborn infants with respiratory distress syndrome. The baby has no known lethal congenital anomaly or genetic syndromes and has not received more than 24 hours of cumulative intubated respiratory support. The baby is currently stable and ready to be randomized to either NIPPV or nCPAP treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of cocaine dependence. He has been abstinent from all drugs of abuse, except nicotine, for three days prior to admission to the CTRC. He has no significant hematological, endocrine, cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, gastrointestinal, or neurological diseases. He is not currently taking any psychotropic medications or opiates, and he has not received synthetic glucocorticoid therapy or exogenous steroid therapy within one month of the test session. He is willing to remain abstinent from drugs of abuse (except nicotine) for the duration of the study and has provided informed consent to participate. The patient meets the general inclusion criteria for the study and will be evaluated for participation based on his BMI and clinical judgment of the study staff.

Patient is a 7-year-old girl with a formal diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), who has had limited exposure to physical activity and has never participated in martial arts. The patient's parents have expressed concern about their child's social interaction skills and are interested in exploring alternative interventions to traditional therapies. The child is able to follow and understand English verbal instructions during the screening process and is able to walk and move without using adaptive equipment. The family is excited to participate in this study to explore the benefits of taekwondo as an intervention for their child's social interaction skills and everyday life.

A 56-year-old woman who participated in a previous screening colonoscopy study came to the clinic for a follow-up colonoscopy examination. She had no family history of colorectal cancer and had no other colonoscopies except the baseline screening colonoscopy. She was asymptomatic during the first screening colonoscopy and had no history of gastrointestinal disease. Her past medical history was unremarkable except for hypertension for which she was taking lisinopril. She had a healthy lifestyle, followed a balanced diet, and exercised regularly. She had no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. Her last bowel movement was normal. She was willing to participate in the follow-up colonoscopy examination and signed the informed consent form.

A 58-year-old male presented to the emergency department with chest pain, shortness of breath, and dizziness. He reported a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. The patient was diagnosed with a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) based on his ECG and elevated cardiac biomarkers. His hemoglobin level was found to be less than 100 g/L, indicating anemia. The patient was admitted to the hospital and treated with standard therapies for NSTEMI. He was approached about participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of blood transfusions in patients with myocardial infarction and anemia. The patient was informed of the potential risks and benefits of the trial and agreed to participate. He met all the inclusion criteria and did not have any exclusion criteria. The patient was randomized to receive either a higher or lower amount of blood transfusion. The trial staff ensured that the patient received appropriate follow-up care and monitoring after discharge. The patient's medical history and current medication regimen were reviewed to ensure that he was not taking any medications that could interfere with the trial results. The patient was monitored for any adverse events related to the blood transfusion and was asked to report any symptoms or changes in health status.

A 42-year-old female with a history of chronic constipation for more than 6 months with spontaneous bowel movement (SBM) less than 3 times per week within recent 3 weeks. She experiences straining, lumpy or hard stools, and incomplete evacuation during defecation. She has undergone a barium enema within the past year, which did not reveal any organic diseases. She does not meet the criteria for irritable bowel syndrome. She has no contraindications to gastroscopy or colonoscopy, and she is not taking daily non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. She has not received abdominopelvic radiotherapy treatment, and she has no history of GI tract surgery. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she has no known swallowing disorder or allergy to conscious sedation, polyethylene glycol or metoclopramide. She is willing to swallow the vibrating capsule and is able to provide written informed consent.

This is a 59-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. The tumor is localized and has been classified as stage T1c. The patient is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic radical prostatectomy in the next 3 to 6 weeks. He has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and potential chemopreventive effects of synthetic genistein (BONISTEIN™) in patients with prostate cancer. The patient has not had any previous or concurrent hormonal therapy or chemotherapy, and does not have a history of other hormone-dependent malignancies. He does not have concomitant thyroid disease or currently taking thyroid hormone replacement medication. The patient is not currently taking high dose soy, micronutrient or herbal supplements, and does not have any extreme dietary habits. He is not on oral anticoagulants and does not have a history of liver or pancreas diseases. The patient has not had any previous hypersensitivity to Genistein or soy containing products, and does not have any malabsorption conditions which might interfere with absorption of the investigational product. He has signed the informed consent form to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been self-conscious about the freckles on her face for several years. She has a fair complexion and has noticed that the freckles have become more pronounced over time, especially during the summer months. She has tried various over-the-counter creams and serums, but has not noticed any significant improvement. She works as a marketing executive and is concerned that her appearance may affect her professional image. She has no history of significant sunburns or skin cancer in her family. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She takes no medications and has no known allergies. She has not undergone any cosmetic procedures in the past. She is interested in exploring the option of using a fractional CO2 laser for the treatment of her freckles.

A 13-year-old male is diagnosed with nWHO Grade IV glioma. He underwent surgery and radiation therapy and is currently receiving chemotherapy. He has no other medical conditions and is in good physical health. He is not allergic to any of the study drugs. His platelet count is within normal limits, and his hemoglobin level is above 9 g/dl. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 80. He has not received any other immunotherapies within the last 30 days. He and his parents are willing to sign the informed consent form and understand the investigational nature of the study. He is negative for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C seropositive. He has no prior invasive malignancy or autoimmune disease requiring medical management with immunosuppressant(s). He has no active infection requiring intravenous antibiotics or active immunosuppressive disease. He has no major medical illnesses or psychiatric impairments that would prevent administration or completion of protocol therapy. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has not been diagnosed with connective tissue disorders or AIDS. He meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 24-year-old male diagnosed with severe hemophilia A with no history of Factor VIII inhibitory antibody. He has been receiving prophylactic infusions twice a week for the prevention of bleeding without any relevant interruption for the past 3 years. The patient has a documented history of joint bleeds and their locations prior to the start of prophylaxis, and bleeding history and/or treatments received during the last 5 years are documented in the patient's medical records. The patient has had more than 12 bleeds per year in the last 5 years and has experienced joint bleeds in the ankles and knees. The patient has no other coagulopathies and is not HIV seropositive. The patient has not undergone synovectomy or joint replacement surgery within the last 6 months and does not have any orthopedic surgery planned during the investigation period. The patient and their legal representative have provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 50-year-old man who has been diagnosed with essential hypertension for the last 5 years. He takes Lisinopril 20 mg once daily to manage his blood pressure. He is currently scheduled to have an elective surgery and has no contraindication for inhalation anesthesia or postoperative morphine pain control. The patient has no history of liver or renal disease, and no events of myocardial infarction, cardiac bypass surgery, unstable angina, cerebrovascular events, congestive heart failure, significant arrhythmia, or thoracic surgery in the last 6 months. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no dementia or conscious disturbance. The patient is willing to participate in the study to help researchers determine whether the use of opiate analgesics for postoperative pain management differs between patients with essential hypertension and those without.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and a dual chamber pacemaker implanted due to sick sinus syndrome. He has been experiencing occasional palpitations and shortness of breath despite being on anti-arrhythmic medication. His pacemaker interrogation revealed that he has an AF burden of 30%. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any other medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol, but his BMI is 31. His recent echocardiogram showed a normal ejection fraction and no significant valvular dysfunction. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of a new medication, BMS-914392, in reducing his atrial fibrillation burden. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman with no significant medical history who is scheduled for a cesarean delivery. She has no known allergies and is currently taking prenatal vitamins. She has never had any complications during previous pregnancies or deliveries. The patient has been informed of the possibility of experiencing hypotension after the subarachnoid block and has consented to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy and side effects of two doses of norepinephrine bolus (6 mcg and 10 mcg) in managing maternal hypotension during cesarean delivery. She understands the importance of the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

Pt is a 45yo M with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension who presented to the ED with fever, chills, and altered mental status. On examination, the patient was found to have a fever of 39°C, hypotension with a systolic blood pressure of 90 mmHg, tachycardia, and tachypnea. Blood tests revealed elevated white blood cell count, elevated lactate levels, and positive blood cultures indicating septic shock. The patient was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluids were aggressively administered. Despite these interventions, the patient remained hypotensive and required vasopressors to maintain his blood pressure. It was determined that the patient required surgical intervention for source control and was scheduled for general anesthesia. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of lidocaine as an adjuvant for ketamine in induction of anesthesia in septic shock patients.

The patient is a 15-year-old high school student who complains of difficulty falling asleep at night and feeling sleepy during the day. She reports that she usually falls asleep around midnight and wakes up at 6 am on weekdays. She also reports feeling tired and unmotivated during the day, which affects her school performance. She does not have any diagnosed physical or mental health problems, but she does have trouble sleeping on school nights. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to help adolescents manage their sleep through a mobile phone app. She has access to an iPhone and is willing to use a study-provided iPhone if required. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands that she may be randomized to either the SOmNI Intervention group or the Control group. She is also willing to wear a monitoring device to track her sleep and provide feedback through the app. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old non-smoking woman who has been experiencing a persistent cough for the past six months is seeking treatment. She has already tried several over-the-counter cough medications, but none have provided relief. Her cough is described as dry, non-productive, and worse at night. She does not have a history of asthma or respiratory infections, and her chest x-ray from six months ago was normal. She has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She has no allergies and has not had any recent surgeries. She works as a teacher and reports that her cough is interfering with her ability to speak in class. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options for her persistent cough.

The patient is a 72-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with localized prostate cancer during a routine check-up. He is in overall good health and has no significant medical history. He has a PSA level of 6.2 ng/mL and a biopsy revealed a Gleason score of 7 (4+3) in 2 out of 12 cores. He has no urinary symptoms and his digital rectal exam is normal. He is interested in exploring treatment options and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help further research on the treatment of aggressive prostate cancer in elderly patients.

A 26-year-old female patient is scheduled for a tonsillectomy due to obstructive sleep apnea. She has a history of seasonal influenza vaccination and has not experienced any life-threatening reactions to previous vaccinations. She is generally healthy and willing to complete the informed consent process. She has no history of asthma, allergy to egg or egg products or to vaccine components. She does not have any active systemic or serious concurrent illness, and there is no known or suspected impairment of immunologic function. She has not been hospitalized in the past year for congestive heart failure or emphysema nor has she been diagnosed with chronic Hepatitis B or C. She is not currently taking immunosuppressive medication, including systemic glucocorticoids, and has no history of blood dyscrasias, renal disease, or hemoglobinopathies requiring regular medical follow-up or hospitalization during the preceding year. She has not taken any influenza antiviral medication within 48 hours prior to the study vaccination. She has not received a live, attenuated vaccine within 60 days prior to enrollment of planned vaccination prior to completion of the last study visit. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she has no medical or psychiatric condition or occupational responsibilities that preclude participant compliance with the protocol. She is eligible to participate in the study.

55 yo M with a history of rectal bleeding and weight loss presents to the GI clinic with a biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma of the rectum. CT scan shows a locally advanced T3 tumor with suspicious involvement of the mesorectal fascia. Patient agrees to participate in a clinical trial involving genetic testing of tumor tissue and blood samples to predict response to chemoradiation. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. No history of cancer in the patient or his family. No prior radiation or chemotherapy. Current Medications: Amlodipine 5mg daily, Atorvastatin 20mg daily, and acetaminophen as needed.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma two years ago. She has received multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation treatments but the disease has relapsed and is now refractory to treatment. Her recent bone marrow biopsy confirms the presence of multiple myeloma cells. Her performance status is ECOG 1 and her life expectancy is greater than 3 months. Her ANC is 980/mm³, platelet count is 56,000/mm³, and hemoglobin is 10.2 g/dL. The patient has no history of cardiac disease but has a history of controlled hypertension and diabetes mellitus. She is currently taking metformin and lisinopril for her diabetes and hypertension respectively. She has no known allergies to boron or mannitol. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is able to comply with the follow-up regimen.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), with clear-cell histology. He had previously received first-line treatment with sunitinib and had a partial response, according to Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1 criteria. He subsequently received second-line treatment with an mTOR inhibitor, which eventually failed after 8 months. He has not received any Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) targeted Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (TKI) as a second-line treatment. He has radiological and clinical evidence of progressive disease according to RECIST 1.1 criteria. He has measurable or evaluable disease as defined by RECIST 1.1. His WHO performance status is 1. His life expectancy is estimated to be more than 12 weeks. He is aged 55 years or older. He is able to receive oral medication and provide written informed consent. His hematologic function is adequate: Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) is 2.0 x 109/L, platelets are 120 x 109/L, and Hb is 12.0 g/dL. He has no brain metastases. He has no other current malignant disease except for basal cell carcinoma of the skin. His hepatic function is adequate: serum bilirubin is 1.1 x Upper Limit of Normal (ULN), Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) is 1.5 x ULN, and Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST) is 2.0 x ULN. His estimated glomerular filtration rate is 60 mL/min. He is using effective contraception and has a negative pregnancy test. He has no history of uncontrolled hypertension or recent myocardial infarction. He has no significant central nervous system or psychiatric disorders that would hamper his compliance, and he has no other major illnesses that would substantially increase the risk associated with his participation in the study.

A 22-year-old college student with no significant past medical history presents with an interest in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of hydrocortisone on cognition. The patient reports no current medications or significant medical conditions. They are a non-smoker and do not consume alcohol or recreational drugs. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements. They understand the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and have provided informed consent.

A 56-year-old male was recently diagnosed with esophageal squamous carcinoma after experiencing difficulty swallowing and chest pain. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled on medication. He has never received chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy before. He is a non-smoker and denies alcohol consumption. Physical examination showed no remarkable findings except mild tenderness in the epigastric region. Laboratory studies showed a normal hematocrit, platelet count, and liver transaminase levels. His creatinine clearance is above 40 ml/min, and he meets all the baseline organ function criteria defined by the study. He has no history of interstitial pneumonia or autoimmune diseases. His ECOG PS is 1. He is willing to undergo treatment and adhere to the study protocol. He is able to provide written informed consent. He is a good candidate for the study as his disease is surgically resectable and the tumor is limited to the esophagus.

A 55-year-old female presented with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years, hypertension for the past 5 years, and a body mass index of 31. She reported occasional shortness of breath during moderate activity. She denied chest pain, palpitations or syncope. She takes metformin, lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide for her medical conditions. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her vital signs were stable in the primary evaluation. The physical exam was unremarkable except for obesity. She underwent a cognitive testing at rest and a maximal cardiopulmonary exercise test (CEPT) with gas exchange analysis. During CEPT, cerebral oxygenation (measured by near-infra red spectroscopy) and cardiac hemodynamics responses (impedance cardiography) were measured continuously. She was diagnosed with metabolic syndrome as per the criteria (Alberti et al. 2005): presence of at least three of five criteria, namely abdominal obesity (waist circumference cut-off depending on the recently published ethnic-based variations, triglycerides > 1.70 mmol/l, decreased HDL-cholesterol (< 1.0 mmol/l in men and < 1.3 mmol/l in women), systolic blood pressure > 130 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure > 85 mmHg, and FPG > 5.6 mmol/l. The patient provided written informed consent and had sufficient initial physical and intellectual capacities allowing an independent daily living.

53-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 8 years ago presents with complaints of pain, burning sensation, numbness, and sensory loss in the lower extremities. HbA1c levels at the time of screening were 8.5%. The patient has a score of 6 on the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and a physical examination score of 3 on the Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument Score (MNSI). The patient has no history of peripheral neuropathy caused by other causes other than diabetes or other painful conditions that are so severe that diabetic neuropathy cannot be assessed. The patient is not suffering from any progressive or degenerative neurological disorder. The patient has a systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 140 mmHg and a diastolic blood pressure (DBP) of 85 mmHg. The patient has no history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B (HBV), or hepatitis C (HCV), liver dysfunction, renal dysfunction, or thyroid dysfunction. The patient has no history of amputation or infections of the lower extremities. The patient has no history of clinically significant liver, kidney, lung, or hematologic disease, cancer, substance abuse or chronic alcohol abuse, suicide attempts or suicidal tendencies, and psychiatric history. The patient is not currently taking medication for other research and has not participated in other studies within 4 weeks before participating in the trial. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity or clinically significant hypersensitivity reactions to the drug substance and soybean oil, soy, or peanut. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is not receiving treatment with chlorpromazine, mesoridazine, thioridazine, fluphenazine, perphenazine, trifluoperazine, haloperidol, loxapine, or other drugs known to cause epileptic seizures. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and meets all inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 10-year-old child who has been admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit with a severe asthma exacerbation. The child is experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness. The child has a history of asthma and has been using a combination therapy of inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists for the past year. The child's vital signs are stable, but oxygen saturation is low and requires supplemental oxygen therapy. The child is a candidate for continuous albuterol nebulization as per current policies and procedures. The child is not on invasive or non-invasive ventilation. The child and their parents have provided written consent for participation in the study.

42-year-old female with a history of recurrent pharyngitis presents to the clinic with a sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and fever. She reports that her symptoms started 2 days ago and have been worsening. Upon examination, she has erythema and swelling of the tonsils and pharynx with exudates on the tonsils. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to follow the trial protocol and abstain from oral and inhaled treatments during the trial period. She has not taken any analgesic or antipyretic medication within the past 24 hours. She reports that she has only used inhaled therapy on an intermittent basis in the past week. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help with the development of new treatment options for sore throat pain.

Patient is a 35-year-old Chinese male with a diagnosis of cerebellar ataxia. He presents with symptoms of uncoordinated balance, gait, extremity and eye movements. He has a family history of cerebellar ataxia, as his father was also diagnosed with the condition. The patient is able to comply with trial procedures and visit schedule, and he and his legal guardian are willing to complete the informed consent process.

A 54-year-old woman presents with a history of melanoma on her left thigh that was completely excised. She has no evidence of metastasis and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 90% and an ECOG performance status of 1. Her laboratory parameters are within normal limits, with ANC, platelets, and Hgb levels in the normal range. She has no known allergies to any of the components of the vaccine, and is not currently receiving any medications that would exclude her from the study. The patient is not pregnant and has no medical contraindications or potential problems in complying with the requirements of the protocol, as confirmed by the investigator. There is no evidence of active pulmonary disease or systemic autoimmune disease with visceral involvement. The patient has no clinically apparent skin infection or other clinically evident inflammation involving the skin adjacent to the melanoma biopsy scar.

The patient is a 34 year old woman who has been diagnosed with mild persistent asthma by her physician. She has been experiencing asthma symptoms, such as coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, more than twice a week for the past month. She has not had any unscheduled asthma related health visits in the past month and has missed only one day of work due to her asthma. She uses her albuterol inhaler less than 4 times a week. She is fluent in English and has access to a telephone. She confirms that she will use birth control while in the study and has had a negative pregnancy test at baseline. She is not pregnant and is not a prisoner. She does not have any chronic illnesses other than asthma, allergic rhinitis and eczema. She is able to perform spirometry, which is necessary for lung function assessment. She has not received probiotics in the past 6 months and does not have immunosuppression or any conditions that would make her ineligible for the study. She does not have diarrhea or constipation and is able to feed orally and consume cornstarch. She does not have any lung disease other than asthma and is not at an increased risk of developing infective endocarditis. She is not allergic to Vancomycin or Cefepime.

Maria is a 35-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis by a rheumatologist. She has been experiencing joint pain, swelling, and stiffness in her fingers, wrists, and ankles for about 6 months. She also has psoriasis on her scalp and elbows that has been present for several years. She is currently not on any medication for her psoriasis or arthritis, and her symptoms have been impacting her daily life, making it difficult to perform her job as a hair stylist. She has no known allergies to any medications and has never participated in a clinical trial before. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow the treatment protocol. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant within the next 6 months. She has a regular menstrual cycle and uses birth control pills. Her blood tests, including full blood count and liver function tests, are within normal limits. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to improve her joint pain and quality of life.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male with a BMI of 35.6 kg/m2 presents with a history of obesity and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). He reports feeling fatigued, has difficulty climbing stairs, and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has no history of bariatric surgery, but he has attempted various weight loss diets without success. He does not smoke or consume alcohol excessively. His blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, and his blood work shows elevated liver enzymes and an HOMA-IR score of 3.5. His liver ultrasound confirms the diagnosis of NAFL

Samantha is a 10 year old girl who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) six months ago. She has not received any treatment for CHB yet. She is a student and lives with her parents and two siblings. Samantha is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. She weighs 22 kg and her estimated creatinine clearance is 90 mL/min/1.73m^2. She and her parents are willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in children with CHB. They have read and understood the informed consent/assent form and are willing to provide written consent/assent. Samantha has not had any other co-infections with HCV, HIV or HDV. She has not had any history of clinical hepatic decompensation, malignancy or bone marrow transplant. Samantha is not on any therapy with immunomodulators or immunosuppressants.

45-year-old post-menopausal female with no significant medical history and scheduled for a screening colonoscopy presents for enrollment in the clinical trial. She has a body weight of 68 kg, is a non-smoker, and does not consume excessive caffeine or alcohol. She has no known allergies to food colorants. She has not taken any medication within the last 2 weeks. She has normal routine hematology and blood chemistry tests, as well as a normal ECG. She provides written informed consent and is able to understand and comply with the protocol. She will be administered food-grade dyes orally during preparation with KleanPrep for screening colonoscopy, and will be assessed for quality of mucosal staining of the colon, adenoma detection rate, and adverse events.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who sustained a spinal cord injury (SCI) at the C6 level during a motor vehicle accident 18 months ago. She has incomplete motor function in both upper and lower extremities with motor scores of 4/5 in her upper extremities and 3/5 in her lower extremities. She reports difficulty with fine motor tasks such as buttoning her shirt and opening jars, as well as difficulty with walking and balance. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for blood pressure control. She has no history of seizures or other neurological disorders, and no history of implanted devices or metal in her body. She is able to follow instructions and perform the required tasks for the study. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

55 year-old male with a history of heartburn, acid regurgitation and belching for the last 3 months. The symptoms have been interfering with his daily activities and he has been taking over-the-counter antacids for relief. He visited a gastroenterologist and was diagnosed with GERD. He has been prescribed proton pump inhibitors and has noticed some relief in his symptoms. He is interested in participating in a study about GERD and its management to increase his knowledge and understanding of the disease. Past Medical History: Hypertension treated with lisinopril.
