A 24-year-old female university student who wears contact lenses for nearly every day for the past 2 years. She has a spherical prescription of -2.50D in both eyes and no astigmatism. She is in good health and does not have any ocular or systemic disorders. She has not undergone any ocular surgery and does not use any topical medication. She is willing to comply with the wear schedule and follow the protocol. She has not participated in any other contact lens clinical trial or research in the past two weeks. She is interested in being part of this study to contribute to the development of better contact lenses.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic urticaria with or without angioedema, and/or pruritus for at least 6 weeks. She has been taking anti-histamines as needed to manage her symptoms. She has undergone skin prick tests and/or RAST tests that have shown negative results for all food allergens tested. She has no other underlying medical conditions that could account for her symptoms. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not taking any CNS acting agents. She is willing to follow a low histamine diet for 4 weeks and record her symptoms and dietary intake in a food diary. She is also willing to attend weekly follow-up calls with a dietitian to ensure compliance with the diet.

This is a 32-year-old female who has a history of asthma since childhood. She has been using her inhaler as needed and has had several exacerbations in the past year, requiring emergency room visits. She presents to the ER with shortness of breath, wheezing, and coughing. Her peak flow rate is 50% of predicted. She consents to participate in a clinical trial exploring the combination of systemic steroids and inhaled steroids for acute asthma treatment. She has no other chronic medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications other than her rescue inhaler. She will be randomized into either the study group or the control group and will receive the standard ER treatment of beta 2 short-acting inhalation and IV solumedrol. The study group will receive three additional inhalations of Budesonide 1000 micrograms each during the first hour. Her PFT will be followed at 0, 30, 60, and 120 minutes.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a history of chronic back pain and has been scheduled for Thoracic Surgery. She currently takes a daily dose of oxycodone for pain management. She has not used any other opioids or dexmedetomidine within the last 28 days prior to the day of surgery. She has no history of major psychiatric disorder, congestive heart failure, or abnormal liver or renal function. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no contraindications to the use of NSAIDs, Acetaminophen, or IV opioids. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

This is a 46-year-old female with Down syndrome who does not have a diagnosis of dementia. She currently lives at home with her parents and has a caregiver who provides regular updates on her cognitive status. She has no history of neurodegenerative disorders other than Down syndrome, and no clinically significant medical comorbidities. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to better understand the relationship between Down syndrome and Alzheimer's disease. She will be part of the DS group in the study, which includes 15 DS subjects aged 21 and older who do not qualify for the diagnosis of dementia at the beginning of the study. She is willing to provide a blood sample to assess the apolipoprotein E (ApoE) genotype. She understands the requirements of the study, has provided written informed consent, and agrees to abide by the study restrictions and return for the required assessments.

56-year-old post-menopausal woman with a history of ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer that has metastasized or recurred locally. The patient must have objective evidence of progression on or after the last systemic therapy prior to starting the study treatment. The patient must not have received more than one line of endocrine therapy for advanced disease, and no more than one line of chemotherapy for advanced disease. The patient must not have received prior treatment with fulvestrant, oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD), or related therapies. The patient must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG)/World Health Organization (WHO) performance status of 0 to 1. The patient must have at least one lesion, not previously irradiated, that can be measured accurately at baseline as ≥10 mm in the longest diameter or in absence of measurable disease as defined above, at least one lytic or mixed (lytic+sclerotic) bone lesion. The patient must not have had any cytotoxic chemotherapy, investigational agents, or other anti-cancer drugs for the treatment of breast cancer from a previous treatment regimen or clinical study within 14 days of the first dose of study treatment. The patient must not be using systemic estrogen-containing hormone replacement therapy within 6 months prior to the first dose of study treatment. The patient should not have any contraindications listed in the exclusion criteria section of the study.

A 56-year-old Latino man living with HIV was recently diagnosed with high blood pressure and obesity. He is currently taking antiretroviral therapy and has a viral load of less than 200 copies/mL. He has been living in Miami for the past year and expects to stay for the next six months. He is interested in participating in the Happy Older Latinos Are Active (HOLA) Health Promotion Study to improve his overall health and prevent chronic diseases. He has no history of diabetes or bipolar disorder, and he has medical clearance from his physician to participate in physical activity. He is willing to provide informed consent and attend interviews and walking groups as part of the study.

This is a 48-year-old male who has been experiencing subjective, unilateral or bilateral, non-pulsatile tinnitus for the past 8 months. The tinnitus has been bothersome and has had a major impact on his daily life. He reports difficulty concentrating and remembering things, and has noticed a decline in his cognitive functioning. He has tried several over-the-counter remedies for tinnitus with no improvement. He is computer-literate and has access to a computer for at least 60 minutes per day, 2 days per week, for five consecutive weeks. He is willing to work on the Brain Fitness Program® that will be provided and attend all study visits as required. He does not have any central neurological conditions, anxiety disorder or psychiatric co-morbidity that may complicate the interpretation of study results. He is not currently taking any medications that may affect cognition or are contraindicated with DCS. He is willing to use a study-approved form of contraception and not try to become pregnant during the duration of the study. He is able to provide valid informed consent and speaks English fluently.

58 year old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who suffered a left middle cerebral artery stroke 6 months ago. He has residual non-fluent aphasia with difficulty in word retrieval, sentence formation and repetition. He has not received any speech therapy before. He is right handed and has completed 12 years of education. MRI brain showed infarction in the left middle cerebral artery territory. He has no history of epilepsy or cardiac pacemaker. He is currently on antiplatelet therapy and statins.

A 15-year-old Caucasian male with type 1 diabetes presents for his routine appointment at Boston Children's Hospital. He was diagnosed with diabetes 2 years ago and his blood sugar levels have been difficult to manage. He reports feeling overwhelmed and frustrated with the constant monitoring required to control his diabetes. He has missed a few appointments in the past due to feeling discouraged. He lives with his parents and an older sibling. He attends high school and is in 10th grade. He is interested in playing sports but finds it difficult to keep up with the demands of his diabetes management while participating in sports. He is generally compliant with his medication regimen but has experimented with alcohol and marijuana on a few occasions with friends. His parents are present during the appointment and are supportive of his diabetes management but are unaware of his substance use. They are interested in learning more about how they can support him in managing his diabetes. His HbA1c level is 8.5%.

A 27-year-old Caucasian female presents with a history of atopic eczema for the past 5 years. She has a family history of allergic rhinitis and asthma. Her eczematous lesions are mainly on her arms and legs, with occasional involvement of the chest and back. She has tried various topical steroid creams in the past, but her symptoms tend to recur when she stops using them. She has not used any topical steroids or light therapy in the past 2 weeks. She uses a moisturizing cream regularly to help with her dry skin. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the tolerance of a new strong steroid cream and the preventative properties of a moisturizing cream on skin that has been previously cleared from eczema.

Patient A is a 35-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe abdominal pain. The pain is located in the right lower quadrant and radiates to the back. The patient reports nausea and vomiting but denies any fever, diarrhea or constipation. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medication. On physical examination, the abdomen is tender and there is guarding and rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. Laboratory studies showed a WBC count of 13,000/mm3. The patient is suspected to have an acute surgical emergency and is eligible for the non-enhanced MSCT study to aid in diagnosis.

Pt is a 45yo Caucasian female presenting with symptoms of stress urinary incontinence (SUI) for the past year. She reports leakage of urine during physical activity such as running, jumping or coughing. She has no symptoms of urge incontinence. A physical exam reveals no evidence of pelvic organ prolapse (POP-Q<2) and urodynamic testing confirms a diagnosis of urodynamic SUI with a positive cough stress test (CST) at a bladder filling volume of 250 ml in lithotomy position. The patient has no history of previous urinary incontinence or pelvic organ prolapse surgery, and no other pelvic organ pathology is present. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for a prospective randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing an inside-out trans-obturator sling (TOT) with an innovative fixation single-incision sling (SIS) in patients undergoing primary surgery for urodynamic SUI.

The patient is a 29-year-old pregnant woman in her 9th week of pregnancy, experiencing persistent vomiting and severe nausea that has caused her to lose weight and become dehydrated over the past few days. She has a history of mild motion sickness but has never experienced anything like this before. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She has no known allergies and takes only her prescribed medication. Her family history is negative for any major illnesses. She presents to the hospital with a high level of distress due to the constant vomiting and nausea. Her vital signs are stable, but she is noted to be dehydrated with elevated ketones in her urine. She is eligible for inclusion in the clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria for persistent vomiting and dehydration due to NVP. She is informed about the possibility of being randomized to either the day care or inpatient management of NVP and agrees to participate in the study after providing informed consent.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who was diagnosed with invasive breast cancer 10 months ago. She completed her active treatment, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy, 4 months ago. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She has no history of any other cancers, except for basal cell carcinoma, which was treated 2 years ago. She does not have any cognitive or psychological problems and is fluent in English. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help researchers learn more about the role of diet and lifestyle in breast cancer survival. She is willing to complete the questionnaires and keep a food diary. She would like to know if her dietary and supplemental intake of phytoestrogens can affect her breast cancer progression and survival.

Patient is a 30-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of sickle cell disease (SCD). She has a history of recurrent SCD-related pain crises, but is currently in stable clinical condition as determined by her physician. She is currently receiving scheduled standard of care RBC exchange transfusion therapy, with at least 3 transfusions already received. The patient has no history of metal devices affected by MRI or any contraindications for MRI, and is able to lie still for at least 5 minutes without experiencing claustrophobia. She has not experienced an acute pain crisis requiring hospitalization within the past 4 weeks, and is at steady state as determined by her physician. The patient has not received hydroxyurea therapy within the past 3 months.

50-year-old female with a history of migraines and recent onset of intermittent headaches presented with confusion and difficulty with speech. MRI revealed a non-enhancing, non-tumoral lesion in the left frontal lobe. The patient underwent a stereotactic biopsy, which revealed a diagnosis of focal cortical dysplasia. The patient is currently undergoing clinical and MRI follow-up for more than 24 months. An FDOPA-PET scan was performed within the last 2 months before the biopsy. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and is eligible for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer six months ago. She has been receiving chemotherapy for the past four months, which has caused mild nausea and hair loss. She has not received any other systemic anticancer therapy before this. She is otherwise healthy with no history of autoimmune disease, HIV infection, or other significant medical conditions. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and her blood counts and liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. She is using effective contraception and is willing to participate in the study. She has a family history of breast cancer and is currently married with two children. She works part-time as a teacher and enjoys gardening and hiking in her free time. She has a positive attitude towards her treatment and is looking forward to exploring new treatment options.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with the diagnosis of autistic disorder. He has difficulties in social interaction and communication, and restricted, repetitive and stereotyped patterns of behavior. He also exhibits serious behavioral problems including irritability, aggression, and self-injurious behavior. He is currently under treatment with psychotherapy and behavior modification but has not shown significant improvement. He is a student and is in the fourth grade. He has difficulty making friends and is often bullied by his classmates. He enjoys playing video games and watching cartoons. His parents report that he has difficulty sleeping and often wakes up in the middle of the night. He has no known medical conditions and is not on any medication at present. His BMI is within normal limits and his physical exam is unremarkable.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) by a child psychiatrist. He has difficulties with social communication and interaction, as well as repetitive behaviors and restricted interests. The patient has been receiving speech therapy and occupational therapy for the past year, with some improvement in communication skills and sensory processing. He has no other significant medical history and takes no medications. The patient's parents have consented to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of sulforaphane in the treatment of ASD. The patient will undergo a screening evaluation to confirm the diagnosis of ASD and to assess eligibility for the study. The patient is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that it will help him improve his social skills and decrease his repetitive behaviors.

A 55-year-old man is brought to the emergency room by paramedics following an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with ventricular fibrillation. He is resuscitated after 20 minutes of advanced cardiac life support. The patient is intubated and mechanically ventilated. He has no past medical history, and his initial ECG shows an ST-elevation myocardial infarction. His estimated weight is 85 kg. The patient's Four Motor Score is 3, indicating severe impairment in motor function. His temperature is 36.5°C. He is enrolled in the study within 50 minutes of the event. He has no history of alcohol or substance abuse or dependence. His liver function tests are within normal limits. The patient is not receiving IV vasopressin or lidocaine hydrochloride. The patient's family is informed about the study, and they provide informed consent for his participation.

The patient is a 45 year old Asian male with a BMI of 29. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago and has been on multiple medications to control his blood sugar levels. Despite his treatment regimen, his HbA1c levels have remained above 8%. He also has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He works as an accountant and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has struggled with weight loss in the past. He is married with two children and enjoys spending time with his family. He has no history of previous surgeries and has not had any major medical issues in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks associated with the surgical and medical treatment options. He is motivated to improve his diabetes control and is open to considering the surgical option if it is determined to be the best treatment for him.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on a stable dose of medication for the last 6 months, including metformin, lisinopril, and simvastatin. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He reports occasional chest discomfort and shortness of breath with exertion. His recent lipid profile shows total cholesterol of 240 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol of 160 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 45 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 200 mg/dL. His blood pressure is well-controlled at 130/80 mmHg. He reports occasional muscle pain but no weakness or tenderness. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He does not have any known liver, thyroid, or kidney problems. He is currently not taking any medication that could affect lipid levels or insulin resistance. His HbA1c level is 6.5%. He has not had any viral or bacterial illness in the past 3 months. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with all study requirements.

This is a 32 year old female who has been experiencing pelvic pain for the past 3 years. She was diagnosed with endometriosis after a laparoscopy was performed to investigate the cause of her symptoms. She has tried various hormonal treatments in the past but has not experienced significant relief from her symptoms. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and has no history or suspicion of hormone dependent tumor. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her endometriosis-associated pelvic pain.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing widespread pain, fatigue, and stiffness in her muscles for more than three months. She also reports difficulty sleeping and feels constantly exhausted. She has seen multiple specialists and received various treatments, but none have provided lasting relief. She has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that combines two therapies to manage her symptoms. She has no history of depression and is willing to adhere to the therapy protocol.

The patient is a 40-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder who has been admitted to an inpatient detoxification unit. He has been drinking heavily for the past 10 years and has tried to quit several times but has been unsuccessful. He is experiencing physical and psychological discomfort including tremors, anxiety, and insomnia. The patient has no other substance use disorders and has no history of serious psychiatric or medical illnesses. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol. He is not currently taking any anti-cholinergic medications or has any implantable electronic devices.

A 42-year-old male patient is scheduled for an elective craniotomy due to a meningioma. He has a history of occasional headaches that are usually managed with over-the-counter analgesics. He has no known drug allergies and takes no regular medications. The patient has no significant medical history, and his vital signs are within normal limits. Preoperative imaging shows the meningioma to be located in the left frontal lobe. He has given written consent to participate in the study. The patient is randomly assigned to the study group that will receive 7.5 mg of midazolam and 100 mg of diclofenac as premedication. The patient undergoes induction of anesthesia with propofol and maintenance of anesthesia with fentanyl, rocuronium, and sevoflurane. Infiltration of the surgical site is done with a combination of 2% lidocaine and epinephrine. The patient is admitted to the neurosurgical ICU for postoperative observation. Pain assessment occurs at bedrest state using a 0-10 scaled visual analogue scale (VAS) on days 1-5, and rescue analgesics are given according to the patient's needs. The investigators intend to examine whether the preoperative administration of 100 mg diclofenac reduces the incidence and severity of postcraniotomy headache on the first and fifth postoperative days, as well as the difference in incidence and severity of headache between patients who underwent infra- or supratentorial interventions. The patient's intraoperative and postoperative analgesic needs, as well as any postoperative complications, will also be recorded.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who presented with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His chest pain was relieved by nitroglycerin, and he was admitted for further evaluation. His electrocardiogram showed ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF. Cardiac enzymes were elevated, indicating an acute coronary syndrome. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to the culprit lesion in the left anterior descending artery, which was successfully treated with stent implantation. He is now scheduled for a follow-up angiogram and possible PCI of a non-culprit lesion. He has provided informed consent for participation in the study and has vascular access of at least 6F.

A 22-year-old female who has not yet undergone puberty, with no onset of breast development or menstruation. She has been evaluated by an endocrinologist and has a low level of estrogen and progesterone, as well as consistently low levels of gonadotropins. She has no other medical problems, and there is no family history of reproductive disorders. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the potential genetic basis of her condition and to potentially inform future treatment options.

We are seeking healthy male volunteers aged between 30 and 65 years for a Mass Balance Study of [14C]-Orvepitant Oral Solution. The ideal candidate must have a BMI between 18.0 to 35.0 kg/m2 and must not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 2 years. The candidate should not have a habit of smoking or have consumed more than 21 units of alcohol per week. The candidate should not have been exposed to radiation more than 5mSv in the last 12 months or 10mSv in the last 5 years, excluding background radiation but including diagnostic x-rays and other medical exposures. The candidate should not have any clinically significant abnormal clinical chemistry, haematology, or urinalysis as judged by the Investigator. They should not have a confirmed positive drugs of abuse test result or positive hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis C virus antibody (HCV Ab) or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) results. They should also not have evidence of renal impairment at screening, as indicated by an estimated creatinine clearance (CLcr) of <80 mL/min using the Cockcroft-Gault equation. The candidate should not have a history of clinically significant cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, chronic respiratory, or GI disease, neurological or psychiatric disorder, as judged by the Investigator. If you fulfill these criteria and agree to adhere to the contraception requirements, you may be eligible to participate in this study.

A 15-year-old male with a history of bipolar disorder and psychotic features presents with complaints of significant weight gain over the last year. He has been taking olanzapine for 18 months and his current dosage is 15mg/day. His BMI is 28.5, which is more than 10% above what is expected for his age and height. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. He has no family history of diabetes or cardiovascular diseases. He denies any regular exercise routine and reports a diet high in carbohydrates and fats. He is compliant with his medication regimen and reports no significant side effects. He is currently living with his parents and attending school. He has no history of substance use or abuse. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his weight gain.

A 62-year old retired accountant underwent colonoscopy for the first time as part of his routine screening. He has a family history of colon cancer. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and a previous episode of diverticulitis. He is taking medications for his conditions. He denies any abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or change in bowel habits. The patient is alert and cooperative, and he understands the importance of regular colonoscopy screening. The colonoscopy detected a polyp, and the patient was advised to undergo polypectomy. He is interested in participating in this study to potentially improve the accuracy of polyp classification and diagnosis.

A 28-year-old male presents with symptoms of fever, cough, and body aches for the past 2 days. He reports having close contact with a coworker who was recently diagnosed with the flu. Upon examination, the patient has a temperature of 101.2°F and shows signs of respiratory distress. A rapid influenza test is performed, which comes back positive for Influenza A. The patient is then considered for the clinical trial to further investigate the presence of the H1N1 strain. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial as he has tested positive for Influenza A on the rapid test. He does not meet the exclusion criteria as he has not tested positive for Influenza B on the rapid test. The patient consents to participate in the trial, and RNA is extracted from his influenza A-positive specimen for real-time PCR testing to detect the presence of the swine H1 gene. His symptoms will also be monitored and recorded for the trial.

A 25 year old female patient presented to the Department of TMD in Zabrze, Polska with chronic pain in her jaw and neck, accompanied by headaches and difficulty in opening her mouth. She has been diagnosed with TMD and has been taking painkillers for the past 6 months with no significant improvement. She is otherwise healthy, non-smoker, and has no known allergies. She has all her teeth except for the third molars. She has not used cannabis before and has no history of addiction. She is not currently taking any medications that affect muscle function. She wears a removable dental prosthesis. On examination, her sEMG activity values were elevated, confirming the presence of myofascial pain of masticatory muscles. She agreed to participate in the research study and was randomly assigned to the experimental group, receiving cannabis cream for topical skin application.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who reports vaginal dryness, itching, and pain during intercourse. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 years and has not sought treatment. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is not currently sexually active but desires to resume sexual activity with her partner. Her BMI is 30. She has not used oral estrogen therapy in the last 6 months and has no history of cancer or renal/hepatic insufficiency. She has not undergone vaginal radiotherapy therapy and does not have vulvovaginitis. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of fractional CO2 laser treatment and local estrogen therapy in treating her vaginal atrophy symptoms.

This is a 40-year-old female who was diagnosed with schizophrenia 8 years ago. She has been on various antipsychotic medications, but her symptoms have not been well-controlled. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles but has not gone through menopause yet. She is physically healthy and does not have any endocrine disorders. She has no history of breast or uterine cancer, and no family history of these cancers. She is a non-smoker and does not use recreational drugs or alcohol. She is willing and able to comply with study instructions and has provided informed consent. She currently has a PANSS score of 85, with a PANSS positive subscale score of 20 and a PANSS negative subscale score of 17. She meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria. She will be randomized to receive either a 200 µg estradiol patch or a placebo patch as an add-on to her current antipsychotic medication.

A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with a suspicious mass in her right breast is scheduled for a large core breast biopsy at the Radiology Department at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center Boston. The patient is a working mother with two school-going children. She is otherwise healthy, non-smoker, and non-alcoholic with no history of psychiatric illness. The patient is anxious about the biopsy procedure and worries about the outcome of the biopsy. The patient speaks fluent English and is able to give informed consent.

A 55-year-old male patient presents with a history of right-sided ischemic stroke that occurred 6 months ago. He has been experiencing post-stroke spasticity in his right leg, with decreased range of motion and difficulty with walking. He reports pain and stiffness in his right leg, which is affecting his daily activities. He has no other neurological diseases and is not taking any antispastic medication. He is able to adopt the prone or supine position on the treatment table and is able to sit, stand and walk with assistance. He has good language and communication skills and is able to understand the informed consent. He has not suffered any traumatic injury to his lower limbs in the last three months and does not have any infectious diseases, inflammatory vascular conditions, acute inflammation, hemorrhagic fever or other contraindications to functional massage. The patient has a score of 26 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and a score of 1 on the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) for hip and knee flexion, and ankle dorsiflexion on his right leg. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his post-stroke spasticity and regain his mobility.

A 25-year-old healthy woman, who is not pregnant or lactating, volunteered for this clinical trial. She is from Rwanda and has a normal BMI. She consumes beans as a staple food in her diet every day. She has no history of any chronic or gastrointestinal disease, and has not donated blood in the last 6 months. She is not taking any long-term medications. She is willing to participate in the study to help understand the iron absorption from biofortified beans with different levels of phytic acid. She is excited to be part of the study and contribute to the research that can potentially help her community combat iron deficiency anemia.

A 40-year-old man came to the clinic with complaints of a large lump on his upper thigh that has been growing slowly for the past year. He also complained of mild pain and discomfort in the area. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. On physical examination, a firm, immobile, and non-tender mass measuring approximately 10cm in diameter was palpated on his upper thigh. There were no signs of inflammation or infection. The rest of the physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory tests were within normal limits. A biopsy of the mass confirmed the diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma. The patient was offered participation in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of perifosine in treating advanced soft tissue sarcoma. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and is willing to participate in the study after being counseled on the investigational nature, potential risks, and benefits of the study.

A 58-year-old male patient was diagnosed with Philadelphia positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) a month ago. He has no significant past medical history, except a history of high blood pressure that is well-controlled with medications. He is retired and lives with his wife. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. His physical examination is significant for mild pallor, but no other abnormalities. His blood tests show elevated white blood cell count and presence of the Philadelphia chromosome. He has not received any prior treatment for his leukemia, except for pre-phase chemotherapy. He has a good performance status (WHO 1). He is interested in participating in clinical research to help advance treatment options for his condition.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who recently experienced chest pain and was diagnosed with a heart attack. She has no history of heart disease or high blood pressure, and she does not smoke. She is married and has two children. She works full-time as a nurse and is physically active, exercising regularly and maintaining a healthy diet. Her troponin level was positive and she was diagnosed with NSTEMI. Coronary angiography revealed a tear in the arterial wall (SCAD) that was not related to trauma. She has no other significant medical history or drug allergies. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to better understand SCAD and its natural history, as well as improve diagnosis and management of this condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old Taiwanese man who has a history of smoking for over 30 years. He is currently a heavy smoker, smoking around 1.5 packs of cigarettes per day. The patient is concerned about his lung health and has decided to pay for a low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening at National Taiwan University Hospital Chu-Tung Branch (NTUHCT). He has no history of lung cancer or any other types of cancer. He has no significant past medical history and does not take any regular medications. The patient has no known allergies. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he reports no respiratory symptoms such as cough, shortness of breath, or chest pain. The patient has provided informed consent for the LDCT screening and the telephone follow-up for this retrospective epidemiological study on lung cancer.

28 year old woman with a confirmed tubal ectopic pregnancy based on ultrasound findings. She has not experienced any significant abdominal pain and her hCG levels have not risen optimally over the past 48 hours. Her hCG level is currently at 4500 IU/l. She is haemodynamically stable and has a mean diameter of adnexal mass of 3.3cm. She has no history of allergies to Methotrexate. Past Medical History: Asthma and allergic rhinitis, managed with inhaled corticosteroids and antihistamines respectively. No previous surgery.

The patient is a 38-year-old female diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) 2 years ago. She presented to the clinic with shortness of breath and fatigue during activities. She claims mild dyspnea after climbing 1 flight of stairs, no dyspnea at rest and no angina (New York Heart Association class 2). Currently, she is being treated with ambrisentan 10 mg every day for the past 6 months. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with levothyroxine 50 mcg/day. She is not allergic to any medications. Her family history is negative for any cardiac or pulmonary disease. Her lab study is as follows: Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL, White Blood Cell Count: 6.5 × 10^3/µL, Platelet Count: 240 × 10^3/µL, Sodium: 140 mEq/L, Potassium: 4.0 mEq/L, Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL, Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST): 25 U/L, Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT): 22 U/L. She is able and willing to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

A 65-year-old man presents to the ophthalmology clinic with complaints of blurred vision and difficulty seeing at night. He is known to have benign prostatic hyperplasia and has been on tamsulosin for the past 3 years. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has no known allergies. He reports no previous eye surgeries or injuries. His ophthalmic examination reveals cataracts in both eyes, and he is a candidate for cataract surgery. He is informed about the potential risk of Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS) during surgery due to his tamsulosin treatment. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to reduce the incidence and severity of IFIS by using anterior corneal incisions during surgery. He is able to understand and sign the informed consent.

A 58-year-old man was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after experiencing abdominal pain and jaundice. He has a history of chronic hepatitis B and alcoholic liver disease. He is currently at BCLC stage C and is not eligible for radical treatment. He has not received any prior systemic anti-tumor treatment for HCC but has undergone TACE with stable disease for more than 4 weeks. He has no history of central nervous system metastasis or active tuberculosis. He has Child Pugh score of 6 and good organ function. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and follow-up visits. He is currently taking no aspirin or other drugs that inhibit platelet function. He has no history of severe bleeding tendency, coagulation dysfunction, or thrombolysis. He has no history of pulmonary fibrosis, interstitial pneumonia, pneumoconiosis, drug-related pneumonia, severe impairment of lung function or other lung diseases. He has no history of major surgery or local treatment for liver cancer within 4 weeks before the first administration. He is willing to use effective contraceptive measures during the whole treatment period and 6 months after the last medication. He has signed the written informed consent and is able to follow the visit and relevant procedures specified in the plan.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is currently at 16 weeks of gestation. She has no history of diabetes but has a family history of type 2 diabetes. She has been attending regular prenatal visits at National Taiwan University Hospital and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effect of early screening and intervention for gestational diabetes mellitus on pregnancy outcomes. She has no known allergies, has no current exposure to steroids, and is willing to undergo an OGTT for the trial.

Patient is a 40-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of respiratory tract infection and/or acute bronchitis, including cough, sputum production, and chest pain during coughing for the past week. He has not received any treatment for his symptoms yet. The patient has a history of seasonal allergies and asthma, but has not had any asthma exacerbations in the past year. He does not smoke and has not had any recent travel history. The patient is willing to participate in an observational, non-interventional multicentric study comparing the inhalation therapy with Ectoin inhalation solution and Pari NaCl (0.9%) inhalation solution. He meets the inclusion criteria as per the instruction for use and does not meet any exclusion criteria. The patient will be assessed using the bronchitis Severity Score (BSS) for standardized use in clinical studies.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy with a pre-operative diagnosis of cyanotic congenital heart disease. He is scheduled to undergo surgical repair of his heart defect. He has no significant medical history other than his heart condition. His pre-operative vital signs are stable with a heart rate of 95 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, and blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg. The patient's parents have given informed consent for him to participate in the study.

47 yo F diagnosed with primary Sjögren's syndrome with a history of recurrent episodes of dry mouth, dry eyes, and difficulty swallowing. Current medications include hydroxychloroquine and artificial tears with limited symptom relief. Serum testing reveals elevated ANA and RF levels. Patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential new treatment for pSS. Past Medical History: - Primary Sjögren's syndrome - Hypothyroidism - GERD - Allergic rhinitis - Depression - Migraines - Anxiety - Fibromyalgia

A 52-year-old male with a spinal cord injury (SCI) at the T7 level resulting from a motor vehicle accident 15 years ago is interested in participating in this clinical trial. He is non-ambulatory and dependent on a wheelchair for mobility. He is married and lives with his wife who is his primary caregiver. He has completed the Impact of Age on Cardiovascular, Cerebrovascular and Cognitive Health study and is interested in continuing his participation in the longitudinal study. He has a history of hypertension and has been on medication to control it for the past 5 years. He has not had any recent acute illnesses or infections. He is fluent in English and has no history of traumatic brain injury, stroke, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, or psychiatric disorders. He is interested in contributing to the research on aging with SCI and hopes to learn more about how cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and cognitive changes impact his life as he ages.

52F with recurrent episodes of palpitations and shortness of breath was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) two years ago. Despite treatment with rate-controlling agents, she continues to have symptoms and has been admitted to the hospital for cardioversion twice. She is currently on metoprolol and anticoagulation therapy with warfarin. She is frustrated with the frequent episodes of AF and is interested in alternative treatments. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of tedisamil in converting AF to normal sinus rhythm. She has no history of acute myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular accidents, coronary syndromes, or congestive heart failure (NYHA IV). She is currently not pregnant or lactating and is willing to sign the informed consent before screening examinations are performed and before the study drug is administered.

7-year-old girl with a history of recurrent nosebleeds is brought in by her parents to the ENT clinic. The nosebleeds have been occurring approximately once a week over the past month and are often difficult to control. The parents report that the nosebleeds usually start spontaneously without any apparent cause. Examination of the nose reveals prominent vessels on the anterior nasal septum. The child has no history of bleeding disorders and no known allergies to peanuts, neomycin, or chlorhexidine. The parents are interested in enrolling their child in a clinical trial to evaluate treatments for recurrent nosebleeds.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was recently treated for pulmonary tuberculosis. He completed the chemotherapy treatment for TB one month before Study Day 0. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He works as a teacher and is married with no children. He has no history of allergic reactions or immunodeficiency states. He has no chronic illness or any acute or chronic illness that may interfere with the evaluation of the safety of the vaccine. He has not used any investigational drug therapy or vaccine within 182 days before the first dose of study vaccine in this protocol. He has never received any adenovirus-based vaccine previously. He is compliant with the previously prescribed tuberculosis therapy and agrees to complete currently prescribed tuberculosis therapy. He has no plans to move from the study area during the duration of the study. He has completed simultaneous enrollment in Aeras Vaccine Development Registry Protocol. He is willing to avoid elective surgery and pregnancy for the full duration of the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) within the last 2 years. She has experienced symptoms such as muscle weakness, numbness, and difficulty with coordination. She is able to perform high-intensity aerobic training and transport herself to and from training sessions. She has no comorbidities that would hinder her participation in the study. She is willing to sign the consent form to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old man with a history of Stage II high-risk colon cancer comes to the clinic for follow-up after surgical resection. His pathology report confirmed R0 resection. He has completed three months of standard adjuvant chemotherapy and has detectable circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) prior to the start of adjuvant chemotherapy. He has no history of microsatellite instability high tumors, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Adequate hematologic and organ function has been confirmed in his most recent lab results. The patient has not received neo-adjuvant chemotherapy prior to surgery, systemic immunosuppressive medication within 2 weeks prior to initiation of trial treatment, or any other investigational drug within the past 28 days. He has no known allergies, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to RO7198457 or its excipients. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and will be randomized to either the RO7198457 group or the watchful waiting group.

The patient is a 56-year-old man with a history of hypertension and smoking, presenting to the emergency room with chest pain that started 3 hours ago. The pain is located in the center of the chest and radiates to the left arm. He also complains of shortness of breath and sweating. His vital signs are stable with a heart rate of 80 beats per minute, blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, and oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. He has no known allergies and takes medications for hypertension. The initial electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF consistent with an inferior myocardial infarction. He is diagnosed with Type 1 MI and is admitted to the cardiac care unit. During the hospitalization period, he will be eligible for enrollment in the HELicobacter Pylori Screening in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction (HELP) pilot study. He will be screened for Helicobacter pylori infection with a bedside urea breath test (UBT) incorporated into his routine care. As a smoker, he will be at an increased risk for upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) in the future, and therefore, screening and subsequent eradication therapy for Hp infection may reduce the risk of hospitalization for UGIB. The patient will be eligible for inclusion in the trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of Type 1 MI. However, he will be excluded from the UBT screening if he has a history of gastric surgery, acute gastrointestinal bleeding, suspected gastric infection, or known atrophic gastritis.

A 28-year-old Hispanic woman who is 8 weeks pregnant is scheduled for a medical abortion at a clinic. She has no medical history and is not taking any medication. She is married and has one child. She works full-time as a receptionist. She is fluent in English and Spanish. She has no known allergies. Before the procedure, she is prescribed a seven-day course of doxycycline as a preventive measure against infection. She is informed about the potential side effects of the medication and instructed to complete a self-administered, computer-based questionnaire 7-14 days after taking mifepristone to report any side effects and her adherence to the prescribed regimen. She is willing to participate in the study and provide honest and accurate responses to the questionnaire.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing leg swelling, pain, and fatigue for the past 5 years. She has noticed that her legs feel heavy and achy, especially after prolonged periods of standing or sitting. She has tried compression stockings and elevation of her legs, but has not found much relief. She has also noticed that the skin on her legs is becoming discolored and has developed varicose veins. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and she takes medication for this condition. Her family history is significant for venous disease in her mother and sister. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find new treatments for her chronic venous insufficiency and improve her quality of life.

10-year-old male with a history of asthma and no known drug allergies presented to the emergency department with a displaced and angulated distal radius fracture. The patient was in significant pain and distress on presentation. The patient was otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. The patient's parents reported that the patient was able to communicate effectively and had no developmental delays. The patient and parents were able to speak and understand English. The patient was deemed appropriate for procedural sedation for fracture reduction. The patient was randomized to receive either etomidate or ketamine for sedation as part of this clinical trial.

A 25-year-old female, who is a non-smoker, is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the pharmacokinetics and side effects of fenobam. She has no known medical conditions and her BMI is 22. She has not taken any prescription or non-prescription medications, vitamins, herbals, dietary and mineral supplements or grapefruit products within the last 14 days. She has no history of addiction to drugs or alcohol and is not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to comply with study guidelines and provide informed consent. She does not have lactose intolerance.

The patient is a 25 year old male who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of pain and discharge from the area between the buttocks for the past 6 months. He has noticed that the symptoms worsen with prolonged sitting and physical activity. He has never undergone any surgical procedure for this condition. He is otherwise healthy, non-smoker and has no known drug allergies. He works as a software engineer and sits for long hours in front of his computer. He practices good personal hygiene and has no family history of similar condition. On examination, there is a small opening with surrounding erythema and induration in the midline of the sacrococcygeal area. There is no evidence of abscess or acute inflammation. The patient is interested in the new minimally invasive technique for the management of his condition.

A 45-year-old male was recently diagnosed with chronic phase chronic myelogenous leukemia. He has not received any prior treatment with interferon-alpha. He has a normal performance status and is able to perform daily activities with ease. He has no significant hepatic diseases. He is not pregnant nor possibly pregnant. He is willing to participate in the study to assess the efficacy, safety, and long-term prognosis of imatinib for chronic phase CML.

A 42-year-old Caucasian woman has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed for the past 6 months. She has seen a psychiatrist and has been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder based on DSM-5 criteria. Her Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) score is 18. She has tried two different antidepressants in the past without achieving significant symptom relief and experienced side effects such as gastrointestinal discomfort and drowsiness. She is currently not taking any medication for depression. She has no history of neurological disorders, substance abuse, or other medical illnesses. She has no family history of mental health disorders. She is not pregnant, and she has not been diagnosed with any personality disorders. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will compare a combinatorial pharmacogenomics (PGx) test with standard treatment for Major Depressive Disorder.

Patient is a 28-year-old primigravida with a singleton pregnancy at 37 weeks (+/- 2 days) of amenorrhea. She has no history of prior caesarean section and her fetus is in cephalic presentation. She is seeking to participate in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the efficacy of acupuncture in reducing the caesarean section rates for cervical dystocia. The patient has no contraindication to vaginal delivery and has signed an informed consent to participate in the trial. She is willing to be randomized to receive either traditional chinese acupuncture, sham acupuncture, or usual care only, and is willing to undergo a 5-week follow-up.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. He has been on antipsychotic medication in the past, which has been effective in managing his symptoms. However, he has experienced a recent exacerbation of his symptoms, including delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized thinking. He is currently not on any medication for his condition and is willing to participate in the study. He does not have any other medical illnesses and is not currently using any substances of abuse. He has no history of schizoaffective disorder or single episodes of schizophrenia in partial remission.

52 year old male with a history of familial hypercholesterolemia and a myocardial infarction 2 years ago. Despite being on maximum tolerated doses of atorvastatin and ezetimibe, his LDL-C levels remain elevated at 120mg/dL. He has no history of renal dysfunction or nephrotic syndrome, and his BMI is 28kg/m2. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if bempedoic acid can help further reduce his LDL-C levels and decrease his risk of future cardiovascular events.

65 year-old male with a recent diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma presenting with jaundice, dark urine and pale stools. CT scan of the abdomen showed a mass at the hilum of the liver causing obstruction of the biliary tree. The patient is unresectable and is being considered for palliative treatment with biliary stenting. He has a past medical history significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a remote history of smoking. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 2. He is able to provide informed consent and has no severe dysfunction in other organs.

A full-term Caucasian male infant born at 39 weeks gestational age presents with signs of neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) due to maternal opioid use during pregnancy. The mother was on a methadone maintenance program throughout her pregnancy, and the infant's meconium tested positive for methadone. The baby was admitted to the NICU at the University of Massachusetts Memorial Hospital, where he will be assessed for eligibility for a clinical trial. The infant weighs 3.5 kg and is otherwise healthy, with no other medical complications or congenital abnormalities. The infant will be monitored for symptoms of NAS, including tremors, excessive crying, sleep disturbances, and gastrointestinal issues. If eligible, the infant will be randomized to receive either stochastic vibrotactile stimulation (SVS) or standard of care treatment. The study aims to examine the effectiveness of SVS in reducing the severity and duration of NAS symptoms and improving neurobehavioral outcomes in opioid-exposed newborns.

This is a 52-year-old female with a history of myocardial infarction (MI) within the past 6 months. She has a family history of heart disease and has been experiencing symptoms of depression and anxiety since her MI. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help identify the link between emotional stress and heart disease in women. She is willing to attend one clinic visit, undergo one week of at-home monitoring, and receive follow-up phone calls every 6 months for 3 years. She is currently taking anti-depressants and is not on any other psychotropic medications. She does not have a serious medical disorder that may interfere with study results and her blood pressure is within the acceptable range for the study. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

Pt is a 45yo male with a history of chronic hepatitis B infection. He has been diagnosed with HBeAg negative hepatitis B and has been on antiviral therapy for the past 2 years. His current viral load is undetectable and he has normal liver function tests, but he continues to have detectable levels of HBsAg. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of extended therapy with peginterferon alpha 2a in HBeAg negative chronic hepatitis B patients. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, co-infection with HIV, HCV, or HDV, autoimmune hepatitis, or neoplastic diseases of the liver. He is willing to undergo regular testing and follow-up for the duration of the study.

56 year old postmenopausal woman, diagnosed with node-positive breast cancer (stage II) after undergoing a total mastectomy. The tumor was estrogen receptor-positive, with a histopathologic examination of 10 positive nodes out of 12. She is not on any hormone replacement therapy and has no nonmalignant systemic disease that would preclude protocol therapy or prolonged follow-up. Her blood work shows WBC greater than 4,000 and platelets greater than 100,000. She has no psychiatric or addictive disorder that would preclude informed consent. She is geographically accessible for follow-up. She has not undergone any prior therapy for breast cancer other than potentially curative surgery.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer that has spread to his liver. He underwent surgery to remove the pancreatic tumor followed by chemotherapy with gemcitabine for 6 cycles. However, his cancer progressed despite treatment. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of over 3 months. He has not received any anticancer therapy in the last 4 weeks and has recovered from any side effects of prior therapy. His ANC, platelet count, and hemoglobin levels are within normal limits. He has no significant liver

This is a 64-year-old female with a histological diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. She was initially diagnosed in [**10/2119**] after presenting with abdominal pain and weight loss. She underwent a Whipple procedure followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. She had a partial response to treatment but has since developed cancer-related cachexia, with an involuntary weight loss of more than 10% of her pre-illness body weight over the previous 6 months. Despite continued treatment with chemotherapy, her appetite has decreased, and she has difficulty maintaining her weight. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her weight and appetite. She has no history of depression or other medical conditions that would interfere with the study procedures. She is not currently taking any anabolic agents or appetite stimulants and has no recent history of highly emetogenic chemotherapy. She has no contraindications for MRI scanning, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She provides written informed consent prior to screening.

A 50-year-old Japanese man with type 2 diabetes who is currently being treated with one oral antidiabetic drug is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. His HbA1c levels at screening are between 6.5% and 9.0%. He has a BMI between 18.0 and 40.0 kg/m2 and is between the ages of 20 and 70. He has not had a myocardial infarction, stroke, or transient ischaemic attack within the past 6 months, and does not have any clinically relevant concomitant diseases other than T2DM, hyperlipidemia, and medically treated hypertension. He is not under treatment with any concomitant medication except for statins, antihypertensives (diuretics not allowed), alpha-blockers for benign prostate hypertrophy, and occasional use of acetylsalicylic acid, ibuprofen, or paracetamol. He is willing to provide written informed consent and is able to comply with the requirements of the trial.

A 56-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, presenting for pulmonary vein isolation as part of his atrial fibrillation ablation. The patient has been experiencing episodes of atrial fibrillation for several years and has been taking anticoagulant medication to manage his condition. The patient has no known allergies or contraindications to adenosine and is able to give informed consent. The patient is not currently taking dipyridamole, verapamil, or theophylline. The patient is not a breastfeeding mother. The patient will be randomized to either the treatment or control group in the study. The patient will be followed up at clinical visits to examine for any adverse effects of the procedure and/or adenosine administration as well as atrial fibrillation recurrence.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing knee pain for the past 6 months. She has had knee osteoarthritis for several years and has been managing her symptoms with pain medication. She is able to walk short distances without assistance, but has difficulty with stairs and standing for long periods of time. She is retired and spends most of her time at home. She has never participated in a formal exercise program and is interested in exploring non-pharmacological options for managing her knee pain. She does not have any other medical conditions that would limit her physical ability.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage III non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are all well controlled with medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has been started on chemotherapy and is scheduled to undergo high-dose melphalan conditioning followed by autologous stem cell transplantation. He has been experiencing diarrhea, abdominal pain, and nausea after starting chemotherapy. His performance status is 1 (able to carry out light work). He has no history of allergies and is not taking any other medications except for the ones prescribed for his chronic medical conditions. He lives with his wife and two adult children. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help reduce the side effects of his treatment.

Maria is a 52 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with prediabetes. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and heart disease. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2 and her waist circumference is 38 inches. She works as an accountant and spends most of her day sitting at her desk. She is married and has two children. She enjoys cooking and eating out with her family and friends, but has noticed that her diet is not as healthy as it should be. She also admits that she does not exercise much, except for occasional walks during weekends. She has normal blood pressure and lipid levels. She does not smoke but drinks alcohol on social occasions. She is willing to make lifestyle changes to prevent the onset of diabetes and improve her overall health.

The patient is a 6-month-old male infant who was born prematurely at 28 weeks gestation. He spent 10 weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit due to respiratory distress syndrome and sepsis. His birth weight was 900 grams and his Apgar score was 5 at 1 minute and 8 at 5 minutes. He has been referred to high-risk follow-up at the hospital due to his prematurity and his increased risk for developmental delays. He has no known genetic disorders or other medical conditions. He lives with his parents and an older sibling. His parents are interested in participating in the study and have a smartphone with a camera to record his spontaneous movements.

A 42-year-old man was diagnosed with HIV infection 5 years ago and has been receiving highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for the last 4 years. During a routine checkup, he was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma, which has been treated with chemotherapy. However, the cancer has relapsed and now he is being considered for hematopoietic cell therapy (HCT). His viral load has decreased to less than 5000 copies/ml plasma on HAART therapy. He is currently taking his medications as prescribed and has a good adherence history. He has been approved for an allogenic regimen at the Patient Care Conference. The donor could be either allogeneic or autologous gene modified cells.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a history of Crohn's disease. She has been experiencing abdominal pain and cramps, and her gastroenterologist has recommended a small bowel capsule endoscopy. She has not had any previous gastric or small bowel surgeries, and she is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not on any prokinetic agents and does not have any known allergies to medications. Her renal function is normal. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 26-year-old male was diagnosed with high-grade soft tissue sarcoma of the left leg, which was confirmed by biopsy. The tumor is measurable and is located in the extremities. The patient underwent limb-sparing surgery and received involved-field irradiation using megavoltage equipment with an electron boost. There was no evidence of metastasis to the CNS. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy for soft tissue sarcoma. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial and has been randomized to receive either adjuvant treatment with doxorubicin and ifosfamide with mesna (with G-CSF) for five cycles beginning post-operatively or observation. The patient has a performance status of ECOG 1 and a life expectancy of at least 8 weeks. The patient has a normal hematopoietic system with ANC greater than 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin greater than 9.0 g/dL, and platelet count greater than 50,000/mm3. The patient has normal hepatic and renal function, with bilirubin less than 2.0 mg/dL and creatinine less than 1.5 mg/dL. The patient has no major disorders of the cardiovascular or pulmonary system. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is HIV negative. The patient is eligible to participate in this clinical trial.

A 35-year-old male patient is admitted to the hospital after a severe head injury sustained from a motor vehicle accident. The patient was not wearing a helmet at the time of the accident and was found unconscious at the scene. The patient is currently comatose with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 5, indicating severe brain damage. The treating physician has determined that targeted temperature management will be initiated to prevent further brain damage. The patient does not have any known esophageal deformity or esophageal trauma, nor has the patient ingested any acidic or caustic poisons within the prior 24 hours. The patient weighs 70 kg and has no known allergies. The patient has no history of achalasia, swallowing disorders, or esophagectomy. The patient has not been diagnosed with cirrhosis or esophageal varices. The patient has no history of severe cardiac conditions requiring pacing. The patient does not have a "do not resuscitate order" or terminal disease that could lead to early-onset therapeutic withdrawal.

A 45-year-old male patient who was recently diagnosed with prediabetes is interested in participating in this clinical trial. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes and is concerned about developing the disease himself. His BMI is 28 and he has been trying to lose weight through diet and exercise but has not been successful so far. He works a desk job and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, liver dysfunction, or any other severe diseases. He does not smoke or drink alcohol but admits to having a sweet tooth. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to follow the exercise and diet plan recommended by the research team. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who underwent total hip arthroplasty 5 years ago due to osteoarthritis. He has experienced pain and loss of function in his hip for several years prior to the surgery. Following the procedure, he had a good recovery and was able to return to his normal activities. However, he started to experience pain and swelling around his hip joint a few months ago. He was diagnosed with chronic infection of his hip prosthesis and has been referred for implant exchange. He has no known allergies or medical conditions and is currently taking acetaminophen for pain relief. He is employed full-time and has health insurance coverage. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed informed consent. He has been counseled on the importance of effective contraception during the study period.

A 32-year-old male was diagnosed with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma 4 years ago. He completed curative intent first line treatment with anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and has been in complete remission for the past 3 years. He has been experiencing sexual dysfunction, including decreased libido and erectile dysfunction, for the past year. His last physical exam and lab study showed the results bellow: A well-nourished man, non-icteric, cooperative and alert Weight: 78 kg Height: 183 BP: 120/80 HR: 80/min RR: 18/min Testosterone level: 7.2 nmol/L EORTC Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 (QLQ C30) score: 50 EORTC Sexual Health Questionnaire 22 (SHQ-22) score: 40 International Index of Erectile Function with 5 questions (IIEF-5) score: 12 He is literate in Danish and has no known allergies to additives in Testogel.

The patient is a 35-year-old morbidly obese male who has undergone Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) surgery. He has a BMI of 45 and has struggled with obesity for most of his adult life. He has no significant medical history besides his obesity and has not been diagnosed with any psychiatric illnesses. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He is fluent in German and has a good understanding of the procedures and risks associated with the study. He is willing to adhere to the protocol and sign the consent form, which includes dietary and physical restrictions such as avoiding alcohol and xanthine-containing liquids, having an identical dinner the night before the study sessions, and refraining from strenuous exercise for 24 hours before each treatment. He is independently mobile and does not have any significant cognitive or communication issues. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and has not consumed high fiber diets or supplements. He is not allergic to any foods and does not have any dietary restrictions.

A 27-year-old female, who has been wearing glasses for the past 5 years, is interested in participating in the study. She has a stable prescription with a mild to moderate myopia of -3.75 D in both eyes and astigmatism of -1.50 D in her right eye and -1.25 D in her left eye. She has had no previous corneal surgery and has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 30 days. Her overall ocular health is good, and she has no known ocular diseases or corneal abnormalities. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study. She is capable of following all study procedures and is willing to undergo bilateral PRK surgery for the correction of her myopia.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 5 years. She experiences joint pain and stiffness, particularly in her hands and feet, which makes it difficult for her to perform daily activities such as cooking, cleaning, and typing on a computer. She has been prescribed various medications to manage her symptoms, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. Despite treatment, she still experiences some level of pain and limitation in her daily life. She speaks French as her primary language and would like to participate in a study to help validate a French version of the Health Assessment Questionnaire II (HAQ-II) for rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient is a 26-year-old pregnant woman who is in labor and admitted to the maternity ward in Medellin, Colombia. She is a first-time mother and is currently at 38 weeks of gestation. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has not used any form of contraception in the past. She is interested in using a highly effective form of contraception after delivery but is unsure which method is best for her. She has no significant medical history or allergies to medications. The patient speaks Spanish as her primary language and is willing to participate in a study that aims to improve postpartum contraceptive counseling and provision in the maternity care setting. She is willing to be contacted for follow-up visits at 6-8 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer after presenting with difficulty passing urine and frequent urination. He underwent a prostate biopsy which confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a maximal tumour length of 8mm. He has no history of diabetes and has never taken metformin before. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril and amlodipine for control. His past medical history is otherwise non-significant. He is scheduled for a radical prostatectomy as the treatment of choice. His ECOG performance status is 0. His haemoglobin level is 12.5g/dL, absolute neutrophil count is 3.5x109/L, platelet count is 180x109/L, renal function with an eGFR of 82 ml/min (calculated by Cockcroft Gault), AST and ALT are within normal limits and total bilirubin is 0.7mg/dL. He is able to swallow the drug and agrees to comply with the study requirements.

A 14-year-old girl presents with difficulty in managing her blood glucose levels due to severe insulin resistance and complete insulin deficiency. She was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus two years ago, and her insulin dosage is several times that of other children her age with type 1 diabetes. The patient was also diagnosed with panniculitis associated acquired lipodystrophy syndrome, characterized by inflammatory infiltration and subcutaneous fat deficiency. Genetic testing excluded congenital lipodystrophy syndrome, and her leptin levels were found to be low. She has no nutritional deficiency or catabolism, and autoantibodies were present. The patient has no history of HIV, HBV, or HCV, and is not currently in the active period of infection. She does not have any active malignant tumors or fatal diseases, nor does she have any mental or psychological disorders. The patient is eligible for the study, which aims to evaluate the effectiveness of cyclophosphamide in improving insulin resistance and glucose metabolism in patients with panniculitis associated acquired lipodystrophy syndrome and type 1 diabetes.

The patient is a 65 year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 4 years ago. He underwent a radical prostatectomy and was treated with adjuvant radiation therapy. His PSA level was initially undetectable after the surgery and radiation but has been rising steadily over the past year. His most recent PSA level was 15 ng/mL. He has no history of bone pain or fractures. He has been on intermittent androgen deprivation therapy for the past 3 years. At baseline, his testosterone level is < 50 ng/dL. He has not received prior treatment with taxane-based chemotherapy for prostate cancer, but has been treated with abiraterone and enzalutamide. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history. He is married, retired, and lives with his wife. He has no history of substance abuse. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for 6 months after the last dose of study drug.

62-year-old female with a history of smoking and chronic bronchitis who was referred for a bronchoscopy due to persistent cough and shortness of breath. The patient was diagnosed with bronchitis 10 years ago and has been on inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators since then. She reports occasional wheezing and chest tightness despite the medications. She has no history of significant allergies or adverse reactions to anesthesia, but reports occasional alcohol consumption. Her past medical history includes hypertension, which is controlled with medication, and no surgical history. The patient is an ASA grade II and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss for the past 6 months. His CDAI score and SES-CD indicate that he has active Crohn's disease. He has already tried budesonide, systemic corticosteroids, and immunosuppressants (azathiopurine, 6-mercaptopurine, or methotrexate), but none of these treatments have been effective. He has not been treated with any biologics or integrin antagonists. He is willing to use an approved contraceptive method during the study. He has not received prior treatment with mongersen (GED-0301) and has not participated in any clinical study involving mongersen (GED-0301). He is willing to comply with all study requirements and attend all study visits.
