The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with stage III colon cancer. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy every three weeks and has a baseline hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications other than those prescribed for his cancer treatment. He has no history of hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, or thrombosis. He has not received any transfusions of white blood cells or packed red blood cells within the last 28 days. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with study requirements. He is a retired accountant and is married with two adult children. He enjoys playing golf and reading in his spare time.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl who attends a school where head lice infestation is common. She has been experiencing severe itching and has found live lice in her hair during routine checks by her parents. The patient's hair is long and thick, measuring at least 3 cm in length. The patient has not used any chemical head lice treatment in the past 7 days and has not taken any antibiotics in the past week. The patient has no open wounds or skin irritation in the treatment area. The patient's parent or guardian has given written informed consent for the patient to participate in the trial. The patient has no known allergies to any of the gel's components. The patient is able to be combed with a fine comb dense ASSY2000.

52-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on maintenance hemodialysis for the past 2 years. He has been receiving hemodialysis 3 times a week for 4 hours each session through an arteriovenous fistula. His current dialyzer has a KUF of 45 mL/hr/mmHg and a surface area of 1.8 square meters. He has no history of recent hospitalization or blood transfusion, and has not participated in any other clinical investigation in the past 12 weeks. The patient has no known infections, inflammation, or surgery in the past 12 weeks. He has no history of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or human immunodeficiency virus. The patient is able to understand the informed consent form and has provided written consent to participate in the study.

A 25-year-old man was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection based on a positive lab test. He has never received antiretroviral treatment before and has a viral load of over 1000 copies/ml. His physician has prescribed him NNRTI plus two NRTIs as his first-line ART treatment. He initiated the treatment between February 1 and April 30, 2017. He has completed follow-up from baseline for at least 96 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He is currently not infected with HIV-2. He doesn't have any comorbidities and is not on any concomitant medication.

A 42-year-old woman is admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) due to severe pneumonia. She is intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and a previous episode of pneumonia. She is currently receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics and sedation. The patient is awake and cooperative with no behavioral agitation. She has no history of neuromuscular disorders. The patient is of African American ethnicity, is 5'7" tall and weighs 176 lbs. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient is eligible for the study as she requires invasive mechanical ventilation.

A 50-year-old female with a 5-year history of rheumatoid arthritis was previously enrolled in study D4300C00008 and has been taking fostamatinib as part of her treatment for 6 months. She reports improvement in her symptoms and is able to carry out daily activities with less difficulty. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is married and has two children. She works as an accountant and is able to complete her job responsibilities without difficulty. She has no known allergies to any medication. She is willing to participate in the long-term study to assess the safety and tolerability of fostamatinib in patients with rheumatoid arthritis in Asia.

A 32-year old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident and was brought to the emergency department (ED) with multiple injuries. He was initially conscious, but his condition deteriorated rapidly and he was intubated for mechanical ventilation. The patient has a history of hypertension and is a smoker. He is currently unemployed and lives alone. On examination, the patient has multiple fractures, including a femur fracture, and a head injury. His blood pressure is low and he requires vasopressors to maintain his blood pressure. The trauma team has activated and he will be transferred to the ICU for further management. As he requires intubation for mechanical ventilation, he will be eligible for the clinical trial investigating the effect of etomidate on outcomes of trauma patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with CD20 positive diffuse large b-cell lymphoma. He is currently undergoing treatment with systemic rituximab in combination with CHOP, CHOEP, or EPOCH. He has been deemed to be at high risk of CNS relapse and is eligible for central nervous system prophylaxis with intrathecal therapy. The patient has no history of spinal surgery and is eligible for intrathecal injections. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment. The patient has a good overall health status with no significant comorbidities. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 62-year-old man with a clinically-confirmed diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson disease is interested in participating in the study. He is fluent in English and willing to provide informed consent. He is retired and lives with his wife in a rural area that is far from any movement disorder specialist centers. He experiences motor symptoms that fluctuate throughout the day and would like a more continuous monitoring system to track his symptoms. He takes medication for PD and has no history of deep brain stimulation. He has no cognitive deficits and is able to follow instructions. He is excited to participate in the study and help improve outcomes for PD patients who do not have easy access to movement disorder specialists.

The patient is a 15-year-old girl attending a boarding school in the Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra, India. She is generally healthy but complains of feeling tired and weak often. She has light menstrual periods and has experienced occasional dizziness. Her hemoglobin level is found to be 10.5 g/dL (normal range: 12-15.5g/dL) and her serum ferritin is 15ng/mL (normal range: 12-150 ng/mL). She is diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia and is eligible for the Feeding Trial of Bio-fortified Pearl Millet. She is not taking any iron supplements or medications that could interfere with iron absorption, and has no chronic illnesses.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who suffers from non-septic knee arthritis diagnosed as rheumatoid arthritis according to the ACR-EULAR criteria. She has not received any biologic treatment nor conventional DMARD for the last 6 months. Corticosteroids, colchicine, and NSAIDs have been stopped for at least 24 hours prior to inclusion. She has no history of septic arthritis. She experiences pain, swelling, and stiffness in her affected knee, which has limited her mobility and daily activities. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that examines the effectiveness of local cryotherapy in reducing inflammation and pain in non-septic knee arthritis.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with stage IV metastatic cancer. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation treatments, but his cancer has continued to progress. He is experiencing extreme fatigue, weight loss, and pain. His performance status is ECOG 2. He has a supportive family and is willing to try new treatments to fight his cancer. He has no history of adult asthma, emphysema, pulmonary insufficiency, or pulmonary edema. He has not been diagnosed with AIDS or positive HIV serology. He is not pregnant.

A 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and is seeking treatment options. He has a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection and is currently being treated for cirrhosis of the liver. The patient has undergone ultrasound scanning, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans to determine the extent of the disease. However, the changes in liver structure resulting from cirrhosis have made it difficult to identify the HCC. The patient is now interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves functional imaging using Ga-68-PSMA and F-18-FDG. He hopes that this test will provide a complete picture of the extent of the disease and enable him to make a more informed decision about his treatment options. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the study and is willing to participate.

A 32-year old active duty service member, who is currently 10 weeks pregnant, received a single dose of BioThrax® vaccine during a routine military deployment. She has no medical history of note and is not taking any medications. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated so far, and she plans to continue with routine prenatal care. She has no known allergies to vaccines or other medications. She is currently stationed at a military base in the United States and is willing to participate in the BioThrax® (Anthrax) Vaccine in Pregnancy Registry study to contribute to the understanding of the potential effects of the vaccine on maternal, pregnancy, or infant health outcomes. The patient is aware that her participation in the study will involve completing several surveys over the course of her pregnancy, and her infant's health will be monitored up to one year of age. She is willing to provide informed consent for her participation in the study.

A 62-year-old man who is a retired construction worker has a history of smoking for 40 years. He was diagnosed with COPD two years ago after a persistent cough and shortness of breath. He has been attending primary health care clinics for regular check-ups and medication refills. He experiences shortness of breath with minimal exertion, and he has difficulty sleeping due to coughing. He takes his inhalers regularly but sometimes forgets to use them. He lives alone and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has been hospitalized once for exacerbation of COPD in the past year. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his quality of life and control of his COPD.

This is a 62 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma after presenting with fatigue, night sweats, and unexplained weight loss. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and the patient received 6 cycles of CHOP therapy. The patient achieved an unconfirmed partial remission and is now being considered for the Yt90-Zevalin therapy clinical trial. The patient's performance status is Zubrod 1 and they have measurable disease. The patient has no evidence of CNS involvement by lymphoma and they have not had prior antibody therapy for lymphoma. The patient has not had any previous antineoplastic treatment other than CHOP for the initial treatment of DLBCL. The patient's serum creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits and they do not have any active uncontrolled infections. The patient's platelet and neutrophil counts are within acceptable ranges for the trial. The patient has provided

We are looking for adolescent participants between the ages of 12 and 17 who experience an average of 3 to 12 migraine headaches per month and whose initial onset of migraine headaches was at least 12 months prior to screening. Participants should weigh between 77 lbs and 220 lbs and be generally healthy based on the results of a medical history, physical examination, 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), and laboratory profile. Participants must not have a history of allergic reaction or sensitivity to valproate or similar drugs, a history of noncompliance with medication or medical instructions, a history of cluster headaches, seizure disorder, or suspected history of seizure disorder, and must not have failed more than 2 adequate regimens of prophylactic antimigraine medications. Females of childbearing potential must be using an effective method of birth control. Participants must not be using any prophylactic antimigraine medication within a period equivalent to less than 5 half-lives of that medication before entering the Baseline Phase, nor can they use any analgesic, ergotamine preparation, or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agent. Participants must not use aspirin and/or any aspirin-containing product within 5 half-lives prior to randomization or at any time during the Experimental Phase of the study. They must not have received an investigational drug within 30 days prior to study drug administration or scheduled to receive any other investigational drug anytime during the study. Participants must not exhibit any of the ineligibility criteria during the Experimental Phase of the study.

This clinical trial is looking for women in Burkina Faso who are of reproductive age between 15 and 49 years old, residing in rural areas, and living in villages with limited access to electricity. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a mass media family planning campaign, which includes radio campaigns to encourage the use of contraception methods. The women participating in the trial will be randomly assigned to receive the media campaign or not. The trial will measure the impact of the campaign on total and modern contraceptive prevalence rates, perceptions of family planning, contraception-related behavior, and general gender norms. The study will be conducted in villages that are more than 5 km away from the radio stations, which are the source of the campaign to limit the overlap between treatment and control groups. The campaign will focus on financial and health benefits of family planning, and information on the different types, sources, advantages, and disadvantages of different contraceptive methods. The study will involve a household listing survey, village survey, and clinics survey to monitor the demand and supply of contraceptive methods in different areas. The study will be conducted by Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA), an NGO specializing in conducting randomized control trials with experience in Burkina Faso. The women participating in the trial will be selected randomly and invited to take the baseline survey and a follow-up survey three years later. The trial is powered to detect a minimum of 6 percentage points increase in the modern contraceptive prevalence rate.

Patient A is a 25-year-old male who has been struggling with cocaine addiction for the past year. He has attempted to quit using cocaine on his own several times, but has been unsuccessful. He currently uses cocaine at least twice a week and spends approximately $400 a month on the drug. He has no other substance abuse issues and is a non-smoker. Patient A is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help him overcome his addiction. He has no significant medical history and has not taken any medications that could interfere with the study. He is aware that he will be receiving either a low-dose or high-dose modafinil, or a placebo, and will also receive cognitive behavioral therapy throughout the study. He agrees to comply with all study procedures and will use an effective method of birth control during the study period, as he is sexually active.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of schizophrenia for the past 5 years. She was initially diagnosed after experiencing hallucinations and delusions, and has been on antipsychotic medication since then. She is currently taking risperidone 4mg daily and has been stable on this medication for the past year. She has no other psychiatric diagnoses and is considered reliable and capable of performing all study procedures. She is willing to use an effective method of birth control and has tested negative for pregnancy. She lives with her parents and is currently not employed. She has no history of participating in a clinical trial involving an investigational product or non-approved use of a drug or device. She understands the nature of the study and has given her informed consent. She has no current or past medical history of seizures, leucopenia, uncontrolled diabetes, liver or renal insufficiency, or thyroid disorder. She has not had electroconvulsive therapy within the past 3 months and is negative for Hepatitis B and C.

As this is an observational study, there are no eligibility criteria for patients to enroll in this clinical trial. However, the study focuses on Asian-Pacific Chinese and Japanese sibling pairs who have been diagnosed with hypertension. Therefore, siblings of Asian-Pacific Chinese or Japanese origin who have been diagnosed with hypertension may be eligible to participate in this clinical trial. The study aims to map the major genetic loci underlying hypertension in this population, and will use linkage analysis and candidate gene approach to identify the genes for hypertension. The study will also investigate intermediate phenotypes related to hypertension pathophysiology, such as renin, Ang II, and endothelin, to identify more homogeneous subgroups of hypertension. Participants will be asked to provide their medical history, undergo physical examination, and provide blood and urine samples. The study does not involve any intervention or treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years. She presents with complaints of frequent urination, thirst, and fatigue. Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She takes medications for these conditions, including lisinopril and atorvastatin. She has no history of bone fractures, osteoporosis, or other bone-related disorders. Her current laboratory results show an HbA1c level of 7.2%, total cholesterol of 190 mg/dL, triglycerides of 150 mg/dL, LDL cholesterol of 110 mg/dL, and HDL cholesterol of 45 mg/dL. She is eligible for the clinical trial because she meets the inclusion criteria of being a resident of Western Mexico with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus of at least 5 years of evolution and is willing to sign an informed consent letter. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the trial.

A 58 year old male complains of chest pain that started 2 hours ago. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but he is not on any medications. He denies any history of heart disease or previous chest pain. Physical examination reveals normal vital signs with no significant findings except for mild tenderness on palpation of the chest. EKG shows ST-segment elevation in leads V1 to V6. He is diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and is immediately taken to the catheterization lab for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The culprit artery is found to be the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and is occluded at the time of admission coronary angiography. The patient is given preliminary oral informed consent and is asked to sign the informed consent form as soon as possible.

A 35-year-old male came to the clinic complaining of persistent pain in his left elbow after a previous traumatic injury. He had a history of a distal humerus fracture that was repaired surgically in 2014. He reported difficulty in extending his arm fully and experienced pain when performing daily activities such as lifting and gripping objects. His medical history was remarkable for gout, for which he was taking allopurinol. He denied having diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, or any other chronic illnesses. His BMI was 28. His serum uric acid levels were monitored regularly and were within the normal range. The X-ray of his elbow joint showed evidence of heterotopic ossification. He was interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the relationship between heterotopic ossification and serum uric acid levels.

A 53-year-old man was admitted to the ICU after experiencing a heart attack. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. He underwent a coronary angioplasty procedure and is currently on mechanical ventilation. He has been in the ICU for 3 days and has been sedated with propofol. The medical team is concerned about his level of wakefulness and cognition, and has decided to start him on modafinil to promote wakefulness and improve cognitive function. He has not received modafinil before and has no known allergies to any medications. He is married and has two adult children. He works as an engineer and enjoys spending time outdoors.

John is a 54-year-old male who presented to the emergency room with chest pain within 24 hours. ECG revealed ST elevation, and he was diagnosed with an acute coronary syndrome. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He has no known drug allergies. He has never been treated with anticoagulants or thrombolytic agents. He has not received glycoprotein IIb-IIIa inhibitors. He has no history of bleeding or clotting disorders. His platelet count is within normal range (150,000-450,000 cells/mm3), and his hemoglobin level is normal (13.5 g/L). He has a normal liver and renal function. He has no history of cardiac shock or severe left ventricular dysfunction. He has no sick sinus syndrome or second-degree AV block without a permanent pacemaker. He is not currently taking any cytochrome p450 3a inhibitors or enhancers. He is mentally stable and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up requirements. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has not participated in any drug studies in the previous three months.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from hand and foot eczema for the past two years. Her eczema is moderate to severe, with intense itching, redness, and flaking of the skin. She has tried several topical corticosteroids and moisturizers, but they have not provided lasting relief. She works as a nurse and frequently washes her hands, which exacerbates her condition. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she is in generally good health. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is capable of understanding and providing a signed informed consent. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use an approved method of birth control during the study period. She has not used any topical or systemic medications for her eczema in the past eight weeks. She is willing to make frequent visits to the study center as an outpatient.

56-year-old woman with sudden hearing loss in her right ear that occurred 14 days ago. She underwent initial systemic prednisolone therapy, but her hearing threshold did not recover sufficiently. There is no history of middle ear inflammation, ear canal inflammation, or conductive hearing loss. She has no history of ototoxic treatment and is not currently taking any experimental drugs or participating in any clinical studies. She has not had any previous otologic surgeries, and there is no presence of conditions or symptoms that indicate that her hearing loss is not ISSNHL. She has no history of drug abuse or alcoholism and no history of an ischemic disorder. The patient is capable of understanding the informed consent form and has signed it. She has no psychiatric syndrome requiring treatment with neuroleptics, antidepressants, hypnotics, or anxiolytics.

A 22-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 8 years and has been using B-adrenergic agonist and anti-inflammatory medications for more than 6 months. She is in good health except for her asthma and does not suffer from any chronic condition that might affect her respiratory function. She has had a chest X-ray within the last 12 months, which was not diagnostic of any respiratory disease. She is willing and able to comply with study procedures and visit schedules and is capable of completing daily diary cards and medical event calendars. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is not currently participating in any other clinical trial, except for Sepracor studies 051-353 or 051-355. She has never been hospitalized for asthma in the past 45 days, and she is not scheduled for any in-patient hospitalization or elective surgery during the trial. She has no known sensitivity to levalbuterol or racemic albuterol, and she is not using any prescription drug with which albuterol sulfate is contraindicated. She has no history of cancer or any other chronic condition that might interfere with the successful completion of the study.

57-year-old woman with a history of hepatitis B and cirrhosis, who is scheduled for a living donor liver transplantation. The patient has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medication. The patient has no known history of renal dysfunction, and laboratory tests indicate normal renal function. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meet all the inclusion criteria. The patient has no history of severe cerebral artery disease or severe cardio-pulmonary disease. The patient is informed about the procedures involved and the potential risks and benefits of the study and provides written informed consent.

A 57-year-old man was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit smoking 5 years ago. He is married and works as a construction worker. He has no significant past medical history except for high blood pressure which is well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies. He underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the rectum. The immunohistochemical analysis of the biopsy showed epidermal growth factor receptor expression. Imaging studies showed one index lesion that is bi-dimensionally measurable. He has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy for the treatment of colorectal cancer before. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the study protocol.

A 50-year-old man was admitted to the hospital after experiencing a sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. He was diagnosed with a left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke based on his symptoms and a CT scan. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication regularly. He is married and has two children. He is a former smoker, quitting five years ago, and he drinks alcohol socially. On examination, he has a right hemiparesis with a Medical Research Council (MRC) score of 3/5 in the upper and lower extremities. He has dysarthria and a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. Brain MRI confirms the diagnosis of ischemic stroke. He is able to communicate with the examiner and understands the purpose of the study. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer and undergoing chemotherapy treatment at the Department of Internal Medicine V (Hematology and Oncology) of the University Hospital of Innsbruck was invited to participate in a clinical trial investigating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cancer patients' quality of life. He lives alone, is retired, and spends most of his time at home due to his treatment. He has been feeling anxious and worried since the onset of the pandemic and is concerned about his increased risk of contracting COVID-19 due to his cancer and weakened immune system. He has been following the guidelines and recommendations of his healthcare providers to stay safe, but he still feels uncertain about the future. He agreed to participate in the study to help researchers better understand the experiences of cancer patients during this time and to potentially help develop interventions to improve their quality of life.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who lives 4 km away from school. She has been commuting to school passively for the last 6 months and owns a bike. She has no history of any chronic medical conditions and is generally healthy. Her BMI is within the normal range for her age and height, and she is not currently taking any medications. She has no history of regular physical activity but is willing to start cycling to school as part of the study. Her parents have given written consent for her participation in the trial.

A 52-year-old female patient who has been edentulous for the past 5 years is seeking treatment for complete dentures. She complains of difficulty eating and speaking due to the absence of teeth. She has no history of systemic diseases and is not allergic to resins. She has a healthy oral cavity with no pathological changes of residual ridges. She is cooperative and willing to participate in the clinical trial. She has not undergone any previous dental treatment and is not experiencing xerostomia.

A 30-year-old female with a BMI of 24.5 comes to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is in good health, does not smoke, and is not currently taking any medication or supplements. She is physically active, but only exercises for 3 hours per week. The patient reports no significant changes in weight in the past 3 months and is not currently dieting for weight loss. She does not consume more than 20 grams of alcohol per day. The patient is interested in participating in a study investigating the postprandial response of fresh-squeezed and processed orange juice in lean and obese subjects. She is willing to consume different beverages and to record all meals throughout the day. The patient understands the study's purpose and is willing to have blood samples taken at several times throughout the day. She meets all of the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 58 year-old male who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past 6 months. His MRI reveals significant degenerative changes at the L4-L5 and L5-S1 levels, and he has been recommended to undergo thoracic and/or lumbar spine fusion surgery at Oregon Health and Science University. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He does not have any history of smoking or alcohol consumption. He is currently taking acetaminophen for pain relief. He has no history of chronic steroid use, is not pregnant, not decisionally impaired, and not a prisoner.

A male neonate who was born at 38 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 2,200 g. The baby was delivered via emergency cesarean section due to fetal distress. Following delivery, the baby had a low Apgar score of 3 at 1 minute and 5 at 5 minutes. The baby was resuscitated for 10 minutes and later admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) for moderate encephalopathy. The baby underwent therapeutic hypothermia therapy for 72 hours continuously. The baby is now 10 days old and has been diagnosed with hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy. The baby's parents have received adequate information about the study and have voluntarily given their consent to include their child in the trial. The baby has no known congenital abnormalities or chromosomal anomalies, and there are no plans for surgery or radiation therapy. The baby's blood glucose level is normal, and there is no evidence of active or severe infection. The baby meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage 2 non-Hodgkin's lymphoma six months ago. She underwent chemotherapy and achieved complete remission. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is managed with levothyroxine. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0. Her actual body weight is within the ideal body weight range. She is planning to undergo an autologous peripheral hematopoietic stem cell transplant. She has not undergone any previous stem cell collections. Her bone marrow lymphoma cells involvement is less than 20%, as assessed by bone marrow biopsy within 4 months before signing the informed consent form. She does not have active central nervous system involvement and has fully recovered from all acute toxic effects of prior chemotherapy. She is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception from Day 1 through ≥3 months following plerixafor treatment.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing leg cramps during her sleep for the past few months. The cramps are painful, causing her to wake up several times at night, and she has difficulty in moving her leg, which affects her quality of sleep. She has no known history of mental disorders, renal or liver function impairment, or any known serious organic disease. She is not currently taking any medication for her leg cramps. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of herbal medicine in relieving her leg cramps. She is able to fill out the VAS for leg cramp and is willing to provide written informed consent. She is referred to the Yan Oi Tong Mrs Shirley W K Siu Medical Centre for screening and possible enrolment in the study.

As this clinical trial does not have any particular inclusion or exclusion criteria, it is not necessary to generate a patient description. However, potential participants may include individuals with a diagnosis of schizophrenia or Parkinson's disease who have experienced hallucinations.

32-year-old female with a documented history of acute intermittent porphyria with 8 or more acute attacks per year. The patient has been on preventive heme therapy for the past 2 years but has experienced 3 acute attacks in the last 6 months. Hemoglobin levels have been stable at 12 g/dL for the last 6 months. The patient has no other significant medical history, is not pregnant, and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. Urinary porphobilinogen levels during acute symptoms have been at least 20 mg/24 hours. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to tin mesoporphyrin or any intravenous heme preparation, and does not have any conditions that may increase the risk of participation in the study. The patient is willing to avoid sunlight during treatment and for 2 months thereafter.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian male who has been diagnosed with lentigo maligna (LM) in situ on his forehead. The lesion has been biopsied and confirmed by a dermatologist. The patient has a history of sun exposure and fair skin. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has no known allergies. The patient has been referred to a Mohs micrographic surgeon for treatment of the LM. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study as the location of the LM is appropriate for Mohs surgery and he is able to tolerate surgery. He is willing to comply with all appointments including follow-up appointments and is able to understand and sign a written informed consent document.

Pt is an 80yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis who presented to the emergency department after a fall at home. Imaging revealed a left intertrochanteric hip fracture with no other injuries. The patient is scheduled to undergo intramedullary nailing for intertrochanteric fracture in the next 48 hours. The patient is on lisinopril and atorvastatin for his hypertension and hyperlipidemia, respectively, but is not on any medications contraindicated with tranexamic acid. The patient has no prior history of prothrombotic state, cardiac stent, mechanical heart valves, deep vein thrombosis, aortic stenosis, kidney dialysis, or malignancy. The patient speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast 3 years ago. She underwent a left breast lumpectomy, sentinel lymph node biopsy, followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide, and adjuvant radiation therapy. She is currently receiving adjuvant hormonal therapy with tamoxifen. She had no recurrence or metastatic lesions until her last follow-up visit, where she complained of fatigue and abdominal discomfort. A CT scan revealed multiple liver, lung, and bone metastases. She underwent a biopsy of the liver, and the pathology report confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer. The HER-2 status of her primary tumor was negative, but HER-2 positive circulating tumor cells were detected in her blood sample. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal organ function. She has no history of other malignancies or significant comorbidities. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understand the potential risks and benefits of the study.

A 28-year-old female contact lens wearer visited the clinic complaining of mild to moderate dry eye symptoms. She has been wearing contact lenses for 5 years and usually experiences discomfort after 4-5 hours of use. She has no known ocular or systemic diseases and has not undergone any ocular surgery in the past 3 months. She has not used topical cyclosporine before and is willing to provide informed consent and participate in all study visits.

The patient is a 54-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of KRAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). He has undergone first-line oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy for mCRC for over 3 months but has shown signs of progressive disease. The patient has measurable disease per modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors Version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has not received prior treatment with irinotecan or an investigational or approved human epidermal growth factor receptor (HER)-targeted agent. The patient's last anti-tumor therapy was completed more than 4 weeks prior to Cycle 1, Day 1. The patient does not have leptomeningeal disease, active infection requiring intravenous antibiotics or untreated/active central nervous system metastases. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any malignancies other than colorectal cancer within the last 5 years, except for adequately treated basal or squamous cell skin cancer and carcinoma in situ of the cervix.

A 45-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain that radiates to her left arm and jaw. She reports feeling short of breath and nauseous. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no prior history of myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization. Electrocardiogram shows ST segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Troponin levels are elevated. She is diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome with ST segment elevation and is scheduled for urgent coronary angiography. She agrees to participate in the Stent For Life Observatory study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing pelvic pain and discomfort during her menstrual periods for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with endometrioma on her left ovary by transvaginal ultrasound with a diameter of 3.5 cm. She has regular menstrual cycles and has not had any previous ovarian surgery. She is not currently taking any hormonal medications and does not have any endocrinal diseases affecting ovarian function. The patient is interested in undergoing laparoscopic surgery to remove the endometrioma and improve her symptoms. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate. She understands the risks and benefits of both laparoscopic ovarian cystectomy and laparoscopic cyst deroofing and is comfortable with being randomized into either study group. She is willing to undergo pre-operative and post-operative measurements of AMH, AFC, and ovarian volume.

This is a 1-year-old male infant with a history of Pierre Robin syndrome. The patient has a small chin (micrognathia) and a cleft palate, which can make it difficult for the infant to breathe and eat. The patient has undergone surgical correction of the cleft palate but still has a difficult airway due to the small chin. The infant is scheduled to undergo a procedure that requires general anesthesia and endotracheal intubation. The anesthesia team will need to intubate the infant with one of three different intubation devices (Miller blade, Truview VL, or Glidescope Cobalt video-laryngoscope) to ensure safe and effective ventilation during the procedure. This study aims to determine which device is most effective for intubating pediatric patients with difficult airways, such as those with Pierre Robin syndrome.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who has been experiencing occasional dizziness and difficulty maintaining balance. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are under control with medication. He has no neurological disorders such as Parkinson's, stroke, or multiple sclerosis. His Berg Balance Scale score is 24 and he has a minimum head velocity of 200°/s on the dynamic visual acuity test. He is an active individual who enjoys walking and light exercise, but he is worried about his balance and has recently cut back on his activities. He is interested in participating in this study to improve his balance and gait performance. He owns a smartphone and has some experience with computer-based technology. He is willing to commit to attending the required sessions and completing the exercises as instructed.

7yo boy with a history of seasonal allergies and occasional allergic rhinitis. He has been previously treated with over-the-counter antihistamines with good symptom relief. The boy and his parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the taste acceptability of two commonly prescribed allergy medications. The boy is in good health and not currently taking any medications or supplements.

This is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with cirrhosis two years ago. She has been experiencing muscle cramps, particularly in her legs, for the past few months. These cramps have been negatively impacting her quality of life and interfering with her daily activities. She has tried stretching exercises and over-the-counter pain relievers but has not experienced any significant relief. She is currently stable and ambulatory, and her MELD score is 17 with a platelet count of 50,000. She is able to complete a written questionnaire in English and is interested in participating in this pilot study to see if hydroxychloroquine can provide relief from her muscle cramps. She has no history of allergies to medications and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with localized prostate cancer. He has undergone radical prostatectomy six months ago and has received external beam irradiation therapy. Bone scan results have indicated no bone metastases. The patient has not received hormone ablation therapy for more than three months before or after the surgery. He has not been treated with bisphosphonates or any other drugs known to affect the skeleton within the past year. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the effect of zoledronic acid on circulating and bone marrow-residing prostate cancer cells.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with type 2 diabetes five years ago. She has a BMI of 34 and is currently taking 1.5g of metformin daily as background therapy. She has not made any changes to her diabetes treatment in the past 90 days. She has never used SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists before. She has no history of pregnancy, lactation, systemic antibiotic treatment, spironolactone use, oral contraceptive or hormonal replacement therapy use, immunosuppressive drug use, heart failure New York Heart Association III-IV, severe liver disease, or malignant disease. She is interested in participating in the study to help further the understanding of the effects of diabetes medications on adrenal function and intestinal microbiota.

A 14-year-old boy who underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation six months ago presents with chronic GVHD. His skin is affected in more than 50% of his body surface area, with lichenoid and sclerodermatous changes. He has been treated with prednisone for the past two months with no improvement in his symptoms. He has not failed more than two immunosuppressive regimens. His platelet count is low, and his onset is progressive. The patient and his family are willing to commit to regular follow-up appointments and doses of medication. He has no active infections and has a Karnofsky performance score of 70. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial.

A 36-year-old pregnant woman who is 35 weeks and 4 days gestation came to the clinic for her scheduled cesarean section. She is a primigravida with no significant medical history. She had a normal pregnancy course and has gained an appropriate amount of weight during pregnancy. She has no allergies to any medications. She is married and works as a teacher. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any drugs. She has a regular menstrual cycle and uses barrier methods of contraception. She has no history of preterm labor or any other pregnancy complications. She is excited to meet her baby and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help improve neonatal respiratory outcomes.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been struggling with cocaine dependence for the past 5 years. He has sought treatment before, but has been unsuccessful in achieving long-term abstinence. He has a history of depression and has been receiving treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) for the past year. He has no history of other substance use disorders, except for occasional alcohol and cannabis use. He is currently unemployed and lives with his girlfriend who is supportive of his efforts to quit cocaine. He has no other medical or psychiatric disorders that would interfere with participation in the study, and is willing to give informed consent. He has undergone urine testing for cocaine metabolites and has tested positive. He is a candidate for the study medication of levodopa, carbidopa and entacapone (LCE) and agrees to undergo brain imaging and participate in the outpatient treatment trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who has been trying to conceive with his partner for over a year without success. He has undergone a fertility evaluation and has been diagnosed with azoospermia, which means he has no sperm in his semen. He has no history of chemotherapy, bone marrow transplantation or radiation. He has a regular exercise routine and a healthy diet. He does not smoke, but drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known genetic syndromes. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the effect of low electrical current on testicular spermatocyte count.

A 63-year-old Caucasian man with a history of T2DM for 15 years presents with severe renal insufficiency (GFR of 20 mL/min). He has been on insulin therapy for the past 5 years. His blood sugar levels are not well-controlled despite being on a high dose of insulin. He has been experiencing frequent episodes of hypoglycemia, which has led to falls and injuries. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no known drug allergies. He has been participating in the core study and has consented to the extension study. He is compliant with his medications and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old Danish man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is currently taking metformin 1000mg twice daily for his diabetes. He reports feeling tired and sluggish lately, and has noticed his blood sugar levels have been fluctuating more than usual. He has a BMI of 28 and reports doing light exercise twice a week. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally on weekends. His family history is positive for type 2 diabetes on both sides, but negative for any other metabolic disorders. His current medication list includes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. His most recent lab work showed a 1,25OHvitD level of 45 nmol/L, indicating vitamin D insufficiency. He has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been struggling with generalized anxiety disorder for the past 4 years. She has been on various antidepressants for the past 8 weeks but has not seen any significant improvement in her symptoms. Her anxiety is affecting her daily life and she has difficulty with concentration and sleep. She has a score of 10 on the OASIS (Overall Anxiety Severity and Impairment Scale). She has no history of other psychiatric disorders, is not currently undergoing cognitive behavior therapy, and does not have any marked intellectual disability. She denies any current suicidal ideation or plan and has no history of psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, or substance abuse/dependence. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He reports feeling increasingly fatigued over the last few months, and a recent blood test showed low levels of hemoglobin and platelets. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of AML, and the patient has no prior history of cancer or chemotherapy. His physical exam is notable for pallor and mild splenomegaly. His laboratory studies showed: WBC count 32,000/μL with 70% blasts, hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL, platelet count 50,000/μL, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, AST 52 U/L, and ALT 48 U/L. The patient has no history of cardiac disease, but he does report a history of heavy alcohol use in the past. The patient has no known allergies to medications and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old Korean man who recently underwent a transrectal prostate biopsy and was diagnosed with prostate cancer. His PSA level was 8ng/ml and his biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 6. He has no symptoms related to the cancer and his clinical stage is T1. He has no history of prostate cancer or any other cancer. He is currently taking medications for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He is willing to attend follow-up visits and is interested in participating in the active surveillance program for his low-risk prostate cancer.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer. He has been on ketoconazole therapy for castration resistant prostate cancer for more than 28 days but has experienced disease progression. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and ongoing gonadal androgen deprivation therapy with LHRH analogues. He has been maintained on effective LHRH analogue therapy and his testosterone level is less than 50 ng/dL. He has evidence of metastatic disease based on a positive bone scan or objective imaging on CT scan. His PSA level has risen on at least 2 successive occasions, at least 2 weeks apart and is currently at 5 ng/ml. He has no prior therapy with chemotherapy for metastatic prostate cancer. He has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks and has no significant comorbidities. He has not received any hormonal therapy, supplements, or complementary medicines/botanicals within 4 weeks of first dose of study drug. He has completed radiation therapy more than 4 weeks prior to enrollment and has not received chemotherapy for castration resistant prostate cancer. He has a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, and his blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of myocardial infarction or congestive heart failure. He is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and is willing to participate in the study.

A 72-year-old retired teacher has been experiencing memory problems for the past 6 months. She has trouble remembering names, dates, and appointments. Sometimes she forgets where she put things or why she went to a certain place. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She also takes a low dose of aspirin for primary prevention of heart attack and stroke. She has never had any major surgery, but she has had a few minor procedures in the past, and she recovered well from them. She has no family history of dementia or other neurological disorders. She is fluent in English and can communicate well with the study team. She is interested in participating in the study to help researchers understand the relationship between brain waves and memory problems after surgery. She understands that she will need to wear a sticker on her forehead during surgery and complete cognitive and functional tests before and after surgery. She is willing to undergo these procedures to contribute to medical research.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing abdominal pain and diarrhea for the past 6 months. She has been diagnosed with IBS-D according to modified Rome III criteria. The patient has tried several over the counter medications without success. She is currently taking a probiotic and a low FODMAP diet. Her past medical history is significant for anxiety and depression, for which she has been taking sertraline 50mg daily for the past year. She is a non-smoker and her family history is negative for gastrointestinal diseases. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and she has no other significant medical history. She is willing to discontinue her current medications and follow the study protocol.

A 55-year-old male came to the clinic with difficulty swallowing solid foods, weight loss, and chest pain. He had these symptoms for the past 2 months. He works as a construction worker and has a history of smoking for 20 years, quitting 5 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no significant past medical or surgical history. Physical examination revealed no palpable masses or lymph nodes in the neck. Endoscopy was performed revealing a tumor located at 25-28 cm from the incisors, occupying the whole circumference of the esophagus, and with ulceration. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma. CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis was performed showing no evidence of distant metastasis. The tumor was deemed potentially resectable by the thoracic oncologist. He has an ECOG score of 1. His fasting blood sugar is 7.2mmol/L, and his blood pressure is controlled with antihypertensive medication. He has no other significant medical history or current medical conditions.

This clinical trial does not require recruitment of new patients. It is a long-term follow-up study of subjects who have already received at least one dose of an ACTR T cell product in an investigational or other treatment setting, such as compassionate use, named patient IND, expanded access program, or equivalent settings. Therefore, no patient description is needed.

The patient is a 65 year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of smoking, alcohol abuse, or drug abuse. She is currently taking a daily multivitamin supplement. The patient has not received any prior treatment for her breast cancer. She has no history of eye injury or corneal surgery. The patient is not currently receiving oestrogen replacement therapy. Her estimated life expectancy is greater than 12 weeks.

25-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 23 kg/m2 who is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She has no significant medical history and her vital signs, 12-lead ECG and laboratory tests are within normal limits. She is a non-smoker and does not have any history of substance abuse. She is not currently using any medications, including oral contraceptives. She has a negative pregnancy test and is not lactating. She agrees to use barrier contraception throughout the study period and for 3 months after discontinuation of treatment. She has not participated in any clinical study with an investigational drug in the last 3 months and has not donated or lost more than 500 mL of blood in the last 3 months. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for the anticipated time on study of up to 11 weeks.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She has a regular menstrual cycle and no significant medical history. Her body mass index is within the range of 18 to 29. She has both ovaries and her basal levels of estradiol and progesterone on day one of her cycle are ≤ 80 pg/ml and ≤ 1.6ng/ml respectively. Her day three FSH level is <12IU/L. She has never undergone an HSG before but is willing to have one done before starting the stimulation. The patient will be undergoing her first IUI attempt with clomiphene citrate and is interested in participating in the study to assess the effect of luteal phase supplement on her pregnancy rate.

A 32-year-old female was admitted to the hospital with a history of acute spinal cord injury (SCI) that occurred three weeks ago. She was diagnosed with a complete injury at T6 level due to a car accident. Since her admission, she has been experiencing recurrent urinary tract infections (UTI) leading to hospitalization. She has been treated with antibiotics multiple times, but her symptoms keep reoccurring. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of immunomodulation therapy with UroVaxom in preventing UTI. She is willing to take one tablet of either Uro-Vaxom or a placebo daily for 90 days and is ready to provide blood and urine samples before and after the treatment. She has no history of hypersensitivity to investigational products, immunosuppressant therapy, oncological condition or therapy, autoimmune diseases, nephropathy, bladder stones, or other therapies for preventing UTIs. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has not participated in another study with an investigational drug within the 30 days preceding the present study.

Patient is a 45-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with chest pain lasting for more than 30 minutes. The patient reported a history of hypertension and smoking. Upon examination, the patient's blood pressure was elevated, and an electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4. The patient was diagnosed with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and was immediately transferred to the cardiac catheterization laboratory for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The patient underwent successful PCI with stent placement and was started on appropriate medical therapy including aspirin, beta-blocker, and statin. The patient's hospital course was uneventful, and he was discharged home on day 3 with a plan for outpatient cardiac rehabilitation. The patient will be followed up for 12 months with regular visits to monitor his cardiac status and collect data for the STEMI registry.

A 45-year-old Japanese male who has been diagnosed with Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) and completed the 6-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group comparative trial (243-07-003) is eligible for this long-term extension trial. The patient did not experience any significant adverse events during the 6-week trial and is willing to continue the treatment with SPM 962 following once-a-daily transdermal administration within a range of 2.25 to 6.75 mg/day for up to 53 weeks. The patient has not experienced persistent hallucination or delusion during the previous trial and does not have any psychiatric conditions such as confusion, excitation, delirium, or abnormal behavior at baseline. The patient's orthostatic blood pressure is within normal limits and the patient has not had a history of epilepsy or convulsions. The patient's laboratory values are within normal limits and the patient is not planning to become pregnant during the trial.

Pt is a 35yo F with a history of mild to moderate asthma and a positive wheal reaction on skin prick testing to at least one common aeroallergen. She has a prebronchodilator FEV1 of 75% of predicted at screening and experiences both an early asthmatic response (EAR) and a late asthmatic response (LAR) to inhalational allergen challenge. Her methacholine PC20 is ≤16 mg/mL at screening. She has not used any oral, injectable, or dermal steroids within the past 3 months or inhaled steroids within the past month. She has not used cromoglycate, nedocromil, leukotriene receptor antagonists, inhibitors of 5-lipoxygenase, theophylline-containing agents, or long-acting β2-agonists within the past 4 weeks. She is not undergoing allergen desensitization therapy or immunotherapy. She has not participated in a clinical trial and has not received an investigational product within the past 30 days or 5 elimination half lives of the investigational product, whichever is longer. She provides written informed consent and is deemed suitable for entry into the study by the investigator.

A 24-year-old female presents with discomfort and pain in the lower right back of the mouth. She reports difficulty in eating and cleaning the area due to the presence of a fully-impacted lower third molar. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. On examination, the tooth is found to be fully-impacted and is causing inflammation in the surrounding gum tissue. The patient is deemed eligible for the study and is informed about the two different flap techniques that will be used during the surgical extraction. She agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form. The procedure is scheduled, and the patient is provided with instructions for pre- and post-operative care. The quality of life questionnaire is administered before the surgery, and clinical assessments are conducted at regular intervals after the surgery to evaluate the healing process.

A 32-year-old female office worker is experiencing low back pain for the past 2 months. She has no history of any systemic or musculoskeletal pathology. She has not received any physical therapy or exercise regimen for the past 3 months. She has not taken any analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for the previous week. Her pain severity ranges from 3 to 7 on the NPRS. She has not undergone any surgery, epidural injection treatment, or nerve block in the lumbosacral region. She is not pregnant or has had a recent pregnancy in the past 6 months. She has no sensory or motor deficit in the lower extremities. She does not exhibit any signs of red flags such as tumors, constitutional symptoms, integumentary issues, or cauda equina syndromes. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for Myofascial Release and Joint Mobilization Therapy in Non-Specific Low Back Pain.

Patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease and is scheduled for cardiac surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and has been on medication for several years to manage his blood pressure. The patient has no history of kidney disease and his renal function is within normal limits. The Accuryn Monitoring System will be utilized to collect data on the patient's physiologic signals before, during, and after the surgery to monitor for acute kidney injury (AKI) and hypertension. The patient will be enrolled in the Accuryn Registry Study and his data will be retrospectively and prospectively analyzed to determine any correlations between measured physiologic data and clinical outcomes. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 30 yo F who accidentally burned her hand while cooking at home. The burn is about 2 inches in diameter and is a second degree burn. The burn is not visibly infected and is not close to her eyes or genitalia. She is able to take in oral fluids and is willing to comply with the daily dressing changes. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if it can help minimize the appearance of the resulting scar.

The patient is a 78-year-old man who has sustained a cervical hip fracture after a fall at home. He has a medical history of hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia. He takes amlodipine 5mg daily and tamsulosin 0.4mg daily. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is scheduled for hip replacement surgery under spinal anesthesia. He has never had a femoral nerve block before. He reports some discomfort in his hip and thigh that interferes with his mobility. He has no significant sensory or motor deficits in his lower extremities. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 135/80 Hgb: 12 g/dl WBC: 8000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl.

The patient is a 50 year old man living in Guatemala who has been diagnosed with hypertension. Despite taking medication, his blood pressure remains high (more than 140/90 mmHg). He receives care at a government health facility and has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of a multicomponent intervention program aimed at improving hypertension control in Central America. The program will include protocol-based treatment, team-based collaborative care, BP audit and feedback, home BP monitoring, and health coaching on antihypertensive medication adherence and lifestyle modification. The program will last for 18 months, during which his blood pressure and other indicators will be measured at baseline and at months 6, 12, and 18. The primary clinical outcome is the difference in the proportion of patients with controlled BP at 18 months. The patient is excited to be a part of this trial and hopes that the program will help improve his hypertension control and overall health.

A 34-year-old female presented with a history of generalized weakness, fatigue, and intermittent abdominal pain for the past 3 years. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and hypothyroidism. She denied fever, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Her family history was negative for any genetic disorders. Physical examination revealed no significant abnormalities except for mild hypertension. Laboratory tests showed proteinuria, elevated creatinine, and low estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Further investigations, including renal biopsy and genetic testing, confirmed the diagnosis of Fabry disease. The patient was informed about the Replagal clinical trial and expressed interest in participating. She meets the inclusion criteria as a female heterozygous carrier with evidence of Fabry disease defined as a mutation in the Alpha-galactosidase A gene and clinical evidence of the disease with renal dysfunction consistent with Fabry disease. She has not received any investigational therapeutic agents for Fabry disease and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She will be enrolled in the study and receive intravenous Replagal every other week for 6 to 12 months with close monitoring of her vital signs, physical examinations, and laboratory tests.

45 yo M with traumatic brain injury admitted to the ICU with no evidence of improvement despite maximal management. The clinical team has discussed with family the possibility of brain death and they have agreed to pursue brain death testing. The patient has a history of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. On exam, the patient is unresponsive with absent brainstem reflexes and apnea. Neurological death is declared and the family consents for organ donation. The patient meets inclusion criteria for the study as a high-risk donor due to type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. The patient's laboratory values are within the acceptable range for liver biopsy, making them eligible for the study.

A 17-year-old male presented to the clinic with concerns about his genitalia. He had been raised as a female but had always felt different and uncomfortable with his body. On examination, he had ambiguous external genitalia, with a small penis and no scrotum. His testes were palpable in the inguinal canals. He had never experienced a menstrual cycle. A karyotype study revealed 46, XY. Further investigations revealed elevated levels of androstenedione and low levels of testosterone and dihydrotestosterone. The HCG stimulation test confirmed the diagnosis of 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 deficiency. The patient and his family have agreed to participate in the clinical trial to determine the molecular basis of this rare genetic disorder.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as it is focused on studying the impact of virtual patient designs on students' reasoning pattern and therapeutic decision making. Participants are students enrolled in the comprehensive dentistry course at the time of the study.

A 45-year-old female presents to the bariatric clinic with a history of jejunoileal bypass (JIB) surgery performed 20 years ago. The patient underwent JIB for weight loss due to morbid obesity. She has been experiencing recurrent abdominal pain, steatorrhea, electrolyte imbalance, and protein calorie malnutrition (PCM) symptoms for the past 6 months. The patient has been treated with parenteral nutritional support and optimized medical management, but her symptoms persist. The patient meets the NIH criteria for weight loss surgery, and a laparoscopic approach for revisional bariatric surgery is indicated. She is excluded from other types of revisional bariatric procedures and open approach for revision surgery. The patient has fully informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to undergo a one-stage laparoscopic re-operative gastric bypass surgery for failed and/or complicated JIB for weight loss. She understands that the study aims to analyze the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the procedure, as well as determine what factors or strategies are associated with a successful outcome. The patient's medical records are complete and available for analysis.

30 yo pregnant woman diagnosed with HIV during her prenatal care seeks to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of anti-HIV therapy on red blood cells of HIV-infected mothers and their infants. She has been on antiretroviral therapy since her diagnosis and is currently in her third trimester. She has no other significant medical history and has been following with a high-risk obstetrician throughout her pregnancy. She plans to deliver at either Duke University or the University of North Carolina and has consented to participate in the study. She understands that her baby will also need to have blood drawn at specific time points throughout the first six months of life. She is committed to following up with the pediatric infectious disease clinic at either institution for the study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old male of Asian descent with a history of alcohol abuse for the past 20 years. He has been diagnosed with advanced cirrhosis with a MELD score of 11 based on clinical and radiological criteria. He has been abstinent from alcohol for the past 3 months and is currently receiving treatment from a hepatologist. His medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He has no known food allergies or gastrointestinal resections. He is married and works as a construction worker, but has had to take a leave of absence due to his medical condition. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatments for his cirrhosis and improve his overall health.

32 yo female with good oral hygiene presents to the dental clinic with a fractured right first molar. Clinical examination and radiographs reveal a large carious lesion with extensive involvement into the dentin. No periapical pathology or periodontal pockets are noted. The tooth is determined to require a full-coverage crown. Patient is interested in participating in the study comparing digital and conventional impressions for crown fabrication. She has no history of any prior dental treatment on the tooth in question and the opposing tooth is free of any indirect restoration. The patient is compliant with oral hygiene and has no other medical conditions that would preclude dental treatment. The tooth in question has adequate abutment height after tooth preparation, and the anticipated crown margin is expected to be supragingival or equigingival on natural tooth structure.

A 28-year-old Caucasian woman has been diagnosed with moderate to severe psoriasis for the past 5 years. She has tried various topical treatments and medications, but her symptoms have not significantly improved. She has a family history of psoriasis, with her mother and maternal grandmother both being diagnosed with the disease. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of major medical illness. She is currently not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the course of the study. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially find a more effective treatment for her psoriasis.

A 55-year-old man diagnosed with heart failure complains of fatigue, shortness of breath, and anginal pain with less than ordinary physical activity. He has evidence of at least one clinical episode of HF diagnosed by a physician as pulmonary congestion. He has not been hospitalized for heart failure in the past three months, and there have been no medication changes for the past month. His resting heart rate is below 95 bpm, and he has no dyspnea at rest. He is not diagnosed with Pickwickian syndrome, obstructive sleep apnea, aortic stenosis, or atrial fibrillation. He is not receiving antidepressant therapy or nocturnal CPAP or oxygen therapy. He is able to walk without assistance and speaks/reads English fluently.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of tinnitus that has been ongoing for the past 6 months. He complains of constant ringing in his ears, which often interferes with his daily activities and sleep. Upon further questioning, he reports occasional pain and clicking in his jaw, especially when chewing or yawning. He denies any history of trauma to the jaw or head, dental problems, or chronic stress. The patient is willing to undergo an examination to assess the presence of temporomandibular disorders as part of this clinical trial. He has no history of head and neck space-occupying lesions or previous degenerative diseases of the temporomandibular joint.

45-year-old male with a clinical diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the right knee based on the American College of Rheumatology criteria with radiologic evidence of OA (K-L score ≥2 for the right knee) at the screening visit. The patient reports moderate-to-severe pain in the right knee, with a WOMAC average pain subscale score of 6 at both the screening and randomization visits. The patient has a history of at least 12 weeks of analgesic use for pain due to OA of the right knee and has been on regular use of analgesic medications for OA pain, including NSAIDs, selective cyclooxygenase 2 inhibitors, and paracetamol/acetaminophen. The patient is willing to discontinue current pain medications and adhere to study requirements for rescue treatments. The patient does not have a history or presence of non-OA inflammatory joint disease, neuropathic disorders, or tumors or infections of the spinal cord. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not allergic to fasinumab or any of its components.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy woman who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has no history of H7N9 virus infection or suspected infection. She is literate and willing to provide written informed consent. She is willing to comply with the rules of the clinical trial scheme and accept blood examination before and after immunization, as well as cooperate with follow-up visits. She has no history of allergies to any component of the trial vaccine, especially allergies to eggs. She has a normal spleen function and does not suffer from autoimmune diseases or immunodeficiency. She has not received any immunosuppressant treatments in the past six months. She has not suffered from any acute illness or chronic disease in the past 7 days, nor has she received blood products in the past three months before getting inoculated testing vaccine. She has not been inoculated with an active virus vaccine in 14 days or subtype or inactivated virus in 7 days before getting inoculated testing vaccine. She has not been infected by any acute diseases and has not had fever in the past 3 days (axillary temperature < 38 ℃). She is not participating in another clinical trial and has no allergies, convulsions, epilepsy, encephalopathy, psychosis history, or family history. Her laboratory detection indexes are normal before getting inoculated testing vaccine. She is not in the suckling period, pregnancy, plan of pregnant or pregnancy tests (positive). She has not had fever in the past 3 days (axillary temperature < 37.1 ℃). She is not suffering from thrombocytopenia or other coagulation disorder, which may result in intramuscular injection contraindication. The investigator thinks that there are no other situations that may affect the trial evaluation.

The patient is a healthy non-smoking 30-year-old female who is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have any clinical evidence of significant cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, hematological, neurological, psychiatric, or other diseases that may interfere with the objectives of the study and/or pose safety concerns. She is not taking any medications except for stable doses of oral contraceptives. She is not allergic to eggs and is able to provide written informed consent before participating in the study. The patient's screening weight is less than 96 kg. Additionally, the patient has not taken any multivitamins for at least one week before the study and is able to comply with the requirements for the entire study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman diagnosed with triple negative breast cancer that has metastasized to other parts of her body. She has already received several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has recently received the news that her cancer is resistant to treatment.
