She is feeling overwhelmed and uncertain about what her next steps should be. She is interested in learning more about her options and would like to be better informed about resistance to treatment. She is open to participating in a clinical trial that will help her communicate better with her oncologist and other healthcare professionals. She is fluent in French and has no difficulty understanding the language.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and has been struggling to control his blood sugar levels with lifestyle modifications alone. He has a history of dyslipidemia and has been on a low-fat diet for the past six months. His BMI is 30, and he has a family history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He doesn't smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. His initial blood work showed an HbA1c level of 8.5%, fasting blood glucose level of 180 mg/dL, total cholesterol level of 220 mg/dL, triglyceride level of 400 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol level of 35 mg/dL, and LDL cholesterol level of 150 mg/dL. The patient is antidiabetic drug naïve and has not taken any medications for dyslipidemia in the past. The treating physician recommends enrolling the patient in the FAME ROSI clinical trial to determine the best treatment option for his diabetes and dyslipidemia.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has had a healthy pregnancy with no complications and is expected to have a normal vaginal delivery. She has not used any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) in the two weeks leading up to birth and has not received any antenatal antibiotics treatment during pregnancy. She has not been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus or uncontrollable hyperthyroidism during her pregnancy. She is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. She occasionally drinks alcohol in social settings but has abstained throughout her pregnancy.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been living with HIV for the past 10 years. He has a history of salivary gland disease and has been experiencing symptoms such as dry mouth and difficulty swallowing. Upon examination, he was found to have elevated BK polyomavirus viral loads in his oral cavity. The patient has been on antiretroviral therapy and has been adherent to his medication regimen. He has no known allergies to fluoroquinolones or any other medications. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. The patient reports occasional alcohol use and he has never smoked. He has no history of seizures or tendon disorders. His most recent laboratory results show a CD4 count of 550 cells/mm³ and an undetectable viral load. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his salivary gland function and quality of life.

The patient is a 56-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced cervical carcinoma. She underwent radical hysterectomy followed by adjuvant chemoradiation therapy. However, a recent PET-CT scan showed metastatic disease in the lungs and liver. She is currently experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and doesn't drink alcohol. She has no known drug allergies. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. She is postmenopausal and not using contraception. She has no history of autoimmune disease or active infections. Her laboratory screening panel is within normal limits. She has not received any prior anti-PD1/PDL-1 therapy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of her cancer.

58 yo M with a history of metastatic melanoma with progressive disease after receiving prior Melan-A peptide vaccine and achieving a detectable immune response. The patient has been deemed ineligible for other protocols due to progressive disease or maximum number of vaccine injections with stable disease has been attained. The patient's tumor expresses MART-1/Melan-A antigen and is HLA-A2 positive. The patient has a performance status of 1 and normal whole blood counts and pulmonary function. The patient's transaminases and gamma-glutamyl-transferase are less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal and bilirubin is normal. The patient has a creatinine clearance greater than 70 mL/min and has no major uncontrolled heart disease or arterial hypertension. The patient has received prior chemotherapy, biologic therapy, radiotherapy, and/or surgery.

The patient is a 9-month-old male infant who was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease at 6 months of age. He was born full-term via uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has no significant medical history except for the kidney disease. He has been receiving care from a pediatric nephrologist and is currently on a low-protein diet. His weight at the time of screening is 5.5 kg. His hemoglobin level is 8.7 g/dL, and his transferrin saturation is 22%. He has not received any erythropoiesis-stimulating agents within the past 12 weeks and has not had any blood transfusions within the past 12 weeks. He has not been on any immunosuppressants, and his blood pressure is stable without medication. He has no known allergies or sensitivities. The infant is currently not receiving antibiotic therapy for systemic infection and has not had any major surgeries.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 5 years ago. She has been taking highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) regularly for the past 3 years and has achieved undetectable viral loads. She has a CD4 count of 500 cells/mm^3 and has not experienced any opportunistic infections. She is currently on a regimen containing drugs of at least two different classes. She has a Karnofsky performance score of 100 and has no history of skin disease or autoimmune disease. She has not been exposed to any experimental HIV vaccine or immunomodulating therapy in the past 6 months. She has not received any vaccine in the past 30 days. She has no history of drug or alcohol use or dependence. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to use acceptable forms of contraception. She has no history of diabetes or bleeding disorders. Her laboratory results are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of LC002, an experimental therapeutic vaccine, in HIV-infected adults currently receiving HAART.

28-year-old female who is 14 weeks pregnant visited her obstetrician with vaginal bleeding and cramping. An ultrasound revealed that the fetus had stopped developing at 10 weeks. The patient has decided to undergo a termination of pregnancy (TOP) due to the non-viability of the fetus. She will be enrolled in a clinical trial that will investigate the levels of LIF and ACTH in fetal and maternal blood samples during various gestational weeks. The blood samples will be taken during the TOP procedure. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy.

35-year-old Caucasian male with a sedentary lifestyle and no history of low back injury or musculoskeletal disorder presents to the clinic for assessment of spinal stability. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. His BMI is 26. He reports occasional mild lower back pain after prolonged sitting but denies any other symptoms. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. He is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the research and potentially benefit from the non-invasive techniques being developed to measure intervertebral kinematics of the lumbar spine. He has no plans of becoming pregnant during the study period.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 within the last 3 days. She has been experiencing mild symptoms of the virus such as cough, sore throat, and fatigue. She has not received any SARS-CoV-2 vaccine or monoclonal antibody treatment in the past. She has no known allergies to any components of the investigational medicinal product. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she does not have any chronic or clinically significant medical condition that would jeopardize her safety or rights during the trial. She is not pregnant or lactating and has been using contraception. Her blood test results show a normal neutrophil count, hemoglobin level, and platelet count. Her ALT, AST, and total bilirubin levels are within normal range, and her eGFR is above 60 ml/min/1.73m². She has not received any systemic corticosteroids, immunosuppressive anti-cancer, or other significant medications within the last 6 months. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C. He has been experiencing fatigue, nausea, and abdominal pain for the past 6 months. His lab results show elevated liver enzymes and a positive HCV RNA test. He does not have any other significant medical history or chronic liver disease. He is not currently taking any systemic antiviral, antineoplastic, or immunomodulatory treatments. His hemoglobin, platelet count, and neutrophil count are all within normal limits. He has no history of serious mental illness or immunodeficiency. He is in a committed relationship with a partner of reproductive age and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for 6 months after the study is completed. He has read and understood the study requirements and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

56 y/o male with a history of lung cancer diagnosed in [**2019**] and treated with chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient was found to have a METΔex14 mutation on a recent biopsy. Multiple brain metastases were also discovered and treated with stereotactic radiosurgery. A recent MRI showed stable disease in the brain, but progression of disease in the lungs with new nodules. The patient is currently experiencing shortness of breath and intermittent cough. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has adequate organ function. The patient has no history of cardiovascular disease or clinically significant infections, but he does have peripheral neuropathy due to prior chemotherapy. He has not undergone major surgery in the past 4 weeks, and he has not been diagnosed with any other primary malignancy aside from the lung cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to undergo additional testing to confirm his eligibility.

25-year-old female with no significant medical history, currently working as a research assistant. She is fluent in German and has a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She practices safe contraception and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of psychiatric or somatic disorders and does not have any contraindications to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Her blood count, blood chemistry, and coagulation status are within the normal range. She has a normal ECG and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of triflusal on episodic memory and cognitive functions in healthy participants.

A 52-year old male office worker was diagnosed with coronary artery disease after experiencing chest pain during exercise. He underwent angiography, which showed a bifurcation lesion in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and diagonal branch. The side branch reference diameter was measured at 2.5 mm and was deemed stentable. He is currently on dual antiplatelet therapy and is being considered for percutaneous coronary intervention with a drug-eluting stent. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is taking medications. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He is married with two children and lives an active lifestyle. His occupation involves sitting for long hours in front of a computer. He is interested in participating in the COBIS II registry to contribute to the research on coronary bifurcation stenting and to potentially benefit from the long-term clinical results of this study.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus. His mother, who is his primary caregiver, reports that she has a hard time reading and writing in English. The patient has been receiving diabetes education classes for the past year, but his glycemic control has been poor despite following the recommended treatment plan. The patient's medical history is significant for no other chronic illnesses or cognitive disorders. The patient is fluent in English and Spanish. The patient's most recent hemoglobin A1C level was 9.5%.

The patient is a 10-month-old baby girl who has been diagnosed with classic infantile-onset Pompe disease (IOPD) through newborn screening. She has not received any prior investigational drug or biologic for Pompe disease. She has experienced a clinical decline in her current standard of care and requires respiratory assistance through a non-invasive ventilation mask. Her family history is negative for any genetic disorders. She has no allergies or hypersensitivity to any medication. Her parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial and give informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old female critical care nurse who works full-time at an ICU in a hospital. She has been working in the ICU for the past 5 years and is experiencing significant levels of stress and burnout. She reports feeling emotionally exhausted and having negative thoughts and feelings related to her work. She has a baseline score of 75 on the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC) and a score of 20 on the emotional exhaustion dimension of the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI). She is interested in participating in the study to learn techniques to manage her stress and improve her resiliency. She has no history of bipolar or psychotic disorder, substance dependence, or self-harm. She is willing to participate in the entire study protocol and is not employed on a time-limited contract.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ovarian cancer two years ago. She had a hysterectomy followed by six cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy. Her most recent scan showed that the cancer has returned, and her doctor has recommended participation in a clinical trial. The patient has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or central nervous system metastasis. She is able to swallow tablets and has given written informed consent prior to any study procedures. Her blood counts, hepatic and renal function are all adequate. Her performance status is 1 on Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use birth control while on the study and for three months after stopping the study drug. The patient has not taken any medications or grapefruit juice within 7 days of initial dose of study drug. She is eager to participate in the study to help advance research for ovarian cancer treatment.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with nasopharyngeal carcinoma based on pathology or cytology. The cancer is non-metastatic and classified as UICC/AJCC 2010 Stage T2N1M0. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Score of 80 and is expected to survive for more than 3 months. The patient has no dysfunction of heart, lung, liver, kidney or hematopoiesis. The patient has been receiving weekly complete blood count during radiotherapy. The patient has not received any colony stimulating factor such as erythropoietin. The patient does not have any signs of infection before radiotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman from the United States who has been diagnosed with interstitial cystitis and vulvar pain. She experiences persistent localized vulvar pain characterized as "burning," suggestive of a neuropathic pain response. She has agreed to be contacted for an in-office examination as part of Part 2 of the study. The patient is capable of giving informed consent and willing to follow all study procedures. Her past medical and drug history are unremarkable. Her BMI is 25, BP: 118/72, HR: 76/min.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which he takes medication. He denies smoking and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a sedentary lifestyle and does not exercise regularly. His recent laboratory results show an HbA1c level of 8.5% and FPG level of 170 mg/dL. He has never been on insulin therapy and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new investigational drug for the management of his diabetes.

The patient is a 27-year-old male of Caucasian ethnicity with a history of recurrent kidney stones. He has been experiencing episodes of severe pain in his lower back and sides accompanied by nausea and vomiting. He has noticed that his urine is discolored and cloudy during these episodes. He has been diagnosed with uric acid or calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis and has a urinary pH of less than 5.5. He denies any excessive intake of animal protein or gastrointestinal alkali loses. He reports that his father and grandfather also suffered from recurrent kidney stones. He is willing to participate in a genetic study to identify the factors that contribute to the development of nephrolithiasis in patients with gouty diathesis. He understands the purposes of the study and is able to provide written informed consent according to the Declaration of Helsinki guidelines.

A 35-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of botulism, including muscle weakness and difficulty breathing. He was diagnosed with botulism and required mechanical ventilation. He has no history of renal or cardiac problems. He is not pregnant and is above the age of 18. He has no history of hepatic failure. He is eligible for the clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of 3,4-diaminopyridine in severe botulinic poisoning.

The patient is a 55 year old man who has been diagnosed with advanced liver cancer that has spread to his lungs. He has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy in the past, but the cancer has continued to progress. His performance status is ECOG 1 and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 3 months. He has no significant medical history aside from the cancer diagnosis. He has not undergone any prior treatment with irinotecan. His liver function tests are within normal limits, with a bilirubin level of 1.1 mg/dL and AST level of 40 IU/L. His WBC count is 6,000/mm^3 and platelet count is 130,000/mm^3. He has no active infections and is HIV negative. He is not currently taking any anticoagulants. He is willing to undergo biopsy of his metastatic lesions for the purpose of this study. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to participate.

A 35-year-old female is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic surgery for removal of ovarian cysts. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been experiencing pelvic pain for the past few months. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any chronic medical conditions. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has never undergone surgery before and is anxious about the procedure. The estimated duration of the surgery is less than 60 minutes. She has no allergies to anesthetics and is not on any chronic pain medication. She is eligible to participate in the clinical trial.

A 55-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of rectal bleeding, abdominal pain and constipation. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are controlled with medications. She has no allergies to medications. She has never taken vitamin D supplements before. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her diet consists of mainly vegetables, fruits, and lean protein. She works as a teacher and is physically active by taking daily walks. A colonoscopy revealed a rectal polyp and a biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. The patient was scheduled for an elective colorectal surgery. She is able to sign informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 35-year-old female patient who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus for 10 years came to the clinic for a follow-up. She has a history of hypoglycemic episodes and glucose fluctuations. She is currently using an insulin pump and monitoring her glucose levels with a continuous glucose monitoring system. She has a skin phototype of 2 and is fluent in Danish. She has no extensive skin changes, tattoos, or diseases on the probe application site, and no known allergies to medical-grade alcohol or adhesives. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or attempting to conceive. She has no medical history or condition that could compromise her ability to participate in the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve non-invasive glucose monitoring devices for diabetic patients.

The patient is a 20 year-old full-time community college student who has been experiencing heavy drinking episodes recently. She drinks at least four drinks on one occasion and exceeds the weekly NIAAA drinking recommendations (8 drinks for women) regularly. She owns a smartphone with text-messaging capability. She is concerned about her drinking habits and wants to make a change. She has no history of alcoholism in her family and no past history of alcohol treatment. She is currently not taking any medications and has no known medical conditions. She is looking for a convenient and user-friendly alcohol intervention that can fit into her demanding lifestyle as a community college student.

A 45-year-old man is scheduled to undergo elective nephrectomy. He has been experiencing chronic pain in his lower back for the past 6 months, which has been managed with over-the-counter painkillers. He has no history of substance abuse, and his medical history is unremarkable. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His creatinine level is within normal limits, and he has no contraindications for pregabalin. He has never had a peptic ulcer or any other major medical conditions such as angina pectoris, myocardial infarction or stroke. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) about 2 years ago. She underwent chemotherapy with R-CHOP regimen but her disease relapsed 6 months after the completion of treatment. She received salvage chemotherapy with RICE regimen, but unfortunately, she did not achieve complete remission. She is now scheduled for an autologous stem cell transplantation. She has no significant past medical history or allergies. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for some cervical lymph nodes. The laboratory tests reveal normal liver and kidney function. The echocardiogram shows normal cardiac function. The pulmonary function test reveals FEV1, FVC, and DLCO corrected for Hgb are all >/= 50%. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. She is a non-smoker and not pregnant. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient A is a 35-year-old English speaking man from the United States who participated in the Framingham Heart Study (Offspring and Omni Group 1 Cohorts) in-person examination on 10/5 at the FHS Research Center in Framingham, Massachusetts. He owns an iPhone with compatible iOS version 10.0 or higher and is proficient in reading English language. He has signed and dated informed consent within the eFHS mobile app and has given permissions for notifications and data sharing with the Research Center. He does not have any reading limitations and is eligible to participate in the randomized trial to test the effect of administering half of survey modules every 2 weeks versus all survey modules every 4 weeks on improving participants' response rates. He will receive a series of digital surveys modules to complete on a regularly occurring schedule. The survey assessments will include cognition, pain, mood, physical function and performance, physical activity, and events. The administration of the physical function, physical activity, and events modules will be delayed by 2 weeks in the experimental group as compared to the control group.

A 27-year-old pregnant woman residing in the peri-urban area of Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso presents with a history of intermittent fever and chills for the past few days. She is currently in the second trimester of her pregnancy and has a positive history of malaria in the past. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medication at present. On examination, her temperature is 38.5°C, and her blood pressure is normal. She has an enlarged spleen on palpation. Laboratory investigations reveal a positive test for malaria, and she is diagnosed with uncomplicated malaria in pregnancy. She is counselled regarding the IPT with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) strategy and agrees to participate in the clinical trial. She resides in the health area of Lafiabougou or secteur 24 and meets all the inclusion criteria. She has no history of bleeding during pregnancy or eclampsia and is willing to provide free and informed consent. She is monitored closely and treated with SP at the designated intervals as per the study protocol.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic diarrhea for the past six months. He reports having loose stools with a frequency of at least three times a day. He has tried various over-the-counter medications with no improvement. He has a history of lactose intolerance and has noticed that his symptoms worsen after consuming dairy products. He has no history of bowel resection or any other significant medical conditions. He is willing to use reliable contraception during the study period and has access to an acceptable smartphone/tablet with internet access. The patient is a native English speaker and resides in the United States.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis) and has been in remission after receiving induction therapy (corticosteroids and immunosuppressive agents) for the past 8 months. The patient has also been diagnosed with high cholesterol levels but does not currently take any cholesterol-lowering medication. The patient has no history of cardiovascular disease or other systemic vasculitis diseases. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent. The patient is affiliated with a social security system and has no known allergies to rosuvastatin or its excipients. The patient is not pregnant and has no chronic HCV, HBV, or HIV infection. The patient has not participated in any interventional studies in the past 3 months. The patient has no other medical or psychiatric conditions that would prevent them from participating in the trial.

This is an 18-year-old female who was born on the Isle of Wight in the United Kingdom between January 1, 1989 and February 28, 1990. She has a history of asthma and other allergic diseases and has been followed by study researchers since she was 1 year old. She has previously provided blood samples at her 10-year study visit. She will be returning for a study visit to complete questionnaires on asthma and allergy symptoms and environmental exposures, including tobacco smoke and pollution. She will also undergo blood collection, an allergy skin prick test, lung function testing, and a bronchial challenge test to assess airway function. She is willing to participate in this study and has provided consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman diagnosed with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. She has received treatment with gemcitabine and cisplatin but has not responded to the therapy. She has no history of other cancers and no significant past medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has no brain metastases and no other significant medical conditions. Her blood tests show hemoglobin of 10 g/dl, platelet count of 120,000/mm3, and WBC count of 4,500/mm3. Her renal and liver function tests are normal. She has no history of autoimmune diseases or immunodeficiency disorders. She is willing to use birth control during the study and for four months after the treatment. She has given informed consent and is enrolled in the companion protocol (Cell Harvest and Preparation to Support Adoptive Cell Therapy Clinical Protocols and Pre-Clinical Studies) and has available TIL cultures for therapy. She meets all the other eligibility criteria for the study.

45 year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with right-sided abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past month. He denies any nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. His physical exam is unremarkable except for mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis is ordered and reveals a 3 cm focal hepatic lesion. The patient is a non-smoker and denies any alcohol or drug use. He has no other significant past medical history. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with sigmoid colon cancer after undergoing a colonoscopy for rectal bleeding. The biopsy confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma. CT scan shows no evidence of distant metastasis. The patient has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. His hemoglobin level is 12 g/dL, white blood cell count is 6,000/mm3, and platelet count is 180,000/mm3. He has no evidence of heart or lung dysfunction. He has been offered the option of participating in a clinical trial to compare single incision laparoscopic sigmoidectomy to conventional laparoscopic sigmoidectomy for the treatment of his colon cancer. The patient has no allergies or contraindications to any of the proposed treatments and has agreed to participate in the study.

35 y/o female with a history of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) diagnosed according to DSM-IV-TR. The patient reports an inadequate response to at least one antidepressant treatment, including the current treatment. The patient has been experiencing irritability for the past 10 weeks and has a pre-defined mood (irritable) score. The patient has been receiving SSRI or SNRI antidepressant treatment at the same dosage for the past 2 weeks and has been receiving this treatment for the past 6 weeks. The patient has not started cognitive or behavioral therapy within the past 6 weeks and does not plan to start during the study. The patient denies any current or history of substance abuse or dependence, excluding nicotine or caffeine. The patient has not received electroconvulsive therapy within the past 6 months and has not had vagus nerve stimulation or a deep brain stimulation device implanted for the management of depression. The patient meets other inclusion criteria at the screening visit and has fulfilled the DSM-IV-TR criteria for MDD. The patient has no current psychiatric disorder or Axis I disorder, established as the principal diagnosis, other than MDD and does not have a current Axis II diagnosis of antisocial, borderline, paranoid, schizoid, schizotypical, or histrionic personality disorder. The patient has not experienced hallucinations, delusions, or any psychotic symptomatology in the current MDE and is not at significant risk of suicide.

17 yo female diagnosed with Ulcerative Colitis two years ago presents to the gastroenterology clinic for a follow-up appointment. She reports ongoing symptoms including abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding despite multiple medication trials. She is currently taking mesalamine and prednisone, but is concerned about the side effects of long-term prednisone use. She is also worried about missing school and social events due to her symptoms. She has a history of anxiety and depression and is currently seeing a therapist. She has a smartphone and is comfortable using technology. She is interested in learning more about her treatment options and is willing to use a web application to help with decision making regarding her UC management. She is fluent in English.

A 25-year-old female college student came to the clinic with concerns about her marijuana use and difficulty with staying focused on her schoolwork. She has been using marijuana daily for the past 3 years to help her relax and cope with stress. She reports having difficulty concentrating on her schoolwork and often forgets deadlines. She has a history of ADHD, diagnosed when she was in elementary school, and was prescribed Ritalin at that time. She stopped taking Ritalin when she entered college, as she didn't like the side effects. She has no other medical conditions and doesn't take any other medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help her reduce her marijuana use and improve her ADHD symptoms.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was recently admitted to the hospital due to unstable angina. She has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 5 years. Her blood pressure has been difficult to control and her doctor has recommended more frequent monitoring. She has been fitted with an invasive arterial line (A-line) for continuous blood pressure monitoring in the hospital. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She is able to wear the wristband device and understands the purpose of the study. The patient has no known allergies and is currently not taking any medication for the past 5 hours. She is alert and oriented, and her vital signs are within normal limits.

The patient is a preterm male infant born at 26 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 800 grams. He was delivered by emergency c-section due to maternal preeclampsia. He required mechanical ventilation for 4 weeks and was gradually weaned off to nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP). He had a prolonged course in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to recurrent episodes of apnea and bradycardia. He also had a gastrointestinal surgery for necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) at 34 weeks postmenstrual age. Currently, he is 36 weeks postmenstrual age and his respiratory support has been weaned off to room air. However, he still requires gavage feeding due to poor sucking coordination and strength. The baby has been referred to this clinical trial to improve his oral feeding skills and reduce his hospital stay. His parents are fully informed about the trial and have provided written consent for their baby's participation.

A 10-year-old boy with myelomeningocele presents to the Pediatric Urology Department with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections and difficulty with bladder control. He has undergone previous urodynamic studies which were uncomfortable and difficult for him to tolerate. The patient has no history of bladder augmentation surgery and is currently not experiencing a urinary tract infection. The patient and their family have provided consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of chronic bronchitis, who has been experiencing an acute exacerbation of his condition for the past week. He presents with coughing up yellowish phlegm, shortness of breath, and wheezing. He has tried using his inhaler, but it is not providing adequate relief. His past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He does not have any known allergies. He is a non-smoker and lives a sedentary lifestyle. He is seeking an alternative treatment for his phlegm-heat syndrome and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for Zhuli Capsule.

72-year-old retired teacher who had a stroke 6 months ago and is now living at home with the assistance of her daughter. She is able to walk with the aid of a cane and has difficulty performing everyday activities such as dressing herself and preparing meals. She is interested in participating in a group exercise program to improve her ability to function independently. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or significant joint pain, and is able to follow verbal instructions and speak and read English fluently. She has not participated in any formal exercise or rehabilitation program since her stroke. She is willing to obtain medical clearance from her healthcare provider and sign a liability waiver.

The patient is a 48-year-old female who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis and is currently under the care of the Royal Wolverhampton Trust. She is currently taking methotrexate and has not experienced any severe side effects. She works as a nurse in a hospital and has been following strict social distancing measures due to the COVID-19 pandemic. She has been concerned about the potential impact of the virus on her health and quality of life, as well as the impact of social distancing on her mental health. She has a validated mobile phone number linked to her hospital record and is willing to participate in the study.

62-year-old female with a history of breast cancer who is scheduled for a mastectomy under general anesthesia. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and hypothyroidism, all of which are well controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and denies any history of lung disease. Physical examination reveals normal vital signs and no signs of infection or inflammation at the proposed catheterization site. CT imaging shows no anatomical abnormalities of the subclavian artery or vein/clavicle, and there is no evidence of lung parenchymal disease or pneumo/hemothorax. The patient agrees to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been struggling with alcohol dependence for the past 10 years. He has been enrolled in an intensive outpatient substance abuse treatment program for the past 3 weeks. He has a DSM-IV diagnosis of alcohol dependence and has been experiencing severe withdrawal symptoms. He is willing to participate in the research and be randomized. He has a 6th grade reading level and is able to provide the names of several informants who will know his whereabouts during the follow-up period. He has no acute medical or psychiatric problems that preclude outpatient treatment and has not used IV heroin in the past year. He does not anticipate involvement in other forms of intensive treatment during the 6-month period after enrollment.

A 49-year-old woman was diagnosed with melanoma 2 years ago. She underwent surgery to remove the primary tumor but developed metastasis to the lymph nodes and liver. She received ipilimumab as the first-line therapy. After 6 months of treatment, the disease progressed, and she started taking a BRAF inhibitor. The disease was stable for 8 months, but then it progressed again, and she started taking a MEK inhibitor. The disease was stable for 4 months, but now there are new lesions in the liver and lung. She is interested in exploring other treatment options and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. She doesn't have any other significant medical history, and her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance status is 1. She is currently taking medications for blood pressure and cholesterol. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to conceive in the near future. Her lab results show adequate organ function.

The patient is a premature baby boy born at 28 weeks gestation weighing 900g. He was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit due to respiratory distress and required intubation and mechanical ventilation. On day 5 of life, his platelet count was found to be 80 x 10^9/L. Despite being treated with antibiotics and receiving packed red blood cells, his platelet count continued to decrease and reached 45 x 10^9/L on day 10 of life. His parents have been approached to participate in a clinical trial investigating the impact of thrombocytopenia and platelet transfusions on neonatal bleeding and inflammation. They have agreed to participate and have provided written informed consent. The baby will undergo a series of clinical and laboratory data collection, including bleeding score, hemoglobins, hematocrits, PLT counts, Immature Platelet Fraction percentage (IPF%) and Immature Platelet Count (IPC) measurements, and plasma separation for future measurements of dsDNA and MPO-DNA ELISA, markers of NET formation, TAT complexes, and serum cytokines/vascular injury markers by Luminex. The baby will be followed until resolution of the severe thrombocytopenia, death or discharge, whichever comes first.

A 62-year-old male smoker with a long history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and scheduled for elective coronary artery bypass graft surgery. He has been experiencing chest pain on exertion for the past few months and his cardiologist recommended surgery for his condition. His left ventricular systolic function is moderately impaired and he has agreed to participate in the study. He has given written informed consent and is willing to undergo moderate hypothermia or normothermia during surgery. He is not pregnant or of childbearing potential, and is not currently taking nicorandil or sulfonylurea medication. However, he has a history of mild renal dysfunction, which will be assessed by the study team to determine if he meets the eligibility criteria.

Pt is a 58yo M with a diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has progressed despite previous treatments, including chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The tumor measures 2.5cm in its longest dimension, and the patient is being considered for stereotactic radiotherapy. The patient has not received any treatment for this current problem. The patient is in otherwise good health, with no significant comorbidities. The patient is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient is not pregnant or nursing.

A 68 year old woman visits the clinic complaining of difficulty in walking and memory loss. She reports that she has become increasingly forgetful, often misplacing items and having trouble remembering conversations from the day before. She has also noticed that her walking has become slower and she tires more easily. She has a history of hypertension and arthritis but is otherwise healthy. She is currently taking medication for her hypertension. Upon examination, her gait speed is slower than normal and her Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score is 24. She meets the criteria for Motoric Cognitive Risk Syndrome (MCR). She is literate and has no history of mental illness or dementia caused by other factors. She is also not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials and is expected to be compliant with the study protocol.

A 57-year-old man, diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer, has undergone multiple courses of chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He has a history of hypertension and type-2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled on medications. He has a history of alcohol consumption but quit drinking 10 years ago. He has undergone a left nephrectomy due to renal cell carcinoma 2 years ago. His liver function test shows elevated levels of bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase. He has no evidence of brain metastasis, and his ECOG performance status is 1. He is not currently on any anticoagulant therapy. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and amlodipine. He is willing to use appropriate methods of birth control during the study period.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a history of panic disorder with agoraphobia. She experiences unexpected panic attacks that are accompanied by intense fear and physical symptoms such as chest pain, sweating, and palpitations. These attacks have caused her to avoid certain situations and places such as crowded spaces, public transportation, and shopping malls. She is currently not receiving any psychological treatment for her condition but has tried medication in the past with limited success. She is able to read and write in Swedish and is interested in participating in a study that evaluates a new treatment approach using virtual reality (VR) exposure therapy for agoraphobia. She has no other primary axis-I disorders or ongoing substance abuse. Her current medication includes Sertraline 50mg per day.

The patient is a 20-year-old male with a history of Usher Syndrome Type 1B. He was diagnosed with the disease at the age of 5 and has since experienced progressive hearing loss and retinitis pigmentosa. He experiences difficulties with night vision and peripheral vision. He is currently using hearing aids and has had some vision training to help him adapt to his visual impairment. He lives with his parents and two siblings and is currently in college studying computer science. He has no known allergies and takes no medication other than vitamins. He has undergone genetic testing and confirmed to have mutations in the MYO7A gene. He has previously participated in the TDU13600 protocol and received a subretinal injection of SAR421869. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in this long-term study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of SAR421869.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of biliary colic. He was diagnosed with cholelithiasis and has been advised to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He is generally healthy, with no known medical conditions and no history of surgical procedures. He doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. His BMI is 28.5 and his blood pressure is within normal range. He has no family history of eye diseases or glaucoma. He has never had any eye surgeries or eye trauma. He is an ASA 2 physical status patient and the surgery will be elective. He has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate.

The patient is a 35 year old male who is a recreational runner and has completed four half marathons in the past. He has been training for a full marathon for the past six months and is expected to finish within the time frame of 2:10 to 4:30. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. He does not smoke cigarettes and only drinks alcohol socially. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his time sitting at a desk. He is physically active and goes for a run or to the gym four times a week. The patient has no history of claustrophobia or any contraindication for MRI. He is excited to participate in the clinical trial to learn more about the changes in his skeletal muscles after completing a full marathon.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for the past 3 years. He has been on mesalamine and steroids, but they have not been effective in controlling his symptoms. He has never been treated with adalimumab before. He has a total Mayo score of 7 with an endoscopic sub-score of 3. He has experienced frequent abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and weight loss. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no history of other medical conditions, surgeries, or hospitalizations. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential of dose escalation and de-escalation of adalimumab in treating his ulcerative colitis.

A 24-year-old pregnant woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 30 weeks of gestation presents to the obstetrics clinic with complaints of frequent uterine contractions in the past 2 days. She reports pelvic pressure, low back pain, and vaginal discharge. She has no significant past medical history and her previous delivery was a full-term vaginal delivery. She denies any recent illness, fever, or vaginal bleeding. On examination, her uterus is contracting every 5 minutes with a cervical dilation of 1 cm and 50% effacement. Her fetal heart rate is 150 beats per minute, and there is no evidence of cervical bleeding. An ultrasound reveals a single viable fetus in the cephalic presentation with no fetal anomalies. The patient is diagnosed with preterm labor and is offered enrollment in a clinical trial aimed at identifying non-invasive predictors of preterm delivery. She meets the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. She is provided with detailed information about the study and consents to participate. The study team collects maternal blood and cervical/vaginal fluid for analysis, and repeat sampling of cervical fluid is scheduled as often as weekly until the time of delivery.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl with suspected cerebral visual impairment. Her parents noticed that she has difficulty recognizing familiar faces and objects, and often bumps into things. She also has difficulty with hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills. The child was born full-term and had no complications during birth. She has no other medical conditions and is currently attending a preschool program. The patient is cooperative, alert and well-nourished. The ophthalmological assessment showed no issues with the eyes or vision. The child will undergo a comprehensive visual perceptual assessment, cognitive evaluation, and motor function testing. MRI with DTI will be performed to investigate the presence of brain lesions and their correlation with visual and motor function. The ultimate goal of the study is to develop a prediction model to identify CVI early based on neuroimaging data.

A 28-year-old woman with a history of atopic dermatitis since childhood presented to the clinic with a flare-up of her symptoms. She has had recurrent episodes of pruritic and erythematous skin lesions on her arms, legs, and trunk. She reports that her symptoms worsen during the winter months and when she is stressed. She has tried several topical treatments in the past, including corticosteroids and emollients, but has not found significant relief. She has no history of viral skin infections or malignancy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options for her condition.

52 year old male veteran who has been unemployed for the past year and has been struggling with depression and anxiety. He has had difficulty finding and maintaining employment due to his mental health symptoms. He is currently enrolled in a work services program at the VA Connecticut Healthcare System and is interested in participating in this study to improve his job performance and overall quality of life. He speaks fluent English and has no known medical or psychiatric conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 22-year-old woman who has been struggling with acne vulgaris for the past year. She has tried various over-the-counter products, but none have been effective in clearing her skin. She has approximately 25 non-inflammatory lesions and 30 inflammatory lesions on her face. Her baseline IGA score is moderate. She is currently using a topical antibiotic for her acne, but it has not been helping much. She is not pregnant and is using a reliable form of birth control. She is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions. Her methemoglobin level is normal. She does not smoke or use any drugs. She is willing to participate in the study and is excited to try a new treatment for her acne.

A 45-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse presents to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain, jaundice, and confusion. Laboratory tests reveal elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, with a MELD score of 27. Imaging studies reveal liver cirrhosis and the presence of ascites. The patient is diagnosed with hepatic failure and is in medium period. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the plasma diafiltration therapy of hepatic failure. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial. However, the patient has a history of severe sepsis and is currently on antibiotics for a urinary tract infection. Therefore, he is not eligible for the trial due to the exclusion criteria.

A 29 years old female, working as a software engineer, presents with a history of severe menstrual pain for the past 6 months. The pain is described as crampy and dull in nature, radiating to the lower back and thighs. The pain lasts for 2-3 days and is associated with heavy menstrual bleeding. She has not had any previous gynecological surgeries or medical conditions related to reproductive organs. She is not on any contraceptive methods and has no plans for conception in the near future. She has negative pregnancy test results. On examination, no significant physical disability or abnormal findings have been detected. Pelvic ultrasonography showed no identifiable pelvic pathology. She has not participated in any clinical investigation in the last 30 days. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to use Nanoone Woman Underwear during her menstrual cycles.

The patient is a 52-year-old man diagnosed with hypertension six months ago. He has been taking medication regularly, but his blood pressure levels remain high. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to manage his hypertension better. He is literate, has no sensory losses, and is open to communication and cooperation. He has internet access and a phone that can be reached. He is classified as having high blood pressure level in the stage 1,2 and 3, risk group A and B, with no additional organ damage. He does not have any metabolic disturbances or diseases that prevent him from participating in the study. He is excited to learn more about managing his hypertension and improving his quality of life.

There is no need for a patient description for this clinical trial as it is a descriptive analysis of the appearance of the first cases of COVID-19 diagnosed in the city of Nice and does not involve patient recruitment or intervention.

The patient is a 15-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 5 years. She has been using a short-acting-beta-agonist (SABA) on an as-needed basis for symptom relief. Despite this treatment, she experiences frequent asthma symptoms such as coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, especially during exercise. She has not been previously treated with inhaled corticosteroids or long-acting beta-agonists. She is a non-smoker and has no other significant medical conditions. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of BI54903, an inhaled corticosteroid, administered twice daily via Respimat® inhaler, as a potential new treatment option for her asthma.

A 45-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of numbness and tingling in her right hand, particularly in the thumb, index, and middle fingers. She reports that the symptoms have been present for the past 6 months and have worsened over time. She also reports pain and weakness in her hand, which has made it difficult for her to perform her daily activities. She has never had an operation on her median nerve. Upon physical examination, the patient has decreased sensation in the distribution of the median nerve and a positive Tinel's sign. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to alleviate her chronic pain and prevent recurrence. She agrees to be randomized to either the midazolam or dexamethasone group as an adjuvant to local anesthetics in the ultrasound-guided hydrodissection of the median nerve.

A 45-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a complaint of pain in her right heel for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain is worse in the morning when she first gets out of bed or after prolonged periods of sitting. The pain is located on the inside of her heel and feels as if it is coming from under the heel. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, icing, and stretching exercises but has not found any relief. She works as a nurse and is on her feet for most of the day. She has no history of trauma or injury to her foot. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, and she takes medication for this condition. She has no known allergies. She does not smoke or drink alcohol but drinks caffeinated beverages regularly. She denies any history of drug or alcohol dependence. She has no known neurological disorders and no history of surgery on her feet. She is not currently pregnant and has no plans for pregnancy in the near future. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for her foot pain.

The patient is a 62-year-old female who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She has a smoking history of 30 pack-years and continues to smoke 5 cigarettes per day despite multiple attempts to quit. Her lung function tests show a post-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 45% predicted and a FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio of 0.65. She experiences dyspnea on exertion and has had exacerbations in the past requiring hospitalization. She is not currently experiencing a respiratory tract infection and has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help identify an appropriate dose of QAB149 for delivery via a multiple dose inhaler for use in the COPD Phase III program.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing significant hip pain for several years. She has a history of osteoarthritis and has tried non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy and pain medication without significant relief. She has now decided to undergo total hip arthroplasty to improve her quality of life. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She does not have any known allergies or intolerances to medications. The patient is independent in her activities of daily living and lives with her husband. She is motivated to have a successful surgery and recovery, and is willing to participate in the study protocol.

No patient description is needed for this clinical trial as it is a pilot study with no experimental aspect. The study is only assessing the measurements of endotracheal tube cuff pressure in patients who have been endotracheally intubated emergently in the emergency department or in the field by prehospital personnel. The eligibility criteria only includes patients who meet the inclusion criteria of being emergently endotracheally intubated with a cuffed endotracheal tube and excludes patients who had the procedure performed in a setting other than the prehospital or emergency department of participating institution, or non-emergent or elective endotracheal intubation.

The patient is a 70-year-old Chinese woman who lives alone in a small apartment in Hong Kong. She has a history of falls in the past year and is concerned about her risk of falling again. She reports having difficulty with balance and sometimes feels unsteady on her feet. She is able to walk independently with the use of a cane and can walk for at least 10 meters. She has no history of blindness or other significant medical conditions. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to understand and communicate in Chinese.

50-year-old man with a diagnosis of Huntington's disease (HD), CAG > 36, and motor UHDRS score > 5. He has been experiencing difficulty with movement, balance, and speech. He lives with his wife, who is 45 years old, and they have been married for 10 years. She is his primary caregiver and has been experiencing increased stress and burden due to the progression of the disease. They both have agreed to participate in the clinical trial to better understand their psychosocial status and needs as a couple and caregiver. They have been communicating effectively with the investigator and are committed to the study. They do not have any other chronic neurological disorders or psychiatric diseases.

A 65 yo F with no significant medical history, non-smoker and non-drinker, who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research. She is currently not taking any medications and has not taken any disallowed medications in the past 3 months. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with heart failure due to dilated cardiomyopathy. He reports shortness of breath and fatigue with minimal exertion, such as walking up a flight of stairs. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. He has never had a heart attack. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes per day for the past 30 years but is now motivated to quit. He is married and has two adult children. His echocardiogram shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% and a QRS duration of 140ms. He is currently in NYHA Class III heart failure. His cardiologist has recommended cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) and he is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits. He has no other significant medical history and no known allergies. His kidney function is normal. He is covered by a social protection system.

A 54-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer was referred to the clinic by her oncologist. She has been previously treated with one round of chemotherapy and several hormonal therapy regimens, but the disease progressed. She has no visible brain metastases on CT or MRI. The patient is currently on anticoagulants for a previous thromboembolism. She has no other serious medical or psychiatric illness and has a performance status of ECOG 1. Her liver and kidney function tests are normal. She is postmenopausal, has 2 children, and does not smoke.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent headaches, dizziness, and confusion for the past two months. Upon further evaluation, she was diagnosed with CNS lymphoma. She has no other significant medical history and is in overall good health. She speaks English fluently. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, including a white blood cell count of 6,000/mm³, platelet count of 200,000/mm³, hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL, serum bilirubin level of 0.8 times the upper limit of normal, and creatinine level of 1.1 mg/dL. She has not participated in any other therapeutic clinical trials in the past 30 days and is not currently taking any immunosuppressive medications. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to undergo chemotherapy with or without brain radiotherapy to induce remission before starting the vaccine therapy and GM-CSF treatment.

A 62-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU due to COVID-19 infection. He was diagnosed with severe pneumonia and required mechanical ventilation. He had a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which were well-controlled with medications. The patient did not have any history of thyroid disease. His oxygen saturation was 85% on room air, and he required supplemental oxygen to maintain oxygen saturation above 92%. He was started on remdesivir and dexamethasone therapy. He has been in the hospital for 7 days, and his respiratory status has not improved. The patient's family was informed about the clinical trial and has given their consent for the patient to participate in the study. The patient was randomized to receive either triiodothyronine or placebo.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman scheduled to undergo an elective surgery for a hernia repair. She has no significant past medical history and is generally healthy. She does not have any history of smoking or lung disease, and has not had radiation or chemotherapy for cancer. She is not currently being treated for any medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She has no history of obstructive sleep apnea or asthma. She is able to lie in a supine position for the duration of the surgery. She has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a body mass index within the range of 19.0 ~ 28.0 kg/m2. He has no history of tuberculosis or severe active chronic or local infection, and has not received antibiotics treatment within four weeks prior to administration. He has no clinically relevant previous or concomitant disease including hepatic, renal, neurological, respiratory, gastrointestinal, endocrine, hematologic, oncologic, cardiovascular, urinary, musculoskeletal or psychiatric, autoimmune disease/disorders. He has not experienced any chronic or relevant acute infections, and has tested negative for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C. He has not had a fever greater than 38.3℃ within a week prior to administration of study drug. The patient has no history of drug abuse.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and stable angina. He is scheduled for an elective cardiac surgery, and his height is 6 feet (183 cm). He has no history of coagulation disorders, and his current medications include lisinopril and aspirin. He has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is cooperative and willing to participate in the study. He will undergo central venous catheter insertion through the right internal jugular vein and insertion of a TEE probe as part of his surgery. The patient understands the study and has provided informed consent.

52 yo female who presented with a family history of colon cancer. She reports no symptoms and has no personal history of colon polyps. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled on medications. She has no known allergies or adverse reactions to medications. The patient has provided informed consent and is between the ages of 45-80 years old. She is scheduled for a full colonoscopy as per her physician's recommendation. She does not have a known history of inflammatory bowel disease, active colitis, coagulopathy, familial polyposis syndrome, or any other medical conditions that would exclude her from participation in this study.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with osteoporosis 6 years ago and has been taking bisphosphonate therapy since then. She has not experienced any fractures, but is concerned about the potential side effects of the medication. She is able to walk independently and lives alone. She has no history of cancer, small bowel resections, malabsorption, Paget's disease of the bone, osteomalacia, active malignancy, prior bone metastasis, osteogenesis imperfecta, or fibrous dysplasia. She has not been diagnosed with cognitive impairment or dementia. She is willing to participate in a longitudinal study that will require her to undergo radiographs and bone density scans three times over the course of three years. She understands that she may be referred back to her primary care provider if a fracture is found during the study.

A 6-year-old male child, with no known medical history, is scheduled for a minor elective ambulatory surgery. He has no allergies to medications, and his weight and height are within normal limits. He has not experienced any recent illnesses, and he is not taking any medications. His family history is negative for any significant medical conditions. He has no history of gastric reflux, convulsions, cardiovascular, or neuromuscular diseases. His airway exam is within normal limits, and there is no suspicion of a difficult airway.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been trying to conceive with his partner for over a year without success. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. The patient has undergone a semen analysis that showed reduced semen quality, with a total count of motile sperm less than 10 million sperm/ejaculate. The patient is physically active and follows a healthy diet. He is willing to participate in the study and must give written informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a recent diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are currently well-controlled with medication. His BMI is 30. He works as a teacher and enjoys walking his dog in his free time. He has been taking metformin for 3 months, with no side effects, but his HbA1c remains above 7.5%. He has no history of cardiac disease, gastric surgery, or any other significant medical conditions. His physical exam is unremarkable, with normal vital signs, and no signs of peripheral neuropathy. His fasting C-peptide value is 1.2 ng/mL. He does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. His blood tests are all within normal limits, except for his HbA1c, which is 8.2%. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance research on new treatments for Type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 48-year-old female office worker who spends most of her day in front of a computer. She complains of dry eyes, redness, and a gritty sensation that worsens as the day goes on. She has tried using over-the-counter eye drops, but they only provide temporary relief. She has no significant medical history and takes no medication. She wears contact lenses occasionally but has not used them in the past few weeks due to discomfort. Her vision is 20/20 in both eyes, and her intraocular pressure is within normal limits. She has no allergies or adverse reactions to medications. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for dry eye syndrome treatment and willing to adhere to the treatment for more than one month.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma six months ago. She received two lines of chemotherapy with rituximab and anthracycline, but her disease progressed. PET imaging showed active disease in multiple sites, including the liver, spleen, and bone marrow. She has an ECOG performance status of 1, with occasional fatigue and mild dyspnea on exertion. She has no significant medical history except for well-controlled hypertension. Her laboratory tests show normal organ function, including creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min and a normal bilirubin level. She is willing to undergo tumor biopsies and has adequate vascular access for leukapheresis. She has not received any prior CAR T-cell therapy or genetically-modified T-cell therapy. She has not received any experimental therapy within the last eight weeks. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she agrees to use effective contraception during the study. She does not have any active autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppressive therapy. She is negative for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, CNS pathology, or significant bleeding. She has not received any SARS-CoV-2 vaccine within the last 14 days.

The patient is a 38-year-old man who has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss for the past few months. He was referred to a gastroenterologist for evaluation and was diagnosed with Crohn's disease. He has not received any treatment for this condition before. He is a software engineer and enjoys playing basketball in his spare time. He has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. His height is 178 cm and his weight is 65 kg. He has a BMI of 20.5. His vital signs are all within normal limits. His labs: FBS: 80 mg/dl TG: 100 mg/dl Cholesterol: 150 mg/dl LDL: 80 mg/dl HDL: 50 mg/dl. He has no known allergies. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who is planning to conceive in the next 6 months. She has a history of consuming high-mercury fish such as swordfish and shark twice a week. She is aware of the risks of mercury exposure during pregnancy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the benefits of consuming fish with lower mercury levels but high in omega-3 fatty acids. The patient has no known allergies to seafood and is not currently pregnant or nursing. Her hair mercury level was measured at 1.2 ppm, indicating high exposure to mercury. She is in good health, with a normal BMI and no significant medical history. She is willing to consume the selected fish species for 12 weeks in hopes of reducing her hair mercury levels and improving her omega-3 fatty acid levels. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to follow the study protocol.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with gastroparesis 3 years ago. She has experienced frequent nausea, vomiting, bloating, and early satiety, and has lost approximately 10% of her body weight in the past year. She has been taking medications for gastroparesis, including prokinetic agents and antiemetics, but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She has a history of cholecystectomy and has never had any other abdominal surgeries. She is currently not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to try the nutritional formula and is able to adhere to the study visit schedule. Her height is 165 cm and weight is 60 kg. She is willing to give informed consent and would like to find a more effective treatment for her gastroparesis symptoms.

46-year-old female with a history of breast cancer, who completed chemotherapy and radiation therapy 1 year ago, presents with a new onset of headaches, nausea, and vomiting. MRI of the brain reveals a 2 cm enhancing lesion in the right frontal lobe, suspicious for brain metastasis. She is referred to the neurosurgery department at MSK for evaluation and treatment. Upon further workup, the patient is found to have no other evidence of metastatic disease. She is scheduled for surgical resection of the right frontal lobe lesion and will be evaluated for eligibility to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is willing to sign informed consent, and is able to receive intravenous gadolinium contrast per MSK Department of Radiology guidelines.

35-year-old male who suffered a sudden onset of severe headache and nausea was brought to the emergency department. He was diagnosed with a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) after a CT scan. The patient is currently admitted to the neurology department and is being treated for the SAH. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, but he does have a history of hypertension. The patient has given consent to participate in the study and will undergo pupilometer measurements during daily neurological routine examinations.

A 55-year-old man who suffered a stroke 6 months ago, resulting in left-sided hemiparesis. He has been undergoing traditional physical therapy and rehabilitation but still experiences difficulty with daily tasks requiring the use of his left hand. He has no serious muscle spasms and has a Modified Ashworth Scale proximal part of ≤ 3 and Modified Ashworth Scale distal part of ≤ 2. His myoelectric signal can be detected to activate the instrument. He has unilateral paresis with an FMA score of <60 but has no serious cognitive impairment with a Mini Mental State Exam score of >24. He is willing to provide informed consent for the trial and is not currently participating in any other research. He has not received Botulinum Toxin injection within the last 3 months.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer in stage IV. He had already undergone platinum-based chemotherapy but experienced disease progression. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He is a retired businessman who enjoys spending time with his wife and grandchildren. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He has a BMI of 24 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable, and he has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1. He is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form. He has not received any prior anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody or small molecular compounds therapy such as gefitinib, cetuximab, erlotinib, or trastuzumab. His EGFR gene test showed a wild type result.

30 year old female with a body mass index (BMI) of 26.2 kg/m2, non-smoker, with no prior history of diabetes or other medical condition affecting glucose or insulin levels. The patient has no difficulty in traveling to the testing location, and is able to consume the meal tolerance test drink/shake and provide finger stick glucose or saliva samples for the study. The patient is interested in learning how different foods impact insulin levels and how this could aid in personalized weight loss or maintenance advice.

Maria is a 53-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction. She will start radiation therapy to the whole breast/chest wall area next week. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of allergies or chronic illnesses. She takes no medications and is a non-smoker. She is a stay-at-home mom and lives with her husband and two teenage children. She reports some anxiety related to the upcoming radiation therapy and is interested in participating in a study that may help prevent and treat radiation dermatitis. She has no wounds or other ongoing medical issues that would exclude her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of smoking and hypertension. He presents with symptoms of intermittent claudication, including pain and cramping in his legs with walking, which resolves with rest. A physical exam reveals decreased pulses in his lower extremities and a bruit over his right femoral artery. Imaging studies confirm a de novo stenosis of at least 50% in his right femoropopliteal artery, extending over a length of 40mm. There is a clear healthy segment between the lesion in the superficial femoral and common femoral artery, and between the popliteal and tibioperoneal trunk. He has at least one patent tibial vessel with distal run-off. The patient has not undergone any previous interventions for this condition and has no contraindications for combined antiplatelet therapy or known allergy to nickel or paclitaxel.

The patient is an 18-year-old female diagnosed with medulloblastoma. She underwent surgery to remove the tumor, followed by radiation therapy and chemotherapy. However, the tumor has come back and has spread to other parts of her brain. She experiences headaches, nausea, and vomiting. The patient is alert and oriented, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15. She has no history of allergies or significant medical conditions other than her cancer. She is not pregnant and agrees to use birth control during the study.
