The patient is willing and able to swallow capsules or mini-tabs without chewing or crushing. Her body surface area is 1.6 m^2. She has undergone prior therapy including surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy, and has fully recovered from any acute side effects related to these therapies. Her peripheral absolute neutrophil count and platelet count are within normal limits. She has no significant medical history of diabetes or gastrointestinal conditions. The patient agrees to undergo tumor tissue collection as part of the study.

The patient is a 4-year-old child who has been diagnosed with hepatoblastoma, a rare form of liver cancer. The diagnosis was confirmed through a biopsy. The child is currently not receiving any anti-cancer therapy except for surgical resection of the hepatic malignancy that took place before enrolling in the clinical trial. The child is otherwise healthy with normal renal and pulmonary function. The parents have given their consent to participate in the Phase 3 multi-institutional study that includes response-adapted therapy for patients with metastatic disease and a randomized assessment of sodium thiosulfate as auditory protection for children with localized disease. The child’s performance status is good, corresponding to an ECOG score of 0. The child has not received any prior chemotherapy or tumor-directed therapy, and is not currently receiving any other investigational or anticancer agents.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with a history of Ewing sarcoma. The patient has undergone previous treatment with doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, and ifosfamide. The patient has recurrent tumors with no known curative treatment options. The patient has evidence of Ewing sarcoma translocation by FISH or RT-PCR. The patient has measurable disease on CT or MRI by RECIST 1.1. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has adequate organ function. The patient is able to swallow capsules. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 6 months following the last dose of study medication. The patient is capable of reading, understanding, and providing written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past few weeks. She has also noticed a decrease in appetite and has lost a few pounds. She has a family history of ovarian cancer, with her mother being diagnosed with the disease in her late 60s. She has never been diagnosed with cancer before and has no other significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. On physical examination, there is mild abdominal distension, but no palpable masses. A transvaginal ultrasound shows a complex cystic mass in the ovary. Her CA-125 level is elevated at 250 U/ml. She undergoes exploratory laparotomy, and a frozen section biopsy confirms the diagnosis of invasive epithelial ovarian cancer. She is considered eligible for the clinical trial and gives her informed consent to participate.

52 year old female presenting with stress urinary incontinence (SUI) for the past year. She reports leakage of urine during activities such as coughing, sneezing, and exercise. She has tried pelvic floor exercises without improvement. She has no history of pelvic surgery or radiation therapy. She has not been pregnant in the past 20 years. She denies any other urinary symptoms such as urgency, frequency, or dysuria. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is not taking any medications. She has not had a prior urodynamic study or pad test. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the accuracy of using pad weight to estimate the severity of SUI, and to assess the effect of natural diuresis on the accuracy of the test. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and will be enrolled after providing informed consent.

A 2-month-old healthy baby boy was brought to the clinic for vaccination. His parents are concerned about the recent outbreak of polio in neighboring countries and want to make sure their child is protected. The baby has no significant medical history and is up to date on his routine vaccinations. The parents have signed the informed consent form and are willing to participate in the study. The baby has not received any blood products, immunosuppressant therapy, or live attenuated vaccines within the past 30 days. He has not experienced any acute illnesses or exacerbations of chronic conditions within the past 7 days. The baby's axillary temperature is normal.

A 34-year-old man with severe hemophilia A has a history of high-titer inhibitors with a Bethesda unit (BU) of 10. He has been using bypassing agents, including prothrombin complex concentrates (PCCs) and activated factor VII (rFVIIa), to treat his recurrent bleeds. In the past 6 months, he has had more than 6 bleeds requiring bypassing therapy, affecting his daily activities and quality of life. His last physical exam and lab study was performed yesterday and showed the results below: He has a well-controlled blood pressure, and his cardiovascular and respiratory systems are within normal limits. He weighs 70 kg and is 175 cm tall. Hemoglobin level is 12.5 g/dL, Platelet count is 150,000/mm3, and his liver function tests are within the normal range. His current medication includes PCCs and rFVIIa for bleeding episodes, and he is not on immune tolerance therapy.

The patient is a 9-year-old female student who lives in an urban area in the Philippines. She is currently enrolled in primary school and has no known history of developmental disabilities, medical history of cardiac or pulmonary problem, medical history of diabetes, or any sensory deficits. She is of Filipino nationality and was born and currently resides in the same area. Her parents have Filipino nationality and she has no multiracial parental background. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to explore the role of culture and environment in the regulation of behaviour in auditory processing. She will be asked to watch a silent movie and listen to a block of sound stimulus presentations while her autonomic activity (heart rate variability and electrodermal activity) will be measured and recorded using Polar H2 heart rate monitor and eSense skin response. She is excited to contribute to the research and learn more about how her culture and environment can affect her behaviour.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has a known history of sickle cell disease. He presents to the emergency department with a fever and severe pain in his arms and legs. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 24 hours. The patient's past medical history is significant for multiple hospitalizations due to vaso-occlusive crises. He is currently taking hydroxyurea for his sickle cell disease. The patient's physical examination reveals a temperature of 38.5°C, tachycardia, and diffuse tenderness in his arms and legs. His chest examination is unremarkable. As part of his workup, the patient will undergo both pulmonary ultrasound and frontal chest x-ray to evaluate for acute thoracic syndrome. The patient and his parents have provided informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

A 27-year-old male with a history of gang involvement was admitted to Harborview Medical Center for a gunshot wound to the leg. He has no known allergies and is not on any medications. He has a history of substance abuse but is currently sober. He is not currently employed but is actively seeking work. He has a high school diploma and is fluent in English. He lives in King County with his girlfriend, who is also involved in the gang. He has a cell phone and can provide alternate contacts. He plans to live in King County for at least 6 months following hospital discharge. He is willing to participate in a study to help reduce future violence and criminal activity.

A 42-year-old male with a history of retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and cystoid macular edema (CME) presents for a clinical trial investigating the therapeutic potential of recombinant human Nerve Growth Factor (rhNGF) eye drops treatment. The patient's RP is of typical and atypical forms and has a measurable ERG with a significant decrease in amplitude. The patient also has a reduction of the visual field with values of mean deviation greater than -3 decibels assessed with the Humphrey field analyzer- HFA 24-2. The patient's RP is associated with CME documented by OCT with macular thickness greater than 250 uM that has been present for at least three months and not in treatment for at least one month. The patient's best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is between 20/100 (2/10 or 0.1 logMAR) and 20/25 (8/10 or 0.7 logMAR), and the best corrected visual acuity for near does not exceed II character. The patient has no other ocular confounding diseases and is medically able to undergo the testing and study procedures required in the flowsheet of exam procedures. The patient does not have diabetes-related macular edema or macular edema associated with other causes such as choroideal neovascularization or after eye surgery. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus and has not undergone eye surgery in the previous three months. The patient does not have evidence of an active eye infection or previous uveitis or evidence of intraocular inflammation. The patient has no history or evidence of glaucoma or elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) greater than or equal to 21 mm Hg at baseline. The patient also has no abnormalities of the anterior segment or media opacities that prevent the assessment of the posterior segment of the eye. The patient has not undergone treatment with corticosteroids (systemic, periocular, or intravitreal) for at least three months and has not used any topical medication other than the study drug for the treatment of ocular pathologies. The patient does not have any systemic or ocular disease or condition that may significantly limit visual acuity or visual field, hindering the effectiveness of treatment in the study or its evaluation, or could interfere with the interpretation of the study results, or may be judged by the investigator incompatible with the visit program or with the procedures in the study. The patient is not known to have any hypersensitivity to the study drug or drugs procedural. The patient has not participated in another clinical study during the same period of this study or within 90 days of the screening visit/baseline. The patient has no history of drug use, illegal drugs, or alcohol abuse or addiction. The patient is a male and is available to use highly effective measures of birth control if needed.

A 52-year-old man presents with a history of locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. He recently underwent curative treatment with radiation therapy and surgical resection. He has completed the treatment and is currently in remission. The patient has no significant medical history and is in good overall health. His performance status is 0-1. He has no known allergies or contraindications to erlotinib. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits associated with the maintenance therapy.

A 24-year-old physically active male with a BMI of 25.5 kg/m² who exercises moderately to vigorously more than three times per week. He has no known food allergies or metabolic disorders. He is a non-smoker and has no history of chronic diseases. He follows a balanced diet but is interested in optimizing his physical performance. He consumes dairy products regularly and is willing to consume higher amounts of calcium-rich foods for the duration of the study. He is available to participate in the study for 2 weeks and willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing lower back pain for the past 6 months. The pain is mostly localized to his lower back and buttocks, and it is worse with activity. He has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy, pain medications, and chiropractic adjustments, but his symptoms have not improved. He has no history of trauma or injury to his back. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medications. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. His physical exam is notable for tenderness to palpation in his lower back and limited range of motion. Imaging studies revealed adjacent level disease (ALD) at L4-L5. His laboratory studies are within normal limits. His BMI is 28. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of his ALD.

56F with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed for the past 5 years, currently taking glyburide 10mg once daily for the past 8 months. Despite the medication, the patient's blood glucose levels remain elevated, with an HbA1c of 8.2%. The patient reports occasional episodes of hypoglycemia while taking glyburide. The patient has no history of diabetic neuropathy, retinopathy, or nephropathy. The patient is not being treated with insulin or PPAR gamma agonist. The patient has no other significant medical history or medication use. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meet all other inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital due to severe COVID-19 symptoms. He was diagnosed with SARS-CoV-2 infection by PCR test within 72 hours of hospitalization. The patient has been experiencing severe respiratory distress and requires high-flow oxygen therapy. He has never been intubated for more than 72 hours, nor has he received any convalescent plasma or COVID-19 vaccine, or anti-spike (S) SARS-CoV-2 therapy. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and comply with study requirements and restrictions. He has no history of severe chronic respiratory disease, septic shock, or shock. The ALT and AST levels are within the normal range. The patient is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. The patient is a WBCP and agrees to use an approved highly effective birth control method throughout the study. The patient is eligible for the study and will be randomized into either the SCTA01 or placebo group.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman who is concerned about the appearance of her lower eyelids due to fat bulging. She has not had any prior cosmetic facial surgery or placement of tissue fillers within the last 6 months, laser therapy or chemical peeling of midface within the preceding 3 months, and the use of topical retinoids for the face within the past 1 month. She is in good overall health with no history of keloid or hypertrophic scar, severe allergies, bleeding disorders or active skin disease on the lesional skin. The patient is willing to undergo local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine and 1:100,000 epinephrine for the treatment. She understands the treatment protocol involving the use of AGNES micro-insulated needles with radiofrequency applicators and is willing to comply with the aftercare instructions, including gentle cleansing of the face with tap water and avoiding sun exposure until the next day.

The patient is a 33-year-old woman who has had two consecutive miscarriages in the first trimester, both confirmed by ultrasound. She has no known anatomical anomalies or antiphospholipid antibodies. She and her partner are trying to conceive and are motivated to improve their lifestyle. She has a BMI of 26.5 kg/m2 and is otherwise healthy. She does not have any disabilities or medical conditions requiring a priori anticoagulation. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs. She is willing to participate in an intervention that includes regular exercise and a balanced diet to improve her chances of a successful pregnancy.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for 3 years. She is currently on metformin medication to control her blood sugar levels. Her fasting low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol is less than 160 mg/dL and triglycerides (TG) is less than 400 mg/dL. She has a sitting systolic blood pressure of less than 160 mm Hg and sitting diastolic blood pressure of less than 90 mm Hg. Her hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) is between 7% and 11%. She has not had any significant surgeries within the last 3 months, and she is not currently taking any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents or vitamins. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she is willing to use a reliable method of birth control during the study. She does not have any active infections or inflammation, and her serum creatinine, ALT, ALP, and TB levels are within normal limits. She is not currently using aspirin, nitroglycerin or long-acting nitrates and does not have any documented cerebrovascular or coronary artery disease. She is not directly affiliated with the study, nor is she an immediate family member of anyone who is.

There is no patient required for this clinical trial. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a workshop-based educational experience to improve medical students' skills in performing the pediatric physical examination.

14-year-old male student entering the first year of secondary school (Enseñanza Secundaria Obligatoria, ESO) in a selected high school in Spain. The student is generally healthy but has a Body Mass Index (BMI) indicating that he is overweight for his age and height. He is not currently involved in any structured physical activity but enjoys playing video games and watching TV. His diet consists mainly of fast food and sugary drinks, with little to no intake of fruits and vegetables. His parents are concerned about his weight and overall health and have agreed to participate in a school-based educational program aimed at promoting healthier lifestyle behaviors and reducing the risk of obesity and cardiovascular disease. The student is willing to participate and is excited to learn more about healthy eating and physical activity.

The patient is a 72-year-old male with a histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The tumor is localized and scheduled for lobectomy surgery in 20 days. The patient has a friend who will act as a caregiver before and after surgery. The patient is able to read and comprehend English, has access to a smartphone or telephone for study intervention sessions and study text messages, and is willing to wear a wristband pedometer for the duration of the study period except on the day of surgery. The patient is willing to answer telephone calls from the City of Hope Call Center.

This is a 9-year-old male with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and obesity. He has difficulty with food selectivity, but is able to eat at least 6 different foods and accepts one fruit or vegetable. He does not exhibit significant mealtime behavior problems on the Brief Autism Mealtime Behavior Inventory (BAMBI) Food Refusal subscale. His body mass index (BMI) percentile is in the obese range (> 95th percentile). His primary caregiver has agreed to participate in the study and is able to speak, understand, read, and write in English. He is not on any medication associated with weight gain in ASD and does not have any serious behavioral problems or medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study.

The patient is a healthy non-smoking 25-year-old female with a body mass index (BMI) between 19 and 30 kg/m2. She has no known history of drug allergies, food allergies, or any condition that interferes with the absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion of drugs. She has normal findings in the physical examination, 12-lead ECG and vital signs, with blood pressure between 100-140/60-90 mmHg, heart rate between 50-99 beats/min, and temperature between 35.8°C and 37.5°C. She has negative results for drugs of abuse, nicotine, hepatitis B-surface antigen, hepatitis C and HIV. She is not pregnant and is willing to use contraception up until one month after the end of the study. She has not taken any prescription medication within 14 days preceding the study and has not used over-the-counter medication (except for spermicidal/barrier contraceptive products) within 14 days preceding entry into this study. She has not participated in a clinical trial with an investigational drug within 30 days preceding this study.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl diagnosed with cystic fibrosis. She experiences frequent respiratory tract infections and has difficulty breathing, particularly during exercise. Her medical history includes regular attendance at a cystic fibrosis clinic, and she undergoes spirometry tests periodically. Her FEV1 is currently above 40% predicted for her height, age, and gender. She is compliant with her therapy and treatment protocols. She has not experienced any significant weight loss in the past six months and has no known allergies to medications. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to use appropriate contraception during the study. Her parents or legal guardian have provided written informed consent for her participation in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a cytologically confirmed diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The tumor is located in the pancreatic head and is deemed to be borderline resectable by radiographic criteria. The patient has no evidence of distant metastasis and is considered to have locally advanced disease. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and is estimated to have a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. The patient has adequate renal, hepatic, and bone marrow function. The patient has not received prior radiation therapy or chemotherapy. The patient does not have any co-morbidities that would limit their ability to comply with the protocol. The patient has no concurrent serious infection and has not had any malignancies of other histologies within the last 5 years. The patient is willing to use an effective method of birth control if in their reproductive age group.

A 30-year-old male with a regular sleep-wake pattern, typically sleeping between 6.5 to 8 hours per night, and not oversleeping by more than 3 hours on weekends. He is in good health and has no clinically significant medical abnormalities. He has no history of serious physical or psychiatric illness, and he is not currently considered a suicide risk. He has no known or suspected sleep disorder, excessive daytime sleepiness, or any other diagnosis that would interfere with assessing sleepiness. He is able to provide written, signed, and dated informed consent to participate in the study.

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his mother due to fever and cough. He has no significant past medical history and his vaccines are up-to-date. Upon examination, he is found to have a temperature of 38.5°C, a mildly elevated heart rate, and some rhonchi in his lungs. The attending pediatrician decides to collect a saliva sample from the child for the purpose of detecting human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) using direct DNA amplification, viral isolation and specific antibody measurement. The mother consents to the collection of the sample and the child is given a salivary collection kit. The kit includes 3 swabs for DNA research, 1 for antibodies research, and 1 for virus isolation by cell growth. The pediatrician collects the saliva sample from the internal face of the child's mouth using the swabs provided in the kit. The child is enrolled in the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of being aged between 3 months to 6 years and presenting to the emergency department. The mother is informed of the study and gives her consent for her child to participate.

The patient is a 64-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 2 years ago. She has been treated with lenalidomide in combination with dexamethasone for the past 3 weeks. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She denies any known allergies and reports a history of occasional alcohol use. The patient reports no symptoms related to her multiple myeloma and is able to perform all activities of daily living independently. Physical examination is unremarkable, and laboratory studies are within normal limits. The patient has been informed about the observational nature of this study and has signed an informed consent form. She will be followed up for up to 36 months after the end of her lenalidomide treatment period to assess her status. No intervention will be performed on her physician, and her treatment will be according to her physician's regular clinical practice.

The patient is a 35-year-old Caucasian male who has been experiencing symptoms of a complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI) for the past week. He complains of dysuria, urinary frequency, and suprapubic pain. He also feels feverish, with a temperature of 38.5°C. He has no significant medical history, and he is not taking any medications. He is sexually active with his girlfriend and uses condoms inconsistently. His urinalysis shows pyuria (WBC count > 10/μL in unspun urine) and moderate bacteriuria. He has not received any antibiotic treatment for the infection yet. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study. He is willing to be hospitalized for the administration of all doses of IV study therapy, and he can commit to a minimum of 35 days and a maximum of 42 days of subject participation. He does not have any allergies to β-lactams or quinolone antibacterials. He is not immunocompromised and does not have severe impairment of renal function. He meets all other inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 9-month-old male infant who was recently diagnosed with infantile-onset glycogen storage disease-II (Pompe disease). He has a medical history of poor feeding and muscle weakness, and a clinical examination revealed an enlarged liver and heart. The patient has documented GAA deficiency as illustrated by an endogenous GAA activity less than or equal to 2% of the mean of the normal range as assessed in cultured skin fibroblasts. In addition, the patient has a Left Ventricular Mass Index greater than 2 standard deviations above the mean for age. The patient and his legal guardians have provided written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. The patient is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history, and he is not currently taking any investigational products. He is eligible to receive recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase (rhGAA) as a potential enzyme replacement therapy for GSD-II, and will be closely monitored for safety and efficacy throughout the study.

45-year-old female with partial edentulism in the mandibular arch. She has good overall health with no history of smoking or metabolic disorders. She has never received radiation treatment to the head and is not pregnant. She presents with para-functional habits of bruxing and clenching. The patient is interested in receiving dental implants to improve her oral function and esthetics. She agrees to all protocol visits and is physically able to tolerate surgical and restorative dental procedures.

55-year-old male who was diagnosed with rectal cancer and underwent radiation therapy to the pelvic area 6 weeks ago. He is scheduled for a non-emergency total mesorectal excision (TME) and low anterior resection (< 10cm from the anal verge). The patient has no known allergies to nickel and is not taking regular steroid medication. The patient has signed and dated the informed consent form and understands the study procedures. The patient has no evidence of extensive local disease in the pelvis, no bowel obstruction or perforation, no peritonitis, no bowel strangulation, no local or systemic infections, and no signs of inflammatory bowel disease.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with binge eating disorder for the past year. She has a BMI of 32 and has been stable in weight for the past 3 months. She is right-handed and does not smoke. She is not currently taking any medications, and she does not plan on participating in any weight loss programs. She is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has a history of depression and anxiety, but is currently not on any medication for these conditions. She experiences frequent episodes of binge eating, which she describes as feeling out of control while consuming large amounts of food in a short period of time. She reports feeling guilty and ashamed after these episodes. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the mechanisms behind her binge eating disorder and to potentially help in the development of treatment strategies.

54-year-old male with a history of recurrent metastatic breast cancer, previously treated with multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation, presents with a palpable right axillary lymph node. Biopsy confirms metastatic breast cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria for vaccination with Flt3L, radiation, and Poly-ICLC. The patient has no active autoimmune disease, no active infection requiring systemic therapy, and no evidence of leptomeningeal disease or lymphomatous meningitis. The patient has not received any investigational therapy within 28 days prior to the first dose of treatment and has not received prior radiotherapy within 2 weeks of starting study treatment. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient has good performance status and is willing to comply with study requirements.

Patient is a 60yo male with a history of osteoarthritis in the left knee. The patient has been experiencing pain in the knee for the past few years and has been treated with various medications including acetaminophen and NSAIDs, but these have not provided adequate relief. The patient has been advised to undergo total knee replacement surgery, but is unable to schedule the surgery due to work commitments. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial and is able to comply with the study requirements. The patient has a combined WOMAC A (pain) and C (function) subscale score of 25 at screening, using the WOMAC 5-point Likert scale. The patient understands the study requirements and is able to communicate with the Investigator and site staff.

65-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 2 years ago presented to the clinic with complaints of dizziness and lightheadedness when standing up. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. He has no history of hypertension, diabetes, or coronary artery disease. He is currently taking levodopa-carbidopa for his Parkinson's disease symptoms. His vital signs are blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, heart rate 70 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Physical examination is unremarkable except for a mild tremor in his right hand. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no known drug allergies. He is able to swallow without difficulty. He is fully informed about the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

A 55 year old man with a history of hyperlipidemia, currently on a low-fat diet and exercise regimen. The patient has been taking atorvastatin 10mg daily for the past 6 months but has not achieved the desired reduction in LDL cholesterol. The patient has no known allergies, no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and no significant comorbidities. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 23-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a dengue vaccine. She has no history of neurological or behavioral disorders, seizures, drug abuse, or alcohol consumption. She has not had any allergic reactions to vaccines or mosquito bites. She is not pregnant nor planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no chronic or acute disease, and is not taking any medication that might affect her immune system. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and able to read and understand the information provided in the subject information sheet and consent form. She is available for 11 visits over the course of 9 months and is willing to undergo mosquito feedings during follow-up visits.

There is no patient description necessary for this clinical trial as it is focused on improving the management of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia through the use of information technology and the study involves pediatric providers and all newborns in the newborn nursery that meet the gestational age criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of fatigue, weakness, and occasional dizziness. She has a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and has been diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia in the past. Her current hemoglobin level is 10 g/dL, and her serum ferritin level is 15 μg/L. She is not currently taking any iron supplements or medications that may interfere with iron metabolism. She has a BMI of 25 and is otherwise healthy. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently taking any herbal supplements or antibiotics. She has no known gastrointestinal diseases or long-term illnesses requiring active treatment. She is willing to discontinue any vitamin supplements for the duration of the study. She does not have a history of asthma or any other conditions that would compromise her well-being during the study. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that the results will help improve iron supplementation options for individuals with iron deficiency anemia.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He was diagnosed with abdominal sepsis and underwent emergency abdominal surgery for bowel resection with anastomosis. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medications. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs. He has no known allergies and has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. His laboratory results are as follows: WBC count 16,000/mm3, hemoglobin 12 g/dL, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, and liver function tests within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 62-year-old Japanese female recently diagnosed with osteoporosis after experiencing a low-impact fracture in her wrist. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has no history of metabolic bone disorders or cancer in the past 5 years, and has no other severe or disabling conditions. She is concerned about the risk of further fractures and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially help improve her bone density and reduce her risk of future fractures.

A 33-year-old man was diagnosed with bipolar I disorder and is currently experiencing a manic episode. He has been experiencing symptoms such as high energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, and impulsive behavior for the past two weeks. He has tried several antipsychotic medications in the past, but they have not been effective in controlling his symptoms. He has no other mental health diagnoses and is not currently experiencing any physical health issues. He has no history of seizures or other neurological conditions. He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to provide written informed consent.

58-year-old Chinese male with a history of smoking for 40 years, currently abstinent for the last 5 years, presented with a productive cough and shortness of breath on exertion. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He reports no history of asthma or tuberculosis. He reports that his cough and shortness of breath have been present for several years. He denies any chest pain, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or lower extremity edema. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and no recent changes in weight or appetite. He has been taking tiotropium bromide inhalation powder for the past 3 months as prescribed by his physician. His BMI is 28.9. He is interested in participating in a study to learn more about COPD and to potentially improve his management of the disease.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with no history of any clinically significant medical conditions or complications. He has a body weight of 70 kg and a BMI of 22 kg/m2. He does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly. He has not undergone any surgery related to the gastrointestinal tract. He is not taking any medication with a long half-life, and has not taken any medication that may affect the results of the trial within the past 7 days. He has not participated in any other clinical trial involving an investigational drug within the past month. He is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the study site and refrain from smoking during the trial days.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II ER/PR positive, HER2 negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast, treated with lumpectomy followed by chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. She started adjuvant endocrine therapy with letrozole, and for the last few weeks, she has been experiencing hot flashes, night sweats, and joint pain. She is married and has two children. Her husband is supportive, but she is struggling to keep up with her daily activities due to her symptoms. She is currently working part-time as a teacher, and her job is important to her. She is fluent in English and has no cognitive impairment. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trial for breast cancer but is interested in participating in one that could help her manage her symptoms better. She scores 6 on the NCCN adapted distress thermometer study screening question related to her symptoms. She lives in Boston and is willing to participate in a virtual program.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with high cholesterol levels after a routine blood test. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or any other endocrine disorders. Her BMI is 26 kg/m2 and she is considered otherwise healthy. She has not taken any cholesterol-lowering prescription drugs in the last 6 months and has not used any non-prescription supplements for cholesterol lowering in the last month. She has never been diagnosed with anemia or bleeding disorders. She exercises regularly, but does not exceed 15 miles per week or 4,000 kcal per week. She has no history of eating disorders or drug and alcohol abuse. She is willing to follow the dietary recommendations and use the birth control method necessary to participate in the study. She is motivated to participate in the study and understands the importance of compliance with product consumption. She is able to give informed consent and agrees to participate in the study.

Patient B is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has been experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has also been experiencing trouble sleeping and has been feeling very anxious about the upcoming birth of her child. She has been feeling this way for several weeks and has noticed that it is starting to impact her ability to function in her daily life. She has access to broadband internet and a computer at home, as well as a smartphone, and is proficient in English. She has completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and scored a 15, indicating elevated levels of depression. She is interested in participating in the study to receive treatment for her depression and help improve outcomes for other women experiencing perinatal depression. She is not currently experiencing active suicidal ideation and is able to provide informed consent and engage in all study activities delivered in English.

A 17-year-old male with a history of epilepsy diagnosed at the age of 10. He has been experiencing recurrent seizures despite being on antiepileptic drugs for several years. He has tried two different types of antiepileptic drugs at therapeutic doses with no improvement. The seizures occur once or twice a month, are usually tonic-clonic, and last for about 1-2 minutes. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of any other neurological or gastrointestinal disorders. He lives with his family and is currently enrolled in high school. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He has not been on any antibiotics in the last 60 days, nor has he had any surgery in the last 3 months. He is not on any special diets or participating in any other clinical trials.

35 year old female, BMI of 38, undergoing Roux en Y gastric bypass surgery in 3 weeks. She has a history of obesity since childhood and has failed multiple attempts at weight loss through diet and exercise. She currently exercises regularly for at least 30 minutes, 3 days a week, and is motivated to continue with her exercise routine after surgery. She reports no chronic pain or mobility issues that would impair her participation in the study. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is interested in exploring potential methods to improve weight loss outcomes after surgery.

A 25-year-old female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and no significant medical history came to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial. She is a non-smoker and has never been pregnant. She is currently taking no medications and is not allergic to any medication. Her blood pressure was normal at 118/77 mmHg and her heart rate was 72 bpm. Her ECG showed a QTc interval of 420 msec and a QRS interval of 100 msec. She has no family history of myocardial infarction, congenital long QT syndrome, torsades de pointes or clinically significant ventricular arrhythmias. She has normal levels of potassium, magnesium and corrected calcium. She has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the study and is willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with lymphoma and is undergoing a BEAM conditioning regimen prior to an autologous stem cell transplant. She has experienced nausea and vomiting with previous chemotherapy treatments and is seeking a new treatment option to prevent these side effects. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to swallow oral medications. She has no known allergies to the study drugs and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of anxiety-induced nausea and vomiting. She is not on any medications that would interfere with the study drugs and has no other gastrointestinal conditions that would affect the absorption of the drugs. The patient is not taking any benzodiazepines as antiemetics and has no history of QT prolongation or electrolyte abnormalities.

The patient is a 30 year old healthy non-smoking female who is not taking any medications. She has no history of coagulation disorder or other illnesses. She has no acute or chronic airway problems and is willing to provide informed consent for participation in this trial. She has not engaged in extreme physical activity or consumed any polyphenol-containing food such as red wine, apples, cabbage or garlic for 24 hours prior to the study. She has not consumed any caffeine-containing drinks or dark chocolate for 48 hours prior to the study. She is willing to undergo inhalation of oxygen (80% inspiratory fraction) via reservoir-face-mask for the purpose of the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation and has been taking warfarin once daily for the past 6 months. His INR has been consistently within the target range of 2.0-3.5 and he has regular monitoring. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2. He is not taking any other medications or supplements. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has no history of coagulopathy and has not consumed any health products or supplements containing vitamin K. He is willing to be trained in the use of CoaguCheck devices.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing dry, itchy, and red eyes for the past 6 months. She has difficulty wearing contact lenses and often feels like there is something in her eye. Her symptoms are worse in the morning and towards the end of the day. She has never been diagnosed with any ocular surface corneal disease, but has been previously diagnosed with meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD). She has not had any reconstructive or cosmetic eyelid surgery that may affect the normal function of the lids. She has not undergone any invasive glaucoma or corneal surgery, nor has she had any corneal refractive surgery or cataract extraction in the past year. She has not used any ophthalmic corticosteroids, NSAIDs, antibiotics, antihistamines, or IOP lowering medication in the past 30 days. She has no serious systemic disease or uncontrolled medical condition that could confound study assessments. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 57-year-old male diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, specifically in the pharynx. He has undergone cisplatin-based chemotherapy for metastatic disease 6 months ago but has been experiencing progressive disease for the past few weeks. The patient has no known brain or bone metastasis. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. The patient takes no other medications. His ECOG performance score is 1. His physical examination is unremarkable except for a mass in the pharynx. His laboratory tests show normal absolute neutrophil count, platelets, and hemoglobin levels. Serum creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits, and AST/ALT levels are slightly elevated but less than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. The patient is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and has no known allergies.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic cluster headache (CCH) and has been experiencing severe unilateral periorbital and temporal pain attacks with autonomic symptoms for the past year. He has tried various medications for the prevention of chronic cluster headache, but they have not been effective in reducing the frequency or intensity of his attacks. He has no other significant medical or psychiatric conditions. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to commit to applying the neurostimulation outside of an attack every day for 20 minutes during 4 to 8 weeks. He is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the treatment and has provided informed consent.

A 48-year-old female patient with a history of gingival recession in her mandibular and maxillary incisors and premolars approached the clinic seeking treatment. She has no known systemic diseases and takes no medications. She does not smoke and has no history of blood-borne diseases. Her teeth are vital and have no occlusal trauma. She has no restorations or decay in the tooth neck (collum dentis) and has a completely or partially fixable enamel-cement border. She has no periodontal pockets exceeding 3 mm in the teeth undergoing treatment and they are rotation-free with no mobility. She is older than 18 years of age. She will be informed in detail about the risks and benefits of each step of the study, and her signed consent will be obtained.

The patient is a 55 year old African American male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father dying of a heart attack at the age of 63. The patient underwent a coronary angiogram which revealed significant blockages in two major coronary arteries. He underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents (DES) placed in his coronary arteries. The patient is currently on dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel. He works as a construction worker and his job requires a lot of physical activity. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin for the management of his diabetes and hypertension.

53-year-old female diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) six months ago. She underwent a right frontotemporal craniotomy with gross total resection of the tumor followed by adjuvant radiation therapy and temozolomide. Her postoperative course was unremarkable, and she was able to return to work as a teacher two months after surgery. However, she developed progressive right-sided weakness and difficulty with speech and language function. An MRI revealed progression of the tumor, and a stereotactic biopsy confirmed recurrent GBM. She was treated with bevacizumab, but her disease continued to progress. She has an ECOG performance status of 2 and is otherwise healthy. She is able to swallow intact capsules and has not received any chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, or investigational agents within the last 4 weeks. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore other treatment options for her recurrent GBM.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been experiencing knee pain for more than a year. She describes the pain as dull and achy, and it is mainly located in her right knee but also affects her left knee. The pain has been progressively getting worse, and she has difficulty walking up and down stairs and standing for long periods of time. She has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis by her primary care physician and has tried various medications and physical therapy with limited success. She is interested in alternative treatments and is willing to try acupuncture. She has no history of allergies and takes only a multivitamin daily. She lives alone and is retired. Her knee X-rays show Kellgren-Lawrence grade Ⅲ. Her VAS score is 55mm. She has not had any knee surgeries or injections in the past year. She has not received acupuncture or massage within the past month. She has no history of coagulation disorders or metal allergies. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate and has signed the informed consent.

58-year-old male diagnosed with indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) and mild anemia with hemoglobin levels ranging from 90-110 g/L. The patient has not received any anti-neoplastic therapy in the last 6 weeks and has not had any red blood cell transfusions in the last 8 weeks. The patient has a demonstrated stainable iron in bone marrow aspirate, and has not received any rhEPO treatment in the last 12 weeks or any iron therapy in the last 4 weeks. The patient is not currently experiencing any active infectious or inflammatory disease, has a performance status of 0-2 on the ECOG scale, and has no folate or B12 deficiencies. The patient's kidney function and liver function are within normal limits, and their serum ferritin levels are less than 800 ug/L. The patient is willing to use an approved contraceptive method during the study and for 3 months after the study. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian man residing in Davidson County. He was admitted to Vanderbilt University Hospital due to acute respiratory symptoms. His medical history is positive for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are managed with medication. He reports no history of smoking or alcohol use. He received the influenza vaccine this season. He has no allergies. He is married and has two adult children. His HAM-D score is 2.

10-year-old male with a history of asthma and mild eczema, scheduled for a tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy under general anesthesia. The patient is classified as ASA II and is expected to undergo a surgery lasting approximately 2 hours. There is no planned intraoperative hemorrhage exceeding 15% of their blood volume. The patient has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, and there is no central brain lesion. The patient is not receiving any psychotropic treatment or morphine agonist-antagonist. The patient has no known allergies to latex, propofol, remifentanil, morphine, muscle relaxant, or any of their components. The patient has not been previously administered remifentanil or any derivate of fentanyl, and there is no scheduled postoperative ventilation or sedation.

This clinical trial does not involve patient recruitment as it is a population-based survey of school-age children in the Caribbean region to assess their iodine status. Therefore, there is no patient description required for this study.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who is fluent in English and able to communicate effectively via mobile phone and text messaging. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and has given written informed consent to participate in the trial. She is willing to take a curative antibiotic regimen after inoculation with B. pertussis according to the study protocol. She has no inviolable commitments within 3 months of discharge from the inpatient phase of the study to make contact with unimmunized or partially immunized children and infants aged < 1 year or pregnant women >32 weeks who have not received pertussis vaccination at least a week prior to contact. She has no household contacts working with unimmunized or partially immunized children and infants aged < 1 year or pregnant women >32 weeks who have not received pertussis vaccination at least a week prior to contact. She has not participated in other interventional clinical trials in the last 12 weeks, and has no history of receiving B. pertussis vaccination in the last 5 years or never being vaccinated against B. pertussis. She is not a current smoker and has not used systemic antibiotics within 30 days of or during the challenge. She has no confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immune-deficient state, including HIV infection, asplenia, recurrent, severe infections, and chronic immunosuppressant medication within the past 6 months. She has no history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the inoculum and has no contraindications to the use of azithromycin or macrolides. She is not pregnant, lactating, or intending to become pregnant during the study. She has no clinically significant abnormal findings on biochemistry, haematology, toxicology or serological blood tests, urinalysis or clinical examination. She has no other significant disease, disorder, or finding that may significantly increase the risk to the volunteer because of participation in the study or affect the ability of the volunteer to participate in the study, for example, recent surgery to the nasopharynx.

The patient is a healthy male, aged 30, who consumes alcohol only occasionally and within the recommended limits. He has no history of tuberculosis or any other immunocompromising condition. He has not received any live vaccines or steroid treatment in the past month or biologic agents in the last three months. He has no allergies to humanized monoclonal antibodies or severe post-treatment hypersensitivity reactions. He has not had any malignancy, except for basal cell or squamous epithelial carcinomas of the skin that have been resected with no evidence of metastatic disease for 3 years. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the tolerability and pharmacokinetics of two formulations of a study drug, LY3074828. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and has provided informed consent.

A 52-year-old male veteran was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) 6 years ago. He is currently on metformin and his fasting blood sugar is well controlled. He has mild diabetic peripheral neuropathy and mild diabetic retinopathy. He is overweight with a BMI of 32 kg/m2, and he has been experiencing symptoms of hypogonadism, such as decreased libido, decreased muscle strength, and fatigue. His morning testosterone levels have been measured twice, and the average value was 250 ng/dL. He has no history of prostate or breast cancer, and his digital rectal exam was normal. He has no history of testicular disease, and his hematocrit level is within the normal range. He is not on any medication that affects bone metabolism, and he has no history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. He is a non-smoker and does not consume more than three drinks per day. He has not used any anabolic steroids or selective androgen receptor modulators. His bone mineral density T-scores are within the normal range. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of testosterone therapy on bone quality in men with diabetes and hypogonadism.

55 year old female with a history of varicose veins in her left leg causing discomfort and swelling, and some discoloration of the skin. She reports experiencing occasional pain and cramping in her left leg, particularly after prolonged periods of standing or walking. She has tried conservative treatments such as compression stockings, elevating her legs, and regular exercise, but has not seen significant improvement. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. She has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications except for occasional use of over-the-counter pain relievers for her leg discomfort. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial. She gives informed consent to participate in the MOST Study.

A 55 yo male patient who has been diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity. The patient is scheduled to receive radiation therapy with a total dose of at least 5000 cGy using 200 cGy/fraction. The patient has no open mouth sores at study entry and has no known intolerance to capsaicin. The patient has no allergy to citric acid, cherry flavorings, or FC and C red dye #3 or #40. The patient has not received prior radiotherapy to the oral mucosa and does not require tube feeding. The patient is willing to be randomized to either receive capsaicin lozenges or placebo lozenges four times daily, beginning within the first 3 days of radiation therapy and continuing during and for two weeks after radiation therapy is completed.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer within the past year. She is currently receiving care at the MGH Cancer Center and is fluent in both verbal and written English. She has recently experienced a progression on scans and is now starting a new line of breast cancer therapy. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to fill out a brief survey about her goals and preferences for care. She wants to make sure that her doctors and nurses address all of her concerns and preferences during her visits and believes that this study will help improve communication and decision-making in her breast cancer care. She is not enrolled in hospice and is medically able to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old woman, who is 6-months pregnant, is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the performance of the Dip Home-Based Dipstick Analyzer (HBDA). She has no medical history of any kidney or urinary tract problems. She is willing to provide informed consent and has facility with both hands. She is currently taking prenatal vitamins and has no known allergies to any medications. She is willing to follow the study procedures and provide a urine sample for the evaluation of the HBDA device.

Maria is a 56-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. She has a history of smoking for 25 years and has a family history of lung cancer. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but her cancer has progressed. She has no other medical problems and her performance status is 1. She has not received any immunotherapy or therapeutic anticancer vaccines before. Her brain imaging did not reveal any metastases. She is not currently experiencing any active infections or autoimmune disorders. She has a measurable lesion that has not been previously irradiated. Her HPV status is unknown since her cancer is not oropharyngeal HNSCC. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive an alternative treatment option.

The patient is a 28 year old female who is a non-smoker and has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to use a medically acceptable method of birth control throughout the study. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and has not participated in any clinical trial involving the administration of an investigational or marketed drug within the last 30 days. She is not breastfeeding and does not wear dentures or have orthodontic braces. She has no tongue piercings or surgical manipulations of the tongue. She presents as a healthy individual who meets the eligibility criteria for this bioequivalence study of TNX-102 SL 2.8 mg sublingual tablets from two manufacturers.

The patient is a 50 year old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. He has been struggling to control his blood sugar levels with diet and exercise alone and has been taking a stable dose of metformin for the past 3 months. His most recent HbA1c level was 8.5%. He has signed up for this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a new-brand of repaglinide X® in comparison to Novonorm® for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is mentally competent and willing to participate in the study. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and his liver and kidney function tests are normal. He has not participated in any other investigational drug trial within the past month.

A 25 year old female with a history of no significant medical problems presenting with a tibial plateau fracture after a skiing accident. The patient underwent an open reduction internal fixation procedure and is currently non-weight bearing. The patient is motivated to return to her previous level of function as soon as possible and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effect of a standardized early weight bearing physical therapy protocol that utilizes immersion therapy on the clinical outcomes of lower extremity periarticular fractures. The patient has no other injuries that would preclude safe participation in physical therapy.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is physically active and exercises regularly. She has no current medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She has not experienced any recent hospitalizations or surgeries. She is currently in the premenopausal phase and has regular menstrual cycles. She is a non-smoker and does not use any tobacco products. She is interested in participating in the study to gain knowledge about the effects of exercise on vascular function. She has no history of hepatic disease or infection with hepatitis B, C or HIV. She is able to give consent and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, currently taking Lisinopril 10mg daily. She has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past month, which has led to her being referred for elective coronary angiography. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or other significant medical conditions. Her family history is negative for cardiovascular disease. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has provided informed consent to participate in this study and is able to complete the experimental protocol.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis according to ACR criteria functional class II. She reports experiencing pain and stiffness in multiple joints, including her hands, wrists, and feet, and has at least 6 swollen joints and 6 tender joints on physical examination. She has been on methotrexate therapy for the past 6 months, at a stable dose of 20 mg per week with 1 mg of folic acid supplementation p.o. daily. Her C-reactive protein level at screening is 1.2 mg/dL, and her erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 30 mm/Hr. She is Rheumatoid Factor positive. She has not previously received any biologic agents for her arthritis, but has taken non-biologic DMARD therapy in the past. She is not currently taking any disease modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) other than MTX. She is not pregnant and is using two methods of contraception with her partner. She has no active infections or surgical procedures within the last 30 days. She has a history of hypertension and a mild elevation in her ALT level (1.3 ULN) at screening, but her renal function is normal. She is capable of signing the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

32-year-old African American female, living in a low-income neighborhood within one of the 16 target ZIP codes, presents to the hospital with her 7-year-old daughter, who has been experiencing severe abdominal pain and vomiting. The patient reports that her daughter has been sick for several days, and she has not been able to afford to take her to a doctor until now. She is the primary caregiver of her daughter and also has two other children at home. The patient reports that she struggles to put food on the table for her family and often has to skip meals to make sure her children have enough to eat. She reports that she has never heard of community-based food supports and is interested in learning more about them. The patient speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study. She reports no prior experience with the HealtheRx program.

A 62-year-old female presents with a history of severe COPD for the past 5 years. She has been on optimized treatment as recommended by the SPLF and has not experienced an exacerbation in the past 3 months. She has been weaned from tobacco for the past 8 months and has received pneumococcal vaccination. She has not participated in a pulmonary rehabilitation program in the past 6 months. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she is taking medications. She denies any history of malignancy, colonized bacterial infections, or recent hospitalizations. She reports occasional dyspnea with daily activities and uses her rescue inhaler 2-3 times a day. She has not used nebulized bronchodilators at home in the past 6 months. She is not currently under non-invasive ventilation and has no indication for oxygen therapy in the coming year. Her physical exam is remarkable for decreased breath sounds and expiratory wheezing. Her FEV1 is 35% of the theoretical value. She is not pregnant.

55 yo F with a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, referred by her primary care physician for evaluation of metabolic syndrome. She reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in processed foods. Physical exam reveals a waist circumference of 100 cm, and blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg. Fasting blood glucose is 6.5 mmol/L, triglycerides are 2.2 mmol/L, and HDL cholesterol is 0.9 mmol/L. The patient is a non-smoker with no history of diabetes or sleep apnea. She is not currently taking any medications that would affect the measured parameters. The patient is interested in making lifestyle changes to improve her health and is willing to participate in a study to determine the effects of dietary weight loss and exercise on metabolic and cardiovascular parameters.

3-year-old girl diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 1 year ago. She is currently using an insulin pump and a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) to manage her blood sugar levels. Her parents are familiar with the carbohydrate ratio for meal boluses and have experience managing her diabetes. She has a total daily insulin dose of 8 units/day and weighs 30 lbs. She has no history of severe hypoglycemic events with seizure or loss of consciousness in the last 3 months or history of more than one DKA event in the last 6 months. She does not have any chronic renal disease or adrenal insufficiency, and her hypothyroidism is adequately treated. She is proficient in reading and writing English, and her parents are willing to participate in all training sessions as directed by study staff. She is not currently using any non-insulin glucose-lowering agents and does not have any conditions that would put her at risk according to the study procedure manual.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a newly diagnosed breast cancer. The biopsy showed that the tumor is HER2 positive and hormone receptor negative. The tumor is unifocal and the size is 3 cm. The patient has no evidence of metastasis. She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy including taxol and Herceptin for 12 weeks. After the completion of neoadjuvant therapy, the patient underwent image-guided biopsy, which showed that there is no residual cancer in the breast. The patient is interested in breast-conserving therapy and is willing to consider participating in the clinical trial that aims to eliminate surgery after systemic therapy in treating patients with HER2 positive or triple negative breast cancer. The patient has no history of any other cancer and is not pregnant. The patient has undergone nodal ultrasound, which shows no more than four suspicious lymph nodes.

A 56-year-old man was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 6 months ago. He has been trying to manage his blood sugar levels with diet and exercise alone but has not achieved adequate glycemic control. His HbA1c level is currently 8.5%. He has a BMI of 32 kg/m^2 and has no significant past medical history. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is currently taking no medications. He is able and willing to monitor his blood glucose levels at home and record them in a diary. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. He is not currently pregnant or lactating, and he agrees to use adequate contraception during the study period. He is fluent in English and able to comply with the study requirements. He has no other physical or psychiatric conditions that may affect the study outcomes.

A 48-year-old woman presents with a history of obesity and type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. She is currently on metformin and insulin therapy to control her blood sugar levels. She reports fatigue and mild discomfort in the upper right quadrant of her abdomen. Her medical history reveals that she has high blood pressure and high cholesterol levels for which she is on medication. She does not drink alcohol nor does she smoke. Her BMI is 32 kg/m² and her waist circumference is 104 cm. Her fasting glucose level is 8.5 mmol/L. She has not undergone bariatric surgery nor has she taken any steatosis-inducing medication. She has no history of liver disease or other chronic medical conditions. She has medical insurance and has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She has no metallic foreign body or pacemaker and is not claustrophobic.

A 62-year-old male patient presents with chronic knee pain and stiffness that has been ongoing for the past year. The pain is localized to the right knee joint and is described as a dull ache that worsens with prolonged standing or walking. The patient reports difficulty with ascending and descending stairs and reports a decrease in physical activity due to the pain. The patient has a history of obesity and hypertension but is otherwise healthy. The patient has tried over-the-counter pain medications with no relief. The patient's primary care physician has recommended Euflexxa (hyaluronic acid) injections as a treatment option. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the characteristics of synovial fluid and cartilage matrix in osteoarthritic knee after hyaluronic acid injection. The patient has Kellgren-Lawrence grade II on prior x-rays and has a knee pain score of 60 mm on a 100 mm visual analogue scale for the past month. The patient does not have any contraindication to MRI and has not received viscosupplementation therapy within the past 6 months.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 2 years ago. Despite treatment with mesalamine, the patient is still experiencing active disease. The patient's symptoms include bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and urgency. The patient has a disease extent of more than 15 cm. The patient has not undergone colon resection and has no history of toxic megacolon or fulminant colitis. The patient has no evidence of infectious colitis, celiac disease, or bleeding hemorrhoids. The patient has no history of ischemic heart disease, myocardial infarction, peripheral arterial disease, ischemic stroke, or transient ischemic attack. The patient has no severe concomitant renal, endocrine, or psychiatric disorder. The patient has no known systemic disease or history of cancer in the last five years. The patient's hepatic function is normal, and there is no evidence of liver cirrhosis. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to soy or Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP). The patient has not been treated with steroids, methotrexate, Tumor necrosis factor-alpha-antagonists, azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, anti-integrin, or coumarins. The patient has not been treated with other investigational drugs. The patient is not pregnant, and there is no intention of pregnancy or breast-feeding.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of generalized anxiety disorder for the past 2 years. She reports feeling anxious most of the time, with frequent episodes of panic attacks characterized by shortness of breath, sweating, and rapid heartbeat. She has not experienced any major life stressors recently and there is no significant history of alcohol or drug use. She has never been pregnant or lactating. She has no known allergies and takes no medications. She has a family history of hypertension and anxiety disorders. Her physical exam is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and no evidence of any significant medical conditions. She has a HAM-A scale score of 25. She has not undergone psychotherapy and has no history of depression or suicidal ideation. She has no known heart, liver, lung or kidney conditions, and no history of gastrointestinal ulcers, hyperthyroidism, neoplasia or coagulation disorders.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who underwent a traumatic transtibial amputation of her left leg 2 years ago. She has been using a prosthesis with an active vacuum-assisted suspension system for at least 6 months and 6 hours a day. She is classified as a Medicare functional level K4, indicating that she is highly active. She enjoys jogging and other outdoor activities and is seeking to improve her functional capacity, reduce residual limb pain, and increase overall satisfaction with her prosthesis. She has no history of neurological, cardiovascular, or pulmonary diseases that could affect her walking performance. She is willing to participate in the study and follow all the necessary procedures.

The patient is a 26-year-old English-speaking male with no significant medical history. He has no prior experience of chronic pain disorders and is not currently experiencing any pain. He has no history of cardiovascular, neurological, pulmonary, kidney, or liver diseases. The patient does not have any degenerative neuromuscular disease, nor any history of cancer in the past three years. He does not have a severe psychiatric condition, such as schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, and has not been hospitalized for any psychiatric condition in the past three years. The patient does not have nasal polyps or any history of chronic intranasal drug use. He has no history of drug or alcohol dependence or abuse in the past three months. The patient is not taking any antidepressants, ADHD medication, non-over-the-counter painkillers, methadone, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, and/or narcotics. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is not color-blind, does not have impaired or uncorrected hearing, and is right-handed. The patient does not have any allergies or sensitivities to creams, lotions, or food coloring. He has no non-organic implants or non-removable metal devices, such as a pacemaker, cochlear implants, stents, surgical clips, or non-removable piercings. He has not suffered any prior eye injury and does not have a foreign body in the eye. The patient does not have any persistent functional impairment due to a head trauma. He is not afraid of closed spaces and does not have any other contraindications for MRI. The patient has not participated in any "Pain Perception in the Brain" studies in the Colloca lab previously, nor has he failed any drug tests.

Patient is a 65-year-old male who was previously tested for celiac disease as part of routine lab work. However, the results were not communicated to him and he is unaware of his status. The patient has a history of chronic diarrhea, bloating, and abdominal pain, but no formal diagnosis of celiac disease. He is interested in participating in the study to determine if his symptoms are related to undiagnosed celiac disease and to potentially benefit from treatment. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to undergo further testing and follow-up appointments as part of the study.

A 50-year-old female diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma and currently undergoing medical therapy to control intraocular pressure (IOP). Despite the current treatment, the patient is experiencing inadequate IOP control and progression of the disease based on the optic nerve head appearance and visual field changes. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the safety and efficacy of two different drops, brimonidine 0.1% and apraclonidine 0.5%, which will be given prior to a glaucoma laser procedure. The patient is able to understand and provide informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to follow study instructions and attend all required visits. The patient does not have a documented allergy to either brimonidine or iopidine and does not have angle-closure glaucoma, congenital/juvenile glaucoma, neovascular glaucoma, or active uveitis.

45-year-old male with a BMI of 42 and a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents with a desire to undergo gastric bypass surgery. He has tried various diets and exercise regimens in the past with minimal success in achieving significant weight loss.
