He currently takes metformin and lisinopril for his diabetes and hypertension, respectively. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has not engaged in regular exercise for several years. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of high-intensity exercise before gastric bypass surgery on postoperative outcomes.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer with a history of a mastectomy and axillary node dissection. She has received adjuvant chemotherapy with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide for six cycles. The patient has no known allergies, and there is no significant family history of cancer. She is in good physical condition with no significant comorbidities. Her vital signs are stable and her ECOG performance status is 1. Physical examination is unremarkable, except for mild tenderness in the surgical scar site. Her laboratory workup shows a WBC of 4,500/µL, platelets of 120,000/µL, hematocrit of 37%, and normal liver and renal function tests. There is no evidence of active infection or HIV infection. She is not pregnant and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient has no history of organ transplantation or immunodeficiency diseases. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits of the therapy.

A 55-year-old male patient is scheduled for lumbar decompression and fusion surgery for chronic low back pain that has been present for over a year. The patient reports constant pain in the lower back that is aggravated by prolonged standing or sitting. The pain is described as aching and burning with occasional sharp shooting pain radiating down the right leg. The patient has tried conservative measures including physical therapy, chiropractic care, and pain medications with limited relief. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus for which he takes medications. He has a BMI of 32 and is a former smoker. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of thromboembolic or ischemic events. He is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was diagnosed with glioblastoma, a type of brain cancer, that has progressed based on imaging or surgery. He has measurable disease and has received no more than 3 prior chemotherapy regimens. He has recovered from the toxicity of prior therapy and has an interval of at least 3 months since the completion of the most recent course of radiotherapy; at least 3 weeks since last non-nitrosourea containing chemotherapy regimen or molecularly targeted agent; at least 6 weeks since the completion of a nitrosourea containing chemotherapy regimen. He has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks and is able to tolerate MRIs. He is willing to use adequate, highly effective contraception measures while on study and for at least 45 days after the last dose of study drug. He has not undergone any major surgical procedure or significant traumatic injury within 28 days of starting therapy or minor surgical procedure within 7 days. He is not currently receiving other study agents or prior therapy with an anti-VEGF agent. He has no history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to tivozanib. He is not receiving any medications or substances that are inhibitors or inducers of CYP450 enzymes. He has no significant cardiovascular disease, non-healing wound, bone fracture or skin ulcer. He has no active peptic ulcer disease, inflammatory bowel disease, ulcerative colitis or other gastrointestinal condition with increased risk of perforation; abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation or intra-abdominal abscess within 4 weeks prior to administration of first dose of study drug. He has no uncontrolled intercurrent illness, significant thromboembolic or vascular disorders within 6 months prior to administration of first dose of study drug, significant bleeding disorders within 6 months prior to administration of first dose of study drug, currently active second primary malignancy, or HIV positive and on combination antiretroviral therapy. He is able to swallow capsules, has no malabsorption syndrome or gastrointestinal disease that severely affects the absorption of study drugs, major resection of the stomach or small bowel, or gastric bypass procedure.

A 32-year-old male came to the clinic seeking treatment for cocaine dependence. He has been using cocaine for the past 5 years, and recently, he has been struggling to quit. He reports experiencing strong cravings and urges to use cocaine when he encounters drug-related cues, which often leads to relapse. He has no history of other substance abuse, except for occasional alcohol use. He has no significant medical history, except for a mild asthma that is controlled with an inhaler. He works as a freelance graphic designer and is currently single. He is willing to remain abstinent from all drugs of abuse, except for nicotine, and is willing to participate in random assignment to the DCS vs. placebo conditions. He lives within a 20-mile radius of the research facility and has reliable transportation. He is willing to undergo fMRI scanning procedures before and after the extinction protocol to examine the neural substrates of extinction learning. He is right-handed, and there is no evidence of any significant hematological, endocrine, cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, gastrointestinal, or neurological disease. He is not taking any medications that could adversely interact with study medications. He is willing to maintain abstinence from alcohol and other drugs of abuse (except nicotine) prior to and between the cue procedures. He is not currently taking any psychoactive medication or anti-seizure medications that could potentially interfere with fMRI.

A 16-year-old male patient has been admitted to the hospital due to recent suicide ideation. The patient has a history of drinking alcohol in the past three months, which was confirmed by a screening question. The patient is between the ages of 13-17 and owns a smartphone along with his parent/guardian. The patient communicates fluently in English and has no developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, or psychosis. The patient's parent/guardian will also participate in the study. The primary goal of this study is to test the acceptability and feasibility of iASIST (integrated Alcohol and Suicide Intervention for Suicidal Teens), a novel adjunctive intervention for alcohol use and alcohol-related suicidal thoughts and behaviors for suicidal adolescent inpatients. The study will involve an individual intervention with the adolescent in which motivational enhancement techniques are used to explore alcohol use as a risk factor for continued suicide-related thoughts and behaviors in order to build the adolescent's motivation to reduce or stop their alcohol use and to create a complementary change plan. Additionally, there will be a family intervention in which the interventionist facilitates a discussion between the adolescent and parent about the change plan using motivational enhancement techniques to align the parent with the adolescent to strengthen the adolescent's self-efficacy and commitment to the change plan as well as the parent's ability to support the adolescent in their plan to reduce or stop drinking. Finally, there will be a post-discharge mHealth booster to adolescents focused on strengthening their commitment to the change plan, and to parents focused on their commitment, confidence, and ability related to supporting the adolescent in reducing or stopping drinking.

A 58-year-old woman with a history of chronic bronchitis and severe COPD (FEV1 post-bronchodilator less than 50% predicted) presents with shortness of breath and frequent exacerbations. She has been receiving bronchodilator treatment but her symptoms have not significantly improved. The patient is interested in participating in the post-marketing surveillance study of Roflumilast being conducted in Korea as an add-on to her current treatment regimen. She has not previously participated in this study and is willing to sign the informed consent form. Her liver function tests and immune system are within normal limits, and she does not have any active infections or cancer. The patient has never experienced depression with suicidal thoughts or behaviors and does not have any genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. She is excited to participate in this study to potentially improve her COPD symptoms and contribute to the real-life evaluation of Roflumilast's safety and efficacy.

A 45-year-old female presented with chronic low back pain that has been continuously present for 18 months. She has no specific history of trauma to the back, but the pain started gradually and has been persistent. She experiences pain with prolonged sitting and standing, and sometimes even during walking. She has tried various treatments, including analgesics, physical therapy, and massage therapy, but with no significant improvement. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her low back pain. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of physiotherapeutic interventions on quality of life in patients with chronic low back pain.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is scheduled for a cesarean section due to a breech presentation of her baby. She has no history of allergy to drugs or significant medical conditions. The patient is at 38 weeks gestational age and has had an uneventful pregnancy so far. She has opted for a regional anesthesia for the cesarean section. The incision will be made in the lower abdomen (pfannenstiel incision). The patient is concerned about pain after the surgery and is willing to participate in the study to help reduce her postoperative pain. The patient has been provided with a detailed explanation of the study design and the risks and benefits of the study. She has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension. He has a history of smoking and has been a heavy smoker for over 20 years. He reports experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain during physical activity. He is currently taking medications for his condition, which have helped to improve his symptoms. He owns a smartphone and has internet access at home. The patient has not participated in any pulmonary rehabilitation programs in the past. He is eager to participate in this study to improve his exercise capacity and quality of life. He has no cognitive, sensory, or musculoskeletal limitations that would preclude him from participating in an exercise program.

The patient is a 16-year-old girl who was admitted to the hospital with a major cutaneous abscess on her right leg. She has a history of recurrent skin infections and has been diagnosed with cellulitis in the past. She presents with pain and redness around the abscess, with a surface area of approximately 100 cm2. She has a fever of 38.5°C and her white blood cell count is elevated. The patient weighs 65 kg and has no significant medical history. She has no known allergies to antibiotics. She is suspected to have an acute bacterial skin and skin structure infection caused by a Gram-positive pathogen. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive treatment with either oral CEM-102 or oral linezolid for 10 days.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and is scheduled to undergo surgical treatment. He is a non-smoker and has a history of a healthy lifestyle, including regular physical activity and a balanced diet. He is fluent in English and has received approval from his doctor to participate in the study. He is interested in the study and has invited his spouse to join him as a buddy.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 17 weeks pregnant with a viable singleton pregnancy. She has a history of one previous uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery. She is seeking an abortion due to personal reasons and has decided to participate in this clinical trial. The patient is fluent in English and has no known allergies to any medications. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any prescription medications. She is able to give informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol. The patient is looking for a less uncomfortable method for cervical preparation for the D&E procedure and is interested in participating in this study to help contribute to the research in this area.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a longstanding history of type 1 diabetes for more than 5 years. He was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 16. He has been on insulin therapy since then but has been experiencing complications such as frequent hypoglycemia and decreased quality of life. His fasting c-peptide levels are not detectable. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of oral GABA treatment. He is not on any immunosuppressant therapy or oral/injected anti-diabetic medications other than insulin. His HbA1c is within the acceptable range. He has no history of cancer, sleeping apnea, or pulmonary disorder with carbon dioxide retention in blood. He has no history of epilepsy, myasthenia gravis, head trauma or cerebrovascular accident, or clinical features of continuous motor unit activity in proximal muscles. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has no significant illness other than diabetes within 2 weeks prior to the first dosing. He is not known to have any hypersensitivity to benzodiazepines or any excipients of study drugs. He is willing to comply with the provisions of the protocol and follow the study procedures.

56 year old man with newly diagnosed essential hypertension. He has never been on any drug therapy for hypertension and has not taken any medication for at least 2 weeks prior to entering the study. His blood pressure readings are consistently high with MSDBP 95 mmHg and MSSBP 150 mmHg. He will be randomized to either receive amlodipine alone or a combination of losartan and amlodipine to determine if the combination is non-inferior in lowering blood pressure compared to amlodipine alone. He has no known secondary hypertension or any intolerance or contraindication to dihydropyridines or angiotensin II receptor blockers. He is not currently taking any antihypertensive medications.

10-year-old male with intellectual deficiency and no clear diagnosis after initial evaluation. The patient is currently enrolled in special education classes and has been experiencing difficulty with academic and social activities. There is no family history of intellectual deficiency or any known genetic conditions. The patient has not previously undergone genetic investigations. The patient has national health insurance coverage and both parents have agreed to provide samples for genetic testing. The patient does not have any learning disorders.

A 65-year-old man was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising. He underwent induction chemotherapy and achieved complete remission. The bone marrow biopsy performed within 4 weeks of treatment initiation confirmed the remission. However, due to his age and medical history, he is not a candidate for allogeneic stem cell transplant. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He has a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Scale. His screening labs were performed within 10 days of treatment initiation and were within normal limits. He has not received any transfusions in the preceding 2 weeks. He agreed to use an acceptable birth control method as he is sexually active with his partner. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of pembrolizumab on the duration of remission in AML.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD. He struggles with inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity, which have impacted his academic performance and social interactions. He has previously tried medication but has not found it to be effective or tolerable. His parents have noticed that he has difficulty staying focused for long periods and often interrupts others during conversations. He has no significant medical history and takes no other medications. He has no known cardiovascular disease or other serious medical conditions. He speaks English fluently, and his parents have provided written informed consent for him to participate in the study. He has previously undergone genotyping, which confirmed the presence of a specific gene mutation implicated in glutamatergic signaling and neuronal activity. He scored ≥28 on the ADHD-RS-5 at the Baseline Visit and meets DSM-5 criteria for a primary diagnosis of ADHD. He does not have any significant emotional problems that could interfere with the study evaluations.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with psoriasis, a chronic autoimmune disorder that causes red, scaly patches on the skin. She has been experiencing a significant amount of stress and emotional distress due to the appearance of the patches and the effect they have on her daily life. She has tried various treatments with little success and is interested in exploring alternative therapies. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing two mindfulness-based interventions to determine their effectiveness in reducing her psoriasis symptoms and improving her psychological well-being. She is open to giving blood samples at various intervals throughout the course of the study and completing self-report questionnaires to help researchers better understand the link between immune functioning and psychological factors. She has not participated in a formal 8-week mindfulness program in the past and does not have any extraneous health issues that may influence immunological activity.

This is a 56-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol use who was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal. The patient presented with symptoms of rectal bleeding, pain, and difficulty with bowel movements. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of SCC of the anal canal, and staging studies showed T3N1M0 disease. The patient is in good general health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Laboratory studies showed adequate medullar function, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2.0 x 10^9/L, platelets of 120 x 10^9/L, and hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL. The patient has normal liver and kidney function, with AST and ALT levels within normal limits, and a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL. The patient has not had any major surgical procedures within the last 4 weeks and has no history of systemic or psychiatric disease. The patient has not received any previous treatment for anal canal carcinoma or any other cancer. The patient has signed a written informed consent and is willing to participate in this study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has a long-standing history of peripheral arterial disease (PAD). He presents with pain and cramps in his lower legs, especially during walking or exercise, and has a non-healing ulcer on his right foot. He has undergone multiple revascularization procedures in the past, but they have been unsuccessful. He is currently on a statin and an anti-platelet agent for his PAD. His blood pressure is well-controlled with medication, and he has no other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve blood perfusion in critical limb ischemia (CLI) and reduce the risk of amputation.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman scheduled to undergo a laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. She has no history of previous surgeries or medical conditions, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She is fluent in both English and Spanish and is willing to give informed consent for the study. There are no contraindications for her participation in the study, and she meets all the inclusion criteria. She has not taken any anticoagulant medications such as heparin or Plavix. Her platelet count is greater than 100,000/mm3, and her INR is less than 2. She has no history of nasal obstruction or any other condition that would compromise her safety or the quality of the data.

A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and ischemic cardiomyopathy presented to the emergency department with dizziness and palpitations. He underwent an electrocardiogram, which revealed complete heart block, and he was subsequently implanted with a dual-chamber pacemaker. The procedure was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home with a plan for follow-up care. However, due to the patient's comorbidities and previous history of infections, the patient is considered high-risk for developing CIED infections. The treating physician suggests that the patient may benefit from prophylactic treatment with continuous in-situ ultra high-dose antibiotics (CITA) under regulated negative pressure-assisted wound therapy (RNPT) prior to any future replacement of the device. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of this prophylactic treatment in high-risk patients.

A 5-year-old boy was brought in by his mother due to complaints of ear pain and fever. He has been experiencing symptoms for the past two days, and his mother noticed that he had trouble sleeping and was more irritable than usual. The boy has no significant past medical history, and his immunizations are up to date. He attends kindergarten where he interacts with other children daily. He has never had ear infections before. His mother states that he is allergic to penicillin and has had a reaction in the past. The boy is cooperative during the examination, but he appears to be in discomfort and has a fever of 101.5°F. Upon examination, there is erythema and bulging of the left tympanic membrane with decreased mobility. The right tympanic membrane appears normal. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial evaluating the effects of telithromycin in children with acute otitis media.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She has a history of multiple abdominal surgeries, including a hysterectomy, appendectomy, and cholecystectomy. CT scan of the abdomen revealed a small bowel obstruction caused by abdominal adhesions. She was admitted to one of the 6 participating centers in Denmark and consented to participate in the study. Her medical records will be reviewed to collect relevant clinicopathological demographics, including her age, medical history, imaging studies, laboratory results, and treatment course. The patient will be followed up for 90 days after the start of treatment, and her long-term outcomes will be assessed at 1, 3, and 5 years follow-up. She meets the inclusion criteria for this observational study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old male with a history of marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) that has relapsed after the initial chemotherapy regimen was unsuccessful. He has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a smoking habit for the past 20 years. The patient is currently taking lisinopril for his hypertension and simvastatin for hyperlipidemia. Upon examination, the patient's platelet count is found to be low, which is a common side effect of the medication he was previously on. The patient has not been on any other anti-cancer treatment for the past 21 days and has adequate renal and hepatic function. The patient is willing to comply with contraception measures and understands the informed consent process. The patient has an ECOG performance status grade of 1, which indicates that he is able to carry out light work but is restricted in physically strenuous activity.

This is a 62-year-old female with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia who presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. She was found to have evidence of myocardial ischemia on her initial diagnostic workup, which prompted a coronary angiogram. The angiogram showed a visually estimated stenosis of > 50% and < 100% in a major artery, with a target lesion length of 22 mm. She was deemed a suitable candidate for stenting and was offered participation in the SPIRIT V Diabetic sub-study. She provided written informed consent and was randomized to receive the XIENCE V® EECSS. Her target vessel reference diameter was estimated to be 3.5 mm, and the target lesion was located within the left anterior descending artery. She did not meet any of the exclusion criteria and was able to undergo the required follow-up examinations. She received a maximum of 2 stents, and her target lesion was successfully treated.

54 yo F scheduled for elective primary unilateral first metatarsal bunionectomy surgery (osteotomy and internal fixation) with no collateral procedures. The patient has a history of chronic back pain and has been on opioid analgesics for the past 2 months. She has been advised to discontinue opioids 4 days prior to surgery. She has no known allergies to opioids and is willing to provide written informed consent prior to any study procedures. The patient is able to communicate clearly with the Investigator and staff. She has no history of alcohol, opiate or other drug abuse or dependence within 12 months prior to screening. She is willing and able to refrain from alcohol consumption for a period beginning 24 hours prior to surgery through the end of the Treatment Period. She has not taken non-opioid analgesics (including cyclooxygenase-2 [COX-2] inhibitors) or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) within 12 hours of the Baseline assessments. The patient has not taken any prescription or over-the-counter medication within 4 days prior to surgery that, in the opinion of the Investigator, is expected to confound the analgesic response. The patient has no clinically significant condition or a significant laboratory abnormality that would preclude study participation. She has not received another investigational drug within 30 days of scheduled surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese male who was recently diagnosed with avascular osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH). He has a history of glucocorticoid therapy, with a total dose equivalent to 2500 mg of Prednisone over the last 3 months. He is experiencing pain and discomfort in his hip joint, which has been affecting his mobility and quality of life. He does not have any history of trauma in the lower limbs or pelvis, and has not been addicted to alcohol. His medical records show no evidence of renal failure, organ transplant, graft versus host disease, inflammatory bowel disease, HIV infection or leukemia. The patient has no family history of idiopathic ONFH. He has given his written informed consent voluntarily to participate in the trial. The patient is an otherwise healthy individual with no other significant medical history.

A 40 year old man presented to the cardiology clinic with a history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and fatigue for the last 6 months. He had no history of chest pain or myocardial infarction. His medical history revealed idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy and he was on optimized medical treatment. Physical exam revealed a regular heart rhythm, a grade 3/6 holosystolic murmur heard best at the left lower sternal border and bibasilar crackles. His 12-lead ECG showed left ventricular hypertrophy and left bundle branch block. Echocardiography revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40%. The patient was informed about the clinical trial involving the infusion of autologous bone marrow cells and showed interest in participating.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) for the past 2 years. He has never received any treatment for his CLL. He is generally in good health, with no other chronic medical conditions. He has not had any previous exposure to the shingles vaccine or the live varicella zoster virus (VZV) vaccine (Zostavax). He has not had any active, symptomatic VZV or herpes zoster infection within the last 12 months. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, meaning he is fully active, but with some limitation in physically strenuous activity. He is fluent in English and able to comprehend the investigational nature of the protocol and provide informed consent.

A 57-year-old female with a history of extensive stage small cell lung cancer, previously treated with first-line chemotherapy, presented with worsening dyspnea on exertion, cough, and fatigue. Imaging studies showed disease progression with new lung nodules and pleural effusions. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. She does not have any symptomatic brain metastases or uncontrolled medical conditions that would affect her ability to receive the study regimen. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits. She has negative pregnancy test results and is willing to use appropriate methods of contraception during the study. The patient has not received any investigational drug in the past 30 days and does not have a history of Grade ≥ 2 peripheral neuropathy. She does not have any known hypersensitivity or intolerance to study-related medications or their excipients. The patient does not have any other active malignant tumors, and her bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function meet the eligibility criteria.

A 56 year old male patient is diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer that is unresectable. The patient has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating and changes in bowel habits for the past few months. The biopsy confirmed the presence of BRAFV600E mutation in the tumor tissue. The patient has not received any prior treatment for cancer and is eligible for first-line treatment with drugs registered for mCRC in his country. The patient has provided informed consent for the use of his data in the study. The patient is from a European country and will be enrolled in a multi-center longitudinal study to document the current practices for first-line treatment of BRAF-mutant mCRC, and their effectiveness and safety in a real-world setting.

The patient is a 27-year-old Caucasian female with a body mass index (BMI) of 31 kg/m2. She has not been pregnant in the past year and has had only one previous pregnancy. She does not have any chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, epilepsy, cancer, or kidney disease, and has not experienced any acute illnesses such as pneumonia or urinary tract infections recently. She is not a current smoker and has not used any antibiotics or dietary supplements including multivitamins in the past 30 days. Her typical alcohol consumption is less than 2 drinks per day, and she has not consumed any alcohol in the week preceding testing. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine if there is a difference in the short-term response in serum folate after a single dose of folic acid in normal weight and obese women of childbearing age. The study requires participants to be female, between the ages of 18-35, and have a BMI of 18.5-24.9 or >30 kg/m2.

A 38-year-old woman presents with chronic migraine for the past 5 years. She reports having headaches at least 5 days per month, lasting for several hours. She currently takes triptans for her migraines and has been taking them for the past 3 years. She reports that the triptans provide some relief, but the headaches still interfere with her daily life. She has no significant past medical history or allergies. She does not smoke and only drinks alcohol occasionally. Her blood pressure, heart rate, and BMI are all within normal limits. She reports feeling stressed and anxious due to her chronic headaches. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of an interdisciplinary multimodal integrated care program for her chronic migraine.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with pancreatic cancer of the head and peri-ampullary area. He has been experiencing jaundice, abdominal pain, and weight loss for the past 2 months. His medical history includes high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has never had any prior abdominal surgeries. After undergoing several imaging tests and a biopsy, he was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer and advised to undergo a cephalic duodenopancreatectomy as part of his curative treatment plan. He was informed about the possibility of infectious complications post-surgery due to biliary contamination during preoperative bile duct drainage, and was given an information leaflet to read and discuss with his support person. He agreed to participate in this observational prospective study and will be hospitalized in the ICU for post-operative care.

A 19-year-old patient has been diagnosed with high-grade glioma without H3 K27M or BRAFV600 mutations. The patient has no prior history of tumor-directed therapy, including radiation therapy, chemotherapy, molecularly targeted agents, or immunotherapy. The patient must have a performance status corresponding to Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scores of 0, 1, or 2. The patient must have eligibility confirmed by rapid central pathology and central molecular screening reviews performed on APEC14B1. The patient has a negative result for H3 K27M by immunohistochemistry (IHC) and a negative result for BRAFV600 mutation by next-generation sequencing (NGS). Pre-operative and post-operative brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with and without contrast must be obtained. The patient must not have received any prior tumor-directed therapy including radiation therapy, chemotherapy (tumor-directed therapy), molecularly targeted agents, or immunotherapy for the treatment of HGG other than surgical intervention and/or corticosteroids. The patient must be enrolled and protocol therapy must be projected to begin no later than 31 days after definitive diagnostic surgery (Day 0). The patient must not have known constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMR-D)/biallelic mismatch repair deficiency (bMMRD). Sexually active patients of reproductive potential are not eligible unless they have agreed to use an effective contraceptive method for the duration of their study participation and for 6 months after the last dose of protocol-specified chemotherapy.

Lila is a 8 year old girl who has been struggling with attention and focus in school. Her parents and teachers have noticed that she is easily distracted, forgetful, and has trouble completing tasks. She often interrupts others and has difficulty waiting her turn. Lila's parents brought her to the clinic for evaluation and she was diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) based on standardized clinical diagnostic tools. She has no history of major depression, bipolar, or autism. She has never taken any psychotropic medication for a condition other than ADHD. Lila has not experienced any seizures, severe head injuries, or loss of consciousness. She has no known intolerance to guanfacine. She has given her assent and her parents have given their consent for her to participate in the clinical trial.

32F with a history of neuropathic POTS presents with symptoms of muscle weakness and pain, as well as increased muscle fatigue upon physical activity. She reports difficulties in sticking to a regular aerobic exercise routine due to exercise intolerance and reduced sweat production of the extremities. She has been previously diagnosed with POTS and is currently taking medications for it. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. She is interested in participating in a study examining muscular and cutaneous dysfunction in POTS using MVRC recordings, dependent both on orthostatic stress and exercise training as well as body temperature regulation. She is able to adhere to the training protocol and provides informed consent for the study.

Patient is a 6-year-old boy from Taiwan who attends a nearby primary school. His parents report that he is a picky eater and often refuses to eat vegetables and fruits. He is an active child who enjoys playing sports and games with his friends. He has no significant medical history and has not experienced any recent acute illnesses. His parents report that he has a normal BMI for his age and height. The family's socioeconomic status is middle-income, and they have access to a varied diet. The parents are willing to sign the consent form and complete the questionnaire for their child's participation in the study.

62-year-old male with a history of pancreatic adenocarcinoma that has progressed on prior chemotherapeutic regimens. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has been diagnosed with evaluable or measurable disease per RECIST 1.1. He has adequate hematological, hepatic, and renal function. The patient has not received any antibody/drug targeting T cell co-regulatory proteins (immune checkpoints) such as anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen-4 (CTLA 4 antibody) previously. The patient has not received any other investigational agents and has not had any major surgical procedures or chemotherapy or experimental drug treatment within the designated period before enrollment. The patient has no known significant acute or chronic infections, and no active autoimmune disease. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no known alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has no clinically significant cardiovascular/cerebrovascular disease or inherited bleeding disorder and is not on live vaccines. The patient is eligible for this phase IB/II study of M7824 in combination with gemcitabine in a safety run-in of 6-18 patients, and if safe and tolerated, will proceed to an expansion phase II cohort with a standard Simon Minimax design.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). She has a cutaneous lupus activity and has a CLASI score greater than or equal to 10 at baseline. She has tested positive for one or more RNA autoantibodies. She is currently taking hydroxychloroquine, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone, which have not been able to completely control her symptoms. Her renal function is normal, and she has no active central nervous system (CNS) involvement. She has no history of hepatitis B, C, or HIV infections. She has not received cyclophosphamide, rituximab, or belimumab in the past 3 to 6 months. She is not currently breastfeeding nor pregnant and is willing to comply with the protocol-specified procedures.

26-year-old transgender male who has been living as male for over 2 years and is scheduled for gender-affirmation top surgery. The patient has no significant medical history and is currently taking testosterone therapy. The patient has been experiencing discomfort and pain due to the size of their breasts and is highly motivated to undergo the surgery. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is ASA class I and meets all inclusion criteria. The patient has no history of breast surgeries, breast cancer, chronic pain syndromes, or coagulopathy, and does not have an allergy to local anesthetics. The patient is expected to follow the postoperative pain control regimen, including filling out pain diaries and documenting opioid use.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 6 months ago. She underwent induction chemotherapy followed by an autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT) and achieved a partial response. However, a recent bone marrow biopsy showed relapse of the disease. She is in good general health with no significant comorbidities. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has a suitable sibling donor who is HLA-identical and willing to donate stem cells for an allogeneic transplant. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to comply with the Lenalidomide Pregnancy Prevention Risk Management Plan. Her peripheral neuropathy is grade 1 and well-controlled with medication. She has no history of other neoplasia except for cervical carcinoma in situ treated 5 years ago. She has no known hypersensitivity to bortezomib or other components of the treatment regimen. She is willing to receive thromboprophylaxis during the consolidation phase. Her age is 45 years and her measurable disease status satisfies the inclusion criteria for the phase II trial.

56 year old man with a history of HIV-1 infection for 10 years, currently on HAART (tenofovir, emtricitabine, and darunavir) for the past 2 years. His most recent DEXA scan showed a T-score of -2.5, indicating osteopenia. He has not experienced any virological failure or toxicity with his current HAART regimen, and his plasma HIV-1 RNA has been undetectable for the past 12 months. He has no known resistance mutations to abacavir and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient does not have a history of intolerance or toxicity to abacavir, nor is he positive for HLA B*5701. He does not have any secondary causes of osteoporosis/osteopenia, such as vitamin D deficiency or thyroid disease, and has not received therapy with bisphosphonates in the last 12 months.

The patient is a 34-year-old Caucasian male who has been diagnosed with psoriasis vulgaris for at least six months. The condition involves approximately 15% of total body surface area (BSA) and has been affecting his quality of life. He has tried various topical treatments with little success. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of significant medical conditions. The patient has no history of HIV, Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C, and is not currently experiencing any active bacterial or viral infections. He is not taking any immunosuppressive therapy. He is currently employed and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

The patient is a 30 year old man diagnosed with HIV and currently on antiretroviral treatment. He has been experiencing fatigue, muscle weakness, and occasional headaches. He resides in the city of Pachuca, and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of microencapsulated red pomegranate juice as a supplement to reduce oxidative stress in HIV+ patients. He has not taken any antioxidant supplements and is not currently taking angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors. He is not pregnant and is committed to adhering to at least 95% of the supplementation.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was brought to the hospital due to sudden onset of weakness on the right side of his body. He feels numbness and has difficulty speaking. He has a history of hypertension, but no history of heart disease or stroke. Upon examination, the patient is found to have a moderate to severe stroke with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 12. The patient is eligible for the trial as the onset of the stroke was within 5 hours and 30 minutes before randomization. The patient is able to give informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial. He will receive either Abciximab or a placebo for 12 hours. The patient will be closely monitored for any adverse events and will undergo laboratory tests, vital sign monitoring, and physical examinations throughout the study.

The patient is a 75-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue for several months. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago after smoking for 40 years. She has been diagnosed with severe senile degenerative aortic valve stenosis and has been deemed unsuitable for surgical aortic valve replacement due to the high risk of complications. She has been classified as NYHA Functional Class II. Her echocardiogram revealed a mean aortic valve gradient of 40 mmHg and an aortic valve area of 0.8 cm². Her left ventricular ejection fraction is 45%. She has agreed to participate in the PREVAIL-20J clinical trial and has signed an informed consent.

25 yo F, recently graduated from nursing school and started working at a hospital. Experiences frequent back pain due to the nature of her job, which includes moving and lifting patients, long-time standing and frequent bending. She has not participated in any other pain prevention studies and has not used a lumbar support in the last 6 months. She has not experienced low back pain symptoms within the last year and does not have any chronic pain disorders. She has not had any spinal operations or any chronic cardiac, respiratory, liver, and kidney issues that would affect her participation in the study. She is not pregnant and has no plans to have a baby in the next year. She is interested in participating in the study to prevent future low back pain and improve her overall quality of life.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with unresectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) and is planning to initiate systemic chemotherapy within the next 4 weeks. He has an ECOG performance score of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 3 months as determined by his primary oncologist. He has experienced a 5% weight loss over the past 6 months and is currently at 70 kg. He has been given permission by his primary oncologist to engage in a low to moderate intensity exercise regimen. He speaks English fluently and is able to give written informed consent. He has no history of major surgery in the past 4 weeks and is not experiencing dysphagia that requires enteral or parenteral feeding for nutrition. He is not enrolled in hospice care at the time of consent. He is not currently engaged in an active exercise routine and is not using any nutritional supplements containing EPA/DHA. He has not been taking vitamin D supplementation or St. John's wort that can influence efficacy and safety parameters. He does not have any known hypersensitivity or allergy to any of the study products. His AST/ALT levels are within normal range, and his serum creatinine, absolute neutrophil count, hemoglobin, and platelet count are also within normal range.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic ankle instability for the past 6 months. He reports a history of multiple ankle sprains and feels that his ankle gives out frequently, causing him to lose balance and fall. He has not received any treatment for his ankle instability in the past 3 months. He does not have any other lower limb disease, fractures, or infections. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the near future. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial involving dry needling at the gluteus medius trigger point to alleviate his ankle instability symptoms.

58-year-old female with a history of Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma (NHL) diagnosed two years ago. She has been treated with CHOP chemotherapy and radiation therapy with initial response, but is now experiencing progression of her disease. She reports fatigue, night sweats, and occasional fevers. On examination, she has multiple enlarged lymph nodes in her neck, axilla, and groin. Biopsy of one of the lymph nodes confirms recurrence of DLBCL. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 2 months. Laboratory values are within normal limits except for an elevated LDH of 350 U/L. She has not received any treatment for her NHL in the past 3 weeks and has not undergone any major surgery in the past 3 weeks. She is willing to undergo tumor tissue biopsies as part of this study. She has no history of CNS lymphoma or brain metastases, neuropathy ≥ Grade 2, or history of allogeneic stem cell transplantation. She is not currently taking any drug that is a known clinically relevant inhibitor or inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4. She has not received an investigational drug within 21 days of study entry and is not currently participating in another study.

A 26-year-old female presented with impacted mandibular third molar on the left side. She reported discomfort and pain in the affected area, which led her to seek dental care. Her medical history was unremarkable, and she denied any allergies to medications and local anesthetic agents. She did not have any concurrent treatment with NSAIDs or corticosteroids. Intraoral examination revealed swelling, redness, and tenderness in the lower left third molar region. Panoramic radiograph confirmed the presence of an impacted mandibular third molar with mesioangular impaction. The patient was scheduled for surgical removal of the impacted mandibular third molar. The purpose of the study is to evaluate the efficacy of pre-emptive paracetamol in reducing intraoperative pressure and postoperative pain after surgical removal of impacted mandibular third molar using visual analogue scale. The patient was deemed eligible for the study as she met the inclusion criteria and did not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of chest pain and shortness of breath upon exertion. He has been diagnosed with ischemic heart disease by his cardiologist and has been on medical management for the past year. Despite treatment, he still experiences symptoms and has been referred to the Coronary Artery Surgery Study (CASS) to compare the benefits of coronary artery surgery with medical management. He is eligible for the study as he is under 67 years old and has a confirmed diagnosis of ischemic heart disease. The patient will undergo a thorough evaluation, including physical examination, laboratory tests, catheterization, and angiography to determine if he meets the criteria for specific subsets for randomization to either surgical or medical therapy. The primary endpoints of the study include death and myocardial infarction. The patient will be followed for a 10-year period to evaluate the effectiveness of each treatment option.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been referred for a colonoscopy due to a family history of colon cancer. He has no significant medical history, takes no regular medications, and has no known allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is sexually active with one partner and uses barrier contraception. He is willing and able to follow the study procedures and comply with instructions. He has provided written informed consent and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

The patient is a 70-year-old American woman who has been diagnosed with dementia. She has been experiencing agitated and aggressive behaviors, which have become a significant challenge for her and her family caregiver. She is able to participate in at least 2 activities of daily living, such as bathing and dressing. She lives with her family caregiver who is accessible by telephone and plans to live in the area for at least 6 months. She has been on a stable dose of psychotropic medication for at least 60 days. She speaks English and her family caregiver is also an English speaker. She has not been diagnosed with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder and her dementia is not secondary to probable head trauma. She is not in active treatment for cancer and has not had more than 3 acute medical hospitalizations in the past year.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presented with acute onset of vertigo and vomiting. She described the vertigo as a spinning sensation that started suddenly while she was at work. The symptoms were constant and did not change with head movement. She denied any hearing loss, tinnitus, or focal neurologic symptoms. She was otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She had no history of ear infections or surgery. She did not smoke or use any illicit drugs. On examination, she had a positive head impulse test to the right, along with spontaneous nystagmus to the left. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver was positive for left-sided geotropic horizontal nystagmus. Her hearing was normal by bedside testing. The caloric testing showed a 50% reduction in response on the left side compared to the right. She was diagnosed with vestibular neuronitis and was offered a trial of prednisone treatment. She agreed to participate in the clinical trial and was randomized to the treatment arm. She was started on prednisone 60mg daily for 7 days, followed by a taper over the next 7 days. She was followed up for 12 months with serial evaluations of clinical response, self-perceived handicap, and laboratory parameters.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with stomach cancer. She has a history of smoking, but she quit 5 years ago. She underwent a total gastrectomy to remove the cancerous tissue. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy with 5-FU, but her oncologist has recommended that she switch to capecitabine. She is in good overall health, with no significant medical history other than her cancer diagnosis. She has no history of heart disease, liver disease, or kidney disease. She does not have any allergies to medications. She is post-menopausal and is not currently taking any hormone replacement therapy. She is married and lives with her husband. She has two children who live nearby. She is able to perform activities of daily living independently. She is highly motivated to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 8-month-old infant with sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by auditory brainstem response testing. The infant has tested positive for congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) through urine culture or polymerase chain reaction test. The infant is between 1 and 12 months of age at the time of randomization. The infant does not have any other known causes contributing to SNHL, such as meningitis or ototoxicity. The infant has no evidence of intracranial calcification, hydrocephalus, microcephaly, petechiae, or chorioretinitis. The infant was not born prematurely (less than 32 weeks gestational age) and weighed at least 1800 g at birth. The infant has not been exposed to a language other than English or Spanish, and the parent or guardian is able to speak English or Spanish and complete hearing assessments and communication questionnaires. The infant has not been treated with antiviral medications or immune globulin therapy, and the mother is not HIV positive. The infant is not receiving any other investigational drugs and is not breastfeeding from a mother receiving antiviral or immunosuppressive medication. The infant has no known hypersensitivity reaction to valganciclovir, ganciclovir, or any components of the investigational product formulation. The infant does not have ALT five times baseline U/L, hepatomegaly, or significant gastrointestinal disorders, and does not have ANC less than 500 cells/mm^3, Hemoglobin less than 8 g/dL, or platelets less than 50,000/mm^3, splenomegaly, or significant hematologic disorders. The infant has no creatinine clearance less than 60 mL/min/1.73m^2 or significant renal disorders. The infant is not currently using any prohibited medication specified by the package insert.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female with cerebral palsy who has been diagnosed with cervical dystonia for over a year. She has been taking antispasmodics for the past month, but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She experiences painful spasms in her neck, which cause her head to tilt or turn involuntarily. She has no known allergies to botulinum toxin. She has a full range of motion in her cervical spine. She has not had a fever, infection or cancer, and has not experienced uncontrollable seizures. She does not have generalized neuromuscular junction disease. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant within the next 12 weeks. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She has not recently undergone changes in her medication, such as antispasmodics, benzodiazepine, or anticholinergics. She has not received botulinum toxin injections in the past 6 months or undergone intrathecal baclofen, selective peripheral denervation, or deep brain stimulation. She meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

68F with a medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and stroke presented to the clinic with complaints of memory loss and difficulty with daily activities such as cooking and managing finances. She reports that her symptoms started about 6 months ago and have been gradually worsening. She denies any history of alcohol or substance abuse. Her current medications include lisinopril, metformin, and atorvastatin. She underwent a neurological examination which revealed mild cognitive impairment and a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 20/30. An MRI of the brain showed multiple small vessel ischemic changes consistent with vascular dementia. She has a reliable caregiver who is willing to participate in the study. The patient is able to read simple articles and write simple sentences. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 1 month. She meets the inclusion criteria for mild to moderate vascular dementia with an MMSE score of ≤26 and ≥11, aged ≥55 and ≤80 years old, weighing of ≥45kg and ≤90kg, and adequate vision and hearing ability to complete all study tests. She does not have a history of other dementia types or medical conditions that can lead to cognitive impediment. She is not currently taking cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, nimodipine or herbal medicine with function of improving cognition. She does not have severe cardiovascular disease, severe liver or kidney dysfunction, uncontrolled diabetes, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, multiple neuritis, myasthenia gravis and muscle atrophy, severe indigestion, gastrointestinal obstruction, gastric and duodenal ulcers or other gastrointestinal disorders that can affect drug absorption. She is not allergic to the experimental drug and does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent her from completing the study.

A 52-year old woman was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She is currently undergoing her first line of chemotherapy and is expected to continue treatment for at least 3 months. She complains of difficulty sleeping at night and often wakes up feeling tired and fatigued. She has tried over-the-counter sleep aids but has not found them to be very effective. She also reports feeling anxious and moody since her diagnosis. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and she takes medication to control it. She lives with her husband and two adult children. She works part-time as an accountant. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no known allergies to medications. She is willing to participate in the trial and is able to swallow the study medication. She is not currently taking any benzodiazepines, hypnotics, anticonvulsants, antipsychotics or antidepressants. She has not received any investigational drugs in the past 30 days. She is not currently being treated with warfarin and does not have brain metastases.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing depressive symptoms for the past year. She has never been diagnosed with depression or any other mental health disorder before. She has a history of obesity with a BMI of 36 and has been trying to lose weight by following a low-calorie diet for the past few months. She does not smoke or use recreational drugs but drinks coffee regularly. She has no known allergies or autoimmune disorders. She is not currently taking any prescription medications but has taken over-the-counter painkillers occasionally in the past. She has no history of fainting during blood draws or any other medical procedures. She is interested in participating in the Leucine for Depression Study (L-DEP) and is willing to comply with the study procedures and dosing regimens.

A 54-year-old male with a history of melanoma presented to the oncology clinic with new in-transit metastases (ITMs) on his left thigh and right arm. The patient was initially diagnosed with melanoma 3 years ago and underwent surgical resection of the primary tumor. He also received adjuvant therapy with interferon-alpha for 1 year. The patient had no evidence of disease until now. The patient underwent a biopsy of the ITMs which confirmed melanoma. The treating physician discussed treatment options, including surgery, regional therapy, and systemic therapy, but the patient was interested in participating in a clinical trial. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the trial, including having at least two in-transit lesions at distinct distances from the primary site. The patient provided written informed consent and underwent further evaluation, including metabolic and immune profiling of the ITMs. The patient was found to be treatment-naive and negative for HIV, Hep B, and Hep C. The trial will provide valuable information on the evolution of metabolic and immune dysfunction in in-transit melanoma, which may lead to improved treatment options for patients with this disease.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with multiple and recurrent large tumors. He underwent a complete resection of all Ta/T1 papillary disease two months ago. The pathology report showed high-grade/G3 tumors with no evidence of lymphovascular invasion. CT and MRI scans done four weeks ago showed no evidence of metastasis. The patient is BCG-naive and has not received any prior radiotherapy to the bladder. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. The patient's blood test results show hemoglobin levels at 12.5 g/dL, absolute neutrophil count at 1.5 × 10^9/L, and a platelet count at 100 × 10^9/L. His serum bilirubin levels are within normal limits, and his ALT and AST levels are within 2.5 × ULN. His measured creatinine clearance is 60 mL/min. The patient is covered by national health insurance. He is a candidate for BCG treatment and is willing to participate in the study. Tissue provision from the initial surgery, formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded (FFPE) is mandatory for DNA extraction and next-generation sequencing.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who presents to the clinic with abdominal pain and rectal bleeding. He has a history of smoking, consuming an average of 10 cigarettes per day for the last 20 years. He underwent colonoscopy, which revealed a mass in his colon. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic colorectal cancer. He has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. His performance status is 1, and he is otherwise healthy. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has signed written informed consent to participate in the study. His lab results show neutrophils >1.5 x 109/L, platelets >100 x 109/L, Hgb >9 g/dl, total bilirubin 1.2 x UNL, ASAT (SGOT) and/or ALAT (SGPT) <2.5 x UNL, alkaline phosphatase <2.5 x UNL, creatinine clearance ≥50 mL/min, and INR or aPTT ≤1.5 × ULN. He has not received any previous treatment for metastatic disease, and he meets the criteria for measurable disease according to RECIST1.1.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 38 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has been experiencing regular contractions for the past 6 hours and has been admitted to the hospital for delivery. The pregnancy has been uncomplicated thus far and she has no significant medical history. The fetus is in a vertex presentation and the patient wishes to have an epidural for pain management. Due to the need for internal monitoring, she has been approached to participate in a clinical trial comparing the accuracy and reliability of fetal heart rate and uterine contraction monitoring methods. She has been fully informed about the study and has provided consent to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and has been recommended for stem cell transplantation. He is currently receiving chemotherapy treatment and is expected to be ready for the transplantation procedure in six weeks. The patient has an ECOG status of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work but may experience symptoms of fatigue and reduced endurance during strenuous activity. The patient has no history of serious falls or osteolytic lesions, and is not currently participating in any other nutritional or exercise intervention trials. The patient has no history of acute cardiovascular events, epilepsy, or severe neurological diseases, and does not have any energy active metals in his body. The patient has no history of acute vein thrombosis or rheumatic diseases, and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient has no history of psychiatric disorders that would affect his legal or cognitive capacity.

The patient is a 25 year old African American female who has been experiencing painful and recurring abscesses in the armpit and groin areas for the past year. She has been diagnosed with hidradenitis suppurativa and has been using topical treatments with limited success. She reports that the condition has greatly impacted her quality of life and she is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find a more effective treatment. She has no history of diabetes or other chronic medical conditions and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to give written informed consent.

63-year-old woman diagnosed with small cell lung cancer with brain metastases. She underwent biopsy which confirmed her diagnosis of small cell lung cancer with brain metastases. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Prior to her diagnosis, she was active and independent with no significant medical problems. She underwent a course of systemic chemotherapy and radiotherapy for her primary tumor, which resulted in a good response. However, she continued to have symptoms related to her brain metastases despite the systemic therapy. Her MRI revealed 2 intracranial lesions consistent with brain metastases. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to avoid the side effects of whole-brain radiation therapy. She is able to provide informed consent and complete the quality of life questionnaires.

The patient is a 30-year-old female diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes since the age of 10. Despite multiple insulin injections and strict adherence to a healthy lifestyle, her blood glucose levels remain unstable with frequent episodes of severe hypoglycemia. She has experienced at least one episode of severe hypoglycemia in the past 12 months and has a Clarke score of 5, indicating reduced awareness of hypoglycemia. Her HbA1c is 9.5% and her BMI is 26. She has not had any history of malignancy, active infections, or alcohol/substance abuse. Her serum creatinine levels are normal, with a calculated GFR of 90mL/min. She is willing to use effective contraceptive measures for the duration of the study. She has been followed by a qualified physician for diabetes management for more than 12 months. She is mentally stable and able to comply with the procedures of the study protocol. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the possibility of islet transplantation as a potential cure for her Type 1 diabetes.

The patient is a 56-year-old Japanese female diagnosed with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medication to manage these conditions. She has never experienced a stroke or systemic embolism but has a CHADS2 score of 2, indicating a moderate risk for stroke. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of rivaroxaban for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation. She has no significant mitral stenosis or other contraindications for anticoagulant therapy.

A 65-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU due to acute respiratory failure secondary to pneumonia. He required invasive mechanical ventilation due to hypoxia and respiratory distress. He has a medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is currently receiving antibiotics and vasopressors to maintain hemodynamic stability. He has a BMI of 30 and is sedated to facilitate mechanical ventilation. The patient has no history of lung surgery or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. His coagulation profile is normal. He will be considered eligible for the study after meeting the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a preterm infant with a postmenstrual age of 28 weeks and a gestational age of 26 weeks. The infant is currently receiving nasal CPAP for respiratory support. The medical team has noted at least 4 episodes of desaturation (SpO2 <80%) in the last 8 hours using a standard pulse oximeter. The infant has no congenital cyanotic heart disease and has been receiving full treatment support. The average FiO2 during the last 24 hours was 0.50. There is no evidence of congenital malformations of the lung or diaphragm, nor any clinically clear evidence of seizures. There is no ongoing sepsis and the infant has not required a blood transfusion during the study.

A 56 year old male patient presents to the clinic with a long-standing history of COPD. He has been a smoker for 30 years and has a history of frequent exacerbations of COPD. His post-bronchodilator FEV1 is 40% of predicted normal and the FEV1/FVC ratio is 60%. He has not had an exacerbation in the last 6 weeks and has not used any investigational drugs in the last 4 weeks. He has no known respiratory disorders other than COPD and no history of alcohol, drug or solvent abuse. He is not currently receiving beta-blockers and does not require daily long-term oxygen therapy. The patient consents to participate in this clinical trial to compare the efficacy of SERETIDE 50/500mcg versus tiotropium bromide on exacerbation rates in severe COPD over a two year study interval.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who sustained a lower extremity fracture due to a car accident. The patient is scheduled for operative fixation of the fracture at the University of Iowa. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. The patient does not have any known allergies or adverse reactions to povidone-iodine. The patient is able to provide informed consent for the study. The patient is excluded if they are unable to provide informed consent due to head trauma or dementia.

This is a 59-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of advanced endometrial carcinoma. She underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and lymph node dissection, which confirmed the presence of endometrioid adenocarcinoma with high-grade features. Imaging studies have further revealed the presence of multiple lung nodules and pelvic lymph node enlargement, indicating advanced disease. As a result, she is now considered a candidate for first-line chemotherapy. She has no prior history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy, and her overall health status is good with an ECOG performance status of 1. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, including leukocytes and platelets, and her renal and liver function are preserved. She has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of participating in this clinical trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 65-year-old female was diagnosed with a periampullary carcinoma after presenting with jaundice and abdominal pain. She underwent a CT scan which revealed a mass in the pancreatic head with no evidence of distant metastases. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol use. She has been deemed surgically fit according to ASA criteria. She has been offered pancreatoduodenectomy and has been given the option to participate in a clinical trial comparing the artery-first approach with mesopancreas dissection to the standard approach.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been referred for his first MRI exam due to recent headaches and blurred vision. He is generally healthy and active, but has expressed some anxiety about the upcoming exam. His parents are concerned about the potential need for sedation or anesthesia to complete the exam. The patient has no history of epilepsy or mental illness, and does not have any language barriers. He is covered by his parent's social security scheme and they have been fully informed about the study and have provided informed consent. The patient is open to participating in the study and using virtual reality as a tool to help reduce his anxiety and improve the quality of the exam.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who works as a carpenter. He has been experiencing pain in his right elbow for the past 6 months, which has been affecting his ability to perform his job. He has tenderness on the lateral epicondyle of his elbow, and he experiences pain when he extends his elbow or flexes his wrist. He has not had any elbow surgery or corticosteroid injections in the affected elbow. He does not have a history of fibromyalgia, and he has not been diagnosed with multilevel nerve compression. He is not pregnant and has not used systemic steroid medication within the last 6 months. He has not had any allergic reactions to the study medication.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who was diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma that has not responded to chemotherapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is expected to have a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. She has measureable disease as defined by RECIST 1.1 criteria. Her blood coagulation parameters meet the eligibility requirements, and she has adequate venous peripheral access for apheresis. She has not participated in any other trial that included investigational study drugs within the past 28 days. She has not received any anticancer medication in the 2 weeks prior to receiving her first dose of study treatment and is not receiving any other concurrent chemotherapy or immunotherapy. She does not have active invasive cancer other than pancreatic adenocarcinoma, nor does she have known HIV, HCV, or HBV. She does not have active autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppressive therapy within the past 4 weeks, nor does she have ongoing or active infection. She does not have a clinically significant pericardial effusion or CHF, and she is not on active anti-coagulation therapy. She is willing to use approved contraceptive methods during the study and for 3 months following the last dose of the study cell infusion. She understands and has signed the study-specific informed consent.

The patient is a 72-year-old female from Peterborough, England who has recently suffered a displaced intracapsular fracture after a fall. She is experiencing pain, swelling, and difficulty moving her hip joint. She has a history of osteoporosis and has been receiving treatment for this condition for the past 10 years. She is also taking medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. She is otherwise healthy and independent in her daily activities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the best treatment option for her hip fracture. She understands that she may be randomly assigned to receive either a cemented hemiarthroplasty or an uncemented Furlong hemiarthroplasty with hydroxyapatite coating. She is willing to attend follow-up appointments and complete any necessary questionnaires or tests as part of the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer. He has undergone multiple lines of chemotherapy and has failed to respond to standard therapy. He has a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (EGOG) Performance Scale. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and he has no other medical conditions. He has no prior malignancies. He has at least one measurable metastatic lesion according to Response Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST). He has not received chemotherapy, radiotherapy or biological therapy within 4 weeks prior to study Day 1. He has no known central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or expecting to conceive or father children during the study. He is not HIV-positive or has active Hepatitis B or C infection. He is not using growth hormone or growth hormone inhibitors. He requires no treatment with immunosuppressive agents other than prescribed corticosteroids at stable doses for at least two weeks prior to the first dose of study drug. He is not using medication(s) that strongly or moderately induce or inhibit cytochrome P450. He is not currently enrolled in a study with an investigational compound or device. He agrees to provide archival tumor tissue sample or undergo biopsy for analysis of gene expression levels.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who suffered a left-hemisphere stroke 3 months ago. She is a native speaker of German and right-handed. She has been experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has also been experiencing difficulty communicating and understanding spoken language, as confirmed by the Aachen Aphasia Test. She has less than the maximum score of 10 error points on the first part of the Token Test, indicating a basic comprehension of spoken instructions. She is in the late subacute or consolidation phase of stroke recovery and is within the 1-12 month post-stroke period where the risk of post-stroke depression is particularly high. She has no pre-morbid history of depression or other psychopathological or neurological conditions. She has not had any changes in antidepressant medication within six weeks prior to study enrollment.
