She has normal vision and is able to engage in intensive communicative-pragmatic social interaction during therapy or testing. She is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 68-year-old retired teacher is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a herpes zoster vaccine. She lives alone and is in good health. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has never had shingles before but is concerned about the risk of developing it as she ages. She received the Zostavax vaccine more than 5 years ago. She is interested in participating in the study to help researchers evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the new vaccine. She is able and willing to comply with the requirements of the study and provides written informed consent. She has not received any other vaccines or investigational products in the 30 days prior to the study and is not taking any medications that would interfere with the study. She reports feeling well with no fever or acute illnesses at the time of enrollment. She has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products in the past 3 months and has no significant underlying illness that would prevent her from completing the study. She is willing to receive intramuscular injections as required by the study.

A 52-year-old Hispanic man presented with fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and dark urine. He reported a history of injection drug use in his past, but has been abstinent for the past 5 years. He was found to have chronic hepatitis C infection during routine blood testing. His genotype was identified as 1a. He has not received any treatment for hepatitis C before. His medical history was significant for high blood pressure and he is currently taking Lisinopril. He denied any other significant medical problems, recent surgeries, or hospitalizations. He also denied any allergies. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His vital signs were stable in the primary evaluation. Physical exam revealed mild abdominal tenderness without hepatosplenomegaly or ascites. His laboratory tests showed a hemoglobin of 13.8 g/dL, WBC count of 5,000/mm3, platelets of 120,000/mm3, and normal kidney function. His HCV RNA viral load was 2,000,000 IU/mL. His serum 25(OH)D level was 22ng/mL. He had no significant cardiac or pulmonary history. He agreed to genetic testing.

This is a 32 year old female who has a history of endometriosis and has undergone radical endometriosis surgery. She has been experiencing severe pelvic pain that has been interfering with her daily life and despite the use of hormonal treatments and pain medications, her symptoms have not improved. She has no other obvious pathology than endometriosis that has been histologically confirmed at previous surgery. Pelvic imaging, including transvaginal ultrasound examination and pelvic MRI, has been performed to confirm that there is no recurrent or residual endometriosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical study to evaluate if sacral neuromodulation could alleviate her pelvic pain symptoms and related dysfunctional symptoms and improve her health-related quality of life. She understands that a test pulse generator will be placed uni- or bilaterally under local or general anesthesia and used during a 2-3-week test period. If marked improvement of symptoms is detected, the patient will receive a permanent pulse generator. Women not responding to sacral neuromodulation will not receive a permanent generator but will continue in the 3 year follow-up and serve as the control group if applicable. She understands that she will be excluded from the study if she has present or future desire to become pregnant. The patient is willing to sign informed consent and participate in the study.

This is a 35 year old male with a history of major depressive disorder who has been experiencing symptoms of low mood, lack of energy, and difficulty sleeping despite being on an adequate trial of an antidepressant medication. The patient has no history of psychotic features or substance abuse in the past three months. The patient's depression has not responded to the current medication and the treating physician has recommended risperidone augmentation therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of this treatment option. The patient has no history of bipolar I or bipolar II disorder and is willing to continue on the same dose of the antidepressant medication during the trial.

A 35-year-old woman was involved in a car accident two days ago and has been experiencing severe neck pain since then. She rates her pain as 8 out of 10 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). She has no history of neck pain or injury before the accident. She was initially treated at the emergency department and received pain medication and muscle relaxants. However, her pain persists and she has difficulty moving her neck. She is now admitted to the hospital for further treatment. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or ongoing chronic conditions. She has no allergies to any medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, as her NRS score is ≥ 5, and she requires hospitalization due to acute neck pain caused by the traffic accident. She does not have any of the exclusion criteria listed for the trial.

The patient is a 10-month-old infant who was diagnosed with primary immunodeficiency with recurrent respiratory tract infections since birth. The infant has been receiving subcutaneous IgG (SCIG) therapy for the past 3 months. The treating physician has been monitoring the infant's response to the treatment and is interested in participating in a retrospective chart review study on the use of SCIG in infants less than two years old. The parent has provided consent for the review of the infant's medical records. There are no protein losing conditions or concomitant treatments with plasma or blood products. The infant has been tolerating the SCIG therapy well, with no reported adverse effects.

Patient A is a 10-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic suppurative lung disease (CSLD) six months ago. He has had a persistent cough and difficulty breathing during physical activities. He has been receiving regular care at the pediatric respiratory clinic of UMMC. He has not been on any antibiotics for the past month. His medical history includes recurrent respiratory tract infections and seasonal allergies. He does not have any other chronic conditions or allergies. His current medications include an inhaler for asthma and antihistamines for allergies. His vital signs are within normal limits. He has no history of hospitalization or use of home ventilation. His lung function test shows a mild obstruction, with a pre-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of 75%. He has not undergone any hypertonic saline challenge test before. He and his parents have agreed to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of nebulized 5% hypertonic saline on cough severity and quality of life in children with non-CF CSLD.

A 45-year-old man with a history of hepatitis C and alcohol abuse underwent a liver transplant due to decompensated cirrhosis. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type II, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no known allergies. He is currently on the transplant waiting list and has been informed that he may receive a liver within the next few weeks. He is aware of the risks of the procedure and has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He is currently stable and has no signs of encephalopathy (West Haven criteria I or II). He has not required mechanical ventilation prior to the surgery, and his liver function tests are within the normal range. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

A 56-year-old male smoker presented to the clinic with a persistent cough and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with stage IV nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and has not received any prior systemic treatment for his advanced disease. He has no history of EGFR or ALK-directed therapy. He has one measurable lesion according to RECIST1.1. He has a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Score. His laboratory values are as follows: serum albumin is 3.5g/dL, absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 2.0×10^9/L, while blood cell count (WBC) is 4.5×10^9/L, platelet count (PLT) is 200×10^9/L, and hemoglobin (HGB) is 100 g/L (without blood transfusion within 4 weeks prior to enrollment). His creatinine clearance (CrCl) is 75 mL/min. His alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) are within the normal range. His serum total bilirubin is 0.9xULN. He has not received any live-virus vaccination within 30 days prior to the first dose of trial treatment. He has no known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.

56 year old male who experienced a fall and sustained a right hip fracture. The patient is currently admitted to the hospital and is scheduled for surgery tomorrow. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. The patient is able to communicate in English and has a smartphone. He has not previously used the Patient Gateway app. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve his clinic follow-up and to make it easier to complete surveys after his orthopedic trauma.

A 68-year-old man diagnosed with chronic heart failure is currently being treated with candesartan cilexetil for the past 8 months. He was previously admitted to the hospital for shortness of breath and swelling in his legs. He was diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and prescribed candesartan cilexetil. Since then, he has been compliant with his medication and has been feeling better. He reports a decrease in shortness of breath, less fatigue, and less swelling in his legs. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a retired office worker and lives with his wife. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is able to perform activities of daily living with minimal assistance. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to further improve his heart failure symptoms and contribute to medical research.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with neuroendocrine tumor (NET) and is a potential candidate for I-131 MIBG therapy. He is scheduled to undergo a whole body I-123 MIBG scintigraphy as part of standard care. He has no significant cardiac disease and his echocardiogram shows normal limits with absence of valvular disease and normal LVEF. His serum BNP is within normal limits. He is not taking any medications known to interfere with MIBG uptake, and has no history of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, neurological diseases, or other diseases known to affect the sympathetic nervous system. He is not currently pregnant or nursing, and is using effective birth control methods. He has provided written informed consent in accordance to local guidelines.

A 21 year old male college athlete, who is currently playing for the University of Wyoming Division 1 football team, is interested in participating in a clinical trial for concussion. He has completed the required baseline testing including SWAY balance, King-Devick, and C3-Logix. He has not been previously diagnosed with a concussion within the last 2 weeks. The athlete is willing and able to participate in all study evaluations and allow access to medical testing and records. He has signed the informed consent form and is excited to contribute to this important research.

The patient is a 38-year-old Caucasian woman who has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years without success. She and her partner have been diagnosed with unexplained infertility. The patient has regular menstrual cycles and her BMI falls within the normal range (23). She has not used any fertility drugs in the past 2 months and her thyroid, liver, and kidney function are all normal. The patient has not undergone any previous ovarian surgery and does not have a history of severe endometriosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the efficacy of pre-IVF treatment with transdermal testosterone to enhance ovarian response in poor responders.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who presented with shortness of breath, chest pain and coughing up blood for the past 2 weeks. He has a history of smoking and asbestos exposure. A chest X-ray showed a pleural effusion, and a subsequent CT scan revealed pleural thickening and nodularity. The patient underwent thoracentesis, and the fluid cytology showed atypical cells. A diagnosis of pleural mesothelioma was suspected, and the patient was referred for further evaluation. The patient underwent a CT-guided Abrams needle pleural biopsy, which was inconclusive. A US-assisted pleural biopsy using a cutting needle was then performed, but the results were also inconclusive. Finally, the patient underwent medical thoracoscopy, which confirmed the diagnosis of pleural mesothelioma. The patient is now undergoing treatment for the disease.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman experiencing chronic abdominal pain for the past 6 months. The pain is located in the lower abdomen and is described as a dull ache with occasional sharp, stabbing sensations. The patient has been diagnosed with chronic pelvic pain and has been taking pain medications for the last month with little relief. The pain affects her daily activities and has led to missed work days. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of transcranial Pulsed Current Stimulation and transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on chronic visceral pain. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study, is not currently pregnant, and does not have any contraindications to tPCS or tDCS.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a BMI of 42. She has struggled with obesity for several years and has decided to undergo bariatric surgery. She has chosen to undergo a sleeve gastrectomy at The Methodist Hospital. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications that interfere with vitamin D metabolism. Her physical exam is unremarkable except for her BMI. She is otherwise healthy and motivated to improve her health. Her lab results show that she has a serum 25(OH)D level of 23 ng/mL, which is classified as vitamin D insufficiency. She has no history of hypercalcemia or renal insufficiency. She will be enrolled in the study and receive daily supplementation of 2,000 IU of vitamin D3 and 1500 mg of calcium. She will be instructed to keep a record of her supplement intake and will have her blood drawn at baseline, 4 weeks, and 12 weeks post-surgery to assess changes in her serum 25(OH)D levels, parathyroid hormone, calcium, and phosphorus. She will also be asked to keep a food diary to estimate her dietary intake of vitamin D and calcium. Her participation in the study will help determine the efficacy of vitamin D supplementation in bariatric surgery patients and may improve the long-term outcomes of bariatric surgery.

52-year-old female with a history of hypertension and diabetes presents with symptoms consistent with COVID-19, including cough, fever, and shortness of breath. She tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 antigen on a diagnostic assay five days ago. She has not been hospitalized and is not currently on supplemental oxygen. Due to her age and underlying medical conditions, she is at high risk for disease progression. She has not participated in any clinical studies involving investigational interventions in the past 30 days and has not received any SARS-CoV-2 vaccine, monoclonal antibody, or plasma from a recovered COVID-19 patient prior to participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent rocking dizziness triggered by passive motion for the past 2 years. She has no history of peripheral vestibular disorder, and has been evaluated by a neurologist and an ear, nose and throat specialist. She is currently not taking any medications. Her past medical history includes migraines, but they have been well-controlled with medication. She is able to interact with the informed consent process and is willing to participate in the study. She has no implanted metal in her body and does not have a personal history of seizures or epilepsy. She is not pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant during study enrollment.

A 42-year-old man who works in a construction company has been experiencing low back pain for the past three months. The pain is not associated with any radiation or referred pain. He has no history of systemic disease, cancer, or spinal fracture. He is able to fill out the questionnaires and scales related to the study. He does not have any rheumatologic inflammatory disease, fibromyalgia or other conditions that would require referral for surgery. He is currently taking over-the-counter pain medication for his low back pain. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about managing his low back pain.

55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with an ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). He underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a stent placement. He is scheduled to undergo a vascular closure device (VCD) placement to minimize the risk of bleeding and hematoma formation at the access site. He has no known allergies to any of the components in the closure material and has not had a puncture on the same site within the last 30 days. He is able to provide valid informed signed consent for the randomized comparison of the ExoSeal® and Angio-Seal VCDs in the CLOSE-UP II trial.

Pt is a 78-year-old F who fell at home and sustained a hip fracture. She presents to the emergency department with complaints of severe pain in her hip and is unable to bear weight on that leg. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. Imaging shows a displaced intracapsular fracture of the left femoral neck. The patient is admitted to the hospital and scheduled for surgery. The patient is able to provide informed consent and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. There is no evidence of periprosthetic fracture or pathological fracture.

46 year old male with a history of glaucoma, presenting with complaints of decreased visual acuity and peripheral vision loss in both eyes. Patient's ophthalmologist has noted thinning of the RNFL and ganglion cell layer thickness during routine eye exams. Past Medical History: - Glaucoma, diagnosed 5 years ago, currently managed with prescription eyedrops - Hypertension, well controlled on lisinopril - Hyperlipidemia, managed with statin therapy - No history of retinal disease or ocular surgery. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of RT-View, a spectral domain technology diagnostic tool, in predicting glaucoma.

A 57-year-old female diagnosed with endometrial carcinoma that has spread to other parts of the body, including the lungs and liver. The patient underwent a prior systemic, platinum-based chemotherapy regimen for EC, but experienced radiographic evidence of disease progression. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has a measurable target lesion according to Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, and agrees to use a highly effective method of contraception during the treatment period and for at least 120 days after the last dose of study treatment if assigned to receive pembrolizumab and lenvatinib. The patient has recovered adequately from any toxicity and/or complications from major surgery prior to starting therapy. The patient has a historical or fresh tumor biopsy specimen for determination of mismatch repair (MMR) status. The patient has no history of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy (in dosing exceeding 10 mg daily of prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to study start. The patient has no active autoimmune disease (with the exception of psoriasis) that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years. The patient has not received prior treatment with any treatment targeting VEGF-directed angiogenesis, any anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent. The patient has not received prior treatment with an agent directed to a stimulatory or co-inhibitory T-cell receptor other than an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent, and who has discontinued from that treatment due to a Grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse event. The patient has not received prior radiation therapy within 21 days of study start with the exception of palliative radiotherapy to bone lesions.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with severe abdominal pain that began abruptly and radiated to his back. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and smoking. He reports that he had a similar episode of abdominal pain 2 years ago but did not seek medical attention. His physical exam revealed tenderness in the upper abdomen and elevated levels of amylase and lipase. He was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis and is being considered for inclusion in a clinical trial that aims to determine whether genetic polymorphisms and immune response can predict severity and outcome in patients with acute pancreatitis. Patient A is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

A 42-year-old man was recently diagnosed with mild to moderate essential hypertension during a routine health checkup. His diastolic blood pressure readings were consistently between 90-109 mmHg. He has no history of secondary hypertension and is otherwise healthy. He does not have any gastrointestinal, hematological, or hepatic diseases. He is not taking any medication for hypertension currently. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. He is not a heavy drinker or smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the last 12 weeks.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman living in the Corte de Pedra, Bahia, Brazil, presenting with a single skin lesion on her left arm that has been present for the past two months. The lesion has a diameter of approximately 2 cm and is ulcerated with raised borders. The patient reports no pain or itching but is concerned about the appearance of the lesion. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Physical examination revealed no other abnormalities, and laboratory results showed normal aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, serum creatinine, and blood urea nitrogen levels. The patient tested positive for Leishmania braziliensis by PCR. She is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the clinical trial assessing the efficacy and safety of Transition-state Analog Inhibitor of Human Purine Nucleoside Phosphorylase for topical use associated with standard antimonial for the treatment of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of stage IV breast cancer diagnosed 1 year ago. She has multiple sites of new osseous disease that are clinically obvious metastatic disease. She has received at least one prior hormonal therapy for metastatic disease. The patient has no symptomatic brain or CNS metastases but has previously treated brain or CNS metastasis with radiotherapy completed at least 8 weeks before study entry. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 1, and her MUC-1 antigen level is greater than 2 times the upper limit of normal and has increased by 1.5 times since her last measurement. She has no known sensitivity to fluorouracil and no dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency. She has no other malignancy within the past 5 years except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. She has had no prior oral cyclophosphamide or capecitabine for metastatic disease. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception if she is fertile.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He is physically active, but he recently experienced acute musculoskeletal pain in his lower back after lifting a heavy load. He has no history of allergies or systemic disorders. He stopped taking any anti-inflammatory or analgesic medication two days ago in order to participate in the study. He is generally in good health but reports occasional mild pain in his lower back due to his job. He is married and has two children. He understands the instructions and agrees to comply with the protocol. He is willing to avoid sun exposure and not introduce any new personal care products during the study. He is able to read and provide written informed consent.

50 yo F with a history of hypertension and diabetes was admitted to the hospital with sudden onset left-sided weakness and slurred speech. Emergency CT scan showed a large clot in the middle cerebral artery, and she was treated with intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. Follow-up CT scan at 24-36 hours showed evidence of hemorrhagic infarction. She is now being considered for enrollment in the HITs study, which will explore the efficacy and safety of early antiplatelet therapy after hemorrhagic infarction in acute ischemic stroke treated with intravenous thrombolysis. The patient, along with her family, has provided informed consent to participate in the study. Her current medications include lisinopril and metformin. She has no known allergies to medications.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma. He has never received any treatment for cancer before. He has experienced symptoms such as difficulty swallowing, hoarseness, and a persistent sore throat. Imaging studies revealed a large tumor in the nasopharynx with involvement of nearby lymph nodes. The patient has no significant past medical history except for hypertension and has never received radiation therapy to the head and neck area. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his consent to receive a weekly dose of nimotuzumab in addition to concurrent radiation therapy. He is currently in good overall health and is expected to live longer than 6 months.

52-year-old Caucasian male with a history of primary essential hypertension for the past 5 years, currently under medication with amlodipine 10mg/day and losartan 100mg/day. Despite the treatment, he has been experiencing uncontrolled hypertension with an average clinic sitting DBP of 100 mmHg and SBP of 160 mmHg over the last month. He has no history of coronary artery disease, stroke, or diabetes. He is a non-smoker, occasional alcohol drinker, and has a BMI of 30. He reports no symptoms of orthostatic hypotension or fluid depletion. He is compliant with his medication and follows a low-sodium diet. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 32-year-old male military service member who was deployed to a combat zone has been experiencing sleep disturbances for the past 3 months. He reports difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, and waking up feeling refreshed. He has also been experiencing nightmares related to his deployment. He reports feeling fatigued during the day and having difficulty concentrating. He is currently not taking any medication for his sleep disturbances. He has not received acupuncture or psychotherapy in the past month. He is willing to participate in a group psychotherapy and individual interview via telephone. He has no history of substance use disorder, surgery, or other medical conditions that could impact sleep. He is not pregnant. He is willing to abstain from sedative-hypnotics and sleep aids throughout the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 5 years. She is currently on regular prescribed controller therapy but has experienced poor control of her asthma symptoms. She reports using her rescue inhaler more than 2 times per week for the past month and has had nocturnal asthma awakening at least once a week. She has had one emergency department visit in the past 6 months due to asthma exacerbation. Her BMI is 32 kg/m2 and she has struggled with weight loss in the past. She has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or liver cirrhosis. She reports no history of major psychiatric disorders or illicit drug use in the past 12 months. She is a non-smoker and has never had bariatric surgery. She is currently not taking roflumilast or theophylline. She is willing to practice an adequate birth control method for the duration of the study. She resides within the area of one of the seven centers of the American Lung Association- Airways Clinical Research Centers (ALA-ACRC).

This is a 65 year old male with a history of peripheral neuropathy, hypertension and osteoarthritis, who presents with complaints of unsteadiness when standing up. He reports having difficulties maintaining his balance and describes a feeling of trembling in his legs. He also reports occasional falls, but denies any other neurological symptoms such as weakness or sensory loss. He has been referred for an electroneuromyogram (ENMG) to assess his peripheral neuropathy. He is able to stand for the duration of the test and has expressed his willingness to participate in a research study. During the study, the presence of orthostatic tremor will be investigated systematically using surface EMG (polygraphy). The aim of the study is to estimate the prevalence of OT in patients with peripheral neuropathy and unsteadiness, and to determine the demographic, clinical, and electrophysiological characteristics of patients with OT.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from the US who has been diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer with liver metastasis. He has a history of chronic hepatitis C and mild liver dysfunction with no signs of decompensation. He has completed one cycle of first-line systemic therapy, and his disease has progressed. His ECOG performance status is 1. His laboratory study is remarkable for AST: 50 U/L, ALT: 70 U/L, Total bilirubin: 1.2 mg/dL, Albumin: 3.5 g/dL, INR: 1.0. He is not on any medication that may affect the metabolism of crizotinib.

A 52-year-old male patient diagnosed with CD19+ follicular lymphoma is seeking treatment options for his chemotherapy-resistant condition. He has received 2 cycles of combined chemotherapy but has not achieved a complete response. He has a performance status score of 1 and is expected to live longer than 12 weeks. His creatinine level is within normal range and his liver function tests are within 3 folds of normal range. He has reliable contraception and is willing to sign an informed consent form. He has no central nervous system invasion or other concurrent uncontrolled malignancies but has a medical history of smoking and hypertension. He is eligible for the clinical trial and wants to participate.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with inflammatory osteoarthritis. She has been experiencing joint pain, stiffness, and swelling for the past 5 years, which has significantly affected her daily activities. Despite taking pain relief medications, her symptoms have not been fully relieved. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatments for her condition. She has no major medical conditions and has never had a heart attack or stroke. She is not pregnant and has no history of cancer or gastrointestinal ulcers. She has been on a stable dose of pain medication for the past 6 months and is willing to maintain this pattern during the study. She is willing to consume juice or placebo drink for 21 consecutive days and to participate in screening measures, including a blood draw, before and after the intervention period. She has not used any nonpharmacologic pain therapies including acupuncture, ultrasound, or transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation within the past 30 days.

The patient is a 55 year old Japanese woman who has been postmenopausal for 2 years. She has noticed a gradual decline in her height over the past year and has developed mild back pain. She reports no history of fractures. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, but she is otherwise healthy. A bone density scan confirms the diagnosis of osteoporosis with a T-score of -2.5 in the lumbar spine. She has not been taking any medication for osteoporosis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the optimal dose of lasofoxifene for postmenopausal Asian women with osteoporosis.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is a descriptive drug utilization study aimed at collecting data from existing databases on the characteristics and patterns of use of new users of aclidinium bromide and other medications for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in Europe. Therefore, no patient enrollment is required.

The patient is a 60 year old man who was recently diagnosed with de novo coronary artery disease. He has one lesion with a diameter between 2.5 and 3.5 mm and a length of up to 33 mm that requires treatment. He experienced chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion for the past month. His medical history includes hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type II diabetes, all of which are well controlled with medication. He has not had a myocardial infarction within the last 72 hours and does not have a restenotic lesion. He has been referred to the study to evaluate the efficacy of sirolimus-eluting stent implantation and will be followed up at 30 days, 3 months, 6 months and 12 months. At 3 months, he will undergo angiographic and OCT evaluation to assess the effectiveness of the treatment. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia who has had a Foley catheter in place for over 30 days due to urinary obstruction. His medical history is significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and a previous myocardial infarction. He has no active urinary tract infections and is currently being treated with antibiotics for a mild skin infection. The patient has the ability to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his catheter care.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage III squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He underwent a complete tumor resection and postoperative radiotherapy. He has been disease-free for the past four months. His performance status is ECOG 1, and he has no other medical conditions. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse but has quit both since his diagnosis. He is not currently taking any medications or vitamin supplements containing vitamin A. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study period.

A 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a benign thyroid disease has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and anxiety. She has been considering thyroidectomy as a treatment option and is interested in participating in this study to gain a better understanding of the potential impact on her Quality of Life. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She has no history of neck surgery or irradiation and is able to read and write in Greek. She does not have any other significant medical history and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials.

This is a 62 year-old male with a history of non-small cell lung cancer that has progressed despite previous treatment with an anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy. The patient has been diagnosed with Stage IV squamous or non-squamous NSCLC and has progressed on treatment with an anti-PD-(L)1 monoclonal antibody (mAb) administered either as monotherapy, or in combination with other checkpoint inhibitors or other therapies. The patient is not eligible for an approved targeted therapy and is able to provide archival tumor tissue sample collected either within 5 years or within the interval from completion of last treatment but before entering the screening period or newly obtained core or excisional biopsy of a tumor lesion not previously irradiated obtained within 90 days of treatment initiation. The patient has completed all screening procedures within the 35-day screening window and has adequate organ function within 10 days of initiation of study treatment. The patient is willing to use contraception if male, or not pregnant or breastfeeding if female. The patient has not received prior radiation therapy to the lung that is >30 Gray (Gy) within 6 months of the first dose of study treatment and has not received a live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose of study treatment. The patient has not had a severe hypersensitivity reaction to treatment with monoclonal antibodies (including pembrolizumab) and/or any of their excipients, and has not had an allogenic tissue/solid organ transplant.

A 45-year-old male presented with a 6-month history of enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, axilla, and groin. He also reported fatigue and night sweats. A biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma expressing CD20 antigen. He received initial treatment with chemotherapy, which resulted in a complete remission. After six months, he was eligible for this clinical trial and signed an informed consent form. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his expected survival is greater than or equal to 3 months. He has not received rituximab or other anti-CD20(+) monoclonal antibody treatment within 1 year before enrollment. He also meets the requirements for hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. He has no other malignancies, active opportunistic infections, or serious nonmalignant diseases. He is not seropositive for HCV antibody, HIV antibody, or hepatitis B virus surface antigen (HBsAg). He has not received live vaccine within 4 weeks prior to study entry. He has never had a history of allergic reaction or protein product allergy including murine proteins. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to accept birth control methods. He is considered suitable by the principal investigator for the study.

The patient is a 25 year old female who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for 7 years. She has moderate to severe nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy in both eyes but has not undergone panretinal photocoagulation. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She is a non-smoker with a body mass index of 25. She has no history of organ transplant, malignancy, or heart disease. She is willing to comply with the intensive medical management of diabetes and immunosuppression protocols. She has no other ocular conditions that might affect the progression of diabetic retinopathy or macular edema. She is interested in participating in the study to compare the effectiveness of islet cell transplantation with medical therapy for the treatment of diabetic eye disease.

A 45-year-old female presents to the oncology clinic with a diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer. She was initially diagnosed with breast cancer 2 years ago and underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, the cancer has spread to other parts of her body, and she has been experiencing worsening symptoms, including fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss. She has been treated with several standard anti-tumor therapies, including PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, but has failed to respond to them. Her ECOG Performance Status is 1, and her life expectancy is estimated to be at least 12 weeks. Laboratory results show that her absolute neutrophil count, platelets, hemoglobin, albumin levels, total bilirubin levels, ALT and AST levels, serum creatinine, and creatinine clearance are within normal limits. She is willing to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures and agrees to use a highly effective method of birth control/contraception. She provides signed informed consent and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study. She does not have a history of hypersensitivity to any components of the SHR-1316 product, autoimmune disease, active CNS metastases, clinically significant cardiovascular condition, or active infection. She has not received any investigational or concurrent cancer therapy within the last 4 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer. She is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old HIV-positive male who has been receiving care at the University of Alabama at Birmingham clinic for the past year. He reports smoking at least 10 cigarettes per day for the past 5 years and is interested in quitting smoking. He has previously attempted to quit smoking but was unsuccessful. The patient is currently taking antiretroviral therapy for his HIV and reports good adherence. He has no significant medical history other than his HIV diagnosis. The patient is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. He has no current suicidal or manic symptoms and is stable enough to participate in the study.

50-year-old female with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and central obesity presents for evaluation of metabolic syndrome. She reports occasional headaches but is otherwise asymptomatic. Blood pressure at the time of visit is 140/90 mmHg, and waist circumference is 95 cm. Fasting glucose is 105 mg/dL, triglycerides are 165 mg/dL, and HDL cholesterol is 38 mg/dL. She is not currently taking any medications for her conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her metabolic health and has no known allergies to plant sterols. She does not smoke, exercise vigorously, or consume more than 2 alcoholic drinks per day. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning pregnancy in the next 6 months.

A 49-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents to the emergency department with fever, chills, and shortness of breath. He reports feeling unwell for a few days and has a cough producing yellow sputum. On examination, he is found to have crackles in his lungs and is diagnosed with severe sepsis. He is started on IV antibiotics and fluid resuscitation. The patient's creatinine level is elevated, and he has a history of chronic kidney disease. The treating physician is considering using HES 130/0.4 as a colloid to stabilize the patient's circulation, but is concerned about its potential effects on the kidneys. The physician discusses the Scandinavian Starch for Severe Sepsis/Septic Shock Trial with the patient and obtains informed consent to enroll him in the study.

A 62-year-old male patient came to the clinic with complaints of urinary frequency, urgency and difficulty in urination. He had no significant medical history and was not on any medication. The physical examination was unremarkable except for an enlarged prostate gland on digital rectal examination. His PSA level was elevated (10 ng/mL) and biopsy of the prostate confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the prostate. Further imaging studies did not reveal any evidence of metastatic disease. The patient has been referred to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the incidence of nodal metastases among newly diagnosed patients of prostate cancer using Choline-PET. The patient has provided informed consent and is eligible for the trial as he is presumed to be non-N1 and non-M1.

Patient A is a 16-year-old male who presents to a primary care clinic for a routine physical exam. He reports feeling generally healthy and denies any current health concerns. However, during the screening process, he admits to having engaged in physical aggression towards a friend in the past year, specifically pushing and hitting. He reports that the incident was a one-time occurrence and that he and his friend have since reconciled. He denies any history of violence towards strangers, acquaintances, or dating partners. He speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent/assent. He is interested in learning more about the SafERteens study and is willing to participate in the pilot study.

A 68-year-old Egyptian man was referred to the study center by his neurologist, who diagnosed him with Parkinson's disease based on the United Kingdom Brain Bank criteria. The patient reported a gradual onset of resting tremor in his left hand that progressed to involve his left leg within a year. He also complained of slowness of movements, stiffness, and difficulty in initiating movements. He had no history of stroke or exposure to dopaminergic neurotoxins. His medical history was significant for hypertension that was well controlled with medication. He reported occasional constipation and loss of sense of smell. He was currently taking levodopa-carbidopa combination therapy that provided partial improvement of his symptoms. He was interested in participating in the study to contribute to the understanding of Parkinson's disease among the Egyptian population and to potentially benefit from the study findings.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has scheduled to undergo a total knee replacement surgery due to osteoarthritis. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of cognitive dysfunction or psychiatric illness. He is active and exercises regularly. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially. He is interested in participating in the study to help improve pain management for future patients undergoing similar surgeries.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with schizophrenia at the age of 23 after experiencing auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions. She has been on antipsychotic medication for the past 9 years and has had multiple hospitalizations due to exacerbations of her symptoms. Despite her diagnosis, she is able to live independently and manages to maintain employment as a data entry clerk. She reports occasional tremors in her hands, but no other motor difficulties. She does not have any history of drug use or motor disabilities. The patient has completed high school education and has no further formal education. She reports difficulty in her social relationships due to her symptoms but is motivated to improve her functionality and quality of life. She is interested in participating in this study to contribute to the understanding of the relationship between motor neurological soft signs and schizophrenia, and to potentially improve clinical and rehabilitative practices for individuals with the condition.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it is focused on collecting data from graduates of master's nursing programs in Taiwan. Instead, the study aims to understand the models of master education in nursing in Taiwan, explore the clinical competencies, and career development of the graduates. The inclusion criteria for the study are graduates who have completed a master's nursing program in Taiwan in recent three years and are willing to participate by filling out a questionnaire in Chinese. The exclusion criteria include individuals who cannot read or write Chinese or are unable to fill out the questionnaire by themselves.

The patient is a 34-year-old Caucasian man who was recently diagnosed with bipolar disorder. He has a history of experiencing manic episodes, followed by periods of depression. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to his symptoms. He is currently on a combination of mood stabilizers and antipsychotic medication, but he still experiences some mood swings and struggles with maintaining stable moods. He is willing to participate in a long-term follow-up study to help understand the effectiveness of different treatment strategies for bipolar disorder. He lives in the defined mixed urban and more rural area where the study is taking place and has consented to be tracked and interviewed at regular intervals. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently started on atorvastatin for her high cholesterol levels. She has a family history of heart disease, with her mother having suffered a heart attack in her 60s. The patient herself does not have any other significant medical history and reports no current medication use, supplement use, or over-the-counter medication use. She is compliant with her atorvastatin regimen and has not experienced any adverse effects. She is interested in participating in the study to determine if genetics play a role in how individuals respond to statins.

A 50-year-old Chinese male, a non-smoker, has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer with an EGFR genetic mutation. The patient has a history of chronic hepatitis B and has been receiving antiviral treatment for more than three months. The patient's liver function is stable with ALT and AST levels within the normal range. The patient's BMI is 23.5, and he has no other underlying medical conditions. The patient has not received any previous treatment for his cancer. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of TKIs in Chinese patients with non-small-cell lung cancer and hepatitis B.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy diagnosed with ADHD. He experiences significant difficulties with attention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity which have negatively impacted his academic and social functioning. He has never received any medications specifically to treat ADHD or any other psychiatric disorders. The patient and his parents are able to communicate effectively with the study investigators and are reliable to keep appointments for clinic visits and all tests, including neuropsychological testing and venipunctures. The patient has normal intelligence and is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the study. He does not have any other comorbid psychiatric disorders, seizure disorders, or cardiovascular disease. The patient and his parents have provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old male with a history of psoriasis for the past 10 years is seeking treatment for his condition. He has been experiencing moderate to severe chronic plaque-type psoriasis for the past 6 months, with a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) score of 15, an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score of 4, and a total body surface area (BSA) affected of 12%. He has tried various topical treatments, phototherapy, and systemic therapy in the past but has not been able to achieve adequate control of his symptoms. He has no significant medical problems, and his blood tests have not shown any hematological abnormalities. He has no history of tuberculosis, lymphoproliferative disease, or malignancy. He is not pregnant or nursing. He has not been previously treated with secukinumab or any drug that targets IL-17 or IL-17 receptor. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of autoinjector administered secukinumab for psoriasis.

A 27-year-old female from Uganda who has been using DMPA as her birth control method for the past 2 years is interested in trying a new injection method. She is in good health and reports feeling well. She is married and has 1 child. She works as a teacher and is financially stable. She has no known allergies or medical conditions. She received her most recent DMPA injection 8 weeks ago from a family planning provider in her community. She is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent document. She is also willing to provide contact information and be interviewed three months after enrollment.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with cirrhosis and end-stage liver disease (ESLD). He has been referred to transplant physical therapy and has a MELD score of 15. He owns a smartphone and has an understanding of its functionality. He has home wireless internet and does not have recurrent or persistent overt hepatic encephalopathy. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to promote physical activity and improve his health status. He is currently not following a physical activity regimen due to his health condition. He is married and has two adult children. He works as an accountant and spends most of his time sitting at his desk. He is willing to explore the features of EL-FIT and Fitbit apps and follow the physical activity recommendations provided by the research team. He is not using any drugs that might interfere with the study outcome. His general health is stable, and he has no other significant medical history. He is motivated to participate in the study and contribute to its success.

25 year old female marathon runner with 3 years of cross training experience, currently training for a half marathon race in 4 months. She has no history of cardiovascular, metabolic, or endocrine disease and is a non-smoker. She drinks alcohol occasionally and reports no allergies to fish, shellfish, algae, or seaweed. She is not pregnant nor planning to be pregnant in the near future. She is not taking any medication to control blood pressure, lipids, or blood glucose and has never taken anabolic-androgenic steroids. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of antioxidant supplementation on multiple endurance race performance, physiology, and recovery.

The patient is a 21-year-old college student enrolled in the University of Illinois at Chicago. She has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression for the past few months, which have been affecting her academic performance and social life. She owns a smartphone and is willing to participate in the trial of the IntelliCare Hub app. She is interested in trying out new interventions to manage her mental health and is willing to use the app daily as instructed. She has not sought counseling services previously but is open to seeking help if needed. She understands the importance of mental health literacy and is willing to complete the assessments and surveys within the app. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial.

50-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of invasive lobular carcinoma through breast biopsy. The patient has no history of allergies or autoimmune diseases, and is willing to undergo FES-PET/CT scanning for imaging evaluation. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is not currently undergoing treatment with estrogen receptor agonists and has not had any surgical resection of the site(s) of biopsy proven invasive lobular carcinoma. The patient is willing to have their clinical records reviewed for at least 24 months after enrollment.

Patient is a 2-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with pneumonia according to western medicine diagnostic criteria. She has been experiencing gasp-cough and has been diagnosed with TCM pneumonia meeting wind-heat blocking lungs pattern (feng re bi fei zheng). The disease has progressed within 72 hours. The patient's guardian has given informed consent for the child to participate in the clinical trial. The patient does not have any complications with other pulmonary disorders, heart disease, liver disease, kidney disease, blood disorders, or psychopathy. The patient is not allergic to the interventional medications. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months.

The patient is a 52-year-old overweight male with a history of snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness. He has been diagnosed with moderate obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) with an apnea-hypopnea index of 20. The patient has a history of hypertension with a blood pressure of 150/92 mmHg on antihypertensive monotherapy. He is willing to stop his current medication for at least 4 weeks prior to the screening visit. The patient has no known cardiovascular pathologies and is not currently participating in another clinical trial. He has signed the informed consent form and is affiliated with social security. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, does not have acute hepatic failure or biliary cirrhosis, and has a Cockcroft clearance of >30 ml/min/1.73m2. The patient is not allergic to Valsartan and is not currently taking drugs that act on arterial blood pressure or lithium. He is not under tutelage or curatelle and is not kept in detention or hospitalized.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of locally advanced and metastatic solid tumor. The patient has received standard therapy, however, has progressed on the treatment and is now intolerant to it. Radiologically measurable and clinically evaluable disease has been confirmed, with at least one tumor lesion of accessible non-critical location to biopsy. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and adequate hematological, liver, and renal function. The patient has negative serum pregnancy test results and agrees to remain abstinent or use effective methods of contraception. The patient has no active or untreated central nervous system metastases, spinal cord compression, or leptomeningeal disease. The patient has not received oral or IV antibiotics within 14 days prior to Day 1 and has no significant uncontrolled concomitant diseases. The patient has not received any investigational therapy or anti-cancer therapy within 28 days prior to the first RO6958688 infusion. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease or known hypersensitivity to any of the components of RO6958688 and atezolizumab.

45 year-old male with a history of smoking and asthma presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath, cough and chest pain. He was found to have low oxygen saturation on room air and was admitted to the hospital with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure. He has no prior history of COPD or congestive heart failure. He has been receiving supplemental oxygen therapy via nasal cannula at 6 L/min with some improvement in his oxygen saturation levels. He has not required intubation or invasive mechanical ventilation. The patient is alert and oriented with a Glasgow coma score of 15. He does not have cardiogenic shock or severe hemodynamic instability with a systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg and no evidence of decreased urinary output. His urinary output is normal. He has no upper airway disorders, severe ventricular arrhythmia, or active upper gastrointestinal bleeding. He is able to clear respiratory secretions and has no severe organ dysfunction in addition to respiratory failure. He meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial comparing high-flow nasal cannula system and non-invasive ventilation in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of Type 2 diabetes and a lower limb wound infection. The wound is grade 2 and located on the right foot. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He takes metformin and amlodipine daily. He has not received any antibiotics in the past three months. His wound has been treated with local wound care and debridement. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who had a stroke 6 months ago. He is able to walk independently, but his comfortable gait speed is less than 1.0 m/s and he exhibits stance time and step length asymmetry. He uses a knee brace for support. He has no history of balance deficits or unexplained falls, but he does have uncontrolled hypertension. He has not received botulinum toxin to the lower limb within the past 6 months, and he has not undergone physical therapy concurrently. He has no communication impairments and is able to understand the purpose and procedures of the study. He scored 28 on the MMSE.

This clinical trial is an observational study and does not involve recruitment of new patients. The first cohort comprises patients who underwent an attempt to close a post-infarct VSD using the AMPLATZER™ PIVSD Occluder via Emergency and Compassionate from 2011 until the end of 2016. The second cohort comprises patients who have previously been successfully implanted with the AMPLATZER™ PIVSD Occluder and have post-procedure echocardiogram available for evaluation of residual shunt by the echocardiography core laboratory. Therefore, there is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a diagnosis of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He has undergone previous systemic treatment for HCC, including sorafenib, but experienced a relapse. He has a Child-Pugh score of 6 and is classified as BCLC stage B. His AFP level is greater than 200 ng/mL, and he has at least one measurable lesion per RECIST v1.1. He is HLA-A 02:01 allele positive and has liver AFP expression IHC tests positive. He is in good general health, with an ECOG score of 1, and has an expected survival of greater than 12 weeks. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is greater than 50%, and his laboratory values are well within normal ranges. He does not have any active pulmonary infections and has normal pulmonary function. He has no contraindications for apheresis and has received apheresis by laboratory, and passed QC. He has not received any other anti-tumor systemic therapies not recommended in guidelines, immunocheckpoint inhibitors, genetically modified T cell therapy, or stem cell therapy. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he agrees to use effective contraceptive measures during the trial. He is willing to abstain from alcohol during the study period. He does not have any other primary cancer, significant clinical gastrointestinal bleeding, bone metastasis or central nervous system metastasis, or hepatic encephalopathy, epilepsy, cerebrovascular accident, and other central nervous system involvement diseases. He is not infected with hepatitis virus, syphilis, or other acquired, congenital immunodeficiency disorders. He has no heart insufficiency subjects of Grade III or IV according to NYHA classification criteria. He has not received systemic therapeutic steroid doses or other immunotherapy within two weeks before Leukocyte apheresis or radiotherapy within 6 weeks before Leukocyte apheresis.

A 12-year-old boy has been diagnosed with junctional epidermolysis bullosa (JEB) caused by COL17A1 mutation. He has had persistent large wounds and recurrent erosions for more than 3 months. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. The patient and his parents have been informed about the clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of autologous cultured epidermal grafts containing epidermal stem cells genetically modified with the aid of a gamma-retroviral vector carrying COL17A1 complementary DNA (cDNA) for restoration of the epidermis in patients with JEB. They have provided signed and dated informed consent prior to any study-related procedures. The patient is willing to undergo the required biopsy to collect the autologous epidermal cells to be used to produce the tissue for the treatment. The patient is cooperative and willing to comply with the study protocol as well as follow-up procedures. The patient has not participated in another clinical trial where investigational drug was received less than 6 months prior to screening Visit. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial.

54-year-old male with a history of essential hypertension (stage 2) presented to the clinic for a routine check-up. His blood pressure readings were consistently high, with no significant response to lifestyle modification or medications prescribed during the day. His blood pressure readings during the daytime were 150/90 mmHg, while his readings at nighttime were 140/85 mmHg. His medical history is significant for hyperlipidemia, which is well-controlled with statins. He has no history of diabetes, liver or renal disease. The patient is a non-smoker, with no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is not allergic to any medication. His BMI is 27, and he is physically active with no significant comorbidities. He is married and has a stable job with no significant stressors. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is focused on surveying healthcare providers' attitudes towards patients with substance use disorders before and after the implementation of the SBIRT model in the emergency room.

The patient is a 5-year-old male with a history of congenital myotonic dystrophy (CDM) diagnosed at birth. He had respiratory insufficiency, talipes equinovarus, feeding difficulties, and hypotonia at birth. He has a g-tube for feeding and requires bi-level positive airway pressure (BiPAP) at night. He has also been experiencing delays in motor development and difficulty with speech. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medication. He lives with his parents and two older siblings. He attends a special needs school and receives occupational, physical, and speech therapy on a regular basis. He is able to walk with assistance and is able to communicate using a combination of sign language and verbal communication. He has been seen by a geneticist and confirmed to have CDM through genetic testing. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance the understanding of the disease and potentially help their son and other children with CDM.

A 14-year-old boy with a history of peanut allergy visited the clinic with his parents. He had experienced severe allergic reactions in the past, requiring hospitalization. His allergy was confirmed by a positive patch test and specific IgE levels of f13>12 IU/mL and rAra h2>5.8 IU/mL. He had been following up with an allergist for the past year and had undergone a Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Food Challenge (DBPCFC) with a positive result below the threshold of 2 grams. His asthma was well-controlled, and he had no uncontrolled atopic dermatitis. The family lived close to a medical center in case of an emergency. The boy and his parents were motivated to participate in the study and understood the importance of maintaining a daily logbook of clinical monitoring.

55-year-old male with a history of chronic low back pain and bilateral radiculopathy on both lower extremities with radiating pain (VAS >=40) is being evaluated for eligibility for a clinical trial comparing two surgical approaches for spinal stenosis. The patient has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and medication but has not achieved significant relief. MRI findings demonstrate moderate to severe spinal stenosis at the L3-L4 level. The patient is interested in surgical intervention and is willing to consider participation in the clinical trial. The patient has no history of revision surgery, spondylolisthesis Gr II or higher, degenerative lumbar scoliosis with a Cobb angle >20, herniated disc, or other spinal diseases. The patient is mentally competent and is able to provide informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

This is not a clinical trial that involves patients, but rather a community-based research project that aims to promote family well-being and neighborhood cohesion in Kwun Tong community. Therefore, there are no specific patient descriptions required for this study.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who is scheduled for a routine blood test. She is generally healthy and has no significant past medical history. She is afraid of needles and has experienced anxiety and pain during previous venipunctures. She is able to report pain verbally and has no cognitive impairment. Her parents are present during the procedure and are supportive. She has not received any analgesics within the past 8 hours and has no damage, denuded or broken skin in the site of Buzzy application.

A 65 year old woman with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic knee pain is scheduled for a primary total knee replacement. She is able to ambulate without assistive devices, but experiences occasional instability and discomfort in her knee. Her anesthesia for the surgery will be spinal and regional block with adductor canal block. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the impact of the timing of physical therapy initiation on postoperative length of stay and the time to physical therapy clearance following the surgery. She is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 42-year-old female patient was recently diagnosed with invasive breast carcinoma. A biopsy confirmed that the tumor was HER2-positive. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no allergies to medications. The physical examination shows no significant findings except for a palpable breast lump measuring 2 cm in diameter. A bilateral mammogram has been performed, and a clip has been placed. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. The baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was normal as determined by MUGA scan. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, biologic therapy, or radiation therapy for breast cancer. She has no evidence of disease outside the breast or chest wall, except ipsilateral axillary lymph nodes. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of other malignancies other than adequately treated carcinoma in situ of the cervix or basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. The patient has no evidence of sensory and/or peripheral neuropathy and no serious, uncontrolled, concurrent infections. The patient is willing to use a reliable and appropriate contraceptive method as she is of childbearing potential.

35 yo F with a history of psoriasis for 5 years presents with dry, itchy, and scaly skin on both sides of the body. She has tried several over-the-counter moisturizers without much relief. She is currently on methotrexate for her psoriasis but still experiences dry skin. On examination, she has symmetrical bilateral target lesions that are at least 1.5 cm in diameter on both her arms and legs. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new spray for dry skin relief in eczema and psoriasis. She is willing to apply the study drug and placebo sprays three times a day to the assigned, randomized sides of her body and discontinue the use of moisturizers for the duration of the study. She is able to understand the consent form and comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with end-stage renal disease due to IgA nephropathy. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 2 years and is currently undergoing evaluation for living donor kidney transplantation. The potential living donor is his sister, with whom he has been HLA typed. The crossmatch test showed that he has anti-donor HLA antibodies, requiring pre-transplant desensitization. He has no history of prior transplants, splenectomy, or complement deficiency. He is in good general health with no active infections. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and he is compliant with his current hemodialysis regimen. He has received the required vaccinations against Neisseria meningitides, Pneumococcus, or H. influenzae at least two weeks prior to beginning desensitization. He is willing to comply with the protocol, and he has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 2-day-old healthy newborn boy delivered at 39 weeks and 2 days of gestation to a 28-year-old primigravida mother. The pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the delivery was a vaginal, spontaneous delivery with no significant perinatal events. The baby weighed 3.4 kg at birth and has been feeding well with no complications. The baby has not received any other painful stimuli except for the Vitamin K injection immediately after birth. The mother did not use opioids during pregnancy, labor or delivery and had no history of any chronic diseases or medical conditions. The baby is being cared for in a rooming-in facility and is within the age range of 12 to 72 hours. The parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 42-year-old woman complains of heartburn and regurgitation for the past 6 months. She has a history of chronic gastritis and has been diagnosed endoscopically. She has not taken any PPI or H2RA therapy in the last 2 weeks before enrollment. She has a GerdQ score of 9. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of gastrointestinal diseases. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol for 24 weeks.

The patient is a 63-year-old female with a history of smoking and a family history of pancreatic cancer. She has been experiencing mild to moderate upper abdominal pain for the past six months, with occasional nausea and vomiting. The patient had a CT scan which revealed a mass in the head of the pancreas measuring 4 cm in diameter. Biopsy of the mass confirmed it as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The patient underwent chemotherapy for three months, but had to discontinue due to severe side effects. The patient's ECOG performance status is 2 and she has no distant metastases or malignant ascites. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for EUS-RFA for unresectable pancreatic cancer. She has no known allergies and her vital signs are within normal limits.

The patient is a 55 year-old cancer survivor who has completed radiation therapy for breast cancer. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril for management. She also has a history of depression and has been on sertraline for the past year. She reports experiencing persistent fatigue and occasional insomnia. She is currently not receiving any other cancer treatments. She has no history of cardiovascular disorders and does not use any medications that affect cardiac rhythm. She has never had a pacemaker or defibrillator. She has no history of seizure disorder or altered cognitive abilities. She does not have any substance abuse or dependence issues. She has no history of brain metastases, primary brain cancer, or altered cognitive abilities. She does not use any long acting opioid medications. She speaks fluent English and is interested in participating in a non-pharmacologic therapy to improve her cancer survivorship.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with palpitations and shortness of breath. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and has been taking medication for both conditions. She reports occasional chest pain and dizziness, but denies any history of heart disease or stroke. On examination, she has an irregularly irregular heartbeat with a rapid ventricular response. Her blood pressure is elevated at 160/90 mmHg. An electrocardiogram reveals atrial fibrillation. The patient is admitted to the hospital for further evaluation and treatment. She agrees to participate in the atrial fibrillation registry study and provides written consent.

A 55-year-old woman recently diagnosed with endometrial cancer with deep myometrial invasion is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help detect lymph node metastasis. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. She has never had surgery before. She is not currently undergoing any treatment for her cancer and has not received radiation or chemotherapy. Her pregnancy test is negative. She is willing to undergo a PET/CT scan prior to surgery and is able to control her serum glucose to a value of =< 200 mg/dl for fludeoxyglucose F-18 [FDG]-PET/CT. She is interested in learning more about lymph node mapping and is willing to undergo intraoperative lymph node mapping with indocyanine green solution during full lymphadenectomy.

This is a 58-year-old Hispanic woman who is at risk for disability due to her sedentary lifestyle. She has identified herself as a Latino/Hispanic and is able to speak Spanish fluently. She reports engaging in less than three days of aerobic exercise per week and has danced less than two times per month over the past year. She is willing to be randomly assigned to either the treatment or control group and has no plans to leave the country for more than two consecutive weeks in the next year. She does not have uncontrolled cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, pacemaker in situ, severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), or any recent healing or unhealed fractures. She does not use any assistance device to walk (cane, walker, or wheelchair). She is excited to participate in this study and hopes to improve her physical and cognitive function through the BAILAMOS© program.

A 45-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of COVID-19, including fever, cough, and fatigue. He tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 in his most recent PCR test, which was conducted 24 hours ago. He has no known history of any chronic illness or medical conditions. He has been informed about the CONCOVID study and is willing to participate. He has provided written informed consent to receive a one-time infusion of 300mL of convalescent plasma (convP) from COVID-recovered donors, as well as standard of care treatment. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria. He is a suitable candidate for the study and will be randomized between the infusion of convP and standard of care treatment.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with glaucoma and has been attending the Wills Eye Glaucoma Clinic since 2012. He has been compliant with his follow-up appointments in the past but has missed his most recent appointment. He is married, has two grown children, and works as an accountant. He has no significant medical history other than the glaucoma diagnosis. He does not smoke or drink alcohol and exercises regularly. He takes no medications other than his glaucoma eye drops. He is concerned about the potential for vision loss and is motivated to maintain his eye health. He has a good understanding of his glaucoma diagnosis and treatment plan. His visual acuity is 20/30 in both eyes, and his intraocular pressure is well-controlled with medication. He has no significant ocular history other than the glaucoma diagnosis.

A 44-year-old woman with a history of moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis for the past 10 years presents with worsening symptoms despite previous treatment with cyclosporine and methotrexate.
