She reports experiencing significant discomfort and difficulty with daily activities due to the appearance and itching of her lesions. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she is taking amlodipine and atorvastatin respectively. She is generally in good health with no significant physical findings on exam other than the presence of erythematous, scaly plaques on her elbows, knees, and scalp. She is not pregnant and has no history of calcium metabolism disorder. She is willing to discontinue systemic and topical psoriasis treatments for the duration of the study and avoids UVB or PUVA phototherapy.

78-year-old female admitted to the acute geriatric unit with a history of hypertension, osteoporosis, and osteoarthritis. She has been taking multiple medications including amlodipine, lisinopril, alendronate, and ibuprofen for several years. She has experienced falls in the past and has mobility issues. She lives alone and has difficulty managing her medications. Her daughter helps her with medication management but is unable to be present during her hospital stay. She has a history of adverse drug reactions to antibiotics and has been hospitalized in the past due to medication-related complications. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

Pt is a 63yo postmenopausal F with a history of locally recurrent breast cancer presenting with new complaints of left-sided chest wall pain and shortness of breath. CT scan revealed multiple pulmonary nodules, pleural effusion, and left-chest wall soft tissue mass. Biopsy confirmed metastatic breast cancer. The patient received neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection followed by adjuvant radiotherapy to the chest wall. She then received adjuvant tamoxifen therapy for 2 years, following which she developed a local recurrence. She was treated with surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy, after which she developed multiple bone metastases. She received bisphosphonate therapy for the management of bone metastases. The patient was started on anastrozole for the management of metastatic breast cancer. She was randomized to the gefitinib arm of the study and was started on oral anastrozole and oral gefitinib once daily. Follow-up CT scans showed a partial response to treatment with no new metastases. The patient tolerated the treatment well and did not experience any significant adverse effects.

A 7 year old girl with medical complexity is being considered for this clinical trial. She has a tracheostomy and requires daily suctioning and assistance with breathing. She also has a history of frequent respiratory infections and has been hospitalized several times in the past year. Her parents are interested in participating in the study as they believe that the telehealth device may provide a more convenient and efficient way to manage their daughter's care. They have access to reliable internet at home and are fluent in English. The family is currently enrolled in the CCCMC program at ACH-OL and have provided consent for their daughter to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who visits the dentist regularly for check-ups and cleanings. She has a history of gum disease and has been told by her dentist that she has thin gingival tissue. She has one missing tooth in the premolar area and has natural teeth on either side. She is interested in dental implants and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve her peri-implant soft tissue. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol and is in good general health. She has no history of bleeding disorders or anticoagulant therapy. She maintains good oral hygiene and has no debilitating diseases. Her BMI is within normal range and her blood glucose level is normal. Her periodontal charting shows deep pockets in the missing tooth area. She is eager to participate in the study and wants to learn more about the CTG and T-PRF techniques.

The patient eligible for this clinical trial is a premature infant who was born weighing less than 1000 grams and had an MRI scan of the brain done at term gestation. The infant should not have any known genetic or chromosomal abnormalities. The study aims to correlate the volumes of the brain obtained from MRI scans with their corresponding development at 18 months corrected age. The parents or legal guardians of the infant should be willing to participate in the study and provide written consent.

9-year-old male with beta thalassemia major and a history of multiple blood transfusions presents with elevated liver function tests and positive serology for hepatitis C virus. The patient is currently being managed with chelation therapy for iron overload. The patient has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. The patient and their parents have provided informed consent to participate in this clinical trial to investigate the effect of Spirulina on serum hyaluronic acid levels in beta thalassemic children with hepatitis C.

A 62-year-old man comes to the clinic with complaints of urinary urgency and frequency. He has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and is currently taking an alpha blocker medication. He reports having to urinate frequently during the day and night, with an average of 10 micturition episodes per day and 3 nocturia episodes per night. His International Prostate Symptom Score total score is 12. He has a prostate-specific antigen level of 3.5 ng/mL and there is no history of prostate cancer. He has a post void residual volume value of 50 mL. He has no lower urinary tract pathology and his maximum urinary flow (Qmax) is 10 mL/second with a minimum voided volume of 150 mL. He does not have uncontrolled hyperglycemia or hypertension. He is not taking any medications that could interfere with the study. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a vaccine against human cytomegalovirus (HCMV). She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has never been diagnosed with HCMV and has a negative test result. Her BMI is 23 kg/m². She is using a combination of oral contraceptive pills for birth control. She is willing to forego receipt of other routine vaccinations (with the exception of seasonal influenza vaccination) for five months after study entry. She understands the requirements of the study and is willing to comply with them. She has no tattoos or dermatological conditions in the area of the injection site. She is able to return for follow-up visits as required by the study.

Patient is a 60-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with stage III prostate cancer. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has undergone hormonal therapy with flutamide for the past 6 months but has experienced progressive disease. He has no other significant medical history, and his laboratory studies are within normal limits. He has measurable tumors, and bone metastases have been detected. He is currently not enrolled in any other clinical trial and is willing to participate in this study.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl who attends a local elementary school. She has been experiencing symptoms of head lice infestation, including itching and scratching for the past week. Upon examination by a healthcare provider, she was found to have at least 10 live lice and viable nits. She has not used any other lice treatments or medicated products for at least four weeks prior to the visit. The patient and her parent/guardian are willing to participate in the study and agree not to use a nit comb during the study. She is generally healthy, with no known allergies or skin conditions that would interfere with the evaluation. The patient's parent/guardian is willing to bring her to the study site and adhere to the study requirements.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy with recurrent urinary tract infections. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and frequent urination for the past few months. He was diagnosed with vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) after undergoing a voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) test. The VUR causes urine to flow backward into his kidneys, leading to recurrent kidney infections. The boy is scheduled to undergo a DMSA scan to evaluate his renal function and scarring. He has no known medical allergies or significant medical history. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. The boy is in the second grade and enjoys playing soccer with his friends. He is a healthy weight and has no known significant medical history. There is nothing remarkable in his physical exam.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the intensive care unit due to severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to pneumonia. He has been on veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) for the past 48 hours and has required full neuromuscular blockade to control his respiratory effort. His Riker Sedation-Agitation Scale (SAS) is currently 2, indicating adequate sedation. An esophageal balloon and a catheter will be placed to monitor respiratory effort. The medical team has determined that the patient requires neuromuscular blockade to ensure toleration of ECMO and is willing for the patient to undergo a trial of partial neuromuscular blockade. He has no contraindications to esophageal catheterization or neuromuscular blockade.

A 25-year-old medical student presents with a history of feeling overwhelmed and stressed, which has been impacting their ability to focus on their studies. They have noticed a decline in their mood, with feelings of sadness and hopelessness. They have also been experiencing physical symptoms such as fatigue, headaches, and difficulty sleeping. They have no prior experience with mindfulness techniques but are interested in exploring this as a potential tool to help manage stress and improve their mental health. They have no history of psychiatric illness, substance abuse, or other medical conditions that would exclude them from participating in the study. They have access to a computer and are comfortable with using online platforms for learning.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with AIDS-related Kaposi's sarcoma. He has visible skin lesions and has reported experiencing pain and discomfort in the affected areas. The patient has a history of opportunistic infections, including candidiasis and tuberculosis, but is currently on stable antiretroviral therapy. His performance status is 1 and his blood counts, liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has not received prior systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy for Kaposi's sarcoma and has not undergone radiation therapy within the past 7 days. The patient is willing to participate in the quality of life assessments and has given signed, written informed consent.

5-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) type II presented to the clinic with progressive weakness, difficulty walking, and frequent falls. The patient has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and has been receiving physical therapy to maintain muscle strength. The patient's genetic testing confirmed homozygous deletion of exon 7 in the SMN1 gene. The patient has not been on any medication for SMA previously. The patient and their caregiver provided written informed consent and agreed to participate in the open-label phase I/II clinical trial to assess the safety and dosing effect of valproic acid (VPA) on SMN levels in SMA patients. The patient will undergo baseline laboratory and physical examination assessments to monitor their liver, hematologic, metabolic, and nutritional status. They will also undergo various secondary outcome measures, including gross motor function, electrophysiological measures of denervation, DEXA estimates of body composition, bone mineral density and content, measures of pulmonary function, and quantitative SMN mRNA and protein levels in blood cells. The patient will need 2-3 baseline visits over a 3-6 month period prior to enrollment, and follow-up visits will be scheduled at 3, 6, and 12 months on treatment.

A 45-year-old office worker was scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent gallstones. She initially presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She has a history of hyperlipidemia and is on atorvastatin. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has no history of any significant medical problems and has never had any surgeries before. Her body mass index is 25. She is married and has two children. She works in an office and enjoys cooking and gardening in her free time. She attended the preoperative anaesthesia assessment clinic and was cleared for surgery. She has arranged for her husband to take a few days off from work to take care of her after the surgery.

A 7-month-old Caucasian male infant is scheduled to undergo palatoplasty. The baby was born at 36 weeks of gestation via vaginal delivery, with a birth weight of 2.8 kg. The pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the baby has been healthy since birth. The infant is currently breastfed and is up to date on all vaccinations. The family history is unremarkable for any genetic disorders or chronic medical conditions. The baby has not been on any chronic pain treatments or analgesics prior to the scheduled surgery. The physical exam shows no abnormalities other than the cleft palate. The infant's American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status is 2. The family has been informed about the study and has given consent for their child to participate.

This is a 60 year old postmenopausal female with a history of osteoporosis for the past 5 years. She has been taking bisphosphonates for the past 2 years as per her physician's prescription. She has not experienced any side effects related to the medication. She has a history of gingivitis and is currently undergoing treatment for it. She has never had any dental implants. She is interested in participating in a study to investigate the effects of bisphosphonates on alveolar bone among osteoporotic women. She understands that the study will involve taking panoramic radiographs and Cone-beam CT scans. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has always maintained an active lifestyle. She exercises regularly and eats a healthy diet. She has no history of spine surgery, hip implantation or replacement, scoliosis, or other spine deformity. She does not use walking canes or a wheelchair. She is interested in participating in a study to help researchers develop procedures to ensure that different CT scanners measure the same results for the same amount of fat or muscle. She is in good health and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is willing to undergo CT scans on different scanners to contribute to the development of reliable procedures for future research studies.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently 12 weeks pregnant with her second child. She has a BMI of 28 and a family history of type 2 diabetes, as her father was diagnosed with the condition at age 55. Her first child was born weighing 4,200 grams. She does not smoke and has no known allergies. She is currently not taking any medications and has no chronic medical conditions. She experienced mild nausea during the first trimester but it has since resolved. She is interested in participating in a study to investigate the effects of soy protein and isoflavones on glucose metabolism and lipid levels during pregnancy, as she is aware of the increased risk of gestational diabetes due to her family history and previous pregnancy history.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with advanced breast cancer that has progressed despite previous treatment. She has had breast cancer surgery at NUH (lumpectomy or mastectomy) or a diagnostic core biopsy for breast cancer. Consent has been obtained for blood taking and access to archival tissue. The patient is due to start a new course of anti-cancer therapy and is eligible for this clinical trial.

Patient is a 65-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer. His biopsy results reveal adenocarcinoma in the prostate gland. His PSA level is 15 ng/dL and his Gleason score is 7. He has no other history of cancer except for basal cell carcinoma. He has not undergone any previous radiotherapy or radical surgery for carcinoma of the prostate. He has no hip prosthesis and his prostate volume is less than 60 mL. He has no major medical or psychiatric illness that would prevent him from participating in the study. He is in good health with a Zubrod performance status of 1. He understands the study requirements and is willing to use effective contraception if necessary.

15-year-old female with a history of epilepsy diagnosed at age 8. She has been on antiepileptic medication since diagnosis and has had 2 seizures in the past year. She is currently in high school and struggles with organization, time management, and completing tasks. Her parents report that she often forgets homework assignments and has difficulty following through with her responsibilities at home. She has no other medical or developmental conditions and is fluent in English. Both the patient and her parents are willing to participate in the study and have given their consent and assent to participate. They live within 20 miles of the study site.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing recurrent patellar dislocations for several years. She has tried conservative management with physical therapy and bracing, but her symptoms have persisted. She has no significant past medical history and no history of prior knee surgeries. On examination, she has a positive apprehension test and a lateral patellar tilt. Imaging studies show evidence of trochlear dysplasia and a high-riding patella. The patient is interested in undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction to address her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to comply with the follow-up requirements.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. She has been experiencing memory loss, confusion, and difficulty with daily activities for the past year. She has no history of other neurological disorders. She has a reliable study partner who accompanies her to all visits and can answer questions about her. She has a diagnosis of probable Alzheimer's disease according to the National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders and Stroke Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders Association criteria with a MMSE score of 20. She has a positive visual read on an amyloid PET scan consistent with a diagnosis of AD. She has no other clinically relevant hematological, hepatic, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, metabolic, endocrine, or CNS disease or medical conditions that would interfere with the study objectives. She is not pregnant or nursing and is using an effective method of contraception. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or allergy to drugs. She has not received any investigational medication within the last 3 months or 5 elimination half-life. She has no contraindications for MRI.

This is a 58-year-old male who presented with chest pain and was diagnosed with a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). He underwent a coronary angiogram which showed significant stenosis in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). The patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the implantation of a BioMatrix AlphaTM stent as per clinical practice. The patient is currently stable and eligible for dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) according to guidelines. The patient has agreed to comply with the follow-up requirements and has a life expectancy of greater than one year at the time of consent. The patient has no planned surgery within six months of the PCI procedure and has not received any additional stent apart from the BioMatrix AlphaTM stent during the index procedure.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who presents with a sore throat and difficulty swallowing. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past three days and rates her pain as moderate to severe on the visual rating scale. She reports no fever or cough but has had some mild nasal congestion. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. She works as a teacher and has missed several days of work due to her symptoms. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of completing patient diaries and remaining at the doctor's practice for the initial three hours following the first intake of study medication. She has never had acute pharyngitis before and has not taken any antibiotics or steroids in the past week. She does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse, and she is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 6-month-old baby boy with a history of recurrent infections and a family history of immune disorders. He has been diagnosed with severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome (SCID) and has decreasing T cells, any B cells, and increasing natural killer (NK) cells. The patient's parents have been tested and are not a match for bone marrow donation. The baby will require a transplant from either an unrelated donor or umbilical cord blood. The patient's pediatrician recommended this clinical trial and the parents have agreed to participate. The patient is currently in good health and has not had any recent infections. The family understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to commit to the long hospital stay and follow-up appointments. The patient will be admitted to the hospital for the transplant and will remain there for up to 6 weeks. The patient will receive a preparative regimen of busulfan, fludarabine and antithymocyte globulin (ATG). After the preparative regimen, cells from the donor will be given. To prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), cyclosporine will also be given. The patient will be monitored closely for immune recovery and any potential side effects.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer (Stage II). She has been married to her partner for 15 years and they have two children. She reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious since receiving the diagnosis, and is concerned about how the cancer will affect her body image and sexual functioning. Her partner is also feeling stressed and worried about how he can best support her during this time. They are both willing to participate in a study that aims to improve their communication and coping skills as a couple in the face of cancer. They are fluent in German and able to commit to the study requirements.

The patient is a 62-year-old male diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He had an angiogram recently and his doctor recommended a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) due to the complex nature of his condition. He is scheduled to undergo the procedure in two weeks. He has a history of hypertension, and he is taking lisinopril 20mg once daily. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is not allergic to iodinated contrast. His eGFR is 70 ml/min/1.73m², suggesting a moderate decline in kidney function. He has given his informed consent to participate in the clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy of the Dynamic Coronary Roadmap in reducing the total iodinated contrast volume related to PCI.

A 45-year-old female with a history of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) diagnosed by Society of Hepatology, Chinese Medical Association criteria in 2019, presented with mild abdominal discomfort and an elevated ALT level of 70 U/L on routine blood work. She reports no significant alcohol consumption, and her liver-to-spleen ratio on CT scan was less than 1. She has no known history of viral hepatitis or secondary liver diseases. She is not on total parenteral alimentation and has no autoimmune or metabolic liver disease. She has no severe cardiovascular or renal dysfunction. She has not been diagnosed with diabetes and her fasting glucose level is 5.2 mmol/L. She is not currently taking statins. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the direct effects of a Chinese herb formula on liver fat, liver function, insulin sensitivity, lipid profile, non-esterified fatty acids, and adipokines in subjects with NAFLD.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with cervical cancer. She has been experiencing symptoms such as pelvic pain, abnormal vaginal bleeding, and abnormal discharge. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of cervical cancer, and her oncologist has recommended a combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy to treat the cancer. The patient is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. However, her recent blood work shows that her hemoglobin levels are between 9-13 g/dL, which is below the normal range. She is experiencing some fatigue and shortness of breath as a result. She has been informed about the clinical trial that involves the use of NESP to stimulate the body to produce more red blood cells during treatment for cervical cancer. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve her anemia and overall quality of life during treatment. She has signed the consent form and meets all eligibility criteria, including a Karnofsky Performance Status score of 70 or higher, and no evidence of hemolysis, GI bleeding, or bleeding due to recent surgery.

A 32-year-old woman with a history of Postural Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) for the past 5 years. She experiences significant and sustained increase in heart rate (>30 beats/min) upon positional change from supine to standing and has symptoms of palpitations, lightheadedness, and mental clouding which improve on recumbence. She has tried various pharmacological treatments and non-pharmacological interventions such as salt and fluid loading, exercise, and physical countermaneuvers, but her symptoms persist. She has also been prescribed compression garments, but is unsure of their effectiveness. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of compression in POTS and determine what configuration is most effective. Her past medical history includes mild hypertension which is currently controlled with medication. She is able and willing to travel to the Libin Cardiovascular Institute of Alberta Autonomic Testing Lab at the University of Calgary for the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 38-year-old male was diagnosed with extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma (nasal type) a year ago. He received 6 cycles of chemotherapy and achieved partial response. However, 3 months ago, he presented with recurrent symptoms, including nasal congestion, epistaxis, and skin rash. Biopsy confirmed disease progression. He was referred to the oncology department for further management. He has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with amlodipine. He is a non-smoker and denies any illicit drug use. He has a stable family and social life. He is currently working as a software engineer. He complains of fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional nausea. Physical examination reveals nasal crusting, skin rash, and palpable cervical lymph nodes. Laboratory findings are significant for elevated LDH and beta-2 microglobulin levels. CT scan shows multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions, as well as splenomegaly. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for his relapsed NK/T cell lymphoma and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis for the past 5 years. He has been taking regular medication for the management of his condition. The patient complains of stiffness and pain in his hands and wrists, which has been affecting his daily activities. He reports difficulty in gripping objects and performing tasks that require fine motor skills. The patient has no history of finger amputation, finger infection, neurological disease, trauma or surgery involving the upper extremity, and psychiatric or cognitive problems. He is willing to participate in the study to assess his hand functions and wrist joint position sense.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, as it focuses on evaluating the sustainability of a risk management program in primary care offices. Therefore, there is no patient description required.

The patient is a 40 year old woman living in the UK. She has been struggling with depression for the past few months and is currently seeking treatment for it. She often feels lonely and isolated, despite having a few close friends and family members. Her loneliness is affecting her mood and is making it difficult for her to engage in social activities. She has a history of anxiety and has tried various treatments in the past, including therapy and medication. She is currently on antidepressant medication and attends therapy sessions every two weeks. She works part-time as a receptionist and spends her free time reading and watching TV. She is interested in trying new activities and making new friends, but feels stuck and unsure of how to do so. She is willing to participate in a group-based behavioural programme to reduce her feelings of loneliness and improve her interpersonal functioning. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) in his left eye. He reports experiencing sudden vision loss in his left eye, with a visual acuity of 2/10. He has not received any previous treatment for his condition. His medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes medication. He has no known allergies or history of eye surgery. The patient's central macular thickness is greater than 250µm, and there are no signs of neovascularization or other eye diseases. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who has been experiencing eye discomfort and dryness for the past few months. She reports a feeling of grittiness in her eyes, as well as itching and burning sensations. She has no history of ocular or lacrimal surgery, nor has she ever used contact lenses. She has no known allergies and has not had any recent antibiotic usage. She has a history of rosacea but reports no other systemic diseases with ocular involvement. She has not been diagnosed with any liver problems and has no known sensitivity to cyclines. Upon examination, she scores at least one in two symptoms and two signs of posterior blepharitis according to the study criteria. She is eligible for the clinical trial and will be randomly assigned to receive either oral azithromycin or oral doxycycline in a double-blinded fashion. She will be instructed to apply warm compress and eyelid scrubbing 2 times a day for 5 minutes each in the treatment period. Symptoms and signs will be recorded for her at baseline visit (before treatment) and then in the days 7, 31, 37 and 61 after treatment.

A 56-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and blood in his stool. He had a previous history of colorectal cancer and had undergone surgical resection and chemotherapy. His most recent CT scan showed no evidence of metastatic disease. His ECOG performance status was 1. The pathology specimens from his previous surgery were available for the study. His medical history was notable for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all controlled with medications. He did not have any known allergies and was not taking any herbal supplements or alternative medicines. He provided informed consent to participate in the AlfaOmega Master Observational Trial.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who leads a healthy lifestyle, exercises regularly and has no significant past medical history. She has never smoked and does not take any medications. Her blood pressure is 129/78 mmHg, fasting blood glucose is 85 mg/dL and LDL cholesterol level is 110 mg/dL. She has a BMI of 23 and has maintained a stable weight for the past year. She has no history of neurological or psychological disorders in the past three years, and has not taken any oral antioxidants in the past two weeks. She is interested in participating in the Predictive Medicine Research study to help establish normal values for novel markers of risk for cardiovascular disease. She is willing to undergo various tests and evaluations including blood tests, spirometry test, stationary bike exercise capacity evaluation, bone density scan, ultrasound of the artery of the neck and arm, nerve conduction study, bio-impedance, and questionnaires to assess memory and mood. She is able to give informed consent and is looking forward to contributing to the study.

A 63-year-old postmenopausal woman was referred to the clinic by her primary care physician due to a recent fracture in her wrist after a minor fall. She has a medical history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She has no history of cancer or other bone diseases. Her BMI is 27. She has not taken any medication to treat osteoporosis before. She is able to self-administer injections and has no known allergies to the study drug or raloxifene HCl. She has not had any vaginal bleeding due to unknown causes or other severe or chronically disabling conditions. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

Pt is a 55yo male with a history of occupational asbestos exposure presenting with advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma. The patient has completed six cycles of first-line, pemetrexed-based regimen for advanced or metastatic disease, with non-progressive disease. ECOG Performance Status is 1. Adequate baseline bone marrow, hepatic and renal function. Measurable or non-measurable disease according to malignant pleural mesothelioma-modified RECIST criteria. No prior investigational agents. No history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or serious cardiac arrhythmia requiring medication. No uncontrolled hypertension. No history of Central Nervous System disease. No active or uncontrolled systemic disease/infections or serious illness or medical conditions incompatible with the protocol. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who presented with hematemesis and melena. The patient was diagnosed with bleeding peptic ulcers with major stigmata of recent hemorrhage, and the ulcers were treated with local injection of diluted epinephrine 1:10000. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is on antihypertensive, lipid-lowering, and hypoglycemic medications. The patient does not smoke or use illicit drugs. The patient's physical exam and laboratory studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 11 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a medical history of noise-induced hearing loss. The patient has experienced sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear for the past 8 months. The patient's Pure Tone Audiometry (PTA) results indicate that the hearing loss is mild to moderately severe, with a score of 60 dB in the affected ear. The patient has not participated in any previous FX-322 clinical trials and is not currently taking any medication consisting of valproic acid, valproate sodium, or divalproex sodium. The patient has no perforation of tympanic membrane or other tympanic membrane disorders that would interfere with the delivery and safety assessment of an intratympanic medication. The patient has no conductive hearing loss greater than 15 dB at a single frequency or greater than 10 dB at two or more contiguous octave frequencies in the study ear. The patient has no history of head or neck radiation treatment or exposure, platinum-based chemotherapy treatment, or exposure to another investigational drug within 28 days prior to injection of study drug. The patient is willing to use highly effective contraception during the study participation or remain abstinent, and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 8 years. She has been treated with methotrexate and two other DMARDs, but her condition has not improved. She is currently experiencing moderate to severe pain and stiffness in her joints, especially in her hands, wrists, and ankles. The pain is more severe in the morning and decreases throughout the day, but it often returns in the evening. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued, which makes it difficult for her to complete daily activities. She has trouble sleeping due to the pain and stiffness. She has a history of depression but is currently not experiencing any depressive symptoms. The patient is currently not pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of RoActemra/Actemra in treating her rheumatoid arthritis symptoms and reducing her fatigue levels.

A 14-year-old male diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is being considered for a Phase 2 clinical trial of pamrevlumab (FG-3019) for non-ambulatory subjects with DMD. The patient has been non-ambulatory for the past 2 years and has a Brooke Score for Arms and Shoulders of 5. The patient's medical history confirms the Duchenne mutation in available genetic testing. The patient's pulmonary function test shows a percent predicted FVC between 40 and 90, inclusive. The patient is currently on a stable dose of corticosteroids for a minimum of 6 months and meets all other inclusion criteria. The patient has not been exposed to any other investigational drug or approved product for DMD within the last 28 days prior to start of study treatment. The patient and their legal guardian have given written consent/assent to participate in the clinical trial, and the patient will be closely monitored for safety throughout the study.

Patient is a 2-year-old boy from the United States who has had two episodes of wheezing in the past 3 months. His parents have a history of asthma and eczema. He also has a history of eczema and food allergies. He has not been diagnosed with asthma, but due to his risk factors, he is at high risk for developing persisting asthma. His skin test is positive for dust mites and his specific Immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibody titers are elevated for cat and pollen. He has not received immunotherapy before and does not have any severe systemic conditions or chronic lung diseases.

This is a 24-year-old female diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at the age of 6. She has been admitted to King's College Hospital due to an acute infective pulmonary exacerbation characterized by an increase in respiratory symptoms. She is currently receiving intravenous antibiotics to treat her exacerbation. She has a history of moderate to severe lung disease with frequent exacerbations requiring hospitalization. She reports having difficulty clearing her airways and often experiences shortness of breath and coughing fits. She has no known allergies or other medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in this study. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in a randomized controlled crossover study to investigate the efficacy of high frequency airflow oscillation (HFAO) delivered using the Aerosure device to improve sputum clearance in patients with CF.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She has no prior history of systemic therapy or radiotherapy for breast cancer. Her current chemotherapy regimen is either Doxorubicin and Cyclophosphamide (AC) or Doxorubicin, Cyclophosphamide, and 5-FU (CAF) under standardized dosage. She has experienced a fall in her white blood cell count, measuring between 1,000 to 3,000/mm3 or a fall in her absolute neutrophil count to between 500 to 1,500/mm3 on Day 8 or Day 15 while on Cycle 1. She has normal liver and kidney function, and her hemoglobin is above 8.7 g/dL. She is not pregnant, and a negative pregnancy test result has been obtained. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to bean products, no history of myocardial infarction or angina, and no uncontrollable acute or chronic diseases, including hypertension or diabetes. She has not participated in any investigational drug study within the past 30 days.

The patient is a 52-year-old Chinese male diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B. He has been receiving nucleotide antiviral therapy and is willing to undergo laboratory tests related to renal function, including glomeruli filtration rate (eGFR), urea nitrogen (BUN), blood creatinine, uric acid, beta 2 microglobulin, alpha 1 microglobulin, and urine protein. He has no decompensated liver cirrhosis, HIV infection, or malignant tumors. He has no severe mental illness or cognitive impairment and is willing to participate in the study. His medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well controlled with medication. He has not participated in any clinical research of new drugs within the past three weeks and understands and expresses informed consent.

A 35-year-old male who enjoys drinking orange juice on a regular basis is eligible for this study. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, gastrointestinal, liver or kidney disease, alcoholism, diabetes or metabolic diseases. He is not currently taking any vitamin or mineral supplements, antibiotics, antiacids or any drugs. He is a non-smoker and not trying to conceive a child with his partner. He is willing to participate in a cross-over study where he will receive either "Bahia" orange juice, "Cara-Cara" orange juice or a isocaloric control drink. He is interested in contributing to scientific research on the effects of orange juice intake on human metabolism.

A 45-year-old male diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, specifically diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, is seeking treatment options for his relapsed/refractory condition. He has previously undergone one cycle of combination chemotherapy but has not experienced a significant improvement in his condition. He presents with measurable disease on cross-sectional imaging, with the largest lesion measuring 4 cm in the longest diameter. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score of 1, indicating he is ambulatory and capable of light work. His laboratory results show an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2,000 cells/mm^3, a platelet count of 80,000/mm^3, and a calculated creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min. His serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase/aspartate aminotransferase (SGOT/AST) and serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase/alanine transaminase (SGPT/ALT) are within normal limits, as is his serum total bilirubin. He is not a candidate for autologous stem cell transplant and has no history of active CNS lymphoma or other malignancies within the past year. He is negative for HIV and hepatitis B and C. He is willing to follow the pregnancy precautions outlined in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with a pituitary tumor. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She does not have any history of cardiac or pulmonary disease, and she is a non-smoker. She has no known drug allergies. She is scheduled to undergo transsphenoidal surgery to remove the tumor. Her preoperative laboratory tests are within normal limits. She has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiac surgery in the past year, and she has not taken any sedatives or opioids prior to the surgery. She is a native English speaker and is able to understand and complete the QoR-40 questionnaire. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 50-year-old male patient diagnosed with rectal cancer underwent anterior resection of the rectum with sphincter preservation and received a protective ileostomy. The patient is scheduled for ileostomy closure surgery in 2 months. He has no history of cognitive impairment and is able to sign the informed consent. The patient does not receive active treatment with Qt or Rt. He does not have a history of fecal incontinence prior to the anterior rectal resection surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the study.

A 42 year old woman came to the clinic complaining of dizziness and lightheadedness on standing up. She had a past medical history of spinal cord injury due to a car accident 1 year ago, and had been experiencing these symptoms since then. She had been taking pain medication and muscle relaxants for her injury, but her symptoms of orthostatic hypotension (OH) persisted. During the physical exam, her blood pressure was 120/80 mmHg while lying down, but dropped to 90/60 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing. She had no other significant medical history or medication use that could cause her OH. She was eligible for this clinical trial and was randomized to the midodrine-only treatment group. She was educated on the treatment and will follow up after 1 and 3 months.

A 52-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and is currently being evaluated for treatment options. He has a history of alcohol abuse and has been experiencing abdominal pain, weight loss, and fatigue for several months. He has undergone a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. He has Child-Pugh class A liver disease and has adequate hematological, renal, cardiac, and pulmonary function. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) as a predictive biomarker for HCC. He understands that the study involves the collection of DNA samples from his plasma, blood cells, and solid tumor tissues, which will be analyzed to identify cancer-specific variations in cfDNA and primary tumor lesions. He hopes that the findings of this study can help diagnose HCC in early stages and aid in monitoring the response to treatment.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer through a mammogram. The tumor is small, measuring 2.5 cm in diameter, and is located in her right breast. The patient has no other known medical conditions and has never had surgery before. She is concerned about the prospect of losing her breast and asks about the possibility of breast-conserving surgery. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, as she is between 35-75 years old, has a tumor smaller than 4 cm, and has no multifocality. She is offered the option of having a preoperative breast MRI to evaluate if there are any additional lesions that could affect her eligibility for breast-conserving surgery. The patient agrees to participate in the study and undergoes the MRI. The results reveal no additional lesions and confirm the eligibility for breast-conserving surgery. The patient proceeds with the surgery and receives adjuvant therapy as recommended by her treating physician.

45 yo F diagnosed with metabolic syndrome (MS) based on Adult Treatment Panel - III criteria. She has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and impaired fasting glucose. She has been struggling with weight loss despite attempts at diet and exercise modifications. She is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has no history of chronic renal failure, diabetic neuropathy, intestinal malabsorption diseases, systemic autoimmune diseases or liver failure. She does not have active cancer. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. She does not consume high fiber dietary supplements or omega 3 acids. She is not taking anorexic drugs and is not under a diet for weight loss implemented by a health professional. Her current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin and metformin. She has not had bariatric surgery in the past. Her blood pressure is currently well controlled at 130/80 mmHg and her lipid panel shows elevated triglycerides of 220 mg/dL and LDL cholesterol of 150 mg/dL.

A 58-year-old woman living in West London has received an invitation for breast screening from the NHS. She has a family history of breast cancer and recognizes the importance of attending her appointment. However, she has a busy schedule and is concerned about forgetting the appointment. She has a mobile phone and is comfortable receiving text messages. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of differently worded text message reminders on the uptake of breast screening appointments. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and has not undergone bilateral mastectomies nor has she opted out of breast screening. She understands that she will be randomly allocated to receive one of three text messages and that the trial aims to improve screening attendance in West London. She consents to participate in the trial and is excited to be part of a study that could improve breast cancer detection rates.

Patient is a 52-year-old woman from the United States who has been recently diagnosed with stage III breast carcinoma. She has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She is postmenopausal and has completed chemotherapy. Her tumor is ER/PR-positive. Her performance status is ECOG 1, with no history of seizures or CNS metastases. Her laboratory studies show ANC of 1,800/mm(3), platelet count of 95,000/mm(3), serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, creatinine clearance of 70mL/min, bilirubin of 1.5 times normal, SGOT of 2 times normal, alkaline phosphate of 2 times normal, and fasting triglycerides of 2.5 times normal. She has no allergies to study medications and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. She has given informed consent and is medically and psychiatrically stable.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of stage III ovarian cancer, previously treated with primary debulking surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy, presents with a rising CA-125 level and evidence of peritoneal carcinomatosis on imaging. She has no significant comorbidities and an ECOG performance status of 0. She is a candidate for aggressive cytoreductive surgery and has no evidence of extra-abdominal disease. She is willing to undergo a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy if necessary. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, and she has no active infections. She has not received any chemotherapy within the previous 3 weeks and has a preoperative diagnosis of ovarian cancer. She has no evidence of cardiac or pulmonary conditions that would preclude aggressive surgery.

32F with a history of occasional recreational use of sedatives referred to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the abuse potential of Neurontin. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of drug dependence. She has no current or past diagnosis of any type of drug dependence within the past year. She has no active suicidal ideation or suicidal behavior within 5 years prior to screening as determined through the use of the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS). The patient reports no significant medical history and is willing to participate in the study under fasted conditions. She has no allergies to any of the study drugs and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

58 yo F with a 6-month history of lower back pain and bilateral leg pain radiating down to the feet, worse with standing or walking. MRI shows spinal stenosis at L4-L5 with a grade I spondylolisthesis measuring 5 mm. No prior history of lumbar spinal surgery in the region of stenosis. Patient has been treated conservatively with physical therapy and medications (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, and gabapentin) without significant symptom relief. Patient is interested in exploring surgical options and has been referred to the study. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. No history of diabetes or heart disease. Medications: Lisinopril, atorvastatin, and calcium/vitamin D supplement.

A 65-year-old male patient presents with persistent anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia for the past 6 months. He reports occasional fatigue and weakness, but denies any fever, night sweats, or weight loss. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no significant family history. Physical examination is unremarkable except for mild pallor. Laboratory tests show a hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, white blood cell count of 3.4 x 10^9/L, and platelet count of 89 x 10^9/L. Peripheral blood smear reveals hypochromic and microcytic red blood cells, along with a few immature myeloid cells. Bone marrow biopsy reveals a normocellular marrow with trilineage hematopoiesis and no blast cells. The patient does not meet the minimal diagnostic criteria for MDS but is diagnosed with CCUS. The patient is eligible to participate in the follow-up study of ICUS and CCUS patients.

A 26-year-old woman diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 15 presented with severe gastrointestinal symptoms, including abdominal pain, bloating, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months, affecting her daily activities and quality of life. She has been taking insulin therapy for the past 10 years, and her blood glucose levels are well controlled. She has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or infections, and she has not taken antibiotics or morphine in the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the near future. She has not undergone any abdominal surgeries in the past. Her current medication includes insulin, metformin, and lisinopril. She speaks Danish and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and pilot-efficacy of faecal microbiota transplantation as a treatment for severe gastrointestinal neuropathy in patients with diabetes mellitus type 1. She scores above 40 on the GSRS-IBS questionnaire and meets all other inclusion criteria for the trial.

A 62-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of osteoporosis presents to the clinic with lower back pain that started four weeks ago. The patient reports that she has been taking over-the-counter analgesics to manage the pain, but it has not improved. She reports no history of trauma, falls or other injuries that could have caused the pain. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, for which she takes amlodipine and atorvastatin, respectively. She denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. On physical examination, tenderness is elicited on palpation of the lower lumbar spine, and there is no neurological deficit. Imaging studies confirm a recent vertebral osteoporotic fracture. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess a new medication for her condition.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained a moderate traumatic brain injury. He lost consciousness for 2 minutes and experienced post-traumatic amnesia for 30 minutes. The patient was admitted to the neurosurgical department of the University Hospital of Messina, Italy, for treatment. His Glasgow Coma Score was 10. The patient has no pre-existing neurological disorders affecting the brain or spinal cord, and he does not have severe hypertension, diabetes, or chronic renal disease. The CT scan showed a Marshall Scale class IV injury. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written consent.

A 45-year old female patient was diagnosed with primary invasive breast carcinoma with lymph node involvement. She underwent curative surgery and is now scheduled to receive TAC (Taxotere, Adriamycin, cyclophosphamide) chemotherapy. She has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is currently taking medications for hypertension which is well-controlled. Her cardiovascular function is normal and her renal function is within normal limits. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any hematologic disorders. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to prevent neutropenia after using G-CSF with TAC chemotherapy.

A 32-year-old woman with a clinical diagnosis of asthma has been experiencing frequent asthma symptoms such as cough, wheeze, and breathlessness. She is currently on regular inhaled medication but has had to use oral steroids in the past 12 months and has had more than six short-acting beta-agonist inhalers in the past six months. She has had to visit the A+E department for asthma in the past year, which has caused a significant interference with her daily life. She is able to use the internet and has access to mobile technology. The patient speaks English and is willing to be contacted via phone, text, and email. She is not planning to travel abroad for prolonged periods during the trial period. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to give written informed consent. She does not have any medical conditions that can present with asthma-like symptoms, such as COPD, heart failure, or lung cancer. She is not on long-term oral steroids or theophylline, and she does not have a history of ITU admission for asthma. The patient is not currently using a self-management app.

This is a 52-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with chest pain, shortness of breath, and diaphoresis. He reports that his symptoms started approximately 18 hours ago at rest and have been ongoing since then. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. Upon arrival, he was found to have ST-elevation on his electrocardiogram and was immediately taken to the catheterization lab. Coronary angiography revealed a large thrombus within the left anterior descending artery. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the study and provided informed consent for participation. He did not have any contraindications for heparin, aspirin or thienopyridines nor did he have any contraindications for cardiac magnetic resonance examination. He was randomized to the thrombus aspiration group and underwent the procedure successfully. He will be followed up regularly for the next year to assess his outcomes.

6-year-old male patient with a history of congenital heart disease and a scheduled cardiac surgery is being evaluated for participation in a clinical trial. The patient has a weight of 25 kg and has no other significant medical history. The patient is currently stable with no evidence of sepsis or hepatic dysfunction during the hospital course. Parental consent has been obtained for participation in the study.

The patient is a 44-year-old man who has been diagnosed with epilepsy and has been suffering from partial onset seizures. He has been on medication for the past 2 years, and his seizures have been under control. His medical history includes a concussion from a car accident about 5 years ago. He currently takes a daily dose of 1500 mg of levetiracetam. He has experienced some mild side effects such as drowsiness and difficulty concentrating, but they have not been severe enough to affect his daily activities. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is interested in participating in this study to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of levetiracetam in controlling his seizures. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and follow-up visits. He is not currently pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue for the past few months. He also complains of chest pain and palpitations when he exerts himself. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin respectively. He does not smoke, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has never had any cardiac surgeries in the past. His family history is positive for heart disease, with his father having had a heart attack in his 50s. He has been diagnosed with mitral regurgitation and his doctor has recommended mitral valve repair. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent for the collection of his clinical data. He does not have any known sensitivity to nickel or chromium.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 10 years ago. He has a history of poor glycemic control, and his current HbA1c is 9.5%. He has developed a foot ulcer under the metatarsal heads of his left foot, which has not healed despite several weeks of conventional wound care. The ulcer is small in size, and there is no evidence of infection or ischemia. The patient reports some discomfort and difficulty walking due to the ulcer. He has no previous history of Charcot foot or foot deformities that necessitate custom-made shoes. He speaks and reads Swedish fluently, and he has appropriate social support. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of a sealed therapeutic shoe versus a total contact cast for the treatment of his diabetic foot ulcer. He is willing to wear the shoe day and night and attend regular follow-up appointments with a cast technician and physiotherapist.

The patient is a 60-year-old man scheduled for an elective laparotomy due to a suspected colonic tumor. He has no known allergies and no significant medical history. His BMI is 25. He is currently taking medication for high blood pressure which is well-controlled. The patient has been informed of the study and has given his consent to participate. The patient is randomized into one of two groups, the CI-Sugammadex group or the IB-Neostigmine group. The patient will receive epidural analgesia before induction of general anesthesia. The anesthesiologist will monitor the patient's vital signs and maintain the central core temperature above 35°C throughout the surgery. After the surgery, the patient will be monitored in the PACU for at least 60 minutes and will be followed up for 24 hours. All adverse events and serious adverse events will be documented.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pain in her left hip for the past year. She has a history of osteoarthritis and avascular necrosis. She underwent physical therapy, cortisone injections, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but the pain has not subsided. The patient was evaluated by an orthopedic surgeon and was recommended to undergo total hip arthroplasty (THA) with a ceramic-on-ceramic acetabular cup. The patient is in good health and has no known allergies to metal. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the study requirements. The patient is willing to comply with the rehabilitation program and follow-up visits prescribed by the study protocol.

A 62-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes for 15 years presents with complaints of burning and tingling pain in both his feet. He describes the pain as a constant burning sensation that sometimes feels like pins and needles. The pain is worse at night and disrupts his sleep. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not provided relief. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity. He is a non-smoker and rarely drinks alcohol. The physical examination reveals decreased sensation to light touch and vibration in both feet. The patient's blood glucose level is well-controlled with oral medications. The patient was previously enrolled in the double-blind phase of a clinical trial for diabetic peripheral neuropathy and received pregabalin during the first 3 weeks of the study. He did not experience any serious adverse events related to the study medication. The patient is now interested in participating in the long-term open-label extension study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of pregabalin for his neuropathic pain.

A 45-year-old male with a known history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) presents with occasional chest discomfort and palpitations. He has a family history of sudden cardiac death and has been previously evaluated for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD), but was deemed not to meet criteria. He is currently on beta-blocker therapy and has had an echocardiogram showing left ventricular hypertrophy with a maximum wall thickness of 20 mm. He is scheduled for routine ambulatory monitoring for risk stratification and has agreed to participate in the study. He is followed at the Chanin T. Mast HCM Center at Morristown Medical Center and has no history of persistent/permanent atrial fibrillation (AF). He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He leads an active lifestyle and enjoys hiking and playing tennis.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with HIV. He has no history of antiretroviral therapy and is otherwise healthy. His CD4 T cell count is 400 cells/mm³, and his plasma viral load is 150,000 copies/mL. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of raltegravir in reducing HIV replication in lymphatic tissues. He is not currently taking any medication and has no known allergies. He is mentally stable and understands the protocol requirements. He is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant. He is willing to undergo surgical and endoscopic procedures as required by the study protocol.

A 67-year-old woman has been experiencing moderate-to-severe pain in her right knee for the past year, which has not been relieved by her current analgesic therapy. She has a history of osteoarthritis of the knee, and her knee joint X-ray shows a K-L score of 3. She has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and is generally in good health. She has not had any intra-articular injections of hyaluronic acid in the past 90 days or systemic corticosteroids in the past 30 days. She does not have any significant concomitant illness that would adversely affect her participation in the study. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of REGN5069 for pain due to osteoarthritis of the knee.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was admitted to the emergency department with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech. A CT scan showed evidence of acute ischemic stroke involving the right middle cerebral artery territory. She is currently within the 24-hour window period for thrombolytic therapy and is eligible for treatment with BIII 890 as part of this clinical trial. She has no history of seizures, dementia, or other neurological diseases. Her blood glucose level is within normal limits. She has no history of orthostatic hypotension or fainting spells. She is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the informed consent form. She has no other medical conditions that would interfere with the trial or pose an additional risk.

A 45-year-old male who suffered a stroke 6 months ago resulting in left-sided weakness and foot drop. He has been attending the Leeds FES Service follow-up clinics for the past 4 months and uses a single-channel Odstock Medical ODFS functional electrical stimulator. He reports difficulty lifting his left foot while walking and has experienced trips and falls in the past due to foot drop. He walks with the assistance of a cane and can walk up to 10 meters without stopping. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the procedures involved. He has no other significant medical history, is not currently taking any medications, and does not use any other assistive devices for walking.

The patient is a 55 year-old male who was admitted to the hospital due to respiratory distress. He was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation due to a diagnosis of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently under control with medication. He has no known drug allergies and has not experienced any seizures. His renal function is within normal limits with a creatinine clearance of 90 mL/min. He has no evidence of shock or third degree burns. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits.

A 10-year-old boy with a history of congenital heart disease is scheduled for a tonsillectomy due to recurrent tonsillitis. He underwent open-heart surgery to correct a ventricular septal defect and atrial septal defect when he was 6 months old. He has since been followed by a pediatric cardiologist and is currently on medication for mild pulmonary hypertension. His last echocardiogram was done 6 months ago and showed mild right ventricular enlargement but no significant valvular dysfunction. He has no other medical problems and is otherwise healthy. His parents are concerned about the risk of anesthesia and surgery due to his heart condition and would like to participate in a study that can help them make informed decisions about his care.

Maria is a 58 year old female who has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 20 years. She has been experiencing decreased vision in her left eye and has been diagnosed with high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy in that eye. Her best corrected visual acuity in her left eye is currently 20/400. She has no history of prior scatter or focal/grid photocoagulation in the past 6 months. She has no fibrovascular proliferation with retinal traction or any other cause of retinal neovascularization. Her HbA1C is 9.2%. She has no significant systemic diseases or history of malignancy. She is not pregnant or nursing and is postmenopausal for more than 12 months. She has no known allergies to fluorescein or components of Lucentis® formulation. Her systolic blood pressure is 150 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure is 90 mmHg. She is willing to provide written informed consent and to return for all trial visits.

Patient is a 32yo man who has been diagnosed with HIV and has a CD4 count of 450 cells/ul. He is a MSM and was recently treated for high-grade anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN) using cryotherapy. The treatment was successful and the lesions are in remission. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent recurrence of high-grade AIN. The study involves vaccination with the quadrivalent HPV vaccine (Gardasil) or placebo vaccination at months 0, 2 and 6. The patient will undergo screening for AIN by high-resolution anoscopy (HRA) at inclusion (first vaccination) and at last vaccination (6 months), and repeated at 6 and 12 months after the last vaccination. The primary end point will be the cumulative recurrence of HG AIN at 12 months after the last vaccination, as assessed by HRA, with biopsies taken of suspect lesions. The patient is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of being an HIV-positive MSM with a CD4 count > 350 cells/ul and intra-anal high-grade AIN that was successfully treated in the past year with conventional cauterization, cryotherapy, or other forms of local treatment. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria such as immunosuppressive medication, allergy against the constituent of Gardasil vaccine or peri-anal AIN2 or 3. The patient will be required to undergo two extra HRAs and will receive 3 vaccinations with the quadrivalent vaccine Gardasil or placebo. The study aims to evaluate the efficacy of qHPV vaccination in preventing recurrence of high-grade AIN in HIV+ MSM with CD4 counts >350 x 10E6/l who were successfully treated for high-grade intra-anal AIN in the past year.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has undergone lumbar discectomy 2 years ago due to a herniated disk. She is now scheduled to undergo a cervical laminectomy to relieve neck pain that radiates to her left arm. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medication except for a daily multivitamin. She has no history of blood clots or bleeding disorders, and her pre-operative coagulation parameters are normal. She is willing to participate in this observational study to assess the effect of possible exposure to THROMBIN-JMI® on her coagulation parameters. She understands that she may or may not be exposed to THROMBIN-JMI® during her upcoming surgery, and that her coagulation parameters will be monitored at 48 hours post-surgery. She has no sensitivity to bovine thrombin and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is available for follow-up visits at 48 hours, 4 weeks, and 8 weeks post-surgery.

Patient is a 60-year-old male from the United States who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. He has not received any prior treatment for prostate cancer and is currently scheduled to receive ADT treatment as a standard of care for more than 6 months in combination with radiotherapy or oral AR-targeted systemic treatment as prescribed by his treating physician. His performance status is 1 and he has no other active secondary malignancy that requires systemic therapy. He has a BMI of 28 and does not have any contraindications for treatment with ADT. He has a history of mild depression but is not currently pharmacologically treated for it. He does not have any diagnosed condition that causes known sleep disturbance but has reported occasional nocturia at night. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent according to ICH/GCP regulations.

Preterm infant born at 27 weeks gestation weighing 840 grams, admitted to the NICU due to respiratory distress and requiring mechanical ventilation. The infant has no known major malformations and is stable on a TPN regimen for nutritional support. The parents have provided consent for their infant to participate in the randomized intervention study to determine the role of fatty acids in serum and breast milk in preventing Retinopathy of Prematurity. The infant will be closely monitored for the development of ROP and other neonatal morbidities.

52-year-old male with a history of uncontrolled type 2 diabetes diagnosed 5 years ago, is currently on a diet and exercise therapy. He is 5'9'' and weighs 195 pounds, which puts his BMI at 28.8 kg/m2. He has no other significant medical history, and he is not currently taking any anti-diabetic agents. His fasting plasma glucose values range from 180 to 240 mg/dL at screening, after wash-out and placebo run-in. He has not experienced any episodes of severe hypoglycemia within the last 6 months and is not diagnosed with hypoglycemia unawareness. He has not undergone any bariatric surgical procedures in the past. He has not had any significant weight changes in the past 3 months. He has no history of proliferative retinopathy or maculopathy or severe neuropathy. He is willing to use barrier contraception and is not planning to conceive during the trial. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the initial anti-diabetic activity of MLR-1023.

A 55-year-old man presents with a history of Type II diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been relatively compliant with his medication regimen and his last HbA1c level was 9.5%. He noticed a small wound on his left foot about 3 weeks ago, which has now grown in size and has not healed despite his attempts at home care. He also reports numbness and tingling in his feet for the past 2 years. Upon examination, a diabetic foot ulcer is noted on the plantar aspect of his left foot measuring approximately 2cm x 2cm. The wound is full thickness with no exposed ligament, tendon, joint capsule or bone. The patient has an Ankle Branchial Index (ABI) of 0.90 and a bi-phasic Doppler flow pattern. He is able to tolerate and comply with the off-loading method using a Removable Cast Walker (RCW) provided in the study. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 62-year-old woman experienced shoulder pain and limited range of motion for several months. She initially tried physical therapy, but her symptoms persisted. Imaging studies showed a massive rotator cuff tear in her left shoulder. After discussing her options with her orthopedic surgeon, she has elected to undergo reverse shoulder arthroplasty (RSA). She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is fluent in English and has no impairments that would prevent her from answering surveys. She has signed the informed consent and Protected Health Information (PHI) form. She meets the inclusion criteria for this study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who recently experienced a failing tooth in the maxillary arch (between teeth 15-25) and has been advised to undergo implant placement therapy. She has adjacent and opposing natural teeth and sufficient mesial-distal and inter-occlusal space for the implant and definitive restoration. The patient had an intact socket wall prior to extraction and there is sufficient apical bone to place an immediate implant with minimum primary stability of 30 N/cm. She does not have periodontal disease but is a heavy smoker, smoking more than 10 cigarettes per day. The patient has no medical or general contraindications for the surgical procedure and there is no active infection at the implant site. She has agreed to participate

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who gave birth to a premature baby boy at 31 weeks gestation. The baby was born with a birth weight of 1.7 kg and is currently receiving care in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The baby is on enteral feeding and is being monitored closely for any signs of digestive complications. The mother has no significant medical history and is currently breastfeeding the baby. The parents have given informed consent for the baby to participate in the study. The study will involve collecting a stool sample from the baby's diaper once a week, from birth until discharge from the hospital, and every day during any gastrointestinal events (interruption of enteral feeding over 48 hours). The study will evaluate the performance of the rapid assay of fecal calprotectin by quantitative immunochromatography compared to the reference method by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The aim of the study is to evaluate a clinico-biological predictive score, associating the faecal calprotectin, for the diagnosis of enterocolitis and enteropathy of the preterm neonates.

45F with a history of chronic low back pain for over 1 year. She has tried multiple treatments including physical therapy, chiropractic care, and pain medications without significant relief. She reports that her pain is worse with prolonged sitting and standing and has limited her ability to perform daily activities such as household chores and work.
