She denies any numbness or tingling in her legs or feet. She currently sees a pain specialist who has recommended her for participation in this clinical trial. She is fluent in French and has regular access to a computer and the internet. She has not received any previous treatment with the didactic tools being investigated in this study and is not currently undergoing any other educational or cognitive-behavioral treatments for her back pain. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating.

As this is a clinical trial for healthcare workers, a patient description is not applicable. However, eligible participants for this trial are employees of CHUV (University Hospital of Lausanne) or PMU (University Policlinic of Lausanne) who work regularly in contact with patients and must do the recruitment visit at the occupational medicine unit of the CHUV. They must be 18 years or older with no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has no history of other cancers, but has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother and aunt both being diagnosed in their 50s. She has good performance status and preserved organ function. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for breast cancer, but had a lumpectomy and radiation therapy for early-stage breast cancer five years ago. She has no active brain metastasis. She is not currently on any other concurrent therapy.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has had a history of premature ejaculation for the past 2 years. He reports that he experiences ejaculation within 1-2 minutes of penetration, which has caused significant distress and dissatisfaction in his sexual life. He has no history of cardiovascular disorders, implanted pacemaker/defibrillator, hypertension, or diabetes mellitus. He does not have any local dermatological disease, local skin irritation/lesions, neurological disorder, or psychiatric disease, nor has he taken any psychiatric medications. He is familiar with self-stimulation and is able to follow study instructions and complete study assessment tools. He has agreed to undergo a washout period of two weeks prior to the study. The patient is in good general health and is eager to participate in the study to potentially prolong his ejaculatory latency time and improve the quality of his sexual life.

As this is a pilot study for military pilots, there are no specific patient descriptions required. However, eligible participants for this study would be pilots or cadets with flight experience and candidates for pilots without flight experience who are healthy and aged between 18 and 30 years old. They should not have any cardiovascular disorders and should not have consumed alcohol within 24 hours prior to the study. They should provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

45-year-old female with chronic low back pain and radiculopathy. Previous treatments include physical therapy, chiropractic care, and multiple epidural steroid injections. Currently on gabapentin for pain management. No history of coagulopathy, systemic infection, or allergies to contrast dye. Able to provide informed consent in English. Referred by treating physician for bilateral transforaminal epidural injections.

The patient is a 56 year-old female with a history of hypertension and elevated cholesterol levels. She is currently taking medication to manage her blood pressure and cholesterol. She is interested in improving her diet to reduce her risk of cardiovascular disease. She is of Nordic descent and regularly consumes traditional Nordic foods, including berries, grains, and fatty fish. However, she is uncertain if her current diet is adequate to improve her cardiometabolic risk factors. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the association between the Nordic Diet and cardiovascular outcomes. She is willing to adhere to the dietary intervention and attend all study visits required for the trial.

The patient is a 10-month-old infant who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. The infant has been diagnosed with asthma by a pediatrician and is currently receiving rescue inhaler therapy as needed. The infant has been eating solid foods for over a month and is in good overall health. The infant has had at least three episodes of asthma or asthma-like symptoms, with one episode occurring within the past six months of the Prestudy Visit. The infant is in need of controller therapy according to the criteria established in the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) guidelines. The infant has not been hospitalized or visited the emergency room due to asthma within the past two weeks.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been a Vitality member for the past 2 years. She works a desk job and finds it difficult to maintain an active lifestyle due to her sedentary work schedule. She has a history of high blood pressure and is motivated to improve her health by increasing her physical activity. She currently engages in light physical activity such as walking and yoga but has not been able to meet her weekly physical activity goals. She is interested in participating in a study that can help her achieve her goals and improve her overall health. The patient is generally healthy and has no known medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is compliant with her medications and is willing to follow the study protocol.

A 45-year-old man with a family history of colorectal cancer presented to his primary care physician for a routine colonoscopy screening. He has no history of bowel resection, inflammatory bowel disease, polyposis syndrome, or poor taste perception. The patient is concerned about the bowel preparation process due to previous experiences with unpleasant taste and texture of the laxative. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve the tolerability of bowel preparation for colonoscopy. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history, and takes no regular medications. He works as an IT specialist and enjoys playing basketball and hiking in his free time. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His BMI is within normal range, and he has no known food allergies.

A 65-year-old male patient was referred to the cardiology department with a history of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction 2 years ago, which was treated with angioplasty and stenting of the left anterior descending artery (LAD). He is currently on a daily dose of aspirin, metoprolol, and atorvastatin. The patient reports progressive exertional dyspnea and chest pain in the last 3 months. On physical examination, the patient is alert, oriented, and in no acute distress. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is 80 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air. Cardiac auscultation reveals a regular rhythm with a grade III/VI systolic murmur at the apex. Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly with clear lung fields. ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy and left bundle branch block. Echocardiography reveals severe mitral regurgitation, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, and an ejection fraction of 35%. The patient is scheduled to undergo cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass for mitral valve replacement and tricuspid annuloplasty.

Patient is a 57-year-old man from the United States who was diagnosed with acral lentiginous melanoma which has metastasized to his liver and lungs. He has a history of hypertension that is well controlled with medication. He has no known cardiac or renal issues. His performance status is 1, and he is able to carry out light activities such as walking around the house or office. His lab values are within normal limits. The patient has no history of brain metastases or spinal cord compression. He has not undergone any major surgery or radiation therapy in the past 4 weeks. The patient has no known HIV infection or chronic liver disease. He has not been treated with any antiangiogenic agents in the past. The patient has a measurable site of disease which is greater than 1 cm in greatest dimension. Tumor blocks or slides are available of the patient's primary or metastatic tumor site for c-kit mutation testing. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

A 45-year old immigrant from a high tuberculosis prevalence country presented to the clinic with a cough that has been present for over a month. He also complains of night sweats and loss of appetite. He denies any chest pain or hemoptysis. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He lives with his wife and two children. The patient works as a construction worker and has no previous history of tuberculosis. He doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. He speaks limited English and needs a translator for communication. The patient is concerned about his symptoms and is willing to participate in the study to help with the development of a more accurate diagnostic test for tuberculosis.

A 58-year old retired teacher was diagnosed with multiple myeloma two years ago. She underwent chemotherapy and stem cell transplant but experienced relapse six months ago. She has been experiencing bone pain and fatigue. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and osteoporosis. She lives with her husband and they have two adult children. The patient complains of difficulty walking and has experienced two falls in the past month. Her laboratory tests show elevated beta-2 microglobulin and monoclonal protein in her blood. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her relapsed multiple myeloma. Her doctor has recommended isatuximab and she has agreed to participate in the clinical trial. She is willing to complete the study-related questionnaires and has given signed informed consent prior to study start. The patient is able to understand and communicate well in English.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy. She has been experiencing shortness of breath during physical activity and occasional chest pain for the past few months. She has been on antihypertensive medication for several years, but her blood pressure remains elevated. She has no history of heart failure, ischemic heart disease, valvular heart disease, arrhythmias, peripheral vascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, neurologic disorders, diabetes mellitus, or renal dysfunction. She is otherwise in good health and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effect of Valsartan on left ventricular myocardial functions in hypertensive patients with left ventricular hypertrophy.

A 58-year-old male patient with a history of stable angina presents with recurrent chest pain for the past week. The patient had a previous cardiac catheterization procedure that revealed significant stenosis in his left anterior descending artery (LAD). The patient is currently on aspirin and a beta-blocker medication. The patient is a non-smoker with a BMI of 26. The patient has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. The patient is able to understand the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the new paclitaxel-eluting CoroflexTM Please stent in percutaneous coronary intervention. The patient does not have significant left main stem stenosis, bifurcating disease, or in-stent restenosis.

A 55-year-old male presented with gross hematuria and flank pain. He underwent a CT scan that showed a 3.5 cm mass in the upper pole of his left kidney. A biopsy was consistent with high-grade urothelial carcinoma. He underwent a radical nephroureterectomy and was found to have pT3N0M0 disease. Postoperative imaging was negative for distant metastases. His ECOG performance status is 1. He was referred to the urologist for follow-up and surveillance. During his first cystoscopic examination, he was found to have a 1.5 cm bladder tumor at the bladder neck that was treated with transurethral resection. The pathology report confirmed the diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MZL) two years ago. She received six cycles of chemotherapy with rituximab and bendamustine, followed by radiation therapy. However, her disease has relapsed and progressed despite these treatments. She currently complains of enlarged lymph nodes in her neck, armpits, and groin, and has experienced unexplained weight loss. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 1, and she has no significant medical history. Her renal and hepatic function tests are within normal limit, and bone marrow biopsy shows adequate reserves. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 30 days and is willing to participate in this study. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she agrees to use adequate contraception during the study period.

22-year-old male with a history of first episode psychosis, has been referred to OnTrack New York for treatment. The patient is fluent in English, is willing to participate in a study, understands the requirements of the study and has given informed consent. The patient has not experienced any recent episodes of self-harm, suicidal thoughts or behavior, and is considered clinically stable by his treating physician. The patient is interested in technology and has a history of playing video games, making him a potentially good candidate for the OnTrack>The Game study.

Pt is a 30yo M without significant medical history, presenting for participation in a clinical trial comparing the absorption of tiotropium from four test inhalation products and two reference inhalation products. Pt is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. Pt is willing and able to provide informed consent and will agree to use adequate contraception throughout the study. Pt is willing to withhold all alcoholic beverages for 48 hours and all xanthine-containing foods and beverages for 24 hours prior to reporting to the clinic. Pt does not have any clinically significant allergies or adverse reactions to study drugs. Pt has not received any prescription medications within four weeks or investigational medications within 12 weeks of study enrollment. Pt has not received any non-prescription medications within 14 days prior to dosing, except for paracetamol use within two days.

The patient is a 40-year-old man diagnosed with AIDS and has been taking zidovudine (AZT) for the past six months. However, the patient's condition has deteriorated, and he is experiencing complications associated with AIDS despite being on AZT. The patient is not eligible to participate in Phase II ddI programs due to geographic restrictions and exclusion criteria. The patient is willing to participate in an open-label study regimen to receive didanosine (ddI). The patient is not currently taking any medication other than AZT to manage his condition. The patient has provided informed consent and is available for monthly follow-up while taking ddI. The patient has undergone laboratory tests within 14 days prior to initial drug dosing, and the results meet the required baseline values. The patient does not have acute pancreatitis, poorly controlled seizure disorder, or grade B or greater peripheral neuropathy. The patient has not received therapy in the preceding 15 days with any other antiretroviral except AZT.

The patient is a 30 year old woman who has been experiencing chronic pelvic pain for the past 6 months. She describes the pain as a constant dull ache in the lower abdomen and pelvis, which worsens during menstruation. She has not sought any treatment for the pain yet. She reports occasional headaches and jaw pain, especially after prolonged talking or chewing. She has not been diagnosed with any temporomandibular joint disorder. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not taking any hormonal therapy or regular medication. She has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 22 kg/m2 and does not have any bone disease or previous vertebral fractures. She has not been diagnosed with any major spinal or jaw abnormality and is not using any orthotics or prosthetics. She is interested in participating in the study to understand the potential relationship between chronic pelvic pain and lumbopelvic alignment and temporomandibular joint kinematics.

45-year-old female with a history of papillary thyroid cancer confirmed by biopsy and being followed with active surveillance at MSKCC. The index nodule is less than or equal to 2 cm in maximum dimension, and thyroid and neck ultrasound have been performed and interpreted by a MSKCC radiologist within the past 6 months. No prior history of thyroid surgery or radiation therapy. The patient is currently asymptomatic and has no significant medical history.

47yo female with a previous diagnosis of high grade serous ovarian cancer, who underwent surgical resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. Despite a good initial response, she had a recurrence within 6 months of completing her treatment, with the development of malignant ascites and pleural effusion. She was started on a second-line chemotherapy regimen with gemcitabine and carboplatin, but after 3 cycles, the disease progressed again. She was then tested for BRCA mutation and found to be positive. She has no other significant medical history and has a performance status of 1.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy followed by radiation therapy. She was subsequently started on aromatase inhibitor therapy (letrozole) due to estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. Unfortunately, her cancer has recently progressed despite this therapy. She now presents with recurrent breast cancer with metastasis to the lungs, liver and bones. She has no significant past medical history and has never smoked. She is currently on a daily dose of letrozole. Her ECOG performance status is 1, with no other significant symptoms. Her blood work reveals a normal complete blood count and chemistries, including liver and kidney function tests. She has no known allergies to any of the study medications. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment.

A 9-month-old female infant diagnosed with microcephaly associated with Zika virus Syndrome. She was born at term without complications, but her mother reported having a rash during pregnancy. The child was diagnosed with microcephaly at birth due to a head circumference of 31 cm. The patient is currently being assisted by a neurologist and is undergoing physical therapy once a week. She has been experiencing seizures and reflux and is taking anticonvulsant and antireflux medication. The infant has no osteomioarticular disorders and has not been previously exposed to the aquatic environment. The mother is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided consent for her child to be part of the study.

42-year-old male with a BMI of 34 who recently underwent a full night polysmnographic sleep study for suspected sleep apnea. The results indicated moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea with an AHI of 38 events/hr. During the evaluation, the echocardiography revealed the presence of pulmonary hypertension with a mPAP of 45 mmHg. The patient has no history of chronic pulmonary disease, left ventricular heart disease or chronic thromboembolic disorders. The patient has not been on long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT), and there is no evidence of respiratory neuromuscular weakness or chest wall deformities. The patient has no history of end-organ failure or malignancies. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to comply with the CPAP therapy with an average cumulative adherence of at least 4 hours per day for more than 70% of nights.

A 68-year-old woman presents with a history of atrial fibrillation and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3. She has never been treated with Apixaban or Warfarin and is a candidate for oral anticoagulation as assessed by her treating physician. She has no history of valvular atrial fibrillation, active bleeding or recent stroke within the last 7 days. She has no history of dementia, implanted devices not compatible with MRI, claustrophobia, active alcohol/drug abuse, or life expectancy less than 1 year. She is not currently taking aspirin with >100mg doses, and has no known hypersensitivity to warfarin or Apixaban. Her renal function is normal, and she has no prior history of severe bleeding, intracranial bleeding, GI bleed requiring transfusion, or bleeding from other sites requiring transfusion. She is mentally competent and has no psychosocial reasons that make study participation impractical. She is not currently enrolled in another IND or IDE trial that has not completed the primary endpoint or that clinically interferes with the current study endpoints. She has no co-morbid conditions that could limit her ability to participate in the trial or to comply with follow-up requirements, or that could impact the scientific integrity of the study. She is not a prisoner or involuntarily incarcerated, nor is she compulsorily detained for treatment of either psychiatric or physical illness. She is not currently on any systemic treatment with strong dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-gp, nor does she require dual anti-platelet therapy with aspirin and another agent such as thienopyridine.

Patient is a 32-year-old woman from the United States who has been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She has a past medical history of asthma, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of anxiety or depression. She and her partner have no known fertility issues. She has undergone preliminary testing and has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility. She has opted to undergo IVF treatment and is currently in the process of her first cycle. She is interested in participating in a study that investigates the relationship between stress levels and IVF outcomes.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old woman with Fitzpatrick skin type II who has not been pregnant or lactating in the past year. She is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications, nor is she using any topical medications on her skin. She has no history of skin cancer, severe photodamage, or any major illnesses within the past 30 days. Additionally, she has not participated in any previous patch test studies or been exposed to any ultraviolet radiation in the past 4 weeks. The patient is willing to comply with study instructions and is capable of understanding and providing written informed consent.

5-year-old male with cerebral palsy who is scheduled to receive botulinum toxin injection for spasticity management. The patient has a history of developmental delay, with difficulty walking and fine motor skills. He is classified as ASA physical status 2. The patient is not overweight and does not have any history of heart disease or difficult airway. He has not had any recent upper respiratory tract infections or gastroesophageal reflux. The patient has not reported any allergies to medications used during the procedure.

The patient is a 53-year-old man who was admitted to the ICU of St. Antonius Hospital after suffering a severe stroke that left him unable to communicate verbally. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. He is married with two adult children and works as a computer programmer. His wife reports that he has been experiencing occasional headaches and neck pain for several months prior to the stroke. He is currently intubated and sedated for airway protection and is receiving intravenous pain medication as needed. His vital signs are stable, and he is being monitored closely for any signs of neurological deterioration. The patient's wife is very involved in his care and is eager to participate in any pain management interventions that may help to improve his comfort and overall outcome.

The patient is a 67-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has undergone bilateral orchiectomy and has been on leuprolide therapy. He has been receiving treatment with docetaxel for his metastatic prostate cancer for 6 months but has not shown any improvement. He has new/enlarging lesions on his CT scan and his PSA level is 30 ng/mL. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medication. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. His serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase (ALT), bilirubin, creatinine, and platelet count are all within normal limits. He has no history of heart disease, angina, or myocardial infarction. He also has no history of carcinomatous meningitis or brain metastases. He has no serious concurrent medical illness or active infection. He has not undergone any major surgery within the past 21 days. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given his written informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been admitted to the intensive care unit for more than two calendar days due to severe pneumonia. She has required intensive care unit level support with non-invasive ventilation for a cumulative duration of 6 hours. She has no history of active malignancy, metabolic bone disease, or hypoparathyroidism. She is not pregnant and has an estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate of 60 ml/min. She is not currently receiving renal replacement therapy, and her platelet count is 250 10^9/L. Her international normalized ratio is 1.2. She is not currently taking any anti-fracture agents, and her Bone Mineral Density T-score is -2.2. She weighs 75 kg and is able to undergo Bone Mineral Density testing. She does not have poor dentition or oral hygiene, dental infection, or any known contraindication to denosumab or zoledronic acid. She is interested in participating in the Bone Zone trial to prevent bone loss during and after her critical illness.

A 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Type I Gaucher disease and no prior enzyme replacement therapy, gene therapy or bone marrow transplantation. He experiences recurrent bone crises and has a history of pathological fractures related to Gaucher disease. He also has lytic lesions and medullary infarctions as documented in his medical history. His bone density by DEXA is ≥ 1.5 standard deviation (SD) below age-adjusted normal value. He is ambulatory and has not undergone joint replacement surgery. He has no major concurrent disorders or known disorders that affect bone, and he is not taking any medications that affect bone homeostasis. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent and comply with the requirements of the study.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather undergraduate physiotherapy students who will be participating in a manual skills training session. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this study.

As an observational study, this clinical trial does not require a specific patient description. However, potential participants could include individuals who have suffered from mountain accidents in Austria, including but not limited to those involving lightning, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, frostbite injuries, and accidents with flying vehicles. The study aims to analyze the characteristics of these accidents and provide medical information on the patient's condition and outcome. The study does not have any specific exclusion criteria, but only individuals who have suffered injury and required medical attention are eligible for inclusion.

32-year-old male who has been wearing soft daily wear contact lenses for the past two years. He has a stable refractive error with a cylindrical power of -1.50 DC in both eyes. He reports wearing contact lenses for 5 days a week and 8 hours a day. He has no history of any eye diseases, ocular surgeries or injuries, and does not use any systemic or ocular medications. Best corrected distance visual acuity in each eye is 20/20 and he is willing to not use rewetting/lubricating drops during the study. He has no known allergies to silicone hydrogel materials.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was diagnosed with chronic phase myelofibrosis six months ago. He presents with a history of fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and early satiety. He has a history of hypertension, and he quit smoking 10 years ago, but he currently drinks alcohol occasionally. He takes amlodipine for his hypertension. On physical examination, his spleen is palpable 8 cm below the left costal margin. His laboratory findings show a hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL, a leukocyte count of 14,000/mm³ with 10% blasts, and a platelet count of 80,000/mm³. A bone marrow biopsy was performed and revealed an IDH2 mutation. He was started on ruxolitinib 20mg twice daily four months ago, but his splenomegaly has persisted, and his hemoglobin level has decreased. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his condition.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing painful symptoms in her lower limbs for the past 3 months. She reports a sensation of heaviness and discomfort in her legs that worsens throughout the day and is relieved by elevating her legs. She also experiences a burning and itching sensation, as well as cramps at night. The patient has no history of deep venous reflux or thrombo-embolic diseases, but has been diagnosed with C1s venous disease grade in her lower limbs. She is not currently taking any venotonic treatments or vascular protectants and has not taken any analgesic or anti-inflammatory treatments within the last 7 days. She does not have any known hypersensitivity to diosmin or its excipients. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of diosmin 600mg versus placebo on her painful symptomatology.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who needs to undergo surgery for a gallbladder removal. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He has no known allergies or neuromuscular disorders. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the last 30 days. He is not pregnant nor breast-feeding. He has given written informed consent to participate in the trial. The participant is classified as ASA class 2, with mild systemic disease, but his hypertension is stable and well-controlled. The anticipated duration of anesthesia for the surgery is more than 120 minutes.

Patient is a 25-year-old male who was treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital 12 years ago. He is experiencing difficulty falling asleep at night and has been diagnosed with neurocognitive impairment, specifically in the areas of memory and executive functioning. The patient has a full scale intelligence quotient (FSIQ) score of 75, which is below the inclusion criteria of the study. He is fluent in English and has no known allergies to melatonin or any of its ingredients. He is not currently taking melatonin or any medication that would interfere with the study. The patient has no history of sleep apnea or other sleep disorders, diabetes mellitus, or uncontrolled seizure disorder in the past 12 months. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and no major psychiatric illness. The patient is not employed in a position that requires night work. He is not currently pregnant or lactating/nursing. The patient has no history of a neurologic event unrelated to cancer or its treatment and has no sensory impairments. Overall, the patient meets the inclusion criteria for Cohort 2 and is eligible to participate in the study.

A 56-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) 3 months ago is being referred to Thomas Jefferson University (TJU) Blood and Marrow Transplantation Program for further treatment. The patient has already undergone front-line therapy with chemotherapy, but the prognosis is not promising. The patient's performance status is good, with a Karnofsky score of 90%. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction with an ejection fraction (EF) of 55%. The patient has no history of liver or kidney disease. The patient's hematologic profile shows anemia and thrombocytopenia. The patient's blood type is A+. A donor, who is a relative and has a 4 antigen match at the HLA-A; B; C; DR loci, is available for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial of a reduced intensity regimen that is given in two steps. The patient meets all eligibility criteria, including having a performance status of >80% (TJU Karnofsky) and an HCT-CI Score of <4 points. The patient is willing to use contraception if needed and is able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been experiencing visual disturbances in his right eye for the past few weeks. He reports blurred vision, distortion, and difficulty reading. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no history of diabetes. On examination, his visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye. The anterior segment examination is unremarkable. Dilated fundus examination of the right eye reveals a subretinal hemorrhage and fluid accumulation in the macular area. The left eye examination is normal. His fluorescein angiography confirms the diagnosis of exudative ARMD, and he is referred to a retinal specialist for further evaluation and treatment. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the sensitivity and specificity of the Heidelberg retinal tomograph (HRT) for the presence of macular edema in exudative ARMD patients. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any exclusion criteria.

A 72-year-old woman presents with a history of hypertension. She is currently taking Lisinopril 10 mg once daily for hypertension control. She reports exercising regularly on land for at least 3 days a week, but she has not tried any water-based exercises before. She has no other chronic diseases or conditions and is a non-smoker. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2. She is interested in participating in a study to assess the immediate ambulatory blood pressure response to water exercise.

52-year-old female with a history of dry eye syndrome for the past 6 months. The patient reports a persistent sensation of grittiness and dryness in both eyes, particularly in the morning and after prolonged reading or computer work. She has tried over-the-counter artificial tears without significant relief of symptoms. She has no history of ocular infections or inflammation, drug toxicity, contact lens wear, ocular allergy, or ocular surgery within the last 3 months. Her medical history includes well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is not currently taking any medications that may affect ocular surface or tear film. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the expression of chemokines in dry eye syndrome to help advance the understanding and treatment of this condition.

The patient is a 52 year old male with a history of metastatic malignant solid tumor. The cancer has already spread to the liver, lungs, and bones. The patient has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiotherapy but the cancer has progressed despite the treatment. He is experiencing significant pain and fatigue due to the cancer and its treatment. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2. His white blood cell count is within normal range but platelet count is low. His serum bilirubin and creatinine levels are within normal limits but his alkaline phosphatase levels are elevated due to bone metastasis. He has no evidence of significant active infection. He has no history of seizures but has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has not been treated with anthracyclines before and has not taken valproic acid in the last five days. He is willing to undergo biopsies as required for the study. He has no other concurrent medication or therapy.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has received Shingrix vaccination 3 years prior. She is generally in good health and is not currently taking any medications. She has no history of shingles or any other significant medical conditions. She has never participated in a clinical study involving investigational products. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not received any blood products in the past 3 months. She agrees to participate in the study and is willing to receive a challenge dose of Zostavax.

A 50-year-old man was diagnosed with chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after undergoing hematopoietic cell transplantation for acute myeloid leukemia 2 years ago. Despite receiving primary systemic therapy, including corticosteroids and calcineurin inhibitors, his symptoms have persisted and progressed over the past few months. He presents with skin rash, oral mucositis, gastrointestinal symptoms including abdominal pain, diarrhea, and nausea, and joint pain. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of extensive chronic GVHD. The patient has no history of allergies or other medical conditions, and he is currently on no medications except for prednisone and cyclosporine. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with study procedures and reporting requirements. The patient understands the requirements of the study and gives informed consent. He is willing to use contraception during the study period as he is not surgically sterile. The managing physician has also agreed to comply with study procedures and reporting requirements.

The patient is a 60 year old man, who is undergoing a routine screening colonoscopy due to his age. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He has no family history of colorectal cancer. He reports occasional constipation and occasional rectal bleeding. He has no other gastrointestinal symptoms. He is retired and leads a sedentary lifestyle. His BMI is 28 and his blood pressure is 130/80. He has never had a colonoscopy before and is nervous about the procedure. He has followed the bowel preparation instructions provided to him by his doctor. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 10 year old girl diagnosed with asthma complains of frequent wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath. She has to use her inhaler multiple times a day, which affects her daily activities and school performance. Her parents are concerned about her condition and are looking for better healthcare services in their area. They learn about the CYPHP Evelina London model of care and decide to enroll her in the trial. They live in Lambeth and Southwark and their daughter has been registered with a participating practice. They believe that the new model of care will help them manage their daughter's asthma better and improve her quality of life.

A 7-year-old boy with droopy eyelids presents to the ophthalmology clinic at Cairo University Specialized Pediatric Hospital. He has had congenital ptosis since birth and his parents are concerned about his vision and appearance. Upon examination, his levator function is found to be more than 4mm. The patient has no other ocular syndromes and has not had any previous attempts for repair. He does not have any traumatic or acquired ptosis and has a positive Bell's phenomenon. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the surgical effect of levator aponeurosis resection versus two-point fixation levator aponeurosis tucking for congenital ptosis.

A 56-year-old man with a history of Crohn's disease underwent an ileostomy surgery three months ago due to a severe flare-up. He has been managing his ostomy with a 1-piece flat product with open bag and a custom cut base plate. He has been experiencing occasional leakage, which has been affecting his daily life and causing skin irritation around the stoma. He has not received any radio- or chemotherapy or systemic steroid treatment in the past month. He does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any medication other than those related to his Crohn's disease. He is able to handle the ostomy appliance himself but occasionally receives help from his spouse. He has given written informed consent to participate in the investigation and is willing to test two different 1-piece products within the study.

A 25-year-old male college student living in New Haven, CT, who has been experiencing symptoms of psychosis for the past year. He has been feeling paranoid and anxious, experiencing hallucinations, and has a hard time concentrating on his studies. He has never received any psychiatric care and is not currently taking any medication. He speaks English fluently and is willing to travel to a local First Episode Service (STEP) for treatment. He has not been diagnosed with bipolar disorder or MDD with psychotic features, and his psychosis is not due to substance use or a medical illness. He is not legally mandated to enter treatment and is able to give free, informed consent. He is able to reliably determine the duration of untreated psychosis (DUP).

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He is currently taking a combination of sulphonylureas and metformin to manage his blood glucose levels, which are still not adequately controlled with HbA1c of 9.2%. He has a BMI of 29 and a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He reports a history of albuminuria, with 24-hour urinary albumin excretion rates of 0.5 g/day, and occasional episodes of hypoglycemia. He has no significant history of cardiovascular disease, pancreatitis, or thyroid disorders. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He works in an office and does not engage in regular exercise. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his diabetes management and reduce his risk of complications associated with diabetic nephropathy.

A 55-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of difficulty hearing in noisy environments. She reported having subjective hearing loss and occasionally asking people to repeat themselves. She is a native English speaker and has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders. She has not used any hearing aids before. Her IQ score was 98 on the two-subtest Abbreviated Wechsler's Adult Scale of Intelligence, which is within the normal range. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial that investigates the effects of short-term music training on auditory processing in older adults. She enjoys music and singing, but has no formal music training. She is open to joining a weekly remote choir for 10 weeks, directed by a professionally trained conductor from USC Department of Choral Music, and to receive individual singing lessons at home.

Lila is a 3-year-old girl who was diagnosed with Chromosome 18 abnormality at birth. She has been experiencing developmental delays, including delayed speech and motor skills. Her parents have been struggling to find comprehensive medical and educational resources to help their daughter. They have heard about the Chromosome 18 Clinical Research Center and are interested in participating in the clinical examination aspect of the study. Lila's general health is good, and she meets the minimum age requirement for the study. Her parents are excited about the opportunity to gather more information about Lila's condition and potentially receive treatments that can help her overcome the negative effects of her chromosome abnormality.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has undergone a urological surgery for a bladder issue. He was discharged from the hospital 2 days ago, and his parents are concerned about the surgical site. They noticed some redness and swelling around the catheter insertion site. They have contacted the NP on the phone and have been randomized to the experimental (PEC) group. They have agreed to send a digital photograph of the surgical site to the NP for assessment and advice. The patient has no known allergies, and he is not taking any medications other than those prescribed after surgery. He lives with his parents and younger sister and attends school. His parents speak English fluently and have access to email and a digital camera.

The patient is a 30-year-old African American woman who has been struggling with obesity and type 2 diabetes for the past few years. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension, and she has been on a regimen of oral hypoglycemic medication and insulin to control her blood sugar levels. She has noticed dark, velvety patches of skin on her neck and underarms, which she finds embarrassing and uncomfortable. She has been diagnosed with acanthosis nigricans and is interested in participating in a study that could help improve her symptoms. She is willing to undergo treatment with Metformin and follow all study-related procedures. She is not currently lactating, pregnant, or planning to become pregnant. She understands the risks involved and has signed the informed consent form. She is motivated to improve her health and is looking forward to participating in the study.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been experiencing difficulties in paying attention and following instructions at school. His teacher has reported that he is easily distracted and has a hard time completing tasks. He often forgets to turn in assignments and frequently interrupts others while they are speaking. His parents have noticed similar behavior at home, where he has trouble finishing his homework and chores. They have tried behavioral interventions, but have not seen any significant improvement. The patient has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He has a normal weight for his age and is able to swallow capsules. His intelligence is within the normal range.

Pt is a 52yo M with type 2 diabetes mellitus and has been diagnosed with moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. He has a history of high blood pressure, controlled with medications, and has never had eye surgery. His best corrected visual acuity is 6/12 (ETDRS chart) and his central macular thickness is 280 um on his most recent optical coherence tomography examination. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has signed the informed consent.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who presents with hematuria and pain upon urination. He has a past medical history of hypertension and is currently on amlodipine. He has a BMI of 28, BP: 145/90, HR: 80/min, and otherwise healthy. His laboratory studies are remarkable for hemoglobin: 12.5g/dL, creatinine: 1.3mg/dL, and PSA: 2.8ng/mL. Biopsy confirmed variant urothelial carcinoma histology. Imaging studies reveal clinical T2 disease with no evidence of metastasis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study including undergoing treatment, scheduled visits, and examinations including follow-up.

A 26-year-old healthy female came to the clinic to participate in a Phase 1 study of Hemay007. She has a BMI of 23 and weighs 60 kg. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any nicotine-containing products. She is not currently taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications or herbal supplements, except for occasional use of paracetamol. She is not pregnant and has not lactated in the past 3 months. She has been using effective contraception for the past year and has no history of any clinically severe medical conditions or surgeries. Her laboratory tests, including 12-lead ECG and vital signs, are within the normal range. She understands and is willing to comply with all study procedures and restrictions and has given written informed consent to participate in this study.

A 64-year-old man living in a peri-urban area of Nepal is invited to participate in a clinical trial aimed at preventing blindness. He has never had his eyes checked before and has noticed some blurriness in his vision recently. He lives with his wife and two grown children and works as a farmer. He has been diagnosed with high blood pressure and takes medication regularly but has no other underlying health conditions. He is able to walk for long distances without any difficulty and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been scheduled for a minor surgical procedure. He has no history of hypertension or any other medical condition that affects arterial pressure. The patient is not taking any medication that influences arterial pressure and has provided informed consent to participate in the adaptive clinical trial. The patient is able to understand the experiment and is willing to participate voluntarily.

15-month-old Korean male, currently in good health with no history of hepatitis A or previous hepatitis A vaccination. The child's parents have provided written consent for the child to participate in the study. The child has no history of sensitivity to neomycin, formaldehyde, gentamicin sulfate, or any preventive vaccines. The child's immune system has no disorders or congenital/acquired immunodeficient diseases, and has not received an immunosuppressive dose of systemic corticosteroids therapy within 12 weeks prior to vaccination. The child has not had moderate to severe acute or chronic infectious disease within 48 hours prior to vaccination. The child is not planned to receive any other vaccines within 4 weeks after the vaccination date nor received other vaccines within 4 weeks prior to the vaccination date. The child has not used immunoglobulin formulation or human plasma nor received a transfusion within 12 weeks prior to the vaccination date. The child has not participated or is participating in another clinical trial within 12 weeks prior to the vaccination date. The investigator has determined that there are no medical history or physical examination results that would prevent the child from participating in the clinical study.

The patient is a 68-year-old English-speaking woman living in a community setting. She has no history of dementia or mild cognitive impairment. She wears glasses and has adequate vision and hearing for testing. The patient has mild difficulties in getting along with other people, as identified by the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Scale (WHO-DAS). She has a Telephone Interview for Cognitive Status (TICS) score of 34, indicating no significant cognitive impairment. Her Geriatric Depression Scale score is 5, indicating that she is free of major depression that can interfere with neural efficiency for social-emotional regulation. Her EXAMINER composite score is 0.68, indicating decreased neural efficiency of frontal regions compared to cognitively healthy older adults in general. She has no contraindications for MRI.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic migraines for the past 5 years. She experiences an average of 18 headache days per month, of which at least 10 are migraine-specific acute medication-ergotamine or triptans. She has failed multiple prophylactic treatments including anti-seizure medications and TCA's. She has also received Botox treatment, but it did not result in at least a 30% reduction in the number of headache days per month. She has not received botulinum toxin in the last 4 months. She is able to differentiate migraine from other types of headaches. She is generally in good health, with no known systemic diseases, but has a history of hypothyroidism that is adequately controlled with medication. She is not pregnant and is using a medically acceptable form of contraception. She is able to understand the study requirements and has agreed to complete headache records as required per protocol.

A 14-year-old girl was brought to the emergency department after falling off her bike and hitting her head. She was not wearing a helmet and was unconscious for a few seconds. She reports a headache and mild nausea since the incident. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She is able to speak and read English fluently. On examination, she is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Her neurological exam is normal, and there are no signs of any other injuries. CT scan of the head is negative for any intracranial abnormalities. The patient is diagnosed with mild traumatic brain injury and is offered enrollment in a clinical trial. She agrees to participate and meets all the inclusion criteria, including the ability to comply with study procedures and follow up, and has a CBCL score of less than 65. She is not taking any medications that impair cognition, has no pre-existing neurologic impairment, and has no history of concussion or any other cognitive disorders. She will undergo Diffusion Tensor Imaging study within 96 hours of injury and will have blood drawn in the ED and three times as an outpatient for repeat testing. She is eligible for the mTBI group and will be closely monitored for any signs of axonal injury.

A 45-year-old male office worker with a history of chronic low back pain for the last 6 months, which has been worsening lately. The pain is located in the lower back area and radiates to the right leg, causing difficulty in walking and standing for long periods. He has tried conservative treatments, such as physical therapy, acupuncture, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), but with limited success. He is otherwise healthy, with no known history of coronary artery disease, osteoarthritis, or other orthopedic diseases that limit his walking capacity. He is fluent in Hebrew and has not received any steroid injections to the epidural space in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided his consent.

This is a 28-year-old African-American woman who is 16 weeks pregnant with her first child. She is concerned about her weight gain during pregnancy, as she has struggled with her weight in the past and has a BMI of 29. She is interested in participating in a study that focuses on healthy lifestyle during pregnancy and is willing to use technology to facilitate her engagement in the program. She currently owns a cell phone with a text messaging plan and is a member of Facebook social networking site. She is able to participate in physical activity and is committed to complying with all study-related procedures. She has no history of major medical or psychological conditions that would compromise her safety for successful participation in the study. She is excited to participate in a program that is specifically designed to meet the needs of low-income, Black mothers and hopes to improve her health and the health of her baby.

The patient is a 35-year-old HIV-positive male who has been diagnosed with high-grade anal squamous intraepithelial lesions. He has declined routine surgery or is not a candidate for surgical excision of HSIL. The patient has evidence of HIV infection through serologic testing or culture, with a CD4 count of at least 200 x 10^6/L and an HIV RNA level of no greater than 500 copies/mL. He has been on stable highly active antiviral therapy (HAART) for at least 4 weeks before the study. The patient has no prior history of invasive anal or cervical cancer and no concurrent untreated cervical HSIL. He has a life expectancy of at least 12 months, with a hemoglobin level of at least 10 g/dL, platelet count of at least 75,000/mm^3, and an absolute neutrophil count of at least 1,000/mm^3. The patient's AST and ALT levels are no greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal, and his creatinine level is no greater than 1.5 times the ULN. The patient has no prior severe allergic reactions or history of collagen-vascular or autoimmune disorder requiring treatment within the past 5 years. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. If fertile, he will use two forms of effective contraception during and for 3 months after the study. The patient has no other concurrent medical or psychiatric illness that would preclude the study. He has not received any concurrent medications that suppress immune function.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a genetically confirmed mitochondrial DNA transfer ribonucleic acid (tRNA)Leu(UUR) m.3243A>G mutation. She completed the KH176-202 study and is willing to continue receiving the medication. Her past medical history is significant for fatigue, exercise intolerance, muscle weakness, and ataxia. She also experiences occasional heart palpitations but has not been diagnosed with any heart conditions. She has no history of drug abuse or hypersensitivity to any of the components of the investigational drug. She is not pregnant and is not breastfeeding. The patient is on no medication known to affect cardiac repolarization, nor is she on strong Cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A4 inhibitors or inducers. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate is >60 mL/min according to the CKD-EPI formula at screening. The patient has not had surgery of the gastrointestinal tract that might interfere with absorption. She is willing to comply with the study requirements, including swallowing study medication.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who was diagnosed with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) two days ago. She was admitted to the hospital with a sudden onset of a severe headache and vomiting. A CT scan revealed a ruptured aneurysm in the brain. She underwent an urgent surgery to clip the aneurysm and is currently recovering in the neuro-intensive care unit. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, but she has no history of heart or lung disease. She is alert and oriented, with no neurological deficits. Her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. She is being considered for enrollment in the clinical trial to investigate cardiopulmonary complications in aSAH patients.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman experiencing pelvic pain and difficulty getting pregnant. She has been trying to conceive for the past eight months with no success. The pain is described as a dull ache in the lower abdomen that worsens during menstruation. She has no history of sexually transmitted infections, but she does experience painful intercourse. She has not taken any hormonal treatments for at least three months prior to the laparoscopy. Her last menstrual period was 10 days ago and lasted for five days. She has a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days. She has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has never had surgery in the pelvic area. She is interested in participating in the study to help find a more accurate diagnostic method for endometriosis and endometrioma.

A 16 yo F diagnosed with anorexia nervosa, presenting with a BMI of 16.5 kg/m², restrictive type with a history of weight loss of 15% over the past 3 months. She reports a fear of gaining weight and is preoccupied with food and weight. She has a history of amenorrhea, fatigue, poor concentration, and cold intolerance. She has no other significant medical or psychiatric history. She has been referred to an eating disorders clinic for treatment and has given written informed consent to participate in this study. She will complete several questionnaires to assess changes in motivation, symptoms, self-esteem, and coping style over a nine-month treatment period. Clinical AN diagnosis and BMI will be re-assessed at the end of the study.

This is a 65-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with localized prostate cancer and is scheduled to undergo external beam radiation therapy. He reports feeling significant fatigue that has interfered with his daily activities and quality of life. He has not previously used systematic light exposure therapy or any other fatigue-preventing treatments. He speaks and reads English and has access to the internet. He has no active infections or chronic fatigue disorders, and there are no underlying medical conditions that might contribute to his fatigue other than cancer and its treatments. He has no history of bipolar disorder, mania, seasonal affective disorder, sleep apnea, restless legs, or other sleep disorders known to affect fatigue. He is not on any photosensitizing medication and does not plan to travel across more than 2 time zones during the study period. He is not a shift worker and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman scheduled for a transvaginal urogynecological surgery due to stress urinary incontinence. She is generally healthy and her physical status is classified as ASA I. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known allergies to medications. She is nervous about the upcoming surgery and would like some form of sedation to help her relax. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Her BMI is 25 kg/m2. She speaks the local language and is able to understand the pain scale.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has a history of osteoporosis and has been undergoing bone SPECT/CT imaging for the last few years. She is currently asymptomatic and has not experienced any fractures in the past year. She has given her informed consent to participate in this study. She is insured and does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent her from undergoing the SPECT-CT exam. She is able to withstand the extended position with her arms behind her head for 15 minutes. She is not currently participating in any other studies and has not been in an exclusion period determined by a previous study. She is not under judicial protection or any kind of guardianship. She has no contra-indications for the treatment necessary for this study. She is not pregnant, parturient or breastfeeding. She does not have any osteosynthesis material or any other material that would generate an artifact during SPECT-CT in her spine. She is able to cooperate and follow instructions during the image acquisition.

The patient is a 28-year-old male chess player with a valid ELO-number. He is physically healthy with no history of diabetes mellitus or any other chronic diseases that require prescription drugs. He also has no history of psychiatric diseases, addiction to psychoactive substances, or smoking. He drinks two cups of coffee per day and has a regular day-night-rhythm. He is interested in participating in the study to explore the effects of stimulating substances on cognitive performance during chess games and neuropsychiatric tests.

The patient is a 22-year-old female student currently enrolled in the nursing program at the Anschutz Medical Campus at the University of Colorado. She has been experiencing high levels of stress and anxiety due to the demands of her academic workload and clinical rotations. She has no prior experience with formal meditation practices and is interested in exploring the potential benefits of incorporating meditation into her daily routine. She is comfortable with using technology and has access to a reliable internet connection.

47 yo M seeking treatment for alcohol dependence. Reports drinking at least 6 standard drinks 5 days per week over the past 28 days. Has a history of binge drinking and has attempted to quit on his own in the past without success. Currently, he is in good health with no major medical conditions or allergies to medications. He has no history of alcohol withdrawal seizures or delirium. He is not currently taking any psychotropic medications. He is able to provide informed consent, comply with study procedures and is interested in participating in the trial. Past Medical History: - Hypertension (controlled with medication) - Mild depression (currently not on medication) - Hyperlipidemia - Seasonal allergies

A 31-year-old mother of a 3-year-old boy with autism is interested in participating in the study. The boy has been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder and is the first-born in the family. He has no underlying medical conditions that would interfere with his participation in the study. The mother is the primary caregiver and is under the age of 35. She has completed at least 5th grade and speaks English fluently. She has access to a computer and a broadband wired or wireless internet connection. The family is not currently receiving any ABA treatment, and the mother has no history of mental illness. She is willing to commit to the 6-week intervention, which includes one session per week.

Patient B is a 65-year-old female who was diagnosed with heart failure 6 months ago. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2. She is currently taking medications for both conditions but has difficulty adhering to the prescribed regimen. She reports experiencing shortness of breath with minimal exertion, fatigue, and swelling in her legs. She has not been able to perform her daily activities as usual due to these symptoms. She is a retired teacher and lives alone. She reports feeling lonely and isolated since her diagnosis. She has tried to make dietary changes, but finds it challenging to maintain a healthy diet. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her blood pressure is 140/85 mmHg, pulse rate is 85 bpm, respiratory rate is 18 breaths/min, and O2 saturation is 96% on room air. Her physical examination reveals jugular venous distention, bibasilar crackles, and pitting edema in her legs. Her laboratory results show a serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, BNP of 400 pg/mL, and HbA1C of 7.5%. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her manage her heart failure symptoms and improve her quality of life.

This clinical trial is not suitable for individual patient recruitment as it involves obtaining normal breast tissue samples from organ donors and collecting risk factor data from next-of-kin. The study is aimed at obtaining a better understanding of how normal breast tissue develops and responds to stresses that increase the risk of developing breast cancer. Girls or women aged 11 years or older are eligible for the study, while men are excluded. This is a pilot project, and the feasibility of obtaining normal breast tissue samples from organ donors and collecting risk factor data from next-of-kin will be determined. If the feasibility is demonstrated, additional funding will be pursued for a larger study with optimized procedures. The goal of this initiative is to determine the associations between stages of breast development, risk factors for breast cancer, and gene expression. The identity of the participants will be kept confidential.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been struggling with alcohol dependence for the past year. She has a history of binge drinking and has experienced negative consequences as a result, including difficulty maintaining relationships and trouble at work. She is currently seeking treatment for her alcohol use disorder and is motivated to quit drinking. She has no current medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study.

10-year-old female student attending primary school in Hong Kong. She is in grade 3 and lives with her parents and younger brother. Both of her parents are smokers and smoke inside the home daily. She has been experiencing frequent coughing and wheezing, especially at night. She has also expressed concern about her parents' smoking habits and wishes they would quit. Her family is interested in participating in a trial aimed at reducing exposure to secondhand smoke and promoting smoking cessation.

The patient is a 47-year-old female diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with multiple liver metastases. She has received prior treatment with chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery. Her medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and depression. She currently takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and sertraline. She has no known allergies. Her latest laboratory results are within normal limits. CT scans confirm multiple liver metastases, which are confirmed to be from breast cancer. She is eligible for first-line treatment with taxanes according to national guidelines. She has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial investigating the use of focused ultrasound and microbubbles in enhancing chemotherapy delivery to liver metastases. She understands the risks and benefits of the treatment and is willing to comply with the follow-up schedule. She has no contraindications for ultrasound contrast-enhancement agent Sonovue® and is not currently pregnant.

This is a 4-year-old boy who was diagnosed with Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD) at the age of 3. He has had difficulty with social interaction, communication, and repetitive behaviors. He has not yet started school and spends most of his time at home with his parents. He has no other medical diagnoses and is otherwise healthy. His parents are literate and have no known chronic psychiatric or physical illness. They are willing to participate in a pilot trial of a Developmental, Individual-Difference, Relationship-Bases (DIR)/Floortime parent training intervention to help improve their child's developmental progress and decrease his autistic behaviors. They are able to attend follow-up visits as required by the study.

A 56-year-old woman presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no previous cardiac events. After undergoing diagnostic tests, the patient was diagnosed with severe coronary artery disease and recommended for a cardiovascular surgery. The patient is anxious and worried about the upcoming surgery and potential complications. She is interested in exploring non-pharmacological options to manage her anxiety and pain during the surgery and postoperative recovery. The patient has no psychiatric antecedents, claustrophobia, acrophobia, or visual or hearing impairments. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has given her consent.

A 62-year-old male patient was admitted to the internal medicine ward with hyperglycemia. He has a history of type 2 diabetes and is managed with oral medications. He has a sedentary lifestyle and a body mass index (BMI) of 30. He complains of fatigue, polyuria, and polydipsia. His blood glucose level was 250 mg/dL at the time of admission. He has no known complications of diabetes and no prior hospitalizations due to hyperglycemia. He has no history of hypoglycemia, hyperosmolar state, or ketoacidosis.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl with severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). She was diagnosed with SCID at birth and has been receiving regular medical treatment for the condition. She has a histocompatible sibling donor and is eligible for allogeneic bone marrow transplantation as a curative treatment. The patient has no significant medical history other than SCID and has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of allogeneic bone marrow transplantation in patients with primary immunodeficiencies.

The patient is a 27-year-old Muslim man with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus for 15 years. He has been using the FreeStyle Libre (FSL) flash glucose monitoring system and multiple daily injections (MDI) to administer insulin. He has received proper education on carbohydrate counting and adjusting insulin doses according to the carbs consumed through DAFNE structured education program. He is planning to fast Ramadan and willing to participate in the clinical trial. His most recent HbA1C level was 8.2%, and he has no significant diabetes-related complications. He has no hypoglycemia unawareness or other medical issues that could exclude him from the study. He is aware of the risks associated with fasting during Ramadan and is willing to adhere to the study protocol, including attending study visits and responding to daily messages and calls.

50-year-old male with advanced bilateral osteoarthritis of the knees and scheduled for simultaneous bilateral total knee arthroplasty. The patient has a history of opioid sensitivity and a strong desire to minimize the use of opioids postoperatively due to concerns of addiction and side effects. The patient has no history of chronic pain disorder or substance abuse, and normal renal function. The patient is willing to participate in the study and be randomly allocated to either the opioid-sparing protocol or the opioid-based patient-controlled analgesia protocol.

A 35-year-old male guardian, who is the father of a 4-year-old child enrolled in a partnering Head Start site, is seeking to participate in a clinical trial that can help enhance his parenting skills and improve his child's behavior. The male guardian is in good physical health and has no history of mental health issues that would prohibit his involvement in group-based prevention studies. He is enthusiastic about engaging in the Fathers Supporting Success in Preschoolers (FSSP) Program and is committed to attending all sessions. The male guardian is a working professional with a flexible work schedule that allows him to attend the program sessions without any difficulty. He is fluent in English and has good communication skills. He is motivated to learn and implement evidence-based parenting interventions in his daily life to support his child's success in preschool.

52-year-old male with a history of myocardial infarction (MI) and an implanted ICD for the treatment of a drug-refractory monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT). The patient has had multiple hospitalizations due to recurrent VT episodes despite medical management with antiarrhythmic drugs. The patient's LVEF is 30%. The patient has been advised to undergo an ischemic VT radiofrequency ablation procedure. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing outcomes of the procedure using the Niobe ES system versus a standard manual catheter ablation approach. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is available for follow-up assessments.

34-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia as per DSM IV criteria, currently taking conventional neuroleptics for at least 6 months, presents with prominent negative symptoms as defined by a total score of 45 on the scale for the assessment of negative symptoms (SANS). No history of substance abuse or dependence, and no history of seizures or any other serious neurological disorder. No unstable medical illness or allergies. The patient has a stable home environment and is capable of completing a cognitive battery. The patient is not pregnant or nursing. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of D-cycloserine augmentation of antipsychotic treatment on negative symptoms and cognitive function in schizophrenia.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma (BCC) on her face. She has a history of frequent sun exposure due to her outdoor job and she admits to not consistently using sunscreen. She is otherwise healthy with no other known medical conditions. She has no history of skin cancer or any other type of cancer in her family. She is currently taking no medications. She has been referred to a skin cancer surgeon who will perform Mohs surgery to remove the BCC. The surgeon will check frozen sections to ensure adequate margins are obtained. The patient has consented to providing freshly excised or freshly frozen leftover tissue obtained during the Mohs surgery to be discarded after histological diagnosis for the Spectrally Guided Mohs Surgery study. She is over 18 years old and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with rectal cancer. He experienced rectal bleeding and changes in bowel habits for about 6 months before seeking medical attention. He underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of rectal cancer. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He is employed as a construction worker and leads an active lifestyle. He has been married for 25 years and has two children. He enjoys spending time with his family and playing sports in his free time. He is fluent in English and has no problem understanding and communicating with his healthcare providers. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks of the study. He is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. His renal function is normal. He is willing to undergo additional imaging tests as part of the study and to comply with the follow-up appointments.

A 32-year-old woman with a history of depression presents to the clinic with a chief complaint of low mood, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 3 months. She reports no suicidal or homicidal ideations. She has a past medical history of asthma and has been using an inhaler as needed. She is currently not taking any medications for depression. The patient is alert and oriented to time, place, and person. She has no apparent distress. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is remarkable for mild wheezing in the lungs. Laboratory tests reveal no abnormalities. She meets the criteria for Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and has a 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS) score of 21. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the effects of Escitalopram on depressive symptoms and brain activity. She has no metallic implants and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing low back pain for the past year. The pain is located on the right side of his lower back and radiates down to his right leg. He rates his pain as 8 out of 10 on the pain scale. He has tried various treatments, including physical therapy and pain medications, but they only provide temporary relief. He underwent a lumbar medial branch block and experienced more than 70% pain relief. He has no history of spine surgery or metal hardware at the lumbosacral spine, and there is no neurological deficit. He is able to communicate in English and has no severe medical condition that would prevent him from participating in the study. He is interested in participating in the study to see if the Neurolyser XR can provide long-term pain relief.

A 31 year old female who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) and is currently taking an antidepressant. She has been experiencing residual depression symptoms despite taking the medication. She has no significant medical history and is able to swallow capsules.
