She is willing to comply with any applicable contraceptive requirements of the study. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence disorder and has not been hospitalized for her current MDD episode. She has no current or lifetime history of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or any co-morbid psychiatric disorder. She is not considered a suicide risk and has no history of seizures or any neurological disease. She has no history of symptomatic cardiovascular disease, advanced arteriosclerosis, structural cardiac abnormality, cardiomyopathy, serious heart rhythm abnormalities, coronary artery disease, or other serious cardiac problems. She is not pregnant or nursing.

A 10-year-old boy with a diagnosis of microtia is scheduled for rib cartilage harvest from three ribs for auricular reconstruction. He has no history of analgesic administration within the past 24 hours and has no known coagulation disorders or allergies to local anesthetics. He is in overall good health with no history of renal insufficiency or any other significant medical conditions. He is able to express pain scores and severity of nausea and understands how to use the patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) device. His parents have provided informed consent for him to participate in the study and have no objections to intercostal nerve blocks or paravertebral block.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic vulvar pain for at least 6 months. She has been diagnosed with provoked or non-provoked vulvar vestibulitis by a qualified medical professional. Her typical pain score is at least 40 out of 100 on a visual analog scale. She has tried various pain relief medications but is willing to decrease their use during the study. She is not currently using any hormonal interventions such as birth control pills or topical or oral estrogen agents. She has not had any surgical or procedural interventions to treat her vulvar vestibulitis. She does not have any active infections or wounds in the areas to be treated with the laser. She does not have any neurological disorders such as Multiple Sclerosis or photosensitivity disorder. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study. She has no serious mental health illness, developmental disability or cognitive impairment that may preclude adequate comprehension of the consent form or ability to record study measures.

This is a 52 year old male with a history of stage IIIB follicular lymphoma diagnosed in 2016. The patient was treated with 6 cycles of R-CHOP followed by radiation therapy to the involved field. The patient achieved a complete response which was confirmed on PET scan. In 2018, the patient presented with fatigue, night sweats, and a 10-pound weight loss. The patient underwent a biopsy which confirmed the relapse of follicular lymphoma. The patient received 2 cycles of bendamustine and rituximab and achieved a partial response. The patient is currently experiencing disease progression and is a suitable candidate for this clinical trial. Past Medical History: 1. Follicular lymphoma 2. Hypertension 3. Hypercholesterolemia 4. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus 5. Obesity

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). He has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath for the past few months. His blood work shows low red blood cell counts and platelets, and his bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of MDS with an intermediate-2 or high-risk score according to the IPSS. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore potential treatment options. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol requirements and has given voluntary written informed consent. He has a life expectancy of more than 6 months, and his performance status is 1 according to the WHO. He has no known active infectious hepatitis type B or C, or HIV infection. His platelet count is currently at 30 x 10^9/L without transfusion support within 7 days before the test, and his ANC is at 0.6 x 10^9/L without the use of growth factors. His AST and ALT levels are below 2.5 times the upper limit of normal, and his total bilirubin level is below 1.5 times the ULN. His serum creatinine level is also below 2 times the ULN. The patient is not currently using erythropoietin and is epoetin-resistant. He is willing to use an acceptable method for contraception during the study drug therapy and for 4 weeks after discontinuation of thalidomide therapy.

47 yo M with a history of anxiety and depression presents to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has been on a stable dose of warfarin for the past 6 months due to a history of DVT. He reports occasional difficulty sleeping and feeling anxious, but has not sought treatment for these symptoms. He does not smoke, but drinks alcohol occasionally on the weekends (average of 2 drinks per week). His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research and improve his own health.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He is currently not taking any medication and has not taken any investigational drug or device in the past 30 days. He is able to give informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or using any form of contraception. He has no known hypersensitivity to baclofen and has not had any significant history of cardiac, neurologic, psychiatric, oncologic, endocrine, metabolic, renal or hepatic disease. The patient is proficient in English and has not worked a night shift in the past 24 hours.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with gastric cancer. He underwent a gastrectomy and was found to have stage IV metastatic disease with liver and lung metastases. He has received several courses of chemotherapy and is currently experiencing some fatigue, nausea, and vomiting. He has completed all standard of care therapies for his disease and is looking for alternative treatments. He has never been treated with targeted therapy before. He is willing to provide blood samples for research purposes and has signed the informed consent form. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications that could interfere with the study.

There is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial as it is a retrospective analysis of data gathered from the neonatal surgery intensive care unit at Ihsan Dogramaci Children's Hospital. However, the study is focused on newborns who had surgical problems and were hospitalized in the neonatal intensive care unit at Hacettepe University. Therefore, the patients included in the study are likely to be newborns with congenital anomalies requiring surgical treatment.

The patient is a premature infant born before 33 weeks gestational age who required supplemental oxygen at 36 weeks gestational age and was discharged home after neonatal intensive care. The infant does not have any major congenital anomalies or tracheostomy tubes. The family speaks English and lives within 150 miles of the clinic. The infant will be randomly assigned to either community-based follow-up or medical-center based follow-up. If assigned to community-based follow-up, the family will receive a telephone call twice weekly in the first month after discharge, weekly in months two through four, and monthly thereafter until the infant reaches 12 months adjusted age. The nurse specialist will coordinate care for the infant by communicating with home health nurses, public health nurses, early intervention specialists, physical therapists, and pediatric sub-specialists. The primary caregiver can contact the nurse specialist on a toll-free long distance line with voice mail which records messages when the phone is not attended. If assigned to medical-center based follow-up, the infant will be seen in a regional, high-risk infant multidisciplinary clinic at Wake Forest University School of Medicine. The first clinic visit will occur approximately one month after their discharge. A multidisciplinary team consisting of the social worker, the nurse specialist and the neonatologist will obtain detailed interim medical history and perform a complete physical examination. The infant will be scheduled for visits at four, eight, and twelve months adjusted age. The family will receive twenty dollars as compensation for each time they complete study questionnaires and when home visits are made.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who lost his right leg below the knee in a car accident six months ago. He is currently using a prosthesis with an elastomeric liner and experiences daily volume fluctuations in his residual limb, which cause his prosthesis to fit poorly. He works as a computer programmer and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He is able to walk continuously with his prosthesis for at least 5 minutes at a time, as well as sit and stand without difficulty. However, he experiences difficulty stepping up a height of 5.0 cm. He has no known allergies, and he is not taking any medications. He is in overall good health and has no history of skin breakdown or other issues related to his residual limb. He is interested in participating in this trial to potentially improve the fit and comfort of his prosthesis.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman with a history of knee pain due to osteoarthritis. She has tried conservative treatments such as activity modification, weight loss, and corticosteroid injections for over 6 weeks without significant improvement. She has radiographically confirmed Kellgren-Lawrence I-III OA without bone-on-bone. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares two different styles of FDA-approved needles for bone marrow aspiration concentrate (BMAC) injection. The patient is not currently taking any anti-inflammatory medications or herbal therapies and is not a smoker. She has not undergone radiation therapy, has no history of anemia, bleeding disorders, or inflammatory joint disease, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent and is eager to explore new options for treating her knee pain.

John is a 32-year-old construction worker who suffered an open fracture of his left tibia in a worksite accident. He was rushed to the emergency room of the local hospital where he underwent emergency surgical intervention. He received intravenous antibiotics within 1 hour of injury and continued for 72 hours. He has no significant medical history and he is a non-smoker. His laboratory studies are within normal limits. His radiographic studies showed a Gustilo grade IIIA fracture. He is able and willing to sign an informed consent form and is committed to complying with the study protocol. He has no known allergies to medications and has not participated in any clinical trial in the last 30 days. He is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. He agrees to use highly effective contraception during the study period. He has no known history of metabolic bone diseases or diabetes. He is willing to be randomized into either the study investigational arm or the study control arm.

A 40-year-old male with a history of plaque psoriasis for 3 years visited the clinic complaining of worsening of his skin lesions. He has tried different topical treatments with minimal improvement. His BMI is 28, and he does not have any other medical conditions. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His psoriasis lesions involve approximately 5% of his body surface area, excluding the scalp. He has at least one target plaque on his trunk that is at least 3 cm x 3 cm in size, and his PGA score is 3. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new topical treatment for plaque psoriasis.

A 55-year-old female office worker has been experiencing hip pain for several years. She was diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has tried various conservative treatments, including physical therapy and medications, but her pain has continued to worsen. She has lost significant range of motion in her hip and has difficulty with daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. She has no significant past medical history and does not smoke. She is married and has two adult children. She has scheduled an appointment with a surgeon to discuss the possibility of a total hip replacement. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial and understands that she will need to return to the hospital for follow-up appointments.

We are seeking healthy adults who weigh over 130 pounds (male) or over 155 pounds (female) and are at least 5 feet 1 inch (male) or 5 feet 5 inches (female) in height. Participants must have a hemoglobin level of at least 13.3 g/dL. You will be asked to donate a unit of your own blood, which will be processed and then split into two equal units. One unit will be transfused back into your body between 3-7 days after donation, while the other unit will be stored for 42 days before transfusion. Blood samples will be drawn before, during, and after transfusion to measure levels of various analytes. You will be ineligible if you have a systolic blood pressure above 180 or below 90 mm Hg, diastolic blood pressure above 100 or below 50 mm Hg, heart rate below 50 or above 100, temperature above 99.5 F prior to donation or above 100.4 F or if you experience subjective feeling of illness prior to transfusion. Additionally, you must have a negative result on standard blood donor infectious disease testing and cannot be pregnant. Your participation in this study can help us to determine if fresh or old blood is better for transfusion.

50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and obesity was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and was diagnosed with COVID-19 pneumonia. Despite receiving oxygen therapy, his condition rapidly deteriorated, and he was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. The patient has been in the ICU for the past 3 days and has not shown any improvement in his respiratory status. He has been informed of the CONFIDENT clinical trial and is interested in participating. Upon evaluation, the patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and consents to participate.

52F with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a prior coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery 5 years ago. During a routine follow-up visit with her cardiologist, the patient reported symptoms of chest pain with exertion that has been occurring for the past 2 weeks. Further evaluation revealed evidence of myocardial ischemia on a stress test. The patient agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent. She is currently on Aspirin (75mg/day) and Clopidogrel (75mg/day) and has been compliant with the medication regimen for the past 6 months. Upon angiographic evaluation, the patient was diagnosed with in-stent restenosis in a non-coated metallic stent. The target reference vessel diameter was estimated to be between 2.5 and 4 mm, and the target lesion was estimated to be ≤22mm. The patient also had a visual estimate of the restenosis between 50 and 99% and a TIMI flow grade >1. The patient did not have any other exclusion criteria and agreed to undergo all protocol scheduled follow-up examinations.

A 37-year-old woman presented with a lump in her right breast that she noticed during a self-examination. The patient has no family history of breast cancer. The lump was confirmed through a biopsy to be triple-negative breast cancer. The patient has no other significant medical history and is generally healthy with an ECOG score of 0. The patient's blood work and other organ functions are normal, including TBIL, ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, BUN, Cr, and coagulation tests. The patient has not previously received antitumor treatment or radiation therapy for any malignant tumor, excluding cervical carcinoma in situ, basal cell carcinoma, or squamous cell carcinoma. The patient is not experiencing any severe heart disease or discomfort, and her LVEF is over 55%. She has not previously been treated with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2 drugs or drugs that target another co-inhibitory T cell receptor. The patient has agreed to abstinence or use of an effective method of contraception during treatment and at least 7 months after the last dose during study treatment. The patient has signed the informed consent and is eligible to participate in the study.

62-year-old male with a history of hypertension and prostate adenocarcinoma was referred to radiation oncology for evaluation of treatment options. Biopsy results showed Gleason 7 adenocarcinoma with T2b staging and PSA level of 40 ng/mL. Imaging studies did not reveal any lymph node involvement or bone metastasis. The patient's prostate volume was estimated to be 50 cc on MRI. He has no prior history of pelvic irradiation, rectal surgery or cancer. He is currently on a hormonal therapy and his IPSS score is 6 without alpha blocker treatment. The patient's general health condition is good with a WHO performance index of 0. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and tolerance of pelvic-prostatic hypo-fractionated radiotherapy followed by boost in patients with prostate adenocarcinoma adverse intermediate risk or high localized risk.

A 55-year-old Asian man arrives at the hospital with chest pain that has been ongoing for over 30 minutes. He is sweating profusely and experiencing shortness of breath. The patient has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, but has never had a heart attack before. His vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 155/95 mmHg, heart rate 110 bpm, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 95% on room air, and temperature 37°C. The physical examination reveals a pale, diaphoretic man with diffuse chest discomfort. The ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads V1 to V4. The patient meets all of the inclusion criteria for the study, has never received TNK-tPA (tenecteplase) before, and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. However, he has a history of major surgery six weeks ago, which is an exclusion criteria for the study. Therefore, he is not eligible to participate in the trial.

A 30-year-old healthy male presents with interest in participating in a clinical trial focused on evaluating the immune response to two vaccines against meningococcal serogroups A, C, W-135 and Y. The patient has no history of meningococcal disease, allergies, autoimmune diseases, or immunodeficiency. He has not received any meningococcal vaccine previously and is willing to comply with all study requirements. The patient is willing to allow his General Practitioner and consultant to be notified of his participation in the study. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for three months thereafter if female and of childbearing potential. The patient is in good health, as determined by medical history, history-directed physical examination, and clinical judgment of the investigator. The patient is aged between 18 and 70 years, inclusive, and has given written informed consent to participate in the study after the nature of the study has been explained. The patient is willing to have a total of 5 visits in a period of 2 months, with a total of 5 blood samples taken (5x20mL= 100 mL of blood taken in a 2 month period) for analysis prior to each immunisation, 7 days following the first immunisation and 7 and 28 days following the second immunisation.

A 25 year old healthy male with no medical or neurological history is being sought for a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a cooling system designed to lower the body's central temperature and cool the brain. The trial aims to study thermal responses in normal volunteers and to derive cooling parameters that will be used in a future study involving patients with epilepsy. The patient should not be taking any medication, including prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medicines. They should weigh more than 80 pounds and not be excessively overweight. Additionally, they should not have any history of gastrointestinal disorders or difficulty swallowing. The patient will be required to undergo a medical history, physical, and neurological examination, as well as an electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrocardiogram (EKG). Core temperature will be measured with a temperature-sensing pill, and a hand-held infrared thermometer will be used to measure temperatures from various locations, including the scalp, face, mouth, ears, arms, legs, and abdomen. They will be seated in a comfortable chair and fitted with the cooling system, a portable unit with a circulating coolant, for two overnight stays, which will be 2 to 3 days apart. Cooling will last for 30 minutes for the first session and 60 minutes for the second. Participants will be monitored for at least 30 minutes after each session to track temperature changes and have a post-cooling EEG recording.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing persistent lower back pain for the past few months. Imaging studies reveal a large mass in his left kidney, which is consistent with renal cell carcinoma. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of clear cell carcinoma. Further imaging studies show multiple metastases to the lungs and bones. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and has never received treatment for cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. He is willing to undergo nephrectomy and is able to provide informed consent. His blood work is within normal limits, and he has no active infections or autoimmune diseases. He has not received any systemic antitumor therapy within 28 days before screening, and he is not currently taking any anticoagulants. The patient is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception if he is a female of childbearing potential. He has a Karnofsky performance status of greater than 70%. The patient does not have any known significant coagulation abnormalities or thyroid abnormalities that cannot be maintained in the normal range with medication. He has not had any major adverse reactions to previous vaccinations or known hypersensitivity to sunitinib or chemically related products. The patient is not currently experiencing any symptoms related to CNS metastasis, and he does not have any clinically significant gastrointestinal abnormalities. He has not been diagnosed with an active or latent virus disease, and he has not had a prior history of invasive cancer within 5 years before screening.

A 65-year-old Caucasian man with a body mass index of 27 kg/m2 complains of feeling fatigued and having difficulty with physical activities. He is a retired accountant and spends most of his time sitting. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known history of diabetes or drug and alcohol abuse. He has no contraindications to perform exercise training. He has not been diagnosed with any acute or chronic infections. His INR is 1.2, and he is not taking any anticoagulants. He is willing to undergo an 8-week training intervention to improve his exercise tolerance and overall health.

A 35-year-old Cantonese-speaking man suffered a stroke 6 months ago, which was his first-ever stroke. He was hospitalized for 2 weeks and discharged to his home with mild right-sided weakness and difficulty with fine motor control. He has been receiving outpatient rehabilitation therapy twice a week since his discharge and has made some progress in regaining his strength and mobility. However, he still experiences difficulty performing daily tasks such as dressing, preparing meals, and using the computer. He feels isolated and frustrated with his slow progress and is worried about his ability to return to work as a computer programmer. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His Montreal Cognitive Assessment score is 25, and his modified Rankin Scale score is 3, indicating moderate disability. He is interested in participating in a program that could help him improve his community reintegration and psychosocial outcomes.

A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with metastatic renal cancer with clear cells. She was previously healthy with no significant medical history. She underwent a left radical nephrectomy and was started on Sutent© as a first-line targeted therapy. She has been experiencing side effects, including fatigue, diarrhea, and nausea. She has difficulty managing these side effects on her own and has expressed the need for more guidance and support. She is married and has two adult children who live nearby. She works as a part-time accountant and has taken a leave of absence due to her illness. She is interested in participating in a therapeutic education program to learn how to better manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She is in good general health and has a WHO performance status of 1. She does not have a history of any other cancer or severe psychiatric illness.

A 56-year-old man who had a hip replacement surgery three months ago is experiencing non-healing wounds in the surgical site despite receiving multiple courses of antibiotics. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. He smokes half a pack of cigarettes a day and drinks occasionally. He lives alone but has a home health nurse visiting him twice a week. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in this experimental phage therapy and is willing to provide a signed informed consent.

The patient is a 8-year-old child who has been experiencing a persistent runny nose with greenish-yellow discharge, cough, and facial pain for over 10 days. The symptoms have not improved with over-the-counter medications. The child has a history of allergies to penicillin but has never taken amoxicillin-clavulanate. The child's parents are fluent in English and have agreed to participate in the study. The child has not taken any antibiotics within the last 15 days and does not have any other concurrent infections. The child does not have asthma, allergic rhinitis, immotile cilia syndrome, cystic fibrosis or immunodeficiency. The child does not have systemic toxicity or wheezing on exam. The child has a baseline score of 12 on the Pediatric Rhinosinusitis Symptom Scale. The child meets the inclusion criteria for "persistent" presentation of sinusitis and is eligible to participate in the clinical trial to determine if antibiotic therapy is necessary for their condition.

The patient is a 48-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with Stage IVB nasopharyngeal carcinoma. He has been experiencing symptoms such as a persistent sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and a lump in his neck. He has no history of prior malignancy and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He underwent a CT scan of his nasopharynx and chest x-ray, which revealed a large tumor in his nasopharynx and metastasis to his lymph nodes. He underwent a liver function test and liver scan which were both normal. His bone scan is also normal. His performance status is at 2 according to the ECOG System. He has not received any prior treatment for his cancer.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) for the past 2 years following a traumatic event. She has been diagnosed with PTSD by a mental health professional using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI) and has not had any changes to her psychotropic medications in the past 4 weeks. She has no metal implants or devices within 30 cm of the magnetic rTMS coil and has no contraindications to rTMS, including no history of seizures (except childhood febrile seizures), no recent and unexplained syncope, no first-degree relative with a history of epilepsy, and is not pregnant. She has no history of psychosis or psychotic disorder, bipolar type I disorder, or organic mental disorders. She has not abused any substances within the past 3 months and is not at active risk for suicide. She does not have borderline or antisocial personality disorder and does not have any acute medical illnesses or significant central nervous system disorders. She is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

25-year-old pregnant woman in her 22nd week of pregnancy presents for recruitment in the clinical trial. She has a pre-pregnancy BMI of 22, is a frequent consumer of dairy products, eggs, and meat (pork, beef, poultry), and has a project of exclusive breastfeeding until at least the 45th day postpartum. She has no history of eating disorders and is not a vegetarian, vegan, or flexitarian. She has no known allergies to food products involved in the study and is willing to consume all food products delivered. She has read and signed the written consent form. She does not have a multiple pregnancy and is not living with more than 2 adults and 3 children (excluding fetus). She is not under legal protection (guardianship, trusteeship, etc.) and is not deprived of liberty. She has no history of prematurity and has no plans to interrupt breastfeeding before the 21st postpartum day.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage III ovarian carcinoma. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. She underwent optimal debulking surgery and has no residual disease. Her performance status is good, and she has a good general condition. She has no history of prior cancer or chemotherapy. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any illicit drugs. Her physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 12 g/dL WBC: 8000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL BUN: 12 mg/dL

A 8 year old child with a diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) and scheduled for open-heart surgery for repair of a ventricular septal defect (VSD) and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). The child has no prior history of renal failure or hepatic disease. The child's medical history is significant for CHD and recurrent respiratory tract infections. The child weighs 30 kg and has no known allergies. Preoperative hematocrit value, white blood cell and platelet counts, biochemical parameters (blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, electrolyte values), and RACHS1 score have been recorded. During the intraoperative period, the operation time, CPB time, aortic cross-clamp time, circulatory arrest time, body temperature and lowest body temperature reached during CPB, cardioplegia amount, The ACT (activated coagulation time), urine amount, intraoperative blood gas values, lactate, mean arterial pressure, glucose values, and the amount of crystalloid and colloid, erythrocyte, fresh frozen plasma, platelet and cryoprecipitate used in intraoperative period will be recorded. The child will be monitored for SIRS using the age-specific SIRS criteria determined by the International Pediatric Sepsis Consensus Conference at postoperative 6th, 12th, 24th and 48th hours. The child will be evaluated for SIRS rates and risk factors in both cyanotic and acyanotic patients.

62 year old male with a confirmed diagnosis of stage IV lung cancer. He has been experiencing severe pain as a result of his cancer and has been prescribed oral morphine for symptom palliation. His blood pressure is within normal limits and he does not have any active systemic infections. He is able to swallow tablets without difficulty. The patient has no prior history of hypertension, diabetes, tuberculosis, epilepsy or psychiatric and neurological illness. His performance status is within normal limits with a Karnofsky Performance Status score of 70. He has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old primigravida woman in her first trimester of pregnancy, estimated at 12 weeks of gestation. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles and has had no complications in her previous medical history. She is currently not taking any medications and has no allergies. She presents for her routine pregnancy check-up and is interested in participating in the Preeclampsia Sequential Screening clinical trial. She is fully informed about the study and its procedures and signs the informed consent form. A blood sample will be taken during her first appointment to determine the risk of chromosomal disorders, but this same sample will also be used to analyze angiogenic factors without requiring a new blood extraction. During the first-trimester ultrasound scan, the mean uterine arteries pulsatility index will be determined, as well as mean arterial pressure. The patient's medical history will be reviewed and she will be classified into one of three risk groups (low-risk, moderate-risk, and high-risk) based on her medical history, MAP, Pregnancy-Associated Plasma Protein A (PAPP-A), and Uterine Artery Pulsatility Index (UTPI). If the patient is classified as intermediate risk, Placental Growth Factor (PlGF) will be determined from the blood sample kept in biobanks. Based on her risk classification, the patient may be offered prophylactic treatment with AcetylSalicylic acid (ASA) until 36 weeks of pregnancy to prevent preeclampsia. All data collected during the regular pregnancy check-up will be used for the study without requiring additional appointments.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has a history of recurrent calcium oxalate kidney stones. He reports experiencing pain and discomfort in his lower back and abdomen, and has had multiple episodes of passing kidney stones in the past. He has been taking over the counter hydroxycitrate supplements for weight loss. The patient is willing to participate in the study to understand the effect of hydroxycitrate supplements on urine chemistry. The patient has no known kidney disease, and has no family history of renal stones. He is able to read and follow instructions for 24 hour urine collections, and is willing to sign an informed consent form. The patient is in good physical health, with no significant medical history.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been suffering from perennial allergic rhinitis for the past 3 years. She also has a history of asthma and has been using an inhaler daily for the past year. The patient has been experiencing persistent nasal congestion, sneezing, itching, and runny nose despite using various antihistamines and intranasal corticosteroids. She has never been prescribed Monterizine capsules before. The patient has no significant past medical history, but she has a family history of allergic rhinitis and asthma. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She provides informed consent and is willing to participate in the observational study to evaluate the therapeutic effectiveness and safety of Monterizine capsules.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who underwent a heart transplant surgery two years ago. He is currently on maintenance immunosuppressant therapy and is stable with no current signs of heart failure. His blood pressure is well controlled with medication, and he has no history of ventricular tachy-arrhythmias or AV block. He has normal liver and kidney function tests. He does not have any known allergies, and he has not participated in any other studies in the last month. He does not take any vitamin supplements. He is willing to participate in the study after providing written informed consent.

A 55 year old Chinese man visited the clinic with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing pain in his feet for the past 2 years, which has gradually worsened. The patient reported a tingling sensation and burning pain in his feet, making it difficult to walk or stand for long periods of time. He reported an average daily pain score (ADPS) of 6 on a scale of 0-10. The patient's HbA1c level was 8.5% at screening, and his creatinine clearance was 70 mL/min. There is no history of any other severe pain or neurological disorders unrelated to DPN. The patient's psychiatric status is stable, and he is currently taking medications for his diabetes. He is interested in participating in the study to find relief from his diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been taking atorvastatin for the past 3 months to treat his high cholesterol levels. He has been experiencing muscle pain and weakness for the last few weeks which has been interfering with his daily routine. He also reports experiencing difficulty in climbing stairs and carrying heavy objects. He has never experienced such symptoms before starting the medication. The patient has no other relevant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. He is currently not taking any other medications. He is willing to donate blood samples and agrees to undergo a muscle biopsy if necessary. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with stage IIb Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer. He has completed four weeks of standard chemotherapy and radiation therapy and is now in remission. He has no evidence of disease, but he is concerned about the possibility of cancer recurrence. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help to prevent the recurrence of cancer. He has no history of HIV, Hepatitis B or C, or any other acute medical conditions. He has not participated in any other investigational studies or prior cancer vaccine therapy. He is willing to use adequate birth control during the study period. He is not allergic to any vaccine components and has not had any adverse reactions following administration of any vaccines. He is not a woman who is pregnant, intends to become pregnant or is breastfeeding.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who has been experiencing shortness of breath and dry cough for the past 6 months. She has a history of smoking for 10 years but quit 5 years ago. She has no significant past medical history and her family history is negative for any lung disease. She has not been diagnosed with any interstitial lung disease or pneumonia before. She is willing to provide a blood sample and has given written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial to help further research into the development of biomarkers for ILD.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain started after lifting a heavy object at work. She describes the pain as a constant dull ache in her lower back that becomes sharper with certain movements such as bending or twisting. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy without much relief. She has no history of any other medical conditions and takes no medications regularly. She is interested in participating in a study that could help improve her quality of life by reducing her low back pain. Her physical examination shows evidence of clinical lumbar instability, including increased lumbar lordosis and decreased lumbar range of motion. She is able to walk without assistance, but reports difficulty with prolonged standing and sitting. Her MRI shows no evidence of disc herniation or other structural abnormalities.

This is a 35 year old male with a past medical history of HIV-1 infection and has been on a stable antiretroviral (ARV) regimen consisting of a boosted protease inhibitor (limited to darunavir [DRV] or atazanavir with low-dose ritonavir [rtv] or cobicistat [COBI], or lopinavir with rtv) combined with emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (FTC/TDF) for at least 6 consecutive months preceding the Screening visit. His on-treatment plasma human immunodeficiency virus type 1 ribonucleic acid (HIV-1 RNA) concentrations are less than (<) 50 copies per milliliter (copies/mL) or HIV-1 RNA undetectable by a local HIV-1 RNA test between 12 and 2 months prior to the Screening visit and have HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at the Screening visit. He has a normal electrocardiogram (ECG) at Screening. He does not have a history of failure on DRV treatment and DRV resistance-associated mutations (RAMs), if documented historical genotypes are available. He has no history of a new acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)- defining condition diagnosed within the 30 days prior to Screening. He is negative for acute hepatitis within 30 days prior to study entry, hepatitis C antibody, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). He does not have cirrhosis as diagnosed based on local practices.

Pt is a 25yo male with a 3-year history of progressive keratoconus in both eyes, with worsening vision and difficulty wearing contact lenses. The patient has no other ocular abnormalities and has not had any previous ocular surgeries. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no cognitive insufficiency. The patient is planned for corneal crosslinking and is eligible for the study. The patient will receive Epi-off PiXL in one eye and Epi-on PiXL in high oxygen environment in the fellow eye. The patient will be evaluated at baseline and at 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months after treatment, and ocular discomfort will be evaluated at specific time intervals up to 1 week postoperatively.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl with a history of cerebral palsy and a gastrostomy tube placed for feeding purposes. Her parents have noticed the formation of excess tissue around the site of the gastrostomy tube, which is causing discomfort and occasional bleeding. They have tried various home remedies but have not seen significant improvement. The girl is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies or medical conditions. She is able to communicate effectively and participates in physical therapy twice a week. Her parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial to help find the best treatment option for their daughter's granulation tissue.

27-year-old mother of a 6-month-old baby boy residing in a rural area of Pakistan. She has a working android smartphone and is able to use it comfortably. The mother has completed her own vaccinations during pregnancy and is aware of the importance of vaccination for her child but sometimes forgets the vaccination schedule due to her busy routine. She has faced difficulty in accessing healthcare services due to limited resources and transportation issues. She is willing to participate in this study to improve her child's vaccination coverage and is interested in learning about new technologies that can help her manage her child's health more effectively.

The patient is a 40-year-old HIV-positive man who participated in the A4001050 study and received Maraviroc as part of his treatment. He has been responding well to the drug and wishes to continue taking it. He has no significant medical history other than his HIV diagnosis and is compliant with his treatment plan. He is willing and able to attend scheduled visits and follow study procedures. He is currently residing in India and is unable to obtain Maraviroc commercially.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been struggling with weight management for the past few years. She has a BMI of 32 and has been diagnosed with hypertension and dyslipidemia. Despite previous attempts to lose weight with diet and exercise, she has not been successful in achieving sustainable weight loss. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other options for weight loss. The patient has no history of drug abuse or significant medical conditions and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to comply with the study requirements, including daily medication and lifestyle intervention.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with sinus node disease and an intrinsic AV delay of maximal 260 ms. He has had a pacemaker implanted to regulate his heart rate. He has been experiencing occasional episodes of dizziness and fatigue, and his cardiologist has suggested the EnTRINSIC clinical trial as a possible option to optimize his pacemaker settings. He has no history of atrial fibrillation or other cardiac diseases, and his New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification is II. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and has no known drug allergies. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and drinks alcohol occasionally in moderation. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 125/80 Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl

A 42 year old woman who works from home and spends most of her day sitting in front of a computer is interested in participating in a clinical trial for monitoring sedentary behavior and physical activity. She is concerned about the health effects of prolonged sitting and wants to learn more about her own activity patterns. She is willing to wear multiple sensor devices on 7 days for 12 hours per day and a wrist accelerometer on 7 days for 24 hours per day. She is physically fit and able to walk unassisted. She is able to read and understand study materials in English.

The patient is a 58 year old Hispanic male who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking for the past 20 years. He has been advised by his physician to undergo coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) to treat his symptoms. He has agreed to undergo the surgery and has been scheduled for the procedure within 24 hours. The patient is currently taking blood pressure medication and cholesterol-lowering medication as prescribed. He has no history of bleeding disorders or abnormal blood clotting. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a construction worker and enjoys playing soccer on weekends. He is willing to participate in a research study that aims to understand how blood clotting factors are activated during open heart surgery and how to prevent bleeding and clot formation. He has signed informed consent forms and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) according to the criteria of the international AIH Group. She has been receiving treatment with azathioprine and corticosteroids for 18 months, and a recent liver biopsy showed a histological remission with periportal inflammatory activity less than 2. There is no evidence of decompensated liver cirrhosis, and she is a non-pregnant woman with no intention to become pregnant. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of chloroquine for the maintenance of remission of autoimmune hepatitis. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she is taking lisinopril 10mg daily. She has no history of significant ocular or neuromuscular disorders. Her family history is negative for liver disease. Her current medications include azathioprine, prednisone, and lisinopril. Her BMI is 25, and she is a non-smoker. She has an appointment in the ophthalmology department in two weeks for an initial ocular evaluation.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and underwent an allogeneic stem cell transplant from a matched-unrelated donor at the City of Hope National Medical Center. The patient is now 8 months post-transplant and is undergoing regular follow-up appointments with her hematologist. She has a history of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) affecting her skin and gut, which was managed with topical and oral medications. She has been compliant with her immunosuppressive medication regimen and has not experienced any GVHD flare-ups in the past 2 months. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial studying the effectiveness of the influenza vaccine in preventing flu in patients who have undergone stem cell transplant. She is willing to have nasopharyngeal washes performed every 2 weeks during the flu season and complete case report forms detailing any flu-like symptoms she experiences in the 2 weeks before sample collection. The patient is fully eligible for this trial, having undergone a stem cell transplant for the treatment of a hematological malignancy and being within the 100-365 days post-transplant time frame. The patient is also interested in contributing to medical research that could benefit other patients like herself.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing knee pain and stiffness for the past 9 months. She was diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis by her primary care physician, and her X-ray showed Kellgren Lawrence grade II. She has been taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief, which provide only temporary relief. The patient has a BMI of 28 and is generally in good health. She has no history of alcoholism, drug abuse or mental illness in the past 3 years, and no other unsuitable conditions that may affect her participation in the clinical trial. She has not undergone knee prosthesis or any other open surgery related to knee joint operation in the past 6 months. She has not received any other intra-articular injections, including hyaluronic acid, hormone, PRP, BMP, hypertonic glucose, or any other medication for KOA in the past 3 months preceding the trial. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial after signing the informed consent form and screening tests.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit with respiratory distress due to severe pneumonia. He required invasive mechanical ventilation delivered via an endotracheal tube and was expected to require ventilation for more than 24 hours. The intubation was performed in a unit where the specific endotracheal tube allowing subglottic secretions drainage (SSD) was available during the SSD period of the trial. The patient was able to provide informed consent and had social insurance. He was fluent in French and did not have any previous inclusion in the study. He was not pregnant, parturient or breastfeeding, and was not under guardianship or curators. The patient was not currently enrolled in any other clinical trial for VAP prevention.

A 32-year-old male patient, who has been enrolled in the University of Cincinnati Physicians Company-Opioid Treatment Program (UCPC-OTP) for the past year, presents with a smoking habit of more than 15 cigarettes per day. He is currently stable on his methadone dose for the past one week. He has tried to quit smoking in the past but has failed. He smokes the majority of his cigarettes within the first 4 hours of methadone dosing. He has no history of any psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, or any other psychiatric condition. He does not have any suicidal or homicidal tendencies, and his medical history is unremarkable. He is willing to comply with all study procedures, including trying to stop smoking during designated weeks, and to comply with medication instructions. He has not taken any investigational drugs in the past 30 days. He is not taking any concomitant medications that could increase the likelihood of smoking cessation. He has no known hypersensitivity to varenicline or the nicotine nasal spray (NNS). No history of electronic cigarette or tobacco products use in the past week. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He gives informed consent in English and agrees to use a reliable method of birth control if he is female and of childbearing potential.

A 62-year-old man noticed a slight tremor in his left hand about 12 months ago, which has progressively worsened. He also noticed that his left arm felt "heavier" than his right arm. He reports some difficulty buttoning his shirt and writing. He denies any slowness of movements or stiffness. He has no family history of Parkinson's disease or any other neurological disorders. He is a smoker and has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. On examination, he has a mild tremor in his left hand and mild bradykinesia in his left arm. He has no rigidity, postural instability or gait disturbance. His neurological examination is otherwise normal. Brain MRI was unremarkable except for mild age-related changes. The patient was diagnosed with possible Parkinson's disease by a general neurologist and started on levodopa/carbidopa. However, the patient did not notice any significant improvement in his symptoms after 6 months. Therefore, he was referred to a specialized movement disorders center for further evaluation.

A 32-year-old Caucasian male was involved in a traffic accident while driving his car. The patient was the only occupant of the car and was not wearing a seatbelt. He was brought to the hospital by ambulance 45 minutes after the accident. On arrival, he was found to have a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 8, indicating severe brain injury. The patient was intubated and transferred to the trauma center for further management. The initial CT scan showed a large subdural hematoma with midline shift. The patient underwent emergency craniotomy for hematoma evacuation and decompression. He was subsequently admitted to the intensive care unit for further management. The patient had a past medical history of hypertension and was taking Lisinopril. The patient was single and worked as a construction worker. He was a high school graduate and had no recent history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient was included in the study as a primary incident hospital admission due to traffic accidents.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking 1 pack per day for 20 years presents with dyspnea on exertion and dry cough for the past 6 months. He has lost 10 pounds unintentionally during this time. He has no history of lung disease or respiratory infections. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medications. He has no known family history of pulmonary fibrosis. His current medication list includes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He is retired and lives with his wife. He denies any recent travel or exposure to environmental toxins. His pulmonary function tests show a forced vital capacity (FVC) of 70% predicted and a carbon monoxide diffusing capacity (DLco) of 45% predicted. He is able to walk 250 meters in 6 minutes with oxygen saturation maintained at 93% on 3 L/min oxygen. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his condition.

The patient is a 45-year-old female from Canada with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 5 years. She has been on several medications, including methotrexate and sulfasalazine, but has not achieved adequate disease control. Her rheumatologist has recommended starting adalimumab as the first biological therapy. She has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. She is currently experiencing joint pain, swelling, and stiffness, with a DAS28-CRP score of 5.2. She has no scheduled surgeries during the follow-up period and has a life expectancy that exceeds the length of the study. She has no other diseases that could flare if adalimumab is tapered. Her current medications include methotrexate, folic acid, and naproxen. She has no known drug allergies or intolerances. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 66 year old woman, residing in Denmark and has not had a cervical cytology or screening invitation in the past 5 years. She has not undergone a hysterectomy and has not migrated to or from Denmark. She is generally in good health with no significant medical history. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about the HPV-based screening and self-sampling kit. She is able to understand and follow instructions and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including follow-up appointments and questionnaires.

The patient is a 30-year-old American woman who is overweight with a BMI of 30 kg/m2. She has regular menstrual cycles and is using hormonal contraception. She has a history of binge eating in the past but has not had any episodes in the last 6 months. She is currently taking Vit D3 supplements but no other medications or supplements. She exercises occasionally but not regularly, and has no plans to begin a strenuous exercise program in the next 4 months. She does not smoke, drink excessively, or use any illicit drugs. She has no significant dietary limitations or requirements. She has undergone no weight loss surgeries and has not gained or lost more than 3% of her current weight in the past 3 months. She has no current medical conditions or history of eating disorders, and has no current or past history of alcohol or substance abuse. She eats fish occasionally but not more than 2 times a week on average. She is interested in participating in the study and is able to understand the consent form and provide informed written consent.

The patient is a premature male infant born at 27 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 950 grams. He was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress at 24 hours of life. There is no family history of genetic or metabolic syndromes. The parents are willing to sign the consent form for their infant to participate in the study. The infant has no congenital malformations, surgical conditions, or pre-existing hypotension. The infant is expected to have a life expectancy beyond 24 hours. The infant will be closely monitored by the clinical team to ensure the safety and efficacy of the treatment.

The patient is a 16-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past six months. She reports feeling sad most of the day, every day, and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has difficulty sleeping and has lost her appetite, resulting in a weight loss of about 5 pounds over the last month. She denies any history of suicidal or homicidal ideation or behavior. She has no medical history of note and is not taking any medications. She has no family history of mood disorders, but her father has a history of alcohol abuse. She is currently in high school and is struggling to keep up with her schoolwork due to her lack of motivation and concentration. She has daily access to a cell phone and is comfortable with using text messaging. She speaks English fluently. She has not been diagnosed with any other psychiatric disorders, such as bipolar disorder or autism spectrum disorder, and does not have a history of substance abuse or conduct disorder. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help her learn new coping skills and manage her depression symptoms.

This clinical trial is seeking male and female participants aged 50 and older who are currently living in the town of Montana, Bulgaria. The trial aims to investigate the effects of increasing alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) intake by 2 or 4 grams per day on inflammatory markers linked to cardiovascular disease. The study uses a double-blinded placebo-controlled, randomized cross-over design, with participants consuming different combinations of healthy oils and ALA supplements or placebos over a 24-week period. Participants will be required to cook and eat foods prepared exclusively with the study oils and nothing else every day of the week at least 2 meals per day for 24 weeks. They must also be willing to eat no more than one meal per week prepared out of the home, take 4 or 8 capsules with ALA or placebo every day for 24 weeks, and provide personal and next of kin address and phone number for follow-up visits to the home. They must be able and willing to provide informed consent to be screened and to take part in the study. Exclusion criteria include a history of active or prior cardiovascular disease, cancer diagnosis or treatment in the past two years, chronic renal disease, any serious illness not otherwise specified that would interfere with participation, and taking certain medications or supplements that cannot be stopped.

Patient is an 11-year-old boy who sustained a fall onto his outstretched hand while playing football. He complains of tenderness and pain in his elbow, and upon examination, an undisplaced Mason type I radial head fracture is diagnosed. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient and their legal guardian are willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the use of a brace versus casting in the treatment of pediatric radial head fractures. The patient is able to express their pain level and perform daily activities.

A 45-year-old female patient with a history of recently diagnosed breast cancer is being considered for participation in this clinical trial. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently taking oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy. The patient has no history of major medical conditions, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She is experiencing mild anxiety related to her breast cancer diagnosis and upcoming surgery. She has been informed of the study and has provided informed consent to participate. Further evaluation will be conducted to determine her menstrual phase, and interleukin-1β and IL-6 levels will be measured to evaluate the effect of timing of breast surgery on systemic responses to trauma during different phases of her menstrual cycle.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation and is starting oral anticoagulation therapy for the first time. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medications for these conditions. The patient is fluent in Portuguese and has a phone. He has no visual or hearing impairments and is able to understand and answer questions. The patient has no history of cancer and has not started the Warfarin for surgical purposes.

The patient is a 25-year-old primigravida woman who is currently at 38 weeks and 4 days gestational age. She has not experienced any vaginal bleeding or regular contractions. She has a Bishop score of 4, indicating an unfavorable cervix for labor induction. She has been experiencing occasional mild cramping but nothing that is causing her significant discomfort. She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal checkups and has not experienced any medical issues during her pregnancy. She is a non-smoker and denies any alcohol or drug use. She is currently not taking any medications, including any over-the-counter medications. She is excited to meet her baby and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help improve the understanding of predicting successful induction of labor.

The patient is a 55 year old male who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 6 months ago. He is currently taking levodopa and carbidopa but has noticed that his symptoms are not well controlled. He experiences tremors in his right hand, stiffness in his legs, and has difficulty with balance. He has a Modified Hoehn & Yahr stage II and a UPDRS motor score (part III) of 12. He has no history of surgery for the treatment of PD and has not experienced dyskinesias, motor fluctuations, or loss of postural reflexes. He has never taken pramipexole or SLV308 before. He is a retired teacher and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren. He is eager to participate in this clinical trial to potentially improve his symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 57-year-old male diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis. The patient underwent bone marrow biopsy which revealed a mutation in CALR exon 9. The patient has no other significant past medical history and his performance status is at ECOG-scale 2. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 3 months and has sufficient bone marrow function, with leucocyte count at 2.5 x 10^9/L, granulocyte count at 1.8 x 10^9/L, thrombocyte count at 50 x 10^9/L, and hemoglobin level at 12.5 g/dL. The patient's creatinine level is within normal limits at 60 µmol/L and liver function tests indicate normal levels of alanine aminotransferase and bilirubin. The patient is willing to use contraceptive methods with a failure rate of less than 1% per year during the treatment period and for at least 120 days after the last treatment. The patient has not had any other malignancies and has not had any significant medical conditions that could affect his compliance. The patient is not taking immune suppressive medications or other experimental drugs and has not received chemotherapy or immune therapy within the last 28 days. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive the CALR Exon 9 mutant peptide vaccine.

A 47-year-old female presented with persistent headaches, difficulty swallowing, and a lump in her neck that had been present for several weeks. She reported feeling fatigued and having a decreased appetite. She had no significant medical history and denied any tobacco or alcohol use. Imaging studies revealed a large mass in the nasopharynx with extension into the parapharyngeal space and bilateral cervical adenopathy. Biopsy confirmed the presence of non-keratinizing nasopharyngeal carcinoma, WHO type III. Her tumor was staged as T2N2M0 (AJCC 8th edition). She was eligible for the clinical trial comparing GP vs PF as induction chemotherapy combined with concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma. She met all the inclusion criteria, including adequate hematologic and renal function, a satisfactory performance status, and no prior treatment for NPC. She provided informed consent to participate in the trial. She was randomly assigned to receive either GP (gemcitabine and cisplatin) or PF (cisplatin and fluorouracil) as induction chemotherapy combined with concurrent chemoradiotherapy. She underwent radical radiotherapy and received cisplatin every three weeks for two cycles during radiotherapy. She received gemcitabine and cisplatin every three weeks for three cycles in the investigational arm.

Pt is a 16yo M who was recently diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. He has a positive diabetes autoantibody test and has been referred to an endocrinologist for routine diabetic care. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of efalizumab in protecting his remaining beta cells. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is committed to following the study protocol for the 2-year duration. He is currently not on any immunosuppressive medications and is negative for HIV, Hepatitis B or C, and has no history of organ or bone marrow transplantation, sickle cell disease, cystic fibrosis, autoimmune anemia, seizures, autoimmune thrombocytopenia, leuko/lymphopenia, vasculitis, or other autoimmune diseases. He is not pregnant or planning a pregnancy during the study period.

The patient is a 14-year-old adolescent who has recently been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. The patient has not received any antiretroviral treatment before, and the plasma HIV-1 RNA level is ≥ 1,000 copies/mL. The CD4+ cell count is > 100 cells/µL. The patient weighs more than 35 kg (77 lbs) and is able to swallow oral tablets. The patient has adequate renal function, clinically normal ECG, and hepatic transaminases ≤ 5 x upper limit of normal. The patient's genotype report shows sensitivity to FTC and TDF. The patient has no active pulmonary tuberculosis, and the screening for active pulmonary tuberculosis was performed within 6 months of the screening visit. The patient has adequate hematologic function, and the serum pregnancy test is negative for all females. The patient is willing to comply with all study requirements and has a life expectancy of ≥ 1 year. The patient has no serious or active medical or psychiatric illness that would interfere with treatment, assessment, or compliance with the protocol. The patient has no history of malignancy within the past 5 years or ongoing malignancy other than cutaneous Kaposi's sarcoma, basal cell carcinoma, or resected, non-invasive cutaneous squamous carcinoma. The patient has not participated in any investigational trial involving administration of any investigational agent within 30 days prior to the study dosing. The patient is not receiving ongoing therapy with any disallowed medications, including drugs not to be used with EVG, COBI, FTC, TDF or individuals with any known allergies to the excipients of EVG/COBI/FTC/TDF STR tablets.

Sarah is a 57 year old woman who suffered an acute ischemic stroke 8 months ago. She received intensive physical therapy and supportive care but did not show any improvement beyond the initial 90-day period. She still experiences residual left arm weakness and has difficulty with grasping and holding objects. She is a non-smoker and has no history of seizures. Her medical history includes hypertension, for which she takes medication regularly, and hypothyroidism, which is managed with hormone replacement therapy. She has no history of claustrophobia or emphysema. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her motor function and quality of life.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman recently diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She has no history of prior radiation therapy to the affected area and has not received any treatment that may affect this treatment for at least 4 weeks. Her ECOG Performance Status is 1, and she is expected to survive for at least 90 days. The patient has no active or persistent infectious disease within the irradiated area and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has well-functioning main organs and does not have any serious complications. The patient does not have any electronic devices in her body that could be affected by radiation therapy. She is willing and able to cooperate with the treatment requirements and maintain the gestures required during the irradiation process. The patient is between 20-75 years old and meets all the inclusion criteria for the early-phase safety of proton therapy equipment clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old Hebrew-speaking male with no history of neurological or psychiatric diagnoses. He has intact vision and comprehension. He is interested in participating in a study examining the effect of hyperbaric oxygen treatments (HBOT) on cognitive abilities. He has no chest pathology, inner ear disease, or claustrophobia. He is a non-smoker and does not use stimulants for attention disorders. He is willing to undergo a comprehensive physical and neurological examination prior to participation. The patient is seeking to improve his cognitive abilities and is willing to participate in a randomized study where he will be placed in either a HBOT condition (2 ATA 100% oxygen for 90 minutes) or control condition (1 ATA for 90 minutes breathing air). The patient is highly motivated to participate and willing to undergo the testing battery in a group setting.

32 yo F diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) 2 years ago, currently receiving intermittent treatment with interferon beta-1a. Patient reports experiencing occasional relapses characterized by increased fatigue, weakness, and vision problems. Patient is independently ambulatory with occasional use of a cane for balance support. Patient is able to use a mobile application and has no history of substance or alcohol abuse. No recent changes in medication or symptomatic treatment. Patient is enrolled in a Social Security program and has signed the informed consent form. No evidence of neurologic or psychiatric disorder other than MS. No history of inflammatory disease or major head trauma. Patient has no hearing aids or vision issues that may affect test performance. Patient is able to use both hands for the Coordination test (MCT).

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history or medications. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. He occasionally drinks alcohol but has not consumed more than 7 drinks per week. He has a BMI of 24 kg/m2. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last 30 days and is not currently participating in any. He has no history of exposure to radiation ≥ 15 mSv/year or any clinically significant chronic disease. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or substance abuse. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and visit schedules, and is able to follow verbal and written instructions. He is able to stay within the residential facility for the required period and attend up to 3 additional outpatient visits. He is willing to refrain from strenuous activity during the course of the study. He has no history of blood loss or donation within 60 days prior to signing informed consent and does not intend to donate blood or plasma or undergo elective surgery during the study participation or within 60 days after the last study visit. He has no history of malabsorption, previous gastrointestinal surgery, or clinically significant abnormality of the hepatic or renal system. He has no clinically significant abnormal 12-lead ECG that may jeopardize his ability to complete the study. He is able to provide written informed consent prior to participation in the study.

57-year-old woman recently diagnosed with stage II colon cancer with a recommended treatment plan that includes chemotherapy. She is fluent in English and has access to the internet through her smartphone. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or any unmedicated mental or psychiatric disorder. She does not have any debilitating medical disorders like progressive muscle paralysis, advanced cardiac, respiratory, or renal disease, or AIDS. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand her treatment plan and improve her participation in her care.

A 25-year-old female athlete presents to the clinic with a recent history of ankle sprain. She experienced the injury during a football match, which caused her discomfort and pain in the ankle joint. She has been advised by her coach to seek medical assistance before the condition worsens. The physical examination revealed a grade II inversion sprain of the ankle. The patient has no history of previous trauma or orthopedic disorders, and she does not have any systemic diseases. She has been referred to the LED (627 +/- 10 nm) therapy trial for the treatment of her ankle sprain. She is an active individual who is looking forward to participating in the study to reduce her pain and swelling.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of diabetes for 5 years presents to the clinic with complaints of high blood sugar levels despite treatment with an intermediate-acting insulin and insulin aspart. She is currently on a basal-bolus regimen for the past 20 weeks. Her HbA1C level is 9.5%. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of insulin detemir on blood glucose control in subjects with insulin requiring diabetes. She has normal renal and hepatic function and no history of serious heart diseases. She does not have hypoglycemia unawareness or recurrent major hypoglycemia. She does not have any proliferative retinopathy or maculopathy requiring acute treatment. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication. She is currently on a total insulin dose of 60 IU/day. She is not on any systemic corticosteroids. She has given her informed consent to participate in the trial.

Patient A is a 45-year-old woman who tested positive for COVID-19 three months ago. She has noticed a decreased sense of smell since then and has difficulty identifying smells. She has no history of olfactory disorder before COVID-19 infection. She is currently taking no medication and has no other significant medical history. She is fluent in English and able to read and write. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of tuberculosis or herpes infection. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help with her anosmia recovery.

A 46-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago. She had undergone a lumpectomy, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. One year later, she was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer, which was HER2-positive. She underwent treatment with trastuzumab and a taxane, followed by lapatinib. Despite these treatments, her cancer continued to progress. She is currently experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, loss of appetite, and new bone pain. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1 and her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 55%. She has not received any chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy in the past 21 days, and has not been previously enrolled in a trastuzumab emtansine containing study. She does not have any untreated or symptomatic brain metastases and does not require radiation, surgery, or corticosteroid therapy to control symptoms within 1 month of randomization.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was recently hospitalized for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). She has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. She is postmenopausal and has been on hormone replacement therapy for the past 10 years. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and is a former smoker. She has no history of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) and is scheduled to undergo invasive coronary angiography. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

Linda is a 25-year-old female who came to the dental clinic with severe tooth pain. She had trouble sleeping at night and eating due to the pain. She had a history of dental caries, and her dentist confirmed that she needed root canal therapy for her maxillary second molar. She was experiencing pain to cold and biting, indicating symptomatic irreversible pulpitis and symptomatic apical periodontitis. Linda is an otherwise healthy individual with no known allergies to ibuprofen or acetaminophen. She is not pregnant and is able to give informed consent. Her American Society of Anesthesiologist classification is I. She has never undergone anesthesia before. She works as a teacher and is looking for a pain management option that doesn't interfere with her daily activities.

A 28-year-old male was brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. On arrival, he had a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 7 and was intubated for airway protection. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the head showed evidence of moderate to severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) with multiple intracranial hemorrhages and a midline shift. The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) and was monitored for intracranial pressure (ICP) and arterial pressure.
