He met the inclusion criteria for the Multicenter Italian INCEPT study, which aims to investigate the impact of postraumatic cerebral ischemia (PTCI) on disability at hospital discharge and on 6-month morbidity and mortality in a population of moderate and severe adult TBI patients. The patient's age and severity of TBI fit the inclusion criteria for the study, and he was monitored with invasive ICP and arterial pressure monitoring as required by the study protocol. The patient's family provided informed consent for his participation in the study.

A 12-year-old girl was recently diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus after presenting with symptoms of polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss. She has no family history of diabetes and is the only one in her family diagnosed with the condition. Her HbA1c level was 9.5% at diagnosis, and she has been on daily insulin therapy for 6 months. She has no known allergies and is in good health otherwise. She has not participated in any clinical trials before and is willing to participate in this trial.

This clinical trial is looking for patients who have undergone a radical cystectomy for stage III or stage IV transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder urothelium. The patient must be histologically confirmed to have transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder urothelium, no pure squamous cell or adenocarcinoma tumors, and no evidence of microscopic residual disease. The patient must have a performance status of WHO 0-1, WBC at least 3,500/mm^3, platelet count at least 120,000/mm^3, SGOT/SGPT less than 2.5 times upper limit of normal (ULN), alkaline phosphatase less than 2.5 times ULN, bilirubin normal, glomerular filtration rate greater than 60 mL/min, and no clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia or congestive heart failure. The patient must not have any clinically abnormal auditory function, grade 2 or greater peripheral neuropathy, or known hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived drug preparations. The patient must not have any other prior or concurrent malignancy except adequately treated carcinoma in situ of the cervix, treated basal cell skin cancer, or treated incidental prostate cancer (pT2, Gleason score no greater than 6, and PSA less than 0.5 ng/mL). Patients who have had prior systemic chemotherapy or radiotherapy to the bladder are not eligible. The patient must be considered fit for cisplatin-containing combination chemotherapy. The patient must not be pregnant or nursing, and fertile patients must use effective contraception during and for 6 months after the study. Any psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical condition that would preclude study involvement is not allowed.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of osteoporosis came to the clinic for a routine check-up. She has been experiencing back pain and decreased height over the past year. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol and is currently taking medications for both. She does not smoke, but she consumes a mostly vegetarian diet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to learn more about how vitamin K may impact bone health. She has not taken any osteoporosis medications in the past 3 months and has not used acid reducers more than twice a week. She does not have any kidney, gastrointestinal, or liver disease requiring treatment and does not have a blood clotting disorder or abnormal clotting time. She has not used warfarin or anticoagulant medication in the past 12 months and is not currently pregnant or using oral contraceptives. She is willing to adhere to a controlled diet plan for the duration of the study.

Patient is a 12-year-old boy from the United States who was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes a year ago. He is currently on multiple daily insulin injections, including basal long-acting insulin and rapid-acting insulin before each meal. His most recent HbA1c level was 7.8%. He has no food allergies or untreated coeliac disease. He is not a vegetarian or vegan and does not have any religious dietary restrictions. His parents have a freezer to store the test meals. He is willing to comply with all requirements of the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of smoking for over 30 years. He has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is currently taking medication for it. He experiences shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue. He has not taken Advair for at least four weeks prior to screening. He has no history of myocardial infarction or stroke, but has hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of kidney disease or liver disease. He is not pregnant or lactating. He is able to understand instructions and hold still for approximately 10 seconds. He has no contraindications to MR scanning. He is willing to participate in the study and will be categorized according to the GOLD COPD severity classification.

A 54-year-old man with a history of ischaemic cardiomyopathy and no prior cardiac surgery or acute coronary syndrome is eligible for this clinical trial. He has been experiencing occasional palpitations and shortness of breath during physical exercise. He currently takes medications for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has no history of arrhythmia or sudden cardiac death in his family. He is able to give informed consent for the study.

A 10-year-old boy with a history of ITP presents to the clinic with a low platelet count of 15 x 10^9/L. The patient is otherwise healthy with no history of bleeding episodes. The treating physician has suggested IVIG as a treatment option to raise the platelet count. The patient and family have agreed to participate in a clinical trial comparing IVIG alone to IVIG with corticosteroids. The patient has no history of splenectomy or organ-threatening hemorrhage, and there are no contraindications to IVIG or corticosteroids. The patient has not failed to attain a platelet count above 50 x 10^9/L with prior treatment and has no co-existing situations that could affect platelet response to therapy. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures, including platelet count monitoring and completion of questionnaires.

A 9-year-old boy named Alex has been experiencing stomach pain and discomfort for several weeks. His parents brought him to the pediatric gastroenterologist for evaluation. The doctor recommended performing a pediatric endoscopy to further investigate the issue. Alex and his parents were informed about the procedure, its benefits, risks, and alternatives. However, they expressed concerns about understanding the information and the process. Therefore, the doctor offered them the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve their comprehension of the informed consent process by using a video intervention. Alex and his parents consented to participate in the study and were randomized into the intervention group. They were provided with a video explaining the procedure and its risks and benefits, followed by a discussion with the doctor to ensure their understanding. Alex is an English-speaking child who is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history.

A 56-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and coronary artery disease is scheduled for an elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. The patient's BMI is within normal limits at 25.5. The patient has not had any prior surgeries and has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. The patient is willing to participate in a prospective observational study to assess microcirculation of the thenar eminence using NIRS technology and its correlation with length of stay in the intensive care unit and organ dysfunction. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent for participation.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male with a history of HIV infection for the past 5 years. He has not started any antiretroviral therapy yet. He reported to have been noticing skin lesions for the past few months and has been experiencing shortness of breath and abdominal pain for the past few weeks. He was diagnosed with disseminated Kaposi sarcoma (KS) after a skin biopsy and imaging studies showed pulmonary and gastrointestinal involvement. His CD4 count is less than 100 cells/mm3. He has no history of other cancers or hepatitis B or C. He is not currently receiving corticosteroids. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent document. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study as he has AIDS and disseminated KS.

The patient is a 62 year old woman with a diagnosis of type II diabetes. She experiences moderate risk of foot ulceration as defined by detection in less than 8/10 sites on the plantar aspect of the foot using a 10 g monofilament and foot deformity defined and graded using a foot deformity score previously developed for people with diabetes. She has also been diagnosed with peripheral neuropathy as defined by the ability to detect a 10g monofilament at 5 sites per foot on the plantar aspect of the toes and metatarsophalangeal joints. She has no feeling in less than 8 sites indicating increased risk of foot ulceration. She has limited ankle dorsiflexion and hallux joint stiffness. She is able to walk for 10 meters with or without using a walking aid and attend 6 sessions over a 6 week period. She is over 18 years of age and is not experiencing any of the exclusion criteria such as plantar ulceration, rheumatoid arthritis, ankle and 1st MTP osteoarthritis or Dupuytren's contractures. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess whether ankle and big toe joint mobilisations and home program of stretches in people with diabetic peripheral neuropathy can improve joint range of motion and reduce forefoot peak pressures.

The patient is a healthy adult aged between 18 to 50 years, who is willing to participate in a clinical trial for a new Ebola vaccine. They must be able to comply with all study requirements and provide written informed consent. Females must be willing to practice continuous effective contraception during the study and have a negative pregnancy test on the day(s) of screening and vaccination. The patient must not have participated in another research study involving receipt of an investigational product in the 30 days preceding enrolment or plan to participate during the study period. They must not have received any live, attenuated vaccine within 28 days prior to enrolment or any subunit or killed vaccine within 14 days prior to enrolment. The patient must not have any confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immunodeficient state, including HIV infection; asplenia; recurrent, severe infections and chronic (more than 14 days) immunosuppressant medication within the past 6 months. They must not have any history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine or any history of hereditary angioedema, acquired angioedema, or idiopathic angioedema. The patient must not have any history of anaphylaxis in reaction to vaccination or any history of cancer (except basal cell carcinoma of the skin and cervical carcinoma in situ). They must not have any current or previous psychiatric illness, poorly controlled asthma or thyroid disease, seizure in the past 3 years or treatment for seizure disorder in the past 3 years. The patient must not have a bleeding disorder (e.g. Factor deficiency, coagulopathy or platelet disorder) or any other serious chronic illness. They must not be currently on anti-tuberculosis prophylaxis or therapy, suspected or known current alcohol abuse as defined by an alcohol intake of greater than 42 units every week or suspected or known injecting drug abuse in the 5 years preceding enrolment. The patient must not be seropositive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), have a history of contact with suspected, probable or confirmed cases of Ebola in the previous 21 days or any clinically significant abnormal finding on screening biochemistry or haematology blood tests or urinalysis.

The patient is a 20-year-old female undergraduate student of Obafemi Awolowo University who has been experiencing primary dysmenorrhea for at least five days during her menstrual cycle. She reports that her menstrual cramps are often severe and are accompanied by lower abdominal pain, back pain, and bloating. The patient is currently single and has no history of conception. She has not been using any analgesia for pain relief during her menstrual cycle. She has no known history of pelvic diseases or cardiac problems. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy of Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) on pain intensity associated with primary dysmenorrhoea.

This is a 9-year-old girl with a history of atrial septal defect (ASD) diagnosed at birth. She has been closely monitored by her pediatric cardiologist and it has been determined that she is a suitable candidate for percutaneous ASD closure. The diameter of her defect is 6 mm and there is an increasing volume load on her right heart. The distance between the defective edge and the coronary venous sinus, inferior caval vein, superior vena cava, and pulmonary vein is greater than 5 mm and the distance between the atrial-ventricular valve is greater than 7 mm. There are no other cardiac anomalies that require surgical intervention. She has not been diagnosed with hypertension, coronary artery disease, or diabetes. She is not taking any medications for atrial fibrillation or oral contraceptives. She has not taken Aspro, clopidogrel, or warfarin in the past 2 weeks. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help evaluate blood clotting after percutaneous ASD closure and to explore optimal anticoagulation plans.

54-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with a sudden onset of left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. He was diagnosed with acute ischemic stroke in the anterior circulation and is currently being managed with intravenous thrombolytic therapy. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. His baseline mRS score is 0, and his NIHSS score at screening is 8. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. MRI confirms the absence of any new ischemic lesion in the cerebellum or brainstem, and his infarct area is localized. He has not experienced any seizures after the onset of ischemic stroke and has no medical history of neurological event such as stroke or head trauma within the past 180 days. He does not have poor blood pressure or glycaemic control, and he has no severe liver, kidney, heart, or pulmonary dysfunction. He does not have any severe infections or complications that would affect his ability to participate in the study. He has no history of malignant tumors or allergy to products derived from human tissues, bovine or porcine, or streptomycin. He has not undergone splenectomy in the past and is not scheduled to undergo any revascularization procedures.

A 29-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for a year is interested in participating in a clinical trial to aid in fertility assessment. She has a regular menstrual cycle and both ovaries present. She has no history of PCOS or ovarian endometrioma and has not undergone ovarian surgery. She is not currently pregnant and has not used hormonal contraceptives prior to enrollment. She is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all protocol requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired accountant who has been experiencing worsening knee pain for the past 5 years. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of both knees and has tried various conservative treatments without much improvement. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His BMI is 32. He has undergone a few surgeries in the past, including a hernia repair and a cholecystectomy. His current medications include losartan for hypertension, aspirin for cardiovascular prophylaxis, and occasional acetaminophen for pain relief. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo simultaneous bilateral total knee arthroplasty. The patient has normal preoperative laboratory values and does not have any known allergies or contraindications to tranexamic acid.

25yo female with moderate to severe inflammatory acne on her face and back, with a history of unsuccessful treatment with topical anti-acne medication. She presents with 30-40 facial inflammatory lesions (papules, pustules, and nodules) and 15 non-inflammatory facial lesions (open and closed comedones) at baseline. The patient is not currently taking any oral/systemic treatment for acne and has not received any systemic or lesional injected corticosteroids or systemic immunomodulators in the past 4 weeks. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use contraception during dosing of study treatment, if sexually active.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with a fasting serum triglyceride level of 200 mg/dL and a fasting LDL-C level of 130 mg/dL. He is of African American ethnicity and has no known chronic medical conditions or history of seizures. He is not incarcerated or institutionalized and is not planning any pregnancies during the study. He has no known metabolic disorders that require carnitine therapy. He has never participated in any other clinical trial before. He is willing to adhere to the study protocol during the run-in phase and is committed to completing the full 6-month trial.

The patient is a 20-year-old male who was diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) six months ago. He had initially undergone chemotherapy with fludarabine, cytarabine and G-CSF (FLAG), but unfortunately, he has relapsed. His current disease is refractory, and he has not responded to any other treatment. The patient has a performance level of Karnofsky >50%. He has no history of DNA fragility syndromes or Down syndrome. The patient has no known allergies to any of the drugs used in the study. He has adequate renal and hepatic functions. He is not currently receiving any other investigational drugs. He does not have any significant concurrent disease or illness that would compromise patient safety or compliance. The patient is willing to use an effective method of contraception approved by the investigator during the study and for a minimum of 6 months after study treatment. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) three months ago. She has already received two lines of treatment and now her oncologist plans to prescribe regorafenib as the third-line therapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score of 1 and no other significant medical history. She has measurable disease according to RECIST criteria version 1.1. Her organ and bone marrow functions are adequate, with total bilirubin, ALT, AST, ALP, amylase, lipase, creatinine, GFR, INR/PTT, platelet counts, hemoglobin level, and absolute neutrophil counts all within normal limits. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study. She is willing to use adequate contraception measures since informed consent until at least 12 weeks after the last study drug administration. She understands the study requirements and is willing to sign the written Informed Consent Form (ICF). The patient has not received regorafenib within the last 28 days and has not participated in any investigational drug study within the last four weeks. She has no concurrent cancer or prior treatment for other carcinomas within the last five years, except curatively treated non-melanoma skin cancer, superficial bladder tumors, and cervical cancer in-situ. She has not received extended field radiotherapy within 28 days or limited radiotherapy within 14 days prior to randomization. She has not undergone major surgery within 28 days prior to the start of study treatment. She has no uncontrolled intercurrent illness or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction in the past 12 months, active gastrointestinal bleeding, central nervous system disorders, psychiatric illness, or social situation that would limit compliance with study requirements. She has no history of myocardial infarction, deep venous or arterial thrombosis, or cardiovascular accident (CVA) during the last six months. She has no uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmias, unstable angina, or newly-onset angina within three months prior to study entry. Her blood pressure is controlled with medication. She has no known central nervous system (CNS) metastases. She is able to take oral medications and is compliant with her treatments.

This clinical trial is seeking children between the ages of 8 and 18 who are being treated for a chronic disease at the multidisciplinary paediatrics department of the Timone Hospital. The patient should have been receiving treatment for their chronic disease for at least three months and require at least two hospital consultations per year. The patient should be able to complete the questionnaire and speak French. The patient and their parents must provide consent to participate in the study. Patients with intellectual disabilities or a low proficiency in French, as well as patients without social security coverage, will be excluded from the study. This trial aims to study the effects of short stature on the quality of life of children with chronic diseases, as well as the quality of life of their parents and siblings.

This is a 58-year-old male with a history of locally-advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) of the oropharynx. He was diagnosed with stage IV HNSCC without distant metastases and underwent surgery to remove the tumor. He is now eligible for adjuvant radiochemotherapy and has no contraindications for PET/MRI or radiochemotherapy. His ECOG performance status is 0/2 and he has provided informed consent. He has not had any previous PET/CT scans, induction therapy, or secondary malignancies that might influence the outcome of the radiochemotherapy. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 30-year-old Greek woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has a history of hypertension but is currently well-controlled with medication. She has no previous history of cesarean section, and her pregnancy has progressed normally with no complications. She plans to deliver at one of the 22 participating maternity units in Greece, where she will be randomly assigned to either the intervention or control group. She has provided informed consent to participate in the trial and is willing to follow the obstetricians' recommendations for labor management. She is excited to be a part of this trial, which aims to reduce the rates of unnecessary cesarean sections in Greece and improve the safety of childbirth for both mothers and babies.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as the study is focused on evaluating the effect of an automaton on the dosimetry of operators who prepare radiopharmaceuticals in nuclear medicine departments. It aims to reduce the exposure of operators to radiation during the preparation of radiopharmaceuticals and improve the precision of prepared syringes. The eligibility criteria involve operators, specifically Technologists in Medical Electro-Radiology or/and Pharmacy Technicians, who are experienced and autonomous in labelling radiopharmaceuticals with technetium-99m and have agreed to participate in the study.

65-year-old Caucasian male, retired, with no known ocular disease or diabetes, presents for participation in the Northern Ireland Sensory Ageing Study. He is cognitively intact and has no history of cognitive impairment. He has normal blood pressure, no history of smoking, and exercises moderately. He wears glasses for mild myopia and has never had any ocular surgeries. He has no known allergies to medications or substances. He is interested in participating to help advance knowledge on aging and visual function.

A 32-year-old woman was diagnosed with infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the left breast. She underwent a biopsy after presenting with a palpable mass in her breast. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma. Further workup, including a mammogram, ultrasound, and MRI, showed no evidence of metastasis. The patient was referred to an oncologist, who recommended neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction and adjuvant radiotherapy. The patient has no significant past medical history, and she is a non-smoker. She has no known drug allergies. The patient has a good performance status with a WHO score of 0. She has a stable social situation and is affiliated with the Social Security System. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.

A 25-year-old healthy female who is not pregnant and currently practicing an approved contraceptive regimen is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new drug. She has no significant medical history or chronic illnesses, and her laboratory values are within normal limits. She has not had any major surgeries within the past 90 days and has not participated in any other investigational drug studies within the past 60 days. She does not have a history of illicit drug use or chronic alcohol dependence within the past 2 years. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and is available to participate in the study as scheduled by the trial investigators.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who underwent surgery for nerve reconstruction after a traumatic injury to his left arm. Despite the surgery, the patient has been experiencing persistent pain, numbness, and decreased range of motion. The patient has undergone physical therapy and medication management, but has not seen any significant improvement. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of chronic diseases or substance abuse. The patient is a Polish citizen and is willing to participate in the study. Prior to the surgery, the patient's INR will be checked to ensure it is not above 2.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in his first remission 6 months ago. He has no significant past medical history and has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past 3 months. He has a matched unrelated donor (9/10) and has given informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. He has no active infection and no known allergies to Flu/Bu/CTX. His liver and renal function tests are within normal limits. He is mentally stable and able to understand and sign the informed consent. The patient is scheduled to receive intravenous Busulfan (iv-Bu) 1.6mg/kg twice daily for 4 days as part of the conditioning regimen for allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Blood samples will be obtained after the first and seventh dose of iv Busulfan for pharmacokinetic analysis.

A 43-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes was admitted to the hospital after a car accident. He suffered multiple injuries, including a head injury, and was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) for further management. The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated due to respiratory failure. He was also started on vasopressors to maintain blood pressure. The ABCDE protocol will be implemented in his care plan to prevent the development of delirium, provide early mobility, and improve outcomes. The patient's legally authorized representative will be available to provide consent to participate in the trial within 48 hours of ICU admission.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy with axillary lymph node dissection and the pathology report showed invasive ductal carcinoma with lymph node metastasis. The patient underwent adjuvant chemotherapy with a regimen of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide and is currently receiving adjuvant radiation therapy to the breast and lymph nodes. During a routine follow-up MRI, a brain lesion was detected. The patient is experiencing mild headaches and dizziness. The MRI showed a single metastatic lesion in the left parietal lobe with a maximum diameter of 3 cm. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient is currently taking tamoxifen as part of her adjuvant treatment plan. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has not received any investigational agents in the past 5 half-lives. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the use of TPI 287 in combination with Fractionated Stereotactic Radiotherapy (FSRT) to treat her brain metastasis.

63 year-old man with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed 2 years ago. He has undergone androgen deprivation therapy and has recently progressed to hormone-refractory prostate cancer (HRPC) as evidenced by an increase in PSA over the past few months. He has a PSA level of 18 ng/mL and testosterone level less than 50 ng/dL. He was previously treated with docetaxel-based chemotherapy for 8 weeks and has had no prior treatment with more than one chemotherapy regimen. He has evidence of metastatic disease in the bone as confirmed by a positive bone scan. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and meets the lab values for the study. He has recovered from any significant toxicities from his prior treatment and has no concurrent illnesses that would preclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who underwent surgery for rectal cancer with ileostomy formation 9 months ago. He has been living with the ileostomy since then and is now interested in having it closed. He has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification of 2 and has no history of bleeding disorders or insulin-treated diabetes. His pre-operative investigation did not show any anastomotic leakage or stricture. He has an adult supervision at home for the first 24 hours after discharge and has given informed written consent for the study. He has a phone and is able to manage himself at home post-operatively. He is mobilized and able to maintain per oral nutrition. He has obtained oral and written information about symptoms of sepsis and bowel obstruction and has obtained the telephone number of a contact-nurse. He meets all the eligibility criteria and is a suitable candidate for the day-case closure of ileostomy in rectal cancer clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been referred to the clinic for a hand-held screening ultrasound examination due to a lump in her left breast. She has no prior history of breast cancer or any other significant medical history. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She has no family history of breast cancer. She doesn't smoke or use any drugs. She is currently not taking any medications. She is 165 cm tall and weighs 68 kg. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg and her heart rate is 75 beats per minute. She reports occasional breast tenderness and swelling during her menstrual cycle. Her breast tissue is dense according to the mammogram report. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of automated breast ultrasound in detecting breast lesions.

A 10-year-old boy came to the clinic with a red, painful bump on his leg that has been growing for the past three days. He has no underlying disease and is not on any medication. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He lives with his parents and three siblings. He attends school and plays on a soccer team. He has not been hospitalized in the last 14 days and has not used mupirocin, clorhexidine, or bleach water baths in the last month. His culture test from his previous skin abscess was positive for MRSA.

Patient is a 64-year-old man from the United States who has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He has undergone coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in the past and is currently on medication for his conditions. He has recently experienced some discomfort and pain in his legs when walking a short distance. He visited his physician, who recommended a vascular repair or reconstruction surgery that necessitates the use of a patch. The patient has been informed about the study and is willing to participate. He is in good physical condition and has no known allergies. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol and follow-up period and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who is currently pregnant and scheduled for vaginal delivery. She has a history of uncomplicated pregnancies and has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. Her current pregnancy has been monitored regularly and there have been no complications so far. She has expressed a desire for pain relief during labor and is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing continuous versus intermittent epidural analgesia. She has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of both methods and has provided informed consent. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 43-year-old woman with a BMI of 43.5 kg/m2 has struggled with obesity for most of her adult life. She has tried various diets and exercise programs but has been unable to sustain significant weight loss. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. She was recently diagnosed with prediabetes and has been advised to consider bariatric surgery to help manage her weight and blood sugar levels. She has been referred to the Center for the Surgical Treatment of Obesity at the University of Chicago and has met the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial. She is interested in participating in the study to help researchers understand more about the metabolic effects of bariatric surgery. She has no known systemic illnesses, is not currently pregnant or lactating, and has not donated blood or participated in another clinical study in the last 4 weeks. She has signed the informed consent form and is excited to be part of this study.

This is a 50 year-old female who was diagnosed with early stage glaucoma after a routine eye exam showed optic disc changes consistent with the disease. She has no other ocular diseases and her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She has not undergone any ocular surgeries or experienced any ocular traumas. She has no significant medical history, but has a family history of glaucoma. She is currently not taking any ocular or systemic hypotensive medications. She is able to understand the instructions and perform the tests required for the study, and is willing to comply with the study schedule and treatment. She has signed informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35 year old male who has been experiencing recurring abdominal pain, nausea, and bloating for the past few months. He has also noticed a loss of appetite and occasional heartburn. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle, spending most of his time behind a desk. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medication. He has never undergone any gastrointestinal surgery and has no history of malignancy. He consumes a regular diet that includes spicy and oily food, and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not taken any antibiotics or antacids in the past three months. He is married and has two children. He is willing to receive treatment for his symptoms and has given informed consent to participate in the study. He is not currently pregnant or nursing and is not planning to conceive during the study period. He has no history of substance abuse and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer and scheduled for modified radical mastectomy surgery. She is in good general health with no known allergies to opioids or NSAIDs. She weighs 65 kg and has an ASA physical status of II. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She reports occasional headaches but is not currently taking any medications. She understands the use of the visual analogue scale (VAS) to evaluate her pain intensity. She has no history of gastric or duodenal ulcers, and has not received any blood transfusions or preoperative NSAIDs, steroid or opioid medications 48 hours prior to the operation. She understands the purpose of the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who works as a housekeeper in a hotel. She has been experiencing respiratory symptoms, such as coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, for the past six months. She has never smoked and has no history of allergies or asthma. She has previously sought medical attention for her symptoms but has not received a clear diagnosis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to better understand the potential link between her workplace and her respiratory symptoms. She is willing to undergo nasal swab collection and answer questionnaires. She has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to sign it.

A 52-year-old male patient comes to the clinic complaining of upper abdominal discomfort that started few weeks ago. He reports that the pain is mostly present after meals and is associated with bloating and nausea. The patient also reports that he has noticed a lump in his upper abdomen that seems to be getting bigger over time. He has no history of gastric or duodenal ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding or any other gastrointestinal conditions. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. Physical examination reveals an upper abdominal mass. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) shows a subepithelial tumor in the stomach measuring approximately 2.5 cm in diameter. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the derivative study and is offered to participate in the clinical trial for Endoscopic Ultrasound-guided Needle-based Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy for Diagnosis of Gastric Subepithelial Tumors.

A 35-year-old sexually active woman visited the clinic with complaints of chronic pelvic pain for more than 6 months. She reports pain during sexual intercourse and has been avoiding it. She has been previously diagnosed with non-cyclic chronic pelvic pain and has tried various medications and therapies, but the pain persists. She is not pregnant and not trying to conceive. She doesn't have any active infection and is neurologically intact. She is willing to use an intravaginal electrical stimulation device and has no history of any implanted neuro-modulatory devices. She is not currently undergoing pelvic floor physical therapy and has no active malignancy.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who suffered a stroke 6 months ago. He has a lower limb motor impairment and has difficulty walking without assistance. He is able to walk with a cane for short distances. He is currently undergoing rehabilitation at a local rehabilitation center. He has no other known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is able to understand and follow instructions. He has no musculoskeletal problems that affect his ability to walk. He has no concurrent pulmonary or neurological diseases. He is able to walk overground with body-weight support if necessary for at least 10 minutes at a comfortable walking speed. He weighs 80 kg and is 173 cm tall.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing migraine headaches for the last 2 years. She experiences migraines at least 3 times per month, with a duration of up to 3 days per episode. She is currently not taking any medication for migraine prevention or acute treatment. Her past medical history is significant for anxiety and depression, which are well managed with sertraline. Her family history is positive for migraine headaches in her mother and sister. She reports that her migraines affect her ability to carry out her daily activities, including work and social life. She is able to take oral medication and is comfortable using electronic devices such as a Personal Digital Assistant (PDA). Her lab results are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of combining topiramate and almotriptan malate for the treatment of her migraine headaches.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after receiving an allogeneic bone marrow transplant for his leukemia 2 years ago. He had a partial response to initial treatment with Prednisone but developed a flare of cGVHD upon steroid taper. He has been steroid-dependent for the past 6 months and has experienced intolerable side effects of steroid therapy. He has no evidence of stable disease but still has some symptoms that are not well controlled by current treatment. His creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits, and he has no history of HIV or other uncontrolled malignancies. He is willing to comply with medical therapy and follow-up and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the therapeutic effects of hydrogen on his cGVHD.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has had a history of asthma for the past 20 years. She has been on high doses of inhaled corticosteroids and a long-acting beta-adrenergic agent, but still experiences severe persistent asthma symptoms. She has had at least one asthma exacerbation in the past year and has evidence of treated, severe, persistent asthma in postbronchodilatory pulmonary function tests. She is a non-smoker and has never been a smoker. She is able to use the Respimat® inhaler correctly and perform all trial related procedures including technically acceptable pulmonary function tests and use of the electronic diary/peak flow meter. She is willing to sign and date an informed consent form consistent with ICH-GCP guidelines and local legislation prior to participation in the trial. She does not have a significant disease other than asthma, clinically relevant abnormal screening haematology or blood chemistry, and has not had a recent history of myocardial infarction, hospitalization for cardiac failure during the past year, any unstable or life-threatening cardiac arrhythmia or cardiac arrhythmia requiring intervention or a change in drug therapy within the past year, known active tuberculosis, malignancy for which the patient has undergone resection, radiation therapy or chemotherapy within the last five years, lung diseases other than asthma (e.g. COPD), significant alcohol or drug abuse within the past two years, or have undergone thoracotomy with pulmonary resection. She is not currently in a pulmonary rehabilitation program or have completed a pulmonary rehabilitation program in the 6 weeks prior to the screening visit (Visit 1). She is not using oral corticosteroid medication at stable doses exceeding 5 mg prednisolone or prednisolone equivalent every day or 10 mg prednisolone or prednisolone equivalent every second day. She does not have known hypersensitivity to anticholinergic drugs, BAC, EDTA or any other components of the tiotropium inhalation solution. She is not pregnant or nursing and is using a highly effective method of birth control. She has not taken an investigational drug within four weeks or six half-lives (whichever is greater) prior to Visit 1. She has not been treated with the long-acting anticholinergic tiotropium (Spiriva®), beta-blocker medication, oral beta-adrenergics, other non-approved and according to international guidelines not recommended ´experimental´ drugs for routine asthma therapy (e.g. TNF-alpha blockers, methotrexate, cyclosporin) within four weeks prior to the Screening Visit (Visit 1) or during the screening period. She has not had any asthma exacerbation or respiratory tract infection in the four weeks prior to the trial. She has not previously been randomized in this trial or in the respective twin trial (205.416 versus 205.417) or is currently participating in another trial. She does not have a known narrow-angle glaucoma.

A 14-year-old male patient who has been diagnosed with bradycardia and has been recommended to undergo epigastric cardiac pacemaker surgery. The patient has a history of occasional headaches but is otherwise healthy with no known allergies or medical conditions. He is currently taking no medications. The patient and his parents are concerned about postoperative pain and want to explore options for pain management. They are open to participating in a clinical trial that aims to examine the effect of subcostal transverse abdominis plane block on postoperative pain and opioid consumption.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Upon further evaluation, a subepithelial tumor was identified in her upper gastrointestinal tract that cannot be treated with standard techniques. The patient is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including visits, laboratory investigations, and endoscopic procedures. She lives within 75 km of the treatment site. The patient has no significant renal, hepatic, or pulmonary disease or cancer. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, nor does she plan to become pregnant in the next 18 months. She is not taking anticoagulant therapy and is not scheduled for any gastric surgery within 60 days post-intervention. The patient has no GI stenosis or obstruction and is not currently participating in any other studies.

10-month-old male infant with a fever of 101.5°F who presents to the emergency department with his mother. The infant is alert, responsive, and has no signs of distress. The mother reports that the fever has been present for 12 hours and the infant has been irritable, fussy, and has decreased appetite. The infant has no significant past medical history and has not received any medication for the fever. The mother is able to communicate with the study personnel and is willing to participate in the study. The infant is otherwise healthy and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study.

65 year-old male with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease for over 10 years. He has been on a stable dose of L-dopa/dopa decarboxylase inhibitor but has been experiencing dyskinesia. His symptoms include involuntary movements, tremors, and difficulty with coordination. He has no history of drug-induced or atypical parkinsonism and has no cognitive impairment. He has no history of Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders IV (DSM IV) diagnosed major depression or psychosis. His clinical laboratory tests are within normal limits. He has no history of poorly controlled diabetes, obesity associated with metabolic syndrome, uncontrolled hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, or any form of clinically significant cardiac disease, symptomatic orthostatic hypotension, renal failure, history of abnormal renal function, seizures, alcohol/drug dependence, or previous surgery for Parkinson's disease. He does not consume more than two 4-oz (120 mL) glasses of wine or their equivalent on a daily basis. He has no allergies or sensitivity to study drug or its excipients. He is not currently participating in any other clinical study.

A 30-year-old female with a pre-existing diagnosis of type II diabetes, of at least 6 months' duration, presents for prenatal care in her first trimester of pregnancy. She is currently taking metformin for her diabetes and has no known allergies to medications. She has a history of uncomplicated pregnancies and deliveries. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the role of low-dose aspirin in preventing placental dysfunction-related adverse perinatal outcomes, such as pre-eclampsia, fetal growth restriction, preterm birth or perinatal death. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and does not have any of the exclusion criteria. She is provided with detailed information about the study, including the potential benefits and risks, and is given the opportunity to ask questions. After careful consideration, the patient consents to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old male of Han Chinese ethnicity who was diagnosed with HCV infection in a university-affiliated hospital in China. He was previously enrolled in the Protocol AI452009 (i.e., the CCgenos cross-sectional phase, ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01293279) and had his genotype characterized at the time of diagnosis. He has not received any antiviral treatment for HCV infection yet. He has agreed to participate in the follow-up study (AI452-018, CCgenos follow-up phase, ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01293279) to observe and describe long-term patient management and treatment patterns with associated outcomes in real-world clinical practice in China. He has no significant medical history or co-morbidities, and his physical examination is unremarkable. He works as a construction worker and is married with two children. He smokes 10 cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is willing to be followed up for the next 5 years.

8-year-old female with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs) presents to the pediatric clinic with symptoms of dysuria, frequency, and urgency. Urinalysis confirms the presence of bacteria and she is diagnosed with an acute UTI. She is started on a course of antibiotics and is eligible for the clinical trial on cranberry-lingonberry juice as a preventative measure for future UTIs. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. She has no known allergies, takes no medications, and has no recent hospitalizations. The patient's parents are willing to participate in the study and understand the importance of complying with the juice regimen. The patient has no severe congenital kidney or urinary tract anomalies and is within the age range of 1-16 years.

The patient is a 9-year-old Hispanic boy from a rural area of New Mexico. He has a history of moderately severe to severe asthma and has experienced multiple emergency room visits due to his asthma symptoms. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. His parents work long hours in the fields, and they have limited access to healthcare resources due to their location and language barriers. The family has limited knowledge about asthma management and self-care techniques. The patient's asthma symptoms include wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, which often interfere with his daily activities and school attendance. He has been prescribed various asthma medications, but his symptoms continue to persist. The patient and his family are interested in participating in a self-management education program that could enhance their knowledge and skills in managing the patient's asthma symptoms. They hope that the program will improve the patient's overall health and reduce the need for emergency room visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was admitted to the emergency department with a sudden onset of chest pain that lasted for more than 30 minutes. The patient had ST elevation of more than 1mm in leads II, III, and aVF. The electrocardiogram performed within 15 minutes after arrival at the emergency department showed an ST-segment elevation of 0.1 mV in the V3R or V4R lead, indicating right ventricular infarction. The patient had no previous history of myocardial infarction or coronary artery bypass surgery, and did not have electrocardiographic evidence of bundle branch block. The diagnosis of acute inferior wall myocardial infarction was confirmed with a 2-fold increase in serum creatine kinase levels. The patient will be enrolled in the study as a first attacked acute inferior MI patient.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman who is generally healthy and physically active. She is a student at the university and enjoys participating in various sports activities. She has no history of chronic pain, musculoskeletal disorders, or neurological conditions. Her body mass index is within the normal range, and she is not currently taking any vasoactive medication. She has not undergone spinal manipulation in the past month and does not have any red flag signs such as a malignant tumor, inflammatory, or infectious disease that contraindicates manual therapy. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial examining the immediate effects of upper thoracic manipulation on skin surface temperature in the region of T3 and the biceps brachii muscle.

A 47-year-old woman diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer with a lump in her left breast that measures approximately 4 cm in diameter. Despite receiving chemotherapy, her symptoms are not well controlled, and she experiences significant discomfort and pain in her breast. The patient is physically and mentally fit for high-dose palliative radiotherapy and is willing to undergo treatment to achieve lifetime control of local morbidities. The patient's target tumor is accessible for intra-tumoral injection, and the tumor diameter measures more than 30 mm. The patient has not received prior radiotherapy to the target area and does not have anatomical issues that would make injection difficult. The patient has offered written informed consent and is available for a minimum of three months of follow-up post-treatment. The patient has undergone a negative pregnancy test within seven days of starting radiotherapy, and she is willing and able to protect against pregnancy for three months post-radiotherapy.

A 76-year-old male patient was referred to the oncology clinic with a diagnosis of metastatic colorectal cancer. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He is a retired mechanic who is living with his wife and is dependent on her for activities of daily living. He has a history of falls and mild cognitive impairment. He underwent a colonoscopy which showed a mass in the sigmoid colon, and biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. Imaging studies demonstrated liver and lung metastases. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2. His creatinine clearance is 45 ml/min, hemoglobin is 10 gr/dl, platelets are 120,000/mm3, and neutrophil count is 1300/mm3. The patient is interested in participating in the study and agrees to comply with the oral medication regimen.

A 42-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for 5 years is currently taking metformin and a sulfonylurea with stable doses for the past 3 months. His most recent HbA1c level was 8.5%. He has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and has not used any insulin therapy in the past 2 years. He has no history of severe hypoglycemia or hypoglycemia unawareness. His creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dL and his liver function tests are within normal limits. He has not taken any glucose-lowering medications other than those listed in the inclusion criteria in the past 3 months.

This is a 29 year old female who delivered her first child via vaginal delivery at 38 weeks gestation. She is currently experiencing significant breast engorgement, characterized by a significant increase in breast size between the 2nd and 10th day postpartum, pain, and obstructed milk outflow. Her self-rated engorgement scale is at level 4 and her volume of milk outflow is less than 20ml. She has never had any surgical breast intervention or breast implants and is not allergic to kinesiology taping. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of kinesiology taping in relieving the symptoms of breast engorgement.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who recently tested positive for HIV. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He is sexually active with multiple partners and uses condoms inconsistently. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is interested in participating in a study that could potentially interrupt or reduce the spread of the virus in his body. He is willing to commit to follow-up visits for at least 96 weeks and to use a barrier method of birth control during the study. He is not currently taking any anti-HIV drugs and has not received any treatment for HIV in the past. He has no conditions that would interfere with intestinal absorption.

A 68 year old woman has been receiving oral anticoagulation treatment with phenprocoumon for atrial fibrillation for the past 2 years. She has had several INR measurements below the target range, and has experienced one major bleeding event and one thromboembolic event requiring hospitalisation during this time. She is interested in participating in a study that could help improve her management of OAC therapy, and has no history of severe cognitive impairment or terminal illness. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the trial.

62F with a history of diabetes mellitus type II and cataracts in both eyes was referred to participate in a clinical trial for the prevention of macular edema after cataract surgery. The patient reports no current symptoms of visual impairment, but acknowledges having occasional blurriness in her vision. She is currently being treated with metformin and insulin for her diabetes and reports good control of her blood sugar levels. On examination, she has a visual acuity of 20/40 in both eyes, bilateral cataracts with a grade of 3+ and no evidence of macular edema. She has no history of ocular surgery or other ocular pathology. She is willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits and other study procedures, and understands the possible off-label use of intravitreal bevacizumab and/or subconjunctival preservative-free TA. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has none of the exclusion criteria, except for her diabetes mellitus. The patient is interested in participating in the study and will be randomized to receive one of the preventive strategies for the occurrence of CME after cataract surgery.

The patient is a 51-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML). He has a history of hypertension, which is being controlled with medication. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. He works as a construction worker and has been feeling weak and fatigued. His lab results show an IDH2 mutation, and he has relapsed after previous treatments, including chemotherapy and stem cell transplantation. He has an ECOG performance score of 1, and his platelet count is 25,000/μL, which requires transfusions. His AST and ALT levels are within normal limits, and his serum total bilirubin is 0.9 x ULN. His serum creatinine is 1.2 x ULN, and his creatinine clearance is 55 mL/min based on the Cockroft-Gault formula. He is a non-smoker, and he has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past month. He has signed and dated written informed consent prior to admission to the study.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl who was diagnosed with leg length discrepancy of 4cm during a routine check-up. She has no history of fractures or trauma to her legs. Her growth and development have been normal, and she has no other significant medical history. She has no known allergies to medications or anesthesia. Her family history is negative for any orthopedic conditions. She is currently in middle school and enjoys playing basketball and volleyball. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing two different surgical techniques for the correction of her leg length discrepancy.

25-year-old female with a BMI of 23kg/m2 and a body weight of 60kg who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate and compare the pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, safety, and tolerability of different combinations of Gemigliptin and Rosuvastatin. She is in good health with a blood pressure of 120/70 mmHg and fasting glucose level of 90mg/dL. She is surgically infertile and agrees to use two or more methods of contraception to prevent pregnancy during the trial. She has no history of genetic disorders, gastrointestinal diseases, or clinically significant drug-induced hypersensitive reactions or drug-related muscular diseases. She has a good understanding of the clinical trial and is willing to collect blood samples during the trial period.

A 45-year-old female with a BMI of 32, presents to her primary care physician with complaints of increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Her fasting glucose level is 106 mg/dL and her 2-hour glucose level after a 75g OGTT is 163 mg/dL, confirming impaired glucose tolerance. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent the progression of prediabetes to diabetes. She has no current use of glucose-lowering or weight loss drugs and is willing to comply with a lifestyle modification program. She is able to use a CGM as confirmed by the investigator and has no physical limitations or underlying medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. She provides written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma, with mild to moderate disc damage and visual field loss in the right eye. He has been on branded latanoprost eye drops for the past year, but his intraocular pressure remains above 20mmHg. He reports good adherence to his medication regimen and has never been on any other IOP-lowering medication. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with amlodipine and lisinopril. He has no history of ocular trauma, ocular infection, or ocular surgery. The patient currently wears glasses for presbyopia, and his visual acuity is 20/30 in the right eye. He reports no ocular symptoms such as redness, itching, or pain. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of preservative-free tafluprost/timolol fixed combination given once in the morning versus once in the evening, with placebo given in the alternate dosing period. He understands the study instructions and is willing to attend all follow-up appointments and comply with medication usage.

A 62-year-old male patient presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and the implantation of a bare-metal stent (BMS) five years ago. He is currently on a daily dose of aspirin and a statin. He reports compliance with his medications and a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise and a balanced diet. An electrocardiogram indicates ST-segment depression in the inferolateral leads, and cardiac biomarkers are elevated. Angiography reveals a significant stenosis in the right coronary artery, and the decision is made to perform a PCI with a drug-eluting stent (DES) to treat the obstruction. The patient is offered the opportunity to participate in the FReIburger STent Registry (FRIST) to determine the long-term safety and efficacy of DES in a "real-world" patient population requiring stent implantation. He agrees to participate and provides written informed consent.

A 45-year-old female with a history of dry mouth and eyes for the past 2 years presented to the clinic. She had previously been diagnosed with primary Sjogren's syndrome and had an ESSDAI score of 8. She had elevated serum titers of ANA (1:320) and was seropositive for anti-SSA and anti-SSB antibodies. Her stimulated whole salivary flow rate was less than 0.5 mL/min. She had never received B-cell depleting therapy, prednisone, anti-BAFF mAb, CTLA4-Fc Ig (abatacept), anti-TNF-α mAb, cyclophosphamide, or azathioprine. However, she had been taking hydroxychloroquine for the past 6 months. She had no history of primary or secondary immunodeficiency, active or recent history of clinically significant infection, or vaccination within the past 2 months. She was interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of VAY736 monoclonal antibody in patients with primary Sjogren's syndrome.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of chronic allergic contact dermatitis on her forearms and hands. She reports that the rash started after she switched to a new brand of dishwashing detergent. She has tried various over-the-counter creams with little improvement. She denies any other known allergies or medical conditions. Her past medical history is only significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of skin cancer or immunodeficiency disorders. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use an effective contraceptive method during the study. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study. Her physical examination shows moderate to severe chronic allergic contact dermatitis, covering approximately 5% of her total body surface area. She has an Investigator's Global Assessment score of 3 and a positive patch test reaction after application for 2 days for the suspected allergen. She has no active atopic dermatitis lesions or clinically infected allergic contact dermatitis lesions. She has not used any topical medicated treatment for allergic contact dermatitis within 2 weeks prior to Day 1.

Patient is a healthy male volunteer between the ages of 20-35 with no known medical disorders and a BMI of 18.5 - 39.9 (kg/m2). The patient does not have any known allergies to paracetamol or tropisetron and does not consume excessive amounts of tobacco, tea, or coffee. The patient also does not have a history of recreational drug addiction and is not currently taking any medication on the trial days. The patient is interested in participating in the study to better understand the mode of action of paracetamol and its effects on pain. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of participation and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has been struggling with binge eating disorder for the past 3 years. She reports having at least 5 episodes of binge eating per week, where she consumes large amounts of food in a short period of time and feels a loss of control over her eating. She has tried various diets and weight loss programs in the past, but has been unable to sustain any significant weight loss due to her binge eating episodes. She is not currently receiving psychotherapy or weight loss support for her disorder. She has no history of psychosis, mania, hypomania, dementia, or ADHD. She has no known history of cardiovascular disease or hypertension. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has not undergone any weight loss procedures in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the efficacy of SPD489 in reducing the number of binge eating days per week.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who has been diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer. He has previously undergone standard chemotherapy, which has failed to control the progression of the disease. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. He has been tested and found to have MET gene abnormality. The patient has at least one measurable lesion and has not received any c-MET inhibitors or other systemic anti-tumor treatments within the last four weeks. He has adequate organ system function and a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of at least 50%. The patient is willing and able to sign an informed consent form. He has not been diagnosed or treated for any other malignancies in the last three years and does not have any uncontrollable congestive heart failure or arrhythmia. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use adequate contraceptive measures during the study.

A 28-year-old male soccer player presents with a history of ACL injury, which was diagnosed as grade II by a stress X-ray with Telos. The patient reports no other injuries or musculoskeletal problems and has no collateral ligament or meniscus injuries. He has no joint pain, knee joint effusion, or history of previous injuries in other structures of the lower extremities that resulted in ligamentous laxity at the ankle and hip. He has no current medical problems such as vestibular system, visual system, or neurological conditions that can impair his ability to perform a sidestep cutting task. The patient has no joint or structural deformities such as flat feet, genu valgus, or genu varus. He can complete functional tests such as single hop for distance and triple hop for distance, and the distance is not less than 85% of the unaffected side. The patient is interested in participating in a study that investigates the effects of elastic therapeutic tape on biomechanical changes of the knee joint during drop vertical jump in ACL injuries. He understands the purpose, methods, and advantages of the study and is willing to sign a consent form.

The patient is a 45 year old female who works as a nurse at a local hospital. She has been experiencing chronic pain in her right shoulder for over a year now. Despite undergoing physical therapy and taking pain medications, her condition has not improved. Her orthopedic surgeon has recommended surgery to repair a torn rotator cuff. The patient is anxious about the surgery and has several questions about the procedure, post-operative care, and expected outcomes. She is concerned about the level of pain she may experience after the surgery and how it may affect her ability to perform her job. She lives alone and has no one to help her with daily activities during her recovery. She is eager to participate in the clinical trial to receive formal pre-operative education from an occupational or physical therapist to help her better understand the surgery and ease her anxiety.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of dyspepsia and GERD. She has been taking proton pump inhibitors (PPI) for the past 6 months. She complains of epigastric pain, bloating, and nausea. She has not been tested for Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection before. She has not taken any antibiotics, H2 receptor antagonists, or other medications that could affect H. pylori test results in the past four weeks. She has not been pregnant in the past year. She is willing to undergo endoscopy and biopsy to confirm H. pylori infection and participate in the study. She understands that the study will involve two different test meals for the 13C-urea breath test and that she may need to discontinue PPI use for a short period before the test. She is willing to adhere to the study protocol and give written informed consent.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and underwent a non-myeloablative stem cell transplant from his 6/6 matched, sibling donor three weeks ago. He is currently in good condition without any signs of graft-versus-host disease. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. His donor is CMV sero-positive and has an HLA type of HLA-B*07. The patient's HLA type is HLA-DR*1. The patient and donor both understand and have provided signed informed consent for the clinical trial. The patient lives within a reasonable distance to Duke University Medical Center and is able to return for adequate follow-up as required by the protocol. The patient has not experienced any Grade 3 or 4 non-hematologic major organ toxicity in the preceding week, and his non-major organ toxicities have resolved to grade-2 or less.

82-year-old woman, residing in a nursing home, who fell and sustained a hip fracture. She underwent surgery to fix the fracture and is now recovering in the hospital. Her medical history includes hypertension, osteoporosis, and mild cognitive impairment. She is currently taking lisinopril and calcium with vitamin D supplements. Her haemoglobin level is measured to be 6.5 mmol/l on the 4th day after surgery. The patient is able to ambulate with assistance but has reduced mobility due to pain and weakness. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was diagnosed with indolent Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma 5 years ago. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with partial response but has experienced frequent relapses. Recently, she has been experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She has a Karnofsky performance status score of 70% and adequate organ and bone marrow function. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for her recurrent indolent NHL.

A 58-year-old male presents with metastatic prostate cancer that has not responded to hormone therapy. The patient has bidimensionally measurable disease, bone only metastases with rising PSA levels, and PSA only disease. The patient has not received prior chemotherapy or estramustine alone or in combination with other chemotherapy. The patient has not received taxanes before and has only undergone one prior chemotherapy regimen. The patient is currently on LHRH agonist for primary hormonal therapy. The patient has no other active malignancies within the past 5 years except nonmelanomatous skin cancer or other in situ cancer. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 2 and a life expectancy that is not specified. The patient has an absolute granulocyte count of at least 1,500/mm3 and a platelet count of at least 100,000/mm3. The patient's bilirubin is no greater than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) and SGOT is no greater than 2 times ULN. The patient's creatinine is no greater than 2.0 mg/dL.

32 y/o female with a history of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) 3, who had previously participated in the GX-188E phase II trial (GX-188E_CIN3_P2) and received the GX-188E DNA-based therapeutic vaccine. The patient is willing to participate in the follow-up study to investigate changes in immune response and lesion condition. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would make her ineligible for the study. She has provided informed consent to be a part of the study and is able to commit to the required visits for the next three years.

The patient is a 28-year-old Chinese female who has been trying to conceive for more than a year. She has a regular menstrual cycle, but it is longer than 35 days, and she experiences occasional amenorrhea. She has undergone one cycle of ovulation induction with clomiphene citrate, which was unsuccessful. She has no known history of thrombophlebitis or thromboembolism, but she has a family history of these conditions. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication that could interfere with the study. She has a normal BMI and has not abused alcohol or drugs. She has no known tumors or malformations of the sexual organs. She has a normal cervical examination and has no abnormal vaginal bleeding. She has normal levels of LH, prolactin, E2, progesterone, total testosterone, and TSH. Her partner has undergone a semen analysis, which shows acceptable values. She has not undergone any treatment with clomiphene citrate, metformin, gonadotropins, or GnRH analogs within one month prior to randomization. She has normal bilateral tubal patency documented by a hysterosalpingography or sonohysterography or laparoscopy within 2 years prior to screening. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

A 68-year-old retired teacher has been experiencing persistent abdominal pain for the past few months. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She denies any history of smoking, alcohol or drug use. She has lost some weight in the past few months, but she attributes it to loss of appetite due to her abdominal discomfort. She has reported pain in the upper abdomen that radiates to her back. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but the pain persists. Her primary care physician has referred her to a gastroenterologist for further evaluation. She had CT scan of the abdomen which revealed a pancreatic mass. She underwent endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) which confirmed pancreatic cancer. She was told that the cancer is inoperable and that she would need treatment for pain. She has been referred to participate in a clinical trial comparing EUS-guided radiofrequency ablation (EUS-RFA) vs. EUS-guided celiac plexus neurolysis (EUS-CPN) for pain management in pancreatic cancer patients. She is interested in participating in the trial since she is experiencing significant pain and is looking for a better option for pain management.

The patient is a 45-year-old Asian woman who presents with progressive dyspnea and dry cough for the past 6 months. She has a history of dermatomyositis diagnosed 2 years ago based on the Sontheimer-Bohan-Peter criteria. Her serum creatine kinase is within normal limits. High-resolution CT scan shows interstitial pneumonia, and lung function tests reveal a DLCO of 50% predicted. Her serum KL-6 levels and serum anti-MDA5 are elevated. She has not been treated before with any immunosuppressive or target treatment for dermatomyositis. She has no history of active infections or malignancies. Her renal and liver function tests are within normal limits. She is willing to use contraception during the study period.

A 78-year-old Hispanic male with low health literacy is concerned about the risk of colorectal cancer. He has a family history of colon cancer, with his father diagnosed at the age of 60. The patient has never undergone colorectal cancer screening and is unsure about the different screening options available. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He is retired and lives with his wife. He is able to read, but he finds medical forms and information difficult to understand. He reports occasional constipation but denies any rectal bleeding or abdominal pain. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to learn more about colorectal cancer screening and make an informed decision about his health. His primary care physician has recommended that he undergo screening due to his family history, but the patient has not made a decision yet. The patient is interested in learning more about the risks and benefits of different screening options and how to engage in shared decision-making with his physician. His baseline knowledge of colorectal cancer screening is limited, and he rates his confidence in filling out medical forms by himself as "not at all confident."

A 62-year-old French-speaking woman with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease presents with symptoms such as tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia.
