She also reports experiencing difficulty in expressing her emotions and understanding the emotions of others. The patient has a reliable informant who can provide additional information about her socio-emotional functioning. She has a history of hypertension, but her other medical conditions are well-controlled. The patient has no history of psychiatric illness or substance abuse. She is able to read, write, and draw without any difficulty. The patient's MMSE score is 24, indicating mild cognitive impairment. MRI imaging shows no contraindications for the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

56 yo M with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation, with disease progression on imaging. The patient has an easily accessible recurrent lymph node that can be biopsied for study inclusion. The patient has no history of heart disease or other comorbidities and an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has adequate organ function and hematopoietic function, and is willing to use two effective methods of contraception as the patient's partner is of childbearing potential. The patient has not received any investigational anti-cancer drugs within the past 2 weeks and has no active concurrent malignancy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has provided informed consent after being thoroughly educated about the investigational nature, risks and benefits of the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old pregnant woman in her second trimester. She lives in Kampala, Uganda, and is attending antenatal care at the Infectious Disease Institute. She has tested positive for syphilis using a rapid treponemal antibody test. She is aware of the risks of untreated syphilis during pregnancy and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to increase the number of male partners who come to the clinic for syphilis testing and treatment. She has a mobile phone and is able to read and send text messages. She has a steady sexual partner who is at risk for syphilis and is willing to participate in the study. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to be randomized into one of three arms of the study. She has no history of neurosyphilis and is not illiterate.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has a history of sexual assault. She presents to the clinic with symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder, including intrusive thoughts, nightmares, and avoidance behaviors. She reports that her assault occurred 5 years ago and she has not sought treatment for her symptoms until now. She describes feeling anxious and on edge most of the time, and has difficulty sleeping. She reports avoiding situations that remind her of the assault, including social situations and intimate relationships. The patient has no history of psychosis, mental retardation, or current addiction to drugs or alcohol. She is not currently suicidal or parasuicidal. The patient is able to read and write. Her baseline assessment for PTSD symptoms shows significant impairment in several areas, including re-experiencing, avoidance, and hyperarousal symptoms. She has feelings of guilt and shame associated with the assault and reports a negative perception of herself and her surroundings. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this study and is willing to participate in the therapy sessions.

A 35-year-old female presents with notable extrinsic dental stains on her 6 maxillary labial front teeth. She has been self-conscious about the appearance of her teeth for a long time and is interested in participating in the clinical trial for ToothWave powered toothbrush for extrinsic stain reduction. She has a good overall health and regularly brushes her teeth twice a day. Her last teeth whitening procedure was more than 3 years ago. She has not had any oral surgeries in the past 6 months and does not have any active conditions in her oral cavity. She is not pregnant or nursing and does not have any active electrical implants in her body. She is willing to comply with the study procedure and schedule, including follow-up visits and refraining from using any other teeth whitening technologies during the study period. She understands the benefits and side effects of the treatment and is willing to sign the Informed Consent Form.

A 50-year-old man with a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and type 2 diabetes comes to the clinic for a metabolic syndrome screening. The patient is overweight with a body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m², and has a waist circumference of 105 cm. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and his fasting blood glucose level is 120 mg/dL. His HDL cholesterol level is 39 mg/dL, and his triglyceride level is 170 mg/dL. The patient is not currently taking any lipid-lowering medication other than statins, and has not taken high doses of thiazide diuretics or any other blood pressure medication in the past 4 weeks. He has not used plant sterols from sources such as Benecol or Take Control margarines in the past 4 weeks, nor has he used any fish oil supplements in the week prior to screening. He does not have any hospitalization for coronary disease in the last 6 months, nor does he use nitroglycerin or other nitrates. The patient does not have unstable liver, renal, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, or mental disease, and is not medically unstable for other reasons. He does not have any alcohol intake greater than 2 drinks/day, any illegal drug use, smoking, chronic NSAID use or NSAID use within 5 days before the brachial artery reactivity (BAR) study. The patient is not currently lactating, nor does he intend to become pregnant within one year or one year prior. He does not have an irregular menstrual cycle and is not using any oral or patch contraceptive. The patient is willing and able to comply with study requirements.

32-year-old female diagnosed with idiopathic recurrent pericarditis with a history of two documented episodes of pericarditis at least 4-6 weeks apart. She has been on NSAIDs and colchicine therapy for the past two weeks. The patient has voluntarily signed the Informed Consent Form for participation in the study and is willing to comply with all protocol requirements, including subcutaneous injections by qualified personnel of the study site. She is willing to use highly effective contraceptive methods throughout the study and has tested negative for pregnancy. The patient has no history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to human, humanized or murine monoclonal antibodies. She has not been previously diagnosed with auto-inflammatory diseases and has not received any prior therapy with rilonacept, canakinumab, anakinra, TNF inhibitors, IL-6 inhibitors, Janus kinase inhibitors, or any other biological preparations. The patient has not received live attenuated vaccines within the past three months and does not require the use of this type of vaccine within three months after the discontinuation of the study drug. She has no active bacterial, fungal, viral or protozoal infection and no history of opportunistic infections and/or Kaposi's sarcoma. The patient is mentally stable and does not have a history of alcohol or psychoactive substance abuse. She has no severe renal impairment and does not have any other significant comorbidities that may affect her participation and well-being in the study. The patient has not participated in any other clinical studies at the moment of the beginning of the screening or used any not approved (investigational) medicinal products within 4 weeks of 5 half-life periods (depending on what is longer) up to the baseline assessment (Day 0 of the run-in treatment period).

A 52-year-old male patient with a history of alcohol abuse presents with confusion, agitation, and disorientation. He has a known history of liver cirrhosis and has been non-compliant with his treatment plan. Upon admission to the hospital, he is diagnosed with hepatic encephalopathy and is admitted to the intensive care unit. The patient's Glasgow Coma Score is 9 and his early warning score is 7. He is started on lactulose therapy and his vital signs are stable. The patient has a history of smoking and has a BMI of 32. Imaging studies reveal no evidence of cerebral edema or intracranial hemorrhage. The patient is enrolled in a clinical trial to assess the impact of standardized nursing supervision on the prevention of complications in patients with hepatic encephalopathy in the ICU.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been experiencing memory loss and difficulty with concentration for the past year. He has been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score of 21. He is currently taking donepezil for his MCI. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril, but is otherwise healthy. He has no history of diabetes or insulin allergy. He speaks and understands English fluently. He has a dedicated family member who is willing to attend all visits and report on his status. He has undergone a brain MRI as part of his diagnostic workup, which is compatible with the diagnosis of probable AD.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who recently had a stroke. He was admitted to a sub-acute rehabilitation facility for his rehabilitation. He has a medical history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are currently well-controlled with medication. He is independent in his activities of daily living, but he has difficulty swallowing food. He has been experiencing coughing and choking episodes when eating solid foods and is unable to consume anything but pureed foods and thickened liquids. He reports feeling anxious and frustrated about his inability to eat normally. The patient has not received any previous behavioral or NMES swallowing therapy. He has no history of other neurological disorders or head/neck surgery that may impact his swallowing ability. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. His Mini-Mental test score is 27 and his Western Aphasia Battery comprehension quotient score is 80%.

A 42-year-old female who was previously bitten by a stray dog in a rural area of Madagascar 5 years ago, received post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for rabies. She received the TRC ID protocol of four sessions over one month, and has not received any rabies vaccine booster since then. She is in good health with no known allergies or severe unwanted effects related to the previous PEP. She has consented to participate in the clinical trial to determine the long-term immunity conferred by the abbreviated IPC protocol. She will be required to undergo two visits, the first visit will include blood sample collection and administration of two intradermal doses of 0.1 mL, and the second visit will be a follow-up visit to collect a second blood sample and document any unwanted effects that may have occurred during the seven days between the inclusion visit and the follow-up visit.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who fell from a ladder while cleaning the gutters. He landed on his left arm and experienced immediate pain and swelling in his shoulder. He visited the emergency room and was diagnosed with a proximal humeral fracture. The fracture was less than 5 days old and he had completed his skeletal development. He does not have any history of alcohol or drug abuse or any other known diseases that could affect the healing process. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates different treatments for proximal humeral fractures. He is currently experiencing moderate pain and has limited range of motion in his left arm. He is willing to undergo radiological evaluations and complete the Constant and Neer score assessments at 12 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after the treatment.

A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer and underwent radical prostatectomy 5 years ago. A routine follow-up imaging revealed a painful bone metastasis in the right iliac bone. The patient reported a constant dull pain in the right hip that is exacerbated by standing or walking. He rates the pain as 8 out of 10 on the visual analog scale. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His weight is 80kg, and his height is 180cm. The MRI showed a 2.5cm metastatic lesion in the right iliac bone, accessible by HIFU-MRI. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the research objectives and risks. He has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He has been struggling with maintaining a healthy lifestyle and is interested in participating in a study that could improve his overall health. He is a non-smoker and has not been diagnosed with ischaemic heart disease or congestive heart failure. He does not experience joint or limp pains that would prevent him from participating in recreational soccer. He is not on anticoagulant therapy but takes aspirin occasionally. He is willing to commit to a 6-month structured recreational soccer training program and willing to undergo various testing throughout the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who is concerned about the wrinkles on her forehead and the position of her eyebrows. She has never undergone any facial surgery or trauma. She has no history of any neurological or autoimmune disorders. She has been using botulinum toxin injections for the past two years to treat her forehead wrinkles, but she feels like they do not provide the same effect as before. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different techniques for forehead lift fixation.

The patient is a 14-year-old male who was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (ICU) due to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). He had a history of asthma but had not had a recent exacerbation. On admission, he was hypoxic and required mechanical ventilation. His chest x-ray showed diffuse bilateral infiltrates consistent with ARDS. He was treated with high-flow oxygen therapy and was started on inhaled bronchodilators and intravenous steroids. He had a prolonged ICU stay and required multiple interventions, including prone positioning and neuromuscular blockade. He was eventually weaned off the ventilator and transferred to the general pediatric ward. At discharge, he was still using supplemental oxygen and had a persistent cough. The family was instructed to follow up with their primary care physician and to seek medical attention if there were any respiratory symptoms. The patient was invited to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the outcomes of pediatric ARDS survivors and to determine whether an earlier diagnosis using a computerized decision support system would improve care.

A 32-year-old male with a 5-year history of ulcerative colitis. He was diagnosed with UC after experiencing bloody diarrhea, cramping, and weight loss. He has been treated with mesalamine and corticosteroids on and off, but has experienced only partial relief of symptoms. His disease is limited to the rectum and sigmoid colon, as confirmed by colonoscopy. He has never received anti-TNFα therapy or any other biologic agent. He has no history of tuberculosis or hepatitis B or C infection. He is not currently taking any medication for UC. He has no other significant medical history or allergies. He is willing to undergo sigmoidoscopy and biopsies for the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle collision. He was the driver of a car that collided with a truck, and he was not wearing a seatbelt at the time of the accident. He was extricated from the car by emergency responders and transported to the Level I Adult Trauma Center. Upon arrival, he was hypotensive with a systolic blood pressure of 80 mm Hg, and he had an initial hemoglobin level of 7.5 g/dL. The patient had no known medical history and was not taking any medications. He was noted to have multiple injuries, including a closed head injury, a right femur fracture, a left tibia fracture, and multiple rib fractures. He was intubated in the emergency department and was started on a massive transfusion protocol due to ongoing hemorrhage. His ABC score was 2, indicating a high likelihood of requiring a massive transfusion. He was randomized to the experimental arm of the PROPPR trial, and he received a transfusion of plasma, platelets, and RBCs in a 1:1:1 ratio. The patient remained in the hospital for several weeks and required multiple surgeries to repair his injuries. He ultimately survived the accident and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old female with no significant medical history. She has no known allergies or drug dependencies, and she does not smoke or use tobacco products. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She is interested in participating in a clinical study to evaluate the bioequivalence of AG-013736 tablets. She has signed and dated the informed consent document for the study. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has undergone tubal ligation. She is available to attend all study visits and comply with the requirements of the clinical study.

A 32-year-old African American woman with a history of sickle cell disease presents to the emergency department with severe pain in her arms, chest, and back. The pain started 2 days ago and has been worsening gradually. She has been hospitalized multiple times in the past due to sickle cell pain crises. The patient is currently experiencing a crisis and is being treated with intravenous narcotics for pain management. She is able to provide informed written consent to participate in the study. Blood and urine samples will be collected during the study. Cameras and blood flow monitoring equipment will be used to measure blood flow in the forearm during the sickle cell pain crisis and about 4 weeks after the crisis has resolved. Additionally, healthy volunteers matched by age and gender with the sickle cell patients will have one or two study visits. Blood samples will be collected during at least one of these visits, and cameras and blood flow monitoring equipment will be used to measure blood flow in the forearm. The study aims to determine if changes in blood flow cause pain crises in people with sickle cell disease and to measure the endothelial response to shear stress in sickle cell subjects during acute pain crisis and after recovery from pain crisis.

Patient A is a 50-year-old male with a history of advanced solid tumors or glioblastoma multiforme. The patient has previously undergone standard therapy, but the disease has not responded. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 70-100% and meets laboratory criteria, including ANC >= 1,500/μL, WBC >= 3,000/μL, platelet count >= 100,000/μL, and hemoglobin >= 9 g/dL. The patient has no history of thyroid abnormality and has normal serum calcium levels. The patient has not experienced thrombosis or bleeding diathesis within the past 6 months and has no poorly controlled hypertension. The patient has no conditions that would impair the ability to swallow and retain sunitinib malate tablets. The patient has not undergone radiotherapy or systemic antineoplastic therapy within the past 4 weeks and has recovered. The patient has no other concurrent anticancer agents or therapies and no concurrent combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV-positive patients. The patient is not taking

A 50 yo M with a history of HIV infection and chronic HCV infection was recently diagnosed with liver cirrhosis based on a liver stiffness measurement of 16 kiloPascals. He has not experienced any previous or concomitant decompensation of liver disease. He has been receiving antiretroviral therapy for his HIV infection for the past 5 years, with good control of his viral load. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has abstained from alcohol for the past year. He is currently asymptomatic but is concerned about the long-term effects of his liver disease. He is willing to participate in the study to help further understanding of the natural history of liver cirrhosis in HIV/HCV-coinfected patients.

65-year-old Caucasian man with a history of Alzheimer's disease, diagnosed based on clinical signs and symptoms, with a MMSE score of 20. He has no history of diabetes mellitus, liver disease, kidney disease, or endocrinological disease other than well-controlled hypothyroidism. The patient does not have any other CNS-illness other than diagnosed depression treated with SSRI. He has no history of chronic or acute pancreatitis, and no other clinically relevant abnormal biochemical values. The patient is not currently treated with TCA or neuroleptics, and he has no known abuse of alcohol or drugs. He does not have any allergies to liraglutide or any of its components. He has not participated in a clinical trial in the last 3 months and has not had any significant abnormities in the brain detected by MR scanning. The patient's weight is within normal range and he does not have any ferro-magnetic prosthesis, pacemaker, or other metals incorporated in his body.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing knee pain for the past six years. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain relief. However, the pain has become unbearable and has affected her daily activities. She has been scheduled for primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty (TKA) with Dr. Eugene Krauss or Dr. Ayal Segal. She has no history of blood transfusions or allergies to aspirin. Her preoperative hemoglobin is 12mg/dL and her preoperative platelet count is 200,000. She has no history of venous thromboembolism (VTE), stroke, or trans-ischemic attack. She has no active cancer or liver disease. She has no history of psychiatric or mental illness. She is willing to undergo blood transfusion, if necessary. She has no contraindication for the use of the monopolar electrocautery or the pneumatic tourniquet applied in the operating room. She is willing to complete all study-related procedures.

A 4-year-old boy named Alex was recently placed in foster care due to parental substance abuse and neglect. He currently lives in Lane County, Oregon, and is set to enter kindergarten in the fall. Alex has a history of delayed development and has not yet been enrolled in a preschool program. He has difficulty with self-regulation and is easily distracted. He has been in two previous foster placements and has experienced multiple living transitions. He is generally cooperative and sociable but has difficulty following directions and focusing on tasks. Alex is in good physical health and does not have any known medical or developmental conditions that would prevent him from participating in the assessment tasks. He has not previously been involved in any Oregon Social Learning Center treatment programs. Alex's foster caregiver is his maternal aunt who has been caring for him for three months. She is actively involved in his care and is willing to participate in the KITS program to enhance his school readiness.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of high blood pressure, and proteinuria for the past 6 months. She has been taking ACE inhibitors for her hypertension, but her proteinuria has not improved. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of liver or kidney disease. Physical examination reveals a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg, and no edema or palpable masses. Laboratory tests show a UPCR of 4.5 g/g, serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL, and estimated GFR of 75 ml/min/1.73 m². A kidney biopsy confirms the diagnosis of membranous nephropathy. Further testing reveals the presence of anti-PLA2R antibodies at a level of 60 RU/mL. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and agrees to follow the contraceptive guidance during the treatment period and for at least 3 months after the last dose of MOR202.

A 35-year-old male patient who suffered a spinal cord injury 8 weeks ago resulting in partial paralysis of his upper limbs, came to the clinic seeking potential treatment options to restore his arm function. He is able to give informed consent and can remain comfortably seated with provision of trunk stability. He has no orthopaedic implants across or between electrode sites, no active cardiac implant, and no skin conditions, scars, or carcinogenic tissue at the site of stimulation. He reports no uncontrolled pain or epilepsy. He has no skin reactions to electrodes and no open wounds or injuries. He is not pregnant or planning for a pregnancy. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to restore his arm function through the use of electrical stimulation and mobile arm supports.

50 year-old male diagnosed with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and currently receiving riociguat therapy for the condition. The patient has persistent or recurrent PH despite undergoing pulmonary endarterectomy. The diagnosis of CTEPH was confirmed by either ventilation/perfusion scan (V/Q), pulmonary angiography, or computed tomography pulmonary angiography. The patient has undergone clinical right heart catheterization which confirmed mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) greater than 25 mmHg and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) greater than 300 dyne/sec/cm5. The patient is not currently taking phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE-5) inhibitors, endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs), or prostanoids ≤3 days prior to starting the riociguat treatment. The patient has no history of epicardial coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction within the 3 months prior to screening. The patient has no severe proven or suspected coronary artery disease and is not requiring nitrates. The patient has controlled arterial hypertension with a systolic blood pressure of less than 180 mmHg and a diastolic blood pressure of less than 110 mmHg. The patient's resting heart rate in an awake state is between 50 and 105 beats per minute. The patient has no history of uncontrolled atrial fibrillation within the last 3 months prior to screening and no history of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. The patient has no clinical evidence of symptomatic atherosclerotic disease or peripheral artery disease. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using highly effective contraception methods. The patient has a glomerular filtration rate greater than 30 ml/min and ALT or AST levels within the normal range. The patient has no contraindication to MRI imaging. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study after receiving adequate previous information and prior to any study-specific procedures.

32 y/o female with no significant past medical history, non-smoker, and no medication use. She is a college graduate and currently working as a software engineer. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the effects of hypnosis on the brain. She reports no history of psychiatric diagnosis, head injury or seizure disorder, and has no clinical evidence of peripheral or central conduction disorders. She scored a 16 on the Tellegan absorption scale, indicating high hypnotisability. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with lung cancer. He has a history of smoking, having smoked 1 pack per day for the past 30 years. He presented with a persistent cough, shortness of breath and weight loss. CT scan showed a 2.5 cm mass in his left lung which is located less than 2 cm from the chest wall. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. The patient's performance status, as measured by the Karnofsky Performance Status, is 80. The lab results showed the following: Hgb: 12 g/dL, WBC: 8000 /mm3, Plt: 250000 /ml, AST: 30 U/L, ALT: 25 U/L, Alk P: 70 U/L, Bill total: 0.8 mg/dL, Na: 140 mEq/l, K: 4.5 mEq/l, Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dl, BUN: 15 mg/dl. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new radiation planning and treatment delivery technique called Deep Inspiration Breath Hold (DIBH) and expiration technique. He is willing to comply with treatment and follow-up visits.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2. He has no history of smoking or significant medical conditions. He has never had an anaphylactic reaction to any drug and has not previously received any GLP-1 mimetic compound. He has not been diagnosed with hepatitis B, hepatitis C or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). He has no significant cardiovascular or pulmonary dysfunction and has not experienced excessive bleeding in the past. He has no history of liver disease, alcohol or substance abuse, thyroid disease or dysfunction, gastrointestinal surgery or disease, or pancreatitis. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the pharmacokinetics of warfarin when coadministered with albiglutide.

This is a 65-year-old woman who was diagnosed with mild Alzheimer's disease about a year ago. She has noticed that she has been forgetting things more often and has difficulty recalling recent events. She has also had some trouble with daily activities such as cooking, cleaning, and shopping. She is currently taking donepezil for her condition. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She lives alone but has family members who check on her frequently. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help improve her memory and overall cognitive function.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty with her vision due to cataracts. She reports that her vision has been gradually deteriorating over the past few years, and she now has trouble seeing objects at a distance as well as up close. She currently wears glasses for nearsightedness and astigmatism but finds them to be uncomfortable and inconvenient. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial as she would like to explore the possibility of achieving spectacle independence. Upon examination, the patient has age-related cataracts and a preoperative corneal astigmatism of 0.50 D. Her visual acuity is 0.2 with correction, and she has no other relevant ophthalmic diseases or history of ocular surgery or trauma. The patient expresses a willingness to undergo multifocal implantation and has realistic expectations for the outcome of the study.

The patient is an 18-year-old French-Canadian woman residing in New Brunswick. She has been feeling increasingly anxious and depressed over the past few months, with symptoms such as feelings of hopelessness, lack of energy, difficulty concentrating, and trouble sleeping. She has not sought treatment for her symptoms yet. She speaks French as her native language and has good comprehension of written French. She has reliable access to the internet and is willing to share relevant personal information. She has not received any cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) in the past and has not changed her medication in the last one month nor does she intend to change it in the next two months. The patient has a clinical level of depression, as indicated by her PHQ-9 score of 15, and generalized anxiety disorder, as indicated by her GAD-7 score of 10. She has no history of severe depression or suicidal thoughts. She is interested in participating in an 8-week online course that can help her manage her symptoms of anxiety and depression.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese man who has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) for the past 5 years. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking antihypertensive medications regularly. He is currently not on dialysis and is being followed up regularly in a nephrology clinic. His most recent laboratory results showed a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 45 mL/min/1.73m2 and proteinuria of 0.6g in 24 hour urine collection. He has been experiencing occasional bone pain and his doctor suspects that he may have Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral and Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD). He is interested in participating in the Chinese CKD-MBD Prevalence Survey (CRISS-MBD) to help advance knowledge and improve the treatment of CKD-MBD in the Chinese population.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been diagnosed with essential hypertension. Despite being on amlodipine, his blood pressure has remained elevated. He has no history of stroke, myocardial infarction, heart failure, chest pain, or abnormal heart rhythm. He has no known liver, kidney, or pancreas disease but has a history of insulin-dependent diabetes. He is not allergic to any medications used to treat high blood pressure. He has been advised to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness and safety of a combination treatment of valsartan/amlodipine.

A 58-year-old male with a history of hypertension and smoking was admitted to the hospital with acute stroke symptoms. CT scan showed an ischemic stroke in the left middle cerebral artery territory. The patient was clinically stable and was selected to receive physiotherapy during hospitalization. He has a caregiver who will assist him throughout the trial. The patient has an adequate understanding of Spanish and has given his written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no significant cognitive impairment and is able to follow instructions.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of ER-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced breast cancer that has progressed despite at least 6 months of previous endocrine therapy. She has received limited prior chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and targeted therapy for advanced or metastatic disease. Her most recent imaging shows radiologic or objective evidence of disease progression on or after the last systemic therapy. She is postmenopausal, having undergone a bilateral oophorectomy previously. Her ECOG performance status is 0-1. She has not received any anticancer therapy, including endocrine therapy, chemotherapy, or targeted therapy, within 30 days prior to the first dose of study treatment. She has no untreated or symptomatic or progressive CNS metastases.

A 35-year-old male patient with a history of spinal cord injury at the T4 level presented with neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction (LUTD). He has been experiencing urinary urgency and frequency, as well as incontinence, for the past year despite taking antimuscarinics. He has also been suffering from chronic urinary retention that is refractory to alpha-blockers. His neurological disease has been stable for the past 2 years. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study. He has not received botulinum A toxin injections into the detrusor and/or urethral sphincter in the last 6 months. He is not pregnant or under 18 years old. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has no other specific medical conditions.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a diagnosis of moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest tightness during physical activity for the past year. She was recently diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension, with a pulmonary systolic pressure greater than 40mmHg. She is currently on oxygen therapy and taking medications for COPD management. She has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit 10 years ago. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has no known allergies to medications. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial and is willing to comply with the research protocol.

A 55-year-old male residing in Yuetan subdistrict in Beijing is admitted to the hospital with a fever, chills, and cough. He has a history of smoking and hypertension but is not currently taking any medications. He reports feeling weak and experiencing shortness of breath. Upon examination, he is found to have a high heart rate and low blood pressure. Blood tests show elevated levels of white blood cells and C-reactive protein. A chest X-ray reveals signs of pneumonia. He is diagnosed with sepsis according to the "Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International guidelines for management of severe sepsis and septic shock:2012" and is admitted to the ICU for further treatment. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has lived in Yuetan subdistrict for over 10 years.

A 30-year old woman is pregnant with her second child. Her first delivery was a spontaneous vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia. She is currently 38 weeks pregnant and has been attending regular prenatal visits. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies. She works as a teacher and is married with one child. She states that her first delivery was smooth, and she had no complications. She plans to breastfeed her baby and is looking forward to the experience. She is open to participating in a clinical trial that aims to compare maternal outcomes following manual lysis of the placenta. She understands the study's purpose and is willing to be randomly assigned to one of the two groups. She has no history of thalassemia and has not experienced any active bleeding or intrapartum infection during her pregnancy. She is excited to be part of this study and help contribute to improving maternal outcomes during delivery.

Pt is a 23yo M who is a currently enrolled student at Accademia Italiana di Medicina Osteopatica in Saronno, Italy. He is in good health and has no history of oral cavity pathology or drug use. He is not currently taking any oral contraceptives. He has agreed to participate in a study investigating the effect of cranial manipulation on autonomic nervous system activity. During the study, he will be asked to provide saliva samples before and after receiving a specific craniosacral technique, compression of the fourth ventricle CV4, using the salivary marker alpha amylase. The aim of the study is to test the effectiveness of the CV4 technique in modifying physiological parameters related to the activity of the autonomic nervous system. The study will involve four saliva collections from the patient: at the initial time, after administration of a stressful event (hand immersion in ice water), immediately after application of the CV4 technique and thirty minutes after the application of the CV4 technique. The patient will be instructed to abstain from eating, smoking, drinking any beverages and exercising 2h prior to the experiment.

A 52 year old male patient with a history of hypogonadism visited the clinic for follow-up after completing the MTE08 clinical trial. He has been taking the Testosterone MD-Lotion for 4 months with no significant side effects. He is currently on no other medication and has no significant medical history. He reports having a stable mood and energy level since starting the treatment. His PSA level is within the normal range. He is married and his partner is postmenopausal. He is willing to continue participation in the trial and follow the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, currently being treated with non-insulin therapy. He has a body mass index of 36 kg/m2 and has been experiencing symptoms of hypogonadism, such as reduced libido, fatigue, and decreased muscle mass. He has not received any previous treatment for hypogonadism. The patient has no history of prostate or breast cancer, severe benign prostatic hyperplasia, or elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA > 4.0 lg/l). He has not had any acute coronary events or procedures in the past six months and does not have severe heart failure. The patient does not have chronic obstructive lung disease, hypothyroidism, severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), or active infection. He does not have rheumatoid arthritis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is scheduled for an elective cesarean section delivery. She has no known allergies, hepatitis history, or liver/kidney disease. She has not taken Tylenol or any opiates within the last 24 hours. She

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been experiencing recurring chest pain for the past 3 months. He reports that the pain is retrosternal and angina-like, but he has been cleared of any cardiac issues by a cardiologist. He has tried over-the-counter antacids and H2 blockers without relief. He has no history of thoracic, esophageal or gastric surgery, nor does he have any primary or secondary esophageal motility disorders. He is not taking any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or aspirin. An upper endoscopy reveals no signs of Barrett's esophagus, erosive esophagitis, peptic stricture, or duodenal or gastric ulcer. Biopsies were taken and ruled out eosinophilic esophagitis. The patient has no underlying psychiatric illnesses and is not pregnant. He has agreed to participate in a study evaluating the effect of PPI and SSRI therapy for different subtypes of NCCP patients using multichannel intraluminal impedance and pH (MII-pH) monitoring.

A 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, referred by his primary care physician for a transthoracic echocardiogram to evaluate a possible aortic stenosis. The patient reports occasional shortness of breath and fatigue with exertion but has no chest pain or syncope. He denies any history of cardiac surgery or interventions. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. On examination, the patient is hemodynamically stable, with a regular rhythm and no murmurs. The carotid pulse is palpable bilaterally, and no carotid bruits are heard. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He has no open skin lesions at the target site for the Vivio examination.

70-year-old man, fluent in Danish, who has been married to his wife for 40 years. The patient has reported difficulty hearing and understanding his wife, which has caused frustration and tension in their relationship. He feels as if he is missing out on important conversations and has become increasingly isolated. The patient has not sought any psychological help but is interested in participating in an online intervention to help alleviate his emotional distress and improve his relationship with his spouse.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl diagnosed with neuroblastoma. She presents with abdominal distension, poor appetite, and weight loss. She has no significant past medical history and no family history of cancer. The physical examination reveals a palpable mass in the abdomen, and the ultrasound confirms a large retroperitoneal mass. The biopsy confirms the diagnosis of intermediate-risk neuroblastoma. The patient has no abnormal organ function, no paresis, and her performance status is not affected. The patient and her family agree to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with anaplastic thyroid cancer. He has no other medical conditions and has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the past 4 weeks. He is able to perform activities of daily living but has experienced symptoms such as hoarseness, difficulty swallowing, and a lump in his neck. His performance status is Zubrod 1. He has undergone imaging of the neck, brain, and chest/abdomen within the past 4 weeks. The imaging results confirmed the presence of anaplastic thyroid cancer. His blood work shows ANC >= 1,500 cells/mm^3, platelets >= 100,000 cells/mm^3, and hemoglobin >= 9.0 g/dl. His total bilirubin is < 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal, and AST or ALT is

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She has been feeling hopeless, sad, and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. Her Hamilton Depression Scale score is 22. She speaks fluent English and is post-menopausal. She has no history of psychiatric disorders other than major depressive disorder. She has no unstable medical conditions or metal implants in her body. She has no history of alcohol or drug dependence or abuse within the past year. She is not currently taking any excluded medications and has not used any unapproved drugs within the last 30 days. Neither she nor any of her family members work at McLean Hospital.

16 y/o male currently receiving treatment for substance use disorders at the University of Michigan Addiction Treatment Services (UMATS) clinic. He has a history of alcohol use problems and is eligible to participate in the study. He does not have any severe mental illness such as psychotic symptoms, which is an exclusion criterion for the study. The patient will undergo neurophysiological assessments at the beginning and end of the study, as well as participate in the computerized bias retraining treatment protocol. The study will also assess substance use and psychiatric disorders at baseline, 6 weeks after baseline, and 6 months after baseline. The patient will be monitored for drug use through drug tests and will receive cognitive behavioral therapy to assist in reducing any feelings of craving. This clinical trial will help identify brain measures that are associated with treatment response in adolescents with substance use disorders.

The patient is a 45-year-old male of French origin who has been on peritoneal dialysis for the past 6 months. He has end-stage renal disease and has been undergoing regular dialysis sessions to manage his condition. His BMI is 27, and he has social insurance. He is not on any anticoagulant medication, and there is no history of major bleeding or hypersensitivity reactions to apixaban. He is not currently taking any non-steroid anti-inflammatory medication at an anti-inflammatory dosage of more than 300mg. He has not received antibiotic treatment in the past 14 days. He is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

42-year-old female diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) presents with symptoms of insomnia. She has a history of depression for the past 10 years and has been on antidepressants intermittently during this time. She has tried cognitive-behavioral therapy in the past, but it did not help with her insomnia. She reports difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep, waking up frequently during the night, and feeling tired during the day. She denies any history of substance abuse or psychiatric hospitalization. Her current medications include sertraline 50 mg daily, which she has been taking for the past 2 months. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She has no major physical or neurological illness and does not have any contraindications to the use of Seroquel XR.

The patient is a 25-year-old Japanese healthy adult male who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He is currently not taking any prescription medication and has no significant medical history. The patient weighs 68 kg and has a BMI of 22.5 kg/m^2. He is willing to use an appropriate method of contraception throughout the treatment period. The patient does not smoke and does not consume more than 2 servings of caffeinated beverages per day. He has not undergone any blood collection or blood component collection in the past 12 weeks, and has no clinically relevant abnormality in vital signs or ECG. The patient has no history of drug abuse, cancer, or allergies. He is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study.

A 3-year-old boy is experiencing diarrhea for the past 24 hours. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He has no allergies and is up-to-date on his vaccinations. He has been drinking fluids and there have been no signs of dehydration. His parents are concerned and are unsure of what to do. They call the SAMU call center seeking advice. The boy is eligible for the study as per the inclusion criteria for the diarrhea theme. The nurse on the call center platform provides tailored pediatric counseling based on the child's symptoms and history. The family is advised to continue with fluids and a light diet, and to call back if the diarrhea persists or if the child becomes dehydrated. The family is also advised to seek medical attention if the child develops fever, bloody stools, or severe abdominal pain.

The patient is a 25-year-old man diagnosed with schizophrenia who has been admitted to the psychiatric hospital after experiencing a significant increase in paranoid and delusional thinking. He has been struggling with these symptoms for the past year and has been non-compliant with his medication regimen. He reports hearing voices that are telling him to harm himself and others. He has a history of substance abuse, specifically marijuana and alcohol use, but has been sober for the past month. He has no significant medical history and has never received any psychosocial treatment for his condition. He speaks and reads English fluently and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is currently on a pharmacotherapy regimen and will continue to receive this treatment throughout the study. The patient has no significant cognitive impairment and is able to participate in regular hospital groups.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma. She underwent total thyroidectomy with no complications. The patient has no history of hypoparathyroidism or calcium metabolism disorders. Preoperative lab work showed normal serum calcium and PTH levels. The surgery was performed under general anesthesia, and the duration of the procedure was approximately 2 hours. The patient was started on calcium and vitamin D supplementation postoperatively. The patient's hospital course was unremarkable, and she was discharged on the second postoperative day. The patient will be followed up for the next five postoperative days to monitor serum calcium and PTH levels and to assess the presence of symptoms of hypocalcemia. The patient has signed the informed consent form for the study.

A 15-year-old female adolescent presents with a history of emotional hyperresponsiveness, relational instability, identity disturbances, and self-aggressive behavior. She has a history of exposure to traumatic life events, including physical and emotional abuse from her parents. The patient has been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder (BPD) according to the criteria of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for mental disorders, fifth edition (DSM-5). She has a CGA-S score above 20, indicating a level of general psychopathology compatible with participation in the study. The patient also meets the criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) according to DSM-5 criteria. She is fluent in French and is affiliated with the social security scheme. The patient and her legal representatives have signed informed consent for participation in the study. She does not have any other severe chronic psychiatric comorbidity or physical pathology in progress. She is not illiterate or sensory impaired. The patient has not been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, schizophrenia spectrum disorder, and other psychotic disorders, or bipolar disorder. She does not have a history of severe head trauma, anoxic coma, or contraindication to MRI. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not participating in any other biomedical research protocol during the present study.

A 55-year-old female with type 2 diabetes presents with a history of a recently healed plantar ulceration on her left foot. She reports that she is currently not experiencing any foot pain or discomfort. She has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is on medication for both conditions. She reports that she is physically active and enjoys walking. The patient has no history of peripheral neuropathy, untreated infection, osteomyelitis, or gangrene. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the effect of therapist-directed versus self-directed re-loading on the incidence of ulcer recurrence.

55 yo F with a history of T2DM, hyperlipidemia, and hypertension presents with symptoms of worsening heart failure, including shortness of breath on exertion, fatigue, and lower extremity edema. She has a past medical history significant for a myocardial infarction 5 years ago and has been on optimal medical therapy including ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and diuretics. An echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 30% and left bundle branch block. She is a candidate for cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator (CRT-D) and is enrolled in a clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of multipolar left ventricle (LV) lead pacing versus bipolar LV pacing in T2DM patients with stable chronic heart failure. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and provides informed consent to participate. She is randomized to receive the CRT-D via multipolar LV lead pacing and is followed up for 12 months. During the follow-up period, her lead functionality parameters, arrhythmic events, PNS episodes, LV catheter dislodgments, and clinical outcomes are monitored and recorded.

45 yo female with a strong family history of breast cancer. Patient's mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 42 and her maternal aunt was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 50. Patient has been seen by her primary care physician within the past year and has expressed concern about her risk for developing breast cancer. Patient's Gail Model score indicates that she is at high risk for developing breast cancer. She has not undergone genetic testing but is interested in exploring her options for breast cancer prevention. Patient is a fluent English speaker and has no history of breast cancer or LCIS. She has no reading or vision difficulties and has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to pilot a web-based decision aid system for breast cancer prevention.

A 63-year-old man recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He underwent a biopsy after a routine check-up and was found to have a Gleason score 8 prostate adenocarcinoma. His PSA level was 120 ng/mL. Imaging studies showed no evidence of metastases. He has no history of heart disease or neuropathy. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history. He is currently asymptomatic but is concerned about the potential progression of his disease. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of chemotherapy in prostate cancer.

A 42-year-old female presents with a newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer. A biopsy confirms the tumor is hormone receptor-negative and HER2-positive. Her medical history includes a previous surgery for an ovarian cyst and a history of hypertension which is controlled with medication. She has never received any anti-cancer therapy or radiation for any malignancy. Recent laboratory tests show normal liver, kidney and hematologic function, with a serum creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL, AST of 25 U/L and ALT of 20 U/L. Echocardiography shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. She has no evidence of any other serious medical condition or any mental health issues. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

12 year-old male diagnosed with Crohn disease of the small bowel. He has been undergoing treatment for the past year, which has included a combination of immunosuppressant medication and dietary changes. He has had several MR enterography (MRE) scans to monitor the status of his disease. The most recent MRE showed some improvement in disease activity, but the patient continues to experience some symptoms, including abdominal pain and diarrhea. The patient has been referred for a follow-up imaging study and is being considered for inclusion in a clinical trial comparing the accuracy of bowel ultrasound to MRE in the follow-up of pediatric small bowel Crohn disease. The patient has no history of metal implants or other contraindications to MRE imaging.

A 25-year-old woman who is fluent in English and in good general health is interested in participating in the NIMH IRP clinical studies as a healthy research volunteer. She has no history of significant medical or mental health conditions requiring treatment and has never endorsed self-injury or suicidal thoughts or behavior. She denies the use of illicit drugs and has never been found to have an abnormal physical exam or laboratory result that may require treatment or further evaluation. She has completed high school education and has an IQ above 70. She is not an NIMH employee, staff member, or first degree relative of an NIMH employee or staff member. She is comfortable with having a brain MRI scan and does not have metal in her body that would make having an MRI scan unsafe. She does not have any discomfort in small closed spaces and can lie comfortably on her back for at least 45 minutes. She is not pregnant and does not have any metal in her body that would cause artifacts on MEG recordings.

A 48-year-old Taiwanese female patient with a history of hypertension and non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) presented to the hospital with complaints of fatigue and shortness of breath. She also reported experiencing occasional chest pain and palpitations. The patient's medical history included type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and hyperlipidemia. Her current medications included metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. Her physical examination revealed a heart rate of 98 beats per minute and a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg. Laboratory tests showed a serum creatinine level of 1.9 mg/dL and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 35 mL/min/1.73m2. An electrocardiogram (ECG) confirmed the presence of NVAF. The patient's treating physician decided to initiate treatment with Xarelto for the prevention of brain attack and blockage of an artery in the non-central nervous system. The patient was informed about the study to gain information on the safety of Xarelto and was enrolled in the study. She will be followed up for 12 months to collect information on her well-being and any medical events.

The patient is a 58-year-old Caucasian man who was diagnosed with colorectal adenocarcinoma. His primary tumor is located on the right side of his colon, and radiologic evidence suggests that he has initial unresectable liver metastases. His RAS/BRAF gene is confirmed to be wild-type. His ECOG score is 1, and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 6 months. He has good hematological function, with a neutrophil count of 2.1x109/l, a platelet count of 120x109/l, and an HB level of 12g/dl. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has signed the written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He has no known hypersensitivity to any component of the study treatment. He has no clinical related coronary heart disease or history of myocardial infarction in the last 12 months, and his left ventricular ejection fraction is within the normal range. He has no acute or subacute intestinal obstruction. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no other malignant tumors within the last 5 years, except for skin basal cell carcinoma. He does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has legal capacity. He has no peripheral neuropathy.

A 52-year-old male with a history of glioblastoma multiforme presented with symptoms of headache and confusion. MRI showed a large enhancing mass in the left temporal lobe. He underwent surgical resection of the tumor with histopathological confirmation of glioblastoma multiforme. He received radiation and chemotherapy with temozolomide for six months. However, the patient developed recurrent symptoms of headache and confusion after six months, and the MRI showed a new enhancing mass in the same location. The patient's KPS score is 80, and he is able to perform activities of daily living independently. He has no history of other malignancy and is not currently on any other investigational therapy. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is adequately controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history, and he is not currently on any medication that may interact with the study treatment. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) six months ago. He has undergone chemotherapy, but his disease has relapsed. His oncologist has recommended an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) from a partially matched related donor or an unrelated donor. The patient has a brother who is a two antigen mismatched donor. The patient has no history of heart disease or liver dysfunction, and his kidney function is normal. He has a performance status of 80% (TJU Karnofsky) and an HCT-CI score of 3 points. He is willing to use contraception if he is of childbearing potential. His HIV test is negative.

48-year-old woman with a history of immobilization for 6 weeks following surgical repair of a severe Achilles tendon tear. She has been experiencing persistent pain in the affected leg and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate muscle properties and tension. She is able to cooperate and follow simple commands. She has no known history of stroke, myofascial pain, or hyperthyroidism. She is in overall good health with no other significant medical history or comorbidities.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman with a history of chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) and recurrent sinus infections. She has been experiencing symptoms such as facial pain, pressure, nasal congestion, postnasal drip, and a decreased sense of smell for the past 6 months. She has tried multiple courses of antibiotics and nasal steroid sprays without significant improvement. The patient has not used antibiotics in the past year and has not had any other airway infections or autoimmune diseases. She is not pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the microbiota of the upper respiratory tract in CRS patients to help better understand the pathology of her condition and potentially develop new treatment strategies.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who recently noticed bleeding while brushing her teeth. She has never been to a dentist before and has not had any prior dental treatment. She is a non-smoker and does not have any chronic medical conditions. Her oral examination reveals generalized redness and swelling of the gums with significant plaque accumulation. Her gingival bleeding index (GBI) is higher than 85%. She is interested in natural herbal products and is willing to participate in the study to improve her oral health. She is not under any regular medication or antibiotic therapy and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She uses regular toothpaste for oral hygiene.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to Rochester Methodist Hospital due to chest pain and shortness of breath. During the admission process, it was discovered that the patient had been a smoker for the past 20 years and was smoking a pack of cigarettes per day. The patient expressed his desire to quit smoking, and the healthcare team informed him about the current clinical trial that aims to help hospitalized patients quit smoking. The patient was interested in participating in the study and met the inclusion criteria as a current smoker, a resident of Olmsted County, and able to participate fully in all study aspects. The patient was not receiving any active treatment for tobacco use before hospitalization, which made him eligible for the study. The healthcare team approached the patient with the study details, and he agreed to participate in the study. The patient was randomized to receive either a brief quitline facilitation intervention or a control intervention of a brief stop-smoking message. The study will follow up with the patient after discharge to assess smoking abstinence rates and healthcare costs and utilization in the first six months following hospitalization.

The patient is a 2-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with an embryonal central nervous system tumor. He presents with symptoms such as headaches, vomiting, and difficulty walking. His parents noticed that he had a loss of coordination and balance, and he seemed to have trouble with his vision. He has no significant past medical history, and his family has no history of cancer. He has undergone a biopsy of the tumor, which confirmed the diagnosis of a medulloblastoma. His physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any other abnormalities. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, and he is not currently taking any investigational agents. The child's parents are willing to participate in this study to help advance the understanding of the genetic processes involved in his cancer.

55-year-old woman who has been post-menopausal for over a year and is in good health overall. She has a BMI of 28 and has never smoked or used drugs. She has a history of a normal mammogram and Papanicolaou test within the last 13 months. She does not have a history of breast cancer or a high risk of developing it according to the NCI's Breast Cancer Risk Assessment Tool. She is not on hormone or estrogen therapy and has not taken SERMs within the last 3 months. She has normal thyroid and endocrine function tests and is not taking any thyroid medication. She has not used antibiotics within the last 3 months and has no history of substance abuse or addiction. Her alcohol intake is less than 2 drinks per day and she does not use tobacco. She is willing and able to reduce her soy intake below 20mg genistein/day or 40mg isoflavone/day during the study period. She is able to read and comprehend the Informed Consent and has a life expectancy of at least 6 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a BMI of 30.5 kg/m2 who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years. He has been taking metformin and following a low-calorie diet, but his blood sugar levels are still not well-controlled. He has never smoked or consumed alcohol excessively. He has no history of infections or active inflammatory disorders. He has not received any immunomodulating treatment or undergone bariatric surgery. He is planning to start treatment with liraglutide and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to understand the immunological effects of this medication on his diabetes and obesity.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with Crohn's disease two years ago. He experiences frequent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He has been on medication to manage his symptoms but has recently experienced a flare-up. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide blood, urine, and stool samples. He is also willing to undergo a diagnostic colonoscopy as part of routine Crohn's disease care. The patient is not pregnant.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage I endometrial cancer last year. She underwent total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and is currently in remission. She is obese with a BMI of 31. She is a retired teacher and has been married for 30 years. She has two adult children and three grandchildren. She is concerned about her weight and wants to improve her quality of life. She has a sedentary lifestyle and her diet is high in processed foods and carbohydrates. She has no significant medical history, and her physical exam is unremarkable, except for her weight. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. She is interested in participating in a program that will help her lose weight and improve her quality of life. She is willing to commit to weekly contact with a dietitian and exercise intervention for 6 months, and physician counseling at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months. She is also willing to undergo quality of life assessments and clinical assessments at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months.

The patient is a 10-year-old child who was recently diagnosed with leukemia. The child's primary caregiver, the mother, is 35 years old and is willing to participate in the study. The child and the mother are both fluent in English and have no cognitive impairment. The child is expected to have continuous contact with the Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital for the next three weeks due to chemotherapy treatment. The mother is willing to attend appointments, infusion visits, or be present in hospital rooms/clinics as needed. Both the child and the mother are willing to participate in Yoga sessions as part of a dyad to help manage the psychological and physiological stress associated with chemotherapy infusion.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with invasive pulmonary aspergillosis. He has been receiving treatment with voriconazole for the past week. He is 185 cm tall and weighs 80 kg. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is willing and able to provide informed consent and to be confined to the Clinical Research Unit as required by the protocol. He has not experienced any adverse effects from the voriconazole treatment so far. His labs are within normal limits. He has no conditions that would affect drug absorption.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with chronic heart failure. She experiences shortness of breath, fatigue, and difficulty exercising. She has been on diuretics and afterload reducing agents for the past month, which have helped manage her symptoms but have not improved her overall heart function. She has been classified as NYHA class III. Her echocardiogram shows severe left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 25%. She has been referred to the study by her cardiologist and is interested in participating in the CRT pilot study for children with heart failure.

54-year-old male with a history of metastatic prostate cancer presents to the oncology clinic complaining of increased fatigue and worsening bone pain. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He underwent prostatectomy two years ago after being diagnosed with prostate cancer and received radiation therapy for bone metastases one year ago. His most recent laboratory values show a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level of 25 ng/mL (normal range < 4 ng/mL). A bone scan shows multiple new metastatic lesions. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to perform most activities of daily living without assistance. He is currently not receiving any chemotherapy or immunotherapy. The patient is informed of the clinical trial and expresses interest in participating. He is able to provide written informed consent and meets all of the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer. He has undergone one line of previous treatment, but the disease has progressed. The patient has a history of smoking and has a pack-year history of 45. He has a performance status of 1 and has no significant comorbidities. The patient has been experiencing symptoms such as cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. The patient has undergone a CT scan, which revealed metastatic lesions in the lungs and lymph nodes. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study.

A 35 year old man is scheduled for an elective surgery to remove his gallbladder due to recurrent stones. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history, and is classified as American Society of Anaesthesiologist Physical Status 2. He weighs 80 kg and has a mouth opening of 3 cm. He has given oral and written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He has no pharyngeal, laryngeal or tracheal pathology, and no history of airway infections. He has no psychiatric disease or dementia. He is not pregnant and not breastfeeding. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trial.

A 55-year-old male was recently diagnosed with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML). He had a history of high blood pressure and had been on amlodipine for 3 years. He was otherwise in good health, had no complaints of fatigue or fever, and had a normal physical examination. His blood work showed a white blood cell count of 20,000/µL, with 80% monocytes, 10% granulocytes, and 10% lymphocytes. His hemoglobin was 12 g/dL, and his platelet count was 50,000/µL. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of CMML. He was not receiving any treatment for CMML at the time of diagnosis. He was interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ruxolitinib. He was informed about the potential risks and benefits of the study and provided informed consent. He met all the eligibility criteria for the study and was enrolled in the phase 1/2, two-stage, sequential cohort dose escalation study.

The patient is a 34-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained multiple rib fractures on both sides of his chest. He is currently hospitalized and experiencing significant pain, which is affecting his ability to breathe deeply and cough. He is requesting regional anesthesia for pain control and is willing to participate in a cryoneurolysis procedure. He has no history of chronic opioid use and is not currently pregnant. He is able to communicate effectively with the investigators and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. He has no localized infection at the treatment site or any contraindications specific to cryoneurolysis. He is able to correctly perform incentive spirometry, which is an outcome measure for this study. The investigator believes that study participation would be in the patient's best interest.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with CLL. He has experienced fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats for a few months. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a former smoker and quit 5 years ago. The physical exam is remarkable for palpable lymph nodes in the neck and axilla, and he has splenomegaly. The laboratory results show elevated white blood cell count (50,000) and low hemoglobin (10.5). The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has no contraindication to chemotherapy as first-line therapy. He has not received any previous treatment with rituximab, alemtuzumab, ofatumumab or any other chemotherapeutic agent for CLL.

A 12-month-old healthy boy is brought in by his parents for routine vaccination. He was born full term with no complications during pregnancy or delivery. He has been meeting all developmental milestones on time and has had no major illnesses or hospitalizations. He has received all routine vaccinations according to the recommended schedule. He lives with his parents and older sibling who is currently attending preschool. Both parents report being up-to-date with their vaccinations. The child has not had any recent exposure to anyone with measles, mumps, rubella, or chickenpox. The parents are interested in enrolling their child in this clinical trial to receive the GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) Biologicals combined vaccine to prevent these diseases.

A 42-year-old female office worker presents with numbness and tingling in her right hand, mainly in the thumb, index, and middle fingers. The symptoms are worse at night and wake her up from sleep. She has no history of trauma to the wrist or hand. She has never had any surgery on the wrist or hand. She has no known allergies to corticosteroids and local anesthetics. She has never been diagnosed with any neurological disorders. She is otherwise healthy and takes no regular medications. She was diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome through electrophysiological tests and is being offered a steroid injection as part of a clinical trial to assess sonographic changes of the median nerve.

A 28-year-old man who identifies as Khothi or Double-decker and resides in Tamil Nadu state, India, is eligible for this clinical trial. He has engaged in unprotected sex with another man within the past 3 months. He is able to understand and complete the informed consent procedures. The patient is not transgendered or under the age of 18. The patient may have concerns about discrimination and violence in the stigmatizing environment surrounding MSM in India. The patient may also struggle with issues related to self-acceptance, substance use, and social support. The patient is interested in participating in a behavioral HIV prevention intervention that addresses these psychosocial issues and aims to reduce HIV risk.

A 35-year-old male with a history of NAFLD and HbA1c level of 6.2%, complains of fatigue and poor appetite. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally, but not more than 2 drinks per week. He has a BMI of 25 and has never undergone bariatric surgery. He has no known allergies to drugs or any liver diseases other than NAFLD. He has not taken any regular medication, drugs or herbals known to affect liver physiology. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and has provided signed informed consent. His liver biopsy was performed six months ago, and it showed a mild accumulation of intrahepatic fat. He has no inflammatory bowel conditions, viral hepatitis, or fructose malabsorption. He has no implants or prostheses that might interfere with the MRI. He is interested in participating in the study to gain better insights into the pathogenesis and progression of NAFLD and to contribute to the development of future dietary interventions and regulatory actions.

The patient is a 12-year-old male with a history of asthma for the past 5 years. He presents with symptoms of wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath, which are often triggered by exposure to allergens such as dust mites and pet dander. Despite his current treatment regimen of albuterol as needed and daily use of inhaled corticosteroids, he reports that his asthma symptoms are only partially controlled. He has experienced two exacerbations of asthma within the past year, which required oral corticosteroids and a visit to the emergency department. Skin prick tests have shown that he is allergic to dust mites and cat dander. He has not received any bacterial lysate immunostimulation or allergen immunotherapy within the past 6 months.
