The patient and his parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the potential benefits of Polyvalent Mechanical Bacterial Lysate (PMBL - Ismigen®) as an add-on treatment to his current asthma therapy.

Maria is a 56-year-old woman who was admitted to the ICU with pneumonia and sepsis. She has a history of hypertension, but otherwise has been in good health. Her condition has not improved despite aggressive antibiotic therapy and mechanical ventilation. She is currently on enteral nutrition, but is losing weight and has been diagnosed with moderate to severe malnutrition. Her expected length of stay in the ICU is greater than 10 days. She is tolerating enteral feeds and has no known allergies to nandrolone. She is not pregnant and has no history of breast or prostate cancer. She is not on anticoagulation therapy and does not require renal replacement therapy. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve her nutritional status and overall health outcomes.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past year. She works as a nurse and spends most of her day on her feet, which exacerbates her pain. She has tried several treatments, including physical therapy and over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not provided long-lasting relief. Her primary care physician has prescribed her a stable dose of NSAID, which has been helping to manage her pain. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatments and potentially find a long-term solution for her pain. She has no history of fibromyalgia, complex regional pain syndrome, uveitis or inflammatory bowel disease. She has not undergone any spinal surgery and is willing to provide informed written consent. She has tested negative for TB within the past 4 weeks.

The patient is a 72 year old man who lives alone after the passing of his wife. He has been experiencing occasional episodes of forgetfulness and confusion, which have been causing him distress. He has also been feeling down and not interested in activities he used to enjoy. He has never been diagnosed with depression before. He has mild hypertension that is being treated with medication. He has no other significant medical history. He is retired and spends most of his time at home watching TV or reading. He has been advised to increase his physical activity by his doctor. He eats fish once a week and has never taken fish oil supplements. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain for the past few months. She presents to the hospital with worsening symptoms and is diagnosed with symptomatic moderate to severe valvular heart disease on admission. She is found to have moderate to severe mitral valve regurgitation and a mitral valve area of 1.4cm2. She is hospitalized for elective valve surgery (mitral valve repair) and is consecutively included in the study. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are controlled with medication. She reports no other significant medical history and is otherwise in good health. She is a Dutch-speaking woman and is expected to have a length of stay greater than 48 hours. The patient has a life expectancy greater than 6 months.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with supratentorial intracerebral hemorrhage. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is otherwise healthy. She was admitted to the hospital 2 days ago and her Glasgow Coma Score is 14. She is able to provide informed consent to participate in the study. She has no known inflammatory conditions or active infections and is not pregnant. She is not currently taking any anti-inflammatory medications. She does not have any lower extremity injuries or weight over 250 kg. She is motivated to participate in the study and follow the exercise regimen as instructed. Her family is supportive of her participation in the study.

Patient is a 34-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He has no significant past medical history and is not allergic to any medication. He is willing to participate in the study and able to provide written informed consent. He has no contraindication or intolerance to any of the components of the standard chemotherapy by induction (7+3). His physical examination is unremarkable except for some mild fatigue. The laboratory study shows a white blood cell count of 75,000/mm3 with 50% blasts, hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 30,000/mm3. Bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of AML.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who works in a corporate setting in a mid-level management position. He has been experiencing high levels of stress due to the demands of his job and the recent changes in his department. He has noticed that his stress levels have been affecting his sleep and overall well-being. The patient is fluent in English and is willing to attend a full day training program at the Lake Nona Institute during the designated training date. He is willing to provide email and phone number as a contact method and has a valid e-mail address. He is able to comprehend and follow the requirements of the study and is willing and able to comply with all study procedures for the duration of the study. The patient meets the stress or resilience parameters as defined by the study and is willing to consent and sign the Informed Consent Form.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with a neuroendocrine tumor. The tumor is located in her small intestine and was found during a routine colonoscopy. She has no significant medical history and her family history is negative for any cancer. She currently works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She is interested in participating in the SwissNET registry to help contribute to the understanding and management of neuroendocrine tumors. She understands the importance of giving informed consent and is willing to provide the necessary information for the registry.

58-year-old female with a history of smoking and a recent diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. The patient has undergone initial treatment with chemotherapy, but unfortunately, the cancer has continued to progress. The patient has a PD-L1 positive tumor and is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring new treatments for her type of cancer. She is in good general health aside from her cancer diagnosis, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1. She has no known sensitizing epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) or anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) mutation expression. The patient has at least one measurable lesion per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST v1.1). She has not received any live vaccines against infectious diseases in the past 28 days and does not have a concurrent medical condition requiring the use of supra-physiologic doses of corticosteroids or immunosuppressive medications. The patient has not tested positive for Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C virus antibody, Hepatitis C qualitative RNA or human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) antibody. She has no active autoimmune disease or a documented history of autoimmune disease or syndrome that required systemic treatment in the past 2 years, except for resolved childhood asthma. The patient has not had any prior malignancy active within the previous 2 years.

The patient is a 75-year-old man who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and valvular heart disease. He has undergone previous cardiac surgery and has pre-existing renal impairment with a plasma creatinine concentration of 1.6 mg/dL. His left ventricular ejection fraction is below 50% and he is classified as New York Heart Association class III/IV. He has insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus but is otherwise healthy. The patient has been offered valvular surgery or concomitant valvular and coronary artery bypass graft surgery. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy and safety of intravenous sodium bicarbonate in preventing acute kidney injury following cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who works as a nurse at a local hospital. He consumes an average of four sugar-sweetened beverages per week and is interested in improving his overall health and wellness. He is proficient in English and able to commit to attending all three study visits over the course of 12 months. The patient does not anticipate taking any extended leave of absence or family medical leave during the study period.

52yo male with a history of osteonecrosis of the femoral head and severe hip pain, which has failed conservative management. He has undergone a total hip arthroplasty (THA) without cement at the Institute of Orthopedics and Traumatology, Hospital das Clinicas, Faculty of Medicine, University of São Paulo (IOT - HC - USP). The patient's BMI is 34, classifying him as obese (class II). He has no systemic involvement and has received a prosthetic type Lépine. The patient is able to walk with the aid of crutches but experiences significant discomfort in the operated leg. The patient is willing to participate in the study to determine the effect of early load versus late load on the rehabilitation of THA patients.

35-year-old male diagnosed with AIDS-related complex (ARC) with a CD4+ cell count between 100 and 300 cells/mm3, and an estimated life expectancy of at least 6 months. The patient has not received any systemic medications, radiation therapy, or potential nephrotoxins, or neutropenic agents within 72 hours prior to study entry. The patient is not currently on any biologic response modifier agents, corticosteroids, cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents, rifampin or rifampin derivatives, systemic anti-infectives, or phenytoin or barbiturates. The patient has not been diagnosed with any active opportunistic infection requiring ongoing therapy, except for being treated topically for oral thrush. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to polyene antibiotics. The patient is willing to sign an informed consent and comply with all protocol requirements.

6-year-old male, with a recent history of recurrent headaches and vomiting, was referred to the pediatric neurology department for evaluation. MRI showed no abnormalities but a lumbar puncture was recommended to rule out meningitis. The patient has no known allergies and no history of previous lumbar punctures. He has no significant medical history and is up to date on all vaccinations. The patient and his parents have given informed consent to participate in the study to establish an optimized lumbar puncture management process. The patient is able to understand the procedure and has expressed his willingness to participate. The patient does not have any skin infections or coagulopathy. The patient's vital signs are stable and he is able to lie still during the procedure. The patient will be evaluated using the FLACC scale to assess his level of pain during and after the lumbar puncture. The patient will not be included in the study if there is a need for repeated puncture during the procedure.

A 38-year-old woman with a history of scleroderma presented to the clinic complaining of shortness of breath, fatigue, and decreased exercise capacity. She was diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) three months ago and is currently receiving treatment with sildenafil. Her WHO functional class is II. She reports limited physical activity due to her symptoms. Her BMI is 23 and she does not have any other known medical conditions. She does not smoke and is not currently taking any medications other than sildenafil.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with substance abuse for several years. She has attempted to quit on her own multiple times, but has been unsuccessful. She is now seeking help and has enrolled in a residential substance use treatment program at a Veteran's Administration hospital. She is open to trying new approaches to treatment and is interested in pursuing hobbies such as gardening or music as a way to aid in her recovery. She has no known comorbid psychiatric disorders or medical issues that would prevent her from participating in the Natural Recovery Program.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with locally advanced adenocarcinoma non-small cell lung cancer 2 months ago. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and molecular testing revealed an EGFR mutation. She has no significant medical history and her ECOG performance status is 1. Her latest physical examination and laboratory tests revealed the following results: Weight: 65 kg Height: 165 cm BP: 120/80 HR: 80/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 12.5 g/dL WBC: 8000 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 5500/mm3) Plt: 250000 /ml AST: 30 U/L ALT: 40 U/L Alk P: 110 U/L Bill total: 0.7 mg/dL ESR: 25 mm/hr. She is currently not receiving any systemic anti-cancer treatment and is a suitable candidate for treatment with Tarceva according to the Summary of Product Characteristics and local label.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) for the past year. He reports having difficulty starting and stopping his stream, as well as having to urinate frequently throughout the day and night. He has tried various medications to alleviate his symptoms, but has not experienced significant improvement. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history and takes no medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a sales executive and is able to work from home most of the time. He is interested in participating in the ProVerum First in Man PROVE Study to potentially improve his symptoms of BPH and avoid the need for surgery in the future. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol, including regular follow-up visits and procedures.

A 50-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. She has a history of gallstone disease and has had previous episodes of biliary colic. On physical examination, she has tenderness in the right upper quadrant and a positive Murphy's sign. Laboratory tests show elevated bilirubin levels and liver enzymes, specifically aspartate transaminase (ASAT) and alanine aminotransferase (ALAT). An ultrasound of the abdomen reveals dilated common bile ducts and a suspicion of common bile duct (CBD) stones. The patient is informed of the possibility of an MRCP or an intraoperative cholangiography during cholecystectomy to investigate the presence of CBD stones. She consents to participate in the study and is randomized to the operation first pathway. The patient undergoes cholecystectomy and an intraoperative cholangiography is performed, revealing the presence of CBD stones. The stones are successfully removed during the same operation, and the patient is discharged from the hospital after two days. All data related to her hospital stay are entered into an online database as part of the study.

45-year-old male with a history of manual labor presents with chronic pain in his right elbow. The patient reports pain over the lateral humeral epicondyle which has been ongoing for the past 9 months. The pain is aggravated by gripping and resisted wrist/middle finger extension. The patient reports a VAS score of 70/100. The patient has not received any treatment for elbow pain by a health care practitioner in the preceding 6 months. The patient has no concomitant neck or other arm pain causing disability or requiring treatment within the last 6 months. The patient denies any history of upper limb fractures or prior elbow surgery. The patient has not received an elbow steroid injection in the past 3 months. The patient has no history of systemic inflammatory disorder or malignancy. The patient is not pregnant nor breastfeeding.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with a singleton pregnancy. She is in her 37th week of gestation and requires continuous electronic fetal monitoring during labour. She has no known gross fetal abnormalities and has not experienced any complications during her pregnancy. The woman has a history of a previous uncomplicated vaginal delivery and is in good health. She is able to give consent to participate in the trial as judged by the attending clinicians.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on hemodialysis for the past 3 years. He has a dysfunctional arteriovenous (AV) fistula in the upper extremity that has been causing him discomfort and limited blood flow during dialysis. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia that are well-controlled with medications. He is compliant with his current dialysis regimen and has no other significant medical problems. His lab results are within normal limits, including his hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelet count. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the purpose of the study. He has no history of major surgeries within the past 30 days and is not planning to have any in the next 30 days.

This is a 25 year-old female who is currently not pregnant and not breastfeeding. She has regular menstrual cycles and is willing to participate in a study involving the collection and analysis of urine samples to determine the existence of alternating redox status between two consecutive menstrual cycles. She does not smoke or use any form of hormonal contraceptives, nor does she use any hormonal therapies for acne or other conditions. She does not have any significant medical disorders that could potentially affect the study results. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available to participate for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old male who was referred to the ED by his school due to behavioral problems. He comes from a middle-class family and lives with both parents and two younger siblings. He is in the 7th grade and has been struggling with his grades and has been showing signs of aggression towards his classmates. He is not involved in any extracurricular activities and has no history of medical or psychiatric problems. His parents are willing to provide informed consent for him to participate in the study, and he is willing to provide assent.

The patient is a 4-month-old infant who was born via vaginal delivery and has a birth weight between the 10th and 90th percentile for gestational age. The infant has been breastfed for at least 4 weeks and at least half of their feeds have been from breastfeeding. The infant is no longer exclusively breastfed and if they are still breastfeeding, it is no more than once a day. The infant does not have a family history of celiac disease, any known allergies or intolerances to cow's milk protein, and has not received any antibiotics or probiotics in the week prior to inclusion in the study. The infant's parents are willing and able to participate in the study for the entire duration.

A 28-year-old male who identifies as homosexual presented with a history of no significant medical conditions. He reports regular sexual activity with male partners, with a recent history of condom use. He has no history of injecting drug use or high-risk sexual behavior. His last HIV test was negative 3 months ago. His CD4 count is within normal range. He has no known allergies to egg products or neomycin. He has not received any live attenuated vaccines within 60 days prior to study entry or experimental agents within 30 days prior to study entry. He has not received any prior HIV vaccines or rabies immunization. He has not received any blood products or immunoglobulin within 6 months prior to study entry. He has no history of immunodeficiency, chronic illness, autoimmune disease, or use of immunosuppressive medications. He has no history of anaphylaxis or other serious adverse reactions to vaccines. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has no occupational responsibilities that preclude compliance. He has negative ELISA and Western blot for HIV. He is willing to receive frequent injections of ALVAC-HIV vCP205 or ALVAC-RG rabies glycoprotein (vCP65) at days 0, 7, 14, and 21, followed by boost with rgp120/HIV-1 SF2 at days 28 and 84 or ALVAC-HIV vCP65 on the same schedule followed by boost with placebo.

Patient is a healthy 7-week-old infant with no known medical conditions or history of S. pneumoniae infection or vaccination. The infant's parent is willing to provide voluntary written/thumb-printed informed consent and comply with study requirements and procedures. The infant has not received any investigational medicinal products prior to randomization and has not received any other vaccines within 30 days of study start. The infant has no history of anaphylactic shock or allergic reactions to vaccines and has not been diagnosed with a blood disorder or primary immunodeficiency. The infant has not had meningitis, seizures, or any neurological disorders. The parent understands that the study will involve the administration of either Pneumosil or Synflorix vaccines, with the possibility of a booster dose at 9 months of age, and is willing to participate in the assessment of immune responses and safety of the vaccines.

The patient is a 9-year-old Nigerian girl who is presented by her parents due to short stature. Her parents noticed that their daughter's height is not in line with her age and she is shorter than her peers. She has no significant medical history and no family history of growth disorders. On examination, her height is 120 cm (-3.5 SD) and her weight is 25 kg (25th percentile). There are no physical abnormalities or dysmorphic features. Her bone age is 8 years old. Her pre-treatment IGF-1 level is 100 ng/mL (-1.5 SD). Her peak GH level after stimulation is above 10ng/ml. She has not received any prior treatment with chemotherapy, radiation or steroids. Her BMI is 20 (50th percentile) and her puberty status is Tanner 1. The patient and her parents are able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 25-year-old pregnant woman came to the clinic for a regular antenatal check-up. She was diagnosed with HIV 2 years ago and has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) since then. She is currently on DTG for the past 6 months with good adherence. She has a history of hypertension and is currently well-controlled with medications. She has no history of any other chronic illness or significant medical problems during her pregnancy. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use any recreational drugs. She is eager to participate in the study to help advance scientific knowledge and improve the health of other HIV positive pregnant women. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with them.

A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman who has completed her last natural menstrual period at least 12 months ago is seeking treatment for hot flashes. She experiences a minimum of 7 moderate to severe hot flashes per day or 50 per week, which are recorded for 7 consecutive days. Her BMI is less than or equal to 34 kg/m2. She has no history or suspicion of estrogen-dependent neoplasia, malignancy, or treatment for malignancy within the previous 2 years. She has no active or recent arterial thromboembolic disease and no history of venous thromboembolism. She also has no history of cerebrovascular accident, stroke, or transient ischemic attack. She has no major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, psychotic disorder, or generalized anxiety disorder requiring therapy. Her blood pressure is within normal limits. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of DVS-233 SR for the treatment of hot flashes associated with menopause.

The patient is a 35 year old Caucasian male with a body mass index (BMI) of 45 kg/m2. He has a past medical history of hypertension and sleep apnea, which are both managed with medications. He has tried multiple diets and exercise programs to lose weight but has been unsuccessful in achieving significant weight loss. He is scheduled to undergo bariatric surgery to improve his health and quality of life. His preoperative laboratory values are within normal limits, including his blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine, and lactate levels. He has no history of cardiac arrhythmias, peripheral artery disease, or significant pulmonary pathology. The patient is able to perform respiratory volume >6 ml/kg/min on mechanical ventilation. He has no history of hepatic or renal impairment. He is aware of the risks and benefits of the surgery and has provided informed consent for the study. He has been randomly assigned to the PVI group, where fluid management will be based on PVI values. Anesthesia induction will be done with 2 mg/kg propofol and 1μgr/kg remifentanil. Propofol dose will be adjusted to keep the bispectral index scale (BIS) between 40 and 45 throughout the operation. Crystalloid replacement will be adjusted according to the PVI values, which will be targeted to be kept below 13% above 5%. If PVI is >13% for more than 5 minutes, a 250 ml bolus Gelofusine® will be administered. If PVI is still >13% following this, it will be repeated every 5 minutes until PVI<13%. Meanwhile, 5 mg bolus ephedrine will be administered to keep mean blood pressure over 65 mmHg, when necessary. He will be monitored for PVI, heart rate, mean arterial pressure, perfusion index value, and other parameters throughout the operation. Postoperative laboratory values, urine output, and fluid intake will be recorded. The patient will be followed up for postoperative complications related to fluid management.

8-year-old male child who has been experiencing compulsive behavior such as excessive handwashing and organizing items in a cluttered area. His parents note that he spends more time in the bathroom and is often late for school because of this. The child also exhibits repetitive behaviors with light switches, turning them on and off repeatedly before leaving the room. He has no other medical conditions and is otherwise healthy. The child's parents have provided written informed consent for him to participate in this study.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Behçet's disease and has a history of recurrent uveitis in her left eye. She has experienced at least two exacerbations of intermediate uveitis in the past six months that have caused a decrease in visual acuity. She has been taking prednisone at a dose of 15mg daily, and her condition has not improved. She has not received any intravitreal corticosteroid injections in the past six weeks. She has not received any systemic biologic therapy in the past three months. She has not been treated with cyclophosphamide or chlorambucil. She has not received any live or live-attenuated vaccines in the past two months. She is interested in participating in the study to see if SQ AIN457 can reduce the rate of exacerbations of uveitis in her left eye.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of advanced non-small cell lung cancer. The patient has received two or more standard treatment schemes according to NCCN Non-small cell lung cancer guidelines, but has not responded to treatment. The patient's cancer tissue has tested positive for ++ or +++ thioredoxin reductase expression, making them eligible for the study. The patient has an anticipated overall survival of more than 3 months and an ECOG performance status of 0-2. They have not received chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery in the past 4 weeks and have normal blood counts. The patient is negative for EGFR/ALK mutations and does not have symptoms of brain metastasis. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any serious uncontrolled diseases. The patient's urine protein levels are within normal limits.

Patient is a female aged 35 years who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. The patient's tumor has been classified as triple negative breast cancer, and she is scheduled to undergo surgery to remove the tumor. The patient has consented to donate her tumor sample to the NUHS Tissue Repository for research purposes. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to help uncover potential biomarkers and drug targets for breast cancer. The patient understands that there is no direct benefit to her, but hopes that her participation will contribute to the development of better prognostication, follow-up, and treatment selection for future breast cancer patients.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with a history of cough, fever, and shortness of breath. He has been diagnosed with COVID-19 based on a positive test result. The patient's condition has progressively worsened and he has developed severe respiratory distress, requiring mechanical ventilation. He now meets the inclusion criteria for the SARSCoV2 Convalescent Plasma Expanded Access Protocol (EAP) trial as he has severe or immediately life-threatening COVID-19. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the trial. He has no known contraindication to transfusion and has not experienced any prior reactions to blood products.

A 10-year-old child with a history of neurogenic bladder due to spina bifida came to the clinic with complaints of frequent episodes of urinary tract infections and difficulty in emptying the bladder completely. The child has been using intermittent catheterization for bladder management for the past 6 months. The parents have tried various methods to prevent catheter-associated urinary tract infections, but the child has still been experiencing frequent infections. The child is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies to any medications or materials. The parents and child have both provided informed oral and written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old female with bilateral cataracts. She has been experiencing progressive blurring of vision and glare, impacting her daily activities. Her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/80 in the right eye and 20/100 in the left eye. She has no history of ocular trauma or surgery, and her medical history is unremarkable. Her systemic diseases are well-controlled with medications. Preoperative examination reveals nuclear sclerotic cataract graded 2+ or 3+ in both eyes with naturally dilated pupils (in dim light) > 4.0 mm. Her preoperative corneal astigmatism is less than 2.5 D, and central corneal thickness is within normal limits. She is willing to give informed consent and is available for follow-up visits. She is between the ages of 55 and 80 and has sufficient cognitive awareness to comply with examination procedures. She does not have any exclusion criteria such as severe dry eyes, history of corneal surgery, or other ocular or systemic diseases that would increase risk or confound study results.

A 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer six months ago is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has received prior anti-HER2 therapy, including trastuzumab and pertuzumab, which have failed to control her disease progression. The patient is currently receiving chemotherapy and has no known allergies to any medications. Her BMI is 24. She is married, has two children, and works as a teacher. She has no history of CNS metastasis and has LVEF ≥50%. Her ECOG PS is 1, and she is expected to survive more than three months. She is willing to use effective non-hormonal contraceptive methods during the study period and at least six months after the last dose. She understands and voluntarily agrees to sign the informed consent form.

A 42-year-old male who has been experiencing rectal bleeding and abdominal cramping for the past 6 months. He has not received any treatment for these symptoms and has not been diagnosed with ulcerative proctosigmoiditis before. He has a past medical history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He does not have any known renal impairment, is not pregnant or lactating, and has a good compliance history with medication. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to find relief for his symptoms.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who is a mother of a 14-year-old girl diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus since 2 years ago. She is married and works as a teacher. She reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious about her daughter's diabetes management. She is concerned about her daughter's frequent hypoglycemic episodes and feels guilty about not being able to control her daughter's blood sugar levels. She is also worried about her daughter's future and the potential complications of diabetes. She reports feeling stressed and irritable lately and has difficulty sleeping. She is currently not receiving any psychological or social support. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn more about her own psychological well-being and how it affects her daughter's diabetes management. She hopes that by participating in this study, she can gain a better understanding of how to support her daughter and improve her family's overall quality of life.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been diagnosed with partial seizures. He has been taking Depakote twice a day for the past 6 months, but he is experiencing side effects such as drowsiness, nausea, and stomach upset. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is currently taking medication. He has no history of substance abuse, and he is not currently taking any other medication that could interfere with seizure control. The patient is able to maintain an accurate, complete, written daily seizure diary, and he is willing to complete the QOLIE, the Beck Depression Inventory, and the SSQ. He is able to give written informed consent and is compliant with clinic visits. The patient is able to swallow Depakote-ER and is interested in participating in the study to see if the once-a-day dosing will be more tolerable and effective for him.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who was diagnosed with CD19-positive B cell lymphoma three years ago. She has received multiple prior treatments including chemotherapy and monoclonal antibody therapy, but her disease has relapsed and is now refractory to treatment. She is experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. Her recent laboratory results showed a neutrophil count of 1.2 x 10^9/L and a platelet count of 60 x 10^9/L. Her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She has an ECOG score of 1 and is expected to survive for at least 12 weeks. She is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use effective contraception during the trial. She has no history of drug addiction or mental illness. She is interested in participating in the trial and hopes to find a new treatment option for her relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphoma.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with hypereosinophilic syndrome. He has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and shortness of breath. He has also experienced skin rashes and itching. His absolute eosinophil count has been consistently high for the past three months, with one reading during the screening period showing an absolute eosinophil count of above 1,500/mm3. He has been on corticosteroids previously but has not responded well to them. He has also shown signs of organ damage, with his cardiac function being affected. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2. The patient has not received any investigational or commercial therapies within the past 28 days and is willing to commit to abstinence from heterosexual contact or use highly effective contraception during the treatment period and for 12 weeks after discontinuation of study treatment. The patient has no history of HIV or chronic active hepatitis B or C. He has not undergone any major surgery within the past four weeks and has a life expectancy of more than six months.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who was admitted to the intensive care unit due to respiratory failure caused by pneumonia. He has been on invasive mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours, and his condition is stable. He has no history of neurological or orthopedic conditions that would prevent him from being mobilized. His vital signs are within normal limits, with a heart rate of 80 beats per minute, blood pressure of 120/70 mmHg, respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 95% on FiO2 of 40%. The patient has a Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) score of 0, indicating that he is alert and calm. The patient is able to walk without assistance before being admitted to the ICU. He has no major pressure ulcers in the calcaneal region and no orthopedic fractures in the lower limbs. The patient has a platelet count of 120,000 and no signs of hyperglycemia or active gastrointestinal bleeding.

The patient is a healthy 28 year old male who is a long term resident of a rural village in Mali. He works as a farmer and has no history of chronic illnesses or significant allergies. He is willing to remain in the village for the duration of the study and undergo all necessary tests and procedures. He has not taken any anti-malaria drugs or antibiotics with known antimalarial activity in the past 30 days. He has not received any investigational product in the past 30 days and has never received a malaria vaccine candidate before. He does not have a history of recurrent severe infections or chronic immunosuppressant medication use. He has not used immunoglobulins or blood products within the past 3 months, and does not have a history of allergic disease or significant reactions against mosquito bites. He is not currently pregnant or lactating, and he is willing to use reliable contraception for the duration of the vaccination phase. He has no history of injecting drug abuse or suspected current alcohol abuse. He has not been diagnosed with any immunosuppressive or immune modulating disorder, hematuria, proteinuria or glucosuria. He has no clinically significant abnormalities on a 12 lead ECG or any other significant disease or disorder. He is willing to provide blood for safety data and undergo an HIV test and other tests needed for determining exclusion.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of primary biliary cirrhosis (PBC) came to the clinic complaining of fatigue, itching, and abdominal pain. Her liver enzymes were elevated, and her bilirubin levels were borderline high. She was diagnosed with PBC four years ago and had previously participated in the LUM001 201 (CLARITY) study. She is interested in continuing her treatment with LUM001 and is willing to participate in a long-term safety and tolerability study. She is able to understand and sign the informed consent form. She has no history of non-adherence to treatment protocols.

A 65-year-old woman was diagnosed with Alzheimer Disease by her neurologist. She has been experiencing memory loss, confusion, and difficulty with everyday tasks for the past year. She has been taking donepezil for the past 6 months, but has not seen any significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially help her condition. She has no history of major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder or schizophrenia. She does not participate in any non-pharmacological trials related to improving cognition. She is willing to receive intravenous infusions for the study and is available to participate for up to 12 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is scheduled to undergo a screening colonoscopy due to his age and family history of colon cancer. He has no known allergies and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has not experienced any bowel obstruction in the past and is not currently suffering from any severe illness. He has been informed about the study and has provided consent to participate.

A 60-year-old Caucasian male with a history of lung cancer presents with a new metastatic lesion in his liver. He underwent surgery and chemotherapy 8 months ago and was declared cancer-free. However, he developed new symptoms of abdominal discomfort and a CT scan confirmed the presence of a 5 cm mass in his liver. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a retired teacher and a non-smoker. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. His labs show an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm³, a platelet count of 130,000/mm³, and normal liver and kidney function tests. He has no known allergies to medications. He understands that this is a phase I clinical trial and there is a possibility that he may not receive any benefit from the treatment. He is willing to participate in the study and is committed to attending all the required visits and tests.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy scheduled for a tonsillectomy under general anesthesia. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient has no known allergies and has had no previous surgeries. He is currently in good health with a BMI of 18. The preoperative evaluation shows no abnormalities, and the patient meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis (UC) for 5 years. She has been on several medications including aminosalicylates, systemic corticosteroids, and TNF-α blockers, but has not experienced significant relief of her symptoms. During a recent colonoscopy, she was found to have active UC with a Mayo endoscopic subscore of 3 and a modified Mayo score of 6. She has no history of surgery for UC or colorectal cancer or dysplasia. She has not received more than 2 TNF-α blockers and has not received any integrin antagonists. She has stopped using any corticosteroid or 5-ASA enemas or suppositories for at least 2 weeks before screening. Her laboratory results show a white blood cell count of 5,500/mm3, a platelet count of 180,000/mm3, and a serum creatinine level of 0.8 mg/dL. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has agreed to use effective contraception during the study. She does not have any significant medical history or conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

50-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset severe headache and vomiting. CT scan revealed a large intracerebral hemorrhage in the right frontal lobe with surrounding edema. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes losartan and hydrochlorothiazide for blood pressure management. On admission, his blood pressure was 200/120 mmHg. The patient is conscious but disoriented and has mild right-sided weakness. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the ICH ADAPT trial and does not have any exclusion criteria.

This clinical trial is seeking a healthy male or female adult between the ages of 19 and 55, who weighs at least 45 kg and has a BMI between 18.0 and 30.0 kg/m^2. The participant should not have any uncontrolled neurological, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, metabolic, gastrointestinal, urological, immunologic, endocrine disease, or psychiatric disorder. Additionally, the participant should not have any known hypersensitivity to any component of the formulation of TAK-935. This trial is not suitable for individuals with any significant medical history or abnormal safety laboratory test results. The participant will be required to make two visits to the clinic, including one 7-day period of confinement to the clinic. The study will consist of 6 cohorts with 8 participants in each cohort. The participant will receive a single dose of TAK-935 or placebo following a 10-hour fast. The starting dose will be 15 mg followed by planned doses of 50, 200, 600, 900 and not to exceed 1350 mg in subsequent cohorts. The overall time to participate in this study is up to 51 days.

A 62-year-old man was recently diagnosed with stage D0 prostate cancer and started on androgen deprivation therapy. He has no significant past medical history and takes only medications for mild hypertension. He is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys gardening and taking walks. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is concerned about the impact of prostate cancer treatment on his bone health and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may prevent bone loss. He is willing to take calcium and vitamin D supplements and to receive alendronate therapy for one to two years. He has not been diagnosed with renal failure, hyperthyroidism, Cushing's syndrome, or metabolic bone disease. He is not using glucocorticoids or certain anticonvulsants, and he is not currently on osteoporosis therapies. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to undergo bone density tests every six months.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma. He has a history of alcohol abuse and has been a heavy smoker for over 30 years. The patient reports experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and unintentional weight loss over the past few months. Imaging studies revealed a 6 cm mass in his liver. His liver function tests are within normal limits, and he has a Child-Pugh score of A. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo a hepatectomy if deemed appropriate by the surgical team. He has no history of mental illness and does not have any other co-existing malignant tumors. The patient has no known allergies to indocyanine green. However, he does have a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to undergo all necessary testing and evaluations.

A 35 yo F with a 3-year history of ankylosing spondylitis, currently taking NSAIDs and synthetic DMARDs for management of symptoms. She reports experiencing stiffness and pain in her spine and peripheral joints, leading to limitations in physical activities and a reduced quality of life. She is interested in participating in a physical training program to potentially alleviate her symptoms and improve her overall function. She has no contraindications to the physical training program, such as cardiac failure, pregnancy, or painful arthroplasty or lower limb damage.

A 28-year-old female presents with no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker, with a body mass index (BMI) of 23.5 kg/m^2 and weighs 55 kg. She is right-handed and fluent in English. She has no history of seizures, epilepsy, mood disorders, or any other neurological disorders. She is not currently taking any prescribed or over-the-counter medications, and has not taken any within the past 4 weeks. She has no personal or familial history of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV. She is willing to use contraceptive measures during the study. She has no dietary restrictions that would prohibit the consumption of standardized meals. She is able to comply with the study restrictions and is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical research.

The patient is an 8-year-old child who has recently been diagnosed with epilepsy. The child is experiencing partial-onset seizures with secondary generalization. The seizures have been occurring for the past 6 months and have been increasing in frequency over the past few weeks. The child's parents are concerned about the impact of the seizures on the child's development and quality of life. The child has never been treated for epilepsy before and has not been exposed to more than one standard antiepileptic drug. The child's weight and height are within the 5th to 95th percentile for their age based on standard Child Height and Weight Charts from the Centers for Disease Control (CDC). The child's parents are willing to participate in the study and accurately maintain the participant take-home record and seizure diary. The child is able to understand the nature of the study and provide assent for their participation. The child does not have a surgically implanted and functioning vagus nerve stimulator and does not have a history of seizures as a result of a correctable medical condition. The child has not had uncontrolled seizures while previously taking either topiramate or levetiracetam, and does not have a history of non-epileptic seizures. The child does not have myoclonic or absence seizures.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. He is 5'9" tall and weighs 210 pounds. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He also has high cholesterol and takes medication for that as well. He has been experiencing tingling and numbness in his feet and hands for the past year. He is concerned about his symptoms and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore potential treatment options. He has no history of diabetes or other chronic illnesses. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His labs show an HbA1c of 6.5%, triglycerides of 180 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 35 mg/dL, and LDL cholesterol of 120 mg/dL. He has no family history of hereditary neuropathy. He is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control during the study period.

An 70-year-old woman presents with a history of frequent falls in the past 6 months. She has been referred to a falls rehabilitation group class by her physiotherapist. She reports that she has noticed a decrease in her balance and mobility over the past year. She denies any recent illness or hospitalizations, but does have a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. She reports that she is independent in her activities of daily living but has some difficulty with household tasks due to her balance issues. She speaks English fluently and is able to read and comprehend written materials. She is not currently experiencing any symptoms of cardiac syncope/pre-syncope or postural hypotension. She has a Mini Mental State score of

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of nasopharyngeal carcinoma, who underwent re-irradiation due to local recurrence, presents with persistent disease despite previous treatments. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 and adequate organ function. The patient's disease is measurable on the basis of RECIST v1.1. The patient has not received platinum-based chemotherapy previously and has no confirmed systemic metastasis. The patient is not diagnosed with immuno deficiency, systemic corticosteroid therapy, active autoimmune disease, interstitial lung disease, or any other additional malignancy that is progressing or requires active treatment. The patient is HBV negative and HCV negative with no cirrhosis. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to establish the antitumor activity and safety of the anti-programmed death 1 receptor monoclonal antibody, Treprilimab, in patients with local recurrent/residual nasopharyngeal carcinoma after re-irradiation.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who was admitted to a hospital after a suicide attempt by overdose. She has a history of depression and anxiety, and reports feeling hopeless and overwhelmed with life stressors. She is unmarried and lives alone, and has no children. She works as a teacher at a local school. She has been hospitalized for psychiatric reasons before, but has never received cognitive behavioral therapy. She is currently taking antidepressant medication, but reports that it has not been effective in reducing her suicidal thoughts. She is alert and cooperative, but expresses feelings of worthlessness and guilt. She reports feeling isolated and lonely, and has a history of self-harm behaviors. She agrees to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form.

54 year-old male with end-stage renal disease on haemodialysis for the last 4 years. His serum phosphorus levels are well-controlled with a stable dose of sevelamer carbonate. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and has maintained a stable phosphorus diet. He reports no symptoms of hyperphosphatemia, such as bone pain or muscle weakness. He has no significant medical comorbidities and has not participated in any clinical studies with experimental medication or biological products in the last 30 days. He has a BMI of 25.7 kg/m2 and has no history of significant gastrointestinal motility problems or substance/alcohol abuse. He is a non-smoker and has no history of seizures or drug allergies. He has a negative HIV test result and is willing to use appropriate contraception.

A 28-year-old woman was diagnosed with asthma when she was 18 years old. She has been experiencing symptoms of coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath that are not adequately controlled with her current anti-asthma medication. She has a BMI of 24.5 and is physically inactive, only walking for around 20 minutes per day. She does not have any other inflammatory or metabolic diseases, and she has not used oral anti-inflammatory medication or antibiotics in the last 8 weeks. She is interested in participating in a study that may help improve her asthma control through lifestyle changes.

A 55-year-old man with end-stage liver disease is listed for a deceased donor liver transplant at the University Health Network. The patient has a history of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis and is currently under treatment for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient has no prior history of liver transplantation or any other organ transplantation. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient's plasmatic Factor V levels will be measured on postoperative days 1º, 2º, 3º, 5º and 7º, and they will be followed up to 12 months. The study outcomes for the patient will be early graft dysfunction, and graft and patient survival. The patient understands that graft loss will be defined as the need for retransplantation in the study period, and that no other intervention will be done to him during the study period.

A 62-year-old male patient presents with a history of congestive heart failure. He has been diagnosed with left ventricular dysfunction of ischemic etiology, with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35%. Despite treatment with optimal drug regimen as per current European guidelines, the patient still experiences symptoms characterized by NYHA functional class II. The patient is in sinus rhythm with a spontaneous heart rate of 70 bpm. He has not undergone any cardiac pacing or neck surgery in the electrode zone. The patient has no risk factors for right carotid artery stenosis and has no history of peptic ulcer disease or upper gastrointestinal bleeding. He has no severe respiratory diseases or advanced diabetes mellitus. He has not undergone any recent acute myocardial infarction, coronary artery surgery, or revascularization. The patient has not had any cerebrovascular events or significant valvulopathy. He has not undergone any previous heart transplant or current LVAD device therapy. The patient's life expectancy is estimated to be more than one year for non-cardiac causes. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided signed and dated informed consent.

This is a 32 year-old Japanese female with a history of severe asthma for the past 3 years. Despite being on medium to high-dose ICS and at least one additional asthma controller medication, her asthma remains inadequately controlled with documented history of at least 2 asthma exacerbation events within the past 12 months. She presents with symptoms of dyspnea, wheezing, and coughing. ACQ-6 score is 2.5 at screening. She has no history of pulmonary diseases other than asthma, cancer, clinically significant infection, chronic alcohol or drug abuse, or anaphylaxis following any biologic therapy. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of hepatitis B, C or HIV. She has never been randomized in a previous tezepelumab study.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing cramping pain in her legs when walking for the past 6 months. She was diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and has been taking medication and following a walking exercise routine three times a week. However, her symptoms have not improved significantly. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. She underwent a coronary artery bypass grafting surgery 2 years ago. She has quit smoking 10 years ago and rarely drinks alcohol. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with study procedures.

A 45-year-old male patient with end-stage renal disease due to IgA nephropathy presents for evaluation for kidney transplantation. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gout, all of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of prior malignancy or significant infectious diseases. After thorough evaluation, he is deemed a suitable candidate for live donor kidney transplantation and is placed on the waiting list. After several months, a compatible live donor is found, and he undergoes successful transplantation with Alemtuzumab induction therapy. He is then randomized into the study and assigned to receive either standard-release Tacrolimus (Prograf) or extended-release Tacrolimus (Advagraf). He is followed closely by the transplant team and is monitored for any signs of rejection or adverse effects. He is asked to complete a short Health-Related Quality of Life questionnaire (SF-36) before transplantation and at 1 year post-transplant and a Medication Adherence Rating Score at 3, 6, and 12 months post-transplant.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired teacher who has recently noticed a decline in her ability to remember things. She is concerned that she may be developing Alzheimer's disease, as her mother had it. She has a history of high blood pressure, but it is currently well-controlled with medication. She does not have any allergies and is not taking any medications other than her blood pressure medication. She lives alone but has close friends who check on her regularly. She is able to perform her daily activities without assistance. Her Mini-Mental State Exam score is 26. She has completed high school and has a good work history. She is fluent in English and able to communicate effectively with study personnel. She is willing to undergo repeated MRIs and at least three Positron-Emission Tomography (PET) scans. She is also willing to have blood drawn for Apolipoprotein (APOE) epsilon, CYP2D6 and biomarker testing and lumbar puncture for the collection of CSF. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to provide written informed consent prior to any study procedures. She is eligible for this study as per the inclusion criteria.

30-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23.5, non-smoker, and non-alcoholic, without any significant medical history, is eligible for the trial. He has not participated in any other drug studies in the last 60 days and has not donated blood or received transfusion in the last 30 days. He does not have a history of drug abuse, allergies, or hypersensitivity reactions. The subject has not taken any prescription or non-prescription medications within 14 days of screening, which can affect the results of the clinical trial. The subject has no history of myopathic disorder or family history of the same. The subject is willing and able to comprehend the study objectives, contents, and the property of the study drug before participating in the trial.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has no history of prior allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT). His treating physician recommended HCT and he was found to have a willing unrelated adult donor who is a 7/8 HLA match. The patient is in remission by standard testing and has no relapse of his primary malignancy. He has no uncontrolled viral, bacterial, fungal, or protozoal infections at the time of study enrollment. The patient and his legal guardians have signed a written informed consent. He is otherwise healthy, with no serious psychiatric disease or inherited predisposition to cancer. His estimated GFR is 75 mL/min/1.73m2, and his cardiac ejection fraction is 55. The patient is eligible to participate in this Phase 2 trial for extended vs short-term abatacept dosing for graft versus host disease prophylaxis.

The patient is a 50-year-old Egyptian man who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus infection and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on oral hypoglycemic therapy for the past 2 years. The patient reports fatigue, nausea, and abdominal discomfort. He has a history of smoking and consumes alcohol occasionally. The patient's medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient's vital signs are stable with blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, heart rate of 70 bpm, and respiratory rate of 16/min. The patient's BMI is 28. The patient has not been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma or liver cirrhosis. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided consent for the study.

Pt is a 58yo M with a history of smoking who developed shortness of breath and cough. Evaluation revealed a right upper lobe mass and biopsy confirmed non-small cell lung cancer. He underwent treatment with chemotherapy with a partial response, but developed recurrent disease in the same area. He underwent radiation therapy with a good response but developed progressive disease again. He is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the use of erlotinib in recurrent or refractory non-small cell lung cancer. His ECOG performance status is 1 and he has measurable disease on CT scan. He is willing to comply with the study and follow-up procedures and has no contraindications to taking oral medication. He has previously undergone an investigation to determine his EGFR levels in tumor tissue and has archival diagnostic paraffin-embedded tumor tissue available for testing. He is not currently receiving any anti-cancer therapy and has recovered from any reversible acute effects of prior therapy.

The patient is a 62-year-old man with a history of chronic renal impairment, with a creatinine clearance (CLcr) level of < 30mL/min, but he is not currently undergoing hemodialysis. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, but these are well-controlled with medications. His body weight is within the acceptable range for this study, and he meets all the laboratory parameters required for subjects with renal impairment. He has no history of hepatitis or hepatic insufficiency. He has not had any significant changes in his chronic treatment medication within 14 days prior to inclusion in the study. The patient has been certified as healthy by a comprehensive clinical assessment, and his normal renal function is defined by the Cockroft-Gault formula with a creatinine clearance (CLcr) > 80mL/min. He is not positive for any tests for hepatitis B surface (HBs) antigen, anti-hepatitis C virus (anti-HCV) antibodies, HIV1 antibodies, or anti-HIV2 antibodies. He is willing to use a double barrier method of contraception with his partner during the study.

62-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed 3 years ago, presents with metastatic disease to bones and lymph nodes. The patient has been on androgen deprivation therapy with anti-androgens for the past 2 years, with a recent increase in his prostate-specific antigen level to 10 ng/mL. The patient reports increasing bone pain and is found to have new lytic lesions on bone scan. The patient is otherwise in good health with no other significant medical comorbidities. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options and is willing to use effective barrier contraception during and for 2 months after completion of the study treatment.

44-year-old female admitted to the internal medicine ward for uncontrolled hypertension and chest pain. The patient has a past medical history of hypothyroidism and depression, for which she is currently taking levothyroxine and escitalopram, respectively. Upon admission, her labs reveal hypomagnesemia with a magnesium level of 1.7 mg/dL. The patient reports occasional leg cramps and muscle weakness. She consents to participate in the clinical trial examining whether magnesium replacement therapy affects mortality, length of hospital stay, and overall well-being. The patient has no history of kidney disease, severe diarrhea, or malnutrition. She is not currently receiving magnesium supplements.

The patient is a pregnant woman at risk of giving birth before 28 weeks of gestational age. She has been identified as having a high-risk pregnancy due to her medical history or symptoms. She is willing to participate in the study and provide necessary samples for the research. The patient is being closely monitored by her obstetrician and neonatal specialists for any signs of preterm labor. If the baby is born before 28 weeks, the infant will be admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit and monitored closely. The mother will provide amniotic fluid and blood samples, while the infant will provide placenta, blood, urine, and tracheal aspirates samples for inflammatory parameter analysis. After discharge from the hospital, the infant will be followed according to a specific protocol until 5 years of age.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is in her second trimester and has been experiencing some anxiety and depressive symptoms since the COVID-19 pandemic began. She is worried about the potential impact of the virus on her and her baby's health, as well as the effects of social isolation and quarantine measures on her emotional wellbeing. She works as a nurse at a hospital and has been experiencing high levels of stress and anxiety due to her job and the pandemic. She has no prior history of psychiatric disorders and is otherwise healthy. She is currently receiving antenatal care at a clinic and is willing to participate in the study.

45-year-old male, recently diagnosed with hepatitis C virus (HCV), presents for his first office visit for HCV management. He is referred to the Hepatology Outpatient Clinic at the University of Kentucky in Lexington. He has a history of substance use disorder and is currently in recovery. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He reports occasional alcohol use but denies any recent use. He is currently employed but has limited access to transportation due to living in a rural area. He is motivated to receive treatment for HCV but expresses concerns about the potential side effects of treatment and the financial burden of treatment. He has not seen a specialist for HCV treatment before and is open to different treatment options.

The patient is a 53-year-old male with a history of smoking, consuming 1 pack per day for 30 years. He was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, and the tumor is unresectable. He has not undergone any prior radiation therapy or chemotherapy. His Karnofsky performance status is 80%, and he is able to perform most activities of daily living. His creatinine clearance is >60 mL/min, and he has no history of mental illness. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with muscle-invasive transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder. He presents with symptoms of hematuria, urgency, and dysuria. He has undergone histological confirmation of the diagnosis and has undergone standard radiological assessments with CT or MR for staging. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has adequate pre-treatment hematological and biochemical parameters. He has no significant co-morbidities that would exclude him from having radical treatment. He has not undergone any previous treatment for the diagnosis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer or other pelvic radiotherapy. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and has a history of mild depression that is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has given written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer confirmed with biopsy 3 years ago. She has been receiving chemotherapy with anthracycline and taxane therapy as the first and second line of treatment, respectively. However, her disease progressed after these treatments. She was then treated with Halaven® (Eribulin) as the third-line treatment, which resulted in objective response and stability for more than 9 months. She has no significant past medical history and no family history of breast cancer. Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her laboratory results show hemoglobin: 12 g/dL, white blood cell count: 6,800/µL, platelet count: 250,000/µL, and serum creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL. She has liver metastases, which will be closely monitored in this study. She has provided written consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a premature infant born at 31 weeks and 4 days gestational age. The baby has been in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit for 5 days and is currently stable on room air. The infant's weight is 1.5 kg and is receiving enteral feeds every 3 hours. The baby's mother is available and willing to participate in the study. The infant has no known congenital malformations or neurological dysfunctions. The baby is not on mechanical ventilation support or analgesia morphinics at high dosage and has not been diagnosed with septic shock or severe pulmonary arterial hypertension. The baby is eligible for skin-to-skin care and will be monitored for cardio-respiratory coordination during the SSC session. The study will be conducted twice, 5-10 days apart, and the baby will participate in the study for a maximum of 10 days. The study will last for a total period of 18 months and 10 days.

A 45-year-old woman was referred to the clinic by her optometrist after being diagnosed with ocular hypertension. She has no family history of glaucoma or ocular disease. She was started on a regimen of dorzolamide-timolol combination eye drops but did not tolerate them due to ocular discomfort and redness. She has no other medical problems and takes no other medications. Her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes with or without correction. She wears contact lenses for correction. She is concerned about the potential side effects of ocular hypotensive medications and desires a preservative-free option.

The patient is a 50-year-old non-smoking woman who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She underwent curative surgery 4 months ago and is currently free of recurrence. Her histology shows non-squamous cell carcinoma. She has no other concurrent medical conditions and her Karnofsky performance status is 80%. Her hematology results show a WBC count of 4,500/mm^3 and a platelet count of 120,000/mm^3. She has no history of splenectomy, and she has not received any prior radiotherapy to the spleen. She is not pregnant, and she is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She does not take any immunosuppressive drugs or anti-inflammatory drugs.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia and has been receiving antipsychotic medication for the past year. She lives with her parents and works as a part-time sales assistant. She has no history of head trauma, neurological disease, or serious physical illness. She does not use any psychoactive substances and has no history of substance abuse or dependence. Her IQ is above 70. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. She is able to understand and follow the instructions given for the cognitive tasks and is able to perform the tasks accurately. She has a basic knowledge of the objects that will be presented in the study and is able to recognize them. She has no visual or motor impairments that would interfere with the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding at the time of the study.

The patient is a 45 year old female who has been experiencing hoarseness and vocal fatigue for several months. She is a high school teacher and relies heavily on her voice for work. She has sought treatment with a local speech therapist, but has not seen significant improvement. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing traditional on-site treatment versus telemedicine treatment for muscle tension dysphonia. She has no history of head and neck cancer, spasmodic dysphonia, tremor, respiratory compromise, or dysphagia.

A 35-year-old male with a history of schizophrenia, currently being treated with antipsychotic medication for the past six months, presents with a BMI of 30. He reports smoking at least a pack of cigarettes a day for the past five years and expresses a desire to quit smoking and lose weight. He has no history of binge eating or other eating disorders, nor has he used any weight loss or antidiabetic medications. He reports no substance use other than nicotine and caffeine. He denies any seizure disorder, unstable cardiac problems, or other unstable medical conditions. He is not currently pregnant or nursing.

A 55-year-old Japanese man was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus infection. He is experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional abdominal discomfort. His medical history includes hypertension, for which he takes medication. He has never received treatment for hepatitis C virus infection before. His HCV RNA level is greater than 100,000 IU/mL. He doesn't have hepatocellular carcinoma or co-infection with hepatitis B virus or human immunodeficiency virus. He has no severe or uncontrollable complications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of Asunaprevir and Daclatasvir combination therapy versus Telaprevir therapy.

Patient is a 65-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage II invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has been on tamoxifen for the past 5 years and has been stable with no evidence of recurrence. She has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother being diagnosed at the age of 60. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and alendronate. She is followed by the breast oncology clinic at the National University Hospital and has an available archival paraffin-embedded tumor block stored at the Department of Pathology, NUH. She has been identified as a potential participant for a study that aims to create a gene expression-based prognostic device that complements or exceeds the prognostic utility of conventional biomarkers of breast cancer outcome. The study will utilize high-throughput gene expression platforms to profile RNA extracted from the sections of her tumor block. The results generated from her tumor sample will not impact her clinical management but will contribute to the development of archival tumor-derived genomic tests for breast cancer management in the future.

50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and moderate renal insufficiency. The patient takes medication for hypertension and has not smoked or used any nicotine-containing products for the last 3 months. The patient has a BMI within the range of 18 to 35 kg/m^2. The patient has not had any major surgery or donated blood within the last 8 weeks and has not participated in any investigational study within the last 4 weeks. The patient does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse within the last 6 months. The patient does not have a history of nephrolithiasis or kidney removal or functioning renal transplant. The patient is willing to refrain from or anticipate the use of strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, excessive amounts of alcohol or caffeine, and illicit drugs during the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who has suffered from spinal cord injury due to a car accident four years ago. He reports difficulty with ejaculation and has been referred for evaluation of ejaculatory dysfunction. The patient reports that he has never fathered a child and is concerned about his fertility. He is currently using a catheter to empty his bladder due to urinary retention. The patient has given his informed consent to participate in the study and has social insurance affiliation. He does not have any history of justice protection. The patient is between 18 and 65 years old, meeting the inclusion criteria of the study.

Patient is a 54-year-old woman from the United States with a history of ovarian cancer. She has completed chemotherapy and is currently on maintenance therapy. She presents with abdominal distension, nausea, and vomiting. A CT scan reveals a potential malignant bowel obstruction. She has no history of bowel obstruction, hernias or abdominal surgeries. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has no known drug allergies. She is currently on lisinopril 20mg daily and atorvastatin 40mg daily. Her BMI is 27, BP: 130/78, HR: 85/min. She is interested in participating in clinical research that may improve her quality of life and help other patients with similar conditions.

A 58-year-old male with a history of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (RCC) presented with metastatic disease to the lungs and liver, confirmed by CT scan. He has no history of prior surgery or systemic treatment for metastatic RCC. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and has been assessed with favorable or intermediate MSKCC or Heng risk score. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of predominantly clear cell RCC. The primary tumor is asymptomatic and suitable for nephrectomy, and the metastatic disease is documented with up to three different sites. He has ≥ 3 metastatic lesions, platelets > 100,000/ml, haemoglobin > 9.0 g/dl, neutrophils >1,500/mm3, bilirubin < or = 2 mg/dl, AST and ALT < or = 2.5 times the UNL, and serum albumin > the LNL. He is of childbearing age and will use contraceptive methods during the study. The patient does not have brain and liver metastases, non-clear-cell histology, poor prognosis as defined by MSKCC or Heng criteria, documented widespread disease, oligometastatic disease suitable of metastasectomy, symptomatic primary tumor at presentation, or high surgical risk in the opinion of the urologist.
