The patient also does not have bilateral RCC, or > 3 of the following surgical risk factors: serum albumin CTCAE v 4.0 grade 2 or worse, serum LDH > 1.5 times upper limit of normal, symptoms at presentation due to metastases, clinical stage T4 disease, history of malabsorption syndrome, pregnant or breastfeeding, concomitant cardiac disorders, uncontrolled diabetes, deep phlebitis not treated with LMWH or arterial thrombosis within the last 6 months, HIV infection, active infections (> Grade 2 NCI-CTC v.3.0), or other cancer within the previous 5 years (except for in situ skin carcinoma, superficial bladder Ta, Tis, T1 and carcinoma of the cervix or every cancer with curative treatment within 5 years).

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with AIDS (CDC definition) with a documented weight loss of 10% of his baseline weight over the past 3 months. He experiences anorexia and cachexia, with a perception that the weight loss is affecting his well-being. The patient is currently taking ganciclovir and has no history of substance abuse. He has no history of heart failure, deep vein thrombosis, or poorly controlled hypertension. The patient is able to provide informed consent, read and write in English, and has a life expectancy of at least 20 weeks. He has not been started on zidovudine within the past 8 weeks and has no contraindications to high-dose megestrol acetate. He does not have diarrhea or active systemic infections at the start of treatment. The patient has no obstruction to food intake or impaired digestive/absorptive functions. He has not been hospitalized or suffered an exacerbation of his illness associated with weight loss within the past 2 weeks. The patient is not menstruating.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who has been experiencing visual disturbances in his left eye for the past 2 months. He reports seeing distorted and blurred images and has difficulty reading and recognizing faces. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications regularly. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs but drinks alcohol occasionally on weekends. His family history is notable for his father having high blood pressure, but otherwise, no significant ocular history. On examination, the patient's visual acuity in his left eye is 20/50, and there is subretinal fluid observed on OCT. The doctor diagnoses him with subacute central serous chorioretinopathy and recommends him for this clinical trial. The patient is willing to participate and meets the eligibility criteria.

A 65-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer was referred to the clinic for evaluation of bone pain. His medical history was significant for a radical prostatectomy followed by adjuvant radiotherapy. His latest PSA level was 15 ng/mL. Bone scan showed multiple metastases. He has been receiving hormonal therapy for the past 3 months but has been experiencing persistent bone pain despite treatment. He reported difficulty sleeping and performing daily activities due to the pain. Laboratory studies showed normal renal function and a corrected serum calcium level of 2.4 mmol/L. He provided written informed consent and is eligible for the study.

63-year-old female with a h/o keratoconus and multiple failed corneal grafts presented to the ophthalmology clinic with decreased visual acuity and contrast sensitivity. She underwent penetrating keratoplasty in her right eye 2 years ago and lamellar keratoplasty in her left eye 1 year ago. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. On examination, best-corrected visual acuity was 20/60 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealed clear corneal grafts bilaterally with mild astigmatism. Fundus examination was unremarkable. The patient was enrolled in the study and underwent quick contrast sensitivity function (quick CSF) testing and filled out the 9-SF life quality questionnaire. The normal group would be covered by the positive spherical lens of 1.0D to 6.0D to repress the BCVA to 0.1 to 0.9 respectively to compare the visual functions with the keratoplasty patients on the same visual acuity.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme 2 years ago. She underwent surgical resection and radiation therapy but has had a recurrence of the tumor. She is currently experiencing headaches and seizures. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and depression. She is currently taking anti-seizure medication. She is married with two teenage children. She works as a teacher but has had to take a leave of absence due to her illness. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to travel to the study site for treatment. She does not have any other significant medical conditions and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 27-year-old healthy female who works as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial involving colchicine and grapefruit juice. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 23 and does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any drugs. She has no history of allergies to any drugs or food. She is currently not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses a reliable form of contraception. She has never participated in a clinical trial before and has not donated blood or plasma in the past month. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication that inhibits or induces cytochrome (CYP) P450 enzymes and/or P-glycoprotein (P-gp). She is interested in contributing to the advancement of medical research and is willing to comply with all study requirements, including multiple blood draws over a period of several days.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been enrolled in a Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MMCO) for the past 2 years. She has not been up-to-date with her colorectal cancer screening and has not had a home fecal occult blood test, flexible sigmoidoscopy, double-contrast barium enema, or colonoscopy within the past 10 years. She is registered to receive primary care from a participating Community/Migrant Health Center, Diagnostic and Treatment Center or other participating practice in New York City. She has a telephone available and has no plans to move for at least a year. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of an enhanced telephone support intervention (Prevention Care Manager [PCM]) to promote colorectal, cervical, and breast cancer screening among women enrolled in a Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MMCO). She will be randomized to receive either the PCM intervention or usual care from her primary care physician. The study will follow her for 18 months.

A 25-year-old African American woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, joint pain, and skin rash. She was diagnosed with SLE two years ago after presenting with malar rash, photosensitivity, and arthritis. She has been prescribed hydroxychloroquine and prednisone but has struggled with medication adherence due to financial hardship and difficulty scheduling appointments around her work schedule. She has missed several appointments and laboratory tests in the past six months, which has led to worsening of her symptoms. She reports feeling overwhelmed and unsupported in managing her chronic illness. She is interested in participating in a program that can help her navigate the healthcare system and provide practical support to improve her SLE management. She speaks fluent English and has access to a telephone.

50 year old woman diagnosed with stage IV ovarian carcinoma with metastasis to the liver and lungs. She has undergone three prior cytotoxic chemotherapeutic regimens for the management of her primary disease. She has a GOG performance status of 1 and has adequate organ and marrow function. She has no prior therapy with topotecan, no history of unstable angina or myocardial infarction within the past six months, and no known brain metastases. Her cholesterol and triglyceride levels are within the normal range, and she is not receiving any potent enzyme-inducing antiepileptic drugs or any other potent CYP3A4 inducers. She is willing to sign a written informed consent document and is able to understand the study requirements.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a biopsy, which confirmed the presence of invasive ductal carcinoma. The tumor is located in her left breast and is approximately 2.5 cm in size. She has not received any treatment for her cancer yet. The patient is currently scheduled to undergo surgical resection of the tumor. She has no history of other invasive malignancies, with the exception of non-melanoma skin cancer. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent. The patient is not currently pregnant or nursing and has undergone a urine pregnancy test within the 24 hour period prior to administration of [18F]ISO-1, which was determined to be negative. The patient is able to tolerate 60-90 minutes of PET imaging.

A 32-year-old female patient is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic surgery for endometriosis. She has a history of painful periods and a previous laparoscopy for endometriosis treatment. She has no known allergies, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient is a non-smoker, doesn't consume alcohol, and has a BMI of 25. Her physical examination is normal, and her preoperative laboratory workup is within normal limits. She has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status classification of I. The patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial to reduce post-operative shoulder-tip pain following laparoscopic surgery.

47-year-old female with a history of ulcerative colitis for the past 10 years presents with rectal bleeding and abdominal pain. The patient has been experiencing increased frequency of bowel movements with diarrhea and urgency. She has been on mesalamine and prednisone but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. The patient is scheduled for a colonoscopy to evaluate the extent and severity of her colitis and to obtain biopsies for histological evaluation. The patient is interested in participating in the study to gain more insight into the pathogenesis of her disease and to potentially contribute to the development of new treatments. The patient is able to provide informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer three years ago. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy, but unfortunately, the cancer has recurred and metastasized to her lungs. She has been receiving treatment with a combination of chemotherapy and targeted therapy for the past six months. She has experienced some side effects, including fatigue and hair loss, but is able to maintain her daily activities. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to monitor her HER2 amplification status and specific mutations abundance in plasma samples. She has no other significant medical history and is in good overall health. She has no allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with all study procedures. She is within the age range of 18 to 75 years old and has an ECOG score of 1. She has evaluable tumor lesions and is expected to survive more than three months. She has no major organ dysfunction and is able to implement a treatment plan based on her condition. She has voluntarily enrolled in the study and is willing to be followed up and observed.

62-year-old male smoker with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented with a persistent cough and was found to have a peripheral pulmonary nodule on chest CT. Further workup revealed a diagnosis of stage IA lung cancer. Due to comorbidities and patient preference, the patient was deemed not suitable for surgical treatment and agreed to undergo ablation therapy. The ablation procedure was successful, and the patient is currently in remission. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to monitor the efficacy of cfDNA methylation in detecting lung cancer recurrence after ablation therapy. The patient is compliant with follow-up appointments and understands the study's objectives and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes. He has been managing his diabetes with lifestyle modifications and oral medications for the past five years. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing structured care versus usual care in the management of diabetes. His fasting plasma glucose level has been consistently above 7.0 mmol/L on multiple occasions, and his HbA1c level is above 6.5%. He is able to return for regular follow-up at 3-4 monthly intervals and is willing to undergo comprehensive assessments at baseline, month 12, and month 24. He does not have type 1 diabetes, reduced life expectancy, or a mental condition that would prevent him from understanding the nature and scope of the study. He is not currently enrolled in another intervention study.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has recently been diagnosed with leukemia. Her parents are English speaking and have been struggling to cope with the uncertainty and stress that comes with managing their daughter's illness. The girl has been receiving treatment at a medical center and is returning for follow-up appointments. The family is willing to participate in the study, and the girl has agreed to give her assent to participate. The girl is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical or psychiatric conditions. The family is interested in learning more about how to manage the uncertainty surrounding their daughter's illness and are open to participating in clinic-based interventions to help them cope better.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue for the past 6 months. She was diagnosed with heart failure of unknown origin and has been on optimal medical therapy for the last 3 months, including ACE inhibitors, beta blockers and diuretics. Despite this, her symptoms have persisted and she is classified as NYHA class III. She has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia and is a former smoker. Her ECG shows a QRS duration of 130ms. Her echocardiogram reveals an ejection fraction of 30% and left ventricular end-diastolic dimension of 60mm. She has no known reversible cause of heart failure and her life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 6 months. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the potential of Tissue Doppler Echocardiography in selecting patients for Cardiac Resynchronisation Therapy.

63 year old female admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory failure secondary to pneumonia. She has a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease. The patient was started on continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) due to worsening kidney function and fluid overload. The patient’s weight is 76 kg, and her creatinine level is 2.8 mg/dL. Due to the patient’s critical illness, she has an indication for pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis. She has not been receiving any anticoagulant therapy prior to admission. The patient’s legal representative has provided written informed consent for the patient to participate in the study. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for slow low efficient daily dialysis (SLEDD) due to her oliguria, with a urine output of less than 0.3 mL/kg/h for more than 24 hours. She is randomized to the study group and will receive a continuous infusion of tinzaparin in addition to the bolus dose during SLEDD. The patient is not pregnant and has no known hypersensitivity to tinzaparin or any other heparin. This patient is an appropriate candidate for the clinical trial.

28-year-old nulliparous woman at 39 weeks gestation with a diagnosis of intrauterine fetal growth restriction. She is presenting with complaints of decreased fetal movements for the past 2 days. The ultrasound shows estimated fetal weight of 2800 grams with normal amniotic fluid index. The patient is admitted for induction of labor with vaginal misoprostol. She has no history of previous uterine surgery or preterm premature rupture of membranes.

28 year-old pregnant woman with a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, currently at 26 weeks gestation, seeking prenatal care at a low-income clinic. The patient is fluent in English and has access to a mobile smartphone. She is interested in participating in a study aimed at improving diabetes education and support during pregnancy. The patient reports difficulty managing her diabetes and is looking for additional resources to help her stay on track. She is motivated to learn more about diabetes management during pregnancy and is willing to use a mobile health behavior tool to receive educational and motivational content. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the individual testing phase and is excited to participate in the study to help improve diabetes care for pregnant women in similar situations.

65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and heart failure presents with complaints of fatigue, shortness of breath, and periodic loss of consciousness. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He reports a history of snoring and feeling unrested upon waking up. His sleep partner reports that he experiences episodes of snoring followed by periods of silence, and then gasps for air. The patient underwent a sleep study and was diagnosed with Cheyne-Stokes respiration. He is currently on medications including a diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, and a beta-blocker for his cardiac disease. He has no history of obstructive sleep apnea. He has consented to participate in the study to evaluate the effect of oxygen on core temperature in patients with cardiac disease and Cheyne-Stokes respiration.

A 35-year-old woman calls the New York State Smokers' Quitline seeking assistance to quit smoking. She has been smoking for the past 10 years and is currently smoking 10-15 cigarettes per day. She has tried quitting in the past but has not been successful. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She has a supportive family and social network and is motivated to quit smoking for her health and to save money. She speaks fluent English and is a resident of New York State. She is not enrolled in any special programs for quitting smoking. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing "Yale coaching" counseling and "Yale" print information to standard care counseling and standard care print information to determine which intervention is more effective in promoting smoking cessation. She is willing to set a quit date within 2 weeks of her initial call and receive follow-up counseling and materials.

A 58-year-old male with a history of recurrent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) complains of palpitations and shortness of breath. He has had several episodes of AF, with the most recent one occurring a month ago. He has tried several medications in the past, including Class I and III antiarrhythmic medications, but they were either ineffective or caused side effects. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and occasionally drinks alcohol. He has not undergone any previous ablation or surgical treatment for AF. His ejection fraction is above 35%, and LA diameter and volume are within normal limits based on his most recent imaging. He has no valvular disease, pulmonary vein stenosis, or any implanted cardiac devices. He is willing to undergo an ablation procedure and participate in all testing associated with the clinical trial. He is currently not enrolled in any other concurrent study.

67-year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. She has a history of previous coronary artery bypass grafting surgery and was found to have severe stenosis of the left main coronary artery and the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiography. She is scheduled for isolated coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. She is not a Jehovah's Witness and has no contraindications to blood transfusion. She is not on any anti-platelet or anticoagulant agents other than aspirin. She has no history of endocarditis, renal failure or dialysis dependence, and has not had prior ECMO or LVAD support.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic idiopathic pruritus for the past 6 months. She has tried various over-the-counter creams and antihistamines, but they have provided only temporary relief. She has no history of dermatological or systemic conditions that could be causing the pruritus. She rates her pruritus as 7 out of 10 on the Numeric Rating Scale. The patient has no history of suicidal crisis, psychosis, or bipolar disorder. She has been diagnosed with anxiety disorder in the past, but it is currently well-managed with medication. The patient is interested in exploring alternative treatments for her pruritus and is willing to participate in a clinical trial testing the efficacy of hypnosis.

This clinical trial is not suitable for patient enrollment as it is a diagnostic performance evaluation study for COVID-19 serology and the participants are sub-populations consisting of patients and staff members from Cornish Hospital Union. Therefore, it is not appropriate to generate a patient description for this trial.

35 y/o female with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosed 5 years ago. She has been experiencing proteinuria, hematuria, and hypertension for the past 6 months. Renal biopsy revealed Class IV lupus nephritis. She has been treated with hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACE inhibitors) for the past 3 months with little improvement in her symptoms. She has no history of cytotoxic drug use in the past 8 weeks, systemic infections, or hepatitis B or C, or HIV. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of CellCept in lupus nephritis.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with essential hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her average systolic BP is measured at 150mmHg and LDL-C levels are at 120mg/dL. She is currently not on any medication for her conditions. She has a family history of heart disease and is concerned about her risk. She is married with two children and works as a sales representative. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She exercises regularly and tries to maintain a healthy diet. She has no history of diabetes or any other major health conditions. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help manage her hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

58-year-old male with a history of colonoscopy that revealed a polyp which was removed and diagnosed as colorectal adenoma. The patient has no family history of colorectal cancer. He is in overall good health with no significant medical history. He is on no medications and denies any current symptoms such as rectal bleeding, abdominal pain, or changes in bowel habits. The patient is willing to participate in a study to evaluate the effectiveness of aspirin in preventing colorectal cancer. He understands the requirements of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol. He has no known allergies to aspirin or any of its components. He understands that he will be randomized to one of three arms and may receive aspirin or placebo. He agrees to use adequate contraception during the study period. He has no history of invasive malignancy or other significant medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of lung cancer presented with symptoms of chest pain, shortness of breath, and cough. He has been receiving chemotherapy for the past few months, but his symptoms have not improved. Upon examination, he was found to have malignant pleuritis. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no respiratory failure. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially benefit from medical thoracoscopy.

Patient A is a 42-year-old female who recently underwent surgical treatment for breast cancer, specifically a modified radical mastectomy with complete axillary dissection. She is currently in the postoperative stage, which is between 20 to 80 days after the surgery. She has no history of bilateral surgery or ongoing radiotherapy treatment. Patient A is experiencing functional limitations in her upper limbs, which are affecting her daily activities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effects of rehabilitation robotics in improving upper limb functionality.

A 35-year-old female office worker with a sedentary lifestyle has been experiencing lower back pain for the past few months. She has a history of mild scoliosis and occasional muscle spasms in her lower back. She reports difficulty in maintaining an upright posture and frequently experiences discomfort while sitting for long hours. A physical examination revealed restricted hip flexion with a range of motion of less than 80 degrees due to tightness in her hamstrings. She has no history of musculoskeletal injuries or neurological disorders, and her current medication does not affect her musculoskeletal system. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her mobility and alleviate her lower back pain.

The patient is a 12-year-old child diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after presenting with fatigue, easy bruising, and gum bleeding. The diagnosis was confirmed by bone marrow biopsy showing > 20% blasts. The patient has undergone induction chemotherapy with cytarabine and daunorubicin but failed to achieve complete remission. The patient is negative for FLT3-ITD mutation and cytogenetic abnormalities. The treating physician has recommended enrollment in a clinical trial due to a lack of available standard therapies for the patient's advanced AML. The patient has no significant past medical history and no allergies to any medications. The patient's Karnofsky performance status is 70%. The patient's parents are willing to comply with the study requirements and understand the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial.

Pt is a 25-week-old male preterm infant, weighing 700 grams, born by emergency C-section due to maternal hypertension. The infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit and required mechanical ventilation for the first 3 days of life. The infant has been receiving enteral nutrition via a nasogastric tube since birth. The infant has tolerated the feeds well without any significant complications. The infant is now 32 weeks gestational age and weighs 1500 grams. The medical team is considering whether to switch to an orogastric feeding tube to see if this will result in earlier establishment of oral feeding. The infant does not have any known severe neurologic deficits or genetic syndromes. The infant does not have a gastrostomy tube and has not been transferred to another hospital during hospitalization.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with a pancreatic tumor in the body and tail. He has no significant medical history, and his performance status is ECOG 0. Imaging studies have shown no evidence of distant metastases. His laboratory results including white blood cells count, platelet count, and liver and kidney functions are within normal limits. He has no active respiratory illness, chronic renal failure or liver cirrhosis. He is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

35-year-old female UC Merced staff member who reports high levels of work-related stress and is interested in exploring mindfulness-based interventions to manage stress. The participant owns a smartphone and uses it regularly. The participant has not participated in any regular meditation practices in the past three months. The participant is fluent in English and is willing to participate in an 8-week mindfulness intervention using the app Headspace. The participant is willing to complete questionnaires at baseline, week 4, week 8 (post-intervention), 4-month, and 12-month follow-up periods (20-30 minutes each time) and participate in everyday life assessments (4 days per week during baseline, 2 weeks, 5 weeks, 8 weeks, up to 5-10 minutes a day). The participant is willing to wear a Fitbit to assess their activity, sleep, and heart rate data. The participant is willing to attend one 60-minute orientation session to receive training on using the mobile app and receive a fitness watch that will be collected upon completion of the study.

Linda is a 68-year-old retired teacher who has always been interested in keeping her mind sharp. She enjoys crossword puzzles and reading books on a wide range of topics. She is in good overall health, with no history of major medical or psychiatric disorders. She takes medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol but is not currently taking any medications that would exclude her from participating in the study. Linda is fluent in English and has a Mini-Mental Status Examination (MMSE) score of 28. She is willing to commit to the time requirements of the study and is excited to participate in research that could benefit her and others. Linda is right-handed and has no reported or observed difficulties with her dominant hand.

62 F with a history of smoking and emphysema who has been experiencing worsening dyspnea on exertion and decreased exercise tolerance. CT scan showed evidence of emphysema with a CT value of 920 and multiple pulmonary bullae. The patient has been compliant with her inhaler regimen but still experiences symptoms despite maximal therapy. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent. She has no history of heart failure, lung cancer, or other underlying lung diseases. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all follow-up appointments.

A 28-year-old male was brought to the emergency department following a motor vehicle accident. He was the driver of a car that was hit by a truck from the side. Upon arrival, he was found to be unconscious with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) of 6/15. CT scan of the brain revealed subarachnoid hemorrhage with no other associated injuries. The patient was intubated and transferred to the ICU for further management. His medical history is unremarkable with no known allergies. He has no previous history of any medical conditions or surgeries. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or any recreational drugs. On physical examination, there is no evidence of any other injuries or neurological deficits. His vital signs are stable with BP: 120/80, HR: 90/min, respiratory rate: 18/min, and oxygen saturation of 98% on mechanical ventilation. The patient's family has been informed about his condition and has given consent for his participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who works as a software engineer and spends long hours sitting at a desk. She complains of sudden onset of neck pain with no obvious cause that has been bothering her for the past 4 days. The pain is located at the base of her neck and radiates towards her shoulders. She rates her pain as 70 out of 100 on a visual analogue scale. She also reports tenderness in her neck muscles upon examination. She has no history of neck injury, surgery, or any underlying medical conditions. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new treatment for acute non-specific neck pain.

50 yo Caucasian male with primary open angle glaucoma has been on maximum tolerated medical therapy for the last year, but his IOP remains uncontrolled. He has also shown progression of visual field loss over the past year. He has been referred to the ophthalmology clinic for evaluation for surgical intervention. He has no other significant ocular or medical history. His visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and his intraocular pressures are 20 mmHg in the right eye and 22 mmHg in the left eye. He has no significant visual field defect. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the InnFocus Microshunt implantation versus trabeculectomy in primary open angle glaucoma. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and complete the required follow-up visits. He has no history of previous ocular surgery, uveitis or other ocular comorbidities, and he is not currently using ocular hypotensive glaucoma medications in the fellow eye. He is suitable for inclusion in the study.

15 y/o female with the complaint of frequent headaches and neck pain for the past 6 months. She reports difficulty in opening her mouth wide, clicking and popping sounds in her jaw, and occasional teeth grinding. She denies any history of trauma to the head or neck. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Upon examination, her occlusion is Angle Class II division 1, with an overjet of 7mm and overbite of 4mm. She has mild tenderness upon palpation of the temporomandibular joint and cervical spine. She has a forward head posture and a rounded shoulder posture. She is not undergoing any orthodontic treatment and has all first molars present. She is an eligible candidate for this study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 6 months. He reports that the pain is constant, dull, and achy, and it is often exacerbated by prolonged sitting or standing. He has also been experiencing numbness and tingling in his legs, particularly when he walks or stands for an extended period of time. The patient has been diagnosed with spinal stenosis and neurogenic claudication. He has tried various conservative treatments such as physical therapy, medication, and epidural steroid injections, but has not experienced significant relief. He has no history of spine surgery, fractures, systemic inflammatory disease, malignancies, or infections affecting the spine. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

A 57-year-old postmenopausal woman diagnosed with endometrial cancer after presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding. The patient underwent total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and was found to have stage III endometrial cancer with lymph node metastasis. The patient received external beam radiation therapy to the pelvis followed by brachytherapy. After 6 months, the patient developed recurrent disease with a CT scan showing multiple lung nodules and a pelvic mass. Biopsy of the pelvic mass confirmed recurrent endometrial adenocarcinoma. The patient has no other significant past medical history and has never smoked. Her physical examination is remarkable for a palpable pelvic mass. Laboratory analysis is within normal limits. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the effectiveness of combination therapy for the management of her recurrent endometrial cancer.

A 10-year-old boy was diagnosed with Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome (CCHS) after birth, and his PHOX2B mutation-confirmed CCHS was discovered. He has been receiving treatment for his condition since then. He is currently enrolled in school and is able to participate in most activities with some accommodations for his condition. He experiences occasional episodes of ANS dysregulation, including sweating, flushing, and tachycardia, which can be managed with medication. He has a history of hospitalizations due to respiratory distress and has been on mechanical ventilation. He has been referred to the International CCHS Registry to provide detailed phenotypic information about his condition. His parents are interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of CCHS and improve treatment options for their son and others with this rare condition. They are aware that participation is voluntary and there is no compensation for taking part. They are also interested in potentially participating in clinical trials and have agreed to allow their de-identified data to be shared with researchers conducting clinical trials.

Patient is a 29-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with severe von Willebrand disease (VWD). He has a history of requiring substitution therapy with von Willebrand factor (VWF) concentrate to control bleeding. He is scheduled to undergo an elective surgical procedure and is willing to participate in the study. His vital signs are within normal limits and his laboratory studies are unremarkable except for low VWF:RCo activity (less than 20 IU/dL) and VWF:Ag (less than 3 IU/dL). He has no history of pseudo VWD or other hereditary or acquired coagulation disorder, thromboembolic events, liver or renal disease, or hypersensitivity to any of the components of the study drugs. He is not pregnant or lactating, has not participated in another clinical study involving an investigational product (IP), and is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past year without success. She has undergone previous IVF cycles and has frozen embryos available for transfer. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and was diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) two years ago. She has no history of hydrosalpings or uterine myomas. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is feeling overwhelmed and anxious about her diagnosis and upcoming treatment. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has been taking medication for these conditions for the past 5 years. Despite her anxiety, she is motivated to find ways to cope with her illness and improve her quality of life. She is interested in alternative therapies and has some experience with meditation and yoga. She is physically able to participate in the program and is willing to commit to attending the mindfulness-based day-care clinic group program.

55 year-old male presenting with sudden onset slurred speech, right facial droop, and right arm weakness. He reports no prior history of stroke or transient ischemic attack. The patient has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is on lisinopril and atorvastatin respectively. A non-contrast CT of the head was performed which did not show any acute intracranial hemorrhage. The patient was started on aspirin and admitted to the stroke unit for further evaluation and management. MRI of the brain revealed acute infarct in the left insular cortex and left basal ganglia. The patient is being considered for enrollment in the BRAIN clinical trial to evaluate the clinical utility of a novel blood test, the Triage Stroke Panel, as an aid in the diagnosis and assessment of stroke. The patient meets the inclusion criteria as he is 18 years or older and has cerebral ischemia suspected within 24 hours of symptom onset. There are no exclusion criteria that apply to this patient.

A 65-year-old retired teacher who is generally healthy and active is being recruited for this study. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, stroke, or diabetes, and her blood pressure and cholesterol levels are within the normal range. She completed the neuropsychological assessment at baseline and did not have a diagnosis of dementia. She enjoys reading, doing crossword puzzles, and traveling with her husband, and she is excited to participate in this study to learn more about how her cardiovascular health may impact her cognitive performance in the future.

A 32-year-old female who experienced sexual assault two years ago and has been diagnosed with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is eligible for this clinical trial. She has not received any previous treatment with Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) or Metacognitive Therapy (MCT) for her PTSD. She is not actively suicidal, psychotic or suffering from severe depression, and there is no evidence of alcohol or drug dependence. She has been experiencing symptoms of PTSD for more than three months. The patient does not have borderline personality disorder and is able to understand and speak Norwegian.

This is a 55 year-old African American male with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years. He has been on various medications but continues to have elevated blood pressure readings. He has a BMI of 29 and is interested in improving his diet to potentially lower his blood pressure. He is proficient in English and has access to a smartphone and email. He has not participated in any related trials and has not had any cardiovascular events in the past 6 months. He is motivated to improve his health and is interested in participating in this study to learn how to adopt the DASH eating pattern through a digital intervention.

A 67-year-old woman is scheduled for elective laparoscopic abdominal surgery. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her BMI is 28.5. She has not used any opioids in the past 5 days. Her kidney function is normal, with an estimated creatinine clearance of 75 ml/min by the Cockcroft-Gault formula. She is classified as ASA II. She has never received methadone for pain management before. She is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the use of methadone for perioperative pain management in elderly patients.

A 16-year-old white male with ependymoma had surgery to remove most of the tumor, but there is still a small amount remaining. He has not received chemotherapy or radiation therapy yet. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical or surgical history. He has no known allergies or history of drug reactions. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is a high school student and enjoys playing soccer. He has no neurological symptoms, such as headaches, visual disturbances, or seizures. His Karnofsky performance score is 70. His MRI shows a small amount of residual tumor in the posterior fossa. His CSF cytology is negative for malignant cells. His laboratory values are within normal limits, with a creatinine clearance of 85 ml/min/1.73 m², a total bilirubin level of 0.8 mg/dL, an SGOT level of 30 U/L, an SGPT level of 25 U/L, an ANC of 1,500/μL, and a platelet count of 120,000/μL. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive GM-CSF to potentially improve his outcome.

25-year-old female who has a history of recurrent ankle sprains over the last 2 years. She is an active individual and enjoys playing soccer, but has been limited by ankle instability. She reports feeling like her ankle gives out frequently during physical activity and she is unable to confidently perform cutting movements or change direction quickly without fear of re-injury. She has not received any formal rehabilitation for her ankle and is interested in participating in a study to address her concerns. She reports a score of 12 on the Identification of Functional Ankle Instability (IdFAI) questionnaire and a score of 85 on the Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM) Activities of Daily Living (ADL) subscale. She meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

A 65-year-old woman presents with a history of ischemic stroke affecting the left cerebral hemisphere, which occurred 4 weeks ago. She reports impaired finger tapping on the left side of her body and difficulty flexing her left wrist. She has been receiving standard stroke care and physiotherapy since the onset of her stroke. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and ibuprofen as needed. She reports no known allergies. She is alert and oriented, with no acute distress. Her vital signs are stable, and her physical examination is unremarkable except for left-sided deficits. She is able to communicate effectively and has no history of alcohol or drug addiction or any neurologic or psychiatric disease. She is interested in participating in the study and willing to comply with the program assessment and follow-up.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman from the United States who was recently diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer. She has undergone surgery to remove the tumor and has completed several cycles of chemotherapy, but her cancer has progressed. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. Her laboratory results are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria for this study.

55-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of ALS according to El Escorial criteria. The patient has been experiencing symptoms for 2 years and has a forced vital capacity of 50%. The patient has a stable nutritional state and does not have any other neurological or psychiatric disorders. There is no history of treatment with steroids or immunoglobulins in the last year. The patient has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 3 months and has no history of malignancy or cancer. The patient is HIV-negative and has no antibodies against hepatitis B or C in the serological studies. The patient does not have tracheostomy or use mechanical ventilation. The patient has no clinical suggestive data of infection in the site of lumbar puncture.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma in his right kidney. He is scheduled for surgical resection of the affected kidney. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other medical conditions and is not on any medications except for his blood pressure medication. The patient has no history of any other malignancy. He denies any symptoms related to his kidney cancer such as hematuria, flank pain or weight loss. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness on palpation of the right flank. His laboratory values including complete blood count, electrolytes, and liver function tests are within normal limits. His renal function is normal with a serum creatinine of 1.0 mg/dL. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

45 yo F with a history of differentiated thyroid cancer that has progressed despite multiple rounds of conventional curative and palliative treatments. Patient has multiple metastatic lesions visible in images and has not responded to therapeutic doses of iodine. Patient also has persistent local disease progression not amenable to surgical or radiation therapy management. ECOG score is less than 2 and life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 3 months. Adequate bone marrow, liver and renal functions have been confirmed. The patient is physically, intellectually, and emotionally able to take oral medication. A negative serum pregnancy test has been performed within 7 days prior to start of treatment. The patient has agreed to use adequate contraceptive methods. The patient has not received chemotherapy or cancer immunotherapy in the 4 weeks prior to admittance to the study. The patient has not received radiotherapy in the 4 weeks preceding admittance to the study. The patient has not received tyrosine kinase inhibitors or other targets agents, or monoclonal antibodies that target VEGF or VEGF receptors prior to admittance to the study. The patient does not have a known or suspected allergy or hypersensitivity to sorafenib. The patient does not have any condition according to the judgment of the treating physician that could jeopardize the patient's safety or compliance to the study. The patient has voluntarily consented to their participation and the same has been recorded in a written informed consent form.

The patient is a 67-year-old man who has a history of atrial fibrillation and is currently taking warfarin and aspirin daily. He has recently undergone a pacemaker implantation and has developed a complicated wound at the site of the incision. The wound is not healing properly, and there is a risk of hematoma due to the patient's anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy. The patient is experiencing pain and discomfort, and the wound has not responded to traditional wound care methods. The patient is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of receiving anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy.

52-year-old male admitted to the ICU with severe pneumonia and respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. He has no known allergies to medications, including monoclonal antibodies. He is able to provide written informed consent or his legally authorized representative is available to do so. The patient has not been diagnosed with Pseudomonas infection or colonization in the last 30 days, and is not immunocompromised. He has not taken any investigational drugs or prohibited therapy for the past month or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer. He does not have acute liver injury related criteria or other contraindications for the study, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of hepatitis B infection. He was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis five years ago and has been under the care of a hepatologist. He has been taking medications for his liver disease and has had no major complications. However, he recently developed some mild symptoms such as fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and occasional nausea. His hepatologist recommended him to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new medication called danoprevir. The patient is interested in participating in the study as he wants to contribute to the development of new treatments for liver disease. He does not drink alcohol or smoke cigarettes. He has no significant medical history other than his liver disease. He weighs 75 kg and his BMI is 28 kg/m2. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his laboratory tests show a creatinine clearance of 80 mL/min. He has never donated or lost more than 450 ml of blood in the last 60 days. He is willing to abstain from alcohol, grapefruit, and grapefruit juice during the study period.

The patient is a 8-year-old boy with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). He has been recommended for equine-assisted occupational therapy (EAOT) by his primary care physician due to his difficulty with social, behavioral, and occupational functioning. He has mild to moderate symptoms of ASD and has never participated in EAOT before. He is able to tolerate a helmet and follow safety rules while riding horses. He has no previous experience with EAOT in the last 6 months and his weight is within the set exclusion criteria. He is currently taking medication for anxiety and has been receiving speech therapy and occupational therapy for the past year. His parents are very supportive and willing to participate in the study. They are willing to bring him to Hearts and Horses Therapeutic Riding Center for the 10-week intervention and will be able to fill out weekly measures of his social functioning, self-regulation, and occupational performance.

This is a 9-year-old girl with a clinical diagnosis of type III spinal muscular atrophy. She was diagnosed at the age of 3 with progressive muscle weakness and early fatigue, which has limited her mobility. She is able to stand independently but requires support to walk long distances. She has no history of fractures or other complications related to her condition. She is currently under the care of a paediatrician at the neuromuscular clinic at the Duchess of Kent Children's Hospital in Hong Kong. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the safety and feasibility of whole body vibration therapy (WBVT) for children with SMA. She and her parents have provided informed consent for her participation in the study. She will be able to stand on the vibration platform with or without support and undergo clinical examination and DXA evaluation. She has not been using any medications that would exclude her from participation in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old American man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 6 months ago. The biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 3+4=7. He has no history of any other malignancy, and his PSA level was 12 ng/mL at the time of diagnosis. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, which is well controlled with lisinopril. He is married and has two children. He is a retired factory worker who likes to spend his free time gardening and fishing. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications other than lisinopril. His vital signs are stable, and he is in good overall health. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive the Proscavax vaccine and contribute to the advancement of prostate cancer research.

Patient is a healthy 25-year-old woman with a BMI of 22 kg/m² who is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of chronic diseases or gastrointestinal disorders and is not a smoker. She is not a vegetarian and does not have any food restrictions. She does not consume more than 2 alcoholic beverages per day and is not currently taking any medication or dietary supplements that affect lipid absorption or transport. She has no known allergies or intolerances to any of the study products.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past year. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy. She has difficulty sleeping and has lost weight unintentionally. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, but her mother had depression in her later years. She takes medication for high blood pressure and has no other major medical conditions. She lives within a 45-minute drive from New York Hospital-Westchester Division. She scored 20 on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale and 26 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). She does not have claustrophobia or any implanted metal. She is interested in participating in the study to help understand her condition better and contribute to future research.

This is a 45 year-old female who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer to the liver and bones. She has been started on a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) for the past 2 weeks as part of her treatment regimen. She has no known history of muscular or neurological disorders. Routine blood tests have been planned as part of her treatment and she has been informed about the study. She has consented to participate and is willing to provide blood samples for the study.

Kirsten is a 65-year-old woman who was diagnosed with head and neck cancer six months ago. She underwent radiation treatment and chemotherapy, which resulted in some difficulties with swallowing. Her medical history also includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. Kirsten lives alone but has a strong support system with her two children who visit her every day. She is able to sit in a chair for extended periods and can clear her throat when necessary. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Kirsten has been referred to occupational therapy for a swallowing assessment, and she has expressed interest in participating in this research study.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was diagnosed with Intermediate-2 risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) two years ago. He has received six cycles of 5-azacitidine but has not responded to the treatment. He is not a candidate for stem cell transplant due to his age and overall health. He is currently not receiving any other treatments for MDS, including filgrastim and erythropoietin. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has been off any standard or investigational MDS therapies for the past four weeks. He is willing to adhere to the prohibitions and restrictions specified in the protocol and has signed the informed consent document indicating his understanding of the purpose of and procedures required for the study. He is willing to participate in the study and adhere to the contraceptive requirements specified in the protocol. He has no history of HIV-1 seropositivity, active infections, uncontrolled hypertension, uncontrolled intercurrent illness, poorly controlled seizures, or other major medical conditions that would limit his ability to tolerate and/or comply with study requirements. He has not undergone major surgery recently and has fully recovered from any previous surgeries. He is not currently receiving any other investigational agents, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy.

32-year-old male diagnosed with temporal lobe epilepsy, who has been on antiepileptic treatment for 1 year with no significant improvement, is being referred for participation in a clinical trial investigating the role of inflammation in epilepsy. The patient has had consistent EEG evidence and clinically documented partial seizures, and seizure focus localization has been determined by standard clinical, neurophysiologic, and imaging studies. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or dependence and is able to give written informed consent. The patient has no prior diagnosis of brain disease other than epilepsy and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient will be undergoing blood and urine laboratory testing, PET scans with [11C]PBR28, and a brain MRI. The patient has no history of claustrophobia or any other medical illness that would interfere with the study procedures.

6-month-old male infant diagnosed with RSV bronchiolitis presenting with a cough, difficulty breathing, and fever for the past two days. The infant is not on any supplemental oxygen and has no history of congenital anomalies of the heart or chronic lung disease. The infant is alert and responsive but appears to be working hard to breathe with intercostal retractions and nasal flaring. The infant has no difficulty feeding and has been taking in fluids well. The family is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was brought to the emergency department with cardiac arrest. After 35 minutes of resuscitation, he achieved return of spontaneous circulation. His initial rhythm was ventricular fibrillation. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Upon arrival at the hospital, he was intubated and mechanically ventilated, and a central venous catheter was inserted. His baseline temperature was 37.8°C. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the COOLCATH study and will be considered for enrollment. The medical team will randomize the patient to receive either the RhinoChill transnasal cooling system or standard care using the Blanketrol III cooling blanket. The patient's tympanic and oesophageal temperature will be monitored every 10 minutes until he reaches therapeutic hypothermia (<34°C). Once TH is achieved, the RhinoChill system will be discontinued, and the patient will receive maintenance therapy using the Blanketrol III cooling blanket for 24 hours.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of cerebral infarction 10 days ago. The patient presents with severe hemiparesis on the left side of the body, as measured by a Fugl-Meyer motor scale score of 20, and a Screening Motricity Index score of 65. The patient has no history of previous clinical strokes or psychiatric disorders, including psychosis and substance abuse. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and has no known CNS pathology such as brain tumor, significant language dysfunction, or severe neglect. The patient does not have a history of seizures, left ventricular hypertrophy, or mitral valve prolapse. The patient has no significant renal or hepatic failure, and is not currently using anti-epileptic medications, psychostimulants, or neuroleptics. The patient is not currently on diazepam, phenytoin, propranolol, tricyclic antidepressants, steroidal contraceptives, cyclosporine, or theophylline. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is interested in exploring new treatment options to enhance motor recovery following a stroke.

A 58-year-old post-menopausal woman presents with complaints of vaginal dryness, irritation, and dyspareunia for the past 6 months. She reports that these symptoms are affecting her quality of life and causing discomfort during sexual activity. She has not used hormone replacement therapy for the past 3 months and has not consumed any high soy diet or remedies for post-menopausal symptoms. On examination, she has < 5% superficial cells on cervical cytology and a vaginal pH of >5. She has a normal pelvic and breast exam. She is otherwise healthy with no history of significant cancer or any other significant medical conditions. She has a BMI of 25 and is able to adhere to the visit schedule and protocol requirements. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

61-year-old male with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) for the past 4 years. He has been on anticoagulation therapy with warfarin and rate control with metoprolol since his diagnosis. He has experienced occasional palpitations and shortness of breath despite being on medication. He has been referred to the cardiology office for evaluation and possible enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the effects of colchicine on C-reactive protein (CRP) levels in patients with AF. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits, and he has no history of myopathy or neutropenia. He reports occasional mild GI discomfort after meals, but no known GI disorders. He has no known allergies or contraindications to colchicine use. He is willing to participate in the trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 10 to 12-month-old infant residing in the rural area of Matlab HDSS intervention area in Bangladesh. The infant has completed all doses of EPI immunizations, including BCG, DPT, HBV, Hib, OPV, and measles, at least four weeks prior to enrollment. The infant is healthy and does not have any acute medical illness with or without fever within the last 72 hours or an axillary temperature (≥ 37.5°C) at the time of vaccination. The infant is not severely or moderately malnourished, has no history of prematurity, underlying medical conditions, serious chronic disease, or known or suspected impairment of immunologic function. The infant has not received a JE vaccine or measles vaccine within 4 weeks prior to, or scheduled to receive a vaccination during, the conduct of this trial. The infant is not enrolled in another clinical trial involving any therapy and is able to attend the scheduled visits and comply with the study procedures.

The patient is a healthy 24-year-old female who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her last menstrual period was one week ago. She has a BMI of 23. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg and her heart rate is 80 beats per minute. She has no abnormal findings on physical examination. She is interested in participating in the trial and is willing to comply with all the study requirements and procedures. She has no history of travel to cholera-endemic areas, and she has not received any cholera vaccine. She has never had a history of cholera or ETEC infection. She has no history of any allergies or previous adverse effects to antibiotics. She has not used any laxatives in the past six months, and she has no history of eating disorders. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study and for four weeks before and after the challenge. She has no history of immunodeficiency, cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, endocrine disorder, liver disease, renal disease, gastrointestinal disease, anal or rectal disorders, or neurologic disease. She has a good comprehension of the study requirements and has passed the comprehension assessment test with a score of 85%.

The patient is a 65-year-old female presenting with pain and stiffness in her right thumb for the past 6 months. She reports difficulty with gripping and holding objects, and the pain has been progressively worsening. The patient has a history of osteoporosis and hypertension. She is currently taking calcium and vitamin D supplements and an ACE inhibitor for her hypertension. Upon physical examination, there is tenderness and swelling at the base of the right thumb, and limited range of motion in the thumb joint. Radiography confirms the diagnosis of rhizarthrosis, and the Dell's stage is determined to be moderate. The patient is considered eligible for the clinical trial and is provided with information about the study. After reviewing the information sheet and understanding the requirements of the clinical trial, the patient consents to participate. She is able to read and speak French fluently. The patient will be followed up for 3 months and will undergo intra-articular injection of hyaluronic acid as part of the study treatment. The main criterion for evaluating the effectiveness of the treatment will be the influence of the radiological stage on the outcome.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who recently underwent a prostate biopsy which confirmed a diagnosis of low-risk prostate cancer. The patient has a PSA level of 4 ng/mL and a biopsy GS of 3+4 with only 2 positive cores. The patient has no known metastatic prostate cancer and has not undergone any prior treatment for prostate cancer. The patient has a life expectancy of over 10 years and is able to provide consent in English or Spanish. The patient has not yet made a treatment decision and is interested in learning more about the OncotypeDX Prostate Cancer Assay and how it may impact his treatment decision. The patient has no history of psychiatric or psychological conditions and has no contraindications to primary treatment according to the physician's judgment.

A 50-year-old male with a history of high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes was recently diagnosed with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). He has not received any prior therapy for CLL. His Rai stage is III, and he has a World Health Organization (WHO) performance status of 1. His ECG shows a normal QTc interval, and his liver, hematologic, and renal functions are all within acceptable range. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and diabetes. He does not have a history of seizures, autoimmune diseases, or other serious medical conditions that would affect the evaluation of adverse events. He is willing to practice effective contraception during the study and is able to continue contraception for 12 months after his last dose of study treatment.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who has been experiencing coughing fits attributed to a respiratory tract infection for the past 5 days. The coughing worsens at night, leading to disrupted sleep for both the child and the parent. In addition, the coughing has been frequent during the day, causing discomfort and making it difficult for the child to engage in normal activities. The child has not received any antihistamines or cough medicine in the past 24 hours and has not been diagnosed with any chronic respiratory condition. The parent is willing to provide written consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial. The child has no known sensitivity to the components of the cough syrup or placebo.

Patient is a 65-year-old male scheduled for unilateral cataract surgery with posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation. He has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. The patient has no known allergies to medications. He is not currently taking any medications that are disallowed for the duration of the study. The patient has been informed of the study and has signed the Informed Consent Form. He is willing and able to follow all instructions and attend all study visits. The patient is able to self-administer the study drug or has a caregiver available to assist. He is not currently pregnant, nursing, or planning a pregnancy. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has not used any investigational drugs or devices in the past 30 days and has no conditions or situations that may put him at increased risk or interfere with his study participation.

Patient is a healthy 30-year-old woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the feasibility of a larger study comparing zanamivir and trivalent split virus influenza vaccine for prophylaxis against influenza infection. She has no known allergies to any component of the influenza vaccine or zanamivir and has not received the influenza vaccine since March of 2008. She has no history of adverse events associated with the use of antiviral medications and is not expecting to be unable to take zanamivir for more than 72 hours during the study period. She does not plan to spend more than 2 consecutive weeks outside of Canada or more than 100 km from the study site during the study period. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding a child under 12 months of age, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has not received immunoglobulin within six months of study entry and does not have any immunocompromising condition or therapy that would be expected to reduce the efficacy of vaccination. She has no plans to receive cytotoxic or radiation therapy during the study period and does not have a history of cardiovascular or pulmonary disease that has required hospital admission within the past year. She does not have a history of asthma or other chronic respiratory disease and is not participating in a trial that will result in the receipt of an investigational medication during the period that zanamivir may be taken (15/Nov/2008 to 30/Apr/2009).

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a known history of coronary artery disease. He has been on aspirin therapy for the past year and is scheduled to undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the next few weeks. His treating physician has recommended dual antiplatelet therapy with prasugrel (Effient®) or ticagrelor (Brilinta®) following the procedure. The patient provides written informed consent for the VerifyNow® PRUTest® Cardiovascular Population Expected Values On-Drug Study. He is currently not receiving any investigational antiplatelet agent and has not received GP IIb/IIIa therapy (ReoPro®, Integrilin®, Aggrastat®) or any therapy containing dipyridamole (Persantine®, Aggrenox®) within the past 2 weeks. The patient is not a woman who may be pregnant or of childbearing potential.

This clinical trial is seeking participants for the evaluation of elimination and control strategies for T. solium, a neglected parasitic disease complex that affects both humans and pigs. The study will be conducted in the Katete district in the Eastern Province of Zambia, an area known to be endemic for T. solium. Participants must be willing and able to participate in all aspects of the study, including providing blood and stool samples, participating in a questionnaire survey and group discussions, and taking oral anthelmintic tablets (for the elimination arm only). They must also be aged five years or older and without epilepsy. Those who are seriously ill and unable to engage in normal daily activities without assistance are excluded from the study. Participation in this clinical trial will contribute to the evaluation of effective strategies for the elimination and control of T. solium in highly endemic areas of Sub-Saharan Africa.

John is a 58-year-old man who has been diagnosed with COPD by his physician. He has been experiencing dyspnea as a main symptom that has limited his daily activities. He has had no exacerbations in the past 4 weeks and has not had any changes in his medications. His forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) is less than 50% predicted. He does not have any obvious pulmonary bullae demonstrated by chest CT scan or X-ray. He has not had any recent facial, upper airway, or upper gastrointestinal tract surgery that would preclude receiving NIV therapy. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medications. He has no history of coronary artery disease, cardiac arrhythmias, or other respiratory diseases. He has no musculoskeletal or neurological disorders. He is willing to comply with the research protocol.

42yo male with a history of smoking and COPD exacerbation, admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to pneumonia. The patient was intubated and started on mechanical ventilation with pressure support ventilation (PSV). Despite aggressive treatment, the patient remains on mechanical ventilation with persistent hypoxemia and increased respiratory distress. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is being considered for enrollment to compare the effects of PSV with neurally adjusted assist (NAVA) and assisted mechanical ventilation controlled by patient through a button.

25 year-old healthy male with no significant medical history, who weighs 180 pounds and is 5'10" tall. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any recreational drugs. He has not consumed any caffeine in the past 24 hours. His most recent physical exam was within the past year and was normal. He has no known allergies to medical equipment or materials. He is interested in participating in the trial to help advance medical knowledge and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 53-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with recurrent Clostridium difficile infection (CDI). She had been treated with antibiotics twice in the past 90 days, but her symptoms had not resolved. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but she was not on any medications at the time of admission. On physical examination, she had diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Laboratory investigations showed leukocytosis, elevated creatinine, and positive C. difficile PCR assay. She was approached to participate in an open-label, randomized controlled trial comparing fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) to standard antibiotic therapy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

A 72-year-old retired man with diabetes and hypertension has a stage III pressure ulcer on his buttock. He was recently hospitalized for pneumonia and received antibiotics. He is currently being treated for his pressure ulcer by a nurse at home. He has difficulty with mobility due to arthritis in his knees and relies on a wheelchair for transportation. He lives with his spouse who helps with daily activities. He has no history of skin diseases or allergies. He takes daily medications for diabetes and hypertension. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to avoid frequent visits to the hospital and reduce the burden of transportation on his spouse.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who has a history of congenital heart disease. She has previously undergone cardiac surgery and is currently being monitored by a cardiologist. She is in good general health and has no other significant medical problems. She is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and wishes to continue the pregnancy to term. She has not experienced any complications during her pregnancy so far. She has no history of smoking or substance abuse. She speaks English fluently and is able to understand and follow instructions clearly. She is willing to participate in a study that will evaluate her cardiac function using echocardiography and serum B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) measurements. She understands that the study will require multiple visits to the hospital and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

25 yo F, college student, physically active, but has not engaged in strength training for the last 6 months. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the effect of heavy, explosive strength training on bone mineral density in young women. She has no history of fractures and no known bone disorders. Her past medical history is unremarkable. She is not currently taking any medications that may affect bone metabolism. She is willing to participate in a 12-week strength training program, consisting of 3 sessions per week. She understands that she will be randomized to either the intervention group or the control group. She is looking forward to contributing to the research and improving her overall health.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with myasthenia gravis. He has been experiencing muscle weakness and fatigue, especially in his arms and legs, and has difficulty swallowing. His neurologist has recommended therapeutic apheresis procedures as part of his treatment plan. He has been referred to the Apheresis clinic at University of Texas Southwestern University Hospital and Clinics for TAP. He speaks and reads English and is available for appointments during the clinic's operating hours. He is not currently undergoing chemotherapy.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with COVID-19 and hospitalized due to severe respiratory symptoms, including cough, fever, and shortness of breath. She required mechanical ventilation and was in the hospital for 3 weeks before being discharged with residual lung dysfunction. She complains of persistent shortness of breath and cough, and her recent chest X-ray shows radiological changes consistent with interstitial lung disease (ILD). She is now a candidate for follow-up examinations, including clinical and functional lung examinations, HR-CT scans, and immunofibrotic pattern determination in peripheral mononuclear cells (PBMCs) at 1, 3, and 6 months after discharge. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the declaration of consent according to ICH-GCP Guidelines.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of asthma and allergic rhinitis for over a year. She has a positive skin prick test for D. pteronyssinus, birch pollen, and a 5 grass mixture. The patient has a history of completely reversible bronchial obstruction and has been diagnosed with allergic asthma. She has not had any exacerbations of asthma or rhinitis recently.
