The patient has not taken any inhaled glucocorticoids in the past month, antihistamines in the past 7 days, short-acting β2 agonists in the past 12 hours, long-acting β2 agonists in the past 2 days, or leukotriene receptor antagonists in the past 14 days. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient does not have any significant permanent allergy symptoms and has not had any active airway infections in the past month. She does not have any psychiatric disorders or a history of alcohol or narcotic abuse. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed written consent.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 5 years presents with worsening joint pain and swelling in her hands and feet. She has been on methotrexate for the past 12 weeks and is currently taking oral corticosteroids at a dose of 5mg/day prednisone. She has tried several other medications in the past without much relief, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs). She is sexually active but currently not pregnant nor lactating. She is willing to comply with the scheduled visits, arthroscopy, laboratory tests, and other procedures required for the study.

Maria is a 52-year-old woman who works as a teacher. She started experiencing muscle weakness in her left arm and hand around 18 months ago, which gradually spread to her other limbs. She also noticed difficulties with speaking and swallowing, and has lost a significant amount of weight due to her difficulty swallowing food. Maria was recently diagnosed with ALS according to the El Escorial criteria. She has no significant medical history other than hypertension, for which she takes medication. She has no history of autoimmune disease, cancer, or any systemic infection. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Maria is interested in taking part in a clinical trial for ALS and is willing to undergo two intrathecal administrations of mesenchymal stem cells, if she meets the inclusion criteria. She has a good understanding of the protocol and is willing to grant the informed consent.

Patient is a 35-year-old man who works in construction and has been suffering from severe chronic hand dermatitis for the past year. He has tried several topical treatments, including corticosteroids and tacrolimus, but has not seen any improvement in his symptoms. His dermatitis is affecting his ability to work and perform daily activities. He has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse in the past 12 months and has not used any investigational agents in the past 30 days. He has not used systemic retinoids or methotrexate in the past 6 months and has not used tetracycline or other vitamin supplements containing vitamin A in the past 4 weeks. He is willing to use effective contraception if he has a female partner of childbearing potential. He has normal liver function tests and no diagnosis or symptoms of inflammatory bowel diseases or active depression. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to try a new treatment option for his severe chronic hand dermatitis.

A 62 yo F with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease presented to the hospital with progressively worsening chest pain and shortness of breath over the past week. She was diagnosed with triple vessel coronary artery disease and scheduled for combined cardiac surgery procedures during normothermic CPB. She has preserved left ventricular function with an LVEF of 55% and normal preoperative S-creatinine levels. She has no contraindications to radiocontrast and has not had a cardiac transplantation or dissection. She is interested in participating in a study that investigates the effects of CPB on renal perfusion, filtration, and oxygenation.

This is a 32 year-old male who was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B, confirmed by positive HBsAg and HBeAg for more than 6 months. He has been experiencing fatigue, nausea, and abdominal discomfort for the past few months. His ALT level has been consistently elevated for the past three months, with a level of 220 IU/L. He has never received treatment for hepatitis B before. He denies active consumption of alcohol or drugs, and has no history of autoimmune hepatitis or neoplastic diseases of the liver. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the changes of cytokines during antiviral therapy.

The patient is a 24 year-old healthy female who is not currently taking any medication. She has a body mass index of 22.5 kg/m2 and has no clinically significant findings on physical examination. She has a regular menstrual cycle and has not been pregnant before. She is sexually active and will use protocol-specified contraception throughout the duration of the study and for 2 months after the final dose of study drug. She has no history of any active or unstable clinically significant medical condition.

A 32-year-old male veteran with a C7 spinal cord injury, resulting in impaired sensation, is currently using a manual wheelchair for mobility. He has been using a wheelchair for the past 3 years and has a history of pressure injuries related to sitting. He is currently being treated for a stage 2 pressure injury on his left ischial tuberosity. The patient reports difficulty consistently performing weight shifts due to lack of sensation in his lower extremities. His medical history is significant for hypertension and depression. He is currently taking Lisinopril and Sertraline. The patient is interested in participating in the Comprehensive Mobile Assessment of Pressure (CMAP) Refinement for Pressure Injury Prevention trial to improve his ability to prevent pressure injuries by using a mobile platform-based pressure mapping system. He is able to communicate verbally and cognitively with the study team and is interested in using CMAP at home as a self-management strategy for pressure injury prevention. The patient's seat cushion is standard and does not have a customized immersion style.

This is a 27-year-old female who underwent a double lung transplant due to end-stage cystic fibrosis. She received the transplant in [**4/2020**] and has been stable since then. However, she has been experiencing some gastrointestinal issues, including malabsorption, which can affect the absorption of her anti-rejection medication, mycophenolate mofetil (MMF). She has been taking a standard starting dose of 1000mg twice daily at her transplant center, but there is limited information on the pharmacokinetics (PK) of MMF in CF patients. This study aims to evaluate the effects of MMF on the body in lung transplant patients who have cystic fibrosis to improve survival outcomes. As part of the study, the patient will have three biweekly PK study visits, during which she will be admitted to the Michigan Clinical Research Unit (MCRU) at the University of Michigan Health Center. After administration of her morning dose of MMF, serial blood samples will be collected at specific intervals to determine PK parameters of MPA and MPAG. The patient will also have serum creatinine and albumin drawn, and samples will be obtained to measure IMPDH and correlated with PK parameters. The study will compare the patient's PK parameters to a cohort of non-CF lung transplant patients. The patient is eligible for the study as she is between 18-70 years of age, greater than 1 year post-transplant, has no evidence of acute rejection, and has stable renal function. However, she will be excluded from the study if her serum creatinine is greater than 2 mg/dl, she has received pulse steroids within 3 months of the study entry, she has chronic diarrhea, or is concurrently on interacting medications.

The patient is a 35 year-old male who has been a smoker for the past 10 years. He smokes about 10 cigarettes per day and has tried to quit multiple times in the past without success. He is in generally good health with no history of significant medical conditions. He has no known allergies to drugs or other substances. He is currently not taking any medications and has not had any recent surgeries. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new method of administering varenicline to help him quit smoking. He has no known skin conditions that may affect drug absorption through the skin.

32-year-old female with a past medical history of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) diagnosed according to the McDonald criteria (2005) and with an EDSS score of 3.0. She has been experiencing recurrent episodes of blurred vision, weakness, and numbness in her legs for the past 2 years. Her current medications include glatiramer acetate and vitamin D supplements. She has not received any corticosteroid treatment for her MS in the last 6 months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of biomarkers to monitor medication treatment in RRMS. She does not have any metal implants or pacemakers and is not currently pregnant. She is willing to sign a consent and follow study procedures. She will undergo neurophysiological testing with navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation (nTMS), electromyoneurography (EMNG), neuropsychological assessment, and immunoassays on blood samples at 3 different time points: before the intake of steroids, 5 weeks after taking the steroids, and 6 months after taking the steroids. The overall testing will be accomplished in three days during each phase.

The patient is a 44-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. The tumour is a T3 lesion with axillary lymph node involvement. She has no past medical history of cancer or other chronic medical conditions. Her WHO performance status is 1, and she has no history of prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy to the treated breast. She is not currently taking any medications. She has a calculated creatinine clearance of 70 ml/min, and her cardiac function is normal. She is willing to undergo an additional core biopsy prior to the second cycle of chemotherapy. She does not have any known contraindications to bisphosphonate therapy and is not taking tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitor medication. She is not pregnant or lactating.

A 58-year-old male with a history of liver cirrhosis and alcohol abuse presents to the hospital with hematemesis and melena. He reports feeling weak and dizzy for the past few days. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hepatitis C. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol regularly. He has not had any previous episodes of variceal bleeding. On examination, he is pale and jaundiced with a distended abdomen. His blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, and his heart rate is 110 bpm. His laboratory workup reveals thrombocytopenia and an elevated prothrombin time. An esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) is performed, which reveals active bleeding from esophageal varices. The initial endoscopic treatment is unsuccessful in controlling the bleeding. The patient is eligible for the trial under Arm 2 and is randomized to receive either standard therapy or the self-expandable metal stent. The patient is monitored closely, and the outcome is recorded for further analysis.

A 58-year-old male with a history of stable angina and a single atherosclerotic lesion in his native coronary artery is being considered for a clinical trial comparing two drug-eluting stent systems. His left ventricular ejection fraction is 45%. He has not undergone any coronary revascularization within the past 6 months and has no planned treatment of more than one qualifying lesion at the time of enrollment. The target lesion is less than or equal to 28mm in length and is located in a vessel that is 2.5-3.5mm in diameter. The target lesion diameter stenosis is >50% and <100% by visual estimate. The target lesion is a minimum of 10mm distance from any previously treated segment of the target vessel. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and has provided written informed consent. He does not have a known sensitivity to sirolimus, paclitaxel, the polymeric matrices, stainless steel or cobalt chromium, and there is no planned treatment of the target lesion with any device other than the pre-dilatation balloon angioplasty catheter. He has not had a myocardial infarction within the past 72 hours, is not in cardiogenic shock, and has not had a cerebrovascular accident within the past 6 months. His creatinine level is within normal limits, and he does not have a contraindication to aspirin or clopidogrel. He is not currently taking immunosuppressant therapy and has not been treated with either Rapamune or paclitaxel within 12 months of the procedure. He is not a female with a positive pregnancy test or is lactating. He does not have an active infection or co-morbidities that could interfere with completion of study procedures, or life expectancy less than 24 months. He is not participating in another investigational drug or device trial that has not completed the primary endpoint or would interfere with the endpoints of this study. He meets the angiographic inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the angiographic exclusion criteria.

A 68-year-old Japanese woman was diagnosed with mild Alzheimer's disease 6 months ago. She has been experiencing memory loss, difficulty with language, and poor judgment. She frequently forgets appointments, faces difficulty in solving problems, and has trouble managing finances. Her Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 22. She is currently taking donepezil to manage her symptoms. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She has no significant neurological or psychiatric disorders other than Alzheimer's disease. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance the development of Alzheimer's disease treatment.

A 60-year-old male with a history of colonic diverticulitis (CD) and occult obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB) was recruited for the San Valentino Vascular Screening Project (SVVSP). He has been experiencing intermittent abdominal pain and rectal bleeding for the past year. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. The patient has been compliant with his medications and has not had any recent changes in his medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is physically active and walks for 30 minutes a day. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has chosen to be treated with polyglucosamine (PG) in addition to the Standard Management (SM) protocol. The patient will follow the diet and lifestyle modifications as outlined in the SM protocol. The patient will undergo the Hemoccult Sensa Fecal Occult Blood Procedure to measure OGIB at baseline, after one month, and after three months. The patient will also complete a visual analogue scale (VAS) to measure daily gastrointestinal discomfort (GID) at baseline, after one week, and after one and three months. The patient has been classified as DICA 2 according to the Diverticular Inflammation and Complication Assessment (DICA) classification. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with coronary artery disease (CAD) 6 months ago. He has a known history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He presented to the hospital with chest pain and underwent coronary angiography, which revealed a de-novo lesion in the left anterior descending (LAD) artery with 80% stenosis. The patient was advised to undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a paclitaxel-eluting balloon catheter. The patient understands the purpose of the trial and voluntarily agrees to participate. He has signed the informed consent form and is willing to follow up for the study. The target lesion in the LAD artery is 20mm in length, and the reference diameter of the target vessel is 3.5mm. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction is 50%. He is currently taking aspirin and clopidogrel, which he can tolerate well. He has no history of bleeding or coagulation disorders, and his renal function is normal. The patient has no history of peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding in the past 6 months. He does not have any other surgeries scheduled during the follow-up period.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with a history of angina (Canada Cardiovascular Society Class II) and hypertension. He has been taking medication for hypertension for the past 2 years, but his blood pressure remains high (average systolic blood pressure of 150 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure of 95 mmHg). He has also been experiencing episodes of chest pain and discomfort during physical activity. His resting ECG shows ST-T changes of LVH (Romhilt-Estes or Framingham Heart Study criteria, with typical LV strain pattern, or isoelectric, inverted or biphasic T waves) and ST-T changes of ischemia (ST depression, isoelectric, biphasic, negative or inverted T-waves). His serum potassium level is below 5.0 mmol/L. He has not had a myocardial infarction or coronary artery bypass graft surgery in the past 90 days, and he has not undergone percutaneous coronary intervention in the past 30 days. He has not been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation, implanted pacemaker, stroke, left or right ventricular branch block, or any other condition that would prevent him from adhering to the trial protocol. He is willing to comply with scheduled visits and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with congestive heart failure (CHF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) for the last 3 years. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been taking medications for his conditions, including ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and diuretics. His recent blood work showed a serum creatinine level of 2.5mg/dL and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 35mL/min/1.73m². He has no history of heart attack or stroke. He lives with his wife and has two adult children. He works as a retired accountant and enjoys playing golf in his free time. He has not participated in any other clinical studies for the investigational treatment of heart failure or chronic kidney disease.

A 35-year-old man presented to the obesity clinic with a BMI of 35 Kg/m2. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has struggled with weight loss for years. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no known allergies and is not taking any probiotics or dietary supplements. He does not have a pacemaker or any implanted electrical devices. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him lose weight and improve his overall health.

A 35-year-old female presents with a history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) with a platelet count of 25,000. She has received prior therapy for ITP and is experiencing bleeding that is uncontrolled with conventional therapies. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in an open label study of romiplostim. The patient has no history of hematological malignancy, myeloproliferative disorder, myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), or bone marrow stem cell disorder. She has not participated in any study evaluating PEG-rHuMGDF, recombinant human thrombopoietin (rHuTPO), or related platelet products. She is not known to have a hypersensitivity to any recombinant E coli-derived product. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and the investigator has no concerns regarding her ability to comply with the protocol procedures.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who suffered a traumatic brain injury due to a motor vehicle accident 2 years ago. She has been experiencing several cognitive, physical, and emotional symptoms since then, including memory loss, difficulty concentrating, balance problems, and depression. She is currently not physically active but can stand and walk without assistance. She has no prior history of exercise intolerance or any other significant medical or psychological conditions. Her medical records show a previous MRI scan that revealed mild diffuse axonal injury and no signs of intracranial hemorrhage. The patient is fluent in English and can provide informed consent. She is not currently taking any medications that would affect aerobic capacity or treadmill performance. However, she is a smoker and will need to refrain from smoking at least 4 hours prior to exercise testing sessions. Her BMI is within normal limits.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer with bone metastases. He reports experiencing back pain and stiffness, which has been affecting his daily activities and quality of life. He has undergone previous radiation therapy to some of his bone metastases, but the pain has persisted. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score of 80 and his systemic disease is currently controlled. Diagnostic spine MRI with and without contrast has confirmed the presence of vertebral metastases from C3 to L5. The lesions are solitary and involve two contiguous levels. The patient has no history of hematologic malignancies, connective tissue disease, or primary neoplasms of the spine. He is willing and able to participate in study activities and has given his informed consent to be enrolled in the trial.

A 14-year-old boy was referred to the school health nurse by his teacher due to excessive worry and avoidance behaviors. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few months, which have been impacting his school performance and social life. His parents also reported that he has been irritable and easily frustrated lately. He scored 28 on the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale (SCAS) and answered positively to the first question of the Children's Anxiety Life Interference Scale (CALIS), indicating that his anxiety is interfering with daily life. He and his parents are fluent in Norwegian and have provided signed informed consent for the study. He does not have any behavioral or learning problems that would make it difficult for him to participate in a group program.

28-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and cocaine addiction, currently in outpatient treatment program. He has been struggling with addiction for the past 5 years and has attempted to quit multiple times without success. He has experienced negative consequences such as job loss and relationship issues and has been diagnosed with depression and anxiety. He has never received any mindfulness-based education or self-efficacy training but is willing to participate in the study. He is able to communicate effectively and is interested in finding new ways to manage his addiction and improve his self-efficacy perception.

52 yo M with hypertension, abdominal obesity, and glucose intolerance diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. Patient has no previous history of cardiovascular disease. Patient reports difficulty incorporating fruits and vegetables into his diet due to time constraints and lack of access to fresh produce. The patient is interested in participating in a study to improve his health without the use of medications. Past Medical History: - Hypertension, diagnosed 5 years ago - Abdominal obesity, BMI 32 - Glucose intolerance, diagnosed 3 years ago - No history of cardiovascular disease - No history of cognitive impairment or terminal illness. The patient speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent. The patient does not have any known food-drug interactions or co-existing illnesses associated with systemic inflammation.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who presents to the emergency department with chest pain that has been ongoing for the past hour. The patient reports that the pain is a 9 out of 10 in intensity and radiates to his left arm. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and occasional smoking. An electrocardiogram reveals ST-segment elevations in the inferior leads, and the patient is diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The patient is taken to the catheterization laboratory for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stenting. After informed consent, the patient is randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either ticagrelor or prasugrel as part of the study. The patient does not have any known allergies to prasugrel or ticagrelor, and he has not taken any thienopyridine class of ADP receptor inhibitors. He is not currently on any oral anticoagulants, and he has not had any major surgery or trauma within the past 6 weeks. The patient's hemoglobin and hematocrit levels are within normal limits, and he does not have thrombocytopenia or polycythemia. He does not have any bleeding diathesis or history of gastrointestinal, genitourinary, or other site abnormal bleeding within the previous 6 months. The patient is able to give informed consent and is not expected to be unavailable until Day 5 of the study.

Patient is a 45yo male who presents with moderate to severe pain in his left shoulder after a fall from a ladder. X-ray shows a proximal humerus fracture that requires surgery for treatment. The patient has no history of shoulder surgery or fractures in the past. There are no neurovascular deficits noted on physical examination. The patient is able to sign the consent form and agrees to participate in the trial. The patient lives in close proximity to the facility and is expected to be able to attend all follow-up visits.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of major depressive disorder for the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and has lost interest in her usual activities. She also reports difficulty sleeping, changes in appetite, and decreased energy. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of bupropion extended-release and escitalopram oxalate in treating her depression. She is willing to comply with the study requirements, including attending regular study visits and taking the study medication as prescribed. Her liver function tests are within normal limits, and she has no history of seizures or other medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 6 months and has not received any psychotherapy in the past 3 months.

Pt is a 55yo F with a history of pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence, presenting for surgical intervention. The patient is otherwise healthy and has had no prior surgeries. She has a supportive family member who will be able to care for her at home post-operatively. The patient has been counseled regarding the study and is willing to participate. The patient is ASA class 1 with no significant comorbidities. All pre-operative testing and evaluation has been completed and there are no contraindications to same-day discharge.

This is a 42-year-old female who has been trying to conceive for over a year without success. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). She has undergone several rounds of fertility treatments in the past, including clomiphene citrate and letrozole, but has not had any success. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate a novel method to predict ovarian reserve and responsiveness, in order to increase her chances of success with future IVF cycles. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to receive a single hCG 10000 IU injection on cycle day 2-4, as part of the study protocol. She does not have any known allergies to human chorionic gonadotropin.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with multiple chronic conditions, including diabetes, hypertension, and arthritis. She requires regular medical attention and treatment to manage her conditions. She also has a caregiver, her daughter, who helps her with daily activities and accompanies her to medical appointments. They are both willing to participate in the study and have provided their consent. The patient and her caregiver have experienced challenges in navigating the healthcare system and coordinating their care, and they hope that the study will help improve the quality of care they receive. The patient is able to communicate effectively and is motivated to participate in the study to improve her health outcomes. She is open to collaborating with healthcare professionals to find the most effective treatment options for her conditions. Her caregiver is supportive and actively involved in her care, and is interested in learning more about how to best support the patient's health and well-being.

A 50-year-old woman presented to the clinic with a history of fibromyalgia for the last 7 years. She experiences chronic pain in her neck, shoulders, and back every day. The pain is worse in the morning and gets better with light exercise. She has been on a variety of medications, but none have provided relief. She has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. She is married with two children and works as an office manager. She has tried physical therapy and massage therapy, but the pain persists. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatments for her fibromyalgia.

A 40-year-old woman with a BMI of 39.5 kg/m2 presents with complaints of shortness of breath, fatigue, and difficulty in performing daily activities. She has a history of hypertension and sleep apnea, which are well controlled with medication and a CPAP machine, respectively. She has tried several diets and exercise programs but has not been able to sustain weight loss. She is interested in bariatric surgery for weight loss and has been approved for the procedure by her physician. She is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and does not have any current or past history of cancer, heart disease, kidney disease, liver disease, gallbladder disease, or chronic inflammatory diseases.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with a one-week history of cough, fever, and progressive shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is not currently taking any anticoagulants or antiplatelet medications. On examination, he is tachypneic, with an oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. Lung auscultation reveals bilateral crackles. He has no other significant findings on physical examination. His laboratory tests show a positive SARS-CoV-2 test and an elevated D-dimer level (3 times the upper limit of normal). His platelet count, INR, and fibrinogen levels are within normal limits. Based on his presentation, he meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and has no exclusion criteria. He provides informed consent to participate in the trial.

14 year old female student with no history of depression or other psychiatric disorders, currently in good health with no history of seizures or neurological conditions. She is a fluent English speaker, with no visual disturbances and has an IQ greater than 80. She is currently in puberty with normal development. The patient and her legal guardian have provided informed consent for the study. She is willing and able to attend all study visits, including EEG measurements and neurofeedback sessions.

A 35-year-old female who has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep for the past 3 months. She reports that she typically goes to bed around 10 pm and tries to fall asleep, but finds herself tossing and turning until around 1 or 2 am. She wakes up multiple times during the night and has trouble falling back asleep. She reports feeling tired and sluggish during the day and has difficulty concentrating at work. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of 2 dosage strengths of Lemborexant on a Multiple Sleep Latency Test in participants with Insomnia Disorder. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, including meeting the DSM-5 criteria for Insomnia Disorder, having an Insomnia Severity Index score greater than or equal to 15, and having regular bedtime and wake time. She also does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, such as having a history of drug or alcohol dependency, currently using prohibited medications, or having a prolonged QT/QTc interval.

14-year-old male with HIV infection diagnosed at age 9. The patient is currently on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with a combination of tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz. He has a history of well-controlled HIV viral load and stable CD4 counts. The patient has no known drug allergies and is compliant with his medications. He has experienced mild gastrointestinal side effects with ART in the past but has not had any significant adverse reactions. The patient is being followed by a pediatric HIV clinic and meets the inclusion criteria for the PENTA Fosamprenavir Study.

This is a 56 year old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presented with chest pain and was diagnosed with an acute myocardial infarction. EKG showed ST segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6. He was taken to the catheterization lab for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a drug-eluting stent placed in the left anterior descending artery. He has no history of prior myocardial infarction or bleeding disorders. He is currently on aspirin and clopidogrel therapy. He has no implanted pacemakers, defibrillators, intracranial metallic implants, or other medical devices. He is not pregnant and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 2 months.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with metastases to the liver, lymph nodes, and bone. She has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy in the past, but her cancer has progressed despite these treatments. She has tested positive for EGFR expression and is now seeking alternative treatment options. She is otherwise healthy with normal blood and organ function. She is currently not using any contraception but is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 12 weeks after the last dose of IMGN289. She is willing to sign informed consent and follow the study schedule and other protocol requirements. She has not received any other anti-cancer treatments during the study and does not have any symptomatic brain metastases or clinically significant diseases. She is not taking any medication for chronic skin conditions and has not experienced a severe rash requiring discontinuation of prior EGFR targeted therapy. She is not receiving therapeutic doses of warfarin or heparin for anti-coagulation and does not have a known diagnosis of HIV or active viral hepatitis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

55-year-old male with newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus confirmed by biopsy. The tumor stages and disease grades were classified according to the TNM classification (sixth edition) of the International Union against Cancer (UICC). CT scans of the neck, chest and abdomen, bone scan, endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS), endoscopy and esophagography were performed to determine the extent of the disease. The patient has a performance status of 1, with white blood cells >3,000/microL, platelets >100,000/microL, serum total bilirubin <2.0 mg/dl, serum transaminase <3 times the upper normal limit, serum creatinine <1.5 mg/dl and creatinine clearance >60 ml/min. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. The patient has no serious cardiac disease.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has a history of pulmonary MAC infection. He has been treated for the infection for 9 months with a combination of antibiotics, but the infection has persisted. The patient has moderate pulmonary disease due to MAC and has not been treated previously for this infection. He has no history of HIV infection and no extra-pulmonary infection of MAC. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has no other significant medical conditions, but takes medication for hypertension. The patient is willing to participate in the study and agrees to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been diagnosed with bilateral lung emphysema after a CT scan. He has been on guidelines-based therapy of COPD, including vaccinations against Pneumococcal infections and seasonal influenza. He has abstained from nicotine for the past three months and his CO-HB (haemoglobin) level is less than 2%. He has difficulty breathing and has been experiencing wheezing and coughing for the past year. His FEV1 (Forced Expiratory Volume 1 / one second capacity) is less than or equal to 45% of the reference value after bronchodilatation. His total lung capacity (TLC) is greater than or equal to 100% of the reference value and his residual volume (RV) is greater than or equal to 175% of the reference value. He has been deemed suitable for endoscopic lung volume reduction according to the multidisciplinary decision of the pneumology and thorax surgery division. He has signed the informed consent and understands the nature, significance, and implications of the study. He is able to understand and follow instructions of the study staff. He has not been hospitalized due to a COPD-exacerbation in the last three months and has not had more than three steroid-treated exacerbations in the last year. He has not had an increase of FEV1 (Forced Expiratory Volume) greater than or equal to 20% after bronchodilatation and does not have severe diffusion impairment (DLCO < 20%). He is not on a permanent anticoagulation therapy and does not have an indication for one besides ASS. He is not experiencing pulmonal cachexia, and he is not pregnant or lactating. He is not on a permanent treatment with more than 20 mg Prednison per day.

A 45-year-old male who underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation for acute myeloid leukemia three months ago presents with symptoms of acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD). He presents with a rash, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. After evaluation, he is diagnosed with Grade III aGVHD. The patient has no history of allergy to valproic acid and no active and severe infection. He is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trial and did not receive GVHD prophylaxis with valproic acid. The patient has no severe organ dysfunction, including heart, lung, liver, and kidney.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with end-stage renal failure and has been receiving maintenance hemodialysis treatment for the past 2 years. He reports having difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep, resulting in daytime fatigue and decreased quality of life. He has no history of surgical trauma, infection, or trauma in the past 3 months. The patient has stable heart function and no limb paralysis or speech disadvantages. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. The patient has no severe cardiovascular disease, sequelae of cerebral infarction or history of cerebral hemorrhage, history of COPD, history of myasthenia gravis, history of angle-closure glaucoma, blood system disease, or mental system disease. He is highly compliant with medical treatment and has good medical attitude. The patient has normal hearing and vision and has completed high school education.

45-year-old male diagnosed with HIV-1 infection for 5 years and has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with abacavir for 2 years. During a routine check-up, the patient was found to have the genetic marker HLA-B*5701 and was subsequently withdrawn from the CNA106030 study. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in this retrospective observational study. The patient resides in France and is affiliated to a social security category. The patient has no history of severe hypersensitivity reactions to medications and is currently experiencing no adverse events related to the ART. The patient has a CD4 count of 450 cells/mm3 and an undetectable viral load. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus, all of which are well-controlled with medications. The patient has no known drug allergies and is compliant with his current ART regimen.

Patient is a 62-year-old man from the United States who has a history of smoking for 40 years and has been diagnosed with emphysema. He has had several hospitalizations in the past year for COPD exacerbations and has been prescribed various medications to manage his symptoms. His BMI is 28, BP: 140/85, HR: 90/min. His pulmonary function tests show a FEV1 of 25% of predicted value and a residual volume of 160% predicted. The patient is not alpha-1 antitrypsin deficient.

33-year-old female presenting with chronic constipation for the past 6 months. She reports having bowel movements every 4-5 days with difficulty passing stool and feeling of incomplete evacuation. She also experiences bloating and abdominal discomfort. She denies any recent changes in her diet or exercise routine. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is currently well-controlled on levothyroxine. She is not taking any medications known to cause constipation or opiate medications. She has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or obstruction. She is not bedridden and is able to ambulate independently. She meets the Rome III criteria for functional constipation and is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the effects of lubiprostone on small bowel and colonic bacteria.

Sophie is a 32 year old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating for the past week. She made an appointment with her general practitioner, Dr. Smith, who suggested using point-of-care ultrasound (POC-US) to better evaluate her condition. Sophie agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent form. During the consultation, Dr. Smith used POC-US to examine Sophie's abdomen, and then provided her with a unique ID-number and a link to an online questionnaire about her experience with POC-US in the consultation. Sophie accessed the questionnaire using her phone and answered the questions about her experience with the ultrasound. She reported feeling more informed and involved in her care with the use of POC-US. She also appreciated the visual representation of her condition and the opportunity to ask questions during the examination. Sophie's responses will be used to evaluate patient experiences with POC-US in general practice.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension, on antihypertensive medication for the past 2 years. Despite treatment, his BP remains elevated with a systolic blood pressure ranging from 150-170 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure ranging from 90-100 mmHg. He has no significant past medical history and takes no other medications. Workup for secondary hypertension revealed an elevated aldosterone-renin ratio (ARR) of 1850 pmol/L per ng/mL/hr. The patient underwent a CT scan of the adrenals which showed a 2.5 cm right adrenal nodule. The patient was referred to the endocrine team for further evaluation and management. The endocrine team recommends further testing with adrenal venous sampling (AVS) and metomidate PET-CT to determine the lateralization of aldosterone secretion and whether adrenalectomy is indicated. The patient has no contraindications for either test and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male Gulf War I veteran who has been experiencing chronic pain in his lower back for the last 6 months. The pain is rated as a 7 out of 10 on the pain severity scale of the BPI-SF. Along with the back pain, he also experiences fatigue, mood swings, and gastrointestinal issues. He is currently taking medication for depression and anxiety, which has been stable for the last 4 weeks. He is willing to remain on the medication throughout the trial. He has a pacemaker implanted and has a history of seizures, which are currently under control with medication. He is not currently experiencing any psychotic symptoms or substance abuse issues, and he has not participated in any other clinical trials. He is willing to comply with the use of contraception during the trial. He is able to read, understand, and sign the informed consent form and is willing to attend all scheduled clinic visits.

The patient is a 48 year old male who was diagnosed with gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) 3 years ago. The tumor was localized and surgically removed, and the patient was then treated with imatinib and sunitinib, with the latter showing initial response but then disease progression. The patient has been on third-line therapy, but has shown progressive disease within the last 3 months before study entry. The patient is married and has two children. He is a construction worker and enjoys outdoor activities such as camping and fishing. His performance status is 1, and he has an estimated life expectancy of at least 6 months. His BMI is 28 with the BP of 130/80. His laboratory tests show adequate hematological and hepatic function. He has no significant cardiovascular disease, but has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He has not had any major surgeries or other significant illnesses. He has not received any previous treatment with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibodies or with axitinib. He is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male presented with painless blood in his urine for the past 2 weeks. He denied any lower urinary tract symptoms or flank pain. His medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. His family history was unremarkable. Physical examination was normal except for a palpable mass in the lower abdomen. Laboratory investigations revealed microcytic anemia and microscopic hematuria. CT scan revealed a 4 cm bladder mass with no evidence of regional or distant metastasis. Biopsy of the mass confirmed transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) of the bladder. The patient was assessed to be fit for a radical course of radiotherapy and was offered participation in the RAIDER clinical trial. He was informed about the possible treatments: 1) standard whole bladder radiotherapy, 2) standard dose tumour focused adaptive radiotherapy, and 3) dose escalated tumour boost adaptive radiotherapy. He was also informed about the study procedures and follow-up schedule. He provided a written informed consent and was enrolled in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage heart failure. He has been on the waiting list for a heart transplant for six months, and he has just received a heart transplant. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no significant past medical or surgical history. He is currently being treated with immunosuppressive medications, including tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone. He is at risk for post-transplant renal dysfunction due to his diabetes. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of daclizumab in combination with mycophenolate mofetil and sirolimus in preventing acute rejection of his transplanted heart. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing wrist pain and limited mobility in her right hand for the past year. She was diagnosed with a distal radius malunion with dorsal deformity and has been experiencing significant disability due to the condition. The patient has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. She does not have any inflammatory arthritis or radio-carpal osteoarthritis. The patient has been identified as eligible for the clinical trial and will be randomized to receive either bone graft or CaP bone cement during surgery to correct the malunion. Follow-up will be conducted for 24 months to monitor the patient's progress and assess the effectiveness of the treatment.

The patient is a 55 year-old male with a history of progressive dyspnea on exertion for the last 6 months. He denies any history of smoking or exposure to environmental toxins. He has no history of connective tissue disease or drug-induced toxicity. Pulmonary function tests reveal a restrictive pattern with decreased diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide. High resolution chest CT scan shows diffuse interstitial lung disease with a pattern not consistent with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. He is referred for a surgical lung biopsy to clarify the diagnosis of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia (IIP). He has no contraindications to undergo a surgical lung biopsy and is willing to provide informed consent.

56 yo M with a history of end-stage renal disease and on hemodialysis for the past 4 years. The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. He is compliant with his medications and has no history of alcohol or tobacco use. He has no known allergies. His current hemoglobin values have been stable on epoetin alfa at a dose of 150 Units/kg/week. His hemoglobin values over the past 4 weeks have been 11.0, 11.2, and 11.3 g/dL, respectively. The patient has a transferrin saturation (TSAT) of 25% and a ferritin level of 180 ng/mL. The patient has a history of a stable cardiovascular disease status and no symptomatic inflammatory disease. The patient is willing to give informed consent and is available for follow-up for the duration of the study.

A 40-year-old Caucasian woman with a family history of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease presents to the clinic. She has been diagnosed with ADPKD by genetic testing of PKD1 mutations and has more than 10 cysts in each kidney. She has a history of hypertension for the past 2 years, which has been managed with metoprolol and amlodipine. Her blood pressure is currently controlled at 140/90 mmHg. She has a BMI of 28.0 kg/m2 and her kidney function corresponds to CKD stage 2 (eGFR 60 mL/min/1.73 m2). She has no clinical signs of diseases in the heart, lungs, endocrine organs, brain, or neoplastic disease. Her blood and urine tests are within normal limits. She has never had a cerebrovascular insult or clinical evidence for aneurysm. She is a non-smoker and does not abuse alcohol or drugs. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not taking any medication except for her antihypertensive agents. Her electrocardiogram is normal.

32F primigravida, G1P0 at 39 weeks of gestation with no significant medical history presents for delivery at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Québec. Patient reports regular prenatal care and no complications during pregnancy. Fetal ultrasound showed no abnormalities. Patient denies any vaginal bleeding or discharge, abdominal pain or contractions at the time of admission. Upon examination, the cervix is found to be fully dilated, and the patient is in active labor. There are no signs of placenta previa or any other abnormalities. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and will be enrolled in the study. The research nurse will obtain 2 vaginal/anal samples using standard techniques, one sample will be used to detect GBS with the approved BD GeneOhm StrepB assay, and the other sample will be used for the development of the new point-of-care rapid detection GBS test. The participation in the study involves being observed for 30 minutes.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been smoking for the past 30 years. He was diagnosed with COPD two years ago and has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing. He had a hospitalization due to a COPD exacerbation 6 months ago but has been stable since then. He is currently taking inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids. His spirometry results show a post-salbutamol FEV1/FVC of 60%, and his post-salbutamol FEV1 is 45% of predicted normal value. He has no history of asthma, cardiovascular diseases, or other respiratory conditions. He has no prostate hypertrophy nor bladder obstruction. He is willing to participate in the study and has no other significant medical history. He is currently married with two children and works as a construction worker.

Maria is a 55 year old woman who works as a librarian. She has been experiencing subjective memory complaints for the past year, such as forgetting where she put things or having trouble recalling people's names. She also feels that her cognitive activities and physical activities have been lower than usual. She has no family history of mental diseases, but her father had a stroke in his 60s. Maria has never had any neurological diseases or brain injuries that led to loss of consciousness. She doesn't smoke or drink alcohol, but she does consume caffeine regularly. She has no history of substance dependence. Her vision and hearing are normal, and she doesn't use any hearing aids. She is interested in participating in the study and has voluntarily signed the Informed Consent Form.

A 14-year-old Haitian boy living in Miami-Dade County was referred to the study by his school counselor due to concerns of drug use and delinquent behavior. He has expressed feeling disconnected from his Haitian heritage and struggles to balance his Haitian identity with American culture. He lives with his mother, father, and three younger siblings, and they have been in the US for four years. He has never received mental health care or medication for any condition. He has been in trouble with the law for vandalism and petty theft, and he has experimented with marijuana. His parents are concerned about his behavior and are willing to participate in the study to help him.

Patient A is a 10-year-old male who fell off his bike and sustained a fracture in his right forearm. The fracture is located in the proximal one-half of the radius and requires a reduction maneuver. He has no other injuries or medical conditions, and no history of previous fractures. His primary language is English, and he and his parents are competent in English. They live in the same city as the study site and have no difficulty with maintaining follow-up. They have agreed to participate in the study and have provided informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old Korean man who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B six months ago. He has been undergoing clinical follow-up at a registered institution and has given informed consent to participate in the study. He has not undergone antiviral therapy for chronic hepatitis B before and is not concomitantly infected with HCV, HDV, or HIV. He does not have chronic alcoholism and has not been diagnosed with right-sided heart failure. He has undergone liver fibroscan and the result is valid. He is not pregnant at the time of registration.

The patient is a 5-year-old child who has been experiencing difficulty breathing and coughing for the past three days. The cough has been productive of yellowish sputum. The child has a fever of 38.5°C and is lethargic. On examination, there is chest indrawing and respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute. The oxygen saturation level is 85% on pulse oximetry. The child is diagnosed with severe pneumonia and requires hospital admission for further management. The family consents to participate in a clinical trial comparing solar-powered oxygen delivery to standard oxygen delivery. Blood samples will be taken and data will be collected to determine the non-inferiority of solar-powered oxygen delivery. This study could potentially improve outcomes and save numerous lives in resource-poor settings in Africa and Asia.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been suffering from mucosal-dominant pemphigus vulgaris (mPV) for the past 2 years. She has painful blisters in her mouth, nose, throat, and genitals that make it difficult for her to eat, drink, and speak. She has tried several standard immunosuppressive therapies, but none of them have been effective in managing her symptoms. Her anti-DSG3 antibody ELISA test was positive at screening, indicating the presence of mPV. She has no active cutaneous lesions associated with PV, and her prednisone dosage is less than 0.25mg/kg/day. She has no other autoimmune disorders requiring immunosuppressive therapies. Her absolute lymphocyte count is above 1,000/µL at screening. She is very motivated to participate in this study as she hopes to find a treatment that can lead to complete and durable remission of her mPV symptoms.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman with cataracts in both eyes. She reports a gradual decrease in vision over the past year, with particular difficulty in reading and driving. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She has no known allergies. Her visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/30 in the left eye with correction. The corneal astigmatism in her right eye is measured to be 0.75D and in her left eye is 1.0D. The difference between her eyes is 0.25D. She is interested in reducing her dependence on glasses after cataract surgery and is willing to participate in the study. She provides written informed consent before surgery. Her corneal topography is regular in both eyes, and she does not have any other ophthalmic diseases that would exclude her from the study.

30-year-old female who works at a desk job for long hours and has noticed decreased flexibility in her back and legs. She has no current physical or mental health problems and is not pregnant. She is interested in ways to improve her overall health and wellbeing and is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating a mind-body approach to improving flexibility. She is able to commit to attending the required sessions and follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) two years ago. She is currently taking methotrexate and prednisone to manage her symptoms. She has no known allergies to eggs or previous adverse reactions to seasonal influenza vaccines. She has never received the H1N1 vaccine. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the H1N1 vaccine in patients with rheumatic diseases. She is able to provide informed consent and is within the age range of 18-65.

47 year old man diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B infection for the past 4 years. He has been treated with entecavir for the past 2 years with no significant improvements in his condition. He is currently experiencing fatigue, abdominal discomfort and a decrease in appetite. He has no history of autoimmune disease, HIV or HCV infection. He has not been on antiviral therapy other than entecavir for the past 3 months. He is willing to continue taking entecavir throughout the study.

The patient is a newborn baby boy who was born at 36 weeks gestation. He was delivered via vaginal birth and weighed 3.2 kg at birth. He was diagnosed with uncomplicated hyperbilirubinemia at 48 hours of life and was placed under phototherapy treatment. His current total serum bilirubin concentration (TsB) is 15 mg/dL. He is otherwise healthy and has no other medical issues. His parents are both in good health and have no history of medical problems. The baby is not in an incubator and is able to receive phototherapy treatment with light emitting diodes (LED's) at a distance of 20, 29, 38 or 47 cm from the mattress. The baby's medical team will monitor his TsB levels before and after 24 hours of treatment and will measure the irradiance every 8th hour.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic migraines for the past year. She also complains of jaw pain and difficulty opening her mouth. She has tried various medications with limited success in managing her migraines. She has not received any previous treatment for her temporomandibular joint disorder. She is currently employed as a data analyst and reports that her migraines and jaw pain have been affecting her work productivity and quality of life. She has no known neurological or psychiatric disorders, and has not undergone any physical therapy or dental treatment in the past 6 months. She has not had any surgery or trauma to the orofacial region. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatments that may help relieve her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with cervical cancer. She underwent a radical hysterectomy and now requires preventative placement of a ureteral stent. She has no known allergies and currently takes medication for high blood pressure. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her past medical history is significant for a cholecystectomy and an appendectomy. She works as a teacher and is physically active, regularly practicing yoga and jogging. She has no history of urinary tract infections or any other genitourinary issues. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given her informed consent.

A 58-year-old woman has been diagnosed with relapsed large B-cell lymphoma that has not responded to previous treatments. She has undergone two lines of systemic therapy in the past. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and presents with multiple lymph nodes of at least 1.5 cm in size that are measurable. The patient has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled. Her absolute neutrophil count is 2.5 x 10^9/L, and her platelet count is 80 x 10^9/L. Her creatinine clearance is 60 mL/min, and her serum ALT/AST levels are within normal limits. She has no evidence or history of lymphoma involving the central nervous system (CNS). The patient has not undergone autologous or allogeneic stem cell transplantation, nor has she received CD19 targeted therapy or chimeric antigen receptor therapy. The patient has not had any live vaccines within six weeks prior to the planned start of conditioning regimen, and she is willing to practice birth control from the time of consent through six months after the completion of anakinra injections. The patient is planned to receive standard of care therapy with axicabtagene ciloleucel and has agreed to participate in the clinical trial.

54-year-old male patient with a diagnosis of colon cancer with hepatic metastases who has failed or is intolerant to at least one systemic chemotherapy or liver directed therapy. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 at study entry. He is seeking alternative treatments as his current chemotherapy regimen has not been successful in reducing the size of his liver tumors. He has not had any previous treatment with irinotecan-based regimens. The patient has a life expectancy of >12 weeks. He has liver dominant disease defined as >/=75% tumor body burden confined to the liver and less than 60% liver tumor replacement. At least one month has elapsed since his most recent prior cancer therapy. The patient has measurable disease that will be directly treated with intrahepatic therapy (as defined by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors [RECIST] 1.1) and has at least one measurable liver metastasis> 2 cm. His main portal vein is patent. The patient has adequate hematologic function as defined by ANC >/= 1500/mL, Hemoglobin >/= 9.5 g/dL and a Platelet count >/=75,000/mL with INR </=1.3 prior to receiving DEBIRI-TACE. The patient has adequate hepatic function, as defined by Total bilirubin</= 2.0 mg/dL, AST and ALT </= 5 x the upper limit of normal (ULN), Albumin >2. The patient has adequate renal function, as defined by Serum creatinine</=2.0. The patient has a baseline international normalized ratio (INR)<1.5. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures, scheduled visits, and treatment plans. The patient is not allergic to contrast media and has no evidence of substance abuse or medical, psychological or social conditions that may interfere with the patient's participation in the study or evaluation of study results.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has never had a colonoscopy before. She has a family history of colon cancer, with her father being diagnosed at the age of 60. The patient has been experiencing occasional episodes of abdominal pain and bloating, but no blood in her stool. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Her physical examination is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and abdominal exam. She is willing to undergo a screening colonoscopy and is open to receiving sedation if needed. She is able to provide informed consent for the trial.

A 32-year-old female presented with a history of chronic diarrhea, bloating and abdominal pain for the last 2 years. She reports having several bowel movements a day with occasional urgency and loose stools. She denies any blood in her stool, weight loss or fever. She has tried several over-the-counter medications for her symptoms with no relief. Her medical history is significant for anxiety and depression for which she is taking an anti-depressant medication. She has no known drug allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. Physical examination was unremarkable except for mild tenderness in the lower abdomen. Laboratory studies including complete blood count, liver function tests, and renal function tests were all within normal limits. Serologies for celiac disease and stool studies for infectious diarrhea were negative. Colonoscopy showed no evidence of inflammatory bowel disease or malignancy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating to help improve her symptoms.

The patient is a 35-year-old male smoker who has been smoking for 10 years. He smokes an average of one pack per day and reports experiencing cravings whenever he tries to quit smoking. He has attempted to quit smoking several times in the past but has been unsuccessful. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He reports that he is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring cigarette cravings in smokers. The patient scores a 7 on the Fagerström Test for Cigarette Dependence. He is willing to abstain from smoking for 4 hours prior to each laboratory visit. He is not currently using cigarette cessation products and does not have any endocrinological problems. He is mentally and physically healthy and is not pregnant. The patient is motivated to quit smoking and hopes that this clinical trial will provide him with tools to overcome his cravings and successfully quit smoking.

The patient is a 42-year-old female diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) for the past 8 months. She has been experiencing moderate pain and stiffness in her joints, with a disease activity score (28 joint) calculated using the C-reactive protein formula (DAS28-CRP) ranging from 3.5 to 4.8. She reports having at least 3 swollen joints and 3 tender/painful joints during screening and baseline. She has been taking methotrexate for the past 6 months but has not seen significant improvement in her symptoms. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of adding etanercept to her current treatment plan. She has no history of prosthetic joint infection, and has not used more than one experimental or commercially available biologic DMARD. She is otherwise in good health and meets all eligibility criteria for the study.

This is a 65 year-old female with a history of smoking for 40 years who was recently diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). She has not previously undergone any chemotherapy. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is rated as 2. Clinically or radiologically measurable disease has been identified per RECIST criteria. She does not have any gastrointestinal abnormalities or other active malignancies but has been diagnosed with hypertension and controlled hyperlipidemia. She does not have any uncontrolled brain metastases, significant cardiac disease, or severe abnormalities of the cornea. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of erlotinib versus standard chemotherapy for NSCLC patients with ECOG PS 2.

The patient is a 50-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She does not smoke and drinks no more than one cup of coffee or tea per day. She is willing to stop drinking coffee or tea during the study period. She is willing to use two acceptable methods of contraception during the study and at least 3 months before the start of the study. She has not taken any prescribed, herbal or over-the-counter medication within 2 weeks prior to the first dosing. She has no history of any clinical significant medical conditions or lipid disorders. She has not tested positive for HIV-1 or HIV-2, hepatitis B or hepatitis C. She has no history of intolerance to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or aspirin, history of gastric or duodenal ulceration, personal or family history of abnormal clotting or bleeding. She is interested in participating in the study and contributing to medical research.

The patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has no other significant medical history and is generally healthy. He is scheduled for an elective robotic prostatectomy at the Josie Robertson Surgical Center. The patient reports occasional mild back pain but otherwise has no significant pain or discomfort. He is alert and cooperative during the examination. The patient has a BMI of 30 and is not taking any medications or supplements that are contraindicated for this study. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient is a 24-year-old female who wears glasses for mild myopia. She is a student and spends long hours in front of the computer. Her glasses prescription is -2.00 D in both eyes. She has no history of eye diseases, allergies or infections. Her last eye exam was 6 months ago, and no abnormalities were found. She is interested in trying contact lenses for the first time. She has no known systemic diseases and is not currently taking any medications.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been scheduled for an elective vaginal hysterectomy due to uterine fibroids. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She reports no other medical conditions or chronic pain. The patient has never had surgery before and is nervous about the procedure. She is able to read and understand the information sheet and has signed the consent form. The patient has an American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) physical status of 2. She has a BMI of 28.5 and her renal function is normal. She has been instructed to fast for 8 hours before the surgery. The patient will receive general anesthesia using propofol and sufentanil. She will be monitored for her heart rate, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation throughout the procedure. She will not receive any regional anesthesia for postoperative pain relief. The aim of the study is to determine the effectiveness of measuring nociception at the end of surgery to predict postoperative pain. The patient will be evaluated for pupillary dilation reflex and heart rate variability after a standardized electrical stimulus, and the results will be used to predict the amount of opioid analgesia needed to alleviate postoperative pain. The patient will be asked to rate her pain levels at regular intervals after the surgery.

Patient is a 45-year-old man with a BMI of 45 who has been diagnosed with severe obesity and has been advised to undergo laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. He has a history of chronic low back pain and has been taking NSAIDs for the past 5 years. He has no known allergies to medications and has never undergone any surgical procedures in the past. The patient has been classified as ASA II and is otherwise healthy. He has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate.

A 50-year-old male who underwent bilateral nerve-sparing retropubic radical prostatectomy six months ago and is currently experiencing erectile dysfunction. The patient has no history of severe erectile dysfunction requiring medical therapy prior to the procedure and has a PSA level consistent with the absence of prostate cancer. He has a history of sexual potency prior to the radical prostatectomy without requiring medical therapy. The patient is in a monogamous heterosexual relationship with their current partner for at least three months and is willing to make at least four attempts at intercourse per month without using any other treatments for erectile dysfunction. The patient has no allergy or hypersensitivity to PDE5 inhibitors or any of the components of these drug products. The patient is not currently taking any medication that interferes with the metabolism by the CYP 3A4 enzyme and has a stable hormone replacement therapy dose for at least three months. The patient is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including scheduled study visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

A 62-year-old retired teacher with a family history of Parkinson's disease (PD) is concerned about the possibility of developing the same condition. She has noticed a slight tremor in her left hand and a decrease in her sense of smell. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of major medical conditions. She has not taken any investigational drugs or radiopharmaceuticals for the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could detect early changes in dopamine cells in her brain, even before symptoms of PD become apparent. She is willing to undergo DaTSCAN™ brain imaging and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study. She is a non-smoker and does not have any known allergies or sensitivities to iodine-containing products.

The patient is a 15-year-old female who has been diagnosed with scoliosis. She has a curvature of her spine with a Cobb angle of 40 degrees and has been recommended to undergo spinal surgery. She has no known medical conditions and is otherwise healthy. Her parents have consented to her participation in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis by a rheumatologist. She is currently under treatment with a combination of DMARDs, NSAIDs and corticosteroids. She has no history of COVID-19 infection and has agreed to be vaccinated against COVID-19. She is affiliated with Social Security and has signed a consent form to participate in the COVID-RIC3 study. She is not under legal protection and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

As this clinical trial is focused on resident scheduling in the ICU, there is no specific patient description required. However, patients who meet the inclusion criteria mentioned in the eligibility section of the trial, that is, patients admitted to an ICU during either period of the study, will be included in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago. He underwent orchiectomy and was started on LHRH agonist treatment. He has received 6 cycles of docetaxel in the past and has shown progression of the disease with increasing PSA levels. He is currently on palliative radiation therapy for bone metastases in the right femur. He does not have any other significant medical history and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. His physical exam is unremarkable except for the prostate gland that is hard and nodular. His PSA level is 150 ng/mL, and his bone scan shows multiple bone lesions in the pelvis and spine. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore additional treatment options.

The patient is a 60-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis in her right knee. She experiences significant pain that impairs her daily activities and quality of life. She is scheduled to undergo an elective total knee replacement surgery under spinal anesthesia. She has no known allergies or contraindications to regional anesthesia. Her BMI is 30. She is otherwise healthy and classified as an ASA physical status classification system II. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. The patient is able to follow instructions and report any sensations or changes in her leg muscles during the procedure.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with no history of fertility disorders. He has a good body build and secondary sexual characteristics. He does not have any congenital anomalies of the testis or chronic illnesses. He has no problems with male fertility, varicocele, or sexual performance disorders. He tested positive for COVID-19 and is currently recovering from the acute phase of the infection. He has not experienced any symptoms related to his reproductive system. He is willing to participate in the study to help researchers understand the effect of COVID-19 on spermatogenesis.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was recently admitted to the hospital with acute heart failure syndrome and reduced ejection fraction. His chief complaints were dyspnea and fatigue, and he had elevated left ventricular pressure. His projected length of stay is greater than 2 days, and he is currently undergoing targeted treatment for heart failure, including IV diuretics. The patient has not been previously diagnosed or treated for sleep disordered breathing, but an attended inpatient sleep study during the index hospitalization confirmed the diagnosis of severe obstructive sleep apnea with more than 50% of the events being obstructive. The patient's LVEF is less than 45%, and he has not been previously treated for sleep apnea with positive airway pressure therapy. The patient does not have chronic respiratory insufficiency or overt neurological deficits, and he does not require renal replacement therapy. The patient is not on the heart transplant list or considered for LVAD implantation in the subsequent year. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effect of in-hospital diagnosis and treatment of sleep disordered breathing on post-discharge mortality and readmissions in hospitalized patients with acute heart failure syndrome and reduced ejection fraction.

Patient is a 65-year-old male with stage III pancreatic cancer who has been receiving radiation therapy for the past 2 weeks. He reports feeling very weak and has noticed a significant decrease in his appetite, resulting in a weight loss of 5% in the past 30 days. He complains of feeling full after only a few bites of food and has been experiencing nausea and occasional vomiting.
