The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance score of 1 and is mentally competent to complete study assessments. He has a history of controlled hypertension and takes lisinopril 10mg daily. The patient is not currently on any appetite stimulants or steroids, and has no known allergies to megestrol acetate. He is willing to use an adequate and reliable method of contraception as he is sexually active, but not planning on fathering any children.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has a healthy pregnancy with no complications and is hoping to have a water birth. She has attended prenatal classes and has expressed a desire for a natural birth with minimal medical interventions. She has no history of any chronic illnesses or mental health conditions. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or drugs. She is excited about the prospect of a water birth and hopes it will help her to have a positive birth experience.

The patient is a 35-year-old African American woman who has been diagnosed with asthma since childhood. She has been experiencing symptoms such as wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that are triggered by various environmental factors such as pollen, dust, and pet dander. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators to manage her asthma symptoms. Her past medical history is significant for allergic rhinitis and eczema. She has no smoking history and has never been diagnosed with any other lung diseases. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her lung examination reveals wheezing on auscultation. Her spirometry results show a decreased forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) and forced vital capacity (FVC) consistent with her diagnosis of asthma. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to find new approaches for empowering studies of asthma in populations of African descent. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to provide blood and skin samples, undergo a physical exam, and perform a breathing test.

Patient is a 60-year-old male from the United States with a history of chronic knee pain and difficulty walking due to osteoarthritis. He has tried various non-surgical interventions such as physical therapy, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and corticosteroid injections without significant improvement. He has a BMI of 30, BP: 135/85, HR: 80/min, and laboratory studies within normal limits. He is scheduled to undergo a total knee arthroplasty with the Triathlon Tritanium cementless knee components. He is able to ambulate independently and is willing to return for follow-up visits for a minimum of two years after surgery.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing eye redness, itching, and irritation for the past three months. She wears contact lenses regularly and has been using over-the-counter eye drops to alleviate her symptoms. She was diagnosed with blepharokeratoconjunctivitis (BKC) by an ophthalmologist and was advised to discontinue contact lens use for the duration of the study. The patient is willing to comply with the study procedures and is not currently participating in any other clinical investigations. She has no known hypersensitivity to tobramycin or ocular corticosteroids and has not undergone any ocular surgery in the past three months. She has no uncontrolled systemic diseases or debilitating conditions that could interfere with the safety and efficacy evaluations of the study drug.

Patient is a 30-year-old female with a BMI of 32. She has a history of occasional binge eating and has noticed that her eating behaviours have worsened in the last 6 months. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is fluent in English and is right-handed. She has no metal implants, tattoos, or claustrophobia. She has normal hearing and temperature perception. She is willing to be informed about chance findings of pathology. She has no current or past history of drug or alcohol dependency and does not smoke. She has no food allergies but follows a vegetarian diet. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the effect of intranasal insulin on cognitive processes and appetite.

John is a 26-year-old healthy male who works as a software developer. He has no significant medical history and has never been diagnosed with any chronic disease. John is physically active and exercises regularly. He has a bodyweight of 70 kg and his BMI is within the normal range. He has no history of malignancy or cardiac abnormalities. John does not have a history of drug addiction or excessive alcohol use. His recent serum uric acid level was found to be within the range of ≥4.5 and <9 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to the scientific community and to earn some extra money.

A 65-year-old female diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and experiencing memory loss for the past year. She has no history of substance abuse or neurological disorders such as epilepsy, cerebral aneurysm, or multiple sclerosis. She has no intracranial implants or cardiac pacemakers. She is English speaking and willing to provide consent to participate in the study. She has signed HIPAA authorization and uses an effective method of birth control. She is not pregnant nor breast feeding. She does not use any medications known to lower the seizure threshold and/or affect working memory.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 5 years. He experiences shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing, which significantly affect his quality of life. He has been treated with bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids but has not seen significant improvement. The patient's CT scan showed emphysematous, bullotic changes in the upper lobes of his lungs. His pulmonary function tests showed a total lung capacity (TLC) of 120%, residual volume (RV) of 180%, diffusion of lung CO (DLCO) of 70%, and forced expiratory volume 1 second (FEV1) of 25%. His 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) is 150 meters. The patient has no history of heart disease, arrhythmia, or pulmonary hypertension. He is not currently undergoing cancer treatment and has a life expectancy of more than 2 years. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial as he hopes to find a more effective treatment for his COPD symptoms.

The patient is a 59-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced unresectable non-small cell lung cancer. He has completed definitive chemoradiation therapy and is now being considered for IMFINZI as maintenance therapy. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago, with a smoking history of 40 pack-years. He has not experienced any severe side effects from his previous therapy. However, he has had some mild radiation pneumonitis, which has been well-managed with corticosteroids. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who previously participated in the Phase I clinical trial ISS T-001 for Recombinant HIV-1 Tat vaccine. He was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 3 years ago and has been receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) since then. He has been compliant with his ART regimen and has an undetectable viral load. He is generally in good health and has no significant medical history other than HIV-1 infection. He is willing to participate in this observational study to evaluate the persistence of the anti-Tat humoral and cellular immune responses for an additional 3 years. He is aware of the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent. He is available for follow-up visits every 24 weeks and is willing to provide blood samples for evaluation of the anti-Tat specific humoral and cellular immune responses.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is focused on assessing the knowledge, attitude, and practice of a group of dental interns towards caries risk assessment. It is not a patient-focused study and does not involve any individual patients.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for over two years. She has been experiencing significant psychotic symptoms with a PANSS total score of 79. She has been hospitalized for her condition and is willing to stay in the hospital for the duration of the study. She has not taken clozapine in the past 60 days and has no history of bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder. Her psychosis severity is rated as moderate (CGI-S 4) and she has no known suicidal risk. She has no history of disallowed concomitant psychotropic medication and has no other clinically significant illnesses. Her laboratory results are within normal limits.

A 50-year-old Chinese male patient with a diagnosis of neovascular glaucoma presents with complaints of blurred vision, severe eye pain, and headache. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for blood pressure control. The primary evaluation reveals neovascularization of the iris and angle, with elevated intraocular pressure readings in the affected eye. The patient has a visual acuity of light perception or better in the study eye. The patient is willing and able to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures and provides signed informed consent. The patient has not used any intraocular anti-VEGF agents in the study eye in the past 3 months and does not have an active ocular or periocular infection in the study eye. The patient has no history of thromboembolism, congestive heart failure, renal failure, myocardial infarction, or stroke. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not participating in another simultaneous medical investigator or trial.

A 26-year-old woman who is currently serving in the military is interested in participating in a clinical trial studying the effects of suvorexant and zolpidem on sleep induction. She has no history of sleep disorders and reports sleeping an average of 7 hours per night. She does not use any prescription or over-the-counter sleep aids and has not traveled across multiple time zones recently. Her morning wake-up time is 0600 and her lights-out time is usually around 2200 during weekdays. She does not take naps frequently and does not have any symptoms suggestive of a sleep disorder. She is fluent in English and has passed the "Volunteer Comprehension Assessment" with a score of 85%. She is not pregnant or lactating and is on oral contraceptives. She does not have a history of neurological disorder, cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, or liver disease. She does not use any illicit drugs or have any heavy alcohol use. She has a BMI of 23 and has a resting blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg and resting pulse of 80 beats per minute. She is interested in participating in the study to contribute to the advancement of knowledge in the field of sleep medicine.

This is a 72-year-old woman with a history of severe aortic valve stenosis. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain with exertion. She is scheduled for a Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) via the trans-femoral route. She has been informed about the transShield Embolic Protection System (EPS) feasibility study and has agreed to participate. Her femoral artery iliac arteries are appropriate for the 12French transShield Expandable Introducer and 20F Embolic Protection Device. She has no history of carotid artery stenosis >70% in either carotid artery, severe vascular tortuosity, or contraindication to anticoagulation therapy. Additionally, she has not had a history of bleeding diathesis, stroke, transient ischemic attack, or acute myocardial infarction within the prior 6 months. She is willing and able to comply with the study inclusion/exclusion criteria and complete the follow-up requirements.

55 yo female with a history of recurrent ovarian cancer, who has previously undergone primary surgery and chemotherapy, presents with abdominal swelling and discomfort. Imaging reveals evidence of recurrent disease, and biopsy confirms the presence of platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian cancer. The patient has received at least one prior platinum-based therapy and has had disease progression within 6 months of most recent platinum therapy. The patient has measurable disease, and is in good overall health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has not previously received treatment with a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor, including durvalumab, and meets all other inclusion criteria. The patient has not been involved in the planning or conduct of the study, and is willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study. The patient has no history of primary immunodeficiency or allogeneic organ transplant, nor any current autoimmune disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or uncontrolled intercurrent illness. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or of reproductive potential.

A 54-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 3 months ago and started chemotherapy treatment. She is currently receiving a combination of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide every 3 weeks. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, she is concerned about the risk of contracting the virus during her treatment. She has no history of respiratory illnesses or allergies. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no known history of liver, renal, or cardiac disease. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to understand the study and give informed consent. She has tested negative for COVID-19 at study entry as measured by routine testing. She does not currently take any other medications and is able to swallow tablets.

A 12-year-old girl presented to the dermatology clinic with multiple warts on her hands and feet that have been present for several months. She reported no pain or discomfort but was self-conscious about their appearance. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. Physical examination revealed multiple, small, raised, and rough-surfaced skin lesions on her hands and feet that were consistent with verrucae. She has not used any over-the-counter or prescription treatments for her warts in the past month. She is willing and able to comply with study instructions, including applying the occlusive heat patch(s) as directed, and returning to the clinic for required visits. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to any of the components of the patches, including the adhesives. Her parents and she have given written consent and assent, respectively, to participate in the study. She is not currently taking any systemic therapy, and she is not immunocompromised or known to be HIV+. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning a pregnancy during the study period.

The patient is a 29 year old woman who has been diagnosed with stage 3 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) due to polycystic kidney disease. She has been married for 2 years and she and her husband are considering starting a family. She has been taking medications for her CKD and has been regularly seeing a nephrologist. She has no history of hypertension or diabetes. She is fluent in English and is able to provide informed consent for the study. She is interested in participating in this study to better understand the risks associated with pregnancy and to help other women with CKD who are considering pregnancy.

A 42-year-old male patient was referred to the Samsung Medical Center Geropsychiatry and Affective Disorder Clinics in Seoul, Korea. He has a history of depression and has been treated with various antidepressants over the past 5 years. He has a family history of depression on his mother's side. He has no other significant medical conditions, but he smokes a pack of cigarettes a day. He has not taken any psychotropic medication in the past 2 weeks and has not taken fluoxetine in the past 4 weeks. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to provide blood samples for pharmacogenomic and peripheral lymphatic biomarker testing.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few weeks. Her doctor has recommended a cardiac computed tomography (CT) to rule out any underlying cardiac conditions. However, the patient is feeling anxious about the procedure and is unsure of what to expect. She has read through the written information provided by the hospital, but still feels ill-prepared. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to use media to reduce anxiety for patients undergoing cardiac CT. She is willing to provide informed consent and is not currently an inpatient at the hospital.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was rushed to the hospital after experiencing difficulty moving her right arm and leg, along with slurred speech. She was diagnosed with acute moderate ischemic stroke based on a head CT scan. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is currently under control with medication. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her family history is negative for stroke or other neurological diseases. She lives with her husband and two children. Her pre-morbid mRS score was 0. Her NIHSS score is 10. She is able to speak and understand language, but her speech is slurred. She has some weakness in her right arm and leg. She is able to move them, but with difficulty. She is able to walk, but with a limp. She has no serious neurological deficits before onset. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is in good health, with no history of coagulation disorders. He has not had any recent surgeries or blood transfusions, and he is not currently taking any medications known to alter coagulation. His laboratory coagulation test results are within the normal reference range. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed a consent form. He is not pregnant or lactating and does not have a history of drug abuse or excessive alcohol consumption. The subject is able to provide written informed consent and is not incarcerated at the time of the study. This patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 30-year-old male presents with a history of premature ejaculation for the past 3 years. He reports that he ejaculates within 1-2 minutes of penetration during sexual activity. He is currently not in a relationship and reports that his premature ejaculation has negatively impacted his past relationships. He has no significant medical history and denies any drug or alcohol abuse. He is not currently taking any medications. He responded to the advertisement about the study on social media and is interested in participating. He is willing to use the device FLIP HOLE for manual masturbation at least five times per week for six weeks. He is willing to come to the Instituto Sexológico Murciano (ISM) for weekly follow-ups and to complete the required questionnaires. He is informed about the collaborative nature of the study and provides his informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old Chinese woman who has been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia for 5 years. She has a history of auditory hallucinations and delusions of persecution. She is currently taking Risperdal (risperidone) 4mg daily and has been stable on this medication for the past 8 weeks. She is able to perform daily activities and is independent in her self-care. Her family history is negative for any mental illness. She has completed high school education and is currently unemployed. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve her cognitive function and working memory. She has no history of seizures, metal implants, or cochlear implants. Her vital signs are within normal limits: BP: 120/80, HR: 75 bpm, RR: 16/min, and O2sat: 98%. She understands the study procedures, and she is willing to sign an informed consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing heartburn and regurgitation for the past three months. He has been taking over-the-counter antacids with little relief. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol excessively. He has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or other significant medical conditions. He is able to understand and complete questionnaires, and is willing to give written informed consent. He has access to a telephone for follow-up appointments. He has not taken any H2 receptor antagonists, antibiotics, or other medications that would exclude him from participating in the study within the past 7 to 14 days. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially receive treatment with rabeprazole sodium 20mg, esomeprazole 20mg or esomeprazole 40mg.

A 16 year old girl was admitted to the hospital with abdominal pain, jaundice, and confusion. She had no significant past medical history and was not taking any medications. Laboratory tests showed elevated liver enzymes, total bilirubin and a prolonged prothrombin time. She was diagnosed with acute liver failure (ALF) and was started on supportive care. Despite aggressive medical management, her condition continued to worsen and she was deemed a potential candidate for liver transplantation. However, due to her small size and severity of illness, the risk of surgery was deemed too high. She was then approached to participate in a clinical trial that involves hepatocyte transplantation. She will be officially listed for both liver and hepatocyte transplantation, and if a donor liver becomes available, she will receive a solid organ transplant. If not, she will undergo hepatocyte transplantation. She will be monitored closely for any adverse events and will receive immunosuppression therapy to prevent rejection of the transplanted cells. The goal of this treatment is to provide liver support until a donor liver becomes available or until her liver function recovers.

A 58-year-old male patient diagnosed with locally advanced gastric cancer after presenting to the emergency department with abdominal pain, weight loss, and persistent vomiting. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and he is a non-smoker and non-drinker. The physical exam revealed epigastric tenderness with no rebound, and the laboratory analysis showed anemia and elevated tumor markers. The CT scan revealed a large mass in the stomach with enlarged lymph nodes. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2. He is interested in participating in the study and has agreed to undergo randomization for neoadjuvant treatment.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) two years ago. She has been trying to conceive for the last six months and is currently 12 weeks pregnant. She has a history of irregular periods, acne, and hirsutism. Her BMI is 27, and she has a family history of type 2 diabetes. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions, and her physical examination is unremarkable. She lives in Odense and plans to continue residing there throughout her pregnancy.

A 28-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo egg collection for in vitro fertilization (IVF). She has been experiencing menstrual pain and dysmenorrhea for the past 5 years. She is not currently taking any pain medication. She has no hearing problems and has no phobia of music. She works as a teacher and enjoys listening to classical music in her free time. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. She has no history of chronic diseases or surgeries. She is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effect of music therapy on pain during egg collection.

The patient is a 65-year-old Danish woman who has been experiencing difficulty remembering things lately. She has noticed that she forgets where she put things and has trouble recalling recent conversations. She is generally healthy and takes no medications. She has no history of psychiatric illness or neurological disease. She speaks Danish fluently and has no issues with eyesight or hearing. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 30-year-old male was involved in a car accident 3 years ago, which resulted in a traumatic brain injury. Since then, he has been experiencing cognitive and emotional problems, such as difficulty with memory, attention, and concentration, as well as depression and anxiety. He has been receiving treatment for these issues, but has not seen significant improvement in his ability to participate in activities with family, friends, and in the community. He lives at home with his wife and two children, and is able to provide informed consent and collaborate in the goal-setting process. He is fluent in Norwegian and has no history of substance abuse or violence. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options that could improve his quality of life and help him better cope with the long-term effects of his traumatic brain injury.

68-year-old male with a history of osteoporosis and no prior fractures presents with pain and inability to bear weight on his right leg after a fall. X-rays reveal a subtrochanteric femur fracture, with the distal fracture limit within 4 cm below the trochanter minor. The patient is otherwise healthy and fit for surgery. The patient is informed of the study and agrees to participate. The patient has no cognitive impairment and is able to give informed consent.

50-year-old woman with a history of uterine leiomyoma, presenting with heavy and prolonged menstrual bleeding, pelvic pain, and pressure. She reports having to change her tampon or pad every hour and has had to miss work due to her symptoms. Ultrasound shows a uterine volume of 450 ml with multiple leiomyomas. She has opted for a vaginal hysterectomy and has minimal anatomic conditions for the surgery. She has no history of gynecologic malignancy and is not currently being treated with any hormonal therapy. She has no significant past medical history, no allergies, and is a non-smoker. She is compliant with medications and is able to attend regular follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is generally healthy and has no history of respiratory, gastrointestinal, hepatic or renal disease. She is a non-smoker and has not used nicotine products in the last 3 months. She weighs 60 kg and has a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2. She works as a receptionist and enjoys outdoor activities like hiking and swimming. She has no history of severe allergies or hypersensitivity, and has not donated plasma or blood in the past month. She is willing and able to use the Turbuhaler according to the provided instructions. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and does not take any medications. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help advance medical research.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 6 months. He is a construction worker and reports that his job requires him to lift heavy objects and perform repetitive motions. His pain is rated at 7/10 on the Numerical Rating Scale and is described as a dull ache that worsens with movement. He has tried over-the-counter pain medication with limited relief. He has no history of spinal surgery, cancer, or other major medical conditions. He is fluent in both written and spoken English. He is married and has two children. He does not have any implanted devices or metallic implants in his low back. He is willing to participate in the study and agrees to adhere to the treatment protocol. He signs the informed consent form and is enrolled in the study.

54-year-old female diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer. She has no known family history of breast or ovarian cancer. She is currently undergoing treatment and has consented to participate in the study. The patient is able to read, write and understand the material presented to her as part of the study. She has not undergone BRCA testing prior to the study enrollment.

A 52-year-old Caucasian female is diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has spread to her liver and lungs. She has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. Her ECOG performance status score is 1. She is not currently taking any targeted therapy for her cancer. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hypothyroidism which are well controlled with medication. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has not undergone any major surgeries in the last 4 weeks. She has not had any history of thromboembolism or severe unmanageable diarrhea. She has not received any TKIs within the past 4 weeks. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates a new drug for advanced solid tumors.

As this is a clinical trial focused on the implementation of an electronic medical record-based system for tracking post-discharge test results, a patient description is not necessary as it does not involve patient enrollment. The study is focused on physicians who are enrolled as study attendings at Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH) and Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) and patients who had their test results finalized after discharge and prior to subsequent admission.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing fatigue, decreased appetite, and increased thirst for the past 6 months. Laboratory tests revealed an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 20 mL/min/1.73m2, indicating stage 4 chronic kidney disease. His serum creatinine levels were elevated, and he had proteinuria. He has been prescribed medications to control his blood pressure and blood sugar levels. He has not undergone any previous treatment for kidney disease. He is willing to participate in this study to help evaluate the feasibility of estimating the prevalence of stage 4 CKD in the Gard department of France.

Pt is a 38yo F diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis per International Autoimmune Hepatitis Group criteria. She has had an incomplete response to standard therapy and is seeking alternative treatment options. Her liver biopsy with Ishak modified HAI indicates active AIH. She has not received any prior B-cell depleting therapy within the past year and her B-cell count is above 50 cells/µL. She is not regularly using any medications with known hepatotoxicity and does not have decompensated cirrhosis. She does not have a diagnosis of overlap syndrome with AIH or drug-related AIH. She has no history of drug abuse or unhealthy alcohol use. She has never been diagnosed with malignancy of any organ system. She is not currently pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who underwent a liver transplant 6 months ago at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. She is concerned about her weight gain since the transplant and is looking for ways to improve her health and maintain her new organ's function. She is married and has two children. She works part-time as a receptionist and enjoys gardening in her free time. She has a smartphone with a data plan and is willing to receive text messages. She is willing to walk and sync a wearable device daily during the 2-week run-in period to determine her baseline [for Arms 2 & 3]. She is also willing to provide a final weight at the end of the study. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she is not currently enrolled in any financial incentive-based exercise program using a wearable device. She has no other medical conditions that would prohibit participation in a physical activity program and has no severe vision, hearing, or mobility impairment that would preclude her from participating. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to improve her overall health and well-being.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who underwent a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) 2 months ago for an acute coronary syndrome. He received a bare metal stent and was discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and clopidogrel. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently being treated with atorvastatin 40mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50mg daily, lisinopril 20mg daily, and metformin 1000mg twice daily. His blood pressure and blood glucose levels are well controlled. The patient reports occasional heartburn and has been taking over-the-counter omeprazole as needed. He has not experienced any gastrointestinal bleeding or adverse events related to DAPT. His most recent lipid panel showed LDL cholesterol level of 70 mg/dL. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

43 yo male patient with a history of HIV infection for the past 5 years presented to the clinic for routine follow-up. He has been on ART therapy since his diagnosis and has been compliant with his medications. His current regimen includes Tenofovir, Emtricitabine, and Efavirenz. His viral load has been undetectable for the past 2 years. He reports no major side effects from his current ART regimen but expresses concern about the possibility of long-term toxicity. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has no history of substance abuse. His family history is unremarkable. He works as a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. He reports no recent travel or exposure to sick individuals. He has no history of diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidemia. His BMI is 23. He is interested in learning more about the pharmacokinetics of his current ART regimen and is willing to participate in the Encore1-PK sub-study.

A 42-year-old male came to the clinic with a history of metastatic renal cell carcinoma. He was previously treated with sunitinib and pazopanib but stopped responding to treatment after initially responding. His most recent CT scan showed progression of his disease with new metastases in his lungs and bones. His performance status was assessed as 1 and his blood work showed high lactate dehydrogenase levels. He is not currently taking any medications and has no other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the study treatment.

The patient is a 56 year-old male who has been diagnosed with end-stage liver disease and has been listed for liver transplantation. He has a history of alcohol abuse and has been sober for the past 6 months. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume any recreational drugs. He lives alone and has a supportive family. He has been experiencing fatigue, jaundice, and abdominal swelling. His MELD score is 23 and he has been waiting for a donor liver for 3 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old man presenting with chronic diarrhea, weight loss, and abdominal pain. He has been experiencing daily, watery, and frequent diarrhea for the past 6 months, along with abdominal distention and discomfort. He has also noticed a significant decrease in his appetite and has unintentionally lost 10 pounds over the past few months. He reports experiencing fatigue and muscle weakness and has noticed a decrease in his ability to concentrate. He has had no recent travel history or changes in his diet. His lab work shows anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and low vitamin D levels. His fecal calprotectin level is high. He has no history of mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction or pregnancy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the cause of his symptoms and receive appropriate treatment.

Patient A is a 28-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the effects of amoxicillin on oral microflora. She is generally healthy and has not taken antibiotics within the previous three months. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not allergic to penicillin. She speaks Swedish and English fluently and is able to understand the study procedures. She is not currently participating in any other medical product studies and is not taking any medications, health food preparations or probiotics. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to contribute to the understanding of how antibiotics affect oral microflora.

This is a 45 year-old male with a history of mandibular fracture that required surgical intervention. The patient is generally healthy with no significant medical history or known allergies. The surgery is expected to last around 3 hours under general anesthesia. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and has complete medical records. The patient has no history of difficult intubation and has a BMI of 28 kg/m2. The patient does not have any contraindications for the use of NSAIDs and has no allergies to diclofenac sodium or metoclopramide. The patient does not have any major tranquilizer or opiate addiction and is mentally and physically cooperative.

This is a 57 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and atrial fibrillation for the past year. He has been on various antiarrhythmic drugs with suboptimal control of his symptoms. The patient is experiencing persistent atrial fibrillation for more than 7 days and is willing to undergo an ablation procedure. He has undergone cardioversion in the past and has failed to maintain sinus rhythm. The patient has no history of thyroid disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, or significant mitral valve disease. He has a left atrial anteroposterior diameter of 42mm and an ejection fraction of 55%. He is currently not participating in any other clinical studies and has the ability to provide informed consent.

35-year-old female sex worker in Kenya who is registered in the North Star Alliance electronic health record system. She has not been accessing HIV testing regularly despite recommendations to do so every 3 months. She owns a mobile phone and has a valid mobile phone number listed in the system. She has not had an HIV test in the past 3 months and has had fewer than four HIV tests recorded in the system in the past 12 months. She has no indication that she is HIV-positive.

35F with recent complaints of fatigue, weight gain, and constipation. She reports that she has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6-8 months. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. On examination, the patient is noted to have a BMI of 30 kg/m2, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She has no significant physical exam findings, except for a slightly enlarged thyroid gland. Her initial laboratory findings reveal a TSH level of 12 mU/L and a free T4 level of 0.8 ng/dL, consistent with hypothyroidism. She is diagnosed with primary hypothyroidism and started on levothyroxine (L-T4) therapy. She is eligible for the study and consents to participate.

Patient is a 7-year-old boy who is scheduled to undergo dental surgery for the extraction of multiple teeth. He has no significant past medical history and is generally healthy. He is classified as ASA 1 for this study. No pre-existing cardiac, renal, pulmonary or endocrine disease. The patient has no allergies to medications and no history of adverse reactions to anesthesia. The patient's guardian has provided informed consent for the patient's participation in the study.

A 11-year-old boy was referred to the hospital for further evaluation of headaches and episodes of dizziness. His medical history was unremarkable, and he had never undergone any surgeries. The physical examination did not reveal any abnormalities. However, his pediatrician recommended an MRI of his brain to rule out any underlying pathology. The MRI was scheduled to include contrast-enhanced imaging with Gadavist. The patient has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He is in good general health and has no history of renal disease.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing palpitations and occasional fainting episodes for the past few months. She has a history of atrial fibrillation and was previously treated with medication, but it was not effective in controlling her symptoms. Her cardiologist has recommended an insertable cardiac monitor to monitor her heart rhythm continuously. She meets the inclusion criteria for the Confirm Rx SMART Registry as she has an approved indication for continuous arrhythmia monitoring with an ICM, has a compatible mobile transmitter, and is able to provide informed consent and comply with the follow-up schedule. She has not had a previous ICM placement and is not implanted with or indicated for an implantable pacemaker, ICD, or CRT device. She is willing to participate in the study to assess the safety and performance of the Confirm Rx ICM system.

68-year-old male with a history of idiopathic Parkinson's disease diagnosed 3 years ago. The patient presents with moderate rigidity and bradykinesia, and has been experiencing mild to moderate musculoskeletal pain in the lower back and hips. He reports feeling anxious and depressed due to the limitations Parkinson's has placed on his daily activities. The patient has no cognitive impairment and scores above 24 on the Mini Mental Test. He is currently taking carbidopa-levodopa and has stable clinical status, with no recent changes in his medication regimen. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve his core stability, abdominal muscle function, and quality of life. He has no history of musculoskeletal or cognitive impairment that would affect the evaluation and treatment, making him eligible for participation in the study.

35-year-old male with a history of severe plaque-type psoriasis involving more than 10% of his body surface area, which has not responded well to topical treatments. The patient has no significant medical history, including renal, cardiovascular, respiratory, or neuropsychiatric illness, and no history of excessive alcohol consumption. He has not received any systemic treatment for psoriasis in the past 4 weeks or topical treatment in the past 2 weeks. His body mass index (BMI) is within normal range. He is willing to maintain contraception during and 3 months after completion/stopping of treatment as required for the study.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. She has had symptoms for about 3 years, including auditory hallucinations and delusions. She is currently on risperidone, which has helped to reduce her symptoms. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She reports being generally healthy, with no chronic medical conditions. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is a college student and reports that her symptoms have not interfered with her studies. She has no history of swallowing difficulties or gastrointestinal issues. She is not planning to undergo any medical procedures or imaging studies in the near future. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements of the ambulatory assessment period. She has a smartphone and is comfortable using the symptom rating app.

This is a 10 year old male with a past medical history of asthma, allergic rhinitis, and occasional bronchitis. He presented to the emergency department with cough, fever, and difficulty breathing. Chest x-ray showed bilateral infiltrates consistent with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). He was intubated and mechanically ventilated with moderate-severe ARDS for less than 48 hours per PALICC guidelines. He has met the inclusion criteria of the PROSpect clinical trial. He does not have perinatal related lung disease, congenital diaphragmatic hernia or congenital/acquired diaphragm paralysis, respiratory failure explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload, cyanotic heart disease, cardiomyopathy, unilateral lung disease, primary pulmonary hypertension, intubated for status asthmaticus, obstructive airway disease or active air leak, bronchiolitis obliterans, post hematopoietic stem cell transplant, post lung transplant, home ventilator or home oxygen dependent, neuromuscular respiratory failure, critical airway or anatomical obstruction of the lower airway, facial surgery or trauma in previous 2 weeks, head trauma or intracranial bleeding, unstable spine, femur or pelvic fractures, acute abdominal process/open abdomen, or known pregnancy. He has not been previously enrolled in the current study or any other interventional clinical trial not approved for co-enrollment.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She also has a history of depression, which has been treated with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) for several years. She is a non-smoker and has no significant family history of cancer. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her blood tests show a normal complete blood count and liver and kidney function. Her electrocardiogram (ECG) shows a normal QTc interval. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study. She has no significant gastrointestinal absorption impairment and can swallow pills. She has not received any prior systemic treatment or cytotoxic chemotherapy. She has not undergone any major surgery or radiation therapy in the past 4 weeks. She is willing to undergo blood, tumor tissue, and hair follicle sample collection for pharmacokinetic and correlative studies.

45-year-old female with a history of cervical cancer who had undergone pelvic radiotherapy 2 years ago. The patient has been experiencing pelvic pain, vaginal discharge, and spotting. A pelvic MRI showed a 4 cm pelvic recurrence of cervical cancer. The patient is not a surgical candidate due to significant comorbidities including hypertension and diabetes. The patient's Karnofsky performance status is 70. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial for high dose rate interstitial brachytherapy with three-dimensional printing template for recurrent gynecologic tumors. The patient has regular access to follow-up and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with localized prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 4+3=7. The cancer is confined to the prostate gland and has not spread to other parts of the body. The patient has undergone a multiparametric MRI that has identified a focal lesion in the prostate gland. The patient is interested in exploring treatment options that will not result in the removal of the entire prostate gland. The patient is in good health with no significant medical history and no prior surgeries. The patient's lab work is within normal limits. The patient is willing to undergo a MRI guided focal laser ablation procedure as part of this clinical trial.

This is a 35 year old male who developed symptoms of fever, cough and shortness of breath 5 days ago. He presented to the emergency room and was diagnosed with COVID-19 after a positive PCR test. He does not have any significant past medical history and has not been on any medications. He has mild symptoms and no evidence of hypoxia or respiratory distress at the time of presentation. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of zinc with chloroquine in the treatment of COVID-19. There are no contraindications or hypersensitivity to chloroquine.

A 55-year-old male with a history of Type II Diabetes for the past 15 years presents with chronic diabetic foot ulcers on the plantar surface of his left foot. The ulcers have been present for more than 4 weeks and are not larger than 15 cm2 in size. He has been receiving regular medical care for his diabetes and is compliant with his medications. His random blood sugar levels are usually under control with medications. The patient does not have any history of substance or alcohol abuse. He has not participated in any clinical trial for the past 60 days. The patient has no known allergy to primary or secondary dressing materials used in the trial. The patient has not undergone any wound treatments with enzymes, growth factors, living skin, dermal substitutes or other advanced biological therapies within the last 30 days. The patient has adequate circulation to his foot as documented by an ankle brachial index (ABI) of 0.80. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements and procedures involved.

The patient is a healthy male volunteer between 18-55 years of age, weighing at least 60 kg within 15% of their ideal weight. He has no significant medical history and has clinically normal laboratory profiles and ECGs. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs and has not consumed any drugs or substances known to be strong inhibitors or inducers of CYP enzymes within the specified time frame. His blood pressure is not less than 110/60 mmHg at screening or 100/55 mmHg before dosing, and his pulse rate is not lower than 55 b.p.m. at screening or 50 b.p.m. prior to dosing. He has not vomited, experienced diarrhea, or undergone vigorous and prolonged exercise (without drinking) within 24 hours prior to dosing, nor has he been on a special diet during the specified time frame. He has not participated in another clinical trial within 28 days prior to the first dose and voluntarily consents to participate in the study.

Seeking participants for a clinical trial of an electronic Patient Reported Outcome (ePRO) mobile application designed to improve care for older adults with complex care needs. Participants must be 60 years or older, have two or more chronic conditions, have had 10 or more visits to their primary health care provider in the last 12 months, and be thinking about or ready to make changes to support their self-management. Participants must also be physically capable of using a tablet or have a caregiver who can use the tablet on their behalf, and be able to read and write in English or have a caregiver who can do so on their behalf. The trial will take place at 6-16 Family Health Teams in Ontario and will utilize a stepped-wedge randomized method with an embedded case study of implementation at four sites. Participants will receive training on how to use the ePRO tool and will complete pre and post surveys every 3 months. Participants will also be asked to attend a minimum of two scheduled appointments with their provider during the study to track progress towards goals.

8-year-old boy with a history of asthma diagnosed at age 5 with symptoms of wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. He has been on regular inhaled corticosteroids for the past year with no change in dose in the preceding 4 weeks. The boy is a mouth breather and has difficulty breathing through his nose due to nasal congestion. He has been experiencing more frequent and severe asthma attacks and has missed several days of school due to his symptoms. The family is interested in exploring alternative therapies to help manage his asthma and improve his quality of life. The boy has no other respiratory diseases or conditions and has not had any respiratory infections in the past 15 days.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. He is concerned about the side effects of radiation therapy and would like to explore other treatment options. He is married and has two adult children. He is a retired school teacher who enjoys reading and taking walks in his neighborhood. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. His PSA level is 7.2 ng/mL, and his Gleason score is 7 (3+4). He underwent a biopsy that confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma of the prostate. He has no history of pelvic radiation, brachytherapy, cryosurgery, HIFU, TURP, or radical prostatectomy. He is aware of the potential benefits and risks of both SBRT and conventional radiation and is willing to be randomly assigned to either treatment option. He is in good physical condition, with an ECOG Performance Status of 1.

A 13-year-old Caucasian male adolescent presents with obesity and insulin resistance. He has a BMI-SDS of 2.7 and a HOMA-IR of 4.1. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of diabetes or endocrine disorders. He is of Dutch descent and speaks fluent Dutch. He has not used anti-hyperglycemic drugs or ritonavir, and is not on ACE inhibitors. He has no history of alcohol abuse and has normal renal and hepatic function. He and his parents have provided informed consent to participate in the study. He meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study on the effectiveness of metformin in reducing BMI and insulin resistance in obese children and adolescents.

A 12-year-old boy was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection two years ago and has been receiving highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) since then. He participated in a clinical trial using experimental therapies to treat HIV infection but has completed the trial. The patient is not currently participating in any ongoing long-term follow-up studies. His CD4 cell count and viral load data have been stable, and he has not experienced any significant opportunistic infections or adverse reactions to medications. The patient's parent is willing to provide signed informed consent for the minor's participation in the study.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who is preparing for pregnancy. She has a history of smoking for 5 years but quit smoking 3 years ago. During a routine check-up, her chest CT scan reveals a pure pulmonary ground glass nodule (GGO) with a diameter of 1.5 cm. Follow-up CT scan after 3 months confirms that the GGO remains. She has no history of any other medical issues and is not currently taking any medications. Her family history is negative for any lung diseases. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the nature of her GGO and receive evidence-based treatment if necessary.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who is concerned about the appearance of her glabellar frown lines. She has noticed that the lines have become more noticeable over time and they are starting to affect her confidence. She has no significant medical history and takes no medication regularly. The patient has not had any previous cosmetic treatments for her frown lines. On examination, the patient's glabellar frown lines are moderate to severe, with a severity score of 2 or 3 on a 4-point facial wrinkle scale. There is no marked facial asymmetry or ptosis of the eyelid or eyebrow. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the safety and efficacy of NT 201 (Xeomin®/Bocouture®) to OnabotulinumtoxinA (Vistabel®) for the treatment of her glabellar frown lines.

A 45-year-old woman with two children presents to the gynecologist's office with complaints of urinary incontinence for the past year. She experiences leakage of urine during activities such as coughing, laughing, and sneezing. She also experiences the urge to urinate frequently and sometimes cannot hold it. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of neurological disorders or gynecological cancer. She has not been pregnant in the last 3 years and is not currently pregnant. She understands the electrical stimulation procedure and is willing to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old female patient presented to the dental clinic with a complaint of bleeding gums and bad breath. She reports that she has noticed these symptoms for the past year but has not sought any treatment due to fear of dental procedures. She is a non-smoker and has no known history of chronic diseases. Upon examination, the dentist diagnosed her with advanced gum disease (periodontitis) with pockets measuring up to 7 mm. Her general oral hygiene is poor, and she has not visited a dentist in the past three years. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and to receive either conventional pocket debridement or ultrasonic debridement with diode laser. She is committed to attending follow-up review appointments and providing informed consent.

A 62-year-old male smoker presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the past month. Imaging studies reveal a mass in the right lung and a biopsy confirms a diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The patient has no other significant medical history and is not on any medications. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the benefit of large-panel next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis in companion diagnosis of advanced lung cancer patients. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and has no known exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IV colorectal cancer that has spread to his liver and lungs. He had a colonoscopy after experiencing rectal bleeding and was found to have a large tumor in his colon. He underwent surgery to remove the tumor and was started on FOLFOX chemotherapy. After several cycles of FOLFOX, he had a CT scan that showed progression of his disease with new liver and lung metastases. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has no significant medical history except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. His physical exam is unremarkable except for a palpable liver edge. His lab studies show a hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL, a white blood cell count of 7,500/mm3, a platelet count of 200,000/mm3, a creatinine level of 1.0 mg/dL, and a normal liver function test. He has no history of bleeding or clotting disorders. He has not had radiation therapy or other treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer, and he has no history of brain metastases or active infections. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for first-line treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty speaking for the past 2 years. Her voice sounds weak and breathy, particularly after voiceless consonants (such as "s" or "h"). The patient reports that her symptoms become worse with prolonged speaking or when she is anxious. She has not undergone any surgical treatment or botulinum toxin injections for her condition. She has no history of respiratory difficulties, laryngeal disease, or neuromuscular disorders. The patient is a non-smoker and does not have any history of major depression or psychiatric disorders. She is willing to undergo a botulinum toxin injection in the thyroarytenoid muscle. The patient will undergo a physical examination and a fiberoptic nasolaryngoscopy to confirm the diagnosis of abductor spasmodic dysphonia. She will also undergo an airway interruption test to measure phonation threshold pressure. Blinded measures of symptom frequency will be made before and after treatment to determine if symptoms are improved.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired school teacher who is concerned about her memory and cognitive abilities as she ages. She has noticed some forgetfulness and difficulty with word recall. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She is a native English speaker and has good hearing and vision. She has not had any head trauma or stroke in the past year and does not have any central nervous system disorders. She is willing to commit to the time requirements of the study and has no scheduled trips or absences for more than 1 week during the training. She has not used cholinesterase inhibitors and is not currently active in another clinical trial. Her Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score is 27. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her cognitive abilities and memory.

A 72-year-old man with Type 2 diabetes who has been taking insulin injections for the past 5 years is interested in participating in this clinical trial. He takes 2 injections of insulin per day and uses glargine insulin as his basal insulin. He has a stable insulin dose for the past 3 months. He has no allergies to tape or adhesive and has no visual or cognitive impairments. He is eager to try new technology to manage his diabetes and is willing to participate in the study. He has no prior experience with CGM sensors. He takes medication for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He is retired and lives with his wife. He has three adult children who live nearby.

A 68-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia was admitted to the medical ICU with severe pneumonia. The patient was intubated via orotracheal route and mechanically ventilated for 10 days. The patient has no history of ENT surgery or swallowing disorders. On day 10, the patient passed a spontaneous breathing trial and met the usual medical criteria for extubation. Before extubation, the patient will undergo a pre-extubation evaluation of the swallowing function and oropharyngeal motricity by a trained physiotherapist using a bedside scale based on 3 tests: cervical, oral, labial and lingual motricity, the gag reflex, and swallowing. The aim is to determine whether this scale is a reliable predictor of airway secretion-related extubation failure. The patient will be monitored for the ability to cough and swallow, secretion volume, and the need for suctioning immediately after extubation, then at 24, 48, and 72 hours. The final objective of this study is to lower the mortality related to extubation failure.

A 30-year-old healthy female came to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial for a sustained-release formulation of deferiprone. She has a BMI of 22 and has a weight of 60 kg. She currently does not smoke and has no significant medical history. She signed the informed consent form and has an acceptable alcohol and drug screen. She is sexually inactive and does not use any form of contraception. She has not taken any acetaminophen in the last 2 weeks and has not participated in any other investigational drug studies in the last 30 days. Her blood chemistry, hematology, and urinalysis values are within clinically acceptable limits. She has not donated blood in the last 30 days and is not currently breastfeeding. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 44-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with grade II essential hypertension. She has no history of cardiovascular disease but does have a family history of hypertension (her mother and two sisters). She is currently taking no medications and has no allergies to any medications. She works as a nurse and reports feeling stressed at work. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. Her blood pressure readings taken from two different visits are consistently around 160/95 mmHg. She has no symptoms related to hypertension such as headaches, dizziness, or chest pain. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her hypertension and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is an African American female adolescent aged 16, diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 6 months ago. She has been experiencing fatigue, joint pain, and rashes on her face and arms. She is currently taking prednisone and hydroxychloroquine. She attends high school and has been struggling to keep up with her schoolwork due to the symptoms of her disease. She lives with her mother and two younger siblings. Her mother works as a nurse and her father passed away from cancer when she was 12. She reports feeling isolated from her peers and worried about her future. She has not received any counseling or education on how to cope with her disease. She is interested in participating in the study to learn new coping skills and improve her quality of life.

A 42-year-old male veteran who served in the Iraq War, presented to the VA hospital with chronic lower back pain that has been present for the last 5 years. The patient describes the pain as a dull ache that radiates to the left leg, worsening with prolonged standing or sitting. He has been taking opioids for the last 2 years to manage the pain. He has a history of depression and anxiety, for which he takes sertraline and alprazolam. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. He is divorced and lives alone. He is currently unemployed and reports feeling isolated and hopeless. He reports that he is not able to do the things he enjoys, such as hiking and fishing, because of the pain. He is motivated to find a treatment that will help him manage the pain and improve his quality of life.

Dr. Maria is a 38-year-old physician working in a busy hospital. She is a mother of two children, ages 6 and 9, and lives with her husband who works in a different hospital. Dr. Maria is concerned about her risk of contracting COVID-19 while working in the emergency department and intensive care unit, as she is exposed to high-risk patients every day. She has no history of COVID-19 infection or any other significant medical conditions. She does not take any supplements or medications on a regular basis. Dr. Maria is interested in participating in the PREPARE-IT trial to reduce her risk of infection and subsequent morbidity and mortality associated with COVID-19.

This is a 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus who presented to the emergency department with fever, chills, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with sepsis secondary to pneumonia and admitted to Penn State Hershey Medical Center for further management. During his hospitalization, he will be enrolled in a clinical trial investigating the expression of GPR43 receptors in patients with sepsis. Blood samples will be collected at standardized time points throughout his illness and recovery to determine the expressed quantity of GP43. No interventions will be made in the standard clinical management of the patient. The patient has the ability to give informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

50-year-old Korean male with a history of pancreatic cancer diagnosed through histological examination. The patient has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy for the cancer. The patient will voluntarily participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form for compliance. The patient does not have a history of cancer in any other organs and falls within the age range of 20-80 years old.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from lower back pain for the past 6 months. She works as a nurse and spends most of her day standing and walking. The pain is dull and aching in nature and is located in the lower back region. The pain is constant and does not respond to any over-the-counter pain medications. The patient has not had any imaging studies done for her back pain. She has no history of spine surgery, trauma, or infection. The patient has no other significant medical history and has not been involved in any worker's compensation claims. The patient speaks and understands English fluently and is able to read and write. The patient is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve her back pain and feels that the physical therapy sessions may be beneficial for her.

A 25 year old healthy male with a BMI of 23 comes to the clinic for a research study on cardiac lipids. He has no known medical conditions and takes no medications. He has no history of claustrophobia or implanted devices. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given his written informed consent. He has been instructed to maintain his normal diet but to restrict physical activity for two days prior to the study. The patient is expected to attend five independent MR-examinations distributed over two days separated by one or two weeks, each including a measurement in the morning after an overnight fast and one in the afternoon (8 hours after breakfast, 3.5 hours after lunch). The patient is aware of the possible risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with the protocol.

A 58-year-old man with severe knee osteoarthritis is experiencing significant pain and difficulty with mobility. He has tried conservative treatments, such as physical therapy and pain medication, but has not seen significant improvement. He is a candidate for primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and is being considered for a clinical trial comparing TKA with and without a pneumatic thigh tourniquet. He has a hemoglobin level above 12 and does not have a history of diabetes or blood dyscrasia. He has a BMI within the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is open to either treatment option. The patient will be followed for two weeks after the surgery to assess parameters such as blood transfusion, blood drainage, postoperative wound hematoma, VAS for thigh pain, and clinical DVT.

An 80-year old retired school teacher was admitted to the geriatric ward of a hospital in Northumberland due to a fall resulting in a hip fracture. The patient has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis. She lives alone and has two grown children who live in another city. She reports having difficulty maintaining her oral hygiene due to her limited mobility and arthritis in her hands. She wears a partial denture but complains of discomfort while eating. She reports no dental pain or bleeding from gums. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She is able to give consent for the study. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs.

Pt is a 35yo M who was involved in a high-speed motor vehicle collision. Upon arrival in the trauma bay, he is found to be unresponsive with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 5. The patient's airway is secured with an esophageal tracheal combitube (ETC) by the pre-hospital team. He is hemodynamically unstable with a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg and a heart rate of 120 beats per minute. The primary survey shows no other immediate life-threatening injuries. The trauma team initiates aggressive resuscitation, including blood transfusion and administration of vasopressors. The decision is made to keep the ETC in place for the initial resuscitation. The patient is stabilized and transferred to the operating room for further management. The study team will document the timing and safety of the exchange of the ETC to an endotracheal tube during the primary survey and initial resuscitation of the trauma patient.

34-year-old male with a history of opioid abuse, currently seeking treatment at a community-based treatment center. He has been struggling with addiction for the past 5 years, and has been in and out of rehab programs. He has been sober for the past 2 months, but is struggling to stay motivated and maintain his abstinence. He has a supportive family, but feels isolated and anxious about the possibility of relapse. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could offer him additional support and motivation to remain sober. He is willing to be randomly assigned to either receive standard treatment or standard treatment plus contingency management, and is committed to attending all required appointments and follow-up assessments.

The patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man who has been recently diagnosed with elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) despite treatment with statins. He has a family history of heart disease and has been smoking for the past 20 years. He has been taking atorvastatin for the past 6 months, but his LDL-C levels have remained high. He has no history of drug abuse or unhealthy alcohol use. He has no history of severe hypertension, active liver disease, HIV infection, or other serious diseases. He has not experienced any major adverse cardiovascular events in the past 3 months. He has no allergies to the investigational compound or compound class. He is willing to use basic methods of contraception during the dosing of investigational drug.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few days. She visited the emergency department and was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis, which requires an emergent laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC). She is currently admitted to Kingston Health Sciences Centre in Ontario, Canada

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who was diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome at age 11. He is currently at Tanner stage 4 pubic hair and has never been exposed to exogenous androgens. He has a history of difficulty with concentration and short-term memory, but no other cognitive or physical impairments. He has no history of diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease. He is overweight, with a BMI of 29.2 kg/m2, and has a family history of heart disease and diabetes. He is able to participate in exercise studies and MRI procedures. He is willing and able to comply with study procedures and give informed written consent.

The patient is a 17-year-old boy diagnosed with autoimmune hemolytic anemia six months ago. He experiences episodes of fatigue, pale skin, and shortness of breath. His hemoglobin levels drop to 8 g/dL or lower during these episodes. He has been prescribed steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) but has not responded well to these treatments. He has been diagnosed as refractory to standard therapies for autoimmune cytopenias. He has no family history of autoimmune diseases. He is currently studying in high school and lives with his parents. He is interested in playing basketball and video games. He has a BMI of 22 with normal BP. There is nothing remarkable in his physical exam.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) after experiencing easy bruising, petechiae, and frequent nosebleeds. Her platelet count is < 30 × 109/L, and her physician has recommended treatment to increase her platelet count. She has never received any treatment for ITP before and has no other significant medical history. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of eltrombopag in combination with a short course of high-dose dexamethasone compared to dexamethasone monotherapy as first-line treatment for newly diagnosed ITP. She understands the study procedures, has signed the informed consent, and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old African American male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV. He is sexually active with other males and is fluent in English. He has at least one supportive contact in his network who is willing to attend face-to-face and telephone mini-booster sessions. The patient owns a cell phone that is not shared with anyone else and is willing to receive text-message mini-booster sessions. He is between the ages of 16-29 years old and is willing to attend intervention sessions. The patient plans to stay in the area for the next 12 months and is willing to return for assessments.

A 34-year-old man who is currently incarcerated in Connecticut is eligible for this clinical trial. He has a history of opioid dependence and has been confirmed to be HIV-infected. He is scheduled to be released from prison within the next 30 days and has reported drug- or sex-related HIV risk behavior prior to incarceration. He is willing to provide locator information and is able to read and understand the questionnaires and consent form. He has no untreated bipolar or psychotic disorder and does not have suicidal or homicidal ideation. He is interested in participating in the study and has no anticipated circumstances that would impede his participation.

The patient is a 50 year old Hispanic male who was recently diagnosed with stage IV colon cancer with metastasis to the liver and lungs. He has undergone surgery to remove the primary tumor and has completed six cycles of FOLFOX chemotherapy. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin daily. He works as a construction worker and is able to perform his job without difficulty. He has a wife and two children and enjoys spending time with his family. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore additional treatment options for his cancer.

A 52-year-old male patient with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who is currently undergoing dialysis for hyperphosphatemia is eligible for this clinical trial. He has been on hemodialysis for the past year and has been taking phosphate binders to control his serum phosphorus levels. He has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or disorders. He has a history of hypertension, and his current blood pressure is controlled with anti-hypertensive medication. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and agrees to use acceptable contraceptives throughout the study.

Patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of chronic cerebral ischemia (CCI) due to atherosclerosis and arterial hypertension. The patient has been on basic therapy for the past 3 months, but despite this, has been experiencing cognitive impairment. The patient has no other neurological diseases and no known allergies to the medication. The patient is willing to participate in an open-label, prospective, observational, multicenter study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Divaza in treating cognitive disorders associated with CCI. The patient will be prescribed to take 2 tablets of Divaza 3 times per day for 12 weeks. The patient will be assessed by neurologists using the MoCA scale before starting therapy with Divaza (visit 1) and 12 weeks after the treatment (visit 2). The patient has signed an informed consent form to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old male Chinese patient with a body mass index (BMI) of 35 kg/m2 and a history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) for 3 years visited the clinic for a consultation regarding metabolic surgery. He has failed to control his blood glucose levels despite oral hypoglycemic agents and lifestyle modifications. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has no major gastrointestinal surgery. He is willing to comply with the procedures required by the protocol and is able to comprehend and sign the study informed consent document. He has not participated in any other clinical study in the past 5 half-lives of an investigational drug.
