45 y/o female with history of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (stage IIB) diagnosed in [**2015**], treated with radiation therapy and achieved partial remission. Patient relapsed in [**2018**] and was treated with systemic chemotherapy, but achieved no remission. Currently has multiple skin lesions and is experiencing pruritus and pain. Patient has ECOG performance status of 1 and has no extra-dermal lesions. Lab results show ANC of 1.2x10^9/L, PLT of 70x10^9/L, and HGB of 100g/L. TSH is within normal range. Patient has no history of uncontrolled active infection, organ transplantation, or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Patient has no history of active autoimmune disease or mental illness. No history of interstitial lung disease, bleeding or thrombotic disease. Patient is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus for the past 7 years. She has been on oral antidiabetic agents, but her glycemic control has been poor with HbA1C levels consistently above 8%. She is able to self-measure her blood glucose levels and has been compliant with her medication regimen. She has no other significant medical history and is not on any other medications. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to potentially improve her glycemic control and gain more knowledge about insulin glargine.

A 40-year-old female with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis with hypertension and psoriatic arthritis confirmed by a rheumatologist. She has previously been treated with methotrexate and ciclosporin with unsatisfactory response and is now a candidate for adalimumab therapy. The patient has never been treated with adalimumab before and is willing to self-administer the injections or has a qualified person available to administer them. She is fluent in English and willing to give informed consent for data collection and forwarding to AbbVie. The patient is not currently participating in another study program or clinical trial and meets all local treatment recommendations for the use of bDMARD in psoriasis in her country. The patient has no contraindications as outlined in the latest version of the Humira syringe® Summary of Product Characteristics (SPC) and Humira Pen® SPC.

A 55-year-old man with no prior history of colorectal cancer came to the clinic for routine colonoscopy screening. He has no family history of colon cancer and no personal history of polyps or inflammatory bowel disease. He has never had a colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy before. He is not currently experiencing any gastrointestinal symptoms. He is not currently taking any medications and does not smoke. He is willing to participate in the study and be randomized to either the conventional colonoscopy or chromocolonoscopy group.

This is a 50 year old male with a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who was diagnosed with rectal cancer and received neo-adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NACRT) prior to surgery. He is scheduled to undergo elective rectal cancer resection and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of a 9 week exercise programme on fitness and quality of life in rectal cancer patients after NACRT and before surgery. The patient is able to perform exercise and has no contraindications on the American Thoracic Surgery CPET safety guidelines. He is willing to be randomly assigned to either the structured responsive endurance training programme (SRETP) group, where he will exercise 3 times a week for 9 weeks, or the control group that will receive exercise advice. The patient hopes to improve his physical fitness, change his behavior towards exercise, and improve his quality of life following NACRT. He understands that the results of this study will contribute to the design of a larger, multi-centre trial to determine whether a SRETP increases physical fitness with a reduction in adverse outcome following surgery.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who resides in a rural area in Guangdong province, China. He has been experiencing blurry vision and occasional headaches for the past few months. After visiting a local clinic, he was diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma and referred to a rural hospital for further evaluation and treatment. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is currently being managed with medication. He has no history of ocular surgery or laser treatment. Upon evaluation, his intraocular pressure was found to be above the normal range and his Cup to disk ratio was greater than 0.6 in the right eye, which is the study eye. He has good vision in both eyes, with a best corrected visual acuity of 20/20 in the left eye and 20/40 in the right eye. He has completed 8 years of formal education and works as a farmer. He lives approximately 30 km from the hospital and has no difficulty traveling there. He owns a mobile phone and can be reached at any time. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of selective laser trabeculoplasty versus trabeculoplasty in lowering intraocular pressure in patients with medically uncontrolled open-angle glaucoma in rural China.

A 35 year old man is scheduled for surgery to remove a benign tumor from his liver. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. Upon preoperative evaluation, he was found to have a Mallampati score of III, a thyromental distance of 5 cm, and a sternomental distance of 16 cm. His neck mobility was normal, and he had no history of difficult intubation. His vital signs were within normal limits, and his physical exam was unremarkable. He was consented to participate in this study, which aims to develop a predictive model for difficult intubation using multiple airway assessments.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with rectal cancer during a routine colonoscopy. Biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma, and subsequent imaging studies showed a T3B tumor with no evidence of distant metastasis. She underwent neoadjuvant chemoradiation therapy and is now being evaluated for clinical complete response (cCR) before undergoing surgery. On digital rectal examination, no mass or ulcer is found. Endoscopic examination showed no visible tumor, only a flat scar. MRI showed no residual tumor in the primary site or lymphatic drainage area. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is within normal limits. The patient has no history of other malignant tumors or serious medical conditions, and her hematopoietic functions of heart, lung, liver, kidney, and bone marrow are all adequate for surgery. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 4 weeks and is willing to sign informed consent for surgery.

This is a 55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and Atherosclerotic Renal Artery Stenosis (ARAS). She has been on two antihypertensive medications for the past year and has had difficulty controlling her blood pressure, with systolic blood pressure consistently above 155 mm Hg. She has no history of diabetes or other significant medical conditions. She has an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 50 ml/min/1.73 m2 calculated using the Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) formula. She is being considered for percutaneous transluminal angioplasty of the renal artery (PTRA) to improve blood flow to her kidneys. She has no contraindications to angiography or non-contrast magnetic resonance evaluations. She is able to comply with the protocol and is willing to provide written informed consent. She is a woman of childbearing age and has agreed to use two forms of contraception for 3 months following receipt of the study drug. She has not received an investigational drug within the past 30 days and has a serum sodium level above 135 mmol/L on the day of, and prior to, the PTRA. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 35-year-old female who is generally healthy and interested in alternative therapies for stress management. She has no history of neurological or mental disorders and has never received acupuncture treatment before. She is not claustrophobic and weighs 65 kg. She is interested in participating in this study to investigate the potential benefits of YNSA acupuncture on brain networks.

42F, generally healthy with no significant medical history, is interested in participating in a study evaluating the synergy of a dietary supplement with and without a probiotic on the human microbiome. She maintains a balanced diet and exercises regularly. She reports no history of lactose intolerance and is not currently taking any medications or supplements that may interfere with the study. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and clinic visits and provide required samples. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman scheduled to undergo transurethral resection of the bladder due to a history of recurrent bladder infections and hematuria. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She is able to communicate fluently in Spanish and has no visual problems that would limit her ability to read written material. She is eager to participate in the study to improve her understanding of the procedure and potential risks.

The patient is a 12-year-old Taiwanese boy who has been struggling with school for several years. He has difficulty paying attention in class and often interrupts the teacher and other students. His parents report that he is impulsive and has trouble controlling his behavior, especially when he is excited or upset. He also has trouble with organization and completing tasks. He has been diagnosed with ADHD by a board-certified child psychiatrist and is currently taking medication to manage his symptoms. The patient and his parents have consented to participate in a genetic study on ADHD and are willing to provide blood samples for analysis.

A 4-year-old child who attends a local kindergarten is being considered for participation in the Prevention Through Activity in Kindergarten Trial. The child is currently in good health, with no known medical conditions that would restrict physical activity. The parents are enthusiastic about the possibility of their child participating in an exercise intervention program in the kindergarten, and they are willing to participate in educational training to support their child's participation. The child has no history of significant developmental delays or motor skill difficulties. The family is committed to completing activity homework as part of the program. The child is within the age range of 43-67 months, and attends one of the kindergartens located in and around Wuerzburg in Germany that are included in the study.

A 25-year-old man has been diagnosed with primary effusion lymphoma (PEL) which has been confirmed by a pathology review at NIH. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the safety and efficacy of the chemotherapy drugs DA-EPOCH-RP in combination with Pomalidomide. He has not received any previous treatment with modified DA-EPOCH or Pomalidomide for KSHV-associated lymphoma. His HIV status is negative. He is in good health, with an ECOG performance status of 0. The patient has undergone blood tests and scans and is now eligible to participate in the trial. He must agree to use effective birth control methods and be willing to register into the mandatory POMALYST REMS program. The patient is willing to comply with all the requirements of the study and sign a written informed consent document. He has no history of malignant tumors other than KS or KSHV-associated MCD, and his renal and hepatic functions are within pre-specified limits. He has no ANC or platelet abnormalities, and no history of hypersensitivity reactions attributed to thalidomide, lenalidomide, or pomalidomide. His intercurrent illness is under control, and he does not have any other serious co-morbid conditions that would prohibit administration of planned chemotherapeutic intervention.

The patient is a 73-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) based on bone marrow aspiration and biopsy performed within 14 days prior to registration. The patient is not a candidate for standard AML cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens and has not received prior systemic chemotherapy for acute leukemia, except for hydroxyurea. The patient has a WBC count of 25,000/cmm within 1 day prior to registration, bilirubin level of 1.2 x Institutional Upper Limit of Normal (IULN), SGOT level of 2 x IULN, SGPT level of 2 x IULN, and serum creatinine level of 1.3 x IULN. The patient has completed all chemotherapy and radiotherapy for a prior malignancy 6 months prior to study registration, with no plan to begin therapy for the prior malignancy at the time of study registration. The patient is expected to require treatment with enzyme inducing antiepileptic drugs (EIAED) and is not eligible for this study. The patient must be informed of the investigational nature of this study and must sign and give written informed consent in accordance with institutional and federal guidelines.

The patient is a healthy adult between the ages of 19 and 50 with a weight between 55.0 kg and 90.0 kg and a body mass index (BMI) between 18.0 and 28.0. They do not have any clinically significant liver, kidney, nervous system, immune system, respiratory system, endocrine system, or blood or tumor disease, cardiovascular disease, or mental disease. They have not had gastrointestinal diseases that may affect the safety and pharmacokinetics evaluation of investigational drugs, and they have not had gastrointestinal surgery (except for simple appendic surgery and hernia surgery). They have not tested positive for Helicobacter pylori, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Their blood AST and ALT levels are within 1.5 times the upper limit of the normal range in screening tests, including additional tests.

The patient is a 75-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He presents with a 2-month history of a mass in the right side of his neck and difficulty swallowing. A biopsy of the mass shows squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. Physical examination reveals a 4 cm mass in the right tonsil area with no palpable lymphadenopathy. The patient has a KPS score of 70 and a creatinine clearance of 25 cc/min. Laboratory studies reveal WBC of 4800/ul, granulocyte of 2100/ul and a platelet count of 120,000/ul. Total bilirubin, AST and ALT are within normal limits. The patient gives documented informed consent to participate in this study. He has not received prior head and neck radiation or chemotherapy, and there is no evidence of distant metastases. The patient is eligible for this study due to his age and co-morbidities that preclude treatment with standard platinum-based chemotherapy.

A 52-year-old man diagnosed with sporadic ALS within the past 5 years presents with progressive weakness and muscle atrophy. He reports difficulty with activities of daily living such as getting dressed, grooming, and walking. He has lost approximately 10 pounds in the past 3 months. He is currently taking riluzole and has not experienced any adverse effects. He has no significant past medical history and has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to medications. Physical examination reveals marked atrophy of the upper and lower extremities, weakness in the hands and legs, and decreased deep tendon reflexes. His vital capacity is 60% of predicted. He expresses interest in participating in a clinical trial that may help slow the progression of his disease.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking medications for both conditions and has been managing them effectively. He has no known allergies to nuts or any other food items. He is interested in participating in the study to explore the potential benefits of consuming one ounce of walnuts per day for twelve weeks to improve his endothelial function. He is willing to travel to the study center at Brigham and Women's Hospital for the required visits and is able to provide informed consent and blood samples. He has not had any major surgical operations in the past three months and is not currently participating in any other clinical trials.

This is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic melanoma. She has been receiving treatment for her condition since 2012 and has been continuously enrolled in her healthcare plan for at least 6 months before and at least 6 weeks after the index date. She received at least 1 dose of study drug in CA209-067. The patient has been experiencing adverse events related to her treatment and is interested in participating in a study to assess and compare the costs of these adverse events with different follow-up frequencies.

The patient is a 62-year-old male smoker who has been diagnosed with peripheral artery disease (PAD) and has been experiencing pain in his left foot while walking. He is currently at Rutherford Stage 4-5 and has mild/moderate/severe calcium. He is taking aspirin and clopidogrel to manage his condition. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He has no allergies, and his family history is negative for any vascular diseases. The patient is able to understand the aim of the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the Clinical Investigation Plan. He is able to return for all required post-index procedure follow-up visits and acknowledges the associated risks and benefits of the clinical trial. The patient has a target lesion that is ≥ 2cm in length and the composite target lesion length is ≤ 27 cm. The patient has visible calcification in two views and the length of calcium ≥ 25% of total lesion length or ≥ 2 cm total length. The target vessel reconstitutes at or above the ankle with inline flow to at least one patent pedal vessel. The patient has not undergone prior vascular surgery of the index limb to treat atherosclerotic disease, and he is not scheduled to undergo a major amputation. The patient has not received stent placement in the target lesion and has not had unsuccessful guidewire crossing or subintimal guidewire placement. The patient does not have persistent inflow disease left untreated or unsuccessfully treated, and he has no non-ischemic ulcers or ulcers at or above the ankle.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking and recently diagnosed with unresectable stage III NSCLC. He completed concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation therapy and is now eligible to receive durvalumab. He is currently experiencing shortness of breath and coughing. He is willing and able to use the mobile application and connected devices and complete QoL assessments. He does not have any comorbidities that will prevent consistent and reliable measurement assessments with multiparametric mobile technology. He is not currently oxygen dependent and is not on other immunotherapy or systemic immunosuppressants. He has no active or prior autoimmune disease or history of immunodeficiency. He is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 50 year-old male who has been suffering from chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) for the past 5 years. He has a nasal polyp score of 6 out of a maximum score for both nostrils, with a score of 3 for each nostril. He has a SNOT-22 score of 25, indicating his symptoms have a considerable impact on his quality of life. He experiences nasal obstruction, congestion, and discharge, as well as facial pain and pressure. The patient's BMI is 26 kg/m2 and his total body weight is 75 kg. He has not used any investigational drugs or prohibited therapy for this study within the required timeframe. The patient has no history of severe life-threatening anaphylactic reactions and has not participated in any interventional study for the treatment of CRSwNP in the past 3 months. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or substance abuse.

67 year old man with occasional joint discomfort in both knees and hips, which has been affecting his mobility and physical performance. He has no history of joint surgery or degenerative osteoarthritis, and does not consume nutritional supplements containing antioxidant substances. He is not taking any medications for his joint discomfort, but occasionally takes over-the-counter analgesics for pain relief. He is generally healthy and has no known allergies to any components of the study product. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all well-controlled with medication. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet.

The patient is a 45-year-old man diagnosed with cervical dystonia for the past two years. He experiences involuntary muscle contractions in his neck and shoulders, which cause twisting and repetitive movements. He has been experiencing pain and discomfort due to his condition, which has negatively impacted his quality of life. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or head injury. He is not currently taking any medications for cervical dystonia treatment. He does not have severe head tremors. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help advance research and improve the management of cervical dystonia.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 12 months. He works as a construction worker and his job requires him to lift heavy objects frequently. His pain is located in the lower back region and he rates it as an 8 out of 10 on the pain scale. He has tried various treatments for his back pain such as physical therapy, chiropractic care, and pain medication but has not experienced significant relief. He does not have a history of hernia or any neurologic disorders. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his chronic low back pain.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with stage 4 chronic kidney disease. He was diagnosed with hypertension 10 years ago and has been taking medication regularly to control his blood pressure. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works in an office where he sits for most of the day. He has no history of allergies and takes only over-the-counter pain medication occasionally. He lives with his wife and two children. His recent lab tests show that his serum magnesium levels are within the normal range, but he has a slightly elevated serum phosphate level. He has no history of diabetes or cancer. He is not currently taking any magnesium-containing supplements or calcimimetics. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 28-year-old male patient was involved in a car accident and sustained a traumatic spinal cord injury at the level of C6. The patient is currently in the early phases of recovery, which is expected to last for the next six months. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is currently under control with medication. He does not have any history of autonomic dysreflexia or pressure ulcers. The patient does not have a cardiac pacemaker and does not have any skin rashes. The patient is motivated to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to commit to the required therapy program. The patient is currently unable to flex or extend his fingers or thumb and has weak wrist extension. He is interested in improving his grasping function and restoring as much independence as possible.

The patient is a 35-year-old African American woman who has been smoking for 10 years. She currently smokes an average of 15 non-menthol cigarettes per day and has a screening saliva cotinine level of 220 ng/ml. She has no history of cardiac disease, asthma or severe allergic rhinitis, and her blood pressure is normal. She is in good health and is not taking any regular medication. She has access to a refrigerator to store saliva specimens collected at home. Her body mass index (BMI) is 29. She denies any current illicit drug use and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is fluent in English and able to read and fill out forms. She has not had any recent "no shows" for screening or study visits and is willing to comply with study procedures. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare low yield cigarettes in African Americans vs. Whites.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 2 years ago. He is currently taking levodopa immediate release and benserazide three times daily, and his symptoms are generally well controlled, though he experiences predictable peak dose dyskinesia of at least mild severity and causing at least mild disability. He is able to perform most activities of daily living independently, but his dyskinesia interferes with his work as a mechanic. He has no history of neurosurgical procedures for Parkinson's disease, and he has not taken any medications contraindicated by the study protocol within the past 8 weeks. He has experienced no significant changes in his medication regimen or other medical conditions for at least 4 weeks prior to screening. He is able to complete the required home diary and has completed two consecutive 24-hour periods with no more than 4 missing periods per 24 hours in the diary, completed at the end of the screening period, in the 48 hours prior to Day 1. He has no history of major psychiatric disease or impulse control disorder, and no history of drug and/or alcohol abuse within 12 months prior to screening. His cognitive function is intact, with a MMSE score of 29. He has no contraindications or allergies/sensitivities to the study drug or its excipients. He is willing and able to follow the contraceptive guidance during the treatment period if he is a WOCBP. He has provided written informed consent before the study screening procedures commencing.

The patient is a 45 year old man who visited the endocrinology department for evaluation of his acromegaly symptoms. He reported a gradual increase in the size of his hands and feet, as well as a change in his facial features over the past few years. He has a history of hypertension that is currently managed with medication. He works as a construction worker and is a non-smoker. He reports occasional alcohol consumption. On physical examination, he is noted to have enlarged hands and feet, a prominent forehead, and a prognathic jaw. His nasal examination is normal. He has no previous history of nasal surgery or any nasal problems. He is interested in participating in the study to help with the research related to his condition.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who needs to undergo surgery for a left total hip arthroplasty. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has never undergone surgery before and is slightly anxious about the procedure. She is able to read and understand the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no known history of alcohol or illicit drug use and has not experienced any head traumas or cerebrovascular accidents in the last 10 years. She has no major psychiatric conditions or severe visual or auditory disorders. She is able to comprehend and perform the study assessments, according to the investigator's judgment.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of stage IV lung cancer that has metastasized to his liver and bones. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy, but the tumors have continued to grow. His performance status is 1, and he is able to perform most activities of daily living with some limitations. His most recent lab results showed normal blood counts, liver function tests, and renal function tests. His ECG showed a QTc interval of 420 msec. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to stay in the clinic for at least 4 days.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) six months ago. She is currently being treated with oral medications for PAH and is stable with no recent hospitalizations. She complains of dyspnea on exertion and decreased exercise capacity. She is able to perform activities of daily living but experiences shortness of breath with exertion. She has been referred to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new smartphone app for the 6 minute walk test (6MWT). She owns an iPhone and is able to use it. She is willing to participate and give informed consent for the study. She is not on long-term oxygen therapy and does not have any cognitive impairments or rheumatological diseases that limit the measurement of finger oxygen saturations. She is classified as PAH group 1 and is able to undertake the 6MWT off-oxygen. She is not pregnant.

The patient is a 26-year-old female who has never received the pneumococcal vaccine. She has no history of serious chronic disorders and is in good overall health. She works as a teacher and has not travelled outside of the country in the last year. She is sexually active and currently using hormonal birth control. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical knowledge and is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception during the study period.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer that has metastasized to multiple organs. She has a performance status of 1 according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Her leukocyte count is within the normal range, but her platelet count is below 100,000/mm3. Her hemoglobin level is 10.2 g/dL. Her total bilirubin level is 0.8 mg/dL, and her AST (GOT) and AST (GPT) levels are both within the normal range. Her BUN level is 20 mg/dL, and her creatinine level is 0.9 mg/dL. Her 24-hour creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min. She has no synchronous multiple cancers or infections, and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of ischemic cardiac diseases or active gastrointestinal ulcers. She has no severe drug allergies or nerve disorders. She has not been treated with other pyrimidine fluoride antineoplastic agents or flucytosine. She is willing to provide written informed consent to enter this study.

7-year-old female with mild to moderate plaque psoriasis presents for a clinical trial that will evaluate the safety and efficacy of calcitriol 3 mcg/g ointment. The patient has been diagnosed with plaque psoriasis for the past 3 years, with lesions primarily on the elbows, knees, and scalp. The patient has not responded well to previous treatments including topical corticosteroids and emollients. The patient has no history of hypercalcemia, kidney stones, vitamin D deficiency, or other concomitant dermatological diseases. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history.

A 65-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of progressive knee pain and stiffness, which has significantly affected his mobility and daily activities. He reports the pain to be constant, aching, and sometimes sharp, with occasional swelling of the knee joint. He has no history of trauma to the knee, and the pain is not relieved with over-the-counter pain medications. On physical examination, there is tenderness and swelling over the knee joint, with a limited range of motion. There is no warmth or erythema noted over the joint. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. X-ray of the knee shows mild osteoarthritis. The synovial fluid analysis confirms the presence of hydarthrosis, and the patient is diagnosed with painful knee osteoarthritis. He is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of painful osteoarthritis and hydarthrosis.

This is a 14-year-old female with a history of recurrent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding for the past year. She was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis based on colonoscopy findings and histological examination of colonic mucosal biopsies. Her disease activity is moderate according to the ImproveCareNow (ICN) Physician Global Assessment (PGA). She has no history of previous bowel resection or other serious medical conditions. She is not pregnant and does not have inadequate liver or renal function. She is not on any prescription medication for active infectious disease and does not have a history of drug/alcohol abuse. She is willing to participate in clinical trials and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old Hispanic woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, diagnosed 5 years ago. She has been receiving treatment with metformin and sitagliptin, but her hemoglobin A1C levels have been difficult to control. Her BMI is 32, and she is a non-smoker with no history of alcohol abuse. She has no history of fractures or any other significant medical problems, and she has not been taking any medications that could affect bone metabolism. She is not currently taking any vitamin D or calcium supplements. The patient has been started on pioglitazone, a thiazolidinedione, as an add-on therapy to her current diabetic medications. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. She has no history of immobilization or bed rest, and her GFR is within normal limits. She has not undergone pancreatectomy or has any malabsorption syndromes. She is not in perimenopause or menopause.

A 50-year-old man was diagnosed with rectal cancer during a routine colonoscopy screening. His past medical history is significant for high blood pressure, which is well-controlled on medication. He has no known drug allergies and has never smoked. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a supportive spouse who will help him during his treatment. He has undergone some diagnostic tests, including a CT scan of the chest and abdomen, and MRI of the pelvis, which showed a T3 CRM-negative rectal cancer. He has not received any treatment for his cancer yet, and his surgeon has recommended that he undergo neoadjuvant chemotherapy before surgery. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of two neoadjuvant chemotherapy regimens.

A 67-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents to the clinic for routine follow-up. He reports feeling well and denies any recent symptoms. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg and his blood glucose is within normal limits. His physical exam is unremarkable. However, given his age and risk factors for stroke, he is approached about participating in a clinical trial investigating the yield of AF screening with a continuous ECG monitor (ECG247). The study aims to estimate the prevalence of silent AF and prevent stroke in the future. The patient is interested in participating and provides informed written consent for the study. He is eligible based on his age and risk factors for stroke, and he has no history of chronic AF or any inability to cooperate.

55-year-old male patient diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck presented to the oncology clinic for follow-up. The patient has been undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy for the past 4 weeks at Fox Chase Cancer Center. He reports experiencing difficulty swallowing, mouth sores, and significant weight loss. The patient is currently taking pain medication for his symptoms. He is married and lives with his wife and two children. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He does not have a history of psychiatric disorders or other co-morbidities. The patient speaks and reads English fluently. He is interested in participating in the study to receive additional support for symptom management and coping during his cancer treatment.

As this clinical trial is not focused on recruiting patients, there is no need for a patient description. Instead, the trial is focused on evaluating the composition of human milk and health outcomes in children, using data and samples collected from a larger birth cohort study. The inclusion criteria is limited to human milk samples from mothers and health outcomes of children from the same cohort study, with data collected from birth through two years of age.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU due to septic shock secondary to pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no history of diabetes. On admission, his blood glucose level was 140 mg/dL. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and vasopressors. Due to his critical condition, he required mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours and was started on a vasoactive infusion of norepinephrine. His blood glucose levels were monitored closely, and he required insulin therapy to maintain blood glucose levels between 70-110 mg/dL. He did not experience any low blood sugar episodes during the initial phase of insulin therapy. The patient is eligible for inclusion in the clinical trial to test the feasibility of using a computerized decision support tool for blood glucose management in critically ill patients.

54-year-old female admitted to the internal ward for management of community-acquired pneumonia. The patient has a history of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She denies any history of smoking, alcohol, or drug abuse. The patient is alert and oriented, and vital signs are stable. The patient consents to participate in the study and is willing to wear the VSMS device on her chest for the duration of her hospitalization. The patient has no history of skin irritation or any other skin condition that might affect the adherence of the device. The patient is classified as ASA physical status classification 2.

Maggie is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe back pain for the past several months. She has tried various medications and physical therapy, but her pain has not improved. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has a BMI of 28 Kg/m-2. She has been diagnosed with a herniated disc in her lumbar spine and has been scheduled to undergo thoracic or lumbar spinal surgery. The surgeon has informed her that during the surgery, she will undergo TcMEP monitoring to help prevent damage to her spinal cord. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 25-year old woman who lives in a low-income area in England is currently pregnant with her first child. She works as a part-time cashier and her partner is a full-time warehouse worker. They rent a small apartment and struggle to make ends meet. The patient has a history of anxiety and depression and is currently on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). She speaks English fluently and is able to understand and provide informed consent. She has not received any previous maternity care and was referred to the MCC caseloading team by her general practitioner. She is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and is excited about having her first baby, but also feels anxious about the process of childbirth and being a new mother.

50 yo F with recently diagnosed stage II breast cancer, positive axillary lymph nodes, and no prior chemotherapy or hormonal therapy. Patient underwent lumpectomy and axillary dissection with clear margins and is now being referred for consideration for adjuvant chemotherapy. Patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is not currently taking any medications and has no known drug allergies. Patient is premenopausal and reports regular menses. She is willing to use effective barrier contraception during the study period. Patient has no history of cardiac disease or significant cardiovascular risk factors. All laboratory values are within normal limits. Patient is willing and able to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 60 year old male of Korean descent who presents with moderate claudication in his left leg. He is retired and enjoys playing golf with friends. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are currently well-controlled with medication. He has never smoked and does not drink alcohol. He underwent an angiogram that showed a 70% stenosis in his left iliac artery. His ABI is 0.8, confirming the diagnosis of peripheral artery disease. The patient is interested in participating in the K-EPIC registry to potentially improve his quality of life and prevent further progression of his disease. He understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to sign informed consent.

The patient is a 20-year-old female college student who has been experiencing symptoms of depression including persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, and feelings of worthlessness. She scored a 16 on the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), indicating moderate depression. She has access to the internet and is fluent in English. She is a first-year student at a participating institution and is willing to provide consent to participate in the study. She has not received any other treatment for her depression.

A 28-year-old man with a history of cocaine dependence came to the clinic seeking treatment. He has been using cocaine heavily for the past year and has experienced several negative consequences, including job loss, difficulty maintaining relationships, and financial problems. He reports using crack cocaine daily and has tried to stop using on his own but has been unsuccessful. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for treatment options. He has no history of seizures or psychiatric disorders requiring medication therapy. He is not pregnant or nursing and does not have a dependence on alcohol, benzodiazepines, or other sedative/hypnotics. He reports no history of acute hepatitis or other medical conditions that would deem participation in the study unsafe. He agrees to the conditions of the study and signs the informed consent form.

56 year old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for 8 years, currently taking metformin for the last 6 months. He has a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and his HbA1c is 8.5%. He has never been treated with insulin or DPP-4 inhibitors. He has a history of hypertension, which is currently well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies or intolerances to trial products or related products. He has never been treated with thiazolidinedione (TZD) or GLP-1 analogues within the last 2 months. He has no history of cardiovascular disease in the last 12 months. He has normal liver and renal function. He has mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, which is currently stable. He is not a female of childbearing potential and has no known or suspected abuse of alcohol, narcotics or illicit substances. He is able and willing to take one subcutaneous injection every day and perform mandatory SMPG measurements.

The patient is a 35-year-old male from China who has been diagnosed with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. He has never received treatment for his condition and is currently experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional abdominal discomfort. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and he does not smoke or drink alcohol. His family history is negative for liver disease. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing two antiviral medications for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-negative HBV infection. The patient is not currently breastfeeding and is using effective contraception. His renal function is normal, and he has no history of hepatocellular carcinoma or clinical hepatic decompensation. The patient is willing to comply with the dosing requirements of the study and sign a written informed consent form.

A 53-year-old Caucasian man who has been a heavy drinker for the past 20 years presents with elevated liver enzymes. He consumes at least 6 to 8 beers per day and has a history of binge drinking on weekends. He complains of abdominal pain, bloating, and fatigue. He has lost 10 pounds in the past month without any significant changes in his diet or exercise routine. He has a family history of liver disease, with his father and grandfather both dying of cirrhosis. He has never been diagnosed with any chronic liver disease, and this is his first time seeking medical attention for his symptoms. He does not have any other significant medical history and does not take any medications regularly. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo genetic testing. His ethnicity is Caucasian.

50-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) requiring hemodialysis for the past 6 months. The patient has been on intravenous vitamin D therapy (paricalcitol or doxercalciferol) for the past 3 months, with a historical biointact parathyroid hormone (biPTH) level of 300 pg/ml and corrected serum calcium of 9.2 mg/dl. The patient's biPTH level at screening is 350 pg/ml with a corrected serum calcium level of 9.1 mg/dl. The patient is experiencing symptoms of secondary hyperparathyroidism (HPT) such as bone pain and fatigue. The patient is willing to participate in a trial that compares the effectiveness of Sensipar® and low dose vitamin D or escalating doses of vitamin D alone in achieving the National Kidney Foundation-Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (NKF-K/DOQI) treatment targets for both biPTH and calcium-phosphorus (Ca x P) product. The patient has not undergone parathyroidectomy in the past 3 months, has no current gastrointestinal disorder that may affect medication absorption, and is willing to use highly effective contraceptive measures throughout the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with asthma. She reports experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness, especially during physical activity. She has been using an albuterol inhaler as needed for symptom relief but has not been on any maintenance medications for her asthma. The patient has a history of seasonal allergies and has been using over-the-counter antihistamines for symptom relief. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She has no known cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, hematological, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, metabolic, endocrine, neurological or psychiatric diseases. She has no known allergies to the active substances or lactose. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is using proper contraception. She has not donated blood or lost a significant amount of blood within the last 90 days and has not participated in another investigational medicinal product trial within the last 90 days. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old male presents with a history of locally advanced head and neck cancer that has spread to the lungs. The patient has received standard treatment including radiation therapy and chemotherapy but has experienced relapse. The patient is experiencing difficulty breathing, fatigue, and weight loss. The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG PS) is 1. The patient has measurable disease based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. The patient has adequate organ function and is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with the protocol. The patient has not been diagnosed with any active second malignancies other than non-melanoma skin cancers. The patient has no history of interstitial lung disease or severe pulmonary compromise. The patient has not received prior immunotherapy with a Grade 3 or higher or any unresolved ≥Grade 2 immune-related adverse event.

30 year old female with a history of Crohn's disease diagnosed 5 years ago. The patient has had multiple flares requiring hospitalization, and has failed multiple medical therapies including steroids, biologics and immunomodulators. She has been recommended to undergo an ileocolic resection for symptomatic management of the disease. She has been informed of the clinical trial and has expressed interest in participating. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study. She does not require formation of a stoma at the time of surgical resection and has more than 200cm of small bowel as assessed intra-operatively. The patient is within the age range of 16 to 80 years.

A 52-year-old woman presents with a history of papillary thyroid cancer that was diagnosed 5 years ago. She had undergone total thyroidectomy and radioiodine ablation therapy but now she has developed metastatic disease to the lungs and bones. She has received chemotherapy previously but the disease continued to progress. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, except for hypertension which is well-controlled with medications. She has no known allergies and is not taking any other medications. She reports occasional fatigue and shortness of breath, but is able to perform her activities of daily living independently. In the physical exam, there is no evidence of palpable lymphadenopathy or thyroid mass. Her vital signs are stable. Her laboratory values including complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and thyroid function tests are within normal limits. A CT scan of the neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis shows multiple pulmonary nodules and bone metastases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her condition.

The patient is a Chinese individual who has been diagnosed with bacterial conjunctivitis based on clinical observation. They are over 18 years of age, able to understand and sign the approved informed consent, and willing to complete all required study procedures and visits. They do not have any systemic or ocular disease or disorder that would negatively affect the conduct or outcome of the study, and have not had signs and symptoms of bacterial conjunctivitis for longer than 4 days prior to screening. They are not pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy, and do not wear contact lenses. They also have vision correctable to 0.6 logMAR or better in both eyes.

The patient is a 65 year old male who was recently diagnosed with Parkinson's disease after experiencing tremors and difficulty with movement for the past year. He is currently taking levodopa and a decarboxylase inhibitor to manage his symptoms, but has been experiencing motor fluctuations characterized as end-of-dose phenomena and "wearing-off" effects. He is able to keep an accurate patient diary of his "on" and "off" periods during the day. He is retired and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren and gardening. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to manage it. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the efficacy and safety of Pramipexole tablets compared to Bromocriptine tablets in managing his Parkinson's disease symptoms.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 3 years ago. She has been taking oral hypoglycemic agents for the past 2 years to control her blood glucose levels. She has a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and her blood pressure is well controlled with medication. She exercises for 30 minutes a day, 3 times a week, and follows a healthy diet. She has no history of diabetic complications. Her latest HbA1c level was 8.5% and fasting blood glucose level was 220 mg/dL. She is not on any other medication currently except for her anti-diabetic medication. She has no known allergies and is in good health overall. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of TA-7284 for the treatment of type 2 diabetes.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with severe COPD (FEV1<50%) according to the GOLD guidelines. She has a history of smoking and her current smoking status is unknown. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for the last 3 years. She has been hospitalized twice in the last year due to exacerbations of her COPD. She is currently on inhaled bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids as well as oxygen therapy. She has no significant comorbidities and is able to perform activities of daily living with some difficulty. She is interested in participating in a coaching program to increase her daily physical activity level and improve her quality of life. She is able to provide informed consent and is not currently attending a pulmonary rehabilitation program.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has had a history of hepatitis C for the last 10 years. He was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis three years ago and has been undergoing regular check-ups. In his last check-up, a liver CT scan revealed the presence of a 3 cm hepatic nodule, which was confirmed to be HCC by biopsy. The patient has no other known medical conditions and is currently taking antiviral medication for his hepatitis C. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore additional treatment options and to potentially modify his current treatment plan.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who suffered a minor ischemic stroke 2 weeks ago. She has a medical history of hypertension and high cholesterol. She is able to walk independently but experiences fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion. She has no history of heart disease, lung disease, or peripheral vascular disease. She is mentally competent and able to provide informed consent. She has no other severe uncontrolled medical problems or neurological diseases. She is interested in participating in an exercise program to improve her mobility and endurance.

John is a 27-year-old male who suffered a spinal cord injury in a car accident two years ago. The injury resulted in a loss of sensation and movement in his legs. He has been using a wheelchair since the accident. John has no history of seizures, loss of consciousness, hypertension, psychosis, heart conditions, or allergies to any of the drugs. He is not currently taking any medications. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the mechanisms responsible for plasticity of the motor system. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocols. John is willing to undergo transcranial magnetic stimulation and take the drugs administered in the study to determine the mechanisms behind plastic changes in his brain. He is excited to contribute to the research and hopeful that the study may lead to new treatments for spinal cord injury.

The patient is a 65-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease and a previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) procedure with stent placement. He has been experiencing recurrent chest pain and was found to have a longer lesion in his left anterior descending artery during coronary angiography. The lesion is between 18mm to 40mm in length with a diameter stenosis greater than 50%. The patient is stable and an acceptable candidate for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and understands the requirements and treatment procedures. The patient has not been previously treated with any anti-restenotic drug-coated or drug-eluting coronary stent and does not have any known sensitivity to paclitaxel. He meets the angiographic inclusion criteria for the study and has a target lesion that is completely coverable by up to 2 study stents. The patient does not have any of the general exclusion criteria for the trial and is not currently participating in another investigational drug or device study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with glaucoma. He has a family history of the disease, and his father has been living with glaucoma for the past 10 years. He is currently experiencing mild to moderate vision loss in his peripheral vision and has been prescribed topical medication to lower the intraocular pressure. He has good visual acuity and no other ocular abnormalities. He wears glasses for mild myopia and astigmatism. He has no other significant medical history, and he does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. He works as a computer programmer and spends a lot of time in front of a computer screen. He is willing to make the required visits for the study and is tolerant of dilating drops. He understands the importance of early treatment and monitoring of his glaucoma to prevent further vision loss.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male has been recently diagnosed with stage III colorectal cancer. He underwent surgery and is scheduled to start chemotherapy in the next few weeks. He is currently experiencing mild fatigue and has lost some weight. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. His blood pressure is currently well controlled. He has no history of cardiac or respiratory illnesses. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is married and has two children. He is an accountant and works full-time. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may reduce the side effects of chemotherapy. His ECOG performance status is 1.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for the past 2 months. He has lost some weight without trying and feels fatigued. He has a past medical history of hypertension and takes lisinopril. His BMI is 26, BP: 130/85, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for hemoglobin: 11.8g/dL, WBC: 7.5 x 10^3/uL, Platelets: 240 x 10^3/uL, Creatinine: 1.2mg/dL, Bilirubin: 1.7mg/dL, AST: 30U/L, ALT: 25U/L. He underwent a CT scan which showed a locally advanced pancreatic mass, and imaging confirms no distant metastasis. He has been declined for surgery based on the designation of LAPC. He provided informed written consent and is willing to receive standard multimodality therapy at Mayo Clinic, Rochester.

A 27-year-old female office worker living in Smithers, British Columbia is interested in participating in the clinical trial for evaluating the effect of HEPA air filters on subclinical markers of cardiovascular health. She lives in a non-smoking household with her husband and two cats. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or any other major health concerns. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. Her home is equipped with a wood stove and she is concerned about the potential effects of woodsmoke on her health. She is not currently taking any medications and has never participated in a clinical trial before.

A 35-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with pre-diabetes came to the clinic seeking to participate in a clinical trial. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension that was diagnosed 3 years ago. Her current medications include hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Her last menstrual period was two months ago. She has no history of gastrointestinal symptoms and her current lifestyle is regular. The patient is willing to give informed consent and is available for the entire study period of 8 weeks. She is able to keep a 24-hour dietary record a day prior to each visit. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the potential effects of D-allulose (psicose) with sucrose beverage on glucose tolerance and insulin levels.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing memory problems for the past year. She has difficulty remembering recent events, appointments, and conversations. Her family has noticed that she is becoming increasingly forgetful and disoriented. Her doctor has diagnosed her with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease based on her medical history and cognitive testing. She has recently had a CT scan that ruled out other causes of dementia. She lives at home with her husband, who acts as her caregiver. She has no history of B12 or folate deficiency, chronic hepatic disease, hematologic/oncologic disorders, or recent myocardial infarction. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially improve her memory and cognitive function. She is willing to have 12 weeks of administration of ST101, or placebo, and is looking forward to seeing if this new treatment can help her manage her Alzheimer's disease.

A 45-year-old woman who is cognitively normal without any history of sleep disorders is sought for a clinical trial. She will undergo initial screening that includes PET imaging or CSF amyloid-beta-42 concentration to ensure she is negative for amyloid deposition. She is expected to sleep an average of 6-10 hours per night. She should not have any neurologic injuries or tremors in the non-dominant upper extremity, or any history of sleepwalking or sleep parasomnia. She should not have any clinical dementia rating (CDR) greater than 0 or any diagnosis and treatment of stroke, myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, congestive heart failure, asthma, COPD, bipolar disorder, major depression, schizophrenia, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, liver disease, or kidney disease resulting in renal impairment. She should not be currently taking blood thinner medications or sedative-hypnotic medications such as benzodiazepines, and should not have a BMI greater than 40 or any contraindication to lumbar puncture. She should not be pregnant, using tobacco or alcohol at bedtime, or have a sleep schedule outside the range of bedtime: 8pm-12am and waketime 4am-8am. She should not have difficulty sleeping in an unfamiliar environment and should not have participated in another investigational medicinal product or investigational device within the last 30 days.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has a BMI of 27.5 kg/m² and is not currently taking any antibiotics, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressants. He has no history of cognitive difficulties or inflammatory digestive pathology. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the written consent before enrollment. He has no previous history of ORL cancer treated by radiotherapy or surgery, and is not currently taking any experimental medication or participating in another clinical therapeutic study. He is able to follow the requirements of the study and has not been deprived of his rights by administrative or judicial decision.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with head and neck cancer. She is scheduled to undergo radiation therapy to the affected area. She reports a history of heavy smoking and social drinking. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is married and works as a teacher. She reports a decreased appetite and weight loss since her diagnosis. She complains of dry mouth and difficulty swallowing. She is an alert and cooperative woman who does not have any signs of cognitive impairment. She does not have any known allergies.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a lump in her left breast that she noticed during her monthly self-examination. She went to her primary care physician, who referred her to a breast specialist. Biopsy results confirmed the presence of invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR positive and HER2 negative. The tumor measures 15mm on ultrasound and is well-defined. There is no evidence of cancer in the opposite breast, and a breast MRI confirms this. The patient has no history of breast cancer or other cancers, and there are no other significant medical conditions. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is within the age range of 18 to 80. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore local treatment by thermic destruction of primitive breast cancer.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with asthma since the age of 3. She has experienced several attacks in the past, often triggered by allergies or respiratory infections. Her current symptoms include wheezing and shortness of breath. Her parents are concerned about her condition and are looking for a way to better manage her asthma. They have agreed to participate in a clinical trial that uses a digital stethoscope to record and analyze her breathing sounds during an acute exacerbation and after treatment with bronchodilators. The study will also involve recording her respiratory function using a lung function test. The goal of the study is to develop an artificial intelligence algorithm that can accurately diagnose and classify childhood asthma exacerbations, and improve the management of asthma in children. The parents have provided their consent for their daughter to participate in the study.

Patient is a 28-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) according to McDonald criteria #1-4. She has a baseline EDSS between 0.0 and 5.0, inclusive. The patient has experienced at least one relapse within the 12 months prior to randomization and has a prior cranial MRI demonstrating lesion(s) consistent with MS or shows evidence of Gd-enhancing lesions of the brain on an MRI performed within the 6 weeks. She has no history of malignancy or severe allergic reactions to drugs. The patient does not have any abnormal laboratory results indicative of any significant cardiac, endocrinologic, hematologic, hepatic, immunologic, metabolic, urologic, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, dermatologic, psychiatric, renal, neurologic (other than MS), and/or other major disease. She has not had any drug or alcohol abuse within the 2 years prior to randomization. The patient has not had an MS relapse within the 50 days prior to randomization and has no history of previous treatment with FUMADERM®, FAG-201, or BG00012. She is willing to take appropriate measures to prevent pregnancy and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

55F immigrant from China, fluent in Mandarin, currently residing in the Washington DC area, is eligible for this study. She has never had a mammogram and is overdue for screening by two years. She has no personal history of breast cancer. She has lived in the United States for 10 years and has limited English proficiency. She is married with two adult children and works part-time as a housekeeper. She is interested in learning more about breast health and is open to participating in a small-group discussion. She reports no family history of breast cancer. Her primary care physician has recommended that she receive a mammogram but she has been hesitant due to fear and uncertainty about the screening process. She is motivated to learn more about mammography and breast health and hopes that this study can help her overcome her fears and misconceptions.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian male who has a history of coronary artery disease. He was diagnosed with CAD two years ago and had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at that time. The patient has been receiving regular follow-up care and medication to manage his condition. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He has a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in any regular physical activity. The patient reports occasional chest pain during physical activity and shortness of breath. The patient's blood pressure is within normal limits, and his heart rate is regular. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are all well controlled with medications. The patient is not on any anticoagulant treatment or has any implanted implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) or cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). The patient does not have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease GOLD IV, and his ejection fraction is more than 30%. The patient is willing to participate in the study to improve his condition and contribute to the research on the effect of exercise on CAD patients.

A 45-year-old sexually active woman who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence for several months. She is planning to undergo a mid-urethral sling procedure to address her condition. She has had no prior surgeries for incontinence or prolapse with transvaginal mesh. She is a non-smoker and does not have a history of pelvic radiation. She is not pregnant and is not currently incarcerated. She speaks English fluently and is able to comprehend the concept of randomization. She is willing to remain compliant with the instructions and study follow-up visits.

A 35-year-old male patient was diagnosed with schizophrenia at the age of 25. He has been on a stable dose of risperidone for the past 2 years, with no recent adjustment in medication dosage. He reports experiencing occasional heartburn and acid reflux, which is usually relieved by over-the-counter antacids. He has no history of substance abuse or dependence and has never been diagnosed with any significant medical or neurological conditions. He has no known allergies. He is currently living independently and is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 16-year-old male who was brought to the pediatric emergency department by his parents due to a fever and abdominal pain. He reports feeling tired and experiencing a loss of appetite for the past few days. His vital signs were: blood pressure 116/76 mmHg, heart rate 90 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and temperature 38.5°C. Upon examination, he was found to have tenderness in the right upper quadrant of his abdomen. Blood work showed elevated white blood cell count and liver enzymes. The patient is fluent in English and is accompanied by his parents who can provide informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old Chinese woman with no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 22 and has never been diagnosed with COVID-19. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant within the next 6 months. She has no known allergies to any vaccine ingredients and has never had a serious vaccine allergic reaction. Her urine pregnancy test is negative. She has not received any immunosuppressant therapy, anti-allergic therapy, or cytotoxic therapy in the past 6 months. She has not received any live attenuated vaccines within the past month or subunit or inactivated vaccines within the past 14 days. She is willing to comply with the planned visits, treatment schedule, laboratory tests, and other requirements of the trial. She has undergone screening tests, including hematology, biochemistry, and urinalysis, and all results are within normal limits. She is negative for HIV antibody, nucleic acid screening of SARS-CoV-2, and antibodies (IgG and IgM) screening of SARS-CoV-2. She has no imaging features of COVID-19 in chest CT. She has no significant abnormalities in blood routine, blood biochemistry, coagulation function, and urine routine, or no clinical significance was determined by doctors. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 5 on hemodialysis for the past 2 years. She receives dialysis via an arteriovenous fistula and her current dry weight has been stable for the past 4 weeks. She has not experienced any instability on dialysis or emergency medical attention, infusion of additional fluid, loss of consciousness, arrhythmia or chest pain in the last 4 weeks. She is fluent in English and able to follow simple instructions. She has no active infection, malignancy or contraindication to MRI scanning. She is not mentally incapacitated and is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

63-year-old male diagnosed with low rectal cancer with the inferior pole of the tumor located below the peritoneal reflection. The primary tumor has been histologically confirmed as rectal adenocarcinoma and has been diagnosed as Stage II (T3, N0, M0) disease. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate hematological function with neutrophils of 2.5 x 109/l and platelet count of 120 x 109/l, and hemoglobin of 11g/dl. The patient has adequate hepatic and renal function with serum bilirubin of 0.8 x upper limit of normal (ULN), alkaline phosphatase of 70 IU/l, and serum transaminase (either AST or ALT) of 65 IU/l. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 28.5 kg/m2 and no history of serious pre-operative comorbidity, including cardiovascular disease, pulmonary dysfunction, liver insufficiency, renal insufficiency, and arterial circulation disturbance. The patient has not undergone any previous abdominal surgery and has provided written informed consent for participation in the trial.

A 27-year-old male patient with a diagnosis of schizophrenia for the past 2 years is seeking to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of a new treatment. The patient has been treated with oral antipsychotic medications in the past, but has experienced lack of efficacy and tolerability issues. The patient is willing and able to fill out self-administered questionnaires during the study and has given informed consent to participate. The patient has no history of substance dependence or hypersensitivity to risperidone or paliperidone or excipients. However, the patient has a medical history of hypertension and chronic gastritis, which are currently stable and controlled with medication. The patient is not currently using any investigational drugs and has not participated in more than one investigational drug study in the past 12 months.

A 40-year-old woman came to the clinic with concerns about her skin. She has been experiencing redness and bumps on her face for the past year. She has tried different topical creams and antibiotics, but nothing has worked. The bumps are often filled with pus and sometimes painful. She feels self-conscious about her appearance and avoids social situations. She works as a teacher and exposure to the sun makes the symptoms worse. She has a family history of skin problems, but she has never had any skin issues until now. She has no other significant medical history, does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try a new treatment for her papulopustular rosacea.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital due to a urinary tract infection. She has a history of dementia and lives in a nursing home. The patient has difficulty communicating and is nonverbal due to severe dementia. She has no known neurological or neurosurgical diseases associated with cognitive impairment other than dementia. The patient was excluded from the study's exclusion criteria, as her pre-existing delirium was not considered a factor.

56-year-old female with no history of GI bleeding, colorectal surgery, inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, or polyposis syndrome. She is scheduled to undergo a routine screening colonoscopy as part of her regular health check-up. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial, as she is between the ages of 40-70 and is undergoing an average-risk screening colonoscopy.

53-year-old female diagnosed with stage III NSCLC with positive EGFR mRNA by ELISA. The patient has not received any previous paclitaxel liposome and carboplatin (TP) chemotherapy or targeted treatment of TKI or EGFR antibodies. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal functions of major organs. The patient does not have a history of serious allergy, other malignant tumors, or drug addiction. The patient is willing to comply with the clinical trial requirements and is using adequate methods of contraception.

45 year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of invasive HER2-positive breast carcinoma with a primary tumor size of 3.5 cm by standard local assessment technique. She has not received any previous anti-cancer therapy or radiotherapy for any malignancy. The patient is chemotherapy-naïve and presents with no signs of metastatic breast cancer or inflammatory breast cancer. She has a positive history of hormone receptor status (estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor). The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status is 1. Baseline left ventricular ejection fraction is >= 55% measured by echocardiography. The patient has no concurrent anti-cancer treatment in another investigational trial, no major surgical procedure unrelated to breast cancer within 4 weeks prior to randomization, and no serious cardiac illness or medical condition. The participant has no other concurrent serious diseases that may interfere with planned treatment, including severe pulmonary conditions/illness. The patient has no abnormalities in liver, kidney or hematologic function laboratory tests immediately prior to randomization. The participant is not pregnant or lactating.

This is a 42-year-old female diagnosed with breast cancer that has metastasized to the liver. The patient is currently enrolled in U8700 RSRB # A Phase II Study For Using Radiosurgery On Limited Metastases Of Breast Cancer. She has given informed consent to participate in this study. The patient has no contraindications for MRI procedures. She is in good health and able to perform simple breath-holding exercises as part of the study protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with locally advanced rectal cancer. The patient reports experiencing intermittent rectal bleeding, abdominal pain, and changes in bowel habits for several months before seeking medical attention. A colonoscopy revealed a large tumor located approximately 5cm from the anal verge. Biopsy of the tumor confirmed adenocarcinoma. Imaging studies including CT and MRI showed no evidence of metastasis. The patient has no significant medical history, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group score is 1. He is currently not receiving any treatment for his cancer. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help optimize neoadjuvant chemotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer.

A 52 year old woman who is the primary caregiver for her 74 year old mother with Alzheimer's Disorder is experiencing feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and a lack of interest in daily activities. She reports difficulty sleeping, decreased appetite, and fatigue. She has no history of psychiatric illness or drug or alcohol abuse. She speaks and understands English fluently and is able to give informed consent. She is currently not participating in any meditation or guided imagery practices, and has not had any thoughts of harming her mother. She is not currently undergoing any medical treatments or planning any surgeries. Her Mini Mental State Examination score is above 24, indicating no significant cognitive impairment.

A 28-year-old woman who has been wearing soft contact lenses for over a year with no complications. She has a myopic refractive error and wears -3.00 D contact lenses.
