She has never had any ocular or systemic diseases, and she does not take any medications. Her last eye exam was six months ago, and she had no clinically significant findings. She has never had any allergy or sensitivity to any contact lens solution. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy. She has not participated in any clinical trial in the last 30 days.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She is currently at 38 weeks and 4 days of gestation. She has not experienced any complications during her pregnancy and has been healthy overall. However, during her labor, she is experiencing slow progress, including prolonged latent phase and labor arrest. She has a BMI of 25, which falls within the normal range. She has no history of any medical conditions and is not taking any medications currently. She has consulted with her obstetrician about the possibility of participating in a clinical trial to receive tafoxiparin as an Adjunct Treatment to Oxytocin to help with her labor.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl with a history of allergic reaction to hen's egg. She experienced hives, itching, and difficulty breathing after eating scrambled eggs. Skin prick testing and specific IgE detection by CAPtest confirmed IgE-mediated hen's egg allergy. Her specific IgE level to Gal d 1 is below 1.2 kU/mL. She has not experienced grade 4 anaphylaxis due to egg ingestion. The parents are willing to adhere to a certain egg step-containing diet on a regular basis at home and to participate in the study. The girl is at least 12 months old, and the investigators are considering introducing heated egg to her.

A 4-year-old girl is scheduled for laparoscopic hernia repair surgery. She has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. She lives with her parents and an older brother. The patient is active and enjoys playing with dolls and coloring books. She is a bit shy but warms up quickly to new people. Her parents are concerned about her pain after the surgery and want to ensure that she has the best possible pain control. She has not had any surgeries before and is a bit scared but is willing to cooperate with the doctors and nurses. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications regularly. Her parents are willing to participate in the study to help improve pain management for children undergoing laparoscopic surgery.

The patient is a 35-year-old right-handed female who works as a writer. She has been experiencing involuntary co-contraction of her hand muscles during writing for the past year. This has caused her difficulty in completing her work and has led to a significant decrease in her productivity. She has tried different treatments, including medication, without any significant improvement. She has no other neurological or psychiatric diseases. She is not taking any anticholinergics or sedating medication. She is willing and able to participate in video calls. She has not received botulinum toxin treatment in the past 3 months. She is not pregnant or suspected to be pregnant, and she has no cardiac pacemaker or metal implants. She wears glasses for a mild degree of ametropia. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve her writing abilities and quality of life.

The patient is a 64-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. His PSA levels are within normal range, and his biopsy results show a Gleason score of 6. He has no history of prior prostate cancer treatment, and his prostate volume is less than 75-cc, as determined by ultrasound. He has no significant medical history, is not taking any medications, and has no allergies. The patient is able to complete questionnaires independently or with assistance, and is willing to participate in a patient-reported outcomes survey program, inclusive of the Expanded Prostate Index Composite and CTCAE instruments. He understands the risks and benefits of proton-based stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy (SABR) and is willing to provide informed written consent. The patient is not immunocompromised due to HIV positive state, has no medical or psychiatric conditions that preclude informed decision-making or adherence, and has not previously registered for an Institutional Review Board-approved therapeutic research study that includes proton beam therapy or photon-based radiotherapy.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of smoking for over 30 years. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue and coughing for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer with infiltration of the main carina and mediastinal involvement after undergoing a series of tests including CT scan and biopsy. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is married and has two adult children. He is retired and enjoys spending time with his family, reading and gardening. He is physically active and exercises regularly. His BMI is 26 and his blood pressure is 130/80. There are no notable findings on his physical examination. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to assess the presence and amount of circulating tumor cells in patients undergoing thoracic resection with and without intraoperative use of ECMO or CPB. He understands the nature of the study and has provided informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer after experiencing back pain and was found to have multiple bone metastases on imaging. She has no prior chemotherapy treatments for her advanced disease and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and she has no history of heart disease. Her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was measured to be 60% within the past month. She has agreed to participate in this clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. She is not currently receiving any hormonal or chemotherapy treatments, and her cancer is not overexpressing the Her2/neu protein.

A 30-year-old male with a BMI of 23 presents to the hospital for elective surgery. He has provided written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial exploring the pharmacodynamic interactions of propofol and dexmedetomidine on intravenous anesthesia. He has no previous history of intolerance to the study drugs or related compounds and additives. He has no existing significant hematological, endocrine, metabolic, or gastrointestinal disease. The patient is in overall good health and is motivated to participate in the study.

The patient is a 2-year-old girl who has been admitted to the hospital due to acute watery diarrhea that has been lasting for more than 12 hours but less than 72 hours. She has lost 5% of her body weight, and her skin turgor is abnormal. She is not vomiting, but she has a high frequency of loose stools. She has no underlying chronic diseases, and she is not immunocompromised. She has not taken antibiotics or probiotics in the past month. She lives with her parents and two older siblings. She attends daycare regularly and enjoys playing with her siblings. She is a picky eater, and her parents have a hard time getting her to eat vegetables and fruits. She is alert and responsive but appears tired and irritable due to the diarrhea.

A 42-year-old male presents with a positive COVID-19 test result and reports mild fever and cough for the past two days. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical study to explore the effects of KB109 on gut microbiota structure and function. He reports no hospitalization or ongoing requirement for oxygen therapy. He has no chronic lung disease and reports no shortness of breath in resting position. He is not diagnosed with sleep apnea requiring Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure (BIPAP) / Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP). He is not currently pregnant or lactating. He understands the study requirements, is able to adhere to the study visit schedule, and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 12 years. She has been experiencing a non-healing ulcer on her left ankle for the past 20 weeks. The ulcer is painful and measures approximately 35 cm² in area. She has been receiving wound care treatment for the past 12 weeks but has not seen any improvement. She smokes 5 cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. She takes metformin and lisinopril for her diabetes and hypertension, respectively. She has no known allergies to any medications or porcine products. She lives with her husband and two children and is able to attend all study visits and comply with the off-loading regimen.

A 4-year-old boy named Daniel has been diagnosed with Pervasive Developmental Disorder (PDD) and his parents are seeking treatment options for him. He currently attends a kindergarten in Ashdod, Israel and has been receiving various therapies for his condition, including speech therapy and occupational therapy. He is able to communicate verbally but struggles with social interactions and play skills. He has no other underlying medical conditions or intellectual disabilities. Daniel's parents are interested in enrolling him in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of Integrative Therapy and help improve their son's communication and overall functioning.

A 23-year-old male who wears glasses and was diagnosed with myopia since the age of 10 has been identified as a potential candidate for this clinical trial. He is of East Asian ethnicity and has no significant ocular or medical history apart from his myopia. His last eye examination was performed 3 months ago and showed the following results: Best corrected visual acuity: 6/6 in both eyes Refraction: -9.50 D in the right eye and -9.75 D in the left eye Intraocular pressure: 15 mmHg in both eyes Gonioscopy: Open angles in both eyes Fundus exam: No obvious pathology noted in both eyes. The patient has been informed about the clinical trial and has provided informed consent for participation. He has no family history of glaucoma or other optic neuropathy, and he does not have any of the exclusion criteria specified in the study description.

56-year-old male with a history of hypertension, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease presents to Herlev Hospital, Department of Radiology for a CT-scan to evaluate a suspected kidney stone. The patient is concerned about the use of contrast agents and has heard about potential adverse reactions. The patient is otherwise in good health and has never had a reaction to a contrast agent before. The patient is referred to participate in a prospective study investigating the safety profile of iodine-containing and gadolinium-based contrast agents in CT and MR-examinations. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is randomized into Group C (case group) and undergoes a CT

The patient is a 15-year-old female diagnosed with Crohn's disease six months ago. She has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. She has tried various medications with limited success and is looking for a new treatment option. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try natalizumab to see if it can help alleviate her symptoms.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with strabismus and is scheduled for elective strabismus surgery under general anesthesia. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. Her parents have given informed written consent for her participation in the clinical trial. The patient is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) I patient. She has no history of hyperactive airway disease or respiratory diseases, bleeding or coagulation diathesis, developmental delays, mental or neurological disorders or sensitivity to the anesthetics used in the study. She has not had previous surgery in the same eye.

33-year-old woman in her first pregnancy presents to the labor and delivery unit in early labor with cervical dilation of 3 cm. She is otherwise healthy with no history of back or spinal surgery, allergies to the drugs used in the study or contraindications to neuraxial anesthesia. The patient has an assigned ASA physical status of 1 and is carrying a singleton pregnancy. She has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

No patient description is needed for this clinical trial as it specifically states that only healthy male participants with certain criteria for eligibility are eligible to participate. Therefore, no patient with a particular medical condition or history is being targeted for this study.

A 32-year old female school teacher was diagnosed with major depressive disorder a year ago. She experiences persistent sadness, loss of energy, difficulty sleeping and concentrating, and feelings of worthlessness. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled on medication. She lives alone and has no children. She enjoys reading, hiking, and spending time with her friends. She recently had a breakup with her long-term partner, which has contributed to her depressive symptoms. She is currently not taking any medication for her depression. She has never taken desvenlafaxine sustained release (DVS-233SR) before. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore long-term treatment options for her depression. She is aware of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 15-year-old female diagnosed with bipolar II disorder is currently on lithium therapy. The patient has been experiencing depressive episodes frequently over the past few months with occasional hypomanic episodes. She has an average intelligence level and is currently attending high school. The patient has no history of substance abuse and is not currently taking any other medication apart from lithium. The patient's parents have given their informed consent for her participation in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from Italy who has been recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has a history of heavy smoking for 30 years, and his past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of significant lung disease or other comorbidities. A chest CT scan revealed a 3.5 cm mass in the upper lobe of his right lung. Pulmonary function tests showed a carbon monoxide lung diffusion capacity of 65%. He is scheduled to undergo video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy for the removal of the tumor.

A 38-year-old woman diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) presenting with symptoms of depressed mood, loss of interest in activities, and feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness. She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and seasonal allergies. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She has been on several antidepressants in the past with no significant improvement. She is currently not taking any antidepressants or other psychiatric medication. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for her depression.

A 54-year-old male smoker with a history of hypertension, presented with a cough and shortness of breath. A CT scan showed a mass in his lung and biopsy confirmed it was non-small cell lung cancer. The patient was diagnosed with stage III cancer, which is unresectable, and was offered to participate in a clinical trial that involves concurrent chemoradiotherapy combination with Anlotinib. The patient is willing to participate and has signed the informed consent. He meets the eligibility criteria as he has no history of small cell lung cancer or hemoptysis, and his tumor is measurable. He has not received any systemic anti-tumor therapy within the last 4 weeks. His organ function is normal, and he has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥50% lower limit of normal (LLN) and forced expiratory volume in first second (FEVI)≥1.45L/s. He is not diagnosed with any severe and/or uncontrolled disease that can affect the oral medication. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he has not participated in any other anti-tumor drug clinical trials within the last 4 weeks. The patient is expected to have a survival time of more than 3 months.

A 42-year-old female with a history of advanced triple negative breast cancer that has metastasized to the lungs and liver. The patient has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. Her estrogen and progesterone receptors are negative, and her human epidermal growth factor receptor (HER-2/neu) is not over-expressed based on immunohistochemistry (IHC) or FISH. The patient has not received any other investigational agents within 4 weeks and has not undergone radiation therapy within 2 weeks prior to the first dose of the study regimen. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. Her leukocyte count, absolute neutrophil count, and platelet count are within normal limits. She has a total bilirubin level within the institution's upper limit of normal and AST/ALT levels within 2.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal. The patient has a creatinine clearance of >50 mL/min and a left ventricular ejection fraction of >

Patient is a 6-week-old infant with a diagnosis of congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The baby was born at 37 weeks gestation via C-section due to decreased fetal movements. The baby was intubated in the delivery room due to respiratory distress and transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit. The baby was diagnosed with a left-sided diaphragmatic hernia and underwent surgical repair on day 4 of life. The patient is currently stable on mechanical ventilation and receiving a combination of fentanyl and midazolam for sedation and analgesia. The parents have provided written informed consent for the baby to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with end-stage arthritis of the right knee. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well controlled with medication. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. His current medications include lisinopril and amlodipine for hypertension. He has tried conservative treatment for his knee, including physical therapy and pain medication, but with no significant improvement. His preoperative hemoglobin level is 12.5 g/dl, and he has not used any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents for one week before the operation. He has not had any previous knee surgeries or infections. He has normal liver and renal function, and he has never had deep vein thrombosis, ischemic heart disease, or stroke.

A 32-year-old female presents with moderate-to-severe Atopic Dermatitis (AD) that has been present for the past 5 years. She reports a history of chronic itching, dry and scaly skin, and occasional skin infections. She has tried multiple topical medications such as corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, and emollients without significant improvement. She has no history of phototherapy or systemic medications for AD. Her past medical history is otherwise unremarkable, with no history of immunosuppression or chronic infections. She denies any history of pregnancy or breastfeeding. On physical examination, there is erythematous, excoriated, and thickened skin with lichenification on the flexural surfaces of both forearms, behind both knees, and on the neck. The Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score is 21 and the Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score is 4, indicating severe AD. She has AD involvement of about 15% of her body surface area.

This is a 20 year-old female who presented to the emergency department (ED) with a complaint of abdominal pain. She reports that the pain started after she had unprotected sex with her boyfriend last night. Upon further questioning, she admits to having multiple sexual partners in the past 3 months and inconsistent use of condoms. She also reports occasional binge drinking on weekends. The patient has access to a personal cell phone with SMS features and is interested in receiving information and skill building to improve her health behavior. She is not currently pregnant nor planning to become pregnant in the next 3 months and has no history of drug/alcohol treatment or psychiatric treatment.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis has been scheduled for a laparoscopic surgery to remove the cysts. She is married with no children and works as a teacher. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications except for occasional painkillers for menstrual cramps. She has no history of central nervous system disease or psychiatric disorders. Her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no contraindications for the use of propofol or the closed-loop system. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions.

55 year-old male with a history of angina and coronary artery disease. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath with exertion for several months. His stress test showed significant ischemia and his angiogram revealed triple vessel disease. He has been scheduled for elective on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. He has no history of diabetes and is not considered a high risk patient. His ischemic time during the surgery is expected to be less than 120 minutes.

A 52-year-old woman presents with a history of melanoma and has been diagnosed with advanced melanoma (stage III-IV). She has undergone previous treatments including surgery and chemotherapy, but the disease has progressed, and she is now scheduled for anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in a pilot study investigating the feasibility and efficacy of Tc-99m-tilmanocept as a marker for imaging M2-like TAMs in melanoma metastasis. She has had an FDG PET/CT scan within 4 weeks before screening and has biopsy samples available for analysis. She has at least three lesions detected in her FDG PET/CT scan. The patient does not have ocular melanoma and has not undergone previous immunotherapy. She does not have any known allergy to dextran or any other adverse reaction to dextran exposure. The patient is fluent in the language of the project and is able to provide informed consent and follow procedures.

A 45-year-old male with a history of Parkinson's disease presents to the clinic with complaints of difficulty with fine motor control, tremors, and stiffness especially on the right side of his body. He is currently on medication but has noticed a decrease in effectiveness over time. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He has no history of seizures, intracranial surgery, metal implants in the head or neck or any brain radiotherapy. He is able to participate in the consent process physically and cognitively.

A 32-year-old woman was diagnosed with HIV infection 3 years ago, and she has been on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for 2 years. She has been compliant with all her medications and has achieved an undetectable viral load (< 50 copies/mL) for the past year. She works as a nurse and is in good general health. She has no history of opportunistic infections or malignancies. She has never been pregnant and is not currently pregnant. Her current CD4+ T cell count is 560 cells/mm3, and her nadir CD4+ T cell count was 280 cells/mm3. She has no history of anemia or bleeding disorder. Her hemoglobin level is 12.2 g/dL, and her platelet count is 180,000/mm3. She has no history of liver disease or abnormal liver function tests. Her liver function tests are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance the understanding of HIV pathogenesis and potentially help find a cure for HIV.

A 42 year old woman who has been experiencing chronic pain and discomfort for several years. She has visited multiple doctors and has undergone numerous medical tests, but no physical cause for her symptoms has been identified. She has been diagnosed with a somatic symptom disorder and is experiencing distress and functional impairment as a result. She is interested in participating in a new cognitive behavioural therapy group designed specifically to address her concerns and improve her quality of life. She has no history of acute depression, suicidal ideation, severe PTSD symptoms, current psychosis, substance use disorder, or severe cognitive impairment. She is a registered patient of St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton.

35-year-old F with a history of opioid and benzodiazepine dependence. She has been receiving buprenorphine maintenance treatment for the past 6 months and is currently taking a daily dose of 8mg. She has also been taking lorazepam 2mg/day for the past 2 years. She has expressed a desire to quit the benzodiazepine, but has been unsuccessful in previous attempts due to severe withdrawal symptoms including anxiety, insomnia, and tremors. She has been enrolled in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of valproate in reducing the severity of benzodiazepine withdrawal symptoms during a gradual discontinuation of the medication. She has no history of convulsions or unstable somatic diseases but is not pregnant. She has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

A 54 year old woman with advanced ovarian cancer is referred to the clinical trial. She has been receiving chemotherapy for the past six months but has not shown significant improvement. She has no history of brain metastases or active infection. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 and is expected to live at least 12 weeks. She understands the study procedures and has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 56-year-old male patient is scheduled for thoracic surgery due to a pulmonary mass. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and his past medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient has a normal neck range of motion and has no difficulty in opening his mouth. The thyromental distance is 7.5 cm and the sternomental distance is 13 cm. The patient has no history of gastroesophageal reflux or any other gastrointestinal problems. He is not pregnant and has no plans of becoming pregnant. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. He has noticed a gradual increase in urinary frequency and urgency, as well as difficulty in initiating and maintaining a steady stream of urine. A digital rectal exam revealed a firm nodule on the right lobe of his prostate gland, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of prostate adenocarcinoma. He is being referred to Careggi University Hospital for further evaluation and treatment. The patient is willing to participate in an exploratory study of SLPI expression in prostate cancer patients to help further understand the disease and improve treatment options.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who is currently in her 36th week of pregnancy. She has a singleton pregnancy without any complications. During her routine antenatal examination, she expressed her interest in participating in a study about coffee consumption during pregnancy. She is an occasional coffee drinker and usually consumes one cup of coffee per day. She has no history of hypertension, preeclampsia, chromosomal anomaly, intrauterine growth restriction, fetal anomaly, collagen vascular disease, ruptured fetal membranes, or multiple pregnancies. She also has normal amniotic fluid volume.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with a suspicious breast mass after undergoing a mammogram and ultrasound. She is scheduled to undergo a breast biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. The patient is feeling anxious and fearful about the procedure, and has expressed concern about experiencing pain and discomfort during the biopsy. She has no history of nausea, vertigo, or labyrinthitis. The patient is able to communicate effectively and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing bilateral knee pain for the past year. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee according to the American College of Rheumatology criteria. She has a functional capacity class rating of II according to ACR classification. She has been taking over-the-counter analgesics for her pain but was asked to discontinue them prior to the study. She has no history of inflammatory arthritis, gout, pseudo-gout or Paget's disease. She has no history of joint replacement surgery at the index joint. She has no significant medical conditions requiring daily medications. She has not experienced any asthma, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs. She has no prior history of peptic ulcer disease and/or gastrointestinal bleeding. She is not taking analgesic medications, glucosamine or chondroitin. She is not taking long-acting opioids or opioids that cannot be discontinued over the first 5 days of the washout period. She has not received either a corticosteroid injection or hyaluronic acid recently. She is able to discontinue any topical drugs applied to the knee. She has not previously failed treatment with celecoxib or with two COX-2 specific inhibitors other than celecoxib. She is not taking class I anti-arrhythmic drugs.

58-year-old male with metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) with documented disease progression within 12 weeks of the last dose of anti PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy. He has previously received systemic therapy for RCC and has Karnofsky performance status of 80. The patient has no significant immunodeficiency due to underlying illness and is not currently taking immune-suppressive medication, including high-dose corticosteroids. He has not undergone major surgery within the last 4 weeks and has no ongoing severe inflammatory skin condition requiring prior medical treatment. The patient does not have a history of eczema requiring prior medical treatment. He has no tumor(s) invading a major vascular structure or other key anatomical structure, nor does he have a viable central nervous system malignancy. The patient has no clinically significant and/or rapidly accumulating ascites, pericardial and/or pleural effusions. He has no symptomatic cardiovascular disease or significant coronary artery disease requiring angioplasty or stenting within the preceding 12 months. The patient is willing and able to suspend treatment with anti-hypertensive medication for 48 hours prior to and 48 hours after all Pexa-Vec treatments and does not use interferon/pegylated interferon (PEG-IFN) or ribavirin that cannot be discontinued within 14 days prior to any Pexa-Vec dose. The patient does not have known active Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C.

The patient is a 6-year-old child who is in good health and has no history of chronic severe disease. The child has received three doses of a diphtheria, tetanus and poliomyelitis containing vaccine within the first 6 months of life and a booster dose at 16-18 months of life. The child's parents have given informed consent for the child to participate in the study. There is no history of immune impairment or humoral/cellular deficiency, neoplastic disease, or depressed immunity. The child has not received any vaccines in the previous 30 days and has no scheduled vaccinations during the course of the study. The child has no known hypersensitivity to the components of a study vaccine or to streptomycin, neomycin or polymixin B. The child has not presented with encephalopathy, seizure disorder or progressive, evolving or unstable neurological condition. The child has not had severe hypersensitivity following an earlier immunization against diphtheria and/or tetanus. Finally, the child does not have a known history of thrombocytopenia or any coagulation disorder that would contraindicate intramuscular injection, and does not have an acute severe febrile illness or oral temperature ≥37.5°C at the time of vaccination.

50-year-old postmenopausal female with a positive family history of osteoporosis presented to her primary care physician with a complaint of occasional back pain. She has a history of smoking for 10 years before quitting and no history of any fractures. Her BMI is within the normal range. She is not taking any medications and has not undergone any surgical procedures. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness upon palpation of the spine. She agrees to participate in the osteoporosis screening trial and is willing to have her bone mineral density measured.

32 y/o female with a history of atopic asthma, diagnosed at age 18. She has been on a daily dose of 250mcg fluticasone for the past 2 years, which has helped to control her asthma symptoms. She reports experiencing worsening of her symptoms every time she gets a respiratory infection. She is a non-smoker and has no history of other respiratory diseases. She has no current symptoms of allergic rhinitis and has not had an exacerbation or virus within the previous 6 weeks. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no contact with infants or elderly at home or at work. She is not currently using any nasal spray, anti-histamine or anti-leukotriene medications. She has no known antibodies to rhinovirus 16.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has recently experienced a transient ischemic attack (TIA). He reports feeling weakness and numbness on the right side of his body, and difficulty speaking. The symptoms resolved after a few hours, but he has been concerned about the possibility of having a stroke. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been taking medication for these conditions but has not been able to control his blood sugar levels well. The patient has undergone a carotid ultrasound, which revealed >30% stenosis in the carotid artery. He has been referred to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of long-term food supplementation with a tomato extract containing lycopene. The patient is interested in participating as he would like to explore alternative treatment options for his condition. He has no known allergies to tomatoes or gadolinium, and he is not scheduled for surgical/endovascular intervention within the next 3 months. The patient has not been taking high-dose statin therapy or other lipid-lowering therapy, and he is not chronically using high-dose aspirin. He has no contraindications for MRI studies and has no significant renal impairment. He is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to participate in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who has a history of fainting episodes and has been diagnosed with a torsade de pointes event. He is currently on medication for hypertension and has no family history of sudden cardiac death. His ECG shows a QTc interval of 470ms. He is willing to undergo genetic testing and blood collection for this study.

The patient is a 9-month-old infant who has been diagnosed with gastro-esophageal reflux disease (GERD). The infant has been struggling with vomiting, irritability, and difficulty feeding since birth. The infant's parents have tried various medications and lifestyle modifications, but the symptoms have not improved. The infant has been referred to the study by their pediatrician. The infant is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or comorbidities. The parents are willing to participate in the study and have provided informed consent. The infant is scheduled to undergo an operative intervention for the GERD. The surgeon has agreed to use the proposed cardiaplication technique in the study. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

We are seeking participants for a clinical trial studying the effects of palmitoleic acids on insulin resistance. We are looking for individuals between the ages of 18 and 70 with a body mass index (BMI) between 25 and 40. Participants should have normal fasting plasma glucose levels and no diagnosed diabetes. Individuals with normal kidney and liver function, as well as normal thyroid and gastrointestinal function are eligible to participate. Participants should not have major chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disease, active cancer, end stage renal disease, dementia, severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or significant liver disease. Participants must not be pregnant or breastfeeding, and should be willing to adhere to the study protocol. Individuals who have taken supplements containing fish oil or other lipid supplements within the past 3 months or who consume more than 2 servings/day of cheese, whole-fat milk, or whole-fat yogurt are not eligible to participate. Additionally, individuals who take medication known to affect lipid metabolism or hormone therapy medications containing estrogen are also not eligible. Participants will receive vegetable oil capsules containing either trans-C16:1 or cis-C16:1 during two 9-week phases, with a minimum of a 4 week off-study period between the two phases. Blood will be drawn at baseline, 3 weeks, 6 weeks, and 9 weeks during each phase. The study will have a total length of about 18 weeks, not including the break between phase 1 and phase 2. Payment will be provided and a social security number will be required for payment and IRS forms.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been experiencing obsessive-compulsive symptoms for the past 6 months. She has intrusive thoughts and compulsions that interfere with her daily life, such as checking and rechecking if the doors are locked, touching things in a particular order, and repeating certain phrases. Her parents have noticed that her symptoms have been worsening over time, and she has become increasingly anxious and distressed. She has no significant medical history, and her family history is non-significant for mental health disorders. She has not been treated with fluvoxamine or any other medication for OCD in the past 2 months. Her weight is within the range of standard weight - 2 standard deviations based on the standard weight for her age. Her parents have provided written informed consent for her participation in the study.

This is a 13 year-old Japanese male who was recently diagnosed with a fungal infection caused by Candida or Aspergillus species. He has been experiencing persistent fever, cough, and shortness of breath for the past week. A chest x-ray revealed a pulmonary infiltrate and cultures were positive for the fungi. His medical history is significant for asthma and eczema but he is otherwise healthy. He has not received any antifungal treatment for this infection yet. The patient and his family are interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance the treatment options for pediatric patients with fungal infections.

65-year-old female with a history of smoking presents with persistent cough and shortness of breath. A diagnostic non-contrast enhanced CT scan was performed, revealing a suspicious lung mass. Biopsy results confirm the presence of NSCLC, but the specific subtype (adenocarcinoma, SCC, or large cell carcinoma) has not yet been determined. The patient is scheduled for further testing, including a CT-based radiomic signature analysis, to aid in the identification of the tumor histology.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital due to severe pneumonia. She requires invasive mechanical ventilation and is receiving oxygen therapy via the Optiflow system. She has been stable for the past 24 hours and her doctor has approved physiotherapy sessions. She has no neurological or orthopedic problems and has not undergone any abdominal surgery. She has a BMI of 28 and is 1.7m tall. She is willing to participate in the study and has no history of psychiatric illness or severe agitation. She has no cardiac stimulator or defibrillator. She is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has no history of neuromuscular disease, epilepsy, or stroke. She has no dermatological problems that would prevent her from participating in the study. The patient has no hemiplegia or sequential hemiparesis. Lastly, the patient has no contraindications to electrostimulation on her lower limbs.

The patient is a 70-year-old female who has been diagnosed with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in her left eye. She has a distance BCVA of 20/200 in her left eye, with subfoveal disciform scarring. She is not currently using any anti-VEGF therapy and has not used any within the past month. She has no history of ocular or systemic gene transfer product. She has not received any investigational product within the past 120 days. She has not had any intraocular surgeries in her left eye within the past three months and is not a likely candidate for intraocular surgery in the next year. She has adequate dilation of pupils to permit thorough ocular examination and testing. She is willing to have samples of anterior chamber fluid collected from her left eye. She has no active herpetic infection or significant poorly controlled illness that would preclude study compliance and follow-up.

45 year old male with a past medical history of cholecystitis and multiple episodes of renal colic. He is scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent episodes of cholecystitis. He has a BMI of 30, is 6 feet tall, and weighs 220 lbs. He has no history of cardiovascular or respiratory disease. He is willing to comply with the specified follow-up evaluations and has signed the written informed consent form. He is affiliated with social security.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman was recently diagnosed with a pelvic fracture following a low-energy fall. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The fracture is located in the anterior column of the pelvis and was confirmed by CT scan. She is not currently receiving any treatment for osteoporosis. Her mental status is consistent with completing the study protocol. She is interested in participating in the study to help advance medical knowledge about fracture healing. She understands that she may be randomly assigned to receive either teriparatide or a placebo for the duration of the 16-week study. She is willing to take daily calcium and vitamin D supplements throughout the study and attend regular functional evaluations. She meets all inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria based on laboratory results. She is excited to potentially help advance medical knowledge and improve treatment options for pelvic fractures.

The patient is a 27 year-old healthy male with no history of psychiatric diseases or brain disorders. He has not used any antidepressant or antipsychotic medications in the past and has no regular use of medications that could interfere with the pharmacodynamics or pharmacokinetics of escitalopram. He has no significant abnormalities on ECG or structural abnormalities in the brain confirmed by MR examination. He does not have claustrophobia and has no metal devices or implants in his body. He has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions that would make him unsuitable for the study or put him at additional risk. He understands and is able to comply with the study requirements.

A 35-year-old female presents with shortness of breath and fatigue upon exertion. She was previously diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension and is currently taking an approved PAH medication. She has been classified as WHO functional class II and has a right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) of 40% as determined by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Her 6-minute walk test (6-MWT) distance is 350 meters. Her plasma NT-ProBNP levels were elevated, indicating impaired RV function, and serum catecholamine levels were also elevated, indicating sympathetic activation. The patient reports a decreased quality of life due to her symptoms. She has never been diagnosed with asthma and has not had any significant illnesses or hospitalizations in the past 30 days. She is not pregnant nor is she planning to become pregnant during the study period. She does not have a history of bradycardia, AV block, or sinus tachycardia. Her blood pressure is stable at 120/80 mmHg. She has not been treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs. The patient is willing to participate in the study and agrees to comply with all study requirements.

A 54-year-old Hispanic man who is currently uninsured presents to a Parkland primary care clinic for a routine check-up. He has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit 5 years ago. He has a family history of colon cancer, with his father being diagnosed at the age of 55. He has never had a colonoscopy or stool blood test (FIT) and is not up-to-date with colorectal cancer screening. He reports no symptoms related to colorectal cancer such as abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or changes in bowel habits. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are currently well-controlled with medications. He has no history of inflammatory bowel disease or colon polyps. He is willing to participate in the study and is informed of the study requirements and procedures. His contact information is up-to-date and he is not incarcerated.

A 25-year-old male who is an avid runner and runs approximately 20-25 km per week is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining the effects of a pre-workout supplement on energy expenditure during moderate-intensity treadmill running. He has no history of medical or surgical events, including cardiovascular disease, metabolic, renal, hepatic, or musculoskeletal disorders. He does not use any medication, nutritional supplements, or consume caffeine regularly. He has not participated in any clinical trial or investigation of another investigational product within 30 days prior to screening/enrollment. The subject is willing to adhere to the study protocol and record 2-day food logs prior to each laboratory visit.

The patient is a 14-month-old healthy baby girl who has not had any previous vaccinations for measles, mumps, rubella or varicella. She has no history of any allergic reactions or significant medical conditions. The parents are interested in participating in the study to evaluate the investigational vaccine for its safety and efficacy in comparison to the standard frozen vaccine. They are willing to comply with all the study requirements and attend all the scheduled follow-up visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of bilateral melasma on her face. Her melasma developed during her first pregnancy and has persisted despite the use of various topical treatments. She is not currently pregnant or nursing and is not using any hormonal birth control medication or any hormonal therapy. She has not undergone any laser or dermabrasion to the face within the past 9 months. She does not have poor wound healing, recurrent herpes simplex, or current skin infections. She does not have photosensitivity or a history of hypertropic scar/keloids. The patient has realistic expectations and is willing to participate in the study. She will undergo detailed history taking, dermatological examination, and Wood's light examination to estimate the depth of her melasma.

Pt is a 60yo male with a diagnosis of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with a history of prior chemotherapy. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and an expected survival time of at least 24 months. His hematologic, renal, and liver function are adequate with a WBC greater than 3.5 x 109/L, Absolute neutrophils count greater than 1.5 x 109/L, Platelet count greater than 80 x 109/L, Hemoglobin at least 90g/L, AST less than 2 x upper limit of normal (ULN), and Creatinine less than 1.5 x ULN. He has no obvious abnormalities in the electrocardiogram. The patient has not had any major surgery or prior autologous bone marrow transplantation within 4 weeks of enrollment. He has not participated in any other therapeutic clinical trial with an experimental drug in the 4 weeks prior to this trial. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently presented with symptoms of community-acquired pneumonia, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She was admitted to the hospital and diagnosed with CAP. She has no known allergies to any of the antibiotics being tested in this trial. She has not received any antibiotic treatment prior to admission. The patient is willing to participate in this study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Wegener's granulomatosis for the past 3 years. She has been previously treated with corticosteroids and immunosuppressants but has experienced a recent relapse. She is experiencing symptoms such as joint pain, fatigue, decreased appetite, and shortness of breath. Her most recent laboratory results show elevated inflammatory markers, including an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 60 mm/h and a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 4.5 mg/dL. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril 10mg daily. She has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 30-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with bipolar disorder and has been experiencing extreme mood swings. She has been prescribed medication to manage her symptoms, but she is interested in exploring additional options to improve her quality of life. She works as a freelance writer and feels that her bipolar disorder is hindering her ability to focus and be productive. She has access to a computer and is comfortable with using videoconferencing technology. She is fluent in English and lives in England. She has not received any talking therapy for her bipolar disorder. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to try Method of Levels therapy delivered online via videoconferencing. She is excited about the prospect of having more control over her therapy and being able to talk freely about her goals and problems.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of bronchial asthma came to the hospital for a scheduled major pelvi-abdominal surgery under general anesthesia. She had been taking inhaled corticosteroids and a short-acting beta agonist for her asthma for the past two years. She is otherwise healthy and her physical status is ASA II. She does not have any known allergies or sensitivities to medications. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. Her family history is negative for any significant medical conditions. She currently drinks one cup of coffee per day. The patient is interested in participating in the study to see if aminophylline as premedication can affect the extubation and recovery time after surgery.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 6 years. He is currently on a stable dose of metformin and sulfonylurea for the past 3 months. His HbA1c value is between 7% and 10%. He is compliant with his diet and exercise regimen. The patient has no history of insulin use or hypoglycemia unawareness. He has not been hospitalized for poor glucose control in the past 6 months. The patient has no gastrointestinal disease that significantly impacts gastric emptying or motility. He has no history of cardiac disease, functional status that is New York Heart Association Class II, III, or IV, or a history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or decompensated congestive heart failure in the past 6 months. His blood pressure is well-controlled with antihypertensive medications. He has no evidence of liver disease, acute or chronic hepatitis, or repeated alanine transaminase (ALT) levels >2.5 times the upper limit of the reference range at screening. The patient is not on any lipid-lowering agents and has no hypertriglyceridemia. He has no evidence of a significant active, uncontrolled endocrine or autoimmune abnormality. The patient has no history of seizure disorder or any active or untreated malignancy or been in remission from a clinically significant malignancy for less than 5 years. He is a good candidate for this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of LY2599506 in controlling his blood sugar.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial as it focuses on evaluating the effects of a novel integrated clinical prediction tool on antibiotic prescription patterns of nurses for acute respiratory infections (ARIs) and not on patients directly.

The patient is an 82-year-old woman who resides in a nursing home facility. She has a history of hypertension and Type 2 diabetes, which is well controlled with medication. She has been living in the nursing home for the past 6 months due to her decreased mobility and difficulty in completing activities of daily living independently. She has no history of recent hospitalization or surgery. She receives assistance with her daily activities such as bathing, dressing, and toileting. She has no known history of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) but is at risk due to her prolonged stay in the nursing home. She has no known allergies to medications or environmental factors. She speaks English fluently and has provided informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 30-year-old Hispanic female who previously participated in the "SOPHIE" study. She has been identified as having the F129L non-synonymous variant of OAT3. She has no known history of allergic reactions to cephalosporin antibiotics or severe hypersensitivity to penicillin. She reports no prior history of renal or hepatic dysfunction and is not currently taking any medications that could confound study results. She has consented to participate in the study and is not pregnant, as confirmed by a urine pregnancy test.

The patient is a 65-year-old Taiwanese male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer through biopsy. His PSA value is 3.5 ng/mL, and his Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score is 1. He has not received any hormone therapy, 5-α-reductase inhibitor, or investigational drug within the last 28 days preceding the screening visit. He has no history of severe untreated asthma, anaphylactic reactions, severe urticaria and/or angioedema. He is not considered a candidate for curative therapy, such as radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy. He has no clinically significant disorder other than prostate cancer that may interfere with the trial participation or affect the conclusion of the trial. His life expectancy is more than 168 days.

The patient is a 62-year-old Caucasian man who recently developed a painful rash on his left chest wall. The rash has been present for 5 days and he has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in the affected area. He reports that the pain is sharp and burning in nature and is interfering with his daily activities. He has no history of renal, hepatic diseases, coagulopathy, steroid therapy, or malignancies. He is not currently taking any chemotherapy or radiotherapy. He has not received any treatment for the rash yet. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent.

Pt is a 65yo M with a confirmed diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease made 2 years ago. He reports mild to moderate tremors in his right hand and leg, and he has noticed a slight decrease in his ability to perform activities of daily living such as dressing and grooming. Hoehn & Yahr stage 2. He has no other significant medical or surgical history and takes levodopa/carbidopa 25/100 mg orally three times per day. He has no known allergies to medications, and no previous history of severe hypersensitivity to medications. The patient is able to read and speak English and understands the nature and purpose of the study. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study, and is willing and able to comply with all study procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, diagnosed 5 years ago. The patient's HbA1c levels have been consistently above 7% despite oral anti-diabetic medications. The patient has also been diagnosed with stable cardiomyopathy with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 40%. The patient has not been hospitalized in the cardiology department in the last month before inclusion. The patient has no history of coronary events or symptoms of cardiac ischemia. The patient has not used any antioxidant or anti-inflammatory drugs in the last 6 months prior to inclusion. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding or suffering from acute infectious or inflammatory diseases. The patient is affiliated to a social security scheme and has signed an informed consent form. The patient does not have severe renal insufficiency and is not using drugs that can activate PPARs.

A 28-year-old healthy male is interested in participating in the clinical trial for GSK424887. He works as an accountant and has no underlying disease. He drinks alcohol occasionally, but not to excess. He does not smoke or use any recreational drugs. He is not on any medications. He exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. His past medical history is unremarkable. He has not donated blood within the last 90 days. He is willing to comply with contraceptive requirements during the study period. His average daily caffeine intake is within the protocol requirements.

56-year-old male with a history of heavy alcohol use in his 20s and 30s, who has never been screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. He is due for colorectal cancer (CCR) screening and has not had any symptoms of liver disease. He has a family history of liver cancer in his father, who died at the age of 68. He is currently on treatment for hypertension and has a history of smoking. He is interested in participating in a screening program for HCV and CCR and is open to different screening strategies. He attends a primary care center in one of the selected health areas and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

This is a 62-year-old male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis and portal hypertension who presented to the emergency room with acute onset hematemesis and melena. The patient underwent emergency endoscopy within 12 hours of presentation which confirmed acute esophageal variceal bleeding. The patient was hemodynamically stable and underwent endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) as the primary treatment for the variceal bleeding. After successful arrest of the bleeding, the patient was enrolled in the clinical trial comparing the efficacy of EVL plus somatostatin infusion versus EVL plus losec infusion for 5 days. The patient has no history of gastric variceal bleeding and has never received endoscopic injection sclerotherapy (EIS) or EVL within one month prior to the index bleeding. The patient's Child-Pugh's score is 9, indicating mild liver disease.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was admitted to the UVA medical ICU with a diagnosis of septic shock. He has been receiving norepinephrine infusion at a rate of 10 mcg/min for the past 4 hours to maintain his blood pressure. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has a feeding tube in place for enteral access and is able to tolerate tube feeding. He has no allergies to medications, including midodrine, and has not been taking midodrine prior to admission. He does not have cirrhosis of the liver or any known ocular conditions. His attending physician intends to target a mean arterial pressure of > 65 mmHg. He is able to communicate in English.

The patient is a 68-year-old female who underwent bicompartmental knee arthroplasty 5 days ago. She is a retired teacher with a sedentary lifestyle but otherwise healthy. She has no history of autoimmune or rheumatic diseases, obesity, or diabetes mellitus. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is not taking any anti-inflammatory medication currently. The patient is able to bear weight on the operated knee and is following the hospital's standard analgesic therapy protocol. The vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg and heart rate of 70 bpm. The patient is willing to adhere to a Mediterranean diet during the study period. She has no known allergies or contraindications to the study interventions.

No patient description can be generated for this clinical trial as it is not suitable for individual patients. The trial is seeking to recruit pancreatectomised patients and healthy subjects who meet specific inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study is not designed for individual patients but rather to evaluate the impact of gastrointestinally derived glucagon secretion on postprandial glucose tolerance in a group of patients who have undergone total pancreatectomy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 3 years. He currently takes metformin and a sulfonylurea to manage his blood sugar levels, but his HbA1c is still above 8%. He has a BMI of 32 kg/m² and has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. He has no history of hypoglycemia unawareness, metabolic acidosis, or coronary, carotid, or peripheral artery revascularization procedures. He has not used any investigational drugs in the past month, and he has not used weight loss drugs in the past 3 months. His laboratory findings are within normal limits, with no evidence of liver or kidney dysfunction. He has not had a history of pancreatitis or medullary thyroid cancer. He gives his signed written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with anaplastic astrocytoma 1 year ago. He underwent maximal surgical resection and fractionated external beam radiotherapy. He received one cycle of systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy for initial disease 6 months ago. The patient recently underwent MRI scan which revealed recurrence in the brain. The patient has not received leflunomide (SU101) therapy before. The patient is currently on stable doses of corticosteroids for at least 7 days prior to the MRI scan. The patient is in good general health, with a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. The patient's absolute neutrophil count is above 1,500/mm3, platelet count is above 75,000/mm3, and hemoglobin level is above 9 g/dL. The patient's AST level is within 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) and bilirubin level is less than 1.5 times ULN. The patient's creatinine level is below 2 mg/dL or creatinine clearance is at least 40 mL/min. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and has tested negative for pregnancy. The patient is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 3 months after the study. The patient has no known allergy to etoposide and no other acute or chronic medical illness or psychiatric disorder. The patient has not received epoetin alfa, filgrastim (G-CSF), or sargramostim (GM-CSF) in the past 4 weeks and has recovered from prior chemotherapy for at least 4 weeks. The patient has not received hormonal therapy and has not undergone interstitial radiotherapy or implanted carmustine wafers. The patient has not undergone surgery or biopsy for anaplastic astrocytoma in the past week. The patient has not received any investigational agents in the past 4 weeks and is not receiving any other concurrent investigational agents.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple blunt force injuries. He was rushed to the emergency department with active torso hemorrhage that is not responding to standard treatment. The patient has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it. He is not allergic to any medication, and he does not use any recreational drugs. His vital signs are stable, but he is experiencing severe bleeding that requires immediate attention. The patient is conscious and responsive and has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

This is a 42 year-old healthy female who has not had any symptoms of COVID-19 for the past 3 months. She has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to vaccines in the past. Her body mass index is within the range of 18.5 to 30 kg/m3. She is able to attend all scheduled visits and procedures for the study. She has agreed to use effective contraceptive methods throughout the study and during the observation period for possible post-vaccination reactions. She has not been in contact with COVID-19 patients for 14 days prior to the start of the clinical trial. She does not have any acute or chronic diseases of the cardiovascular, bronchopulmonary, neuroendocrine system, as well as diseases of the gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidneys, surgery on the gastrointestinal tract (except appendectomy). She has not been vaccinated with any vaccine within one month prior to vaccination, taken immunoglobulin drugs or blood products within last 3 months prior to the study, or had any acute infectious or non-communicable diseases, exacerbation of chronic diseases within less than 4 weeks before the start of the study. She has not participated in other clinical trials within less than 3 months prior to the start of this study. She is mentally stable and does not have any history of mental illness or neurasthenia. She has provided a signed and dated informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 60 year old man who has a history of coronary artery disease. He had a heart attack 3 years ago and underwent percutaneous coronary angioplasty (PCI) and stenting. He has been following a strict medication regimen since then and has not experienced any anginal symptoms. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife in a suburban area. He enjoys gardening and taking walks in the park. He has a BMI of 27 and his blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. His resting heart rate is around 70 beats per minute. He does not have any implanted pacemaker, cardioverter, or defibrillator. He has not had any stroke or transient ischemic attack. He is interested in participating in this study to potentially improve his heart health and reduce the risk of future cardiac events.

25-year-old female with a history of mild allergies to penicillin and cephalosporin antibiotics. She presents with a reddish and tender area on her right arm that has been progressively worsening and increasing in size over the past few days. The area is warm to the touch and has some purulent drainage. She denies any recent trauma or insect bites in the area. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical problems. She is not pregnant and has a negative urine pregnancy test. A sample for microbiologic culture was obtained from the primary infection site within 48 hours prior to study drug administration.

A 52-year-old Caucasian female patient presents to the oncology clinic with a recent diagnosis of stage II breast cancer. She has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. Her BMI is 24, and she reports a good performance status with no significant fatigue. The physical examination reveals no remarkable findings. The patient's breast cancer is ER/PR-positive and HER2-negative, and the treatment plan includes four cycles of chemotherapy with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide followed by radiation therapy and hormone therapy. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial and expresses interest in participating in the study to potentially alleviate chemotherapy-related fatigue. She provides informed consent and is enrolled in the study. During the screening interview, she reports mild fatigue, and the Brief Fatigue Inventory questionnaire shows a score of 3 out of 10. She is deemed eligible to proceed with the study and is randomized to receive either Guaraná extract or a placebo. The patient is followed up closely throughout the study period, and her cancer diagnosis, treatment history, and concurrent medication are recorded at each visit.

A 25-year-old male comes to the clinic seeking help for his alcohol dependence. He has been drinking heavily for the past two years, and he has tried to quit multiple times but has been unsuccessful. He is currently drinking about six to eight beers per day. He reports experiencing withdrawal symptoms, including tremors and anxiety, when he tries to quit. He has no other significant medical or psychiatric history. He is currently unemployed and living with his parents. He is literate in English and expresses a willingness to participate in behavioral treatments for alcoholism. He is not taking any medications and has no known allergies. He has no plans to move in the next three months. He is not pregnant, lactating, or using any form of contraception. He is willing to participate in a 13-week clinical trial and receive weekly CBT sessions.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease for the past 5 years. She has a medical history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. She has tried different medications, including corticosteroids and immunosuppressive agents, but they did not provide adequate relief. She has also noticed that certain foods worsen her symptoms and has been trying to identify them on her own. She avoids dairy products, wheat, and beef, but she is not sure if they are the only triggers. She has been referred to this study by her gastroenterologist to determine if certain food antigens are associated with her condition. The patient has no known drug allergies and has not received TNF-α inhibitors. She is willing to undergo blood tests to detect IgG antibodies to different food antigens and eliminate them from her diet if necessary. She understands that this study is aimed at identifying potential food triggers for IBD and may help her manage her symptoms better.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the rectum three months ago. He has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but the tumor is still inoperable. He is experiencing abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, and changes in bowel habits. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He is not on any other medications. He has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG/WHO scale. His current thrombocyte count is 80 billions/l and INR is 1.1. He has been offered the standard of care and all available alternatives but wants to explore other treatment options. The multidisciplinary team has agreed that an endoscopic treatment with calcium electroporation may be suitable for him. He understands the possible risks and benefits of the treatment and has signed the informed consent. He has no coagulative disturbances and is not pregnant or lactating. He has not participated in any other clinical trial involving experimental drugs within the last 4 weeks.

A 42-year-old Chinese male with a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis established at least 3 months prior to screening by clinical and endoscopic evidence corroborated by a histopathology report. He has moderately to severely active UC as determined by a complete Mayo score of 7 with an endoscopic subscore of 3 within 10 days prior to the first dose of study drug. He has evidence of UC extending proximal to the rectum (≥15 cm of involved colon) and has a family history of colorectal cancer. The patient has demonstrated an inadequate response to immunomodulators and corticosteroids. He has not been exposed to any approved or investigational anti-integrins, mucosal addressin cell adhesion molecule-1 (MAdCAM-1) antagonist, or rituximab. He has not used a topical (rectal) treatment with 5-acetyl salicylic acid (5-ASA) or corticosteroid enemas/suppositories or traditional Chinese medications for treatment of UC within 2 weeks of the administration of the first dose of study drug. The patient does not have evidence of abdominal abscess or toxic megacolon at the initial screening visit and has not had extensive colonic resection, subtotal or total colectomy. He has no existing ileostomy or colostomy, nor known fixed symptomatic stenosis of the intestine. The patient is not anticipated to require surgical intervention for UC during the study. He has no history or evidence of adenomatous colonic polyps that have not been removed, or has a history or evidence of colonic mucosal dysplasia including low or high-grade dysplasia, as well as indeterminate for dysplasia. He has no suspected or confirmed diagnosis of Crohn's enterocolitis, indeterminate colitis, ischemic colitis, radiation colitis, diverticular disease associated with colitis, or microscopic colitis. The patient has no evidence of or has had treatment for C. difficile infection or other intestinal pathogen within 28 days prior to randomization. He has no chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection or chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. He does not have active or latent TB. The patient does not have any identified congenital or acquired immunodeficiency, any history of malignancy, and major neurological disorders.

Patient is a 62-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset left-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. CT scan revealed a right-sided ischemic stroke. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no prior history of stroke. He is currently receiving standard of care treatment for his stroke, including intravenous thrombolysis and anticoagulation therapy. The patient is able to provide oral consent to participate in the trial during the acute phase, and has signed the informed consent form after the acute phase of care is completed. There are no other conditions that prevent the patient from entering the study, according to the investigator's judgment.

A 54-year-old male presented to the emergency department with severe chest pain and shortness of breath. He had a past medical history significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia and smoking. On arrival, he had an acute anterolateral ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement in the left anterior descending (LAD) artery. Post-procedure, he was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for close monitoring and was transferred to the clinical unit after 3 days. His vital signs were stable and he was started on dual antiplatelet therapy, statin, beta-blocker, and ACE inhibitor. He denied any history of neurological disease or congenital heart disease. He was informed about the study and agreed to participate.

A 27-year-old pregnant woman, who is a first-time mother, is admitted to the labor and delivery unit. She is in active labor and has requested epidural analgesia for pain relief. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated with a reassuring fetal heart tracing. She is able to read, comprehend, and sign the informed consent form. She has no contraindication to epidural anesthesia and no history of chronic pain or spinal pathology. The cervical dilation is less than 7cm at the time of admission. She is eligible for this clinical trial and has consented to participation.

A 7-year-old male patient with a history of asthma and recurrent episodes of bronchitis who presents with severe cough and shortness of breath. The patient has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 24 hours and is currently unable to tolerate oral intake. The patient's parents report that the patient may have inhaled a foreign object while playing with small toys. A chest x-ray reveals a partially obstructed right mainstem bronchus. The patient is scheduled to undergo a rigid bronchoscopy for the removal of the foreign object. The patient has no known allergies and is otherwise healthy.

55 year old female with a history of hypertension and chest pain who underwent cardiac catheterization showing a nondilated left ventricle with mild hypertrophy and normal systolic function. She was diagnosed with HCM after further testing with echocardiography revealed a maximal LV wall thickness of 17 mm. She has been asymptomatic but is being followed closely with serial echocardiograms to monitor for changes in her LVH. She has a family history of HCM, with her mother being diagnosed at a young age and her brother also having left ventricular hypertrophy. She is interested in participating in the study to determine whether her genetics may play a role in her condition and to potentially help future patients with HCM. She is able and willing to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

Pt is a 28yo F with no significant medical history, non-smoker, and BMI of 21 kg/m2. She has no history of pulmonary disease, atopic reactions, or significant concurrent illnesses. She has not consumed alcohol, caffeine, or engaged in strenuous exercise within the past 72 hours, nor has she consumed grapefruit within the past 7 days. She has not been exposed to any investigational agents within the past 30 days and has tested negative for drugs of abuse. She is willing to practice contraception during the study period as she has a male partner. She is able to tolerate a nebulization test with sterile water for injection.

The patient is a 56-year-old Chinese man who has been experiencing sudden weakness on the right side of his body for the past 2 hours. He is unable to move his right arm and leg, and has difficulty speaking. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but is not on any medications for these conditions. He smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. His family history is negative for stroke or any other neurological conditions. He lives with his wife and two children and works as a construction worker. Upon arrival at the hospital, a CT scan confirms that he has suffered an ischemic stroke. He is eligible for this clinical trial as he has reached the hospital within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing recurrent pain and discomfort in the anal region for the past year.
