He has noticed that there is a small opening near his anus which occasionally drains pus or blood. The pain is often worse during bowel movements and he has noticed some difficulty controlling bowel movements in the past few months. He has tried conservative management with sitz baths and over-the-counter pain relievers, but the symptoms have persisted. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Physical examination reveals a small opening near the anus with some surrounding inflammation. The patient is otherwise healthy and willing to undergo surgical treatment for the anal fistula.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who weighs 170lbs. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is willing to participate in the research study and has provided informed consent. He meets all the inclusion criteria, and there are no exclusion criteria applicable to him.

45-year-old female office worker who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 6 months, which has been interfering with her daily activities. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, physical therapy, and chiropractic treatment but has not experienced any significant relief. She reports no history of inner ear infections or cerebral trauma. She has not undergone any vestibular disorder treatment in the last 6 months. She is not currently on pain medication. She is interested in participating in the mental imagery portion of the study as an adjunct to her current treatment plan.

The patient is a 70-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. He presents with dysphagia, weight loss, and chest pain that started three months ago. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows a large mass in the middle third of the esophagus with biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma. The CT scan of the chest and abdomen shows T3N0M0 esophageal adenocarcinoma. The patient is not a surgical candidate and ineligible for chemotherapy due to neuropathy, cardiac disease, and performance status 2. The patient has ECOG performance status 1 and the life expectancy is anticipated to be more than 4 months. The patient has never been treated with chemotherapy or radiotherapy for this tumor. The patient is willing to participate and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study.

A 38-year-old man with a BMI of 32, and a family history of hypertension, comes to the clinic for a routine check-up. He is currently not taking any medications and has no known allergies. He has never been diagnosed with any chronic conditions such as diabetes, COPD or kidney disease. His blood pressure is within normal limits. He works a sedentary job and has not been exercising regularly. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of acetazolamide and furosemide on obesity-induced glomerular hyperfiltration.

A 55-year-old man presented with a history of chronic low back pain, which has been present for over a year. The pain is exacerbated by standing or walking, and he reports bilateral buttock, thigh, and calf discomfort. He has tried various conservative treatments, including medications and physical therapy, but has not experienced significant relief. He underwent an MRI of the lumbar spine, which showed lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and is able to comply with home exercises as prescribed. His BMI is 30, and he is able to tolerate a 6-min treadmill test. He has not had any knee surgeries in the past 6 months and does not have any psychiatric disorders that would prevent him from participating in assigned physical therapy sessions.

A 7-year-old boy named Max is being recruited for a clinical trial testing the effectiveness of smoke alarms in awakening children from stage 4 sleep. Max lives with his parents and younger sister in a suburban home. He is in good health and has no history of any sleep disorders. Max's family speaks English and he is able to communicate effectively

A 45 year old female patient presents with headaches, confusion, and difficulty with balance over the past few weeks. Imaging studies reveal a high grade glioma. She has a Karnofsky Performance Score (KPS) of 80 and is able to read and write. She has no prior history of brain tumors or neurological disabilities. She has no major comorbidities and is not currently on any medications. She is willing to fill out quality of life questionnaires and is able to tolerate the fluid load associated with the study medication. She is not pregnant or nursing, and has not been treated with other investigational drugs within the last 30 days. She has no hypersensitivity to Temozolomide and/or Dacarbazine.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has a family history of heart disease. He is generally healthy and does not have any chronic medical conditions. The patient is currently taking a multivitamin and occasionally uses over-the-counter pain medication for headaches. He does not currently use any Omega-3 supplements but is interested in potentially adding them to his regimen for their possible cardioprotective effects. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and is motivated to participate in the study to potentially improve his heart health.

45-year-old female diagnosed with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and previously participated in the clinical trials of Eculizumab (JSC "GENERIUM"). She has been on Eculizumab therapy for the past 6 months and has shown significant improvement in the quality of life with a decrease in hemolysis and the incidence of thrombosis. The patient has been vaccinated against meningococcal infection and is willing to undergo booster vaccination while participating in this research. She has provided written informed consent to participate in this multicenter open-label study of the safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy of Eculizumab (JSC "GENERIUM") in patients with PNH who completed participation in previous clinical trials of Eculizumab (JSC "GENERIUM"). She is willing to use a reliable method of contraception during the study period. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the study drug or the vaccine for the prevention of meningococcal infection. She has no comorbidities or conditions that may put her safety at risk while participating in the study. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or addicted to alcohol, drugs or any other substances.

49-year-old female with chronic knee pain in the right knee for at least 6 months. The patient reports difficulty walking and climbing stairs due to pain. The patient has a history of meniscectomy in the right knee. Physical examination revealed tenderness of the medial tibiofemoral joint. X-rays show a Kellgren-Lawrence Score of 3 in the medial compartment of the right knee. MRI shows evidence of bone marrow edema in the medial compartment of the right knee. The patient has tried conservative treatments such as pharmacological therapy and physiotherapy, but these have not provided long-lasting relief. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and attend all follow-up appointments and radiographic evaluations. The patient does not have any concurrent rheumatic or immunological diseases or malignancies, and has not undergone surgical treatment in the right knee within the last 12 months. The patient's BMI is within the range of eligibility for the trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing episodes of unexplained syncope for the past six months. He has undergone various medical tests, including ECGs and echocardiograms, but no underlying cause has been found. His doctor has recommended an implanted loop recorder (ILR) to monitor his heart activity and detect any abnormal rhythms that may be causing his syncope. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of remote monitoring (RM) and patient-centered alarm settings in patients with ILR. He is willing to provide informed consent and is committed to attending follow-up visits as required by the study protocol.

A 35-year-old male with a 10-year history of plaque psoriasis affecting 10% of his body surface area, including his scalp, arms, and legs. He has tried multiple topical agents in the past with little to no improvement in his symptoms. He has not used any systemic treatments for his psoriasis. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker, social drinker, and is not currently sexually active. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements and restrictions of the study, including the use of effective contraception during the study period.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with GH deficiency. He was previously enrolled in the NCGS Core Study 85-036 and is currently receiving treatment with a GH dose of 0.5 mg/kg/week. He is now at Tanner Stage 2 with testes measuring 4 mL. He has no history of diabetes or cancer. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in this clinical trial and remain on therapy until epiphyseal closure is achieved. They are also able to attend follow-up appointments throughout the study.

16 year-old female who is the older sister of a 12 year-old brother with ASD. She has been experiencing increased stress and anxiety related to her brother's condition and feels overwhelmed at times. She has access to a smartphone and the internet, and is an English speaker. She has not been hospitalized for any psychiatric conditions in the past year.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B. He has a family history of liver disease, and he is concerned about his long-term health. He has not received any previous treatment for his condition, and his current HBV DNA level is greater than 10^5 copies/ml. He is currently experiencing mild fatigue and occasional abdominal discomfort. His ALT levels are within normal limits, and he has no evidence of cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol only occasionally. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He is employed as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore potential treatment options for his condition.

A 50-year-old female patient came to the clinic with a history of knee pain for the past 6 months. She describes the pain as a dull ache that gets worse when walking or standing for long periods of time. The pain is located in both knees, but is worse in the left knee. She reports difficulty with daily activities such as climbing stairs and kneeling. She has no history of knee injuries or surgeries. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is not currently taking any medication for knee pain. Physical examination revealed mild swelling and tenderness in both knees. Range of motion was slightly limited in the left knee. X-rays showed mild osteoarthritis in both knees according to Ahlback's classification. She met all the inclusion criteria and did not meet any of the exclusion criteria, except that she has a history of hypertension.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese man who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus five years ago. His HbA1c level is 8.2%, and he is currently on oral hypoglycemic agents. His BMI is 27 kg/m2, and he has no history of diabetic coma, precoma, or ketoacidosis. He has no renal impairment or clinically significant renal disease. His fasting plasma glucose level is 160 mg/dL, and he is compliant with his current medication regimen. He does not have any other significant medical history or current medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. He is interested in participating in this study to help advance research for the treatment of type 2 diabetes.

A 40-year-old female has recently been diagnosed with cutaneous melanoma at the Dermatology Department of the Nice University Hospital. She has noticed an irregularly shaped, dark-colored mole on her upper back that has been growing in size over the last few months. The dermatologist has recommended surgical resection of the melanoma for a complete diagnosis and treatment. The patient has social security affiliation and is willing to participate in the study. She has no contraindications for surgical resection and is not pregnant or nursing.

A 35-year-old male veteran has a history of felony conviction for drug abuse and possession. He was released from prison three months ago and is now living in a halfway house. He has a diagnosis of bipolar disorder and opioid use disorder. The patient reports feeling depressed, anxious, and having difficulty with attention and concentration. He has been attending group therapy and individual counseling sessions for his mental health and substance use issues. He has expressed interest in finding employment, but feels discouraged by his criminal history and lack of recent work experience. He has been receiving vocational services through the halfway house but has not yet found employment. He is motivated to participate in this study to improve his chances of finding employment and to receive ongoing support. The patient does not have any signs of dementia or active psychosis.

The patient is a 55 year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and chronic hepatitis C. He was recently diagnosed with liver cirrhosis and has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. His liver function tests are abnormal and he has a Child-Pugh score of B. He is currently on medication to manage his liver disease. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol anymore. He is married and has two adult children. He has no significant past medical history or allergies. He has been recommended to undergo a surgical intervention for a non-hepatic medical condition and has been informed about the risk of developing acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

45 yo F with a BMI of 45 kg/m2, diagnosed with morbid obesity, is scheduled for bariatric surgery in the next month. She has a history of hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea, which is currently being treated with continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. She takes lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension. She has no history of neuromuscular diseases and is not currently taking any drugs that could interfere with neuromuscular transmission. She has no known allergies to neuromuscular agents of the aminosteroids class. She has been advised of the study and has signed an informed consent to participate. Her renal function is normal. She is a suitable candidate for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has completed curative-intent radiation therapy for head and neck cancer at MD Anderson Cancer Center in the past 15 years. He has been referred to the Section of Speech Pathology and Audiology for swallowing evaluation. The patient has no history of recurrent or second primary H&N, central nervous system, or thoracic cancer at the time of modified barium swallow (MBS) study. He has not undergone previous H&N surgery excluding diagnostic procedures, transoral surgery, or non-radical neck dissection. The patient has no functionally limiting chronic or acute cardiac, pulmonary, or neuromuscular disease and is not tracheotomy or oxygen dependent at the time of MBS. He has a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 28 and has the ability to understand and willingness to sign written informed consent.

A 50-year-old female with advanced ovarian cancer who has been experiencing severe nausea and vomiting despite receiving standard antiemetic medications. The patient has failed two medications for nausea and vomiting and is still experiencing breakthrough emesis. The patient has adequate organ function and a calculated creatinine clearance of 50 mL/min. The patient is expected to have a life expectancy of more than one month and is able to read Thai. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to sign an informed consent document. The patient has not received abdominal radiotherapy or chemotherapy within the last week and is not taking fluoxetine. The patient does not have a history of heart failure or myocardial infarction in the past 6 months and has a normal QTc interval on ECG.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been struggling with methamphetamine addiction for the past 2 years. He is currently unemployed and has difficulty maintaining relationships with family and friends due to his addiction. He has tried to quit on his own but experiences severe withdrawal symptoms such as fatigue, depression, and intense cravings that lead to relapse. He is otherwise healthy with no history of asthma or convulsions. He currently uses methamphetamine daily and is motivated to quit. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and sign the informed consent form.

56-year-old male with a history of high-grade upper urinary tract transitional cell carcinoma (UUTTCC) that was completely ablated with ureteroscopy or antegrade percutaneous access. The patient is unwilling or unfit to undergo radical nephroureterectomy. The patient has a performance status of 0-1 on the ECOG Performance Scale and has adequate organ function, as demonstrated by screening labs performed within 28 days of treatment initiation. The patient has provided tissue from an archival tissue sample or newly obtained core or excisional biopsy of a tumor lesion. The patient has not received prior systemic chemotherapy, targeted small molecule therapy, or radiation therapy for UUTTCC, but has confirmed recurrence of the disease after previous treatment. The patient is not currently undergoing treatment for active or progressive metastatic disease, has not received monoclonal antibody therapy within 4 weeks prior to study Day 1, and has not had active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the past 2 years. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, expecting to conceive or father children within the projected duration of the trial, and has not received prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137, or anti-CTLA-4 antibody. The patient does not have a known history of HIV or active Hepatitis B or C, tuberculosis, or muscle invasive renal pelvis cancer or transitional cell carcinoma of the upper urinary tract.

Pt is an 80yo M living in his own home with a history of falls, including a fall resulting in a hip fracture last year. He is concerned about his balance and has limited mobility due to chronic knee pain. He reports feeling unsteady on his feet and has had near falls recently. He is currently taking medication for hypertension and high cholesterol. He is willing to participate in a fall injury prevention study and meets the inclusion criteria of being at least 70 years of age and answering 'yes' to one or more of the following questions: Have you fallen and hurt yourself in the past year? Have you fallen 2 or more times in the past year? Are you afraid that you might fall because of balance or walking problems? He is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer. She underwent a mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Despite treatment, her cancer has progressed and she now has metastases to the liver, lungs, and bones. She has no other treatment options available to her and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. The patient reports a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She denies any history of cardiovascular disease or cerebrovascular disease. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG PS) is 1. Her lab studies show: Hemoglobin: 11.5 g/dL White blood cell count: 6.2 x 10^9/L Platelet count: 199 x 10^9/L Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL Aspartate aminotransferase (AST): 27 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT): 29 U/L Total bilirubin: 0.9 mg/dL Alkaline phosphatase: 75 U/L

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of Child-Pugh Class C liver cirrhosis. He reports fatigue, abdominal pain, and swelling in his legs. He has a history of alcohol abuse and has been abstinent for 6 months. He is not currently taking any selenium supplements. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine if selenium supplementation can improve his nutritional status and alleviate his symptoms. He is willing to take the assigned supplement and follow the study protocol. His renal function is within normal limits, and he does not have an urgent need for liver transplant.

44-year-old female with a history of recurrent anal fistulas was referred to undergo evaluation for participation in a clinical trial. The patient reported chronic pain, swelling, and discomfort in the perianal area. She has a history of hypertension and obesity with a BMI of 33. She has undergone multiple attempts at fistula closure with no success. The patient has not been a smoker for the past 6 months and is not currently pregnant. She has no known history of active tuberculosis, insulin-dependent diabetes, or prior pelvic irradiation. The patient has undergone an MRI scan to confirm the presence of high trans-sphincteric fistulas. A seton has been placed for more than 6 weeks prior to fat injection. The patient has provided informed, written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

This clinical trial is not applicable for patients as it is focused on creating a proficiency-based virtual reality simulation training programme for laparoscopic assisted colectomy for surgical trainees. Therefore, no patient description is needed.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy to remove the tumor and is now considering radiation therapy as a follow-up treatment. She is concerned about the side-effects of traditional radiation therapy, including skin burns and fatigue. She is interested in exploring alternative options that may be less invasive and have fewer side-effects. She lives with her husband and has two grown children. She works as a part-time accountant and enjoys spending time with her family and friends. She is generally in good health and has no significant medical history. She has a BMI of 25 and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that is investigating the use of permanent breast seed implant (PBSI) as a form of partial breast irradiation. She understands that this is a relatively new technique and that more research is needed to evaluate its safety and effectiveness. She is willing to undergo the procedure and participate in the registry study to help advance the field of breast cancer treatment.

A 16-year-old female diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) by a rheumatologist according to ILAR criteria. She has been experiencing arthritis-related pain during regular activities, with a pain score of 50 on a 100-millimeter (mm) visual analogue scale (VAS) in the past month. She is currently on a JIA specific medication regimen that is not expected to change during the study period. She reports not meeting Health Canada's and American College of Sports Medicine's guidelines for physical activity (<60 minutes of moderate to vigorous PA per day) and is not using physical interventions/treatments other than medication prescribed for JIA pain relief or over the counter medication. She understands English and is capable of using and accessing the Internet weekly for the study duration. She has no contraindications to exercise according to the treating rheumatologist.

The patient is a 60 year old Hispanic male who has been diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. He has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and has a history of high blood pressure and elevated triglyceride levels. He is currently taking medication for hypertension. He reports feeling tired and low on energy throughout the day. He has a history of lactose intolerance and avoids dairy products. He works as a construction worker and leads an active lifestyle. He enjoys eating meat and vegetables, but has difficulty controlling his portion sizes. He is willing to participate in a dietary intervention study to improve his metabolic health. He does not have a history of diabetes, cancer, or any other chronic inflammatory conditions.

Pt is a 10yo M diagnosed with ADHD per DSM-5 criteria. He participated in a previous randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of TNS for ADHD, and was randomized to the sham condition. The patient is currently not taking any medication with CNS effects. The patient has parents who are able and willing to monitor proper use of the TNS device and complete all required rating scales. Both the parent and participant are able to complete study rating scales and other measures in English. The patient is interested in participating in the 4-week open-trial of TNS to potentially benefit from the active intervention. The patient will receive nightly active TNS during sleep and return for clinic assessments at Weeks 2 and 4. If the patient achieves clinically significant improvement from active TNS over the 4-week open trial, he may be invited to receive a year of nightly active-TNS therapy as part of a 12-month extension study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer and is scheduled to undergo a pulmonary lobectomy via open thoracotomy. He has a history of moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is currently taking inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids. His pain levels are at a 7 out of 10 on the pain scale and he has a history of opioid intolerance. The patient has been informed about the option of participating in a clinical trial for pain control after surgery using peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS) of the intercostal nerves. The patient is interested in participating in the trial and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

Catherine is a 50-year-old female who was diagnosed with colon cancer two years ago. She underwent surgery, followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Her cancer was in remission until she developed abdominal pain and weight loss a month ago. She was seen by her oncologist and underwent imaging studies that showed metastatic lesions in her liver. Catherine's MSI-H/dMMR status was confirmed by the central laboratory. She has completed first-line therapy with FOLFOX (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, and oxaliplatin) but has experienced documented disease progression. She has an ECOG of 1 and no other significant medical history. Her lab studies are within normal limits. She has agreed to effective contraception during the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman from a rural community in North-Central Nigeria has just tested positive for HIV during her antenatal care visit. She has never been tested before and is unaware of her status. She is married and has two children. Her husband is a farmer and they live in a small village where health services are limited. She has never received any ARV prophylaxis or treatment for HIV. She is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and is worried about the health of her unborn child. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive integrated PMTCT services and hopes that this will improve her chances of having a healthy baby.

32-year-old healthy male with no history of chronic alcohol consumption or drug addiction. He has no serious gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic or cardiovascular disease, tuberculosis, epilepsy, asthma (during the past 5 years), diabetes, psychosis or glaucoma. He has not taken any investigational drug within thirty (30) days prior to the first dosing of the study. He has not donated blood and/or plasma for at least thirty (30) days prior to the first dosing of the study. He has no history of allergic responses to the class of drug being tested. He is willing to abstain from sexual intercourse or use a reliable barrier method (e.g.condom, IUD) of contraception during the course of the study (first dosing until last blood collection). He has no implanted or injected hormonal contraceptives use in the past 6 months or oral hormonal contraceptives within 14 days before dosing. He is willing to provide urine samples to be assayed for the presence of drugs of abuse as part of the clinical laboratory screening procedures and at each check-in. He has normal clinical laboratory measurements including HIV and Hepatitis-B, C Screen. He has no clinical laboratory test values that are greater than 20% outside the normal range.

56 year old woman with a history of maxillofacial bone loss due to a large cyst in her jaw. She has had the cyst removed and is now seeking a bone grafting procedure to fill the void left behind. She is in good general health, with no history of diabetes, heart disease, or renal failure. She has good oral hygiene and is a non-smoker. She is not currently taking any medications that would exclude her from participating in the study. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is able to understand the study procedures and agree to follow-up procedures. She has up-to-date panoramic X-rays and meets the inclusion criteria for bone grafting after removal of cysts from jaws.

The patient is a 65 year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago. He underwent radiation therapy, and his PSA levels were monitored regularly. His latest PSA level showed a rise above his nadir level plus 2 ng/ml, indicating a possible biochemical recurrence. He has not experienced any symptoms related to the recurrence. He has no significant medical history, and he is not taking any medication on a regular basis. He has no known allergies to medications or contrast agents. He has no contraindications to MRI or endorectal examination. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the IRB-approved informed consent.

This is a 47-year-old right-handed female who suffered a moderate traumatic brain injury (TBI) in a car accident approximately two years ago. She has since developed chronic aphasia, as confirmed by the Aachener Aphasie Test (AAT). She has not seen any improvement in her language abilities despite undergoing standard speech therapy. She has no history of dementia or other neurological diseases, severe alcoholism, or drug use. She also does not have any severe untreated medical problems such as cancer. She has not had any severe psychiatric disorders such as depression or psychosis, and if she did, they are currently in remission. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates whether a tDCS-accompanied intensive naming therapy can improve her language abilities.

This is a 25 year old female who is in good health and has no significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help better understand the metabolism of CYP2D6 in healthy individuals. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She understands French and is able to provide written informed consent. She meets the eligibility criteria for this study as her BMI is within the acceptable range and she has a CYP2D6 genotype activity score of ≥1 (EMs-UMs). She is using reliable contraception and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not participated in any other interventional clinical studies within the past 3 months.

The patient is a 40 year old man who received a kidney transplant one year ago at the University Hospital of Montpellier. He has been experiencing some mild symptoms like fatigue and intermittent lower back pain for the past few weeks. During routine check-up, his physician noticed the presence of a de novo DSA and recommended a graft biopsy to assess the risk of antibody mediated rejection. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed the informed consent form. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies or medical conditions. He is not pregnant or lactating and is not a vulnerable person. He has a social security scheme and is willing to provide a plasma sample on the day of graft biopsy for future use in research programs.

A 28-year-old male who is a soldier in the French Army presents with ringing in both ears and hearing loss after an explosion in the field. He reports being exposed to loud noise during training exercises regularly. He denies any history of hearing problems or ear infections. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. On examination, there is no visible damage to the external ear or tympanic membrane, but pure tone audiometry shows significant hearing loss in the high-frequency range. He is diagnosed with acute acoustic trauma and is enrolled in the clinical trial within 72 hours of the injury.

A 56-year-old man arrived at the emergency department due to a sudden onset of weakness and difficulty speaking. He is married and has two children. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol moderately. He has a family history of stroke, with his father having suffered from a stroke at the age of 65. He works as a construction worker and does not exercise regularly. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. His medical history includes hypertension that is treated with medication. His last medical checkup was three years ago. He is able to understand and give consent for the study.

A 20-year-old woman is interested in participating in the Personalized Nutrition in Young Adults study. She is a full-time university student and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She has no known allergies and likes to eat fish occasionally. She is not currently taking any medication and has no history of chronic illnesses. She is interested in learning more about her genetic information and how it may affect her diet and health. She lives in the same city as the University of Guelph and is able to attend study visits. She is comfortable with giving blood samples for the study. She is not planning to become pregnant in the near future.

54-year-old man diagnosed with low-grade B-cell lymphoma of the cervical lymph nodes. The patient has previously undergone radiation therapy and is currently in a partial response. The patient is in good overall health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has at least one site of disease that is accessible for intratumoral injection of SD-101. The patient has at least one site of measurable disease, other than the injection site, which is not included in the radiation field. The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is greater than or equal to 1000/mm^3 independent of growth factor support, platelets are greater than or equal to 100,000/mm^3 or greater than or equal to 50,000/mm^3 if known or suspected bone marrow involvement, and hemoglobin is greater than or equal to 8 g/dL (may be transfused). The patient's creatinine clearance is greater than 25 ml/min, and the aspartate aminotransferase (AST)/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are less than or equal to 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN). The patient's bilirubin levels are less than or equal to 1.5 x ULN. The patient has not been treated with standard or investigational chemotherapy, biochemotherapy, surgery, radiation, cytokine therapy, any monoclonal antibodies, or immunotherapy for at least 4 weeks and has recovered from any clinically significant toxicity experienced during treatment. The patient is willing to comply with the treatment schedule and has the ability to understand and sign a written informed consent document.

32 F admitted to Butler Hospital for severe depression and suicidal ideation. Patient has a history of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and has been on antipsychotic medications for the past 5 years. She is a current smoker, smoking 1 pack per day, and expresses a desire to quit smoking during her hospitalization. She is able to give written informed consent and meets the age criteria for the study. She has no known adverse reactions to varenicline and is not currently taking varenicline or undergoing dialysis. Her renal function is normal. She will be assessed with the QIDS-SR16, Minnesota Nicotine Withdrawal Scale, and FISER at baseline and daily during the trial. She has expressed a willingness to continue varenicline post-discharge if it helps decrease her nicotine cravings.

A 45-year-old female cancer survivor living in a rural area, with a history of breast cancer, is interested in participating in Project EXCEL. She completed her cancer treatment 2 years ago and has been struggling with fatigue and weight gain since then. She is physically able to participate in mild levels of activity and is interested in starting an exercise program that is tailored to her needs. She has access to the internet and is comfortable with participating in online exercise programs if necessary. She is fluent in English and is excited to become a lifelong exerciser to improve her overall health and wellbeing.

28 yo female who has been using marijuana for the past 5 years, typically smoking 2-3 times per day. She has tried to quit using marijuana several times in the past year but has been unable to do so without formal treatment. She reports experiencing withdrawal symptoms such as irritability, anxiety, and difficulty sleeping during her previous attempts to quit. She is interested in participating in this study to help identify effective quitting strategies and to better understand her withdrawal symptoms. She speaks English fluently and is able to give valid informed consent.

The patient is a 24-year-old male student of Health Care Professions who is a regular smoker, smoking more than 10 cigarettes per day for the past 3 years. He also consumes caffeine on a daily basis. He has no known chronic diseases or cardiovascular problems. He is interested in participating in a study investigating the accumulation of AGEs (advanced glycation end-products) in the tissues of individuals who smoke in comparison with individuals who do not, as well as the effect of caffeine consumption on AGEs levels. He is informed that the study will involve non-invasive measurement of haemodynamic parameters, such as cardiac output, stroke volume, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, mean pressure, pulse rate, interbeat intervals, arterial compliance and systemic vascular resistance, using the Finometer device. Additionally, skin-autofluorescence measurements will be taken to assess tissue AGEs accumulation using the AGE Reader device. He is willing to abstain from smoking for 2 hours prior to measurements, and to abstain from any physical activity on the day of the scheduled measurements. He gives his informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who has no previous medical history or significant illnesses. She is currently not on any medication and has not taken any glucocorticoid therapy in the past. She has no history of allergies to any medications. She is surgically sterile and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of escalating doses of oral PF-04308515. She understands the nature of the study and has given informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with a body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m2 and a body weight of 70 kg. He has no history of diabetes or any other significant medical conditions. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has no known allergies to medications or food. He works as an accountant and leads an active lifestyle, exercising regularly and eating a healthy diet. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help further the development of a new medication that could potentially help people with type 2 diabetes. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He is available to participate in the study for the entire duration and is willing to undergo all the necessary tests and procedures.

58-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of primary osteoarthritis of the right hip. The patient's medical history includes hypertension, for which they take amlodipine 5mg once daily, and hyperlipidemia, for which they take atorvastatin 20mg once daily. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. They have never had any surgeries in the past. The patient denies any history of alcohol or opioid abuse. They are not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study. They have been advised of the risks and benefits of the study and have agreed to participate.

54-year-old male with a history of smoking and an unresectable laryngeal neoplasm that has been diagnosed by positive biopsy. The patient has been assessed by an oncologist and is deemed unsuitable for surgical resection. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1 and a prothrombin time ratio of 60%. The platelet count is 90x10^9/L. The patient is currently taking anti-platelet therapy but is willing and able to stop the medication for seven days prior to and seven days post NanoKnife procedure. The patient is able to comprehend and willing to sign the written informed consent form (ICF) and has a life expectancy of at least 6 months. The patient has no history of cardiac insufficiency, ongoing coronary artery disease or arrhythmia, and has no active implanted devices. The patient is not pregnant nor a woman of child-bearing potential. The patient has not received treatment with an investigational agent/procedure within 30 days prior to treatment with the NanoKnife™ LEDC System and is able to comply with the visit schedule and protocol evaluations.

35-year-old male, presented to the hospital with complaints of fever, weight loss, and fatigue for the past two months. He had no significant medical history, and was not on any medications. He reported no recent travel history, but had been living in an endemic VL region in India for the past year. Physical examination revealed hepatosplenomegaly, and laboratory investigations showed pancytopenia, elevated liver enzymes, and elevated serum creatinine levels. A spleen aspirate was performed, which confirmed the diagnosis of VL. The patient was HIV negative and had no other intercurrent diseases that may affect the outcome of the study. The patient has no history of allergy or hypersensitivity to amphotericin B, and no previous treatment for VL within two weeks of enrollment into the study. The proteinuria was negative. The patient was willing to participate in the clinical trial and met all the inclusion criteria.

This is a 42-year-old male who was diagnosed with sporadic ALS approximately 18 months ago. He has been on a stable dose of riluzole for the past six months and has not taken any fluoroquinolone antibiotics for at least 30 days prior to screening. He has not been diagnosed with any other neurodegenerative diseases and does not have any significant pulmonary or central nervous system disorders. He has no history of tendinopathy or any severe uncontrolled medical conditions other than ALS. The patient does not have any allergies to fluoroquinolones and has not been enrolled in any other clinical trials involving experimental drugs or devices. His forced vital capacity (FVC) is greater than 50 percent predicted.

Patient is a 35-year-old man with a history of type 1 diabetes for 10 years. He is affiliated to Social Security and is currently under ambulatory medical follow-up. He has not had any ketoacidosis episode or hypoglycaemia with loss of consciousness requiring the intervention of a third person during the previous month. The patient is able to move around freely and is not bedridden. He has provided written consent to participate in the study. The patient is not pregnant, parturient or breastfeeding. He is not a prisoner, hospitalized without consent or protected by the Law. The patient is not terminally ill and does not have any physical or psychological health issues that could interfere with obtaining informed consent and compliance to the protocol.

This is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 2 years. Despite being on a stable regimen of dopaminergic antipsychotic medication, she continues to experience residual symptoms, including auditory hallucinations and disorganized thinking, with a PANSS total score of 90. She has no history of antipsychotic treatment resistance and is not currently taking clozapine. She has no history of moderate to severe alcohol or substance use disorder within the past 6 months and has tested negative for HIV and hepatitis B virus. She has no history of renal disease or currently taking any medications to treat renal disease.

The patient is an 8-year-old girl complaining of sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes. She experiences these symptoms every year during the pollen season. She has no other medical conditions and is not on any medication. Her parents are willing to participate in the study and can comply with the procedures. They understand the dosing and visit schedules and can report any adverse events to the investigator. The girl has a positive skin prick test for grasses and birch and has a total symptom score of 10 with a nasal congestion score of 3 and a non-nasal symptom severity score of 2. She has intermittent asthma with occasional coughing and wheezing, which will be evaluated at visit 1. She has never taken desloratadine (Aerius) or any other antihistamine before. She is a healthy and active child who enjoys playing outside but is limited by her hayfever symptoms during the pollen season.

A 9-year old girl was admitted to the hospital due to severe respiratory distress. She was diagnosed with pneumonia and was started on antibiotics. However, her respiratory status continued to worsen, and she was eventually intubated and mechanically ventilated. She was diagnosed with ARDS based on the Berlin Definition criteria. She is currently receiving mechanical ventilation support and is being monitored closely in the ICU. Her past medical history is significant for asthma and allergies. She lives with her parents and two siblings. She is currently alert and oriented, but she appears fatigued due to her respiratory distress. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for her participation in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and is scheduled to have a mastectomy. She is currently experiencing anxiety and is worried about the surgery and the pain that may follow. She speaks English fluently and is able to read and write in Yoruba and Pidgin. She has no prior history of chronic pain or mental health disorders. The patient is seeking a pain management solution that does not rely solely on pain medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial on music therapy for preoperative anxiety and pain after mastectomy. She is willing to communicate with the researcher through WhatsApp and is open to selecting music that is specific to her culture and psychological needs. She is hoping that the music intervention will help her manage her anxiety and pain and improve her overall satisfaction with pain management after the surgery.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) based on the presence of multiple café-au-lait spots, axillary freckling, and a positive family history of NF1. She has been experiencing significant pain due to an internal plexiform neurofibroma (PN) in her lumbar plexus that is causing nerve compression and loss of function in her right leg. Surgery is not feasible due to the location and potential morbidity of the PN. The patient has not previously received mTOR inhibitors and has no known hypersensitivity to RAD001. She has a Karnofsky score of 80%, normal liver and kidney function, and no other severe or uncontrolled medical conditions that could affect her participation in the study. The patient is not pregnant and agrees to use effective birth control methods during the study. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 50 year old Chinese man who has been diagnosed with coronary heart disease (CHD) and has undergone at least two coronary angiography (CAG) procedures within the last 12-24 months at the same coronary intervention center. He is currently on medication for his CHD and has no history of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). He is not pregnant and does not have any other medical conditions that would prevent him from being included in the study. He is willing to participate in a national multicenter retrospective study to investigate the risk factors associated with the progression of coronary plaque in Chinese patients with CHD. The study will involve data collection from medical records and imaging results, and will last for a total of 21 months. The primary aim of the study is to identify the risk factors that promote the progression of coronary plaque, and to develop effective strategies for secondary prevention of CHD.

The patient is a resident of Mirpur, a part of the Dhaka metropolitan area in Bangladesh. They are above 1 year of age and have not taken a cholera vaccine in the past. They live in a high-risk area for cholera and are willing to participate in the study. The patient is generally healthy and has not been diagnosed with any chronic illness. They are willing to provide informed consent for participating in the study. The patient is not pregnant or less than one year old.

The patient is a 55-year-old non-smoking woman who has been experiencing persistent coughing and shortness of breath for several weeks. She underwent a series of tests that revealed a diagnosis of advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer with stage IV. The patient has a positive EGFR-sensitive mutation and has not received any prior systemic treatment, including chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, or biotherapy. She has no history of interstitial lung disease, and her cardiac function is within normal limits. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has one measurable lesion according to RECIST (version 1.1) criteria. Her life expectancy is estimated to be at least 12 weeks. Her ANC, platelet count, hemoglobin, total bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT, creatinine clearance, and other organ functions are within normal limits. She is willing to comply and participate in the study, and has signed the informed consent form.

John is a 52-year-old male who has been experiencing severe back pain for several weeks. The pain has been getting progressively worse and is now affecting his daily activities. He has a history of osteoporosis and has recently experienced a fall which has resulted in a fracture of vertebral bodies Th10-L2. John has been advised by his physician to undergo an operative treatment known as Thoracoscopic Ventral Spondylodesis. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and has given his informed consent. John's liver function is normal and he is not taking any clotting inhibition therapy. He is considered ASA II. He is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the near future. John has no history of revision of the trailing edge.

A 55-year-old male veteran with a history of chronic heart failure for 2 years presented to the clinic complaining of excessive daytime sleepiness and frequent awakening during the night. He had a diagnosis of moderate to severe central sleep apnea 6 months ago, with an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of 28 events per hour. He is compliant with his heart failure medications including diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and beta-blockers. He has no history of hospitalization for acute decompensated heart failure in the past year. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He reports occasional alcohol use. He has no history of stroke or heart transplant. He works as a security guard and drives to work every day. He reports that his job requires a lot of standing and walking. He has no history of insomnia or other sleep disorders. His Epworth Sleepiness Scale score is 14. His oxyhemoglobin saturation is 92% on room air. He is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the effectiveness of different therapies for central sleep apnea in patients with heart failure.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and is experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS). Despite trying nasal Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (nCPAP) therapy, he is still experiencing EDS and is refusing to continue with the treatment. The patient has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 34 and has no history of substance abuse or dependence. He has not been diagnosed with any psychiatric diseases or sleep disorders other than OSA. The patient is not currently taking any medication for EDS, and there are no other significant medical conditions that could affect his ability to participate in the study. He has signed and dated the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol, including discontinuing any current therapy for EDS if necessary. The patient has no allergies or known hypersensitivity to the study medication.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who recently had a hospitalization for heart failure. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes medication for both conditions. He is a retired engineer, married with two adult children who live out of state. He lives with his wife and has no mobility issues. He has been compliant with his medications and diet since his hospitalization. He has a landline telephone and is proficient in English. He has no plans for cardiac surgery or transplant. He is interested in participating in this study to better manage his heart failure and reduce the likelihood of future hospitalizations.

A 42-year-old woman is scheduled for an elective upper endoscopy procedure to investigate her recent complaints of upper abdominal discomfort and bloating. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any sedative agents prior to the procedure. She has never been sedated before and is feeling anxious about the procedure. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is happy to participate in the study and has given written and informed consent. Her physical examination reveals no abnormalities and is classified as ASA I. She has no history of respiratory, cerebrovascular, or cardiovascular diseases. She has a normal airway, with a mouth opening of more than 3 cm and a Mallampati score of 1. She is not pregnant and has no neurological disorders.

The patient is a 7-year-old child who has been experiencing bedwetting at least two nights per week for the past year. The child has no other known medical conditions and has successfully completed toilet training. The child's parent reports that they are compliant with recording data related to the bedwetting episodes. The child has not been diagnosed with any anatomic abnormalities or other comorbidities such as daytime incontinence or recurrent urinary tract infections. The child has not been prescribed any medications for the bedwetting. The child's parent is interested in participating in the study to explore the possibility of using a new technology for the bedwetting alarm trigger. The child has been referred to a pediatric urology specialist for evaluation and potential enrollment in the study.

A 32-year-old female patient with missing upper teeth is interested in dental implant placement to restore her smile. She has a history of good oral hygiene and has never required any significant dental treatment before. The patient does not smoke and has no systemic diseases. She has no history of bone grafting or augmentation. The patient has a mesio-distal dimension of 7 mm, bone height of 13 mm, and bucco-lingual dimension of 9mm, as assessed by CBCT. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of low-speed drilling versus conventional drilling techniques in implant placement.

A 62-year-old man was recently diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis, and the surgical treatment recommended by the cardiac surgeon was aortic valve replacement. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. His cardiologist referred him to the QEII Health Sciences Center in Halifax, Nova Scotia, for the surgery, and he was informed about the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial for pain management after cardiac surgery. He meets the inclusion criteria of the trial and is willing to participate. His height is 175 cm, and his weight is 80 kg. He does not have any allergies to medications, including ropivacaine. His ejection fraction is 55%, and he is not on extracorporeal membrane oxygenator (ECMO) or intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP). He has not received any preoperative vasopressors or inotropes, and his liver and kidney functions are within normal limits. He is able to provide valid consent for the study before the surgery.

The patient is a 28-year-old male competitive cyclist who has been training for the past 2 years. He cycles for at least 2-3 hours daily and participates in weekend races. He is in good physical health and has no history of cardiovascular or metabolic disease. He has a body mass index of 22. He does not smoke and does not have any food allergies. He does not use any dietary supplements, except for protein powder occasionally. He is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription medications, including phosphodiesterase 5 (PDE5) inhibitors. He has not participated in any clinical trials or studies in the past 4 weeks. He is willing to follow the supplementation guidelines and other instructions provided by the experimenter. He is able to understand the procedures to be undertaken as part of the study and has given informed, voluntary, written consent to participate.

A premature baby boy was born at 26 weeks gestation and is currently being treated in the neonatal intensive care unit. He has been intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress syndrome. The baby's parents have given written consent for him to participate in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of heated humidity high flow nasal cannula (HHHFNC) and Nasal Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (NCPAP) in the immediate post-extubation period. The baby has no known genetic or chromosomal disorders, and his mother did not have ruptured membranes for more than three weeks. The baby has been successfully weaned from mechanical ventilation for 24 hours and is eligible for the trial.

Patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman diagnosed with severe preeclampsia at 32 weeks of gestation. She presents with symptoms of severe hypertension, severe headache, epigastric pain, and edema. She has no previous medical history and is currently receiving antihypertensive medications and magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis. The patient has no history of ocular trauma or surgery, pre-existing heart disease, known pulmonary disorders, pneumonia, or interstitial lung disease. She has accepted mental status and is willing to participate in the study.

52 year old woman with a past medical history of hypertension for 10 years, currently on amlodipine 10mg and metoprolol 50 mg daily. Despite medication compliance, blood pressure readings have been consistently above 150/95 mmHg. Patient reports experiencing occasional headaches and dizziness. No known history of diabetes, heart failure, or kidney disease. No previous diagnosis of neoplastic disease. The patient is post-menopausal and not currently pregnant. BMI is 28 kg/m2.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been experiencing memory problems for the past year. He has difficulty remembering recent events and often forgets where he has put things. He has also had trouble with language and communication skills. His family has noticed a change in his personality, becoming more irritable and easily upset. He has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease according to the criteria of the National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders Association (NINCDS-ADRDA). He has not taken any antidepressants, neuroleptic, sedative-hypnotic drugs for at least two weeks before the assessment. He is able to give informed consent, and his caregiver will also be informed about the study protocol. He has no history of stroke, metabolic disturbances, epilepsy or any other major medical illness. He does not have any metallic objects in his body and has not undergone any craniotomy in the past. He will be randomly assigned to one of the three groups (anodal tDCS, cathodal tDCS, or sham tDCS) to receive daily stimulation for 10 consecutive days (5 days/week for 2 weeks) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Cognitive functions and cortical excitability will be assessed before, after 10th sessions, and then after 1 and 2 months. He is hoping to participate in this trial to help improve his cognitive function and potentially slow down the progression of his Alzheimer's disease.

The patient is a 15-year-old adolescent who has completed at least 3 weeks of double-blind treatment and reached Visit 3 of the antecedent study (SPD489-305) without experiencing any clinically significant adverse events (AEs) that would preclude exposure to LDX. The patient does not have a current, controlled or uncontrolled, comorbid psychiatric diagnosis with significant symptoms such as severe Axis I disorder, Post Traumatic Stress Disorder, bipolar illness, severe obsessive-compulsive disorder, or severe anxiety disorder. The patient does not have a history of seizures, any tic disorder, or a current diagnosis and/or a known family history of Tourette's Disorder. The patient does not have a known history of symptomatic cardiovascular disease, advanced arteriosclerosis, structural cardiac abnormality, cardiomyopathy, serious heart rhythm abnormalities, or coronary artery disease. The patient is not taking any medication that is excluded, has no documented allergy, hypersensitivity or intolerance to amphetamine, and has no recent history (within the past 6 months) of suspected substance abuse or dependence disorder (excluding nicotine) in accordance with DSM-IV-TR criteria. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

Maria is a 35 year old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. She has been on a conventional antidepressant medication for six months but has not experienced significant symptom relief, as she still reports feeling sad, hopeless, and having difficulty sleeping and concentrating. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. Maria has a history of anxiety and has received psychotherapy in the past, but it did not help her depressive symptoms. She does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any medications that would interfere with her participation in the study. Maria is interested in participating as she feels that her current treatment is not working and is eager to try something new. She has no history of substance abuse, and is not actively suicidal. Maria is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

Karen is a 53-year-old woman who has been suffering from severe knee pain due to end-stage osteoarthritis. She has tried various conservative treatments, but nothing has provided long-lasting relief. She has been scheduled for a total knee arthroplasty to relieve her pain and improve her mobility. Karen has no surgical history of urinary system, urinary tract infection, or any systematical condition like renal disease, renal failure, or chronic renal insufficiency. She has no indwelling catheter at the time of the surgery. Karen is willing and able to return for follow-up over at least a 1-month postoperative period. She has given her consent to participate in the study investigating whether urinary catheterization can be avoided for patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty under combined spinal-epidural analgesia plus multi-site infiltration analgesia.

The patient is a premature infant born at 27 weeks gestation and admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at Advocate Children's Hospital, Park Ridge within 48 hours of birth. The infant is currently on a feeding plan and receiving breast milk or formula through a feeding tube. The baby has no history of gastrointestinal anomalies, lethal malformations or any other medical condition. The infant is closely monitored by a trained NICU staff and is in stable condition. The baby's feeding tolerance will be monitored throughout the study which will last for a minimum of 28 days. The parents of the infant have given their consent for the baby to participate in the study.

10-year-old male diagnosed with a solid tumor of the kidney. The patient's parents have given their consent for the child's participation in the study. The patient has no other significant medical history and is affiliated with a French social security scheme. Both biological parents are available for participation in the study. The patient and both parents will undergo trio-based whole exome sequencing to identify potential genetic predisposition to cancer. Tumor analysis will also be performed to identify therapeutic targets and investigate potential links between constitutive mutations and tumor phenotype. The patient is being treated at the CHU de Montpellier.

A 3-year-old girl from a rural village in Sylhet district, Bangladesh, is brought to the community health clinic by her mother. The child has been coughing and having difficulty breathing for the past few days, and her mother is concerned that she may have pneumonia. The child has no fever or other visible symptoms, but her breathing is rapid and shallow. The mother is worried, as she has lost a child to pneumonia in the past. The community health provider listens to the child's lungs with the Smartscope, a digital stethoscope, and records the lung sounds at four sequential locations. The recorded sounds are uploaded to a server and securely stored. Later, the lung sounds will be processed and analyzed by an automated algorithm and a listening panel comprising pediatricians. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Smartscope in diagnosing childhood pneumonia at the community level in rural areas of Bangladesh. The child's eligibility for the study is assessed, and if eligible, she will be enrolled in the study after obtaining written informed consent from her mother. The study will also collect socioeconomic and other related confounders' data, including immunization information, weight, mid-upper arm circumference, and length/height, from all enrolled cases at the household level within seven days of enrolment. Focus group discussions will also be held with carers, community health care providers, and community leaders to gather opinions about the Smartscope's acceptability as a pneumonia diagnostic tool.

A 54 year old woman with a recent diagnosis of metastatic soft tissue sarcoma with no prior systemic therapy regimens presenting with fatigue, nausea, and occasional vomiting. CT revealed multiple liver metastases. The patient has no known drug allergies and is on no regular medications. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with lisinopril. Her physical exam was unremarkable except for the presence of hepatomegaly. Lab results showed a platelet count of 80,000/mm^3. She was started on gemcitabine and docetaxel chemotherapy regimen. She is otherwise in good health with no pre-existing heart disease, blood clotting problems or platelet disorders, and no history of brain cancer. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to study the effect of eltrombopag on chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia.

This is a 28-year-old male who is in good health and has no significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research. He has provided written informed consent and is able to understand the trial procedures and possible adverse events. The patient is aware of the contraceptive requirements and agrees to comply with them. He has not used any illicit or prescription drugs in the past year and has a negative urine drug screen. The patient is willing to comply with all the requirements and is able to complete the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma since childhood. She has been taking albuterol as a rescue inhaler as needed for wheezing and shortness of breath. She has not been on a daily maintenance inhaler for the past year due to cost concerns and difficulty in accessing healthcare. She reports that her asthma symptoms have been well controlled with the use of her rescue inhaler alone. She does not have any other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. She is currently employed and has health insurance coverage through her employer. She is interested in participating in the PRIME study to learn more about the standard treatments for mild asthma and to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge in the field of asthma management. She is able to use electronic devices and has access to the internet to complete the e-diary.

The patient is a 24 year-old female who has been diagnosed with Anorexia Nervosa. She reports a preoccupation with food and weight, and has been restricting her food intake for the past 6 months. She has lost approximately 20 pounds during this time period and her Body Mass Index (BMI) is currently 16. She reports feeling anxious and guilty when she eats more than a certain amount of food or when she eats foods that she considers "unhealthy". She has not received any treatment for her eating disorder in the past. She is not currently pregnant and does not plan on becoming pregnant in the near future. She does not have a history of psychosis or manic episodes.

A 32-year-old woman presents to the Assisted Reproduction Unit at Almana General Hospital with a history of infertility for the past 2 years. She has undergone several cycles of ovarian stimulation with gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist induction protocol. During her previous cycle, she developed abdominal distension, nausea, and vomiting, and her ultrasound showed large ovaries with significant fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity. Her maximal ovarian diameter was 12 cm, and she had to cancel embryo transfer due to the risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). She is now interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of 3-day cetrotide therapy for the management of women at high risk of developing OHSS. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study, including having more than 20 retrieved oocytes, an elevated serum E2 level, and a maximal ovarian diameter of more than 10 cm on the day of ovum retrieval. She has signed a written consent form to participate in the study and undergo embryo freezing. She is randomized to the study group and will receive 3-day cetrotide subcutaneous injection in addition to embryo freezing. She will be monitored daily for symptoms of OHSS, serum E2 levels, and maximal ovarian diameter.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with urothelial cancer of the ureter, which requires stent placement. He complains of intermittent flank pain, hematuria, and urinary frequency. He has a history of smoking and hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. His physical exam is unremarkable. He has no known allergies to medication. He has signed the informed consent and agrees to participate in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 14-year-old female who received a kidney transplant 6 months ago due to end-stage renal disease. She presents with a 40% decline in her baseline renal function, as indicated by a rise in her serum creatinine level. A biopsy confirms an acute rejection episode. She is able and willing to give written informed consent, and her parents are supportive of her participation in the study. She has no prior history of treatment with Rituximab or severe allergic reactions to monoclonal antibodies. She has no history of HIV or Hepatitis B/C. She has no ongoing infection or major episode of infection requiring hospitalization or IV antibiotics in the past 4 weeks. She is not currently on high dose steroids or any unstable steroid dose. She has no history of drug or chemical abuse. She has no significant cardiac or pulmonary disease. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is compliant with study and follow-up procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of infectious pleural effusion. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and fever for the past week. A chest x-ray revealed a large amount of fluid in his pleural space. A thoracentesis was performed, and laboratory analysis of the pleural fluid showed that it was an exudate. The patient was started on antibiotics and underwent a pleural drainage procedure to remove the fluid. He has been receiving usual medical treatment but is still experiencing some discomfort and difficulty breathing. He has no known history of respiratory or cardiovascular disease. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is able to perform spirometry and participate in physiotherapy exercises. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes since she was 15 years old. She has a history of disordered eating patterns and has been withholding her insulin to lose weight. She has been actively receiving treatment for her eating disorder at EDI for the past year, which includes regular appointments with her RD, CDE, RN, LP, and MD. The patient has expressed an interest in participating in a monthly support group with other individuals who have type 1 diabetes and an eating disorder. She is committed to attending at least 66% of the group sessions and has received approval from her EDI/DM team to participate in the study. The patient does not have any additional eating disorder issues that would make her attendance in the group inappropriate. The patient is psychologically ready for group therapy and does not have type 2 diabetes.

Patient is a 52-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19. He has been experiencing symptoms for the past week, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Upon admission, he was found to have interstitial pneumonia and laboratory findings consistent with early severe COVID-19 infection. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He has not received any other treatment for COVID-19. The patient is willing to participate in the SARCOVID clinical trial and has given informed consent. He meets the inclusion criteria of the study, but does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with metastasis to the liver and bones. She has completed neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy with anthracycline and taxane-based regimens for her primary breast tumor. She is HER2 negative and not eligible for anti-HER2 therapy. She has no history of autoimmune disease, CNS disease, HIV, or active hepatitis B or C. She has no history of significant cardiovascular disease and is able to perform daily activities. She has no known hypersensitivity to the study drugs. She is willing to provide informed consent and meet the other inclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Stage 4 chronic kidney disease (CKD) and anemia, not on dialysis. He has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all of which are well controlled with medications. He presents with fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath upon exertion. His most recent central laboratory Hb value during the screening period was 9.5 g/dL, and his ferritin and TSAT levels were 70 ng/mL and 20%, respectively. His ALT, AST, and total bilirubin levels were within normal limits. He has not received any erythropoietin analogue treatment within the past 6 weeks, and he has no history of congestive heart failure, recent cardiovascular events, or chronic liver disease. He does not have any known hereditary hematologic diseases or retinal vein occlusion or proliferative diabetic retinopathy. His renal ultrasound did not show any renal cell carcinoma, and his blood pressure is well controlled with medications. He has not had any red blood cell transfusions or significant blood loss during the screening period. He is not currently receiving roxadustat or any HIF-PHI treatment and has not participated in any other clinical study that included drug treatment within the past month. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent.

45-year-old female with a history of chronic neck pain due to a C5-C6 disc herniation that was diagnosed on MRI. The patient has tried conservative management for 6 weeks without improvement in symptoms. She reports neck pain, shoulder pain, and numbness/tingling down her left arm. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Imaging studies confirm the primary diagnosis, and the patient is willing and able to comply with all study procedures. She does not have any of the exclusion criteria, including no prior fusion at the level to be treated, no metabolic or systemic bone disorder, and no active or latent infections. The patient is a non-smoker and fluent in English. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) with anxious distress for the past 2 years. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m^2 and has been experiencing moderate to severe depression as evidenced by an inventory of depressive symptomatology, clinician rating-30 (IDS-C30) total score of 40. She has not responded well to her current antidepressant treatment, which has been ongoing for 8 weeks with no improvement greater than 50%. She is currently taking sertraline and has not undergone more than 2 previous failed antidepressant treatments. The patient has a negative serum pregnancy test and is not currently experiencing suicidal ideation. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse within the past 6 months and has not been diagnosed with any other psychiatric conditions. The patient does not have any clinically relevant medical conditions that could alter the absorption, metabolism, or excretion of the study intervention.
