She has not undergone electroconvulsive therapy or deep brain stimulation in the current episode and has no history of demyelinating diseases.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and is on dialysis. He has been on the transplant waitlist for two years and has now been notified that a kidney is available for him. He is excited but nervous about the transplant surgery and the postoperative care. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are well controlled with medications. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and he only drinks alcohol occasionally. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 11 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 150000 /ml Creatinine: 8 mg/dl BUN: 70 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy. He is aware of the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to be randomized to either group 1 (tacrolimus and everolimus) or group 2 (tacrolimus and mycophenolate mofetil) for his immunosuppressive therapy. He is hopeful that the study will help him achieve better kidney function and avoid complications associated with immunosuppressive medications.

A 56 year old woman who has previously been diagnosed with multiple myeloma is experiencing symptoms of relapse. She has undergone one previous line of treatment and her disease has progressed despite this treatment. She has been experiencing bone pain, fatigue, and anemia. Her peripheral neuropathy is Grade 1. She does not have any hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron or dexamethasone. Her disease is measurable and progressive. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who lost his maxillary right premolar due to trauma. He is a non-smoker and has no history of drug abuse or psychiatric disorders. He is in good general health and takes no medication. He works as a sales executive and is highly motivated to restore his missing tooth. His oral hygiene is good and he regularly visits his dentist for check-ups. He has a ridge width of 6mm and adequate vertical inter-arch space to accommodate the restorative components. He does not have any para-functional habits such as bruxism or clenching. He has no contraindications for implant therapy and is willing to participate in the study.

52-year-old female with a history of stress urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse presents to the clinic for preoperative counseling before undergoing surgery. The patient has been experiencing symptoms of urinary incontinence for the past 2 years and has noticed a worsening of these symptoms over the past few months. She reports occasional pelvic pain and pressure but denies any bowel or bladder symptoms. The patient is currently taking ibuprofen for pain management. She is able to speak and read English fluently and is scheduled for surgery in 2 weeks. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve preoperative counseling for women undergoing pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence surgery. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the Telephone Intervention to Increase Patient Preparedness and Satisfaction Trial (TIPPS) and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 32 year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years with no success. She also complains of pelvic pain that has been present for the past 6 months. She has regular menstrual cycles and denies any abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge. She has no known medical conditions and does not take any medications. She has never had surgery before. She is sexually active with her husband and uses condoms for contraception. She has no history of sexually transmitted infections. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the use of serum macrophage migration inhibitory factor as a potential diagnostic tool for endometriosis.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer. His PSA level was found to be elevated during a routine check-up, and further investigations revealed bone and lymph node metastases. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He underwent a bilateral orchiectomy as a part of his treatment, and currently, he is receiving Abiraterone for mCRPC. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of major surgeries or serious cardiovascular events in the past 12 months. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is medically cleared to undergo a symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise test and vigorous aerobic and resistance exercise training. The patient is not currently participating in any vigorous aerobic exercise or structured resistance exercise. The patient's bone scan has been reviewed and approved by the Exercise Coordination Centre. He is fluent in the language designated by the institution at which he would be enrolled and is willing and able to use the technological aspects of the trial.

A 32 year-old woman with a history of repaired tetralogy of Fallot presents with increasing dyspnea on exertion and fatigue. She reports that her symptoms have been present for several months and have been progressively worsening. On examination, she has a harsh systolic ejection murmur heard best at the upper left sternal border with radiation to the back. A transthoracic echocardiogram shows severe pulmonary regurgitation with a pulmonary trunk diameter of 25 mm and a dilated right ventricle. The patient is diagnosed with right ventricular dilatation and is found to be a suitable candidate for pulmonary valve replacement. She is willing to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria. She has no contraindications to the procedure and is medically stable.

65-year-old male patient with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic cancer with no standard therapy options. Patient has undergone 3 prior treatment regimens with no notable improvement in their condition. Patient has not received any chemotherapy in the past 4 weeks and has not undergone radiotherapy to at least 30% of bone marrow in the past 4 weeks. The patient's performance status is within the range of 60-100% on the Karnofsky scale and their life expectancy is at least 2 months. The patient's hematopoietic system is within the normal range, with a WBC count of at least 3000/mm3, an absolute neutrophil count of at least 1500/mm3, and a platelet count of at least 100,000/mm3. The patient's bilirubin levels are normal, and their SGOT/SGPT levels are no greater than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal. The patient's creatinine levels are within the normal range or their creatinine clearance is at least 60 mL/min. The patient has no symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, or cardiac arrhythmia. The patient has no clinically significant neuropathy and is not pregnant or nursing. The patient is not allergic to platinum compounds or antiemetics and has no uncontrolled active infection or other illnesses. The patient is not currently receiving any other concurrent anticancer therapy or investigational agents. The patient is not HIV positive and not receiving antiretroviral therapy (HAART). The patient is willing to use effective contraception if they are fertile.

Patient is a 56-year-old male from the United States who presents with severe abdominal pain and is diagnosed with a perforated appendix. He has a history of smoking and hypertension, but is otherwise healthy. His BMI is 27, BP: 140/90, HR: 82/min. He is scheduled to undergo open abdominal surgery under general anesthesia. Based on his ARISCAT score, he is at high risk for post-operative pulmonary complications. He has not had any previous lung surgeries, does not require home oxygen therapy or non-invasive ventilation, and does not have a history of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

A 50-year-old female with a history of stage IV breast cancer presents with disease progression despite multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient has no comorbidities and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has measurable disease and is able to swallow oral capsules. Hematology shows a hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, platelets of 150,000/cu.mm and neutrophils of 1800/cu.mm. PT and PTT are within normal limits. Biochemistry tests show a total bilirubin level of 1.2 x ULN, AST/ALT of 2.5 x ULN, serum creatinine of 1.5 mg/dL, serum calcium of 10.5 mg/dL, and fasting serum triglycerides of 2.0 x ULN. The patient has never received retinoid therapy or large doses of Vitamin A, and has no history of thyroid or pituitary disease. The patient has never participated in the study before and is not currently enrolled in any other investigational drug or device study. The patient has no known sensitivity to any of the ingredients in the study medication and is not pregnant, nursing or planning a pregnancy. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal disorders that may interfere with the absorption of the study medication. The patient has no clinically significant abnormalities on screening ECG. The patient is willing to follow study instructions and is likely to complete all study requirements.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who lives in Dauphin County, Pennsylvania. He attends a local elementary school and is in good health. His parents have noticed that he snores loudly at night and seems to have restless sleep. They are concerned that he may have sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) and have filled out a questionnaire provided by the study. The questionnaire revealed that the patient is at high risk for SDB, so he has been selected to participate in the second part of the study where he will be evaluated in a sleep laboratory. The patient has no history of asthma, allergies or other respiratory problems. He is not taking any medication, and his medical history is unremarkable. The patient is cooperative, and his parents have given informed consent for his participation in the study.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has been admitted to the hospital with diarrhea that has persisted for a week. He reports having frequent bowel movements, with loose and watery stools. He has also experienced abdominal cramping and discomfort during this time. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. He works as a software engineer and enjoys spending his free time playing video games and watching movies. He is married and has two children. His BMI is 28 and he has a blood pressure of 130/80. He is able to communicate effectively and has given his consent to participate in the study.

A 48 yo male with a history of lower back pain, radiating to the right lower extremity, and difficulty walking. The patient reports that his symptoms have been worsening over the past 6 months despite conservative measures such as physical therapy, exercise, and medication management. Imaging studies revealed degenerative spondylolisthesis with grade 2 slippage at the L4-L5 level. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the Paradigm Spine Dynamic Stabilization System (DSS) study as he has objective evidence of neurologic impairment and failed previous fusion at the index level. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up examinations. The surgeon has determined that the DSS™ System is an appropriate treatment for the patient. The patient does not have any of the exclusion criteria such as active infections, systemic diseases, or foreign body sensitivity to the implant material. He does not have significant osteopenia and is not involved in a study of another investigational product for similar purpose.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is currently enrolled in a Pfizer-sponsored trial comparing the effectiveness of atorvastatin with a combination of atorvastatin and CETP inhibitor. She has no history of pacemaker, defibrillator, or brain aneurysm clips. She does not have any implanted active medical devices such as neural stimulators, cochlear implants, or insulin pumps. She does not suffer from severe claustrophobia and is not allergic to gadolinium-based contrast agents. The patient is willing to travel to the NIH to participate in the NHLBI MRI/IMT study.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been diagnosed with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1). He has a history of difficulty with breathing during sleep and has been experiencing frequent episodes of snoring, gasping, and choking during the night. He has also been feeling excessively tired during the day. He has not been diagnosed with any cardiac arrhythmias, but he is concerned about his risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD) due to his condition. He has never undergone any sleep study or polysomnography tests. He is currently not on any medication or devices for his DM1. He lives alone and works as a software developer. He has no history of smoking or illicit drug use. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the relationship between sleep breathing disorders and cardiac arrhythmias in DM1 patients.

The patient is a 35 year old Chinese male who was recently diagnosed with HIV. He has never received antiretroviral therapy before and has a viral load of greater than 500 copies/ml. He also has a history of hepatitis B and hepatitis C co-infection. His liver function test showed mild impairment with AST and ALT levels slightly elevated. He works as a factory worker and lives with his wife and two children. He does not have any history of drug abuse and is a non-smoker. He can read and write in Chinese and is willing to participate in the study to determine which antiretroviral therapy regimen would be safer for his liver function.

The patient is a 68-year-old Caucasian male with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and a reported memory concern verified by a study partner. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. His past medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He has a Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) score of 3 and a Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI) total score of 5, with no score higher than 2 in any domain. He has normal vision in both eyes and is able to hear well enough to participate in cognitive testing. He scored below the cut-off on the Logical Memory II subscale (Delayed Paragraph Recall, Paragraph A only) from the Wechsler Memory Scale - Revised (9 for 8-15 years of education), and has a Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score of 25. He has a Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Score (CDR) of 0.5 (memory box score must = 0.5). He has undergone a Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scan within the past 9 months with a Modified Hachinski Score <4 and no evidence of infection, infarction (ischemic or hemorrhagic), or other focal lesions (tumors, subdural hematomas, malformations, etc.). He has not had a positive amyloid PET scan in the last 3 years. He is not taking any excluded psychoactive medications and is able to cooperate for the duration of the study with procedures and assessments.

10-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with Fanconi anemia presented to the hospital with complaints of fatigue, pallor, and easy bruising. Physical examination revealed a blood pressure of 110/70 mmHg, heart rate of 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, and temperature of 98.6°F. He had mild splenomegaly and petechiae on his lower extremities. Laboratory studies showed a hemoglobin level of 7.5 g/dL, white blood cell count of 2.8 × 10^3/µL, and platelet count of 20 × 10^3/µL. Bone marrow biopsy revealed hypocellular marrow with trilineage dysplasia. The patient was diagnosed with Fanconi anemia and severe aplastic anemia. He was deemed eligible for the clinical trial investigating the use of risk-adjusted chemotherapy-based cytoreductive regimen plus a CD34+ selected T-cell depleted peripheral blood stem cell (PBSC) stem cell transplant. The patient's parents were informed about the study and signed the informed consent form. The patient was willing to participate in the trial and met all other eligibility criteria. A matched unrelated donor was identified, and the patient underwent the transplant following the preparative regimen of busulfan, fludarabine, anti-thymocyte globulin, and cyclophosphamide.

The patient is a 8-year-old girl who has a history of cow milk allergy. She experiences immediate type reactions during oral provocation tests for a cumulated dose of less than 100 mL of milk. Her IgE-mediated cow milk allergy has been confirmed with detectable specific IgE (> 0.10 KU/l). The girl and her parents have given their informed consent to participate in the study. She has not participated in any drug trial during the last 3 months and does not have any immune deficiency or disabling disease that would prevent her from practicing sublingual treatment. The girl is not receiving steroid therapy and is willing to participate in the study. She does not have any severe food neophobia and has not experienced any severe anaphylactic reaction with milk during the last 6 months.

A 50-year-old man diagnosed with chronic liver disease due to alcohol abuse. He has been experiencing fatigue, jaundice, and abdominal swelling for the past few months. He has been diagnosed with liver cirrhosis and has been advised to undergo liver transplantation. However, he is unable to do so due to the high cost and lack of donors. He has been advised to participate in a clinical trial that uses autologous MSCs to treat liver cirrhosis. He is Child's B stage with a life expectancy of more than 6 months. He has signed an informed consent form and is willing to participate in the trial. He does not have any active infections or multiple infections and has controlled hypertension and diabetes. He is not immunosuppressed and is not HIV positive. He is not pregnant or lactating.

A 65-year-old male patient presents with a history of blurred vision and difficulty in reading small print. The patient was diagnosed with cataracts and scheduled for phacoemulsification surgery. The patient has no significant medical history and takes no regular medications. The patient has no known allergies. The patient is able to attend follow-up appointments at one week and one month post-surgery. The patient has no history of ocular inflammation, glaucoma, previous ocular surgery, or diabetes. The patient is not currently using any systemic anti-inflammatories or topical therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who was diagnosed with Turner syndrome at birth. She has a history of aortic dilation and hypertension, which has been managed with medication. She has also experienced occasional chest pain and shortness of breath. She has no significant past medical history other than Turner Syndrome. She has been on hormone therapy for the past 5 years to induce puberty and maintain bone density. She is otherwise healthy and has never smoked or consumed alcohol. She has a normal body mass index (BMI) and is physically active. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the heart, aorta and blood pressure in Turner Syndrome to better understand the risks and potential complications associated with the condition.

A 6-year-old girl is scheduled to undergo a tonsillectomy procedure. She has no significant medical history and is in good health. She weighs 25 kg and her height is 115 cm, which is within the normal range for her age. She is accompanied by her mother who is anxious about the procedure. The girl is cooperative and able to follow instructions. She has no known allergies to medications. She has not eaten or drunk anything for the past 8 hours. Her vital signs are normal, with a heart rate of 85 beats per minute, a blood pressure of 100/60 mmHg, and a respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute. Her physical examination is unremarkable. The anesthesiologist explains the study to the mother and obtains her consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II endometrial cancer. She has no significant past medical history and is currently in good health. She reported experiencing abnormal vaginal bleeding for several months prior to diagnosis. She underwent a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection. The pathology report showed endometrioid adenocarcinoma involving the endometrium with metastasis to two pelvic lymph nodes. She is now a candidate for adjuvant treatment, but before starting any treatment, she will be enrolled in a clinical trial to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of a new magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique, the diffusion weighted imaging with body background signal suppression (DWIBS), in the detection of lymph node pathology in patients with gynaecologic malignancies. She meets the eligibility criteria for the trial and has no contraindications to the MRI.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV melanoma with unresectable tumors. He has undergone one prior cytotoxic therapy for the treatment of metastatic disease and has fully recovered from the acute toxicities related to the therapy. He has measurable disease, with at least one lesion that can be accurately measured in at least one dimension (longest diameter to be recorded) as ≥10 mm with spiral CT scan. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and normal organ and marrow function. He expresses HLA class I allele HLA-A*0201 for NY-ESO-1/LAGE and has proven positive tumor sample for NY-ESO-1 as determined by an H score for immunohistochemistry staining. He has no active brain metastases or history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to cyclophosphamide or other agents used in the study. He is willing to use reliable methods of contraception during the study and has the ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 2 years ago. He has undergone two previous lines of treatment, including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory drug. He has experienced relapsed disease and is now interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 70% and his labs show a total white blood cell count of 3,500/μL, an absolute neutrophil count of 1,200/μL, a platelet count of 85,000/μL, and a hemoglobin level of 9.5 g/dL. His creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL, and his ALT and AST levels are within normal limits. He has CD20-positive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with evidence of relapsed/refractory disease that has failed conventional therapy and failed/not eligible/refused studies of a higher priority. He has measurable disease greater than 1.5 cm in diameter. He has HLA-haploidentical or mismatched related donor match based on a minimum of intermediate resolution DNA based Class I typing of the A and B locus (at least 2/4 class I allele) and absence of recipient anti HLA antibodies against selected donor. He is willing to use effective contraception during therapy and for 4 months after completion of therapy. He has recovered from the acute effects of prior therapy, with at least 2 weeks elapsed since the last dose of chemotherapy. He is interested in participating in the phase I trial with pilot expansion of HLA-haploidentical or HLA-mismatched related donor nicotinamide expanded-natural killer (NAM-NK) cell based therapy for patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (MM) or relapsed/refractory CD20-positive non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with symptomatic gallstones and is scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA class II. She is currently not taking any regular medications and has no known allergies to local anesthetics. The patient understands the purpose of the study and has provided informed written consent for participation. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits. Her vital signs are within normal limits, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 80 bpm, and a BMI of 25. Her abdomen is soft and non-tender on examination. She has no history of liver disease and has not undergone any previous abdominal surgeries. The patient is allocated to either the S-TAP block group or P-TAP block group through a draw/ballot method, as per the study protocol.

A 45 year old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 8 months ago. She has been taking methotrexate 20mg/week orally for the past 6 months but has not achieved disease remission. She was previously treated with adalimumab for 3 months but had to discontinue it due to side effects. She complains of morning stiffness, fatigue, tender and swollen joints in both hands, wrists, and ankles. Her ACR functional status is Class II. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, malignancy, or tuberculosis. She is not currently taking any medication for dyslipidemia. She has not participated in any clinical research study evaluating another investigational drug or therapy within 5 half-lives or 60 days of the first investigational medicinal product administration.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who received an allogeneic stem cell transplant 3 years ago for acute myeloid leukemia. He is currently admitted to the hospital with a positive COVID19 diagnosis and requires supplemental oxygen due to severe respiratory symptoms. He has a history of hypertension but is otherwise in good health. The patient has not received any cytokine targeting treatment before blood sampling. The transplant team has identified him as eligible for the study and will approach him to participate. The patient will be required to provide a 10 ml clotted blood sample and a 10 ml EDTA blood sample within 72 hours of admission for centralized cytokine and lymphocyte subset analysis. The patient's demographic and clinical characteristics, blood results, clinical course, therapy, and outcome data will be collected for follow-up surveys at 30 and 100 days after the start of supplemental oxygen therapy for COVID19 infection.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with symptomatic hypogonadism. He reports decreased libido, fatigue, and decreased muscle mass. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications or supplements. His BMI is 28, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for serum testosterone levels of 250 ng/dL. He has no history of liver or kidney disease, CAD, malignancy, or coagulopathies. He does not consume more than 2 standard drinks of alcohol per day and has no history of psychiatric disorders.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23. He does not have any chronic illnesses or neurological or psychiatric disorders. He does not smoke, use illicit drugs, or consume alcohol excessively. He is not currently taking any medications or participating in any other clinical trials. He has no history of any surgeries that could interfere with the pharmacokinetics of the trial medication. He is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site and is able to understand and comply with study requirements. He is sexually abstinent and does not plan to donate blood or sperm during the trial. He has normal blood pressure, pulse rate, and ECG findings. His laboratory values are within the normal range. He is willing to use a highly effective method of birth control if he has a female partner who is a woman of childbearing potential. He is able to provide signed and dated written informed consent prior to admission to the study.

50-year-old female, who was recently diagnosed with uterine fibroids, is scheduled to undergo open abdominal hysterectomy. She has a history of hypertension and has been on anti-hypertensive medication for the past 5 years. She is a non-smoker and non-alcoholic. She has no significant past medical or surgical history. Her BMI is 27 kg/m². She is able to perform activities of daily living independently without any assistance. She has no history of respiratory problems or cognitive deficits. She is aware of the possibility of postoperative pain and complications and is willing to participate in the trial. She has received counseling about the study's procedures and has signed the informed consent form.

Pt is a 65yo M with a recent diagnosis of invasive carcinoma of the bladder. He has no history of pelvic radiotherapy and is planned to receive hypofractionated radiotherapy to the bladder. The patient has provided written informed consent and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. He does not have a urinary catheter in situ, which would affect the quality of the cone beam CT images that will be evaluated during the study. The patient is otherwise healthy and able to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a history of psoriasis for the past 10 years. The patient has tried multiple topical and systemic therapies for the management of his condition with limited success. The patient presents with multiple erythematous, scaly plaques on the scalp, elbows, knees, and trunk. The patient is otherwise healthy with no known allergies or medical conditions. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of UVA1 or UVB light therapy for the treatment of psoriasis. The patient lives within a reasonable driving distance of Ann Arbor, Michigan and is able to attend all scheduled appointments during the study. The patient is willing to receive UVA1 or UVB light therapy as directed in the protocol and follow all restrictions. The patient signs the informed consent form and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and occasional nausea for the past year. He underwent an upper endoscopy, and biopsy samples were taken, which confirmed the presence of H. pylori infection. The patient was prescribed a course of antibiotics, but after completing the treatment, his symptoms persisted, and upon retesting, H. pylori was still present. Further susceptibility testing was conducted, which showed that H. pylori was sensitive to all antibiotics. The patient was then referred to this clinical trial to determine whether mixed strain H. pylori infection is the reason for eradication failure during treatment. The patient has no significant medical history and is generally healthy.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with TTP. She has a history of thrombocytopenia and has been experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, headaches, and petechiae. She has been referred for Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE) treatment within the next three days. She has no known severe hypersensitivity reactions to plasma-derived products or FFP. She has no history of IgA deficiency or documented antibodies against IgA. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trial and has not participated in any clinical trial in the past month. She has no severe deficiencies of protein S. She is willing to give voluntary written informed consent before any study-related procedure is performed that is not part of standard medical care, with the understanding that consent may be withdrawn at any time without prejudice to future medical care. The patient is not currently taking ACE-inhibitors and has not taken them within the past 24 hours.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl scheduled for laparoscopic appendicectomy. She weighs 30 kg and is overall healthy with an ASA score of I. She is accompanied by her mother who consents to the regional anesthesia technique. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders, liver disease, or peritonitis. She is not currently experiencing any skin lesions or sepsis. The family lives in a suburban area and the patient attends school regularly. The patient is comfortable with the idea of regional anesthesia and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

This is a 35 year old male who was diagnosed with HIV 2 years ago. He has been on a stable anti-HIV drug regimen without any harmful drug side effects or serious illness. His most recent HIV-1 RNA level was 150 copies/ml. He has not participated in ACTG 388 previously. The purpose of this study is to compare the effects of two different three-drug anti-HIV drug regimens on reducing levels of HIV in the blood. The study also aims to evaluate whether patients discontinue the regimens because of drug side effects. The patient will be randomly assigned to receive either a protease inhibitor (PI)-sparing regimen of 2 nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) with efavirenz (EFV) or an NRTI-sparing regimen of EFV with lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r). The patient will be evaluated for safety and for virologic and immunologic responses at regular intervals throughout the study. The study will last for 1.5 to 3 years. The patient must be using an acceptable method of contraception and must not be allergic to any of the study drugs.

A 10-year-old male patient was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and underwent Allo-HSCT with stem cells from an unrelated donor. Despite receiving a first line therapy with steroids for aGvHD, the patient developed stage III gut GvHD with diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss. The GvHD did not improve after 5 days of treatment with corticosteroids at 2 mg/Kg methylprednisolone equivalent dose. The patient's parents are concerned about the lack of improvement and the potential long-term complications of GvHD. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies or intolerances to medications. The patient and his parents are willing to participate in this clinical trial and understand the potential risks and benefits of the treatment with Leukotac (inolimomab).

A 14-year-old adolescent was diagnosed with primary hyperoxaluria type 1, with a molar ratio [oxaluria / creatinuria] of 0.1 since diagnosis. She has been on vitamin B6 and potassium citrate treatment for the past 6 months, with no significant improvement in her symptoms. Her Glomerular Filtration Rate is 60 mL / min / 1.73m2. She is fluent in French and her parents have read and signed the information note and consent form for the clinical trial. She does not have any significant medical history other than primary hyperoxaluria. She is not currently taking any medication that affects hepatic metabolism or the renal tubule. She does not have any known allergies or contraindications to stiripentol. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is not under guardianship.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been admitted to the intensive care unit with a diagnosis of anoxic brain injury due to a cardiac arrest. She was found unresponsive at home and was brought to the hospital by emergency medical services. Upon arrival, she was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. The patient has a past medical history significant for hypertension and high cholesterol, but no history of lung disease. On physical examination, the patient is unresponsive, with no response to verbal or painful stimuli. She has a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 3. The patient's vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/70 mmHg, heart rate of 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on mechanical ventilation with a tidal volume of 8 mL/kg. The patient's laboratory studies are significant for a partial pressure of carbon dioxide of 45 mmHg and a partial pressure of oxygen of 80 mmHg. The patient's chest x-ray shows bilateral opacities consistent with acute respiratory distress syndrome. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study as she has an acute brain injury and is receiving mechanical ventilation.

17F with a history of osteosarcoma of the right femur, status post-limb salvage surgery with total knee replacement and adjuvant chemotherapy, presented with a symptomatic relapse of the right femur, as confirmed by biopsy. The patient underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate, cisplatin, and doxorubicin, followed by limb salvage surgery with resection of the recurrent tumor and endoprosthetic replacement of the right femur. Pathology confirmed high-grade osteosarcoma with positive margins. The patient then received adjuvant chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate, cisplatin, and doxorubicin, followed by maintenance chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate and ifosfamide. Despite these treatments, the patient had a recurrence of disease in the form of multiple pulmonary nodules. The patient was referred to participate in the clinical trial of high dose isofosfamide through elastomer for patients with relapsed/ refractory osteosarcoma. The patient is under 40 years of age and has completed at least one cycle of HD IFO through elastomer (14g/mq) in 14 days. Disease evaluation according to RECIST criteria v.1.1 has been performed.

A 35-year-old avid cyclist who has been cycling for over 5 years, with a history of participating in local cycling clubs, has recently suffered from a cycling-related injury. The injury has caused him pain and discomfort, which has been affecting his ability to cycle regularly. He has been experiencing pain in his lower back and right shoulder for the past 2 weeks. He has not sought medical attention for his injuries and is hesitant to do so as he fears he will have to take a break from cycling. He is fluent in English and interested in participating in this study to help researchers better understand the behavior of cyclists in response to pain.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been diagnosed with kidney stones and is scheduled for extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. He has no other significant medical history and is generally healthy. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His vital signs are within normal limits with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, heart rate of 75 bpm, and respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. He has no significant physical findings on examination. The patient is able to understand and provide informed consent for the study.

This is a 62-year-old woman who suffered a stroke six months ago and has been experiencing hemiparetic gait dysfunction since then. She is able to walk with the help of a cane, but has difficulty with balance and often feels unsteady on her feet. She has not received any formal rehabilitation for her gait issues and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her improve her walking ability. She has no history of cardiovascular conditions, and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of diabetes or renal failure. She is able to understand and follow simple instructions, and has no cognitive impairment or history of depression or psychiatric disorder. She has no significant lower limb arthritis or pain, and her lower limb spasticity is mild. She has no skin conditions on her trunk, and has not been diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm. She is not on anticoagulation with warfarin. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to test a novel patient sensing automated treadmill device that may help her improve her walking ability and reduce her fall risk.

25 yo F with a history of allergic rhinitis for the past 2 years, presenting with nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and nasal itching, all of which have persisted despite the use of over-the-counter antihistamines. Patient has a positive skin test for at least one airborne allergen and has been advised to undergo budesonide therapy. The patient is currently not on any medication for allergic rhinitis and has not used any oral, nasal or inhalant corticosteroid agents for at least 2 weeks. The patient has not had any infections of the airways in the past 30 days and has no significant co-morbidities. The patient is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is capable of understanding and following all study procedures. The patient is 18 years or older and has an NIS scale score of > 4 points at the randomization visit.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is generally healthy and has a BMI of 30 kg/m2. She has never smoked and has no significant medical history. She is currently not taking any medications. She leads an active lifestyle, exercising regularly and following a balanced diet. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance medical research. She has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She has no history of cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, endocrinologic, hematologic, hepatic, immunologic, metabolic, urologic, pulmonary, neurologic, dermatologic, psychiatric, renal, or any major disease or malignancy. She has undergone the physical examination, ECG, and clinical laboratory tests and has been found to have no clinically significant abnormalities. She is committed to staying at the clinical unit for the duration of the study and following all study protocols.

52yo man with a history of severe angina pectoris, despite maximal medical therapy, presenting with recurrent chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. He has been evaluated by cardiology and is not a candidate for conventional revascularization procedures due to the location and severity of his coronary artery disease. He has a baseline LVEF of 30% and evidence of ischemia on myocardial stress SPECT imaging. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled on medication. He has no other significant medical history, including no history of cancer or rheumatoid arthritis, and has not had a recent myocardial infarction. He does not have any known occlusive peripheral vascular disease or gastrointestinal hemorrhage.

A 42-year-old accountant has been experiencing chronic low back pain for more than six months. The pain is localized in the lower back and buttocks region and radiates to the back of the left leg. The patient rates his pain as 7/10 on a numeric rating scale. He reports that the pain is worse after sitting for prolonged periods or when he is stressed at work. The patient has tried various pain medications, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and opioids, but they provided only temporary relief. The pain has severely affected his ability to work and perform daily activities. The patient has also been experiencing negative thoughts about his pain, such as worrying that the pain will never go away and that he will never be able to work or enjoy his hobbies again. He has been referred to physical therapy and has attended a few sessions but reports no significant improvement. The patient does not have a history of diabetes or rheumatologic disease and is not pregnant. He is eager to participate in this clinical trial to explore potential associations between his pain catastrophizing thoughts and the ability to dampen pain.

A 52 year old woman diagnosed with Waldenstrom Macroglobulinemia comes to the clinic for a follow-up consultation. She has been experiencing recurrent or refractory symptoms despite multiple treatments. She reports fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged lymph nodes. Her serum IgM level is greater than 2 times the upper limit of normal. She has an ECOG physical strength score of 1. She has no history of other malignant neoplasms or organ transplantation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of ICP-022.

This is a 4-year-old male with no significant past medical history who is scheduled for a bilateral orchidopexy procedure. He is in good health with no pulmonary, cardiac, neurological, hematological, or renal conditions. He does not have a history of being premature or being obese. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial.

Patient is a 60yo man with a diagnosis of coronary artery disease who is scheduled for a trans-radial cardiac catheterization procedure. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin, and aspirin. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who is experiencing moderate to severe symptoms of vulvovaginal atrophy (VVA) such as dryness and dyspareunia. She is currently in the postmenopausal period and has been experiencing these symptoms for several months. She has tried using over-the-counter lubricants and moisturizers, but they have not provided sufficient relief. The patient is generally in good health and has no significant medical history. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements that may interfere with the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial in order to find a safe and effective treatment for her VVA symptoms. She is able to understand the informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and coronary artery disease has been scheduled for an elective surgery. He lives with his wife in their home and is able to perform his activities of daily living independently. He is fluent in Hebrew and Russian and has basic technological knowledge in the use of applications. He has a password to the Maccabi Online website and has wireless internet access at home. He has been evaluated by an anesthesiologist and has a score evaluation of level 2. He does not have any cognitive or dementia problems. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has signed the consent form.

A 42-year-old male patient underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy four days ago. He noticed a small opening in his abdominal incision site which has been gradually getting bigger and more painful. The patient reports no other symptoms and has no significant past medical history. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a 5 cm x 5 cm subcutaneous wound opening in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen with mild erythema and tenderness. Laboratory tests reveal no abnormalities. The patient is diagnosed with an iatrogenic subcutaneous abdominal wound healing-impairment (ISAW) and is eligible for the clinical trial. The patient can be included in the study and undergo either Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (NPWT) or Standard Conventional Wound Therapy (SCWT) for the treatment of his wound.

20-year-old male college student with no history of Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) or illicit drug use. He has at least average IQ and is willing to comply with caffeine specifications for the study. He has no family history of ADHD and has not used Adderall before. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of substance use disorders. He has no contraindications to stimulants such as tics, Tourette's, cardiac disease, or hypertension. He has no uncontrolled medical illness or active contagious infection. The patient is interested in participating in this study to further the research on the effects of stimulant medication on cognitive performance, and is willing to undergo neuroimaging to investigate how participants' expectations of medication affect their performance on neurocognitive tasks.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with advanced cervical cancer that has metastasized to other parts of her body. She has previously received treatment with ordinary paclitaxel and platinum drugs for more than 28 days. Her KPS score is 70, and she is expected to live for more than 3 months. She does not have any brain metastases or other serious complications. Her bone marrow, liver, and kidney function are normal, and she does not have any other malignancy within the last five years. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraception during the trial. The patient has measurable and assessable tumor lesions, and she is compliant and able to follow up regularly. She does not have any mental illness that is difficult to control. The patient is eligible for the clinical study of albumin-bound paclitaxel plus nedaplatin in cervical cancer.

55 y/o African American woman with a BMI of 32, pre-diabetic, and interested in improving her overall health. She works as a customer service representative and spends most of her day sitting. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but is currently managed on medication. She reports difficulty with portion control and finding the motivation to exercise regularly. She is interested in trying new methods to improve her health and is excited about the possibility of participating in a health game tailored to African American older adults. She is fluent in English and has no history of cognitive impairment or physical limitations that would prevent her from participating in a physical activity program.

Maria is a 58 year old woman who recently noticed a sudden blurring in her right eye. She reported that her vision had been normal prior to this and there was no history of trauma to the eye. On examination, her right eye showed retinal vein occlusion with macular edema. Her left eye was normal. Her visual acuity was 20/60 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye. She was referred to the study center for further evaluation and treatment. She has no history of glaucoma or diabetic retinopathy. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not have any other ocular or systemic diseases. Her family history is unremarkable for ocular diseases. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given her informed consent.

The patient is a 55 year old man who was recently diagnosed with persistent atrial fibrillation. He has been experiencing palpitations, shortness of breath and fatigue for the past few months. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are being managed with medications. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol socially. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He is married with two children and leads an active lifestyle, participating in tennis and hiking regularly. He is interested in exploring alternative treatment options as he is not satisfied with the results of anti-arrhythmic drugs. He has not undergone any previous catheter ablation procedures and is willing to participate in the study. His physical examination is unremarkable except for an irregular heart rhythm.

A 62-year-old man presents with a history of prostate cancer. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago and has been on androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for the past 2 years. His PSA levels have been stable, but his testosterone levels remain above castrate range (>150ng/dL). He is experiencing hot flashes, decreased libido, and erectile dysfunction as side effects of ADT. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is married and has no plans to have children. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his side effects and improve his quality of life.

A 46-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years, currently taking metformin and sulfonylurea, presents with a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 30. He complains of difficulty losing weight despite dietary changes and regular exercise. His HbA1c is 8.5%. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works a desk job. He has no history of heart disease, stroke, or other major medical problems. He does not smoke but drinks alcohol occasionally. He is motivated to lose weight and improve his diabetes control. He has not taken any weight loss drugs or participated in any weight loss programs within the past 6 months.

56 year-old man with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease (CKD) who has been receiving hemodialysis for the past 4 months. He has been receiving a stable dose of Epoetin alfa RB (EPOGEN®) for the past 6 weeks with a mean hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dL. The patient's blood pressure is well controlled with medications. He has no history of severe hyperparathyroidism or current use of immunosuppressive therapy. The patient is interested in participating in the study to see if the efficacy of Epoetin alfa DT is equivalent to that of Epoetin alfa RB for the treatment of his anemia.

Mary is a 60-year-old retired teacher who has recently suffered a cerebrovascular accident (CVA). She was admitted to the New York Presbyterian inpatient rehabilitation unit (Baker 17) for rehabilitation. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2, which are both well controlled with medication. She has a supportive family and lives with her husband. Her physical exam reveals right-sided weakness and mild dysarthria. She has no other significant medical problems and is able to participate in routine assessments and rating scales as part of her care. She has agreed to participate in this observational study to help improve stroke rehabilitation outcomes for future patients.

A 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis 2 years ago. He has been experiencing various symptoms such as visual changes, sensory irregularities, and motor coordination issues. He has been on medication, but the side effects have been difficult to tolerate, and he has not experienced significant improvement in his symptoms. The patient is interested in alternative treatments and has been researching stem/stromal cell therapies. He is medically stable and has been cleared by his primary care physician and neurologist. The patient is capable of undergoing the necessary procedures and providing informed consent to participate in the study. He is willing to undergo follow-up neurologic exams with investigators or his own neurologist. The patient is not currently pregnant, and he understands that he should avoid becoming pregnant for three months post-treatment. He meets the inclusion criteria and has the potential for improvement with AD-cSVF treatment.

Patient A is a 14-year-old male who underwent a kidney transplant 2 years ago due to chronic kidney disease. He is currently on immunosuppressive therapy to prevent rejection of the transplanted kidney. He has no history of travel to areas with high prevalence of hepatitis E virus (HEV) and has not been diagnosed with HEV infection before. He is currently asymptomatic and has no abnormal liver function tests. His family has accepted the protocol for the study and they have social security available. The patient will be enrolled in the study to determine the prevalence of HEV infection in pediatric transplant recipients in Lyon.

A 45 year old man with type 2 diabetes and chronic periodontitis comes to the clinic for enrollment in the clinical trial. He has been diagnosed with diabetes for the past 10 years and is currently taking metformin to manage his blood sugar levels. The patient has a history of smoking in the past but quit 2 years ago. He has not received any antibiotic treatment or non-surgical periodontal treatment in the past 6 months. His HbA1c level is currently at 7.5%. On clinical examination, he has bleeding on probing and pockets with a depth of 5mm or more in at least 2 different quadrants. There is radiographic evidence of bone loss and attachment loss. His BMI is 24 kg/m2. The patient is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the role of adipokines in the pathogenesis of periodontal disease and the effect of non-surgical periodontal treatment on these adipokines.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer who has undergone a lumpectomy with axillary dissection. The surgery was successful, but the patient is currently experiencing pain and limited range of motion in her arm. She is interested in exploring alternative therapies to manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life. The patient has no history of autoimmune disease, drug or alcohol abuse, or fibromyalgia. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient has never received acupuncture treatment before. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and meet all other eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). She has a history of smoking, and has been experiencing shortness of breath and persistent cough for about 6 months. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of advanced-stage unresectable NSCLC. She has not undergone any prior surgical or locoregional therapies, but has received chemotherapy for another malignancy several years ago. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score is 1. Her life expectancy is estimated to be at least 12 weeks. She has measureable disease by RECIST criteria. Her laboratory tests show an absolute neutrophil count of 2000 mm3, a platelet count of 120×109 L, a hemoglobin level of 11 g/dL, a total bilirubin level of 1.5 mg/dL, and an aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase (AST/ALT) level of 2 times the upper limit of normal range. Her serum creatinine level is within normal limits. She is not pregnant and is using an adequate method of contraception. She is willing and able to comply with the study and follow-up procedures. The patient does not have PTEN expression by immunohistochemistry, or has known prior activating PI3K or inactivating PTEN gene mutations.

72 year old female with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis presents to the neurosurgery clinic for evaluation of recurrent headaches. MRI reveals a small meningioma and the patient is scheduled for a planned neurosurgical operation lasting up to 4 hours. The patient's preoperative Glasgow Coma Scale is 15 and her American Society of Anesthesiologists risk score is II. The patient is not on any benzodiazepines and has a preoperative blood pressure of 140/85 mmHg. The patient has no known allergies and is not taking any antiepileptic drugs or rifampicin.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of heart failure for over 3 months. He has been experiencing symptoms of shortness of breath, fatigue, and swollen legs, and has been diagnosed with NYHA Class III heart failure. He is currently taking medications for heart failure, but his symptoms are not well controlled. He has no history of other severe illnesses that would limit his survival to less than a year. He understands the English language and can operate the Cordella™ Heart Failure System. He has sufficient cellular and/or Wi-Fi internet coverage at home and is willing to comply with the study protocol. He has given written informed consent to participate in the PRODIGY registry and is willing to return to the treating Investigator for all scheduled follow-up visits. He does not participate in any other investigational trial.

The patient is a 35 year old male of Hispanic origin who was diagnosed with aplastic anemia 2 years ago. He has been receiving regular blood transfusions and has been taking cyclosporine A for the past year. Recently, he has been experiencing episodes of hemoglobinuria and anemia despite the treatment. The patient underwent a Flow cytometry test which confirmed the diagnosis of Subclinical Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) in addition to the aplastic anemia. The patient has not participated in any Levamisole studies before. The patient has a history of hypertension which is under control with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as a software engineer and is excited about the potential of the new treatment option.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV rectal cancer. She has no history of cancer in her family. She has been experiencing rectal bleeding and abdominal pain for the past six months. She underwent a colonoscopy which revealed a rectal mass. She had a CT scan which showed metastasis to her liver. She has not received any treatment for her cancer yet. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She has no history of other medical conditions. She works as a teacher and has two children. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her hematopoietic, hepatic, and renal functions are all within normal limits. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant. She has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy for her metastatic disease. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and comply with its requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old African American man who has been diagnosed with stage IV chronic kidney disease. He has been receiving medical treatment for the past year and his condition has not improved. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a delivery driver and has some difficulty performing his job due to fatigue and weakness. He is interested in receiving a kidney transplant but is hesitant to discuss the possibility of living related kidney donation with his family due to cultural and emotional barriers. He has concerns about the process and fears that he may not be able to afford the medical expenses. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. He is not currently on dialysis and has no history of cancer, heart disease, liver disease, HIV or chronic infections. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that offers culturally tailored behavioral interventions to help him and his family make informed decisions about living related kidney donation.

This clinical trial is seeking children aged 9-10 years, either born preterm or full-term, who are enrolled in the French school curriculum since 1st grade. The child should have normal medical, neurological, and brain imaging assessments. Non preterm children must be born full term with no abnormal event (>=37 weeks of amenorrhea), while preterm children must be delivered before 33 weeks of amenorrhea. The child should not have any sudden cognitive impairments due to stroke, head injury associated with loss of consciousness for more than one hour, or encephalitis. Additionally, the child should not have any chronic neurological, psychiatric, infectious, or liver condition, endocrine disruption, or past or current medical condition such as cancer, diabetes, chronic lung condition, cardiac, metabolic, hematological, endocrine, or immunological disorder. The child should not be taking medication that may interfere with brain imaging measures (psychotropics, hypnotics, anxiolytics, neuroleptics, benzodiazepine, steroidal anti-inflammatory, anti-epileptics, painkillers, muscle relaxants). The child should not have left-sided handedness, color blindness or non-corrected visual disturbances, diagnosed developmental disorders, diagnosed cerebral palsy, or diagnosed fine motor disturbances. The parents of the child must be affiliated with the Social Security and able to join at each time of the study.

The patient is a 45 year old African American female who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer (MBC) a year ago. She has a history of estrogen receptor positive (ER+) breast cancer and is currently receiving anti-estrogen therapies. She experiences significant side effects such as musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and mood changes. Her previous lab work showed a serum 25(OH)D level of 22 ng/ml, indicating a deficiency in vitamin D. She has a history of kidney stones and is currently taking calcium supplements (500 mg/day). She works as a teacher and has been able to continue working during her treatment. She has a supportive family and a strong social network. She is willing to participate in the study and is committed to complying with the study protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing headaches and blurred vision for the past few weeks. He visited his primary care physician who ordered a brain MRI which discovered a mass in his brain. He was referred to a neurosurgeon who performed a biopsy and confirmed the diagnosis of glioblastoma multiforme. The patient underwent a partial resection of the tumor and is scheduled to receive chemo-radiotherapy with temozolomide as standard of care. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. He is a non-smoker and works as an accountant. His family history is unremarkable for any cancers. He has a Karnofsky Performance Score (KPS) of 70%. His blood work results indicate adequate bone marrow, hepatic and renal functions. He has no known allergies to medications. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and follow study instructions.

A 56-year-old male with a history of ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy presenting with symptomatic heart failure in NYHA functional class III. The patient has an automatic implantable cardioverter defibrillator (AICD) and has had a worsening heart failure hospitalization within the last 6 months. The patient has been receiving appropriate clinical standard of care heart failure therapy for at least 30 days prior to screening. The patient is not a candidate for reasonable revascularization procedures that will produce clinical improvement. The patient has an LV wall thickness ≥ 7mm at the anticipated target injection area. The patient's hemodynamic stability is without IV vasopressors or support devices. The patient is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits and tolerate study procedures. The patient will voluntarily provide a personally-signed and dated informed consent. The patient does not have severe primary valvular heart disease, LV thrombus, or any planned heart failure-related device interventions or planned cardiac procedures. The patient does not have a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack within 3 months of screening, or any active malignancy requiring surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiation in the past 12 months. The patient does not have allergies to any equine, porcine or bovine products, and has a BMI < 40 kg/m2 at screening. The patient is not on anti-angiogenic drugs or chronic exposure to cytotoxic therapy for oncologic or chronic non-oncologic reasons in the prior 3 months or expected requirement over the course of the study. The patient is not currently participating in another interventional clinical trial or receiving experimental intervention within 30 days of screening.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy scheduled for an orthopedic surgery to repair a broken femur after a recent skiing accident. He is in good health and has no history of infectious diseases or bleeding disorders. He is accompanied by his parents who are willing to participate in the trial and provide consent. The patient has adequate forehead surface area available for probe attachment and does not have any skin lesions at the thermometer target site. The surgery is expected to take approximately 2 hours and the patient will be positioned supine during the procedure. The patient is not undergoing any head and neck procedures, cardiothoracic procedures, tonsillectomy, cosmetic, or other brief surgical or nonsurgical procedures. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe knee pain that is affecting her daily activities for the past year. She has been diagnosed with Non-Inflammatory Degenerative Joint Disease (NIDJD). She has tried various conservative treatments, such as physical therapy and medications, but they have not provided significant relief. She has signed up for the ShapeMatch Cutting Guide Functional Outcomes Study to receive a primary total knee replacement (TKR) using the Triathlon® Cruciate Retaining Total Knee System (Triathlon® CR) with patient-specific cutting guides. The patient is willing and able to comply with postoperative scheduled clinical and radiographic evaluations and rehabilitation. She does not have a BMI ≥ 40, varus or valgus deformity greater than 10 degree or flexion contracture greater than 20 degree, or any other exclusion criteria mentioned in the eligibility criteria. The patient is excited to participate in this study to potentially improve her quality of life and alleviate her knee pain.

A 55 year old woman is admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of septic shock. She had a history of diabetes and hypertension. She was originally admitted to the hospital for an infected wound on her leg, which had worsened and resulted in sepsis. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and vasopressors for hypotension. Her laboratory results showed elevated creatinine levels and abnormal liver function tests. The patient was assessed and deemed eligible for a clinical trial investigating the use of therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) in septic patients. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 30 days and is not pregnant. The patient has no history of bleeding disorders or polyneuropathy. She is willing to participate in the study and understand the risks and benefits of the treatment.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who is currently 16 weeks pregnant with her second child. During her first trimester screening test, her healthcare provider informed her that her pregnancy is considered high-risk due to her age. She has no significant medical history and has had a normal pregnancy so far. She works as a marketing executive and enjoys spending time with her husband and four-year-old daughter. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. Her physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any abnormalities. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve prenatal screening methods and provide a safer diagnostic option for future mothers. She is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of colorectal adenocarcinoma with hepatic metastasis. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 and is considered a potential candidate for a major hepatic surgical procedure. The patient has undergone primary tumor and regional nodes resection with clear surgical margins and no evidence of extrahepatic disease. The patient's liver metastases have been determined by a hepatic surgeon

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old woman who has not received an influenza vaccine for at least four years and has no experience in giving intramuscular or subcutaneous injections. She is not currently taking any medications for chronic diseases and has no known allergies to eggs or thimerosal. She is in good health as assessed by the study clinician and is able and willing to provide informed consent. The patient has not received immunosuppressive therapy within 6 weeks of enrollment and has no documented immunosuppressive syndrome. She has not had a serious allergic reaction or other problems after exposure to influenza vaccine and has no active respiratory infections or other illnesses. The patient has no chronic metabolic diseases, renal dysfunction, hemoglobinopathies, or immunosuppression caused by medications or HIV. She has no chronic disorders of the pulmonary or cardiovascular systems, including asthma, and has no history of Guillain-Barré syndrome. The patient is not pregnant nor expecting to become pregnant within the next 6 weeks. She has no history of thrombocytopenia or bleeding disorders and has not received a blood or plasma transfusion of immunoglobulin during the past 12 months. She reports no current drug abuse or alcoholism and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse in the last 5 years. The patient has not taken any immunosuppressive medications for the duration of the study and is not currently participating in any other clinical trial or planning to participate in any clinical trial in the 6 months follow-up period. Finally, the patient is willing and able to return to the clinic for the scheduled one month follow-up.

The patient is a 8-year-old boy who has been struggling with inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity for the past year. His teacher has raised concerns about his behavior in the classroom, and his parents report difficulty with completing homework and maintaining focus during family activities. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has no family history of early onset cardiac disease, autism spectrum disorder, or intellectual disability. The patient will undergo clinical assessment and complete the Vanderbilt ADHD scales to confirm the diagnosis of ADHD. He will be randomized to either the intervention arm, which will receive collaborative tele-mental health care by physicians trained in ADHD assessment and management, or the control arm, which will receive treatment as usual with referral to specialized mental health services at Al Jalila Children's.

A 12 yo F, born to a mother with epilepsy, who was taking Carbamazepine/Tegretol during pregnancy. The child has no known history of exposure to other teratogens during pregnancy, no serious brain injury or medical illness unrelated to AED exposure, and no history of child abuse. She is currently not on any centrally active medication other than sympathomimetics for ADHD. The child's mother, father, and a primary relative of the mother will also participate in the study. The child's mother is fluent in English and has an IQ above 70. The child's medical history includes a diagnosis of ADHD and no special education or remedial math or reading requirements.

A 28 year old female diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) presents with a history of decreased interest in previously enjoyed activities, fatigue, difficulty concentrating and changes in appetite and sleep patterns. She has been taking an antidepressant medication for the past 6 weeks and is stable on her current dose. She is able to read, write and speak the language in which psychometric tests are provided, with acceptable visual and auditory acuity. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to validate reward-related biomarkers in individuals with psychiatric disorders.

55-year-old male with chronic knee pain for the past year due to osteoarthritis. He has tried non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), physical therapy, and cortisone injections with limited relief. He reports difficulty walking and climbing stairs, and his pain has impacted his daily activities and quality of life. He has no known allergies, and his medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. He is able to attend follow-up visits and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to acute cholecystitis. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia and is currently on medication for both conditions. Post-surgery, the patient was intubated due to respiratory failure, and mechanical ventilation was initiated. He has been receiving mechanical ventilation for 11 hours and is eligible for the trial. The patient has no history of cerebral trauma or surgery, and he has not participated in this trial before. He understands the study procedures and willingly signs the written informed consent form.

A 55-year-old Asian male patient presents with a complaint of decreased vision in both eyes for the past 6 months. The patient reports no history of ocular trauma, surgery, or systemic illness. He has a family history of cataract in his mother. The patient is myopic and has an axial eye length of 26.5 mm in both eyes. His best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is 20/100 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. The slit-lamp examination shows mild nuclear cataract in both eyes. The intraocular pressure is within normal limits in both eyes. The patient is deemed a suitable candidate for bilateral cataract surgery and is scheduled for the procedure. He is informed about the clinical trial comparing the Stellaris Standard Infusion with Stellaris Elite and agrees to participate, signing the written informed consent form.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis in the right knee leading to severe pain and reduced mobility. She has been scheduled for a primary total knee arthroplasty. Her body mass index is 31, and she has no pre-existing quadriceps weakness. She has not used opioids within the last 4 weeks. She is able to provide informed consent for regional anesthesia. The patient has an iliac-to-patella distance of 45cm, which meets the inclusion criteria for the study. She has no contraindications to regional anesthesia.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been experiencing lower back pain for the past 6 months. The pain is localized to the lower back and radiates down her left leg. She has tried non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications, but they have not provided long-lasting relief. An MRI revealed grade II degenerative spondylolisthesis at the L4-L5 level with central stenosis. She is interested in surgical intervention and has been referred to a spine surgeon. She has no history of lumbar fusion surgery or spondylolysis. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of the XLIF and TLIF procedures for treating her condition.

A 42-year-old man has been diagnosed with unilateral inguinal hernia and scheduled for herniorrhaphy surgery. He is in good general health with no chronic illnesses and has an ASA physiologic state of II. His BMI is within the normal range. He does not have any bleeding or coagulation disorders, nor does he have renal or hepatic insufficiency. He is not taking any chronic non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications. He has never had a hernia before and this is his first surgery. He experiences occasional mild to moderate pain in his lower abdomen and groin area. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of tizanidine in reducing pain and analgesic consumption after herniorrhaphy.

The patient is a 32-year-old non-smoking female with a BMI of 22, who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She has no known allergies to drugs or other substances. She has not used immunotherapy within the last 3 months and has not been diagnosed with tuberculosis or tested positive for Tuberculin Skin Test or QuantiFeron- TB®-Gold test. She is a non-childbearing potential female who has agreed to use two methods of highly effective contraception for 3 months post last dose if her male partner is included in the study.
