The patient has a pre-bronchodilator Forced expiratory volume in 1 sec( FEV1) of > 70% (adjusted for age, sex, and race) and meets the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) definition of mild asthma. She has normal liver function test results and has screened negative for hepatitis-B surface antigen (HBsAg), antibodies to the hepatitis C (HCV) or antibodies to the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) 1,2.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who has been diagnosed with placenta previa and is scheduled for an emergency cesarean section under epidural anesthesia. She has no history of chronic pain or regular use of analgesics. Her pre-pregnancy BMI was 28. She is currently at 38 weeks and 2 days of gestation. Her past medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension, which was well controlled with medication throughout the pregnancy. She has no known allergies to any medication. She has been informed about the study and has given her consent to participate.

30-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 3 years by a referring psychiatrist. The patient has been stable on treatment for the past 6 months with minor changes in medication. He has a BMI of 23 kg/m² and is medically stable with no significant abnormalities in clinical laboratory tests or vital signs. He has no history of substance dependence within the past 6 months and is a non-smoker. The patient is willing to participate in the pharmacogenomic component of the study, as indicated by the separate written informed consent. He has not failed to respond to two different antipsychotic drugs in the past and has a PANSS score of 60. There is no history of suicidal risk or command hallucinations. The patient is not on clozapine and has not used more than two antipsychotic drugs within 3 months before dosing until follow-up.

Patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of symptomatic patellofemoral osteoarthritis for the past year. He complains of pain in the front of his knee, difficulty with stairs and walking, and occasional swelling. He has been treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and physical therapy in the past without significant improvement. He also has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient is able to read and understand the informed consent and the WOMAC questionnaire. He is willing to comply with the study protocol, including daily medication logs and brace usage. His BMI is 27.5, which is within the inclusion criteria. He has no contraindication to the use of the braces and is motivated to try different bracing options for the management of his knee symptoms.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a body mass index of 32. He reports difficulty sleeping for at least 4 days a week for the past 6 months or longer, with a total sleep time of less than 6.5 hours per day. He also reports struggling with weight loss despite attempting various diet and exercise programs. He has not been diagnosed with any sleep disorders and is not currently taking any medications that affect sleep. He is willing to participate in an 8-week study that aims to improve his sleep quality and quantity through a sleep intervention, in addition to a traditional diet and exercise approach to weight loss. He is available for clinic visits and is able to give written informed consent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). He has undergone sustained therapy of luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone analogue (LHRHA) and bilateral orchiectomy. However, there is evidence of prostate cancer progression despite treatment. He has previously been treated with Abiraterone and Docetaxel, but treatment failed. He is unable to tolerate Docetaxel chemotherapy and is not suitable for it at the time of screening. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) of 1. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He has no history of seizures or cardiovascular disease. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has given voluntary written informed consent.

A 16-year-old Hispanic male presents with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 and a history of type 2 diabetes. He has completed one year of multidisciplinary treatment, which included dietary counseling, exercise, and behavioral therapy, but has not achieved significant weight loss. He is currently taking metformin for his diabetes. He is at Tanner stage 5 and has no known obesity syndromes or brain damage. Vital signs are within normal limits. A comprehensive medical history and physical examination reveal no comorbidities other than diabetes. The patient and his parents have been informed about the study and have consented to participate. They understand the risks and benefits of both surgical and conservative treatment options and are willing to be randomized to either group. The patient will be followed up for a total of 10 years with visits to a multidisciplinary team every 3 months at the Morbid Obesity Center.

This is a 32-year-old female who has been struggling with obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors for the past 5 years. She has been diagnosed with OCD and has tried various forms of therapy and medication with limited success. She is currently receiving outpatient care at Sørlandet Sykehus, Solvang DPS and has a Y-BOCS score of 19. She speaks fluent Norwegian and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to further her treatment options. However, she has a history of bipolar disorder and is currently taking antidepressants. She is willing to remain on a stable dosage of her medication during the four intervention days but is unwilling to refrain from anxiety-reducing substances, such as benzodiazepines, during the two days of exposure. She lives within a 1-hour drive from the treatment location and has a BMI-index that is suitable for participation in psychological treatment. She has not had a full course of prior CBT for OCD.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is 24 weeks pregnant with her first child. She is 171 cm tall, and her weight is 105 kg (BMI: 35.9). She has a history of obesity and has struggled with her weight for several years. She is a homemaker and has been married for three years. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has never had any chronic diseases before pregnancy and has not undergone any gastric bypass or other obesity-related surgeries. She speaks Danish fluently and has given confirmed consent to participate in the study. She is excited about the opportunity to help improve the quality of fetal ultrasound in obese women and is eager to learn more about the alternative techniques that will be used in the study. She is looking forward to the three different fetal ultrasounds at GA 13, 15, and 21 weeks and hopes that participating in the study will help ensure the health of her baby.

The patient is a 56-year-old Caucasian man with a history of cirrhosis, which was diagnosed two years ago due to chronic alcohol abuse. He has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and bloating for the past few months. The patient is currently being treated with spironolactone and rifaximin for his cirrhosis, and he has been compliant with his medications. He has no known drug allergies and no prior history of liver transplant. The patient has a BMI of 27 and is a current smoker, smoking a pack a day for the past 20 years. He has no known history of pneumonia, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis. The patient has provided his consent to participate in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a diagnosis of hypertension and diabetes. He has been struggling to manage his conditions and is interested in finding new ways to improve his cardiovascular health. He is an active Twitter user, regularly engaging with others on the platform and sharing his own experiences with managing chronic illness. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that examines the conversation on Twitter about cardiovascular diseases and their associated sequelae. He is eager to learn more about how social media can be used to improve access to health information and implement behavior modification.

Patient is a 28-year-old female from the United States who is generally healthy and has a history of dentinal hypersensitivity. She has a normal BMI and no significant medical history. She has been taking no medications for the past three months. She has at least two sensitive teeth that meet the study criteria and has not received dental prophylaxis within the last four weeks or desensitizing treatment within the last eight weeks. She does not have any gross periodontal disease or caries and is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and restrictions. She is willing to use the allocated dentifrice as directed and is able to attend all study visits.

A 28-year-old female patient presents to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few months. She describes the pain as intermittent, dull, and located in the upper left quadrant of the abdomen. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Physical examination is unremarkable except for mild tenderness on palpation of the abdomen. Imaging studies reveal a small mass measuring 2.5 cm on the junction of the body and tail of the pancreas. Biopsy confirms it is a benign tumor. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of smoking or alcohol use. She is eager to undergo a minimally invasive surgical approach and is interested in participating in the clinical trial for laparoscopic enucleation of Frantz's tumor of the pancreas.

This is a 45-year-old female patient who has been diagnosed with severe asthma and has been followed in the outpatient clinic for the past year. Despite the treatment conducted, she continues to experience symptoms and has not achieved asthma control. She has a BMI of 35 kg/m2 and her pre-bronchodilator FEV1 is between 50 and 80% predicted. She is a non-smoker and has never been pregnant. She has no history of neoplasia, HIV, or other comorbidities that may interfere with the study. She is willing and able to give her free and informed consent for the study procedures. She has no other lung diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, or any other lung diseases that may interfere with the study evaluation. She is adherent to standard asthma treatment and is able to perform lung function assessment tests. She has not experienced a pulmonary exacerbation in the past 30 days before the first study evaluation. Overall, she fits the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and would be a suitable candidate for the study.

A 54-year-old male presents to the neurology clinic with complaints of tremors in his left hand that have been present for the past 6 months. He reports that the tremors are more pronounced when he is at rest and subside when he is engaged in an activity. He also reports stiffness and difficulty initiating movements, especially in his left leg. He denies any slowness of movements, falls, or loss of balance. He has no significant past medical history, is not on any medications, and denies any family history of neurological disorders. On examination, he has a resting tremor in his left hand, cogwheel rigidity in his left leg, and reduced arm swinging on his left side during ambulation. His gait is steady, and he has no difficulty with tandem walking. The rest of the neurological examination is unremarkable. He is diagnosed with early Parkinson's disease as per UK Brain Bank Criteria and is eligible for the clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of DA-9805. He meets the inclusion criteria as he is a male between 30 and 79 years old, has a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease for two years or less, and is on stable doses of Amantadine for treatment of Parkinson's disease. He has no clinically significant abnormalities in physical exam, neurological exam, and laboratory assessments that would exclude him from the study. He is willing to comply with the study protocol requirements and is capable of providing informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV HER2-positive breast cancer two years ago. She has undergone multiple treatments including chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and targeted therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Despite these treatments, the cancer has continued to progress and spread to other parts of her body. The patient is currently experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and shortness of breath with minimal exertion. She reports mild pain in her bones and joints. Her latest scans show that the cancer has spread to her liver and lungs. Her laboratory results show: white blood cell count: 4,500/ul, absolute neutrophil count: 2,000/ul, platelet count: 120,000/ul, hemoglobin: 9.5 g/dL, bilirubin: 1.2 mg/dL, AST: 60 U/L, ALT: 70 U/L, and creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL. The patient has a performance status of 1 and has not had any recent cardiac issues. She has undergone brain imaging and does not have any active brain lesions. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore different treatment options for her advanced breast cancer.

A 65-year-old Caucasian man was diagnosed with Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD) 6 months ago. He has noticed a gradual decrease in his visual acuity in his right eye, which has been affecting his ability to read and perform other daily activities. He wears prescription glasses for distance, but they do not help with his central vision loss. He has never received any visual rehabilitation training. His past medical history is unremarkable. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use recreational drugs. He is retired and lives with his wife. His hobbies include reading, gardening, and playing chess. He speaks English fluently and has completed high school. His visual acuity in the affected eye is 20/200 (ETDRS scale). His mini-mental state exam score is 28 out of 30. He has no other ocular pathology that can reduce central vision. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares eccentric view (EV) training vs. closed circuit television (CCTV) training for AMD rehabilitation.

8-year-old male diagnosed with mild atopic dermatitis affecting approximately 10% of his body surface area. He has been experiencing sleep difficulties for the past 3 months, including difficulty falling asleep and frequent awakenings during the night. The child has no history of drug abuse or mental health dysfunction, and is compliant with medical appointments. He has not received any medication for insomnia in the past 4 weeks. The child is not taking any antihistamines, oral immunosuppressant medication, or antidepressant medication. He is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to get pregnant. The child has no other medical conditions or previous/current treatments that would preclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male who has no chronic diseases and is not taking any medications. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2 and has no history of drug allergies. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally (less than 5 units per week). He has no history of mental illness and has not participated in any clinical studies within the last 6 months. He is currently not planning to have children or donate sperm during the study or for 3 months after drug administration. He is willing to use double contraception during the study period. The patient is interested in participating in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and smoking presents with shortness of breath on exertion and fatigue. The patient states a gradual onset of symptoms over the past 6 months, along with swelling in both legs. The patient reports no chest pain or palpitations. The patient's medical history includes a previous myocardial infarction (MI) with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) 5 years ago. He was also diagnosed with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and has been receiving optimal medical therapy for the past 6 weeks. The patient's physical examination reveals elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral rales in lung bases, peripheral edema up to mid-thighs, and a regular heart rhythm with a soft systolic murmur. The patient's lab work shows an elevated BNP level, and his echocardiogram reveals a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 40%. The patient is classified as NYHA class II. The patient's medication regimen includes aspirin, a beta-blocker, an ACE inhibitor, and a diuretic. The patient has no history of COPD, PVD, or anemia. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 2-year-old toddler who is enrolled in Early Head Start home visits. The child has no known medical conditions and is developmentally on track for their age. The child's parents have expressed concerns about their child's eating habits, as the child often refuses to eat certain foods and has a preference for sugary snacks. The child's parents are motivated to participate in the study and are willing to have the curriculum delivered during their home visits. The child's parents are able to provide informed consent for their child's participation in the study.

25-year-old female psychology undergraduate student who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past year. The pain is described as a constant dull ache and is exacerbated by prolonged sitting or standing. The patient has tried various treatments including physical therapy, massage, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but none have provided significant relief. The patient has no history of seizures, head injury or neurological illness, and is not taking any analgesic medication at present. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. The patient does not have any metal in her head or any implanted medical devices.

45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago and underwent mastectomy and chemotherapy. She has completed her treatment and has been cancer-free for 18 months. She reports experiencing difficulty with concentration and memory since her treatment ended. She is fluent in English and able to walk unassisted. She has no history of dementia or organic brain syndrome and is not currently pregnant. She is interested in participating in a research study aimed at improving cognitive function in breast cancer survivors through physical activity. She has consulted with her physician, who has given consent for her to participate in the study.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has recently received a diagnosis of acromegaly. She has never received any treatment for the disease and has a microadenoma measuring less than 10mm. She is experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, hyperhidrosis, headache, swelling of extremities, arthralgia, and carpal tunnel syndrome. Her GH levels are above 2.5 μg/liter, and her IGF-I levels are also abnormal. She has not undergone surgery or radiotherapy for the condition. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form. She does not have a mixed GH-PRL adenoma and does not require immediate surgery due to neurological symptoms or emergency conditions.

This is a 27 year old female with a history of physician-diagnosed asthma who experiences symptoms of wheezing and shortness of breath during and after exercise. She has been a non-smoker for the past year and has a smoking history of less than 1 pack year. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and agrees to practice an adequate birth control method for the duration of the study. She has not had an asthma exacerbation in the last 4 weeks and has no history of severe reaction to allergy skin testing. At Visit 1, she will complete questionnaires about demographics, asthma control, and exercise habits. Skin prick testing for allergies will be performed and she will undergo sputum induction and peripheral blood drawn for microRNA analysis. At Visit 2, she will undergo baseline spirometry and Eucapnic Voluntary hyperventilation testing, followed by a second exhaled nitric oxide quantification, sputum induction, and peripheral blood drawn for microRNA analysis. The total time for both visits will be approximately 5 hours.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Marfan syndrome at the age of 13. She has a family history of the disorder, as her mother and two siblings also have Marfan syndrome. The patient has a known mutation in the FBN1 gene and has experienced a range of symptoms, including joint pain, scoliosis, and vision problems. She has undergone multiple surgeries to correct these issues, including spinal fusion and lens replacement. Despite her condition, the patient is active and enjoys hiking and yoga. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to further understand the variability of the disorder and potentially improve care for future patients.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been experiencing vision changes in her left eye for the past few months. She reports blurry vision, difficulty reading, and distortion of straight lines. She has been previously diagnosed with Leber's miliary aneurysm after undergoing a fluorescein angiography which revealed many aneurysms with leakage in the temporal mid-peripheral retina and near the macula. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed moderate to marked cystoid macular edema and subretinal fluid. There were no abnormal findings in the cornea, anterior chamber, or lens. The patient has no known allergies or previous adverse reactions to intravitreal injections or laser photocoagulation. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and provide written informed consent.

45 yo F with persistent knee pain for the past 9 months, despite multiple consultations with various physicians, and inconclusive x-rays and MRI. The patient has described her pain as sharp and localized to the medial aspect of the knee, with occasional radiation to the hip and thigh region. She reports difficulty with weight-bearing activities and has had to take time off from her job as a cashier due to the pain. Upon examination, the patient exhibited tenderness to palpation in the retro trochanteric region and responded positively to a local anesthetic injection in the area. She will be enrolled in the study for further evaluation and randomized to either a stretching regime or conservative and symptomatic treatment. Past Medical History: - Hypothyroidism - Seasonal allergies - History of depression, currently on sertraline - No history of hip or knee surgery - No history of trauma to the lower extremities

A 32-year-old right-handed female suffered a mild traumatic brain injury from a car accident 9 months ago. She has fully recovered from the injury and is now interested in participating in a study to improve her motor function. She has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, drug or alcohol abuse, or cognitive deficits. She is able to concentrate and perform tasks required for the study. She has no metal in her body and has no visual disturbances. She is not pregnant and is willing to commit to the time involved in the study. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study. Her Edinburgh handedness inventory shows a laterality index (LI) of greater than 75 for dexterity. She has never played a musical instrument or been trained as a typist. She has not experienced any post-traumatic seizures or litigation regarding the trauma.

45 y/o female with chronic periodontitis and multiple teeth with periodontal probing pocket depths ≥ 5 mm. No known allergies to penicillin or history of autoimmune diseases. No recent consumption of systemic antimicrobial or anti-inflammatory drugs in the last 2 months. No history of prosthetic heart valve replacement, skeletal joint replacement, previous infective endocarditis, or rheumatic fever. No current pregnancy or lactation. No known history of diabetes or hypertension.

A 32-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis has been taking interferon beta-1a for the past year, but has been experiencing spasticity in her legs. She has recently discussed her symptoms with her neurologist and has decided to transition to glatiramer acetate (Copaxone®) for the next 6 months. She is able to ambulate with unilateral support and understands, speaks, and reads English. She is interested in participating in the study to determine if transitioning to glatiramer acetate (Copaxone®) will decrease her spasticity and improve her quality of life. She has no history of severe gait disability or total gait disability. She is willing to complete the study instruments and sociodemographic questionnaire via email or mail, and is committed to returning them at the end of the study period.

Patient is a preterm infant born at 28 weeks gestational age who required mechanical ventilation for respiratory support within the first 7 postnatal days. The infant has no major congenital anomalies or neuromuscular diseases. The patient has been stable for at least 6 hours with FiO2 < 0.40, PaCO2 < 65 mmHg, pH > 7.20, and MAP < 7 cm H2O. The infant will be included in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness and safety of HHHFNC and nCPAP techniques for preventing extubation failure. The patient will receive either oxygen-air mixture of 4-6 l/min flow rate in the HHHFNC group or pressure set to 5-8 cm H2O in the nCPAP group. The patient will be monitored for reintubation criteria such as apnea, acidosis, and increased need for FiO2. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the two methods in preventing extubation failure within 7 days following the first extubation.

The patient is a 25 year old female who suffered from a burn injury about 3 months ago. The burn injury occurred on her right forearm and has resulted in a raised, red and itchy scar. She is experiencing difficulty moving the affected area and is quite self-conscious about the appearance of the scar. She is Fitzpatrick skin type III and resides in Winnipeg. She has not received any previous treatment for the scar and has no history of keloid scarring. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve the appearance of her scar and regain full range of motion in her forearm.

A 50-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with low to intermediate risk prostate cancer after a transperineal prostate biopsy. He has a serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level of 12 ng/mL and a clinically significant lesion that correlates with an mpMRI visible lesion. He has not received any prior radiation therapy to the pelvis or androgen suppression therapy for prostate cancer. He has not used a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor in the past 3 months. He has a life expectancy of at least 10 years and is willing to undergo transrectal ultrasound (TRUS). He does not have any known allergies to latex or gadolinium (Gd). He has not undergone previous electroporation, radiofrequency ablation, high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU), cryosurgery, thermal or microwave therapy to treat cancer of the prostate. The patient is willing to undergo pelvic MRI scanning and meet all the other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45 year old male who was admitted to the hospital due to worsening respiratory distress. The patient is currently receiving positive pressure ventilation via an endotracheal tube and is on enteral nutrition support. A chest radiograph showed bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and a PaO2 to FiO2 ratio of less than 200. The patient has no clinical evidence of left atrial hypertension. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient's blood work showed no abnormalities and he is negative for HIV. The patient has no known food allergies and is not taking any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or ketoconazole. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 2-year-old girl with a history of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis. Her parents report a history of itchy, dry and flaky skin on her arms, legs, and face. The child has Fitzpatrick skin type III, and the atopic dermatitis severity index (ADSI) score is 5 with an erythema sub-score of 3, indicating moderate severity. The child has not used any prescription or over-the-counter eczema treatments for the past 3 days, and the parents are willing to continue this for the duration of the trial. The child has no known allergies or adverse reactions to skincare products or the investigational products (IPs). The child does not have any other skin conditions that may influence the outcome of the study. The child's parents are not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman diagnosed with schizophrenia. She experiences auditory hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech. She is currently taking antipsychotic medication, but still struggles with cognitive deficits and difficulty with daily functioning. She lives alone and is currently unemployed. She is willing to try new treatments to improve her cognitive functioning and reduce her symptoms. She has no history of substance abuse or dependence, traumatic brain injury, or visual or auditory impairments that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is fluent in English and able to read and write. She is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been a heavy drinker for the past 15 years. He consumes about 12-15 drinks per day. He smokes a pack of cigarettes per day and has a sedentary lifestyle. He recently experienced abdominal pain, jaundice, and loss of appetite. He visited the hospital and was diagnosed with severe alcoholic hepatitis based on elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels. He was informed about the high mortality rate associated with this condition and was offered a chance to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the safety and efficacy of G-CSF therapy. The patient is willing to participate and meets the eligibility criteria, including having a Maddrey's Discriminant Function score of ≥ 32. He understands the potential benefits and risks of the trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old female office worker who presents with chronic neck pain that has been ongoing for the past 6 months. She reports experiencing a dull ache in her neck that radiates up to the base of her skull and down to her shoulders. The pain is worse when she sits in front of a computer for prolonged periods. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and hot/cold packs, but the pain has persisted. She has no history of whiplash injury or cervical/thoracic spine injury. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. Her vital signs are normal, and she is able to perform all activities of daily living. She rates her neck pain as a 7 out of 10 on the pain scale. She is motivated to participate in the study to improve her neck pain and function. Her baseline NDI-TH score is 15 percent.

54-year-old male patient with a subacute ischemic stroke that occurred 3 months ago. The patient has muscle weakness in the extensors and knee flexors on the Lovetta scale below 3 and functional disorders of the lower limb. The patient is currently undergoing rehabilitation therapy and has shown good cooperation with the therapist. The patient has no cognitive impairment and is able to understand commands. The patient has not undergone any other rehabilitation therapy in the past 28 days. The patient does not have rigid fixed contractures within the lower limb and has no significant spasticity according to the Ashworth scale.

A 50-year-old woman with a history of mild liver disease presents with complaints of fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and occasional nausea. She has a history of alcohol consumption but has been sober for the past year. Her liver function tests show mild elevations in AST and ALT levels, and her Child-Pugh score is Class A. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of tasimelteon in individuals with mild or moderate liver disease. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and restrictions and is using an acceptable method of birth control. She has not taken any investigational drugs within the past 30 days and has not donated blood or experienced significant illness within the past two months. She does not have a history of autonomic dysfunction or bronchospastic disease. She is not pregnant or lactating and does not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 12 months. She is willing to limit her smoking consumption during the study period. Her physical examination and laboratory evaluation are consistent with her mild liver disease. She agrees to participate in the study and undergo a single 20-mg dose of tasimelteon, after which safety assessments will be performed.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing knee pain and discomfort for the past year. She has a history of knee injury due to a sports-related accident that resulted in osteochondral lesions on both knees. She had previously undergone mosaicplasty and ACI more than 18 months ago, but there has been no improvement in her symptoms. Her subjective International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) score is less than 65, indicating disabling and clinically meaningful symptoms. She has no significant obesity with a BMI less than 30. She has accompanying ligamentous and meniscal lesions, joint malalignment and patella femoral instability which would be corrected concurrently. The patient is able to understand and sign the informed consent form and is affiliated with a national health insurance system. She has undergone a pregnancy test, which was negative, and is willing to use an effective birth control method during the entire study. The patient has no history of osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or any other condition of the knee joint likely to compromise the allograft's outcome. There is no excessive laxity or recurrent instability that could affect the score evaluation without concomitant ligamentoplasty. The patient has no history of ulcerative disease, heavy smoking, tuberculosis, chronic psychiatric disorder, or disease requiring long-term treatment with a medication that would affect bone or joint metabolism. She has no history of cancer or a current diagnosis of cancer. The patient is not deprived of her freedom by a judicial or administrative decision and is able to provide her consent.

The patient is a newborn infant born to a mother who experienced a spontaneous preterm delivery at 35 weeks of gestation. The mother had foul-smelling amniotic fluid during labor. The infant was born at the CNHU (Centre National Hospitalier et Universitaire, Cotonou, Benin). The mother lives in Abomey-Calavi, Benin. The infant is at high risk for developing sepsis and will be enrolled in the study to assess neonatal immune dysfunction associated with the risk of newborn sepsis in a malaria-endemic area in Benin. The parents have consented to participate in the study. The infant has no known HIV exposure, and the mother's HIV status is negative.

A 3-year-old female named Emily, who attends a licensed childcare center in a low-income community in Maryland, is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. Emily is a healthy and active child, who attends childcare center 5 days a week. Her caregiver is her mother, who is fluent in English and willing to participate in the study. The childcare center staff is also willing to participate in the trial. Emily has no health problems that would interfere with her participation in physical activities. Her mother is excited to participate in the trial to help promote healthy habits for her daughter and reduce the risk of pediatric obesity.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HPV16-associated cervical cancer (stage II) a year ago. She has completed definitive treatment and has no evidence of disease recurrence. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1. The patient has not received any HPV vaccination before. She has no history of immunosuppression, active autoimmune disease, or other medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study schedule and other protocol requirements. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and has completed her primary treatment. She lives in Bernalillo County, New Mexico and is interested in improving her lifestyle behaviors to promote her overall health and wellbeing. She currently consumes fewer than 5 servings of fruits and vegetables per day and does not meet the recommended guidelines for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity. She has no pre-existing medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in a home gardening intervention, such as severe orthopedic conditions or recent surgery. She has no prior experience with vegetable gardening and is excited to learn from a certified Master Gardener as part of the "Southwest Harvest for Health" program. She has access to a location with adequate sunlight and running water and is able to participate in the 10-month intervention from mid-February through early November 2020. She is committed to making positive lifestyle changes and is excited to participate in this program to improve her physical functioning and health-related quality of life.

A 4-year-old boy from a rural area in Senegal will be enrolled in this study to assess the impact of national Vitamin A Deficiency (VAD) control strategies in Senegalese children. The study will measure the current vitamin A total body stores in relation to his infectious status. The child is not planning to move from the study area for the duration of the study and does not have severe illness at the time of enrollment. He will receive doses of labeled vitamin A: 6µmol of D4-Vitamin A, and 6 µmol of D8-Vitamin A at d0 and d44 respectively. Blood sampling will be done 3 times during the study: at Baseline (d-7) and 2 weeks after each dose of labeled vitamin A (d14 and d58). The blood will be drawn from the child and immediately wrapped on aluminum foil and placed in a cooler while in the field. The blood samples will be transported to the lab and treated under dim light. Dietary intake information will be collected using 24 hour recall questionnaire, food frequency questionnaire, and infectious frequency questionnaire will be submitted to the child's mother at d-7. Anthropometric measurements (weight and height) of the child will be recorded also at d-7. The study design is longitudinal with repeated measures and will be implemented in rural area. The study aims to identify health, socioeconomic and food determinants that can influence children's micronutrient status.

Patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing vaginal discharge and a fishy odor for the past week. She has also noticed irritation and itching in the vaginal area. Upon visiting her healthcare provider, she was diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis through the Amsel test. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the effectiveness of a vaginal tablet containing lactose in modulating the bacterial flora of women with BV. She is willing to take one tablet of lactose or placebo twice a day for 7 days and is able to provide written informed consent.

10 yo M with a recent injury to the right arm after a fall from a bike, presenting with a dislocated both-bone forearm fracture. The fracture was repositioned and stabilized, and the patient is now being considered for enrollment in a randomized clinical trial to compare treatment with and without Kirschner wire fixation. The patient is under the age of 16 and meets the inclusion criteria for the trial. The patient's medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The study will involve outpatient clinic visits and monitoring for a period of 6 months to assess the number of re-dislocations, re-operations, consolidation and dislocation on X-ray, function of both arms, complaints in daily living, and any complications. The patient and their guardians have provided informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been struggling with his weight for the past year. He has a BMI in the 99th percentile and has been diagnosed with obesity. He has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. He has been referred to the pediatric weight management program at Baystate Children's Hospital by his primary care physician. He is currently not involved in any regular physical activity and has a poor diet consisting of fast food, sugary drinks and snacks. He owns a smartphone and is able to read and understand English. He is interested in using technology to help him make healthy lifestyle changes and is open to using the Kurbo app as part of his weight management program.

15-year-old female presented to the emergency department with a sudden onset of fever, headache, and neck stiffness. The patient's mother also reported that her daughter was feeling lethargic and had a decreased appetite. Upon examination, the patient was found to have a fever of 102°F, nuchal rigidity, and positive Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs. Blood tests showed elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein levels. Lumbar puncture was performed, which revealed cloudy cerebrospinal fluid with elevated protein and low glucose levels. Neisseria meningitidis was isolated from the cerebrospinal fluid culture. The patient was admitted to the hospital and treated with intravenous antibiotics. She recovered well and was discharged after a week of hospitalization.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension under control with medication. He has no history of hospitalization in the last six months due to illness or any other significant medical conditions. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive medication or corticosteroids. He has not received any live virus vaccine within the past 28 days or killed virus vaccine in the last 14 days. He has not received any influenza vaccine in the past 6 months. He has no known allergy to egg proteins. He has not received any blood products in the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in the study, understands the study requirements, and is willing to comply with all aspects of the study protocol.

A 4-year-old male child with no significant medical history was brought by his parents to the School of Dentistry at the University of Sao Paulo, Brazil, for dental treatment. The parents reported that the child has never had any dental problems before, and they were concerned about his dental health. Upon examination, the dentist noted that the child had at least one primary molar in his mouth. The child did not present any behavior problems during the examination. The dentist informed the parents about a clinical trial being conducted to evaluate the impact of radiographic examination on the diagnosis and treatment decision of caries lesions in primary teeth, and asked if they would be interested in participating. The parents agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent form. The child was randomly allocated to the experimental group, which would receive a radiographic examination in addition to the visual inspection for caries detection. The dentist performed the necessary procedures and elaborated a treatment decision plan. The child will be followed up for 2 years, with evaluations after 12 and 24 months after the ingress of the child in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who recently had a routine check-up and was found to have high cholesterol levels. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having suffered a heart attack in his late 50s. The patient is currently not taking any medications for cholesterol control but has been advised by his physician to start taking Crestor (rosuvastatin). He works as a bank manager and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He does not have any significant medical history and has not been hospitalized in the past. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has a BMI of 28, indicating that he is slightly overweight. He has recently started to make some dietary changes and is trying to incorporate more fruits and vegetables into his meals. He has agreed to participate in this study to help evaluate the effectiveness of Crestor in reducing his cholesterol levels and his risk of heart disease.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with chronic HCV infection. Her genotype is 1b, and she has non-severe fibrosis as per the Metavir score. She has insulin resistance and is currently on medication for diabetes mellitus. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for antiviral treatment and has no prior exposure to any IFN, RBV, or approved or experimental HCV-specific DAA. She is generally in good health, with the exception of her chronic HCV infection and glucose abnormalities. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent and comply with the dosing instructions for study drug administration. She has no history of significant psychiatric disorder or malignancy within the past five years. She is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use two effective methods of contraception during the study and for 14 days after the last dose of study drugs. She does not have any significant drug allergies and is not currently participating in any other clinical trial. Her laboratory parameters at screening show normal ALT and AST levels, direct bilirubin levels within normal limits, platelets above 75,000/μL, creatinine clearance above 50 mL/min, hemoglobin above 10 g/dL, albumin above 3 g/dL, and INR within normal limits. She has no chronic liver disease of a non-HCV etiology, no infection with HIV or HBsAg, and no clinically-relevant alcohol or drug abuse within the past 12 months. She is not currently taking any prohibited concomitant medication.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman with a clinical diagnosis of type 1 diabetes for more than a year. She has been using an insulin pump and insulin for at least six months and consistently using insulin parameters such as carbohydrate ratio and correction factors to dose insulin for meals or corrections. The patient has access to the internet and is willing to upload data during the study as needed. She is not currently known to be pregnant or breastfeeding, and if sexually active, she agrees to use a form of contraception to prevent pregnancy while participating in the study. The patient is willing to suspend the use of any personal CGM for the duration of the clinical trial once the study CGM is in use. She is willing to switch to lispro (Humalog) or aspart (Novolog) if not already using and to use no other insulin besides lispro (Humalog) or aspart (Novolog) during the study. The patient's total daily insulin dose (TDD) is at least 10 U/day, and she is willing not to start any new non-insulin glucose-lowering agent during the course of the trial. The patient is willing to eat at least 100 grams of carbohydrates per day and has an understanding and willingness to follow the protocol and signed informed consent. The patient does not have a history of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or severe hypoglycemia resulting in seizure or loss of consciousness in the 12 months prior to enrollment. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the trial and is not breastfeeding. The patient does not have a history of cardiac arrhythmia, clinically significant electrocardiogram (ECG) abnormality, or use of diuretics (e.g. Lasix, Thiazides). Her eGFR lab value is equal to or above 60 mL/min/1.73 m². The patient does not have a known medical condition that might interfere with the completion of the protocol such as severe renal impairment, end-stage renal disease, or dialysis. The patient is not currently enrolled in another clinical trial and does not have a family member employed by Tandem Diabetes Care, Inc. or having a direct supervisor at the place of employment who is also directly involved in conducting the clinical trial. The patient is willing to restrict alcohol to no more than 2 drinks per night in men and no more than 1 drink per night in women and is not on a low carb diet (less than 100g per day).

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC) 3 months ago. The tumor was confirmed to be wild-type KRAS by a central laboratory. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has previously received a regimen containing irinotecan for metastatic disease and a regimen containing oxaliplatin for metastatic disease. She has also previously received a thymidylate synthase inhibitor (fluorouracil) for treatment of CRC. Her disease has progressed despite these treatments, and she now presents with a measurable lesion per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1 guidelines. She has adequate hematologic, renal, hepatic, and metabolic function. She has not received prior anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) therapy, small molecule EGFR inhibitors, or any antitumor therapy within 21 days before randomization, and has not received radiotherapy within 14 days before randomization. Her corrected QT (QTc) interval is within normal limits. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

Karen is a 54 year old woman who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her right big toe for the past 6 months. She has difficulty walking and is unable to wear her favorite shoes due to the discomfort. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not provided much relief. Her medical history is notable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are managed with medication. She has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. On examination, there is tenderness and swelling in the first metatarsophalangeal joint and limited range of motion. X-rays confirm the diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the great toe. She has good bone stock and is a candidate for arthrodesis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of an implant in the treatment of her osteoarthritis.

A 35 year old woman with a BMI of 32 is concerned about her high sugar diet and its potential link to cancer. She reports consuming at least 3 servings of sugary foods per day, such as candy, soda, and baked goods. She does not have any medical or psychiatric conditions that would interfere with compliance with the diet recommendations. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has not undergone bariatric surgery. She has not experienced any significant weight loss in the past six months and has not started or changed the dosage of any weight-affecting medication in the past three months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the effectiveness of a home computer-based inhibitory control training in reducing her intake of high-sugar foods and improving her overall diet.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of smoking and high blood pressure. He experiences leg pain when walking short distances, which improves with rest. He has no history of diabetes or heart disease. He is currently taking medications for his blood pressure. On examination, his leg pulses are weak, and he has decreased sensation in his feet. An ultrasound shows a blockage in his femoral artery. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of this condition and has no known allergies to heparin, aspirin, clopidogrel, paclitaxel, paclitaxel compounds and contrast agents. He is able to comply with the study protocol and is willing to sign the informed consent.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who was diagnosed with glioblastoma 3 years ago and has undergone concomitant temozolomide chemotherapy with radiotherapy. He has experienced one previous recurrence/progression of glioblastoma and has reintroduced an altered schedule of temozolomide. He has KPS score of 90 and has a confirmed measurable lesion by response assessment in neuro-oncology criteria. He is otherwise healthy and has no other known malignancies or major comorbidities. He has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks and is willing to sign an informed consent form. He is not currently taking any VEGF targeted agents and has not undergone major surgery or investigational drug treatment in the past 4 weeks.

Patient is a 15-year-old male with a BMI in the 99th percentile for his age and gender. He has a history of being overweight since childhood and has tried various diets and exercise programs with limited success. He has no known chronic medical conditions and is not taking any weight-loss-inducing medications. He has not participated in any other weight loss-study or slimming diet in the past 2 months. The patient and his parents have expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial that could help him achieve a healthier weight and improve his metabolic parameters. The patient is able to comply with the study requirements, including attending weekly sessions with a dietitian and a psychologist, completing self-reports of food diaries, and undergoing regular tests and measurements over a 12-week intervention period and 9-months of follow-up. The patient is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) by a board-certified psychiatrist according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition. He has a total score of 6 on the 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAM-D). He is right-handed and aged between 18 to 35 years. He has no history of major depressive episode within the past three months. He has no pacemaker or deep brain stimulation and no metal implants in the head or neck area. He has no other major mental disorders including autism spectrum disorders, mental retardation, psychotic disorders, bipolar disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and neurocognitive disorders. He has no history of alcohol or other illicit substance abuse. He has no neurological diseases involving the central nervous system and no major debilitating systemic diseases. He is not pregnant and not breast-feeding. He does not smoke cigarettes and has no color blindness. He has not taken part in another study within the last 4 weeks.

The patient is a 58-year-old Caucasian female who has experienced multiple episodes of syncope in the past few months. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She reports feeling lightheaded and dizzy before each episode of syncope, but has not experienced any chest pain or shortness of breath. Her physical exam is unremarkable, with no signs of heart failure or arrhythmia. An electrocardiogram (ECG) reveals sinus bradycardia with a heart rate of 40 beats per minute. A Holter monitor confirms frequent episodes of sinus pauses greater than 3 seconds, consistent with bradyarrhythmic syncope. The patient is deemed eligible for the clinical trial and undergoes pacemaker implantation. She is followed up for the occurrence of any syncopal relapses after the procedure.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing migraines for the past 5 years. She describes the headaches as pulsing and moderate to severe in intensity, and she experiences nausea and sensitivity to light and sound during the attacks. She has tried various medications prescribed by her neurologist, including NSAIDs and Propranolol, but has not found significant relief. She has a history of mild iron deficiency anemia but is otherwise healthy. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she does not have any active skin lesions or wounds over the PC6 acupoints. She works as a teacher and is married with no children. She is interested in trying a non-pharmacological approach to managing her migraines and is willing to participate in a clinical trial testing the effectiveness of acupressure at PC6. She is willing to complete the Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS) questionnaire and comply with the study requirements.

50-year-old male diagnosed with advanced oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma with T4 classification, who is eligible for neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by radiotherapy concomitant to chemotherapy. The patient has not undergone any head and neck surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy in the past. The patient is able to comprehend speech pathology intervention and has no cognitive deficits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent before any specific procedure.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder for the past 5 years. She experiences episodes of both mania and depression, which have negatively impacted her personal and professional life. She is currently taking lithium and has had some success with managing her symptoms, but she continues to have occasional mood swings. She has no history of schizophrenia or other psychiatric disorders. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history and takes no other medications. She is willing to participate in this clinical trial to help advance research on treatments for bipolar disorder.

A 62-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with difficulty breathing, coughing, and wheezing, which had been worsening over the past week. He had a history of COPD for 10 years and had been a heavy smoker for more than 30 years. His symptoms were not relieved by his inhaler, and he had to use his rescue inhaler multiple times a day. He had a history of hospitalization for COPD exacerbation two years ago. His oxygen saturation was 88% on room air, and his arterial blood gas showed a pH of 7.21, partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) of 65 mmHg, and partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2) of 55 mmHg. He was diagnosed with acute exacerbation of COPD and was admitted to the ICU. The patient was evaluated for non-invasive mechanical ventilation (NPPV) with perfect monitoring conditions and reasonable human resource allocation. The patient agreed to participate in the study and met the inclusion criteria.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with severe heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30%. He experiences shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion. He has a prolonged QRS duration of 140ms and has been referred for conventional cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT). His past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidaemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no allergies to any medication. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 70 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to give consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with glaucoma in both eyes. He complains of occasional blurry vision and has been using timolol eye drops twice daily for the past six months. Despite using the medication, his intraocular pressure (IOP) remains high. He has no other significant ocular or medical history. He does not wear contact lenses and has not undergone any eye surgeries or laser procedures in the past six months. He has not used oral or injectable corticosteroids in the past three weeks. He is willing to participate in the study and can attend all scheduled visits.

68yo male with a history of atrial fibrillation and hypertension, currently on Rivaroxaban for the past 6 months for prevention of stroke and systemic embolism. He is compliant with his medication and has not experienced any major bleeding events. Patient reports occasional dizziness and fatigue, but otherwise has good functional status. He is fluent in German and willing to participate in a survey and phone interview regarding his satisfaction with treatment and quality of life related to his anticoagulation therapy.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing menstrual pain (dysmenorrhoea) for many years. The pain is usually severe and affects her daily activities, including work and social life. She has tried using different painkillers, but they only provide temporary relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new treatment option for dysmenorrhoea, called the OVA TENS apparatus. She is not currently pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study period. She is willing to commit to using the apparatus during every other menstruation for a period of four months and to fill in daily forms about her pain perception. She hopes that this study will provide her with a more effective treatment option for her menstrual pain.

A 28 yo F who has been wearing lotrafilcon A contact lenses in both eyes for at least 5 days a week, 8 hours a day, for the past 6 months. She removes her contact lenses daily as prescribed by her regular eye care practitioner. She has a distance visual acuity of at least 20/40 in each eye with her current lenses. She has not had any eye injury or surgery within the past year, is not currently enrolled in any clinical trial, and has not had corneal refractive surgery in the past.

A 62-year-old male with a history of localized prostate cancer treated with high dose rate radiation therapy is experiencing a recurrence of the cancer. The patient has a prostate volume less than 50 cm3 and is not eligible for surgery or curative radiotherapy. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is expected to survive for at least 8 months. The patient has sufficient bone marrow reserve and adequate renal and hepatic function. The patient does not have locally advanced or metastatic disease and has not been treated with seed implantation brachytherapy. The patient's Gleason score at initial diagnosis was less than 8. The patient has not had surgery within the past week and does not have a concomitant infection or severe concurrent disease. The patient has the mental capacity to understand and give informed consent and is not allergic to verteporfin for injection (VFI) or porphyrins. The patient is not currently enrolled in another therapeutic clinical study and does not have a history of grade 3 or greater proctitis attributed to radiation.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities for the past 6 months. She has difficulty sleeping and has lost her appetite, resulting in significant weight loss. She feels fatigued and has difficulty concentrating on tasks. She has no past history of depression or psychiatric illness. She is not currently taking any medication and has no known allergies. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for the 8-week duration of the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been experiencing mutational falsetto for the past year. He has a history of vocal strain due to excessive singing during his college years. He works in a call center and his voice has been affecting his job performance. He has tried voice therapy and vocal exercises, but they have not been effective. He has no history of smoking or allergies to medical tape. He has a BMI of 22 and has no cognitive limitations. He is willing to provide consent for the study.

A 58-year-old male patient presents with complaints of abdominal pain and weight loss. The patient has a history of hepatitis B and has been regularly screened for liver function. The patient's most recent liver function tests revealed elevated liver enzymes and an AFP level of 120 ng/mL. A triphasic CT scan was performed, which showed a 5 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver with evidence of vascular invasion. A liver biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy or other malignancies. The patient's comorbidities are well-controlled, with the exception of mild renal failure. The patient has been informed of the trial and has given informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with chronic liver disease of unknown etiology. She has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past year. A recent liver biopsy showed stage 2 fibrosis by Metavir score. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient's BMI is 32 kg/m2. She has no known history of cardiac disease or bleeding diathesis. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, and there is no evidence of hepatic decompensation. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and provide written informed consent. She is not pregnant and is willing to use contraception as specified by the study protocol.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who suffers from chronic low back pain and difficulty walking due to degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis (DLSS). She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months, which have gradually worsened over time. She describes the pain as a dull ache that radiates down to her legs and is aggravated by walking and standing. The pain score measured by NRS questionnaire is 6 out of 10. The patient has tried various medications, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but they have not provided significant relief. An MRI scan revealed mild-moderate-severe lumbar central canal spinal stenosis. The patient has a Roland-Morris score of 10. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for DLSS. The patient has no history of spinal instability or other serious medical conditions. She is not currently taking any pain control drugs and has not received acupuncture in the past 30 days. She is mentally competent and able to give informed consent.

N/A - This clinical trial is not recruiting patients. It is focused on testing the efficacy of a new disinfectant against C. difficile and evaluating its impact on reducing the incidence of CDAD. Therefore, patient descriptions are not applicable for this trial.

Group 1-3: This is a 68 year-old female with no history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus, acute inflammation, malignant diseases, heart failure, arrhythmia of high degree, acute or terminated kidney disease, cardiovascular diseases, or anemia. She is in generally good health and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.   Group 4: This is a 75 year-old male with angiographical signs of apparent atherosclerosis, including cardiac artery disease and degenerative valvular heart disease. He does not have a history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes mellitus, acute inflammation, malignant diseases, heart failure, arrhythmia of high degree, acute or terminated kidney disease, cardiovascular diseases, or anemia. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 12-year-old boy with previously diagnosed Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy due to a nonsense mutation presents for a clinical trial. The patient has previously received ataluren treatment in a prior PTC-sponsored clinical study in DBMD. The patient is willing to comply with scheduled visits, drug administration plan, study procedures, laboratory tests, and study restrictions. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients or excipients of ataluren. The patient is willing to abstain from sexual intercourse or employ a barrier or medical method of contraception during ataluren administration and the 6-week follow-up period. The patient is not currently using coumarin-based anticoagulants, phenytoin, tolbutamide, or paclitaxel or systemic aminoglycoside therapy. The patient has no ongoing uncontrolled medical/surgical condition, ECG findings, or laboratory abnormalities that would adversely affect their safety or make it unlikely that follow-up would be completed.

The patient is a 28 year old male who was playing soccer when he felt a pop and sudden instability in his right knee. He was unable to bear weight on the affected leg and had significant swelling in the joint. MRI confirmed a complete tear of the ACL. He has no history of previous knee injuries or surgeries. He is physically active and plays soccer and basketball regularly. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his workday sitting at a desk. He has no significant medical history, allergies or current medications. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His BMI is 25 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He has undergone physical therapy for the knee before surgery to strengthen the muscles around the joint. He is interested in participating in the trial to contribute to the advancement of surgical techniques for ACL repair.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the breast. She has breast cancer that has spread to other parts of her body, and the cancer is chemosensitive. She has no clinical evidence of brain metastases. She has no other concurrent malignancy, and she has not received any hormonal therapy for breast cancer. Her granulocyte count is at least 1,500/mm3, platelet count is at least 50,000/mm3, and hemoglobin is at least 8 g/dL. Her bilirubin is less than 1.5 times normal, and she is negative for hepatitis B surface antigen. Her creatinine is less than 1.8 mg/dL, and her creatinine clearance is normal. Her blood urea nitrogen (BUN) is less than 1.5 times normal. Her ejection fraction is at least 45% by MUGA, and she has no uncontrolled or significant cardiovascular disease. Her PFT-FEV1 is at least 60% of predicted DLCO, and her FVC is at least 60% of predicted. She is not pregnant and has tested negative for HIV. She has no serious medical or psychiatric illness.

32 year old male presenting to a TB clinic in Cape Town, South Africa with a persistent cough, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss over the past 4 weeks. He reports no history of TB exposure or prior TB infection. He is a non-smoker and has no known medical conditions. He provides written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial investigating the prevalence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb)-containing bioaerosols in suspected TB patients. The patient is over 13 years old and meets inclusion criteria for the study.

A 45-year-old obese man underwent elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes medication. He has a history of smoking but quit 3 years ago. He reports that he has a high tolerance for pain and has requested pain medication in the past. After surgery, he has significant pain despite receiving a high dose of opioids. He is interested in participating in this study and is willing to receive ketamine if it is recommended by the attending anesthesiologist.

A 52-year-old woman has been experiencing frequent headaches accompanied by vomiting and confusion for the last few weeks. She has also noticed a change in her vision, with blurring in one eye. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. A CT scan and MRI of the brain show a single lesion in the left frontal lobe. A stereotactic biopsy confirms the diagnosis of primary central nervous system lymphoma. The patient has no previous history of malignancy and has not received any treatment for the lymphoma. She is in good general health, with an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no history of hepatitis B or C, HIV, or immunodeficiency. Her bone marrow function, renal function, cardiac function, and hepatic function are normal. She has signed informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 30-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of difficulty falling asleep and feeling fatigued during the day. He is a full-time software engineer and works 5 days a week from 9 am to 5 pm. He maintains a regular sleep schedule and goes to bed at 11 pm and wakes up at 6:30 am. He has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep for the past 2 months and has been using over-the-counter sleep medications to help him fall asleep. He reports that he has not had a good night's sleep in weeks and is feeling exhausted during the day. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any medical conditions. He does not smoke and does not consume caffeine regularly.

The patient is a 52-year-old female with a history of chronic periodontitis. She has been receiving non-surgical periodontal therapy for the past few months but still has interproximal probing depths of 5mm or more and two or three-wall intrabony defects that are at least 3mm deep. She has no known systemic illnesses and is not taking any medications that may affect the outcomes of periodontal surgery. She is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of titanium-prepared platelet-rich fibrin (T-PRF) treatment on angiogenic biomarkers in gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) in infrabony defects.

A 24-year-old healthy male with a body mass index (BMI) of 25 kg/m2 and a total body weight of 70 kg volunteers for a clinical study to estimate the effects of itraconazole on the pharmacokinetics of PF-06649751. He has no history of hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurological or allergic disease, including drug allergies. He has not taken any investigational drug within the last 30 days and is willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. He has no history of allergy or intolerance to azole antifungal drugs. He is a non-smoker and has not consumed alcohol or caffeine within 24 hours before the study. He gives his informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has a family history of cardiovascular disease. He has been diagnosed with hypertension and hyperlipidemia and has been on treatment for both conditions for the past 3 years. He takes amlodipine and lisinopril for his blood pressure, and atorvastatin for his cholesterol. He has a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in saturated fats. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He has regular check-ups with his primary care physician and has been compliant with his medications. His blood pressure and cholesterol levels have been well-controlled during the observation period. He has not experienced any adverse effects from the medications.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who underwent kidney transplantation 2 years ago due to end-stage renal disease secondary to diabetes. She presents with a sudden increase in serum creatinine levels along with decreased urine output and hypertension. A biopsy confirms acute rejection of the transplanted kidney. The patient is otherwise healthy with no known allergies. She has been compliant with her immunosuppressive medications and has not received any investigational drugs or treatments. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of single-dose rATG infusion for the treatment of acute rejection.

A 35 year old woman comes to the clinic complaining of heavy menstrual bleeding and abdominal pain. She has been experiencing heavy periods for several months, with blood loss exceeding 80ml per cycle. The pain is located in the lower abdomen and radiates to her lower back. The patient has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids, with a diameter ranging from 3 to 10 cm, according to a recent transvaginal ultrasound. She has regular menstrual cycles with an interval of 28 days and her FSH level is within normal limits. The patient is interested in preserving her fertility and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of ulipristal acetate (UPA) in treating symptomatic uterine fibroids. She has not received any treatment for her condition in the past and is not currently taking any medication that could interfere with the study. Her clinical examination shows a uterine size of less than 16 weeks of gestational age. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in participating.

65-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a recent exacerbation leading to mechanical ventilation. He is currently sedated with benzodiazepines and narcotics. He has a Sedation-Agitation Scale (SAS) score of 3 and requires sedation for comfort and to facilitate mechanical ventilation. He has no known hearing impairment and is not pregnant. He is not currently on vasopressin or curarisation.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who suffered a traumatic brain injury a year ago. He has been in a vegetative state (VS) since the accident and has not shown any signs of improvement. He has no history of mental illness or alcohol or substance abuse. He does not have epilepsy or frequent spontaneous movement. He is not taking benzodiazepines or any other medication that may affect the study. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he does not have any organic heart disease or intracranial metal devices or pacemakers. The patient is right-handed. The patient's family is interested in exploring all possible treatment options to improve his condition and has given consent for him to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with systemic sclerosis according to the new ACR/EULAR SSc criteria. She reports experiencing recurrent digital ulcers, with pain and swelling in the fingers and toes. She has previously been treated with a combination of vasodilators and immunosuppressive medications but has not seen significant improvement. She is seeking treatment to prevent the formation of new digital ulcers and promote the healing of existing ones. Her medical history includes hypertension and Raynaud's phenomenon. She is currently not experiencing any active digital ulcers but has a history of several in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that would help identify the best treatment combination for preventing and healing digital ulcers in patients with systemic sclerosis.

A 68-year-old woman came to the clinic with difficulty remembering important dates and events, forgetting recent conversations, and having trouble with language. Her symptoms have been present for about a year, and she has had to rely on her husband to help her with daily tasks.
