She has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, for which she takes medication. She is retired and used to work as a teacher. She has a family history of Alzheimer's disease, with her mother and grandmother both having been diagnosed with the condition. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has a primary caregiver, her husband, who can also provide informed consent. She has not had any loss of consciousness or unstable medical conditions that would prevent her from safely participating in the study.

A 45 year old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of acromegaly, presenting with symptoms of headache, visual disturbances and joint pain. She has previously undergone pituitary surgery but has not achieved disease control. Her IGF-I levels are elevated and she has a pituitary macroadenoma. She has no significant comorbidities except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She reports feeling fatigued and has noticed an increase in her shoe size in the past year. She has not received any medical treatment for acromegaly yet. She is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study and is anticipated to have follow-up visits with her treating physician at least once every year.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a family history of colon cancer. She has no symptoms of colon cancer but is interested in undergoing colonoscopy for preventive screening. She has no history of chronic inflammatory bowel disease or colonic strictures. The patient has not undergone any colonoscopy in the past. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

A 55-year-old Caucasian male presents with persistent bone pain and fatigue for the past few months. He reports a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, which are well-controlled with medication. He denies any recent infections or significant weight loss. Physical examination reveals tenderness in the lower back and hips. Laboratory results show elevated serum creatinine levels (1.8 mg/dL), serum calcium levels (11.2 mg/dL), and serum protein electrophoresis consistent with monoclonal gammopathy. He is diagnosed with multiple myeloma and is eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation. He has not received any prior treatment for multiple myeloma or any other malignancy in the past 5 years. He meets the pre-treatment lab criteria and is therefore eligible to participate in the study. He is informed about the study and its purpose, risks, and benefits. After providing written informed consent, he is enrolled in the study to receive the PAD treatment consisting of bortezomib, doxorubicin, and dexamethasone. He will undergo peripheral blood stem cell collection and autologous stem cell transplant following the PAD treatment. He will attend monthly visits with the Study Doctor for 1 year after the start of treatment and attend a final follow-up visit at 2 years. His quality of life will be assessed using the AQoL. The safety of the treatment will be evaluated throughout the study by monitoring for adverse events.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who works in a healthcare setting. She has a past medical history of seasonal allergies and has been experiencing mild symptoms of hay fever recently. She currently takes over-the-counter antihistamines for relief of her allergy symptoms. She has not received any vaccination for the past year. She is sexually active but not pregnant and does not plan to get pregnant during the study period. She has never been diagnosed with any chronic illness or psychiatric disorder. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

Patient B is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) three years ago. He has undergone two courses of chemotherapy, but his disease has progressed, and he is now considered refractory. He is a former smoker, with a 30-pack-year history. He has no other significant medical history and is currently asymptomatic. A recent CT scan showed multiple lung nodules, the largest measuring 2.5 cm. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of NSCLC. Lab work is reported below: Hgb: 13.5 g/dl WBC: 8000 /mm3 Plt: 200000 /ml AST: 20 U/L ALT: 18 U/L Alk P: 45 U/L Bill total: 0.7 mg/dl Na: 140 mEq/l K: 4.2 mEq/l Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dl BUN: 14 mg/dl ECOG performance status is 1. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore treatment options for his refractory NSCLC.

A 45-year-old female presents with a history of acid reflux symptoms including heartburn and regurgitation for the last 6 months. She has tried over-the-counter antacids but still experiences some symptoms. She underwent a gastroscopy which revealed erosive esophagitis. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of DA-5204 and proton pump inhibitor combination therapy compared with proton pump inhibitor alone therapy in patients with gastroesophageal reflux Disease.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is scheduled for an elective surgery that requires general anesthesia and tracheal intubation. He has no history of congenital or acquired upper airway lesions and is not at high risk of aspiration. The patient has a BMI of 28 and no significant medical history. He is able to understand and comply with the study protocol and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy diagnosed with Crigler-Najjar disease. He experiences unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia and is currently undergoing phototherapy and/or phenobarbital treatment. The patient's parents are concerned about the impact of the intensive phototherapy regimen on their son's quality of life and are interested in alternative treatment options. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of orlistat in decreasing plasma unconjugated bilirubin levels. He has no history of cholestasis, chronic malabsorption syndrome, or pregnancy.

The patient is a 22-year-old female who is scheduled to undergo surgery to remove two impacted wisdom teeth, one in the mandible and one in the maxilla. She has a history of occasional headaches and menstrual cramps but is not currently taking any pain medication. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical examination is unremarkable. She has no known allergies to ibuprofen or acetaminophen. She is not pregnant and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has agreed to follow the study protocol and to participate in the follow-up protocol, which includes completing pain diaries. She will receive either a single dose of intravenous ibuprofen or intravenous acetaminophen thirty minutes prior to surgery. She will be asked to report her pain intensity using a 100 mm VAS scale with anchors of "no pain" and "worst pain imaginable" and a 4-point category scale ("none", "mild", "moderate", and "severe") at 30-minute intervals during the post-surgical time. She will be monitored for any adverse effects related to the study medication.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a history of ACL injury in his left knee. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He has a BMI of 25.5. The patient has opted for ACL surgery with allograft and has consented to be randomized for the trial. He is able to understand and follow instructions in English. He has no history of chronic pain or neurologic disorder that can interfere with pain sensation, nor does he have any contraindications to the medications or procedures used in the study. He has been advised that he may receive Percocet for pain management and is willing to take it if needed.

A 45-year-old male came to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, jaundice and abdominal pain. He had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but was not taking any medication for these conditions. His lab results showed elevated liver enzyme levels, with ALT at 4 times the upper limit and ALP at 2 times the upper limit of normal. His total bilirubin was also elevated at 2.5 mg/dL. He did not have a history of alcohol abuse nor any viral infections. He mentioned taking some over-the-counter pain relievers for his back pain a few weeks ago. He was diagnosed with drug-induced liver injury and was referred to participate in the clinical trial. He agreed to participate after fully understanding the nature of the study and signing the informed consent form.

35-year-old female with a history of chronic abdominal pain, fatigue, and jaundice presented to the gastroenterologist with complaints of recurrent episodes of vomiting and diarrhea. She underwent an abdominal ultrasound which showed ascites and an enlarged liver. Subsequent CT scan revealed thrombosis of the hepatic vein consistent with Budd-Chiari syndrome. She was diagnosed with vascular liver disease and started on anticoagulation therapy. She will be eligible to participate in the Vascular Liver Disease Evaluation, Follow Up and Non-Invasive Diagnostics Program clinical trial, which aims to study risk factors, methods of detection, therapy, and prognosis in order to improve the management of patients with vascular liver disorders. Data on clinical condition, laboratory results, diagnostic tests, interventions, and outcome will be collected anonymously using standardized review of medical charts by a trained investigator. The study will collect data from baseline up to 3 years to create a basis for continuous collections for a large variety of research purposes, including prognostic research, systems biology research, and clinical trials using various designs adapted for rare diseases.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman from the United States who was recently diagnosed with metastatic uterine cancer. She has been experiencing abnormal vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain for several months. The diagnosis was confirmed by a biopsy and imaging studies. The patient has already received one line of cytotoxic treatment for her advanced disease but her cancer has progressed. Her performance status is 1 and her blood work is within normal limits. She has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. She has provided her archival tumor tissue for testing and is willing to undergo new biopsy if needed. She is premenopausal and has a normal urine beta-HCG. She is willing to use effective contraception during and after the treatment with nivolumab. She has no history of autoimmune disease or serious uncontrolled medical disorder. She has no bowel obstruction, refractory ascites, or bowel perforation due to advanced disease within the past 3 months from start of study treatment. She has no prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti-CD137, anti-CTLA-4 antibody or any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T cell co-stimulation or immune checkpoint pathways. She is not currently taking any corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medications. She has no history of malignancy other than uterine cancer, and she has completed her previous treatment for breast cancer more than 3 years ago. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have any positive test for hepatitis B virus surface antigen or hepatitis C virus ribonucleic acid indicating acute or chronic infection. She has no known history of testing positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or known acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). She has no known allergy or adverse drug reaction to nivolumab or any of its components.

A 32-year-old mother with a healthy 12-month-old infant daughter who has no developmental delays or medical problems since birth. The mother is not allergic to puffed grains or cheerios, and neither is the infant. The mother is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol excessively, or use controlled substances. The infant was a full-term birth with a normal birth weight. The mother is interested in the study and is able to attend the weekly 45-minute classes and home practice sessions. The mother is willing to fill out the Daily Home Practice Survey and is available for the pre- and post-intervention assessments.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with Fibromyalgia Syndrome 2 years ago. She has been experiencing widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, depression and anxiety since then. She has tried different treatments including medications, physical therapy and acupuncture but has not found significant relief. Her pain level is usually around 7 out of 10 on the visual analogue scale. She also reports having difficulty sleeping and feeling isolated due to her condition. She is interested in participating in group therapy to manage her symptoms and improve her emotional well-being. She is literate, between the ages of 18-65 and has no other significant medical conditions. She is willing and able to attend group sessions regularly every week for 9 weeks. She is not currently taking any medication for her Fibromyalgia Syndrome.

This is a 49-year-old woman diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer four years ago. She underwent primary debulking surgery followed by six cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy. After a year, she had disease recurrence and was given carboplatin and paclitaxel, which resulted in a partial response. However, she developed platinum-resistant relapse after the fourth cycle of chemotherapy. She received a bevacizumab-containing regimen, but after the third cycle, she had disease progression. She was then enrolled in a phase I clinical trial of a PARP inhibitor and had a partial response, but it was not durable, and her disease progressed again. She has a measurable lesion according to RECIST v1.1 and an ECOG performance status of 1. She has adequate organ function and has resolved adverse events from previous treatments to ≤ Grade 1 based on CTCAE. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective contraceptive measures. She understands and agrees to comply with the protocol.

28 year old male diagnosed with schizophrenia at the age of 22. Currently on stable doses of risperidone and sertraline for the past 6 months. He reports experiencing frequent auditory hallucinations and delusions, and has difficulty with social interactions and completing daily tasks. He is fluent in both Mandarin and English, and has an IQ score of 90. He has no history of head trauma, neurological disorders, or drug abuse. He has no family history of epilepsy, and has not experienced any seizures. He has no focal brain lesions on T1- or T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion-recovery magnetic resonance images. He reports occasional anxiety and depressive symptoms, with HAMA and HAMD scores of 8 and 7, respectively. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been struggling with weight loss for the past 5 years. She has a BMI of 31 and has been unable to maintain a healthy weight despite trying various diets and exercise programs. She is generally healthy and exercises regularly, but finds it difficult to control her food intake. She is not pregnant and does not have any food allergies or medical conditions that would prevent her from following a diet and exercise program. She is willing to participate in a State of Slim group class for the first 16 weeks of the study and is willing to participate in 5 study visits over the 12 month study period. She is interested in trying a soy protein-based diet and is excited to potentially be a part of a program that could help her achieve her weight loss goals.

The patient is a 25-year-old female with a history of vitiligo. She presents with depigmented patches of skin on her face and neck, which have been present for the last 6 months. She has not noticed any new areas of depigmentation or enlarging areas of depigmentation recently. She has no history of hypertrophic scarring or keloids. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other medical problems. She does not smoke and does not take any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of two different techniques in the melanocyte keratinocyte transplant procedure and two different dressings used in the procedure. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with spastic hemiplegic cerebral palsy. He attends a primary school and is currently in the 4th grade. He has difficulty using his right hand and arm due to the spasticity, which affects his daily activities such as writing, drawing, and buttoning his clothes. He also has some difficulty with his balance and walking, but he is able to walk independently. He is receiving physical therapy twice a week at a rehabilitation center, and his parents are interested in enrolling him in a clinical trial to further improve his motor function. He has no significant medical history, and his cognitive function is within the normal range for his age. He is able to follow instructions and communicate effectively. He enjoys playing video games and reading books in his free time. He has a supportive family who are willing to participate in the study and attend the intervention sessions with him.

65-year-old male with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) and hypertension presented to the cardiology clinic complaining of episodes of palpitations and shortness of breath. The patient has had two or more AF episodes for at least 30 seconds in length within the last six months. The patient's physical exam was significant for an irregularly irregular pulse, but was otherwise unremarkable. The patient's electrocardiogram showed evidence of PAF. The patient has been taking metoprolol succinate 50mg orally once daily for the past year, but is still experiencing episodes of PAF. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new device that may help with the treatment of PAF. The patient is not pregnant, does not have any known allergies to contrast media or heparin, and has not had any recent cerebrovascular events. The patient's kidney function is satisfactory, with a GFR of 60 mL/min/1.73m². The patient has no history of structural heart disease, myocardial infarction, or ventricular tachyarrhythmia. The patient has no history of bleeding or thrombotic abnormalities.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer after a mammogram showed a suspicious lesion in her left breast. A biopsy confirmed the presence of cancer cells, which had also spread to her lungs. The patient underwent a mastectomy and received chemotherapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. She now experiences shortness of breath and fatigue. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. The patient has no history of CNS disease, and she has not received biologic or immunotherapy treatment in the past 3 weeks. She has not undergone full field radiotherapy in the past 4 weeks. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have a chronic renal or liver disease, and she does not have any gastrointestinal issues. The patient is not on warfarin sodium or similar oral anticoagulants metabolized by the cytochrome p450 system. The patient is willing to come to the clinic once a week to receive the study treatment. She understands that she should not eat grapefruit or drink grapefruit juice during this study.

Patient B is a 14-year-old female who has been experiencing migraine headaches for the past year. She typically has 2-3 migraine headaches per month, which are characterized by moderate to severe head pain, sensitivity to light and sound, nausea, and vomiting. She has tried several over-the-counter pain relievers, but they have not been effective in treating her migraines. She is currently taking a single migraine preventive medication, which she has been on for the past 3 months. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. She is able to swallow oral medication and is willing to complete a headache diary. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the long-term safety of almotriptan malate in treating her migraines.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing excessive anxiety and worry for the past 6 months. She reports feeling restless, fatigued, and has difficulty concentrating. She is also easily irritable and has muscle tension. She has been diagnosed with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) and has tried two selective Serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) in the past year, but has not experienced adequate relief of her symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 65-year-old male recently diagnosed with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). He has no previous history of cancer or chemotherapy. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild fatigue and pallor. His blood work shows a white blood cell count of 20,000/mm³, hemoglobin of 9 g/dl, and platelets of 70,000/mm³. The bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of AML. He has no significant past medical history, but he has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled on medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use illicit drugs. He is willing and able to provide informed consent for the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman with a history of hypertension presents with symptoms of preeclampsia, including high blood pressure, proteinuria, and edema. She is currently in her second trimester and has had a previous uncomplicated pregnancy. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She is seeking treatment for her preeclampsia and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to further research on this condition. The patient is willing to undergo blood tests and other procedures as required by the study protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past year. She has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder and has been taking an antidepressant at a standard clinical dose for the past six months without significant improvement. She has no history of neurological illness or autoimmune disorders and is in good physical health. She does not smoke cigarettes or consume any substances of abuse. She has not been treated with electroconvulsive therapy or mechanical brain stimulation in the previous six months. She is willing to take medication for the duration of the trial and has previously taken antidepressants for the duration of the trial. She is presently taking an antidepressant at a standard clinical dose. She has no known intolerance or allergy to the medications being used in the trial. She is lactose tolerant. She agrees to participate in all phases of the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old female diagnosed with Stage II breast cancer, who has completed her chemotherapy regimen three months ago, is experiencing peripheral neuropathy symptoms such as paresthesia, numbness, and glove-and-stocking sensory loss distribution in her limbs. She has not received any acupuncture treatments for one month before recruitment. Her baseline von Frey Monofilament test shows a target force of 0.1 gms in her hand and 0.5 gms in her foot. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and grading of peripheral sensory neuropathy in National Cancer Institute- common terminology criteria for adverse events, v5.0 (NCI-CTCAE5) of 2. She has not been diagnosed with diabetic neuropathy or any nerve compression conditions. She is currently not taking any analgesia medications, including duloxetine, pregabalin, venlafaxine, minocycline, topical gel, oxycodone, naloxone, cannabinoids, or angiotensin II type 2 receptor antagonist. She has no severe hemorrhagic coagulopathy or bleeding tendency and no unstable cardiovascular disease. She does not have any severe skin lesions around the treatment sites. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided a written informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman presents for a routine check-up. She has no history of hypertension or cardiovascular disease but has a family history of hypertension. She is physically active and maintains a healthy diet. Her blood pressure has been consistently within normal limits during previous visits. She has no current medical conditions and is not taking any medications. The patient's arm circumference is within the eligible range for the study. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions provided for the wait time before blood pressure measurement.

A 55-year-old male patient with a BMI of 36 came to the clinic with complaints of severe knee pain while walking and at rest. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis in his right knee and has tried non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy, steroid injections, and hyaluronic acid injections, but none of them provided relief. He has a stable health condition and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which he takes medication. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is not involved in any other clinical studies. He has a preoperative flexion of 120 degrees, varus 5 degrees, and valgus 5 degrees. He is interested in remaining active and pain-free and is willing to participate in follow-up therapy at Rebound facilities in Vancouver, WA.

A 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Late-Onset Male Hypogonadism and is currently being treated with Testosterone Replacement Therapy (TRT). He has a BMI of 27 and has been experiencing symptoms such as decreased libido, fatigue, and decreased muscle mass. He has not had any recent hormonal treatment and does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. However, he does have insulin resistance with a HOMA index of 3.2. He is interested in exploring alternative treatments for his condition and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 17-year-old male with a history of ADHD taking Ritalin for the past 3 years. He has complained of difficulty focusing and staying alert while driving. He recently obtained his driver's license and his parents have become increasingly concerned about his driving abilities. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric problems other than ADHD. He is otherwise healthy and active in sports, playing on the high school football and lacrosse teams. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to assess his driving performance while taking his medication and without it.

A 47-year-old woman with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in first remission presents for evaluation for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. She has received chemotherapy and has been in remission for the past six months. Her performance status is ECOG 1. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The patient has an HLA-matched sibling who is willing to donate hematopoietic stem cells. She has no known allergies to any of the test compounds, materials, or contraindication to test products. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate. She is able to understand and willing to sign an IRB-approved written informed consent document.

The patient is a 55-year-old Caucasian man who recently found a small nodule in his lung during a routine chest X-ray. His doctor referred him to a CT-guided lung biopsy to determine if it is cancerous. The patient is literate and speaks English fluently. He has never had a lung biopsy before and is feeling anxious about the procedure. He does not have a history of psychosis or dementia. The patient prefers to be awake during the procedure and does not require monitored anesthesia care or general endotracheal anesthesia. He does not have any hearing or visual impairments. He works as a mechanic and enjoys spending time with his family in his free time. He is married and has two children. His family has no history of lung cancer.

Patient is a 62-year-old male from the United States who was recently diagnosed with low-risk prostate cancer and has been placed in active surveillance. He has no significant past medical or drug history, and his BMI is 27. His PSA level at diagnosis was 4.2 ng/mL, and his prostate biopsy showed a Gleason score of 6 (3+3). He has no known allergies to MRI contrast and has normal renal function. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

A 12-year-old girl with genetically confirmed Rett Syndrome is being considered for a new clinical trial. She has been diagnosed with Rett Syndrome since she was 2 years old. She has severe neurological impairment that affects her motor functions, cognitive abilities, and breathing. She requires support to ambulate. She has been on a strict medication regime for years, but her symptoms are still present. Her medical history is unremarkable other than her diagnosis of Rett Syndrome. The family history is negative for any neurological disorders. The patient and her guardians are willing to participate in the study and have given written informed consent. Her Qtc is within normal limits. She has no history of immunodeficiency or allergy/sensitivity to Glatiramer Acetate or mannitol.

A 55-year-old patient presents with complaints of blurry vision and glare while driving at night. The patient reports no significant medical history, but complains of mild dry eyes. The ophthalmic examination reveals nuclear sclerosis grade 2-3 with a best corrected visual acuity of 20/40 in both eyes. The patient's intraocular pressure is within normal limits and there are no signs of glaucoma, uveitis, or pseudoexfoliation syndrome. Axial length is within the range of 21.5 mm to 24.5 mm. The patient is not on any systemic or topical steroids or NSAIDs. The patient has not undergone any previous ocular surgeries. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the impact of using high fluid parameters during cataract surgery on macular thickness.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with IgA nephropathy based on a kidney biopsy. He has a history of high blood pressure, which is currently well-controlled with medication. His urine protein creatinine ratio is 2.5 g/g and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 45 mL/min/1.73 m2. He is currently taking an angiotensin-receptor blocker (ARB) as part of his standard of care. He reports occasional fatigue and mild swelling in his legs. He has no other significant medical history and is willing and able to comply with study requirements. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his kidney function and reduce proteinuria.

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has a family history of kidney disease. Upon examination, his blood pressure is 148/92 mmHg and his blood glucose level is 180 mg/dL. Urine analysis reveals proteinuria of 1.2 g/24 hours. His serum creatinine level is 1.4 mg/dL and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 45 mL/min/1.73 m². He is diagnosed with chronic proteinuric nephropathy and is being treated with ACE inhibitors and ARBs. He is eligible for the Remission Clinic study as he meets the inclusion criteria of proteinuria greater than 0.5 g/24 hours and a change in serum creatinine or creatinine clearance of less than 30% in the last 3 months. He has not received corticosteroids or immunosuppressants in the last 6 months and does not have any exclusion criteria. The Remission Clinic program aims to stabilize his renal function and normalize his urinary protein excretion. He will have access to a dedicated database computer network to record his clinical, laboratory and treatment data. By participating in this study, he will help to verify if the multidrug approach of the Remission Clinic will improve the clinical course of chronic proteinuric nephropathy.

A 35-year-old Punjabi woman who has been living in the Greater Vancouver Area for the past 3 years presents with a history of wheezing and shortness of breath. She has been diagnosed with mild to moderate asthma by her physician and is currently taking an inhaled corticosteroid and a bronchodilator. She reports difficulty understanding the instructions on her medication and feels unsure about how to manage her asthma symptoms. English is not her first language, and she has limited health literacy in English. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to develop and test culturally appropriate asthma videos and educational materials in Punjabi that would help her better understand her condition and manage her symptoms. She is able to give informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who is in good health and meets all the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial. He has no history of allergies to vaccines or drugs and has never had mumps before. He has received one dose of vaccine containing mumps at the age of 18-24 months before enrollment. He lives with his parents and a younger sister and attends primary school. He is able to communicate well with investigators and understands the requirements of the trial. His parents have read and signed the informed consent form and are willing to comply with the trial requirements. He has not received any immunosuppressive therapy or blood products in the last six months and has not received any other research medicines during the same period. He is not suffering from any chronic illness or congenital deformity, and his physical examination and laboratory tests are normal. He is excited to participate in the trial and contribute to the prevention of mumps.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and dysphagia who will undergo an esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) to evaluate for Barrett's esophagus (BE). He has been experiencing frequent heartburn and regurgitation for the past 6 months and has noticed difficulty swallowing solid foods. The patient has not undergone any prior endoscopic procedures. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent and is not on anticoagulation therapy. He is not pregnant and has no known hemostasis disorders. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help improve the accuracy of diagnosing and monitoring BE.

A 56-year-old woman presents with a missing upper molar on the right side. The patient is concerned about the appearance of her smile and desires a removable partial denture that is metal-free. She reports good oral hygiene practices and has no history of bruxism or clenching. The patient is medically healthy and free from any T.M.J. disorders. The distal abutment teeth bilaterally are premolars, and they are in good periodontal condition. The patient has sufficient inter-arch space, and there are no modifications spaces in the arch to be treated. The tongue size is normal, and the patient is motivated to undergo the treatment. The patient is not on radiation therapy, does not have xerostomia, and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse or psychiatric disorder. The patient is eligible for the Polyetheretherketone vs Cobalt-chromium Telescopic Removable Partial Denture in Kennedy Class I Patients Regarding Oral Health Related Quality of Life clinical trial.

A 60 yo male has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer after a biopsy within the last 6 months. His prostate cancer is considered low or intermediate risk, with a Gleason score of 7 or lower, a local tumor stage of T2c or lower, and no evidence of metastases. His PSA level is 20 ng/ml or lower. He is either scheduled for a radical prostatectomy or is on active surveillance for stable disease for at least 12 months prior to the study. He has not received any invasive treatment for prostatic disease in the past 2 years. He has no history of autoimmune disease, except for Non-Insulin Dependent Diabetes Mellitus. He has adequate bone marrow function and must practice a reliable form of contraception while being treated with the vaccine. He has no history of any cancer other than prostate cancer within the last 5 years, nor is he suspected of having metastatic cancer. He has not participated in another research study involving an investigational product in the 30 days preceding enrollment or planned use during the study period. He has not received immunoglobulins or any blood products within the three months preceding the planned administration of the vaccine candidate. He is seronegative for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and HIV. He has no confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immunodeficient state, asplenia, recurrent, severe infections, and chronic immunosuppressant medication within the past 6 months. He does not have a platelet count >400,000/μL; Monocytes >80,000/μL; Hemoglobin <11g/dL. He has no known allergy to neomycin, no history of allergic response to previous vaccinia vaccinations, no history of hypersensitivity and haemorrhagic cystitis, and no history of anaphylaxis. He has no suspected or known current injecting drug or alcohol abuse, nor does he have a history of serious psychiatric conditions or other circumstances that may be associated with not understanding or complying with the study protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with invasive breast cancer. She has a tumor size of 2.5 cm and it has been confirmed to be estrogen receptor (ER)-negative, progesterone receptor (PR)-negative, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (Her2)-negative. She has no evidence of disease outside the breast or chest wall, except ipsilateral axillary lymph nodes. She has measurable disease as defined by a positive mammogram or ultrasound with at least one dimension ≥ 1cm. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 to 1. Her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is normal by multigated acquisition (MUGA) scan or echocardiography. She has signed informed consent and has adequate organ function. She has not received prior chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, biologic therapy, investigational agent, targeted therapy or radiation therapy for current breast cancer. She has no history of major surgery within 4 weeks of starting study treatment. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate contraception. She has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy, known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or chronic hepatitis B or C, thrombolic or embolic events such as a cerebrovascular accident including transient ischemic attacks within the past 6 months, and cardiac disease > class II New York Heart Association (NYHA). The patient has no known brain metastasis or cardiac ventricular arrhythmias requiring anti-arrhythmic therapy.

The patient is a 60 year old man who had an ischemic stroke 10 months ago, affecting the left side of his body. He has residual upper limb movement, but still experiences moderate to moderately severe disability. His Modified Rankin Score is 3 due to the stroke. He has no history of connective tissue disorder, congenital disorder of the cerebral vessels, or a disorder of thrombosis. He is able to comprehend verbal commands and carry out study assessments. He has no medical conditions that would preclude neurosurgery with appropriate preparation and management. He is not currently taking selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRI) or antispasticity medications. He is willing and able to attend study visits and complete all study assessments, including providing informed consent.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer with a Gleason score of 9 and a PSA level of 22 ng/mL. The patient is scheduled for a laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (with or without robotic assistance) and has been deemed fit for surgery by his physician. The patient has no prior pelvic radiotherapy or androgen-deprivation therapy for prostate cancer. The patient has no contraindications to standard-of-care MR imaging and does not have any medical illness that would preclude administration of the tracer. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

Pt is a 55yo F with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. She has been recommended to start a new regimen of pembrolizumab as a single agent according to standard of care. She has no prior exposure to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, and she does not have any known autoimmune disease or chronic infection. She has not been on chronic treatment with immune suppressive medications, including steroids, at the time of study enrollment. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and be available for the duration of the study.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a history of dental pain in the lower left posterior region for the past few months. She had a root canal treatment for the same tooth 2 years ago. The pain has been intermittent and is accompanied by swelling and tenderness in the gum area. The tooth has been sensitive to hot and cold food and drinks. She visited her dentist, who referred her to an endodontist. The endodontist diagnosed an endodontic failure with periapical periodontitis and recommended non-surgical retreatment. The patient agreed to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the success rate of non-surgical retreatment performed in one compared to two visits. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not pregnant. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and restrictions. She has no significant oral abnormalities and is diagnosed with apical periodontitis in a single-rooted tooth.

The patient is a 45-year-old Thai woman who has been experiencing recurring episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and nausea. She has been diagnosed with non-ulcer dyspepsia and underwent an upper endoscopy, which revealed the presence of Helicobacter pylori (H.pylori) infection. She has not received any treatment for H.pylori before and has not taken any antibiotics, proton pump inhibitors, or bismuth within the past 2 weeks. She has no history of drug allergy for levofloxacin, clarithromycin, or rabeprazole. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no severe underlying diseases such as end-stage renal disease, cirrhosis, or malignancy. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has not taken any medications that interact with the research treatment.

28 year old female with no significant medical history, BMI of 21, and in good health. She is able to comprehend the study requirements and is available for the required study period. She has access to a telephone on a consistent basis and is willing to provide written, informed consent for participation after reading the informed consent form. As per screening, she has a HI titer < 1/40 for the swine-origin A/California/07/2009 H1N1-like X-179A strain in sera. She has a negative serum pregnancy test result and consistently uses effective birth control for at least 28 days prior to vaccination. She has no plan to become pregnant for at least 60 days post vaccination. She does not have any significant acute or chronic, uncontrolled medical or neuropsychiatric illness and does not have any fever or autoimmune disease. She has not received any vaccine within a 30 day period prior to study enrollment or planned administration within the period from the first vaccination up to blood sampling at Day 21 or within 30 days prior to blood sampling at Day 201. She has not received any investigational or non-marketed product within 30 days prior to study enrollment or planned use during the study period. She has not received any systemic glucocorticoids at a dose exceeding 10 mg of prednisone per day, or equivalent for more than 7 consecutive days or for 10 or more days in total, within one month of first study vaccine administration, or any other cytotoxic or immunosuppressant drug within three months of vaccination. She has no significant disorder of coagulation, no treatment with warfarin derivatives or heparin, and no history of allergy to any of the constituents of H1 VLP (H1N1) study vaccine, or the phosphate buffer. She does not have a history of allergy to egg-based vaccines such as allergy or hypersensitivity to egg proteins, severe allergic reactions or anaphylaxis or severe asthma, or tobacco allergy. She has not used anti-histaminics continuously for 4 weeks or more at any time in the past year, prior to randomization. She does not have a rash or dermatological condition that may interfere with injection site reaction rating. She has not received a blood transfusion within 90 days prior to vaccination, and is not known to be pregnant or lactating. All vital signs are normal and no history of cancer or treatment for cancer within 3 years of study vaccine administration or history of Gillian Barre Syndrome.

This is a 56 year old male who presented to the hospital with fever, cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 after a positive polymerase chain reaction test on nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs. He was admitted to the hospital and enrolled in a clinical trial studying the efficacy of probiotics in the treatment of COVID-19. Past Medical History: 1. Hypertension 2. Hyperlipidemia 3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus 4. Obesity (BMI 33) 5. Gout 6. Mild Chronic Kidney Disease 7. Previous history of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism on anticoagulation therapy 8. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease 9. Benign prostatic hyperplasia. The patient had not consumed probiotics for at least 3 months prior to admission, did not have any intolerances to probiotics or their components, and provided informed consent to participate in the study. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have cancer or psychoemotional disorders. He is currently taking antiviral, antibacterial, anticoagulant, and anticytokine drugs as part of his treatment for COVID-19.

A 45-year-old man presents with a history of gout attacks for the past 5 years. He reports experiencing intermittent pain, swelling, and tenderness in his left big toe and right ankle, which are consistent with gout flares. He has a history of hypertension and takes amlodipine 5 mg daily for the past 3 years. His blood pressure is well-controlled, with a reading of 128/84 mmHg. His BMI is 29, indicating that he is overweight. Laboratory tests show elevated uric acid levels of 7.8 mg/dL. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He has social insurance affiliation and is not under legal guardianship. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 35-year-old man with SEPN1-RM genetic disease is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He was diagnosed with the disease at the age of 30, and since then, he has experienced progressive muscle weakness and respiratory failure. He is currently taking corticosteroids to manage his symptoms. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He is a non-smoker and does not have any major dietary restrictions. He has never taken N-acetylcysteine (NAC) or any other antioxidants before. He is willing to commit to not making any significant changes in his diet or lifestyle during the study period. He is excited to participate in the study to potentially improve his condition and contribute to research on this rare genetic disease.

A 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma and underwent autologous transplantation of hematopoietic stem cells and was treated with Melphalan. He complains of changes in his sense of taste and smell and reports that it is affecting his quality of life. He has no history of eating disorders such as bulimia, anorexia, or binge eating disorder. He is not allergic to any food or any of the components of liposomal sprays (Liposaliva or liponasal). He lives within 80 km of the technical center (Mas de Saporta, Lattes) and has no visual or hearing deficits that may affect the proper completion of the questionnaires. He does not have a reading level in French that may interfere with a good understanding of the protocol and the questionnaires. The patient is not under curatorship or tutorship and is not deprived of liberty. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to sign the free and informed consent to participate in the sensory rehabilitation program to improve his quality of life, psychological well-being, and nutrition.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather healthy individuals who meet certain eligibility criteria. The study is seeking individuals aged 18 or older who are in good health, with normal vital signs, and do not have any medical conditions that would prevent them from donating peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Donors must also test negative for certain infectious diseases and have adequate levels of hemoglobin, platelets, and white blood cells. Females who are pregnant or breastfeeding are not eligible to participate. The study involves collecting PBMCs through apheresis, a process that separates white cells from red cells and plasma using a machine. Donors will undergo this procedure and their PBMCs will be used for research studies for new cancer therapies. Once collected, the PBMCs will be cryopreserved and used to expand the T cells of patients with cancer over a period of two to three weeks. Up to 500 individuals will be enrolled in this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 7 years ago. She is currently on a combination of metformin and glipizide to control her blood glucose levels. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to any supplement ingredients. Her last HbA1c was 7.5%. She has no history of diabetic retinopathy but has experienced occasional blurriness in her vision. Her corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She has no history of any serious eye disease or any other significant medical history. She is fluent in English and willing to participate in a clinical trial for the potential benefit of her diabetic eye health.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is 33 weeks and 4 days pregnant with her first child. She has a history of gestational diabetes, and her blood sugar levels have been well-controlled with diet and exercise. Her prenatal care has been unremarkable, and she has had no complications during pregnancy. She is scheduled for a C-section delivery in 3 weeks due to a breech presentation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that assesses the reliability of a new non-invasive device to assess the blood coagulation status in newborn babies. She has given written parental informed consent for her baby to participate in the study. The baby is expected to be term, and there are no congenital anomalies or chromosomal abnormalities detected on ultrasound.

The patient is a 62 year old male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer with metastasis to the liver. He has been previously treated with chemotherapy and radiation therapy but the tumors have progressed. He has also been diagnosed with hypertension and takes medication for it. He has no history of thrombo-embolic disease and his cardiovascular condition is stable. He has not received any investigational drugs in the past 4 weeks. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore other treatment options and is willing to undergo further testing to determine his eligibility for the trial.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking for 40 years presented with chronic cough, dyspnea, and wheezing. He was diagnosed with COPD and had a FEV1 of 40% predicted. He was admitted to the hospital twice in the past year due to COPD exacerbations. He lives in the southern part of Rogaland county in Western Norway and was monitored at home by telemedicine video consultation (TVC) during a pilot project period from 16 April 2010 to 31 December 2011. He gave written informed consent to participate in the observational study. He has no comorbidities and is not taking any medication other than inhalers for COPD. He completed a questionnaire about patient satisfaction and impact on his quality of life after the TVC.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) due to a severe pneumonia. She was intubated and is currently receiving mechanical ventilation. The patient has no history of any chronic medical conditions, but she is a lifelong smoker. The patient's vital signs are stable, and she has been on the ventilator for 24 hours. The patient is able to be placed on the study protocol within 8 hours of intubation, making her eligible for the study. She weighs 155 lbs and has no orthopedic injuries, head injuries, or unstable spinal injuries.

10-year-old student, attending a public school in Karachi, Pakistan, with a history of overweight and sedentary lifestyle. The student spends more than three hours a day watching TV or working on the computer and has a habit of snacking on fast food and sweetened beverages. The student's parents are concerned about their child's health and would like to see an improvement in their physical activity levels and dietary habits. The student is eligible for the School Health Education Program in Pakistan (SHEPP) clinical trial, which aims to increase physical activity levels, promote healthy dietary habits, and provide basic health education to children aged 8-11 years in three schools in Karachi for a period of one year. The trial will include 140 minutes of physical activity per week, healthy diet teaching, and healthy heart teaching. The parents will also receive group health education to reinforce these habits in their children. The investigators hypothesize that SHEPP will improve physical activity levels, dietary habits, and knowledge about healthy heart in children, ultimately leading to a decrease in cardiovascular risk factors such as blood pressure, body mass index, waist circumference, and body fat percentage.

Patient A is a 55-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and congestive heart failure (NYHA CHF Class III). She has previously undergone coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and is now in need of a repeat CABG procedure. She is experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath, and her cardiologist has recommended the bypass procedure with the use of the heart-lung machine. However, due to her history of congestive heart failure and diabetes, she is at an increased risk for postoperative complications such as heart attack, stroke, or heart failure. Therefore, her cardiologist has recommended her to participate in the PRIMO-CABG II clinical trial to evaluate if the study drug (pexelizumab) can reduce such side effects and be given safely during the bypass procedure with the use of the heart-lung machine. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 50-year-old woman with a history of non-Hodgkin lymphoma presents with recurrent disease. She has received several rounds of chemotherapy in the past and has not been able to achieve a complete response. She has a positive CD19 tumor and is considered eligible for the study. She has a Karnofsky performance score of 70% and her bilirubin and AST levels are within normal limits. She has no active infections, is not pregnant or lactating, and is willing to use effective birth control methods during the study and for 6 months after its conclusion. She has an available autologous or syngeneic activated peripheral blood T cell product with CD19.CAR expression of at least 15%. She understands the nature of the study and has given informed consent to participate. She will be followed for a total of 15 years to monitor for any long-term side effects of gene transfer.

A 45-year-old Hispanic man who was diagnosed with HIV five years ago presented to the clinic for a follow-up visit. He was taking antiretroviral therapy and his viral load was undetectable. He reported no significant medical history other than hypertension and occasional migraines. He had no known allergies and denied any recent illnesses. He was interested in participating in a clinical trial studying the H1N1 influenza vaccine immunogenicity in HIV-1 infected patients. He was informed about the study and provided written consent. The study staff confirmed his eligibility and scheduled him for an appointment to receive the vaccine and donate blood samples for immunologic studies. He was instructed to report any adverse reactions to the vaccine and to follow up for a second blood sample 21 days later. He was willing to participate as he believed it could lead to better protection from influenza for himself and others living with HIV.

A 58-year-old male with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation (AFib) for the past 6 months was referred to the clinic for consideration of direct current cardioversion (DCC). He has been on a beta-blocker for the past 3 months, with no improvement in his AFib symptoms. The patient was eligible for DCC and underwent the procedure, which was successful in restoring sinus rhythm. The patient was then randomly assigned to receive either Ranolazine low, intermediate, or high dose or a placebo, given twice daily. The patient is able to attend all the visits scheduled in the study and has given written informed consent. He will report trans-telephonic ECGs on a daily basis to a central core ECG facility and will record any symptoms indicative of AFib in a diary. The patient has no known concurrent temporary secondary causes of AFib and is not taking any medications that are contraindicated for the study. The patient is not taking any class I or Class III antiarrhythmic agents within 3 days of planned randomisation and has not taken Dronedarone or oral Amiodarone within 2 weeks and 3 months of planned randomisation, respectively. The patient has no history of long QT syndrome and a QTc interval ≥500 msec at Screening. The patient has congestive heart failure NYHA grade II and is not taking Metformin at a total daily dose greater than 1000 mg or Simvastatin at a total daily dose greater than 20 mg.

This is a 52 year old female who was recently diagnosed with stage IIA breast cancer after a routine mammogram. She underwent a lumpectomy and is scheduled to receive adjuvant radiation to the whole breast. She has no significant medical history other than hypertension that is well controlled with medication. She does not smoke and has never had chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past. She is currently not on any hormonal therapy or targeted therapies for breast cancer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help prevent radiation dermatitis and has no plans for breast reconstruction.

A 53-year-old post-menopausal woman is experiencing hot flashes and night sweats multiple times per day for the past year. She has tried over-the-counter supplements and herbal remedies, but they have not been effective. She has no history of breast cancer, and her mammogram and pap smear are up to date. She takes medication for hypertension and has well-controlled blood pressure. She has a BMI of 28 and is a non-smoker. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test TU 025 Keishi Bukuryo Gan for hot flash management.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has tested positive for COVID-19 and has been admitted to the medical ward with hypoxemic respiratory failure. The patient requires oxygen supplementation to maintain SpO2 levels above 92%. The patient has no known history of respiratory or cardiovascular disease but has a history of smoking. The patient is able to comply with continuous measurement of SpO2 by pulse oximetry. The patient's oxygen requirement is less than 10 liters/min at admission.

A 55-year-old female presents to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain and weight loss. She has a past medical history of hypothyroidism and hypertension, which are well-controlled with medications. She reports no family history of gastrointestinal cancers. Physical examination reveals tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. Laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes, and imaging studies reveal a mass in the pancreas. A biopsy confirms pancreatic cancer. The patient is eligible for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria of having a cytologically or histologically proven carcinoma of pancreatic origin and being over 18 years old. She is affiliated with the French social security-welfare system and agrees to sign the informed consent form. She is not under any legal guardianship and is not a foreign patient under the AME scheme. There are no clinical, psychological, or social reasons that could influence her compliance with the protocol. She does not refuse to participate in the study. She will be enrolled in the prospective interventional cohort and followed up for 10 years to evaluate the relationship between tumor microenvironment, host factors, and survival in pancreatic cancer.

A 26 year old female with a history of schizophrenia and a previous unsuccessful treatment with oral atypical antipsychotic medication. She has been experiencing symptoms of emotional instability, detachment from reality, delusions and hallucinations, and withdrawal into the self. She is currently on oral antipsychotic medication but still experiences symptoms. She is willing to participate in a study exploring the efficacy, tolerability, and safety of flexibly dosed paliperidone extended-release (ER) and has signed an informed consent document. She is sexually active and agrees to practice an effective method of birth control throughout the study. She has no history of tardive dyskinesia or neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

The patient is a 55-year-old male veteran who receives primary care services at the local VA medical center. He has a BMI of 32 and has been struggling with his weight for the past few years. He has a family history of obesity and related health conditions. He is interested in participating in a weight management program to improve his health and overall well-being. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and high cholesterol. He has no history of major medical conditions such as diabetes or cardiovascular disease. He is able to walk for exercise but finds it difficult to maintain a regular exercise routine due to his work schedule. He is willing to participate in a program that provides education and support to help him make lifestyle changes to improve his health.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl scheduled for elective day surgery. She has no significant past medical history and is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class I. The patient and her parents have no known allergies or sensitivity to aromatherapy oils. The patient is able to smell in the postoperative period. She is willing to participate in the study and has not been excluded based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

Patient is a 42-year-old female from the United States who is interested in improving the appearance of her skin. She has given birth to two children and is currently using a medically accepted form of birth control. She is in good health and has no known skin disorders or infections. She does not smoke and has no history of diabetes or chronic illnesses. She is not currently taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and has no implanted medical prostheses. She has some skin laxity on her upper arms and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve the appearance of her skin.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence (SUI) symptoms for the past 6 months. She reports leakage of urine during physical activities such as running, jumping, and even coughing or sneezing. She has tried pelvic floor exercises and lifestyle modifications but has not seen any significant improvement. She has no history of pelvic surgery, active catheter use, or neurological diseases affecting bladder storage. She has not undergone any incontinence surgery in the past. She is currently not pregnant and has completed her childbearing. Her physical exam shows no significant abnormalities, and her urine dipstick is negative for leukocytes and nitrites. She is willing to undergo non-conservative therapy for her SUI and is eligible for SUI surgery. She does not have any active malignancy of the cervix, uterus, fallopian tube(s), or ovary beyond Stage I or bladder of any Stage. She has not undergone pelvic radiation therapy or had synthetic mesh placed on a vaginal approach in the anterior compartment. She has not had any prior urethral diverticulum, augmentation cystoplasty, or artificial sphincter. She is available for 12 months of follow-up and can complete study assessments. She has signed the consent form to participate in the study.

As this is a clinical trial focused on testing competing sets of information for consumers on how to interpret hypothetical SARS-CoV-2 home test kit results, there is no specific patient description required. However, eligible participants need to be over 18 years old, communicate in English, and reside in the United States. Respondents who complete the survey in under a minute will be excluded from the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with chronic hepatitis B with a history of the disease for the past 8 years. He presents with fatigue, loss of appetite, and jaundice. He also reports mild abdominal discomfort and bloating. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His family history is negative for liver disease. His lab study shows HBsAg positivity for more than 6 months, HBV DNA of 5 log10 copies/mL, and ALT levels of 4 times the upper limit of normal (ULN). He had a liver biopsy performed 4 months ago and has readable biopsy slides. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent. He is not currently taking any nucleoside, nucleotide, or interferon therapy and has not received any such therapy in the past 6 months. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive agents or other immunoregulates, systemic cytotoxic drugs, or other antiviral agents, including Chinese herb medicine. He has no active alcohol intake or drug abuse, which could hinder his compliance with treatment or participation in the study.

A 58-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with chest pain that started 4 hours ago. He describes his pain as a pressure-like sensation that radiates to his left arm. He also feels lightheaded and nauseous. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He currently takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. Upon arrival, his electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, consistent with an inferior wall myocardial infarction. He was treated with aspirin, heparin, and ticagrelor, and underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention with stenting of the right coronary artery. His troponin level peaked at 12 ng/mL. He has no history of cardiogenic shock or active ischemia. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to determine whether remote ischemic preconditioning results in an increase in interleukin 10 levels in patients following acute myocardial infarction.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) 5 years ago. She has been treated with glatiramer acetate (GA) but has experienced suboptimal response in terms of efficacy. She has had several relapses and experiences fatigue, cognitive difficulties and walking problems. The patient has access to the internet and is able to complete online assessments on a computer. She has a complete blood count (CBC) available within 6 months of initiation of treatment with dimethyl fumarate (DMF). The patient has decided to initiate treatment with DMF under routine clinical care and is willing to participate in the study. She understands the purpose and risks of the study and has provided signed and dated informed consent and authorization to use Protected Health Information in accordance with national and local patient privacy regulations.

The patient is a 38-year-old Caucasian male, living in Oslo, Norway. He is overweight with a BMI of 32. He has been struggling with his weight for the past few years and has tried various diets and exercise programs without any significant results. He is currently not suffering from any chronic illnesses and is not taking any medications. He has never participated in a weight loss program before. He is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study. He understands the Norwegian language written and spoken easily. He is not pregnant and he is not breastfeeding. He is motivated to lose weight and is willing to comply with the visits and dietary instructions provided by the study. He has not experienced any significant weight changes in the last 3 months.

A 55-year-old man presents with a history of smoking and a chronic cough. A chest X-ray revealed a mass in his right lung that was confirmed by a CT scan. Further evaluation revealed that the mass was malignant and he was scheduled for thoracic surgery with one-lung ventilation. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He denies any history of heart disease or neurologic disorders. He has never had surgery before and is nervous about the procedure. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He does not consume alcohol or smoke anymore. He has a BMI of 25. His oxygen saturation level is within normal range.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who suffered burns on his right arm and hand about a year ago. The burns have since healed but have left restrictive scars that limit his range of motion by more than 20%. The patient has been undergoing physical therapy to try and improve his range of motion but has not seen significant improvement. The patient has no history of keloid scars or any other skin conditions that may affect the treatment. The patient is in good general health with no history of chronic alcohol or drug abuse, and has no known allergies to gentamycin or amphotericin B or sensitivity to materials of bovine origin. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and is able to provide written informed consent.

A 42-year-old man with liver cirrhosis secondary to hepatitis B virus infection presented to the hospital with acute gastric variceal bleeding. He has a history of alcohol abuse and cigarette smoking. He has never had upper gastrointestinal bleeding before. He is currently not on any medications or treatments for his liver cirrhosis. Imaging results show no abnormal portosystemic shunt. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effect of endoscopic injection of a mixture of cyanoacrylate and lipiodol versus cyanoacrylate and lauromacrogol in gastric varices.

45 yo M with genetically confirmed Friedreich's ataxia diagnosed 5 years ago presenting with worsening gait instability and frequent falls. Currently able to ambulate short distances with a walker but requires a wheelchair for longer distances. No significant medical history other than FRDA. Current medications include CoQ10 and Vitamin E. Patient has no known allergies. Patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the use of Nicotinamide in the upregulation of the Frataxin gene. Past Medical History: - Friedreich's Ataxia (genetically confirmed) - No other significant medical history Medications: - CoQ10 - Vitamin E Allergies: - None

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has given birth vaginally three times. She complains of vaginal laxity and has noticed a decrease in sexual satisfaction. She has no history of pelvic organ prolapse or prior reconstructive vaginal surgery, and her Pap smear is up to date with no evidence of dysplasia. She reports no current urinary tract infections or active sexually transmitted infections. She is willing to take valacyclovir for a history of recurrent episodes of genital herpes. She has a body mass index of 28 and is not currently taking any anti-inflammatory medications or immunosuppressive drugs. She has no history of pacemaker or other electrical health maintenance device. She is not currently participating in pelvic floor muscle strengthening exercises. She has no clinically significant anxiety or depression that would prohibit completion of treatments. She is currently using oral contraceptives and is willing to continue taking them throughout the study.

A 65-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and chest pain. He is diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction and is admitted to the medical ICU. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He is currently taking metformin and lisinopril. His BMI is 28, and his HbA1c level on admission is 7.5%. His blood glucose level on admission is 250 mg/dL, which is managed with an insulin drip. His APACHE II score is 25. He has no history of hemoglobinopathy or recent blood transfusions. He is intubated and started on mechanical ventilation. He develops sepsis on day 3 of admission and is treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics. He also requires hemodialysis due to acute kidney injury. His hospital course is complicated, and he is eventually discharged to a rehabilitation facility after a prolonged hospital stay.

A 45-year-old female referred for elective colonoscopy with a history of occasional constipation. She has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks 2-3 cups of coffee daily. Her physical examination is unremarkable. She has no abdominal distension, tenderness, or palpable masses. Her bowel movements are infrequent and hard, and she occasionally uses laxatives. She has no known allergies and has never undergone colonic resection or had inflammatory bowel disease. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has been selected to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of adding stewed apricot juice to senna for pre-colonoscopic preparation.

35 year-old woman who is overweight with a BMI of 30.2 and has a family history of cardiovascular disease. She is currently not taking any medications and has no history of diabetes or liver disease. She has been struggling with her weight for the past few years and has tried various diets with little success. She is interested in participating in a study to help understand how different diets affect the body's fat synthesis and the risk of cardiovascular disease. She is willing to comply with the study's requirements, including staying in a research ward for two nights at the end of each 10-day feeding period. She does not have claustrophobia or any metal implants.

The patient is a 28 year old Hispanic female who was diagnosed with severe preeclampsia during her pregnancy. She had a difficult pregnancy and was admitted to the hospital multiple times due to high blood pressure readings. She delivered a healthy baby via C-section but her blood pressure remained high in the postpartum period. She has a history of hypertension prior to her pregnancy, which was managed with lifestyle modifications. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. She works as a receptionist at a dental clinic and enjoys cooking and spending time with her family. She has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of diltiazem for the control of blood pressure in postpartum patients with severe preeclampsia.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme 12 months ago. She underwent surgery followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy with temozolomide. Her last MRI, performed 2 weeks ago, revealed a recurrent tumor in the same location as the original tumor. She is currently experiencing headaches, vomiting, and seizures. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has no history of heart failure, renal failure, or metal implants in the head and neck region. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant. She is willing to undergo BNCT as a potential treatment option for her recurrent glioblastoma. She has read and understood the study description and has given her informed consent to participate in the study. Her performance status is 1 on the World Health Organization scale. Her white blood cell count is 4,500/mm3 and her platelet count is 150,000/mm3. Her serum creatinine level is 80 umol/L.

A 45-year-old male patient was diagnosed with familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) and underwent an ileostomy procedure a year ago. He has been experiencing malnutrition, weight loss and weakness since the surgery. His appetite has been poor and he has been avoiding certain foods due to concerns about potential bowel obstruction. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that focuses on the outcomes and complications after ileostomy closure.

A 45-year-old patient with a history of MDD for the past 10 years, who has tried several antidepressants but failed to achieve satisfactory improvement in symptoms, is seeking alternative treatment options. She has also tried ECT, but it did not provide sustained relief. Her HAMD-17 score is currently 22, and her GAF score is 45. She has no history of psychotic or bipolar disorders, substance abuse, or suicidal ideation in the past year. She is not currently taking any medication that could interfere with the treatment. She has no significant medical history, except for hypertension controlled with medication. She has no known allergies to MRI contrast agents or any other medications. She has not had any intracranial surgery or deep brain stimulation. Her cognitive function is normal, with a score of 28 on the MMSE. She has no metallic implants or clips in the sonication pathway, and less than 30% of her scalp in the sonication pathway is covered by scars or other disorders. She is willing and able to undergo the prolonged stationary supine position required during treatment. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 25-year-old non-smoking woman with normal ophthalmic findings and no history of ocular disease came to the clinic. She is interested in participating in a study that measures the response of total retinal blood flow to diffuse luminance flicker stimulation. Her medical history and physical examination were normal, and she has no ametropia greater than 3 diopters. Her blood pressure was within normal limits with a systolic blood pressure of 120 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure of 80 mmHg. She has not taken any medications in the last three weeks and has no symptoms of any clinically relevant illness.
