She has not participated in any clinical trial or donated blood in the last three weeks. She does not have a family history of epilepsy or alcohol abuse, and she is not pregnant. She is willing to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

Pt is a 55yo M with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) for the past 3 months. Despite the use of anti-arrhythmic drugs (AADs) other than beta-blockers, the patient's symptoms have not improved. The patient is otherwise healthy with no history of heart failure or thrombocytopenia. The patient has agreed to participate in the FREEZE cohort study and undergo cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for the first ablation of AF. The patient has provided written informed consent and is over 18 years of age. The patient has not had a stroke or TIA within the past 6 months and has no contraindication to chronic anticoagulation. The patient is not pregnant and has a life expectancy of greater than 1 year.

A 42-year-old woman presents as a kidney transplant recipient. She received a kidney transplant 2 years ago due to end-stage renal disease secondary to lupus nephritis. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, depression, and anxiety. She is on a regimen of immunosuppressive medications, including mycophenolate mofetil and prednisone, taken twice daily. She reports occasional missed doses due to forgetfulness and her busy work schedule. She is employed as a customer service representative and works full time. Her social support system includes her husband, who is supportive of her medical condition and helps with medication reminders. She is fluent in English and has access to a telephone. Her most recent lab work shows no signs of kidney dysfunction or rejection. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her medication adherence and potentially improve her long-term outcomes.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of heartburn, acid regurgitation and stomach acidity for the past 6 months. He has been diagnosed with Barrett's esophagus by histology confirmation and has been advised to undergo treatment. He has no history of previous gastric surgery or allergic reactions to esomeprazole. The length of his esophageal metaplastic mucosa is 2 centimeters. The patient has no serious concomitant illnesses and is not pregnant. The patient has not undergone any previous treatment for Barrett's esophagus.

This is a 63-year-old male with a past medical history of atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, who has been taking rivaroxaban for the past 6 months to prevent stroke related to his atrial fibrillation. He presents to the hospital with symptoms of gastrointestinal bleeding, including abdominal pain and dark, tarry stools. The patient reports he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 3 days. He denies any history of bleeding disorders, recent surgeries, trauma, or use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. The patient has not been taking any other medications besides rivaroxaban. Upon admission, his vital signs are stable, and laboratory tests reveal a hemoglobin level of 9 g/dL, which is lower than his baseline. The patient is started on intravenous fluids and is monitored closely for any further bleeding. He is eligible for the study as he has been admitted for GI bleeding while being treated with a NOAC.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Fibromyalgia. She has been experiencing chronic pain, fatigue, and sleep disturbances for the last 2 years. She has tried various treatments, including painkillers and physical therapy, but has not found significant relief. She is currently not taking any medications for Fibromyalgia. The patient is willing to participate in a 4-week, twice-a-day treatment trial at Massachusetts General Hospital for transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) as a potential treatment for her Fibromyalgia pain. She has a 12th grade English-reading level and speaks English as her primary language. She has no history of cardiac, respiratory, or nervous system disease that would preclude her participation in the study. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing hoarding symptoms for the past 5 years. She lives in Stockholm and has access to a computer with internet and a mobile phone. She has not received more than 10 CBT sessions for Hoarding Disorder in the past. She has a history of depression but is currently stable on medication. She is interested in participating in group therapy and is comfortable using the internet for support. She has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. Her baseline neurocognitive profile will be assessed before the start of the treatment.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with Stage II triple negative breast cancer. She underwent a mammogram and an ultrasound, which revealed a mass in her left breast measuring 3 cm in diameter. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of triple negative breast cancer. The patient has no significant past medical history and she reports no family history of breast cancer. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. The patient is in good physical condition and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0. Her lab work shows adequate bone marrow reserve, liver and renal function. She has no pre-existing peripheral neuropathy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for neoadjuvant therapy and is eligible for the study since she has not received any prior treatment for primary breast cancer. She is willing to undergo definitive surgery after completion of the study treatment. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stable angina pectoris. He has been experiencing chest pain and discomfort during physical activity for more than 6 months. Further evaluation revealed that he has a de novo atherosclerotic lesion in his native coronary artery that is up to 28 mm in length, with a diameter of 3.5 mm. He is a suitable candidate for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is ≥ 30%. He has not undergone any treatment for the target vessel with any anti-restenotic drug-coated or drug-eluting coronary stent, nor has he undergone any treatment with intravascular brachytherapy in the target vessel. He is not planned to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) post-index procedure. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is willing to comply with all specified follow-up evaluations and understands the study requirements and the treatment procedures, and provides written informed consent before any study-specific tests or procedures are performed.

A 43-year-old woman presented with chronic post-surgical neuropathic groin pain that has persisted for over a year. She underwent a laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy and oophorectomy for symptomatic fibroids. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and mild depression. She has tried various conservative treatments such as medication, physiotherapy, and interventions, but none have been effective in managing her pain. The pain level has been consistently high, ranging between 70-80mm on the visual analogue scale (VAS) in the primary pain area (groin pain). She is willing and able to comply with the examination and trial schedule. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. She has not been treated with corticosteroids or radio frequency therapy on an area scheduled for stimulation in the last 30 days or 3 months respectively. She has not been treated with an active implantable device or participated in another clinical study in the last 30 days. She is not suffering from an infection and has no coagulation disorders or taking anti-coagulants. She has not been diagnosed with malignancy in the past 2 years. She is able to operate the stimulation device and has given consent in writing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection with genotype 1. He has previously been treated with a nonstructural protein (NS)3/4A protease inhibitor plus pegylated interferon (PEG)/ribavirin (RBV) regimen but did not achieve sustained virologic response (SVR). His HCV RNA level is greater than 10,000 IU/mL. He has cirrhosis, and a liver biopsy has been performed to confirm the diagnosis. His screening laboratory values are within the defined thresholds. He is currently not on any systemic immunosuppressive agents. He has no history of clinical hepatic decompensation or hepatocellular carcinoma. He is not co-infected with HIV or hepatitis B virus. He is sexually active and agrees to use two effective contraception methods. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir fixed dose combination (FDC) with or without ribavirin (RBV) administered for 12 or 24 weeks in treatment-experienced subjects with chronic genotype 1 hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection.

A 35-year-old male who has recently recovered from COVID-19 is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help others who may be suffering from the disease. He experienced mild to moderate respiratory symptoms including fever, dry cough and shortness of breath, which lasted for approximately 2 weeks. He did not require hospitalization or any specific treatment. He has a history of seasonal allergies, but is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs or consume alcohol. He weighs 170 pounds and has adequate peripheral venous access for plasma donation. He is willing to have his blood samples stored for future research use. The patient has not participated in any other medical research that required more than 100 mL of blood to be given in any 8-week period of time. He has not received any unlicensed drug or vaccine within the past month or during the duration of this study.

A 40-year-old woman who has been smoking for 20 years presents with concern about cessation-related weight gain. She smokes at least 15 cigarettes per day and has tried to quit smoking unsuccessfully on multiple occasions. She is motivated to quit smoking and willing to participate in a clinical trial. She has no major medical problems and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She is using an intrauterine device (IUD) as her contraceptive method. She has no history of seizure disorder or head injury, and no current or historical psychosis or bipolar disorder. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse within the previous year, and no current or historical eating disorder. She is not using any antidepressant medication, monoamine oxidase inhibitor, or lithium in the previous month, and has no multiple drug allergies. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to help her quit smoking and control weight gain.

A 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy was referred to a tertiary hospital due to high blood pressure and proteinuria. She was diagnosed with early onset preeclampsia at 29+4 weeks of gestation. Her blood pressure was 150/100 mmHg, and she had 2+ proteinuria in a urine dipstick test. Her ultrasound showed fetal growth restriction with an estimated fetal weight of 800g. She was started on expectant management and given antihypertensive medication. She is willing to participate in the ESOPE trial to receive esomeprazole as a potential treatment for her pre-eclampsia. She has no history of contraindications to the use of a proton pump inhibitor and has not used it before.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing headaches and vision problems for the past few months. A recent MRI revealed the presence of a pituitary adenoma, and the patient has been advised to undergo transsphenoidal surgery for its removal. The patient has no prior history of surgery, and is in good general health with no significant medical conditions. He is able to provide consent for the surgery, and is willing to participate in the clinical trial testing the use of intraoperative ultrasound devices during the procedure. The patient is motivated to ensure complete resection of the adenoma, and is willing to undergo the additional testing and monitoring required for the trial.

As this clinical trial is focused on comparing intubation devices used during infant resuscitation, there is no patient description needed. The study will be conducted with paramedics who have no clinical experience in infant intubation.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple fractures and a traumatic brain injury. He has been in the ICU for the past 2 weeks and has been unable to tolerate oral intake due to his injuries. The patient has recently undergone a PEG tube placement for enteral nutrition. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal disease, and his past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently receiving mechanical ventilation, sedation, and pain control. He has a BMI of 28.5 and is 5'9" tall. The patient is alert and oriented to person only. He is able to follow simple commands but requires assistance with activities of daily living. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with invasive breast carcinoma a year ago. She underwent a lumpectomy with axillary lymph node dissection, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide. She also received radiotherapy and tamoxifen therapy for 6 months. However, she developed metastatic disease with multiple bone lesions and a liver metastasis. She received first-line chemotherapy with anthracycline-based regimens and showed stable disease. She is now a candidate for maintenance therapy with an anti-hormonal treatment of physician's choice. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0, and she has no comorbidities. She is willing to provide archived formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue block or a partial block from primary surgery and/or tumor or metastasis biopsy that can be used for further breast cancer research. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies to any drugs. Her laboratory results show normal organ function, and her estimated creatinine clearance is >60 mL/min. She has no evidence of active infection or other severe acute, uncontrolled, or chronic medical or psychiatric conditions that may increase the risk associated with study participation or investigational product administration. She is not pregnant or lactating and has negative urinary pregnancy test.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the rectum. He underwent surgical resection of the tumor and is now recommended for adjuvant radiation therapy. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. He is able to understand written and oral information and has provided written consent to participate in the study. He has no synchronous colonic tumors and is not currently on any immunosuppressive therapy. He does not have diabetes with systemic complications. He is physically fit and has no impaired general condition.

55 year old female with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to pneumonia, intubated and mechanically ventilated for past 2 days in the ICU. She is currently on continuous sedation with fentanyl and propofol. She has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or asthma. Her past medical history includes hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics for her pneumonia. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 150 mmHg. She is being monitored closely for any signs of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). The patient is alert but not oriented and is able to follow simple commands. She has no known drug allergies. The patient has no plans for withdrawal of life support and will be a good candidate for the study.

52-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of non-resectable glioblastoma (GBM). Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and the multidisciplinary team has recommended a clinical trial of cilengitide in combination with standard treatment. The patient has undergone dynamic MRI and FET-PET scans prior to randomization, and a Gd-MRI has been performed. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has been on a stable dose of steroids for 5 days prior to randomization. The patient does not have a history of recent peptic ulcer disease, bleeding disorders, or thromboembolic events. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction during the past 6 months prior to enrollment or uncontrolled arterial hypertension. The patient has provided written informed consent and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to possibly prolong life and learn more about her disease.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with fever, chills, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia and started on antibiotics. However, despite treatment, his condition deteriorated, and he was diagnosed with severe sepsis. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His weight is 85 kg. He is currently in the ICU, receiving mechanical ventilation, and his APACHE score is 25. He has acute kidney injury and metabolic acidosis. His white blood cell count is 16,000/mm3, and his neutrophil count is 85%. He has a serum sodium level of 140 mEq/L. He has never received IVIG therapy in the past.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 22 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has gained about 20 pounds so far during her pregnancy and has a family history of type 2 diabetes. During a routine glucose screening, her blood glucose levels were found to be elevated, and she was diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) according to the IADPSG criteria. She has not used insulin or any other oral hypoglycemic agents during this pregnancy. The patient is fluent in French and has social insurance. She has no history of bariatric surgery or any known hypersensitivity to dietary supplement ingredients. She is able to self-monitor her blood glucose levels and has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder. He presents with delayed language development, difficulty with social communication, and repetitive behaviors. He has difficulty making eye contact, responding to his name, and engaging in interactive play with peers. He also displays repetitive behaviors such as hand flapping and lining up toys. He currently receives speech therapy and occupational therapy twice a week, but his parents are interested in enrolling him in a 12-week early intervention program to further address his social communication deficits. The family is available to participate in the program hours and testing procedures.

10-year-old male diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) based on clinical features with onset of symptoms before the age of five. He has elevated serum creatine kinase levels and absence of dystrophin expression, as determined by immunostain or western blot (<2%) and/or DNA confirmation of a dystrophin mutation. He is currently ambulatory and has not been excluded based on corticosteroid treatment. The patient has no contraindication to an MR examination and does not have any unstable medical problems. He is able to cooperate during testing and does not have a secondary condition that may impact muscle metabolism, muscle function, or functional ability. The patient is not a participant in competitive sports specific training in excess of 8 hours per week, but does participate in multiple recreational sports activities.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with amblyopia in her right eye. She complains of poor vision in the affected eye and has difficulty reading and seeing objects from a distance. The patient has no history of eye injury or surgery. The ophthalmologist has detected no organic cause for the amblyopia. The patient has not received previous treatment for amblyopia. The patient's visual acuity in the affected eye is 6/60 Snellen's or counting fingers only, while her visual acuity in the unaffected eye is 6/6 Snellen's. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria of having strabismic amblyopia and is of any age.

Patient is a 3-year-old girl who was recently diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. She lives with her parents and has no other comorbidities. She has previously experienced severe hypoglycemic events and her A1C at screening is 9.5%. She is currently on multiple daily injections of Humalog and Lantus. Her parents and caregivers are fluent in English and are confident in their ability to operate all study devices and adhere to the protocol. The patient is willing to wear the system continuously throughout the study and participate in the supervised meal and exercise challenges. The patient has not been diagnosed with sickle cell disease, hemophilia, or any other bleeding disorders, nor does the patient have any skin conditions that would affect sensor or pump placement. The patient has not taken oral or injectable steroids within the past 8 weeks and is not planning to take them during the course of the study. The patient is willing to use only Humalog, Novolog, Admelog, or Apidra during the study and is willing to use the Dexcom App on the Omnipod Horizon™ PDM as the sole source of Dexcom data during the hybrid closed-loop phase. The patient's parents/legal guardians are willing and able to sign the informed consent form.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer, who had undergone a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy 5 years ago, presents with a 2-month history of persistent cough and weight loss. A chest X-ray revealed a right lung mass, which was further evaluated with a CT scan. The CT scan showed a 5 cm mass in the right upper lobe with mediastinal and hilar lymph node involvement. A biopsy of the mass confirmed adenocarcinoma of the lung. The patient was started on first-line chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel, but after 3 cycles, the disease continued to progress. The patient has no history of peripheral neuropathy or hypersensitivity reaction to prior paclitaxel therapy. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial of Epothilone D for advanced solid tumors and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 7 years. He has a history of smoking for 20 years, with a smoking cessation 5 years ago. He is currently taking two inhalers, one for bronchodilation and another for steroid treatment, but his symptoms including shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing are not well controlled. He has no known allergies or other medical conditions. His FEV1/FVC ratio is <0.70, and post-bronchodilator FEV1 is 50% predicted normal value calculated using the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III) reference equations, and is greater than or equal to 750 mL. He is willing to adjust his current COPD therapy as required by the protocol. He is a non-smoker and is not currently taking any other medications. He is willing to give signed written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to agree to approved contraceptive methods.

Pt is a 55yo male with a history of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that has progressed despite one round of systemic anti-cancer chemotherapy. The patient has Child-Pugh A and mild grade B (≤7) liver disease according to the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) staging system. The patient has lesions that can be assessed by imaging according to the Response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (RECIST) 1.1. The patient has not received antitumor immunoregulation therapy, immunosuppressive therapy, corticosteroids > 20 mg/day, growth factor therapy, or transfusion therapy within 14 days before use of the investigational drug. The patient has recovered from any toxic or side effects caused by previous treatment, with the exception of hair loss and other tolerable events as judged by the investigators. The patient does not have any peripheral neuropathy within 28 days prior to use of the investigational drug. The patient is not known to have any allergy or hypersensitivity to platinum drugs. The patient has not received any antitumor therapy like chemotherapy, biotherapy, radiotherapy, endocrine therapy, or target therapy within 4 weeks before use of the investigational drug. The patient has not undergone major surgery within 28 days before use of the investigational drug. The patient does not have any acute bacterial, viral or fungal infections requiring systemic treatment or unexplained fever during screening before the first administration of drug (body temperature> 38.5℃). The patient does not have moderate or massive effusion of body cavity that requires treatment. The patient does not have any history of mental illness or HIV carriers or AIDS patients. The patient does not have any of the following conditions within six months before signing the informed consent form: uncontrolled congestive heart failure, angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, stroke (except lacunar infarction), coronary/peripheral artery bypass surgery, or pulmonary embolism. The patient is not using any investigational drug or device within 28 days before the use of investigational drug. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to use effective adequate double contraceptives during the study or within three months after completion of the study.

The patient is a 10-month-old infant who has been suffering from mild to moderate eczema for the past 2 weeks. The eczema is primarily located on the face, neck, and upper extremities. The infant has not been treated with topical steroids class II or higher, oral steroids, or antibiotics prior to inclusion. The infant has no severe comorbidities and the parents are fluent in Dutch. The infant's diet consists of breast milk and baby formula, and there is no known family history of eczema or other allergic diseases. The parents are willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the therapeutic effects of a selected probiotic mixture on the severity of eczema.

The patient is a 27-year-old, right-handed, college graduate with no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is mentally healthy with no history of depression or psychosis. The patient has no contraindications for MRT and is not claustrophobic. The patient has no metallic implants or ferromagnetic metals in the body. The patient is not pregnant. The patient will undergo an unobtrusive neuropsychological screening to determine eligibility for the study.

A 5-year-old boy named Jack has been experiencing hearing difficulties and ear pain for the past few months. He has been diagnosed with otitis media with effusion and has been on watchful waiting treatment for 3 months. His parents are concerned about his condition and are looking for alternative treatment options to help alleviate his symptoms. Jack is an otherwise healthy child with no known medical conditions. He has not undergone tympanostomy in the past and is not taking any steroids or cytotoxic drugs. His parents are willing to participate in the study and have given their consent for Jack to receive acupuncture treatment if he is randomized into the acupuncture group.

A 47-year-old male with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) presents with steroid dependence and resistance. He has been on a prednisone equivalent dose of 30 mg/day for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with MDS 5 years ago and has been on supportive care with red blood cell transfusions and erythropoiesis stimulating agents (ESAs) for anemia. His last bone marrow biopsy showed 25% blasts, and he was classified as intermediate-2 risk according to International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS). He has no previous history of hypomethylating agents. His liver and kidney functions are normal. He is not a candidate for allogeneic stem cell transplantation due to lack of donor availability. He has no history of other malignancies, psychiatric illnesses, or serious medical conditions. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has no insurance affiliation.

A 45-year-old man with end-stage renal disease secondary to hypertension and diabetes is scheduled for a living donor kidney transplant. His sister is the donor and has been evaluated and cleared for donation. He is currently on hemodialysis three times per week, with no significant comorbidities. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve outcomes for transplant recipients. He is able to provide informed consent and is negative for tuberculosis and HIV. He meets all standard institutional criteria for kidney donation and Health Agency compliance with kidney donation regulations. He is not currently receiving treatment with an immunosuppressive agent other than a physiologic dose of corticosteroid.

Pt is a 45yo Chinese male with a 10-year history of rheumatoid arthritis. He reports experiencing joint pain and stiffness, particularly in his hands and feet, with occasional swelling. He has tried several nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) in the past, but has not found complete relief. He is currently taking ibuprofen as needed. He is interested in participating in this study to see if rofecoxib may be a more effective treatment option for his rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of COPD (Gold stage 2) as defined by post-bronchodilator spirometry FEV1 of 60% predicted, and FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.6. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and coughing for the past year. He has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. His BMI is 28 kg/m^2. He is currently taking tiotropium and salmeterol inhalers as well as albuterol as needed. He has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. He is willing and able to wear the designated devices for up to 24 hours per day and participate in laboratory and field-based exercise tests. He is capable of giving written informed consent and complying with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

The patient is a 25 year old healthy male who works as a software engineer. He has no significant medical history and his BMI is in the normal range. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He is willing to comply with the contraception requirements for this study. He has not participated in any clinical research studies or taken any investigational medicinal products in the last 90 days. He is willing and able to communicate and participate in the whole study and has provided written informed consent. He has no known drug or alcohol abuse history and has no allergies requiring treatment. He has not donated or lost more than 400 mL of blood in the last 3 months. He has no ongoing fungal infections or any other medical conditions that would preclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 55 year-old man who was recently diagnosed with liver cirrhosis. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption for over 20 years, and was found to have elevated liver function tests during a routine check-up. Abdominal ultrasound revealed a liver mass of 4 cm in diameter. He has no previous history of liver disease or viral hepatitis infection. He is a non-smoker and does not have any significant medical history aside from alcohol abuse. He has no family history of liver cancer. He currently takes no medications and does not have any allergies. He has agreed to participate in the study and will have his serum samples collected and tested for PIVKA-II, AFP and other tumor markers, as well as biochemical indexes including ALT, AST, GGT, AFU, etc. He has not received any treatment for his liver cirrhosis or liver mass, and his diagnosis will be established according to the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of Liver criteria.

A 32-year-old male patient was involved in a motorcycle accident and sustained a left tibial fracture. He was taken to the Emergency Department and had his left leg immobilized with a plaster cast. He is an otherwise healthy individual with no significant medical history. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. He is employed as a construction worker and leads an active lifestyle. He was advised to take bed rest for the first few days after the injury and then gradually start moving around with crutches. He is scheduled for a follow-up visit in 12 weeks to assess the healing of the fracture. The doctors have advised him that he may be at risk of developing blood clots in his leg due to the immobilisation and have offered him the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial to assess the risk factors for thrombosis in patients with lower limb injuries. The patient has consented to participate in the trial.

A 26-year-old female came to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial for avian flu vaccine. She is a healthy young adult with no history of chronic or acute illness requiring medical or surgical care. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and is committed to complying with study requirements. She is not pregnant and uses an effective form of birth control. She does not have a history of jaundice, hepatic injury, or hepatitis B and C. She has no abnormality in ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, or total bilirubin levels. She has not participated in any research involving investigational product within 45 days before planned date of first vaccination. She has not received any vaccine in the 4 weeks preceding the study vaccination, nor any A/H5N1 avian influenza vaccine at any time. She has no known or suspected immunosuppressive condition, acquired or congenital, and is not taking any immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within 6 months prior to the administration of the study vaccine. She has not received immunoglobulins and/or any blood products within the 3 months preceding the administration of the study vaccine or during the study. She has no acute disease at the time of enrollment and no known disturbance of coagulation. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse.

Patient A is a 65-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IV prostate cancer that has not responded to hormone therapy. He has been experiencing symptoms of prostate cancer such as difficulty urinating and bone pain for several months. He has a performance status of ECOG 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. His medical history includes hypertension, controlled with medication, and nonmelanoma skin cancer which was treated successfully 7 years ago. His blood work shows a WBC count of 4,500/mm3, a neutrophil count of 2,800/mm3, and a platelet count of 150,000/mm3. His liver function tests are normal with bilirubin level within the normal range and ALT within 1.5 times the upper limit of normal. His alkaline phosphatase is within 4 times the upper limit of normal. He has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy previously, and it has been at least one month since his last investigational agent. He agrees to complete written questionnaires and diaries throughout the study.

The patient is a 14 year old boy who recently underwent hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) for his leukemia. He is currently in the hospital for developing respiratory distress and requires mechanical ventilation for the past 3 days. His chest X-ray shows bilateral infiltrates and his oxygen saturation is low. His blood pressure and heart rate are stable. He has no prior history of asthma or any other lung disease. He has no allergies and takes no medications other than those prescribed for his leukemia. He lives with his parents and two siblings. He enjoys playing video games and watching movies. He is in the 9th grade and attends a local high school. He is fluent in English and has no difficulty in communicating. His BMI is 21 and he has no remarkable physical exam findings other than his respiratory distress.

A 55-year-old male with a history of smoking and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presented with shortness of breath and exercise intolerance. He has been diagnosed with moderate COPD according to the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease guidelines. His lung function test shows moderate airflow limitation with a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 50% predicted. He reports desaturation during exercise with an end-exercise SpO2 of 87% during his last exercise test. The patient does not require long-term oxygen therapy but is currently using low-flow oxygen during exercise. He is interested in participating in a study that evaluates a new system that automatically titrates oxygen flow during exercise to maintain stable SpO2.

A 28-year-old woman presents for her first antenatal visit at 11 weeks of gestation. She has regular menstrual cycles and has been trying to conceive for 6 months. She is a non-smoker and non-drinker. She has no significant medical or surgical history. Her family history is unremarkable. She is excited about her pregnancy and wants to ensure that everything is going well with her baby. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the learning curve for first trimester fetal anomaly scan. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and provides written consent to participate.

A 56-year-old man came to the clinic with a history of prostate cancer. He underwent radical prostatectomy 1 year ago, but his PSA level has been rising steadily for the past 6 months. His PSA level was 0.6 ng/mL at the reference value, and it has increased to 1.2 ng/mL and 1.5 ng/mL in the subsequent 2 measurements, respectively. He has no history of other malignancies, and he has never received any hormonal therapy. He has no known history of HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection. His Karnofsky Performance Score is 100, and his hematologic and biochemistry lab values are within normal limits. He has a Gleason Score of 7 in the prostatectomy specimen. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to use an effective barrier method of contraception during the study duration and for 3 months following discontinuation of the study drug. He has a life expectancy of more than 6 months. He is currently taking no medication except for a daily multivitamin.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it is focused on assessing the internal contamination prevalence by antineoplastic drugs in nursing staff who administers these chemotherapies or is in charge of patients treated by these chemotherapies. The study aims to identify contamination-associated factors in exposure characteristics and personal protective equipment use. The inclusion criteria are for nurses who have used at least one of the five antineoplastic drugs and/or to have cared one patient treated by one of the five antineoplastic drugs in the workday of participation to the study. The exclusion criteria are for nursing students, those treated or have been treated in the year before the workday of study participation by one of the five antineoplastic drugs, and those who have at home someone treated by one of the five antineoplastic drugs in the month before the workday of study participation.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He comes to the clinic complaining of shoulder pain, which has been present for the past 6 months. The pain is located in the anterior area of his shoulder and it worsens with overhead activities. He also reports difficulty lifting and carrying heavy objects. He does not have any known medical conditions and he does not take any medications. He is a non-smoker and he drinks alcohol occasionally. On physical examination, he has a painful arc of movement during flexion and abduction. The Neer and Kennedy-Hawkins impingement tests are positive, and he experiences pain on resisted lateral rotation and abduction. He has no clinical signs of full-thickness rotator cuff tears or shoulder capsulitis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effects of scapula based and scapula&rotator cuff based rehabilitation programs on symptoms, functional limitations, and acromiohumeral distance in individuals with subacromial pain syndrome.

A 55-year-old female patient with a history of advanced ovarian cancer that has failed first-line platinum and taxane-based regimen presents with progressive disease. The patient's disease relapse occurred within 1 year after completion of first-line therapy, making her eligible for the refractory disease stratum. The patient has at least 1 measurable lesion that is at least 20 mm by conventional techniques or at least 10 mm by spiral CT scan. The patient's hematopoietic system is functioning well with a neutrophil count of at least 2,000/mm^3 and a platelet count of at least 100,000/mm^3. The patient's liver function is normal with bilirubin less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) and alkaline phosphatase, SGOT, and SGPT no greater than 2.5 times ULN (no greater than 5 times ULN if hepatic metastases present). The patient's creatinine level is no greater than 1.7 mg/dL, indicating normal renal function. The patient has no unstable systemic disease or active uncontrolled infections. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use effective contraception as necessary. The patient has not undergone any major surgeries within the past 2 weeks and has not received any other concurrent anticancer agents or investigational therapy. The patient has no psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that would preclude compliance. This patient may be eligible to participate in the clinical trial testing nitrocamptothecin in treating patients with advanced ovarian cancer.

Patient is a 7-year-old boy who has never undergone anesthesia or surgery before. He has been scheduled for a same-day surgery to have his tonsils removed due to recurrent throat infections. He speaks English fluently and is accompanied by his mother who also speaks English. The child has no developmental delays or psychological or emotional disorders. He is not currently taking any sedative or psychoactive medication. The child has no known allergies to any of the medications used in the study. The family has no history of malignant hyperthermia or any other medical condition that would exclude him from the study. The child's surgery is not an emergency and he is not at risk of violent behavior during induction of anesthesia. Consent has been obtained from the parents and they are willing to participate in the study.

Patient is a 32-year-old male involved in a motor vehicle accident, presenting with multiple traumatic injuries, including a significant head injury. The patient's Glasgow Coma Scale score is 6, and he is requiring mechanical ventilation. Due to worsening respiratory status, the decision has been made to perform a prehospital emergency intubation. The patient has no known allergies or medical history that would preclude intubation.

A 62-year-old woman has been experiencing pain and cramping in her legs while walking for the past six months. She has noticed that the pain goes away when she stops walking and rests for a few minutes. She has a medical history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, but she is currently taking medication for both conditions. She does not smoke and does not have any history of diabetes. She has seen a specialist who has recommended an endovascular procedure to treat the peripheral artery disease (PAD). She has been informed of the study and has given her consent to participate.

35-year-old healthy Japanese female with no clinically relevant abnormalities identified by a detailed medical history, full physical examination, including blood pressure and pulse rate measurement, 12-lead ECG, and clinical laboratory tests. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 23.5 kg/m2 and a total body weight within the range of 50 to 100 kg. She has four Japanese grandparents who were born in Japan. She is not a smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has not taken any prescription or nonprescription drugs, vitamins and dietary supplements within 7 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) of the first dose of study medication. She is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. She has signed and dated an informed consent document or has a legally-acceptable representative who has signed on her behalf.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing bruising and petechiae for the past two months. She also reports fatigue, weakness, and occasional nosebleeds. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. Physical examination reveals multiple ecchymoses and petechiae on her arms and legs. Initial laboratory testing shows a platelet count of 22 x 10^9/L, and all other laboratory tests are within normal limits. She is diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) and started on a course of corticosteroids, but her platelet count fails to respond to first-line therapy. The treating physician recommends participation in a clinical trial investigating the combination of danazol with berberine in the treatment of ITP. The patient is informed of the potential benefits and risks of the trial and agrees to participate.

The patient is a 16-year-old female with severe acne who has been recommended to receive isotretinoin for therapeutic reasons. She weighs 110 lbs and has no known allergies to dextromethorphan, vitamin A, or isotretinoin. She is not pregnant and is able to follow the isotretinoin risk evaluation and mitigation strategies (REMS) program. She does not have a chronic or persistent cough, fever, kidney disease, liver disease, diabetes, or obesity (BMI <30 kg/m2). She does not have bipolar disease, attention deficit disorder, or social phobia. She is not currently taking any medications known to interact with DM or CYP2D6 or increase the risk of adverse effects from DM. She is willing and able to fast for 4 hours prior to the study and is able to provide written informed consent/assent.

A 55-year-old female diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease 3 years ago, currently taking medication to manage symptoms. She experiences occasional tremors, stiffness, and difficulty with balance and gait. She has no significant medical history beyond the Parkinson's diagnosis and is otherwise healthy. She is willing to commit to the study protocols and is interested in trying Tai Chi to improve her motor and cognitive function as well as her quality of life. She does not have a history of atypical parkinsonism, stroke, head trauma, brain tumor, brain injury, seizures or other central nervous system condition, orthopedic impairment or other disease that could contribute to a gait disturbance or parkinsonism. She is not currently experiencing any acute medical event or significant psychiatric illness. She meets all eligibility criteria and is excited to participate in the study.

The patient is a 57 year old male who has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few months. He visited his primary care physician who referred him to a gastroenterologist for further evaluation. After undergoing a series of tests including CT scans, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) and biopsy, he was diagnosed with gallbladder cancer. He has no prior history of chemotherapy and has a life expectancy of greater than 3 months. His ECOG performance status is 1 and his blood work shows leukocytes of 4,500/uL, absolute neutrophil count of 2,300/uL and platelets of 120,000/uL. His creatinine levels are within normal limits. His total bilirubin is slightly elevated (2.5 times the institutional upper limits of normal) but he meets the criteria for inclusion in the trial. He has no known allergies to any medications and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

50 year-old man who has been experiencing chronic joint pain and stiffness for the past 6 months, particularly in the small joints of his hands and feet. He has also noticed swelling and redness in these areas, which is worse in the mornings and improves throughout the day. He has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, but they have not provided much relief. He has never been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis before, but has a family history of the disease. He is interested in participating in a genetic and functional study of DNA repair system and the susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis. Past Medical History: 1. Hypertension 2. Hyperlipidemia 3. No history of autoimmune diseases.

A 28-year-old male with a history of alcohol and drug abuse, who has been recently admitted to outpatient addiction treatment services at RMHS Evergreen program. He has been screened positive for alcohol and mental health problems on the AUDIT and Modified MINI Screen (MMS) respectively. The diagnosis has been confirmed by SCID. The patient has a history of multiple hospitalizations and has attempted suicide in the past. He is currently stable and willing to provide informed consent. The patient has a job, but his work has been affected due to the substance use disorder.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired teacher who is fluent in English. She is living alone in her apartment and spends most of her day sitting down. She used to exercise regularly, but since she retired, she has become more sedentary. She is interested in participating in the trial to help her stay motivated to exercise. She has a personal computer and high-speed internet connection at home. She can walk 1/4 mile without stopping but currently engages in less than 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise and less than 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity exercise each week. She has not used a pedometer in the last 30 days and plans to stay in the area for the duration of the study. She has no history of myocardial infarction, stroke, transient ischemic attack, major cardiovascular surgery, deep venous thrombosis, or pulmonary embolus in the last 6 months. She does not have New York Heart Association Class III or IV heart failure, severe aortic stenosis, history of cardiac arrest, use of cardiac defibrillator, or severe angina. She has not had a hip fracture, total hip replacement, total knee replacement, or spinal surgery in the last 6 months. Her blood pressure is well-controlled, and she does not require supplemental oxygen. She has no diabetes mellitus requiring insulin therapy, severe osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis, end-stage renal disease requiring hemodialysis, movement disorder (e.g., Parkinson's disease), dementia, or major psychiatric disorder (e.g., schizophrenia or bipolar disorder). She does not consume ≥ 14 alcoholic drinks per week.

The patient is a 35 year-old male who was recently diagnosed with HIV infection. He has no known history of opportunistic infections or malignancies. He is currently not taking any antiretroviral therapy (ART). He smokes occasionally and consumes alcohol in moderate amounts. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to control his blood pressure. He has no known allergies to any medication. He has a stable job and is in a committed relationship with his partner. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old male from Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire who was recently diagnosed with HIV-1 infection during a blood donation. He has an estimated date of seroconversion and has never received ART for curative purposes. He is currently HIV-seronegative at the preceding donation and has returned to the clinic to be informed of his HIV test result. He has undergone HIV serology testing that has been confirmed with two specific tests in two different laboratories. He is aware of the study objectives and has signed informed consent. He is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history.

The patient is a 60 year old man who was incidentally found to have a small pulmonary nodule during a routine chest X-ray. Further evaluation with a CT scan revealed a 1.5 cm nodule in the right upper lobe of the lung. The patient has a history of smoking for 30 years but quit 5 years ago. He has no symptoms related to the nodule and has not experienced any weight loss, cough, or chest pain. His medical history is unremarkable and he is not taking any medications. His physical exam is normal and his vital signs are within normal limits. The patient is interested in minimally invasive surgical options for the removal of the nodule and is a candidate for VATS resection. However, the nodule is not deemed to be easily visualizable during VATS and therefore the intracavitary thoracoscopic ultrasound technique will be used to locate the nodule during the procedure. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to provide informed consent.

Pt is a 25yo M who has been wearing contact lenses for the past 3 years for myopia correction. He has no known ocular or systemic diseases and has not undergone any previous refractive surgery or orthokeratology treatment. His spectacle lens powers are -3.50 DS and -3.00 DS with no more than 1.5 diopters of astigmatism in each eye. He has good personal hygiene and has not experienced any adverse reactions to contact lens care products. He is willing to wear lenses in both eyes and has manifest refraction visual acuity equal to or better than 0.10 log MAR (20/25 Snellen) in each eye. The patient is not pregnant or planning a pregnancy within the next 3 months and is not a member, relative, or household member of the office staff. He is able to adhere to the instructions set forth in the protocol and able to keep all specified appointments. The patient meets the eligibility criteria and is a suitable candidate for the Acuity 200 (fluoroxyfocon A) Rigid Gas Permeable Contact Lens clinical trial.

A 56-year-old male patient was diagnosed with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) two months ago. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit smoking after his diagnosis. He has a cough with sputum, shortness of breath, and occasional chest pain. He is married and has two adult children. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He has not undergone any previous chemotherapy or targeted therapy. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has lost 3% of his weight in the past three months. His pulmonary function test shows that his FEV1 is 70% of predicted value. His laboratory tests show normal hepatic, renal, and hematologic functions, and creatinine clearance rate is 60 ml/min. He has no history of HIV, Hepatitis B or C, or other active malignancies. He is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

This is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids. She has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding, abdominal pain, and pressure. She has tried non-surgical treatment options, such as hormonal therapy, but has not seen any significant improvement in her symptoms. She is interested in laparoscopic myomectomy as a potential treatment option. She has an ASAPS classification of I and has no other significant medical history. She is not currently pregnant and has no history of suspicious findings of malignant gynecologic diseases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the surgical outcomes and efficacy of 3-dimensional (3D) versus 2-dimensional (2D) imaging systems in laparoscopic myomectomy.

This is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with liver cancer and is scheduled to undergo a major hepatic surgery for resection of greater than or equal to three hepatic segments. He is in good overall health with an ASA score of 2. He weighs 80 kgs and has no history of allergy or intolerance to indocyanine green or paracetamol. He has not taken paracetamol in the week leading up to the surgery. He has no history of psychiatric or intellectual disorders and is capable of understanding the protocol. He is not pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who has been coughing for the past two days due to a cold. The cough is more frequent at night and has been disturbing his sleep, as well as his parents' sleep. The child has not received any cough medicine or antihistamines in the last 24 hours. He has no history of asthma, sinusitis, or allergic rhinitis, and has no known sensitivity to any of the components of the placebo or the "Poliflav M.A.-honey cough syrup". The child's parent has provided written consent for the child's participation in the study.

A 7-day-old neonate was admitted to the NICU due to respiratory distress and apnea. The baby was born at 38 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery to a mother with no prenatal complications. The baby was intubated and started on a continuous infusion of fentanyl due to pain and agitation. The baby's medical history is otherwise unremarkable. The baby's weight is 3.2 kg, and the baby is currently receiving mechanical ventilation. The baby is expected to require opioid infusions for at least four days. The baby's parents have been informed and have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a neonate born prematurely at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 900 grams. The baby was admitted to the NICU due to respiratory distress syndrome and required intubation and mechanical ventilation. The baby's condition stabilized after surfactant therapy and a course of antibiotics for suspected sepsis. The baby is currently stable but requires close monitoring of respiratory rate, heart rate, and oxygen saturation levels. The parents have given written informed consent for the baby to participate in a clinical trial evaluating a novel non-contact physiological monitoring system in the NICU.

A 60-year-old female with a diagnosis of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease is being sought for a Phase II clinical trial. She should have a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 12-24 and must be living in the community with or have at least daily visits from a responsible carer who can assist with medication and attend assessments. The patient must not have any primary, secondary or pseudodementias other than probable Alzheimer's disease, must not have any clinically significant and/or uncontrolled conditions, and must not have taken medication for symptoms of dementia for less than 3 months prior to enrollment. The patient must not have been treated with any drugs known to have a well-defined potential for hepatotoxicity in the previous 3 months and must not be taking anti-oxidant supplements. Additionally, the patient must not be an active smoker of tobacco and should not be considered malnourished (with a body mass index of less than 19). Finally, the patient must not be contra-indicated for a lumbar puncture. Written consent should be obtained from the patient and responsible carer.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of periodontal disease. He has noticed bleeding and inflammation in his gums with a bad breath for the past few months. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He has a BMI of 26 and his blood pressure is normal. On examination, there is visible inflammation and bleeding in the gums, with deep pockets of 6-9mm. Radiographic examination shows significant alveolar bone loss. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. She is currently on metformin 1000mg twice a day and has well-controlled blood sugar levels. She has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. She denies any symptoms of chest pain, palpitation, or shortness of breath. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 28 kg/m2 and blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. Her most recent hemoglobin A1C level is 7.2%. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the prevalence and determinants of subclinical cardiovascular dysfunction in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in the study. She has no history of angina pectoris or limiting dyspnea, major atherosclerotic disease, atrial fibrillation or flutter, moderate or severe valvular heart disease, history of heart failure or cardiomyopathy, type 1 diabetes mellitus, or stage III-V renal disease.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who sustained a traumatic brain injury (TBI) in a car accident 6 months ago. He suffered a loss of consciousness for a few minutes and has been experiencing balance dysfunction since the injury. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medication that may affect his balance or muscle coordination. He is fluent in English and has 20/20 vision in both eyes. He is able to follow commands and is willing to participate in the study. He has not had any physical or occupational therapy for balance disorder in the past 30 days. He is currently not enrolled in any other research study that may affect his participation in this clinical trial.

Patient is a 58-year-old man with a history of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has received multiple lines of therapy including gemcitabine, nab-paclitaxel, FOLFIRINOX, and recently completed treatment with a PARP inhibitor. His disease has progressed despite these treatments, and his performance status is ECOG 1. Imaging studies show multiple liver metastases and mild ascites, but no brain metastases. Genetic testing of his tumor demonstrates an activating KRAS mutation. He has no significant cardiovascular disease, but has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled on medication. He has no active infections and no history of significant immunosuppressive therapy. His renal and hepatic function are within normal limits. He has measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 criteria. He is willing to comply with the scheduled visits, drug administration plan, protocol-specified laboratory tests, other study procedures, and study restrictions.

A 55-year-old man with a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection for the past 15 years presented with abdominal discomfort and mild jaundice. He has been compliant with his antiviral therapy, but his most recent liver function tests indicated a mild elevation in liver enzymes. He has no history of alcohol consumption or drug abuse. Physical examination revealed hepatomegaly and mild jaundice. Transient elastography (TE) was performed by a trained operator, but the result was considered unreliable due to an inability to obtain a valid measurement. The patient agreed to participate in this clinical trial and will undergo a second evaluation by an experienced operator (>500 explorations) using the standard size (M) probe. If still inadequate, a third exploration will be performed using the XL (obese size) probe. Diagnostic accuracy will be estimated in patients with liver biopsy to identify significant fibrosis with a TE cut-off value of 7.6 kPa (kilo pascal). The patient provided signed informed consent and meets all eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He has no history of any other medical conditions, surgeries, or allergies. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol on rare occasions. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating for the past few months, leading him to seek medical attention. Imaging studies confirmed the presence of a mass in the pancreas, and biopsy results confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer. The patient underwent surgery for pancreatic cancer, and the abdominal incision was double-closed with continuous suture of linea alba and fascia with absorbable suture, and skin was sutured with skin staples. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and will be monitored for any signs of heterotopic ossification of the abdominal incision for one year after surgery.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been on dialysis for the last 3 years due to end-stage renal disease. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking multiple medications, including insulin, metformin, lisinopril, and simvastatin. He has been approved for a deceased donor kidney transplant, and his surgery is scheduled in a month. He has no history of allergies or surgeries in the past. His family history is negative for any kidney diseases. He is married and has two children. He lives with his wife and has a stable job as an accountant. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide signed written informed consent. He understands the study procedures and is willing to comply with them. He agrees to use an acceptable method to avoid pregnancy if he has a female partner during the study period. He has no active systemic infection that requires the continued use of antibiotics, and his HIV and hepatitis B and C tests were negative. He has no neoplasia except for localized skin cancer that has been treated. He has no other medical conditions that might interfere with his participation in the study.

A 52-year old woman with type 2 diabetes was diagnosed five years ago. She is under follow-up with an endocrinologist and is taking Metformin as well as Insulin glargine. She has a history of hypertension and takes Lisinopril. The patient has a smoking history, but she quit smoking six months ago. She works as a teacher and experiences bleeding while brushing her teeth. She also complains of sensitivity while eating cold food. The patient has never undergone orthodontic treatment. Her last complete blood count was within normal limits. The patient is not pregnant and has no history of cancer. She has not taken antibiotics or anti-inflammatory medication in the past six and three months, respectively. The patient is willing to participate in the study and agrees to attend all follow-up visits.

A 57-year-old man presented to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and rectal bleeding. He had a history of smoking and alcohol use. On physical examination, he was found to have a palpable mass in his rectum, and a colonoscopy confirmed the presence of a tumor. A biopsy was performed, and the patient was diagnosed with T4 adenocarcinoma of the rectum. Imaging studies showed no evidence of distant metastases. The surgeon evaluated the patient and determined that the tumor was mobile and completely resectable with negative margins. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or pelvic irradiation therapy. His ECOG performance status is 1. His labs are remarkable for WBC count of 4500/uL, platelets of 110,000/uL, serum creatinine of 1.8 mg/dL, serum bilirubin of 1.5 mg/dL, alk phos of 80 U/L, and SGOT of 50 U/L. The patient has no active inflammatory bowel disease or other serious medical illness that might limit his ability to receive protocol therapy.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic back pain for the past year. She has been prescribed opioid pain medication for management, but has noticed that she experiences infrequent bowel movements and abdominal discomfort. She has not been using any laxatives to relieve the symptoms. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or allergies. She has not had any recent surgeries or procedures and is not currently taking any prohibited medications. The patient is willing to discontinue the use of any laxatives and use only the rescue laxatives provided throughout the study duration. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of naldemedine in the treatment of opioid-induced constipation.

The patient is a 16-month-old child who was diagnosed with spastic cerebral palsy by a pediatric neurologist. The child was born at term and had a normal birth weight. The diagnosis of spastic CP was made after the child's parents expressed concerns about delayed developmental milestones. The child has difficulty with sitting and crawling, and is unable to walk. There is no history of seizures or other neurological disorders. The child does not have any medical conditions that would prevent the administration of rehabilitation therapies at the intensity required by the study. The child's parents are motivated to participate in the study and are able to commit to the required therapy sessions. The child is currently receiving physical and occupational therapy once a week, which is the standard of care in the Western Hemisphere. The child is classified as GMFCS level II, indicating moderate motor dysfunction. The child does not have any co-morbidities that are not typically associated with CP, and there are no anticipated pharmacological interventions or procedures that would interfere with the study.

63 yo Caucasian male diagnosed with gastric cancer, presenting with complaints of abdominal pain, nausea, and weight loss. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He is currently not on any pain medications and has not received any palliative care. He denies any history of smoking, alcohol or drug use. He is retired and lives with his wife who is his primary caregiver. He has two grown children who live out of town. The patient is able to complete the symptom assessment form on his own. He has regular appointments with a GI oncologist and is scheduled to attend a clinic on one of the specified intervention days. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

32-year-old female with a history of chronic Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection diagnosed six months ago. The patient is HBeAg positive and has a HBV DNA level of 2x10^7 copies/mL by Abbott real-time PCR. She has not received any oral treatment for HBV in the past. She reports no significant medical history, allergies, or medication use. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study drug regimen and all other study procedures and requirements. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent before any study assessment is performed. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using an acceptable method of contraception. She is not currently abusing alcohol or illicit drugs and has no history of alcohol or illicit substance abuse within the preceding two years. The patient has no other concurrent medical or social conditions that are likely to preclude compliance with the schedule of evaluations in the protocol or confound the efficacy or safety observations of the study.

The patient is a 67 year old man who recently had a stroke and was diagnosed with 80% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery by angiogram. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes for which he is taking medications. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He has no contraindications for anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy. He has a reference vessel diameter of 5.5 mm at the target lesion and a vessel diameter distal to the target lesion of 4.5 mm. He is willing and able to comply with all follow-up requirements and has provided a signed informed consent prior to participation in the Registry.

A 50-year-old man visited the clinic with a history of hypertension and diabetes. He had been diagnosed with coronary artery disease a year ago, and had undergone angiography. His high sensitivity C-reactive protein was measured as 2.5 mg/L in his last check-up. He had been taking guideline-based secondary prevention medications for the past 6 months. He had no history of retinal disease and his liver function tests were within normal limits. His estimated glomerular filtration rate was 70 mL/min/1.73m². He was not anemic and had normal platelet and white blood cell counts. He had no contraindications for hydroxychloroquine usage. He had no active hemorrhage, cancer or plans for percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass grafting. He was not pregnant or lactating. His New York Heart Association functional class was class II.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma about 2 years ago. She initially received R-CHOP chemotherapy and achieved a complete response. However, after 6 months, she experienced a relapse with new lymphadenopathy and was treated with R-GDP chemotherapy. She achieved a partial response but relapsed again after 4 months. The patient is currently experiencing night sweats, fatigue, and a 5% weight loss over the past 3 months. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2. She has no significant medical or surgical history and is not taking any medications. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for palpable cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes. Her laboratory results show: Hemoglobin: 11.0 g/dL White blood cell count: 6.0 × 10^9/L with 40% neutrophils, 40% lymphocytes, 15% monocytes, and 5% eosinophils Platelet count: 110 × 10^9/L Blood chemistry: Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL Albumin: 3.2 g/dL AST: 20 U/L ALT: 18 U/L Alkaline phosphatase: 90 U/L LDH: 400 U/L Beta-2 microglobulin: 3.5 mg/L The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive novel combination therapy for relapsed and refractory aggressive B-cell lymphoma.

A 35-year-old man presents to the clinic with a history of feeling sad and hopeless for the past few months. He reports a loss of interest in activities that he previously enjoyed and has been experiencing trouble sleeping and poor appetite. He has a history of depression and has been previously treated with antidepressants. He is currently not taking any medication for his depression. He reports feeling frustrated and exhausted with his current state and is seeking help to improve his mood and quality of life. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He enjoys reading and playing soccer but has stopped participating in these activities since his mood has worsened. He is willing to participate in a 14-week psychotherapy treatment and is interested in exploring different types of therapy.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has had a history of smoking for 30 years, but quit 10 years ago. He was diagnosed with stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) on a recent CT scan, and his pulmonary function tests showed a preoperative FEV1 of 75% and DLco of 79%. He is scheduled to undergo a lobectomy with incomplete fissures on CT scan. He has no other significant medical history, and his physical examination findings are normal. He has no allergies to any medications or substances. He has been informed about the study and has provided written consent to participate.

A 45-year-old Asian-American man was referred to the hepatology clinic for management of newly diagnosed chronic hepatitis C infection. He reported no significant past medical history and denied any symptoms related to liver disease, such as jaundice, abdominal pain, or fatigue. He reported occasional alcohol use and denied any history of injection drug use. Physical examination was unremarkable except for mild hepatomegaly on palpation of the abdomen. Laboratory tests showed elevated liver enzymes with ALT of 87 U/L and AST of 65 U/L. Serologic testing was positive for anti-HCV antibodies and quantitative PCR confirmed the presence of HCV RNA with a viral load of 4.5 million IU/mL. Liver biopsy revealed chronic active hepatitis with stage 2 fibrosis. The patient was interested in participating in a clinical trial and was found to be eligible for the study of nitazoxanide in the treatment of chronic hepatitis C.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing progressive weakness and numbness in his legs for the past 8 months. He reports difficulty with walking and has noticed a decrease in his overall coordination. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. The patient underwent an MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine, which showed a syrinx extending from C6-T1. The patient was diagnosed with syringomyelia and referred to the study for further evaluation. He has not received any surgical or interventional treatment for his condition. His physical examination is significant for decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick in his lower extremities, with normal strength in his upper extremities. He has no gait abnormalities and is able to walk independently. The patient is willing to participate in the registry and donate biosamples for research purposes.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman who suffered from a second-degree burn injury on her left arm about 8 months ago. She has been experiencing erythema, pruritus, and surface irregularity on the affected area which has been causing her discomfort and self-consciousness. She has not undergone any previous laser treatment for her burn scars and desires laser treatment to improve the appearance of the affected area. She is willing to participate in a two-year study and is able to follow the protocol requirements. The patient is not pregnant, does not have any open wounds, is not taking systemic steroids or immunosuppression medication, and does not have any connective tissue disorder. She is medically fit to undergo anesthesia and does not have any other condition that may compromise study objectives.

A 68-year-old woman presents with a diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer, which has spread to her bones and liver. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and hormone therapy, but the disease has progressed despite treatment. She has been referred to the palliative care team at the University Hospital Basel for symptom management and support. She reports feeling anxious and depressed about her prognosis and is struggling to find a sense of purpose and meaning in her life. She speaks German fluently and is willing to commit to at least three contacts over 7-10 days to participate in the study. She is alert and oriented, with a normal cognitive function, and has no history of delirium or other substantial cognitive impairment.
