She is motivated to explore different interventions that may help her feel more dignified, find meaning, and relieve her psychological distress.

Patient is a 45-year-old healthy male who does not smoke or use nicotine-containing products. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse in the last 2 years and has not participated in any clinical study with an investigational product in the last 60 days. The patient has no history of serious allergic reactions to any medication and has not donated blood or plasma or had any other loss of blood exceeding 500 mL within 3 months before dosing. The patient is willing to comply with all protocol requirements and procedures, and agrees to use birth control during the study and 3 months post last visit.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has a BMI of 22 and normal results on his biochemistry, CBC, and urinalysis tests. He does not have any allergies or known allergies to MRI contrast agents. He abstains from alcohol and caffeine consumption within the last 48 hours prior to the administration of the study contrast agent, and has not participated in any other investigational trials or received any contrast agents within the last 28 days prior to study enrollment. He is willing to comply with the protocol and sign the informed consent form.

32 F with a history of infertility who underwent in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycle with frozen embryo transfer (FET) and is scheduled for transfer in the next cycle. She has a regular menstrual cycle and no history of uterine abnormalities. BMI is 25 kg/m2. No history of irregular heartbeats or high blood pressure. She is not currently taking any medications that interact with cytochrome P450 activity. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the past three months. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He has been advised to undergo allogeneic HCT by his medical team. He is fluent in English, has completed high school education and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has access to a telephone for study-related communication. He has no history of other major illnesses or comorbidities, and his physical examination shows no abnormalities. He is currently on chemotherapy and is expected to undergo transplantation in the next 3 months. He has no language or communication barriers. He is able to read and write in English and is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

70 yo F who underwent minimally invasive TKA in her left knee 4 months ago. She has been experiencing difficulty in walking and climbing stairs since the surgery. She has a history of hypertension, but it is well controlled with medication. She is not currently participating in regular exercise and does not have any neurological conditions affecting her mobility. She speaks fluent English and is interested in participating in the study to improve her mobility and overall health. She has not had any recent falls and has not had any malignancies or life-threatening illnesses in the past 6 months. She is cleared by her physician to participate in the study.

As this is an observational study, there is no specific patient description needed for this trial. However, to provide context, a potential patient who could be eligible for this study would be a 60-year-old male with a history of chest pain and diagnosed with 3-vessel coronary artery disease. He is scheduled for elective off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting surgery. He has no history of cerebrovascular accident, arteriovenous shunts, intracardiac shunts, or stenosis of the internal carotid artery of > 60%. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old man who has been dealing with moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis for several years is seeking a long-term treatment option. He has tried various medications in the past including topical creams and oral medications, but none have provided the relief he needs. He is generally healthy, with no underlying medical conditions or allergies. He is currently taking a daily multivitamin and exercises regularly. He has not participated in this study before and is willing to use an acceptable method of contraception if necessary. He is committed to completing all dosing requirements and following the study's protocol.

A 55 year old male patient presented to the clinic with a history of unilateral knee pain for the past 5 years. He reports that the pain has become progressively worse and now severely limits his mobility and daily activities. He has been diagnosed with unicompartmental tibiofemoral osteoarthritis of the knee and has been recommended for a unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. The patient has a BMI of 30, with no other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the MOTO Post-marketing Surveillance Study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) during a routine cervical cancer screening. She has aspirations for future pregnancies and is interested in conservative management instead of immediate cervical conization. She has a history of smoking but has quit for the past two years. She has been in a monogamous relationship for the past five years and has not had any recent sexually transmitted infections. Her physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable for any other abnormalities. She has been informed of the risks and benefits of both cervical conization and active surveillance of HSIL and has chosen the latter. She is committed to attending follow-up visits at regular intervals and will be followed-up regularly with colposcopy, cytology, human papillomavirus (HPV) testing, and biopsies. If the lesions progress or HSIL persists after 24 months of follow-up, conization will be indicated. The patient has positive high-risk (hr) HPV cytology but is otherwise in good health.

Pt is a 60yo M who suffered a stroke 8 months ago resulting in mild-moderate gait impairment. He is able to walk independently with a cane but has difficulty maintaining a consistent speed and experiences occasional falls. He has completed formal rehabilitation and is looking for additional ways to improve his walking ability. He is otherwise healthy with no significant cardiac or pulmonary disease. He speaks English fluently and is able to follow instructions. He has no significant lower extremity spasticity but does experience mild depression, with a PHQ-9 score of 8. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new rehabilitation strategies for stroke survivors.

The patient is a 55 year old male who was diagnosed with stage IIIb non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) two months ago. He is a former smoker and quit smoking 10 years ago. He has a history of mild hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history or allergies. He works as a chef and enjoys cooking in his free time. He has a supportive family including a spouse and two adult children. He is interested in participating in clinical trials and is willing to undergo any necessary tests or procedures. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and his life expectancy is estimated to be at least 6 months. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for his NSCLC.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with advanced breast cancer with HER-2 positive histology. She has been receiving trastuzumab along with chemotherapy for the past 6 months. She has not shown any evidence of disease progression and has an estimated life expectancy of at least 3 months. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is less than 2. She has adequate bone marrow, liver, kidney, and cardiac function. She is willing and able to comply with study procedures and answer the study questionnaires. She has been informed about the study and has signed the informed consent document for entry into the trial. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using a non-hormonal contraceptive method. She has no history of uncontrolled brain metastases, severe dyspnea at rest, or any other concomitant serious systemic disease that would prevent her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix two years ago. She has undergone treatment with one regimen of chemotherapy, but her cancer has progressed and was deemed inoperable. The patient is still able to function with an ECOG performance status of 1. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to provide written informed consent. The patient has no known additional malignancy that is progressing or requires active treatment. She has never received radiation therapy within ≤2 weeks of first ADXS11-001 infusion. The patient has no contraindication to administration of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole or ampicillin. She does not have implanted medical devices that pose a high risk for colonization and/or cannot be easily removed. The patient is an ideal candidate for the clinical trial.

50-year-old female diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer, which has been successfully treated with surgery and chemotherapy. The patient has p53-positive ovarian cancer, and therefore may be eligible for participation in a clinical trial of a p53 vaccine. She has an ECOG performance status of 0, demonstrating that she is fully active and able to carry out all pre-disease activities without restriction. Her expected survival is more than 3 months. She has not received chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy or systemic doses of steroids for at least 4 weeks prior to starting vaccination and has recovered from all acute toxicities of previous treatment. Her platelet count, creatinine, serum bilirubin, SGOT, and SGPT levels are all within the normal range. She is HIV and Hepatitis B and C negative. She is not pregnant or nursing and has agreed to use adequate contraception. She has no active ischemic heart disease, arrhythmias or other cardiac diseases. She has no history of CNS metastases or autoimmune diseases. She is willing to sign an informed consent document and has HLA-A2.1 haplotype. She is eligible for the trial, and the trial may provide a potential option to help boost her immune system to fight against any remaining cancer cells.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease for the past 2 years. She has been on a stable dose of donepezil for the past 6 months. Her Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) total score is 20, and Modified Hachinski Ischemic Scale (MHIS) score is 2. She has a history of hypertension and controlled type 2 diabetes. She has no history of significant sensitivity or allergy to any drug. She has not received any investigational product within 6 weeks prior to study drug administration. She has no significant neurological disease other than AD. She has no significant current suicidal ideation as evidenced by the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) completed at Screening. She has had a computerized tomography or magnetic resonance imaging scan within 36 months prior to randomization, which showed no evidence for an alternative etiology for dementia.

A 32-year-old male patient was admitted to TIRR Memorial Hermann with a diagnosis of traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI) resulting in paraplegia. The patient had a motor vehicle accident four weeks ago, which resulted in a T10 neurologic level injury. The patient is currently taking pain medications due to severe neuropathic pain in the lower extremities. The patient is fluent in English and able to communicate effectively. The patient has no history of peripheral neuropathy, nervous system disorders, or chronic pain. The patient is not dependent on a ventilator and is able to speak. The patient has no intolerance to electric stimulation and is willing to participate in the trial sessions. The patient is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce their neuropathic pain and spasticity.

45-year-old male patient with chronic mid-thoracic back pain that radiates towards the left arm. The patient has been experiencing the pain for over a year, despite trying various non-invasive treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications. The patient has no known allergies or coagulopathies. The patient has been scheduled for a transforaminal epidural injection in the mid-thoracic region (T5-T7) to relieve the pain. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial comparing anterioposterior versus oblique view approach method for fluoroscopically-guided epidural block.

This is a 55 year-old male with a history of hepatocellular carcinoma who has been scheduled for laparotomic liver resection. He has no known contraindications to spinal anesthesia or intrathecal morphine and has not had any issues with drug dependence or chronic pain. His body mass index is 27 kg/m2 and he has no history of sleep apnea. He has been informed about the study and has given his consent to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who suffered a cervical spinal cord injury resulting in tetraplegia. He has limited or no use of both hands and has less than grade 4 muscle strength in elbow extension and wrist extension, as well as less than grade 2 strength in finger flexor and abduction on the contralateral side to the implant. The patient reports that he is unable to perform functional activities with the hand contralateral to the implantation. He is over 1 year post-injury and reports no worsening in neurologic status for the previous 6 months. The patient is between the ages of 22-70 years old and lives within 1 hour of the University of Pittsburgh. He is able to communicate with the investigators in English and has shown an understanding of the study goals and the ability to follow simple directions. The patient has normal limits on neuropsychological and psychosocial assessment, and has a stable psychosocial support system and caregivers who are able to perform the necessary daily care of the participant's skin and pedestal site. The patient has a life expectancy greater than 18 months and has provided informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with low-to-intermediate-risk prostate cancer. He has been informed of various treatment options and has chosen to undergo I-125 LDR brachytherapy at the Sunnybrook Odette Cancer Centre. His prostate volume on TRUS is less than 60 cc. He is able to give informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have locally advanced or metastatic disease, has not undergone prior Trans Urethral Resection of the Prostate (TURP), and his International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) is less than 18. He is not receiving salvage or boost treatments after primary external radiation or brachytherapy and is not currently on any other study protocols with prescription doses other than 145 Gy. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help advance the field of prostate cancer treatment and to potentially benefit from the use of a novel machine learning algorithm in treatment planning. He is willing to attend follow-up appointments and comply with the study protocol.

Patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been admitted to the hospital for pneumonia and is currently under isolation precautions due to the presence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs). She has been in the hospital for 10 days and has experienced significant deconditioning during this time, resulting in a decrease in motor strength. She has been assessed by the managing team and deemed to be unfit for discharge within the next 2 weeks. The patient is able to give consent and has a motor power grading of 3/5. She does not have any underlying medical disorders that result in pre-existing lower limb weakness.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. She was exposed to the virus while caring for her elderly mother who was also infected. She was admitted to the hospital for difficulty breathing and low oxygen levels. She requires supplemental oxygen and is currently on noninvasive ventilation. She has a history of hypertension and hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with medication. She does not have any known drug allergies or sensitivities. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is concerned about missing work due to her illness. She is willing to participate in the study and follow all instructions given by the study team.

A 62-year-old Asian male presents with a history of metastatic colorectal cancer. He was initially diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the colon and underwent surgical resection. However, the cancer recurred and spread to the liver and lungs. He has received two prior regimens of standard chemotherapies, but his cancer has continued to progress. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to take medication orally. His bone marrow, kidney, and liver function are adequate. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. A pregnancy test is not applicable as he is male.

The patient is a 55-year-old individual diagnosed with type II diabetes for the past five years. The patient has a history of poor blood sugar control despite taking metformin 500mg twice a day, with the most recent HbA1c level being 8.5%. The patient has mild hypertension controlled with lisinopril 10mg daily. The patient reports occasional headaches, sleep disturbances, and mild anxiety but denies any depression symptoms, infections, or skin problems. The patient's diet is balanced, with no specific restrictions on sugar intake. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine if Kombucha can help improve their blood sugar control and overall quality of life. The patient owns a glucometer and is capable of monitoring their blood sugar levels daily.

A 32-year-old male OIF/OEF veteran presented to the primary care clinic for follow-up after experiencing traumatic events during his military service. He reported symptoms of feeling on edge, nightmares, and flashbacks. He was diagnosed with PTSD based on the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-IV (CAPS) and referred to the Behavioral Activation (BA) intervention for PTSD treatment. He is fluent in English and has no history of bipolar disorder, psychotic disorders or substance dependence. He is willing and able to comply with study regulations and assessment and therapy schedules. His current medication includes sertraline and he has no history of suicidal ideation or behavior. He is interested in participating in the study and contributing to research that may benefit other OIF/OEF veterans with PTSD.

A 48-year-old Hispanic man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 7 years came to the clinic with complaints of erectile dysfunction. He is currently taking oral hypoglycemic agents to manage his diabetes. He has been in a stable heterosexual relationship for the past 10 years. The patient reports a decreased frequency of morning erections and difficulty achieving and maintaining erections during sexual activity. His initial IIEF score was 18. The physical examination revealed no abnormalities. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any nitrates or anti-coagulants. He has no significant history of heart disease or myocardial infarction in the past 6 months. The patient is willing to sign informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

67 year old male with a history of rheumatic heart disease, presenting with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis and requiring aortic valve replacement. Preoperative echocardiography showed aortic valve area of 0.7 cm2 and mean gradient of 45 mmHg. The patient has no known allergies and is currently taking aspirin and atorvastatin. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and has no significant non-cardiac medical history. The patient has good functional status and is able to perform daily activities with minimal limitation. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and is geographically stable.

A 52-year-old male with a history of ocular adnexal MALToma that has recently been diagnosed with low-grade mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma in the colon. The patient has no significant medical history or comorbidities and has not received any prior treatment for the colon MALToma. The patient is experiencing mild abdominal discomfort and occasional diarrhea. The patient has been evaluated for Helicobacter pylori (HP) infection and the results are negative. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy of frontline HPE (clarithromycin, amoxicillin, and omeprazole) in the treatment of early-stage extragastric MALToma. The patient understands the possible benefits and risks associated with the trial and has provided informed consent for participation.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids and will be undergoing major abdominal surgery. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to manage her blood pressure. The patient reports no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. She is classified as an ASA physical status II patient. The patient is not experiencing any symptoms related to her hypertension and her blood pressure is well controlled on her current medication regimen. She has no history of arrhythmia or severe right ventricular failure. The patient is willing and able to participate in the study and understands the requirements and procedures involved.

An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension presented to his primary care physician's office for routine blood pressure measurement. He has been taking medication for hypertension for the past 5 years. He has a history of falls in the past year and is worried about his overall health. He lives alone and is independent in performing his daily activities. He has no history of cardiovascular disease, stroke, or myocardial infarction. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has a regular exercise routine and follows a healthy diet. He has no known allergies or current medical issues. He has been a registered patient with his current general practitioner for the past 10 years.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of recurrent and metastatic ovarian cancer is seeking treatment options for her condition. She has undergone two prior platinum-based regimens and has recently been experiencing worsening symptoms. She has no allergies to any medication and has not received gemcitabine in the past. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and her life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 6 months. Her blood work shows normal leukocyte and platelet levels, with a creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. She has no history of brain metastases or Li Fraumeni syndrome. She is not pregnant and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for 6 months after completion of M6620 administration. She understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

A 63-year-old male presents with chronic back pain and increasing fatigue over the past few months. On evaluation, laboratory tests reveal anemia and elevated calcium levels. Further diagnostic workup reveals multiple lytic bone lesions and a bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of multiple myeloma. The patient has not received any prior systemic therapy for multiple myeloma. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and his calculated creatinine clearance is 65 mL/minute. He has no history of uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes. He has no active infections or significant neuropathy. He has no contraindications to the required concomitant drugs or supportive treatments. He is willing to comply with the drug administration requirements and does not have any gastrointestinal procedures that could interfere with oral absorption or tolerance of treatment. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials with investigational agents.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who has been experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and swelling in his legs and feet for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He has a family history of heart disease but no personal history of cancer or other serious illnesses. He underwent a series of tests, including blood tests, imaging, and a biopsy, which revealed a diagnosis of primary systemic amyloidosis. He has not received any prior treatment for this condition. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria, including having no uncontrolled diabetes, active peptic ulcer disease, or medical condition that precludes high-dose steroids. He will be closely monitored throughout the trial and receive dexamethasone plus interferon alfa as part of the treatment plan. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is committed to following the study protocol.

This clinical trial does not involve patients directly. Instead, it will analyze data from various National Quality Registries and population surveys in Sweden to investigate the variability of patients' self-reported overall health on the visual analogue scale (EQ VAS) across different disease groups and over time. Therefore, there are no specific eligibility or exclusion criteria for patients.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who owns a handgun for self-defense purposes. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has experienced suicidal ideation in the past. She is currently receiving therapy and taking medication to manage her mental health. She lives alone in a rented apartment in a high-crime area of the city. She works full-time as a customer service representative and spends her free time reading and watching movies. She is willing to participate in the study and is interested in learning more about gun safety. She has never used a gun lock before but is open to using one if it can help keep her safe. She is available for all three study sessions and is willing to complete online assessments.

A 53-year-old man with a history of smoking came to the clinic complaining of abdominal pain and weight loss. He has lost approximately 10 kg in the past month and has been experiencing severe abdominal pain that radiates to his back. A CT scan showed a mass in the head of the pancreas that is causing obstruction of the bile duct. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The patient has not received any previous chemotherapy or radiation therapy for the disease. His ECOG score is 1, and his blood work is within normal limits. He is a candidate for first-line systemic chemotherapy according to standard practice. The patient has signed the consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

An 67-year-old Caucasian female presented with a new lump in her right breast. She noticed it about a month ago and it has remained the same size since then. She has no family history of breast cancer and no other significant medical history. She takes medication for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Physical exam revealed a firm, non-tender mass in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast measuring 1.5 cm. No axillary lymph nodes were palpable. Mammography and ultrasound confirmed a well-defined, oval-shaped mass with smooth margins and no calcifications. Biopsy confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma, estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative, and grade 2. The patient is planned for a partial mastectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy. She is otherwise in good health with a WHO performance status of 1. She is 67 years old and meets all other inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

A 50-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant with reduced intensity conditioning. The patient developed diarrhea that was not responsive to standard peri-/post-transplant supportive care. The patient has not had any history of chronic intestinal disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 70%. The patient has no other active malignancy within the last 2 years and has not had any allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition to the study agent. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to be followed for the planned duration of the trial.

A 62-year-old man was brought to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He takes metformin and lisinopril. The patient is a smoker with a 40 pack-year history. The last cigarette was smoked 2 hours before the onset of symptoms. On examination, the patient is awake, alert, and oriented. He has right-sided facial droop, right-sided hemiparesis, and mild dysarthria. NIH Stroke Scale score is 10. The CT scan of the brain shows no evidence of hemorrhage. The patient is eligible for thrombolytic therapy, and alteplase is administered within the first hour of symptom onset. The patient is admitted to the stroke unit for further management. Brain MRI with IVIM sequence is performed within 24 hours of symptom onset.

The patient is a 75-year-old Taiwanese woman who lives in a rural area with her husband. She has a history of falls and difficulty with mobility. She scored 4 on the Canadian Study of Health and Aging Clinical Frailty Scale (CSHA_CFS) Chinese Telephone Interview Version (replaced by In-Person Interview Version in 2009 study) and has a frailty index ≥1. She has been diagnosed with osteoporosis and depression. She has some difficulty with daily activities due to pain in her lower back and hips, and has trouble sleeping. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She is able to speak Mandarin and Taiwanese fluently. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has no hearing or visual impairments that interfere with communication or daily activities. She is unable to walk for 5 meters without assistance, but is able to move around her home with the help of her husband. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

A 56-year-old man was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He underwent biopsy and imaging studies, which revealed a tumor measuring 4 cm in diameter. The PET/CT scan showed no evidence of distant metastases, and the patient was deemed eligible for treatment. He has no significant past medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker with occasional alcohol use. He denies any history of prior radiation therapy or chemotherapy. His ECOG performance status is 1. Laboratory analysis is within normal limits. He has no contraindications to treatment, and his cardiac workup including EKG and echocardiogram is normal. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has provided informed consent. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study's requirements.

The patient is a 54-year-old man diagnosed with stage II soft tissue sarcoma in his left thigh. The patient has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. The patient is currently working as a computer programmer and has no physical limitations. The patient is willing to undergo pre-treatment core needle biopsies and is able to complete the self-assessment questionnaires. The patient has not undergone any prior radiotherapy to the site of present STS and is not receiving any concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or investigational agents. The patient has received adjuvant chemotherapy for STS in the past year. The patient is negative for HIV.

A 28-year-old male was involved in a severe motor vehicle accident and sustained a traumatic brain injury. He was intubated and admitted to the neurosurgical intensive care unit with a post-resuscitation Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 5. A CT scan revealed diffuse axonal injury and subarachnoid hemorrhage. He underwent a decompressive craniectomy and was started on prophylactic levetiracetam (1000 mg every 12 hours) to prevent seizures. He has no history of epilepsy or seizure disorder and was not taking any medication that could affect the pharmacokinetics of levetiracetam. He weighs 75 kg and his baseline serum creatinine is within normal limits. The primary neurosurgical provider anticipates his survival to be greater than 72 hours from injury. The patient is married and has two children.

58 yo M with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and peripheral artery disease (PAD) presents with increasing claudication symptoms in his left leg. He reports difficulty walking more than two blocks without rest and is very interested in any available treatment options to improve his quality of life. On physical examination, he has decreased pulses in the left foot and an ABI of 0.72. Peripheral angiography shows a de novo lesion in the left external iliac artery with a reference diameter of 8 mm and a stenosis of 80%. The lesion is eligible for percutaneous revascularization with a stent. The patient has no known allergies to clopidogrel and is willing to comply with the required medication regimen. He provides informed consent to participate in the clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of the peripheral, cobalt-chromium sirolimus eluting stent (PERS) compared to the cobalt-chromium balloon-expandable (Neptune C) stent in patients with symptomatic iliac arteries disease requiring revascularization.

A 65-year-old man was recently diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer. He has been experiencing bone pain and difficulty urinating. He underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of prostate cancer. The cancer has spread to his bones, lungs, and liver. His physician has recommended androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and docetaxel to treat the cancer. The patient is concerned about the side effects of the treatment and is interested in exploring other treatment options. His medical history includes hypertension, managed with medication. He does not have any allergies to medications. He has not undergone any prior cancer treatment. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore a combination of docetaxel with M7824 and M9241. He understands that the study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of the combination treatment to delay the progression of prostate cancer. He is willing to travel to the clinic for follow-up visits and agrees to use medically accepted barrier methods of contraception during the study treatment and for 3 months after the last dose of docetaxel or M7824 or M9241, even if oral contraceptives are also used.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing vision problems in her left eye for the past few months. She complains of a central scotoma, distorted vision, and difficulty reading. Examination reveals a macular hole in the left eye, and the diagnosis of idiopathic macular hole is confirmed. The patient has signed the informed consent form and has a course of IMH less than 3 years. She does not have hyperopia and has not experienced any traumatic injury to the eye. She does not have any other fundus disease or retinal detachment, nor has she undergone vitrectomy or surgery for any other eye condition. The patient's glaucoma is controlled by medication and she does not have any other eye condition that may affect her visual acuity. She is compliant with medical treatment and is in good general health, capable of undergoing surgery. There are no dioptric media opacities that would affect her ability to undergo examination and OCT measurements.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who has recently been discharged from the hospital after suffering a stroke. She has been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment, but is able to provide informed consent. She owns an Android smartphone which she uses frequently for communication, browsing the internet, and using various apps. She lives alone and is able to manage her daily activities with some assistance from her family. The patient has no history of psychiatric or behavioral conditions that would interfere with compliance. She is willing to participate in the study and is committed to using her smartphone as usual during the 3 month study period.

45-year-old female with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes for 6 years, currently on oral medications including metformin and a sulfonylurea, with an HbA1C of 9.5% and a BMI of 30 kg/m2. She has not had any severe hypoglycemic events in the past 6 months and has not had any significant weight changes. She has no history of insulin use or diabetic ketoacidosis. She is willing to perform self-monitoring blood glucose and comply with study visits and tasks as required per protocol. She has no history of autoimmune disease, gastrointestinal surgery, or conditions that would impede the passage of the device through the upper GI tract. She is not currently taking anticoagulation therapy or P2Y12 inhibitors and is able to discontinue NSAIDs during treatment. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using an acceptable method of contraception. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and comply with study requirements.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with low-grade lymphoma, confirmed by biopsy. She presented with fatigue, night sweats, and enlarged lymph nodes in her neck and groin. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and depression, which are well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has a supportive family and works as a teacher. After careful consideration of the options available, she has decided to participate in the clinical trial. She is willing to undergo either radiation therapy alone or radiation therapy followed by 6 cycles of chemotherapy. The patient is in good overall health and meets all the eligibility criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male who exercises regularly and maintains a healthy lifestyle. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. His family history is negative for cardiovascular disease or any other significant medical conditions. He is fluent in English and understands the consent process. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his BMI is 23. He has no history of peripheral artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, or any other chronic medical conditions. He does not have any implanted devices or neurological disorders. The patient is interested in participating in a study regarding the effects of red light energy on blood flow in healthy adults.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of mania. He has a previous diagnosis of bipolar I disorder with multiple manic episodes in the past. He reports feeling very energetic, impulsive, and irritable. He has not slept for 2 days and has been engaging in risky behavior, such as spending large amounts of money and making impulsive decisions. He has a history of substance abuse and is currently not using any illicit drugs. His medical history includes a broken arm from a car accident 10 years ago and a childhood diagnosis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) for which he was treated with Ritalin. He is not currently taking any medications except for occasional ibuprofen for pain. The patient's Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) score is 30 at Visit 1 and 28 at Visit 2. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus and has not received any psychotropic medication within 2 days prior to Visit 2.

The patient is a 58-year-old post-menopausal woman who has been diagnosed with stage 1 (pT1) breast cancer. She underwent a segmental mastectomy with negative margins and was found to be clinically N0 with no regional lymph node involvement (pN0). The patient has never undergone radiation therapy to the ipsilateral breast. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies or current medications. FSH testing confirmed post-menopausal status. The patient has refused to undergo standard six-week radiotherapy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing radiation fibrosis with five versus three fractions of partial breast irradiation (PBI). She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements, including completing treatment within one week and participating in follow-up visits every 6 months for the first year and then yearly for the next 10 years. The patient understands that PBI is considered a research domain and should only be offered in the context of a clinical experimental protocol. She meets all eligibility criteria for the study and is interested in potentially helping to advance breast cancer radiation therapy for future patients.

The patient is a 58 year old male with a history of type 2 diabetes and coronary heart disease. He has been experiencing microalbuminuria [urinary albumin excretion (UAE): 200 mg/day] for the past 6 months. He is currently taking metformin (1000mg twice a day), aspirin (81mg once a day), and atorvastatin (40mg once a day). His most recent HbA1c was 7.2%, and his blood pressure is well-controlled with a reading of 130/80 mmHg. He has not experienced any episodes of acute heart failure, and his eGFR is 55 ml/min/1.73m^2. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options for his microalbuminuria.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence (SUI) for the past year. She is currently attending the Lois Hole Hospital for Women Urogynecology Clinic and has been referred for physiotherapy to treat her SUI. She is able to toilet independently and is able to undertake hip rotation exercises. She speaks and reads English fluently. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of neurological or cognitive impairment and is not currently using any other treatment for incontinence. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to improve her SUI symptoms with the training interventions.

A 45-year-old male who underwent a left transfemoral amputation due to a traumatic injury 2 years ago is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating balance reactions. He has been walking with a prosthetic leg and has undergone physical therapy to improve his gait and balance. He reports occasional difficulty maintaining balance while standing and walking on uneven surfaces. He has no history of neurological, orthopedic, or cardiology diseases that impair his balance. He is currently working as a software engineer and enjoys playing tennis and hiking with his family. He is eager to participate in the clinical trial to help improve his balance and potentially help other amputees in the future.

25 yo F with no significant past medical history and fluent in German language. The patient reports no history of mental disorders, allergies to capsaicin or sesame oil, intake of psychopharmacological drugs, illegal drugs, or alcohol consumption in the last twelve hours. The patient is not a student in medicine, pharmacy, or psychology and has not completed studies in medicine, pharmacy, or psychology. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the long-term effects of expectations on mood through the use of a placebo nasal spray. The patient is willing to watch sad film sequences and have their mood assessed before and after receiving the nasal spray.

A 46-year-old woman came to the clinic with symptoms of chronic sinusitis for the past 3 years. She has a history of recurrent sinus infections and has failed previous medical management including antibiotics and nasal steroid sprays. CT scan of the sinuses revealed chronic sinusitis and nasal polyposis. She is scheduled for functional endoscopic sinus surgery with balloon dilation. She has no history of nasal trauma or previous sinus surgery. She is not currently taking any medications. She works as a teacher and complains of frequent headaches and nasal congestion which affect her ability to work. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history.

The patient is a 52-year-old male smoker who has been experiencing shortness of breath and cough with occasional blood-streaked sputum for the past 3 months. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol levels. He works as a construction worker and is married with two children. He has no known drug allergies. His physical examination shows decreased breath sounds in the left lung and the presence of a non-tender left supraclavicular lymph node. His chest X-ray shows a mass in the left lung. Further evaluation with a CT scan reveals a 4 cm mass in the left lung with no evidence of metastasis. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of small cell lung cancer. He is deemed eligible for radiotherapy and chemotherapy with platinum and etoposide. He has a performance status of 1 and is affiliated with a health insurance system. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial.

This is a 45-year-old female patient who was admitted to the hospital with a severe headache, nausea, vomiting, and loss of consciousness. A CT scan revealed a subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a ruptured aneurysm. She underwent surgical clipping of the aneurysm and was subsequently transferred to the ICU for further management. She is currently in stable condition, with no signs of neurological deficits, and will be monitored for any new complications that may arise. She has provided signed consent to participate in the study and to allow for analysis of the samples collected during her clinical routine. She is not taking any study drugs and is not participating in any other clinical trials.

This clinical trial is not a medical intervention and does not involve patients or subjects. Instead, it is an educational intervention for boys and girls aged 9-14 who are currently enrolled in school or intervention sites. Therefore, there is no patient description to generate.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman living in a rural area of Masaka, Uganda. She has a history of unprotected sexual intercourse with multiple partners and recently noticed some unusual discharge. She decided to get tested for HIV at a local clinic and was diagnosed as HIV positive through home-based HIV counselling and testing (HBHCT). She has never received any HIV care before and is willing to participate in the study. She lives with her parents and three siblings and works as a farmer. She is fluent in Luganda and understands English. She has no known medical conditions and takes no medications. She is willing to receive follow-up counselling at home and understands the importance of being linked to pre-ART care.

35 year old female patient with paraplegia due to a T10 spinal cord injury sustained in a motor vehicle accident. Currently in her first rehabilitation phase and able to actively engage in physical activity. She is a manual wheelchair user and has no history of cardiopulmonary disease or other progressive disease. She has a BMI of 23 and is able to use an arm-crank ergometer without any issues related to spasticity or any physical impairment. She is willing to participate in an 8-week endurance training program to improve her physical fitness and quality of life.

The patient is a 28-year-old non-smoking male with a body mass index of 22 kg/m3. He has no history of respiratory, cardiovascular or neurological problems. The patient has never been exposed to solvents in his work environment. He is not on any chronic medication and does not have a history of chronic or abusive alcohol consumption. The patient has not consumed alcohol within 24 hours before or 18 hours following exposure. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the impact of thermal stress on the pulmonary absorption and toxicokinetics of organic solvents.

The patient is a 10-year-old male with a diagnosis of Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia. The patient has a positive family history of high cholesterol levels and has been on a low-fat diet for the past six months, with no significant improvement in his cholesterol levels. The patient's LDL cholesterol level is greater than 4 mmol/l. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies to medications. The patient has not been taking any cholesterol-lowering medications in the past. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently on any contraceptives. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of atorvastatin in reducing cholesterol levels in children with Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia.

A 57 year old male was diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma that has spread to nearby tissue (locally advanced). He has undergone first-line chemotherapy and may have responding, stable or progressive disease. He has a Karnofsky performance scale (KPS) of 80% and a Southwestern Oncology Group (SWOG) performance status of 1. His absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 1,200/mm^3, lymphocyte count is 500/mm^3, and platelet count is 100,000/mm^3. His serum creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL, total bilirubin is 1.5 mg/dL, and SGPT and SGOT are both 3.5 times normal. He has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 50% at rest. He is willing to use an effective method of contraception and has a negative pregnancy test within 7 days of being registered for protocol therapy. He has not undergone any major surgery or experienced any significant traumatic injury within the past 28 days. He is not currently breastfeeding and is capable of being compliant with the treatment.

Patient A is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is currently at 37 weeks gestation. She has been diagnosed with breech presentation, a condition in which the fetus is positioned with its head up and buttocks or feet down. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She has expressed a desire to attempt external cephalic version (ECV) to manually rotate the fetus into a head-down position, in order to avoid a cesarean delivery. The obstetrician has offered the option of combined spinal-epidural analgesia (CSE) to provide pain relief during the procedure, and to potentially improve the success rate of the ECV. Patient A is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the impact of CSE on the success rate of ECV and to contribute to the existing evidence base on this topic. She is willing to be randomized to either the CSE or control group and understands the potential risks and benefits of participation.

This is a 45 year-old male who has been experiencing lower back pain for over a year. The pain is usually present throughout the day and is worsened by prolonged sitting or standing. The patient describes the pain as a dull ache that is sometimes accompanied by a sharp, shooting sensation down the back of the leg. The patient has tried various treatments including physical therapy, chiropractic care, and medication, but has not found significant relief. The patient has not had any recent injuries or surgeries and does not have any known spinal deformities or neurological issues. The patient has a BMI of 28 and is otherwise healthy. The patient reports a high level of disability on the Oswestry Disability Score and has identified specific activities that are difficult to perform due to the pain on the Patient Specific Functional Scale. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help identify the most effective treatment for their chronic lower back pain.

The patient is a 57-year-old man with a diagnosis of stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with multiple metastases to the liver and bones. He has undergone previous treatments including radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is willing to receive further treatment. The patient is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials and has not received cabazitaxel within the last 2 years. There is no history of severe hypersensitivity to taxanes or Polysorbate-80. The patient has adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal organ function. The patient is willing to use a highly effective contraceptive method of birth control and has a negative pregnancy test within the 7 days prior to registration. The patient has measurable disease as defined by the most current version of the Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST) 1.1. The patient is free of any concurrent serious illness or medical condition, including active infection or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

Patient is a 28-year-old man from the United States who is in good health and has no significant medical history. He has no allergies and is not currently taking any medications. His BMI is 22.5, BP: 120/75, HR: 70/min. He has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. He is interested in participating in clinical trials as a healthy volunteer.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian female who has been experiencing fecal incontinence for the past 6 months. She reports having uncontrolled loss of liquid or solid fecal material at least once a week and finds the condition very bothersome. She has tried using adult diapers and pads, but they have not been very effective. She has no history of colorectal or anal malignancy, inflammatory bowel disease, rectovaginal fistula, or cloacal defect. She has never had rectal prolapse or undergone any colon or rectum removal or diversion. She is fluent in English and able to conduct telephone interviews. She has not taken any loperamide or diphenoxylate plus atropine in the last 30 days and has not received supervised anal sphincter exercise/pelvic floor muscle training with biofeedback in the past. She is not currently pregnant or nursing and is not planning to become pregnant before the end of the study follow-up period. She has not had any childbirth within the last 3 months and is not currently taking anti-retroviral drugs. She has no known neurological disorders that affect continence, such as spinal cord injury, advanced multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, or debilitating stroke. She does not have any chronic abdominal pain in the absence of diarrhea.

Patient is a 24-year-old Hispanic woman from Texas who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes a year ago. She is currently struggling to manage her blood glucose levels and her most recent A1c was 8.5%. She speaks English and Spanish fluently and has access to a local healthcare provider. She owns a laptop and is willing to participate in the 6-month REAL-T intervention. She has no cognitive impairment or severe disability limiting her life expectancy. She is not currently pregnant nor planning to become pregnant within the next 12 months.

The patient is a 55 year-old man who was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer with the Kras mutation. He has already undergone surgery, radiation therapy and multiple rounds of chemotherapy, but his cancer has progressed and he is now refractory to cisplatin. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is married with two children and is retired. He enjoys spending time with his family and traveling. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. He understands the nature of the clinical trial and is willing to comply with all protocol requirements.

A 8-year-old boy was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) three months ago. He has been undergoing chemotherapy treatment and has been responding well to the treatment. However, for the past two days, he has been experiencing high-grade fever (39°C), chills, and fatigue. He also complains of a sore throat and difficulty swallowing. The parents brought him to the hospital, and the doctors suspect a bacterial or viral infection. The patient is currently undergoing evaluation for the cause of the fever, and the doctors have suggested participating in a clinical trial investigating if RNA expression signature can discriminate bacterial from viral infection or non-infectious inflammation in children with cancer. The parents have been informed about the study, and they have decided to enroll their child in the trial.

30 yo healthy non-smoker with no significant past medical history, not currently taking any medications or drugs. BMI is within the range of 18-30. The patient has no history of substance abuse or hypersensitivity to ketamine.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma less than 3 cm in diameter. He has undergone transarterial chemoembolisation (TACE) and is currently in remission. He is not a candidate for surgery. The patient has no history of serious heart, lung, or kidney problems but has mild hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of mental or cognitive disorders. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 52-year-old woman comes to the clinic to participate in a clinical trial for type 2 diabetes. She has been diagnosed with diabetes for 4 years and has been taking glimepiride and following a strict diet and exercise regimen for at least 12 weeks. Her glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level at screening is 8.5%. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m2. She has not participated in any TAK-875 study before, and she is not currently taking any investigational compound or investigational antidiabetic drug. She has no history of drug abuse or alcohol abuse in the last 2 years. She is willing to monitor her glucose levels with a sponsor-provided home glucose monitor and consistently record her own blood glucose concentrations and participant diaries. She is a non-sm

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is currently enrolled as a student at Logan University. She has been experiencing lower back pain for the past six months and has not sought any treatment for it. She does not have any prior history of lower extremity, first rib or spine injury, surgery, or any local infection or malignancy affecting the nervous system. She does not take any prescription or herbal muscle stimulants, relaxants or other medications that could affect the nervous system. She is not pregnant and does not have any significant lower lumbar involvement. She does not have diabetes, shortness of breath on light physical activity or cardiovascular disease. She does not experience numbness or tingling in the lower extremities. The patient shows the DeJarnette Category II indicators and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the relationship of pelvic blocking and protocol for cranial adjusting with specific pain areas.

A 25-year-old male smoker presents with a history of smoking at least 10 cigarettes per day for the past 5 years. He has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. He reports experiencing cravings and withdrawal symptoms when attempting to quit. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He has no history of substance abuse or mental health disorders. He is aware of the risks associated with smoking but finds it difficult to quit due to the addictive nature of nicotine. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of altered composition cigarettes on reducing the abuse liability of standard cigarettes. He is willing to comply with study procedures and follow the guidelines for smoking during the study period. He is not currently planning to quit smoking in the next 30 days and does not use any other tobacco products.

Pt is a 55yo male with a history of hypertension for 5 years, currently uncontrolled despite taking lisinopril 20mg daily for the last year. Pt has no history of diabetes or cardiovascular disease, and his current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. BP measurements taken on three different occasions show stage 2 diastolic hypertension with DBP >= 100mmHg. Pt has no other concurrent diseases or conditions that may interfere with the study. The patient has not participated in any investigational drug study in the last 30 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, and has no history of hypersensitivity to nebivolol or other β-blockers or any contraindication to β-blocker use. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and is available for follow-up visits.

A 45-year old woman recently suffered a stroke 6 weeks ago which was confirmed by a CT scan. She presents with moderate to severe motor impairment of her right upper limb. She is right-handed and the loss of function in her dominant arm has been a significant challenge for her. She is married and has two children who are in their early teens. Prior to her stroke, she worked as a teacher and enjoyed spending time with her family and friends. She currently experiences difficulty with basic daily activities such as dressing and grooming herself, and has to rely on her husband and children for assistance. She also experiences muscle stiffness in her arm and has difficulty controlling her movements. She has been compliant with her medications and has not experienced any seizures or other medical issues. Her husband is very supportive throughout her rehabilitation process and encourages her to attend her rehabilitation sessions. She is motivated to recover as much function as possible in her arm and is excited to participate in this clinical trial that may help her regain her independence.

Patient is a 35-year-old female with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 who has been struggling with obesity for several years. She has tried various diets and exercise programs without success. She has normal to mildly hypertensive blood pressure and is not currently taking any medication. She does not have any physiological or psychological illnesses that could influence the study results. She is a non-smoker and does not have any substance abuse or dependence. She has not donated blood within the past 3 months and does not drink more than 21 alcoholic units per week. She does not have any food allergies or special diets, and does not dislike any of the foods served during the study. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is committed to following the study protocol.

A 54-year-old female patient presented to the cardiology clinic with a history of atrial fibrillation. She had undergone direct current cardioversion twice in the past year and was currently in sinus rhythm. She reported occasional palpitations and shortness of breath. She had a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She was currently taking lisinopril, metoprolol, atorvastatin, and metformin. She denied any history of coronary artery disease, stroke or valvular heart disease. Her vital signs were stable at the time of the clinic visit. Physical exam revealed a regular rhythm, no murmurs or gallops, and no peripheral edema. A 12-lead EKG showed sinus rhythm with a heart rate of 75 beats per minute. A limited 2D echocardiogram was performed, which showed left atrial size of 39 mm, left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%, and no significant valvular disease. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial and underwent radial artery applanation tonometry and pulse wave analysis to calculate central aortic pressure and other parameters using commercially available SphygmoCor® system. She was followed up by her cardiologist for recurrence of atrial fibrillation within 6 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese man who presented with a three-month history of nasal obstruction and occasional epistaxis. He has no previous history of cancer but reports a strong family history of NPC in his mother and uncle. CT scan of the head and neck revealed a mass in the nasopharynx. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of NPC. He underwent concurrent chemoradiotherapy and had completed his treatment eight weeks ago. He has no significant medical history and takes no regular medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks occasionally. His physical examination is unremarkable. The vital signs are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and signs the written consent form.

A 16-year-old male with a genetic predisposition for familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is being evaluated for a clinical trial. He has a family history of colon cancer and has undergone genetic testing, which confirms his genotype-positive FAP. He has no history of colon cancer or other serious medical conditions. His colonoscopy shows no evidence of severe dysplasia or greater and no more than 10 adenomas ≥ 1 cm or 100 adenomas of any size. His blood work is within normal limits, and he has no history of hypersensitivity to COX-2 inhibitors, sulfonamides, NSAIDs, or salicylates. He has not received any investigational agents in the past 3 months and has not undergone chemotherapy in the past 6 months. He is not currently taking any NSAIDs, nasal steroids, or fluconazole. He is willing to use effective contraception if necessary and understands the study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing severe hip pain and limited mobility due to non-inflammatory degenerative joint disease. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has tried non-surgical treatments with little relief. He has received medical clearance for surgery and is willing to comply with the follow-up schedule. He has no active infection or sepsis and does not have any emotional or neurological conditions that would prevent his participation in the study. He does not have acute hip trauma such as a femoral neck fracture.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B six months ago. He has been taking nucleoside analogue antivirals for the past 24 weeks and has responded well to the treatment. His HBsAg titer is between 10-1,000 IU/mL and his HBV DNA is negative. He has no history of

The patient is a 5-year-old boy who has experienced two or more episodes of croup in the past 12 months. Croup is characterized by an acute onset of inspiratory stridor, barking cough, and respiratory distress. The patient has been evaluated and does not have any exclusion criteria such as subglottic stenosis, hemangioma, or other conditions that may cause stridor. The patient is otherwise healthy and not currently receiving any steroid therapy for other medical conditions. The parents have consented for the child to participate in the study to compare the effectiveness of daily inhaled steroids versus observation with oral steroids on an as needed basis for preventing future episodes of croup.

The patient is a 38-year-old Asian male who recently traveled to a dengue-endemic area and developed fever, headache, muscle and joint pain, and a rash. He visited the doctor and was diagnosed with dengue fever based on positive dengue NS1 antigen test. He has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication, and no other significant medical history. He is currently not taking any medication other than his blood pressure medication. He works as a sales representative and has been on sick leave since the onset of symptoms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help find a treatment for dengue fever. He has read the eligibility criteria and believes he meets the inclusion criteria. He is willing to undergo MRI and chest X-ray, and keep a diary of pain medication usage and side effects. He does not have any allergies or contraindications to the study drug, ketotifen. He is fully aware of the potential benefits and risks associated with participating in a clinical trial and has given written informed consent.

A 35-year-old male with good general health and a minimum of 20 permanent natural teeth, excluding third molars, presented for the clinical trial. He had an initial gingivitis index of 1.5 and an initial plaque index of 2.0 as determined by the Loe and Silness Gingival Index and Quigley and Hein Plaque Index (Turesky Modification), respectively. He had not received any dental prophylaxis during the past two weeks prior to baseline examinations and had no history of allergies to oral care or personal care consumer products or their ingredients. The patient reported no current prescription medication use that might interfere with the study outcome nor any existing medical condition which prohibits eating or drinking for periods up to 4 hours. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or drugs. He agreed to participate in the six-week clinical research study and signed the informed consent form.

A 28-week gestation male infant with a birth weight of 1400g was born through a vaginal delivery to a 26-year-old Caucasian mother. The mother had an uncomplicated pregnancy, but due to preterm labor, she delivered early. The infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and required mechanical ventilation for the first week of life. Currently, the infant is receiving parenteral nutrition due to poor enteral feeding tolerance. The infant has been on parenteral nutrition for the past 12 days, receiving a compounded binary TPN solution with lipids administered separately in Y-line. The infant is stable and requires no additional oxygen support. The infant's medical history is unremarkable. The infant's parents have given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

30 year-old woman with a history of regular pap smears and no prior history of abnormal cervical findings. She presents for her routine gynecological exam and pap smear. She is sexually active with one partner and uses condoms for contraception. She has no history of HPV vaccination. She has no history of cervical cancer or precancerous lesions. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications.

A 45 year old male office worker visited the clinic complaining of constipation. He is on medication for hypertension and has a history of hyperlipidemia. He reports that his bowel movements have become infrequent and difficult since starting his new medication. He has tried various over-the-counter laxatives with no relief. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no known allergies to the medications being tested. He is of average weight and height, and has no prior history of gastrointestinal issues. He has not undergone any colon diagnostic examinations in the past 5 years. The patient is willing to comply with the study plan and has provided written informed consent.

A 42 yo F with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who received induction chemotherapy and achieved complete remission. The patient is planned for an allogeneic stem cell transplant from a matched unrelated donor. The patient is seropositive for CMV and has not had any known active CMV reactivation or antiviral therapy for the past month. The patient has not received a CMV vaccine and does not have hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). The patient has provided written informed consent and is considered suitable for the study by the investigator.

A 62-year-old woman who suffered a left middle cerebral artery stroke 6 months ago and was recently discharged from the hospital. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She completed high school education and worked as a teacher before the stroke. She now experiences difficulty with reading comprehension, especially when it comes to complex sentences and long paragraphs. She often needs to reread the same sentence several times to understand it fully. She has no visual field defects and has reliable answers to yes-no questions. She speaks English fluently and has no history of learning disabilities or psychiatric diagnoses. She is interested in participating in the study and has given informed consent.

A 14-month-old Kenyan toddler was brought to the clinic for enrollment in the Nasopharyngeal Carriage Study. The toddler had received a primary dose of pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) per local practice prior to enrollment. The parents provided written informed consent and were fully capable of comprehending and complying with study requirements and procedures. The child had no significant medical history and was not born premature, had a birth weight of >2.5 kg, and had a weight-to-height Z-score of ≥ -2 at the time of enrollment. The child had not received any investigational or non-registered drug within 90 days prior to screening, nor had any immunodeficiency or chronic medical condition. The child was not born to a mother with a history of alcohol abuse during pregnancy and had no evidence of congenital abnormality or developmental delay. The child was enrolled in the study's PCV-primed only cohort and was allocated to Cohort 1 (300 µg PATH-wSP). The child completed a total of 5 scheduled visits, with nasopharyngeal swabs taken at each visit. No treatments were administered during the study, and the child remained safe and well-tolerated over the course of the study.

26-year-old female with regular menstrual cycles and no history of organic heart disease presenting with symptoms of palpitations and occasional chest discomfort. The patient reports experiencing these symptoms intermittently over the past year, with no identifiable triggers. She has not previously sought medical attention for these symptoms. The patient is otherwise healthy with a BMI within the normal range. She is not currently using hormonal therapy or any other medications. The patient is interested in participating in a study to investigate the possible relationship between sex hormone levels and idiopathic right ventricular outflow tract arrhythmia.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman diagnosed with CLL based on the presence of lymphocytosis and typical CLL morphology on peripheral blood smear. She has no prior therapy for CLL. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is on amlodipine, lisinopril and atorvastatin, and reports no adverse reactions to these medications. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for the presence of palpable cervical and axillary lymph nodes. Her laboratory workup reveals hemoglobin of 13.5 g/dL, platelets of 180,000/µl, absolute neutrophil count of 2,500/µl, creatinine clearance of > 60 ml/min, total bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, AST of 30 U/L, and ALT of 25 U/L. Serological testing for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV is negative. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has given written informed consent and is willing and able to comply with the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a confirmed clinical diagnosis of Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) due to a defect in the LDL receptor. She has been on maximal lipid-lowering therapy for the past 10 years, including statins, ezetimibe, and PCSK9 inhibitors, but her LDL cholesterol levels remain above 400 mg/dL. She has a family history of premature coronary artery disease, with her father and two siblings being diagnosed with coronary artery disease before the age of 50. She has no history of smoking, diabetes, or hypertension, and her BMI is within the normal range. She has undergone multiple coronary artery calcium scans, which have shown significant calcified plaque burden. She has undergone a coronary angiogram, which showed multiple stenotic lesions in the proximal and mid portions of the left anterior descending artery and the circumflex artery. She has no history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), coronary artery bypass graft (CABG), or stroke within the past 3 months. She is currently not on any oral anticoagulants and has not undergone LDL or plasma apheresis within the past week. She is willing and able to comply with the plasmapheresis visits and other study requirements.

The patient is a 55 year old male who has been diagnosed with Hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1 infection. He was diagnosed with cirrhosis through a liver biopsy and has early clinical decompensation with a model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) score of 8. He has no history of hepatocellular carcinoma and has an expected survival without liver transplantation of greater than 1 year. He has been approved by a third-party payer for the FDA-approved combination of sofosbuvir (SOF) plus ribavirin. He has not had any previous treatments for HCV. He has no other chronic liver diseases and has no serious underlying medical conditions. He has no known hypersensitivity or serious adverse reactions to any of the study drugs. He is not pregnant and has no history of significant drug interactions related to the study medications. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). He has not received any prior chemotherapy for this condition. He is in generally good health with normal liver function, cardiac function, and renal function. He has a Karnofsky Performance score of 80. He has target lesions and non-target lesions. He has not previously received oxaliplatin, and therefore does not have any residual neurotoxicity greater than grade 2. He does not have any brain metastasis or peripheral or central nervous system abnormalities. He does not have diabetes or neuropathy. His blood glucose before meals is less than 8mmol/L and HBA1C is less than 7.0%. He is expected to live for at least 3 months. He meets all the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and none of the exclusion criteria.

A 9-year-old girl was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) after presenting with persistent fatigue, abdominal pain, and easy bruising. Her bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and she is currently awaiting initiation of therapy. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of chronic illness or major surgeries. Her parents have provided informed consent for her to participate in the study of intermediate metabolism in children with ALL. She will be undergoing blood sampling prior to the initiation of therapy.
