A healthy 9-year-old girl from the outpatient clinic of the 2nd Pediatric Department of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki will serve as a matched control for this study.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who is in good health and speaks and understands Danish fluently. He does not have a history of alcohol or medicine abuse, and has not participated in any QST-trial or medical trial within the last 2 months. The patient does not have any serious comorbidities and is not undergoing treatment for any chronic pain. Additionally, the patient has not worked night shifts or undergone any treatment for sleep disorders.

A 56-year-old male with a history of hypertension presents to the emergency room after collapsing at home. He was found by his wife and she reports that he was unresponsive with no pulse. Emergency medical services arrived on the scene and initiated cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) with automated external chest compression and an impedance threshold device. The initial rhythm was ventricular fibrillation and two shocks were delivered. The patient was intubated and transported to the hospital. Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient remains unresponsive and in cardiac arrest. The emergency physician confirms that the patient meets the inclusion criteria for the SNPeCPR clinical trial and the patient is enrolled in the study. The patient receives an injection of either sodium nitroprusside or placebo as part of the study protocol. The patient is monitored closely for response to treatment and for any adverse effects. The study team collects data on the patient's cardiac function, blood pressure, and SpO2 during the resuscitation process. The patient is expected to participate in the study for six months, during which time he will receive follow-up care and monitoring.

A 62-year-old retired teacher was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) three years ago. She had no symptoms at the time of diagnosis and the cancer was discovered during a routine check-up. She underwent surgical resection of the tumor and received adjuvant chemotherapy. She has been followed closely with imaging studies every six months. However, during her last check-up, a recurrence of the tumor was detected. The tumor is localized and she has no evidence of extrahepatic metastasis. Her liver function tests are within normal limits and she has no other significant medical problems. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the efficacy and safety of pre-administrative Sorafenib and Latter radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in Recurrent HCC. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing increasing knee pain and stiffness for the past year. She was diagnosed with tibiofemoral osteoarthritis and has been recommended to undergo a corrective osteotomy. She has no history of epilepsy, thrombophilia, or severe renal insufficiency. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. Her BMI is within the normal range. She does not abuse alcohol, drugs, or medication. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

This is a 34 year old male who tested positive for COVID-19 and has been experiencing a loss of sense of smell for the past week. He has no history of chronic nasal or sinus infections, and has not undergone any endoscopic sinus surgery. He has not experienced loss of taste or any other symptoms associated with COVID-19 infection. He has no known allergies to fish or omega-3 supplements, and has no history of psychiatric or developmental disorders. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman experiencing joint pain in her knees, hips, and shoulders for the past 6 months. She has difficulty in flexion and extension movements, and experiences stiffness in her joints, especially in the morning. She rates her pain as 6 out of 10 on a visual analogue scale. She has no history of any systemic or dermatologic disorder that could interfere with the study results. She is willing to avoid prolonged exposure to UV radiation during the study period and not use any other topical treatments in the treatment areas. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to practice a reliable form of birth control during the trial. She is able to give written informed consent and comply with the study requirements. She has not participated in any other interventional clinical trials in the past 30 days. She does not suffer from Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Psoriatic Arthritis, Gouty Arthritis, or any other complications of OA. She is not suffering from any severe stomach infection or peritonsillar abscess. She has not been using any long-acting or slow-release analgesics or anti-inflammatory drugs for the past 24 hours before the trial. She does not have any known sensitivity to the constituents of the test product and has not used or plans to use immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory medication.

A 45-year-old Chinese male, who works in the construction industry, presents to the hospital for a routine checkup. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. He reports occasional indigestion and bloating after meals, but no other gastrointestinal symptoms. He denies any family history of gastric cancer or other malignancies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no respiratory issues or other medical conditions that would disqualify him from participating in the study. He is interested in participating in the study and has given his informed consent.

A 55-year-old man came to the clinic with a history of chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity for the past 6 months. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) 2 years ago. He has been taking aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, and metoprolol for the past 2 years. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all of which are well controlled with medication. He is a smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle. In the physical examination, the patient's blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg, heart rate was 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate was 16 breaths per minute. His body mass index (BMI) was 32. He had a regular heart rhythm and no murmurs were heard. His lungs were clear on auscultation. His extremities had no edema or cyanosis. His electrocardiogram (ECG) showed ST-T changes consistent with ischemia. The patient met the inclusion criteria for chronic stable angina pectoris and was diagnosed with Qi stagnation and blood stasis syndrome according to TCM. The patient signed the informed consent form and was enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl diagnosed with a brain tumor located in the posterior fossa. She has undergone surgical resection and radiation therapy, but her tumor has since recurred. She experiences headaches, nausea, and difficulty with balance and coordination. She has no history of allergies, and her family history is negative for cancer. She is currently not taking any medications. Her Karnofsky performance score is 60. The results of her blood tests, including liver and kidney function, are within normal limits. She has no disseminated disease, and her life expectancy is predicted to be greater than eight weeks. She has not received any chemotherapy in the past three weeks or radiation therapy in the past four weeks. She has no known allergies to eggs, soybean oil, or safflower oil. The patient and her parents or legally authorized representatives have signed a written informed consent.

An 70-year-old Caucasian man with a history of hypertension and mild cognitive impairment presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath on exertion. He reports that these symptoms have been gradually worsening over the past few months. He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. He is not a smoker and denies any alcohol or drug use. He reports that he has been eating a healthy diet and regularly exercising for at least 30 minutes a day but has not noticed any improvement in his symptoms. His physical examination is unremarkable except for mild pallor. Laboratory tests reveal a hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL and no obvious cause of the anemia. He is diagnosed with unexplained anemia and is found eligible for the clinical trial. The patient understands the study requirements and gives informed consent to participate.

A 65-year-old man had a left hemisphere stroke 9 months ago. He has difficulty walking and has a history of falls. He is independent with activities of daily living and has no cognitive impairments. He is on medication for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is a retired engineer and lives with his wife. He is motivated to improve his gait and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 22-year-old female who has been experiencing significant weight loss, with a BMI of 16.5. She is constantly preoccupied with her weight and body shape, and has been avoiding eating and social situations that involve food. The patient has also been experiencing depression and anxiety, and has difficulty sleeping. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will examine the effectiveness of Group Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (G-CBT) for anorexia nervosa. The patient has received primary education and is right-handed. She has no history of mental illness, severe physical or cognitive impairment. The patient is seeking treatment to improve her quality of life and overcome her eating disorder.

As this is a retrospective analysis study, there is no need for a patient description. The study will analyze existing data from patients who have already undergone the Satellite™ Nucleus Replacement surgery. Therefore, the eligibility criteria only require patients to have signed a Patient Data Release Form and to be at least 18 years old and skeletally mature at the time of surgery. Patients who have not reached the age of legal consent according to local laws are excluded from the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who is a former smoker with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) confirmed on spirometry. He experiences shortness of breath with minimal exertion and has difficulty performing daily activities. He has not attended pulmonary rehabilitation in the last two years and has not had an exacerbation of COPD within the last four weeks. He has no comorbidities that would prevent him from participating in an exercise training program. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a home-based pulmonary rehabilitation program that could potentially improve his symptoms and reduce healthcare costs.

A 45-year-old female with a 7-year history of Rheumatoid Arthritis presents with moderately to severely active RA that is not adequately controlled by non-biologic DMARDs. She has no experience with self-administration of medication using an autoinjector or pen. She has no contraindications to anti-TNF agents, nor any history of tuberculosis or primary or secondary immunodeficiency. She is currently biologics-naive and is willing to self-inject BI 695501. She has an American College of Rheumatology functional Class II and is able to walk and perform daily activities with some difficulty. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to assess the handling experience of the BI 695501 autoinjector and would like the opportunity to continue using the medication during the extension phase.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who woke up with a sudden onset of weakness on the right side of his body. He was unable to speak clearly and had difficulty understanding others. He also experienced a severe headache. His wife called for an ambulance, and he was transported to the stroke unit at Copenhagen University Hospital, Roskilde. He lives in the Eastern part of Denmark, within the geographical area covered by both the Helicopter Emergency Medical Service (HEMS) and the Ground Emergency Medical Service (GEMS). The patient has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol levels. He takes daily medication for both conditions. He has never experienced a stroke before. He arrived at the hospital within 4 hours of symptom onset. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the impact of HEMS on prognosis in stroke patients.

A 30-year-old pregnant woman, fluent in English, is currently at approximately 22 weeks gestational age. She has experienced one past episode of Major Depressive Disorder, but has been in symptom remission for the past 3 months. She is interested in participating in the Perinatal Emotion and Relationships Longitudinal Study to better understand how the birth and early postpartum period may impact her emotional processes and social behaviors, and to potentially contribute to research in the field. She has no history of severe head trauma, stroke, neurological disease, or other medical illnesses that would exclude her from the study. She is able to follow study procedures and is not currently experiencing any psychotic episodes or suicidal/homicidal thoughts.

A 57-year-old overweight woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus was referred to a clinical trial to assess the effects of potato consumption on measures of cardiometabolic health. She works as a receptionist and has a BMI of 31 kg/m2. She was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 5 years ago and is currently taking metformin to regulate her blood glucose levels. She is a non-frequent white potato consumer and consumes them less than twice a week. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, and her blood pressure is well-controlled. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no other active chronic diseases and is not currently participating in a weight loss program. She exercises for 30 minutes a day, 4 times a week. She is willing to follow a dietary regimen involving the consumption of 100 g of white potato or 75 g of calorie-matched cooked long-grain white rice daily for 12 weeks, with a 2-week washout period between interventions. She will be required to attend the study site for bi-weekly visits to pick up the assigned dietary regimen, and will also be asked to complete three-day food records and daily diaries. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has struggled with weight loss for several years. She has tried different diets and exercise programs but has only been successful in losing a small amount of weight. She is currently 5'5" and weighs 210 pounds, giving her a BMI of 35. She reports difficulty with executive functioning, particularly with planning and organization. She forgets to pack healthy meals, has trouble sticking to a consistent exercise routine, and often finds herself snacking impulsively. She has never undergone bariatric surgery and is not currently enrolled in any weight control program. She has no history of psychiatric conditions or substance abuse. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and does not plan to become pregnant during the study. She is currently taking medication for depression but has not had any changes in her medication in the past 3 months. She is interested in participating in a research study that could help address her neurocognitive deficits and improve her weight loss outcomes.

A 45-year-old woman complains of frequent and urgent urination, with occasional incontinence. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months, which have been affecting her quality of life. She has tried behavioral modifications and anticholinergic medications with minimal improvement. She does not have a history of neurogenic disorders such as cerebrovascular accident or spinal cord injury. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a minimally invasive procedure for the treatment of overactive bladder and non-obstructive urinary retention.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who presents to the clinic with a fever of 39C and complains of cough, sore throat, and general malaise for the last 24 hours. She has a history of seasonal flu and has been suffering from these symptoms annually for the past few years. Her body weight is 60 kg, and she is not pregnant or lactating. She has no history of depression or psychiatric disorders, chronic pulmonary, cardiac, renal, or metabolic disorders. She is currently not on any immunosuppressive therapy and does not have HIV infection. Her nasal swab rapid test confirms the presence of influenza A.

A 60-year-old Caucasian male presents with sudden onset of weakness on his right side, difficulty speaking and understanding speech. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and is a smoker. His vital signs are within normal limits. On examination, he has right-sided facial droop, right-sided arm and leg weakness, and dysarthria. He is unable to raise his right arm or leg. The FAST test is performed on him, and he scores 1 for speech, 1 for facial palsy, and 1 for arm motor function. The time of onset of symptoms is estimated to be 30 minutes ago. The emergency technician then performs the FAST PLUS test and scores 1 for severe arm motor deficit and 1 for unilateral occurrence of this deficit. The patient is diagnosed with acute ischemic stroke and is transported to the hospital for CT and CT angiography evaluation within 12 hours of the onset of symptoms. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and will undergo FAST PLUS test evaluation as part of the study.

A 65-year-old man presents with memory loss and difficulty with daily tasks such as paying bills and keeping track of appointments. He has noticed these symptoms progressing slowly over the past year. He is currently taking donepezil for his symptoms, but has not noticed much improvement. He is married and has two adult children who are willing to participate as his caregivers throughout the study. The patient is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. At screening, his MMSE score was 24. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled on medication. He has no history of cerebrovascular disease or psychiatric disorders. His MRI shows no evidence of brain aneurysm clip, implanted neural stimulators, or other implanted medical devices that would exclude him from the study. He is confirmed to have MCI likely due to AD based on IWG-2 criteria and a positive amyloid PET scan within the past six months. His CDR Scale Global Score is between 0.5 and 1. He is not currently taking any anticoagulant therapy or other medication that would exclude him from the study. He is willing to comply with the study visit schedule and other study procedures.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently homeless and living in the Lotus House shelter with her 4-year-old daughter. She has struggled with substance abuse in the past but has been sober for six months. She speaks English fluently and has a high school education. She has no history of mental illness but reports feeling stressed and overwhelmed due to her current situation. Her daughter has no known developmental delays but has been exhibiting behavior problems, including tantrums and aggression towards other children. The family is interested in participating in a parenting program to address these issues and improve their overall well-being. They have not participated in any parenting programs previously.

An 11-year-old boy was referred to a pediatric neurologist due to episodes of staring and hand waving that were triggered by exposure to bright lights. After a comprehensive neurological examination and medical history review, he was diagnosed with Sunflower Syndrome. Despite being on anticonvulsant medications for the past year, he continues to experience an average of 6 seizures per week. His parents report that his seizures have significantly impacted his quality of life, as he has been bullied at school due to his unusual motor movements. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy of ZX008 (fenfluramine hydrochloride) in reducing seizure frequency and improving their son's quality of life. The boy is currently in good health, except for his seizures, and has no known allergies to any medications.

54 year-old man with a history of chronic cough and recurrent hemoptysis for the past 5 months. He also reports a weight loss of 6 kgs and malaise. He denies any fever or dyspnea. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. A CT scan of the thorax was ordered which showed a right upper lobe cavitary lesion with surrounding fibrosis and consolidation. A sputum culture grew Aspergillus fumigatus, and the patient's Aspergillus-specific IgG level was found to be elevated at 45 mgA/L. He was diagnosed with chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA). The patient was started on itraconazole 200 mg twice daily for a total of 6 months as per standard practice. However, he experienced disease relapse and required prolonged therapy. In this randomized controlled trial, he is being considered for enrollment to compare the clinical outcomes of six months versus twelve months of itraconazole therapy in treatment naïve subjects with chronic pulmonary aspergillosis.

This clinical trial does not involve direct patient participation. It is a pragmatic, prospective, multicentre, controlled, before-after study to evaluate the impact of selective reporting of antibiotic susceptibility test results for E.coli positive urine cultures in adult outpatients on the prescription of broad-spectrum antibiotics frequently used for urinary tract infections. The study will be conducted in 41 laboratories in the Lorraine region of France, and will collect data from the French health insurance database SNDS. The target study population is adults with an E. coli positive urine culture on which an AST is realised, who are prescribed an antibiotic by primary care physicians located in the geographic areas served by all the 41 laboratories studied.

67-year-old male, retired, presented to his primary care physician with complaints of persistent back pain, fatigue, and weight loss. Physical examination revealed tenderness to palpation in the lower thoracic and lumbar spine without any neurological deficits. A complete blood count showed mild normocytic anemia, and serum protein electrophoresis showed the presence of a monoclonal protein. A bone marrow biopsy was performed, and the results were consistent with multiple myeloma. The patient received initial treatment with bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone, but the disease progressed after 6 months of therapy. The patient is now being considered for second-line therapy and is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient has no history of peripheral neuropathy or cardiac disease. The patient is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control for a defined period of time if female or agrees to use an acceptable barrier method for contraception for a defined period of time if male. The patient is willing to comply with the visits and lab tests required by the trial.

A 7-year-old boy was referred to the clinic by his primary care physician due to persistent asthma symptoms. He experiences frequent coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, particularly during physical activity. He has no known allergies and does not smoke. He is currently not taking any medication for his asthma. He is a native English speaker and is accompanied by his mother who speaks fluent English. They are interested in participating in the study to help improve the management of his asthma symptoms.

A 52-year-old male diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with metastasis to the lungs, liver, and bones. The patient has been treated with sorafenib, a vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), but experienced disease progression after 6 months of treatment. The patient is not eligible for surgery or radiation therapy due to the location and extent of the metastasis. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. The patient has no history of CNS disease and has not been previously treated with avastin or mTOR inhibitors. The patient has no significant cardiovascular disease but is receiving therapeutic anticoagulants for deep vein thrombosis. The patient has not had any major surgical procedures or traumatic injuries within the last 28 days and has no history of abdominal fistula, gastrointestinal perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess within the last 6 months. The patient is willing to provide paraffin-embedded tumor blocks or at least 10 unstained, paraffin-embedded slides for correlative studies. The patient is HIV-negative and has a life expectancy of greater than 3 months.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who recently underwent orthopedic surgery for a broken ankle. She has no significant medical history, takes no regular medications, and has no known allergies to acetaminophen, ibuprofen, or any other medications. She is a non-smoker, has a BMI of 22, and is in good health. The patient is willing to receive multiple doses of parenterally administered nonopioid analgesics over a prolonged period of time and is expected to stay at the study site for at least 48 hours. She is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study and understands the procedures and study requirements. If female and of childbearing potential, she is practicing a medically acceptable method of birth control. The patient has not participated in another clinical study of Maxigesic® IV or received any investigational drug or device or investigational therapy within 30 days before screening.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C. He has a history of intravenous drug use and has been in recovery for the past year. He currently takes no medications and denies any significant medical history. He has no known cirrhosis and has not received any prior treatment for hepatitis C. His laboratory results show HCV genotype 3 with a viral load of 1,200,000 IU/ml. His liver function tests are within normal limits. He has a negative HIV and hepatitis B surface antigen test. He has a normal chest X-ray and eye exam. He is willing to use two acceptable methods of birth control during the study and for 6 months after the last dose of study drug. He does not have any pre-existing psychiatric condition and does not have a history of substance abuse. He is not diabetic and does not have high blood pressure. He is not currently diagnosed with any other medical condition that could interfere with participation in the study.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who attends middle school in South Carolina. He comes from a low socioeconomic background and his parents have given their consent for him to participate in the study and be randomly assigned to one of the two after-school programs. The patient is in good physical health, with no medical conditions that would interfere with physical activity. He is not currently receiving treatment for a psychiatric disorder and is developmentally appropriate to participate in the intervention. The patient is excited to be a part of the study and is motivated to increase his physical activity levels.

Priya is a 30-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She went in for an ultrasound at 8 weeks of gestation which revealed a complete hydatidiform mole. Her previous medical history is unremarkable, and she has had no prior surgeries. She has no family history of cancer or any other medical conditions. She is currently taking prenatal vitamins and has not had any complications during her pregnancy. She has been advised to participate in a clinical trial comparing single evacuation versus double evacuation for treatment of hydatidiform mole for prevention of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. She has provided her consent for the study and meets all the inclusion criteria.

A 28-year-old male with a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis due to ragweed for the past two years. He experiences symptoms such as nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, itchy and watery eyes, and throat irritation during the summer and early fall months. He has tried over-the-counter antihistamines and nasal sprays, but they only provide partial relief. He has not used any forbidden concomitant medications and does not have any clinically significant condition that might interfere with the treatment evaluation. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of levocetirizine and montelukast in reducing his symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis during exposure to ragweed pollen.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been in menopause for two years, confirmed by laboratory diagnostic tests. She has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. She exercises regularly, but has not engaged in any formal resistance training program in the last year. The patient is willing to participate in the study and sign the consent form. She reports no orthopedic limitations and has not been diagnosed with any diseases such as type II diabetes mellitus, hypertension, or cardiovascular disease. The patient is able to provide necessary information for the development of the study.

28 year old male, healthy volunteer, with a body mass index of 22 kg/m2, and no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has no known allergies to any medications and has not donated blood or participated in another investigational drug study within the last 3 months. He is willing to abstain from any medications for at least 2 weeks before and throughout the duration of the study.

The patient is a 33-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past year without success. She has been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and is currently undergoing IUI treatment at the MUHC reproductive center. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient is fluent in both English and French and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. She will be randomized into either the pre-washing group or the control group for her IUI procedure. The patient is hopeful that this study will increase her chances of becoming pregnant and starting a family.

The patient is a 62-year-old male diagnosed with venous stasis leg ulcers. He has been experiencing pain, swelling, and redness in his legs for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and albuterol inhaler. He has never had a history of drug or alcohol abuse. He does not smoke but has a history of smoking in the past. He does not have any implanted metallic devices in his lower extremities. He has not had any surgery on his lower extremities in the past 6 weeks. He is currently not on any systemic agents or immunosuppressive therapy that may influence wound healing. He is capable of providing informed consent and has normal cognitive and communicative abilities. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trial or study and does not have any litigation or malpractice lawsuits pending.

A 56-year-old European woman with a medical history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus presented with symptoms of severe abdominal pain and vomiting. She was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis and was scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy surgery. She was currently taking Metformin and Insulin Glargine for her diabetes. She denied any history of cardiovascular disease, stroke or pulmonary embolism. She was a non-smoker and had no known allergies. Her vital signs were within normal limits and physical examination was unremarkable except for mild epigastric tenderness. Her HbA1c level was 8.9% and her fasting blood sugar was 150 mg/dL. She was admitted to the hospital and received preoperative counseling regarding her diabetes management during the perioperative period. She was instructed to discontinue Metformin two days prior to surgery and was advised to continue her Insulin Glargine while monitoring her blood sugar levels closely. She received appropriate perioperative care and was discharged from the hospital on postoperative day 2 without any complications.

A 7-year-old male child with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2 presents to the clinic with no symptoms. He is the only child of a healthy couple, with no known family history of obesity, hypertension, or heart disease. The child has no history of medication use, hypertension, diabetes, or any other systemic disease. He has been physically active for at least 1 hour/day for the past year. His parents are willing to participate in this clinical trial and have given written informed consent. The child has not yet entered puberty, and there is no indication of any infectious or inflammatory disease.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of moderate-to-severe COPD. He experiences shortness of breath even with minimal exertion, and often feels tired and fatigued. His FEV1 is 50% predicted, and he has an FEV1/FVC ratio of less than 70%. He has not had a respiratory infection or exacerbation in the past 4 weeks. He has no exercise-limiting heart disease, primary asthma, congestive heart failure, or peripheral arterial disease. He has not participated in a formal exercise program in the past 12 weeks. He is not pregnant and does not use methadone. He is able to walk on a treadmill. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his exercise capacity and reduce his symptoms.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is generally healthy with no significant medical history. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker. She is currently not pregnant and is using an effective method of birth control. The patient has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 90 days and has not donated blood or experienced significant blood loss within the past 90 days. The patient's laboratory assessments, including hematology, clinical chemistry, and urinalysis, are within normal ranges. She has not undergone any surgery that could affect gastrointestinal absorption or motility. The patient has no history of liver or renal dysfunction and has not experienced any allergic reactions to drugs. She has not consumed any prescription or non-prescription medications, except for hormonal contraceptives. The patient does not consume large quantities of methylxanthine-containing beverages or grapefruit, orange, or cranberry juice. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and has provided written informed consent prior to the conduct of any study-related activities.

The patient is a healthy 35-year-old male with a BMI of 24.5 kg/m^2, who has no significant medical history or current symptoms. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent form. The patient's blood pressure is 120/70 mmHg, and his heart rate is 65 bpm. The results from his electrocardiogram (ECG) are normal, and he has no known allergies or intolerances to any active substance or drugs. The patient is not currently breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed during the study period. He has no history of any loss of vision or known hereditary degenerative retinal disorders.

A 56 year old post-menopausal woman with a BMI of 35 comes to the clinic for consultation about bariatric surgery. She has a family history of breast cancer and is concerned about her risk. She has tried various diets and exercise programs but has not been able to lose a significant amount of weight. She is planning to undergo primary bariatric surgery and is willing to provide a core tissue biopsy at baseline and with repeat tissue collection after 2 weeks and 12 months post-bariatric surgery. She has no history of malignancy except for adequately treated non-melanoma skin cancer. She has no known allergies to gadolinium or lidocaine. She has not received therapeutic anticoagulation in the past month and has no medical reason why post-operative prophylactic anticoagulation could not be held for 12 hours. She has not received prior breast irradiation or used chemopreventatives such as tamoxifen or raloxifene.

The patient is a 35-year-old Caucasian woman with a BMI of 32 kg/m^2, who is interested in losing weight through an online program. She is currently employed as a graphic designer and spends most of her day sitting in front of a computer. She has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past, but has struggled to maintain weight loss in the long term. She is fluent in English and feels comfortable using a computer and the internet. She reports being able to walk 2 blocks unassisted without stopping. She has no history of heart disease or chest pain, and has never lost consciousness. She is not currently pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the next 6 months. She is not currently participating in any other weight loss program, and has not participated in a weight loss study at the Weight Control and Diabetes Research Center of Brown University and The Miriam Hospital within the last 2 years. She is excited to participate in a trial that may help her learn more effective strategies for weight loss and maintenance.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who presents with a history of a badly decayed and fractured posterior tooth. The tooth has been previously restored with a large filling, but the restoration has failed and the tooth is now causing pain and discomfort. The patient has good oral hygiene and is able to withstand conventional dental procedures. She is interested in receiving a single posterior crown to restore the function and aesthetics of her tooth. The patient has no active periodontal or pulpal diseases, and her teeth are in good condition except for the affected tooth. She is able to return for all follow-up appointments and evaluations. The patient is able to read and sign the informed consent document and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the one-year clinical performance of milled BioHPP (PEEK) versus zirconia veneered single crowns.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy diagnosed with amblyopia in his right eye due to strabismus. He has been wearing glasses for the past 6 months, but his visual acuity in his right eye is still lower than his left eye. His best-corrected visual acuity in his right eye is 0.5 logMAR and in his left eye is 0.1 logMAR. The interocular visual acuity difference is 0.4 logMAR. He has not undergone any binocular amblyopia treatment in the past 3 months. He has no other ocular or systemic diseases and no developmental delays. His parents are willing to forgo patching treatment during the 12-week study period and have provided informed consent for him to participate in the study. The child has demonstrated understanding and ability to play binocular games.

A 25-year-old male with an ASD diagnosis according to DSM-5 criteria visited the clinic seeking help with his self-harm behaviors. He reported feeling overwhelmed and unable to cope with his emotions. He has an IQ of 85 and is able to hold down a part-time job as a dishwasher. He is currently not taking any medications and has never received any formal therapy for his ASD or self-harm behaviors. He has a history of suicidal ideation and has attempted suicide twice in the past six months. He expressed willingness to participate in the study and has health insurance through his employer. He lives with his parents but is able to attend the therapy sessions independently.

The patient is a 55-year old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She is currently on adjuvant endocrine therapy and is experiencing hot flashes as a side effect. She has not participated in a regular exercise program in the past 12 months and is not a smoker. The patient does not have a history of chronic disease, but has occasional joint pain due to osteoarthritis. She is willing and able to travel to the exercise facility and understands the study requirements. The patient is not currently taking NSAIDs and is not planning on reconstructive surgery during the study period.

A 12-year-old female patient was diagnosed with ASS-deficient tumor, and has failed prior treatments. She was previously treated with chemotherapy, but the treatment was discontinued due to AEs associated with the systemic agent. She has a measurable disease that has been evaluated by RECIST 1.1 criteria for solid tumors. The patient is generally in good health and has undergone no major surgery in the last 4 weeks. She has no history of seizures or HIV. She has not received any anticancer treatments in the 2 weeks prior to entering the study. The patient has a serum uric acid level of 7.2 mg/dL, and her creatinine clearance is 75 mL/min. She has not been previously treated with ADI-PEG 20. The patient and her parents have provided written consent for her participation in the study, and she is willing to use appropriate contraception for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. He has previously received treatment with antineoplastic therapy but has since experienced relapse or progression of the disease. The patient has at least one measurable tumor mass that has not been previously irradiated, or has grown since previous irradiation. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. The patient has an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 2.0 x 109 cells/L, platelets of 120 x 109 cells/L, and normal liver and kidney function. He has no clinical or radiographic evidence of central nervous system lymphoma. The patient is not taking any strong CyP3A inducers and has not previously been treated with both Velcade and Temsirolimus. He is willing to practice effective contraception during the study treatment period and through a minimum of 30 days after the last dose of study drug. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction or New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV heart failure.

The patient is a 60 year old male veteran who has recently experienced some forgetfulness and difficulty with remembering names and appointments. He is still able to perform his daily activities without assistance and is not experiencing any significant functional decline. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are controlled with medication. He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He has a hobby of gardening and enjoys walking in his neighborhood. He has never been diagnosed with any neurological disorder and is not currently taking any medication for cognitive impairment. He lives alone but has regular contact with his children who visit him once a week.

A 54-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and underwent surgery. A follow-up brain MRI revealed that she had developed brain metastases. She is currently being evaluated for radiation therapy options and has been deemed eligible for this clinical trial. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80, and she has no major medical or psychiatric illnesses that would prevent her from completing the protocol. She has not received any previous radiation therapy to the brain and has signed the study-specific informed consent form. She is not pregnant and is willing and able to undergo MRI scans.

This is a 42 year-old female with a long-standing history of depression and has been on multiple antidepressant medications with suboptimal response. She presents with a current major depressive episode with symptoms of sadness, anhedonia, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. She has no history of suicide attempts or hospitalizations. The patient has no known allergies to medications and has not been diagnosed with any significant medical conditions. She has not used any anti-inflammatory drugs or immunomodulatory medications within the last 5 half-lives. The patient is willing to undergo PET scans and has the capacity to give informed consent.

62-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic constipation for the past 6 months. She reports having only two or fewer spontaneous bowel movements per week, with very hard or incomplete stools, and the need to strain during bowel movements. She has not made any changes to her diet or lifestyle, and her use of laxatives has not provided long-term relief. She has no history of drug-induced constipation, endocrine or metabolic disorders, neurologic disorders, or any other gastrointestinal or endocrine disorders. She has not undergone surgery for constipation or has any known or suspected organic disorders of the large bowel. She has mild hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is willing to comply with the study's requirements and is aware of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial.

A 55-year-old man has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 5 years. His diabetes is poorly controlled despite being on metformin and insulin therapy. He has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and has struggled with weight loss. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in carbohydrates. His most recent HbA1c is 8.5%. He denies any history of cardiovascular disease, liver disease, or renal disease. His AST and ALT are within normal limits, and his serum creatinine is 1.2. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help him improve his glycemic control and potentially reduce his medication use.

A 21-year-old female university student is experiencing high levels of anxiety and depression due to the COVID-19 pandemic. She is feeling overwhelmed by the constant changes and uncertainties, and finds it difficult to focus on her studies. She has been experiencing sleep disturbances, loss of appetite, and frequent crying spells. She feels that she needs support to cope with these challenges and would like to participate in a psychological intervention study. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, and is currently not taking any medications. She is a Turkish citizen and resides in Turkey.

The patient is a 58-year-old female who is diagnosed with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). She has started treatment with erlotinib (Tarceva®) at a dose of 150 mg per day within the last three days. She has developed a skin rash as a side effect of the treatment and is seeking treatment for the rash. The patient reports no allergies to tetracyclines, but has a history of photosensitivity. She is not currently using any concurrent agents for the rash and is not receiving any other anticancer agents. The patient has not used any antibiotics within the last 30 days and is not currently using any topical steroids or systemic immunosuppressants. She has a negative pregnancy test and is not lactating. The patient reports a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease but is not currently experiencing any symptoms. She has an ECOG performance status of 2 and reports smoking cessation 10 years ago. She is not currently using any agents that are strong inducers or inhibitors of CYTP3A4. The patient's liver function tests are within normal limits.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring an EGFR activating mutation in exon 21. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. He complains of shortness of breath and coughing up blood. His physical exam and lab studies show no other abnormalities except for a mass in the left lung. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He is willing to comply with the required protocol

The patient is a 29-year-old healthy woman who is a non-smoker and not currently taking any prescription medication. She has a BMI of 24 and has sufficient subcutaneous tissue for an injection in the abdomen, arm, and thigh. She has no history of drug or alcohol dependence and has never had a seizure or other neurological disorder. She has no history of cardiovascular, hematologic, gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, or psychiatric disorders. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to sumatriptan or similar drugs. She has no tattoos or birthmarks that would restrict injection site selection. She is fluent in English and provides written informed consent to participate in the study. She agrees to use acceptable birth control during the study period.

The patient is a 13-year-old female who has suffered a recent ACL injury while playing soccer. She complains of instability in her knee joint and has difficulty with walking and running. She has undergone a clinical examination and has been diagnosed with a uni-lateral ACL injury after a KT-1000 test showed >3mm difference compared to the contralateral knee. She has no other previous knee injuries or symptoms of meniscus or concomitant knee ligament injuries. She is fluent in English and meets the inclusion criteria, which requires her to be skeletally immature at the knee joint, have no other injuries, and be willing to return for follow-up test sessions. She also passed the standardized screening protocol, which includes no joint effusion, full range of motion, and no pain during a straight leg raise test, among others. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effectiveness of neuromuscular training in improving knee joint stability and function in adolescents with ACL injuries. The patient will be randomly assigned to either Group A or B and will complete the 5-week NMT protocol under the supervision of a Certified Athletic Therapist or Physiotherapist at the Pan Am clinic. She will undergo several follow-up testing sessions to evaluate her knee function and laxity, among other factors. The study has the potential to minimize the development of secondary meniscal tears and premature joint degeneration commonly demonstrated following an ACL injury.

A 32-year-old woman is interested in participating in a clinical trial for an influenza vaccine. She is a healthy individual with no significant medical history, and she has never received the flu vaccine during the 2007-2008 flu season. She is non-pregnant, non-lactating, and practices adequate contraception. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and can provide written informed consent. She does not use any investigational or non-registered products and has not received systemic glucocorticoids in the past 30 days. She has not received immunosuppressant, cytotoxic, or other immune-modifying drugs (other than glucocorticoids) or irradiation in the past 6 months. She has not received immunoglobulins and/or blood products in the past 3 months. She has no history of anaphylactic or other allergic reactions to vaccines or vaccine components/excipients, nor has she ever had Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS). She does not have any acute disease, febrile illness, or upper respiratory infection at screening, and she has never had a splenectomy. She has no immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive condition, and she is not currently treated with warfarin or heparin derivatives. She has not taken any analgesic or antipyretic medication within 12 hours prior to treatment for the purposes of prophylaxis of adverse events. She is an ideal candidate for this clinical trial.

Patient is a 47-year-old male with a history of stage IV colon cancer with metastasis to the liver and lungs. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with little improvement in his condition. He is currently experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional nausea. The patient's WHO performance status is 1. He is not currently on any chemotherapy or radiotherapy treatments. The patient has no history of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, and has not had any significant bowel resections. The patient is willing and able to eat a high-fat breakfast within a 30-minute period.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He presents to the clinic with a persistent cough and shortness of breath for the past month. He has lost about 10 pounds over the past month but denies any fevers or night sweats. He has a 30 pack-year history of smoking and continues to smoke about a pack a day. He denies any recent travel or exposure to sick contacts. Physical examination reveals crackles in the left lower lobe of the lung. Lab work shows a borderline positive ANCA test result. The patient has not been previously diagnosed with vasculitis, malignancy, or chronic inflammatory diseases. The patient is not pregnant.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease. His serum creatinine level is 2.5 mg/dL and his glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is within 15-60 mL/min. He has been receiving darbepoetin alfa therapy every three weeks for the past five months to manage his anemia, and his hemoglobin level has been stable at 12.5 g/dL. He has no history of uncontrolled high blood pressure, severe congestive heart failure, or severe stable or unstable coronary artery disease. He does not have any known hypersensitivity to mammalian cell-derived products or human albumin. He is not receiving dialysis and is not scheduled to receive dialysis during the course of the study. He is interested in participating in this study to evaluate the hemoglobin stability after switching from darbepoetin alfa to epoetin alfa. He has a negative urine pregnancy test and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 25-year old female college student who enjoys playing volleyball and basketball presented to the orthopedic clinic with a history of shoulder dislocation while playing volleyball a few months ago. She was diagnosed with traumatic anterior shoulder instability (TASI) and was recommended for Bankart surgery. The patient reported experiencing recurrent shoulder instability and pain with overhead activities. She has no significant past medical history, and she is not taking any medications. She is fluent in Norwegian, and she has no known language barriers. She is willing to participate in a supervised exercise program, and she is available for follow-up visits. She is excited to try the SINEX program as she hopes it will help improve her shoulder stability and enable her to return to playing sports without pain or fear of dislocation.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of heart failure. He has been experiencing shortness of breath on exertion, fatigue and weakness for several months. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a myocardial infarction that occurred two years ago. He is currently on stable medical therapy for heart failure, including diuretics, beta-blockers, and an ACE inhibitor. His baseline echocardiogram revealed an ejection fraction of 30%. He is in New York Heart Association functional Class III. He has not had any inotropic support within the past 30 days and has not been hospitalized for decompensated heart failure within the past 30 days. He does not have any potentially correctable causes of heart failure, such as valvular or congenital heart disease. He is willing and able to return for all follow-up visits. He is not scheduled for any cardiac procedures, has not had a myocardial infarction within the past 90 days, and does not have a mechanical tricuspid valve. He has not had a left ventricular assist device or heart transplant. He is not on dialysis and is not participating in any other experimental protocols. He is able to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old Caucasian woman presented to her dermatologist with a suspicious mole on her left forearm that has been growing in size over the past few months. She reported no other concerning symptoms, but had a family history of skin cancer. Upon examination, the dermatologist identified the mole as a potential melanoma and recommended a skin biopsy. The biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of early-stage melanoma and the patient was scheduled for surgery to remove the affected tissue. The patient has also been diagnosed with a history of benign skin diseases and has been treated for atopic dermatitis. She has no history of chronic illnesses or allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance the technology used for skin cancer diagnosis and treatment.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who was hospitalized due to pneumonia and acute respiratory failure. He was intubated and has been on mechanical ventilation for 72 hours. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He has a history of smoking for 40 years and quit 10 years ago. He is currently receiving intravenous antibiotics and his fever has resolved. His blood pressure is 140/80 mmHg and his heart rate is 90 beats per minute. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. His Glasgow Coma Scale score is 15. His chest X-ray shows improvement in pneumonia. He is able to follow commands and has no signs of respiratory distress. He has no significant muscle weakness, and his grip strength is appropriate for his age. Blood tests show a hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL, a white blood cell count of 12,000/mcL, and a serum creatinine level of 1.2 mg/dL. He has no significant comorbidities and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

75-year-old male with a history of lower back pain and numbness and weakness in the legs when walking or standing, which resolves when sitting. The patient has been diagnosed with lumbar central canal stenosis by MRI or CT scan. The patient has no history of cognitive impairment and is able to provide informed consent and complete assessment instruments in English. The patient has no clinical co-morbidities that could interfere with the collection of data concerning pain and function, and has no severe vascular, pulmonary, or coronary artery disease that limits ambulation. The patient has no spinal instability requiring surgical fusion, no severe osteoporosis, no metastatic cancer, no excessive alcohol consumption or evidence of non-prescribed or illegal drug use, and is not currently pregnant. The patient does not have concordant pain with internal rotation of the hip, active local or systemic infection, abnormal coagulation, any allergy to local anesthetic, steroid, or contrast, or any previous lumbar spine surgery. The patient does not have any rheumatological disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosis. The patient has not received an epidural steroid injection within the previous 6 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who presented with a headache, visual disturbances, and intermittent nausea. An MRI revealed a sellar lesion, which was confirmed to be a non-functioning pituitary adenoma after further testing. The patient is scheduled for surgery and has no history of hyperthyroidism, Cushing's syndrome, or long-term glucocorticoid use. The patient does not have any known co-morbidities that could influence the HPA-axis function, and has not undergone radiotherapy of the pituitary gland. The patient is willing to participate in a randomized controlled study to compare the outcomes of perioperative glucocorticoid replacement versus non-replacement therapy for surgical patients with sellar lesions. The patient will undergo an insulin tolerance test for assessment of pituitary function at enrollment and will be randomized into one of the four groups based on their pituitary function and glucocorticoid replacement regimen. The patient's primary outcome will be the HPA-axis function, evaluated by plasma cortisol and ACTH levels, while secondary outcomes include HPT-axis function, postoperative water-electrolyte balance, infection, recurrence, and health-related quality of life.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who works as a marketing executive and enjoys exercising regularly. She has a BMI of 22 and a waist size of 80 cm. She exercises at least three times a week and enjoys activities such as jogging, cycling, and yoga. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use any drugs. She does not take any medications or dietary supplements. She has no known medical conditions and has not been diagnosed with any neurological disorders. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of sage extracts on cognitive function during exercise. She has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary hyperparathyroidism. She has noticed bone pain and fatigue, and has been experiencing frequent headaches. She has no significant medical history, and is not taking any medications that could affect bone or mineral metabolism. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is generally in good health and is able to comply with the requirements of the study protocol. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She will be followed-up for one year, during which time she will receive treatment with alendronate (Sedron 70 mg once a week taken orally). She will have at least 4 visits to the hospital, during which her bone mineral density will be measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) every six months. Blood samples and 24-hour urine specimens will be taken before and after 3, 6 and 12 months of study. The patient will be carefully monitored for any adverse events, and will be in regular contact with study staff to ensure compliance with the treatment regimen.

A 45-year-old male patient with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus came to the clinic complaining of uncontrolled blood glucose levels despite being on metformin monotherapy for the past 3 months. His latest HbA1c reading was 8.5%, and he has been experiencing symptoms such as frequent urination, thirst, and fatigue. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. His BMI is 29.5, and he has no other significant medical history or allergies to medication. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the protocol to test the efficacy and tolerability of adding sitagliptin to his treatment regimen.

52-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and ischemic cardiomyopathy presented with worsening shortness of breath and fatigue. He was diagnosed with NYHA class III heart failure and started on maximal medical therapy including beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics. An echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 35% and left ventricular wall thickness of 7mm. He was deemed not a candidate for percutaneous or surgical revascularization due to significant multi-vessel coronary artery disease. He underwent cardiac catheterization which confirmed the presence of multi-vessel coronary artery disease and was referred for intramyocardial injection of adipose-derived regenerative cells (ADRCs). He has not had any recent episodes of acute coronary syndrome, TIA, or stroke and has not had any recent revascularization procedures. He is not pregnant or lactating.

A 23-year-old African American woman who is sexually active with her boyfriend is seeking to participate in a clinical trial for a computerized HIV/STD prevention program. She has been diagnosed with chlamydia in the past and is concerned about her risk of contracting other STIs, including HIV. She is interested in learning more about safe sex practices and is open to using condoms with her partner. She is not pregnant and does not plan on becoming pregnant in the next 3 months. She attends the STI clinic regularly and is looking for ways to be proactive in her health.

A 32-year-old woman who has been feeling persistently sad and hopeless for the past three weeks is seeking medical help for her symptoms. The patient reports difficulty sleeping, low energy, loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed, and feelings of worthlessness. She denies any history of psychiatric illness, substance abuse, or chronic pain. She is currently not taking any medication and has not received any treatment for depression in the past. The patient has a history of seasonal allergies, for which she takes over-the-counter antihistamines. She is generally in good health and has no other significant medical history. She has no known drug allergies. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and understands the study requirements. She is willing to provide written informed consent and undergo taste testing before and after ingesting the prescribed antidepressant. She is not currently infected with coronavirus or advised to self-isolate.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who is generally healthy and has a normal body mass index. He has no significant medical history and has never participated in a clinical trial before. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or any recreational drugs. He has not consumed any prescription or over-the-counter medication in the two weeks leading up to the trial. He has a normal blood pressure and has never experienced seizures. He has no family history of neurological disorders. He has not consumed grapefruit juice or any xanthine-containing foods or beverages in the 48 hours prior to the trial. He has no history of difficulty with donating blood or difficulty accessing veins. He has a normal 12-lead ECG and chest X-ray. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study and understands the nature and purpose of the trial.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who was diagnosed with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) after a routine physical exam revealed an enlarged kidney. The patient has no symptoms, good blood pressure control, and normal kidney function. His family has a history of ADPKD, and his father and grandfather both died from complications of the disease. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. The patient and his parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance the understanding and treatment of the disease, and they are willing to comply with all study requirements.

An 8-year-old boy weighing 30 kg is scheduled for a tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy. The patient has a history of obstructive sleep apnea and recurrent tonsillitis with difficulty breathing at night. The patient has no known allergies, and his medical history is unremarkable. The patient is accompanied by his mother, who is his legal guardian, and both have provided informed consent for the surgical procedure and study participation. The patient is cooperative and able to follow commands. He has no peripheral neurologic or neuropathic disorders, and his upper extremities are free from edema. The patient is eligible for this study.

Patient is a 3-year-old boy from Kenya who is brought to the clinic by his mother. He presents with severe malnutrition, as evidenced by a mid-upper arm circumference of 11cm and a weight for height z score of -4. His mother reports that he has been losing weight over the past few months and has had frequent diarrhea episodes. He has not received any vaccinations and his past medical history is unremarkable. Physical examination reveals a height for age z score of -3 and nutritional oedema in both feet. Laboratory testing shows an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 35mm/hr. The patient's mother provides informed consent for his participation in the study.

A 47 year old woman presents to the clinic complaining of persistent stomach pain and discomfort. She also reports acid reflux and bloating after meals. She has a history of gastritis and has been diagnosed with H. pylori infection. She has never received any treatment specifically for H. pylori. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. Biopsy specimens will be obtained during gastroduodenoscopy for bacterial susceptibility testing.

A 6-month-old male infant was brought to the pediatrician by his parents due to a persistent abnormal posture of the head and the neck. The infant was born at full term with no past medical history or complications during pregnancy or delivery. The parents noticed that the infant's head was tilted to the right side and that he had difficulty turning his head to the left side. The infant has been diagnosed with congenital muscular torticollis (CMT) after a physical examination. The parents have been advised to start physical therapy to prevent further complications. The physical therapist documented an asymmetrical deformation of the skull or plagiocephaly with a difference in head circumference between the right and left side of the head. The physical therapist also noted that the infant's facial features were asymmetrical. The parents reported to the pediatrician that the infant has been sleeping on his back since birth. A CT scan of the skull was performed and the images have been included in the study database. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial.

32yo woman with a 5-year history of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) who presents with significant fatigue and muscle weakness. She reports difficulty with daily activities and has noticed decreased endurance during exercise. She has tried various medications for her MS, including interferons and glatiramer acetate, but has had limited success in controlling her symptoms. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications or supplements. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help improve her quality of life and better understand the link between her fatigue and nutritional deficiencies.

The patient is a 25-year-old male diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 17. He has been insulin-dependent for the past 8 years and currently requires three or more injections of insulin per day to maintain his blood sugar levels. He has a history of hypoglycemia, experiencing at least one episode of severe hypoglycemia in the past year. He practices intensive diabetes management, checking his glucose levels at least three times a day, and has regular clinical evaluations with an endocrinologist. He experiences reduced awareness of hypoglycemia. He has never received a pancreas or islet transplant before and has no history of malignancy or active infections. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to conceive during the study period. He has a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and weighs 70 kg. His HbA1c level is 8.5%. His glomerular filtration rate is 100 ml/min/1.73m2. He has no history of severe coexisting cardiac disease or liver disease. He has not received any immunosuppressive therapy in the past and is not currently taking any anti-diabetic medication other than insulin. He is willing to comply with study procedures and able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has a history of diabetic macular edema in her right eye for the past year. She has noticed a decrease in her visual acuity to 20/60 in the affected eye. She is currently under treatment with ranibizumab which she receives every 4 weeks. She is a homemaker and spends most of her time at home. She has a BMI of 27 and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. Her physical examination is unremarkable. She has no history of vitreoretinal surgery or laser photocoagulation. She has not received any intraocular or periocular corticosteroids or anti-angiogenic drugs in the past. She has no active proliferative diabetic retinopathy or history of uveitis. She has not had cataract surgery or yttrium-aluminium-garnet capsulotomy in the past 90 days. She has no vitreomacular traction or epiretinal membrane that would affect her central vision. She has no concurrent disease in the study eye that could compromise VA or require medical or surgical intervention during the study period. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to practice adequate contraception during the study.

A 36-year-old man diagnosed with schizophrenia according to DSM-5 seeks to participate in a clinical trial investigating the glutamatergic and GABAergic system in schizophrenia. He has been diagnosed for 6 years and is currently taking antipsychotic medication. He has no other psychiatric comorbidities and is mentally and contractually capable of giving consent. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has no history of structural neurological disease or pregnancy. He is willing to undergo blood tests, EEG measurements, MRI scans, and neuropsychological tests as part of the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who is 5'5" tall and weighs 180 pounds, resulting in a BMI of 30. She is interested in losing weight and has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past with limited success. She is generally healthy and has no history of diabetes, heart disease, or other major illnesses. She has good oral hygiene and no known sensitivity to flavors, sweeteners, or other ingredients in sugar-free chewing gum. She is not currently participating in any weight-reduction program and is a non-smoker. She is willing to commit to chewing gum following meals and in place of snacks for a minimum of 90 minutes per day. She is available to attend clinic visits at baseline, 4 weeks post-randomization, and 8 weeks post-randomization, and is willing to participate in telephone contacts at 2 weeks and 6 weeks post-randomization to assess adherence to the gum chewing protocol. She is not currently pregnant or nursing, and is willing to take adequate contraceptive measures if potentially fertile.

80-year-old female with a history of heart failure and recent hospitalization for cardiac decompensation. She has been diagnosed with pre-frailty or frailty according to the Fried frailty scale and fulfills at least one criterion. The patient is experiencing reduced quality of life and functional parameters due to her condition. She is currently receiving pharmacological treatment for heart failure and comorbidities but is interested in participating in a comprehensive intervention program that includes physical, nutritional, hormonal, and pharmacological interventions to improve her survival and reduce cardiac decompensation and hospital admissions. The patient is willing to undergo regular medical and nursing visits as well as follow the intervention plan for a period of 12 months. The patient has signed the consent form and is eligible for the study.

A 30-year-old man was recently diagnosed with classical Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) in Stage IIB with mediastinal bulk. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He has no history of hypertension or cardiac disease, and his echocardiography shows a normal left ventricular ejection fraction. His DLCO and FEV1 tests are both within normal limits. He is currently not on any medications and has no history of other malignancies. He understands the purpose of the study, and is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. He has access to PET-CT scan facilities qualified by FIL. He is married but currently not planning to conceive, and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. He has signed an informed consent form.

45 yo female with a history of hypertension and recent onset of severe headaches and confusion. MRI revealed a mass in her brain which was biopsied and diagnosed as primary CNS lymphoma. The patient has no prior history of cancer and is HIV negative. She has no significant past medical history except hypertension. She is currently able to perform activities of daily living and has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to undergo combination chemotherapy plus radiation therapy. She is not pregnant and has no severe uncontrolled infection. She has not received any prior chemotherapy or organ transplantation.

A 48-year-old woman with a history of metastatic breast cancer that has progressed after three lines of chemotherapy. She has a performance status of 1 and reports experiencing mild fatigue and occasional bone pain. She has no history of allergies to hydralazine or valproate. She has never used experimental drugs and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of rheumatic disease, central nervous system disease, heart failure from aortic stenosis, or postural hypotension. She is willing to undergo study evaluation and acetylation status typing before treatment. She has measurable disease in the form of multiple bone metastases visible on CT scan. Her blood counts, liver, and kidney function are within normal limits.

The patient is a 45-year-old Japanese woman who was diagnosed with BRCA2-mutated breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, the cancer has metastasized to her liver and lungs, and she has failed previous standard treatment for her cancer. She has no history of CNS metastases or other malignancies. She is currently on medication for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She is a homemaker and lives with her husband and two children. She is willing to fast for at least 14 hours and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer her a new treatment option.

Patient is a 68-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of neovascular AMD in her left eye. She has not received any treatment for the condition yet. Her visual acuity in the left eye is currently 20/80, and there is edema present in the retina causing a thickness of at least 300um. The patient's right eye has a best corrected visual acuity of 20/40. There is no evidence of scarring CNV or fibrosis greater than 75% of the lesion area in the left eye. The patient is otherwise in good health and is excited to participate in this study to potentially improve her vision.

The patient is a 35 year old male with no significant medical history. He does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. He works as an engineer and maintains an active lifestyle by regularly exercising and playing sports. He has no history of heart or lung disease and has never undergone any cardiac or pulmonary imaging studies. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help improve the accuracy and efficiency of cardiac MR imaging protocols. He understands the study involves undergoing MRI scans without any contrast agents and has no concerns about the procedure. He is able to comply with the study requirements and is willing to attend follow-up appointments as needed.
