Unfortunately, as this is a screening trial, there is no specific patient description that can be provided. The trial is targeting all women aged 50-69 who attend mammography screening in Bergen in 2018 and 2019. Women willing to participate in the study will sign an informed consent form. However, women with breast implants are excluded from the trial.

A 62-year-old male who underwent total hip arthroplasty (THA) in his right hip 4 years ago and is currently experiencing some discomfort in his left hip. He has no history of heart or lung diseases but was diagnosed with mild osteoarthritis in his left hip during a routine check-up. He has been working as a construction worker for the past 30 years and is physically active. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the best course of action for his left hip and to improve his overall physical health.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease who is scheduled to undergo coronary angiography. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are all well-controlled with medications. He has no known history of kidney disease. His current medications include aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He is not currently taking any vitamin D supplements or other lipid-regulating drugs. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of vitamin D supplementation in reducing the risk of contrast-induced nephropathy.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 10 years ago. He has been on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for the past 6 months, but his viral load has remained detectable despite his medication. His most recent CD4 count was 250 cells/mm3. He has a history of smoking and moderate alcohol consumption. He works full-time as a sales representative and lives alone. He has no history of allergies or significant medical problems other than his HIV diagnosis. He is willing to comply with all protocol requirements and procedures of the clinical trial. His viral load is currently >1,000 copies/mL, and he has documented resistance to at least one antiretroviral medication from each of three classes of antiretroviral medications as measured by resistance testing. He has a history of at least 6 months on antiretroviral treatment and is currently receiving a stable HAART regimen. He is willing to continue that regimen until Day 14 of the study. He has full viral sensitivity/susceptibility to at least one antiretroviral agent, other than ibalizumab, as determined by the screening resistance tests and is willing and able to be treated with at least one agent to which his viral isolate is fully sensitive/susceptible according to the screening resistance tests as a component of OBR. If sexually active, he is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the study and for 30 days after the last administration of the study drug.

A 27-year old medical student, who is generally healthy, is interested in participating in a clinical trial that would help advance medical technology. She is interested in cardiology and would like to contribute to the development of new techniques to image the heart and blood vessels using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). She doesn't have any history of cardiac or renal diseases, nor is she currently pregnant or lactating. She currently exercises regularly and has no problem with claustrophobia. She is willing to undergo the MRI scan and possible injection of gadolinium contrast agent. She is excited to participate in this study and help advance medical science.

A 56-year-old male with a history of chronic constipation and hemorrhoids presented to the gastroenterology clinic for evaluation of a polyp that was found during a routine colonoscopy. The polyp was located in the sigmoid colon and measured 25 mm in diameter. The patient had no significant past medical history, and his medications included only a daily multivitamin. He had no known allergies and had never undergone any previous surgeries. The patient reported no current symptoms and denied any abdominal pain, diarrhea, or rectal bleeding. His family history was significant for colon polyps in his father, who had undergone a colon resection at age 65 for a large adenomatous polyp. The patient was a non-smoker and did not consume alcohol. He was physically active and had a BMI of 27. On physical exam, he appeared healthy with normal vital signs. His abdomen was soft and non-tender, and bowel sounds were present. There was no palpable mass or tenderness. The patient was interested in participating in the study and able to sign the informed consent.

A 68-year old retired teacher who lives alone and has been diagnosed with dyslipidemia for the past six months will be a suitable candidate for this clinical trial. She has been regularly taking her medication prescribed by her primary care physician. She has not engaged in any physical activity for the past three months. She enjoys reading books and watching movies in her spare time. She has no history of any cardiovascular disease or orthopedic issues. She is a non-smoker and does not use hormone therapy drugs. She has no known allergies. She is enthusiastic about participating in this clinical trial as she is eager to improve her health and quality of life.

A 32-year-old female with Fitzpatrick Skin Type II is planning to undergo full-face fractionated ablative CO2 laser resurfacing. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She has no history of keloids or hypertrophic scars. She is willing to comply with study instructions and complete the entire course of the study. She has regular menstrual cycles and is willing to use an acceptable form of birth control during the entire course of the study. She has never participated in any clinical trials for investigational drugs or devices. She understands the terms of the protocol and has provided a completed and signed informed consent, HIPAA, and photography release forms.

45-year-old male United Methodist Church pastor, serving a local church as a Bishop in the North Carolina Annual Conference. The patient has a history of obesity and related complications, such as hypertension and diabetes, and has experienced high levels of stress and depression. The patient is interested in improving their overall health and well-being and is willing to participate in a two-year holistic health program designed specifically for United Methodist clergy. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate in surveys and health screenings throughout the study period. The patient understands that they will be randomized to one of three cohorts and may have to wait to receive the intervention, but is still interested in participating in the study.

A 30-year-old healthy male with no significant past medical history and no medications is eligible for this clinical trial. He is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol or any illicit drugs. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He works as a software engineer and has a sedentary lifestyle. He has no known allergies and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past three months. He is willing to follow all the guidelines and can comply with the study requirements. He has no history of high blood pressure, impaired glucose tolerance, diabetes, or any other major diseases or chronic conditions. The patient is not receiving any oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy.

A 28-year-old male with congenital factor XIII deficiency is eligible for this clinical trial. He has been previously diagnosed with FXIII A-subunit deficiency and his diagnosis has been confirmed by genotyping. His body weight is 75 kg. He has no known inhibitors towards FXIII and does not have any other congenital or acquired coagulation disorder. His platelet count is 120 x 10^9/L. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is using adequate contraceptive methods. He has previously participated in trial F13CD-1725 and is willing to continue the monthly replacement therapy of recombinant factor XIII until the product is commercially available.

42yo male with a history of mildly-to-moderately active ulcerative colitis for the past 5 years, with symptoms including abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. The patient has been on oral mesalamine for the past 4 weeks but has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He has no history of Crohn's disease or any other inflammatory bowel disorder, and has not received any immunosuppressive treatments. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other investigational drugs. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the requirements of the study.

55 year old male cancer survivor, diagnosed with colon cancer three years ago and successfully underwent surgery and chemotherapy. Has not engaged in structured exercise since the diagnosis and has been struggling with fatigue and low energy levels. Has the approval of his oncologist to engage in physical activity. Has access to a laptop and phone with Zoom software and an active email address. Fluent in English. Willing to participate in a 12-week home exercise program and complete study questionnaires before and after the program, and 3 months after the program.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer through histopathological investigation. She is currently scheduled to undergo chemotherapy, which includes neoadjuvant chemotherapy, postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy, or palliative chemotherapy for advanced breast cancer. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 0-1, indicating her physical condition is good. She has no history of nervous system disease and is able to understand the study and give informed consent. Her blood routine and ECG are normal, and she has no fatigue symptoms confirmed by the checklist individual strength (CIS) and the brief fatigue inventory (BFI) before chemotherapy. She has no other tumors or brain metastases and pleural effusion. She has no untreated anemia or thyroid dysfunction. She has no heart and lung diseases or respiratory system diseases affecting blood oxygen saturation.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who sustained a concussion during a car accident 6 months ago. Since the accident, she has been experiencing persistent headaches, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and irritability. She has tried various medications prescribed by her primary care physician, but none have provided significant relief. The patient is currently working part-time due to the severity of her symptoms and has had to give up many of her hobbies and social activities. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for her post-concussion symptoms. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she is not currently taking any medication for her post-concussion symptoms. The patient has not undergone TMS therapy in the past, and she does not have any contraindications for TMS treatment. She is willing to maintain her current pharmacologic management throughout the study protocol. The patient understands that the study will involve a four-week treatment protocol with 20 treatments, and she is willing to participate in all follow-up assessments over the course of 6 months.

A 65-year-old male diagnosed with biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma of the stomach. The cancer has progressed to an advanced stage and is being treated with palliative intent. The patient has been experiencing symptoms such as bleeding, pain, and obstruction that are indicative of locally advanced gastric cancer. The patient has not received any prior abdominal radiotherapy and is not on chemotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in the study to receive the proposed radiotherapy dose of 36Gy in 12 fractions to alleviate symptoms and improve quality of life. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the treatment and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old female who sustained a concussion due to a head trauma 3 months ago is seeking treatment for persistent post-concussion symptoms (PCS). She is a native Danish speaker, resides in the Central Denmark Region, and has a RPQ score of 25. She has no previous history of concussion leading to persistent PCS within the last two years, and has no objective neurological findings or acute trauma CT scan indicating neurological disease or brain damage. She does not have severe misuse of alcohol, prescription drugs or illegal drugs, and has no psychiatric morbidity or severe neurological disease that impedes participation in the program. She is interested in participating in the GAIN 2.0 clinical trial to receive evidence-based treatment for her persistent PCS.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol abuse. He has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and has lost a significant amount of weight in the past few months. He has been diagnosed with inoperable oesophageal cancer with grade 3 dysphagia. The patient's medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are managed with medication. He has no history of heart disease, lung disease, or renal disease. The patient is retired and lives with his wife. He has two adult children who live nearby. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive treatment for his dysphagia and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been experiencing snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness. She has no significant medical history and her medications include only multivitamins. She reports that her symptoms have been gradually worsening over the past few months and her husband has also noticed that she stops breathing during her sleep. She has not been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) but her doctor has advised her that she is at high risk of developing it. She has not used any medication to improve her sleep before or during the study. The patient is currently retired and lives with her husband. She has three adult children who live nearby. She has no history of smoking, but she drinks alcohol socially. Her blood pressure is within normal limits and she has no history of cardiovascular or metabolic diseases. Her BMI is 27. She is interested in participating in this study to improve her sleep quality and reduce the risk of developing OSAS.

This is a 62-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease who underwent placement of a dual-chamber pacemaker for complete heart block 6 months ago. He has been stable and compliant with his medications since the procedure. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the safety of a new security device for patients with implanted cardiac electronic devices. He has no history of malfunction in his device nor low battery voltage.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was diagnosed with HIV several years ago. He is a daily smoker who has been smoking for over 20 years. He has tried to quit smoking in the past but has been unsuccessful. He is concerned about the health risks associated with smoking, particularly as an HIV-positive individual. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past year. He lives alone and works as a freelance graphic designer. He is motivated to quit smoking and willing to participate in a clinical trial to help him achieve this goal. He speaks fluent English and is able to provide informed written consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with no history of chronic disease or medication use. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 25 and weighs 75 kg. He does not smoke or consume alcohol, and has no history of illicit drug use. He has not donated blood or plasma within the last 56 days or 30 days, respectively. He has normal blood pressure and heart rate, and no history of cardiovascular disease or gastrointestinal disorder. He is not pregnant or nursing, and does not plan to become pregnant during the study period. He has no allergies or hypersensitivity to tenofovir. He is willing to use adequate contraceptive methods throughout the study. He has not been diagnosed with HIV, HBV, or HCV. He is interested in participating in the study to help further scientific research.

Maria is a 68-year-old Spanish-speaking Hispanic woman who lives with her husband. She has noticed difficulty remembering things, such as appointments and where she put her keys. Her husband has also noticed that she repeats herself and forgets conversations they've had. Maria has a history of hypertension, but her other medical history is unremarkable. She takes medications for her blood pressure and vitamins. She is retired and enjoys spending time with her grandchildren, gardening, and cooking. Her husband is her main caregiver and he has noticed that he is feeling overwhelmed with the added responsibilities of taking care of her. Maria is interested in participating in this study to see if it can help her with her memory and to help alleviate some of the burden on her husband.

Patient A is a 25-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with HIV after experiencing flu-like symptoms. His viral load is 10,000 and his CD4 count is 400. He has not yet started any antiretroviral therapy. He is generally healthy and does not have any other significant medical history. He has never participated in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who underwent a renal transplant 2 years ago. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and is currently on metformin 1000mg twice daily with an HbA1c of 9.5%. His serum creatinine levels have been stable with less than 10% deviation in the last 2 months. He has not experienced any episodes of acute rejection or graft dysfunction since the transplant. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. He has no history of liver disease, and his estimated GFR is 35 ml/min/1.73 m2. He is not on insulin therapy and has no skin disorders that may interfere with the laser Doppler flowmetry investigations. The patient is willing to use an effective method of contraception throughout the study period and for 90 days following discontinuation of the study drugs.

38 F with a history of nonspecific low back pain for the past 5 months. She reports the pain as a constant ache, and it worsens with prolonged standing and sitting. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications with no significant relief. She has no history of any specific low back pain etiology such as infection, tumor, osteoporosis, ankylosing spondylitis, fracture, inflammatory process, radicular syndrome or cauda equina syndrome. She is interested in trying wet cupping therapy and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She has no history of any conditions that would exclude her from the study, such as AIDS, active hepatitis, tuberculosis, syphilis, regular use of anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs, anemia, thrombocytopenia, hemorrhagic disease like hemophilia, severe cardiovascular disease, kidney diseases, and vertebra surgery. She is not pregnant nor planning for conception. She has not received any low back pain treatment during the last 2 weeks or wet cupping treatment within the last 3 months.

This is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history of systemic sclerosis and Raynaud's phenomenon. She complains of increasing shortness of breath with minimal exertion and fatigue over the last few months. She denies chest pain, cough, or fever. On examination, she has digital ulcers and sclerodactyly. Her lung exam reveals fine bibasilar crackles. Echocardiography shows evidence of right ventricular dysfunction with an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 50 mmHg. She is scheduled for a right heart catheterization to confirm the diagnosis of pulmonary arterial hypertension. She has not been diagnosed with PAH before and has not received any PAH-specific therapy.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with Stage II non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent coughing and shortness of breath. The cancer is located in the upper lobe of her right lung and is deemed resectable by her medical team. She has a WHO performance status of 1 and has no significant medical history. Her team recommends that she consider participating in a clinical trial studying the role of perioperative chemotherapy in Stage I/II NSCLC to further improve her chances of survival after surgery.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with gastric adenocarcinoma. She experienced symptoms such as heartburn, nausea, and bloating for several months before seeking medical attention. Her physical exam was significant for a palpable mass in the upper abdomen. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma. Her imaging studies showed no evidence of distant metastasis. She is otherwise healthy, with a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, well-controlled on medications. She is married and has two adult children. She works part-time as a teacher. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the use of proton radiotherapy and chemotherapy for her cancer. She understands the potential risks and benefits and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

45 yo female diagnosed with primary IgA nephropathy 6 months ago presents with a history of hypertension, proteinuria (2.5g/24hr), and eGFR of 50 ml/min/1.73m2. She is currently on a maximal tolerated dose of losartan (100mg daily) and has been compliant with the medication. She denies any history of cancer, infection, diabetes mellitus, connective tissue disease or liver dysfunction. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is willing to comply with the study and follow-up procedures.

A 62-year-old retired accountant was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation two years ago. He has been experiencing palpitations, fatigue, and shortness of breath. He is on anticoagulation therapy and his current medication includes Metoprolol and Dabigatran. He has no history of heart disease or any other significant medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol moderately. He has a sedentary lifestyle and is not physically active. He is fluent in German and has given his informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 5-year-old child who is scheduled for a tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy under general anesthesia. The child has no history of pulmonary disease and is generally healthy. The child has a mild cold but has not had any upper or lower respiratory tract infections within the past 2 weeks. The operation is scheduled and is not an emergency. The child's vital signs are stable.

The patient is a 58-year-old veteran who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease (CAD) and has a depressed left ventricular function with an ejection fraction (EF) of less than 40%. The patient is acutely stable and there is no evidence of cardiogenic shock or evolving myocardial infarction. The VA Salt Lake City Health Care System Cardiothoracic Surgery team has determined that the patient is a suitable candidate for surgical revascularization by means of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG). The patient has abnormal cardiac wall segments on preoperative data, and the NHYA/CCA classifies the patient as Class I or higher. The patient has no history of alcohol or substance abuse, psychiatric issues, or systemic malignancy. The patient has no contraindication to general anesthesia and is able to give informed consent.

A 9 year old child diagnosed with HIV is currently on an antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen for the past 2 months. The child lives in a village near Masafu General Hospital in Busia and has no history of malaria infection. The child's ART regimen is based on efavirenz (EFV) and the child weighs 25 kg. The child's guardian has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP) in HIV-infected children on EFV-based ART. The trial will involve multiple venous blood collections to accurately estimate drug exposure over time. The primary goal of the study is to assess the pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety of DP in the setting of co-administration with first-line ART regimens (EFV-, LPV/r- or DTG-based ART) in children without malaria. The trial will involve up to 190 children and adolescents, and the child will be enrolled in the HIV-infected children age 3 - 10 years on EFV-based ART group. The child's eligibility criteria includes being malaria-uninfected at the time of enrollment, provision of informed consent, residency within 30km of Masafu General Hospital, and confirmed HIV infection. The child must not have a history of significant comorbidities such as malignancy, active tuberculosis, or other active WHO stage 4 disease, and must not have received any medications known to affect CYP450 metabolism (except ART) within 14 days of study enrollment. The child's hemoglobin levels should be above 7.0 g/dL, and the child should not have any current or recent malaria infections.

57-year-old female with a history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and occasional rectal bleeding presented to her gastroenterologist for a colonoscopy screening. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. The patient underwent bowel preparation as recommended by the gastroenterologist and is scheduled to undergo colonoscopy without sedation. The gastroenterologist will evaluate the technical difficulty of the examination, and the patient's data will be used to develop a clinical model to predict the complexity of colonoscopy. The patient is able to give informed consent and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

A 54 year old female patient diagnosed with colorectal cancer that has spread to her liver and lungs. She has received chemotherapy treatment containing irinotecan and oxaliplatin regimens for unresectable or recurrent colorectal cancer but has not shown significant improvement. She is found to have the KRAS mutation. She does not have any moderate or severe ascites or pleural effusion requiring treatment, and she has no metastasis to the CNS. Her ECOG performance status is 1 and her white blood cell count is 7,200/mm³. Her neutrophil count is 4,500/mm³ and her platelet count is 130,000/mm³. Her total bilirubin is 0.9 mg/dL, AST and ALT are 45 U/L and her serum creatinine level is 0.8 mg/dL. She is not pregnant or nursing and is able to take capsules orally. She has no active infections or serious complications. She has no history of thrombosis, cerebral infarction, myocardial infarction or pulmonary embolism. She has not received any prior therapy with S-1, chemotherapy included irinotecan and oxaliplatin as first- or second-line treatment, or radiotherapy. She is not receiving concurrent continuous treatment with steroids or flucytosine. She is eligible for this study as third-line therapy for her colorectal cancer.

56-year-old woman with a history of knee pain for the past 5 years. She has tried multiple conservative treatments including NSAIDs, hyaluronic acid injections, and corticosteroids but has not experienced significant relief of her symptoms. She reports pain with weight-bearing activities and stiffness in the morning. She has been diagnosed with medial compartment knee osteoarthritis with a Kellgren-Lawrence score of 3. She has a BMI of 27 and does not have any history of malignancies, rheumatic diseases, diabetes, or metabolic disorders of the thyroid. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who was hospitalized due to a heart condition. During her hospital stay, she was prescribed a hypnosedative drug to help with her sleep. She has never taken this medication before and is concerned about its potential side effects. She is able to answer questionnaires in French and will be returning home at discharge. She has no history of cognitive impairment and scored above 24 on the Mini-Mental State Examination. She has no physical disabilities and is able to participate in the study. She has no severe depression or other psychopathological conditions. She is not undergoing any parenteral treatment for cancer or in a palliative care program. She is not dependent on alcohol or drugs. She is willing to participate in the study and can be reached by phone for follow-up interviews.

A 62-year old female was diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in the chronic phase. She was started on imatinib mesylate (Gleevec) for treatment. She has been on this medication for 4 weeks and her platelet count dropped to less than 50 * 10(9)/L. She experiences easy bruising, nosebleeds, and gum bleeding. She had no previous history of bleeding disorders or thrombocytopenia. She is a retired teacher and has two children. She has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia, which are well controlled with medications. She has no history of heart disease or arrhythmias. She has no known allergies to E. coli. She is negative for pregnancy. She is alert and oriented, with no cognitive or memory deficits. She is willing to participate in the study and signed the informed consent.

A 22-year-old female presents with moderate to severe pain following the surgical extraction of three impacted third molars. She reports difficulty in eating and discomfort while speaking due to the pain. She has a history of good oral hygiene and has never experienced any dental surgeries before. Her medical history is free of significant hepatic, renal, endocrine, cardiovascular, neurological, psychiatric, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, hematologic, or metabolic disorders. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. She is currently not taking any medications for pain relief. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing migraines with aura for the past 5 years. She has an average of 6 migraine attacks per month, which last for 2-3 days and are usually associated with nausea and photophobia. She has tried prophylactic treatment in the past, including beta blockers and topiramate, but experienced intolerable side effects. She currently uses triptans as abortive treatment for her migraines, but is interested in finding a more effective prophylactic treatment. She is in good general health, exercises regularly, and has a BMI of 23 kg/m2. She is not currently pregnant or lactating, and uses a barrier method of contraception. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past month.

A 44-year-old female who works as a receptionist presented with low back pain that has been bothering her for the past 6 months. She describes the pain as a dull ache that is present throughout the day, worsens with prolonged sitting and standing, and improves with rest. She denies any radiating pain below the knee or any neurological symptoms. She has tried over the counter pain medications such as ibuprofen and acetaminophen but they only provide temporary relief. She has never had any history of neurological disease, severe lumbar trauma, or surgery. She is not currently taking any muscle relaxants or analgesics. She does not have diabetes, heart, kidney, thyroid disorders, or any other chronic diseases. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in the study to try a new exercise intervention that may help her manage her low back pain.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy with a non-syndromic unilateral cleft lip and palate. He has not undergone any previous surgery to correct the alveolar cleft. His jaw is aligned and ready to receive the graft. The patient's canine has not erupted yet, and he has completed his orthodontic treatment. The patient has had a CT scan to document the alveolar cleft. He is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial comparing mesenchymal stem cells obtained from autogenous deciduous dental pulp associated with biomaterials versus iliac crest autogenous bone graft for secondary alveolar cleft repair.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her joints, particularly in her hands and feet, which has been affecting her daily activities. She has been treated with a biosimilar medication for the past 6 months but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. Her treating physician has decided to switch her to either Flixabi (infliximab) or Imraldi (adalimumab) and she has consented to participate in this study. She has no history of psoriasis and is willing to be followed up at the same investigator site for 2 years after the baseline.

A 24-year old university student is looking to participate in the MBA Intervention clinical trial. She is currently studying psychology and is an avid runner. She has been running for three years and runs about three times a week. She enjoys running as it helps her clear her head and feel better overall. However, she has noticed that sometimes she gets too caught up in her appearance and how running affects her body. She has struggled with body image issues in the past and currently uses running as a way to manage her weight. She is looking to participate in this trial to learn how to focus on the enjoyment of physical activity rather than how it affects her physical appearance. She has no history of body image disorders and is not currently receiving treatment for any related issues.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing muscle weakness and fatigue for the past year. She noticed that her symptoms worsen with activity and improve with rest. She has no significant medical history except for hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with medication. She takes levothyroxine (100 mcg) daily. She has no known allergies to medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her family history is negative for autoimmune diseases. On physical examination, she has ptosis and diplopia, with normal reflexes and sensation. She has no muscle atrophy or fasciculations. Her laboratory tests showed positive AChR antibodies. She was diagnosed with myasthenia gravis and started on pyridostigmine (60 mg three times daily) and prednisone (20 mg daily). Despite treatment, her symptoms persisted, and she was referred for therapeutic plasma exchange.

48-year-old male with a history of tobacco and alcohol abuse, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He had a previous coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery 3 years ago. On examination, he is found to have a new-onset murmur and electrocardiogram (EKG) changes suggestive of ischemia. Coronary angiography showed in-stent restenosis in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) with 70% diameter stenosis. The patient has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 46-year-old female presents with a history of locally advanced, unresectable epithelioid sarcoma of the right knee with lung metastases. She has completed 5 cycles of doxorubicin-based chemotherapy with stable disease on imaging. She has no significant comorbidities and an ECOG performance status of 1. She is currently taking no medications and has no known allergies. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial for gemcitabine plus ascorbate and is willing to tolerate a 15g ascorbate infusion. She has measurable disease with a right knee mass measuring 6 cm and multiple pulmonary nodules. She has had no prior exposure to gemcitabine for metastatic disease. She has not received radiation therapy within the last 4 weeks and has recovered from the side effects of prior chemotherapy. She is not currently on any other anti-cancer therapy or radiation therapy. She is willing to use two methods of contraception, one being a barrier method, during the study and for 3 months after the last study drug administration. She has no history of HIV or significant history of non-compliance to medical regimens. She is willing to provide written informed consent prior to participation in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been wearing glasses for the past 5 years due to her myopia. She is interested in the Berkeley Orthokeratology Study as she is looking for a non-surgical alternative to correct her vision. Her current glasses prescription is -2.50 in both eyes, and she has no other ocular or systemic health conditions. She has never worn contact lenses before and is excited to participate in this study to potentially reduce her dependence on glasses. Her corneal curvature readings are within the eligible range for the study, and her corrected visual acuity is 6/6 or better in each eye. Her astigmatism is less than 0.75 D, and she has no anisometropia. Her myopia is between 1 and 4 D, making her an ideal candidate for the study. She is willing to commit to the study protocol and attend regular follow-up appointments for 1.5 years to monitor her progress.

A 32-year-old woman presents with a history of ankle pain and swelling for the past 2 years. She has a history of playing basketball and volleyball. She has tried various conservative treatments including rest, physical therapy, and anti-inflammatory medications but has not experienced significant improvement. She has noticed difficulty with walking, running, and jumping. An MRI of the ankle shows a partial cartilage defect (size: 10 cm2) in the ankle joint. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer a new treatment option for her condition. She has no known allergies to bovine protein or gentamicin antibiotics. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of autoimmune disease or cancer. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and make regular visits to the hospital for examination and evaluation.

31 yo F diagnosed with Provoked localized Vulvodynia 3 years ago. Patient reports severe pain with vestibular touch and attempted vaginal entry. Patient has been avoiding sexual activity due to pain. Physical examination shows varying degree of vestibular erythema and a positive Q-tip test. Patient has tried several treatments including topical lidocaine, oral gabapentin and amitriptyline without significant improvement. Patient is not pregnant, uses effective contraception and is not interested in becoming pregnant during the study period. No known Nifedipine allergy. No medical diseases. Willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of topical Nifedipine cream for the treatment of Provoked localized Vulvodynia.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the presence of malignancy in the breast tissue. She noticed a lump in her breast about 3 months ago and decided to seek medical attention. She has no history of breast cancer in her family. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. Physical examination revealed a 2 cm palpable mass in the upper outer quadrant of her left breast. There are no palpable axillary lymph nodes, but the ultrasound showed a suspicious lymph node measuring 5mm. She has no history of claustrophobia or pacemaker implantation. She has not undergone any neoadjuvant chemo-, immune- or endocrine therapy in the past. She has not had any axillary surgery or treatment in the past.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with gastric adenocarcinoma. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medication for both conditions. He has no prior history of cancer and has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 70 and a life expectancy of more than 2 months. He has measurable disease according to the RECIST criteria. His lab results show that his ALT and AST levels are within normal limits, his serum albumin level is 3.2g/dL, serum AKP is 1.8 times ULN, serum creatinine is within normal limits, and his bilirubin level is 1.1 ULN. His WBC count is 4,200/mm3, absolute neutrophil count is 2,800/mm3, platelet count is 110,000/mm3, and his Hb level is 11.5g/dl. He has no brain metastasis and has never been treated with any systemic therapy for metastatic gastric cancer. He is able to take oral medication and has no contraindications for nuclear magnetic resonance imaging. He has no allergies to any of the investigational agents. He has no severe heart disease, but he has mild neuropathy. He has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

8 year old male with cerebral palsy and intellectual disability, presenting with a history of dental caries, difficulty eating, and pain with oral hygiene. Parents report difficulty in maintaining oral hygiene due to the child's limited mobility and behavioral issues. The child has had previous dental procedures under general anesthesia, including extractions and fillings. The child is on a soft food diet and has a BMI within normal range for age and height. The family has a home phone and is able to be contacted for follow-up appointments. The child's medical history is significant for cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, and a history of seizures for which he is on anticonvulsant medication. The child is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The parents have provided consent for the child to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea by a physician. He weighs 85 kg and has been using a nasal pillows mask for the past 6 months to treat his condition. He is currently compliant with PAP therapy, using it for at least 4 hours per night for 80% of nights. The patient is fluent in English and is able to provide informed consent. He does not possess any anatomical or physiological conditions that make PAP therapy inappropriate. He is not currently diagnosed with any respiratory disease or CO2 retention. The patient is interested in trying a new nasal pillows mask to treat his OSA and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 52-year-old woman has been diagnosed with invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva that is greater than 1mm in thickness as measured from the nearest rete peg. The tumor size is between 2-6 cm. She has no history of any other invasive malignancy within the past 5 years except for non-melanomatous skin cancer. The patient has not undergone any prior cancer therapy that contraindicates the therapy in this study. She has no known hypersensitivity to phenylethane compounds. The patient has not undergone any prior groin dissection. On physical examination, there are no grossly suspicious or inflamed groin nodes. The patient's GOG is between 0-3, and her life expectancy is not specified. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate.

A 12-year-old male, diagnosed with neuroblastoma, has undergone standard first-line therapy and has been found to have disease progression. The patient has been referred to participate in a clinical trial testing Y-90 DOTA/Retinoic Acid for Neuroblastoma and Neuroendocrine Tumor (NET). The patient has measurable, evaluable disease that has either never been irradiated or has been previously irradiated and has since demonstrated progression based on COG response criteria. The patient has normal organ and marrow function, with platelets >100,000/mm3, total bilirubin <1.5 x nl for age and weight, and creatinine <1.0 for children <5 years of age; <1.2 for children 5-10 years of age; <1.7 for >10 years. The patient has a cardiac ejection fraction > 50% by bi-plane method of echo. The patient has not received any other investigational anti-neoplastic therapies for the treatment of the refractory somatostatin-receptor positive tumor during the course of the study, excluding somatostatin analogues and bisphosphonates. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation. The patient understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is in good health and is not currently taking any medications. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m² and is a non-smoker. She is interested in participating in a research study to evaluate the sensitivity of pharmacokinetics to differences in particle size distribution of nasal sprays. The patient has never had any history of lung, liver, or respiratory diseases, and has never had any nasal surgery or known clinically relevant abnormalities. She is not pregnant and uses highly effective methods of contraception. The patient reports no allergies or sensitivities to activated charcoal or benzalkonium chloride. She has not used any systemic, topical, inhaled, or nasal corticosteroids within the past 30 days and has not used any nasally administered products within the past 30 days. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and attend scheduled study visits.

A 34-year-old woman has been diagnosed with chronic idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) six months ago. Despite standard doses of rituximab treatment, her platelet count has not improved and remained below 30,000/mL. She has not received more than two courses of rituximab and has not received cyclophosphamide in the last three months. She had a splenectomy five months ago, and her platelet counts improved to 80,000/mL for a short period but then declined again. Her last physical exam and lab study was performed yesterday, and the results showed the following: A healthy young woman, non-icteric, alert, and oriented to time, place, and person. Weight: 55 kg Height: 160 cm BP: 110/70 HR: 80/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 12 g/dL WBC: 7500/mm3 (Neutrophil: 4400/mm3) Plt: 25,000/mL AST: 25 U/L ALT: 35 U/L Alk P: 85 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl ESR: 30 mm/hr. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has given written informed consent.

50-year-old male who was diagnosed with poliomyelitis at the age of 5. He was able to achieve partial functional recovery after the acute phase but has since developed slowly progressive muscle weakness and decreased endurance, with generalized fatigue, muscle atrophy, and muscle and joint pain. These symptoms have persisted for at least one year, and other neuromuscular, medical, and skeletal abnormalities have been excluded as causes of the symptoms. The patient is ambulatory and able to walk 150 meters in the 6-minute walking distance test. He has not participated in any other therapeutic trial in the past three months and has not used L-citrulline or L-arginine during this time. He has no known hypersensitivity to L-citrulline, and there is no known or suspected malignancy. The patient has no chronic disease or relevant limitation of renal, liver, or heart function according to the investigator's discretion. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has a calculated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) above 30 ml/min.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman experiencing pain and tension in her jaw. She reports discomfort when opening her mouth wide or chewing, and has noticed that the muscles in her face feel tight and sore. She has a history of temporomandibular disorder (TMD) and has been diagnosed with RDC/TMD 1a and 1b. She has tried various treatments in the past, including physical therapy and pain medications, but has not found significant relief. She is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or medical conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a new treatment for TMD. She is willing to undergo surface electromyography to measure muscle tension and pain intensity, and is willing to use a topical ointment containing bee venom or a placebo for 14 days. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 27-year-old active male who sustained a non-contact injury to his right knee while playing soccer. He reports that he felt a popping sensation in his knee followed by severe pain and swelling. He is unable to bear weight on the affected leg and has significant instability in the knee joint. MRI shows a complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) with no other significant ligamentous injuries or meniscal tears. He has no history of prior knee surgeries or other significant medical conditions. The patient is highly motivated to return to his previous level of physical activity and is willing to participate in the study to compare the use of double bundle tibialis anterior allograft or quadruple bundle hamstring allograft in ACL reconstruction.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has undergone a unilateral skin sparing mastectomy for breast cancer. She has had a DIEP flap breast reconstruction immediately following the mastectomy. Her oncologist has recommended adjuvant post-mastectomy radiotherapy (PMRT) due to her high risk of chest wall recurrence. She is considering whether to undergo PMRT with her DIEP flap breast reconstruction or to delay the radiotherapy until after a subsequent delayed DIEP flap reconstruction. She is willing to participate in a study that investigates the effect of radiotherapy on DIEP flap reconstructions. She has no contraindications for participation in the study and is able to stand for the 3D imaging and complete the English language questionnaire and interview.

A 50-year-old woman with a history of thyroid cancer. The patient underwent a total thyroidectomy with neck dissection followed by radioactive iodine therapy. However, she developed disease progression with lung metastases and is no longer responding to radioiodine therapy. A recent CT scan showed an increase in the size of the lung metastases. The patient is asymptomatic and has an ECOG performance status of 1. Laboratory analysis is remarkable for elevated thyroglobulin levels. She has a history of hypertension and has been well controlled on an ACE inhibitor. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. Her cardiac function is normal, and she has no history of arrhythmias. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. She has no history of allergy to pasireotide or everolimus. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

26F with a history of cannabis use disorder presents with symptoms of cannabis withdrawal, including irritability, restlessness, insomnia, decreased appetite, and anxiety. She reports attempting to quit cannabis use in the past but experiencing withdrawal symptoms that led to relapse. She is currently unemployed and has a history of depression and anxiety, but is currently not taking any medications for these conditions. She reports no other substance use disorders or medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She speaks English fluently and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including not driving while receiving medication. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and is on a reliable contraceptive.

The patient is a 70-year-old retired teacher who lives with her husband. She has a history of knee and hip osteoarthritis that causes pain and stiffness, making it difficult for her to perform daily activities such as walking, climbing stairs, and standing for long periods. She also has hypertension and hyperlipidemia that are managed with medication. She reports feeling generally good otherwise, but recognizes the importance of increasing her physical activity level. She is interested in participating in a program that can help her achieve this goal and improve her overall health. She does not have a history of chest pain or loss of balance, and has not had any recent surgeries or significant injuries. She is able to hear and see well, and has not experienced any recent falls. She is willing to commit to making a change in her physical activity level over the next 3 months.

A 25-year-old woman, fluent in English, presents to the emergency department with suicidal thoughts and a recent suicide attempt. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has been receiving outpatient treatment for the past year. She is currently unemployed and lives alone. She reports feeling hopeless and overwhelmed, with a lack of social support. She denies any current substance abuse. On examination, she appears tearful and distressed, with a flat affect. She has no acute medical issues and is hemodynamically stable. She meets the inclusion criteria for the CAMS-RAS feasibility study and does not meet the exclusion criteria.

23 year old healthy male with no significant medical history, no known allergies, and no medication use or recreational drug use. The patient has a BMI within the range of 20kg/m²~27kg/m² and is normotensive, with SBP ranging between 90 and 140 mmHg, and DBP ranging between 60 and 100 mmHg. The patient's pulse rate ranges between 45 and 100 bpm. The patient is able and willing to sign the informed consent form to participate voluntarily and able to comply with the trial requirements. The patient is available for follow-up visits and willing to provide blood samples during the study period. The patient has not had any clinically significant hepatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, endocrine, psychiatric, hematooncologic, or cardiovascular disease. The patient has not had any skin diseases or grafts that could affect drug absorption. The patient has not used any investigational product in a previous clinical trial within 60 days of the screening test and has not donated blood within 60 days prior to the screening test.

This clinical trial is seeking young healthy volunteers between the ages of 18 and 40 who are right-handed and native English speakers. Individuals with a history of neurological disease, post-traumatic stress disorder, other psychiatric disorders, or a history of physical or sexual abuse may not participate. The trial involves utilizing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to identify brain regions involved in performing certain tasks, especially those involving emotions. Participants will undergo MRI scanning while performing tasks involving the viewing of pictures on a screen, some of which may be violent or pornographic. The purpose of the study is to localize the neural regions and systems mediating the forms of knowledge representations hypothesized to be stored in the human prefrontal cortex. The data obtained in these studies will be used to constrain theories of frontal lobe function and to provide evidence for the role of specific frontal cortex sectors in specific cognitive functions.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman with a history of alopecia areata. She has had hair loss for the past year, with multiple patches of hair loss on her scalp. She has tried various treatments, including corticosteroid injections and topical immunotherapy, but has not seen any improvement. She is frustrated with her hair loss and feels self-conscious about her appearance. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any significant medical history. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and she drinks alcohol occasionally. Her physical exam is unremarkable, except for the hair loss on her scalp. Her blood tests are within normal limits, including liver and kidney function tests. She is not pregnant and is not taking any immunosuppressive medications. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if Stem Cell Educator therapy can help improve her hair loss.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who regularly visits her local community pharmacy for her medication refills. She has a history of asthma and seasonal allergies, and her medications include an inhaler and an antihistamine. She has not received any vaccines in the past year and is unsure if she is up-to-date on all her recommended adult vaccinations. She is interested in learning more about which vaccinations she may need and is open to receiving them at the pharmacy if recommended by the pharmacist. She is willing to participate in the study and provide consent for her vaccination history to be reviewed and monitored by the pharmacist utilizing the innovative care model.

A 65-year-old woman with a history of atrial fibrillation has been prescribed a novel oral anticoagulant drug (NOAC) by her doctor. The patient is concerned about taking the medication due to a fear of side effects and potential complications. She has previously taken warfarin but found the process of monitoring her blood levels to be inconvenient and time-consuming. The patient is generally compliant with her medication regimen but has a tendency to forget to take her pills at times. She is interested in learning more about the medication and would appreciate regular follow-up with a pharmacist to ensure she is taking it correctly and safely. The patient is willing to participate in a study that examines the impact of pharmacist interventions on behavioral patterns in patients using NOACs. She hopes that her participation will not only benefit her own health but also contribute to the development of better strategies to improve the effectiveness and safety of NOACs for other patients.

62 y/o male stroke survivor with right-sided hemiparesis due to a left-sided ischemic stroke 4 years ago. Able to grasp and hold a stylus for the duration of the experiments. Passive motion throughout the right upper extremity within 20° of normal. Affected side is dominant. No lesion in brainstem or cerebellum. No presence of other neuro-disease impairing motor skills. Able to understand 3-step directions. No pain, orthopedic condition or impaired corrected vision that would alter reaching. No history of incomplete spinal cord injury. No medical, orthopedic, neurological, or uncorrected visual condition that would limit the ability to participate in upper extremity testing.

A 12 yo boy who has been recently diagnosed with ulcerative colitis. He has been experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding for the past few months. His pediatric gastroenterologist has determined that he requires anti-tumor necrosis factor-alpha antibody (infliximab) therapy due to the severity of his condition. The patient has not undergone any other treatment for his ulcerative colitis prior to this study. The patient and his parents have provided written consent to participate in the study. He has no history of significant medical conditions and meets all of the eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 28 year-old woman who has been struggling with opioid use disorder for several years. She began using opioids recreationally in her late teens and her use has escalated over time. She has tried to quit on her own several times, but has been unsuccessful. She is currently using heroin and fentanyl, and has experienced several overdoses in the past. She is motivated to quit using opioids and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help her overcome her addiction. She has no major psychiatric or medical conditions that would interfere with study procedures and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male veteran who served in the military for over 10 years. He was diagnosed with major depressive disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder, and panic disorder. He has been receiving treatment at the Ralph H. Johnson VAMC for several months but has not seen much improvement. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares different therapies for veterans with depression, PTSD, and panic disorder. He is willing to commit to 12 weekly 45- to 60-minute treatment sessions and complete pre-, mid-, and post-treatment assessments to track his progress through the study. He is able to provide informed consent for research participation and is not currently hospitalized or undergoing chemotherapy or radiation treatment.

A 24-year-old female university student with no significant medical history is interested in participating in a clinical trial related to eye health. She wears glasses with a prescription of -0.75 diopters in both eyes. She has no history of smoking or regular alcohol consumption. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 3 weeks and has not taken any medications in the last 3 weeks. She has not donated blood in the last 3 weeks. She is not currently pregnant nor planning to become pregnant during the trial period. She has never experienced any clinically significant illness in the past 3 weeks. She is excited to participate in the trial to contribute to the understanding of age-related macular degeneration and glaucoma.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of hypoglycemia for the past year. She reports that these episodes occur frequently, and she experiences symptoms such as sweating, tremors, and confusion. The patient states that she has tried to manage her symptoms with dietary changes and glucose monitoring, but has not been successful in preventing the episodes. She has no prior diagnosis of hyperinsulinemia, and her endocrinologist has recommended her for this clinical trial. The patient has no significant medical history, with the exception of a history of migraines managed with sumatriptan as needed. Her laboratory studies show a blood glucose level of 45 mg/dL at the time of her most recent episode, and a c-peptide level of 1.8 nmol/L. The patient has no significant liver disease or cardiac history. She is not currently pregnant or nursing, and is using a highly effective method of contraception. She provides written informed consent prior to treatment, and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study.

A 30-year-old male with second-degree burns on both arms and legs due to an industrial accident is admitted to the hospital. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and does not use illicit drugs. The patient has no history of psychiatric illness, and he is not taking any medications. He reports moderate pain and itch in his affected areas, with a score of 5 out of 10 on the Numerical Rating Scale for average itch or pain. The patient is able to read and understand English, and he is willing to participate in the study. He has been receiving pharmacologic therapy for burn related itch according to the standard itch protocol. The patient is able to provide informed consent for study participation. The patient is admitted to the hospital and is expected to be an inpatient for several days.

A 64-year-old man with a history of diverticulitis presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting. He is diagnosed with perforated diverticulitis with purulent peritonitis and is scheduled for emergency surgery. He has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He has no known allergies. His BMI is 27. He has been referred to participate in a national study evaluating clinical results and health outcomes in patients who have undergone emergency surgery for perforated diverticulitis with purulent peritonitis. The study will compare the traditional treatment of colon resection to laparoscopic lavage. The patient will be asked to provide informed consent and complete a questionnaire evaluating his health and well-being post-surgery.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who presented to the hospital with fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising. He was found to have low blood counts and a bone marrow biopsy was performed which showed acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Molecular testing revealed that he has an IDH1 mutation. He has no significant past medical history and has never received chemotherapy. He is married with two children and works as a carpenter. He is generally in good physical condition and is able to perform his daily activities without much difficulty. His performance status is ECOG 1. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who was diagnosed with bowel cancer that has advanced to the metastatic stage. He has previously undergone first-line treatment with oxaliplatin combined with fluorouracil, but unfortunately, the treatment has failed. The patient has one or more measurable lesions with the longest diameter of the spiral CT scan at least 10 mm, and the diameter of the conventional CT scan is at least 20 mm. The patient has an Eastern Cancer Cooperative Group (ECOG) general status score of 0-2. Bone marrow capacity, liver and kidney function of the patient have reached the required criteria. The patient has not previously used irinotecan or anti-egfr therapy for advanced colorectal cancer. The patient's RAS, B-RAF gene is wild type. The patient is willing to take effective contraception as he has fertility. The patient has not experienced any significant heart disease, neurological or psychiatric problems, severe infection, and active disseminated intravascular coagulation. The patient has not previously had any malignant tumors within the last 5 years. The patient is not currently experiencing any chronic intestinal diseases, infectious intestinal diseases, or intestinal obstruction. The patient is willing and able to comply with all protocol requirements and procedures.

A 46-year-old woman diagnosed with cervical cancer 3 years ago is experiencing recurrent cancer that has progressed despite prior systemic chemotherapy. She has a history of smoking, but quit 2 years ago. She is married and has two children. Her past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is not allergic to any medication. She reports no significant abdominal pain or bleeding. Her last Pap test was 6 months ago, and showed abnormal cells. Her physical examination is unremarkable except for a palpable mass in the cervix. The ultrasound and CT scan confirmed the recurrence of cervical cancer with multiple lymph node involvement. Her current performance status is 1. Her blood test results show normal kidney and liver function. She is not currently pregnant or nursing. She is willing to use contraception during the study period. Her ECG shows no evidence of significant cardiac disease. She has no history of brain metastases, hepatitis B or C. She is willing to undergo regular follow-up visits and blood tests.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and has been receiving continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD) for 6 months. He currently uses a specific solution for CAPD and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new experimental solution. He is married and works as a software engineer. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He has no history of peritonitis or other serious illnesses. His blood pressure is well controlled with medications. His labs: Creatinine: 6.8 mg/dL, BUN: 65 mg/dL, Potassium: 4.2 mmol/L, Calcium: 8.4 mg/dL, Phosphorus: 4.9 mg/dL, Hemoglobin: 11.8 g/dL. He is interested in participating in the trial to help advance the development of new treatments for end-stage renal disease.

A 45-year-old male patient presents with partial edentulism in the posterior mandible. He is a non-smoker and has no history of diabetes or metabolic bone disease. The patient has no known history of therapeutic radiation to the head and is not currently pregnant. He has agreed to return for each follow-up visit and is physically able to tolerate surgical and restorative procedures. The patient has at least 1mm of bone available at the buccal and lingual aspect of the implant and at least 1mm of bone below the apex. The inter-arch distance is greater than 7mm and bone width is at least 6mm, with a bone height of at least 11mm. The patient is a good candidate for the placement of the Osseotite Prevail implant to support a short fixed bridge with immediate occlusal loading.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has had a history of asthma for the past 5 years. He has been using an inhaled glucocorticoid (GCS) at a dose of 400 µg/day for the past 3 months to control his symptoms. He experiences wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath occasionally, and the symptoms interfere with his daily activities. He has never smoked and does not have any known allergies to medications. He is seeking a better treatment option for his persistent asthma and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of Symbicort Single Inhaler Therapy with his current treatment.

A 50-year-old male with Type II diabetes mellitus was referred to the clinic by his primary care physician for the management of his diabetic foot ulcer. The patient has had diabetes for over 10 years and has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol levels. His glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level was 10% during his last visit to the primary care physician. He has been following his physician's advice for diabetic management which includes diet, exercise, and medication. The patient's foot ulcer has been present for over 3 weeks and has not shown any signs of improvement with standard of care treatment. The ulcer is on his left foot, measures approximately 2 cm2, and is located on the plantar surface of the foot. The patient has no known allergies to any medications or medical products. He is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and maintain the required dressing changes and off-loading for the location of the ulcer. He has not participated in any other clinical trials involving device or systemically administered investigational study drug/treatment within 30 days of randomization. The patient has adequate vascular perfusion of the affected limb as determined by an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) of 0.8.

A 45-year-old woman came to the hospital with vaginal bleeding and lower back pain for the past 3 months. She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has not had a Pap smear in the past 2 years. Pelvic examination revealed a 4 cm cervical mass with parametrial involvement. Biopsy confirmed squamous cell carcinoma. MRI showed a cervical mass extending into the parametrium, with no evidence of distant metastasis. The patient has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. She has a BMI of 25 and is physically active. Her family history is negative for cancer. Her laboratory results are within the normal range. A clinical staging workup revealed stage IIa2 cervical cancer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive neoadjuvant therapy before radical hysterectomy and pelvic lymphadenectomy.

A 12-year-old Caucasian male presents with a diagnosis of Crohn's disease. He has been experiencing chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss for the past 6 months. His medications include mesalamine and prednisone, which have provided some relief but not complete remission of symptoms. He has not had any surgeries related to his condition. His growth and development have been affected by the disease, as he has lost weight and is below the 10th percentile for his age and height. He reports decreased quality of life due to his symptoms, including missing school and social activities. He and his family are interested in exploring alternative treatment options to complement his conventional medications. He is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not use recreational drugs or alcohol.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female with a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes for the past 3 years. She currently manages her diabetes using an insulin infusion pump and rapid-acting insulin. She has a history of good glycemic control with a HbA1c of 7.2%. She has no significant medical history other than diabetes and is not currently taking any medications other than insulin. She is willing to participate in a study that compares the speed with which insulin and glucagon are absorbed when administered via traditional needle injection versus an injection device that uses microneedles to deliver medication into the top layer of the skin. She is able to consume a sufficient amount of carbohydrates to cover 5 units of rapid-acting insulin and has a stimulated C-peptide level of less than 0.1 nmol/L after a liquid mixed meal tolerance test. She does not have any exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a previous diagnosis of high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer. She has received platinum-containing chemotherapy for primary disease and is currently in remission. Her cancer was found to be platinum-sensitive with no recurrence within 12 months of last receipt of platinum/chemotherapy. Her histology is high-grade serious. She is willing to undergo HRD testing. She has not received bevacizumab or other anti-angiogenic therapy and has not participated in a PARP inhibitor trial after relapse. The patient has not had any major injuries or surgery in the past 21 days prior to starting study treatment. She has no other major medical illnesses that would interfere with her participation in the study. She has a performance status of 0-2 and adequate organ function. She is able to take oral medications and has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. She has no concurrent cancer therapy or concurrent treatment with an investigational agent. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use adequate birth control for the duration of the study. She does not have a history of significant thromboembolic events, cerebral vascular accident, transient ischemic attack, or subarachnoid hemorrhage within the past 3 months. She does not have a history of clinically significant hemorrhage in the past 3 months. She has no known uncontrolled hypersensitivity to the investigational drugs and does not have a history of a major thromboembolic event, uncontrolled and/or symptomatic CNS metastasis or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. She has no significant cardiovascular diseases, including uncontrolled hypertension or clinically relevant cardiac arrhythmia. She has no radiographic evidence of cavitation or necrotic tumors with invasion of adjacent major blood vessels.

The patient is a 6-month-old baby boy who was born at 40 weeks gestational age and is currently in good health. The baby is breastfed and sleeps in a separate crib in the same room as his parents. The parents report that the baby has difficulty falling asleep at night and wakes up frequently during the night, leading to sleep deprivation for both the baby and themselves. They have tried various methods to help the baby sleep better, such as playing soft music, using a pacifier, and rocking him to sleep, but none have been successful. The parents are interested in participating in a sleep hygiene-based intervention program for their baby to help improve his sleep patterns and overall well-being. They are fluent in Chinese and are willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

5-year-old male patient with developmental delay and a history of enteral feeding intolerance on standard polymeric formulas was referred to a pediatric facility. The patient has a history of cerebral palsy and has been dependent on enteral feeding to meet 90% or more of their energy needs. The patient has been receiving enteral nutrition with an intact protein formula for two weeks prior to the switch to a Peptide based formula due to intolerance. Medical records indicate that the patient has had difficulty meeting enteral nutrition goals and has experienced gastrointestinal symptoms. The patient's medical history is notable for recurrent upper respiratory infections but no active infections are present at the time of admission. Comprehensive medical evaluation has been performed and the patient is stable with no recent abdominal surgeries or changes in tube position/placement.

Patient is a 12-year-old boy from the United States who has been diagnosed with primary motor stereotypy. He has been experiencing repetitive arm flapping, hand waving, or finger wiggling movements for at least 4 months, occurring at least 10 times a day. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical, neurological or psychiatric conditions. He has not taken any medications that affect the central nervous system, including tranquilizers or psychotropic drugs, in the past month. The patient and their legal guardian have been informed about the clinical trial and have given their consent for participation.

A 28-year-old female presented with symptoms of a common cold, including a runny nose, cough, and sore throat. She was prescribed Amoxicillin by her primary care physician and is scheduled to start the medication tomorrow morning. She has a refrigerator at home and telephone access. She is fluent in English and is able to speak and write in Spanish. She has no chronic conditions and is not taking any other medications except for over-the-counter anti-pyretic medicines. She has no known allergies to strawberries or penicillin class antibiotics. She is not currently experiencing diarrhea and has no history of lactose intolerance. Her baseline physical exam shows normal vital signs, including a systolic blood pressure of 120, diastolic blood pressure of 80, oxygen saturation of 99%, pulse rate of 80, and respiratory rate of 16. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the safety of BB-12 supplemented strawberry yogurt for healthy adults on antibiotics.

A 58-year-old man who has been a heavy smoker for over 30 years came to the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath and coughing. He has been diagnosed with severe emphysema, and his pulmonary function tests showed a severe reduction in lung function. He has tried various treatments and medications, but nothing seems to provide him with relief. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the IBV Valve System. He has mostly upper lobe emphysema and is able to participate in standard exercise testing. He is committed to abstaining from smoking for the required duration of the trial and is ready to participate in multiple visits to a medical center for health assessment tests. He understands that the trial is randomized and blinded, and he is willing to complete the required follow-up visits during the study period.

45 year old male with no significant medical history other than mild hypertension controlled with lifestyle modifications. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. He takes no medications and has no known allergies. He is willing to provide informed consent to participate in this study.
