A 15-year-old male high school student presents to the emergency department after a head injury during a football game. He reports being tackled and hitting his head on the ground. He reports a headache, dizziness, and nausea. The patient's vital signs are stable, and his neurological exam is significant for mild confusion and delayed verbal response. The patient is diagnosed with a concussion, and the medical team recommends rest and close monitoring for the next few weeks. The patient is approached about participating in a research study to further investigate the use of the BrainPulse device in detecting concussions. The patient is interested in participating and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. The patient signs the informed consent along with his parent/legal guardian and agrees to participate in the study, which will involve BrainPulse recordings for 21 days following the initial injury. The patient will be asked to complete a symptom checklist and undergo physical examination and BrainPulse recordings during multiple visits throughout the study period.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer two months ago. The biopsy confirmed that her cancer is HER2-negative (0 or 1+ by immuno-histochemical (IHC) or non-amplified by FISH). She has no history of cardiac disease, arrhythmias, or uncontrolled paroxysmal diseases, and her Karnofsky performance status (KPS) is above 70. She has not received any systemic cancer therapy and is not currently participating in any other investigational trials. She has at least one measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 and her life expectancy is estimated to be more than 12 weeks. She is able to understand and willing to sign the Institutional Review Board (IRB) approved written informed consent document. Her laboratory values for ANC, PLT, Hb, TBiL, AST, ALT, ALP, and Scr are within normal limits. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she does not have any known allergies to investigational drugs.

This is a 55 year-old female with type-2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 2 years ago. She has a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in any regular exercise. She does not smoke and her blood pressure is currently well controlled. She has not lost more than 5% of her total body weight in the last 6 months. She does not have any alcohol addiction in the last 12 months and does not use insulin hormone. She does not have any neuropathy or retinopathy. She has not had any acute cardiac event in the last 6 weeks and has not had any disease in the last month.

This is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) six months ago. She received induction chemotherapy followed by consolidation chemotherapy and then underwent reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) and allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using fludarabine/busulfan (FLU/BU) conditioning. She received graft versus host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis consisting of tacrolimus/sirolimus (SRL). Currently, she is between day +60 and day +90 after allogeneic HCT. She meets all inclusion criteria for enrollment in this phase II trial, including a diagnosis of ALL, planned allogeneic HCT using FLU/BU conditioning, planned GVHD prophylaxis consisting of TAC/SRL, and less than or equal to 5% blasts on bone marrow examination within 60 days of starting conditioning. She also meets all inclusion criteria prior to ibrutinib administration, including age >=18 years, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of =<2, and adequate organ function. She does not meet any exclusion criteria for enrollment in this trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear while playing basketball. She has been experiencing severe pain in her right knee for the past few months and has difficulty walking or standing for long periods of time. She has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. She has been advised by her orthopedic surgeon to undergo elective day-orthopedic surgery for the repair of her ACL, with or without posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) and medial collateral ligament (MCL) damage. She is willing and able to provide informed consent for the clinical trial. She has not used any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID's), steroids, anti-emetics, or opioids. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. The patient is eager to participate in the clinical trial to help improve the management of postoperative pain after orthopedic surgery.

A 55-year-old man with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption was recently diagnosed with esophageal cancer. He underwent an abdominal-thoracic esophagectomy with radical lymphadenectomy. Following the surgery, he was admitted to the ICU due to complications related to the surgery, including respiratory distress and a high SOFA score. His inflammatory markers, including interleukin-6, were significantly elevated. He has not participated in any other interventional trials and is not currently taking high dose steroids or immunosuppressants. He does not have any known diseases of the immune system. He is willing to participate in the trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for two years without success. She has been diagnosed with infertility due to a blockage in her fallopian tubes, and has decided to undergo in vitro fertilization (IVF) with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) at a fertility clinic. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has a regular menstrual cycle and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has undergone previous fertility treatments, but none have resulted in a successful pregnancy. She is scheduled to undergo IVF with ICSI and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of laser-assisted ICSI versus conventional ICSI. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

This is a 24 month-old female who is in need of at least one immunization. She has an address in a specified study county listed in the state immunization registry. The child’s parents have not opted out of the Colorado Immunization Information System (CIIS). The child has not received all of the recommended immunizations for her age and is eligible to participate in the study. The parents are interested in helping to improve the effectiveness of immunization reminder/recall methods and are willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who was diagnosed with focal hand dystonia two years ago. He has been receiving onabotulinumtoxinA injections for the past year and a half and has experienced some improvement in his symptoms. He complains of involuntary movements in his right hand that make it difficult to write and perform other fine motor tasks. He reports that the severity of his symptoms has been relatively stable over the past several months. He is currently taking no other medications for his condition. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare two different techniques for administering the onabotulinumtoxinA injections. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. She has been scheduled to undergo hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. She is currently undergoing standard medications and is in otherwise good health. She has no known orthopedic or neurological issues that could affect her functional capacity. She is a non-smoker and has no history of asthma or COPD. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to attend rehabilitation sessions. She has no acute infections or pneumonia and has no contraindications to exercise training. Her physical activity level is low due to her medical condition, but she is motivated to improve her physical condition.

A 50-year-old non-smoking male came to the clinic with a history of bronchiectasis exacerbations (BEs) for the past 2 years. He experiences shortness of breath, coughing, and chest tightness. He is clinically stable and has not had any acute upper respiratory tract infections for the past 4 consecutive weeks. He has been treated with ambroxol (30mg thrice daily) and chest physiotherapy (10 min, twice daily). He is not suffering from any other systemic illnesses, nor is he taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the guidelines.

The patient is a 68-year-old Chinese woman who has experienced shortness of breath and fatigue for the past six months. She has a history of hypertension, but otherwise, she is in good health. Upon examination, her blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and her heart rate is 80 beats per minute. A heart murmur is detected during auscultation. Echocardiography shows that she has moderate aortic stenosis, with a valve area of 1.2cm2 and a mean pressure gradient of 25mmHg. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to learn more about her condition and receive the best available treatment.

Patient is a 40-year-old man with end-stage renal failure secondary to chronic glomerulonephritis. He has been on hemodialysis for the past two years and is currently listed for living donor kidney transplantation. The patient's blood type is B, and he has high titers of anti-A antibodies (IgG titer of 1:512 and IgM titer of 1:32). The patient has no evidence of HLA sensitization, and pre-transplant crossmatching is negative. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the safety and efficacy of a novel desensitization protocol using combined apheresis for ABO-incompatible kidney transplantation. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. The patient understands and has provided signed written informed consent to participate in the study.

65-year-old male with symptomatic aortic valve disease, presenting with shortness of breath, chest pain, and syncope. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and aortic valve stenosis. The patient is eligible for surgical AVR but may also be a candidate for the less invasive transcatheter alternative to surgical AVR. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the expected health outcomes and personalized decision assistance tools associated with both surgical and transcatheter AVR. The patient is not excluded from the study based on endocarditis or emergency/salvage status.

The patient is a 58-year-old man with a history of hypertension. He has been prescribed antihypertensive medication but has struggled to remember to take it consistently. He has a Priority Health Care Health Insurance Coverage. He has access to a cell phone and uses it on a daily basis to send text messages. He has access to the internet. He reports no heart failure, no need for artificial oxygen, no cancer, and no kidney disease requiring dialysis. He has no history of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or dementia. He is interested in participating in a study that will help improve his medication adherence and blood pressure control.

The patient is a 25-year-old female diagnosed with Down Syndrome since childhood. She has no significant medical history, aside from the diagnosis of Down Syndrome. She takes no medications and her last physical examination was done 6 months ago which showed normal findings. She has no history of fractures or falls. She is physically active and enjoys walking daily. She is alert and oriented, with no acute distress. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, heart rate is 80 bpm, and BMI is 25. Her abdomen is soft and non-tender, and her extremities show no signs of edema or deformities. She is accompanied by her legally authorized representative who is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and has been scheduled for off-pump coronary artery bypass surgery. He has a history of smoking and quit two years ago. He also has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it, which has been well controlled. He has never had any previous surgeries or major medical conditions. His physical examination is unremarkable, except for slightly elevated blood pressure. The laboratory tests show normal values except for mild dyslipidemia. He has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a BMI of 45, diagnosed with morbid obesity. He has tried various non-surgical weight loss treatments in the past, including diet and exercise, but has been unable to achieve significant weight loss. He does not have any endocrine disorders or other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study. He is psychologically stable and fully understands the study protocol. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. He has not undergone any previous surgeries for morbid obesity. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the benefits of the laparoscopic greater curvature plication with a single gastro-ileal anastomosis on weight loss and postoperative complications.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of significant myopia (-8.75 D OU) and a recent diagnosis of a full-thickness macular hole in his right eye. His best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in that eye is 20/400 (logMAR 1.3). He reports central distortion and difficulty with fine visual tasks such as reading and driving. His OCT shows a macular hole with a minimum diameter of 550 μm. He has no history of prior vitreous surgery, cystoid macular edema, or retinal detachment. He is otherwise healthy with no other ocular or systemic conditions that would preclude him from participating in the study. He is interested in exploring treatment options to improve his visual function and has provided informed consent for the clinical trial.

A 60-year-old man was diagnosed with lung cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. He underwent first-line chemotherapy, but his disease progressed. He is currently experiencing shortness of breath, cough, fatigue, and loss of appetite. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. He has never smoked and does not drink alcohol. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he has no cardiac symptoms. His ECOG performance status is 1. Imaging tests show measurable lung lesions. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options.

A 35-year-old man with a diagnosis of Schizophrenia has been stable on his medication regimen for the past 6 weeks. He works as a librarian and lives alone. He has a high school diploma and has never been married. He has no history of substance abuse or dependence. He has no significant medical illnesses and takes no other medications. He has no history of allergic rhinitis, and no known hypersensitivity to oxytocin. He is not currently pregnant nor is he planning to become pregnant in the near future. He has no history of cognitive impairment and has the ability to provide informed consent.

A 55 year old male patient was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer after undergoing colonoscopy and biopsy. The patient had previously received treatment with fluorouracil and irinotecan chemotherapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. The patient is in generally good health and has an ECOG performance status of 1. Hematopoietic function is within normal limits, with a granulocyte count of 4,500/mm^3, a platelet count of 180,000/mm^3, and a hemoglobin level of 12 g/dL. The patient's liver function tests are also normal, with a bilirubin level of 0.8 mg/dL and AST/ALT levels within normal limits. Renal function is also normal, with a creatinine level of 0.9 mg/dL and creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min. The patient has no active infections and no other malignancies within the past 5 years. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III breast cancer. She has undergone neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by a mastectomy and axillary dissection. Her pathology report revealed a residual disease of 2 cm in size and involvement of two out of ten lymph nodes. She is scheduled for radiation therapy and adjuvant chemotherapy. She has no history of autoimmune disorders or other medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. A CT scan revealed a target tumor lesion in her liver which is accessible for percutaneous access. She has been off any anticoagulant medication for the past month and her platelet count, PT/INR and liver function tests are normal. She has no known allergies to bovine or murine products. She has signed the study-specific informed consent and agrees to use adequate contraception.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman scheduled for an elective orthopedic surgery on her right knee. She has a history of osteoarthritis and has been experiencing knee pain and stiffness for the past year. She has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has a BMI of 26 kg/m2. The estimated duration of anesthesia for her surgery is 2 hours. She will receive intravenous narcotic analgesics (Sufentanil and Remifentanil) during the surgery and will use an electronic intravenous analgesia pump after the surgery. She has provided informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 5 years. She has been treated with Tocilizumab for the past year along with a DMARD and takes 5mg of corticoids daily. Her recent blood tests show that she is in remission according to the ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria with a DAS 28 score of 2.4. She has not had any destructive structural progression in the past year on the hand and feet x-rays. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the feasibility of a step down strategy on Tocilizumab in RA patients in remission. She has given her informed consent to participate in the study and has been prescribed a stable dose. She is fluent in French and is affiliated with social security. She is not currently pregnant and has no surgical interventions programmed in the next 24 months.

The patient is a 30-year-old non-smoking female with a history of asthma symptoms including shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness. She has been using a SABA inhaler on an as-needed basis but has been experiencing worsening symptoms despite using her inhaler. She has been diagnosed with mild-to-moderate persistent asthma and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help with the management of her symptoms. She is otherwise healthy and has not used tobacco in the past year.

This is a 29-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA) who completed the ApoPharma study LA29-0207. She has a past medical history of hypertension and mild iron overload. She is currently on a stable dose of blood pressure medication. She has no history of neutropenia, agranulocytosis, or thrombocytopenia. She is able to complete T25FW and has a score of less than or equal to 5 minutes on the 9HPT. She has not experienced any serious adverse events or any other adverse events during the LA29-0207 study that would prevent her participation in the extension study. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. Her QTc interval is within normal limits. She has not been on any antioxidants prior to the start of study treatment. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and able to attend study appointments and evaluations.

50 year old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, who was admitted to the hospital for a minor surgical procedure that requires peripheral intravenous therapy. He has no significant past medical history other than hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well controlled with medication. He has no history of abnormal bleeding or clotting disorders and has no sensation abnormalities in his arms. He has not received IV therapy in the past 30 days, has not had any recent radiation or chemotherapy, and has no history of seizures or strokes. He is not sick and has not had any infections in the past 30 days. His temperature is within normal range. He has signed the consent form and his health form has been approved by his professional practitioner.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who underwent allogeneic bone marrow transplantation 6 months ago for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia. He has been experiencing chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) with symptoms including skin rash, dry eyes, and mouth, and chronic fatigue. He has been receiving treatment for cGVHD from his healthcare provider but still struggles with daily functioning due to his symptoms. He lives with his wife who is his primary caregiver and helps him with daily activities. The patient is able to speak and read English fluently and is willing to participate in an interview and complete questionnaires to share his experience with cGVHD. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

38-year-old female with a history of breast cancer and a positive BRCA1 mutation. The patient was diagnosed with stage II invasive ductal carcinoma in the left breast, as confirmed by core needle biopsy. Staging workup revealed no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and no significant comorbidities. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for her breast cancer. The patient is a Polish resident and has provided signed informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

Patient A is a 40-year-old mother of a 6-year-old boy with autism. She is currently working as a part-time accountant, but her main focus is taking care of her son. She spends more than 10 hours per week caring for her son, including attending therapy sessions, doctor's appointments, and helping him with daily activities. She reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the demands of caring for her son and balancing work and family responsibilities. She has no history of using psychotropic medication and has not experienced any changes in medication doses within the last year. She is interested in participating in the Cognitive Based Compassion Training (CBCT) program to learn skills to manage stress and improve her mental wellbeing. She is willing to commit to attending eight two-hour weekly long sessions and twenty-minute meditation sessions.

A 35-year-old woman with a BMI of 35 presents for the clinical trial. She has a history of class I obesity for the past 5 years and has been unsuccessful in losing weight with diet and exercise alone. She has no history of psychological disorders, eating disorders or drug/alcohol abuse. She is not pregnant or breast-feeding. She has a normal menstrual cycle and is not taking any medication known to affect appetite or induce weight loss. She has no history of bariatric surgery, metabolic diseases or malignancies. She has no gastrointestinal, kidney, liver, lung or cardiovascular disease. She does not have lactose intolerance. She is interested in participating in the study to help identify the maximum carbohydrate intake that is still associated with appetite suppression in a low energy diet.

A 55 year old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, diagnosed 8 years ago, with an HbA1c level of 8.3% at the last visit. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. He had a myocardial infarction 12 months ago, and has since undergone angioplasty and stenting. He has been compliant with his medication and has a good exercise routine. He is currently in good health and has no symptoms of cardiovascular disease.

35 yo male presenting with left testicular pain and discomfort. Physical examination revealed a palpable left varicocele. The patient underwent a scrotal ultrasound which confirmed the presence of a varicocele. Semen analysis revealed low sperm count with poor motility and morphology. The patient decided to undergo microsurgical varicocelectomy due to persistent pain and discomfort. The patient has no history of infertility and is not actively trying to conceive with his partner. He will be monitored for changes in his semen parameters after the surgery. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Allergic rhinitis - No previous surgeries.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic solid tumors with mismatched repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H). The patient has previously received or refused prior cancer therapy regimen(s) for advanced disease. The patient must have at least one measurable lesion as defined per RECIST Version (v) 1.1 and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status score of 0 or 1. The patient should not have had prior therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2 or any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T-cell co-stimulation or checkpoint pathways. Additionally, the patient should not have active leptomeningeal disease or uncontrolled brain metastasis, clinically significant pleural effusion, pericardial effusion or ascites, active autoimmune diseases or history of autoimmune diseases that may relapse, any active malignancy, or any condition that required systemic treatment with either corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medication ≤ 14 days before the first dose of study drug. The patient should also have adequate organ function and meet other protocol defined inclusion/exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55 year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic heart failure associated with cardiomegaly. He has been experiencing symptoms for over a year and has been classified as NYHA Class II. His left ventricular minor is less than 45% (measured by the Teicholtz method) and he has been diagnosed with inspiratory muscle weakness with a PiMáxima of less than 70% predicted. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² and has never smoked. He has no history of angina, myocardial infarction or heart surgery within the past three months. He has no orthopedic diseases or respiratory comorbidities such as asthma or COPD. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the regional pulmonary distribution volume and the influence of the thoracoabdominal enclosure system during quiet breathing and exercise for inspiratory muscle, and its correlation with functional data. The patient will use the Threshold Inspiratory Muscle Trainer for 3 minutes during the exercise to the inspiratory muscles. The patient will be monitored using opto-electronic plethysmography to measure the volume changes of the thoracoabdominal system. The results of this study will help to better understand the effects of inspiratory muscle dysfunction on patients with chronic heart failure, and may lead to improved treatment options for these patients.

The patient is a 4-year-old child who has been diagnosed with childhood apraxia of speech (CAS). The child has been experiencing inconsistent consonant and vowel errors over productions of repeated trials, difficulties forming accurate movement between sounds and syllables, and prosodic errors. The child has been experiencing at least four of the following characteristics: vowel errors, timing errors, phoneme distortions, articulatory groping, impaired volitional oral movement, reduced phonetic inventory, and poorer expressive than receptive language skills. The child has normal structure of the oral-peripheral mechanism and has passed a hearing screening conducted at 20 dB SPL at 500, 1000, 2000, and 4000 Hz. The child has not undergone prior DTTC treatment and is between the ages of 2.5 and 5 years old. The child does not have a positive history of neurological disorder, developmental disorder, genetic disorder, dysarthria, or fluency disorder.

Pt is a 45yo M, active duty military member with a history of recurrent skin and soft tissue infections. The patient was diagnosed with community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infection, which failed to respond to treatment with multiple antibiotics. Despite a prior history of allergy to aminoglycosides, the patient's medical team has determined that arbekacin is the only available treatment option for this multidrug-resistant organism. The patient has adequate venous access for intravenous administration of arbekacin and is willing to provide informed consent for participation in the clinical trial. The patient is sexually active and agrees to use an effective method of contraception during and after the treatment period.

This is a 54-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with Morbus Hodgkin. He has completed his first-line treatment and is currently in a stable phase for more than 6 months. He is being followed up by his treating physician and has been recommended to participate in this study for multidisciplinary follow-up. He has no other significant medical history and is capable of filling out electronic questionnaires. The patient has given informed consent for participation in this study.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been experiencing migraines for the past year. She typically experiences 5-6 migraines per month with a duration of 24-48 hours. The migraines significantly interfere with her daily routine, making it difficult for her to complete work tasks and care for her family. She has tried several over-the-counter medications and triptans for acute treatment, but the relief is temporary and she still experiences frequent migraines. She has not tried any preventive medications yet. She is in good general health, does not have any known allergies to medications and is using a reliable form of contraception. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and provides written informed consent prior to any screening procedures.

55 yo F with a personal history of breast cancer, treated with mastectomy, chemotherapy and radiation 2 years ago. Family history includes a maternal aunt with breast cancer and a paternal grandfather with colon cancer. Patient is interested in participating in a study that could help identify genetic and environmental factors that may have contributed to her cancer diagnosis and its treatment. She is also interested in learning about her risk of developing other cancers and how to reduce that risk. The patient is willing to provide a blood sample for genetic testing and is open to participating in additional research studies as well.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been suffering from excessive sweating in the armpit area for several years. The sweating is causing him significant embarrassment and affecting his quality of life, as he is constantly worried about sweat stains and body odor. He has tried various over-the-counter antiperspirants without success. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He leads an active lifestyle and exercises regularly. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new treatment for his condition.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is an active-duty military personnel. He had an amputation of his right leg below the knee due to a combat injury 6 months ago. Since then, he has been experiencing phantom limb pain, which is described as a burning sensation and shooting pain in the missing limb. He has been taking painkillers, but they do not seem to provide much relief. His medical history includes depression and anxiety, for which he is currently on medication. He has no other significant medical conditions or allergies. He speaks English fluently and is able to read and write. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who recently suffered a myocardial infarction (MI) and underwent angioplasty revascularization. He is currently in sinus rhythm and has a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 45% according to his Simpson Biplane echocardiography. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle, but he has expressed a willingness to improve his health and functional abilities after the MI. He does not have any comorbidities or contraindications to cardiac rehabilitation. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he does drink alcohol occasionally on the weekends. He is fluent in English and has a smartphone. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and will be randomized into one of two groups: a control group receiving standard rehabilitation, or a group that will receive a re-training program adapted to his heart rate variability (HRV) measured daily via a smartphone app. He will undergo a cardiopulmonary test, a walking test, and complete a SF36 questionnaire at the beginning and end of the program to assess his functional abilities and quality of life. The rehabilitation program will last 4 weeks with 5 training sessions per week, or 20 training sessions.

52-year-old male, diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, with a history of smoking tobacco for 30 years and consuming alcohol regularly for the past 20 years. The patient underwent surgery followed by radiation therapy and is currently in remission. He has expressed interest in participating in a study to help others who may be facing a similar diagnosis. He is covered by health insurance and able to provide written informed consent. His social and geographical situation allows him to undergo medical follow up. He has no history of other cancers in the past five years and is not currently pregnant or nursing.

45-year-old woman with a 5-year history of fibromyalgia, characterized by widespread chronic pain and stiffness, fatigue, and sleep disturbances. She has tried several medications and alternative therapies, but none of them have provided significant relief. She reports a high level of pain catastrophizing, often expecting the worst and feeling helpless and hopeless about her symptoms. She experiences stiffness and tightness in her muscles and has difficulty with daily activities such as walking and reaching. She has no joint deformities and is able to walk independently. She is not currently undergoing any other form of physiotherapeutic treatment.

As this is a retrospective analysis of de-identified deceased HCC patients, there are no specific patient characteristics needed for participation. The study will look at patients who were not surgical candidates and had biopsy-proven HCC.

This is a 65-year-old male patient with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness, difficulty speaking, and drooping of the right side of his face. A CT scan revealed a left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke. He was treated with tPA and started on aspirin therapy (80 mg/day) to prevent further stroke. He also reports chronic knee pain and has been taking dipyrone as needed for pain relief. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial investigating the interaction of aspirin and dipyrone in stroke patients. The patient is not in reanimation or cardiogenic shock, which are the exclusion criteria for this trial.

A 52-year-old woman is scheduled for an elective surgery. She has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication, and seasonal allergies. She is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and is physically active. She has never had surgery before and is feeling anxious about the procedure. She is interested in participating in this study to better understand the potential risks and complications associated with her surgery. She has read and understood the informed consent document and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled for a radical prostatectomy surgery. He has no history of diabetes mellitus or alcohol abuse. He is not taking beta-blockers and is otherwise in good health. He has given informed consent to participate in the study. The patient will have a central venous catheter (CVC) placed during surgery as it is standard practice. The patient is able to understand written and spoken information and is willing to comply with the study procedures. The patient's American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score is II, indicating that he has mild systemic disease.

Pt is a 55yo M with a history of hepatitis B virus infection and underwent curative hepatic resection for a 6 cm HCC lesion with negative margins. Pathology revealed a poorly differentiated tumor with vascular invasion. The patient meets the criteria for high risk of recurrence and has no previous treatment for HCC. The patient has Child-Pugh A liver function and no evidence of metastasis to the lymph nodes and/or distant metastases. The patient has no history of cardiac disease, active clinically serious infections, or known history of HIV infection. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use adequate barrier birth control measures during the course of the trial. The patient is not taking any excluded therapies or medications and has not undergone autologous bone marrow transplant or stem cell rescue within four months of the start of the study drug.

This is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing erectile dysfunction for the past 6 months. He has been in a stable relationship with one female partner and his partner is not pregnant or lactating, and is taking proper contraceptive measures. He has voluntarily decided to participate in this clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. He has attempted sexual intercourse on more than 3 different days (once/day) during the 4-week free run-in period, and his failure rate for sexual intercourse is more than 50%. His EF domain score is less than 18 points (moderate to severe erectile dysfunction) in the IIEF questionnaire after the 4-week free run-in period. He has not had spinal injury or radical prostatectomy, and does not have anatomical malformations of the penis. He has not had surgery in the pelvic cavity within 6 months prior to participation in the study, and does not have neurogenic or endocrine ED. He does not have major refractory psychiatric disorder or significant neurological abnormalities. He is not addicted to alcohol or drugs of dependence. He does not have hepatic or renal dysfunction, diabetic retinopathy or hematopathy which can be a predisposition to priapism. He has not had a stroke, TIA, MI, or fatal arrhythmia. He does not have hypotension or unregulated hypertension. He is not administered with nitrate/nitric oxide, androgens, anti-androgen, trazodone, anticoagulant or agents that significantly affect the CYP450 3A4 intermediary metabolism. He does not have a history of hypersensitivity to other PDE-5 inhibitors or who have not responded to them, primary hyposexuality, or have taken other investigational products within 4 weeks before the study. He meets all of the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 55-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a history of a fall from a ladder. He complains of severe pain and swelling in his right elbow. On examination, there is tenderness and crepitus over the distal humerus with limited range of motion. X-rays show a displaced intra-articular distal humeral fracture (AO 13-C2). After the patient is stabilized, surgical intervention is planned. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of polyaxial locking plates in treating distal humeral fractures. He is informed about the study and provided with written informed consent. The patient is randomized to receive either the DePuy Synthes VA-LCP 2.7/3.5 mm or the Medartis Aptus Elbow system 2.0/3.8 mm. The patient undergoes surgery with general anesthesia and a single dose of 1.5 mg cephalosporin is given preoperatively for prophylaxis. Postoperative physiotherapy is initiated using the same rehabilitation protocol for both groups. The patient is followed up for 12 months to evaluate the outcomes of the surgical intervention.

4 yo M with history of strabismus and amblyopia in the left eye with visual acuity of 20/60 and no improvement after previous 12 weeks of patching. The patient is currently wearing glasses and tolerating them well. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies to medications. Past medical history is negative for any serious illnesses or surgeries. The patient is able to follow instructions and has no other developmental delays. The patient and their legal guardian are willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all scheduled visits.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He is scheduled to undergo an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) in the next few weeks. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical problems and is not taking any other medications. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and drinks alcohol occasionally on social occasions. He has one child who is 12 years old. He works as a teacher and is eager to return to work as soon as possible after his transplant. He has been informed of the risks associated with HSCT, including the risk of developing hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD). He is willing to participate in this study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 2 years ago. Despite following a strict diet and exercise regimen, her HbA1C levels have been consistently high, above 7.5%. She has not been taking any medication for her diabetes. She has no history of diabetic coma, heart failure, or active hepatitis. Her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of malignant tumors. She is willing and able to comply with the contraceptive measures required for the study.

This is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing severe pain in her left arm, shoulder, and neck for over a month. The pain is dull and achy and is accompanied by numbness and tingling sensations in the affected area. The patient has tried various conservative treatments such as physical therapy, pain medication, and heat therapy, but none of them have provided significant relief. Imaging studies have revealed degenerative spondylosis and/or disk herniation in her cervical spine. She has a current mean pain VAS score of 8. The patient has no history of vertebral fracture, tumor, or infection of the cervical spine, nor has she received any cervical corticosteroid injections in the past 3 months. She does not have a coagulopathy or allergy to iodinated contrast media.

A 55-year-old male patient presented to the emergency department with chest pain that had started 2 hours ago. He described the pain as a pressure sensation in the center of his chest, radiating to his left arm, and accompanied by shortness of breath and sweating. The patient had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but no previous cardiac history. He was a smoker, with a 30-pack-year history. The patient's vital signs were within normal limits, and his physical examination was unremarkable, except for mild tenderness in his chest. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed ST-segment depression in leads V1 to V5. The patient was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and was admitted to the hospital. He was randomized to the Enoxamed® group and received an intravenous injection of enoxaparin at a curative dose of 100 IU/10 kg. The patient's anti-Xa activity was measured between H0 and H4. The patient did not have any contraindications to enoxaparin or heparin in general and was not taking any anticoagulants in the last three months.

A 32-year-old woman with a history of ulcerative colitis underwent an ileal pouch anal anastomosis (IPAA) six months ago. She now presents with a peri-pouch fistula that has been refractory to conventional medical therapy, including corticosteroids, 5-ASA drugs, immunomodulators, and anti-TNF therapy. The fistula tract arises from the ileal pouch body and travels to the perianal skin. The patient has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease of the pouch based on clinical symptoms, pouchoscopy with biopsy, and enterography. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use acceptable contraception methods during participation in the study. She has no contraindications to MR evaluations. The patient has no history of cancer or other clinically significant medical conditions in the past six months. She has not received any investigational drugs within the past thirty days. The patient is competent and able to provide written informed consent and able to comply with the protocol.

A 24-year-old pregnant woman who is currently participating in CenteringPregnancy group care at Boston Medical Center. She speaks fluent English and is able to complete a written survey in English. She is in good health and has no history of trauma or mental health issues. She is married and lives with her husband in a stable home environment. She is expecting her first child and is excited to learn more about how to prepare for parenting and manage the common stresses that come with it. She is willing to participate in the study and attend all sessions.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has struggled with weight loss for several years. She has a BMI of 35 and has a history of essential hypertension and dyslipidemia, with high LDL (180 mg/dL) and high total cholesterol (260 mg/dL). She has tried various diets and exercise programs, but has been unsuccessful in achieving significant weight loss. She does not have type 2 diabetes or a history of eating disorders. She is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription weight modifying drugs. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the weight loss effect of CP-945,598.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was previously diagnosed with high-grade glioma. He underwent surgery and received standard radiotherapy and chemotherapy but has now relapsed. The patient reports headaches, blurred vision, and difficulty concentrating. The Karnofsky score (KPS score) is 70. MRI confirms recurrent high-grade glioma. The toxicity has returned to ≤1 grade after chemotherapy. The patient has expected survival of ≥3 months. The patient has no major organ dysfunction and specific laboratory indicators are within normal limits. The patient agrees to take adequate contraceptive measures throughout the study period. The patient voluntarily joined the study and signed a written informed consent. The patient is not currently taking any small molecule anti-angiogenesis targeted drugs. The patient has not participated in clinical research of other anti-tumor drugs within four weeks. The researcher deems the patient suitable for inclusion in the study.

32F with no known family history of glaucoma, presenting for routine eye examination. The patient reports no visual complaints and has no history of ocular surgery or trauma. Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and intraocular pressure (IOP) is measured at 16 mmHg in each eye. Dilated fundus examination reveals normal appearing optic discs and RNFL, and Swedish interactive thresholding algorithm (SITA) standard perimetry tests are within normal limits with no evidence of glaucoma hemifield test (GHT) abnormalities. The patient is eligible to participate in the study as a healthy volunteer.

A 35-year-old Chinese woman with a BMI of 24.5 presents for a routine physical exam. She works as a software engineer and spends most of her day sitting. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. She exercises occasionally and follows a balanced diet. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She has never been pregnant. She is interested in participating in a study that investigates the factors and importance of brown adipose tissue in Chinese adults. She is willing to undergo a PET/CT scan and provide blood samples for analysis.

A 68-year-old woman with a history of wet age-related macular degeneration (wAMD) presents to the ophthalmologist for a routine visit. She has been receiving Anti-VEGF injections for the past year, but has noticed some difficulty in adhering to the treatment plan. She reports missing a few appointments and has concerns about the frequency of the injections. The patient is generally healthy otherwise, with no significant medical history and is able to perform daily activities independently. She is interested in participating in a study that will observe her current course of therapy, without any changes to her medical care. The patient is willing to answer a short questionnaire during her visits to the study center and participate in four independent phone interviews during the study period. The patient is a resident of Germany and meets all the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 28-year-old healthy male volunteer with a BMI of 24 kg/m² and a body weight of 68 kg presents for the clinical trial. He has no significant medical history and no previous exposure to canagliflozin or probenecid. His laboratory test results and physical examination are unremarkable. His BP: 120/80, HR: 72/min and no abnormalities are noted in his 12-lead ECG. He is informed about the nature of the study, its procedures, and possible risks and benefits. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has provided written informed consent. He is enrolled in the study and will receive canagliflozin and/or probenecid based on the study protocol.

A 23-year-old male who was recently in a transitional housing program for homeless youth is eligible for this clinical trial. He has a history of substance abuse and has been using drugs in the past month. He is able to speak and understand English. The patient has expressed interest in reducing substance use and establishing permanent supportive connections during this transitional period. He is willing to participate in the computer-assisted social network intervention and is open to motivational interviewing techniques. He has no significant medical or psychiatric conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with complaints of fatigue, shortness of breath, and chest pain on exertion. The patient is currently on Telmisartan for hypertension, but her lipid profile has not improved despite being on Rosuvastatin for the past year. Her blood pressure is consistently above 140/90 mmHg, and her LDL-C levels are above the target range. The patient is non-smoker, non-diabetic, and has no history of cardiovascular disease. She has no history of allergies or significant adverse drug reactions. She is currently taking no other medications except for Telmisartan and Rosuvastatin. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Telmisartan/Rosuvastatin co-administration in hypertensive patients with hyperlipidemia. She is willing to practice adequate contraception throughout the study, and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 7-month-old infant who was born at full term with a birth weight of 3 kg. The infant has not received any influenza vaccination before and is eligible to participate in this study. The infant's parents are willing and able to provide informed consent, attend all scheduled visits, and comply with all trial procedures. The infant has no reported allergies to egg or chicken proteins or any other constituent of Fluzone vaccine. The infant has not received any vaccine in the 14 days prior to enrollment, and does not have an acute illness with or without fever in the 72 hours preceding enrollment in the trial. The infant has no known bleeding disorder, impairment of immunologic function, or personal or family history of congenital immune deficiency. The infant does not have developmental delay, neurologic disorder, or seizure disorder. The infant's medical history is unremarkable and there is no known chronic medical, congenital, or developmental disorder that could interfere with the trial conduct or completion. The infant's mother is negative for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C infection, and has not received blood or blood-derived products within the past 2 months. The infant has not had Guillain-Barré syndrome in the past. The infant is eligible for the study and will participate in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for over a year. She is currently taking daily basal insulin treatment and metformin. Her HbA1c levels are below 9.0%. She has a body mass index that falls between 18.5 and 38.0 kg/m^2. She has been stable on her current anti-diabetic regimen for over 90 days prior to screening. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to attend all 23 visits with the study doctor. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no known hypersensitivity to trial products or related products. She is willing to use adequate contraceptive measures as required by local regulation or practice if she is of child-bearing potential. She is willing to receive a single dose of insulin icodec on three different occasions, each time injected at a different site, i.e., either on her belly, upper arm or thigh. She is willing to participate in the study for the duration of about 34 weeks.

Patient is a 40-year-old man diagnosed with locally advanced sarcoma and deemed at high risk for relapse or metastasis. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 90 and has no significant comorbidities. The patient is not pregnant, lactating, or trying to conceive and is willing to use effective contraceptive measures during the trial. The patient has adequate hematologic, renal, and hepatic functions. The patient has not received any packed red blood cell transfusion within 2 weeks before study entry and has no history of prior chemotherapy for sarcomas. The patient has no iron deficiency or hypersensitivity to E.coli derived products. The patient has not undergone surgery or radiation therapy within 2 weeks of study entry.

A 25-year-old male athlete has been training for endurance races for the past 2 years. He exercises daily, with a focus on running, and his current aerobic power consumption of oxygen is 60 mL/kg/min. He is interested in improving his performance by lowering his body fat percentage. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications or nutritional supplements. He has a balanced diet, which includes meat, fish, fruits, and vegetables. He does not smoke and consumes alcohol only occasionally. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of high-flavanol cocoa intake on body fat composition and exercise performance.

The patient is a 25-year-old female diagnosed with beta thalassemia major at birth. She has been receiving regular blood transfusions every three weeks since then. Due to the transfusions, the patient has developed chronic iron overload requiring chelation therapy. Her serum ferritin level is above 500ng/mL, and her baseline liver iron concentration is greater than or equal to 5mg iron per g (equivalent dry weight, liver) as determined by FerriScan® R2 MRI. The patient has been on an iron chelation therapy but is willing to discontinue it for a minimum of one to five days before the first dose of SSP-004184AQ and for the

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with heart failure, NYHA Class II, six months ago. He experiences shortness of breath, fatigue, and difficulty exercising. He has been prescribed medication for his heart failure and has been seeing a community heart failure nurse for his ongoing care. However, he has been feeling down and anxious lately, and he has trouble sleeping. He has not received any treatment for his depression and anxiety yet. He is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially, and does not use illicit drugs. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well controlled with medication. He is married, has two adult children, and works as an accountant. He is proficient in English and has access to the internet and a computer.

The patient is a 12-year-old female who has been diagnosed with epilepsy with partial onset seizures. She has been previously treated with one anti-epileptic drug, but her seizures remain uncontrolled. She is currently receiving Lacosamide (LCM) as an add-on therapy to her current medication. Her parents have given written informed consent for her participation in this clinical trial. She is expected to benefit from the study according to her treating physician. The patient is reliable and capable of adhering to the protocol and visit schedule. She has no history of suicide attempts or suicidal ideation in the past 6 months. She is not pregnant or nursing, and her parents report that she is practicing a highly effective method of contraception.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption on weekends and occasional drug use. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. Recently, he has been experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional abdominal pain. He also noticed yellowing of his eyes and skin. He is concerned about his health and decides to visit the emergency department (ED) at the local hospital. Upon arrival, he is evaluated by the screening nurse and deemed clinically stable. The patient is able to provide consent for medical care and agrees to participate in the DETECT HCV Screening Trial.

25-year-old female student at a massage and acupuncture school experiencing high levels of stress and anxiety due to academic workload and personal life responsibilities. She has been struggling with sleep disturbances, muscle tension, and feelings of overwhelm for the past month. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to reduce stress and anxiety through auricular acupuncture. She is available to attend sessions over the course of two months and is not currently pregnant.

A 13-year old female student who attends a local school in Russia. She lives with her parents and siblings. She is in good health and has no known medical conditions. She has not received any vaccines within the last 28 days and is not planning to receive any vaccines within the next 30 days. She has not received any investigational or non-registered product within the last 28 days and does not plan to receive any during the study period. She has not had any serious acute, chronic or progressive disease, or any serious vaccine reactions in the past. She has no known allergies to any vaccine components including diphtheria toxin (CRM-197) and latex in the syringe. She has not had any history of neoplasm, cancer, diabetes, cardiac disease, autoimmune disease, Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), or blood dyscrasias, with signs of cardiac or renal failure or severe malnutrition. She has not had epilepsy or any progressive neurological disease or history of Guillain-Barre syndrome. She has not had any anaphylaxis or any known or suspected impairment or alteration of immune function, either congenital or acquired, or resulting from receipt of immunosuppressive therapy, immunostimulants, or parenteral immunoglobulin preparation, blood products, and/or plasma derivatives. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol and has provided written informed assent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for more than a year with her partner. She has regular menstrual cycles that occur every 28 days, and her periods last for 5 days. She has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. She has undergone a series of diagnostic tests to determine the cause of infertility, including a hysterosalpingogram (HSG) and semen analysis for her partner. Both tests came back normal, indicating that there are no structural abnormalities in her reproductive system and her partner's sperm are healthy. She has been recommended for an intrauterine insemination (IUI) with sperm donor to increase her chances of getting pregnant. Her progesterone levels on the day of hCG administration were found to be slightly elevated, indicating that she may be at risk of premature ovulation. Therefore, she is eligible to participate in this clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of an advanced IUI schedule (24 hours post-hCG) compared to the standard schedule (36 hours post-hCG) based on her progesterone levels. She is willing to be assigned to either group and follow the study protocols. She understands that the study aims to improve the chances of successful pregnancy in women with high progesterone levels during stimulated cycles of IUI, and that the results of this study may be helpful in developing better treatment strategies for infertility.

32-year-old woman with a history of menorrhagia and currently using MIRENA for contraception is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has been using MIRENA for the past 4 years and 6 months and is willing to continue with the method. Her uterus size is normal, corresponding to sound measure of 8 cm. She had a normal cervical smear result within the preceding 12 months and no abnormalities found in the breast examination. She has no menopausal symptoms and is not currently taking estrogen therapy. She is not pregnant and has no history of distortion of the uterine cavity, pelvic inflammatory disease, or abnormal uterine bleeding of unknown origin. She has no active acute liver disease or liver tumor. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend follow-up visits as scheduled.

This is a 35 year-old HIV-infected male who has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF)/Lamivudine (3TC)/Nevirapine (NVP) for the past 8 months. His most recent HIV RNA viral load was undetectable and his CD4 cell count was 320 cells/mm3. He has been compliant with his medications and has not experienced any adverse effects. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to switch his current ART regimen from NVP to Rilpivirine (RPV) to potentially avoid the adverse effects associated with NVP. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or diagnosed with any depressive or psychiatric disorders.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who had a stem cell transplant two years ago for acute myeloid leukemia. Since the transplant, he has developed chronic graft-versus-host disease that has not responded to steroid treatment. His symptoms include skin rash, dry mouth, and eyes, joint pain, and diarrhea. He has tried multiple immunosuppressive treatments, but none have been effective in controlling his symptoms. He is currently on a maintenance dose of prednisone and has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He is not currently taking any other medications or supplements. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period as he is married and does not desire any more children. His laboratory tests are within normal limits, except for elevated liver enzymes, which are attributed to cGVHD. He is interested in the study as he is looking for an alternative treatment to improve his quality of life.

A 45-year-old woman complains of persistent facial redness, particularly on her cheeks, for the past year. She has tried several over-the-counter creams and lotions but they have not been effective. She has no history of facial skin treatments with lasers or electrocauterization, and has no facial hair. She is not pregnant and is currently using birth control. She has a moderate severity of erythema on her cheeks with no more than 12 inflammatory lesions on her face. She is looking for a treatment that is safe and effective for her rosacea.

35 y/o male with a confirmed diagnosis of ulcerative colitis for the past 6 months, presenting with moderate to severe active UC symptoms. The patient has previously undergone conventional and biologic therapy for UC, but has shown an inadequate response to these treatments. The patient has not been exposed to anti-IL-23p19 antibodies, vedolizumab, or natalizumab. The patient is willing to meet the contraception requirements if female. The patient does not have a current diagnosis of Crohn's disease or inflammatory bowel disease-unclassified (indeterminate colitis) and has not had a previous colectomy. The patient does not have current evidence of toxic megacolon and has not experienced prior clinical failure or intolerance to anti-IL12p40 antibodies or anti-integrin antibodies other than vedolizumab and natalizumab within 4 weeks prior to screening endoscopy.

A 26-year-old male athlete and soccer player recently underwent an ACL reconstruction surgery with a patellar tendon autograft. He is currently in good health and meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial. He had no significant prior medical history and is not currently taking any medications or supplements that are banned by the NCAA. His BMI is 24.5, and he has not experienced rapid weight changes recently. He has no history of diabetes, cardiovascular, renal, liver or pulmonary disease. He is willing and able to participate in the rehabilitation program and attend at least 85% of the assigned rehabilitation sessions. The patient is motivated to get back to his sport as soon as possible and is willing to be assigned to either the study or control group.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of mitral valve prolapse presents for evaluation of her cardiac function. She reports mild shortness of breath with exertion and occasional palpitations. She has never undergone a Cardiac MRI before but has had echocardiograms in the past. She denies any other significant medical history or hospitalizations. She is not taking any medications and has no known allergies. Her vital signs are within normal limits, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 72 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. Her physical exam is unremarkable with no signs of edema or jugular venous distention. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and undergo a Cardiac MRI to evaluate her cardiac function with the new Necklace device.

A 54 year old woman is diagnosed with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) that has relapsed following platinum-based systemic chemotherapy. She has undergone two prior lines of therapy and there is no curative treatment available for her. She has a measurable disease with at least one tumor lesion greater than or equal to 10 mm in the longest diameter, as confirmed by computed tomography (CT) scan. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has adequate hematologic, hepatic, neurologic, and renal function. She has no history of liver cirrhosis, hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD), sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS), alcohol dependence or excessive alcohol use. She has no history of stroke or clinically significant cardiac disease within 6 months prior to the first dose of study drug. She has not had a history of cardiac conduction abnormalities, serious infections or prior or concomitant malignancies. She weighs more than 35 kilograms. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, active pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease (ILD) or a history of pneumonitis/ILD requiring treatment with steroids.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been struggling with weight gain for the past few years. She has a BMI of 29 and is considered overweight. She works in an office and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She has tried various diets and exercise programs but has not been able to lose weight. She has a family history of diabetes and is concerned about her risk of developing the condition. She is generally healthy and does not have any significant medical history. She does not smoke or drink excessively. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the role of gene expression and inflammation in overweight individuals. She is willing to undergo a series of tests, including blood tests, body composition analysis, and subcutaneous fat biopsy, to help researchers better understand the mechanisms involved in weight gain and loss. She is also willing to participate in a calorie-restricted diet and follow-up visits to assess any changes in her weight and biomarkers. She hopes that the findings from this study will help identify new treatment options for obesity and ultimately improve her overall health and well-being.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who experienced sudden onset of right arm weakness and difficulty speaking. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She smokes 10 cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her family history is negative for stroke or thrombophilia. On examination, she has right-sided hemiparesis and mild dysarthria. The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score is 6. Imaging studies show a small infarct in the left parietal lobe. The patient is diagnosed with embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS) and is eligible for this clinical trial. She agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 38-year-old male who has a history of intravenous drug use. He presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, abdominal pain, and yellowing of the skin and eyes. Upon examination, he has hepatomegaly and tenderness on palpation of the liver. His blood work reveals elevated liver enzymes and a positive hepatitis C antibody test. Further testing confirms chronic hepatitis C infection. He has no history of hepatitis B or any other underlying medical condition. He is currently not receiving any treatment for his condition.

A 55-year-old male patient is scheduled to undergo spinal fusion surgery at Chung-Ang University Hospital. He has a history of chronic lower back pain and has been taking pain medication for the past year. He does not have any other significant medical history or allergies. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use illicit drugs. During the initial consultation, the patient expressed concerns about postoperative pain management and the potential side effects of pain medication. The patient has consented to participate in a clinical trial comparing two different types of pain management techniques. The trial will involve the use of intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (IV-PCA), either with a constant infusion rate plus demanding dosing or with variable-rate feedback infusion plus demanding dosing. The patient does not have any brain disorder, cardiopulmonary disease, or psychiatric disorders.

The patient is a 40-year-old premenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with operable breast cancer. She underwent a lumpectomy and has negative axillary lymph nodes. The margins of the resected specimen from surgery were histologically free of invasive adenocarcinoma and ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS). The patient has not received any prior systemic anticancer therapy for breast cancer, nor has she received prior radiation therapy for breast cancer. She has no history of motor or sensory neurotoxicity of a severity grade 2 by NCI criteria. Her performance status index is greater than 80%, and she has adequate hepatic, renal, and heart functions. The patient's estrogen and progesterone receptors were performed on the primary tumor prior to randomization. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is not currently taking hormonal replacement therapy. The patient does not have any definite contraindications for the use of corticosteroids.

34-year-old female with two children, currently receiving Medicaid, reports feeling sad and hopeless for the past few weeks. She has difficulty sleeping, has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy, and feels fatigued most of the time. She has no history of bipolar disorder or substance abuse. She is not currently receiving treatment for depression and is not receiving Supplemental Security Income. She is interested in participating in a study that may help her manage her depression and improve her overall wellbeing.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with pemphigus vulgaris presents with lesions on his skin and mucous membranes. He has not received any previous treatment for this condition. He has no significant past medical history, but he is allergic to penicillin. He does not smoke or drink alcohol but has a sedentary lifestyle. He is not obese, with a BMI of 25. He has no history of diabetes, hypertension, or thyroid disorder. His fasting lipid profile and liver enzymes are within normal limits. His thyroid function test is normal. His serum creatinine and urea are also within normal limits. He has no history of cancer or any chronic illness. He is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent.

The patient is a 50 year old female diagnosed with hallux valgus deformity, commonly known as a bunion. She has been experiencing pain, swelling and discomfort in her big toe joint for the past year. Upon examination by her podiatrist, it was confirmed that she has an inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) of 14 degrees. She has not had any prior surgeries on her feet, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. Her weight is 70 kg and her BMI is 28 kg/m2. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and understands the risks and benefits of participating. She has no known complications of diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, or neurological conditions associated with spasticity or lower limb paralysis. She is not pregnant and is willing to take necessary contraception measures. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 50-year-old man came to the gastroenterology clinic with complaints of abdominal pain and discomfort. He has a history of gallstones and was referred for an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreaticography (ERCP) procedure. He is married with two children and works as an accountant. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. He has no history of mental illness or any other medical conditions. He is fluent in the local language and also speaks English. He has never undergone an ERCP procedure before and is interested in learning more about the procedure.

A 48-year-old female presented with a palpable lump in her right breast. She has no family history of breast cancer and no history of other medical conditions. She underwent a mammogram and ultrasound, which revealed a suspicious mass. A biopsy was performed, and the pathology report confirmed that the mass was malignant. She has not yet undergone surgery or any other treatment for breast cancer. She has read about a study that aims to detect circulating tumor cells and cell free DNA in peripheral blood of breast cancer patients to develop clinical applications for early detection and diagnostics. She is interested in participating in the study and willing to sign the informed consent form. She has not undergone any general or regional anesthesia in the past month and has not been diagnosed with any other type of cancer or autoimmune disorder. She has also not been suffering from any chronic or acute infections in the past three months. She meets the inclusion criteria for the cancer group in the study.

This is a 64-year-old female who presented to the dermatology clinic with a history of multiple skin lesions on her face, scalp, and arms. She has a history of sun exposure and has been previously diagnosed with actinic keratosis. Biopsies of her skin lesions show evidence of basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the expression levels of microprocessor complex subunit DGCR8 and RISC components TARBP1, TARBP2, argonaute-1, argonaute-2, and PACT in epithelial skin cancer and its premalignant stage. She is otherwise in good health, with no history of other malignancies.

A 66-year-old Japanese man presents with a history of advanced lung cancer that has spread to other parts of his body. He has already undergone several rounds of standard therapy with minimal response. His performance status is 2 on the ECOG scale, indicating that he is still able to take care of himself with some difficulty. He has adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. He has discontinued all previous cancer therapies for at least 21 days and has no other effective therapeutic options for his condition. He is willing to use medically approved contraceptive precautions during the study as he is still considered to be of reproductive potential. He has an estimated life expectancy that will permit him to complete 8 weeks of treatment. He is not currently receiving warfarin therapy and has not received any cytochrome P450 3A4 modulators within the last 14 days. He has no evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease and has not previously been intolerant of therapy with erlotinib or gefitinib. He meets the eligibility criteria for Part B2 of the study and will receive LY2875358 and gefitinib.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was diagnosed with moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) two years ago. She has a history of smoking for 25 years and worked in a factory with exposure to dust and chemicals for 15 years. She is currently not smoking and has been advised to stay away from any environmental pollutants. She has been using an inhaler for the past year and reports occasional shortness of breath on exertion. Her post-bronchodilator pulmonary function tests show a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 55% predicted and a ratio of FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) of 68%. She has had one exacerbation in the past year that did not require hospitalization. She is not pregnant and is using a reliable method of contraception. She has no history of major medical or surgical disorders that would interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of the study treatment. She has not required continuous oxygen therapy or non-invasive ventilation. She has not had any emergency treatment with antibiotics or systemic corticosteroids or any hospitalization due to COPD within the past 2 months.
