Her screening night PSG shows no evidence of Periodic limb movement disorder with arousal index ≥ 15/h, restless legs syndrome, circadian rhythm disorder, rapid eye movement (REM) behavior disorder, parasomnia including nightmare disorder, sleep terror disorder, and/or sleepwalking disorder but excluding any COPD-related abnormalities.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of depression and insomnia for the past several months. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated most days, and has difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep at night. She has tried over-the-counter sleep aids and relaxation techniques but has not found relief. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to address both her depression and insomnia. The patient is fluent in English and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She works a regular 9-5 job and does not have any rotating shifts. The patient is eager to participate in the study and hopes to find relief from her symptoms.

A 25-year-old female presents to her endocrinologist with complaints of fatigue, headaches, and joint pain. She reports noticing an increase in the size of her hands and feet over the past several years and has had difficulty finding shoes and gloves that fit properly. Physical examination reveals enlarged hands and feet, coarsening of facial features, and a prominent brow ridge. Laboratory studies show elevated serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels and failure of suppression of growth hormone (GH) levels during an oral glucose tolerance test. Magnetic resonance imaging of the pituitary gland confirms the presence of a pituitary adenoma. The patient is diagnosed with acromegaly and is eligible for enrollment in the clinical trial to describe the characteristic associations of signs and symptoms present at the time of acromegaly diagnosis.

A 68-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 25 kg/m2, weighing 75 kg, non-smoker, and non-alcoholic is eligible to participate in the clinical trial. He has no history of liver disease, biliary abnormalities, or neutropenia. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his ECG shows a QTc interval within the normal range. He has no history of regular alcohol consumption, and his urine and serum samples test negative for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C. He has not participated in any clinical trial or used any prescription or non-prescription drugs, including vitamins, herbal and dietary supplements within the last seven days. He is capable of giving written informed consent and willing to comply with the study requirements and restrictions.

The patient is a 59-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with lung cancer. His diagnostic imaging shows a 6 cm tumor located in the upper lobe of his right lung. He is a former smoker and quit 10 years ago. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medications. He has no significant family history of cancer. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may provide additional information about the blood flow rate to his tumor.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing knee pain, stiffness, and grinding for over a year. He is diagnosed with medial femorotibial compartment knee osteoarthritis and has been taking analgesics for the past three months but is dissatisfied with the results. His X-ray reveals grade II osteoarthritis according to the Kellgren and Lawrence classification system. He has a global pain score greater than 60 mm on a 0-100 mm VAS on the knee under study. He has not undergone any joint lavage or arthroscopy or any surgery on the knee under study in the past six months. He has no history of Paget's disease of bone, chondromatosis, or villonodular sinovitis. He is not diagnosed with inflammatory, infectious, or metabolic arthritis such as rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthropathy, or connective tissue diseases. He has a BMI of 28.5, and he has not used any SYSADOA, SERM, or drugs/dietary supplements containing glucosamine, chondroitin sulfate, diacerein, or avocado-soybean extracts in the past three months. He is not allergic to the study treatments or any of its ingredients. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his written consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pelvic pain and heavy menstrual bleeding for the past year. She has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids and her gynecologist has recommended a total laparoscopic hysterectomy to alleviate her symptoms. The patient has no history of urinary incontinence or retention, nor has she undergone any prior bladder or prolapse surgeries. She is able to read and understand English, and has voluntarily agreed to participate in the study. The patient does not take any anticholinergic medications, and has no known neurological or spinal cord injuries affecting bladder function. She is not pregnant and has no evidence of gynecologic malignancy. The patient has been fully informed of the risks and benefits of the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 40-year-old man diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) and has been recommended to undergo a Melphalan-based myeloablative chemotherapy (BEAM) followed by autologous human stem cell transplantation (AHSCT). He has been in complete remission following the most recent anti-neoplastic therapy regimen. He has a cryopreserved autologous stem cell graft containing 2.5 x 10^6 cryopreserved CD34+ cells/kg. The patient has a Karnofsky score of 80%. The patient has no history of cardiovascular congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmias requiring a pacemaker, myocardial infarction or stroke in the past six months or uncontrolled hypertension. He has a mean QTcF value of 430 msec (within normal range) and no history of prolonged QT syndromes. The patient has no history of GI tract cancer, polyps, ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, coeliac disease, tropical sprue, or active pancreatic disease. He has no history of autoimmune disease or any suicidal tendency or clinically relevant psychiatric diseases or substance abuse.

The patient is a 35 year-old female who has been experiencing migraines for the past 5 years. She has a history of migraines occurring once or twice a month which are usually accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. She has tried various over-the-counter medications such as ibuprofen and acetaminophen, but they provide only partial relief. She does not have any known medical conditions and is not currently taking any prescription medications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if breathing 100% oxygen can help alleviate her migraines.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus six months ago. He has been managing his diabetes with diet and exercise. However, his latest HbA1c test showed a reading of 8.9%, which is higher than his target range. He has not experienced any symptoms of hyperglycemia, such as polyuria and polydypsia. He takes lisinopril for his high blood pressure and simvastatin for his high cholesterol. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally at social events. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new vaccine targeting Interleukin-1 beta to help manage his diabetes.

A 23-year-old Caucasian male with a history of grass pollen allergy presents to the clinic with symptoms of rhinoconjunctivitis. He reports experiencing itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, and nasal congestion during the grass pollen season in the past two years. He also reports having to use rescue medication regularly during the season. He does not have any other known allergies and does not have a history of asthma. He is generally healthy and does not take any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is a full-time college student and reports that his allergy symptoms have affected his academic performance in the past. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to alleviate his symptoms and improve his quality of life during the grass pollen season. His SPT for grass pollen is positive, and his RRTSS during the previous pollen season was 14 out of a possible 18.

A 9-month-old infant is referred to the Infant Health project by the community health nurse due to having three or more problems identified at the PUF assessment. The infant's mother is a 28-year-old woman who is currently on maternity leave from her job as a sales assistant. The father is a 30-year-old man who works as a construction worker. Both parents are of Danish ethnicity, and they live in a small apartment in a suburban area. The infant was born at term with a birth weight of 3,500 g and has been healthy so far. The infant's medical history is unremarkable, with no previous hospitalizations, no medication use, and no known allergies or chronic illnesses. The infant has been breastfed since birth and is currently being introduced to solid foods according to the recommended guidelines. The infant's weight is in the 50th percentile, and there is no evidence of overweight or underweight. However, the PUF assessment revealed that the infant has three or more problems, including problems of emotional regulation and difficulties with sleeping and eating. The parents have agreed to participate in the Infant Health project and have been randomized to the intervention group. They will receive

Unfortunately, as this is an observational study, there is no need to generate a patient description. The study is not recruiting patients, but rather collecting data on patients who are already receiving regular blood transfusions due to chronic hematologic disorders.

This is a 46-year-old female diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in [**5/2020**]. She underwent induction chemotherapy with 7+3 regimen and achieved complete remission. However, she experienced relapse in [**10/2021**]. She was then treated with reinduction chemotherapy with idarubicin and cytarabine, but failed to achieve a second remission. The patient has undergone a total of two courses of induction/reinduction therapy. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, and creatinine levels are within normal limits. She does not have any active CNS leukemia, active uncontrolled infection, or other life-threatening illness. She is not pregnant or nursing, and a negative pregnancy test was obtained. She has not received any prior flavopiridol, and has not undergone any stem cell transplantation, chemotherapy, or immunotherapy in the past 3 weeks. She is not diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia (M3), and her blast count is currently under control. She is considered eligible for this clinical trial.

A 50-year-old male presents with a history of persistent nasal congestion, difficulty swallowing, and a feeling of fullness in his throat. He has lost some weight over the past few months and has noticed a lump on his neck. On examination, a mass is palpable on the left side of his neck. Biopsy reveals non-keratinizing carcinoma, and imaging studies confirm the diagnosis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma without evidence of distant metastasis. His performance status is good, with a score of 1 on the ECOG scale. He is willing to participate in the trial and is able to read and understand the questionnaires. He has no history of psychiatric illness and has given written informed consent. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy and does not have any severe intercurrent disease.

A 37-year-old Japanese woman with a family history of breast and ovarian cancer was found to be a carrier of a BRCA1 variant after genetic counseling and testing. She has never been diagnosed with cancer herself. She is married and has one child. She works as an office manager and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about her risk of developing ovarian, fallopian tube, and peritoneal cancers, and the potential benefits of risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy.

A 42-year-old male diagnosed with stage IV melanoma with multiple metastases in the lungs, liver, and bones. He has previously received BRAFi and MEKi combination therapy for 3 months prior to discontinuation due to tumor progression. After 3 months, he underwent chemotherapy and immunotherapy. He now presents with BRAF V600E mutation-positive melanoma. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He has no history of brain metastasis or cardiovascular disease. He is willing to undergo biopsy at week 2 of treatment. He understands that he will receive dabrafenib and trametinib at their recommended doses for combination therapy of 150 mg twice daily (BID) and 2 mg daily (QD). He is willing to comply with study procedures and follow-up visits for a year following first treatment dose.

The patient is a 9-year-old child with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The child frequently exhibits auditory hyper-reactivity, with sensitivity to loud noises and sudden sounds. The child's reactions to auditory stimuli often lead to extreme stress and anxiety for both the child and their family. The child is able to communicate verbally and can utilize the Subjective Units of Distress (SUD) scale. The child has not been diagnosed with Oppositional Defiant Disorder or Conduct Disorder and has no history of child abuse related to sound sensitivity. The family is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at reducing the child's auditory hyper-reactivity through exposure and response prevention therapy.

The patient is a 35-year-old male experiencing mild to moderate hair loss and has a history of androgenic alopecia for at least one year. He has never undergone hair transplants or scalp reductions, nor has he used hair weaves, extensions or wigs in the last three months. The patient has not used minoxidil, oral or topical, or low-level light treatment "combs" for hair growth in the last six months and is not expected to use them during the study. He has not applied topical steroids or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) to his scalp in the last four weeks. The patient is willing to maintain the same hair style, length, and color during the study and undergo the application of a micro-dot-tattoo to his scalp (Stage 2 only). He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse within the last 12 months and is HIV negative.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who is currently overweight with a BMI of 30. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but no other significant medical conditions. She is not taking any medications that affect her weight and is willing to make dietary changes to lose weight. She typically consumes fruits, vegetables, and whole grains on a daily basis. She has not lost more than 10% of her body weight in the past 6 months and is not involved in any competitive sports. She is able to follow recommended diets and attend follow-up visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. She presents with a history of sudden onset of painless loss of vision in her right eye that started 23 days ago. She reports that her vision has been gradually improving over the past few days, but she still has difficulty reading small print and seeing in low light conditions. The patient has never experienced any similar episodes in the past. She is currently taking interferon beta-1a for her MS and has been on this treatment for the past 6 months. She reports no history of liver, renal, or bone marrow dysfunction. Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago, and she reports using a reliable form of contraception. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and provide written informed consent. She has no other known medical conditions that could interfere with the evaluation in the study. The patient has not received any corticosteroids during this episode of optic neuritis and has not participated in any other clinical therapeutic trials.

A 10-year-old male diagnosed with diffuse, intrinsic pontine glioma after presenting with ataxia and cranial nerve deficits. He has no significant medical history and is currently on a fixed dose of steroids. MRI performed within the last 14 days showed more than 50% involvement of the pons with variable contrast enhancement. He has a Lansky performance status of > 40. Hemoglobin, leukocytes, absolute neutrophil count, serum Na+, serum K+, serum creatinine, platelets, total bilirubin, AST (SGOT) / ALT (SGPT) are all within normal limits. His parents understand the informed consent document and are willing to sign it.

A 42-year-old Caucasian male presented with a history of chronic sinusitis and nasal polyps. He has been experiencing recurrent headaches, nasal congestion, and postnasal drip for the past two years. He has also developed a decreased sense of smell and taste. He has been treated with multiple courses of antibiotics and steroids, but his symptoms have not improved. Imaging studies revealed a large nasal polyp obstructing the right nasal cavity and extending into the posterior nasal cavity. After discussion with his medical team, he has elected to undergo a skull base surgery to remove the polyp.  The patient has no known allergies and has not undergone any previous surgeries. He currently takes over-the-counter allergy medication as needed. He understands the risks involved in the surgery and has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.  The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he is over 18 years old, planned for skull base surgery, and has agreed to sign the informed consent form. He does not meet any of the exclusion criteria as he does not have an active skull base infection, and his operating surgeon plans to use DuraGen repair.

A 54-year-old male resident of the 5th Congressional District of Kentucky was recently diagnosed with lung cancer. He has a history of smoking but quit 3 years ago. In addition to smoking, he has worked for 30 years in a coal mine where he was exposed to various environmental carcinogens such as arsenic, chromium, and nickel. He has no other history of cancer, except for basal cell carcinoma. He is able to speak English and has a working phone. He is willing to participate in the study and provide biologic and environmental samples for research purposes. He understands that by participating in this study, he may help researchers understand the causes of lung cancer in the region and contribute to the development of effective prevention and treatment strategies.

A 45-year-old man with a history of HIV infection presents with biopsy-proven Kaposi's sarcoma that has progressed despite standard therapy. He has no severe pulmonary Kaposi's sarcoma and has at least five measurable lesions of at least 10 mm, or lesions present for at least 30 days. The patient's absolute neutrophil count is at least 750/mm3 without transfusion, hemoglobin is at least 8.0 g/dL without transfusion, and platelet count is at least 50,000/mm3 without transfusion. His AST/ALT levels are no greater than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal, and his bilirubin levels are no greater than 2.0 mg/dL (3.0 mg/dL if concurrent indinavir therapy). The patient's creatinine levels are no greater than 1.8 mg/dL, or his creatinine clearance is at least 50 mL/min. He has no concurrent uncontrolled serious infections, and no known allergy to Cremophor or Cremophor-based drug products. The patient has no other active malignancies, acute or chronic medical or psychiatric conditions. He has not received any biologic, chemotherapy, hormonal, or radiotherapy for at least 2 weeks, and has recovered from prior treatments. The patient has stable antiretroviral therapy for at least 2 weeks and has not received any other investigational drugs for at least 3 weeks.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing seasonal allergies for the past 2 years. He complains of nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, and itchy eyes during the fall season. He has tried over-the-counter antihistamines without much relief. He has never been diagnosed with asthma or urticaria. He does not smoke and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is currently taking no medications and has no known medical conditions. He works as an office manager and lives with his spouse and two children. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to find a more effective treatment for his seasonal allergies.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who presented with a history of recurrent sinus infections and worsening nasal congestion. He also complains of fatigue, night sweats, and arthralgia in his hands and feet. Physical examination revealed tenderness in the sinuses and joints, and laboratory testing showed an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 45 mm/hour and C-reactive protein (CRP) of 18 mg/L. The patient was referred to the rheumatology department at Kagawa University Hospital for further evaluation. ANCA testing was ordered to rule out small vessel vasculitis. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He is able to provide informed consent and is eligible for inclusion in the study.

The patient is a 16-year-old female complaining of repeated regurgitation of food during or soon after eating. She has been experiencing this symptom for the past 6 months. The frequency of repeated regurgitation of food is daily, and she has been re-chewing, re-swallowing, or spitting out the regurgitated material. She has lost about 4 kg in the past 6 months. There are no other gastrointestinal symptoms. Her menstrual cycle is regular, and she is not sexually active. She is not using any drugs, not smoking, and not drinking alcohol. She has no family history of gastrointestinal or psychological problems. She is not taking any psychiatric medications. She has no history of any psychological disorder. Her schoolwork has been affected by this symptom, and she is feeling more anxious and low in mood. She is interested in participating in a study to help manage this symptom.

The patient is a 50 year-old male with slightly reduced kidney function (GFR 70 ml/min) and a body mass index of 25. He has a history of high blood pressure, but it is currently well controlled with medication. He follows a normal daily diet with a composition of 45-50% carbohydrates, 35-40% fats and 15% proteins. He does not have any sorbitol or fructose intolerance, and is not currently taking any antacidic drugs. He is not a vegetarian or vegan, and does not take any nutritional supplements. He does not have any cardiovascular, pulmonary, endocrine or metabolic diseases, and does not abuse drugs. He is not currently taking any anticoagulant drugs.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with no significant medical history. He does not take any medications and has no allergies. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past six months. The patient does not have any chronic illnesses or diseases, and he has not had any recent surgeries or hospitalizations. He does not have a history of substance abuse or addiction. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for the study duration.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for two years with her partner without success. She has regular menstrual cycles and has not been diagnosed with any fertility issues. Her body mass index (BMI) is 25, which is within the normal range. She has no history of allergies or endocrine disorders. She is interested in becoming an oocytes recipient in the study to increase her chances of getting pregnant. She has read and understood the informed consent form and is willing to participate.

70-year-old male veteran who experienced an ischemic stroke two weeks ago. The patient is currently receiving acute rehabilitation and has severe arm deficits that limit his ability to perform activities of daily living independently. The patient has adequate range of motion at the elbow, forearm, wrist, and hand to wear the device. Additionally, the patient can generate volitional, consistent, and detectable EMG signals from the upper arm and forearm sensor sites with wrist in neutral or flexed positions as detected by the Myopro software. The patient has a MAS score of 3 for the biceps, triceps, supinators, and pronators of the impaired arm. The patient is able to read and comprehend the English language and follow directions. The patient is medically and psychologically stable. The patient has no history of hemorrhagic stroke, fixed upper limb contractures on the impaired arm and hand, or involuntary movements of the impaired arm. The patient does not have a pacemaker or other implanted devices and has no metal in the skull. The patient is able to safely support the weight of their arm plus 4 lbs (1.82 kg; the weight of the device) without pain even with arm supported. The patient does not have a skin rash or open wound on the impaired arm. The patient has no past history of seizures or family history of medication refractory epilepsy. The patient is not currently taking medications or substances that lower the threshold for onset of seizure. The patient has no inability to understand English.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for the past three years without success. She has a history of infertility and has undergone multiple in vitro fertilization cycles that have all failed to lead to a clinical pregnancy, despite having at least eight fertilized eggs during each cycle. She has never been pregnant before and is currently seeking assistance in identifying the cause of her infertility. She is married and lives with her husband, who has no known fertility issues. She works as a marketing executive and enjoys hiking and reading in her free time. She has no significant medical history aside from her infertility issues. Her BMI is 22, and her blood pressure and physical exam are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in clinical research to help identify the cause of her infertility and potentially contribute to the development of new treatments for others experiencing similar issues.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of hip joint disease (osteoarthritis) is seeking treatment for severe pain and limited mobility in his right hip. He is a candidate for primary hip replacement surgery and has not undergone any previous hip replacement surgeries or partial hip replacements. The patient is able to read and speak English and is willing to follow all study procedures, fill out patient questionnaires, and be available for evaluation throughout the duration of the study. He has no history of infection or unresolved systemic infection, drug or alcohol abuse, psychological disorders or significant neurological or musculoskeletal disorders that may affect his gait or weight bearing. He is not currently participating in any personal injury litigation, medical-legal or worker's compensation claim. His BMI is within the acceptable range for the study, and he does not have any contraindications for hip replacement surgery.

A 35 year old non-menopausal woman has been experiencing regular menstrual migraines for the past year. She has been prescribed a triptan for relief, which she takes as needed. Despite the medication, she still experiences recurring migraines during her menstrual cycle. She has no history of ear disease or intracranial hypertension, and her blood pressure is well-controlled. She does not have a BMI greater than 30 and is not currently experiencing any allergies or flu symptoms. She is interested in participating in a study to help better understand the potential role of intracranial pressure in the pathophysiology of migraine.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman who underwent a sigmoid colectomy with end colostomy for diverticulitis 3 years ago. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on medications for both conditions. She has been experiencing discomfort and pain around her stoma and has noticed a bulge in the area. The patient speaks Danish and is in good physical health with an ASA score of II. She has not undergone any previous mesh operations in the area and has no history of drug abuse or morphine use. The patient is willing to undergo general anesthesia and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no medical conditions that would contraindicate general anesthesia. She does not have any other hernias that require simultaneous repair.

The patient is a 3-year-old male child who has been experiencing symptoms of croup for the past 24 hours. He has a barking cough, a hoarse voice, and difficulty breathing. He has no history of chronic pulmonary disease except for asthma, and has not received any systemic or inhaled glucocorticoids or epinephrine in the previous 48 hours or 4 hours respectively. His croup score is greater than or equal to 2 after a 30 minute waiting period. The child's parents understand English and have signed the informed consent for the clinical trial. The child has no symptoms or signs of alternative causes of stridor and has not been previously intubated. The child is eligible for the study and will be randomized to receive either 40% or 100% humidity through a nebulizer or the usual humidity set-up.

A 26-year-old man with type 1 diabetes for 5 years has been using an insulin pump for over a year. His HbA1c level is 8.5, indicating poor glycemic control. He checks his blood glucose level four times daily and has never experienced severe hypoglycemic or ketoacidosis episodes within the past year. He is fluent in English and can read the pump screen. He has no known dermal hypersensitivity to products that contain medical adhesive. He is not currently participating in any device or drug studies and is not taking any prescription medications that could complicate the management of glycemic control. He is capable of understanding and completing the treatment satisfaction questionnaire.

30-year-old male with a recent history of travel to West Africa presents to the hospital with fever, headache, muscle aches, and malaise. He reports experiencing nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for the past 2 days. Upon examination, the patient is found to have a temperature of 39.5°C, tachycardia, and hypotension. Labs show thrombocytopenia, elevated transaminases, and elevated creatinine. A rapid antigen test for Lassa fever is positive. The patient is admitted to the hospital for treatment and further evaluation.

45-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of glioblastoma. The patient underwent a surgical resection of the tumor and is now scheduled to start the Stupp protocol, which involves external radiotherapy with concomitant oral temozolomide. The patient has no history of hematological disorders and is covered by social insurance. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the GLIOPLAK clinical trial. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical trial and does not have any other cancer.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic knee osteoarthritis for the past 8 months. She reports experiencing moderate to severe pain in her knee that has been affecting her daily activities, such as walking and climbing stairs. She has been taking acetaminophen for pain relief but has not found it to be very effective. She has no history of other medical disorders and takes no other medications. She has a BMI of 28 and is able to read and write English. She reports no allergies to any medications or components of the cream. She is willing and able to apply the cream three times a day for 30 days and to attend all three clinic visits. She understands the study requirements and is willing to provide written informed consent.

A 35-year-old woman is scheduled to undergo breast reduction surgery due to chronic musculoskeletal pain and breathing difficulties. She has no history of previous breast surgeries or radiation therapy. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any allergies to medications. She does not have any neurological conditions such as myasthenia gravis or amyopathic lateral sclerosis. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy lifestyle. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes to improve the appearance of her surgical scar.

A 27-year-old male university student has been experiencing difficulty breathing through his nose for the past two years. He reports that he has always had difficulty breathing through his nose since he was a child, but it has become progressively worse over the past two years. He denies any history of trauma to his nose or any other medical conditions. He has tried over-the-counter nasal decongestants, but they have provided only temporary relief. He reports that his nasal obstruction has affected his daily life, especially with exercise and sleep. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has no history of allergies or asthma. On physical examination, he has a caudal deviation of the nasal septum with narrowing of the nasal airway. The rest of the nasal exam is unremarkable. He is otherwise healthy and able to tolerate general anesthesia.

28-year-old pregnant woman, G2P1, at 19 weeks gestation, presents for her routine level II ultrasound. She has no significant past medical history and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far. She has no known history of cervical incompetence or preterm labor. She provides written informed consent and is willing to comply with protocol requirements. The E-cervix technology will be used to collect cervical indices during her ultrasound to develop cervical elastography nomograms for singletons.

A 68-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital due to pneumonia. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and amlodipine for her medical conditions. Upon admission, she was prescribed intravenous ceftriaxone for 7 days. Her clinical status improved, and she was switched to oral levofloxacin for an additional 5 days. During her hospital stay, she did not develop diarrhea or any other adverse effects related to her antibiotic treatment. The patient was discharged home with a prescription for levofloxacin for another 5 days. However, she was informed of a clinical trial that she may be eligible for, that aims to prevent antibiotic-associated diarrhea, and she expressed her interest in participating. Her latest laboratory results were as follows: Hgb: 12.5 g/dL, WBC: 8000 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 5000/mm3), Plt: 230000 /ml, Glucose: 120 mg/dL, Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL.

The patient is a 20-year-old male of African-American descent who presented with fatigue, fever, and easy bruising for the last 2 weeks. On examination, he was found to have significant hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and petechiae. A complete blood count showed a white blood cell count of 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin of 8.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 20,000/mm3. A bone marrow biopsy was performed, which confirmed the diagnosis of B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) with a Ph-like signature. Further molecular testing revealed the presence of a JAK2 mutation. The patient completed a 4-drug induction regimen with intrathecal chemotherapy (modified aBFM regimen or equivalent) as per institutional standard of care. He is now eligible for this clinical trial which will test the safety and effectiveness of adding ruxolitinib to standard multi-drug chemotherapy regimen. He is in good physical condition with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0. He has no other significant medical history, is not currently taking any medications, and has no known allergies to any drugs. He has a supportive family and is willing to participate in the study after fully understanding the informed consent document.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of sickle cell disease (SCD)-SS. The patient has a history of frequent vaso-occlusive crises (VOC) requiring hospitalization and treatment with opioids. The patient currently takes hydroxyurea as part of his SCD management. The patient's most recent laboratory test results show leukocytes of 3,500/mcL and platelets of 100,000/mcL. The patient's AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT) levels are within the normal range. The patient has an estimated creatinine clearance of 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. The patient has not experienced any acute complications of SCD over the past four weeks. The patient is not on anticoagulation therapy and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. The patient has a good understanding of the study and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

A 25-year-old female presents with a missing upper central incisor due to trauma from a bicycling accident 6 months ago. She is hesitant to undergo traditional tooth replacement with a bridge due to her dental drill phobia. She has a complete bite on the supporting abutment tooth with no signs of active dental disease. She has no other missing teeth and has a minimum of 12 occluding pairs of natural teeth. Her medical history is unremarkable, with no history of debilitating illnesses or complicating medical conditions. She reports no mobility or pain in the supporting abutment tooth and has not undergone any previous dental restorative work on the abutment tooth. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial for no-preparation resin bonded bridges for the replacement of her missing tooth.

The patient is a 56-year-old male diagnosed with coronary heart disease and primary hypercholesterolemia. Despite taking atorvastatin 10 mg daily, his cholesterol levels remain high. He also has a family history of high cholesterol and heart disease. He has completed a 14-week double-blind efficacy and safety study of ezetimibe co-administered with atorvastatin and showed a positive response. He is interested in enrolling in this long-term safety and tolerability study to receive ezetimibe 10 mg once daily co-administered with atorvastatin 10 to 80 mg daily for up to 12 consecutive months. He is willing to practice effective birth control methods during the study period. He does not have any history of HIV or other significant medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been admitted to the hospital due to sepsis caused by a urinary tract infection. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes and takes medication for both conditions. Upon admission, he was diagnosed with severe sepsis and experienced hypotension with a mean arterial pressure of 60 mmHg. He has no history of peripheral vascular disease or major surgery within the past 24 hours. He agrees to participate in the clinical trial and is randomized into the early norepinephrine group.

A 65-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis in both knees presented to the clinic for elective total knee replacement. She has been experiencing pain in both knees for the past 5 years which has progressively worsened. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of cardiac, neurological, or psychiatric diseases. She has never had any surgeries before. Her medication history includes only over-the-counter pain relievers as needed. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day, 5 days a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. She is not diabetic and has no known coagulopathy. She weighs 70 kg and is 165 cm tall. She is excited about the prospect of pain-free knees after the surgery and is willing to participate in the study.

A 17-year-old female student currently enrolled in the Higher Technical Examination (HTX) program at the Technical College in Aars, Denmark. She is a native Danish speaker and has no known pre-existing medical conditions or diseases. She enjoys spending time with her friends, listening to music, and playing video games in her free time. She is an active participant in school clubs and extracurricular activities, including the debate team and the school newspaper. She values education and is highly motivated to succeed academically. She reports feeling happy and content with her life overall, but is interested in participating in this clinical trial to further explore and improve her health-related quality of life.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman from a rural area in China. She attempted suicide by ingesting pesticides due to financial stress and relationship problems. She was hospitalized for a week and received treatment for the poisoning. She has a history of depression and anxiety but has never sought mental health treatment. She lives with her husband and two children and works as a farmer. She has a basic education and has limited access to mental health services in her area. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to communicate effectively in Mandarin. She has a mobile phone and is available for the home visits.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who was admitted to the hospital due to altered mental status. She was found by her family at home, confused and unable to communicate effectively. She has no significant medical history, but her family reports that she occasionally experiences seizures. She denies any recent head trauma, fever or infections. On examination, she is lethargic and disoriented, with no focal neurological deficits. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Initial laboratory tests, including electrolytes and blood glucose, are normal. CT scan of the brain is negative for any acute abnormalities. The neurologist suspects non-convulsive status epilepticus and requests an EEG for confirmation. As the EEG technologist is not available at the moment, the neurology resident requests the patient's consent to participate in the clinical trial that involves placement of an EEG cap. The patient consents, and the resident places the EEG cap on the patient's head. The study team records the time from the request for the EEG cap to its placement and the confirmation or exclusion of NCSE. The EEG interpretation will be performed by two independent EEG interpreters blinded to clinical history, and a third reader will be called in case of disagreement.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with Waldenstrom's Macroglobulinemia after presenting with fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats. She has no prior history of malignancy and her CD20 status was confirmed with bone marrow immunohistochemistry. The patient has not received any prior therapies for her condition. She currently experiences symptoms of symptomatic WM and has measurable disease. Her life expectancy is greater than 12 weeks and her organ and marrow function are adequate. She has not undergone major surgery within the past 21 days and does not have any acute active infections requiring treatment. The patient has no known history of allergy to Captisol and is not currently receiving any other study agents. She has no known brain metastases and does not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to carfilzomib, rituximab, and/or dexamethasone. The patient is not contraindicated to any of the required concomitant drugs or supportive treatments. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is not HIV-positive on combination antiretroviral therapy.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma 3 years ago. She has been using latanoprost eye drops daily since then, which has helped to control her intraocular pressure. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She has no history of diabetes or any ocular or immunologic diseases. She does not have any contraindications for MRI examination. Her most recent visual field test showed mild-to-moderate loss of vision in the superior and inferior visual fields of both eyes. Her optic nerve head had a cup/disc ratio of 0.8, indicating significant glaucomatous damage. She is able to perform daily activities without difficulty but has noticed some difficulty with night vision and driving. She has a mini-mental state exam score of 30/30 and is willing to participate in the study.

A 12-year-old boy with end-stage renal disease requiring regular hemodialysis, with a serum phosphorus level of 5.2mg/dL. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 2 years due to a congenital renal disease that progressed to end-stage renal disease. He is currently taking calcium-containing phosphate binders but has not achieved adequate control of his serum phosphorus levels. He has no known hypersensitivity to phosphate binders and has not experienced any severe gastrointestinal disorders. His parents have provided informed consent for his participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a male newborn diagnosed with X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (XLHED). The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as he has received at least one dose of EDI200 in the neonate study ECP-002. The patient's parents have provided written informed consent for participation in the trial. The patient has not experienced any medically significant postnatal complications or congenital anomalies outside of those associated with XLHED. The patient will continue to be evaluated in the ECP-002e extension study up to age 10 years, with no additional study drug administration planned. The patient's growth and development parameters, frequency of infections and hospitalizations, and age-appropriate assessments of ectoderm-derived organ function will be evaluated. The patient's safety will be monitored through physical examinations, adverse events and concomitant medication documentation, and laboratory testing.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been diagnosed with multidrug-resistant pulmonary tuberculosis. He has been receiving treatment for two months but has not shown any improvement. The patient has a family history of tuberculosis and has been living in close proximity to someone with active TB. He has been experiencing persistent cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath for the past few months. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial for FS-1 drug for the treatment of MDR-TB. He is intellectually capable of understanding the requirements of the study protocol and is willing to comply with all the requirements. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, has no severe mental disorders, and is not allergic to iodine-containing drugs. He is willing to adhere to TB therapy and is able to give signed informed consent.

A 35-year-old married man who works as an accountant came to the urology clinic for an elective vasectomy procedure. He has two children and his wife does not want to have any more children due to the financial burden of raising them. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly by going for a jog every morning. He has no history of anxiety or depression, but he is nervous about the procedure. He is open to wearing VR goggles during the procedure to help alleviate his anxiety. He has no history of vision problems or any other medical conditions that would preclude him from participation in the study. He has read the informed consent and is willing to participate.

A 36-year-old man visited the gastroenterology clinic due to chronic constipation, which he has been experiencing for over a year. He has tried several over-the-counter medications for constipation relief, but none of them have been effective. He has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or surgeries. He is generally healthy, and his past medical history and family history are unremarkable. He doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. He has no significant allergies to medications or foods. He takes a daily multivitamin supplement, but no other medications. His bowel movements are infrequent, with an average of 2 bowel movements per week, and he experiences abdominal discomfort and bloating. He underwent a colonoscopy 5 years ago, which was normal. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a new treatment for constipation, and he is willing to use an electronic daily diary to report bowel movements, symptoms, and medication usage.

A 38-year-old mother of two children, aged 7 and 11, presents to the clinic seeking help to cope with the stress of COVID-19 pandemic. She reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious due to the constant news about the virus and the changes in daily life, such as school closures and social distancing. She reports difficulty sleeping, eating and concentrating, and feels irritable and on edge most of the time. She reports no history of severe mental illness or hospitalization for mental health concerns. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study. Her two children are within the age range of the study criteria.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with high blood pressure. He complains of occasional headaches and dizziness but has no other significant medical history. He is currently not taking any medication for his high blood pressure. His blood pressure, measured on two separate occasions, is consistently above 140/90 mmHg. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the early use of a combination of cholesterol and blood pressure lowering tablets in young hypertensive patients. The patient is willing to comply with all the requirements of the study and has a good understanding of the potential benefits and risks associated with the trial. He has given his informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of obesity and prediabetes. He has been experiencing fatigue and occasional abdominal pain. An ultrasound showed he has non-alcoholic hepatic steatosis (fatty liver disease). The patient does not have a history of alcoholism or hepatitis B or C. He is not currently taking any vitamin supplements or receiving parenteral nutrition. The patient has not experienced significant weight loss in the past month. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to reduce the severity of his fatty liver disease and alleviate his symptoms.

A 62-year-old woman has been suffering from chronic bronchitis for the past 3 years. She experiences a persistent cough with sputum production and dyspnea on exertion. Her CAT score is 12 and her SGRQ score is 35. She has a smoking history of 45 pack years and quit smoking 2 years ago. Her pre-bronchodilator FEV1 is 60% of predicted and she had two COPD exacerbations in the past year. She has a history of hypertension, managed with medication, and mild GERD, which is controlled by proton pump inhibitors. She is able to walk more than 100 meters in 6 minutes without any significant discomfort. She has not had any respiratory infections in the past 6 weeks and is not currently taking any prednisone. She has never had lung surgery or any other lung-related interventions. She is willing to undergo two bronchoscopies and has provided informed consent. She does not have any implantable devices, pacemakers, or unresolved lung cancer. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical investigational studies and has no known sensitivity to the medication required for the study.

42-year-old female, weighing 70kg, with a history of hypertension, presents to the clinic for a routine check-up. She reports having blood pressure readings of 135/85 mmHg on average over the past few months. She has no known allergies and is not pregnant. She is currently not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medication. She has no history of drug abuse or participation in any clinical trials with an investigational compound or device within the past 30 days. She has no gastrointestinal history or suspected acute disease. Upon informed consent, she is eligible to participate in this clinical trial evaluating the pharmacokinetic drug interactions between single and concomitant administrations of amlodipine, losartan, and hydrochlorothiazide.

A 44-year-old man was diagnosed with glioblastoma with a definitive resection that left residual radiographic contrast enhancement of <1 cm in maximal diameter in any axial plane. The biopsy revealed an unmethylated MGMT gene promoter. He is currently experiencing headaches, seizures, and difficulty concentrating. His Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score is 80, and he has no significant medical history. His lab tests showed a hemoglobin level of 12.5 g/dL, an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1,400 cells/µL, and a platelet count of 150,000 cells/µL. His serum creatinine and AST are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he is willing to use a highly effective contraceptive method. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial after providing a signed informed consent approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB).

50-year-old female with a history of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Type I, diagnosed 3 years ago, currently on oral treatment for PAH. She has no other cardiac or pulmonary disease and is willing to provide written informed consent. She has no cognitive or linguistic barriers and is able to actively participate in a 30-minute interview. The patient is interested in exploring different modes of treatment administration and is open to the possibility of subcutaneous injections.

A 62 year old male with a history of heart failure for the past 7 years. The patient has been hospitalized twice in the past 6 months due to heart failure exacerbation despite optimal medical management. The patient has undergone cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) and implantation of an ICD. He is currently in NYHA class III and has been stable on medical therapy for the past 3 months. The patient is willing and able to attend scheduled visits at the Day-Care Unit for Patients With Refractory Heart Failure and is compliant with medical recommendations.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who has been on corticosteroid therapy for rheumatoid arthritis for the past 6 months. She is currently taking prednisone 10mg daily. The patient has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she is taking amlodipine 5mg daily and atorvastatin 20mg daily, respectively. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She is interested in participating in the study to determine if the DASH diet can help mitigate the metabolic side effects of corticosteroid therapy. She is willing to comply with the study visits and follow the DASH diet plan.

Nadia is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing chest pain on and off for the past 6 months. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and is a smoker. She is currently taking medication for her hypertension and high cholesterol levels. Nadia underwent a stress test and was diagnosed with intermediate-grade coronary stenosis. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of the Zurich Pressure Guidewire System and Abbott PressureWire System in measuring fractional flow reserve. Nadia is willing to undergo the intrusive ICA and FFR measurement required for participation in the study. She is aware of the exclusion criteria and has confirmed that she does not have any other serious diseases or contraindications for coronary intervention surgery or ATP. Nadia has provided her consent and is excited to be a participant in this study to help advance the understanding of coronary heart disease treatment.

An 83-year-old woman resides in a nursing-home in Saint Laurent-de-Chamousset, France, where she has lived for the past year due to her limited mobility caused by osteoarthritis. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are both well-controlled with medication. Her last blood test, taken 2 months ago, showed a vitamin D level of 22 ng/mL. She received bolus vitamin D3 supplementation 1 month ago as per the nursing-home's protocol. Two weeks ago, she developed a fever, cough, and shortness of breath, and was subsequently diagnosed with COVID-19 through RT-PCR testing. Her World Health Organization's Ordinal Scale for Clinical Improvement (OSCI) score was 4, indicating hospitalization and oxygen therapy. She was hospitalized for 5 days and treated with antiviral therapy. Her current condition is stable, and she is being closely monitored in the nursing-home. She and her family have agreed to the use of her anonymized clinical-biological data for this study.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is a survey-based study focused on assessing psychological distress and burnout among physicians in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study is not recruiting patients, but rather surveying physicians who are currently practicing in Canada.

This is a 65 year-old male who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation after experiencing palpitations and shortness of breath. He has no prior history of stroke or neurological complications. He does not have a pacemaker or any metal implants. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication regularly. He has no history of vascular or degenerative dementia, brain tumors, severe brain injury, or psychiatric disorders. He is not currently pregnant. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to better understand the impact of his atrial fibrillation on his cognitive function and to explore potential therapeutic interventions to prevent silent strokes.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who presented with enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and armpits. He reported experiencing night sweats and fatigue for the past month. The biopsy of the lymph node revealed a diagnosis of Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma (PTCL). The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. He has never received chemotherapy or radiotherapy for any medical condition. His vital signs are within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets all of the eligibility criteria, including having stage III disease with at least one measurable tumor lesion, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 2 or less. He has given written informed consent and is willing to comply with all aspects of the protocol. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraception throughout the study period.

The patient is a 50-year-old Japanese woman who has been diagnosed with non-hematologic malignancy. She has exhausted all standard treatment options and is looking for alternative treatment options. She is in good overall health, with an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no major medical conditions or significant toxicities from prior chemotherapy, and her renal, hepatic, and bone marrow function are within normal limits. She has no history of stroke or cerebrovascular accident within the last 6 months and has not undergone major surgery in the last 28 days. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or actively being treated for a secondary malignancy. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and is looking forward to participating in the trial to assess the safety and efficacy of defactinib (VS-6063).

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing severe, chronic pain for over 6 months. He describes his pain as a constant burning sensation in his lower back and legs, which is exacerbated by movement. He has tried various non-opioid pain medications, but they have provided little relief. He is currently taking a combination of tramadol and acetaminophen, but it only provides temporary relief. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has a family history of hypertension, but his blood pressure is currently within normal limits. He works as a construction worker and is currently on disability leave due to his chronic pain. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially find a more effective treatment option for his pain.

The patient is a 56-year-old man with a history of excessive alcohol consumption for the last 20 years. He has been diagnosed with decompensated cirrhosis of the liver, which was confirmed through an abdominal ultrasound. The patient's complaints include abdominal distension, fatigue, and jaundice. He has also experienced episodes of hepatic encephalopathy and ascites, for which he has been receiving medical treatment. The laboratory studies show elevated bilirubin, decreased albumin, and elevated INR. The patient has no history of allergies or any other significant medical illness. He is married and has two adult children. He has stopped drinking alcohol since his diagnosis, and his family is supportive of his treatment. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent. He understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old man with a diagnosis of stage IV colon cancer. He has been receiving chemotherapy for the past 3 months and has experienced significant weight loss of more than 5% of his total body weight during the previous 6 months. The patient has a history of hypertension and diabetes, which are currently well-controlled with medications. He has no history of allergies or other medical conditions that would impair his ability to participate in the study. The patient is currently receiving oral chemotherapy medications and is expected to continue receiving chemotherapy for at least one more month. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 6 months. His serum creatinine, SGOT, SGPT, and total bilirubin levels are within normal limits. The patient is able to swallow oral medication and to meet his nutritional requirements via the oral route with food and/or oral supplements. He is not taking any corticosteroids, estrogens, progestins, or any other steroid hormone during the study period. He has not taken Oxandrin or Megestrol acetate for at least 3 months before the start of the study. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and he has a BMI of 29.

A 15-year-old boy with a history of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis since childhood was referred to the clinic due to poor response to topical treatments including corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors and phototherapy. He has been experiencing severe itching, redness, and scaling on his arms, legs, and trunk. He has missed school several times due to discomfort caused by the symptoms. He has no history of any other autoimmune or inflammatory diseases. The patient and his parents are willing to discontinue any current AD medication and interested in participating in the study. He has no history of coagulation disorders, infections, or malignancies. He is currently not taking any medication and has no known drug allergy. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. His weight is 65 kg and his height is 170 cm.

The patient is a 13-year-old Hispanic male who has been diagnosed with persistent asthma of moderate severity. He lives in Pittsburgh with his mother who works as a nurse and his younger sister. He attends a local middle school and enjoys playing basketball with his friends. He has been experiencing asthma symptoms for the past year, including coughing, wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath, especially during physical activity. He is currently taking a daily controller medication as prescribed by his doctor, but still experiences occasional asthma attacks that require the use of a rescue inhaler. He has access to the internet and a smartphone, and is willing to download the AirNow app as part of the study. His mother is supportive of his participation in the study and is willing to attend the education sessions and assist him in following the asthma action plan. The family has no plans to leave the Pittsburgh area in the next 6 months.

A 19-year-old male presented to the clinic with a history of moderate to severe acne that has persisted for over two years. The patient reported multiple unsuccessful attempts at treating his acne with various over-the-counter products. Physical examination revealed numerous comedones, papules, and pustules on the patient's face and upper back, consistent with moderate to severe acne as per Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) score of 3. The patient reported no allergies and was not pregnant.

The patient is a 28 year old female medical worker who has been working at a hospital for the past 2 years. She has been following all the recommended safety protocols for COVID-19, but is still concerned about the potential risks of contracting the virus. She has no known allergies and has not had any adverse reactions to vaccines in the past. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help further the research and development of a safe and effective vaccine against COVID-19.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has a history of obesity and diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing fatigue and abdominal discomfort for the past few months. He underwent an ultrasound scan that showed fatty liver infiltration, which was confirmed by a non-invasive imaging study. He has been advised to undergo bariatric surgery to lose weight and improve his metabolic status. He has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that aims to establish non-invasive tools to accurately diagnose patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The study will involve collection of blood, faeces, and exhaled air samples, and a FibroScan (+CAP) will be performed during a study visit. An MRI will also be performed to estimate the degree of steatosis. He will undergo a liver biopsy during the bariatric surgery for study purposes only. He has been informed that there may be unexpected findings by MRI and histopathologic evaluation of the liver biopsy, and that he will be informed about these. He has also been informed that he will need to follow-up with the study team 3 months post-surgery, during which time follow-up measurements will be taken. He has been informed of the study's exclusion criteria, including liver cirrhosis and/or hepatocellular carcinoma, and chronic use of immunosuppressants.

The patient is a 14-month-old infant who has been experiencing watery or soft stools for the past 24-48 hours, with a frequency of 3 or more per day. The infant has been clinically diagnosed with mild to moderate dehydration, with a Bailey scale score ranging from 1 to 4. The infant is available throughout the study period and will be re-examined on the 7th day from the enrolment. The parents or legal guardian have given their signed informed consent and are mentally capable of understanding and willing to fulfil all the details of the protocol. The infant has not experienced diarrhoea lasting more than 48 hours or clinical signs of severe dehydration with a Bailey scale score of 5 or more. The infant is not malnourished as judged by a body weight/height ratio above the 5th percentile. The infant does not have clinical signs of a coexisting severe acute systemic illness such as meningitis, sepsis, or pneumonia, nor does the infant have immunodeficiency, severe chronic disease including cystic fibrosis, or any food allergy diagnosed by a physician or other chronic gastrointestinal diseases. The infant has not used pre-/probiotics in the previous 2 weeks or antibiotics or any anti-diarrhoeal medication in the previous 4 weeks.

The patient is a 45 year-old woman who has a BMI of 35 kg/m² and has been diagnosed with moderate to severe asthma. She experiences shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing, especially during physical activities. She has been using inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators as part of her asthma management plan. She has a history of smoking but has quit for the last 5 years. She has no other active pulmonary diseases or neuromuscular diseases. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of aerosol deposition in obese asthmatics using heliox. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is able to perform the procedures required for the study. She is looking forward to contributing to the advancement of asthma treatment for obese patients.

A 21-year-old African American woman who lives in Baltimore City came to the clinic seeking to participate in a clinical trial to reduce sexual risk behaviors. She reported experiencing homelessness for a short period of time within the past year and is currently unemployed. She owns a mobile phone with text messaging function and has reported at least one episode of unprotected/unsafe sex in the prior 12 months. She is not currently enrolled in school and is interested in HIV prevention and business educational sessions, as well as a mentored apprenticeship and start-up grant. She is willing to provide consent for study participation and is excited to potentially benefit from the study's intervention to reduce sexual risk behaviors.

The patient is a 62-year-old postmenopausal woman who has been diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. The patient is in relatively good health and has no significant medical history, except for hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. The patient has undergone a biopsy and has confirmed HER2-positive and hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. The tumor size is approximately 2 cm and is located in the right breast. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery, either segmental resection or total mastectomy. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has no history of prior chemotherapy or hormonal therapy for breast cancer. The patient is randomized to receive either lapatinib and letrozole or letrozole and placebo for 2 weeks, followed by lapatinib and letrozole for 14 weeks. Tissue samples will be collected at baseline, at 2 weeks, and at the time of surgery for biomarker and laboratory studies. The patient is able to swallow and retain oral medication and has normal cardiac ejection fraction as determined by echocardiogram.

A 6-year-old boy is scheduled for a laparoscopic orchiopexy due to undescended testes. He has no significant medical history and is classified as ASA I. He is not allergic to any local anesthetics. His parents have given written consent for him to participate in the study. He is able to communicate and follow instructions. He has no bleeding disorders and has never had any surgeries before. He is not currently taking any medications.

A 52-year-old male with a history of inflammatory bowel disease and gallstones presents to the emergency department with acute abdominal pain. After evaluation, he is diagnosed with a bowel obstruction requiring emergency surgery. He is approached to participate in a clinical trial aimed at creating a metabolic signature or 'phenotype' for surgical injury that will help clinicians choose the right surgical treatments for an individual. The study will use a scientific method based on computational analysis of spectra taken from techniques known as Mass Spectrometry (MS) and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. The investigators aim to integrate the metabolic data with genetic information about the patient wherever possible. The study will involve a heterogeneous patient cohort, including those undergoing elective procedures and those undergoing emergency procedures. The patient is informed that samples will be collected at set time points during his surgical journey, including pre-operation, intra-operation, and post-operation. The patient is eligible for the study and consents to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old Vietnamese man who is a regular attendee of methadone maintenance therapy (MMT) for opioid use disorder. During the regular MMT consultation, he reported a history of methamphetamine use and screened positive for recent methamphetamine use on urine analysis. He scored high (27+) on the ASSIST for methamphetamine use. The patient has no known history of psychosis or other interfering problems and is willing to provide at least three pieces of contact information. He has a cell phone and is willing to receive text messages. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his HIV outcomes and reduce his methamphetamine use.

A 50 year old woman comes to the clinic for a follow-up procedure after a coronary stent implantation 5 years ago. She has been experiencing occasional chest pain and shortness of breath during physical activity. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She has not experienced any major cardiovascular events since the stent implantation. She is scheduled for a diagnostic coronary procedure, and willing to participate in the study. She has signed the informed consent and is not pregnant or lactating. She does not have any life-threatening comorbidities that would exclude her from the study.

56 year old man diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the rectum 3 years ago. He underwent surgical resection and received adjuvant chemotherapy. He was then followed up regularly and remained disease-free for 2 years before presenting with recurrent rectal cancer. The recurrent lesion was confirmed by contrast-enhanced CT and MRI. The patient is classified as R0 on pathological diagnosis. The main tumor location is in the middle rectum. There is no distant metastasis on contrast-enhanced CT. The estimated circumferential resection margin is >0 mm. The patient has not received prior pelvic irradiation or surgery for recurrent rectal cancer. He has received systemic chemotherapy for any malignancies and the final dose was administered more than 14 days ago. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0. The patient's measurable lesion is not mandatory. The patient has adequate oral intake and sufficient organ function. Open or laparoscopic surgery is planned. The patient meets all the eligibility criteria and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with multiple myeloma based on the presence of monoclonal plasma cells in his bone marrow and the presence of anemia and renal insufficiency. He has no history of previous anti-myeloma therapy and is eligible for autologous stem cell transplantation. His serum M-protein level is 2.5 g/dL and his urine M-protein level is 400 mg/24 hours. His creatinine clearance is 60 mL/minute, and his corrected serum calcium is 12.5 mg/dL. He has no history of significant neuropathy and has an ECOG status of 1. He has a history of hypertension, which is currently controlled with medication. He has no history of other significant medical diseases or conditions that would interfere with protocol adherence or his ability to give informed consent. He is willing to comply with the study visits and procedures required per protocol and has provided written informed consent in accordance with federal, local, and institutional guidelines prior to initiation of any study-specific activities or procedures. He has agreed to practice contraception during the treatment and for 5 months after the last dose of study drugs.

A 52-year-old male smoker was recently diagnosed with unresectable stage III non-small-cell lung cancer. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit smoking 6 months ago. The patient complained of coughing, chest pain, and shortness of breath. CT scan and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of lung cancer. He has not received any prior treatment for lung cancer, including thoracic radiotherapy or EGFR-TKIs. His performance status is 1 according to the ECOG scale, and he is expected to live for at least 4 months. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. The patient has good compliance with the study procedures and can cooperate with the relevant examination, treatment, and follow-up. He has no other concurrent malignancies or severe systemic diseases that would preclude study participation. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is not currently undergoing any other anti-cancer treatment.

A 35-year-old man was admitted to the surgical service due to appendicitis. He has no history of any chronic disease or previous surgeries. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and exercises regularly. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He takes occasional over-the-counter painkillers for headache or muscle pain. He has no known allergies to any medication. He has a family history of hypertension and diabetes. Upon admission, he consented to participate in the clinical trial on the effect of skin antisepsis on phlebitis. He was randomly assigned to one of the two groups and received either 2% chlorhexidine or 70% alcohol antiseptic solution during the intravenous catheter insertion. He was also given ceftriaxone, ornidazole, and paracetamol through the catheter for his treatment. The catheter was covered with a sterile, transparent, semi-permeable, self-adhesive catheter stabilizer. He was monitored for the development of phlebitis using the "Phlebitis Scale" published by the Infusion Nurses Association every 8 hours for 72 hours.

62-year-old male with a history of smoking and a previous diagnosis of stage IV non-squamous NSCLC. Despite undergoing first-line chemotherapy, the patient's disease progressed, leading to the need for second-line treatment. The patient's performance status is 1, and he has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. He has no history of other malignancies within the last 5 years and has adequate organ function. The patient has measurable lesions by RECIST 1.1 and does not have an activating EGFR mutation or ALK rearrangement. The patient has not been previously treated with docetaxel and has not received radiation therapy within the past 3 months prior to baseline imaging. The patient has no active brain metastases and does not have uncontrolled arterial hypertension, significant arrhythmia, or myocardial infarction less than 12 months before study entry. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, incarcerated or institutionalized. The patient is willing to use double effective contraception as he is of child-bearing potential.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) due to hypertension and diabetes. He has been receiving hemodialysis three times a week for the past 6 months through an arteriovenous fistula in his left arm. He has a history of peripheral vascular disease and has undergone a bypass surgery in his right leg. He is currently taking medications for hypertension, diabetes, and high cholesterol.
