He lives alone and is able to independently perform activities of daily living. He has noticed that his blood pressure drops during hemodialysis, which causes him to feel dizzy and lightheaded. He is interested in participating in this study to see if the pneumatic compression devices can help him maintain his blood pressure during hemodialysis.

A 38-year-old male with a history of functional dyspepsia for the past 6 months, with symptoms including bothersome postprandial fullness, early satiation, epigastric pain, and epigastric soreness. Despite receiving appropriate medical treatment including prokinetics, analgesics, H2-receptor antagonists, proton pump inhibitors, antacids, serotonin receptor antagonists, and antidepressants, the patient has not experienced any improvement in symptoms. The patient's dyspepsia symptoms disrupt daily life with a global overall symptom scale score of 7. The patient has undergone medical tests and imaging, which have shown normal findings, and thus, the possibility of bile dyspepsia cannot be eliminated. The patient has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgery and has no biliary disease, structural modification, systemic disease, or endocrinology-metabolic disease. The patient does not have any disease or damage in the central nervous system or autonomic nervous system. The patient has no renal disorder or electrolyte imbalance. The patient is not taking any medication that can provoke abdominal symptoms. The patient is willing to discontinue any medication that may interfere with the study. The patient has submitted written consent to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) following routine blood work. He reports feeling fatigued and experiencing night sweats for the past few weeks. He has no significant past medical history and denies any previous cancer diagnoses. He is a current smoker with a 30 pack-year history and reports occasional alcohol use. He has no known allergies to medications. He is married with two adult children and works as a retired engineer. His ECOG performance status is 1. His creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dl and total bilirubin level is 2.8 mg/dl. His ejection fraction is 50%. He has not received any prior anti-leukemic therapy. He is interested in participating in clinical trials and wants to know if he is eligible for this study.

A 32-year-old man presented with nasal congestion and recurrent epistaxis for the past 3 months. The patient has a history of hypertension for which he is taking medication. He doesn't smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. On examination, there is a palpable mass on the right side of the nasal cavity. The CT scan revealed a 3 cm mass without lymph node involvement. The biopsy showed histological evidence of NK/T-cell lymphoma. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. Bone marrow and organ functions are adequate. The patient has no other significant medical history. The patient has not received any treatment for this condition in the past.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus at the age of 21. She has been on continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) for the past 5 years. She has a history of poor glycemic control with a HbA1c of 9.5% at her last visit. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m² and a waist circumference of 34 inches. She reports difficulty managing her blood sugar levels especially after meals and has expressed interest in learning carbohydrate counting. She has no known hypothyroidism, renal disease, celiac disease, or other serious illnesses that could interfere with study assessments. She is willing to participate in a 6-month trial to evaluate the effectiveness of carbohydrate counting on glycemic control and quality of life.

54 y/o male admitted to the ICU with septic shock due to pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. Upon admission, he was hypotensive with a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg and tachycardic with a heart rate of 120 beats per minute. He was started on vasopressors and antibiotics. His condition has improved with treatment, but he still requires vasopressor support. His family members have provided informed consent for his participation in the clinical trial. He has no contraindications to Xigris and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old man with congenital intellectual disability. He communicates using aided Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) and has been supported by the same worker in a residential service for adults with ID for the past 2 years. The worker has received training in Key Word Signing (KWS), a specific form of AAC, and has been using this method with the patient for the past 6 months. The patient has mild cerebral palsy affecting his right arm and leg, but he is able to walk independently. He enjoys listening to music and watching movies. He has good relationships with his peers and staff at the residential service, and he participates in various activities organized by the service. His health is generally good, and he does not have any known visual impairments or autism.

The patient is a 27-year-old non-smoking female with a BMI of 21. She has no history of significant illnesses and has normal blood pressure and heart rate. She has been using hormonal contraceptives for the past 6 months and has not had any significant changes in her diet or eating habits. She has not participated in any investigational drug studies in the past 3 months and has not donated blood in the past 3 months. She does not have any known allergies to the ingredients of the test or reference products. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study and has provided a signed written informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been hospitalized with community acquired pneumonia. She has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. She presents with a cough, fever, and shortness of breath. Her physical exam is significant for decreased breath sounds in the left lower lung field. Her chest x-ray confirms left lower lobe consolidation. She is admitted to the hospital and started on intravenous azythromycin therapy. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She has never had a history of pneumonia before. Her past surgical history is not significant. Her family history is negative for any significant medical issues. Her labs show a white blood cell count of 14,000/mm3 and C-reactive protein of 30 mg/L. She is tolerating the intravenous therapy well but expresses interest in switching to oral therapy as soon as possible.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath during physical activity and occasional chest pain for the past few months. He is a former smoker, having quit 5 years ago, and has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history or family history of cardiovascular disease. A transthoracic echocardiogram revealed moderate mitral regurgitation, with an ejection fraction of 50%. He is currently not experiencing any clinical signs of heart failure. The patient is interested in participating in the 3D-PRIME study to help improve risk stratification and cardiovascular outcome for patients with mitral regurgitation.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU due to sepsis and acute respiratory failure. He requires mechanical ventilation and has been hospitalized for less than 48 hours. He has a Clinical Frailty Scale score of 3 and meets all the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial. He has no history of brain damage, psychiatric illness, or cognitive impairment, and does not have any contraindications for mobilization. He weighs 80kg and has not undergone mechanical ventilation treatment for more than 72 hours. He voluntarily consents to participate in this clinical trial and is interested in improving his physical function after ICU discharge.

A 5-month-old full-term infant who was exclusively breastfed for the first 6 months of life. The mother has introduced solid foods to the infant's diet and is considering introducing iron-fortified cereals or meat as the first solid food. The infant has not had any medical conditions and weighs more than 2500g at birth. The infant has not consumed more than 200ml of formula. The parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the safest and healthiest first solid food for their infant.

A 26 year old woman with type 1 diabetes for 5 years comes to the clinic for a regular checkup. She uses insulin pump and frequently monitors her blood glucose levels using a glucometer. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new flash glucose monitoring system, the freestyle Libre. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is willing to wear the device and comply with the study protocol during the entire duration of the same. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m² and her HbA1c is within the normal range. She has no known allergies to patches or skin disinfectants and no skin lesions or irritation that may interfere with the placement of the device. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use contraception during the study period. She has no known disorders of the adrenal glands, pancreatic tumors, or insulinomas. She has no serious medical or psychological conditions that could compromise her safety during study participation.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis. She has been experiencing difficulty in maintaining her balance and has fallen a few times in the past. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, she has been staying at home and has been unable to continue her regular rehabilitation sessions. She is interested in participating in a home-based exercise program that can help improve her balance and reduce her risk of falls. She is able to walk independently with the use of a cane and her Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score is 5. She does not have any other neurological or musculoskeletal disorders that affect her balance. She does not engage in any exercise program currently, and is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial study that compares the effectiveness of the Otago exercise program (OEP) to a control group that gets health awareness videos only. She understands that the study will involve baseline and end-of-program assessments, and follow-up questions about falls will be asked in 6 and 12 months post-treatment. She is willing to be visited at her home each 2 weeks as part of the treatment group, and progress her exercises according to the OEP instructions. She is willing to adhere to the instructions provided by the study team.

29 F with a history of eczema and occasional contact dermatitis triggered by various personal care products. She is currently not taking any medications and has not used any topical or systemic steroids or antihistamines for the past 2 weeks. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test for potential skin irritation or allergy from a chemical agent. She understands and has executed the Informed Consent Form, is capable of following directions, and is considered reliable. She is aged within the eligibility range of 16 to 79 years old.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has a history of dental caries and recently experienced sensitivity and mild pain in her lower left second molar. She visited her dentist for a routine dental check-up where an X-ray revealed a deep cavity that had reached the pulp of the tooth. The dentist recommended pulpotomy to prevent further damage to the tooth and preserve the pulp. The patient is in good health with no significant medical history and is able to return for scheduled recalls. She has no other dental problems and has never had a tooth extraction. The patient signed a consent form and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a parental history of Alzheimer's disease. He has a history of elevated cholesterol levels and has been previously diagnosed with hypertension. He is currently taking lisinopril to manage his blood pressure. He has no history of liver disease or adverse reactions to statins. He has no history of dementia or other neurological disorders. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. He does not consume large quantities of grapefruit juice. He is not currently involved in another investigational drug study. He is willing to undergo lumbar puncture and MRI procedures as part of the study.

A 45 year old woman has recently been diagnosed with acute leukemia and is scheduled to undergo induction chemotherapy. She has no known allergies or intolerances to medications and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to prevent the development of oral mucositis, a common complication of chemotherapy. She is able to attend all follow-up visits and has the capacity to provide written informed consent. However, she has a history of chronic kidney disease with a basal blood creatinine level of 2.2 mg/dL, which makes her ineligible for the trial.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been experiencing abdominal pain and jaundice for the past 2 months. He also reports a loss of appetite and unexplained weight loss. A CT scan reveals a mass in his bile ducts and a biopsy confirms a diagnosis of biliary tract cancer. The cancer has already spread and surgery is not an option. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and all his organ functions are within normal range. He has not received any prior chemotherapy and is not on any investigational agents. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

A 42 year old female with a history of diabetes and a non-healing wound on her left foot has been undergoing hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) for the past week. She has no history of cardiovascular or respiratory disease, psychiatric illness or smoking. She has not experienced any facial or ENT problems or previous complications with HBOT. She is currently not taking any analgesics. She has never had tympanostomy tubes. In this clinical trial, she will undergo audiometric evaluation including tympanometry and basic pure tone audiometry following each of the first five HBOT treatments.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past year. She has noticed that she frequently wakes up during the night and has trouble falling back asleep. She also feels tired and fatigued during the day, despite getting what she feels is enough sleep. She has never been diagnosed with sleep apnea or COPD, but has a family history of sleep disorders. She has also been experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression, including feelings of worry and sadness. She has not been formally diagnosed with either condition, but has noticed that her symptoms have been affecting her daily life. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of CPAP therapy on anxiety and depression in patients with sleep apnea.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who regularly performs physical activity and has experience with strength training. He has not suffered any neural, muscular, skeletal or connective tissue injuries in the last 12 months in the area of the back, hips and legs. He has no history of groin injuries or surgeries in the area. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He has no chronic medical conditions and is not taking any medications. His BMI is within normal range, and he has no known allergies. He is willing to perform new hip adductor exercises using the novelty device and participate in electromyographic (EMG) and kinematic signal capturing. He understands the purpose of the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 49-year-old woman with a diagnosis of advanced cervical cancer. She underwent surgery and radiation therapy as primary treatment, but the disease has progressed despite multiple lines of chemotherapy. She presents with progressive symptoms, including pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, and unintentional weight loss. Her performance status is ECOG 1. She has no significant comorbidities and is otherwise in good health. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and for at least 12 weeks after the last dose of study treatment. She is able to swallow capsules and/or has no surgical or anatomical condition that precludes swallowing and absorbing oral medication on an ongoing basis. She has no history of stem cell transplantation or solid organ transplantation. She has no other malignancies, except for adequately treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma or carcinoma in situ, within the last 3 years. She is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 9-year-old child with a clinical diagnosis of mild persistent asthma is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. The child is currently not on any steroid inhalation or ingestion. The child is able to swallow tablets. The child is attending school regularly and is experiencing difficulty in keeping up with the studies. The child is not experiencing any other health issues and has no history of allergies. The child is living with both parents and has no family history of asthma.

34 yo M with a history of non-seminomatous testicular cancer treated with orchidectomy and cisplatin-bleomycin combination chemotherapy at the University Hospital Groningen in 1995 is being invited to participate in a study investigating cardiovascular morbidity in testicular cancer survivors. The study aims to identify risk factors for cardiovascular disease following testicular cancer, examine the pathway(s) of CVD development, and investigate genetic polymorphisms in pathogenetically important pathways that are potentially involved in the development of treatment-related cardiovascular morbidity. The patient will undergo assessments of their cardiovascular risk factors and the presence of subclinical cardiovascular damage by means of several measurement techniques, and genomic DNA will be collected for studies on polymorphisms in pathogenetically important pathways. The study will provide insight into the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease after treatment for testicular cancer, and the main outcome will be the possibility to select individually those patients who are likely to have an increased risk of encountering specific cardiovascular toxicity during or after chemotherapy treatment for TC.

Patient is a 60-year-old woman with a diagnosis of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and has been prescribed long term oxygen therapy (LTOT+) for more than 3 months, with daily use between 12 and 15 hours. She has a history of smoking for 20 years and has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. She experiences shortness of breath with exertion and has a cough with sputum production. She is able to perform activities of daily living with some difficulty. She is currently not participating in a pulmonary rehabilitation program and has not experienced a cardiorespiratory exacerbation in the past 6 weeks. She is not on any anticoagulant drugs and her hematocrit is within the normal range (35-50%). She is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and provide written, signed informed consent. She will be matched for age (± 5 years), sex, and physical activity (estimated by GPAQ questionnaire ± 15% Mets.min/week) with another COPD patient without hypoxia (LTOT- group) for the EVANIMUS study.

The patient is a 16-year-old male with a body mass index (BMI) of 35 kg/m² who is scheduled to undergo bariatric surgery to treat his obesity. The patient has no history of neurological disorders, developmental delays, or severe sleep apnea. He is not currently taking any medication and has no known allergies to propofol or egg protein. The patient's guardian has provided written consent for the study, and the patient has also provided assent. The study will involve monitoring the patient's response to propofol anesthesia during the surgical procedure, with blood samples taken at scheduled and unscheduled time points to measure propofol concentrations. The patient will also have a Bispectral Index (BIS) sensor placed on his forehead to monitor the depth of anesthesia. The study aims to develop a PK/PD model-based dosing algorithm for individualized propofol dosing in morbidly obese adolescents like the patient, thereby improving the safety and efficacy of anesthesia in this high-risk population.

A 45-year-old male patient has recently been diagnosed with thyroid eye disease. He has been experiencing symptoms such as double vision, eye pain, and difficulty closing his eyes. He has a history of Graves' disease and has been on medication to manage his thyroid levels. The patient has been suggested to undergo orbital decompression to alleviate the symptoms of thyroid eye disease. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that observes the relationship between fibroblast growth factor and fibroblast in thyroid eye disease. The patient understands the potential benefits and risks of participating in the trial and meets the inclusion criteria. The patient is not pregnant and falls within the age range of 20 to 80 years.

A 24-year old college student is interested in participating in a clinical trial to understand immune signaling networks. She is in good general health and exercises regularly. She has not had a cold or flu in the past 6 months. She doesn't have any chronic illnesses or use any medications that affect the immune system. She doesn't smoke or consume any recreational drugs. She is interested in contributing to medical research and is willing to comply with all requirements of the study.

A 65-year-old African American woman is interested in participating in the MIRAGE clinical trial. She has a family history of Alzheimer's Disease as her mother and aunt both had AD. She has been noticing some memory loss and difficulty in completing tasks lately, and she is concerned that she might be developing AD. She has no history of stroke or any other neurological disorders. She is currently taking blood pressure medication and has been following a healthy diet and exercise regimen for the past few years. She has never had an MRI before but is willing to undergo one for the study. She has a sister who is over 50 years old and is cognitively normal, and she is willing to participate in the study as well.

The patient is a 55 year old female smoker who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to other parts of the body. She has received radiation therapy but her cancer has progressed. She is currently experiencing shortness of breath and cough and has lost weight due to decreased appetite. She has no history of other invasive malignancies and her baseline laboratory tests show normal function of her liver, kidneys and bone marrow. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, which means she is able to carry out light work such as office work or household chores but is unable to carry out any physically strenuous activity. She has no history of hypertension or diabetes mellitus but is currently taking aspirin 81mg daily for her history of deep vein thrombosis. A brain CT scan showed no evidence of metastases. She is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the treatment and for 3 months after the completion of the study.

60 year old man who had a single vessel stenosis and underwent angioplasty with stenting, with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. The patient is fluent in English and is motivated to improve his health behaviors and outcomes. He has no contraindications to participating in this trial and is able to provide informed consent. The patient is interested in learning more about his individualized risk profile and is open to participating in the net-present value intervention to reduce his biological age and improve his overall health.

A 40-year-old male presents with a history of pre-diabetes. He was diagnosed with pre-diabetes two years ago during a routine check-up. His BMI is 29.5 kg/m2 and his HbA1c level is 6.2%. He has a sedentary lifestyle and consumes a typical Western diet. He reports occasional episodes of postprandial fatigue and dizziness. He is motivated to participate in the study and willing to comply with the study requirements. He is not taking any medication for treatment of diabetes or any other chronic illnesses. He has no history of bariatric surgery, chronic liver or renal disease or allergy to any component of the test meal. He is not a pregnant woman.

The patient is a 35 year old woman who has been diagnosed with relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS) for 5 years. She has been receiving Tysabri® (natalizumab) as part of her treatment plan for the past 2 years. She reports experiencing occasional relapses despite the therapy and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help validate a newly developed laboratory test for measuring Tysabri® serum levels. She is currently scheduled for her next Tysabri® infusion and has agreed to provide a blood sample prior to the infusion. She has not donated or received any blood products since her last infusion. She is able to fill out a wellness patient reported outcome (PRO) questionnaire along with the blood draw.

A 35-year-old morbidly obese woman with a BMI of 42 has been experiencing difficulty losing weight and has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. She has tried various diets and exercise regimens but has not been able to achieve significant weight loss. She has been referred to the Stanford Hospital General Surgery Bariatric Surgery Clinic and has elected to undergo laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery. The patient is scheduled to have the surgery with Dr. Dan Azagury. She understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing and able to provide informed consent. She has no history of bowel perforation or significant gastrointestinal issues. She is not currently enrolled in any other device or drug study that may confound results. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is a suitable candidate to participate.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial, as it is not aimed at recruiting individual patients for treatment. Instead, it is focused on evaluating the effectiveness of an app called Spot Light for the management of sports-related concussions in youth football teams. The eligibility criteria are related to the "reporter" (i.e., coach or certified athletic trainer) who will be using the app, but there are no specific patient-related criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old African American woman who has been postmenopausal for 3 years. She has a history of high blood pressure and has been taking medication for the same for the past 5 years. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has a family history of hypertension, with her father and two siblings also having the condition. She is currently not taking any other medications and has no known allergies. Her baseline blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and her BMI is 32. Her physical examination is otherwise unremarkable, with no signs of peripheral edema or organomegaly. Her laboratory tests are normal except for mildly elevated levels of CRP and IL-6. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the biochemical and genetic markers of hypertension in women, as she hopes to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge in this area and better control her own hypertension.

45-year-old female patient with a history of frequent asthma exacerbations and cough presents with an abnormal chest X-ray showing migrating ground glass opacity (GGO) and nodular lesions. The patient reports no symptoms related to the pulmonary findings. The patient also reports a history of eating uncooked liver and meat from cows, sheep and chickens. Serum toxocara antibody test is positive. The patient is referred to the study to investigate the incidence of ocular toxocariasis (OT) associated with pulmonary toxocariasis (PT) and to track the results of treatment for diagnosed OT patients. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

56-year-old female with a history of endometrial cancer, diagnosed with stage IIIB disease after undergoing a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The patient completed adjuvant chemotherapy and is now scheduled to receive high-dose-rate vaginal cuff brachytherapy with curative intent. The patient has expressed concern about the potential pain and anxiety associated with the treatment. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the use of virtual reality helmets during the procedure to enhance her tolerance and reduce discomfort. The patient is otherwise healthy and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She has been informed about the study and has agreed to participate.

25-year-old female with Fitzpatrick Skin Type II presents as a healthy volunteer for a Sun Protection Factor (SPF) efficacy study on human skin. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to sunscreens, cosmetics, toiletries, or topical drugs. There is no history of pre-existing dermatologic conditions or other medical conditions, and she is not currently on any chronic medication. The patient is not pregnant or nursing. She has signed and dated the Informed Consent Form and HIPAA Form. The patient has an unambiguous MED or MPPD (Minimal Persistent Pigment Darkening Dose) and falls within the age range of 18-70 years old.

A 35-year-old male who recently had unprotected sex with multiple partners presents to the clinic for HIV and hepatitis screening. He has a history of drug use, including intravenous drug use, and has had multiple partners in the past year. He reports no symptoms of hepatitis or HIV but is concerned about his risk of infection. He is able to sign the consent form and is willing to complete the risk assessment questionnaire. He is also willing to provide blood samples, including a finger stick sample, a serum separator tube, and two anticoagulant tubes. The patient is eligible for enrollment in Population 1 of the trial as he has multiple risk factors for infection with hepatitis B or C and HIV. The study will use both Multiplo HBc/HIV/HCV and Reveal HBsAg to test the patient’s blood samples for all three infections. The results of the investigational tests will be compared to the results of the FDA-approved assays to determine the efficacy of the rapid diagnostic tests.

A 65-year-old male with a history of hypertension and angina pectoris presented with shortness of breath and fatigue upon exertion. The patient was diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis and was recommended for aortic valve replacement surgery. The patient has no history of neurological events, substance abuse, or endocarditis. The patient has not participated in any other clinical studies and is willing to complete all follow-up requirements. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is legally eligible for participation in the study.

32-year-old female office worker with a sedentary lifestyle and history of neck pain and stiffness. She reports spending long hours sitting in front of a computer, which has led to poor posture, including forward head posture. She has tried various treatments including massage and chiropractic adjustments but has not found lasting relief. On examination, she has a craniovertebral angle of 45 degrees and reports neck pain and stiffness, especially at the end of the day. She has no history of whiplash injury or spinal surgery. She is willing and able to participate in a 12-session treatment program to address her forward head posture and improve her functional abilities. She speaks fluent English and is not currently undergoing any other physical therapy program.

A 9-month old baby girl living in Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana is being breastfed and is also given complementary foods. She has no history of major illnesses or hospitalizations. She lives with her parents and 3 siblings in a rural village. Her parents are subsistence farmers, and they grow maize and cassava. The baby is not currently suffering from malaria or any other major illnesses. The baby was weighed and measured during a recent well-baby check-up and was found to be within normal ranges for weight and height. She has not been treated with iron supplements in the past 6 months. The baby is afebrile and has no evidence of edema or any congenital abnormality. Her hemoglobin level is 90g/L, indicating mild anemia. The parents are willing to participate in the study and give informed consent.

A 31-year old woman was admitted to the hospital at 32 weeks of gestation due to premature rupture of membranes. She had a history of urinary tract infections during pregnancy, which were treated with antibiotics. She reported fever, chills and abdominal pain on admission. Laboratory investigations showed elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein. The patient was diagnosed with chorioamnionitis and started on intravenous antibiotics. An emergency caesarean section was performed due to fetal distress. The baby was born weighing 1.8 kg and admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit. The baby had a low platelet count and was diagnosed with thrombocytopenia. She also developed intracranial hemorrhage and retinal hemorrhage. The baby's mother was included in the clinical trial to explore the effect of chorioamnionitis on platelet activation and placental vessel among preterm infants by Wnt-Flt1 signal pathway.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who is HIV-positive and has been diagnosed with relapsed or refractory AIDS-related non-Hodgkin lymphoma. He has previously received chemotherapy and radiation therapy for his lymphoma but has experienced disease progression. The patient has documented Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV)- and/or human herpes virus-8 (HHV-8)- positive infection within the lymphoma. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 70% and a life expectancy of more than 2 months. His ANC is 1,200/mm³ and his hemoglobin level is 9.0 g/dL. His platelet count is 120,000/mm³ and his total bilirubin level is 1.2 mg/dL. His AST/ALT levels are within the institutional upper limit of normal and his serum creatinine level is also normal. He is not pregnant or nursing and has negative pregnancy test. He has no peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 2 and no uncontrolled intercurrent illnesses. The patient is willing to use effective contraception and has no history of hypersensitivity to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition to bortezomib, boron, mannitol, ifosfamide, carboplatin, or etoposide. The patient is not receiving concurrent moderate-to-strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors other than protease inhibitors.

A 32 year old woman is a primary caregiver for her 5 year old son who has cerebral palsy. She has been caring for him for the past 4 years and spends most of her time assisting him with daily tasks and attending his medical appointments. She has no history of regular exercise in the past 6 months and is interested in participating in the investigation of the effects of clinical Pilates exercises. She is fluent in English and is willing to attend sessions twice a week for 8 weeks. She has no serious orthopaedic, neurological, rheumatologic or psychiatric problems that may prevent her from participating in the study. She is not pregnant and has not had a traumatic injury or surgery in the last 6 months.

Pt is a 4-year-old male presenting with unilateral microtia and hemifacial microsomia. The patient has no other significant medical history and has not been diagnosed with any other developmental abnormalities. The patient has no family history of Goldenhar syndrome or any other genetic disorders. The patient is being referred to this study to determine if there is a genetic component to their condition and to contribute to the identification of the first gene involved in Goldenhar syndrome.

42-year-old female with a history of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) presents with urinary incontinence. She reports having at least 3 episodes of urinary incontinence over a 3-day period despite taking anticholinergic medication. She is not currently using an intermittent or indwelling catheter to manage her urinary incontinence. She has no history of myasthenia gravis, Eaton-Lambert Syndrome, or Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of urinary incontinence due to neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) with OnabotulinumtoxinA (BOTOX®).

The patient is a 26-year-old male who has a history of chronic back pain due to a work-related injury. He has tried various pain management techniques including physical therapy, medication, and acupuncture, but has not found significant relief. He is currently not taking any pain medications. He is fluent in English and has normal hearing. He does not have a history of motion sickness or seizures. He is currently not experiencing nausea and is clinically stable. He is interested in exploring alternative pain management techniques and is willing to participate in this study.

A 28-year-old healthy female who is a non-smoker and has a body mass index (BMI) between 18.0 and 30.0 is eligible for this first-in-human clinical trial. The patient must be of non-childbearing potential or use appropriate double-barrier contraception if male. They should be willing to participate in the study and sign an Independent Ethics Committee approved informed consent form. They should not have a significant history of alcoholism or drug/chemical abuse in the past 5 years and must have suitable veins for cannulation and/or repeated venipuncture. The patient should not have any ongoing significant medical history, and their vital signs, clinical laboratory evaluations, and resting 12-lead ECG should be within normal reference ranges or outside of normal reference ranges considered not clinically relevant by the Principal Investigator or designee. The patient should not have used any prescribed medication within 14 days prior to the planned time of dosing or non-prescription or over-the-counter medication, herbal and dietary supplements such as St John's Wort, vitamins, and minerals that could affect the outcome of the study within 1 week prior to the planned time of dosing. The patient should be willing to avoid the use of alcohol within 48 hours before any study visit and while confined to the study center and abstain from heavy physical training from 7 days before first dosing until the final follow-up visit. The patient should not have any significant drug allergy (e.g., anaphylaxis) or any clinically significant allergic condition (excluding non-active hay fever), as determined by the Principal Investigator or designee.

54F with a history of chronic pancreatitis presents to the gastroenterology clinic with abdominal pain and weight loss. Imaging studies reveal a solid mass in the pancreas which requires further evaluation for diagnosis. The patient has no known allergies and is currently taking pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy for her chronic pancreatitis. She has no history of bleeding disorders or active gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient has been informed of the procedure and has provided written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who recently tested positive for COVID-19 through RT-PCR. He is currently experiencing mild symptoms such as cough and fever, and has been advised to self-isolate at home. He has no known pre-existing medical conditions and has not been hospitalized due to COVID-19. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form after receiving clear and honest information about the research. He is covered by a Social Security scheme and is not currently enrolled in any other studies regarding immunomodulators. The patient is alert, cooperative and able to provide accurate information about his medical history.

A 50-year-old woman with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) presents for a routine colonoscopy and upper endoscopy. She has a BMI of 26 and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. She reports no allergies to anesthetics and has no contraindications for gastrointestinal endoscopy. She has given written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient does not have any history of mental illness, epilepsy or chronic pain. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He has a family history of diabetes, and he has been experiencing symptoms such as frequent urination, thirst, and fatigue. He has not been able to control his blood sugar levels through lifestyle modifications alone and has been prescribed medication to manage his diabetes. He is currently enrolled in the LFSS Patient Registry and has read and signed the Informed Consent Form. He does not have any other medical conditions that would affect his participation in the study.

32F with primary infertility, no known systemic disease, and no prior uterine surgery was referred to a gynecologist for evaluation. Upon examination, the patient was found to have a uterine anomaly classified as ESGE U1-A. She reports a history of difficulty conceiving and has experienced recurrent implantation failure and recurrent pregnancy loss. The patient is currently not pregnant and has never given birth. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating U1-A uterine anomalies implantation markers from the lateral walls of the endometrium.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who regularly experiences menstrual flow and currently uses tampons as her primary method of menstrual management. She is fluent in written and spoken English, and does not have any allergies or sensitivities to silicone. She is not currently pregnant, nor does she have plans to become pregnant before the end of the study data collection period. She has not used systemic antimicrobials within the past 14 days, and is able to understand the nature and purpose of the study. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to keep a diary of her menstrual experience for 3 months.

The patient is a 7-year-old child with a history of recurrent febrile episodes, associated with aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis. The febrile episodes typically last for 4 days and recur every 21-30 days. The child has been diagnosed with PFAPA by Dr. Bennett based on clinical and laboratory data. The current standard of care for PFAPA includes corticosteroid treatment, but the child and their family are interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of probiotics in combination with corticosteroids to potentially reduce the frequency and length of febrile episodes, and associated symptoms. The child is not currently taking any probiotics regularly and is not allergic to any of the ingredients in the probiotic or placebo. The child does not have any chronic diseases or immune deficiencies that may interfere with the study. The child and their family are proficient in English and have agreed to the consent and assent forms. The child has not used antibiotics within a month of the study start.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease for the past 10 years. He has been on Duodopa therapy for the past 3 years due to the occurrence of difficult to manage dyskinesias. Despite the treatment, he experiences frequent dystonia and chorea that affect his daily activities. His Hoehn & Yahr stage is 4 at worst. He has not been on any dopamine agonist or glutamate antagonist treatment. He does not have dementia or psychosis and has not been on any typical neuroleptics. He is willing to participate in the study to help find better management for his dyskinesias.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was diagnosed with heart failure a year ago. Her ejection fraction is preserved (>50%) and she currently experiences symptoms consistent with New York Heart Association Class II-III. She is on stable medication and her condition is clinically stable. She is able to exercise and has no other debilitating or unstable diseases that would limit her length of life. She does not have an implanted pacemaker.

A 25-year-old male, who is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol on a regular basis, presented with no significant medical history. He has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18.5 to 29.9 kg/m2. His vital signs, blood pressure (BP) and pulse rate (PR), and 12-lead Electrocardiogram (ECG) were within the normal range. Clinical laboratory tests showed no abnormalities. He has no gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological or hormonal disorders. He has not undergone cholecystectomy or any surgery of the gastrointestinal tract that could interfere with the pharmacokinetics of the trial medication. The patient does not have any diseases of the central nervous system, neurological or psychiatric disorders, orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, or blackouts. He has no history of chronic or acute infections, relevant allergy or hypersensitivity, and has not taken any drugs within 30 days of planned administration of trial medication that might influence the results of the trial. The patient has not donated more than 100 mL of blood within 30 days of planned administration of trial medication or intended blood donation during the trial. He is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site and able to understand and comply with study requirements. The patient's liver enzyme (ALT, AST, GGT) values were within the normal range at the screening examination and he has no history of drug-induced liver injury. He has no history of heart failure, or any evidence of ventricular dysfunction in the history. He does not have hereditary fructose intolerance. The patient does not have a WOCBP partner and does not need to use male contraception. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the BI 730357 clinical trial.

A 12-year old male diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3, secondary to a history of vesicoureteral reflux. He has been on antihypertensive medications for the past year due to uncontrolled hypertension. The patient reported occasional headaches, fatigue, and shortness of breath. He lives with his parents and two siblings. His past medical history is significant for asthma and frequent urinary tract infections. He is an active child who enjoys playing soccer and video games. The patient is compliant with his medications but still experiences high blood pressure readings during his routine clinic visits. The patient's blood pressure is monitored with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) and is currently above the 95th percentile for his age and height. His renal function is stable with no evidence of proteinuria. The patient is fluent in English and does not have any developmental or behavioral limitations that would prevent him from completing the ABPM.

A 45-year-old male patient is admitted to the Ear, Nose, Throat (ENT) department with a history of upper aero-digestive tract obstruction. The obstruction is found to be caused by a tumour and a tracheotomy is performed. The patient is currently wearing a tracheal cannula to facilitate his breathing. He reports feeling anxious during the cannula replacement procedure, which takes place every week. The patient is able to communicate effectively and has given his consent to participate in the study. He is a French citizen and fluent in the language. He has no hearing loss or dementia. The patient is not autonomous in his cannula replacement and has not previously participated in the study. He is married and has two children. He is a member of a social security assurance and has given a signed informed consent form to participate in the study.

A 42 year old woman comes to the clinic seeking to undergo bariatric surgery. She is 5 feet 6 inches tall and weighs 275 pounds, putting her BMI at 44.4 kg/m2. She has a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and sleep apnea. She has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past but has been unsuccessful in losing and maintaining weight loss. She is motivated to lose weight in preparation for the surgery and is willing to participate in a multidisciplinary weight loss program that includes diet, exercise, and psychological support. She agrees to participate in a clinical trial that will evaluate the effectiveness of the weight loss program in obese patients prior to bariatric surgery. She does not have any eating disorders, liver or kidney failure, or any other contraindications to surgery.

A 25-year-old male presents with a history of osteosarcoma in the right femur, which was initially treated with high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, cisplatin and ifosfamide. However, there was a progression of the disease within six months after the initial chemotherapy. The patient has multiple metastases in the lungs and bone, which are measurable according to the Response Evaluation Criteria for Solid Tumors (RECIST 1.1). He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 and normal hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. He has not been previously treated with antiangiogenic TKIs and single IE chemotherapy. He has no severe or uncontrolled medical disorders that could jeopardize the outcomes of the study. The patient has not undergone any surgical procedure or radiotherapy within four weeks of enrollment. He has no active gastroduodenal ulcer, no previous condition associated with a risk of bleeding, and no known allergy to the experimental agents. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has been assessed by the sarcoma board including a thoracic surgeon with at least 10 years of surgical experience.

Patient is a 43-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. She rates her pain as an 8 out of 10 on the NRS scale. She has tried various treatments including physical therapy and massage therapy, but has not experienced significant improvement. She has no plans to move out of the area in the next 6-8 weeks and has reliable transportation to come to the clinic on a regular basis. She is able to read and verbally comprehend English. She has no bone or joint pathology that would contraindicate spinal manipulation. She is not legally blind and has no evidence of alcohol or drug dependence or abuse. Her depression score on the Beck Depression Inventory-II is 15 (mild). She is willing to postpone the use of all other types of manual treatment for her low back pain except those provided in the study for the duration of the study period. She has no comorbidities that would interfere with her ability to participate in the study. She is not pregnant and is not seeking to become pregnant during the active study phase. She is able and willing to comply with the study protocol.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial, as it is focused on the evaluation of a new technology for radiation dose verification in a clinical setting. The trial will involve patients who are already receiving external beam radiotherapy or a radioactive implant under established primary clinical protocols, but the study will not involve any additional interventions or treatments for the patients. Therefore, patient eligibility is based on their willingness to have additional measurements performed and sign an informed consent, rather than any specific clinical characteristics. Pediatric patients and those with cognitive impairments are excluded from the study.

52 yo M with a history of a heart attack 1 year ago. He underwent CMR-DE imaging to evaluate for cardiac scarring, which was positive. He has been asymptomatic since his heart attack and has been on guideline-directed medical therapy. His primary care physician referred him to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of non-contrast DWI imaging compared to CMR-DE in detecting cardiac scarring after a heart attack. He agrees to participate and meets the eligibility criteria. Past Medical History: MI, HTN, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 DM. Current Medications: aspirin, statin, metoprolol, lisinopril, and metformin.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been experiencing tremors and stiffness in his right hand for the past 6 years. He has also noticed a decrease in his sense of smell, constipation, and mild depression. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 3 years ago, based on the United Kingdom Parkinson's Disease Society Brain Bank diagnostic research criteria. He has been on levodopa and carbidopa for the past 2 years, which has improved his tremors and stiffness. However, he has recently developed freezing of gait, which has been affecting his daily activities. His Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 28. He has no history of dementia or other disorders that may resemble Parkinson's disease. The MRI of his brain shows no evidence of stroke or mass lesion, and he does not have any metallic fragments near his eyes or spinal cord. He is not on any neuroleptic, anticholinergic, or cholinesterase inhibitor drugs. He is willing to participate in research procedures involving ionizing radiation and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 35-year-old Hispanic woman who has been experiencing joint pain, muscle weakness, and skin rash for the past year. The joint pain is most severe in her hands and wrists, and the skin rash is on her cheeks and nose and gets worse when exposed to sunlight. She has also noticed hair loss and fatigue. She went to her primary care doctor who referred her to a rheumatologist who diagnosed her with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Her doctor prescribed hydroxychloroquine and prednisone, and her symptoms have improved, but she still experiences occasional flares. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to learn more about her disease and help advance research for new treatments.

A 16-year-old female high school student who is generally healthy with no significant medical history presents for the clinical trial. She is up to date on all her routine vaccinations and has never had any significant adverse reactions to any vaccines. She is physically active and exercises regularly. She does not have any known allergies to any medications. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She has not traveled outside of Korea in the last 6 months. She is interested in participating in the trial and has provided written informed consent. She is reliable and committed to the study requirements and is able to complete the diary card and attend all follow-up visits. She has provided a negative urine pregnancy test as she is of childbearing age. She meets all the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 35-year-old woman with large and heavy breasts came to the clinic to consult with a plastic surgeon for breast reduction surgery. She is a non-smoker with no history of kidney failure, and she is not morbidly obese. She takes no medication and has no known allergies to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the use of ketorolac for postoperative pain control and its potential effect on hematoma rates in breast reduction surgery. She is willing to sign a consent form and comply with the study protocol, including follow-up visits.

46-year-old male with a history of cutaneous melanoma, initially diagnosed 4 years ago, with multiple metastases to the lungs and liver. He has previously received ipilimumab and nivolumab with initial response, but later developed progressive disease. He has also received dabrafenib and trametinib, which were discontinued due to adverse events. He presents with cough, shortness of breath, and weight loss. CT scans show progression of his metastatic disease. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function, and is not pregnant or nursing. He has no known allergies to CREMOPHOR® and/or paclitaxel. He has not received any systemic treatment for at least 28 days and has not undergone any major surgeries in the last 14 days.

Patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing worsening vision due to cataracts in her left eye. She has been scheduled to undergo cataract surgery by phacoemulsification with posterior chamber intraocular lens. She has no history of immunodepression or intolerance to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). She has not taken acetylsalicylic acid at doses > 100 mg daily and can discontinue usage during the study. She has not been treated with local or systemic anti-inflammatory drugs within 10 days prior to inclusion. The patient's preoperative flare is ≤ 15 ph/ms, measured with a laser flare meter (LFM) without pharmacological pupil dilation, within the 2 months preoperatively. The patient is willing to participate in the study and adhere to the study protocol.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing heavy and irregular menstrual bleeding for the past six months. She has no history of hysteroscopy or curettage, ovulatory dysfunction, or endometrial pathology. She is currently not taking any hormonal treatments or using an intrauterine device. She has no known genital infections or pelvic inflammatory disease. She is not pregnant, and there are no vaginal or cervical pathologies causing her bleeding. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the efficacy and safety of hysteroscopy and transvaginal ultrasonography in diagnosing abnormal uterine bleeding.

A 35-year-old female patient came to the clinic with a history of depression, which began after her divorce three years ago. She reported feeling sad, hopeless, and worthless almost every day, with a loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has difficulty sleeping and wakes up tired every day. She has also experienced a significant decrease in her appetite, leading to weight loss. She has a history of anxiety and has sought treatment in the past. She currently works as a teacher and reports feeling overwhelmed with her workload. She has a supportive family but has been struggling to maintain her social life due to her depression. She is seeking help to manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 6-month-old male infant brought in by his mother for evaluation of an asymmetrical head shape. The mother reports that the baby has been lying on his back for most of his waking hours and has developed a flattening of the left side of the head. She has tried repositioning the baby during sleep but has not seen any improvement. The infant has no significant medical history and was born at full term without any complications. He is exclusively breastfed and has been meeting his developmental milestones appropriately. On examination, the infant has a noticeable flattening of the left side of the head with a prominent right frontal bossing. He has no other abnormalities on physical examination. Imaging studies reveal significant Deformational Plagiocephaly requiring helmet therapy. The infant meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study. The mother has given her consent for the infant to participate in the study.

A 58-year-old man diagnosed with multiple myeloma 2 years ago is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may prevent relapse. He is currently in remission and has a performance status of 1 based on Southwest Oncology Group (SWOG) criteria. He has no history of heart attack and his blood counts are within normal limits. He has no allergies to any food or drugs. He is married with two grown children and works as an accountant. He exercises regularly and is in good overall health. He is willing to use acceptable birth control during the study.

Pt is a 50yo M who recently underwent an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for acute myeloid leukemia. The pt has developed a skin rash that has been diagnosed as grade I acute skin graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD). The rash is limited to the trunk and extremities with no involvement of the face or mucous membranes. The pt has a history of hypersensitivity to corticosteroids, making it difficult to treat the skin rash with standard therapy. The pt has been offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of Ectoin Dermatitis Cream 7% as first-line therapy for aGVHD. The pt has agreed to participate and will be monitored for 14 days to assess the effectiveness of the cream on reducing inflammation and stabilizing the skin barrier.

The patient is a 6-month-old male infant who was born at term with no complications during pregnancy or delivery. During a routine pediatric examination, it was noted that the infant had enlarged eyes and elevated intraocular pressure. Upon further evaluation, the infant was diagnosed with primary congenital glaucoma. The infant has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. The parents have no history of glaucoma or other ocular diseases. The infant has not undergone any previous glaucoma surgery. The ophthalmologist has recommended combined trabeculotomy trabeculectomy with mitomycin C to manage the glaucoma. The parents have been informed of the risks and benefits of the procedure and have given informed consent. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the study and will undergo histopathological examination of the peripheral iris tissue specimen following the procedure.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of diabetes and end-stage renal disease requiring chronic hemodialysis. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 3 years and is stable on his current treatment regimen. He has no previous history of cerebrovascular accidents, myocardial infarction, coronary angioplasty, or bypass surgery within the last 6 months. He is willing to give written informed consent for the clinical trial and is able to understand and follow instructions. He has not participated in any other clinical study within the last 30 days and has no known drug or alcohol abuse. He does not have any congenital or acquired bleeding disorders, hepatic failure, or amyloidosis. He has no active major bleeding or increased risk of hemorrhage due to pericarditis or bacterial endocarditis, severe uncontrolled hypertension, active ulcerative and angiodysplastic gastrointestinal disease, hemorrhagic stroke, shortly after brain, spinal or ophthalmological surgery, concomitant treatment with platelet inhibitors, recent surgical procedures, or history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. He is not hypersensitive to heparin, benzyl alcohol, or pork products.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who presented with abdominal pain and rectal bleeding for the past 6 months. She has lost weight and appetite during this period. The colonoscopy showed a mass lesion in the sigmoid colon. Biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma. The CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no evidence of metastases. Her past medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is willing to participate in the study and undergo radical surgery.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who lives alone in the community. She has a history of two falls in the past year, one of which resulted in a fractured wrist. She has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and ibuprofen as needed for pain. She is able to perform activities of daily living independently but has reported feeling unsteady on her feet at times. She speaks English fluently and has no plans to move from the area in the next year. Her mental status is intact, and she scores 8 out of 10 on the abbreviated mental test. She is not a resident of a nursing home.

A 55-year-old man with a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia was referred to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial. He was diagnosed 3 years ago and has received multiple lines of treatment but his disease has relapsed. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and his life expectancy is at least 90 days. He has no history of cardiovascular, renal, neurologic, psychiatric, endocrinologic, metabolic, immunologic, or hepatic disease that would adversely affect his participation in the study. He has not undergone an allogeneic stem cell transplant and does not have any underlying condition that affects absorption or motility. He is married with two children and his wife has undergone surgical sterilization. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of bleeding or thromboembolic events.

The patient is a 70-year-old female diagnosed with multiple myeloma. She has not yet made a treatment decision and is seeking guidance from her healthcare provider. She is fluent in English and has no history of being a prisoner or any other vulnerable person. She is willing to participate in the study intervention and complete post-intervention questionnaires. She is able to use a touchscreen tablet to complete the modified Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (mCGA) and understands the importance of using the mCGA to guide treatment decision-making.

25 yo F admitted to Østmarka Psychiatric Hospital due to acute psychotic episode. Patient reports a history of substance use, including alcohol, marijuana, and cocaine. Patient expresses a desire to quit using substances but has struggled with relapse in the past. Patient is fluent in English and consents to participate in the study. Past Medical History: No prior psychiatric hospitalizations, no significant medical history.

A 68-year-old Japanese man visited the ophthalmologist complaining of blurred vision and difficulty reading fine print. He had a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which were well-controlled with medication. After a comprehensive eye examination, he was diagnosed with age-related cataracts in both eyes. He underwent phacoemulsification surgery with implantation of Clareon intraocular lenses (IOLs) using the Clareon® IOL AutonoMe™ automated preloaded delivery system. His post-operative recovery was uneventful and his visual acuity improved significantly. He has been using glasses for reading and distance vision, but would like to see if he can do without them. He is willing to participate in the post-market clinical survey to help evaluate the delivery performance of Clareon® IOL AutonoMe™.

Patient is a 7-month-old infant with a confirmed diagnosis of intussusception. The patient has been experiencing intermittent episodes of abdominal pain, vomiting, and bloody stools for the past few days. A physical examination revealed a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The patient's vital signs are stable, and there are no signs of peritonitis or pneumoperitoneum. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for the infant to participate in the clinical trial.

A 55-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma 5 years ago, who has undergone two prior lines of therapy with lenalidomide and dexamethasone. The patient has had stable disease on lenalidomide 25 mg, with no progression of disease. However, recently the patient has shown signs of relapse with increased serum M-protein (1.5 g/dl) and urine monoclonal protein (300 mg/24h). The patient is otherwise healthy with no history of peripheral neuropathy or cardiac disease. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80, and the left ventricular ejection fraction is 55%. The patient is able to swallow capsules and tablets, and has no history of non-compliance to medical regimens. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to comply with the fertility and pregnancy test requirements dictated by the Rev-Assist program. The patient is eligible and suitable for the clinical trial of lenalidomide and pidilizumab for the treatment of relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.

A 11-year-old boy, who is fluent in English, lives in a rural area with his parents and two older siblings. His family owns firearms for hunting and he has been exposed to firearms since a young age. He is currently in 6th grade and enjoys playing video games and reading. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study. His parents are supportive of his participation and speak English fluently. He has no siblings who will also participate in the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old female with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and documented sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) by 12-lead ECG or intracardiac ICD interrogation. She has been experiencing at least two episodes of electrocardiographically documented symptomatic, recurrent, sustained monomorphic VT in the 3 months prior to enrollment. She has previously undergone at least one catheter-ablation procedure without control of symptoms or with poor toleration. She has also tried at least one antiarrhythmic medication (i.e. amiodarone, sotalol, mexiletine) without success. The patient has an ICD, and her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is ≤35%. She is willing to participate in a non-invasive cardiac radioablation (CRA) procedure to treat her refractory VT. The patient is not pregnant and has a negative pregnancy test within 14 days of study entry. She has no history of multiple scars on electrocardiographic imaging where the source of reentrant focus is unclear or any prior radiotherapy to the internal organs of the thorax or upper abdomen.

53 year old male with recurrent syncope attributed to complete heart block status post dual chamber pacemaker implantation approximately 3 years ago. He presents with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and tobacco use. The patient is on stable medical management and has no history of significant allergies. He is being considered for an MRI of the brain to evaluate for any underlying structural causes of his syncope. He is being offered enrollment in the SAMURAI Clinical Study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the ImageReady(TM) MR Conditional Pacing System during MRI scans. The patient meets all inclusion criteria, has no known MR Unsafe implants or devices, and is willing and able to participate in the study.

32 F who gave birth to her first child 6 months ago vaginally at term. She has been experiencing urinary incontinence, specifically stress incontinence, with at least 3 episodes per week over the last 3 months. She has been diagnosed with an avulsion injury and has not undergone any prior pelvic floor muscle physiotherapy for this injury. She is not currently pregnant or postmenopausal and does not have any significant prolapse. She does not have incontinence due to other causes such as infection or neurological diseases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of physiotherapy for urinary incontinence in women with a puborectalis avulsion.

The patient is a 55-year-old female diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. She has previously undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy with limited success. Her treating physician has recommended high-dose chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplantation as the next step in her treatment plan. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial investigating the prophylactic use of moxifloxacin to reduce the incidence of bacteremia. Upon assessment, the patient has no signs or symptoms of current infection and has not received any antibiotics in the past seven days. Her vital signs are within normal limits and she has no significant medical history aside from her cancer diagnosis. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the importance of regular follow-up visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old male with a body mass index of 30 and a waist circumference of 100 cm. He is a non-smoker with no active health problems and is not taking any chronic medications. He has a history of stable hypertension that is currently controlled with medication. He does not consume more than 21 units of alcohol per week. His liver and renal function tests have been normal in the past. He has not been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes or any metabolic or viral liver disease. He has not been diagnosed with any bleeding tendency and has no contraindications to MRI scanning. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of fructose consumption on metabolic dysregulation.

52-year-old Chinese female with a diagnosis of overactive bladder and experiencing symptoms of urgent micturition, frequent micturition, and urge urinary incontinence for the past 6 months. She reports urinary frequency of more than 8 times a day and an average volume of single micturition less than 200ml. She is willing and able to complete the micturition diary card accurately. Her urine routine test indicates that she has no urinary tract infection. She has not received any anticholinergic drugs or other drugs for treating OAB within the washout period and is not participating in any other clinical trial. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is taking sufficient contraceptive measures. She signs the informed consent form and is willing to participate in this Phase III study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Propiverine Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsule in the treatment of overactive bladder.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) 5 years ago. She has a family history of DM1, with her mother and two siblings also affected. The patient reports experiencing muscle weakness and stiffness, difficulty with grip strength, and occasional myotonia. She is currently taking no medications for DM1. The patient has no significant medical history, is a non-smoker, and does not consume alcohol regularly. She is able to walk independently, but with some difficulty due to muscle weakness. Her BMI is 25.9. The patient is willing and able to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has undergone IVF/ICSI treatment and has one or two chromosomally normal cryopreserved blastocysts available for transfer. She has regular menstrual cycles between 26-34 days and is undergoing her first frozen-thawed transfer cycle. Her progesterone level was found to be less than 1.5ng/mL on the day of trigger injection in the stimulation cycle from which the embryos to be transferred were created. She does not have polycystic ovarian syndrome, poor ovarian response, uterine abnormalities, history of endometriosis AFS ≥ 2, or any known contraindications or allergy to oral estradiol or progesterone. Additionally, she has not undergone a D&C, does not have hydrosalpinx or Asherman syndrome, and has not undergone ICSI due to severe male factor with testicular sperm. She has not discontinued HRT medication and ovulation has been detected in her research natural cycle. She has not ovulated after day 20 in a natural cycle and the duration of her estradiol exposure is less than 17 days with an endometrium thickness of at least 6mm. She has not experienced spontaneous ovulation in her HRT artificial cycle.

The patient is a 16 year old Caucasian girl with good general health, and no history of any clinical abnormality or medical history. She has all her teeth present including 15, 16, 25, 26, 35, 36, 45, and 46. She has a good understanding of the French language and has one of her parents who accepts the terms of the study and signs the written informed consent. She does not smoke and does not have any pathologies or orthodontic appliance. She has not taken antibiotics in the last 3 months and does not regularly use interdental brushes, dental floss or mouthwash. She is not at risk for infectious endocarditis and is able to answer questions and cooperate with the study. She has periodontal pockets greater than or equal to 3mm at interdental sites 15-16, 25-26, 35-36, 45-46.

Patient is a 55-year-old male from the United States who has been experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) for the past 6 months with an International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) of 12. He denies any history of urinary tract infection or neurogenic voiding dysfunction. He has not had a prostate biopsy within the past 6 months and has not been on any treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) within the past 6 months. His vital signs are within normal limits and his laboratory results are normal except for a serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level of 5.5 ng/mL. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the written informed consent form.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male with a history of heart murmur and shortness of breath on exertion presents to the hospital for evaluation of his mitral valve. He reports experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath while climbing stairs or walking uphill. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. He has no significant past medical history and takes only occasional over-the-counter pain medications. His family history is negative for heart disease. On physical examination, a systolic murmur is heard best at the apex that radiates to the axilla. An echocardiogram shows significant mitral valve regurgitation consistent with Barlow disease, and he is referred for surgery. He undergoes a preoperative cardiac MRI to evaluate the ventricle and mitral annulus as part of a clinical trial investigating the physiological changes of the mitral annulus after annuloplasty in Barlow disease. He is found to be eligible for the study and consents to participate.

As this clinical trial involves early infant and children males, a patient description would not be appropriate. However, it is important to note that the study is aimed at assessing the safety and efficacy of the PrePex device among healthy early infant and children males scheduled for voluntary circumcision. The study will examine the feasibility of performing PrePex circumcision on early infants and children male population. Eligible participants will be healthy infants or children who are uncircumcised, and whose parent/legal guardian is able to comprehend and freely give informed consent for participation in this study.
