The parent/legal guardian must also agree to anonymous video and photographs of the procedure and follow-up visits, and must be willing to comply with the study procedures and requirements, including hospitalization and follow-up visits until complete healing is achieved. Participants with certain diseases or conditions, such as active genital infection, anatomic abnormality, or bleeding/coagulation abnormality, will be excluded from the study.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who was diagnosed with a leg length discrepancy after sustaining a fracture in her left leg. She is scheduled to undergo a distraction osteogenesis procedure at Hadassah Medical Center in Jerusalem. The surgery will involve the application of an external fixation device to her bone, followed by the creation of an osteotomy and gradual, controlled distraction of bone fragments. The patient has no known allergies or metabolic disorders and has agreed to participate in the clinical trial testing the effect of crustacean's gastrolith nutraceutical on mineralization rate during the consolidation phase of her surgery. She will be provided with a monthly supply of gastrolith calcium in a sealed container and will be required to take two 500mg capsules daily during the consolidation phase until the external fixator is removed.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for two years without success. She has undergone several fertility treatments, including ovulation induction and intrauterine insemination, but none of them worked. She has now decided to try in vitro fertilization (IVF) to increase her chances of getting pregnant. She is in good health and has no history of psychiatric disorders. She speaks fluent English and is able to communicate effectively. Her partner is supportive of her decision to undergo IVF treatment. She is aware of the potential emotional difficulties that may come with the IVF process and is open to receiving counseling to help her cope with any stress or anxiety that may arise. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who has been struggling with addiction for the past 5 years. He is currently addicted to opioids and cocaine and has been using both substances on a regular basis. He has attempted to quit on his own but has been unsuccessful. He is not currently enrolled in any treatment program. He is employed as a construction worker and is married with two children. He is in good physical health and does not have any significant medical conditions. He does not smoke or use any drugs other than opioids and cocaine. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help him overcome his addiction. He is willing to attend weekly psychotherapy sessions and comply with the medication regimen. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study as he has a documented history of opioid dependence and current cocaine use, and fulfills DSM-IV criteria for opioid and cocaine dependence. He is not pregnant and does not have any other medical or psychiatric conditions that would prevent him from participating in the trial.

Pt is a 45yo M presenting to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and tenderness. He reports the pain began suddenly and has been worsening over the past 24 hours. The pain is located in the right lower quadrant and is associated with nausea and vomiting. He has no fever and no history of abdominal surgery. Physical exam reveals tenderness to palpation in the right lower quadrant. The examining physician marks the area of tenderness on the patient's abdominal wall prior to ordering an abdominal CT. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is enrolled.

The patient is a preterm infant who was born at 30 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1,200 g. The infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit at Seoul National University Children's hospital due to respiratory distress syndrome and has been receiving respiratory support. The infant has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions or congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. The attending neonatologist has determined that the infant is eligible for enrollment in the clinical trial to identify prognostic urinary biomarkers for acute kidney injury in preterm infants by proteomics. The infant will be monitored for AKI before and after receiving ibuprofen for closing patent ductus arteriosus. Urine samples will be collected for proteomics analysis to identify novel biomarkers for AKI. The aim of the study is to improve early detection of AKI in preterm infants and provide better treatment options.

The patient is a 7-year-old child with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The child experiences severe dental anxiety and has never been able to cooperate with dental procedures in a regular dental environment (RDE). The child's parents report difficulty in finding a dentist who can accommodate their child's needs. The child does not have any medical issues other than ASD, and takes no medications. The parents speak fluent English and are willing to participate in the study. The child's last dental checkup was two years ago, and there were multiple cavities and gingivitis present at that time.

A premature baby weighing 900 grams was born in the neonatal intensive care unit of Kalawati Saran Children's Hospital and Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi. The baby is in the first 48 hours of postnatal life and is currently receiving care in NICU. The parents have given their informed written consent for the baby to participate in the clinical trial. The baby has not received any muscle relaxants, sedatives, or analgesics, and has not undergone any surgery. There are no major congenital anomalies noted in the baby. The baby is not requiring ventilatory support and has not shown any neurological impairment such as HIE or seizures. The baby has a 5-min Apgar score of 8.

The patient is a 55 year old female who has been experiencing knee pain for the past 6 months. She has difficulty walking and climbing stairs due to the pain, which she rated a 7 out of 10 on the VAS scale. She has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis with radiographic evidence showing joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation. She has not received any intra-articular injections in the past 6 months and has not had any knee surgeries in the past 12 months. She has no history of drug abuse or infectious diseases such as Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C or HIV. She is not currently pregnant. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if autologous conditioned serum (ACS) can help decrease her pain and improve her knee functionality.

The patient is a 45-year-old Dutch-speaking woman who has been experiencing chronic nonspecific low back pain for over 6 months. She has a BMI of 32, which puts her in the obese category. She has sought care for her back pain and has access to the internet and a computer/tablet/smartphone. She does not have leg pain with a score of 7 or higher on a numeric rating scale. She has no evidence of specific spinal pathology such as hernia, spinal stenosis, spondylolisthesis, infection, spinal fracture or malignancy. She also does not have evidence of severe underlying comorbidity such as diabetes, cardiovascular problems, or metabolic diseases. She has not received any dietary or exercise interventions in the past.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in multiple injuries, including fractures to his left leg, right arm, and pelvis. The patient was admitted to the ICU and is currently receiving enteral nutrition through a feeding tube. The patient is expected to be in the ICU for more than 48 hours and has a functional access for enteral tube feeding and a central access for administration of test solution. The patient has no significant hepatic or renal failure and is not experiencing any severe metabolic acidosis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets all inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 14-year-old Black female residing in the Mott Haven neighborhood of the South Bronx, New York City. She lives with her mother, who is her primary caregiver, and has a younger sister. She is currently attending 8th grade and is interested in pursuing a career in medicine. She is active in her church youth group and enjoys playing basketball in her free time. She has never been sexually active but is curious about sex and has had several discussions with her friends about it. She feels comfortable talking with her mother about most things but has not yet discussed sex with her. She is interested in participating in a study that will help her and her mother communicate better about sex and make informed decisions about her sexual health.

A 50-year-old male patient was diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma during a routine colonoscopy. The tumour is located in the rectum, within 5 cm of the anal margin. He has no family history of cancer and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication. He has no other significant medical history. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma, and staging workup demonstrated no evidence of metastatic disease. The patient is a candidate for neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAT) to reduce tumour volume and aggressiveness prior to surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the Liquid Biopsies and IMAging for Improved Cancer Care clinical trial to improve monitoring of the response to NAT. The patient is in good general condition, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has measurable disease, and adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. The patient is willing to comply with the treatment and follow-up schedules, and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) due to septic shock of unknown origin. The patient has no significant past medical history, and he has not undergone any surgical procedures in the past. The patient has been intubated and is receiving mechanical ventilation. He has been receiving norepinephrine to maintain his blood pressure, and his lactate levels have been monitored closely. The patient has been unable to tolerate peroral intake due to his critical condition, and enteral feeding through a gastric tube has been initiated. The patient's legal guardian has given informed consent for the patient's participation in the study. The patient's baseline parameters and initial laboratory results have been evaluated, and he meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient will be randomized to either the oligomeric or polymeric enteral nutrition group, as per the study protocol. The aim is to optimize tolerance and nutritional status of the patient during his stay in the PICU.

The patient is a 35-year-old Arabic-speaking woman who has been living in the Piedmont Triad area of North Carolina for the past 5 years. She reports experiencing chronic musculoskeletal pain (CMP) for the past 2 years, which has significantly impacted her daily life, including difficulty sleeping, difficulty completing daily tasks, and missing work. She has sought medical attention for her pain but has faced challenges due to language barriers and limited access to healthcare. She also reports feeling marginalized due to her immigrant status and has experienced discrimination in various forms. She hopes to participate in this study to share her experiences and contribute to a better understanding of CMP in marginalized populations.

This clinical trial is looking for individuals who are at least 12 years old and have mild to moderate facial acne vulgaris. The study will last for 12 weeks and subjects will be randomized to receive treatment with either DFD-03 (tazarotene) Lotion 0.1%, Tazorac (tazarotene) Cream, 0.1%, Vehicle Lotion or Vehicle Cream. Safety assessments will include the investigator's assessment of local cutaneous tolerance/application site reactions on the face, vital signs and adverse events. Female subjects will be required to take a urine pregnancy test and use an acceptable method of birth control if sexually active. Subjects must be willing to comply with sun avoidance measures and not use any product on the face during the entire course of the study except for non-medicated, investigator-approved cleanser, sunscreen, face wash, and make-up as instructed by the investigator. Subjects must be in good general health and not have any facial skin disease or condition that would interfere with the study. They must also not have been treated for alcohol dependence or alcohol or drug abuse in the year.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pelvic pain for the last 2 years. She has been diagnosed with deep infiltrating endometriosis after undergoing clinical and transvaginal/transabdominal ultrasound examinations. She has tried medical therapy, but her pain has not improved. She is scheduled for surgery to remove endometriotic lesions using a minimally invasive approach. She has no other significant medical history and is in good overall health. She is willing to participate in a randomized control study comparing surgical outcomes and postoperative pelvic organ function in women with DIE submitted to robot-assisted or conventional laparoscopy. She provides informed consent to participate in the study and meets all eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 10 years. She experiences coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath, especially during physical activity. She has been treated with inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators. She smokes 10 cigarettes per day and has a history of seasonal allergies. She has never undergone a sputum induction test or FeNO measurement. Her lung function tests show reduced FEV1/FVC ratio and increased residual volume. She has a positive mannitol challenge test indicating airway hyperresponsiveness. She has no other lung diseases or comorbidities.

30 year old female who has been diagnosed with PTSD following a history of childhood abuse and sexual assault. She experiences symptoms such as flashbacks, nightmares, hypervigilance, and avoidance of triggers. She has previously undergone therapy and medication treatment for PTSD with some improvement, but still struggles with symptoms. She has completed an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled treatment trial of divalproex for PTSD and has seen improvement in her symptoms. She is willing to continue treatment and is interested in participating in the maintenance phase trial. She has no current substance abuse or dependence, and her physical and laboratory examination are normal. She has reliable birth control measures in place and is willing to comply with monthly pill counts and valproic acid level assessments. She is able to attend clinic visits regularly and is willing to be contacted in case of emergency.

A 47-year-old premenopausal woman with a history of breast cancer in her mother presents to her gynecologist for a routine check-up. During the clinical breast examination, a small, non-palpable lump is detected in her left breast. Her mammogram and ultrasound showed a highly suspicious lesion measuring 1.8 cm in diameter. A core biopsy confirmed malignancy. Her medical history is remarkable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medication. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She has two children and a supportive family. She is a teacher and leads an active lifestyle. She is interested in exploring non-invasive treatment options for her breast lesion and has consented to participate in the cryosurgery clinical trial.

Patient is a 46-year-old woman from the United States who has been serving as a caregiver for her husband, a veteran of the Iraq and Afghanistan wars. Her husband suffered a traumatic brain injury (TBI) during his deployment and has been receiving treatment at a Veterans Administration Medical Center. The patient has been struggling with the demands of caregiving and feels unprepared and overwhelmed. She has access to a telephone and speaks fluent English. She does not have any significant cognitive or communication problems that would interfere with the study. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her ability to care for her husband and manage the challenges of caregiving.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. He has undergone a biopsy and has been found to be a suitable candidate for palliative chemotherapy. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication to control it. He reports no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. The patient is willing and able to undergo cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) as part of the study. The patient is expected to have a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient is over the age of 18 and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study. The patient's hemoglobin level is above 10g/L, and he has no absolute contraindications for CPET. The patient has no significant relative contraindications for CPET, and his orthopaedic function is not compromised. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits involved.

A 30-year-old Hispanic female, G2P1, currently at 28 weeks gestational age, presents for routine antenatal care. She has a pre-pregnancy BMI of 36 and is being treated for gestational diabetes. Her first pregnancy resulted in a term delivery, but she had difficulty with low milk supply and was only able to breastfeed for 2 weeks. She is interested in using a contraceptive implant postpartum and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the impact of the timing of implant placement on breastfeeding success and duration. She speaks both English and Spanish and is willing to be randomized to one of three groups for the timing of implant placement: within 30 minutes of placental delivery, 24-72 hours postpartum, or 6 or more weeks postpartum. She is willing to be assessed at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months postpartum and is interested in learning more about the continuation and satisfaction with the contraceptive implant, as well as the side effects associated with it. She is committed to meeting her breastfeeding goals and hopes that this study will help support her in achieving them.

A 12-year-old boy diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia is undergoing chemotherapy treatment. He has been receiving treatment for the past six months and has completed two cycles so far. The patient lives with his parents and three siblings. His medical history is unremarkable before the diagnosis. He has been experiencing oral mucositis and gingivitis since starting chemotherapy. He reported difficulty in brushing his teeth due to the sensitivity of his oral tissues. His parents have been helping him with his oral hygiene routine. The patient's overall health status is stable. He is alert and oriented, has normal vital signs, and no signs of fever or infection. He is not allergic to any medications. His parents are willing to participate in the study and provide consent.

We are seeking Hong Kong Chinese-speaking men aged 18 years and above who have engaged in oral or anal intercourse with at least one man in the last six months, and have not received the HPV vaccine before. Participants should have regular internet access and should be willing to be followed up by phone for a period of nine months. Those who have plans to leave Hong Kong for more than one month consecutively within the next nine months will not be eligible for the study. The study aims to evaluate the efficacy of two online, theory-based interventions in increasing HPV vaccination uptake among Hong Kong Chinese MSM. Participants will be randomly allocated into one of three groups, and those in the two intervention groups will be exposed to web-based, interactive and theory-based health communication promoting HPV vaccination uptake. The primary outcome of the study will be whether the participant has taken up all three doses of HPV vaccination within the follow-up period.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with a ureteropelvic junction (UPJ) obstruction. She is scheduled for an open pyeloplasty surgery at The Hospital for Sick Children. She has no significant past medical history, and her physical examination is within normal limits. She weighs 18 kg and is 105 cm tall. She has never undergone any surgical procedures before. The child's parents have been informed about the surgical procedure, and they have given their informed consent for their child to participate in the study. The child is classified as an ASA score 2. Her labs are within normal limits, and she has no known allergies to medications. During the preoperative evaluation, the child appears anxious and fearful of the surgery. The child's parents express concern about the potential for postoperative pain and the use of opioid medications. They are interested in alternative options for pain management.

The patient is a 28-year-old individual who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for over three years. They have been using an insulin pump for more than three months and have been using the Dexcom G5 continuous glucose monitor (CGM) for at least six out of seven days per week. Their HbA1c levels range from 7.0-9.5%. They have an iPhone and a personal computer for uploading pump and CGM data. They are comfortable in speaking, reading, and writing English. They do not use a hybrid closed-loop system and are not planning to follow a specific diet plan for weight loss. They are able to consume "common meals" and do not have gastroparesis or an eating disorder. They are not using medications that can affect blood glucose levels or gastric emptying, and do not have a history of alcohol abuse or pre-conception, pregnancy, or lactation.

62-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease presented with worsening angina and was found to have significant stenosis on cardiac catheterization. He underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement. However, due to the severity of his underlying cardiac disease, he was scheduled for elective, complex cardiothoracic surgery (combined coronary artery bypass graft and valve surgery) with cardiopulmonary bypass. Given his history of bleeding disorders, the patient is at high risk for coagulopathy and is therefore an ideal candidate for this clinical trial. The patient will undergo Point-of-Care based hemotherapy to reduce the need for allogenic blood products in perioperative care. The patient will be monitored for diffuse bleeding after heparin reversal following extracorporeal circulation, intra- or postoperative blood loss exceeding 250 ml/h or 50 ml/10 min.

The patient is a premature baby girl born at 28 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 1.2 kg. She is currently admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) at St. Mary's Hospital in Manchester. Due to her prematurity, she requires intravenous access for parenteral nutrition and medication administration. However, due to her small size, peripheral venous access is challenging, and she has had multiple attempts at cannulation resulting in phlebitis and thrombosis. The medical team is considering enrolling her in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of a safety intravenous cannula with a standard intravenous cannula in neonates to determine the best approach for her ongoing care.

A 25-year-old female university student who is a non-smoker and not addicted came to the clinic to participate in the clinical trial for Paroxetine Hydrochloride. She is in good health, with a body mass index (BMI) between 18.5 and 27. She has no history of serious adverse events, liver, heart, gastrointestinal or renal illness. She consumes no more than 2 cups of coffee or tea per day. She has no history of hypersensitivity to the study drug or to compounds chemically related, nor has she concurrently or recently used any other antidepressives, schizophrenia, or anticonvulsant. She is willing to sign the informed consent and participate in the study.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who has been struggling with self-esteem issues due to the appearance of her chin. She has been referred to the clinic by her plastic surgeon for genioplasty to reposition and reshape her chin. She has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. She has agreed to participate in the study and undergo a CT scan as a part of her diagnosis and treatment. She does not have any craniofacial syndrome, segmental osseous genioplasty, previous osseous genioplasty, previous mandibular trauma or systemic disorders. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that the patient specific implants technique will provide her with the best possible surgical outcome.

45 yo F with recently diagnosed breast cancer scheduled for radical mastectomy. History of occasional low back pain and tension headaches, managed with over-the-counter pain relievers. No known allergies. No history of addiction to alcohol or drugs. No history of heart disease or diabetes. Normal blood pressure during preoperative visit. No known liver or kidney dysfunction. Willing to participate in research study and provide informed consent.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy volunteers who are willing to donate peripheral blood for in vitro studies. You may be eligible to participate if you are a healthy adult with no inflammatory or infectious complications and are not currently pregnant or needing/using drugs. The study aims to better understand the cellular and intracellular mechanisms that regulate leukocyte function, which is critical for immune defense and preventing autoimmune diseases. The investigators have found that hypertonic conditions regulate leukocyte functions through feedback mechanisms involving ATP release and purinergic receptors. By participating in this study, you can help contribute to a better understanding of immune cell regulation, which may lead to novel therapeutic approaches to improve immune function in patients suffering from various diseases.

The patient is a 52-year-old male smoker who has been smoking for the past 30 years. He has been coughing for the past few months and has noticed a decrease in his energy levels. He has also experienced some shortness of breath while climbing stairs. His BMI is 28. His chest X-ray revealed a mass in his right lung, and a biopsy confirmed the presence of lung cancer. He has not undergone any chemotherapy or radiation therapy in the past 3 months. He has no history of diabetes or organ transplant. He has not received any blood transfusions in the past 3 months. His medical history is negative for autoimmune diseases. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to read and write in English. He has provided informed consent for the study.

43-year-old Japanese female diagnosed with active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 5 years. She has tried multiple DMARDs in the past, but none of them have been effective in managing her symptoms. Currently, the patient reports experiencing pain, stiffness, and swelling in over 10 of her joints, making it difficult to perform daily activities. She has no history of acute inflammatory joint disease or any other medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the trial. The patient weighs 70 kg and has had a negative serum pregnancy test at screening. She is willing to participate in the study and is excited about the possibility of trying a new treatment option.

We are seeking healthy children who are full-term and have a single birth (no multiple births) to participate in a clinical trial. Children who have had major illnesses or surgeries requiring hospitalization that may impact outcomes, metabolic, congenital, or allergic diseases that impact food intakes will be excluded from the study. Parents must have sufficient command of the English language to complete the informed consent and study documents. The study will involve three groups of children, with 24 children in each group. Group 1 will consist of children consuming < 25 mg/day DHA and < 400 μg/day lutein. Group 2 will consist of children consuming > 150 mg/day DHA and > 1,200 μg/day lutein. Group 3 will consist of children consuming > 150 mg/day DHA and < 400 μg/day lutein. Children consuming 25-150 mg/day DHA or 400-1200 μg/day lutein will be excluded from the study. Additionally, children of mothers enrolled in studies by our group that involved randomization to supplemental DHA during pregnancy or who do not have complete blood, diet records, or developmental tests at 5 years and 9 months of age will be excluded. Children having a cardiac pacemaker, aneurysm clip, cochlear implant of possible metallic foreign bodies in the eyes or other contraindication as detailed in the C&W MRI Patient Screening Form will also be excluded.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who recently suffered from an acute myocardial infarction and underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stent (DES). He has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are both well-controlled with medications. He is currently taking aspirin and clopidogrel as dual antiplatelet therapy after the PCI procedure. His baseline hemogram shows the Hb level of 12g/dL and platelet count of 150,000/μL. He has no known hypersensitivity or contraindication to heparin, aspirin, clopidogrel, or cilostazol. He is not taking any other antiplatelet agents except for aspirin and clopidogrel. He has not experienced any gastrointestinal or genitourinary bleeding or major surgery within the past 3 months. He is not pregnant.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has no significant medical history. She is currently not taking any medication or supplements. She has completed her primary immunization against poliomyelitis according to local recommendations. She has not received any vaccination for polio (either inactivated or oral) in the past. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance medical research. She is willing to receive intramuscular injections as part of the trial. She is available to participate in the study for 8 days if she is assigned to the adult lead-in cohort.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with good general and oral health who brushes his teeth twice a day. He has a minimum of 16 natural teeth, including at least 10 of the 12 anterior teeth. The patient has classic Vita Shade minimum value of A2 or darker on at least 2 of the 4 maxillary anterior teeth. He has no significant oral soft tissue pathology, systemic-related gingival enlargement, tissue damage due to ill-fitting appliances or restoration, or extreme crowding or overlapping of teeth. The patient has no physical limitations that would preclude the use of normal oral hygiene procedures. He is willing to use the assigned products according to instructions, refrain from using any breath freshener products or unassigned oral care products, and refrain from using any whitening products and smokeless tobacco products within one week prior to and for the duration of the study. The patient is available for appointments and is likely to complete the study. He has not participated in any oral hygiene or product clinical study within the previous 30 days and is not on any medication that might interfere with the outcome of the study. The patient has no dental fluorosis, hypoplasia, restorations, tetracycline stains, or other enamel surface irregularities that may interfere with evaluation of the selected teeth. He has no visual evidence of moderate/advanced periodontitis (ADA Type III, IV) and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is willing to refrain from using any whitening products and smokeless tobacco products within one week prior to and for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who has been experiencing menopausal symptoms for the past year, including hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. She has a history of hypertension and has been on medication for the past year to control it. She has a BMI of 25 and has had a normal mammogram within the past year. She has not received any hormone therapy or implants in the past 12 months and has never been diagnosed with breast or estrogen-dependent cancer. Her last menstrual period was 18 months ago, and she has had no vaginal bleeding since. She has no known liver disease or other conditions affecting carbohydrate metabolism. She is interested in participating in the study to help find the best form of hormone therapy for her menopausal symptoms.

A 60-year-old man with a history of hypertension for 10 years. He has tried multiple antihypertensive medications, including a diuretic, but his blood pressure remains elevated. His most recent blood pressure readings were 150/90 mmHg. He has no history of diabetes or chronic kidney disease. He is currently on a low-salt diet and exercises regularly. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has never participated in a clinical study involving an investigational drug or device.

45 yo female with a history of pre-diabetes, elevated fasting blood glucose levels, and a sedentary lifestyle, working full-time in an office setting as a software engineer. The patient reports no significant medical history, no history of heart disease, renal disease, peripheral neuropathy, retinopathy, PAD, lower limb amputation, substance abuse, psychiatric disorder or immune-compromised conditions. The patient is a non-smoker and has no severe visual impairments. She is willing and able to participate in a light physical activity program and is interested in improving her overall health. She has not previously participated in a physical activity study and is not currently using insulin or an insulin pump.

A 68-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital for a hip replacement surgery. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis. Her preoperative assessment was unremarkable. The surgery was successful and she was transferred to the ICU for postoperative care. On the second postoperative day, she was found to be confused and disoriented. She was diagnosed with hypoactive delirium based on an ICDSC score of 3 and a RASS score of -1. She has no history of delirium prior to admission. She has no active psychosis and no substance abuse in her medical history. She is not pregnant and does not have dementia. She is eligible for the Basel BOMP-AID Randomized Trial. She is willing to undergo the required assessments and participate in the study.

A 42-year-old man with a history of peptic ulcer disease and gastritis visited the clinic for his bi-annual check-up. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and intermittent nausea for the past few months. He has never been diagnosed with Helicobacter pylori infection before. He takes no medication and has no allergies to any medication. He has no other serious health problems and is not pregnant. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the treatment plan for 12 days.

Male or female, 25 years old, BMI of 27, with a history of functional bloating. Avoids certain trigger foods that cause bloating and reports mild symptoms on an average of two days out of three days. No diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome, functional constipation or functional diarrhea. No known chronic gastrointestinal disease or condition including inflammatory bowel disease, coeliac disease. Not on a specific diet such as a strict low-FODMAP diet or taking antibiotics or proton pump inhibitors in the past 2 months. Not routinely taking medication that might modify gastrointestinal function such as prokinetic agents, anti-emetics, corticosteroids, narcotic analgesic agents, anticholinergic agents for irritable bowel syndrome, medications for constipation, 5HT3 antagonists, anti-diarrheal agents, opiate agents used to treat diarrhea, NSAIDs, histamine2 blockers, antacids, or supplements used to treat bloating. Not pregnant or lactating or planning pregnancy. Not consuming probiotics/prebiotic supplements in the past 4 weeks or anticipating changes to smoking habits in the next 2 months. Not abusing alcohol (>40 units per week)/non-prescription drugs/other medication. Willing to follow the protocol and provide consent.

52-year-old male with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) for the past 10 years and a recent diagnosis of Barrett's esophagus on endoscopic evaluation. The patient is concerned about the risk of developing esophageal cancer and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve detection of dysplasia and early cancer. The patient has no known bleeding disorders, and is willing to undergo both confocal laser endomicroscopy and standard endoscopy with biopsy. He understands the risks and benefits of the procedures and is able to provide informed consent.

45 y/o female with a history of chronic right shoulder pain and limited range of motion for 6 months. MRI revealed a rotator cuff tear of approximately 2cm. Patient has failed conservative treatment including physical therapy and NSAIDs. No history of traumatic injury to the shoulder. Past medical history includes hypertension, well controlled on lisinopril, and seasonal allergies. No history of bleeding disorders or liver/renal dysfunction. Patient is not currently taking any anticoagulation medications. Allergic to penicillin. Patient is interested in participating in the study and willing to be randomized to either the TXA or placebo group.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He is scheduled for on-pump cardiac surgery in the next month. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and diabetes. He is a smoker with a 30-pack-year history. His lung function tests indicate mild to moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has a history of stable angina and underwent angioplasty with stent placement three years ago. He is currently taking aspirin, a statin, and a beta-blocker. His echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 55%. He has no history of liver or kidney disease. He lives alone and is independent with his activities of daily living. He is concerned about the surgery and wants to ensure the best possible outcomes.

This is a 65-year-old woman who was admitted to Vancouver General Hospital with heart failure and hyponatremia. She was diagnosed with heart failure several years ago and has been on various medications to manage her symptoms, including furosemide and spironolactone. Despite her medication regimen, she has had several hospitalizations due to worsening heart failure symptoms, including shortness of breath and swelling in her legs. During this admission, her serum sodium levels were found to be below 130 mmol/L, and she was started on tolvaptan as part of this clinical trial. Her sodium levels improved with the medication, and she was able to be discharged home after several days in the hospital. She will be followed for the next 6 months with regular visits to monitor her sodium levels, heart failure symptoms, and overall health status.

A 60-year-old Hispanic male visited the clinic with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years. His blood pressure was 150/95 mmHg on amlodipine 10 mg once daily. The patient does not smoke and has never had a heart attack or stroke. He has a history of dyslipidemia with a total cholesterol of 220 mg/dL and an HDL of 35 mg/dL. His BMI is 29.2 kg/m2, and he has a waist circumference of 100 cm. His eGFR is 70 mL/min/1.73 m2, and his plasma potassium level is within normal range. He does not have diabetes, and he is not taking any prohibited medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 31-year-old female with a history of vitiligo for 6 years is seeking treatment for her condition. She has symmetrical depigmented patches on both arms, legs, and face, with a total affected body surface area of approximately 4%. She has tried various topical treatments in the past, including corticosteroids, but has not achieved satisfactory results. She has no other significant medical history, and she is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of 0.1% tacrolimus ointment and 0.1% mometasone furoate cream for the treatment of her vitiligo. She is able to comply with the study protocol and agrees to attend follow-up appointments at 2, 4, and 6 months to evaluate clinical improvement and report any side effects.

The patient is a male, over the age of 18, who has been diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the prostate within the last 180 days. The patient has a Gleason score of 2-6 and clinical stage T1-2a. The patient's PSA level is under 10 ng/mL and there is no evidence of distant metastases or regional lymph node involvement. The patient has not undergone prior radical surgery, cryosurgery, or high-intensity focused ultrasonography for prostate cancer. The patient has not undergone prior pelvic irradiation, prostate brachytherapy, or bilateral orchiectomy. The patient has not undergone prior hormonal therapy such as LHRH agonists or antagonists, anti-androgens, estrogens or surgical castration. The patient has not undergone prior or concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy for prostate cancer. The patient is willing and able to complete the Expanded Prostate Cancer Index Composite (EPIC) questionnaire. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 0-1 and no severe, active co-morbidity. The patient is not on concurrent 3D-conformal radiation therapy.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was diagnosed with clear cell carcinoma of the kidney and underwent a radical nephrectomy as a primary treatment. However, imaging studies revealed metastatic lesions in the lungs and liver. He has not received any prior systemic treatment for RCC. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. He has adequate organ function and his laboratory studies are within normal limits. His blood pressure is controlled with medication. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has no known contraindications to the study drug.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman diagnosed with primary angle-closure glaucoma (PACG) according to the International Society of Geographical & Epidemiological Ophthalmology (ISGEO) diagnostic criteria. She has been taking intraocular pressure (IOP) lowering drugs for more than 3 months and has mild to moderate cataract. She presents with visual field score ≥18 calculated as per the method used in the Advanced Glaucoma Intervention Study (AGIS). She has no history of secondary angle-closure glaucoma or previous surgery, except for laser peripheral iridotomy. She has consented to undergo Phaco-IOL-EGSL surgery for advanced PACG and cataract. Her preoperative examinations include best corrected logMAR visual acuity (BCVA), slit lamp and fundus examination, gonioscopy, Goldmann applanation tonometry, and ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM). Visual field tests will be conducted with a Humphrey Visual Field Analyzer II. She will be reviewed at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months after surgery. The number of IOP-lowering drugs and IOP will be observed and recorded at each follow-up. The extent of peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS), the BCVA, and the visual field will be recorded at 12 months following surgery. The patient will be monitored for any intraoperative and postoperative complications.

A 10-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with fever and abdominal pain. Blood tests are needed to determine the cause of his symptoms. He is nervous about the venipuncture and expresses fear of needles. He has no known allergies or previous adverse reactions to local anesthetics. He is accompanied by his mother who is willing to participate in the study and rate her son's pain. His skin appears healthy and there is no apparent inflammation or damage at the designated application site. He has not taken any analgesics in the past 24 hours. He is willing to participate in the study and able to demonstrate proper understanding of the Faces Pain Scale-Revised (FPS-R).

6 month old baby boy, born full term with a birth weight of 3.2 kg, who is scheduled to receive his routine immunizations. He has no history of any acute or chronic illnesses. The mother is willing to participate in the study and has given consent. The infant has not been fed 30 minutes prior to the immunization and has not received any analgesic/sedative medication on the day of the immunization. The infant is not diagnosed with any major congenital disorder that may alter behavioral responses to painful stimuli. The mother speaks fluent English and there are no language barriers to obtaining parental consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer. She has undergone two previous chemotherapies and has had a platinum-free interval of more than 3 months. She has been experiencing abdominal pain and bloating, and a CT scan has revealed the presence of measurable disease. The patient has been selected for the study based on a 2X-121 DRP® using Fixed in Formalin and Embedded in Paraffin (FFPE) archival or the latest tumor tissue with an outcome measured as being in the upper 50% likelihood of response. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 16 weeks. She has recovered to Grade 1 or less from prior surgery or acute toxicities of prior radiotherapy, or treatment with cytotoxic, hormonal or biologic agents. Her clinical laboratory parameters are within normal limits. The patient has adequate conditions and protocol values for absolute neutrophils count, hemoglobin, platelets, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST), serum bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, creatinine, and blood urea. The patient has FFPEs tumor tissue available from primary surgery or later. She has a negative serum pregnancy test and is willing to use adequate effective contraception during the study and a period after the last dose of study drug. The patient is not currently participating in or having participated in a study of an investigational agent or using an investigational device within 2 weeks of giving informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of locally recurrent or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma that has progressed after having received one or more prior lines of chemotherapy, including those whose disease has progressed within 6 months of postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy. The patient has a performance status of 1 and adequate bone marrow, liver, and kidney function within 28 days prior to the first dose. The patient has no history of topoisomerase I inhibitor(s) treatment and is not currently receiving any anticancer therapy or investigational drug or device within 2 weeks before C1D1. The patient has no cardiac disease such as unstable angina or myocardial infarction within 6 months of screening, NY Heart Association Class III - IV heart failure, QTc greater than 470 msec, or symptomatic orthostatic hypotension within 6 months of screening. The patient has no history of stroke or transient ischemic attack within 6 months of screening, prior history of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), or peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 2. The patient is not requiring medications with drugs that are inhibitors of UGT1A1 or substrates of CYP1A2, P-gP, BCRP, OATP1B1, OATP1B3 or OCT1 transporters. The patient has no leptomeningeal disease or spinal cord compression unless controlled and asymptomatic with surgery, radiation, and not requiring steroids within 4 weeks prior to C1D1. The patient has no brain metastases unless previously treated and asymptomatic. The patient has not undergone major surgery within 28 days of the first drug dose and is not pregnant or breast feeding. The patient has no evidence of severe uncontrolled systemic disease, bleeding diatheses, renal or liver transplant, active infection with hep B or C or HIV, and no hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction to ganetespib or other HSP90 inhibitors, irinotecan, SN-38 or its derivatives. The patient has no medical, psychological, or social condition that would interfere with the patient's participation in the study.

The patient is a 43-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis for at least 3 months prior to screening. The patient has experienced an inadequate response, loss of response, or intolerance to a treatment course of one or more standard of care medications, including oral 5-aminosalicylic acids, corticosteroids, immunomodulators, anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF) agents, and integrin inhibitors. The patient has not been diagnosed with Crohn's disease, indeterminate colitis, ischemic colitis, pseudomembranous colitis, or any other severe conditions such as fulminant colitis, abdominal abscess, toxic megacolon, or bowel perforation. The patient must agree to follow specific methods of contraception, if applicable. The patient has not been previously exposed to BMS-986165 or a TYK2 inhibitor.

A 25-year-old woman with β-thalassemia major was referred to the study due to severe cardiac iron overload. She has a history of chronic blood transfusions since early childhood and has received more than 100 units of red blood cell transfusions in her lifetime. She complains of fatigue and weakness with exertion and has occasional chest pain. She denies shortness of breath, orthopnea, or lower extremity edema. Her most recent cardiac MRI reveals a myocardial T2* value of 7 ms and a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 62%. Her serum creatinine is within normal range, and her urinary protein/creatinine ratio (UPCR) is less than 1.0 mg/mg. She is currently on deferoxamine therapy, but her iron overload continues to progress. She is interested in participating in the study to explore the potential benefits of combination therapy with deferasirox and deferoxamine followed by deferasirox monotherapy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has a history of smoking and has been experiencing shortness of breath, persistent coughing, and chest pain. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. The patient has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy for his lung cancer. CT scan has confirmed the presence of at least one measurable lesion as defined by RECIST (version 1.1). The patient's EGFR\ALK\ROS1 status is unknown. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meet the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 32-year-old man who was diagnosed with schizophrenia two years ago. He has been taking medication regularly and has completed the acute treatment phase. He lives with his parents and does not work. He experiences auditory hallucinations and delusions but has learned to manage them with the help of therapy. He has a history of substance abuse and has been sober for six months. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his sense of coherence and resilience. He has no other diagnosed mental health conditions or developmental disorders.

Maria is a 60-year-old woman who has had type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years. She has been experiencing vision loss in her left eye for the past few months and came to the clinic for evaluation. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. Her current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. She has not had any previous ocular surgeries or treatments for diabetic macular edema. On examination, her best corrected visual acuity in the left eye is 20/80. There is definite retinal thickening due to diabetic macular edema based on clinical exam and OCT, both at or within 500 microns of the macular center. There is no evidence of vitreoretinal interface disease as the primary cause of macular edema. She has no other ocular conditions that might affect macular edema or alter visual acuity during the first 12 months of the study. She is willing to provide informed consent and agrees to participate in the study.

The patient is a 22-year-old American Indian male enrolled at Salish Kootenai College. He has been smoking cigarettes for the past 4 years and smokes about half a pack per day. He has tried quitting in the past but has been unsuccessful. He is interested in quitting smoking and is willing to participate in a smoking cessation program. He has a valid telephone number and email address and is willing to be followed up for 6 months. He is in good health and has no medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 26-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has a body mass index (BMI) within the range of 18.5 - 24.9 Kg/m2 and weighs at least 45 Kgs. He has no contraindications or hypersensitivity to Ibuprofen, Diphenhydramine citrate, or related group of drugs. He has not had any significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunological, dermatological, neurological, or psychiatric disease or disorder. He is a non-smoker and has not consumed more than 10 cigarettes or bidis/day or tobacco products. He has no difficulty in swallowing solids like tablets or capsules. He has normal blood pressure and pulse rate. He has not taken any prescribed medication during the last two weeks or any over-the-counter medicinal products during the last one week preceding the first dosing. He has not participated in any drug research study within the past 3 months and has not donated blood in the past 3 months before screening. He is willing to give written informed consent and adhere to all the requirements of this protocol.

The patient is a 40-year-old man with HIV infection and renal insufficiency. He has been on dialysis treatment for at least 3 months. He has not been treated with zidovudine (AZT) or any other antiretroviral agent or experimental therapy within the last 2 weeks. He has not received any cytotoxic chemotherapy within the last 30 days. He has no active opportunistic infections, severe malabsorption syndrome, or acute illness. He has no known sensitivity to zidovudine or thymidine-type agents. He does not have diabetes mellitus requiring treatment. He has no active drug or alcohol use that might interfere with the study objectives.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with obesity and hypertension. He is a patient of Picket primary care clinic and owns a smartphone with a data and text messaging plan. The patient has Wifi available in his home. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to test the mobile health platform. The patient has no prior experience with tracking his health data but is willing to learn and use the iHealth wireless scale and blood pressure device to track his weight, blood pressure, and pO2. The patient is willing to wear a fitbit device to track his physical activity and sleep activity. He is also willing to receive daily nutrition and exercise weight loss messages via text messages. The patient is excited about the potential benefits of using the mobile health platform to improve his health outcomes and is looking forward to participating in the trial.

Patient A is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma for 5 years. She has been taking fluticasone 2500mcg/day for the last 2 years, but still experiences daily asthma symptoms. Her BMI is 35, indicating that she is obese. She has never smoked and reports no history of liver disease or psychiatric illness. She has not been pregnant or nursing within the last year. She has never taken Roflumilast or any other PDE4 inhibitor. She has not had any adverse reactions to medications in the past. Her FeNO is 25 ppb, and her peripheral blood eosinophil count is 250 (x10-6/ul). She has had 3 oral steroid bursts within the past year and has required additional daily treatment with other controller medication. She has also had 1 urgent care visit within the past year for her asthma. Her baseline FEV1/FVC is 65%, and her FEV1 is 75% predicted. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of roflumilast in severe asthma.

A 56-year-old man who underwent cardiac surgery with sternotomy 2 weeks ago presents with complaints of persistent chest pain and discomfort. He reports that the pain has been constant since the surgery and is negatively impacting his daily activities, making it difficult for him to sleep or perform household chores. The patient has no prior history of chronic pain or neurological pathologies. He is not currently being treated with antidepressant medication. The patient is interested in participating in a study to better understand the mechanism of this chronic pain and to find ways to prevent or treat it in the future.

The patient is a pregnant woman who is currently in her 27th week of gestation. She has been diagnosed with a high-risk pregnancy due to the premature birth of her previous child. The patient is currently receiving steroid prophylaxis to help with the development of the fetus' lungs. The patient will be delivering the child at a university hospital and will be eligible for the trial if the child is born before 28 weeks gestational age. The patient will not be eligible if there is a decision to intubate the infant before delivery or if there are any known malformations or neuromuscular diseases. The patient will be fully informed about the

A 56-year-old male has been diagnosed with severe COVID-19 infection and is currently hospitalized. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is taking lisinopril and atorvastatin respectively. He has a BMI of 32.9 and has no allergies to drugs or other substances. The patient has been receiving oxygen therapy through nasal cannula, and his oxygen saturation levels have been fluctuating between 90-94%. His respiratory rate is 28 breaths per minute, and he has a fever of 101.5°F (38.6°C). The patient has no prior history of DNR or DNI orders and is willing to participate in the study after providing informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been experiencing a large lump on his arm for several months. The lump is hard, painless, and has grown in size over time. He has been experiencing some mild numbness and tingling in his fingers, which he attributes to the lump pressing on a nerve. He has been previously diagnosed with dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans and has undergone surgery to remove the primary tumor, but the disease has recurred and has metastasized to other parts of his body. He has also received radiation therapy, but the disease continues to progress. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He is physically active and enjoys playing basketball with his friends in his free time. His BMI is 26 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications.

A 65-year-old woman was referred to the clinic for cataract surgery. She had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which were well-controlled with medication. She reported difficulty with reading and driving at night due to poor vision. Her visual acuity was 20/50 in both eyes. She was diagnosed with bilateral cataracts and was scheduled for bilateral phacoemulsification with implantation of a multifocal IOL. She has no known allergies and has not used topical ketorolac previously. She is able to complete all study visits and provides written informed consent.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who is experiencing chronic lower back pain. He works in construction and enjoys playing basketball on the weekends. He has tried physical therapy and medication, but the pain persists. His medical history is unremarkable and he is not taking any medications currently. He has no history of pregnancy and is willing to participate in the follow-up examination.

Pt is a 45yo M who presented to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain radiating to his back, nausea, and vomiting. He had a history of chronic alcohol use and was found to have elevated serum amylase and lipase levels. Abdominal CT scan revealed findings consistent with acute pancreatitis. Pt met the inclusion criteria for the study with a SIRS score of 3 (heart rate >90/min, respiratory rate >20/min, and WBC count of 15,000/mm3). He did not meet any of the exclusion criteria. The study team approached him for participation in the randomized controlled pilot trial of rectal indomethacin in acute pancreatitis. The risks and benefits of participation were explained to him, and he provided informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old Indian man who has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and constipation for the past 6 months. He initially ignored the symptoms, but as they persisted, he consulted a local doctor who prescribed some medications for indigestion. However, the symptoms did not improve, and he lost some weight as well. He then visited a tertiary care hospital where he underwent some tests, including colonoscopy, which revealed a mass in his colon. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of colorectal cancer. His family is from a rural village, and they have limited financial resources. He is the sole breadwinner for his family, which includes his wife, two adult children, and elderly parents. He works as a farmer and has no health insurance. He is worried about the cost of treatment and whether he will be able to continue supporting his family. He has some knowledge about cancer and treatment options through his community members and the internet, but he is not sure about the best course of action. He is willing to participate in the study to understand the financial and non-financial barriers to CRC treatment and help other patients like him.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis. She has a relapsing-remitting form of MS and has not had any relapses or methylprednisolone treatments in the last 30 days. The patient reports functionally significant spasticity in her right lower extremity, which has been causing gait impairment and falls. She is ambulatory but experiences pain in her low back and hip due to the spasticity. Her EDSS score is 4.5. The patient is on a stable medication regimen and is not currently taking any medications that could influence muscle tone or have anti-spasticity effects. She has no known

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Crohn's Disease. She has been experiencing frequent episodes of inflammatory back pain and is enrolled in a clinical trial to evaluate imaging biomarkers in Crohn's-associated Spondyloarthritis. The patient is able to speak English and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She has not been exposed to any biologic agents within the past six months, except for Vedolizumab, which is locally effective. The patient has not been diagnosed with psoriasis or any other inflammatory arthritis. Her medical history does not include any malignancy within the past five years, except for non-melanomatous skin cancer. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any contraindications to MRI.

A 52-year old accountant was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She is on metformin and adheres to a healthy diet and exercise routine. She has never consumed alcohol and has been an abstainer all her life. She is married and has two adult children. She has a sedentary work life and spends most of her time sitting in front of a computer screen. She complains of occasional fatigue and sleepiness during work hours. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or major surgeries. Her latest HbA1c was 7.5%. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who works as a marketing executive in a medium-sized firm. She is married and has two children. She reports drinking alcohol every day after work to relieve stress. Her husband has expressed concerns about her drinking but she has been brushing it off. Recently, she has been experiencing headaches, nausea, and fatigue. She has also missed work a few times due to these symptoms. She has decided to seek help for her drinking problem and is interested in participating in an internet-based intervention. She scored 12 on the AUDIT and reports consuming about 20 drinks per week. She is willing to complete follow-up surveys and is open to being randomized to any of the intervention groups including the no intervention control condition.

This is a 62 year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction. He was admitted to the intensive care unit with signs of septic shock and was intubated and mechanically ventilated. During his stay, he developed a cardiac arrest, with CPR initiated immediately by the medical team. The patient is currently receiving invasive arterial blood pressure monitoring, with the first compression of CPR captured on transmitted arterial blood pressure waveform data. He has an internal jugular central venous catheter in place and systemic vascular resistance is being monitored prior to and during CPR. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the PERSEUS-PS randomized controlled trial and will be allocated into group A for resuscitation with the PERSEUS protocol.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (MZL) a year ago. He had no prior history of cancer and no family history of lymphoma. He underwent chemotherapy with R-CVP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisone) for six cycles and responded well, with a significant reduction in the size of the lymph nodes. However, after eight cycles, his disease stabilized, and the lymph nodes stopped shrinking. He underwent a CT scan, which showed stable disease. The treating physician suggested rituximab maintenance therapy, which the patient agreed to. He has no history of significant medical illnesses, and his liver and kidney functions are within normal limits. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is able to carry out his activities of daily living without assistance. He is married and has two children. He enjoys playing golf and traveling with his family. He is aware of the risks and benefits of the study and has given informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese Han male who recently experienced shortness of breath and chest pain. He is a former smoker and has a family history of deep vein thrombosis. The pain started suddenly and has been constant for the past two days. The patient has no history of heart or lung problems and has never been diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE). He is currently taking medication for high blood pressure. Upon examination, the patient has tachypnea and decreased breath sounds in the left lung. Computed tomographic pulmonary angiography (CTPA) confirmed the diagnosis of acute pulmonary embolism. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria of being a Chinese Han population older than 14 years old with acute VTE diagnosis in 1 month and informed consent. He does not meet the exclusion criteria as he does not have psychosis, contraindications for CTPA, chronic VTE, or recurrence of chronic VTE.

Looking for adolescents who have experienced knee pain in the past 5 years, and those who have not, to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the prognosis of patellofemoral pain (PFP) compared to other types of knee pain. If you are between the ages of 15 and 19, and have experienced knee pain lasting longer than 6 weeks, this study may be of interest to you. Specifically, we are looking for individuals who have experienced anterior knee or retropatellar pain provoked by activities such as prolonged sitting or kneeling, squatting, running, hopping, or stair climbing. Participants must not have any other injuries or pain in the hip, lumbar spine, or other knee structures, and must not have self-reported patellofemoral instability or knee joint effusion. Your participation in this study can help us gain insights into the prognosis of PFP and knee pain, and potentially improve treatment options for individuals experiencing these conditions.

55-year-old male with a history of chronic venous insufficiency presents to the vascular clinic with complaints of pain and swelling in his right leg. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and they have been progressively worsening. He has also been experiencing occasional cramping in his right calf. He reports that his symptoms are worse after prolonged periods of standing or sitting, and are relieved with elevation of his leg. He has no history of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. He has been previously treated with compression stockings and lifestyle modifications, but his symptoms have not significantly improved. He has no known allergies and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

65 year old woman who underwent heart transplant surgery during her current hospitalization. She has a primary caregiver, her daughter, who is actively involved in her care. The patient has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol but has been compliant with medications. She is able to read and speak English fluently. The patient is currently on a stable dose of immunosuppressive medication and has not experienced any complications post-surgery. She is eager to learn about the necessary lifestyle changes that come with having a transplanted heart and is open to receiving education from the nursing staff. She is motivated to maintain her health and is interested in participating in the satisfaction survey to provide feedback on the educational program.

The patient is a 45-year-old male residing in China with a history of chronic renal failure requiring hemodialysis for the past 2 years. He has been diagnosed with secondary hyperparathyroidism with an intact PTH level of 450 pg/mL and a corrected serum calcium level of 9.5 mg/dL. He has been treated with activated vitamin D drugs, a phosphate binder, and a Ca preparation for the past 6 months. He has never received cinacalcet hydrochloride, bisphosphonates, denosumab or teriparatide. He has no history of parathyroidectomy or parathyroid intervention in the past 2 years. Medical records show no history of severe heart disease or hepatic dysfunction. He has well-controlled hypertension and diabetes. He is willing to give written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 24-year-old single woman residing in Lusaka, Zambia. She is a sex worker and at high risk for HIV infection. She is willing to undergo HIV testing, counseling, and receive test results. She plans to stay in Lusaka for at least 12 months and is willing to answer questions related to HIV risk factors, and if infected, questions related to the route and timing of exposure. She is willing and able to return for follow-up visits and provide informed consent. She is willing to undergo pregnancy testing and use an injectable, implant or intrauterine device (IUD) from screening until four months after the last vaccination during the study. She has no history of severe allergic reactions to any substance and is not currently on immunosuppressive therapy. She is eager to participate in the study to help inform recruitment and retention strategies and HIV incidence among high risk women in future HIV vaccine trials.

45-year-old male, who had a fracture in his right elbow six months ago, is experiencing limitation in flexion and extension. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of Graded Motor Imagery (GMI) on function, pain, and range of motion (ROM) in patients with elbow limitation. The patient has no history of complex regional pain syndrome, peripheric nerve injury, heterotopic ossification, myositis ossification or post-traumatic ankylosing. The patient has not received any physiotherapy for elbow limitation before. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to comply with the treatment regimen. The patient has no history of cardiovascular diseases, neurological disorders, rheumatic diseases, or psychiatric conditions. The patient has no visual loss and has full use of the contralateral upper extremity.

The patient is a 55-year-old female with a medical history of type 2 diabetes. She has had the condition for the past 10 years and is currently on medications to manage her blood sugar levels. The patient is scheduled to undergo free flap surgery to reconstruct a breast after mastectomy due to breast cancer. During the pre-operative evaluation, the patient was found to have good circulation in her extremities. She has no history of peripheral vascular disease or any other cardiovascular conditions. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent. The patient will receive alprostadil during the surgery as part of the study protocol. She is otherwise healthy and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study.

Patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer. The tumor is larger than 5 cm in diameter and has involved the chest wall. The patient has not received any prior treatment for breast cancer, including chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or biological therapy. She has no metastases other than regional lymph node involvement. The patient has measurable disease by physical examination, breast sonography, and other imaging studies. Her Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) is 80%. She has adequate bone marrow reserve, liver and kidney function, with white blood cell count (WBC) of 4,200/ mm3, absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1,700/mm3, platelets of 120,000/mm3, total bilirubin of 1.5 mg/dl, serum alanine transaminases (ALT) and aspartate transaminase (AST) within normal limits, and serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dl. The patient is not pregnant or lactating. She has no prior serious cardiac conditions such as angina, myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy, severe cardiovascular disease, or cardiac arrhythmias. The patient has no serious concomitant systemic disorders or secondary malignancy in the past five years before entry of the study (except in situ carcinoma of the cervix, or adequately treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin). She has no active infection or significant neurological or psychiatric disorder. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been experiencing episodes of jaundice and severe abdominal pain. He has been diagnosed with a common bile duct stone and will require an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) procedure. His past medical history is significant for hypertension which is well-controlled with medications. He does not have any other significant comorbidities, and he is not allergic to any medications used in the ERCP procedure. He is able to communicate effectively with the healthcare team and is not deaf. He is not pregnant.

A 28-year-old woman from Reunion Island experienced the tragic loss of her baby during pregnancy. The foetus weighed more than 500 g and was more than 22-weeks-old. She underwent regular prenatal care during her pregnancy, but unfortunately, her baby did not survive. She has agreed to participate in a non-interventional case-control study aimed at identifying the major causes of foetal or new-born death in Reunion Island. The study will screen socio-economic conditions, pregnancy care, and prevention methods to determine which public health actions should be taken to prevent such tragedies in the future.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy individuals, as well as those with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has reported memory difficulties in the last 6 months. She is able to perform her daily activities but has some difficulty in remembering new information. She has no history of musculoskeletal disorders, stroke, or other cerebrovascular diseases with spinal sensorimotor sequelae. She has no contraindications for performing a brain MRI. The patient has consented to participate in the study and agrees to undergo the Korvit® boots and imagination of the walk paradigms. She has no prior experience with MRIs but is willing to undergo the procedure.

The patient is an adult over 18 years of age with a confirmed diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, excluding the lip, nasopharynx, paranasal sinus, and salivary gland. They have stage III or IV disease, with no evidence of distant metastases and a negative chest x-ray. The primary site of the cancer must be identified, and it is considered appropriate for definitive radiotherapy with curative intent. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 0-1 and a life expectancy that is not specified. Their granulocyte count is greater than 1,500/mm^3, and their platelet count is greater than 100,000/mm^3. They have no evidence of pre-existing peripheral neuropathy and no active systemic infection. They have not had prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or

The patient is a 62-year-old Caucasian woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient was admitted to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided facial droop, right arm and leg weakness, and difficulty in speaking. The patient was last seen normal 2 hours ago. CT scan showed no hemorrhage or other abnormalities, and the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 9. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the trial, including being 18-80 years old, with a time from onset to treatment of ≤4.5 hours, and an NIHSS score ≥6, as well as being diagnosed with ischemic stroke. The patient provided signed informed consent to participate in the trial. The patient's blood pressure was stable, and platelet counts were within normal range. The patient was not on any heparin or oral anticoagulation therapy, and blood glucose levels were normal. The patient has not received any other investigational drug or device within the past 3 months, and there were no other exclusion criteria for the trial.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of pelvic organ prolapse. She complains of urinary symptoms such as urgency, frequency, and stress incontinence.
