She also reports a decrease in sexual function and discomfort during intercourse. Her medical history is significant for two uncomplicated vaginal deliveries. Upon physical examination, she is found to have a stage 3 pelvic organ prolapse with a cystocele and rectocele. The patient has no history of other medical problems or surgeries. She is currently not taking any medications.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who has been diagnosed with dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) for the past year. He has a history of Parkinsonism, with bradykinesia, rigidity, and resting tremor. He has also been experiencing visual hallucinations and mild cognitive impairment. His DaTScan test results were abnormal. The patient has been taking Levodopa for the past six weeks, and he is stable on acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and dopamine agonists. He also takes monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MOA-B) for the past four weeks before enrollment. He does not have any significant medical history or psychiatric illnesses apart from his current diagnosis. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and his alcohol intake is moderate. His physical exam is not remarkable for any other abnormalities. The patient's QTc interval is 450ms. He has not taken any medication that could prolong the QTc interval or interfere with Bosutinib. He is willing to undergo LP at baseline and 3 months after treatment. He has provided written informed consent and is capable of providing informed consent and complying with study procedures.

A 55-year-old man with a history of smoking for 30 years came to the clinic with complaints of persistent cough and difficulty breathing. He has been coughing up mucus for the past 6 months, especially in the morning. His chest X-ray showed evidence of bronchiectasis. He has been taking albuterol and tiotropium inhalers for the past 2 months, but he still experiences shortness of breath during daily activities. He is currently not on any other medications, and he does not have any other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the procedures involved.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who has been referred by her pediatrician for an advanced MRI scan to assess a neurological condition. She is accompanied by her mother who consents to her participation in the study. The patient has no known allergies or medical conditions that would interfere with the MRI scan. She is able to lie still for extended periods of time and does not have any breathing problems or motion disorders. She has no history of claustrophobia. Her weight and height are within normal limits for her age. She has not undergone any previous surgeries or medical procedures that would disqualify her from participating in the study. She does not use any electronic or magnetic devices, nor does she have any metal implants, foreign bodies or metallic fragments in her body. She is able to remove any removable devices or jewelry prior to the MRI scan. She is a native English speaker and attends school regularly. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is not a ward of the state, nor has she been institutionalized or imprisoned. She is not an employee of the research site or sponsor.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who presented with fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. She underwent a biopsy, which confirmed a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She has no significant medical history, and her family history is negative for cancer. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her physical examination is remarkable for palpable lymph nodes in the neck and axilla. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Her lab results are remarkable for anemia (Hb 9 g/dL), elevated LDH (500 U/L), and elevated beta-2 microglobulin (3.5 mg/L). She has no evidence of CNS involvement. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, and she gives written informed consent to participate.

Pt is a 30yo M with a history of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) presenting with skeletal pain attributed to XLH/osteomalacia. The patient's diagnosis of XLH is supported by classic clinical features of adult XLH (such as short stature or bowed legs) and a serum intact FGF23 (iFGF23) level > 30 pg/mL by Kainos assay. The patient also has biochemical findings consistent with XLH based on overnight fasting with serum phosphorus < 2.5 mg/dL and a ratio of renal tubular maximum phosphate reabsorption rate to glomerular filtration rate (TmP/GFR) < 2.5 mg/dL. The patient has a score of ≥ 4 on the Brief Pain Inventory question 3 (BPI-Q3, Worst Pain) at Screening indicating skeletal pain attributed to XLH/osteomalacia. The patient has an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 60 mL/min using the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) equation. The patient is willing to provide access to prior medical records for the collection of biochemical and radiographic data and disease history, and is able to complete all aspects of the study, adhere to the study visit schedule, and comply with the assessments. The patient is willing to use two effective methods of contraception as determined by the site investigator if the patient is of child-bearing potential or has a partner of child-bearing potential who has not undergone a total hysterectomy or a bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and is sexually active. The patient has not used any pharmacologic vitamin D metabolite or analog, oral phosphate, aluminum hydroxide antacids, acetazolamides, thiazides, bisphosphonates, denosumab, or teriparatide within the specified timeframes prior to Screening. The patient does not have corrected serum calcium level ≥ 10.8 mg/dL (2.7 mmol/L) at Screening and serum intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) ≥ 2.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN) at Screening. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding at Screening or planning to become pregnant (self or partner) at any time during the study. The patient is able and willing to withhold prohibited medications throughout the study, and does not have a documented dependence on narcotics or a history of positive test for human immunodeficiency virus antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen, and/or hepatitis C antibody. The patient does not have a history of recurrent infection (other than dental abscesses, which are known to be associated with XLH) or predisposition to infection, or of known immunodeficiency. The patient does not have a presence of malignant neoplasm (except basal cell carcinoma) or a concurrent disease or condition that would interfere with study participation or affect safety.

A 9-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with right wrist pain after falling off her bike. X-rays reveal a displaced distal third forearm fracture with an angulation of 35 degrees and 100% translation on the AP view. The patient undergoes closed reduction and is found to have adequate alignment. The treating physician recommends either a long arm or short arm fiberglass cast for immobilization. The patient and her family are informed of the study and are interested in participating. The patient has no history of orthopedic procedures or known pathologic fracture. There is no evidence of compartment syndrome or neuropathy. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is enrolled.

50 year-old male with a history of smoking presents with a left-sided mass in his throat that has been growing over the past 6 months. Upon evaluation, a biopsy of the mass confirms a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. The patient is scheduled to undergo chemoradiation at Stanford. The patient reports experiencing severe dry mouth (xerostomia) as a side effect of previous cancer treatments. The patient is in good overall health with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient is able to swallow d-limonene gelcaps and has adequate hepatic, hematologic, and renal function. The patient has a negative serum pregnancy test and agrees to use a birth control method during the entire duration of d-limonene treatment. The patient is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document.

57-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and recent elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) presents with left ventricular dysfunction. He has no history of acute or chronic pulmonary disease, neurological, neuromuscular, musculoskeletal, or osteoarticular incapacitating. Spirometry shows no abnormalities. The patient is able to maintain spontaneous ventilation on the first postoperative day, has no surgical indication of urgency, and is not morbidly obese. He has stable hemodynamics during the six-minute walking test and is not on prolonged mechanical ventilation. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the consent form. However, he has a history of ventricular tachycardia and atrioventricular block second or degree during exercise, which may put him at increased risk with the beginning of the proposed exercise protocols.

38-year-old female with a BMI of 31.5 kg/m2 who has struggled with weight loss for several years. She has tried various diets and exercise programs with limited success. She is surgically sterile and has no history of eating disorders, bariatric surgery, or diabetes. She is not currently taking any medications for thyroid, renal or hepatobiliary disease, or excessive alcohol consumption. She has not used drugs of abuse and has not donated blood in the last 3 months. The patient is interested in participating in the study to explore new options for weight loss and body composition changes.

Patient is a 45-year-old male from the United States who was diagnosed with acromegaly more than a year ago. He is currently receiving treatment with long-acting somatostatin analogs (LA-SMSA) for at least 6 months. He has no changes in his treatment schedule and is willing to participate in the study. He is married and has two children. His past medical history is significant for hypertension which is well controlled with medication. His BMI is 25, BP: 130/80, HR: 70/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for liver function tests within normal limits, HbA1C: 52 mmol/mol.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was previously enrolled in an Incyte-sponsored clinical trial of itacitinib for the treatment of moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis. She has been receiving itacitinib treatment for the past 6 months and has experienced significant improvement in her condition, as determined by her rheumatologist. Her medical history is significant for rheumatoid arthritis, for which she has been receiving treatment with methotrexate and prednisone. She does not have any other significant medical issues and her family history is non-contributory. She is compliant with her current treatment regimen and has demonstrated good clinical response to itacitinib. She is willing and able to comply with the scheduled visits and treatment plans required for this study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to avoid pregnancy during the study period.

A 22-year-old female university student came to the clinic with complaints of pain and discomfort in her lower right jaw. She reported difficulty opening her mouth and chewing due to the presence of an impacted lower third molar. She had been experiencing these symptoms for the past 3 months, and the pain intensity had increased during the last week. She had no significant medical history and was a non-smoker. She was interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of Concentrated Growth Factor (CGF) and Advanced Platelet Rich Fibrin (A-PRF) on post-operative pain, edema, and trismus after impacted lower third molar surgery.

A 45-year-old male with a history of heavy smoking presents with cough, fever, and chest pain. A chest X-ray shows a cavity in the right upper lobe of the lung. Further evaluation with a CT scan reveals the presence of a fungal ball consistent with pulmonary aspergilloma. The patient has a history of recurrent episodes of pneumonia and has been treated with several courses of antibiotics without significant improvement. The patient is referred for a surgical evaluation to assess the possibility of surgical resection of the infected tissue or bronchial artery embolization. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history or underlying comorbidities. The patient is willing to participate in the retrospective analysis of outcomes after treatment of pulmonary aspergilloma.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been suffering from hay fever for the past 5 years. She experiences moderate-severe symptoms such as nasal congestion, itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, and runny nose during the grass pollen season (mid-May to mid-July). She has a positive skin prick test response to timothy grass pollen, with a wheal diameter of 6 mm. She has not received any grass pollen immunotherapy in the past. She does not have any history of recurrent acute sinusitis or chronic sinusitis, and she has not had any upper respiratory tract infections or acute otitis media recently. She is not currently taking any systemic immunosuppressive treatment or investigational drugs. She has no history of fish allergy or life-threatening anaphylaxis or angioedema. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with study procedures. She has been informed about the potential risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with high LDL levels during a routine check-up. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having suffered a heart attack at the age of 55. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of smoking or other major health concerns. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand his risk for developing atherosclerotic disease and to potentially contribute to the development of new therapeutic measures. He is willing to complete a nutrition questionnaire and provide a 5 cc blood sample for analysis.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection for over 20 years. He has a mild form of the disease that has remained stable and non-progressive. The patient has not received any previous treatment for HCV and has not participated in any clinical trials related to HCV research. He has no other significant medical history and currently has no symptoms related to his hepatitis C infection. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide bone marrow samples for the generation of anti-HCV antibodies.

The patient is a 52-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Sjogren's Syndrome for the past 2 years. She complains of severe ocular dryness, which has been ongoing for the past 6 months. She has difficulty with reading and using the computer due to her symptoms. Her current medications include hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily and ibuprofen 800 mg twice a day for joint pain. She has no history of ocular surgery, and her best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. The patient has not used cyclosporine or ocular steroids in the past 3 months. She has no known allergies to any medications. The patient is not pregnant or lactating.

Patient is a 40-year-old male with a clinical diagnosis of angioid streaks who presented with blurred vision in his left eye. The patient had a history of hypertension and was a smoker. Dilated fundus examination and OCT revealed subfoveal choroidal neovascularization. The patient had not received any prior treatment for this condition. On BCVA testing, the patient had a visual acuity of 20/50 in the left eye. The patient was eligible for the clinical trial and received a primary 2.5 mg injection of Bevacizumab (Avastin) intravitreally. The patient was subsequently evaluated with BCVA at 1, 2, 4, and 12 weeks, and OCT and fluorescein angiography at month 1 and 3. The patient will continue to be followed for 6 months.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for 10 years. She has noticed bleeding gums and bad breath for the past 6 months. She reports that her blood sugar levels have been difficult to control and have been averaging around 200 mg/dL. Her dental exam shows moderate to severe periodontal disease, with pockets of 4-6 mm and bleeding upon probing. She has never received any periodontal treatment before. Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well controlled on levothyroxine. She is a non-smoker and not currently pregnant. Her bloodwork shows: A1c: 9.0% Fasting glucose: 190 mg/dL Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL with eGFR >60 mL/min Aspartate aminotransferase (AST): 14 U/L Alanine aminotransferase (ALT): 16 U/L

The patient is a 55-year-old male veteran with a diagnosis of subclinical hypothyroidism (SCH) made in 2015 at the Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System (CAVHS) during a routine medical check-up. He has been taking levothyroxine (LT4) 50 mcg daily since then. He denies any significant symptoms related to hypothyroidism or previous history of overt hypothyroidism. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril, and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes atorvastatin. He underwent a coronary artery bypass graft surgery in 2018 due to unstable angina. He denies any history of thyroid surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, or antithyroid medications. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial exploring the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of discontinuing LT4 in patients with SCH.

We are seeking women who are pregnant with twins or any higher order multiple to participate in a study to see if daily use of vaginal progesterone gel will prevent preterm birth. To be eligible, you must be between 16-20 6/7 weeks gestational age and have confirmed multiple pregnancy with at least 2 live fetuses. You cannot participate if you have placenta previa, pre-existing hypertension, major fetal anomaly, monoamniotic/monozygotic multiples, history of thromboembolic disease, or plans to move to another city during pregnancy. The study will involve daily use of either vaginal progesterone gel or a placebo gel until 35 6/7 weeks, with data collected on you and your infants to see if the medication prolongs pregnancy.

A 60 year old man came to the clinic with chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. He had a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking for 20 years. After undergoing coronary angiography, he was diagnosed with a severe blockage in his left anterior descending artery, so he underwent elective PCI with stenting. However, he was found to be a clopidogrel low-responder with a MULTIPLATE hep-ADP value of 80 U despite receiving 600 mg clopidogrel the day before. He was screened for eligibility and met the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial. He is randomized to receive either clopidogrel 150 mg or Prasugrel 10 mg once daily for 30 days after the procedure. His follow up will be at 30 days after PCI, where another MULTIPLATE test will be performed to assess platelet inhibition. He is advised to report any bleeding episodes or other complications that may occur during the treatment period. He is not eligible if he needs vit K antagonist, is a woman with childbearing potential, is breastfeeding, has planned surgery within 6 months, is intolerant to clopidogrel, prasugrel, or aspirin, or has a history of stroke.

Patient A is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of bacterial vaginosis such as vaginal discharge, itching and odor for the past week. She is sexually active with a single partner and uses condoms for contraception. She has no history of sexually transmitted infections. She has not used any vaginal suppositories or drugs in the past month. She is not currently menstruating and has not douched or had sexual intercourse in the past 48 hours. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and sign the written consent.

A 50-year-old woman came to the clinic with concerns about memory loss and difficulty with problem-solving that have been getting worse over the past year. She is a legal secretary and has noticed that she has been forgetting important appointments and tasks at work. Her mother was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in her 60s, and her brother was diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer's disease at age 52. She is concerned that she may have inherited the disease and is interested in participating in a study that can help her understand her risk. She has no history of psychiatric illness or other medical conditions that may interfere with the study requirements. She takes multivitamins daily and has no known allergies. She is willing to provide a blood sample for research purposes and is excited to potentially contribute to the development of treatments for Alzheimer's disease.

Patient is a 60yo man who presents with chest pain that has been occurring for the past week. The patient reports that the pain is substernal, squeezing in nature, and radiates to his left arm. The patient has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but no history of coronary artery disease. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. Physical examination is remarkable for an elevated blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg and a regular heart rhythm with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. ECG shows ST depression in leads V1-V3. The patient is referred to a primary care physician who orders the Corus CAD (Age/Sex/Gene Expression score - ASGES) blood test to evaluate the likelihood of obstructive coronary artery disease. The patient provides informed consent and is enrolled in the study. The physician receives the test results two days later, and based on the score, determines that no further cardiac testing or treatment is needed at this time. The patient is advised to continue his current medications and follow up with his primary care physician in 6 months for further evaluation of his symptoms.

A 25-year-old male who has been experiencing moderate common cold symptoms for the past day. He has no history of chronic nasal congestion or sinus issues. He does not have a deviated septum or nasal polyps. He has not taken any antibiotics or had sinusitis in the past month. He is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the study and able to follow the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 18-month-old boy who has been showing some developmental delays. His parents have noticed that he has difficulty with social interactions, such as making eye contact and responding to his name. He also seems to struggle with communication, as he has not yet developed any words or phrases. His parents have a family history of autism, as his older brother was diagnosed with the disorder at the age of 3. The family is seeking early intervention services to help their son develop important social communication skills. The parents are both working professionals and are willing to participate in the study's twice monthly play group sessions and two to three intervention sessions per week for 9 months, usually scheduled within workday hours. They are also willing to participate in monthly evaluations, videotaping of intervention sessions, and weekly or monthly video checks during the 18 months of treatment.

A 45-year-old Italian woman was diagnosed with breast cancer and started chemotherapy at the IRST Cancer Institute. She was prescribed several medications for her symptoms and comorbidities, and was worried about the potential drug interactions. She opted to participate in the Medication Reconciliation in Oncologic Patients trial and chose a community pharmacy close to her home to perform the pharmacological survey before every cycle of chemotherapy. She was able to communicate effectively in Italian and understood the trial requirements. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status was 1, indicating that she was able to carry out normal activities with little restriction. She provided written informed consent and was excited to contribute to the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male of Chinese ethnicity who has been recently diagnosed with gastric cancer. The diagnosis is confirmed through biopsy after presenting with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, and weight loss. He is scheduled to undergo preoperative enhanced abdomen CT and gastrectomy with type D2 lymphadenectomy. He has not received any preoperative therapy such as radiotherapy, chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy. He is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. He has no history of other cancers, major medical illnesses or surgeries. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is currently employed as an accountant and leads a mostly sedentary lifestyle. He has access to reliable transportation and is able to attend all scheduled clinic visits.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy with a genetic mutation. He is able to walk without assistance and can walk up 4 stairs in 8 seconds or less. He weighs 20 kg and is currently on corticosteroids for DMD. He has no history of mental or behavioral issues that would affect his ability to complete the required study procedures. He has not previously taken androgens or human growth hormone, and he does not use a ventilator during the day. He is able to have blood samples collected and receive an injection under the skin. He has not received exon skipping therapies in the past 6 months, and he is not currently taking ataluren or any investigational drug.

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Crohn's disease for the past 5 years. She has a history of moderate to severe abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. She has been treated with immunomodulators and TNF-α antagonists in the past, but has not achieved adequate response. She has had a colonoscopy with photographic documentation of more than 10 aphthous ulcerations (involving a minimum of 10 contiguous cm of intestine) consistent with CD. Her C-reactive protein (CRP) level is > 2.87 milligram per liter (mg/L). The patient is currently experiencing a flare-up of her symptoms and is seeking new treatment options. She is otherwise healthy with no other medical conditions. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion, despite taking his medications as prescribed. He underwent a cardiac catheterization and was found to have severe left main coronary artery disease with an ejection fraction of 25%. He is currently classified as NYHA class III. He has been referred for elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the possibility of requiring mechanical circulatory support during the procedure. He is willing to participate in the PIONEER trial. He does not have a history of bleeding disorders or stroke. He is not allergic to any of the medications listed in the exclusion criteria. He is not currently enrolled in any other studies.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing hearing loss and recurrent ear infections for the past 6 months. He reports that he had a traumatic injury to his ear when he was a child and has had intermittent ear issues ever since. The patient was diagnosed with a chronic tympanic membrane perforation (TMP) by an ear, nose, and throat (ENT) specialist. The perforation has been present for greater than 3 months and is not healing on its own. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or chronic medical conditions. He is not currently taking any medications and has no known allergies. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works as an accountant and enjoys spending time with his family. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially improve his hearing and alleviate his recurrent ear infections. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements, including follow-up visits.

A 55 year old female patient with a clinical diagnosis of cirrhosis of the liver has been admitted to the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. She has a history of alcohol abuse and has been experiencing recurrent hospital readmissions due to poor medication adherence and late detection of clinical deterioration. The patient is able to read and provide informed consent in English and has a cell phone with texting capability. She is willing to receive daily texts and weekly phone calls as part of the telehealth intervention. The patient has a surrogate who is also willing to receive and send text messages on her behalf. The patient has not received a liver transplant and is not discharged to hospice. She is not actively using illicit substances or alcohol. The patient is followed at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania and is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old male who has a history of seasonal allergic rhinitis for the past two years. He experiences exacerbations during the spring season due to exposure to tree pollens. He has a positive skin prick test for tree pollen. He reports symptoms of sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, and itchy eyes. His 12-hour reflective Total Nasal Symptom Score (rTNSS) is ≥6 out of a possible 12 for the morning assessment at screening. He does not have any significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication for his allergies. His parents have provided written informed consent for him to participate in the clinical trial.

This is a 42 year-old female who was diagnosed with T-Cell Lymphoma six months ago. She received first line chemotherapy but has since experienced a relapse of the disease. She has no other significant medical history and her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has no prior exposure to chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the last 2 weeks and has adequate organ and marrow function. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and understands and is willing to sign the informed consent document.

A 62-year-old woman was diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia 6 months ago. Her family members noticed a change in her behavior, including a lack of inhibitions, impulsivity, and inappropriate social behavior. She has been experiencing difficulty with executive function and decision-making, and her family has been concerned about her safety. She has no history of major psychiatric disorders, substance abuse or drug use. She is currently taking donepezil for her dementia but has not seen much improvement in her behavior. Her neurological examination is significant for mild cognitive impairment with deficits in executive function, and her Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 18 out of 30. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if AVP-786 may help with her disinhibited behavior.

68 year old man with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease, who recently underwent a coronary angioplasty with stent placement. He is now under quarantine due to the COVID-19 pandemic and is unable to visit his cardiologist for follow-up visits. He is experiencing occasional chest pains and is concerned about his medication regimen. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will provide remote management of his cardiovascular health issues using an electronic platform. His medical data including imaging and analysis will be uploaded to his personal account on the platform. He will have access to multidisciplinary teams including Cardiology specialists, interventional cardiology, cardiovascular surgery, oncology, infectious diseases, diabetologists, family doctors, psychologists / psychiatrists, priests and religious advisors. The patient will be able to connect with the case coordinator who will provide ongoing assistance and connect him to the specialist teams that establish stage diagnosis and management / therapy behavior. The patient will be monitored in isolation through vital parameters transmitted through wireless devices. The objective of the trial is to establish an integrated distance management strategy for patients with cardiovascular diseases in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. The purpose of this trial is to mitigate the psychological impact of using the distance diagnosis and treatment and implementing the procedures.

60 year old female with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and history of cataract surgery in the right eye presenting with decreased visual acuity and mild eye pain. The patient reports no history of ocular trauma, but states that her eye has been feeling "irritated" for the past few days. She denies any other ocular or systemic symptoms. Visual acuity in the affected eye is 20/40, and there is moderate conjunctival injection and mild corneal edema. The anterior chamber is deep and quiet, and there is no evidence of hyphema or hypopyon. Fundoscopic examination reveals mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy and no evidence of macular edema. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) shows mild thickening of the macula consistent with cystoid macular edema. The patient is a candidate for cataract surgery in the left eye but has not yet undergone the procedure. Past Medical History: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia, Osteoarthritis.

55-year-old female with a history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and occasional rectal bleeding was referred for colonoscopy after positive fecal occult blood test (FOBT) results. The patient reports no history of colon polyps or cancer in her family history. She has been on a high fiber diet for the past week and has followed the bowel preparation instructions provided by the hospital. The colonoscopy is scheduled for next week. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

A 58-year-old man presents with a recent diagnosis of smoldering multiple myeloma based on bone marrow biopsy and blood tests. He has no symptoms related to the disease and feels generally healthy. However, his bone marrow plasma cells are between 10% and 60%, and he has a serum M-protein level of 3.5 g/dL. He has no history of other malignancies and has not received any prior anti-myeloma therapy. His renal and hepatic function are normal, and he has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has not received any live, attenuated vaccines within the past 4 weeks, and has no history of bleeding disorders or recent major surgery. He is currently not on any systemic immunosuppressant therapy or corticosteroids, and has not been vaccinated with live, attenuated vaccines within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test whether the drug ibrutinib can prevent the development of multiple myeloma. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has signed an informed consent form.

A 42-year-old Japanese man visited the clinic with complaints of persistent upper abdominal pain, bloating, and discomfort for more than 6 months. The patient had no prior history of gastrointestinal disorders and had not undergone any abdominal surgeries. He had not experienced any significant weight loss or change in bowel habits. The pain was not relieved by defecation, and he did not have any vomiting or nausea. The patient's medical history was unremarkable, and he was not taking any medications. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He was diagnosed with Functional Dyspepsia according to Rome III criteria. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of rabeprazole compared to placebo.

Patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis and severe hip pain. He is scheduled to undergo primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) with either epidural or lumbar plexus peripheral nerve block with the administration of multimodal medication. The patient has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is able to communicate effectively and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has not had any previous THA revisions, has not required ICU admission postoperatively, and does not have dementia.

Patient A is a 55-year-old female who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for over 5 years. She has been experiencing microangiopathy, as evidenced by albuminuria. She is currently taking metformin and amlodipine for her diabetes and hypertension, respectively. She has no history of myocardial infarction or unstable angina within the last 3 months and has no signs of decompensated congestive heart failure. She has not made any changes to the dosage of her medication in the preceding 6 weeks. Her liver function tests are within normal limits. She is not taking glibenclamide, cyclosporin, or warfarin. She understands the study protocol and is willing to participate in the study after receiving oral and written information.

The patient is a 32-year-old white male who has been diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. He has been treated with immunomodulatory therapy for the past 6 months. He is currently experiencing a relapse characterized by difficulty walking, fatigue, and numbness in his legs. He has not been diagnosed with any other medical condition and he is not taking any other medication. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He drinks alcohol socially but doesn't consider himself a heavy drinker. He is married and has two children. He works full-time as an accountant. His EDSS score is 3.5, indicating moderate disability. He has not undergone any MRI scans in the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of MS and improve treatment options for future patients.

The patient is a 28-year-old female with a history of mild asthma and allergies to house dust mites. She has been experiencing occasional shortness of breath and wheezing, especially during the night and in the morning. She has no other medical conditions and is currently not taking any asthma medications. She is generally healthy with no clinically relevant abnormalities on medical history, physical exam, vital signs, laboratory parameters, or ECG. She has a BMI of 22.5 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She has a documented airway late response to inhaled HDM on Screening Day 3. Her FEV1 is 85% of predicted on Screening Day 2, and her baseline blood eosinophils are 200 cells/μL at Screening. She is a non-smoker and has not used alcohol or recreational drugs in the last 6 months. She is willing and able to perform the lung function tests and other study-related procedures and comply with study protocol requirements. She has provided a signed and dated informed consent. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was previously diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. He has received at least one line of anti-cancer therapy for his advanced disease but has documented disease progression. He is not amenable to surgical resection or locoregional radiation therapy with curative intent. He is willing to undergo baseline and post-baseline biopsy of the lesion which is to be injected. The patient has an ECOG PS of 1 and adequate hematologic, renal, hepatic, and coagulation function. He has no history of active autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppressive medication or recent thromboembolic complications. The patient is currently not using any investigational anticancer agent, immune modulating drugs, or immunologically active topical therapies. He has no history of central nervous system metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis. The patient has no known hematologic malignancy or malignant primary solid tumor that have occurred or recurred within the previous 5 years. The patient is seronegative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) surface antigen, and hepatitis C virus (HCV).

56 year old man with a history of glaucoma and visual field defects consistent with glaucoma. He has been on topical medications to control intraocular pressure for the past 2 years. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. His visual acuity is 20/30 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. He has not undergone any ocular surgeries in the past.

A 30-year-old female who recently gave birth to her first child was referred to the study by her obstetrician. She had an epidural during labor due to prolonged labor and was experiencing post-dural puncture headache. She was willing to participate in the study and gave informed consent. Her medical history was unremarkable and she was not taking any medications or supplements. She was in good health and able to comply with all study requirements. She was within the first 2 days postnatal and had not experienced any hemorrhage greater than 1L. She was not on prophylactic dalteparin and did not have any clotting abnormalities. She was proficient in English and able to read and speak it.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a 5-year history of osteoarthritis of the knee. He reports significant pain and stiffness in the affected joint, which limits his ability to perform daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He takes occasional over-the-counter pain relievers but has not tried any complementary or alternative therapies for his osteoarthritis. He has no known allergies to shellfish, glucosamine, or chondroitin. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl Blood glucose: 100 mg/dl

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been struggling with alcoholism for several years. He has had two previous treatments for alcoholism which did not work for him. He has a history of alcohol abuse and is currently drinking heavily. He is literate and willing to participate in a clinical trial to treat his addiction. He has no psychiatric diagnoses other than alcohol abuse, and he doesn't use any illicit drugs. He is married with two children and works as a construction worker. He has no family or personal history of bipolar disorder or psychotic disorders. He doesn't have any clinical diseases, cardiovascular or hepatic diseases, and his hemogram and electrocardiogram are normal. He is not pregnant or lactating. He understands the trial and has signed the Free and Informed Consent Form.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes 3 years ago. He has been on insulin glargine for the past 2 years and has been exercising regularly for the past year. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his time sitting in front of a computer. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. His blood pressure is within normal range (120/80 mmHg) and his last HbA1c reading was 8.5%. He has a body mass index of 23.5 kg/m^2 and has no history of any major health issues. He is willing to participate in the trial and is committed to following the study protocol.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing abnormal vaginal bleeding for the past week. She presents to the clinic and is diagnosed with incomplete abortion. The doctor recommends endouterine manual aspiration to remove the remaining tissue. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to manage pain during the procedure. She has no known allergies to lidocain. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has no other medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications and has not had any recent surgeries. She is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

This is a 10-year-old boy who fell off his bike and sustained a severe displacement of his radial neck combined with an olecranon fracture in his right elbow. X-rays showed a Judet type III radial neck fracture and a displaced olecranon fracture. His elbow was swollen, and he was unable to move his arm without severe pain. He was brought to the hospital immediately, and the orthopedic surgeon recommended surgery. The surgery was performed using absorbable rods and K-wires via a Boyd incision. The procedure was successful, and he was discharged from the hospital after a few days. He will be followed up regularly to assess the healing process of his fractures.

The patient is a 38-year-old female who has been experiencing joint pain and swelling for the past 6 months. She has also been feeling fatigued and has noticed that her energy levels have decreased. She has never been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis before and has not received any treatment for it. Her blood pressure and glucose levels are within normal limits. She has not had any major surgeries in the past 8 weeks. She has no history of any other autoimmune diseases or inflammatory joint diseases. She is not currently taking any medication for any other medical conditions. She is a non-smoker and has not used any tobacco products in the past 6 months. She is not pregnant or nursing. She does not have any significant medical history, and her laboratory values are within normal limits. She is willing to give written informed consent and comply with the requirements of the study protocol. She has a BMI of less than 42.

Full term newborn, 2 days old, with no significant medical history or congenital abnormalities. The baby was born via normal vaginal delivery to a 28-year-old mother with an uneventful pregnancy. The baby has been feeding well and has had normal bowel movements since birth. No signs of respiratory distress or cyanosis have been observed. The baby meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has been referred for enrollment.

35-year-old male diagnosed with Major Depression. He has a history of depression and has been on various antidepressant medications with limited success. He is currently experiencing symptoms of sadness, guilt, and worthlessness, with significant loss of interest and pleasure in activities he previously enjoyed. He reports difficulty sleeping and feels tired throughout the day. He has no significant medical history, and his vital signs are within normal limits. His current medications include escitalopram 20mg daily and clonazepam 0.5mg as needed for anxiety. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effect of cortisol administration on neural correlates of emotion in depression. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including weight restrictions for MRI scanning.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been suffering from wrist pain for several years. The pain has gradually increased in intensity and has become more frequent. He has difficulty performing daily activities that require wrist motion, such as opening jars, turning keys, and typing on a computer. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the wrist and has a Wrightington X-ray grade of 3. He has tried conservative treatments, such as medication and physical therapy, but they have not provided long-lasting relief. His doctor has recommended total wrist arthroplasty (TWA) surgery with a newly developed TWA implant. The patient is interested in participating in this pilot study to evaluate the efficacy of the new implant and to assess his outcomes pre and postoperatively. He is motivated to improve his wrist function and reduce his pain, as it is impacting his ability to work and perform daily activities. He does not have any history of infection, substance abuse, or mental illness.

A 34-year-old man with a history of schizophrenia for over 5 years was referred to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial. He has been on multiple antipsychotic medications including risperidone, haloperidol, and aripiprazole but has not responded well to any of them. He experiences hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking on a daily basis. His CGI-S score is 5 and his PANSS score is 90. He is currently an outpatient and is willing to participate in the study. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies to any drugs. He has no history of seizures or organic mental disease. He is fluent in English and can read and write.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been experiencing muscle weakness and fatigue for the past few months. He has also complained of difficulty breathing during physical activity. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. His parents report that there is a strong family history of mitochondrial disease, with his maternal grandmother and several maternal aunts and uncles having been diagnosed with the condition. The boy is scheduled to undergo a muscle biopsy as part of his diagnostic workup for possible mitochondrial disease. He has no known allergies or adverse reactions to anesthesia. His physical examination is significant for decreased muscle tone and strength in his lower extremities. His vital signs are within normal limits. The boy is cooperative and able to tolerate a slow induction for emotional reasons. His initial BIS measurement is 98. He has no documented pulmonary disease.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been experiencing worsening knee pain for the past 2 years. He reports difficulty walking, climbing stairs, and getting up from a seated position. He has tried various non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy, medications, and injections, but his symptoms have not improved. He has a BMI of 32 and does not have any history of avascular necrosis or inflammatory arthritis. He does not have any active or suspected latent infections in or around the affected knee joint. He has signed an IRB/EC approved study-specific Informed Patient Consent Form and is willing and able to comply with postoperative scheduled clinical and radiographic evaluations and rehabilitation. He is diagnosed with Non-Inflammatory Degenerative Joint Disease (NIDJD) and is a candidate for primary cemented total knee replacement using the Triathlon Total Knee System with the Triathlon PSR Tibial Insert. He is not participating in the study for a contralateral total knee replacement and does not have any mental or neuromuscular disorders that would create an unacceptable risk of prosthesis instability, fixation failure, or complications in postoperative care. His bone stock is adequate to provide support to the prosthesis and he is not immunologically suppressed or receiving steroids in excess of normal physiological requirements. He does not have lumbar radicular pain or severe instability of the knee joint secondary to the absence of collateral ligament integrity and function. He is not a prisoner and does not have a known sensitivity to device materials.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with HIV infection 4 years ago. He has been on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for the last 2 years and has been experiencing hyperlipidemia as a side effect of the treatment. Despite adopting lifestyle changes such as dietary modifications and regular exercise, his lipid profile remains elevated. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or other comorbidities. His current HAART regimen includes tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz. He has given written informed consent to participate in this study to evaluate the management of HAART-related hyperlipidemia.

28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child and has been scheduled for a Cesarean Delivery due to breech presentation of the baby. She has a history of asthma that is well-controlled with daily medication. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. The patient is excited to learn more about the ERAS protocol and is willing to actively participate in the process to improve her recovery after surgery. She is able to arrive at the hospital on the day of surgery and is looking forward to early mobilization and early oral intake after the procedure.

This is a 42-year-old female with a past medical history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that was initially treated with CD19 CAR-T therapy. However, she experienced relapse and is now seeking alternative treatment options. She has a measurable lesion of 2 cm in diameter and meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial. She has completed all prior treatment regimens and has not received any immunosuppressive therapy or mAb treatments within the last week. She has a normal left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and no active pulmonary infections. She is expected to survive for at least 3 months and has an ECOG score of 0. She has agreed to participate in the study and has signed informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective contraception during the trial. She is not infected with HIV, HBV, HCV, or TPPA/RPR. She has no history of allergy to cellular products or hereditary syndromes such as Fanconi anemia, Kostmann syndrome, or Shwachman syndrome. She has not undergone apheresis in the past and meets the requirements for manufacturing CAR-T cell.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection. She has a history of occasional alcohol consumption but denies any current alcohol use. She is not currently participating in any other studies and has no known systemic illnesses. Her viral load is elevated, and her liver enzymes are mildly elevated. She has not received any previous treatment for her hepatitis C. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow the appropriate supplementation protocol. She has no laboratory abnormalities that would exclude her from the study. Overall, she is in good health and motivated to participate in the study to potentially improve her antioxidant status and overall health.

A 36-year-old male patient is admitted to the depression ward with a diagnosis of major depressive disorder, ICD-10: F33. He has a history of recurrent depressive episodes and has been unable to work for the last 4 months due to his symptoms. His HDRS-17 score is 22, indicating moderate to severe depression. He has no current suicidal ideation, but has had passive thoughts in the past. The patient has no physical condition that would prohibit endurance exercise and has no more than two cardiovascular risk factors. He has a BMI of 26 kg/m2, is a non-smoker and has no history of substance abuse. He has not engaged in regular high-intensity exercise prior to treatment. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been diagnosed with mild asthma for the past 5 years. She experiences occasional coughing and wheezing, especially during the spring and fall seasons. She reports that her asthma symptoms have not been well-controlled and she is interested in learning more about how to manage her asthma better. She has no other significant medical history, and is able to walk several blocks without difficulty. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in this study to learn more about cultural, social, and psychological factors that can impact her asthma management.

A 28-year-old Hispanic woman, gravida 3, para 2, presents to the hospital for an elective cesarean section due to fetal macrosomia. She has a past medical history of gestational diabetes during her second pregnancy. Her prenatal course has been uncomplicated, and her blood pressure has been within normal limits throughout her pregnancy. Her estimated gestational age is 39 weeks, and the estimated fetal weight is 4.5 kg. She has no known drug allergies. During her previous delivery, she experienced postpartum hemorrhage, and her blood loss required an additional dose of oxytocin. She is eager to participate in the study and understands the potential benefits and risks.

A 55-year-old male patient was admitted to the emergency department complaining of chest pain and shortness of breath. The patient was diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction and was treated with thrombolytic therapy. However, the patient developed cardiogenic shock and was referred for emergency Coronary Artery Bypass Graft surgery at Saud Al Babtain Cardiac Center. The patient has no history of any underlying disease except hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no allergies to any food or medication. He is a non-smoker and has never consumed alcohol. He works as a sales representative and is physically active, engaging in regular exercise for 30 minutes a day.

There is no specific patient description that can be generated for this clinical trial as patients will be recruited externally based on their diagnosis of chronic pancreatitis. However, potential participants should note that this study is focused on the epidemiology and translational aspects of chronic pancreatitis, and they will not be enrolled at MD Anderson Cancer Center. Instead, recruitment will occur at external sites that are part of the NIH-funded Consortium for the Study of Chronic Pancreatitis, Diabetes, and Pancreatic Cancer (CPDPC).

The patient is a 55 year old man who has been diagnosed with multiple myeloma by his oncologist. He has received one line of therapy in the past and his disease has relapsed since then. He is currently experiencing symptoms of fatigue, bone pain and weight loss. His ECOG performance status is 1. He is not on any other medication for his condition. His baseline laboratory values show ANC of 2.5 x 109/L, platelets of 120 x 109/L, calculated CrCl of 60 mL/min (MDRD formula), AST and ALT of 1.5 x ULN, serum bilirubin of 1.0 x ULN, and normal levels of serum potassium, magnesium, and phosphorous. His total calcium (corrected for serum albumin) is within the lower normal limits for institution. His baseline MUGA or ECHO shows LVEF ≥ the lower limit of the institutional normal. He is willing to undergo a mandatory bone marrow aspirate sampling at baseline and another later in the study if he experiences a CR or PR. He is capable of swallowing capsules and is able to sign informed consent and to comply with the protocol. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use a double method of contraception during the study and for 3 months after treatment. He has not undergone major surgery ≤ 4 weeks prior to starting study drug or not recovered from side effects of such therapy. He has not shown intolerance to BTZ or to Dex or components of these drugs or has any contraindication to one or the other drug. He meets all other inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with neovascular age-related macular degeneration in her right eye. She has not received any prior treatment for her condition. Her best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) score in the affected eye is 55 letters on the ETDRS chart, indicating moderate visual impairment. She has no other clinically significant ocular disorders that may interfere with the study. The patient is generally healthy, with no known social, psychological, or medical conditions that would preclude her enrollment in the study.

This is a 42-year-old woman who is the primary caregiver for her husband who was diagnosed with MS three years ago. She has been experiencing mild to moderate distress in her caregiver role and is interested in participating in a study that could help her manage her stress levels. She speaks English fluently and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have a diagnosis of MS herself or any psychiatric diagnosis. She is committed to the intervention and interested in learning more about Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) as a form of self-help for carers of people with MS.

A 40-year-old female of Asian ethnicity visited the clinic for the study of immune function. She has no history of diabetes or obesity and her white blood cell count is within the normal range. She is interested in participating in the study and consumes dairy products regularly. Her current weight has been stable for the past 3 months. She reports no history of metabolic diseases or chronic infections, and is not currently taking any medications or supplements. She has no known liver or kidney disease, and her gastrointestinal health is normal. She is able to understand and provide informed consent for the study.

Patient is a 25-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis for the past 8 months. She has tried various topical treatments and oral medications with little to no improvement in her symptoms. She has not received any immunosuppressive, chemotherapy or systemic therapy in the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant and is using effective contraception. The patient has not received phototherapy or photochemotherapy in the past 2 to 4 weeks. She has not received TNF-α inhibitors or alefacept in the past 12 weeks. The patient has not received ustekinumab in the past 12 weeks and has not participated in another clinical trial in the past 4 weeks. The patient does not have a history of intolerance to any of the investigational study product's ingredients. She does not have any skin conditions that could interfere with the study's evaluation of her psoriasis. The patient does not have any active infections or a history of untreated Lyme disease. She has not had a BCG vaccination within the last 12 months and does not have any immunodeficiency conditions. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and wash-out requirements.

A 45-year-old female who underwent low anterior resection with mesorectal excision surgery for rectal cancer two years ago presents with severe bowel dysfunction including fecal incontinence, soiling, urgency, incomplete evacuation, fragmented defecation, and impaired rectal sensation. The patient has been experiencing a "toilet dependence" which has greatly affected her quality of life. The patient is interested in alternative therapies and is willing to try acupuncture as a potential treatment for her symptoms. The patient has no known allergies to stainless steel and does not have an implanted pacemaker. She has no current skin infections and is not needle-phobic. The patient has no history of metastatic disease to the central nervous system and is not currently on any medications such as smecta, dicetel, cisapride or traditional Chinese medicine. The patient is willing to provide signed written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 62-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital for a routine cardiac procedure. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. He reports occasional chest discomfort but denies any shortness of breath or palpitations. He has never worn a Holter monitor before. He is a former smoker with a 30-pack-year history but quit smoking 5 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally but denies illicit drug use. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father passing away from a heart attack at the age of 55. The patient is cooperative and able to follow instructions. He is able to wear the holter monitor for the duration of the study period.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of missing teeth in the posterior region of the mandible. He has been diagnosed with hypovitaminosis D with a serum level of 12 ng/ml. He is in good general health with no medical or intraoral contraindications. He is a non-smoker and does not use corticoids. The patient is interested in getting dental mini-implants to improve his oral function and quality of life. He meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial studying the effect of vitamin D replacement on bone healing in mini-dental implants and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and sensitivity in her front teeth for the past few months. She has noticed a discoloration in one of her teeth and is concerned about the appearance of her smile. She has no other medical conditions and is in good health. Her dental examination reveals internal inflammatory root resorption in one of her front teeth, which is causing the pain and discoloration. The tooth has no mobility and the pocket depth is less than 3mm. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive treatment for her condition. She is compliant with follow-up appointments and willing to undergo the necessary procedures to receive injectable PRF revascularization treatment.

A 42 year old female came to the hospital after undergoing bilateral thyroidectomy due to papillary thyroid carcinoma. She was experiencing symptoms of hypocalcemia, including numbness and tingling in her fingers and toes, muscle cramps, and fatigue. Her calcium levels were found to be less than 8 mg/dL despite receiving calcitriol and calcium supplementation for 24 hours. Her PTH levels were also below the low end of normal range. She was eligible for the clinical trial on teriparatide for postsurgical hypoparathyroidism and was enrolled in the study. She had no history of renal failure or parathyroid pathology, and had no pre-existing hypercalcemia or metabolic bone diseases other than osteoporosis. She was not pregnant and had no history of urolithiasis or digitalis therapy. She had not previously received Forteo therapy for osteoporosis, and had no history of skeletal malignancies or increased baseline risk for osteosarcoma.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a history of prescription opioid abuse. She has been in Suboxone therapy for the past year and is currently on a stable dose of 12mg/day. She has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past six months and has been finding it difficult to manage her pain without the use of opioids. She has been prescribed other pain medications in the past but has found them to be ineffective. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will test the efficacy of pregabalin in reducing opioid-induced hyperalgesia (OIH) and chronic pain. She is in good physical health and does not have any acute medical conditions that would make participation hazardous. She is also willing to sign an informed consent and understands the study protocol.

A 28-year-old woman has been in a committed relationship with her partner for the past 5 years. They are not married but have been living together for the past 2 years. She is currently seeking ways to strengthen their relationship and improve their communication skills. She heard about the Guam Healthy Relationships Education Program and is interested in participating. She is a native of Guam and values her cultural traditions and beliefs. She is open to learning new skills and strategies to enhance her relationship with her partner.

The patient is a 14-month-old male infant who has been experiencing a cough for the past 4 days. He was born full-term and has no significant medical history. His vital signs are within the normal range, with an axillary temperature of 37°C, heart rate of 120 beats/min, respiratory rate of 30 breaths/min, and blood pressure of 90/50 mmHg. He presents with a mild cough, which is more pronounced at night, and is causing disturbance to his sleep and that of his parents. He has no other symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection, such as fever or runny nose. The infant is not taking any medication to treat his cough. The parents are willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of agave syrup, placebo, and no treatment on nocturnal cough and sleep quality for coughing infants/toddlers and their parents. They have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with Tourette Syndrome (TS) for over 10 years. Despite trying various medications and behavioral therapies, her tics have continued to cause incapacitation, severe distress, and a disruption in her quality of life. She experiences motor tics with a subscore of 15 or more on the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (YGTSS). She has been deemed medication refractory, having tried multiple medications at therapeutic doses without improvement. She has also been offered habit reversal therapy/cognitive behavioral intervention therapy (HRT) but did not see significant improvement. She is willing to keep her TS medication stable and unchanged throughout the trial. She has not undergone any previous neurological interventions, has no metal in her head, and does not have any untreated or unstable psychiatric disorders. She has no severe medical co-morbidities that would impact the tolerability of surgery, and her MRI scan shows no abnormalities that would confound the outcome or safety of the surgery. She is not pregnant and has no history of substance abuse or dependence. She is willing to undergo a trial of botulinum toxin treatment if deemed necessary.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids and is scheduled for a myomectomy surgery. She has a past medical history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke and does not have any known allergies. She has no history of bleeding disorders or anemia. Her physical examination is within normal limits. Her oxygen saturation level is 98% on room air. She has no tremors or any anomalies of the fingers. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, chronic cough, fatigue, and chest discomfort for the past year. He has tried different treatments, but none of them have provided significant improvement. He is a non-smoker and has no history of respiratory infections. His pulmonary function tests show a restrictive pattern with a FVC of 62% and a DLco of 44% predicted. The patient is able to perform a 6-minute walk test but gets easily fatigued. He has no significant comorbidities and has not been hospitalized due to an acute exacerbation of IPF. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He has signed informed consent and is in good general health. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive or antifibrotic agents and has no history of malignancy. The patient's medical history and current condition meet the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 47-year-old male who has undergone allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) due to acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He developed acute graft versus host disease (GVHD) with skin rash involvement of more than 50% of his body surface area and diarrhea with a minimum stool volume of 500 mL/day 3 days ago. He was started on systemic glucocorticoids within 72 hours of the onset of GVHD symptoms. He has no history of heart disease or long QT syndrome. He is not taking any medications that may prolong QT interval or induce torsade de pointes. He has not been diagnosed with HIV before his transplant. His baseline multiple gated acquisition scan (MUGA) or echocardiogram (ECHO) demonstrated left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) within the institutional normal before transplantation. His calculated creatinine clearance (CrCl) is greater than 30 mL/min (MDRD Formula), serum potassium, calcium, magnesium, and phosphorus levels are within the normal limits on the day of LBH589 administration. He has signed the informed consent and is willing to comply with the instructions given to him by the study staff.

Patient is a 28-year-old male from the United States who is currently working as a computer programmer. He has no history of liver disease, alcohol abuse, hypertension, or vascular disease. His blood pressure is 126/78 mm Hg, and his weight is 160 lbs. He has no known metal objects in his body, and he is not pregnant. He has no hearing impairment, and he has no relative or specific contraindications for MRI exam. He is physically able to tolerate lying within the bore of the magnet for 1-2 hours and is not claustrophobic. He has no known history of allergies and is not currently taking any medications.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who works as a software engineer. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medication regularly. He enjoys playing basketball and running in his free time. He has no history of drug addiction and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is fluent in English and able to understand and follow instructions. He has no current pain or itch causing diseases or psychiatric disorders. He has no known allergies or discomfort to morphine. He is not participating in any other study where an investigational drug is used. He is willing to cooperate with the study requirements.

As this is an expanded access program, there are no specific eligibility or exclusion criteria provided. However, it is likely that patients who have exhausted all other available treatment options for their cancer and have no viable treatment options left may be considered for this program. Patients may have been previously enrolled in clinical trials for AG-221 or may have had limited exposure to the drug in a compassionate use setting. Patients may have a variety of cancer types, but AG-221 is primarily being developed for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and advanced solid tumors with an isocitrate dehydrogenase-2 (IDH2) mutation. The patient may have experienced disease progression or relapse despite receiving prior treatments such as chemotherapy, radiation therapy, surgery, or other targeted therapies. The patient may also have other comorbidities or medical conditions that will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis by the treating physician and sponsor of the program.

A 3-year-old girl was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at the age of 2. Her parents noticed that she was not hitting her developmental milestones on time. She has difficulty with sitting, standing, and walking independently. Her parents report that she is a happy child who loves to play with her toys and her older brother. She has no other medical conditions. She is currently receiving physiotherapy and occupational therapy twice a week. She is on no medication. Her parents are interested in participating in this study to better understand how their daughter is progressing in her physical development and participation. They hope that the information collected from this study will help them monitor if their daughter is developing as expected in her physical development and participation, and assist them in making decisions about what services their daughter requires to meet their family's goals. They speak English fluently.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pain and stiffness in her right knee for the past year. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been taking over-the-counter pain medication to manage her symptoms. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to possibly find a more effective treatment for her condition. She has no other medical conditions or medications that would affect the bone or cartilage, and is willing and able to adhere to the protocol for the full 14-day study.

A 35-year-old male presents with progressive weakness and atrophy in his facial and shoulder girdle muscles, as well as anterior forearm and foreleg muscles. He has been diagnosed with facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy confirmed by molecular biology. His Vignos scale score is less than or equal to 5, indicating that he is still able to walk. He has health insurance and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that tests the feasibility, clinical and biological tolerance, and efficacy of daily electrostimulation training of shoulder girdle and quadriceps muscles. The patient has not previously undergone electrostimulation training, and his CK levels are normal. He is not pregnant, does not have any joint diseases, and is not currently participating in any other biomedical research. He has signed informed consent and is willing to be followed for at least 6 months.

55 year-old man who has been dealing with pain in his knees and lower back for the past year. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has been taking glucosamine and chondroitin supplements without much relief. He is interested in trying a natural alternative to traditional pain medications and is willing to stop taking his current supplements for the duration of the study. He has no known allergies to eggs or egg products and is not currently taking any remission-inducing or immunosuppressive medications. He weighs less than 250 pounds and is not currently enrolled in any other research studies involving investigational products.

The patient is a 50 year old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath, dry cough and fatigue for the past year. He has a history of smoking for 20 years but quit 5 years ago. He has been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) by a multidisciplinary team and has had a chest HRCT within the past 6 months. His forced vital capacity (FVC) is 65% predicted of normal and his diffusing capacity for the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) is 40% predicted of normal corrected for hemoglobin. He has a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/FVC (Tiffeneau-Pinelli index) ratio of 0.75 based on pre-bronchodilator spirometry. He is on stable supportive care and his condition is stable. He has no known hypersensitivity to any of the study drug ingredients and is not currently on any immunosuppressive therapy. He has no history of malignancy within the past 5 years and has no clinically significant abnormalities on ECG. He has not had an acute IPF exacerbation within 6 weeks prior to screening and has not had a lower respiratory tract infection requiring antibiotics within the past 4 weeks. He has no history of interstitial lung disease or lung volume reduction surgery/lung transplant. He has no unstable cardiac or pulmonary disease other than IPF within 6 months prior to screening. His liver and renal function are normal. He has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

25 year old healthy female with no history of metabolic disorders such as diabetes, hypothyroidism, corticoid therapy, heart or lung disease. She has a history of occasional soda consumption and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the metabolic response to sweetened vs. non-sweetened soft drinks.
