The patient is willing to commit to consuming the assigned soft drinks for a period of 4 weeks and is willing to undergo oral glucose tolerance tests for metabolic assessment.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. She was scheduled to undergo cardiac surgery to treat her condition, but due to the COVID-19 pandemic, her operation has been postponed. She is feeling anxious and depressed about the delay and is concerned about the impact it may have on her health. She has no history of anxiety or depression and has not received any psychological treatment in the past. She is currently taking medication for high blood pressure and has a history of diabetes. She is interested in participating in a study that examines the psychological well-being of patients awaiting cardiac surgery during the COVID-19 pandemic to help future patients going through a similar situation.

This is a 45 year-old female with a Grade II neuroendocrine tumor (NET) located in the small intestine. She has been receiving treatment at the department of Medical Oncology at the University Medical Centre Groningen (UMCG) and is currently under surveillance. She lives in a remote area and has to travel long distances to attend her follow-up outpatient clinic visits, which can be time-consuming and tiring. She has access to the required technology for performing videoconsultation and is interested in participating in the study to receive follow-up care through videoconsultation instead of conventional visits at the outpatient clinic. She has no hearing or visual impairment that would make videoconsultation difficult. She has signed informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing frequent episodes of heartburn and regurgitation of food or stomach contents. She reports experiencing these symptoms for several months and has tried over-the-counter antacids with no relief. She has not been diagnosed with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) but has been referred for pH monitoring procedure to detect acid reflux. She is not currently pregnant or nursing and practices medically acceptable methods of contraception. She has not undergone any abdominal surgeries other than uncomplicated procedures that would be unlikely to cause bowel obstruction. She has no known bleeding diathesis, strictures, severe esophagitis, varices and or obstructions. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the performance of the Bravo® pH Monitoring System and provide feedback on the procedure. She understands the nature of the study and agrees to provide written informed consent.

A 55-year-old man with a history of heart failure is experiencing difficulty with daily activities despite optimal medical therapy. He has been on ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers for over 6 months, and he has an implanted cardio-defibrillator. His left ventricular ejection fraction is 30%, and he has been on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy (CRT) for over 3 months. He is able to walk between 100-350 meters in six minutes. He does not have a history of aortic dissection or Marfan's disease. His systolic blood pressure is between 90-140 mmHg, and his Serum Sodium is above 130 mEq/L. He has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 28 kg/m2. He has no active infection and has not had a myocardial infarction, stroke, or TIA in the past 90 days. He is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trial. He understands the nature of the procedure, is willing to comply with follow-up evaluations, and can provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past 5 years. She has been prescribed opioid analgesics for pain relief, which she has been taking regularly for the past 3 years. She reports that the medication has been effective in reducing her pain, but she has also developed a tolerance to the medication and is concerned about the risk of opioid dependence and misuse. She is motivated to decrease her opioid use and is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She has no history of substance abuse or mental health disorders. She lives with her husband and two children, and works part-time as a receptionist. She is able to attend regular appointments at the CETD in Montpellier.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who has been using cocaine regularly for the past 2 years. He has a history of trying to quit on his own but has been unsuccessful in doing so. The patient reports using cocaine at least 3-4 times per week and is seeking treatment for his addiction. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The patient is able to understand and provide written informed consent. He does not have any plans to father a child in the near future and confirms he is using an effective method of birth control. The patient is motivated to quit cocaine and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help him achieve this goal.

The patient is a 56-year-old postmenopausal woman with metastatic breast cancer. She was initially diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 3 years ago and underwent breast-conserving surgery, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. One year ago, she was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer to the lung and liver and received an aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole) for 9 months with disease progression. She also received palliative radiation therapy to the lung lesion. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is a nonsmoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. Her baseline laboratory studies include WBC of 4,500/mm³, hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL, absolute neutrophil count of 1,800/mm³, and platelet count of 120,000/mm³. Her liver function tests and creatinine are within normal limits. She has no history of thrombotic events or bleeding disorders. She has no active infections and no other significant medical conditions. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trial and has not received any investigational agents in the past.

A 28-year-old male athlete who is an avid basketball player had a knee injury during a game. He was diagnosed with a patellar dislocation and underwent several months of rehabilitation with physiotherapy. However, he continued to experience instability and pain in his knee. Subsequently, he was referred to an orthopedic surgeon who recommended a tibial tubercle osteotomy (TTO) to realign the patella. He is otherwise healthy with no history of bleeding or clotting disorders. He is not currently taking any anticoagulation medication. He has no known renal disorders or sickle cell disease. He is willing and able to provide consent for the study.

A 25 year old healthy male with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has no history of drug abuse, nicotine use, or alcohol abuse. He does not have a tendency towards fainting. He has no underlying medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is interested in contributing to medical research and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

54-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of ovarian cancer, stage III, confirmed by biopsy. CT scan shows radiographically measurable disease in the pelvis and abdomen. The patient is scheduled to undergo standard chemotherapy treatment per the treating physician's recommendation. The patient has no history of other malignancies within the past 5 years, no active infections, and is not of childbearing potential. The expected survival rate is greater than 3 months, and the patient is willing and able to complete the study.

A 32 year old male patient with a history of atopic dermatitis presented to the clinic with symptoms of skin inflammation and itching on his arms and legs. He was diagnosed with birch pollen allergy and the exacerbation of atopic dermatitis due to birch pollen exposure. He has been taking oral antihistamines and topical corticosteroids for the past few months, but his symptoms have persisted. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial for skin testing with recombinant Bet v 1 and hypoallergenic recombinant Bet v 1 fragments. The patient has no other known allergies or significant medical history. He does not have any autoimmune diseases or immune-defects, and is not currently taking any immunosuppressive drugs or psychoactive drugs. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and restrictions.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and is a beneficiary of Medicaid through Louisiana Healthcare Connections. She lives in a low-income area and has been struggling to meet her basic needs, including adequate food and housing. She has been trying to manage her diabetes, but has difficulty maintaining consistent health behaviors due to the stress and financial strain of her unmet basic needs. She has not seen significant improvement in her HbA1c levels, which were 8.5% in her most recent test. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the basic needs navigation intervention can help her to address her unmet basic needs and improve her diabetes outcomes. She is able to participate in telephone-based surveys and interventions and lives independently.

48-year-old man with a history of chronic hepatitis C and elevated liver enzymes who has undergone multiple liver biopsies in the past. He is concerned about the risks and discomforts associated with liver biopsy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates a non-invasive method to evaluate liver fibrosis. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and he is currently taking lisinopril. He denies any history of alcohol abuse or IV drug use. He is willing to undergo ultrasound and sonoelastography as part of the study procedures and has provided consent to participate.

A 28-year-old male, previously healthy, presents with symptoms of high altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) after arriving at a high altitude station in the mountains a week ago. He complains of shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. He is a soldier and has been stationed at this altitude for the past week. He denies any history of heart, lung, or kidney disease. He is not taking any medications. On physical examination, his vital signs are within normal limits. Oxygen saturation is 83% on room air. Lung examination reveals bilateral crackles. No other significant findings are noted. He is suspected to have HAPE and is eligible for the clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of CPAP and Gamow Bag ventilation in treating HAPE. He is expected to be evacuated from the post more than 8 hours later, and there is no speedy evacuation option available at the moment.

The patient is a 3-month-old baby boy who was diagnosed with idiopathic clubfoot. He was born full-term via spontaneous vaginal delivery with no complications during pregnancy, labor, or delivery. At birth, his right foot was noted to be in a fixed equinovarus position. He was referred to BC Children's Hospital for further evaluation and management. Physical examination revealed a right clubfoot with hindfoot equinus and forefoot adduction. There was no family history of clubfoot or any other musculoskeletal disorders. The patient has not undergone any previous interventions for clubfoot. He is otherwise healthy and meeting all developmental milestones. After informed consent from the parents, the patient will undergo manipulation and casting until hindfoot stall is encountered. At hindfoot stall, he will receive Botox injections at 10 IU/kg into the gastrosoleus muscle complex and be recasted. Follow-up appointments will be scheduled to monitor his progress and evaluate the efficacy of the treatment.

52-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and fatigue. He has a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF) of 40% diagnosed last year. He is currently on diuretics and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) but continues to experience symptoms despite adherence to his medication regimen. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. He is a former smoker and quit 5 years ago after smoking for 20 years. He drinks alcohol occasionally but denies drug use. On physical examination, he is found to have bilateral rales and pedal edema. His blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, his heart rate is 85 beats per minute, and his respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute. His laboratory workup reveals elevated BNP levels, indicating worsening heart failure. He is an appropriate candidate for the DIG trial as he meets the eligibility criteria of having clinical heart failure, sinus rhythm, and an ejection fraction less than or equal to 45 percent.

Patient is a 55-year-old female with a history of symptomatic focal vitreomacular adhesion. She presents with blurred vision, distortion, and difficulty reading. Her current best-corrected visual acuity in her study eye is 20/40 Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) and 20/20 ETDRS in her fellow eye. She has not undergone any prior vitrectomy or photocoagulation to the retina in the study eye. She has a stage 2 macular hole in the study eye measuring 300 µm. She has no history of proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD), or retinal vascular occlusion in the study eye. The patient has no history of ocular surgery or intravitreal injection in the study eye within 90 days of study enrollment. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with study requirements.

A 50-year-old male diagnosed with AL amyloidosis with a history of autologous stem cell transplantation presents with recurrent disease. The patient has significant initial improvement in organ function after prior high-dose chemotherapy, including a partial hematologic response with a decrease in serum monoclonal protein levels and less than 5% plasma cells in bone marrow with no clonal predominance. There is also a greater than 50% reduction in proteinuria with preservation of creatinine clearance. The patient's performance status is 1. The initial stem cell yield was ≥ 2 x 10^6 CD34+ cells/kg. The patient has no myelodysplastic syndromes or abnormal bone marrow cytogenetics and is HIV negative. There is no other concurrent malignancy except treated skin cancer.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing irregular menstrual cycles for the past 6 months. She has also been experiencing pelvic pain and discomfort during intercourse. She has not been able to conceive despite trying for over a year. She has a history of hypothyroidism for which she is taking levothyroxine. She is otherwise healthy and not taking any other medications. She has no known allergies. She has a regular exercise routine and follows a balanced diet. Her recent blood work (done 2 weeks ago) showed normal levels of hemoglobin, white blood cells, and platelets. Her serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level was within the normal range. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She has not been pregnant before. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help diagnose and treat her reproductive-related conditions.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) during a routine physical exam. The patient has a history of obesity and type 2 diabetes, which is being treated with metformin. The patient's liver biopsy showed features consistent with NASH without cirrhosis and a NAS score of at least 4. The patient has not used silymarin or other antioxidants or non-prescribed complementary alternative medications in the past 90 consecutive days. The patient's BMI is 35 kg/m². The patient has no known allergy or sensitivity to milk thistle or its preparations. The patient has not used drugs associated with a clinical or histological picture consistent with fatty liver disease or NASH for more than 12 consecutive weeks in the 1 year prior to screening. The patient is willing to adhere to the alcohol consumption guidelines and use two reliable forms of effective contraception during the study. The patient is willing to travel to the clinic for at least 11 visits over a period of 48-50 weeks.

44 yo F with recently diagnosed early-stage breast cancer. She has no history of breast cancer or any other malignancy. Biopsy confirmed her HER2-negative status and her estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor status is confirmed by core biopsy. Her tumor is palpable and measures 2.5 cm in diameter. She is in good condition and has an ECOG performance status of 0. Her hematology test results show an ANC of 2.8 x 10^9/L, platelets of 140 x 10^9/L, and hemoglobin of 12.3 g/dL. Her hepatic function test results show total bilirubin of 0.8 x UNL, ASAT of 1.2 x UNL, ALAT of 1.0 x UNL, and alkaline phosphatase of 1.5 x UNL. Cardiac function is confirmed by ECG and cardiac ultrasound. She has no history of heart disease and her hypertension is well-controlled. She is available and willing to participate in central diagnostics, treatment, and follow-up. She is willing to undergo mandatory research biopsy and blood draw. She has not undergone any previous treatment for breast cancer, including chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, radiation or experimental therapy. She is not currently taking any other investigational or study agents.

This is a 42 year-old female with a history of major depressive disorder, who has undergone electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and has achieved remission from her symptoms. She has been on an antidepressant medication in the past but had to discontinue it due to side effects. She has no current symptoms of mania or suicidal thoughts. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no history of epilepsy, dementia, severe somatic illness, or substance abuse. She is not currently taking any medication that may interfere with the study medication. She has no history of heart attack, liver disease, or glaucoma. She has no known intolerance to escitalopram or nortriptyline. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is available for follow-up visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has no history of cardiovascular diseases or diabetes. He has a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 and is a non-smoker. His blood pressure ranges from 110/70 mmHg to 140/90 mmHg. He is currently not taking any medications and has no known allergies. The patient is in good general health and has no history of significant illnesses or surgeries. He leads an active lifestyle and exercises regularly. His heart rhythm is regular and he has no palpable arterial pulse abnormalities. He has no history of cardiac arrhythmias or pacemaker dependence. He is not pregnant and not planning to become pregnant during the study. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

A 27-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with a primary immunodeficiency disorder (PID) is seeking participation in a natural history study investigating the genetic causes of PIDs. He has a history of recurrent infections and poor response to antibiotics. He reports having a low grade fever for the past few weeks. He has a family history of autoimmune diseases. He is currently taking prophylactic antibiotics to prevent infections. He is willing to undergo genetic testing and provide blood samples for research purposes. He has no history of heart, lung, or kidney disease, bleeding disorders, or viral hepatitis. He is not infected with HIV and is not pregnant. He has never smoked and does not drink alcohol. He works as a computer programmer and is married with no children. His BMI is within normal range. He is interested in participating in the study to help find a cure for his condition and to help future generations.

A 32-year-old woman, with a history of one previous cesarean delivery, presents with a missed abortion at 8 weeks of gestation. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that contraindicate the induction of abortion. Her BMI is within the range of 18.5 kg/m2 to 30 kg/m2, and her hemoglobin level is above 10 g/dL. She has no history of attempted induction of abortion in the current pregnancy. The patient is willing to participate in the study comparing the success rate of Adjuvant isonicotinic acid hydrazide and misoprostol versus misoprostol alone for medical termination of first-trimester pregnancy.

Patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C and cirrhosis, presenting with complaints of abdominal pain and fatigue. Imaging studies reveal the presence of locally advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein thrombosis. The patient has undergone liver function testing, which shows that he is Child-Pugh A-B with a total bilirubin of 1.7mg/dL and an albumin level of 3.1g/dL. Measurable disease was found on imaging studies with a lesion measuring at least 15mm in the largest diameter. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months without any active treatment. The patient has not received any prior treatment for HCC except for an adjuvant therapy given more than 6 months ago. The patient has adequate hematological, renal, and hepatic function as required by the study protocol. The patient has no signs of metastatic disease or clinical signs of CNS metastases. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent and is willing to use two forms of contraception if sexually active during their study participation. The patient is suitable for protocol treatment as determined by clinical assessment undertaken by the Investigator. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

No patient description is needed for this epidemiology study as it is a cross-sectional survey of P. falciparum parasite prevalence and malaria control intervention use in sub-Saharan Western Africa. The study is not enrolling individual patients but rather collecting data from a population of subjects aged ≥6 months and <10 years.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of asthma, currently experiencing ongoing asthma symptoms despite taking inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) at a daily dose of 500 µg/day of fluticasone or equivalent. The patient reports a history of at least 12% reversibility over pre-bronchodilator FEV1 with a percent of predicted FEV1 of 60%. The patient also reports an ACQ score of 2.5. The patient has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or other chronic pulmonary condition other than asthma. The patient has no history of uncontrolled, clinically significant systemic disease, and has not had a respiratory infection within the last 4 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of AMG 853 compared with placebo in improving asthma control.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in her knees for the past year. She was diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis (OA) based on clinical and radiological criteria of the American College of Rheumatology (ACR). She has not been physically active for the past 3 months due to the pain and is currently at an education level of 7th grade. She does not have hypertension, diabetes mellitus, thyroid diseases, or any cardiorespiratory disease. She has been advised to take pain medications by her primary care physician, but the pain still persists. She is interested in participating in this study to compare the effectiveness of supervised resistance muscular training (RT) versus sensorimotor training (SMT) on her knee OA pain and functional improvement. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all the scheduled sessions.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman diagnosed with HIV infection 2 years ago. Her past medical history is significant for recurrent urinary tract infections and a history of depression for which she is currently on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). Her current CD4+ count is 450 cells/mm3 and her plasma HIV RNA level is 15,000 copies/mL. She is currently on zidovudine (ZDV) plus lamivudine (3TC) therapy for the past 6 months. Her medical records show that she has never been treated with protease inhibitors before. She has no other significant medical history. She is an alert female with no acute distress. Her BP: 120/75, HR: 80/min and BMI: 23.5. Her abdomen is soft with no tenderness. There is no evidence of fever, cough or any other acute illness.

A healthy 25-year-old female comes to the clinic interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has no history of any significant illness or medical condition and is not taking any medication. She has a BMI of 22 and weighs 55 kg. She has not smoked and does not have any history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has never been pregnant and is on oral contraceptives. She is willing to use appropriate contraception methods during the study period. She has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic or renal disease, or any other condition known to interfere with absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs. She has no history of severe allergy/hypersensitivity or ongoing allergy/hypersensitivity, as judged by the Investigator or history of hypersensitivity to drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to AZD5718. She is willing to fast overnight for at least 10 hours before receiving the treatment. She is able to provide written informed consent and has suitable veins for cannulation or repeated venipuncture. She is eligible for this study.

A 45-year-old professional woman was diagnosed with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation six months ago. She experiences palpitations, chest discomfort, and shortness of breath during episodes of PAF. She is otherwise healthy and takes no other medications. She is married with two children and works as a marketing manager. Her anxiety level increases during PAF episodes, and she is concerned about the potential long-term effects of the condition on her health. She is fluent in English and has no cognitive impairment. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to attend weekly phone calls and two video visit/phone sessions that are 6 weeks apart. She has no prior experience with mindfulness or meditation.

45-year-old female with chronic periodontitis and at least two teeth in the mandibular molar area with periodontal pockets deeper than 4mm. She has no systemic diseases and is not taking any antibiotics or anti-inflammatory drugs within the past 6 months. She is not pregnant or nursing, and does not smoke. She has not undergone orthodontic treatments or have extensive dental restorations. The patient has not used any mouth rinses during the entire period of the study and does not use removable dentures. The patient is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions on oral hygiene procedures as well as attend all follow-up visits.

32F G2P1A0 at 32 weeks gestational age with a history of previous cesarean section was referred to obstetrics for evaluation of placenta previa. The patient reports occasional abdominal pain and spotting, but denies fever or vaginal discharge. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism and mild depression that is well-controlled with medication. She does not have a history of hypertension or diabetes. On physical examination, the patient appears comfortable and her vital signs are stable. The abdomen is soft with a fundal height consistent with gestational age. Fetal heart rate is within normal limits. Ultrasound shows placenta previa with its lower edge covering the scar of previous cesarean section. She is interested in participating in a study that evaluates the role and cost effectiveness of biochemical markers in comparison with 3D Doppler ultrasound in antenatal diagnosis of abnormal adherent placenta.

The patient is a 45-year-old Filipino woman who has been suffering from moderate to severe chronic non-cancer pain for the past 12 weeks. She is a mother of two and works as a teacher. She describes her pain as a constant dull ache that radiates from her lower back to her legs, making it difficult for her to stand or sit for long periods. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers and physical therapy, but they have not provided adequate relief. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. She is willing to comply with the protocol-defined use of effective contraception. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is able to communicate her pain characteristics and complete self-administered questionnaires. She is currently not taking any opioids or other mu-opioid receptor agonist analgesics. She is not taking Monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors or any other drugs that are contraindicated in this study. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with chronic back pain six months ago. Despite opioid therapy, she still experiences moderate-to-severe pain with a VAS score of 6. She has been on a stable morphine equivalent dose of 80mg/day for the past three months. She has not taken Methadone, Suboxone, Fentanyl, or Tramadol in the last six months, nor has she taken guanfacine or other alpha-2AR agonists during that time. She has not had any changes to her current pain treatment, such as opiates or epidural steroid injection, in the last three months. She is able to independently provide informed written consent. She does not have any sensory deficits at the site of QST, such as peripheral neuropathy, and does not have any intolerable allergies or severe adverse reactions to study medication. She is not taking vitamin B2 more than 1.6mg/day during the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any pending litigation related to neck or back pain. She has not been diagnosed with Raynaud's syndrome, fibromyalgia, or joint osteoarthritis that are predominant over back pain in terms of intensity (VAS). She does not have severe cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease/accident, hepatic or renal impairment, CNS condition, metabolic condition, or history of syncope. Her blood pressure and heart rate are within normal range, and she is not on any antihypertensive drugs or medications that result in hypotension and/or bradycardia. She has not tested positive for illicit drugs, marijuana, or non-prescribed drugs. She does not have any major psychiatric disorders that required hospitalization in the past six months, nor is she currently in a treatment program for alcohol or drug abuse. She is not currently on methadone or buprenorphine for treatment of addiction, nor is she prescribed stimulants for treatment of ADHD. She does not have a history of substance or alcohol abuse per medical record or subject admission. She is not on medications that serve as CYP3A4/5 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers, or medications that are ligands for alpha2-adrenergic receptors, including antipsychotic drugs or tricyclic or tetracyclic antidepressants.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with stage IIB squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. She is scheduled to receive chemo-radiation therapy for her oncologic treatment. She has a Karnofsky score of 70 and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. Her leukocyte count is 4,500/microL, her absolute neutrophil count is 2,000/microL, and her platelet count is 120,000/microL. Her total bilirubin is at 1.0 mg/dL (UIHC limit of normal), and both her ALT and AST are within the normal range. Her creatinine level is 1.2 times the upper limit of normal. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use contraception. She has not undergone a hysterectomy and is not scheduled to have one as part of her cancer therapy. She understands the study requirements and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

A 65-year-old man was diagnosed with Multiple System Atrophy (MSA) two years ago and has been experiencing progressive decline in his mobility, including difficulty walking and maintaining balance. He is still able to walk with assistance. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medication. He is otherwise healthy and takes no other medications. He has never participated in an investigational clinical trial before. He is willing and able to adhere to the study drug regimen and lifestyle considerations. He is willing to use effective contraception as he is sexually active with his partner. He understands the informed consent process and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in his left eye last year. He has been experiencing a gradual decrease in vision in that eye and now has difficulty reading, recognizing faces, and seeing fine details. The patient has had no prior treatment for his AMD in the left eye. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially improve his vision. The patient has good visual acuity in his right eye and is able to administer eye drops. He is able to give written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements. The patient has no history of glaucoma, and there is no hemorrhage or fibrosis under the foveal center of the left eye. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A 62-year-old man had a stroke three years ago and has been experiencing language problems since then. He is a retired veteran with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been taking medication for both conditions and reports good control. His past medical history is also significant for a transient ischemic attack (TIA) 5 years ago. The patient reports difficulty with word-finding abilities, particularly when speaking with others. He has been attending speech therapy sessions for the past year with some improvement in his language skills, but still experiences difficulty with certain words. He speaks English as his first language and has no contraindications to MRI or TMS. He is interested in participating in this study to further improve his language skills and help others who may experience similar difficulties.

45 yo F with a history of hypertension and uncontrolled diabetes, presents to the emergency department with fever, chills, and confusion. She reports feeling weak and unwell for the past 2 days. Upon examination, she was found to have a fever of 101.2°F, tachycardia, and hypotension. Her labs show leukocytosis with left shift, elevated lactate, and acute kidney injury (AKI). A urine sample is collected for the study to determine the level of heparanase activity. The patient is diagnosed with sepsis and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluid resuscitation. She is closely monitored for signs of worsening AKI. The study will help determine if high levels of heparanase activity in urine can predict the risk of developing AKI in sepsis. The patient is eligible to participate in the clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria for sepsis.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with primary glomerulonephritis two years ago. She has been experiencing worsening of her symptoms lately including fatigue, edema, and high blood pressure. She is currently taking medications for her condition but has not seen any significant improvement. She has an eGFR of 45 ml/min and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore alternative treatments. She has no history of heart failure, infectious diseases, neoplasia, hepatic diseases, COPD, inflammatory bowel disease, stroke or acute coronary disease. She is not pregnant and is willing to provide informed consent.

A 40-year-old HIV-positive man was admitted to the hospital for sepsis due to a urinary tract infection. He had a history of unprotected sex and intravenous drug use. His CD4 cell count was 250 cells/mm3 and his HIV viral load was 100,000 copies/mL. He had never taken antiretroviral therapy before. Upon admission, he was transferred to the intensive care area due to his critical condition. His arterial blood gas PaO2/FiO2 ratio was 150 and his SAPS I score was 15. The patient was informed about the study and agreed to participate. He met all inclusion criteria and did not have any exclusion criteria. He was randomized to Arm A, which received HAART (lamivudine, zidovudine, nelfinavir, and efavirenz) for four weeks. The patient was monitored closely for any drug toxicities, immune status, viral load, arterial blood gas, ventilator parameters, and evolution of the presenting illness. Pharmacokinetic trough concentration analyses were performed on him during 3 time points of his illness. He was followed for 24 weeks after entry in the study. The patient also agreed to participate in the second substudy, which evaluated the benefit of HAART in HIV infected patients being treated for pneumocystis carinii pneumonia.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer after noticing a lump in her breast. She has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother and maternal grandmother both having been diagnosed in their 50s. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the presence of invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR positive and HER2 negative. She is currently undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy as part of her treatment plan. She has no other significant medical history, does not smoke or drink alcohol, and takes only occasional over-the-counter pain medication. She is married and has two children, aged 10 and 12. She is eager to participate in clinical research that could potentially help her and other breast cancer patients in the future.

Pt is a 29yo M who identifies as gay and has a history of multiple HIV antibody tests in the past. He reports having engaged in unprotected anal intercourse with male partners of unknown HIV status or known HIV infection within the last 12 months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to reduce his risk of HIV infection. He is proficient in English and does not have a history of injection drug use within the last 12 months.

32-year-old female with a diagnosis of celiac disease 18 months ago. She has been following a gluten-free diet and has been compliant with the diet for the past 12 months. However, her serum activity markers are still elevated, indicating ongoing active disease. She denies any gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea, abdominal pain, or bloating. She has never been treated with enzyme supplements before. She is willing to participate in the study and agrees to continue following a gluten-free diet.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was recently admitted to the hospital with symptoms of a stroke. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient arrived at the hospital within 6 hours of the onset of symptoms. Her neurologic exam shows right-sided weakness and facial droop. She is unable to speak coherently. CT scan of the brain shows a left middle cerebral artery occlusion. She is a candidate for mechanical thrombectomy with the Trevo Retriever. She has no contraindications to thrombectomy. She has no known allergies to contrast material. She is able to provide informed consent. She has a supportive family who will help with her follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been a regular patient at his primary care practice for the past 5 years. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He is a former smoker and has been tobacco-free for the past 10 years. He reports occasional alcohol use but denies any drug use. He has been experiencing increased stress at work and reports difficulty sleeping. He is interested in improving his overall health and lifestyle. He regularly attends his appointments with his primary care physician for wellness checks and chronic disease management. He is eligible to participate in this clinical trial as he is presenting for chronic care at the study practice.

The patient is a 29-year-old man living with HIV. He has been on a stable antiretroviral therapy regimen for the past 5 months. His CD4 T cell count is 180/µl. He has not been taking any lipid-lowering agents for the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in a dietary supplement study to improve his metabolic and immune system functioning. He is willing to follow the recommendations for participating in the study, including not consuming food, alcohol, caffeine, or stimulants 12 hours before each assessment. He has no known allergy to rice, rice bran, mushrooms, or related food products. He does not have any gastrointestinal disorders that could lead to uncertain resorption of the study supplement. He is not currently taking immunomodulatory medication or chemotherapeutic agents. He is a non-smoker and has no history of severe anemia or bleeding disorder. He is not currently pregnant or attempting conception.

Patient is a 62-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease (PD) for 3 years. He has been on a stable dosage of dopaminergic medication for 3 months prior to study enrollment. The patient is in disease stage 2-3 Hoehn & Yahr in the "on" phase. He reports difficulty with walking, including a significant reduction of stride length, forward-flexed trunk, reduced arm swing with asymmetric stride times for lower limbs, and significant stride-to-stride variability. The patient has no significant cognitive impairment, with a MMSE score of 28/30. There are no other orthopedic problems or pathological conditions that may affect gait training. The patient is willing to participate in the 4-week rehabilitation program, which includes daily sessions of traditional physiotherapy followed by 20-minute sessions of overground gait training with Body Weight Support Treadmill Training (BWSTT) or traditional physiotherapy with overground gait training as a control group.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing fever, chills, and pain in her lower back and sides for the past two days. She went to the emergency room and was diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis. She has no other significant medical history, is not pregnant or nursing, and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study. She has not received any investigational drugs in the past 30 days and does not have any allergies to tetracycline or levofloxacin. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help find a more effective treatment for her condition.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of chronic kidney disease (stage III) came to the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath and fatigue while doing daily activities. She has been suffering from these symptoms for the past 6 months. She also has a history of hypertension for 10 years, which is controlled with medication. She doesn't smoke or use illicit drugs. She works as a librarian and usually walks to work. She is willing to participate in the study and doesn't regularly exercise. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 45 cc/minute, as calculated by the Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) equation, and her proteinuria level is 600 mg/g of Creatinine. She has never been pregnant and is willing to use an acceptable method of contraception during the study. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, diabetes, serious systemic disease, congestive heart failure or ejection fraction below 35%, myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular accident, nephrolithiasis, or HIV infection. She has not been treated with vitamin C in the past 3 months and has no history of hypersensitivity to BH4. She is willing to cooperate with the protocol and is not at high risk of poor adherence or poor follow-up.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a family history of breast cancer. She tested positive for the BRCA-1 gene mutation and has decided to undergo prophylactic mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction. She is a non-smoker and has no history of peripheral neuropathy. She lives with her husband and two children. She is active and enjoys running and yoga. She is concerned about the potential loss of sensation in her breasts after surgery and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve sensory recovery. She is willing to undergo electrical stimulation during surgery and participate in follow-up evaluations for up to 2 years. She is aware of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to sign informed consent.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol consumption. He was diagnosed with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and received standard chemotherapy treatment, but the cancer progressed. He is currently experiencing difficulty swallowing and chest pain. A CT scan shows a measurable lesion with a length to diameter of 15 mm. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. His blood routine examination results show that his hemoglobin level is 110 g/L, his ANC is 2.0×109/L, and his PLT is 90×109/L. His biochemical examination results show that his ALB level is 35g/L, his ALT and AST levels are within normal limits, his TBIL level is 1.0ULN, and his plasma Cr level is 1.2ULN. He has no history of other malignancies or mental illness. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the follow-up schedule.

A 50-year-old postmenopausal woman is presented to the clinic with osteoporosis. She has a history of low-impact fractures with a bone mineral density T-score of -2.5 at the lumbar spine and -2.0 at the total hip. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, and she does not have any allergies. She is not currently taking any medication for osteoporosis, and she has not taken any bone health modifying treatments in the past. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effect of mechanical loading with PTH on cortical bone. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 16 year old female with poor oral hygiene conditions, including dental plaque and marginal gingival bleeding at more than 50% of tooth surfaces, is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient is located in the Västra Götaland Region of Sweden and is seeking to improve her oral hygiene habits and prevent periodontal disease progression. The patient does not have any compromised medical or mental conditions that would require special care.

The patient is a 56 year old man with end-stage renal disease who has been on hemodialysis for the past 8 months. He has no significant residual renal function and is not on anti-arrhythmic drugs. He has no history of chronic arrhythmia and does not have a pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. The patient has been experiencing occasional palpitations during his hemodialysis treatments, which has been concerning him. His most recent echocardiogram showed normal cardiac function. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo insertion of the Reveal LINQ insertable cardiac monitoring system to gather data on the incidence of arrhythmia. He is able to provide informed consent and is interested in contributing to research that may improve the lives of patients on hemodialysis.

A 32-year-old male farmer from rural Bangladesh presents with fever, chills, headache, and myalgia for the past 3 days. He reports a history of malaria in the past and has not taken any antimalarial medication in the last 30 days. He denies any recent travel outside his village. His vital signs are stable, and his physical examination is remarkable for mild splenomegaly. Laboratory analysis shows a positive blood smear for falciparum malaria with a parasite density of 7,800 asexual parasites/uL. The patient is otherwise healthy and provides written informed consent to participate in the study. He is willing to stay under close medical supervision for the study duration and meets all the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and underwent an allogeneic stem cell transplant 2 months ago. He received reduced intensity conditioning regimen before the transplant. Currently, he is in complete remission and has no active signs of GVHD. His CMV serology is positive. He is receiving immunosuppressive therapy, including prednisone, which is being tapered down. His absolute neutrophil count is greater than 0.5 X 10^3/for 3 consecutive days. His Karnofsky performance score is greater than or equal to 80%.

A 49-year-old female presents with a history of myopia for the past 25 years. She complains of a sudden decrease in vision, distorted images, and metamorphopsia in her left eye for the past 3 weeks. She has no history of ocular trauma or surgery. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication, and she has no history of thromboembolic events. Her visual acuity in the left eye is 20/200, and the intraocular pressure is within normal limits. Ophthalmic examination reveals posterior staphyloma, chorioretinal atrophy, and papillary crescent in the left eye. Fluorescein angiography confirms the presence of subfoveal choroidal neovascularization (CNV) in the left eye. The right eye is normal. The axial length of the left eye is 28.5 mm, and the spherical equivalent is -8.5 D. The patient has no history of previous treatment for CNV or any other maculopathy. She has clear ocular media, and the duration of symptoms is less than 4 weeks.

10-year-old female patient with no history of sexual activity and no prior HPV vaccination. The patient is currently in good health and has no known allergies to vaccines. The patient's parents have expressed concerns about the HPV vaccine and have not yet decided whether or not to have their child vaccinated. The patient's primary care physician is participating in the HPV 9-10 Trial, which is investigating the effectiveness of early initiation of the HPV vaccine at age 9-10 years. The physician has recommended the patient for the trial, and the patient's parents have agreed to participate. The trial will randomly assign the patient's physician to either recommend the HPV vaccine at age 9-10 or at age 11-12. The trial will assess whether earlier initiation of the vaccine results in higher rates of full vaccination and reduced parental refusal. The patient's participation in the trial will involve regular follow-up appointments with the physician over the course of several years to monitor vaccine completion and assess the effectiveness of the intervention.

A 45-year-old Hispanic male with end-stage renal disease presents to the nephrology clinic for follow-up. He has been on peritoneal dialysis for the past 6 months and complains of feeling bloated and having difficulty breathing recently. He reports complying with his dietary and fluid restrictions recommended by his healthcare team. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals a distended abdomen with shifting dullness on percussion. Laboratory tests reveal an elevated BUN of 50 mg/dL and a creatinine level of 8.5 mg/dL. The patient is diagnosed with volume overload and is a candidate for the Bioimpedance-guided Fluid Management clinical trial. He meets the inclusion criteria, is willing to participate, and signs the informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of diabetes and hypertension. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for the past two weeks. He has been taking over-the-counter medication for the pain, but it has not provided any relief. He has no history of allergy to any medications or imaging procedures. He is not pregnant or nursing. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his consent. The patient is available to undergo an abdomino-pelvic ultrasound examination and has no substitutable examination. He has no objections to the use of his data for research purposes.

A 45-year-old man with a history of alcohol dependence is seeking treatment for his addiction. He has been drinking heavily for the past year, consuming at least 6 standard drinks per day. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help him reduce his drinking. He has no history of drug abuse or dependence, psychotic disorders, or bipolar disorders. He has no current suicidal or homicidal ideation and has tested negative for illicit drugs (except marijuana). He is willing to provide informed consent and agrees not to take over-the-counter analgesics during the study. He has no clinically significant cardiac, hepatic, renal, neurologic, or pulmonary disease, and his baseline aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are within normal limits. He is not currently using disulfiram, acamprosate, or topiramate. He is not pregnant or nursing, and he is using adequate birth control methods. His alcohol breathalyzer level is 0.05 at the screening visit. He has not experienced severe alcohol withdrawal (delirium tremens or withdrawal seizures) within the past year, and he is not currently requiring inpatient treatment for treating alcohol dependence.

Patient B is a 27-year-old female diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 14. She has been managing her condition with insulin therapy and frequent blood glucose monitoring. She works as a graphic designer and enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking and swimming. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the accuracy and efficacy of the G5® Mobile Continuous Glucose Monitoring System with the automated sensor applicator. She has no known allergies to medical-grade adhesives and is not currently pregnant. She is willing to participate in a clinic session involving venous sampling for evaluation of the study end point. She does not use acetaminophen and her hematocrit levels are within the specification of the study-assigned blood glucose meter.

A 42-year-old woman came to the clinic with complaints of pain in her jaw joint and difficulty in opening her mouth. She had these symptoms for six months and is unable to eat solid food. She has been diagnosed with temporomandibular disorder (TMD) by her dentist. She is a writer and spends long hours sitting at her desk. She has a history of sleep bruxism and has been using a night guard for the past two years. She doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. She is not currently taking any medication for her TMD. Her family history is unremarkable for TMD. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate a new treatment option for TMD.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He is currently not on any antiretroviral therapy and is seeking treatment for his condition. He has no significant medical history and is in good overall health. He works as an accountant in a private firm and lives with his partner. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is compliant with his medical appointments and is willing to adhere to the study protocol. He has signed informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the effectiveness, safety, adherence, and health-related quality of life in HIV-1 infected adults receiving bictegravir/ emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF).

A 69-year-old woman was diagnosed with bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement due to severe mitral valve stenosis 2 years ago. She has a history of persistent atrial fibrillation and has been on warfarin therapy since the time of her valve replacement. She has had several international normalized ratio (INR) fluctuations and has had difficulty maintaining therapeutic INR levels. Her most recent INR was 2.8. She has no history of thromboembolic events or bleeding complications. She is currently taking aspirin 100 mg daily in addition to warfarin. She is otherwise in good health with no other significant medical history. Her most recent laboratory results are as follows: Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL, Platelets: 220,000 /mm³, Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL, Alanine aminotransferase: 30 U/L. She is interested in participating in the RIVER trial to explore the safety and efficacy of rivaroxaban compared with vitamin K antagonism in patients with atrial fibrillation with bioprosthetic mitral valves.

The patient is a 30 year-old woman who is 28 weeks pregnant with her first child. She is overweight with a booking BMI of 28 kg/m2. During her routine oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), she was diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and requires pharmacological treatment to control her blood sugar levels. She has no significant medical history apart from mild asthma that is well controlled with an inhaler. She is not taking any medication, and her pregnancy has been uneventful so far. She is fluent in English and has no known allergies to any medication. She is planning to have her antenatal, intrapartum, and postpartum care at the participating center and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol.

35-year-old female with a history of nearsightedness is scheduled for Photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) surgery in two weeks. The patient experiences occasional headaches and mild eye strain but does not take any systemic analgesic drugs. She has no known drug intolerances and has not required any systemic or topical administration of NSAIDs or eye drops for allergy and glaucoma. The patient does not have dry eyes, is not pregnant, and is not currently breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy of gabapentin (Neurentin) and pregabalin (Lyrica) in reducing pain after PRK surgery. The patient understands that she may be randomly assigned to receive one of three options: gabapentin, pregabalin, or a placebo, and that the pain will be measured based on a visual analog scale (VAS) on the day of operation and on the 3rd day (morning, evening) and then compared among the three groups.

45-year-old female breast cancer survivor who underwent mastectomy and radiation therapy to the chest wall. She has been in remission for 5 years and has not received any chemotherapy or other systemic treatment for her cancer. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. Her renal function is normal and she has no known allergies. She is interested in participating in a study that may help detect potential damage to her heart caused by the radiation therapy she received several years ago.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who has a history of hearing loss and is scheduled for cochlear implantation surgery. She has no known drug allergies and has not taken any antibiotics in the past 6 weeks. She reports no current symptoms of infection or illness. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes amlodipine 5mg once daily for blood pressure control. Her blood pressure is well-controlled with this medication. She has no other significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. She will be randomized to one of the two antibiotic treatment groups, which will be determined prior to her surgery. She will be followed up at one week, one month, three months, one year, and two years after surgery to assess for any signs of infection or adverse reactions to the antibiotic treatment.

Maria is a 47 year old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic melanoma in her lymph nodes. She has a history of having a mole on her back that was initially diagnosed as benign but over the years it started to change in color and size. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of melanoma. She has received interferon treatment in the past and has also undergone one cycle of chemotherapy. She has not received any other investigational drug within the last 28 days prior to registration. Her performance status is good, with an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no symptomatic central nervous system metastases, but has small asymptomatic metastases in her liver and lungs. She has not undergone any major surgery within the last 14 days prior to registration. Her organ and marrow functions are normal with leukocytes count of 5,000/mL, absolute neutrophil count of 3,000/mL, platelets count of 150,000/mL, total bilirubin within the institutional upper limit of normal, AST(SGOT)/ALT(SGPT) within 2.5 X institutional upper limit of normal, and creatinine within the institutional upper limit of normal. She has a hemoglobin level of 10 gm/dl. She is not pregnant or nursing and has agreed to use an effective contraceptive method throughout the study. She has no severe and/or uncontrolled concurrent medical disease and is not taking therapeutic doses of coumadin at the time of registration. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study as at least 20% of her tumor cells stain positively for PDGF receptor alpha or beta, or KIT (CD 117) expression by tumor documented by DAKO antibody staining, or c-abl, ARG.

Sarah is a 30 year old woman who has experienced partial seizures with or without secondary generalization for the past two years. She has been attending the outpatient clinic at Assuit University Hospital for her condition. She experiences symptoms such as sudden confusion, loss of consciousness, and jerking movements in her left arm and leg. EEG has shown focal ictal temporal lobe patterns. She has no known history of neurological or psychiatric disorders. She has undergone conventional MR imaging which showed no lesions other than mesial temporal sclerosis. Sarah is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the role of advanced MRI sequences in the diagnosis of idiopathic temporal lobe epilepsy. She is willing to provide informed consent and undergo MRI imaging to help advance the understanding and diagnosis of her condition.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after experiencing abdominal pain and jaundice. His biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. He has not received any prior systemic therapy for his cancer. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and his Child-Pugh score is 6. He has no history of autoimmune diseases or interstitial lung disease. The patient's hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA level is 1200 IU/mL, and he is currently receiving antiviral therapy for his chronic hepatitis B infection. The patient has no evidence of active pulmonary tuberculosis or HIV/AIDS. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his laboratory values are within normal limits. The patient has a measurable lesion based on RECIST 1.1. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

A 35-year-old female who is interested in reducing unwanted fat in her abdominal area. She has a BMI of 26 kg/m2 and is generally healthy with no history of cardiac pacemakers or electronic implants. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of malignant tumors or fever. She has no cardiac disorders or haemorrhagic conditions, and is not currently undergoing anticoagulation therapy. The patient has no scars or open lesions in the treatment area and has not undergone any recent surgical procedures that may disrupt the healing process. She has normal sensation in the treatment area and has no abdominal hernia. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has voluntarily signed the informed consent form.

A 50-year old man was diagnosed with liver cancer and is scheduled for a partial hepatectomy by laparotomy. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and has been sober for the past year. He lives with his wife and two children. The patient has no other significant medical history. He is affiliated with a social security scheme and has given written consent to participate in the research study. The patient has access to intraoperative measurements of vascular pressures and flow rates. He is willing to undergo additional MRI scans as part of the study. The patient is not under guardianship or curatorship and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is eager to participate in the study and hopes that the results will help improve the selection of candidates for liver surgery and reduce the risk of postoperative complications.

A 32-year-old female nurse who works at the University Medicine of Greifswald was referred for participation in a clinical trial aimed at evaluating the effectiveness of auricular stimulation in reducing stress and anxiety related to COVID-19 pandemic. The patient reports feeling overwhelmed and anxious due to the high demand for healthcare services and the increased risk of exposure to the virus. She denies any history of anxiolytic medication use and has no known allergies. The patient is able to understand and fill in the structured questionnaire and provides written informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of psychiatric disease and does not have any prosthetic or damaged cardiac valves or mitral valve prolaps.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has never taken Rimonabant or Paracetamol before and does not have any known hypersensitivities to either medication. He does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol, tobacco, coffee, tea or any illicit drugs. He does not take any other medications and does not have any chronic diseases. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to provide written consent.

32 y/o pregnant female with a BMI of 28.2 kg/m2, scheduled for a cesarean section delivery at Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU). The patient has no known drug allergies and is not currently using narcotic medications. She is in good overall health and has no contraindications to neuraxial anesthesia. The patient is scheduled to receive spinal anesthesia during the cesarean section procedure. The patient's estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is greater than 30 ml/min and her aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are within normal limits. The patient is not carrying multiple fetuses and does not have atypical cholinesterase activity. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of chloroprocaine lavage during cesarean section to improve outcomes related to operative delivery.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been smoking waterpipe tobacco for the past 5 years. She smokes one waterpipe tobacco head per week at home with her friends. She has no history of major physical or psychiatric illnesses and is not currently pregnant. She does not smoke any other tobacco products and takes no medications. The patient lives in a non-smoker home and has not had any visitors who smoked indoors or outdoors in the past month. Her vital signs are within normal limits, with a blood pressure of 120/75, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 16 per minute. She is a non-smoker and has not been exposed to second-hand smoke in the past month. She is interested in participating in the Waterpipe Study to learn more about the effects of waterpipe smoking on her health and to contribute to the research effort to regulate waterpipe tobacco products.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who underwent a kidney transplant 2 years ago due to end-stage renal disease secondary to IgA nephropathy. He has been compliant with his immunosuppressive regimen and has a stable renal function with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 45 ml/min. His plasma urea concentration is 120 mg/dl and plasma albumin concentration is 4.2 g/dl. He has been following a stable protein and salt intake for the last 6 months. The patient has no history of malignancies, autoimmune diseases, or severe infectious diseases in the last 3 months.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with metastatic bone cancer in the left proximal femur. He has been experiencing increasing pain in the left hip area for several months, limiting his mobility, and interfering with his daily activities. Imaging revealed a large tumor involving the proximal femur, and the patient was advised to undergo tumor resection and primary endoprosthetic reconstruction involving the hip joint. He has no other significant medical history, and his vital signs are within normal limits. He is not currently on any medications or undergoing any other treatments for cancer. The patient has been informed of the study and has provided informed consent to participate. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

A 35-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a history of tick bite 10 days ago. She noticed a red rash around the site of the bite and developed a fever of 38.5°C four days ago, which has persisted since then. She denies any cough, shortness of breath, or urinary symptoms. She is a nurse and has been exposed to ticks frequently in the past. She has no significant past medical history, does not smoke, drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. She is currently not taking any medications. Upon physical examination, she is alert and oriented, with no signs of meningeal irritation or focal neurological deficits. The skin around the bite site is erythematous and tender to palpation. There are no other significant findings on examination. The laboratory findings show a mild leukocytosis with a neutrophilic predominance. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 65-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis in his right knee for the past 5 years presented to the clinic for a total knee arthroplasty (TKA). The patient had been experiencing severe pain in his right knee, which had become increasingly worse over the past year, limiting his daily activities. After the orthopedic surgeon's evaluation, the patient is scheduled for a primary unilateral TKA. The patient weighs 80 kg and has a body mass index of 32 kg/m2. He has not taken any opioids, NSAIDs, SSRIs, gabapentin, pregabalin or duloxetine for the past 3 days, and has not taken any MAOIs for the past 14 days. He agrees to use two medically accepted methods of contraception during the course of the study with his partner. He has no history of allergy or hypersensitivity to local anesthetics and does not have any significant pre-operative liver or renal insufficiency. He has no active infection with HIV, HBV, or HCV at the screening visit. The patient is capable of understanding and providing written informed consent.

The patient is a 48-year-old male who has been diagnosed with advanced differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC). He has a history of papillary thyroid cancer that has spread to other parts of his body and has become resistant to radioiodine treatment. He experiences pain in the neck area, fatigue, and difficulty swallowing. He has undergone previous surgeries and chemotherapy treatments. He has no significant medical history other than thyroid cancer. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 120/80 Hgb: 13 g/dl WBC: 9000 /mm3 Plt: 350000 /ml Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dl BUN: 15 mg/dl. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. He is not currently taking any investigational agents, and he has not undergone any major surgeries or radiotherapy within the last 4 weeks.

A 28-year-old male who is an active injection drug user presents with a positive purified protein derivative (PPD) tuberculin skin test. His induration is 12 mm. He reports having injected illicit drugs within the last month and is currently not in a drug treatment program. He has no active tuberculosis on chest x-ray. He is a candidate for isoniazid prophylaxis through the Baltimore City Health Department. He has no prior serious adverse reaction to isoniazid. His hepatic function tests are within normal limits with ALT of 25 U/L. He has not received more than 6 months of prior TB preventive therapy for HIV. No requirement for HIV therapy other than Pneumocystis prophylaxis or antiretrovirals. The patient is willing to participate in a trial to enhance adherence to isoniazid preventive therapy.

A 12-year-old male presents to the emergency department with severe scrotal pain that started suddenly about 4 hours ago. The pain is constant and is not relieved by rest or analgesics. The patient does not report any history of trauma, but he noticed that the affected testicle appears to be higher than the other. Physical examination reveals a swollen and tender left testicle that is tender to palpation. There is no palpable mass or hernia. The patient denies any fever, nausea, vomiting, or urinary symptoms. He has no significant medical history, and he is not taking any medication. The patient is afebrile, his BP is 120/75, HR 95, RR 16, T 37.2, SpO2 99% on RA. Urinalysis is negative for infection. An ultrasound is ordered to evaluate for testicular torsion, and the patient is invited to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the utility of NIRS for the diagnosis of testicular torsion and the prediction of testicular viability after detorsion. The patient and his parents are provided with information about the study, and they agree to participate. The patient is eligible for the study, and he is enrolled.

This is a 52 year-old female presenting to the emergency department with palpitations, chest discomfort and shortness of breath. She has no prior history of atrial fibrillation, but has a family history of heart disease. An electrocardiogram (ECG) reveals that she is in atrial fibrillation with a heart rate of 120 beats per minute. She is experiencing symptoms due to her condition and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help find a better treatment approach. She has no history of persistent AF and is considered stable by the attending physician. She is able and willing to sign informed consent and use a telemetric rhythm recorder.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse for the past 20 years. He presents with complaints of abdominal distension and difficulty breathing. Physical examination reveals ascites and bilateral lower extremity edema. Laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes and low albumin levels. Imaging studies confirm the presence of cirrhosis without evidence of portal vein thrombosis or malignancy. The patient is not currently on any diuretic treatment for ascites. He is a candidate for the clinical trial investigating the use of losartan, an angiotensin II blocker, in preventing the progression of decompensation in liver cirrhosis. He meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

A 64-year-old retired accountant was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer after experiencing abdominal pain and weight loss. He underwent biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has no prior history of cancer or any significant medical problems. He is married and has two adult children. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is currently scheduled for surgery to remove the tumor and is being offered to participate in a clinical trial to assess the feasibility of a new imaging system to detect primary pancreatic cancer and peritoneal invasion from primary pancreatic cancer during surgery. He is otherwise healthy and has normal organ and marrow function. He is willing to follow study procedures and instructions and has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been missing a lower right first molar tooth for the past 2 years. She is seeking dental implantation to replace the missing tooth. Her past medical history is significant for well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which she takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has no history of drug abuse. She is not pregnant and has no active infections. Her inter-occlusal space is adequate for implant placement. A cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) scan reveals a narrow alveolar ridge with a minimum bone width of 3mm and minimum bone height of 10mm in the posterior mandibular area. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates a two-stage splitting approach for horizontal ridge augmentation.

This is a 32-year-old male veteran who served in the army for six years between 2010 and 2016. He has been diagnosed with PTSD stemming from a Criterion A event during his deployment. He reports experiencing flashbacks, nightmares, and avoidance of certain triggers such as loud noises and crowds. He also reports feeling emotionally numb and disconnected from loved ones. He has tried different treatments in the past, including cognitive-behavioral therapy and medication, but has not found significant relief from his symptoms. He is not currently using benzodiazepines and is on a stable dose of antidepressant medication. He has no history of animal cruelty, and he is not opposed to working with dogs. He is fluent in English and is willing to comply with all study procedures. He has read and signed the informed consent form to participate in this pilot crossover randomized controlled trial (RCT) to test the feasibility, acceptability, and initial efficacy of an adjunct intervention for use with Empirically Based Treatments (EBT) for PTSD.

The patient is a 70-year-old retired woman who is interested in maintaining her physical health and staying active. She describes her overall health as good and has no physical limitations that would prevent her from walking. She is not currently participating in a daily walking program but is interested in joining a structured walking program that provides incentives to motivate her to stay active. She enjoys spending time outdoors and believes that walking regularly will help her maintain her mobility and independence as she ages. She is willing to participate in an interview study to share her thoughts and experiences about joining a walking program.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past year. He has been prescribed various pain medications, including codeine and tramadol, but has not found significant relief. The patient is currently being treated at a family medicine clinic and has consented to participate in the study.
