He has a history of hypertension, controlled with medication, and no known drug allergies. The patient will undergo CYP2D6 genotyping to determine his ability to metabolize codeine and tramadol. The results will be placed in his medical record to assist with prescribing pain medications. The patient will be followed for 3 months to assess the effectiveness of the prescribed pain medications and will complete a pain assessment questionnaire at baseline and 3 months.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with confirmed HIV-1 infection. The patient has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 5 years and has achieved virological suppression with undetectable plasma HIV-1 RNA levels for at least 6 months. The patient has a history of multiple antiretroviral drug regimens due to the presence of archived multidrug resistance mutations (DRM). The patient is currently taking a regimen consisting of a boosted protease inhibitor (ritonavir-boosted darunavir), an integrase strand-transfer inhibitor (raltegravir), and a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (abacavir/lamivudine). The patient is experiencing mild side effects such as diarrhea and fatigue, and is interested in a simplification strategy that could reduce the burden of medication and potentially reduce unwanted side effects. The patient is willing and able to adhere to the study regimen and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has no history of liver disease, hepatitis C infection, or hepatitis B surface antigen positivity.

A 62-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with a left hemispheric ischemic stroke. She has reported experiencing spasticity in her left arm, specifically in her wrist flexors and finger flexors, with a score of 2 in the Modifying Modified Ashworth Scale (MMAS). She has no history of severe cognitive impairment, language problems, vision or hearing impairments. The patient has not received any treatment by injection of TBA in the past 2 months and does not have any medical condition that contraindicates dry needling. She has no contraindication for the application of dry puncture and is willing to participate in the study. The patient will receive 6 sessions of DNHS® technique with an interval of 1 week between each session (1st to 4th sessions) and every 15 days (5th and 6th sessions). Before and after each dry needling session, the patient will be evaluated by her usual physiotherapist, using the upper limb block of the Fugl-Meyer scale that assesses motor skills and sensitivity of the affected arm, evaluation of pain through NRS10 and assessment of spasticity of muscles to be treated by MMAS. At the beginning, in the 4th session and at the end of the study, the Euro-QoL 5D-5L quality of life survey will be administered. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and is interested in improving her upper limb functionality.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) for 2 years. She has been experiencing frequent attacks of abdominal pain, vomiting, and constipation. Her urine PBG levels have been consistently high during these attacks. She has no other significant medical history or allergies. She has not started any new prescription medication in the past 3 months. She is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to become pregnant. She is willing to provide written informed consent and comply with study requirements.

A 42-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia was scheduled for a minor orthopedic surgery. The surgery requires laryngeal mask insertion for airway management. The patient does not have any known allergies to ketamine or remifentanyl. He is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent for the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has tested positive for COVID-19 and is currently experiencing symptoms including cough, fever, and shortness of breath. She has been hospitalized and is receiving standard treatment for COVID-19 but has not yet developed moderate or severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). She has no history of anaphylactic transfusion reactions or acute decompensated heart failure. She is willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with ovarian cancer is eligible for this clinical trial. She has had a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with the pathology report confirming stage IIIc high-grade serous carcinoma. The patient has no past medical history of note, is a non-smoker, and has no known drug allergies. She has no significant family history of cancer. The patient is currently undergoing chemotherapy with paclitaxel/carboplatin after primary surgery. She has agreed to participate in the study, and a tissue sample will be taken from her for genotypic analysis. The patient will be followed up for toxicity and survival data as part of the study.

60 year-old man with persistent knee pain for more than a year, which he attributes to osteoarthritis. The pain is typically located at the medial knee joint and is described as a dull, aching sensation that is worse with walking and climbing stairs. He describes his pain as moderate and is unable to perform his regular daily activities, such as gardening and walking his dog, without experiencing discomfort. He has tried over-the-counter pain relievers such as ibuprofen and acetaminophen, but the relief is only temporary. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He has no history of inflammatory arthritis or any other rheumatic disease. He is able to walk without an assistive device and has no significant limitations in his mobility. He meets the American College of Rheumatology clinical criteria for knee osteoarthritis and has a moderate pain rating on the WOMAC scale.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer 5 years ago. He underwent external beam radiotherapy as initial definitive therapy and was declared cancer-free after regular check-ups. However, he recently experienced a rise in his PSA levels and is now suspected to have a biochemical recurrence. He is eligible for the PYTHON clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no history of salvage therapies, adjuvant radiotherapy, cryotherapy, or high-intensity focused ultrasound. He is currently not on any Androgen Deprivation Therapy (ADT) or medication that may interfere with the study. The patient has social insurance cover and is able to provide informed consent. He is willing to undergo all the study procedures, including PET/CT scans with 18F-DCFPyL and 18F-fluorocholine. The patient has no known allergies to investigational or reference products or any excipients. He is able to lie supine for imaging and is cooperative in the Investigator's opinion.

This is a 62-year-old male with a history of smoking and alcohol abuse, who presented with dysphagia and weight loss. An upper endoscopy revealed a mass in the distal esophagus, and biopsy results showed adenocarcinoma. CT scan revealed no evidence of metastasis, and he was diagnosed with local curable esophageal cancer. He is otherwise healthy and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He is able to undergo chemoradiotherapy and has no history of previous or concurrent malignancies.

A 56-year-old man was admitted to the ICU due to severe pneumonia complicated with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and septic shock. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but no history of diabetes. On admission, his blood glucose level was 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L), and he received insulin infusion to maintain blood glucose level between 140 and 180 mg/dL (7.8-10 mmol/L). Despite the insulin infusion, his blood glucose level fluctuated widely during the first 24 hours of ICU stay. The medical team decided to enroll him in the clinical trial to assess the accuracy, feasibility, and safety of the continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS) in comparison with simultaneous laboratory arterial blood glucose (ABG) values. The patient had no broken skin, and his platelet count was within the normal range. The expected length of his ICU stay was longer than 48 hours. He gave his informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. The symptoms started 2 hours ago. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She takes Lisinopril and Atorvastatin. She does not smoke and does not drink alcohol. Her family history is negative for stroke. On examination, her blood pressure is 160/90 mmHg, heart rate is 80 bpm, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. The neurological examination reveals mild dysarthria, right-sided facial droop, and right hemiparesis. The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score is 8. The patient is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (Ta, low-grade) that was removed by transurethral resection. He has a history of smoking, but has quit 5 years ago. He has no significant medical history and is not on any medication. His physical examination and laboratory studies were unremarkable. He has not received BCG therapy before and is willing to participate in this clinical trial. He is aware that he may or may not receive BCG therapy and that he may or may not receive placebo. He is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all required visits. He is not allergic to soy, egg, or peanut products. He understands the potential risks and benefits of participation in this clinical trial.

A newborn baby, born at 38 weeks gestation, is suspected to have perinatal depression due to a low Apgar score of 4 at 10 minutes after birth. The baby required endotracheal intubation and chest compressions for resuscitation. The initial blood gas analysis showed a pH of 6.9 and base deficit of 16. The baby also exhibits moderate to severe encephalopathy with 5 out of 6 modified Sarnat criteria present, including reduced level of consciousness, decreased spontaneous activity, hypotonia, decreased suck, and respiratory distress. Passive cooling therapy was started within 6 hours of birth. The baby has no intrauterine growth restriction, major congenital malformation, suspected genetic syndrome, metabolic disorder or TORCH infection. The baby's head circumference is within normal range for gestation. The parents are willing to consent to the baby's participation in the NEATO clinical trial.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy who has been experiencing headaches, blurred vision, and difficulty with balance and coordination for the past few months. Examination shows cranial nerve deficits and ataxia. MRI confirms the diagnosis of newly diagnosed diffuse intrinsic brain stem glioma. The tumor is predominantly located in the pons and the tumor origin is clearly in the pons. There is no diffuse brain stem enlargement secondary to neurofibromatosis or diffuse leptomeningeal disease. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or biologic therapy. The Karnofsky score is 80%. The patient's family has been informed about the clinical trial and has given their consent for their child to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COPD for the last 5 years. He is a current smoker and has smoked an average of half a pack a day for the past 10 years, resulting in a 15 pack year smoking history. He has experienced chronic bronchitis symptoms such as coughing, wheezing and shortness of breath, which have significantly impacted his quality of life. He has not experienced any COPD exacerbation or respiratory tract infection requiring antibiotics or oral steroids or hospitalization within the last 6 weeks. He is not currently receiving chronic, daily, systemic steroids. The patient has undergone HRCT and has not been diagnosed with severe emphysema. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is fully aware of the potential risks and benefits of participation.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath for the past few months. She has a history of cold sensitivity and has noticed that her symptoms are worse during colder months. She visited her doctor and was diagnosed with primary cold agglutinin disease (CAD) based on a polyspecific direct antiglobulin test (DAT) positive, monospecific DAT strongly positive for C3d, cold agglutinin titer >= 64 at 4 degree Celsius, and immunoglobulin G (IgG) DAT less than or equal to (<=) 1+. Her hemoglobin level was found to be 9.5 g/dL, and her bilirubin level was slightly elevated. She has no overt malignant disease, and her weight is 70 kg. She has not received a blood transfusion within the past 3 months and has not been treated with rituximab monotherapy within 3 months, or rituximab combination therapies (example, with bendamustine, fludarabine, ibrutinib, or cytotoxic drugs) within 6 months prior to enrollment. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of BIVV009 (Sutimlimab) in primary CAD without a recent history of blood transfusion.

A 62-year-old woman with a history of osteoarthritis presents with pain and swelling in her left hip joint. She underwent a left total hip arthroplasty 2 years ago due to severe degenerative changes. The patient reports that her pain has been progressively getting worse over the past 4 months and is now affecting her ability to walk and perform daily activities. She has no fever or chills. Physical examination reveals tenderness and swelling over the left hip joint with restricted range of motion. Blood tests show slightly elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein levels. The patient is scheduled for a presumed aseptic revision arthroplasty, and the diagnostic efficacy of the quantitative electrochemical LE biosensor will be assessed to rule out periprosthetic joint infection (PJI).

A 50-year-old female with a history of non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) was previously treated with platinum-containing systemic therapy but progressed on or after that treatment. She has no known mutations in her tumor and has not received any prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy. The patient is currently experiencing difficulty breathing and has a measurable lesion according to RECIST version 1.1. She has no active brain or leptomeningeal metastases, autoimmune diseases, interstitial lung disease, non-infectious pneumonitis or active pulmonary tuberculosis. She has no history of Grade ≥3 immune mediated AE and is negative for hepatitis B or C, HIV/AIDS, and other potentially metastatic malignancy within the past 5 years. The patient is willing to provide an archived tumor tissue sample taken within the past 2 years or provide a fresh tumor biopsy sample. Her renal, liver, thyroid, and bone marrow function are adequate, and her performance status is 1. She is capable of receiving study treatment for at least 8 weeks.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of bothersome tinnitus that he has been experiencing for the past six months. He describes the sound as a constant buzzing in his right ear that makes it difficult for him to focus on his daily activities. He has been evaluated by an audiologist who confirmed the presence of tinnitus. He reports having no prior meditation experience and is willing to utilize his own smart device or computer for the study. The patient reports no history of anxiety or depression and is able to sit or lie down for at least 30 minutes at a time. He has access to both data and Wi-Fi.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU with respiratory failure due to severe pneumonia. The patient has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. The patient is currently intubated and is expected to require mechanical ventilation for at least 72 hours. The patient is able to operate the push-button device for patient-controlled sedation and has adequate hand strength and cognition. The patient does not have any aggressive ventilatory support needs or any conditions prohibiting the use of the push-button device. The patient has given their consent to participate in the trial.

This is a 45 year-old female with a history of breast cancer. She was initially diagnosed 2 years ago with stage II breast cancer and underwent lumpectomy followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She remained disease-free for 18 months until she noticed a lump in her left breast. Imaging studies confirmed metastatic disease to the liver and bones. She has not received any prior treatment with docetaxel, but has received one prior chemotherapy regimen. Her labs are within normal limits and she has no known bleeding or clotting disorders. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 19-year-old female with a diagnosis of moderate acne vulgaris on her face and back. She has tried various over-the-counter acne treatments with no significant improvement in her symptoms. She is not currently taking any prescription medications and has not used any topical or oral acne treatments in the past two weeks. She is willing to avoid excessive or prolonged exposure to ultraviolet light throughout the study. She is not currently using birth control pills for acne control.

A 30-year-old male who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He works as a software developer and takes no medications. He has no known allergies and has no family history of medical conditions. He is willing to follow the specific methods of contraception required for the study. He has no history of liver disease or any other significant chronic medical conditions.

Patient is a 35-year-old Japanese man who has been diagnosed with atopic dermatitis since childhood. He has moderate eczema-like changes with a chronic or chronically relapsing course. He experiences moderate to severe itching at night or during the day, with 10% to 50% of his body surface area involved. He has not used non-steroid immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory agents within the last four weeks, nor has he used systemic corticosteroids within the last four weeks. He does not have any known malignancy or other skin conditions that would interfere with the assessment of atopic dermatitis. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any severe, progressive, or uncontrolled medical conditions.

A 5-month-old baby boy was born prematurely at 30 weeks gestation. He suffered from a grade II intraventricular hemorrhage and required ventilator support for 2 weeks. He was discharged from the hospital after 2 months and has been meeting his developmental milestones. However, his parents noticed that he favors using his right hand and does not use his left hand as much. They brought him to a specialist who diagnosed him with mild asymmetry and suggested enrolling him in a clinical trial investigating the effect of Baby-CIMT on infants younger than 12 months. The baby has no other underlying medical conditions and is otherwise healthy.

50-year-old male scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia with orotracheal intubation. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He denies any history of difficult intubation or airway problems. Physical examination reveals no facial anomalies or abnormalities. The patient has a normal range of motion of the temporomandibular joint and can open his mouth widely. He is able to perform the Upper Lip Bite Test, which evaluates the ability to cover the mucosa of the upper lip with the lower incisor, without difficulty. The Modified Mallampati classification is also performed and the patient is classified as Class 1, indicating easy visualization of the oropharynx. The patient is excluded from the study if he requires rapid sequence induction or has any facial anomalies.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman from the United States who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer that has metastasized to her brain. She has undergone whole brain radiation therapy in the past and has been on chemotherapy for the past 3 months. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she has adequate bone marrow, renal, and liver function. She has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. Her CNS metastases are accessible for reservoir placement, and she has at least one measurable CNS metastasis that is at least 10 mm per RANO-BM criteria. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and has no known immunodeficiency, active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the past 2 years, or history of active tuberculosis, human immunodeficiency virus, or active hepatitis B or C infection. She has not received any other investigational agents or systemic steroid therapy greater than 10 mg prednisone or equivalent in the past 7 days. She is not pregnant or lactating and is using adequate contraception. She is able to return for required visits and follow-up exams.

A 53-year-old female was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer after presenting with a palpable mass in her right breast that was confirmed to be ER/PR positive and HER2-negative on biopsy. Imaging studies revealed multiple bone metastases. The patient is currently initiating first line therapy for ER/PR positive, HER2-negative MBC. She has no history of other active malignancies or ongoing infections. Her renal, hematologic and hepatic function are within normal limits. The patient has provided a signed informed consent to participate in this clinical trial in Greece.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with grade 2 follicular lymphoma four years ago. She underwent first-line treatment with chemotherapy and achieved a partial response. She subsequently underwent autologous stem cell transplantation and had a complete response. She has been receiving rituximab maintenance therapy since then. Recently, she has been experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. PET-CT scan showed disease progression and biopsy confirmed relapse of follicular lymphoma. She is now being evaluated for potential enrollment in this clinical trial to receive further treatment after relapse following ASCT.

A 12-year-old Caucasian boy with Friedreich Ataxia (FA) experiences difficulty walking and frequently falls. He was diagnosed with FA at the age of 8, and his genetic confirmation showed biallelic for a GAA repeat length of 59 in intron 1 of FXN. He has also been experiencing dysarthria, and his vision has been worsening over the past year. He is homeschooled because of his condition, and his parents are his primary caregivers. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he is not on any medication. He is interested in participating in clinical trials to help researchers better understand FA and find a cure for the disease. He is accompanied by his parents, who have provided written informed consent for his participation in the TRACK-FA study.

The patient is a 23-year-old male diagnosed with cystic fibrosis (CF) at the age of 5. He has a confirmed diagnosis of CF based on a positive sweat chloride test and a genotype with 2 identifiable mutations consistent with CF. He has a history of chronic infection with P. aeruginosa and has had 3 documented positive cultures in the prior 2 years. The study is seeking children aged 6 months to 5 years who have been admitted to Mulago hospital and diagnosed with cerebral malaria according to the World Health Organization (WHO) case definition. The child must have peripheral asexual P.falciparum parasitaemia and be in an unarousable coma lasting more than 30 minutes after a seizure, with no other causes of coma. Patients with recent diarrhea (more than 4 motions/24 hours), any recent anal pathology (such as rectal bleeding, rectal prolapse), or documented quinine treatment in the previous 48 hours will be excluded. The study will involve a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to compare the efficacy of intrarectal versus intravenous quinine for the treatment of childhood cerebral malaria.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at birth. This is a 5-year-old girl diagnosed with McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS). She has been experiencing early puberty with breast development, menstruation, and rapid growth. The patient is eligible to participate in a clinical trial to test the safety and effectiveness of letrozole in treating her precocious puberty and MAS. She will undergo a complete physical examination and blood/urine tests, as well as evaluations of her general health, growth, bone development, endocrine system status, and PFD status. A hand X-ray will be taken at the first visit and every 6 months to measure bone age advance. The patient will begin taking letrozole at the second visit and continue the drug for 6 months. She will be evaluated after 3 months and 6 months on the drug, and again after 3 months and 6 months after stopping treatment. Her parents will keep a record of all episodes of menstrual bleeding and any other symptoms or complaints. If her condition improves, she will be offered another 12 months of letrozole treatment.

The patient is a 32-year-old male complaining of severe constipation that has been ongoing for over 6 months. He reports difficulty passing stools, which are often hard and dry. 29-year-old female with aggressive fibromatosis (desmoid tumor) diagnosed one year ago presented with recurrent disease despite previous surgical intervention and radiation. The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years. 52-year-old male with a history of angina and a recent diagnosis of hypercholesterolemia. 35-year-old male with a history of multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosed 5 years ago. The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 5 years. She has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit 10 years ago. A 23 year old female has been diagnosed with moderate to severe asthma for the past 5 years. She has been using an inhaled corticosteroid at a dose of 250 mcg/day fluticasone propionate inhalation. A 52-year-old man presents with complaints of loud snoring, excessive daytime sleepiness, and frequent morning headaches. He has a history of being overweight and has a BMI of 30. Peripheral venous blood is drawn from the patient for the numeration of CD4+CD25+FoxP3+ regular T cells by flow cytometry and the CD4+CD25+ regular T cells are enriched by MACS and tested for their suppressive functions on proliferation assays. The patient is a 56-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the head-and-neck (SCCHN). The patient underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of SCCHN. A 32-year old software engineer with good oral health is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has no history of thyroid disorders or any other chronic illness. A 55-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of metastatic melanoma with widespread metastases to the liver, lungs, and bones. 45-year-old male with a history of primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) for the past 2 years. The patient has been on low-dose corticosteroids to manage the risk of bleeding. Patient is a 47-year-old man who was diagnosed with advanced stage lung cancer with metastases to the liver and bones. The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been suffering from major depression for the past two years. 62-year-old post-menopausal woman with a recent diagnosis of primary breast cancer. A 58 year old woman who underwent unilateral total hip arthroplasty (THA) with a non-cemented prosthesis 7 months ago due to severe hip osteoarthritis. The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking. A 60-year-old post-menopausal female with a history of surgically treated hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer. 27yo female with no significant past medical history, presenting to the dentist for extraction of impacted mandibular third molars. She has no significant medical history and is a non-smoker. She has not taken any analgesics for the pain in the past 24 hours. On examination, there is no swelling or erythema in the area. The tooth has extensive caries and a pulp exposure is noted. The pulp is necrotic and the radiograph shows no periapical pathology. The patient is informed about the trial and consents to participate. She is given a pain scale chart to rate her pain level before and after the endodontic treatment. She is randomly assigned to the intervention group and her root canal will be irrigated with 5 ml of curcumin solution. The endodontic treatment is performed and the tooth is obturated. The patient is informed to record her postoperative pain level at 8, 24 and 48 hours using the pain scale chart provided.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has had two falls in the past year. She is concerned about her bone health as her mother had osteoporosis. She has had a bone mineral density test within the past year which showed low bone density. She is interested in participating in a study that focuses on exercise interventions to improve posture and sarcopenic indices. She is able to understand and complete the study interventions and is willing to participate in follow-up visits. She is able to stand and walk unaided and has no hearing, visual, or cognitive problems.

The patient is a 65-year-old female who recently underwent uncomplicated cataract surgery 3 weeks ago. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which she takes lisinopril and atorvastatin, respectively. She presents with blurry vision and decreased visual acuity in her right eye. Her best-corrected visual acuity in the right eye is 20/60. She has no other ocular history and has not used any topical or systemic NSAIDs or corticosteroids in the past 14 days. Her ocular examination reveals pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (CME) with a central subfield thickness of 300 microns on OCT. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive treatment for the CME in her right eye.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. He is currently hospitalized due to the severity of his illness and has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fever. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. His BMI is 32, and he has a sedentary lifestyle. He is married and lives with his wife and two children. He works as a manager in a local retail store and has been on sick leave for the last two weeks. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is currently receiving oxygen therapy but has not required mechanical ventilation. The patient is able to change positions from supine to prone without assistance. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was involved in a high velocity road traffic collision. On arrival at the emergency department, he complained of minor head and neck pain but was able to communicate well with the medical staff. He had no apparent injuries to his chest, abdomen, or pelvis on physical examination. His Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score was 15. A whole body computed tomography (WBCT) was performed as part of the standard protocol for high velocity RTC victims. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no opposition to the use of his CT-scan for research purposes. He is not currently under legal protection or incarcerated.

Patient A is a 60-year-old male who was diagnosed with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) 2 years ago. He participated in Study CN002003 and completed the treatment. He has no new medical information or diagnoses since enrollment into Study CN002003 that might confer doubt on the PSP diagnosis. He has a reliable caregiver who accompanies him to study visits and has frequent contact with him. He is able to tolerate Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and perform all protocol-specified assessments. He resides outside a skilled nursing facility or dementia care facility at the time of enrollment. He has no contraindication to undergoing a lumbar puncture (LP) or the MRI examination. He has not been treated with any investigational drugs (including placebo) other than BIIB092 or placebo given in Study CN002003 or devices within 90 days prior to enrollment. He has not received any vaccination within 30 days prior to study drug administration. He has no known history of human immunodeficiency virus. He does not have any evidence of organ dysfunction or significant deterioration from prior values in CN002003 beyond what is consistent with the target population or that would place the patient at increased risk or risk of early study discontinuation. He is able to tolerate venipuncture and/or tolerate venous access.

A 32-year-old woman, who has been trying to conceive for 2 years, is scheduled for frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET) at an IVF unit. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no significant past surgical history. She has a regular menstrual cycle with a 28-day cycle length. She has undergone ovarian stimulation with gonadotropins and had an egg retrieval procedure, which resulted in 5 mature eggs. After fertilization, 3 of the embryos developed into high-quality blastocysts, and one was transferred during the fresh cycle. The remaining two blastocysts were cryopreserved for future transfer. She is now scheduled for FET, and the physician has proposed participation in a clinical trial evaluating the effects of modified luteal support on FET success rate. The patient is willing to participate and meet the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 35-year-old woman who had a cesarean section delivery 3 years ago presented to the clinic with complaints of abnormal uterine bleeding. She reported heavy bleeding during her menstrual cycle, which lasts for more than 7 days, and spotting between periods. She denies any pregnancy or use of intrauterine or hormonal contraceptives. She has a history of anemia but her complete blood count shows normal parameters apart from low hemoglobin. She is not using any medications that affect her coagulation profile. On pelvic ultrasonography, there are no abnormalities such as benign or malignant tumors, ovarian cysts or tumors. She has no evidence of cervical abnormalities upon examination or cervical smears. She has agreed to undergo office hysteroscopy for further evaluation.

A 55-year-old woman has been experiencing joint pain and stiffness for the past six months, particularly in her hands and knees. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers but has not found any relief. She is physically active and exercises regularly, but the joint pain is limiting her ability to do her usual activities. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any prescription medications. The patient has been referred by her primary care physician to the musculoskeletal (MSK) Triage Clinic in Rheumatology for further evaluation and management of her joint pain. She is able to answer study questionnaires independently and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no red flag conditions, inflammatory disease, or non-musculoskeletal conditions. She is 18 years or older and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 35-year-old female with a diagnosis of acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (aTTP), requiring plasma exchange (PE) as treatment. She has no known history of bleeding disorders, hypertension, or chronic renal impairment. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to accept an acceptable contraceptive regimen. She has not participated in any investigational drug or device within the past 30 days and is not currently participating in any other clinical study. She is able to provide signed and dated informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with a lung nodule that requires surgical intervention. She has a history of mild asthma and has been using an inhaler on an as-needed basis. She is currently taking no medications and has no other significant medical history. The patient is otherwise healthy and has a normal BMI. She has been scheduled for a lobectomy and will require one lung ventilation during the procedure. She has been informed about the study and has provided written consent to participate.

The patient is a 12-year-old male who has been diagnosed with heart failure and is currently being treated at the Phoenix Children's Hospital Heart Failure Clinic. He has a past medical history of congenital heart disease and has undergone multiple surgical interventions to correct his heart defect. He presents with symptoms of fatigue, shortness of breath, and edema in his lower extremities. On physical examination, his heart rate is 110 beats/min, blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and respiratory rate is 24 breaths/min. He has jugular venous distension and crackles in his lungs upon auscultation. Laboratory results show elevated BNP levels and decreased cardiac output. The patient is being managed with diuretics, inotropes, and vasodilators. The NIRS device will be used to monitor the patient's cardiac output in real-time during outpatient visits to the heart failure clinic.

16-year-old female with a diagnosis of anorexia nervosa, currently being treated by a multidisciplinary team including a psychiatrist, dietitian and therapist. Patient is experiencing amenorrhea and is not currently on any hormonal contraceptives. Patient has no history of thrombophlebitis, thromboembolytic disorders, hypercoagulation disorders, cerebral vascular or coronary artery disease, uncontrolled hypertension, migraines with focal aura, benign or malignant liver tumor, known or suspected carcinoma of any body system, or diabetes mellitus with vascular involvement. Patient does not have a recent history of alcohol or substance abuse and is not suicidal. Patient is willing to use a reliable non-hormonal alternate method of birth control during the study.

A 45-year-old male presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath, cough, and fever for the past 5 days. He has no significant past medical history, takes no medications, and has no known allergies. He reports no recent travel outside of the country but states that he works as a cashier in a grocery store and has been in contact with many customers over the past week. His initial vital signs show a temperature of 38.5°C, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 91% on room air. Physical examination reveals bilateral crackles on lung auscultation. Chest X-ray shows bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. The patient is admitted to the RECOP unit for further evaluation and management of his dyspnea.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who recently received a breast cancer diagnosis. A biopsy showed that her tumor is ER-positive and HER2-negative. She is currently scheduled for surgery and has been advised to undergo neoadjuvant endocrine therapy before the procedure to increase her chances of breast conservation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore additional treatment options. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She has not undergone any previous cancer treatment. Her performance status is good and she has no active infections. She is postmenopausal and not currently taking any contraceptives. She is willing to undergo breast biopsies as required by the study protocol. She has no history of malabsorption or other gastrointestinal issues. Her blood tests show a creatinine clearance of >50 mL/min and normal liver function. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol.

A 62-year-old retired teacher who is an avid computer user is interested in participating in the HMP usability trial. She has no history of eye diseases or vision problems, but she wears reading glasses. She is currently not participating in any other clinical trials. She speaks and understands English fluently and is willing to sign the consent form and participate in the study.

25 year old healthy male with no significant past medical history, who is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He is not currently taking any medications, does not have any allergies or intolerances to medications, and has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last 6 weeks. He weighs 75 kg and has no planned surgeries or medical interventions in the planned study period. He is able to understand the purpose and nature of the study as well as the associated risks, and is willing to comply with the trial's safety demands.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is scheduled to undergo a caesarean section in the coming weeks due to a breech presentation of the baby. The patient is in good overall health and has no known drug allergies or intolerances. She has provided informed written consent to participate in this clinical trial, which aims to document the pharmacokinetics and metabolism of intravenous ketorolac administration in pregnant women after caesarean section. The patient will receive the standard dosing regimen of 30mg of ketorolac every 8 hours for one day, administered through an IV bolus. Blood samples will be collected at specific intervals after the drug administration and urine samples will also be collected. The patient has agreed to be available for a follow-up visit 6-12 weeks after delivery to allow for intra-subject PK comparison.

The patient is a 15-year-old female with a diagnosis of ADHD for the past 3 years. She is currently taking an FDA-approved standard ADHD medication but still experiences impulsive aggression (IA) behaviors, including physical and verbal outbursts towards herself and others. Her parents report that these behaviors are negatively impacting her school performance and social relationships, and they are concerned about her safety. She has a history of anxiety and depression but is currently stable on medication. She has no history of substance abuse, criminal behavior, or suicidal thoughts or attempts. Her family history is significant for ADHD in her mother and paternal grandfather but no history of IA. Her lab work is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her IA behaviors and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was recently hospitalized due to his first episode of chest pain accompanied by shortness of breath, nausea and sweating. He was diagnosed with unstable angina and underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed significant stenosis in his left anterior descending artery. He underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention with stent placement. He was discharged from the hospital with a prescription for antiplatelet and lipid-lowering medications. The patient is a smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle. He works as an office clerk and is on sick leave due to his hospitalization. He is motivated to improve his health and is willing to participate in a cardiac rehabilitation program.

Patient is a 56-year-old man from the United States who was recently hospitalized with chest pain and diagnosed with non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but no prior history of heart disease or surgery. He is currently on medications for hypertension and cholesterol management. The patient is scheduled to undergo a conventional angiogram to assess his heart and its arteries. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meet the inclusion criteria of high risk NSTE-ACS and planned conventional invasive coronary angiography. However, the patient does not have renal insufficiency, allergy to contrast agent, refractory angina requiring urgent/emergent coronary angiography, contraindication to radiation exposure, or any other exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who recently sustained an ankle sprain while playing basketball. He reports feeling pain and swelling in his ankle, and difficulty putting weight on it. The patient has not sought medical attention for the injury and has been self-treating with rest, ice, compression, and elevation. The patient does not have a history of ankle or foot injuries or surgeries, and is otherwise healthy. He is able to bear weight on the affected ankle but experiences pain and stiffness when doing so. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his ankle function and reduce pain.

A 35-year-old female with a family history of colon cancer was referred for an outpatient colonoscopy. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She reports occasional constipation and occasional abdominal discomfort, but no rectal bleeding. She has never had a colonoscopy before. The patient is a non-smoker and consumes a healthy diet with adequate fiber intake. She is not pregnant and has no history of major psychiatric disorders. She has not undergone any abdominal surgeries in the past. The patient is fully informed about the study and has provided written consent to participate. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria for the study.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of gallstones and recurrent biliary colic, scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She has a past medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with amlodipine. She denies any known drug allergies or adverse reactions to anesthesia. She has never undergone any surgical procedures before and is anxious about the upcoming surgery. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her baseline laboratory studies, including liver and kidney function tests, are within normal limits.

A 23-year-old female college student with a history of dry eye syndrome for the past year. She reports experiencing burning, itchiness, and redness in her eyes, especially during long hours of studying and computer use. She has tried several over-the-counter eye drops with minimal relief. She wears glasses and has no known ocular or systemic conditions. Her OSDI score is 22, NBUT is 3 seconds, Schirmer 1 test is 8mm, and lipid layer grade is 2. She has no known allergies to any of the ingredients in Liposic or Tears Naturale Forte.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath and a persistent cough for the last 6 months. He has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. He has never been diagnosed with any lung disease before. His physical examination was unremarkable except for bilateral crackles heard on auscultation. Pulmonary function tests revealed a restrictive pattern with an FVC of 70% predicted and a DLCO of 40% predicted. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) scan of the chest showed diffuse interstitial fibrosis with honeycombing in both lungs, consistent with a diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). He is currently taking pirfenidone, which has not improved his symptoms. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially improve his quality of life and slow the progression of his disease.

The patient is a healthy individual between the ages of 18 and 55 years old. They have no evidence or history of any clinically significant diseases. They may be male or female and are willing to participate in a study to estimate the effects of food and sprinkling ALO-02 pellets on applesauce on the bioavailability of oxycodone and naltrexone/6-beta-naltrexol from an extended release pellets-in-capsule formulation of oxycodone 40 mg with sequestered naltrexone 4.8 mg. The patient is willing to comply with study requirements and is able to provide informed consent.

A 42-year-old female came to the clinic with a confirmed diagnosis of chronic plaque-type psoriasis, which was diagnosed 2 years ago. She has been experiencing moderate-to-severe psoriasis, with PASI score of 16 and BSA involvement of 12%. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial for a new drug, AUR101, which is expected to treat her condition. She does not have a history of erythrodermic, guttate or pustular psoriasis in the last 12 months. She has not been treated with any biologics for psoriasis in the past. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has never used phototherapy for psoriasis. She does not have any history of major surgery, alcohol or drug abuse, malignancy, and organ dysfunction. She has no history of tuberculosis, HIV, Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C. She is not pregnant or lactating and uses reliable contraceptive methods. She has not received another new chemical entity/investigational drug within the last 28 days. She is willing to adhere to the study restrictions and assessments schedule and sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 22-year-old male with moderate inflammatory acne on his face, chest, and back. The patient has been experiencing acne for the past year and is frustrated with the lack of improvement despite trying various over-the-counter products. He is currently not taking any medication for his acne. The patient has a stable weight and enjoys playing basketball with his friends twice a week. He eats a lot of fast food and sugary drinks due to his busy schedule as a full-time college student and part-time employee at a fast-food chain. His BMI is 24.5 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any other medications. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial as he is motivated to improve his acne and is willing to make dietary changes.

A 62-year-old woman has been experiencing severe knee pain and limited mobility due to osteoarthritis, and has failed conservative management. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in surgical intervention to improve her quality of life and has been advised by her orthopedic surgeon to undergo primary unilateral TKA using MPS-Flex® Total Knee Joint Prostheses. She meets the inclusion criteria for this study, including being between the ages of 18 to 75 years old, having a diagnosis of severe knee pain and disability due to osteoarthritis, and being willing and able to complete scheduled study procedures and follow-up evaluations. The patient is not excluded from the study as she does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including having a contraindication to the product or a diagnosed systemic disease that could affect her safety or the study outcome. She is willing to provide written informed consent and participate in the study, with the hope that it will provide valuable information on the safety and efficacy of MPS-Flex® Total Knee Joint Prostheses in primary TKA.

63-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of incurable stage IV ovarian cancer. Currently experiencing symptoms of anxiety related to her diagnosis and upcoming chemotherapy treatment. Past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. The patient has no prior history of psychiatric illness, substance abuse, or cognitive impairment. The patient is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin with no known adverse effects. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve the quality of life for patients with advanced cancer who are experiencing anxiety symptoms through brief cognitive-behavioral therapy. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to complete study procedures.

A 12-year-old boy was brought to the clinic by his parents who are concerned about his recent behavior. They report that he has been having mood swings, irritability, and aggressive behavior towards his siblings and friends. They also report that he has difficulty sleeping, often wakes up in the middle of the night, and has a decreased appetite. The parents have taken him to see a psychiatrist who diagnosed him with bipolar disorder. The boy is currently taking medication, but his symptoms are not improving. The parents are interested in enrolling him in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. The boy will undergo a comprehensive evaluation by medical doctors with a specialty in this area, and if found eligible, will be treated with N-acetylcysteine (NAC) as part of a 12-week open-label study. The boy will be required to attend weekly visits to closely monitor his response to the medication. The study-related evaluations and visits will be provided at no cost to the family.

A 35 year old woman was diagnosed with AML and underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation (aHSCT) to control the disease. She achieved complete remission after the transplantation, but was found to be MRD positive anytime between day 100 and day 365 post-aHSCT. She has tapered off immunosuppressive medications at least two weeks prior to study entry. She has no history of severe hypersensitivity reactions to any ingredient of study drug(s) or monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and/or their excipients. She has no active Hepatitis B (HBV) or Hepatitis C (HCV) infection. She does not have active acute or chronic graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) of the lungs. She has no history of another primary malignancy that is currently clinically significant or currently requires active intervention. She has no concurrent severe and/or active uncontrolled infection requiring parenteral antibacterial, antiviral or antifungal therapy. She is willing to undergo bone marrow aspirate sample collection for MRD testing. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and no other concurrent severe and/or uncontrolled medical conditions.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with stage IV colorectal cancer with metastasis to the liver and lungs. He has no prior history of cancer and has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy yet. He is currently experiencing mild abdominal pain, bloating, and occasional rectal bleeding. His physical exam is remarkable for mild tenderness in the lower abdomen. His performance status is ECOG 1, and he has no major comorbidities. He has no known history of HIV, hepatitis B or C, and he is not a transplant recipient. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who suffered a mandibular angle fracture due to a recent car accident. He has been evaluated by a maxillofacial surgeon and requires open reduction and internal fixation surgery to repair the fracture. He is a non-smoker, has no history of chronic-degenerative diseases or collagen disorders. He is covered by the Mexican Institute of Social Security and has consented to participate in this clinical trial.

A 26-year-old female college student came to the clinic complaining of frequent mood swings, suicidal ideation, and a history of self-injury. She has been experiencing these symptoms for at least 2 years and has had difficulty maintaining healthy relationships. She has been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder by a licensed psychiatrist and has completed some therapy sessions in the past with little improvement in her symptoms. She is currently not on any medication for her condition. She is willing to participate in the study and lives within a reasonable driving distance of Iowa City, IA.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing claustrophobia for the past 2 years. She reports feeling intense anxiety and fear when entering small or enclosed spaces, such as elevators or planes. Her fear has limited her daily activities and has caused her to avoid situations where she might feel trapped. She has never received any treatment for her claustrophobia. She does not take any psychotropic medications, and she has no history of panic disorder, agoraphobia, or PTSD. She has no medical conditions that would make it dangerous for her to experience heightened emotions or arousal. She is proficient in English and meets the criteria for high claustrophobic fear, as demonstrated by her self-report of moderate anxiety (score of at least 2 out of 4) when lying down in a small dark chamber without windows for several minutes. She also endorsed claustrophobia according to the DSM-5 criteria for Specific Phobia, with a self-reported fear rating at or exceeding 50/100 fear while in the chamber. She weighs less than 250 lbs and is under 6 feet 5 inches in height, meeting the maximum capacity for the claustrophobic chamber. She has not participated in any professional treatment for claustrophobia in the past year and has not changed her psychotropic medication dose in the past 3 months. She is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 67-year-old man diagnosed with prostate cancer two years ago. The cancer has metastasized to his bones, liver and lungs. He has previously undergone chemotherapy with docetaxel and is currently on hormone therapy with leuprolide. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies. He lives with his wife and has two adult children. He reports increasing fatigue and mild pain in his lower back and hips. His PSA level has been rising slowly over the past few months. His ECOG performance status is 1. His most recent CT and bone scans showed progression of his disease. He has not started any new treatment since the progression was detected. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing sexual dysfunction for the past year. She reports difficulty with arousal, lubrication, and achieving orgasm during sexual activity with her partner. She has no history of gynecologic surgery or pelvic organ prolapse. She is not currently pregnant and has no neurological disease. The patient has no known anatomical defects. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her sexual function and is willing to try vaginal electrical stimulation as a potential treatment option.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who has been smoking cannabis regularly for the past three years. He has noticed that he has been having difficulty controlling his use and has experienced cravings for the drug. He has tried to quit in the past but has been unsuccessful. He has no other current or lifetime psychiatric disorders and is not currently on any medication. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to understand the neurobiological basis of addiction and how executive function deficits and craving contribute to substance use. He is willing to undergo whole-brain imaging exams and complete mobile assessments of his daily life executive fluctuations, craving, and substance use. The patient is affiliated with health insurance and is able to provide informed consent.

A 45-year-old Caucasian male presents to the hospital with a diagnosis of multiple myeloma. He has been referred for a bone marrow biopsy and aspiration. The patient is in good clinical condition with an ECOG score of 1, and has no history of allergies to Xylocaïne. He has not been exposed to nitrous oxide previously. He is not pregnant and has no neurological illnesses or significant respiratory disease. He is not on any antidepressant medications or analgesia for other medical conditions. He has normal platelet function and no coagulation disorders. The patient provides informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 54-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was referred to the transplant center for evaluation for lung transplantation. The patient has been struggling with shortness of breath and chronic cough for several years. His pulmonary function tests showed severe obstruction with a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 25% predicted. The patient has been on maximal medical therapy, including oxygen therapy, and pulmonary rehabilitation for the past year with minimal improvement in his symptoms. After an extensive evaluation, he was deemed as a suitable candidate for lung transplantation. The patient underwent bilateral lung transplantation and had an uneventful surgery. He was discharged on postoperative day 10 with no major complications. The patient is now being followed up regularly at the transplant clinic per protocol. As part of the follow-up visits, the patient will be asked to provide exhaled breath, blood specimens, bronchoalveolar lavage and biopsies at specific time points to identify possible biomarkers that will predict the development of PGD and/or CLAD. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital due to acute kidney injury. The patient has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, which are well-controlled with medication. He has no history of kidney disease, but he has recently been experiencing fatigue and decreased appetite. Upon admission, laboratory tests showed elevated creatinine levels and decreased urine output. The patient is not on hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis. He is not currently taking any nutritional supplements. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 9-year-old male student residing in Handeni District Council, Tanzania, is being screened for enrollment in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria using dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine. The student is in class five and has no known history of heart disease or cardiac ailment. The student weighs 20 kg and has no severe infections or conditions requiring hospitalization. The student has not participated in another investigational drug study within the last 30 days and is willing to undergo all study procedures, including physical examination and blood tests. The parent/guardian has provided informed consent and the student has provided assent. The student will be monitored for close follow-up throughout the study period.

A 49-year-old man presents with symptoms of severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), including loud snoring, frequent pauses in breathing, and excessive daytime sleepiness. He has been diagnosed with OSA for several years and has been prescribed continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. However, he finds the CPAP mask uncomfortable and has been unable to tolerate it for more than a few hours each night. Despite his efforts to lose weight and make lifestyle changes, his OSA symptoms persist, and his apnea hypopnea index (AHI) is consistently above 30. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, for which he takes medication. He is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and feasibility of pulmonary artery denervation (PADN) as a treatment for severe OSA.

An 11-year-old girl is seeking treatment for her pectus excavatum, a congenital chest wall abnormality that has caused her to feel self-conscious and uncomfortable in certain activities. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of bleeding disorders, heart disease, or respiratory conditions requiring steroid treatment. She is able to read, speak, and understand English. Her pectus severity index is 4.2, indicating a moderate-to-severe deformity that would benefit from operative intervention. She has undergone a hand/wrist x-ray that shows she is in early puberty, making her eligible for the trial. She and her parents have expressed willingness to follow the treatment protocol, including wearing the external brace and returning for regular follow-up visits. They have also obtained pre-approval from their insurance carrier.

Maria is a 42-year-old woman who works as a nurse. She has struggled with obesity for most of her adult life and has a body mass index (BMI) of 45. She has tried various diets and exercise regimes, but has not been able to achieve significant weight loss. She has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes, but she herself does not have any other significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is currently taking a daily multivitamin and calcium supplement. She has been referred to the UNMC Bariatric Center for a sleeve gastrectomy procedure. She is interested in participating in the Healthy Body, Healthy Bones After Bariatric Surgery Trial to help prevent bone loss associated with the procedure. Her lab studies and physical exam showed no signs of liver or renal disease. She has a serum 25-OH vitamin D level of 28 ng/mL, and has no history of bone-modifying disorders or autoimmune disease impacting bone. She is not taking any bone-active medications and has no known sensitivity to bisphosphonates. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and assessments.

A 65-year-old male patient was admitted to the rehabilitation unit after experiencing a right-sided ischemic stroke. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. The patient was able to speak and follow commands, but he had weakness and spasticity in his right upper and lower extremities. He was able to walk with assistance, but he required assistance for activities of daily living. The patient underwent a comprehensive rehabilitation program, which included physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy. The patient received rehabilitation for four months before being discharged. He was able to walk independently with a cane, and his spasticity had improved. However, he still required some assistance with activities of daily living. The patient will be eligible for this clinical trial as he received rehabilitation in an inpatient clinic for more than three months.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and chest pain for the last month. He has a history of smoking for over 30 years and quit 5 years ago. A chest X-ray showed a mass in the right lung, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of squamous non-small-cell lung cancer. CT scans also revealed regional lymph node metastases. He is ECOG 1 and has no prior chemotherapy, biological therapy, or immunotherapy. He has no brain metastases or uncontrolled pleural effusion. His blood tests show WBC of 5.8*10^9/L, ANC of 3.2*10^9/L, PLT of 180*10^9/L, Hb of 12.4 g/dL, serum bilirubin of 0.9 mg/dL, AST of 28 U/L, ALT of 32 U/L, and creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL. He meets all of the inclusion criteria and signs informed consent to participate in the study.

A 50-year-old male with a history of COPD and hypertension was admitted to the hospital due to severe pneumonia. The patient is currently being treated with invasive mechanical ventilation and is in need of antibiotics. The patient weighs 80 kg and is willing to participate in the clinical trial for the treatment of severe pneumonia. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has no history of facial trauma or surgery, deep venous thrombosis, cardiac pacemaker insertion, unstable spine, femur or pelvic fractures, or lung transplantation. The patient is not pregnant and has no chest tube with air leaks. The patient has not received inhaled nitric oxide or almitrine bismesylate before inclusion and has not undergone extracorporeal membrane oxygenation therapy before inclusion. The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for severe pneumonia and has not been placed in prone position before inclusion. The patient is not deprived of freedom, is not a minor, and is not under a legal protective measure. The patient has no opposition from next of kin.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa, a hereditary disease that causes gradual vision loss. She reports difficulty seeing in dimly lit environments and struggles with peripheral vision. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her vision is currently 20/50 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. She has been referred to the study by her ophthalmologist to receive high resolution retina imaging with the rtx1 camera to monitor the progression of her retinal disease.

No patient description is needed for this clinical trial as it is an observational study that will include all GO patients with a history of at least 10 years who come for a follow-up visit in the GO clinic over a period of 5 consecutive years. Therefore, there are no specific patient characteristics or criteria for this study.

The patient is a 32-year-old healthcare worker who has been working at Fundacion Valle del Lili for the past 3 years. Due to the recent outbreak of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), the patient has been exposed to patients with confirmed COVID-19. The patient is asymptomatic and has not experienced any symptoms related to COVID-19 in the past 14 days. The patient does not have a history of cardiac arrhythmias, epilepsy, kidney disease, seizures, and is not taking any of the concomitant medications that would exclude them from the study. The patient has not recently taken chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine in the last two weeks and is not known to have hypersensitivity to chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will receive chloroquine prophylaxis to assess the efficacy and safety of its use in preventing COVID-19 infections in healthcare workers.

A 42-year-old male patient with a history of cervical dystonia for the past 5 years came to the clinic seeking help for his condition. He has previously received botulinum toxin therapy for cervical dystonia and has not experienced any adverse side effects. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and comply with the follow-up schedule and protocol. He works as a software engineer and has no known allergies to device components or botulinum toxin. He does not have any medical comorbidities that preclude botulinum toxin therapy. He is able to understand and respond to the study.

A 27 year old primigravida woman who is currently 36 weeks pregnant and planning to breastfeed her baby. She has no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. She has attended all of her antenatal appointments and is looking for more information on breastfeeding to help her prepare for her new arrival. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare antenatal and postnatal breastfeeding education strategies.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who underwent laparoscopic appendectomy due to acute appendicitis. She has no past medical history of any systemic or gastric diseases. She does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. The patient has a preoperative Koivuranta vomiting score of 4, indicating a high risk of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). She has not experienced any nausea or vomiting prior to the surgery. The vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 80 bpm, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. She is alert and oriented, with no signs of discomfort or pain. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive treatment for PONV.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with T4 laryngeal cancer. He is a non-smoker and has no significant medical history. He is married with two children, works as a salesman and enjoys playing golf in his free time. He is concerned about the treatment options available and wants to make an informed decision. He has access to and is comfortable with using a computer and the internet. He speaks Dutch fluently and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with stage III hepatocellular carcinoma. He underwent curative surgery to remove the tumor, which was 6 cm in diameter and had no encapsulation. The tumor did not invade any blood vessels, but the pathology report showed that there were multiple satellite nodules present. The patient's performance status is ECOG 1, and he is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient has not received any chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the past, and his blood work showed normal levels of bilirubin, ALT, AST, and alkaline phosphatase. The patient has no serious concomitant illnesses that would be aggravated by the study medication, and he is not currently taking any medications. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits associated with the study medication. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of Lambert Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS). She was diagnosed with LEMS 3 years ago and has been treated with prednisone, azathioprine, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) with limited success. Despite treatment, she experiences frequent episodes of muscle weakness, especially in the arms and legs, which has affected her ability to work and perform daily activities. She has been unable to tolerate higher doses of prednisone due to side effects. She has undergone electrodiagnostic testing which confirmed the diagnosis of LEMS. She has no history of seizures, asthma, or prolonged QT syndrome. She has normal kidney and liver function tests. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial of 3,4-diaminopyridine (3,4-DAP) to help control her symptoms and reduce her need for other therapies. She understands the risks and benefits of the trial and has provided informed consent.

53 yo F with history of stage II breast cancer diagnosed in [**2-2016**] treated with lumpectomy, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy. Patient reports experiencing neuropathy in both hands and feet that has persisted since completing chemotherapy in [**9-2016**]. The neuropathy is described as a pins-and-needles sensation accompanied by numbness, which has limited the patient's ability to use her hands and walk normally. The patient has tried gabapentin and duloxetine, but neither medication provided relief from the symptoms. The patient is interested in trying acupuncture to alleviate the symptoms of neuropathy. Patient is otherwise healthy with no history of cardiac pacemaker, significant emotional or psychological disorder, diabetic or HIV-related neuropathy, or grade III lymphedema. Past Medical History: - Stage II breast cancer, treated with lumpectomy, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy in [**2-2016**] - Neuropathy in both hands and feet since completing chemotherapy in [**9-2016**], despite treatment with gabapentin and duloxetine - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Osteoarthritis of the knees - No history of cardiac pacemaker, significant emotional or psychological disorder, diabetic or HIV-related neuropathy, or grade III lymphedema

A 60-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of breast cancer came to the clinic for a follow-up visit. She had undergone surgery with a curative intent for stage II breast cancer 6 years ago and received adjuvant tamoxifen (20 mg/day) for 5 years. Her hormone receptor status was positive but she did not receive any chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She has been doing well since then, and has not experienced any cancer relapse. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent cancer recurrence and improve her chances of survival. She does not have any history of lipid disorders or other major comorbidities.

The patient is a healthy 28-year-old female of Asian descent with a body mass index (BMI) of 22. She has no history of allergies, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, haematological, endocrine, metabolic, mental, neurological, or other diseases. She is sexually active and using a highly effective method of birth control. She has not been pregnant, is not breastfeeding, and has no plans for pregnancy during the study period. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol regularly. She has no history of nasal surgery or abnormalities, rhinitis, or allergies. She is not a vegetarian and has no strict dietary habits that would preclude her acceptance of standardized meals. She is willing and able to give informed consent, have her personal study-related data collected, archived, or transmitted according to protocol, and cooperate adequately. She is available for study visits/procedures and not a vulnerable subject such as a person kept in detention. She has not been exposed to an investigational medicinal product within the last 3 months.

There is no patient involvement in this clinical trial as it is focused on improving surgical case duration accuracy by leveraging the EHR and predictive modeling. The study is specifically targeting surgeons and OR staff members in the Department of Surgery Gynecology and Colorectal service at the Main hospital or Josie Robertson Surgical Center. New surgeons who start their practice during the study and surgeries that take place at other locations will be excluded from the study. Additionally, cases where input data was not available prior to the prediction generation, including late add-on cases such as urgent and emergent cases that are placed on the schedule less than 24 hours before the surgery, will also be excluded from the study.

53-year-old female with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the endocrine clinic with a newly discovered left adrenal mass incidentally detected on a CT scan for evaluation of abdominal pain. The patient denies any symptoms related to adrenal gland disorders such as palpitations, headaches, sweating, or weight gain. Her only medication is amlodipine for her hypertension. She has no known allergies. Her physical exam is unremarkable. The patient has no history of smoking, alcohol use, or illicit drug use. She has no family history of adrenal or endocrine diseases. The patient has not undergone any prior surgeries or treatments for adrenal disorders. Her laboratory workup including serum electrolytes, CBC, CMP, and 24-hour urine cortisol and catecholamines were within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to further evaluate the functional status of her adrenal mass using a non-invasive approach.

8 year-old male scheduled for a distal midhumerus surgery under general anesthesia. The patient is ASA 2 and has received consent from his parents for regional analgesia.
