He has no known allergies to local anesthetics and does not have any infection on the local anesthetic application area. He has no history of brain tumors, central nervous system infections, anatomical difficulties, or coagulopathy. The patient does not have any syndromic conditions.

A 32-year-old woman was diagnosed with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) after experiencing amenorrhea and menopausal symptoms. She has been trying to conceive for the past year without success. She has no history of chemotherapy, surgery, or radiotherapy. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) injection into the ovary as a potential treatment for POI, and is willing to undergo laparoscopy for the injection. She is otherwise healthy and has no previous history of PRP treatment.

56-year-old male with a history of stable angina and a recent diagnosis of coronary artery disease. The patient is scheduled to undergo coronary angiography with possible PCI and planned use of at least one drug-eluting stent (DES). The patient has not undergone PCI within the previous 30 days and has no history of gastrointestinal bleeding within the last 6 months. The patient is not currently on coumadin anticoagulation or other thienopyridine class of ADP receptor inhibitors. The patient is willing and able to comply with study procedures and protocol, including required study visits. The patient has no severe allergy to stainless steel, contrast dye, unfractionated heparin, low molecular weight heparin, or bivalirudin that cannot be adequately pre-medicated. The patient is not enrolled in an investigational drug or device study that has not reached the time period of the primary endpoint. The patient has no history of thrombocytopenia or hematocrit abnormalities.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of knee pain and stiffness for the past 6 months. The pain is localized to the medial aspect of the right knee and is aggravated by weight-bearing activities. The patient has tried several conservative treatments including physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medications, but has not found significant relief. The patient underwent X-ray imaging and was diagnosed with grade II knee osteoarthritis. The patient reports tenderness on the medial tibial plateau and rates the intensity of pain as 7/10 on a visual analogue scale. The patient has no history of neurological or vestibular system disorders, systematic inflammatory disease, or steroid injections in the last six months. The patient has not undergone any knee surgery in the past.

Maria is a 32-year-old female who works as a nurse. She has been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and lack of interest in activities she used to enjoy for the past 3 weeks. She has difficulty sleeping and feels fatigued throughout the day. She denies any history of previous psychiatric disorders, neurological or ocular diseases, and has never been treated with any antidepressant medication before. She is in good overall health and her medical history is unremarkable. She has no history of smoking, alcohol or substance abuse. She is not currently taking any medication that may interact with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). Her family history is negative for any psychiatric or neurological disorders. Her ophthalmologic examination was normal. She was diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) by the Structured Clinical Interview for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders 5 / Clinical Version (SCID-5 / CV) and started on SSRI treatment. She has a Standardized Mini Mental Test (SMMT) score of 25. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the changes in retinal nerve fiber layer due to SSRI treatment in first-attack MD patients.

A 45-year-old healthy Caucasian male with a body mass index of 23 kg/m2, sitting blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg and a pulse rate of 70 bpm was screened for the study. He had a normal 12-lead ECG and had no history of serious adverse reactions or hypersensitivity to any drug. He did not have any allergies requiring acute or chronic treatment, except for seasonal allergic rhinitis. He had not consumed any prescription medication within 14 days or non-prescription medication within 7 days prior to the administration of the drug. He had not participated in any other clinical trials during the previous month in which an investigational drug or commercially available drug was tested. He had not lost more than 500 mL blood during the 3 month period before the study, nor did he have any surgical or medical condition that might interfere with the absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion of the drug. He had no symptoms of a significant somatic or mental illness in the 4 week period preceding drug administration. He had no history of hepatitis B and / or C, no positive serology results indicating the presence of hepatitis B and / or C, and no positive results from the HIV serology. His liver parameters (SGPT, SGOT) values were within the normal range, and he did not have any known hypersensitivity to BIA 9-1067. He was a non-smoker and had not been exposed to artificial ionizing radiation in the last 12 months. He had not traveled on more than 4 flights (with more than 2 hours flight time) within the last year prior to the administration of the drug.

A 45-year-old female diagnosed with stage III ovarian cancer is scheduled for major abdominal surgery. She has no significant medical history, and her American Society of Anesthesia (ASA) status is II. She has no known allergies to the study drugs, has no significant cardiac, respiratory, renal, or hepatic disease, and has a BMI of 27 kg/m2. She does not have any coagulation disorders, drug or alcohol abuse, or psychiatric illnesses that would interfere with perception and assessment of pain. She has been informed about the study and has provided written informed consent. She will be taught how to evaluate her own pain intensity using the visual analogue scale (VAS), scored from 0 -10 (where 0 = no pain, and 10 = the worst pain imaginable). She will be randomized to receive either intrathecal dexmedetomidine, ketamine or a combination of both with bupivacaine for postoperative analgesia. Her vital signs will be monitored, and VAS scores will be assessed at different time points. Postoperative adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, hypotension, and bradycardia will be recorded and treated.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing frequent headaches, nausea, and vomiting for the past few weeks. Further imaging showed an abnormal mass in his brain, and a biopsy confirmed that he has a grade IV glioblastoma multiforme. The tumor is unmethylated, so the patient is eligible for a clinical trial investigating a personalized neoantigen-based vaccine combined with immune checkpoint blockade therapy. He has not received any prior immunotherapy and is willing to undergo genome sequencing and provide germline and tumor DNA/RNA samples. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%, and his bone marrow and organ function are normal. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive medications, and he has not had any other malignancies in the past three years. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception during the trial and has provided informed consent. However, he has a history of allergic reactions to vaccines and compounds of similar composition to poly-ICLC, so his eligibility for the trial will need to be further evaluated.

The patient is a 45 year old man who has been struggling with his weight for a few years. He has a BMI of 30 and a waist-to-hip ratio of 0.90. His job requires him to sit in front of a computer for hours, leading to a sedentary lifestyle. He is married and has two children, and his wife is also overweight. He has tried different diets and exercise programs in the past, but they have not been successful in achieving long-term weight loss. He has no history of diabetes, hypertension or cardiovascular disease, and is not on any medication. He does not use laxatives or fiber supplements. He has not had bariatric surgery or used anti-obesity drugs in the past three months. He has not used antibiotics or probiotics in the past two months. He is not immunosuppressed and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 60 days. He is willing to follow a regular diet that is in agreement with the national dietary recommendations. He is interested in participating in this study as he hopes to gain control of his weight and improve his overall health.

A 31-year-old woman living in a rural village in Cameroon came to the clinic with complaints of swelling in her legs and face. Upon physical examination, the doctor noticed swelling in her arms, legs, and face. After conducting a blood test, the patient was diagnosed with a Loa loa infection, which is caused by small worms spread by the bite of a fly. The patient was found to have a low level of Loa loa parasites in the blood and is otherwise healthy. She has not taken any medication for Loa loa in the past six months and has not been on any immunosuppressive therapies, including steroids, for the past month. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of chronic kidney or liver disease, and her hemoglobin level is above 10 gm/dL. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and will be randomized to receive a single oral dose of either ivermectin or diethylcarbamazine citrate (DEC) in an inpatient setting in Cameroon. The patient will undergo regular blood samples and physical examinations after treatment to monitor for signs and symptoms and to assess the immunologic mechanisms of post-treatment reactions to the medications. The patient will also be followed up at 6 and 12 months post-hospitalization to determine whether she has experienced Loa-specific symptoms and will be offered a full treatment course if necessary.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman who has been married to her husband for 42 years. She is currently living with and caring for her husband, who was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease a year ago. She has been struggling with the demands and responsibilities of caregiving and is feeling overwhelmed and stressed. She has noticed that her own health has been declining and is concerned about her ability to continue providing care for her husband. She speaks English fluently and is able to participate in the study by telephone. She has no history of mental illness or cognitive impairment. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about self-care techniques and how to manage her own health and well-being while caring for her husband.

A 67-year-old man, previously healthy, was admitted to the hospital due to a sudden onset of right-sided hemiparesis and facial droop that started 3 days ago. He also complained of mild headache and blurred vision. Upon arrival, his blood pressure was 145/90 mmHg, pulse rate 85 bpm, respiratory rate 18 bpm, and temperature 37°C. Neurological examination revealed a right-sided hemiparesis and a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. The patient had a history of occasional palpitations but no history of atrial fibrillation or other significant medical conditions. CT scan of the brain showed a left middle cerebral artery (MCA) infarct. The patient was started on aspirin and statin therapy, and a 12-lead ECG was obtained, which showed sinus rhythm. The patient is now being considered for inclusion in a clinical trial to estimate the prevalence and prognostic significance of frequent premature atrial complexes (PACs) in ischemic stroke patients in relation to death, recurrent stroke, and atrial fibrillation. If included, the patient will undergo further examinations, including echocardiogram, blood sample, and CT scan of carotid arteries with contrast, to improve risk stratification and secondary prevention of ischemic stroke.

A 30-year-old woman with mild-to-moderate allergic asthma has a history of intermittent expiratory flow limitation. She is 5 feet 4 inches tall and weighs 140 pounds. She has been using inhaled beta-agonists for asthma management. Her baseline forced expiratory flow in one second (FEV1) is greater than 70% of predicted after bronchodilator use. She has a positive skin prick-puncture test to house dust mites and a positive inhaled methacholine challenge with a decrease in FEV1 of at least 20%. She has a normal complete blood count, PT, PTT, serum electrolytes, mineral and hepatic panels, EKG and chest radiograph without acute pulmonary infiltrates. She is not pregnant and is willing to adhere to reliable birth control methods during the study. She has no history of hypersensitivity to TNFR:Fc or lidocaine, and has not used theophylline, oral or inhaled corticosteroid, nedocromil sodium, cromolyn sodium, zilueton, leukotriene receptor antagonists, anti-histamines, hydroxyzine or tricyclic anti-depressants within the prior 3 months. She is a non-smoker, has no history of allergy immunotherapy within the past year or allergy to methacholine. She has tested negative for human immunodeficiency virus and hepatitis viruses. She has no history of Crohn's disease, central nervous system demyelinating disorders or hematologic disorders. She is not taking any immunosuppressive therapies for more than 6 months or cytoxic chemotherapeutic agents. She does not have a history of chronic heart failure or coronary artery disease, renal disease, or psoriasis.

The patient is a 73-year-old man who has been experiencing chest pain and difficulty breathing for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels, for which he takes medication. He also has a history of smoking, but quit 10 years ago. His echocardiogram showed severe aortic stenosis, and he has been referred for a transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) procedure. He has completed high school education and has no significant cognitive impairment (MMSE score is 28). He is willing to participate in the CLEVER-TAVR cohort study and has signed the informed consent form. His current medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He has no history of major surgeries or neurological disorders. His family history is negative for any significant cardiovascular or neurological problems. He is retired and lives with his wife who is his primary caregiver.

25 year-old healthy female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the tolerability of multiple doses of HKI-272. She has no significant medical history and is not currently on any medications. She has regular menstrual cycles and has no plans for pregnancy during the study period. The subject is within the age range of 18-50 and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and return to the treatment center for all required clinical evaluations.

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with abdominal pain and weight loss over the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which is well-controlled with medications. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. On physical examination, mild tenderness is noted in the epigastric region. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis reveals a 7 cm mass in the pancreas with multiple liver metastases. Biopsy of the pancreatic mass confirms a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor. His ECOG performance status is 1. Laboratory values within 2 weeks of enrollment show normal hemoglobin, platelet, and absolute neutrophil counts. His serum creatinine and bilirubin levels are within normal limits, and his AST/SGOT and ALT/SGPT levels are mildly elevated at twice the upper limit of normal due to liver metastases. His LVEF by TTE is 60%. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or immunotherapy. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 58-year-old man diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 3 years ago. He has been taking dopamine agonist for the past 6 months as part of his anti-parkinson treatment. Recently, he has been experiencing impulsive behaviors such as excessive shopping and gambling. His mMIDI score is 5, indicating the presence of ICD. He has no history of serious cognitive or behavioral disorders, mental illness, or dementia. His K-MMSE score is 27. He experiences motor fluctuations, but they are not severe enough to require treatment more than 6 times per day. He has no history of dyskinesia, DBS, or any other surgical treatment. He has no history of melanoma or any non-diagnostic skin trouble/skin lesions. He does not have narrow angle glaucoma or any clinically serious surgical or medical condition. He has no history of malignant tumors and is not using any other investigational drugs at the time of enrollment within 4 weeks. He is not pregnant, nursing, or lactating. He has no hypersensitivity or allergy to levodopa/carbidopa. In summary, the patient is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. She has no history of antiviral treatment and has persistently elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels and quantifiable HCV-RNA. The patient has undergone liver biopsy within the past 12 months which was consistent with CHC. She is diagnosed with insulin resistance and has been evaluated by HOMA-R and OGTT. The patient has a negative pregnancy test result. She does not have type 2 diabetes and has a BMI of 27. The patient does not consume alcohol. She does not have any other forms of liver disease, HIV infection, anemia, psychiatric disease, poorly controlled thyroid disease, overt cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma, significant cardiac, renal or pulmonary disease, or seizures. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of Pegylated-Interferon and Ribavirin plus metformin in the treatment of chronic HCV infection and insulin resistance.

Patient A is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with Hodgkin's disease. She has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and is now scheduled to undergo radiation therapy along with peripheral stem cell transplantation. She is in good general health and her Karnofsky performance score is 90%. Her blood work shows an absolute neutrophil count of 1,200/mm3 and a platelet count of 110,000/mm3. She has no history of heart disease or lung disease. She has never undergone bone marrow or peripheral stem cell transplantation before and is not receiving any concurrent chemotherapy or investigational agents. She is not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during the study. She has no active infection or oral mucositis and is HIV negative. She is not sensitive to E. coli derived products.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and has been scheduled to undergo elective off-pump coronary artery bypass surgery. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes enalapril 10 mg once daily. He also has a history of dyslipidemia and is taking atorvastatin 40 mg once daily. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and reports occasional chest discomfort with exertion. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His father had a history of myocardial infarction at the age of 65. His physical exam and lab studies revealed no other abnormalities. BP: 130/85 Hgb: 14 g/dl WBC: 7000 /mm3 Plt: 250000 /ml Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was diagnosed with Crohn's disease 3 years ago. He is currently in remission with a CDAI score of less than 150 and is taking mesalazine (4g/d) as a maintenance medication. He has never experienced acupuncture before and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. The patient reports experiencing occasional functional gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain and bloating, as well as fatigue and insomnia. He denies experiencing depression, anxiety, or perceived stress. The patient is not pregnant, does not have any serious organic diseases, and has not been diagnosed with psychosis. He is not taking any antibiotics, probiotics, or traditional Chinese medicine. The patient has not undergone any abdominal or gastrointestinal surgery in the past half a year and does not have any skin diseases or defects in the selected area of acupuncture and moxibustion that cannot be performed. He signs informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 32-year-old previously healthy male was recently diagnosed with T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) after experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and easy bruising. He has no significant past medical history and has never received chemotherapy. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and his labs reveal a serum bilirubin of 1.8 mg/dL, SGOT of 50 U/L, SGPT of 45 U/L, and serum creatinine of 1.5 mg/dL. He is not pregnant or nursing. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to receive combination chemotherapy with nelarabine to treat his T-cell ALL. He understands that this is a phase II trial and that the study is evaluating the safety and efficacy of adding pegaspargase and venetoclax to the regimen. He is willing to undergo hyperfractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine sulfate, doxorubicin hydrochloride, and dexamethasone (hyper-CVAD) and methotrexate/cytarabine courses, as well as nelarabine and pegaspargase infusions. The patient is committed to participating in maintenance and intensification courses for 30 months and understands that he will be closely monitored for disease progression and toxicity.

32-year-old male, currently serving in the Ohio Army National Guard, with a recent history of at-risk drinking, scoring a 6 on the AUDIT-C questionnaire. The patient owns a smartphone with either Android or iOS operating system and is not currently undergoing treatment for substance use disorders. The patient is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial testing a smartphone app that includes an alcohol brief intervention (SP-BI) versus an Enhanced Usual Care (EUC) condition.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past 2 years. Despite being treated with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) for the past 8 weeks, the patient has not responded adequately to treatment. The patient has a history of inadequate response to at least one other antidepressant treatment during the current MDD episode. The patient has no other significant medical conditions and has a body mass index (BMI) of 25. The patient has not received any new onset psychotherapy within the past 6 weeks and has not used opioid agonists within the past 14 days. The patient has not received electroconvulsive therapy during the current MDD episode and has not attempted suicide within the past 2 years. The patient does not have a history of thyroid pathology, seizure disorder, or neuroleptic malignant syndrome/serotonin syndrome. Additionally, the patient has tested negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has experienced progressive neurological symptoms over the past year, including weakness in her limbs, difficulty walking, and numbness in her hands and feet. She has not received any formal diagnosis for her symptoms yet. She recently had an MRI scan that showed at least 9 T2 brain lesions of minimum 3 mm. She does not wear contact lenses and has not had any recent ocular infections. She is not currently taking any corticosteroids or immunosuppressive medications. She is interested in participating in this study as she is looking for a less invasive diagnostic method for her condition. She is willing to provide tears using a Schirmer strip for analysis of oligoclonal bands. She is willing to be followed up for the duration of the study and to provide any additional samples as needed for the study. She is aware that she may not benefit directly from participating in this study, but hopes that her participation may help advance the knowledge and diagnosis of multiple sclerosis for future patients.

A 25-year-old healthy male who occasionally consumes alcohol is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a product that claims to prevent hangovers. He reports that he usually drinks 2-3 glasses of alcohol per week and has experienced hangover symptoms such as headache, nausea, and fatigue. He is currently not taking any medication or food supplements and has no significant medical history. He weighs 75 kg and is willing to abstain from alcohol for a week before the study. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the protocol.

The patient is a healthy male between the ages of 18 and 55 years old. He has no significant medical history, no current illnesses, and is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the relative bioavailability, influence of pantoprazole coadministration and food effect of different oral formulations of BI 113608. The patient is able to understand and comply with the study procedures and is willing to provide written informed consent.

Female university student between the ages of 18-25 years old, who has been identified as having a higher than average score on the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDEQ-Total) or the Eating Attitudes Test (EAT) based on a previous study conducted among university students in Turkey. The participant must be willing to give consent to participate in a study aimed at promoting healthy eating attitudes and behaviours through a 6-session Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) oriented group program. The participant should not have a current or past history of eating disorders diagnosis, current substance abuse problem, or current or past history of psychotic disorders.

A 27-year-old male who is a professional athlete presents with sudden onset of pain in the back of the thigh while sprinting during a game. He reports feeling a “pop” in his leg at the time of injury. He is unable to continue playing and is taken off the field. He reports difficulty walking and pain with any movement of his leg. Physical examination reveals tenderness and swelling in the posterior thigh. He is unable to perform active knee flexion or hip extension due to pain. MRI confirms a grade II hamstring strain with muscle fiber disruption. He is referred to ASPETAR for physiotherapy and possible participation in a clinical trial evaluating the use of Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) in the management of acute hamstring injuries. The athlete is available for follow-up and is willing to participate in the study. He has no history of diabetes or immuno-compromised state. He is not taking any medication that increases bleeding risk.

54 y/o male diagnosed with liver cancer based on CT scan results. The lesion is 1.5 cm in size and shows wash-out on later phases of contrast administration. No prior history of treatment for liver lesions. The patient is able to provide written and verbal informed consent and can tolerate a complete abdominal MR examination within 3 weeks of CT. The patient has no intraocular metallic foreign body, pacemaker, or other contraindications and is not pregnant. The patient has no severe renal insufficiency or severe liver disease. The patient has no history of previous reaction to contrast media, bronchial asthma, or allergic disorders. The patient has no acute renal insufficiency of any severity due to the hepato-renal syndrome or in the perioperative liver transplantation period.

For the group of patients with hepatic impairment, the ideal candidate is a male or female between the ages of 18 and 65 years with moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class B or C). They should weigh between 50 kg and 120 kg, and have a body mass index between 18.0-36.0 kg/m2. The patient should not have any history of hypersensitivity or idiosyncracies to QAW039 or drugs of a similar class. They should not be taking co-medications that may impact QAW039 exposure. The patient should not have a surgical or medical condition that might significantly alter the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs, or which may jeopardize the subject in case of participation in the study. They should not have a history of malignancy of any organ system, except for localized basal cell carcinoma of the skin, treated or untreated within the past 5 years. The ideal patient should not be pregnant or nursing.   For the healthy matched volunteers, the ideal candidate is a male or female between the ages of 18 and 65 years who is in good health as determined by past medical history, physical examination, electrocardiogram, laboratory tests, and urinalysis at screening. They should match in age (±5 years), gender, smoking status, and weight (± 15%) to an individual patient with hepatic impairment. The patient should not have any history of hypersensitivity or idiosyncracies to QAW039 or drugs of a similar class. They should not be taking co-medications that may impact QAW039 exposure. The patient should not have a surgical or medical condition that might significantly alter the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs, or which may jeopardize the subject in case of participation in the study. They should not have a history of malignancy of any organ system, except for localized basal cell carcinoma of the skin, treated or untreated within the past 5 years. The ideal patient should not be pregnant or nursing. The patient should not have liver disease or liver injury as indicated by abnormal liver function tests, and any single parameter of ALT, AST, γ-GT, alkaline phosphatase or serum bilirubin must not exceed 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN). Any elevation above ULN of more than one parameter of ALT, AST, γ GT, alkaline phosphatase or serum bilirubin will exclude a subject from participation in the study. The patient should not have a positive Hepatitis B surface antigen or Hepatitis C test result.

14-year-old F presenting to the free community clinic in an impoverished urban community in Lima, Peru with complaints of fatigue and frequent headaches. The patient's responsible adult, her mother, is present and able to provide consent for participation in the study. The patient has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. She is overweight with a BMI of 26. Blood pressure reading is elevated at 140/90 mmHg. Fasting blood sugar is within normal limits at 82 mg/dL. The patient will be enrolled in the Peru Longitudinal Study and monitored for changes in disease prevalence over the next 10 years. The study will introduce interventions focused on positively impacting chronic lifestyle-related diseases, including cardiovascular disease, hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, and overweight/obesity. The patient's participation in the study will involve regular follow-up visits, routine measurements of blood pressure, weight, and blood sugar, and the implementation of interventions as deemed necessary by the study team.

Maria is a 48-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer. She has never received chemotherapy for her metastatic disease and is HER2/neu negative. She has a history of breast cancer that was treated with lumpectomy and radiation therapy, followed by adjuvant hormonal therapy. She completed her adjuvant hormonal therapy 2 years ago. Her performance status is 1, and she has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. Her LVEF is normal, and her blood work is within normal limits. She has no history of congestive heart failure or myocardial infarction. She has no history of uncontrolled hypertension or poorly controlled diabetes. She has no brain metastases or other serious underlying disease. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. She has signed the informed consent form and is willing to comply with regular medical follow-up.

A 60-year-old male with a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in second complete remission (CR2) based on morphology (<5% blasts) after receiving prior chemotherapy. The patient has no matched 5/6 or 6/6 sibling donor and is <70 years of age. The patient has a Karnofsky score ≥ 70% and a UCB graft selected according to the current University of Minnesota umbilical cord blood graft selection algorithm. This study is for advanced hematologic malignancies not curable by conventional chemotherapy, and the patient meets the eligibility criteria for AML based on the disease status. The patient's MRD is negative, and the patient is eligible for transplantation. The patient has adequate organ function defined as transaminases ≤ 5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) and total bilirubin ≤ 2.5 mg/dL except for patients with Gilbert's syndrome or hemolysis; creatinine ≤ 2.0 mg/dl (adults) and creatinine clearance ≥ 40 mL/min (pediatrics). Adequate performance status is defined as Karnofsky score ≥ 70% (

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been undergoing intermittent hemodialysis for chronic renal failure for the past 3 years. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus type 2. Her last hemoglobin level was 8.5 g/dL and her PT and INR are within normal limits. She is currently undergoing dialysis at the intensive care unit of Clermont-Ferrand University Hospital and has been advised to undergo intermittent hemodialysis with citrate solution for regional anticoagulation. She is affiliated with a social security scheme and has given a signed agreement after detailed explanation of the protocol on the basis of the information sheet and is likely to comply with it. She does not have severe hepato-cellular insufficiency, psychiatric pathology or cognitive impairment rendering her unable to give informed consent. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not been placed under guardianship, curatorship, deprived of liberty or safeguard of justice.

A 35-year-old female with a history of alcohol use disorder and recurrent unipolar major depression. She has experienced a depressive episode during a period of one-month abstinence. The patient reports consuming 30 standard drinks per week over the past 90 days. She has increased inflammation with a serum C-reactive protein level of 4.2 mg/L. She is able to provide informed consent and has a good understanding of study procedures. She has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or schizoaffective disorder. The patient is not currently taking any medication affecting alcohol consumption or psychotropic medication. She is not enrolled in an alcohol treatment program but is willing to participate in self-help groups. The patient has no active medical conditions that could cause or exacerbate depressive symptoms. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use reliable contraception methods. The patient has no history of a suicide attempt within the past year and no hypersensitivity to dimethyl sulfoxide. She has not participated in an investigational therapeutic or device trial within the past 30 days.

Pt is a 35yo M with a history of Fabry disease, confirmed by genetic testing. He has a family history of Fabry disease and has been experiencing symptoms of chest discomfort and shortness of breath on exertion. He was referred to a cardiologist who performed an echocardiogram, revealing left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). The patient was started on enzyme replacement therapy and his symptoms improved, but the cardiologist recommended further evaluation with an electrocardiogram (ECG) to assess for the severity of the LVH. The ECG revealed abnormal findings consistent with LVH, but the Sokolov-Lyon index was not discriminatory for Fabry disease. The patient was then referred to this clinical trial to evaluate the diagnostic value of different electrocardiographic scores of LVH in Fabry disease. He meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate to help improve the diagnosis and treatment of Fabry disease.

A 28 year old woman has been using contact lenses made of lotrafilcon B material for the past 5 years without any problems. She is in good general health and has no history of eye diseases or disorders. Her vision correction needs are astigmatism correction with a sphere requirement of -2.50 and -2.75 in her right and left eye respectively. She is willing and able to comply with all protocol-mandated procedures and attend all scheduled office visits. She is not currently using any eye drops with a pharmacological effect and has no known local or systemic hypersensitivity to contact lens cleaning and disinfecting solutions. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 20-month-old child who was born with Hypoxic Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) and has been previously enrolled in IRB #504-2011. The child's parents have agreed to participate in a developmental follow-up study at 18-20 months of age. The child has no other significant medical history and has been meeting developmental milestones appropriately, according to the parents. The child's birth weight was 7 lbs 8 oz, and the delivery was via C-section due to fetal distress. The child has been meeting all of the expected growth and developmental milestones since birth. The child's mother has a history of gestational diabetes, and the child's father has no significant medical history. The family is willing to comply with scheduled visits and laboratory tests for the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently 11 weeks pregnant. She is experiencing mild abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. She is married and has one child. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is being managed with levothyroxine. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She has no history of previous miscarriages. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of therapy for threatened miscarriage. She has no contraindications to therapy with Utrogestan or Duphaston, and her attending physician has prescribed one of these medications for her. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is not experiencing any other clinical conditions that would contradict inclusion criteria or make it difficult to interpret the results of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma. She has previously received one line of treatment which was unsuccessful, and now her disease is relapsed or refractory. She has experienced symptoms such as fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. A CT scan has shown at least one measurable lesion that is accessible for biopsy. The patient has confirmed CD20+ B-cell lymphoma which is not CLL/SLL. The patient's haematological and biochemical indices are within the required range. She has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient understands the purpose and risks of the study and is willing to participate in all required evaluations and procedures in this study protocol. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to participate in appropriate pregnancy prevention measures. She has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has no history of other malignancy within the last 2 years, no known central nervous system involvement by lymphoma, and no active or documented autoimmune disease. She is not receiving treatment with chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or immunosuppressive agents. The patient has no significant concurrent, uncontrolled medical condition that in the opinion of the Investigator contraindicates participation in this study. The patient is negative for Hepatitis B, C, and HIV infection. She has not received an allogeneic bone marrow transplant at any time or an autologous bone marrow transplant within 100 days of first dosing. The patient has not received systemic radiation therapy within 4 weeks or prior focal radiotherapy within 2 weeks prior to first dosing. The patient has no previous hypersensitivity to rituximab (≥Grade 3) or murine proteins, or any other excipients used in the formulation of rituximab.

A 35-year-old HIV-positive female patient who is currently on antiretroviral therapy for more than 2 years, with a CD4+ T cell count of more than 450 cells/mm(3) and a viral load below the limit of quantification. She has a history of chronic hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine for its management. She has no evidence of chronic hepatitis B or C virus infection. She is willing to use adequate pregnancy prevention methods during the study, including the use of barrier protection or abstinence during the ATI phase of the study to decrease the risk of HIV transmission. She has no history of receiving 10-1074 or VRC01 or any licensed or experimental non-HIV vaccination within 2 weeks prior to study enrollment. She has no active malignancy that may require systemic chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She has not received any systemic immunosuppressive medications within 3 months prior to enrollment. She is willing to have samples stored for future research and undergo ATI. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding at the time of screening.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who is pregnant with her second child. She has had one previous cesarean section and is scheduled for an elective cesarean section due to concerns for the baby's health. She has no medical disorders such as diabetes or kidney diseases, and has not had any major abdominal surgeries other than her previous cesarean section. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to compare postoperative feeding regimens after a cesarean section. She is willing to adhere to the study requirements and attend all follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 21-year-old woman who is generally healthy and physically active. She regularly drinks coffee with a moderate amount of caffeine and has no known medical conditions. She is not currently taking any medications and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past month. She has no history of hypertension or other cardiovascular disease. She reports no allergies or intolerances to coffee or caffeine. She is able to demonstrate proper use of the ambulatory blood pressure monitoring device and is willing to follow the required abstinence period prior to study interventions. She does not smoke or use any tobacco products. She is not pregnant and is using a reliable form of birth control.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) for the past 2 years. He has been prescribed several antiarrhythmic agents, including quinidine, propafenone, and amiodarone, but none of these have provided significant relief from his symptoms. He has undergone radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) before, but the procedure was not successful in terminating his AF. He is willing to undergo combined ablation strategy, including bilateral circumferential pulmonary vein isolation and linear ablation, and to receive intravenous treatment with nifekalant during the procedure. He has no history of bleeding diathesis, coagulation disorder, intracerebral hemorrhage, gastrointestinal bleeding, or major surgery within the past 30 days. His left atrium has been screened, and no thrombus has been identified. He is not pregnant or lactating. His left ventricular ejection fraction is above 30%. He has not been diagnosed with ventricular tachycardia with prolonged QT interval, Torsades de pointes (Tdp), or Brugada syndrome.

A 30 year old woman is currently participating in a weight management study at the HNRCA. She has struggled with maintaining a healthy diet due to her busy work schedule and finds it difficult to log her food intake regularly. She owns an iPhone and is willing to try the new Food Talk app to help her monitor her food intake more easily. She is generally healthy and willing to sign the informed consent form prior to study entry. She does not hold a graduate degree in nutrition.

A 32-year-old female who has been experiencing migraine headaches for the past 4 years, with an average of 6 attacks per month. The headaches are usually unilateral and throbbing, accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound. She has tried various over-the-counter and prescription medications, but the response has been variable. She does not have any significant past medical history, and she is not taking any prophylactic medication for migraines. She is sexually active and uses combined oral contraceptives for contraception. She is willing to return to the clinic within 4 hours of the onset of a migraine headache and is able to give written informed consent. She does not have a history of hypertension or seizures, and she is not currently taking any cardiovascular drugs. She has not participated in any clinical trial of an experimental drug or device in the previous 30 days.

A 34 year old woman has recently been diagnosed with tuberculosis (TB) and reports that her 3 year old daughter was in close contact with her for prolonged periods of time during her illness. The index case has given her written consent for her daughter to participate in the study. The daughter is asymptomatic but falls within the age range for eligibility for the community-based model in both Cameroon and Uganda. The family resides in a catchment area for one of the study clusters. The daughter has no known underlying medical conditions and is not on any medications. The mother and daughter are willing to participate in the study and have given their consent.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy who has been experiencing symptoms of ADHD for the past few years. He has difficulty focusing in school, has trouble completing assignments, and is often restless and fidgety. He has also been displaying oppositional and defiant behaviors towards authority figures, including his parents and teachers. He has been diagnosed with Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD) along with ADHD. He has no known allergies and is currently not taking any medication for his condition. He has no history of epilepsy, neuro-genetic syndromes, brain tumors, autism, or any other major medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and is accompanied by his parents who are supportive of his treatment.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has tested positive for COVID-19 and has been admitted to Max Healthcare Hospital. He is experiencing shortness of breath and has a respiratory rate of 30/min. His blood oxygen saturation is 91% on room air, and he has lung infiltrates of 60%. He has provided written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma for the treatment of COVID-19. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to blood products and has not received pooled immunoglobulin in the last 30 days. He is not participating in any other clinical trial. He is eligible to receive the convalescent plasma infusion as his clinical status meets the criteria for severe and immediately life-threatening COVID-19. The patient will be closely monitored for any adverse events associated with the infusion of convalescent plasma.

A 35 year old man tested positive for HIV in his early 20s and has been on several antiretroviral therapies since then. Despite following his treatment regimen, his viral load has been consistently high in recent months, indicating a failure of his current therapy. He has experienced some mild side effects from his previous medications, including nausea and fatigue. He is in generally good health but has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options and is interested in learning more about raltegravir.

The patient is a 62-year-old retired male who has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis. He is 5 feet 7 inches tall and weighs 240 pounds, with a BMI of 37.6. He reports difficulty walking and maintaining balance, which has led to a few falls in the past year. He has been taking pain medication for his knee for the past six months. He is married and lives with his wife who helps him with daily activities. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is able to walk around his house but has difficulty walking longer distances. He has not had any joint replacement surgeries. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his postural stability and reduce his risk of falls. He has no cognitive or neurological impairments that would limit his participation in the group exercise sessions.

A 25-year-old male presents to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has no significant medical history and takes no medications. His BMI is 23 and he weighs 80 kg. He reports no symptoms of fatigue, weakness, or shortness of breath. His lab results show a hemoglobin level of 15 g/dL and normal iron stores. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to contribute to medical research and earn some extra income.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who was diagnosed with high-risk acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) at the age of 5. She underwent intensive chemotherapy which included anthracycline and alkylating agents. After completing her treatment, she has been in remission for 4 years. She has been experiencing some mild health issues such as occasional headaches and fatigue, but her routine blood tests and physical exams have been normal. She has a healthy BMI and has been growing normally. She is currently attending school and is in good academic standing. She is willing to participate in this study to help identify potential markers for late effects of childhood cancer treatment.

A 55-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 5 on peritoneal dialysis for the past 8 months. He has been diagnosed with anemia with an average hemoglobin level between 9 to 12g/dL over the last month prior to enrollment. Stable dose of ESAs over the past month prior to enrollment. His hypertension is well controlled with anti-hypertensive medications with systolic blood pressure below 150 and diastolic blood pressure below 90. His Kt/V is above 1, INR is less than or equal to 1.2, and serum albumin is above 3.2. He has adequate iron stores with transferrin saturation above 20% and ferritin above 100 ng/ml. He is willing to provide signed written informed consent to participate in the study. He has no history of uncontrolled hypertension, oral anti-coagulation treatment, or acetylsalicylic acid usage above 325 mg/day. He has no history of congestive heart failure, grand mal seizures, severe hyperparathyroidism, major surgery within 12 weeks of screening, systemic hematologic diseases, current systemic infection, active inflammatory disease, malignancy under active treatment, or history of malignancy within the past 2 years. He has no concurrent severe and/or uncontrolled medical condition that could compromise participation in the study. He is not currently enrolled in or has not yet completed a period of at least 30 days or five half-lives of the investigational drug whichever is longer, since ending other investigational device or drug trial(s) prior to Screening Phase. He has no psychiatric, addictive, or any other disorder that compromises his ability to provide informed consent for participation in this study. He is using acceptable methods of contraception during the study and is not pregnant or lactating. He is not a chronic alcoholic or drug abuser and is not receiving steroid or other immunosuppressive treatment (other than topical or inhaled steroids). He is willing and able to comply with the study procedures. He has no known sensitivity to gentamicin and amphotericin. He has no history of chronic or active hepatitis B and/or C infection or positive serology at screening, and known positive Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) or positive serology at screening. He has no history of blood transfusion within 84 days prior to Screening Visit and has no date for renal transplantation.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with COVID-19 and has been hospitalized for the past two weeks. He is currently receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit. He is experiencing muscle weakness and neuropathy due to prolonged bed rest and paralytics. He is unable to move his legs and complains of pain and numbness in his feet. He has no history of cardiac pacemaker, implanted defibrillator, or other implanted electronic device. He does not have any active wound infection or amputations below the knee. The patient is alert and cooperative but is unable to move his legs due to weakness. He is willing to participate in the study and is able to give informed consent.

The patient is a 70 year old man diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently controlled with medication. He is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys gardening and watching sports on television. He has noticed fatigue and weight loss over the past few months, and upon evaluation, was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. He has no history of other malignancies. His physical exam is unremarkable, except for palpable lymph nodes in his neck and groin. His laboratory values are within normal limits, except for a mild anemia. He is eligible for the study and randomized to receive either CHOP chemotherapy alone or CHOP chemotherapy plus rituximab. He completes his initial therapy and achieves a complete response. He is then further randomized to receive maintenance rituximab or observation alone. He receives maintenance rituximab and is followed regularly.

A 32-year-old Caucasian male with a history of non-infectious intermediate uveitis for the past 5 years is experiencing persistent symptoms despite taking systemic prednisone and cyclosporine. He complains of reduced vision in both eyes and has difficulty performing daily activities due to the inflammation in his eyes. He has no significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He is married and has two children. His vision acuity is 20/200 in the right eye and 20/400 in the left eye. He has been advised to undergo surgery, but he is hesitant due to the potential risks and complications. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial as an alternative treatment option. He has been screened with a medical history and physical examination, blood tests, complete eye examination, and a questionnaire about his vision and daily activities. He is willing to come to the study center every 2 weeks for treatment and evaluation. He is eligible for the study as he is 6 years of age or older, has non-infectious intermediate uveitis of at least three months duration prior to enrollment, and requires treatment during that period to control his intraocular inflammatory disease and avoid sight-threatening complications due to inflammation, with a prescribed dose averaging at least 20 mg/day of systemic prednisone or cyclosporine.

35-year-old Japanese female with a history of osteoarthritis of the left knee joint for the past 2 years. The patient reports chronic pain, stiffness and difficulty walking due to her condition. She has a BMI of 28 and is otherwise healthy with no other significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and weight loss without significant improvement. She is now being evaluated for total knee arthroplasty and has been identified as a candidate for this study. The patient has a pre-operative range of motion of over 120 degrees and is willing and able to comply with post-operative scheduled clinical and radiographic evaluations and rehabilitation. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 54-year-old male who presented with chest pain and shortness of breath for the past 2 hours. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on treatment with amlodipine and atorvastatin. He has never smoked and denies any illicit drug use. His family history is significant for coronary artery disease, with his father having a heart attack at age 60. On physical examination, he is alert and oriented with a blood pressure of 160/90 mmHg, heart rate of 110 bpm, respiratory rate of 20, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, consistent with an inferior wall myocardial infarction. Cardiac enzymes are elevated with a troponin level of 3.5 ng/mL. He is taken emergently to the catheterization lab for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) to the culprit lesion in the right coronary artery. During the procedure, two additional non-culprit coronary artery lesions are identified, one in the left anterior descending artery and one in the circumflex artery, both with 75% diameter stenosis. The decision is made to perform complete revascularization with non-culprit lesions PCI during the same hospital admission. He is then admitted to the cardiac care unit for further management. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will compare the outcomes of complete revascularization with non-culprit lesions PCI during PPCI versus during the same hospital admission.

A 36-year-old female diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after presenting with a persistent fever, fatigue, and bruising. She underwent a successful allo-HCT from a matched unrelated donor and achieved full hematopoietic engraftment. However, she developed relapsed AML with >5% of malignant blasts in the bone marrow, indicating a need for further treatment. She is physically active and has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. Her organ function is normal, and she meets all eligibility criteria for the trial, including availability of additional cells for the first DLI from the same donor. She is willing to comply with all study visits and procedures and is not allergic to ruxolitinib or similar compounds. She understands that she must use highly effective contraception for at least 3 months after the last dose of ruxolitinib if she withdraws consent or study treatment is stopped early.

The patient is a 43-year-old male who suffered a forearm injury while playing sports. He was diagnosed with an ulnar fracture and underwent surgical treatment with open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF). Despite proper post-operative care and rehabilitation, the patient has not experienced any radiological consolidation of the fracture after one year, leading to a diagnosis of ulnar non-union. The patient is experiencing persistent pain and limited mobility in the affected arm and is seeking further treatment options. The patient has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease about a year ago. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her current medications are enalapril and atorvastatin. She reports slowness of movement, stiffness and trembling in her left arm and leg. She has some difficulty with balance while walking and has experienced a few falls in the past year. Her symptoms have not yet been treated with dopaminergic therapy. She has a positive DAT-scan that confirmed the diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. She has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 30 days. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or cognitive impairment. She is covered by health insurance and is able to understand and sign the informed consent form. She has normal blood pressure and heart rate, and her laboratory parameters are within the normal range. She is a post-menopausal woman who has been surgically sterilized. She has no significant medical history of bleeding disorders or cardiac diseases, and her echocardiogram shows LVEF of 55%. Her ECG is normal, and she has no cardiac pacemaker. She is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with the study evaluations.

Pt is a 55yo M with a 10-year history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. The patient is currently on oral hypoglycemic agents and has a fasting blood sugar level of >200mg% on at least two occasions. He is willing to keep a weekly diary and undergo observation for 12 months. The patient has no history of myocardial infarction, CVA or nephropathy.

A 45-year-old male who works as a construction worker has been experiencing pain in his left Achilles tendon for several weeks. The pain has been getting worse and affecting his ability to perform his job. He has visited his primary care physician, who diagnosed him with lower extremity tendinopathy. The physician has referred him to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of Ekstracorporeal shock wave treatment (ESWT) on muscle strength, flexibility and muscle architecture. The patient is interested in participating and is willing to consent to the study requirements. He has no history of systemic inflammatory disease or any lower or upper motor lesion.

A 35-year-old female who has been struggling with asthma since childhood is still experiencing symptoms despite being on high-dose Inhaled Corticosteroids (ICS) and Long-Acting β2-adrenergic Agonists (LABA). She is a non-smoker and works as a teacher. She has had at least two days of asthma symptoms during the baseline period. Her pre-bronchodilator Forced Expiratory Volume in one second (FEV1) is greater than or equal to 50% of predicted. She is willing and able to comply with outpatient follow-up. Her baseline AQLQ score is less than or equal to 6.25. She has not been hospitalized or had any lower respiratory tract infections requiring antibiotics in the past year. She is not using any implantable electrical stimulation device, systemic immunosuppressants, beta-adrenergic blockers, or anticoagulants. She has never been intubated or admitted to the ICU for asthma exacerbations. She does not have any hemorrhagic or malignant tumors or coagulopathy. She does not have any contraindications for bronchoscopy. She is not pregnant or planning to have a baby in the next year. She is interested in participating in the trial to see if the bronchial radiofrequency ablation system can help manage her symptoms.

The patient is a 40-year-old obese male with a BMI of 35 kg/m2 who has been experiencing symptoms of metabolic dysfunction including elevated fasting glucose levels and high triglyceride levels. He does not have a history of cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes, but he has a family history of both conditions. He is currently taking medication for hypertension. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol excessively. The patient is interested in participating in a study that investigates the best dietary approach for improving his cardiometabolic health. He agrees to follow the dietary intervention and undergo regular testing over the course of the study.

70 year old male patient who was recently admitted with chest pain, ECG changes and elevated troponin levels of > 0.06 ng/ml, indicative of a myocardial infarction. The patient has a BMI of 24, indicating a normal weight range. The patient is not currently on any anti-inflammatory medications or immunosuppressants. The patient has no history of chronic inflammatory diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis. The patient has agreed to participate in this study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is affiliated to a social security scheme. The study will involve analyzing the patient's monocyte/macrophage phenotype and their ability to produce MVs, and the content of these MVs in terms of miRNAs. The study will also investigate the potential role of miRNAs contained in the secreted MVs in the transition M1/M2 after MI, and ultimately the goal is to identify VMs that can promote the differentiation of monocytes to an alternative phenotype and identify miRNAs responsible for this effect. This study will help develop new therapeutic strategies to reduce the occurrence of MI or limit the consequences in diabetic patients.

A 35-year-old male with a history of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and substance abuse has been receiving treatment at the Freedom House Recovery Center for the past year. He reports experiencing flashbacks, nightmares, and avoidance behaviors after a traumatic event that occurred three years ago. He also admits to using substances as a way to cope with his symptoms. He is currently on antipsychotic and mood stabilizing medications. He is motivated to participate in this study and understands the requirements for informed consent. He has not been hospitalized or attempted suicide in the past two months. He lives with his mother and is currently unemployed.

58-year-old female who suffered a stroke 5 weeks ago resulting in hemiparesis on her left side. She is able to sit upright for 30 seconds without any assistance and has stable medical conditions. She has a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 25, indicating good understanding of instructions. She has no history of hearing disorders or previous spinal disorders. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to assess the reliability and validity of trunk control tests for patients with post-stroke hemiparesis.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of recurring bone pain, fatigue and recurrent infections. She was newly diagnosed with stage II multiple myeloma based on the results of her recent bone marrow biopsy. Her performance status is Karnofsky 80%. The patient has no history of thalidomide therapy or chemotherapy. Her laboratory studies revealed a bilirubin level of 0.9 mg/dL and AST level of 35 U/L. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and had negative pregnancy test. She is willing to use 2 effective methods of contraception. No other medical conditions or reasons were found that would preclude study participation. The patient is willing to comply with the FDA-mandated S.T.E.P.S program. She is not a heavy alcohol consumer.

A 62-year-old man with a history of smoking presents with worsening shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue. Imaging studies reveal stage IV non-small cell lung cancer that has progressed despite one previous line of chemotherapy. His Karnofsky performance status score is 70%. He is currently being treated with Gemcitabine and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. He reports experiencing some side effects from the chemotherapy, including nausea and fatigue, but is otherwise in good general health. He is motivated to try new treatments that may improve his quality of life and immune function.

The patient is a 3-month-old male infant who was born at 37 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 3.1 kg. He was diagnosed with congenital hyperinsulinism (HI) at birth due to persistent hypoglycemia despite frequent feedings. The patient has been on treatment with diazoxide and octreotide, but his hypoglycemia has not been well controlled. The patient's endocrinologist has determined that he cannot be safely managed with standard medical therapy and surgery is recommended to prevent future episodes of severe hypoglycemia and preserve brain function. The patient is being treated at the Cook Children's Congenital Hyperinsulinism Center and has undergone genetic testing which did not prove diffuse HI disease. The patient is thought to have focal HI disease and the parents wish to proceed with surgery for a possible cure of the HI disease. The patient has no known allergies to Fluorodopa F 18 agent.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing blurred vision and distortion in his left eye for the past 2 months. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medication. He is a smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. On examination, his best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) is 20/60 in the affected eye. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) shows subretinal fluid (SRF) and/or serous pigment epithelial detachment (PED) involving the fovea, and fluorescein angiography (FA) shows active angiographic leakage caused by central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) but not other diseases. Indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) reveals abnormal dilated choroidal vasculature and other features consistent with the diagnosis of CSC. The patient has not received previous photodynamic therapy (PDT) or focal thermal laser photocoagulation for the treatment of CSC and does not have evidence of choroidal neovascularization (CNV), polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy, or other maculopathy on clinical examination, FA, or ICGA. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is a suitable candidate for modified PDT with half-dose or half-fluence.

Patient is a 15yo adolescent with a history of mild to moderate suicidal ideation (SI) without plan or gesture. The patient has expressed interest in participating in the BRAVA trial, a virtual group intervention aimed at reducing SI in adolescents and their caregivers. The patient has access to an electronic device with internet and email capabilities, as well as a functioning camera and microphone. The patient does not have comorbid disorders such as psychosis, schizophrenia, developmental disabilities, major substance abuse or severe eating disorders. The referring clinician has not identified any externalizing disorder as a primary diagnosis or concern, and the patient is not currently participating in regular psychotherapy at least one time per week. The patient is not currently under Children's Aid Society care, or in the CHEO ED on a Form 1 or Form 2, or placed on a Section 17. The patient does not express any difficulty with reading and writing.

58 year old male with a 2 year history of essential tremor affecting both upper extremities. The tremor has progressively worsened and has significantly impacted his ability to perform daily activities such as writing and using utensils. He has tried primidone and propranolol with no improvement in his tremor. He is not currently taking any tremor-inducing drugs. He is able to comply with the required visits for the clinical trial.

Patient is a 30-year-old male who was found unconscious in the ocean after a day of surfing. Upon arrival at the hospital, he was intubated due to severe respiratory distress and hypoxemia. The patient was diagnosed with Spilzman stage 5 drowning and remained in the intensive care unit for several days. Despite initial improvement, the patient developed signs of pneumonia and was found to have elevated inflammatory markers. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the pathogens responsible for respiratory infections associated with drowning in seawater. A bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) will be performed within 24 hours after admission to intensive care, and samples will be analyzed for environmental germs using standard and specific culture media. Antibiotic susceptibility testing will also be performed. DNA extraction will be carried out, followed by universal 16 and 18S rDNA primer amplification and high flow sequencing. The results will be compared with samples taken from seawater near the site of drowning and during a new AML at 72h. The patient will be followed until resuscitation discharge.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He is otherwise healthy with an ECOG performance status of 0. He has not received any prior treatment for his pancreatic cancer, including chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He has no history of autoimmune disorders or deep venous thrombosis. He has not had any recent infections or antibiotic treatments. He is currently not taking any medications or undergoing any other treatments for his cancer. He is willing to undergo surgery for tumor resection with curative intent. His lab results show that his ANC is 2,000, Hgb is 11, and Plt is 150. His renal function is normal with a Cr of 0.8. His total bilirubin is 1.2 x ULN, and his ALT and AST are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he agrees to use effective contraception during the period of therapy and for 90 days following the last dose of RO7009789. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

A 62-year-old retired engineer had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He had a transient ischemic attack (TIA) two months ago. He presented to the hospital with the complaint of right-sided weakness that resolved after a few minutes. He underwent a carotid duplex ultrasound, which showed a high-grade stenosis of the left internal carotid artery. He underwent a left carotid endarterectomy with an Integra Sundt™ carotid shunt three weeks ago. The patient had an uneventful postoperative course and was discharged home on the third day after surgery. He is currently doing well and has no symptoms of stroke or TIA. He is compliant with his medications, which include aspirin and a statin. The patient is interested in participating in the retrospective study to investigate the safety and efficacy of the Integra Sundt™ carotid shunt during endarterectomy procedures.

A 64-year-old retired teacher was diagnosed with stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) six months ago. She initially presented with cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. Imaging studies revealed a large mass in the right lung with multiple nodules in both lungs and liver. She was started on chemotherapy with cisplatin and pemetrexed and had a partial response. However, she developed increasing cough and shortness of breath, and a CT scan showed progression of her lung cancer. She is currently on oxygen therapy and has difficulty with daily activities. She is a former smoker, having quit 10 years ago after smoking for 30 years. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She lives with her husband and has two adult children. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve her quality of life and extend her survival.

A 50-year-old woman with a history of advanced solid cancer that has spread to other parts of her body came to the clinic. She had undergone standard therapies in the past, but they were not effective. Her performance status according to Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) is 1.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been struggling with major depression for the past 5 years. She has tried various antidepressant medications, including selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), but has not responded well to any of them. She has also received psychotherapy, but it has not been effective in improving her symptoms. Her Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) score is currently 24. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse, and no significant medical history. She is not currently pregnant and uses an adequate method of birth control. She has no magnetic material in her head and has no implanted medical devices. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to fulfill the requirements.

A 42-year-old male patient is seeking treatment for liver cirrhosis due to chronic Hepatitis B infection. He was diagnosed with Hepatitis B virus 10 years ago and has been taking Entecavir for the last 2 years. Although his HBV-DNA is under-detectable, he has an Ishak fibrosis score of 5 and has not responded well to anti-fibrosis drug therapy. The patient's Child-Pugh score is less than 7, indicating that he is in the early stage of liver cirrhosis. He has no history of any other chronic liver disease or psychiatric conditions. The patient is not diabetic, does not have any hemoglobin disease, and has no other severe background diseases. He is not taking any immunosuppressant or glucocorticoid medication, and he has not undergone any organ or bone marrow transplantation. The patient is not allergic to the experimental drug, and he has not used any other anti-viral drug within the last 6 months. He is willing to participate in the randomized controlled trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been living with HIV for 5 years. She has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 3 years and has been experiencing lipoatrophy for the past year. She reports significant loss of fat in her face, arms, and legs, which has caused her to feel self-conscious and has affected her quality of life. Her current ART regimen includes stavudine and lamivudine, and her viral load is undetectable. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. Her blood pressure is well-controlled, and she has no other significant medical or psychiatric history. Her most recent CD4 count is 550 cells/mm3, and her creatinine clearance is 70 ml/min. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the nucleoside supplementation or switch to tenofovir can help reverse her lipoatrophy. She understands that the study will last for 48 weeks and will require frequent visits and tests. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is excited about the possibility of improving her appearance and overall health.

A 45-year-old woman with pelvic organ prolapse who has been scheduled for surgery at the University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center is invited to participate in a study assessing preoperative depression and anxiety and their effect on perioperative outcomes. The patient will be asked to provide informed consent prior to enrollment. Demographic information, medical and surgical histories, and a complete physical examination will be obtained during a preoperative visit. Pain management will be standardized and adjusted as necessary using the visual analog scale to assess the level of pain at the surgical site. The patient's postoperative course will be closely monitored for any complications, use of pain medications, and length of hospital stay.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding and pelvic pain for several months. She has been diagnosed with symptomatic fibroids and has been advised to undergo abdominal myomectomy. She has no history of any bleeding disorders or other medical conditions that could affect the surgery. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is currently not pregnant and is not planning to conceive in the near future. She has been informed about the study and has given her consent to participate.

A 45-year old female was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) 5 years ago. She has a history of joint stiffness, pain, and swelling. She has been on methotrexate for 3 years, but her symptoms have not been well controlled. Her past medical history is significant for depression and anxiety. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol. She is currently experiencing moderate to severe joint pain and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and feet, which has affected her ability to perform daily activities.
