She is interested in participating in the study to see if tofacitinib could be a better option for her, as she has not had success with MTX. She is willing to have her medical records and clinical data entered into the Corrona registry.

The patient is a 60 year old male with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease stage 3, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 40 mL/min/1.73m2. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin for his comorbidities. He is scheduled to undergo scheduled cardiac surgery for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in the next month. His preoperative serum creatinine level is 1.5 mg/dL. He is a retired office worker and spends most of his time at home reading books and watching television. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He is married and has two adult children. He is concerned about the risks associated with cardiac surgery and is interested in participating in a study that may help reduce his risk of developing acute kidney injury after surgery.

A 12-year-old boy has been diagnosed with Tourette's Syndrome (TS) and experiences both motor and vocal tics. His tics have caused impairment in his daily routines, affecting his school performance and social interactions. He has not been taking any medication to treat his tics for the past two weeks. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he has no history of mood or psychiatric disorders. He is not currently taking any medication for anxiety, depression or Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder. His parents have consented to his participation in the clinical trial and agree to ensure effective contraception during the study and 30 days after his last study dose if he becomes sexually active during the study. He weighs 45 kg (~99 lbs.) and is in overall good health.

A 23-year-old nulliparous woman who is sexually active and interested in obtaining an intrauterine device (IUD) for contraception. She has never been pregnant before and is anxious about the insertion process. She has heard that IUD insertion can be painful, and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of misoprostol to make the insertion process easier and less painful. She has regular menstrual cycles and has never been diagnosed with an abnormal cervical or uterine condition. She is willing to follow-up for an IUD string check in 1-2 months.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired woman who is interested in improving her overall physical and mental health. She has had a sedentary lifestyle for the past few years and has noticed a decrease in her balance and flexibility. She has no history of falls, but she is concerned about her risk of falling as she ages. She takes medication for hypertension but is otherwise healthy. She is excited about the opportunity to participate in the Zoomers on the Go program and is willing to commit to the 12-week program, attending two sessions per week. She is able to exercise with minimal supervision and has been cleared to perform physical activity by her physician. She is looking forward to exercising with other older adults and being instructed by a peer who has received extensive training in delivering the program. She is willing to participate in all baseline and follow-up assessments and understands that she will not receive any compensation for her participation in the study.

The patient is a 26-year-old Korean woman with a BMI of 22 kg/m². She has no history of significant medical conditions and is in good health according to her medical history, physical examination, ECG recording, and clinical laboratory assessments. She does not have any conditions that may affect drug absorption, such as previous surgery on the gastrointestinal tract or inflammatory bowel disease. She has no history of alcohol abuse or drug addiction. She has given her written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to abide by the study restrictions.

A 2-week-old male infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with severe respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN). The infant was intubated and given surfactant therapy, but his condition continued to deteriorate. Due to the severity of the respiratory failure, the decision was made to initiate ECMO therapy. The infant is currently stable on ECMO therapy, but has required multiple platelet transfusions due to thrombocytopenia. The medical team is concerned about the potential adverse effects of these transfusions and has enrolled the infant in this pilot study to better understand platelet function during ECMO. The infant is being closely monitored for any changes in platelet mass, plasma platelet factor 4 concentration, megakaryocyte mass, and platelet function as quantified by PFA100. The ultimate goal is to reduce the need for platelet transfusions during ECMO, which could lead to improved outcomes for critically ill infants like this one.

A 45-year-old female with a clinical diagnosis of nonmalignant, chronic low back pain (CLBP) is being considered for the ANODYNE-4 clinical trial. The patient has been experiencing CLBP for several hours a day, at least half the days in the previous 6 months, and it is the principal pain condition. The patient's 24-hour average pain intensity (API) mean score for the baseline period is between 4 and 8, measured on the 11-point (0-10) numeric rating scale (NRS), with each individual score above 3. The Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score during the Randomization Visit is between 30% and 60%. The patient has agreed to refrain from taking opiate medications for 7 days after the last dose of the study drug and to limit their rescue pain medications to acetaminophen 2000 mg per day for the duration of the study. The patient is willing and able to discontinue use of non-pharmacological pain management modalities (e.g. TENS, physical therapy, chiropractic manipulations, biofeedback, and acupuncture) for the duration of the study. The patient has been taking a stable dose of a medication with pain prevention potential for at least 6 weeks prior to the screening visit and agrees to not start, stop, or change the dose of any medication with pain prevention potential during the study period. The patient is able to complete study questionnaires, comply with the study requirements and restrictions, and willing to provide written informed consent and authorize HIPAA. The female patient is postmenopausal or less than 1 year post-menopausal, non-lactating, and has committed to using adequate and reliable contraception throughout the study. The patient has no condition consistent with Quebec Task Force Classification 3-11 and has no other painful condition that may require analgesic medications, occurring regularly or intermittently. The patient is not using regular use of medications such as acetaminophen, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), antipsychotic drugs, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, muscle relaxants, blood thinning medications (e.g., warfarin or heparin), or cannabinoids. Low-dose aspirin for cardiovascular disease prophylaxis is permitted. The patient has no diagnosis of any concurrent medical or psychiatric condition that includes chronic unstable debilitating diseases such as Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, cancer, significant renal impairment, significant hepatic impairment, etc. The patient has no history or diagnosis of moderate-to-severe hepatic or renal impairment, and no history of the previous 5 years of abuse of any drug, prescription, illicit, or alcohol. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known-hypersensitivity to components of the investigational drug. The patient has not participated in another study with an investigational drug within 30 days before Visit 1 or during the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) during a routine physical examination. The patient reports no symptoms related to the aneurysm and has never had any prior surgical procedures. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. The patient has never smoked and does not have any known allergies. The patient's physical examination is unremarkable except for a pulsatile mass palpated in the abdomen. Imaging studies confirm the presence of an infrarenal AAA with a maximum diameter of 5.5 cm and a proximal neck length of 15 mm. The patient's proximal neck internal diameter is 22 mm, and the internal diameter at the aortic bifurcation is 20 mm. The angle of the aneurysm relative to the long axis is 45°. The patient's bilateral iliac artery distal fixation sites are 11 mm in length, and the internal diameter of the bilateral iliac arteries is 14 mm. The patient's body habitus is compatible with imaging required by the study, and the patient does not have any comorbid conditions that pose undue risk of general anesthesia or endovascular surgery. The patient is willing and able to discontinue oral anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy at the time of the study procedure. The patient meets all of the other inclusion and exclusion criteria for the study.

25-year-old healthy Caucasian female who is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has no clinically significant medical history or abnormalities in general physical examination, laboratory assessments, or imaging studies. She has a body mass index between 18.5-30 kg/m² with body mass >45 kg and ≤100 kg. She is not allergic to montelukast or any of the excipients of the test and reference products and has no known history of drug intolerance. She has not experienced dehydration due to diarrhea, vomiting, or another cause in the last 24 hours before the beginning of the first period of the study. She has not been diagnosed with any psychiatric disorders, convulsions, epilepsy, or any other neurological disorders. She is not adhering to any low sodium diet, special diet, or lifestyle. She is practicing a non-hormonal method of birth control and is able to understand the requirements of the study, sign a written informed consent, and accept all the restrictions imposed during the course of the study. She agrees to return for the required investigations. She has not consumed xanthine-containing foods and drinks, citrus fruits, or cranberries within the specified time frames prior to the start of the study. She has no acute or chronic cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal diseases, neuroendocrine disorders, renal and/or hepatic impairment, or blood system disorders. She has not undergone surgical interventions on the gastrointestinal tract with the exception of appendectomy. She has no acute infectious diseases less than 4 weeks prior to the start of the study, ECG abnormalities, or abnormal blood pressure or heart rate. She has not used liver enzyme inducers and inhibitors, systemic drugs, or Over-The-Counter (OTC) drugs, including herbs and nutritional supplements, within the specified time frames prior to the First Dosing Date. She has not donated plasma or blood within 2 months prior to the start of the study and does not smoke more than 10 cigarettes per day or have a history of alcoholism, drug addiction, or drug abuse. She has not participated in other clinical trials of medicines within 3 months prior to the start of the study and has a negative test for syphilis, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV. She has no history of phenylketonuria.

The patient is a 65-year-old male diagnosed with mild Alzheimer's disease with a Mini Mental State Exam (MMSE) score of 23. He lives with his wife and is retired. He enjoys gardening and watching TV. He is in good physical health and has no history of seizures, stroke, or migraine headaches. He is not taking any medications that lower seizure threshold or psychiatric medications. He has no active implantable medical devices or profound hearing or visual impairment. He is willing to use the GENUS device at home for 1 hour per day for 6 or 9 months, and he is able to complete the 1st month of at-home stimulation at his primary residence. He is able to travel to the study site, which is within 2 hours of his home, for the evaluations. He is willing to sign the informed consent document.

The patient is a 32 year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and has never been pregnant before. She has regular menstrual cycles with a length of 28-30 days. She has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions and is not taking any medication. The patient is undergoing IVF treatment with a standard GnRH-antagonist protocol for ovarian stimulation. On the day of hCG triggering, she has 8 follicles with a diameter of 12mm or above. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with the requirements of the protocol. She understands the study and has provided appropriate oral and written consent. There is no history of poor ovarian response or hyper-response. She does not have any chronic medical conditions or sexually transmitted diseases.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman diagnosed with OCD for the past 5 years. She has tried multiple medications for the treatment of OCD, including selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and cognitive-behavioral therapy, but has not experienced significant improvement. She currently takes paroxetine, but it has not been effective in controlling her symptoms. Her YBOCS score at screening was 21, indicating moderate to severe OCD symptoms. She has no other psychiatric diagnoses and is currently not taking any other medications. She is willing to discontinue her current medication for the duration of the study and is committed to attending all study visits. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is using an acceptable method of birth control.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who presented to the Emergency Department with sudden onset of severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain. The pain has been intermittent for the past few months but has progressively worsened over the past 24 hours. She reports nausea but no vomiting or diarrhea. The patient has no known history of gallstones or gallbladder disease. Her physical examination is remarkable for tenderness and guarding in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen with no rebound tenderness. Laboratory workup shows no significant abnormalities. A computed tomography scan of the abdomen showed no gallstones but mild distension of the gallbladder. She is diagnosed with biliary colic and is eligible for the study as she is between 18-55 years old, has no history of cholecystectomy, and is not allergic to NSAIDs. She is offered the option to participate in the clinical trial investigating the efficacy of intravenous ibuprofen for the treatment of biliary colic.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of tobacco use and hypertension. He is scheduled to undergo thoracic surgery at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) Passavant Hospital for the removal of a lung nodule. The patient has no history of chronic painful conditions or preoperative opioid use. He has a BMI of 32 and is otherwise healthy, with no history of severe allergies or coagulation abnormalities. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent for the study.

Patient A is a 30-year-old female who has no known history of any skin conditions or allergies. She works as an office administrator and spends most of her day indoors. She has never used petrolatum or Vaseline as a moisturizer or ointment. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help researchers better understand the effects of petrolatum on the skin and immune system. She is willing to undergo patch testing with petrolatum and have small biopsies taken from the skin where petrolatum was applied. She does not take any systemic or topical medications that may affect the outcome of the study. She has no history of keloids or hepatitis B or C, and has tested negative for HIV. She is able to give verbal and written informed consent.

A 28-year-old Caucasian male, with a body mass index of 24 kg/m2, presents for participation in a clinical trial investigating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic and side effect profile of multiple ascending doses of DG3173. He has no significant medical history, is not taking any medications, and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 30 days. He is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies to food or medication. The physical examination and electrocardiogram are within normal limits, and his hematology and biochemistry tests are also normal. He is willing to use medically approved contraception, as he has a partner of child-bearing potential. He has given written informed consent to participate in the study.

75-year-old male with newly diagnosed Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) as per WHO classification, considered unsuitable for intensive chemotherapy, presents with fatigue, shortness of breath, and easy bruising. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease with a previous myocardial infarction. He denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. Laboratory values reveal impaired renal and liver function. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meet all the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing hearing loss for several years. She reports difficulty understanding speech, especially in noisy environments, and often has to ask people to repeat themselves. She has tried various hearing aids in the past, but has not found them to be very effective. She has no significant medical history and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She does not have any ear infections, and her otoscopic examination is normal. Her audiogram shows bilateral severe-profound hearing loss with air conduction thresholds >71dBHL within the frequency range of 250Hz to 4 kHz. She is fluent in spoken English and has been using digital hearing aids for over a year. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was involved in a motor vehicle accident, resulting in multiple fractures and internal injuries. He was admitted to the intensive care unit and is currently on a ventilator. The patient has no history of respiratory problems before the accident. The healthcare team has informed him about the clinical trial for preventing Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia using atropine eye drops by sublingual way. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and is interested in participating in the trial. He is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all scheduled visits. The patient has no history of pneumonia, radiotherapy, or chemotherapy, and does not have any conditions that interfere with saliva production or change normal oral cavity shape.

The patient is a 35 year-old woman who has been diagnosed with OCD and has tried CBT in the past but did not respond to treatment. She has a history of compulsive checking behaviors and intrusive thoughts that cause significant distress and interfere with her daily life. She currently takes medication for anxiety and depression but has not made any changes to her medication in the past 8 weeks. She is fluent in English and able to read and speak it on a daily basis. She does not have any history of drug or alcohol dependence in the past three months, and does not have a history of severe psychiatric problems that require immediate treatment.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for several years. She has tried various treatments including physical therapy, chiropractic care, and medication, but has not found any significant relief. She has been advised to undergo lumbar spine surgery and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves acupuncture therapy for pain management and functional recovery. She is an English speaker and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She has no serious psychiatric illness and has not had acupuncture for four weeks prior to surgery. She agrees to not have elective acupuncture for six weeks after surgery. She will be randomized into either the direct acupuncture therapy group, indirect acupuncture therapy group, or usual care alone group. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that the acupuncture therapy will help her manage her pain and improve her function after surgery.

This is a 7-year-old female student attending a public school in a suburban area of Brasília, Brazil. She has a history of occasional toothache and difficulty eating due to dental pain. She has been avoiding certain foods such as sweets and cold drinks due to tooth sensitivity. She has not received any restorative dental treatment in the past year. Her parents are both employed and have limited financial resources for dental care. The patient has good general health, with no known systemic diseases or disabilities. She is expected to be compliant with the study's requirements and is not participating in any other study. She has at least one cavitated dentin carious lesion in a primary molar with a sensible asymptomatic pulp, making her eligible for the clinical trial.

Patient is a 13-year-old boy from India who has been diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and is undergoing chemotherapy. He has no significant past medical history and is currently on no medications other than chemotherapy. He presents to the clinic with a fever of 38.5°C and complains of mild fatigue. On physical examination, he is found to have a heart rate of 90 beats per minute and a respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute. His blood pressure is within normal limits. Laboratory studies reveal a low white blood cell count and an ANC of 200 cells/microliter. He has no identifiable focus of infection and his culture results are awaited.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic joint pain and stiffness for the past few years. She has noticed a gradual reduction in her mobility, along with difficulty in performing daily tasks. She has a history of multiple fractures in her arms and legs, which have taken a long time to heal. She has visited several doctors, but the cause of her symptoms has not been identified. Recently, she was diagnosed with Hypophosphatasia (HPP) after a series of lab tests, which revealed reduced serum/plasma ALP activity below age and sex specific reference range. She also has a genetically secured ALPL mutation. She has not received any treatment with Asfotase alfa and is not currently participating in any other clinical study. She is willing to participate in the study after signing the informed consent.

55 yo F with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic hip pain. The patient reports difficulty with daily activities such as walking and climbing stairs. She has tried physical therapy and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) without significant relief. The patient is interested in exploring surgical options for hip replacement. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. She is able to read and understand study information and is willing to return for follow-up evaluations. The patient is a good candidate for total hip arthroplasty and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 16-year-old girl who has been experiencing vaginal discharge with a foul odor for the past few weeks. She is concerned about the odor and has been avoiding social situations due to embarrassment. She has not been sexually active and has no history of sexually transmitted infections. She has never had a pelvic exam or Pap smear. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings. She attends high school and is currently in the 11th grade. She is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She is willing to participate in the study and able to comply with all study requirements.

A 62-year-old male who recently suffered an ischemic stroke is being admitted to the UPMC Institute for Rehabilitation and Research for post-stroke rehabilitation. He is right-handed and has been working as an accountant before the stroke. He is married with two adult children. Prior to the stroke, he did not have any significant medical history except for hypertension, which was controlled with medication. The stroke occurred 25 days ago and he received appropriate medical management. He has some residual weakness on the left side of his body and mild cognitive impairment, specifically in attention and working memory. He speaks English fluently and has no history of sensitivity to donepezil. He is not currently taking any medication that would be contraindicated with AchEi therapy. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no history of suicidal attempt in the past one year or inpatient admission for depression in the past one year.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with chondrosarcoma that has metastasized to his lungs. He has undergone chemotherapy in the past, but it did not provide any significant benefit. His performance status is ECOG 1, and he has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. He has no other invasive malignancies except for a history of basal cell carcinoma. He has adequate hematologic, hepatic, and renal function. He has no history of stroke, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, or ventricular arrhythmia requiring medication or mechanical control within the last 6 months. He is not currently taking any medications or foods that are known to be moderate or strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 activity. He has agreed to use adequate methods of birth control throughout the study, and he is willing and able to adhere to the study visit schedule and all protocol requirements. He has provided tumor samples from a new biopsy for the study.

A 55-year-old male patient who suffered from a stroke 6 months ago and is currently undergoing rehabilitation therapy is being considered for a clinical trial. He is able to stand up, walk, and turn around without the assistance of another person. He is undergoing 3D gait analysis as part of his rehabilitation therapy. He has no other significant medical history or complications that would impact his ability to walk. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no bilateral cerebellar syndrome, apraxia, or severe aphasia. He has not received botulinum toxin injection in the last 3 months and has not undergone surgery of the locomotor system in the last 6 months. He is affiliated with a social security system.

25 y/o non-smoker with a physician diagnosis of asthma, residing in Baltimore for at least six months. The patient has experienced asthma symptoms and/or has used reliever medication in the past six months. The patient has completed the observational environmental asthma study "Inhale 1". The patient is not currently pregnant and does not have another major pulmonary disease or significant morbidity. The patient is not currently using an air cleaner in the home and is not planning to relocate or travel away from home for a prolonged period of time during the study period.

A 28-year-old woman who is currently in a long-term relationship with her partner is seeking a safe and effective contraceptive method after experiencing an unexpected pregnancy. She works as a teacher and has no history of significant medical conditions. She has no known allergies to medications and is fluent in English. She lives in the Boston area and has access to emergency medical care if needed. She has a working telephone number and is willing to participate in a study assessing the satisfaction of subjects who have selected either the contraceptive implant or DMPA given on the first day of medical abortion. She is interested in participating in the study and is eligible for medication abortion, etonogestrel implant, and DMPA.

A 2-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his parents who report that he had a seizure with a fever of 39°C (102.2°F). The seizure lasted for about 5 minutes and stopped before the ambulance arrived. The child has not had any prior convulsions or been on antiepileptic medication. The parents are concerned about the chances of another seizure as the child has had multiple episodes of fever in the past. The doctor recommends enrollment in a clinical trial to investigate if the early use of antipyretics can prevent recurrences of febrile seizures. The parents agree to enroll their child in the trial and understand that they will need to give antipyretic medication every time their child has a new episode of fever during the two-year study period.

A 26-year-old woman was referred to a psychiatrist by her therapist for ongoing therapy for borderline personality disorder (BPD). She was diagnosed with BPD 2 years ago and has been receiving therapy but is still struggling with mood swings, impulsivity, and unstable relationships. She has a history of self-harm and suicidal ideation but has not attempted suicide. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is sexually active and uses contraception. She is willing to discontinue any prohibited medications to participate in the trial. She has never participated in any clinical trials before.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. He is a current smoker with a smoking history of 35 years. He has complained of chronic cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing. He is currently experiencing significant weight loss, abdominal distension, and diarrhea. His BMI is 22, and his laboratory results show hypoproteinemia. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve his malnutrition, and he meets the eligibility criteria for this study. He has not used any antibiotics or probiotics within the last 4 weeks. He does not have any significant diseases other than COPD, and he is willing and able to complete the follow-up according to the plan. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

A 25-year-old male presents with moderate erythema, moderate scaling, and mild pruritus in the groin area. The patient reports discomfort and itchiness in the area for the past 2 weeks. The patient has not applied any topical ointment or powder for the condition. The patient has no other significant medical history and is generally healthy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. The patient is not using any medication that could interfere with the study treatment and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 45-year-old male presents with a history of shortness of breath and frequent respiratory infections. He has been diagnosed with alpha 1-antitrypsin (AAT) deficiency and has been receiving AAT protein replacement therapy for the past 3 years. He is a former smoker and has quit smoking 2 years ago. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He is married and has 1 child. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety of an experimental gene transfer procedure to treat his AAT deficiency. He is willing to discontinue his AAT protein replacement therapy and use contraception throughout the study. He is not currently taking any medications that may alter platelet function or have received any investigational study agents in the past 30 days. He is a non-drug user and has no history of facial or chest trauma that may make it medically impossible to perform pulmonary function tests. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was admitted to the hospital due to uncontrolled blood sugar levels and high blood pressure. The patient has a history of smoking and alcohol use, but quit both habits 5 years ago. He is currently taking metformin and insulin to manage his diabetes. The patient has a BMI of 32, indicating he is obese. He has no other significant medical history, and his blood tests show elevated HbA1c levels. The patient provides informed consent to participate in the study and agrees to follow the training concept provided by the medical staff.

A 62-year-old male patient was diagnosed with unresectable, locally advanced recurrent serum AFP-elevated gastric adenocarcinoma. He has not received any systematic treatment for advanced or metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma in the past. His serum AFP level is > 20 ng/ml. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score is 1. He has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. He has at least one measurable lesion or evaluable disease by CT or MRI per RECIST 1.1 criteria. His hematological system, liver function, renal function, and coagulation function meet the eligibility requirements. He has no history of autoimmune disease or active infections. He has no history of serious cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. He has no allergies to anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody drugs or oxaliplatin or capecitabine.

A 25-year-old Caucasian male presents with a history of auditory hallucinations and delusions for the past 6 months. He reports hearing voices that tell him to harm himself and others. He also believes that he is being monitored and controlled by a secret government agency. He has no significant medical history and is not on any medication. His family history is negative for any psychiatric disorders. Mental status examination reveals disorganized speech, poor eye contact, and impaired judgment. He is diagnosed with schizophrenia and is started on paliperidone ER two weeks ago. He reports some improvement in his symptoms but still experiences occasional auditory hallucinations. He is willing to participate in the observational study to document his treatment outcomes with paliperidone ER. He understands the study and has signed the informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman with a recent diagnosis of cervical HSIL after a routine Pap smear. She has no history of abnormal Pap smears or cervical lesions in the past. She is currently using oral contraceptives for birth control and has no plans for pregnancy in the next six months. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude her from the study. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to potentially treat her HSIL and prevent progression to invasive cervical cancer.

A 32-year-old woman diagnosed with Interstitial Cystitis (IC) presents with symptoms of urinary urgency, frequency, and pain in the lower abdomen and pelvis. The pain is often described as a burning sensation and is aggravated by bladder filling. The patient reports an increase in symptoms during menstruation, sexual intercourse, and after consuming acidic or spicy foods. The patient has a history of recurrent UTIs and has been treated with antibiotics multiple times in the past. She is currently not taking any medications for her IC. The patient is able to read and speak English fluently and is interested in participating in the study to help understand her condition better. The patient is not over the age of 65, not pregnant, and has no significant cardiac disease.

The patient is a 63-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer six months ago. He underwent a radical prostatectomy, but subsequent imaging studies showed metastatic disease to his bones. His PSA level is 60 ng/ml. He has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. He has a medical history of hypertension, which is well controlled with lisinopril, and type 2 diabetes, which is controlled with metformin. He has no history of alcoholism or drug addiction. He lives with his wife and is retired from his job as an accountant. He is willing to undergo oral medication and blood sampling. His WHO performance status is 1. He has no symptoms related to brain metastases, and imaging studies have not shown any evidence of progressive brain metastases. He has no known allergies to any of the study drugs. He has reliable contraceptive methods. He has a life expectancy of at least 3 months allowing adequate follow-up of toxicity evaluation and antitumor activity. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 2 years ago. She has been on stable medication for the past year and has not experienced any flare-ups during this period. She is currently not on any biologic drugs. Her SLE activity is classified as inactive to mild. She has no significant medical history apart from SLE and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to participate in a one-month multi-dose study to evaluate the safety and tolerability of 3 intravenous infusions of RSLV-132.

The patient is a 32 year old male who has been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection for the past 6 years. He is currently on antiretroviral therapy but is experiencing adverse effects and toxicities. He has been experiencing fatigue, nausea and diarrhea for the past 3 months which is affecting his daily routine. He is a non-smoker and non-alcoholic. He is a freelance graphic designer and spends most of his time working from home. He is unmarried and lives alone. He has a BMI of 22 and his blood pressure is within normal range. He has no history of drug allergies. His latest HIV-1 RNA test result is < 40 copies/mL and has no documented resistance mutations to PIs, INSTIs or lamivudine. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who is a breast cancer survivor. She had a lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy five years ago. Since then, she has been experiencing moderate to severe neuropathic pain in her right arm and chest area. The pain is usually described as stabbing, burning, and tingling in nature, and it interferes with her daily activities, including housework and sleep. She has tried various pain medications, but the pain persists. She lives in a suburban area with her husband and has two adult children who live nearby. She is retired and spends her time reading and gardening. She has never tried mindfulness or meditation before, but she is open to the idea of an online program. She has access to a computer and a stable internet connection. Her BMI is 25, and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. There is no significant past medical history.

The patient is a 30 year old Hispanic male who works as a nurse in a hospital in a major city. He has been working on the COVID-19 unit for the past 6 months and has been exposed to several positive cases. He is concerned about his risk of contracting the virus and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of hydroxychloroquine and ivermectin as a prophylaxis. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He weighs 75 kg and has a normal potassium and magnesium levels. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and has signed an informed consent form.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and has been receiving androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for the past 6 months. However, his PSA levels have been continuously increasing despite the treatment. He has no significant medical history, except for hypertension controlled with medication. A bone scan and MRI showed metastatic lesions on his spine, pelvis, and ribs. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial and undergo the whole exome sequencing to guide his treatment plan. He has a good understanding of the study and is expected to have a survival period of more than 1 year. He is not currently taking any anticoagulant or anti-platelet aggregation drugs and has no serious systemic diseases that may interfere with the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) during a routine check-up. He has no history of previous treatment for HCC. Imaging showed the presence of PVTT, but no evidence of extrahepatic spread. He has an Eastern Co-operative Group performance status of 0, and his liver function is within normal limits. The patient has been deemed a candidate for resectable disease, which is defined as the possibility of completely removing all gross tumors and retaining a sufficient liver remnant to sustain life, as assessed by the surgery team. The patient does not have a Child-Pugh class C liver cirrhosis, ICG-R15 >30%, or evidence of hepatic decompensation including ascites, esophageal or gastric variceal bleeding or hepatic encephalopathy. The patient's American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score is <3. The patient is interested in exploring all treatment options available to him and is willing to participate in this clinical trial.

This is a 27 year-old female who has been experiencing painful menstrual cramps (dysmenorrhea) for several years. The pain is severe enough to interfere with her daily activities and can last for up to three days. She has not been diagnosed with any underlying pelvic pathology such as endometriosis and has regular menstrual cycles. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m² and has not had any previous treatment for her dysmenorrhea. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Extracorporeal Shock Therapy for dysmenorrhea.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman from Swaziland who recently gave birth to a baby boy. She is attending her postnatal checkup with her infant at a local health facility. The patient has a positive history of HIV infection and is currently on antiretroviral therapy (ART). She is currently breastfeeding her baby and has some concerns about family planning options that are safe for her and her baby. The patient is interested in accessing HIV services and postnatal care services at the same time as she finds it difficult to come to the clinic frequently due to transportation and childcare issues. She is willing to be interviewed and give her informed consent to participate in the study.

A 68-year-old Caucasian woman presented with severe pain in her left knee, which has been getting progressively worse over the past 6 months. She has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are all well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has been taking over-the-counter pain medication to manage her knee pain, but it has not been effective. Physical examination revealed tenderness, swelling, and limited range of motion in her left knee. X-rays showed significant joint space narrowing and bone spurs, consistent with osteoarthritis. She was recommended for knee replacement surgery. The patient underwent the surgery and experienced relief from her knee pain for the first few months. However, she started experiencing pain and swelling in the same knee again after 6 months. She was referred for revision surgery to address the issue. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria of requiring hip or knee replacement surgery for 'late' joint prosthesis infection, present for at least 90 days from the date of the arthroplasty. Her medical history and previous laboratory and radiological examinations will be considered as part of the study.

57-year-old female with a history of breast cancer diagnosed 3 years ago, initially ER/PR positive, HER2 negative, treated with lumpectomy and radiation therapy followed by Tamoxifen. Despite the treatment, the patient experienced recurrence of the disease in the form of bone metastases, and was started on letrozole. However, after 6 months, the disease progressed again with increased pain and new lesions noted on imaging. The patient now has hormone-refractory metastatic breast cancer, and is being referred to the clinical trial for further treatment options. She reports feeling tired easily and experiences discomfort due to the bony metastases. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise in good health. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent. Her ECOG performance status is 1, her bone marrow function, liver and renal function are within normal limits, and she has adequate birth control. Her fasting serum cholesterol and triglycerides are within normal limits. She has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the last 4 weeks and has not received prior treatment with trastuzumab or other HER2-directed therapies or with an mTOR inhibitor within 12 months of study entry. She has no active infection, uncontrolled central nervous system metastases, or life-threatening visceral metastases. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is not taking any chronic systemic treatment with corticosteroids or another immunosuppressive agent. She does not have liver disease, HIV seropositivity, or impairment of gastrointestinal function. She has no known history of hypersensitivity to trial medications, emotional limitations, or active bleeding diathesis.

An 80-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and coronary artery disease presented to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. An ECG showed ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads, and he was diagnosed with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The patient underwent successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a drug-eluting stent placed in the right coronary artery. The patient received a loading dose of 180 mg ticagrelor and was started on a maintenance dose of 90 mg twice daily. His medications also included aspirin, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. The patient is now stable and able to provide written informed consent for the trial. He is randomized to receive either ticagrelor 60 mg twice daily or ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily for 14 days, followed by a crossover to the alternative treatment for another 14 days. Blood samples will be taken at baseline and at specific time points to evaluate platelet function. The objective of the study is to compare the efficacy and safety of the lower dose of ticagrelor to the standard dose in elderly patients with ACS undergoing PCI. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the trial as he is over 75 years old, had ACS at the time of index hospitalization, received a loading and maintenance dose of ticagrelor, and had successful PCI. He does not meet the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme following a biopsy. She underwent standard radiotherapy and temozolomide treatment and her post-treatment MRI scan confirmed stable disease. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she is not taking any medications. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80 and has a life expectancy of more than 12 weeks. Her laboratory results show adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. She has no evidence of recent hemorrhage on the baseline MRI of the brain. She has well-controlled hypertension with antihypertensive medications. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and meets all the eligibility criteria.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy with a moderate hearing impairment. He has been using the N5 system for the past year and is currently attending school. He is an English native speaker and has a good record of attending clinical appointments and complying with habilitation tasks. He has no cognitive impairments or other significant impairments that would impact his ability to undertake task requirements. The patient has a minimum speech perception ability in noise of 40% at +10 decibels (dB) signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). He has been using a cochlear implant for 3 years, including 1 year with his current processor. The patient is an excellent verbal reporter and has expressed interest in participating in the study.

This clinical trial is not suitable for individual patient enrollment as it is a pilot study aimed at generating data critical for informing the design of a planned, more detailed study to evaluate the effect of multiple micronutrient-fortified bouillon cube on biomarkers of nutrient status of women and children in northern Ghana. The eligibility criteria are for the different research activities that will be carried out and are not related to individual patient enrollment. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this clinical trial.

A 52-year-old male smoker was diagnosed with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. He has already undergone one round of platinum-based therapy (cisplatin) but has experienced a relapse. Physical examination was significant for a performance status of 1 according to the Zubrod scale. He has no active infection or bleeding diathesis, and his ANC, platelet count, and hemoglobin levels are within normal limits. His serum creatinine and urine protein levels are also normal. He has no history of congestive heart failure or encephalitis. He has no diverticulitis, gastrointestinal bleeding, or peptic ulcer within the past 3 months. He has no known AIDS or HIV-1 associated complex, and no other prior malignancy except for basal cell skin cancer. He has not undergone any radiation therapy or surgery in the past 21 and 28 days, respectively. He has not received bevacizumab or other anti-angiogenic therapies. He is willing to provide his smoking history and use effective contraception. He is eligible for the study as he meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with chronic periodontitis. He has been in maintenance care for the past year and has at least one 4 mm pocket per quadrant. He has a history of smoking but quit 2 years ago. He brushes his teeth twice a day and flosses once a day but has trouble maintaining good oral hygiene. He has no other medical conditions and takes no medications. His blood pressure, heart rate, and other vital signs are within normal limits. He has no history of orthodontic treatment or wearing removable partial dentures. His dental exam reveals moderate plaque accumulation and gingival inflammation. His oral hygiene index score is 1.8. Dental radiographs reveal moderate alveolar bone loss consistent with chronic periodontitis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent.

52-year-old female with a medical history of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. She presents with a liver mass discovered on routine ultrasound during a follow-up for NAFLD. A CT scan confirmed the presence of a 5 cm mass in the left lobe of the liver. Biopsy results showed hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient was referred to a liver surgeon for evaluation and possible resection. She is scheduled to undergo an elective open liver surgery to remove the tumor. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the clinical study of GATT-Patch for management of haemorrhage during the surgery. She meets all the inclusion criteria for the study and none of the exclusion criteria. Her platelet count is within normal limits, and she is not taking any antithrombotic therapies. Her liver function tests are within normal limits, and she has no known hypersensitivity to brilliant blue (FD&C Blue #1). She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no active or suspected infection at the surgical site. The participant has an ASA classification of 2 and is expected to have a life expectancy of more than 3 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus according to WHO criteria. He has had diabetes for the last 5 years and has been on treatment with insulin for the past year. He does not have any overt diabetic complications and has normal hepatic and kidney function. His BMI is 28.2, and his HbA1c level is 7.5%. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the influence of glucagon inhibition in relation to the anti-diabetic effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1). He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 32-year-old female presents with symptoms of lower urinary tract infection (UTI) such as dysuria, urinary frequency, and urgency for the past 2 days. She has no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. She denies any recent travel, sexual activity or use of vaginal hygiene products. Physical examination shows no abnormalities except for mild suprapubic tenderness. A urine dipstick test shows positive leukocyte esterase and nitrite. A urine culture is sent to the laboratory to confirm the diagnosis. The patient is otherwise healthy with no known allergies. She is informed about the clinical trial and agrees to participate, signing an informed written consent. She will be randomized to the intervention group, where her prescribing healthcare provider will receive educational intervention on guideline-concordant prescribing for uncomplicated UTI. She will be followed up over the phone after completion of treatment to evaluate the clinical outcome. Her anonymity will be maintained and her data will be used for study purposes only.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage IV HER2-negative breast cancer after she started experiencing pain in her left breast and found a lump. The biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and her CT scan showed multiple lesions in her liver and lungs. She has already received 3 chemotherapy regimens and her disease has progressed. She is experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and difficulty sleeping. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial and is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of eribulin mesylate administered biweekly. Her performance status is 1 and she has no other medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use a highly effective method of contraception throughout the entire study period. She provides written informed consent and is ready to start the treatment.

The patient is a 30-year-old female diagnosed with bipolar disorder type II. She has a history of mood swings, with episodes of depression and hypomania. She is currently stable and under medication, but she experienced a relapse a year ago. She is a freelance graphic designer and works from home. She lives with her partner and two cats in a quiet neighborhood. She enjoys reading and painting in her free time. She has a supportive social network including her partner, family, and friends. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help develop better predictive biomarkers for mood relapses. She has a good understanding of connected devices and is willing to use them to monitor her physiological signals. She is not allergic to any materials used in the bracelets. She is affiliated with the Social Security system and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old male with a history of Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA). He has previously participated in the TRO19622 CL E Q 1115-1 or TRO19622 CL E Q 1275-1 clinical studies of olesoxime. He presents with stable motor function, but with some increased weakness in his upper extremities in recent months. He has no current pregnancy nor lactation. He has no known allergies to olesoxime or its excipients. The patient is not currently participating in any other investigational drug or device study, nor has he participated in a survival motor neuron 2 (SMN2) targeting antisense oligonucleotide study in the past 6 months. He has no history of human immunodeficiency virus or hepatitis B infection in the past year. He has no history of illicit drug or alcohol abuse in the past 12 months. The patient has no significant medical conditions or abnormal laboratory tests that would preclude participation in the study, nor does he have any clinically significant abnormal electrocardiogram (ECG) findings.

This is a 42-year-old female patient who has been diagnosed with choroidal neovascularisation (CNV) secondary to pathologic myopia. She has a best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) score of 7 letters (20/160) as assessed by ETDRS chart. Her myopia is ≥ 6 Diopters and she has Fluorescein angiographic documentation of CNV. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has no ocular causes or other ocular disorders leading to vision loss. She has not had previous macular laser including PDT or other forms of therapy including intravitreal injections. She has not had intraocular surgery in the past 3 months and does not have any active infection or inflammation in the eye. Imaging is possible and there is no subfoveal scar or significant subretinal haemorrhage occupying more than 50% of lesion size. She has not had previous retinal detachment and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl diagnosed with cerebral palsy. She has difficulty walking and has a kinetic gait pattern. She has been experiencing these difficulties since birth. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed regional nerve damage. She is able to comprehend and has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She and her family are willing to come to the hospital for follow-up visits as required by the study protocol. She has no history of meningitis, meningoencephalitis, epilepsy, or life-threatening allergic or immune-mediated reactions. She is hemodynamically stable and has no history or current autoimmune disease or acute episode of Guillain-Barre syndrome. She does not have peripheral muscular dystrophy.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML). He has no prior history of cancer or any other major medical conditions. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy, but his disease has not responded to treatment. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has no significant non-hematological toxicities from prior treatment. His liver function, renal function, and coagulation status are within acceptable limits. He has no history of seizures or difficulty swallowing. He is not currently taking any medications that prolong the QT interval. He has no history of upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage, peptic ulcer disease, or bleeding diathesis. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and he and his partner have agreed to use a highly effective method of birth control during the study and for three months following the last dose of study drug. He has no other medical conditions that could interfere with the conduct of the trial.

The patient is a 29-year-old male who has been smoking for the past 10 years. He has tried to quit smoking several times in the past but has not been successful. He recently started using ZYBAN to help him quit smoking and has been taking it regularly for the past 4 months. He is currently employed as a software engineer and works 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. He lives with his wife and two children in a suburban area. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history. He has never been diagnosed with depression or any other mental health condition. He is fluent in English and is comfortable taking the survey online or via a telephone interview. He is interested in participating in the study to help researchers better understand the potential risks associated with the use of ZYBAN and other branded bupropion products.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who delivered a healthy baby boy vaginally at 39 weeks gestation. The delivery was uncomplicated, with the use of epidural anesthesia. The patient had a second-degree perineal laceration that was repaired postpartum. She has no significant medical history and no history of cervical incompetence or preterm labor. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that examines cervical length after vaginal delivery, and has signed an informed consent form.

A 28-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 22 who is interested in maintaining good health through dietary modifications. He exercises regularly and consumes a balanced diet but is interested in exploring the potential immune benefits of consuming mushrooms. He does not take any medications or supplements and is a non-smoker. He does not have any ongoing infections, illnesses, or chronic medical conditions. He is willing to commit to the study protocol, including consuming the prescribed amount of mushrooms for 4 weeks and providing blood samples for analysis.

Nga is a 24-year-old Vietnamese community-based physician assistant (CBPA) who has completed her training program and is now providing primary health care to rural populations. She has been working for two years and has been struggling to keep up with the latest medical advances due to the high cost of attending training programs. She owns a cell phone and regularly uses it to communicate with her patients and colleagues. She is willing to participate in the mCME project as she sees it as an opportunity to improve her knowledge and skills without incurring significant costs. She is enthusiastic about the idea of receiving CME activities via SMS text messages and is willing to adhere to study procedures, including participating in follow-up surveys and adhering to study protocols.

A 45-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C infection, diagnosed 5 years ago, is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He has a BMI of 27 kg/m^2 and weighs 80 kg. His liver function tests have been consistently abnormal, with elevated liver enzyme levels and a mildly elevated bilirubin level. He has no other significant medical history or any skin conditions. He has never been treated for his hepatitis C infection and has not used any medications or supplements for this condition. He does not smoke but occasionally drinks alcohol. He has been using a reliable method of birth control with his partner for the past year and is willing to continue to do so throughout the study. He is interested in learning more about the study and potentially participating to help further research towards finding a cure for hepatitis C.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with a suspicious lung mass on a routine chest X-ray. Further investigation with a CT scan showed a 2.5 cm nodule in the upper lobe of the right lung with mediastinal lymphadenopathy. The patient underwent a PET scan which showed increased activity in the same area. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. She does not have any significant allergies or contraindications to general anesthesia. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare traditional staging techniques to new non-surgical techniques for lung cancer diagnosis and staging.

A 60-year-old woman with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease presents with difficulty breathing and chest tightness. She has a history of smoking for 20 years, but quit 10 years ago. Her Hoehn Yahar scale score is 4, indicating significant impairment in motor function. The patient's MMSE score is 25, indicating no cognitive impairment. She has no history of cardiac or pulmonary surgery, but has experienced occasional episodes of shortness of breath in the past. The patient is willing and able to participate in the study and has no other neurological disorders or psychosomatic disorders.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a history of epilepsy that has been managed with Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS) for the past 5 years. She has previously been implanted with an FDA approved VNS device and has experienced 1 seizure per day. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of adjusting her VNS settings to engage cardioprotective effects. She has been compliant with her medication regimen and has not experienced any significant side effects. She has no other medical conditions and is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the study protocol. Her cognitive and psychiatric status is normal and she has no history of neurological or cardiovascular diseases.

A 49-year-old male with a history of small cell lung cancer, who has received at least four courses of first-line combination chemotherapy as part of an induction regimen. The patient achieved a radiologically confirmed complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) after prior chemotherapy with or without radiotherapy. The patient has no CNS metastases and is asymptomatic with no history of bleeding diathesis. The patient has a performance status of ECOG 0-2 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient's hematopoietic system is normal, with an absolute granulocyte count of at least 1,500/mm^3 and a platelet count of at least 100,000/mm^3. The patient's bilirubin and ALT levels are less than 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN). The patient's creatinine level is less than 1.5 times ULN and calcium level is normal. The patient has no prior ventricular arrhythmia that was symptomatic or required treatment and has no QT prolongation with any medication. The patient is not pregnant or nursing and is willing and able to complete quality of life questionnaires in English or French.

The patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with HIV 10 years ago. He is currently on antiretroviral therapy and has an undetectable viral load. He reports occasional muscle aches and pains, but has no other significant medical history. His past medical history is non-significant. The patient is able to ambulate independently, but occasionally uses a cane for stability. He is an alert male with no acute distress. His BP: 130/75, HR: 70/min and BMI: 26. His abdomen is soft with no tenderness. The lower extremities are normal with no edema. The patient reports moderate physical activity and sedentary time.

The patient is a 25 year old healthy female who exercises regularly and has no history of musculoskeletal surgery or significant injuries in the past year. She is not taking any medication, does not have any cardiovascular disease, and is not pregnant. She has no skeletal problems or history of Morbus Raynaud syndrome. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of whole body cryotherapy on recovery and performance after a muscle damage protocol. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and attend all scheduled appointments.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman residing in Chandpur, Bangladesh. She has been consuming water contaminated with arsenic for the past five years, with an average arsenic level of 90 ug/L. She has been experiencing skin discoloration and dark spots on her torso for the past year, which have been confirmed as arsenical melanosis by epiluminescence microscopy. She has not taken any selenium-containing supplements in the past six months and does not plan to do so during the study period. She is willing to participate in the trial and has a stable home drinking water supply.

The patient is a 30-year-old Chinese woman diagnosed with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH). She has experienced short stature and bowed legs since childhood. She has a confirmed PHEX mutation, and her serum iFGF23 level is ≥30 pg/mL by the Kainos assay. Her biochemical findings consistent with XLH following overnight fasting are serum phosphorus <2.5 mg/dL and a TmP/GFR of <2.5 mg/dL. She experiences skeletal pain attributed to XLH/osteomalacia, as defined by a score of ≥4 on the BPI Worst Pain question. She is on chronic pain medications but is willing to maintain the medications at the same stable dose(s) and schedule throughout the study. She is able to receive conventional therapy (oral phosphate and pharmacologic vitamin D [or metabolites/analogs]) and is willing to participate in the study. She has provided written informed consent, has a negative pregnancy test, and is willing to use an effective method of contraception while participating in the study. She does not have any exclusion criteria, and she is willing and able to complete all aspects of the study, adhere to the study visit schedule, and comply with the assessments.

Patient is a 28-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with schizophrenia. He lives with his parents and has a history of hospitalization due to acute exacerbation of psychotic symptoms. He is currently on an antipsychotic medication and has been adhering to the prescribed dose for the past 3 months. His medical history is unremarkable except for hypertension that has been consistently treated and stable for the past 6 months. He has no history of seizure or epilepsy. He is able to provide signed informed consent and to cooperate with study procedures. He understands spoken English sufficiently to comprehend testing procedures.

The patient is a 55-year-old former smoker with a history of smoking for 30 years and quitting 5 years ago. She is concerned about her risk of developing lung cancer and is interested in participating in a screening study. She has no current symptoms and has not been diagnosed with any cancer before. She is generally healthy with no significant medical history. Her BMI is 25. She is willing to provide a saliva sample and complete a study questionnaire. She is able to understand the nature of the study and has signed the informed consent in accordance with institutional and FDA guidelines. She meets the eligibility criteria for healthy control subjects in this pilot study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who presented to the clinic with symptoms of fever, cough, and body aches. He was diagnosed with influenza after a rapid antigen test. He has never taken statins before. He has a history of high cholesterol but has been managing it through diet and exercise. He is otherwise healthy and takes no other medications. He works as a software engineer and lives with his wife and two children. He is interested in participating in the trial to help find a better treatment for influenza.

A 55-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of knee pain that has been ongoing for the past 6 months. The pain is predominantly on her right knee and is associated with stiffness, popping sounds, and swelling. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not provided much relief. She is generally healthy with no significant medical history or allergies. She has a BMI of 33 and is not on any medications. On examination, there is mild swelling, tenderness, and limited range of motion of the right knee. An X-ray confirms a diagnosis of osteoarthritis of the right knee. She is willing to discontinue her current pain medications until flare criteria are met and is willing to attend all required visits for the study. She is fluent in English and able to read and understand informed consent and questionnaires in English. She has not participated in another clinical trial within 30 days or 7 half-lives of the study agent, whichever is longer, of the screening visit.

54-year-old male with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed two years ago. The patient received standard treatment including rituximab but had a relapse six months ago. Since the relapse, the patient has been experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. Physical examination reveals a palpable mass in the left axilla. A CT scan confirms bi-dimensionally measurable lesions

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, scheduled for elective open cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones. The patient has no history of neurosurgery and is under general anesthesia for the duration of the surgery. American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status is II. The patient has no cognitive impairment, as evidenced by a Mini Mental State Examination score of 28 prior to the surgery. The surgery is expected to last for approximately 2.5 hours. The patient has consented to participate in the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who noticed weakness and muscle atrophy in his right hand for the past 6 months. The weakness has now progressed to involve his left hand and legs. He has difficulty buttoning his shirt, holding a pen, and walking upstairs. The patient has no significant family history of neuromuscular diseases. The nerve conduction study demonstrated widespread denervation in the upper and lower limbs consistent with the diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The patient has been receiving riluzole since the diagnosis was made. The patient meets all eligibility criteria for the iDReAM study and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with metastasis to the liver, lungs and lymph nodes. She has previously received chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has continued to progress. She is currently experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and abdominal pain. She has a history of hypertension and anxiety, which is well controlled with medication. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1 and her Karnofsky score is 80%. Her blood work shows leukocytes at 4,500/mcL, absolute neutrophil count at 2,000/mcL, platelets at 120,000/mcL, total bilirubin within normal limits, AST/ALT at 1.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal, and creatinine within normal institutional limits. She has no history of allergies to medications. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the course of the study. She has not received chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the last 4 weeks and has recovered from any adverse events from previous treatments. She does not have uncontrolled hypertension or intercurrent illness that would limit her ability to participate in the study.

A 57-year-old woman with a history of retinitis pigmentosa presented to the ophthalmology clinic with complaints of progressive vision loss over the past few years. She reported difficulty with activities of daily living such as reading, cooking, and navigating unfamiliar environments. Her best corrected visual acuity was 2/10 in both eyes with severely constricted visual fields. She also had a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but was well-controlled on medications. She was interested in participating in research to improve her visual function and quality of life. She was able to provide informed consent and had no other sensory or cognitive disabilities. She was referred to the clinical trial for evaluation using the VIRARE device for assessment and rehabilitation of visually impaired subjects.

The patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man who has been diagnosed with metastatic lung cancer. He has been undergoing chemotherapy for the past six months, but his disease has continued to progress. He has a history of smoking for 30 years, but he quit smoking 5 years ago. He has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no known allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. He lives alone and is able to care for himself. He is interested in participating in clinical trials and has been informed about the potential risks and benefits of the study.

89F residing in a Residential Aged Care facility. She uses a walker to ambulate and reports some difficulty getting in and out of chairs or sofas. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis. She had a fall last year and has since been more cautious with her movements. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She is able to communicate her needs and follows instructions well. She has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, or severe cognitive impairment. She is interested in participating in group activities and maintaining her independence.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent GERD symptoms despite taking daily PPI therapy for the past 8 months. She often complains of heartburn, regurgitation, and difficulty swallowing. She has been diagnosed with anatomic disruption of the gastroesophageal valve to a Hill Grade II and has evidence of erosive esophagitis during endoscopy. She has a hiatal hernia of 1.5 cm in size and acceptable esophageal motility according to manometry. The patient is willing to cooperate with post-operative dietary recommendations and assessment tests. She has signed the informed consent and is eligible to participate in the study. The patient has no history of other medical conditions or surgeries that preclude her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing rectal bleeding, itching, and discomfort for the past 6 months. He has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of his time sitting at his desk job. He has a history of constipation and often strains during bowel movements. He has tried over-the-counter remedies but has not found any relief. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He does not smoke or use any drugs. He has no allergies to latex or rubber. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to treat his hemorrhoids and restore his quality of life. His physical examination showed second-degree hemorrhoids. His labs are within normal limits. He is eager to try a new treatment option that could potentially alleviate his symptoms and improve his overall well-being.

45 year-old male with a history of chronic cocaine use, seeking treatment to stop consuming psychoactive substances. The patient does not have any co-morbidities, kidney, heart, metabolic, neurological or psychiatric disorders such as psychosis or chronic depression. The patient is willing to participate in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial to examine the combination of two FDA approved drugs, Opipramol and baclofen, which may increase rehabilitation from psychoactive substances. The patient is within the age range of 18-60 and is of any gender.

The patient is a 30-year-old African American male who recently tested positive for HIV. He has no prior history of antiretroviral therapy and has not experienced any HIV-related symptoms. He is currently employed and leads an active lifestyle. He is generally in good health and has no chronic medical conditions. He has a history of occasional marijuana use, but denies any other drug use or alcohol abuse. He is sexually active with his partner, but denies any high-risk sexual behaviors. He is up-to-date on all recommended vaccinations. His most recent laboratory values show a CD4 count of 650 cells/mm3 and an HIV viral load of 20,000 copies/mL. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially provide an effective and safe treatment for HIV with fewer side effects than traditional antiretroviral therapy.
