He understands the importance of regular medical follow-up and adherence to treatment.

This study does not involve patients as it is focused on assessing indoor air quality in Milwaukee County day care facilities and providing educational intervention to day care staff. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable in this case.

A 35-year-old Hispanic male presents with a recent diagnosis of HIV infection. He reports that he has been feeling unwell for several months, with symptoms including fatigue, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss. He has not been taking any antiretroviral medications. His CD4+ T cell count is 150/mm3 and his plasma HIV-1 RNA level is 120,000 copies/mL. He reports no history of opportunistic infections or other significant medical conditions. His liver function tests are within normal limits. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of ritonavir boosted protease inhibitor based therapy versus NNRTI based therapy for patients with advanced HIV disease.

A 52-year-old male with a history of stage III colon cancer complains of abdominal pain and weight loss. He had undergone surgery and completed adjuvant chemotherapy 2 years ago. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes medication. He denies any other medical issues or allergies. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and is a non-smoker. His ECOG performance status is 1. His recent CT scan shows progression of

55 year old man who suffered a first-ever unilateral stroke 8 months ago resulting in hemiplegia. The patient experiences hypertonicity in the upper extremity and restricted range of motion of the shoulder. The patient has no history of nerve blocks, motor point injections or BTX-A treatment for spasticity in the last 6 months. The patient has no severe cognitive deficits or other progressive or severe neurologic diseases, and no contraindications for deep dry needling. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no fear of needles.

A 55-year-old man with end-stage liver disease due to hepatitis C virus presents for evaluation for liver transplantation. He has been on the waiting list for a deceased donor liver for over a year, but due to the scarcity of donor organs, he has not yet received a transplant. His MELD score is 20, indicating a moderate risk of mortality within 3 months. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes mellitus type 2. He is currently on antihypertensive and hypoglycemic medications, as well as a statin. The patient has a BMI of 32 and is a former smoker, having quit 5 years ago. He reports occasional alcohol use but has abstained from alcohol for the past year. The patient is interested in the possibility of a living donor liver transplant and is willing to participate in the trial to assess the validity of different prognostic models for assessing 1-year survival after liver transplantation.

A 62-year-old male diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis with intermediate-2 DIPSS risk category. He has a palpable spleen of 10 cm below the left costal margin and is experiencing active symptoms of MF, including fatigue, early satiety, and night sweats. He has an ECOG performance status score of 1 and is willing to undergo bone marrow biopsy. He has not received prior therapy with JAK inhibitors or PI3K inhibitors. He has a life expectancy of at least 24 weeks and is willing to avoid pregnancy or fathering children. He does not have any active infections or cardiac disease that would jeopardize his safety or compliance with the protocol. He has not received any live vaccines within 30 days of the first dose of study drug.

45-year-old female with a BMI of 42. She has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She has been on a waiting list for bariatric surgery for the last 6 months. She is currently under the care of a nutritionist and a psychologist. She has no history of cardiovascular diseases, severe functional limitations or chronic respiratory diseases. She is not undergoing any other exercise program at the moment. She has expressed interest in participating in an exercise program to improve her health and prepare her for the upcoming bariatric surgery. She has given her written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 62-year-old male diagnosed with bladder cancer is scheduled for a robotic radical cystectomy surgery to remove the bladder. He has no significant medical history and is generally healthy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the concordance between cytokine rise and postoperative ileus. The patient is within the age range of 40-75 years and has provided consent for blood samples for cytokine analysis. He has no known allergies or sensitivities to anesthesia or any other medication. The patient is fully aware of the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with the blood sampling schedule.

Patient is a 42-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with a brain tumor after experiencing headaches and confusion. The patient is currently being treated by the CNS disease management team at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and undergo surgery for resection or biopsy of the tumor to contribute to the establishment of a repository of CNS tumors or metastases to the CNS and related tissues for future research studies of the etiology, pathogenesis, and treatment of human central nervous system tumors. The patient has also consented to the collection of blood and spinal fluid specimens for research studies of cancer and its treatment. The patient is aware that they may choose to withdraw from the study at any time, and that any tissues already collected may be destroyed at their request.

80-year-old female with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoporosis presented to the emergency department with confusion and weakness. She was admitted to the geriatrics acute care unit with a diagnosis of urinary tract infection and delirium. On admission, it was found that she was taking multiple medications prescribed by different doctors, including some potentially inappropriate medications (PIM) according to the Laroche's criteria. The geriatrician proposed changes in medication regimen and medication reconciliation was performed at discharge to ensure that the changes in prescriptions were sustainable beyond hospitalization. The patient was identified to have a usual referent community pharmacist, and after discharge, a member of the pharmacy team contacted the pharmacy to obtain the first non-hospital prescription and compare the number of PIM with the prescription before hospitalization. The patient was affiliated with a social security scheme and was discharged to her home.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has a family history of colorectal cancer. Her sibling was diagnosed with colorectal cancer at the age of 50. The patient has not undergone any colorectal cancer screening despite being eligible according to the standard guidelines. She speaks English as her primary language and has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, or colorectal polyp. She also does not have any hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of tailored interventions for promoting colorectal cancer screening in individuals with a family history of colorectal cancer.

The patient is a 35 year old female who has been trying to conceive for 2 years without success. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has no significant past surgical history. She has regular menstrual cycles and no history of endometriosis or any other gynecological disorders. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. She has been diagnosed with high ovarian response and is undergoing ovarian stimulation for IVF using GnRH antagonist protocol. She has two ovaries present and is under the age of 40. She has been informed about the potential risk of OHSS and has given her consent to participate in the study to determine the optimal dose of GnRH agonist for triggering final oocyte maturation.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who works as a military combatant. He has no known medical conditions and has not been diagnosed with any ophthalmological disorders. He has been experiencing difficulties with his night vision while on missions, which has impacted his ability to carry out his duties effectively. The patient has no history of eye surgery or any other ophthalmic procedures. He is fluent in French and has no difficulty in understanding written or spoken French. The patient has a stereoscopic acuity of 50 arc seconds. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed and signed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with end-stage renal disease due to IgA nephropathy. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 3 years and is now on the waiting list for a kidney transplant. He is CMV seropositive and has no history of CMV disease. He has no other significant medical history and takes no other medications. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. His physical examination and laboratory parameters are within normal limits. His platelet count is 150,000/ml and his neutrophil count is 2,000/ml. He has been informed of the risks and benefits of participating in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman with a medical history of cirrhosis due to HCV genotype 3 infection. She has undergone previous treatment for HCV infection but has not achieved sustained virologic response. She presents to the clinic with a complaint of fatigue and abdominal distension. Her lab studies show elevated liver enzymes, with AST and ALT levels of 150 U/L and 200 U/L, respectively. Her bilirubin level is normal, and her platelet count is 80,000/mm3. She has a history of alcohol use, but she stopped drinking 2 years ago. Her family history is not significant for any liver disease. She is sexually active with her husband and uses oral contraceptives as her primary method of birth control. She has no history of any other chronic medical conditions or allergies. She agrees to participate in the clinical trial and provides written informed consent.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. He has been taking levodopa as part of his treatment regimen for the past year. He reports experiencing motor fluctuations and has difficulty with balance and gait. He is able to stand and walk with assistance. He does not have a history of epilepsy or seizures and is not currently taking any epileptic medication. He has no recent orthopedic injuries that would impact his balance. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is willing to undergo transcranial magnetic stimulation.

The patient is a 41-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HIV five years ago. She has a 14-year-old son and lives with him and her husband. She has a history of alcohol abuse and has been experiencing problems related to her drinking, including blackouts, missed work, and fights with her husband. She has been sober for three months but is struggling to maintain her sobriety. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help her overcome her addiction and improve her parenting skills. She has not used injection drugs in the past three months.

Patient B is a 52-year-old female who has been experiencing facial pain for the past year. She describes the pain as sharp, stabbing, and electric shock-like. The pain is mostly on the right side of her face and is triggered by activities such as eating, brushing her teeth, and talking. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications but they have not provided any relief. She has no history of seizures or other neurological conditions. She is currently on no medications and has no known allergies. She agrees to highly effective birth control and has had a recent CBC and CMP done. She is interested in participating in the study to try a new medication that could potentially help with her pain and improve her quality of life.

This is a 45 year-old female who was referred for her first routine colorectal cancer screening colonoscopy. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She is currently not pregnant nor planning to become pregnant within the next 90 days. She has no contraindications to the bowel preparations being used in the study and is willing to perform indicated lab work. She is able to read and understand the informed consent form and signs the informed consent form. She is willing to complete patient questionnaires following the procedure.

A 51-year-old male Veteran with uncontrolled hypertension and a BMI of 32 is eligible for this pilot study. He has been receiving primary care at the Durham Veterans Administration Health Care System and is motivated to improve his heart health. He is interested in participating in the Heart Health Buddies study to receive and provide social support for engaging in heart-healthy behaviors. He is willing to attend the three structured group meetings and have weekly phone calls with his peer partner to discuss progress and challenges with his action plan. He is also willing to use his personal phone for peer and coach contacts. He lives within 30 minutes of the Durham Veterans Affairs Medical Center and has no contraindication to engage in at least moderate physical activity. He is proficient in English and has no significant hearing impairment. He does not have insulin-dependent diabetes, serious mental illness, active substance use, limited life expectancy, or plan to become pregnant in the next 6 months.

A 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic neuropathic pain for the past 5 years is seeking treatment. He has tried various medications and therapies, but none have provided him with the relief he needs to carry out daily activities. He has decided to undergo spinal cord stimulation therapy and has identified his wife as his caregiver for the trial. The patient reports his pain as 7 out of 10 on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and his quality of life has been significantly impacted. He is currently using opiate medication for pain management. The patient and his wife are both employed and have a good relationship. They live together in their own home and have one child who is currently away at college. They have agreed to participate in this observational trial to assess the potential caregiver burden and satisfaction with spinal cord stimulation therapy. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 22-year-old female student at the University of California, Berkeley. She is interested in becoming more physically active as she has noticed a decrease in her overall energy levels and an increase in stress due to academic demands. She owns an iPhone 7 and is willing to keep it in her pocket throughout the day. She is proficient in English and is able to read and speak fluently. She has no known medical conditions or physical problems that require special attention in an exercise program. She has not had any recent surgeries, is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the next 6 months, and has no history of an eating disorder or substance abuse. She is not currently participating in any lifestyle modification programs or research studies that may confound study results. She is excited to participate in this study and hopes that it will help her improve her physical activity levels and overall health.

A 56-year-old female with permanent atrial fibrillation and a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. She has been experiencing episodes of rate irregularity in the last month and has a standard indication for VVI(R) pacing. She is currently in NYHA Class II and has a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45%. She is compliant with follow-up appointments and willing to comply with the protocol. She is not currently enrolled in any other concurrent studies and is not pregnant. She has not experienced any cardiovascular accidents or transient ischemic attacks with permanent disability.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who has been experiencing vision impairment in her left eye for the past 3 months. She complains of blurry vision and difficulty reading with her left eye. She has no significant past medical history but was diagnosed with hypertension two years ago and has been taking medication for it. On examination, her visual acuity in the left eye is 20/100, and there is evidence of macular edema on optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fluorescein angiography (FA). She is diagnosed with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) and is a candidate for the clinical trial investigating the efficacy of Bevacizumab (Avastin) in combination with Dexamethasone (Ozurdex) or Bevacizumab (Avastin) alone in reducing macular edema associated with the disease.

This is a 52-year-old postmenopausal female who was recently diagnosed with stage IIIC breast cancer. A biopsy of the breast mass revealed HER2-positive invasive ductal carcinoma. She has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She reports occasional fatigue but is otherwise asymptomatic. Her physical exam is notable for a palpable mass in the right breast, multiple palpable axillary lymph nodes, and no evidence of distant metastases. She has a performance status of 1. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, including a WBC of 8,000/mm³, absolute neutrophil count of 4,500/mm³, platelet count of 200,000/mm³, hemoglobin of 11.5 g/dL, SGOT/SGPT of 40 IU/L, bilirubin of 0.8 mg/dL, and creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL. Her LVEF is 60%. She has not undergone any prior surgery, chemotherapy, hormonal therapy, or radiation therapy for breast cancer. She is eligible to participate in this clinical trial.

A 35-year-old male with a history of chronic cough, fever, night sweats, and fatigue for the past 3 months. He has lost weight and has a decreased appetite. He has a history of smoking and has been exposed to tuberculosis in the past. He recently had a chest X-ray which showed infiltrates in his lungs. Sputum cultures confirmed the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The patient is diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and is eligible for the TBTC Study 22.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with peripheral artery disease (PAD) and has been experiencing exertional limb pain during physical activity. He has a history of smoking for 25 years but quit 5 years ago. The patient's medical history also includes hypertension and high cholesterol for which he is currently taking medication. He reports difficulty walking long distances due to the pain in his legs. The patient is covered by the French health insurance and is able to walk on a treadmill. He understands the protocol and agrees to participate in the study by signing the consent form. The patient has no wash-out period for another clinical trial and is available for follow-up appointments related to the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old Caucasian male who underwent skin grafting surgery for a burn injury. He has two partial thickness skin donor sites on his left thigh and right arm. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history. He has no known allergies to any bandage treatments. He speaks English fluently and can read and understand the instructions for both the AltrazealTM and Aquacel® AG dressings. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol for the duration of the study. He is currently taking acetaminophen for pain management. He is married with two children and works in a managerial position. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His skin graft donor sites are approximately the same size, and he is able to provide informed consent and HIPAA authorization. His wounds are not acutely infected, and he does not have any skin or immune system conditions that would increase the likelihood of wound irritation, infection, or early termination.

A 38-year-old female presents with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pain, and abdominal fullness. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 12 months, and they have been progressively worsening. She denies any recent pregnancies or miscarriages. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cancer or other major illnesses. She is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the near future. She has no known allergies to medications or contrast agents. She is able to lie down comfortably for the duration of the procedure. Her most recent hematocrit level is 38%, and her most recent glomerular filtration rate is 70ml/min. MRI reveals multiple uterine leiomyomas with a maximum diameter of 3 cm. She is willing to use contraception during the study period. She is able to communicate effectively and has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days.

Patient B is a 70-year-old female who was admitted to the hospital after a fall at home resulting in a hip fracture. She has a past medical history significant for hypertension and osteoporosis. She underwent hip surgery under general anesthesia with neuromuscular blocking agents. She does not have any preoperative neurologic or psychological problems including dementia, Parkinson's disease or delirium. She is able to communicate well and has no problem with her memory. She is not taking any medications that affect the central nervous system. She will be assessed for postoperative delirium, pulmonary complications, ICU admission, and ICU and hospital stay duration and laboratory findings. She will be randomized into either the sugammadex group or the conventional cholinesterase inhibitors group. Her perioperative laboratory findings, including haemoglobin, haematocrit, and serum levels of total protein, albumin, AST, ALT, creatinine and HS-CRP, will be assessed during the intraoperative period and up to postoperative 24 hours. Her clinical data will be followed up by medical records review, including transfusion amount of packed red blood cell during intraoperative period and up to postoperative 24 hours, postoperative VAS up to postoperative day 1, delayed extubation events up to postoperative day 7, postoperative pulmonary complication, postoperative hypoxia, the event of admission to ICU, duration of ICU stay, and duration of hospital stay.

A 56-year-old male with a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) presents with symptoms of shortness of breath and fatigue. He was recently diagnosed with heart failure and is currently taking lisinopril and metoprolol. His echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 40%. He is a former smoker and has a family history of heart disease. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the impact of Sildenafil on ventricular function in patients with heart failure.

A 58-year-old man was admitted to the hospital with recurrent urinary tract infections. He has a history of Type 2 diabetes and hypertension. He reported symptoms of dysuria, frequency, and urgency for the past 3 months. He was treated empirically with several courses of antibiotics with temporary relief. Urine culture revealed extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) producing E. coli. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics for 10 days with apparent resolution of the symptoms. However, 2 weeks later, he was readmitted with similar symptoms, and urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae with New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase (NDM) resistance. The patient was found to have colonization with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE) in his rectal swabs. He was isolated in a single room with contact precautions. The patient has been on multiple antibiotics with no improvement in the colonization status. He was approached to participate in a fecal transplantation study, which he agreed to.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with septic shock due to pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is a smoker. He has been intubated and mechanically ventilated for the past 3 days and is currently receiving sedation with propofol and fentanyl. The patient has been receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics and is hemodynamically stable. He has not been able to communicate verbally due to the endotracheal tube but is responsive to painful stimuli. The patient has been in the ICU for a total of 5 days.

Patient is an 80-year-old male residing in a nursing home in Ankara. The patient has a Mini Mental Test score of 28 and has no acute or chronic lung diseases. The patient has no physical or mental disabilities or limitations that may prevent them from participating in breathing exercises. The patient is interested in improving their sleep quality and vitality and is willing to participate in a breathing exercise program for three months, three times a week, for 30 minutes at a time. The patient understands that they may be randomly assigned to the intervention group or the control group and that they will be assessed before and after the study for certain physiological parameters, sleep quality, and vitality. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old Caucasian woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She reports feeling constantly tired and having no energy to do anything. She has also lost interest in activities that she used to enjoy, such as spending time with friends and family. She reports feeling sad and hopeless most of the time, and has difficulty sleeping. She has not been taking any medication or receiving any treatment for her depression. She is currently single and does not have any children. Her medical history is unremarkable, with no history of seizures, heart attacks, or any other medical conditions. She does not have any family history of suicide attempts, although her mother has been diagnosed with depression in the past. She is willing to use acceptable methods of birth control throughout the study. Her score on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) is 24.

A 55-year-old woman presents with chronic back pain that has been persistent for the last 8 weeks. The pain is localized to the lower back and radiates down to her legs, particularly her left leg. She has had difficulty performing daily activities, such as walking and sitting for prolonged periods. The patient has been diagnosed with lumbar spinal stenosis and has been recommended by her clinic physician to receive an epidural steroid injection (ESI) as part of her treatment plan. She has not had any lumbar surgery within the last year and does not have any unstable neurological symptoms such as numbness in the groin area, new or worsening weakness in her legs, or new numbness or tingling in her legs. She also does not have cauda equine syndrome, cancer, spinal cord injury (SCI), vertebral fractures, or multiple sclerosis (MS). The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no cognitive impairments that would interfere with questionnaire completion.

A 49-year-old female patient with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) presents with recurrent and refractory disease. She has undergone three prior therapeutic regimens for AML and has been deemed FLT3-ITD mutated positive. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and her potassium, magnesium, and calcium levels are within institutional normal limits. Her serum direct bilirubin and alanine aminotransferase/aspartate aminotransferase levels are within the normal range, and she has no history of Gilbert's Syndrome. Her serum creatinine is 1.2, and her baseline ejection fraction by echocardiogram is 55%. She has not been previously exposed to quizartinib, and she has not consumed grapefruit, grapefruit products, Seville oranges, or star fruit within 3 days prior to the initiation of study treatment. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and she agrees to have a negative pregnancy test and use effective contraception during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of the study. She has no history of long QT syndrome, sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, torsades de pointes, second or third-degree heart block, or complete left bundle branch block. The patient is not taking any CYP3A inducers or medications that prolong QT/QTc interval. She is willing to provide written informed consent and agrees to be followed up at 30 days and then every 3-6 months for up to 5 years.

A 58-year-old male patient was diagnosed with primary liver cancer during routine check-up for hepatitis B. He has no history of alcohol consumption or smoking. The patient has a family history of liver cancer. He underwent a liver biopsy, and the pathology report confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He underwent a CT scan, which revealed that the tumor is 3.5 cm in diameter and located in the right lobe of the liver. The patient's liver function is Child-Pugh A. The tumor is considered to be amenable to surgical resection. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has no other diseases that may affect the treatment. The patient's CK18 expression level is positive. The patient understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the follow-up visits.

A 32 year old female diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) four years ago. She has been experiencing increasing fatigue, muscle weakness, and difficulty with coordination over the past year. She has no personal history of depression or other psychiatric illnesses, and is not currently taking any antidepressant medication. She has completed high school and has a part-time job in customer service. She is interested in participating in the study to help better understand the relationship between MS and depression, and potentially identify any predictive factors for her own mental health.

A 12-year-old girl presents to the pediatric emergency department with a severe headache that has been ongoing for the last 6 hours. The headache is described as a throbbing sensation on the right side of her head, associated with nausea and vomiting. The patient reports that she has experienced similar headaches in the past, but none as severe as this one. She has no history of head trauma, CNS infections, or tumors, and has not undergone any CNS surgery or device. She denies any other significant medical history or allergies. Vital signs are stable, and she is alert and oriented. On examination, she has photophobia, and there is no focal neurological deficit. She rates her pain as 8/10 on a scale from 0-10. The patient has not tried acetaminophen or ibuprofen at home. The treating physician discusses the study with the patient and her parents and explains the potential benefits and risks of participating in the trial. The patient and her parents agree to participate in the study, and the patient is randomized to receive either standard treatment or propofol. The patient is monitored closely during treatment, and her vital signs are monitored regularly. After treatment, the patient reports a significant improvement in her headache, with her pain rating dropping to 2/10. The patient is discharged from the emergency department and is called 24-48 hours later for follow-up.

A 12 year old female presenting with abdominal pain and a palpable mass. Imaging studies revealed a 10 cm x 8 cm x 7 cm heterogeneous mass in the pelvis. Biopsy results showed embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma. The patient has no known allergies and is currently not taking any medications. She has received no prior chemotherapy or radiation for her cancer. The patient is in good general health with a Lansky performance score of 90. She has a normal CBC, electrolytes, and liver and renal function tests. The patient's parents have signed a written informed consent and are willing to comply with the study requirements. The patient will be randomized to receive multi-modality risk-adapted therapy with standard or intensified dose chemotherapy, radiation and surgical resection for intermediate-risk RMS. The patient will also receive 16 weeks of maintenance chemotherapy.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and atrial fibrillation. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and warfarin. He has no known allergies. On physical examination, he has bilateral rales and edema up to his knees. His oxygen saturation is 88% on room air. His laboratory tests show elevated BNP (1200 pg/mL), elevated creatinine (1.5 mg/dL), and hyponatremia (130 mmol/L). He is diagnosed with acute decompensated heart failure and started on IV furosemide. He is expected to need IV diuretic therapy for at least 3 days for significant fluid removal. He is willing to participate in the study and comply with the serial urine collection procedures.

This clinical trial does not involve patient recruitment or treatment, as it is an observational study to collect data on the impact of different types of insecticide-treated bed nets on malaria transmission in Mozambique. Therefore, there are no specific patient eligibility criteria or patient descriptions needed for this trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is interested in reducing the localized adiposity in her abdomen and flank region. She is currently working as a software engineer and spends most of her time sitting in front of a computer. She has tried various diets and exercise programs but hasn't seen significant results in the targeted areas. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has normal kidney and liver function tests and lipid profile. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 27.2 and is classified as overweight. She is willing to participate in a six-week clinical trial that involves radio frequency treatment for localized adiposity reduction in the abdominal and flank region. She is willing to attend 12 sessions of radio frequency application twice a week and willing to follow the instructions given by the investigators. She is willing to undergo diagnostic ultrasound and bioelectrical impedance analysis to evaluate the effects of the treatment.

67 F with a history of non-ischemic systolic heart failure, NYHA class III, and an LVEF of 30% who is being considered for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) to prevent sudden death. She has been on standard therapy for heart failure including an ACE inhibitor, beta-blocker, and aldosterone antagonist for the past 18 months. She has had no previous episodes of syncope or ventricular arrhythmia. Her NT-proBNP level is 400 pg/ml. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given her informed consent. She has no history of malignancy or renal failure treated with dialysis. She is not on the urgent waiting list for a heart transplant and is not receiving any cytotoxic or cytostatic chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy for treatment of a malignancy within the past 6 months. She is not known to be HIV positive, and she does not have any psychiatric illness or other conditions that could confound the study results.

The patient is a 55 year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with a brain tumor. He has a history of hypertension, and he is taking lisinopril 10 mg daily. He has no known allergies. He has never had surgery before. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is married and has two adult children. He works as a teacher and has been experiencing headaches and confusion at work. He was referred to a neurosurgeon who recommended surgery to remove the tumor. He has no signs of active infection such as fever, chills, or cough. He has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy before. His BMI is 27 kg/m2. He has not been diagnosed with any mental illness.

Patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been admitted to the ICU with suspected sepsis. She is experiencing tachycardia, tachypnea, and fever. The patient is not pregnant and has consented to have blood drawn within 24 hours of initiation of mechanical ventilation. The patient is not a prisoner and has not declined consent. The patient has not been on mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours and is expected to need mechanical ventilation for at least 24 hours. The patient has no history of allergy to blood draws or any other known contraindications to participation in the study.

42-year-old female with a history of asthma presents to the ED with acute exacerbation of shortness of breath, chest tightness, and wheezing. She reports using her rescue inhaler without relief. She has no history of smoking or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She consents to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of CPAP in addition to conventional therapy for the management of acute asthma exacerbation. She is able to perform peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) measurements and has no facial abnormalities or pulmonary infiltrations. She is not pregnant and has stable hemodynamics and no arrhythmias. She is enrolled in the study and will be closely monitored.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who suffered a spinal cord injury 3 years ago, resulting in spasticity in his lower limbs. He has been undergoing physical therapy and taking oral medications to manage his spasticity. He reports difficulty with walking and pain in his legs. His medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his time sitting in front of a computer. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He has a minimal score of 1 on the modified Ashworth scale for spasticity in his ankle plantar extensor (triceps surae). He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the metrological properties of the MSPMI.

A 26-year-old nulliparous Chinese woman is currently 38 weeks pregnant and has been experiencing mild contractions for the past 5 hours. She is very anxious about the pain of labor, especially since this is her first pregnancy. She has a history of allergies to certain medications but has not experienced any adverse reactions to opioids or local anesthetics in the past. She has a normal medical history, with no organic dysfunction or contraindications for epidural analgesia. She is seeking a painless delivery and is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating labor analgesia in the latent phase.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who presented to her primary care physician with complaints of upper abdominal pain, nausea, and occasional vomiting. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is a former smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She has no known drug allergies and is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. Her physical exam is significant for tenderness on palpation of the epigastric region. Laboratory studies reveal elevated liver enzymes and amylase levels. An abdominal ultrasound reveals a cystic lesion in the head of the pancreas with a dilated pancreatic duct. A subsequent CT scan confirms the presence of an intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN). The patient has been referred for MRCP with the possibility of therapeutic or diagnostic ERCP or surgery for the IPMN. The patient has signed the Written Informed Consent and HIPAA provisions and has been scheduled for the study. She is not pregnant and has no contraindications for the MRI procedure.

A 35 year old female patient is scheduled for an elective surgery under general anesthesia. She has a medical history of hypertension and asthma, which is well controlled with medications. She has no known anatomical abnormalities in the neck, larynx, pharynx or esophagus. She is able to provide informed consent and agrees to participate in the study. She has no known allergies to any medications. She does not have a history of aspiration tendency or predicted difficult airway. She is not pregnant and has not consumed any food or liquid for at least 8 hours prior to the surgery.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with advanced cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. The patient has undergone previous treatments but has not responded well to them. The patient's cancer has been confirmed to be NY-ESO-1 positive by immunohistochemistry. The patient is HLA-A*0201 positive and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has measurable lesions and is willing and able to undergo at least three leukapheresis procedures and three research PET scans. The patient is able to provide written informed consent. The patient does not have bone marrow involvement based on PET/CT scan at screening, and does not have active or recent herpes simplex virus or cytomegalovirus infections based on symptoms and tests. The patient does not have liver metastases with no other metastatic sites. The patient meets all other eligibility criteria for the clinical trial.

A 36-week gestational age infant was born via cesarean section due to fetal distress. After birth, the baby was noted to have persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn and was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. Despite the use of high-frequency oscillation, the baby's oxygenation index remained higher than 20. The baby has no major congenital malformations or structural cardiac anomalies but is receiving surfactant therapy. The baby's parents have given informed consent to enroll the baby in the clinical trial to test the safety and efficacy of nebulized Iloprost in reducing pulmonary artery pressure.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV melanoma three years ago. She has undergone multiple rounds of systemic therapy, including a combination of a PD-1 inhibitor and an anti-CTLA-4, as well as a BRAF inhibitor. Despite these treatments, her cancer has continued to progress, and she has developed multiple metastases in her lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has measurable disease and is a candidate for the PV-001-DC clinical trial. The patient is willing to undergo apheresis to collect white blood cells and have a small amount of tumor tissue removed for lysate preparation. She understands that she will receive infusions of PV-001-DC approximately every 3 weeks for a total of 4 treatments. The patient is willing to undergo scans to monitor tumor size and have blood and tumor samples taken for immune system analysis. She has a life expectancy of greater than 6 months and is able to comply with the treatment schedule. She agrees to use effective contraception during the study and for 4 weeks following the last study drug. The patient has no history of autoimmune or antibody-mediated diseases, and she is negative for HIV and hepatitis infections. She is not currently taking immunosuppressive therapy or undergoing treatment for active infections. She has not undergone organ transplantation and has no concurrent participation in other treatment-related clinical studies. The patient does not have significant cardiovascular disease or endocrinopathy greater than grade III.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the colon. After undergoing primary tumor resection, she was found to have unresectable liver metastasis. She has no other metastasis and her major organs are functioning well. Her WHO performance status is 1, indicating that she is able to carry out most activities but may experience some restrictions. She has not received any prior cancer therapy. She is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of psoriasis for the past five years. He has moderate to severe plaque psoriasis affecting more than 5% of his body surface area. He has no other active skin diseases or skin infections. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, controlled with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has never been treated with biological therapy for psoriasis. He has a positive family history of coronary artery disease, with his father having a heart attack at age 55. He has no history of myocardial infarction or angina. He is in good general health and is able to give informed consent. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study protocol, including self-administration of subcutaneous injections. He has a carotid or ascending aorta atherosclerotic plaque inflammation target-to-background ratio of 1.6 or more as determined by 18-FDG uptake measured by PET scanning. He is not currently using or planning to use anti-retroviral therapy during the study period.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of hypertension for the past 2 years. He has been taking Losartan 50 mg once daily for the past year. His blood pressure readings have been consistently high with a systolic blood pressure ranging from 150-160 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure ranging from 95-105 mmHg. He has not experienced any adverse effects from the medication. He has no other significant medical history and is not on any other medications. He does not have type 2 diabetes mellitus, heart failure, AMI, angina pectoris, or suspected allergy to sartans or calcium channels blockers. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of Valsartan and Amlodipine to Losartan and Amlodipine in hypertensive patients with moderate hypertension.

The patient is a 10-year-old African American girl diagnosed with sickle cell anemia (HbSS) at age 2. She has a history of recurrent episodes of pain crises requiring hospitalization and blood transfusions. She is currently on hydroxyurea therapy and her most recent hemoglobin level is 9.5 g/dL. Despite her treatment, she has reported difficulty keeping up with her peers during physical activities such as running and playing. She has no history of stroke or avascular necrosis. She is currently attending school and her grades are average. Her family history is significant for sickle cell anemia in her older brother. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergoes maximal exercise testing. She is expected to wait at least 2 weeks following any vaso-occlusive pain episode and 12 weeks following any disease-related complication requiring transfusion support before participating in the study.

This is a 32 year-old female with a long history of alcohol dependence, having started drinking heavily in her early 20s. She has been to rehab multiple times but has not been able to maintain sobriety for more than a few months. She has also always struggled with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms, which were not properly diagnosed until recently. She has difficulty staying focused at work and at home, and often feels restless and easily distracted. She is currently unemployed and has a history of depression and anxiety. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive treatment for both her alcoholism and ADHD. She has no significant medical history, is not currently taking any psychotropic medications, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to comply with the study's requirements and follow up appointments.

28-year-old healthy male, non-smoker and non-alcoholic, with a BMI within the range of -20% to +20%. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunologic, hormonal disorders, and no history of orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells and blackouts. The patient has not had any chronic or relevant acute infections, diseases of the central nervous system or psychiatric disorders, and no history of allergy/hypersensitivity (including drug allergy) which is deemed relevant to the trial as judged by the investigator. The patient has not had any bleeding disorder including prolonged or habitual bleeding, other hematologic disease, cerebral bleeding (e.g. after a car accident), or commotio cerebri. The patient has not taken any drugs with a long half-life (>24 hours) within 1 month prior to administration, and has not used any drugs which might influence the results of the trial within 10 days prior to administration or during the trial. The patient has not participated in another trial with an investigational drug within 2 months prior to administration or during the trial, and has not donated blood within 1 month prior to administration or during the trial. The patient has refrained from excessive physical activities within 5 days prior to administration or during the trial. The patient's laboratory values are within the clinically accepted reference range, and has no history of any familial bleeding disorder. The patient's thrombocytes are ≥ 150000/µl. The patient has signed a written informed consent in accordance with GCP and local legislation.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma. He meets the criteria for high-risk smoldering myeloma, which includes bone marrow clonal plasma cells of 50-60%, abnormal plasma cell immunophenotype, high-risk FISH, MRI with diffuse abnormalities or one focal lesion of ≥5mm, and PET-CT with one focal lesion of ≥5mm with increased uptake without underlying osteolytic bone destruction. The patient has not shown any signs of active multiple myeloma or symptoms related to CRAB criteria but has an elevated serum M protein level of ≥3.0 gm/dL. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and has a negative serum or urine pregnancy test as he is a sexually mature male. The patient has detectable clonality sequence by next-generation sequencing using the clonoSEQ assay, allowing for minimal residual disease measurement. The patient has not received any prior therapy for active multiple myeloma, but has received bisphosphonates for smoldering myeloma. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the Revlimid REMS® program and is able to understand and sign a written informed consent. The patient does not have any serious medical or psychiatric illness that would interfere with participation in the clinical study.

A 9-year-old male child visits the dental clinic with a complaint of toothache in his upper right and lower left molars. The child has no significant medical history and is in good general health. The dentist's examination reveals caries in both teeth without pulpal involvement. The caries are located on the occlusal surface. The child is selected to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy of a papain-based gel in caries removal. The trial requires the child to undergo treatment for both teeth, which will be randomly divided into two groups. The child will undergo either the papain-based gel or conventional technique for caries removal. The trial will record the time required for caries removal, need for local anesthesia, degree of discomfort, changes in the number of viable bacteria, and clinical evaluation of glass ionomer-cement restorations 6-month post-treatment.

A 55-year-old male patient presented to the hospital for mechanical heart valve replacement. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are under control with medications. He has no known drug allergies. The surgery was successful, and the patient is now in the recovery period. The patient is deemed eligible for the ABRIDGE clinical trial, which aims to determine the rate of major bleeding and blood clots when using enoxaparin as a bridge to oral blood thinning medication in patients who have undergone mechanical valve replacement. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria, including being able to self-administer enoxaparin injections at home, having a body weight of 70 kg, and needing oral anticoagulation after discharge from the hospital. The patient also meets none of the exclusion criteria, including having no history of bleeding or bleeding diathesis, no history of ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, and no liver disease. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with it.

A 55 year old man visited the clinic for a regular check-up and his blood test showed high levels of cholesterol and triglycerides. He has a family history of hyperlipidemia and his father had a heart attack at the age of 60. He is otherwise healthy and taking no medications. He has a BMI of 26 and a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. He is interested in participating in the study to help control his cholesterol levels and prevent heart disease.

A 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for over a year with no success. She has undergone two unsuccessful IVF cycles and has a BMI of 26 kg/m2. She has a normal endometrial cavity and is using fresh sperm for fertilization. She has no history of uterine fibroids, uterine anomalies, or intra-uterine adhesions. She does not have any chronic diseases such as uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension. She has not undergone any surgical retrieval of sperm for infertility.

As this study involves immunization of children against malaria, a hypothetical patient description could be as follows:  The patient is a 6-month-old male infant residing in a malaria-endemic region with a high incidence of Plasmodium falciparum infections. The infant was born at term via vaginal delivery, with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. The infant is exclusively breastfed and has been vaccinated with DTPHepB and oral polio vaccine as per the national immunization schedule. The infant has no known allergies and has not received any other vaccines or medications in the past 30 days. The infant has no known chronic medical conditions and is deemed healthy following a medical examination. The infant's parent or legal guardian has provided written informed consent for participation in the study. The infant is not a twin and has not received any investigational malaria vaccines in the past. The infant's hemoglobin concentration is within normal limits (>11 g/dl) and the infant is not malnourished.

The patient is a 45 year old woman with a history of hypertension and elevated blood pressure. She has been on antihypertensive therapy for the past 3 years but has been experiencing episodes of dizziness and fatigue. Her blood pressure measured at home is consistently above 150/90 mmHg. She has no known history of kidney or liver disease, and her blood tests show normal creatinine, AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin levels. She has a diagnosis of primary aldosteronism and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of everolimus as an aldosterone-lowering drug. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is willing to use contraceptive measures during the study. She has no signs of current infection and has normal leukocyte and hemoglobin levels. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is interested in contributing to the understanding and treatment of primary aldosteronism.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is in good health and has no significant medical history. She has noticed that she snores loudly during sleep and wakes up feeling tired and unrefreshed. She reports occasional episodes of stopping breathing during sleep, which has caused her to wake up gasping for air. She has not received any treatment for sleep apnea in the past. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs and has no history of alcohol abuse. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. Her blood pressure is within normal limits, and her urine analysis is negative for proteinuria. Her estimated gestational age is between 14 weeks 0 days and 21 weeks 6 days based on clinical information and evaluation of the earliest ultrasound. She is able to sleep in a stable place with access to the CPAP machine at least 5 nights per week. She does not have asthma requiring systemic steroid therapy, chronic medical conditions requiring oxygen supplementation, or current use of prescribed sleeping pills for insomnia. She does not have chronic renal disease with serum creatinine >1.3 mg/dL or antiphospholipid antibody syndrome. She does not have a history of medical complications such as active liver disease, thrombocytopenia with platelet count <100,000, or active vaginal bleeding at the time of randomization. She has no known chromosomal, genetic, major malformations or fetal demise, or planned termination of pregnancy. She does not have major uterine malformations associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes. She is not currently using opiates or daily opioid use, active drug use, or unstable psychiatric condition. She has not participated in another interventional study that influences preeclampsia, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, or GDM. She plans to receive prenatal care and delivery at a network center where access to complete electronic medical record will be available to research staff. This patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

55-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease as per UK Brain Bank criteria. The patient is currently on stable doses of Parkinson's medications for the last 3 months. The patient has reported difficulty in walking unassisted and experiences frequent falls. The patient reports that his endurance is sufficient to stand for at least 20 minutes unassisted. The patient has no other significant neurological or orthopedic problems. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is able to walk 25 feet unassisted or with minimal assistance. The patient's goal is to improve his mobility and quality of life through non-pharmacological treatment.

A 56 year old woman presents to the hospital with symptoms of fever, chills, flank pain, and dysuria. She has a history of neurogenic bladder due to spinal cord injury and uses an indwelling urinary catheter. She was recently treated with antibiotics for a urinary tract infection but her symptoms have not improved. Laboratory tests show leukocytosis and a urine culture reveals a high bacterial count. Imaging studies confirm the presence of pyelonephritis. She has no other underlying medical conditions and is not on any medications.

A 3-year-old Hispanic male child who attends a non-migrant Head Start program in Yakima County, Washington State is being recruited for a clinical trial on fluoride varnish. The child has at least one sound tooth surface present and is expected to remain in Yakima County for the duration of the study. The child's parents will be required to fill out questionnaires on behaviors such as diet, hygiene, and prior dental care. The study will involve two groups - a Massive Dose (Experimental) group and a Semiannual Dose (Standard) group. The child will be randomly assigned to one of these groups and will receive either three annual applications of fluoride varnish or one annual application, as per the assigned group. The study aims to determine whether the annual application of three fluoride varnish doses over two weeks is at least as effective in reducing cavities as the current semi-annual application. The child will receive basic restorative dental care on decayed surfaces only, as well as toothbrushes for the duration of the study period. The study has an age range of 36-71 months, and the child must be able to give oral assent.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who was diagnosed with prostate cancer three years ago. He had undergone prostatectomy for localized prostate cancer and his postoperative pathology report showed stage pT3aN0M0 prostate cancer with positive surgical margins. His PSA level was undetectable after surgery but has gradually increased to 0.4 ng/mL over the past few months. The patient has no known history of other cancers or pituitary gland adenoma. He is in good general health with an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has not received any prior hormonal therapy or pelvic radiotherapy. The patient has no uncontrolled hypertension and has a life expectancy of more than 10 years. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of radiation therapy with or without goserelin for recurrent or refractory prostate cancer.

A 2-year-old girl is scheduled for a tonsillectomy under general anesthesia. She weighs 15 kg and has no significant medical history. She has no history of respiratory infections and is not currently experiencing any upper respiratory tract symptoms. The child is classified as an ASA class II. She has a normal airway anatomy, with no history of difficult airway management during previous procedures. Her parents have provided written informed consent for their child's participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing frequent abdominal discomfort, bloating, and irregular bowel movements for the past six months. The patient was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) according to Rome III criteria by her gastroenterologist. The patient's symptoms have been affecting her quality of life and causing her anxiety and depression. She has tried dietary modifications and over-the-counter medications, but they have not provided significant relief. The patient has no other known medical conditions and is currently not taking any prescription medications. She has a good general health and is oriented and willing to participate in the study. The patient is interested in trying a probiotic supplement to alleviate her symptoms and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with no history of chronic illnesses. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. He has no known allergies to medications or any other substances. He weighs 75 kg and has a BMI of 23 kg/m2. His blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate are within normal limits. He has no abnormalities on physical examination, including no evidence of liver or renal disease. He has a normal ECG and no history of cardiac disease. He is willing and capable of giving written informed consent for study participation. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past 30 days and has not taken any prescription or non-prescription drugs within 7 days prior to the first dose of study medication. He has no history of sensitivity to heparin or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

Ling is a 56 year old woman who was diagnosed with gastric carcinoma last year. She underwent gastrectomy and adjuvant chemotherapy with docetaxel and cisplatin, but unfortunately her cancer progressed. Ling has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and loss of appetite. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both of which are well controlled with medication. She has no known allergies to medications. Her recent labs showed elevated CEA and CA 19-9 levels. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Ling's oncologist has recommended apatinib as a treatment option and Ling has agreed to participate in this study to help evaluate the efficacy and safety of this drug.

The patient is a 60-year-old male with a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is scheduled to undergo a robot-assisted radical cystectomy due to bladder cancer. He has no history of central nervous system disease or surgery. He is currently taking lisinopril for hypertension and atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia. He has a preoperative MMSE score of 28. He is able to provide informed consent and has volunteered to participate in this experiment. He has an ASA status of II.

The patient is a 14-year-old female diagnosed with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) and scheduled to undergo anterior or posterior spinal fusion surgery with instrumentation. She has no previous major orthopedic surgeries and is of any ethnic background. She is able to understand and respond to outcome measures. She does not have allergies to Clonidine or its excipients, galactose intolerance, myocardial disease, arrhythmias, cerebrovascular disease, Raynaud's/Thromboangiitis obliterans, or chronic renal failure. She is not taking any anti-hypertensive agents and does not have a history of depression. She is able to speak English or French and does not have any diagnosed developmental delay that would interfere with understanding the questions being asked. She does not have any major chronic medical conditions and is not pregnant.

A 40-year-old male patient who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented to the clinic for enrollment in the clinical trial. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. His BMI is 28 kg/m2, and his recent HbA1c is 11.2%. He is willing to voluntarily participate in the trial and agrees to monitor his blood glucose at least once a week. He has not taken any other hypoglycemic medications before. The patient does not have a history of severe infection, urinary tract infection, or proliferative diabetic retinopathy. He has never had ketoacidosis, hyperglycemic hyperosmolar status, or lactic acidosis. He has no hepatobiliary disorders or clinically significant kidney disease. The patient is not pregnant, and he is using highly effective birth control methods. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has not undergone any weight loss, banding surgery, or organ transplant. The patient is willing to comply with the trial's requirements and has signed the informed consent.

47 year old man with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with relapse after multiple lines of chemotherapy and bone marrow transplant. Currently with a WBC count of 20,000 and bone marrow biopsy confirming AML. The patient has also had a prior history of Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) with relapse and has undergone multiple lines of chemotherapy. He is currently experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and a decrease in appetite. Past Medical History: - AML with relapse - Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with relapse - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 diabetes - Obesity - Coronary artery disease - Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease - Gout - Osteoarthritis - Depression - Anxiety

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of endometrial cancer that has persisted despite previous curative therapy. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and a history of breast cancer, which was treated with lumpectomy and radiation therapy 7 years ago. She has not received any systemic therapy for her endometrial cancer. She complains of occasional abdominal discomfort but denies any other significant symptoms. Physical examination is notable for a soft, non-tender abdomen with no palpable masses or hepatosplenomegaly. There is no evidence of lower extremity edema. Laboratory studies show a normal complete blood count and normal electrolytes. Serum creatinine is within normal limits. Urinalysis is negative for proteinuria. Electrocardiogram shows normal sinus rhythm. Echocardiogram shows left ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis show persistent disease with multiple peritoneal nodules and enlarged lymph nodes. The largest nodule measures 3 cm in diameter. MRI of the brain is negative for metastases. She has given informed consent and is willing to comply with study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old man diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) six months ago. He has been experiencing a persistent and debilitating cough for the past three months, which has adversely affected his quality of life. He has tried traditional antitussive agents and corticosteroids, but without significant improvement. He is now looking for alternative therapeutic options to control his cough. His laboratory test results are within the normal range, and his diffusion capacity is above 25% predicted while his forced vital capacity is below 80% predicted. He is able to take aspirin daily as prophylactic anti-coagulation. He is willing to adhere to the study protocol, including regular visits to the study center and completing questionnaires. He has not used any experimental drugs or therapy within the past 28 days and has no history of hypersensitivity to thalidomide or lenalidomide.

A 52-year-old man with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years was enrolled in the DAR-312 study, which involved taking experimental drug darusentan to treat resistant hypertension. The patient successfully completed the Maintenance Period of the study and is now being invited to enroll in the long-term safety extension study of darusentan called DORADO-AC-EX. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and has not experienced any study drug-related adverse events during the DAR-312 study. The patient is interested in participating in the extension study to continue receiving the experimental drug and help contribute to the evaluation of its long-term safety.

Patient is a healthy 30-year-old non-smoking woman who has no history of any major or chronic disease. She has a BMI of 23.0 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She has no history of cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease, hypertension, or infections. She is not currently pregnant or lactating, and is willing to use two forms of contraception, one of which is a barrier method, during the study and for 90 days after the last drug administration. She has no history of drug-related allergy or hepatotoxicity. She has not used hormonal contraceptives within 30 days before the first dose of study medication. She is willing to abstain from alcohol, xanthine-containing beverages or food (coffee, tea, cola, chocolate, "energy drinks") from 72 hours prior to entry in the clinical site center until discharge. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating potential drug-drug interactions between darunavir and danoprevir when administered together with low-dose ritonavir in healthy volunteers.

The patient is a 55 year-old man who has been on hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to end-stage renal disease. He reports that he has been experiencing severe itching on his arms, legs, and back for the past few months. The itching is worse during and after his hemodialysis sessions and is affecting his quality of life. He rates his worst itching as 8 out of 10 on a visual analog scale (VAS) and has experienced this level of itching for at least 5 days during the first observation period. He has not started or changed pruritus treatment in the past 13 days and has not received ultraviolet treatment in the past 27 days. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. He has no significant history of liver disease, heart disease, stroke, or malignant tumor. He has no history of depression, schizophrenia, dementia, epilepsia, convulsive seizure, drug addiction, or alcoholism. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years. He experiences freezing of gait (FOG) episodes that have progressively worsened over the past year. He walks independently without the use of walking devices but has noticed a significant decrease in his mobility due to FOG. He takes levodopa/carbidopa for symptom management, but it has become less effective over time. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no pre-existing or active major neurological diseases other than PD. He has not had any previous history of seizures and does not have any implanted metallic objects that would contraindicate rTMS. The patient is motivated to improve his mobility and cognitive function and is willing to undergo the five consecutive daily sessions of NIBS.

56 year old woman recently diagnosed with breast cancer within the last 15 weeks. She is scheduled to receive her first cycle of first-line pharmacological anti-cancer treatment at an outpatient center. She is literate in German language and able to understand written information or follow an interview. She is not currently receiving care from a palliative care team and is not being treated solely with surgical or radiation therapy.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has no history of smoking, alcohol or drug abuse. His body mass index is within the normal range (23 kg/m^2). The patient has not participated in any clinical trial in the past 3 weeks and has not taken any medication in the past 3 weeks. He has no symptoms of any illness and has not donated blood in the past 3 weeks. The patient's ophthalmic findings are normal, with no ocular hypertension, glaucoma, retinal vasculopathy or other retinal diseases. The patient has no refractive errors greater than 1 diopter. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the nature and purpose of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic back pain for the past 10 years. She is married to a 50-year-old man who has been supportive but has difficulty understanding her pain. The patient reports feeling frustrated and isolated due to her pain and the strain it has put on their relationship. The couple has been married for 15 years and has two children. The patient has tried various pain management techniques but has not found significant relief. She is interested in exploring a new approach to managing her pain that involves her partner as well. They are both open to participating in a research study that may help improve their quality of life and relationship.

Patient is a 70-year-old French-speaking man who was recently diagnosed with neurocognitive disorder. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia for which he takes medication regularly. He has noticed recent difficulties with decision-making, particularly in complex situations. He has agreed to participate in the IMAGISION study to explore the contribution of functional neuroimaging (functional MRI and high resolution EEG) to geriatric expertise, associated with the performance of a battery of neuropsychological tests in the evaluation of decision-making capacity. The patient does not have delirium or major depressive symptoms, and there are no MRI contraindications.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes two years ago. Despite taking Metformin and basal insulin, her blood sugar levels have not been well-controlled, with recent HbA1c levels of 8.5%. She reports feeling fatigued and experiencing frequent episodes of hyperglycemia. She has a history of high blood pressure, but it is well-controlled with medication. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. She works in an office job and tries to maintain an active lifestyle by going for walks during her lunch break. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her diabetes management.

A 34-year-old woman presents with symptoms of major depressive disorder, including a persistent feeling of sadness, loss of interest in activities, difficulty concentrating, and changes in appetite and sleep patterns. She reports having tried multiple antidepressants in the past but has not achieved a significant improvement in her symptoms. The patient's HAM-D17 Total Score at the baseline visit is 20. She has no history of epilepsy or seizure disorders, and no significant psychiatric comorbidities. The patient is willing to discontinue all prohibited psychotropic medication during the study period. She has not received electroconvulsive therapy in the last 10 years.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital for cardiac catheterization due to chest pain. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. She is currently taking medications for her conditions. Her BMI is 28, which is considered overweight. The procedure was performed via femoral venous access, and suture-mediated closure was used to achieve hemostasis. The procedure duration was 45 minutes, and she was under anticoagulation therapy. She reports no complications at the time of discharge. She is able to provide consent for participation in the study.

30-year-old male with no significant past medical history, non-smoker, non-alcoholic, and no history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is in good general health and able to comply with all study requirements. He has not had any acute or chronic infections requiring systemic antibiotic treatment or antiviral therapy within the last 7 days. He has not received any other vaccine within 4 weeks prior to enrollment in this study or planning to receive any vaccine during the study. The patient has not had any laboratory-confirmed seasonal or pandemic influenza disease or received any seasonal or pandemic influenza vaccine within the past 6 months. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. The patient is not pregnant, nursing, or of childbearing potential.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 4. He has been on antihyperglycemic therapy, including insulin and sulfonylurea, for the past 6 months. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 25 ml/min/1.73 m^2 by the Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) formula. His hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) level is 8.5% and his fasting plasma glucose (FPG) is 220 mg/dL at screening. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 35 kg/m^2. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and no significant cerebrovascular or cardiovascular diseases. He has no history of allergies or anaphylactic reactions to any medication. He is fluent in English and able to understand and comply with the study requirements. He has signed the informed consent form and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study period. He is able to monitor his glucose levels at home and record his blood glucose concentrations in a diary.

A 20-year-old female college student is currently enrolled at Rutgers University, studying psychology. She has been feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and the transition to remote learning has been difficult for her. She has been experiencing symptoms of anxiety, including restlessness, difficulty concentrating, and feeling constantly on edge. She has no history of mental illness and has never received any form of psychological treatment. She has an iPhone and is comfortable using it for the study requirements. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.
