A 30-year-old healthy female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2 who works as an accountant is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new influenza treatment. She has no history of chronic or acute illnesses and takes no medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol, and she denies any illicit drug use. She has not received any live or attenuated influenza vaccines in the past year. She is willing to adhere to the study's lifestyle guidelines and agrees to use two acceptable birth control methods throughout the study and for 30 days after the last dose of the IMP. She understands the study's purpose and is willing and able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a premature infant born at 32 weeks and weighing 1.7 kg. The baby was delivered via C-section due to maternal hypertension. The baby required some respiratory support in the form of nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP) for the first few days of life but it was discontinued after the baby stabilized. The baby is now 10 days old and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The baby has not received any osteopathic treatment yet but is expected to receive it in the next 4 days. The baby's parents have given their consent for participation in the study. The baby has not been transferred to/from another hospital and has not been diagnosed with any genetic disorders, congenital abnormalities, cardiovascular abnormalities, neurological disorders, or any other medical conditions that would exclude them from the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old male from South Korea who wears glasses for myopia with a spherical equivalent between 0.00 and -11.00 diopters (D). He has no history of ocular diseases such as glaucoma or age-related macular degeneration, and he does not have corneal abnormalities such as keratoconus or forme fruste keratoconus. The patient has not undergone any ocular or intraocular surgery, and he has no corneal scarring that would preclude accurate measurements. He has no history of diabetes mellitus. The patient does not currently use any eye drops, especially anti-IOP agents, which can change the biomechanical properties of the cornea. The patient is willing to participate in the study and undergo measurements of corneal biomechanical properties using a dynamic Scheimpflug analyzer.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) 5 years ago. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been receiving Edoxaban for stroke prevention for the past year. She is currently experiencing occasional palpitations and shortness of breath. She is otherwise active and independent in her daily activities. She has no history of bleeding disorders or stroke. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study to evaluate the safety of Edoxaban in patients diagnosed with AF who are currently on Edoxaban therapy for prevention of stroke in routine clinical practice in Turkey for stroke prevention up to 1 year following treatment. She will be monitored by specialized and non-specialized physicians in hospital centers.

The patient is a 60 year old male who has been recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He is scheduled for an elective colorectal surgery at one of the participating hospitals. He has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His most recent HbA1c level was 7.2%. He is currently taking metformin 1000mg twice daily for his diabetes. He has no history of gastroparesis or other significant gastrointestinal issues. He has been instructed to fast for 12 hours prior to his surgery, which is the current standard practice. He is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the safety of carbohydrate loading prior to his surgery.

A 52-year-old woman who had previously undergone hysterectomy for benign reasons is experiencing symptoms of vaginal cuff prolapse. She has been experiencing discomfort during intercourse for the past few months, and her pelvic exams have shown a visible prolapse of the vaginal cuff. She has no chronic diseases and is not taking any medications that may interfere with the operation. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare two surgical methods for treating vaginal cuff prolapse. She has no history of oncology and the prolapse is localized.

The patient is a 30-year-old male diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 2 years ago. He is currently on insulin therapy and has a stable HbA1c level of 7.5%. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or other major medical conditions. His BMI is 25 and he weighs 80 kg. He has no active infections and has not been exposed to tuberculosis or mycosis in the last 3 months. He has no history of immune suppressive treatment or demyelinating disease. His renal function is normal with a GFR of 90 ml/min/1.73 m2 body surface. He has no proliferative retinopathy. He is mentally stable and able to comply with the procedures of the study protocol. He is willing to provide written informed consent for participation in the study.

45-year-old male with a BMI of 32 presents for a routine medical check-up at the clinic. He reports a sedentary lifestyle with a history of smoking and occasional alcohol consumption. No significant past medical history or medication use is reported. Physical examination reveals obesity and no other remarkable findings. Blood pressure is within normal limits. Routine laboratory tests are ordered, including lipid profile, liver and renal function tests, and fasting glucose. The patient is interested in participating in research studies related to obesity and is willing to undergo additional testing.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma. He has no significant medical history, except for hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. He works as a teacher and has a supportive family. He has not received any previous chemotherapy for his cancer. He has a performance status of 1 (ECOG) and is able to perform most of his daily activities without assistance. His physical exam and laboratory studies are within normal limits, except for a slightly elevated alkaline phosphatase level. His CT scan shows a large mass in the head of the pancreas with involvement of the adjacent blood vessels. He has suitable vascular anatomy for the PRVI procedure. He understands the study requirements and is willing to participate in the trial.

A 35-year-old male with a BMI of 31.2 is interested in participating in the study. He works a sedentary job and is not involved in any regular exercise. He has a history of overeating and indulging in sweetened beverages. He reports consuming at least two sweetened beverages per day and eating fast food for lunch three times a week. He has tried to lose weight in the past by following different diets, but he has not been able to maintain any weight loss. He has no known allergies or medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is willing to consume macaroni and cheese during breakfast and lunch hours and is willing to eat at least 100 grams of carbohydrates for three days prior to each test day. He is interested in learning about how the form of food affects appetite hormones and is willing to participate in all three phases of the study.

Pt is a 50yo M with a history of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without known targetable molecular alterations in EGFR, ALK, or ROS1, which has metastasized to 3 sites. He has been on systemic therapy for the past 4 months and has shown no signs of disease progression. The patient has a good performance status of 1 and is willing to participate in the study. He has measurable disease at baseline and all 3 sites are technically amendable to SBRT. The patient has no serious medical co-morbidities that would preclude radiotherapy and has adequate baseline organ function to allow SBRT to all relevant targets. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is not pregnant or lactating.

50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and occasional chest pain was referred to the Department of Diagnostic Radiology and Nuclear Medicine at the University of Maryland for evaluation of pulmonary thromboembolic disease. The patient's body mass index (BMI) is 32 kg/m2. The patient has not been diagnosed with decreased renal function and has not had any major allergic reactions to contrast in the past. The patient has given written consent for intravenous contrast administration. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not had a recent serum creatinine level check but will have one done prior to the CTPA scan with contrast to ensure that the level does not exceed 2.0 mg/dL.

A 35-year-old female patient visited the emergency department with a sudden onset of low back pain that has been bothering her for the past week. She has never experienced such pain before and has not taken any pain medication in the past. She reports that the pain is constant, sharp, and worsens with movement. She has no history of trauma or injury to her back. The physical exam reveals tenderness and muscle spasm in the lumbar area. The patient has no history of chronic back pain and has not been taking pain medication prior to this episode.

60 year-old patient who is scheduled for a total knee replacement due to severe osteoarthritis that has been unresponsive to conservative management. The patient reports chronic pain in the knee joint that has severely limited their ability to perform daily activities and has caused significant functional impairment. The patient has an ASA physical status of 2 and is medically stable. There is no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. The patient is able to read and understand English and is willing to participate in a longitudinal observational study for 6 months after surgery. The patient has not participated in any other investigational drug studies within the last 3 months.

A 64 year old woman has been diagnosed with aortic valve disease and has been recommended for aortic valve replacement surgery. She has agreed to participate in the Foldax Clinical trial and is willing to comply with all follow-up evaluations for up to 5 years. She has not had prior valve surgery and does not require emergency surgery. She has no recent history of stroke, cerebrovascular accident (CVA) or transient ischemic attack (TIA) within 3 months prior to planned valve surgery. Her echocardiographic left ventricular ejection fraction is above 25%. She does not have an intra-cardiac thrombus or vegetation. She does not have a history of substance abuse within the last 5 years prior to implant. Additionally, she is not currently incarcerated, pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the duration of participation in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with abdominal pain, fever, and chills. He had a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, which were both poorly controlled. He underwent an exploratory laparotomy for suspected appendicitis, but intraoperative findings revealed a perforated diverticulum in the sigmoid colon. The patient was diagnosed with severe sepsis and was transferred to the general surgical ICU for further management. On admission to the ICU, he required vasopressor support and was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. His laboratory values showed leukocytosis, elevated lactate levels, and acute kidney injury. He received a total of 4 liters of crystalloid fluid resuscitation within the first 6 hours of diagnosis. He also received packed red blood cells and fresh frozen plasma for coagulopathy. The patient remained in the ICU for 12 days due to persistent organ failure and required mechanical ventilation for 6 days. He was eventually discharged from the hospital but required long-term dialysis for his acute kidney injury. The patient consented to participate in this clinical trial to further contribute to the understanding of severe sepsis/septic shock and to help identify risk factors for poor outcomes in surgical patients.

The patient is a 50-year-old female diagnosed with non-metastatic breast cancer. She is scheduled to undergo adjuvant chemotherapy based on the use of anthracyclines. She reports no history of depression, anemia, heart disease or decompensated hypertension, and her thyroid function is normal. She is currently not taking any medications, and her past medical history is unremarkable. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is experiencing fatigue before starting the chemotherapy, but her fatigue score on the brief fatigue inventory is not high enough to be considered as having manifested fatigue. She is willing to participate in the study, and blood samples will be collected before and 21 days after the start of chemotherapy to analyze potential biomarkers of chemotherapy-related fatigue.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman living in a rural area in Burkina Faso. She is married and has three children aged 7, 10, and 12 years old. She works as a farmer and earns a modest income. She has noticed that her children often get sick with fever, cough, and other symptoms, and she is concerned about their health. She herself has had fever and cough in the past and had to visit the local health center, where she was prescribed antibiotics. However, she is not sure whether the antibiotics are always necessary or whether there are other ways to manage the illness. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial, as she believes it could help her family and other people in her community. She is willing to provide blood and other samples and adhere to study procedures. She understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and has given her written consent. She is able to attend the health center for follow-up visits and is willing to return for the follow-up visit on day 7 (+/- 2 days).

A 6-month-old male infant is admitted to the hospital with symptoms of severe gastroenteritis. He has been vomiting and experiencing diarrhea for the past 3 days. The infant was born on January 15, 2021, and is currently 6.5 kg in weight. The mother reports that the infant has been exclusively breastfed and has not received any vaccinations yet. The infant's stool sample is tested positive for rotavirus by PCR. The mother consents for the infant to participate in the study. The infant is otherwise healthy with no underlying medical conditions. The family has no history of adverse vaccine reactions. The infant is currently being treated for dehydration and will remain in the hospital for observation.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman in her first pregnancy at term with no significant medical history. She is scheduled to undergo Cesarean section under spinal anesthesia due to breech presentation. She has no known allergies and takes no medications. Her physical examination is within normal limits. Her vital signs include BP: 120/70 mmHg, HR: 80/min, and BMI: 25. She is able to comprehend and use the verbal rating pain scoring system and patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) pump. There is no evidence of congenital coagulopathy or anatomical abnormalities, and no localized infections. The patient has not used any drugs that may interfere with ropivacaine metabolism. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the purpose and nature of the study.

A 28-year-old female graduate student who is currently pursuing her PhD in neuroscience is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She has no history of any significant medical conditions, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She does not smoke or consume alcohol, and she is not taking any medications. Her BMI is 22, and she has no history of any metal implants or surgeries. She wears contact lenses and has no hearing aids, implants, or pacemakers. She has no history of permanent makeup, tattoos, or dental implants. She is not currently pregnant nor breastfeeding. She is interested in exploring the relationship between CO2 levels and the regional BOLD signal and is willing to participate in breathing exercises to modulate arterial PaCO2 levels.

25 year old male with a BMI of 25.5 kg/m2 who is generally healthy and a non-smoker. He has no history of deep vein thrombosis or intestinal disorders. His fasting blood glucose level is 90mg/dL. He does not smoke or drink more than 3 alcoholic drinks per day. He is not taking any lipid-lowering medications or dietary supplements affecting plasma cholesterol concentration. He is interested in participating in the study to assess the beneficial effects of egg consumption on carotenoids absorption from a complex meal, beyond those found in egg.

A 35-year-old man presented to the clinic with a history of cocaine addiction. He has been using cocaine for the past 5 years and has tried to quit several times but has been unsuccessful. He is currently receiving treatment for his addiction at a Samaritan Daytop Village facility. He is fluent in English and is willing to participate in the study. He does not have a history of neurological disorders or seizures, and he currently takes no medications that would interfere with the study. He has no contraindicated metallic implants or devices and has not experienced head trauma with loss of consciousness for more than 30 minutes. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

An 82-year-old English-speaking woman with advanced dementia resides in a long-term care facility. Her family reports that she has been experiencing weight loss, decreased appetite, and increased confusion over the past few weeks. She is currently unable to communicate verbally and requires assistance with all activities of daily living. Her medical history includes hypertension, diabetes, and a previous stroke. She is not receiving any palliative care services currently. Her Palliative Performance Scale score is 40%. Her family has expressed interest in learning more about palliative care and end-of-life care options for their loved one.

Patient is a 55-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and is scheduled for transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) surgery. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He denies any history of heart disease or respiratory problems. His BMI is 28, BP: 130/80, HR: 70/min. He is otherwise healthy and does not have any other medical conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

This is a 9 year-old male who is in good health with no known chronic medical conditions. He is currently in the 5th grade and has no history of food allergies or intolerances. He has normal vision and his most recent BMI-for-age percentile was in the 50th percentile. He enjoys playing basketball and video games, and his favorite subject in school is science. He has an IQ score of 102. His parents have given consent for him to participate in the study and he is excited to be a part of it.

There is no patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is focused on a population of children in the Archdiocese of Newark School System between third and sixth grade. The study aims to determine if administration of a daily chewable multivitamin-mineral supplement during the academic school year will lead to improved academic performance. Children who are currently taking multivitamins at least five days a week or did not take the Assessment of Skills and Knowledge exam at the completion of the third grade will be excluded. All other eligible children will be randomly assigned to receive either the multivitamin-mineral supplement or an inactive placebo daily during the school week for a 7-8 month period.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been hospitalized due to complications from Crohn's disease. He is currently unable to eat by mouth and requires intravenous nutrition for his recovery. The patient has been receiving PN for the past 5 days and is expected to require PN for at least another 7 days. The patient has no history of allergies or other medical conditions that would exclude him from participation in the study. The patient has been informed about the study and has provided written consent to participate. The patient will be randomized to receive either soybean oil-based lipid emulsion (Intralipid) or olive oil-based lipid emulsion (ClinOleic) as part of his intravenous nutrition treatment. The patient will be monitored for any complications related to the PN treatment, and his length of stay and mortality will be recorded. Metabolic, nutritional, infectious, and inflammatory parameters will also be evaluated in the patient to assess the effects of the different lipid emulsions on these parameters.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is concerned about her risk of contracting COVID-19 due to her job as a nurse in a hospital. She has not had any symptoms of the virus, but wants to be proactive and get tested. She has heard about a new screening program that uses saliva samples instead of nasopharyngeal swabs, and is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of this new approach. She is willing to provide both a saliva sample and a nasopharyngeal swab for comparison, and has no objections to her data being collected for research purposes.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who was diagnosed with giant cell arteritis (GCA) 2 years ago. She has been treated with corticosteroids since her diagnosis and has experienced multiple relapses despite being on treatment. She presents with symptoms of a new relapse, including severe headache, scalp tenderness, and jaw claudication. She has also noticed decreased vision in her right eye. Her sedimentation rate is elevated to 65 mm/h, and her C-reactive protein is 35 mg/L. A temporal artery biopsy confirms the diagnosis of GCA. The patient is currently on prednisone 15 mg/day, but her symptoms have not improved. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatments for GCA relapse. She has no history of allergy to medications or latex. She has never received any organ transplant or hematopoietic marrow allograft. She has no history of cancer or chronic viral hepatitis B or C. She has no active infection at the time of screening. She has no history of psychosis or legal protection. The patient is compliant with her medications and able to provide written consent.

The patient is a 68 year-old woman who lives in Santa Cruz do Sul, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. She has a sedentary lifestyle and has not engaged in any physical activity for the past year. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m², and her waist circumference is 90 cm. She has no history of systemic arterial hypertension or any other major medical conditions. She takes no medication and has no cognitive deficits. She has never used a vibratory platform before. She is interested in participating in the study, and after clarification of doubts, she signs the written consent form. The academics from the nutrition degree of the University of Santa Cruz do Sul (UNISC) perform nutritional evaluations on the subject, and she agrees to keep her eating habits unchanged throughout the trial. She is then evaluated for her level of physical activity, socio-economic status, and general health. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. She is randomly assigned to the group that will receive the intervention with the vibratory platform.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes five years ago. She is currently using an insulin pump and checks her blood glucose levels multiple times a day. She lives with her husband and two children. She works as a teacher and enjoys hiking and cooking. Her skin phototype is 3. She has no known allergies to medical grade alcohol or adhesives. She has no extensive skin changes or tattoos on the probe application site. She has no history of reduced circulation or Parkinson's disease. She has not undergone dialysis treatment. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance non-invasive glucose monitoring technology. She is able to understand and read Danish, and is willing to comply with the protocol instructions. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials.

A 48-year-old woman presents with a history of ovarian cancer. She was diagnosed with stage IIIc ovarian cancer 2 years ago and has undergone maximal cytoreductive surgery followed by chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel. She had a complete response to treatment and has been in remission for the past 6 months. She is now experiencing a relapse with measurable disease on radiologic imaging. Her medical history is significant only for a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She does not have any other active primary tumors and has not received more than one chemotherapy regimen for ovarian cancer. She has adequate hepatic, renal, and marrow function, with AST/ALT levels below three times the upper normal limit, creatinine levels below two times the upper normal limit, and ANC levels above two. Her hemoglobin level is above 90 g/L. She has an ECOG performance status score of 2. She has a negative pregnancy test and is using adequate contraception. She does not have any serious infections or brain metastases, nor does she have severe gastrointestinal symptoms. She does not have grade 2 or higher neuropathy. She is willing to participate in the study and comply with its procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing discomfort and pain in his right groin area for the past few months. After a physical examination and diagnostic tests, he has been diagnosed with an inguinal hernia that requires surgical repair with mesh. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history, and his American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score is II. He has no known allergies to local anesthetics. The patient will undergo elective unilateral inguinal herniography with "mesh" under general anesthesia. He has been enrolled in a clinical trial to study the effect of subcostal transversus abdominis plane block in subacute postoperative pain after inguinal hernia repair. The trial involves two groups, and the patient has been randomly assigned to the subcostal transversus abdominis plane block (STAP) group. After standard general anesthesia application, he will receive 1 gram of paracetamol and 100 mg of contramal, and after surgical closure, transversus abdominis plane block will be applied in the subcostal area to provide postoperative analgesia.

32F with a history of bipolar disorder type I, with a history of four or more symptomatic relapses in the past year, was referred to psychiatry for evaluation of treatment options. She reports having experienced manic episodes that lasted for several weeks, followed by periods of depression. She reports having had difficulty adhering to her medication regimen, which has resulted in frequent relapses. She denies any current psychotic features including hallucinations or delusions. The patient has no current medical conditions that would preclude treatment with Risperdal Consta(TM). Upon examination, the patient had a score of 12 on the Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) and a score of 10 on the Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression-17 item (HAM-D17). She has no history of non-response to Risperidal Consta(TM) and reports no significant suicide risk. She is willing to participate in the study and provide voluntary, written informed consent to participate in this investigation, and is able to understand the study protocol and participate in the outcome measurements.

The patient is a 22-year-old female who has been experiencing pain and swelling in her gums due to her wisdom teeth. She has been referred for third molar extraction and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of the anti-inflammatory drug etanercept (Enbrel) on relieving pain and swelling after the surgery. She is in good general health and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is not allergic to aspirin or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Her past medical history is non-significant, and she is not currently taking any medications that could confound assessment of the inflammatory response or analgesia. She is willing to undergo the surgical procedure and to return for follow-up appointments. She is a candidate for conscious sedation during the surgery.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion. He has a past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently on medications for these conditions, including metoprolol, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 55. He is being referred for scintigraphy to assess myocardial ischemia. He is able to give informed written consent and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no known allergies to IV contrast, but he does have mild renal impairment with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 55 ml/min/1.73m2. He does not have severe uncontrolled asthma and is not claustrophobic.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour (NET) of the lung. He was diagnosed with Grade 2 NET six months ago and has previously received one line of systemic therapy with sunitinib. He has radiological documentation of disease progression within 24 weeks of study enrolment. His ECOG performance status is 1. His bone marrow function, liver function, and renal function are within normal limits. He is not currently on any other anticancer therapy except for somatostatin analogues for functional control. He has no history of autoimmune disease, active infection, or significant acute or chronic medical conditions. He has not received prior treatment with PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA-4 inhibitors. He is willing and able to comply with all study requirements, including timing and nature of treatment and required assessments. He has signed the written informed consent and is aware of the highly effective contraception requirement.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of major depressive disorder, confirmed by Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual. The patient has been experiencing symptoms for the past 3 months, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and worthlessness, as well as loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has a Montgomery-Asberg Depression Scale (MADRS) score of 22 at screening and baseline. The patient has no history of seizures, head trauma, or any clinically significant finding on the neurologic examination. She has never been diagnosed with bipolar or schizoaffective disorder, and has no history of psychotic symptoms during the current major depressive episode. The patient has not responded to two previous antidepressant trials of adequate dose and duration during the current major depressive episode, as determined by the local rater and confirmed by an independent, remote rater prior to the baseline visit. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 26 kg/m2 and weighs 65 kg. The patient reports no history of alcohol or drug-dependence or abuse by Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th edition criteria and confirmed by Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual specific for Clinical Trials within 12 months prior to Screening. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study. The patient is able to understand the purpose, potential benefits and risks of the study and has provided signed and dated informed consent.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic complaining of fatigue, weakness and abdominal bloating. He had a history of heavy alcohol consumption for the past 10 years. His liver function tests were abnormal and he was diagnosed with chronic liver disease. He is currently on the waiting list for a liver transplantation. He has lost 5 kg in the past month and feels weak all the time. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is able to read and write, and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve his nutritional status.

A 50-year-old woman has been referred for colorectal cancer screening. She has no current symptoms, but she has a family history of colon cancer. Her last colonoscopy was performed 5 years ago, and it was normal. She is currently taking no medications, and her medical history is unremarkable. She has no allergies to any medications. She is willing to participate in a randomized controlled trial comparing two different bowel preparations for CT colonography. She understands that she may be assigned to either the group that follows a low-fiber diet or the group that does not restrict fiber intake. She is willing to follow the instructions given to her and attend all necessary appointments. She has signed the informed consent form and is ready to participate in the study.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with a body mass index (BMI) between 18 and 30 kg/m2. He has no history of respiratory, gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic, haematological, lymphatic, neurological, cardiovascular, psychiatric, musculoskeletal, genitourinary, immunological, dermatological, endocrine, connective tissue diseases or disorders. He has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse and does not consume more than 14 units of alcohol a week. He has no significant infection or known inflammatory process and has no acute gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, heartburn). He is not a vegetarian or vegan and has no other medical dietary restrictions. He is able and willing to give written informed consent and communicate reliably with the investigator. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently participating in another study. He is a non-smoker or ex-smoker and his urine pregnancy test is negative at screening and admission to each treatment period.

This study is looking for patients who have suffered a fracture of their upper arm bone (humerus). The fracture must not involve the shoulder or elbow joint, and must be a closed injury (i.e. not an open wound). Patients must be aged 16 years or older, and able to provide informed consent in English. Patients will be excluded if they have certain medical conditions that make them unfit for surgery, have additional spine or limb injuries that may impact on their ability to undergo functional rehabilitation, or are unable to provide informed consent in English. Patients will also be excluded if they have fractures that are completely undisplaced, are considered to be an absolute indication for surgery, or if they have periprosthetic or pathological fractures. Patients who are pregnant or unable to comply with post-operative data gathering will also be excluded. If you are eligible for the study and agree to participate, you will be randomised to either operative or non-operative management of your humeral shaft fracture. Patients who undergo surgical fixation will have a plate and screw fixation of their fracture, while patients who undergo non-operative management will have their arm immobilised in a U-slab or hanging cast, followed by a lightweight prefabricated humeral brace. You will be followed-up in person at several timepoints over a one-year period, and your progress will be assessed using a combination of physical examination, X-rays, and patient-reported outcome scores. The investigators hope that the results of this study will help to inform better decision-making when managing patients with humeral shaft fractures.

A 49-year-old active-duty male service member presented with recurrent right shoulder pain over the last 6 months. The right biceps tendon was tender, with a positive Speed's test and Yergason's test. MRI revealed a partial-thickness tear of the biceps tendon with tenosynovitis. The patient underwent an uncomplicated arthroscopic biceps tenodesis surgery. The patient has no history of smoking, drug or alcohol abuse. There is no history of previous shoulder surgery or significant trauma. He is otherwise healthy with no chronic medical conditions. The patient has been cleared to begin rehabilitation by the surgeon and is scheduled for physical therapy starting in 2 weeks.

The patient is a 65-year-old Japanese male who has been experiencing pain and cramping in his legs during physical activity. He reports a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication. He is 170 cm tall and weighs 75 kg (BMI: 25.95). He is retired and spends most of his time at home. He does not smoke or use any drugs. His BP: 140/90 mmHg, HR: 75/min. His Rutherford Clinical Category Score is 3. He has undergone angiography, which confirmed ≥ 50% stenosis in the superficial femoral artery. The length of the target lesion is 10 cm, and the reference vessel diameter is 5.5 mm. He is interested in participating in the TurboHawk™ Japan Trial to alleviate his symptoms and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with epilepsy for the past 10 years. She is currently taking lamotrigine twice daily as a maintenance treatment and has been stable for the past 6 months. She has no history of poor compliance and is willing to provide informed consent. She has been admitted to the hospital for diagnostic evaluation due to recent unexplained seizures. She has no known disorders of gastric motility or any other condition that may alter the pharmacokinetics of the study drug(s) over the subsequent 5/6 days. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the study and may be randomized to continue on her current lamotrigine or be switched to an alternative equivalent product.

The patient is a 58 year old Dutch-speaking male who was admitted to the hospital 10 days ago after experiencing a right hemispheric ischemic stroke. Upon admission, he was diagnosed with aphasia, which has significantly impacted his ability to communicate with his family and healthcare providers. He has no history of severe psychiatric or cognitive disorders. Imaging (CT) prior to inclusion confirmed the diagnosis of stroke. The patient is able to read and understand simple words and phrases, but has difficulty with expressive language and conversation. He is motivated to participate in therapy and has given signed informed consent to participate in the study.

45 yo F with a history of alcohol dependence for the past 10 years. Patient reports drinking 6-8 beers a day, more on weekends. She has tried to quit drinking on her own several times but has been unsuccessful. She has a family history of alcohol dependence and has a stressful job as a nurse. Patient reports experiencing withdrawal symptoms such as tremors, sweating, and anxiety when she tries to quit drinking. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her alcohol dependence. Her liver function tests are within normal limits, but she reports experiencing epigastric pain after heavy drinking episodes. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help reduce her alcohol consumption and alleviate withdrawal symptoms. Past Medical History: Hypertension, GERD, Depression, Alcohol Dependence. Current Medications: Lisinopril, Pantoprazole, Sertraline.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with hypertension for the past 6 months. His blood pressure has been consistently high with readings ranging from 150/95 to 160/100 mmHg. He has a history of high cholesterol, with triglyceride levels of 2.1 mmol/L and HDL levels of 0.8 mmol/L. He has a fasting plasma glucose level of 6.2 mmol/L and a waist circumference of 105 cm. His BMI is 29.3, which is within the eligible range for the study. He has not been diagnosed with any diseases of the heart, liver, or kidneys. He does not have any chronic inflammatory diseases and is not taking any medication for any other medical condition. He has not used any probiotic products regularly in the past three months. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the probiotic-based product can help control his blood pressure and improve his overall health.

47 year old male scheduled for elective surgery to remove a benign tumor in the abdomen. The patient has no significant medical history and is physically fit for surgery. He has no known allergies to any medications and is able to breathe easily on room air. The patient is willing to be randomly assigned to any of the four anesthetic induction techniques in the study. He is able to follow instructions and provide informed consent for participation in the trial.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with extensive stage small cell lung cancer. The patient underwent four cycles of chemotherapy with cisplatin/etoposide and achieved a partial remission per RECIST 1.1. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has adequate bone marrow and hepatic function. The patient has not undergone any major surgery within the past 4 weeks and is not currently using any immunosuppressants. The patient has no active infections requiring systemic therapy and does not have HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B virus, or hepatitis C virus infection. The patient does not have any autoimmune disease or persisting toxicity related to prior therapy. The patient is not pregnant and has not received any vaccinations within the past 4 weeks. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to the study drugs and does not have any cardiovascular disease. The patient does not have any untreated central nervous system (CNS) metastases or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. The patient does not have any active secondary malignancy or active pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the combination of rucaparib and nivolumab as maintenance therapy for small cell lung carcinoma.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a suspected gynecologic malignancy. She has never had surgery before and is feeling anxious about the upcoming procedure. She is interested in exploring complementary therapies to help manage her stress and pain. She has a history of depression and anxiety, for which she takes medication and sees a therapist. She is fluent in English and able to read and understand study materials.

The patient is a 102 year old man residing in Moscow. He has lived through two World Wars and has many interesting stories to tell about his life experiences. He has never married and has no children. He was a farmer and worked on his farm for most of his life. He has always been an active man and enjoys walking, gardening and reading. He has never smoked and only drinks occasionally. He has a history of hypertension, but it is well-controlled with medication. In recent years, he has developed a hearing impairment and some difficulty with mobility, but he still maintains a positive attitude towards life. He is excited to participate in this study and hopes that the results will help others to age in a healthy way. He has no cognitive impairment and is able to communicate effectively in Russian.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) during a routine check-up with her primary care physician. She has no previous history of heart disease and is currently not being treated by a cardiologist or electrophysiologist. The diagnosis of AF was confirmed on electrocardiogram. She speaks Dutch fluently and is capable of providing written informed consent. She has no cognitive impairment and is willing to participate in the study. She has not received arrhythmologic consult or systematic follow-up at a cardiologist for AF in the past 2 years. She is not terminally ill and is not participating in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is concerned about her weight and overall health. She is a mother of two and works as a part-time accountant. She has a family history of diabetes and heart disease. She has tried various diets in the past, but has had little success in losing weight and maintaining a healthy lifestyle. She is interested in learning more about how certain foods, like pasta, can impact her weight and overall health. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help advance knowledge in this area. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She has a BMI of 29.5, which puts her in the overweight category. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is physically active and enjoys going for walks and practicing yoga. She is looking for a dietary intervention that is sustainable and can help her achieve her goals of losing weight and improving her overall health.

A 58 year old woman has been suffering from atrial fibrillation for the past year. She experiences shortness of breath, fatigue and palpitations. She has been prescribed medications, but they have not been effective in restoring her normal heart rhythm. She has been advised by her doctor to undergo mitral valve surgery and radiofrequency modified Maze procedure, which she has agreed to. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She does not have any other significant medical history or allergies. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is physically active and engages in regular exercise. She is excited to participate in this clinical trial to help evaluate the mid-term results of radiofrequency modified Maze procedure in mitral patients.

A 7-year-old child who was previously enrolled in the CoolCap clinical trial for neonatal encephalopathy. The child is a survivor of the condition and has reached the age of 7-8 years. The child's parents have given their consent for their child to participate in this observational follow-up study. The study will involve a telephone interview with the child's parents to assess their child's functional performance using the WeeFIM questionnaire, which measures a range of abilities from independent functioning to needing total assistance. The aim of the study is to examine the relationship between the outcome previously measured at 18 months and the child's functional outcome at school age. This will help identify the children who may require further neurodevelopmental testing.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with severe asthma since childhood. She has been taking inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators daily to manage her symptoms. She has experienced several exacerbations in the past year, leading to emergency room visits and hospitalizations. Her past medical history is significant for allergies to dust and pollen. She is a non-smoker and lives with her husband and two children. She works as a teacher and has been teaching remotely since the outbreak of CoVid-19. She has been following strict social distancing measures and wearing a mask whenever she leaves the house. She was recently diagnosed with CoVid-19 and was admitted to the hospital due to severe respiratory symptoms. She is being treated with oxygen therapy and remdesivir. She is willing to participate in the study to help researchers better understand the prevalence of critical forms of CoVid-19 in patients with chronic respiratory disease.

A 48-year-old male patient with a history of a proximal humerus fracture 12 weeks ago presented to the orthopedic clinic with persistent pain and stiffness in his right shoulder and arm. He has been experiencing burning pain, swelling, and discoloration in his right hand and fingers, which is affecting his daily activities. The patient was diagnosed with complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS I) and referred for physical therapy treatment. He has no history of autoimmune or peripheral vascular diseases, diabetes, or T4 syndrome. He has never received physical therapy for his current condition. He is a non-smoker and has no illicit drug use history. The patient is currently taking over-the-counter pain medications for pain relief. The patient is motivated to participate in the study and understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the treatment.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus for the past 3 years. She has been on basal-bolus treatment for the past 6 months and her current HbA1c is 9.2%. She has a BMI of 28.5 kg/m^2. She has no known allergies to insulin or related products. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant. She has not received any trial drug within the past month. She has no mental incapacity, unwillingness or language barriers precluding adequate understanding or cooperation. She has no proliferative retinopathy or maculopathy requiring acute treatment within the last six months, no recurrent major hypoglycemia, no impaired hepatic or renal function, no cardiac problems, and no uncontrolled hypertension (treated and untreated). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the safety of insulin detemir produced by a new production method (NN729) with insulin detemir made by the previous production method (NN304).

A 58-year old female office worker was diagnosed with Stage III CKD six months ago. She has a medical history significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia and osteoarthritis. She is married with two adult children. She currently takes Lisinopril and Amlodipine for her hypertension and Atorvastatin for her high cholesterol. She has noticed swelling in her legs and ankles, and feels tired and weak most of the time. She has been advised to reduce her salt intake and has recently started a low-sodium diet. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She exercises occasionally but finds it difficult due to her joint pain. Her BMI is 29. She is concerned about her health and is interested in participating in a study that could help her improve her kidney function and overall health.

The patient is a 60 year old woman who has been diagnosed with coronary heart disease and has a history of high cholesterol levels. She has been taking medication to control her cholesterol levels for the past year but her levels are still elevated. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the additional cholesterol lowering effects of an investigational drug, in combination with her current cholesterol-lowering medication. She is willing to commit to the 10-week study duration and follow all instructions and requirements of the study.

38 F with no significant past medical history who presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of high fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She was diagnosed with COVID-19 and was admitted to the ICU for management. She required invasive mechanical ventilation for more than 72 hours. She was extubated and transferred to the general medical floor after 10 days in the ICU. She complains of difficulty concentrating and forgetfulness since her discharge. She has no history of cognitive impairment or psychiatric illness. She speaks fluent English and is willing to adhere to follow-up appointments. She resides within 300 kms of the referral center.

The patient is a 60 year old man who has been diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer. He has already undergone orchiectomy and antiandrogen therapy but has shown signs of disease progression with a rise in serum PSA greater than 50% of nadir confirmed on 2 measurements 1 week apart. He has also developed new lesions on bone scan and new soft-tissue lesions. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. His blood tests are within normal limits: WBC 6,000/mm3, absolute neutrophil count 3,000/mm3, platelet count 150,000/mm3, bilirubin within normal limits, alkaline phosphatase within 5 times the upper limit of normal, SGOT and SGPT within 2 times the upper limit of normal, creatinine within normal limits, and testosterone not greater than 3.5 nmol/L. He has no history of coagulopathy, myocardial infarction in the last 6 months, cardiovascular accident, congestive heart failure, symptomatic peripheral neuropathy greater than grade 1, or significant neurologic or psychiatric disorders including psychotic disorders, dementia, or seizures. He has not undergone any prior chemotherapy in the past 4 weeks, hormonal therapy in the past 4 weeks (including nonsteroidal antiandrogens, but not LHRH agonists), radiotherapy to greater than 30% of bone marrow, isotope therapy in the past 6 weeks, radiotherapy in the past 4 weeks, or investigational drugs in the past 4 weeks. He is eligible to participate in this study to receive combination chemotherapy in treating his advanced prostate cancer.

This is a 25 year old male who is currently enrolled in college and works part-time in retail. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He does not have a history of psychiatric illness and is not currently receiving any psychological or psychopharmacological treatment. He speaks fluent English and has no visual, motor, or hearing problems that would affect his participation. He is interested in participating in the study to better understand how his cortisol levels and other hormone levels may relate to his anxiety levels during a behavioral task. He is willing to complete interviews, questionnaires, and the Trier Social Stress Task as part of the study.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather family members of adult patients who have been hospitalized for more than 72 hours in a palliative care unit for end-of-life care. Therefore, there is no patient description that can be generated for this study. The study is focused on assessing the incidence and risk factors of prolonged grief in bereaved family members and does not involve any medical interventions or treatments.

The patient is a 72-year-old retired man who was admitted to the hospital for pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are managed with medication. He is currently using a cane due to some difficulty with balance but can walk short distances independently. He is married with three adult children who live out of state. He is retired from his career as an engineer and enjoys woodworking and gardening. He is concerned about his ability to recover from this illness and return to his previous level of function. His blood pressure at admission was 140/90 mmHg, and his blood glucose level was well-controlled at 110 mg/dL. He is able to speak and understand English well. He is not on hospice or bedrest, and he is not wheelchair-bound. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol for ambulation during his hospital stay.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with carotid stenosis of 75% on the right side. He is scheduled for a carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in two weeks. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He has noticed some mild memory problems and difficulty with word finding over the past few months. He is fluent in English and has no known allergies to tetracyclines. He understands the study requirements and is willing to participate. He has no history of stroke or major neurological deficits. His Mini-mental state examination (MMSE) score is 25. He is not currently on oral contraceptives and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with non-CF bronchiectasis after presenting with a chronic cough and shortness of breath. She has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and has been treated with multiple courses of antibiotics over the past year. She reports occasional hemoptysis, but denies any recent episodes of significant bleeding. She has never been diagnosed with asthma or cystic fibrosis, and her pulmonary function tests show a forced, expired volume in 1 second (FEV1) of 70% predicted. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators for her respiratory symptoms. Her CT scan shows evidence of bronchiectasis in multiple lobes of her lungs. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of BAY85-8501.

60 year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic back pain presents with severe right hip pain and stiffness. MRI shows advanced osteoarthritis of the right hip with bone-on-bone contact, and he is scheduled to undergo a primary, unilateral, elective total hip replacement. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well controlled with medications. He has no known history of bleeding disorders or clotting disorders. He does not have any recent history of major surgery or trauma within the last 3 months. He has not had any clinically relevant bleeding or gastric/duodenal ulcers within the last 6 months. He is not currently on any anticoagulants and is not expected to need any during the study treatment period. The patient has no active malignant disease or current cytostatic treatment. He has a normal renal function and liver function tests. He has no recent unstable cardiovascular disease or history of myocardial infarction within the last 3 months. He is not a pre-menopausal woman who is pregnant or nursing, or of child-bearing potential. He is not allergic to radio opaque contrast media or iodine, heparins (including heparin-induced thrombocytopenia), or dabigatran. He has no contraindications to enoxaparin. He has not participated in a clinical trial during the last 30 days. The patient has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 65-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of prostate cancer. He has no prior history of cancer and is generally in good health, with a Karnofsky performance status of 80. The patient has opted for radiation therapy as his primary treatment option and has been referred to this clinical trial. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications that would interfere with the study requirements. The patient has the ability to understand and is willing to sign a written informational form.

A 49-year-old Caucasian female presents with complaints of hot flushes, mood lability, anxiety, and sleep disturbances, which have been ongoing for the past 6 months. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles, but they have become irregular in the last few months. She has not used any form of hormonal therapy or soy supplements in the past. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, stroke, or cancer. She has no known allergies. She is currently not taking any medications or supplements. Physical examination reveals no significant findings. She meets the eligibility criteria for the Soy Estrogen Alternative Study (SEA) and is interested in participating in the trial.

A 56-year-old male presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of right-sided weakness and slurred speech. His medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which were well-controlled with medications. He had no history of heart disease or stroke. On examination, his blood pressure was 150/90 mmHg, heart rate was 80 beats per minute, and his oxygen saturation was 98% on room air. Neurological examination revealed right-sided hemiparesis with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 12. CT scan of the head showed a left middle cerebral artery (MCA) infarct. The patient was eligible for intravenous thrombolysis and was treated with rtPA within 3 hours of symptom onset. He also underwent mechanical thrombectomy. After the procedure, the patient was randomized into one of the two groups for further therapy. The first group was treated with Butylphthalide and Sodium Chloride Injection 100ml twice/day in the initial 14 days, followed by Butylphthalide Soft Capsules 0.2g triple/day for the rest 15th to 90th day therapy. The second group was treated with Butylphthalide Placebo Injection 100ml twice/day in the initial 14 days, followed by Butylphthalide Placebo Soft Capsules 0.2g triple/day for the rest 15th to 90th day therapy. The patient provided informed consent to participate in the study. He will be followed up for 90 days to assess his neurological function and recovery.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer six months ago. She underwent surgery, chemotherapy and radiation therapy and is currently in remission. Despite the successful treatment, she feels anxious and distressed about the possibility of cancer recurrence. She is married and has two children. She works part-time as a teacher and enjoys spending time with her family and friends. She is fluent in Italian and interested in participating in an intervention that could help her cope with her cancer experience and promote positive growth.

This is a 45-year-old female with a history of recurrent kidney stones. She has a single renal stone measuring 9mm in the left kidney. She has been experiencing intermittent left flank pain for the past week. CT scan confirmed the presence of the stone and the urologist has recommended ureteroscopic treatment. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 70-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous open repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) 5 years ago. During a routine follow-up CT scan, a juxtarenal AAA with a maximum diameter of 6.2 cm is discovered. The patient is asymptomatic and has no history of previous endovascular repair. The patient is considered a high-risk surgical candidate due to his age and comorbidities. He is scheduled for endovascular repair using a custom-made device (CMD) and will be enrolled in the Fenestrated-CMD cohort of the clinical trial. The patient has no known allergies to stainless steel, nitinol, polyester, solder, polypropylene, urethane or gold, and does not have a history of connective tissue disorder. He has adequate femoral and iliac access compatible with the requirements of the required delivery system. The patient has no contraindications for the use of contrast material and has no leaking or ruptured aneurysm associated with hypotension. He has a life expectancy greater than 2 years and is willing and able to comply with the follow-up schedule. The patient meets the anatomical inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and does not meet any of the anatomical exclusion criteria.

A 56-year-old woman was diagnosed with acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after undergoing an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant. She has been treated with high-dose steroids for over a week, but her symptoms have not improved and have even worsened after steroid tapering. The patient is experiencing skin rash, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. She has a performance status of ECOG 1 and normal renal function. The patient is willing to use contraception and is able to give informed consent. She has not received any other investigational drug in the last 14 days and has no serious medical or psychiatric illnesses that may interfere with this clinical study. The patient is interested in participating in this research study to test the safety and effectiveness of VELCADE® in treating GVHD.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Dupuytren's disease affecting his left hand. He reports a gradual development of a lump in his palm with progressive curling of his fourth finger towards his palm. He experiences difficulty in performing daily activities such as writing, holding objects, and shaking hands. He has not undergone any previous surgical intervention for Dupuytren's disease. He is fluent in English and willing to participate in the study. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is being managed with medication. He denies any history of carpal tunnel syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, connective tissue disorder, tenosynovitis, or any other conditions that could affect his quality of life.

A 55 year old female patient presents with a history of cataracts in both eyes. She reports experiencing decreased vision over the past year and has trouble seeing objects clearly. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her visual acuity is 20/80 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. She has no corneal pathology, anterior segment pathology or uncontrolled glaucoma. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the enVista trifocal intraocular lens when implanted in the capsular bag. The patient is able to understand and provide written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 48-year-old man with a history of melanoma. He underwent surgery to remove the primary melanoma and a lymph node biopsy, which showed metastasis to one lymph node. The patient did not receive any systemic therapy for melanoma. Recent imaging studies revealed that he has a few small nodules in the same area as the previous lymph node biopsy. He is in good health otherwise, with no significant medical history. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He is willing to undergo surgery to remove the nodules and has met with his treating surgical oncologist prior to randomization. His laboratory values and cardiac function are within normal limits. He has not received any live vaccines within the past 30 days and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is willing to use effective contraception during the study and for 26 weeks after the last dose of protocol treatment. He has not received prior systemic therapy for melanoma, including systemic therapy with an anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-CTLA-4, BRAF/MEK inhibitor combination, and/or TLR-9 agonist. He does not have a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or receiving systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to randomization.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the colon with liver metastases. The patient underwent colon resection surgery, and the pathology report confirmed the diagnosis of colorectal cancer. Imaging studies revealed that the patient has three hepatic metastatic lesions, each less than 5 cm in maximal dimension. The patient is in good clinical condition and is willing to undergo laparoscopic or robot-assisted laparoscopic liver resection or microwave ablation as the treatment for colorectal cancer liver metastases. The patient has no evidence of invasion into major portal/hepatic venous branches and no extrahepatic metastases. The patient's renal function is normal, and there is no history of pregnancy or nursing. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired male veteran who was diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis based on echocardiography results. He has noticed increasing shortness of breath and fatigue with minimal exertion. He is scheduled to undergo either surgical or transcatheter aortic valve replacement at the Minneapolis VA Health Care System. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, all of which are well-controlled with medications. He has no history of cognitive impairment and is able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

45-year-old female diagnosed with Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and currently using a nasal mask for treatment. The patient has reported experiencing discomfort and difficulty using the current nasal mask. The patient has a history of hypertension and hypothyroidism, both which are currently well-managed with medications. The patient has never been pregnant and is fluent in spoken and written English. The patient underwent a diagnostic PSG night and had an AHI of 10. The patient has been prescribed APAP therapy for the treatment of OSA. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a new nasal mask for the treatment of OSA in the home environment.

A 45-year-old male with a history of chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) for the past 10 years presents with symptoms of nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, facial pain, and pressure. The patient has been treated with maximal medical therapy, including antibiotics and nasal corticosteroid sprays, without significant improvement in symptoms. The patient has now been scheduled to undergo bilateral endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) with the placement of bilateral middle meatus spacers postoperatively. The patient is fluent in English and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. The patient does not have a history of immune deficiency, allergic fungal sinusitis, or cystic fibrosis.

58-year-old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath and generalized edema. He reports that the symptoms started two weeks ago and have been progressively worsening. He denies any chest pain, cough, fever, or chills. His vital signs are notable for a blood pressure of 168/98 mmHg, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 89% on room air. Physical exam reveals bilateral crackles on lung auscultation and significant lower extremity edema extending up to the thighs. Laboratory studies are significant for a serum creatinine level of 3.2 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen level of 55 mg/dL, and a brain natriuretic peptide level of 985 pg/mL. The patient is diagnosed with severe acute kidney injury secondary to volume overload and is started on continuous renal replacement therapy. He meets the inclusion criteria for the proposed study and is consented for participation.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic neck and upper extremity pain. The pain started several months ago and has been gradually getting worse. She has tried oral analgesics, physical therapy, and activity modification, but none of these treatments have provided long-lasting relief. She has been diagnosed with cervical radiculitis and recommended for cervical epidural steroid injection (CESI). She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effects of lidocaine versus saline as a steroid diluent on objective upper extremity strength following the injection. The patient has no history of cervical spinal cord lesions, cerebrovascular, demyelinating, or other neuromuscular diseases. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no history of allergy to local anesthetics. The patient is able to communicate and participate in follow-up. She is willing and able to perform handgrip or arm strength testing.

John is a 54-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital for his COPD exacerbation. He has a history of cigarette smoking for 30 years and quit 3 years ago. He also has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia that are well controlled with medications. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year for his COPD exacerbation and has had three ED visits. He requires home oxygen therapy and has had a course of systemic corticosteroid therapy in the past year. He is proficient in English and able to provide informed consent. He lives alone but has a supportive family who can help him with his disease management. His spirometry test confirmed the diagnosis of COPD, and he was started on appropriate medications during his hospitalization. He is motivated to learn more about his condition and is interested in participating in the respiratory disease management program to reduce the number of future hospital admissions and ED visits.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus two years ago. He has been controlling his diabetes with medication (metformin) and lifestyle changes, including a healthier diet and regular exercise. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and no significant medical history. He has no known food allergies or intolerances. He does not take any vitamin or mineral supplements. He has not donated blood in the last three months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effect of a buckwheat beverage on postprandial glucose metabolism.

A 6-year-old boy was referred by his pediatrician for a comprehensive evaluation due to developmental delays and communication difficulties. The parents reported that the child does not make eye contact, has delayed speech development, and frequently engages in repetitive behaviors. The child was diagnosed with ASD by a developmental pediatrician at age 4. The child has been receiving speech therapy and behavior intervention services for the past 2 years. The parents report that the child has a limited diet and refuses to eat most vegetables and fruits. The child has no known allergies or other medical conditions. The child is currently taking no medications or supplements. The child's laboratory results are within normal limits. The child is able to wear a mask during short visits. The parents are willing to participate in a 3-month clinical trial of a vitamin/mineral supplement designed for children with autism.

For Part I of the clinical trial, the patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23kg/m2. He has no history of chronic or acute illnesses, no allergies or current medications, and no history of substance abuse. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol only occasionally. He is willing to stay overnight at the clinical unit and undergo frequent blood sampling and clinical assessments.  For Part II of the clinical trial, the patient is a 40-year-old male with a BMI of 28kg/m2. He has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B and is HBeAg positive. He has not received any treatment for hepatitis B before and has no history of clinical decompensation. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial, undergo frequent blood sampling and clinical assessments, and receive either the study drug or placebo as assigned. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and is committed to complying with the study requirements.

A 45-year-old male smoker who has been smoking a pack of cigarettes per day for the past 20 years visits his physician to seek help to quit smoking. The patient has tried to quit smoking multiple times in the past but has failed due to intense cravings and withdrawal symptoms. He has no significant past medical history and is currently not taking any medications. He reports no allergies to any medications. The patient is motivated to quit smoking and has no plans to smoke during the study period. The physician prescribes Champix tablets 0.5mg, 1mg medication for 12 weeks and explains the possible side effects such as nausea, headache, and insomnia. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is instructed to take the medication as directed. The patient will be monitored for any potential side effects and the efficacy of the medication in helping him quit smoking.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to hypertension. He has been undergoing hemodialysis for the past 3 years and is currently on the transplant waiting list. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. He is a non-smoker and non-alcoholic. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and his serum creatinine level is 8.5 mg/dL. The patient is being considered for an extended criteria donor (ECD) kidney transplantation and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who recently suffered a distal radius fracture due to a fall. The fracture has been deemed severe enough to require surgical treatment. The patient has no history of previous surgeries on the same limb distal to the elbow. He has normal wrist function, and the fracture does not involve the joint. The patient is able to read and understand the informed consent for the study. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would preclude him from participating in the study.

There is no patient description required for this clinical trial, as patients themselves are not the subjects of the study. The study is evaluating a distance-learning tool for training primary care providers and their staff in the use of spirometry to assist in managing obstructive lung disease (asthma and COPD). The trial aims to gather information in a 'real-world' setting that can be used to improve Spirometry Fundamentals™.

65-year-old male diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) with no history of acute bacterial infection of the GI tract and no use of antibiotics or probiotics within 28 days prior to sampling. The patient has been informed about the establishment of a human tissue bank for studying the microbial etiology and pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases, including ALS, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis. The patient has been provided with the tissue bank protocol informed consent/HIPAA authorization document and has agreed to participate in the study by signing the informed consent form. The patient will provide stool and blood samples for the tissue bank. A separate blood sample will not be taken from the patient if the maximum amount of samples allowed have been collected for standard care. The patient's demographic information, medical history, and other relevant details will be recorded in a data collection form and linked to the tissue samples by an individual research code.

A 60-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of three vaginal deliveries presents to the gynecology clinic with complaints of vaginal bulge and pressure sensation. She reports difficulty emptying her bladder and occasional stress urinary incontinence. On examination, she is found to have stage 2 anterior vaginal wall prolapse with no apical involvement according to the POP-Q scoring system. She has no history of pelvic surgery or radiation therapy. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She has no known allergies to any medication or materials. She is not currently sexually active and has no plans for future fertility. She is interested in surgical management of her prolapse and is willing to participate in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old Caucasian male who exercises regularly for at least 150 minutes per week. He has no history of autonomic, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurologic, endocrine, or respiratory disease. He has no history of liver or kidney dysfunction.
