The patient does not smoke or use electronic cigarettes and has not used them consistently in the last year. The patient is not currently taking any medication that cannot be safely discontinued for 5 biological half-lives prior to each study visit based on consultation with the study physician. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

Pt is a 45-year-old male with a 2-year history of progressive muscle weakness and atrophy. The patient experiences difficulty walking and has fallen multiple times due to weakness in his legs. The patient reports difficulty holding objects and performing daily activities such as dressing and grooming. The patient has a family history of ALS, with his father passing away from the disease. The patient has undergone several diagnostic tests and has been diagnosed with definite ALS by a neurologist. The patient is currently not taking any medication for ALS and is interested in participating in a study to better understand the disease.

A 48-year-old woman has been diagnosed with a primary cutaneous malignant melanoma that is thicker than 2 mm. She underwent an excisional biopsy with a margin of 1-3 mm and is now being considered for further surgical treatment. She is fit for surgery and has no other malignancies except for a basal cell carcinoma. She has not experienced any in-transit, regional, or distant spread of the disease. She is willing to participate in the trial and has signed the patient consent form.

The patient is a 55 year old male with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He has a sedentary lifestyle, spending most of his day sitting at a desk job. He has a BMI of 30 and has been diagnosed with the metabolic syndrome, having three of the five characteristic manifestations of the syndrome. He has a waist circumference of 110 cm, blood pressure of 140/90 mm Hg, and HDL-cholesterol level of 35 mg/dL. He has a family history of diabetes and cardiovascular disease. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He enjoys eating out and often chooses fast food and processed foods. He has no known allergies to any foods. He is willing to make changes to his diet and lifestyle in order to improve his health.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease and has been suffering from chest pain for several months. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. He is currently taking medications for these conditions. His cardiologist recommends coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). He agrees to participate in the clinical trial and signs the informed consent form. His laboratory tests show normal values for hemoglobin, platelets, creatinine, AST, and ALT. He has no history of heparin allergy or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. He has not been taking antiplatelet agents or heparin for the last 7 days. He is not currently experiencing any infections or fever.

A 12-year-old Caucasian female presented with recurrent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and bloody stool. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months and has lost approximately 8 pounds during that time. She has been previously diagnosed with ulcerative colitis and has been on mesalamine therapy for the past 3 months without any significant improvement in her symptoms. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. Her physical exam revealed a tender abdomen with no palpable masses or organomegaly. Laboratory tests showed elevated levels of C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and fecal calprotectin. Colonoscopy and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria.

The patient is a 30-year-old non-smoking female with a clinical diagnosis of asthma since early childhood. She is currently on maintenance therapy with inhaled corticosteroid and bronchodilator with good symptom control. She has no history of cardiovascular disorders or any other chronic disease. Her lung function test reveals a FEV1%pred value of 70%. She understands the study procedures and is willing to participate in the study, as indicated by her signature on the informed consent form. She is able to perform a breath hold for at least 16 seconds and can perform reproducible pulmonary function tests. She has no history of respiratory infection in the last four weeks and does not require supplemental oxygen. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no contraindication for MRI imaging.

A 24-year-old college student injured his left wrist while playing basketball with friends. He fell on his outstretched hand and immediately experienced pain and swelling. He went to the emergency room where X-rays were taken and a cast was applied. He has been experiencing persistent pain and difficulty moving his wrist since then. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he has never had a previous injury to his wrist or carpus. He is right-handed and is studying computer science. He lives with his roommate and has no dependents. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He is fluent in Dutch and English.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman with End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) who requires haemodialysis. She has been on dialysis for the past 8 months and has been experiencing difficulty with her current arteriovenous access graft. She has a medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and dyslipidemia. She has no known allergies to ePTFE. The patient is compliant with her medications and is willing to comply with the protocol and associated follow-up requirements. She has a life expectancy of at least 12 months. She has agreed to have her data entered into the registry as per the local hospital consent procedure.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who lives alone and is concerned about maintaining her independence as she ages. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it, but her blood pressure is well-controlled. She also has mild arthritis in her knees and lower back, but it is not debilitating. She enjoys walking and gardening, but has noticed that her balance is not as good as it used to be and she has had a few near falls. She is interested in participating in the study to try Tai Chi and see if it can improve her balance and overall physical function.

The patient is a 35-year-old male diagnosed with ulcerative colitis, with a Mayo score of 8. He has failed to respond to conventional therapies including oral corticosteroids, oral 5-aminosalicylates, and azathioprine. He is currently on a stable dose of Infliximab, but has not achieved remission. His vital signs are within normal limits, and he has no notable medical history. Laboratory results show a total bilirubin of 1.0 mg/dL, ALT of 25 U/L, and a creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL. He has not been exposed to IL-2 previously, and has not received another investigational new drug within the last 5 half-lives. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and has provided informed consent.

56 yo male with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) confirmed by MRI, with a history of hepatitis C and detectable HCV-RNA. Patient has no significant comorbidities except for moderate hypertension which is well controlled with medications. Patient is willing to use adequate contraception. Past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and hepatitis C infection for the past 10 years. The patient has been receiving treatment for hepatitis C infection with antiviral therapy for the past 6 months but has not been responsive to the treatment. The patient has been referred for the sorafenib clinical trial to evaluate the effect of sorafenib on hepatitis C. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the trial, and is willing to comply with the protocol and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 25-year-old female living in a rural area of Brazil with a history of frequent gastrointestinal symptoms, such as abdominal pain and diarrhea. She works as a farm laborer and has completed high school education. She has never been infected with hookworm before and has no known allergies or medical conditions. Her BMI is 22 with the BP of 110/70. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the public health situation in her community. She is willing to comply with the study protocol, including receiving three doses of the assigned study agent given in 56-day intervals and attending all follow-up visits. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use reliable contraception methods up until one month following the third immunization. She is able to correctly answer all questions on the informed consent comprehension questionnaire.

52-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of COVID-19 confirmed by a positive test result. The patient reports difficulty breathing and chest pain. Upon evaluation, the patient's chest imaging reveals lung changes consistent with COVID pneumonia. The patient is experiencing an increase in work of breathing and dyspnea, indicating a severe respiratory distress. The patient has no known history of HIV, Hepatitis C, Hepatitis B, Herpes Zoster or Mycobacterium Tuberculosis. The patient is willing to give informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient's platelet count is above 20,000 and neutrophil count is above 500 cells/mm3.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who fell in his bathroom and fractured his hip. He was diagnosed with a femoral neck fracture through an X-ray. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of any significant medical conditions. He has been advised to undergo surgery. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy woman who is currently in her 39th week of pregnancy. She has not been diagnosed with any chronic illnesses and has not experienced any pregnancy-related illnesses such as preeclampsia or gestational diabetes. She is carrying a singleton pregnancy and has not undergone any fertility treatments. The patient has been taking prenatal vitamins throughout her pregnancy and has been following a healthy lifestyle. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the relationship between maternal 25-hydroxy Vitamin D levels and adverse outcomes in near term and full term neonates. The patient is willing to have her blood drawn for the purpose of measuring her 25(OH) D levels and is committed to attending follow-up appointments with her newborn for the duration of the study.

A 54-year-old male presents with a sudden onset of blurred vision in the right eye. He reports no pain, redness, or discharge. He has a history of hypertension and takes losartan daily. On examination, visual acuity is 20/50 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye. Fundus examination revealed a branch retinal vein occlusion in the right eye with macular edema, confirmed by intravenous fluorescein angiography and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) with a central foveal thickness of 350 microns. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy for retinal vein occlusion. The patient does not have a history of myocardial infarction, ischemia or cerebrovascular accident within 6 weeks of screening, and does not have concurrent proliferative diabetic retinopathy and/or maculopathy or concurrent exudative age-related macular degeneration. The patient is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the duration of the study and does not have a history of allergy or hypersensitivity to study treatment, fluorescein, or any study procedure and treatment-related ingredients.

A 55-year-old Hispanic woman presented with shortness of breath on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. She reported a gradual onset of symptoms over the past 6 months. She denied chest pain, palpitations, cough, fever, chills, or weight loss. Her past medical history was significant for hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her family history was non-contributory. On physical examination, she had a blood pressure of 142/88 mmHg, heart rate of 84 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 92% on room air. Chest auscultation revealed bilateral basal crackles. Her electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy. Her transthoracic echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 50% with evidence of diastolic dysfunction and left atrial enlargement. Her laboratory investigations revealed elevated NT-proBNP levels. She was diagnosed with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and was started on guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure.

This is a 52 year old male who presents with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and weakness in his upper extremities for the past 6 months. On physical examination, there is decreased grip strength in both hands, and he has difficulty with fine motor tasks. MRI of the cervical spine reveals spinal cord compression at the C5-C6 level, consistent with cervical myelomalacia. The patient has no previous history of cervical spinal surgery and does not have any systemic diseases. Past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medications. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol.

A 52-year-old male with a history of hypertension and obesity complains of loud snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness. He reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. He feels tired even after sleeping for 7-8 hours, and he has fallen asleep while driving a few times. He has tried sleeping on his side and using nasal strips, but they have not helped. He has not received any treatment for his symptoms. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works a desk job. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no history of allergies, asthma, or lung problems. His BMI is 35. His vital signs are within normal limits. He is married and has two children. His Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score is 14.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He recently tested positive for COVID-19 and is experiencing mild symptoms such as cough, fever, and body aches. The patient is not requiring hospitalization but is at high risk for severe disease due to his comorbidities. He is able to travel to the clinic and understands the study requirements. He is willing to participate in the study and sign the informed consent form. The patient is not currently taking any investigational agents and does not have any known chronic liver or kidney disease. He is capable of swallowing a capsule and is willing to practice two acceptable methods of birth control during the study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with an activating EGFR mutation (exon 19 deletion) that has progressed after receiving erlotinib and platinum-based chemotherapy-containing regimen. The patient has measurable lesions confirmed by BICR as per RECIST v1.1. The patient has an ECOG PS of 1 at Screening. The patient's laboratory data within 14 days prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 showed adequate bone marrow reserve and organ function, with platelet count of 120,000/mm^3, hemoglobin level of 10.5 g/dL, absolute neutrophil count of 2100/mm^3, serum creatinine level of 1.2 × upper limit of normal (ULN), aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase level of 2 × ULN, total bilirubin level of 1 × ULN, serum albumin level of 3.5 g/dL, and prothrombin time (PT) or PT-International normalized ratio (INR) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)/PTT of 1 × ULN. The patient has received a prior line of EGFR TKI treatment (erlotinib) and platinum-based chemotherapy regimen. The patient must have documented an EGFR-activating mutation detected from tumor tissue or blood sample: exon 19 deletion. Tumor biopsy from at least 1 lesion not previously irradiated and amenable to core biopsy is required. The patient has not received any prior treatment with an anti-human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) antibody or single-agent topoisomerase I inhibitor. The patient has no history of other active malignancy within 3 years prior to enrollment. The patient has no unresolved toxicities from previous anticancer therapy. The patient has no evidence of interstitial lung disease (including pulmonary fibrosis or radiation pneumonitis) or clinically severe respiratory compromise resulting from intercurrent pulmonary illnesses. The patient has no evidence of any leptomeningeal disease or clinically active spinal cord compression or brain metastases. The patient has no inadequate washout period prior to Cycle 1 Day 1. The patient does not have active hepatitis B and/or hepatitis C infection, nor any human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. The patient meets all eligibility criteria and is willing to provide required tumor tissue of sufficient quantity and of adequate tumor tissue content.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been smoking for the last 10 years. She is a working professional who has been trying to quit smoking for the last 6 months without success. She has tried nicotine patches and gum before but found them ineffective. She smokes around 10 cigarettes per day and is aware of the health implications of smoking. She is fluent in Cantonese and Chinese and is willing to participate in the 8-week mindfulness-based relapse prevention (MBRP) program. She has no significant physical illness, cognitive impairment, or history of psychotic disorders. She is not currently pregnant and has no suicidal tendencies. She has a history of mild depression but is not currently on any medication for it. She is interested in trying new techniques to help her quit smoking and is excited about the possibility of participating in this clinical trial. She leads a moderately active lifestyle and exercises for around 30 minutes per day. Her BMI is 23 and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She lives in an apartment with her spouse and two children.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of bacterial vaginosis (BV) for the past week. She reports a milky and thin discharge with a fishy odor, and has noticed some itching and inflammation in the vulva and vagina. She has not used any intravaginal products or antibiotics in the past two weeks, and has not had intercourse in the past week. She is not pregnant and has no known allergies to copper or metronidazole. Her Pap smear is within normal limits. She is willing to refrain from using any vaginal products or having intercourse during the treatment period. She understands the study requirements and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 50-year-old man was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 10 years ago. He has moderate swelling in both of his hands and wrists. He has tried multiple disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) in the past but has not achieved significant relief. He is not currently on any DM

The patient is a 55-year-old man who received a kidney transplant from a deceased donor two weeks ago. He has a history of end-stage renal disease due to diabetes and hypertension. His serum creatinine level has been stable for the past 3 consecutive tests, and it is currently within normal limits. His HLA mismatch number is ≥4, and his PRA value pre-transplantation is <10%. The patient is currently receiving conventional immunosuppressive drugs, and their concentration is within target ranges. He is willing to participate in the study, fully informed, and has signed the informed consent form. The patient has undergone a negative pregnancy test within 24 hours before the start of study medication, and he has agreed to use an acceptable method to avoid pregnancy for the entire study period and up to 3 months after the last dose of study medication. The patient does not have any of the exclusion criteria mentioned in the study protocol.

The patient is a 35-year-old Caucasian man who was diagnosed with Crohn's disease two years ago. He has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms of ileal and colonic Crohn's disease, including abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He has tried conventional therapies, but they have not been effective in treating his symptoms. He has also tried one biologic therapy, but he lost response to it. He has not had any bowel resection in the last 6 months. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and enjoys playing tennis in his free time. He has undergone an endoscopy with evidence of active Crohn's disease with a simple endoscopic score for Crohn's disease (SES-CD) score of 4, excluding the contribution of the narrowing component score, within the last 3 months. He is willing to participate in the study and sign an informed consent form. He has no known tuberculosis infection or any other medical contraindications. He is not obese and does not have normal bowel wall thickness. He is interested in participating in the ultrasound sub-study to assess intestinal ultrasound parameters.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing severe chest pain for the past hour. He has a history of hypertension, but no other significant medical history. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He denies any recent major surgeries or bleeding episodes. On examination, his blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and his heart rate is 100 beats per minute. His ECG shows ST elevation in the inferior leads. His platelet count is normal, and he has no known allergies to any medications. He has not received fibrinolytic therapy in the past seven days, and he is not currently on any GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of smoking for 30 years, with a pack-year history of 20. He reports a persistent cough, mild shortness of breath, and occasional wheezing. He has not had any recent exacerbations of COPD and is not currently receiving oxygen therapy. His medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He has no history of ischaemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, hepatic failure, neurological disease, or obstructive sleep apnoea. He has no known history of dementia or psychiatric disorders. He has normal vision and hearing. He is willing to undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning and neuropsychological assessment. He gives his signed and dated written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. She is currently receiving palliative treatment and has a life expectancy of less than 2 years. She lives alone in her own house and has a daughter who lives in another state. She has a history of hypertension and has been on medication for that for the past 5 years. She is independent in her daily activities but has some difficulty walking long distances due to shortness of breath. She is a retired teacher and enjoys reading and gardening. She speaks English fluently and has had an initial advance care planning conversation with her primary care clinician. She is willing to participate in the study and provide verbal consent.

A 70-year-old man with no history of bone diseases came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has no history of bone fractures or surgeries. He takes no medications and does not have any chronic illnesses. He is able to lie down on a bed comfortably. His latest DEXA (Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry) scan shows a T-score of -1.5 in the lumbar spine and -2.2 in the femoral neck. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new technologies for bone strength measurement.

A 42-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with thyroid cancer and is scheduled to undergo a total thyroidectomy as a primary procedure. She has no other significant medical history and has never had any prior surgeries. She is currently taking levothyroxine for hypothyroidism, which was discovered incidentally during routine bloodwork. She has no known allergies and is in generally good health.

The patient is a 15 year-old girl who has been experiencing shortness of breath and difficulty breathing during exercise for the past year. She has been diagnosed with vocal cord dysfunction (VCD) by her pulmonologist and has been using an inhaler with albuterol as needed. She has no history of asthma or allergies. Her symptoms have been impacting her daily activities, including sports and school. She has had a baseline pulmonary function test (PFT) at the time of diagnosis that revealed mild obstruction. She has not received any prior speech therapy or psychological counseling. She lives with both parents who are supportive and willing to participate in the therapy sessions with her. She is in 10th grade and is an A/B student. She participates in sports and is interested in pursuing a career in medicine.

This clinical trial is a cross-sectional survey that aims to investigate how people's lifestyle decisions and social distancing choices are affected by the medical information they receive. The study is looking for participants who are 18 years of age or older, based in the United States, and able to read and agree to the English-based consent form. Interested individuals must be able to pass the attention check questions in the pre-test and main survey and complete the main survey in 120 seconds or more. The study will recruit an estimated 1400 participants using Amazon's Mechanical Turk to complete the main survey. Respondents who pass the 4 attention check questions within the pre-test will then be invited to complete the main survey. After consenting to participate, participants will be randomized to take one of three surveys each describing a different scenario: one where they likely have COVID-19 but testing is not available, one where they likely have COVID-19 and testing results show a positive result, and one where they likely have COVID-19 and testing results show a negative result. Participants will be asked questions about their activity and behavior intentions, along with a set of demographic questions. The study will exclude individuals who fail any of the attention check questions from the pre-test and main survey or complete the main survey in 119 seconds or under.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer two years ago. She underwent a mastectomy followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. She has been experiencing chronic pain in her right shoulder, right upper back, and right arm for the past 6 months. She reports that her pain is constant and rated as 7 out of 10 on the pain intensity scale. The pain is affecting her daily activities, including her ability to work as a nurse. She has tried physical therapy and medication, but her pain persists. She is interested in participating in a therapeutic horticulture program to manage her pain symptoms. She is able to participate in a moderate physical activity and has her own transportation to the horticulture site. She speaks and writes in English.

The patient is a 47 year-old male who has been diagnosed with a thoracic aortic aneurysm. He is currently experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain, as well as some swelling in his legs. He has a history of high blood pressure and has been taking medication to control it for the past 5 years. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His kidney function is normal according to his most recent blood work. He is scheduled to undergo thoracic aorta surgery with hypothermic cardiac arrest in 2 weeks. He has never received erythropoietin treatment before and is not allergic to it. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with a brain tumor and requires an elective craniotomy. The patient has a history of motion sickness and has experienced postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) in the past after undergoing surgery. The patient is able to actively participate in the study and has no communication problems. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is not excluded based on the exclusion criteria. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is randomly assigned to either the P6 acupressure group or the placebo group. The patient will receive an active acupressure band or placebo band at the end of surgery and will be monitored for 48 hours postoperatively for nausea and vomiting frequency. The patient's use of antiemetics and opioids will also be recorded during the study.

The patient is a 72-year-old man who retired from his job as a construction worker six months ago. He has always led a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of his time watching TV or reading books. He lives alone in a small apartment and relies on public transportation to run errands. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, which are currently under control with medication. He has no history of cancer, heart attack, stroke, or any ongoing mental health or psychiatric condition. He is able to walk across a room without assistance, but he feels a bit unsteady on his feet due to his lack of physical activity. He speaks English fluently and plans to stay in the local area for the next six months. He is interested in participating in a program that can help him maintain his independence for as long as possible.

A 45 year old man with a history of colon cancer underwent a hemicolectomy and has had a colostomy for the past 6 months. He has been using a 1-piece convex ostomy product for the past month but has been experiencing skin irritation and bleeding around the stoma site. The diameter of the stoma is 28 mm. He is willing and able to comply with investigation procedures and has given written informed consent. He is not currently undergoing radio- or chemotherapy or steroid treatment and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease due to hypertension is scheduled for a kidney transplant. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He takes lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin daily. His BMI is 30. He reports no drug allergies. He has never had a TAP block before and has not been on chronic opioid therapy. He is willing to participate in the study and able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old non-Hispanic black male who has been a regular patron of a local barbershop in the Nashville area for the last six months. He has a history of hypertension and is taking medication prescribed by his primary care physician. However, his blood pressure readings have been consistently above 140 mm Hg on two separate occasions. He has no history of severe cognitive impairment, chemotherapy for cancer, or organ transplant. He is fluent in English and has no plans to move or travel out of the area for the next 12 months. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his hypertension management and overall health.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed 3 years ago, has not been able to achieve adequate glycemic control with lifestyle modification (diet/exercise) or metformin. Her fasting plasma glucose is consistently above 275 mg/dL and glycosylated hemoglobin concentration is between 7.0% and 10.0%. She has a body mass index of 30 kg/m2 and a fasting C-peptide concentration of 1.0 ng/mL. She is not currently taking any other medications except for metformin. The patient has no history of cancer, heart failure, coronary artery disease, or psychiatric disorders that may affect her ability to participate in the study. She has not received any investigational drugs in the last 30 days and has no known hypersensitivity to compounds related to SYR-619 or alogliptin. The patient is willing to monitor her own blood glucose concentrations with a home glucose monitor and agrees to use adequate contraception as she is sexually active. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial and is interested in participating.

A 25-year-old female who is generally healthy and a non-smoker, with a BMI of 23, is interested in participating in this clinical trial. She has no history of significant medical conditions, allergies, or substance abuse. She is not currently taking any prescription or non-prescription drugs or dietary supplements. She has never been diagnosed with glaucoma or increased intraocular pressure, and has never experienced a seizure. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently pregnant or nursing. She is willing to comply with all protocol requirements and is able to provide informed consent.

35-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 24.1 and no significant medical history. The patient has no known allergies to any medications and has not recently taken any prescription or non-prescription drugs. He does not smoke, consume alcohol or have a history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient has not consumed any beverages or foods containing methyl-xanthenes or grapefruit in the past 48 hours or 7 days respectively. He is willing to adhere to the study requirements and is willing to be hospitalized if necessary within 3 months after the first study drug administration. The patient has not participated in any bioequivalence or clinical study within the last 6 weeks and has not donated more than 500 ml of blood in the past 7 days or 750 ml in the past 30 days. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits associated with it.

6-week-old male infant diagnosed with congenital transverse unilateral amputation of the forearm segment. The infant is socially insured, and the legal guardians have provided written informed consent for the child's participation in the study. The child has no other high-risk factors for neurodevelopmental disorders and does not have any family history of first-degree neurodevelopmental disorder. The child has not undergone any major surgery, and there is no exposure to any major toxicant. The child has not been diagnosed with any other deficiency forming part of a polymalformative, vascular syndrome or any genetic cause.

The patient is a 46-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes for 5 years. She has been struggling with obesity, with a BMI of 38 kg/m^2, despite various attempts at diet and exercise. She is interested in bariatric surgery and is currently being evaluated as a surgical candidate for either RYGBP, GBS or VSG. She is not currently on any medication that can alter body weight. She does not have a history of any major neurological disorder, stroke, seizures, or cancer. She is willing and able to follow study procedures.

Patient is a 48-year-old male with a history of non-Hodgkin lymphoma involving the central nervous system. The patient received high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) but unfortunately experienced disease relapse. He is currently receiving methotrexate-based therapy, but the disease has continued to progress. The patient is not a candidate for ASCT in the judgement of the treating physician, and therefore, he may be a suitable candidate for the reduced intensity conditioning allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for lymphoma clinical trial. The patient must have a well-matched adult donor willing to donate peripheral blood stem cells, and must have demonstrated a partial or complete response of their CNS and systemic disease to pre-enrollment therapy. The patient must also meet other eligibility criteria including adequate organ function, ECOG performance status ≤ 2, and age ≥ 18 years. Prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 4 weeks prior to the 1st day of conditioning chemotherapy and receiving any other investigational agents are exclusion criteria for this study.

32F with a history of bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder, both diagnosed 5 years ago. The patient has been undergoing psychiatric treatment for the past 3 years and is currently on a combination of mood stabilizers and antipsychotics. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both diagnosed 2 years ago. The patient has been experiencing occasional chest pain and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. Upon examination, the patient was found to have a BMI of 32 and elevated blood pressure. She is a smoker and has been trying to quit for the past year. The patient has expressed interest in participating in self-management training and is able to read the telehealth display in English. She has no history of dementia or cognitive impairment and has a MMSE score of 28. The patient has voluntarily given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

55 year-old male with metastatic lung cancer and persistent pain despite being on around-the-clock opioids. He reports 2-3 breakthrough pain episodes per day which are usually partially relieved by supplemental medication of at least 5mg immediate-release morphine or an equivalent short-acting opioid. He is experiencing moderate pain intensity in the 24 hours prior to assessment by a verbal rating scale at the Screening Visit. The patient is able to evaluate and record pain relief, assess medication performance, and record adverse events. He is willing to give informed consent and agrees to practice a reliable form of contraception. He does not have a history of intolerance to opioids or fentanyl nor is he currently using commercially available oral short-acting fentanyl for breakthrough pain. He has not received investigational study product(s) ≤ 30 days prior to the Screening Visit. He does not have painful erythema, oedema or ulcers under the tongue and has not used monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors within 14 days of the Screening Visit.

The patient is a 45 year old Chinese woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She is planning to undergo treatment with taxanes and is interested in participating in a study to help develop predictive markers for neuropathy. She has no history of poorly controlled or insulin-dependent diabetes or any other condition that may predispose her to neurotoxicity. She is willing to provide blood samples and report any symptoms of peripheral neuropathy that she experiences during or after treatment.

A 48-year-old woman is scheduled for an elective primary arthroplasty of the hip due to severe osteoarthritis. She has been experiencing pain and difficulty with mobility for the past year. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She denies any allergies or skin conditions. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. She is expected to have a total length of stay of 5 days post-surgery.

A 78-year-old retired man who participated in the IMT-002 trial is interested in enrolling in the long-term monitoring study. He has been living with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) for several years and underwent the IMT implantation surgery 3 years ago on his left eye. He has no other significant ocular or medical history, takes daily multivitamins, and has no allergies to any food or drugs. He has no history of non-compliance with medical treatments or appointments. He is able to understand and comply with the requirements of the clinical study and is willing to provide voluntary informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who has been experiencing a constant ringing in her ears for the past 8 months. The ringing is non-pulsatile and has a loudness of 7/10 on the Visual Analogue Scale. She has been struggling with sleep disturbances and difficulty concentrating due to the tinnitus. She has tried various treatments including herbal remedies and sound therapy but has not seen any improvement. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or other medical conditions that may interfere with the study. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to see if the addition of tDCS to TRT can alleviate her symptoms.

This is a clinical trial for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients who require intravenous nutritional support. Therefore, the patient description will be of a newborn baby who has been admitted to the NICU. This baby was born prematurely at 28 weeks' gestational age and weighs only 900 grams. Due to the baby's prematurity, their digestive system is not fully developed, and they require intravenous nutritional support. The baby's medical team has determined that the baby needs lipid injectable emulsions as part of their nutritional support. The baby's parents have been approached by the study team to participate in a clinical trial to compare the tolerance of lipid injectable emulsions in glass versus plastic packaging. The parents have reviewed the study information and have consented to their baby's participation. The baby will receive one of two study parenteral lipid emulsions, and their serum triglycerides will be monitored to assess tolerance. The study will take place entirely in the NICU, and all patient data will be kept confidential.

The patient is a 62 year-old male who was admitted to the ICU for septic shock. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He presented with fever, tachycardia, and hypotension. Blood cultures were positive for gram-negative bacteria. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and received a fluid bolus, but his blood pressure remained low. A central venous catheter was placed and he was started on norepinephrine and vasopressin infusions. The primary medical team ordered the addition of vasopressin to the patient's treatment regimen at a constant infusion rate for at least 3 hours as an adjunctive vasopressor to catecholamine therapy. The patient was admitted to the medical ICU and had a central venous catheter in place. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is willing to participate.

A 45-year-old Mexican woman contacted the clinic seeking psychological support after losing her husband to COVID-19 three months ago. She has been experiencing symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbances. She works as a nurse at a hospital and has been struggling to cope with the loss of her husband while still working in a high-risk environment. She has access to a computer and basic digital skills but has never received any psychological treatment before. She speaks Spanish fluently and is looking for an online intervention that can help her manage her grief and improve her mental health. She has no history of psychotic disorder or recent suicide attempts.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who received dental implants 9-10 years ago within the Swedish insurance system. She has answered the initial questionnaire and her treating dentist has provided her patient files/records. She is in good general health and has no significant medical history. She is experiencing some discomfort in her dental implants and has noticed a slight movement in her prosthesis. She is interested in participating in the clinical and radiographic examination to assess the long-term outcomes of her dental implant therapy. She is willing to undergo a thorough clinical and radiographic examination to evaluate implant loss, loss of prosthesis, and any technical/biological complications. She is also willing to provide patient-centered outcomes to help in the evaluation of the efficacy and safety of dental implant therapy.

A 45-year-old woman underwent a breast lumpectomy surgery to remove a benign tumor in her right breast. The surgery was performed 24 hours ago, and she has been experiencing pain, swelling, and redness around the wound area. She has a history of hypertension and takes medications for it. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She does not have any other medical conditions or allergies. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve the appearance of her surgical scar.

A 25-year old healthy male with no previous medical history is interested in participating in the PK/PD clinical trial of YYD601. He is currently studying at a university and works part-time at a local coffee shop. He has a height of 175cm and weighs 68kg, which falls within the IBW± 20% range. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He consumes a balanced diet and exercises regularly. He is aware of the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to provide informed consent. He has no chronic or congenital illnesses and has undergone all required screening tests, including serum, hematological, blood chemistry, urine, and clinical laboratory tests, and a 12-lead EKG, which have all come back normal. He is excited to participate in the trial and contribute to the advancement of medical research.

The patient is a 25 year old healthy male, who has never used cocaine before. He works as a software engineer and lives a healthy lifestyle with regular exercise and a balanced diet. He has no history of cardiopulmonary disease, hypertension, or substance abuse apart from occasional social drinking. He has not been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus or any other systemic illness. He is not currently taking any medications or supplements. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to improve the scientific understanding of the cardiovascular actions of cocaine. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and gives informed consent to participate.

The patient is a sexually active 25-year-old woman who is in a committed relationship with her partner. She has a regular menstrual cycle that lasts around 28 days. She recently decided to stop using oral contraceptives and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness, safety, and acceptability of Sayana® Press when injected every 4 months. She has no known medical conditions and is in good health as determined by her medical history. She is willing to rely on Sayana® Press as her only method of contraception for the next 12 months and has no plans to become pregnant during this time. She is willing to provide informed consent and follow all study requirements. She has not had any injections of DMPA or norethisterone enanthate in the past 12 months and has not used a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, NuvaRing, contraceptive patch, oral contraceptives or a contraceptive implant in the past 7 days. She has no known allergies to DMPA and has not been diagnosed with any sexually transmitted infections in the past month. She is not lactating and has no plans to move to another location in the next 12 months.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who had a stroke eight months ago. He had right-sided weakness and was admitted to the hospital for rehabilitation. Although he has improved after the rehabilitation program, he still has difficulty performing some daily activities, especially when multitasking is involved, such as turning while walking, stepping back, and stepping down. He has no problem walking unaided, but he feels unsteady and is afraid of falling. He is in good general health, with no other neurological diseases or severe musculoskeletal injuries. He has no severe visual or hearing impairment and can follow instructions in Cantonese. He has not undergone any major surgeries or suffered any severe musculoskeletal injuries in the past six months. He is interested in participating in this study to improve his dual-tasking ability and his confidence in performing daily activities.

A 55 year old African-American man with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol presents with chest pain and shortness of breath. He reports experiencing these symptoms for the past hour and is concerned that it may be a heart attack. He is otherwise healthy and has not had any previous heart conditions. The patient is able to access the internet and is willing to participate in a web-based survey regarding his care-seeking behavior during an acute coronary syndrome episode. He is able to provide informed consent and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been receiving hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to end-stage renal disease. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes, which are well controlled with medications. Her current medications include lisinopril, metoprolol, amlodipine, insulin, and metformin. She has no history of cardiac arrhythmia or renal osteopathy. Her calcium levels have been fluctuating between 2.0 and 2.3 mmol/L, and her intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) level is 300 pg/mL. She has been compliant with her hemodialysis schedule and phosphate binder medication (calcium carbonate). She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent. She has no history of previous treatment with glucocorticoids for any condition. She is interested in understanding how the 1.25 mmol/L calcium dialysate may impact her mineral metabolism and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) for the past 2 years. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 33 and has been struggling with weight loss despite various diets and exercise regimens. She has a sedentary lifestyle due to her work as a desk job employee. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. She has no history of allergies and is not taking any medications currently. Her menstrual cycle is irregular, with a duration of 35-40 days, and she has facial hair growth. The patient has not been pregnant before and is not currently trying to conceive. Her lab studies revealed high levels of testosterone (120ng/dL), insulin resistance (HOMA-IR: 4.5), and lipid profile within normal levels. Her liver and kidney function tests are normal, and she has not been diagnosed with any other endocrine disorders. She is interested in participating in the study to achieve weight loss and improve her PCOS symptoms.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with advanced bladder cancer. He has a history of smoking and has been a smoker for 20 years. He recently started experiencing symptoms of frequent urination, pain during urination, and blood in his urine. He underwent a series of tests, including a biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of advanced bladder cancer. He has no significant past medical history, and his family history is unremarkable. He is currently taking medication for high blood pressure. His vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg and a heart rate of 80 bpm. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, meaning he is able to carry out light work such as office work or light housework. He has no significant laboratory abnormalities, and his organ function is normal. He has not had any prior systemic chemotherapy for his cancer. The patient has been informed of the investigational nature of the study and is willing to sign an informed consent in accordance with institutional and federal guidelines.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who presented with recurrent episodes of painless hematuria. He has a history of smoking for 40 years and has a family history of bladder cancer. Cystoscopy revealed a suspicious lesion in the bladder, and a biopsy confirmed urothelial carcinoma. The patient has agreed to undergo surgery to remove the tumor, and his tissue and urine samples will be collected for this clinical trial. He has not received any prior treatment with FGFR inhibitors.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who lives in Spain. He has a history of smoking, having smoked a pack of cigarettes a day for the past 20 years. He recently started experiencing shortness of breath, especially when walking up stairs or doing any physical activity. He also coughs frequently, particularly in the morning. He is interested in participating in a study on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) prevalence as he wants to learn more about his symptoms and how to manage them. He is able to provide oral consent for the brief telephone interview and is willing to sign the informed consent to continue participating in the study if selected. He does not have any physical or cognitive difficulties that would prevent him from participating in the study tests.

A 20-year-old female presents to the clinic seeking an abortion in her 21st week of pregnancy. She has no known medical or surgical history and is not currently taking any medications. She reports no allergies and denies any significant family history of medical conditions. The patient has a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy with a gestational age of 20 weeks and 4 days. She is interested in participating in a pilot study investigating the addition of osmotic dilators to the preparation prior to labor induction abortion. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no evidence of fetal demise, ruptured membranes, or pelvic infection. She is able to provide informed consent for participation in the trial.

A 27-year-old male with a history of depression and financial difficulties presented to the emergency department with complaints of severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and difficulty breathing. On further inquiry, he revealed that he had ingested an unknown quantity of pesticide tablets as a means of suicide. The patient was immediately intubated and transferred to the Poison Control Center of Ain-Shams University hospitals. He was diagnosed with acute intoxication with Aluminium Phosphide and was enrolled in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of N-acetyl Cysteine, Acetyl L-Carnitine, and Medicated Paraffin Oil as supplements to the routine treatment for Aluminium Phosphide poisoning. The patient met all the inclusion criteria for the study and had no history of cardiac, renal, or hepatic diseases.

Patient A is a 65-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer and is currently being followed and treated at CHUM. His PSA level was found to be elevated during a routine check-up and a biopsy confirmed the presence of cancer cells in his prostate gland. He has no significant medical history and does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. His current treatment plan involves hormone therapy and radiation therapy. His treating physician has requested a PSMA-PET scan to better assess the extent and location of the cancer. He has no history of claustrophobia and is able to complete the imaging procedure.

The patient is a 52-year-old man with a history of stable angina pectoris for the past 3 months. He has been on medical therapy with anti-anginal agents, including nitroglycerin, aspirin, and a statin. He is a non-smoker and does not have any significant past medical history. His physical exam and lab studies are within normal limits. He underwent a coronary angiogram that showed a significant stenosis in his right coronary artery. He has been deemed a candidate for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The treating physician has recommended stent implantation using a sirolimus-eluting stent (SES). The patient has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of the procedure and has provided written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial. He meets the eligibility criteria for this study. He is willing to undergo OCT and IVUS evaluation at post-stenting, 6 months, and 12 months follow-up visits.

A 32-year-old male veteran who served in Afghanistan was diagnosed with PTSD three years ago. He experiences frequent nightmares, flashbacks, and anxiety attacks. He avoids situations that remind him of the traumatic events he experienced during his deployment. He is currently not taking any medication for his symptoms. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help him manage his PTSD symptoms. He has no history of substance abuse, psychosis, or bipolar disorder. He is not currently engaged in psychosocial treatment for PTSD. He has completed high school and has no significant cognitive impairment. He is willing to attend four assessment sessions and up to 15 treatment sessions.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes. She was diagnosed with diabetes 7 years ago and has been taking glimepiride as monotherapy for the past 12 weeks. Her HbA1c level at Visit 1 and Visit 3 was 8.5%. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m^2 and is currently not on any other medications. She has a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in regular exercise. She has no history of allergies or any other medical conditions. Her family history is negative for diabetes. She works as a receptionist and has a stressful job. She has a good support system at home and lives with her husband and two children. She has no history of severe hypoglycemia. Her fasting plasma glucose level at Visit 1 and Visit 3 was 180mg/dl.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male volunteers aged 20 to <40 years old with a BMI of 18.5 kg/m2 to <25.0 kg/m2. The food effect part of the study is specifically looking for Japanese men, while the Caucasian subject part is seeking Caucasian men. Participants must be free of any diseases requiring treatment, history of heart failure, alcoholism or drug addiction, and drug allergies. Additionally, participants must test negative for infectious diseases, except for individuals who are positive for active antibodies produced by hepatitis B vaccination and are not infected with hepatitis B virus at screening. Written voluntary informed consent is required to participate in the study.

36 yo F with recurrent low back pain for over a year, with occasional referred pain to the buttock without any radicular symptoms, presents for evaluation for possible participation in a clinical trial investigating the effect of inspiratory muscle training on proprioceptive postural control in individuals with low back pain. Patient reports at least 3 episodes of disabling low back pain in the past year, with a score of 26% on the Oswestry Disability Index. Patient is willing to sign the informed consent and meets the inclusion criteria for the trial, including age between 18-45 years old and no history of major trauma or orthopedic surgery on the spine, pelvis, or lower quadrant. Patient reports no history of Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis, or stroke, and no history of vestibular disorder, respiratory disease, or current pregnancy. Patient is a non-smoker and is not currently taking strong opioids.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who carries the BRCA1 gene mutation. She has a strong family history of breast cancer, with her mother and sister both diagnosed with the disease before the age of 50. The patient has no personal history of breast cancer. She underwent genetic counseling and decided to undergo prophylactic open nipple sparing mastectomy to reduce her risk of developing breast cancer. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history.

The patient is a 52-year-old female of African American descent who presents with complaints of bloating, abdominal pain, and difficulty in eating. She reports a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has had occasional vaginal bleeding between periods. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. She works as a high school teacher and is married with two children. She smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally on weekends. She underwent a pelvic ultrasound which showed a large ovarian mass. Further investigations revealed the presence of advanced stage (FIGO stage III) ovarian cancer. She is scheduled for primary cytoreductive surgery and has provided written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

28-year-old male native Chinese speaker with normal hearing was referred to the clinical trial by the language department at the university. He has been living in the US for the past 5 years and has been struggling with learning English as his second language. He has completed beginner and intermediate level English courses and is currently enrolled in an advanced course but has hit a learning plateau. He reports difficulty with distinguishing certain English sounds and often feels frustrated when communicating with native speakers. He denies having any hearing difficulties or history of ear infections. He has no other medical history and is not on any medications. He is interested in participating in the study to see if the incidental auditory category training can help improve his English language skills.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who underwent a Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery 8 months ago. She has been experiencing fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath. Her blood work showed a vitamin B12 deficiency with a level of 180 pmol/l. She is married and works as a nurse. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. She is not currently taking any vitamin supplements. Her BMI was 41 before the surgery and currently is 32. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet prescribed by her bariatric surgeon. She has no history of gastrointestinal diseases or psychiatric disorders. She is interested in participating in the study to find the most effective treatment for her vitamin B12 deficiency.

The patient is a 20 year old female diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for the past 3 years. She has been using an insulin pump for the past year and is currently taking a total daily insulin dose of 0.5 units/kg/day. Her HbA1c level is 7.5%. She is willing to infuse 1 ml of hyaluronidase (Hylenex) into the insulin infusion set after insertion on day 1 and day 3 of the week she is assigned to use hyaluronidase. She is also willing to use a Silhouette or Comfort insulin infusion set throughout the study, including the Duo Infusion Tubing for infusion of hyaluronidase. She is willing to eat the same breakfast each morning for the first two weeks of the study and take two 500mg tablets of Tylenol Regular Strength and monitor glucose levels at ½, 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 hours later. She is not currently known to be pregnant and has an understanding of and willingness to follow the protocol and sign the informed consent. She is able to understand spoken or written English.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been smoking for the past 10 years. She smokes at least 10 cigarettes a day and feels motivated to quit smoking in the next month. She is concerned about her weight and reports a weight concern score of 70 on a 100-point scale. She is not currently using any other smoking cessation or weight loss therapies. She has never been diagnosed or treated for an eating disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or schizoaffective disorder. She does not have a history of substance abuse or dependence. She has no current or past suicidal or homicidal ideation. She is generally healthy and able to travel to the study location for appointments. She lives alone and works in an office.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma 2 years ago. She has undergone chemotherapy treatment with doxorubicin and nitrogen mustard, but her disease has relapsed. She presents with an enlarged lymph node in her neck and painless swelling in her armpits. She reports feeling fatigued and experiencing night sweats over the past few weeks. The patient has undergone a biopsy which confirmed a diagnosis of CD30 positive classical Hodgkin's lymphoma. Her PET scan showed that she has FDG-avid disease and measurable disease of at least 1.5 cm by spiral CT. The patient has a cardiac ejection fraction of greater than 45%, and a hemoglobin-adjusted diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide of greater than 50% on pulmonary function testing. Her serum creatinine is less than or equal to 1.5 mg/dL, and her ANC and platelet counts are within normal limits. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to use an acceptable form of birth control. She is HIV negative and has not received more than 1 prior treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial as she hopes to avoid the toxicities associated with ICE chemotherapy prior to autologous stem cell transplant.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 4. He has been diagnosed with anemia and has not received treatment with Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents (ESAs) or HIF-PH inhibitors in the past 8 weeks. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 45 mL/min/1.73m^2. He weighs 75 kg and is 5'9" tall. He has not started dialysis and is not expected to start during the study period. His hemoglobin levels during the screening period have been between 9.0 and 10.5 g/dL, and his ferritin levels are above 50 ng/mL. He does not have a history of congestive heart failure or cardio(cerebro-)vascular events within the past 6 months. He does not have sustained and poorly controlled arterial hypertension or hypotension at randomization. He does not have proliferative choroidal or retinal disease requiring invasive treatment.

Pt is a 10yo M with a history of cerebral palsy due to periventricular white matter injury. The patient is classified as high functioning (level I) on the Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS). The patient has no history of genetic syndrome, brain trauma or operation. The patient is able to sit still for extended periods of time without difficulty. There are no metal implants or baclofen pumps present in the patient.

A 55-year-old man diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. He has been experiencing increased urine protein excretion for the last year, and his HbA1c level is currently at 8%. He has not received any SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy in the last 10 weeks, and his diabetes therapy has been stable for the past 3 months. His ACE inhibitors or ARBs doses have also been stable for the past 3 months. The patient is capable of providing informed consent and is interested in participating in the MEDiaN study to better understand the contribution of fuel metabolism to the development of diabetic nephropathy. He has no significant medical history, is not currently participating in any other clinical trials, and is not taking any anti-obesity drugs or systemic glucocorticoids. The patient is willing to take empagliflozin 10mg daily for 30 days to contribute to the study.

Patient B is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. She is scheduled for a modified radical mastectomy and has agreed to participate in a clinical trial comparing two regional anesthesia techniques. Patient B has an American Society of Anesthesiologists classification of II and has no history of coagulopathies or chronic opioid therapy. She has signed the consent form to participate in the study. Patient B's BMI is 25 and she has no known allergies or contraindications to the administration of the drugs used in the study.

Mary is a 45 year old woman who was diagnosed with melanoma that has spread to other parts of her body. She has a history of sunburns and has fair skin. She noticed a mole on her leg that started to change in color and size over the past few months. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic melanoma. She has no history of other cancers and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable

A 43-year old female patient has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) by her physician. She reports difficulty falling asleep, maintaining sleep, or waking up too early at least 3 nights per week for the past 6 months. She rates her insomnia severity as ≥10 on the Insomnia Severity Index. The patient is an English speaker and has a core score of 28 on the Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE), indicating reduced risk of dementia. She does not have any known untreated sleep disorders such as sleep apnea or restless leg syndrome, and scores <4 on STOP BANG indicating low risk of sleep apnea. She does not report any symptoms that suggest an increased risk of restless leg syndrome on the Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) Diagnosis Index. The patient does not have any other nervous system disorder other than MS and has not experienced a relapse or received corticosteroid treatment in the past 8 weeks.

45 year old overweight man with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and a history of prediabetes has been invited to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of a fibre mixture on SCFA/acetate metabolism. The patient has no known history of cardiovasular disease, cancer, liver or kidney malfunction, or gastroenterological diseases. The patient does not have any plans to lose weight or follow a hypocaloric diet, and does not engage in intensive exercise training. The patient does not regularly use pre- or probiotic products, laxation products, or antibiotics. The patient is a non-smoker and does not regularly consume alcohol or drugs. The patient's diet does not follow vegan guidelines. The patient is interested in participating in the study and will undergo a screening process to determine eligibility.

58-year-old male with a history of hepatitis C infection and cirrhosis presents for a planned elective in situ split liver operation with following resection after approximately ten days. The patient is fluent in German and able to provide informed consent. He has no known psychiatric or neurological disorders and is not taking any psychotropic drugs on a regular basis. The patient's American Society of Anaesthesiologists (ASA) classification is II. He has no significant visual or auditory impairments and scored above 23 on the mini mental state examination (MMSE) at screening. The patient is willing to save and hand out pseudonymised data within the clinical study.

Patient is a 57-year-old male from the United States who presents with a history of transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder. The patient has undergone platinum-containing chemotherapy in the past for the treatment of the tumor, but unfortunately, the disease progressed within 12 months of the last dose. The patient has measurable or nonmeasurable disease and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has adequate hematologic, coagulation, hepatic and renal function. The patient has not received more than 2 prior systemic chemotherapy regimens in any setting. The patient is surgically sterile and compliant with a contraceptive regimen during and for 12 weeks after the treatment period. The patient has not received prior systemic taxane therapy for Transitional Cell Carcinoma of the bladder, urethra, ureter, or renal pelvis in any setting (neoadjuvant, adjuvant, metastatic). The patient has no history of uncontrolled hereditary or acquired bleeding or thrombotic disorders. The patient has no known brain metastases, uncontrolled spinal cord compression, or leptomeningeal disease. The patient has no ongoing or active infection requiring parenteral antibiotic, antifungal, or antiviral therapy. The patient has no known human immunodeficiency virus infection or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. The patient has not received a prior autologous or allogeneic organ or tissue transplantation. The patient has not undergone major surgery within 28 days prior to randomization, or subcutaneous venous access device placement within 7 days prior to randomization. The patient has no serious nonhealing wound, ulcer, or bone fracture within 28 days prior to randomization.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She is currently in her second trimester, between 16+0 to 32+6 weeks. She has been experiencing mild to moderate depressive symptoms, such as feeling sad and hopeless, for the past few weeks. She is interested in participating in the study to try out the Enjoy Your Bump online Cognitive Behavioural Therapy course to help manage her symptoms. She speaks fluent English and has access to the internet. She has not received any psychological therapy in the past and is not currently taking part in any other mental health research studies.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past year. She experiences frequent asthma attacks which are difficult to control despite being on regular anti-asthmatic medication. She has never smoked and does not have any other significant medical history. She is able to swallow capsules and is willing to adhere to the procedures outlined in the protocol, including keeping a diary of her peak expiratory flow rate. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is currently using a medically approved method of contraception. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to medications. She has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

52-year-old male with a history of smoking and recently diagnosed with lung cancer. The patient is scheduled to undergo bronchoscopy for further evaluation and staging of the tumor. The patient has no known history of bleeding disorders or coagulopathy. Platelet count is normal and prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time are within normal limits. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this study.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who suffered third-degree burns on her left arm and hand in a house fire. She has undergone multiple surgeries to release scar contractures and improve function and mobility of the affected limb. However, she continues to experience significant scar contraction, limiting her ability to perform daily activities and causing discomfort and pain. She is a non-smoker and has no psychiatric disorders. She is willing and able to give informed consent for the study. She has sufficient tissue available for a perforator-based interposition flap.

The patient is a 23-year-old female who has no significant medical history and is in good health. She has a body weight of 60 kg and a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She has never had any allergies or hypersensitivity to any drug compound. She does not consume alcohol or other substances. She is interested in participating in clinical trials and is willing to adhere to the protocol and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 5 years. He reports that he has been experiencing difficulty with coughing and clearing his throat for the past few months. He describes the sensation as feeling like he has something in his throat that he can't get rid of. The patient has never smoked and has no history of lung disease or head and neck cancer. He reports that he has not had any recent chest infections. He has been taking medication for his Parkinson's disease, and his last evaluation with his neurologist showed that he is at Hoehn & Yahr stage III. His pulmonary function testing is within normal limits. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is interested in participating in the study to help further understanding of cough function in Parkinson's disease.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She has been married for 5 years and has one child. She and her husband have discussed having more children in the future, but she is now faced with the possibility of losing her fertility due to chemotherapy. She completed her first round of chemotherapy two weeks ago and is scheduled to receive several more rounds over the next few months. She has been using a contraceptive method consistently for the past year, but she is concerned about the long-term effects of chemotherapy on her reproductive system. She has a college degree and works in a professional setting. She was diagnosed with breast cancer at an early stage and has a good prognosis. She is currently experiencing some anxiety and distress related to her diagnosis and the possibility of losing her fertility. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

A 32 year-old male presents with a history of severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and weight loss over the past few weeks. He has a history of ulcerative colitis (UC) for the past 5 years, which has been managed with mesalamine and infrequent courses of prednisone. However, over the past month, his symptoms have worsened despite increasing his mesalamine dose. He has had 8-10 bowel movements per day, with increased urgency, and passage of bloody stools. He reports a 10-pound weight loss over the past month. On examination, his abdomen is tender to palpation in the left lower quadrant. There is no hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy. His laboratory tests are notable for an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 50 mm/h and a C-reactive protein (CRP) of 30 mg/L. Stool studies were negative for infectious etiologies. A colonoscopy was performed, which showed continuous inflammation from the rectum to the splenic flexure. The patient was diagnosed with acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) and recommended for corticosteroid treatment.

Sophie is a 4-month-old infant who was born prematurely at 32 weeks gestation. She was diagnosed with short bowel syndrome shortly after birth, which necessitated the initiation of parenteral nutrition (PN) for her nutritional requirements. Despite aggressive management of her PN regimen, her laboratory values have continued to show evidence of parenteral nutrition-associated liver disease (PNALD), including elevated serum liver enzymes and direct bilirubin. Sophie has been trialed on various therapies to prevent the progression of cholestasis, including the reduction/removal of copper and manganese from daily PN, the trial of enteral feedings, and the use of ursodiol and phenobarbital. However, her condition has not improved. Sophie is otherwise healthy and has no other documented causes of chronic liver disease, nor does she have any contraindications for the use of Omegaven. Her parents have given informed consent for Sophie to participate in this compassionate use protocol.

A 35-year-old woman presents with a history of weight gain over the last year despite being physically active and eating a healthy diet. She reports feeling fatigued and having difficulty concentrating. Her fasting blood glucose level was found to be 110mg/dL during a routine check-up. She has no known allergies to citrus fruits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to test the effects of naringenin and beta carotene on energy expenditure and glucose metabolism. She is willing to commit to an 8-week treatment and undergo assessments such as resting metabolic rate, oral glucose tolerance test, ambulatory blood pressure, and recording of adverse events.

The patient is a 70-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
