He has been on warfarin therapy for several years but was unable to achieve a therapeutic international normalized ratio (INR) despite multiple dose adjustments. The patient has had two previous percutaneous left atrial appendage (LAA) closure procedures, but both were unsuccessful due to significant residual leaks. The patient has a moderate embolic risk (CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3) and a high associated hemorrhagic risk (HASBLED score of 4). The patient has a history of gastrointestinal bleeding and is unable to tolerate oral anticoagulation. The patient has not had any thromboembolic events despite the incomplete LAA closure procedures. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of transcatheter leak closure with detachable vascular coils. The patient has provided written informed consent and is able to comply with the requirements of the study.

Patient is a 32-year-old mother of a 3-year-old child who recently visited the pediatric clinic for a routine check-up. The mother is concerned about the safety of her home and wants to learn more about how to keep her child safe. She is fluent in English and has no history of cognitive or learning disabilities. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve home safety education using a safe home model. The mother is willing to attend a session at the clinic and be randomized to either the safe home model group or the printed safety education materials (TIPP materials) group. She is committed to learning and retaining safety information for the benefit of her child.

The patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman who is scheduled for an elective cesarean section. She is a healthy non-smoker with no medical history of hypertension, diabetes, or any other complications during her pregnancy. Her body mass index is within the normal range, and her height is 170 cm. She has no contraindications to spinal anesthesia and has not been diagnosed with any psychiatric diseases. Her fetal heart rate is normal, and she does not have any excessive bleeding during the surgery. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the study to assess the efficacy and safety of epidural volume extension and intrathecal use of local anesthetics during cesarean sections.

A 33-year-old female with a BMI of 28.5 who has been trying to conceive for over a year with her partner, who has been diagnosed with oligoasthenozoospermia, is interested in participating in a clinical trial for in vitro fertilization. She has normal transvaginal ultrasound during the follicular phase and a normal endometrial thickness of 10mm with a regular echo pattern. She has no history of severe ovarian hyperstimulation or recurrent abortions. She is undergoing her first IVF cycle with no history of PGS or PGD. She has a normal karyotyping and no diagnosed liver or renal disease. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

Patient is a 40-year-old woman with a family history of breast cancer. She recently had a mammogram that showed dense breast tissue (type 3 or 4). She has no current breast symptoms and has never had breast cancer before. She is not pregnant and is not currently breastfeeding. She has no contraindications to breast MBI or breast tomosynthesis. Her BMI is within the normal range. She is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

A 56-year-old male patient with a history of smoking (20 pack-years) was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer two months ago. He underwent 6 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy and had a partial response but still has residual disease. He has no previous history of cancer or any other significant medical illness. He is currently experiencing no symptoms related to the cancer. MRI of the brain showed no evidence of metastases. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore additional treatment options.

A 29-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted to the hospital due to a preterm labor at 32 weeks and 5 days of gestation. She has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections during the pregnancy, which were treated with antibiotics. The patient's obstetric history is unremarkable, and this is her first pregnancy. She is currently receiving magnesium sulfate to prevent seizures and steroids to enhance fetal lung maturation. The patient is in good general health and denies any history of chronic diseases. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. The patient speaks German and English fluently. She agrees to participate in the study and has given her informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has been experiencing symptoms of influenza for the past 24 hours, including headache, fatigue, chills, and cough. He has a fever of 38.5ºC and a sore throat. He has not been diagnosed with any underlying medical conditions and is not currently taking any medication. He has not received a flu vaccination in the past 3 months. The patient is willing to provide a pharyngeal or throat swab and blood sample for the study. He has read and understood the informed consent form and agrees to participate in the clinical trial.

A 50-year-old woman was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer after a routine mammogram. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed HER2-negative breast cancer. The patient has never received chemotherapy before, and her medical history is remarkable for hypertension and hypothyroidism, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of cardiac disease or psychiatric illness. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and she is postmenopausal. An MRI showed several breast cancer lesions in her liver, and a CT scan showed bone metastases. Her laboratory analysis is remarkable for mildly elevated liver enzymes, hemoglobin level of 11.5 g/dl, platelet count of 120,000/ul, and an ANC of 1,800/ul. She is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and has no allergies. She has not received hormonal therapy for metastatic disease, but she received adjuvant tamoxifen for 5 years after her primary breast cancer treatment. She has never received radiation therapy for bone metastases. She is willing to use a medically acceptable method of contraception during the trial.

A 42 year old woman has recently been diagnosed with high grade glioma after experiencing headaches and seizures. She underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis and her performance status is at 70%. The patient has no history of radiation therapy, chemotherapy or any other cancer treatment. The blood test shows that she meets the inclusion criteria with an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mcl, platelets of 150,000/mcl, hematocrit of 35% and an absolute lymphocyte count of 1,200/mcl. Her post-operative treatment plan includes standard radiation and temozolomide. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and has signed the informed consent document. She has no history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical or biological composition to filgrastim or plerixafor or any other agents used in the study. She has not experienced any fresh CNS bleed as evident by MRI or CT. She is not contraindicated for anticoagulation and has no uncontrolled intercurrent illness. She is not pregnant and her HIV status is negative.

A 47-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a history of hypertension for the past 2 years. She is currently taking lisinopril 10mg daily. Her LDL cholesterol level has been consistently above 140mg/dL despite dietary modifications. She has been prescribed atorvastatin 20mg daily for the past 3 months. Her fasting blood glucose levels have been elevated, and she was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus a year ago. Her HbA1C level has been consistently around 7.5% over the past 6 months, and she is taking metformin 1000mg twice daily. She has no history of congestive heart failure, unstable angina, or acute coronary syndrome. There is no significant history of gastrointestinal disorders, peripheral arterial disease, or cancer. She has no known allergies to any medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume more than one alcoholic beverage per week. Her blood pressure is 136/86 mmHg, and BMI is 28. She is a well-nourished woman with no acute distress.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman with a history of alopecia areata. She has patchy hair loss on her scalp, covering about 20% of the surface area. She has not received any treatment for her alopecia areata in the past month. She has no evidence of hair regrowth at baseline. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no known hypersensitivity to Triamcinolone acetonide or its vehicle. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of different concentrations of localized steroid injections in the treatment of alopecia areata.

A 35-year-old man was diagnosed with a soft tissue sarcoma on his left thigh. He was initially treated with radiation therapy and surgery. However, a few months later, he experienced a recurrence of the tumor, which has now spread to the lungs. His past medical history is unremarkable. He doesn't smoke, drink, or use illicit drugs. He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. His performance status is 1. He has a normal blood count, serum creatinine, and electrolytes. He has no history of cardiac disease. He is not taking any medications that inhibit platelet function or anticoagulants. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no history of bleeding disorder or long QT syndrome. He weighs 70 kg. He is willing to use an effective method of birth control during the course of the study and for up to 3 months following the last dose of the study drug. He is aware of the investigational nature of the study and has provided written, informed consent and authorization to release protected health information. A paraffin block from a previous surgery will be available for correlative studies.

The patient is a 3-week-old male infant who was born at 39 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 4.5 kg (LGA). He was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to dysphagia and poor oral feeding intake. The infant's body composition assessment revealed a fat-mass z-score of +1.5. He is otherwise healthy, with no respiratory support needed, no significant neurological morbidities, and no major congenital or genetic syndromes/anomalies. The baby is currently receiving breast milk feedings per standard feeding protocols. The physicians are concerned about his ability to feed orally and are considering enrolling him in a clinical trial to investigate the impact of calorie-restricted feeding on body composition and oral feeding intake volumes in dysphagic LGA infants.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of ventricular tachycardia (VT) and a previous episode of cardiac arrest. He is scheduled for a VT ablation procedure due to recurrent episodes despite being on antiarrhythmic therapy. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 45%. He has no known allergies to medications and has not been enrolled in any other concurrent study. He is willing to provide informed consent and is above 18 years of age. He has no history of pericarditis or previous sternotomy. He is not pacemaker dependent and has no implanted active cardiac or non-cardiac device. He has no known skin irritations to the Physio Control Fast Patch ECG Electrode. He has no history of hiatus hernia or pectus excavatum. He has no known medical conditions that would limit his participation in the study, and he is not pregnant.

25 year old male, right-handed, presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe right shoulder pain after falling from his bicycle while riding downhill. The patient reports that he originally fell onto his outstretched arm and hand, and then his shoulder dislocated anteriorly. He went to an urgent care center, and his shoulder was reduced through manipulation. He reports no prior history of dislocations, subluxations, or instability of the shoulder. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant past medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is a student and works part-time as a waiter. He reports no limitations in his activities of daily living, although he has some pain and difficulty with overhead activities. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the anterior aspect of the shoulder, with no neurovascular compromise. There is no evidence of any other injuries, and range of motion of the cervical spine, elbow and wrist are normal. X-rays show anterior shoulder dislocation and no associated fractures. The patient is willing to participate in the study and comply with the rehabilitative protocol and required follow-up assessments.

The patient is a 40 year old male with second and third degree burns covering 25% of his body. The burn occurred 2 weeks ago from a workplace accident involving an explosion. The patient is experiencing acute stress disorder, with symptoms including recurring nightmares, insomnia, and anxiety. He is currently receiving medical treatment at a burn center and has no history of pre-existing psychiatric disorders. The patient speaks English and is able to provide informed consent.

A 54-year-old male with a medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, and difficulty swallowing. After undergoing further evaluation, he is diagnosed with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the gastroesophageal junction. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy for metastatic disease and has not undergone any major surgical procedures within the past 28 days. He is able to swallow oral medications and has an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient is not currently taking any anticoagulants (other than aspirin and anti-platelet agents) and has not received any immune modulators in the past 30 days. He has not participated in any other investigational device/drug trials within the past 30 days and is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 52-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 8 years and has been on oral antidiabetic therapy for the last 2 years. Despite following a strict diet and regular exercise, his blood glucose levels have not been adequately controlled. He has a BMI of 30 and has a sedentary lifestyle due to his desk job. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He has never been on insulin therapy before and is willing to sign informed consent to participate in the observational study.

50 year old male diagnosed with moderate to severe chronic plaque-type psoriasis for 5 years. He has been treated with topical treatments, phototherapy, and oral medications, but has only achieved a partial response with a PASI score of 50. He participated in the previous clinical trial CAIN457A2304 and received secukinumab, which resulted in a partial response. He has not had any major protocol deviations during the previous trial. He is willing to participate in the current study to assess the safety and efficacy of intravenous and subcutaneous secukinumab. He understands and is able to comply with the requirements of the study. He is not pregnant or lactating, and has not had any ongoing inflammation diseases other than psoriasis that might confound the evaluation of the benefits of secukinumab therapy.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who recently suffered an ankle fracture due to a fall at home. He has a medical history of hypertension and takes medication to manage it. He is generally healthy and active, but is concerned about the potential risks associated with surgery at his age. He has been advised to undergo a minimally invasive surgical approach to treat his ankle fracture and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to track his surgical outcomes and post-operative course.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer presents with metastatic disease to the liver and lungs. She has undergone chemotherapy in the past and has been found to carry a BRCA2 mutation. She is currently experiencing abdominal pain, fatigue, and shortness of breath. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of rucaparib in treating locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer or advanced ovarian cancer. She meets the eligibility criteria as a proven known carrier of a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation and has had no more than 5 prior chemotherapy regimens in the last 5 years. She has measurable disease as assessed by X-ray, computerized tomography (CT), or MRI scan, and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. She has a WHO performance status of 1 and meets the required haematological and biochemical indices. She is willing to provide written consent and capable of co-operating with treatment and follow-up.

56 year old male with a history of root canal treatment on tooth number 14 that has failed and requires retreatment. He has no known systemic diseases and is in good overall health. He reports occasional mild pain in the area but no acute apical abscesses. He is able to understand the measurement tool and has agreed to sign an informed consent form. He is not currently using antibiotics or corticosteroids.

This is a 19 year-old male with a clinical diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) without co-occurring intellectual impairment. He is currently enrolled in high school and is interested in pursuing a post-secondary education. However, he has difficulty with time management and self-regulation, which may impede his success in higher education. He currently receives some support services through his school, but his family is interested in exploring additional resources to ensure a successful transition from high school to college. He does not have any psychiatric disturbances that warrant immediate treatment and does not have an intellectual disability.

A 17-year-old male presented with abdominal pain and distension. The imaging studies showed multiple peritoneal masses and biopsy of the masses revealed desmoplastic small round cell tumor (DSRCT). He has no significant past medical history. His performance status is 1 and he is currently attending high school. His laboratory results are as follows: Hgb: 12g/dL, WBC: 6,500/mm3, Platelet: 240,000/mm3, Creatinine: 0.9mg/dL, Bilirubin: 0.7mg/dL, AST: 28IU/L. His cardiac function is normal without any history of hypertension, myocardial infarction or stroke. He does not have any history of hemoptysis or significant vascular disease. He is willing to use contraception throughout the study.

48-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and liver cirrhosis was recently diagnosed with portal vein thrombosis. He has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and occasional vomiting for the past few weeks. The patient's serum level of AT-III is 65%, which is below the inclusion criteria threshold for this clinical trial. He has not received any anticoagulant therapy in the last 7 days and has no history of allergy to contrast agents. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is able to provide written informed consent. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications.

Mrs. Anderson is a 65 year old retired school teacher who has been experiencing pain and stiffness in her shoulder for the past few years. She has been seeing a local orthopedic surgeon for this and has been diagnosed with glenohumeral osteoarthritis. The surgeon has recommended a total shoulder arthroplasty to alleviate her symptoms. Mrs. Anderson is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the Comprehensive Nano stemless total shoulder prosthesis with the Comprehensive stemmed total shoulder prosthesis. She is a Danish citizen and has been referred to the orthopedic department at Copenhagen University Hospital in Gentofte. She has no cognitive or linguistic impairments, no issues with rotator cuff function, and is otherwise in good health. She has been excluded from previous clinical trials due to poor bone quality, but her orthopedic surgeon has confirmed that she is eligible for this study. Mrs. Anderson is excited to participate in this trial and contribute to the advancement of treatment options for patients with osteoarthritis of the shoulder.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl who was diagnosed with a superficial Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE). She has a visible red, raised lesion on her skin that has been growing slowly over the past few months. The lesion is located on her left arm and is causing her discomfort and itching. She has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. Her parents are concerned about the appearance of the lesion and the potential for it to cause further complications. They are interested in exploring treatment options and are open to participating in a clinical trial. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to tacrolimus. Her parents are willing to comply with all study procedures and availability for the duration of the study.

This is a 34 year old female with no significant medical history who has volunteered to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of pazopanib eye drops. She has a body weight of 60 kg and a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2. Her best-corrected visual acuity is better than 20/80 in both eyes. She is a non-smoker and has no history of regular alcohol consumption. She has not undergone any eye surgery within the past three months, nor does she have any active ocular disease that may interfere with the study assessments or endpoints. She is willing to refrain from wearing contact lenses during the study and up to 2 weeks before the study start. She has not participated in any clinical trial where she has received an investigational product within the past 30 days or 5 half-lives prior to the first dose of study medication. She is capable of giving written informed consent and is willing to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman from the United States who was diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) in 2008. She has been on methotrexate and sulfasalazine, but her symptoms have not improved. Her doctor has recommended starting a biologic DMARD (bDMARD) and has prescribed her with Humira. However, she is concerned about the cost of the medication and the impact it will have on her finances. She has private health insurance that covers both medical and pharmacy benefits, and has no history of using bDMARDs in the past. She is willing to participate in the study to help assess the impact of patient cost sharing on treatment discontinuation of biologic agents in patients with RA.

57 yo male with a history of multiple sclerosis (MS) and relapses in the past year leading to increased disability. The patient has been receiving plasmapheresis (also known as plasma exchange) as a treatment option for MS with citrate anticoagulation. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently on medication for these conditions. The patient has no known bleeding disorders and has not experienced any significant bleeding events in the past. The patient is interested in participating in this study to better understand the effects of plasmapheresis on their coagulation status and to potentially explore the use of fibrinogen concentrate replacement to correct any coagulation disorders induced by the procedure. The patient is a resident of Ljubljana, Slovenia and is willing to undergo repeated plasmapheresis treatments at UKC Ljubljana.

A 55 yo F who suffered from a left-sided ischemic stroke 8 months ago, leading to chronic hemiparesis of the upper extremity. The patient has been taking anti-spasticity medications and injections for the past 6 months. She reports moderate hand impairment and experiences pain in the upper extremity, with a self-reported pain score of 4 on a 10-point scale. The patient is able to follow single-step commands and has no contractures greater than 20 degrees. She is interested in participating in a therapeutic program that could help improve her hand function and quality of life.

A 14-year-old boy with Duchenne muscular dystrophy has been using a wheelchair for the past year as he is unable to walk without assistive devices. He was diagnosed with DMD at the age of 7 through genetic confirmation. His primary relative, his older brother, also has DMD. The patient has been experiencing a decline in his physical abilities and has difficulty lifting his arms and legs. He has difficulty with swallowing and requires assistance with feeding. The patient is able to understand and cooperate with the testing required for this clinical trial. His parents are interested in participating in this study to help further research on DMD and potentially improve treatment options for their son.

Patient is a 26-year-old woman from Brazil who is pregnant with her first child and is participating in the Prenatal Program of the public health system in Uberlandia city. She is in her third trimester of pregnancy and has not experienced any complications. She is sexually active and has had at least one sexual relationship in the last four weeks. She reports being able to contract her pelvic floor muscles. She has no previous history of urogynecological surgery or urinary tract infection. She has no cognitive impairment or neurological condition that could affect muscle activation. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

This is a 58 year old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity who presented to the hospital with symptoms of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infection and admitted to the ICU due to respiratory failure. Despite mechanical ventilation, the patient developed organ dysfunction with a SOFA score of 3 and laboratory findings consistent with immune dysregulation, including low HLA-DR expression on CD14+ monocytes and elevated IL-6 levels. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial for personalized immunotherapy and has provided written informed consent. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria, including no history of malignancy, do not resuscitate decision, active tuberculosis, or HIV infection. The patient also does not have a medical history of systemic lupus erythematosus or multiple sclerosis. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and a urine pregnancy test was negative. The patient has not received corticosteroids or any anti-cytokine biological treatment in the last month.

The patient is a 25 year old female who has recently been diagnosed with relapsing MS based on Poser's criteria. She has been experiencing symptoms such as numbness, tingling, and weakness on the right side of her body for the past 6 months. She has not yet received any treatment for MS and is currently not taking any medication. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. She is able to perform MRI and is willing to participate in the study to determine the reliability of multimodal MRI in MS and to follow up on her condition after treatment with interferon.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who fell off his bike and landed on his outstretched hand, resulting in a distal radius fracture. He experienced immediate pain and swelling in his wrist, which worsened over the next few days. He went to the emergency department, where an x-ray confirmed the fracture. He was initially treated with a cast for 10 days, but this did not provide enough stability for the fracture to heal properly. He was then referred for surgical treatment with a locking compression plate. He has no other significant medical history, is a non-smoker, and does not use drugs or alcohol. He works in construction and is right-hand dominant. He is concerned about the impact of the injury on his ability to work and provide for his family. He is motivated to undergo surgery and follow post-operative rehabilitation protocols to ensure optimal healing and functional outcome.

N/A - This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather analyzes data from a previously conducted longitudinal study of urban Black preschool children and their families. Therefore, there are no patient descriptions needed for this trial.

A 70-year-old African American woman came to the clinic complaining of forgetfulness and difficulty with daily tasks. She has a family history of Alzheimer's Disease and is concerned about her risk. She is currently not engaged in regular physical activity and spends most of her day sitting due to her sedentary job. Her BMI is 28 and her blood pressure is slightly elevated at 140/90 mmHg. She is willing to attend group sessions and is physically capable of exercise. She has no cognitive impairment and scored a 30 on the Mini-Mental State Examination. She is willing to accept randomization and give written informed consent.

28F with a history of irregular menstrual cycles since menarche, hirsutism, and acne. She has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years without success. She was diagnosed with PCOS by her gynecologist and referred to an endocrinologist for further management. On physical examination, she was noted to have central obesity (BMI 26.5 kg/m2), hirsutism, and acne. Her blood work showed elevated levels of testosterone, luteinizing hormone (LH), and insulin. She has no history of diabetes or other endocrine disorders. She is not currently taking oral contraceptives. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve her reproductive and metabolic outcomes.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been feeling fatigued and weak for the past few weeks. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known drug allergies. On examination, he appears pale and has palpable lymph nodes in his neck and axillae. A complete blood count shows leukocytosis (white blood cell count of 40,000/μl) with 50% blasts. His bone marrow biopsy confirms the diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion transcript resulting from t(8;21)(q22;q22). His left ventricular ejection fraction is within normal limits. His bilirubin level is 2.3 times the upper limit of normal. His serum pregnancy test is negative, and he has undergone vasectomy. His corrected QT (QTc) interval is within normal limits.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with upper limb CRPS for the past 8 months. He has been experiencing severe pain, swelling, and stiffness in his right arm, making it difficult to perform regular activities. He has previously tried medication, physiotherapy, and occupational therapy with minimal improvement. He is currently taking gabapentin for pain management. He has no history of allergies, and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is currently undergoing physical therapy for his condition and has been referred for a stellate ganglion block by his physician. He speaks fluent English and is able to understand and complete the Numeric Pain Rating Scale. He is willing to participate in the study and has no objections to being randomly assigned to a treatment group.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of fatigue, recurrent infections, and abnormal bleeding for the past 6 months. She has visited her primary care physician numerous times and has been diagnosed with T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia (T-LGL). Her white blood cell count is reduced and she has an increased number of abnormal cells called large granular lymphocytes (LGLs). She has also been experiencing anemia and thrombocytopenia. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, but she is currently taking vitamin D supplements. She will be screened with a medical history and physical examination, review of pathology studies, skin biopsy, evaluation of rheumatoid arthritis if present, chest x-ray, computerized tomography (CT) scans and other imaging studies as needed, bone marrow biopsy, and blood and urine tests to determine her eligibility for the clinical trial. If eligible, she will receive a single dose of Hu-Mik-beta1 by a 90-minute infusion through a vein. She will be monitored for adverse events for 6 weeks and will undergo follow-up visits for a total of 9 months. She must have normal renal and hepatic function, a Karnofsky performance status of greater than or equal to 70%, and a life expectancy greater than 2 months. She must be able to understand and sign the Informed Consent Document. She cannot be pregnant or actively nursing, test positive for HIV or HTLV-I/II, or have a prior history of a Grade III or greater allergic reaction related to a previously administered humanized monoclonal antibody.

The patient is a 56-year-old female admitted to the hospital for abdominal pain and distension. CT scan showed a small bowel obstruction with a diameter of 4.5 cm. She has been on bowel rest and supportive care for the past 24 hours without significant improvement. The patient is clinically stable with no respiratory distress and does not require more than 2 liters of oxygen via nasal cannula. She has agreed to participate in the study and does not have any respiratory contraindications to 100% oxygen. The patient has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and is not pregnant or lactating. She is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with complaints of severe upper abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He reports a history of alcohol abuse and has a past medical history of hypertension and dyslipidemia. Upon further evaluation, the patient was found to have a high risk bleeding peptic ulcer in the duodenal bulb (Forrest Classification Ia). The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria. He has no known allergies to any medication or medical devices. The patient has no contraindications for endoscopy and is not pregnant.

A 40 year old female diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer that has recurred after initial treatment comes to the clinic. She has a history of hormone therapy and chemotherapy, and is now suitable for treatment with docetaxel. Her hormone receptor status (ER/PR) and Her-2 neu status have been determined by Immunohistochemistry within the last 21 days, and she has radiological investigations conducted within the last 21 days. She has at least one uni-dimensional measurable lesion and a disease-free interval (DFI) less than or equal to 24 months from the time of initial surgery to the current date. The patient has an ECOG status of 1, and has a life expectancy of at least 6 months. She is willing and able to follow instructions and make all required study visits, and gives written consent to participate in the study. She has adequate organ and marrow function as defined in the protocol. All of her blood tests for HIV and Hepatitis B and C are negative within the last 4 weeks prior to enrolment. She is not pregnant or breast-feeding, and has no history of seizure disorder. She is not on COX 1 or 2 prostaglandin inhibitors or H1 antagonists.

The patient is a 17-year-old girl who has been struggling with her weight and body image for several years. She is currently classified as overweight with a BMI in the 90th percentile for her age group. She has been experiencing sub-threshold eating disorder symptoms such as binge eating and feeling guilty or ashamed about her eating habits. She is motivated to make positive changes in her lifestyle and is willing to commit to a 6-week program that includes weekly 1-hour sessions and 3 separate assessment visits to the Mount Sinai Adolescent Health Center. She does not have a current diagnosis of an eating disorder and is not underweight or obese.

Patient is a 55-year-old male who presents to the clinic with a small umbilical hernia that has been present for about 6 months. He reports mild discomfort with lifting and straining activities, but otherwise has no significant pain or other symptoms. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. On physical examination, a small protrusion is noted at the umbilicus measuring approximately 2cm in diameter. The patient is interested in pursuing surgical repair and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is an amateur free diver and has been practicing apnea for the past year. He has no known history of cardiovascular or respiratory diseases and has never experienced a syncope or loss of consciousness during or after a dive. He is able to hold his breath for two minutes or more and has been participating in at least 10 sessions of apnea per year. He has not been diagnosed with any neurological conditions or recent head trauma with loss of consciousness. He does not take any medications that affect the cardiovascular or respiratory system. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to the understanding of the potential risks associated with neck extension during apnea and to improve safety measures for free divers.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has a daughter that is 12 years old. The daughter attends the Schiebler CMS clinic at the University of Florida for regular check-ups. The mother is married and works as a teacher. She has a history of seasonal allergies and has no known drug allergies. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. Her family history is negative for any significant illnesses. She has a good understanding of English and is comfortable using technology such as smartphones and computers. She is interested in receiving reminders about her daughter's HPV vaccine and participating in a phone-based motivational interview to discuss any concerns or questions she may have about the vaccine.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian woman who has recently been diagnosed with malignant melanoma. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment for the cancer. She is in generally good health with no significant past medical history. Her family history is negative for any cancers. She is willing to participate in the study and provide blood and tumor samples for research purposes. She will have about 4 1/2 tablespoons of blood drawn before starting the first day of treatment, and then about 3 tablespoons of blood drawn every 6 to 8 weeks for the next 6 months. She will have a total of up to about 5 blood draws for this portion of the study. She will also have tumor samples collected during her cancer treatment. If she agrees to take part in the follow-up portion of the study, she will have about 3 tablespoons of blood drawn once every 3 months for the next 5 years. She will have a total of about 21 blood draws for this portion of the study. All research done with her blood and tumor samples will be approved by the institutional review board (IRB) of M. D. Anderson.

The patient is a 25-year-old man who has been experiencing persistent cough, night sweats, and weight loss for the past 2 months. He presents to the TB clinic for evaluation and is found to have a positive sputum test for tuberculosis. He has no previous history of TB treatment and is confirmed to have drug-sensitive TB through rapid sputum-based testing. He weighs 70 kg and is willing to use effective birth control methods throughout the study period. He has no history of allergy to any of the trial medications and has not participated in any clinical trials with investigational agents in the past 8 weeks. He has a normal chest x-ray compatible with pulmonary TB and his blood chemistry, including creatinine and liver function tests, are within normal limits. He has no other medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the trial.

A 9-year-old boy with a diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia was admitted to the hospital for an allogeneic bone marrow transplant (BMT) after failing first-line chemotherapy. The patient received a fully matched sibling donor stem cell transplant after a myeloablative conditioning regimen. The patient developed severe mucositis and gastrointestinal toxicity, resulting in the need for enteral feeding via a nasogastric tube. The patient had no prior history of gastrointestinal disorders or nutritional deficiencies. The patient has been receiving tube feeding for over a week, and the care team is discussing the possibility of a gastrostomy tube placement as an alternative feeding option. The patient's parents have expressed concerns about the nasogastric tube causing discomfort and affecting their child's quality of life, and they are open to the idea of a gastrostomy tube. The patient is otherwise stable and has been closely monitored for any complications related to the BMT or tube feeding.

The patient is a newborn infant born prematurely at 27 weeks of gestation. The infant is currently being cared for at a level III neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and is exclusively receiving human breast milk (own mother's milk and/or donor milk). The infant is not being fed with formula and is currently receiving enteral feeds of less than 100 mL/kg/day. The legal guardians of the infant have provided written informed consent. The home clinic of the infant has the necessary logistics to maintain the intervention until gestational week 34+0. There are no known complications or malformations that would exclude the infant from participating in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing headaches and dizziness for the past few months. He visited his primary care physician, who referred him to a neurologist. The neurologist ordered an MRI, which showed a brain lesion. A biopsy revealed that the patient has a glioma with a mutation in the IDH1 gene. The patient underwent surgery to remove as much of the tumor as possible, followed by radiation and chemotherapy. His symptoms have improved, and he is currently stable. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to better understand the biology of IDH-mutant gliomas. He is willing to undergo proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to monitor the quantitative levels of 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) longitudinally. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. He has normal kidney function and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. His Karnofsky performance score is greater than or equal to 60%.

A 62-year-old non-smoking female patient with a history of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer presents with a positive EGFR mutation. She has completed first-line gemcitabine/cisplatin therapy and her disease has not progressed. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no evidence of interstitial lung disease and no hypersensitivity to icotinib or its excipients. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has at least one measurable lesion according to RECIST 1.1. She is alert and oriented with no acute distress. Vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical exam is unremarkable.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes for over 5 years. She has experienced severe hypoglycaemia episodes requiring emergency assistance in the past 2 weeks. Despite attempts to control her glucose levels through multiple daily injections, she has not been successful in preventing hypoglycaemia. She has not used continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in the past 6 months, except for short periods of diagnostic blinded use under clinic supervision. She has access to a smartphone and computer. She is not pregnant or planning pregnancy, nor is she breastfeeding. She does not have any active malignancy or under investigation for malignancy. She has normal visual acuity and manual dexterity. She is willing to participate in the study and give informed consent.

Patient is a 55-year-old male from Australia who has been recently diagnosed with malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) after experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. He has never received chemotherapy before and has undergone a transthoracic biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. His ECOG performance status is 1 and he has measurable disease according to CT-PET scans. He has not received any tumour-directed therapy in the past 3 weeks and has recovered from any toxic effects from previous therapies. His haematologic variables, including haemoglobin, ANC, and platelet count, are all within normal ranges. His serum creatinine and hepatic function variables are also normal. He has signed informed consent and is willing to use adequate contraceptive methods during the study and for three months after the end of treatment.

Patient is a 20-month-old boy living in a vulnerable family. The mother is a single parent who struggles with substance abuse and has a history of domestic violence. The child was born premature at 32 weeks and spent 4 weeks in the NICU. He currently receives regular follow-up care at a PMI clinic. The family has agreed to participate in a research project aimed at identifying and collecting the expression of psychological suffering in children under two years of age. The child does not have any serious genetic or somatic pathologies resulting in physical pain or deficiency. The mother and legal representative have consented to participate in the study.

A 10-year-old girl was referred to the clinic by her school nurse due to a positive tuberculosis skin test result. She has no symptoms of tuberculosis and no known exposure to someone with active tuberculosis. Her medical history is notable for asthma, for which she uses an albuterol inhaler as needed. She has not had any recent illnesses and is up to date on her vaccinations. Her family history is negative for tuberculosis. She is a straight-A student and enjoys playing soccer with her friends. She lives in a suburban area with her parents and younger sister. Her parents are supportive of her participation in the study and understand the importance of monitoring her latent tuberculosis infection.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with insulin resistance. She is concerned about her weight gain and is eager to find a solution to her problem. She has a BMI of 33 and is not currently pregnant. She is not taking any medications, although she does take vitamins and supplements. She has no history of gastrointestinal, liver or kidney disease, and has not had any major medical or surgical events in the last 6 months. She is willing to comply with the protocol, however, she has a busy schedule and is concerned about the time commitment required for the study. She is interested in learning more about the effects of fibre on appetite regulation and is willing to try different breakfast cereals as part of the study.

A 49-year-old female was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and has been receiving chemotherapy for the past three months. She has a medical history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which is currently being managed with medication. She has been experiencing occasional chest pain and shortness of breath, which has caused her to become anxious and worried about her health. She was referred to the PICARO program at the University Hospital of Caen Normandy to address and manage any potential cardiac adverse reactions induced by the chemotherapy. She has provided written informed consent and is a beneficiary of the French social insurance. She has no history of legal protection or guardianship.

A 30-year old woman recently gave birth to a baby boy. She is HIV positive and was diagnosed three years ago. She started taking antiretroviral therapy (ART) immediately after her diagnosis and has been adhering to her medication regimen. The patient is physically healthy and has no other underlying medical condition. She is married and has one other child, who is HIV negative. She breastfeeds her newborn baby. The patient is interested in enrolling her baby boy in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the safety and antiviral activity of VRC01 in HIV-1-infected infants beginning cART within 12 weeks of birth. She is willing to provide written informed consent for her baby's participation in the study, including collection and storage of biological specimens for exploratory virology and immunology investigations. The patient has already talked to her partner about the study and they both agreed to participate. The patient is willing to comply with study requirements and is expected to be available for 48 weeks of follow-up at study entry.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman complaining of persistent knee pain that has been worsening over the past year. She has been diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis based on clinical and radiological criteria of the American College of Rheumatology (ACR). Her symptoms include pain, stiffness, and difficulty with mobility. She has tried acetaminophen for pain relief, but it has not been effective. She has no known history of abnormal platelet counts or other medical conditions. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of glucosamine sulfate versus placebo on the symptoms of knee osteoarthritis after 6 months of treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who is experiencing severe lower back pain that radiates down his left leg. His symptoms have been present for the past 6 months, and he has been diagnosed with lumbosciatic syndrome by a rehabilitation doctor. His job requires him to sit for prolonged periods, exacerbating his symptoms. He has tried different medications and physiotherapy exercises without significant relief. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Vojta Therapy or TENS for his condition. He does not have any history of infection, metastasis, neoplasia, osteoporosis, fracture, or inflammatory arthropathy. He is otherwise healthy, with no known allergies or chronic illnesses. He is able to walk and perform daily activities, but the pain and discomfort limit his mobility and quality of life. He is interested in exploring non-invasive therapeutic options to alleviate his symptoms and improve his functionality.

A 65-year-old male patient with a history of Parkinson's disease presented to the clinic for a routine follow-up. He has been diagnosed with idiopathic PD according to the MDS clinical diagnostic criteria (Postuma et al. 2015). He has no significant medical history other than hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He lives with his wife and is retired. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or neurological diseases other than PD. He is able to walk independently and perform activities of daily living without assistance. He has no visual or auditory dysfunctions that would impair his ability to perform cognitive tests. He is able to understand and speak English fluently. He has not been diagnosed with dementia or MCI.

The patient is a 54-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of advanced non small cell lung cancer. She is experiencing some fatigue and shortness of breath, but is otherwise healthy. She has not received any previous chemotherapy or targeted therapies. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Her blood tests showed normal or near-normal levels of neutrophils, platelets, hemoglobin, bilirubin, ASAT, ALAT, and serum creatinine. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has provided written informed consent according to International Conference on Harmonization/Good Clinical Practice (ICH/GCP). She has no symptomatic brain metastases, no acute or sub-acute intestinal occlusion or history of inflammatory bowel disease, and no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has no legal incapacity or limited legal capacity, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to practice acceptable methods of birth control to prevent pregnancy. She has no clinically relevant peripheral neuropathy and no concurrent malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix. She is not suffering from any psychological, familial, sociological or geographical condition that potentially hampering compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.

This is a 45 year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 two years ago. He has a history of hypertension and has been on antihypertensive medications for the past 5 years. He has not experienced any cardiac symptoms, but his recent echocardiogram showed mild left ventricular hypertrophy. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) has been decreasing gradually over the past year and he is now considered to be at CKD stage 3B. He has no history of ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, diabetes mellitus or heart failure. He is otherwise in good health and is compliant with his medications. He has been invited to participate in a clinical trial investigating the onset and functional consequences of left ventricular interstitial fibrosis in patients with CKD stages 2 to 5. The study will involve a cardiac MRI scan, a cardiopulmonary stress echocardiogram, a 24-hour ECG holter monitor and blood tests. The study will help to determine whether transplantation results in a regression of cardiac fibrosis.

A 32-year-old woman, G2P1, presents to the clinic with a history of hypertension during her previous pregnancy. She was diagnosed with gestational hypertension during her first pregnancy and was treated with methyldopa 750mg/day. Her blood pressure was well controlled with this medication throughout her pregnancy. She delivered a healthy baby at 39 weeks via vaginal delivery. She is currently 3 weeks postpartum and her blood pressure is elevated at 150/100 mmHg. She is not experiencing any symptoms such as headache or visual changes. She has no history of other medical conditions or allergies. She is currently breastfeeding her newborn. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study.

A 65 year-old male with a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis presents with severe pain in his right hip joint. After evaluation, it was determined that the patient requires a total hip arthroplasty. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is currently not taking any anticholinergic drugs, benzodiazepines, opiates/neuroleptic drugs, or any chronic medication that may have potential immune-modulatory effects. The patient has no history of infectious disease in the last month or immune-suppressant therapy within the last two months. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of any cardiovascular or respiratory diseases. The patient is willing and able to participate in the study by completing the T-MOCA test at three different time-points (baseline, 6 weeks post-operatively, and 3 months post-operatively) to evaluate the incidence and duration of perioperative neurocognitive disorders. The patient is able to comply with the anesthesia management and monitoring of physiological parameters during general anesthesia as per standard of care practice.

The patient is a 40-year-old non-smoking female with a history of periodontal disease. She has noticed gum recession on her lower front teeth, which has caused sensitivity to hot and cold. She has good oral hygiene and has undergone scaling and root planing in the past. A dental examination revealed a Miller Class III recession defect on her lower right central incisor with a depth of 3mm and no bleeding on probing. The defect is at least 2mm in length, and the patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate treatment options. She meets all inclusion criteria, and after a thorough screening, no exclusion criteria are present. The patient provides informed consent and is randomly assigned to either the control (CTG) or OrACELL™ (test) group for treatment. Root coverage clinical parameters will be evaluated at baseline, 3-, and 6-months to determine the outcome of the treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing palpitations and shortness of breath for the past 2 weeks. She was diagnosed with atrial flutter (AFL) based on an electrocardiogram (ECG) and has been experiencing dysrhythmic symptoms for more than 3 hours. She has been on adequate anticoagulant therapy, and her QRS is less than 0.14 seconds, as measured on a 12-lead ECG. She has not participated in any other drug studies, and she has not previously received RSD1235. She does not have any serious diseases/illnesses that could interfere with the conduct or validity of the study or compromise her safety. She has not received IV Class I or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs or IV amiodarone within 24 hours prior to dosing. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore possible treatment options for her AFL.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was admitted to the intensive care unit with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) due to pneumonia. He has no history of heart failure or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He is currently on mechanical ventilation for the past 6 hours and has been receiving oxygen therapy. The patient is alert and oriented, but he is dyspneic and complains of shortness of breath. He is able to follow simple commands and has no difficulty communicating. Laboratory results indicate severe hypoxemia with a PAFI of less than 200, and arterial blood gas analysis shows a pH of 7.25 and PaCO2 of 55 mmHg. The patient is a candidate for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been diagnosed with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in his right eye. He reports a decrease in his central vision and difficulty reading small print. His best corrected visual acuity in the right eye is 20/200 and in the left eye, it is 20/30. He does not have any other retinovascular disease or retinal degeneration. He has not had any previous posterior vitrectomy or retinal surgery, periocular infection, or intravenous or intravitreous corticosteroids. He has cataracts in both eyes, but they have not been removed. His intraocular pressure is within normal limits. His medical history includes hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which are well-controlled with medications. He is not currently taking any medication for his AMD. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his vision and quality of life.

The patient is a 55-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with metabolic syndrome. She presents with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. She reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in carbohydrates and fats. She is currently taking lisinopril for her hypertension and atorvastatin for her high cholesterol. Her family history includes a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes in her parents. She is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. Her waist circumference is 96 cm and her blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg. Her fasting plasma glucose level is 110 mg/dL and her serum triglyceride level is 170 mg/dL. Her HDL cholesterol level is 38 mg/dL. She is interested in alternative medicine and is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of Crocus sativus (Saffron) and Berberis Vulgaris (barberry fruit) in the treatment of metabolic syndrome. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is not taking insulin or glucose sensitizing medication. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or psychiatric problems and is willing to comply with the treatment and evaluation schedule.

A 10 year old boy with newly diagnosed medulloblastoma. The tumor was discovered after he experienced headaches and neck pain. MRI showed a mass in the cerebellum. He underwent surgical resection and histopathology confirmed medulloblastoma. No evidence of metastasis to the bone marrow or bones. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

A 28-year-old female presents with a history of eczema and allergic reactions to various skin products. She reports having experienced itching, redness, and rash after using certain soaps and detergents. She was previously patch tested and found to be positive to several surfactants including cocamidopropyl betaine, stearamidopropyl dimethylamine, dimethylaminopropylamine, coconut diethanolamide, oleamidopropyl dimethylamine, and decyl glucoside. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to identify positivity rates to three novel surfactants and co-reactivity with other surfactants in patients with known surfactant sensitivity. She meets the inclusion criteria of the study as she has documentation of a previous contact allergy to one or more surfactants on the screening series. She is not pregnant or lactating and has not used any systemic therapy or phototherapy within the past two weeks.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman with a BMI of 42 who is scheduled for a total knee replacement surgery. She has a history of scoliosis but has not undergone any previous spine surgery. She has consented to receive spinal anesthesia for the surgery and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. She is willing to be randomized to either the ultrasound-guided or standard technique and has been informed of the study procedures and outcomes.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who has been struggling with her weight for several years. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. She has a sedentary lifestyle and admits to eating a diet high in processed foods and sugar. She has recently been diagnosed with the metabolic syndrome, having at least 3 of the NCEP ATP-III criteria. She is motivated to make lifestyle changes to improve her health and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. She speaks English fluently and is available for regular assessments over the next 12 months. She does not have a history of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver or kidney disease, psychiatric illness, chronic substance abuse, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is in good health and does not smoke. She has a normal body weight and has not experienced any head trauma or surgeries. She does not have any cardiac pacemaker or prosthetic heart valve, nor any implanted pumps, neurostimulator, cochlear implants, metal rods, plates, screws, intrauterine device, or hearing aid. She does not have any dentures that might create NMR artifacts. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of propofol on brain waves during induction and recovery from general anesthesia. She understands that her brain waves will be measured using electroencephalogram (EEG) while she is under general anesthesia and that her brain will be imaged using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on a separate day.

56 year old woman who presents with a 5-day history of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She was seen at an urgent care center and tested positive for COVID-19. Her oxygen saturation was 94% on room air, and she was started on supplemental oxygen. The patient was admitted to the hospital and diagnosed with mild-moderate SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia confirmed microbiologically ≤7 days before randomization, and presents: basal oxygen saturation> 90%, CURB-65 ≤1, and PaO2 / FiO2≥300 or SatO2 / FiO2≥315. The patient is hospitalized and is not expected to enter the ICU or die in the next 24 hours. She has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial and has no other significant medical history or laboratory abnormalities of grade ≥ 4.

A 63-year old retired teacher has been experiencing a persistent cough for the last 2 months. She has also been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. She is a former smoker and quit smoking 10 years ago. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and osteoporosis. She lives alone and has two adult children. She enjoys gardening and reading. She has lost 5 pounds in the last month. Her physical exam revealed decreased breath sounds in the right lower lobe of the lung. Chest X-ray showed a mass in the right lung. Further imaging studies revealed a suspicious lymph node in the mediastinum. She was referred to a pulmonologist who recommended a mediastinal staging procedure to determine the extent of the disease. She is interested in participating in the study as she wants to contribute to the advancement of lung cancer management. She is mentally and physically fit to undergo diagnostic surgery. She does not have any other malignancies or respiratory insufficiency. She understands the study and is willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of tingling, numbness, and pain in his left hand and wrist. He works as a computer programmer and spends long hours typing on a keyboard. His symptoms started about 6 months ago and have progressively worsened. He has consulted with his primary care physician, who referred him to a neurologist for further evaluation. The neurologist performed an electrodiagnostic study, which revealed focal nerve disease in the left wrist. The patient is interested in participating in this study to determine if neuromuscular ultrasound can improve the diagnosis of his condition. He has no known allergies and is able to complete the 6 months of follow-up. The patient is cooperative and motivated to find a solution for his symptoms.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her first child. She has a history of gestational diabetes and has been managing it with diet and exercise. She is scheduled to undergo a cesarean section due to fetal distress. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no known allergies. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her prenatal care has been uncomplicated, and the ultrasound scans have shown a healthy fetus. She has consented to participate in a clinical trial investigating the role of a drain in reducing postoperative complications after cesarean section. She will be randomly assigned to either the drain group or the control group. The drain group will have a surgical drain placed in the incision site, while the control group will not. The aim of the study is to determine if the use of a drain can decrease the incidence of wound infection after cesarean section.

The patient is a 12-year-old HIV-positive child who has been on a stable HAART regimen for at least 16 weeks with no anticipated changes in therapy. The patient has received IAIV in at least one of the past 2 years and has a viral load of less than 60,000 copies/ml within 60 days prior to study start. The patient meets certain CD4 cell count and CD4% requirements. The parent or legal guardian has provided written informed consent, and is available to be contacted by phone. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity to any component of IAIV or FluMist, nor a history of Guillain-Barre syndrome. The patient has not received any inactivated vaccine within 14 days prior to the study vaccination, any live vaccine within 30 days prior to the study vaccination, nor has any plans to receive any vaccine within 30 days following the vaccination. The patient does not have any medical illness associated with suppression of T-cell immunity, nor is the patient pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient does not have any condition that would interfere with the study.

50-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the emergency department with chest pain of 2 hours duration. The patient reports a pressure-like sensation in the center of his chest that radiates to his left arm. He denies shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or diaphoresis. The ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads V2-V6, I and aVL. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and is planned for primary PCI. The patient is informed about the remote per-postconditioning study and provides informed consent to participate. The patient does not have a history of previous myocardial infarction, left bundle branch block, or CABG. The patient is not on any medication that may interfere with the study protocol.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was rushed to the emergency room with sudden onset of weakness on the right side of his body, slurred speech, and difficulty in understanding conversations. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. A CT scan revealed an acute ischemic stroke in the left middle cerebral artery distribution. He was admitted to the stroke unit and received thrombolysis therapy within the first hour of admission. He has since been recovering well and has no residual neurological deficits. He is interested in participating in the cytokine registry database study to help advance the understanding of stroke pathogenesis and improve management strategies for future patients.

The patient is a right-handed 28-year-old woman who has normal color vision. She does not smoke and has not been diagnosed with any sleep disorders, neurological or psychiatric disorders in the last 3 months. She has not experienced any acute severe traumas and does not have any chronic diseases that require medication. She does not use recreational drugs or regularly take any medication that would affect the outcome measures. She does not consume excessive amounts of alcohol (less than 18 standard units per week) and has not traveled across more than one time zone in the last month. She has not worked night shifts in the last month. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has a history of coronary heart disease (CHD). He presents to the clinic with a low HDL-C level of 35 mg/dL and an LDL-C level of 130 mg/dL. He is currently taking atorvastatin to manage his cholesterol levels. The patient reports a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and a diet high in processed foods and saturated fats. The patient has not experienced any recent symptoms of CHD, such as chest pain or shortness of breath. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the role of high density lipoprotein-C (HDL-C) subspecies in CHD risk. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the VA-HIT study, as he is male, has established CHD, and has a low HDL-C level.

A 42-year-old male presents with a history of frequent heartburn and regurgitation after meals. He has been taking antacids for the past 6 months with minimal relief. The patient has no significant medical history, but is a smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He has no known family history of gastrointestinal disorders. Endoscopy shows mild to moderate esophagitis and a hiatal hernia. A pH test confirms the diagnosis of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). The patient is interested in surgical intervention and is deemed eligible for the clinical trial evaluating laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication comparing division versus non-division of short gastric vessels. He does not have any history of esophageal motility disorder, hard stenosis, or previous antireflux surgery. He consents to participate in the trial and is randomized to the division of short gastric vessels group. The patient undergoes the procedure and is followed up for long-term outcome evaluation.

A 50-year-old woman presents with complaints of abdominal bloating and discomfort. She also reports difficulty eating and early satiety. She has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. A pelvic ultrasound reveals a large ovarian mass and a CT scan confirms the presence of a 10 cm ovarian tumor with no signs of metastasis. She underwent cytoreductive surgery 4 weeks ago and the pathology report confirmed stage III epithelial ovarian carcinoma. Post-surgery, she has recovered well and is now ready to start her first-line chemotherapy. Her ECOG performance status is 1 and her blood work shows ANC of 2000/µL, platelets of 150,000/µL, hemoglobin of 11.0 g/dL, total bilirubin of 1.2 x ULN, ALT and AST of 2.0 x ULN, and serum creatinine of 1.0 x ULN. She has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has agreed to use adequate contraception during the study. She is able to understand the nature of the study and has given written informed consent.

The patient is a 10-year-old child diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The child has been admitted to Rigshospitalet and is currently receiving high-dose methotrexate (HDMTX) treatment as part of their ALL treatment plan. The child's renal and hepatic function will be evaluated to determine their individualized dosing of HDMTX. The study aims to investigate the role of liver and renal function in methotrexate (MTX) pharmacokinetics and evaluate the predictive potential of pharmacogenetic and pharmacokinetic parameters of MTX elimination during HDMTX. The study will involve urine collection and modelling to predict the individual time span for complete MTX excretion and will reveal early pharmacogenetic/kinetic patterns predictive of elimination of MTX during HDMTX courses in children with ALL.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old woman who is interested in contributing to the advancement of medical research. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She has no known respiratory or cardiovascular pathology and is not claustrophobic. She understands that the study involves exposure to a magnetic field and has no counter-argument to this exposure. She is excited about the opportunity to contribute to the development of a statistical atlas of the human body and understands that her participation may involve imaging procedures such as MRI scans.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male with a body mass index (BMI) of 23 kg/m2. He has no significant medical history, specifically no history of autoimmune or cardiac disease. He does not smoke or use any regular medications. He is willing and able to complete the study and provide written informed consent. He will undergo medical examination to ensure his fitness for participation.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who had a stroke 9 months ago resulting in left-sided hemiparesis. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia and diabetes, all of which are well-controlled with medications. She is currently on aspirin and atorvastatin. She has no history of seizures or recent head trauma. Her Fugl Meyer Upper Extremity Score is between 22-38. She is able to perform some basic activities of daily living with her left hand, but has difficulty with fine motor movements and overall strength. She is motivated to participate in rehabilitation and is able to attend all scheduled sessions. Her vital signs are within normal limits and her physical exam is unremarkable except for the left-sided weakness. She has no metal implants or pacemaker.

John is a 52-year-old man who has been experiencing difficulty in achieving and maintaining an erection during sexual activity for the past 6 months. He also reports having lower urinary tract symptoms such as frequent urination, urgency, and weak urine stream for the last 8 months. He has a stable relationship with his wife who is supportive of his condition. John has a history of hypertension for the last 5 years, which is well-controlled with medications. He has never undergone any surgical procedure in the lower urinary tract. His laboratory studies were within normal limits except for a mildly elevated PSA level of 5.5 ng/ml. He is not taking any nitrates, antiandrogens, estrogens, luteninizing hormone-releasing hormone agonist/antagonist or anabolic steroids. John is willing to participate in this clinical trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia in complete remission after receiving chemotherapy. He is not a candidate for a standard allo-transplant due to his age and poor end organ performance. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a non-myeloablative hematopoietic cell transplantation with mesenchymal stem cell infusion as prevention for graft rejection and graft-versus-host disease. The patient has a related donor (his sister) who has one allelic mismatch at HLA-B and one allelic mismatch at HLA-DRB1. The donor is willing to undergo leukapheresis to donate peripheral blood stem cells. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and has given informed consent to participate.

33-year-old female who recently gave birth to her first child and is currently breastfeeding. She has been a smoker for the past 10 years and has attempted to quit several times in the past but has been unsuccessful. She is motivated to quit smoking for the health of her baby and herself. She has access to a high-speed internet connection and is comfortable with using technology. She is able to read and speak English fluently. She is currently not taking any medications and has no significant medical history. She is willing to participate in an online smoking cessation program with digital coaching support.

Patient is a 55-year-old male from the United States who presents to his primary care physician with complaints of chest discomfort and shortness of breath with exertion. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He is a former smoker and quit 5 years ago. His BMI is 28, BP: 140/90, HR: 85/min. His ECG shows normal sinus rhythm with no ST-T wave changes. His troponin levels are within normal limits. He has not undergone any cardiac testing in the past year. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the best diagnostic strategy for his suspected coronary artery disease.

Patient is a 45-year-old male who underwent bariatric surgery for obesity management 3 months ago. His BMI prior to surgery was 42. He has been cleared by his physician to engage in physical exercise and has no immediate postoperative complications. He has no plans to change his place of residence within the current year. The patient is interested in participating in a study that will help him improve his body composition, cardiopulmonary function, and quality of life after surgery. He is willing to commit to a supervised physical exercise program and follow a prescribed nutritional diet plan.

35F with a history of psoriasis vulgaris on the trunk and extremities. The patient reports occasional itching and scaling of the skin, but no joint pain or other systemic symptoms. The patient has not been previously treated with Daivobet® Gel and has not undergone systemic therapy for psoriasis vulgaris. The patient is not currently using any other topical treatments for psoriasis.
