The patient is willing to use Daivobet® Gel as prescribed by the physician and is able to comply with the study requirements. The patient does not have any contraindications to Daivobet® Gel as listed in the German package insert.

A 28-year-old male presented to the clinic with a history of flu-like symptoms, including fever, sore throat, and muscle aches. He reported unprotected sexual intercourse with a new partner about a month ago. His medical history was unremarkable, and he denied any history of drug or alcohol abuse. His vital signs were stable in the primary evaluation. Physical examination was significant for mild cervical lymphadenopathy. HIV-1 RNA test was ordered, and the result revealed a high viral load of 1,700,000 copies/mL. Confirmatory Western blot assay was positive. He was diagnosed with acute HIV infection and referred to the study. He was able and willing to give informed consent and comply with the time requirements for study visits and evaluations. He had no evidence of an active AIDS-defining opportunistic infection and no contraindication to cART. He was randomly assigned to the cART plus autologous HIV-1 CTL infusion arm of Cohort 1

The patient is a 26-year-old healthy woman with a BMI of 23. She has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medication that could impact her postprandial glucose and insulin response. She has no food allergies or intolerances and is not undergoing any dietary or exercise-mediated weight loss program. She does not follow a ketogenic diet nor does she take regular ketone products such as MCT, ketone esters or ketone salts. Her alcohol intake is limited to one serving per week. She is a non-smoker and is willing to participate in a research project aimed at identifying the MCT formulation matrixes that provide the highest ketoindex values and extended half-life. She has read and understood the informed consent and is willing to sign it prior to study entry.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate adenocarcinoma, which has progressed despite orchiectomy or LHRH agonist therapy. He has a history of stable analgesia for the past 7 days, indicating that his pain is well-controlled. The patient has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80, indicating that he is able to carry out most activities of daily living with only slight limitations. He has not received prior treatment with cytotoxic agents, except for estramustine. The patient's cardiac function is normal, as confirmed by a left ventricular ejection fraction test. He has adequate organ function with neutrophils > 1.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin > 10 g/dl, and platelets > 100 x 10^9/L. The patient's liver function is within normal limits, with total bilirubin < the upper-normal limit of the institution and Alanine aminotransferase and Aspartate transaminase < 1.5 times the upper-normal limit of the institution. His renal function is also normal, with creatinine < 1.5 times the upper normal limit. The patient has no brain or leptomeningeal metastases. He has not received prior radiotherapy to >25% of bone marrow, prior cytotoxic chemotherapy (except monotherapy with estramustine), or prior isotope therapy. The patient does not have symptomatic peripheral neuropathy grade ≥ 2 or other serious illness or medical condition, such as congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, uncontrolled arrhythmias, active uncontrolled infection, peptic ulcer, unstable diabetes mellitus, or autoimmune disease. The patient has not received any other anti-cancer therapy or bisphosphonates.

The patient is a 45-year-old Chinese woman who was diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) five years ago. She has a known BRCA1 mutation and has undergone multiple rounds of platinum-based chemotherapy. However, she has developed resistance to the treatment and her cancer has continued to progress. The patient has provided consent to participate in a study aimed at creating a LOH-HRD model for EOC patients. She will be required to provide tumor tissue samples for genetic testing. The study aims to understand the genetic basis of platinum-resistance in Chinese EOC patients and provide a potential explanation for their prognosis. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria for the trial.

A 55-year-old Asian woman was recently diagnosed with advanced biliary tract cancer. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, and fatigue for the past few months. The diagnosis was confirmed through imaging tests which showed the presence of a large mass in the bile ducts. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her cancer. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to perform all activities of daily living with minimal difficulty. She has not received any prior treatment with taxane therapy and has no known hypersensitivity to trial treatments or their excipients. However, she has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to manage it. She has not received any radiation therapy for her cancer.

This is a 53-year-old woman who has been postmenopausal for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms of vulvar and vaginal atrophy, including vaginal dryness, vaginal and vulvar irritation/itching, and dysuria, which have been bothersome to her. She has also experienced vaginal pain associated with sexual activity and occasional vaginal bleeding during intercourse. She has been diagnosed with <5% superficial cells on vaginal smear cytology and vaginal pH >5.0 at her recent visit, which is indicative of vulvar and vaginal atrophy. Her systolic blood pressure is <150mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure is <90mm Hg. She has no known hypersensitivity to Estradiol vaginal tablets and has not had any abnormal screening mammogram or clinical breast examination results indicating any suspicion of breast malignancy. She has not had any history of undiagnosed vaginal bleeding or significant risk factors for endometrial cancer. Her screening vaginal ultrasonography shows endometrial thickness of <4 mm. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the therapeutic equivalence and safety of Estradiol Vaginal Tablets 10 mcg and Vagifem® (Estradiol Vaginal Tablets) 10 mcg in female subjects with moderate to severe symptoms of vulvar and vaginal atrophy associated with menopause.

A 52-year-old Korean male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the efficacy of low-dose rosuvastatin. He has been on atorvastatin 20mg for the past 6 months with a moderate reduction in his LDL cholesterol levels. His LDL cholesterol level at the last visit was 130 mg/dL. He has never experienced any significant side effects from his medications. He is compliant with his medications and has never missed a dose. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father having a heart attack at the age of 60. He is interested in participating in this trial to potentially reduce his risk of developing cardiovascular disease in the future. He does not smoke or consume alcohol. He is married and has two children. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and attend all required visits.

John is a 65 year old man who has been dealing with peripheral vascular disease for several years. He has been experiencing significant pain in his lower leg and foot due to the lack of blood flow. After consultation with his physician, he has decided to undergo elective below knee amputation to improve his quality of life. John is an ASA physical status II patient and meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial. He is willing to participate in the study to receive either sciatic nerve block using a popliteal approach or a sub gluteal approach. Despite being nervous about the surgery, John is excited about the possibility of experiencing less pain and a quicker recovery with the use of the nerve block. He has no allergies to local anaesthetics and does not have any contraindications to regional anaesthesia.

The patient is a 29-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). She has been experiencing irregular menstrual cycles, weight gain, and excessive hair growth on her face and body. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her symptoms. She is not pregnant and is not taking any medication that alters her hormonal or biochemical profile. She is willing to take the study medication as prescribed and is able to give informed consent.

42 y/o female diagnosed with COVID-19 pneumonia who has been hospitalized for 5 days. She is currently on low flow oxygen therapy with oxygen saturation ranging from 88-92%. She has a history of hypertension and asthma, and is currently taking lisinopril and albuterol as needed. The patient has no known allergies to plasma products or immunoglobulin, and has not received any such treatment in the past 4 weeks. She is willing to sign the informed consent form and is within 10 days of symptom onset. The patient has not undergone any major surgeries in the past 4 weeks and does not have any history of lung transplantation. Her creatinine level is normal and her estimated glomerular filtration rate is above 60 mL/min. There is no evidence of cardiovascular instability or history of thrombo-embolic events. The patient does not have any other severe chronic background diseases. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and has not participated in any other pharmaceutical interventional clinical study within the last 4 weeks.

The patient is a 55 year old man who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant two years ago for acute myeloid leukemia. He has been off systemic immunosuppressive medication for 4 months and has been diagnosed with advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. The cancer has spread to other parts of his body and he has at least one measurable lesion of greater than or equal to 1 cm. He has no history of autoimmune disease or significant intercurrent illness. He has been previously treated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy, but the toxicities have resolved to NCI CTCAE grade 1. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and his laboratory values are within the required limits. He is willing to provide blood and tissue samples for diagnostic biopsies. He has given his informed consent to be a part of the study.

A 52-year-old male with a history of chronic tinnitus for the past 2 years. The tinnitus is a constant ringing in his left ear that is disruptive to his daily life activities. He has tried various conventional measures such as hearing aids and masking but to no avail. The patient reports a severe THI score of 70/100 and a TFI score of 64/100. The tinnitus VAS score is 70/100. The patient has normal to moderate SNHL with a PTA of 0.5, 1 and 2 kHz and a WRS of 80%. The patient has never had any major ear surgery or head trauma. The patient has no history of depression or anxiety. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to seek an alternative solution for his chronic tinnitus.

The patient is a 24-year-old woman who has been experiencing frequent headaches, eye strain, and blurry vision for the past few months. She spends a lot of time on her smartphone, scrolling through social media and reading articles. She has no history of anterior segment diseases or intraocular surgeries. Her prescription glasses are up to date, and she has no history of tropia. The patient is not currently taking any medication that could induce spasm of accommodation. Her vision is 20/20 in both eyes, and she has no history of hypermetropia. The patient is interested in participating in the study to determine if her smartphone use is causing any damage to her eyes.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who sustained a closed head injury due to a fall from a ladder while cleaning her gutters. She was unconscious for several hours and was admitted to the hospital with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 10. Imaging studies revealed a subdural hematoma, and she underwent surgical evacuation of the hematoma. She also suffered multiple fractures of her ribs and a pneumothorax. She was admitted to the intensive care unit, where she was intubated and mechanically ventilated for several days. She was eventually weaned from the ventilator and transferred to the general medical floor. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes lisinopril. She has no significant past medical history and takes no other medications. She has a normal menstrual cycle and is not pregnant or nursing. She has no history of severe mental impairment and does not require a legal guardian. Her hemoglobin level is normal. Her body mass index is 24.5. She has not donated blood during the past month. She is interested in participating in the study and provides her informed consent.

Patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of persistent bronchial asthma. He has not changed his asthma treatment within the last four weeks and is a non-smoker. He has not had any lower airway infection in the last four weeks and does not have a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or any other relevant lung disease. He uses short-acting bronchodilators (beta-agonists) less than 8 puffs per day, on average less than 3 days per week. The patient has normal laboratory values and does not have severe renal insufficiency, active hepatitis, or an HIV infection. He has no history of cancer, chronic heart failure, or any known hypersensitivity or contraindication to roflumilast or albuterol/salbutamol. The patient is not a female of childbearing potential, pregnant or breastfeeding. He has not received any investigational medication or device in the month prior to visit 1 and has no plans to receive another investigational medication during the study.

A 44-year-old woman with limited English proficiency (LEP) has been admitted to MSKCC for surgery due to a diagnosis of colorectal cancer. Her primary language is Russian. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time, and is expected to have at least a two-day hospital stay. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the use of dual-handset interpreter phones to improve communication with LEP patients. Her physician and nurse have also agreed to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with cataracts in his left eye. He has no history of eye surgeries or corneal lesions. He is generally healthy and takes medication for hypertension. He is able to maintain stable fixation during vision tests and has no active inflammation or infection in his eyes. His tear film break up time is greater than 5 seconds. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve the accuracy of his cataract surgery. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 55-year-old African American man from Miami, Florida was recently diagnosed with prostate cancer. His biopsy confirmed primary prostate cancer and he was diagnosed in October 2014. He is currently undergoing treatment with radiation therapy and hormone therapy. He has a family history of prostate cancer; his father was diagnosed with prostate cancer at the age of 70. He has a history of smoking, having smoked half a pack of cigarettes per day for 20 years before quitting 10 years ago. He has a high school education and works as a construction worker. He is interested in participating in the study in order to contribute to the research on prostate cancer among African American men and to better understand the relationship between smoking and prostate cancer. He is willing to participate in all components of the study, including completing questionnaires, providing a saliva sample, and providing tumor tissue.

The patient is a 30-year-old female who has been experiencing recurrent infections and has been feeling generally unwell for the past year. She has visited multiple doctors and has been prescribed antibiotics several times, but her symptoms persist. Upon further testing, it is discovered that her absolute CD4+ T cell count is consistently below 300 cells/microL, and she is diagnosed with idiopathic CD4+ lymphocytopenia (ICL). She has tested negative for HIV and does not have any known immunodeficiency syndromes. She is willing to participate in a long-term study aimed at understanding the natural history of ICL and identifying potential underlying genetic and immunologic causes of the condition. The study will involve regular blood and tissue sample collections, as well as consultations with specialists in rheumatology, pulmonology, ophthalmology, and imaging studies. She will receive the best standard therapy for any opportunistic infections that may arise during the study. Additionally, her blood relatives and household contacts may also be eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45 year old Hispanic male who presented with redness, irritation and blurred vision in his left eye. He works as a construction worker and spends a lot of time outdoors. Upon examination, the ophthalmologist diagnosed him with primary pterygium which has been gradually progressing over the past year. The patient has no significant medical history and is in good health. He is willing and able to attend follow-up visits.

A 30-year-old male diagnosed with keratoconus a year ago. The patient has experienced progressive changes in corneal curvature over the past 12 months, with an increase of at least 1.0 diopter in the steepest keratometry value. The patient's preoperative corneal thickness is 400 microns, which qualifies him for the study. The patient has no history of herpes simplex keratitis, corneal melt, perforated corneal ulcer, descemetocele, prior corneal damage from chemical injury, herpes zoster keratitis, nystagmus, corneal scarring that significantly impairs vision, pre-existing glaucoma, glaucoma suspect, Goldmann applanation pressure exceeding 23 mm Hg, cataract, history of uveitis, or active ocular disease that might lead to infection. The patient is willing to discontinue wear of rigid contact lenses in the eye to be operated on for at least one month before baseline examination, and for the first six months post-operatively. The patient is not pregnant and has no known hypersensitivity to riboflavin. The patient's central corneal endothelial cell count is above 1400 cells per square millimeter, and there is no evidence of past or present herpes simplex of the cornea.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was diagnosed with metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma 6 months ago. He has not received any anticancer treatment except for local radiotherapy to the bone metastasis. He has one measurable metastatic lesion and his ECOG performance status is 1. He has no history of peripheral nerve disease and is willing to comply with the test requirements and regular follow-up. He has no other serious diseases except for a history of basal cell carcinoma that was cured 2 years ago. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. His electrocardiogram shows no abnormalities. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of allergies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally.

72-year-old woman with a history of depression and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is being evaluated for participation in a clinical trial. She has a caregiver who has regular contact with her and is available to facilitate the delivery of the study intervention. The patient is currently taking sertraline for depression and has been on a stable dose for at least 4 weeks prior to study entry. She reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty with word recall. Her Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 25/30. She speaks English fluently and has corrected vision and hearing. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent. She has no significant neurological conditions or metal implants that would preclude safe use of tDCS.

A 35-year-old woman with a history of episodic migraines for more than 5 years is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her symptoms. Her migraines occur without aura and last for at least 4 hours. She experiences moderate to severe pain, as well as nausea and photophobia. On average, she experiences 6 migraines per month and has no more than 10 headache days per month. She has previously tried various treatments, including over-the-counter pain relievers, but has not found them effective. She is not currently taking any medication for her migraines. She is married and has two children. She is not pregnant and is using contraception. She has no history of cancer, psychiatric illness, or drug or alcohol abuse. She is in good general health and is able to use electronic devices, including the eDiary and demo study drug patch. She has no known allergies or sensitivities to zolmitriptan or adhesives. She is willing to comply with study requirements and complete evaluations required for the study.

56-year-old male with a history of smoking, diagnosed with metastatic NSCLC after progressing through first-line chemotherapy. He is currently on second-line treatment but experiencing disease progression with worsening symptoms such as shortness of breath and cough. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and one measurable lesion as defined by RECIST version 1.1. The patient has adequate bone marrow, renal, and liver function, with no known allergies or hypersensitivity to medications. The patient has not had any major surgery or radiation therapy within the last 4 weeks and has no current active infections, including COVID-19. The patient is willing and able to consume and absorb study drug.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer 3 years ago. She underwent surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy and has been taking hormone therapy for the last 2 years. She reports feeling fatigued, having decreased cardiovascular fitness and muscle strength, and experiencing pain in her upper extremities. She has gained weight since her diagnosis and feels that her quality of life has decreased. She is currently not exercising regularly but is motivated to start a program that could help her feel better. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medication that may alter exercise response. She has a supportive family and is willing to commit to a supervised exercise program.

50 year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who presents for a screening colonoscopy. He reports no gastrointestinal symptoms or family history of colorectal cancer. He has never had a colonoscopy before. Bowel preparation was adequate, and caecal intubation was accomplished. During the procedure, a small polyp measuring 6mm in diameter was detected in the sigmoid colon. The polyp was resected using the "resect and discard strategy" without pathological examination. The patient experienced no complications during or after the procedure.

A 6-year-old boy named Jack, who lives with his parents in a suburban area, has a history of asthma since he was 3 years old. He experiences wheezing, coughing, and difficulty breathing during an asthma attack. His medication includes a short-acting bronchodilator, which he takes through an inhaler during an asthma attack. Jack's parents have been instructed on how to manage his asthma and have a spacer to use with his inhaler. At home, Jack's parents have noticed that his asthma attack usually occurs at night or early in the morning, and he has trouble sleeping because of his symptoms. They have been managing his asthma at home with the use of his inhaler and a nebulizer machine, which they have on hand in case of an emergency. His parents have never taken him to the emergency room for an asthma attack, but they are concerned about the possibility of needing to do so in the future.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who recently underwent a radical mastectomy for a histologically confirmed breast cancer. The tumor was found to be biologically aggressive, with a high thymidine-labeling index, poorly differentiated (grade III), and high S-phase fraction. The patient had at least 10 lymph nodes removed, and the histology of the tumor was node-positive (1-3). The estrogen receptor status is unknown. The patient has not had any prior breast cancer or other cancers except for carcinoma in situ of the cervix or basal cell skin cancer treated with radical intent. The patient has no significant alterations in cardiovascular function and no serious psychiatric disorders. The patient's WBC is ≥ 3,500/mL, ANC is ≥ 1,500/mL, platelet count is ≥ 120,000/mL, AST and ALT are ≤ 1.5 times upper limit of normal (ULN), creatinine is ≤ 1.5 mg/mL, and bilirubin is ≤ 1.5 times ULN. The patient is geographically accessible for follow-up.

I apologize, but it seems that there has been a misunderstanding. As a clinical trial specialist, I typically work with clinical trials that involve human participants. However, the trial you have described does not involve patients or human subjects. Instead, it involves undergraduate nursing students who will be randomly assigned to either an experimental group or a control group. The patient is a 23-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with anorexia nervosa. She has a BMI of 16.5 kg/m2 and has been experiencing symptoms for the past 8 months. She reports feeling constantly hungry but has lost her appetite and struggles to eat. She has no history of immune system or metabolic diseases and has not been on any antibiotics in the past 2 months. She is not currently on any psychotropic medication and does not have diarrhea. She is interested in participating in the study and has given informed consent.

A 27 year old French-speaking woman is referred to the clinic by her psychiatrist who diagnoses her with schizophrenia. The patient has been experiencing difficulties with memory, attention, and executive functioning which have been affecting her daily life. She also struggles with social interactions, and has trouble communicating with others. She has been on antipsychotic medication for the past year, but has not seen significant improvement in her cognitive abilities. She has no history of neurological illness or trauma, and does not have any visual or auditory disorders. She is not dependent on drugs or alcohol and does not have any mental retardation. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help improve her cognitive abilities and overall quality of life.

Patient A is a 65-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. She has been experiencing memory loss, difficulty with language, disorientation, and has difficulty performing daily activities. She has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. She has no history of peptic ulcer disease, liver disease, or inflammatory diseases. She has completed at least 6 years of education. She is fluent in English and has a caregiver who can accompany her to all scheduled visits. She is able to ingest oral medication. Her MMSE score is 18 at the screening visit. She has had a CT scan since onset of memory impairment which did not show any clinically significant focal lesion.  She is not taking any NSAIDs or aspirin for any other conditions.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was diagnosed with epilepsy at the age of 15. He has been taking antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) for the past 13 years, but his seizures are still not well controlled. He has been experiencing complex partial seizures, which are characterized by a loss of awareness, staring, and repetitive movements. He also experiences occasional generalized tonic-clonic seizures, which cause him to fall to the ground and shake. His seizures occur about once a week and have a significant impact on his quality of life. He has undergone previous EEG monitoring, MRI, and PET scans to try and locate the source of his seizures, but the results were inconclusive. He is now being considered for epilepsy surgery and has been admitted to the Epilepsy Monitoring Unit for presurgical evaluation. He is eligible to participate in the PROMAESIS study as he meets the inclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C presents with elevated liver enzymes and fatigue. He was previously treated with interferon alfa/ribavirin combination therapy for 6 months, but did not respond to treatment. He has detectable serum HCV-RNA and liver biopsy findings consistent with active fibrosis. His liver disease is compensated (Child-Pugh Grade A clinical classification) but he does have a history of moderate alcohol consumption. He has no history of severe psychiatric disease, seizures, immunologically mediated disease, chronic pulmonary disease, severe allergies, or major organ transplantation. He has no evidence of severe retinopathy or drug abuse. He has not received any systemic anti-viral, anti-neoplastic or immunomodulatory treatment within the past 3 months, and has not received any investigational drug within the past 6 weeks. He is willing to use two forms of effective contraception during treatment and for 6 months after end of treatment, as he is fertile. He is negative for HBsAg and anti-HIV Ab. His Hb is 8.9 mmol/l and his neutrophil count is 1700 cells/mm3. He is able to read and understand English, and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

A 42-year-old male, who has been diagnosed with a left inguinal hernia by his primary care physician. The patient reports a history of hypertension controlled with medication, and occasional episodes of heart palpitations. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is generally in good health with no other significant medical history. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine the minimum effective dose for intrathecal chloroprocaine in inguinal herniorrhaphy using a Combined Spinal Epidural (CSE) anesthesia.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for the past 4 years. He has been taking levodopa and a dopamine agonist for his motor symptoms, but he still experiences occasional "OFF" periods. He has also been diagnosed with depression and has been taking an antidepressant for the past 6 months, but he still has a HAM-D score of 16. He reports feeling sad most of the time, has lost interest in activities he used to enjoy, and has trouble sleeping. He has no history of seizures or loss of consciousness. He has not had any exposure to repetitive TMS in the past. He does not have any intracranial metallic bodies or signs of increased intracranial pressure. He has no implanted pacemaker, medication pump, vagal stimulator, deep brain stimulator, TENS unit, or ventriculoperitoneal shunt. He has no history of substance abuse or known structural brain abnormalities. He does not have bipolar affective disorder or psychotic features. He does not have dementia, as evidenced by a score of 28 on the screening MMSE. He meets the criteria for a depressive disorder based on the MINI interview. He is 62 years old and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a BMI of 32 kg/m^2. He has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it for the past 2 years. His recent blood work revealed fasting plasma triglycerides of 2.2 mmol/L, HDL cholesterol of 0.9 mmol/L, and fasting plasma glucose of 6.5 mmol/L. His waist circumference measures 105 cm, and his blood pressure is consistently above 140/90 mmHg. He has never been diagnosed with diabetes, renal, liver, or thyroid disease. He is not on any lipid-modifying drugs, antihypertensive medication, corticosteroid therapy, or hormone replacement therapy. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand and treat his metabolic syndrome.

A 25-year-old male presents with a history of type 1 diabetes for 5 years. He has been using insulin therapy since his diagnosis and has been on the same type of short-acting insulin (Humalog U-100) for the past 6 months. He has been using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) for the past 3 months and has a total CGM use of at least 2 months in the prior 6 months. He has been treated with long-acting insulin degludec U-100 for the past 6 months. He has no history of emergency room visits or hospitalizations due to poor glucose control within the past 6 months, nor has he experienced severe hypoglycemia within the last 90 days. He is not taking any diabetes medications that are not allowed for study participation. He has an HbA1c of 7.5%, and his most recent CGM data shows time in range of 60%. He is currently employed and lives an active lifestyle.

The patient is a 3-year-old Japanese boy who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate Atopic Dermatitis at the age of 2 years old. He has been using topical corticosteroids and emollients to manage his symptoms but has experienced some adverse effects. He has not participated in any clinical trials before. The boy has no other medical or psychiatric conditions and is generally in good health. His parents are willing to participate in the study and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 34-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with peripheral T-cell lymphoma. He has not received any anti-tumor therapy and is in Ann Arbor disease stage III. His ECOG performance status is 1 and he has no bone marrow involvement. His absolute number of neutrophils is 2.5 * 10^9/L, platelet count is 120 * 10^9/L, and concentration of hemoglobin is 115 g/L. He has no central nervous system or meninges involvement. He has not undergone organ transplantation and has no history of thromboembolic disease or hematencephalon. He has clinically normal gastrointestinal function and no active infections. His hepatic function and renal function are within normal range. He has no other malignancies and is not pregnant or lactating.

A 58-year-old woman is diagnosed with indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma after experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and a persistent cough. She has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. Her diagnostic workup includes a CT scan, which reveals multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, chest, and abdomen. Biopsy of a cervical lymph node confirms the diagnosis of CD20-positive indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as a newly diagnosed patient with CD20-positive B-NHL. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no significant comorbidities. The patient agrees to participate in the trial and is fully informed of the risks and benefits of the treatment. She will receive 6 courses of Pentostatin (4mg/m² on day 1), Cyclophosphamide (600mg/m² on day 1), and Rituximab (375mg/m² on day 0) administered every three weeks. If she achieves complete or partial remission, she will undergo maintenance therapy consisting of 8 courses of Rituximab (375mg/m²) administered every three months over a period of 2 years. The patient will be monitored closely for any adverse effects and will receive regular follow-up care.

A 33-year-old woman has experienced two consecutive miscarriages in the past year. She and her husband have been trying to conceive for 3 years without success. She has regular menstrual cycles and no history of hormone medication or poison contact. Her uterine and adnexal ultrasound is normal, and she has tested negative for TORCH, chlamydia, and mycoplasma. She has no blood type incompatibility with her partner and normal blood chromosome analysis. She has no history of hydrosalpinx, endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome, adenomyosis, or uterine leiomyomata. She has not been diagnosed with thyroid dysfunction or elevated CA125 levels. She is willing to comply with the study procedures and is a suitable candidate for the study.

A 50-year-old male presented to the urology clinic with a history of elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels during a routine check-up. The patient underwent a prostate biopsy, which confirmed the presence of prostate cancer. Clinical staging indicated that the cancer was localized and had not spread beyond the prostate. The patient was scheduled for a radical prostatectomy and was offered participation in a clinical trial comparing no treatment to exisulind therapy. The patient was informed that if enrolled in the treatment arm, he would begin taking 375 mg of exisulind by mouth daily for the 4 weeks prior to the scheduled date of his surgery. The patient was also informed that he would be followed for a total of 2 months from the time of starting the study drug. The patient met the eligibility criteria for the trial as he was over 40 years of age, had prostate cancer, and was scheduled to undergo surgical removal of the prostate at Mayo Clinic. The patient expressed interest in participating in the trial and provided written informed consent.

A 54-year-old Caucasian female presents with abnormal uterine bleeding and pelvic pain for the past few months. She reports having regular menstrual cycles until 6 months ago when she started experiencing heavy bleeding and pelvic discomfort. She has no significant past medical or surgical history. Family history is negative for gynecological cancers. A transvaginal ultrasound showed thickened endometrial lining, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of endometrial carcinoma. The tumor is classified as high grade based on histological analysis. Immunohistochemistry analysis showed positive staining for PD-1/PDL-1 expression. The patient is interested in participating in clinical trials exploring the use of immunotherapy for her cancer.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who works as a hairdresser. She complains of chronic shoulder pain that has been bothering her for the last 6 months. She reports difficulty sleeping on her right side and performing overhead activities at work. She has tried physical therapy and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) but with no significant improvement. On physical examination, she shows tenderness over the supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons, positive impingement signs, and weakness on external rotation. MRI shows a partial-thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon measuring approximately 30%. She has no history of previous shoulder surgeries or corticosteroid injections in the last 6 months. She is not pregnant and has no history of rheumatoid arthritis, infections, or clotting disorders. She is willing to participate in the study and forgo any other concomitant conservative treatment modality including NSAIDs.

The patient is a 32-year-old mother of a 14-month-old boy who was recently diagnosed with developmental disabilities. She comes from a low-income family and lives with her partner and child in a small apartment in South Carolina. She is a stay-at-home mom and has no prior experience with child-rearing. She is struggling with managing her son's developmental needs and is feeling overwhelmed and anxious. She is interested in participating in this study to learn more about positive parenting techniques and to strengthen her parenting skills. She is an English speaker and is willing to allow in-home services. She is willing to commit to the duration of the study and is looking forward to receiving additional support to help her child's development.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who suffered a spinal cord injury resulting in partial tetraplegia. The injury occurred 9 months ago and affected the C7 level of the spinal cord. The patient has impaired sensory-motor response and mobility due to the injury. He does not have any cognitive impairment. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) for the treatment of spinal cord injuries. He is willing to undergo 12 sessions of LLLT over a period of four weeks and is in compliance with the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the trial.

60 year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation and deep vein thrombosis (DVT) presents to the clinic for a follow-up visit. He has been on oral anticoagulation therapy with warfarin for the past year and has been compliant with his medication regimen. He reports no history of bleeding complications or adverse effects from his medication. He lives in Bergen municipality and has expressed interest in participating in a study on self-management of anticoagulation treatment. His general practitioner has deemed him qualified for the study and he is motivated to follow the training program. He has no history of drug abuse or liver disease. He will be enrolled in the study after meeting all inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 34-year-old female who has been experiencing severe back pain and radiating leg pain for the past 2 months. She has tried multiple conservative treatments such as physical therapy, chiropractic care, and over-the-counter pain medications, but these have not provided any relief. She has been diagnosed with lumbar disc herniation and is scheduled to undergo her first transforaminal epidural steroid injection (TFESI). The patient has a history of depression and anxiety, for which she is currently being treated with medication and therapy. She is able to read and understand written information and has given her consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant and does not have any known coagulation disorders.

John is a 28-year-old man with a learning disability. He lives in a residential care home and enjoys spending time with his friends and playing video games. John has a history of falling due to problems with his balance and gait. He has fallen twice in the past year, both times resulting in minor injuries. John's physiotherapist has identified that he would benefit from wearing a lycra splinting garment to improve his posture, movement, and function. John is excited to participate in the trial and hopes that the lycra splinting garment will help him prevent future falls. He has the capacity to consent and understands the purpose of the trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old female with a history of chronic kidney disease (CKD) for the past 3 years. Her recent lab results show a serum phosphorus level of 4.9 mg/dL, which is higher than the recommended K/DOQI range for pre-dialysis CKD patients. Her glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is 24 mL/min/1.73m². She has been on a low-phosphorus diet and taking calcium supplements for the past year, but her serum phosphorus level remains elevated. She has not undergone renal transplant or received dialysis. She is currently not taking any other medications or participating in any other clinical trials. She is interested in participating in this study to help control her serum phosphorus levels and potentially improve her kidney function. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the protocol procedures and schedule.

A 43-year-old man was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1 infection three years ago. He was treated with a direct acting antiviral regimen but unfortunately did not achieve sustained viral response. His most recent HCV RNA level was 5.5 log IU/mL. He has no history of cirrhosis or hepatic decompensation. His current medications include amlodipine for hypertension and simvastatin for hyperlipidemia. His physical exam and lab studies were performed yesterday and showed the results below: A well-nourished man, non-icteric, cooperative and alert Weight: 80 kg Height: 178 BP: 130/80 HR: 84/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 14.5 g/dl WBC: 6200 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 3500/mm3) Plt: 180000 /ml AST: 45 U/L ALT: 50 U/L Alk P: 70 U/L Bilirubin total: 0.8 mg/dl HCV RNA: 5.5 log IU/mL

45-year-old female with a family history of breast cancer presented to the breast clinic for a routine mammography. The mammogram showed dense breast tissue, which makes it difficult to detect any abnormal growth. Therefore, the physician recommended a breast biopsy to further evaluate the breast tissue. The patient agreed to participate in this clinical trial and was informed about the potential benefits and risks of contrast-enhanced spectral mammography (CESM) versus breast MRI for cancer screening. She met the eligibility criteria for the study and was scheduled for both CESM and breast MRI before her biopsy. The patient has no known allergy to contrast media, nor does she have any underlying medical conditions that would make her more susceptible to a contrast reaction. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no metal implants that would make MRI contraindicated. Her BMI is within the normal range, and she does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no current illnesses or symptoms. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the importance of early detection for breast cancer.

52-year-old female with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented with complaints of abdominal pain and weight loss. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the pancreas with involvement of surrounding structures. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The patient was seen by the multidisciplinary team in a participating center prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. The patient underwent treatment with chemotherapy and radiation therapy. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the patient experienced a delay in her follow-up appointments and a delay in her chemotherapy due to the reorganization of the healthcare system. The patient was also concerned about the potential risk of contracting COVID-19 while receiving treatment. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the impact of the reorganization of the healthcare system on her pancreatic adenocarcinoma management.

The patient is a 50 year old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 2 years, for which metformin has been prescribed at a dose of 1.5 g/day. She has been experiencing difficulty in controlling her blood glucose levels despite adhering to her medication regimen and dietary restrictions. Her recent HbA1c level was 9%, which is above the target range. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the efficacy and safety of a fixed combination of insulin glargine and lixisenatide versus insulin glargine alone on top of metformin. She has no history of pancreatitis, heart failure, myocardial infarction or stroke. Her BMI is 30 kg/m^2. She is not pregnant, lactating or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no personal or immediate family history of medullary thyroid cancer, and her alanine transferase levels are within the normal range. She has not received lixisenatide before.

54 year old woman admitted to the ICU with sepsis and in need of a central venous catheter for expected duration of more than 48 hours. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise generally healthy. She has no known allergies to chlorhexidine or any other antiseptics. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 28-week pregnant woman is admitted to the hospital due to premature labor. She is diagnosed with placenta previa and requires an emergency C-section. The baby is born at 26 weeks gestational age with a birth weight of 750 grams. The baby is immediately admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and requires mechanical ventilation and total parenteral nutrition. The baby is eligible for this clinical trial as it requires glutamine supplementation to reduce the risk of death or late-onset sepsis. The parents have provided consent for their baby to participate in the trial.

A 55 year old woman has been experiencing severe pain in her ankle and subtalar joints for the past year. The pain has been constant and has not improved with non-operative management. She has tried physical therapy, pain medication, and cortisone injections but none of these have provided any relief. She is otherwise healthy and has no history of any significant medical conditions. She is able to understand the requirements of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol. The patient is fluent in English and has no visual or reading impairment. She is not a prisoner.

The patient is a 6 year old boy with a history of developmental delay and recurrent ear infections. He was recently diagnosed with mucopolysaccharidosis VII (MPS VII) based on laboratory diagnosis, specifically enzymatic analysis. He is currently being treated with enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) with vestronidase alfa. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. He is attending a special school for children with disabilities and has a full-time caregiver at home. The patient is non-verbal and has difficulty with mobility, requiring assistance with daily activities such as dressing, grooming, and eating. He has a history of hypersensitivity reactions to some medications and has a known allergy to penicillin. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications. The patient and his family are willing and able to participate in the MPS VII Disease Monitoring Program, and have provided written informed consent. They are committed to complying with the DMP visit schedule and providing all necessary information.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing chest pain for the past year. She has already undergone evaluation by a cardiologist and no cardiac cause for the chest pain has been identified. She has been prescribed analgesics and proton-pump inhibitors but has not experienced significant relief from her symptoms. She is interested in exploring other treatment options and has heard about mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) as a potential treatment for chest pain. She is willing to participate in the feasibility randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of MBCT in treating non-cardiac chest pain. She is able to understand and communicate in English and is willing and able to commit to an 8-week mindfulness course and required home practice. She has no active psychiatric conditions or ongoing psychological therapy.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of primary myelofibrosis (PMF) diagnosed 2 years ago. She was initially treated with ruxolitinib for 12 consecutive weeks and experienced treatment interruption due to loss of response. Her JAK2 mutational status is unknown. She has a peripheral blast count of <10% and requires therapy for MF. The patient adhered to the screening phase assessments and underwent a ruxolitinib-free washout period of 2 weeks. Her ECOG performance status is 1. Her bone marrow function is adequate. She provides written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has not undergone spleen radiation or splenectomy and is not currently scheduled for bone marrow transplant. She discontinued ruxolitinib 14 days prior to screening. She is able to receive a starting dose of ruxolitinib of at least 15 mg total daily dose. She has no history of leukemic transformation or clinically significant cardiac disease. She currently has no active bacterial, fungal, parasitic, or viral infections that require therapy.

A 25-year-old individual diagnosed with gender identity disorder (ICD-10: F64.0) is interested in participating in the observational study on Metabolism and Psychopathology in Transsexual Patients. They have not undergone any prior treatment with cross-sex hormones and have given written informed consent after receiving adequate oral and written information. The individual is legally competent and meets the eligibility criteria for the study.

There is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial as it is focused on the assessment of the reduction of acetabular fractures using different methods. Participants will be selected based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria outlined in the description.

The patient is a 45-year-old active male who injured his right shoulder while playing basketball. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He reports pain and weakness in the shoulder, which has been ongoing for the past six months. He has tried physical therapy and pain medication but has not seen significant improvement. MRI results show a full-thickness rotator cuff tear. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares surgical and non-surgical management of rotator cuff tears. He is willing to undergo either treatment and is available for follow-up appointments. He has no history of prior shoulder surgery or other shoulder conditions such as calcific tendonitis, fracture, or adhesive capsulitis.

The patient is a healthy, non-smoking, non-alcoholic male or non-pregnant female between the age of 18-45 years with a body weight within ± 15% of ideal weight as related to height and body frame according to Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) Chart. They have normal findings as determined by baseline history, physical examination, vital signs, haemogram, biochemistry, serology (HIV, Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C), urinalysis, 12 lead ECG and chest X-ray (chest X-ray if required). The patient is willing to follow the protocol requirements as evidenced by written informed consent, and is willing to not use any prescription and over the counter medications including vitamins and minerals for 14 days prior to study and during the course of the study. They have no history of drug abuse in the past one year, and are not using medication for any ailment having enzyme-modifying activity in the previous 28 days, prior to dosing day. They are not suffering from any medical or surgical conditions, which might significantly interfere with the functioning of gastrointestinal tract, blood-forming organs, and have no history of cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, ophthalmic, pulmonary, neurological, metabolic, hematological, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunological, or psychiatric diseases and bleeding tendency. The patient is not a participant in a clinical drug study or bioequivalence study within 90 days prior to present study, and they have no history of malignancy or other serious diseases. The patient is willing to abstain from food for at least 10.00 hours prior to study drug administration and for at least 04.00 hours post-dose, in each study period, and is not contraindicated to blood sampling or have difficulty in accessibility of veins. They are willing to avoid the use of xanthine-containing food or beverages (chocolates, tea, coffee or cola drinks) or fruit juice/grapefruit juice and any alcoholic products for 48.00 hours prior to dosing until the last blood sample collection of last study period. The patient is not found positive in breath alcohol test or urine test for drugs of abuse done before check-in for each study period. They are willing to abstain from consumption of tobacco products 24.00 hours prior to dosing until the last blood sample collection of last study period. Female subjects willing to participate should have a negative urine pregnancy test at the time of screening, and should use acceptable method of contraception from the date of screening until the completion of the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been wearing glasses since the age of 12. Her current prescription is -3.50 diopters in both eyes. She is interested in LASIK surgery to eliminate the need for glasses and contacts. She has no history of eye disease or surgery and has no family history of eye problems. Her eye exam reveals a healthy cornea and adequate corneal thickness for LASIK surgery. She has no other medical problems and is not taking any medications. She is willing to comply with the post-operative follow-up schedule as required by the study.

A 55-year-old man who had a left transfemoral amputation due to a motorcycle accident 3 years ago is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effectiveness of passive, adaptive, and active prosthetic knees. He is currently using a non-microprocessor prosthetic knee with mechanical stance control and is classified as a Medicare functional classification level 3. He is physically active and enjoys hiking and cycling. His body weight is 190lbs, and he has no other major limb amputations. He has stable limb volume, and his skin tissue is intact without open wounds or sores. He has no significant medical conditions and is not expected to require a replacement prosthetic socket within the next 15 months. He does not rely on any assistive device for ambulation. He is excited to participate in the study to help determine which prosthetic knee technology is best suited for his lifestyle and activities.

The patient is a 70-year-old man living alone in his house. He is able to walk with a cane but has difficulty climbing stairs. He has a history of hypertension and is taking medication to control it. He had a heart attack six months ago but has recovered well with no residual symptoms. He has never had any neurological disease or surgery in his lower or upper extremities. He speaks fluent English and is able to follow instructions. He is interested in maintaining his independence and mobility and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve his nutritional and physical status.

A 60-year-old man from Russia with known chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been referred to participate in the clinical trial. He has been managing his COPD with inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids for the last 5 years. The most recent lung function test showed an FEV1 of 60% predicted. He has not received any prior pneumococcal vaccinations. He is willing to consent to the study and agrees to use two acceptable methods of contraception through 6 weeks after study vaccination. He does not have any history of immune dysfunction or autoimmune disease. He has not received any licensed live virus vaccine within the last 3 months before or scheduled within 3 months after the study vaccination. He has not received any investigational drug or other investigational vaccine within the last 2 months before or scheduled within 28 days after the study vaccination. He has not received any blood product or immunoglobulin preparation within the last 6 months before or 28 days after the study vaccination. He has not been hospitalized for acute illness within the last 3 months before the study vaccination. He is not a pregnant woman or nursing mother. He does not have a history of invasive pneumococcal disease or of other culture-positive pneumococcal disease. He has not received antibiotic therapy for any acute illness within 7 days before the study vaccination. He does not have hypersensitivity to any components of the vaccine, including phenol.

A 9-year-old boy was diagnosed with osteosarcoma in his right femur and referred to South Egypt Cancer Institute for chemotherapy. He has no previous history of heart disease or any other chronic illness. His physical examination was unremarkable. His ECG showed normal sinus rhythm with a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. His echocardiogram showed normal left ventricular function with an ejection fraction of 65% and no significant valvular disease. He has no history of renal disease or any other significant medical history. He is scheduled to receive chemotherapy for the next 6 months and will be followed up every 3 months with tissue Doppler assessment of right ventricular function.

This is a 12-year-old male with a past medical history of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) who has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and allogeneic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) but has now relapsed with hypodiploid cytogenetics. The patient has been treated with multiple lines of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (TKI) but has failed to achieve remission. The patient has documented CD19 tumor expression demonstrated in bone marrow and peripheral blood by flow cytometry within 3 months of study entry, and bone marrow with ≥ 5% lymphoblasts by morphologic assessment at screening. The patient is up to 25 years old at the time of screening and must have an apheresis product of non-mobilized cells received and accepted by the manufacturing site. The patient is not pregnant or nursing (lactating) and is willing to use highly effective methods of contraception from signing informed consent and through at least 12 months after the CTL019 infusion. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in this clinical trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes five years ago. She has been taking diabetes medication consistently for the past three months and has been able to manage her blood sugar levels, but experiences occasional high and low glucose episodes. She has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both of which are currently under control with medication. The patient has no known food allergies or intolerances and has never been diagnosed with Celiac Disease. She is not currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially decrease her medication usage and improve her blood sugar control.

The patient is a 55 year old male who has recently undergone a radical gastrectomy for gastric cancer. Postoperative pathology has confirmed stage III gastric cancer according to AJCC/UICC 8th TNM staging classification. The patient has a performance status of 0 on the ECOG within 7 days before the first dose of study treatment. The patient's vital organs are functioning within normal limits and his life expectancy is estimated to be ≥ 6 months. The patient has not received previous chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy or immunotherapy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF). The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use adequate contraception methods or keep abstinence. The patient does not have any active malignant tumors or chronic diarrhea. The patient does not have any unrecovered complications after radical gastrectomy before the first dose of study treatment. The patient is not suffering from myocardial infarction, uncontrolled angina, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, echocardiogram shows left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 50%, chronic diarrhea (watery diarrhea: ≥ 5 times per day), active infection within 14 days before the first dose of study treatment, active tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease by imaging or symptoms, positive HIV antibody, HBsAg, or HCV antibody, need long-term systemic steroid therapy (> 10 mg/d prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 14 days before the first dose of study treatment or during the study period, severe allergic reaction to any antibody-based drugs or existence of any concurrent autoimmune disease. The patient is not receiving any live vaccines within 28 days before the first dose of study treatment or during the study period, and does not have a known history of allogeneic organ transplantation and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. The patient does not have any other serious physical or mental diseases or serious laboratory abnormalities that may increase the risk of participating in the study. The patient is eligible to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with invasive estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. She is planning to take tamoxifen for clinical indications and has never been diagnosed with breast cancer in the breast contralateral to the current diagnosis. She has a referral from a healthcare professional based on her personal risk of breast cancer. She has no contraindications to tamoxifen therapy and does not have any serious medical or psychiatric illnesses that would prevent voluntary informed consent. The patient has no breast implants and no active skin infections or wounds overlying the breast. She has no history of breast cancer or any type of cancer and is not taking any other medications that may affect breast density. She is willing to participate in the study and undergo the required screening, physical exam, and medical history evaluation.

The patient is an 80-year-old Caucasian woman who was recently diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. She has no previous history of cancer and has not received any cytotoxic treatments before. She lives alone, but her daughter visits her every day and helps with household chores. The patient has been experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss for the past few weeks. She also reports occasional night sweats. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis, for which she takes medications. She uses a cane to walk due to knee pain. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or neurological conditions. The patient's ADL score is 6 and IADL score is 7. She has multiple comorbidities with a CIRS score of 6. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 30 year old pregnant woman who is currently at 28 weeks of gestation. She is African American and has a history of hypertension, which is currently well-controlled on medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has no significant medical history and has had a normal pregnancy so far. However, during her recent ultrasound, her baby's weight and head circumference were found to be below the 5th percentile, indicating a small for gestational age (SGA) status. She has been referred to the Brigham and Women's Hospital for further evaluation and management. She meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial which include gestational age less than 36 weeks, birthweight below the 5th percentile, and head circumference at birth below the 5th percentile. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria which include major chromosomal or congenital anomalies, major congenital infections, significant prenatal focal brain lesions, major maternal illness, mental and/or emotional impairment, heroin addiction, and documented alcoholism. She is interested in participating in the study and hopes that the neuropsychoeducational model of intervention can improve the developmental outcome of her SGA preterm infant.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has recently experienced a transient ischemic attack (TIA). He has a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and is a smoker. He works as a sales representative and travels frequently. He is married with two teenage children. He is concerned about the possibility of having another stroke and is willing to participate in the PREVENT trial to reduce his risk factors. He is able to follow simple commands and is willing to make changes to his lifestyle to improve his health. He lives within 75 km of the intervention site and is able to attend the necessary appointments. He does not have any contraindications to exercise testing and training as per American College of Sports Medicine guidelines.

A 62-year-old woman has been experiencing frequent episodes of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue for the past few months. She has a history of hypertension and was previously diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. Her current medications include beta blockers and anticoagulants. Despite medication, her symptoms persist, and her cardiologist has recommended catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial that compares two techniques for catheter ablation. She understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to participate in the study. She has no contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging and has no other medical conditions that would exclude her from the trial.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of being overweight for the past 3 years. Her current weight is 86kg and height is 164cm, resulting in a body mass index (BMI) of 31.9kg/m2, indicating obesity. She reports having tried multiple diets and exercise programs in the past without success. She works as a nurse and has a sedentary lifestyle, spending most of her day sitting at a desk. She has no history of chronic diseases, such as diabetes or cardiovascular disease. Her family history is significant for obesity in her mother and sister. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the effect of two hypocaloric diets with different macronutrient content on body weight loss and gene-diet interactions. She is willing to follow either a high-carbohydrate/low-fat or a high-protein diet for 6 months and attend three in-person meetings, one at baseline and two follow-ups at three and six months after the beginning of the intervention. She is also willing to provide blood samples for genetic analysis and complete online questionnaires regarding her progress. She is excited to receive nutritional counseling and support throughout the intervention to help her achieve her weight loss goals.

45-year-old female with a history of ulcerative colitis diagnosed by endoscopy and histology. She has been in remission for the past 2 months, with a Clinical Activity Index (CAI) of 3 and Endoscopic Index (EI) of 2. Her inflammation extent during the last acute episode was more than 15 cm beyond the anal margin, which ended 2 months ago. She has not undergone any bowel resection leading to diarrhea, and has not had toxic megacolon, gastric or duodenal ulcer, or haemorrhagic diathesis. She does not have symptomatic organic disease of the gastrointestinal tract, except for mild haemorrhoids. She does not have active colorectal cancer or a history of colorectal cancer, and has no serious secondary illnesses of an acute or chronic nature. She has no asthma, and her renal and liver functions are normal. She has not received immunosuppressants or corticosteroids in the last 3 months or NSAIDs for more than 6 weeks. She is not intolerant or hypersensitive to salicylic acid or its derivatives, or any of the other constituents of the study drugs. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using adequate contraception. She has not participated in any clinical trial in the last 30 days and has not previously participated in this trial.

8-year-old male, Asian ethnicity, presented to the pediatric clinic for evaluation of his short stature. He has no significant past medical history, and his parents are of average height. He was born at term with a birth weight of 3.2 kg. His developmental milestones were normal, and he is doing well in school. His only complaint is that he is shorter than most of his peers. On examination, his height was below the 3rd percentile for his age, and his bone age was determined to be 7 years. His thyroid function was found to be normal. His parents consented for him to participate in the clinical trial of DA-3002 for idiopathic short stature.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been receiving maintenance hemodialysis for the past 6 months due to end-stage renal disease secondary to hypertension. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. She has a body mass index of 32 kg/m² and is currently on a low-protein diet. She reports feeling fatigued during dialysis and has been experiencing fluctuations in blood pressure during her hemodialysis sessions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of high versus low protein meals during dialysis on blood pressure and arterial stiffness indices. She has no history of malignancy, major amputations or hospitalization for acute cardiovascular events within the past 3 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman diagnosed with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer. She has inoperable locally advanced disease and has progressed after previous first-line endocrine therapy. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease. Her ECOG performance status is 1 and her Karnofsky score is 70%. She has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has measurable disease with at least one lesion that can be accurately measured in at least one dimension (longest diameter to be recorded) as >= 20 mm with conventional techniques or as >= 10 mm with spiral CT scan. The patient had previously received adjuvant hormonal therapy. She has no history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to tipifarnib (R115777, Zarnestra™) or other agents used in the study. The patient has no rapidly progressive, life-threatening metastases, no symptomatic lymphangitic metastases, no brain or leptomeningeal involvement, and no grade 2 or more peripheral neuropathy. She has no uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmia or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements. The patient is HIV-negative and not receiving combination anti-retroviral therapy.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation. He had a history of smoking for 25 years and had recently quit smoking 6 months ago. He was intubated due to respiratory distress and put on mechanical ventilation. The patient had a hospital stay of more than 3 days and had an IGS-II score of 18. On day 7 of his hospitalization, the patient developed a fever, cough, and purulent sputum. The chest X-ray showed bilateral infiltrates, and the sputum culture was positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae. He was diagnosed with hospital-acquired pneumonia and was started on appropriate antibiotics. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the implementation of evidence-based guidelines to reduce the duration of mechanical ventilation in patients presenting with hospital-acquired pneumonia.

A 53-year-old man with end stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis has been referred to participate in a clinical trial for a pneumococcal vaccine. He has a history of hypertension and has been on dialysis for the past 2 years. He has not received any pneumococcal vaccinations in the past 5 years. He reports no recent episodes of S. pneumoniae infection or any other severe adverse reactions to vaccines. He takes his medications regularly, which include anti-hypertensive drugs and phosphate binders, and follows a low-sodium diet. He leads an active lifestyle and enjoys walking and cycling. He has no known allergies to any food or medications. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance medical knowledge and improve his health.

An 80-year-old man presents with a history of multiple falls at home. He reports severe pain in his right hip that started after a fall. The physical exam reveals swelling and deformity in the right hip. He is diagnosed with a traumatic hip fracture and requires surgical intervention. He has a past medical history of hypertension, but no other significant medical conditions. He reports no history of delirium or cognitive impairment. He is fluent in English and has a Mini-Mental Status Exam score of 27. His attending surgeon is participating in the study, and he is willing to give informed consent. He is scheduled to receive spinal anesthesia for his surgery.

The patient is a 45 year old male who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (alloHSCT) 3 years ago for acute myeloid leukemia. He developed chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGvHD) with skin rash, oral ulcers, and dry eyes and mouth. He received multiple treatments including steroids, calcineurin inhibitors, and mycophenolate mofetil, but his symptoms remained refractory. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking amlodipine for blood pressure control. His performance status is 80% according to the Karnofsky performance scale. His laboratory values are within normal limits, including white blood cells, absolute neutrophil count, hemoglobin, and platelets. His cardiac function and pulmonary function tests are also within normal limits. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his refractory cGvHD. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the trial and is willing to sign the informed consent document. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with a solid head and neck cancer tumor. She is fluent in both Dutch and French languages. She has been experiencing difficulty swallowing and has lost some weight. She has no past history of cancer or other major medical conditions. She is currently taking medications for hypertension and cholesterol control. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is generally independent in her activities of daily living but has reported some recent fatigue and weakness. She has not undergone prior surgical intervention or chemotherapy. The patient is scheduled to undergo curative surgery for her tumor under general anesthesia at the division of maxillofacial surgery or Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery. The patient will be eligible for a geriatric screening as part of routine preoperative staging. The study aims to determine the value of G8 in predicting postoperative morbidity in older patients undergoing elective curative surgery for head and neck cancer.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman with a genetically confirmed diagnosis of myotonic dystrophy. She has been experiencing muscle weakness, stiffness, and difficulty with coordination for several years. She has also noticed some cognitive impairment and occasional episodes of hypersomnia. Her MDRS score is 4, indicating moderate to severe disability. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of chronic renal or liver disease. She has not previously been treated with DHEA. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of DHEA for the treatment of myotonic dystrophy.

Patient is a 68-year-old male who has been experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath for the past several months. He was recently diagnosed with severe aortic regurgitation (AR), which affects the aortic valve in the heart. The patient is at high risk for open surgical valve replacement due to pre-existing medical conditions, and as such, is a candidate for TAVR (Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement) using the JenaValve Pericardial TAVR System. The patient is classified as NYHA functional class II or higher and has been informed of the nature of the study, agrees to its provisions and has provided written informed consent as approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB)/ Ethics Committee (EC) of the respective clinical site.
