The patient does not have congenital uni or bicuspid aortic valve morphology, previous prosthetic aortic valve (bioprosthesis or mechanical) implant, endocarditis or other active infection. The patient is not in need of urgent or emergent TAVR procedure for any reason and is not experiencing cardiogenic shock or hemodynamic instability requiring inotropic support or ventricular assist device. The patient is not experiencing severe mitral regurgitation.

The patient is a 45 year old male who has recently tested positive for COVID-19. He has been experiencing symptoms such as cough, fever and difficulty in breathing for the past week. He has been admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of pneumonia and acute lung injury. The patient is not intubated and is able to understand and provide informed consent for the study. He has no history of immunomodulators or anti-rejection drugs, and has not received any live attenuated vaccine in the past 3 months. His oxygen saturation at rest in ambient air is below 93%. He is willing to comply with any applicable contraceptive requirements if discharged from the hospital prior to completing the study. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medication. He is a smoker with a history of 10 pack-years. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient is married and has 2 children. He works as an accountant and has been working from home for the past 2 weeks. He reports no recent travel history outside of the city. His vital signs are within normal limits except for oxygen saturation.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in her legs for the past few months. She recently underwent a transthoracic echocardiography which revealed a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 40%. Further clinical examination and testing did not reveal any obvious etiology for her LV dysfunction. She has no history of myocardial infarction or coronary artery stenosis. She has not been diagnosed with typical angina or acute coronary syndrome. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no severe allergy to gadolinium or any contraindication for coronary artery angiography. She has not been diagnosed with LVEF dysfunction for more than 8 weeks. She is covered by the social security and does not have any guardianship or consent issues. She has given informed and signed consent for the study. She is eligible for inclusion in the clinical trial to evaluate the sensitivity of CMR for predicting the presence of significant coronary artery stenosis on coronary angiography in patients with reduced LVEF.

The patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of smoking for the past 20 years, currently smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day. He has recently scheduled an elective bariatric surgery for weight loss, 8 weeks in advance. He is motivated to quit smoking before his surgery to improve his overall health and increase the success of his bariatric surgery. He has no history of psychiatric instability, and is willing to participate in an intensive pre- and post-surgical smoking cessation intervention that includes varenicline, behavioral counseling, and monetary incentives for remaining smoke-free. He understands the importance of adhering to the study schedule and is willing to provide study access to his medical records. He has no contraindications for varenicline use, and has been medically cleared for bariatric surgery.

The patient is a 14-year-old male who had a liver transplant three years ago due to acute liver failure. He is currently taking tacrolimus to prevent rejection of the transplanted liver. However, the Medication Level Variability Index (MLVI) calculated at his transplant center over the past two years indicates that he is nonadherent to his medication regimen. His guardian has provided consent and the patient has assented to participate in the study. The patient has not undergone any other organ transplantation and is not currently listed for any other organ transplantation. He is expected to remain at the same transplant center for the duration of the study. The patient is not pregnant and has not been hospitalized for more than 48 consecutive hours in the past three months. Overall, the patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

This is a 62-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer, who has undergone hormonal therapy as well as radiation therapy to the pelvic region. Despite treatment, he has developed metastatic prostate cancer and has increasing PSA levels. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for new treatment options. He has no history of cardiac disease or thrombotic events in the last six months and has normal laboratory values. He is willing to receive counseling related to pregnancy precautions and teratogenic risks of lenalidomide. He is not currently on any other experimental drug or therapy and is willing to participate in patient-reported outcomes assessments.

A 45-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with a BMI of 32 and a history of dyslipidemia. He reports experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father suffering from a myocardial infarction at age 55. The patient reports taking no medications and having no known allergies. He has a history of smoking, but quit 2 years ago and has not used any tobacco products since then. His blood pressure is 138/88 mmHg, with no significant change in position. His fasting glucose is 110mg/dL, triglycerides 165mg/dL, and HDL-C 38mg/dL. His waist circumference is 102cm. His recent liver and kidney function tests are normal. He has no history of coronary artery disease or other artherosclerotic diseases. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of pitavastatin in patients with metabolic syndrome.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has had one previous C-section delivery. She has been trying to conceive for over a year without success and has decided to undergo IVF treatment. She has no history of any other gynecological surgery, and her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is currently not using any form of contraception and has not been an IUD carrier in the last 3 months. She is willing to participate in the study and is able to undergo trans-vaginal scans to evaluate the position of her C-section scar in relation to the uterine fundus and inner cervical os.

The patient is a 62 year old man with end stage renal disease. He has been on hemodialysis for the past 6 months, and his doctor has recommended that he have a brachiocephalic fistula (BCF) placed for his dialysis access. He has a history of hypertension and diabetes, which are well-controlled with medication. He is currently taking lisinopril and metformin. He has no history of heart disease or stroke. He has a BMI of 28 and is physically active, walking for 30 minutes every day. He lives with his wife and adult son, and enjoys spending time with his grandchildren. He has no history of major surgeries or allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written consent approved by the IRB from the University of Chicago.

33-year-old male with a history of cocaine dependence seeking treatment for his addiction. He reports using cocaine at least once a week for the past year and has tried to quit on his own but has been unsuccessful. He does not have any significant medical or psychiatric illnesses besides his substance abuse disorder. He is not physically dependent on drugs of abuse other than cocaine, and he is not pregnant. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of tryptophan and voucher incentives in treating cocaine dependence.

54-year-old male with a history of heart failure presents with New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III symptoms, including shortness of breath with minimal exertion, fatigue, and edema. Echocardiography shows severely reduced left ventricular systolic function with an ejection fraction of 25%. The patient has been scheduled to undergo left ventricular assist device (LVAD) insertion for mechanical circulatory support. The patient has no history of uncontrolled diabetes with peripheral neuropathy, clinical right ventricular failure, or moderate-severe preexisting aortic insufficiency. There is no evidence of disorders that adversely influence exercise ability, such as arthritis, peripheral vascular disease, or pulmonary disease. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the advanced heart failure group of the trial.

A 55 year old woman has been diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer and is undergoing treatment with immunotherapy. She develops an immune-related adverse event (irAE) that requires prolonged steroid use to control. The side effects of the steroids are impacting her quality of life, and her medical team has recommended treatment with either rituximab or tocilizumab. She has no history of immunodeficiency or chronic viral hepatitis. She has a negative urine pregnancy test and is practicing contraception. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent. Her performance status is 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Scale. She has adequate organ function and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She has received pneumococcal vaccine within 5 years of study entry and has no history of tuberculosis or other active infections. She has not received major surgery within the past month.

This is a 35 year-old female who is looking to improve her lifestyle habits. She has a sedentary job and tends to eat fast food meals due to her busy schedule. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to increase physical activity and promote healthy eating habits. She owns a smartphone and is comfortable with using technology. She has no known health conditions and does not take any medications. She is motivated to make changes to her lifestyle and is willing to commit to the study requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in her right knee for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain is worse when she stands or walks for an extended period of time, and it has been interfering with her daily activities and quality of life. She has no history of knee surgery or other connective tissue diseases affecting the knee. She has not received any injections with steroids or hyaluronic acids in the past 3 months. She is not taking anticoagulant medications and does not have a pacemaker. She has not undergone electroacupuncture treatments before. She has been diagnosed with radiologic knee osteoarthritis, with a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 3, by a radiologist. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled on amlodipine 5mg daily. She has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy of radiofrequency neurotomy in treating chronic knee osteoarthritis pain.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with recurrent ovarian cancer. She had a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and omentectomy for stage IIIc ovarian cancer five years ago. She received six cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin as adjuvant chemotherapy. Her disease recurred after two years, and she was treated with three cycles of carboplatin and gemcitabine. She had a partial response to this treatment, but her disease progressed again after six months. She underwent a debulking surgery and received three cycles of liposomal doxorubicin with stable disease. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medication at present. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is generally in good health, with an ECOG performance status of 1. Her current symptoms include abdominal pain, bloating, and fatigue. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 62-year-old man was recently diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx. He underwent curative surgery to remove all macroscopic disease 45 days ago. He is considered to be at high risk of recurrence. He has no evidence of distant metastases. He has no other prior or concurrent malignancy that would preclude study participation. He is in good health with no uncontrolled medical illness. He has not received any prior biologic, chemotherapy, or endocrine therapy. He is willing to participate in a randomized clinical trial comparing different regimens of radiation therapy for head and neck cancer.

A 55 year old woman with a history of open-angle glaucoma presents to the clinic with complaints of irritation and burning in both eyes. She has been using latanoprost 0.005% eye drops for the past year. Upon non-instillation, she experiences mild dry eye sensation and tearing. Her best corrected ETDRS visual acuity score is +0.3 logMAR in both eyes. The fluorescein tear break-up time (fBUT) is less than 10 seconds and corneal and conjunctival fluorescein staining shows a corneal fluorescein staining score of grade I and a combined nasal and temporal staining score of grade II in both eyes. She does not have any corneal abnormality or other condition that prevents reliable applanation tonometry. She has not used any preserved eye drops other than latanoprost, including artificial tears, at screening or within two weeks prior to the screening visit. She has not undergone any ocular surgery or used contact lenses in the past 6 months. She has no contraindications to tafluprost therapy and is willing to follow instructions. She provides a written informed consent and is aged 55 years or more. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme after experiencing severe headaches and seizures. She underwent surgical resection of the tumor and has completed conventional external beam radiotherapy. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80%, and she has a life expectancy of at least 8 weeks. The patient has no history of autoimmune diseases, and she has negative serology for hepatitis B and C, HIV, and syphilis. Her hemoglobin, absolute granulocyte count, and platelet count are within normal limits. She has no active infection, and she is not pregnant or nursing. She has no history of other malignancies within the past 5 years. Her medical history is significant for a history of seasonal allergies, which are well-controlled with antihistamine therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to use effective contraception during the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital after experiencing a sudden and severe headache. A CT scan revealed aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and he was diagnosed with WFNS grade 2 and Fischer grade 1. He has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, drug abuse, or immune deficiency diseases. He is scheduled for surgical intervention to treat the aneurysm. He has no comorbidities and has an ASA grade of 1. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient will be randomized into one of the four groups (Group P, Group I, Group S, or Group D) to receive anesthesia during the intervention. The patient will undergo pre-anesthetic checkup prior to the intervention and will be monitored intra-operatively for various parameters including blood pressure, heart rate, and urine output. The patient will have cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum blood samples collected at various time points to measure the level of caspase 3 enzyme using a quantitative ELISA kit. The patient will be excluded from the study if there are any surgical complications like massive blood loss or prolonged clipping time.

45 y/o female with biopsy confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of cervix. She has no prior history of radiation to the abdomen or pelvis and has good performance status. She is of child-bearing potential and will provide a negative pregnancy test. She has no history of Scleroderma or Inflammatory bowel disease. She is able to receive chemotherapy and concurrent chemoradiotherapy, and has signed a study-specific informed consent. Her lab results are within the study-specific limits. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the feasibility of minimal invasive surgical resection through simultaneously integrated dose escalation for her locally advanced cervical cancer.

52 F with a history of GERD and occasional dysphagia who presents to her gastroenterologist for evaluation. She reports occasional heartburn and regurgitation of acidic contents into her mouth. She also reports some discomfort when swallowing, particularly with solid foods. She has been taking PPI for the past few months with some relief of symptoms. She is concerned about the risk and discomfort associated with upper endoscopy and is interested in a less invasive diagnostic tool. She is willing to undergo capsule endoscopy and sign the informed consent form. She reports no contraindications for capsule ingestion and no prior pelvic or abdominal surgery of the gastrointestinal tract. She is not currently suffering from any conditions that could affect the clarity of the CE images.

The clinical trial is looking for premature infants with a gestational age of less than 28 weeks, who have respiratory distress syndrome requiring assisted ventilation and a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) without any other cardiac anomalies. The study aims to compare the efficacy and safety of oral and intravenous ibuprofen for PDA closure in these high-risk premature infants. The infants will be randomly assigned to receive either oral or IV ibuprofen, and the dosage of ibuprofen will be determined according to echocardiographic PDA flow patterns. The study is expected to last for 2 years, and a total of 31 extremely premature infants with RDS and PDA will be enrolled. Severe congenital anomalies or lethal cardiopulmonary conditions will be exclusion criteria, and informed consent will be obtained from parents.

A 54-year-old Caucasian man with a history of amyloid light-chain amyloidosis involving myocardium complains of shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest pain. He has previously undergone chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation, but the symptoms have persisted. He is currently on medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has never been exposed to lenalidomide within the past 5 years. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He denies smoking or drinking alcohol. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His family history is negative for any cardiac or hematologic disorders. He meets both criteria A and B for cardiac involvement in amyloid light-chain amyloidosis. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 2. His laboratory values are within normal limits, with a serum creatinine of 1.2mg/dl, absolute neutrophil count of 1200/ul, platelet count of 90,000/ul, and hemoglobin of 11.0mg/dl. He understands the risks and benefits of the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the visit schedule, treatment plan, laboratory examination, and other testing procedures.

A 32-year-old woman presents with a history of chronic fatigue that has persisted for more than 6 months. The patient reports feeling tired, weak, and unrefreshed despite adequate rest, and experiences difficulty concentrating and completing daily tasks. She reports no other significant medical history or comorbidities. The patient has been diagnosed with chronic fatigue syndrome based on the Fukuda criteria and Canadian consensus criteria. She is interested in participating in an observational study regarding the use of supplements in chronic fatigue syndrome patients. The patient is willing to answer a detailed questionnaire regarding her diagnosis and onset of symptoms. She is also willing to undergo a double-blind trial using the Karnofsky scale to evaluate her fatigue levels before and after the use of supplements. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria and is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with acute symptomatic proximal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) with evidence of proximal thrombosis that involves at least the popliteal vein or a more proximal vein, demonstrated by imaging with compression ultrasound (CUS), including grey-scale or color-coded Doppler. He is otherwise healthy and has no history of thrombosis or bleeding disorders. He has not undergone thrombectomy, insertion of a caval filter, or use of a fibrinolytic agent to treat the current episode of venous thromboembolism (VTE). He is not currently experiencing active bleeding or high risk for bleeding contraindicating treatment with low-molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and a vitamin K antagonist (VKA). He has no presence of a mechanical valve or intracranial bleeding, intraocular bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding 6 months prior to enrollment date. He is not taking aspirin or dual antiplatelet therapy. He meets the other inclusion criteria for the study.

This is a 55-year-old man who recently completed a 12-week Phase II cardiac rehabilitation program following a diagnosis of coronary heart disease. He has a history of chronic angina pectoris and underwent CABG surgery approximately six months ago. Although he participated in supervised exercise during cardiac rehabilitation, he is concerned about maintaining regular exercise and fitness in the long-term to prevent further events or re-hospitalization. He is able to read and speak English and is willing to consent to medical chart review for disease and treatment variables. He is able to walk unassisted and has no prior history of neurological brain disorders or cognitive impairments. He is interested in participating in a randomized controlled trial that aims to promote exercise maintenance among patients who have completed cardiac rehabilitation.

The patient is a 51-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with prediabetes. She is currently enrolled in the Memorial Health System (MHS) corporate wellness program and has expressed interest in participating in the Mastering Diabetes Study. She is able to participate in physical activity, has reliable daily internet access with a device with a webcam, and has an email account. She is open-minded about eating a plant-based diet and is willing to prepare food at home following recipes and meal examples provided in the online course. The patient is willing to increase her physical activity to 5-6 days per week and participate in an online community for support and coaching. She is fluent in English and is willing to participate in biweekly videoconferencing for support and coaching. The patient does not have any medical conditions that prevent her from participating in physical activity or using email, a smartphone, or the internet.

Pt is a 35yo M in good health with no history of systemic disease or peripheral ischemia. Pt is a non-smoker and is not currently pregnant. The patient is able to understand and give informed consent for the study. The American Society of Anesthesiology has classified the patient as Class 1, indicating that the patient is healthy and has no significant medical conditions. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal pain and frequent diarrhea for several months. She has also noticed weight loss and a decrease in appetite. After undergoing several tests, she has been diagnosed with a neuroendocrine tumor (NET) in her duodenum that has spread to her liver. The tumor is considered advanced and not curable with surgery. The patient will require systemic chemotherapy and has been referred to a multidisciplinary tumor board for further evaluation. She has measurable disease according to the RECIST v1.1 criteria and a TAP CT scan with contrast agents has been performed within the last 4 weeks. The patient has provided tumor tissue, either fresh-frozen or paraffin-embedded, for the MGMT status evaluation. The patient has not received prior chemotherapy using Oxaliplatin or ALKY (streptozotocin, dacarbazin or temozolomide). The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed a written informed consent document.

A 56 year old woman has been diagnosed with lung cancer and has been told that she is not eligible for surgical resection due to the advanced stage of the disease. The patient has multiple lung nodules on CT scan, but none of them are larger than 4 cm. The patient has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the outcome has not been satisfactory. The patient has no other comorbidities and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to investigate the effectiveness of CT-guided microwave ablation for lung cancer. The patient has good compliance and has signed the informed consent. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and there are no large blood vessels or important structures adjacent to the lung nodules. The patient is excited to have a new treatment option that is convenient, easy, and associated with less trauma and fewer complications.

Pt is a 40-year-old male with a history of bipolar I disorder and currently in sustained remission. He has a BMI of 30 and is currently taking medications for bipolar disorder that have caused weight gain and metabolic effects. He has agreed to participate in a 5-month intervention study to examine the potential to reduce metabolic risk factors in patients with bipolar I disorder and improve psychiatric and functional outcomes. He is willing to comply with study requirements and has provided informed consent. He meets all the inclusion criteria, including having an Epworth Scale score of >7 and being a woman of childbearing potential who agrees to use doctor-approved birth control throughout participation in the study. He does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including having previously failed an adequate trial of aripiprazole and having a history of homicidal ideation. He will be assessed and meet with his study psychiatrist at least bi-monthly throughout his participation, more frequently when clinically necessary.

A 26-year-old woman with a history of mild asthma presents for the multiple ascending dose (MAD) study in part B of the trial. She reports symptoms of wheezing and shortness of breath during physical activity, but otherwise has been free of exacerbations in the past year. She is currently using an inhaled corticosteroid and a long-acting beta agonist to manage her asthma. The patient has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. She has no history of hepatitis, HIV, or tuberculosis, and her laboratory results are within normal limits. She has no abnormal ECG findings and has not had a respiratory tract infection in the previous six weeks. She has never used tobacco or nicotine-containing products. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and comply with the study requirements.

A 59-year-old male patient was diagnosed with pancreatic tubular adenocarcinoma and underwent a successful R0 resection. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is currently undergoing chemotherapy with gemcitabine. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not currently pregnant. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the influence of gemcitabine treatment on serological and immunological status and gene expression profile in patients with pancreatic tubular carcinoma after tumor resection.

58-year-old male with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease with a baseline eGFR of 45 ml/min presents with severe aortic stenosis. He is evaluated for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) due to high INTEGER risk score > 11 and high EuroSCORE (European system for cardiac operative risk evaluation). The patient has not had recent (<=30 days) contrast media exposure and is not enrolled in any concomitant studies. The patient is a non-fertile male and meets the inclusion criteria for this study. This patient may be a suitable candidate for the RenPro-TAVI Trial to assess the efficacy of remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) in preventing acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients with impaired renal function undergoing TAVI.

The patient is a 7-year-old child residing in Bangkok, Thailand, who has no history of flavivirus infection or vaccination. The child is in good health, as determined by medical history and physical examination before entering the study. Their parent has given written informed consent for the child's screening and enrollment in the study. The child does not have any chronic medical conditions or allergies to any vaccine components. They have not received any immunoglobulins or blood products in the past six months and are not planning to receive any during the study period. The child's parent has easy access to a fixed or mobile telephone and is not illiterate. The child is willing to attend all 20 study visits, receive four injections, and undergo seven venipunctures.

Patient is a 55-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) for the past 10 years. He has been taking metformin and a sulfonylurea agent for glucose control. He reports occasional abdominal discomfort and feeling of bloating. He has no history of alcohol abuse or other substance abuse. His BMI is 31, BP: 140/82, HR: 80/min. His laboratory results show elevated liver enzymes (AST: 70 U/L, ALT: 85 U/L) and fasting blood glucose of 155 mg/dL. He has been previously diagnosed with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) based on liver biopsy. He has not been treated with any medications for NASH in the past. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of low-dose pioglitazone for NASH treatment.

A 45-year-old woman with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years presents with complaints of bleeding gums and bad breath. She currently manages her diabetes with a combination of diet and oral hypoglycemic agents. Her HbA1c level is 8.5%, indicating poor glycemic control. The patient has at least 15 teeth with more than 30% of the sites exhibiting probing depth and clinical attachment level of 4mm or more. There are also at least six teeth with at least one site showing a PD and CAL of 5mm or more with bleeding on probing. The patient has not undergone SRP in the past 12 months and has not taken any antimicrobial therapies in the previous 6 months. She does not have any medical conditions requiring prophylactic antibiotic coverage or systemic conditions that could affect the progression of periodontitis. The patient is not currently using any mouthrinses containing antimicrobials, has no allergy to metronidazole or amoxicillin, and does not have any periapical pathology, extensive prosthetic rehabilitation, or major complications of diabetes.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath. Biopsy confirmed the presence of cancer in his lungs, but he is deemed to be a high-risk surgical candidate due to his age and underlying medical conditions, including hypertension and coronary artery disease. The patient is interested in exploring alternative treatment options and has been referred to this clinical trial for consideration of percutaneous microwave ablation (MWA). Imaging shows that he has a single lung nodule measuring approximately 2 cm in diameter that is reachable and treatable via MWA. The patient is willing and able to complete the entire study and understands the procedures involved. His life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 6 months.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who recently underwent a diagnostic biopsy that confirmed endometrioid or adenosquamous endometrial carcinoma with evidence of myometrial invasion. She is otherwise in good health with no significant medical history that would contraindicate surgery. The patient is fully informed about the trial and is willing to provide informed consent. She meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria. The patient is scheduled for a hysterectomy with bilateral adnexectomy and may be randomized to receive either systematic pelvic lymphadenectomy or no lymphadenectomy. She will be closely monitored for disease-free survival and overall survival throughout the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who was admitted to the medical ICU with septic shock due to a urinary tract infection. The patient had no prior history of sepsis or any other significant medical problems. During his ICU stay, he required mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support for 3 days before he was successfully weaned off both. The patient's hospital course was complicated by acute kidney injury, for which he required continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for 5 days. He was transferred to the general medicine floor on hospital day 10 and was discharged home on hospital day 14. At the time of discharge, the patient was independent in all activities of daily living, but he reported feeling weak and fatigued. He had no significant cognitive or mental health problems at the time of discharge. The patient has access to a computer and internet connection and is willing to participate in telehealth ICU recovery care. His primary care is within the VUMC network, and he is not receiving hospice care. He has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric disorder that prevents independent living, and he speaks English fluently.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman who gave birth to a premature infant at 28 weeks of gestation. The infant was immediately admitted to the NICU for specialized care. The mother is currently recovering at home and is experiencing feelings of anxiety and stress related to her infant's health and well-being. She is seeking information and support to better understand her infant's condition and what she can do to help. The mother is willing to participate in a clinical trial aimed at organizing the information given to parents of NICU infants in order to reduce their anxiety. She understands that she will be randomly assigned to either a group that will receive organized information or a group that will not. She is willing to answer questionnaires on the first week of her infant's life and on the last week, just before her infant is released home. She meets the inclusion criteria as a parent to a premature infant after being released from the hospital, and does not meet the exclusion criteria of having a term infant or being hospitalized herself.

Patient is a 50-year-old woman from the United States who has just been diagnosed with breast cancer. She has no significant past medical history, and her BMI is 25. Her laboratory studies are unremarkable. She is HER2 negative as determined by immunohistochemistry. She has not received any prior treatment for breast cancer, including chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or hormonotherapy. She has not undergone any prior radiotherapy for breast cancer. She has no history of other neoplasms except for a curatively treated skin carcinoma. She has no evidence of metastatic disease. Her performance status is excellent, with a Karnofsky index of 90. She has adequate cardiac function, hematology, hepatic function, and renal function. She is willing and able to comply with the study treatment and follow-up.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been recently diagnosed with scleroderma. She has a medical history of Raynaud's phenomenon, which was diagnosed two years ago. She has been experiencing skin tightening, muscle weakness, and shortness of breath for the past six months. She is currently taking immunosuppressive medication to manage her symptoms. She is married and has two children, ages 10 and 13. She works as a teacher and enjoys spending time with her family and friends. She is interested in participating in clinical trials to help further research on scleroderma and potentially find new treatments. She is able to give informed consent and is over 18 years old.

The patient is a 55 year old man who has been diagnosed with primary hypertriglyceridemia. His fasting triglyceride levels are consistently above 1000 mg/dL despite being on maximal triglyceride lowering therapy, including Lovaza 4 g/day, fibric acids, and Glucophage for the treatment of hyperinsulinemia. He also has mild renal impairment. He has a family history of heart disease, and his father had a heart attack at the age of 60. He is currently working as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has a history of occasional alcohol use but denies any history of alcoholism. He does not smoke and has never used any illicit drugs. He has no known allergies to fish or any other medication. He has no history of bleeding disorders or conditions affecting the skin. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his BMI is 28. He is motivated to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the trial.

62 year old male with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) who presented with symptoms of urinary hesitancy, incomplete bladder emptying, and nocturia. He has been taking finasteride for the last six months without significant improvement in his symptoms. His baseline prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level is 3.7 ng/ml. He has no history of allergy to alpha-blockers or alpha/beta blockers and has not experienced a "first dose hypotensive episode" upon starting therapy with an alpha-blocker. He is not currently taking medications for hypertension or any other condition that would exclude him from the study. He is able to give written informed consent and is judged to be reliable and able to follow protocol procedures. He has not participated in an investigational drug study within the last four weeks and has no history of genitourinary malignancy or instrumentation of the urinary tract within the last 30 days. He has no history of acute urinary retention within the last three months and no evidence of significant renal dysfunction or laboratory abnormalities. He is a good candidate for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with colorectal cancer. The tumor is located in the descending colon and has not yet metastasized. The patient is scheduled to undergo a resection surgery under general anesthesia, with an expected duration of 3 hours. He has an ASA status of II and is generally in good health. He has no history of severe heart, liver, or kidney diseases, and is not diabetic. His blood work and imaging studies are normal, except for the presence of the tumor. The patient has been informed about the study and is interested in participating to help further research on the effects of general anesthesia on immune response and metastasis. He has no known allergies to general anesthetics, and has not received general anesthesia within the last 3 months. The patient is willing to give signed written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 9-year-old girl attending a primary school in the canton of Zurich, Switzerland. Her parents have given written consent for her to participate in the Luftibus in the School (LUIS) study. The girl has no known history of respiratory problems and is generally healthy. She has never smoked and has no known exposure to environmental pollutants. She is currently not taking any medication. Her height and weight will be measured by the fieldworkers in a standardized way during the school visit. The fieldworkers will perform lung function tests, including spirometry and fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), and double tracer gas single-breath washout (SBW) in the school according to ATS criteria. The parents will be asked to fill out a questionnaire with information about their child's respiratory symptoms, triggers, and medical history. The child will also be interviewed using a shorter questionnaire. The air pollution measurements, including nitrogen dioxide (NO2), inhalable particles of 10 micrometers or less in diameter (PM10), and ozone concentration, will be measured on the roof of the bus at the school site. The results of this study will provide new insights into the respiratory health of schoolchildren in the canton of Zurich and may help to establish new recommendations to improve their health and well-being.

The patient is a 35 year old man who has been experiencing moderate to severe pain in his left testicle for the past 6 months. The pain is described as a dull ache that radiates to the lower abdomen and hip. The patient has tried over-the-counter pain medication but found no relief. He has also noticed a lump in his scrotum that has been increasing in size. Upon examination, the patient was diagnosed with a varicocele on the left side. Medical therapy was initiated with no improvement in pain. The patient has been referred for varicocelectomy to treat the pain. The patient has no history of infertility and is otherwise healthy.

A 32-year-old healthy female office worker is interested in participating in the QazCovid-in® COVID-19 vaccine clinical trial. She has no underlying health conditions and has never tested positive for COVID-19. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use drugs. She exercises regularly and takes a daily multivitamin. She is on birth control and has no plans to become pregnant in the near future. She has no known allergies to any drugs or food. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and is excited to potentially contribute to the development of a COVID-19 vaccine.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who was diagnosed with HIV 2 years ago. She has been on a stable antiretroviral regimen for the past year and has not experienced any significant side effects. She does not have any history of alcohol or substance abuse. Her most recent laboratory values are as follows: CD4 count of 400 cells/mm3, viral load of less than 50 copies/mL, and creatinine clearance of 90 mL/min. She is currently interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating Fanconi syndrome due to antiretroviral therapy in HIV-infected individuals. She has no evidence of Fanconi syndrome and is willing to follow the study protocol, including regular laboratory evaluations and possible adjustments to her antiretroviral regimen. She is able to understand and sign the informed consent form.

A 25-year-old woman with no history of neck pain or injury presents for the clinical trial. She is physically active, engaging in regular exercise and sports activities. She has no chronic medical conditions and takes no medications. The patient has no history of neck surgery or significant trauma to the cervical spine. She provides informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. She has no current acute pain and her Neck Disability Index Score is less than 15. The patient is a suitable candidate for the study to evaluate the effects of additional axial load on cervical motor control in healthy individuals.

38-year-old male with a history of complete spinal cord injury at the T6 level resulting from a motor vehicle accident 2 years ago. The patient reports difficulty achieving and maintaining an erection sufficient for sexual activity despite attempting treatment with oral phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors (PDE5i). The patient has no medical contraindications to the use of Avanafil or Sildenafil and is able to provide informed consent and complete questionnaires. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of Avanafil and Sildenafil in treating spinal cord injury-related erectile dysfunction.

Patient is a 27-year-old pregnant woman from the United States who is scheduled to undergo an elective cesarean delivery. She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. Her BMI is 24, BP: 118/76, HR: 80/min. She has had regular prenatal care and has had no complications during her pregnancy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new method to assess estimated blood loss during her cesarean delivery.

Patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) during a routine prenatal check-up. She is currently in her 28th week of gestation with a singleton pregnancy. The patient has a pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) of 24.5 kg/m2 and has no history of gastrointestinal diseases. She is not on any anti-diabetic therapies and has not used any diabetes nutritional/dietary supplements in the past four weeks. The patient has no known allergies or intolerances to fish, milk, protein, lactose, fiber, or soy. She does not have any significant medical conditions other than GDM and is not currently or previously on a special low/no carbohydrate diet. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and has signed the informed consent.

45 y/o male, Ontario resident with a history of hypertension for the past 10 years. Despite taking multiple antihypertensive medications, blood pressure remains uncontrolled with office systolic blood pressure readings averaging 170 mmHg and an average systolic 24 hour ambulatory blood pressure of 140 mmHg. The patient has been evaluated and optimized by a hypertension specialist as per the American Heart Association guidelines. The patient has no other known medical conditions or secondary causes of hypertension. Imaging studies show suitable renal artery anatomy for renal nerve denervation. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

55 year old male with a diagnosis of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) for 3 years. The patient has been on a stable dose of memantine for the past year with no significant changes in cognitive or behavioral symptoms. The patient is able to perform basic activities of daily living but has difficulty with more complex tasks such as managing finances and driving. The patient has a family history of dementia and has undergone genetic testing which revealed a pathogenic mutation in the GRN gene. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no history of seizures, cerebrovascular disorders, or other neurological diseases. MRI did not reveal any intra-cranial mass or hydrocephalus. The patient has no metal implants in their head or electronic implants.

A 35-year-old male with drug-resistant anterior temporal epilepsy is being evaluated for potential anterior temporal lobectomy. He has a nonverbal IQ of 90 (WAIS-IV). He has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders but has been experiencing visual disturbances. He is affiliated with social security and has given informed consent to participate in the study. He has undergone video-electroencephalography and magnetic resonance imaging to confirm his diagnosis. He is seeking to improve his quality of life through surgical intervention and is willing to undergo neuropsychological testing for this purpose.

A 28-year-old female with moderate to severe atrophic acne scars on the face, who is currently not pregnant or lactating, and has not used oral isotretinoin in the last six months. The patient has not undergone any facial treatments with laser or surgery in the last three months, and does not have any current or previous history of photosensitivity or photosensitive diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus or xeroderma pigmentosum. The patient has not used drugs that may induce hyperpigmentation, such as amiodarone, clofazimine, minocycline or chloroquine. The patient does not have only "ice pick" scars and does not have any coagulopathies or anticoagulating therapy. The patient has no history or current presence of hypertrophic scars or keloids, is not currently being treated with chemotherapy, radiotherapy or corticosteroids at high doses, does not have diabetes mellitus, and is able to understand the goals and risks of treatment.

An 11-year-old boy with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is experiencing clinically significant anxiety symptoms. His anxiety is affecting his daily activities including going to school and interacting with peers. His parents are concerned as his anxiety continues to increase despite previous interventions. The boy is on a stable medication regimen for a year and receives speech therapy and occupational therapy. His IQ score is above 70. He has no history of suicidal behaviors or other psychological disorders. He has had no previous treatment with sertraline or other SSRIs. He is comfortable with swallowing pills. The family speaks English. They are willing to participate in the study remotely through telehealth visits, and are available for the study duration.

A 42-year-old Chinese male diagnosed with advanced colon cancer was referred to the clinic by his oncologist. The patient has received standard chemotherapy and radiation therapy but without significant improvement. The patient has no history of cardiac disease but has a family history of hypertension. His ECOG-PS is 1. He has normal bone marrow, liver, and renal function. His life expectancy is estimated to be more than 3 months. He has no history of thrombotic or embolic events. The patient is willing to participate in an experimental treatment that is clinically and ethically acceptable. He is not currently experiencing any bleeding or other medical conditions that would exclude him from the study.

Pt is a 45yo M who presented to the emergency department with a 2-day history of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with corona virus disease 2019 and his interleukin-6 levels were elevated. He has signed the informed consent and is able to take medicine orally. He agrees to collect clinical samples and is not allergic to Favipiravir or tocilizumab. He has not received any specific antiviral drugs such as lopinavir / ritonavir, ribavirin, arbidol, chloroquine phosphate, hydroxychloroquine, and monoclonal antibodies within one week before admission. He is not in respiratory failure, shock or combined organ failure that requires ICU monitoring and treatment. He is predicted to have a chance of survival and is not in a deep coma that does not respond to supportive treatment measures within three hours of admission. His liver function tests and blood counts are within normal limits. He does not have a clear diagnosis of rheumatoid immunity, malignant tumors or related diseases. He is not taking any long-term oral anti-rejection drugs or immunomodulatory drugs. He has no history of hepatitis, tuberculosis, or bacterial and fungal infections. He has not undergone an organ transplant or has a history of mental disorders.

The patient is a healthy 22-year-old male with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 who does not smoke or consume grapefruit, grapefruit juice or grapefruit-containing products. He has not used any prescription drugs within 30 days and has not donated blood or blood products within 60 days. The patient has not been involved in any other investigational study within 30 days and has not consumed more than 300 mg of caffeine per day. He is willing to use a double barrier method of contraception, condom plus spermicide, during the study and for 4 weeks following initiation of dosing with study drug. His hemoglobin is 14.2 g/dL and his urine cotinine is <400 ng/mL. He is interested in participating in the study and is able to comply with the study requirements.

A 61-year-old retired accountant has a history of atrial fibrillation and was implanted with a St. Jude dual-chamber pacemaker 5 years ago. He also has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue lately, and his doctors have determined that his pacemaker leads need to be removed and replaced. He has no history of prior lead extraction. He is alert and oriented, with no signs of dementia. He is willing to participate in the post-market clinical study and has provided informed consent.

54-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of stage IV colorectal cancer with non-resectable primary tumor and/or metastases. The patient has received palliative standard systemic treatment with FOLFOX in combination with Bevacizumab and is currently under the respective treatment. Despite the treatment, the patient still has stable disease, partial response, or complete response according to routine imaging, and resection of tumor and/or metastases is still impossible. The patient has been tested positive for tumor-reactive T cells in the blood as detected by ex vivo IFN-γ EliSpot assay and classified as a response in a blood sample. The patient has an ECOG-performance status of 0 or 1 and adequate vein status at both cubital fossas for 16 G puncture. The patient is willing to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures and has provided written informed consent. The patient has a negative pregnancy test (if applicable) and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and three months last application of T cell therapy. The patient's laboratory parameters are within the specified ranges. The patient has no brain or leptomeningeal metastases, no previous malignancy within the past 5 years (except for curatively treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin, early gastrointestinal cancer treated by endoscopic resection, and/or in situ carcinoma of the cervix), no history of organ allograft or prior hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, no history of inflammatory bowel disease, no history of symptomatic autoimmune disease, no clinically significant cardiac disease (NYHA Class III or IV), no other serious illnesses, no serious intercurrent illness requiring hospitalization, no HIV and/or HBC/HCV positivity, no active infection or signs or symptoms of infection, and no history of hypersensitivity to the investigational medicinal product or any excipient present in the investigational medicinal product or to anti-coagulance auxiliary medicinal product (Heparin prophylaxis). The patient is not currently treated with immunosuppressive drugs (except for intermittent, anti-emetic steroid application during treatment with FOLFOX in combination with Bevacizumab) and has not received any approved anti-cancer therapy, live attenuated vaccine, or other investigational agent or participated in another interventional clinical trial within the specified time frames prior to enrolment.

A 56 year old male patient was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer 6 months ago. The patient received chemotherapy for 4 cycles and had documented disease control. The patient has a positive HLA-A*0201 status and TERT-positive NSCLC. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not received any prior treatment with cancer vaccines, immunotherapy, or investigational drugs in the last 4 weeks. The patient's medical history does not indicate any brain metastases or mixed small cell and NSCLC histologies.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who is generally healthy and up to date on her vaccinations. She attends school regularly and has not had any recent illnesses or hospitalizations. Her parents are interested in having her participate in a clinical trial for an A/H1N1 S-OIV (swine flu) vaccine. They are aware of the potential risks and benefits and have decided that the potential gain of vaccine protection outweighs any potential risks. The patient has never had a serious reaction to any vaccine in the past and has no known allergies to vaccine components. She has not received any other influenza vaccines within the past week, nor does she plan to receive any other influenza vaccines within a week before or after study vaccinations. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 58-year-old Caucasian female who presented with a history of weight loss, abdominal pain, and jaundice for the past month. She was evaluated with imaging studies, which revealed a mass in the biliary tract. Following biopsy, she was diagnosed with bile duct cancer. The patient has no significant medical history, and she has not received any prior treatment for cancer. She does not smoke, and she drinks alcohol occasionally. Her physical examination is notable for scleral icterus and jaundice. Laboratory studies showed an elevated bilirubin level of 3.5 mg/dL, elevated alkaline phosphatase level of 450 U/L, and a mildly elevated AST and ALT levels. Her CA 19-9 level was elevated at 500 U/ml. The patient's ECOG performance status score is 1, and her expected survival time is estimated to be longer than 3 months. The patient is willing to participate in the study and agrees to have tumor samples collected for further analysis.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been diagnosed with Ménétrier disease. He has been experiencing gastrointestinal symptoms that interfere with his daily life and is considering surgery. He has failed medical therapy that was given for six months. He does not have Helicobacter pylori infection. He is not pregnant or nursing and has a negative pregnancy test. He is fertile but agrees to use effective contraception during the study. He does not have NYHA class III-IV cardiovascular disease or clinically unstable pulmonary disease. He does not have any chronic disease requiring ongoing therapy for stabilization, including uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, malignancy, thyroid disease, hypertension, active infections requiring systemic antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals, uncontrolled seizure disorder, or active neurological disease. He does not have unstable coagulation disorders that require medical management. He is willing to participate in the study and receive cetuximab IV on days 1, 8, 15, and 22.

A 78-year-old female patient with a history of dementia has been experiencing increasingly problematic behavioral symptoms, including agitation and aggression towards caregivers and other residents in her skilled nursing facility. Despite attempts at behavioral interventions, the symptoms have persisted and there is concern for the safety of both the patient and others in the facility. The patient's family is also becoming overwhelmed and unsure of how to manage the situation. The patient is currently taking multiple medications for comorbidities, including hypertension and diabetes. The patient and her family have agreed to participate in a telemedicine-based intervention to receive recommendations from a multidisciplinary team of behavioral neurologists, social workers, advanced practice providers, primary medical team, and nurse coordinators to reduce the risk of unnecessary hospitalization and improve overall care for the patient.

Patient is a 35-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with a major depressive episode. He has a history of suicide attempt 3 years ago, where he ingested a large amount of prescription pills. He was hospitalized for 2 weeks and received psychotherapy and medication. He has been in therapy since then and has not made any further suicide attempts. He is currently taking an antidepressant medication and has no history of inflammatory diseases. He is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent. He is able to understand the nature, aims, and methodology of the study.

A 6-month-old baby boy was brought to the clinic by his parents due to concerns about his feeding. He has been exclusively formula-fed since birth and has been experiencing diarrhea, vomiting, and rash. He was diagnosed with cow's milk allergy and has been on an amino acid formula (Alfamino) for the past month, which has helped improve his symptoms. His parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the acceptability and tolerance of a new hypoallergenic amino acid formula with HMOs. The baby is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. The parents speak English fluently and are willing to comply with the study protocol. They have provided written informed consent for their baby to participate in the study.

Patient is a 25-year-old male from the United States who arrived in Manang, Nepal yesterday after flying to Kathmandu two days prior. He is an experienced hiker and has trekked at altitude before. He reports a headache and nausea that began this morning and has progressively worsened. He denies any chest pain, cough, or shortness of breath. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 120/80, a heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and an oxygen saturation of 92%. He has no past medical history of note and is not taking any medications.

45 y/o male who sustained a traumatic brain injury in a motor vehicle accident 6 months ago. He has been in a minimally conscious state since the accident, with no consistent signs of awareness or communication. He is receiving care at a rehabilitation center and does not require mechanical support. He has no history of scalp skin sores or skin damage at the electrode sites. He has no metallic implants in his face or skull, and he has not undergone craniectomy or cranioplasty. He has no evidence of auditory startle in clinical observations, and his brainstem auditory evoked potentials are intact. He is able to lay flat for prolonged periods of time and has no contraindications for MRI.

45-year-old male admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of septic shock. The patient has persistent hypotension despite aggressive fluid resuscitation and requires vasopressor therapy to maintain a mean arterial pressure above 65 mmHg. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient's blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg, with a heart rate of 110 beats per minute. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a pH of 7.25, pCO2 of 45 mmHg, pO2 of 70 mmHg, and HCO3 of 18 mmol/L. The patient requires arterial blood pressure and cardiac output monitoring to guide fluid and vasopressor therapy. The patient has no history of Raynaud disease, ulnar artery occlusion, or atherosclerosis. The Allen test is positive, indicating adequate collateral circulation from the ulnar artery. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets all inclusion criteria.

32F with a history of bipolar disorder type II, presents with symptoms of both depression and mania. The patient reports feeling very sad and hopeless, with a loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. Additionally, she has been experiencing racing thoughts, irritability, and difficulty sleeping. The patient has been on a stable dose of lamotrigine and quetiapine for the past year, but her symptoms have worsened in the past month. She denies any suicidal ideation or intent. Physical exam is unremarkable. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her symptoms and is willing to discontinue her current antidepressant medication if necessary. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using an oral contraceptive. She has no known allergies to medications.

The patient is a 2-month-old infant born at 38 weeks gestation without any significant maternal or perinatal history. The infant is not allergic to any vaccine components and has not received any immunoglobulin or blood product since birth. The family lives within 30 minutes of the commune health center and anticipates living in the study area for the next 22 months. The infant has not received any vaccines through the Expanded Programme of Immunization (EPI) program and is not planned to receive Quinvaxem (DTP-Hib-HBV). The infant has not had an acute infection, corticoid therapy or any symptoms that interfere with normal activities. The parent/legal guardian has provided written and signed informed consent for the infant to participate in the trial.

A 36-year-old female with a confirmed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis as per the revised 2017 criteria presented to the neurology clinic. She reported experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, muscle weakness, numbness, tingling, and difficulty with coordination. She had an EDSS score of 4.5, indicating significant disability but still able to walk without assistance. She had been previously treated with interferon beta-1a subcutaneous injection, but it was not effective in controlling her symptoms. Therefore, she was recommended to initiate treatment with ocrelizumab within the next 3 months. She expressed interest in participating in a clinical trial investigating symptom burden in patients treated with ocrelizumab, and was informed about the study eligibility criteria, procedure, and possible risks and benefits. She was able to read, write and comprehend English language, and provided written informed consent to participate. She had no history of significant medical comorbidities, untreated psychiatric illness, or active substance abuse disorder. She was not pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period or currently breastfeeding.

The patient is a 55-year-old Indian man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for 3 years. His HbA1c level at the screening visit is 8.2%. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and has been treated with basal insulin for the past 6 months. His current daily dose of basal insulin is 30 U. He is not taking any other glucose-lowering agents. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and mild diabetic retinopathy. His current medications include metoprolol, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He has no history of pancreatitis or gastrointestinal disease. He has not had any recent changes in his insulin regimen or dosage. He is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and is available for follow-up visits.

A 62-year-old female who underwent bilateral cataract surgery with intraocular lens implantation 6 months ago. She received Tecnis One monofocal lenses in both eyes. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and no other significant medical history. She currently wears glasses for reading and distance vision, but would prefer not to rely on them. Her best corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. She is interested in participating in a study investigating the ability of intraocular lenses to accommodate, as she would like to potentially reduce her dependence on glasses. She does not take any medications that would interfere with accommodation.

The patient is a 4-year-old girl from a low-income family who has been experiencing severe tooth decay for the past year. She has already been treated under general anesthesia for her dental issues and her parents are concerned about her oral health. The girl's parents struggle to provide her with proper dental care due to financial constraints and lack of knowledge about oral hygiene. The family has been referred to the pediatric dentistry department at Eastman Dental Institute in Stockholm County Council for further treatment. The family is offered to participate in a telephone-based case management intervention for caries prevention in children with severe early childhood caries. The intervention aims to provide support and education to the parents to help prevent further caries development in their child. The family is informed about the study and given written information. After an initial interview, the family is assigned to either the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive telephone-based support from a dental health coach who will provide information, support parental self-efficacy, and motivate the family to keep preventive measures that have been individually agreed upon. The control group will receive treatment as usual, but will also be followed up after 1 year for comparison with the intervention group. The girl's medical history is unremarkable and she does not have any learning disabilities.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a BMI of 32. He works as a software engineer and spends most of his day sitting at his desk. He admits to having a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in regular exercise. He reports that his diet consists mainly of convenience foods and takeaways, and he does not consume enough fruits and vegetables. He has tried various diets and exercise programs in the past but has not been able to sustain them. He has no history of smoking, substance abuse, excess alcohol intake, or any chronic medical conditions. He is not currently taking any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the use of stable isotope labeling to optimize the delivery of propionate to the colon as a potential treatment for obesity. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow a controlled diet during the study period.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes. He is in good overall health and is not currently taking any medications for any conditions. He has experienced some discomfort and mild pain in his eyes since the onset of his cataracts, which has gradually increased over time. He is scheduled to undergo routine cataract surgery in the upcoming weeks and has been invited to participate in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of loteprednol etabonate versus vehicle for the treatment of postoperative inflammation and pain following cataract surgery. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets the eligibility criteria including being at least 18 years of age and not having any severe ocular or medical conditions that may preclude study treatment or follow-up.

This is a 25 year-old female student who experiences periodic menstrual cramps accompanied by moderate levels of pain. She has no prior history of cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, or other chronic pain conditions. She is fluent in German and has a BMI within the range of 18.5 - 30 kg/m². She is available for the ten sessions of one-hour music listening in a laboratory within three consecutive weeks. She does not have any major mental disorders or substance dependence, and is not currently taking any pain drugs or psychotropic drugs. She is a non-smoker and is willing to refrain from smoking for 2.5 hours if needed.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who underwent a total hysterectomy and bilateral oophorectomy five years ago. She experiences hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. She was prescribed hormone replacement therapy (HRT) but discontinued it due to concerns about the risks associated with long-term use. She brushes her teeth twice a day and has good dental hygiene. She has no history of allergies or medical conditions that would contraindicate the use of estrogen. She has not used any vaginal estrogen products for the past three months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of estrogen in toothpaste as an alternative delivery method to HRT. She understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She is willing to have blood samples taken before, during, and after an eight-day course of once-daily toothpaste that is admixed with 0.5 mg estradiol.

The patient is a 19-year-old female who lives in the Khayelitsha community in Cape Town, South Africa. She dropped out of school six months ago and has not completed matric or N3 certificate. She has been using alcohol and drugs, including heroin and methamphetamine, at least weekly for the past 90 days. She reports having unprotected sex with a male partner in the last 90 days. She is concerned about her health and the risk of contracting HIV. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that will test a combination biobehavioral HIV prevention approach and provide referrals for care to resources. She is able to provide informed consent to participate in the study. She is currently not pregnant and does not have any other medical conditions. She is looking for help to reduce her drug and alcohol use and to learn how to protect herself from HIV infection.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with lumbar disc herniation and is scheduled for lumbar discectomy. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications regularly. The patient is sexually active and uses a medically accepted form of contraception. He has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to rThrombin or any of its components. The patient has not undergone any surgical procedures requiring cardiopulmonary bypass or involving the aortic arch in the past. He is not currently breastfeeding and has not received any experimental agents within the last 30 days. The patient understands the study requirements and has provided written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

A 35-year-old female patient presents with persistent thoracic pain for the past 6 months. The pain is described as a constant ache, with occasional sharp pains. The patient reports no history of trauma or injury to the area. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but has not experienced significant relief. The patient has no previous history of spinal arthritis, aortic aneurysm, collagenosis, or any other neuromuscular disease. She does not have any contraindications to spinal manipulative therapy of the thoracic spine. MRI of the thoracic spine shows no abnormalities. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate how different dosages of spinal manipulation could potentially improve her symptoms.

This is a 34-year-old active-duty service member who sustained a mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) while on deployment approximately 8 months ago. He continues to experience symptoms, such as headaches, dizziness, and occasional difficulty with balance, despite being outside of the acute stage according to the VA/DoD clinical practice guidelines. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating objective dual-task turning measures for use as rehabilitative outcomes and as tools for return-to-duty assessments in individuals with mTBI. He has no other medical history that could potentially explain balance deficits, and he does not currently meet criteria for substance-use disorder. He is able to communicate fluently in English.

54 yo M with chronic low back pain and bilateral leg radicular pain thought to be due to lumbar disc herniation and spinal stenosis. The patient has been on conservative treatment with physical therapy and NSAIDs with minimal relief. He has no history of allergies to local anesthetics or contrast medium, coagulopathy, local infection at the injection site, or systemic infection. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - Obesity (BMI 32.1) - Chronic Kidney Disease - Coronary Artery Disease (Stent placement in [**12-01**]) - Osteoarthritis - Depression - Chronic Pain Syndrome

As this study focuses on South Asian ethnicity, the patient should be of South Asian origin. The patient is a 45-year-old male of Pakistani origin who has been living in the UK for the past 15 years. He is a smoker and has a sedentary lifestyle due to his desk job. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father and two uncles experiencing heart attacks in their early 50s. The patient has been experiencing episodes of chest pain for the past six months and has not sought medical attention due to fear of the diagnosis. He is now willing to participate in the study and undergo necessary medical tests. He has no history of diabetes or hypertension and his BMI is 26.

A 63-year-old Caucasian man with a history of high blood pressure and benign prostatic hypertrophy complains of frequent urination and difficulty starting and stopping the urine stream. His PSA level was elevated, and a biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma of the prostate. The cancer was diagnosed within the past 9 months. The patient is asymptomatic and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status of 0. MRI shows that the prostate volume is 50cc. The patient is medically fit for brachytherapy, and his AUA score is 15. He is willing to complete quality of life questionnaires in English. He has signed the consent form and is willing to take precautions to prevent pregnancy while on the study. He has not received any prior or current androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) or alpha-reductase inhibitors (ARIs) within the past 90 days. He has not had radical surgery for carcinoma of the prostate, prior pelvic radiation, prior chemotherapy for prostate cancer, prior TURP, or prior cryosurgery of the prostate. There is no evidence of metastatic disease, and he does not have any serious active or co-morbid medical conditions, laboratory abnormalities, psychiatric illness, active or uncontrolled infections, or serious illnesses or medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study or being managed according to the protocol.

A 16-year-old female patient with a recent diagnosis of Hodgkin Lymphoma presents for her first cycle of anthracycline chemotherapy. She has no significant past medical history, and her family history is unremarkable. She is currently on no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. A physical examination is unremarkable except for a palpable cervical lymph node on the right side. Laboratory values are notable for a normal complete blood count, liver function tests, and renal function tests. She has no contraindications for the study, and her platelet count is 180,000. She is able to tolerate upper arm blood pressure inflation. She is English-speaking and is interested in participating in the study.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past year. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated most of the time. Her symptoms have been affecting her ability to work and socialize with friends and family. She has never been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, psychotic personality disorder, borderline personality disorder, and/or narcissistic personality disorder. She has no history of substance abuse/dependence or regular meditation practice. She is currently taking an anti-depressant medication with a stable regimen for the past month. Her IDS score is 26 and PHQ-9 score is 17, indicating moderate to severe depressive severity. The patient is fluent in English and is capable of providing informed consent, completing questionnaires, and understanding instructions. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for blood collection, including being generally healthy by self-report on the day of collection, no infections within two weeks prior to collection, and no known sickle cell disease.
