She weighs at least 110 pounds and has not donated blood for clinical or research purposes within the preceding eight weeks. She has not had more than one blood draw during the preceding week. The patient does not have a history of medical illness associated with possible changes in cerebral tissue or cerebrovasculature, neurologic abnormality, or significant head trauma, and does not have current suicidal ideation.

A 24-year-old male who recently tested positive for untreated urethral gonorrhea within the past 2 weeks is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. He must be willing to abstain from all sexual intercourse or use condoms until the study completion. The patient must not have any complications or systemic infections related to gonorrhea, and they should not have received any antibiotic treatment for their gonorrhea in the past. Additionally, they should not have used any systemic or intravaginal antibiotics within 7 days prior to the study drug administration. The patient should not have a history of significant intolerance or allergy to macrolide or cephalosporin antibiotics.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired woman who enjoys reading and spending time with her grandchildren. She lives at home with her husband and is able to walk 500m without the need of any walking aids. She is fluent in German and has a smartphone which she uses to read the news. She has been identified as "at risk" for functional decline by the risk screening instrument developed in the PreventIT project. She does not currently participate in an organised exercise class or engage in moderate-intensity physical activity for at least 150 minutes per week. She has no history of cognitive impairment or any of the medical conditions listed in the exclusion criteria. She is available for home visits for the following 6 weeks and is interested in participating in the PreventIT Trial in Young Older Adults to improve her overall health and prevent functional decline.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome (OSAS). He has recently started CPAP therapy and has been experiencing dry mouth as a side effect. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and exercises regularly. He has no known allergies and no history of immune disorders. He is able to attend visits at the research site and is willing to participate in the study. He understands and can sign the consent form. He does not have any open mouth sores, and is not currently using any other prophylactic mouthwashes. He is not pregnant, nursing, or on a low sodium diet. He is not currently on medication or treatment for xerostomia.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who speaks fluent English and is the primary caregiver for her mother who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. She has been taking care of her mother for the past 3 years and has been experiencing emotional distress, depression, and anxiety due to the demands of caregiving. She is currently not employed and spends most of her time providing care for her mother. Her mother's condition has been slowly deteriorating, and she finds it increasingly challenging to manage her mother's daily activities. She has been looking for support and resources to help her cope with the challenges of caregiving and improve her quality of life. Her past medical history is not significant for any other medical issues, and she is not currently taking any medications. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore new methods of support and assistance for caregivers like her.

The patient is a 40-year-old man who has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 32, which classifies him as obese. He works as an office manager and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. His diet consists mainly of fast food and processed snacks due to his busy work schedule. He has tried to lose weight in the past but has been unsuccessful in maintaining the weight loss. He does not have any physical impairments that would make the intervention unsafe, and he is committed to attending the assessment visits. He has not participated in any formal weight loss programs in the past year and has not lost more than 5% of his current body weight in the previous 6 months. The patient is a non-smoker and has no plans to move from the area. He is not currently participating in any other research studies and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old professional male or female cyclist with a maximal oxygen consumption of at least 55-60 mL⋅kg-1⋅min-1 or at least 4-5 L⋅min-1, depending on gender. The patient should not have any history of uncontrolled respiratory or cardiac disease, should not be pregnant, should not smoke, and should not have diabetes. The patient should be willing to participate in a controlled yet sport-specific exercise protocol and be comfortable with the administration of salbutamol.

A 35-year-old male suffered from a severe burn injury while cooking at home. He has 40% TBSA of second-degree burn on his torso, arms, and legs. He has no history of any allergies, nor is he currently taking any medications. He has no prior surgical history and has never participated in any clinical trials before. He is currently not pregnant or lactating. He is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study-related procedures.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II ovarian cancer. She underwent surgery to remove the tumor and is currently undergoing chemotherapy. Her medical history includes high blood pressure and hyperlipidemia, which are well controlled with medication. She has never smoked and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has social insurance and is willing to participate in the study. She has a tumor available for TP53 characterization and is able to undergo blood collection. She has signed the informed consent form and is approved by the relevant authorities to participate in the study.

The patient is a 22-year-old female medical student who has been experiencing symptoms of depression for the past 6 months. She reports feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated most of the time, with a loss of interest in activities she used to enjoy. She also has difficulty sleeping, with frequent nightmares and restless sleep. She reports feeling anxious and worried about her academic performance and future career prospects. She denies any history of drug use or psychiatric disorders, and has not received any other psychological treatment recently. She has never attempted suicide and has a low score on the suicide risk scale. She is currently enrolled in the Autonomous University of Baja California at the Faculty of Medicine and Psychology and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive the Behavioral Activation Therapy.

55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for 10 years presents with a right foot ulcer and fever. The patient reports having noticed the ulcer about a week ago and it has been gradually increasing in size. He has been treating it at home with over-the-counter antibiotics and wound dressings, but the fever prompted him to seek medical attention. The patient has a history of peripheral neuropathy and poor glycemic control. Upon examination, the ulcer is located on the plantar surface of the right foot and is approximately 3 cm in diameter with surrounding erythema and edema. The patient is admitted to the hospital for further evaluation and treatment of a moderate diabetic foot infection. Blood work is ordered and shows an elevated CRP level. The patient is enrolled in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of inflammatory biomarkers to diagnose and monitor diabetic foot osteomyelitis. Bone cultures are obtained and show a positive result for osteomyelitis. The patient's CRP level is monitored throughout treatment and follow-up for resolution of infection.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 20 years. He was diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy during a routine eye exam. His visual acuity is currently 20/100 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye. He has not received any previous laser treatment for diabetic retinopathy. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is currently well-controlled with medication. He is otherwise in good health and is able to comply with the study requirements.

A 50-year-old male patient presents with a history of liver transplantation for chronic hepatitis C genotype 1, which was diagnosed and treated 8 years ago. The patient is currently stable and has not received any treatment for hepatitis C following transplantation. The patient's liver function tests are within normal limits, and there is no evidence of significant liver disease in addition to hepatitis C. The patient has no history of decompensated liver disease. The patient is willing to have a liver graft biopsy during the screening period if required. The patient has no co-infection with human immunodeficiency virus or hepatitis B virus. The patient has no active malignant disease or history of malignant disease within the past 5 years, including hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient is willing to use two effective methods of birth control from screening until 6 months (if female) or 7 months (if male) after the last dose of ribavirin. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of telaprevir in combination with Peg-IFN-alfa-2a and ribavirin for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1 in stable liver transplant patients.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) after presenting with hematuria. He underwent a transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) and was found to have Ta high-grade urothelial carcinoma. He received BCG induction therapy but failed to achieve a tumor-free state after 2 courses of BCG therapy. He is not a candidate for radical cystectomy due to underlying medical conditions. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus for which he takes lisinopril and metformin, respectively. He denies any history of alcohol or tobacco use. He has a Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) of 90 and is able to perform all activities of daily living independently. He has no history of psoriasis or any other skin conditions. He is willing to use two methods of birth control as his wife is of childbearing age. Urine and blood pregnancy tests are negative. He has satisfactory bladder function and is able to retain instillate for at least 1 hour.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing chronic cough and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. He has a history of cystic fibrosis and has been treated for recurrent lung infections in the past. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to pneumonia. He reports that his symptoms have worsened in the past few weeks and he has been experiencing chest pain. He has not noticed any triggers for his symptoms and has not recently traveled or been exposed to any new environments. His vital signs are stable and his physical examination reveals wheezing and crackles in his lungs. His chest x-ray shows infiltrates in both lungs. His total IgE level is elevated, but his specific IgE levels for common allergens are negative. He has been referred to the chest department for diagnosis of allergic pulmonary Aspergillosis.

Maria is a 42-year-old female who is morbidly obese. She weighs 310 pounds and has a BMI of 45. She has been struggling with her weight for many years and has tried various diets and exercise programs without success. She has a medical history of hypertension and diabetes, which are both well-controlled with medication. Maria has been scheduled to undergo elective laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery as a weight loss intervention. She has no history of COPD and is not dependent on home oxygen. She is not pregnant or nursing and has not participated in another clinical trial in the past 30 days. Her skin is clear and does not have any condition that would interfere with the application of the forehead sensor. Maria will be asked to participate in the study to determine the incidence of hypoventilation and hypercapnea as measured by transcutaneous pCO2 monitoring in post-surgical bariatric patients. The study will require an overnight admission to Beaumont/Royal Oak Hospital. Maria will be required to give her consent to participate in the study.

Pt is a 42yo M with a BMI of 32, diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus managed with metformin monotherapy. He has an HbA1c of 7.5% at screening. He is sexually active with his wife and they use condoms as their contraceptive method. He is willing and able to self-inject study drug for the duration of the study. He has no history of pancreatitis or pancreatic abnormalities, inflammatory bowel disease or other severe diseases that would affect the upper gastrointestinal tract. He has no significant hepatic disease, renal impairment, hypertension or any clinically important abnormalities in rhythm, conduction or morphology of the resting 12-lead ECG. He has no history of neoplastic disease, substance dependence or psychiatric disorders requiring treatment with medication. He has not donated blood within 1 month of screening.

A 56 year old woman was diagnosed with high-risk primary gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after undergoing surgery to remove the tumor. The tumor size was 12 cm in maximum dimension and there was no evidence of tumor rupture. The patient's ECOG/Zubrod performance status is 1. The tumor was confirmed to be GIST and stain positive for the Kit receptor tyrosine kinase on immunohistochemistry. The patient has had a chest x-ray and a post-operative CT scan with IV and PO contrast of the abdomen and pelvis within the past 28 days. The patient's creatinine, WBC, platelet, total bilirubin, AST, and ALT levels all meet the eligibility criteria. The patient has not undergone post-operative chemotherapy, radiation therapy or investigational treatment. The patient has not received prior therapy with STI571. The patient is not taking full dose warfarin. The patient has no active infection requiring antibiotics within the past 14 days. The patient is not breastfeeding and has no New York Heart Association class 3 or 4 cardiac disease. The patient is willing to provide a signed and dated written informed consent prior to registration and any study related procedures.

The patient is a 52-year-old female with a history of hypertension for the last 5 years. She has been taking Aliskiren 300 mg for the past 2 years, which has helped control her blood pressure. She has a family history of hypertension and heart disease. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. Her BMI is 26 kg/m2. She is currently not taking any other medications for her hypertension. She has no history of diabetes, heart failure, angina pectoris, or stroke. She is not pregnant or nursing. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to follow the high and low sodium diet requirements.

72 year old man who is currently living independently in his community. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but these are well-controlled with medication. He has no significant history of falls, but reports feeling anxious about falling. He has a Standardized Mini Mental Test score of 27 and is able to communicate effectively. He does not have any musculoskeletal or neurological disorders that would affect his balance, and he is not currently taking any medications that may affect his balance. He has agreed to participate in this study voluntarily.

A 13-year-old male patient has just been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He presents with fatigue, weakness, and a fever of unknown origin. A complete blood count revealed pancytopenia with blasts comprising 45% of the bone marrow. The patient has no significant past medical history and has never been hospitalized before. He has no known allergies and is not taking any medications. His family history is negative for any hematologic malignancies. He lives with his parents and two younger siblings. He attends middle school and is in the 8th grade. He enjoys playing video games and basketball with his friends. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. His BMI is within normal limits. The patient and his parents have provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty reading and focusing on near objects due to a cataract in her right eye. She has no other ocular comorbidities that would compromise the primary outcome of the study. She is a good candidate for a presbyopic intraocular lens and is interested in potentially receiving the ReSTOR lens in her right eye with a monofocal or phakic lens in her left eye. She does not have cataracts in her left eye.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing low back pain for the past 6 months. The pain started after a heavy lifting incident at work. He works as a construction worker and has to lift heavy objects on a daily basis. He has tried physiotherapy and various pain medications with little improvement. He has not undergone any prior surgery for his back pain. He has no history of significant medical illnesses, but does have a history of smoking. On physical examination, he has tenderness in the lower back and decreased range of motion. His MRI shows a herniation at the L4-L5 level. He is interested in the Disc FX procedure as an alternative to traditional surgery. He has received detailed information about the procedure and has consented to participate in this prospective observational trial.

Patient is a 28-year-old healthy male from the United States who works as a software engineer. He has no significant past medical history or drug allergies. He does not smoke or use any tobacco products and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and has not taken any prescription medications within the last 14 days or over-the-counter medications within the last 7 days. His laboratory results are within normal limits, including a negative hepatitis panel and negative HIV antibody screen. He is willing to use adequate contraceptive methods throughout the study. He is able to comprehend and willing to sign an Informed Consent Form (ICF).

A 23-year-old female college student presented with complaints of chronic anxiety, which has been affecting her academic performance, social life and daily activities. She reported experiencing excessive worry, restlessness, and difficulty concentrating. She also reported experiencing physical symptoms such as muscle tension, headache, and difficulty sleeping. She denied any history of major psychiatric disorders but reported having occasional panic attacks. She is currently not on any medication for anxiety. She has a good support system from her family and friends. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help her better manage her anxiety. She is willing to try mindfulness-based relaxation techniques and is open to the use of non-intrusive biofeedback devices to enhance her self-regulation capabilities. She is a full-time student with no history of Attention Deficit Hyperactive Disorder.

This clinical trial does not involve patients as it is focused on cellular research. Participants in this trial will be healthy individuals willing to donate 50mls of whole blood for stem cell research. The study aims to assess the effect of ground based microgravity on co-cultured vascular cell types, and does not involve any medical treatment or intervention for patients.

Unfortunately, a patient description cannot be generated for this clinical trial as it is an observational study that does not involve direct interaction with patients. The study aims to examine the variability between diverse methods to measure creatinine in plasma and urine in a heterogenous group of Caucasian people with and without renal function loss. Therefore, the eligibility criteria only include patients who are over 18 years and presenting at the laboratory facility for a 24-hour creatinine clearance or undergoing renal replacing therapy by means of hemo-/peritoneal dialysis that had a KT/V appointment between May 2010 - January 2011. Patients under 18 years are excluded from the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) and has undergone treatment in the past. He has a high-risk cytogenetic feature, specifically the presence of 17p deletion. The patient experiences fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work and most daily activities but may need to rest occasionally. The patient has not received any treatment with ibrutinib or any other drug that specifically inhibits Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). The patient has not undergone any major surgery, chemotherapy, or immunotherapy within the last 21 days, and there is no evidence of hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, or known HIV infection. The patient has not undergone autologous hematologic stem cell transplant within 3 months of study entry, and has not experienced transformation of CLL to aggressive Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma (NHL) (Richter's transformation). The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of ublituximab in combination with ibrutinib for high-risk CLL patients.

47-year-old Egyptian female diagnosed with primary knee osteoarthritis (OA), with a body mass index (BMI) of 39.5 kg/m2, was referred to the Rheumatology and Rehabilitation Department at Mansoura University for evaluation. She has no previous history of exercise and has been leading a sedentary lifestyle. The patient reports occasional knee pain and stiffness that interferes with her daily activities. She has been diagnosed with hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient denies any other medical conditions contraindicating moderate aerobic exercising, such as ischemic cardiomyopathy, chronic lung disease, asthma, uncontrolled hypertension, neuromuscular or lower extremity conditions, or any other medical condition that could prevent them from floor walking as upset affecting movement of the pelvic arch or pace, history of previous hip or knee surgery, periarticular fractures, or lower limb injuries. She has not had any recent joint injections or recent joint infections. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is able to understand and follow commands. She is able to walk independently and has no neurological deficits. The patient underwent bilateral AP standing x-ray to verify the presence and degree of human knee OA, and X-rays confirmed the diagnosis of knee OA of KL grade ≥2 in both knees. The patient's WOMAC score was collected at baseline.

The patient is a 62-year-old Caucasian woman who was a light smoker in the past but quit smoking 5 years ago. She was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer that has relapsed after prior chemotherapy. She has no history of brain metastasis or squamous cell histology. Her performance status is 1. Her recent blood tests show ANC of 2,000/mm³, platelet count of 120,000/mm³, ALT and AST of 1.5 times ULN, alkaline phosphatase of 2 times ULN, and bilirubin of 1.2 mg/dL. Her creatinine clearance is 65 mL/min. She is not pregnant and has negative pregnancy test results. She is currently using a barrier contraception method. She does not have any cardiac disease or hypertension, and has not experienced any thrombolic or embolic events in the past 6 months. She does not have any active clinically serious infections, wounds, or fractures. She has no known allergies to sorafenib tosylate or any other medications. She has not undergone any major surgery or open biopsy in the past 4 weeks. She has not been treated with sorafenib tosylate before and is not concurrently taking St. John's wort or rifampin. She is not on concurrent anticoagulation therapy.

A 45-year-old male with a history of lower back pain and mild hip discomfort was referred for an MRI of the lumbar spine and right hip. He has no known history of neoplastic, inflammatory or hematologic diseases, osteoporosis or osteopenia, or hip orthopedic hardware. He has no history of chronic renal failure or hyperparathyroidism. He is not pregnant and not a prisoner. He has given informed consent for the MRI examination and is able to cooperate. He has no metallic foreign body intraorbital and no absolute contraindication to 3Tesla MRI. He will require gadolinium injection for the clinical needs. The MR images of his hip and lumbar spine appear normal.

Patient A is a 45-year-old female who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is currently undergoing usual care treatment for breast cancer and is willing to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of an individualized additional complementary medicine treatment in addition to usual care. She is able to communicate in German or Italian language and has not received any complementary treatment at the Hospital Meran in the last 6 months. She understands that if she is randomized into the usual care group, she will have to refrain from complementary treatment for 6 months. She is willing to provide informed consent and participate in the study.

A 32-year-old male with a history of Hodgkin's lymphoma presents for VATET for resection of anterior mediastinal mass. He has a history of hypertension and is well controlled on lisinopril. He is a non-smoker and denies any shortness of breath, chest pain, or palpitations. Physical exam is unremarkable except for a palpable mass in the anterior mediastinum. Pre-operative labs show a hemoglobin of 11.7 g/dL and a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL. The patient is otherwise healthy and is classified as an ASA II. He has no known allergies to medications. The patient denies any alcohol or illicit drug use. He gives informed consent for the procedure and enrolls in the study.

The patient is a 63-year-old male with a history of hypertension and ischemic heart disease. He was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath and chest pain. The patient was treated with nitroglycerin and started on vasoactive drugs due to hemodynamic instability. The patient's blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg and heart rate is 110 beats per minute. The patient is alert and oriented, but complains of chest pain, shortness of breath, and dizziness. The patient has arterial and pulmonary catheters in place for hemodynamic monitoring. The patient is also receiving continuous oxygen therapy. The patient is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. The patient has no known allergies. The patient's laboratory tests show elevated cardiac enzymes and troponin. The patient is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was previously diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She has received treatment with EC145 (vintafolide) as part of an Endocyte-sponsored, IRB-approved clinical trial. Her last evaluation showed stable disease, and no more than 10 weeks have elapsed since that evaluation. She is currently experiencing no symptoms related to her cancer. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and her bone marrow reserve, hepatic, and renal function are adequate. She has no history of receiving any investigational treatment or other systemic therapy directed at controlling cancer since the subject's last dose on the parent EC145 study. She is not pregnant and has tested negative on a serum pregnancy test. She is willing to practice contraceptive methods as she is of childbearing potential.

This is a 27-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her 25th week of pregnancy. She has been experiencing chronic low back pain for over 3 months without any irradiation for her knees. She has not been under medication or physical therapy treatment for her low back pain in the last three months. She has been performing physical activity consistent with her pregnancy and has normal conditions of responsiveness, cognition, and speaking. She has been enrolled in a clinical trial to assess the effect of an intervention program based on the functionality and trunk neuromuscular activity and postural control in pregnant women with low back pain. The trial will involve a 6-week intervention program with lumbar stabilization exercises and clinical orientations. The participant will be evaluated before and after the intervention using electromyography measurements, force platform parameters, and clinical outcomes such as pain intensity, perception of disability, and fear and avoidance. The participant will be randomized into two groups: G1, which will perform therapy with specific exercises for lumbar stabilization, and G2, which will perform conventional therapy including stretching of lower limbs and trunk. The intervention will follow the CONSORT recommendations for randomized controlled trials. The participant will not be blind to the study due to the characteristic of the exercises that often reflect to the improvement of the symptoms. The participant meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any of the exclusion criteria for the trial.

A 47-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with HER2 positive metastatic breast cancer. She had a lumpectomy and radiation therapy for breast cancer 5 years ago. She is married with two children and works part-time as a teacher. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has no known allergies and is not on any medications. She has no history of smoking or alcohol abuse. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is willing to use a highly-effective contraception method during the study treatment and for at least 7 months after the last dose of study treatment.

A 45 year old man was diagnosed with chronic phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) 2 years ago and has been receiving nilotinib as second-line therapy for the last 8 months. He has achieved a complete cytogenetic response (CCyR) and has not undergone treatment for any other form of cancer in the past 5 years. He is fluent in English and has provided informed consent. He has not received treatment with another tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) other than nilotinib. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 (Karnofsky ≥60%) and normal organ and marrow function as defined in the study protocol. He is willing to use adequate contraception (barrier method of birth control) for the duration of study participation and 4 months after completion of Ruxolitinib and nilotinib administration. He understands the study protocol and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. He has not had a prolonged QT interval (QTc >480) and has no other uncontrolled intercurrent illness. He is not HIV-positive and is not currently receiving any drugs considered to be strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors. He is eligible for enrollment in the study.

A 9-month-old male infant was born at 30 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 1.2 kg. He spent 3 months in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to respiratory distress syndrome and sepsis. He was discharged home with oxygen support and was followed up in a high-risk clinic. At 8 months of age, he developed cough, fever, and tachypnea. He was diagnosed with bronchiolitis and was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) of Vietnam National Children's Hospital. He required non-invasive ventilation for 3 days and was discharged home with supplemental oxygen. His follow-up appointments showed persistent cough and wheeze, requiring frequent hospitalizations for respiratory illnesses. His parents are both healthy and non-smokers. He has no siblings. He is up to date with his vaccinations according to the national immunization schedule. His current weight is 4 kg.

A 9-month-old infant was brought to the clinic by his parents due to difficulty breathing and wheezing for the past 2 days. Upon examination, the infant was found to have increased respiratory rate, nasal flaring, and intercostal retractions. The infant was diagnosed with moderate to severe bronchiolitis based on the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) criteria and a Respiratory Distress Assessment Instrument (RDAI) score of 7. The infant has no significant past medical history and has not received any bronchodilator or steroid treatments prior to the clinic visit. The infant has no congenital heart disease, immunocompromise, upper airway obstruction, chronic lung disease, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, basilar skull fracture, facial traumas, or craniofacial malformations. The parents have consented to the infant's participation in the study and are willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 16-year-old female presents with a history of relapsed CD19+ leukemia. She has previously undergone chemotherapy and an allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT), but unfortunately her leukemia has recurred. Her most recent bone marrow biopsy showed 0.05% disease involvement. She is currently not receiving any treatment for her leukemia. She weighs 50 kg and has a BMI of 20. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has no history of HIV, Hepatitis B or C. Her Lanksy performance status score is 70. She has no active GVHD and has not been on immunosuppressive therapy for 4 weeks prior to enrollment. She has recovered from the acute toxic effects of prior chemotherapy and has not received any systemic corticosteroids within 7 days of enrollment. Her serum creatinine, total bilirubin, and ALT are within normal range. She has an ejection fraction of 55% by echocardiogram. She has an absolute lymphocyte count of 150 cells/ul. She has no active CNS dysfunction. She is willing to follow effective contraception measures for 12 months after T cell infusion. She is capable of tolerating the apheresis procedure. She and her parents/legal guardian have agreed to participate in long-term follow-up for up to 15 years.

The patient is an 18-year-old American male who was previously diagnosed with Ewing's sarcoma, a rare type of cancer that affects bones or the soft tissue around them. The patient underwent initial chemotherapy treatment with or without surgery, which resulted in complete remission or very good partial remission (at least 50% reduction in measurable tumor burden). However, the cancer has recurred and has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic). The patient has not received any prior dose-limiting irradiation to any organ site. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%, indicating that the patient is able to carry out normal activities but may need some assistance with more strenuous activities. The patient's life expectancy is greater than 3 months. The patient has a granulocyte count of at least 1,000/mm3 and a platelet count of at least 100,000/mm3. The patient's bilirubin level is less than 2.0 mg/dL and creatinine clearance is greater than 50% of normal. The patient is HIV-negative and not pregnant.

8-year-old male with a history of severe hemophilia A with no prior exposure to blood components or factor VIII replacement products is being considered for enrollment in this clinical trial. The patient has had multiple bleeding episodes, including joint bleeds, and has required frequent factor VIII infusions for treatment. The patient's legally authorized representative has been informed of the purpose and risks of the study and has provided signed and dated informed consent. The patient meets the weight requirement of at least 3.5 kg at the time of screening, and the hemophilia A diagnosis has been confirmed with less than 1 IU/dL (<1%) endogenous FVIII documented in the medical record. The patient has no history of positive inhibitor testing or hypersensitivity reactions associated with any rFVIIIFc administration. The patient has no other coagulation disorders in addition to hemophilia A, and there are no concurrent clinically significant major diseases that would make the patient unsuitable for enrollment. The patient is not currently receiving systemic treatment with chemotherapy and/or other immunosuppressant drugs.

56F with newly diagnosed extensive stage small cell lung cancer. She underwent a CT scan which showed a large mass in the right lung with mediastinal lymph node involvement. She is scheduled to receive front-line platinum-based chemotherapy with cisplatin and etoposide. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no history of tobacco use, but she has a family history of lung cancer. The patient is able to understand and sign an institutional review board (IRB)-approved informed consent document. She has no pacemaker or defibrillator and is not currently on any chemotherapy or surgery in the last 6 months. She has no major chronic diseases known to adversely affect phase angle. Her body mass index (BMI) is within the range of 18 to 29. She is willing to follow the protocol requirements and is not pregnant.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing urinary burning, urgency, and dysuria along with pelvic pain and a fever of 38°C. She has not taken any antibiotics for this condition before and has not had an episode of pyelonephritis in the past 6 months. She is not pregnant or lactating, has no known immunodeficiency or allergies to antibiotics, and is not taking concomitant corticosteroids or immunosuppressive therapy. She has not had any tendon or epilepsy related issues in the past. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of 5 days versus 10 days of antibiotic treatment for uncomplicated acute pyelonephritis.

47-year-old male patient with a diagnosis of pancreatic cancer located in the head of the pancreas is scheduled to undergo pancreaticoduodenectomy. The patient does not have any significant medical history other than the cancer diagnosis. The patient has not used any gastrointestinal prokinetic medication, antipsychotic medication or antidepressants within the last 4 weeks. The patient has not used Japanese herbal (Kampo) medicines within the last 4 weeks. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent before initiation of study-related procedures.

A 45-year-old male with a long-standing history of ADPKD was referred to Asan Medical Center for kidney transplantation. His medical history includes hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and moderate proteinuria. The patient has no history of intracranial aneurysm. Upon physical examination, the patient is alert and oriented, and his vital signs are within normal limits. His abdomen is distended with multiple palpable renal masses. Blood and urine samples were collected for routine pre-transplantation evaluation. The patient was deemed eligible for kidney transplantation and bilateral nephrectomies were performed as a part of the procedure. Arterial tissues from the iliac and renal arteries were collected for analysis of vascular characteristics and gene mutation associated with ADPKD. The aim of this study is to evaluate the mechanisms associated with intracranial aneurysm occurrence in ADPKD patients.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with malignant melanoma three months ago. She underwent surgery to remove the tumor, but further imaging revealed the presence of metastasis to her liver. She underwent chemotherapy for four weeks, but due to the side effects, the treatment was discontinued. She is currently seeking alternative treatment options and has been referred to this clinical trial. She is otherwise healthy, with an ECOG score of 0 and a life expectancy of over three months. Her blood work shows normal values for WBC, ANC, PLT, and Hb, and her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. She has no history of autoimmune diseases or herpes virus infection. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who recently suffered a humeral fracture in a work-related accident. He has no other significant medical history and has no known allergies. The fracture was diagnosed using X-rays and confirmed by a CT scan. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no pre-existing neurological or musculoskeletal conditions. The patient has been advised to undergo surgical intervention using the NovaLign™ Intramedullary Fixation System within 14 days of injury. The patient has a fully functioning contralateral limb and is skeletally mature. The patient is willing to undergo surgery and participate in the post-market clinical study.

A 35 yo M who sustained a traumatic brain injury in a motor vehicle accident and is currently receiving inpatient rehabilitation services at Quality Living, Inc. in Omaha, NE. He is fluent in English and is scheduled to receive post-acute rehabilitation services either through telerehabilitation or at an outpatient facility after his discharge from Quality Living, Inc. He is interested in participating in the study to help further research on the effects of different types of rehabilitation services on the well-being and quality of life of people with traumatic brain injury.

A 35-year-old female patient with a body mass index (BMI) of 35 kg/m2 is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She is otherwise healthy and does not have any significant medical history. She does not smoke and does not consume alcohol. She is able to communicate well in English. She has no difficulty lying flat and is not pregnant. Her airway assessment revealed no features suggestive of difficult mask ventilation or difficult intubation. She has no significant respiratory, cardiac or gastrointestinal diseases. Her hemoglobin level is within normal limits. She has no known allergies to any of the agents used for induction of general anesthesia in the study. She has no neuromuscular disorders and does not have any clinical or radiological evidence of increased intracranial pressure. She has good collateral circulation to the hand and is able to tolerate the apneic period. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

Patient is a 16-month-old male infant from Ecuador who was recently admitted to the Children's Hospital with severe pneumonia. The infant has a history of recurrent respiratory infections since birth and was born at full term with no significant medical history. The infant's parents are both farmers and have limited access to nutritious foods, and they report that the infant is breastfed but also consumes a limited variety of solid foods. The infant's current symptoms include coughing, difficulty breathing, and fever. The infant's physical examination is remarkable for tachypnea with a respiratory rate of 50 breaths per minute, chest retractions, and oxygen saturation of 89% on room air. The infant's laboratory studies are remarkable for a low baseline plasma zinc level of 60 micrograms/dl. The infant's parents have provided written informed consent for the infant's participation in the Zinc as Adjunct to Treatment of Pneumonia clinical trial.

A 28-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia and cannabis addiction seeks treatment for his drug addiction. He has been diagnosed with schizophrenia since the age of 20 and has a history of hospitalizations for psychotic episodes. He has been using marijuana regularly for the past 3 years and has tried to quit multiple times with little success. He is currently taking olanzapine to manage his schizophrenia symptoms. He does not have any medical conditions that would prevent him from taking clozapine. He has no history of seizures or granulocytopenia. He is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is willing to use contraception if necessary.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who enjoys hiking and has previously hiked in high altitude areas. He is planning a hiking trip to the Himalayas and is looking for ways to prevent acute mountain sickness (AMS). He has experienced mild AMS symptoms in the past, such as headaches and nausea, and wants to avoid these symptoms during his upcoming trip. He is currently not taking any medications and has no known medical conditions. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that is looking at an over-the-counter device (Theravent) worn while sleeping to reduce AMS symptoms.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has a history of COPD and has been diagnosed with pneumonia. He was prescribed Ceftriaxone 1g once daily for 7 days. Despite taking the medication as prescribed, he still experiences shortness of breath, cough, and fever. He has no allergies to any medications, and his other medications include Spiriva and albuterol inhalers for his COPD. He does not smoke but has a history of smoking for 20 years in the past. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are well controlled with medication. He lives alone and is retired. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He agrees to undergo a flexible bronchoscopy to determine if the antibiotic concentration in his lungs is sufficient to treat his pneumonia. He signs the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

Maria is a 28-year-old female who works as a nurse. She has been experiencing chronic knee pain for the past year, and after an MRI, she was diagnosed with a torn ACL. She has a BMI of 23kg/m2 and is in good physical health. She has no history of allergies to local anesthetics or any other medications. She has not had any knee surgery in the past. She is scheduled to undergo arthroscopic knee ligament reconstruction. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the SOFT block technique.

Patient is a 7-year-old child with a physician-diagnosed asthma for at least a year. The child has had at least one acute exacerbation of asthma in the past 12 months that required a visit to the emergency department, hospitalization or an unscheduled office visit for acute care and/or a course of oral steroids. The child is currently taking daily controller medications or symptoms consistent with persistent asthma. The family has access to a phone and can speak English. The child does not have any other disease that requires regular monitoring by the pediatrician, and there is no sibling already enrolled in the study. The child's primary asthma provider is a community pediatrician.

The patient is a 45 year old male with a history of coronary heart disease and a myocardial scar tissue verified by CMR. He has recently undergone the implantation of an ICD. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle due to his work demands. He has a family history of heart disease and is a current smoker, consuming 10 cigarettes per day. He has no history of depression or anxiety. He has not undergone any revascularization procedure or arrhythmia ablation following the ICD implantation. He does not have long QT-syndrome, Brugada syndrome, WPW syndrome, drug-induced torsades, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, right ventricular cardiomyopathy, dilated cardiomyopathy, aortic stenosis, mitral valve prolapse, anomalous origin of coronary arteries, myocardial bridging or ongoing myocarditis. He is interested in participating in an exercise program to improve his quality of life and overall health.

The patient is a 32 year old woman who is scheduled for an elective cesarean section due to a breech presentation. She has had a previous cesarean section and is in good health with no chronic medical conditions. Her BMI is within normal limits and she has no history of prolonged rupture of membranes, diabetes, hypertension or anemia. She is not on any corticosteroid therapy or immunosuppressive medications. The patient has no known allergies to betadine or any other medications. The study will involve randomization to one of two groups, with one group receiving subcutaneous swabbing of the cesarean section wound with povidone iodine and the other group receiving no swabbing. The patient will receive a single dose of prophylactic antibiotic during the induction of anesthesia. She will be followed up during her hospital stay and at outpatient clinic visits one week and one month after delivery for surgical site complications which will be evaluated by the researcher. The study aims to determine the efficacy of subcutaneous swabbing of cesarean section wounds with povidone iodine to prevent postoperative wound infection.

The patient is a 45-year-old female diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 5 years. She has been on methotrexate (MTX) for the past 6 months but has had an inadequate response to the treatment. Her previous medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no other significant medical conditions. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Her BMI is 25. She has 8 tender and 6 swollen joints out of the 68/66 joint count. Her DAS28 4v-CRP score is 4.5, and her CRP level is 1.2 mg/dL. She is positive for anti-CCP2 antibodies. She is currently not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the next six months. She is willing to use contraception during the study. She has not participated in any clinical trials involving investigational drugs for RA in the past three months.

A 56-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with persistent high LDL cholesterol levels despite maximum doses of statins and other lipid-modifying therapies. The patient has no prior history of treatment with PCSK9 antibodies and is scheduled to receive Alirocumab as part of their clinical routine. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or under the age of 18. They are able to undergo magnetic resonance imaging of the carotid artery.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who sustained partial and full thickness burns over 30% of his total body surface area in a house fire. He was initially admitted to the hospital for burn wound care and received multiple skin grafts. Due to the extensive nature of his injuries, the patient was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for close monitoring and management of his condition. He has been in the ICU for 10 days and has been intubated for respiratory support since admission. The patient has been receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics to prevent infection and has undergone multiple surgical procedures for wound debridement and skin grafting. His medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril, and he has no known drug allergies. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 30-year-old female patient with a history of bronchial asthma is seeking treatment for her symptoms. She reports experiencing shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest tightness frequently, especially during the night and early morning. Her symptoms are mild to moderate, and she has not taken any antiasthmatic treatment in the past week. She has no history of other significant medical conditions, and she is not taking any medications. Her pulmonary function test shows Raw ≤ 5 cm H2O/l/s. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effect of fenoterol metered dose inhaler with disodium cromoglycate (DSCG) metered dose inhaler on the lymphocyte β2-receptor population.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is a study focused on assessing the impact of COVID-19 on pediatric dental practice among a group of pediatric dentists in Egypt. Participants in this study are Egyptian pediatric dentists with at least a Master's degree and their work place should be located in Egypt. The exclusion criteria include participants who refuse to participate in the study.

52F with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and occasional headaches is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effects of ginseng and ginkgo on cognitive function and enzymes that process drugs. She is currently taking amlodipine and atorvastatin, but is otherwise drug-free and a non-smoker. She has no history of drug, tobacco, or alcohol abuse or chronic physical complaints. Her laboratory test values are within acceptable range. She is interested in exploring the potential benefits of herbal medicines and is willing to participate in a double-blind, randomized, prospective study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained a severe traumatic brain injury. He was admitted directly to the trauma ICU and is expected to require mechanical ventilation for more than 48 hours. The length of his ICU stay is expected to be longer than 3 days, and he is expected to survive for more than 48 hours. The patient requires enteral nutrition during his ICU stay. He does not have any chronic illnesses that are not under control. He has not been hospitalized within one month prior to his ICU admission, and he has not used any prebiotic fiber containing enteral or oral formula or probiotic preparations within one week. He has not received antibiotics within the previous month, nor is he on steroids or immunosuppressants at the time of admission. He has not undergone active chemotherapy/radiation treatment, and he does not have renal failure requiring dialysis or liver cirrhosis class C.

A 30-year-old male with a history of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD) for the past 5 years. He has tried various topical treatments and phototherapy, but his symptoms have not improved. He is currently experiencing frequent flare-ups of itchy, dry, and red skin on his arms, legs, and trunk. His Scorad score is 20. He has no significant medical history, and he is not taking any other medications. He is willing to use a contraceptive method during the trial and for 5 months after the end of the trial as he is a male participant. He understands and is willing to comply with all aspects of the protocol. He has health insurance coverage and is registered in a social security system. He is not pregnant nor lactating. He is not currently taking any systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressive treatment, and he has not received local corticosteroid treatment within a week before inclusion. He has no contra-indication to methotrexate or cyclosporine. He has not received phototherapy with a cumulative dose greater than 2000 J/cm2.

52-year-old female of Circassian ethnicity living in Israel who participated in a previous study 10 years ago. She has no known history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and is interested in participating in the follow-up study. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has a BMI of 28.5 kg/m2 and reports no significant changes in weight or dietary habits over the past 10 years. She is willing to undergo fasting blood glucose testing and follow-up evaluations to determine her risk for future development of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

A 34-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive for 2 years visits the clinic. She has been diagnosed with hydrosalpinx through a hysterosalpingogram (HSG). Her gynecologist recommended laparoscopic surgery, but it was found to be contraindicated due to extensive pelvic adhesions. She is willing to try a new treatment method and participate in the clinical study. She has no allergies to nickel or contrast media and has good general and gynecologic health. She has no history of pelvic infection and is not currently pregnant or suspected to be pregnant. She signed the informed consent form and is eager to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male diagnosed with Crohn's disease approximately 6 months ago. He has been experiencing chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss. He has tried several medications, including mesalamine and budesonide, but they provided little to no relief. His gastroenterologist has recommended starting Cimzia® as a treatment option. He is currently not taking any other medications. He is willing to participate in the SECURE registry and provide written informed consent. He has no history of other medical conditions, allergies, or surgeries. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He lives with his wife and two children and works as a software engineer. He is excited to participate in this study and hopes that it will contribute to the development of better treatments for Crohn's disease.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. He has never received any antiretroviral therapy and is willing to participate in clinical trials to explore new treatment options. His last ELISA test was negative six months ago, but he has experienced symptoms of acute seroconversion in the past few weeks, including fever, fatigue, and rash. He has no history of substance abuse or major psychiatric illness. He is currently not in a committed relationship and is using condoms during sexual intercourse. His viral load is high (100,000 copies/mL) and CD4 count is 450 cells/mm³. His genotype screening confirms that his virus is CCR5-tropic. He is eager to take an active role in managing his condition and is interested in learning about new treatment options that could potentially lead to a cure.

A 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for the past 3 years. He is currently taking metformin to manage his blood sugar levels. His HbA1c value at screening was 8.5%. He has a BMI of 28 kg/m^2 and his blood pressure, pulse rate, and other laboratory test results are within acceptable range for the study. He is willing to comply with the study restrictions, including abstaining from smoking and limiting alcohol intake. He has not had any heart disease or stroke in the past 6 months and has not been hospitalized for poor control of diabetes in the past 6 months. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance research in the management of diabetes.

A 50-year-old male patient with a history of Type 2 diabetes presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue and occasional chest pain on exertion. His blood glucose level on presentation is 180 mg/dL and HbA1c is 7.5%. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. He reports occasional alcohol use and has a history of smoking, but quit 2 years ago. His lipid profile reveals elevated triglycerides (> 150 mg/dL), low HDL (<45 mg/dL), and LDL (<190 mg/dL). His Lp(a) level is <30 mg/dL. He has no known coronary artery disease and has not undergone any lipid-lowering therapy in the past 6 weeks. His creatinine clearance is >75 ml/min based on the Cockcroft-Gault equation. He has no history of diabetic retinopathy, nephropathy, or neuropathy. He has not undergone any surgeries or invasive procedures in the past 6 months. He does not have any known malignancy or inflammatory disease. His liver enzymes and CK levels are within normal limits. He is a male and postmenopausal. He is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old Caucasian male who was previously diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and has undergone first-line therapy. The participant has relapsed after initial treatment and has been diagnosed with FMS-like tyrosine kinase (FLT3) mutation-positive AML. The participant is refractory to or has relapsed after first-line AML therapy and is suitable for pre-selected salvage chemotherapy. The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of ≤ 2 and meets the clinical laboratory test criteria for the study. The participant is suitable for oral administration of study drug and has a negative urine pregnancy test if female. The participant agrees not to participate in another interventional study while on treatment. The participant has not received prior treatment with ASP2215 or other FLT3 inhibitors (with the exception of sorafenib and midostaurin used in the first-line therapy regimen as part of induction, consolidation, and/or maintenance). The participant does not have BCR-ABL-positive leukemia or AML secondary to prior chemotherapy for other neoplasms (except for MDS). The participant does not have clinically active central nervous system leukemia or another malignancy, unless disease-free for at least 5 years. The participant is not in the second or later hematologic relapse or has not received salvage therapy for refractory disease. The participant does not have clinically significant abnormality of coagulation profile, such as disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and has not had major surgery or radiation therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first study dose. The participant does not have congestive heart failure New York Heart Association (NYHA) class 3 or 4, or a history of congestive heart failure NYHA class 3 or 4 in the past, unless a screening echocardiogram performed within 3 months prior to study entry results in a left ventricular ejection fraction that is ≥ 45%. The participant does not require treatment with concomitant drugs that are strong inducers of cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A, strong inhibitors or inducers of P-gp, or drugs that target serotonin 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 1 (5HT1R) or 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2B (5HT2BR) or sigma nonspecific receptor, with the exception of drugs that are considered absolutely essential for the care of the subject. The participant does not have an active uncontrolled infection, is known to have human immunodeficiency virus infection, active hepatitis B or C, or other active hepatic disorder, and does not have any condition which makes the participant unsuitable for study participation. The participant does not have active clinically significant GVHD or is on treatment with systemic corticosteroids for GVHD. The participant has an FLT3 mutation other than FLT3-ITD, FLT3-TKD/D835 or FLT3-TKD/I836.

Patient is a 14yo male with a confirmed diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). He is able to speak and hear English at home at least 50% of the time. The patient has no history of nonverbal mental age below 18 months and has sufficient manual dexterity to work with a tablet or phone-based app. The patient has difficulties coping with auditory stimuli in the environment, which can be extremely debilitating and lead to anxiety and disruptive behaviors. The patient's difficulties also interfere with the ability to process and understand speech. The investigators will develop and test a cognitive/behavioral intervention (a tablet-based game app) that is highly engaging and accessible to a wide range of individuals with ASD. The intervention is designed to train the patient to adapt and attend to auditory cues. The objective of the trial is to evaluate whether the intervention leads to improvement in auditory attention as assessed by behavior changes over the course of training. The trial will also investigate the impact of the intervention on behavioral assessment of problems hearing speech in noisy environments, neural processing of sounds, and changes in parent report on responses to sounds that impact the daily lives of the participants. The trial aims to determine which adolescents with ASD benefit the most and least from interventions such as this one.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has undergone in vitro fertilization (IVF) and has embryos frozen in storage at Boston IVF. She is married and has been trying to conceive for the past 3 years. She was diagnosed with infertility due to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). She has a history of irregular menstrual cycles and has been treated with clomiphene citrate (Clomid) to induce ovulation. She has undergone multiple rounds of IVF without success. She is interested in embryo donation as an option to help others undergoing infertility treatment. She is currently employed as a teacher and has a supportive spouse who is also interested in embryo donation. She is in good health and takes no medications. She is excited to participate in this study and hopes to gain a better understanding of the options available for her frozen embryos.

A 30-year-old woman who has been using hormonal oral contraceptives for the past two months is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the rate and extent of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) absorption between two treatments. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles before starting the combined oral contraceptive pill. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25, and her vital signs are within normal limits. She has no history of cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, haematological, gastrointestinal, immunological, dermatological, endocrine, genitourinary, neurological, or psychiatric diseases. She is not on any medications, including over the counter medications and herbal remedies. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She is sexually active and uses male condoms with spermicide as an additional contraceptive method. She has no history of drug, alcohol, caffeine, or tobacco abuse. She is not pregnant or lactating and has a negative pregnancy test at screening. She understands the nature and purpose of the study and is willing to comply with the requirements of the entire study.

14-year-old male with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections presents with severe right flank pain that radiates to the groin. The pain began suddenly and is associated with nausea and vomiting. He has a family history of kidney stones. Physical exam is significant for right costovertebral angle tenderness and a positive Murphy's sign. Urinalysis is positive for blood and urine pH is 6.5. Ultrasound of the kidneys demonstrates a 6mm stone in the right renal pelvis. The patient is scheduled to undergo a renal CT scan to further evaluate the extent of the urolithiasis. This patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and will be enrolled to assess the efficacy of the low dose CT protocol for diagnosis of urolithiasis.

A 32-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident on the highway with a high-speed collision. The patient was a restrained driver and was trapped in the car. He was extricated by the local fire department with the Jaws of Life and transferred to the nearest medical center via aeromedical ambulance. He was unconscious on arrival to the hospital with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) of 7. The patient had multiple injuries, including facial fractures, chest trauma, and abdominal injuries. He was hemodynamically stable on arrival, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, pulse rate of 90 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute. The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated. A code 3 trauma activation was initiated, and the patient was transferred to the trauma bay for further evaluation and management. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial due to direct admission from the scene via aeromedical ambulance.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been diagnosed with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) with WHO group I classification. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue, and dizziness for the past few months. Her past medical history includes an episode of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) for which she was treated with anticoagulants. She has no history of liver or kidney disease and her current medications include only anticoagulants. She is a non-smoker and has no known drug allergies. The patient has not received any treatment for PAH before and is going to start a therapy with prostanoid. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent for participating in the study. She is not pregnant or lactating and uses an effective and secure method for birth control. The patient has a life expectancy that is longer than the course of the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old Caucasian male who has been experiencing moderate to severe atopic dermatitis for more than a year. He has tried several topical treatments, including corticosteroids, but with limited success. He has an Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score of 18, body surface area (BSA) of 12%, and an Investigators Global Assessment (IGA) score of 4. He has not used any systemic or topical Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors before. He has not used dupilumab or any systemic therapies for AD including corticosteroids, methotrexate, cyclosporine, azathioprine, phosphodiesterase type 4 (PDE4)-inhibitors, and mycophenolate mofetil within 4 weeks prior to the Baseline. He is currently not enrolled in any other clinical study. The patient is willing to use an additive-free, bland emollient twice daily for at least 7 days prior to Baseline.

Patient is a 55-year-old man from the United States who presented to the emergency department with chest pain that started 2 hours ago. The pain is substernal, crushing, and radiating to the left arm. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. His blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 85 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical examination, he appears uncomfortable, with diaphoresis and cold extremities. An electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. Troponin I is elevated at 5 ng/mL (normal range: <0.04 ng/mL). The patient is scheduled for percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI).

60 year old male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and systolic heart failure (ejection fraction 35%) presents to the hospital with worsening dyspnea over the past week. The patient reports increasing shortness of breath with minimal exertion, orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Upon examination, the patient is noted to have bilateral crackles on lung auscultation, jugular venous distention, and lower extremity edema. The patient is admitted to the hospital and started on diuretics and intravenous nitroglycerin. The patient also receives a two-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-2) screening for depression which is positive and is confirmed with a PHQ-9 score of 16. After being stabilized, the patient is approached about a clinical trial for blended collaborative care for heart failure and co-morbid depression. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria. The patient speaks English and has a household telephone. The patient agrees to participate in the trial and is enrolled.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease (PD) 5 years ago. He experiences tremors in his right hand, stiffness, and difficulty with balance and coordination. He is currently taking levodopa and has noticed some improvement in his motor symptoms. He reports having some non-motor symptoms such as anxiety, depression, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping. He has no history of other neurological disorders, and his Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score is 26. He does not have any cardiovascular or orthopedic problems that would interfere with gait, but he has some mild arthritis in his knees. He is able to walk independently but sometimes needs to use a cane for support. He has not had deep brain stimulation and is not expected to change his PD medications during the study. He is interested in participating in the study to see if mild body exercise can improve his quality of life and non-motor symptoms.

A 52-year-old woman diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the breast, with stage IV metastatic disease and at least one measurable lesion as per the RECIST criteria. The patient has undergone prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and has not received any prior chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer. She has a life expectancy of at least 24 weeks and has not received any experimental drug therapy within the last four weeks. The patient has normal cardiac function and has not received any prior treatment with bevacizumab or other anti-VEGF therapy. She does not currently have brain or leptomeningeal metastases and has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. The patient has no concurrent treatment with any other non-protocol anticancer therapy, except for radiation therapy that does not affect all target lesions being followed. She has no clinically significant cardiovascular disease, no active peptic ulcer disease, inflammatory bowel disease or any other gastrointestinal condition increasing the risk of perforation.

The patient is a 43-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cervical cancer. The patient had been experiencing vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain for the past few months. A biopsy confirmed the presence of cervical cancer. The patient has no significant medical history and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She had no allergy history to medications. Physical examination confirmed the presence of a cervical mass. CT scans revealed metastasis to the pelvic lymph nodes. The laboratory tests revealed that she has a platelet count greater than or equal to 75,000/mm^3, absolute granulocyte count (AGC) greater than or equal to 1,000/mm^3, serum creat

Pt is a 45yo M with a 6 month history of recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and nausea. He reports that his symptoms are worse after eating fatty foods. An ultrasound of his abdomen revealed multiple gallstones in his gallbladder. After discussing his options, he has decided to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient has no history of previous surgeries and is otherwise healthy. He meets the inclusion criteria for this study and is randomized to Group 1, which will undergo cholecystocholangiography during his surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor. He was experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating for several months before his diagnosis. His past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are currently well-controlled with medication. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He is physically active and enjoys hiking and biking. He has not received any prior treatment for his tumor. He has undergone imaging studies, which confirmed the diagnosis of locally advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor. His tumor size is greater than 5 cm and mitotic count is greater than 5/HPF. He is otherwise healthy with good liver and renal function. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He is willing to undergo surgical resection of his tumor after being treated with imatinib mesylate for 6 months.

The patient is a 58-year-old Caucasian male who was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer. He has already received one prior systemic therapy for his cancer (cisplatin/vinorelbine) and is now considering participating in a clinical trial that uses genotyping to identify appropriate targeted therapies. He has a performance status of 1 and is able to perform most of his daily activities, but does experience some fatigue and shortness of breath with exertion. He has a history of smoking, but quit 5 years ago. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is married and has two adult children. He has a positive attitude and is willing to undergo a biopsy or surgical procedure to obtain tissue for molecular testing if necessary. He is fully aware of the study's procedures and has provided written informed consent.

55-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of osteoporosis and a minimum of either one moderate or two mild atraumatic vertebral fractures, and a minimum of seven evaluable nonfractured vertebrae. She has normal or clinically nonsignificant abnormal laboratory values, including serum calcium, PTH(1-84), and urine calcium within normal limits at baseline. She has a 25-hydroxyvitamin D level between the lower limit of normal and three times the upper limit of normal at baseline. The patient has not been treated with any drug known to affect bone metabolism in the 6 months prior to randomization and has not been treated with any investigational drug during the month prior to the calcium and vitamin D run-in phase. The patient has not received any treatment with androgens or other anabolic steroids in the 6 months prior to randomization or treatment with corticosteroids. She has not received treatment with fluorides in the 6 months prior to randomization or for more than 60 days in the 24 months prior to randomization. The patient has not been treated with oral bisphosphonates in the 3 months prior to randomization or for more than 60 days in the 24 months prior to randomization; treatment with intravenous bisphosphonates in the 24 months prior to randomization. She has not received treatment with vitamin D >50,000 IU/week, or with any dose of calcitriol, analogs, or agonists in the 6 months prior to randomization. The patient has not received treatment with aluminum-containing antacids, calcium-containing antacids, or any other drug known to affect bone metabolism in the 6 months prior to randomization.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and aortic stenosis. He is scheduled for cardiac surgery to replace his aortic valve. He reports experiencing occasional chest pain, which is managed with nitroglycerin. He is able to verbally communicate his pain level and has no known neurological or mental health conditions. He does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse. He is not currently taking any medications other than nitroglycerin. He has been informed about the study and has provided written consent to participate.

A 28-year-old woman delivered a premature baby boy at 32 weeks gestation. The baby weighed 1.5 kg at birth and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) due to respiratory distress syndrome. The baby was treated with surfactant therapy and mechanical ventilation, and gradually transitioned to nasal continuous positive airway pressure (NCPAP) for respiratory support. The baby had a prolonged hospital stay of 6 weeks due to feeding difficulties, and he was discharged from the hospital with a weight of 2.1 kg. The mother was a non-smoker with no significant medical history, and she received regular prenatal care during her pregnancy. She agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed the informed consent form. The baby will be followed up regularly for the next 3 years to monitor his physical development and neuropsychological development.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman who has been receiving primary care at NorthShore University HealthSystem for the past year. She is sexually active with her partner and is interested in starting a family in the near future. She has never been pregnant before and is unsure about the steps she needs to take to ensure a healthy pregnancy. She has not received any preconception or contraceptive counseling thus far.
