She is interested in learning more about contraception options and how to optimize her health before becoming pregnant. She is willing to participate in this study to help improve the quality of care provided to women seeking reproductive healthcare.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was admitted to the ICU due to septic shock secondary to a urinary tract infection. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and was taking lisinopril and atorvastatin for these conditions. Upon admission, she was febrile with a temperature of 39.2°C, tachycardic with a heart rate of 120 beats per minute, and hypotensive with a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg. She was started on intravenous fluids and vasopressors to maintain her blood pressure. Her APACHE II score was 12, indicating a high severity of illness. She was found to have hypermetabolism with an extremely increased REE. She was eligible for the study and was enrolled. She did not have hypercortisolism, thyroid disease, tracheoesophageal fistula, or require high levels of FiO2 or PEEP in mechanical ventilation.

A 30-year-old female research assistant, who lives near Oxford, is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new tuberculosis vaccine. She has received BCG vaccination more than a year ago and is in good health. She is not taking any immunosuppressive medications, has no history of allergies, anaphylaxis or psychiatric conditions. She has not participated in any research study involving an investigational product in the past 30 days and does not plan to participate in any during the study period. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding but is willing to practice effective contraception during the study period. She has no history of injecting drug or alcohol abuse and is seronegative for hepatitis B and C. She has no significant disease or disorder that may put her at risk or influence the result of the study. She is willing to comply with all study requirements, including allowing the investigators to discuss her medical history with her general practitioner. She has signed a written informed consent form and is willing to refrain from blood donation during the course of the study.

A 45-year-old woman with a history of hepatitis C virus infection for the past 5 years is being considered for a clinical trial to measure specific chemokines, antibodies, and antibody-producing B cells in her blood. She was diagnosed with HCV infection during a routine health check-up and has been under the care of a hepatologist since then. She has no other liver diseases or chronic medical conditions. Her medical records indicate that she has been treated with antiviral therapy in the past, but she did not achieve sustained virologic response. She is interested in participating in the study to help researchers understand the immune response to HCV infection and to potentially contribute to the development of new treatments. She has healthy veins and is willing to undergo blood collection for the study. She has been fully informed about the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 26-year-old active-duty military member who has expressed suicidal ideation to a colleague. The patient reports feeling disconnected from their peers and family and is struggling with feelings of being a burden to others. The patient owns a smartphone and is willing to participate in a computerized intervention designed to reduce perceived burdensomeness and thwarted belongingness. The patient has no planned moves or deployments for the next 3 months. There is no indication of immediate hospitalization or emergency intervention needed. The patient has a history of depression and anxiety and is currently taking medication to manage these conditions.

A 30-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history presents for screening for a clinical trial. The patient reports no history of drug or alcohol abuse and is a non-smoker. The patient has not participated in any clinical trials within the past three months. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and willing to stay in a clinical facility for up to 7 days. The patient has adequate venous access and is willing to abstain from alcohol and illicit drugs during the study. The patient's BMI is within the range of 18 to 32 kg/m2. The patient is willing to abstain from nicotine-containing products during the study. The patient has not donated blood or had significant blood loss within the past three months. The patient has no history of HIV, CMV, hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection, alcohol or drug abuse, anemia or bleeding disorders, gastrointestinal disorders, chronic illness, or regular medication use. The patient has not had recent illness requiring treatment within the past month. The patient has no history of renal failure or renal insufficiency. The patient has normal electrocardiogram and vital signs. The patient has no known hypersensitivity to any ingredients in the MBX-400 capsules or placebo capsules. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent.

As this is a study focused on the construction of the therapeutic alliance between inpatient psychiatric patients and nurses, the patient should have a psychiatric disorder that requires hospitalization. Therefore, the patient is a 32-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder and suicidal ideation. She is currently experiencing a depressive episode, with symptoms of hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, and poor appetite. She has a history of non-compliance with medication and has been hospitalized several times in the past. She is single and lives with her parents. She has completed high school and has a part-time job. She has no significant medical history or allergies. She is currently taking a combination of antidepressants and mood stabilizers. She has been admitted to the inpatient psychiatric unit for close monitoring and treatment adjustment. She expresses a desire to work on her recovery and build a positive relationship with her nurses and caregivers.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman with a family history of breast cancer. Her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at the age of 50, and her sister was diagnosed at the age of 46. The patient has no personal history of breast cancer, but she has been undergoing routine screening and diagnostic imaging (mammography and ultrasound) every year for the past 5 years. She has no symptoms, but she is concerned about her risk of developing breast cancer. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She has no significant medical history or allergies and is not taking any medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. During her routine screening, she was invited to participate in this clinical trial and provided informed consent. She meets the inclusion criteria for the screening population and is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with end-stage renal disease and is in need of peritoneal dialysis. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently prescribed medications for these conditions including metoprolol, atorvastatin, and metformin. The patient reports that she is not currently experiencing any symptoms related to her kidney disease. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial comparing open versus percutaneous insertion of CAPD catheters to determine which technique is associated with less complications and shorter hospital stay. The patient is able to provide informed written consent and has no history of previous abdominal surgery via midline incision. She is fit for general anaesthetic and is willing to attend follow-up appointments as required by the study protocol.

A 62-year-old male, who underwent total laryngectomy 10 months ago, presents with a history of electrolarynx use for communication. He is a primary English speaker with no history of speech, language, cognitive, or hearing disorders. The patient has adequately functioning sEMG sensor sites for recording from muscles of articulation due to Cancer treatment. He is available and healthy enough to comply with multiple test sessions lasting 4-6 hours. The patient is capable of providing signed informed consent.

58yo daughter of a terminally ill cancer patient who has been serving as the primary caregiver for her mother for the past 6 months. The patient has metastatic breast cancer and has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery. The patient is now receiving palliative care at home and requires constant supervision and support. The caregiver has been experiencing high levels of anxiety, depression, and emotional exhaustion due to the demands of caregiving and witnessing her mother's declining health. She has no history of cognitive impairment and is willing to participate in a psychological intervention to alleviate these symptoms.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of cervical disc herniation at C6-C7 level, resulting in chronic unilateral neck and left upper extremity pain. The pain has been present for more than 2 weeks and is rated at 7/10 on the numeric pain rating score (NPRS). The patient is able to understand and provide consent in English and is willing to comply with the outcome instruments used. MRI shows a disc herniation at C6-C7 level, corresponding in location with the patient's radicular pain. The patient consents to treatment with epidural injection in a shared decision-making process with the treating physician. The patient has not received any epidural steroid injections in the past 12 months and does not have a history of prior cervical surgery or spondylolisthesis at the involved or adjacent segments. The patient does not have any progressive motor deficits or clinical signs of myelopathy. The patient is not involved in active litigation relevant to their pain and is not receiving remuneration for their pain treatment. The patient is able to attend follow-up appointments and is not incarcerated. The patient does not have any allergies to contrast media or local anesthetics and does not have a BMI>35. The patient does not have systemic inflammatory arthritis or active infections. The patient does not have medical conditions causing significant functional disability or chronic widespread pain or somatoform disorder. The patient does not have addictive behavior, severe clinical depression, or psychotic features.

This study is seeking healthy volunteers aged 18-40, who have a stable weight, and follow a Western diet. Participants should have regular bowel movements and consider themselves healthy. They should not have any gastrointestinal diseases, nor have traveled to Asian, African, or South American countries within the last six months. They should not be pregnant or lactating, nor using contraceptive pills. Participants should not have any hypersensitivity or food allergy to products used in the study, including lactose and penicillin. They should not have hepatic disease or renal failure, nor be using medication other than paracetamol, acetylsalicylic acid, hay fever, or asthma medications. Participants should not have used antibiotics in the last three months, nor probiotics or prebiotics in the last month. The participants will be required to sign an informed consent form, and they should be willing to have their family doctor informed about their participation in the study.

A 12-year-old girl with a history of tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) presents with multiple facial angiofibromas (FA). The FA started to appear at the age of 4 and have been progressively increasing in number and size. She is self-conscious about their appearance and has been bullied at school. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. Her medications include vigabatrin for seizure control and sirolimus for the treatment of subependymal giant cell astrocytomas (SEGA). Her last seizure was 6 months ago and her SEGA is stable on MRI. She is not on any topical treatments for her FA. She has not had any destructive treatments in the past 6 months. She has no known allergies and is covered by national health insurance. Her parents provide written informed consent for her participation in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with retroperitoneal liposarcoma. She underwent surgery to remove the tumor and it was determined to be resectable. The patient has no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. She has a good functional status (ECOG 0) and no evidence of metastases in any location. The patient has no history of serious cardiovascular diseases or systemic pathologies that may interfere with the treatment. She has normal medullar function and cardiac function, as well as normal levels of bilirubin, creatinine, and transaminases. The patient has not participated in any clinical trial or received any investigational agent in the past 30 days. She is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective contraceptive methods during the trial. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 45 year old man came to the clinic with a history of a fall on his outstretched hand. He complains of pain and swelling on the wrist. There was obvious deformity on the wrist and tenderness over the distal radius. There was no neurovascular deficit. X-ray showed a displaced distal radius fracture. Closed reduction was achieved with manipulation and he was advised to undergo conservative management of the fracture with cast immobilization. He is a right-handed individual, works in an office and leads a sedentary lifestyle.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. She has no significant family history of cancer, but she is concerned about her prognosis and wants to explore all possible treatment options. She works as a marketing executive and has a busy schedule, but she is willing to participate in the study to potentially benefit from personalized medicine. She has already undergone surgery to remove the tumor and is currently undergoing chemotherapy. She lives with her husband and two children and enjoys spending time with her family on weekends. She has no known cognitive impairment and is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently involved in a workplace accident that resulted in second-degree burns on his right arm and leg. He is currently receiving treatment at a burn center and is scheduled for daily wound care. He reports moderate pain during the wound care procedure and is interested in exploring non-pharmacological pain management options. He is a native English speaker and is able to communicate orally. He has no history of delirium, psychosis, or any form of Organic Brain Disorder. He is open to using virtual reality as a form of distraction during wound care and is able to wear a VR helmet without any medical restrictions. He is able to complete subjective evaluations of pain and is comfortable communicating verbally.

A 28-year-old Caucasian man diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) since the age of 13. He has been on insulin therapy since then, currently using MDI of insulin with a daily dose of 0.8 U/kg. He has a good understanding of T1DM and has been compliant with his insulin therapy. His most recent HbA1c value was 8.5%. He has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 85 mL/min/1.73 m2. He has no history of severe hypoglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis in the past 3 months. He has no history of irregular sleep/wake cycle, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, or TIA in the last 3 months. He has no history of severe gastroparesis or brittle diabetes. He has no history of liver disease, eating disorders, or cancer. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is not taking any other antihyperglycemic drugs except for insulin. He has not participated in any other clinical trial in the last 30 days. He understands the trial requirements and is willing to comply.

Patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with advanced solid tumor. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently on any medication. He has a BMI of 27, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. His laboratory results show normal blood counts and normal liver and kidney function. He has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. He is able to understand the study requirements and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. He has no history of radiation therapy, hormonal therapy, biologic therapy or chemotherapy for cancer within the 21 days prior to study Day 1. He has not had major surgery within the 28 days prior to study Day 1 or minor surgical procedures within the 14 days prior to study Day 1. He is willing to use adequate contraception for three months following discontinuation of study drug. He is able to self-administer or has a caregiver who can reliably administer subcutaneous injections.

A 28-year-old woman came to the clinic with complaints of feeling sad, hopeless, and anxious. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past two months and has trouble sleeping and concentrating. She has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medication. Her BMI is 25, and she does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no history of substance abuse. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with study procedures.

A 54-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She is a non-smoker and lives a healthy lifestyle. She has no other underlying medical conditions but has a family history of breast cancer. She has never undergone any chemotherapy or radiation before. She works as an accountant and exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. She has no known allergies to any food or drugs. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to try a new treatment for her cancer.

52-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of Mantle Cell Lymphoma, confirmed by bone marrow aspiration, and an ECOG performance status of 1. The patient has not received any prior treatment for their lymphoma and is in need of treatment for Stage Ann Arbor II-IV disease. The patient has no severe cardiac disease (NYHA grade 1-2), normal liver function (ALAT/ASAT 1.5 ULN, bilirubin <1.5 ULN), normal renal function (calculated creatinine clearance > 50 ml/min), and no other organ dysfunction that would interfere with treatment. The patient has a life expectancy of more than 3 months and is willing to sign a written informed consent. The patient is affiliated with a social security system. The patient has no history of chronic liver disease, hepatic veno-occlusive disease, or sinusoidal obstruction syndrome. The patient has ANC ≥ 1,500 /mm3 and platelet counts ≥ 75,000/mm3. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and is not a fertile man or woman of childbearing potential. The patient has no malignancy that has been treated but not with curative intent. The patient is not seropositive for HIV or HCV and has no other active infection uncontrolled by treatment. The patient has no known history of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The patient does not have a history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to humanized or murine monoclonal antibodies or known sensitivity or allergy to murine products. The patient does not have any psychiatric illness or condition that could interfere with their ability to understand the requirements of the study. The patient is not under legal protection or deprived of their liberty by a judicial or administrative decision.

A 40 yo F who was diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis 5 years ago is currently experiencing lower back pain and stiffness. She has not been previously diagnosed or treated for osteoporosis, and has not experienced any bone fractures associated with osteoporosis. She is not currently taking any medication that affects bone metabolism. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has no history of metabolic bone diseases such as Paget's disease, osteomalacia, or hyperparathyroidism. The patient does not have a history of diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, or kidney, liver, and intestinal diseases. She has a BMI of 24.1 and has never used corticosteroids.

Patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has no significant medical history other than hypertension that is well-controlled with medications. The patient's Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status is 1. He has all of the required laboratory test results performed within 14 days prior to enrollment in the study. The patient is not currently on any medication for AML. He has provided written informed consent for participation in the study and is willing to be hospitalized during the dose limiting toxicity (DLT) evaluation period. The patient is capable of orally taking quizartinib and is willing to use highly effective birth control upon enrollment, during the treatment period, and for 6 months following the last dose of investigational drug or cytarabine, whichever is later, as he is a male of childbearing potential. The patient does not have a diagnosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), French-American-British classification M3 or WHO classification of APL with translocation, t(15;17)(q22;q12), or BCR-ABL positive leukemia. The patient does not have a history of other malignancies, cardiovascular diseases, active acute or chronic systemic fungal, bacterial, or viral infection, or active clinically relevant liver disease. Overall, the patient meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for this Phase 1, multicenter, open-label study to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics (PK) of quizartinib in combination with standard induction therapy and consolidation therapy in Chinese patients with newly diagnosed AML.

A 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with COVID-19 and required intensive care at Uppsala University Hospital. She was admitted to ICU for 12 days and received mechanical ventilation, vasopressor support, and renal replacement therapy. She was discharged from ICU after 22 days and transferred to a general ward for further care. The patient has a history of hypertension and is a non-smoker. She was discharged from the hospital after 43 days and has been recovering at home with the support of her family. The patient is now 3 months post-discharge and has experienced some difficulty with activities of daily living and has noticed some neurological symptoms. She is currently working from home but has had to decrease her working hours due to fatigue. She is interested in participating in this study to help understand the long-term effects of COVID-19 and to contribute to the development of treatments for this disease.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who has been recently prescribed statins for her high cholesterol levels. She has a history of muscle ache/pain due to statin therapy, which has led to discontinuation of statin therapy in the past. She is otherwise healthy, with normal liver and kidney function, and is not taking any medications other than the prescribed statins and ezetimibe. She has no history of alcoholism or malnutrition. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if the Vitamin D supplementation will help decrease the occurrence of muscle ache/pain due to statin therapy and allow her to continue taking statins as prescribed.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, as it is focused on investigating the anatomy of soft tissues in the temporal region during surgeries for zygomaticofacial or craniofacial fractures. Therefore, there is no patient description needed for this trial.

The patient is a 40 year old male who has been experiencing chronic pain in his lower back for the past 2 years. The pain started after he lifted a heavy object at work and has been gradually worsening over time. He has tried various pain medications and physical therapy, but the pain persists. His pain level is around 6 out of 10 on the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). He works as a construction worker and the pain is affecting his ability to perform his job duties. He has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help alleviate his chronic pain.

A 28-year-old male patient with thalassemia major was referred to the clinic for cardiac MRI evaluation. He had been receiving regular blood transfusions since the age of 5 and had been on chelation therapy for the past 12 years. His latest serum ferritin level was 1500 ng/mL, and his liver T2* was 11 ms. He had no history of cardiac disease, but he complained of fatigue and shortness of breath during routine activities. His physical exam revealed no abnormalities except for mild hepatomegaly. The patient had no contraindications to MRI and agreed to participate in the study to determine the presence of myocardial iron overload.

A 24-year-old healthy male came to the clinic for the clinical trial. He has no medical history of any significant illness, and all his vital signs, including blood pressure, pulse rate, and electrocardiogram (ECG), were within the normal range. His body mass index (BMI) was 22. He has no history of gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, immunological, or hormonal disorders. He has not undergone surgery of the gastrointestinal tract, except appendectomy. He has no history of relevant orthostatic hypotension, fainting spells, blackouts, chronic, or acute infections. He has not experienced any relevant allergy or hypersensitivity, including allergies to drugs or their excipients. He has not taken any drugs with a long half-life (>24 h) within one month or less than 10 half-lives of the respective drug prior to administration or during the trial. He has not used any drugs that might reasonably influence the results of the trial or that prolong the QT/QTc interval based on the knowledge at the time of protocol preparation within 10 days prior to administration or during the trial. He has not participated in another trial with an investigational drug within 2 months prior to administration or during the trial. He is a non-smoker and has no alcohol or drug abuse history. He has not donated blood (more than 100 mL within 4 weeks prior to administration or during the trial) or had excessive physical activities (within 1 week prior to administration or during the trial). All his laboratory values are within the reference range, and he is willing to comply with the dietary regimen of the trial site. He is willing to use adequate contraception, including condom use plus another form of contraception e.g., spermicide, oral contraceptive taken by female partner, sterilization, intrauterine device, during the whole trial period from the time of the first intake of trial drug until 3 months after the last intake.

The patient is a 13-year-old male who has been experiencing recurrent bone pain and fractures since the age of 7. The patient was initially diagnosed with rickets, but his symptoms persisted despite treatment. He was referred to a specialist who suspected hypophosphatasia (HPP) due to his low alkaline phosphatase levels and characteristic skeletal abnormalities seen on X-rays. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of juvenile-onset HPP. The patient has a history of multiple fractures, including a femoral fracture that required surgery and prolonged hospitalization. The patient also experiences muscle weakness, difficulty walking, and fatigue. He has no other significant medical history and has not received any treatment for HPP. The patient and his family are interested in participating in this study to help improve understanding of this rare disease and potentially help future patients.

John is a 35-year-old man living in a rural area in a low to middle-income country. He was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 3 years ago and started his second-line ART regimen, which includes a boosted protease inhibitor (darunavir/ritonavir) and two NRTIs, 2 months ago. He has been adherent to his medications and has achieved undetectable viral load. He has no history of TB or symptoms of TB. He is currently working as a farmer and has no known chronic medical conditions. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and his BMI is 24.2 kg/m2. He is married and his wife uses an effective contraception method. He has no history of any drug allergies or hypersensitivity reactions. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent document.

A 65-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia was admitted to Alexandria University Hospital for open heart surgery due to severe aortic stenosis. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders. He is retired and lives with his wife. He takes daily medications for his hypertension and dyslipidemia. He has no allergies to any medication. He has had no previous surgeries. He is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has had an Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator (ICD) system implanted in the pectoral region for the past 10 months. He has a history of ischemic heart disease and has undergone coronary artery bypass grafting in the past. He is under the care of a cardiologist and receives regular follow-up. His ICD has been functioning appropriately since the time of implantation with no history of inappropriate shocks or arrhythmias. He is free of any symptoms related to arrhythmias or heart failure. His height is 175 cm and he weighs 85 kg. He has no known allergies to medication or medical devices. He has no history of twiddler's syndrome or any other condition that may affect the functioning of the ICD. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no plans for cardiac surgery in the next six months. He is willing and able to complete all testing required by the clinical protocol and will be available for all follow-up visits at the investigational site.

A 35-year-old male patient has a history of episodic cluster headaches for the past 4 years. He was diagnosed with episodic cluster headaches based on his symptoms and tests which confirmed the diagnosis according to IHS criteria. The patient experiences severe pain behind his right eye, which he describes as sharp and stabbing. The pain usually lasts for 45 to 90 minutes and occurs up to eight times per day during the cluster period. His cluster period usually lasts for 6 weeks but can extend up to 8 weeks. He has tried various medications, including triptans, oxygen therapy, and preventive medications, but the relief is temporary and not effective. The patient is not allergic to capsaicin and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Civamide Nasal Solution (Zucapsaicin) in treating his episodic cluster headache. Over the past three days, the patient has experienced at least one headache per day.

Patient is a 50-year-old French-speaking man who was recently hospitalized in intensive care at CH Dron for COVID-19 infection. He has recovered and is now in a follow-up consultation. He is willing to participate in the study and provide a verbatim during a semi-structured interview to evaluate the psychological, physical, social, professional, and family impact of his hospitalization in intensive care. The patient has no known comorbidities and is generally in good health. He has no history of mental health issues or substance abuse. The patient is able to communicate effectively in French and is willing to provide consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who has been experiencing difficulty with memory and recall for the past year. She was referred to a neurologist who diagnosed her with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), which is a prodromal stage of Alzheimer's disease. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. She is a retired teacher and is currently living with her husband. She is physically active and enjoys walking and yoga. She has no history of neurological or cardiac illnesses other than MCI. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may improve her cognitive function and is willing to undergo physical and neurological examinations.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer. She is scheduled to receive anthracycline chemotherapy followed by anti-HER2 therapy at MSKCC. She has no history of heart disease, but she is concerned about the potential cardiotoxicity associated with the anti-HER2 therapy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of carvedilol on heart function during treatment with anti-HER2 medication(s) including trastuzumab. She is able to swallow capsules and willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol. She has a resting heart rate of 70 beats per minute, and her sitting systolic blood pressure is 120 mmHg. She has not been previously treated with ACE-inhibitors or beta blockers, and she has no allergies or intolerance to these medications. She is not currently enrolled in any other therapeutic intervention trial in the Breast Medicine service.

A 45-year-old male patient presents with a history of fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. The physical examination reveals lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. The biopsy confirms the diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, classified as stage III. Further diagnostic workup reveals no evidence of extranodal involvement. The patient has not received any chemotherapy before and is not diagnosed with any other tumors. The patient is 18 years or older and is interested in participating in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer. She underwent a mastectomy and chemotherapy three years ago, but recent imaging revealed metastases to her spine. The metastases are located in T7 and T10. The patient is experiencing moderate pain that affects her daily activities. She has a WHO performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health. The patient has not received radiation therapy to the spine before and is willing to participate in this clinical trial. She has no allergies to contrast used in imaging scans or any medical contraindications for MRI.

Patient is a 62-year-old male who presented with complaints of abdominal pain and jaundice. CT scan and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The tumor is classified as T3N0M0. The patient has no prior history of treatment for pancreatic cancer and has good performance status (ECOG 1). The patient has no major comorbidities and an estimated life expectancy of greater than 3 months. The patient is willing to use effective means of contraception if of child-bearing potential. The patient has adequate hematologic, renal, and hepatic function with a calculated creatinine clearance greater than 50 mL/min. The patient has no history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy and does not have poorly controlled diarrhea. The patient has not had any major surgical procedure, open biopsy or significant traumatic injury within the last 28 days prior to Day 0.

45-year-old male with a history of pulmonary MDR-TB, who has failed multiple previous treatment courses including first-line and second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs. The patient has been experiencing persistent cough, weight loss, fever, and night sweats for the past 3 months. The patient has been diagnosed with co-infection with hepatitis B and C virus, and also has a history of intravenous drug use. The patient has been started on a new regimen of second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs including linezolid, bedaquiline, and clofazimine, and has consented to participate in the clinical trial for monitoring the drug concentrations and their correlation to the time to sputum culture conversion. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

A 65-year-old Caucasian man was hospitalized for an acute ischemic stroke that affected his left brain hemisphere. He received thrombolytic therapy and was admitted to the hospital for 5 days. He is scheduled to be discharged home with his wife as his primary caregiver. Before the stroke, he worked as an engineer and was very active, playing tennis twice a week. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a previous myocardial infarction, for which he was compliant with his medications. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His wife is willing to help him with the digital platform if needed. He has some experience with internet use, checking emails on his tablet at least once a week. His cognition is normal. He is motivated to improve his health and prevent future strokes.

A 25-year-old Caucasian male, weighing 80kg and with a BMI of 22 kg/m2, is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He works as an office clerk and exercises regularly. He is in good health and has no significant medical history. His blood pressure, heart rate, and body temperature are within the normal range. He has no history of allergies or autoimmune diseases. He is currently using two acceptable methods of contraception and is not planning to father a child in the next 3 months. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and has given written informed consent. He has not taken any medications in the last 14 days and has not received any investigational drugs or vaccinations in the last 3 months. He has not donated blood or blood products in the last 3 months and has not undergone plasmapheresis in the last 4 weeks.

A 32-year old female office worker presents with a history of episodic migraine for the past 7 years. She experiences severe headaches that last for 2-3 days, accompanied by sensitivity to light and sound, and occasional nausea. She reports having 2-3 migraine attacks per month on average. She has tried various over-the-counter medications for acute relief, but none have been consistently effective. She has never tried any preventive medication for migraine. She has a family history of migraine - her mother also suffers from frequent headaches. She is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or ongoing medical conditions. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol regularly. She currently works full-time in an office job and is married with no children. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for migraine prevention to reduce the frequency and severity of her migraine attacks.

A 35-year-old woman who works as a web developer is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She is generally in good health and has no known medical conditions. She has a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 25. She has normal blood pressure and resting heart rate. She uses hormonal birth control and is not currently pregnant or nursing. The patient has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to any medication. She doesn't have any history of neuropathy, chronic pain or diabetes. She doesn't take benzodiazepines or pain medications on a daily basis. The patient is interested in the study and willing to participate in the sensory function tests.

A 58-year-old Caucasian male was diagnosed with esophageal cancer 6 months ago. He had previously undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy but showed no significant improvement. The patient is currently experiencing difficulty swallowing, chest pain, and weight loss. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has a Karnofsky performance status (KPS) of 80 and is expected to have a lifespan of more than 6 months. His platelet count is 100×109/L, white blood cell count is 4×109/L, neutrophil count is 2.5×109/L, and hemoglobin level is 90 g/L. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial testing the combination of cryosurgery and NK immunotherapy for advanced esophageal cancer after standard therapies have failed or the patient refuses them.

The patient is a 22-year-old woman who is an experienced contact lens wearer with a history of wearing both 1 Day Acuvue Moist and Dailies Aqua Comfort Plus lenses on a daily basis. She has no systemic or ocular diseases and is not currently taking any medications that may affect the study outcome. Her corrected visual acuity is 20/20. She has no known sensitivity to the diagnostic pharmaceuticals used in the study and is not pregnant, lactating, or planning a pregnancy. She has not undergone any refractive error surgery. The patient is willing and able to follow instructions and maintain the appointment schedule for the duration of the study.

This is a 56 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia who presented with chest pain and was diagnosed with non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). The patient is scheduled to undergo coronary angiography and may require percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The patient is not currently on ticagrelor or clopidogrel for antiplatelet therapy. The patient has a stable baseline cardiac troponin I level before the procedure and has an estimated life expectancy of greater than 6 months.

A 50-year-old male patient visited the hospital with complaints of shortness of breath, chronic cough, and wheezing. He was diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) based on his spirometry results. His post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio was less than 0.70, indicating moderate to severe airflow limitation. He was a smoker for the past 20 years but quit smoking 6 months ago. He was clinically stable without any exacerbations requiring therapy in the past 6 weeks. He had no other comorbidities that could interfere with the study. He gave informed consent to participate in the study and was willing to perform the required exercises at home using the Wii Fit system. The patient did not require supplemental oxygen during the initial assessment. The patient was instructed to record his exercise sessions in a diary and perform at least 30 minutes of exercise on most days of the week. The patient was excited to participate in the study and was looking forward to improving his quality of life.

A 70 year old male patient is admitted to the medical intensive care unit with a diagnosis of cardiac failure. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. After being on mechanical ventilation for more than 48 hours, he is considered a high risk candidate for extubation failure due to his age and pre-existing conditions. The patient's BMI is 32 and he has difficulty managing respiratory secretions. The patient has no history of facial trauma or active gastrointestinal bleeding. The patient is able to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hepatitis C infection. He was diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) during a routine abdominal ultrasound. The diagnosis was confirmed with a CT scan showing a 4 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver with arterial enhancement and washout on delayed phase imaging. The patient has not yet been started on any treatment for the HCC. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has signed an informed consent form. The patient has a good performance status and a life expectancy of at least 8 weeks. The patient has not received sorafenib in the past and is not currently receiving sorafenib. The patient is not enrolled in hospice care.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with stage III laryngeal cancer. He received radiation therapy as part of his treatment and has completed the therapy one month ago. He reports feeling weak and has lost a significant amount of muscle mass. The patient is motivated to regain his strength and is open to participating in an exercise program. He has no history of musculoskeletal or neuromuscular conditions that would prevent him from participating in physical activity. The patient is able to walk without assistance and is willing to travel to the University of Calgary for the study. He is fluent in English and able to follow verbal instructions. The patient has received approval from his physician to participate in the study.

The patient is a 26-year-old Taiwanese male with developmental dentofacial disharmony (Class III). He has had difficulty chewing and biting for several years and has been experiencing mandibular protrusion. He underwent orthognathic surgery, specifically bilateral sagittal split osteotomy, to correct his jaw alignment. However, he has been experiencing lip numbness or paraesthesia since the surgery. The patient has no medical condition associated with systemic neuropathy and has never undergone previous facial surgery. The patient reports no positive pain sensation at the first week of post-surgery, and has not experienced any altered sensation before the orthognathic surgery. The patient is willing to sign informed consent to participate in the study and perform sensory retraining exercises at home.

A 40 yo F with chronic lower back pain for the past 8 months, rated at 7/10 on a pain scale, and a BMI of 30. She reports difficulty with daily activities due to her pain and has tried various treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications, but has not found significant relief. She also reports struggling with weight management and has tried different diets and exercise programs but has not been successful in maintaining weight loss. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her manage her pain and also address her weight concerns. She is fluent in English and has no plans to relocate within the next 12 months.

A 27-year-old healthy female presents for the study investigating the safety and tolerability of a single dose of AZD6482. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and weighs 55 kg. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no history of bleeding disorders or vascular malformations. She has not had any acute illness, surgical procedures or trauma in the past 2 weeks. She is not known to have impaired glucose intolerance or Gilbert's syndrome. She provides written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her physical exam is unremarkable.

56 year old male with chronic periodontitis who presents with a mandibular molar with a degree II furcation defect on the buccal surface. The patient reports no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. The tooth is endodontically vital and there is radiolucency in the furcation area. The patient has not received any periodontal therapy or antibiotics in the past 6 months. Periodontal examination reveals a pocket depth of 5mm or greater and a horizontal pocket depth of 3mm or greater in the furcation area. The patient is a non-smoker and has no known allergies to any medications.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is in good health and has a body mass index (BMI) between 19 and 27 kg/m2. He is a non-smoker and has refrained from any tobacco usage, including smokeless tobacco and nicotine patches, for the past 6 months. He has negative serology for Hepatitis B, C or HIV in the last 3 months. He does not have any history of drug or alcohol abuse in the past two years. He has not taken any prescription medication within 14 days prior to the study, nor over-the-counter (OTC) medication, herbal preparations, and/or vitamins within 48 hours prior to the start of study drug administration on Day 0. He has not donated or lost more than a unit of blood within 30 days prior to the screening visit. He has a normal 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) with a PR interval < 240 msec, QRS duration <110 msec, and QTc interval < 430 msec in males or QTc interval < 430 msec in females, with no clinically significant minor STT wave changes. He does not have any other laboratory values outside of the normal range at the screening visit that are deemed by the principal investigator to make the subject an inappropriate candidate for the study. He is capable of understanding and complying with the protocol and has signed the informed consent document prior to performance of any study-related procedures. He is willing to reside in the study unit during the study period and cooperate fully with the principal investigator and site personnel.

This is a 45 year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis and chronic joint pain. She has been on 75mg Indomethacin ER capsules for the past 6 months and reports good pain relief. She has no known allergies to indomethacin or related drugs. She is in generally good health with no abnormal findings on physical exam or medical history. She is willing to participate in the study to help others with similar conditions.

An 68-year-old woman presents with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has a past medical history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and arthritis. She is a non-smoker and occasionally drinks alcohol. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help prevent influenza. She has no history of egg allergy or adverse effects from previous influenza vaccinations. She has not received any influenza vaccinations in the last six months. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to adhere to all study procedures. She is generally in good health and has not been diagnosed with any significant medical conditions that would prohibit her inclusion in the study as determined by the investigator.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer three months ago. She has a history of infiltrating duct carcinoma of the left breast, which was surgically removed two years ago. Her HER-2 status is negative. She received adjuvant chemotherapy with an anthracycline and a taxane. She has previously received chemotherapy for metastatic disease and has been treated with a bisphosphonate. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and her CBC and SMA are within normal limits. She has not received any steroids, NSAIDs or anticoagulants for non-protocol reasons. She is able to visit the clinic for outpatient treatment and evaluation. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

50-year-old male stroke survivor with left hemiparesis and chronic functional constipation for over a year presents for evaluation. The patient has the capacity for independent gait and complains of constipation despite using laxatives and increasing fiber intake. The patient has no history of abdominal incisions or tumors, fractures, rheumatic disease, or infectious processes in the acute phase. The patient is able to understand the proposed evaluations and has the ability to walk and maintain balance in an independent manner. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effect of visceral mobilization on symptoms of functional constipation and static balance in stroke survivors.

John is a 55-year-old man who has been diagnosed with COPD. He has a history of smoking two packs of cigarettes per day for 30 years, and has had several hospitalizations for exacerbations of his lung disease. He takes bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids on a regular basis, but still experiences shortness of breath and coughing. His recent high resolution computed tomography (HRCT) scan showed emphysema and airway wall thickening. He has no other significant medical history or allergies. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He is physically fit for the procedure and has no contraindications to bronchoscopy.

A 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing migraines with aura for the past 2 years is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She typically has 2-3 migraines per month that last for about 24 hours. She has no significant medical history and takes only occasional over-the-counter pain medication for her migraines. She is not currently pregnant and uses an oral contraceptive for birth control. She is willing and able to attend all necessary visits at the study center and is able to provide written informed consent. She has never been diagnosed with trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias, hemiplegic migraine, or migraine with brainstem aura. She does not have chronic migraines or medication overuse headaches. She does not have any significant risk factors for coronary artery disease and has not had any vascular surgery in the past 3 months. She does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse within the past 2 years. She has not used triptan or ergot-based medication more than 12 days per month in the past 2 months.

The patient is a 75-year-old male with a history of diabetes and hypertension. He presents to the emergency department with a fever, productive cough, and shortness of breath. Vital signs are: blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 110 beats/min, respiratory rate 24 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. Physical examination reveals crackles in the left lung base. Laboratory results show a white blood cell count of 18,000/mm3, a lactate level of 2.5 mmol/L, and a creatinine level of 1.8 mg/dL. The patient is diagnosed with sepsis due to suspected pneumonia and organ dysfunction, as evidenced by the hypotension, elevated lactate level, and acute kidney injury. He is admitted to the ICU for further management. In this clinical trial, the patient would be eligible for inclusion based on the presence of suspected infection and organ dysfunction, specifically hypotension and acute kidney injury.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with chronic heart failure (NYHA Class III) due to arterial hypertension. She has been clinically stable with diuretic treatment and has been taking furosemide 40mg/day. She has left ventricular hypertrophy diagnosed by echocardiogram and has no history of ischaemic cardiopathy or recent disease. The patient does not have heart failure due to aortic stenosis or hypertrophic myocardiopathy, recent coronary syndrome (within the last 3 months), recent myocardial infarction (within the last 6 months), unstable angina pectoris, or severe cardiac arrhythmia. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently taking aldosterone antagonists or loop diuretic treatment over study doses. The patient also does not have a known hypersensitivity to study drugs and does not have liver disease (SGPT or AST < twice upper normal limit), renal impairment (Serum creatinine < 2.5mg/dl), or insulin-dependent diabetes. She is not included in another simultaneous study and does not have lactose intolerance. She is not taking lithium concomitant treatment or chronic treatment with NSAIDs or aminoglycoside antibiotics, etacrynic acid. The patient has provided signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 42-year-old Caucasian male diagnosed with glioblastoma complains of headaches, confusion, and difficulty with speech. He has previously undergone radiation therapy and chemotherapy. He was initially diagnosed with glioblastoma 2 years ago and underwent surgical resection followed by radiation therapy and temozolomide chemotherapy. His symptoms have worsened over the past few weeks, and he has been experiencing seizures. His Karnofsky performance status (KPS) is 80%. He is currently taking a stable dose of steroids. He has no other significant medical history. His family history is negative for any neurological disorders. His MRI scan shows recurrence of glioblastoma. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. He has not received any investigational agent(s) within 28 days of the first day of administration of study drugs. His serum creatinine, aspartat-aminotransferase (AST) and bilirubin levels are within normal limits. He has a negative pregnancy test. He is willing to employ an effective method of birth control throughout the study and for up to 6 months following discontinuation of study drug. He meets all the eligibility criteria for the CUSP9v3 treatment protocol.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who was diagnosed with pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) two years ago. He underwent radical surgical treatment of primitive neoplasia, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. However, during a routine follow-up, he was found to have lung metastasis of PDAC. The CT scan showed multiple nodules in both lungs. The patient underwent surgical removal of the lung metastasis for therapeutic purposes. The histological examination confirmed the presence of PDAC metastasis. The patient provided informed consent to participate in the LUMACA Trial. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. He has no significant family history of cancer. His performance status is good, and he has no other significant comorbidities.

A 40-year-old man presents with a deep burn wound on his thigh that requires a split-thickness skin graft donor site wound. He has no known systemic infections or chronic skin diseases, and he is not immunocompromised. He is able to read and write and is willing to follow the study protocol. He has no known allergies to cellulose, chitosan, sericin, or chlorhexidine. He is mentally sound and has no psychotic disorders. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. He is available for appointments related to the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who visited a gastroenterologist due to abdominal discomfort and intermittent diarrhea for the past two months. Physical examination and laboratory tests showed no significant abnormalities except for elevated serum CA19-9 (110 U/mL). Abdominal CT scan revealed a 3 cm mass in the pancreatic head. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) was performed, and the biopsy was recommended for further diagnosis. The patient was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, well-controlled with medical treatment. He was able to provide informed consent for the trial and met the inclusion criteria of age >19 years and a solid pancreatic mass lesion. The patient was not excluded from the trial due to coagulopathy or inability to consent.

There is no patient description needed for this particular clinical trial as it does not involve patients or participants with HIV. The study is focused on the usability of a self-test prototype for HIV screening among lay users, and the eligibility criteria are based on age, literacy, and prior experience with HIV self-testing.

45-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection genotype 3a, with previous treatment failure on interferon-based regimen. He was diagnosed with cirrhosis of the liver and has been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. The patient has not been treated with any investigational drug or device in the last 30 days. He is sexually active and willing to use highly effective contraception methods during the study period. The patient has no history of direct-acting antiviral drug targeting HCV NS5B polymerase exposure. He has no current or prior history of clinical hepatic decompensation, excessive alcohol ingestion, or significant drug abuse. The patient's screening laboratory values are within defined thresholds.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with advanced gastric cancer. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medication. He has no significant medical history otherwise. The patient is currently experiencing symptoms such as abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging studies have shown multiple lesions consistent with metastatic disease in his liver and peritoneum. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, meaning he is able to carry out light activities such as light housework or office work. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and understands the nature of the study.

40-year-old male patient who has been referred for colonoscopy due to positive fecal occult blood test. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He reports occasional constipation but denies any history of bowel obstruction or resection. The patient is not pregnant, lactating or taking oral contraceptive. He does not have any known allergies to polyethylene glycol (PEG) or bisacodyl. The patient is willing to participate in the study and signs the consent form.

As there are no eligibility criteria mentioned in the description of the clinical trial, a patient description cannot be generated. However, it is worth noting that the trial was conducted in the late 1980s, and current clinical trials would have eligibility criteria to ensure patient safety and efficacy of the treatment being tested.

A 64-year-old man with a history of Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL) was initially diagnosed 4 years ago. He received six cycles of R-CHOP and achieved a complete remission. Two years later, he relapsed and received treatment with ibrutinib for 18 months. During this time, he had a partial response, and then, unfortunately, he experienced disease progression. He discontinued ibrutinib treatment and had been without treatment for the past 2 months. His recent PET/CT scan revealed persistent disease in the lymph nodes and spleen. The patient is asymptomatic and has an ECOG performance status of 1. His laboratory values are within normal limits, except for mildly elevated LDH. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore the effectiveness of lenalidomide in relapsed or refractory MCL following ibrutinib treatment.

A 42-year-old male diagnosed with non-traumatic myelopathy has been experiencing difficulty in maintaining balance while standing or sitting. He also complains of a lack of coordination in his lower limbs and difficulty in walking for extended periods. His neurological level of injury is below C4 and he has a duration of illness less than 6 months. He has no severe orthopedic or medical impairment that interferes with sitting and his upper limb muscle power is above 3/5. He has no cognitive or visual impairment.

The patient is a 45-year-old male scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication. He has no history of other medical conditions and is generally healthy. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has never undergone surgery before and is slightly anxious about the procedure. He understands the study and is willing to participate. He meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

A 32-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of axial spondyloarthritis complains of chronic back pain that has been affecting his quality of life for the past few years. He has been experiencing stiffness in his back upon waking up in the morning, which improves with exercise. He has been taking NSAIDs for pain relief and has been advised to start biologic therapy by his rheumatologist. He is interested in alternative therapies and is willing to participate in a study evaluating the effectiveness of add-on mindset and physical therapy based on the "Wim Hof Method." He does not have any other significant medical history, and his family history is negative for autoimmune diseases. He has been a regular smoker for the past 10 years and drinks alcohol socially. He is currently employed as a software engineer and is physically active, engaging in cycling and swimming regularly. He is willing to abstain from any other alternative therapies during the trial period and is committed to following the study protocol. His current ASDAS score is 3.2, and his CRP value is 10.2 mg/L.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with severe pneumonia and respiratory distress. The patient had to be intubated and was transferred to the ICU due to her critical condition. During her stay in the ICU, she experienced several organ failures, including renal failure, which required extrarenal purification. The patient was also administered catecholamines to support her cardiovascular system. Despite receiving adequate medical care and treatment, the patient developed malnutrition during her ICU stay, which further complicated her recovery. After being discharged from the hospital, the patient continued to experience reduced quality of life, including difficulty in completing routine activities, and experienced frequent hospitalizations due to complications related to her malnutrition. The patient is now being considered for the clinical trial to investigate the relationship between nutritional status during ICU hospitalization and long-term outcomes.

A 35-year-old female presents with irregular menstrual cycles and an inability to conceive despite trying for over a year. She has a history of hypothyroidism, which is well-controlled with medication. Blood tests reveal elevated levels of prolactin, leading to a diagnosis of hyperprolactinemia. She is prescribed Cabergoline 0.5 mg twice a week for a month. The patient is concerned about the side effects of the medication and would like to receive health education on alternative ways to reduce prolactin levels. She agrees to participate in a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of nurse-led health education in managing hyperprolactinemia. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and is not currently pregnant or lactating.

A 26-year old female who is in good physical and mental health is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She does not have a history of regular drug use, except for oral contraceptives. She has never been diagnosed with any acute or chronic illnesses, nor does she have a known history of allergies or hypersensitivity reactions. She is a non-smoker and does not abuse alcohol or drugs. She is willing to participate in a study that involves the administration of methylene blue and chloroquine in order to investigate the bioavailability of the drugs. She is interested in contributing to research that may ultimately help prevent or treat malaria.

A 30-year-old male presented to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, weight loss, and recurrent fever for the past two months. He had no significant past medical history and no known drug allergies. Laboratory testing revealed a HIV-1 RNA viral load of 12,000 copies/mL and a CD4 count of 130 cells/mm3. The patient tested positive for R5 HIV-1 as verified by the Monogram Bioscience Trofile® assay with enhanced sensitivity. He has never received any antiretroviral therapy for HIV before. He has no evidence of resistance to atazanavir, tenofovir, and emtricitabine. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help with the development of a new treatment regimen for HIV.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and obesity. He has been diagnosed with a venous leg ulcer on his left leg, which has been present for the past 4 months. The wound is located below the knee and measures approximately 4 cm x 3 cm. The patient has been receiving standard compression therapy for the past 2 months, but the wound has not shown significant improvement. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the eligibility criteria, including having a venous insufficiency confirmed by duplex Doppler ultrasound examination and an acceptable state of health and nutrition. The patient has no history of anaphylaxis or serum sickness and has not been exposed to HP802-247 or its vehicle before. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and has provided informed consent to participate.

A 6-year-old boy referred for evaluation of social communication difficulties by his teachers and parents. The parents have noticed that he has difficulty making eye contact, does not initiate conversations, has repetitive language, and prefers to play alone. He is in first grade and has difficulty following instructions, staying on task, and interacting with peers. His parents report that he has always been a "quirky" child and has had difficulty with transitions and changes in routines. He has no history of seizures, hearing impairment, or other medical conditions. He has no history of developmental regression, and his early developmental milestones were met within normal limits. He has no family history of autism spectrum disorder, but his older sister was diagnosed with ADHD. He is currently receiving special education services at school but has not had a formal diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of colon cancer. The patient underwent a colon resection with no evidence of metastasis. However, a follow-up CT scan revealed a suspicious nodule in the liver. The patient was referred for an MRI with contrast to further evaluate the liver nodule. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently taking lisinopril. The patient has no known allergies to contrast agents and has normal renal function with an eGFR of 70 mL/min/1.73 m². The patient agrees to participate in the trial and is willing to undergo two MRIs, one with gadopiclenol and one with gadobutrol for the evaluation of the liver nodule.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes for the past 5 years. He is currently not on insulin treatment and has not experienced any previous cardiovascular events. However, he has high LDL cholesterol levels (>130 mg/dL), high triglycerides (>200 mg/dL), and low HDL cholesterol levels (<35 mg/dL for males). His blood pressure is also consistently above 140/90 mmHg. He is a smoker and has a BMI of 30, indicating obesity. The patient has been informed about the Multifactorial INtervention in type 2 Diabetes - ITaly (MIND.IT) study and has given written consent to participate. He is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of having at least two of the specified cardiovascular risk factors and being between the ages of 50 and 70 years. He does not have any of the exclusion criteria, such as a history of previous cardiovascular events or active neoplasms.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with breast cancer. She has a palpable lump in her left breast that is greater than 2 cm in size. She has not undergone any previous treatment for her breast cancer. She has been scheduled to receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy as part of her treatment plan. She is fluent in English and able to read and write. She has no history of psychiatric or addictive disorders that may limit her ability to give informed consent or complete the trial. She is not pregnant nor breastfeeding. Her TNM cancer staging is T2, and her histology is invasive ductal carcinoma. She is willing to have fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) after the first, second, and third cycle of chemotherapy and if the chemotherapy regimen is changed, an additional FNAB after the first cycle of the new chemotherapy.

The patient is a 35-year-old mother of a 5-year-old child who has been admitted to the pediatric ward due to pneumonia. The mother is an Israeli citizen who works as a graphic designer. She is well-educated and has a bachelor's degree. The mother is concerned about her child's health and is willing to participate in the study to provide her opinion on physicians' attire. She has had previous experiences with doctors and has varying opinions on their attire, but overall she prefers a more casual and relaxed dress code. She believes that a physician who dresses casually appears more approachable and easy to communicate with. She hopes that her feedback will be taken into consideration and help improve the attire policy for physicians in the pediatric ward.

The patient is a 25-year-old female college student who has been struggling with depression for over a year. She has been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder and has been on a stable dose of antidepressant medication for the past 6 months. She has also been using cannabis regularly for the past year to self-treat her depression symptoms. She reports using about 2 grams of cannabis per day and has a CUDIT score of 16. She is a non-treatment seeking cannabis user and has never sought professional help for her cannabis use. She is motivated to participate in the study and has a Full Scale IQ score of 96 as determined by the WTAR. She has no history of head injury or neurological or medical condition that affects cognition. She is willing to commit to a 28-day abstinence period from cannabis and is willing to attend weekly behavioural coaching sessions to help maintain abstinence. Her baseline HDRS-17 score is 18 and her urinary THC-COOH levels are 200 ng/ml.

This is a 28-year-old female who is scheduled to undergo a dental procedure at the Craniofacial Pain Center. She is fluent in English and able to hear, write and read in English. She has access to a smart tablet and is able to operate it. She is willing and able to give informed consent. She has no known acute psychiatric disorder. The patient has reported experiencing anxiety and pain during previous dental procedures and is interested in exploring non-pharmacological ways to manage these symptoms. She is excited to participate in this Phase I pilot trial to test the feasibility of a Comfort Talk® app to reduce anxiety, pain, and periprocedural drug use during dental procedures. She understands that she will be randomized to either listen to a calmative Comfort Talk® app or app with white noise and will be asked to record her levels of anxiety, pain, and drug use daily for 7 days after her visit. She is eager to contribute to this study and hopes that the results will benefit future patients.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male, 178 cm tall and weighing 85 kg. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol or use any drugs. He has a BMI of 26.8 and has not participated in any clinical trial or received any investigational or marketed drugs in the past two months. He has not donated blood in the past two months either. He has no history of local or systemic infection disease with fever or requiring antibiotics within four weeks of drug administration. He has no corrected QT interval above normal and all laboratory test results are within normal range. He has no mental incapacity, unwillingness or language barriers precluding adequate understanding or cooperation. He has not used any system course of corticosteroids or other medication known to cause insulin resistance in the past six weeks. He has no history of hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, hypertension, heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias, or diabetes. He is not on any medication for overactive bladder or bladder outlet obstruction.

Patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of peripheral arterial disease, scheduled for arterial dilation of his right leg due to a chronic occlusion in his right femoral artery. The patient has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well-controlled with medications. The patient has no history of heart disease or any other significant medical condition. His BMI is 26. He has a normal sinus rhythm on his preoperative ECG. The patient is not on any ACE inhibitors. The patient has given informed consent for the study and is willing to comply with study procedures.

A 35-year-old female presented to the clinic with complaints of chronic pain in the jaw joint while speaking and chewing. The pain has been present for the past 6 months and has been worsening gradually. She denies any history of trauma to the face or previous surgery at the temporomandibular joint. The patient has not undergone any dental procedures recently. She does not have any known rheumatic diseases. On examination, localized tenderness was noted at the temporomandibular joint, and her mouth opening was limited to 25mm. The patient's pain level was measured using a visual analogue scale (VAS) 100, and it was recorded at rest and during temporomandibular joint movement. The VAS score was 60/100 at rest and 80/100 during movement. The patient was prescribed a home-based exercise program that consisted of lateral deviation, protrusion/retraction, and mandibular opening exercises, along with isometric cervical muscle strengthening exercises. The patient was also given a reminding handout and an individual demonstration of the exercises. The severity of the patient's temporomandibular joint affection was assessed using the Fonseca's questionnaire at the entry point to the study, and it will be assessed again after 6 months.

A 10-year-old girl with a history of recurrent infections presents with enlarged lymph nodes and spleen. She has been experiencing these symptoms for over a year and has been diagnosed with autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS). Her primary care physician has referred her to a clinical trial investigating the use of valproic acid (Depakote [R]) to treat ALPS. The patient meets the eligibility criteria, including having documented nonmalignant lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly for at least a year, and having a TCR alpha/beta+ CD4-CD8- T cell count greater than 1% in her peripheral blood. She is willing to sign a consent form and has a personal physician who is willing to follow the protocol required evaluations during the study period. The patient is not on immunosuppressive medications, and her hematologic parameters meet the inclusion criteria. She has no history of seizure disorders and is not currently receiving valproic acid. The patient's parents understand that she will need to have periodic blood tests to monitor possible side effects of treatment and comply with other major requirements of the study.

Patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer complicated by brain metastases. She has undergone previous treatment for her brain metastases including external beam radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and surgery. However, she has demonstrated progression of her brain metastases and is not a candidate for surgical resection or further stereotactic radiosurgery. She has extracranial metastases but is otherwise in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. Her hormone receptor status is not specified. She has a life expectancy of at least one month and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study. She will receive irinotecan and temozolomide combination therapy every 28 days for the duration of the study, with follow-up every 4 weeks after completion of study therapy.

55-year-old woman with a history of dry eye disease and visually significant cataract in her right eye. The patient has a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/30 in both eyes. She has no history of LASIK or PRK, but has worn soft contact lenses intermittently for the past 10 years. The patient has no history of corneal scarring, macular or retinal pathology, or cataract surgery complications. She is not pregnant and is not currently using topical glaucoma medications.
