The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of an intracanalicular dexamethasone insert to improve the accuracy of intraocular lens measurements for cataract surgery.

A 25 year old female with a history of dental anxiety is scheduled for a dental procedure on her mandibular posterior teeth. She is nervous about the potential pain associated with the injection of local anesthesia. She has no known allergies and does not have any systemic diseases. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness and complications of intraligamentary anesthesia (ILA) with conventional inferior alveolar nerve block (IANB) during the injection and dental treatment of her mandibular posterior teeth. She understands that she may be randomly allocated to either the ILA group or the IANB group and that her pain and stress levels during the injection and dental procedure will be assessed using a Numeric Rating Scale. She is willing to provide consent and follow the eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is experiencing vaginal discharge with a strong fishy odor and itching for the past week. She is sexually active with multiple partners and uses condoms inconsistently. She denies any pain during intercourse or urination. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. She had a negative pregnancy test result at her last visit to the OB/GYN office. Upon examination, her vaginal mucosa appears erythematous with a thin, grayish-white discharge. The pH of the vaginal fluid is 6.0. Wet mount microscopy reveals clue cells and a predominance of Gram-variable rods, consistent with bacterial vaginosis. She is willing to refrain from using any intravaginal products and agrees to use an acceptable form of birth control throughout the study period. She understands and is willing to sign the informed consent form and comply with the requirements of the protocol. She has no history of alcohol or substance abuse, and her medical history is unremarkable. She has not participated in any other clinical trial.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in his left leg. He presented to the hospital with symptoms of pain, swelling, and redness in his leg. Imaging studies confirmed the diagnosis of DVT, and he was started on anticoagulant therapy. He has no prior history of DVT or pulmonary embolism (PE). He is a non-smoker and does not use hormonal contraceptives. He has no known family history of thromboembolic disease. He is willing to participate in the BREIZH-Cohorte study to help identify risk factors for recurrent thromboembolic disease in young patients like himself.

Pt is a 20yo F university student who has been experiencing mild to moderate anxiety for the past few months. She has been struggling to manage her anxiety, which has led to difficulties in concentrating on her studies and socializing with friends. She has no significant medical history or current medical conditions. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new ways of managing her anxiety and improving her overall well-being. She is able to commit to attending four 2-hour group sessions over four weeks and completing pre- and post-intervention assessments. She does not have a history of dissociation and meets all inclusion criteria for the study.

John is a 32-year-old surgeon who has been practicing for 3 years after completing his specialization in General Surgery. He has basic laparoscopic skills and is capable of performing an appendectomy. He does not have diabetes or Addison's disease, and he does not take any steroids or medication that affects heart rate such as beta-blockers, calcium antagonists, antiarrhythmics, or digitalis. He is a non-smoker and has no history of cardiovascular disease. John is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to study the effect of intraoperative pauses including a sugar-containing drink on surgeon's stress levels during simulated operations.

A 65-year-old man was diagnosed with muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) after presenting with gross hematuria and dysuria. The biopsy confirmed urothelial carcinoma, and imaging studies revealed a 4 cm bladder tumor invading the muscle layer. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, which is well controlled with oral medication. He has a history of smoking, having quit 10 years ago, and he drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient underwent a transurethral resection of the bladder tumor (TURBT) within the past 30 days, which confirmed muscularis propria invasion. The local site pathologist confirmed 30% viable tumor content in the TURBT sample. Due to his medical history, the patient is not eligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy. He is scheduled to undergo a radical cystectomy, but the investigators propose neoadjuvant therapy with intravesical CG0070 and IV Nivolumab as part of a clinical trial. The patient is willing to provide tumor tissue, blood, and urine samples for research, and he is fit for TURBT and radical cystectomy. However, he has a history of hearing impairment and neuropathy, both of which are Grade 2 by CTCAE criteria. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria except for the hearing impairment and neuropathy.

The patient is a 58 year-old male diagnosed with heart failure for the past six months. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was hospitalized twice within the past year for acute exacerbation of heart failure. He has a BMI of 29 and has a sedentary lifestyle due to fatigue and shortness of breath. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He is able to read and understand English. He lives with his wife who is able to provide support but he is not dependent on her for daily activities. He is currently taking lisinopril, carvedilol, and furosemide for his heart failure.

The patient is a 62-year-old male diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 5 years ago. He presents with chronic pain, which has been persistent for the last 6 months. The pain is characterized as burning, tingling and stabbing in his lower back and legs. He reports the pain to be constant, with occasional periods of exacerbation. The pain score on the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) is 7 out of 10. The patient is currently on a stable regimen of dopaminergic drugs, including levodopa and dopamine agonists, and has been on this treatment for the past 6 months. He is also taking acetaminophen as a step 1 analgesic for his pain. The patient has no history of hypersensitivity to oxycodone or levodopa, and has not been treated with any opioid drugs (step 2 and 3). He has no known cognitive impairment and is able to complete the various scales used in the study. The patient has no history of claustrophobia, hearing aids, cardiac prosthesis, pacemaker, surgical clips, or angle-closure glaucoma, and is willing to be informed of any abnormalities detected on MRI.

Unfortunately, as this particular clinical trial does not involve direct patient participation, it would not be appropriate to generate a patient description. This study aims to improve the quality of care provided by anaesthesia personnel through an e-learning course, but does not involve patients directly.

There is no patient description necessary for this clinical trial as it is a secondary study that will be recruiting subjects who are already enrolled in protocol 22001. These subjects will be asked to participate in additional testing and contribute a blood sample for DNA collection.

A 55 year old woman with osteoarthritis of the knee has been scheduled for an elective total knee replacement surgery. She has previously undergone a meniscus surgery on the same knee. She is otherwise healthy, has no history of heart disease, stroke, or deep vein thrombosis. She is able to give written informed consent and has no contraindications to MRI imaging. She is eligible to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of surgical tourniquets on cerebral emboli during TKR surgery.

A 28-year-old healthy male came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He is a non-smoker and his BMI is 22. He works as a software developer and exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. He is not on any medications or supplements. He drinks alcohol socially but not more than 2 drinks per week. He has no history of chronic diseases, and his blood pressure and ECG are normal. He has never participated in any clinical trial before. He is willing to use an acceptable method of contraception during the study period and for 30 days following the last dose of the study medication.

The patient is a 55 year old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He recently experienced chest pain and was diagnosed with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). He was admitted to the hospital and underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for the treatment of STEMI. He has no history of previous myocardial infarction or revascularization procedures. He is currently not taking any statin or ezetimibe medication. He is a smoker with a 20 pack-year history and is willing to quit smoking. He is a retired engineer and enjoys spending his free time reading books and gardening. He has a BMI of 26 and his blood pressure is well controlled on medication. His physical exam is unremarkable. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a pregnant woman in her 33rd week of gestation. She had an uneventful pregnancy and no significant medical history. She presents to the hospital with spontaneous onset of contractions and her membranes ruptured spontaneously. She was admitted to the delivery room for vaginal delivery. The baby was delivered without any complications and required resuscitation in the delivery room. The baby presented with respiratory distress and required respiratory support. The baby is eligible for the study as per the inclusion criteria. The parents have been informed about the study and have provided written informed consent.

A 32-year-old woman has been experiencing intense fear of public speaking since high school. She reports feeling extremely anxious and nervous when speaking in front of groups of people, and has avoided public speaking opportunities whenever possible. She has been able to manage her fear to some extent by limiting her exposure to public speaking situations, but it continues to impact her personal and professional life. She is currently working as a marketing manager and feels that her fear is limiting her career growth. She has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, and is not currently taking any psychotropic medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) to treat anxiety and phobias. She undergoes a prescreening assessment and is found to be eligible for the study. She is randomly assigned to receive either LLLT alone or sham LLLT alone. She completes a baseline assessment and then undergoes the treatment procedure. Two weeks later, she returns to the lab for a follow-up assessment. She completes self-report questionnaires and two behavioral approach tests to assess her fear of public speaking in both the treatment and generalization contexts.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with esophageal cancer after experiencing difficulty swallowing and persistent heartburn for several months. He has no significant past medical history and has never had surgery before. The patient's BMI is 24.5 kg/m2, and he is able to tolerate oral fluids. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, meaning he is able to carry out light work and normal daily activities without restriction. The patient has been informed of the study and has consented to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea. He reports excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, and witnessed apneas during sleep. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m², and his neck circumference is 16 inches. He works as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He drinks alcohol occasionally with his friends. He has no known cardiac or pulmonary problems and is not taking any medication that could influence breathing, sleep/arousal, or muscle physiology. He has never been diagnosed with any other sleep disorders. He is not claustrophobic and can sleep supine. He has no known allergies to lidocaine or oxymetazoline HCl. He is not pregnant.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with an endometrioma on her left ovary. She has been experiencing severe pelvic pain and heavy menstrual bleeding for the past few months. Her menstrual cycles are irregular, and she has been trying to get pregnant for the past year without success. She has never used any hormonal contraception. She has a history of chlamydia infection and was treated with antibiotics. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She works as a nurse and exercises regularly. Her BMI is 22.8. Her lab results show that her anti-mullerian hormone (AMH) level is 1.5 ng/mL, which is within the normal range for her age. She is considering laparoscopic cystectomy for her endometrioma and is open to receiving preoperative depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) to help preserve her ovarian reserve.

34-year-old male IDF's staff member who works in an administrative position and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has a BMI of 30 and has a family history of diabetes. He reports a sedentary lifestyle and consumes fast food frequently due to his busy work schedule. He has expressed concern about his weight and overall health and is interested in making lifestyle changes to improve his health. He has no known history of cardiovascular or respiratory disease but has been diagnosed with high blood pressure.

The patient is a 23 year old female with a history of severe menstrual pain. She has been diagnosed with primary dysmenorrhea by a gynecologist and is not pregnant. Her menstrual cycle is regular with a duration of 28 days. She is nulliparous and has a menstrual pain intensity above 5cm according to Visual Analog Scale. She has no gastrointestinal, urogynecologic, or psychiatric disease, and has no history of pelvic surgery. She is not using oral contraceptives or antidepressants for at least 3 months. She has no irregular menstrual cycles (lasting less than 21 or more than 35 days) and no history or ultrasonographic observation of pathological conditions indicating secondary dysmenorrhea. She experiences fatigue and sleep disturbance during her menstrual cycle. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine the effects of connective tissue manipulation on her menstrual pain, fatigue, sleep quality, general health status, systemic symptoms, anxiety and depression. She is willing to undergo CTM therapy for the duration of the trial and is committed to attending all follow-up appointments.

A 45-year-old married couple, John and Sarah, both are working professionals and have been married for 10 years. John is a software developer and Sarah is a physician. John has been diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) for the past 5 years and Sarah is at risk for T2D due to her family history. They are interested in participating in the Couple Interaction and Health Behaviors study to better understand how their relationship dynamics affect their health behaviors. They are both in good physical health and have no major health conditions other than John's T2D. They have no history of mental illness or substance abuse. They are comfortable with being video recorded during the study activities and are willing to visit the laboratory at a time that is convenient for them. They have been married for more than 6 years and they both feel that they have a strong and committed relationship. They are excited to participate in the study and hope that their participation will help to better understand how couple interactions can affect their health behaviors.

This is a 42 year old male with a past medical history of hypertension and occasional heartburn. He has been experiencing difficulty with swallowing solids and liquids for the past 6 months. He has lost 10 pounds unintentionally and has noticed regurgitation of food and liquid. He has been evaluated by a gastroenterologist who performed an esophageal manometry and diagnosed him with idiopathic achalasia with an Eckardt score of 6. He has not had any previous treatment for his achalasia except for occasional use of calcium channel blockers. He is fluent in English and capable of filling out questionnaires. He has no history of esophageal diverticula or esophageal or gastric surgery. He is interested in participating in the POEM trial to compare the efficacy of POEM to that of pneumodilation as the initial treatment for his achalasia. He is not pregnant and does not have any liver cirrhosis or esophageal varices.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with a fever of 39.0°C, productive cough, and shortness of breath. Chest X-ray reveals bilateral infiltrates. Sputum culture grows Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The patient is started on intravenous meropenem and admitted to Surrey Memorial Hospital. He has been in the hospital for 3 days, and his fever has resolved. The patient's blood cultures are negative, and there is no clinical evidence of sepsis. The patient has no allergies to any medication. His renal function is normal, and he is not pregnant nor wishes to become pregnant. The patient is willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

9-year-old female with a history of partial-onset seizures that started at the age of 6. She has been previously treated with levetiracetam and lamotrigine but still experiences seizures. She is in good general health apart from epilepsy and has no history of substance abuse or attempted suicide. The patient has no known allergies or intolerances to OXC or CBZ. She is currently taking a stable dosage regimen of two AEDs for the last month. She has good compliance with her medication and keeps a diary of her seizures. The patient and her parent have given written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is premenarchal and practices an effective non-hormonal contraception method. She is within the 10th and 90th percentiles for her age and sex for weight. Brain CT scans and MRI have excluded rapidly progressive neurological diseases. Based on the inclusion criteria, the patient is eligible for the screening phase of the study.

8-year-old Nicaraguan child enrolled in the Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study (PDCS) who had Zika virus (ZIKV)-like symptoms in January 2016. The child was tested for ZIKV and found to have acquired the infection. The child will be participating in a longitudinal study to evaluate the presence and persistence of neurological symptoms associated with ZIKV infection and to test whether ZIKV-infected children are at greater risk for developing neurological outcomes compared to uninfected children. The child will undergo clinical assessment of neurological impairment (e.g., vision, hearing, motor, and sensory functioning) by direct observation, neuropsychological assessment battery, and evaluation of factors related to neurological functioning (e.g., mood and sleep disorders) in the 2019/2020 study visit. The child must be willing to participate in the study and have written parental permission and assent to participate. The child must not have evidence of a diagnosis of a neurological or neurodevelopmental disorder before January 2016.

A 45-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis for the past 10 years is being considered for enrollment in the Argentinian Registry of Patients with Rheumatic Diseases and COVID-19 Infection. She has been on methotrexate and prednisone for the past 5 years with good control of her rheumatic disease. Recently, she tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection with no symptoms. She is interested in participating in the study to help further the understanding of how rheumatic diseases and COVID-19 interact.

A 3-year-old Hispanic boy, who lives with his parents and two siblings in a low-income neighborhood, has a BMI greater than or equal to the 50th percentile according to CDC age and sex reference standards. The boy's parents express concerns about their child's weight and have been seeking ways to improve his eating habits and physical activity level. The boy enjoys playing outside and watching TV. His parents state that they often struggle with providing healthy meals due to limited access to fresh fruits and vegetables in their neighborhood. The family speaks Spanish at home, and the parents have limited English proficiency. The boy's pediatrician recommends the NET-Works study as a way to help the family make sustainable changes in their eating and activity habits over time. The family is interested in participating and is willing to commit to the three-year intervention. They express gratitude for the opportunity to receive support in creating a healthier environment for their child.

A 25 year old male patient with spinal cord injury (SCI) due to a motor vehicle accident six months ago approached the clinic for participation in the clinical trial. He was diagnosed with ASIA scale C at neurological level T6. He has no history of hypertension, arrhythmias, coronary artery disease, diabetes, renal disease or cancer. He is not using cardioactive medications and has no current pressure ulcers. He has no history of peripheral nerve compressions or rotator cuff tears that limit his ability to row. He is medically stable and has a body mass index of 24. He is able to follow directions and his leg muscles are responsive to Functional Electrical Stimulation (FES). He is interested in participating in the Hybrid-FES exercise to prevent cardiovascular declines in acute SCI trial to improve his physical function and overall health.

A 42-year-old female patient comes to the clinic complaining of difficulty losing weight despite multiple attempts. She has a BMI of 35 and has been diagnosed with hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Her fasting blood glucose levels are consistently above 120 mg/dL, and her blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg. She reports having a sedentary lifestyle and often eating fast food due to her long work hours. She is interested in improving her health and willing to make changes in her diet, physical activity, and weight. She agrees to give informed consent and is willing to accept randomization to each group. She is a patient of one of the participating PCPs and meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with triple-vessel coronary artery disease and recommended for an elective coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has undergone percutaneous coronary intervention in the past and is currently on aspirin therapy. He smokes a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. His platelet function test revealed increased platelet activity (hypercoagulable) with a maximal amplitude (MA) of 75. He has no history of bleeding disorders, peptic ulcers, or allergic reactions to aspirin or clopidogrel. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and able to give informed consent.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and underwent a mastectomy with axillary dissection 6 months ago. She has been experiencing moderate to severe pain around the surgical site, with a median VAS score of 7. She has no history of cognitive or psychiatric troubles and is able to read, write, and understand French. She is interested in participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has not undergone immediate breast reconstruction. She has a PS score of 1 and is eager to explore new treatment options to alleviate her pain.

As this is a clinical trial focused on improving child outcomes, there is no specific patient description required. Instead, the trial will focus on recruiting low-income children who speak English and/or Spanish, and their parents and teachers. Children with significant developmental disabilities or who primarily speak a language other than Spanish or English will be excluded. Teachers who are currently participating in other research studies or who have recently completed similar studies will also be excluded.

This is a 35 year old male with a history of varicocele who is scheduled to undergo elective varicocelectomy surgery. He is in good general health with no significant medical history and is classified as an ASA 1 patient. He has no known allergies to any medications and is not currently taking any prescription medications. He has been informed about the study and has consented to participate. He does not have any coagulopathy or any contraindication for spinal anesthesia. He is willing to be randomized into one of the three groups: TAP Group (Group T), QL Group (Group Q), or Control Group (Group K). He understands that all three groups will receive spinal anesthesia and that he may receive a TAP or QL block after completion of the surgery. He will be assessed for postoperative pain using a visual analog scale and will be monitored for analgesic consumption, side effects, and overall satisfaction with the pain management protocol. He understands that he may withdraw from the study at any time and that his participation will not affect the quality of care he receives.

A 25-year-old female with a history of Hidradenitis Suppurativa presents with bilateral lesions in the axilla and groin area. She reports frequent episodes of painful nodules, abscesses, and sinus tracts that have significantly impacted her quality of life. The patient has a Fitzpatrick skin type I-II and no significant medical history. She is not pregnant and able to communicate with study personnel. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial for IPL laser therapy to alleviate her symptoms and improve her overall well-being.

64-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is currently undergoing hemodialysis treatment three times a week for the past six months. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He has a patent left internal jugular vein and requires a catheter for his hemodialysis treatment. He has no history of active infection, sensitivity to heparin, or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. His coagulation parameters are within normal limits, and he has no contraindications to dialysis at flow rates up to 450 mL/min. He is not pregnant, and he is not planning to get pregnant during the study period. He is willing and able to commit to follow-up visits and study procedures throughout the course of the study. He has not been enrolled in any randomized clinical trial (RCT) and is not concurrently enrolled in any RCT. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in this clinical trial.

A 35-year-old male patient was admitted to the respiratory care center with a history of traumatic brain injury due to a car accident. He was in a comatose state upon arrival and was intubated and mechanically ventilated. The patient had an APACHE II score of 30 upon admission to the ICU. A brain CT scan revealed evidence of intracranial hypertension with edema. The patient had a history of peptic ulcer disease diagnosed via PES more than 3 months ago, but had not received any PPI or H2 blocker therapy in the past week. The patient had a history of UGI bleeding in the ICU before transferring to the RCC, which was proven by NG aspirate of coffee ground substance. The patient had not received any PPI or H2 blocker therapy in the past week and had been taking NSAIDs for more than 7 days. The patient had no bleeding tendency or major disease. The patient and family were willing to participate in the study.

Patient B is a 42-year-old female who has been diagnosed with a benign tumor in her uterus. She has no significant past medical history, does not smoke and does not use any illicit drugs. She works as a teacher and is physically active. Her BMI is 27. She is scheduled to undergo an elective abdominal surgical procedure under general anesthesia that is expected to take more than two hours. She is classified as an ASA Physical Status 2. She has no symptoms of infection or sepsis, and her renal function is normal. She is eligible for this study and is able to provide informed consent.

55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and advanced proliferative diabetic retinopathy presents with decreased visual acuity and progressive vision loss in the left eye. Ophthalmologic examination reveals a macular traction retinal detachment lasting for three months or less. The patient has no history of previous intraocular surgery other than cataract surgery, hemodialysis, or bleeding disorders. The patient is not currently taking any anticoagulant drugs other than aspirin and has normal prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, and platelet count.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman from the United States who has been diagnosed with locally advanced breast cancer (LABC) and needs pre-surgical chemotherapy. She has undergone endocrine therapy for her estrogen and progesterone positive tumor, but it has failed. Her tumor has been found to be resistant to taxane and anthracycline regimens. She is currently in good health, with a WHO performance status of 1. Her laboratory tests show her neutrophils and platelets are within normal range, and her bilirubin and serum creatinine levels are also normal. Her breast cancer tissue has been analyzed for hormone receptor and HER2 status, and the primary tumor or at least one metastatic lesion is available for biopsy collection at protocol inclusion. She has no comorbidities that would preclude the use of cyclophosphamide at actual doses. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up schedule, and has given written informed consent according to national and local regulations.

A 55-year-old black man was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. He has been experiencing high blood pressure and has been taking antihypertensive medication for the past 6 months. He does not have any known allergies to medication. He exercises regularly for about 30 minutes a day and maintains a healthy diet. He has no symptoms of exercise intolerance or contraindications to exercise. He has not taken any ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers before. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the short-term effects of ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers on cardiac and renal protection in black type 2 diabetics patients.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) three years ago. She has been experiencing fatigue, joint pain, and a facial rash for the past year. She was recently diagnosed with lupus nephritis after presenting with edema and proteinuria. Her creatinine levels have been increasing, and her doctor has recommended treatment with immunosuppressive therapy in addition to corticosteroids. She has no history of kidney transplant, and she is not currently on dialysis. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of CellCept in treating lupus nephritis.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing frequent and severe migraine headaches for the past year. She has a history of unilateral migraine headaches that occur approximately 70% of the time. She has tried various medications and lifestyle changes to manage her symptoms, but without much success. She is currently taking birth control and has no other significant medical history. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the potential causes of migraine headaches and the effectiveness of different treatments. She is willing to undergo MRI scans and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no known allergies to medications and has not been diagnosed with any disorders of iron overload.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who has tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection by qPCR assay within the past 7 days. He is experiencing mild COVID-19 symptoms such as fever, cough, and fatigue. His oxygen saturation level is greater than 92%, and he is not short of breath at the time of enrollment. He does not have retinal eye disease or glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficiency. He does not have chronic kidney disease, stage - 5 or receiving dialysis. He is not currently taking any of the medications listed in the exclusion criteria. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He is able to tolerate oral medications, and he has no known allergies or adverse reactions to hydroxychloroquine sulfate, ribavirin, or nitazoxanide. His QTc interval is within normal limits, and he has no history of Torsade de Pointes VT or prior cardiac arrest or congenital long QT interval. He is fluent in English.

A 28-year-old male with a family history of schizophrenia is eligible to participate in a family-based genetic long-term study of brain function in schizophrenia. He has been diagnosed with schizophrenia by a psychiatrist and meets the criteria listed in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition, Text Revision (DSM-IV-TR). He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. A blood sample of 10-20 c.c will be taken from him for genetic testing. He has no history of substance abuse or major mental illness other than schizophrenia. He will participate in a 30-45 minute interview with a psychiatrist to further assess his symptoms and family history. The participant is capable of understanding the procedures and assays of the experiment.

9-year-old female with a previous diagnosis of severe aplastic anemia and no prior treatment with immunosuppressive therapy is being referred to participate in a clinical study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of eltrombopag in combination with immunosuppressive therapy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of fatigue, pallor, and shortness of breath. She has no history of previous bone marrow transplant, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is not a viable option for her. The patient is currently on no medication for her condition. She meets all inclusion criteria, has no exclusion criteria, and has normal karyotype as determined by bone marrow aspirate and biopsy. The patient will be offered the opportunity to participate in an additional 3-year long-term follow-up period upon completion of the treatment and follow-up periods. The patient's legal guardian has signed a written informed consent form for the study.

46-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of periodontal disease and tooth fracture. The patient is in good health, an ASA III, with a HbA1c level below 9%. She has been referred for a non-complicated tooth extraction and will require intraoral local anesthesia. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse. She has no known allergies to the drugs or food used in the study. The patient has been informed of the study and has given written consent to participate.

Patient is a 7-year-old boy with a history of short stature, with a height SD score less than -2.25. The patient has no history of growth hormone therapy or any other disease or drug treatment that might interfere with linear growth. The patient has had a growth hormone stimulation test and meets the inclusion criteria for this study. The patient has not had any major acute illness or surgery in the past six months, and weighs more than 15 kg. The patient's parents have provided written informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic knee pain and stiffness for the past several years. She has difficulty walking and performing daily activities due to her knee pain. She has tried conservative treatments such as physical therapy and medication but has found no relief. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and is a candidate for total knee arthroplasty. She meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial, and her physical and mental state allows her to respond to the standard questionnaires. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is aware that she will be randomly assigned to receive either a nonmodular all-polyethylene tibia (AP) fixed-bearing posterior cruciate substituting design or a modular posterior cruciate substituting rotating platform (RP) design for her total knee arthroplasty. She understands that the study will compare the clinical, functional, and radiographic results of the two designs and that the primary hypothesis is that there will be no difference in the outcome measures at a minimum two-year follow-up.

The patient is a 7-month-old infant named Liam who was brought to the Emergency Center at Beaumont, Royal Oak due to a persistent cough, difficulty breathing, wheezing, and decreased oral intake. Liam's symptoms are consistent with bronchiolitis. Liam's parents have provided informed consent for him to participate in a research study that evaluates the difference in effectiveness of nasal suction between two different suction devices (NoseFrida and bulb syringe) in infants that have bronchiolitis. Liam has no history of structural upper airway disease, including cleft palate, trachemalacia/laryngomalacia or subglottic stenosis. Liam's respiratory rate is normal and does not require respiratory support. Liam's parents have been given education on how to use their assigned suction device, which for Liam is a NoseFrida. They will monitor his breathing, eating/drinking, sleeping and how many times he has been seen by a medical provider in the 7 days post discharge from the Emergency Center. At 7 days after discharge from the Emergency Center, Liam's parents will complete a survey asking questions about how Liam has been doing over the past week.

A 50-year-old Caucasian male presented to the pulmonologist's office with symptoms of chronic cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He had a history of smoking for 30 pack-years but quit smoking 5 years ago. He reported no significant family history of lung disease or autoimmune disorders. Physical examination revealed bilateral end-inspiratory crackles in the lower lung fields. Spirometry showed mild obstruction with a FEV1/FVC ratio of 70%, and a DLCO of 60% predicted. A high-resolution CT scan showed evidence of reticular opacities and honeycombing consistent with a diagnosis of interstitial lung disease. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed the informed consent form. The patient has no history of psychiatric disorders and is able to collaborate with the researchers.

A 42-year-old accountant is scheduled to undergo surgery on his left wrist. He has a history of carpal tunnel syndrome on his left hand and has been experiencing numbness and tingling on that hand for the past year. He is otherwise healthy and doesn't take any medications regularly. The patient is married and has two school-aged children. He is right-handed and would like to return to work as soon as possible after the surgery. The patient has never undergone surgery before and is a bit anxious about the procedure. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He has no history of neuropathic lesions or polyneuropathic conditions, and he has no implanted electrical devices or allergies to local anesthetics. The patient is a suitable candidate for the study and will be included in the sample size of 60 participants for the trial.

A 35-year-old man was diagnosed with primary restless legs syndrome (RLS) two years ago. He has been taking pramipexole daily for the past six months, with the first dose taken at 4 PM. He experiences RLS symptoms mainly in the evening and at night, which disrupt his sleep. He has no history of allergies or major psychiatric or neurological disorders. He is not currently pregnant or lactating. He uses condoms for contraception. He has no history of other major sleep disorders, but he does experience occasional insomnia. He has not taken any dopamine antagonist or tramadol in the past year or three months, respectively. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

80-year-old female admitted to a skilled nursing facility following hospitalization for pneumonia. She has a history of osteoporosis, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. She has been recovering well from her pneumonia but has noticed a decline in her physical function, specifically difficulty with walking and getting out of bed. She is motivated to improve her physical function and return home. She is able to participate in physical therapy and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. Her Mini-Mental Status Exam score is 24. She has not been diagnosed with any neurological disorders or any of the other exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with ADHD by his pediatrician. He has symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that interfere with his daily functioning at home and school. He is currently taking no medications for ADHD. He is in the 5th grade and has been struggling with his grades due to his symptoms. He enjoys playing video games and watching TV in his free time. He has no significant medical history and has never been hospitalized. He is not currently on any medication, and his parents are willing to comply with any contraceptive requirements if needed. He weighs 70 pounds and his BMI is within the normal range. He has no history of seizures or cardiac problems in his family. His most recent ADHD-RS-IV score is 32 and his CGI-S score is 5.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who is not currently on any medications and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 4 weeks. He has no history of chronic illnesses, drug or alcohol abuse, or bleeding disorders. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use an effective method of contraception from 4 weeks prior to vaccination until at least 4 weeks after vaccination. He has not received any vaccines in the past 4 weeks and has not received any blood or blood-derived products in the past 3 months. He does not have a history of immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive therapy, and has not been diagnosed with HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. He has no known allergies or hypersensitivities to any vaccine components or previous adverse reactions to any vaccines. He is not currently experiencing febrile illness or acute illness/infection on the day of vaccination. The patient is willing to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all trial procedures.

A 25-year-old healthy female with no significant medical history, currently not taking any prescription or over-the-counter medications, and with a body mass index within the range of 19-30 kg/m2 is being considered for this clinical trial. She is non-smoker and non-alcoholic, and has no history of drug or alcohol addiction or abuse. She has no history of allergies or any clinically significant disorders involving any system of the body. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study period. She has no history of participating in any other clinical trial within the last 30 days. She has provided informed consent and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

28-year-old female, sex worker in Shinyanga, Tanzania. She has been working as a sex worker for the past 3 years and reports having multiple sexual partners. She has never been tested for STIs before and does not consistently use condoms during sexual encounters. She reports occasional genital itching and discharge, but has never sought medical care for these symptoms. She earns more than half of her monthly income through sex work. She is willing to participate in the study and provides oral informed consent. She is not pregnant and has a referral card from the pre-selected recruitment venue.

A 7-year-old girl was brought to the clinic by her parents for a routine check-up. She has no significant medical history and has been developing normally. She has no history of recurrent urinary tract infections or fecal incontinence. She has not undergone any genitourinary or renal surgeries, and has not been on medication for incontinence. She has not undergone any pelvic reeducation in the last 6 months. She doesn't have any neurologic problems that may influence continence. Her parents have consented to her participation in the study.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with schizophrenia 8 years ago. He has been taking olanzapine as monotherapy for the past 7 months and has a PANSS baseline score of 55. He has a history of metabolic syndrome, with a waist circumference of 100 cm, triglycerides of 200 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 35 mg/dL, and blood pressure of 130/85 mmHg. He is currently not taking any medication for his metabolic syndrome. He has completed high school education and has no history of seizures or other organic brain diseases. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 45-year-old male suffered from hemispheric ischemic stroke with a non-lacunar stroke pattern. He was admitted to the stroke unit within 24 hours of onset and has a NIHSS score greater than or equal to 7, including motor score greater than or equal to 3. He did not undergo decompressive craniectomy and is able to follow a rehabilitation program. Before the stroke onset, he had a Modified Rankin scale of 0. MRI showed no contraindication for the treatment. He has no history of cancer or pre-existing dementia, and no active inflammatory or autoimmune diseases. He is not participating in any other therapeutic trial and is a member of a social security scheme. He has provided written informed consent for the trial.

A 35 year old male patient who has been diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 10 years ago and has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for the past 6 years. Despite receiving ART, his viral load has remained detectable and he has experienced treatment failure with at least one NRTI, NNRTI, and PI class of drugs. He has been recently enrolled in an early access program for a new investigational PI and has not received Fuzeon before. He is currently seeking further treatment options and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the safety and efficacy of the investigational PI combined with Fuzeon and other background antiretroviral medications. He is not pregnant or breast-feeding, and he has no evidence of active, untreated opportunistic infection or malignancy requiring chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman who was diagnosed with HIV infection 5 years ago during routine screening. She has not started antiretroviral therapy yet as her CD4 count is above 500 x 10^6 /l and she has not experienced any HIV-related clinical manifestations. She has a history of asthma but it is well-controlled with inhalers. Her cholesterol level is 5.8 mmol/L, blood pressure is within normal range and she has no family history of cardiovascular disease. She does not take any NSAIDs or immune modulating therapies. She is not pregnant and uses effective birth control. Her liver function tests and creatinine clearance are within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the efficacy of a study drug on markers of immune activation and vaccine responses in HIV-infected patients.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with HAM/TSP based on World Health Organization diagnostic criteria. She presents with difficulty in walking, stiffness in legs, and frequent falls. She has a history of HTLV-1 infection for the past 10 years. She is currently receiving treatment with corticosteroids, but her symptoms have worsened over the past few months. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hypothyroidism, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of substance abuse or psychiatric illness. Her family history is not significant for any neurological or infectious diseases. She is willing to participate in the protocol evaluations and procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with a benign brain tumor. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril 10mg daily. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is married and has three children. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no known allergies. His pre-operative lab tests are within normal limits. He is scheduled for craniotomy in 2 days and is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the effect of acupuncture on inflammation and immune function after craniotomy. He is willing to provide informed consent and is available for acupuncture treatment starting within 48 hours after the surgery.

50 year old male with a family history of colon cancer. He has never had a colonoscopy before and is scheduled for a screening colonoscopy. He has occasional constipation and abdominal discomfort but denies any rectal bleeding or weight loss. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well controlled with medications. He does not have any allergies or contraindications for colonoscopy. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 1-year-old child diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and is homozygous for the F508del mutation (F/F). They have either completed the 24-week treatment period and safety follow-up visit in a previous study (Study VX16-809-122 Part B) or have not participated in any previous LUM/IVA treatment studies. The child has not undergone any solid organ or hematological transplantation and does not have any clinically significant laboratory abnormalities that would interfere with the study assessments or pose an undue risk for the subject.

A 32-year-old male patient fell off his bike and landed on his right shoulder. He immediately felt severe pain in the shoulder, which radiated down to his arm. He was taken to the Emergency Department where an X-ray revealed >50% superior displacement of the lateral tip of the clavicle to the acromion, and he was diagnosed with an acute acromioclavicular dislocation. The patient has no history of shoulder trauma or dislocation in the past. He is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially, and has no known drug allergies. He has no significant medical history and takes no medication. The patient is an active man and works as a personal trainer. He speaks Danish fluently and has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient will be evaluated clinically, functionally, and radiologically at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after the injury. The primary endpoint of the study is at the 3-month mark, where the patient's self-reported shoulder-related quality of life will be evaluated using the Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index. The secondary outcomes will include functional limitations, pain levels, and clinical evaluation of range of motion, the presence of scapular dyskinesia, and antero-posterior/superior-inferior instability of the clavicle.

A 35-year-old woman presented to the clinic with a history of chronic low back pain for the past 6 months. She described the pain as a dull ache that radiates to her hips and legs. The pain worsens with prolonged sitting or standing and improves with walking. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications with minimal relief. She works as a receptionist and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She has no history of surgery or inflammatory symptoms in the spine. She has not received any physical therapy or used analgesics and non-steroids in the past 6 months. She volunteered for the study and meets the inclusion criteria. She does not have any systemic infections, undiagnosed breathing difficulties, or bowel and bladder problems. She is willing to participate in the study for the next 4 weeks.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who underwent ovarian cortex cryopreservation at the age of 23 due to a diagnosis of cervical cancer. She received chemotherapy and radiotherapy as part of her treatment plan. She has been in remission for five years and is now interested in learning about her residual ovarian function and the possibility of having children in the future. She has had regular gynecological check-ups and hormone level tests since her treatment, and has not experienced any significant menopausal symptoms. She is currently in a stable relationship and would like to explore her options for fertility preservation.

A 44-year-old female with newly diagnosed primary invasive breast cancer with a clinical stage of T2. The tumor is HR positive and HER-2 negative confirmed by IHC. There is at least one measurable objective focus with a diameter > 2cm. ECoG physical fitness score is 0-1 and LVEF is ≥55%. Bone marrow function is normal with neutrophil count ≥ 1.5 × 109 / L, platelet count ≥ 100 × 109 / L, and hemoglobin ≥ 90g / L. Liver and kidney function are also normal with serum creatinine ≤ 1.5 times the upper limit of normal value, AST and ALT ≤ 2.5 times the upper limit of normal value, and total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 times the upper limit of normal value. The patient has good compliance with the planned treatment, can understand the research process of this study, and has signed the written informed consent. The patient has not received cytotoxic chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, biological therapy or radiotherapy for any reason and does not have stage IV metastasis at the initial diagnosis. The patient has no serious systemic infection or other serious diseases and is not known to be allergic or intolerant to chemotherapy drugs or their adjuvants. The patient has not had any other malignant tumors in the past 5 years, except for cured carcinoma in situ of cervix and skin cancer without melanoma. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and is willing to take appropriate contraceptive measures during the trial. The patient has not participated in other experimental studies within 30 days before the administration of the first study drug and is judged suitable for the study by the researchers.

58 yo F with advanced stage ovarian cancer with metastases to the liver and lungs, currently receiving palliative care with a life expectancy of more than 1 month. Patient presents with significant fatigue and asthenia with a score of 7/10 on the visual analogical scale. Karnofsky index is 60%. Chemotherapy and immunotherapy were stopped 4 weeks ago. Patient is not a candidate for further chemotherapy. Patient has signed an informed consent form and has social security affiliation. Past Medical History: - Ovarian cancer with liver and lung metastasis - Hypothyroidism - Hypertension - Hypercholesterolemia - Depression - Anxiety - Chronic pain - Anemia - GERD - Osteoporosis - Scoliosis - Fatty liver disease

This is a 62 year old male with history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who presented with a transient episode of right-sided weakness and slurred speech. The symptoms resolved within an hour. An ultrasound examination revealed a carotid artery stenosis of 50%. The patient has no history of cardiac disease, clotting disorder or neurological disorders other than the current symptoms. The patient is not scheduled for carotid endarterectomy or stenting and has no severe comorbidities or contraindications for MRI. The patient has not had a TIA or minor stroke in the past 3 weeks.

A 50-year-old Caucasian woman presents with a history of elevated serum C-reactive protein (CRP) levels ranging from 3-25 mg/L. She has no significant medical history, is not taking any anti-inflammatory medications, and has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to examine the role of cherry consumption in reducing risk factors for chronic inflammatory diseases. She is willing to supplement her diet with 280 g/d of pitted Bing cherries for 28 days and return to her normal diet for the remaining 28 days of the study. She is able to follow the study protocol and record all foods and drinks consumed during the study. She is willing to have fasting blood samples collected on study days 1, 8, 22, 36, and 64. She meets all the eligibility criteria for the study.

A 65-year-old African American woman visited the ophthalmologist with complaints of blurry vision and difficulty in seeing at night. She was diagnosed with open-angle glaucoma with a high intraocular pressure (IOP) of 32 mmHg in her left eye. She was prescribed bimatoprost 0.03%/timolol 0.5% drops, which she has been using for the past 4 weeks. However, her IOP remained uncontrolled at 30 mmHg in her left eye despite regular use of the medication. She has no known allergies and a medical history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Her visual acuity is 20/40 in both eyes, and she has no corneal dystrophies. She is willing to discontinue all other ocular hypotensive medications for the duration of the study, and is able to attend all study visits. She provides informed consent to participate in the study.

A 25-year-old woman has been experiencing abdominal pain, bloating, and irregular bowel movements for the past 6 months. She has tried various diets and over-the-counter medications with no improvement. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any prescription medications. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She underwent a colonoscopy and was diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Her gastroenterologist recommended her for a fecal calprotectin collection protocol study to evaluate the severity of her IBD symptoms. She has agreed to participate in the study and is willing to provide stool samples for testing. She understands the study protocol and requirements and is willing to follow them. She has provided informed consent in accordance with the IRB approved form.

The patient is a 47-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage III cervical cancer after presenting with abnormal vaginal bleeding and pelvic pain. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of squamous-cell carcinoma. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled on medications. She has never received pelvic or abdominal radiotherapy, nor has she undergone a total or partial hysterectomy. She is not currently receiving any form of antineoplastic treatment apart from weekly concomitant cisplatin (40 mg/m2) due to her diagnosis. She is able to tolerate the chemotherapy well so far. MRI imaging of her pelvis and retroperitoneal space has been performed and she is considered suitable for curative treatment with definitive radio-(chemo)therapy including MRI guided brachytherapy. She has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who suffered an ischemic stroke three months ago. She experiences persistent weakness and difficulty moving her left arm, which has affected her ability to perform daily activities such as dressing and grooming herself. She has a moderate disability and requires some help from her family members. She has no history of hemorrhagic stroke or functional disability prior to her stroke. She does not have expressive or receptive aphasia and is able to understand instructions and verbalize discomfort. She has no history of severe emphysema, bullous disease, spontaneous pneumothorax, or chest surgery. She also does not have a history of depression requiring medications and is not pregnant. She has not undergone any non-conventional rehab therapies such as acupuncture, botulinum toxin injections, or massage therapy. She does not have significant claustrophobia and is willing to attend daily hyperbaric oxygen therapy treatment and two osteopathic manipulative therapy sessions per week for up to six weeks.

A 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with coronary artery disease by his cardiologist is scheduled for elective coronary angiography at the Cardiology Department of Abant İzzet Baysal University İzzet Baysal Training and Research Hospital. He has not previously undergone this procedure and has not received any training on the process. He is able to read and write and has no hearing loss or psychiatric illness. The patient is conscious and willing to participate in the study aimed at investigating the effects of education and music listening on anxiety and physiological parameters during coronary angiography.

Patient Description:  The patient is a 32-year-old female diagnosed with Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1 (PH1) four years ago. She has a history of recurrent kidney stones and has undergone several surgeries in the past. Her most recent 24-hour urine oxalate excretion was 96 mg and her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 70 mL/min/1.73 m2. She is currently taking vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) and has been on a stable regimen for the past 6 months. She has no history of liver disease or any other major medical condition, and her liver function tests (LFTs) are within normal limits. She has not participated in any clinical study or received any investigational agent in the past 6 months. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and comply with study requirements.

An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension and coronary artery disease was referred to the clinic for heart surgery due to worsening symptoms of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has been experiencing irregular heartbeats and was diagnosed with atrial fibrillation one year ago. He takes multiple medications including anticoagulants and beta-blockers. He has never had heart surgery before. He is retired and lives with his wife. He is able to perform activities of daily living but has limited mobility due to arthritis.

The patient is a 48-year-old female who has a history of high cholesterol (LDL-C ≥ 3.40 mmol/L) and a BMI of 25.5 kg/m2. She is currently taking thyroid medication and an antihypertensive agent to manage her hypertension. She does not smoke or drink alcohol heavily. She has no history of cardiovascular events or chronic diseases, and her laboratory results at screening showed no clinically significant abnormalities. She is not currently involved in any clinical trials or taking any medication or supplements that would interfere with the study parameters. She has no allergies or sensitivities to the test product ingredients, nor to the three antibiotics (Clindamycin, Erythromycin, and Ampicillin). She is interested in participating in the study to assess the effects of Lactobacillus reuteri NCIMB 30242 on her plasma bile acid profile.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is interested in undergoing a breast augmentation procedure. She is unhappy with the size and shape of her breasts, which has caused her to feel self-conscious and uncomfortable with her appearance. The patient has not had any previous breast implant surgery and is seeking primary breast augmentation. She has adequate tissue available to cover implants and is willing to undergo regular MRI scans at designated sites throughout the trial. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, and has no history of abscess or infection in the body at the time of enrollment. She is in good overall health, with no clinically known conditions that may impact wound healing ability or pose a surgical risk. The patient is psychologically prepared for the surgical procedure and the use of breast implants, and is willing to undergo further surgery for revision if medically required.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been paralyzed since a car accident two years ago. He has a spinal cord injury at the T12 level and uses a manual wheelchair as his primary means of mobility. He reports experiencing upper extremity pain and discomfort when propelling his wheelchair for extended periods of time. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to improve his manual wheelchair propulsion technique to minimize pain and improve efficiency. He has not competed in wheelchair racing in the past year and is more than one year post-inpatient rehabilitation.

The patient is a healthy male of any ethnic origin between the ages of 18 and 55, with a body mass index (BMI) between 18 and 31 kg/m2. He must have a body weight greater than 50 kg and should not have any clinically significant disorders, including neurological, gastrointestinal, renal, hepatic, cardiovascular, psychiatric, respiratory, metabolic, endocrine, haematological or other major disorders. He must not have a positive urine drug screen or alcohol breath test result at screening or first admission, or a history of substance abuse in the last 12 months prior to the start of the study. He should not have any significant history of alcoholism or drug/chemical abuse. He must not smoke more than 5 cigarettes or the equivalent in tobacco per day. The patient must be willing to use appropriate contraception such as condom with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository from the time of the first dose until 3 months after the final dosing occasion. The patient must have given written informed consent to participate in the study and to abide by the study restrictions.

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and frequent nosebleeds since her teenage years. She has been diagnosed with von Willebrand disease type 2B by her hematologist and is currently on treatment with desmopressin and von Willebrand factor replacement therapy. She has no other significant medical history, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol socially. She is a social insured patient and has agreed to participate in the clinical trial. She is not pregnant and has provided her consent to participate in the sublingual capillary bed analysis by video-microscopy to assess her hemorrhagic risk. Her hematologist believes that this non-invasive technique may be beneficial in predicting her risk of bleeding from angiodysplasias.

A 32-year old office worker was admitted to the hospital for a scheduled surgery on her left knee. She is generally healthy, with no significant past medical history except for occasional knee pain. She lives alone in a small apartment in the city. She is a non-smoker and doesn't consume alcohol or use any illicit drugs. The patient is anxious about the upcoming surgery but is looking forward to returning to work soon after recovery. She is expected to be hospitalized for 5 days. She has no known allergies to any fabrics or materials. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve the patient experience.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages 3, 4, or 5, confirmed by the Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) using the CKD Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) formula. The patient has stable HemoCue Hgb levels ranging from 8.5 to 10.5 at the screening visit (Week -4) and from 8.5 to 10.0 g/dL at randomization (Day 1). The patient has not received any intravenous (IV) iron dose between screening visit and randomization (Day 1), but may be on stable maintenance oral iron supplementation. The patient is capable of giving signed informed consent and is willing to comply with the contraceptive guidance during the treatment period and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose of study treatment. The patient has

This is a 45-year-old male veteran with a past medical history of a psychotic disorder consistent with criteria established by the Serious Mental Illness Treatment Research and Evaluation Center (SMITREC). He has been receiving outpatient mental health treatment for the past six months, with at least two outpatient visits during this time. He has a patient-identified family member or caregiver who he sees for at least one hour or more on a monthly basis. The treating therapist or psychiatrist has assessed him as clinically stable enough to participate in the program. The patient has decisional capacity to provide informed consent. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the brief Family Member Provider Outreach (FMPO) intervention in engaging families in the processes of care and improving the quality of care for persons with severe mental illness. The patient has not attended FPE group sessions or had monthly clinician contact in the last six months, and is not homeless.

A 42-year-old woman was diagnosed with high-grade soft tissue sarcoma in her left thigh. She reported a 3-month history of a painless, progressively enlarging mass in her thigh. She denied any history of trauma or radiation exposure. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, which was well controlled with medications. Her family history was negative for any cancer. Physical examination revealed a large, firm, and immobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm in diameter in her left thigh. No evidence of metastasis was seen on chest X-ray or abdominal CT scan. Biopsy of the mass confirmed the diagnosis of high-grade soft tissue sarcoma. The patient was scheduled to undergo treatment with chemotherapy followed by surgery. She was enrolled in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of PET scan combined with CT scan in evaluating treatment response in patients undergoing treatment for bone cancer or soft tissue sarcoma. She underwent a baseline FDG-PET/CT scan, which revealed increased glucose metabolic activity in the left thigh mass. She then underwent FDG-PET/CT scans at 2 weeks and 12 weeks after the start of treatment.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain, chest distress, and palpitations for the past month. He was diagnosed with unstable angina pectoris and has been taking medication for his symptoms. The patient also has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and meets the inclusion criteria, including a score of 18 on the Chinese medicine symptoms scales of "Xueyu Zheng" for Blood Stasis Syndrome. He has not experienced any infections, fever, trauma, surgery, or inflammation in the past month and has no history of tuberculosis, rheumatological disorders, hematopoietic system diseases, or mental disorders. His liver and renal function are within normal limits. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic knee pain due to a meniscus tear. The patient is scheduled for arthroscopic knee surgery. The patient has no known allergies and has an ASA physical status of II. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. The patient does not have any contraindications to the peripheral nerve block. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is scheduled for a unilateral knee arthroscopy and is eligible to receive either dexamethasone with bupivacaine or dexmedetomidine with bupivacaine as part of the multimodal analgesic regimen.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing knee pain and difficulty walking for the past few months. He has been diagnosed with a meniscal tear and is scheduled for a diagnostic knee arthroscopy. He has no history of diabetes, renal or hepatic dysfunction, and has not experienced any allergic reactions to medications in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo a femoral nerve block with either a long-acting local anesthetic alone or with an adjuvant of Dexmedetomidine.

The patient is a 35-year-old Danish woman who has been experiencing persistent health anxiety for the past year. She often fears that she has a serious illness and frequently visits her doctor to seek reassurance. Despite multiple medical tests showing no significant health issues, she finds it difficult to believe and continues to worry about her health. She has been struggling with sleep and appetite disturbances, as well as difficulty concentrating at work due to her constant health worries. She has no history of substance abuse or psychotic conditions. She speaks Danish as her native language and has never received cognitive-behavioral treatment in the past. She works as a nurse and has been able to maintain her job despite her health anxiety.

72-year-old male with a history of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and recent onset blurry vision in his right eye with suspicion of the presence of choroidal neovascularization (CNV). He has been previously treated with intravitreal injections of anti-VEGF agents. He reports no other ocular history, including no history of uveitis, diabetes, or other ocular conditions. The patient is able to provide informed consent and has no known allergies to angiographic dye. His best corrected visual acuity in the study eye is currently 20/40. The patient has no family history of AMD and no concurrent unrelated eye diagnosis that would interfere with image acquisition or interpretation. He is willing to undergo multiple imaging modalities to detect the cellular immune response in the study eye.

A 47-year-old male patient with a medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented with a large, raised, and irregularly shaped mole on his left shoulder. The mole had started to itch and bleed occasionally, and the patient had noticed a change in its size and shape over the past few months. The patient underwent a biopsy that confirmed the presence of BRAF V600E mutation-positive metastatic melanoma. The patient has not received any prior treatment with BRAF or MEK inhibitors. The patient has measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1 criteria, with multiple lung and liver metastases. The patient has Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status score of 1, and his baseline organ function is adequate. The patient has no history of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency or any serious pre-existing medical conditions that could interfere with the participant's safety, obtaining informed consent, or compliance with study procedures. The patient does not have any known cardiovascular risk factors, retinal vein occlusion (RVO), or central serous retinopathy (CSR). The patient has no history of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis. The patient has signed written informed consent and is willing to undergo tumour and skin biopsies. The patient is a non-smoker and is not currently pregnant or lactating.

This is a 42-year-old female who recently received a diagnosis of high cholesterol levels during a routine check-up at her primary care physician's office. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes, and she is currently not taking any cholesterol-lowering medications. She is concerned about the long-term health implications of high cholesterol and is interested in discussing treatment options with her GP. She is fluent in Danish and able to read and understand medical information in Danish.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of gastric cancer. He underwent a biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of locally advanced gastric cancer. The patient has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. He has no known allergies to any medications. The preoperative examination (CT/MRI) demonstrated a resectable gastric cancer with T4 stage. His cardiac, renal, liver, and bone marrow functions are all adequate. The patient has not received any cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy prior to enrollment in the trial. The patient is willing to participate and has provided written informed consent. He will be randomized into either the HIPEC group or the control group and will undergo either radical gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and HIPEC with paclitaxel and 5-Fu or just radical gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy. The patient will receive postoperative chemotherapy (SOX or XELOX) for 6 cycles and will be followed up for 5 years or until death.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been struggling with depression for the past 5 years. She has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) and has tried various antidepressants with little to no success. She is currently taking fluoxetine at a dose of 40mg/day for the past 8 weeks, but she still feels hopeless, lost interest in activities she used to enjoy, and has difficulty sleeping. Her HAMD-17 score is 22, and her cognitive factors score is 8. She is married, works as an accountant, and has two children who are 7 and 9 years old. She reports feeling guilty about not being able to take care of her children and husband as she used to. She denies having any suicidal thoughts or attempts. She has no history of liver, kidney, or endocrine diseases, cardiovascular or respiratory system diseases, hematologic diseases, or cancer. She has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past one month. She is willing to participate in this study and is hoping to find relief from her depressive symptoms.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who was diagnosed with probable Alzheimer's Disease (AD) a year ago. She presents with memory loss, difficulty with language and communication, and trouble with daily tasks such as dressing and bathing. Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. She is currently taking donepezil for AD. She lives at home with her husband, who is her primary caregiver. She has no history of C. difficile infection and has not taken antibiotics or been hospitalized in the past 6 months. She has no known allergies to rifaximin. She is willing and able to comply with all scheduled clinic visits and has a family caregiver who has regular contact with her. She has not participated in another investigational drug trial in the past 30 days. Her Mini Mental State Exam (MMSE) score is 18. She is eligible for the study and may benefit from rifaximin's unique properties of altering gut microbiota and lowering blood ammonia levels to improve her cognition and function.

A 45-year-old Hispanic male with a BMI of 35 and waist circumference of 105 cm presented to the clinic complaining of fatigue and difficulty in performing daily activities. He has a history of hypertension and hypertriglyceridemia. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He works in an office and does not have any regular exercise habits. He has been diagnosed with metabolic syndrome with a fasting glucose level of 125 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol level of 38 mg/dL, and triglyceride level of 200 mg/dL. He has no history of ischemic heart disease or diabetes. He is currently not taking any medications for his conditions. He has no significant past medical or surgical history.
