He is married with two children and lives in a suburban area in Brazil. He has a sedentary lifestyle and has not had any weight loss attempts in the past. He is fluent in Portuguese and has no difficulty in reading or understanding instructions. He is willing to participate in a 12-week lifestyle intervention program to improve his cardiometabolic health.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for the past 6 months. He has been taking 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) but has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He reports experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and blood in his stool. He has a Mayo Scoring System Assessment of Ulcerative Colitis Activity score of 6 at the time of screening. He has never had a diagnosis of Crohn's disease or indeterminate colitis. He does not have any known allergies to any of the ingredients in the study drug. He has not made any changes to his therapy within the past 2 weeks. He does not have any other significant medical conditions or laboratory abnormalities that would preclude him from participating in the study. He is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. He agrees to use two medically reliable methods of contraception during the study period. He has adequate cardiac, renal, and hepatic function as determined by the principal investigators. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have a history of active alcohol or drug abuse and has not smoked tobacco within the past 2 weeks before study entry.

The patient is a 65-year-old female with a history of wet age-related macular degeneration (wet-AMD) in her right eye. She has been experiencing blurriness and distortion in her right eye for the past 6 months. Her best corrected visual acuity in the affected eye is 20/80. She has no significant past medical history other than controlled hypertension and occasional migraines. She is currently taking amlodipine and ibuprofen PRN. She has never received any treatment for her wet-AMD. Her ophthalmic examination reveals subfoveal and perifoveal active choroidal neovascularization (CNV) lesions secondary to AMD with a total area of 20 mm2. The best corrected visual acuity in her left eye is 20/20. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits.

Patient is a 22-year-old sedentary female from the United States who presents to the clinic with no specific complaints. She reports no significant medical or surgical history and is not taking any medications. She denies any history of neurological or lower limb dysfunction or pain. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. Her vital signs are within normal limits and her physical examination is unremarkable. She is interested in participating in a study evaluating the effects of proprioceptive exercises on a vibratory platform versus a stable surface.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with mild-moderate aphasia after suffering a stroke a few days ago. His Token Test Score ranges between 7 and 40, indicating mild to moderate language impairment. He is right-handed and his mother tongue is Dutch. He has undergone a standard imaging procedure (CT or MRI) prior to inclusion in the study. He is able to undergo functional and specific linguistic testing and therapy in the acute phase following the stroke. He has no history of other diseases of the central nervous system, psychological disorders or developmental speech and language disorders. He has not undergone any prior brain surgery. He does not excessively use alcohol or drugs. He has signed the informed consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with ovarian cancer. She underwent surgery to remove the tumor and has now been recommended for chemotherapy with taxane/carboplatin. She has a Karnofsky score of 80 and a life expectancy of more than 6 months. She has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. She has never smoked and does not consume alcohol. She reports occasional nausea and vomiting during her menstrual cycle but has no other significant medical history. She is not currently taking any medication and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy who was born at full term with no complications during pregnancy and delivery. However, his parents noticed that he was not meeting developmental milestones such as sitting up or crawling at the expected age. His pediatrician referred him to the Department of Children and Adolescent Psychiatry at Kaohsiung Chang Gung Memorial Hospital for evaluation. After a joint assessment by a team of experts, he was diagnosed with developmental delay. His parents were offered a family-based early intervention program at the hospital, which they agreed to participate in. The child's primary caregiver is his mother who is a stay-at-home mom. The family lives in the city and has access to transportation to the hospital. The child is not diagnosed with autism or cerebral palsy.

A 9-year-old boy with no known underlying medical conditions is being recruited for a study on respiratory particle production in children. He is currently in the third grade and enjoys playing video games and reading books. He has no history of respiratory issues, and his parents report that he has never been hospitalized. He has no allergies to food or medications. He has been wearing a face mask to school due to the COVID-19 pandemic and has no difficulty wearing it for extended periods. His parents have given their consent for him to participate in the study.

42-year-old male with no significant past medical history presents to the emergency department with a terrible triad injury of the right elbow. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustained an elbow dislocation along with fractures of the coronoid process of the ulna and the radial head. The patient reports severe pain and difficulty moving the affected arm. The elbow is visibly swollen and tender to touch. The patient is neurovascularly intact. Imaging studies confirm the diagnosis of terrible triad injury. The patient is deemed a candidate for surgical treatment and is enrolled in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to his liver and bones. He has already undergone chemotherapy and radiation, but unfortunately, the cancer has progressed despite the treatment. The patient has no other significant medical history, and his performance status is 1 (able to carry out light work). His blood tests are normal, and he has no major organ dysfunction. The patient has measurable disease as defined by RECIST 1.1, and at least one tumor site is accessible for biopsy. He is willing to undergo biopsy of the tumor site to obtain a sample for the personalized vaccine. The patient is not currently receiving any other anti-cancer therapy or immunotherapy, and has not received any investigational agents within 28 days prior to the first dose of study drug. The patient has not received a solid organ transplant or allogeneic bone marrow transplant. If female, the patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study participation and for 90 days following completion of therapy.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who recently underwent enucleation surgery due to ocular melanoma. She is now scheduled for orbital ball implant surgery and is concerned about the pain and discomfort associated with the procedure. She has a history of mild hypertension and takes medication for it. The patient is generally healthy and active but is anxious about undergoing surgery. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help improve pain management and reduce the risk of side effects from anesthesia.

A 45 year old male veteran with a history of military service and combat exposure presenting with symptoms of depression including low mood, loss of interest in activities, feelings of worthlessness, and fatigue. Patient has a PHQ-9 score of 15 and has previously received treatment for depression with both psychotherapy and antidepressant medication. The patient is willing to provide signed, informed consent to participate in the study and is interested in exploring personalized treatment options for their depression. The patient has no current serious co-occurring psychiatric illness and is not currently using an antipsychotic medication or augmentation therapy. The patient is not currently incarcerated and does not require urgent or inpatient care.

28-year-old female of Indian descent, residing in India, with a BMI of 20. She is sexually active and at risk of pregnancy. She has no history of venous or arterial thrombotic/thromboembolic events or cerebrovascular accidents. She does not have migraines with focal neurological symptoms, diabetes mellitus with vascular involvement, severe hypertension, severe dyslipoproteinemia, pancreatitis associated with severe hypertriglyceridemia, or severe hepatic disease. She is not experiencing undiagnosed vaginal bleeding and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has not participated in any investigational drug use or clinical trial in the last 2 months.

78 year old woman, living alone and independently. She has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis. She has had a few falls in the past year and reports feeling unsteady on her feet. She can rise from a high chair and stand without support, but she experiences occasional balance impairment. She does not have a dementia diagnosis and does not engage in intense exercise more than 3 hours per week. She is interested in participating in this study to improve her strength and balance in order to prevent falls and maintain her independence. She is open to using a mobile application or a booklet for exercise guidance.

Patient is a 54-year-old male from Germany who was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. He presents with cough, dyspnea, and occasional chest pain. His BMI is 24, BP: 130/80, HR: 80/min. His laboratory study is remarkable for elevated CEA level, but otherwise within normal limits (Ca: 9.5mg/dl, Phosphorus: 3.0mg/dl, PTH: 32pg/ml). CT scan revealed a 5 cm mass in the right upper lobe of the lung with ipsilateral hilar and mediastinal lymph node involvement. PET/CT showed no distant metastasis. Brain MRI is clear. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria. He is willing to participate in the NEOMUN study and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old post-9/11 veteran who served in the Marine Corps for four years. He was deployed to Iraq twice and Afghanistan once. He reports experiencing multiple concussions during his deployments, but has not received a formal diagnosis of TBI. He also reports experiencing symptoms of depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbance. He currently works as a mechanic and has difficulty completing tasks due to chronic pain in his back and knees. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but reports occasional alcohol use to cope with his symptoms. He lives alone and has limited social support. He is interested in participating in the study remotely due to scheduling conflicts with work.

I apologize, but this clinical trial does not involve patients as it focuses on the impact of emotional labor on job satisfaction and burnout among nurses. It aims to gather data and analyze the results to improve the working conditions and well-being of nurses. Therefore, there is no patient description needed for this study.

A 58-year-old African American woman came to the clinic with a history of non-small cell lung cancer. She was diagnosed with stage IV adenocarcinoma with metastasis to the lungs, liver, and bones. She has lost 8% of her body weight in the past 6 months, and her BMI is now 19 kg/m2. She has been experiencing fatigue, nausea, and vomiting for the past few weeks. She is currently receiving chemotherapy with a platinum-based regimen and pemetrexed. She has normal renal and liver function. She has signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial to determine the safety and tolerability of PF-06946860 for the treatment of cachexia associated with cancer. She will be receiving subcutaneous doses of the study drug every 3 weeks for a total of 5 doses during the 12-week treatment period. She will be monitored for changes in body weight, blood pressure, heart rate, and Lumbar Skeletal Muscle Index (LSMI) by CT scan. Blood samples will be collected to evaluate safety, measure the amount of the study drug in the blood, examine the effects of the study drug on levels of a specific cytokine, and for exploratory samples for bio banking. The impact of the study drug on appetite, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, physical function, and health-related quality of life will be measured with questionnaires. The impact of study drug on physical activity will be monitored using wearable digital sensors. The effect of study drug on ability to complete anti-tumor treatment and survival will be evaluated in participants with cancer and cachexia. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not planned radiation therapy as part of the primary anti-tumor therapy regimen.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history, currently not taking any medications or herbal supplements. He has a BMI within the range of 20-25 and has not experienced any recent injuries or surgeries. He does not smoke or consume alcohol beyond the recommended limits. He has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 3 months and has not donated blood within the past 2 months. He has not been diagnosed with any gastrointestinal diseases and has not consumed grapefruit juice within 7 days prior to the study. His clinical laboratory test values are negative for HBsAg, HCV Ab, HIV Ag/Ab, and VDRL. He is willing to adhere to the protocol requirements and sign an informed consent form.

A 32-year old pregnant woman is scheduled for an elective cesarean section due to a previous cesarean section delivery. She is in good health with no pre-existing medical conditions. She is expecting her second child and is excited to welcome a new addition to her family. She is of Hispanic origin and speaks fluent Spanish and English. She has no known allergies and does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. The patient is fully informed about the study by a member of the research team and has given written consent to participate. She will be randomly assigned to one of three groups. The control group will receive no active warming, study group 1 will have pre- and intraoperative intravenous fluid warming, and study group 2 will have the same as study group 1 with additional intraoperative warming air blown into a blanket covering the body. Her temperature will be monitored at regular intervals, and she will be assessed for shivering and comfort level with regard to her temperature. Following delivery of the placenta, a blood sample taken from the placental cord will be sent for analysis of cord blood gases. The patient is excited to participate in the study and hopes that the findings will help improve the recovery process for future patients undergoing cesarean sections.

The patient is a 55-year-old Chinese man who recently experienced chest pain and was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but no other major medical conditions. He is currently taking medication for his hypertension and cholesterol. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is concerned about the risk of recurrent cardiac events and is interested in participating in a genetic study to understand the role of genetic factors in ACS recurrence. He is willing to provide blood samples for DNA extraction and is committed to attending follow-up appointments for 2 years. He hopes that the study will help identify personalized treatment strategies based on his genetic profile and improve his long-term prognosis.

The patient is a 7-year-old male child who was diagnosed with spinal lipoma during a routine check-up. The child's parents were concerned about frequent urination and occasional loss of bladder control. The child has no other underlying medical conditions and has not undergone any major surgeries. The child's height and weight are within normal limits for his age. The child's neurological examination revealed normal reflexes, but a slight weakness and decreased sensation in the lower extremities. The child's MRI showed a tethered spinal cord with a lipoma at the lower end. The child is undergoing surgery to remove the lipoma and mobilize the spinal cord. As part of the clinical trial, the child's blood, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid will be collected before and during the surgery to identify lipid species that can be used as potential biomarkers for predicting neurological deterioration. The child's parents have given informed consent for their child's participation in the study.

A 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease requiring haemodialysis support was recently diagnosed with COVID-19. He has been experiencing mild symptoms such as fever and cough for the past 5 days. He has been hospitalized in one of the study centers in Lyon, France. He is currently on oxygen therapy at 2L/min and his arterial pressure is stable at 120/70 mmHg. He has not been treated with non-steroids anti-inflammatory agents in the last 14 days. He is not currently pregnant and is not under guardianship or curatorship. He has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who experienced an anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) within the last 30 days. He had a successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent implantation to the infarct-related artery (IRA) within the last 30 days with residual stenosis no greater than 30%. The patient has a screening left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 42% by echocardiography which was repeated after 4 days of the procedure. The patient is considered hemodynamically stable at the time of enrollment and immediately prior to cell delivery. He has no significant coronary lesions, other than the index lesion of the IRA. The patient does not have a history of significant ventricular arrhythmia not related to the index STEMI or a history of cerebro-vascular accident or transient ischemic attack within 6 months of enrollment. The patient has no significant co-morbidities that would preclude his participation in the trial. The patient has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with study follow-up visits.

As a clinical trial specialist, I must clarify that this is not a trial involving the recruitment of patients. Instead, it is a clinical utility study aimed at evaluating the impact of the Decipher test on the treatment recommendations of radiation oncologists. The patient cases used in this study are based on real but de-identified patient data collected in a separate IRB-approved protocol. Therefore, there are no patient descriptions to generate for this study.

The study is looking for neonatal patients who are currently admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit and are receiving non-invasive respiratory support such as nasal cannula, continuous positive airway pressure or nasal prong ventilation. The study will measure nasopharyngeal pressure to determine the actual upper airway pressure created by the therapy. Infants with oral, nasal, or palatal deformities will be excluded from the study. Any neonatal patient who meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet the exclusion criteria is eligible for the study.

This is a 25-year-old male who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma involving the mediastinum. The patient underwent radiation and chemotherapy treatment and is now in remission. The patient has no history of cardiac disease and has never experienced any symptoms of chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. The patient is not pregnant and has no contraindications to cardiac MRI. The patient's glomerular filtration rate is within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of the long-term effects of radiation and chemotherapy treatment on cardiac health among Hodgkin's lymphoma survivors.

A 47-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). He has completed six cycles of CHOP-based therapy and has achieved partial response (PR) per the investigator's assessment. He is currently under evaluation for participation in a clinical trial that will evaluate the efficacy of pralatrexate in extending response and survival following CHOP-based chemotherapy. He is in good health and has no history of other malignancies except for non-melanoma skin cancer, which was treated and resolved more than five years ago. He has normal blood, liver, and kidney function. He has agreed to practice a medically acceptable contraceptive regimen during the study treatment initiation until at least 30 days after the last administration of pralatrexate. He has given written informed consent and is willing to attend regular clinic visits to evaluate his disease and health.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman scheduled for abdominal surgery to remove a benign tumor. She has no known allergies to any medications and has not had any previous surgeries. She has a history of hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She does not have any neurological or eye diseases, and she is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have a pacemaker or any other implanted medical devices. She does not have any known history of gravis or other neuromuscular diseases. She is able to provide informed consent and is not currently under psychiatric care. She is not currently residing in a healthcare or social institution. She is not experiencing a medical emergency.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with a history of advanced metastatic prostate cancer, which has progressed despite multiple lines of conventional treatment including chemotherapy and radiation therapy. The patient has a performance status of 1 on the ECOG scale and is considered to have a life expectancy of at least 3 months. The patient's hematological, hepatic, and renal functions are within normal limits. The patient has no active concurrent malignancy and has not received any investigational or conventional chemotherapy, targeted therapy, endocrine therapy, or immunotherapy within the past 4 weeks. The patient has not received any radiation therapy within the past 28 days and does not require therapeutic levels of anticoagulation therapy. The patient has not failed treatment with a bone marrow transplant and does not have active uncontrolled infection or any other serious illness that would impair the ability to receive protocol treatment. The patient has not been exposed to RH-1 previously. The patient has given written informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to practice a medically acceptable contraceptive regimen from study treatment initiation until at least 90 days after the last administration of RH-1.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with asthma and has been using inhaled therapies for the past 5 years. He works as a teacher and has a busy schedule, often finding it difficult to manage his asthma symptoms during the day. He has noticed that he sometimes forgets to use his inhaler or uses it incorrectly, leading to worsening of his symptoms. He has tried various inhalers but finds it difficult to remember which one to use at what time. He is currently under the care of a pneumologist and has a home health provider who monitors his respiratory equipment. He has a mobile phone and is willing to participate in the study to improve his adherence to the inhaled therapies. He speaks fluent French and is covered by a social security scheme.

32F diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) with a history of recurrent malar rash, joint pain, and afternoon fever lasting for more than six months. Patient complains of edema, weight gain, and decreased urine output. On examination, she has a blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, bilateral pitting edema of the lower limbs, and a positive lupus serology. Urine analysis reveals proteinuria (UPCR 2.5 g/g) and red blood cell casts. Renal function tests show serum creatinine of 1.2 mg/dL and serum albumin of 3.2 g/dl. She underwent a renal biopsy which showed class IV lupus nephritis. The patient was started on immunosuppressive therapy with prednisolone and cyclophosphamide. She will be included in the study and will be monitored for more than six months after the start of therapy to assess treatment response.

45-year-old male with a history of carbon monoxide intoxication resulting from a gas leak in his home. He was found unconscious and was hospitalized for several weeks. Following his discharge from the hospital, he began experiencing symptoms of Parkinsonism, including gait disturbances, mask face, rigidities, and small steps. He has not responded well to levodopa treatment. His medical history is significant for hypertension, and he is currently taking lisinopril to manage his blood pressure. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He is able to tolerate PET scanning and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing erectile dysfunction for the past 8 months. He has no significant medical history and is generally in good health. He has tried PDE5 inhibitors but has been unable to achieve and maintain an erection sufficient for penetration. He has an International Index of Erectile Function score of 14. He is in a stable heterosexual relationship of 5 years. He has not undergone any pelvic surgery or radiotherapy treatment. He is not taking any blood thinners or anti-androgens.

This is a 42-year-old woman who is overweight with a BMI of 31. She has a sedentary lifestyle and does not engage in vigorous activity for more than 30 minutes per day, more than two times per week. Her waist circumference is 38 inches, and she has no history of hypertension or diabetes. Her HbA1c is 6.2%, and her fasting glucose is 110 mg/dL. She has a triglyceride level of 165 mg/dL and a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg. She is not currently taking any antihypertensive medications, diabetic medications or medications known to alter insulin sensitivity. She does not have any chronic diseases or history of cardiac arrhythmias, myocardial infarction or stroke. She has no renal or hepatic dysfunction, and her hematocrit is 38%. She is not currently participating in a weight loss program and has not received any investigational drug therapy in the past month.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with clear cell renal cell carcinoma two years ago. She underwent a radical nephrectomy and received VEGF-targeted therapy as a first-line treatment. However, after 10 months of treatment, her disease progressed and the therapy was discontinued. She is now experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and lower back pain. Imaging studies show progression of the disease and she is considered to have advanced or metastatic renal cell carcinoma. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial and is willing to be treated with cabozantinib tablets according to the current local Summary of Product Characteristics in France as a second-line treatment. She is otherwise in good general health and has no other significant medical history. She is able and willing to provide informed consent.

A 12-year-old boy was diagnosed with a glioblastoma multiforme tumor in his brain. He underwent surgical resection of the tumor followed by radiation therapy and chemotherapy. However, the tumor has recurred and has progressed despite previous therapies. He is currently experiencing headaches, seizures, and difficulty with speech and coordination. He has no underlying medical conditions, and his medical history is unremarkable. He is not taking any medications or supplements. He lives with his parents and two siblings, who are all supportive of his treatment. He is a good student and enjoys playing video games and soccer.

John is a 65-year-old retired accountant who has been diagnosed with bilateral dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) in the past year. He has a valid driving license and still drives frequently to visit his grandchildren who live in another state. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/30 in both eyes, and his binocular visual field is 140° along the horizontal meridian and 25° above and below the same meridian. He has no other ocular diseases and maintains good overall health. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how his condition may affect his driving abilities and whether there are any interventions he can take to improve his driving skills.

This is a 45 year-old female who is generally healthy and has no history of smoking, medication use, or known diseases that require regular medication. She has no known risk factors for cardiovascular disease such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, heredity, obesity, or peripheral vascular disease. She does not engage in regular physical activity, but is not considered an athlete. She has no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, atrial fibrillation, or other obvious arrhythmias. She is not currently taking any medications containing dipyridamole or known to cause hypersensitivity to adenosine.

25 yo F with single ventricle physiology post-Fontan palliation, referred by cardiology clinic for exercise intolerance and dyspnea on exertion. She describes difficulty walking up stairs, and has stopped participating in sports. She denies chest pain or syncope. She has a history of pulmonary valve replacement at age 12, and has been doing well, without any significant hospitalizations since. She takes aspirin and enalapril daily. On physical exam, she is afebrile, BP 110/70, HR 85, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air. Her lungs are clear and her heart sounds are normal, with no murmurs or gallops. She has no peripheral edema. Pulmonary function tests show mild restrictive lung disease with a FEV1/FVC ratio of 80%. She is classified as NYHA functional class II. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her exercise capacity. Past Medical History: Single Ventricle Physiology post-Fontan palliation, pulmonary valve replacement at age 12. Medications: Aspirin, Enalapril.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis for more than 6 months. She has a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) score of 15 and a body surface area (BSA) score of 20%. She has an Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) score of 4 on a 5-point scale. She has not participated in any bimekizumab study before. She is a candidate for systemic psoriasis therapy and/or phototherapy and/or chemophototherapy. She has no history of erythrodermic, guttate, pustular form of psoriasis, or drug-induced psoriasis. She has no chronic or recurrent infections, serious or life-threatening infections, or herpes zoster within the last 6 months prior to the baseline visit. She has no primary immunosuppressive conditions, no TB infection, high risk of acquiring TB infection, latent TB infection (LTBI), or current or history of NTMB infection. She has no laboratory abnormalities as defined in the study protocol. She has not been exposed to more than one biological response modifier (limited to anti-TNF or IL-12/-23) or any biologic response modifier during the three months prior to the baseline visit. She has not received previous treatment with any anti-IL-17 therapy for the treatment of psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis. She does not have any inflammatory conditions other than psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis. She is not taking psoriatic arthritis medications other than nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or analgesics.

A 45-year-old male with end-stage liver disease due to chronic hepatitis B virus infection is scheduled for a living-donor liver transplant. He has a history of hypertension and is currently on antihypertensive medication. He has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to anesthesia medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His BMI is 25 kg/m2 and his ejection fraction is 55% on preoperative echocardiography. He has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial comparing propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia and desflurane-based balanced anesthesia for hepatic protection during liver transplantation.

The patient is a 25-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Danon disease based on a genetic test positive for LAMP2 mutation. The patient has a history of cardiomyopathy and is currently being treated with medication for the same. He also has a history of skeletal myopathy and cognitive impairment. The patient has a family history of the disease, and his younger brother was diagnosed with Danon disease at the age of 18. The patient is currently experiencing no symptoms and is able to carry out daily activities of living independently. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide information about his medical history through surveys and medical records. The patient is willing to undergo the multidisciplinary team's assessments at the University of California, San Diego, including cardiac testing, pulmonary function testing, neuromuscular assessment, cognitive tests, vision exam, laboratory tests, questionnaires on quality of life, and abdominal ultrasound. The patient is also willing to provide a needle skeletal muscle biopsy (only for patients over 18 years old) if needed for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer. She underwent a mastectomy and chemotherapy but was later found to have developed metastases in her brain. She has been experiencing headaches, dizziness, and difficulty with balance and coordination. MRI scans revealed multiple brain metastases, with the largest one measuring 2 cm in diameter. The patient is otherwise in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the best treatment for her brain metastases and is willing to undergo either surgery or radiotherapy, or a combination of both. She has no history of leptomeningeal disease, germ cell tumor, small cell lung cancer or hematological primary malignancy. She is able to complete neurocognitive testing without assistance and is willing to undergo MRI scans as required by the study.

A 52-year-old woman with stage III breast cancer presented to the M. D. Anderson Emergency Center with complaints of shortness of breath and chest pain. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy and has been taking multiple prescription medications, including tamoxifen, for the past six months. She also takes over-the-counter supplements such as vitamin D and calcium. She is able to read and write English and has agreed to participate in the study. She lives alone and does not have a caregiver. She has no history of mental illness or cognitive impairment. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has no history of drug allergies.

The patient is a 49-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) after experiencing fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and elevated liver enzymes. She has a history of obesity and has struggled with weight loss for many years. Her BMI is 32 kg/m2, and she has insulin resistance with an HbA1c level of 6.7%. She is currently taking metformin for her diabetes and has no other significant medical history. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Hoodia Gordonii for the treatment of her NAFLD. She has signed the informed consent form and is excited to potentially benefit from an alternative treatment option.

A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with CRPS three months ago after a fall that caused a fracture in her wrist. She experiences intense pain in her wrist, hand, and arm along with swelling, stiffness, and sensitivity to touch. Her pain level is consistently high, averaging 8 on the Numerical Rating Scale. She has no history of epilepsy, psychological or psychiatric disorders, or neurologic illness. She is not pregnant and is not currently involved in any legal action or disability claim. She does not have any metal implants or devices near the site of stimulation. She is willing and able to perform the experimental task and procedures.

A 30-year-old female with a BMI of 23.5 Kg/m2 visited the clinic complaining of fatigue, thirst, and frequent urination. She has no family history of diabetes, and her medical history is unremarkable. Her laboratory tests showed a fasting glucose level of 118 mg/dl, and an HbA1c level of 6.2%. She was diagnosed with prediabetes and advised to modify her lifestyle and diet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the link between vitamin D and Type 2 diabetes risk in normal weight and overweight UK adults. She is willing to undergo regular blood tests and follow study guidelines to determine whether vitamin D supplementation can help reduce her risk of developing Type 2 diabetes in the future.

A 24-year-old male with severe intellectual disabilities was referred to the study by his family members. The patient has a history of depression and has been receiving psychiatric care for the same for the past 2 years. He communicates through non-verbal gestures and has difficulties in performing daily activities. The patient has no significant medical history and is not on any medication. The patient's family members provide him with 24-hour care, and his mother is willing to participate in the study as a caregiver. She is available for weekly-fortnightly treatment sessions with the practitioner and currently provides a minimum of 15 hours of support per week to the participant. The patient is not suicidal and is willing to participate in the study. The patient's GP has been contacted and has given permission for the patient to take part in the study.

An 68-year-old retired Army veteran presents with chronic low back pain (cLBP) for the past 6 months. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and occasional knee pain. He has no history of surgery or hospitalization in the past 2 years. He reports lower back pain on most days and is not satisfied with his current level of physical function. He is currently on acetaminophen and ibuprofen for pain management. Physical examination reveals normal vital signs, no neurological deficits, and no signs of radiculopathy. His lower extremity strength, sensation, and reflexes are normal. He is able to walk 8 feet in 7 seconds and perform a 10 second semi-tandem stand. He does not have any cognitive impairment or significant hearing loss. The physical therapist determines that he is safe to participate in the intervention based on baseline examination and clinical expertise.

A 32-year-old male from Tanzania presents to the clinic with a persistent cough for the past 2 weeks. He has been experiencing night sweats, fever, and weight loss. He works in a factory and has a history of smoking for the past 10 years. He has no known allergies, no history of tuberculosis or other respiratory diseases, and no previous medical conditions. He reports having unprotected sex with multiple partners in the past year. On examination, his vitals are stable, and he has bilateral crackles on auscultation of the lungs. His chest X-ray shows infiltrates in the upper lobe of the left lung. Sputum samples are positive for tuberculosis. His hemoglobin level is 12.5 g/dL. He is willing to stay in Dar-es-Salaam for at least two years after the start of TB therapy and grants informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is not pregnant, and his Karnofsky score is greater than 40%.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic constipation for the past 5 years. She has tried taking laxatives and fiber supplements for her constipation, but these have not been effective in improving her symptoms. She has also undergone biofeedback therapy for her obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS), but has not been able to complete all recommended sessions due to the time-consuming nature of the treatment. She has no significant medical history other than her constipation and has not undergone any prior treatment with Botox. The Altomare Obstructed Defecation Syndrome score is 17 points and she is unable to relax the puborectalis muscle at electromyography. The patient does not have any anal pain, fecal incontinence, or rectal prolapse. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trial and is willing to give informed consent for this study.

32-year-old Caucasian female G2P1 at 38 weeks of gestational age presented to the OB clinic for routine follow up. Her pregnancy has been uneventful so far, except for mild nausea during the first trimester. She is not on any medications and has no history of chronic diseases. No allergies or intolerances were reported. Her prenatal supplements only contain folic acid and iron. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her BMI is 24. She has no history of preterm labor or preterm birth. She previously delivered a healthy baby girl via vaginal delivery without any complications. Her ultrasound scans throughout the pregnancy have been normal, with no evidence of fetal growth restriction. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of probiotic VSL#3 on the metabolic and immunological profile of breast milk. She is willing to give informed consent and has no history of twin pregnancies or any pregnancy diseases.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU with a diagnosis of severe sepsis with septic shock. The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. On admission, the patient's APACHE III score was 120. The patient was intubated, and mechanical ventilation was initiated. The patient was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and vasopressor support. On day 2 of ICU admission, the patient's serum calcium levels were found to be low with a corrected whole blood calcium level of 7.2 mg/dL. The patient did not have any signs of tetany or seizures. The patient's serum creatinine level was 1.5 mg/dL. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial examining the use of Zemplar to increase serum calcium levels in ICU subjects.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, characterized by recurrent pain attacks for the past 6 months. He has been taking Tramadol for pain control for the past 4 months. His medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes lisinopril. He denies any allergies or other medical conditions. He presents with a radiopaque pancreatic stone measuring 8mm, obstructing the main pancreatic duct in the pancreatic head. He has no evidence of biliary obstruction or pancreatic cancer. He has not undergone previous ESWL for pancreatic stones. He has signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial investigating the efficacy and safety of digital catheter-based pancreatoscopy for the management of symptomatic pancreatic duct stones in selected patients with chronic pancreatitis.

57F diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) stage IIIB, EGFR/ALK wild type. She has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit smoking 10 years ago. She presented with cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for 2 months before diagnosis. She underwent a biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of NSCLC. The patient has no other significant past medical history, no history of allergies, and no history of chemotherapy or radiation therapy. ECOG performance status is 0. Labs show WBC of 5,500 cells/μl, platelets of 200,000/mcL, and hemoglobin of 11 g/dL. Total bilirubin, AST, ALT, and Creatinine are all within normal limits. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the requirements.

A 32-year-old female presents with a complaint of anterior knee pain that has been bothering her for the past 6 months. The pain is sharp and is felt around the patella, especially when she is walking up and down stairs, squatting, or sitting with her knees bent for a prolonged time. She has no history of trauma to the knee or any other significant medical conditions. She is physically active and enjoys jogging and weightlifting. On examination, there is tenderness over the patella and pain with resisted knee extension. X-ray findings show no joint space narrowing or osteophyte formation. She has been diagnosed with patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) by her orthopedist. The patient is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the morphology of the vastus medialis obliquus (VMO) in patients with PFPS and healthy controls under 50 years old. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

A 27-year-old Albanian-speaking woman who recently migrated to Switzerland is experiencing feelings of sadness and hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping. She has been struggling with these symptoms for several months and has not sought any professional help. She speaks limited German and feels isolated from the community. She has access to a smartphone and occasionally uses the internet to stay in touch with her family back in Albania. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her cope with her depressive symptoms.

This is a 60 year-old male recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. He has no prior history of chemotherapy and is scheduled to receive repeated consecutive cycles of moderately emetogenic chemotherapy. He is in generally good health with an ECOG Performance Status of 1. His laboratory results are within acceptable limits for receiving a moderately emetogenic regimen. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and is committed to using contraceptive methods throughout the clinical trial. He has no known hypersensitivity or contraindication to 5-HT3 receptor antagonists or dexamethasone. He has not previously received an NK1 receptor antagonist and is not currently participating in a clinical trial involving oral netupitant administered in combination with palonosetron. There are no concurrent medical conditions that would preclude administration of dexamethasone for 4 days.

A 58 year old woman presents to the clinic with a history of chronic heart failure for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing worsening symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and difficulty with physical activity over the past 2 weeks. She was hospitalized for acute decompensation and required intravenous diuretics and vasodilators to manage her symptoms. She has a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% and a proBNP level of 1500 pg/ml at admission. She is otherwise healthy with no other comorbidities limiting her functional capacity. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the short-term effects of an early-start aerobic exercise training program on functional capacity, symptoms and neurohormonal activation in chronic heart failure patients with recent acute hemodynamic decompensation.

The patient is a 16-year-old adolescent with single ventricle congenital heart disease who underwent the Fontan procedure at the age of 2. His recent echocardiography revealed moderate to severe dysfunction of the right ventricle, with an ejection fraction of 40%. He also has a history of atrial fibrillation, which is currently under control with anti-arrhythmic therapy. His symptoms include fatigue, shortness of breath with exertion and dizziness. He is not currently enrolled in any interventional drug trials, nor has he completed one within the past 30 days. He has no known allergies or sulfonamide allergy. His renal function is normal. He has no implanted devices that would preclude him from undergoing MRI screening.

The patient is a 38-year-old woman with a history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) confirmed by fulfilling Rome III diagnostic criteria. She reports moderate-severe disease activity with an IBS-Symptom Severity Score of 200. She has tried several medications and dietary changes, but her symptoms persist. She is able to read and speak Danish. Her colonoscopy performed within the past year was normal. She has not had any other chronic gastrointestinal disease or surgeries in the gastrointestinal region. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or abuse of alcohol or drugs. Her fecal calprotectin level is below 50 mg/kg. She is not pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding. She has not ingested probiotics or antibiotics within the past 8 weeks.

The patient is a 3-year-old boy brought to the emergency department by his mother due to a fever and cough for the past 2 days. The child has no history of ear infections or respiratory problems. The child's temperature is 101.5°F, and he appears to be in mild distress. Upon examination, the attending pediatrician suspects that the child may have acute otitis media (AOM) due to redness and bulging of the tympanic membrane. The doctor informs the mother that the child may be eligible to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of a smartphone otoscope attachment for diagnosing AOM. The mother is provided with information about the study and asked to provide consent for her child's participation. If eligible, the child will be randomized to either the smartphone otoscope attachment or a classic otoscope for evaluation by two participating residents. The goal of this study is to improve the accuracy of AOM diagnosis and potentially decrease the unnecessary use of antibiotics.

Patient is a 32-year-old man with a history of psoriasis for the last 10 years. The patient has been treated with etanercept for a minimum of 6 months and discontinued treatment due to loss of efficacy. The patient's latest psoriasis treatment failed after a period of three months. The patient has a psoriasis area severity index (PASI) score of 15 and a physician global assessment (PGA) score of 4. The patient has no history of tuberculosis and has had a negative tuberculin skin test within 1 month prior to the first administration of the study drug. The patient is not currently enrolled in any other investigational device or investigational drug trial(s), and has no known hypersensitivity to Enbrel® (etanercept) or any of its components or known to have antibodies to etanercept. The patient has never been treated with cyclophosphamide therapy or concurrent sulfasalazine therapy. The patient has no positive HBV test or known history of any other immuno-suppressing disease. The patient has no active or chronic infection within 4 weeks before screening visit, or between the screening and baseline visits. The patient has no history of listeriosis, histoplasmosis, chronic or active Hepatitis B infection and Hepatitis C, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, immunodeficiency syndrome, chronic recurring infections or active TB, or other opportunistic infections. The patient has no severe comorbidities that would make participation in the clinical trial detrimental or otherwise unsuitable. The patient is not pregnant, nursing or planning pregnancy and is using acceptable methods of birth control during the trial. The patient has no history of non-compliance with other therapies. The patient is not currently using immunosuppressants, antimalarials, or sulfasalazine, other Ani-TNFs, cyclosporine, efalizumab, azathioprine, hydroxyurea, live vaccines, tacrolimus, or oral retinoids (isotretinoin,acitretin,bexarotene) or undergoing ultra violet light therapies.

This is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years. She has been on a diet and exercise regimen and is currently being treated with immediate release metformin. However, despite this treatment, her HbA1c levels have remained above 7.0%. She has not received any other antidiabetic medication in the last 12 weeks prior to randomization. Her HbA1c level at screening was 10%, making her eligible for the randomized treatment arm of the trial. She has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and has signed and dated written informed consent in accordance with GCP and local legislation. She has no history of acute coronary syndrome, liver disease, impaired renal function, or any other medical conditions that would jeopardize her safety while participating in this clinical trial. She has not undergone bariatric surgery or any other gastrointestinal surgeries that induce chronic malabsorption. She has not been treated with anti-obesity drugs or systemic steroids in the past three months. She is not pregnant or nursing and is using an acceptable method of birth control. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse that would interfere with trial participation or any ongoing condition leading to decreased compliance to study procedures or study drug intake.

A 45-year-old woman presented to the hospital with fever, chills, and fatigue. She had been feeling unwell for the past 3 days and her symptoms were progressively worsening. She has a history of hypertension and was previously diagnosed with urinary tract infection. Her vital signs at admission were: blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and temperature of 39.2°C. Blood tests revealed an elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein level. She was diagnosed with sepsis according to the Surviving Sepsis Campaign criteria. The patient was enrolled in the study after providing written consent. Exclusion criteria were reviewed and the patient did not have any conditions that would exclude her from the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have any malignancy. She has not experienced any potentially elevated plasma midkine apart from sepsis. The patient has not been discharged or deceased within 24 hours of ICU admission.

40-year-old Arab Canadian Muslim woman with a family history of type 2 diabetes, who is overweight and has been living in Canada for more than 10 years. She has a history of mild hypertension and impaired glucose tolerance. She leads a sedentary lifestyle and is interested in making positive lifestyle changes to reduce her risk of developing type 2 diabetes. She is not currently enrolled in any other clinical research trial and does not have any uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina, pulmonary or metabolic disease, or severe arthritis or rheumatologic problems.

The patient is a 7-year-old child who has been experiencing persistent headaches and vomiting for the past month. An MRI revealed a tumor in the brainstem, which was later diagnosed as a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG). The child has not received any prior anti-cancer therapy such as chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy or bone marrow transplant for the treatment of DIPG. The patient has a body surface area of 0.45 m^2 at the time of study enrollment. The Karnofsky performance score is 70% and the patient is currently able to walk with assistance. The patient's laboratory values are within the eligibility criteria, with a peripheral absolute neutrophil count of 1500/mm^3 and platelet count of 120,000/mm^3. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has agreed to use effective contraception during the study period. The patient is able to swallow capsules and does not have any uncontrolled infections or major cardiac diseases. The patient and their parents/legal guardians have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

27 y/o male, BMI 28.5 kg/m2, works a desk job 5 days a week and eats out for most meals due to lack of time and cooking skills. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medication that affects energy expenditure or eating. He does not smoke or use any nicotine products. He has no food allergies or limitations to eating certain foods. He is not currently dieting to lose weight but has expressed interest in starting an exercise program to become more active and healthy. He currently exercises once a week by playing basketball with friends. He reports liking most of the study foods and is willing to consent to the study conditions.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with congestive heart failure and implanted with an ICD system with "Cardiac-Compass" (Medtronic)-diagnostic feature, three months ago. His New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class is II and his left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 35%. He is currently on stable pharmacological therapy for the past three months. The patient's load capacity is at least 50 watt at baseline. He is able to perform daily activities with some difficulty and experiences shortness of breath and fatigue with exertion. He has no history of acute coronary syndrome in the past thirty days, hemodynamically relevant valvular defect, unstable arterial hypertension, severe COPD, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM), or pulmonary-arterial hypertension (PAP systolic ≥ 60 mmHg). The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the exercise program.

A 28-year-old woman gave birth to a healthy baby boy weighing 3.2 kgs at full term. She has decided to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate different protein content of formulas on the nutrition status of infants. She is currently considering whether to exclusively breastfeed or formula feed her newborn. She has a healthy medical history with no known allergies or chronic conditions. She is excited to learn more about the study and the potential benefits it could have for her baby. She is willing to commit to the study procedures and attend all required appointments.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing symptoms of fatigue and weakness for the past few months. She reports a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and has been diagnosed with borderline iron deficiency anemia with a ferritin level of 20 ng/ml. She has not been taking any iron supplements or multivitamins for the past two weeks. She has a normal BMI and weighs 60 kg. She has no history of any gastrointestinal or metabolic diseases and is not on any long-term medication. She is fluent in English and is able to communicate effectively. She has not donated blood in the past 4 months and has not participated in any other clinical trial in the past 30 days. She has no known allergies or eating disorders. She is highly motivated to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 48-year-old male smoker with a history of hypertension and high cholesterol visited his cardiologist due to chest pain. Further examination revealed that he had ischemic heart disease and was advised to undergo percutaneous coronary intervention. He has no known allergies to any medications and is willing to participate in clinical trials. He speaks Danish fluently and is willing to comply with the treatment requirements. He has never been included in this study or any other stent studies before.

A 52 year old female patient diagnosed with COPD stage 3 for the past 4 years, with a smoking history of 15 pack-years, presents to the clinic complaining of shortness of breath and coughing up yellowish phlegm for the past week. She has had 3 moderate exacerbations in the past 12 months. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting bronchodilators. She is willing and able to comply with study procedures, and is able to use a smartphone and give written consent. She has a good understanding of written and spoken English. She has no other significant lung disease or known history of significant systemic and other organ-related disease. She is not pregnant and has not participated in any interventional clinical study within the past 3 months.

A 30-year-old female living in a rural area of Vietnam presents to the clinic with a history of fever, chills, and headache for the past three days. She reports feeling weak and has been experiencing intermittent fevers. Upon examination, she has a tympanic temperature of 38.5°C and mild splenomegaly. Her blood test shows a parasitemia of 300/µl asexual forms of Plasmodium vivax. She has no known underlying chronic or severe diseases, nor is she taking any medication. She is able to swallow oral medication and is willing to comply with the study protocol for the duration of the study. She provides informed consent and is eligible to participate in the clinical trial to test the effectiveness of Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine (DHA-PPQ) or Chloroquine (CQ) for the treatment of vivax malaria in Vietnam.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with gallstones and is scheduled for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril to control it. He has no history of respiratory or airway-related conditions. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is not currently taking any sedating or analgesic medications. His BMI is 28. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is able to walk up two flights of stairs without any difficulty. His vital signs are within normal limits: BP: 130/80 mm Hg, HR: 80 bpm, RR: 16 breaths/min, SpO2: 98%. His airway assessment shows Mallampati class II, thyromental distance of 6 cm, and full neck mobility.

A 45-year-old female patient presented with chronic abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past 6 months. She reports having lost 10 pounds unintentionally over the same period. The patient has a history of heavy alcohol use, but she has been sober for the past 2 years. She has no history of diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidemia. She reports a family history of pancreatic cancer, but no other family members with chronic abdominal pain. The patient currently works as a school teacher and is married with two children. She reports feeling stressed at work and at home due to her symptoms and decreased ability to participate in activities. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help manage her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She has access to a computer at home and is willing to complete the online assessment.

A 55-year-old Korean woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has never had herpes zoster or received the varicella or zoster vaccine. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use an acceptable method of birth control. She has not received any immunoglobulins or blood products other than autologous blood transfusion in the last few months. She has not received any live or inactivated vaccines in the last 4 weeks or 7 days, respectively. She is not on immunosuppressive therapy and does not have any known or suspected immune dysfunction. She has not used nontopical antiviral therapy with activity against herpes virus and does not have active untreated tuberculosis.

This is a 45 year-old male with a history of erectile dysfunction. He has tried oral medications, such as sildenafil, but has not responded well to these treatments. He is sexually active and interested in exploring alternative treatment options for his condition. He has not participated in any other clinical studies involving investigational drugs or devices, and is willing to undergo the procedure necessary for this study. The patient has no active infections or fevers, and has a life expectancy greater than 2 years due to other illnesses.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been diagnosed with aggressive periodontitis. She has been experiencing gum bleeding, halitosis and mobility of teeth for the past few months. She is generally healthy and not taking any medications. Her medical history is unremarkable and she has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions. She does not smoke and is not using alcohol or drugs. She is interested in participating in the research to help understand the molecular and immunological basis of aggressive periodontitis. She has been informed about the study and its procedures and has given her consent to participate.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who has been diagnosed with bipolar I disorder. He has a history of multiple depressive episodes and has been taking a combination of mood-stabilizing medications including lithium and olanzapine for the past year. Despite treatment, he continues to experience symptoms of depression such as loss of interest in daily activities, feelings of worthlessness and low energy. He has participated in a previous Cephalon-sponsored Phase 3 clinical trial for armodafinil treatment as adjunctive therapy for depression associated with bipolar I disorder and has completed 8 weeks of treatment. His Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) total score is 12 at the enrollment visit and he has no history of alcohol or substance abuse. He is willing to continue treatment with the same protocol-allowed mood stabilizers at dosages considered appropriate by the investigator.

The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of congestive heart failure (CHF) for the past 5 years. He was diagnosed with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and his ejection fraction is less than 30%. He has been on optimal medical therapy, including ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and diuretics. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year for acute exacerbations of CHF, with symptoms of shortness of breath on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He quit smoking 10 years ago and does not consume alcohol. He reports being limited in his daily activities and is unable to walk more than 1 block without experiencing dyspnea. He has not undergone any cardiac procedures in the past year. His ECG shows sinus rhythm with LBBB (QRS duration of 150ms). His echocardiogram shows LV end-diastolic diameter of 75mm, EF of 25%, and moderate mitral regurgitation. He has no known allergies and is compliant with his medications. He is interested in participating in the study to explore the potential benefits of cardiac resynchronization therapy on his symptoms and exercise tolerance.

A 27-year-old female with a history of recreational opioid use for the past year presented herself to the clinic. She is a non-dependent user of opioids, consuming for psychoactive purposes on at least ten occasions within the last year and at least once in the 12 weeks before the Screening Visit. The patient reported experience with intranasal opioid administration, defined as intranasal use on at least three occasions within the last year before screening. She has a body mass index (BMI) of 25.5 kg/m² and a total body weight of 60 kg. The patient has no clinically relevant abnormalities identified by a detailed medical history, full physical examination, 12-lead ECG, and clinical laboratory tests. The patient is able to speak, read, and understand English sufficiently to comprehend the nature of the study and to understand the informed consent form (ICF) and consent process. She has no history of substance and/or alcohol dependence or any clinically significant hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, or allergic disease.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 2 years. He is a former smoker with a history of 20 pack-years and has quit smoking 2 years ago. He is currently using a long-acting bronchodilator and inhaled corticosteroid inhaler for COPD maintenance therapy. He has no history of asthma and has not experienced a COPD exacerbation requiring systemic corticosteroids or antibiotics in the past 4 weeks. He has not undergone lung volume reduction surgery in the past 12 months and is not currently using long-term oxygen therapy. He has no other significant medical conditions that could impact his ability to participate in the trial. He is able to read, comprehend, and record information in English and is willing to comply with the study procedures and restrictions. He has never used the ELLIPTA inhaler before and is able to demonstrate correct use of the inhaler within three attempts at Visit 1. He has provided signed and dated written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has a history of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath and fatigue during physical activity. He has been diagnosed with NYHA class II status and has a 6-minute walk distance of less than 80% of the predicted value. His left atrium has been found to be enlarged, and his pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) was measured to be 28 mmHg during supine bicycle exercise on hemodynamic monitoring. The patient's left atrial pressure is greater than his right atrial pressure by at least 5 mmHg. He has no history of recent myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass grafting, and he has no untreated coronary artery disease that requires revascularization. The patient has no history of stroke, pulmonary embolism, or major surgery. His atrial fibrillation is under control. The patient has no history of cardiomyopathy or pericardial disease. He is able to perform a 6-minute walk test. He has no clinically significant valvular disease. The patient has no severe COPD, anemia, or morbid obesity. His hypertension is controlled. The patient is not a woman of childbearing age. His right atrial pressure is less than or equal to 15 mmHg and his pulmonary vascular resistance is less than or equal to 4 wood units. The patient consents to participate in this clinical trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of the atrial flow regulator (AFR) device.

A 56 year old man comes to the clinic complaining of tremors and stiffness in his right hand for the past 6 months. The symptoms have slowly progressed to involve his right leg as well. He has no family history of Parkinson's disease. He has been diagnosed with early stage Parkinson's disease by a Movement Disorder Specialist. He is currently not taking any medications for PD. The patient has no history of psychiatric disorders, surgical interventions for PD or participation in any investigational drug study in the last month. He is willing to abstain from alcohol during the study and is ready to provide blood samples for mRNA and DNA analysis. He is willing to follow the requirements of the study protocol. The patient has no history of significant non-PD central nervous system disorder or any other exclusion criteria mentioned in the study. He is willing to provide written informed consent and all authorizations required by local law. If female, he confirms that he is postmenopausal for at least 1 year or surgically sterile. The patient meets the eligibility criteria to participate in the BIIB014 Phase 2a Monotherapy clinical trial.

The patient is an 80-year-old German woman who has been admitted to the hospital for a complex treatment that requires a stay of at least 7 days. She has a history of hypertension, osteoporosis, and type 2 diabetes. She takes several medications, including Metformin, Lisinopril, and Alendronate. She lives alone at home and has a caregiver who visits her regularly. Her past medical history is remarkable for a stroke 2 years ago, which left her with mild hemiparesis. She has no known drug allergies. The patient is able to provide written informed consent for participation in the study, and her caregiver is available to assist if needed.

A 42-year-old woman arrives at the Emergency Department (ED) complaining of severe abdominal pain and nausea. She has been experiencing this for the past two days and the pain has gradually increased in intensity. The pain is located in the upper abdomen and radiates to the back. She rates the pain as severe, 9/10 on a visual analogue scale. She reports no history of chronic pain or cyclic vomiting. Upon questioning, the patient reports that she has been taking over-the-counter ibuprofen for the past two days without relief of symptoms. She denies any known drug allergies. Her medical history includes hypertension, for which she takes lisinopril. She denies any other medical history or recent surgeries. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use any illicit drugs. Her vital signs are within normal limits. The patient speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old presbyopic female with a history of wearing soft contact lenses for the past 5 years is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She has a physiologically normal anterior segment without any biomicroscopy findings Grade 2 or greater and/or presence of infiltrates. She is able to correct her vision through spherocylindrical refraction to 42 letters (0.1 logMAR) or better (distance, high contrast) in each eye and requires contact lens correction from -5.00 D to +3.00 D in each eye. She also requires near add correction from +1.00 D to +1.75 D in each eye. She is currently an adapted monovision soft contact lens wearer or multifocal soft contact lens wearer or an adapted spherical soft contact lens wearer who also uses spectacles for near vision correction. She is willing to use a lens care system as required by the lens replacement schedule. Her distance spherical equivalent refraction is between -5.50 D and +3.00 D. She does not meet any exclusion criteria, such as not being correctable to 32 letters (0.3 logMAR) in each eye with soft spherical contact lenses, having corneal infiltrates of ANY GRADE, or having anisometropia (spherical equivalent) of greater than 2.00 D.

The patient is a 55-year-old male veteran who has been experiencing low back pain for over 6 months. The pain is severe, with a rating of 8 out of 10 on a numeric rating scale. He has tried medications, including opioids, but has not found them helpful. He is interested in non-pharmacological therapies to manage his pain. He is generally healthy, with no significant medical history. He is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys spending time outdoors and participating in recreational activities such as golf and fishing, but his pain has made it difficult to continue these activities. He is able to speak, read, and write fluently in English. He receives care at the VA Medical Health Care System and is willing to participate in the trial of non-pharmacological therapies for pain. His current treatment plan is stable, and he is not scheduled for any surgery or pain procedures during the expected study period.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of congestive heart failure. He presents to the clinic with shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. The patient reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 months and they have been progressively worsening. He reports a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking a beta-blocker, an ACE inhibitor, and a diuretic for his heart failure. His most recent echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 30%. His lab studies showed: A1c: 7.2% Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL AST: 20 U/L ALT: 18 U/L Sodium: 138 mEq/L Potassium: 4.0 mEq/L Chloride: 102 mEq/L Bicarbonate: 24 mEq/L The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially improve his heart failure symptoms. He reports that he is a non-smoker and is willing to comply with the study procedures.

Patient is a 29-year-old pregnant woman from the United States who is currently at 26 weeks of gestation. She has been diagnosed with severe left congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) with liver up and her ultrasound shows a lung-to-head ratio (LHR) of less than 25%. She is carrying a singleton pregnancy and her fetal karyotype has been confirmed to be normal. She has no history of incompetent cervix with or without cerclage and no placental abnormalities. She has no known maternal-fetal Rh isoimmunization, Kell sensitization, or neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia affecting the current pregnancy. She has no known maternal HIV, Hepatitis-B, or Hepatitis-C status positive. She has no uterine anomaly such as large or multiple fibroids or mullerian duct abnormality. She has no history of participation in another intervention study that influences maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality or participation in this trial in a previous pregnancy. She has met all inclusion criteria and has given informed consent to participate in the Fetoscopic Endoluminal Tracheal Occlusion (FETO) therapy pilot trial.

44 yo female with fibromyalgia diagnosed 6 years ago presents with chronic widespread pain, fatigue, and difficulty with daily activities. She reports a pain score of 6/10 on an 11-point NRS and has tried multiple treatments with limited success. She has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and is of childbearing potential but agrees to use effective birth control during the study. She has not participated in any other interventional study in the past and is willing to complete daily diaries throughout the duration of the study. She reports she has been compliant with daily pain recordings during the Baseline Diary Run-In period and agrees to maintain usual level of activity for the duration of the study. She is not currently using any protocol specified prohibited medications and has not filed any disability claims or legal litigations.

The patient is a 12-year-old girl who is currently attending middle school. She is interested in science and has a general positive attitude towards physical activities such as dancing, but she struggles with maintaining a healthy diet. She is a member of a minority group and comes from a low-income family. She has limited access to healthy food options and physical activities due to financial constraints. She is fluent in English and has no known condition that would interfere with her ability to participate in physical activities. The patient is willing to participate in a summer program that focuses on health and wellness to learn more about nutrition and healthy habits. She hopes to gain more knowledge about science and develop new skills that will help her make positive changes in her life.

This is a 14 year old female who has been struggling with Nonsuicidal Self-Injury (NSSI) behavior for the past year. She has a history of anxiety and depression and has been seeing a therapist regularly. She reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed, and often turns to cutting as a way to cope with her emotions. She has a smartphone and is able to send and receive text messages.
