She and her parents have agreed to participate in an 8-week clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of text message intervention for NSSI in adolescents. Her parents are supportive of her participation in the study and have signed the informed consent form.

A 47-year-old male with a history of elevated blood glucose levels and newly diagnosed with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT). The patient has a BMI of 27 kg/m2 and a blood pressure of 130/85 mmHg. The patient is a non-smoker and has no history of microvascular or macrovascular complications of diabetes. The patient has mildly elevated cholesterol levels (6.5 mmol/L) but does not have severe hyperlipidaemia. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of rosiglitazone and ramipril on pre-clinical vasculopathy in newly diagnosed diabetic and IGT individuals. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

52yo male with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and angina pectoris who will undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and aortic valve replacement due to severe coronary artery disease and aortic stenosis. He has been on a stable regimen of aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol for the past year. He reports occasional shortness of breath with minimal exertion and chest pain on exertion. He is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has no known allergies to medications.

A 45-year-old woman who works as a teacher comes to the clinic for her annual flu vaccination. She has a history of seasonal allergies but has never experienced a severe allergic reaction to a flu vaccine. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to determine the safety of Flublok in comparison to traditional inactivated influenza vaccines. She is a member of Kaiser-Permanente, Northern California (KPNC) and has been receiving her flu vaccine from KPNC for the past five years. She is willing to have her electronic health records (EHR) included in the study and is interested in contributing to the advancement of influenza vaccine research.

A 42-year-old male patient with a history of recurrent renal calculi and discomfort presents to the hospital for evaluation and possible treatment. He has a BMI of 30 and is otherwise healthy. CT scan shows renal calculi measuring smaller than 25mm. Preoperative urine culture is negative. The patient agrees to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the influence of SMP on renal pelvic pressure. He is randomized to group 1 for the study. The patient undergoes the SMP procedure under general anesthesia without complications. Renal pelvic pressure is measured during the procedure. Postoperative pain is well controlled with analgesics. The patient is discharged from the hospital after 2 days and is instructed to follow up in 1 month.

A 55-year-old male patient presents to the clinic for a routine colorectal cancer screening. He has no history of colon cancer or polyps and has never undergone a colonoscopy before. He reports occasional constipation and mild abdominal discomfort, but denies any rectal bleeding, diarrhea, or weight loss. He takes a daily multivitamin supplement and has no known drug allergies. His family history is significant for colon cancer in his paternal grandmother, who was diagnosed in her late 60s. On physical examination, he appears healthy and his vital signs are within normal limits. His abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no palpable masses or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory tests, including complete blood count, electrolytes, liver function tests, and renal function tests, are all within normal limits. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial and agrees to be randomized to either the study method or conventional method for performing the colonoscopy.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who sustained a spinal cord injury at the level of C6-C7 due to a motor vehicle accident 10 years ago. He has been using a wheelchair for mobility since then. The patient reports having difficulty maintaining his body temperature during winter months and often experiences shivering and chills. He has no history of kidney, peripheral vascular or cerebral vascular disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes mellitus, acute illness or infection, dehydration, or smoking. The patient is not currently pregnant. He is willing to participate in the study and agrees to avoid caffeine and alcohol, maintain normal salt and water intake, and avoid strenuous exercise for 24 hours prior to the study. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 62-year-old male with a history of metastatic urothelial cancer of the bladder, upper or lower urinary tracts, previously treated with at least one cisplatin or carboplatin-based multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen. The patient must have measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 and available tumor specimen C-MET/RON expression results that meet the criteria for one of the three molecularly defined cohorts. The patient must have an ECOG performance status of 0-2, adequate liver function, bone marrow function, and renal function, and must be able to swallow oral medication. The patient must not be currently receiving any other investigational agents or a prior c-MET inhibitor or crizotinib. The patient must not be pregnant or breastfeeding and must not have uncontrolled and current illness, prolonged QT interval, or a history of active malignancy other than urothelial carcinoma within the prior 12 months of the date of treatment consent. The patient must not have a medical condition requiring the use of strong CPY3A inhibitors or inducers, or be receiving any medications that are CYP3A substrates with a narrow therapeutic range. The patient may be screened for study participation though may not begin study treatment within 4 weeks of major surgery, within 2 weeks of prior systemic therapy, within 2 weeks of prior non-palliative radiotherapy, within 48 hours of completion of palliative radiotherapy (≤ 10 fractions), or until recovery of adverse events due to prior therapies to ≤ 1 (except alopecia). The patient must not have untreated brain metastases or ≤ 6 months from prior treatment (from the time of enrollment), active neurologic symptoms, or the use of prohibited medications in subjects with a history of brain metastases.

54F with history of multinodular goiter presented to the endocrine clinic with a complaint of increasing neck mass and difficulty swallowing. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy revealed follicular neoplasm and she was scheduled to undergo a total thyroidectomy. The patient has no history of hypocalcemia or parathyroid disease. She denies any symptoms of hypercalcemia or hypercalciuria. The patient reports no history of malabsorption syndrome, liver or kidney disease. She is not currently taking any vitamin D supplements and denies any known hypersensitivity to vitamin D. She has not had any prior thyroid or parathyroid surgery. The patient is not pregnant and has no history of calcic lithiasis. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and is affiliated with the social security system.

46-year-old male with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus, presenting to the emergency department with fever, chills, and altered mental status. He is found to have septic shock with a positive blood culture for E. coli. His initial blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg with a heart rate of 120 bpm. He is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and requires vasopressor support. His serum creatinine is 1.5 mg/dL and urine output is decreased. He has not received any fluid resuscitation yet.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain for the past month. He underwent a chest CT scan, which revealed a mass in the lower lobe of the left lung. A biopsy was performed, and the patient was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. The cancer has advanced to stage IV and is deemed unresectable. The patient has no prior history of chemotherapy or targeted therapy. He is able to perform activities of daily living without considerable assistance. His bone marrow, kidney, and liver function are adequate. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed informed consent.

The patient is a 55 year old male who recently underwent cardiac surgery. The surgery was performed to treat his coronary artery disease which caused severe chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia which are well controlled with medications. He is a former smoker and quit smoking 5 years ago. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is married and has two children. His BMI is 27 and his blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg. He has no significant physical findings on examination, and his laboratory results are within normal limits. He was intubated and mechanically ventilated after the surgery and was admitted to the ICU. He is now eligible for the clinical trial that aims to assess the effectiveness of pulse pressure variation in guiding fluid therapy in cardiac surgery patients.

The patient is a male or female between the ages of 18 and 75 with mild or moderate liver impairment as determined by a hepatologist/gastroenterologist. The patient must have a stable Child-Pugh score of 5-9 points for at least 3 months prior to screening and during the trial. The patient must have a Body Mass Index between 18.5 and 34 kg/m2 and a Creatinine clearance >40 mL/min according to Cockcroft & Gault. Female patients must either be postmenopausal or use adequate contraception during the study and until 2 months after study completion. The patient must not have any relevant deviation from healthy conditions, except those caused by liver impairment. The patient must provide signed and dated written informed consent prior to admission to the study in accordance with Good Clinical Practice and the local legislation.

A 35-year-old female with a history of atopic dermatitis for the past 10 years is seeking participation in a clinical trial for a new treatment. She has been experiencing moderate to severe flare-ups of atopic dermatitis for the past 6 months, despite adhering to a strict skin care regimen and avoiding known triggers. She has not undergone any systemic treatments for atopic dermatitis in the past year. Her Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score is 12, indicating moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and is able to provide written informed consent. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, nor any medical conditions that would put her at risk for participating in the study. She is sexually active and agrees to use medically acceptable form of contraception throughout the study. She is hopeful that the study drug will improve her quality of life by reducing the frequency and severity of her atopic dermatitis flare-ups.

A 35-year-old female was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus at the age of 15. She has been on insulin injections to control her blood glucose levels since then. She developed end-stage renal disease (ESRD) secondary to diabetic nephropathy and started hemodialysis 2 years ago. She underwent simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation (SPK) 6 months ago. Her postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged on postoperative day 7. Her immunosuppression regimen includes tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone. She is compliant with her medications and follow-up appointments. Her last physical examination and laboratory studies were performed yesterday and showed the results below: A well-nourished female, non-icteric, alert, and cooperative. Weight: 65 kg Height: 165 cm BP: 130/80 HR: 80/min RR: 16/min Hgb: 12 g/dL WBC: 7000 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 4500/mm3) Plt: 250000 /ml Glucose: 110 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Lipase: 30 U/L Amylase: 60 U/L Proteinuria: 50 mg/dL AlloSure: 0.5% AlloMap: 10 (stable)

The patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a missed abortion in the first trimester. The diagnosis was made during a routine ultrasound exam, which showed no fetal heartbeat. The patient has not experienced any symptoms such as vaginal bleeding or cramping. She is over 18 years old and has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient does not have any known hypersensitivity to prostaglandins or a history of vaginal bleeding. She does not have suspected ectopic pregnancy, an intrauterine device (IUD), heart disease, hypertension, cerebral vascular disease, epilepsy, intrauterine infection, or clotting disorders. The sac diameter measures less than 8 weeks. The patient will be given misoprostol vaginally to induce the abortion and the effectiveness of the treatment will be assessed based on the vaginal PH.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who works as a teacher and has been experiencing vocal fatigue and hoarseness for the past six months. She has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She reports that her voice becomes weaker and strained as the day progresses, and she often experiences discomfort in her throat. She has tried vocal rest and warm-up exercises, but they provide only temporary relief. Her physical examination is normal, and there are no visible abnormalities in her larynx. She has no allergies or contraindications for wearing the device. She is willing to complete all clinical/research assessments and give informed consent. She meets the inclusion criteria for the experimental group with a diagnosis of muscle tension dysphonia and a recommended treatment of voice therapy.

A 42-year-old non-smoking female visited the dental clinic for a routine check-up. The patient is in good health with no underlying medical issues and is not taking any medication. She has a regular exercise routine and follows a balanced diet. The patient has a history of dental caries and has undergone multiple fillings and restorations. She has no known allergies to any medications or materials used in dental procedures. The patient shows Miller Class I gingival recession in the maxillary anterior teeth. She has requested treatment for the recession due to aesthetic concerns.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with Stage III melanoma about 6 months ago. She underwent a surgical resection for the melanoma and is currently free of the disease. Her past medical history includes hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. Her family history is negative for any significant medical conditions. She is currently on no medications other than the blood pressure medication. Her lab study is as follows: Hemoglobin: 12.5 g/dL, White Blood Cells: 5.2 x 10^3/uL, Platelets: 200 x 10^3/uL, Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin: 1.2 mg/dL, AST: 30 IU/L, ALT: 25 IU/L, Alkaline Phosphatase: 80 IU/L, LDH: 200 IU/L. She is positive for HLA-A0201. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She has not undergone any prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy. She has had a CT scan of chest, abdomen, pelvis, and a MRI or CT scan of the brain performed within the last 4 weeks. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant. She has not undergone a hysterectomy or been naturally postmenopausal for at least 24 consecutive months. She is willing to use an accepted and effective method of contraception (including abstinence) while on treatment and for a period of 3 months after completing or discontinuing treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old non-smoking female with a history of hypertension. Her BMI is 25, and she is in good general health with no significant medical issues or laboratory abnormalities. She has not had any surgeries or illnesses within the past 8 weeks prior to the study. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study period. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and does not regularly consume alcohol. She does not use any medications that are known to affect hepatic drug metabolism. She has no history of allergic reactions to donepezil or related drugs. She does not have any gastrointestinal, neurological, endocrinal, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematological, immunologic, psychiatric, or metabolic disease. She has not used any investigational drugs or participated in any investigational studies within the past 30 days. She is not on any special diet or food restrictions. She has no difficulty swallowing medications. She has never donated plasma or whole blood within the specified timeframes. She has no history of asthma or obstructive pulmonary disease. She meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

65-year-old F with a history of osteoarthritis in the hip joint presented with severe pain and limited mobility. The patient has tried conservative treatment options such as physical therapy and pain medication but it was not effective in reducing the symptoms. The patient has no history of active infection, hepatitis, HIV, AIDS, or IV drug abuse. The patient is willing and able to return for required follow-up visits and has provided signed consent for the total hip arthroplasty surgical procedure. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial comparing INSORB absorbable staples with metal staples in total hip replacement.

A 58-year-old man with a 10-year history of chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis three times per week. He has been on a stable regimen of calcium carbonate for his hyperphosphatemia, but his serum inorganic phosphorus levels have been consistently above 5.5 mg/dL and below 9.0 mg/dL in the last three tests. He is able to comply with the study procedures and medication and has provided written informed consent. He has no history of malignancy or severe cardiovascular disorders but has experienced occasional cramping during hemodialysis. He has not received any investigational drugs within the last 30 days.

42 y/o female with history of Crohn's disease diagnosed at age 26, currently on mesalazine for the past 10 years. No history of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection or anogenital warts. No history of abnormal cervical cytology or HPV vaccination. Non-smoker, sexually active with one male partner for the past 5 years. No history of inherited immune disorders, human immunodeficiency virus infection, invasive malignancies or psychomotor retardation. No high-dose corticosteroids received in the past 6 months.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with central lobe epilepsy (CLE). She experiences an average of 4 seizures per day, which have not responded to treatment with at least 3 anti-epileptic drugs. Her seizures arise from the primary sensorimotor cortex and have a significant impact on her quality of life. She is mentally and physically capable of giving informed consent. She does not have any known coagulopathy or allergies to materials of the implant. She does not have any known progressive neurological or systemic diseases. She does not have any known brain lesions that place her at an elevated risk for bleeding. She has not undergone any previous surgeries for epilepsy. She is interested in participating in a new clinical trial that may help manage her epilepsy.

A 60-year-old man who is scheduled for elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) at the Karolinska Hospital and has no history of renal disease presents for a pre-operative consultation. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. His current medications include metformin, aspirin, and a statin. On physical examination, his blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg, his heart sounds are regular with no murmurs, and his lungs are clear. His creatinine level is normal at 0.9 mg/dL, and his eGFR is 75 mL/min/1.73 m². He understands the study and provides written consent to participate in the trial.

A 35-year old female who works as a nurse is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She has no known allergies and does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She is interested in contributing to the advancement of medical research and is willing to undergo all necessary procedures for the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of non-small cell lung cancer. The patient was diagnosed with lung cancer 8 months ago and has received first-line chemotherapy with a platinum-containing combination scheme. The patient presents with less than 3 brain metastases and has not received any intracranial local treatment before. The patient is not currently undergoing major surgery or experiencing ununited wounds. There is no evidence of hemorrhage in the intracranial metastasis.

A 30-year-old mother gave birth to a preterm infant at 31 weeks of gestation. The infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) immediately after delivery and stayed there for 4 weeks. During her stay at the NICU, the mother experienced high levels of stress and anxiety and was worried about her baby's health and well-being. Currently, the infant is 6 months old (corrected age) and has been discharged from the hospital. The mother is still experiencing high levels of stress related to parenting, including anxiety related to managing the infant's health, feeding, and sleep patterns. The mother speaks French and resides within a 50-kilometre radius of the hospital. The infant has no congenital anomalies or foreseeable disabilities during the neonatal period. The mother has no known psychiatric history. The aim of this study is to assess the impact of an early psychological intervention program, Triadic parent-infant Relationship Therapy (TRT), on parenting stress, parental mental health, and preterm infant development in the motor, cognitive, emotional and behavioral domains at a corrected age of 18 months. The mother and infant will be enrolled in the intervention program and monitored for the next 12 months.

A 65-year-old man was referred to an ophthalmologist for a routine eye exam. He has a family history of glaucoma, and he has been diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma in both eyes. His current treatment regimen includes a single topical ocular hypotensive medication, which he has been taking for the past year. During the

8-month-old F with no significant past medical history presents to the pediatrician's office with a fever of 38.5°C, irritability and decreased urine output. Urinalysis is positive for leukocytes and nitrites, and urine culture is positive for E. coli with a colony count of 10^5 CFU/ml. The diagnosis of a urinary tract infection (UTI) is made. The patient is started on an appropriate antibiotic and scheduled for a follow-up visit in 7 days. After completing the antibiotic course, the patient is randomized to receive either E. coli Nissle strain or placebo for 15 days. The intervention drug is administered orally and the patient is monitored for any adverse effects. Follow-up appointments are scheduled monthly for 6 months to monitor for any new UTIs or other infections.

A 55-year-old male was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and has undergone chemotherapy treatment, but the cancer has relapsed. He has no history of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). He is married and has two children. He works as a teacher and has taken a leave of absence due to his illness. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He has no other medical issues and has never had surgery. He does not smoke, drink alcohol or use recreational drugs. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy lifestyle. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is willing to participate in clinical trials to improve his chances of survival.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been diagnosed with systolic chronic heart failure for the past 6 months. He has no history of acute coronary syndrome, myocarditis or any other significant cardiac events. He is currently on medication for his heart failure and has been referred to the cardiac rehabilitation center for a 5-week training program. He has a history of smoking but has quit 2 years ago. He is not currently on any medication that would affect his eligibility for the trial. He is affiliated with social security coverage. He is motivated to participate in the study and is willing to provide his signed consent.

The patient is a 54-year-old man who has been diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy. He had undergone vitrectomy surgery two years ago due to recurrent diabetic vitreous hemorrhage in his left eye. Despite the initial improvement in vision, he has been experiencing recurrent vitreous hemorrhage in the same eye for the past few months. He is currently on insulin therapy and has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His visual acuity is 20/200 in the affected eye. His intraocular pressure is within normal range. He has no history of ocular trauma or surgery other than the previous vitrectomy. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide in clearing the recurrent vitreous hemorrhage.

2.5-year-old male diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). He has difficulties with spontaneous and prompted imitation skills as observed during pre-treatment assessments. The child meets the inclusion criteria for this study as he has a community diagnosis of ASD and has scored above the cutoff for "Autism" or "Autism Spectrum" on the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, 2nd Edition. The child's parents have agreed to participate in the study and have provided written consent. The child does not have any siblings who are participating in the study. The study will evaluate two different versions of Reciprocal Imitation Training (RIT) for young children with ASD. The child will receive either two 60-minute weekly sessions of therapist-implemented RIT or one weekly 60-minute session of therapist-implemented RIT and one weekly 60-minute session of parent education about using RIT in the home environment. The investigators will examine child and family outcomes between these two intervention types, including the child's imitation skills and social communication skills, as well as parent stress and parent and child behaviors during parent-child play interactions.

The patient is a 42-year-old female with a history of hypothyroidism for the past 3 years. She is currently taking levothyroxine 50 mcg daily and has been stable on this dose for the past year. She reports no symptoms of hypothyroidism such as fatigue, weight gain, or hair loss. She has no history of thyroid cancer or goiter. She denies any current use of alternative medicines or supplements. Her most recent thyroid function test showed a TSH level of 2.5 mIU/L (normal range: 0.5-5.0 mIU/L) and a free T4 level of 1.2 ng/dL (normal range: 0.8-1.8 ng/dL). She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the effect of Carum Carvi on thyroid function.

A 54-year-old man was diagnosed with prostate cancer a year ago and underwent surgery to remove his prostate gland. He has been cancer-free since then but has been experiencing cancer-related fatigue (CRF) for the past few months. He reports feeling tired and lacking energy throughout the day, which has been affecting his quality of life. He works a desk job and spends most of his time sitting at his desk. He has tried to increase his physical activity by going for a walk during his lunch break, but he finds it challenging to stay motivated. He is fluent in English and has access to a computer with internet connectivity. He has not received chemotherapy for his prostate cancer. He is interested in participating in a study that can help him reduce his sedentary behavior and improve his CRF.

Patient is a 16-year-old male high school student who plays football and basketball. He has recently suffered a concussion during a football game and has been diagnosed by a sports medicine physician at Children's Hospital Colorado. He reports experiencing symptoms such as headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. He scored a PCSS of 11 at the time of enrollment. He has no pre-existing neurological disorders or learning disabilities. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of lower extremity injuries affecting balance or structural brain injury confirmed with neuroimaging. He is motivated to participate in the study and has the ability to complete initial testing within 14 days of the injury. He has more than one month remaining in the current athletic season.

42F with a long-standing history of dry eye disease presents with complaints of burning sensation and foreign body sensation in both eyes. She reports that she has tried different over-the-counter artificial tears with minimal relief. She also admits to having difficulty wearing contact lenses due to excessive dryness. On examination, the patient has bilateral superficial punctate keratitis and decreased tear break-up time. She has no history of allergy or autoimmune disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the use of a new device to improve dry eye symptoms. The patient is capable of giving informed consent and speaks English fluently. She has not undergone any nasal or sinus surgery and has no history of coagulation disorders. She is not pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or nursing. The patient is willing to forego the use of contact lenses during the study period.

A 35 year old man presented with severe back pain and radiating leg pain. MRI revealed a herniated disc at the L4-L5 level causing severe compression of the nerve roots. He was diagnosed with lumbar disc herniation and scheduled for surgery. Preoperative laboratory studies were within normal limits. He had no significant medical history, except for occasional lower back pain. He consented to participate in the clinical trial and was randomized to receive either 24 hours of antibiotic treatment postoperatively or antibiotics for the duration of time the spinal drain was in place. During surgery, a spinal drain was placed and he received the appropriate antibiotic treatment according to his randomization. He was followed for one year postoperatively for the incidence of surgical site infection.

A 25-year-old female with a history of cervical dystonia presents for participation in a clinical trial investigating the role of the cerebellum in the cortical plasticity underlying sensorimotor adaptation in patients with dystonia. She has not received botulinum toxin treatment in the past three months and is not currently taking any medication that alters cortical excitability. She agrees to use a medically acceptable method of contraception throughout the study. She has no other neurological or psychiatric illnesses, and her physical and neurological examinations are normal except for her cervical dystonia. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not legally protected. She is enrolled in social security.

32-year-old female diagnosed with myofascial temporomandibular disorder and sleep bruxism. She reports experiencing pain and tension in her jaw, face, neck, and shoulders, as well as headaches upon waking up. The patient has a history of clenching her teeth during sleep and has been diagnosed with bruxism by her dentist. She has not received any prior physical therapy treatment for her condition. The patient is willing to undergo deep dry needling treatment in the masseter and temporalis muscles to alleviate her symptoms. She does not have any bleeding disorders or systematic joint or muscle disease. The patient does not have an insurmountable fear of needles and is able to tolerate the procedure.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease. He had a myocardial infarction 3 years ago and underwent successful percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA). He has been asymptomatic since then and takes aspirin and atorvastatin daily. He has a normal electrocardiogram and exercise stress test. He does not smoke and has no history of asthma. His blood pressure and lipid profile are well controlled. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any other medications.

A 12-year-old male patient, who is overweight with a BMI of 27.5, presents to the pediatric clinic for a routine check-up. His family history is remarkable for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia in both parents. The patient is a 7th grader and spends most of his time watching TV and playing video games. He does not participate in any sports activities and his diet is mainly fast foods and sugary drinks. He denies any symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. The physical exam shows blood pressure of 140/88 mmHg, heart rate of 85 bpm, and a waist circumference of 90 cm. His lipid profile shows elevated LDL cholesterol of 150 mg/dl and normal HDL and triglycerides. The patient is interested in participating in a physical activity program to improve his health and prevent cardiovascular diseases.

A 35 year old female with a history of mild to moderate persistent asthma comes to the clinic complaining of cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath. She reports experiencing these symptoms more frequently over the past few weeks, especially at night and in the early morning. She uses her short-acting beta-agonist inhaler on average 3 times a week and has never been hospitalized for her asthma. Her FEV1 at her last visit was 72% predicted. She denies any allergies or recent upper respiratory infections. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is otherwise healthy and not taking any other medications.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman of Asian descent who is currently pregnant and has been diagnosed with hepatitis B virus (HBV). Her HBV-DNA levels are greater than 105 IU/mL. She has a history of mild asthma and seasonal allergies, but is otherwise healthy. She has not received any prior treatment for HBV hepatitis and has not experienced any hepatitis-related symptoms during her pregnancy. The patient is currently receiving prenatal care at a participating center and is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of serovaccination in preventing mother-to-child transmission of HBV.

John is a 52-year-old man who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with monocytic differentiation. He was initially treated with chemotherapy, but unfortunately, his disease relapsed. He is now experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and fever. On physical examination, he has mild splenomegaly, but no other significant findings. He has no significant past medical history, and his laboratory studies are notable for leukocytosis and anemia. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. He has been informed about the clinical trial and is willing to participate. He understands the study requirements, is willing to provide informed consent, and is able to comply with the protocol requirements. He has not received any systemic anti-cancer therapy or radiotherapy within 7 days prior to the first day of study drug administration. He has not previously received IO-202, and he has not undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) within 60 days of the first dose of IO-202. He has not received any investigational agent within 7 days prior to their first day of study drug administration. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He does not have uncontrolled, active infection, and he is negative for hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)-related illness. His cardiac function is normal. He does not have any psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical condition that potentially hampers compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule.

25 y/o female with a diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) presenting with irregular menstrual cycles and elevated serum free testosterone. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus, pulmonary, cardiac, renal, hepatic, cholestatic, neurologic, psychiatric, infectious or malignant diseases. The patient has no history of breast cancer or deep vein thrombosis. The patient is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient has normal thyroid function tests and serum prolactin levels. The patient is willing to comply with the requirements of the study and able to provide signed, witnessed informed consent.

The patient is a 40 year old male who was admitted to the ICU with respiratory distress and was intubated for mechanical ventilation. He was diagnosed with ARDS according to the Berlin definition. His medical history is significant for hypertension and obesity. His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. Upon admission, his oxygen saturation was 86% on room air and improved to 98% with a FiO2 of 60%. His chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral infiltrates. His PaO2/FiO2 ratio was 150 mmHg. He has been receiving mechanical ventilation for the past 48 hours and is expected to require mechanical ventilation for at least another 48 hours. The patient does not have any chronic pulmonary disease and is clinically stable to undergo CT scans. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 32 year old female who has been recently diagnosed with primary hypothyroidism. She reports symptoms of fatigue, weight gain, and constipation. She is currently not taking any thyroid hormone replacement therapy. She has a history of depression and is currently taking an antidepressant medication. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. She has a BMI of 25 and her blood pressure is within normal range. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of combined therapy with L-Thyroxine and L-Triiodothyronine to L-Thyroxine alone. She is willing to undergo blood tests, urine tests, and other required procedures. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

A 12-year-old Caucasian male with a confirmed diagnosis of cystic fibrosis presented to the clinic with a history of recurrent episodes of wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. He had a positive culture for Aspergillus fumigatus in his airway flora. He had been treated for these episodes with antibiotics and bronchodilators, but the symptoms persisted. The patient's clinical history and laboratory tests were consistent with Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA), and he was enrolled in the study. The patient is not currently taking oral steroids and has not had a pulmonary exacerbation requiring hospitalization in the past 14 days. The patient will undergo T-cell response testing to Aspergillus antigens and be monitored throughout the study for any adverse reactions.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who recently noticed a small, painless lump on the side of his tongue. He also reports occasional difficulty swallowing and a sensation of something being stuck in his throat. He has a history of heavy tobacco and alcohol use for over 20 years. Upon examination, a biopsy revealed early-stage oral squamous cell carcinoma. Further evaluation with imaging studies confirmed no evidence of metastasis. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or allergies. He speaks English fluently and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

A 26-year-old man presents with a history of injecting heroin and sharing needles. He has been using for the last 3 years and is motivated to quit. On examination, he has no signs of liver disease but has a positive history of Hepatitis C. His PCR test confirms active infection with HCV genotype 1. He has no history of HIV and has not participated in any drug trial in the last 30 days. His platelet count is normal at 250000000 /ml and his alanine transaminase (ALT) is within normal limits at 30 Units/l. He is able to provide informed consent and agrees to participate in the clinical trial. He is advised of the limited safety data in pregnancy and confirms that he is not pregnant nor is he breast-feeding. He is

A 12-year-old male patient with a history of Molar-Incisor Hypomineralization (MIH) presents to the dental clinic with complaints of dental sensitivity and yellow-brown discoloration on the affected teeth. The patient was born at full term and had no complications during delivery. The patient has no history of any systemic illness and is not on any medications. The patient maintains good oral hygiene practices, including regular brushing and flossing. Clinical examination reveals enamel demineralizations on permanent molars and incisors in two different quadrants. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is provided with a toothpaste containing biomimetic hydroxyapatite. The Investigator explains the proper oral care procedures, and the toothpaste is applied for the first 7 days of the month for 6 months, as the demineralizations are moderate. The patient will attend regular follow-up visits to evaluate the efficacy of the treatment. The BEWE, Bleeding Index, Gingival index, Plaque index, and Dental sensitivity test will be evaluated at each visit.

A 27-year-old outdoor enthusiast was hiking in a remote area and was bitten by a snake on the lower right leg. He reported immediate pain, swelling and erythema at the site of the bite. He is normally healthy, with no significant medical history, and he is not taking any regular medications. He has no known allergies to medications or food. He was transported by helicopter to the nearest hospital, where he was admitted to the emergency department. Vital signs were stable, and the initial physical exam was significant for a 3 cm area of erythema and swelling around the bite site. He had no neurological symptoms or signs of envenomation on initial presentation. However, his platelet count was noted to be low at 30,000/mm3. The nurse initiated administration of CroFab antivenom and the patient was closely monitored in the emergency department. After 2 hours, his platelet count had decreased to 20,000/mm3. The decision was made to enroll him in the clinical trial to receive either Anavip or CroFab. He provided informed consent and was randomized to receive Anavip. The patient was monitored closely for the duration of the study, with regular blood draws to monitor platelet count, fibrinogen level, and venom levels. He reported no adverse effects from the treatment and was discharged from the hospital on day 3 with a platelet count of 100,000/mm3.

The patient is a 60 year old male who has been experiencing progressive muscle weakness and wasting in his arms and legs for the past two years. He has been diagnosed with sporadic inclusion body myositis (s-IBM) and has been receiving treatment with prednisone and methotrexate for the past six months. However, he has not experienced any significant improvement in his symptoms. He is willing to undergo therapy with alemtuzumab and is interested in participating in this clinical trial. He has no history of active malignancy, immunodeficiency syndrome or cardiac insufficiency, and his platelet count and hemoglobin levels are within normal limits. He is currently not taking any immunosuppressive drugs and is willing to travel to the Clinical Center for planned studies and treatment as required by the protocol. He is a retired engineer, enjoys reading and watching movies, and lives with his spouse. He has two adult children who live in a different state. He has agreed to use an acceptable method of birth control during and for six months after the completion of treatment.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic melanoma, stage IV, with BRAF V600E mutation. She has already undergone one standard of care regimen but has experienced disease progression. She is in good overall health, with an ECOG performance status of 1, and has adequate hematologic, renal, and liver function. She has no active CNS lesions or history of spinal cord compression or carcinomatous meningitis. She is not currently undergoing any anti-cancer therapies other than those administered in this study. She has not previously been treated with a BRAF inhibitor or MEK inhibitor. She has no severe cardiovascular disease within the past 6 months and has not had any previous malignancies within the past 5 years, except for basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, melanoma in-situ and carcinoma in-situ of the cervix.

This is a 15-year-old female who has recently shown early signs of anorexia nervosa, including fear of gaining weight, avoiding certain foods, and excessive exercise. She lives with her parents and younger sibling, and has no significant medical history or current medication use. She has not been diagnosed with anorexia nervosa, but meets two to three criteria for the disorder. She has not previously participated in any study treatment and is not currently undergoing psychological treatment. She is medically stable for outpatient treatment and is receiving no other treatment for an eating disorder.

58-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis of the thumb joint for 2 years, with a recent worsening of pain in the past 6 months. The patient reports pain in the affected joint as 7 on an 11-point numerical pain rating scale in the week prior to screening. The patient has tried acetaminophen for pain relief but has not experienced significant improvement. The patient has no known allergies to oxycodone, NSAIDS or tramadol. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and has no other medical conditions that may interfere with the assessment of pain thresholds. The patient is not taking any concurrent medications that are contraindicated with any of the study medications. The patient has an estimated renal clearance of greater than 30 mL/min based on the Cockcroft Gault equation.

The patient is a 9-year-old child who has been diagnosed with a congenital heart defect and requires an elective surgical procedure under general anesthesia. The child has never undergone surgery before and is experiencing significant anxiety about the upcoming procedure. The child and their parents understand Swiss German and possess a smartphone with internet access. The child has no hearing impairment or neurologic disorder and does not require postoperative intensive care. The child has never received anesthesia before and has an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score of II. The child's parent has provided informed consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial.

28-year-old nulliparous female, with a singleton pregnancy, currently in the 9th week of gestation, with a primary school education, and receiving antenatal care at the hospital where the research is being conducted. The patient has no current medical conditions and has not experienced any complications during her pregnancy thus far. She is willing to participate in the study voluntarily and has no plans to seek antenatal care elsewhere during the course of the study.

A 16-year-old female presents with a BMI of 32, which is above the 95th percentile for her age group. She has been struggling with her weight for the past few years and has tried various diets with little success. She spends an average of 6 hours per night on her cell phone and has a hard time falling asleep before midnight due to her academic demands and extracurricular activities. She reports feeling fatigued and groggy throughout the day. She has no history of sleep disorders or severe mental illness. Her physical exam is unremarkable, and she appears healthy otherwise.

A 9-year-old male student living in a rural area of Uganda. He attends a primary school located in a high malaria transmission area. His parents work as subsistence farmers and live in a small house without mosquito nets. The student has had malaria twice in the past year, and he missed several days of school due to the illness. He is generally healthy and has no known allergies or chronic medical conditions. His parents have provided written consent for him to participate in the study, and he has assented to participate.

This is a 35-year-old male with a past medical history of epilepsy diagnosed at the age of 12. The patient has been on multiple antiepileptic medications such as carbamazepine, valproic acid, and lamotrigine but has never been able to achieve seizure control. The patient has been experiencing an average of 4 seizures per month for the past 6 months. The patient has undergone an MRI which revealed a focal lesion in the left temporal lobe. The patient is interested in surgical options for the treatment of his epilepsy and has been referred to the clinical trial of MgLiTT for medical refractory epilepsy. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to participate in the trial. The patient has no contraindications for MRI and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 28-year-old female with a long-standing history of jaw misalignment, which has caused her significant aesthetic and functional issues. She has been experiencing difficulty speaking and chewing, and her confidence has been negatively affected due to the appearance of her face. The patient has tried non-surgical options such as braces, but they have not provided her with the desired results. She is otherwise healthy and has no underlying medical conditions. The patient has been referred to Toulouse Teaching Hospital for orthognathic surgery as a potential solution to her jaw misalignment. During the pre-operative consultation, the surgeon and patient have decided to proceed with outpatient surgery, and the patient has given her oral agreement. The patient is excited about the prospect of improving her quality of life and is looking forward to the procedure.

A 35-year-old male with a history of TBI complains of difficulty walking due to equinovarus foot deformity. He has been experiencing this problem for the past 6 months, and it is affecting his daily activities. He cannot walk without the support of braces, and it is causing him significant discomfort. He has tried physical therapy and ankle-foot orthosis, but they have not provided satisfactory results. He is married and has two children. He works as a software engineer and sits at a desk for most of the day. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no significant medical or family history. He has not received botulinum toxin or serial casting in the past 4 months. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and be available for the duration of the study. His Modified Ashworth Scale is 2.

A 32-year-old woman and her husband have been trying to conceive for 3 years. They have undergone multiple cycles of IVF and ICSI with no success due to fertilization failure. The woman's medical history is significant for endometriosis and laparoscopic surgery for the same 2 years ago. She has a regular menstrual cycle of 28 days, and her hormonal profile is normal. She has no history of sexually transmitted infections or pelvic inflammatory disease. Her husband's semen analysis shows normal volume, count, and motility. The couple has no history of genetic disorders. They are willing to participate in a clinical trial to improve their chances of success in the next ICSI cycle.

A 25 year old female is interested in making minor changes to the appearance of her nose. She has never undergone any cosmetic treatments or surgeries on her nose in the past. She is not pregnant or nursing and does not have any known allergies to any components of the study ingredients. She is not taking any medications for bleeding disorders, aspirin, ibuprofen, St. John's Wort, or high doses of Vitamin E supplements. She is willing to understand the purpose and aspects of the study, sign the consent and complete the required treatment and follow-up visits.

26 y/o female with a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) as per the 1997 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Modified Classification Criteria. The patient has been diagnosed for 2 years and has a history of skin rash, joint pain, fatigue, and photosensitivity. The patient is currently taking hydroxychloroquine and prednisone for management of her SLE symptoms. The patient has no history of lupus nephritis or other major organ involvement. The patient is able to provide written consent and is willing to participate in the study.

There is no patient involved in this clinical trial. The trial is focused on assessing the perspectives of Habilitation Assistants and parents/legal guardians on end-of-life care for medically fragile and intellectually disabled children and young adults in a long-term care facility.

Pregnant women in their second trimester, aged between 25-35 years, with no past medical history of UTIs or kidney disease, and not currently taking any antibiotics, are eligible for this clinical trial. The patient must have been diagnosed with a urinary tract infection through clinical examination and urine analysis. The trial includes three groups: group 1 consists of pregnant women with cystitis, group 2 consists of pregnant women with pyelonephritis, and group 3 consists of pregnant women with asymptomatic bacteriuria. Patients with any anatomical abnormalities in the urinary tract will be excluded from the trial. The patient must be willing to provide urine samples and undergo bacterial culture testing for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was admitted to the hospital with fever, chills, and confusion. He was diagnosed with severe sepsis and septic shock based on ACCP/SCCM criteria. Blood cultures were drawn, and broad-spectrum antibiotics were initiated immediately. His medical history revealed hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has no history of liver or kidney disease. His current medications include metformin and lisinopril. Upon admission, his blood pressure was 80/50 mmHg, and he required vasopressor support. His laboratory results showed elevated white blood cell count, high lactate levels, and elevated procalcitonin levels. He was randomized to the PCT-guided algorithm group, and PCT levels were measured at randomization, day 4, 7, 10, and 14. The initial PCT level was 20 ng/mL. Antibiotic therapy was started, and the patient received intravenous sodium selenite as a bolus and then a continuous infusion for 21 days. The patient's condition improved, and he was weaned off vasopressors and mechanical ventilation. He was discharged from the ICU after 14 days and transferred to the medical ward for further management. His most recent PCT level was 0.5 ng/mL, and antimicrobial therapy was stopped according to the PCT-guided algorithm. The patient was informed about the clinical trial and provided informed consent to participate.

A 35-year-old heterosexual married woman and her husband came to the clinic concerned about their sedentary lifestyle. They both work in an office and feel that their work routine has made them less active. They have been living together for 7 years and have no children. The woman has a BMI of 26.8 and has no history of severe cardiovascular or pulmonary diseases, diseases or injuries of the musculoskeletal system, degenerative neurological diseases, or paraplegia. She has a good understanding of the German language. Her husband has a BMI of 28.5 and also has no history of severe cardiovascular or pulmonary diseases, diseases or injuries of the musculoskeletal system, degenerative neurological diseases, or paraplegia. He also has a good understanding of the German language. They are both interested in participating in a clinical trial to enhance their daily physical activity and would like to be randomly assigned to one of the intervention groups.

9-year-old male with a history of chronic snoring and allergic rhinitis. He has a history of frequent upper respiratory infections and is currently not taking any medications for his allergies. He has never undergone adenotonsillectomy. He has been referred for evaluation for possible sleep apnea due to his snoring and restless sleep. He has no known craniofacial, neuromuscular, syndromic, or genetic abnormalities. He has not received systemic corticosteroid therapy or antibiotics in the past 2 weeks. He is not currently on immunotherapy.

A 45-year-old female presents with a family history of colorectal cancer. She has never undergone a colonoscopy before and is nervous about the procedure. She reports occasional abdominal discomfort and constipation, but otherwise has no significant medical history. Her physical exam is unremarkable. Her gastroenterologist has recommended a colonoscopy to screen for colon cancer and polyps. The patient is given the option to participate in a clinical trial comparing water infusion colonoscopy to air insufflation colonoscopy. She is provided with detailed information about the study and consents to participate.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with confirmed EGFR-activating mutation after disease progression during/after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. She presents with worsening cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and has no history of other cancers. Her family history is not significant for any cancers. Her lab study is as follows: FBS: 95 mg/dl, HbA1c: 5.2%, cholesterol: 165 mg/dl, TG: 100 mg/dl, LDL: 100 mg/dl, HDL: 45 mg/dl. She has completed one round of platinum-based chemotherapy and has documented radiological disease progression during/after most recent treatment regimen for locally-advanced or metastatic disease. She has at least one measurable lesion per RECIST version 1.1 and has Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 at Screening. She is willing to provide archival tumor tissue from a biopsy performed within 6 months of consent and performed after progression during/after treatment with most recent cancer therapy regimen OR has at least 1 lesion, not previously irradiated, amenable to core biopsy and is willing to undergo tumor biopsy. She has no history of interstitial lung disease (ILD) or clinically active central nervous system metastases. She is not taking any drugs that are known to prolong the QT interval.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who has been referred to the clinic for evaluation of her bone health. She has no history of mobility handicap and has never been treated with growth hormone, oral corticoids, or anti-calcineurin. She is not currently taking any medication, including aspirin or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. She has no chronic inflammatory disease, systemic diseases, renal failure, or diabetes. She has no serious intercurrent disease, and she is not pregnant. She is affiliated with the French universal healthcare system. She has never received vitamin D supplementation and her nutritional status is considered normal. Her parents have provided written informed consent for her participation in the study. The patient will be evaluated for vitamin D serum concentration and bone assessment by HR-pQCT.

The patient is a 55 year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis and underwent aortic valve replacement surgery. The surgery was uncomplicated and he was transferred to the Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit (CVICU) for post-operative management. He is currently intubated and ventilator-dependent. He has a history of smoking and quit 5 years ago. He has no known drug allergies. His creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min and his liver function tests are within normal limits. He is currently receiving propofol and fentanyl infusions for sedation and pain control respectively. The patient has residual neuromuscular blockade with a Train Of Four ratio of <0.9.

A 47-year-old Hispanic man, who received a kidney transplant five years ago, reported to the clinic with a history of recurrent UTIs and lower back pain. The patient had a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and obesity. His current medications included tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and prednisone for immunosuppression. The patient had no history of cancer in his family, and he had never been diagnosed with any cancer before. The physical examination revealed a palpable mass in the right flank. Further investigations showed the presence of a renal mass, and the biopsy confirmed renal cell carcinoma. The patient underwent a nephrectomy, and the histopathology report showed clear cell renal cell carcinoma. The patient was referred to an oncologist for further management.

50-year-old male with a history of stable angina and known severe coronary artery disease confirmed on coronary angiogram with >95% stenosis of at least one major coronary artery. The patient has not undergone any previous percutaneous or surgical revascularization. The patient has no evidence of ongoing infection or inflammation and no known malignancy. The patient's serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dl and he does not have diabetes.

A 28-year-old woman who is generally healthy is interested in participating in the clinical trial. She is not taking any medications currently and has no significant medical history. She has a BMI within the range of 18-30 kg/m2. She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She has never been pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements. She underwent screening procedures and laboratory tests and was found to be eligible for the study.

A 45 year old woman with diffuse systemic sclerosis who has been experiencing rapid deterioration in pulmonary function over the past 6 months. She has a skin score of 18 and has been diagnosed with interstitial or pulmonary vasculitis with evidence of alveolitis by bronchoalveolar lavage. She has proteinuria of 750 mg/24 hours and her DLCO is 60% predicted. The patient is ineligible for autologous or allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell or bone marrow transplantation. She has not received any immunosuppressive therapy for at least 4 days. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80%. Her hematopoietic system is normal with an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mm3 and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. Her hepatic system is normal with a bilirubin level of 1.5 times ULN and SGOT level of 2 times ULN. Her renal system is functioning with creatinine clearance of 45 ml/min. She is HIV negative and has no active uncontrolled infection. She is not pregnant and has tested negative for pregnancy. She has no known hypersensitivity to rabbit proteins and has no history of hemorrhagic cystitis requiring transfusion.

A 28-day-old preterm infant girl was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit with a birth weight of 1200 grams and a gestational age of 30 weeks. She had a history of anemia and required blood transfusions. The infant had a respiratory rate of 54 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation of 92% on room air, heart rate of 150 beats per minute, and blood pressure of 65/42 mmHg. She had no signs of sepsis, shock, severe intracranial hemorrhage, NEC, abdominal or cranial surgery. The infant was placed on a continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machine and received intravenous fluids before the blood transfusion. A near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) device was placed on her forehead to measure cerebral oxygenation during the blood transfusion. Blood transfusion was performed over two hours, and the NIRS device was continuously monitored during this time. The infant's vital signs were closely monitored throughout the procedure. After the blood transfusion, the infant's respiratory rate decreased to 40 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation increased to 97%, and blood pressure increased to 75/50 mmHg. The NIRS device showed an increase in cerebral oxygenation during the blood transfusion. The infant was observed for any adverse reactions or complications after the transfusion.

A 70-year-old male with a history of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and a myocardial infarction 2 years ago presents with symptoms of shortness of breath and fatigue. He has been compliant with his medications and blood pressure is well controlled. His HbA1c is 7.2% and he is on oral hypoglycemic agents. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He has no known history of atrial fibrillation or flutter, and has not had a pacemaker implanted. His echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 45%. He has no history of skin allergies or end-stage disease. He has not undergone an ECG recording by continuous single-lead device before. He is willing to participate in the study to assess his risk of atrial fibrillation.

42-year-old male patient with a history of chronic plaque psoriasis vulgaris presented to the clinic. He has been suffering from psoriasis for over 5 years with lesions covering approximately 8% of his body surface area. His condition is clinically stable, and he is not currently receiving any standard, FDA-approved psoriasis therapies. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of oral Curcuminoid C3 Complex® for the treatment of psoriasis. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which he takes amlodipine 5 mg daily, and hyperlipidemia, which is controlled with atorvastatin 20 mg daily. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. His physical exam reveals moderate plaque thickness on his back, elbows, and knees. He is willing to give written informed consent and is available for the total duration of the study. He is sexually active with his female partner, who is surgically incapable of childbearing. He is not allergic to turmeric or curry powder. He has not received any experimental drug or medical device within the last 30 days prior to screening. His laboratory results are within normal limits, and he is able to swallow pills.

A 51-year-old Chinese-Canadian man with a history of elevated blood pressure visited his primary care physician for a routine check-up. He has no significant medical history, except for mild hypertension that was diagnosed two years ago. He used to smoke but quit 10 years ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally but never more than 2 drinks per week. He works in the IT industry and is married with two children. He speaks Mandarin fluently and is able to read and write Chinese. He has access to a telephone. He has not used any antihypertensive medications or other medications that raise or lower blood pressure during the previous three months. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that explores the effects of a culturally sensitive dietary intervention targeting Chinese Canadians with hypertension.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic pain in her right hand and forearm due to a previous injury. She has been scheduled for surgery to repair a damaged tendon in her wrist. She has no known allergies to local anesthetics or any other medication. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has never had a supraclavicular block before but is willing to consider it as a means of reducing her pain during and after the procedure. She does not have any respiratory issues and does not smoke. She is not pregnant and is not currently taking any opioids for her pain. She has no history of neuropathy or any other nerve-related conditions. She is able to cooperate with the study procedures and follow-up assessments.

A 16-year-old Chinese girl was referred to the clinic by her school counselor due to complaints of difficulty sleeping and feeling down most days. She reports having trouble falling asleep and staying asleep, as well as waking up too early. She also reports feeling sad, hopeless, and unmotivated most days. She denies any past history of substance abuse or dependence, manic or hypomanic episodes, schizophrenia spectrum disorders, neurodevelopmental disorders, organic mental disorders, or intellectual disabilities. She has no known medical conditions that affect her sleep quality. She is not taking any medications that affect her sleep continuity or quality. She denies any suicidal ideation with a plan or attempt. She has not been enrolled in any other clinical trial investigational products within the past month. She has not received structured psychotherapy before. She has no hearing or speech deficit and is not a night shift worker.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital for elective surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. He has an ASA physical status of 2 and needs to undergo general anesthesia with nasotracheal intubation. The patient has been informed of the study and has given signed written consent to participate. The patient is anticipated to have a difficult airway and has been enrolled in the study. The patient does not have any contraindications to nasal intubation.

A 57-year-old woman came to the clinic with a complaint of severe dry mouth that started after she underwent radiotherapy for head and neck tumours 8 months ago. She has been experiencing difficulty in speaking, swallowing, and chewing food. She has tried using different types of mouthwash, but none of them have been effective in relieving her symptoms. The patient explained that she had received a total radiation dose of 60 Gy to the head and neck region. The physical examination revealed that the salivary glands were not functioning properly, and the amount of saliva produced was significantly reduced. The patient was informed about the study and expressed her willingness to participate. She has no known allergies, and her medical history does not include any of the exclusion criteria listed for the study.

The patient is a 49-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital with a high fever, chills, and a productive cough. He has been diagnosed with pneumonia and sepsis. His vital signs are unstable with a blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg and a heart rate of 120 beats per minute. His laboratory results show an elevated lactate level of 5 mmol/L and altered mental status. The patient's family has given written consent for him to participate in a clinical trial comparing initial resuscitation with plasma to initial resuscitation with balanced crystalloids. He has no history of myocardial infarction or congestive heart failure, or any contraindications to blood transfusions or central venous line and arterial line placement. He meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and is eligible for randomization.

A 10-year-old girl was diagnosed with Rasmussen Encephalitis (RE) after experiencing frequent seizures and weakness on the right side of her body. She has undergone multiple treatments, including immunoglobulin and corticosteroid therapy, but her seizures have been resistant to all treatment options. The patient has been started on adalimumab, an anti-TNF treatment, as a last resort for her RE. She has been compliant with the treatment and has shown some improvement in her symptoms. The patient's family is willing to participate in the study to provide long-term data on the efficacy and safety of adalimumab in the treatment of RE.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who is retired and spends a lot of time at home. She has noticed that she is forgetting things more often and has difficulty concentrating on tasks for long periods of time. She has a computer and internet access at home and is looking for ways to keep her mind active and engaged. She has no history of dementia or other cognitive impairments, and is interested in participating in this study to see if the brain training programme can help improve her cognitive abilities.

A 52-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 10-year history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). She reports pain and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and knees. She has tried multiple medications in the past, including methotrexate, with limited success. She currently takes methotrexate once a week at a dose of 20mg. She is married with two children and works part-time as a librarian. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of infections or surgeries in the past year. Her most recent blood work shows an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 34 mm and a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 18 mg/L. She is positive for rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

A 45-year-old male with a history of a soft tissue defect following a traumatic injury that has not healed properly despite conventional therapies. The defect is located on the lower leg and has been present for over a year. The patient has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves the use of his own stem cells obtained from subcutaneous fat harvested by liposuction. The patient understands the risks associated with the clinical trial, including the possibility of infection, bleeding, and the potential for the therapy to fail. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study protocol and is able to read, understand, and sign the informed consent form.

This is a 62-year-old male who underwent allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (alloHCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) six months ago. He received standard antiviral therapy for CMV viremia that was diagnosed two weeks ago, but his CMV viremia is still persistent. He has no history of CMV infection prior to alloHCT. He has no known allergies and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He has no history of drug abuse or alcoholism. He has no known genetic mutations associated with antiviral drug resistance. He has been in morphologic remission since alloHCT. His ALT and AST are within normal limits and his total bilirubin is slightly elevated due to CMV infection. He meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the ATA230 clinical trial. He is willing and able to provide written informed consent.

This is a 45-year-old female who is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic hysterectomy for a benign indication. She has no history of chronic opioid use and has not taken opioids within 2 weeks of her scheduled surgery. She is fluent in English and has no history of epilepsy or claustrophobia. She will be under the care of either Dr. Jamal Mourad or Dr. Nichole Mahnert during her surgery. She has been given the option to participate in a study that will test the effectiveness of virtual reality in reducing pain scores and oral and intravenous opioid consumption during the immediate postoperative period after her surgery. She has been provided with information about the study, including the risks and benefits, and has voluntarily consented to participate. She will be given a subject number to de-identify her during the study. She will be asked to rate her pain at defined intervals in the post anesthesia recovery unit (PACU) and complete a survey assessing her satisfaction with her post operative recovery at her two week post op visit. She will be able to discontinue use of the VR goggles at any time she wishes.

This is a 52-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection of genotype 1a. He was diagnosed with HCV 3 years ago and has not received any prior treatment for the same. He has been experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite, and occasional abdominal pain for the past few months. He has no history of hypertension, cardiac disease, or any other significant medical condition. His liver function tests show mildly elevated AST and ALT, but normal bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase levels. He has a BMI of 26.2 and weighs 75 kg. He has no known drug allergies and has not consumed alcohol in the last month. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and restrictions and is capable of giving written informed consent. He has no family history of prolonged QT syndrome or sudden cardiac death. He has not had any major surgeries or significant gastrointestinal tract surgeries. He is not lactating and has not participated in any clinical trial in the last 30 days.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer, which has spread to her bones and lungs. She has previously received two different chemotherapy regimens for her cancer, but her tumors have continued to grow. She has not received any prior treatment with capecitabine. She is currently experiencing mild fatigue and some shortness of breath on exertion. Her performance status is 1, meaning she is able to carry out most activities of daily living but may require some assistance with more strenuous activities. She has no history of significant medical problems and her blood work, including liver and kidney function, is within normal limits. She has no evidence of brain metastases. She is not pregnant and has been using adequate contraception. She is willing and able to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 32-year-old American woman who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 4 years. She experiences symptoms of cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath at least twice a week despite being on a stable therapeutic regimen for the past 4 weeks. Her spirometry reveals post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of 60% of predicted and post-bronchodilator FEV1 of 70%. She has a history of allergies to pollen and dust mites. She has not been hospitalized for asthma in the past year and has not participated in any other clinical trials involving MEDI-563. She has a history of smoking for 5 years, but quit 2 years ago. She is currently not smoking and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse in the past year. She has no evidence of active infection or acute illness. She is willing to maintain the same therapeutic regimen and doses throughout the study and is able to complete the follow-up period as required by the protocol. She is willing to forego other forms of experimental treatment and study procedures during the study and during an 84-day period after the last dose of study drug. She is able to provide spirometric readings that meet ATS standards. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using two effective methods of avoiding pregnancy. She has no history of coagulation disorders that would contraindicate mucosal biopsies.

A 52 yo F with metastatic breast cancer, diagnosed 3 years ago, currently receiving treatment with docetaxel, with evidence of progressive disease on imaging studies.
