The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are currently well-controlled with medication. Imaging studies show measurable disease with N-cadherin expression in tumor tissue. The patient has not received prior treatment with ADH-1 or any investigational drug in the last 4 weeks. The patient has not had any history of spinal cord compression, primary brain tumors, or brain metastases. The patient has not had any clinically significant evidence of active bleeding, stroke, major surgery, or other major tissue injury in the last 4 weeks. The patient has no history of uncontrolled congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, or life-threatening arrhythmias.

Patient is a 60-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with chest pain and was diagnosed with an acute myocardial infarction. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. He is a non-smoker and has never had a heart attack before. The patient has no known contraindications for contrast-enhanced CMR and is clinically stable. He has no history of congestive heart failure, arrhythmias, ongoing chest pain, or ECG changes suggestive of acute/ongoing ischemia. His systolic blood pressure is 130 mmHg and well-controlled on his current medications. The patient has a telephone number and address for follow-up and is not claustrophobic. He is willing to participate in the study and understands its purpose and risks.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl diagnosed with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) by a pediatric hepatologist. She has been experiencing severe itching for several months, which is affecting her sleep and quality of life. Her mother is her primary caregiver and has noticed a significant decrease in her daughter's energy level and mood due to the constant itching. They have tried various treatments, including antihistamines and topical ointments, but nothing has provided significant relief. She is willing to participate in a 2-week validation study to assess the effectiveness of the ItchRO instrument in measuring her itching symptoms. She is able to speak and understand English and is comfortable using electronic diaries to report her symptoms.

46-year-old male with a history of high-grade non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) diagnosed 2 years ago. The patient underwent transurethral resection of the bladder (TUR-B) and adjuvant instillation therapy with Bacillus Calmette-Geerin (BCG). The patient has been recurrence-free for the past year, as detected by flexible cystoscopy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the potential clinical impact of a highly sensitive urinary marker, the Xpert Bladder Cancer Monitor, regarding possible reduction in the number of flexible cystoscopies in an outpatient setting without decreasing recurrence-free survival or increasing the risk of progression. The patient is able to understand the Participant Information sheet orally and in writing and is willing to comply with the trial protocol. The patient has no history of any upper urinary tract tumor regardless of grade and stage within the last 5 years prior to randomization, and no CIS or invasive tumor within 3 months before randomization.

A 25-year old female office worker living in London, UK has been suffering from hayfever for several years now. She has tried different over-the-counter (OTC) antihistamines but none of them seem to work well for her. She recently purchased Pirinase Hayfever Relief for Adults 0.05% Nasal Spray to relieve her symptoms. She has been using it for the past 10 days and has noticed a significant improvement in her symptoms. She is willing to participate in the online survey to provide feedback on the product. She has no known allergies and is generally healthy. She does not smoke and does not take any other medications. She lives alone and works from home due to the pandemic.

The patient is a 30-year-old man who has been diagnosed with recurrent Hodgkin's Lymphoma. He has failed standard therapy and is now being considered for high dose therapy and autologous stem cell transplantation. He has been found to have CD30 positive tumor and EBV seropositivity. The patient has recovered from acute toxic effects of all prior chemotherapy at least one week ago and 30 days from prior chemotherapy before entering this study. His bilirubin, AST, and serum creatinine levels are within normal range. His pulmonary function is adequate with FEV1, FVC, and DLCO at 50% or greater of expected corrected for hemoglobin. The patient is sexually active and willing to utilize one of the more effective birth control methods during the study and for 6 months after the study concludes. He has not received anti-CD30 antibody-based therapy within the previous 6 weeks and has no history of hypersensitivity reactions to murine protein-containing products.

A 62-year-old Chinese man with a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with severe pain in his right knee due to osteoarthritis. He has difficulty walking and performing daily activities due to the pain. The patient is scheduled for an elective primary unilateral total knee replacement surgery. He is able to speak and understand Cantonese and is willing to provide informed oral and written consent to participate in the study. The patient has no known allergies to opioids, local anaesthetic drugs, paracetamol, or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) including COX-2 inhibitors. He has no history of chronic pain other than chronic knee pain and is not taking daily glucocorticoids or strong opioids. The patient has no history of severe heart disease (NYHA 2) or alcohol or drug abuse. He has no impaired renal function and is not on immunosuppressants. The patient is not pregnant and has no local infections. He is willing to use patient controlled analgesia (PCA) and is not on immunosuppressants.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been diagnosed with lung cancer. He has been scheduled for a lobectomy surgery using the MicroCutter Stapler and Reloads for hemostasis during the procedure. The patient has a history of smoking and has been experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. He has undergone several imaging tests, including PET-CT, which showed a single lesion in the right upper lobe of the lung. The patient has been referred to a thoracic surgeon for further management. The patient is willing to participate in the MATCH registry and has signed the informed consent form. Pre-operative data including medical history and demographics have been collected, and the surgeon will provide objective and subjective evaluation of the use of the stapler during the procedure. Post-operative data will also be collected at hospital discharge and during the clinician's standard post-operative follow-up.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing muscle weakness and difficulty breathing for the past few years. He has a history of respiratory infections and has been experiencing weight loss and poor appetite. He has a family history of Pompe disease, and his brother was recently diagnosed with the condition. The patient is concerned that he may also have Pompe disease and is looking for a way to get an accurate diagnosis. He is married and has two children. He works as an accountant and enjoys playing basketball in his free time. He has not noticed any significant changes in his heart function. He is willing to participate in the study and provide a blood sample for the development of a new biomarker for the early and sensitive diagnosis of Pompe disease.

A 62-year old retired librarian was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She has been managing her blood sugar levels with metformin and has not required insulin therapy yet. The patient complains of infrequent bowel movements and discomfort. She reports having a bowel movement only once or twice a week, and she has to strain to do so. She is careful about her diet and drinks plenty of water. She also takes a fiber supplement, but it does not seem to help much. She has not experienced any significant weight loss or changes in appetite. She is alert and oriented, and her cognitive functions are intact. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are being managed with medications. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has been experiencing blurred vision in his right eye and was diagnosed with cataracts. The patient has never been diagnosed with dry eye disease and has no history of ocular surface disease. The patient has not used any topical ophthalmic medication or lubricating eyedrops in the last 4 days. The patient has a Shirmer test result of 20 mm/5' and a BUT of 10 seconds. The patient is interested in participating in the study and is able to sign the informed consent form. The patient does not have any of the exclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with ulcerative colitis and underwent surgery to create a J-pouch. She has been experiencing chronic pouchitis for the past year, with recurring episodes of bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and fever despite repeated antibiotic treatments. She has been taking ciprofloxacin and metronidazole for the past 3 months. Her symptoms have not improved, and she is looking for alternative treatment options. The patient is generally healthy and has not been diagnosed with any other medical conditions. She has no history of allergies or severe reactions to medications. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given her informed consent. She will undergo screening for infectious diseases and complete an extensive questionnaire regarding her medical history before being included in the study.

The patient is a 52 year old man with a history of heart failure due to ischemic cardiomyopathy. Despite being on optimal medical therapy, his heart function has continued to deteriorate, and his cardiologist has recommended left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation as a bridge to transplant. He has been found to meet clinical and socioeconomic screening criteria for elective LVAD implantation by the University of Washington Mechanical Circulatory Support Program. He is scheduled to undergo LVAD implantation in 3-4 weeks. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of nicotinamide riboside (NR) on heart function in heart failure patients undergoing LVAD implantation. He has no history of liver or kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes-related complications, or substance abuse. He has no known allergies to niacin, nicotinamide or warfarin. He is able to comply with study visits and procedures and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been diagnosed with dermatomyositis (DM) according to the criteria of Bohan and Peter. She has experienced muscle weakness in the neck, shoulders, and hips, and has been treated with glucocorticoids and other immunosuppressive agents, to which she has not responded adequately. She has also been diagnosed with anti-Mi-2 autoantibodies. She has a low-grade fever and a rash on her face and hands. She is a teacher and is married with two children. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She has no history of active malignant disease or recurrent bacterial, viral, fungal, mycobacterial, or other infections. She has no history of major surgery, immunodeficiency, or severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to human, humanized or murine monoclonal antibodies. Her body weight is 70 kg, and her laboratory values are as follows: serum creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL, platelet count: 150,000/mm3, hemoglobin: 11.5 g/dL, white blood cell count: 6,000/mm3, absolute neutrophil count: 3.5 x 109/L (3500/mm3), absolute lymphocyte count: 1.5 x 109/L (1500/mm3). She is willing to use an effective method of contraception during treatment and for twelve months after completion of treatment. She has provided written informed consent.

32 y/o female with a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes for the past 5 years, currently using a rapid-acting insulin analog for insulin delivery. BMI is 24 kg/m². Hemoglobin A1c level is 7.5%. No known allergies or history of hypersensitivity to insulin lispro. No episodes of severe hypoglycemia in the past 6 months. No more than 1 episode of diabetic ketoacidosis in the past 6 months. The patient is interested in participating in the study to assess the safety, functionality, and performance of the predictive low glucose suspend feature in an automated insulin delivery system.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who is scheduled for an open chest surgery for a programmed coronary bypass. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medications for both conditions. He has no other significant medical history and has never participated in any clinical trials before. He is interested in participating in this study to contribute to scientific research and potentially improve future treatments for patients.

The patient is a 13-year-old girl accompanied by her mother for a routine check-up. The mother is a 38-year-old Spanish-speaking woman who is fluent in English as well. The child has received her first dose of the HPV vaccine but has not yet received the second dose. The family receives their healthcare at one of the 5 CHICA clinics. They are interested in learning more about the HPV vaccine and any additional information that can help them make informed decisions. They are willing to participate in the study and provide feedback on the integrated digital approach used during their office visit.

Pt is a 43yo F with a history of low HDL cholesterol levels. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. She does not smoke, drink alcohol in moderation, and exercises regularly. She does not take any medications or dietary supplements. She reports consuming fish once a week and has no known allergies to the study food. The patient is interested in participating in the feeding trial to determine how combinations of different dietary bioactive ingredients influence HDL metabolism. She is willing to consume a milkshake with different combinations of marine and dairy fats and vitamin supplements on three separate days and provide blood and urine samples throughout the study.

This clinical trial is looking for participants who are healthy smokers of traditional cigarettes or e-cigarettes, as well as healthy non-smoking volunteers without any history of lung disease. Eligible smokers must have a minimum of 1 packyear smoking history for traditional cigarette smokers and a minimum of 1 year of smoking history for e-cigarette smokers. Participants must not be currently on inhaled corticosteroid therapy and not have any respiratory infections for at least 6 weeks prior to study enrollment. The trial will involve spirometry tests and the collection of exhaled breath condensate before and after smoking a traditional or electronic cigarette. The goal of the study is to evaluate and compare the acute response to traditional and electronic cigarettes in healthy smokers and assess the concentration of markers of airway inflammation released in smokers.

56 year old female who underwent gastric bypass surgery for morbid obesity 1 month ago. The patient presented with persistent abdominal pain and fever. CT scan showed anastomotic leak from the gastric pouch. She underwent an endoscopic procedure to drain the collection and was started on nil per mouth. The patient has a past medical history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obstructive sleep apnea. She is currently on metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, and a CPAP machine. The patient has no known allergies and is currently insured. The American Society of Anesthesiologists score is 3.

The patient is a 45-year-old man diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) 2 years ago. He has been on a treatment regimen that includes tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) and a ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitor. His most recent viral load was undetectable, and his CD4 count was 540 cells/mm³. He has no history of kidney disease and his estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is above 60 mL/min. He has no history of hepatitis B infection or decompensated liver disease. He is willing and able to comply with study procedures and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance medical knowledge in the field of HIV treatment.

The patient is a 65 year old male with newly diagnosed prostate cancer. The cancer is localized and has not spread outside the capsule (T1 and T2). The patient is scheduled to undergo localized prostate XRT treatments. He has a Zubrod performance status of 1 and his Karnofsy score is greater than 80. His pre-randomization serum PSA is less than 25 and his Kattan nomogram is less than 15%. He has normal blood CBC and biochemistry up to two weeks before screening, with normal CBC, ANC, platelets, hemoglobin, serum creatinine, serum bilirubin, SGOT/SGPT and normal values of the PT, PTT, and INR tests. He is able to comprehend and give informed consent for participation in this study. The patient has no prior history of radical prostatectomy, cryosurgery or radiotherapy for prostate cancer or other local therapy for prostate cancer. He has not undergone prior radiotherapy to the pelvis, including brachytherapy at the same body organ. The patient has no history of unstable angina and/or congestive heart failure requiring hospitalization within the last 6 months prior to screening, transmural myocardial infarction within the last 6 months prior to screening, acute infection requiring intravenous antibiotics at the time of screening, bleeding disorders, uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, HIV positive or any other immunosuppressive disorder, renal failure, inflammatory diseases of the perineal skin, urinary tract infection or acute or chronic prostatitis, active inflammatory bowel disease, rectal carcinoma, or cognitive disorder. The patient is not currently participating in any other clinical study and there is no physician objection to including him in this clinical trial.

35 yo F with a BMI of 42, with a history of multiple failed attempts at weight loss. She presents to the bariatric clinic for evaluation for surgical intervention. She has a history of hypertension, sleep apnea, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), which she manages with proton pump inhibitors. She is a non-smoker and denies any significant medical or surgical history. After a thorough evaluation, the patient is deemed an appropriate candidate for a one-anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) as a primary bariatric procedure. She is informed of the potential postoperative pain and the possibility of being enrolled in a clinical trial. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is randomized into the TAP group. She undergoes the TAP blockade procedure and receives intravenous acetaminophen analgesia (1g/6h) postoperatively. Postoperative pain is evaluated 24 hours after surgery using a Visual Analogic Scale (VAS), ranging from 0 to 100mm.

The patient is a 50-year-old Korean man diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer with metastasis to the bone. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain in his right shoulder and hip that has been impacting his daily activities for the past month. The patient has been prescribed various analgesics, including oral opioids, but the pain has not been adequately controlled. The patient's oncologist has decided to start the patient on OROS hydromorphone to manage his pain. The patient has no history of serious gastrointestinal diseases and is able to swallow pills without difficulty. The patient will be monitored for pain control and any adverse events that may occur as a result of taking the medication.

Jennifer is a 42-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a malignant brain tumor three months ago. She underwent radiation therapy, which helped to reduce the size of the tumor, but it is still present and growing. Jennifer is experiencing headaches, seizures, and difficulty with speech and memory. She has a Karnofsky Performance score of 80, indicating that she is able to carry out normal activities with some difficulty. Jennifer is willing to practice effective birth control during the study period. She has no history of allergic reactions to iodine or gadolinium-DTPA. She is not obese and does not have any metal in her body that would interfere with the MRI. Jennifer has not undergone any chemotherapy yet. Her lab studies are within normal range, including platelet count, PTT, PT, creatinine, total bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, and alkaline phosphatase. The presence of the target antigen, EGFRvIII, has been identified on her tumor tissue by immunohistochemistry. She has no signs of impending, life-threatening cerebral herniation syndrome. Jennifer does not have any subependymal or CSF disease. She meets all the eligibility criteria to participate in the study.

A 9-year-old boy came to the clinic with his mother. He is currently overweight with a BMI at the 90th percentile. His mother has concerns about his sedentary lifestyle and would like to enroll him in a weight management program. The boy is interested in playing video games and his mother has a TV and internet connection at home. The family speaks English and is willing to participate in the study. The boy is able to participate in physical activity similar to exercise gaming. He has no significant medical history, developmental delay or other comorbid conditions. The family is willing to attend 16 weekly core sessions followed by 8 monthly mastery group sessions. The boy will wear the activity monitor for 1 week during waking hours and return it at the next session. They are willing to participate in the study and have signed the consent/assent form.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has struggled with her weight for the past 5 years. She has a BMI of 30 and a waist circumference of 95 cm. She is currently taking medication for hypothyroidism and has a family history of type 2 diabetes. She works a desk job and does not engage in regular physical activity due to lack of time. She has tried various diets and weight loss programs in the past but has been unsuccessful in maintaining the weight loss. She is highly motivated to make changes in her dietary habits and is willing to commit to a 12-month intervention program. She does not have any significant cardiovascular, renal, or endocrine disease, and is not currently pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 35-year-old Latina woman living in Southern California who has not undergone cervical cancer screening. She has heard about the Pap test from friends and family but feels uncomfortable discussing her reproductive health with her healthcare provider due to cultural and societal stigmas surrounding cervical cancer. She has concerns about the procedure being painful and invasive, and worries about the potential costs and time required for the test. Additionally, she has limited access to healthcare services due to financial barriers and lack of insurance. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about cervical cancer screening and to receive support and guidance in navigating the screening process. She speaks both English and Spanish and is open to participating in a culturally relevant and innovative social marketing intervention to overcome stigma and improve timely and appropriate screening practices for cervical cancer.

The patient is a 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who was recently diagnosed with endometrial cancer. She underwent a biopsy which revealed that her cancer is of the endometrioid type. She has no history of any other cancer within the past five years and has not had a hysterectomy or any previous therapy for endometrial cancer. She is currently being evaluated for surgery but has been informed that she may be eligible for a clinical trial examining the safety of omitting lymph node dissection in ultra-low-risk endometrial cancer. She has undergone a pelvis MRI and CA125 test which satisfied the KGOG criteria. There is currently no evidence of distant metastasis. She is excited to participate in this trial to potentially avoid unnecessary lymph node dissection and improve her quality of life.

A 42 yo F with end-stage liver disease secondary to chronic hepatitis C infection. She has been on the liver transplant waiting list for the past year and now has a potential living donor, her sister. She is interested in exploring the possibility of adult-to-adult living donor liver transplant (LDLT). The study aims to study the effects of pressure and flow on the outcomes of LDLT, to determine the prevalence, course, and predictors of poor Health Related Quality of Life (HRQOL) outcomes associated with living donor donation and to collect data and biosamples prior to, during, and after a living donor liver transplant (LDLT) among all donors and recipients for use by other adult-to-adult living donor liver transplant studies and future studies. She is eligible for the study as she is 18 years or older, has had a living donor identified and accepted and LDLT is planned, and informed consent has been obtained. She will need to undergo imaging studies to measure the size of the liver and spleen before and after the surgery, provide blood samples to the NIDDK Biosample Repository at various time points, and answer questions about quality of life after the surgery. She is eager to participate in this study to advance the science of liver transplantation and improve outcomes for future recipients and donors.

A 64-year-old woman, who was previously active, has been experiencing knee pain due to osteoarthritis for the past year. She has been diagnosed by her healthcare provider and has been receiving physical therapy for the past 6 months. Despite her best efforts, she has not been able to adhere to her prescribed exercise regimen due to her busy schedule and difficulty understanding the written instructions provided by her physical therapist. She speaks and reads English fluently and has access to a smartphone. She has not received cortisone injection to the joint within the past 30 days and is not undergoing physical therapy post-total joint replacement or in preparation for total joint replacement in the next 3 months. She has no history of serious mental illness or serious/terminal illness. She is highly motivated to continue with her physical therapy and is interested in trying new technology to improve her adherence to the exercise regimen.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a BMI of 28 and is looking for healthier snacking options to help her lose weight. She has a history of hypertension that is well controlled with medication. She also has a family history of type 2 diabetes, but she has not been diagnosed with the condition. She enjoys eating breakfast every morning and is willing to eat the test snacks provided during the study. She does not have any allergies, and is not pregnant or lactating. She has not been engaged in any intensive physical activity training regimens in the last six months but does exercise moderately 3 times a week. She is willing to adhere to the study schedule and procedures.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who has been experiencing decreased libido and erectile dysfunction for the past year. He has also noticed a decrease in muscle mass, strength, and stamina. His medical history is significant for a right orchiectomy due to testicular cancer at the age of 30. He is currently on testosterone replacement therapy with injections, but he is interested in trying the testosterone gel to see if it is more convenient and effective. He has no significant medical conditions, and his psychiatric evaluation is normal. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. His blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, and his laboratory studies show a low testosterone level of 200 ng/dL. He is willing to comply with daily application of the testosterone gel and attend all required follow-up visits.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman in her first trimester. She has a history of obesity and has been struggling to maintain a healthy weight throughout her pregnancy. She is currently taking a prenatal vitamin supplement that contains folic acid. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to observe the effect of folic acid on her child's birth weight, fat content and metabolism related hormone secretion. She is a Chinese citizen and meets all other inclusion criteria for the study.

30-year-old male with a history of dental pain and scheduled for elective surgical extraction of impacted mandibular 3rd molars. The patient is in good health with an ASA status of I or II. The patient is experiencing moderate to severe pain within 4 hours after the completion of surgery. The patient has not taken any other analgesics, sedatives, or narcotic drugs within 24 hours prior to the surgery. The patient is able to use and understand Visual Analog Scale and Verbal Rating Score to assess their pain level. The patient does not have any other acute or chronic painful physical condition and is not taking microsomal enzyme inducers.

A 25-year-old woman with a long history of multiple neurofibromas presents with concerns about her health. She was diagnosed with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) at a young age and has been experiencing symptoms such as frequent headaches and vision problems. She has also had a history of seizures and was found to have a brain tumor at the age of 13, which was successfully removed. She has been under the care of a neurologist and a neuro-oncologist for the past several years and is currently stable. She is interested in participating in the Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Patient Registry Initiative (NPRI) to help researchers gather more information about the disease and potentially help others living with NF1. She is comfortable with filling out a 30-minute online questionnaire to provide her medical and social history. She is eager to contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge about NF1 and hopes that her participation will help others in the future.

The patient is a 60-year-old Japanese man who has been experiencing nocturia for the past six months. He wakes up at least five times every night to urinate and this has been affecting his quality of life, making him feel tired and groggy during the day. He has been to see his doctor who diagnosed him with nocturnal polyuria and prescribed him with some medications, but they did not alleviate his symptoms. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of cardiac or renal disease, and his blood pressure and blood sugar levels are well-controlled. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to try a new treatment option for his condition.

A 43-year-old HIV-positive patient who has been on triple antiretroviral therapy for the past 6 months and has a plasma viral load below the detection threshold is experiencing cognitive impairment. The patient is familiar with using computer tools and has access to a computer with an internet connection. The patient is not diagnosed with any psychiatric pathology that could interfere with the psychometric evaluation, except for mild depression with a Beck score of 14. The patient is not under guardianship and has not experienced any severe clinical events recently. The patient is fluent in French, affiliated with the social security system, and has given written informed consent to participate in the study. The patient has had a cerebral MRI or brain CT that has eliminated any other cause of cognitive disorders.

A 52-year-old male construction worker with a history of ventral hernia presents with pain and discomfort in the abdominal region. He complains of a bulge in the abdomen that increases in size with coughing and physical activity. He has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. On examination, a midline ventral incisional hernia measuring 6 cm in diameter is identified. The hernia is not incarcerated, and there is no evidence of strangulation. CT scan confirms the diagnosis. The patient has no history of narcotic use or connective tissue disorder. He is otherwise healthy and meets all other eligibility criteria for the study. He is informed about the study and has given his consent to participate.

56 year-old male with a previous diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma with metastasis to the lungs and bones. The patient has undergone standard of care treatment, including systemic therapy and radiation, but has experienced disease progression. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 90%, and adequate organ function, including renal and liver function. The patient is not currently on any immunosuppressive therapy, and does not have a history of autoimmune disease or primary immunodeficiency disorder. The patient is willing to use acceptable methods of contraception from enrollment through at least 12 months after CTX130 infusion. The patient has not received prior treatment with anti-CD70 targeting agents, CAR T cells, or any other modified T or natural killer cells. The patient does not have any active HIV, hepatitis B virus, or hepatitis C virus infections. The patient has not undergone prior solid organ or bone marrow transplantation, and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding.

A 45-year-old man with a family history of coronary artery disease is scheduled for cardiac catheterization due to chest pain and shortness of breath. His father had a heart attack at the age of 60 and his older brother had a heart attack at the age of 50. He is a smoker and has high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He has no history of bone marrow transplant, kidney disease, cancer, or recent myocardial infarction. He has agreed to participate in the study and provide a DNA sample.

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of chronic renal insufficiency is admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of sepsis. The patient has a history of diabetes and hypertension. On admission, the patient's hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL. The patient is receiving fluid resuscitation with crystalloids. The patient has a central venous access in the superior vena cava. The patient is not pregnant and has no history of renal transplantation. The patient is willing to give consent for the clinical trial. The patient's renal function is stable at the time of admission. The patient is not experiencing active bleeding. The patient has no documented arrhythmia. The patient's ultrasound RRI evaluation is available. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial.

62-year-old male with a history of metastatic lung cancer that has progressed despite multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Recent imaging studies demonstrated disease progression in the lung, liver, and bones. Biopsy of a liver lesion revealed an activating FGFR1 mutation. The patient is symptomatic with cough, shortness of breath, fatigue, and pain in the right hip. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is otherwise medically fit. He has no history of pancreatitis, alcohol abuse, or bleeding disorders. His blood pressure is well-controlled on medication, and his laboratory tests show adequate organ function. The patient is willing to undergo a biopsy or surgical procedure to obtain tissue for molecular evaluation. He has not received any prior FGFR targeted therapy and is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period. The patient understands the nature of the study and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been suffering from chronic migraines for the past year. She experiences headaches on more than 15 days each month, with at least two of the following characteristics: unilateral location, pulsating quality, moderate-severe pain intensity and/or aggravation by or causing avoidance of routine physical activity. She also experiences nausea and/or vomiting or photophobia and/or phonophobia. She has tried various migraine prophylaxis medications, but they have not been effective in reducing the frequency or severity of her headaches. She is able to understand questionnaires and keep headache logs, and is physically able to undergo treatment administration. She has no allergies to botulinum toxin-A or any of the product components. She has not received previous treatment with botulinum toxin-A for chronic migraine. She is not pregnant or planning to conceive during the trial duration, and is not breastfeeding. She has no contraindications to fMRI procedure, and is not exhibiting severe depression or suicidal ideation. She is willing to taper off her current migraine prophylaxis medication and undergo a 4-week washout period prior to baseline assessments and Botox treatment. She is able to attend all clinic follow-up visits and fMRI scans as required by the trial protocol.

The patient is a 28-year-old pregnant woman who is currently at 28 weeks of gestation. She was diagnosed with intrauterine growth restriction during her routine ultrasound scan. She has a history of hypertension and has been taking medication for it throughout her pregnancy. She does not smoke or consume alcohol. She has no known allergies. She lives with her husband and two children. She is scheduled for a planned cesarean section at 32 weeks of gestation due to her medical condition. The baby's estimated weight is 1200 g. The mother has provided her consent to participate in the study.

This is a 62 year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who has been newly diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis. He is scheduled for aortic valve replacement surgery. He has no significant past medical history and is currently on lisinopril for his hypertension. He denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. He had a recent echocardiogram that confirmed his diagnosis of severe aortic stenosis with an ejection fraction of 60%. He is able to give written informed consent and has no contraindications to transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) or the proposed intervention.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been experiencing daily episodes of lightheadedness, dizziness, and palpitations for the past six months. She has noticed that these symptoms worsen when she stands up or sits up from a lying position. She has tried increasing her fluid and salt intake, but this has not improved her symptoms. The patient has never smoked and does not have any known medical conditions. She is not taking any medications that could affect her blood pressure. She is willing to provide informed consent and is able to comply with the study protocol. The patient undergoes a complete physical exam, including an electrocardiogram (EKG), and is found to meet the criteria for postural tachycardia syndrome (POTS) based on her history and examination. She has an upright plasma norepinephrine level of at least 600 pg/mL. She is not pregnant according to a negative urine beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (b-hCG) test. She does not have any significant cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, or hematological disease based on her medical history and screening results. Her blood pressure is within normal limits, and she does not have any evidence of cardiac structural disease or significant conduction system delay on EKG. The patient is eligible for the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who will undergo an elective surgery for a hernia repair. He has no significant past medical history and does not take any medications regularly. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. He has no known allergies. His physical exam is unremarkable except for the hernia. His vital signs are within normal limits. He is able to provide written informed consent for the study. He has no history of neuromuscular disease, renal or hepatic disease, and is not taking anti-seizure medication or oral anti-cholinesterase. There are no open skin sores in the locations needed for electrode application on his forearms. He is not receiving magnesium sulfate treatment.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and type 2 diabetes. He was diagnosed with Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) two years ago and has been struggling to manage his symptoms through medication and lifestyle changes. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will examine the effects of different diets on MetS. He has not been on insulin treatment and was enrolled in the MICOL study in 2005-2006. He is willing to follow a specific dietary intervention for the duration of the trial and attend follow-up visits at months three and six. He is otherwise in good health and has no history of any other medical conditions.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been smoking a pack of cigarettes a day for the past 10 years. He has tried to quit smoking several times but has been unsuccessful. He has been referred to the smoking cessation unit of the Virgen del Rocio University Hospital in Seville, Spain by his primary care physician. He is motivated to quit smoking and has agreed to participate in the SoLoMo clinical trial of the SmokeFreeBrain project. He owns an Android smartphone and is willing to install the "Libre de Humos" smoking cessation app recommended by the doctor. He is a software engineer and spends most of his working hours sitting in front of a computer. He is married and has two children. He enjoys playing football on weekends and spends time with his family. His BMI is 25 and his blood pressure is normal. He has no known adverse effects on the pharmacological treatment included in the study (Bupropion & Varenicline). He is willing to sign an informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female with a BMI of 23.5 kg/m2. She has no known medical history and is not taking any medication. Her vital signs, ECG, and clinical laboratory results are within normal limits. She has no history of anaphylaxis, hypersensitivity reaction or any clinically significant idiosyncratic reaction to any drug. She has no history of neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, hematological, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, pulmonary and/or musculoskeletal disease, glaucoma, psychiatric disorder or any other chronic disease, whether controlled by medication or not. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

35 year old woman with a BMI of 32, who reports episodes of binge eating over the past 4 weeks. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not currently taking any vasoconstrictor or vasodilator medication. She reports occasional alcohol use but denies alcoholism or drug dependence. The patient has no history of Bulimia Nervosa as defined in DSM 5, and has not used opiate-containing medications in the last 30 days nor plans to use them during the study participation period. She has no medical conditions that are contraindicated with intranasal procedures. She is able to complete written informed consent procedures and agrees to comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old female with a diagnosis of primary open angle glaucoma in both eyes. She has been using Xalatan eye drops once a day for the past year to control her intraocular pressure. Her most recent eye exam showed that her intraocular pressure was still elevated at 22 mmHg in both eyes. She has no history of intraocular surgery or uveitis, and her central corneal thickness is within the normal range. She is not allergic to sulfa or benzalkonium chloride. She has not used any steroids for the past 3 months and does not anticipate needing them during the study. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to compare the efficacy of adding Azopt eye drops three times a day to her current Xalatan regimen versus adding a placebo.

25 year old healthy female with no history of hepatitis B or A infection. The patient is interested in receiving the hepatitis A and B combined vaccine and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the efficiency of protection against hepatitis B virus using different vaccination schedules. She has no known allergies to any vaccine components and is not occupationally exposed to hepatitis B virus. The patient is willing to comply with the contraceptive program during the course of the study. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the trial.

A 36-year-old single mother of two children aged 7 and 10 is seeking help to improve her parenting skills. She is concerned about her children's behavior, as they are frequently disobedient and have difficulty following rules. She works as a cashier in a grocery store and has limited financial resources. She is interested in enrolling in a parenting program that could help her improve her parenting skills and the behavior of her children. She has never participated in the Parent Centre's Positive Parenting Skills Training or the Parenting and Leadership Training. She is willing to participate in the study and has the ability to attend all the sessions.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman with a history of tooth pain on the lower right side of her mouth. She reports experiencing intermittent and severe pain that wakes her up at night. She has tried over-the-counter painkillers with little relief. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. Her dental examination reveals evidence of symptomatic apical periodontitis in her mandibular right second molar. She is eligible for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the pain scales used to measure post-operative pain. She will be randomly assigned to either the experimental group or the control group and will take either clindamycin or a placebo before the start of the root canal treatment. She will be required to complete a 7-day diary to record postoperative pain and swelling.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was admitted to the medical intensive care unit due to complications from pneumonia. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. His physical exam is significant for decreased breath sounds on the right side of his chest and an elevated heart rate of 110 beats per minute. His lab results show a white blood cell count of 18,000/mm3 and elevated inflammatory markers. He is currently receiving oxygen therapy and antibiotics. The patient has never talked with his family about his end-of-life wishes and is uncertain about code status. He is willing to participate in the study and learn more about code status and advance directives.

A 67 year old postmenopausal woman came to the clinic with a complaint of burning sensation in her mouth for the past year. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She has tried various mouthwashes, lozenges and medications to relieve the symptoms but none of them have been effective. Upon examination, there were no visible abnormalities in the oral mucosa. She also reported a loss of taste and hyposalivation. Her medical history is significant for hypothyroidism and osteoporosis for which she takes levothyroxine and calcium supplements. Her blood tests including iron studies and vitamin B12 levels were within normal limits. She fulfilled the inclusion criteria and signed up for the clinical trial. She was randomized to the acupuncture arm of the study and received the treatment as per the protocol. At the follow-up visit, she reported a significant improvement in her symptoms and her VAS score decreased from 8 to 2. She also reported an improvement in her quality of life as measured by SF-36 score.

32-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia. She has been hospitalized in a sterile area of a hematology unit for the past 4 weeks and is experiencing high levels of anxiety due to the isolation and unfamiliar surroundings. She has no known allergies to sweet almond oil and has no physical injuries that would prevent her from receiving touch massage. She is able to sit in an ergonomic chair for the duration of the massage. She has not yet met the nurse who will be providing the touch massage.

An 80-year-old widow who lives alone in her apartment is being discharged from the hospital after a 6-day stay due to pneumonia. She has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol. The patient is ambulatory with the help of a cane and needs assistance with activities of daily living, such as bathing and dressing. She has some difficulty with swallowing and has experienced weight loss in the past few months. She is concerned about her nutritional status and has expressed a desire to improve her diet to ensure proper nutrition. The patient speaks fluent French and has social security coverage. She has read the briefing note and has given her consent to participate in the study.

28-year-old male with a BMI of 23 and a regular exercise routine consisting of weight training and cardio. He has no known metabolic impairments or chronic medical conditions, and does not take any over-the-counter medications. He has no personal or family history of epilepsy, seizures, or schizophrenia. He is interested in exploring non-animal derived dietary proteins for ethical and environmental reasons and has no known allergies to mycoprotein or edible fungi. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare the muscle anabolic response between mycoprotein as a whole food and protein isolated from mycoprotein.

72 yo female with a history of bilateral cataracts and no other significant ocular pathology presents for evaluation. The patient reports difficulty with driving at night and reading small print. The patient has no history of corneal surgery, glaucoma, or diabetes. The patient is willing to undergo additional ophthalmic tests and has been assessed to be able to dilate to a minimum of 6 mm pre-operatively. The patient's pupil size is ≥ 4.5 mm in mesopic conditions. The patient has no planned adjunctive surgery and has not previously participated in a clinical investigation within 30 days prior to enrollment.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who underwent an emergency laparotomy due to perforated appendicitis. During the surgery, his wound was classified as dirty due to the contamination from the ruptured appendix. He was managed with an open abdomen for two days and then underwent delayed primary closure using traditional wound management techniques. He experienced wound complications including surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, and prolonged healing time. He is currently seeking alternative surgical wound management methods and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that utilizes negative pressure wound therapy for delayed primary closure. He is otherwise healthy and meets all inclusion criteria for the trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who suffered a T12-L1 spinal cord injury in a car accident a year ago. He has an incomplete spinal cord injury and has been undergoing physiotherapy and rehabilitation since the injury. He has good sitting balance and can sit for more than four hours a day. He is able to bench 20° forward in trunk flexion. He has no progressive pathologies or problem in vestibular system, and his vision is intact. He has some hand function but is diagnosed with tetraplegia. He is not experiencing any acute pain or contraindications on ethical grounds. He is motivated to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form after being properly informed about the study.

A 35-year-old man has been suffering from moderate to severe chronic plaque-type psoriasis for the past 5 years. He has participated in a previous phase III study for secukinumab and has shown at least partial response (PASI 50 or better) at Week 52. He is interested in continuing on this medication and is willing to participate in this extension study. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. He is not currently taking any prohibited psoriasis or non-psoriasis treatments. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the protocol, including the use of effective contraception if he is of child-bearing potential. He provides written informed consent to participate in the study.

35-year-old male who sustained an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury while playing soccer. He is a physically active person who enjoys playing sports regularly. He has been experiencing pain, swelling, and instability in his knee since the injury. MRI confirms the diagnosis of a complete tear of the ACL. He has no history of malignancy or rheumatoid arthritis. The patient reports no other knee ligament instability. His BMI is 27, which is within normal range. He has never been diagnosed with Morbus Bechterew. The patient is interested in participating in the study to determine which graft option (hamstring or quadriceps tendon) will provide him the best outcome.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 2 years ago. She has been experiencing mild to moderate symptoms, including abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. She has been on mesalamine for the past 6 months, but her symptoms have not improved. Her Mayo Score is 7, and her endoscopic subscore is 2. She is not using any other medications or supplements, and she has no history of major comorbidities, including renal, hepatic, cardiac, pulmonary, or malignancy. She has not received any anti-TNF agents within the last 3 months, or used oral or rectal corticosteroids within the last 4 weeks. She has not had any surgical bowel resections, and she is not currently experiencing any local or systemic complications or other pathological states requiring therapy with corticosteroids and/or immunosuppressive agents. She is willing to use effective methods of contraception during the study period. She is interested in participating in the study to explore alternative treatment options for her ulcerative colitis.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman diagnosed with Macular Telangiectasia (MacTel) in both eyes. She has previously participated in the NTMT-01 and NTMT-02 protocols and has received the NT-501 implant. She is generally in good health and does not have any significant medical conditions besides MacTel. She has not experienced any adverse events related to the NT-501 implant and is interested in participating in the extension study to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of the implant. She has no history of smoking or drug use and is not currently taking any medications. She is able to review and understand the informed consent form and agrees to participate in the study. She is willing and able to attend all study visits and comply with study requirements. She is excited to be a part of the study and contribute to the development of new treatments for MacTel.

The patient is a 57-year-old female who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 7 years ago. She is currently taking metformin 1000mg twice daily and following a diet plan recommended by her dietician. Her most recent hemoglobin A1C level was 8.2%. She has a family history of diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of mulberry leaf extract on blood glucose control. She does not have a history of hepatic or renal disease, is not pregnant, and is not currently taking insulin. She is able to maintain a diary of her food intake, exercise, and glucose levels. She is eager to try natural remedies to improve her diabetes control and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 26-year-old woman diagnosed with spastic cerebral palsy at the age of 2. She has bilateral spasticity affecting her ankle and knee joints, with a Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) score of 3 in both joints. The patient is able to ambulate without walking aids for at least 10 meters but experiences a pathological knee extension pattern during gait. She has not received botulinum toxin type A (Btx-A) treatment in the past 6 months and has not undergone orthopedic surgery on her lower extremities in the past 18 months. She reports no cognitive impairment and is not pregnant or planning pregnancy. The patient has not received any new treatments affecting the musculoskeletal system in the past four weeks, such as pain killers, physical therapy, or acupuncture. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to investigate the effects of Btx-A in adults with cerebral palsy and hopes to improve her range of motion, gait function, and overall quality of life.

A 7-year-old boy with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS), as indicated by parent-reported habitual snoring and an obstructive apnea index of 1-20/hr of total sleep time or obstructive apnea hypopnea index of 2-30/hr of total sleep time. The patient has not had adenotonsillectomy and has not used nasal corticosteroids for more than 2 weeks in the past year. The patient has no history of severe OSAS or significant hypoxemia or hypercapnia on polysomnography. The patient does not have a history of recurrent throat infections or other major illnesses such as craniofacial anomalies or neuromuscular disease. The patient's parents are willing to provide informed consent for participation in the clinical trial.

A 52-year-old woman presents with severe headaches, nausea, vomiting, and difficulty with walking. Imaging studies reveal a large mass in her brain, and a biopsy confirms the diagnosis of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). She underwent maximal debulking surgery and received radiation therapy in combination with temozolomide. The patient has a Karnofsky score of 80 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trial and is not pregnant. Her platelet count, neutrophil count, and liver and renal function are all within the normal range. She has not had any hypersensitivity reactions to temozolomide or DTIC. The patient is willing to participate in the study and to use effective contraception during the trial. She understands and has signed the informed consent. The treatment start date is at least 4 weeks out from surgery and at least 4 weeks out but not more than 7 weeks from the later of the last dose of concomitant temozolomide or radiotherapy. The patient is eligible for the trial and will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: treatment with the NovoTTF-100A device in combination with temozolomide chemotherapy or treatment with temozolomide alone as the best known standard of care. She will be monitored closely and will return to the clinic once every month for routine examinations and MRI of the head.

A 55-year-old Caucasian man with a history of low-grade non-Hodgkin's lymphoma was previously treated with chemotherapy and radiation therapy. He experienced a partial response to the treatment but started experiencing symptoms of fatigue, night sweats, and generalized weakness. The patient has no significant past medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is married and has two children. On physical examination, the patient has cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. His Zubrod and Karnofsky performance status are both 1. His platelet count is 90,000/mm^3, absolute neutrophil count is 2,000/mm^3, and hemoglobin is 12 g/dL. His liver function tests and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He has no history of autoimmune disease or significant gastrointestinal bleeding. He has not received any biologic therapy or endocrine therapy for lymphoma for the past 3 weeks. He has not undergone any surgery for the past 2 weeks. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who is scheduled for a cardiac catheterization procedure next week. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. He has been taking medications for these conditions for the past 5 years. He reports occasional chest pain that is relieved with rest and nitroglycerin. He has no history of heart attack or stroke. He works as a retired accountant and spends most of his time at home. He lives with his wife and has two adult children who live nearby. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has a BMI of 27 and his blood pressure is well-controlled with medications. He has no known allergies and his physical exam is unremarkable.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who was recently diagnosed with Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. He lives with his parents and younger sibling in a urban area. He experienced mild symptoms such as fever, cough, and fatigue, but did not require hospitalization. He is now in the recovery phase and his symptoms have resolved. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. His parents have consented to his participation in this study to assess short and long-term clinical outcomes and immune responses after SARS-CoV-2 infection in children.

A 55-year-old male with a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 35%) on optimized drug therapy. His current medications include furosemide, carvedilol, and lisinopril. He is able to perform activities of daily living but experiences shortness of breath with exertion such as climbing stairs or walking up hills. He reports feeling fatigued and limited in his ability to participate in hobbies he once enjoyed. He has never participated in a formal exercise program and is interested in improving his functional capacity and quality of life. He has no history of atrial fibrillation or implantable device, and no history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or biomechanical limitations to physical activity. He is willing to be randomized to either a 12-week combined aerobic and resistance physical training program supervised by a physical educator or to receive only medical prescription for regular physical exercise. He is able and willing to attend regular study visits and adhere to the study protocol.

The patient is a 50-year-old Caucasian woman who was previously diagnosed with melanoma that has metastasized to other parts of her body. She has undergone immunotherapy in the past but has not responded well to it. She is now BRAF wild-type and is eligible for molecularly targeted therapy. Her performance status is good with an ECOG score of 1, and she has a life expectancy of at least 3 months according to her treating oncologist. Her hemoglobin, leukocytes, ANC, and platelet count are within normal limits. Her liver and kidney functions are also normal. She has measurable disease with at least one lesion that can be accurately measured. She is willing to undergo up to two surgical resections/biopsies to collect tumor for research purposes. She has not received radiation therapy or MEK inhibitors in the past. She is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use two forms of adequate contraception during the study period and for four months following completion of study therapy. She understands the protocol and is willing to comply with it. She agrees to provide archival tissue and a blood sample for research purposes.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was admitted to the ICU due to acute exacerbation of his respiratory symptoms. He has a past medical history of hypertension, which is currently managed with medication. He was a former smoker but quit smoking 5 years ago. He has no history of head or neck trauma, upper leg surgery, or any other respiratory diseases. He has given consent to participate in the study and is currently receiving mechanical ventilation in the ICU.

62-year-old female with a BMI of 24 kg/m2 who has good general health and no disease states or physical conditions that would impair evaluation of biopsy sites. She does not take Lovaza or any other medications that may affect the biomarkers of interest. She does not use frequent NSAIDs or steroids and is not allergic to soybean, soybean oil, peanuts or seafood. She has not received an experimental drug or used an experimental device in the 30 days prior to admission to the study. She does not have a history of keloids or any other condition that would complicate wound healing. She has not had any allergic reactions to local anesthetics.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who has been recently diagnosed with ADHD. He struggles with attention and concentration in school and at home. He is easily distracted and has difficulty following instructions. He has been experiencing sleep difficulties, such as trouble falling asleep and staying asleep throughout the night. He often wakes up feeling tired and struggles to focus during the day. He has no other known psychiatric disorders and is not currently taking any medication for his ADHD. He is in good physical health and has no known allergies. He is currently in the second grade and has a supportive family who is willing to participate in the study.

34-year-old female with a history of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis for the past 8 months, covering approximately 30% of her body surface area. She has been experiencing significant itching and discomfort due to the psoriasis. Her psoriasis area and severity index (PASI) score is 16 and her static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) score is 4. She has not received any biologic therapies targeting Interleukin (IL)-17A, IL-17A/F, IL-17 receptor A, IL-12/IL-23p40 or IL-23p19. She has not been exposed to retinoid-related orphan receptor (ROR)-γ inhibitors. She has no history of erythrodermic psoriasis, pustular psoriasis, guttate psoriasis, medication-induced psoriasis or other skin conditions such as eczema or severe acne.

A 27-year-old male professional soccer player with a history of previous hamstring injuries. He plays as a forward and has been playing soccer since childhood. During a recent soccer match, he experienced a sudden sharp pain in the back of his thigh while sprinting to receive a pass. He was immediately taken out of the game and evaluated by the team physician. Physical examination revealed tenderness and swelling in the back of his thigh, suggesting a hamstring strain. He was advised to rest, ice, compress, and elevate his leg and was referred to the clinical trial for further evaluation and treatment. MRI and sonographic assessments were performed to determine the extent of the injury. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo biomechanical testing to determine when he can fully return to playing soccer.

The patient is a 68-year-old woman who has undergone surgery for breast cancer. Her multidisciplinary team has recommended adjuvant radiotherapy to improve her chances of survival. The patient is hesitant about radiotherapy, especially if it requires many treatment sessions. She is interested in a treatment schedule that is shorter yet effective. The patient has no history of previous radiation treatment, no distant metastases, and no planned reconstructive breast surgery. She has a life expectancy of more than 2 years according to her medical team, and has no condition that would make toxicity evaluation difficult. The patient is mentally capable of understanding the nature and scope of the study, and is likely to comply with the protocol. The patient will be eligible for the clinical trial and can be randomized to either the 5-fraction or 15-fraction treatment arm, or can choose to enter the parallel observational arm if she has a strong preference for one of the schedules.

This clinical trial is looking for healthy adult human subjects between the ages of 18 and 45 with a normal BMI. The study involves testing the pharmacokinetic profile of metformin liquid after a dose administration of 10 mL (1000 mg) under fasting conditions, after a low-fat meal, and after a high-fat meal. The study requires the completion of three periods with a washout period of seven days between each period. Subjects will need to undergo a medical history and physical examination to ensure they are of normal health and free from organ dysfunction or any clinically significant deviation from the normal. Female subjects must not be pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential without practicing an acceptable method of birth control. Subjects with a history of allergy to metformin, drug dependence, excessive alcohol intake, or enzyme-modifying drugs within the last 30 days are ineligible for the study.

A 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus 5 years ago came to the clinic complaining of chronic fatigue and depression. She has been experiencing fatigue for the past 3 years, which has affected her daily activities, including her work and social life. She has also been experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities she once enjoyed. She has been taking hydroxychloroquine and prednisone for her systemic lupus erythematosus, and her disease has been stable for the past 3 months. She has no history of seizures, brain tumors, or brain injuries. She is not pregnant and does not have any other comorbidities. She has never had a cardiac pacemaker, implanted neurostimulator, or cochlear implant.

Patient A is a 25-year-old female with a BMI of 22 kg/m2. She is generally healthy and usually eats breakfast. She does not have a history of diabetes or any other major health conditions. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the trial. She is not taking any medication or supplements that may influence carbohydrate metabolism. She does not have any history of disordered eating, alcohol or substance abuse. She is not following any restrictive diets. She has no intolerance or allergic reaction to oats. She has not had any significant physical trauma or major surgery in the past 3 months. She is willing and able to comply with all trial requirements and is excited to participate in the study to help determine the effects of oat polyphenols on post-prandial glucose response.

The patient is a postmenopausal woman aged 55 years with a history of amenorrhea for the past 2 years. She has been experiencing symptoms of vaginal dryness, itching, and painful intercourse for the past 6 months. She has not used any hormonal therapy for the past 2 months. Her medical history is non-significant. She has had a normal Pap smear within the past year. She is willing to abstain from sexual intercourse and use of over-the-counter vaginal products for 7 days before the collection of vaginal samples. The patient provides written informed consent for the study. She has no active sexually transmitted diseases or untreated cervical, vaginal, or vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia. She is not a pessary-user and has no undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. She has not been diagnosed with breast cancer, endometrial cancer or endometrial hyperplasia, hypertriglyceridemia, or venous thromboembolism. She is not immunocompromised and has not received chronic glucocorticoid use or active treatment with immunosuppressive agents.

A 50 year old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to the emergency department with chest pain and shortness of breath. An ECG revealed ST-elevation in the anterior leads and the patient was diagnosed with an acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction. The patient was taken to the catheterization lab and underwent successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) with stent placement in the proximal left anterior descending artery. The patient remained stable after the procedure and was discharged two days later. The patient has agreed to participate in the Resistance STEMI Study to evaluate changes in microvascular resistance of the infarcted area and correlate it to long-term outcome. The patient meets the inclusion criteria, is able to give informed consent, and has no contraindications for MRI.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who has no significant medical history. He has no allergies or any contraindications to MRI scanning. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial as a normal volunteer. He has not undergone any MRI scans in the past and is willing to undergo intravenous administration of commercially available MR contrast media and exercise as part of the study. He understands the study involves ground work for specific patient protocols and is willing to provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 23-year-old man who has been diagnosed with ADHD since childhood. He experiences symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and restlessness, which have caused several restrictions in his daily life. He has no history of drug abuse or dependence and is currently not taking any medication for ADHD or any other psychiatric disorder. He speaks fluent German and is able to read and understand study information. He has no significant medical history or physical disorders that would interfere with the study. He is not at risk of suicide and has no known intolerance to the study medication. He has no relationship of dependency with the sponsor or the investigator. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understand the importance of keeping to the study protocol.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer six months ago. She has previously undergone chemotherapy with a platinum-based therapy but the disease has progressed and is now resistant to the treatment. She experiences abdominal pain and bloating, and has lost weight in the past few months. She has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and is otherwise healthy. The patient has no history of allergies or significant CNS or psychiatric disorders. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

Unfortunately, as this trial is not focused on recruiting individual patients, it is not appropriate to generate a patient description. This study is focused on implementing a quality improvement initiative across a community of clinicians and medical centers in order to improve outcomes for patients with heart failure or heart attack.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who is scheduled for inguinal hernia surgery under general anesthesia. He has no significant past medical history and takes no regular medications. He speaks, reads and writes the Turkish language fluently. He has no hearing or vision problems. He has no active opioid use, nor does he regularly use anxiolytics. He is willing to participate in the study and has no objection to listening to music.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who is scheduled for abdominal surgery in the next month. She has a history of motion sickness and frequently experiences postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) after surgery. She quit smoking six months ago and does not use any other tobacco products. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not taking any medications that would interfere with the study. She is interested in exploring options to reduce the likelihood of experiencing PONV after her upcoming surgery.

A 42-year-old male with a history of sinonasal polyposis and chronic rhinosinusitis for the past 5 years, presenting with nasal obstruction and discharge, olfactory dysfunction, and recurrent sinus infections. Despite prior medical management, he has experienced no significant improvement in his symptoms. He has undergone previous endoscopic sinus surgery with bilateral total ethmoidectomy. He is currently not taking oral corticosteroids and is not on any other medications. He has no history of autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiencies, or malignancies. He is a non-smoker and is not currently pregnant or nursing. He has no known allergies to medications or substances. He is a member of a social security program and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

As this is a study on a program to reduce unprotected sex rates in high-risk youth in New York, there is no specific patient description needed for this clinical trial. Participants will be selected based on their age and school attendance, while those with certain exclusion criteria will not be eligible to participate.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer during a routine mammogram. She has no family history of breast cancer and is otherwise in good health. The biopsy results indicated that she has ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and will require a modified radical mastectomy. She is concerned about the potential complications of the surgery, particularly the formation of seromas, which she has heard can be painful and cause delays in her recovery. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the use of electric and harmonic scalpels in mastectomy, as she hopes that the results of the trial will help her make an informed decision about her surgical options.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic vulvar pain for the past 2 years. She has been diagnosed with vulvodynia and has tried various Western medicine treatments with no relief. The pain is described as burning, stinging, and rawness in the vulva area, and it is exacerbated during sexual intercourse. She has a history of anxiety and depression and is currently taking sertraline for those conditions. She has no history of other chronic pain conditions or illnesses affecting the genital area. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore non-traditional treatment options and improve her quality of life. She speaks and reads English fluently.

A 32-year-old male living in the Gem Village of Nyanza province in Western Kenya has not received HIV care in the last 6 months. He presents with complaints of fever, cough and malaise for the past 3 weeks. He has had unprotected sex with multiple partners in the past, and he is worried he may have contracted HIV. He works as a farmer and earns a modest income to support his family. He has never been tested for HIV before and is hesitant to go to a clinic due to stigma and fear of discrimination. He lives with his wife and two children and has noticed that his wife has been sick with similar symptoms. He is interested in knowing his HIV status and seeking treatment if found positive. He has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. He denies any alcohol or drug use.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who has been experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness, snoring, and choking episodes during sleep for the past year. He has not received a diagnosis of sleep apnea but has been referred to a sleep specialist by his primary care physician due to his symptoms.
