He is overweight with a BMI of 29 kg/m², and his recent blood test showed moderate hypertriglyceridemia with a fasting triglyceride level of 3.5 mmol/L. He has a history of hypertension, which is controlled with medication. He does not have any known endocrine disease, liver or kidney issues, or muscular disease. He has not undergone any previous sleep studies or received any treatment for sleep apnea. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the potential benefits of fenofibrate on his sleep apnea symptoms.

Mary is a 55-year-old woman who was admitted to the hospital with chest pain that radiated to her left arm. She was diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement. She is now clinically stable and receiving standard of care for ACS including aspirin, clopidogrel, and a statin. She has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. Her blood pressure is well controlled with medication. Mary does not have a history of bleeding disorders or any other significant medical conditions. Her hemoglobin level is within normal limits. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to further improve her outcome after ACS.

The patient is a 32-year-old Indian woman who has been experiencing migraines for over a year. She suffers from migraines at least three times a month and requires prophylaxis medication. She has been diagnosed with migraine with aura as per the international headache society criteria. She has tried different acute treatment medications but has not found relief. She is interested in participating in this study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of topiramate in preventing migraines. She has no history of other medical conditions and is not currently taking any other medications. She is willing to be monitored monthly for three months and understands that the study is open-label.

2-day-old male infant diagnosed with respiratory distress syndrome requiring supplemental oxygen and mechanical ventilation. Past medical history is unremarkable. Physical exam reveals tachypnea, intercostal retractions, and nasal flaring. Chest X-ray shows diffuse bilateral opacities consistent with RDS. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and does not have any exclusion criteria such as pneumothorax, surgical disease, or major congenital defects.

A 45-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU for severe pneumonia and respiratory failure. He had a previous history of hypertension and diabetes. He was intubated for 7 days and received continuous sedation during his ICU stay. He had difficulty communicating with healthcare providers during his ICU stay due to the endotracheal tube. After extubation, he was found to have mild to moderate weakness in his extremities and was unable to perform daily activities without assistance. His ICU stay was 12 days, and he was discharged to a step-down unit. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the Exercise With Music for ICU Survivors trial and has no exclusion criteria. He is able to communicate in English and is motivated to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old man visited the clinic for his 5-yearly colonoscopy screening. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. During the colonoscopy, a 6mm polyp was identified in the sigmoid colon. He has never had a polyp detected during prior colonoscopies. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve the removal of the polyp. He is not pregnant, does not have inflammatory bowel disease, and does not have any known polyposis syndromes.

A 17-year-old Caucasian male who recently completed his orthodontic treatment is interested in participating in this clinical trial. He has been wearing his removable retainer as directed by his orthodontist. He has good oral hygiene practices and brushes twice a day and flosses once a day. He has never had periodontal disease or inflammation. He does not have any systemic diseases and is in good health. He does not smoke or use any tobacco products. He has all his permanent teeth, except for his wisdom teeth, which have not erupted yet. He is interested in participating in this study to help improve orthodontic treatment outcomes for future patients.

32 y/o male diagnosed with schizophrenia at age 23. Despite receiving different antipsychotic medications at a dose equivalent to at least 600mg/day of chlorpromazine for at least 2 six-week trials, his symptoms remain unresponsive. His BPRS score is currently above 60 and the Clinical Global Impressions rating is greater than 4. He experiences frequent hallucinations and delusions, with marked conceptual disorganization and suspiciousness. He has a history of substance abuse, but has been sober for the past 6 months. He has no major medical problems that would preclude the use of clozapine or chlorpromazine. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and there is no indication of a serious suicide or homicide risk. The patient (or the patient's authorized legal representative) has been informed about the study and has signed the informed consent.

A 63-year-old woman is admitted to the medical ward for management of her newly diagnosed diabetes. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis. She has a urinary catheter in place due to difficulty with mobility. Her urine is sent for culture as part of routine management. She denies having any symptoms of a urinary tract infection.

A 7-year-old girl with a diagnosis of cerebral palsy has been experiencing problems with saliva control. She drools excessively and often has to use a bib to avoid getting her clothes wet. She has not been using any medication for this condition. She is not allergic to Kinesio Taping tape. She is able to communicate well and is able to follow instructions. Her parents are willing to have her participate in the trial and are committed to the treatment plan. She has no other active medical conditions and her general health is good.

A 50-year-old female is scheduled to receive her first kidney transplant due to end-stage renal failure. She has a history of hypertension, which has been controlled with medications. Her current medications include lisinopril, amlodipine, and furosemide. Her physical exam is unremarkable except for mild tenderness over the right flank. Her laboratory studies show a serum creatinine of 7.8 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen of 67 mg/dL, and a parathyroid hormone level of 180 pg/mL. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to participate. She has no history of bone disease unrelated to renal failure, has not been treated with bisphosphonates or calcitonin in the past month, and has no current malignancy. She is not pregnant nor lactating, and is willing to use an effective form of contraception during the duration of the study.

A 25-year-old female comes to the clinic with a desire to improve her overall fitness and health. She is currently working as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle due to the nature of her work. She has no history of significant medical problems and takes no medications. Her BMI is 23.5 kg/m2, and her HbA1c value is 5.4%. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and wants to prevent developing it. She has no current weight loss efforts but wants to start an exercise program. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of exercise training on the body's regulation of sugar and body weight. She is physically able to exercise at 50% of her predicted heart rate reserve at baseline.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been experiencing persistent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for the past few months. He has been losing weight unintentionally and has noticed black, tarry stools. Upon evaluation, he was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the stomach. He has not received any chemotherapy before and has no history of neuropathy or brain metastases. His performance status is good, with a WHO score of 1. His blood work shows neutrophils and platelets within normal range, bilirubin within normal limits, and ASAT and ALAT less than three times the upper normal limit. His creatinine clearance is above 60 ml/min. He has no known DPD-deficiency or allergy to taxanes or platinum. He is not pregnant or lactating and is willing to use contraception. The patient has given his consent to participate in this study.

65-year-old female with a known history of osteoarthritis of the right knee with chronic pain for the past 6 months. She has tried various analgesics and medications for chronic pain, but none have provided adequate relief. The patient has also undergone physical therapy and joint injections but has not found any significant improvement in her pain levels. She is able to provide informed consent and has not had any alcohol or drug abuse within the past 6 months. She does not have any implanted brain medical or metallic devices and has not had any history of unexplained fainting spells or neurosurgery. The patient is not pregnant and is not trying to become pregnant in the next 6 months. She has not experienced any momentary loss of consciousness due to head injury and does not have uncontrolled diabetes, uncompensated cardiac issues, heart failure, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The patient is willing to undergo transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) in conjunction with transcranial ultrasound (TUS) to assess the effects of these treatments on her pain perception and functional limitations.

A 55-year-old male with a history of Mantle Cell Lymphoma presents with relapsed disease following chemotherapy with R-CHOP and radiation therapy. The patient has multiple comorbidities including hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. The patient has a history of smoking and has quit for 5 years. A recent CT scan revealed multiple sites of disease, including enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, axilla, and groin. The largest measurable node is 2.5 cm x 1.8 cm. The patient's ECOG performance status is 1. The patient has not received any treatment within the past four weeks and has recovered from any acute toxic effects of prior therapy. Hematology, chemistry, and creatine kinase values are all within normal limits. The patient has signed the consent form and agrees to use adequate contraception during the study. The patient is located within a reasonable driving distance from the participating center and is accessible for treatment and follow-up. The patient does not have a history of CNS involvement by lymphoma or significant neurologic or psychiatric disorder.

The patient is a 58-year-old male diagnosed with metastatic colon cancer that has spread to the liver. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy but has not responded well to standard therapy. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1, indicating that he is able to carry out light work such as office work or walking. His left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is ≥50% by echocardiogram, and he has no history of serious cardiovascular disease. He has normal electrolytes and is not taking any medication known to cause QTc prolongation. He has not used tobacco for 4 weeks prior to day 1 and during the study and has agreed to use adequate contraception. He has not undergone any major surgery within 4 weeks prior to day 1 and has no untreated central nervous system metastases. He does not have chronic or acute GI disorders resulting in diarrhea. The patient is eligible for the study.

The patient is a 30 year-old woman who has a BMI of 24. She has been diagnosed with mild hypertension and her blood pressure is currently well-controlled with medication. She does not have any known gastrointestinal diseases and does not regularly take any medication or supplements. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She occasionally drinks Coca-Cola and Diet Coke, but does not consume them on a daily basis. She is willing to discontinue use of any supplements or medications that may interfere with the study. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the nutritional value of these products.

Patient is a 25-year-old male from the city of Baney or community of Rebola, Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea. He has been residing in the area for at least two years and is in good health based on history and clinical examination. He has not been diagnosed with malaria by blood smear at screening and is not suffering from any chronic illnesses, including HIV/AIDS. He is willing and able to come for complete one year follow-up and has demonstrated his understanding of the study and study procedures by correctly answering 10 out of 10 questions. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to inform the study doctor and release medical information concerning contra-indications for participation in the study. He is living with a third party who will contact the study team if there is any alteration of consciousness during the first six months of the study. He is willing to be attended by a study clinician and take all necessary medications prescribed during the study period. He is available through mobile phone 24 hours during the whole study period and agrees not to participate in another study or donate blood during the study period. He is willing to attend all study visits and undergo HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests. He has not planned to travel outside the Bioko, Equatorial Guinea in the first nine months of the study and does not have a history of arrhythmias or prolonged QT-interval or other cardiac disease. He has not received an investigational malaria vaccine or participated in a malaria drug study in the past.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who has been feeling low and hopeless for the past few months. She has been experiencing difficulty sleeping, a lack of energy, and a decreased interest in activities she previously enjoyed. She has also been feeling irritable and has been having trouble concentrating at work. She was referred to the Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) service by her primary care physician and has been diagnosed with depression using DSM-IV criteria. She scored 15 on the PHQ-9 indicating caseness for depression. She has no significant risk issues, co-morbid anxiety disorder, or previous in-patient admission. She has not had significant contact with mental health services in the past and has no visual impairment or language barriers. She has not had any history of overdoses or self-injury and is not currently abusing substances. The patient has consented to participate in the study and will be randomly allocated to one of two arms: 'reformulation letter CAT' or 'no reformulation letter CAT'. The patient will receive eight sessions of CAT with follow-up assessment at eight weeks post-therapy. The therapist conducting the therapy will be one of three trainee clinical psychologists in their final year of training. The therapy sessions will be audiotaped for supervision purposes and reviewed by the CAT qualified supervisor.

A 68-year-old retired teacher has been experiencing subjective memory complaints, such as misplacing objects, forgetting appointments, and difficulty recalling names of familiar people. She is concerned that these symptoms may be an early sign of Alzheimer's disease, as her mother was diagnosed with this disease in her 70s. The patient reports no history of psychiatric disorders or sensory deficits. She takes medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She has completed the Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) and scored 27 out of 30, indicating no significant cognitive impairment. She is interested in participating in a study that examines the effectiveness of visual perceptual training in improving cognitive abilities in older adults with subjective memory complaints. She understands that the study involves three neuropsychological assessments over a three-month period and may involve computerized perceptual-cognitive training twice a week for seven weeks.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C infection three years ago. He underwent treatment with combination directly acting antiviral agents (DAAs) in the past, but failed to achieve sustained virologic response (SVR). He experienced post-treatment relapse and discontinued therapy prematurely due to side effects. He has a history of alcohol abuse but has been sober for the past six months. His current medications include omeprazole for acid reflux and ibuprofen for occasional headaches. He has no history of organ transplantation, HIV or hepatitis B infection. He is willing and able to complete the informed consent process and follow-up visits. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study.

32 yo F involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a traumatic brain injury. Upon arrival to the emergency department, she is found to have an altered mental status and a motor response of 3. CT scan revealed a subdural hematoma with midline shift. She is intubated and transferred to the ICU for further management. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the ProTECT III study and consented to participate. She is able to initiate the study drug infusion within 4 hours from the time of injury. Blood samples will be drawn just prior to the initiation of the study drug infusion and at 24 and 48 hours from the time she was enrolled in the study to test for biomarkers that may help predict how severe the injury is and how well she improves. The investigators will also test to see if the study medication is being absorbed and is staying at a consistent level in the blood stream.

Pt is a 45yo M with a 6-month history of generalized edema, fatigue and weight gain. He has a past medical history significant for hypertension and high cholesterol, but otherwise healthy. He presented to the clinic with significant swelling of his legs and face. Physical exam was remarkable for diffuse 3+ pitting edema and a BMI of 31. Laboratory studies showed a urine protein to creatinine ratio of 4,300mg/g, serum albumin level of 26 g/L and elevated cholesterol level. The patient was diagnosed with Nephrotic Syndrome and started on diuretic therapy. He is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating thyroid function in patients with Nephrotic Syndrome. The patient has no known history of thyroid disease or current/past thyroid medication use. He does not have diabetes mellitus or autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus or RA. He is not currently taking any medications known to affect thyroid function. The patient does not have liver cirrhosis or chronic liver disease.

Patient A is a 68-year-old female who has been recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has a sedentary lifestyle and is a non-smoker. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2 and her resting blood pressure is 135/80 mmHg. She has impaired glucose tolerance with a fasting glucose level of 110 mg/dL and a 2-hour OGTT of 160 mg/dL. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, hepatic, renal, muscular/neuromuscular, or active hematologic/oncologic disease. Her total cholesterol is 230 mg/dL, triglycerides are 150 mg/dL, ALT is 40 U/L, AST is 50 U/L, and Alk Phos is 180 U/L. She has no contraindications to moderate exercise and is willing to comply with the protocol as written. She has not engaged in a regular exercise program and has a VO2 max pre-training value of 50 ml/kg-fat free mass-min, indicating low fitness. She does not have stress test symptoms and has not experienced any signs or symptoms of cardiovascular decomposition. She is not on any medications that would interfere with the study.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who was diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) six months ago. He is the first child of a married couple who live in a suburban area. He attends a special education school full time and receives speech and psychomotor therapy twice a week. He has no comorbidities, and there is no family history of psychiatric or medical disorders. He was diagnosed with ASD based on the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) at the time of diagnosis. His baseline score on the French version of the Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) was 36. His parents have agreed to participate in the study and have at least one Smartphone©. They have signed the consent form for participation.

A 62-year-old male with a history of mesothelioma, who has undergone a platinum-based chemotherapy treatment with pemetrexed and cisplatin, presents with recurrent symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, coughing, and fatigue. A CT scan reveals disease progression, which makes him eligible for this clinical trial. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his overall health is good. He is willing to provide tissue and blood samples for research and is expected to survive for at least 12 weeks. He does not have any other active malignancy requiring concurrent intervention. He has not received prior therapy with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, anti- CD137, or anti-CTLA-4 antibody or participated in any other Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) clinical trial for nivolumab or ipilimumab. He has not tested positive for HIV or hepatitis B or C virus infection. He does not have any autoimmune disease or other serious or uncontrolled medical disorder or active infection that could increase the risk associated with the study. He is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, laboratory tests, and other requirements of the study.

The patient is a 50-year-old female who underwent a lobectomy for lung cancer three months ago. She developed a persistent cough with purulent sputum and fever despite receiving adequate antibiotic therapy. Imaging revealed the presence of a bronchial fistula. She is currently in a compromised condition and cannot undergo surgical intervention. She has no significant medical history, and her family history is non-contributory. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment.

The patient is a 36-year-old female with a clinical diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) with symptom onset at least 6 months prior to the screening visit. She has a history of active plaque psoriasis and has demonstrated an inadequate response or intolerance to or contraindication for conventional synthetic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARD) therapy(ies). The patient has at least one erosion on radiograph as determined by central imaging review or high sensitivity C-Reactive Protein (hsCRP) ≥ 3.0 mg/L. She has never received treatment with a biologic agent and does not have a known hypersensitivity to risankizumab. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the safety and efficacy of risankizumab versus placebo for the treatment of moderately to severely active psoriatic arthritis (PsA).

A 38-year-old male was diagnosed with chronic Hepatitis B infection 4 months ago during a routine check-up. His HBsAg test has been positive for 6 months, and he has not been treated with any antiviral therapy before. His medical history is unremarkable, and he does not have any other liver disease or other medical conditions. He has been experiencing mild fatigue and occasional abdominal discomfort for the last few months. His laboratory tests indicate an HBV DNA level of 2.3 x 10^6 copies/mL, and his ALT value is 2 times higher than the upper limit of normal. The patient has read about the clinical trial and expressed his interest in participating. He is a non-smoker, and he does not have any significant allergies or history of severe adverse drug reactions. He has provided written consent and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who underwent Post-Percutaneous Coronary Artery Intervention (PPCI) three months ago and is currently in a stable condition. He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia for which he takes medication regularly. He does not have a history of substance or alcohol abuse. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. His liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses medically acceptable birth control. The patient is willing to adhere to the protocol requirements and has signed an informed consent form.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has been experiencing decreased sexual desire and energy levels for a few months. He has also noticed a decrease in muscle mass and an increase in body fat. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. The patient has undergone blood tests, which revealed low levels of testosterone, indicating hypogonadism. He has been prescribed TESTIM® for testosterone replacement therapy and has provided written informed consent to participate in the non-interventional study. The patient is generally healthy with no current contraindications for TESTIM® therapy according to the Summary of Product Characteristics. The study will document his testosterone levels throughout the course of therapy and assess changes in his quality of life, including motivation, activity, and fatigue.

A 40-year-old African American man was diagnosed with HIV 6 years ago. He has been on a stable antiretroviral therapy for the past 3 years, consisting of a protease inhibitor and two NRTIs. His latest two consecutive Roche Ultrasensitive Amplicor tests showed a plasma HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/ml, and his CD4 count is 250 cells/ml. His fasting LDL-cholesterol is 4.0 mmol/l. He has no known history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, peripheral artery disease, or cerebrovascular disease. He has no contraindications for the study medication and has not been on a lipid-lowering drug for the past 4 weeks. He is not currently on non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, testosterone or anabolic steroids, or any immunomodulators. He is not using drugs or alcohol and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse.

This clinical trial does not require a patient description as it is a tissue collection study with no specific inclusion or exclusion criteria for individuals. The study will recruit all non-melanoma skin and bladder cancer patients who are recommended for surgical removal of tumor tissues regardless of their age, gender or ethnicity background, as long as the tumor size will not affect their pathological diagnosis or treatment procedures.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her second child. Her first pregnancy was complicated by pre-eclampsia and postpartum hemorrhage. She had a vaginal delivery with a blood loss of 1500 mL. Her BMI is 32 kg/m2, and she is a smoker, smoking 10 cigarettes per day. Her medical history is significant for superficial vein thrombosis during her first pregnancy. She has no known allergies to medications and is not currently taking any medication. Her platelet count, hemoglobin, and blood pressure are within normal limits. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

35 year old woman with a history of strabismus and amblyopia. She has had intermittent double vision and decreased depth perception since childhood, which has been managed with prism glasses. She has undergone multiple unsuccessful strabismus surgeries in the past. Her visual acuity with correction is 20/25 in the right eye and 20/30 in the left eye. Stereopsis testing reveals a moderate degree of stereoacuity impairment. She has no other significant ocular or medical history.

A 57-year-old female with a history of hypertension and diabetes presents with chronic renal impairment. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 45 mL/min/1.73 m^2. She weighs 70 kg with a BMI of 24 kg/m^2. She is not on any medications for her renal function. She has no history of drug allergies, but she is a smoker and has been smoking five cigarettes per day for the past year. She has no history of major organ diseases, such as liver, digestive tract, blood, or metabolic diseases. Her blood routine, blood biochemistry, urine routine, albumin/creatinine ratio, creatine kinase (CK), and coagulation function are stable and consistent with the severity of her renal impairment. She has no history of anesthesia accidents and has no contraindications for deep sedation/general anesthesia. She understands the procedures and methods of the study and is willing to comply with the clinical trial protocol.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman diagnosed with stage III colon cancer. She is scheduled to receive her first course of chemotherapy with cisplatin, a highly emetogenic drug, administered as a single intravenous dose of 80 mg/m2 over 2 hours on study Day 1, in combination with 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin. She has not received any previous cytotoxic chemotherapy but has undergone surgery to remove the tumor. She has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and her hematologic and metabolic status are adequate for receiving a highly emetogenic cisplatin-based regimen based on laboratory criteria. She is a non-smoker and has no history of alcohol abuse. She is not pregnant or lactating, and is willing to use contraceptive methods throughout the clinical trial. She has no known hypersensitivity or contraindication to 5-HT3 receptor antagonists or dexamethasone. She is not currently taking any medication with known or potential antiemetic activity.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who was referred to the gastroenterology clinic after experiencing recurring episodes of epigastric pain and vomiting. He reports a history of alcohol abuse and smoking. He has no significant medical history, but lab work showed elevated pancreatic enzymes indicating potential pancreatitis. He underwent an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with difficulty in cannulating the common bile duct. The physician performing the procedure will determine if the patient meets the criteria for difficult cannulation based on the literature. The patient is being considered for this clinical trial to determine if the placement of a prophylactic pancreatic stent during pancreatic sphincterotomy can decrease the risk of post-ERCP pancreatitis. The patient has given consent to participate in the study.

A 35-year-old female with a history of ulcerative colitis and currently in remission with stable maintenance therapy. The patient is sexually active and willing to use an effective method of birth control during the study. She is able to take multiple capsules orally and has not received systemic non-topical antibiotics within the past 14 days. She has no active HIV, Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C infections and no history of recurrent Clostridium difficile infection or fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in the past 6 months. The patient does not have any other active gastrointestinal conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome or celiac disease. She is not currently undergoing chemotherapy or suffering from any other significant uncontrolled systemic disease that could interfere with study participation or objectives.

A 23-year-old woman comes to the clinic with complaints of persistent acne on her cheeks and chin for the past 6 months. She has tried over the counter acne products with no improvement. She has a history of acne during her adolescence, which was treated with topical antibiotics. She does not have any other dermatologic or systemic illnesses. She is not taking any medications or supplements. She has a healthy diet and exercises regularly. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is not pregnant. She is concerned about the appearance of her face and its impact on her social life. Her acne is moderate with papules and pustules on her cheeks and chin. Her skin is oily with blackheads and whiteheads. Her BMI is 23. Her vitamin D level is 20 ng/mL.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking came to the clinic complaining of pain in his legs when he walks. He works as a truck driver and spends most of his day sitting. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but both are under control with medications. He has not had any previous surgeries or hospitalizations. He denies any history of heart disease, stroke, or diabetes. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is married and has two adult children. He exercises occasionally, but not regularly. He speaks English fluently.

A 28 year old male university student volunteered for the clinical trial as he is interested in contributing to research in the medical field. He is generally healthy and does not have any known medical conditions. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He is not currently taking any medication, including oral contraceptives or corticosteroids. His most recent lab results show a serum potassium level of 4.3 mmol/L and an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 85 mL/min. He is willing to receive hypoglycemia treatment as part of the study protocol.

Patient is a 20-year-old college student enrolled in the physical education program. They have no history of neurological or systemic diseases, overuse injuries, or orthopedic surgeries to the lower limbs within the past six months. They are not familiar with or have not previously worn the Nike Free shoe. The patient has read and signed the informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 40-year-old obese woman with a body mass index of 35. She has been struggling with weight loss for many years and has tried various diets and exercise regimens without success. She has no history of cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immunologic, dermatologic, neurologic, or psychiatric disease. She has not experienced any recent cardiovascular events and her blood pressure is within normal limits. She has no history of glaucoma or increased intraocular pressure, kidney stones, cholelithiasis or cholecystitis within the last 6 months. The patient is not currently on any prescription or OTC medication, except for hormonal contraceptives. She does not have a history of alcoholism or drug abuse and has not experienced any suicidal ideation. She is a non-smoker and has not used any tobacco or nicotine-containing products within the last 6 months. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has reviewed and signed the informed consent form.

This is a 56 year old male with a history of a slowly growing lump in the right preauricular region. The lump is painless and has been present for the past 6 months. An ultrasound of the area showed a 3 cm mass in the superficial lobe of the right parotid gland. Fine needle aspiration biopsy confirmed a benign pleomorphic adenoma. The patient has no history of any facial nerve palsy or any other significant medical history. The patient has been referred for a parotidectomy and has been enrolled in a clinical trial to analyze the incidence of complications associated with the surgery.

The patient is a pregnant woman residing in the Strasbourg Eurometropolis area. She is between 18-40 years old and is currently undergoing ultrasound follow-up for her pregnancy at HUS. She is fluent in French and has expressed no opposition to participating in the study. She is living in a socio-economically deprived neighborhood, which may affect her physical activity levels during pregnancy. She has no obstetric pathologies that may prevent her from participating in physical activity. She is willing to provide informed consent for the collection of data for the study.

The patient is a 2-year-old girl who was brought to the emergency room due to vomiting and diarrhea that started 2 days ago. She has experienced 4 episodes of diarrhea and 2 episodes of vomiting in the past 24 hours. The mother reports that the child is refusing to eat and drink and has become lethargic. Physical examination showed mild dehydration and positive stool sample for RV. The child's medical history is unremarkable, and she has not received any vaccinations for RV GE. The parent has given written informed consent for the child's participation in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has recently been confirmed positive for COVID-19 infection. He has been experiencing shortness of breath and difficulty breathing and is now admitted to the ICU where he has been intubated and is currently on mechanical ventilation. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial as he has a confirmed COVID-19 infection in a respiratory tract sample and has been diagnosed with ARDS as defined by the Berlin criteria. The patient has no history of significant comorbidities and is willing to participate in this observational study to contribute to the understanding of ARDS caused by COVID-19.

A 28-year-old male athlete presents with a history of ACL injury during a soccer game. He experienced immediate pain and swelling in his knee and was unable to bear weight on the affected leg. MRI revealed a complete tear of the ACL and a decision was made to proceed with surgery to reconstruct the ligament using the patellar tendon. He is in good health, with no significant medical history. He has no known allergies or contraindications to the use of PRP. He is an active individual and is motivated to return to his pre-injury level of activity. He has no other knee ligament injuries, chondral lesions, or osteoarthritis. He is willing to comply with the rehabilitation protocol and follow-up visits. He is not planning to have any other surgeries during the time of the study. He understands the nature of the study and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing severe pain in the lower back and right leg for the past 8 months. The pain is sharp and shooting, and it radiates down to his right foot. He has tried various conservative treatments, including physical therapy and medication, but the pain persists. He has no history of previous back surgeries or spinal cord injuries. The patient reports that the pain in his leg is worse than the pain in his back. The physical examination shows that the patient has limited range of motion and tenderness in the lower back. There is also pain on palpation of the right sciatic nerve. MRI imaging confirms a diagnosis of lumbar disc herniation at the L5-S1 level. The patient meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who has been experiencing symptoms of depression, including feelings of sadness, hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty concentrating. She has also noticed a significant decline in her processing and gait speed, which is impacting her ability to perform daily tasks. She has been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and her Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD) score is greater than or equal to 18. She meets the eligibility criteria for this clinical trial as she is aged 60 years or above, has a diagnosis of MDD, and has decreased processing speed and/or gait speed. She is willing and capable of providing informed consent and complying with study procedures. She does not have any exclusion criteria such as substance abuse, history of psychosis, or severe medical or neurological illness. She will be randomized to receive either levodopa, aerobic exercise, their combination, or a placebo in a 2x2 design. She will undergo evaluations before and after the 12-week duration study to assess cognitive domains, psychiatric symptoms, gait kinematics and mobility, and task-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) focused on effort-based decision making and reward processing. The data collected from this study will contribute to the development of improved treatment and prevention strategies for older adults with neuropsychiatric disorders.

The patient is a 24-year-old Korean man who was diagnosed with Crohn's disease 2 years ago. He has a family history of IBD, with his mother and younger sister both diagnosed with ulcerative colitis. He currently takes mesalamine daily and has had one course of corticosteroids in the past year for a flare-up. He experiences abdominal pain, diarrhea, and occasional rectal bleeding. He has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink. He is currently a student and lives with his parents and sister. He reports mild to moderate stress levels and follows a generally healthy diet. He has not taken antibiotics or probiotics in the past 4 weeks. He is willing to participate in the study and provide blood and fecal samples for genetic and microbiome analysis.

A 62-year-old male diagnosed with prostate cancer is considering participation in a clinical trial aimed at improving radiation treatment through the use of fiducial markers. The patient has undergone a biopsy and has received a confirmed diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the prostate gland. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is able to provide informed consent. The patient has no history of pelvic or prostate radiotherapy, and he does not have any contraindications to transrectal needle placement or MRI. He has no chronic inflammatory bowel disease or distant metastatic disease. The patient will be required to take levofloxacin for two days prior to the placement of the fiducials, and he will undergo evaluations including a physical exam, blood work, urine tests, and if appropriate, an MRI or bone scan. The patient will be anesthetized and have an antenna-like tube placed into the rectum for approximately 45 minutes to allow for placement of four gold fiducial markers into the prostate. Following the procedure, the patient will undergo a seven-week course of standard radiation therapy. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve his chances of successful treatment and is willing to undergo the necessary procedures and evaluations.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has a strong family history of breast cancer. Her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at the age of 45, and her maternal grandmother also had breast cancer. Genetic testing revealed that she is a BRCA1 mutation carrier. She has never had breast cancer or any abnormal breast findings on physical exam. She has had a mammogram in the past, which was negative for any abnormalities. She does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is not pregnant or lactating, and her menstrual periods are regular. Her physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to learn more about her breast cancer risk and to potentially detect any abnormalities at an early stage.

55 year old woman with recurrent ovarian cancer with a history of total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Pathology from the surgery showed a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma involving the ovary and fallopian tube. The patient subsequently underwent six cycles of adjuvant carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy. Imaging studies done after completion of chemotherapy showed no evidence of disease. The patient had no evidence of disease for 13 months, when she developed increasing abdominal distention and abdominal pain. A CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a 12 cm omental mass and ascites. A diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed the radiographic findings and a biopsy of the omentum revealed recurrent ovarian cancer. The patient was then treated with second-line chemotherapy consisting of liposomal doxorubicin and carboplatin. The patient had a partial response to this chemotherapy, but developed grade 3 palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia and the chemotherapy was discontinued after 5 cycles. The patient was then treated with bevacizumab for 9 cycles, but developed progressive disease. The patient is now eligible for this clinical trial. Past Medical History: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with pelvic organ prolapse. She has been scheduled for a 23-hour observation surgery to treat this condition. She is fluent in English and is able to understand the informed consent document. The patient has expressed anxiety regarding the surgery and is considering bringing a family member or close friend to her pre-operative appointment to help with her anxiety and to provide support during the informed consent process. The patient is willing to participate in a study to determine if having a support person present during the informed consent process will impact her anxiety, satisfaction, preparedness, and knowledge regarding her surgery.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who experienced an abnormal vaginal bleeding two weeks after a missed period. She underwent a pregnancy test which came out negative. She then underwent a pelvic ultrasound which revealed an enlarged uterus with multiple cystic spaces. She was then referred for a hysteroscopy and biopsy which revealed a diagnosis of gestational trophoblastic tumor. She has a prognosis score of 5 and is eligible for the clinical trial. She has no serious medical conditions and is physically fit with a Karnofsky score of 80. She is willing to comply with the follow-up and sign the informed consent form. She has not received any clinical trials of other drugs or Chinese medicine.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who is currently using an intrauterine device (IUD) as a form of contraception. She has no history of psychiatric disorder or major medical illness. She has a BMI of 23 kg/m2 and weighs 60 kg. Her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. She has no abnormal physical examination, vital signs, or ECG findings. She has never been pregnant and has never given birth. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She has a deviated nasal septum but no associated symptoms. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of intranasal esketamine.

The patient is a 63-year-old woman who was diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma six months ago. She underwent a radical resection but the cancer recurred and spread to her liver. She has no history of other malignancies or autoimmune diseases. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status of 1, experiencing mild fatigue and occasional abdominal discomfort. The patient has not received any prior PD-1 inhibitor or Apatinib therapy. She has measurable lesions based on RECIST v1.1 criteria. Her laboratory results indicate adequate organ function. She has no history of allogeneic organ transplantation or any other surgery. She has no history of psychotropic drug abuse or drug abuse. She is not currently pregnant or lactating. She understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. She is willing to use acceptable forms of birth control during the study.

A 42 year old woman comes to the clinic seeking to participate in a clinical trial for cancer prevention. She has a family history of breast cancer, but has tested negative for BRCA1 mutation. She has never been diagnosed with cancer, except for non-melanoma skin cancer. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and is able to give informed consent. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has a sub-optimal selenium level in her blood and is interested in dietary modifications or supplementation to reduce her risk of cancer. She agrees to undergo regular blood tests and imaging to monitor her health during the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old male with end-stage renal disease, currently undergoing Automated Peritoneal Dialysis (APD) for the last 3 months. He has been stable and using an icodextrin long dwell for the last two months, but has noticed a decrease in his ability to remove fluids over time. He has residual urine volume of less than 500 ml/24 hours and has no known allergies. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has not been scheduled for a transplant in the next year and has a life expectancy of at least 6 months. He is using Baxter PD solutions and has a systolic blood pressure above 100 mmHg on most occasions. He is willing to use the bimodal solution for at least one exchange overnight in at least 5 out of 7 days and can tolerate an 8-10 hour long dwell.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who is in good health and has no history of cardiac or pulmonary disease. He is a recreational climber and has experience climbing at moderate altitude (2500-4500m). He is interested in participating in a study to investigate the incidence of silent interstitial pulmonary edema at high altitude. The patient is able to provide consent and agrees to undergo chest ultrasound, Lake Louise score, cerebral sensitive score, and non-invasive hemodynamic parameters testing during a glaciology study on the Ortles Glacier in South Tyrol (3905m). The patient is not currently experiencing any acute lung, heart, kidney, or brain conditions, and does not have a neoplastic disease.

A healthy, non-smoking 27-year-old female with a BMI of 22, who has not undergone any sterilization procedures, and is not currently pregnant or lactating, is eligible to participate in this clinical trial. She has no significant medical history, and her physical examination, laboratory profiles, vital signs, and electrocardiograms are all within normal limits. She does not consume more than two units of alcohol per day and is willing to abstain from sexual intercourse or use a condom with spermicide during the study period. She does not take any medications, herbal remedies, or vitamin supplements, and has not participated in another clinical study within the last 30 days. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the study procedures in the informed consent form. She does not have any scars or tattoos that may obscure the injection site.

The patient is a 45-year-old female who has been experiencing lumbar radicular pain for the past 3 months. She complains of sharp, shooting pain that radiates down her left leg and is exacerbated by movements such as bending and lifting. She rates her pain as an 8 out of 10 on the visual analog scale. The pain is affecting her daily activities and she has been unable to work. She has no history of neurological diseases, peripheral polyneuropathy, or sensory changes. She has not recently undergone any surgery or suffered from acute injury. She is not pregnant and has no history of drug abuse. She has never received acupuncture before and is willing to try it as a form of treatment. She has not taken any pain medication for the past week and is willing to abstain from taking gabapentin during the trial.

The study is seeking 60 patients between the ages of 18 and 40 years who require surgical extraction of a single impacted mandibular third molar under local anesthesia. The patients must be ASA class I individuals and free from acute infection at the extraction site, pregnant or lactating, smoking or using tobacco/areca nut, and must have good oral hygiene. Patients with immunocompromising conditions, systemic diseases, or medication therapy that could interfere with wound healing are also excluded from the study. The patients will be randomly allocated to one of three groups, and each group will receive different preoperative medication: Group A will receive intramuscular dexamethasone, Group B will receive submucosal dexamethasone, and Group C will serve as the control group without any preoperative medication. The study will evaluate the efficacy of preoperative submucosal dexamethasone in reducing facial pain, swelling, and trismus after third molar surgery. The patients will be followed up at postoperative days 1, 3, and 7 to assess their pain, swelling, and trismus levels. The study is being conducted at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Guanghua School of Stomatology, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, and ethical approval has been obtained from the Institutional Ethics Committee of Guanghua School of Stomatology prior to the beginning of the study. The patients will be given amoxicillin and paracetamol postoperatively, and will be instructed not to seek medical help for any postoperative discomfort without prior information to the surgeon.

A 42-year-old female came to the clinic with a complaint of shoulder pain that has been bothering her for the past two weeks. She reported that the pain started after she overexerted herself during a workout. The pain has been constant and has limited her ability to lift her arm above her head or perform any activities that require upper body movement. She has no history of shoulder surgery, no corticosteroid use in the last two weeks, and is not currently pregnant. The patient will be tested within the first two to three therapy visits and must be between 18 to 64 years old to be eligible for the study. She is willing to participate in the study and will sign an informed consent form.

A 58-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the hospital with chest pain. An ECG reveals ST-elevation in the anterior leads and she is diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction. She underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with the placement of a drug-eluting stent. She was discharged home after 3 days with instructions for cardiac rehab and medication management. She has a high school education and has been working as a cashier for the past 20 years. She lives with her husband who is retired and they have two adult children who live out of state. She has a landline phone and is interested in participating in an education program to learn more about managing her heart health. She reports being compliant with her medications but has not yet started cardiac rehab due to transportation issues.

The patient is a 4-month-old baby boy who was born full-term with no complications during delivery. He is currently being exclusively fed with a free amino acid based infant formula due to his inability to tolerate cow's milk-based formulas. He was diagnosed with a milk protein allergy by his pediatrician after experiencing frequent vomiting and diarrhea with other formula types. The baby's parents are willing to participate in the surveillance program and have provided written informed consent. The baby has been growing and developing normally according to his pediatrician, with no reported adverse events related to the use of the amino acid-based formula.

A 56-year-old male patient presents with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) and a previous myocardial infarction. He has been on optimal medical therapy (OPT) for the past 4 months, which includes beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, and diuretics. He has been experiencing episodes of heart palpitations and shortness of breath on exertion. His ECG reveals a QRS duration of 110 msec. His echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 30% with no evidence of valvular disease. His medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement in the past. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He has no history of cerebrovascular accidents, transient ischemic attacks, or atrial fibrillation. He is not currently being considered for cardiac transplantation and has a life expectancy of more than 12 months. He is compliant with follow-up schedules and is willing to undergo quadripolar LV lead implantation if selected for the treatment group.

As this is a registry study, there is no specific patient description required for this trial. Patients who have been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma in the last 3 months, are over 18 years old, and are willing to sign an informed consent form are eligible to participate in this study. Patients who have previously participated in the 3K observational study or who have any conditions that would significantly complicate their follow-up may be excluded from the study at the investigator's discretion.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She came to the clinic complaining of neck pain and dizziness. Her physical examination showed no neurological deficits, but the carotid artery ultrasound revealed an unstable plaque. She has not had any previous vascular issues or surgeries. Her current medications include amlodipine, atorvastatin, and aspirin. She has no known allergies to any medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the efficacy and safety of Chinese herbal and insects medicine as an alternative treatment for her unstable carotid artery plaque. She understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to comply with the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who recently returned from a trip to an endemic area for schistosomiasis. She presented to her primary care physician with a history of fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Blood tests revealed eosinophilia and a positive western blot for schistosomiasis. Microscopy examination also confirmed the presence of schistosomiasis eggs in her stool. She has no significant past medical history and is not under guardianship. She has consented to participate in the retrospective study of clinical practice and management of imported schistosomiasis in France.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who describes himself as a "night owl". He has had difficulty falling asleep before 2-3 am and has trouble waking up before 10 am. He reports feeling tired during the day and has trouble concentrating at work. He has no history of medical or psychiatric illness in himself or his family members. He is not currently taking any medications or vitamins and does not follow a vegan diet. He has no significant visual problems and has not traveled across time zones recently. He does not have a history of rotating shiftwork. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his sleep and daytime functioning.

The patient is a 14-year-old boy from the United States who has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss for the past 6 months. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he is not taking any medications. His BMI is 18.5, BP: 110/70, HR: 75/min. Laboratory studies show a C-reactive protein level of 40mg/L (normal range <5mg/L) and hypoalbuminemia (2.8g/dL). Colonoscopy reveals a mucosal ulcer in the ileum and histological examination confirms the diagnosis of Crohn's disease. The patient has no family history of inflammatory bowel disease.

A 12-year-old male with a history of idiopathic aplastic anemia, diagnosed 2 years ago, presents with fatigue, weakness, and pallor. He has received multiple blood transfusions in the past and has been on immunosuppressive therapy with horse antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine for the past 6 months with no improvement in his pancytopenia. Bone marrow biopsy shows a cellularity of 20% with severe hypocellularity and trilineage hematopoietic suppression. The patient's parents have refused hematopoietic stem cell transplantation due to financial constraints. The patient has no history of viral infections or drug toxicity. The patient's laboratory results show a hemoglobin level of 7.5 g/dL, platelet count of 25,000/mm3, and an absolute neutrophil count of 0.2 × 109/L. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial investigating the use of eltrombopag in children with idiopathic aplastic anemia and the parent has provided written informed consent.

A 55-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital for an acute stroke that occurred 2 weeks ago. She has since regained some movement in her arm and leg, but her hand remains weak, making it difficult for her to pick up or hold objects. She has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, and she takes medications to manage these conditions. She is motivated to participate in rehabilitation and has some family support to help her with the SaeboGlove if needed. Her modified ashworth score at wrist and fingers is less than or equal to 2 and she has some initiation of gross active finger flexion. She has at least 10 degrees of passive range of motion wrist extension and is considered able to learn to use the SaeboGlove with or without the help of a willing carer. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and is not participating in any other stroke rehabilitation trial.

The patient is a 46-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with endometrial cancer. She is scheduled to undergo a minimally invasive hysterectomy in the coming weeks. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and she reports no other major medical concerns. She has access to a smartphone and is comfortable with technology, including using online platforms and automated phone systems. The patient is fluent in English and is willing to provide her phone number and email address for the purpose of self-reporting postoperative symptoms. She has a supportive family and lives in a house with easy access to transportation. The patient is motivated to participate in this pilot study to potentially improve the care and outcomes of future patients undergoing similar surgeries.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with cataracts. She has no other medical conditions and is currently taking no medications. She has noticed a gradual worsening of her vision, which has begun to affect her daily activities such as reading and driving. Her cataract surgery has been scheduled and she is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining the size of the corneal incision made during intraocular lens implantation. She is able to comprehend and sign a statement of informed consent and is willing and able to complete all required postoperative visits. Her preoperative astigmatism is less than 1.0 D and her calculated lens power falls between 18.0 D and 27.0 D. She has never had any previous corneal or refractive surgery and has no systemic diseases that affect the cornea. She meets all of the inclusion criteria for the study and has no exclusion criteria.

32 year-old woman with a history of infertility due to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) who is planning to undergo intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) following long GnRHa protocol. She has been unsuccessfully trying to conceive for the past 2 years. She has no history of moderate or severe endometriosis, hydrosalpinx, uterine abnormalities, myoma, or previous uterine surgery. She is currently not pregnant and is not using any hormonal therapy for contraception.

The patient is a 20-month-old boy who attends a public day care center in São Paulo. He is in good health and has no history of chickenpox or hepatitis A. The child's parents have provided written informed consent for their child to participate in the study. The child has not received any vaccine with a live attenuated strain of virus within the last 30 days, nor is he on any immunosuppressive therapy. He has not been diagnosed with any condition that may interfere with the evaluation of adverse events after immunization. The child is available for follow-up for at least 45 days.

A 35-year-old female who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and has no plans to become pregnant during the study. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m^2 and meets the criteria for being a CYP2C9 extensive metabolizer based on genotyping assessment. She has no history of bleeding disorders or significant head trauma. She does not take any prescription or over-the-counter medications, including vitamins or herbal supplements. She has not consumed grapefruit, cranberries, or any products containing these fruits in the past 7 days. She is willing to use reliable birth control during the study period. The patient has read and understands the study requirements and has given written informed consent approved by the ethical review board governing the site.

A 35-year-old female who gave birth to her second child at 38 weeks gestation. The delivery was uneventful, but shortly after, she began to experience postpartum bleeding that did not respond to initial medical management. She was referred to the obstetrics clinic for further management. The patient has no known bleeding disorders and has a history of uncomplicated vaginal deliveries. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study and undergo the novel approach of Hayman uterine compression sutures for management of severe atonic postpartum hemorrhage.

A 12-day-old infant with suspected systemic infection is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability and PK of ticarcillin-clavulanate. The infant was born at 29 weeks' gestation and has been in the neonatal intensive care unit since birth for respiratory distress syndrome. The infant's mother had an asymptomatic urinary tract infection during pregnancy, which was treated with a cephalosporin. The infant's vital signs are within normal limits, but the infant has been febrile for the past 24 hours with a temperature of 38.5°C. The infant has been receiving standard of care antibiotics for the past 24 hours. The infant has a peripheral intravenous catheter in place for administration of medications and fluids. The infant's serum creatinine level is 0.8 mg/dL, and the infant has a urine output of 2 mL/kg/hr over the prior 24 hours. The infant's parent has provided written permission for participation in the study.

40-year-old Hispanic male recently diagnosed with HIV and enrolled in CPCRA 006 protocol. He has a history of substance abuse and currently smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day. He lives alone and works as a waiter in a busy restaurant. He speaks English as his primary language and reports having a supportive family who live out of state. He is compliant with his antiretroviral therapy but has missed a few clinic visits due to work schedule conflicts. He is willing to participate in the study and has given consent for his involvement.

A 42-year-old woman with severe asthma has been experiencing frequent exacerbations despite optimal treatment. She has had at least one exacerbation requiring oral corticosteroids in the past 12 months. Her variable bronchial obstruction is between FEV1 >30 and <70% of theoretical. The patient is under the care of the Pneumology Department of BICHAT Hospital in Paris and is covered by French national health insurance. She has no history of severe exacerbation or adverse reactions related to a bronchoscopy. Her oxygen saturation measured by pulse oximetry is >90% in ambient air, and she has no clinically significant electrocardiogram abnormalities. The patient has no uncontrolled comorbidities or coagulation or platelet abnormalities. She has no habitual contraindications to a bronchial endoscopy and is not pregnant or lactating.

This is a 55-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 8 years. She has been taking metformin and glipizide for the past 6 months and has achieved a HbA1c level of 6.5%. She has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and weighs 78 kg. She has no other significant medical history and is in overall good health. She has no known allergies to medications, including GLP-1 receptor agonists. She is willing and able to adhere to the study procedures and has provided written informed consent. She is not currently taking Byetta or Victoza and has not received PB1023 Injection before. She has normal cardiovascular function, with a screening blood pressure of 128/80 mmHg and a mean QTc interval of 420 msec. She has normal renal and hepatic function, with an eGFR of 70 mL/min, normal urine protein, and liver function tests within normal limits. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. She is not currently participating in any other study and has not received any other investigational drug or device within the past 30 days. She meets all eligibility criteria for participation in this clinical trial.

55 yo F with a history of osteoarthritis in both knees, and now scheduled for a total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in 6 weeks. Patient works as an accountant and has experience using a computer, tablet and smartphone. Patient is interested in exploring the use of a mobile application to supplement her rehabilitation after surgery. She has reliable access to the internet and owns a smartphone. Patient speaks fluent Dutch and is willing to complete the patient reported outcomes online. She has no history of Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, cerebrovascular accident or any other medical condition that may interfere with the rehabilitation process. She agrees to be randomized and understands that she may or may not be assigned to the group that uses a mobile application for rehabilitation. The patient is compliant with her medication and has no allergies.

The patient is a 54-year-old male who has been diagnosed with locally advanced rectal cancer located 10 cm from the anal verge. He has no distant metastasis and has not undergone any prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy to the pelvis. The cancer is palpable and appears fixed. The patient has measurable disease and is otherwise in good health with an ECOG performance status of 1. His laboratory tests are within normal limits, and he has no known existing uncontrolled coagulopathy. He has not been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine therapy and has no known sensitivity to 5-Fluorouracil or DPD deficiency. He is not taking warfarin and has no serious concomitant systemic disorders that would be incompatible with the study. The patient has negative pregnancy test results and is not currently breastfeeding. He has no prior malignancies, except for a basal cell carcinoma of the skin 2 years ago that was curatively treated. The patient is not currently taking any medications that would interfere with the protocol therapy.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who presented with a 6-month history of persistent epigastric pain and unexplained weight loss. He has no significant past medical history and has never smoked. Computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen demonstrated a 4 cm mass in the head of the pancreas with encasement of the superior mesenteric artery and vein, as well as involvement of the celiac axis lymph nodes. A biopsy of the mass confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. The patient has no evidence of metastatic disease on imaging studies. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and is otherwise in good health.

The patient is a 42 year old man who has been struggling with alcohol dependence for several years. He has a history of heavy drinking, experiencing withdrawal symptoms when attempting to quit, and continued use of alcohol despite negative consequences in his personal and professional life. He has not received treatment for his alcohol dependence in the past 3 months and reports having at least 6 Heavy Drinking Days (HDDs) in the 4 weeks preceding the screening visit. The patient has no history of severe psychiatric disorders or personality disorders but has expressed concern about suicidal thoughts in the past. He is not currently taking any medications for his alcohol dependence or any other medical condition. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

Pt is a 55yo M with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia who was admitted to the hospital due to pneumonia. He has been hospitalized for more than 24 hours and is eligible for the CODBAHRE study. The patient is willing to participate and has provided his non-opposition to the rectal swab and the completion of the questionnaire. He has been informed about the study and understands its purpose. The patient is able to answer the questionnaire and has no contraindications to the rectal swab.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) six months ago. She has already received one line of platinum-based doublet chemotherapy, but her cancer has metastasized to other parts of her body. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and no symptoms of brain metastases. She has provided sufficient tissue specimens for PD-L1 or TMB or blood samples for subsequent analysis. She has no other malignant tumors within the past five years, and she has never received anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-CTLA-4 or Car-T immunotherapy. She has no severe interstitial pneumonia or autoimmune diseases that require long-term hormone therapy. Furthermore, she has no uncontrolled pleural effusion or pericardial effusion, no uncontrolled pulmonary infection, and no acute cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is expected to live for more than three months. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

This is an 82-year-old female who sustained an intertrochanteric fracture of the left hip after a fall at home. She has a history of osteoporosis and hypertension, for which she is currently taking calcium supplements and lisinopril. She is otherwise in good health and is able to perform activities of daily living independently. She underwent surgical treatment for her fracture and was randomized into the intervention group for this clinical trial. Her surgeon completed the teaching video on how to evaluate intraoperatively the fracture, the reduction and the implant positioning and followed the reduction algorithm documenting that all intraoperative steps have been correctly accomplished. She will be followed up for radiologic outcome to assess the effect of the educational intervention on the quality of reduction and internal stabilisation of her intertrochanteric fracture.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has been experiencing severe pain in the lower right side of his mouth. He reports that the pain started a few weeks ago and has been gradually getting worse. The patient has never had any dental procedures before and has no significant medical history. Upon examination, the dentist diagnoses the patient with necrotic pulp in his mandibular posterior teeth. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as he falls within the age range of 18-50 years, has no medical conditions, and has necrotic mandibular posterior teeth. The patient is interested in participating in the study as he wants to receive the best possible treatment and ensure the long-term success of his endodontic treatment. He understands the potential benefits and risks of participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of open-angle glaucoma. He has been using an alpha agonist and a prostaglandin analog for the past year, but his IOP has been consistently above target at his last three visits. His current IOP is 26 mmHg OD and 28 mmHg OS. He has no known allergies or medical problems, and is not taking any other medications. He has provided signed, written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is not planning a pregnancy, and is using a reliable method of contraception.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman diagnosed with nonmetastatic adenocarcinoma of the breast with lymph node invasion. She recently underwent a complete surgical resection which included the removal of at least 5 lymph nodes, and with no residual tumor, within the past 42 days. The patient has no prior history of breast cancer or any other malignancy. She has no contraindication to anthracycline therapy and has no chronic medical or psychological condition. The patient is not pregnant and is using effective contraception. She is HIV negative and has no active infection. She has no geographic or social reason that would preclude study therapy. The patient is expected to have a life expectancy that is not specified. Her performance status is WHO 0-1, and she does not have any dyspnea at rest or supplemental oxygen dependence. Her hematopoietic system is within normal limits, with a WBC of at least 2,000/mm^3 and platelet count at least 100,000/mm^3. Her ALT and AST are no greater than 1.5 times upper limit of normal (ULN), alkaline phosphatase is no greater than 2.5 times ULN, and bilirubin is no greater than ULN. She is hepatitis B and hepatitis C negative and has no hepatic dysfunction. Her creatinine is less than 1.3 mg/dL OR creatinine clearance is greater than 60 mL/min, and her ECHO and LVEF are normal. The patient is a candidate for combination chemotherapy with or without trastuzumab in treating women with breast cancer that has spread to lymph nodes in the axilla (under the arm).

The patient is a 24-year-old HIV+ male who resides in the Tenderloin district of San Francisco. He was diagnosed with HIV two years ago and has been taking antiretroviral medication since then. He has experienced some side effects with his current medication and is interested in switching to Atripla. He is able to provide informed consent and is willing to complete all study procedures. He does not have any issues with substance abuse, cognitive function, or psychosis. He is otherwise healthy and committed to managing his HIV.

A 30-year-old pregnant woman in her 39th week of gestation presents to the hospital for induction of labour. She has a single fetus and uncomplicated pregnancy, with no medical risk factors. She has never had a caesarean section before and has no history of uterine scar. The woman is well-informed and has read the information leaflet regarding the clinical trial. She is willing to participate in the study and provides full informed consent. The woman is randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups, either the trans-cervical balloon catheter or the vaginal prostaglandin 10mg (Propess). She is allocated using block randomisation, stratified by site (St. George's and Medway) and parity (nulliparous and multiparous). The woman is given a recruitment survey to complete, which will include closed questions and comment boxes to examine her understanding of the trial and her reasons for participating. She is also given a follow-up questionnaire to complete after the trial, which will assess her satisfaction with the experience and the level of information provided. The woman is willing to participate in the qualitative study and provides her telephone details, so she can be contacted postnatally to confirm whether she is still happy to participate in an interview. She is assured of confidentiality and her rights to decline consent for observation or interview.

The patient is a 35 year old woman scheduled for a minor surgical procedure under general anesthesia. She has an ASA score of I, with no significant medical history, no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and no neurological disease or neurosurgical operations.
