She does not take any medications that might interfere with the EEG. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. Initial EEG recordings have been performed and there are no pre-existing epileptic EEG patterns. She is in good health with a normal body mass index (BMI) and no history of pulmonary disease. Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. The surgery is expected to last approximately 30 minutes.

The patient is a 73-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). He has not received any treatment for the disease yet. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications except for occasional aspirin for headaches. He reports feeling tired and weak, with occasional fevers, but denies any bleeding or bruising. He lives with his wife and is retired. He enjoys spending time with his grandchildren and going on walks in his neighborhood. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. His laboratory results show normal kidney and liver function, with bilirubin levels within normal limits. He has no active infections or other significant illnesses. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and understands the potential benefits and risks associated with the study.

The patient is a 70-year-old Japanese man who is generally healthy and has a BMI of 23 kg/m2. He has no history of Quincke oedema or angiooedema, nor has he experienced repeated episodes of urticaria. He has no history or present symptoms or signs of asthma, airway hyperreactivity or obstructive lung disease. He is not taking any medications and has not participated in any clinical trials within the last 3 months. He lives alone and is retired. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance scientific research.

This is a 22-year-old female with cystic fibrosis who has a history of frequent respiratory exacerbations. She has been managing her condition with a stable maintenance medical regimen for the past six weeks. She has experienced at least two respiratory exacerbations per year requiring oral and/or intravenous antibiotics for the past two years, but no more than 4 exacerbations requiring intravenous antibiotics during either of those years. She has not had any previous anti-reflux or peptic ulcer surgery and has not used PPIs within the past two weeks. She has not had a pulmonary exacerbation requiring antibiotics within the previous 2 weeks and is not on parenteral hyperalimentation. She does not smoke cigarettes and is not currently being treated with azoles, iron, anti-coagulants, digitalis or any investigative drugs within the previous month. She has not used any over-the-counter acid suppressor agents, including acid neutralizers. She is willing to undergo a 6-month randomized, placebo-controlled intervention study to evaluate the effect of proton pump inhibitors on CF pulmonary exacerbations.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with a history of heart failure with functional class II-III according to the New York Heart Association. The patient's echocardiogram from the last 6 months showed an ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≤ 45% and cardiac hypertrophy (left Ventricular Diastolic Diameter (LVDD) > 55mm and Diameter Systolic left Ventricular (LVSD) > 45mm). The patient is clinically stable and optimized from the point of view of drug therapy. The patient's body mass index (BMI) is <30 kg/m2. The patient does not have unstable angina, recent myocardial infarction, or heart surgery within the last three months. The patient does not have chronic orthopedic, infectious, or metabolic diseases. The patient's FEV1/FVC is above 70%, indicating no obstructive respiratory disorder. The patient is a non-smoker. The patient does not have any limitations on the use of noninvasive ventilation (NIV) and does not have claustrophobia, inability to remain with their mouths closed, abdominal distention, hemodynamic instability, heart rate (HR) <60 bpm, recent trauma, nausea, or vomiting.

A 52-year-old male smoker presented with a persistent cough and shortness of breath. A CT scan revealed a 1.5 cm pulmonary nodule located in the upper lobe of the right lung. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He has a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smokes half a pack of cigarettes per day. The patient has signed informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is scheduled for surgery to remove the pulmonary nodule.

The patient is a 45-year-old male from Canada who was diagnosed with Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD) two years ago. He has a history of smoking 20 cigarettes per day for the past 15 years. He presents with symptoms of dyspnea on exertion and cough for the past six months. The spirometry test shows FEV1/SVC <70% of predicted value post bronchodilator, and FEV1 < 80% of predicted value post-bronchodilator. CT scan confirmed the diagnosis of emphysema. He has a rare phenotype related to AAT deficiency, and his AAT serum level is ≤ 11 micromole. He had two moderate exacerbations in the past year, both requiring hospitalization and systemic steroids. He is able and willing to sign the informed consent and can self-administer inhaled AAT. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he is not currently on any medication. His family history is negative for any lung disease. His vital signs are stable: BP: 120/80, RR: 16/min, HR: 80 bpm, BMI: 27, O2sat: 95%. He has negative serology for HBsAg, HCV, and HIV-1. He is not pregnant, lactating, or using any contraceptive method.

A 58-year-old man comes to the hospital with a complaint of chest pain that started about an hour ago. He describes the pain as a tightness in the chest that radiates to his left arm. He has never experienced this type of pain before. The patient has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, but he has never been diagnosed with any heart condition. His vital signs are within normal limits, and the physical examination does not reveal any significant findings. Blood tests show that his troponin levels are below the threshold used to diagnose a heart attack. The patient is a suitable candidate for the trial as he has not been diagnosed with a heart attack and his troponin levels are within the normal range.

A 52-year-old male construction worker complains of persistent shoulder pain and stiffness for the past 6 months. He describes the pain as a dull ache that worsens with movement, especially reaching overhead. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and physical therapy, but the symptoms are still present. He reports no history of diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, or shoulder trauma. He has no other significant medical history and is not on any medication. He is otherwise healthy and active, with no significant family history. He has never had any allergic reactions or coagulopathy. His shoulder movement is limited, with a range of motion of only 50% compared to the opposite shoulder. He rates his pain as 7 out of 10 on the visual analogue scale during movement and 4 during rest. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of ultrasound guided shoulder intra-articular ozone injection versus pulsed radiofrequency application for adhesive capsulitis.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who has been experiencing knee pain for the past year. She has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and has been taking acetaminophen to manage her pain. She is otherwise in good health and is able to walk comfortably for short distances. She is willing to limit her intake of alcohol and caffeine for the duration of the study. She speaks English fluently and is able to understand and complete the study questionnaires. She has previously benefited from the use of NSAIDs and acetaminophen for pain relief.

This is a 34 year-old female with a long history of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), presenting with symptoms including abdominal cramps, bloating, and diarrhea. She has tried various diets and medications to alleviate her symptoms with no significant improvement. She has never been diagnosed with celiac disease, wheat allergy, or inflammatory bowel disease. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to determine if a gluten-free diet will alleviate her symptoms and improve her quality of life. She understands the study involves a six-week dietary intervention, followed by further testing to determine if she has non-celiac gluten sensitivity. She is willing to comply with the study protocol and any necessary dietary restrictions.

A 32-year-old woman in her first trimester of pregnancy, with a singleton pregnancy and no history of neural tube defects, is eligible to participate in the Optimal Nutrition for Prevention of Hypertension in Pregnancy clinical trial. She does not take any medication that interferes with B-vitamin metabolism. The study aims to investigate the effect of riboflavin supplementation, alone or in combination with 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, on blood pressure during pregnancy in women with a specific genetic polymorphism. The woman will be required to provide a buccal swab to collect DNA for genotyping, a non-fasting blood sample, and complete a health and lifestyle questionnaire and a 4-day food diary. At the 16th gestational week, she will be randomized to receive either riboflavin, riboflavin in combination with 5-MTHF, or placebo until the end of pregnancy. She will also have her blood pressure and weight measured at various time points throughout the study. After delivery, samples of cord blood, umbilical cord, and placenta will be collected, and the weight and length of the newborn will be measured. The woman and her baby will also be visited at home when the baby is 2-4 months old to measure the infant's weight, length, and blood pressure. This study is aimed at identifying the impact of B-vitamin supplementation on blood pressure during pregnancy and its influence on the blood pressure of offspring.

A 42 yo male with a history of asthma since childhood, presents with symptoms of coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath. He has been using his rescue inhaler more frequently and has had to miss work due to his symptoms. He reports that he is compliant with his current medication regimen of inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-agonist, but it is not providing adequate relief. On physical examination, he has decreased breath sounds and expiratory wheezing. Spirometry reveals a forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of 60% predicted. He meets the criteria for not well-controlled asthma and is therefore eligible for this clinical trial.

A 54-year-old male patient with a history of aero digestive cancer (squamous cell carcinoma) presents to the clinic for implant surgery after undergoing external head and neck radiotherapy and mandible reconstruction by microanastomosed fibula flaps. The patient has a performance status of 80 and has adequate bone volume to support the implant. The patient has no other concurrent diseases or contraindications to general anesthesia. The patient is affiliated with a social security system and has provided written, voluntary, and informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who has been diagnosed with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). She has been on immunosuppressive therapy for the past year, including methotrexate and corticosteroids. She has not received the Hepatitis A vaccine previously and has no known history of Hepatitis A infection. Her parents have provided written informed consent for her participation in the clinical trial, and she has provided written assent. She has been compliant with her medications and has no bleeding disorders that would contraindicate IM injection or blood collection. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has not received any Hepatitis B vaccine within the past 28 days and routine childhood vaccines (except MMR and Varicella) were separated from the study vaccination by at least 7 days.

47 yo female with a recent diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer. The patient underwent a biopsy within the last 12 months confirming HER2 status by either immunohistochemistry (IHC), Silver In Situ Hybridization (SISH) or Fluorescent In Situ Hybridization (FISH). The patient has a target lesion diameter of ≥15mm that has not been previously irradiated. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 0-2 and has a life expectancy of > 3 months. The patient has adequate organ function as defined by Hb≥10g/L, WBC≥3.0 x 109/L, PLT≥80 x 109/L, Serum creatinine ≤1.4mg/dl, SGOT and SGPT ≤2 x ULN, and Total bilirubin ≤ 2 x ULN or 3.0 mg/dl in patients with Gilbert's syndrome. The patient must have been appropriately staged using FDG-PET within 42 days of study entry and additional imaging according to local standard of care. The patient has not received any other investigational agent within the last 14 days and is not on therapeutic doses of anticoagulants or has a raised prothrombin time. The patient is willing to use contraception (barrier, abstinence, non-hormonal) for 3 weeks after injection of [18F]GE-226. The patient provides written informed consent before admission to the study.

45-year-old male with a 3-month history of right-sided neck pain radiating to his right shoulder and arm. He reports numbness and tingling in his right thumb and index finger but no weakness or loss of coordination. He has no previous history of cervical or thoracic spine surgery. He reports no other significant medical history or medications. He works as a computer programmer and spends long hours sitting in front of a computer. He denies any history of smoking or alcohol use. On physical examination, he exhibits limited cervical range of motion with pain, decreased strength of the right triceps muscle, and a positive Spurling's test on the right side. MRI of the cervical spine reveals a herniated disc at C6-C7. His BMI is 28. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to manage his symptoms.

There will be no human subjects for this clinical trial, as researchers will be using public data from birth certificates, driver's licenses, voter registration, and death certificates in North Carolina and Iowa to link to the Agricultural Health Study. The study will focus on how early life exposures to farms are linked to cancer and other negative health outcomes in the offspring of AHS participants born between 1975-2009. Therefore, no patient description is needed.

A 28-year-old woman has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 3 years. She experiences delusions, paranoia, and disordered thinking, which have significantly impacted her daily life. She has previously tried various medications to alleviate her symptoms but has not experienced significant improvement. She is a non-smoker and has no history of cardiovascular illness or neurological illness other than schizophrenia. She is not currently abusing any substances and has never been on clozapine. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially improve her symptoms and quality of life.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has been diagnosed with short bowel syndrome type II for the past 7 months. The patient has a history of multiple abdominal surgeries due to the complications of Crohn's disease. His current medications include pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy and vitamin supplements. He has a history of recurrent episodes of nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis, which require frequent hospitalizations. His most recent bloodwork showed an abnormal level of oxalate in his urine. He is referred to this study to determine if measuring the plasma oxalate level can help predict his risk of developing renal complications due to hyperoxaluria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with a BMI of 30. She was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 3 years ago and has been on a combination of metformin and glipizide to control her blood sugar levels. However, her HbA1c levels have remained above 8.0 despite her compliance with the medication regimen and lifestyle modifications. She has a family history of diabetes with her father and two siblings also being diagnosed with the disease. She has not undergone any abdominal surgeries in the past and does not have any known coagulopathies or liver cirrhosis. She is interested in participating in the study and has shown an understanding of the mechanisms of action of the duodenal exclusion procedure. She is not currently pregnant and is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up schedule.

35-year-old male veteran who served in Operation Enduring Freedom/Operation Iraqi Freedom (OEF/OIF) is in a committed relationship with a female partner. He has a history of physical aggression towards his partner, including at least one act of male-to-female severe violence in the past 12 months. He has experienced trauma during his military service and is currently struggling with managing his anger. He is willing to participate in a therapeutic intervention aimed at reducing intimate partner violence and managing anger. He does not have any active psychosis or suicidal/homicidal ideation. His reading skills are adequate to complete the assessment instruments. He does not have a history of alcohol or drug dependence.

The patient is a 40-year-old female who works at a desk job and has been experiencing pain in her right elbow for the past 6 weeks. She reports that the pain is worse when she grips objects or performs activities that involve using her elbow. She also reports a reduced grip strength and an increased sensitivity to manual palpation over the lateral epicondyle. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and rest, but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. The patient has no history of upper limb fractures, surgery or concomitant disease. She is mentally stable and able to give informed consent. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to see if tissue flossing can help alleviate her symptoms.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) 8 months ago that was confirmed through histological biopsy. The patient's tumor was found to have an activating EGFR TK mutation. The patient was started on gefitinib as first-line treatment for the cancer, however, after 6 months of treatment, the disease progressed. The patient is currently experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain. The patient has no history of interstitial lung disease or any other major health issues. The patient is willing to consider participating in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. The patient is a retired engineer and lives with his wife. He enjoys spending time with his grandchildren and traveling. The patient currently has a good appetite and is able to carry out daily activities without much difficulty. The patient does not have any other co-existing malignancies and has not received any other treatment for cancer, with the exception of gefitinib.

53F with a history of hypertension and occasional alcohol use was referred to the University of Maryland clinic for a routine check-up. She reports occasional gambling during her visits to the casino, but does not consider it a problem. She denies any issues related to her gambling behaviors and does not believe it affects her daily life. She has never sought treatment for gambling-related issues and has never been screened for gambling behaviors during previous medical appointments. She is proficient in English and fully capable of understanding and providing informed consent for the study.

This is a 4-year-old girl with a history of Tetralogy of Fallot defect who underwent a systemic to pulmonary artery shunt procedure at the age of 6 months. She has been followed closely by her cardiologist ever since and has been stable with no significant medical issues. Recently, her cardiologist has recommended that she undergo a complete repair of her defect, but there is uncertainty as to the optimal timing for this surgery. She has no significant medical history and has been compliant with all of her medical appointments and medications. Her parents are concerned about the risks and benefits of the surgery and would like more information about the optimal timing for the procedure. They are considering enrolling her in this clinical trial to help determine the best course of action for their daughter.

The patient is a 55-year-old Asian female who presents with no ocular complaints. She has no significant past medical history, no history of ocular trauma, and no family history of glaucoma. Her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. Slit lamp examination of both eyes reveals clear corneas and open angles with no peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS). Intraocular pressure (IOP) is within normal limits, and optic nerve head evaluation shows no evidence of glaucomatous optic neuropathy or cup-disc ratio (CDR) greater than 0.7. She has mild corneal guttae but no other corneal abnormalities. She is not on any chronic medications and has no known systemic health problems. She has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to be followed for 5 years to assess the effectiveness of prophylactic treatment in preventing blindness due to primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG).

30-year-old female who has struggled with obesity for several years and has a BMI of 28. She recently completed the NovinDiet Plan and lost 15% of her initial weight. She is interested in maintaining her weight loss and is willing to participate in the study. She exercises regularly and has no allergies to nut products. She is not pregnant or planning to become pregnant in the next 6 months, does not take medication that could affect metabolism or change body weight, and has no history of heart problems, chest pain, or cancer within the last five years. She does not smoke and has not yet reached menopause. She has no chronic diseases and her thyroid hormone levels are normal.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis for the past 5 years. He has tried various topical treatments, including corticosteroids, emollients, and calcineurin inhibitors, but they have not provided any significant relief. He has been experiencing significant itching, redness, and dryness on his face, neck, and arms, which impacts his daily life activities. The patient has no history of substance abuse, and he is not planning any surgical interventions during the study. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or intending to become pregnant during the study. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and evaluation schedule.

30 yo female with a history of asthma, currently taking inhaled corticosteroids and short-acting bronchodilators but experiencing frequent symptoms of wheezing, shortness of breath, and coughing. She has a BMI of 28 and a history of seasonal allergies. She reports occasional alcohol use and non-smoker. She works as a teacher and has no known environmental triggers for her asthma. She has not had any recent exacerbations and has not required oral steroids in the past year. She will be a good fit for this clinical trial as she meets the inclusion criteria for a diagnosis of asthma and does not have any exclusion criteria. Her asthma symptoms and adherence to treatment will be assessed using the ASK-20 questionnaire and reviewing the number of prescriptions for asthma during the last 6 months. The study will also analyze the relation between the level of asthma control according to the ACT score and smoking habit, obesity, and concomitant diseases such as rhinitis and gastroesophageal reflux.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been living with severe emphysema for the past 5 years. He experiences moderate to severe dyspnea and has difficulty performing everyday activities such as climbing stairs or walking long distances. He has tried standard-of-care medical management but has not experienced significant improvement in his symptoms. He is able to walk a minimum of 140 meters in the six minute walk test. The patient has at least one airway with the intention to be treated with a 9 mm Spiration Valve based on a calibrated balloon sizing of the airway. The patient is willing to participate in the study, complete the required follow-up visits, and maintain consistent nutrition and exercise habits during the study period. The patient does not have co-existing major medical disease that will limit evaluation, participation, or follow-up in the study. The patient has not had prior lung volume reduction surgery, intra-bronchial valve therapy for emphysema, or major lung procedures.

54-year-old female with a history of metastatic breast cancer and prior chemotherapy treatment that was unsuccessful in controlling her disease. She presents with progressive disease and is interested in participating in a clinical trial. She has no known history of liver disease or myocardial infarct. She is willing to receive intravenous administration of the study drug and to take oral ketoconazole tablets.

The patient is a 65-year-old postmenopausal woman who underwent surgery for primary breast cancer three weeks ago. The surgery involved a lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection, and the histology confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma with estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor-positive status. No neoadjuvant therapy was given prior to surgery. The patient has completed all diagnostic staging investigations, including a mammogram, abdominal ultrasound, chest x-ray, and bone scan, which were negative for metastatic disease. The patient has not received any prior endocrine therapy or aromatase inhibitors, and her medical history is negative for any other non-breast malignancies. She has no concurrent medical or psychiatric conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study. The patient is willing and able to take oral medication and has adequate oral intake to maintain reasonable nutrition status. She meets the postmenopausal criteria, defined as being over 60 years of age or having spontaneous cessation of menses for more than one year prior to study entry, or having menses cease within the past year due to hysterectomy or spontaneously and a follicle-stimulating hormone level prior to study entry in the postmenopausal range. The patient's performance status is ECOG 0-2, and she has a life expectancy of at least five years.

The patient is a 33-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder. She has a history of treatment-resistant depression and has failed to respond to at least two previous antidepressant treatments. Her current symptoms include feelings of hopelessness, loss of interest in activities, and disrupted sleep patterns. She has been hospitalized voluntarily for psychiatric treatment. She drinks occasionally and has no history of drug abuse. She has adequate social support and can rely on a friend to provide transportation to and from outpatient ketamine infusion visits. She has no history of schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder, nor does she have active psychotic symptoms. She is not currently on lithium treatment and has no history of poor antidepressive response to or poor tolerability of ketamine. She is willing and able to provide informed consent and pass the comprehension assessment test related to the effects of ketamine and trial objectives and criteria.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. He has been experiencing chest pain and discomfort during physical exertion for the past few months. His BMI is 29. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no prior history of heart disease, but his father had a heart attack at the age of 60. His blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, and his total cholesterol level is 250 mg/dL. He is scheduled for a CT scan to evaluate coronary artery plaque. He has no contraindications to have an MRI scan. He is aware of the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to participate. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

22-year-old female diagnosed with Hodgkin's Lymphoma 2 months ago, currently undergoing chemotherapy at the National Institutes of Health. She reports experiencing some anxiety and depression related to her cancer diagnosis and treatment. She has weekly contact with her mother who lives in another state. Her mother will also participate in the study as a parent participant. The patient has no history of mental health problems or treatment prior to her cancer diagnosis. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to be audio recorded during the K-SADS-PL interview.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage IV renal cell carcinoma. She is married and has two adult children. She has a history of hypertension and has been a smoker for 20 years, but quit 10 years ago. She underwent left nephrectomy four months ago and has been receiving sunitinib as a first-line treatment. However, her disease has progressed and she is no longer responding to the treatment. She complains of fatigue, loss of appetite, and shortness of breath. She is offered CDX-1127 as a potential second-line treatment. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. She has adequate blood, bone marrow, liver, and kidney function. She is not receiving treatment with immunosuppressive agents including systemic steroids and does not have an active infection requiring systemic therapy. She has little or no side effects remaining from prior cancer therapies.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been struggling with opioid addiction for the past three years. He has a history of intravenous drug use and has been using opioids daily for the past year. He has no significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He is interested in receiving treatment for his addiction and is willing to participate in a clinical trial. He meets the criteria for narcotic maintenance treatment and has no evidence of anti-active DSM-IV Axis I psychiatric disorder or significant medical illness. He is not currently pregnant.

The patient is a 28-year-old sexually active woman who has a regular menstrual cycle. She has no history of vaginal infections, and she is not currently experiencing any symptoms of vaginal discomfort or discharge. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivities to any medications or supplements. She is not currently pregnant or going through menopause. She does not have any chronic medical conditions, and her medical history is unremarkable. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the effect of an oral probiotic on the vaginal flora.

A 30-year-old female presents with recurrent fever, fatigue, weight loss, and muscle pain. She reported experiencing claudication of her left arm and leg and decreased pulses in her left brachial and femoral arteries. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she has no history of smoking, hypertension, or diabetes mellitus. Laboratory tests showed elevated ESR levels (56 mm/h) and CRP levels (18 mg/L). Vascular magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) showed stenosis of the left subclavian artery, and computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed stenotic lesions in the aortic arch, left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery, and left iliac artery. The patient was diagnosed with Takayasu's arteritis based on the American College of Rheumatology 1990 classification criteria. She has not received any treatment for Takayasu's arteritis before and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and type 2 diabetes. He is currently taking two or more Stars medications to manage his conditions. He is a current customer of RightSource and fills his prescriptions through their pharmacy. He has been struggling with medication adherence and often forgets to refill his prescriptions on time. He has no known allergies to medications and is not currently taking any other medications that may interfere with his Stars medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to determine if synchronizing his prescription refill schedule will improve his medication adherence.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who was diagnosed with Crohn's disease at the age of 22. He has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms of the condition for the past year, including abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He has been managed with various medications, including corticosteroids and immunosuppressants, but has not achieved complete remission. He has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgery or been diagnosed with stenosis or fistula in the small intestine or colon. He is currently taking mesalamine and experiencing some relief, but his symptoms are still affecting his daily activities. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a new medication, MT-1303, for the treatment of Crohn's disease. His BMI is within normal range, and his vital signs are stable. He is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the study, including regular clinic visits and blood draws.

A 45-year-old male patient with a BMI of 28 kg/m2 was referred for elective laparoscopic surgery. The patient had no history of eye disease, cardiovascular or neuromuscular disease, and was not using any antihypertensive agents. The patient had an American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) status of II. The patient was informed about the study and gave written consent to participate. The patient was randomly assigned to one of the four groups (Group C, L, M, or H) for the study. The patient was scheduled to undergo surgery with an intra-abdominal pressure of 9, 12, or 15 mmHg, depending on the group assigned. The patient's intraocular pressure was measured binocularly before, during, and at the end of the surgery using a contact tonometer.

Pt is a 40yo M with no significant medical history, seeking to participate in a clinical trial studying the effects of Zanthozylum armatum fruit extract on cognitive function and cerebral blood flow. The patient has no known allergies, nor is currently taking any prescription medication or dietary supplements. The patient speaks English fluently and has a BMI of 23. The patient has never had surgery requiring general anesthesia and is not currently pregnant, seeking to become pregnant or lactating. The patient does not have learning difficulties or a visual impairment that cannot be corrected with glasses or contact lenses. The patient is a non-smoker and does not consume nicotine containing products. The patient does not have a history of alcohol or drug abuse and does not have any food intolerances/sensitivities. The patient is willing and able to complete all of the study assessments and has a bank account for payment.

Patient A is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with severe hemophilia B at a young age. He participated in a gene transfer clinical study between 2001 and 2004, where he received various doses of AAV2-hFIX16 manufactured by Avigen, Inc. He did not experience any adverse events during the study period and was monitored for efficacy. The study was suspended by Avigen, Inc., and the IND 9398 was transferred to The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia in May 2005. Since there were no guidelines for long-term follow-up of the trial subjects at the time, the US FDA issued guidelines for the 'long-term follow-up of gene transfer subjects' in response to events in an unrelated study conducted in France. The investigators plan to enroll Patient A in this observational study to follow him for up to 15 years after gene transfer. The study will consist primarily of annual history, physical examination, blood tests, urinalysis, and periodic liver ultrasound to characterize clinical outcomes and to detect any adverse events. Patient A is willing to participate in the study and is capable of performing the endpoints.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy Asian male with a body mass index (BMI) of 23.5 kg/m². He has no known history of hepatic or gastrointestinal diseases, and he does not smoke or consume alcohol or illicit drugs. The patient has not been on any regular medication for the past two weeks and has not participated in any pharmacokinetics study in the past six months. He has not donated or lost more than 450 mL of blood in the past three months or more than 1500 mL in the past 12 months. The patient is sexually inactive or using an efficient contraceptive method with a failure rate of less than 1%. He has no known hypersensitivity to the drug being studied or to any chemically related compounds. The patient has no clinical abnormalities or laboratory parameters outside the reference range for the population being studied. He is able to understand the nature and purpose of the study and has shown good intention to cooperate with the researcher. The patient is eligible to participate in this bioequivalence study of rosuvastatin calcium 20 mg tablets.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). He has been experiencing shortness of breath, cough, and fatigue for the past 6 months. He has a history of smoking but quit 10 years ago. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. His lung function test shows a Carbon Monoxide Diffusion Capacity (corrected for Hb) of 30% predicted of normal. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage his IPF symptoms. He is willing to comply with the study's requirements and follow-up visits. He signs the written informed consent and meets most of the inclusion criteria. However, he does not have any relevant airways obstruction, nor any bleeding risk or significant heart disease.

A 28 year old woman has been diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and has been undergoing treatment for the past year with various medications, but has not seen significant improvement in her lupus nephritis. The patient is experiencing symptoms such as fever, joint pain, fatigue, and swelling. A renal biopsy has shown that she has class III or IV glomerulonephritis. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that evaluates the safety and effectiveness of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) infusions for treatment-refractory lupus nephritis. She is not pregnant and has no history of malignancy or active infections. She has no evidence of cardiovascular disease or other illnesses that would make her unable to tolerate the treatment. The patient is able to give informed consent and is excited to participate in this new therapeutic approach to improve her lupus disease.

A 43-year-old woman was diagnosed with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer 10 months ago. She has already received two prior chemotherapy treatments and is currently seeking further treatment options. She is experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and difficulty sleeping. Her medical history shows that she has normal organ function, including bone marrow function, renal function, liver function, and cardiac function. She has an ECOG score of 1 and is expected to have a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to comply with the program requirements. She has signed and dated an informed consent form for the evaluation of Icotinib in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after second-line therapy.

A 60-year-old man presents with painless blood in his urine. He has a history of smoking and has been experiencing frequent urinary tract infections. The patient's PSA levels were normal, and a cystoscopy revealed a tumor in the bladder. Biopsy confirmed the presence of urothelial carcinoma. The patient is scheduled to undergo a transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) or modified GC regimen neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus radical total cystectomy. He is 18 years old and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. He is willing to provide written informed consent and has no contraindications to MRI or MRI contrast agent. The patient has no history of liver or kidney disease, heart failure, myocardial infarction, or severe heart and lung disease. He has no known central nervous system metastases or severe central nervous system diseases. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and is not participating in other drug trials. He has good general health and no autoimmune diseases.

The patient is a 26-week-old premature baby, weighing 900 grams, who was born via emergency C-section due to maternal hypertension. The baby was intubated at birth and has been on mechanical ventilation since. A 2D echocardiogram revealed a patent ductus arteriosus with a diameter of 2.0 mm. The baby has been receiving parenteral nutrition and has been tolerating feeds well. The parents have provided written informed consent and are willing to comply with the study procedures and treatment. The baby does not have any major congenital malformations or systemic illnesses other than the PDA. The medical team has deemed the baby fit for the trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who recently had a concussion after a fall while playing basketball with friends. She is currently experiencing symptoms such as headaches, fatigue, forgetfulness and difficulty concentrating. She is a part-time student and works as a server at a restaurant. She lives with her roommate and doesn't have any children or dependents. She has a smartphone and is comfortable using technology. She is able to read, write, and understand English. She has been seeing a healthcare practitioner for her concussion and has been recommended to participate in the trial. She is interested in trying out the Parkwood Pacing and Planning™ app to assist with managing her symptoms and improving her daily activities.

The patient is a 65-year-old male complaining of knee pain and stiffness. He has a history of osteoarthritis and has been experiencing symptoms for several years. He has tried various conservative treatments such as physical therapy and medication but has not found significant relief. He is interested in undergoing total joint arthroplasty for his knee. He has no history of inflammatory arthritis or hypercoagulable state. He is not currently taking any medications. He does not have any other significant medical history. He is retired and lives with his wife. He is able to perform his activities of daily living but has difficulty with walking and standing for extended periods of time due to his knee pain. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial examining the use of wound additives in primary total joint arthroplasty to improve postoperative wound healing and reduce complications.

This is a 55 year old male from Franklin County, Ohio who has a family history of colorectal cancer. He has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and occasional constipation for the past few months. He is interested in learning more about colorectal cancer and screening options. He is willing to participate in an educational intervention that could potentially improve his knowledge about colorectal cancer and increase his likelihood of getting screened. He is able to walk through the inflatable colon exhibit or view the PowerPoint presentation and flip books/flip charts.

A premature baby boy was born at 29 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 1100 grams. He was intubated and put on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory distress syndrome. He was given the standard dose of surfactant therapy at birth. He is now 10 days old and has been showing signs of respiratory decompensation, with a rise in his severity score to 4.0. He has not received any postnatal steroid therapy for lung disease. He has no known congenital malformations and his life expectancy is estimated to be greater than 7 days from enrollment.

50 year old female with a 5 year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the clinic with complaints of pain and numbness in her feet. She reports difficulty walking and performing daily activities due to the pain. She has been taking gabapentin for the past 3 months but has only experienced minimal relief. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new topical medication to treat her neuropathic pain. Physical examination reveals decreased sensation in both feet and positive Tinel's sign at the ankle. There are no local wounds or skin abnormalities in the applicable areas. The patient is interested in the trial and able to give consent. She has no allergies to capsaicin and does not have any other significant medical conditions or take any medications that may worsen her neuropathy.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy with a history of congenital immune deficiency. He has been diagnosed with a life-threatening cytomegalovirus infection and is currently undergoing treatment. His medical history includes recurrent respiratory tract infections and frequent hospitalizations. He is not currently taking any other medications aside from topical acyclovir. His blood work shows a normal ANC and platelet count. He has no known allergies to acyclovir or ganciclovir. He is able to communicate clearly and follow instructions. His weight is 25 kg and his height is 120 cm. His parents have given informed consent for him to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 55-year-old female who was diagnosed with indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) six months ago. She has already undergone treatment with rituximab-containing regimens but did not respond to the treatment. CT imaging at screening verified the disease and the tumor was found to be CD20 positive. She is currently in Stage III of the disease and has an ECOG Performance Status of 1. She has a life expectancy of at least 6 months and is willing to undergo a combination therapy of ofatumumab and bendamustine. She has no history of allogeneic stem cell transplant or previous autologous stem cell transplant, fludarabine therapy, or radioimmunotherapy in the past 12 months. She has no history of external beam radiation therapy to the pelvis or high dose steroids greater than or equal to 60 mg prednisone/day (or equivalent) within 3 months of randomization. She has no history of prior bendamustine treatment within 1 year of randomization not resulting in a CR or PR for at least 6 months. She is not currently undergoing treatment with anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody within 3 months of randomization. She has no known CNS involvement of indolent lymphoma and no other past or current malignancy. She is willing to comply with the protocol activities and is not lactating or pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old Hong Kong Chinese woman who was diagnosed with osteosarcoma at the age of 16. She underwent a complete course of treatment and has been in remission for 9 years. She is currently working as a graphic designer and living with her parents in a small apartment in Hong Kong. She enjoys spending time with her family and friends, watching movies, and playing video games. She has noticed some physical limitations and chronic pain in the affected limb since the completion of her treatment. She has also been experiencing feelings of anxiety and depression and has difficulty sleeping at times. She is fluent in Cantonese and can read Chinese. She is interested in participating in this study to help raise awareness of the holistic wellness of osteosarcoma survivors in Hong Kong.

A 35-year-old woman presents with persistent pain in her lower left jaw. She has a history of a failed root canal treatment in one of her molars. The patient is otherwise healthy and takes no medication. Clinical examination shows an asymptomatic single-rooted tooth with chronic apical periodontitis. Intraradicular posts are not present, and there is no evidence of overfilling or sinus tract. The patient agrees to participate in the study and signs the informed consent form. She is randomized to the ProTaper Universal group and undergoes retreatment using the D1, D2, and D3 files with a full rotational motion. Before the treatment, the clinician explains the pain report form to the patient, and she understands the instructions. The patient is asked to report her preoperative level of pain and to fill out the pain report form at 24, 48, and 72 hours following the retreatment. The patient is prescribed 400 mg ibuprofen to take in case of severe pain, at 6-hour intervals. She is requested to record the number of analgesic pills consumed each day and to call the contact number on the form if she encounters severe pain or has any questions regarding the treatment. The forms are collected on the 4th day following the retreatment, and a phone call is made every day for 3 days to obtain information on the postoperative pain and the frequency of analgesic intake.

A 27-year-old man with a history of epilepsy, refractory to antiepileptic drugs, undergoes a noninvasive workup and is found to be an excellent candidate for resective surgery. He has a past medical history of depression and anxiety, for which he takes selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. The patient reports experiencing focal seizures with impaired awareness, typically lasting 1-2 minutes, occurring 3-4 times per week. He describes auras characterized by a rising sensation in his stomach, followed by a feeling of fear or anxiety. During the seizure, he is unable to respond to verbal or tactile stimuli and experiences confusion upon awakening. The patient has no history of head injury, stroke, or brain tumors. He is currently employed as a software engineer and reports no significant cognitive deficits. He is interested in participating in clinical research to better understand the micro-physiology of his epilepsy and cognitive function.

The patient is a 14-year-old male dependent of a US Military member who is overweight with a BMI of 30. He has no known history of liver disease or any other medical conditions. He does not take any medications or supplements. He is active in sports and participates in soccer and basketball. He has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes. He has no known allergies or phobias related to MRI scans. His parent or legal guardian has provided written informed consent for his participation in the study.

The patient is a 6-month-old female infant who was admitted to the University Children's Hospital in Zurich due to fever symptoms. The infant's parents noticed that their baby was warm to the touch and had a temperature of 38.5°C. The infant has no significant medical history and has no known allergies. The infant's parents signed the informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The infant is currently staying in the hospital for more than 1 day and will have two temperature-sensing research prototypes applied to the skin (lateral ribcage and foot) in addition to the standard clinical monitoring procedures. The infant's rectal temperature will be measured every 8 hours, and ear temperature will be assessed every 4 hours with an infrared ear thermometer. The measurement procedure will last for a minimum of 18 hours and a maximum of 72 hours, depending on the stationary stay of the patient.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is 38 weeks pregnant with a singleton fetus. She has no significant medical history, is not taking any medications, and does not have any allergies. She is scheduled for an elective cesarean section due to breech presentation of the fetus. She is experiencing moderate anxiety related to the upcoming surgery and is interested in non-pharmacological methods to reduce her anxiety. She has no history of auricular acupuncture and is willing to participate in the study. She has social security affiliation and is able to provide informed consent. She does not have any psychological disorders that would prevent her from providing informed consent. She does not have a pacemaker, and her cesarean section is not for placenta accreta.

The patient is a 45-year-old African American man who has been diagnosed with HIV for the past 10 years. He has a history of smoking for 20 years and currently smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day. He is on antiretroviral therapy and his viral load is undetectable. He has a history of hypertension and is taking lisinopril to control his blood pressure. His past medical history is remarkable for a deep vein thrombosis in his left leg 5 years ago, which was treated with anticoagulants. His family history is positive for diabetes in his mother. The patient is motivated to quit smoking and has tried to quit in the past but was unsuccessful. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the cardiovascular effects of smoking cessation in HIV patients. He has access to a cellular phone and is able to participate in the study for 3 years.

The patient is a 27-year-old male who presented to the emergency department at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital (KCMH) with a rash that started about 2 hours ago. The rash consists of itchy, raised wheals of various sizes on his arms, chest, and back. He has no history of chronic urticaria and has not taken any antihistamines or steroids in the past 48 hours. He has no known allergies to chlorpheniramine maleate or any other medications. He denies any medical illnesses or conditions such as heart disease, kidney disease, or diabetes mellitus. He is not currently pregnant nor has been in the past. He does not have any other symptoms such as difficulty breathing or swelling of the throat. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves adding a short burst of corticosteroid to the conventional treatment of H1 antihistamines.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with complaints of pain and cramping in his right leg while walking. He reports that the symptoms have been gradually worsening over the past few months and have started to impact his daily activities. The physical examination reveals reduced pulses in the right foot and ankle with no other significant findings. The vascular ultrasound confirms the presence of significant stenosis in the right femoral artery. The patient is scheduled for endovascular treatment with the Passeo-18 Lux paclitaxel releasing balloon catheter as part of the BIOLUX P-III all-comers registry to collect clinical performance data on the device. The patient meets the inclusion criteria and has agreed to sign the Patient Data Release Form to participate in the study.

63 yo M with long-standing type 2 DM, on insulin therapy (70 U/day), presenting with a non-healing ulcer on the right foot. Patient reports a 6-month history of progressive pain and decreased sensation in the affected limb. Imaging revealed severe stenosis in the right external iliac artery and left superficial femoral artery, and an abnormal ankle-brachial index (ABI) of 0.3. The patient is not a candidate for revascularization due to the severity and location of the stenosis. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of autologous bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) for critical limb ischemia (CLI), as he has exhausted all standard treatment options. Past Medical History: - Type 2 DM - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Chronic kidney disease stage 3 - Diabetic retinopathy - Diabetic neuropathy - Previous myocardial infarction - Previous stroke - Peripheral arterial disease - Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease - Gastroesophageal reflux disease - Sleep apnea - History of tobacco use (quit 10 years ago)

51yo male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral vascular disease who underwent below-the-knee amputation on the right leg for a gangrenous foot ulcer. Patient has no current phantom limb or stump pain and wishes to participate in the study to prevent the onset of long-term pain. He is willing to have a percutaneous catheter placed and have ambulatory infusion for up to 6 days following hospital discharge.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been diagnosed with heart failure for the past 2 years. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and has had two previous hospitalizations for worsening heart failure symptoms. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath with exertion, fatigue, and edema in his lower extremities. He is currently taking furosemide, carvedilol, and lisinopril for his heart failure management. Despite being compliant with his medications, the patient reports that he still experiences symptoms and is concerned about his disease progression. The patient has given his consent to participate in the study and is willing to undergo additional ultrasound examinations during his routine outpatient heart failure clinic visits. He does not have any other medical conditions that would exclude him from participating in the study.

A 50-year-old male patient with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma was treated with CTL019/CTL119 under UPCC13413/NCT02030834 and achieved complete remission for over 6 months. However, the lymphoma has relapsed, and the patient has no available curative treatment options. He has no known history of hepatitis B or C, HIV infection, or active infection. He has no uncontrolled active medical disorder and has a performance status (ECOG) of 1. The patient's creatinine level is within normal limits, and his bilirubin and ALT/AST levels are within normal limits. He has measurable disease according to the "Revised Response Criteria for Malignant Lymphoma" (Cheson et al., J. Clin. Onc., 2007). His LVEF is above 40%, and he agrees to contraceptive requirements outlined in Section 4.3. He has provided written informed consent for the study.

40-year-old woman with a long-standing history of type 1 diabetes presents to the clinic for an annual diabetes check-up. She reports that her blood sugar levels have been well-controlled with insulin therapy. The patient denies any history of excessive alcohol consumption or illicit drug use. She does not have any known viral hepatitis and has never been diagnosed with any liver disease. The patient is interested in participating in a research study to explore the link between type 1 diabetes and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). She understands that the study will involve non-invasive screening methods such as MRI, ultrasound, and other diagnostic tools to detect the presence and severity of NAFLD. The patient consents to participate in the study and undergoes the necessary screening procedures. She also agrees to participate in follow-up assessments over the next several years to monitor any changes in her liver function and to evaluate the potential correlation between NAFLD and micro-or macrovascular complications in patients with diabetes.

A 45-year-old working woman who often dyes her hair, recently noticed some mild blurriness in her vision. She is otherwise healthy with no history of eye problems. She has been dyeing her hair for the past 10 years using a product that contains aromatic amines. She does not have any allergies to any food or drugs. She is not pregnant or lactating. She does not take any medications regularly. She is interested in participating in the study to help understand the potential risks associated with hair dye products containing pPD type aromatic amines.

A 32-year-old female with a BMI of 25.5, who is generally healthy, enjoys an active lifestyle and exercises at least three times a week. She has been trying to lose weight for the past 6 months with a combination of diet and exercise but has not been successful. She does not smoke and does not take any medications or dietary supplements. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes, but she has not been diagnosed with any chronic illnesses. She has a balanced and varied diet, but she sometimes feels hungry and craves sweets in the afternoon. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of a low-calorie beverage containing alginate on body weight and appetite sensation. She is not a vegetarian and is willing to consume a hypocaloric diet.

The patient is a 35-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus infection. He has not received any treatment for hepatitis C virus infection in the past 3 months and is not anticipated to begin treatment within 1 year after enrollment. He has no history of anaphylaxis or allergy to vaccine components and Tetanus and Diphtheria Toxoids Adsorbed (Td). He has no clinical signs suggestive of cirrhosis and has not had a liver biopsy showing bridging fibrosis or cirrhosis. He is negative for HBsAg and has no known chronic liver disease or evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma on liver biopsy. He has not had a liver transplant and is not anticipated to have one within 1 year of enrollment. He has not been vaccinated with a live virus vaccine in the past 30 days or an inactive virus vaccine in the past 14 days. He is not pregnant or breast-feeding, and he is not planning to impregnate. He has no active drug or alcohol abuse and is not at high risk for HIV infection. He agrees to use an acceptable method of birth control through week 52 of the study.

85-year-old female with a recent hip fracture scheduled for surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and osteoporosis, managed with amlodipine and calcium supplements. The patient has no known history of significant cardiac disease, but has been experiencing mild shortness of breath with exertion. The patient is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study. The patient is not currently taking lithium.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who has been an avid sports enthusiast for the past 10 years. He participates in a variety of sports including soccer, basketball, and running. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, he has been unable to participate in his usual group sports activities and has been limited to individual exercises at home. He is concerned about the impact of the pandemic on his overall physical fitness and his ability to return to group sports activities in the future. He has no significant medical history and is not currently on any medications. He has not been diagnosed with COVID-19 and has not been in contact with anyone who has been diagnosed with COVID-19. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help provide information on safe return to community sports during the pandemic.

A 58-year-old man with a history of smoking came to the clinic complaining of abdominal pain and weight loss. On physical examination, the physician felt a mass in the upper abdomen. A CT scan revealed a mass in the pancreas. A biopsy was performed and confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. The patient was scheduled for surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. He has no history of kidney disease, no pacemaker, cochlear implant or neurostimulator, and is not claustrophobic. He agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent form.

A 2-year-old male toddler was brought to the emergency department with a history of cough and difficulty breathing for the past 2 days. His parents noticed that he was not feeding well and had lost his usual playful behavior. The child has no significant past medical history and is up to date on his immunizations. On examination, he was lethargic and had a respiratory rate of 40 breaths per minute with retractions. The oxygen saturation was 88% on room air. The chest x-ray showed bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and the nasopharyngeal swab was positive for Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). The child was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit and started on non-invasive ventilation with BiPAP. He was given nebulized bronchodilators and corticosteroids but showed no significant improvement. His parents consented to participate in a clinical trial of Azithromycin treatment for RSV-induced respiratory failure. The child is randomized to receive either placebo or Azithromycin at a standard or high dose. The parents are informed of the potential side effects of azithromycin, including GI upset and QT prolongation, and are willing to comply with the study protocol.

Patient is a 27-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. She has a history of multiple suicide attempts and self-mutilation episodes over the past year. The patient is currently taking fluoxetine for depression but still experiences urges to self-harm and has difficulty controlling her emotions. The patient is currently living with her parents and is stable enough to participate in the study. The patient is willing to use effective birth control if sexually active and is not participating in any other forms of treatment during the study. The patient has no history of organic mental syndromes, lifetime schizophrenic or bipolar disorders, psychotic disorders, or mental retardation. The patient is not currently receiving treatment for an acute medical illness or other debilitating problem, including substance abuse or anorexia nervosa. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding.

67-year-old male with a history of adenocarcinoma of the prostate, on primary hormonal therapy, now experiencing progressive disease. He has no evidence of metastasis but his PSA levels have risen on successive occasions, and he has measurable disease with lesions greater than 10mm on CT scan. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 70% and no serious intercurrent infections or nonmalignant uncontrolled medical illnesses. He has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy for prostate cancer and has completed any other systemic chemotherapy ≥ 2 years prior to study. The patient has no other currently active malignancy except for nonmelanoma skin cancer. He is not receiving any other hormonal therapy or concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or radiotherapy. The patient has not received prior ketoconazole, aminoglutethimide, or corticosteroids for the treatment of progressive prostate cancer. He has not received prior immunotherapy and is not initiating bisphosphonate therapy within 1 month of starting study therapy. The patient has not received any other concurrent investigational or commercial anticancer agents or therapies.

A 38-year-old female patient presents with a cavity in the upper left second premolar. She has a history of dental anxiety and requires local anesthesia for the procedure. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and seasonal allergies. She is currently taking lisinopril for hypertension and loratadine for allergies. She reports no known allergies to any dental anesthetic agents. She is a non-smoker and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Her blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, pulse rate is 78 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. Her BMI is within normal range. She has no physical or behavioral limitations that would prevent her from completing the study requirements.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who is admitted to the hospital with chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Vital signs are: blood pressure 140/90 mmHg, pulse rate 80 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST segment elevation in the inferior leads, and cardiac biomarkers (troponin) are elevated. Coronary angiography confirms an acute inferior myocardial infarction with a patent infarct-related artery (IRA) and TIMI flow grade = 3. The patient underwent successful revascularization with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with one stent only. His peak CK is 2500 IU, and infarct size is 30% as measured by MRI. The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction is 30%, and he has a regional wall motion score index of 5 out of 16 akinetic segments. He is being considered for the injectable BL-1040 implant clinical trial.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He has undergone at least two prior lines of therapy for his disease, but has relapsed or is refractory to treatment. His serum monoclonal protein level is greater than or equal to 1 gm/dL or his urine monoclonal light chain level is greater than or equal to 200 mg/24 hours. His ECOG performance status is less than or equal to 2 and he has a life expectancy of more than 3 months. He has no significant cardiac or liver disease and his renal function is normal. He is not pregnant or nursing and is willing to use adequate contraception during the trial. He has not received any other investigational agents within 2 weeks prior to the date of enrollment and has recovered completely from the side effects of any previous treatment. He has no history of allergic reactions to compounds of similar chemical composition to P276-00. He is able to understand and willing to sign a written informed consent document.

A 58-year-old female patient has recently been diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. She has no history of chemotherapy or radiotherapy treatment. She reports feeling fatigued and experiencing occasional coughing fits. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and her ANC is greater than or equal to 2.0 x 10^9/L. She has not been treated with any experimental agent in the past 30 days and does not have any symptomatic brain metastases. The patient is not currently enrolled in any other investigational device or drug trial.

56 yo M with a diagnosis of invasive urinary bladder tumor scheduled for elective open radical cystectomy. Baseline serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dl, and the patient has an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status of II. The patient has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medications. No history of allergies to alpha-2 adrenergic agonist or any anesthetic drugs. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and there is no clinically significant neurologic, cardiovascular, respiratory, or hepatic disease.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman from Guatemala who gave birth to a healthy baby girl 5 months ago. She is currently exclusively breastfeeding her daughter and has been doing so for the past 4 months. She has no acute illnesses and is willing to stay in the clinic for breast milk sampling and adhere to all study procedures. She breastfeeds her daughter about 10 times a day and has not experienced any problems with breastfeeding. She has a normal body mass index and mid upper arm circumference. She does not take any supplements except for iron and folic acid. She reports no allergies to milk, milk products, or peanuts. She is interested in participating in the study to learn more about the impact of her diet on her breast milk composition and the effect of a lipid-based nutrient supplement on her breast milk micronutrient levels.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with fraternal twins. She has had a smooth pregnancy thus far with no complications. She has a family history of Down syndrome and is concerned about the possibility of her twins being affected. She has elected to undergo non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) using the MaterniT21 PLUS and/or GENOME Laboratory Developed Test to screen for trisomy 21. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to the research on the clinical performance of NIPT in multiple gestation pregnancies.

A 47-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage IV melanoma after experiencing persistent fatigue, unexplained weight loss, and difficulty breathing. The melanoma had metastasized to her lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. She has not received any chemotherapy or immunotherapy for metastatic melanoma. She has no other significant medical history, and her cardiac function is normal. She takes low-dose aspirin for her mild hypertension. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to receive Avastin (bevacizumab) in combination with fotemustine to treat her advanced melanoma.

Patient is a 28-year-old male who suffered a severe traumatic brain injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident. The patient has a motor Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 4 and has been admitted to the intensive care unit for monitoring and management. The healthcare provider has indicated the need for hyperosmolar therapy for elevated intracranial pressure (ICP). The patient has no history of incarceration or pregnancy and has not been diagnosed with brain death or any life-threatening systemic injuries. The patient is within the age range of 18-89 years and is eligible for the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus according to the criteria of the American Diabetes Association (ADA). He has not received treatment with oral hypoglycemic agents or insulin within the last 12 weeks and has been managing his diabetes with diet and physical exercise. His glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels at the screening visit are between 7.5% and 10.5%. His body mass index (BMI) is between 20 kg/m2 and 40 kg/m2. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He has not participated in any clinical trial protocol within the previous 12 months and does not have any condition that may render him inadequate for study participation.

This is a 62 year-old male who recently underwent a colonoscopy due to changes in bowel habits and was diagnosed with rectal cancer. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis and the patient is being considered for neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. The patient has no significant medical history and is in overall good health. The patient has no contraindications for CECT or MRI/CE-MRI. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent. The patient has no other active cancers and is not pregnant. Fasting serum glucose level is within normal range. The patient is physically able to undergo WB MR-PET.

A 55-year-old male patient with a history of prostate cancer presents with 4 metastases on CT-scan. The primary tumor was treated with surgery and chemoradiotherapy. The patient has functional liver volume of more than 1000cc and a lung diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) of more than 30%. There is no evidence of liver cirrhosis or metastases from another carcinoma. The patient has not undergone any systemic treatment within the last month. The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to explore the potential benefits of stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic cancer.

The patient is a 43-year-old man diagnosed with high-grade soft tissue sarcoma or bone sarcoma. The patient is scheduled to undergo surgery, and his tumor is operable. He has an ECOG performance status of 1, and his hemoglobin, ANC, and platelet count are all within normal limits. His total bilirubin, ALT, and AST are all within normal limits, and his creatinine level is also within normal limits. The patient is not HIV-positive, and he does not have chronic hepatitis B or C. He does not have any serious infections or heart conditions that would prevent him from participating in the trial. Additionally, he does not have a history of bleeding diathesis or coagulopathy. The patient is willing to use effective contraception during and for two weeks after completion of the study therapy. He has given signed informed consent to undergo the neoadjuvant therapy and surgery as part of the trial.

The patient is a 29-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the study risks and benefits. He has no history of drug or alcohol addiction or abuse, and his clinical laboratory test values are within the accepted reference range. He is not currently breastfeeding or pregnant. He has no history of allergic response to leflunomide or related drugs and no history of clinically significant allergies. He has not taken any drug known to induce or inhibit hepatic drug metabolism or donated blood or plasma in the past 30 days. He has not received any investigational drug within the past 30 days and has not taken any prescription medication in the past 14 days, except for postmenopausal women on HRT who may continue their HRT and topical products without systemic absorption. He has no intolerance of direct venipuncture and has not consumed an abnormal diet during the past 28 days. He has not taken any product containing leflunomide within the past 180 days and has not taken any herbal products within the past 7 days.

A 63-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of stage II breast cancer, treated with lumpectomy, radiation therapy, and adjuvant letrozole, presents with osteopenia and is at risk for developing osteoporosis. Her bone density testing revealed a T-score of -2.3 in the lumbar spine and -1.9 in the femoral neck. She has no evidence of recurrent or metastatic breast cancer. She has a history of hypertension, well controlled with lisinopril, and hypercholesterolemia, controlled with atorvastatin. She has no history of dental problems and has no known hypersensitivity to zoledronate or other bisphosphonates, letrozole, calcium, or vitamin D. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of zoledronate in treating her osteopenia and preventing the development of osteoporosis while receiving adjuvant letrozole therapy for breast cancer.

The patient is a woman born between 1914 and 1948 who currently resides in central Sweden. She is interested in participating in a study that aims to investigate the relationship between diet, lifestyle factors, and the risk of breast cancer. She has no history of breast cancer herself but is aware of the importance of early detection through mammography screening. She is willing to complete questionnaires regarding her diet, physical activity, medical history, and lifestyle factors. She understands that her information will be linked to national registries to track incidents of cancer and other diseases as well as causes of death. She is committed to participating in the study for the long term and is willing to complete follow-up questionnaires as needed.

A 45-year-old healthy woman who exercises regularly and has no history of cardiovascular disease is needed for a clinical trial investigating the hemodynamic effects of dry sauna followed by cold water immersion. The study will take place at the Montreal Heart Institute Prevention and Cardiac Rehabilitation center. The subject must have had a recent complete medical evaluation that includes a normal resting ECG and a normal symptom-limited treadmill exercise test. She must not have any cardiac conditions, hypertension, or type I diabetes, and must not be taking any medications that may affect blood pressure.
