The study will involve spending 10 minutes in a dry sauna at 85 degrees Celsius followed by immersion in a cold water bath at a temperature of 5 degrees Celsius for approximately one minute. Blood pressure, ECG, gas exchange, and thoracic impedance will be measured during both conditions. The study aims to determine the safety of this practice and to measure the blood pressure response, heart rate, presence of arrhythmias, cardiac output, and cerebral perfusion during both conditions.

The patient is a 35 year old man who suffered a spinal cord injury resulting in incomplete tetraplegia at the C6 level two months ago. He has partial paralysis in both arms and legs and is currently dependent on his caregivers for daily activities. He has been receiving conventional therapy for his hand muscles but has not seen significant improvement. He is otherwise healthy with no history of neurological disorders, cognitive impairments, or pressure sores. He has no history of epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, or multiple sclerosis. He is able to sit for at least an hour without discomfort and does not experience excessive spasm. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his hand muscle function through BCI-FES therapy.

43-year-old female with a history of HER2/neu+ breast cancer diagnosed 2 years ago, initially treated with a taxane and trastuzumab followed by chemotherapy. She has now progressed and has measurable disease by RECIST. She is currently experiencing fatigue and mild shortness of breath but has an ECOG performance status of 1. Prior MUGA scan or echocardiogram shows left ventricular ejection fraction greater than or equal to 50%. No known history of cardiac disease, stroke, or conduction abnormalities. She has not received radiation therapy in the past 2 weeks, chemotherapy in the past 3 weeks, or noncytoxic investigational agents in the past 4 weeks. She is not pregnant or nursing. She has no history of hypersensitivity or intolerance to apricoxib, lapatinib, capecitabine, 5-FU, sulfonamides, aspirin, or NSAIDs, and no history of severe renal insufficiency or upper GI bleeding, ulceration, or perforation. She has not received prior lapatinib therapy or capecitabine.

A 35-year-old male presents to the dental clinic for a scheduled appointment to have his natural teeth prepped for dental crown placement. The procedure is expected to last at least an hour and is scheduled as the first appointment of the day. The patient has a history of good oral hygiene and has no known allergies to dental materials or medications. He reports no symptoms of COVID-19, such as fever, cough, or shortness of breath. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old man diagnosed with prostate cancer. He underwent several diagnostic tests, including a prostate biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis. The medical team recommended a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy procedure to remove the cancerous prostate gland. The patient has a medical history of hypertension, well-controlled with medication. He has no known history of thrombosis or embolism. The patient is currently taking aspirin daily for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease. He has been instructed to stop taking aspirin 7 days prior to surgery. The patient provided informed consent for the robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy procedure and agreed to participate in the retrospective analysis investigating the risk factors for thrombembolic events after robot-assisted surgery in urology.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chronic back pain due to a herniated disc. The patient has been referred to an orthopedic surgeon for a minimally invasive procedure to relieve his pain. The surgeon has recommended a peripheral nerve block to be performed before the procedure to provide postoperative pain control. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of Computer Assisted Instrument Guidance (CAIG) for peripheral nerve blocks. The patient is able to give written informed consent and meets all other inclusion criteria for the trial.

A 45-year-old male presents to the emergency department complaining of chest pain that started while he was at work. He describes it as a squeezing sensation in the center of his chest that radiates to his left arm. He has no past history of any cardiac disease or risk factors for coronary artery disease such as hypertension, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia. He denies any shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. He has never smoked and does not consume alcohol. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination is unremarkable. EKG shows no ST-segment elevation or depression. Laboratory studies including cardiac enzymes are within normal limits. The patient meets the Diamond-Forrester criteria for low-to-intermediate risk of coronary disease. The patient is willing to undergo stress echocardiography or coronary CT to determine the cause of his chest pain.

The patient is a 62-year-old man diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. He is a former smoker with a 20-pack-year history. He is currently not smoking and is compliant with his medications. He reports shortness of breath with minimal exertion and cough with sputum production. He is able to perform his activities of daily living but has difficulty with more strenuous activities. He has been hospitalized once in the past year due to a COPD exacerbation. He has no other medical conditions and is not taking any medications other than those prescribed for COPD. He is willing to participate in the study and follow the instructions given by the investigators. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent gallstones. She has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She denies any history of significant abdominal surgeries or other medical conditions that would preclude laparoscopic surgery. The patient is able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the study period. The patient has not participated in any other clinical study within the last 60 days prior to the start of this study and is not planning to participate in any other clinical study during the study period.

A 31-year-old woman was diagnosed with dermatomyositis according to the criteria of Bohan and Peter. She has been on prednisone, with a dose of 0.3 mg/kg/day, for the last 2 months. She has not been physically active for the last 6 months due to muscle weakness and fatigue. She does not have a history of neoplasia-associated myositis, overlapping myositis, or diabetes mellitus. She does not smoke and is not taking any lipid-lowering drugs.

Juan is a 26-year-old man with muscular dystrophy. He has been diagnosed with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) when he was 5 years old. He has been using a wheelchair for the past 10 years, and his respiratory function has been gradually worsening. He experiences shortness of breath during physical activity and sometimes while resting. He has no history of cardiac pacemakers or metal implants. He is able to understand and follow test instructions and can report pain and discomfort. He has no relevant concomitant comorbidities or psychiatric disorders. Juan is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help monitor his respiratory function using a wearable device.

A 25 year old, right-handed female presents to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial investigating head repositioning accuracy during experimental neck pain. She reports no current pain in the neck or shoulder area, has not had any prior surgery in the neck or shoulder region, and is not currently pregnant. She does not have any history of drug addiction or self-reported neurologic, musculoskeletal, or mental illnesses. She speaks and understands fluent English and is interested in participating in the study.

The patient is an 8-year-old girl who has been struggling with coordination and movement skills. She has difficulty with tasks such as throwing and catching a ball, and her parents have noticed that she often appears clumsy when playing with other children. She has no known medical conditions or visual impairments. Her teachers have also noticed that she struggles with tasks that require fine motor skills, such as writing and cutting with scissors. She has been previously diagnosed with Developmental Coordination Disorder and has scored below the 5th percentile on the MABC-2. Her parents are interested in participating in the study to see if the gaze training intervention could improve her motor skills and psychosocial outcomes.

The patient is a 72-year-old man who has been experiencing mild cognitive impairment for the past year. The patient has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and has undergone a comprehensive evaluation by a dementia specialist, including general medical and neurological examination, mental status testing, laboratory testing, and structural neuroimaging. The patient meets the Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) for clinical amyloid PET/CT scans. The patient is a Medicare beneficiary and is fluent in both English and Spanish. The patient has had a head MRI and/or CT within the past 24 months, and clinical laboratory assessment within the past 12 months, including a complete blood count (CBC), standard blood chemistry profile, thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), and vitamin B12. The patient is able to tolerate amyloid PET required by the protocol, to be performed at a participating PET facility. The patient is not currently residing in a skilled nursing facility, and has a life expectancy of at least 24 months based on medical co-morbidities. The patient is willing and able to provide consent.

A 62-year-old male patient presents with recent onset of shortness of breath and cough. He has a history of smoking and was diagnosed with stage IV non-squamous NSCLC three months ago. He has already undergone one cycle of chemotherapy but with no significant improvement. CT scan shows multiple lung nodules and pleural effusion. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has a life expectancy of at least three months. The patient has not received any VEGF inhibitors or pemetrexed for NSCLC before, and he has not participated in any clinical trial in the past four weeks. MRI shows a target tumor lesion that can be accurately measured. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent. He has no history of major thrombotic or clinically significant major bleeding event in the past six months and has adequate kidney, liver, and blood clotting function. However, he has a history of hypertension controlled by medical therapy and has undergone major surgery two weeks ago.

The patient is a 60-year-old who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma about a year ago. She underwent an allogeneic progenitor cell transplantation from a related donor who was HLA-compatible (6/6). The patient has achieved only a partial remission and is currently relapsing. The patient is currently feeling well and has a Zubrod Points Scale (PS) score of 1. She has no history of central nervous system disease and has no uncontrolled acute or chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). She is willing and able to sign an informed consent form.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme after experiencing frequent headaches and seizures. He underwent surgery at UCLA and had more than 70% of his tumor mass removed. Pathological diagnosis confirmed the presence of malignant glioma (WHO Grade IV). He is currently receiving standard treatment including radiotherapy. He has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. He has no history of autoimmune disorder, organ allografts, or sensitivity to the components of the dendritic cell vaccine. He is HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and syphilis serology negative. He is not currently taking any steroid medication and has no acute infections. He is willing to use effective contraception as he is fertile.

45 year old male with a history of hydrocephalus and ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement at the age of 12. The patient has been experiencing headaches, blurred vision, and difficulty with balance over the past few months. MRI of the brain shows significant ventriculomegaly and the patient is scheduled for a shunt revision surgery. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy.

A 32 year old male veteran of OEF/OIF/OND visited the clinic for a compensation examination due to back pain. He reported a peak pain of 6 out of 10 in the last 28 days. He has been treating with ibuprofen and naproxen, but he has not experienced any relief. He also reported having a history of risky alcohol use, drinking more than 14 drinks per week on average. The patient has no physiological dependence on alcohol or drugs. He is able to participate in the study both physically and psychologically and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who was involved in a motorcycle accident and suffered severe traumatic brain injury. He was brought to the hospital where he was diagnosed with an intracranial hemorrhage and underwent surgical intervention to relieve pressure on the brain. He is currently in the intensive care unit and is being managed with mechanical ventilation and sedation. On examination, the patient is unresponsive to painful stimuli, has a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 5, and is displaying signs of increased intracranial pressure. His vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute. He has no history of chronic cardiac or renal failure and is not allergic to any of the treatments being used in the study.

Patient is a 5-year-old boy from Egypt who was admitted to Assuit University Pediatric Hospital with a history of cough and fever for the past week. On physical examination, he was found to have decreased breath sounds on the left side of his chest. A chest X-ray showed a left-sided pleural effusion. The patient was diagnosed with parapneumonic effusion and underwent thoracentesis, which confirmed the diagnosis. The pleural fluid analysis showed exudative fluid with a C-reactive protein level of 90 mg/L. The patient was started on appropriate antibiotics and responded well to treatment. He will be followed up for one year to evaluate the outcome of the effusion.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis in the left hip joint. The patient has been experiencing pain and difficulty walking, which has significantly impacted his quality of life. After consultation with his orthopedic surgeon, it has been decided that the patient will undergo total hip replacement surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication for this condition, but there are no other significant medical issues. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits, and the physical examination reveals no abnormalities except for tenderness and limited range of motion in the left hip joint. Laboratory results are within normal ranges. The patient is deemed eligible for the study and has provided informed consent to participate. The patient will be randomized to either the conventional lung protective group or the group that receives mechanical ventilation based on driving pressure. The patient's intraoperative hemodynamic and respiratory parameters will be monitored, and fluids will be administered according to PVI values. The patient will be closely monitored for any pulmonary complications during and after the surgery. The investigators will evaluate the patient's postoperative mechanical ventilation, ICU stay, and discharge times as secondary outcome parameters.

The patient is a 28-year-old female diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes for the past 8 years. She has been using insulin pump therapy for the past 4 years with a stable basal rate for the past 2 weeks. Her latest HbA1c was 7.3% and her BMI is 28. She regularly practices physical activity, including jogging and cycling for at least 30 minutes, at least 3 times a week. She has no history of severe hypoglycemia or other complications related to diabetes. She is not pregnant and is not currently under any legal guardianship. She has agreed to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old male farmer from a rural area of Peru. He reports a 2-month history of a non-healing ulcer on his right arm that has gradually increased in size and is now approximately 2 cm in diameter. He reports no systemic symptoms such as fever, chills, or weight loss. The lesion is located on the dorsal aspect of the forearm and is primarily ulcerative with some verrucous changes at the periphery. There is no evidence of cellulitis. The patient is generally healthy and gives informed consent to participate in the study. The investigator determines that the lesion is suitable for collecting samples by dental broach and scraping. The patient has not received treatment for leishmaniasis in the past 2 months and there is no evidence of manipulation of the lesion.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic vulvar pain for the past 2 years. She was diagnosed with vulvodynia by a gynecologist and has been receiving multidisciplinary treatment for the last 3 months, including topical creams, pelvic floor physical therapy, and cognitive-behavioral therapy. Despite these interventions, she still experiences pain during intercourse and everyday activities, which has significantly affected her quality of life. She has no history of genital infections, inflammatory vulvar disease, or neoplastic vulvar disease. She has not experienced any recent vulvar trauma or pudendal neuralgia. She is not pregnant and has not given birth in the past 6 months. She does not have a history of epilepsy or major neurologic or psychiatric morbidity, and she does not have any active systemic infections or autoimmune disorders. She has not received previous treatment with ionizing radiation in the area to be treated and does not have a history of wound healing disorders or fever. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the potential benefits of vulvovaginal laser therapy in reducing her vulvar pain and improving her sexual health and quality of life.

Sarah is a 28-year-old female who was diagnosed with Goodpasture's disease (GP) three months ago. She presented with shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema, and was found to have elevated creatinine levels and hematuria. She was started on pulse-methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, and intravenous cyclophosphamide (CYC) combined with plasma exchange (PLEX) therapy. Despite treatment, her renal function continued to deteriorate, and she is now considering other treatment options. She has an eGFR of 10 ml/min/1.73 m2 and has been on dialysis for the last two weeks. Her urine analysis revealed persistent hematuria. Sarah tested positive for anti-GBM antibodies by ELISA, and her antibody levels are considered toxic by the investigator. She is in good general health otherwise and is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. She has no history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or stroke. She is not pregnant and is using highly effective contraception. She has no ongoing bacterial or viral infections and has not received any investigational drugs in the last 30 days.

A 28-year-old male presents with Inherited Erythromelalgia and has been experiencing moderate pain (4/10) for the past year. He is generally healthy apart from his pain and has not sought professional psychological support for dealing with IEM. He has not been treated for depression within the last 6 months. He takes no prescription medications but occasionally takes ibuprofen for his pain. He is willing to stop using his usual pain medications for 9 days. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses adequate contraception. He does not have HIV, Hepatitis B or C. He does not have a history of alcoholism or substance abuse. He is willing to comply with all dietary and activity restrictions during the study.

Pt is a 50yo M with a recent diagnosis of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) following an episode of palpitations and shortness of breath. He has no significant medical history, and his EKG shows AF with a rapid ventricular rate. He underwent a thorough cardiovascular evaluation, which did not reveal any structural heart disease. He is currently on rate control medication and has been advised to consider rhythm control therapy. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of catheter ablation versus anti-arrhythmic drug therapy for paroxysmal AF. He meets all eligibility criteria and is willing to participate in the study. He will be implanted with an implantable loop recorder and will be followed every three months.

A 65 yo F with a history of uncomplicated cataracts has been scheduled for phacoemulsification and posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation. She has no history of prior intraocular procedures or any eye diseases such as uveitis, glaucoma, or diabetic retinopathy. She has no systemic autoimmune diseases and is not allergic to corticosteroids or any component of the study medications. She has not used corticosteroids, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), or immunomodulating agents within 3 months prior to surgery. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 6-month-old baby girl who was born at full term and is in good health. She is currently wearing disposable diapers and has at least two diaper changes per day, with an additional change during the night. Her parents are educated on the importance of good hygiene and diaper rash prevention. The baby has not had any previous episodes of diaper rash. She has a skin phototype of II according to the Fitzpatrick scale. She is not currently on any medications and does not have any known allergies. Her parents have given their written informed consent for her participation in this clinical trial.

Sophia is a 35-year-old female who was diagnosed with Hodgkin's Lymphoma 2 years ago. She received chemotherapy and radiation therapy as a part of her initial treatment, but unfortunately, her disease has returned. Her PET scan shows that the cancer cells are positive for Epstein Barr Virus (EBV). The investigators are conducting a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of C7R-EBV T cells for the treatment of EBV-positive lymphoma. Sophia meets the eligibility criteria for the study as she has EBV-positive Hodgkin's Lymphoma that has relapsed after initial treatment. She weighs more than 10 kg, has a life expectancy of more than 6 weeks, and her bilirubin, AST, creatinine, and Hgb levels are within the acceptable range. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and she does not have an active and uncontrolled bacterial, viral, or fungal infection. She is willing to provide informed consent for the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment. Sophia will undergo a series of standard medical tests before treatment, including a physical exam, blood tests, and imaging studies to measure the tumor. She will then receive C7R-EBV T cells and may also receive standard chemotherapy medicines to make space in the blood for the T cells to grow after receiving them. The investigators will monitor Sophia for side effects and follow up with her for 15 years to ensure that there are no long-term side effects of gene transfer. Sophia is willing to participate in the study and hopes that this treatment will help her overcome her cancer.

A 34-year-old woman has been experiencing symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) for the past year. She has abdominal pain and discomfort, bloating, and diarrhea that has been affecting her daily activities. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. She works as an office manager and has a busy lifestyle. She has tried various diets and elimination plans but has not found any relief. She is interested in exploring alternative approaches to manage her IBS symptoms and is willing to try nutritional counseling. She has no known allergies or food intolerances. She is married with two children and enjoys cooking and trying new recipes.

The patient is a 52-year-old male diagnosed with recurrent metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. The patient has previously undergone surgical resection with curative intent but has experienced recurrence of the disease. The lesion is amenable to biopsy and is capable of yielding at least 4 biopsy cores. The patient is 18 years or older and able to provide and sign informed consent. The patient does not have cognitive impairment prohibitive to providing informed consent and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial aimed at developing patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) from fresh, real-time biopsies to test sensitivity to Ontario funded chemotherapeutic regimens. The patient understands that PDX drug testing results will be provided to the treating medical oncologist to guide care at the oncologist's discretion, and hopes for improved chemotherapy responses with this strategy.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who has been suffering from severe knee pain for several years. He has been diagnosed with osteoarthritis and has tried various non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy and pain medication, but without significant improvement. He is now considering total knee arthroplasty as a treatment option. He has no history of knee surgery or significant trauma to the knee. He is generally healthy, with no major medical conditions, and is not taking any medications that would interfere with surgery. He has good range of motion in his knee, but experiences pain with activities such as walking, standing, and climbing stairs. He is able to perform activities of daily living, but with some difficulty. He is retired and lives with his spouse. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help determine which prosthesis is better in total knee arthroplasty.

A 54-year-old male patient was diagnosed with inoperable gastric cancer by gastroscopy and biopsy. He had a history of chronic gastric pain and indigestion for several months before the diagnosis. The patient underwent a CT scan, which revealed a large tumor in the stomach with no evidence of distant metastasis. He received first-line chemotherapy with cisplatin and fluorouracil (5-Fu) for six cycles, but the tumor progressed. He was referred to our clinic for further treatment. The performance status of the patient is 80, and he has no significant comorbidities. He has no history of allergy to any drugs, including 5-Fu. His blood counts are within normal limits, and his liver and kidney function tests are normal. He has no history of CNS metastasis, epilepsy, or psychiatric disorders. He is not participating in any other clinical trials, and he is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 6-year-old Caucasian boy presented with a history of recurrent itchy rashes on his skin, which he has been experiencing since he was 3 years old. The rashes are mostly on his hands, feet, and face, and sometimes spread to other parts of the body. The boy's parents reported that the rashes were sometimes accompanied by dryness, scaling, and crusting of the skin. The boy's medical history was unremarkable, and he was not taking any medications. There was no family history of atopy or allergic diseases. Physical examination showed erythematous, scaly, and excoriated patches on the boy's hands, feet, and face. The patches were pruritic and some had vesicles, papules, and crusts. The boy's vital signs were within normal limits. The diagnosis of atopic dermatitis was confirmed by the criteria of Hanifin and Rajka. The boy was enrolled in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of 0.3% and 1% OPA-15406 ointment, which will be applied twice daily for 4 weeks. The boy did not have an active viral skin infection or a current or history of malignancy, and was therefore eligible to participate in the study.

Due to recurrent rectal bleeding and a positive fecal occult blood test, the patient, a 55-year-old male, was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the rectum. The tumor was located approximately 5 cm from the anal verge and preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) suggested a T2N0 lesion without distant metastasis. The patient had no history of abdominal or pelvic surgery, and his American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2. After discussing the potential benefits and risks of the surgical options with the surgeon, the patient decided to undergo low anterior resection for rectal cancer using the Micro Hand S robot or da Vinci robot. The patient provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 45-year-old male who is scheduled for an upcoming MRI scan to investigate his chronic lower back pain. The patient has a history of anxiety and is concerned about the upcoming procedure due to his claustrophobia. The patient has no known cardiac or respiratory conditions and is in good general health. He has given his consent to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the MRI-compatible vital signs sensor system that will monitor his respiratory and heart rate during the MRI scan. The patient will complete the State Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) questionnaire before and after the MRI scan to assess his anxiety level. The fiber-optic sensor system will be placed under the patient's back to monitor his vital signs without interfering with the quality of the imaging. The patient will be closely monitored throughout the procedure to ensure his safety and comfort. The results of this clinical trial will help to determine the feasibility of using the fiber-optic sensor system in routine MRI procedures to monitor patient anxiety levels.

68-year-old male presented to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain, jaundice, and loss of appetite. He had a history of smoking and alcoholism. On physical examination, the patient appeared jaundiced and had mild epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding. Laboratory studies showed elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the head of the pancreas and dilated intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts, suggestive of malignant biliary obstruction (MBO). The patient was deemed eligible for percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage (PTBD) and consented to participate in the clinical trial investigating the bile etiology, proteomics, and metabonomics of MBO with biliary infection. Bile, blood, and urine samples were collected for culture, susceptibility testing, and biomarker analysis. The patient was closely monitored for any adverse events related to the PTBD procedure and the trial interventions.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been experiencing blurred vision in her left eye for the past 6 months. She was diagnosed with branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) by an ophthalmologist based on a comprehensive eye examination that included fluorescein angiography and optical coherence tomography (OCT). The patient has chronic macular edema secondary to BRVO, which has been present for over 3 months. At baseline, her visual acuity in the study eye is equivalent to 20/50 on an ETDRS chart measured at 4 meters. Her central macular thickness is measured to be greater than 225 μm by OCT. She has no other relevant ocular diseases such as uveitis and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is able to understand the nature and consequences of the clinical trial and has provided informed consent. She has no history of hypersensitivity to ranibizumab or any drugs with similar chemical structure. Additionally, she does not have arterial hypertension refractory to medical treatment. The patient is interested in participating in the RABAMES study to compare the functional and anatomic outcomes of chronic macular edema secondary to BRVO treated with argon laser photocoagulation versus intravitreal ranibizumab versus a combination of both.

Patient B is a 45-year-old male who presented to the hospital with sudden onset of severe chest pain that radiated to his back. The pain started while he was at rest and was associated with shortness of breath, nausea, and vomiting. He has a history of high blood pressure and smoking for the past 20 years. He had never been diagnosed with any heart or lung condition before. Upon arrival, his blood pressure was 170/100 mmHg, heart rate was 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate was 24 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation was 93% on room air. CT scan of the chest revealed a Type B aortic dissection with a maximum diameter of 4.5 cm. Laboratory tests showed elevated levels of troponin I and D-dimer. The patient was stabilized with intravenous medications to control his blood pressure and started on anticoagulation therapy. He is interested in participating in the Zenith® Dissection Clinical Trial to explore the possibility of endovascular treatment for his condition.

32-year-old pregnant woman diagnosed with asthma in her first trimester, with a history of moderate asthma symptoms. She has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing. Her asthma is currently managed with a combination of a short-acting beta-agonist and an inhaled corticosteroid. She is currently in her second trimester and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of asthma medications during pregnancy. She has no other significant medical history and is receiving regular prenatal care.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis. He has been taking 10mg/kg rifampicin daily for the past 2 months as part of his treatment regimen. He has a body weight of 70kg and has demonstrated good treatment compliance with no adverse effects. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written, informed consent. He has no known history of drug or alcohol abuse and is not receiving antiretroviral therapy or any other medication that could potentially affect the PK of rifampicin and/or the probe drugs. He is non-pregnant and non-lactating. He has no history of Hepatitis B or C and has no clinically relevant metabolic, gastrointestinal, or other abnormalities that could alter the PK of rifampicin and/or the probe drugs. He has normal ECG findings and normal ALT and AST levels. He does not have any known allergies to the phenotyping probe drugs that will be used in the study.

This is a 50-year-old female who has been struggling with dental issues for several years. She has lost multiple teeth due to decay and gum disease and has been considering dental implants as a replacement option. She has a good oral hygiene routine and is a non-smoker. She has no active infections or inflammation in the areas intended for implant placement. She is physically able to tolerate conventional surgical and restorative procedures. She has agreed to be evaluated for each study visit, especially the yearly follow-up visit. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially benefit from the Certain Prevail implant system and contribute to advancing dental implant technology.

13 yo M with Type 1 diabetes diagnosed 2 years ago, currently using Medtronic insulin pump and testing blood glucose 6-7 times per day. Hemoglobin A1c at baseline visit was 8.5%. The patient and family have a smartphone and are able to upload data from devices such as meter, pump, and sensor. No diagnosis of a mental health disorder and both parent and child are fluent in English. Past Medical History: - Type 1 diabetes - No other significant medical history

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with fever, chills, and generalized weakness. She reports feeling unwell for the past few days and her symptoms have progressively worsened. She denies any recent travel or sick contacts. Her medical history is significant for hypertension and she takes medication to control it. On physical examination, she is febrile and tachycardic. Blood tests show elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein. She is suspected to have a bacterial infection and is admitted to the hospital for further management. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is approached for consent to participate in the clinical trial.

35-year-old female who was diagnosed with COVID-19 infection 4 months ago with mild symptoms including fever, cough, and fatigue. She was not hospitalized and recovered from the acute phase of the infection. However, she is still experiencing persistent symptoms including shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue. She reports difficulty in performing daily activities and has missed work due to these symptoms. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She has no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. She is interested in participating in this study to help further our understanding of the long-term effects of COVID-19.

A 32-year-old woman who is 34 weeks pregnant was diagnosed with HIV during her prenatal care. She has no symptoms of AIDS and otherwise enjoys good health. She has not received any antiretroviral therapy during the current pregnancy prior to labor and delivery. The medical staff will provide her with intravenous or oral ZDV during labor to prevent transmission to her baby. She has agreed to participate in a clinical trial to help prevent transmission of the virus to her baby. Her baby will be enrolled in the trial if it is born without complications and is delivered within the next 48 hours. If eligible, the baby will be randomized to one of three treatment arms: Arm A- ZDV, Arm B- ZDV plus nevirapine, and Arm C- ZDV plus nelfinavir and lamivudine. The baby will have a medical history and physical exam, DNA testing, CBC and liver function tests, cells for long-term storage and RNA/CD4/CD8 testing if HIV positive. The mother will also be evaluated during the delivery visit and the baby will have a 1-week, 2-week, 4-week, 3-month and a final 6-month visit. The initial study drug doses will be given to the baby while in the hospital, and the mother will administer the infant's remaining treatment doses at home depending on ability.

An 80-year-old woman who lives alone in Zurich, Switzerland came to the clinic with complaints of difficulty in walking and maintaining balance. She has a history of falls in the past year, with the most recent one resulting in a fracture of her right hip. She is currently using a walker to aid in her mobility. She has also noticed a decline in her memory and has difficulty in performing simple tasks such as cooking and cleaning. She has no history of alcoholism or epileptic seizures. She has undergone a hip replacement surgery in the past but has no other prosthetic implants. Her joint diseases are well-controlled with medication.

A 47-year-old woman with a history of melanoma presents with advanced disease after treatment with all standard therapies. The disease has progressed, and there are no appropriate available therapies. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has measurable disease by RECIST 1.1. She has available adequate archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded block(s)/slides containing tumor or adequate pre-dose fresh tumor biopsy tissue. She has not received any anticancer therapies within the past 2 weeks, except for LHRH analogue therapy for adenocarcinoma of the prostate. She has not received any CTLA4 antibody within the past 6 weeks or nivolumab or any PDL1 or PDL2-directed antibody within the past 4 weeks. She has not received pembrolizumab within the past 4 - 12 weeks. She has not had any life-threatening (Grade 4) immune-mediated AE related to prior immunotherapy. She has recovered from any immune-related toxicity from prior cancer therapy to ≤ Grade 1, except if previous immune-related endocrinopathy is medically managed with hormone replacement therapy only. She has recovered from any other toxicity (other than immune-related toxicity) related to previous anticancer treatment to ≤ Grade 2. She does not have active known or suspected autoimmune disease. She does not have any condition requiring systemic treatment with corticosteroids, prednisone equivalents, or other immunosuppressive medications within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug (except that inhaled or topical corticosteroids or brief courses of corticosteroids given for prophylaxis of contrast dye allergic response are permitted).

Pt is a 40-year-old male scheduled for an elective surgery under general anesthesia. The patient has no known history of neurological or psychiatric diseases and has provided written informed consent. The surgery does not involve the head. The patient is not pregnant nor planning for breeding. The patient is eligible to participate in the trial.

8-year-old male with a history of recurrent cold sores presents with current symptoms of a cold sore. He has had at least two episodes of cold sores in the last year, with each episode lasting for approximately 7-10 days. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history or allergies. The patient and their parents are willing to comply with all requirements of the study and have provided informed consent. The patient has not used any other topical medications, over-the-counter products, or cosmetic products in or around the oral area during the current recurrence. The patient has not mechanically disrupted the area affected by the cold sore. The patient is not currently taking any immunomodulatory agents and has no significant skin conditions in the area affected by the cold sore. The patient is not pregnant or nursing.

32 year-old pregnant woman with a history of gestational diabetes and hypertension. She is currently at 38 weeks of gestation and scheduled for a caesarean section. The patient has a BMI of 28 and a height of 165 cm. She has no history of neurological symptoms or contraindications to neuraxial techniques. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and will be randomly assigned to either receive spinal prilocaine with sufentanyl or spinal bupivacaine with sufentanyl. Vital parameters will be monitored closely throughout the procedure and postoperative follow-up will be conducted to assess for any postoperative symptoms.

Pt is a 30yo F, generally healthy, who is interested in participating in a clinical trial evaluating the antibody response of influenza vaccination following exposure to bimekizumab. The patient has not received any vaccinations within the past year and has not had the influenza vaccine within the past 2 years. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and agrees to use a medically accepted form of birth control during the study. The patient weighs 60 kg and has a BMI of 23 kg/m2. She has no known hypersensitivity to any excipients of bimekizumab or history of hypersensitivity to the influenza vaccine. The patient is not currently institutionalized or diagnosed with a mental health condition that would impede her from providing voluntary informed consent. She has no history of gastrointestinal ulceration or other gastrointestinal disease, such as inflammatory bowel disease, and is not currently experiencing an active infection. The patient is negative for viral hepatitis B or C, HIV infection, or HTLV-1.

The patient is a 12-year-old boy with cerebral palsy, who has been experiencing significant spasticity in his lower limbs for the past few years. Despite multiple attempts with oral medication, the spasticity has been resistant to treatment and has significantly impacted his quality of life, making it difficult for him to walk and engage in everyday activities. The patient and his family have been informed about the potential benefits and risks of intrathecal administration of Baclofen and have given their informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including sufficient body weight and no hypersensitivity to oral Baclofen. The patient will be evaluated using standardized and internationally accepted scales to assess the effect of the treatment on his spasticity.

A 12-year-old male with Down syndrome (DS) and a weight of 30 kg is brought to the clinic by his parents. The patient's Vineland-II Adaptive Behavior Scales (VABS-II)/Parent/Caregiver Rating Form (PCRF) standard composite score is greater than 55. The patient has been diagnosed with DS by chromosomal analysis (karyotyping) and has not been treated with any cholinesterase inhibitors in the past 3 months. The patient is a native English speaker and is verbal, able to communicate most of the time. The patient has a parent who will act as a reliable informant and complete the VABS-II/PCRF accurately. The patient is in good general health with no clinically significant or unstable medical conditions. The patient has stable Type II diabetes and is monitored regularly to ensure adequate glucose control. The patient has no history of seizure disorder within the past 6 months and is independent in ambulation with the aid of a walker. The patient has not been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder or any other primary psychiatric diagnosis other than DS. The patient and his parents agree to complete all procedures scheduled during the study, including all efficacy and safety parameters.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis C infection. He presents with recurrent episodes of variceal bleeding and has undergone multiple endoscopic treatments with band ligation and sclerotherapy. His most recent endoscopy showed the presence of large varices with high-risk stigmata for bleeding. He is currently on beta-blocker therapy for prophylaxis of variceal bleeding. On physical examination, he has mild ascites and splenomegaly. His laboratory tests show low platelet count, elevated bilirubin and liver enzymes, and prolonged prothrombin time. Imaging studies confirm the presence of cirrhosis and a patent portal vein. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of real-time 3D roadmap guidance during TIPS creation.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who is scheduled for thoracic surgery. He has no significant past medical history and is classified as ASA I. He does not smoke and has a normal BMI. His lung function tests are within normal limits. He has no history of heart failure or any other significant cardiac conditions. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

47-year-old male with 15% total body surface area deep dermal burns and 12% total body surface area post-burn raw area. The patient was admitted to the burn unit after a fire accident in his garage. The burns were caused by a propane heater explosion. The patient had surgical debridement of his deep dermal burns and is in need of epidermal replacement. The patient does not have any pre-existing local or systemic bacterial infections and has no pre-existing medical conditions that would interfere with wound healing. The patient has given informed consent to participate in the study comparing non-cultured autologous keratinocyte suspension versus traditional split skin graft for burn wounds treatment.

This is a 28 year old female who is currently pregnant with her second child. She was diagnosed with COVID-19 two weeks ago and has since tested positive for the virus through a nasopharyngeal swab. She has been experiencing mild symptoms such as a dry cough, fever, and fatigue. The patient has been scheduled for a cesarean section due to a previous low transverse incision and is now eligible for this clinical trial. She has no known allergies and has not had any previous major medical conditions. The patient is aware of the risks associated with COVID-19 and has given her informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who attends a school offering compulsory secondary education. She spends most of her free time using her mobile phone and other electronic devices. She is interested in physical activity, but she lacks motivation and feels that she does not have enough time to practice sports. She has no history of any disease or surgical operation that would prevent her from participating in physical tests or the follow-up of the established intervention, and she has access to a mobile device that allows access to the technological sports applications used in the intervention. She is willing to participate in the study and complete required questionnaires and tests.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been wearing complete dentures for the past 10 years. She has good oral hygiene and is in good general health, with no medical conditions that could complicate the surgical phase or affect osseointegration. She has been experiencing some discomfort and difficulty with her current dentures, particularly when eating and speaking. She has adequate bone height for implants, with a minimum length of bone of 10mm and a minimum diameter of bone of 5mm. She has enough inter-arch space for a screw-retained prosthesis. She does not have any intra-oral pathological conditions, but she does have a slightly flappy ridge. She does not have any parafunctional habits. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to improve her dental function and overall satisfaction with her dentures.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing pain in his right knee for the past six months. He reports that the pain began after he twisted his knee while playing soccer. The pain is located in the medial aspect of the knee joint and is exacerbated by physical activity such as running, squatting, or climbing stairs. He has no history of knee surgery, and his contralateral knee is healthy with no pain or functional limitation. Physical examination reveals tenderness to palpation over the medial joint line and a positive McMurray test. MRI confirms the presence of a chronic meniscal tear. He is generally healthy with no known allergies or substance abuse. His BMI is 28. He is interested in participating in the trial to evaluate the effects of ACP injection following partial meniscectomy.

John is a 35 year old male who was admitted to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. He was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis which is predicted to be severe, based on the high levels of pancreatic enzymes in his blood. He has a history of occasional alcohol consumption and smoking 10 cigarettes per day. He has no allergies to any medications, and his medical history is otherwise unremarkable. His physical examination revealed a tender abdomen with a positive Cullen's sign. His laboratory studies were consistent with pancreatitis. John is able to provide informed consent and is over 17 years of age. He has no history of seizure disorder or demyelinating disease and is not currently receiving any immunosuppressive therapy. He is not nursing or pregnant. His echocardiogram was normal and he has no history of tuberculosis. He is willing to participate in the study and will be monitored for up to four months after participation.

54 yo F with a recent diagnosis of stage III colorectal cancer. She has recently started on a chemotherapy regimen of 5-fluorouracil and leucovorin. She presents to the oncology clinic with a chief complaint of persistent diarrhea, which is interfering with her daily activities. She reports having 5-6 loose stools per day, which are watery in consistency. She has tried over-the-counter medications such as loperamide but has not found any relief. She is generally healthy and does not have any significant medical history. On examination, she appears dehydrated and has mild abdominal tenderness. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the best treatment for her chemotherapy-related diarrhea.

A 50-year-old woman with a history of Raynaud's phenomenon presented with skin thickening in her hands and face, accompanied by difficulty swallowing and shortness of breath. She was diagnosed with systemic scleroderma and interstitial lung disease (ILD) based on clinical findings, pulmonary function tests, and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). She has been on prednisone 10 mg daily for the past 3 months. She has no history of bleeding disorders or thromboembolic events. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her past medical history is remarkable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medications. She has no known allergies to any medication. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and suitability of dabigatran etexilate to inhibit thrombin in scleroderma. She understands the potential benefits and risks of the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

38-year-old female presents to the clinic with a red rash on her thigh that has been expanding over the past few days. The rash is approximately 6 cm in diameter and is accompanied by flu-like symptoms, including fatigue, headache, and muscle aches. The patient reports a tick bite in the same area a few weeks prior. She has no known history of Lyme disease and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has no known immunocompromised conditions and has not had a serious adverse reaction to a beta-lactam or tetracycline drug in the past. She has not received any antibiotics with known anti-borrelial activity within the past 10 days. The patient does not have multiple erythema migrans lesions or any extracutaneous manifestation of Lyme disease.

A 56-year-old woman came to the clinic with complaints of forgetfulness and difficulty in performing daily activities. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. She also reports that she has trouble finding words and frequently loses her train of thought in the middle of a conversation. She has no history of significant head injury, stroke, or seizures. She is a retired teacher and has a family history of Alzheimer's disease; her mother was diagnosed with the disease in her late 70s. She reports no history of psychiatric disorders. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is currently taking donepezil for her symptoms, which has been effective in slowing down the progression of the disease. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of lecanemab in participants with early Alzheimer's disease. She understands that she will be required to visit the clinic for the infusion and will also have to undergo MRI scans. She has a study partner who is willing to provide follow-up information throughout the course of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic low back pain for the past year. She reports the pain as a dull ache that radiates to her left leg, making it difficult for her to stand or walk for long periods of time. She has tried various treatments such as physical therapy and pain medications, but with little success. She is currently not taking any psychotropic medications and has no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders. She has normal visual acuity and is affiliated with social security. She has not had any recent trauma or surgery and is able to comprehend French well. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help further understand the body schema alterations associated with musculoskeletal disorders.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with locally advanced gastric cancer. He has not received any prior anti-tumor therapy and is scheduled for neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery. He has an ECOG physical status score of 1 and has a pathologically confirmed CT3/CT4N+M0 adenocarcinoma of the gastroesophageal junction. He has a measurable lesion according to RECIST1.1 and is expected to survive more than 3 months. His blood routine, liver function, renal function, and coagulation function are all within normal limits. He has no history of autoimmune diseases or pulmonary fibrosis, and no active infections requiring systematic treatment. He has not received any live virus vaccines within the past 4 weeks and is not lactating or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study. The investigator deems him suitable for the study and he has voluntarily signed the written informed consent.

32-year-old male diagnosed with ADHD and currently taking immediate release methylphenidate (MPH IR) three times a day. He has been on stable treatment for the past 4 weeks and has shown improvement in his symptoms. He is satisfied with his current treatment and tolerates it well. He does not have a history of Tourette's syndrome, Autism, seizures, or recent drug or alcohol dependence. He has mild asthma and allergies, acid reflux syndrome, and hypercholesterolemia. He has a past history of depression and anxiety disorder but has been free of both for more than 6 months, as confirmed by a structured diagnostic interview and clinical exam. He is currently taking a stable medication regimen for anxiety and depression. He does not have any metabolic, neurological, hepatic, renal, cardiovascular, hematological, opthalmic, or endocrine disease, and all his baseline laboratory values are within normal range. He is fluent in English and has an IQ above 70. He has never been pregnant nor is currently lactating.

The patient is a 53-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and is currently undergoing adjuvant systemic chemotherapy. She has received 4 cycles of chemotherapy with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide, and she is scheduled for 4 more cycles with paclitaxel. The patient has reported experiencing tingling and numbness in her hands and feet, which are affecting her daily activities and causing discomfort. She has no history of diabetes or neurological diseases that may affect the conductivity of her nerves. The patient has no history of smoking, alcohol abuse, or illicit drug use. She is able to walk independently and has no history of falls. The patient has no history of musculoskeletal, endocrine, psychiatric, hematologic, or cardiovascular diseases. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. The patient's grip strength and fine motor skills will be assessed before and after chemotherapy, along with sensory tests using the Semmens-Weinstein Monofilament Test (SWMT). Additionally, the patient will fill out quality of life scales, including the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC-QLQ-C30) and the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Breast (FACT-B+).

The patient is a 57-year-old male who underwent coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery 8 months ago due to a history of coronary artery disease. The patient reports feeling depressed and anxious since the surgery, and is experiencing difficulty sleeping and concentrating. He has no history of severe cognitive impairment, psychiatric comorbidity, or debilitating illness other than coronary disease. The patient is currently taking sertraline for depression, but reports little improvement in his symptoms. He is interested in participating in the trial to explore alternative treatment options. The patient is a retired accountant and lives with his wife. He reports having a supportive social network, but feels isolated due to his recent health issues. The patient is willing to commit to the study's 12-week treatment period and follow-up assessments. His baseline depression, anxiety, and health-related quality of life will be assessed at the beginning of the study.

A 52-year-old male with a history of metastatic lung cancer complains of severe headaches, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating for the past 2 weeks. He was diagnosed with lung cancer 6 months ago and completed radiation therapy and chemotherapy 3 months ago. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking amlodipine, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He quit smoking 5 years ago but admits to using smokeless tobacco occasionally. His family history is negative for any neurological problems. His performance status is 80. He is willing to undergo a tumor resection or biopsy to differentiate between tumor progression versus treatment-induced effects following radiation therapy and/or chemotherapy. His lab work shows a normal complete blood count, blood chemistry, and renal function test. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He agrees to use adequate contraception. He has no cardiac or neurological symptoms.

30-year-old male, non-smoker, with no known medical conditions and no regular medications, is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of fructans on fermentation in the colon and transit. He is able to give informed consent and is willing to abstain from smoking for the duration of the study. He reports no history of gastrointestinal disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease, coeliac disease, pancreatitis, gallstone disease, diverticulitis, or cancer of the gastrointestinal tract. He has not undergone any previous resection of any part of the gastrointestinal tract other than appendix or gallbladder, and does not have an intestinal stoma. He reports no medical conditions that would compromise participation in the study, such as diabetes mellitus or respiratory disease that would limit his ability to lie in the scanner. He does not have any contraindications for MRI scanning, such as metallic implants or pacemakers. He reports no alcohol dependence, and is willing to abstain from drugs known to alter GI motility during or in the 2 weeks prior to the test, with the exception of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and low dose tricyclic antidepressants. He has not undergone any antibiotic or probiotic treatment in the past 4 weeks. He is able to lie flat and does not exceed scanner limits of weight <120kg. He has a good understanding of English language and is not participating in night shift work the week prior to the study day. He reports no strenuous exercise greater than 10 hours per week, and has not participated in any medical trials for the past 3 months. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has no cognitive dysfunction or chaotic lifestyle related to substance abuse.

A 55-year-old woman with advanced ovarian cancer was referred to the trial after failing standard chemotherapy. She has a performance status of 1 and an estimated life expectancy of more than 3 months. Her medical history includes hypertension that is well-controlled with medication. She is not currently taking any immunosuppressive or glucocorticoid medications. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use an adequate method of contraception throughout the study and for at least 6 months after the study is complete. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. Her organ function is normal, and she has no other active malignancies or autoimmune diseases. She has not received programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) or programmed cell death protein ligand (PD-L1) antibody treatment and has not had any > 3 degree immune-related adverse events during any previous immunotherapy. She has not had a severe hypersensitivity reaction to monoclonal antibody drugs in the past. She has not had spinal cord compression, cancer meningitis, or new onset of central nervous system metastasis. She has no hypothyroidism over 2 degrees or active autoimmune diseases. She has no interstitial lung disease or non-contagious pneumonia and does not require systemic antibacterial, antifungal, or antiviral treatment. She has no unstable pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, or ascites. She has no significant cardiovascular disease and her blood pressure is well-controlled with medication. She is negative for hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C. She has not received any vaccine or attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks prior to the first dose and has not undergone major surgery or suffered unhealed wounds, ulcers, or fractures within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

A 67-year-old retired man who has not been engaging in any physical activity for the past few years is interested in participating in a clinical trial that can help him regain muscle mass. He has no known allergies to whey, casein or soy. He has no history of heart disease, rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, or any other health conditions that might affect his participation in the study. He is a non-smoker and has never been diagnosed with hypertension. He is currently not taking any medications, but he has been prescribed aspirin by his doctor for his mild osteoarthritis. He is excited to participate in the study and is willing to comply with all the requirements.

The patient is a 35-year-old male veteran who served in Iraq and Afghanistan. He was honorably discharged from the army two years ago and has been struggling with alcohol use disorder since his return from deployment. He reports drinking 8-10 drinks per day and experiencing intense alcohol cravings, particularly in the evening. He has attempted to quit drinking on his own but has been unsuccessful. He has been diagnosed with PTSD and depression and is currently taking sertraline for his depression symptoms. He has no known allergies and is in good general medical health. He is fluent in English and can read and write. The patient has expressed a desire to cut down on his alcohol use and is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help with his cravings and decrease his alcohol consumption.

53-year-old female with a history of chronic bronchitis presenting with an acute exacerbation of her disease. She has a productive cough with yellowish sputum, increased shortness of breath, and wheezing. She has a history of smoking, with a 20 pack-year history but quit smoking 3 years ago. She is not on any chronic medications and has no known allergies. Her physical exam reveals decreased breath sounds in the lower lobes with scattered expiratory wheezes. Spirometry shows FEV1 value of 60%. She has never been hospitalized for her chronic bronchitis, and she has not participated in any clinical trials with any product in the past 30 days. She is not pregnant or lactating, and she is not using any effective contraception method. She has no history of immunosuppression or other severe diseases. She has no known hypersensitivity against telithromycin, macrolides, or any of the excipients.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with mild to moderate rosacea. She has a history of sensitive skin and has tried various topical treatments in the past with little to no improvement. She has not used any topical or oral medications for rosacea in the past 2 months. She does not have any known allergies to the study products or their components. She is not currently using any anatabine-containing supplements or medications. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all four visits over the eight-week period.

A 35-year-old woman gave birth to a male neonate at 38 weeks and 3 days of gestational age via vaginal delivery. The neonate weighed 3 kg and had an Apgar score of 8 at 1 minute and 9 at 5 minutes. The mother had an unremarkable pregnancy and received prenatal care regularly. The neonate was admitted to the neonatal unit due to respiratory distress, characterized by a respiratory rate of 68 breaths per minute, a SpO2 of 88% in room air, and an Ilvermman score of 2. The neonate was not exposed to meconium during labor and had no signs of sepsis. The neonate did not receive enteral feeding before admission. The parents provided their consent to participate in the clinical trial evaluating transient tachypnoea of the newborn in term and near-term neonates.

A 20-year-old healthy Caucasian male with a body mass index (BMI) of 22 presents to the trial center to participate in a clinical trial. He reports no significant medical history or symptoms, and his vital signs are within the normal range (blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg, heart rate: 70 bpm). He has never been diagnosed with any autoimmune disorders, kidney, or liver diseases. He has never tested positive for HIV, HBs antigen (HBsAg), or HCV. The patient weighs 70 kg and has signed the informed consent form. The laboratory tests conducted during the screening process showed normal and clinically irrelevant results. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman who is in her second trimester came to the clinic. She is a chronic hepatitis B carrier, with a positive serum test for both HBsAg and HBeAg. Her HBV DNA viral load is ≥ 2 × 10^6 IU/mL. She has no history of miscarriage or congenital malformations in any previous pregnancy. She has never received any antiviral treatment (except the use of antiviral drugs to prevent MTCT in previous pregnancy and antiviral drugs that have been discontinued for more than 6 months before this pregnancy). She does not have liver cancer or liver decompensation. She has no history of renal dysfunction. She exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. She has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. Her past surgical history is insignificant. She is married for 3 years and her husband is not a chronic hepatitis B carrier. She has no other co-infection with HIV-1, Hepatitis A Virus, Hepatitis C Virus, Hepatitis D Virus, Hepatitis E Virus infections or sexually transmitted diseases. She has no clinical risk/signs of abortion.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) two years ago based on clinical presentation. He exhibits muscle weakness, difficulty walking, and frequent falls. He has a history of corticosteroid treatment for the past year. He is currently able to walk with assistance but has difficulty climbing stairs and getting up from the floor. He has no history of respiratory distress or acute infections. He is not currently on any other medications. His parents are willing to consider stem cell therapy as a potential treatment option.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has a history of hypertension and atrial fibrillation. He is scheduled to undergo a routine cardiac procedure, specifically an EP study, to assess the electrical activity of his heart. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in this study, which involves the placement of a 20 pole catheter (Medtronic StableMapr intracardiac steerable electrode catheter) in the RV apex during the procedure. The patient is able to comply with the study requirements and does not have any physical conditions that contraindicate the use of the device per approved labeling. The patient's medical history, including blood clotting abnormalities or a recent coagulopathy or embolic event, do not exclude him from participation in this study. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and is interested in contributing to research that may improve the understanding and treatment of cardiac conditions.

The patient is a 70 year old male diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is currently taking medication for both. He is retired and lives with his wife in a suburban area. He has a good support system with his wife and adult children who live nearby. He enjoys gardening and reading books. He has undergone a biopsy and imaging studies that confirmed the diagnosis of lymphoma. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, indicating that he is fully ambulatory but has some limitations in physically strenuous activities. He has signed the written informed consent and serology tests for HIV, Hepatitis B and C came back negative. He has no history of cardiac failure. He is interested in participating in the trial and reducing the frequency of hospital visits.

A 13-year-old female with a history of Lafora Disease diagnosed by genetic testing with confirmed abnormal glycogen accumulation in muscle biopsy. The patient has experienced rapid neurological deterioration with myoclonus, seizures, and cognitive decline. She is currently on concomitant medications, including anticonvulsants, for her disease management. The patient's parents are interested in exploring alternative treatment options for their child's condition and have consented to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effects of a ketogenic diet on Lafora Disease. The patient and her parents understand the potential risks and benefits of the study and are willing to comply with the dietary restrictions and follow-up visits required for participation. The patient is not currently pregnant and will be using adequate contraception during the study period.

58-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis in both knees, with the right knee being the most severely affected, leading to chronic pain and limited mobility. The patient has tried various non-surgical treatments, including physical therapy and pain management, but has not achieved significant relief. The patient has no history of infections or other contraindications for knee replacement surgery. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different approaches to skin incision in Vanguard PS artificial knee joint total replacement surgery to determine which method provides a better outcome. The patient is willing to undergo surgery and follow-up evaluations as required by the trial protocol.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with unresectable melanoma after experiencing symptoms of weight loss, fatigue, and a persistent cough. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and he has no history of autoimmune diseases or inflammatory bowel disease. He has not received any prior treatment for his melanoma. The patient has measurable disease that can be biopsied and is willing to undergo both baseline and on-treatment biopsies, as well as stool and blood biomarker collection throughout the study. The patient is willing to participate in the antibiotic or antibiotic placebo treatment lead-in to prime the gut microbiome for engraftment of the oral microbiome study intervention. The patient must also be willing to undergo tumor biopsy on treatment.

Patient A is a 50-year-old Mexican woman who was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. She has never received any pharmacological treatment for her condition and has been managing her diabetes with diet and exercise. Her fasting glucose levels range between 130-200 mg/dL and her AIc is between 7% to 9%. She has a BMI of 30 Kg/m2 and her blood pressure is below 140/80 mmHg. She works as a teacher and has no significant medical history. She is not pregnant or nursing, and does not have any hypersensitivity to biguanides or any other medication. She has not used any investigational drug within the last 30 days, and does not have any history of liver, heart, kidney or thyroid disease. Her total cholesterol is below 300 mg/dL and her triglycerides are below 400 mg/dL. She is able to communicate and meet the requirements of the study, and has provided written informed consent before participating in the study.

A 55-year-old man was recently diagnosed with stage IV non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) after experiencing persistent cough, fatigue, and shortness of breath. A biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. He has no history of smoking but has a family history of lung cancer. He has been referred to an oncologist who is currently recommending a standard of care platinum-doublet chemotherapy regimen. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could potentially improve his outcome. He meets the eligibility criteria for the Denosumab in Combination with Chemotherapy as First-line Treatment of Metastatic Non-small Cell Lung Cancer trial and is willing to participate. He has no known brain metastases, and his dental and oral health is good. The patient has been informed of the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and has provided informed consent.

This is a 45 year-old female who was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of COVID-19. She was diagnosed with COVID-19 via a laboratory confirmed positive SARS-CoV-2 rtPCR test within 14 days prior to randomization. She is currently in the intensive care unit and her clinical status on the COVID-19 Ordinal Scale is 6 or 7. Her coagulation levels are within normal limits with INR ≤ 1.5×ULN, and APTT ≤ 1.5×ULN. She has not been enrolled in a study to investigate a treatment for COVID-19 and is not currently taking an anti-androgen of any type including androgen depravation therapy and 5-alpha reductase inhibitors. She is not allergic to the investigational product or similar drugs and does not have malignant tumors in the past 5 years. She does not have known serious cardiovascular diseases, congenital long QT syndrome, torsade de pointes, myocardial infarction in the past 6 months, or arterial thrombosis, or unstable angina pectoris, or congestive heart failure. She does not have any uncontrolled medical conditions that could compromise participation in the study. She is not diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis C, active hepatitis B, or treponema pallidum. Her ALT or AST levels are within normal limits. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is > 30 ml/min and she does not have severe kidney disease requiring dialysis. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use highly effective contraception throughout the study and for 3 months after stopping GT0918 treatment. She is not likely to transfer to another hospital within the next 28 days and is willing and able to provide informed consent.

A 28-year-old healthy nulliparous woman who is at 39 weeks of gestation with a singleton pregnancy and is experiencing spontaneous labor or spontaneous rupture of membranes. She has no systemic diseases, such as diabetes mellitus or hypertension, and has not been using any chronic analgesic medications. She has not received any systemic opioid labor analgesia and has a vertex presentation. The patient has requested neuraxial analgesia and is willing to participate in a clinical trial assessing the association between fluid administration, oxytocin administration, and fetal heart rate changes.

A 62-year-old man has a history of prostate cancer and has undergone surgery in the past.
