His prostate cancer has recurred and is metastatic, and he has been receiving androgen ablative therapy for the last few months. His PSA level has been increasing despite the therapy, and he is experiencing symptoms such as bone pain and fatigue. His biopsy confirms adenocarcinoma of the prostate. He has no history of other malignancies, diabetes, or HIV. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he is able to perform most daily activities with some difficulty. He is currently on hormone therapy and has discontinued anti-androgens for at least 4 weeks prior to study entry. He must continue therapy with LHRH agonist, and his testosterone level is at castrate level (< 1.7 nmol/L). He has not received any chemotherapy regimens for recurrent disease. He is eligible for this clinical trial as his PSA level is ≥ 5 ng/ml, and he has radiologically documented metastatic disease. He has formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue available for translational studies. He must sign a consent form prior to enrollment in the trial to document his willingness to participate. He is accessible for treatment and follow-up and will be treated and followed at the participating centre.

The patient is a 32-year-old female who has been actively using injection drugs for the past 5 years. She visits a local syringe exchange program regularly to obtain clean needles and syringes. She has heard about hepatitis C (HCV) but does not have much knowledge about it. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to educate active drug users about HCV and its prevention. She is fluent in English and is able to provide informed consent. She is interested in the study and hopes to learn more about HCV and how she can protect herself from contracting it.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with spinal cord injury (SCI) who was recently admitted to the hospital for treatment of Clostridium difficile infection. He was diagnosed with SCI 10 years ago and has been experiencing bowel dysfunction since the injury. He presents with symptoms of diarrhea, abdominal pain, and fever. A stool sample tested positive for Clostridium difficile. He has not received any antibiotics that are active against Clostridium difficile for the past 24 hours. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and depression, which is being treated with medication. His family history is non-significant. He is able to provide informed consent for the study.

A 55-year-old male smoker presents with a persistent cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath for the past 6 weeks. He has a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension, which are both well-controlled with medications. He denies any weight loss, fever, or night sweats. A chest X-ray shows a mass in the right lung. A CT scan of the chest and upper abdomen is done, which shows a 5 cm mass in the right upper lobe of the lung and enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum. A mediastinoscopy confirms the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with N2 involvement. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial and agrees to participate.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with locally advanced colon adenocarcinoma. The tumor is located in the ascending colon and is classified as poor prognosis T3 and N2 by abdominal CT scan. The patient has no metastases to the lung, liver or peritoneum and the primary tumor is non-obstructive, non-perforated and non-bleeding. The patient's RAS status is WT. The patient has not received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy within the last 5 years and has no history of colorectal cancer within the last 5 years. The patient has a life expectancy of 5 years or more and has a performance status of 1. The patient's blood counts and liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. The patient has not had any major surgical procedures or traumatic injuries within the last 28 days and has no known hypersensitivity reactions to any of the study treatments. The patient has no other medical, geographical, sociological, psychological or legal conditions that would exclude them from the study. The patient is able to provide signed written informed consent prior to any study specific screening procedures.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who attends elementary school. He has no significant medical history and is up to date on his routine vaccinations. He lives with his parents who are both in good health. He enjoys playing video games and soccer with his friends. His mother is interested in enrolling him in a clinical trial for an influenza vaccine. He has never had an allergic reaction to any vaccine before. He does not have any chronic illnesses or allergies. His family is willing to comply with the schedule of the trial and attend all scheduled visits. He is willing to receive the vaccine and give blood samples for laboratory testing.

A 62-year-old male who has been smoking for the past 30 years presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing. He has a history of COPD and is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids/long-acting β2-agonist (free combination) for the past 6 months, but his symptoms are not well controlled. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to COPD exacerbation. He has no known respiratory disorders other than COPD. He has a history of hypertension and is on medication for the same. He denies any history of heart disease or stroke. He is retired and lives with his wife. He has two children who live in a different city. He is interested in participating in the study as he hopes to find a better treatment for his COPD symptoms. His FEV1 is 55% of predicted normal, and FEV1/FVC ratio is 0.6. He has not had any COPD exacerbations in the past 6 weeks.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing upper gastrointestinal symptoms, such as heartburn and difficulty swallowing, for several months. He underwent an upper endoscopy two weeks ago, which revealed a polyp in his stomach. His gastroenterologist recommends a therapeutic upper gastrointestinal endoscopy to remove the polyp. He has a past medical history significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He does not have any known allergies. He is an active smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. He works as a construction worker and reports no difficulties with his job. He is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

A 32 year old female who underwent LASIK surgery 2 years ago complains of blurred vision in her right eye. Her recent eye exam showed a residual refractive error in her right eye. She has no other ocular or systemic medical history. Her current medications include over the counter vitamins only. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that involves the use of tissue sealant to prevent epithelial ingrowth from gaining access under a LASIK flap with repeat LASIK surgery. She is willing to adhere to the study protocol and attend all follow-up visits.

A 60-year-old male patient diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis according to the WHO standard (2016 version) was referred to the study. The patient had a JAK2 mutation and was classified as high-risk according to the Dynamic International Prognostic Scoring System plus (DIPSS-plus) risk grouping criteria. The patient had splenomegaly with palpable splenic margin above the subcostal by 6 cm. The patient had not previously been treated with JAK inhibitors and had an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 1500/uL and a platelet count of 100 × 109/L without growth factor. The patient had no significant clinical or laboratory abnormalities and a normal functioning of major organs, with alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) at 2×upper limit of normal (ULN), direct bilirubin (DBIL) and total bilirubin (TBIL) at 1.2×ULN, and serum creatinine within normal range. The patient voluntarily signed the informed consent and was able to follow the study and follow-up procedures.

The patient is a 35-year-old American woman who works from home and has a sedentary lifestyle. She spends most of her day sitting in front of the computer and watching TV at night. She is overweight with a BMI of 28 and has been struggling to lose weight for the past year. She reports eating unhealthy foods and having difficulty controlling her portions. She does not engage in any regular physical activity and reports only walking short distances for errands. She has no history of heart conditions, chest pain, or loss of consciousness during physical activity. She has no joint problems or prescription medication usage related to heart conditions. She is willing to have TV Allowances attached to her TVs at home and is open to participating in an 8-week pilot study to examine the effects of two different leisure-time activity prescriptions on dietary intake, leisure-time activities, and weight loss.

Patient A is a 45-year-old female who has been diagnosed with chronic back pain due to degenerative disc disease. She underwent a Precision® spinal cord stimulator system implantation procedure one year ago, which has helped alleviate her pain to some extent. She is currently experiencing pain scores of 7 on the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) and has been on a low frequency stimulation program for the past 6 months. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to assess the efficacy and preferability of high frequency stimulation programming for the spinal cord stimulator system. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and is using a barrier method of contraception. She has not been on any investigational drugs within the last 30 days and is not taking any medication or herbal agents with central nervous system (CNS) effects. She has no history of cognitive impairment or unstable medical or psychiatric illness.

As this is a genetic study, a patient description is not applicable. Participants for this study would need to meet the inclusion criteria of having a confirmed diagnosis of tuberculosis and possessing the NRAMP 1 polymorphism. The study would not have any exclusion criteria.

42 yo M with flu-like symptoms and positive COVID-19 test result. The patient has no significant past medical history or co-morbidities. He is currently experiencing mild to moderate symptoms such as fever, cough, fatigue, and body aches. He has not received any treatment for COVID-19 yet. The patient's BMI is 23.5 kg/m. He has no known allergies to any drugs. The patient has not undergone RT-PCR testing more than 3 days prior to enrollment. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

This is a 27-year-old female who has generally healthy skin with occasional mild acne breakouts. She does not have a significant medical history or current skin diseases. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of over-the-counter skin products on skin health. She has no known allergies to any of the products being tested and is willing to comply with the protocol requirements. She is able to understand and communicate with the investigator and has provided informed consent. She does not foresee any intensive UV exposure during the study period.

19-year-old male college student with a history of Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosed at the age of 8. The patient has previously participated in the NIMH Child Psychiatry Branch ADHD study and has undergone neurobiological measurements, particularly magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, through other research studies. The patient has a history of hyperactivity and impulsivity with ratings above the 95th percentile on the Conners Rating Scales-Revised and Strengths and Weaknesses of ADHD and Normal Behavior (SWAN). The patient has no other known genetic conditions that are likely to be etiologic, no onset of medical conditions that could produce symptoms of ADHD through non-genetic mechanisms, no presence of other psychiatric disorders that can produce symptoms similar to ADHD, no presence of neuropsychiatric conditions that may confound evaluation of ADHD, no intelligence quotient less than 80, and no reading achievement standard scores less than 75 or reading-intelligence discrepancy greater than 2 SD. The patient will be undergoing psychiatric interviews, neuropsychological tests, and another MRI as part of the ongoing study of individuals with ADHD to learn more about the genetics of the disease.

The patient is a 32-year-old Asian male with a known history of chronic hepatitis B. The patient has been diagnosed with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positive for more than 6 months and is also HBeAg positive with anti-HBe negative. The patient has been on nucleoside analog therapy with Entecavir for the past 12 months, with a recent HBV DNA level of less than 2000 IU/ml. The patient has no history of Telbivudine treatment and the liver function tests show normal levels of ALT. The patient has compensated liver disease with no history of decompensated cirrhosis. The patient's age is within the range of 18 to 70 years, and the patient has given written informed consent. The patient has no history of neutropenia or thrombocytopenia and is negative for hepatitis C virus and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). The patient has no other acquired or inherited causes of liver disease and has no contraindications for alfa-interferon therapy. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no substance abuse history. The patient is eligible for enrollment in the study.

This is a 42 year old female who has been diagnosed with fibromyalgia. She has been experiencing chronic pain, fatigue and sleep disturbances for over a year, which have significantly affected her ability to perform daily activities and has also impacted her quality of life. She resides in Penticton and is fluent in English. She has tried various treatments including medications, but has not found significant relief. She is interested in participating in the community-based intervention for fibromyalgia pilot trial, which involves a 10-week comprehensive care program provided by a team of healthcare providers. She is willing to attend sessions with a psychiatrist, physiotherapist, certified exercise therapist, dietitian, rheumatologist, and mental health clinician, and is also open to attending a peer-led pain self-management support group provided by the Arthritis Society. She is looking forward to learning more about self-management of her symptoms and is hoping to see an improvement in her quality of life.

A 28-year-old woman in her 28th week of pregnancy came to the clinic with a history of hypertension discovered during her pregnancy. She was diagnosed with preeclampsia at 24 weeks gestation and has been on medications since then. She reports poor sleep quality, snoring, and waking up gasping for air at night. She also feels excessively tired during the day. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use, and her family history is negative for hypertension or sleep apnea. She is a first-time mother who has had an uncomplicated pregnancy so far except for her hypertension. She is currently taking methyldopa and aspirin for her blood pressure control. Her BMI is 28 kg/m², and she has no other significant medical history. She is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent.

A 40-year old woman was diagnosed with triple negative breast cancer six months ago. She underwent lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection. Pathology showed a 2.5 cm invasive ductal carcinoma with negative margins and 1 of 12 lymph nodes positive for metastasis. She received adjuvant chemotherapy with AC-T (doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, paclitaxel) and completed radiation therapy. She tolerated the treatments well and had no significant side effects. However, a recent follow-up CT scan showed new liver metastasis. She is experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite and abdominal discomfort. She is married and has two children. She works as a teacher and is currently on medical leave. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her past medical history is unremarkable. She is currently not taking any medications except for over-the-counter pain relievers. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options.

A 28-year-old Turkish female presents to the dermatology outpatient clinic for a routine skin checkup. She has no prior history of skin or hair-related issues. She reports that she has been feeling self-conscious about the presence of excessive hair growth on her upper lip, chin, chest, and lower abdomen for the past few years. She has not been pregnant nor lactating in the past year. She does not use any permanent epilation methods but has been using temporary hair reduction methods such as waxing and threading for the past 4 weeks. She is not taking any oral contraceptives, corticosteroids, cyclosporin, or spironolactone in the last 3 months. She has a BMI of 23.4 and reports regular menstrual cycles. She denies any history of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, or thyroid disease, and has no family history of hirsutism.

The patient is a 53-year-old postmenopausal woman with an intact uterus who has not taken any hormones or oral contraceptives within the last year. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m² and is of Caucasian and Hispanic ethnicity. She has no history of significant abnormal blood pressure or heart rate. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of lanabecestat on rosuvastatin when taken together. She will undergo screening within 45 days prior to enrollment and will be on study for 21 days with a follow-up at least 7 days afterwards.

The patient is an 11-year-old boy who has been diagnosed with ADHD by a pediatrician. He currently takes methylphenidate daily as prescribed. The patient has a history of learning difficulties but is currently receiving additional support at school. His parents have consented for him to participate in the study. The patient's IQ is within normal limits. He has no history of mood or psychotic disorders. He does not have any of the exclusion criteria. The patient is alert, cooperative, and in good general health. The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. The patient is able to understand and follow instructions.

The patient is a 56-year-old man who was diagnosed with stage III non-small cell lung cancer. He is a smoker for the past 30 years and has a pack-a-day smoking history. He is a retired construction worker who lives alone. He is complaining of cough and shortness of breath. He has lost 10 pounds in the past month. On physical examination, he has decreased breath sounds in the right lung field. CT scan shows a 4 cm mass in the right upper lobe with mediastinal lymph node involvement. His performance status is ECOG 1. His labs: WBC: 7.5 K/uL, Hgb: 12.8 g/dL, Platelets: 180 K/uL, Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL, Bilirubin: 0.8 mg/dL, AST: 28 U/L. He has no history of heart disease or any other significant medical illness. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the requirements and potential risks.

The patient is a 70 year old man who retired from his work in a farm a year ago. He lives in a rural area in Gironde with his wife. He has noticed some changes in his memory and cognitive abilities recently. He has difficulty remembering names of people he has met before, often forgets where he put his belongings and struggles to follow a conversation. He has no history of mental illnesses or neurological disorders. He has never had an MRI before but has no known contraindications for it. He is right-handed and has a good general health status. He is interested in participating in this study as he wants to know if these changes in his memory and cognitive abilities are a normal part of aging or if they could be indicative of a more serious condition like dementia.

Pt is a 45yo F with a 7-year history of psoriatic arthritis. She has been treated with methotrexate and sulfasalazine for the past 5 years and has maintained good disease control. She has no history of COVID-19 infection and has not yet received a COVID-19 vaccine. She is interested in participating in the study to better understand the immune response to the vaccine in patients with rheumatic diseases. She is not currently pregnant and has no active infections or untreated malignancies.

This is a 57 year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B and cirrhosis. A recent ultrasound revealed a 2cm lesion in the right lobe of the liver. Further imaging with MRI showed the lesion to be suggestive of HCC. Blood work shows normal liver function tests and Child-Pugh class A. The patient has been referred for curative purpose of RFA and has signed informed consent. There are no other visible lesions and no evidence of vascular tumor thrombosis or extrahepatic metastasis. The patient has no severe coagulopathy with PLT above 80K and PT within normal range.

A 35-year-old female patient with a history of ocular cicatricial pemphigoid presented with complaints of blurry vision and a feeling of discomfort in her left eye. The patient had been diagnosed with ocular cicatricial pemphigoid five years earlier and had been treated with topical steroids and immunosuppressive drugs with little success. On examination, it was found that the cornea of the left eye had become vascularized with surrounding conjunctival epithelium growing over it, leading to scarring and opacification. The patient was diagnosed with limbal stem cell deficiency (LSCD) and was offered the option of participating in a clinical trial for limbal epithelial stem cell transplantation. The patient met the inclusion criteria for the trial and provided voluntary written informed consent. The patient will undergo a limbal biopsy from the good eye, where available, and the epithelial stem cells will be expanded in the laboratory on a biological substrate. The patient will be transplanted with standardized limbal stem cell grafts onto the diseased eye after removal of scar tissue using a novel surgical technique developed by the research team. The patient will be followed-up by the Department of Ophthalmology at the University Hospital in Antwerp to monitor the safety and efficacy of the transplantation. The aim of the trial is to provide an effective treatment option for LSCD, which can lead to corneal blindness, and to improve the quality of life of patients suffering from this condition.

A 56-year-old woman with a BMI of 33 presents with elevated liver enzymes (ALT 86 U/L, AST 71 U/L) on routine blood work. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and occasional binge drinking. She denies any history of viral hepatitis, autoimmune disease, or recent medication use. An abdominal ultrasound shows evidence of hepatic steatosis, and a liver biopsy confirms the diagnosis of NASH with a NASH activity score of 6, including steatosis, hepatocellular injury, and inflammation. She has no history of diabetes but has impaired fasting glucose with a fasting blood glucose of 105 mg/dL. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to undergo regular monitoring and liver biopsies. She is not pregnant and agrees to use effective contraception during the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old male with a history of elevated PSA levels and a prior negative prostate biopsy. He is scheduled for a repeat prostate biopsy due to persistently elevated PSA levels. The patient has no known history of antibiotic resistance or recent hospitalizations. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. The patient reports no symptoms of urinary tract infections, such as dysuria or hematuria. He has no history of allergies to antibiotics or other medications. Physical examination is unremarkable, with no signs of infection or inflammation. The patient has consented to participate in the study and is willing to undergo a rectal swab culture prior to the prostate biopsy.

A 32-year-old male patient with a history of diabetes mellitus and visual problems was diagnosed with Wolfram syndrome type 2. The patient's diabetes is poorly controlled despite being on multiple oral hypoglycemic agents, including metformin, and regular insulin. He also experiences frequent episodes of hypoglycemia. The patient reports difficulty with night vision and has been experiencing progressive visual loss over the past year. He has no significant past medical or surgical history, and he is a non-smoker. The patient has no known allergies, and he is not taking any other medications. The patient is cooperative and willing to participate in the clinical trial.

45-year-old male diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) that failed to meet National Cancer Institute (NCI) Working Group criteria for complete or partial response after therapy with a regimen containing fludarabine phosphate (FLU) and experienced disease relapse within 12 months after completing therapy with a regimen containing FLU. The patient is not eligible for conventional allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) and has disease expected to be stable for at least 100 days without chemotherapy. The patient has a related donor who is HLA genotypically identical at least at one haplotype and may be phenotypically or genotypically identical at the allele level at HLA-A, -B, -C, -DRB1, and -DQB1. The patient has adequate veins for leukapheresis or agrees to placement of central venous catheter (femoral, subclavian). The patient has not been previously treated with a high priority curative autologous transplant and does not have rapidly progressive, aggressive NHL unless in minimal disease state, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML), any current central nervous system (CNS) involvement with disease refractory to intrathecal chemotherapy, presence of circulating leukemic blasts (in the peripheral blood) detected by standard pathology for patients with AML, ALL or CML, symptomatic coronary artery disease or ejection fraction < 35% or other cardiac failure requiring therapy, poorly controlled hypertension, DLCO < 30%, TLC < 30%, FEV1 < 30% and/or receiving supplementary continuous oxygen, liver function abnormalities, active bacterial or fungal infections unresponsive to medical therapy, age less than 12 years, identical twin, pregnancy, infection with HIV, known allergy to filgrastim (G-CSF), current serious systemic illness that would result in increased risk for G-CSF mobilization and harvest of peripheral blood stem cells (PBSC).

The patient is a 32-year-old pregnant woman who is currently in her 23rd week of gestation. She has been diagnosed with a left-sided diaphragmatic hernia in her baby and is seeking treatment to improve the chance of survival for her baby. She has had a routine prenatal check-up and her fetus is anatomically and chromosomally normal. The patient is willing to participate in the TOTAL trial and is able to provide written consent. She is accepting of randomization and understands the consequences of the further management during pregnancy and after delivery. The patient is willing to remain close to or at the FETO center or travel swiftly and within an acceptable time interval to the center until the balloon is removed. She is also willing to comply with the suggested guidelines for standardized postnatal treatment. The patient has no medical conditions that would make fetal intervention risky and is not currently experiencing preterm labor or any other complications with her pregnancy.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with malignant pleural mesothelioma with pleural effusion. He underwent several cycles of palliative chemotherapy, but his condition did not improve. He is not a candidate for surgical procedures like decortication or pleuro-pneumectomy due to his medical and functional status. He has no history of autoimmune disease or major organ allografts. His bone marrow function, hepatic function, and renal function are within normal limits. He has no history of coronary heart disease, stroke, or peripheral vascular disease. He is not taking any immune-modulating drugs and has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He is willing to use contraception during the course of the study and for 24 months after the adoptive transfer. He has signed the informed consent after being fully informed about the study. He is eligible for the trial and can be enrolled as a candidate for adoptively transferred FAP-specific re-directed T cells.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who presents to the emergency department with redness, warmth, and swelling in her left lower leg. She reports that the area has been progressively getting worse over the past few days and is now painful to the touch. The patient has a history of obesity, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. She reports that she has had similar episodes in the past, which were treated with antibiotics. The patient is currently taking metformin and lisinopril. On physical exam, the left lower leg is erythematous, warm to the touch, and tender. The patient has no fever and no signs of systemic illness. The diagnosis of cellulitis is suspected, and the patient is admitted to the hospital for intravenous antibiotics. The patient is eligible for the study as she meets the inclusion criteria of having a presumed clinical diagnosis of cellulitis by the medicine team and is able to understand and sign informed consent. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria, including abnormal vital signs, known pregnancy, or a history of transplantation. The patient is randomized to the active arm and receives a dermatology consultation within 24 hours of hospital admission. She is followed throughout her hospital stay and after discharge to assess the impact of the dermatology consultation on her length of stay, readmission rates, and antibiotic usage.

The patient is a 35-year-old Korean man who was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 2 years ago. He has been taking antiretroviral therapy (ART) since his diagnosis and has had good viral suppression. However, his recent viral load test showed detectable levels of the virus, prompting his physician to switch his ART regimen to include Kaletra (lopinavir/ritonavir). The patient has no known allergies or adverse reactions to any medications. He is willing to participate in the Post-Marketing Surveillance study and has given verbal consent to use his personal and health data. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril 10mg daily. The patient has no other significant medical history or comorbidities. He currently works as a graphic designer and leads an active lifestyle. He reports no recent illnesses or hospitalizations. The patient is compliant with his medication regimen and has not missed any doses of ART in the past year.

A 14 year old male came to the clinic with his parents, complaining of a gradual loss of vision in both eyes over the last 2 years. His family has a history of visual impairment, and his diagnosis of Leber's Hereditary Optic Neuropathy (LHON) was confirmed by genetic testing. He has no other ocular or medical conditions, and has not been previously treated with idebenone. The patient is willing to comply with study procedures and visits, and is currently using a reliable method of contraception. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old woman presents with a history of chronic low back pain and radiating pain in the left leg that started six months ago. She reports having tried various treatments including physical therapy, oral anti-inflammatory medications, and local steroidal injections, but the pain persists. She rates her pain as 8 out of 10 on a visual analog scale. She reports that the pain limits her daily activities and she experiences a decrease in her quality of life. She is otherwise healthy, has no known allergies, and can read and understand English. She has not received a surgical intervention for low back pain or lumbosacral radiculopathy/radiculitis within the previous 6 months, and has not received an epidural steroid injection in the prior 3 months. She is willing to be randomized to either an experimental or a control group and is willing to refrain from unnecessary or self-directed pain management/treatment plan changes during the study. She has daily access to the internet via cell phone, tablet, or computer.

This is a 49-year-old male patient who was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) due to respiratory distress secondary to pneumonia. He required mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours and failed the first weaning test. The patient has a medical history of hypertension, but no history of peripheral or central nervous system pathology, psychiatric pathology, or agitation. The patient does not have any clinical worsening, and his Glasgow scale is 11. His PaO2/FiO2 ratio is 280 with no respiratory distress signs. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not under legal guardianship or protection. He has health insurance coverage and meets the age criteria of at least 18 years.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who lives in an endemic area of malaria in Juruá Valley, Brazil. He presents with symptoms of fever and chills, and a recent blood test confirmed mono-infection by Plasmodium falciparum with a parasite count of 500/µl. He reports to have taken quinine three days ago for an unrelated condition. He is not pregnant, and his malnutrition status is within normal limits. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to comply with the schedule of visits and monitoring for 42 days. The patient does not have a history of hypersensitivity to the components of the ASMQ combination.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who has a BMI of 26.5 kg/m2. She has regular menstrual cycles and is not planning on becoming pregnant during the course of the study. She has no history of cardiovascular disease or metabolic disorders, including diabetes. She does not smoke cigarettes or take any medications to induce weight loss or change appetite. She is willing to refrain from restrictive dieting during the study. She reports occasional hunger pangs and feelings of fullness after meals, but no significant changes in her weight over the past six months. She has no known food allergies or intolerances.

A 56-year-old Caucasian male presented to the hospital with complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been smoking for the past 30 years and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient underwent a coronary angiogram that revealed a significant stenosis in the left anterior descending (LAD) artery. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed through the right femoral artery using 6 Fr access. The patient was diagnosed with severe common femoral arterial disease after angiography. The ACT was less than 300 seconds. The patient meets the inclusion criteria of the study and has not undergone any ipsilateral closure device use, other than VASCADE. The patient's Plt count is within normal limits, and there is no inherent coagulopathy. Therefore, he is eligible to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who suffered an ischemic stroke 6 months ago, resulting in a motor deficit that has significantly impacted her quality of life. She has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication to control it. She has no other significant medical history and is generally in good health. MRI findings show a subcortical infarction in the middle cerebral artery distribution. She has a Modified Rankin Score of 3 and an FMMS score of 45. She has not received any investigational drugs or devices in the last 30 days and has not received any cell infusions other than blood transfusion. She is willing and able to meet all follow-up requirements and undergo post-physical therapy/rehabilitation. She has no disabling psychological or psychiatric disorders and is not currently using any antiepileptic medication. She does not have a history of seizures or other major neurological diseases or injuries. She has no history of malignancy, primary or secondary immune deficiency, and her creatinine, liver function tests, hematocrit/hemoglobin, total WBC, and platelet count are all within normal limits. She is not using antiplatelet drugs less than 2 weeks before surgery. She meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

A 40-year-old female with a BMI of 35 presents with complaints of difficulty losing weight despite significant efforts at diet and exercise. She has no known chronic medical conditions and is a non-smoker. She reports occasional bloating and constipation. She has not taken any antibiotics, anti-inflammatory drugs, or laxatives in the past three weeks. She is not currently taking any medication or nutritional program affecting body weight or glucose control. Her basal glycemia is within normal limits. She has no history of immune deficiencies, HIV, chemotherapy, radiotherapy or organ transplant. She is not currently participating in any other clinical trials and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She reports never having consumed probiotic products.

Patient is a 26-year-old medical trainee at Scripps Green Hospital. She is a first-year resident in the internal medicine program. She has no known history of any significant medical conditions nor mental health conditions. She is unmarried and lives in on-campus housing provided by the hospital. She owns a Samsung Galaxy S9 smartphone which is capable of running all study software. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all protocol-specified procedures. She is reliable, cooperative and able to understand and grant informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been in a monogamous relationship with her male partner for the past year. She underwent tubal ligation after the birth of her second child. She has regular menstrual cycles and has undergone regular Pap smears. She has no history of gynecological abnormalities or significant medical conditions. She is willing to abstain from intercourse and use non-spermicidal, lubricated condoms from the first day of each menstrual cycle until 72 hours before expected midcycle. She is willing to give voluntary consent, sign an informed consent form, and comply with study procedures as required by the protocol. She has no known allergy to 3% N-9, latex, ingredients in ContraGel, or silicone. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and she is not currently participating in any other investigational trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence for the past 5 years. She reports that she leaks urine when she coughs, sneezes, laughs, or exercises. She has tried pelvic floor muscle exercises and bladder training but has not seen any improvement in her symptoms. She has two children and had vaginal deliveries for both. She reports having a mild pelvic organ prolapse, but it does not bother her. She has no other medical problems and takes no medications. She is interested in surgical treatment for her incontinence and is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing laparoscopic Burch colposuspension with midurethral slings.

52-year-old Chinese male with a medical history significant for relapsed indolent non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (iNHL) without past or current central nervous system involvement. The patient has received prior anticancer chemotherapy or immunotherapy, but has recovered from the toxic effects (Grade <2) of previous treatments. The patient has at least one measurable lesion according to the Lugano Classification and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 1. The patient has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks, a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 50%, and adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. The patient is able to understand and sign an informed consent form and has agreed to use highly effective contraception from signing of the informed consent form until at least 1 month after the last study drug administration. Additionally, the patient has not been previously treated with PI3K inhibitors and is not currently taking strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 or St John's Wort.

A 28-year-old active male presents to the clinic with pain and swelling in his right calf muscle. He reports that he was playing basketball when he heard a popping sound and felt sudden pain in his calf. He had to stop playing immediately and has been limping ever since. He has been using ice packs and taking over-the-counter pain medication, but the symptoms have not improved. He denies any history of hematological conditions or anticoagulation in the past two weeks. He is not pregnant. Upon examination, there is tenderness and swelling in the right calf muscle. MRI confirms a grade 2 muscular lesion. He has never had any surgeries before and his past medical history is unremarkable. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to test the efficacy of platelet-derived repairing factors in the treatment of muscular lesions.

A 58-year-old male non-smoker was recently diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. The tumor is located in the upper lobe of his left lung and is currently classified as stage IIIA. He is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status is 0. He has not undergone any prior treatments for his cancer. He has adequate pulmonary function to undergo curative lung cancer surgery. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and understands the risks and benefits of the treatment.

This is a 8-year-old child who has been experiencing recurrent sore throats and tonsillar infections for several months. The child has been diagnosed with chronic tonsillitis and is scheduled to undergo tonsillectomy surgery. The child does not have any other known systemic diseases or otolaryngological disorders. The purpose of the surgery is to remove the infected tonsils and to evaluate the correlation between Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress and tonsillar tissue disorders. The study aims to explore the structure of diseases related to the immune system and to identify potential markers of ER stress and apoptosis in tonsil tissues. The child will be enrolled in a prospective study and tonsil tissues will be evaluated using Real-time PCR and Western blot methods to assess ER stress markers and apoptosis markers.

A healthy 25-year-old woman who has had a tubal ligation procedure done 2 years ago is eligible to participate in the study. She has a body mass index of 23 kg/m2 and weighs 65 kg. She does not smoke and has no history of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or HIV. She has no clinically significant medical conditions, including allergic, hematological, endocrine, dermatologic, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, or neurological disease. She is not at risk for suicide or any history of suicide attempts. She has not undergone any gastrointestinal surgery. In the last 7 days, she has had normal bowel movements at least once per 24 hours and is able to provide a fecal sample prior to study drug dosing on Day -1 or Day 1.

45-year-old male patient diagnosed with coronary artery disease, scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, well-controlled with medications. He has no known allergies to anesthesia or pain medication. The patient is able to provide informed consent and agrees to participate in the study. He does not have any physical disabilities or require mechanical ventilatory support.

A 55 year old man came to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain, bloating, and blood in his stool. A colonoscopy was performed and revealed a mass in his colon. Biopsy confirmed it to be colorectal cancer. The patient underwent surgery to remove the tumor and is now in the recovery phase. The doctors have recommended that he undergo liquid biopsy testing as part of a clinical trial for further diagnosis and personalized treatment options. The patient has stable vital signs and is willing to participate in the study. He has signed the informed consent form and is ready to undergo further testing.

48F with a history of right breast cancer treated with right mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection. She is currently planning to undergo breast reconstruction with tissue expanders. The patient has no history of radiation therapy or chemotherapy. She has no significant medical history and is currently not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 25. She is motivated to participate in the study and understands the requirements for at home dosing. She has no history of psychological conditions or drug or alcohol misuse. The patient is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with stage IIIa pulmonary adenocarcinoma. He has completed his first-line chemotherapy and has responded well to the treatment. He is planning to undergo maintenance therapy and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that combines traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with targeted therapy maintenance. He is in good physical condition with an ECOG PS score of 1 and has an estimated life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. His blood chemistry is within normal limits and he has no major organ dysfunction. He has no history of other malignant tumors and has not received any other anticancer treatments. He is fully informed about the study and willing to provide informed consent.

53 y/o male with a history of Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC), underwent surgical resection of a liver mass with curative intent, 6 months ago. Post-surgery, the patient developed recurrent symptoms of fatigue, abdominal pain, and weight loss. Imaging studies revealed a residual lesion, confirmed by post-operative digital subtraction angiography (DSA). The patient's alpha fetoprotein (AFP) levels remained elevated above the upper limits of normal (according to local lab's range) for the past 2 months. Radiological review confirmed no visible residual tumor on the eligibility scan (CT or MRI) performed >2 weeks after surgery. The patient has physically and mentally recovered from surgery and is considered to be able to tolerate Sorafenib therapy by the investigator's judgment. The decision to treat with Sorafenib has been made, and the patient is willing to participate in this clinical trial.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and has been recommended to undergo chemotherapy treatment. This is her first experience with chemotherapy. She has a high school education and works as a cashier at a local grocery store. She has no history of neurological conditions and is able to communicate effectively with medical personnel. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to validate the Patient Neurotoxicity Questionnaire (PNQ) in Greek.

The patient is a 7-year-old girl who was recently diagnosed with Turner Syndrome. She has not started puberty yet and her breast development is at Tanner stage I. She is below the 10th percentile for her age in terms of height. She has no history of receiving any growth-promoting therapy in the past 3 months, and her chromosome analysis does not show any Y component. She has no clinically significant cardiac, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, hepatic, or renal disease and has not had any malignancy. No hematuria or proteinuria was detected during her pretherapy evaluation. She has no history of diabetes mellitus or chronic infection. She is not taking any medication that is known to interfere with growth hormone secretion or actions. Her parents are not substance abusers, and she comes from a home where appropriate emotional development is expected. She is available to attend scheduled appointments for the duration of the clinical trial.

45F with a 20 pack-year smoking history, enrolled in the Duke Smoking Cessation Program for tobacco cessation. She reports smoking 10 cigarettes per day for the last year, and feels motivated to quit smoking. She is fluent in English and has access to a smartphone and the internet. She is willing to watch instructional videos and receive counseling calls as part of the study. She does not use any other form of tobacco or nicotine products and is not currently taking any smoking cessation medication. She reports no history of cognitive or emotive disorders. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and scores below the exclusion criteria on the AUDIT-10 and DAST-10. She also scores below the exclusion criteria on the PHQ-2 depression scale. She is willing to set a quit date within the next 2 weeks and attend investigational visits.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with AML and has undergone chemotherapy but has not achieved complete remission. Due to her age and medical history, she is not eligible for standard TBI- or Busulfan-based myeloablative conditioning for allogeneic transplantation. In this study, she may be eligible to receive dose escalated treosulfan as a substitute for busulfan, which may reduce toxicity while improving myeloablation and disease control. She must have an HLA matched related or unrelated donor willing to donate either peripheral blood stem cells or bone marrow. The patient should not have bilirubin levels greater than 3.0 mg/dl, transaminases greater than 3 times the upper normal limit, creatinine greater than 2.0 mg/dl, ECOG-Performance status greater than 2, uncontrolled infection, abnormal lung diffusion capacity (DLCO < 40% predicted), severe cardiovascular disease, CNS disease involvement, pleural effusion or ascites greater than 1 liter, known hypersensitivity to fludarabine or treosulfan, or psychiatric conditions/disease that impair the ability to give informed consent or to adequately co-operate.

Patient B is a 35-year-old office worker who has been experiencing pain in the outer part of their elbow for the past few months. The patient reports that the pain began after a period of increased computer use at work. They have tried over-the-counter pain relievers and rest, but the pain persists and is now affecting their ability to perform daily activities. The patient has no history of surgery or other interventions for elbow pain. They have not received physiotherapy or chiropractic care for the past 6 months. The patient is willing to comply with treatment and follow-up assessments. They are between 30 and 60 years of age and do not have severe neck or shoulder problems that could be causing or maintaining their elbow complaints. The patient has not been diagnosed with posterior interosseous nerve compression or any congenital or acquired deformities of the elbow. They do not have any systemic musculoskeletal or neurological disorders. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial investigating the effects of Mulligan and muscle energy techniques on lateral epicondylitis.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer five years ago. He underwent radical prostatectomy, but his PSA level has been rising steadily over the past year. His current PSA level is 0.5 ng/mL. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He reports occasional urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. His vital signs and laboratory tests are within normal limits. His serum creatinine is 1.5 mg/dl, total serum calcium is 9.8 mg/dl, total bilirubin is 1.2 mg/dl, platelet count is 150,000/uL, and his hemoglobin level is 12 g/dl. He has no history of hypocalcemia or seizure disorder. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

42-year-old Taiwanese male with a diagnosis of stage III colon cancer who has completed surgery and chemotherapy. He has reported experiencing fatigue that has been impacting his daily activities and quality of life. He is able to communicate verbally and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. He does not have any cognitive impairment and is able to fill out the questionnaires completely.

The patient is a 35-year-old male living in Cameroon. He has been diagnosed with HIV-1 and HSV-2. He recently noticed recurrent episodes of genital herpes, which are painful blisters in the genital and anal areas. He has been receiving antiretroviral therapy for HIV-1 for the past year, but has not been treated for HSV-2. He works as a mechanic and is married with two children. His wife is also HIV-1 positive, but has not been diagnosed with HSV-2. He is willing to participate in the study and to take the study medication as directed. He is fluent in French and has completed high school education. He is generally healthy with no known allergies to medications. He is not planning to move out of the area during the study period. He is willing to undergo clinical evaluations and adhere to the follow-up schedule. He has not had any bacterial STDs in the past two weeks.

Patient is a 45-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes and primary hyperlipidemia. Her total cholesterol level is consistently above 200mg/dl and triglycerides are above 150mg/dl. She is postmenopausal and has undergone a hysterectomy. She is currently on mechanical contraception. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the study. She does not have secondary hyperlipidemia, morbid obesity, alcohol or drug abuse, acute or chronic inflammation, congestive heart failure (NYHA III or IV), unstable ischaemic heart disease, moderate or severe hypertension, cancer in the last 5 years, chronic kidney disease (stage III-V), or liver failure. Her alanine transferase levels are within the normal range, as are her creatine kinase, haemoglobin, platelet count, and white blood cell count. She is a compliant patient and willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy Chinese man with a BMI of 21 kg/m2 and a weight of 65 kg. He has no significant medical history and is not a smoker. He has not taken any prescription drugs within the past four weeks or over-the-counter medication within the past two weeks. He has not participated in any other clinical investigations within the past four weeks. He has not donated or lost more than 400 ml of blood within the past eight weeks. He has not had any significant illness within the past two weeks. He has no personal or close family medical history of clinically significant cardiac abnormalities. He has no history of acute or chronic bronchospastic disease or clinically significant drug allergy. He does not have any known hypersensitivity or severe adverse event to darifenacin or similar drugs. He does not have any surgical or medical condition that may significantly alter the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of drugs or which may jeopardize participation in the study. He does not have any immunodeficiency diseases, including a positive HIV or Hepatitis B surface antigen or Hepatitis C test result. He has not engaged in drug or alcohol abuse within the past 12 months. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

A 7-year-old Caucasian girl has been experiencing moderate to severe persistent allergic rhinitis symptoms for the past year. She presents with symptoms such as frequent sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, and itchy eyes. She has a history of seasonal allergies and has undergone skin tests that have confirmed her sensitization to aeroallergens. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days and is not on any immunotherapy treatment. She has no history of hypersensitivity to desloratadine or prednisolone, nor does she have any contraindications to corticosteroid use. She has no other clinically significant diseases such as hematopoietic, cardiovascular, renal, neurological, psychiatric or autoimmune disorders. She is not on any monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) and has not taken any oral antihistamines or decongestants in the past 15 days. She has not been treated with systemic corticosteroids in the last month and does not have uncontrolled asthma, chronic sinusitis, drug related rhinitis or nasal anatomic abnormalities. Her weight is 25 kg.

50-year-old African-American woman with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years. She takes medications for hypertension but has not achieved optimal blood pressure control. She has a history of diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia and is a current smoker. She has no history of coronary disease, cerebrovascular disease, or peripheral arterial occlusive disease, and has not been diagnosed with left ventricular hypertrophy. She has a serum creatinine level of 200 umol/L and no proteinuria. She is interested in participating in a study to help determine the prognosis of essential hypertension and is willing to undergo regular biomarker testing.

As a clinical trial specialist, it is important to note that this study is not recruiting patients, but rather medical and nursing staff who work on acute medical and surgical admissions at the Queens Medical Centre Nottingham. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable for this trial.

A 60-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is scheduled for robot-assisted prostatectomy in 3 weeks. He has no known allergy to magnesium and has never experienced chronic pain or taken opioids or NSAIDs. His medical history is unremarkable, and he has never experienced any cardiac or neurologic conditions. His renal and liver function tests are normal. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

Patient is a 32-year-old man with a diagnosis of schizophrenia for the last 5 years. He has been clinically stable with no change in his current antipsychotic medications. His PANSS and CGI scores meet the criteria for the study. He has a BMI of 25 kg/m2. He is sexually active and agrees to practice an effective method of birth control throughout the study. He does not have a history of alcohol or substance dependence, tardive dyskinesia, or neuroleptic malignant syndrome. He has no clinically significant medical illness and has not been treated with any protocol disallowed therapies. His screening laboratory and ECG results are within normal limits.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male living in and around Ahmedabad city, India with a body mass index (BMI) of 22. He has no significant medical history or any clinically significant abnormal findings during screening, medical history, physical examination, laboratory evaluations, 12- lead ECG and X-ray chest (P/A view) recordings. He does not have any known hypersensitivity or idiosyncratic reaction to Valsartan or any related drug. He has not taken any medicine, including herbal remedies, within 14 days before dosing in Period-I. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has not donated blood or received any investigational medicinal product or participated in a drug research study within a period of 90 days prior to the first dose of study medication. He has not consumed grapefruit or grapefruit products within 48 hours prior to dosing. He is willing to abstain from smoking during the study and has given voluntary written informed consent for participation in the trial.

The patient is a 40-year-old male diagnosed with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). He has been on nilotinib as first-line therapy for the past 18 months, and his disease is in sustained, good molecular response with a molecular response (MR3) of 0.01% on IS ratio. He has been compliant with his medication and has not experienced any adverse effects. He has no history of autologous or allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. A recent bone marrow biopsy shows no evidence of disease progression. He speaks fluent English.

A 32-year-old male Iraq War veteran visited the clinic with symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). He was deployed in Iraq for 12 months and experienced traumatic events during his service that still haunt him. He suffers from nightmares, flashbacks, and recurrent thoughts about the events that he experienced. He has been avoiding social situations and has been feeling increasingly isolated. He has tried talking to friends and family, but it doesn't seem to help. He has never been diagnosed with a traumatic brain injury. He is interested in participating in a study that compares Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction to a supportive therapy control group to help manage his PTSD symptoms.

Maria is a 45-year-old woman who works as a nurse in a hospital. She came to the clinic with symptoms of fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Her physical exam revealed a temperature of 38.5°C, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 93% on room air. She has no history of chronic disease and has not recently traveled outside of the country. She is married and has two children who are healthy. She has not been in contact with anyone who has tested positive for COVID-19. Her nasopharyngeal swab was taken for SARS CoV2 RT-PCR testing. She agreed to participate in the study and signed the informed consent form. The study nurse collected general and clinical data and two nasopharyngeal swabs were taken from her. One sample was used to test the prototype of the RT-LAMP and the second one was used for the classic RT-PCR. The results will be compared in a second step.

The patient is a 55 year old male who has been diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx. He has undergone surgery and radiation therapy, but the cancer has recurred and is now considered incurable with standard therapy. He has also received one course of platinum-based chemotherapy, but it was unsuccessful. He is experiencing difficulty swallowing, hoarseness, and weight loss. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 2, indicating that he is ambulatory and capable of self-care, but unable to work and requires some assistance with activities of daily living. He has no history of other malignancies and is not currently taking any medications for his cancer. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and understands the potential risks and benefits of the treatment.

A 52-year-old man with a history of hypertension has been taking amlodipine besylate tablets for the past 6 months to control his blood pressure. His doctor has recommended him for a clinical trial investigating the bioequivalence of a generic version of amlodipine besylate to the brand name version Norvasc®. He has no known allergies or adverse reactions to the medication and has not taken any enzyme-altering drugs. He is in good health and has no significant abnormalities in his physical examination or clinical laboratory results. He is willing to participate in the study to help improve the availability of affordable medications for patients with hypertension.

A 5-year-old boy was diagnosed with stage III Wilms tumor and scheduled for a major abdominal surgery. He has no known allergies or significant medical history. He is currently in good health and has an average weight and height for his age. His serum albumin level is within normal range. He has not been taking any psychotropic medication and does not have mental retardation. He is classified as an ASA II patient. The parents have given their informed consent to participate in the study.

43 yo F with a history of idiopathic primary pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) diagnosed via right heart catheterization within the last year. She is currently classified as functional class III and has a baseline 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) of 75 meters. She has not previously been treated with PDE-5 inhibitors. She has no significant valvular disease, history of cardiac arrest or respiratory arrest, and no history of chronic lung disease or restrictive lung disease. She is not currently taking nitrates or nitric oxide. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial evaluating the effects of oral sildenafil on mortality in adults with PAH.

A 42-year-old man is scheduled to undergo surgery for a hernia repair. During his visit with the anaesthetist, he reported a history of drinking 4-5 beers a day for the past year. He has never sought out treatment for alcohol addiction and does not believe he has a problem. He is a smoker and admits to occasional marijuana use. He is otherwise healthy and takes no medications. He is an electrician and enjoys spending time with his family on weekends. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with the requirements.

57 yo F with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with a recent diagnosis of impaired fasting glucose. She is a non-smoker and leads a sedentary lifestyle. Her BMI is 28 kg/m2. She is currently not taking any medications for lipid or glucose lowering. Her thyroid stimulating hormone, fasting triglycerides, creatinine, liver function tests, hematocrit, and white blood cell count are within normal limits. She has not used hormone replacement therapy in the past year. She is interested in participating in the study to determine if defects in GLP-1 may explain her abnormal EGP and diminished insulin secretion, and if increasing circulating GLP-1 levels with sitagliptin can reverse these defects.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy men, women, or diverse individuals between the ages of 18 and 70, with a BMI between 23 and 40 kg/m². Participants must have no history of diagnosed lymphedema, lipedema, or any indication for therapy with flat-knitted compression garments. They must also not have any skin infections, gangrene, or large coagulum in the leg vein. Participants should not have undergone surgery in the test area within the last 4 weeks, or have open wounds in the test area. All female or diverse participants of childbearing potential must either be surgically sterile or agree to use a reliable method of contraception. Participants should be willing to follow protocol requirements and provide conscious informed consent. The study will measure the fit of made-to-measure compression garments in healthy individuals for a maximum of 7 hours, simulating daily activities, and AE's will be documented throughout the study.

25 yo M with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia in remission, who is currently lacking a suitable unrelated donor for stem cell transplantation. The patient has been offered the option of a single or double-unit umbilical cord blood transplantation (UCBT) as a potential treatment option. The patient is in good general health and is able to tolerate a myeloablative conditioning regimen. The patient is willing to participate in a prospective and randomized study comparing the outcomes of single versus double unit UCBT for acute leukemia in remission. The patient is available to undergo transplantation at one of the allogeneic transplant centers in France and has access to at least 2 UCB units that are 4/6, 5.6 or 6/6 HLA identical to the patient and contain more than 3 x 107 nucleated cells per kilogram of recipient for the first unit and more than de 1.5 x 107 nucleated cells per kilogram of recipient for the second. The patient does not have a history of allogeneic stem cell transplantation or total body irradiation, and is not currently experiencing organ failure or a general status that would be incompatible with a myeloablative conditioning regimen. The patient is not pregnant and does not have a positive HIV serology.

A 58-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with painless hematuria for the past month. He underwent a cystoscopy and biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. He has no significant comorbidities and is not taking any medications. His renal function tests, AST, and ALT are within normal limits. He has no history of other cancers or immunosuppressive therapy. He is randomly assigned to receive either spinal anesthesia or general anesthesia for transurethral resection of the bladder tumor. He undergoes regular follow-up with urine analysis, urine culture, urine cytology, cystoscopy every 3 months, and CT urography every year for 2 years post-surgery to assess for recurrence of the bladder cancer.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been on hemodialysis for the past year due to end-stage renal disease. She has a history of diabetes and hypertension, which are well-controlled with medications. Her serum ferritin levels have been consistently elevated above 2000 ng/ml, and her transferrin saturation (TSAT) is above 30%. She has no history of malignancy or active infection requiring systemic antibiotic therapy. She is able to tolerate hemodialysis well and attends her sessions regularly. She has no known allergies to contrast agents used in MRI. She is informed that this study will involve the use of MRI to evaluate iron deposition in her organs, and that blood samples will be taken to measure various iron-related parameters. She is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

A 55-year-old male presents with a history of dyslipidemia and has been on lipid-lowering medications in the past. He has a family history of cardiovascular disease, but no other significant medical history. His LDL-C levels were 150 mg/dL, and his triglyceride levels were 280 mg/dL. The patient is willing to withdraw from any current anti-dyslipidemic medications or other prohibited medication for approximately 6 weeks prior to randomization (4 weeks prior to qualification visits) and for the duration of the study. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is not planning to become pregnant or breastfeed for the duration of the study. The patient is willing to commit to using a medically acceptable method of birth control such as oral contraception, intrauterine device (IUD), or a double-barrier method of contraception if the patient is female. The patient has no history of allergy, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to niacin, simvastatin, atorvastatin, ezetimibe, rosuvastatin, or their derivatives. The patient has no history of active gallbladder disease within the preceding 12 months, pancreatitis, liver disease, persistent uncontrolled or untreated severe hypertension, Type I or Type II diabetes, persistent uncontrolled or untreated hypothyroidism, arterial bleeding, unstable angina, myocardial infarction, coronary artery bypass graft surgery, or angioplasty within the preceding 6 months, stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or deep vein thrombosis (DVT) within the preceding 6 months, congestive heart failure NYHA class III or IV, active cancer within the last 5 years or a diagnosis of cancer within the last 5 years (excluding basal cell carcinoma), fibromyalgia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis, unexplained muscle pain or weakness, and/or discontinuation of a statin because of myalgia, and/or life expectancy < 2 years. The patient has no abnormalities of CPK elevation > 3xULN, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) > 1.3xULN, serum creatinine ≥ 1.5 mg/dL, creatinine clearance < 30 mL/min, as calculated using the Cockroft and Gault formula by the central laboratory, active gout symptoms and/or uric acid level > 1.3xULN, and/or active peptic ulcer disease at any of the Screening or Qualification Visits.

Patient is a child with a central motor disorder who is ambulant or stationary and is currently receiving treatment at the Rehabilitation Center Affoltern am Albis. The child should be able to understand test instructions and sit upright for at least 25 minutes. There should be minimal activity in the upper limb that will be assessed. The child should not have severe visual and/or auditory problems, nor should they have an acute lesion in the upper limb to be assessed

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who lives in a deprived neighborhood in Barcelona, Spain. She is sexually active and not currently using any form of contraception. She does not have any children and is not planning on getting pregnant within the next year. She is interested in learning more about contraception options but has limited access to healthcare resources. She is willing to participate in a community-based counseling intervention to improve her knowledge of contraceptive methods and improve her consistent use of very effective methods. She is open to learning about culturally-developed and theoretically-based brief counseling in a community setting.

52-year-old woman with a history of endometrial cancer diagnosed 2 years ago. She underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel, which resulted in a partial response. However, imaging studies showed progression of disease with new liver and lung metastases. She has no history of other malignancies, recent infections, or any cardiac disease. Her Karnofsky performance status is 80. She has no known allergies to ixabepilone, and all previous therapy directed at endometrial cancer was discontinued 21 days prior to the start of the study treatment. She has measurable disease that has progressed since her last chemotherapy. Additionally, she meets all other inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 70-year-old male who experienced sudden onset left-sided hemiparesis and difficulty speaking while at home. The patient's wife witnessed the onset of symptoms and immediately called emergency medical services (EMS). The EMS team arrived at the scene within 10 minutes of the call and assessed the patient. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is on antihypertensive medication. The EMS team evaluated the patient's RACE score and found it to be 7. The patient's vital signs are stable, and he is alert but unable to speak clearly. The patient's medical history and physical examination suggest the possibility of a large vessel occlusion. The EMS team estimates that the transportation time from the scene to the CSC is approximately 45 minutes, which is longer than the time to reach the nearest stroke unit or telemedicine hub. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial and agrees to participate.

35-year-old female presenting with complaints of chronic neck pain for the past 6 months. The pain is described as a constant ache with occasional sharp, shooting pain, and is rated 6/10 on the visual analog scale (VAS). The pain is localized to the upper trapezius muscle on the right side of the neck. The patient reports no previous history of neck fractures, radiculopathy, previous surgeries or needling treatments in the last 6 months, or psychiatric disease. The patient currently takes no analgesic medications and is willing to forgo such medication during the course of the study. The patient was diagnosed with an active myofascial trigger point in the right upper trapezius muscle. The patient has no other significant medical history and is willing to participate in a study evaluating the effectiveness of different dry needling dosages in the treatment of myofascial neck pain.

A 28-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his friend after he found him unconscious in his apartment. The patient is known to have a history of depression and is currently unemployed. According to his friend, he has been struggling with his mental health and has been taking paracetamol tablets in high doses for the past few days. The patient is not able to provide information about how many tablets he has taken. On admission, his vital signs are stable, but he is drowsy and unresponsive. The patient is intubated and started on NAC therapy. Blood tests reveal elevated liver enzymes, indicating potential liver damage. The patient is closely monitored over the next 24 hours, and his condition stabilizes. The patient is then transferred to the study team for further evaluation. The study team takes blood samples from the patient and runs tests to identify new biomarkers that can accurately predict liver injury. The patient is informed about the study and is able to provide consent to participate. The study team continues to monitor the patient's liver function and uses the new point-of-care test to detect any further liver damage.

A 38-year-old female presents with a history of glioblastoma multiforme, for which she has undergone surgery and radiotherapy. Despite previous treatment, the patient's cancer has progressed and she is now experiencing severe headaches and difficulty with speech and balance. Her Karnofsky performance score is 80%. The patient has not received any biologic therapy or endocrine therapy. She completed her last chemotherapy four weeks ago and has not had any nitrosoureas or mitomycin in the past six weeks. Hematopoietic function is normal, with a granulocyte count of 2,200/mm3 and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. Her liver function is within normal limits, with a bilirubin level of 1.8 mg/dL and SGOT level of 3 times normal. Her renal function is normal with a creatinine level of 1.1 mg/dL. She does not have any symptomatic pulmonary disease, and her FEV1 is 1.5 L. She has no other concurrent malignancies and is not currently pregnant or lactating. She has agreed to use effective contraception during the study.

A 45-year-old man presents with fatigue, weight loss, and night sweats for the past several weeks. Physical examination showed mild splenomegaly. His complete blood count showed a WBC count of 75,000/microl, hemoglobin of 11.9 g/dL, and a platelet count of 305,000/microl. Peripheral blood smear revealed leukocytosis with a left shift and basophilia. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) in the chronic phase. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is married and has two children. He is a non-smoker and rarely drinks alcohol. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is willing to participate in the study and complete all follow-up assessments.

A 63-year-old retired teacher with a family history of Alzheimer's disease. Her mother and two of her siblings were diagnosed with the disease in their 70s. The patient has been experiencing some memory lapses lately, but nothing that is significantly impacting her daily life. She completed a college degree in education and has been teaching for 30 years before retiring. She speaks fluent English and French. She is currently taking atorvastatin for high cholesterol. She has no history of heart disease or arrhythmia. She is in good physical health and exercises regularly. The patient is willing to undergo lumbar punctures and has no issues with genetic testing. She is determined to adhere to the study protocol and will limit her use of over-the-counter or prescription medicines that can prolong QTc interval. She has no history of alcohol or drug abuse.
