The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1 infection and compensated cirrhosis. He has previously received pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) and ribavirin (RBV) treatment for 4 weeks without achieving sustained viral response (SVR). He does not have co-infection with HIV or hepatitis B virus (HBV) and does not have a history of clinical hepatic decompensation. The patient is not currently using any systemic immunosuppressive agents and has no clinically significant illness or medical disorder that may interfere with treatment, assessment, or compliance with the protocol. The patient is willing to use specific contraceptive methods if sexually active and is not pregnant or nursing.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman living with HIV. She was diagnosed with HIV three years ago and has been receiving antiretroviral therapy. She has a history of irregular Pap test screening and has not had a Pap test for over a year. She is able to read and write in English and is willing to provide written consent to allow the research team to audit her medical records for Pap test use. She has not undergone a hysterectomy and is not currently pregnant.

A 45-year-old woman with a past medical history of diabetes and functional dyspepsia according to Rome III criteria presented at the clinic complaining of bloating, early satiety, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She has been experiencing these symptoms for over a year and is currently on a low-fat and low-fiber diet. Her gastric emptying test revealed delayed gastric emptying with t1/2 for solids ≥ 109 min. She did not have any oesophagitis, gastric atrophy, or erosive gastroduodenal lesions on endoscopy or any major co-morbidities. She is on insulin and metformin for diabetes management. She has no underlying psychiatric illness and is not taking any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, steroids, or drugs affecting gastric motility. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who complains about her appearance, particularly her face and skin. She spends hours examining herself in the mirror, searching for flaws that others might find unnoticeable. She feels devastated by her perceived imperfections and avoids social situations, fearing that others will judge her. She has tried many cosmetic procedures and spends most of her income on them. She has a history of depression and anxiety and has taken medication for it. Despite this, she still feels unhappy and unsatisfied with her appearance. She is currently not in a relationship and has difficulty maintaining friendships because of her social anxiety. The patient is well-groomed and appropriately dressed. She appears to be anxious and self-conscious during the assessment. She meets the DSM-5 criteria for BDD and is assessed as eligible to participate in the study.

A 52-year-old man came to the clinic with complaints of abdominal pain, jaundice, and anorexia. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the pancreas, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). He has no history of autoimmune diseases or psychiatric disorders. He has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and a HLA-A2 genotype. He has no history of previous malignancies or treatment for PDAC. He has received 8 cycles of FOLFIRINOX induction chemotherapy and has shown stable disease. He has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. He has no unresolved toxicities from previous anticancer therapy other than Grade 1 neuropathy. He has adequate organ function, with a normal white blood cell count, platelet count, and serum creatinine level. He has no active infections or bleeding disorders. He has not received any live vaccines in the past 30 days. He has not undergone major surgery within the past 28 days. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he is not under tutelage or guardianship. He has signed and dated the informed consent document and is willing and able to comply with protocol requirements.

A 68-year-old man who presents to the ER with complaints of shortness of breath and chest pain. He reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past few hours, and they have been getting progressively worse. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and he takes medication for both conditions. He denies any recent travel or sick contacts. On examination, he is found to be tachycardic and hypotensive. An ECG is done and shows ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads. He is diagnosed with an acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and emergent cardiac catheterization is recommended. The patient is anxious and concerned about his condition and the potential for adverse health events. He is eligible for this clinical trial as he is aged 65 or older and has an unplanned ER visit.

A 53-year-old woman was diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis 7 years ago and has been receiving treatment on an outpatient basis. She experiences pain, stiffness, and swelling in her fingers, wrists, and elbows. She has been taking methotrexate and prednisone for the past 4 years, which has helped alleviate some of her symptoms. She is a non-smoker, has no known allergies, and exercises regularly. She has no history of fractures or luxations in her hands. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. She is interested in participating in this study to help advance the understanding of the disease and potentially improve treatment options for others.

Newborn infants above 32 weeks of age and less than 36 hours old who are admitted to the neonatal ward with suspected or probable clinical signs of illness will be considered for blood sampling in this clinical trial. The study will evaluate the use of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) as a decision support tool for health care personnel to determine when to send a potentially sick newborn to a higher level neonatal unit. The study will involve the use of the new point-of-care technology for LDH analysis called "Hilda Neo" by the Swedish company Calmark Sweden AB. The LDH test will be performed using an easy-to-use consumable test card together with an "App" on an ordinary smartphone, which will provide the result within minutes. The study will also include daily LDH tests at the routine clinical laboratory to evaluate the usefulness of LDH when deciding if a baby is ready for transfer from the NICU to ordinary care. The study will include a total of 120+20 patients, and parental consent is required for participation. Infants with gestational age less than 33 weeks and postnatal age above 36 hours will be excluded from the study.

A 28-year-old female college student who is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the effects of commonly used medications on mood and choice. She is in good health and has never been diagnosed with a psychiatric or substance use condition. She has no known allergies to any administered drugs and does not smoke. She is fluent in English and has a Body Mass Index (BMI) within the range of 18.5 to 35. She uses a hormonal contraceptive and is not planning to become pregnant in the near future. She has no history of any other serious diseases or conditions that might affect life expectancy or make it difficult to successfully manage the subjects according to the protocol. She is currently not taking any medications that would interfere with the study participation.

A 49-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation (alloSCT) 6 months ago. He initially responded well to the transplant but recently developed a relapse of AML. The patient has received multiple lines of chemotherapy with no response. He currently has persistent disease post-alloSCT and is no longer receiving immunosuppression therapy. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and CD3+ donor chimerism of 40%. He has no evidence of GVHD and has normal renal and liver function. The patient has signed written informed consent and is interested in participating in this clinical trial to receive nivolumab treatment for his relapsed AML.

A 45-year-old man was admitted to a detox facility due to alcohol addiction. He has a history of alcohol abuse for the past 10 years, with no history of drug abuse. He has been consuming 1-2 bottles of whiskey a day for the past year. He has never taken acetaminophen before. He is divorced, has two children, and is currently unemployed. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He has not participated in any clinical trials in the past three months. He is willing to provide written informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was admitted to the intensive care unit due to hypoxemic respiratory failure. He has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse. He was diagnosed with ARDS on previously healthy lungs and has a PaO2/FIO2 ratio of less than 200 mm Hg. The patient has no previous intubation and is not currently experiencing hypercapnia or left ventricular failure. He is affiliated with the French social welfare system and has provided informed consent for the study. The patient is not pregnant, does not have a tracheostomy, and is not currently on home noninvasive ventilation. He has not received NIV sessions for ARDS before hospital admission and has no history of recent gastric or esophageal surgery.

45 year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV-1 infection who has been receiving anti-HIV drugs for the past twelve months. The patient is currently experiencing a decline in CD4+ and CD8+ T cell counts and has a detectable viral load. The patient has never received any HIV vaccines or immunogens in the past. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Remune + Amplivax in reducing viral load and increasing immunity against HIV-1. The patient has no history of alcohol or drug abuse and is willing to comply with study requirements. The patient is aware that the study is double-blind and randomized, and that he may receive either the treatment group Remune + Amplivax or the placebo group Amplivax. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of heart failure (NYHA II) despite adequate therapy. He is scheduled to undergo cardial contractility modulation (CCM) implantation. He has an implanted pacemaker and has given written informed consent. His recent blood work shows a hemoglobin level of 12 mg/dL. He has no history of chronic atrial fibrillation or flutter, mechanic tricuspid valve prosthesis, or known inflammatory or infiltrative illnesses. He has no access issues via subclavian vein and is not currently being treated for acute myocardial ischemia or acute coronary syndrome. He does not have aortic or tricuspid valve issues or any significant ectopy, as defined by less than 8,900 PVCs during 24 hours at the beginning of Holter monitoring. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has not recently experienced heart failure after sepsis.

An 68-year-old woman was recently hospitalized due to heart failure. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes, and has been taking ACE inhibitors and beta blockers to manage her heart condition. She lives in the Genk-Hasselt region and is able to communicate effectively in Dutch. Her left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 38%, indicating severe systolic heart failure. She is able to use a smartphone and is interested in participating in a study that would help her monitor and manage her heart condition more effectively. She does not have a cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) device and is not currently enrolled in a cardiac rehabilitation program. Her renal function is normal with an eGFR of 60ml/min/kg. She does not have severe COPD.

A 45-year-old male presents to the clinic with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years. He reports occasional episodes of exertional dyspnea and stenocardia, despite being on antihypertensive medications (an ACE inhibitor and a calcium channel blocker). He denies any history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism, and smoking. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities, and blood pressure is well controlled. The patient is informed about a clinical trial aimed at finding early predictors of myocardial dysfunction in hypertensive patients with normal resting echocardiography and without changes in epicardial coronary arteries in coronary angiography. The study will include tests such as electrocardiogram, 24-hour blood pressure monitoring, echocardiography at rest and during submaximal exercise, flow-mediated dilatation, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and measurement of serum markers such as cystatin C, cardiotrophin-1, metalloproteinases (MMP-2, MMP-7, MMP-8, MMP-9), Procollagen III N-Terminal Propeptide (PIIINP), Syndecan 4 (SDC4), and NT-proBNP. The patient is eligible for the study as he meets the inclusion criteria of being between 40-60 years old, having stage I or II primary hypertension according to the European Society of Hypertension, and having no exclusion criteria such as coronary artery disease, unstable hypertension, or NYHA class III-IV heart failure. The patient is informed about the potential benefits of the study, including the possibility of early detection of abnormalities and optimal treatment for hypertensive patients with asymptomatic myocardial dysfunction. The patient gives written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing dyspepsia and stomach pain for the past few months. She has a history of peptic ulcer disease and is currently taking proton pump inhibitors to manage her symptoms. She has not received any treatment for Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection before. The patient is generally healthy, with no known allergies to any medication. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and does not have any history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has confirmed H. pylori infection through a positive breath test. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of two different treatment regimens for H. pylori eradication. The patient has not taken any antibiotics or bismuth salts in the past four weeks. The patient will be required to attend regular appointments and follow-up visits to monitor the effectiveness of the treatment.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a history of alcohol abuse and chronic liver disease. He presents with jaundice, coagulopathy, and ascites that developed within the last 4 weeks. He has also started experiencing episodes of encephalopathy. The patient has no history of hepatocellular carcinoma or portal vein thrombosis. He is willing to participate in the study and has not been diagnosed with sepsis or multi-organ failure. The patient's hepatic encephalopathy is currently at grade 2.

The patient is a 40-year-old male diagnosed with IgA nephropathy 2 years ago. He has been on ACE inhibitor for the past 6 months to maintain adequate glucose control. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is controlled with medication. There is no history of diabetes, cancer, or transplant. His recent biopsy confirmed IgA nephropathy. He has normal liver and bone marrow function. His recent blood tests revealed that his eGFR is at 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and ACR is 2000 mg/g. He has no history of cerebrovascular events, aneurysms, or left-sided cardiac disease. He is an alert male with no acute distress. His BP: 130/80, HR: 78/min and BMI: 29. His abdomen is soft with no tenderness. The lower extremities are normal with no edema.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently hospitalized due to acute heart failure. He complains of shortness of breath even when resting and has pulmonary congestion. His blood pressure is 130/80, and his renal function is impaired with an eGFR of 50 mL/min/1.73m2. He has no history of recent major surgery, acute coronary syndrome, or other investigational drug use. He is able to provide informed consent for the trial. There is no evidence of fever or sepsis, and he has not suffered any recent major neurologic events.

A 35-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation (SCT) with a human leukocyte antigen (HLA) matched unrelated donor. The patient's SCT was complicated by acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) of the skin, treated with prednisone and tacrolimus. The patient is currently at day 21 post-transplant, and the clinical status allows tapering of steroids to less than 0.5mg/kg prednisone or other steroid equivalent. The patient has not developed any viral infections or reactivation, and does not have acute GVHD grades II-IV. The patient has not received infusion of ATG or alemtuzumab within 2 weeks of VST infusion, and alemtuzumab levels are less than or equal to 0.15. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial for prophylactic infusions of viral specific T-lymphocytes (VSTs) to prevent viral infections after allogeneic SCT.

A 62-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with shortness of breath, cough with sputum production, and wheezing for the past 3 years. He has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is currently on inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids. He has had no hospitalizations or exacerbations in the last month and is clinically stable. The patient is interested in participating in a study investigating the effects of pulmonary rehabilitation on lung function in patients with COPD. The patient has no concomitant respiratory diseases, severe psychiatric conditions, neurologic/musculoskeletal conditions, or unstable cardiovascular disease. The patient is able to provide informed consent.

25-year-old healthy male with no known history of cardiac, pulmonary, or neurological disease, and not currently on any medication, including opioids. He has a BMI of 23 and no history of allergies to naloxone, remifentanil, fentanyl analogues, or metoclopramide. He has not participated in any medical clinical trial where opioids have been used in the last 30 days or any other medicinal clinical trial where follow-up has not been completed. He is willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the trial and has signed and dated the informed consent.

32-year-old female with a history of opioid use disorder for the past 2 years presents seeking treatment for her addiction. She has been on buprenorphine maintenance for the past 6 months and is currently buprenorphine-maintained. She is willing and motivated to receive antagonist therapy and is willing to abide by the contraception requirements for the duration of the study. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m^2 and is able to provide informed consent and government-issued identification. She has no history of seizures or anticonvulsant therapy and has not used naltrexone (oral or VIVITROL) within the 90 days prior to Day -5. She has no current diagnosis of schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or untreated and unstable major depressive disorder. She is not currently physiologically dependent on any psychoactive substance (except opioids, caffeine, or nicotine) requiring medical intervention for detoxification. She has no history of hypersensitivity or adverse reaction to buprenorphine, naltrexone, VIVITROL, or naloxone.

Patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with advanced heart failure and is experiencing symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and edema. Despite receiving standard medical therapy, his condition has deteriorated and he has developed cardiogenic shock. He is being evaluated for mechanical circulatory support device (MCSD) therapy, including the possibility of receiving a ventricular assist device (VAD) or heart transplant. The patient has provided informed consent to participate in the RESCUE registry, which aims to gather information on patients who receive MCSD therapy for cardiogenic shock. The registry seeks to improve the understanding and application of MCSD therapy, and to develop consensus "best practice" guidelines to improve clinical management and reduce complications. The patient will be followed and monitored for outcomes related to his MCSD therapy.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who enjoys outdoor activities such as running, hiking, and playing soccer. He lives in an area with high sun exposure and has a history of sunburns in the past. He uses sunscreen regularly with SPF 50 or higher but often finds that it feels greasy and uncomfortable on his skin. He has no known allergies or sensitivity to sunscreen ingredients or other materials. He has not participated in any clinical or subjective product performance study in the last 30 days and has not used any Investigational New Drug in the last month. He does not have respiratory allergies or asthma.

A 45-year-old female teacher was recently diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis. She has been experiencing fatigue, nausea, and abdominal discomfort for the past few months. She has no significant past medical history, and her family history is negative for liver disease. She is not a smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is currently taking over-the-counter pain medications for her abdominal pain. Her laboratory results show elevated liver enzymes (AST and ALT) and high levels of IgG. A liver biopsy was performed, which revealed mild lymphocytic piecemeal necrosis (interface hepatitis). She has not received any immunosuppressive therapy yet. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options.

The patient is a 58-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 years ago. She underwent a lumpectomy and radiation therapy, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. She completed her chemotherapy regimen 2 years ago and has been on tamoxifen since then. However, she has developed metastatic disease, with extensive bone involvement and a solitary pulmonary nodule. She underwent a CT-guided biopsy of the pulmonary nodule, which revealed metastatic breast cancer. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and she is experiencing mild pain in her ribs and back, which is well-controlled with acetaminophen. Her laboratory studies are remarkable for creatinine clearance of 80 mL/min per Cockcroft-Gault formula, total bilirubin within normal limits, AST/SGOT and ALT/SGPT each less than 1.5 x ULN, and adequate hematologic function. Her echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 55%. She is willing to use medically acceptable methods of birth control for the duration of the study treatment, including 30 days after the last dose of SRF231. She is able to adhere to the study visit schedule and all protocol requirements. She has signed and dated the institutional review board (IRB)/independent ethics committee (IEC)-approved informed consent form before any screening procedures are performed. She has not received an anti-CD47 antibody or SIRPalpha targeted therapy in the past.

A 26-year-old female who is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 21 kg/m2 presents to the clinic for a pharmacokinetic study. She has no significant medical history and has normal vital signs and skin examination. She has undergone general biochemistry, hematology and urinalysis which all come back normal. She is interested in participating in the study and has given her informed consent. She is not pregnant and weighs 60 kg.

A 35-year-old male came to the clinic complaining of repetitive behaviors and involuntary movements. He reported that he had been experiencing these symptoms for the last 5 years and that they have been interfering with his daily activities. He also reported that he sometimes feels an "urge" to perform these behaviors and that they are often accompanied by sensory phenomena. He has never been treated with any medications for these symptoms. He is otherwise healthy and currently taking no medications. He is fluent in English and does not have any disabilities that would prevent him from completing the study procedures. His electrocardiogram (EKG) and liver function tests came back normal. He did not report any allergies or hypersensitivity to medications, nor does he have any heart disease, electrolyte imbalances, or hepatic impairment. He meets the diagnostic criteria for a tic disorder according to DSM-5 criteria, and his symptoms are rated as moderate to severe.

A 52-year-old female patient with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (oropharynx) treated with concomitant radiochemotherapy 3 months ago is being sought for a clinical trial. The patient should not have undergone a cervical CT with injection of iodinated contrast for therapeutic monitoring within the last 14 days. The patient must not have any uncontrolled infectious diseases or allergy to iodine. The patient's renal clearance should be at least 30ml/min according to Cockcroft. The patient must provide written informed consent and be affiliated with a social security scheme. The patient must not have any history of malignancy, including head and neck carcinomas, previously treated outside the basal cell cancer or cervical cancer, treated and cured. The patient must not be pregnant or breastfeeding, and effective contraception must be ensured in reproductive years. The patient must not have any medical or psychological condition that may compromise their ability to participate in the study or submit to medical monitoring for geographical, social, or psychic reasons.

The patient is a 46-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma who needs to undergo autologous blood stem cell transplant. He has completed his initial therapy for the primary disease and is now eligible for stem cell mobilization using bortezomib and G-CSF. His platelet count is within normal limits, and his absolute neutrophil count is above 1.0x109/L. He has no history of myocardial infarction or heart failure and has no significant ECG abnormalities. He has never been treated with VELCADE in the past 30 days or radiation therapy within 3 weeks before randomization. He is willing to practice effective methods of contraception during the study treatment period and 30 days after the last dose of VELCADE. The patient has given informed consent and understands that he may withdraw his consent at any time without prejudice to future medical care.

The patient is a 55-year-old male veteran who has been a heavy smoker for the past 35 years. He has attempted to quit smoking several times in the past but has been unsuccessful in his previous attempts to quit using nicotine replacement therapy. He has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension. The patient reports feeling depressed and anxious, particularly when he tries to quit smoking. He is interested in participating in a research study to evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of two mood-focused adjunctive treatments aimed at reducing and potentially ceasing smoking behavior.

This is a 52 year-old female who was recently diagnosed with stage IVB cervical cancer. She reports experiencing pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, and difficulty urinating. A biopsy confirmed invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix. She has not undergone any prior chemotherapy or radiation treatments. Her Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score is 1 and her Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) is 80. She has no known allergies to chemotherapeutic drugs and her hemodynamic indices are within normal limits. The patient has been informed of the study and has signed the informed consent form. She is willing to undergo systemic chemotherapy followed by primary lesion radiotherapy as a part of this clinical trial.

The patient is a 65 year old sedentary man with a BMI of 30 kg/m2. He visits his primary care physician with concerns about his declining cognitive abilities and struggles with memory retention. He has no history of diabetes, familial hypercholesterolemia or any other medical condition that may interfere with the study. His fasting plasma glucose, serum total cholesterol and triacylglycerol levels are all within normal range. He is a non-smoker and does not consume more than 3 alcoholic beverages per day. He is not currently taking any medication to treat blood pressure, lipid or glucose metabolism. He is willing to give up being a blood donor from 8 weeks before the start of the study, during the study and for 4 weeks after completion of the study. He has no history of difficult venipuncture. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his cognitive abilities and is willing to commit to the 8-week aerobic-based exercise program.

As this is a clinical trial for an after-school program, there is not a patient description required. Instead, the eligibility criteria state that the study participants must be children in grades 3-5 (aged 8-12) who are enrolled in a YMCA after-school program. The exclusion criteria indicate that children who have any cardiovascular, metabolic, or neurological disorders that would affect their ability to participate in the program or testing will not be eligible to participate.

I apologize, but there is no patient involved in this clinical trial as it is focused on adapting an evidence-based team approach for school mental health teams. The study is seeking mental health providers, teachers, school leaders, and community mental health agency leaders as participants to explore the feasibility, acceptability, and utility of the adapted approach on inter-professional collaboration, teamwork, and student outcomes in eight schools.

48-year-old female diagnosed with stage I endometrial cancer with a BMI of 35 kg/m^2. She is nulliparous, and her periods were regular before the diagnosis. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, well-controlled with medications. Her medical history is negative for musculoskeletal, cardiorespiratory, or neurological diseases that preclude participation in exercise. She is self-ambulatory and does not use any assistive walking devices. The patient has no history of smoking or drug use. She is married and lives with her husband and two children. She is currently employed as a teacher and leads a sedentary lifestyle. She is concerned about her weight and is willing to participate in the study to promote weight loss. The patient has a good understanding of the study requirements and is willing to comply with the exercise and diet regimen. Her physician has assessed her and determined that she is not a candidate for immediate hysterectomy due to her desire to preserve fertility. She has agreed to take progestin agents to control her disease while the intervention is ongoing.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who is a veteran of the United States Armed Forces. He has no known acute or chronic ocular issues and is seeking routine eye care services. He is a patient at the Atlanta VA Medical Center (VAMC) New Comprehensive Eye Clinic. He has no difficulty with technology and is comfortable using electronic devices. He will sign informed consent to participate in the study and undergo the Technology-based Eye Care Services (TECS) protocol, followed by a standard face to face ophthalmologic exam on the same day.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who is a moderate drinker, consuming approximately 10 standard drinks per week on average. He has no history of drug or alcohol dependence in the past 12 months and has never received treatment for substance use disorder. He has a body mass index (BMI) of 24.5 kg/m2, within the range of 19.0 to 34.0 kg/m2 required for enrollment in the study. His vital signs are within the normal range and he has no history of any condition where alcohol consumption is contraindicated. He denies any recent use of illicit drugs or any prescription medications that may interfere with the study. He is willing to abstain from alcohol consumption for 24 hours prior to the study visit and is able to provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who recently experienced a seizure and was transported to the emergency department by ambulance. She is conscious but confused and disoriented. She has no history of renal failure or hepatic impairment, but she is not sure if she is pregnant or not. She is currently not taking any medications, and there are no other contraindications to study enrollment. The patient is a candidate for enrollment in the STILL study, which will assess the effectiveness of intravenous levetiracetam and lorazepam in managing seizures in the ED setting. The study will enroll adults over the age of 18 who have had a seizure within an hour of ED arrival and do not have hypotension. The patient will be classified into the SE or non-SE group depending on their clinical presentation. The study will compare IV LEV vs. the current standard-care of placebo in non-SE patients and [IV LEV + lorazepam 2mg] vs. [lorazepam 3 mg] in SE patients. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and side effects of the medications in achieving seizure control.

A 28-year-old man has been diagnosed with epilepsy for 4 years. He experiences frequent nocturnal seizures that often go unnoticed, and he has been hospitalized several times due to complications such as tongue biting and aspiration pneumonia. His current medication regimen includes levetiracetam and clobazam, but he continues to experience seizures despite optimal dosing. He lives with his parents, who are concerned for his safety and often check on him during the night. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a novel seizure detection system that could potentially improve his safety and quality of life. He is willing to undergo monitoring with scalp electrodes and have a duplicate novel medical device placed in his bedroom for the duration of the trial. The patient understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing tension headaches for the past 6 months. She describes the pain as a dull, achy sensation that feels like pressure around her forehead and temples. She experiences these headaches on most days and they can last for several hours. She has tried over-the-counter pain relievers, but they only provide temporary relief. She has no history of head trauma or cervical spine problems. She works as a computer programmer and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. She has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to test the effectiveness of manual therapy vs exercises with foam rolling for tension headache.

The patient is a 72-year-old Caucasian man who has been experiencing memory loss for the past year. He has difficulty remembering recent events and often forgets appointments. His family members have noticed that he repeats himself and asks the same questions repeatedly. He also has been experiencing difficulty with word finding and struggles to communicate effectively. There is no history of stroke or other neurological disorders in his family. He reports no hearing or visual impairments. He is retired and lives alone. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medication. He is willing to undergo MRI procedures for research purposes. His MMSE score is 23.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). He has been recommended for surgery, but there are currently no other effective treatment options for advanced HCC. He has no other major systemic diseases or coagulopathies. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the use of autologous peripheral blood monocyte-derived dendritic cells (DCs) pulsed with autologous tumor lysate to elicit T cell cytotoxicity against HCC cells ex vivo. The patient will be required to provide peripheral blood for generating the DCs and undergo HCC primary culture. The DCs will be derived from peripheral blood monocytes by triggering differentiation with recombinant human granulocyte macrophage colony stimulating factor (rhGM-CSF) and interleukin-4 (rhIL-4) to immature DCs. Immature DCs will be pulsed with autologous HCC cell lysates and matured by using a cytokine cocktail. The patient will also undergo T cell proliferation and cytotoxicity tests against primarily cultured HCC cells. The patient understands the potential risks and benefits of participating in the trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been smoking 20 cigarettes per day for the last 10 years. She is motivated to quit smoking and plans to do so in the next month. She has tried quitting before, but has always relapsed within a few weeks. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will provide her with nicotine patches and counseling to help her quit smoking. She is comfortable with using a phone-based IVR system to record her progress and is willing to complete monthly questionnaires online or on paper. She speaks and writes English fluently and is a US citizen. She does not use any other tobacco products and has not used any smoking cessation medication or counseling in the past month. She does not have any medical conditions that would prevent her from using nicotine patches. She does not work overnight shifts and has not used electronic cigarettes in the past month.

The patient is a 35-year-old male veteran who served in the OEF/OIF. He has been diagnosed with mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) due to an improvised explosive device (IED) explosion that occurred during his deployment. He has been experiencing sleep disturbances, including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, and waking up early. He scored 40 on the MOS-Sleep Scale (MOS-SS). The patient has also been experiencing chronic pain and PTSD symptoms, including anxiety, depression, and intrusive thoughts related to his deployment experiences. He has no history of serious psychiatric comorbidity, suicidal intent or inpatient psychiatric admission in the last 3 months. The patient has no progressive/advanced neurodegenerative disease or terminal illness. His chronic medical conditions are stable, and he is not currently taking any medication for sleep apnea or substance dependence disorder. He does not have narcolepsy or frequent nocturia.

72 yo F with end-stage renal disease secondary to diabetic nephropathy, currently receiving hemodialysis three times a week at a dialysis center. Patient reports difficulty with the current dialysis regimen due to transportation issues and desire for more independence. Patient has been receiving counseling on the possibility of transitioning to peritoneal dialysis (PD) and has expressed interest in this option. However, patient reports concerns about decreased manual dexterity and visual acuity, which may impact the ability to perform necessary tasks for PD. Patient has no history of PD and has never used a connection-assist device. Past Medical History: Type 2 Diabetes, Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia, End-Stage Renal Disease.

A 68-year-old male presents with complaints of fatigue, weight loss, fever, and night sweats. He reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past several months. The patient has a history of polycythemia vera (PV) which was diagnosed 8 years ago, and following that he was diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis (MF) 3 years ago. He has been on hydroxyurea treatment for his PV and ruxolitinib for his MF but he has not experienced any significant improvement in his symptoms. On examination, there is hepatosplenomegaly present. The spleen measures 10 cm below the costal margin. His blood work shows that he has anemia with hemoglobin level of 8.2 g/dL and a high white blood cell count (WBC) of 32,000/uL. His circulating blasts are 5%. He is currently on furosemide and enalapril for his hypertension. He is able to perform self-care, has adequate bone marrow reserve, and is not a candidate for stem cell transplantation. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for the treatment of his MF.

A 45 yo F with a history of high triglyceride levels, but no other significant medical history, presents as a potential candidate for a clinical trial to determine the effectiveness of n3 LC-PUFA-enriched yogurt in reducing cardiovascular risk factors and inflammatory biomarkers. The patient reports no current use of blood-diluting or lipid-lowering medications or glucocorticoids, and has no history of gastrointestinal or metabolic diseases such as diabetes mellitus or hyper- and hypothyroidism. The patient also reports no known allergies or food intolerances, and does not take dietary supplements such as fish oil capsules or vitamin E. The patient does not smoke, engage in high levels of physical activity, or consume alcohol on a daily basis. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial and can be considered for participation.

A 48-year-old female patient presented with a 2-year history of joint pain, tenderness, and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and ankles. She also reported fatigue, morning stiffness lasting more than an hour, and mild fever. She had no family history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The patient was previously diagnosed with hypertension, and she is currently taking enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide. The patient has no history of diabetes mellitus or other autoimmune diseases. The patient has been receiving methotrexate and sulphasalazine for the past 6 months, but the disease activity remains high based on the DAS28 score. She is a non-smoker and denies any history of alcohol consumption. Her vital signs were within normal limits, and the physical exam revealed swelling and tenderness in the proximal interphalangeal joints, metacarpophalangeal joints, and wrists bilaterally. The clinical trial team will evaluate her eligibility for the trial based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 27-year-old female who suffers from seasonal allergic rhinitis with symptoms that require pharmacologic therapy during the ragweed pollen season. She has a documented allergy to ragweed pollen and experiences a total symptom score of at least 18 points. She has no history of nasal anatomic deformities or acute sinusitis within 30 days of Period 2. She has not initiated or advanced an immunotherapy regimen, and has not received immunotherapy injections within 48 hours of pollen exposure. She has no impaired hepatic function or history of malignancy. She is not intolerant to histamines and does not have asthma requiring medication more than occasionally.

A 5-day-old male infant was admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of congenital heart disease. The baby was born at 38 weeks of gestation through normal vaginal delivery. The baby's birth weight was 3.2 kg. The baby's echocardiography revealed a complex congenital heart disease that required surgery under extracorporeal circulation. The baby is currently hospitalized in the preoperative period at the Nantes University Hospital. There is no history of respiratory distress or any other significant medical history. The baby is not intubated and has not received any inotropic medication. The baby's vital signs are stable, and there is no evidence of preoperative instability. The parents have given written consent for their baby to participate in the clinical trial. The baby is suitable to be transported for an MRI without risk.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who has been experiencing knee pain for several months. He has been previously diagnosed with osteoarthritis of the knee and has been taking over-the-counter pain relievers to manage his symptoms. However, his pain has become more severe and has started to affect his daily activities, such as walking and climbing stairs. He has no known allergies to any medication. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication daily to manage it. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He lives with his wife and two adult children. He is retired and enjoys gardening and walking his dog.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was diagnosed with coronary artery disease (CAD) 6 months ago. She recently experienced chest pain and underwent an angiogram that confirmed multi-vessel CAD. She is scheduled for an elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. She has a medical history of hypertension, for which she takes amlodipine and lisinopril. She also has a history of hyperlipidemia and is on statin therapy. She has no history of heart failure, arrhythmia, or valvular heart disease. Her echocardiogram shows diastolic dysfunction with an E/E' ratio of 16. She has no history of pulmonary disease or renal disease. She is not a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is interested in participating in the study to help with the advancement of research on fluid responsiveness in patients with CAD and diastolic dysfunction.

A 57-year-old Caucasian woman was diagnosed with a stroke in the left hemisphere of her brain a year ago. She experiences difficulty with using her right arm and hand, which has limited her independence in performing daily tasks. She has undergone traditional physical therapy but has not seen significant improvement in her mobility. She is interested in participating in a new rehabilitation approach called Action Observation Treatment (AOT) that is based on mirror neuron system (MNS) to rebuild motor function despite injuries by engaging the brain regions active during action execution in individuals with limited mobility. She has never experienced AOT before and is willing to participate in this study. She has undergone MRI to confirm the diagnosis of stroke and her cognitive function is sufficient to understand the experimental instructions. Her Chedoke-McMaster stroke Assessment Scale score is greater than 1, indicating the presence of some residual movement in her affected upper limb. She provides informed written consent to participate in the study. She does not have severe sensory deficits in the paretic upper limb or cognitive impairment or behavioral dysfunction. She has no other current severe medical problems that would exclude her from the study.

A 22-year-old college student at Logan University is interested in participating in a clinical trial for vibration therapy effects on muscle firing patterns. The student is pursuing a degree in health sciences and has no history of ankle injury or surgery. She is an active individual who enjoys running and practicing yoga. She has no history of systemic illnesses that affect balance and does not take prescription or herbal muscle stimulants, relaxants or other medications that could affect her balance. The student has no visual or vestibular conditions that would affect her balance. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in the study to help further the research on the effects of vibration therapy on muscle firing patterns.

The patient is a 57-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. She was diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia and sepsis. Her NEWS2 score was 7, and her clinician determined that immediate intravenous fluid resuscitation was necessary. She has no known allergies or adverse reactions to any medications. She has no history of chronic renal replacement therapy, traumatic brain injury, or permanent incapacity. She is not undergoing palliative or end-of-life care, and she has no religious beliefs precluding the administration of human albumin solution or balanced crystalloid. She has never been enrolled in this clinical trial, and she has not participated in any CTIMP studies within the last 30 days.

A 29 year old woman has been diagnosed with Crohn's Disease for over a year. She has been experiencing abdominal pain, diarrhea, and nausea frequently. Her Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) score is between 220-400. She has not taken any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or corticosteroid enemas within the past month. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to try and improve her symptoms.

32 year old female smoker who has been smoking for 18 months, averaging 20 cigarettes per day with a recent carbon monoxide level of 14 ppm. She is currently using a contraceptive method and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has no history of heart disease, renal or hepatic diseases, and has not been on any psychotropic medications. She has no history of major depression, bipolar affective disorder, schizophrenia or panic disorder. She has not used any drugs or treatments for drug or alcohol addiction within the past 5 years, and has no known allergies to varenicline. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test the effects of varenicline and nicotine interactions in humans.

The patient is a 35 year-old female who has been suffering from chronic pain in the jaw and facial muscles for the past 6 months. She reports that the pain is worse in the morning and improves throughout the day. She also complains of difficulty chewing and opening her mouth fully. She has not received any treatment for her symptoms yet. She has a history of dental caries and has undergone multiple dental procedures in the past. She takes over-the-counter pain medications occasionally for her symptoms. She has no known allergies and is not currently pregnant. She does not have any significant medical history or use any medications regularly.

A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer after a routine mammogram. She is otherwise healthy with no history of cancer in her family. Her cancer is HR-positive and HER2-negative, as confirmed by biopsy. She has no metastatic disease and is eligible for surgery. She has not received any prior treatment for breast cancer and has no active infections or serious concurrent illnesses. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed informed consent. She has good bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. Her performance status is good (ECOG scale ≤ 1). She has no history of psychiatric disorders or altered mental status that may interfere with the study process. She does not have any gastrointestinal disorders that may interfere with drug absorption. She has a paraffin-embedded tumor block (FFPE) taken at diagnostic biopsy for Ki67 determination (IHC).

A 55-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with Grade IV glioma (GBM) and completed the prescribed standard of care regimen of radiation and temozolomide (TMZ) treatment. He is currently eligible for adjuvant TMZ treatment based on the current standard of care. He has a Karnofsky rating of 80 and is able to communicate effectively during the ExAblate BBBD (Blood Brain Barrier Disruption) procedure. He has no history of cardiac disease, hypertension or significant depression. He is not receiving any other concurrent therapies such as chemotherapy wafers, immunotoxins, regionally administered gene or viral therapies, immunotherapies, focal irradiation with brachytherapy, stereotactic radiosurgery, laser interstitial thermotherapy, and tumor treatment fields therapy. He has no history of a bleeding disorder, coagulopathy, spontaneous tumor hemorrhage, cerebral or systemic vasculopathy, drug or alcohol use disorder, active seizure disorder or epilepsy, or significant liver dysfunction. He is not on anti-coagulant therapy or medications known to increase the risk of hemorrhage. He is not pregnant and has no non-MRI-compatible implanted devices. The patient is willing and able to attend all study visits and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months.

63F with history of systolic dysfunction, presenting with decompensated heart failure. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, and is currently taking lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. She has a Medtronic device with Thoracic Impedance Monitoring capabilities implanted. She reports shortness of breath on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. She denies chest pain, palpitations, and syncope. On physical examination, she has elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral crackles on lung auscultation, and lower extremity edema. Her blood pressure is 140/90 mmHg, heart rate is 90 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. Labs reveal elevated BNP and NT-proBNP levels. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with COPD grade D according to the GOLD Guidelines Revised 2011. He is a current smoker with a history of smoking for the past 35 years with a pack-year of 40. He has been prescribed an inhaled combination therapy for COPD (inhaled corticosteroid / long acting β2-agonist bronchodilator) for the past 2 months. He complains of difficulty in performing morning activities such as dressing up and brushing his teeth due to shortness of breath. He has experienced exacerbation of COPD symptoms in the past month and has a history of allergic rhinitis. He has no history of lung carcinoma or any other respiratory condition that may limit the airflow circulation. He is willing and able to complete the CDLM questionnaires and record the values showed on the pedometer screen.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with severe haemophilia B. He has been experiencing chronic pain and functional restrictions due to his condition, which has negatively impacted his physical performance and quality of life. He has been advised to engage in physical activity to improve his condition, but due to the local distribution of supervised sports therapy, he has not been able to participate in it. He has internet access and is interested in participating in this study to improve his physical performance by using a mobile application to generate an online-guided, individualized home training program. He has the ability to perform sports and has submitted written consent to participate in the study.

32F with a history of mild COVID-19 infection confirmed with a laboratory antigen or SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR nasal swab within the past 48 hours is eligible for this study. The patient reports mild symptoms which include a sore throat, fatigue, and lack of taste and smell without shortness of breath or dyspnea. She has access to the internet and is willing to use a smart phone, tablet, laptop, or desktop computer to submit daily study-required information during the study period. The patient is willing to use a highly effective birth control method such as hormonal contraceptives (e.g. combined oral contraceptives, patch, vaginal ring, injectables, and implants) or an intrauterine device (IUD) or intrauterine system (IUS). The patient has been using hormonal methods for at least 30 days prior to the first study drug administration. She does not have any clinical contraindications, as judged by the Qualified Medical Practitioner. The patient has not been diagnosed with prior COVID-19 infection (>48 hours from the time the test is reported prior to the time of screening).

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with age-related macular degeneration and requires vitreoretinal surgery. He has no history of cognitive dysfunction and is classified as ASA Class II. The patient's blood pressure is well controlled with medication and is within the acceptable range for the study. The patient's BMI is within the normal range. The patient's hemoglobin is within normal limits. The patient has not experienced any recent organ failure. The patient's MMSE score is above 24. The patient has no contraindications for retrobulbar block.

A 32-year-old man, who works as an engineer, has a history of Type 2 diabetes for 5 years. He is currently taking tolbutamide for his diabetes management. He has no known allergies to any drugs or food. He does not smoke and avoids second-hand smoke. He exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day at least 5 days a week. He is not on any other medications. He has no history of gastrointestinal or liver disease. He is married for 2 years and uses condoms for contraception. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse. He has participated in the Pharmacogenetics Registry at the University of Minnesota and has been identified as having the CYP2C9*1/*3 genotype. He is interested in participating in a research study to investigate how his genetic profile affects his response to drugs and drug interactions.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with coronary artery disease and is scheduled for cardiac surgery with the aid of the heart-lung machine. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. He takes medications for these conditions, including lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no known allergies to medications. He has given written consent to participate in the study.

56-year-old male diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the stomach. The cancer has been staged as II or III and the patient has undergone D2 resection. The patient is able to receive oral administration, has normal function of other organs including heart, liver, and kidney, and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1. The patient has not received any other chemotherapy or radiation for this disease. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of TS-1 plus oxaliplatin versus TS-1 single as adjuvant chemotherapy after D2 resection in patients with gastric cancer. The patient is willing to provide informed consent and does not have a history of other malignancy or allergic reactions to S-1 or oxaliplatin.

A 45-year-old female presents with a history of difficulty falling and staying asleep. She reports that she has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months, with an average of only 4 hours of sleep per night. She has tried various sleep aids, including over-the-counter medications and herbal remedies, with little to no success. She reports feeling tired and groggy during the day, with decreased productivity at work. She denies any history of depression, substance abuse, or other psychiatric disorders. She reports that she does not smoke and only drinks alcohol occasionally. She has a BMI of 25 kg/m2 and does not have any known allergies. She is currently not taking any medications but has a history of taking benzodiazepines for anxiety, which she discontinued over a year ago. She is willing to refrain from alcohol for 24 hours before presenting to the sleep lab for sleep studies. She is interested in participating in the LFMS clinical trial and is willing to spend a total of 5 nights in the sleep laboratory.

The patient is a 65-year-old man scheduled to undergo a total knee replacement surgery due to osteoarthritis. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and arthritis. He takes medications for hypertension, statins, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for arthritis. He has no allergies and is a non-smoker. He lives with his wife and is retired. He reports that he enjoys walking and gardening as a form of exercise. He speaks English fluently and has access to an IOS device. On physical examination, he is alert and oriented, with a normal gait. His vital signs are stable, and his laboratory studies are within normal limits. He is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman who was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis 3 years ago. She has reported falling twice in the past 2 months and uses a cane for support when walking. She can walk 100 meters with intermittent assistance from the cane and does not require resting. She is clinically stable with no relapses within the past 30 days and is fluent in written and spoken English. She has daily access to email and is willing to respond to a daily email questionnaire. She is interested in participating in the Free From Falls educational program to improve her balance and reduce her risk of falls.

A 55-year-old Japanese male with a history of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and currently receiving FLOLAN injection treatment at a dose of 50ng/kg/min for the past 6 months. He has a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, all of which are well controlled with medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His exercise tolerance has decreased over the past few months, and he has experienced shortness of breath with minimal exertion. He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. On examination, he is comfortable at rest with a respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation of 94% on room air, and blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. Cardiovascular examination reveals a regular rhythm with no murmurs or gallops. Respiratory examination reveals scattered wheezing but no crackles. The abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no hepatosplenomegaly. His laboratory investigations are remarkable for elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels. The echocardiogram shows evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy and dilatation, and estimated right ventricular systolic pressure is 60 mmHg. He is considered eligible for the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the thermostable formulation of FLOLAN injection.

This is a 34-year-old HIV-positive male with a CD4 count of 175 cells/mm3 and a viral load of 45,000 copies/mL. He has been on antiretroviral therapy for 4 years with good adherence and no significant side effects. He has a history of lactose intolerance but denies any other medical conditions or significant symptoms. He does not have any active substance abuse and denies any recent use of excluded medications or systemic therapy for Kaposi's sarcoma. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the safety and effectiveness of bis-POM PMEA in HIV-infected patients.

A 25-year-old non-smoking female presents with a history of asthma symptoms such as episodic cough, wheeze, and breathlessness. She has never used oral or inhaled corticosteroids for the treatment of asthma, nor has she used leukotriene antagonist for the treatment of asthma. She reports hyperreactivity to methacholine and an increase of 15% in FEV1 following inhalation of 200μg salbutamol. She is not pregnant and has no history of lung disease other than asthma. She has never participated in any clinical trial before.

Pt is a 43yo F with locally advanced breast cancer, recently diagnosed, presenting with a palpable mass in the right breast. The patient underwent biopsy which confirmed the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma. The patient is planned for neoadjuvant chemotherapy prior to surgery. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to determine whether an experimental imaging method, Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIR), can be used to examine the breasts for cancer. The patient meets the study's eligibility criteria and is able to provide written informed consent.

38-year-old mother of two, recently tested positive for the BRCA gene mutation. She has a family history of breast cancer and has been concerned about her own risk for some time. The results of her genetic testing have left her feeling overwhelmed and unsure about how to approach the topic with her children. Although her children are still relatively young, she worries about their future risk for breast cancer and wants to make sure they have accurate information and support. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to gain more insight and guidance on how to talk to her children about hereditary breast cancer and manage her own emotional well-being.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who has a history of smoking for over 30 years. He has recently been experiencing shortness of breath, especially during physical activity. He also reports a chronic cough and occasional wheezing. He has not been diagnosed with any respiratory conditions previously, but he is concerned about his symptoms and their potential impact on his quality of life. The patient is interested in participating in a study that aims to identify clinically significant COPD using a new tool called CAPTURE, which involves a self-administered questionnaire and selected use of peak expiratory flow (PEF) measurement. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for the duration of the study.

The patient is a 32-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia with psychotic features. He has reported difficulties in cognitive functions, including processing and memory. He has intact auditory and visual perception, with no history of mental retardation. He speaks German fluently and is able to participate in the cognitive training program. He is interested in participating in the study to potentially improve his cognitive abilities and overall quality of life.

45 yo female with a 9-month history of right shoulder pain and limited range of motion. MRI revealed a partial thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon, 1.5 cm in size. Non-operative treatment including physical therapy and corticosteroid injections had been attempted without significant improvement. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history, allergies, or medications. She has a BMI of 28 and is willing to provide informed consent for the study. The patient is scheduled for arthroscopic surgery to repair the partial thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who works as a computer programmer. He has been experiencing pain in his elbow for the past month, which has been affecting his ability to work and perform daily activities. He was diagnosed with epicondylitis, and his physician recommended physical therapy. The patient has no history of chronic illnesses or surgeries, and he is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the treatment plan, including the use of a Therapeutic Percutaneous Electrolysis and Vacuum Myofascial Therapy device once a week for four weeks, as well as performing eccentric exercises at home.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who experiences recurrent migraines. She has been suffering from migraines for the past five years, and they have been affecting her daily life. She takes medication for her migraines, but she still experiences frequent headaches. She has not taken any dietary supplements, vitamins or herbal products for the past six weeks. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to help her manage her migraines. Her BMI is 23. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not changed her regular diet and lifestyle recently. She has not changed the type and dosage of her regular medication(s). She is generally healthy and has no inflammatory disease that requires her to take anti-inflammatory drugs for more than two weeks. She is excited to participate in the study and hopes that this trial will help her manage her migraines.

This is a 68-year-old male with a medical history of ischemic heart disease and hypertension. He has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion for the past year. He was diagnosed with triple-vessel coronary artery disease and has been scheduled for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with the use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). He has no history of cerebrovascular disease, but has a family history of Alzheimer's disease. He is currently on medication for his hypertension and has never smoked or consumed alcohol. He has a high school education and works as a retired accountant. He is able to perform activities of daily living independently and has no significant cognitive impairment at baseline.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who was present at the World Trade Center site during and after the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001. He is complaining of worsening respiratory symptoms, including cough, wheezing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness. He also reports trouble sleeping due to his symptoms. He has been referred to the pulmonary function laboratory for evaluation of his symptoms following exposure to WTC dust. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no history of smoking or other lung conditions. He is able to perform testing and is between the ages of 18-80, meeting the inclusion criteria for the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old right-handed male who works as an engineer. He is interested in the study of human evolution and is fascinated by the use of tools throughout history. He has no history of neurological or psychiatric illness and is not taking any psychoactive medications. He has no known allergies or intolerance to loud noises. He is registered with the French Social Security System and is willing to give informed consent for the study. He has no metallic or electronic implants in his body, and he has not had any surgeries or procedures that would exclude him from the study. He does not have any tattoos near his head or neck regions, nor does he have any permanent makeup. He has a BMI of 24 and his blood pressure is within normal limits. He is a non-smoker and does not use recreational drugs. He has no history of claustrophobia. He is excited to participate in the study and hopes to contribute to the understanding of how humans are able to use and evolve tools.

56-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease requiring hemodialysis 3 times a week for the past year. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She reports frequent gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. She has no history of inflammatory bowel disease, radiation to the bowel, or large bowel resection. She is not currently taking any antibiotics, prebiotics, or probiotics. She is able to provide informed consent and is willing to comply with all aspects of the study requirements. She is not pregnant or nursing.

34-year-old male laborer who sustained an injury to his left hand in a work-related accident 8 months ago. He has been experiencing persistent numbness and weakness in his left hand and forearm, which has significantly impacted his ability to work and perform daily activities. He has been evaluated by a hand surgeon who has recommended surgical reconstruction of the damaged nerve. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help speed up his recovery and improve the function of his left hand. He meets the eligibility criteria for the trial, including having a deficit of upper extremity function of MRC grade 0-2, being a candidate for surgical reconstruction, and having no ongoing infectious or wound healing complications related to his injury or previous surgery. He has no history of cancer or severe liver disease, and his blood tests and vital signs are within normal limits. The patient agrees to participate in the study and is excited about the potential benefits of the tacrolimus treatment.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been experiencing chronic nasal congestion for the past 2 years. She has previously tried various medical treatments, but none of them have been successful in improving her condition. She is now considering endoscopic surgery nasosinusal as a possible solution. She has noticed that her sense of smell has also been significantly impaired, which has been affecting her quality of life. She has no history of any other medical conditions and is not currently taking any medication. She is affiliated with a social security and has provided her signed consent to participate in the clinical trial.

56 year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B and cirrhosis presents with abdominal pain and distension. CT scan of the abdomen shows a large mass in the liver with portal vein tumor thrombus extending into the main portal vein. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. Patient is not a candidate for resection, liver transplantation or percutaneous radiofrequency ablation due to the extent of the tumor and thrombus. Child-Pugh classification grade A, ECOG performance status score of 1. No previous treatment for HCC or portal vein tumor thrombus. Platelet count of 80 × 10^9/L and prothrombin activity of 65%. No history of renal failure, cardiac dysfunction or end-stage disease. Willing and able to cooperate during the procedure.

This is a 28-year-old female who is generally healthy and has no significant medical history. She has never received an influenza vaccine before and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of a new GSK influenza vaccine candidate. She is of childbearing potential but is currently using adequate contraception and has had a negative pregnancy test. She is willing and able to comply with the requirements of the protocol and has provided written informed consent. She has not received any investigational or non-registered product within 30 days prior to the administration of the study vaccine and has not received any immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within 3 months prior to vaccination. She has no history of confirmed influenza infection within the past year and has not received an influenza vaccine during the Northern Hemisphere season 2007-2008. She is not currently participating in another clinical study and has no known immunosuppressive or immunodeficient condition. She has no history of allergic disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine(s). She has no acute or chronic, clinically significant pulmonary, cardiovascular, hepatic or renal functional abnormality. She is not pregnant or lactating and has no plans to become pregnant or discontinue contraceptive precautions during the study period. She does not have a history of chronic alcohol consumption and/or drug abuse. Overall, she meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for this clinical trial.

A 25-year-old female university student who has been experiencing panic attacks for the past year. She describes experiencing sudden and intense physical sensations such as heart palpitations, sweating, and shortness of breath, which she believes are harbingers of a heart attack. These panic attacks have been interfering with her daily life, making it difficult for her to attend classes and socialize with friends. She has never sought treatment for her anxiety before, but now wants to try Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT) to learn how to manage her panic symptoms. She is fluent in German and is currently not receiving any other psychiatric or psychotherapeutic treatment. She does not have any significant medical conditions that could interfere with hyperventilation testing.

The patient is a 17-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS) based on genetic confirmation using a DNA method. His body mass index (BMI) is 30 kg/m2. He has not experienced weight excursion beyond 10% of his baseline weight. He has a reliable caregiver who has been caring for him for over 6 months and provides a separate written informed consent to participate. The patient has been on a stable diet and exercise regimen for the past 3 months. He is not currently enrolled in any clinical trial involving investigational drugs or devices, and he does not live in a group home for more than 50% of the time. He has no history or presence of any medical illness that would preclude study participation. He has an estimated glomerular filtration rate above 60 mL/minute/1.73 m2 and no macroalbuminuria or hematuria. He is not hypertensive and is not on weight loss medications or has a history of bariatric surgery. He is willing and able to refrain from taking drugs known to be significant inhibitors or inducers of Cytochrome P450, family 3, subfamily A (CYP3A) enzymes and/or P-glycoprotein (P-gp), and medications that prolong the QT/QTc interval. He is not currently taking simvastatin >10 mg per day, atorvastatin >20 mg per day, or lovastatin >20 mg per day, and has no history of statin-induced myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with high cholesterol levels and has been taking atorvastatin for the past 8 months. She has no history of cardiovascular disease but has a family history of high cholesterol levels. She does not smoke, but her BMI is slightly elevated. She has been compliant with her medication and has not experienced any adverse effects. She is interested in participating in the study to assess her progress towards reaching her cholesterol target values.

Sarah is a 57-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) following a biopsy. She has never received any treatment for lymphoma in the past. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril, and she has no history of heart disease or stroke. Her physical exam and lab studies were normal aside from the diagnosis of DLBCL. The biopsy showed CD20-positive DLBCL, which is one of the diagnoses eligible for this study. She has an IPI status of 4, which is within the range of eligibility, and she has an ECOG performance status of 1. Her left ventricular ejection fraction is within the normal range, and her hematologic function is adequate. Sarah is postmenopausal and has no plans to become pregnant. She is willing to use contraception during the study and has agreed to ongoing pregnancy testing. She has no history of any other malignancy, except for basal cell carcinoma, which was treated successfully. She has never received any systemic anti-lymphoma or investigational therapy in the past. Sarah is interested in participating in this clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who wears contact lenses occasionally for social events. She has no history of cataract or corneal refractive surgery, corneal distortion or keratoconus. She has no known allergies to sodium fluorescein or topical anesthetics. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has no history of infectious disease, immunosuppressive disease, or anaphylaxis. She is not using any topical medications such as eye drops or ointments and is not currently taking oral or inhaled steroids or anti-inflammatory medications. She has not participated in any other contact lens or care solution clinical trials in the last two weeks. Her ocular surface signs are Grade 1 or 2, with no evidence of corneal edema, corneal vascularization, corneal staining (white light evaluation), tarsal conjunctival changes or any other abnormality which would normally contraindicate contact lens wear.

The patient is a healthy 30-year-old woman who is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a potential vaccine against Shigella sonnei. She has no history of allergies or autoimmune disorders and is not currently taking any medications. She is willing to undergo a physical examination and provide blood and urine samples for testing.
