She is also willing to receive three vaccinations, four weeks apart, through either intradermal, intranasal or intramuscular route. She understands that the vaccine dosage and route of administration will differ between the three cohorts and that she may be assigned to receive either the vaccine or a placebo. She is available for follow-up for the duration of the study and agrees to abstain from medications or other agents that are applied via the nasal route from 24 hours prior to each nasal dosing through to the safety assessment 1 week later. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and agrees to use acceptable birth control measures for the entire study duration. She understands that BMI > 30 kg/m2 is an exclusion criterion and is aware of the potential risks associated with participating in the study.

A 55-year-old male patient was diagnosed with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) after experiencing painless hematuria (blood in urine) for several weeks. He underwent transurethral resection of the bladder (TURB) and was found to have a low-grade Ta tumor. He received intravesical chemotherapy and was scheduled for follow-up flexible cystoscopy 4 months after TURB. The patient is a non-smoker and has no significant medical history. He has normal renal function and no other symptoms related to his bladder cancer diagnosis.

A 60-year-old male was diagnosed with Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma a year ago. His intraocular pressure has not been well-controlled with maximum tolerated medical therapy, and his ophthalmologist recommended surgical intervention. He was enrolled in the INN-005 clinical study and was randomized to receive the PRESERFLO® MicroShunt device. He completed his Month 24 Follow-Up Visit in the study and did not experience any significant adverse events. He is willing and able to comply with all study requirements and is interested in participating in the long-term follow-up study to evaluate the safety of the device through 5 years post-operative follow-up.

A 32-year-old non-smoking female patient presented with a missing front tooth due to trauma. She has good oral hygiene habits and regularly visits her dentist every six months. Her periodontal health is excellent with no signs of active disease. She has no history of systemic diseases or medications that could affect the healing process. The patient has a small dehiscence in the buccal bone plate (<2mm vertical bone loss and <5mm horizontal bone loss) at the implant site. She is interested in immediate implant placement with either a connective tissue graft or socket shield. The adjacent teeth are natural and healthy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the study protocol.

This is a 28 year old male with no significant past medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or use recreational drugs. He has no family history of coronary artery disease before the age of 45 in males or 55 in females. He has no history of diabetes, liver disease, kidney disease, or other chronic debilitating illnesses. He is not claustrophobic and is able to lay flat with his arms positioned next to his head for approximately 20 minutes. He is not pregnant and does not have breast implants. He does not have morbid obesity or asthma. He has not used anabolic steroids. The patient is interested in participating in the study to establish normal distributions of Rb-82, N-13 ammonia, and F-18FDG in the heart using PET imaging. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male who works as a software engineer in a city located at sea level. He enjoys hiking and outdoor activities and has never experienced any altitude-related symptoms before. He doesn't smoke or consume alcohol. His height is 178 cm and his weight is 75 kg. His BP: 120/80, HR: 70/min and his BMI is: 23.68. His labs: FBS: 80 mg/dl TG: 90 mg/dl Cholesterol: 170 mg/dl LDL: 85 mg/dl HDL: 40 mg/dl He exercises regularly and his cardiac assessment is normal. He has no history of respiratory or sleep disorders. He is interested in participating in the study to understand the effects of high altitude exposure on his breathing pattern.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been experiencing chronic back pain for the past 5 years. The pain is dull and aching in nature and is localized to the lower back. The pain is not relieved by over-the-counter pain medications. The pain affects his daily activities and he has missed work due to the pain. The patient also reports feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities that he used to enjoy. He has been diagnosed with major depression and has been prescribed antidepressants by his primary care physician. He has not received any treatment for his back pain other than over-the-counter pain medications. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to treat both his depression and chronic back pain. The patient is currently enrolled in Group Health Cooperative and plans to stay enrolled for the duration of the study and 1 year after the study.

32-year-old female with a 5-year history of type 1 diabetes. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m^2 and is a non-smoker. She is currently taking insulin degludec (NN1250) for diabetes management. She reports occasional episodes of hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia despite adhering to her insulin regimen. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the variability in the blood glucose-lowering effect of NN1250. She is willing to refrain from smoking and use of nicotine gum or transdermal nicotine patches during the inpatient period. She is excited about the opportunity to contribute to diabetes research and hopes that her participation will lead to better treatment options for people with type 1 diabetes.

The patient is a 35 year old Chinese male who was diagnosed with peripheral T cell lymphoma (PTCL) 2 years ago. He has undergone systemic chemotherapy, systemic and local palliative radiotherapy, and target therapy, but his condition has relapsed and is refractory to treatment. He has an ECOG score of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months. His computed tomography (CT) scans show the presence of at least one of two vertical orientations of tumor lesions that could be measured, with the longest diameter of intranode lesion > 1.5cm and the longest diameter of extranode lesion > 1.0cm (according to the 2014 Lugano standard). He had discontinued systemic corticosteroids (prednisone > 10 mg/day or equivalent dose) at least 2 weeks before enrollment, and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT) has been completed at least 4 weeks before enrollment. Before enrollment, major surgery requiring general anesthesia must have been completed at least 4 weeks. His previous anti-tumor biotherapy has been completed at least 4 weeks before enrollment. His routine blood tests show hemoglobin ≥ 80 g/L, neutrophil ≥ 1.0 ×109/L, platelet ≥ 80×109/L. His serum creatinine is ≤ 1.5×ULN, and creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula). His total bilirubin is < 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) < 2.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN). His thyroid function indicators: thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and free thyroxine (FT3/FT4) are within the normal range. He is willing to provide a tissue sample for pathological diagnosis and able to receive follow-up visits as scheduled.

A 56-year-old female presents with a diagnosis of breast cancer. She is planned for chemotherapy treatment with anthracycline and has a history of hypertension and atrial fibrillation. She is currently taking anti-hypertensive medication and has a BMI of 32 kg/m2. She has no history of coronary artery disease or diabetes mellitus. She is willing and able to provide consent and is able to read. She has no prior chemotherapy treatment. Her primary care physician has referred her for participation in a clinical trial aimed at early detection of heart problems in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy. She will receive an extra echocardiogram to determine if heart problems can be detected earlier. The trial will also include a clinical assessment at 3 to 6 months and repeat echocardiography as per standard care to evaluate any differences in strain pattern between pre-chemo and post 2 cycles studies to identify patients who are more likely to have cardiac issues later. She will have standard of care visits at 3 month, 6 month and 12 month and will be evaluated for cardiac status and survival. Her medical records will be reviewed at 5 years to check cardiac status and survival.

There is no patient description for this clinical trial as it is an experimental study that does not involve patients. Instead, the study will recruit young adult drivers from Central Ohio through advertisements. The participants must be between 18-21 years old and have a current driver's license. Those who have motion sickness will be excluded from the study.

A 50-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and recommended to undergo chemotherapy. She is married and has two teenage children. She works as a teacher and has a good support system in her family and friends. She has no other underlying health conditions and is generally healthy. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She takes multivitamins and calcium supplements regularly. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that could help her manage her chemotherapy better and improve her quality of life. She is willing to follow instructions and attend all study visits.

A 5-year-old girl, accompanied by her mother, is scheduled for the removal of tonsils at the outpatient department of specialized surgeries. The family is French-speaking and the child is currently living at home. The mother has given her consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial and agreed to the filming of the child for the double-reading animated film. The child has not undergone surgery before and is not currently on any anxiolytic treatment. The family is affiliated with social security and has a support system available at home that can watch the movie on the internet. The child has not been diagnosed with any associated disability such as blindness, profound deafness, or autistic disorders. The surgery is scheduled in 10 days.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing headaches and seizures for the past few weeks. Following a brain MRI, he was diagnosed with glioblastoma (GBM). He underwent a gross total surgical resection of the tumor mass, and post-surgical MRI showed less than 1.0 cm of residual enhancement away from the resection cavity perimeter. He has a histopathologically confirmed diagnosis of GBM and has a tumor sample available. His Karnofsky Performance Status is ≥ 60%, and he has adequate bone marrow, hepatic, and renal function. He has no severe, active comorbidities, and is not currently undergoing any other therapeutic clinical trials. He has not received prior or planned chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic therapy, radiation therapy, radioimmunotherapy, hormonal therapy, or experimental therapy for brain tumor. He has no history of severe allergic reaction to contrast media or known hypersensitivity to murine proteins. He is able to undergo an MRI. He is willing to use an effective contraceptive method as he is sexually active. He is willing to give written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedures being implemented.

A 55-year-old male with a history of basal cell carcinoma on the upper back presents for evaluation and treatment of his skin cancer. The patient has had multiple skin cancers in the past and is interested in a non-invasive option for treatment. The patient has no history of photosensitivity and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for photodynamic therapy and is willing to undergo imaging to optimize the laser exposure for treatment. The patient understands the risks and benefits of the study and is able to provide informed consent. Past Medical History: - Basal cell carcinoma on the upper back - History of multiple skin cancers - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Diabetes mellitus type 2 - Past surgical history includes appendectomy and cholecystectomy.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain and swelling in her mouth due to wisdom teeth eruption. She does not wear braces and has all of her incisor teeth. She has no history of aspiration and is not currently pregnant. She speaks fluent English and is a patient at NUH. She has been scheduled to undergo wisdom teeth extraction under general anesthesia with the use of LMA.

A 35-year-old female presented to the ophthalmology clinic with complaints of redness, itching, and discharge in her right eye. She had a history of wearing contact lenses for the past 5 years. She reported that the symptoms started 2 days ago and have been getting progressively worse. On examination, her right eye showed conjunctival hyperemia, mucopurulent discharge, and mild lid edema. Her visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes. She denied any history of eye trauma or previous eye surgery. She was diagnosed with bacterial conjunctivitis and advised to discontinue contact lens wear. She was offered to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy and safety of AzaSite and Tobramycin for bacterial conjunctivitis. She met all the inclusion criteria and was willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been experiencing blurred vision and glare in his left eye for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. The patient has been advised by his ophthalmologist to undergo cataract extraction with lens replacement surgery in his left eye. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He has no known allergies to the study medications and is not taking any medications with the same activities as the active ingredients in OMS302. The patient is in good general health and is able to undergo surgery under topical anesthesia.

14-year-old African American female, overweight with a BMI in the 95th percentile, presents to the clinic for participation in a clinical trial focused on strength training and nutrition development for African American youth. She reports no known medical conditions, no use of medications known to affect body composition or insulin action/secretion, and no current participation in any weight loss or exercise program. She has no syndromes or diseases that may influence body composition and fat distribution. She is interested in participating in the trial to improve her overall health and to learn about better nutrition and exercise habits. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and heart disease. Her parents provide written informed consent for her participation in the trial.

A 10-year-old Turkish boy with cerebral palsy and spastic quadriplegia who was referred to the pediatric gastroenterology outpatient clinic because of feeding/swallowing problems. He was born full term with a birth weight of 3000 g. He had a history of seizures since neonatal period and was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at age 2. He was non-ambulatory and non-verbal. He had a gastrostomy tube inserted when he was 4 years of age due to inadequate oral intake and recurrent aspiration pneumonia. His current medications include antiepileptic drugs and muscle relaxants. He had frequent episodes of vomiting and regurgitation, which caused significant distress to the patient and his caregiver. His physical examination was notable for drooling, decreased oral motor control, and spasticity of all extremities. He was unable to sit unsupported and had a history of recurrent respiratory infections. His past medical history was significant for gastroesophageal reflux disease, aspiration pneumonia, and recurrent urinary tract infections. He had no known drug allergies. His mother, who is his primary caregiver, is a 35-year-old housewife with no significant medical history. His father is a 40-year-old factory worker who is a smoker. They have no other children. They live in a rural area and have limited access to medical care. His BMI is in the 10th percentile for his age and gender.

9-year-old girl presents to the McMaster Children's Hospital Emergency Department with a complaint of sore throat for the past 2 days. She also reports a low-grade fever, difficulty swallowing, and mild fatigue. The patient has no known drug allergies and is not currently taking any medications. Upon physical examination, the patient's throat is inflamed with visible redness and swelling, but no tonsillar exudate or lymphadenopathy is noted. The patient is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. A throat swab is ordered for GAS testing, and the patient is deemed eligible to participate in the rapid POC GAS diagnostics trial.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) at the age of 4 years. He has difficulty in communicating and interacting with others and often engages in repetitive behaviors. He is currently on a stable medication regimen for the past 6 months. The patient has language delay and is unable to produce fluent phrase speech, as confirmed by the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule- Generic (ADOS-G). The patient's epiphyses are open and he has no history of neoplasia, intracranial hypertension, hepatic or renal insufficiency, or cardiomegaly/valvulopathy. The patient has no known allergy to IGF-1. The patient's parents are willing to participate in the clinical trial and give informed consent for their child's participation.

The patient is a 24 year old male who is an amateur baseball player. He has been playing baseball since he was 10 years old and practices regularly. He has noticed that after long periods of pitching, he experiences fatigue and weakness in his shoulder muscles. He has never had any shoulder surgery or injuries, and does not currently have any pain in his shoulder. He is in good overall health and has no allergies to topical agents. He is interested in participating in the study to determine if dynamic taping can help prevent muscle fatigue and improve his pitching performance.

Patient is a 25-year-old male with no significant past medical history. He does not smoke and has no history of anemia. The patient has not been diagnosed with any medical conditions and takes no medications. He reports feeling generally healthy and has not experienced any recent illnesses or hospitalizations. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to assess the accuracy of Spry Health's Loop oximetry in detecting hypoxia.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been recently diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and requires treatment per iwCLL guidelines. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and adequate organ and marrow function. He has no history of CLL-directed therapy, transformation of CLL to aggressive lymphoma, or CLL with deletion of chromosome 17p and/or TP53 mutation. He has no history of confirmed progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) and no known hypersensitivity to any active ingredient in the study drugs. He does not have active bleeding or a known bleeding disorder, and he is not taking any medication known to cause QT prolongation or torsade's de pointes. He has no severe and/or uncontrolled medical conditions or other conditions that could affect his participation in the study. He has not received live-virus vaccines within 28 days prior to the initiation of study treatment. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he does not intend to become pregnant during the study. He is willing and able to participate in all required study evaluations and procedures and to provide a signed and dated informed consent form (ICF) and authorization to use protected health information.

55-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and recurrent respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation presents to the ICU with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to pneumonia. The patient has been intubated and on mechanical ventilation for 10 days with poor gas exchange and difficulty weaning off the ventilator. The ICU team has decided to perform a percutaneous tracheostomy to facilitate weaning from mechanical ventilation. The patient has no history of neck infections or previous surgical interventions in the neck. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study on the use of a double lumen endotracheal tube for percutaneous tracheostomies in ICU.

A 26-year-old woman is seeking a new contraceptive method after discontinuing oral contraceptives due to side effects. She is nulliparous and has a regular menstrual cycle with moderate bleeding. She is not currently sexually active but plans to be within the next year. She has no known allergies or medical conditions and is not taking any medications. She is interested in trying the Levonogestrel IntraUterine System (LNG-IUS) and has been properly counseled by her physician about contraceptive options. She understands that the LNG-IUS is mainly for contraceptive purposes and not to treat heavy menstrual bleeding. She is capable of reading and writing and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been suffering from severe hip pain and disability for the past year. She has been experiencing difficulty in performing daily activities such as walking or climbing stairs due to the pain. She has been diagnosed with primary osteoarthritis of the hip. She has no significant past medical history other than hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in a follow-up program based on physical examination and medical history. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study. She has not undergone any previous hip surgeries and has not been diagnosed with any conditions that would exclude her from participation in the study.

72 yo woman with a left hip fracture (OTA/AO 31A2) requiring surgical treatment of the fracture. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of cognitive deficits or chronic opioid use. She is able to provide informed consent and is not currently taking any medications that would exclude her from participation in the study. The patient has no known allergies to amide-type local anesthetics. She will be randomized to receive either the standard of care treatment or the long-acting local anesthetic Exparel, and her pain control, narcotic requirements, delirium, and length of stay will be monitored post-operatively. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential benefits and risks.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 10 years ago. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are both well-controlled with medication. His recent lab work shows an eGFR of 50 mL/min/1.73m2 and a UACR of 450 mg/g. He has been on a stable dose of ACE inhibitor and ARB for the past 6 months. The patient has no history of polycystic kidney disease, peripheral vascular disease or obstructive uropathy. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate a new medication that may potentially improve his kidney function.

The patient is a 35 year old Hispanic female who presents to the clinic with concerns about the appearance of her glabellar lines. She has noticed the lines becoming more prominent over the last few years and feels self-conscious about them. She works as a marketing executive and has a busy lifestyle. She has no history of medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the clinical trial. She has not undergone any cosmetic procedures in the past and has no skin disorders at the injection site. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Neuronox compared with Botox for the treatment of moderate to severe glabellar lines.

A 45-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes mellitus who is currently being treated with metformin and insulin therapy. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She describes herself as having a Type A personality, often feeling impatient and proactive in her daily life. She has experienced some stress in her personal and professional life, which she manages through exercise and meditation. She has no history of psychiatric illness and has never received psychological counseling. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to investigate the relationship between behavioral type and diabetes. She understands that the study will involve answering some questionnaires, a clinical psychology interview, and providing a blood sample. She agrees to participate in the study and provides written informed consent.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with medically refractory epilepsy. He has been diagnosed with epilepsy for 15 years and has been treated with multiple antiepileptic drugs without significant improvement. His seizures are focal and occur 2-3 times per month. He has been referred to Dr. H.Z., a neurosurgeon at a single center, for epilepsy surgery. The patient is being considered for craniotomy to remove the area of the brain causing his seizures. The risks associated with the surgery are a concern, and the patient is interested in learning more about the potential complications. The patient has not undergone any neuromodulation therapy and meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial. The patient will be monitored for three months after surgery to assess for any complications and to identify any associated risk factors. The goal of the study is to improve the understanding of the risks of epilepsy surgery and to develop a nomogram to predict the probability of complications for individual patients.

A 30-year-old female office worker who spends approximately 40 hours a week sitting in front of a computer at work, experiencing occasional low back pain. She has no history of serious injury, spinal surgery, malignant pathology, or severe disability. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in a study that aims to investigate the long-term effectiveness of a workstation ergonomic intervention for work-related posture and low back pain. She is excited to be a part of this study that will hopefully help her and others in her profession to reduce the risk of work-related injuries and improve their overall health and well-being.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman, who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis for the past 10 years. She has had significant pain and stiffness in her hands and has failed to respond to conservative treatment options. She has been recommended for a primary metacarpophalangeal arthroplasty of all 4 digits. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no history of connective tissue disorders, previous surgeries of MP joints, or revision metacarpophalangeal arthroplasty. She is currently taking methotrexate for her rheumatoid arthritis along with folic acid supplementation. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to determine if the NeuFlex implant will provide greater range of motion and grip strength following her surgery.

The patient is a 42-year-old woman who has been experiencing chronic widespread body pain, fatigue, and depression for the past year. Despite seeing multiple healthcare providers, she has not received a clear diagnosis or effective treatment. She has missed work and social activities due to her symptoms, which has resulted in feelings of isolation and frustration. She is married with two children and works as a teacher. She has a master's degree and a middle-income job. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications and has been prescribed antidepressants, but neither have provided significant relief. She has a supportive family, but they do not fully understand her condition and often suggest that she is exaggerating her symptoms. She is interested in participating in this study to better understand and address the stigma surrounding fibromyalgia.

Pt is a 12yo M with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and has been undergoing hemodialysis (HD) for the past 9 months. Pt has been experiencing dyslipidemia and increased oxidative stress markers, with recent lab results showing increased levels of C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum lipids. The patient has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any antioxidant treatments or vitamin E supplements. The patient's guardian has provided informed consent for participation in the study.

As this study is an individual patient level meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, there are no specific patient descriptions required for enrollment. Participants will be selected based on their enrollment in previous RCTs related to the duration of dual antiplatelet agent therapy. The study will evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the relative tradeoff between ischemia and bleeding, and will analyze data from a diverse patient population. Therefore, patients of all ethnicities who meet the inclusion criteria may be considered for participation in this study.

The patient is a 28-year-old male with a history of heroin use disorder. He has been abstinent for 10 days at the time of screening and is not currently on any opioid use disorder treatments. He has no other substance use disorders except for nicotine use. He is in good physical health, with no medical or psychiatric contraindications for MRI or CBD administration. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and is using an appropriate method of contraception. He speaks fluent English and has not been court mandated to attend treatment centers. He did not test positive for cannabinoid use during screening. He is interested in participating in the study to investigate the effects of CBD on craving and anxiety in abstinent heroin users.

A 58-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with complaints of shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing for the past few months. He reports a history of smoking and working in a factory with exposure to dust and chemicals. He was diagnosed with COPD and prescribed inhalers and other medications to manage his symptoms. However, he admits to forgetting to take his medication regularly and often runs out of his prescription before refilling it. He also has difficulty understanding the instructions and proper use of his inhaler. He lives alone and has no support system to remind him to take his medication. He works full-time and has limited time to attend medical appointments or educational sessions. He is interested in learning how to better manage his condition and is willing to participate in a study that could help him identify barriers to medication adherence and receive tailored support to improve his adherence to therapy. He speaks French fluently and is affiliated with the social security regime. He is available for a follow-up of 1 year.

A 4-year-old girl named Lily has been diagnosed with cerebral palsy (spastic type) by her pediatrician. She has a history of low muscle tone, muscle weakness, and difficulties in coordination, balance, and movement. Her parents noticed that she had delayed motor milestones and couldn't sit or crawl like other kids at her age. Lily's parents have been taking her to rehabilitation therapy sessions for the past year, but they feel that their daughter's progress is slow and limited. They have heard about scalp acupuncture treatment as a complementary therapy for cerebral palsy and are willing to try it to improve their daughter's motor function and quality of life. Lily's medical history is unremarkable, and she has no known allergies or bleeding tendencies. She is not taking any herbal therapies or muscle relaxants, and she is not currently participating in any other clinical trials. The family lives in Shanghai, China, and they are interested in participating in the study at Children's Hospital of Fudan University.

This is an 82-year-old male veteran with a diagnosis of dementia. He has been a resident of a nursing home for over three weeks and has been experiencing sleep disturbances. He has a Mini-Mental State Examination Score of 20 and sleeps less than 80% of the night, with frequent awakenings. During the day, he takes multiple naps, lasting up to an hour each time. He is often agitated and exhibits disruptive behaviors, including hitting and cursing. He has been on medication for sleep and behavior disturbances but has not shown significant improvement, and the medication has caused adverse side effects. He is interested in participating in a trial that investigates the effect of individualized activities on sleep and behavior.

Sophia is a 3-year-old girl who has been suffering from recurrent pharyngitis and tonsillitis for the past six months. Her parents have taken her to the doctor multiple times, and she has been prescribed antibiotics on three separate occasions. She has missed several days of daycare due to her illness, and her parents are concerned about her immune system being compromised from frequent antibiotic use. Sophia was born at 38 weeks gestation and had a normal birth weight. She has no other significant medical history, and her physical examination is unremarkable. Her parents are willing to have her participate in a clinical trial to see if probiotics can reduce the duration of her symptoms and severity of pain associated with pharyngitis and tonsillitis. They understand the potential risks and benefits of participating in the study and have provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been experiencing recurrent and unexpected panic attacks for the past year. She reports experiencing intense fear, sweating, palpitations, and shortness of breath during these episodes. Her panic attacks occur at least once a week and have caused her to avoid certain situations such as driving on highways and going to crowded places. She has never been diagnosed with a mental illness before and is currently not taking any medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help manage her panic disorder and improve her quality of life.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who works as a software developer and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He describes himself as generally healthy but does not engage in regular exercise. He smokes cigarettes occasionally but has no known history of cardiovascular disease. He is interested in improving his cardiovascular fitness and is excited to participate in a study that could help him achieve that goal. He has no history of participation in regular exercise programs and does not meet the American College of Sports Medicine's recommendations for weekly aerobic exercise. He is available to commit to three training sessions per week for eight weeks and is willing to perform high-intensity interval training on a stationary bike.

An 68-year-old woman who lives alone and is retired presented to the emergency department with severe pain in her left hip. After imaging, it was determined that she had sustained a hip fracture and underwent surgery to repair it. She has a history of hypertension and mild osteoporosis. She currently takes lisinopril for her blood pressure and calcium and vitamin D supplements for her bones. She has never had surgery before and is concerned about her recovery process, as she lives alone and does not have much support. She is able to communicate effectively in both French and English. She is eager to participate in a program that can help her regain her mobility and independence.

The patient is a 35-year-old Caucasian male with a history of schizophrenia. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to acute psychotic episodes. He was recently discharged from an inpatient psychiatric unit and referred to the Transitional Care Clinic for follow-up care. He has been diagnosed with schizophrenia for the past 5 years and has been on antipsychotic medication since then. He has a history of nonadherence to medication and has had multiple relapses as a result. He lives alone in an apartment and is currently unemployed. He has a high school education and no significant medical history. He has expressed interest in being more involved in his treatment decisions and improving his quality of life. He has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and signed informed consent. His HAM-D score is 12.

Patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of advanced liver disease (cirrhosis) due to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. The patient has previously undergone treatment with pegylated interferon and ribavirin for at least 24 weeks with undetectable HCV RNA at the end of therapy but detectable HCV RNA six months after treatment cessation. The patient's liver biopsy within the last 2 years showed an Ishak fibrosis score of >4 or radiological evidence of cirrhosis (ultrasound scan or fibroscan reading >10.6). The patient has chronic genotype 3 HCV infection confirmed at a local laboratory. The patient's HBsAg is negative, and there is no clinical evidence of co-infection with HIV. The patient's platelet count is >50,000 cells/mm3, and neutrophil count is > 600 cells/mm3. The patient is willing to use two forms of effective contraception during treatment and 6 months after treatment end. The patient is able and willing to give informed consent and comply with study requirements. The patient does not have poorly controlled diabetes, severe retinopathy, evidence of ascites seen on previous liver ultrasound, haemoglobin concentration <11 g/dL in females or <12 g/dL in males, albumin levels <35 G/L, and history of severe psychiatric disease or immunologically mediated disease. The patient does not have any other on-going serious medical condition in the opinion of the investigator that would prohibit treatment, poorly controlled thyroid dysfunction, history of major organ transplantation with an existing functional graft, severe pre-existing cardiac disease, history or laboratory testing showing evidence of a haemoglobinopathy, and concomitant administration with active substances that are highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance and for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious and/or life-threatening events.

Patient A is a healthy 25-year-old male with a normal body weight for his height. He has no known allergies to quinapril, hydrochlorothiazide, or any sulfonamide derived drugs. He is not currently experiencing anuria, gout or dry cough, and has not experienced diarrhea or vomiting in the last week. He has no evidence of organ dysfunction or any clinically significant deviation from the normal, as determined by medical history and physical examination within the last 14 days. He has voluntarily given written informed consent to participate in this study. He does not have any disease markers for HIV 1 or 2, Hepatitis B or C viruses or syphilis infection. His hemoglobin, total white blood cells count, differential WBC count, and platelet count are all within normal ranges. He has not tested positive for urinary screen testing of drugs of abuse (opiates or cannabinoids). His serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST), serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT), serum alkaline phosphatase, serum bilirubin, plasma glucose, and serum cholesterol are all within normal ranges. His urine analysis is normal and his ECG and Chest X-ray are clinically normal. He has no history of serious gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, cardiovascular, pulmonary, neurological or hematological disease, diabetes, glaucoma or angioedema due to any cause. He has no history of any psychiatric illness which may impair the ability to provide written informed consent. He is not a regular smoker and does not consume excessive alcohol. He has not used any enzyme modifying drugs within 30 days prior to Day 1 of this study and has not participated in any clinical trial within 12 weeks preceding Day 1 of this study. His hemoglobin concentration is within 7% of the lower limit of the reference range.

This is a 53-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presented with complaints of abdominal pain, nausea, and jaundice. He was found to have elevated liver enzymes and a liver biopsy showed evidence of cholestatic liver injury. Upon further history, he reported recent use of a newly prescribed medication for his hypertension. He meets the criteria for drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and is eligible for this clinical trial. He has no history of viral hepatitis, alcoholic liver disease, autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cirrhosis, Wilson's disease, hemochromatosis, congestive heart failure, hypoxia, or sepsis. He will undergo genetic testing to assess for polymorphisms in UGT1A1 and 1A7 to determine if they are associated with his cholestatic DILI. He will also be randomized to either the UDCA treatment group or the control group to evaluate the treatment effect of UDCA in the DILI, with special reference to the cholestatic hepatotoxicity.

Pt is a 35yo M with a diagnosis of Hodgkin's lymphoma in complete remission. He has no history of significant comorbidity and has a Karnofsky score of 80. He has undergone successful mobilization of peripheral blood stem cells and is familiar with the participant information sheet. The patient has signed the informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study. He has no history of participation in other clinical trials or intake of study drugs within the prior 3 months. The patient's laboratory tests are within normal limits, and he has no medical history of heterotopic ossification. The patient is currently undergoing high-dose chemotherapy with subsequent autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been referred to the Austrian Breast Imaging Center for follow-up screening for breast cancer. She has no personal history of breast cancer and has not undergone any breast surgery. She has no family history of breast cancer. She reports no breast symptoms or pain. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent. She is able to tolerate breast compression and understands the study requirements. She has no breast implants. She will undergo both Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) and routine Full Field Digital Mammography (FFDM) imaging as part of the study.

30-year-old female diagnosed with absolute uterine factor infertility due to congenital absence of the uterus. She has a history of failed IVF attempts and has been excluded from the previous uterus transplantation trials (Gothenburg I and II) due to donor criteria. She has no systemic disease and is not on any standing medication. Her BMI is 28 and her waist circumference is 80cm. She has a satisfactory ovarian reserve and is psychologically stable. She is interested in participating in the uterus transplantation trial from a deceased donor. She has been informed about the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to sign the informed consent form.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been experiencing intermittent abdominal pain for the past 6 months. The pain is located in the upper abdomen and radiates to his back. He has no other symptoms and has not experienced any weight loss or changes in bowel movements. He has a history of smoking and heavy alcohol consumption, but he quit both 5 years ago. His physical exam is unremarkable, and his blood work is within normal limits. A contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CE-CT) scan revealed a solid pancreatic lesion with an iso- or hypervascular contrast pattern. The patient is willing to participate in the study to further evaluate the lesion and determine the features associated with malignancy using endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS).

The patient is a 10-year-old girl with a history of cleft palate. She was born in December 2006 and treated at the Montpellier University Hospital. The patient had undergone surgery for cleft palate when she was an infant. She has no known allergies to medications. Her parents report that she has had recurrent ear infections and difficulty hearing. She currently wears hearing aids. The patient has no history of respiratory issues or nasal obstruction. She has no known medical conditions other than cleft palate. The patient and her parents have agreed to participate in the study and attend the ENT check-up at the hospital.

32-year-old female diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) 2 years ago. She presents with symptoms of fatigue, dizziness, and shortness of breath on exertion. She is currently on standard and stable PAH therapy including a prostacyclin and phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor but continues to be in NYHA class III. She has a history of cigarette smoking but has quit 6 months ago. She has no history of malignancy or coronary artery disease. She has a normal serum pregnancy test and is using a barrier method of contraception. Her echocardiogram shows evidence of right ventricular dysfunction. Her right heart catheterization shows a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 30 mmHg, pulmonary capillary occlusion pressure of 12 mmHg, and pulmonary vascular resistance of 6 mmHg/L/min. Her six-minute walk distance is 360m. She has no baseline cytopenias or liver disease. Her renal function is normal with a creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL. She has no history of lung transplant and is not currently enrolled in any other investigational treatment protocol for PAH.

32 y/o male with a history of cocaine and alcohol dependence, using both substances within the past 6 months. He has not been on methadone or any other forms of drug addiction treatment other than IOP. He is currently judged clinically appropriate for IOP with no evidence of a psychotic disorder or severe dementia, and no acute medical problems requiring inpatient treatment. The patient is willing to participate in research and is able to provide the name, verified telephone number, and address of at least two contacts who can provide locator information on the patient during follow-up. The patient is a metropolitan area resident and has access to a telephone. He does not have a regular IV heroin use during the past year. The patient is open to exploring several possible treatment options and willing to be randomized for the study.

47 year old man who was vaccinated against hepatitis B over 10 years ago as a requirement for his job. He has never tested positive for hepatitis B and has no history of liver disease. He is generally healthy and speaks English fluently. He has no allergies to the hepatitis B vaccine or its components and has not received any blood or blood components in the last 6 months. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient is available for all four visits within the designated timelines of 30 days.

A 42-year-old male with a history of Crohn's disease diagnosed six months ago presents with a complex perianal fistula that has failed to respond to previous biologic and conventional therapies. The fistula has one internal and one external opening, including a previously converted branching fistula tract. The patient reports medication intolerance and is willing to comply with study requirements. He is in overall good health and has no other significant medical conditions that would compromise his safety during the study. The patient is not pregnant and is using an adequate method of contraception during the entire duration of the study. The patient is willing to undergo Magnetic Resonance (MR) evaluations and/or MR contrast and does not have any history of clinically significant fat-directed autoimmunity. The patient does not have a history of recto-vaginal fistula or ileal anal pouch perineal fistulas. The patient does not have an active, unresolved infection requiring parenteral antibiotics, and has not undergone any major surgery of the gastrointestinal tract within the last 3 months. The patient has not had a definitive surgical procedure for the target fistula or a perianal procedure that resulted in a large soft tissue defect within 6 months prior to screening visit. The patient does not have a compromised abdominal region due to a previous cool sculpting procedure, abdominal radiation, chemotherapy, recent tattoos, local infection, or other reasons that may compromise the adipose tissue for study use. The patient has not been treated with Cx601/Alofisel or other allogeneic or autologous stem-cell therapy within the past 6 months. The patient does not have any contraindications to the anesthetic procedure (local and general) or to the adipose tissue collection procedure. The patient's perianal fistula type and anatomic presentation meet the inclusion criteria for the study. Additionally, the patient does not have evidence of moderately or greater active luminal CD, ongoing systemic or rectal steroids for CD in the last 2 weeks prior to screening and baseline study visits, or history of, or concurrent high-grade dysplasia, adenocarcinoma, and carcinoma in situ on colonoscopy within 5 years of screening visit. The patient's renal function, hemoglobin, serum AST, and ALT levels are within normal limits, and the patient does not have undrained peri-anal sepsis or known coagulopathy or thrombocytopenia.

7 year-old male with a 10% TBSA partial-thickness burn injury sustained in a house fire 5 days ago. The patient was admitted to the pediatric burn unit and has a feeding tube in place due to difficulty tolerating oral feeds. The patient has no history of gastrointestinal disorders and has no known milk allergies or insensitivities. The patient's caregiver has provided informed consent within 10 days of the injury. The patient has not sustained any non-burn related injuries.

A 7-year-old boy with developmental delay and multiple congenital anomalies, including microcephaly, cleft palate, and clubfoot, is being evaluated by a clinical geneticist. He has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and feeding difficulties requiring a gastrostomy tube. His parents report that he has global developmental delay, with limited mobility and communication skills. He has undergone multiple genetic tests without a definitive diagnosis. His family is interested in participating in the NCGENES 2 study to potentially identify a genetic cause for his condition and to contribute to the advancement of genomic medicine. The parents are both fluent in English and have provided informed consent for themselves and their son.

42 yo female with a history of chronic jaw pain for the past year. She reports difficulty chewing and speaking, as well as headaches and neck pain. She was evaluated by her primary care physician and diagnosed with temporomandibular joint syndrome. She tried non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and physical therapy, but only experienced temporary relief of symptoms. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of radial shock wave therapy on her symptoms. She has no history of other medical conditions or surgeries and does not take any medications regularly. She does not smoke or drink alcohol.

The patient is a 45-year-old Palestinian woman living in East Jerusalem. She has a family history of diabetes, with her mother and aunt both being diagnosed with the condition. The patient is currently overweight with a BMI of 30 and has been diagnosed with prediabetes. She is a homemaker and spends most of her time at home taking care of her children. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial in order to improve her health and reduce her risk of developing diabetes. She is willing and able to commit to the intervention timetable and is excited to learn more about healthy eating and physical activity.

The patient is a 17-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with Ewing's sarcoma after presenting with pain and swelling in his right thigh. Imaging studies revealed a large mass in the thigh and metastases to his lungs and liver. He has no significant past medical history and has not received any prior chemotherapy. His cardiac function is normal, with an ejection fraction of 60%. His renal function is also normal, with a glomerular filtration rate of 90 mL/min. He is not pregnant and is willing to use effective contraception during and for 3 months after completion of study treatment. He has no history of chronic diarrhea, bowel obstruction, sub obstruction, Crohn's disease, or ulcerative colitis. He is concurrently enrolled in the EURO-Ewing99 clinical trial. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the potential risks and benefits of irinotecan treatment.

38yo man with a history of HIV infection, currently on triple combination therapy with a viral load of < 500 copies/ml. He is currently experiencing mild side effects such as fatigue and difficulty sleeping. He is fluent in French and has not previously been treated with NNRTI-based therapy.

47-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia presents for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He reports no significant surgical history and is currently on metformin and lisinopril. His physical exam is normal, and his labs are within normal limits except for a slightly elevated hemoglobin A1c at 7.8%. He provides informed consent and is enrolled in the observational study. His pUSIS score is calculated at the end of surgery, and he is followed up for short term post-operative clinical outcome parameters, including time duration from end of surgery till discharge from PACU, time duration from end of surgery till discharge from hospital, and occurrence and severity of complications during hospital stay according to a predefined list.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who recently underwent surgery to remove a brain tumor. The histopathology report confirmed that the patient has a glioblastoma or gliosarcoma. The patient has recovered well from the surgery and has no other major health issues. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive radiation therapy and temozolomide treatment. The patient has signed the informed consent and is willing to undergo regular check-ups and follow-up visits as required by the study protocol. The patient has no known allergies to temozolomide. The patient is not pregnant and is willing to use medically acceptable forms of contraception if sexually active. The patient has provided a tissue sample for histopathologic central review and MGMT status, which confirmed the diagnosis.

This is a 54-year-old woman with a history of non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) that was diagnosed with a sensitizing EGFR mutation. She initially responded well to osimertinib, a third generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), but eventually progressed. Upon progression, a thorough and complete osimertinib resistance analysis was performed to determine the resistance mechanisms present. A histological biopsy and blood sample for ctDNA analysis were obtained. The results of the analysis revealed alteration of downstream signal transduction proteins, including KRAS mutation. The patient is now eligible for subsequent treatment and willing to participate in this clinical trial to explore new therapeutic strategies that target this resistance mechanism. She has not discontinued osimertinib or initiated a new line of anticancer therapy before the blood draw and/or histological tumor biopsy.

A 45-year-old female was recently diagnosed with endometrial cancer and is scheduled for surgery at the Paoli-Calmettes Institute. She has a history of hypertension and a BMI of 30. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. She is willing to participate in the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Program and has given informed consent for her data to be collected for the purposes of this database. She understands that this program includes multimodal approaches to her perioperative care with the goal of achieving an early recovery after surgery and a decreased length of hospital stay. She is enthusiastic about the prospect of contributing to the quality of surgical management and follow-up, and is eager to be a part of this research study.

The patient is a 27-year-old healthy male with a body mass index of 23 kg/m2 and a weight of 70 kg. He has no history of neurological, haematological, psychiatric, gastrointestinal, hepatic, pulmonary, or renal disease. He has never participated in a PET study before. He has no history of trauma or sickness in the last 2 weeks before the first PET examination. He does not suffer from claustrophobia. He is currently not taking any medication and does not have any known allergies.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy woman who works as a nurse in a hospital. She has no known history of HIV infection, nasal disease, malignancy, or abnormality. She has no known allergies or asthma and does not smoke or use illicit drugs. She is not currently taking any medications, including nasal medications, and has not received any investigational agents within the past three months. She is willing to use appropriate contraception methods during the study period, including pregnancy testing before immunisation. Her physical exam and lab studies were unremarkable for any conditions that would interfere with study participation. She is fluent in English and is available for the duration of the study. Her weight and height are within the range of a healthy BMI (Body Mass Index). She is interested in participating in the trial to help advance HIV vaccine research.

A 31-year-old Caucasian woman with primary infertility for 2 years is planning to undergo IVF/ICSI. She has regular menstrual cycles and no previous medical or surgical history. Her AMH levels are within the normal range, and her partner's semen analysis is normal. The couple has undergone three cycles of IUI, but all have been unsuccessful. She is not on any medications and does not have any known allergies. Her BMI is 22. She has 10 follicles on the day of hCG administration, and her doctor recommends oocyte retrieval. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial that compares the effectiveness of single lumen needle without flushing and double lumen needle with follicle flushing during oocyte retrieval.

30 year old HIV+ male on Atripla for the past 6 months with a viral load < 50 copies/mL. He has been diagnosed with insomnia and has been experiencing sleep disturbances for the past 3 months. Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate is > 70 mL/min. The patient has not been on any antiretroviral therapy prior to Atripla. The patient is not pregnant and is able to provide informed consent. The patient is not currently enrolled in another study.

The patient is a 65-year-old male who has been referred to a urologist for evaluation of an elevated PSA level of 6.5 ng/dL. Upon digital rectal examination, a hard nodule is palpable in the prostate gland. A hypoechoic lesion is also observed on ultrasound of the prostate gland, which is suspicious for cancer. The patient has no history of prostate surgery or rectal cancer, and his cognitive function is intact. The patient has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to verify the effectiveness of shear wave elastography for detecting prostate cancer.

A 25-year-old female with a history of chronic anemia, splenomegaly, and frequent episodes of jaundice and cholecystitis. She also had a history of prolonged neonatal jaundice. Despite previous medical evaluations, the cause of her symptoms has not been clearly determined. She is seeking further evaluation and potential diagnosis for her condition. The patient is willing to participate in the PIECE study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with soft tissue sarcoma on his left thigh. He has been on chemotherapy but his tumor has progressed and is now considered unresectable. He has no history of allergies and takes only over-the-counter medications as needed. He works as a software engineer and is married with two children. He has an ECOG performance score of 1 and is willing to give written informed consent. He has measurable tumor lesions and has failed standard therapy. His lab tests for hematology, liver function and renal function are all within required parameters. He has no active or chronic infection with HIV, Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C. He does not have untreated or uncontrolled brain metastases and does not have a history of other active malignancy within last 2 years. He does not have autoimmune disease or any serious uncontrolled medical disorder or active infection that would impede treatment. He does not have underlying medical or psychiatric condition that would cause administration of the vaccine. He has not undergone any non-oncology vaccine therapy up to 1 month before or after any dose of vaccine. He is not on concomitant therapy with IL-2, interferon, other non-study immunotherapy, or cytotoxic chemotherapy; immune-suppressive agents within 30 days of registration; other investigational therapies; chronic use of systemic corticosteroids. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not a prisoner or compulsorily detained.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who recently underwent coronary angiography and was found to have at least one coronary vessel with a stenosis of ≥50%. He complains of chest pain on exertion and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently on medications for both conditions. He has no previous history of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or myocardial infarction (MI). He is a non-smoker and does not have any significant respiratory illness. He has no history of heart failure or valvular disease. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given written informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old Pakistani woman who presented with complaints of generalized body weakness and fatigue for the past 6 months. She also reports frequent episodes of bone pain and muscle cramps. She has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of her time indoors. Her medical history is significant for a recent diagnosis of hypothyroidism and she is currently taking levothyroxine. She denies any history of renal or liver disease. On physical examination, she appears pale and has diffuse tenderness over her bony prominences. Her height is 5'3" and weight is 75 kg, giving her a BMI of 29.4. Laboratory investigations reveal a Vitamin D level of 15 ng/dL and a corrected calcium level of 9.2 mg/dL. Her liver function tests and renal function tests are within normal limits. She meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not have any of the exclusion criteria.

A healthy 25-year-old male with a height of 173 cm and a body mass index of 22, who has no history of cardiovascular or respiratory diseases, and is not taking any chronic medications. The patient has a normal blood pressure, heart rate, and cardio-pulmonary auscultation at rest, and a normal electrocardiogram. The patient is able to understand the aims and constraints of the study and has national health insurance. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 55-year-old man has been diagnosed with multiple myeloma for the past 2 years. He has been undergoing treatment for his condition and has experienced relapses in the past. Recently, he has been experiencing progressive disease and has been recommended to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of carfilzomib. He has measurable disease with a serum M-protein level of 1.2 g/dL. He is in otherwise good physical condition, with an ECOG performance status of 1. His liver function is adequate, with bilirubin levels within normal limits and AST and ALT levels within 3 times the upper limit of normal. His LVEF is 45% and his ANC is 1200/mm3. Hemoglobin and platelet count are within normal limits. His creatinine clearance is 20 mL/min. He has provided written informed consent and is willing to use an effective method of contraception during the study. He has not received glucocorticoid therapy within the last 7 days, cytotoxic chemotherapy within the last 28 days, or treatment with bortezomib, thalidomide or lenalidomide within the last 21 days. He has not undergone any major surgery within the last 21 days and does not have active congestive heart failure, symptomatic ischemia, or conduction abnormalities. He does not have an active infection requiring systemic antibiotics, antiviral, or antifungal agents, and is not known to have HIV or hepatitis B or C virus infection. He has not had a myocardial infarction within the last 6 months and does not have acute active infection. He has no significant neuropathy or peripheral neuropathy with pain, and is not pregnant or lactating. He does not have a history of allergy to Captisol® or prior carfilzomib treatment. He has not participated in any Onyx-sponsored phase 3 trial and does not have a contraindication to dexamethasone. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and is able to provide informed consent.

A 42-year-old female hospital employee at the Heart Hospital at North Shore University Hospital has a history of smoking cigarettes for 10 years and currently smokes half a pack per day. She has a family history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and heart disease, with her mother and father both having experienced heart attacks in their 60s. She reports having a sedentary lifestyle and has a BMI of 29. She is interested in learning more about how to reduce her risk factors for cardiovascular disease and is willing to participate in a 6-week program designed specifically for women. She has no prior history of heart attack or stroke and is not currently pregnant. She is aware that she has a higher risk of developing heart disease due to her family history and lifestyle, and is motivated to make changes to improve her heart health.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) for two years. She experiences fatigue, joint pain, and mild kidney dysfunction. She is currently taking hydroxychloroquine and prednisolone daily to manage her symptoms. She is sexually active and uses condoms for contraception. She is concerned about her risk of developing cervical cancer and is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the quadrivalent HPV vaccine. She has never received any HPV vaccine before. She has no known allergies to vaccines or vaccine components. She is willing to undergo regular follow-up visits and blood tests to evaluate the response to the vaccine. She is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the trial and has given informed consent to participate.

This is a 25-year-old female with good overall health who has been experiencing discomfort in her right maxillary tooth. Upon examination, it was found that she has necrotic pulp and periapical periodontitis in the tooth. She has good oral hygiene and her tooth is straight and non-curved with normal occlusal contact with the opposing teeth. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial investigating the healing potentiality of blood clot, S-PRF, and A-PRF in the treatment of teeth with this condition. She is not illiterate and is able to estimate pain levels on the pain scale (NRS). She does not have any systemic diseases, is not on systemic corticosteroids therapy, and is not pregnant. She also does not have any allergies to ciprofloxacin or metronidazole. However, she reports bruxism and clenching, which may affect the success of the treatment.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of chronic alcohol abuse and cirrhosis diagnosed via liver biopsy 6 months ago. He presents with symptoms of ascites, such as abdominal distension and discomfort, and has been treated with diuretics with little improvement. He has not received non-selective beta-blockers within the last 3 months. His past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He denies any history of cardiac or pulmonary disease. His family history is negative for liver disease or any other significant medical conditions. His lab study shows: ALT: 65 U/L AST: 60 U/L Bilirubin: 1.2 mg/dL Albumin: 2.8 g/dL INR: 1.5 Platelets: 80,000/mm3 creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL.

32 yo F with history of bipolar I disorder, currently in remission with sub-threshold symptoms, presenting with a BMI of 28.5, high blood pressure, and a family history of heart disease. The patient reports difficulty maintaining regular sleep/wake and social rhythms, and struggles with maintaining a healthy diet and consistent physical activity. She has a history of anxiety disorder but is currently stable on medication. The patient is interested in participating in a study aimed at reducing medical risk factors in individuals with bipolar disorder in order to improve psychiatric and functional outcomes. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements and provide informed consent. The patient is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no other medical conditions that would prevent her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has a history of high blood pressure for the past 5 years. He is currently taking amlodipine 5mg once a day, but his blood pressure is not adequately controlled. His sit DBP readings are consistently above 90 mmHg, despite being on medication. He is a retired accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has no significant medical history except for hypertension. His current blood pressure readings are 150/94 mmHg. He has no known allergies to any medications. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

A 45-year-old male with a waist circumference of 105cm and a BMI of 32kg/m2 presents to the clinic with complaints of abdominal obesity and insulin resistance. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication, and has never been diagnosed with diabetes. His fasting plasma triglycerides concentration is 180mg/dL and his plasma LDL-c concentration is 160mg/dL. He has not undergone any bariatric surgery and is not currently taking any lipid-decreasing medication. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

A 14-year-old male with a known history of type 1 diabetes for the last 3 years, managed with insulin pump therapy, presented for enrollment in the Super-Bolus clinical trial. The patient was diagnosed with T1DM after presenting with polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss. The patient's insulin pump settings include a basal rate of 0.6 U/hour and a bolus ratio of 1:10 (1 unit of insulin for every 10 grams of carbohydrates). The patient's last HbA1c was 7.5%, and his blood glucose levels were fairly well controlled with an average blood glucose level of 140 mg/dL. The patient has no other comorbid conditions and is not taking any other medications. The patient's BMI is at the 60th percentile for his age and sex. The patient and his parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with asthma for the past 10 years. She has a history of acute exacerbations with frequent episodes of dyspnea, wheezing, and cough. Her previous exacerbations have required emergency department visits and systemic steroid treatment. She has difficulty using her inhaler properly and has not received proper education on the correct technique. She lives alone and does not have a caregiver to assist her with her asthma management. She has also been experiencing cognitive impairment and is deficient in magnesium, which is believed to be contributing to her exacerbations. She will be enrolled in the study to receive multidisciplinary interventions, including education on proper inhaler technique, a personalized asthma action plan, and daily magnesium supplementation. She will also have access to an emergency call system in case of acute exacerbation. The study will monitor her lung function, number of exacerbations, health-related quality of life, and serum magnesium levels over the course of one year.

A 50-year-old male presents with symptoms of Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), including swelling, pain, and discomfort in his legs. He has a Comprehensive Classification System for Chronic Venous Disorder (CEAP) Score of 3. He has a sedentary lifestyle and spends most of his day sitting at a desk. He has a history of smoking, but he quit 2 years ago. He has no underlying medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He is interested in participating in the study to improve his symptoms and overall quality of life. He speaks English fluently and can read and write in English. He is willing and able to commit to the 12-week structured exercise program, including the walking program, ankle range of motion exercises, and resistance exercises as outlined in the "Strength From Within" booklet. He is able to attend all baseline and follow-up appointments and is physically able to perform the exercises as demonstrated.

A 12-year-old child diagnosed with type 1 diabetes (T1D) is currently being treated with insulin injections. The child's parents are looking for alternative treatment options to improve glycemic control and overall quality of life. The child is generally healthy and active, with a BMI within the normal range. The family has national health insurance and is interested in exploring insulin pump therapy. They are willing to participate in a clinical trial to compare different pump devices and evaluate the impact on glycemic control, technical difficulties, and quality of life. The child is under the care of a pediatric endocrinologist and attends regular clinic visits. There are no restrictions on the child's HbA1c value or the use of continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGMS).

A 10-year-old male patient who has been diagnosed with a congenital heart defect and has a history of respiratory issues. He is currently being treated by a pediatric cardiologist and has been recommended to undergo an MRI scan for further diagnosis. The patient is generally healthy with no history of heart or lung disease, but occasionally experiences shortness of breath and coughing due to his respiratory issues. The patient and his legal guardian have given written informed consent to participate in this study. The patient will be categorized as a part of the "older children capable of controlled breathing/breath-holding on command" group and will undergo the prescribed imaging protocol for respiratory monitoring. MRI data will be collected during a routine cardiac MRI and transferred to the Pediatrics Imaging Research Laboratory for analysis. The data collected will be used to improve image quality and develop better imaging methods for future patients with similar conditions.

A 35-year-old male with a diagnosis of bipolar disorder and obesity has been receiving treatment for his condition for the past 6 months. He has a history of hospitalizations due to psychiatric instability and has been experiencing symptoms of depression and anxiety. He is currently taking medications prescribed by his psychiatrist and has been enrolled in a weight loss program. He speaks English fluently and is willing to use technology to receive support for his condition. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to improve his self-management skills and receive peer support. He gives voluntary consent to participate in the study.

56F with history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 15 years, presents with complaints of fatigue, muscle weakness, bone pain, and difficulty concentrating. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetic neuropathy, and diabetic retinopathy. She reports that over the past year, she has been experiencing more frequent episodes of hypoglycemia despite adjusting her insulin dosages accordingly. Her most recent laboratory results show an elevated creatinine level of 2.5 mg/dL and a urinary albumin/creatinine ratio of 1200 mg/g. She has not undergone any neck surgery in the past and is not currently taking cinacalcet.

An 8-year-old girl was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease and has been undergoing treatment for the past 6 months. She has experienced slow growth during this time, with her height measuring at 2 standard deviations below the average for her age. Her bone age is also below average, with a Tanner Stage I pre-pubertal development. She has not received any prior growth hormone treatment and is not currently taking any glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants. Her liver functions are normal and she has tested negative for Hepatitis B virus. She does not have any chronic systemic diseases or infections. Her parents have given their informed consent for her to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of recombinant human growth hormone injection to address her short stature due to chronic kidney disease before transplantation.

42-year-old male with no significant medical history presents to the dental clinic with complaints of sensitivity and pain while eating. On examination, 4 occlusal caries lesions are detected in the molar teeth. The patient has a healthy periodontal status and is likely to be available for follow-up visits. The patient does not have any adverse medical history or potential behavioral problems. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial evaluating two low-shrinkage composites and is willing to undergo the required procedures, including cavity preparation with either an Er,Cr:YSGG laser or conventional diamond bur and restoration with either Filtek Silorane or Kalore. The patient is willing to complete a survey to evaluate their satisfaction with the preparation methods.

55-year-old male living in the urban population of Shanghai. He has a 20 pack-year history of smoking and has not attempted to quit smoking despite previous health concerns. He has no significant medical history and no family history of lung cancer, COPD or cardiovascular disease. The patient is asymptomatic and has not had any chest discomfort or respiratory issues. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to undergo low-dose CT scan at baseline and one year later. He understands the potential benefits of early detection of lung cancer, COPD and CVD and is motivated to participate in the study to improve his health outcomes.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with metastatic melanoma after noticing a mole on her back that had changed in size and color. She underwent surgery to remove the melanoma and has completed one round of chemotherapy.
