Her medical history includes hypertension, which is well controlled with medication, and she has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. Her most recent physical exam and lab study showed the following results: Weight: 66 kg, Height: 165 cm, BP: 130/80, HR: 85/min, RR: 18/min, Hgb: 12.5 g/dl, WBC: 8000/mm3, Neutrophil: 4000/mm3, Plt: 200,000/ml, AST: 40 U/L, ALT: 45 U/L, Alk P: 90 U/L, Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl, ESR: 30 mm/hr. The patient has not received immunotherapy with programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) or cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen (CTLA-4) targeted therapy. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of MK-3475 and INCB024360 in patients with metastatic melanoma.

A 45-year-old male was brought to the emergency department with a high-grade fever of 102°F, chills, and shortness of breath. He had a recent history of a urinary tract infection that was treated with antibiotics. However, his symptoms suddenly worsened, and he became increasingly lethargic. The patient was diagnosed with septic shock and transferred to the ICU. He has no significant past medical history, does not smoke, and drinks alcohol occasionally. Lab results showed elevated lactate levels (3.5 mmol/l) and decreased blood pressure (88/52 mmHg) requiring vasoactive drugs. He is expected to stay in the ICU for at least 2 days. The patient is affiliated with a social security system and has given informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 54-year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He was admitted to the hospital with chest pain and was diagnosed with unstable angina. After being evaluated by a cardiologist, it was determined that he required a coronary angiogram. The decision was made to perform the procedure via transradial access using a 6F sheath. Prior to the procedure, his blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg. During the procedure, the patient was administered 500-µg nitroglycerin through the radial sheath before sheath removal. Following the procedure, a continuous patent hemostasis was applied using an oximetry to maintain an oxygen saturation of >95%, measured in the finger of the accessed arm until the compression device was totally removed. The day after the procedure, a doppler ultrasound of the accessed artery was performed to evaluate the presence or absence of antegrade flow in the radial artery while compressing the ulnar artery. The internal lumen radial artery diameter was measured by doppler ultrasound as the distance between the inner walls of the artery. The patient's systolic blood pressure remained stable throughout the procedure and was recorded at 130/80 mmHg at the end of the procedure.

A 14-year-old female adolescent is brought in by her parents who express concern over their daughter's recent weight loss. The patient has lost approximately 15 pounds over the past 3 months and has expressed dissatisfaction with her body image. She has been restricting her food intake and has been exercising excessively. The patient's parents report that their daughter has become more withdrawn and isolated from family and friends. She has a history of anxiety and depression, but has never received any formal treatment. The patient is currently in eighth grade and is struggling in school due to her preoccupation with her weight and food intake. The patient's parents are willing to attend therapy sessions with their daughter to help her address her eating disorder. The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for anorexia nervosa according to the DSM-IV TR. The patient and her parents are medically cleared for outpatient care by their primary care physician. The patient does not have any co-morbid diagnoses of psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, or substance dependence. The patient has no diagnosis of mental retardation or pervasive developmental disorder. The patient's BMI is less than 90% of her ideal weight, as determined by weight history and CDC growth curves. The patient is not at acute risk for suicide.

A healthy Chinese adult woman aged between 25 to 30 years, who has no history of smoking or any medical illness is required for this clinical trial. She must agree not to donate eggs for the purpose of assisted reproduction during the study and until Day 113. She should not have any known allergies or clinically significant reactions to murine, chimeric, or human proteins, mAbs or antibody fragments, or to any components of the formulation of JNJ-64304500 and its excipients used in this study. She should not have had any major illness or surgery, requiring general anesthesia within 12 weeks before screening and should not have surgery planned during the time the participant is expected to participate in the study or until Day 113. She should not plan to undergo non-major elective surgery within 4 weeks prior to study intervention administration through the end of the study.

Pt is a 52yo male with newly diagnosed stage III thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. He has not received any prior anticancer therapy and is expected to survive more than 6 months. His WBC count is 5.2×109/L, neutrophil count is 2.3×109/L, platelet count is 120.0×109/L, and hemoglobin level is 12.0g/L. His liver and kidney functions are within normal limits. He has a KPS of 90 and has signed the informed consent form. He has no known allergies to cisplatin and 5-Fu and has no concomitant hemorrhagic disease. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has not had prior surgery that would prevent the use of a gastric conduit after esophagectomy. He does not have any significant peripheral neuropathy and has no prior malignancy other than esophageal carcinoma.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes for the past 10 years. He has been on angiotensin converting enzyme-inhibitor (ACE-I) medication for the last 2 years. His recent laboratory reports show elevated levels of albuminuria. His glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels are below 10.5%. The estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is above 60 mL/min/1.73m^2. The patient has not undergone renal dialysis or had acute kidney injury (AKI) within the last 3 months. He has not had a renal transplant. The serum potassium level is within the normal range of 3.5 to 5.0 mmol/L. The patient does not have clinically significant hypotension. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of MT-3995 in subjects with Type II Diabetic Nephropathy with Albuminuria.

The patient is a 32-year-old female diagnosed with bipolar disorder several years ago. She has been experiencing depression symptoms for the past 6 months despite taking several different medications at various dosages. She has no other medical conditions and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has experienced suicidal thoughts and has a history of self-harm. She reports difficulty concentrating, sleeping difficulties, loss of appetite, and feelings of hopelessness. She has had no response to previous treatments for bipolar depression, including multiple antidepressants and mood stabilizers. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. She has a good understanding of the study and is willing to comply with all testing and examination requirements. She is well-nourished and well-groomed, but appears tired and sad during the interview. The patient's score on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) is 28 at the time of screening. The patient is a candidate for the study and may benefit from the investigational drug felbamate.

A 55-year-old Hispanic male presented to the hospital with a history of diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He reported a recent episode of a foot ulcer that had resolved within the past 6 months. He had sensory abnormality with no skin breakdown/ulcer and had absent sensation to 10 g monofilament exam at 2 sites. Pedal pulses were palpable on both feet (dorsalis pedis & posttibialis). He was able to understand the use of the technology and had a life expectancy greater than the duration of the study. He was willing and able to maintain the required offloading and adhere to the routine calibration schedule required for the proper ongoing functioning of the device. He had diabetic shoes that were compatible with the Orpyx device. He did not have any gross foot deformity that would impact anatomical plantar pressure distribution, active infection or abnormal toe, ankle and/or foot range of motion that would preclude his ability to offload pressure alerts. He met all the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the study.

45 year-old male with a history of chronic periodontitis, presenting with bleeding gums, bad breath, and loose teeth. The patient has a good systemic health with no history of smoking, alcohol consumption, or use of smokeless tobacco. The patient has a minimum of 20 teeth, with at least one site in each quadrant having a probing pocket depth (PPD) of 4-7 mm and clinical attachment level (CAL) of 2 mm or greater. The patient has not undergone any periodontal therapy during the previous 6 months and is not on antibiotics or immunosuppressant medication. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and does not have any acute illnesses or intraoral lesions. The patient has provided consent to participate in the study and is willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 22-year-old young woman who has recently been diagnosed with anorexia nervosa and borderline personality disorder, and is currently receiving treatment. She lives with her parents and has a good relationship with them. She has a younger sister who is currently studying at college. She is currently unemployed and is taking a break from her studies. She enjoys reading books and watching movies in her free time. She has a history of anxiety and depression, and has been on medication for the same. She has also been to therapy in the past, but this is her first time receiving treatment for her eating disorder and personality disorder. She is fluent in Norwegian and has given her consent for her relative or close friend to participate in the psycho-educational group program. Her parents are concerned about her health and are looking for ways to support her better. They have agreed to participate in the program along with her.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been trying to conceive with her partner for over a year without success. She was diagnosed with anovulatory infertility and has undergone 5 ovulatory cycles of Clomiphene citrate induction (in a dose of 100 mg/day in two divided doses starting from day 3 of the cycle for 5 days) but without conception (clomiphene citrate failure) with thin endometrium (<8mm) in at least 3 cycles. She has normal baseline FSH, LH, and free testosterone levels, patent tubes on hysterosalpingography, and normal male semen analysis. She has no major medical problems, male factor infertility, endocrine abnormalities such as hyperprolactinemia or abnormal thyroid functions, prior ovarian or adnexal surgery, or organic pelvic pathology. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that involves using sildenafil vaginal gel in addition to Clomiphene citrate to improve her endometrial thickness and increase her chances of conception.

A 52-year-old female with a history of ovarian cancer presented to the oncology clinic with complaints of abdominal discomfort and bloating. The patient was diagnosed with stage IIIc ovarian cancer two years ago and underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy with a combination of taxane and platinum. However, the cancer recurred six months ago and the patient received additional chemotherapy with no response. The patient has a measurable lesion and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She has a life expectancy of more than three months and has no history of other malignancies within the past five years. The patient is not taking Coumadin or other warfarin-containing agents and has no active or suspected acute or chronic uncontrolled infection. She is not HIV positive and is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 65 year old woman who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. She has been experiencing symptoms of depression and cognitive decline that have been affecting her daily activities. She has no known history of any structural brain disease or other significant medical conditions. She is currently taking medication for her Parkinson's disease but is still experiencing non-motor symptoms. She is able to provide written informed consent and has a good understanding of the study. She is not currently undergoing any form of psychotherapy and has not had any changes to her depression treatment regimen in the past two weeks. She has never attempted suicide or had any history of substance abuse or dependence. She is not pregnant or considering becoming pregnant during the length of the study.

The patient is a healthy, full-term infant born with an Apgar score of 8. The infant is currently one month old and has not received any vaccinations for Hepatitis B. The infant's guardian has signed informed consent and is able to comply with the requirements of the clinical trial. The infant has not received any immunoglobulin during the following period and has an axillary temperature of 36.5℃. The infant has no history of nervous system damage, mental illness, epilepsy or encephalopathy. The infant is not immunodeficient, does not have vitamin deficiency, and has no congenital malformations, developmental disorders or serious chronic illness. The infant is not currently experiencing any acute febrile or infectious diseases, and has no history of thrombocytopenia or other coagulation disorders. The infant is not participating in any other clinical trial during the period of the clinical trial and does not have any circumstances that may affect clinical trial evaluation.

A 35-year old woman who works as a teacher was diagnosed with atopic dermatitis 5 years ago. She has tried several creams and ointments, but her symptoms have persisted. She reports experiencing severe itching, redness, and scaling on her arms, legs, and torso. Her AD has made it difficult for her to sleep at night, and she also reports feeling embarrassed and self-conscious about her skin. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her physical exam reveals erythematous, scaly plaques on her arms, legs, and torso. Her Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score is 20 and Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) is 4. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to receive dupilumab and undergo molecular profiling of her skin lesions. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the protocol. She is not pregnant or nursing and will use adequate contraception during the study period.

The patient is a 6-year-old boy scheduled for an elective penile surgery (hypospadias / circumcision). The patient has no known history of neurological or muscular disorders. The patient's parents have provided informed consent for the study. The patient has not undergone any peripheral nerve blocks for this surgery or any other surgeries in the past.

A 6-year-old boy with a history of recurrent upper respiratory infections presents to the emergency department with a fever, cough, and shortness of breath for the past 3 days. He has been using an inhaler for wheezing episodes but has not had any recent episodes. His parents report that he has been fatigued and not eating well. On physical examination, he is febrile with a temperature of 38.8°C, tachycardic with a heart rate of 120 bpm, and tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute. Lung auscultation reveals crackles in the left lower lobe. A chest x-ray shows consolidation in the left lower lobe consistent with community-acquired pneumonia. He is admitted to the pediatric ward and started on antibiotics. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial, and his parents consent to participate.

This is a 32 year-old female with a history of schizophrenia who has completed treatment with antipsychotic medication and is now stable. She is fluent in English and lives in New York City. She is currently unemployed but looking for work. She has not participated in cognitive remediation in the past 12 months. She is interested in participating in this study to see if it can help improve her cognitive functioning and daily functioning. She has no hearing or visual impairments and no other neurological illness that may affect brain physiology. She meets the inclusion criteria for this study.

A 9-year-old boy with a body weight of 18 kg has been suffering from perennial allergic rhinitis for the past year. He has been experiencing moderate to severe symptoms such as nasal congestion, sneezing, and itchy eyes. His serum specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) caused by house dust mites is 3 or higher. He has not been treated with any medications that may affect the evaluation of the investigational drug. He has not been diagnosed with any other nasal or respiratory diseases that may affect the evaluation of the investigational drug. His parent will be able to enter his symptoms in the Patient Diary. He is eligible to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with malignant pleural mesothelioma. He has a history of exposure to asbestos at his previous job as a construction worker. He has already undergone one cycle of first line chemotherapy (pemetrexed and cisplatin) but did not respond well to the treatment. He is currently experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain, and his performance status according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) is 1. He has measurable disease by CT scan and the predominant burden of disease is in an arterial distribution which is accessible for transarterial chemoperfusion treatment. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He has no history of severe allergic reactions to any chemotherapy agents or intravenous contrast media. His laboratory values are within normal limits, and he is surgically sterile. He has no other significant medical conditions, and he is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, laboratory tests, imaging studies, and other requirements of the study.

The patient is a 55 year old man who was previously diagnosed with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and underwent chemoradiotherapy treatment three years ago. Unfortunately, the cancer has recurred in the same area that was previously treated with radiation. The patient is experiencing difficulty swallowing and has noticed a visible lump in his neck. Biopsy confirmed the presence of recurrent cancer. The patient is currently being evaluated for salvage surgery to remove the cancerous tissue. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise in good health. The patient has been informed about the clinical trial that will evaluate the use of fluorescence in salvage surgery for recurrence of head and neck cancer in irradiated area and has expressed interest in participating.

A 68-year-old woman was referred to the clinic because of hypertension and high cholesterol levels. She has been taking medication for both conditions for the past 2 years. She is currently retired and lives alone at home. Her last physical exam and lab study was performed 3 months ago and showed the results below: A well-nourished woman, non-icteric, cooperative and alert Weight: 65 kg Height: 163 cm BP: 140/90 HR: 80/min RR: 18/min Hgb: 12.5 g/dl WBC: 6900 /mm3 (Neutrophil: 4400/mm3) Plt: 280000 /ml AST: 32 U/L ALT: 35 U/L Alk P: 98 U/L Bill total: 0.8 mg/dl LDL-C: 170 mg/dl HDL-C: 50 mg/dl Triglycerides: 220 mg/dl

A 32-year-old male smoker presents with a 10-year history of smoking 10-15 cigarettes per day. He has tried to quit smoking several times in the past, but has been unsuccessful. He expresses a strong desire to quit smoking and is highly motivated to try new methods. He reports occasional alcohol use, but denies excessive drinking. He does not use chewing tobacco, snuff or cigars. He has no history of depression or suicidal tendencies. He is comfortable using technology and has access to a computer with an internet connection.

A 32-year-old woman with a history of congenital heart disease was diagnosed with Eisenmenger's Syndrome. She has been experiencing shortness of breath and fatigue for the past few months, which has been gradually worsening. She is a non-smoker and has no other significant medical history. She has previously undergone corrective surgery for her congenital heart disease but was left with residual pulmonary hypertension. Her six-minute walk test revealed a distance of 280 meters, and echocardiography showed an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 80 mmHg. She has been started on bosentan therapy, but her symptoms have not improved significantly. The treating physician decided to add sildenafil to her treatment regimen to further improve her pulmonary arterial pressures and oxygenation. She has been compliant with her medications and has not experienced any adverse effects.

28 year old female seeking a long-acting reversible contraceptive method. She is nulliparous with no history of vaginal deliveries. She has a BMI of 24 kg/m2 and is fluent in both English and Thai. She has never used an intrauterine device (IUD) before and is interested in trying the Copper T IUD. However, she is concerned about the potential pain associated with the insertion procedure. She has no known allergies or medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study. She has not taken any analgesics or anxiolytics within the last 24 hours.

A 52-year-old woman with a history of pulmonary arterial hypertension presents with shortness of breath and chest pain. She has been on sildenafil for the past 6 months and is currently stable. She has no history of bleeding disorders or recent surgeries. Her blood pressure is 130/85 mm Hg, heart rate 90 bpm, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air. She is afebrile and has no signs of infection. Her laboratory workup is unremarkable except for a mildly elevated D-dimer level. A right heart catheterization is performed to assess her pulmonary hypertension and blood samples are collected during the procedure for the study. She has no history of renal, hepatic, or thyroid dysfunction, malignancy, or abnormal red blood counts. She is not currently receiving any anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy. She is interested in participating in the study to help improve the understanding of her disease and possibly contribute to the development of new treatments.

A 57 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and is currently undergoing induction chemotherapy. She is considering undergoing a hematopoietic cell transplant with a preparative regimen that includes total body irradiation (TBI). She has undergone a serum creatinine test within the past 7 days which has confirmed adequate renal function. She is willing and able to provide written consent. She does not have any ferromagnetic implants, history of shrapnel or shot gun injury, cardiac pacemakers or other implanted devices that are not MR-compatible, or large tattoos.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy non-smoking female with a BMI of 22. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and is using effective contraceptive measures. She has no history of significant illnesses or drug abuse. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine the effect of steady-state colchicine on the pharmacokinetics of theophylline administered as a single dose. She is also willing to undergo blood sampling and monitoring for adverse events throughout the study period. She has no allergies or sensitivity to colchicine or theophylline or aminophylline.

John is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23 kg/m2. He works as a software engineer and has no history of any chronic or acute illness. John does not smoke or drink alcohol, and he does not take any medications or supplements. He has no history of drug allergies. John has not participated in any clinical study within the last 30 days. He is willing to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures. John has provided a personally signed and dated informed consent document indicating that he has been informed of all pertinent aspects of the study. He has no history of irregular bowel movements, IBS, or lactose intolerance. He does not have any occupation that requires exposure to radiation or monitoring of radiation exposure. John has no partners who are currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. He is willing and able to use two highly effective methods of contraception for the duration of the study and for at least 90 days after the last dose of investigational product, as outlined in the protocol.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with atrial fibrillation during a routine checkup. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes multiple medications. The patient has a history of stroke, which occurred three years ago and left him with mild residual neurological deficits. He is currently taking a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) for stroke prevention. The patient reports that he sometimes forgets to take his medication, especially when he is busy or traveling. He has tried using a pillbox in the past, but found it difficult to remember to refill it every week. The patient is interested in participating in a study that may help him improve his adherence to his DOAC medication. He is able to self-administer his medication and is willing to use a pillbox. The patient agrees to sign the informed consent form and is available for follow-up visits over the course of the 12-month trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He is currently on medication for both conditions and his blood pressure and blood sugar levels are well-controlled. He has a family history of heart disease and stroke. Recently, he has been experiencing episodes of dizziness and occasional blurred vision. Upon further evaluation, carotid artery stenosis was identified on ultrasound, with a plaque thickness of 3.5mm and a stenosis of 50%. He has not had any transient ischemic attacks or strokes in the past 6 months. His LDL cholesterol level is below 100 mg/dL and he has no contraindications to MRI. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided informed consent.

55 yo M with a history of smoking for 30 years presenting with cough and hemoptysis. Chest CT reveals a mass in the left lower lobe suspicious for lung cancer, biopsy confirmed non-small cell lung cancer. The patient is scheduled for lobectomy and preoperative pulmonary function tests showed borderline pulmonary function. The patient has no other tumors, has not received surgery prior to SPECT/CT scan, and is willing to complete preoperative and postoperative pulmonary function tests as well as scans. The patient has normal renal and liver function, does not have poorly controlled diabetes, and is compliant with medical recommendations. The patient has no mental illness and is suitable for clinical trials. The patient has given written and informed consent to participate in the study.

As this is not a clinical trial, a patient description is not necessary. However, if we were to provide a brief summary of the type of participant this study would involve, it would be pregnant women who carried full-term infants between 1991 and 1994.

A 48-year-old male smoker visited the oncology clinic with a cough that he had for 2 months. He also reported shortness of breath and fatigue. He was diagnosed with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer after a biopsy of the lung mass. The patient has no history of any other types of cancer. His performance status is ECOG 1, and he has no symptoms of CNS or leptomeningeal metastases. The patient has no history of liver, renal, or cardiovascular disease, and his laboratory results show WBC of 5500/mm3, hemoglobin of 12.5 g/dL, neutrophil count of 3000/mm3, and platelet count of 120,000/mm3. The creatinine level is 0.9 mg/dL, and the bilirubin level is 1.5 mg/dL. The patient has no active uncontrolled infection, and he is not pregnant or nursing. He has no other medical conditions that would preclude the study. He has not received any chemotherapy or investigational drugs in the past 30 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer). The patient is willing to use effective contraception for 3 months before, during, and for at least 4 weeks after the study.

A 45-year-old male with a history of Type 2 diabetes and currently taking metformin for glycemic control. His HbA1c is between 7% to 9%. He has a BMI of 28 and is willing to maintain a stable diet and exercise routine for the duration of the study. He has not taken any other anti-diabetic medication in the last three months and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He has no significant history of alcohol or substance abuse, epilepsy or recurrent seizures, or depression. He has no history of suicidal ideation or self-harm. He has no known hypersensitivity to cannabinoids or any of the excipients of the IMPs. He is not pregnant, lactating, or planning pregnancy during the course of the study. He has not received any Investigational Medicinal Product within the 12 weeks prior to the screening visit. He is willing to abstain from donation of blood during the study and has no significant disease or disorder that may put him at risk because of participation in the study.

The patient is a 14-year-old female with a diagnosis of Crohn's disease. She was diagnosed at age 11 and has been on methotrexate for the past year to maintain disease remission. Her current medication regimen includes methotrexate once per week and daily folic acid supplements. She reports difficulty remembering to take her daily folic acid supplements and has missed several doses in the past month. She has otherwise been compliant with her medication regimen and has not experienced any disease flares in the past year. Her past medical history is significant for a broken arm at age 8, and she has no known drug allergies. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings and attends school regularly. She is otherwise healthy and active, participating in sports and extracurricular activities. Her current weight is 52 kg and her height is 1.6 meters. She is eager to participate in the study as she hopes it will reduce the burden of daily medication administration.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis. He has been suffering from symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding for more than three months. Despite undergoing conventional treatments such as mesalamine, glucocorticoids, immunosuppressants, and anti-TNFs, the patient has not responded favorably. The patient is willing to participate in the study and must be between 16 and 80 years old. The patient must also have a total Mayo score of at least 6, including a centrally read endoscopic subscore of at least 2, a rectal bleeding subscore of at least 1, and a stool frequency subscore of at least 1 at baseline. Additionally, the patient must be willing to undergo a flexible sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy, including biopsy sample collection, during screening. The patient must not have any significant concurrent medical condition and must not have received SHP647 or any other biologics or immunomodulatory treatments within a specific period before the baseline visit. The patient must also not have any history of cancer or lymphoproliferative disease within the previous five years, and must not be pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study period.

The patient is a 72-year-old male who was admitted to the ICU after suffering a heart attack. Despite initial treatment, his condition has deteriorated and he is now intubated and unable to make decisions for himself. His family members, including his wife and two adult children, are serving as his surrogate decision makers. They are all fluent in English and able to read and write. The patient has no known history of advance care planning or end-of-life discussions. The family is experiencing significant emotional distress and uncertainty about making decisions regarding their loved one's care. They have expressed a desire to be more involved in the decision-making process and to fully understand their options. They have agreed to participate in the study and use the web-based tool to improve communication and shared decision making with the ICU clinicians.

A 25-year-old female volunteer who is interested in participating in the clinical trial came to the clinic. She is in good health and has not been diagnosed with any chronic diseases. Her BMI is 22 kg/m2, and she maintains an active lifestyle by regularly attending fitness classes. She is not pregnant, and she is not breastfeeding. She does not smoke or drink alcohol frequently. She has not taken any investigational drugs in the past 30 days. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is willing to comply with all study procedures.

A 52-year-old male patient presents with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. He has been experiencing pain in his legs while walking for the past few months and has noticed that the pain subsides after resting for a few minutes. On examination, the patient is found to have reduced pedal pulses bilaterally and a bruit is heard over the femoral arteries. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.65 on the left and 0.72 on the right. The patient is diagnosed with peripheral artery disease (PAD) and is started on treatment with Rivaroxaban 2.5mg tablet, co-administered with acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) for the prevention of atherothrombotic events. The patient is willing to participate in this study and signs the informed consent form. The patient's medical history reveals that he has had a previous myocardial infarction (MI) and coronary artery disease (CAD) is also diagnosed. The treating doctor decides to continue the patient on the current treatment regimen and enroll him in the clinical trial to assess the effectiveness and safety of the medication combination.

15-year-old male with a history of social anxiety and depressive symptoms, as reported by both the patient and parent on the Revised Children's Anxiety and Depression Scale. The patient is seeking help for his symptoms and is currently not receiving any treatment. He has no history of other psychiatric disorders, psychosis, or acute suicide risk. The patient has adequate language proficiency and no intellectual disability.

A 65-year-old man presented to the clinic with a history of smoking for 40 years. He has been experiencing cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue for the past few months. A chest X-ray showed a solitary pulmonary lesion. A CT scan revealed a 2 cm mass in the upper lobe of the left lung. The patient has no history of lung cancer and does not have any other medical problems. He has never had any surgery before. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with end-stage renal disease due to hypertension. He has been on dialysis for the past 2 years and is now a candidate for kidney transplantation. He has no history of malignancy or systemic infection. His BMI is 24, and he has not had any previous organ transplant surgeries. He is not currently pregnant or lactating, and has signed informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He is willing to undergo transplantation with a deceased donor kidney that meets the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 28-year-old male who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a C5 spinal cord injury. He has no known medical history and has not had any previous spinal cord injuries. He is currently experiencing sensory and motor deficits below the level of the injury and has a modified Frankel Scale score of B2. He is able to provide written informed consent and does not have any allergies to the drug scheduled to be used in the study. He is not currently nursing or pregnant.

Patient is a 28-year-old woman who was diagnosed with anti-LGI1 encephalitis based on sera or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples in the National Reference Center of autoimmune encephalitis from 2011/06 to 2019 July 1st. She has a history of faciobrachial dystonic seizures and cognitive disorders. The patient is currently undergoing clinical follow-up in France. She does not have any other autoimmune encephalitis associated with anti-LGI1 antibodies, and she is not a foreign patient.

The patient is a 30 year old healthy male with no history of prostate cancer or other significant medical conditions. He has no pacemakers, surgical implants or foreign metal objects in his body. He has no known allergies to contrast agents used in MRI imaging. The patient is willing to participate in the study as a healthy volunteer and understands that the study involves the use of an eight-channel paddle coil system to be used in future Hyperpolarized (13C) Pyruvate Injection studies. The patient has been fully informed of the study procedures and has provided written consent.

10-year-old male, overweight with a BMI of 27. He is generally healthy with no known medical conditions or allergies. He has been experiencing occasional constipation, but no other gastrointestinal symptoms. He takes a daily multivitamin but has not taken antibiotics or probiotics in the past 6 months. He has a family history of obesity and type 2 diabetes, with both parents and siblings being overweight. He is active and participates in regular recreational activities. He is willing to provide a stool sample for the trial.

A 52-year-old male patient with a history of gout is being considered for a Phase 3 extension study for a new treatment combination of lesinurad and febuxostat. The patient has been diagnosed with gout for 10 years and has been on febuxostat for the last 4 years. The patient has a serum uric acid level of 8.2 mg/dL and has experienced recurrent flares despite being on febuxostat. The patient has no history of cardiovascular disease, hypertension, diabetes or any other major illness. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks involved. The patient has no history of allergies to any drugs and is not currently on any medication other than febuxostat. The patient is willing to use an effective non-hormonal method of birth control during the study period.

Patient A is a 25-year-old male who was bitten by a copperhead snake on his right foot while hiking in a forested area. He presented at a nearby health care facility within 12 hours of the envenomation with a swollen and tender foot. He reports feeling a sharp pain at the time of the bite, but no other symptoms. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. He is able to read and comprehend written assessment tools and is willing to complete the follow-up schedule of assessments. He is sober, competent, and able to complete verbal and written informed consent. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and he has not had a previous snake envenomation to any body area within 30 days prior to screening/enrollment. He is at least 18 years old and is not a prisoner. He is eligible for enrollment in the Copperhead Envenomation Observational Study.

Patient A is a 2-month-old baby boy who was born at full term pregnancy with a birth weight of 3.2 kg. He is currently in good health and has no known medical conditions. His parents have agreed to participate in a clinical trial to assess the immunogenicity and safety of a new combination vaccine for diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, and polio. The trial requires three doses of the vaccine to be administered at 2, 4, and 6 months of age. The parents are able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with all trial procedures. The baby has not participated in any other clinical trials within the last 4 weeks and does not have any congenital or acquired immunodeficiency. He has not received any blood or blood-derived products in the past or planned administration during the trial. There is no history of a life-threatening reaction to vaccines or any vaccine components. The baby has not had any vaccinations within the last 3 weeks and has no history of diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, or poliomyelitis infection. He does not have any bleeding disorders or contraindications to intramuscular vaccination. The baby has no known family history of congenital or genetic immunodeficiency.

A 56-year-old female with a history of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) presents with symptoms of palpitations, shortness of breath, and fatigue. She has been on several anti-arrhythmic medications but has been unable to control her symptoms. She has no history of cardiac surgery or thoracic surgery. She is interested in exploring other treatment options and is open to participating in a clinical trial. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. She is willing to undergo general anesthesia if required for the procedure.

A 45-year-old male presents to the emergency department with shortness of breath, cough, and wheezing. He has a history of asthma and is a non-smoker. His vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 94% on room air. Physical examination reveals bilateral expiratory wheezing, and the patient is diagnosed with an acute exacerbation of asthma. He is admitted to the hospital for treatment and is offered the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial comparing collaborative, integrated pathway-based healthcare versus usual care in reducing the length of hospital stay for patients with acute exacerbation of asthma. The patient meets the eligibility criteria for the study and provides informed consent to participate.

A 35-year-old healthy female presents with no significant medical history. She is physically active and maintains a healthy lifestyle. She is not pregnant and has no plans to become pregnant in the next 8 weeks. She reports no symptoms of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, and has no family history of such conditions. The patient has no internal metal medical devices, nor any non-removable jewelry. She is able to walk 50 yards without stopping and follow a 3-step command. The patient is willing and able to travel to the hospital for study visits, and able to remain in the magnetic resonance (MR) scanner for up to 2 hours. She reports no serious mental illness that might preclude her ability to comply with study treatment. She is not currently taking hormonal birth control and is a non-smoker.

A 47-year-old man was diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma six months ago. He received standard chemotherapy containing anthracycline, but he did not respond and the disease progressed rapidly. He was then treated with rituximab, but he relapsed after eight months. He is now experiencing severe night sweats, unexplained weight loss, and fatigue. His ECOG performance status is 1. His lab results show that his creatinine level is 120 micromol/L, and his platelets count is 110 G/L. He has not been treated with any investigational drug in the past 30 days and has not received any radiotherapy in the past four weeks. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form.

An 80-year-old female patient with a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia presented to the memory clinic with subjective complaints of memory loss and difficulty with daily activities. She reported that her symptoms had been progressively worsening over the past year. She denied any history of depression, anxiety, or other psychiatric disorders. Her family history was significant for Alzheimer's disease in her mother and maternal aunt. Her physical examination was unremarkable. Cognitive testing revealed a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 18/30, consistent with mild cognitive impairment. She was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and was referred to the clinical trial for further evaluation. She provided informed consent and was included in the trial. Her medication history included amlodipine, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. She had not taken any antibiotics or had any recent gastrointestinal illness or hospitalization in the past month.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pain in her right hip joint for several years, which has gradually worsened over time. She has a history of osteoarthritis and has tried different medications and therapies, but none have provided long-lasting relief. She has been advised by her orthopedic surgeon to undergo a total hip replacement surgery, and she is scheduled to have the surgery in two weeks. She reports feeling anxious about the procedure and has difficulty sleeping at night due to the pain. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history or concurrent illnesses. She is not taking any medication that could interfere with the study drug. She is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and follow the medication regimen as directed.

The patient is a female who has been diagnosed with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. She has had prior debulking surgery and has received one or two prior systemic cytotoxic regimens, including platinum-based chemotherapy. The patient has a measurable lesion according to RECIST v1.1 and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 to 1. She is over the age of 18 and has recovered from any prior cytotoxic therapy-associated acute toxicities. The patient has adequate organ function, including normal bone marrow reserve, hepatic function, renal function, and cardiac function. The patient has not had prior exposure to PLD or anthracycline therapy or prior exposure to FR-targeted therapy. The patient is not currently pregnant or nursing and does not have any other concurrent malignancy requiring therapy. The patient is willing to undergo imaging with the FR-targeting investigational diagnostic agent EC20 during the screening period to assess binding of the imaging agent EC20 to tumors. The patient is willing to participate in a Phase 3 clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the combination of EC145 and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD) compared to PLD and placebo.

The patient is a 45-year-old Caucasian female who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). She underwent a hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) as a treatment for her advanced-stage leukemia. The patient is currently in remission and no active GVHD is present. The patient is eligible for the clinical trial as she is considered high-risk for relapse after HSCT. She has no history of serious infection or organ failure and is willing to undergo the GPBPCI regimen comprised of G-CSF-primed PBSCs instead of harvested non-primed donor lymphocytes and short-term immunosuppressive agents for prevention of GVHD after GPBPCI. The patient understands that chimerism status will be examined before and after prophylactic treatment with GPBPCI. She has been fully informed about the study and has given written and oral consent to participate.

The patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of HIV and HCV coinfection. He has been under antiretroviral therapy for the past 2 years, and his CD4 count is 420/mm³. He was previously treated with pegylated interferon alpha 2a and ribavirin for 3 months but did not respond to treatment. He has a Metavir score with histological fibrosis score F2. He is currently not taking ribavirin. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adding IL-2 to his current treatment regimen. He has no history of cirrhosis or other liver disease and is not pregnant. He is willing to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

No patient description can be generated for this clinical trial as it does not involve recruiting individual patients. The trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of a family-based economic empowerment intervention for AIDS-orphaned children in Uganda. The study will be conducted via a three-group cluster randomized control trial, with participants being families of AIDS-orphaned children who are enrolled in grade 5 or 6 of primary school and living within a family.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with a unilateral invasive breast carcinoma. She has no history of malignancy within the last 5 years and has not undergone any neoadjuvant treatment. Imaging techniques estimate the tumor size to be less than 5 cm. She has no clinical evidence of distant metastasis and is planned for breast-conserving surgery with postoperative external whole-breast irradiation. The axilla appears to be clinically and sonographically tumor-free prior to core biopsy. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial, which will randomly assign her to either no axillary surgical intervention or axillary sentinel lymph node biopsy.

The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of mild liver impairment due to chronic hepatitis B. She has been on antiviral treatment for the past 6 months with stable liver function tests. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of liver transplantation, liver failure, or cirrhosis. She has a BMI of 26 and weighs 59 kg. Her vital signs are within normal limits, and her laboratory test results show an ANC of 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelet count of 100 x 10^9/L, Hgb of 12.5 g/dL, ALT and AST of 3 times the upper limit of normal, and a CLcr of 80 mL/min. She has no significant abnormalities on physical examination, 12-lead ECG, or EEG. She has not had any major surgeries or infections within the past 6 months. She is not pregnant, lactating, or planning to become pregnant during the study. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who has no known chronic medical conditions and is not on any medication. He has no personal history of transient ischemic attacks or life-threatening diseases. He has a systolic blood pressure of 130 mm Hg and a diastolic blood pressure of 80 mm Hg. The patient has never had any surgical treatment for atherosclerotic lesions localized in the extracranial brachiocephalic system. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to help advance the understanding of asymptomatic atherosclerosis and contribute to the development of effective diagnostic tests.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). He has been treated with fludarabine and chemoimmunotherapy, but unfortunately, he has not responded well to these treatments. The patient is feeling tired and weak and has also experienced night sweats and weight loss. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has no other major medical conditions and has adequate organ function and laboratory parameters. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the trial. He agrees to use a medically accepted method of contraception should he become sexually active while participating in the study. The patient has not previously been treated with ofatumumab, dinaciclib, or other CDK inhibitors. He is hopeful that this trial will help him achieve better outcomes and improve his quality of life.

The patient is a 65-year-old French-speaking male who has a medical history of coronary artery disease with a previous myocardial infarction. He is currently taking antiplatelet therapy and a beta-blocker medication to manage his condition. He is retired and lives with his wife in a suburban area. The patient has a BMI of 29 and has never smoked or consumed alcohol heavily. He is scheduled to undergo elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass for aortic valve replacement. He has no history of psychiatric disorders or epilepsy and has completed his preoperative neurocognitive tests. He has not had any recent episodes of delirium. He has no known family history of Alzheimer's disease or other neurological disorders. He has normal kidney function and does not require dialysis. The patient has given written and verbal consent to participate in the study.

34 yo F with a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and depression referred to Exercise for Health (EFH) program by her GP due to inactivity. She is currently on medication for her hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is seeing a therapist for her depression. She has expressed interest in starting an exercise program but is unsure of where to start and is worried about her ability to keep up with a regular exercise routine. She has been referred to both Centre A and Centre B for the EFH program and will be given the option to participate in either the adapted EFH program or the standard EFH program. She is fluent in English and able to understand the participant information sheet.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has been experiencing chronic pelvic pain for the past year. She has been diagnosed with endometriosis and her gynecologist has recommended laparoscopic surgery to remove the affected tissue. She is currently taking birth control pills as a treatment for her condition. She has no history of chronic diseases, mental illnesses or immunodeficiency. She is a non-smoker and abstains from alcohol and drug use. She has signed a written informed consent to participate in the study and has agreed to follow instructions and complete all required questionnaires. She is willing to undergo the planned laparoscopy for the treatment of her endometriosis and is expected to have a surgery duration that exceeds 60 minutes.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He was diagnosed with diabetes 5 years ago and is currently taking metformin to manage his blood sugar levels. He has no significant history of cardiovascular, muscular, lung, kidney or psychiatric disease. His 12-lead ECG is normal. He works an office job and exercises moderately, approximately 3 times a week. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially. He is not currently taking any medication that can affect the autonomic nervous system. He has never been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or ischemic heart disease. He does not have a history of malignant disease, HIV, alcoholism or drug abuse.

The patient is a 62-year-old woman diagnosed with endometrial cancer of grade II. She has no history of prior treatment for her cancer and has clinically uterine confined disease. The patient is scheduled for minimal invasive surgery with sentinel lymph node assessment with IC-GREEN planned as part of standard of care. Her Eastern Cooperative Group (ECOG) performance status is 1. She has undergone a negative pregnancy test within 72 hours before administration of Lymphoseek and is postmenopausal for at least 2 years. The patient has provided written informed consent and is not currently participating in another investigational drug study. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient has no known iodine allergy.

Samantha is a 32 year old woman who is 38 weeks pregnant with her first child. She has no significant medical history but has been diagnosed with gestational diabetes. She monitors her blood sugar levels regularly and follows a strict diet. Samantha is 165 cm tall and weighs 70 kg. She has an uneventful pregnancy and has no history of hypertension or preeclampsia. She has no known allergies to medications or hydroxyethylstarch. She has not undergone any spinal surgeries or has any neurological disorders. She is scheduled for an elective Cesarean section due to a breech presentation. Her physical exam and lab studies were normal. Samantha is willing to participate in the clinical trial and follow the study protocol.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who was diagnosed with pulmonary stenosis after experiencing shortness of breath and chest pain. She has a history of congenital heart defects and underwent corrective surgery as a child. She has been experiencing increasing symptoms for the past year and has been referred to a German cardiological center for further evaluation and treatment. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has given informed consent. She is not pregnant or nursing and has no other clinically relevant diseases. She is able to undergo MRI and spiroergometry.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with type II diabetes. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. Her blood pressure has been consistently between 130-140 mmHg for the past few months, indicating prehypertension. She has not been on any antihypertensive or diabetes treatment before. Her HbA1c level is between 7.0-8.0. She has no known allergies and is willing to participate in the study. She has no history of chronic renal disease, heart or respiratory failure, recent MI, or shock. She is not pregnant or lactating. She will be required to attend clinical examinations at various intervals throughout the 3-year study duration.

A 56 year old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of severe headaches, blurred vision and difficulty in walking. The patient has also been experiencing numbness in her arms and legs. The patient reports a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and was treated with R-CHOP combination therapy two years ago. Recent brain MRI revealed CNS involvement, and a biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. The patient has not received any previous treatment with high-dose methotrexate-based chemotherapy and/or brain irradiation. The patient's bone marrow function, renal, cardiac, and hepatic function are normal. The patient is negative for HIV infection and detectable HCV-RNA and/or HBsAg and/or HBV-DNA. The patient has no other concurrent malignancies and is non-pregnant and non-lactating. The patient is sexually active and is implementing adequate contraceptive measures. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given written consent to the study protocol and follow-up schedule. The patient has no other serious medical conditions that could impair her ability to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma. He has no significant past medical history and is a non-smoker. He is scheduled to undergo an elective open hepatectomy surgery at Queen Mary Hospital in Hong Kong. He has not received any chemotherapy or steroid therapy in the past year. He is not currently on any medication. He is willing to participate in the randomized, controlled trial comparing the effects of TIVA versus inhalational anaesthesia on circulating tumour cells in hepatocellular carcinoma patients.

This is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with sarcoma that is locally advanced and at high risk for relapse or metastasis. She is eligible to participate in a clinical trial that aims to compare two treatment schedules of Aloxi (palonosetron) in patients receiving chemotherapy with adriamycin and ifosfamide. The main purpose of the study is to evaluate the safety of the drug and schedules, and the effect of palonosetron on patients' quality of life. The patient will have several blood samples taken to monitor blood counts during chemotherapy, and will be asked to fill out a QOL questionnaire about nausea and vomiting. She will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups, and will receive palonosetron as an intravenous infusion over 30 minutes. She will also receive chemotherapy as part of her standard treatment, which will include at least 2 cycles of adriamycin and ifosfamide. The patient will be asked to return to the clinic every 3 weeks for evaluation of her disease, by having a chest x-ray, a CT scan, an MRI scan, and a physical exam performed. Additional blood samples will be taken before each cycle and as often as needed to measure her blood counts and electrolytes. The patient will be asked to contact the study doctor or nurse about any bad side effects she experiences or any medications she takes during the treatment period. Her treatment will continue for at least 6 cycles, unless her disease gets worse or she experiences intolerable side effects. Once she stops treatment, she will have an end-of-study visit to evaluate her disease status and have a final blood draw for routine tests. Her participation in this study should end at about 18 weeks (4 to 5 months).

Patient is a 57-year-old man from the United States who was recently diagnosed with Stage III MCC. He has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. He is currently not on any other medications. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is willing to undergo a diagnostic biopsy and whole blood sample. He has not received any prior systemic cytotoxic chemotherapies or novel immunotherapy treatments for MCC, but is willing to participate in this Phase II trial to determine the effects of aNK infusions in combination with ALT-803. He understands that he may be randomly assigned to receive the combination therapy and that he may experience certain side effects from the treatment. He is willing to provide voluntary written informed consent and understands that he may withdraw from the study at any time without prejudice to future medical care. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old overweight woman who is pregnant for the first time. She is in the first trimester of her pregnancy and has a history of high blood pressure. She is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is married and works as a nurse. She is currently taking prenatal vitamins and has not taken any aspirin or heparin. She does not have any allergies to medication. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help prevent preeclampsia, as she is aware of the potential risks associated with this condition.

The patient is a 35-year-old healthy male with no significant medical history. He has a BMI of 24 and weighs 75 kg. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has not been taking any medications, including herbal or natural health products, for the past 2 weeks. He is sexually active and uses condoms as a method of birth control. He has no known allergies to any of the study medications. He is willing to abstain from alcohol for 3 days prior to and during the study. He has no history of hypertension or heart disease and is not currently taking any medications for these conditions. The patient is able and willing to sign informed consent prior to any study-related activities.

Patient A is a 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with Pompe disease at the age of 25. He has been receiving enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) with Myozyme for the last 5 years, but his condition has been slowly deteriorating. Despite the ERT, he experiences muscle weakness, difficulty breathing, and fatigue. He works as a software engineer and enjoys spending time with his family. He is interested in participating in the expanded access program for ATB200/AT2221 and is willing to sign the authorization form for sharing clinical data with Amicus Therapeutics and its agent Early Access Care LLC. He has not received any gene therapy in the past and is not currently taking any of the excluded medications.

The patient is a 67-year-old woman who underwent an aortic valve replacement surgery five years ago due to severe aortic valve stenosis. She received a Carbomedics Carbo-seal valve replacement in the surgery. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. Currently, her medical conditions are well controlled with medications. She complains of occasional shortness of breath on exertion but otherwise feels well. She lives with her husband and has two adult children who live in a different state. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. Her last echocardiogram showed preserved left ventricular systolic function, and her valve function was normal. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to help advance the understanding of valve replacement and to contribute to medical research.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. He has been taking metformin and amlodipine for the past year. Recently, he has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath, especially during physical activity. He was diagnosed with stable angina and is scheduled for an elective coronary intervention. He has no history of chronic renal failure or cancer. His serum creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dl. He has not been taking statins for the past three months and has no contraindications to statin therapy. He has not received contrast media injection within the preceding 10 days and has consented to participate in the study.

This is a 58-year-old male with a history of smoking, who presented with cough, hemoptysis, and shortness of breath. Imaging studies revealed a mass in the right lung and subsequent biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic Stage IV Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) with an activating epidermal growth factor receptor mutation (EGFRmt). The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has not received any prior systemic chemotherapy for Stage IV NSCLC. Adequate tumor material is available for analysis. The patient does not have interstitial pneumonia or interstitial fibrosis of the lung and does not have pleural effusion, pericardial fluids or ascites requiring drainage every other week or more frequently. The patient has not undergone major surgery in the last 2 weeks and is not pregnant or lactating. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the efficacy of the study drug LY2875358, given together with erlotinib, against erlotinib alone.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection two years ago during a routine check-up. He has no significant medical history except for a history of occasional alcohol consumption. He is not currently on any treatment for his CHB infection. His latest lab results show a detectable level of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and a high level of HBV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) of 50,000 IU/mL. He denies any symptoms related to his CHB infection such as fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or jaundice. He is not currently pregnant nor lactating. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of multiple oral doses of Selgantolimod (Formerly GS-9688) and its antiviral activity for the treatment of CHB infection.

52-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis B who previously completed an Idenix-sponsored trial with telbivudine. The patient did not discontinue treatment in the previous study due to an efficacy response and requires further treatment. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is not co-infected with hepatitis C, hepatitis D, or HIV.

A 56 year old man was diagnosed with COVID-19 and was hospitalized due to severe respiratory symptoms. Despite being treated with oxygen therapy, his condition has worsened and he is now at high risk of developing life-threatening hyperinflammation. His C-reactive protein (CRP) level has been rising since the last 24 hours and it is currently at 90 mg/dl. He also has an elevated ferritin level of 800 mcg/L. The hyperinflammation team has recommended anti-interleukin treatment with Tocilizumab (TCZ) in addition to standard of care. He has no known hypersensitivity to TCZ or its components and is not on any immunosuppressive therapy. He has no active bacterial or fungal infections or other clinical conditions that contraindicate TCZ treatment. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has no known prior liver disease. He has been informed of the study and has given his consent to participate in it.

A 45-year-old Hispanic woman with a history of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) presented with complaints of dizziness and lightheadedness upon standing after hemodialysis sessions. She reported a decrease in blood pressure of 25 mmHg systolic and 10 mmHg diastolic within 5 minutes of standing. She further reported feeling light-headed and dizzy with a VAS score of 4. She has been on regular hemodialysis sessions for the past 6 months and her current hemoglobin level is 10.4 g/dL. She has no history of hypertension, liver disorders or severe disease that would limit her survival during the study period. She is currently not taking any anti-hypotensive drugs or investigational products. She is willing and able to comply with the study procedures and has provided written informed consent. She is not pregnant, lactating or planning to be pregnant within 3 months, and is currently using a medically recognized method of contraception. Her peripheral vascular disease and coronary artery disease status is unknown. She has no history of hemorrhage complication within 3 months before the screening visit and is not likely to require blood transfusions during the trial period. The investigator believes that she is suitable for participation in the trial.

The patient is a 10-year-old male attending 4th grade in good health. He has a BMI of 23.5, which falls in the overweight category. He is right-handed and has no known food allergies. He typically eats breakfast at least 4 mornings per week. He is not taking any medications for chronic illness or disorder that may affect the outcome of the study. He has no history of left-hand dominance. The patient will be required to fast overnight for at least 10 hours prior to the start of the study. The patient will be asked to consume a breakfast meal or skip breakfast, as determined by random allocation to one of the study groups. The patient will also be given a morning snack and observed for cognitive function, memory, and learning abilities.

The patient is a 35-year-old female diagnosed with bipolar disorder type II. She has been on medication for 2 years and has been taking lithium at a stable dose for 4 weeks with a serum level of 0.5 mEq/l. She has experienced mixed episodes in the past that have been difficult to manage. Her current symptoms include a persistent depressed mood, difficulty sleeping, racing thoughts, and irritability. She has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 weeks. Her Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) score is 16 and her Montgomery Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score is 18. She is currently not pregnant and is using a clinically accepted method of contraception. She has no other medical conditions that contraindicate psychoactive medications. She has never been exposed to quetiapine (QTP) before. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol.

Patient is a 35-year-old female with a diagnosis of left-sided infective endocarditis, which was confirmed based on Duke criteria. The patient's blood culture showed multi-susceptible Streptococcus/Enterococcus sp. bacteria that are susceptible to amoxicillin with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of ≤0.5 mg/L. The patient has received appropriate parenteral antibiotics treatment for 10 days, and during the last 48 hours, she has been apyrexial (temperature < 38°C). At the time of randomization, the patient's blood cultures have been sterile for at least 5 days. The patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 22 kg/m² and a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 60 ml/min/1.73m². The patient is willing and able to take oral antibiotics and comply with the follow-up required for the trial. The patient has adequate social support to discharge from the hospital and continue treatment at home. The patient is not planning to undergo valvular surgery within the next 6 months. The patient is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or on childbearing age without effective contraception. The patient does not have a history of IE in the last 3 months, and there is no other infection requiring parenteral antibiotic therapy. The patient is not taking estrogen-progesterone treatment interacting with rifampicin, and there is no known allergy to amoxicillin.

A 9-month-old Hispanic boy was admitted to the ICU after experiencing respiratory distress. He was intubated and placed on a ventilator due to his severe condition. The medical staff has been closely monitoring his breathing, but they are interested in evaluating the effectiveness of a noninvasive respiratory monitor called the Respiratory Volume Monitor (ExSpiron). The study aims to determine if the monitor accurately measures the amount of air going in and out of the lungs, the number of breaths taken per minute, and the amount of air going in and out of the lungs per minute in infants less than 12 months of age. The boy meets the inclusion criteria for the study and his parents have provided informed consent for him to participate. The stickers for the monitor will be placed on his chest to collect data on his breathing patterns. This information may help the medical staff detect breathing problems early on and improve his care.

A 16-year-old male is currently incarcerated at a youth correctional facility. He has been experiencing symptoms of urethral discharge and dysuria. He has no known allergies to medication and is otherwise healthy. He tested positive for chlamydia during a routine screening at the facility. He has not received any antimicrobial therapy for C. trachomatis within the last 21 days prior to the screening. He is willing to comply with study procedures and provide written consent.

A 14-year-old male student with a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is the ideal candidate for this clinical trial. He was diagnosed with ASD when he was 6 years old, and he receives treatment from a developmental pediatrician and a speech therapist. He is currently in the 8th grade and attends a mainstream school with the support of an educational assistant. He has difficulty with social interaction, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. He has average intelligence, but he struggles with language comprehension and expression. He enjoys playing video games and watching cartoons. He has no history of head injury, schizophrenia, or ADHD. His parents are supportive of his participation in the study and have signed the informed consent form.

The patient is a 40-year-old woman diagnosed with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (heFH) with a past medical history of hypertension and mild obesity. She has been on a stable dose of atorvastatin for the past 6 months without experiencing significant side effects. Her most recent LDL-C level was 120 mg/dL. The patient is willing to follow the NCEP ATPIII TLC diet, or an equivalent diet plan, starting at screening and continuing until the last study visit. She is a non-smoker and consumes alcohol occasionally. Her BP: 140/85, HR: 75/min and BMI: 30. Her abdomen is soft with no tenderness. The patient has a negative urine/serum pregnancy test at the start of the study.

A 24-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of difficulty in social interactions and communication and restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior. She was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) at the age of 8. She has difficulty making eye contact and initiating conversations with others. She also has a tendency to engage in repetitive behaviors, such as rocking or hand flapping, as well as a narrow range of interests. She has a full scale IQ score of 85 on the WASI-II. She is currently not taking any medication for her ASD symptoms. She has a study partner who is willing to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and has agreed to use an effective contraceptive method during the study period. She has not had any significant changes in her psychosocial interventions or behavioral therapy regimens for the past 6 weeks. She has no history of clinically significant affective or psychotic disorders or neurologic disorders that may interfere with the assessment of safety or efficacy endpoints. All her laboratory test results are within the normal range. She is interested in participating in the study to explore new treatment options for her ASD symptoms.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who has been experiencing recurring episodes of rectal bleeding for the past few months. He has also noticed a change in his bowel movements, with more frequent episodes of diarrhea and occasional constipation. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. A fecal occult blood test was positive, and he has been referred for a colonoscopy to determine the cause of his symptoms. He is generally healthy but is concerned about the potential discomfort of the procedure and would like to participate in a study to determine the most comfortable and efficient position for colonoscopy.

Patient is a 65yo man with a history of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who has progressed on docetaxel therapy. The patient's androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) has been continued with LHRH agonist therapy. Serum testosterone levels were <50 ng/mL within 21 days before prescreening. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. The patient has not previously been treated with cabazitaxel or had any known hypersensitivity reactions to the drug. The patient has not received chemotherapy or immunotherapy (other than LHRH analogues) within the last 4 weeks before study inclusion. The patient has not received treatment with both abiraterone and enzalutamide in the post-docetaxel setting. The patient has not received radiotherapy to 40% or more of the bone marrow. The patient does not have any concurrent or planned treatment with strong inhibitors or strong inducers of cytochrome P450 3A4/5. The patient does not have concomitant vaccination with yellow fever vaccine. The patient has normal liver and hematological functions. The patient will be asked to undergo prescreening consisting of a CTC count and, in case ≥3 CTCs are detected, AR V7 determination. If the patient has ≥3 CTCs with AR-V7 expression, they will be asked to sign a second informed consent to enter the treatment study. In this study, they will receive Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² every 3 weeks plus prednisone 10 mg daily, and undergo repeated blood sampling for biomarker sample collection.
