A 29-year-old woman, who is pregnant for the first time, comes to the hospital with complaints of abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. She is currently at 28 weeks of gestation. Upon examination, the obstetrician determines that she is experiencing premature labor and admits her to the Labor and Delivery unit. The obstetrician requests a neonatology consult for counseling about prematurity. The patient is nervous and anxious about the situation, and she is interested in learning as much as possible about the potential outcomes of her premature delivery. She speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study. Her support person is her husband, who also speaks fluent English and is willing to participate in the study. The patient has no known genetic abnormality or congenital anomaly that would affect survival or counseling that parents receive. She is excited to participate in the study to learn more about prematurity and how to best care for her newborn.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman with chronic lower back pain that has been resistant to non-surgical treatments. She has tried physical therapy, medications, and injections, but none of these have provided long-term relief. She has been referred to the Palliative Pain Management Clinic at the Sourasky Medical Center in Tel Aviv and has undergone a multidisciplinary evaluation. She has been deemed a candidate for neurosurgical treatment to address the damaged nerve transmission and processing system in her lower back. During the preoperative evaluation, she was given an explanation about the possibility of participating in the study and has agreed to participate by signing an informed consent form. She is capable of performing various tasks before and after surgery, including answering pain questionnaires and undergoing neuropsychological evaluations. She is not pregnant.

The patient is a 25-year-old Black woman who has a history of drug use and criminal justice involvement. She reports engaging in unprotected vaginal sex with multiple male partners in the past 90 days and has used illicit drugs in the past 6 months. She lives in a low-income neighborhood in New York City and works as a part-time cashier. She has never been pregnant and is not currently trying to conceive. She speaks English fluently and is interested in participating in a program that can help her prevent HIV and other sexually transmitted infections. She is willing to provide vaginal swabs for STI testing and attend multiple sessions for the WORTH program. She reports experiencing symptoms of depression and anxiety but has not received any formal diagnosis or treatment.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of cystinuria and recurrent kidney stones. He has been experiencing intermittent pain in his right flank for the past few months and has been referred to a urologist for further evaluation. On examination, the patient appears uncomfortable and reports a current pain score of 7 out of 10. Imaging studies reveal a 5mm stone in his right ureter. The patient has a history of multiple kidney stone episodes in the past and is currently taking potassium citrate to manage his urinary pH levels. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the use of a Lit-control®pH meter for daily self-monitorization of his urinary pH levels compared to the standard of care reactive strips. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocols and understands the potential benefits and risks of participating in the trial.

A 7-year-old boy with a history of recurrent tonsillitis was referred to the clinic for tonsillectomy. He has had at least five episodes of tonsillitis in the past year, with each episode lasting for 7-10 days. He has been taking antibiotics to manage the condition, but his parents are concerned about the long-term effects of antibiotic use. The boy is otherwise healthy, with no history of significant medical problems. He is an active child who enjoys playing soccer and basketball with his friends. His parents report that he is generally healthy and has not had any surgeries in the past. They are interested in participating in the clinical trial to help their son manage postoperative pain and decrease the need for opioid medication.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who suffered a left hemisphere stroke 2 years ago, resulting in right-sided hemiparesis. She has completed the acute and subacute rehabilitation in the hospital and has been undergoing outpatient therapy for 1 year. She has limited range of motion and spasticity in her right upper limb, with a Modified Ashworth Scale score of 2. She has no history of seizure, brain surgery or trauma, and drug or alcohol abuse. She has a pacemaker implanted for bradycardia. She has no pressure sores or wounds on her head or upper extremities, and no metal implants in her head or neck. She has no history of rheumatism disorders, cognitive or psychiatric disorders, and malignant neoplasm. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore a new approach for her upper extremity rehabilitation.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who works as a computer programmer. She wears contact lenses regularly for at least 3 days a week, 8 hours a day. She has no history of ocular diseases and has had an oculo-visual examination in the last two years. Her vision is correctable to 20/20 in each eye with her habitual vision correction. She has clear corneas, no active ocular disease, and no evidence of lid abnormality or infection. She has no significant slit lamp findings or any other active ocular disease. She is not currently taking any medication that may affect her ocular health. She has not undergone any corneal refractive surgery or wears monovision. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing and able to follow instructions and maintain the appointment schedule.

A 47-year-old man who has been on dialysis for 2 years due to end-stage renal disease is being evaluated for a deceased donor kidney transplant. He has no history of significant medical comorbidities and is not on any medications. He has no known allergies. The patient has been on the waiting list for 6 months and has been informed about the possibility of participating in a clinical trial comparing hypothermic machine perfusion (HMP) to static cold storage (SCS) for kidney transplantation. He is interested in participating in the trial and meets the inclusion criteria for a single kidney transplantation from a deceased donor at the Medical University of Innsbruck between 08/2015 and 12/2019.

A 52 year old woman with a history of smoking and shortness of breath comes to the clinic for evaluation of her lung nodules. A biopsy confirms non-small cell lung cancer with metastatic disease. The patient has a plan for systemic therapy and is currently receiving carboplatin/paclitaxel/pembrolizumab. She reports cough and moderate dyspnea that is affecting her daily activities. Imaging shows a centrally located tumor that is threatening the airway. The patient has a KPS score of 70 and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. She is informed of the Quad Shot radiation therapy schedule which can be delivered in fewer days and is found to be less disruptive to her systemic therapy. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and agrees to practice effective contraception.

Patient is a 60-year-old male diagnosed with B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (B-CLL) confirmed by expression of CD19, CD5, and CD23 by flow cytometry. The patient is in Rai Stage III with an absolute lymphocyte count of 10,000/microliter and a lymphocyte WBC differential of 80%. The patient also has a platelet count of 150,000/microliter. The patient has adequate organ function with bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), aspartate transaminase (AST), and alanine transaminase (ALT) levels within normal limits. The patient is not taking carbamazepine, phenobarbital, or phenytoin. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and does not have central nervous system (CNS) metastases. The patient does not have any serious concomitant systemic disorder that would compromise their ability to adhere to the protocol.

35yo male with a history of chronic sinusitis, scheduled for endoscopic sinus surgery. Patient has no significant medical history, is not on any medications, and has no known allergies. The attending anesthesiologist has determined that the patient does not have a difficult airway and is suitable for nasal intubation. The operator has performed over 50 prior GlideScope intubations (both oral and nasal).

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with endometriosis-associated pain (EAP) and has undergone surgical confirmation of the diagnosis. She reports moderate to severe pain in the pelvic area during menstruation and throughout the month. She has been taking analgesics but has not experienced adequate relief. She has completed the 6-month treatment period in the Edelweiss 3 study and is willing to continue the treatment. She has no known allergies to any medications and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She is not planning to get pregnant during the duration of the study. She is willing to comply with the requirements of the study protocol for the duration of the extension study. She has not been diagnosed with any other gynecologic conditions that might interfere with the study efficacy and safety objectives. She is willing to continue to use only the analgesic rescue medication permitted by the protocol during the Treatment and Follow-up Periods. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

A 45-year-old female was brought to the emergency department with severe headache and vomiting. CT scan revealed subarachnoid hemorrhage, and further investigations confirmed the presence of a cerebral aneurysm. The patient underwent successful endovascular coiling of the aneurysm and had an external ventricular drain placed for management of hydrocephalus. The patient has a Hunt Hess grade of 3 and a Fisher grade of 4. The patient is currently being managed in the intensive care unit and is stable. Consent has been obtained from the patient's legally authorized representative, and the patient meets all other inclusion criteria for the study. The patient does not have any exclusion criteria, and the treating physician believes that the patient may benefit from intrathecal nicardipine treatment for cerebral vasospasm.

The patient is a 55-year-old Indian man who has been recently diagnosed with advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer after prior chemotherapy. He complains of persistent cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit smoking 5 years ago. He is currently not using any drugs, smoking or drinking alcohol. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He has no history of autoimmune disease or any other malignancy. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He has undergone radiotherapy and it was completed 3 weeks ago. He is married and has 2 children. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore other treatment options.

A 58-year-old male presents with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) for the past year. He has tried multiple antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) but has not responded well to any of them. He is currently experiencing recurrent symptomatic PAF episodes, which have been documented via ECG and Telemetry Strip. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and is not on any medication other than AADs for his PAF. He is interested in alternative treatment options and is willing to comply with all pre-, post-, and follow-up testing and requirements. His left atrial size is less than 50mm, and he does not have any other pre-existing conditions that would preclude him from enrollment in the study. The patient is provided with the patient informed consent form and is willing to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old man came to the clinic with a family history of colon cancer. He has not had any symptoms but decided to undergo a colonoscopy for screening purposes. He has never had a colonoscopy before and is nervous about the bowel preparation process. He has a history of irritable bowel syndrome but does not take any medication for it. He is otherwise healthy and takes no other medication. He has no history of allergies or adverse reactions to medication. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally.

Patient is a 42-year-old man from the United States who has been suffering from chronic constipation for the past two years. He has tried different laxatives, but they have not provided any relief. He defecates less than 2 times per week and has no awareness of defecation. He has been diagnosed with slow-transit constipation and has been excluded from having any colorectal organic disease. He is mentally stable and has no surgical contraindications. He is willing to undergo surgery and is looking for a treatment that can provide long-term relief from his symptoms.

A 65-year-old male presents with metastatic prostate cancer that has progressed despite hormonal therapy. The patient has a history of prostate cancer and has been undergoing androgen deprivation therapy for the past year. The patient's PSA levels have been rising steadily, and recent scans have shown the presence of new bone lesions. The patient has a Zubrod performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. Blood tests have shown that the patient has ANC ≥ 1,500/mm³, Hemoglobin ≥ 10 mg/dL, and Platelet count ≥ 100,000/mm³. The patient has not received any immunotherapy in the past 6 weeks and has not received chemotherapy in the past 28 days. The patient is willing to be followed at Baylor College of Medicine and does not have any serious intercurrent medical illness. The patient has not undergone any primary or secondary immunodeficiency and does not have a known history of cardiac arrhythmia or ischemic heart disease.

This is a 32-year-old healthy female who owns an iPhone 7. She is interested in increasing her physical activity levels but often finds it challenging to stay motivated. She currently does not use any activity trackers or smartphone apps to monitor her physical activity. She works during the day and does not work night shifts. She does not have any medical conditions that would prohibit her from increasing her physical activity levels. She is enrolled in a complementary health insurance plan and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to test a smartphone app that includes a chatbot-based coaching and incentives to increase physical activity.

This is a 62-year-old female who has been diagnosed with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis for the past 8 years. Despite being on methotrexate for the past 6 months, she has been experiencing moderate-to-severe joint pain and stiffness with limited mobility. She has tried one anti-TNF biologic agent in the past, but it was ineffective and caused adverse effects. She has a history of osteoporosis and hypertension, which are well-controlled with medications. She regularly sees her rheumatologist and primary care physician for management of her conditions. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially find a more effective treatment option for her rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman with a history of metastatic breast cancer. She has received multiple lines of chemotherapy and has progressed on her most recent treatment regimen. She has also undergone radiation therapy to her chest and axilla. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of greater than 12 weeks. Genetic testing has revealed that her tumor harbors alterations in FGF or FGFR genes. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has not received any other investigational study drug for any indication within the past 21 days. She has adequate liver, renal, hematopoietic, and cardiac function parameters within the protocol-defined range. She has not received radiotherapy within the past 2 weeks.

Samantha is a 46 year old woman who was recently diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. She lives with her husband and two teenage children in San Francisco and works part-time as a graphic designer. Samantha is currently undergoing chemotherapy and has experienced some side effects, including fatigue and nausea. She is interested in participating in a study that could help her improve her quality of life during and after treatment. Samantha is able to walk unassisted and has regular access to the internet. She is comfortable using technology and believes that she would be able to navigate the Fitbit® website and input data without difficulty.

10 year old boy diagnosed with type 1 diabetes 2 years ago, who is currently on multiple daily injections and has an HbA1c of 8.5%. He lives within 10km of the CHU Sainte-Justine and is interested in transitioning to insulin pump therapy to improve his glycemic control. His parents are supportive and willing to provide consent for their child's participation in the study. The patient has not experienced any severe hypoglycemic episodes in the past 6 months. Past Medical History: Type 1 diabetes diagnosed 2 years ago, managed with multiple daily injections. No other significant medical history.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy female who works as an accountant. She does not smoke or use any drugs or alcohol. She has a BMI of 22 kg/m2 and her weight is 58 kg. She has no clinically significant medical history, physical examination, laboratory profiles, vital signs that would interfere with the study. She has no history of alcoholism or drug abuse. She is not pregnant, lactating, or of childbearing potential. She has no history of anemia or decreased RBC. Her creatinine clearance is estimated to be >80 mL/min at screening. She has no history of hypersensitivity or idiosyncratic reaction to the study drugs or related compounds. She has no history of clinically significant medical or psychiatric condition or disease. She has not used nicotine-containing products for at least 3 months prior to the first dose and throughout the study. She is willing and able to comply with the protocol requirements as outlined in the ICF. She has the ability to understand and sign a written informed consent form (ICF), which must be obtained prior to initiation of study procedures.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic periodontitis. She presents with bleeding on probing and probing depths of 5 mm or more on the buccal surface of two contralateral and homologous teeth in the incisor to premolar region. She has not undergone any periodontal treatment in the past 6 months and is not currently taking any medication that could influence the response to periodontal treatment. She has not received treatment for dentin hypersensitivity in the past 3 months and does not have any periapical or pulpal changes. She is not currently undergoing orthodontic treatment or smoking. She is not pregnant.

The patient is a full-term newborn baby boy with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. He has been healthy since birth and has had no complications or congenital defects. The mother is a 28-year-old woman with no history of allergies or asthma. She plans to breastfeed exclusively but is open to supplementing with formula if necessary. The family has no history of milk allergy. They have agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the influence of early and continuous exposure of infants to cow's milk formula on the prevention of milk allergy.

45 year old female with a recent diagnosis of diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) as defined by 2001 LeRoy and Medsger. Disease duration is less than 3 years with no prior history of TNF-α inhibitors, IL-6 inhibitors, abatacept, JAK inhibitors, or rituximab use. Patient is a non-smoker and is willing to use effective contraception during the study period. Patient has no history of SSc with tumor, lung infections, asthma, or other lung diseases such as bronchiectasis. Patient has no severe heart, liver, kidney or other important organ dysfunction, and meets all evaluation criteria. Patient has no current acute or chronic infections, history of peptic ulcer or bleeding within 6 months before screening, allergies or multiple drug allergies, mental illness or other reasons that may interfere with treatment. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent and is a suitable candidate for this clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability and efficacy of iguratimod in adult subjects with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis.

A 55-year-old Caucasian woman who is postmenopausal with a BMI of 25 kg/m2. She has a low vitamin K-status and is apparently healthy without any history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, metabolic or gastrointestinal disease, chronic degenerative and/or inflammatory disease, or diabetes mellitus. She does not abuse drugs and/or alcohol and is not receiving corticosteroid treatment. She is not using oral anticoagulants or blood pressure-lowering medication, cholesterol-lowering medication, multivitamins, or vitamin K supplements. She does not consume high amounts of vitamin K-containing food products and does not have cow's milk allergy or lactose intolerance. She has given written consent to take part in the study.

A 45-year-old male patient who has been experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and nausea. After consultation with a gastroenterologist, he was diagnosed with gallstones and recommended for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The patient is generally healthy, with no significant medical history or allergies. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical trial and has provided written informed consent.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been experiencing dryness and discomfort in her eyes for the past several months. She reports feeling a burning and gritty sensation in her eyes and often finds herself rubbing them to alleviate the discomfort. She wears glasses and has no history of using contact lenses. She has been using over-the-counter ocular lubricants intermittently but with minimal relief. She has no known allergies to any medication or ingredient. She has no history of significant medical or ocular conditions, and her current medications include only over-the-counter multivitamins. She is willing to discontinue the use of any ocular lubricants for a period of 10-14 days before starting the study. She is highly motivated to participate in the study and is committed to attending all study visits.

The patient is a 44-year-old male diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 6 years ago. He has been on monotherapy with LPV/r (400/100 mg BID) for the past 7 months, with sustained viral load suppression. His most recent cholesterol test showed a total cholesterol level of 210 mg/dL and an LDL-cholesterol level of 140 mg/dL. He has not been taking any lipid-lowering medications. The patient has a calculated creatinine clearance of 82 mL/min, according to the Cockcroft-Gault formula. He has no history of TDF or FTC resistance and has adequate treatment adherence. He has no acute or chronic renal documented pathologies. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

A 38-year-old male diagnosed with Crohn's Disease involving the sigmoid colon and rectum is in clinical remission for the last 6 months. He is currently on stable therapy with mesalazine and biologics without any therapeutic modifications in the last 3 months. The patient reported a history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss before the diagnosis. He does not have any significant past medical history or family history of inflammatory bowel disease. He is a non-smoker, non-drinker, and does not use illicit drugs. The patient has not been on steroid therapy for the last 6 months. His fecal calprotectin levels at baseline are 160 microg/g. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed informed consent.

We are seeking full-term infants born to mothers with diabetes who were admitted to a large medical center for delivery. We will be reviewing medical records of 250-300 infants in order to retrospectively follow up glucose levels and determine risk factors for developing hypoglycemia. Eligible infants must be singletons without congenital malformations and not born prematurely. The study will collect data on gestational age, birth weight, delivery mode, type of maternal diabetes, other maternal diseases, and feeding mode. Glucose levels will be recorded according to the newborn protocol (1,2,4,6 hours after delivery, and then every 8 hours for a total of 48 hours) and any hypoglycemia treatment given will also be noted. The aim of the study is to determine safe time and glucose levels to stop monitoring IDM glucose levels.

A 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and coronary artery disease presented with chest pain and shortness of breath. Upon evaluation, he was found to have a 90% blockage in his left anterior descending artery and was scheduled for urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). He has no history of bleeding disorders or anticoagulant therapy. His preoperative laboratory values were within normal limits, and his platelet count was 240,000/mm³. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally.

A 35-year-old woman presents to the gastroenterologist with symptoms of abdominal pain, bloating, and irregular bowel movements. She was diagnosed with celiac disease 2 years ago and has been on a strict gluten-free diet ever since. However, her symptoms have not improved and she was recently diagnosed with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) based on Rome III criteria. She has no significant past medical history and has not undergone any abdominal surgeries. She is not currently taking any medications, including probiotics. Her vital signs are within normal limits and physical examination reveals no abnormalities. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine if a probiotic mixture could improve her symptoms.

A 62-year-old male patient who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease for 4 years presents with difficulty in performing activities of daily living due to upper limb dysfunction. He is classified as stage II on the Hoehn & Yahr motor staging scale. He is a retired engineer and has completed higher education. He is currently taking levodopa, carbidopa, and entacapone for the management of his symptoms. He resides in the city of Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, and is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to improve upper limb functionality in individuals with Parkinson's Disease. He has no recent injuries or limitations that would prevent him from participating in the trial. He is willing to sign the informed consent form and is open to receiving treatment with the Leap Motion Controller device or conventional physiotherapy.

22-year-old collegiate rower with a history of competitive rowing for the past 4 years. The patient is currently part of the varsity rowing team and is training for upcoming competitions. The patient has no history of cardiovascular diseases, pulmonary diseases, metabolic diseases, or other contraindications to exercise. The patient has been maintaining a healthy lifestyle with regular exercise and a balanced diet. The patient is willing to participate in the study and will attend two sessions of fitness testing, one in the fall 2020 and one in the spring 2021. The testing will include the modified Wingate test to examine anaerobic capacity, the graded exercise test to examine the aerobic capacity, and the 2,000-meter rowing test on rowing ergometers to assess rowing performance. The patient is interested in understanding the association between the changes in physiological variables based on fitness testing and the changes in rowing performance.

10-year-old male patient from China with moderate to severe hemophilia A who has never received treatment before. The patient has a family history of hemophilia A as his younger brother was diagnosed with the same condition. The patient has experienced frequent bleeding episodes, including spontaneous bleeding in the joints and muscles which has led to pain and discomfort. The patient's treating physician has prescribed ADVATE as the predominant therapeutic agent for the management of hemophilia A. The patient and/or legal representative have provided informed consent to participate in this post-marketing safety study. The patient does not have any other inherited or acquired hemostatic defect and does not have any clinically significant chronic disease. The patient has not participated in any other investigational FVIII drug study during the course of the observation period.

A 42-year-old male who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, decreased sexual drive, and poor appetite. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy and has not used any appetite stimulants or other anabolic agents in the past three months. He is willing to provide written informed consent and has not participated in any other clinical trials with investigational agents within the past month. He has not used any medications that interfere with gonadal axis such as androgens, estrogens or anti-androgens.

72-year-old female with a history of dysphagia and recurrent pneumonia, who is being managed by the UW Health Inpatient Swallowing Consult Service. The patient has been diagnosed with dysphagia based on videofluoroscopic swallow study with observed airway invasion and has a Penetration-Aspiration Scale score of 4. The patient is able to provide consent, submit oral samples, and swallow a sachet of probiotic (dissolved in thickened liquid, as needed). The patient has not recently taken antibiotics or probiotics and is not currently receiving immunosuppressive therapy. The patient is able to return to UWHC for week 2 and week 4 visits. The patient does not have a diagnosis of head and neck cancer or upper airway disease and has not had prior surgery to the head and neck region that would have affected the muscles of swallowing or the salivary glands. The patient has not received chemotherapy or radiation to the head and neck region and does not have severe periodontal disease. The patient is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant.

65-year-old Caucasian male with a history of cirrhosis of the liver, presented with increasing abdominal distension and pain, fatigue, and loss of appetite. The patient was previously treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and radiation therapy for his liver cancer, with no response to treatment. Physical examination revealed jaundice, ascites, and hepatomegaly. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and alcohol abuse. He is a retired construction worker and a former smoker, having quit smoking 10 years ago. The patient's laboratory studies showed elevated liver function tests, including AST and ALT, total bilirubin, and alkaline phosphatase. His serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) was elevated to 400 ng/mL. Imaging studies revealed multiple liver lesions with the largest measuring 7 cm in diameter, consistent with metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80%. He has no history of neuropathy or chronic pulmonary disease. He has normal renal function with a creatinine clearance of 80 mL/min. His platelet count is 80,000/µL, and his leukocyte count is 3,800/µL. The patient had no prior exposure to oxaliplatin or capecitabine. He has no history of allergies to platinum compounds or antiemetics. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given informed consent.

A 45 yo F with a history of chronic cough and shortness of breath for the past 6 months. She has a history of smoking and was diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) last year. She has been on inhalers and bronchodilators for the same. She now presents with worsening cough and wheeze for the past week. Her chest X-ray showed features of bronchitis and she was planned for a diagnostic flexible bronchoscopy to rule out other causes. She does not have any known allergies and has not required sedation for any procedures in the past. She is willing to participate in the trial and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. She has a history of auditory hallucinations and delusions that have been affecting her daily life. She is currently taking antipsychotic medication and is stable. She has a family history of schizophrenia. She is right-handed and has a normal IQ. She is interested in participating in research studies related to schizophrenia and hopes to contribute to the development of new treatments. She has no history of neurological illnesses or surgeries that may impact the study of brain physiology. She has not participated in any brain imaging studies before.

The patient is a 32-year-old HIV positive man who has been detained in Fulton County Jail for the past two months. He was diagnosed with HIV three years ago and has been receiving medical care for his condition. However, he is concerned about maintaining his medical care and treatment after he is released from jail. He has expressed interest in participating in the Planning for SUCCESS study to improve his connection to community care after his release. The patient is mentally capable of giving consent and speaks fluent English.

This is a 62 year-old female with a family history of Alzheimer's disease. She has no history of cardiovascular disease, cancer, or thyroid issues. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol regularly. She is not a regular exerciser and has not taken n-3 PUFA capsules in the last 3 months. She is postmenopausal and is interested in participating in a study to explore how dietary fish oil can be delivered to the brain. She is willing to take DHA supplements for the study duration and attend two study visits six months apart. She understands that blood and cerebrospinal fluid levels of DHA will be measured and brain imaging by MRI will be obtained at baseline and conclusion of the study. She is excited to potentially contribute to the development of interventions for Alzheimer's disease.

The patient is a 55 year-old male who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma 2 years ago and has undergone treatment with lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor. He has experienced relapse and is now seeking further treatment options. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has measurable disease with serum M protein levels of 800 mg/dL. His organ function is adequate with ANC of 1500/mm^3, platelets of 90,000/mm^3, hemoglobin of 100 g/L, creatinine clearance of 50 mL/min, total serum bilirubin of 1.2*ULN, and liver transaminases within normal range. He has not undergone autologous stem cell transplant within the last 60 days and has no active graft-versus-host disease. He has recovered from prior myeloma treatment with sensory neuropathy at Grade 2. He is currently taking prednisone at a dose of 5mg/day for his neuropathy.

Mary is a 35-year-old female who was admitted to the burn unit due to a kitchen accident that caused second-degree burns on her arms, chest, and neck. She is currently in the high care unit and has been intubated due to the severity of her burns. Mary has a history of asthma and is currently taking albuterol as needed. She has no other significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her vital signs are stable, and she is receiving intravenous fluids and pain management. The healthcare team will be monitoring Mary's SOFA score to assess her risk of mortality during her stay in the burn unit.

Patient A is a 56-year-old female who has been diagnosed with uterine fibroids and has been scheduled for an elective laparotomy. She is generally healthy, with no known medical conditions other than the uterine fibroids. She has never undergone any previous abdominal surgeries and has no history of allergies to any medications. The patient is able to provide informed consent for the surgery and is classified as ASA Class II. She has been briefed on the use of PCA morphine for post-operative pain management and is able to use it. The patient will be randomized into either the short stitch (SS) or the long stitch (LS) group for closure of the abdominal wall. After the surgery, the patient will be closely monitored for any signs of surgical site infection and will be assessed for post-operative pain using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the amount of PCA morphine used. The patient will be discharged from the hospital based on the discharge criteria set by the surgeon in charge and will be followed up in the outpatient clinic at regular intervals.

A 53 year old woman was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia and is currently receiving chemotherapy. She is scheduled to undergo allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in a few weeks. The patient reports feeling weak and tired and experiences shortness of breath with minimal physical activity. She has a past medical history of hypertension and is on medications for it. Her BMI is within normal range. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the relationship between physical activity and pulmonary and physical functions in allogeneic-HSCT candidates.

The patient is a 50-year-old female diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. She has been treated with oral antidiabetic agents and insulin for the past 2 years. Her BMI is 40 kg/m2 and she has a history of unsuccessful weight loss attempts through diet and exercise. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has not been on any pharmacological treatment that could affect glucose metabolism. The patient is scheduled for laparoscopic surgery for weight loss. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the procedure.

The patient is a 25 year old healthy individual who has no history of brain injury, stroke or epilepsy. She is not pregnant and is willing to participate in the study. She has no known swallowing difficulties or disorders. She is interested in contributing to the research on the effect of rTMS on swallowing coordination and is available for the duration of the study.

A 56-year-old man with a history of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer with metastasis to the liver and bones is seeking treatment. He has previously received chemotherapy but his disease has progressed. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. His blood work shows a WBC count of 5500/mm3, an absolute neutrophil count of 2500/mm3, and a platelet count of 120,000/mm3. His bilirubin level is 1.2 mg/dL, and his transaminases are within normal limits. His creatinine level is 1.1 mg/dL, and his creatinine clearance is 80 mL/min. He has no history of myocardial infarction or congestive heart failure. He has mild neuropathy but it does not interfere with his daily activities. He has not experienced vomiting or severe anorexia. He has not lost more than 5% of his body weight in the past 6 months. He is not pregnant, nursing, or planning to be pregnant. He is willing to use effective birth control during the study and for at least 6 months afterwards. He has no other concurrent medical illness that would preclude study participation.

A 27-year-old male patient was admitted to the orthopedic surgery department with a diagnosis of osteomyelitis in his right foot. He has a medical history of uncontrolled type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Gram-positive cocci were identified in his culture, and the bacteria were found to be resistant to lincosamides, quinolones, and rifampicin. However, the bacteria were susceptible to teicoplanin with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 4 mg/L. The patient is currently receiving balanced teicoplanin intravenously. He has no known allergies to teicoplanin and has no central catheter or implantable chamber. The patient is not on hemodialysis and is not participating in any other biomedical research. The patient has consented to participate and is affiliated with social security.

The patient is a 40-year-old married woman who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past 6 months. She has tried multiple pain management strategies including physical therapy and medications, with little improvement. The pain is described as constant and rated 6 out of 10 in intensity, with an interference rating of 7 out of 10, affecting her ability to perform household tasks and participate in social activities. The patient's spouse is also participating in the study and has been in a romantic relationship with the patient for the past 5 years. The spouse is supportive of the patient's pain management efforts, but often struggles with how to respond to the patient's expressions of pain and distress. Both the patient and spouse are fluent in English and meet the eligibility criteria for the study. They are excited to participate in the study to better understand how to communicate and respond to each other's pain experiences in their relationship.

The patient is a 46-year-old man diagnosed with chronic liver disease 3 years ago. Recently, he started experiencing a rapid reduction in renal function with a doubling of serum creatinine to 3.2 mg/dL in less than a week. Despite diuretic withdrawal and plasma volume expansion, there has been no sustained improvement in renal function. The patient has proteinuria less than 500 mg per day, and there is no evidence of granular casts in urinalysis or ultrasonographic evidence of obstructive uropathy or parenchymal renal disease. The patient has no ongoing shock or uncontrolled bacterial infection, and there are no current significant fluid losses. The patient has not received any nephrotoxic drugs within the last 4 weeks. The patient is not pregnant, and he has no evidence of intrinsic or parenchymal renal disease. The patient has not participated in any other clinical studies within the last 30 days. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of terlipressin for the treatment of hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) type 1.

The patient is a 46-year-old man who had a left leg amputation below the knee due to a work-related accident. He experiences ongoing localized pain in the residual limb, which has been diagnosed as a neuroma. The pain significantly interferes with his ability to use his prosthetic leg, and he has difficulty performing daily activities such as walking and standing for prolonged periods. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not currently taking any medication for pain management. He has a history of hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He speaks English fluently. He has not participated in any other ongoing studies related to neuropathic pain. He has undergone an MRI to confirm the presence and location of the neuroma.

A 30 yo female with a history of moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa for over a year presents for evaluation of treatment options. She has tried various topical and oral antibiotics with little improvement. She has not received any targeted biologic therapy for HS in the past. She has multiple areas of involvement, including Hurley stage II and III, with at least 3 abscesses and inflammatory nodules. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of bermekimab and is willing to comply with the study protocol. She is not pregnant and is willing to use a highly effective method of contraception during the study period. She has not received any live vaccines in the past 28 days and has not undergone major surgery requiring general anesthesia in the past 28 days. She has normal liver function and is not immunocompromised.

An 80-year-old male patient with a history of Alzheimer's disease and behavioral disorders is admitted to the reinforced hospital unit for further management. The patient has a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been living in a nursing home for the past year, and his family reports that his behavioral symptoms have been worsening over the last few months, including agitation, aggression, and irritability. The patient has a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 14/30, indicating moderate cognitive impairment. The patient is able to communicate verbally, but his speech is often disorganized and tangential. He has no history of hearing loss and is willing to participate in the study. He is prescribed the standard therapy for Alzheimer's disease, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and memantine, and is randomized to receive either music therapy or standard care.

Patient is a 30-year-old healthy male with a body weight of 80kg and BMI of 22. He has no history of liver, kidney, neurology, immunology, pulmonary, endocrine, hema-oncology, or cardiology diseases. The patient has never had any surgeries related to the gastrointestinal tract, including ulcer or pancreatitis. He has no history of drug hypersensitivity reactions to aspirin or antibiotics. The patient has not participated in any other clinical trials in the last 2 months and has not donated whole blood in the last 2 months or had any component blood donation or transfusion in the last 1 month. He is a non-smoker or has not smoked in the last 3 months. The patient's fasting plasma glucose level is between 70-125mg/dL. The patient has been informed about the clinical trial, understands the progress of the study, and has signed a consent form to participate in the study.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of Hepatitis C. He was diagnosed with intermediate stage Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) and was recommended for Transarterial Radioembolization (TARE) treatment by his oncologist. He has no prior history of cancer or other significant medical conditions. He has a history of social drinking and no significant family history of cancer. The patient is willing to sign the informed consent and undergo MRI scans for evaluation of his treatment response and prognosis.

A 37-year-old male came to the clinic complaining of bleeding gums and bad breath. He is overweight with a BMI of 32 and has a history of smoking. He brushes his teeth once a day and does not floss. His dental exam was remarkable for 30% of periodontal pockets with depths greater than 4 mm and 25% of bleeding on probing. Radiographs showed bone loss in multiple teeth. He was diagnosed with periodontal disease and obesity. He does not take any medication and is not allergic to any medications.

A 25-year-old pregnant woman is admitted to the hospital at 26 weeks and 4 days of gestational age due to preterm labor. She has a history of infertility and underwent in vitro fertilization (IVF) to conceive. She has been receiving antenatal care throughout her pregnancy and was started on antenatal steroids to promote fetal lung maturation at 24 weeks of gestation. The woman is currently stable, with no signs of infection or other complications. She is a non-smoker and denies any drug or alcohol use during pregnancy. She is currently experiencing regular contractions but the cervix is only 1 cm dilated. The fetal heart rate is within normal limits. The obstetrician discusses the option of participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of assisted ventilation during delayed cord clamping for extremely preterm infants. The woman is interested in participating and is determined eligible for the study.

A 48-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II breast cancer, with the presence of positive axillary lymph nodes. She underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy for 4 cycles with a combination of anthracycline and taxane-based regimen. She also received neoadjuvant trastuzumab as her tumor was HER-2 positive. After completing neoadjuvant chemotherapy, her axilla

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic malignant melanoma. She has undergone surgery and radiation therapy in the past, and has residual tumor in her lymph nodes. She is currently considering further treatment options and has agreed to participate in a microdosing study to evaluate a new PET imaging agent that may improve the detection of cancer. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study, including normal cardiac function, ANC>1000/mcl, and platelets>100,000/mcl. She has no history of thyroid disease or other medical illness that would preclude administration of the tracer. She is using an acceptable form of birth control and has a negative serum pregnancy test. She is willing to lie in the scanner for 30 minutes and does not have claustrophobia.

A 56-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, fever, and cough. She was intubated and put on mechanical ventilation due to respiratory failure. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She has been in the hospital for 3 days and developed a new infiltrate on chest x-ray. Her Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) II score is 20. Clinical examination reveals rales and decreased breath sounds in the left lower lobe. The patient is started on empirical antibiotics for ventilator-associated pneumonia. She has no known history of moderate or severe hypersensitivity reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics and her renal function is normal. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing intravenous ceftolozane/tazobactam with piperacillin/tazobactam for the treatment of VAP.

The patient is a 45-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma. He has been receiving Lenalidomide maintenance therapy as part of his first-line treatment and has experienced a biochemical relapse. The patient has measurable disease with serum monoclonal protein value greater than 1 g/dL of IgG M-Protein and urine light-chain excretion of more than 200 mg/24 hours. The patient has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has not had any active infectious hepatitis type B or C and no known HIV infection. The patient has not had any clinically significant illness that would increase the patient's risk for toxicity. The patient has not had a currently active malignancy, other than non-melanoma skin cancer and carcinoma in situ of the cervix. The patient has not had any prior exposure to HDACi and has not taken anti-arrhythmic drugs or other medicinal products that led to QT prolongation and cumulative high dose of anthracycline. The patient's laboratory values within 28 days before baseline day 1 of the cycle 1 are within normal limits.

The patient is a 52-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. The patient has confirmed CD20+ B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with intermediate grade disease and has already received an anthracycline containing regimen. The patient is not eligible for bone marrow or stem cell transplant. The patient does not have CNS involvement by lymphoma. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks. The patient has an absolute neutrophil count of at least 1,500/mm3, a platelet count of at least 75,000/mm3, and a hemoglobin level of at least 10 g/dL. The patient has normal creatinine levels and no history of heart disease. The patient is not pregnant or nursing, has tested negative for pregnancy, and uses effective contraception. The patient has not undergone prior rituximab treatment in the past 12 months, no prior interleukin-12, and has not received fludarabine or 2-chlorodeoxyadenosine unless CD4 count normal. The patient has recovered from prior chemotherapy and is not currently undergoing chemotherapy. There is no concurrent steroid therapy, radiotherapy, or surgery.

54 yo F scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia requiring intubation. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled on medication. She denies any history of breathing difficulties or prior intubation. She has no known allergies to medications. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provides informed consent. She does not meet any of the exclusion criteria for the study.

A 55-year-old male with a history of cirrhosis due to alcoholic liver disease presents with confusion, lethargy, and difficulty with concentration. On examination, the patient appears drowsy with asterixis present. The patient is diagnosed with hepatic encephalopathy, and treatment with lactulose is initiated. However, after few days, the symptoms did not improve. The patient is now being evaluated for participation in a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of polyethylene glycol 3350-electrolyte solution (GOLYTELY) in the treatment of hepatic encephalopathy. The patient has been informed about the study, and a representative is willing to comply with all protocol procedures and sign an informed consent document on the patient's behalf. The patient has not received more than 1 dose (30 cc) of lactulose prior to enrollment and does not have uncontrolled infection with hemodynamic instability requiring vasopressors.

This is a 32 year-old female who was recently diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). She has been experiencing joint pain, fatigue, and skin rash for several months. She has a positive anti ds-DNA antibody and low complement levels. She is currently on a stable dose of 10mg prednisone daily for the past 3 months. She has no history of severe lupus nephritis or neuropsychiatric SLE. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial exploring the safety and efficacy of MT-1303 in treating SLE.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IV colon cancer two years ago. Despite undergoing multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, his cancer has progressed and has not responded well to standard treatments. He has a history of high blood pressure, which is currently under control with medication. He is married and has two children. He works as a lawyer and enjoys reading books and watching movies in his free time. He is physically active and exercises regularly. His BMI is 25 and he has no remarkable physical exam findings. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may offer a potential treatment option for his advanced cancer. He has never participated in a clinical trial before and is willing to undergo skin biopsies as part of the study requirements. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the trial and is willing to sign a written informed consent document.

A 50-year-old Hispanic woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with sudden onset of floaters and decreased vision in her left eye. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which was diagnosed 10 years ago. She was taking metformin and amlodipine regularly. She also reports having a family history of diabetes and hypertension. On examination, her visual acuity in the left eye is found to be 20/200 with dense vitreous hemorrhage. Fundus examination reveals extensive active fibrovascular proliferations in both eyes with severe proliferative diabetic retinopathy. The right eye has a visual acuity of 20/50. The patient is eligible for the "very severe proliferative retinopathy with useful vision" group in the DRVS clinical trial. The patient is provided with all the information and is willing to participate in the study.

35-year-old healthy male without any history of significant medical conditions or allergies. He has not received any flu vaccination in the past four years and has not experienced any symptoms of upper or lower respiratory illnesses in the last six months. He is not seropositive for H5N1 or H1N1 and has no history of nose bleeding or any clinically relevant abnormal laboratory values. He is not currently taking any immunosuppressive drugs and has no history of renal, hepatic, GI, cardiovascular, haematological, skin, endocrine, neurological or immunological diseases. He is willing to provide written informed consent and adhere to the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with End-Stage Renal Disease receiving hemodialysis for the past year. She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has been advised to follow a low potassium diet due to hyperkalemia. Her diet mainly consists of vegetables and fruits, and she has been struggling to find low potassium options. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to find out if low potassium content vegetables can help control her serum potassium levels. She has no other significant medical history, and her current medication includes antihypertensive drugs prescribed by her doctor. Her lab reports show elevated serum potassium levels despite following a low potassium diet, and she is interested in finding alternative dietary options to manage her condition. She has given her consent to participate in the study and is willing to follow the dietary instructions provided by the investigators.

72-year-old male with a history of mild memory impairment and occasional forgetfulness. The patient is frequently reminded by his spouse to take his medication and remembers past events with difficulty. The patient has a Mini-Mental Status Exam score of 26, which is within the range of mild cognitive impairment. The patient is currently not taking any medication for memory impairment. The patient has no history of significant head trauma, seizures, or stroke. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient is interested in participating in research to potentially improve his memory and cognitive functioning.

A 55-year-old male patient visited the clinic with concerns about his elevated liver enzymes. He has a history of obesity and type II diabetes for the past 10 years. He is currently taking metformin and has been on a stable dose for the past 6 months. He does not drink alcohol regularly and denies any history of drug abuse. He exercises twice a week for 30 minutes and has a BMI of 33. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 10-year-old child has been diagnosed with scoliosis and requires surgery to undergo posterior spinal fusion at Nationwide Children's Hospital. The child's parents are willing and able to provide informed consent, and the child is able to provide assent. The child has no pre-existing bleeding disorders or any other circumstance that would put them at increased risk, making them eligible for the study.

A 15-year-old Caucasian male presented to the dermatology clinic with moderate to severe acne vulgaris. The patient has a history of acne for several years, which is not responding to over-the-counter treatments. The acne is primarily located on the face with some lesions also present on the chest and back. The patient is in good health with no known allergies or chronic medical conditions. He is not taking any medications or supplements. The patient has not participated in any clinical trials within the past 30 days and is not currently on any investigational drugs or devices. He has not used any topical or systemic medications for his acne within the last two weeks. The patient is interested in participating in this clinical trial and is able to provide written and verbal informed consent.

A 55-year-old man with a history of multiple myeloma is seeking treatment for his relapsed and/or refractory disease. He has previously received immunomodulatory agents, proteasome inhibitors and histone deacetylase inhibitors as part of his prior therapeutic regimen. He has measurable disease with a serum M-protein level of 1.5 g/dL and an abnormal free light chain ratio. He has no history of non-secretory or hyposecretory multiple myeloma or POEMS syndrome. He has not received any chemotherapy, steroid therapy or radiation therapy within the past 2 weeks. He has not participated in any investigational therapeutic study within the past 3 weeks. He has no history of allergy to boron or mannitol. He has no major surgery planned within the next 2 weeks. He has no significant neuropathy at the time of enrollment. He has no contraindications to the required concomitant drugs, including proton-pump inhibitor, enteric-coated aspirin or other anticoagulant. He is willing to comply with the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements and receive outpatient treatment and laboratory monitoring at the institute that administers the drug. He has no serious psychiatric or medical conditions that could interfere with treatment. He has no known or suspected HIV infection or active hepatitis A, B, or C infection. He is willing to adhere to RevAssist® program requirements.

45 yo F with a history of locally advanced soft tissue sarcoma that has recurred despite standard curative therapies. She has undergone surgery and radiation therapy in the past, but the tumor has progressed and now has metastasized. She has no history of stem cell transplantation, chemotherapy or high dose chemotherapy and stem cell transplantation. She has measurable disease outside of the irradiated area and meets the criteria for enrollment in the trial. She has a performance status of 1 and no other concurrent serious diseases. She is not pregnant, nursing or planning to become pregnant during the trial period. She is willing to use effective contraception during the trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. She has received multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with no significant improvement in disease progression. She has been recently started on a PD-1/L1 therapy but has not shown any response. She is currently on pain medication for bone metastasis and has an ECOG performance status of 1. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She is a non-smoker and has no history of illicit drug use. Her physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable for any other abnormalities. The patient is willing to undergo tumor biopsy for the study and has no contraindications for the study's inclusion and exclusion criteria. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to employ effective birth control during the study period.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who recently received a diagnosis of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in chronic phase. His initial cytogenetic analysis confirmed the presence of the Philadelphia chromosome of (9;22) translocations and the Breakpoint cluster region gene-abelson proto-oncogene (Bcr-Abl). He has not received any previous treatment for CML except for a short course of hydroxyurea. He reports no significant medical history or drug history. His physical examination and laboratory results show adequate end organ function. He is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or of childbearing potential. He is using barrier contraceptive precautions throughout the trial. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided written informed consent.

28F with BMI of 22.4, no significant past medical history, and no current medication use is being recruited for a clinical trial studying the effect of postprandial hyperinsulinaemia on VLDL-triglyceride metabolism. The patient is a non-smoker and denies alcohol or substance abuse. She has provided written consent to participate in the study. The patient has no known diseases and is considered generally healthy.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with ocular hypertension. He has no history of glaucoma or other eye conditions but has a family history of glaucoma. He has been experiencing occasional headaches and blurred vision, which he attributes to his ocular hypertension. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore potential treatments for ocular hypertension and is willing to comply with study requirements and follow-up visits. He is currently taking no medications and has no allergies.

55 year old woman who has recently been diagnosed with high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) and is seeking treatment options. She has a history of HPV infection and has never been pregnant. She experiences discomfort and itching in the affected area and is concerned about the risk of recurrence. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of ultrasonic aspiration versus CO2 laser ablation for the treatment of VIN. She is available for follow-up visits and willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus 2 years ago. She has been taking metformin 500mg twice a day for the past year, but her recent HbA1c level was 7.9%. She has no other significant medical history or complications related to diabetes. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her BMI is 28. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past 3 months. She is not pregnant and does not plan to become pregnant during the clinical trial.

The patient is a 25 year old male who is currently studying at university. He has no chronic medical conditions and is not on any medication. He has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m2 and weighs 75 kg. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no family history of any significant medical conditions. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial to contribute to medical research and gain a better understanding of his own health.

A 52-year-old male was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of cough, chest pain, and shortness of breath. He was diagnosed with Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) and was treated with antibiotics. However, his condition worsened and he was placed on mechanical ventilation for acute respiratory failure. He also received high-flow oxygen therapy with a FiO2 of 50% or more and a P/F ratio less than 300. He is affiliated with the social security scheme. He has no history of cystic fibrosis or post-obstructive pneumonia. He is not treated with vasopressors for septic shock. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding. He has no hypersensitivity to corticosteroids. He is not on judicial protection. He is willing to sign an informed consent form.

Patient is a 14-year-old male with a history of type 1 diabetes for 2 years. He is currently on multiple daily injections (MDI) of Humalog and Lantus insulin. His most recent A1C was 8.5%. He is willing to wear the Omnipod Horizon™ Automated Glucose Control System continuously throughout the study and is willing to travel to participate in meal and exercise challenges during the hybrid closed-loop phase. The patient is fluent in English and has a parent who is willing to be an overnight companion if needed. He is not currently on any medications other than insulin and is not planning to take any oral or injectable steroids during the course of the study. The patient's TSH is within the normal range, and he is not pregnant or lactating. The patient has not participated in any other clinical studies using an investigational drug or device within the preceding 30 days and is willing and able to sign the Informed Consent Form (ICF) with parental consent.

A 42-year-old Greek woman who works as a teacher and spends long hours reading and grading papers on the computer. She wears glasses for near-vision but has been experiencing some difficulty with reading small print lately. She has no history of dyslexia or attention-deficiency, and has never been diagnosed with any mental or psychiatric diseases. She is interested in participating in this study to help improve the accuracy and convenience of online reading tests.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of chronic alcohol abuse and cirrhosis. He presents to the emergency department with melena and hematemesis for the past 24 hours. Endoscopy reveals the presence of esophageal and gastric varices with active bleeding. The patient is stabilized with endoscopic variceal ligation and glypressin 1mg q6h injection for 3 days. He is not currently showing signs of infection, with normal vital signs and no fever. He has not received any antibiotics within the past 2 weeks. The patient is informed about the clinical trial and agrees to participate. He is randomly allocated to Group I and receives ceftriaxone 500 mg IV bolus stat and then q12h for 3 days as prophylactic antibiotic. The patient is closely monitored for rebleeding within 14 days, infection during admission, transfusion amount, and hospitalization days. The patient's demographic data, vital signs, transfusion amounts, hemogram, U/A, CXR, ascites routine, and endoscopic findings are recorded. The patient is informed that he may switch to Group II and receive ceftriaxone 500 mg IV bolus stat and then q12h for 7 days if rebleeding occurs.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman diagnosed with leukemia, who recently underwent stem cell transplant at the Mayo Clinic in Arizona. She lives with her husband and has two children. She is currently experiencing fatigue and loss of appetite, but no other significant symptoms. Her husband is her primary caregiver, and he is responsible for taking her to and from the hospital frequently, as well as managing her medications and other household responsibilities. The patient and her husband speak, read, and write English fluently, and have access to a working phone and e-mail account. They have no visual or hearing impairments. They are both interested in participating in the study to explore how digital stories shared by HCT survivors may impact their psychosocial wellbeing during the recovery process.

The patient is a 50-year-old male diagnosed with stage III colon cancer. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment that includes oxaliplatin. He has no history of polyneuropathy or any other neurological disorders. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works as an office manager. He is married with two children and has no history of alcohol or drug abuse. He has a BMI of 28, blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg and a resting heart rate of 75 bpm. He reports mild fatigue and occasional nausea as side effects of his chemotherapy. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to prevent chemotherapy-related polyneuropathy and improve his quality of life during treatment. He is physically capable of performing the training program implemented within the experimental intervention or the control intervention arm.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic cancer. He reports a loss of appetite, significant weight loss, and fatigue. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes medication to control it. He is a non-smoker and non-drinker. He works as a manager in a local company and has a supportive family. The patient has received one line of chemotherapy with gemcitabine, but the disease has progressed. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. His performance status is ECOG 1. His laboratory values are within normal limits except for elevated liver enzymes (AST 2.7x ULN, ALT 2.5x ULN, bilirubin 1.3x ULN). Imaging studies have shown multiple liver metastases, lung nodules, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. The largest measurable lesion is a liver metastasis that measures 3.2 cm in diameter. The patient has no brain metastases.

The patient is a 52-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stable angina. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. She exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet. She is a non-smoker and has no family history of coronary artery disease. She presents with chest pain upon exertion and shortness of breath. Her cardiac evaluation reveals a significant stenosis in a small coronary artery with a diameter of less than 2.75 mm. She is a suitable candidate for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and may be eligible for this clinical trial to compare drug-eluting balloon (DEB) versus standard therapy with second generation drug-eluting stent (DES) for small coronary vessel disease treatment. She has no known allergies or intolerances to any drugs and has not recently participated in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 58-year-old man who was diagnosed with multiple myeloma two years ago. He has undergone two lines of anti-myeloma therapy, including a combination of lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor. His disease has progressed despite undergoing these treatments, and he has developed resistance to his last line of treatment. He has measurable disease and a performance status of 1 on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Scale. He has never received prior therapy with an anti-programmed cell death 1 receptor (anti-PD-1), antiprogrammed death-ligand 1 (anti-PD-L1), antiprogrammed death-ligand 2 (anti-PD-L2), anti-CD137, or anti-cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated antigen-4 (CTLA-4) antibody. He has not received live, attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to Study Day 1. He is a non-smoker and has no history of anaphylaxis or hypersensitivity to thalidomide, lenalidomide, pomalidomide, or dex. His peripheral neuropathy is Grade 1. He has no clinical evidence of central nervous system (CNS) or pulmonary leukostasis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, or CNS multiple myeloma. He has no clinically significant cardiac disease. He is not a female who is pregnant, nursing, or breastfeeding, or who intends to become pregnant during the participation in the study.

The patient is a 54 year old African American male who has never been screened for prostate cancer. He is generally in good health and does not have a personal history of prostate cancer. He is interested in learning more about prostate cancer screening and wants to make an informed decision about whether or not to undergo screening. He is willing to participate in an educational intervention to learn more about the risks, benefits, and consequences of prostate cancer screening. He understands that he will have the opportunity to undergo screening if he decides to do so after the educational component. He does not have any active malignancy or metastatic disease and is not currently undergoing treatment for malignancy.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). She has completed standard chemotherapy but her disease has progressed. A biopsy confirmed that her lymphoma cells express CD2. She has a Karnofsky Performance Status of 80% and a life expectancy of more than 2 months. Her blood tests show a granulocyte count of 1,500/mm3 and a platelet count of 80,000/mm3. Her serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL, SGOT and SGPT are within normal limits, and her bilirubin level is 1.8 mg/dL. She has not received MEDI-507 or any other monoclonal antibody before. She understands the study procedures and has signed the informed consent form.

A 45 year old woman has been suffering from chronic urticaria for the past year. She has tried treatment with anti-H1 medications from three different classes as well as a combination of two different anti-H1 medications for more than three months, but has not found relief from the symptoms. She continues to have urticarial lesions for at least seven days every month, which affects her daily life and quality of life. She is not taking any medications currently and is not using any contraception. She has a history of hypertension and is currently on medication for it. She has no known allergies or contraindications to methotrexate, but has never been treated with it before. She has no history of neoplasia or chronic respiratory failure. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is aware of the possible risks and benefits of methotrexate treatment.

Patient is a 60-year-old man diagnosed with colon cancer. He has undergone several rounds of chemotherapy and is now recommended for minimally invasive colorectal surgery using the ALF-X robotic platform. He has no significant history of medical conditions and has been cleared for surgery by his physician. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with severe hearing loss in both ears. He is scheduled for cochlear implant surgery at the ENT department of the university hospital Vienna (AKH Wien). He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications regularly. He does not have any allergies to medications or anesthesia. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate triamcinolone levels in cochlear perilymph. His lab results show normal blood chemistry and no signs of inflammation. He has not received cortisone treatment in the past and does not have any contraindications for the administration of Volon A. The patient will be randomized to one of the four groups and will receive either Volon A 10mg or 40mg either 20-24 hours or 1-2 hours before the cochlear implant surgery. The patient will be required to provide a perilymph sample and a blood sample during the surgery, which will be stored and analyzed by the pharmaceutical laboratory. The patient is willing to comply with the study protocol and can withdraw consent at any time during the study.

A 62-year-old Caucasian male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia is admitted to the medical intensive care unit due to respiratory distress and is subsequently intubated. He has no significant past medical history or surgical history. He is currently on a continuous infusion of vasopressors to maintain his blood pressure. His current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. He denies any current or previous tobacco use, alcohol consumption or substance abuse. He is married and has two adult children. His current body mass index is 28. His current laboratory values show glucose of 168 mg/dL, creatinine of 1.3 mg/dL, and total bilirubin of 1.5 mg/dL. He is currently receiving prophylactic anticoagulation with enoxaparin. He has no history of gastrointestinal surgery or obstruction. His enteral access is via a nasogastric tube. He has never received enteral nutrition prior to this hospitalization. He speaks English fluently.

The patient is a 60-year-old female diagnosed with non-resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with no extrahepatic disease. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is not a candidate for liver transplantation due to the extent of the tumor and her age. She has been on chemotherapy for the past 3 months, which was terminated 4 weeks ago. Her medical records show elevated liver enzymes and alpha-fetoprotein levels.
