The recent biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. The patient is an alert female with no acute distress. Her BP: 140/85, HR: 80/min and BMI: 28. Her abdomen is soft with no ascites or tenderness. The lower extremities are normal with no edema.

A 68-year-old woman was referred to the clinic with a history of hypertension, which was diagnosed 6 years ago. She has been taking a combination of three antihypertensive medications – Lisinopril, Atenolol and Hydrochlorothiazide – to control her blood pressure. However, her average 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure was 145 mmHg (with directly observed medical therapy, DOT) and office blood pressure was 155 mmHg, indicating that her hypertension was not adequately controlled. She also has a history of atrial fibrillation, but it is rare and intermittent. The patient has no history of heart failure, stroke or TIA. She is on a stable dose of Levothyroxine for hypothyroidism. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is able to travel to the clinic for all scheduled visits and is willing to comply with the study requirements. The patient is interested in participating in the study to improve her hypertension control.

A 45-year-old man was involved in a motorcycle accident and landed on his left leg. He felt immediate pain in his left knee and was unable to bear weight. He was taken to the emergency department where an X-ray revealed a tibial plateau fracture with involvement of the posterior proximal tibial plateau. The fracture was classified as a Type C3 according to the revised three-column classification. The patient was referred to a specialist who recommended surgical intervention with the WAVE-plate. The patient has no prior history of knee injury or surgery. He is otherwise healthy and does not smoke. He has a physically demanding job as a construction worker and is eager to return to work as soon as possible. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to receive the most advanced treatment and to contribute to the advancement of medical research.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was diagnosed with type B aortic dissection three months ago. He has been experiencing worsening chest and back pain, along with shortness of breath and fatigue. His vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, heart rate of 80 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 96% on room air. Imaging studies show the presence of an expanding false lumen and involvement of visceral arteries. The total diameter of the dissected aortic segment is 5.5 cm, which has increased by 1 cm within the past month. The patient is not on any anticoagulation therapy and does not have renal failure or ongoing infection. He has no history of cancer, and his life expectancy is estimated to be over 24 months. The patient has been counseled on the risks and benefits of the endovascular treatment and has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

A 48-year-old man who has been experiencing low energy levels, decreased sex drive, and difficulty maintaining an erection for the past year presents to the clinic. Upon evaluation, his total serum testosterone levels are found to be below 300 ng/dL. He has no history of prostate cancer but his PSA levels are elevated at 4.2 ng/mL. The patient is interested in exploring treatment options for his symptoms and is eligible for the clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of Androxal™ in men with secondary hypogonadism.

The patient is a 57-year-old man who has been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension for over 5 years. He also has a history of heart disease and has been on medication for it. He has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) between 25 and 60 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent high albuminuria. He is currently being treated with an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi) or angiotensin-receptor blocker (ARB) and has been on a stable dose for at least 3 months. He is not on combination therapy with both ACEi and ARB. He has not had any major gastrointestinal tract surgery, pancreatic injury, or pancreatitis in the past 6 months. He is not being treated with nitrates, PDE5 inhibitors including nonspecific inhibitors, soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulators, or renin inhibitors. His hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) is less than 11%. He has not participated in another clinical study or been treated with another investigational product for the past 90 days.

The patient is a 10-year-old boy who has been experiencing difficulty swallowing for the past year. He complains of food getting stuck in his chest, nausea, and vomiting. He has a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease and has been on proton pump inhibitors for the past 6 months. He has no known allergies and takes no other medications. He lives with his parents and two siblings and is in good health otherwise. The patient has undergone multiple endoscopic dilations in the past year due to esophageal strictures but has not experienced significant symptom relief. The patient is willing to participate in the study and meets all eligibility criteria. The patient's medical history and physical examination will be evaluated to ensure that he does not have any exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 65-year-old retired woman who has been diagnosed with bullous pemphigoid (BP) by her dermatologist. She has been experiencing blistering and itching all over her body for the past 2 months. Her skin lesions are spreading and causing a lot of discomfort, making it hard for her to sleep at night. She has already been treated with superpotent topical steroids, but her symptoms have not improved. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial that investigates the efficacy of an anti-C5aR1 antibody in addition to superpotent topical steroids compared to superpotent topical steroids alone in BP patients at 3 months. She has no history of allergies or other autoimmune diseases. She is not currently taking any medications for other medical conditions and she is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She lives alone but has a supportive family who can help her with transportation to the study site. She is able to understand the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to comply with the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease. He presents to the emergency department with complaints of shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He reports that he has been experiencing these symptoms for the past week, but they have worsened over the past 24 hours. Vital signs are as follows: blood pressure of 160/90 mmHg, heart rate of 100 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. Physical examination reveals bilateral crackles in the lungs and pitting edema in the lower extremities. The patient is admitted to the hospital with a diagnosis of acute heart failure. He agrees to participate in the French Observatory of Acute Heart Failure study.

A 55-year-old male with a history of multiple myeloma is seeking alternative treatment options after conventional therapies have failed. He has undergone stem cell transplantation in the past and has been receiving chemotherapy for the past year. His latest bone marrow biopsy shows that he is relapsing and resistant to treatment. His serum creatinine level is 2.5 mg/dL and his measured creatinine clearance is 20 mL/min. His ANC is 1200/mm3 and his platelet count is 40,000/mm3. He has no active infections and is not currently receiving any other anticancer treatments. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in a clinical trial and is willing to meet all follow-up obligations. He has signed the IRB-approved informed consent form and is willing to use dual methods of contraception as he is sexually active with his female partner of child-bearing potential.

The patient is a 35-year-old male who suffered deep dermal burns on 10% of his body surface area (TBSA) due to a scalding accident while cooking at home. He has no known allergies to polyurethane and has not had any exposure to investigational agents or other treatments/devices that may interfere with NovoSorb BTM integration. He is willing to comply with all study procedures and is expected to be available for the duration of the study. The patient has no significant medical history and does not have any conditions that might interfere with treatment evaluation or require a change in therapy. He is not currently pregnant and is not planning to become pregnant during the course of the study. The patient agrees to use effective contraceptive methods throughout the study.

A 54-year-old male presents to the neurology clinic with progressive muscle weakness, difficulty speaking and swallowing, and muscle twitches all over his body. He has noticed these symptoms for the past 12 months and has been experiencing significant functional decline. His medical history is significant for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking. He is currently on medications for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His family history is negative for any neurological disorders. On examination, he has prominent fasciculations in all four limbs, with wasting and weakness involving the tongue and bulbar muscles. He has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) by a neurologist with expertise in MND. Despite being ambulatory, he has difficulty with daily activities and requires assistance. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol of the Serial Fasciculation Measurements in Motor Neurone Disease study and can give signed informed consent. He meets all the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria.

A 45-year-old female who was diagnosed with stage IIIA cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) 6 months ago. She presented with red, scaly patches on her skin that were not itchy. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of CTCL. She has been started on phototherapy and topical steroids, which have been helpful in controlling her skin lesions. She has no significant medical history and has not received any prior treatment for CTCL. She is willing to participate in this study and undergo disease assessment by physical examination, full-body photographic documentation of skin disease, biopsy, and blood sampling at baseline and then at least annually thereafter. She is also willing to provide tissue and blood samples for proteomic and molecular analysis. She has tested negative for Human T-cell lymphotrophic virus (HTLV) I/II and is not pregnant.

45 yo M diagnosed with dyslipidemia with LDL cholesterol levels of 160 mg/dL, total cholesterol levels of 220 mg/dL, and triglyceride levels of 155 mg/dL. The patient is Mestizo Mexican with both parents and grandparents born in Mexico. The patient has a BMI of 30 kg/m² and is able to read and write. The patient has not suffered a cardiovascular event, does not have diabetes or catabolic diseases, and has not experienced significant weight loss in the last three months. The patient is a non-smoker and is not taking any antihypertensive drugs or other excluded medications. The patient is interested in participating in the trial and has agreed to consume one bottle of Chaya water beverage per day for six weeks.

52-year-old female diagnosed with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (MBC) in [**2018-07-01**]. She had received multiple lines of therapy including neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery and adjuvant trastuzumab. She progressed to metastatic disease in [**2019-06-01**] and was started on first-line chemotherapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Due to disease progression, she was switched to T-DM1 under the Spanish compassionate use program in [**2020-02-01**]. She has been followed up regularly in the oncology clinic and has had regular imaging studies to monitor her disease status. Despite experiencing some side effects including fatigue and thrombocytopenia, she has responded well to T-DM1 and remains on treatment with stable disease. She has consented to participate in the study to contribute to the understanding of the real-world effectiveness and safety of T-DM1 and Pertuzumab in Spanish patients with HER2-positive MBC.

65-year-old Caucasian female presented to the rheumatology clinic with complaints of bilateral knee pain that has been present for more than 6 months. The pain is worse with weight-bearing activities and is associated with morning stiffness lasting for 20-30 minutes. The pain is rated as 7/10 on a visual analogue scale. The patient has been previously diagnosed with osteoarthritis based on radiographic evidence according to the criteria of the American College of Rheumatology. The patient is not currently taking any medications for the management of the osteoarthritis. The patient has no past history of other joint diseases or surgeries. The patient has a history of hypertension, but it is well controlled with medication. The patient has no history of liver or kidney problems. The patient's laboratory tests including liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits, and the serum CRP level is less than 10 mg/l. The patient has not received any intra-articular injections of corticosteroids in the past 3 months or hyaluronan in the past 6 months. The patient is willing to participate in a 3-month clinical trial that evaluates the safety, tolerance and clinical efficacy of an oral formulation of salmon calcitonin for the management of osteoarthritis. The patient will be randomized to receive either a placebo, 0.5 mg sCT or 1 mg sCT and will be asked to take the tablet every day in the morning 15 minutes before breakfast.

A 56 year old man who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery two days ago and is currently on postoperative antiaggregatory therapy with aspirin. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, but otherwise has no known allergies or conditions that would exclude him from participating in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who is generally healthy and has not received a flu vaccine in the past year. He works in a busy office and is concerned about the potential for contracting influenza during flu season. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial for the Butantan quadrivalent influenza vaccine candidate in order to potentially receive protection against a broader spectrum of influenza strains. He has no chronic medical conditions, is not taking any immunosuppressive medications, and has no known allergies to egg or chicken proteins. He is willing to complete all study visits and procedures, and is looking forward to contributing to the research on the safety and efficacy of this vaccine candidate.

A 42-year old female presented with a swollen and tender right breast. She reported that the swelling has been increasing over the past two months. On examination, her right breast was red, swollen, and tender. There was no nipple discharge or palpable lump. Her axilla was negative for lymphadenopathy. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, for which she takes medication. She is married and has two children. She is a homemaker and reports no history of tobacco or alcohol use. She is concerned about her symptoms and wants to explore all treatment options available. Further tests revealed that she has inflammatory breast cancer. She is eligible for this clinical trial as she hasn't received any chemotherapy or radiation therapy yet. She has a good performance status and normal liver, kidney, and bone marrow function. Her echocardiogram indicates that her left ventricular ejection fraction is greater than or equal to 50%, and she has no clinical symptoms or signs of heart failure. The patient is willing to participate in the study and agrees to use an accepted and effective method of contraception during the study.

Sarah is a 16-year-old high school student who has been experiencing difficulty falling asleep at night. She usually goes to bed around 11 pm and wakes up at 6 am for school. However, she finds herself staying up until 1 or 2 am several times a week due to homework and social activities. She has noticed that this is affecting her ability to wake up on time and has resulted in her being late to school on several occasions. She is otherwise healthy, with no known chronic diseases that affect sleep or ongoing therapeutic treatment relationship. She is interested in participating in the SleepHelsinki! study to better understand her sleep patterns and to learn how to improve her sleep regulation.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a BMI of 28. She has a family history of cardiovascular disease and is concerned about her overall health. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of water-only fasting and refeeding on insulin resistance and cardiovascular health. She has no history of stroke or heart attack within the last 90 days and has no active malignancy or inflammatory disorder. She is willing to undergo a water-only fast of at least 10 consecutive days and provide informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 56-year-old woman who provides care for her husband who has a traumatic brain injury (TBI). She reports feeling overwhelmed and stressed as a caregiver, and has experienced a decline in her own health. She endorses feeling frustrated and distant from family and friends. She provides approximately 15 hours of care per week, including direct assistance with activities of daily living. She has been approved by her Primary Care Provider to participate in physical exercise. She is proficient in spoken and written English. She has no history of psychiatric disorder with psychotic features or suicidal/homicidal ideation, and no current alcohol or substance abuse. She has not participated in another caregiver intervention within the past year. She has regular access to the internet. She does not plan to transfer care of her husband to another caregiver or nursing home within the next 12 months. She has no severe cardiac disease or morbid obesity. She is able to read, verbalize understanding, and voluntarily sign the Informed Consent.

A 55-year-old man came to the clinic with a history of prostate cancer and has elected to undergo external beam radiation therapy. He complains of over-active bladder (OAB) symptoms such as urgency, frequency, and nocturia. He has been experiencing these symptoms for the past 6 months. His medical history is significant for hypertension, and he is currently being treated with metoprolol. He has no known allergies to medication. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is willing to complete the American Urology Association Symptom Score (AUASS) Questionnaire. Physical examination and laboratory tests were unremarkable. He has not been treated with medication for alleviation of OAB symptoms within 12 months prior to the Screening Visit. He is ambulatory and is willing to participate in the study.

This clinical trial is looking for preschool-aged children from low-income communities in Los Angeles County who are already enrolled in participating preschools. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a multilevel intervention to support healthy eating and physical activity in preschools to address childhood obesity. The study involves two groups with stratified cluster randomization at the level of the preschool. The intervention group will receive support for healthy nutrition and physical activity, while the control group will receive usual care. The primary outcome of the study is child BMI z-scores, and secondary outcomes include parent-reported child nutrition and physical activity. The study will also examine the implementation process to understand factors that may facilitate or hinder intervention uptake and success. Eligible participants should be between 2.5-5 years old, enrolled in the participating preschool, and eat at least one meal on-site per school day. Child primary caregivers who can read and write in English or Spanish are also eligible to participate.

A 28-year-old ultra-Orthodox male resident of Jerusalem area with limited sun exposure due to religious dress code and daily routine seeks to participate in a clinical trial assessing the correlation between vitamin D levels and bone mineral density. He has no known chronic illnesses, but he is not under any chronic medication. He has never been diagnosed with any malabsorptive, granulomatous, or genetic disorders. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He reports occasional muscular pains but no general fatigue. He is interested in learning more about his vitamin D status and its potential consequences on his bone health. He is willing to undergo blood and urine samples, bone mineral density examinations, and vitamin D supplementation if necessary.

A 52-year-old man with a family history of cardiovascular disease and high blood pressure visited the clinic for a routine check-up. He works in an office and spends most of his day sitting in front of a computer. He exercises regularly, about 3 times a week. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no history of stroke, heart attack, or peripheral vascular disease. He has been diagnosed with hypertension and is currently taking medication for it. He also takes medication for high cholesterol levels. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help better understand the differences in vascular function and stroke risk between men and women.

A 30-year-old Caucasian male with no significant medical history is interested in participating in a clinical trial. He is in good physical condition and exercises regularly. He is not currently taking any prescription medications or herbal remedies, except for occasional paracetamol and nasal adrenergic anticongestants. He has never participated in a clinical trial before.

A 54-year-old male who underwent a coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) procedure 2 weeks ago visited the clinic for a follow-up visit. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes lisinopril and atorvastatin. He is married, has two children, and works as a construction worker. He has been a smoker for 20 years, but quit smoking 2 months ago. He drinks alcohol occasionally. His physical examination is unremarkable. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, and his heart rate is 70 beats per minute. His serum creatinine level is 1.2 mg/dL. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of aspirin and clopidogrel on his bypass grafts after CABG surgery.

A 27-year-old female presents with a history of growth hormone deficiency (GHD) for the past 4 years. She has not received any growth hormone therapy in the past. She reports fatigue, decreased stamina, and difficulty losing weight. She denies any history of diabetes, hypertension or vascular disease. Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements. Physical examination reveals a BMI of 29 kg/m2 and no significant findings on cardiovascular, respiratory, or abdominal examination. Laboratory results show low serum levels of insulin-like growth factor 1 and free thyroid hormone, while other hormonal levels are within normal limits. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effects of growth hormone supplementation on metabolism and adipose tissue molecular phenotype. She is willing to comply with scheduled visits, study procedures, and laboratory tests.

The patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and has been receiving transfusions for anemia for the past 4 months. He has tried standard treatments for MDS but did not respond to any of them. His bone marrow biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of refractory anemia with excess blasts-2 (RAEB-2). He has no suitable matched sibling donor for bone marrow transplant and does not wish to undergo the procedure. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and he is not on any other treatment for MDS. His blood work shows anemia with hemoglobin levels of 8.5 g/dL and a reticulocyte count of 40,000/μL. His platelet count is 70,000/μL and absolute neutrophil count is 900/μL. He has no active infection and his serum creatinine is 1.3 mg/dL. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the investigational nature of the study.

The patient is a 42-year-old male who was diagnosed with HIV infection 5 years ago. He has been on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate (TDF) and Emtricitabine (FTC) along with a protease inhibitor (PI/r) for the past 2 years. His HIV viral load has been undetectable (<50 copies/mL) for the last 18 months. He has no history of neurological symptoms or severe neurocognitive impairment. He has previously participated in a longitudinal study on HIV in CNS at the University of Gothenburg and had a lumbar puncture performed between 6 and 18 months before the study entry. He is not pregnant.

A 42-year-old man with a history of follicular lymphoma, initially diagnosed 5 years ago, presents with relapsed disease after receiving multiple courses of chemotherapy and rituximab. He has advanced Ann Arbor stage and has not received more than 200mg/m^2 of anthracycline. He is currently experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss. His cardiac, renal, and hepatic functions are normal, and he is negative for HIV, HBV, and HCV. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing and able to provide informed consent.

A 38-year-old African American woman with a BMI of 38.7 kg/m2 came to the clinic for a pre-surgical evaluation before her scheduled laparoscopic surgery. She has a history of hypertension, which is currently being managed with medication. She has never taken any medication that acts on the central nervous system. She is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history. She has given informed consent to participate in the clinical trial investigating the pharmacokinetics of dexmedetomidine in obese patients.

The patient is a 28-year-old female diagnosed with Hodgkin's Disease (HD) six months ago. She has undergone two chemotherapy regimens which have failed to produce any significant improvement. Her past medical history is non-significant. She is not on any medications currently. Her medical records show a positive diagnosis of HD on biopsy tests. The recent CT scan shows multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, chest, and abdomen. There is no evidence of liver or spleen enlargement. The patient is experiencing fatigue, night sweats, and a 5-pound weight loss over the past month. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance rating of 1. Her vital signs are within normal limits. Her BP: 120/70, HR: 80/min, and BMI: 23. Her abdomen is soft with no tenderness. The lower extremities are normal with no edema. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the investigational nature of the study. She is not pregnant and agrees to use effective contraception methods during the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is healthy and not currently taking any form of hormonal contraceptives. She has no known contraindications to Loestrin 1.5/30 (the combined oral contraceptive used in this study), famotidine (an H2 blocker), or fluconazole. She has no history of drug or alcohol dependency, and has not used any investigational drug or device within 30 days preceding informed consent. She has no known history of clinically significant drug allergy or food allergies, and is not presently experiencing significant seasonal or perennial allergy. She has not engaged in strenuous exercise within 2 weeks before check-in, and has not taken any food supplements or medications that may affect cytochrome P4503A4 enzyme within 1 week before dosing. She is willing and able to comply with all aspects of the protocol and has provided written informed consent.

56 year old man with end stage renal disease who has been on chronic hemodialysis for the last 5 months. He has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on erythropoiesis stimulating agent and intravenous iron for the treatment of anemia secondary to CKD. He has a BMI of 30.8 kg/m2, and his ALT and total bilirubin levels are within normal limits. He has not received a blood transfusion in the past 3 months, and he has not experienced any myocardial infarction, acute coronary syndrome, stroke or transient ischemic attack within the last 6 months.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing stress urinary incontinence (SUI) for several years. She has had multiple pregnancies and vaginal deliveries, and her symptoms have worsened over time. She has tried behavioral therapy, such as pelvic floor exercises and bladder training, but has not seen significant improvement. She is otherwise healthy and takes no medication. She works as a teacher and is very active in her community. She is interested in a minimally invasive procedure to address her SUI but is hesitant to undergo surgery in a hospital setting. She is willing and able to stand for the procedure and is excited about the possibility of having the procedure done in a more comfortable and convenient setting. She understands and agrees to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old male who has no history of cardiovascular or respiratory diseases, ongoing medication use, or other medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and has not experienced any recent traumas or illnesses. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial to contribute to scientific research and better understand the effects of cyclooxygenase inhibitors on blood pressure, cerebral blood flow, and renal hemodynamics following chronic intermittent hypoxia exposure. He is willing to provide informed written consent and is available for the study duration. The patient is physically active and maintains a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise and a balanced diet. He is eager to participate in the study and is committed to following all protocol requirements.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has been suffering from moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis for over two years. She has tried various topical medications with little improvement. She experiences intense itching, redness, and flaking of the skin on her face, neck, and limbs. The patient has a history of seasonal allergies and mild asthma but is otherwise healthy. She does not have any other significant medical conditions or take any medications regularly. She has not used tanning beds or phototherapy in the past six weeks. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and uses a reliable form of contraception. She has not had any recent infections or received any immunosuppressive therapy. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all study visits.

44-year-old female with a history of recurrent sinusitis and nasal polyps presents to the ENT clinic for a scheduled endoscopic sinus surgery. She reports experiencing chronic nasal congestion, facial pain, and impaired sense of smell for over a year, despite medical management. She has no known drug allergies and takes no regular medications. She is fluent in English and came to the appointment unaccompanied. During the pre-operative counseling session, the surgeon explained the risks and benefits of the procedure and provided her with a structured surgery-specific consent form to read and sign. She expressed understanding of the information provided and signed the form. She will be given a self-administered survey on the same day to assess her comprehension and satisfaction with the pre-operative counseling process.

A 42-year-old woman presents with a history of psoriasis for the past 5 years. She has tried various topical treatments including corticosteroids, vitamin A and D analogues, and moisturizers without significant improvement. She has never received systemic therapy for her psoriasis. Her medical history is significant for hypertension controlled with amlodipine. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. On physical examination, she has symmetric target lesions on both thighs measuring 3 cm in diameter with a baseline Target Lesion Score (TLS) of 7 for each target. Her skin is otherwise unremarkable. Her vital signs are stable with a BP of 120/78 mmHg, HR of 75 bpm, and BMI of 25. She has no significant findings on laboratory testing, including normal liver and kidney function tests, serum glucose, hemoglobin, platelet count, and WBC count. She is willing to use two forms of contraception throughout the study and for 60 days after the last dose of study drug.

56-year-old female with a history of hypertension and obesity is scheduled for elective laparoscopic hysterectomy due to uterine fibroids. She has no known drug allergies and is currently taking lisinopril and metformin. She reports occasional lower abdominal pain and discomfort due to the fibroids. During the preoperative consultation, she expresses concern about postoperative pain management and potential opioid use. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial comparing the efficacy of TAP blocks with liposomal bupivacaine (Exparel) and continuous epidural blocks for pain management after surgery. The patient is able to use IV PCA systems and is expected to require parenteral opioids for at least 72 hours after surgery. She has no history of liver or kidney disease and is not on anticoagulant therapy.

A 32-year-old female patient was admitted to the hospital after a motor vehicle accident that resulted in a traumatic brain injury. She has been in a coma for the past 4 weeks and has not shown any signs of consciousness. The initial clinical examinations have indicated a vegetative state, but the diagnostic and prognostic usefulness of neuroimaging methods have not been established in her case. She is hemodynamically stable and has no other significant medical history. She is not on any medication that could interfere with the study. She has no known allergies to any medication or contrast media. She is cooperative and able to follow simple commands such as opening her eyes and gripping her hand. Her family is aware of the study and has provided consent for her participation.

A 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) for the past 2 years. She experiences joint pain, stiffness, and swelling, mainly affecting her fingers, toes, and lower back. She also has a history of psoriasis. Her current treatment includes methotrexate and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). She has been recommended to start a standard of care biologic treatment such as TNFi. She has no history of other autoimmune diseases or cancer. Her blood pressure and other vital signs are within normal limits, and she has no significant medical history. She is willing to provide written informed consent and is able to tolerate phlebotomy for blood donation.

32 yo M with a history of mild asthma since childhood, with symptoms occurring greater than 2 times a week but less than once per day with normal Forced Expired Volume in 1 second (> 80% predicted). The patient has a clinical history of allergic symptoms to cat allergen and demonstrated skin reactivity. The patient has never smoked and has not been exposed to agents associated with pulmonary disease such as asbestos or silica. The patient is willing and able to give informed consent and expressed the desire to participate in an interview with the principal investigator. The patient has not taken antihistamines within 7 days of the screening visit and has not participated in a research study involving a drug or biologic during the 30 days prior to the study. The patient is not intolerant to albuterol, atropine, or lidocaine. The patient has never had an anaphylaxis episode and has no history of pulmonary disease, coronary disease, congestive heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, history of a cerebrovascular accident, renal failure, cirrhosis, or any other significant disease that would pose a significant risk for the subject or confound the results of the study. The patient is not using systemic steroids, increased use of inhaled steroids, beta blockers, or monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and has not had a visit for an asthma exacerbation within 1 month of the screening visit. The patient has never had a history of asthma-related respiratory failure requiring intubation or hospitalization due to asthma. The patient has no contraindication to methacholine challenge testing and has a BMI under 32.

The patient is a 25 year old male who has been diagnosed with anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear and is scheduled for arthroscopic reconstruction surgery. He has no history of renal impairment, liver failure or asthma. He is not pregnant and not currently breastfeeding. The patient is classified as ASA I or II.

The patient is a 6-year-old girl diagnosed with epilepsy and is currently on a Ketogenic diet to control her seizures. The patient has been on the Ketogenic diet for the past year and is currently taking a comprehensive micronutrient supplement as part of her dietary management. The patient's parents report that she has been compliant with the Ketogenic diet, but sometimes struggles with taking her supplement due to its taste and texture. The patient's medical history is significant for developmental delay and she has received early intervention services since the age of 2. The patient is able to communicate effectively and has no known food allergies or intolerances. The patient's current medications include lamotrigine and levetiracetam for seizure control. The patient's most recent laboratory results showed a normal complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic panel. The patient's parents are interested in enrolling her in a clinical trial to assess the taste and acceptance of FruitiVits as a potential alternative to her current supplement.

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for the past 5 years. He has a smoking history of 30 pack-years and has been on various inhalers and bronchodilators for symptom management. He experiences frequent episodes of shortness of breath, especially during physical activity, and coughs up sputum on most days. He has not had any recent exacerbations requiring hospitalization. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He does not have a history of asthma or other chronic lung diseases. He does not take antioxidant therapy. He has not had any new or recurrent symptomatic myocardial ischemia, severe arrhythmia, cardiac insufficiency, or cerebrovascular disease. He does not have senile dementia or cognitive impairment. He does not have cancer. He does not have severe liver or kidney dysfunction. He speaks fluent English and does not have any limb activity disorders. He has not participated in any sports training in the last 3 months.

Pt is a 35yo M, a heavy smoker for the past 15 years, and a heavy drinker for the past 10 years. He smokes at least one pack of cigarettes per day and drinks 5-6 standard drinks per day. He has tried to quit smoking and cut back on drinking on his own, but has been unsuccessful. He is seeking treatment to quit smoking and reduce his alcohol consumption. He has a Fagerstrom Test of Nicotine Dependence score of 5 and an Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT) score of 12. He is in good general health and is able to provide written informed consent.

52-year-old male with a history of smoking presents with hoarseness and difficulty swallowing for the past 6 months. Physical exam reveals a lesion on the supraglottic region of the epi-larynx. Biopsy confirms squamous cell carcinoma. CT scan shows no evidence of distant metastasis. Patient's case is discussed in a multidisciplinary meeting and a decision is made to perform a unilateral endoscopic axillary neck dissection at lymph node levels IIa, III and IV of the Robins classification using the da Vinci robotic system to reduce scarring, while respecting patient safety. Patient is available for 12 months of follow-up and has given informed and signed consent. Patient has a BMI of 22 and no history of cervical spine surgery, instability of the cervical spine, surgery in the shoulder or pre-pectoral region, ipsilateral neck surgery, cervical radiotherapy or breast implants.

7-year-old girl with a recent diagnosis of IgE-mediated cow's milk allergy confirmed by positive double-blind placebo-controlled food challenge (DBPCFC) performed in the last 2 months. She has been successfully avoiding cow's milk and all dairy products since then. She has been experiencing no symptoms related to cow's milk consumption. She has no other significant medical history or chronic diseases. She has not taken any short-acting, medium-acting, or long-acting antihistamines within the last 3, 7, or 21 days, respectively. She has not received any oral steroids within the last 21 days prior to the DBPCFC. She has not been exposed to any other suspected food allergens. She and her parents have provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has a family history of colon cancer. He is generally in good health, with no significant past medical history except for mild hypertension, well controlled with amlodipine 5 mg daily. He has no history of diabetes or other chronic illnesses. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the dietary influence of grapes in colon cancer prevention. He is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. His latest CBC, CMP, AN and UA results were within normal range. He underwent a limited flexible sigmoidoscopy on Day 15 and the results were normal. He is willing to follow the study diet and consume the prescribed amount of fresh red grapes. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and has signed the informed consent form.

50 year-old man with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain radiating to his left arm. Pain started suddenly while he was at rest and has been ongoing for the past 30 minutes. He also reports shortness of breath and diaphoresis. Upon arrival, the patient is noted to be in severe distress with a blood pressure of 180/110 mmHg and a heart rate of 110 beats per minute. An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, indicating an acute inferior myocardial infarction (MI). The emergency medical services (EMS) are activated and the patient is quickly assessed by the Ground Emergency Medical Services (GEMS) team. The GEMS team performs advanced cardiac life support (ACLS) and administers aspirin and nitroglycerin before rapidly transporting the patient to the nearest hospital with cardiac intervention capabilities. The patient is then transferred to the cardiac catheterization lab, where a percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is performed, resulting in successful revascularization of the occluded coronary artery. The patient is stabilized and admitted to the cardiac intensive care unit.

52-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and a previous myocardial infarction, who is scheduled to undergo coronary intervention with bare metal stent placement for treatment of a de novo lesion in a native coronary artery. The target lesion is located in a vessel with a diameter between 2.25-4.0 mm and is less than or equal to 25 mm in length. The patient has no bifurcation, left main or ostial RCA lesions. The patient is on antiplatelet therapy and has well-controlled hypertension and diabetes.

Maria is a 45 year old female who has been experiencing chronic cough with sputum production for the past year. She reported having recurrent respiratory infections and difficulty breathing. She has a history of pneumonia in the past and was diagnosed with bronchiectasis based on a high resolution computerized tomography (HRCT) scan. Maria has been producing sputum daily and can provide at least 2 of the 3 required baseline sputum samples with an average of 3 mL or more. She is currently on a stable treatment regimen as prescribed by her doctor. She has no other significant medical history and is not on any other medication. Maria is a non-smoker and does not have any allergies. She is interested in participating in the study to investigate the effect of AZD5069 in patients with bronchiectasis.

25 yo F diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus at the age of 20, currently using insulin lispro for the past 2 years. She has been compliant with her treatment regimen and has an HbA1c level of 9%. She has no history of smoking and has normal lung function. She has no known history of liver or kidney disease. She is interested in participating in the study to see if the human insulin inhalation powder plus insulin glargine is more effective in controlling her blood sugar levels compared to her current treatment regimen. She is open to trying new treatments to better manage her condition.

A 55-year-old male with recently diagnosed Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer is scheduled to begin concurrent chemoradiation treatment. He reports a history of smoking for 30 years and has recently quit. He is in good physical health, has no major comorbidities, and is able to perform activities of daily living independently. He is fluent in English and does not require assistance with self-care ADLs. He has a history of anxiety but has passed the screening tool for this study. He has no history of depression. He is married and has two adult children. He works full-time as a sales representative and is concerned about missing work due to treatment-related side effects. He is motivated to participate in the study to potentially reduce the severity of mucositis and prevent dehydration. He has access to a telephone and is able to read and write in English.

A 45-year-old man was scheduled for coronary artery bypass graft surgery due to chest pain and shortness of breath during exertion. He has a history of high blood pressure and high cholesterol, and his BMI is 35. He has been struggling with obesity for several years and has tried different diets and exercise programs without success. He does not smoke and is not diabetic. His ECG showed a normal sinus rhythm. He was able to read and understand the consent form in French and provided informed consent to participate in the study.

32-year-old non-smoking female with a history of gingivitis associated with dental plaque. She has no clinical signs of destructive periodontal disease and has a clinical attachment loss of less than 3mm. She has a minimum of 20 teeth, with no gross caries, extensive restoration, or orthodontic bands. She does not have any systemic diseases that could impair immune response, such as diabetes mellitus, immunological disorders, hepatitis, or HIV infections. She has not used antibiotics, anti-inflammatory, or immunosuppressive drugs within the last 3 months. She has not undergone periodontal therapy within the last 3 months, and she is not pregnant or lactating. She is not using oral contraceptives.

54 year old male with a history of smoking and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who was admitted to the hospital with severe shortness of breath and cough. Rapidly progressed to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation. Imaging revealed significant lung heterogeneity. Despite standard treatment, the patient remains hypoxemic and continues to require high levels of oxygen support. The patient has signed informed consent to participate in this clinical trial to evaluate the effects of three different recruitment maneuvers on lung heterogeneity in ARDS patients. The patient has stable vital signs and is not currently enrolled in any other clinical trials.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. He has been experiencing nonmotor symptoms such as depression, anxiety, and cognitive impairment that have been affecting his daily life. He has been treated with various medications, but they have not been effective in managing his symptoms. His neurologist has recommended that he undergo Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) surgery under local anesthesia at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. He is fluent in English and able to participate in intraoperative testing. He is interested in participating in this study to help further the understanding of Parkinson's disease and potentially improve treatment options for himself and others living with the disease.

32 F with no significant medical history and no medication use, who is fluent in English and able to provide informed consent. She is interested in participating in a research study on cognitive function and brain activity. She has no contraindications for MRI, is not claustrophobic, and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She reports no history of neurological, mental, or cardiovascular disorders, liver or kidney disease, hypertension, or diabetes. She denies any history of psychotic or panic disorders, violent or suicidal behavior, psychiatric institutionalization or imprisonment. She is not on any psychiatric serotonergic antidepressant medication or drugs of abuse currently or within the last 5 weeks, and does not have a history of panic attacks or color blindness. She is willing to complete a delayed match-to-sample task, psychomotor vigilance test, and visual-motor task, as well as undergo fMRI measurements before and after ingesting a USP methylene blue or placebo. She understands that she will be asked to complete a short questionnaire one week after the study. She is willing to participate in the study and understands that she may be randomly assigned to receive either USP methylene blue or placebo, and that the study is double-blind.

80 year-old man, community-dwelling, living with his wife of 50 years. He has a history of hypertension, but is otherwise in good health. He reports feeling more fatigued and less mobile in recent years, and has had some trouble with balance and stability. He is able to complete activities of daily living, but with some difficulty. He is interested in improving his physical function and maintaining his independence. He is willing to commit to a 3-month exercise intervention, and is open to trying different types of exercise. He is motivated and committed to making positive changes to his lifestyle.

Patient is a 65-year-old man from the United States who was recently diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently taking medication for both conditions, including lisinopril and atorvastatin. His BMI is 27, BP: 140/90, HR: 80/min. Laboratory studies show elevated levels of LDL cholesterol (160 mg/dL) and hs-CRP (5 mg/L). He has no history of diabetes, liver or kidney disease, nor has he had an acute cardiovascular event in the past 3 months. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow-up visits.

55 y/o female who has noticed difficulty with near vision in the past year. She currently wears glasses for distance vision but has been struggling with reading, particularly in low light or small print. She has no history of previous eye surgeries or chronic eye diseases. She is mentally competent and able to understand and comply with the requirements of the study, and is able to provide written informed consent. She has no history of chronic systemic diseases such as diabetes, heart disease, or Lupus. She has not participated in a device clinical study for the operative eye within the last 3 months and has not been implanted with PSI devices in this or any other study.

The patient is a 65-year-old man who lives in a rural area in Maryland. He has been diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and hypertension. He takes anti-hyperglycemic oral therapy for his diabetes mellitus. He has difficulty traveling long distances to receive medical care due to his health conditions and the distance to the nearest health care facility. He lives alone and has a limited support system. He is willing to try new technologies to manage his chronic conditions and is able to operate the telehome care system. He is interested in participating in the study to see if it will improve his health outcomes and quality of life.

56 year old man with type 2 diabetes and a history of peripheral sensory neuropathy. He was diagnosed with diabetes 10 years ago and has been struggling to manage his blood glucose levels. He reports tingling and numbness in his feet, which has been affecting his balance and gait. He also reports difficulty sleeping due to the discomfort in his feet. He has no history of foot ulcers or amputations. His current medications include metformin and insulin. He is able to walk independently but experiences occasional falls due to his balance issues. He is interested in participating in the study to see if the Anodyne Therapy System can improve his peripheral sensation and quality of life.

The patient is a healthy newborn baby boy, born to an HIV-1-positive mother in Nairobi, Kenya. He was born full-term and weighs 3.2 kg. The mother received antenatal care and was on antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy, with a viral load of <50 copies/mL at delivery. The baby's HIV status was confirmed negative through a filter paper and RNA test prior to vaccination. The parents have given written informed consent for their baby to participate in the clinical trial. The baby has not received any other HIV-1 vaccine or drug trial before. The baby is currently healthy, with no signs of acute illness or fever. The baby has not received any other vaccinations apart from the standard KEPI immunizations. The parents are willing and able to comply with all the requirements of the study protocol. There are no plans for the family to travel away from the study area.

A 58-year-old man comes to the clinic complaining of blurred vision and headache for the past few months. He has a history of hypertension and wears corrective lenses for myopia. The patient reports a family history of glaucoma. His vision acuity is 20/40 in both eyes. An intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement reveals high pressure levels of 26 mm Hg in the right eye and 27 mm Hg in the left eye. Visual field testing confirms peripheral vision loss in both eyes. The patient is diagnosed with bilateral primary open-angle glaucoma and is recommended to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of OPA-6566 ophthalmic solution for the treatment of primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.

A 32-year-old woman who works as a teacher has been trying to conceive for two years. She is married and lives with her husband in a suburban area. She has been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and underwent controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) prior to in vitro fertilization (IVF) with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) as part of the P05714 clinical trial. She received corifollitropin alfa during COS and had a fresh embryo transfer. The participant is now 14 weeks pregnant and has had an ultrasound confirming an ongoing pregnancy. She is willing to participate in this follow-up trial to monitor her pregnancy, delivery, and neonatal outcomes. She has had a healthy pregnancy so far with no complications, and she is excited to welcome her first child. She is currently taking prenatal vitamins and has had regular prenatal check-ups with her obstetrician. The participant has no history of chronic illnesses, and she does not smoke or use any illicit drugs.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who tested positive for COVID-19 and is experiencing shortness of breath and coughing. He has been hospitalized due to his symptoms and is currently receiving standard of care supportive therapy. The patient has no known allergies and is not currently taking any medications. He is able to provide informed consent and agrees to use medically-accepted double-barrier methods of contraception during the study if randomized to a treatment arm. The patient has no history of severe cardiac, renal, or liver disease, and his electrolyte levels are within the normal range. He has not participated in another clinical trial of an investigational medicinal product (CTIMP). The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding. His hemoglobin level is above 80 g/L, and he has no significant electrolyte disturbance. The patient is willing and able to comply with drug administration plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who has been undergoing HD treatment for the past 7 years due to chronic kidney disease. He experiences frequent hypotensive events during his dialysis sessions, which cause him to feel dizzy and sometimes faint. He also suffers from cramps, headaches, and nausea during these sessions. His dialysis session time is typically 4 hours, and he receives bicarbonate dialysis. He has no vascular access-related problems and is able to tolerate a blood flow rate of 300ml/min. He has not participated in any other clinical trials in the past and is willing to provide informed consent for this study. The patient is generally in good health aside from his kidney disease, and he has a life expectancy that is greater than the study period. He is able to understand and follow the study protocol.

This is an 8-year-old male with a history of uncontrolled asthma for the past 6 months. He has a history of intermittent wheezing, cough, and shortness of breath, which has been exacerbated in the past few months. He has been using a rescue inhaler more frequently and has had multiple emergency room visits due to asthma exacerbations. He has been prescribed a single controller medication for asthma, which has not been effective in controlling his symptoms. He has no prior history of lung infection or antibiotic use. He is otherwise healthy and has no other significant medical history.

A 32-year-old English-speaking mother of a 4-year-old child with elevated disruptive behavior problems according to the Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory. She reports having a smartphone and is able to use the CIAS program on her phone. The child does not have an Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, intellectual disability, or is currently receiving treatment for Oppositional Defiant Disorder or ADHD. The mother is interested in participating in the Parenting Young Children Check-up Evaluation and is willing to be randomly assigned to either the intervention or control group.

20-year-old female college student, enrolled at the University of Nevada, Reno, seeking help at the Counseling Services due to moderate to severe suicidal ideation. The patient has been experiencing intense feelings of hopelessness, worthlessness, and lack of interest in activities that used to bring pleasure. She has been having recurrent thoughts of wanting to end her life, and has made a plan to attempt suicide in the past. The patient has not received any mental health services at the UNR Counseling Services in the past three months. The patient is willing to give informed consent to participate in a pilot study that will test the feasibility of utilizing an adaptive intervention strategy for college students who are suicidal when first seeking treatment.

The patient is a 55 year-old postmenopausal woman who has been experiencing symptoms associated with vulvovaginal atrophy, including dryness sensation, dyspareunia, itching/irritation and pain. She has previously refused estrogen therapies for treatment of these symptoms or has contraindications for such therapies. She has given her informed consent to participate in the study and meets all the eligibility criteria. She is affiliated with a health social security system, and has not participated in another clinical trial. She has not been deprived of her freedom by administrative or legal decision or under trusteeship/guardianship. She does not have a known tendency to develop hypertrophic or keloid scars, and has not experienced bacterial, fungal or viral infections in or close to the area of interest or treatment for these affections. She does not have a history of cancer in areas close to the injection site (vulvar, vaginal or cervical cancers) or ongoing cancer distant from the injection site. She has not undergone treatment with a trophically targeted electromagnetic treatment of the vaginal mucosa (pulsed CO2 laser, LED, radiofrequency, etc.) within 6 months prior to inclusion. She has not been treated with anticoagulant, antiplatelet agents, NSAIDs or Vitamin C within 1 week prior to inclusion, and has not undergone local hyaluronic acid-like hydrating treatment within 4 weeks prior to inclusion. She is not under hormonal treatment, antidepressant agents or selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) treatment targeted against vaginal dryness within 4 weeks prior to inclusion. She has not undergone vulvovaginal treatment with DESIRIAL® or similar indication implants (resorbable or slowly resorbable) within 1 year prior to inclusion. She has not undergone vestibular and/or vaginal treatment with non-resorbable implants. She is willing to attend 6 to 8 visits over a period of 11 up to 12 months and undergo the injection of DESIRIAL® or placebo.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She is currently 38 weeks pregnant and is scheduled for a cesarean section due to breech presentation of the baby. She has no significant medical history and does not take any medications. She has had a normal pregnancy with no complications. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. Her prenatal ultrasounds have been normal, and there are no indications of any pelvic abnormalities. She has a supportive partner and is looking forward to the arrival of her baby. She is interested in participating in research studies that may help improve her post-cesarean section recovery and uterine scar healing.

The patient is a 53-year-old man who has been experiencing upper abdominal discomfort for several weeks. He has a history of chronic pancreatitis and was previously diagnosed with a pancreatic pseudocyst. His gastroenterologist has recommended an endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) to determine the extent of the pseudocyst and to evaluate any other potential pancreatic or biliary abnormalities. The patient has never undergone an EUS before and is somewhat anxious about the procedure. He is generally healthy otherwise, with no significant medical history or current medications. He is a nonsmoker and has no allergies. He is employed as a software engineer and is married with two children. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to be randomized to either the conventional or balloon inflated insertion arm.

Patient is a 26-year-old male from the United States who has been diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes for over 7 years. He is currently using an insulin pump and reports performing self-monitoring blood glucose testing at least 4 times daily for the past 6 months. His HbA1c level at screening is 7.2% (55 mmol/mol). He has not been diagnosed with hypoglycemic unawareness and is not currently receiving oral steroid therapy or undergoing dialysis treatment. He has no known allergies to medical grade adhesives and is considered technically capable of using the Abbott Sensor Based Glucose Monitoring System. He has not participated in any other device or drug study that could affect glucose measurements or glucose management. He is not currently using a continuous glucose monitoring device or sensor augmented pump therapy and is not planning to use a CGM device during the study. He is not a pregnant or breastfeeding mother, nor does he have a pacemaker or any other uncontrolled medical condition.

25 yo F, G1P0 at 16 weeks gestation, presenting for routine prenatal care during the COVID-19 pandemic. She has had no complications thus far in her pregnancy and is considered low-risk. Due to the pandemic, her prenatal appointments have been conducted via telemedicine. She reports feeling comfortable with this mode of care but is interested in participating in a study to evaluate the differences in care perception between remote consultations and face-to-face appointments adapted to confinement. She is a member of a social security scheme and is fluent in French. She is willing to complete self-questionnaires and is not opposed to the exploitation of her data. She plans to give birth at the regional academic Maternity of Nancy. Past Medical History: - No significant medical history.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with gallstones and requires surgery to remove her gallbladder. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and has an ASA score of 1. She has scheduled her surgery as an outpatient procedure and is compliant with the pre-surgical fasting rules. However, she reports feeling anxious about the procedure and has difficulty sleeping the night before. On the day of surgery, she arrives at the pre-anesthesia room and undergoes a qualitative and quantitative ultrasound evaluation of her gastric contents. The ultrasound reveals a small amount of fluid in her stomach, which is not considered a full stomach. The anesthetic management proceeds as planned, and the patient is safely discharged home later that day.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy female who works as a teacher. She has no history of cardiovascular or respiratory disease and does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is not taking any medications or herbal supplements. Her BMI is 23.5, and her PFTs results are within the specified limits. She has never participated in any clinical trial before and is willing to follow study procedures and remain in-patient for the entire treatment period. She is not pregnant or lactating and had a negative serum pregnancy test before enrollment. She has no history of allergies or exposure to Technosphere® Inhalation Powder. She is willing to avoid alcohol and strenuous activity 48 hours prior to study enrollment and during the study. She is willing to consume a study-specific diet and remain in a quiet, controlled environment during specific timepoints. Her blood pressure and pulse rate are within normal limits, and she has no history of fainting, unexplained loss of consciousness or convulsions. She has no known risk factors for Torsades de pointes (TdP) and has never experienced cardiac arrhythmia or taken anti-arrhythmia drugs.

A 45-year-old woman has been experiencing heartburn and regurgitation for the past 6 months. She has been taking a daily dose of PPIs for the past 4 weeks but has only experienced partial relief of her symptoms. She reports that her symptoms are worse after eating large meals and when lying down. She denies any history of gastrointestinal surgery, laxative use, or structural abnormalities of the gastrointestinal tract. She is otherwise healthy and takes no other medications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the potential benefits of adding tegaserod to her current PPI therapy to manage her GERD symptoms.

A 58-year-old man with no symptoms came to the clinic for a routine check-up. He has never had a colorectal cancer screening before. His medical history is remarkable for controlled hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He has no family history of colorectal cancer or polyps. He exercises regularly and does not smoke. He is interested in participating in a screening program for colorectal cancer.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea. She reports experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness and loud snoring at night. She has tried using a continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machine in the past but has found it uncomfortable and difficult to use. She currently sleeps in a bedroom with a temperature of approximately 72 degrees Fahrenheit. She has not made any significant changes to her lifestyle or environment to manage her sleep apnea. The patient reports no history of central sleep apnea. She is otherwise healthy and has no significant medical history or comorbidities.

A 40-year-old female patient who has been diagnosed with breast cancer and has completed chemotherapy treatment three months ago. The patient is currently experiencing persistent fatigue that has been ongoing for at least two months after the completion of her chemotherapy treatment. She reports her fatigue level to be at 6/10 on a scale of 1-10, with 10 being the most severe. The patient has no history of anemia or thyroid disorder. She is not currently on any medication for depression, anxiety or pain management. The patient has not had any acupuncture treatment in the past six weeks. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of acupuncture treatment for chronic post-chemotherapy fatigue.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was involved in a car accident and suffered a traumatic head injury. He was brought to the emergency room by ambulance and was immediately assessed by medical personnel. He was unconscious with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 8 and a Kremlin-Bicêtre score (KBS) of 6. The medical personnel recorded the scores on a standardized collection sheet as part of the study. The patient was intubated and transferred to the intensive care unit for further management. At 6 months follow-up, the Glasgow Outcome Scale- Extended will be used to assess the patient's neurological outcome. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and is affiliated with a social security scheme.

A 54-year-old female patient who was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with metastasis to the lungs, liver, and bones. She has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and targeted therapy with no significant improvement in her condition. The patient has been informed about the PEACE study and has given her oral and written consent to participate, including the harvesting of her tumor tissues after her death. The patient has no history of IV drug abuse or high-risk infections. She is currently receiving palliative care and is under the care of a hospice team.

The patient is a 34-year-old woman from Solomon Islands who presents with symptoms of fever, headache, and joint pain. She reports that she has been feeling unwell for the past few days and has noticed a rash on her arms and legs. She has no significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. She lives in a rural area and works as a subsistence farmer. Upon examination, her temperature is 38.5°C and she has tenderness in her joints. She reports no recent travel outside of Solomon Islands. The patient has agreed to participate in the study and sign the informed consent.

28 F with a history of nasal obstruction and dissatisfaction with the appearance of her nose. She underwent rhinoplasty with an open technique on [**2148-05-20**]. She did not have any complications during or immediately after the surgery. She was instructed to use cold gel pads for short-term application group for 4 hours and 20 minutes per hour. She reported experiencing edema and ecchymosis around both eyes and moderate pain on the 1st and 4th hours postoperatively. However, she reported less edema and ecchymosis and lower pain levels on the 2nd day postoperatively. She was followed up regularly and discharged with no further complications. She was invited to participate in a clinical trial investigating the effects of different cold application times on postoperative edema, ecchymosis and pain after rhinoplasty, but was excluded due to not meeting the inclusion criteria.

A 13-month-old boy who received three doses of the new DTPa-HBV-IPV/Hib vaccine at 2, 3 and 4 months of age is being considered for this booster study. The child is in good health and has no known medical conditions. The child's parents are willing to comply with all requirements of the study, including completing the diary cards and returning for follow-up visits. The child has not received any investigational or non-registered product (drug or vaccine) within 30 days preceding the booster dose of study vaccine, nor is any such product planned for use during the study period. The child has not received chronic administration of immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within six months prior to the booster dose. The child has not received any vaccine not foreseen by the study protocol within 30 days prior to vaccination, nor is any such vaccine planned for administration during the study period. The child has not participated in another clinical study within three months prior to enrollment in the present booster study or at any time during the present booster study, in which the subject has been or will be exposed to an investigational or a non-investigational product (pharmaceutical product or device). The child has no evidence of previous or intercurrent diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, poliomyelitis, and Hib vaccination or disease since the conclusion visit of study 113948 (NCT01248884). The child has no serious chronic illness and no confirmed or suspected immunosuppressive or immunodeficient condition based on medical history and physical examination. The child has no history of any reaction or hypersensitivity likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccines, neurological disorders, seizures, immunoglobulins or any blood products within the 3 months preceding the booster dose of study vaccine. The child has not experienced any anaphylactic or other hypersensitivity reaction, encephalopathy, temperature of ≥ 40.0°C (axillary) or 40.5°C (rectal) within 48 hours of vaccination, not due to another identifiable cause, collapse or shock-like state (hypotonic-hyporesponsive episode) within 48 hours of vaccination, persistent, inconsolable crying occurring within 48 hours of vaccination and lasting ≥ 3 hours, or seizures with or without fever occurring within 3 days of vaccination. The child has no acute disease and/or fever at the time of enrollment.

The patient is a 62-year-old postmenopausal woman who was diagnosed with advanced breast cancer two years ago. She received chemotherapy followed by Fulvestrant, which she has been taking for the past 60 days. However, her recent scans showed disease progression, and her oncologist recommended this clinical trial. She has HER2-negative breast cancer and has completed menopause. She has no history of any other malignancy, and her family history is negative for breast cancer. She is in good general health, with an ECOG performance status of 1, and has a life expectancy of more than 6 months. Her blood work is normal, except for a slightly elevated total bilirubin level (1.4 times the upper limit of normal). She has no known allergies to any of the study medications or their analogues. She has no significant medical or psychiatric illness that could interfere with the completion of the study. She is willing to undergo pre- and post-treatment research biopsies to confirm ER/PR/HER2 status, and to provide a baseline specimen for molecular analysis. She is not currently taking any medications that could interfere with MLN9708. She has no evidence of central nervous system involvement, ongoing or active systemic infection, or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions. She has no GI disease or GI procedure that could interfere with oral absorption or tolerance of MLN9708. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits involved.

67 year old woman with a history of glaucoma in both eyes, currently on bimatoprost/timolol ophthalmic solution (Ganfort®) once daily, presenting for a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a new formulation of bimatoprost/timolol ophthalmic solution (formulation A) compared to her current medication. She has no history of eye surgery or laser treatment within the last 6 months and does not require chronic use of any other eye medications. She does not wear contact lenses and has not used oral, intramuscular or intravenous corticosteroids within the last 21 days.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who has been experiencing knock knees for several years. Her parents first noticed her legs starting to curve inward when she was around 7 years old. She has been evaluated by an orthopedic surgeon and has been diagnosed with genu valgus. Despite the use of braces and physical therapy, her condition has not improved. She is still growing, and her parents are concerned that her condition may worsen if left untreated. She has no other medical conditions or past surgeries. She enjoys playing soccer and swimming, but her knock knees have made it difficult for her to participate in these activities. She is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. Her parents are interested in exploring surgical options to correct her knock knees and are willing to consider participating in a clinical trial to compare two surgical techniques.

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a BMI of 32. She has been diagnosed with binge eating disorder (BED) and has been struggling with it for the past 5 years. She has a history of depression and anxiety, for which she takes an antidepressant medication. She is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has regular menstrual cycles. The patient has a stable weight for the past 3 months and exercises moderately for 3 hours per week. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. The patient has no metal implants or non-removable metallic dental retainers. She likes pizza and is willing to consume it during the ad libitum meal. The patient is right-handed, without claustrophobia, and is able to undergo an fMRI scan.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has received a diagnosis of fetal anomaly during her pregnancy. She has decided to undergo termination of pregnancy, and she is scheduled for the procedure at the Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto. She speaks fluent English and is able to read and write in English. She is willing to participate in a study that aims to investigate the impact of a telephone-based support intervention on the long-term well-being of women undergoing termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly. She is not currently seeing a therapist or undergoing psychiatric care, and she meets all of the inclusion criteria for the study. She is willing to complete four questionnaires at the time of induction of labour and be reassessed at 3, 6, and 12 months. She is also willing to participate in biweekly supportive calls for 6 months post-termination.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a history of headaches and dizziness. He was recently diagnosed with a supratentorial brain tumor and is scheduled for elective surgery. He has an American Society of Anesthesiologists-Physical Status (ASA-PS) of II, is 75 kg in weight, and is in generally good health.
