He has no history of respiratory or cardiac dysfunction, renal insufficiency, liver impairment, or bleeding disorders. His Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) is 15. He is able to provide informed consent for participation in the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who works as a construction worker. He has been experiencing intermittent shoulder pain for the past 8 months, which has started to interfere with his work. He has tried over-the-counter pain medications and rest, but the pain persists. He has no history of shoulder injuries or surgeries. He has not seen a healthcare provider for this issue yet. He is a native English speaker and resides within the greater San Francisco area. He has no known cognitive, visual, or auditory impairments. He is not currently pregnant, and he has no history of cancer or neurological disorders. He has no cardiac or respiratory issues that would prevent him from engaging in light to moderate physical activity. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore a digital exercise program as a potential solution for his shoulder pain.

A 42-year-old man complains of hearing difficulties in his left ear. He had a recent ear infection that was treated with antibiotics, but the hearing loss persisted. Upon examination, the clinician noted a grade 2 retraction pocket of the tympanic membrane. The patient reported occasional ear pain and a feeling of fullness in the ear. The patient has no history of craniofacial abnormalities, cholesteatoma, or nasopharyngeal tumors. He has not undergone any previous middle ear surgeries and is not currently using anticoagulant medication. The patient has been referred to the study to evaluate the feasibility of undertaking a UK multi-centre randomized controlled trial of BET for the treatment of moderate (grade 2 or 3) retraction pockets. The study aims to determine if BET can improve symptoms scores, audiometry and otoscopic appearance of Grade 2-3 pars tensa RPs in adult patients with Eustachian Tube dysfunction (ETD).

The patient is a 4-year-old boy scheduled for elective lower abdominal surgery. He is in good health with no known cardiac, pulmonary, or neurological diseases. He has no history of psychiatric illnesses, bleeding disorders, or allergies to local anesthetics. He weighs 18 kg and is within the required weight range for the study. He has never had surgery before and is accompanied by his parents who are willing to consent to the study. The surgery is expected to take approximately 1 hour and the patient is expected to stay in the hospital for 1 day post-surgery.

A 8-year-old boy with a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has difficulty with gross and fine motor skills. His parents report that he has difficulty with social interaction and communication. He attends a special education program at school and has speech and occupational therapy. He has not participated in any organized physical activity program (OPA) previously. His parents are interested in enrolling him in a dance program as they have heard that it might be beneficial for his motor skills and socialization. They are willing to attend weekly dance classes with their son for 10 weeks and participate in surveys and assessments designed to measure the impact of the program on their son's motor skills, ability to succeed in related or divergent goals or tasks, quality of life, adaptive function, and social communication.

27-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a history of an ankle sprain following a fall while playing soccer. He reports severe pain and swelling on the lateral aspect of his right ankle. X-rays reveal a Weber type C fracture with an associated syndesmotic injury. He is referred to the orthopedic surgeon for further management. The patient is otherwise healthy, with no significant past medical history. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He is fluent in English and able to comprehend the study requirements.

55-year-old male who underwent a heart transplant on [**2147-10-1**] due to end-stage heart failure. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. The patient is seropositive for CMV, with positive IgG antibodies against CMV. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an individualized preventive strategy against CMV infection based on the specific basal response of the lymphocytes against CMV (ELISPOT Interferon-γ assay). The patient is able and willing to provide blood samples post-transplant to perform the ELISPOT IFN-γ assay. The patient is not pregnant or breastfeeding and is willing to use effective contraceptive measures during and after the treatment period. The patient has no contraindications for the use of valganciclovir or ganciclovir and is not receiving thymoglobulin as induction therapy.

A 14-year-old active boy who participates in multiple sports including soccer and basketball, presented with a painful right hip after a fall. X-rays revealed an anterior-superior iliac spine (ASIS) avulsion fracture. He has no other medical conditions, and his past medical history is unremarkable. He is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the use of absorbable screws as a new fixation material for ASIS avulsion fractures.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital within 48 hours of the onset of severe abdominal pain. The pain is located in the upper abdomen and radiates to the back. He has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and smoking. Examination reveals tenderness on palpation of the abdomen and abdominal distension. Blood tests show elevated levels of amylase and lipase, confirming the diagnosis of acute pancreatitis. CT scan also confirms the diagnosis and shows mild pancreatic necrosis. The patient has no signs of organ failure at this time. The patient is eligible for this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. The patient is informed about the clinical trial and gives informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 44-year-old woman who is scheduled to undergo an elective laparoscopic surgery for gallbladder removal. She has a history of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) after previous surgeries and is considered at moderate-to-high risk for PONV. She has no known allergies to anesthesia or any medications. She is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history and no current medications. She has not smoked and does not consume alcohol regularly. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for the past 2 years. She has been receiving outpatient treatment with methotrexate for the past 6 months, but has not experienced significant improvement in her symptoms. She reports persistent joint pain and stiffness, especially in her hands and feet, and has difficulty with daily activities such as dressing and cooking. She has not been treated with any other biologic agents or disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) besides methotrexate. She is willing to participate in the study and receive retreatment with MabThera (rituximab) in combination with methotrexate.

The patient is a 9-year-old boy who has been experiencing breathing difficulties during sleep for the past few months. His parents have noticed that he snores loudly and sometimes gasps for air during the night. He has also been feeling tired and irritable during the day, and his school performance has been affected. He has no known medical conditions and is not taking any medications. He has a healthy diet and exercises regularly. He has no history of allergies or asthma. He has had a polysomnography test which confirmed that he has mild obstructive sleep apnea with an AHI of 3/h. He has no malformation syndromes or craniofacial anomalies or neuromuscular disorders. His BMI is 20.2 which is within a healthy range. His parents are interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore the efficacy of intranasal corticosteroids as a non-surgical treatment option for his condition.

A 35-year-old male, who works as a construction worker, presented to the hospital after a fall from a height of 10 feet while working at a construction site. He complains of severe back pain and is unable to move his lower limbs. Upon physical examination, he was found to have a thoracolumbar fracture at the level of T12-L1. He does not have any known medical conditions and is not on any medications. He has no history of allergies to any food or drugs. He does not smoke but drinks alcohol occasionally. He has never had any surgery in the past. MRI and CT scans showed that he had a type A3 fracture according to the AO classification. He has no other injuries except for the thoracolumbar fracture. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is able to consent.

A 28-year-old pregnant woman in her 39th week of gestation presents to the hospital with complaints of painful contractions for the past 8 hours. She is a nulliparous woman with an unremarkable medical history, and her pregnancy has been uncomplicated so far. Her prenatal care has been regular, and all her ultrasound examinations have been normal. On examination, she is found to have mechanical dystocia with the foetus not engaging in the pelvis near full dilation. There are no significant abnormalities in the foetal cardiac rhythm. The patient is able to provide informed consent, and there are no medical contraindications to her undergoing the optimized birthing position intervention.

The patient is a healthy adult between the ages of 18 and 30 with a BMI of 18 to 30 kg/m² and a body weight of at least 50 kg. The patient has no history of bleeding or clotting disorders, arterial or venous thrombosis, liver or renal dysfunction, significant cardiac, vascular, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, endocrine, neurologic, hematologic, rheumatologic, psychiatric, neoplasm, metabolic disturbances, or poor venous access. The patient has normal physical examination, vital signs, 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) and laboratory test results. The patient must not have taken any agents that can potentially increase the risk of bleeding within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug administration. The patient must not have any clinically significant drug or food allergies and must be willing to consume the standardized high-fat breakfast menu provided in the study. Women who are pregnant or who have a history of excessive menstrual bleeding are excluded from the study. The patient must be able to tolerate venipuncture.

The patient is a 45-year-old man diagnosed with invasive thymoma with metastasis. He has previously undergone chemotherapy but it was not effective in treating his cancer. He has measurable disease per RECIST, and the previously radiated area is not the only site of disease. His laboratory data shows that his AST and ALT are within the acceptable range, as well as his total bilirubin, WBC count, ANC, platelets, INR, and aPTT. His urine protein:creatinine ratio is 1.0 at screening. He has no prior history of malignancy in the past 5 years except for basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma of the skin. He has not used an EGFR inhibitor or anti-angiogenic agent before and has not used any investigational agent within 30 days prior to registration for the study protocol. He has no contraindications to the use of erlotinib or bevacizumab as per the package labeling for either product. He has no uncontrolled hypertension, history of unstable angina, myocardial infarction, or congestive heart failure. He has no history of stroke, clinically significant peripheral vascular disease, bleeding diathesis, or coagulopathy. He is not taking drugs known to inhibit platelet function. There is no evidence of central nervous system involvement or brain metastases, and he has not undergone any major surgical procedure or significant traumatic injury within 28 days prior to registration for protocol therapy. There is no anticipation of need for major surgical procedure during the course of the study.

This is a 42-year-old woman who has been on maintenance hemodialysis for the past 3 years due to end-stage renal disease. She has been compliant with her treatment regimen and has not had any major complications. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that seeks to evaluate the feasibility of next-generation algorithms for ultrasound data processing. She is excited about the potential benefits of this technology and is willing to provide written informed consent for participation. She has no anatomical characteristics or comorbid medical conditions that would prevent her from completing the ultrasound scanning using the study device. She is looking forward to contributing to this study and helping to advance medical technology.

The patient is a 92-year-old individual who was recently admitted to the ICU for respiratory distress and sepsis. The patient has a history of congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and hypertension. During the ICU stay, the patient required mechanical ventilation and vasopressor support. After a week, the patient has improved and was successfully extubated. The patient is now being transferred to a step-down unit for further care. The patient has two adult children who are both in their 60s and are actively involved in the patient's care. The family is concerned about the patient's recovery and the potential impact on their own mental health. They are interested in participating in a study that focuses on the impact of critical illness on family/caregivers of very old ICU survivors and how to minimize the stress and anxiety associated with it.

A 28-year-old woman is seeking help for her premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). She is married for 3 years and has no children. She works part-time as a freelance writer and has a history of depression. She has never been diagnosed with any other mental health disorder, and she is not on any medications. She has regular menstrual cycles, lasting 30 days on average. She has never taken any steroid contraceptives. She abstains from alcohol and does not use any illegal drugs. She is willing to participate in the study and keep a daily log of her mood symptoms for 7 consecutive menstrual cycles. She is willing to complete all procedures conducted in each of the three phases of the study. She has no metallic implants, and she is able to give voluntary written informed consent.

A 32 yo F who self-identifies as Hispanic/Latina and owns a smartphone. She is interested in improving her physical activity and walking habits but feels that she lacks social support and finds it challenging to find safe walking areas in her neighborhood. She speaks both English and Spanish fluently and is willing to participate in an online survey and focus groups to provide input on the development of a smartphone app that could help her connect with other Latinas in her community who are also interested in improving their physical activity behaviors. She is open to using the app for a four-week period during the usability testing phase of the study.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is generally healthy and has no chronic diseases. She is currently not pregnant and is not breastfeeding. She has a body weight of 55 kg and a BMI of 21 kg/m2. Her blood pressure during screening tests was within the range of 90 to 139 mmHg for systolic blood pressure and 60 to 89 mmHg for diastolic blood pressure. She does not have any history of gastrointestinal surgery or genetic problems such as galactose intolerance or Lapp lactose deficiency. She does not smoke and does not exceed the alcohol consumption criteria. She has not participated in any bioequivalence tests or received any investigational products within the past 6 months. She is willing to comply with the cautions and agrees to contraception during the participation of the clinical trial.

The patient is a 35 year-old female with a bra cup size of C who recently underwent a diagnostic mammogram due to a lump she felt in her left breast. The mammogram revealed a lesion in the left breast on the craniocaudal view. She has no personal history of breast cancer or breast surgeries. She is not currently breastfeeding and has no known skin rash or nipple discharge. The patient has no physical limitations that would prevent her from lying prone for up to 30 minutes at a time. Her body weight is within the study criteria. She is willing and able to comply with all study procedures and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 45 year old female who has been experiencing chronic lower back pain for the past 6 months. She has no history of cancer or any known pathology in the CNS or thorax. She has recently been referred to a urologist due to recurrent urinary tract infections and is suspected to have urolithiasis. She has no known allergies to iodinated contrast media and her serum creatinine level is within normal limits (0.9 mg/dl). She is willing to provide written informed consent and is in a stable physical condition.

A 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease is seeking a solution for his uncontrolled blood pressure. He has been taking multiple antihypertensive medications, but they have not been effective in regulating his blood pressure. He has a BMI of 30 and is a non-smoker. He has no history of heart disease, stroke, or other significant health issues. He is willing to comply with the study requirements and understands the informed consent process. He is

A 30-year-old woman who recently gave birth to a healthy baby boy is experiencing nipple pain during breastfeeding. She has noticed blistering, redness and cracking on her nipples, which is causing significant discomfort. She speaks and understands English and has access to a telephone. She has no known allergies to lanolin and has no health conditions that may interfere with breastfeeding. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of lanolin for the treatment of nipple pain and to help other breastfeeding women.

A 48-year-old male patient presented to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, abdominal pain, and yellowing of skin and eyes for the past 3 months. He has a history of intravenous drug use for 10 years but has been clean for the past 5 years. He has a past medical history of hepatitis C virus infection for the past 8 years, which he did not receive any treatment for. He denies any history of alcohol use. On examination, his abdomen was tender on palpation and his liver was enlarged. Laboratory tests showed elevated liver enzymes and a positive HCV RNA test. A liver biopsy was performed revealing chronic hepatitis with moderate fibrosis. The patient was started on standard antiviral therapy with peg-interferon plus ribavirin combination therapy. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to analyze the role of biliverdin reductase A (BLVRA) in HCV infected patients prior and during/after standard antiviral therapy in association with viral clearance, disease progression, and treatment response in comparison with healthy subjects.

Patient is a 75-year-old man who is living independently at home. He is able to walk without any assistance but has been experiencing falls recently. He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He does not have any history of terminal illnesses or use of benzodiazepines. He has a Mini-Mental State Examination score according to his schooling. He is willing to participate in the study and provide answers to the questionnaire about his history of falls.

Michael is a 54-year-old man who works as a construction worker. He came to the emergency room with a complaint of chest pain that started 2 hours ago. The pain was described as a squeezing sensation and radiated to his left arm. He also felt lightheaded and short of breath. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He smokes one pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol occasionally. His physical exam revealed tachycardia, blood pressure of 170/100 mmHg, and bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed ST-segment elevation in leads V1 to V4. Michael was diagnosed with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). He was taken immediately to the catheterization laboratory and underwent PPCI. He met the inclusion criteria for this clinical trial and was randomized to the PPCI + RIPC group. He completed the remote ischemic per-conditioning (RIPC) protocol and will be followed up for 6 months to assess the infarct size by contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR).

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who is currently pregnant with her second child. Her first pregnancy was uneventful, and she gave birth via a normal vaginal delivery. However, during her current pregnancy, she was diagnosed with abnormally invasive placenta, which has caused her to experience heavy bleeding and pain. Her obstetrician has recommended that she undergo a hysterectomy procedure to manage the condition. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and is in good overall health, with no history of chronic medical conditions. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs and has not had any previous surgeries. She is married and has a supportive partner who is willing to help her during her recovery.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 5 years ago. He has been on metformin for the past 2 years, with a dose of 2000mg/day, and has been taking sitagliptin 100mg/day for the past 6 months. However, his glycemic control is not optimal with a HbA1c level of 8.5%. He is currently working as an accountant and has a sedentary lifestyle. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. His body mass index (BMI) is 28 kg/m^2. He has no history of any chronic disorder, acute pancreatitis, or any significant cardiovascular event. He has impaired liver function, with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels at 2.2 times the upper normal limit. His estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 80 mL/min/1.73 m^2 per modification of diet in renal disease formula. He has been informed about the trial and is willing to participate.

The patient is a 15-year-old male with a diagnosis of autism. He has a moderate to severe level of irritability, aggression, and self-injury, which interfere with his daily routine and social interactions. He has been taking antipsychotic medications but has not seen significant improvement. He is able to swallow pills and is in overall good physical health. The patient has no prior history of neuroleptic malignant syndrome and is not hypersensitive to paliperidone ER. The patient's mental age is 16 months based on testing. He is post-pubertal and has a Tanner stage of IV. The patient is interested in participating in the study to see if paliperidone ER can help reduce his irritability, aggression, and self-injury.

A 45-year-old female office worker is seeking medical attention for dry eyes. She reports experiencing gritty, burning, or scratchy sensation in her eyes, particularly after prolonged screen time at work. She also reports redness in her eyes and occasional blurred vision. She has a history of using eye drops for dry eye symptoms, but they have not provided significant relief. She is in good health and has no history of ocular infections or surgeries. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is using an acceptable means of birth control. The subject has given her written informed consent for this clinical trial and is willing to participate in the study.

Maria is a 50-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. She will be undergoing an elective laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy to remove the cancer. She has no history of abdominal surgery, pancreatitis, or sphincter of Oddi dysfunction. Maria is willing to undergo pre-operative endoscopy and has consented to the procedure. She has no contraindications to abdominal surgery or general anesthesia. Maria is in good overall health and is excited to participate in the study to help advance medical knowledge and potentially prevent complications from her surgery.

The patient is a 45-year-old male admitted to the intensive care unit due to respiratory failure. The patient has been diagnosed with severe pneumonia and requires mechanical ventilation. The patient has no history of chronic lung disease or immunodeficiency. The patient has a history of smoking and alcohol abuse. The patient has been intubated with an endotracheal tube and is randomized to receive either an endotracheal tube with subglottic suction drainage or a standard endotracheal tube. The patient will be closely monitored for signs of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) and will undergo regular chest radiographs, blood tests and tracheal aspirate cultures. The patient will be followed up until extubation or death.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the ICU following a severe traumatic brain injury sustained in a motor vehicle accident. He was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation for respiratory support due to respiratory failure. He has been on mechanical ventilation for 4 days and is expected to remain on it for at least a few more days. The patient has no significant past medical history and is currently sedated and receiving pain medication. He meets the eligibility criteria for a prospective observational study aimed at detecting patient-ventilator asynchrony in brain-injured patients. The study requires the use of esophageal pressure monitoring in combination with airway pressure and flow waveforms to detect asynchrony. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has given his informed consent.

A 12-year-old boy named Jack has been recently diagnosed with leukemia. He is currently undergoing chemotherapy and is expected to continue treatment for the next 6 months. Jack's parents have expressed concerns about his treatment and the impact it will have on his overall health and well-being. Jack's father works as a software engineer and has expressed interest in using technology to monitor Jack's symptoms and improve his quality of life. Jack is an avid gamer and enjoys spending time on his computer and iPad. He speaks fluent English and is comfortable using electronic devices. Jack's parents are both fluent in English and have agreed to participate in the study. They are excited about the possibility of using technology to help manage Jack's symptoms and improve his overall health outcomes.

A 30-year-old healthy male or female with a body mass index between 18 and 29.9 kg/m2 is eligible for this clinical trial. The patient should not have any clinically symptomatic biochemical or structural abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract and should not have undergone any surgery on the small intestine or colon, excluding appendectomy or cholecystectomy. Additionally, the patient should not have any clinical evidence of significant cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, hematologic, metabolic, endocrine, neurologic, psychiatric disease, or any condition that may interfere with the subject successfully completing the trial or that would present a safety risk. It is essential that the patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of different formulations of AZD1722 while taking Omeprazole.

This is a 65-year-old gentleman who has been experiencing frequent nocturia, waking up to urinate more than twice every night for the past six months. He has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and has been on terazosin therapy for four weeks, but his symptoms have not improved significantly. He reports feeling fatigued during the day due to the lack of good quality sleep. He has no history of bladder tumours, bladder stones, or urethral strictures, and he has normal mobility. He is not on any medications for bladder control or sleep disturbances. He has never had prostate surgery or radiotherapy, nor has he experienced acute urinary retention or used an indwelling catheter. His serum PSA levels are within normal limits. He has not experienced any urinary tract infections in the recent past. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effectiveness of combined alpha-blocker and diuretic therapy for nocturia in men.

This clinical trial is seeking participants who have received a two-dose priming vaccination in a previous phase I trial for an inactivated pandemic influenza (H5N1) vaccine. Participants must be healthy adults who are able to provide legal identification and understand and sign the informed consent. Exclusion criteria include a history of allergic reactions to vaccines or eggs, autoimmune disease or immunodeficiency, uncontrolled hypertension, active or treated malignancy, Guillain-Barre Syndrome, and administration of any other investigational research agents or live attenuated vaccines within 30 days before the dosing. Participants must also not have received any subunit or inactivated vaccines within 14 days before the dosing and not be currently receiving anti-TB prophylaxis or therapy. Any medical, psychiatric, social condition, occupational reason or other responsibility that impairs a volunteer's ability to give informed consent is also a contraindication to protocol participation.

25-year-old male patient with a history of opioid use disorder according to DSM-5 criteria. The patient has been in early abstinence for the past 2 weeks and is currently seeking treatment for his addiction. He reports a history of occasional heroin and prescription opioid use, with a peak of 2 grams of heroin per day for the past 6 months. He has no other serious medical or mental illness, and he is currently not taking any medication. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial investigating the role of repetitive Trans-cranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) in reducing craving among opioid use disorder patients. The patient has no contraindications to rTMS and has not undergone any previous treatment with rTMS.

A 9-year-old male child presented with frequent coughing, fatigue, and loss of appetite. The child's parents reported that he had been experiencing these symptoms for the past 2 weeks. The family recently moved to a new neighborhood, where several cases of tuberculosis (TB) have been reported. The child had not received the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine. Upon physical examination, the child appeared to be in good general health with stable vital signs. Chest auscultation revealed coarse crackles in the left lung. A Mantoux test was performed, and the result was induration of 12 mm. The child was referred to the University Hospital of Siena, where he was enrolled in a clinical trial to evaluate the use of the QuantiFERON-TB Gold In Tube test (QTF-GIT) in the diagnosis of TB in children. The child's parents provided informed consent for their child's participation in the study. The doctor administered a clinical-anamnestic questionnaire to gather information about the child's medical history, including previous vaccination with BCG, and any symptoms suggestive of active TB. Blood samples were taken for routine purposes, and an additional blood sample was taken to run the experimental IGRA test. The child's eligibility for the study was confirmed, and he was enrolled. The aim of the study is to analyze the potential contribution of the IGRA test, QTF-GIT, in the diagnosis of TB (active or latent) in pediatric subjects recently exposed to infection or with clinical suspicion of active TB, and to compare the results obtained with those of the TST, which is the gold standard. The child's participation in the study will help the researchers to evaluate the sensitivity and specificity of the QTF-GIT test in pediatric patients with TB, and to determine if the test can be used together with the TST to improve the diagnosis of TB in children.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with no known medical conditions. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He has a balanced diet and consumes an average of 2000 calories per day. He does not take any dietary supplements or medications. His family history is negative for any chronic diseases. The patient is aware of the study objectives and is willing to participate in the trial. He has no history of renal disease, diabetes mellitus, metabolic diseases, or osteoporosis. The patient is not postmenopausal and is not currently pregnant or lactating. The patient is between 18-60 years of age and is willing to comply with the study requirements, including fasting and consuming the assigned dietary supplement.

28 yo F with C4 spinal cord injury resulting in tetraplegia. Patient has a history of respiratory insufficiency with frequent episodes of shortness of breath and difficulty breathing. Patient has been on a ventilator for several months and has experienced limited success with other therapies. The patient is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the diaphragmatic reinnervation by inferior laryngeal nerve in tetraplegic patients with ventilatory insufficiency. The patient has no history of pacemaker placement and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. The patient is willing to undergo the necessary evaluation and procedures to participate in the study.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy who suffered a moderate traumatic brain injury (TBI) following a fall from a playground swing. He was hospitalized overnight and received medical treatment for his injuries. The parents have noticed changes in his behavior since the injury, including difficulty with impulse control and expressing emotions. The family speaks English and the parents are willing to provide informed consent to participate in the study. The child lives with both parents and has no history of hospitalization for psychiatric problems. He does not have a diagnosis of moderate or severe mental retardation, autism, or a significant developmental disability.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who has a history of asthma for the past 5 years. She has been experiencing episodes of wheezing, coughing, and chest tightness, especially during physical activities and at night. She has been on inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) and a short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) for the past 3 years. Her asthma has been poorly controlled despite being compliant with her medications. She has been missing school days and has had to visit the emergency department several times due to asthma exacerbations. The patient and her parents are interested in participating in the clinical trial to better understand her asthma and to potentially improve her asthma management. The patient is generally healthy and has no other medical conditions. She is active in sports but feels limited by her asthma. She is alert and cooperative during the examination. The lung function test shows a moderate reduction in her forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) and forced vital capacity (FVC). She has no significant past medical history and is not taking any other medications. The patient and her parents are willing to comply with the study requirements and restrictions, including twice-daily peak flow measurements and daily symptom diaries.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who has been diagnosed with arrhythmia and is scheduled for a routine clinical MRI examination. He is currently taking medication for his arrhythmia and has never had any prior heart surgeries. He is an avid runner and enjoys participating in marathons. He is married with two children and works as a software engineer. He has a history of hypertension but it is currently well managed with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no contraindications for MRI examinations and has never had a pacemaker or any ferromagnetic vascular clips. His blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg and his heart rate is 75 beats per minute. He has no other significant medical conditions and is interested in participating in the study to help improve the quality of MRI imaging for patients with arrhythmia.

A 45-year-old male with a history of stage IV non-small cell lung cancer presents with a new metastatic lesion in the liver. He has previously received multiple lines of chemotherapy and radiation therapy with no significant response. His ECOG performance status is 1, and he has no history of brain metastases or other significant comorbidities. He has no contraindications for intra-tumoral injections or immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. His laboratory values are within normal limits, including creatinine, liver function tests, and blood counts. He is willing to provide a signed informed consent and agrees to use two forms of contraception throughout the study. He is eligible for the study as he has refractory malignancy and meets the inclusion criteria for the study. He will undergo pre-treatment screening radiographic tumor assessments within 30 days prior to the initial dose.

This clinical trial is not suitable for patient recruitment as it is a post market clinical follow-up study for patients who have already undergone primary Total Hip Arthroscopy with MicroPort Orthopedics or Wright Medical Technology femoral stem and PROCOTYL C Acetabular Components implanted. Therefore, there is no need for patient recruitment.

The patient is a 27-year-old female of Hispanic ethnicity. She is in good general health with a BMI of 22. She is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She has no history of drug allergies or any significant medical conditions. She has been on oral contraceptives for the past 6 months and reports regular menstrual cycles. She consumes a balanced diet and exercises regularly. The patient has not ingested any alcoholic or caffeine-containing food or beverage within the last 48 hours. Her laboratory evaluation, including a urine drug screen, was negative. The patient has no history of depression, mania, seizure, narrow-angle glaucoma, or suicidal ideation or behavior. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and has no difficulty swallowing.

A 42-year-old male office worker with a history of chronic low back pain for the past 8 months that has not responded to over-the-counter pain relievers presents to a physical therapy clinic. The pain is mostly located in the lower lumbar region with occasional radiation to the right buttock. MRI of the lumbar spine was performed and ruled out any structural deformities or disc herniation. The patient has not received any physiotherapy sessions in the last 6 months. The pain is aggravated by prolonged sitting and relieved by walking. The patient has no history of spinal surgery, fibromyalgia, or pregnancy. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of dry needling technique on the hamstrings muscle to improve low back pain.

A 30-year-old male patient is scheduled for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy due to recurrent biliary colic. He has no significant past medical history, no allergies, and is a non-smoker. His vitals are stable, and he has a BMI of 25. The preoperative airway assessment revealed a Mallampati class II airway, and there are no other known anatomical concerns. The patient has no history of hypertension, poor dentition, symptomatic gastro-esophageal reflux or cervical spine instability. The patient has been informed about the trial, and he has provided written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 30 year old male who works in a factory and has been exposed to individuals with tuberculosis. He presents to the clinic with a history of coughing and fever for the past two weeks. He has a history of smoking 1 pack of cigarettes per day for the past 10 years. He has never been diagnosed with tuberculosis, but his skin test of Tuberculin Pure Protein Derivative (TB-PPD) is strongly positive (the average diameter of PPD skin test induration is greater than or equal to 15mm and/or local blisters, necrosis). He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to prevent tuberculosis. He has no significant past medical history, and he is not currently taking any medications. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and is willing to sign the informed consent. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the clinical trial protocol and be followed.

Pt is a 32-year-old male with a 10-year history of refractory epilepsy, diagnosed with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE). The patient has tried multiple antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) at recommended dosages but has failed to achieve adequate seizure control. The patient experiences an average of 4 seizure-days per month, which are disabling complex partial seizures with or without secondary generalization. The patient has a global IQ of 90 and is able to complete self-administered questionnaires. The patient has a reliable collateral historian and has expressed a preference for non-resective surgery. The patient is willing and able to give written informed consent. MRI shows evidence of epileptogenic lesions within the mesial temporal region, and there are no brain lesions that preclude electrode implantation. The patient does not have any progressive neurological disorders or medical or psychiatric conditions that would preclude surgery or interfere with adherence to treatment and follow-up. The patient is not planning a pregnancy during the study and is not currently participating in other studies of new epilepsy therapies. The patient does not have any contraindications for stereotactic surgery.

A 29-year-old woman with a history of severe asthma and frequent exacerbations despite the use of high-dose inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) is being considered for a clinical trial. She has been taking an additional controller medication (LABA) for the past 6 months. She has a history of eosinophilic asthma and had two or more exacerbations requiring treatment with systemic Corticosteroid (CS) in the last year. She is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol or use illicit drugs. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She is willing to commit to consistent and correct use of an acceptable method of birth control for the duration of the trial and for 4 months after the last study drug administration. She has not participated in any study with mepolizumab and received investigational product (including placebo). She is able to give written informed consent and to comply with the requirements and restrictions listed in the consent form and in the protocol. She is able to read, comprehend, and write at a level sufficient to complete study related materials. She is not suffering from any known clinical conditions other than asthma.

The patient is a 40-year-old man diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. He has undergone two rounds of chemotherapy, but the cancer has persisted. He is currently in remission but is at high risk of relapse. He has no significant past medical history and is not taking any medications. His vital signs are stable, and he has no signs of organ dysfunction. He is compliant with medical treatment and has a strong support system. He has given written informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. He is willing to be randomized to either the BeEAM or BEAM regimen for conditioning treatment before autologous stem cell transplantation. He understands the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to undergo the necessary tests and follow-up appointments.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been recently diagnosed with pelvic organ prolapse. She complains of a feeling of "heaviness" in her lower abdomen and lower back pain. She underwent a pelvic exam and was found to have a uterine prolapse. She was advised to undergo vaginal surgery to correct the prolapse. She has no significant past medical history and has never had any major abdominal surgeries. She is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. She is menopausal and has not undergone hormone replacement therapy. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to determine if a cleansing enema before the surgery can prevent complications.

A 45-year-old male with a BMI of 38 kg/m2 is scheduled for endoscopic gastric bypass surgery. He has a past medical history of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea. He is currently taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. The patient reports occasional alcohol use but denies any drug use. He has no known allergies to medications. He is not currently pregnant or nursing. His most recent blood work was completed within the last 6 weeks and showed no significant abnormalities.

A 61-year-old male diagnosed with multiple myeloma presented with measurable secretory disease and documented disease progression after at least one prior line of therapy. The patient has an ECOG performance status score of 2, adequate bone marrow, liver, and renal function. The patient has not received prior treatment with bortezomib, is refractory to high-dose dexamethasone, and has no grade 2 peripheral neuropathy. The patient has not received an allogeneic bone marrow or allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplant and has no prior or current malignancy except for multiple myeloma.

A 45-year-old woman came to the clinic for further evaluation of a suspicious breast abnormality detected on mammography. She has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother being diagnosed at the age of 55. She is currently on hormone replacement therapy for menopausal symptoms. The mammogram revealed a suspicious lesion measuring 1.2 cm in diameter, with irregular margins and microcalcifications. The biopsy is required to determine whether the lesion is cancerous or not. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent form. She has no history of breast implants or recent breast surgery, and her blood glucose level is below 140 mg/dl.

54 yo female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presents with decreased vision in both eyes for the past 6 months. She has no history of ocular surgery or trauma. Fundus exam revealed bilateral diabetic macular edema with moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Her best corrected visual acuity was 20/80 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye. The patient is interested in participating in clinical research studies to help advance the diagnosis and treatment of ocular diseases. She gives written informed consent and is eligible for the study.

A 45-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in accelerated phase despite previous treatments with imatinib, dasatinib, and nilotinib. She has also developed the T315I mutation after these therapies. She has failed all available treatment options and is seeking alternative treatment options. The patient is willing to participate in this expanded access program of ponatinib that may provide a new option for her. The patient is in overall good health and has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1. She understands the risks associated with the trial and is willing to provide written informed consent. She is not currently eligible for any ongoing clinical trials of ponatinib and is not taking any immunosuppressive agents. The patient has no history of significant cardiovascular disease, pancreatitis, or alcohol abuse. Her liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. The patient is not pregnant or lactating and agrees to use effective contraception during the trial. She has undergone no major surgery within 14 days prior to the first dose of ponatinib and has no ongoing or active infections. The patient is hopeful that this trial will provide a new treatment option for her and improve her overall quality of life.

A 30-year-old woman who leads a sedentary lifestyle and is interested in exploring alternative methods to improve her mental and physical health. She has a history of mild depression and anxiety, but is not currently on any medication. She has no significant medical history and her body mass index is within normal range. She has never practiced yoga before and is not pregnant or nursing. She is willing to commit to attending twice weekly, 60-minute yoga sessions for eight weeks.

The patient is an asymptomatic adult between the ages of 21 and 50 living in or near Worcester, Western Cape, South Africa. The patient has no evidence of past or present TB infection or disease and no clinically significant findings from a recent chest x-ray. The patient is willing to undergo an HIV test and has a CD4 count greater than 300 with no history of AIDS-def

A 60-year-old Caucasian male with a history of cataract surgery on both eyes presents with visual distortions. He reports seeing halos around lights and difficulty with night vision. He wears glasses for reading and driving. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He has no history of ocular pathology other than regular corneal astigmatism. He is fluent in English and is able to read and write. He is willing to comply with examination procedures and study visits. He signs informed consent and HIPAA authorization. His current medication list includes lisinopril and atorvastatin. His best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes. His corneal astigmatism is 1.5 diopters.

Patient is a 42yo male with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obesity. He presents with severe dyspnea and shortness of breath, which has been progressively worsening over the last few months. His body mass index (BMI) is 37, and he reports difficulty with mobility and daily activities. The patient has no contraindications to weight loss or unsupervised exercise. He has not participated in any structured diet or exercise program in the past. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided signed informed consent.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who has recently been diagnosed with thyroid cancer through a preoperative fine needle biopsy. She speaks fluent English and is scheduled to undergo surgical excision of the cancer. She has not had any prior thyroid surgery, radiation treatment or chemotherapy. She is mentally and physically capable of providing informed consent and participating in the study. Her input will help us to better understand the expectations of patients undergoing surgery for thyroid cancer and improve patient education and preparation for the procedure.

A 35-year-old woman from Pierce County, Washington, who is currently working as a software engineer is interested in participating in a clinical trial to reduce the risk of breast cancer. She has no history of breast cancer, and her family history is negative for any cancer. Her menstrual cycle is regular, and she is not using any oral contraceptives or any other sex hormones for the past 3 months. She exercises regularly for at least 30 minutes every day, and her alcohol intake is limited to 1 drink per week. She does not smoke or use any tobacco products. She has no history of diabetes, hypertension, or any other chronic medical conditions. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to contribute to breast cancer research and learn more about the benefits of exercise in reducing the risk of breast cancer.

A 30-year-old Japanese female, who is a non-smoker, with a BMI of 23.5, and no significant medical history, has shown interest in participating in a clinical trial for a new medication. She has lived outside of Japan for less than five years and holds a Japanese passport, with all four grandparents being Japanese, as confirmed by interview. She is currently not taking any prescription medications, and her vital signs, physical examination, and lung function measurements are within normal limits. She has a negative serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin at screening and a negative urine pregnancy test at Day -1 prior to the first drug administration. She has agreed not to donate ova from the time of the first administration of study medication until three months after the end of the systemic exposure of the study drug or until the last follow-up visit, whichever occurs later. She is willing and able to adhere to the prohibitions and restrictions specified in the protocol and to comply with the correct use of the devices specified in the protocol. She has no history of asthma, COPD, or any other chronic pulmonary disease or condition. She has no known intolerance/hypersensitivity to any of the excipients/components contained in any of the formulations used in the trial. She is not a heavy caffeine drinker and has not had any bacterial or viral respiratory tract, sinus, or middle ear infection affecting her health status within four weeks prior to randomization. She has no abnormalities on vital signs, ECG, physical examination, or laboratory evaluation of blood and urine samples that the investigator judges as likely to interfere with the study or pose an additional risk in participating.

A 32 year old woman and her partner have been trying to conceive for over two years. They have been diagnosed with unexplained infertility and have been recommended to undergo ART with their own gametes. The woman is a normoresponder and will have ovulation triggered with an intramuscular injection of 10000 IU of HCG. They have at least one good embryo available for transfer. The couple has opted for the long GnRH agonist and GnRH antagonist protocol. The woman will receive routine luteal phase support with progesterone and estradiol valerate, and will also receive two doses of GnRH agonist on the fifth and tenth day after embryo transfer. The woman is under 38 years old and is not considered a high or poor responder. They are hopeful that this trial will increase their chances of a successful live birth.

A 35-year-old female works as a software engineer and lives a sedentary lifestyle. She has a normal BMI and a history of mild gastrointestinal issues such as occasional bloating and constipation. She has tried over-the-counter remedies with little success. She does not have any significant medical history or allergies. She is not a smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. She is currently not on any medications or supplements. She is willing to participate in the study and maintain her physical activity patterns, body weight, supplements/medications, sleep patterns, and habitual diet throughout the trial. She has internet access via computer, phone, or other devices and is able to maintain internet access throughout the trial in order to complete online daily questionnaires. She understands the study procedures and signs forms providing informed consent to participate in the study. She is not pregnant or planning to be pregnant during the study period and is willing to commit to the use of a medically approved form of contraception throughout the study period.

42 yo M with known CAD and previous PCI (LAD stent in 2018) presents for elective PCI of the RCA. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and is currently taking aspirin and atorvastatin. Echocardiogram shows an EF of 45%. The patient is evaluated by the interventional cardiology team and deemed to be at high risk for PCI due to the complexity of the lesion and the patient's underlying cardiac disease. The team decides to use the Impella® Hemodynamics Platform to monitor hemodynamic parameters during the procedure. The patient has no contraindications for the device and provides informed consent to participate in the study. The patient is scheduled for the procedure and will be monitored closely for any adverse events. Past Medical History: - Coronary artery disease with previous PCI (LAD stent in 2018) - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - EF 45% - No history of cardiogenic shock or systemic infection - No known contraindications to heparin, pork, pork products, or contrast media

The patient is a 70-year-old woman who has recently fallen and fractured her femur. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, which are all well-controlled with medications. She has no history of cardiac or pulmonary disease, and she is a non-smoker. She is currently living independently at home and is able to perform all activities of daily living without assistance. She is scheduled to undergo surgery to repair her fracture, and she has been informed that she will be participating in a clinical trial to observe hemodynamic changes and tissue perfusion intra-operatively. She has been informed that she will be monitored with non-invasive cardiac output measurement (NICOM) and non-invasive transcutaneous near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) to observe her hemodynamic changes and tissue perfusion. She has been told that she will also be asked to complete a questionnaire about her quality of life 2 months after her surgery. She has no known allergies to the NIRS patches or NICOM electrodes, and she has no skin lesions over the areas where they will be attached. She has been informed that her participation in the trial will not affect the standard of care she receives during her surgery and recovery.

A 35-year-old male with a diagnosis of schizophrenia who was recently discharged from Rambam Medical Health Center's psychiatric inpatient services is eligible for this clinical trial. He lives alone and has a history of medication non-compliance. He has been hospitalized twice in the past year due to relapses and has difficulty managing his symptoms on his own. He is currently taking antipsychotic medication but has expressed concerns about side effects and the long-term use of medication. He is willing to participate in a psycho-educational group intervention to learn more about his illness and how to manage it effectively. He has no other medical conditions and is able to provide informed consent.

A 29-year-old first-time mother gave birth to a healthy neonate at 39 weeks gestation. The baby weighed 3.1 kg and had an Apgar score of 9 at 10 minutes. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy and delivery. She is currently breastfeeding her newborn and is concerned about her own health during the postpartum period. She reported feeling anxious and stressed since becoming a mother. She is experiencing sleep deprivation due to the infant's feeding schedule and is having difficulty adjusting to her new role as a parent. She has no history of psychiatric illness. She is married and has a supportive husband who helps with household chores and taking care of the baby. She is not taking any medications or supplements. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates whether probiotics use in neonates and infants can improve their mother's life quality.

The patient is a 29-year-old Hispanic woman who is currently 8 weeks pregnant with her second child. She has completed high school and has basic literacy in English. She works part-time at a retail store and lives with her husband and 3-year-old daughter. She has no significant medical history and takes no medications. She has never used any form of contraception and reports that her current pregnancy was not planned. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 63-year-old female who was recently diagnosed with disseminated bladder cancer. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. She reports experiencing fatigue and weakness in her muscles, particularly in her legs, over the past few months. She has lost some weight unintentionally and has noticed a decrease in her appetite. She is currently undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy for localized disease, and her treatment plan also includes chemotherapy and immunotherapy for disseminated disease. Her ECOG performance status is 2. She has provided informed consent to participate in the study.

Pt is a premature infant born at 29 weeks gestation and is currently in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The infant is less than 2 months old and is expected to survive for more than 3 days. The infant does not have any congenital anomalies or genetic disorders that are incompatible with life. The infant has no central intravenous lines in place and does not require any seizure medication, hypertension medication or respiratory support greater than nasal canulae or nasal continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP). The infant has not been diagnosed with any infections and is not receiving treatment for pain control. The parents or guardians of the infant have provided informed consent for the infant to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes. He has been taking oral hypoglycemic medication and has controlled his HbA1c levels between 6%-7%. However, he has been experiencing symptoms of diabetic peripheral neuropathy, including numbness, tingling, and burning sensations in his feet. He has not been taking any antioxidant supplements or anti-inflammatory medicines. He is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding and has no plans to do so during the study. He has no history of cancer or hypersensitivity to N-acetylcysteine. He has provided written informed consent to participate in the study.

45-year-old female with a recent diagnosis of metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. The patient has no history of systemic antitumor therapy for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and has an ECOG performance status of 1. She has no known central nervous system disease and has adequate hematologic and organ function. The patient has measurable disease according to RECIST v1.1 and no history of interstitial pneumonitis or autoimmune disease. She has not received any systemic immunostimulatory agents in the last 4 weeks or any systemic immunosuppressive medications in the last 2 weeks. The patient is not pregnant or lactating, and has no history of allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplantation. She does not have active hepatitis B or hepatitis C, or any serious bleeding events. The patient has no uncontrolled pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, or peripheral neuropathy grade ≥2. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatments for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been suffering from bunion pain for several years. She has tried various conservative treatments like shoe inserts, physical therapy, and pain medications with little improvement. After consulting with her podiatrist, she has decided to undergo bunionectomy surgery to relieve the pain. She is otherwise healthy, with no history of substance abuse or significant medical conditions. She has no known allergies to any medications, and her lab results are within normal limits. After the surgery, she experiences moderate to severe pain despite the use of pain medications. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of XP20B in relieving her pain.

An 68-year old retired teacher has been having memory problems and difficulty in performing daily activities for the past year. The patient's wife noticed significant changes in his behavior and cognitive function. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. The patient is on lisinopril and atorvastatin. He has a BMI of 27. His physical exam is unremarkable. His MMSE score is 22. He has difficulty with naming objects and recalling recent events. The patient is able to perform simple tasks such as tying his shoes and buttoning his shirt, but he has difficulty with complex tasks like preparing meals. The patient is motivated to participate in this trial and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is an 18-year-old male who recently graduated from high school and is preparing to attend a large university in the fall. He is currently living with his parents in a suburban area and is very close with his family. He is an only child and enjoys spending time with his friends, playing video games, and watching sports. He has experimented with alcohol in the past but has never had more than a few drinks at a time. He is excited about the social opportunities that college will bring but is also nervous about the increased freedom and responsibility. He is looking for ways to stay safe while still having fun in college. He is in good health and has no significant medical or psychiatric history. His BMI is within the normal range and he does not smoke. He is willing to participate in the study and is looking forward to learning more about how to stay safe and healthy in college.

The patient is a 45 year old female who was recently diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. She has been admitted to the hospital for her first month of treatment after her diagnosis. She is fluent in French and has signed the informed consent to participate in the pilot study. She has no history of psychiatric disorders or any other conditions that would exclude her from participating. The patient is interested in exploring the spiritual dimension of her illness and is willing to participate in the three intervention interviews. She will complete the quality of life and spiritual well-being scales at the beginning and end of the study.

John is a 56-year-old man who has been diagnosed with heart failure. He was admitted to the hospital after experiencing shortness of breath and difficulty breathing. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes. He is taking several medications including lisinopril, atorvastatin, and metformin. His physical examination shows that he has an elevated jugular venous pressure (JVP) and bilateral crackles in his lungs. His echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 35%, indicating reduced cardiac function. He has been scheduled for a right heart catheterization to evaluate his pulmonary artery pressures and to determine if he needs additional diuretic therapy. He has no history of neck surgery, and his neck is free of any scars or bruising. He has no upper torso central venous catheterization such as a PICC line or dialysis catheter.

Maria is a 28 year old woman who has been experiencing episodes of unexpected strokes. She has a family history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her past medical history includes episodes of renal colic and urinary tract infections. She has never been diagnosed with any chronic disease. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Her lab work is normal except for mild proteinuria. She has been referred to a neurologist for further evaluation. The neurologist suspects that there may be an underlying genetic condition causing her strokes and recommends genetic testing. The genetic testing reveals that she has Fabry disease. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to further understand the disease and contribute to the development of more effective treatments.

The patient is a 30-year-old male who is in good health and has no significant medical history. He works as an accountant and enjoys playing sports in his free time. He does not smoke or use drugs and only drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to medications or other substances. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for Xanax extended-release tablets and is willing to follow all study procedures and requirements. He has provided informed consent and is excited to contribute to medical research.

63 yo M diagnosed with prostate cancer and scheduled to receive radiation therapy for at least five weeks. Patient is fluent in Swedish and has a history of actively managing his health, including monitoring symptoms and seeking medical advice when necessary. The patient has no known severe cognitive impairment and is able to use a smartphone or tablet. The patient is interested in participating in the trial and contributing to the development of innovative healthcare technologies. Past Medical History: - Hypertension - Hyperlipidemia - Type 2 Diabetes - History of smoking (quit 5 years ago) - No history of cognitive impairment

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that cannot be removed surgically. She has a history of liver cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis B infection. She presents with abdominal pain, fatigue, and weight loss. She underwent a liver biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of HCC. Her alpha-fetoprotein level is 950 ng/mL. She has not received any prior chemotherapy for her HCC. Her performance status is Zubrod 1. Her laboratory values reveal a granulocyte count of 2800/mm3, hemoglobin level of 12 gm/dL, platelet count of 80,000/mm3, and serum bilirubin level of 1.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal. She has adequate renal function with a calculated creatinine clearance of 80. She does not have any active or uncontrolled infections. She is not pregnant or breastfeeding. She has agreed to use an effective contraceptive method. She is willing to have a 20cc blood sample drawn with each cycle of chemotherapy.

The patient is a 57 year old man diagnosed with an advanced stage of pancreatic cancer. The tumor is unresectable and has metastasized to the liver. He has already received chemotherapy and radiotherapy but there is no evidence of disease regression. The patient is experiencing severe cancer-related pain and is currently taking opioids to manage it. He has no other significant medical history and his performance status is 1. He is married and has two adult children. He works as an accountant and currently on disability leave due to his illness. He is an ex-smoker with a 30 pack-year history and has quit smoking since his diagnosis. His BMI is 28 with blood pressure of 130/80. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has signed the informed consent document.

54-year-old female with a 6-year history of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), despite treatment with methotrexate (MTX) at a stable dose of 15mg/week for the past 4 months. The patient reports persistent joint pain and stiffness in both hands, wrists, elbows, knees, and ankles, with swelling and tenderness in 7 out of the 66 joints counted. Recent laboratory tests revealed a serum CRP level of 1.5mg/dL. She has never received any biological agents or DMARDs other than MTX. She is currently taking ibuprofen 400mg/day for pain relief. She denies any history of allergies or significant medical problems other than RA. The patient is post-menopausal and has been using a copper intrauterine device for contraception. The patient is willing and able to comply with the study requirements and has provided informed consent.

A 35-year-old male patient presented to the dental clinic with localized pain in the lower left jaw following extraction of a molar tooth. The pain started 3 days ago and has been getting worse. The patient reported no previous extraction complications, no history of smoking, and denies any allergies or hypersensitivity to medications. The patient is not taking any medications and has no significant medical history. The examination revealed localized inflammation, erythema, and tenderness in the extraction site. The patient's VAS score was 70mm. The diagnosis of alveolar osteitis was made, and the patient was offered to participate in a clinical trial for a new treatment option, which he agreed to.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who underwent a bunionectomy procedure under regional anesthesia and propofol sedation. She reports moderate to severe pain, with a pain intensity score of 60 mm on the 100 mm visual analog scale (VAS) and moderate pain intensity per the categorical pain intensity scale. She has no known drug allergies to hydrocodone or acetaminophen. Her past medical history is unremarkable, and she has no history of drug or alcohol abuse/addiction. She is in general good health and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is willing to participate in the study and follow the protocol requirements.

The patient is a 16-year-old female with a history of metastatic refractory osteosarcoma. She has previously received standard front-line treatment, which included multi-agent chemotherapy and surgical resection of the primary lesion. However, despite treatment, the disease has progressed and she now has multiple metastases to the lungs and bone. She is experiencing significant pain and discomfort and has no known curative therapy. The patient has a Karnofsky performance level of 60% and has been relatively stable on her current pain management regimen. She has adequate organ and marrow function and has recovered from the acute clinically significant toxic effects of prior anti-cancer therapy. She has measurable disease, including elevated tumor markers and multiple lung nodules confirmed by imaging. The patient and her parents have been informed of the investigational nature of the trial and the potential risks and benefits of participating. They have signed a written informed consent, and the patient has agreed to use hormonal birth control to avoid pregnancy during the study and for 100 days after discontinuation of study treatment. The patient has been cleared by a pregnancy test within 72 hours of starting the study. She is eligible for enrollment in the trial and will be closely monitored for safety and efficacy during the course of the study.

A 16-year-old male high school student who has been experiencing seasonal allergic rhinitis symptoms for the past few years, with worsening symptoms during the fall months. He reports sneezing, nasal congestion and itching, runny nose and itchy, watery eyes, which have been interfering with his school work and sports activities. He has tried over-the-counter antihistamines in the past with minimal relief. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new investigational nasal spray to see if it can provide faster relief for his symptoms. He is able to read, write and speak English fluently, and he understands the study procedures and is willing to comply with them.

For healthy male and female subjects, the patient is between the ages of 18 and 45, with a BMI between 18 and 30 kg/m2, and weighs at least 50 kg and no more than 100 kg. The patient must not have any clinically significant disease or disorder that may put them at risk for participation in the study or interfere with the study's results. Females must have a negative pregnancy test, must not be lactating, and must be of non-childbearing potential.   For COPD patients, the patient is over 40 years old, with a BMI between 18 and 32 kg/m2, and weighs at least 50 kg and no more than 100 kg. The patient must have a diagnosis of COPD and no other clinically significant disease or disorder that may put them at risk for participation in the study or interfere with the study's results. Females must have a negative pregnancy test, must not be lactating, and must be of non-childbearing potential, as described in the inclusion criteria.

A 54-year-old man with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 5 years has been taking pioglitazone alone for the past 12 weeks. His HbA1c is 8.5% and his BMI is 30 kg/m². He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet plan. He has no history of alcohol or drug abuse, and he has not participated in any clinical trials with an investigational drug in the last 30 days. He has not had any bariatric surgery or gastrointestinal surgeries that induce chronic malabsorption. He has never been diagnosed with cancer or received treatment for cancer. He has no liver disease, impaired renal function, or blood dyscrasias. He has not taken any anti-obesity drugs or systemic steroids at the time of informed consent. He is not premenopausal, nursing, or pregnant. He has agreed to practice an acceptable method of birth control and to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial. He has given signed and dated written informed consent in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation.

A 58-year-old man was diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer and has undergone first-line chemotherapy with good response according to the Recist criteria V1.1. His disease-free survival is less than 10 months, and CT scan evaluation confirmed disease progression. He has signed written informed consent and is eligible for cohort B in the study of genetic and cellular immunological parameters predictive of disease-free survival in patients with metastatic cancer. The patient has no other medical or psychiatric conditions that would make him inappropriate for the study. He is not under guardianship, curator, or under the protection of justice.

A 54-year-old African American man has been HIV-positive for the past 15 years. He has been visiting the Pharmacology/Aging Clinic at Chelsea and Westminster Hospital for regular check-ups and has been managed well on his antiretroviral therapy. He has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled by medication. He is a non-smoker and has a balanced diet. He is interested in participating in this clinical trial as he wants to contribute to the improvement of HIV management for aging patients. He has read and understood the information leaflet provided to him and has signed the informed consent form. He is willing to attend the clinical visits scheduled approximately once a year and to have additional visits if necessary for proper follow-up. He is also willing to have his clinical details marked to show his agreement for their use in this research study.

The patient is a 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with cataracts in both eyes. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. She takes medications for both conditions and they are well-controlled. She is currently on no other medications. She has no allergies to local anesthetics and is able to understand and follow instructions in the language used in the study. She has been recommended to undergo cataract surgery by phacoemulsification and is willing to participate in this clinical trial. Her ASA classification is II.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease stage 3, with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 35 ml/min. He has been diagnosed with anemia and has received treatment with subcutaneous erythropoietin injections in the past, but the therapy was not effective in maintaining his hemoglobin levels to the desired level. He has not received any erythropoietin therapy for the past 6 weeks. He is otherwise healthy and takes medications for his hypertension. He is married and has two children. He is a non-smoker, but drinks alcohol occasionally. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the safety and efficacy of sustained erythropoietin therapy using EPODURE Biopump.
