The patient is a 65 year-old man who has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer after undergoing a prostate biopsy. The biopsy revealed adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 7 (4+3) involving 3 out of 12 cores with a maximum percentage of 60%. His PSA level at diagnosis was 7.5 ng/ml. He has no known history of prostate cancer in his family. He has no other significant medical history and takes no medications. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 0-1. He is willing to undergo any treatment option that is recommended by his healthcare provider.

A 2-year-old male child weighing 12 kg presents to the pediatric emergency department with a rectal temperature of 39°C. The child is accompanied by his parents who report that he has been feeling unwell for the last 24 hours with intermittent fever. The child has no significant past medical history and is up to date on all his immunizations. On examination, the child appears mildly dehydrated, but otherwise, there are no other significant findings. The child is able to take oral medications but has had a few episodes of vomiting in the last 24 hours. The parents are concerned about the child's fever and have no preference for oral versus rectal administration of medication. They have given acetaminophen 4 hours ago, but the fever has not subsided. The child has not received ibuprofen in the last 6 hours. The parents are willing to give informed consent for the child's participation in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with breast cancer. She is scheduled for the insertion of a long-lasting intravenous device under local anesthesia. The patient reports feeling anxious about the procedure and has a history of anxiety disorders. She is currently taking sertraline for anxiety and depression. The patient's medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with lisinopril. She denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse. The patient is not pregnant and does not have any known allergies to medications. She is willing to participate in the study and understands the risks and benefits of the trial.

Patient A is a 55-year-old male who was diagnosed with liver cancer after experiencing right upper quadrant abdominal pain and jaundice. He has a history of alcohol abuse and hepatitis B. Imaging studies showed a 6 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver and multiple small lesions in both lobes of the liver. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. He has no history of prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease or exposure to systemic doxorubicin administered intravenously. He has completed loco regional therapy more than 4 weeks prior to registration. He has no CNS tumors or clinically significant gastrointestinal bleeding events requiring intervention within the past 30 days. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and is well controlled. His ECOG performance status is 1. His laboratory values are within the required range: granulocytes >= 1,500/uL, hemoglobin >= 8.5 g/dL, platelets >= 75,000/uL, creatinine =< 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN), bilirubin =< 3 mg/dL, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) =< 5 x ULN, and prothrombin time (PT)-international normalized ratio (INR) =< 1.7. The patient has signed a written informed consent and is willing to participate in the study.

A 56-year-old man comes to the clinic with complaints of severe pain and cramping in his left leg that started two months ago. He also reports that his left foot is constantly cold and he has noticed a lack of hair growth on his leg. The patient has a history of smoking and diabetes. Upon examination, the patient has decreased pulses in his left foot and a non-healing ulcer on his left heel. CT angiography showed that the patient has critical limb ischemia and is not a candidate for surgical or endovascular intervention. The patient has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of local intramuscular administration of autologous selected CD 133+ cells in patients suffering from CLI. The trial aims to assess the feasibility and efficacy of local intramuscular administration of autologous selected CD 133+ cells in patients suffering from CLI. The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria. The patient will undergo routine physical and instrumental examination including electrocardiogram, chest X-ray, and blood sample analysis. The patient will also undergo contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) imaging to evaluate regional blood flow (RBF) and volume (RBV) and a marrow stimulation procedure with human recombinant granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (rhGCSF) to mobilize CD133+ cells from the peripheral blood

52 year old woman with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 presents with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus for the past 6 years. She has been on multiple oral hypoglycemic agents, including metformin, sulfonylureas, and DPP-4 inhibitors, but her glycemic control remains uncontrolled with HbA1c of 9.2%. She has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea. She has been considering bariatric surgery for weight loss and glycemic control. She is a non-smoker and has no relevant family history of diabetes or cardiovascular disease. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effect of gastric bypass surgery on beta cell function and cardiovascular parameters.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who underwent ventral hernia repair surgery. She has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. She has no known allergies and is not currently taking any other medications. She reports no complications after the surgery and has been following up with her doctor regularly. She has given consent for her medical records to be included in the Danish Ventral Hernia Database and for the use of her data in this clinical trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who presented to the emergency department with chest pain, shortness of breath, and palpitations. The patient has no significant past medical history and is otherwise healthy. Physical examination revealed an irregular heartbeat, and an ECG showed diffuse T wave inversions. Cardiac enzymes were elevated, and troponin levels were at 0.25 ng/mL. No coronary artery disease was found on angiography. The patient was diagnosed with suspected myocarditis and referred for a cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) study to confirm the diagnosis. The CMR study revealed evidence of myocardial inflammation, with two positive Lake Louise Criteria, including early Gd enhancement ratio equal to 4.1 and one focus of late enhancement. The patient will be considered "myocarditis-positive" and will be enrolled in the International Myocarditis Registry study to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of CMR criteria for myocarditis. Follow-up will be performed between 4 and 8 weeks after the initial episode and at 1 year to assess LV function and quality of life.

A 45-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage I endometrial adenocarcinoma (EC), grade 2, three months ago. She has completed her treatment and is now looking for ways to improve her quality of life. She is obese, with a BMI of 34. She has been approved by her gynecologic oncologist to participate in this clinical trial involving assisted exercise on a stationary bike, brain imaging and DNA sampling. She has no history of bariatric surgery or participation in a structured weight loss or exercise program in the past 6 months. She is motivated to participate in this study to improve her fitness, bi-manual dexterity, exercise motivation, self-reported eating behavior, and to achieve sustained weight loss. She is willing to complete 45-minute to 1-hour sessions, three times per week for eight weeks. She understands the risks involved and has received medical clearance from her primary care physician to participate in this study.

54 yo F diagnosed with stage II breast cancer, currently undergoing chemotherapy. The patient reports experiencing moderate to severe pain and has not received opioid therapy in the past 21 days. She has no history of cardiac, nervous system, or respiratory disease that would preclude her from participating in the study. She is able to swallow oral dosage forms with the aid of water. She is postmenopausal and is practicing an effective method of birth control. She has not used monoamine oxidase inhibitors or opioids in the past 21 days. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed an informed consent document.

32-year-old female survivor of sexual assault who has been diagnosed with PTSD for the past year. She has been experiencing flashbacks, nightmares, and panic attacks. She is otherwise healthy and currently not taking any medications for PTSD. She is fluent in English and has no medical or psychological conditions that would prevent her from participating in physical activity. She is interested in exploring alternative therapies to help manage her PTSD symptoms and is willing to participate in a study that involves exercise. She reports being physically active and able to tolerate moderate to high-intensity exercise. She is not pregnant and does not have any medical conditions that would preclude her from participating in the study.

The patient is a 25 year old male who is generally healthy and free from any chronic medical conditions. He is a non-smoker and has not used any illicit drugs in the past 3 months. He is currently not taking any psychoactive medications or dietary supplements that may interfere with the study objectives. He is fluent in German and has easy access to the internet. He is willing to participate in a 5 week study to evaluate the effects of a probiotic supplement on stress and anxiety. He understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with the protocol and restrictions. He is able to provide voluntary, written, informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 31-year-old essential worker who works at a grocery store. She has been working throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, which has been stressful for her. She has a history of depression and anxiety, and has been feeling more down and anxious lately due to the pandemic and concerns about her own health and safety. She has limited access to mental health care due to financial constraints and social distancing restrictions. She has tried using some mental health apps in the past but found them difficult to use and not very effective. She lives alone and spends most of her free time watching TV or scrolling through social media on her smartphone. She is interested in participating in this study because she hopes to find a mental health app that is easy to use and can help her manage her symptoms.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been experiencing shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue for the past 3 months. He has never been diagnosed with lung cancer before and has no history of chemotherapy. Upon further evaluation, a biopsy confirmed that he has advanced stage IIIB NSCLC. The patient's ECOG performance status is 2, and his blood tests show adequate marrow function with ANC of 2500/mm3 and platelet count of 120,000/mm3. His liver function tests and serum creatinine are within normal limits. He has no other major illnesses but has a family history of heart disease. The patient has given informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was involved in a motor vehicle accident resulting in a traumatic wound to her left leg. She was brought to the emergency department where her wound was assessed and debrided. The initial wound measurement was 5 cm x 7 cm x 2 cm. She was admitted as an inpatient and is willing to participate in the study. She has no known allergies and has not participated in any clinical trials in the past 30 days. Her medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. She has no history of bleeding disorders or coagulopathy. She is able to provide her own informed consent and is willing and able to return for all scheduled and required study visits. Her wound is appropriate for NPWT according to approved indications for use and has a 30-day wound history available. She has not received NPWT on the study wound within the last 30 days.

56-year-old female diagnosed with colon adenocarcinoma is currently on her third cycle of chemotherapy. She is able to speak and read English and has access to a mobile phone with internet and text messaging capabilities. She had a colectomy 8 weeks ago, and she has fully recovered from the surgery. Her ECOG performance status is 1, and her physician has consented to her participation in unsupervised moderate intensity physical activity. She has hypertension, which is well-controlled on anti-hypertensive therapy with an average BP of 130/80 mmHg. She has no contraindications to exercise and has been cleared by her physician to participate in the study. She is not currently engaging in 150 minutes/week or more of moderate physical activity or 75 minutes/week or more of vigorous physical activity. She is interested in participating in this study to improve her physical activity levels and overall quality of life.

The patient is a 10-year-old girl who underwent a Fontan procedure due to hypoplastic left heart syndrome at the age of 3 years. She has been doing well, and her most recent echocardiogram showed a stable cardiac function. She is scheduled for a routine cardiac catheterization at Lucile Packard Children's Hospital to monitor her pulmonary and systemic pressures. She has a history of mild asthma that is well-controlled with inhaled corticosteroids. She is not currently taking any vasoactive medications. Her past medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and she has no known drug allergies.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypercholesterolemia and has been taking atorvastatin for the past 6 months. He is generally healthy with no significant medical history, and his current medications include atorvastatin and a daily multivitamin. He has not experienced any adverse effects from the atorvastatin and has been compliant with his medication regimen. He is willing to provide informed consent for participation in this clinical study to explore individual factors influencing statin pharmacokinetics.

The patient is a 35-year-old male with a diagnosis of schizophrenia. He has been off of his previous antipsychotic medication for the last 30 days and is willing to remain off of it for the duration of the study. He has no history of renal or hepatic insufficiency, and his electrocardiogram (ECG) is normal. He does not have a history of clinically significant intolerance to antipsychotic medications. He does not have significant orthostatic hypotension. He does not have any medical or surgical condition that might interfere with the absorption, metabolism, or excretion of orally administered lurasidone. He has not participated in another clinical trial or received an investigational product within 30 days prior to drug administration. He is not using concomitant medications that prolong the QT/QTc interval within 14 days prior to Day -5 to follow-up. He has not received depot neuroleptics unless the last injection was at least 1 treatment cycle before Day -5. He has no difficulty fasting or consuming the FDA high-fat meals. He is not at risk with midazolam dosing with respiratory disease or impaired gag reflex, in the opinion of the investigator. He is willing to remain sexually abstinent or use an effective method of birth control from Day -5 to 90 days after discharge.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been recently diagnosed with gastric cancer after experiencing symptoms of abdominal discomfort, bloating, and loss of appetite. He has received two previous chemotherapy regimens with fluorouracil for his cancer, but did not respond to the treatments. The patient is in overall good health and has no significant medical history other than the cancer diagnosis. He has not experienced any systemic infections or serious complications. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance status is graded as 2, meaning he is able to carry out light work but is unable to perform any strenuous activity. He can be hospitalized from the beginning of the study treatment to the end of the first cycle. His blood tests show well-maintained functions of major organs, including bone marrow, liver, kidney, and lung. He is expected to survive for at least 3 months from the beginning of the study treatment. The patient is an extensive or intermediate metabolizer type (EM/IM) regarding CYP2C9 and CYP2C19. He has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and is not taking any medication known to cause prolonged QT/QTc intervals. He meets all the inclusion criteria for the Phase IIa study, but none of the exclusion criteria. The patient provides written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been struggling with acne scars for the past 5 years. She has tried various treatments, including topical creams and chemical peels, but has not seen any significant improvement. The acne scars are predominantly rolling scars and are located on both cheeks. The patient has a Fitzpatrick skin type II. She is not pregnant or nursing and is not currently taking any medications. The patient has no history of hypertrophic scars or keloids and is not currently experiencing any infections in the treatment area. She is committed to following the study protocol and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to improve the appearance of her acne scars.

The patient is a 55-year-old male presenting with chest pain that started about 2 hours ago. He describes it as a squeezing sensation that radiates to his left arm. He also feels short of breath and diaphoretic. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but no previous cardiac events. On physical examination, he is alert, oriented, and cooperative. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his lung and heart sounds are clear. An electrocardiogram shows ST-segment depression in leads V2-V6 and II, III, and aVF. Laboratory results show elevated troponin T levels of 0.08 μg/l. The patient is diagnosed with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is considered eligible to participate in a clinical trial comparing very early cardiac catheterization (< 2,5 hours after randomization) versus an early invasive approach (within 2-48 hours after randomization) versus a selective invasive approach. He is informed of the study and gives his consent to participate.

The patient is a 50-year-old man with a history of metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. He has undergone multiple rounds of chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but his cancer has progressed. The patient has no history of significant cardiac disease and has an ECOG performance status of 1. He has normal organ and marrow function, with an absolute neutrophil count of 2,000/mcL, hemoglobin of 110 g/L, and platelets of 120,000/mcL. He does not have any symptomatic central nervous system metastasis. The patient has measurable disease according to RECIST 1.1 criteria. He has not received any investigational agents, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, or molecular targeted agents within 28 days prior to enrollment to the study. The patient is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period and for 12 months after receiving the final dose of study drug. He has a signed written informed consent form for this trial.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman who has been experiencing sexual dysfunction and pelvic pain for the past year. She has a diagnosis of interstitial cystitis and dyspareunia. She has tried various treatments in the past, including medication and physical therapy, but has not seen significant improvement. She speaks English fluently and has good manual dexterity. She is not pregnant and has not given birth within the past 12 months. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her sexual health and overall quality of life.

A 32-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer is interested in preserving her fertility. She is scheduled to undergo chemotherapy that can affect her ovarian reserve. She has never been pregnant before and has regular menstrual cycles. Her medical history is unremarkable except for her recent diagnosis of breast cancer, for which she will undergo treatment. She has no known allergies and does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to explore the possibility of using immature oocytes for in vitro maturation followed by vitrification to preserve her fertility before undergoing chemotherapy. She meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is willing to undergo ICSI treatment.

A premature infant, weighing 900 grams, was born at 24 weeks and 5 days gestation via emergency C-section due to maternal hypertension. The infant required immediate intubation and mechanical ventilation. The Apgar score at 1 and 5 minutes was 3 and 5, respectively. The infant was transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for further care. The infant is now 3 days old and is being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the use of Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) and Superior Mesenteric Artery (SMA) Doppler Patterns as predictors of feeding tolerance in very low birth weight (VLBW) intrauterine growth restricted (IUGR) and non-IUGR infants. The infant meets the inclusion criteria for the study, and the parents have provided written informed consent. The infant does not have any major congenital abnormalities, multi-organ failure, or pre-existing cutaneous disease that would exclude them from the study. The primary endpoint of the study is to evaluate the changes in the intestinal perfusion determined by feeding, and the secondary endpoint is to compare changes in the intestinal perfusion induced by feeding between IUGR and non-IUGR infants.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has no significant medical history and is not dependent on narcotic medications. He is interested in undergoing robotic assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy (RALP) and is able to provide informed consent. He is fluent in English and able to communicate effectively with the study team.

A 25-year-old female with a history of ocular allergies and recurrent seasonal conjunctivitis presented to the clinic. She complained of itching, burning, tearing, and redness in both eyes, especially during the spring and fall seasons. Her symptoms were relieved with antihistamines and artificial tears. On examination, there was evidence of conjunctival hyperemia, chemosis, and mild follicular reaction. She had no other ocular or systemic medical history. The patient agreed to participate in the study and met all inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with uveal melanoma involving the ciliary body and the choroid. She is scheduled to undergo I-125 plaque brachytherapy. She complains of blurred vision in her left eye, but her right eye is normal. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which is currently controlled with medication. She does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. She works as a teacher and enjoys reading and gardening in her free time. She is an alert and cooperative woman who is able to maintain stable fixation for OCT imaging. She understands the risks and benefits of the study and is willing to give informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating.

The patient is a 14-year-old girl who was diagnosed with a cyst on her neck. She is scheduled for outpatient surgery at Children's Hospital San Diego. She has no known drug allergies and her past medical history is unremarkable. She has not had any previous surgeries or significant injuries to her neck area. She is able to return for follow-up visits and is willing to comply with the study requirements.

The patient is a 65-year-old Caucasian male who has been diagnosed with benign prostatic hyperplasia and is scheduled to undergo transurethral prostatic resection. He has a past medical history of hypertension, controlled with lisinopril 10mg once daily, and hyperlipidemia, controlled with atorvastatin 20mg once daily. He reports occasional difficulty falling asleep and waking up during the night, but his Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) score is below 6. He has no known allergies to any medications. His body mass index (BMI) is 28 kg/m2. He has not been taking any sedatives or analgesics prior to the surgery. He is fully informed about the study and has agreed to participate.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer that has recurred after hormone therapy. He was first diagnosed with prostate cancer 3 years ago and underwent prostatectomy and radiation therapy. However, his PSA levels began to rise again, indicating a recurrence of the cancer. He was started on hormone therapy, which initially helped to lower his PSA levels, but they have since begun to rise again. He has no history of other cancers in the past 5 years. He has a performance status of ECOG 1 and a life expectancy of at least 6 months. His blood work shows WBC of 4,500/mm3, absolute neutrophil count of 2,500/mm3, platelet count of 150,000/mm3, and hemoglobin of 11 g/dL. His bilirubin, SGOT, and creatinine levels are all within normal limits. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or suramin therapy. He has received radiotherapy more than 4 weeks ago. He has not received strontium therapy in the past. He is willing to participate in the trial and receive intravenous flavopiridol over 72 hours every 2 weeks for at least 4 courses.

A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes is admitted to the Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) due to acute respiratory failure secondary to pneumonia. The patient is alert and oriented but complains of difficulty sleeping due to the constant beeping of alarms and the noise from other patients and staff. Despite receiving medication for pain and anxiety, the patient continues to report poor quality sleep, which is affecting his ability to recover from his illness. The patient is not intubated and is able to communicate effectively with the healthcare team. He has been in the MICU for two days, and it is expected that he will be there for at least another two nights. The patient is interested in participating in a study that aims to improve sleep quality in the ICU using white noise. He meets all inclusion criteria and is not excluded based on any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 14-year-old female who is in good health and has no history of serious chronic diseases. She has not been diagnosed with any impairment of immunologic function and has not received any immune globulin or other blood products within the last 3 months. She has not received any tetanus, diphtheria, or pertussis vaccine within the previous 5 years, and has not received any vaccine 28 days prior to the first study vaccination. The patient has not taken any antibiotic therapy within the 72 hours prior to vaccination on Day 0. She has no known hypersensitivity to either of the two study vaccines or their components. The patient is available for the entire study period and is able to attend all scheduled visits and comply with the study procedures. She has signed the informed assent form, and her parent or legal guardian has signed the informed consent form that has been approved by the Institutional Review Board. The patient agrees to use measures to prevent pregnancy during the study.

A 56-year-old male diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with c-Met gene amplification and EGFR mutation, which progressed after two lines of prior therapy including an EGFR-TKI targeting other than c-Met alterations. Patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score of 1 and has measurable target lesions. The patient has not received prior c-Met inhibitor therapy, and fresh samples of NSCLC are available for c-Met gene alteration characterization. The patient has adequate organ function and no history of significant cardiac disease or arrhythmia. The patient is willing and able to employ a highly effective method of birth control/contraception to prevent pregnancy until the end of the trial.

A 28-year-old nulliparous woman presented to the gynecology clinic seeking a long-acting, reversible contraceptive method. She has a history of regular menstrual cycles with moderate flow and has never used hormonal contraception before. Her medical history is unremarkable, and she is not currently taking any medications. She denies any allergies or previous surgeries. She has never been pregnant and has no history of sexually transmitted infections. Her BMI is within normal range, and she reports no current symptoms or complaints. Pelvic exam shows normal external genitalia, cervix, and vagina. Transvaginal ultrasound shows a normal uterus with no evidence of fibroids or other abnormalities. She has no contraindications for intrauterine device insertion according to the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria for contraceptive use. She is informed about the study and agrees to participate.

A 65-year-old man presented to the clinic with complaints of difficulty urinating and blood in his urine. Further evaluation revealed a PSA level of 23 ng/mL and a biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a Gleason score of 8. The patient has no prior history of treatment for prostate cancer or any other malignancy. He is otherwise healthy with no significant medical history and an ECOG performance status of 1. Imaging studies including bone scan, CT scan, and MRI of the abdomen and pelvis do not show any evidence of metastatic disease. The patient is a potential candidate for radical prostatectomy and neoadjuvant hormone therapy based on the estimated risk of biochemical recurrence. The patient does not have a history of autoimmune or chronic GI conditions associated with diarrhea or bleeding.

This is a 32 year old male with a past medical history of aggressive Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Stage IIIA. He received initial treatment with R-CHOP and achieved complete remission. Unfortunately, he experienced disease relapse 8 months later with lymph nodes enlargement in the neck and the mediastinum. He underwent a biopsy which confirmed relapsed aggressive Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma. He is now being considered for enrollment in a clinical trial investigating the efficacy and toxicity of 2 x R-DHAP followed by high dose chemotherapy R-TEC and autologous stem cell transplantation. He is 32 years old and has an ECOG performance status of 1. His laboratory values are within normal limits with a granulocyte count of 2.0/µm3, a platelet count of 140/µm3, creatinine clearance of 1.5 ml/sec, and GPT/GOT of 0.9 x normal. He has no history of second neoplasia, CNS involvement by lymphoma, respiratory or cardiac insufficiency, or severe neurological or psychiatric disease. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

The patient is a 52-year-old male who was diagnosed with HCV-positive HCC after experiencing abdominal pain and weight loss. He underwent radical therapy, which included surgery and chemotherapy, and was confirmed to have achieved complete cure based on the CT scans taken 10 weeks after the end of the treatment. The patient has a Child-Pugh classification of grade A and a platelet count of 75,000/µL. He is positive for serum HCV-RNA and has an ECOG performance status score of 1. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial for a new drug called Peretinoin, which aims to suppress the recurrence of HCV-positive HCC.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who is overweight and has never been diagnosed with cancer. He has an opposite-sex spouse who is also in the age group of 40-70 and is overweight. The patient is willing to participate in an online or laboratory study that involves reading a health message about cancer risk relevant to himself or his spouse. The patient is willing to answer questions about his beliefs about cancer risk and his intentions to lose weight. The patient has no history of any serious medical condition and is in good health. He is interested in contributing to research that can help improve health communication and disease prevention strategies.

This is a 45-year-old female who has a history of a severe allergic reaction to wasp venom. She experienced grade 3 reaction according to Müller classification with symptoms of generalized urticaria, angioedema, and difficulty breathing. She has avoided wasp stings since then but continues to experience anxiety and fear of another reaction. She is otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history, no medications, no chronic medical conditions, and no current infections. She is fluent in French, and her BMI is 25 kg/m2. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to study the immunological and environmental parameters that define the immune system of allergic patients, with the ultimate goal of identifying novel markers of treatment success. She understands the study requirements and is willing to comply with all scheduled visits at the investigational site. She is affiliated with the French social security and has not participated in another clinical study in the last 3 months. She has not traveled to (sub-)tropical countries within the last 3 months and has no evidence of neurological or psychiatric diagnoses that may affect her ability to participate in the study. Her hemoglobin, platelet count, and liver function tests are all within normal limits.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who is pregnant with her first child. She is currently at 38 weeks of gestational age and has no significant medical history. She has been experiencing mild to moderate contractions for the past few days, and her cervix is dilated to 4 centimeters. She is interested in receiving an epidural for pain management during labor. The patient has a BMI of 25 and is 5'6" tall. She speaks fluent English and has no known allergies. The patient has no previous experience with an epidural and is willing to participate in the study. She has signed the written informed consent form and meets all the inclusion criteria.

A 62-year-old woman living in a rural area was recently diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. She completed chemotherapy and radiation therapy six months ago and underwent surgery last year. She has been feeling fatigued and has not been exercising regularly, with only occasional walks around her neighborhood. She is interested in participating in the JumpSTART program to increase her physical activity level and improve her overall health. She is able to walk for exercise and has no other underlying health conditions. She speaks English fluently and is available to attend the online exercise classes on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays at the scheduled time.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who is experiencing chronic back pain. He reports that the pain has been present for over a year, and it has been progressively worsening. He has tried conservative measures such as physical therapy and pain medication, but they have not provided any significant relief. MRI imaging reveals that he has a deformity of greater than 6 levels in the lumbar region. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of hematologic disorders, infections, malignancies, or terminal illnesses. He has not received any anticoagulant therapy in the past week and is not taking any immunosuppressive medications. The patient has provided written informed consent and is willing to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the use of postoperative drains with blood salvage capabilities to decrease the transfusion rate and volume of adults undergoing posterior spine surgery for deformity correction of 6 levels or more.

The patient is a 40 year old African American woman who has been struggling with her weight for several years. She is a working mother of two children and spends most of her day sitting at a desk. Despite her efforts to exercise and eat healthily, she has been unable to lose weight and is now classified as obese with a BMI of 33. She has a family history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She has not been diagnosed with either of these conditions but is concerned about her risk. She has noticed that she feels tired and sluggish throughout the day and often craves high-carbohydrate foods. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial as she hopes it will help her understand the underlying cause of her weight struggles and improve her overall health. She does not smoke or drink alcohol and is currently not taking any medications.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with an intracranial aneurysm that requires endovascular coil embolization (ECE) treatment. He is in good health and has no history of mental illness. He does not have any recent use of sedatives or analgesics. He is a non-smoker and does not use illicit drugs. His blood pressure, heart rate, and laboratory values are within normal limits. He has sensation and is able to understand and follow instructions. He is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent form. He is classified as ASA II.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who has no significant medical history. She is a non-smoker and has a BMI of 22. She is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics of VNRX-5133. She has no known allergies or intolerances to medications. Her veins are easily accessible for cannulation. She has normal vital signs and laboratory values. She is not an employee of the site or the sponsor. She has not been diagnosed with any cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatic, renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, autoimmune, hematologic, neoplastic, or neurological disorders. She has not tested positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) type 1. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is a suitable candidate for the study.

A 28-year-old male with a diagnosis of abetalipoproteinemia presents with symptoms of severe vision impairment and difficulty walking. Despite taking megadoses of vitamins A and E orally, his symptoms have continued to progress. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that aims to determine whether intravenous infusions of essential fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins can reverse his symptoms. He is able to attend regular blood tests and eye and neurological examinations.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing abdominal discomfort and bloating for the past few months. She has been taking over-the-counter medications for her symptoms but has not noticed much improvement. She has no significant past medical history and does not take any prescription medications. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She has no known allergies. She is interested in participating in a study that may help identify the cause of her symptoms. She has never had an upper endoscopy before but is willing to undergo the procedure.

The patient is a 55 year old man who has been diagnosed with advanced stage of pancreatic cancer. The patient has undergone chemotherapy and radiation therapy that did not lead to significant improvement. The patient's cancer has continued to progress and his performance status is now ECOG 2. The patient has measurable lesions as per RECIST guidelines. The patient has never undergone any clinical trial before. The patient is currently on no other medications. The patient has a history of hypertension and is under medication for the same. The patient does not have any other significant medical history. The patient is married and has two grown children. The patient is a retired electrician and enjoys fishing in his free time. He is able to perform daily activities with some assistance. The patient's BMI is 28 with BP of 140/90. There is nothing remarkable in his physical exam.

A 53-year-old man with a history of severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and high blood pressure recently visited his primary care physician. Despite using continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy, his blood pressure remained elevated, and he had difficulty adhering to the treatment due to discomfort. He is interested in alternative treatments or adjuvants to CPAP. He is a non-smoker, has a BMI of 28 kg/m2, and exercises regularly for 30 minutes a day. He takes medication for his high blood pressure and has no history of heart or respiratory disease. He has no known allergies to food or medication. He is willing to take polyphenols supplementation and has signed the informed consent for the study.

The patient is a 45 year-old woman who has been diagnosed with biopsy-proven breast cancer (BIRAD VI). She has a locally advanced breast cancer and is eligible for neoadjuvant chemotherapy and breast conservative surgery. She is in need of clip placement for tumor localization. She has no history of prior chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or tamoxifen therapy for her current breast cancer. She is not pregnant and does not have multicentric or metastatic breast cancer. She has no contraindications to MRI and is willing to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old female with no history of alcohol or analgesic drugs abuse. She is a non-smoker and has no history of motion sickness or chronic pain. She is scheduled to undergo surgery for a non-emergency medical condition and has an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status of Ⅰ-Ⅱ. She weighs 65 kg and has no severe heart, brain or kidney disease. She has been informed about the use of PCA pump and VAS and has undergone pressure pain threshold(PPT) and pressure pain tolerance(PTO) tests before surgery. The patient has consented to participate in the study and has provided EDTA anti-coagulated blood for genomic DNA analysis. The patient will be administered with dexmedetomidine1μg/Kg，sufentanil 0.5μg/Kg，propofol 2mg/Kg and rocuronium 0.6mg/Kg for anesthesia induction. The patient's vital signs and Narcotrend will be monitored during surgery. Parecoxib 40mg will be administered intravenously before surgery and the patient will be started on a PCA with sufentanil 1ug/ml immediately after surgery. The patient will be monitored for 48 hours after surgery for postoperative pain, side effects such as nausea, vomiting, respiratory depression, pruritus, abdominal distention, urinary retention and dizziness. The patient is willing to adhere to the study requirements and follow-up visits.

A 32-year-old woman with a diagnosis of type 1 diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years, complains of frequent episodes of hypoglycemia unawareness. She uses multiple daily injections of insulin with a basal insulin injection and bolus injections. She checks her blood sugar levels at least 3 times a day. She has a history of severe hypoglycemic episodes in the past 6 months. She is married and has no children. Her HbA1c is 8.5%. She has no history of major renal, liver, or heart diseases. Her vision and hearing are normal, and she can perceive glucose display and alarms. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, substance abuse, or alcohol abuse. She is not currently pregnant, and she is not planning to conceive. She speaks Dutch fluently. She has never used RT-CGM before.

50-year-old male kidney transplant recipient with a history of hypomagnesemia and persistent hyperglycemia despite current medical treatment for diabetes. The patient underwent kidney transplantation 2 years ago and has been taking calcineurin inhibitors for immunosuppression which have been identified as a cause of low plasma magnesium levels. The patient has not been taking any magnesium-containing medications or supplements. The patient has no history of short bowel syndrome or chronic pancreatitis. The patient is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who underwent liver transplantation due to end-stage liver disease caused by chronic hepatitis C virus infection. The surgery was a living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) and was uneventful. The patient was started on immunosuppressive therapy with cyclosporine A (CsA) post-transplantation. Three months after transplantation, the patient had a recurrence of hepatitis C virus infection, which was confirmed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Her liver biopsy showed Metavir score A2F2. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effect of calcineurin inhibitors (CsA and tacrolimus) on the response to antiviral therapy (AVT) for recurrent hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. The patient is currently not pregnant and has no significant medical history other than the liver transplant. She is willing to follow the study protocol and attend all the required follow-up visits.

The patient is a 57-year-old male who was diagnosed with stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with predominantly squamous histology. The patient has already undergone treatment for the first line of advanced disease, but has progressed and is now eligible for a second line of treatment with Erlotinib. The patient has an ECOG performance status between 0 and 2 and is able to take oral medication. The patient is willing to grant informed, preferably in writing, or oral consent before witnesses independent of the research team. The patient does not have uncontrolled or severe systemic disease, an active infection, concomitant or secondary neoplasia to primary disease, except for carcinoma in situ of cervix or adequately treated skin carcinoma. The patient does not have a disease with mutated EGFR, clinically active interstitial lung disease, unstable angina or recent myocardial infarction, uncontrolled and progressive brain metastasis, or is participating in a clinical trial. The patient has not used an inhibitor of tyrosine kinase in first line of treatment and has an estimated life expectancy of more than 2 months.

John is a 25-year-old first-time father living with his partner and their healthy 35-week-old daughter. John is fluent in English and lives within one-hour driving distance of the university. He works full-time as a mechanic and is excited to participate in this study to learn how to better interact with his daughter. John has no known addictions and is in good health. His daughter was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery without any complications, and she did not require any assisted ventilation or suffer from any major congenital anomalies or neurologic disorders. John is interested in learning more about how to support his daughter's development and is eager to participate in the educational intervention.

A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) six years ago. Despite undergoing several treatments, including corticosteroids, immunosuppressive agents, and thrombopoietin receptor agonists, his platelet count has remained persistently low (<30,000/µL). He has not undergone rituximab or splenectomy in the past eight weeks. He has no other significant medical history and his hematologic, hepatic, and renal functions are adequate. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is willing to use medically acceptable methods of contraception during the study and for six months following discontinuation of study drug, as he is married and his wife is of childbearing potential. He does not have a history of receiving a SYK inhibitor in the past. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options for his persistent and chronic ITP.

The patient is a 38-year-old Caucasian woman who has no history of any major health concerns. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will improve her skin health. She has normal BMI, and her skin type falls between 1-111. She has a regular menstrual cycle and does not smoke or consume alcohol. She is not pregnant or lactating. She has not taken any vitamin, mineral, or antioxidant supplements for the past 3 months. She is willing to avoid fermented dairy products and limit her consumption of dark chocolate during the study. She has never been diagnosed with skin cancer nor has any genetic disposition to skin cancer. She is not regularly exposed to artificial UVR and has no plans for a vacation to a sunny destination during the study period. She does not drink excessive amounts of green or black tea nor does she consume fermented dairy products more than 150g per day. She is not a regular participant in high exercise activities such as marathon running, and she does not take saunas or swim daily. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and is excited to participate in a clinical trial that can improve her skin health.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman with a history of gastric adenocarcinoma. She has undergone first-line chemotherapy but has not achieved a complete response. She is not willing to undergo second-line chemotherapy due to the severe side effects she experienced during the first-line treatment. She has also been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and hypertension for which she takes medications. She has no history of allergies or surgeries. Her physical examination is remarkable for a palpable mass in the epigastric region. Her laboratory results show elevated levels of CA19-9 and CEA. CT imaging confirms the presence of a large tumor in the stomach with metastases to the liver. She is able to provide written consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 58-year-old man was recently diagnosed with non-metastatic prostate cancer and is scheduled for radical prostatectomy (RP) within the next three months. He has a history of high blood pressure but it is well-controlled with medication. The patient reports that he has been experiencing a decrease in sexual desire and performance. His baseline score for sexual functioning domain is 45 points on the EPIC-26 questionnaire. The patient has never received testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) before and has no history of male breast or liver cancer. He has a BMI of 26 and is physically active. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates whether TRT can improve functional and oncological outcomes in testosterone deficient men following RP for prostate cancer.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who complains of shoulder pain that has been present for the last 6 months. The pain is described as a dull ache that is worse with overhead activities and at night. She reports no history of trauma or shoulder surgery. She has tried physical therapy and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) without any significant improvement. On physical examination, there is pain with resisted abduction and external rotation of the shoulder. There is no pain with 90 degree abduction-90 degree external rotation position of the shoulder. The range of motion of the shoulder is normal. No neurological deficits are noted. The patient is diagnosed with subacromial impingement syndrome and is a candidate for the study. She is willing and able to complete the entire study procedure. Her past medical history is non-significant.

The patient is a 4-year-old boy with a documented diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) from a licensed professional using DSM-5 criteria. He has no other major medical conditions and has no history of any developmental delay or neurological disorder. He has normal vision and hearing, and his family's primary language is English. He has a receptive language age equivalence of ≥18 months and a non-verbal age equivalent score of ≥24 months on the Mullen Scale of Early Learning. His caregiver is willing and able to bring him to the university for the study sessions and to schedule up to 3 assessment visits prior to intervention start and 3 assessment sessions after intervention end. The patient will participate in a one-group, pre-post feasibility study of an intensive, interdisciplinary (theatre, Occupational Therapy (OT), and Speech Language Pathology (SLP)) intervention targeted at social skill development in children with ASD, aged 3-4. The intervention uses process drama modified with OT and SLP techniques and using typically developing peer models. The program will be conducted with 6 children with ASD and 6 TD peer models 5 days per week for 1 week for 2.5-3 hours each day. The outcome measures that the patient will complete are Social Skills Improvement Scale (SSIS), Theory of Mind (T0M) Battery and Inventory, Structured Play Assessment (SPA), and Communication and Symbolic Behavior Scales (CSBS) scores within 4 weeks of program end. The patient will also participate in an EEG session and complete another EEG session as they did at baseline. Three months after the last testing session, the parents will be contacted to complete an interview to ask how their children are functioning related to play and other interactions with other children and with adults.

The patient is a 28-year-old female who is currently a graduate student. She is generally healthy and has no history of significant medical conditions. She is a non-smoker and does not use tobacco products. Her current medications include a daily multivitamin and occasional use of over-the-counter pain relievers. She has no known allergies to medications, including scopolamine. She has normal weight for her body size and meets the physical readiness test body composition assessment criteria. She is willing and able to comply with study requirements and restrictions and has read and signed the informed consent. She has not used any investigational drugs in the last 30 days, and has not donated blood or experienced significant blood loss in the last 30 days. She has no history of gastrointestinal disorders, asthma, or seizure disorders, and has not been diagnosed with narrow-angle glaucoma or urinary retention problems. She is not pregnant or lactating, and has a hematocrit value that meets the study's criteria. She has not undergone recent nasal, nasal sinus, or nasal mucosa surgery, and has not used prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medication in the past 7 days.

A 55-year-old male with a history of hypertension and obesity presented to the hospital with shortness of breath and a dry cough. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 and developed acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) within 72 hours of admission. Despite being placed on mechanical ventilation, his condition continued to worsen. He has agreed to participate in a clinical trial investigating the safety and feasibility of T regulatory cell therapy for COVID-19 induced ARDS. He is committed to full life support and is able to provide signed written informed consent.

A 14-year-old male was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) last year. He received standard therapy and achieved complete remission, but unfortunately relapsed six months later. He presents to the clinic with symptoms of fatigue, fever, and night sweats. His blood work shows a white blood cell count of 80,000 cells/L and presence of lymphoblasts. He does not have any history of central nervous system (CNS) tumors, severe aplastic anemia, or bone marrow failure predisposition syndrome. He has never been treated with a MDM2 antagonist or venetoclax. He has not received any systemic anticancer therapy, monoclonal antibodies, antibody drug conjugates, or cellular therapy for anti-neoplastic intent within the last 28 days. He has not undergone any major surgical procedure within the last 21 days. He is able to swallow tablets or liquid. He has no known allergies to any food or drugs. He agrees to remain abstinent or use contraception during the treatment period and follow-up period.

Patient is a 25-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with a single-rooted tooth requiring root canal treatment. She has not experienced any swelling, sinus tract, or acute pain. The tooth has no periodontal probing greater than 3mm, internal or external resorption, or fractures. She does not have hypertension, cardiovascular pathologies, diabetes, or any other systemic health issues. She has not used any analgesics, antibiotics, or antidepressants at least one week before treatment. The patient has given her informed consent to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effect of low-level laser therapy on post-endodontic pain. The clinical trial will be conducted by a clinician who will perform all treatment procedures, including access cavity preparation, instrumentation, and root canal filling procedures. The patient will be randomly assigned to either the laser group or the placebo group. The laser group will receive Nd-YAG laser treatment for 60 seconds per tooth, while the placebo group will undergo the same procedures but without the activation of the laser. Postoperative pain will be measured and documented via the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at 4th, 8th, 12th, 24th, 48th and 72th hours. The patient will be informed of the potential benefits and risks associated with participating in this clinical trial.

This clinical trial is looking for Danish patients who have been diagnosed with phaeochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) or have genetic variants that predispose them to PPGLs. The patient should have been diagnosed since 1996 and have tumor tissue or blood samples available in biobanks. The study aims to develop a predictive algorithm for disease prognosis by investigating novel immunohistochemical, genetic, and epigenetic biomarkers in tumor tissue samples. Patients with a poor prognosis (proof of metastases) and good prognosis (non-metastatic) will be included for the identification of novel prognostic biomarkers. The results will be used to develop a new algorithm for clinical prognosis. Participation in the study will involve sharing medical records and tumor tissue samples. Patients who meet the inclusion criteria and do not have any exclusion criteria can participate in this study.

A 32-year-old female presents with a history of recurrent episodes of dermatophytosis on her feet and groin area for the past 1 year. The lesions are itchy, scaly, and red in color. The patient has been treated with oral terbinafine and itraconazole for each episode, but the lesions keep recurring within a month of stopping the medication. She has no history of any other medical illness or medication. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not pregnant. Physical examination reveals erythematous, scaly plaques on both feet and the groin area. The rest of the physical examination is normal. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of low dose oral isotretinoin in preventing recurrences in chronic recurrent dermatophytosis.

A 55-year-old post-menopausal woman with a body mass index (BMI) of 26, who has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, presented for the study. She is a non-smoker and has undergone a hysterectomy. She is not currently taking any medication but has taken hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in the past. She has no known allergies or hypersensitivity to anastrozole or any other drugs. Her laboratory values are within normal limits, and her vital signs are stable. She is able to fast and consume standard meals without difficulty. She is informed of the nature of the study and has given written consent to participate. The patient will be instructed not to take any drugs known to induce or inhibit hepatic drug metabolism for 30 days prior to dosing. She has not participated in any other clinical trial or received an investigational product within the past 30 days. She has donated 250 mL of blood within the previous 30 days and is willing to tolerate venipuncture.

John is a 45-year-old male who underwent a transfemoral amputation on his right leg due to a traumatic injury sustained during a work-related accident. He has been using a prosthetic knee for the past two years, which he has had for more than 90 days in its current condition. John is able to ambulate independently in the community and is classified as a Medicare functional class K3. He has no significant medical history that could hinder his ability to transfer. John is mentally independent and capable of providing informed consent. He will be included in the study as part of the Microprocessor Stance Control Group, using the C-Leg.

The patient is a 55-year-old Asian male who was recently diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) after experiencing chest discomfort and shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol and is currently taking medications for these conditions. He underwent coronary angiography, which revealed significant stenosis in one of his coronary arteries. The patient is eligible for coronary stenting and has agreed to participate in the A-MATCH study to determine whether a fixed-dose (prasugrel 10 mg/d vs. 5 mg/d) vs. phenotype-based prasugrel dose adjustment can match therapeutic zone of platelet reactivity in PCI-treated Asians with acute coronary syndrome. The patient weighs 70 kg and is currently taking aspirin 100 mg/day. He has no history of bleeding disorders, liver disease, or other significant medical conditions. He is able to understand and comply with the study protocol.

A 55-year-old female patient came to the clinic with complaints of difficulty in chewing and speaking due to her ill-fitting dentures. She had undergone extraction of all her mandibular teeth due to severe periodontal disease. She had been using complete dentures for the past 10 years, but she was not comfortable with them. She was interested in implant-supported overdentures, but her mandibular bone was insufficient for the placement of parallel implants. The clinician suggested the use of tilted implants with the OT Equator Smart Box Attachment. The patient agreed to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the retentive power and wear of the attachment. She has no known allergies and no history of smoking.

A 73-year-old woman was referred to the clinic due to worsening shortness of breath on exertion and fatigue. She has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes, for which she is taking medications. She has never smoked and has no history of heart disease in her family. She underwent a transthoracic echocardiogram, which revealed severe aortic stenosis with a mean gradient of 45 mmHg, a valve area of 0.7 cm2, and an ejection fraction of 60%. Her STS score is 12.5, indicating a high surgical risk. She is classified as NYHA class III. She has been referred for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and her heart team, including a cardiac surgeon, has deemed her eligible for the procedure. She has provided written informed consent to participate in the study and comply with all study procedures and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who is an avid runner and has been experiencing pain in his right knee for the past 3 weeks. The pain is located in the area just below the kneecap and worsens with running or jumping activities. He has not experienced any trauma to the knee, and there is no swelling or redness present. The patient has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they have not provided significant relief. He has no history of knee surgeries, but he did have a previous ankle sprain 2 years ago. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore the potential usefulness of a heated lidocaine and tetracaine topical patch for the treatment of pain associated with patellar tendinopathy.

A 45-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, who consumes an average of 30 standard drinks per week and has at least 2 heavy drinking days per week, is seeking treatment options to reduce her alcohol consumption. She has a history of anxiety and adverse childhood events, including emotional abuse and neglect. She has no significant medical conditions, and her physical examination and laboratory results are within normal limits. She is not currently taking any medication for the treatment of AUD or any other medication that may interfere with the study drug. She is not currently pregnant or lactating and agrees to continue using a reliable method of birth control throughout the study and for 6 months following participation. She is a nonsmoker and is willing to participate in a 24-week randomized controlled trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of dutasteride for reducing her alcohol consumption. She understands the study requirements and agrees to comply with all study procedures, including daily medication administration, regular study visits, and completion of study questionnaires.

The patient is a 60 year old man who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease 3 years ago. He has been experiencing tremors and stiffness in his arms and legs. He has never been treated with levodopa (Sinemet) before as his symptoms were not severe enough to require medication. He lives with his wife and is retired from his job as a teacher. He enjoys reading and spending time with his grandchildren. He has mild hypertension which is well controlled with medication. His BMI is 26 and he exercises regularly by taking daily walks in his neighborhood. He has no significant cognitive impairment and is able to perform daily activities without assistance. He has no history of allergies or sensitivity to soy.

A 28-year-old woman presents with a history of irregular menstrual cycles, acne, and excessive hair growth on her face and body. She has been trying to conceive with her partner for over a year without success. She was diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) by her gynecologist. Her body mass index (BMI) is 34 kg/m2, and she has gained 10 pounds in the last three months. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that focuses on weight loss and lifestyle interventions to improve her chances of conceiving naturally. She has no history of binge eating disorder or any other infertility diagnosis besides ovulatory dysfunction caused by PCOS. She is willing to withhold infertility treatment for six months and participate in a multicomponent weight loss intervention. The remote delivery of the intervention is suitable for her as she lives in a rural area and has limited access to weight management programs. She is willing to comply with the recommendations for diet, physical activity, and self-monitoring of weight, diet, and physical activity.

The patient is a 45-year-old man who was diagnosed with GBM 6 months ago. He underwent surgical resection and received external beam radiotherapy and temozolomide. His medical history is significant for hypertension, which is well-controlled with medication. The patient's MRI shows RANO defined tumor progression in comparison to a prior scan. Genetic testing confirmed the presence of an activating mutation in FGFR3. He has no history of prior or current treatment with a FGFR inhibitor. The patient is not currently experiencing neurological symptoms related to his underlying disease and is not taking any Enzyme Inducing Anti-Epileptic Drug (EIAED). His performance status is 1 according to the Karnofsky scale, indicating that he is able to carry out most activities of daily living without assistance.

Patient is a 35-year-old man diagnosed with HIV 2 years ago. He was started on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with Raltegravir (RAL) 400mg twice daily, along with tenofovir and emtricitabine. He has been compliant with his medication regimen and has not had any significant side effects. His most recent viral load was undetectable (<20 copies/mL) and his CD4 count was 600 cells/µL. The patient is willing to participate in the clinical trial to measure plasma and intracellular concentrations of RAL. He has no acute intercurrent illness and is otherwise in good health.

A 56-year-old woman who is a former smoker, quit smoking 5 years ago, presents with shortness of breath and chest pain. She was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with malignant pleural effusion, and CT scan showed measurable disease. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) of 1, which means she is able to independently care for herself and perform light work. Her blood counts and liver and kidney function are adequate. She has no history of treatment for NSCLC with chemotherapy, biological therapy, or immunotherapy, but has undergone radiation therapy. She has no history of bleeding disorders or cardiac disorders. She is interested in participating in clinical trials to find a curative treatment for advanced stages of NSCLC.

A 42-year-old female presents with a BMI of 28. She has a family history of diabetes and high cholesterol. Her past medical history is significant for hypothyroidism, which is well controlled on medication. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally. She is physically active and exercises for 30 minutes daily. Her recent blood work shows total cholesterol of 215 mg/dL, triglycerides of 165 mg/dL, and fasting glucose of 90 mg/dL. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the metabolic effects of a red grape extract-based drink. She does not take any dietary supplements or medications other than her thyroid medication.

A 52 year old African American woman with advanced metastatic breast cancer presents to the palliative care clinic. She reports having difficulty communicating her values and beliefs to her healthcare providers. She feels that her cultural and spiritual values are not being taken into consideration and that it has resulted in sub-optimal care. She is interested in participating in a study that will help providers better understand her personal narrative and integrate it into her care plan. She is able to read and speak English fluently and is willing to provide informed consent. The patient identifies as a member of a racial and ethnic minority group and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She is currently receiving treatment for her cancer and is stable enough to participate in the study.

Maria is a 68 year old woman living in a rural area in Saskatchewan. She has been married for 45 years and has been caring for her husband who was diagnosed with advanced cancer 6 months ago. She is the primary caregiver for her husband and has no other family members living nearby to assist her with caregiving. Maria has been feeling overwhelmed and stressed due to her caregiving duties and has been experiencing feelings of hopelessness and loss of control. She has no history of mental health issues or chronic illnesses. Maria is willing to participate in the Living with Hope Program for Rural Women Caregivers to improve her quality of life and personal health.

A 55-year-old male patient was diagnosed with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on hypervascular liver tumor imaging, elevated alpha-fetoprotein levels, and cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis B infection. The patient was deemed ineligible for local invasive treatment due to the size and location of the tumor. The patient has a history of heavy alcohol consumption and smoking but quit both 6 months ago. The patient has no other significant medical history and is currently asymptomatic. Laboratory results showed normal organ function, with AST and ALT levels within normal limits, total bilirubin levels below 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), and international normalized ratio (INR) below 1.5. The patient has an ECOG score of 1 and is classified as BCLC stage B disease. The patient has not received any previous treatment for HCC. The patient is willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 44-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) for six years. She has been experiencing cognitive difficulties, particularly with memory and attention, and is looking for ways to improve her cognitive functions. She is able to engage in moderate physical activity and is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates computerized brain training tools to improve cognitive functions in patients with MS. She is willing to attend regular appointments at either the UCSF Weill Institute for Neurosciences in San Francisco or the Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland. She has no history of falls in the past 12 weeks and has no psychiatric co-morbidity or anti-depressive or anxiolytic medication that has been changed over the 6 months preceding consideration for study enrollment. She is not colorblind and has not experienced clinically and/or radiologically confirmed relapses or disease progression in the past 12 weeks.

A 35-year-old male who was diagnosed with celiac disease one year ago and has been following a gluten-free diet since then. He has a history of gastrointestinal symptoms, including diarrhea and abdominal pain, which prompted him to seek medical attention. He underwent a duodenal biopsy, which showed Marsh IIIB histopathology, and had positive serum anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG) IgA antibodies. He has been on a strict gluten-free diet for the past year and is now participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the measurement of gluten immunogenic peptides (GIP) in stools as a marker of GFD adherence in CD patients. He will be required to complete a dietary questionnaire and will have his fecal GIP quantified by ELISA (iVYLISA GIP-S kit). He is excited to participate in this study and hopes that the results will help improve the accuracy of monitoring his adherence to a gluten-free diet.

We are seeking healthy volunteers for a study on the metabolism of two magnesium supplements. If you are a non-smoker, not using any pharmaceuticals or supplements, and have not made any major changes to your eating habits within the last week, you may be eligible to participate. Please note that vegans and vegetarians are excluded from this study. The aim of this study is to investigate the pharmacokinetics of Mablet (a dietary supplement) and Magnesium Sulfate (a solution for infusion). If you are interested in participating, please contact us for more information.

Patient is a 55-year-old male from China who was diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer stage III. He is a smoker with a 35 pack-year history. His past medical history is significant for hypertension and dyslipidemia, which are well-controlled with medication. He underwent lobectomy and mediastinal lymph node dissection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy. Pathological examination showed a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with lymphovascular invasion. His tumor was positive for Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) mutation. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue samples from his surgery will be used for the study.

The patient is a 62-year-old former smoker who has been experiencing chest pain during physical activity for the past 3 months. He has a family history of heart disease and underwent a stress test that showed a high probability of coronary artery disease. His doctor has recommended a cardiac computed tomography (CT) scan to evaluate his coronary arteries. Additionally, due to his history of heavy smoking, his doctor has suggested he undergo lung cancer screening. The patient is willing to participate in a pilot randomized study that will test the feasibility, safety, and diagnostic ability of a novel ultra-low-dose CT protocol that allows concomitant coronary artery evaluation and lung screening. He has provided informed consent to undergo the CT scan and has no contraindications to iodinated contrast.

7 yo M with a history of epilepsy diagnosed at age 4. Currently on a stable dose of levetiracetam and lamotrigine for the past 12 weeks with no change in seizure frequency or severity. The patient and their guardian are open to exploring complementary therapies for seizure management. No history of progressive CNS diseases, heart, liver, kidney, or blood diseases. Not pregnant and no plans for pregnancy during the study period. The patient and their guardian are able to accurately report seizure frequency and are willing to complete the study. Past Medical History: - Epilepsy diagnosed at age 4 - No previous history of VNS therapy or other surgical interventions - No history of heart, liver, kidney, or blood diseases - No history of adverse reactions to medication - No history of psychiatric disorders or developmental delays.

The patient is a 52-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with metastatic melanoma. He has no significant medical history other than high blood pressure, which is well-controlled with medication. He does not smoke and is not currently taking any prescription medications or illicit drugs. He has not received any prior treatments for his melanoma. His physical exam and lab studies are unremarkable except for the presence of multiple skin lesions and enlarged lymph nodes. He is willing to practice birth control for four months after receiving treatment. He understands the risks and benefits of the study and has signed the informed consent document. His Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status is 1, and his life expectancy is greater than three months. His serology is negative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B antigen, and hepatitis C antibody. His hematology and chemistry values meet the eligibility criteria. He has no history of coronary revascularization or ischemic symptoms, and his left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is greater than 45%. He has not been diagnosed with any primary immunodeficiency or concurrent opportunistic infections.

35 year-old man with a history of major depressive disorder for the past 2 years. The patient has been previously treated with sertraline but has not achieved adequate response. The patient reports a persistent low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, decreased concentration, and occasional suicidal ideation. The patient reports a lack of interest in socializing with friends and family, and has limited motivation to perform daily activities such as work and personal hygiene. The patient is employed as a software developer with no history of alcohol or drug abuse. The patient has no history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or other psychotic disorders. The patient is willing to visit the doctor's office once a week for a total of 14 weeks.

The patient is a 6-year-old child who has been diagnosed with a neuromuscular disorder characterized by hypotonia, dystonia, and seizures. Despite undergoing treatment, the child's disorder has remained untreatable or poorly treatable. The child has also exhibited reduced viability in cultured fibroblasts under conditions of oxidative stress compared to age-matched control fibroblasts.
