However, the child's fibroblasts have achieved at least 80% viability rescue with EPI-743 at 1micromolar upon exposure to oxidative stress, and have a half maximal effective concentration of EPI-743 of less than or equal to 50 nanomolar. The child will be willing to abstain from initiating the use of dietary supplements and non-prescribed medications, foods or beverages or bars fortified with coenzyme Q(10), vitamin E, super fortified functional foods or beverages, and idebenone. The child will be able to travel to the Clinical Center for at least 8 visits. The child does not have any allergies to EPI-743 or sesame oil, and does not have hepatic, renal insufficiency, or significant malabsorption of fats precluding drug absorption. The child's clinical history does not show any signs of bleeding requiring ongoing medical management or any abnormal red cell parameters requiring ongoing medical management besides iron supplementation. Finally, the child's neutrophils are greater than 500 mm3.

A 45-year-old woman is scheduled for a neck CT scan due to a history of thyroidectomy for thyroid cancer. She has a BMI of 30 and a short bull neck. During her last surgery, the anesthesiologist had difficulty intubating her due to her neck anatomy. She is concerned about complications during future surgeries and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to improve the accuracy of identifying the cricothyroid membrane using ultrasound. She meets the inclusion criteria of the study as she has neck pathology and is scheduled for a neck CT scan.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with severe aplastic anemia that is unresponsive to immunosuppressive therapy. He has a matched unrelated donor willing to donate marrow or peripheral blood stem cells. The patient's serum bilirubin is within normal limits, and his serum creatinine is 1.5 mg/dl. He has no symptomatic cardiac or pulmonary disease and has a PS of 1. His left ventricular ejection fraction is 50%, and he has no uncontrolled arrhythmia or symptomatic cardiac disease. His FEV1, FVC, and DLCO are all above 50%. The patient has no clonal cytogenetic abnormalities associated with AML, MDS, or other hematologic malignancies. He has no history of allergic reactions to any of the drugs used in this trial. The patient is willing to participate in the trial and has signed informed consent.

54-year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension is admitted to the hospital with a fever and septic shock. Blood cultures are drawn and empiric antibiotics are started. The patient remains hypotensive despite fluid resuscitation and vasopressor support. The blood culture results reveal a gram-negative bacteremia with an unknown source. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the clinical trial to evaluate the safety and performance of the Seraph 100 Microbind Affinity Blood Filter in reducing pathogen load from the blood in septic patients with suspected, life-threatening bloodstream infection. The patient has received IV antibiotic therapy for less than 12 hours and has a Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score that has increased by at least two points since admission. The patient's Procalcitonin (PCT) levels are >0.5 ng/mL. The patient has no comorbid conditions or other medical, social, or psychological conditions that would limit their ability to participate in the clinical investigation or comply with follow-up requirements. The patient provides written consent to participate in the trial.

The patient is a 68-year-old man who has been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He has never been treated with chemotherapy before but has been receiving androgen deprivation therapy. Recent tests have shown that his cancer has become resistant to this therapy and his PSA levels have started to rise. The patient is otherwise healthy without any serious medical conditions or laboratory abnormalities. He has no known brain metastases or infectious hepatitis. The patient has not been previously treated with temsirolimus and is willing to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements. He has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 2 or less and adequate liver and renal function. His bone marrow function is adequate and he has no other malignancies. The patient agrees to use a latex condom during sexual contact with a female of childbearing potential. His last treatment for prostate cancer was at least 4 weeks ago. The patient is eligible to participate in this open label phase II study and will receive single agent Torisel® at 25 mg weekly until disease progression, patient's withdrawal, unacceptable toxicity or the investigator's discretion.

A 65-year-old male patient is admitted to the ICU after being resuscitated from a cardiac arrest. The patient was found unresponsive at home and brought to the emergency department where he was resuscitated with CPR and defibrillation. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia but is otherwise healthy. Upon arrival to the ICU, the patient is intubated and started on therapeutic hypothermia. He is currently stable on low doses of epinephrine and norepinephrine infusions. The patient is responsive to verbal commands but agitated and restless despite the use of sedatives. He has no known contraindications to the use of inhaled sevoflurane. The patient's family has given consent for him to participate in the study. Arterial line has been placed for hemodynamic monitoring. The patient did not have a prolonged no flow or low flow period during the cardiac arrest.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been struggling with depression for the past 6 months. She has a history of anxiety and depression and has attempted therapy and medication in the past without significant improvement. She is currently not taking any medications for her depression and is open to trying alternative treatments. She owns a Smartphone and is able to commit to doing program practices for 10 minutes a day, 6 days a week for 12 weeks. She has a PHQ-9 score of 12. She has no history of bipolar disorder or psychotic disorder, cognitive impairment, or substance use disorder in the past 3 months. She reports no active suicidal ideation or intent to act. She is not pregnant, breastfeeding, or desiring to become pregnant in the next 6 months. She does not have any major medical illnesses or chronic conditions, and is not currently taking any medications or supplements. She is willing to have her blood drawn at the beginning, 6 weeks, and end of the program to test for high sensitivity-CRP (hs-CRP) levels and interleukin (IL-6) levels. She is willing to wear a HRVB device and is open to receiving curcumin supplementation if randomized to the MHP-CUR group. She speaks and understands English well.

The patient is a 64-year-old woman who has been experiencing severe pain in her right knee due to osteoarthritis. She has been recommended by her orthopedic surgeon to undergo an elective primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty (TKA) to relieve her pain. She has a BMI of 32 kg/m2 and is classified as an American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) physical Class 2. She has no known allergies to chili peppers, capsaicin or the components of CA-008, ropivacaine, ketorolac, acetaminophen, fentanyl, hydromorphone, morphine or oxycodone. She is not on any disallowed medications, except for a stable dose of anti-hypertensive medication. She is willing to sign the informed consent form and complete study procedures and pain scales. She is fluent in English and able to communicate meaningfully. She has no concurrent painful condition other than the pain in her knee to be replaced, which may require pain treatment during the study period. She is willing and able to return for outpatient follow-up visits as required.

35F with a history of myopia since age 13 with stable refraction for the past 5 years on -4.00 sph, -0.50 cyl OD and -4.25 sph, -0.75 cyl OS. Patient is a graphic designer and has complained of reduced quality of vision and glare in twilight or night for the past few months. Patient reports that this has started to impact her ability to work and drive safely at night. The patient denies any other ocular or systemic medical history, as well as any history of ocular surgeries or trauma. On examination, visual acuity is 20/20 with current correction. Binocular vision is normal without any strabismus or amblyopia. Pupils are reactive and normal in size. Slit-lamp examination and fundus examination are unremarkable. The patient is not taking any medications and denies any hormonal variances. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate a night spectacle correction to improve her quality of vision in low light conditions.

This is a 55-year-old male with Parkinson's disease. He was diagnosed with PD based on the Movement Disorder Society (MDS)-PD criteria established in 2015. His Hoehn-Yahr stage is III, and he has been taking anti-Parkinson's disease drugs for over 28 days. His MMSE score is 28, and he has not received any antidepressant or antipsychotic drugs within the past 2 weeks. He understands and is willing to sign a written informed consent document. He does not have any history of psychiatric disorders or suicidal tendencies. He does not have severe cognitive impairment, chronic organ failure or malignant tumors. His ALT and AST levels are within normal reference ranges, and his leucocyte count is above 1000/μl. He is not pregnant or lactating. He has not participated in any other drug tests or received any other research medication within the last 90 days.

A 12-year-old student was diagnosed with dysorthographia. He is currently in the 5th grade and has difficulty spelling words correctly when writing essays or taking exams. He is receiving support from a speech therapist and an occupational therapist. He is motivated to improve his writing and communication skills. He enjoys playing video games and reading books. His parents report that he is otherwise healthy and has no other medical conditions. He is currently in the process of being evaluated for his reading level on the Evalouette test. He has no visual disturbances that would prevent him from using a computer tool.

A 35-year-old male with a history of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection presents with fatigue, abdominal pain, and dark urine. He was previously treated with PEG-Intron plus ribavirin therapy for 12 weeks but was unable to tolerate the treatment due to severe flu-like symptoms and depression. His HCV genotype is 1. He does not have any other medical conditions associated with chronic liver disease such as hemochromatosis, autoimmune hepatitis, or alcoholic liver disease. On physical examination, he has mild hepatomegaly without splenomegaly or ascites. Laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes with an ALT of 85 U/L and AST of 75 U/L. His viral load is 1,250,000 IU/mL. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and agrees to use 2 forms of contraception during the study.

A 56-year-old man presents with a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. He has not received any prior chemotherapy, biologic/molecular targeted therapy or radiotherapy for head and neck cancer. The patient has measurable disease and has been diagnosed with locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (SCCHN) at stage III-IVB. He has not had any prior surgical therapy aside from an incisional or excisional biopsy, and organ sparing procedures such as debulking of airway compromising tumors or neck dissection in a patient with an existing primary tumor. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1 and is 18 years or older. The patient has provided informed consent and agrees to have available archival tumor samples, unstained slides, or blocks from previous diagnostic or therapeutic procedures submitted for correlative studies, including assessment of target molecules EGFR, VEGF, and related biomarkers. The patient's absolute neutrophil count is at or above 1500/µl, and platelet count is at or above 100,000/µl. The patient's creatinine clearance is 60 ml/min or higher calculated using the Cockcroft-Gault formula, and his total bilirubin is within normal limits and AST/ALT is less than 3 times the upper limit of normal. The patient has no significant baseline sensory or motor neurologic deficits and does not have HIV. The patient has not had any significant vascular disease or history of myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 12 months prior to Day 1. The patient has not had any major surgical procedure or core biopsy within 28 days prior to Day 1, and has not had abdominal fistula or gastrointestinal perforation within 6 months prior to Day 1. The patient is not pregnant or breast-feeding.

The patient is a 73-year-old female who is generally healthy and has a BMI of 25. She is a non-smoker and has normal blood pressure and heart rate. She has no history of cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastro-intestinal, hepatic, renal, metabolic, hematological, neurologic, psychiatric, systemic or infectious disease. She does not experience frequent headaches or migraine, recurrent nausea, or vomiting. She does not have symptomatic hypotension and is not taking any prohibited medications. She is able to take up to 8 capsules of study medication and understands the nature and purpose of the study. She has not participated in any clinical trials in the last 3 months and has not received compensation beyond the approved limit. The patient is willing to refrain from consuming certain foods and supplements at least two weeks before inclusion.

A 7-year-old boy was recently diagnosed with Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH) after experiencing bone pain and swelling in his right arm. Imaging studies revealed multiple bone lesions and biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. He has no other significant medical history and is otherwise healthy. He has not received any prior treatment for LCH. His parents are concerned about potential side effects of chemotherapy but are willing to explore all treatment options to ensure the best outcome for their son.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been experiencing pelvic pain for the past two years. She has a history of endometriosis and has tried various treatments such as pain medications, hormonal therapy, and laparoscopic surgery, but has not experienced significant relief. She is not pregnant nor lactating. She has no history or suspicion of hormone-dependent tumors. She is currently not undergoing any treatment for endometriosis and is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and has no other conditions that would prevent her from participating.

A 2-day-old male infant was born full-term with a weight of 3.5 kg to a 30-year-old mother with a pre-pregnancy BMI of 22 kg/m2. The mother has elected not to breastfeed and has no history of hormonal or metabolic diseases, illicit drug or alcohol use during pregnancy. The baby has no cognitive or physical developmental disorders. The parents have provided written informed consent and are willing to comply with the study protocol. They speak French fluently and can be contacted directly by telephone throughout the study. The infant is eligible to participate in the clinical trial to evaluate the growth of healthy term infants fed a partially hydrolyzed follow-up formula.

A 39-year-old female presented with a history of chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after a hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). She complained of skin and fascial thickening, joint contractures, and limited range of motion at the shoulder and elbow. She also reported fatigue and occasional night sweats. Her medical history was significant for hypertension, hypothyroidism, and depression. She takes Levothyroxine, Lisinopril, and Sertraline. She is a non-smoker and has no known allergies. She had received corticosteroids, cyclosporine, and sirolimus for GVHD in the past but has not received any medications for GVHD in the last 4 weeks. Her current dose of prednisone is 20 mg daily. She had no history of hepatitis B or C infection, and her liver function tests were within normal range. Her Karnofsky performance status was 80%. She had no history of prior treatment with imatinib or rituximab. She had no active infections or substance abuse, and she was not pregnant or planning to become pregnant. She agreed to use a form of FDA-approved contraception during the study period. She provided informed consent and was willing to comply with the study protocol.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with a recent diagnosis of CD20 positive DLBCL. He has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for DLBCL. He has a performance status (ECOG) of 1 and has been diagnosed with Ann Arbor stage III. He has at least one bidimensionally measurable lesion of 2 cm by conventional CT. His cardiac ejection fraction is 55% as measured by MUGA. He has a serum creatinine level of 1.5mg/dL and a bilirubin level of 1.8mg/dL. His hemoglobin level is 10g/dL, absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 2000/μL, and platelet count is 85,000/μL. He has a life expectancy of more than 6 months. He has no known history of HIV seropositivity or HCV(+), but he is HBV carrier, and he will be given primary prophylaxis using antiviral agents to prevent HBV reactivation. He has no other malignancies within the past 5 years except for a curatively treated non-melanoma skin cancer. He is not pregnant or lactating, and he is not a woman of childbearing potential. He has no known hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or their ingredients. He is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 28-year old woman was diagnosed with HIV six months ago. She is currently on a once daily regimen of antiretroviral therapy. She lives alone in a small apartment and works as a freelance graphic designer. She reports being forgetful and struggles with remembering to take her medication at the same time every day. She has never missed a dose but worries that she might forget or get distracted. She owns a smart phone and is comfortable using it for different purposes. The patient has no history of substance use, visual or hearing impairment, or cognitive impairment. She is willing to participate in the study to help improve her adherence to medications. She is interested in learning more about the smart phone application and how it can help her remember to take her medication on time. She is excited to have an opportunity to contribute to advancing HIV research.

Aizat is a 28 year old Kyrgyz man who was born, raised and currently resides in a high-altitude area of Kyrgyzstan at an altitude of 3000 meters. He is a farmer and spends most of his day working on his farm. He has been experiencing shortness of breath, fatigue and occasional chest pain for the past year. He went to a local hospital where he was diagnosed with high altitude pulmonary hypertension (HAPH) based on clinical presentation and echocardiography which showed a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 35 mmHg. He has never smoked and has no history of other lung or cardiovascular diseases. He is interested in participating in the study and agrees to attend follow-up examinations.

The patient is a healthy 25-year-old female who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to study the safety and efficacy of NF135 CPS immunization. She is currently not taking any medications and has no known medical conditions. She is willing to stay in the Netherlands during the challenge period and is reachable by mobile phone throughout the entire study period. She is willing to use adequate contraception during the study period and not to breastfeed. She has signed informed consent and is available to attend all study visits. The patient has not been diagnosed with malaria in the past or participated in any malaria vaccine study. She has not received any vaccinations in the 3 months prior to the start of the study and has no plan to receive any other vaccination during the study period or up to 90 days thereafter. The patient is not an employee or student of the department of Medical Microbiology of the Radboudumc or the department of Internal Medicine. She is not taking any immunosuppressive, antibiotic, antimalarial, or other immune-modifying drugs within three months prior to study onset, and is not expected to use any such drugs during the study period.

A 45-year-old male stroke survivor came to the clinic for a follow-up visit. He had a stroke 2 years ago, which affected the right side of his body. He has been able to regain some function with physical therapy, but still requires an ankle foot orthosis (AFO) on his right leg to walk. He has been using the same AFO for the past year, and reports some discomfort and difficulty with walking for extended periods of time. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial comparing two different settings of a commercially available AFO to see if it can improve his walking ability. He has no other significant medical history, is not currently receiving physical therapy, and has no other neurologic or musculoskeletal diagnoses that might impair his gait. His blood pressure and heart rate are stable, and he has no recent history of cardiac or pulmonary disease. He is able to comply with directions and is willing to cooperate with the research team.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a benign lung tumor. She has been experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath for the past few months. She is a non-smoker and does not have any significant medical history or allergies. She works as a teacher and is married with two children. She is an active individual and enjoys yoga and hiking. She is scheduled to undergo minimal invasive thoracoscopic surgery to remove the tumor. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the role of acupuncture in post-operative pain control. She has no abnormal function of coagulation, and her platelet count and INR are within normal limits. She has no severe comorbidity and is willing to cooperate in the study procedures.

The patient is a 56-year-old male who has been diagnosed with relapsed Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). He has previously received first-line treatment with R-CHOP and has experienced a relapse. He is ineligible for high-dose therapy/stem cell transplantation due to his age and comorbidities. His ECOG performance status is 1. He has measurable disease sites on CT scan, with the largest lesion measuring 3 cm. His lab results show adequate hepatic and renal function, and adequate hematologic function. His PT/INR and PTT are both within normal range. He has not undergone any chemotherapy, external beam radiation therapy, or anticancer antibodies within the last 2 weeks, and has not received radio- or toxin-immunoconjugates within the last 10 weeks. He has not previously taken ibrutinib or lenalidomide. He is willing to participate in an international, multicenter, open-label study and meet the inclusion criteria for the study.

A 15-year-old high school student, who is fluent in English, is interested in participating in a study that can help her give back to her community. She has no chronic medical illnesses and is not on any medications. Although her family is of low socio-economic status, she is motivated and hardworking. She has no history of smoking or alcohol use. She is physically active and participates in school sports. She is enthusiastic about getting involved in volunteering activities and is excited to learn more about the benefits of volunteering on cardiovascular health.

The patient is a 14-year-old female who was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes mellitus six months ago. She presents to the hospital with a three-day history of vomiting, abdominal pain, and increased thirst and urination. Her blood glucose level is 450 mg/dL, and her pH level is 7.1, indicating metabolic acidosis. She is diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and is started on insulin therapy and intravenous fluids. She has no known history of cardiovascular disease or other metabolic disorders. Her physical examination reveals tachycardia, dry mucous membranes, and decreased skin turgor, suggestive of dehydration. She has no signs of respiratory distress or neurological deficits. Her urine analysis shows ketonuria, and her serum electrolyte levels reveal low potassium and low bicarbonate levels. An ECG and echocardiogram are ordered to assess for any cardiac involvement.

The patient is a 32-year-old male who experienced a third-degree burn injury from an accident in his workplace. The burns cover approximately 40% of his total body surface area, including his arms, chest, and legs. He has been admitted to the hospital for treatment and is currently stable. He has no history of organ failure, tuberculosis, or any other medical conditions that would preclude him from participating in an exercise program. He is married and has two children. He works as a construction worker and is generally physically active. He is willing to participate in the exercise program as part of his treatment and hopes that it will help him recover more quickly. He is aware of the study's purpose and has given his consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old Caucasian male with Hodgkin's lymphoma is seeking treatment for his relapsed disease after completing first-line chemotherapy. He has less than complete response to chemotherapy and has bulky disease measuring greater than 5cm. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history, and has never smoked or used drugs. He has a normal renal function, as estimated by serum creatinine clearance, and adequate hepatic function. His pulmonary function and cardiac function are also adequate, with FEV1, FVC and DLCO at or above 50% of expected corrected for hemoglobin and left ventricular ejection fraction greater than or equal to 40%. His Zubrod performance status is less than 2. He has not received prior whole brain irradiation, has no active hepatitis B or C, no active inflammatory bowel disease, and is not currently infected with HIV. He has not received radiation therapy in the month prior to enrollment.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing persistent chronic low back pain for the past 9 months. The pain is primarily neuropathic in origin and is accompanied by radiculopathy. She has tried various conservative therapies such as physiotherapy, chiropractic, and hydrotherapy, but none of them have provided long-term relief. Her VAS back pain score is currently at 70 mm. She has not undergone any open spinal surgery and has a total daily dose of opioids equivalent to 150mg of morphine. She has undergone an MRI within the previous 6 months, which showed no evidence of spinal instability, fractures, tumors, or infections. Based on her medical history, the investigator believes that she is a suitable candidate for HF10 spinal cord stimulation.

No patient description can be generated for this study as it is a population-based longitudinal study that does not involve direct patient recruitment or intervention. The study will use existing data from various databases to examine how neighborhood-level factors interact with individual characteristics to predict incidence of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality.

The patient is a 4 year old male who was referred to the dental clinic due to severe early childhood caries. He has been experiencing tooth pain and sensitivity while eating and drinking. The patient has no known chronic medical conditions and is not currently taking any medication. The patient's parents report that they have been brushing his teeth regularly, but he often consumes sugary snacks and drinks. The child's medical history is unremarkable, and he has no known allergies. The patient is cooperative during the dental examination and is able to tolerate the necessary procedures under general anesthesia. The patient's primary dentition is evaluated and found to have severe decay. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is randomly assigned to one of the four groups receiving a fluoride varnish. Follow-up saliva samples are collected from the patient one month and three months after the treatment.

Patient is a 45-year-old man from the United States who comes in for an evaluation for obesity and metabolic disease. He is married and has two children. His past medical history is remarkable for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type-2 diabetes mellitus. His current medications include lisinopril, simvastatin, and metformin. His BMI is 45, BP: 140/85, HR: 80/min. He has been struggling with weight loss and has tried multiple diets and exercise programs without success. He is interested in bariatric surgery and is considering the loop duodenal switch procedure.

This is a 52 year old female who has been experiencing dry eye symptoms for the past 8 months. She reports a persistent feeling of grittiness, burning, and irritation in both eyes. She has been using over-the-counter eye drops for relief, but finds that they only provide temporary relief. She has never had any ocular infections or inflammation. She wears glasses for reading and has not worn contact lenses in the past year. She has not had LASIK surgery or any other ocular surgeries. She is interested in participating in this clinical trial to potentially find a more effective treatment for her dry eye symptoms. She has provided written informed consent and is willing to comply with the study requirements. She has not used any medications known to cause ocular drying in the past 30 days.

The patient is a 24-year-old male who is overweight and has a waist circumference of 102cm. He has no personal history of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, metabolic disease, or dyslipidemia. He is a non-smoker and has been weight stable for the past 6 months. The patient is able to walk for a long period of time without any issues. He is not taking any medications that could influence lipid or carbohydrate metabolism or immune system function. The patient has no physical limitations that would prevent him from participating in structured exercise. He is interested in participating in this study to understand the impact of dietary conditions on the acute responses to exercise.

The patient is a 42-year-old female who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and started using a CPAP machine 6 months ago. She reports struggling with the CPAP mask, finding it uncomfortable and causing irritation to her skin. She has tried different mask types but has not found one that suits her needs. Her AHI from the diagnostic night was 15. She is a non-smoker and does not have any significant medical history. Her BMI is 32, and she is otherwise healthy. She is interested in participating in the study to evaluate the usability and performance of the Headgear with a CPAP Mask as a potential alternative to her current mask. She is willing to use the headgear for the required duration of 2-4 weeks and is able to give informed consent.

This is a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with urothelial carcinoma after presenting with symptoms of hematuria and urinary urgency. He underwent a transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) which confirmed the diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma. Following the TURBT, he received six cycles of cisplatin and gemcitabine chemotherapy. Unfortunately, his disease has progressed and imaging studies have confirmed metastatic urothelial carcinoma. He is now experiencing increasing pain and difficulty with urination. He is still able to perform his activities of daily living but has noticed a decrease in his energy level. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial and has been deemed eligible for a study evaluating the combination of AMG 386 and docetaxel for the treatment of advanced urothelial cancer.

A 56-year-old male presenting with general fatigue, loss of appetite, and weight loss for the past 2 months. He reports feeling generally unwell and has noticed mild abdominal discomfort. The patient reports no significant past medical history, no previous surgeries, and no significant family history of any hematological disorders. Physical examination revealed splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and mild pallor. Laboratory results showed a hemoglobin level of 11.2 g/dL, white blood cell count of 18,200/μL, and platelet count of 750,000/μL. A bone marrow biopsy was performed, which showed hypercellularity with marked pleomorphism and increased numbers of megakaryocytes. The patient was diagnosed with essential thrombocythemia (ET) based on the World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. The patient was started on hydroxyurea, and his platelet count decreased to 400,000/μL after 1 month of treatment. The patient was then enrolled in the clinical trial to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of CD26 positive stem cells in classic myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs).

A 55-year-old male patient was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after experiencing fatigue, shortness of breath, and frequent infections. He has no prior history of cancer or chemotherapy. His cardiac function is normal, and his bilirubin and creatinine levels are within normal limits. He has an ECOG performance status of 1. He is currently undergoing induction chemotherapy with cytarabine and daunorubicin. If he achieves complete remission, he will be randomized to receive either consolidation chemotherapy with daunorubicin or idarubicin, followed by maintenance treatment with interleukin 2 or no treatment. He has signed the informed consent form to participate in the clinical trial.

The patient is a 55-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with COPD for the past 5 years. She presents with a persistent cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing. She has a history of smoking for 20 years, quitting 5 years ago. Her FEV1 measurement is 60% of predicted normal value post-bronchodilator. She is currently taking inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators as prescribed by her physician. She reports occasional exacerbations of her symptoms, but has not experienced one in the past 30 days. She has no other clinically relevant diseases or disorders. She is interested in participating in the study and is willing to comply with all study requirements.

Patient is a 30-year-old pregnant woman from the United States who is scheduled for an elective repeat cesarean section. She is in her 39th week of gestation and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy. She has a BMI of 25, BP: 120/70, HR: 80/min, and has no history of any significant medical conditions. She has consented to participate in the study and is willing to be placed in different positions during the procedure.

34 year old male with a history of neurofibromatosis type 2 diagnosed at the age of 24. The patient has a history of bilateral acoustic tumors and underwent surgical resection on both sides, resulting in total hearing loss. The patient is unable to communicate effectively with others and relies on lip reading and written communication. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the use of the penetrating auditory brainstem implant (PABI) to restore some auditory sensation. The patient speaks English as his primary language and has no medical conditions that would contraindicate the surgical procedure.

A 28-year-old male daily marijuana smoker who is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the analgesic effects of smoked marijuana and oral THC. The patient must be between the ages of 21-45, currently using marijuana and able to perform study procedures. The patient should not have a history of heart disease, significant medical illness, current or repeated use of illicit drugs other than marijuana, or a recent history of significant violent behavior. Women must be practicing an effective form of birth control and should not be currently pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient should not be currently on parole or probation and should not be seeking drug treatment.

The patient is a 25-year-old male who has been struggling with opioid addiction for the past 3 years. He has tried multiple treatment programs in the past, including methadone and buprenorphine-naloxone, but has not been able to sustain abstinence. He is currently seeking treatment for his addiction and has agreed to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of extended-release naltrexone hydrochloride injectable suspension (Vivitrol®) for opioid addiction. He meets the inclusion criteria for the study, including having a current diagnosis of opioid dependence based on the DSM-V criteria, being enrolled in the Norwegian national opioid maintenance treatment program, and completing a stay in a controlled environment with restricted access to substances of abuse for a minimum of seven days. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and is capable of understanding the study requirements. He has no known allergies or medical conditions that would prevent him from participating in the study. He is motivated to achieve sustained abstinence and hopes that this treatment will help him achieve his goal.

The patient is a 45-year-old man from Porto Alegre, Brazil, who has been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis C. He has previously been referred to a gastroenterologist or infectious disease specialist in the Brazilian Public Health System and has undergone previous fibrosis staging or laboratory tests for APRI score calculation. The patient has not undergone treatment with direct acting antivirals and does not have HIV coinfection with antiretroviral treatment incompatible with HCV antivirals. He does not have any significant comorbidity that may interfere with HCV treatment and meets the eligibility criteria for the clinical trial that aims to monitor HCV treatment using telemedicine. The patient is willing to use telemedicine tools, such as instant messaging application, telephone, and video calls, to monitor his HCV treatment and agrees to abide by the requirements of the study.

The patient is a 56 year-old male who was admitted to the Emergency Department with chest pain and palpitations. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he is taking medication. He is a smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. Upon arrival, an ECG revealed ventricular fibrillation and he was immediately given CPR and defibrillation. Despite initial successful defibrillation, he developed recurrent VF and is now in a critical condition. He has been intubated and is receiving mechanical ventilation. He will be enrolled in this clinical trial to determine the optimal level of defibrillation energy for his condition. He meets the eligibility criteria as he is over 21 years of age and has a shockable rhythm.

Pt is a 65yo M with a history of a left hemiplegic stroke 6 months ago. He has significant weakness in his left upper extremity, with a Medical Research Council scale score of 2 for finger and wrist flexor/extensor and elbow pronation/supination. He has been receiving conventional occupational therapy for upper extremity rehabilitation, but has not seen significant improvement in his functional abilities. The patient is able to communicate effectively, has no severe cognitive impairments or pain that would impede rehabilitation, and has no predisposing psychological or neurological disorders. The patient is interested in participating in this study to explore the potential benefits of a novel game rehabilitation system for upper extremity function.

54-year-old male with a confirmed diagnosis of metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon. The patient has unresectable and measurable metastatic disease that meets the RECIST criteria. The patient has not received any prior palliative chemotherapy or bevacizumab. The patient has not experienced bowel obstruction or subobstruction, and does not have a history of inflammatory enteropathy or extensive intestinal resection. The patient has an ECOG Performance Status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has adequate hematological function, liver function, and renal function. The patient is not currently pregnant or lactating and is willing to use effective means of contraception.

The patient is a 47-year-old male with a history of hypertension and smoking. He presents to the emergency department with chest pain that started about 2 hours ago. The pain is described as a heavy pressure sensation in the chest, radiating to the left arm and jaw. He also reports shortness of breath and sweating. He denies any previous cardiac history or surgeries. His blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg, heart rate is 95 beats per minute and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. His ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. The lab results show elevated troponin levels. The patient is diagnosed with Acute ST Segment Elevated Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) and is eligible for the clinical trial. The patient is willing and able to provide informed consent. He does not have any contraindications to the study medications and does not have cardiogenic shock or bleeding diathesis. He has no history of cerebrovascular accident or transient ischemic attack, and his platelet count and hemoglobin levels are within normal range. He does not have any planned surgery in the next 6 weeks and does not have a serious illness that may reduce his life expectancy.

The patient is a 28-year-old woman who has a history of drug use and is currently on probation. She reports engaging in unprotected vaginal sex with multiple male partners in the past 90 days and using illicit drugs in the past 6 months. She does not have a monogamous relationship and does not know the HIV status of her partners. She is able to speak and understand English and is willing to participate in assessments and intervention sessions. She is not actively trying to get pregnant or have a baby. She does not have any psychiatric or cognitive impairments that would prevent her from completing the informed consent process. She was not born male.

A 45 year old female with a BMI of 35.2 kg/m2 is interested in losing weight. She has a history of hypertension and occasional heartburn. She is otherwise healthy and not taking any medications. She is a non-smoker and has no plans to move out of the area within the 12-week study period. She is able to provide informed consent and has received physician's approval to participate in the study. She is not diagnosed with diabetes, coronary event, or any medical condition that precludes adherence to study dietary recommendations. She is not following any weight loss program, previously had bariatric surgery, or currently using weight loss medication. She has no diagnosis of an eating disorder.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) for the past 7 years. She has been treated with various antidepressant medications, but her depression has not improved significantly. Her current Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAMD) score is 20, indicating moderate to severe depression. She has not received any previous treatment with repeated Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) or Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the efficacy of priming rTMS sessions before ECT for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) patients. She is in good health and meets all the inclusion criteria for the study. She has no history of epilepsy or any neurological or systemic disorder that could affect cognition. She provides informed, written consent to participate in the study.

The patient is a 60-year-old male who has been diagnosed with chronic tricuspid regurgitation. He complains of shortness of breath and fatigue during physical activities such as walking or climbing stairs. He has been on diuretic medication but has not seen any significant improvement. The patient is currently in NYHA Class III. The echocardiography shows moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation with an annular diameter of 45 mm and valve systolic pulmonary pressure (sPAP) of 55 mmHg. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 45%. The local site Heart Team has determined that surgery is not a suitable treatment option for this patient. The patient has given written informed consent in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation. The patient does not have any other significant medical conditions, and has not had a cerebrovascular accident (CVA) within the past 6 months. The patient is able to perform a cardiopulmonary exercise test. The patient is a suitable candidate for this clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with bipolar disorder. She has been on several different antipsychotic medications over the past few years but has not found relief from her symptoms. She has experienced weight gain and other side effects from these medications, which have negatively impacted her quality of life. Her doctor has recommended that she participate in a clinical trial to evaluate the effectiveness of pharmacogenomic decision support with GeneSight Psychotropic in guiding the treatment with antipsychotics. The patient is willing and able to provide written informed consent to participate in the study and is committed to completing all study-related procedures. She is not currently on a restricted diet or undergoing weight-reducing interventions. She does not have a history of hypothyroidism or significant medical conditions that would exclude her from participating in the study. She has not participated in another clinical trial within the past 30 days and is not pregnant or lactating.

55 year old male diagnosed with essential tremor for more than 3 years. The patient has been experiencing significant tremors in the right upper limb, causing distress and affecting daily activities. He has been on anti-tremor medication for the past 6 months with little improvement. The patient is able to sign written informed consent in Hebrew and is willing to comply with all study requirements. He has no active implants or major medical conditions that would interfere with participation in the study. The patient has not participated in any other study with an investigational drug or device in the past 90 days. He is not currently pregnant nor attempting to get pregnant. The patient has no other significant neurological or psychiatric disease other than essential tremor. He has not undergone any previous thalamotomy, pallidotomy, or deep brain stimulation procedure. The patient is not treated with any drugs that may induce tremors, nor does he abuse drugs or alcohol. The patient has no malignancy in the past 2 years and is not diagnosed with a terminal illness associated with survival less than 12 months.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with end-stage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). He has been on the waiting list for a lung transplant for the past 6 months and has been experiencing increasing difficulty with breathing and fatigue. He has a history of smoking for 30 years and quit 10 years ago. His current pulmonary function tests show severe airflow obstruction with an FEV1 of 20% predicted and a DLCO of 30% predicted. His oxygen saturation at rest is 88% on room air. He has been using supplemental oxygen at home for the past year. He has a medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medications. He is currently not working due to his illness and is receiving disability benefits. He has a supportive family and lives with his wife and two adult children. He is willing to participate in clinical trials to increase his chances of receiving a lung transplant.

62-year-old female with a long-standing history of open-angle glaucoma (OAG) who underwent uncomplicated phacoemulsification cataract removal and intraocular lens implantation. As a part of her treatment, she received a CyPass Micro-Stent implantation using the CyPass system Model 241. Her medical history was significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which were well controlled with medications. She had no history of any ophthalmic surgeries or interventions prior to this procedure, and she was not diagnosed with any acute angle closure, traumatic, congenital, malignant, uveitic, or neovascular glaucoma. She was compliant with follow-up visits and medication regimen.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who was recently diagnosed with a 10mm kidney stone. He underwent ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy to remove the stone and had a ureteral stent placed two weeks ago. He has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. He works as a construction worker and is physically active. He has no known allergies to medications. He is married and has two children. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he does drink alcohol occasionally. His physical exam is unremarkable, and he has no signs of infection. His baseline labs were within normal limits. He is scheduled for cystoscopy with ureteral stent removal in two days and has been approached to participate in the clinical trial.

A 28-year-old healthy male smoker with a pack history of 10 pack years presented to the clinic for the Study to Investigate Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics & Pharmacodynamics of Single & Repeat Doses of GSK2269557. He has no history of liver disease, congestive heart failure, coronary insufficiency, or cardiac arrhythmia. His spirometry results were normal, and his FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratio were greater than or equal to 80% predicted and 70%, respectively. He does not have a history of drug or other allergy, and he has not taken any medication, including vitamins or supplements, within the last 7 days. He is willing to comply with the protocol and has given written informed consent. He does not consume red wine, seville oranges, grapefruit or grapefruit juice and/or pummelos, exotic citrus fruits, grapefruit hybrids or fruit juices.

52-year-old male with newly diagnosed stage III non-small cell lung cancer, currently undergoing radiation therapy. He has been experiencing fatigue for several weeks, which has made it difficult for him to work and perform his daily activities. He has no history of diabetes, tuberculosis, or fungal infections. He is not currently taking any corticosteroids and has no allergies to medications. He is willing to complete the study surveys and pill diary and understands the requirements of the study.

45-year-old woman with a BMI of 42 and a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and sleep apnea. She has a sedentary lifestyle due to her weight and experiences difficulty performing daily activities. She has tried several weight loss programs in the past, but none have been successful in achieving long-term weight loss. She is interested in bariatric surgery as a potential option to improve her health and quality of life. She is able to provide written informed consent and is willing to complete questionnaires and follow-up visits.

45-year-old male with a history of plaque psoriasis for the past 5 years with at least 20% of total body surface area (BSA) affected. He has been on topical treatments but has not achieved significant improvement. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of PF-06826647. He has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any medications. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and follow the contraception requirements if necessary.

A 54-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF) for the past 5 years came to the clinic for a follow-up appointment. He has been taking warfarin (VKA) for the past year without any significant interruptions. He has an active lifestyle, exercises regularly, and maintains a healthy diet. He works as a salesman and travels frequently for work. He has no allergies to any food or drugs and takes no other medications besides the warfarin. He speaks fluent German and is willing to participate in a structured patient interview. He has not participated in any other clinical or observational studies in the past 3 months.

The patient is a 58-year-old male who was diagnosed with Stage IV Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) with ALK translocation. He has already undergone one round of standard systemic therapy for lung cancer but experienced adverse side effects and did not see much improvement. The patient has measureable disease outside of the radiation field and has a life expectancy of at least 3 months. He has an ECOG performance status of 1 and has not received any systemic therapy for the past 2 weeks. The patient has completed the baseline studies required for eligibility, including a CT scan within the past 28 days, and has tested positive for ALK mutation. He is not currently taking any medications or consuming any foods that are clinically relevant CYP3A inhibitors or inducers. The patient has normal QT corrected using Fridericia's correction method (QTcf) and serum troponin level. He has not had any active infections or systemic use of antibiotics within the past 72 hours. The patient does not have significant co-morbid conditions or diseases that would interfere with the study. He is not pregnant or lactating, and agrees to use adequate methods of birth control throughout the study. The patient has not received any prior treatment with 17-AAG, DMAG, or any other known Hsp90 inhibitor. He does not have active keratitis or keratoconjunctivitis and has an alkaline phosphatase level within the required range. The patient does not have clinically active brain metastasis, uncontrolled seizure disorder, ongoing spinal cord compression, or carcinomatous meningitis.

57 year old man with locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma who has undergone prior chemotherapy treatment with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. CT scan shows measurable disease per RECIST 1.1. ECOG performance status is 1. Past Medical History: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction 5 years ago, hypothyroidism, arthritis. Medications: Metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin, levothyroxine, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, prednisone.

A 45-year-old Caucasian woman visited her dermatologist due to a suspicious mole on her upper arm. The biopsy revealed it was a melanoma, and further testing showed that it was stage III. She underwent surgical resection of the lesion and has no evidence of disease after the surgery. She has one undissected axillary lymph node. She tested positive for HLA-A3. Her medical history is significant for mild arthritis requiring non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. She has no known active addiction to alcohol or drugs. She has never participated in another clinical study within the past 30 days. She is not currently receiving chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunosuppressive therapy. She is not pregnant or nursing, and she is willing to use effective contraception. Her weight is within the range of eligibility for the study. She has no uncontrolled diabetes, and her hemoglobin A1C level is below 7%. She has no known or suspected allergy to any component of the study vaccines. She is HIV-negative and has no autoimmune disorder with visceral involvement. She meets all other eligibility criteria for the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old healthy woman who works in a healthcare setting. She has not received any influenza vaccination in the last year but has received other routine vaccinations according to the national immunization schedule. She does not currently take any medications and has no known allergies. She is sexually active and uses oral contraceptives for birth control. She has a regular menstrual cycle and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She does not have any significant medical history and has not been diagnosed with any chronic illnesses. She has never had a serious reaction to any vaccine in the past, and she has not traveled outside of the country recently. She has not had any acute respiratory infections or fever in the last 3 months. She is willing to comply with all study procedures and is available for all study visits.

A 55-year-old male who was a smoker with a history of 20 pack-years came to the hospital with the symptom of persistent cough with sputum for 3 months. Chest X-ray showed a mass in the right lung. The patient underwent further imaging studies and biopsy, which confirmed the diagnosis of T1 non-small cell lung cancer. The patient underwent a right upper lobectomy and mediastinal lymph node dissection. The pathological report showed a tumor size of 2 cm and no lymph node metastasis. The patient did not receive any adjuvant treatment after surgery. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is taking medications to control these conditions. The patient has a good performance status with no other significant medical history.

The patient is a 45 year old Hispanic female who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis two years ago. She currently experiences pain, swelling, and stiffness in her hands, wrists, and knees. She reports that her symptoms have been getting progressively worse over the past few months, making it difficult for her to perform daily activities such as cooking, cleaning, and dressing herself. She works as a receptionist and finds it challenging to type and use the computer for extended periods. She has never undergone any upper limb surgery and has no uncorrected visual deficit that could compromise her functionality. She is mentally competent and can participate in the study. She is eager to participate in the clinical trial to find out what factors contribute to her activity limitations and how to manage them.

As this study is a population-based prospective study linked to the Quebec and New Brunswick public health surveys, no specific patient description is needed. Participants will be selected based on their previous participation in these surveys and their agreement to be contacted again for this study. However, they must be 18 years or older and reside in Sherbrooke, Moncton or Saguenay-Lac-St-Jean.

A 62-year-old woman presents with a history of hypertension that has been difficult to control with two or more antihypertensive medications. She also reports a gradual decline in kidney function over the past year, with an estimated GFR of 53 mL/min/1.73m2 according to the MDRD formula. She has a history of smoking but quit 5 years ago. Her medical record shows a previous diagnosis of atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis (ARAS) with a luminal reduction of 75% on intra-arterial angiography. She has no history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or stroke in the past 6 months. Her renal longitudinal diameter is 9 cm. She is not on dialysis and has no known allergy to contrast medium. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that evaluates the effectiveness of renal stenting with distal embolic protection.

The patient is a 24-year-old first-time mother who is currently enrolled in WIC and planning to attend her well-baby visits at a participating pediatric clinic. She is a non-smoker and abstained from smoking during pregnancy. She is fluent in both English and Spanish and has access to a telephone and the internet. She plans to stay in the area for at least 6 months after the birth of her infant. She gave birth to a healthy singleton baby at 39 weeks gestation. Both she and her infant have no known health conditions or risks that contraindicate breastfeeding or impact infant growth and development. She is excited to participate in the trial and learn more about healthy infant behaviors and feeding practices.

The patient is a neonate who has been diagnosed with respiratory failure and requires ECMO support. The baby was born at 35 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 2.5 kg. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy but developed premature rupture of membranes at 33 weeks. The baby was delivered by emergency cesarean section due to fetal distress. The baby required immediate resuscitation and intubation for respiratory distress. The baby has a history of meconium aspiration syndrome and has been receiving mechanical ventilation for the past 48 hours. The baby is stable on ECMO support with no evidence of acute neurological events. The baby does not have any known genetic or metabolic disorders.

A 35-year-old Caucasian male was admitted to the emergency room with second-degree burns covering 20% of his body surface area after a kitchen accident. He reports moderate to severe pain during wound care procedures, which is rated at 7/10 on the pain scale. He is currently on Fentanyl for pain management but is still experiencing significant pain. He speaks English fluently and is able to comprehend the study requirements. He is estimated to have a hospital stay of at least 5 days. He has no history of hearing or cognitive impairment and has a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 28. He has no past medical history of insensate conditions. He does not have any contraindications to the study medications. He is single and works as a chef. He has no history of depression or PTSD.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease by a neurologist. He is currently taking medication for his symptoms and has an established medication schedule and dosage. He has not experienced any mentation-related issues. He lives with his wife and is retired. He enjoys taking walks with his wife and spending time with his grandchildren. He has not made any changes to his medication or exercise routine in the past month. He is able to complete the exercise program and is committed to attending all classes. He has not missed more than 2 classes in a row in the past.

The patient is a 65 year old male who has been experiencing chronic pain for the past 6 months in the area where he previously had a Herpes Zoster (HZ) infection. The pain is severe and occurs almost daily, with a rating of 8 out of 10 on the visual analog scale (VAS). He has tried various topical and systemic treatments, including opioids, but has not found any significant relief. He has a history of hypertension, for which he takes medication, and he is a former smoker. He has not had any psychiatric illnesses or other indications for fat grafting. He is willing to participate in the study and is interested in exploring the potential benefits of fat grafting for his chronic postherpetic pain.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with endometrial cancer, which has recurred after platinum-based chemotherapy. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1. She has no other medical history and is not taking any medications. She has no allergies or hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs or their components. She has measurable disease according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1. Her absolute neutrophile count is 2.5 x 10^9/L, platelet count is 150 x 10^9/L, and hemoglobin is 11 g/dL. She has a calculated creatinine clearance of 80 ml/min and her serum total bilirubin is 0.8 x upper normal limit (UNL) and AST/ALT is 1.5 X UNL. She has a life expectancy of more than 16 weeks. She is of childbearing potential but is practicing two medically acceptable methods of birth control since consent signature during the study and 12 months after the end of treatment. She has given her written informed consent to participate in the study and is affiliated to a social insurance regime.

The patient is a 48-year-old woman who was diagnosed with high-grade serous ovarian cancer two years ago. She underwent primary cytoreductive surgery followed by platinum-based chemotherapy. She achieved a complete response and was closely monitored with regular follow-up visits. However, during her most recent visit, a CT scan revealed the presence of new lesions in the peritoneal cavity, indicating disease relapse. Her CA-125 level was elevated, confirming the disease progression. She has no significant medical history other than the ovarian cancer diagnosis. She has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and has a known BRCA mutation. She is planning to receive bevacizumab treatment and has not received any systemic treatment for her current relapse before signing informed consent form (ICF). She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to explore new treatment options and help advance ovarian cancer research.

A 45-year-old female presents with a history of chronic constipation for over 6 months. She has been having 2-3 bowel movements per week and experiences straining and lumpy stools. She has tried increasing fiber intake and taking over-the-counter laxatives but these have not been effective. She does not have any other relevant medical history or gastrointestinal symptoms. She has not had any recent abdominal surgeries or taken antibiotics in the past 4 weeks. She has a BMI of 25 and her weight has remained stable over the past 3 months. She is willing to maintain her normal dietary habits and physical activity levels throughout the study period. She is not currently on any medication or dietary supplements that may interfere with the study. She is a non-smoker and does not have any history of mental health disorders or immunological disorders. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written consent.

The patient is a 20 year old woman who recently gave birth to a healthy baby boy. She and her partner are concerned about their baby's health and are considering all options for ensuring his well-being. They are interested in learning more about the self-paid oral rotavirus vaccine but are unsure if it is the right choice for their baby. They are open to receiving information and guidance from medical professionals to help them make an informed decision. The baby has no fever or any contraindications for oral rotavirus. They are fluent in Chinese and are willing to participate in a clinical trial that aims to evaluate the effectiveness of decision aids in helping them make a decision about their baby's vaccination. Their age is within the eligibility criteria for the study.

This clinical trial is seeking healthy male participants between the ages of 18 and 50 years with a BMI between 18-30 kg/m2. Potential participants should not have any conditions that might interfere with the procedures or tests involved in the study. Additionally, participants should not have a history of drug or alcohol abuse or be current smokers. The study involves the administration of single and multiple doses of GLPG1690, an investigational drug, to evaluate its safety and tolerability. The study will also examine the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of GLPG1690 compared to placebo, and explore the potential of cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A4 induction after repeated dosing with GLPG1690.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer and underwent chemotherapy treatment. She developed chemotherapy-induced polyneuropathy which has significantly affected her ability to perform daily activities such as standing up from a chair, walking and carrying objects. Her symptoms have been graded as NCI CTC grade 2/3. She has no history of psychiatric disorders, plasmatic coagulation disorders, thrombotic/thromboembolic events or seizures. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial and is willing to commit to 15 training sessions in a time period of 12 to 15 weeks. She is able to perform physical exercises and is open to trying whole-body vibration platform training as well.

A 52-year-old male with a history of hypertension for the past 5 years. He was diagnosed with hypertension during a routine check-up and started on medication. He has been taking the medication regularly as prescribed by his physician. His blood pressure readings have been fluctuating between 140-150/90-95 mm Hg, despite being on medication. He is otherwise healthy, with no other significant medical history. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He works in an office and has a sedentary lifestyle. He is interested in exploring alternative treatments for hypertension and is willing to participate in the study. He has no hearing impairment and is able to operate a CD player. His arm circumference is within the range of 22-42 cm. He is willing to fill in a log sheet to track his blood pressure readings.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with end-stage renal disease requiring hemodialysis through a permanent catheter. The patient has experienced multiple episodes of clotting in the catheter resulting in missed dialysis sessions and significant morbidity. The patient has not undergone any rt-PA instillation in the catheter over the previous 21 days. The patient is willing to participate in the study to evaluate the effectiveness of the new "push" protocol using alteplase to remove clots in hemodialysis catheters. The patient has no known allergies to alteplase or its components and does not have any bleeding events or hemostatic defects such as severe hepatic disease or current intracranial / intraspinal neoplasm. The hemodialysis catheter has been in the patient for more than 14 days.

A 56-year-old veteran with no history or risk factors for HIV infection is interested in participating in the study. He has never received the pneumococcal vaccine Prevnar PCV-13 before. He has not had his spleen removed and does not have chronic kidney disease. He has never been diagnosed with lymphoma or leukemia. He is not currently taking corticosteroids, chemotherapy, immunosuppressive medication, or illicit drugs. He is willing to attend 2-3 study visits over the course of 1 month.

A 35-year-old male office worker who leads a sedentary lifestyle is concerned about his weight gain over the past year. He weighs 100 kg and has a BMI of 32. He has no underlying medical conditions and takes no medication. He is a social drinker and does not have a history of alcohol dependence. He has no allergies to any food or drugs. His menstrual cycle is not applicable. He is a non-smoker and has a stable weight for the past 3 months. He has access to a WiFi internet connection at home and is willing to keep a food diary and activity log for 7 consecutive days during screening.

A 54-year-old woman with advanced solid tumors presents with fatigue, abdominal pain, and weight loss. She has exhausted all standard therapeutic treatment options and is looking for alternative options. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1, with adequate organ function confirmed by laboratory testing. She has no history of hematologic malignancy or primary central nervous system tumors. The patient has no mood disorders or significant cardiac diseases but has a history of hypertension controlled with medication. She has not received any chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy in the past 4 weeks and has not undergone any major surgery in the past 4 weeks. The patient is not pregnant, lactating, or of child-bearing potential. She has no history of HIV or Hepatitis B or C infection. The patient is willing to comply with the protocol and sign informed consent.

The patient is a 75-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with coronary artery disease. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes for the past 10 years, all of which are well controlled with medication. He is living with his wife and two adult children who are his primary caregivers. He is retired and spends his free time gardening and reading books. He is able to walk without any aids and is generally active. However, he has noticed a recent decrease in his energy levels and has experienced shortness of breath while walking uphill. He has been advised by his cardiologist to undergo an elective cardiac procedure to improve his coronary artery blood flow. He is willing to participate in the study and undergo frailty assessment. He has no history of dementia or cognitive impairment and is able to provide informed consent.

The patient is a 62-year-old man who was recently diagnosed with advanced stage non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to his liver and bones. He has already received chemotherapy but the disease has progressed despite treatment. He reports feeling fatigued and having difficulty breathing, but no other significant symptoms. He has a history of hypertension which is well-controlled with medication. He takes lisinopril 10mg daily. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs, but he drinks alcohol occasionally. He has no known allergies to medications. His physical exam and lab studies were not remarkable for any other abnormalities. BP: 130/80 Hgb: 10 g/dl WBC: 6000 /mm3 Plt: 200000 /ml Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dl BUN: 20 mg/dl Beta hcg: negative for pregnancy.

The patient is a 10 year-old female with a personal history of hereditary retinoblastoma. She was diagnosed with bilateral retinoblastoma at 6 months of age and underwent external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) for treatment. She has no history of second primary cancer occurring within radiation fields. She is currently asymptomatic and has no history of any other medical conditions. She is not taking any medications and has no known allergies. She is accompanied by her parents who have given their consent for her participation in the study. They reside in the same city as the study site and are able to comply with follow-up study requirements.

The patient is a 65 year old male who has been diagnosed with carotid artery severe (70-99%) stenosis by CDFI and confirmed by CTA. His medical history is significant for hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. He has never smoked and has no history of coronary artery disease. He has experienced a few transient ischemic attacks in the past months, but no cerebral infarction has been identified so far. He is currently under the care of a vascular surgeon who has recommended carotid artery stenting as the best treatment option for him. He is willing to participate in this clinical trial, which will involve ultrasound evaluation of his carotid artery plaques before and after the procedure, as well as follow-up visits for at least 1 year. He is able to comply with the follow-up schedule and has provided his consent to participate in the study.

A 55-year-old woman diagnosed with primary autonomic failure (PAF) has been experiencing symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension (nOH) for the past year. She complains of dizziness, lightheadedness, and fainting spells when standing up from a sitting or lying position. She has plasma NE levels greater than 100 pg/mL in the seated position and has a sustained reduction in BP of ≥20 mm Hg (systolic) or ≥10 mm Hg (diastolic) within 3 minutes of being tilted-up to ≥60o from a supine position, as demonstrated by a tilt-table test. She scores at least a 4 on the Orthostatic Hypotension Symptom Assessment Question #1 at the randomization visit. She does not have any known systemic illness that produces autonomic neuropathy, is not intolerant to other NRIs or SNRIs, and is not using concomitant antihypertensive medication for the treatment of essential hypertension unrelated to autonomic dysfunction. She has not used strong CYP1A2 inhibitors or inducers within 7 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, prior to randomization or requires concomitant use until the follow-up visit. She has not changed the dose, frequency, or type of prescribed medication for orthostatic hypotension within 7 days prior to V1, and has tapered off Midodrine and droxidopa (if applicable) at least 7 days prior to V1. She has no known or suspected alcohol or substance abuse within the past 12 months (DSM-IV-TR® definition of alcohol or substance abuse). She has no clinically unstable coronary artery disease, major cardiovascular or neurological event in the past 6 months, or any significant uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia. She has a Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score >23, and no history of untreated closed angle glaucoma, or treated closed angle glaucoma that, in the opinion of an ophthalmologist, might result in an increased risk to the subject. She has no known congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association [NYHA] Class 3 or 4), and no clinically significant abnormal laboratory findings. She has not demonstrated a history of lifetime suicidal ideation and/or suicidal behavior, as outlined by the C-SSRS (Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale) (Baseline/Screening Version).

A 36-year-old woman who is 38 weeks pregnant is being evaluated for induction of labor due to the presence of pre-eclampsia. Her blood pressure has been elevated for a week, and her physician has determined that it is in the best interest of the patient and the fetus to deliver the baby. Her Bishop score is 4, and she has a favorable cervix. She has no other medical problems and is otherwise healthy. She is a non-smoker and has not had any complications during her pregnancy.

A 6-week-old baby boy was brought to the clinic by his parents for his routine check-up. The baby was born full-term and had no complications at birth. He is exclusively breastfed and has been gaining weight appropriately. His parents have no history of allergic disease or reactions. They have no concerns about the baby's health and are willing to comply with the requirements of the study. They were informed about the study and have given written consent for their baby to participate. The baby has no acute illnesses at the time of enrolment and has not had any episodes of gastroenteritis in the past 7 days. The baby meets the eligibility criteria for the study and is a suitable candidate for the clinical trial.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has been wearing contact lenses for 5 years to correct her myopia. She has a refractive error of -4 diopters in both eyes and has been stable for the past 2 years. She is interested in exploring other options to correct her vision and is considering radial keratotomy. She has no significant past medical history, but she does have a family history of myopia. She works as a computer programmer and spends a lot of time in front of a screen. She has no known allergies and takes no medications. She wears soft contact lenses and has never had any issues with contact lens wear or care. She has been evaluated by an ophthalmologist and meets the eligibility criteria for the study. She understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is willing to participate in the clinical trial.

This clinical trial is seeking preterm infants with a gestational age of less than 37 weeks and a peripheral arterial catheter (ulnary or radial artery). The purpose of the study is to evaluate cerebral oxygenation and blood flow during blood sampling procedures with identical sampling volumes at short (40 seconds) and long (70 seconds) time intervals. The investigators hypothesize that slower sampling procedures will result in less changes in cerebral blood flow. Patients with complex organ malformations will be excluded from the study.
