A 57-year-old man was recently diagnosed with acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL). He has a history of hypertension and takes medication for it. He is a non-smoker and does not use alcohol or recreational drugs. He works as a computer programmer and leads an active lifestyle with regular exercise. He has no known allergies and has not had any recent surgeries. He is married and has two adult children. He has no history of cancer or blood disorders in his family. He is willing to participate in clinical trials and has given his consent for the study.

This is a 50 year-old female with a history of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She has been experiencing fatigue and abdominal discomfort over the past few months. Her primary care physician ordered liver function tests and the results showed elevated levels of ALT, AST, and GGT. She was referred to a gastroenterologist who performed an ultrasound of her liver and found evidence of fatty liver disease. She has a BMI of 35 and her waist-to-hip ratio is 1.1. She has hypertension with a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg and her triglyceride levels are elevated at 2.0 mmol/L. Her HDL-cholesterol levels are low at 0.95 mmol/L. She is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study.

A 32-year-old female with a history of lipedema affecting both legs, presenting with persistent pain in the legs for the past six months. The patient has not found relief with conservative management such as compression stockings, physical therapy or medication. Her pain score is 6 out of 10 on a numerical rating scale. She is motivated to participate in this study to determine if surgical therapy using liposuction is more effective in relieving her pain compared to complex physical decongestive therapy (CDT) alone. She is willing to comply with all study requirements and has no previous history of liposuction. The patient has no significant past medical history and is not currently pregnant or breastfeeding. She understands the need for adequate contraception during the study period.

The patient is a 42-year-old man who has a body mass index (BMI) of 41. He has struggled with obesity for several years and has tried various diets and exercise programs without success. He has developed comorbidities such as hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and sleep apnea. After consulting with his healthcare provider, he has decided to undergo elective bariatric surgery to improve his health and quality of life. He will be undergoing the surgery with the laparoscopic approach and will be staying overnight in the hospital for recovery. He is eligible to participate in this clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not have any exclusion criteria. The study aims to determine the incidence of postoperative complications in adult patients undergoing elective bariatric surgery regardless of their adherence to an enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocol. The results of this study will help identify the type of patients who develop postoperative complications and the perioperative items of ERAS protocols that are associated with a decrease in complications, thus improving the postoperative outcomes of bariatric surgery.

The patient is a 7-year-old boy who has been experiencing bedwetting at night for the past few months. He has no history of any medical conditions and is generally healthy. The bedwetting occurs at least 4-5 times a week and has caused him embarrassment and frustration. The family has tried various methods to manage the bedwetting, including limiting fluids before bedtime and waking him up at night to use the bathroom, but with no success. The patient has not been previously treated with desmopressin or any other medication for nocturnal enuresis or enuresis alarms. He has not been diagnosed with renal diabetes insipidus or central diabetes insipidus with an AVP (arginine vasopressin) deficiency. The patient has not had a urinary tract infection within the past month or a documented positive urine culture at the start of the study. The patient and their family are willing to participate in a 6-week open label cross-over study with 2 different daily doses of Minirin® oral lyophilisate to manage the bedwetting. They understand the potential benefits and risks of participation in the study and are able to provide informed consent.

A 12-year-old boy was admitted to the hospital for intestinal obstruction caused by a congenital malformation. He required surgical intervention and is now dependent on parenteral nutrition (PN) due to intestinal failure. He has been on PN for the past 2 years and has developed liver dysfunction with elevated bilirubin levels. He has undergone multiple interventions to prevent progression of his liver disease, including removal of copper and manganese from PN and advancement of enteral feeding, but has not experienced any improvement. His current direct bilirubin level is 3.2 mg/dL. The patient and his parents have provided informed consent and are willing to participate in this clinical trial evaluating the safety and benefit of a fish oil based fat emulsion in the treatment of PN associated liver disease. The patient has no known allergies and is otherwise healthy, with no history of diabetes, stroke, or cardiac infarction.

5-year-old male patient with Early Childhood Caries (ECC) and a history of regular dental check-ups. The patient has no history of systemic illness or developmental disease of the teeth and jaws that would affect dietary patterns, caries susceptibility, or the selection of restorative materials. The patient has at least two surfaces of caries in the targeted primary anterior teeth. The patient is cooperative and has a positive behavioral rating on the Frankl behavior classification scale. The patient has opposing teeth present, and the parent/guardian has provided written consent for the treatment procedure. The patient does not have allergies or hypersensitivity to nickel. The patient has not suffered from any trauma to the teeth. The patient does not suffer from bruxism or any special needs. The patient does not have any tooth wear on the opposing teeth.

Patient is a 60-year-old man who was diagnosed with prostate cancer through participation in a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening program. The patient has no known family history of prostate cancer and has never experienced any symptoms related to the disease. The biopsy showed adenocarcinoma of the prostate gland, Gleason score 6 (3+3), and a PSA level of 7 ng/mL. The patient is currently considering different treatment options and is interested in participating in a follow-up study to determine the effectiveness, potential complications, and quality of life after different treatments for prostate cancer. The patient is in overall good health with no significant medical history and has no current symptoms related to the prostate cancer.

The patient is a 28-year-old nulliparous woman with a singleton pregnancy at 38 weeks and 4 days of gestational age. She presents to the hospital with complaints of leaking fluid from her vagina for the past 12 hours. She denies having any contractions, vaginal bleeding, or abdominal pain. She has no medical history of chronic illnesses or surgeries. She has been attending regular prenatal care visits and has had an uncomplicated pregnancy. She is not currently taking any medications or supplements. She denies any allergies to medications. She has no history of substance abuse or smoking. She lives with her husband and they have been married for 2 years. She is employed as a teacher and plans to take 12 weeks of maternity leave. Her family history is unremarkable for any genetic disorders or pregnancy complications. She has tested negative for group B streptococcus during her routine prenatal care. She is currently at the hospital and an amniotic fluid test has confirmed the rupture of membranes. Her Bishop score is 3.

The patient is a 56-year-old female who was admitted to the ICU with septic shock due to a urinary tract infection. She has a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Her current medications include metformin and lisinopril. Upon admission, she was started on intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam for the treatment of her infection. Her renal function is stable and her liver function tests are within normal limits. She has no known drug allergies. The patient is able to provide informed consent to participate in the study.

A 45-year-old male office worker has been experiencing chronic neck pain for the past 2 years, which radiates down to his left arm and shoulder. He has tried various conventional treatments, including prescription pain medication, physical therapy, and injections, but none have provided significant relief. He has been diagnosed with intractable neck pain and has a neck pain intensity of 8 out of 10 on the average neck pain VAS. He is on a stable dose of pain medication with a total opioid equivalent of 80 mg and is willing to continue with the same dose until activation of the permanently implanted SCS device. He has no history of substance abuse or dependency in the past 6 months. He has not participated in any clinical investigation that includes an active treatment arm and is not currently implanted with a neurostimulation system or an infusion pump. He has no coagulation disorder, bleeding diathesis, or progressive peripheral vascular disease. He has no moderate or severe cervical stenosis, mechanical neck pain originating from cervical facet joint syndrome, post-herpetic neuralgia, spondylolisthesis, retrolisthesis, or CRPS. He is willing to comply with the study requirements, including the use of an effective method of contraception if he is a female candidate of childbearing potential.

A 45-year-old African American woman was diagnosed with Stage II invasive breast cancer six months ago. She underwent lumpectomy, followed by radiation therapy and chemotherapy. She is currently on tamoxifen. She has a family history of breast cancer, with her mother and aunt both diagnosed in their 50s. She has a BMI of 30 kg/m2 and has been struggling with weight gain since her diagnosis. She lives in the Roseland community in Chicago and has access to a Chicago Park District fitness center. She works as a nurse and has a busy schedule, but is willing to attend twice-weekly classes for six months to participate in a weight loss intervention program. She does not have any medical conditions that would limit her participation in physical activity and has received approval from her primary care physician. She is interested in participating in the study to improve her overall health and reduce her risk of breast cancer recurrence.

62 year old male who underwent total shoulder arthroplasty 2 years ago for severe osteoarthritis. He has completed all follow-up appointments and radiographic imaging at the 2-year mark. He has no history of mental impairment or imprisonment since his surgery. He is willing to participate in the study and understands the purpose of the research.

A 35-year-old active woman was diagnosed with a symptomatic articular cartilage defect of the knee a year ago. She was enrolled in the SUMMIT study and received MACI implant treatment for her condition. She has been continuously monitored for the past 2 years and has shown improvements in her knee function and overall quality of life. She is now eligible for this extension study to assess the 5-year efficacy and safety of MACI compared to arthroscopic microfracture. She exercises regularly and is committed to following the study protocol for the next 3 years. She is willing to attend all scheduled visits and complete all assessments required for the study. She is excited to contribute to the advancement of knowledge about this treatment and is motivated to continue improving her knee health.

The patient is a 38-week-old male baby who is born via vaginal delivery. The baby was born with a weight of 3.5 kg and has no history of fetal distress. Within a few minutes of birth, the baby developed respiratory distress with rapid breathing and retractions. The baby's oxygen saturation level is 88% on room air. Upon physical examination, the baby shows signs of nasal flaring and grunting. The baby has no other medical history or known abnormalities. The baby is eligible for the clinical trial as he meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is a 73-year-old woman who has recently been diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) after undergoing a diagnostic biopsy within the past 4 weeks. She has an ECOG performance status of 1 and her laboratory values meet the inclusion criteria for the study. She has no history of other malignancies and has not received any prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy. MRI scans show that she has a large tumor in the left temporal lobe with surrounding edema. The patient is interested in participating in the clinical trial and has no contraindications for the study treatment. She is willing to comply with the study requirements and follow-up visits.

The patient is a 60-year-old woman who has been experiencing bilateral knee pain for the past year. She has been diagnosed with mild to moderate knee osteoarthritis and has been taking pain medication to manage her symptoms. She has no history of lower limb injury, diabetes, or neuromuscular disease such as stroke or Parkinson's. She has not received a knee HA injection in the last 6 months and has no history of knee or hip replacement. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the effect of hyaluronic acid injection on postural stability and biomechanics of gait and stair climbing. She is willing to undergo assessment using the Biodex stability index and "Timed up and Go" test, as well as gait and stair climbing assessment using the Vicon motion capture system synchronized with four force plates.

A 53-year-old woman presents with chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after undergoing a stem cell transplant for treatment of acute myeloid leukemia. She has been previously treated with steroids but has experienced progression of symptoms including skin erythema, mouth sensitivity and nausea. She has a Karnofsky performance status of 80% and is able to swallow capsules without difficulty. The patient understands the purpose and risks of the study and is willing to participate in all required evaluations and procedures. She is using highly effective methods of contraception during treatment and is not pregnant or breastfeeding. The patient has not been hospitalized for evaluation or management of an infection in the last 8 weeks and has not changed her immunosuppressive regimen within the 2 weeks prior to enrollment. She has no history of noncompliance and has not been treated with ibrutinib for chronic GVHD. She has no history of recurrent or prior malignancy and has no clinically significant cardiovascular disease. The patient has no difficulty swallowing oral medication and has no significant gastrointestinal disease that would limit absorption of oral medication. She has no known history of infection with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and no active significant infection. The patient has no history of drug-specific hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis to study drug and has no active bleeding or history of bleeding diathesis. She is not receiving therapeutic anti-platelet or anticoagulation and has a prothrombin time/international normalized ratio (INR) or activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) within normal limits. The patient is not receiving proton pump inhibitors and has no history of significant cerebrovascular disease or event, including stroke or intracranial hemorrhage, within 6 months before the first dose of study drug. She has not undergone major surgical procedure within 28 days of first dose of study drug. The patient has a negative PCR for hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) and is surface antigen negative. She is not hepatitis C PCR positive and has no Child-Pugh score of C for hepatic impairment. Her absolute neutrophil count and platelet count are within normal limits and she has a glomerular filtration rate of >50 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The patient is not concurrently participating in another clinical trial and is not receiving a non-Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved medication.

A 28-year-old woman is in her 29th week of pregnancy and has been diagnosed with preterm labor. She has been admitted to the hospital for close monitoring and management. Her pregnancy has been healthy so far, with no complications. She does not smoke, drink alcohol or use drugs. She has a BMI of 23 and exercises regularly. She has received counseling on the benefits and risks of delayed cord clamping and cord milking and has provided informed consent to participate in the study. Her baby is expected to be born within the next few days, and the study hospital will provide follow-up care for the infant.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in the upper right side of her abdomen for the past two weeks. She also feels nauseous and has a decreased appetite. She went to see her doctor who diagnosed her with acute cholecystitis based on her symptoms and imaging tests. She is recommended to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy to remove her gallbladder. She has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. She works as a teacher and is generally active, but her symptoms have been limiting her physical activity. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. Her BMI is within the normal range and her blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. Her physical examination reveals tenderness on the right upper quadrant of her abdomen. She meets the inclusion criteria for the trial and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria.

A 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease presents to the hospital for elective cardiac surgery. The surgery involves open-heart surgery to repair aortic stenosis. After the surgery, the patient is admitted to the Vanderbilt Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit (CVICU) and is intubated due to respiratory distress. The patient is extubated after a few days and is deemed to be at high risk for reintubation due to his history of respiratory complications. The patient is approached to participate in a clinical trial comparing high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy (HFNC) to standard care for reducing the risk of reintubation in high-risk cardiac surgery patients. The patient is informed that he will be randomly assigned to receive either HFNC or standard care therapy chosen by the provider. The patient agrees to participate in the trial and signs the written informed consent form.

A 45-year-old male construction worker presented to his family physician with back pain that had been ongoing for several months. The pain started after he lifted a heavy load at work. The pain is localized to his lower back and radiates down his left leg. The patient reports numbness and tingling in his left foot. He has tried over-the-counter pain medication with no relief. He has no significant medical history and is not taking any medications. On physical examination, the patient has tenderness to palpation in the lower lumbar region. Straight leg raise test is positive on the left side. Neurological evaluation reveals decreased sensation in the left L5 dermatome and weakness in the left ankle dorsiflexion. An MRI revealed a disc herniation at the L4-L5 level. The patient has agreed to participate in the clinical and radiological investigation of the Fixateur Ennovate® and has provided consent for documentation of clinical and radiological results.

The patient is a 62-year-old male who has been diagnosed with superficial basal cell carcinoma (sBCC) on his forehead. He has no history of skin cancer and has never been treated for sBCC before. He works as an accountant and spends most of his days indoors. He is generally healthy and takes medication for hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. He is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. He has fair skin and has noticed a small, scaly patch on his forehead that has been slowly growing over the past few months. The lesion is about 1 cm in diameter and is slightly raised with a pearly appearance. He is concerned about the lesion and is willing to participate in the clinical trial. He has agreed to stop using moisturizers and cosmetics in the treatment area 48 hours before each office visit and 48 hours after each PDT session. He is willing to abstain from extensive sunbathing and the use of a solarium during the clinical observation period. He is willing to receive up to 4 PDTs within 3.5 months and excision of the Main Target Lesion either at Visit 5, if clinically cleared, or at the end of the clinical observation period 12 weeks after the start of the last PDT cycle (Visit 8), irrespective of whether the treated Main Target Lesion was clinically cleared or not.

The patient is a 50-year-old man who has been experiencing palpitations and occasional chest discomfort for the past few months. He has a family history of heart disease, with his father and grandfather both having suffered heart attacks in their 60s. He does not smoke, but he drinks alcohol moderately on weekends. He has a sedentary lifestyle and works as an accountant, spending most of his day sitting at a desk. He has no other significant medical history and is not taking any medications. During his visit to his family physician at the Health Care Center of Ljubljana, a 12-channel ECG was performed, but no rhythm disturbance was detected. He is interested in participating in the study and is willing to wear the personal ECG sensor for three days. He is able to use a smartphone and is willing to install the MobECG mobile application. He understands the importance of keeping the sensor on during his daily activities and is willing to keep a journal of his symptoms and feelings during the examination period. He has signed the informed consent form and is eligible to participate in the study.

A 40-year-old male with no significant medical history, who works as a healthcare professional and is interested in participating in a clinical trial for H5 influenza vaccine. He has not received any influenza vaccine this season and has not been diagnosed with any immunocompromising diseases. The patient is willing to comply with all study procedures, and he has no plans for surgery during the study period. He is not allergic to eggs, chicken protein, chicken feathers, or neomycin or kanamycin. He has never participated in a study of H5 avian influenza vaccine and has never been vaccinated with a vaccine containing MF59 or similar adjuvant.

25-year-old female who is sexually active with a regular partner and has been using combined oral contraceptive pills for the past 2 years. She has no history of injecting drug use, gonorrhoea or syphilis in the last 6 months, and has not had unprotected vaginal or anal intercourse in the last 6 months outside of her current relationship. She is willing to use double barrier methods of contraception during the study period. She has no history of drug or alcohol abuse, and is not currently on any regular medication. She is able to read and speak English fluently, and is willing and able to give written informed consent. She is not pregnant or lactating, and does not plan to get pregnant within the next year. She has not received any experimental vaccine containing HIV envelope proteins in the past, and has not received blood products or immunoglobulin within 4 months of screening. She tests negative for HIV1/2 antibody/antigen, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, and serology indicating active syphilis requiring treatment. She has no clinically significant abnormality on ECG performed at the screening visit. She is available for a maximal study duration of 8 months from screening and is willing to abstain from donating blood during her participation in the trial.

57-year-old male with a history of COPD diagnosed as per the criteria of the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease in 2016, presented to the emergency department with acute exacerbation of his symptoms. The patient is a smoker with a pack-year history of 30 and is on home oxygen therapy. He has a history of recurrent hospitalizations for COPD exacerbations and has been intubated twice in the past. The patient is currently experiencing severe dyspnea, cough, and sputum production. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a pH of 7.25 and PaCO2 of 60 mmHg. The patient meets the criteria for inclusion in the HAPPEN study and is willing to participate. Past medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a remote history of myocardial infarction. The patient is compliant with his medication regimen, which includes inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids, and is followed regularly by his pulmonologist. The patient has no history of upper airway obstruction, recent oral/facial/cranial/gastric/esophageal surgery, pneumothorax, severe hemodynamic instability, or intolerance to NPPV. The patient is conscious, cooperative, and able to follow instructions.

The patient is a 35-year-old female who has been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis according to the ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria. She has anti-CCP positivity and has erosions on conventional X-rays of her hands, wrists, and feet. She does not have clinically swollen joints, and her DAS28 (4 variable, CRP) is less than 3.2. She is currently on DMARD monotherapy or combination treatment, in the form of 2- or 3-drug therapy, and has not had any changes in her anti-rheumatic treatment in the previous 6 weeks or more. She has not received any previous treatment with biological medication, and has no contra-indications for TNF-alpha-inhibiting treatment or MRI. Her s-creatinine is within the normal range. She is willing to give written and oral informed consent and fulfill the requirements of the study program with reference to the protocol. She has never received Myocrisin treatment and does not have affected liver enzymes greater than 2 times the upper limit of normal at the time of screening. She has no current or imminent wish to become pregnant, and does not have any known alcohol/drug abuse. She is able to cooperate with the study program and has no physical or mental reasons that would prevent her from doing so.

A 16-year-old female who received a deceased donor renal transplant 10 months ago is being followed up at the transplant clinic. She is currently taking tacrolimus (twice daily) and mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) and is doing well with no evidence of graft dysfunction. She has a history of good medication adherence, but she finds it challenging to take her medications on time due to her busy schedule with school, extracurricular activities, and social events. She has no history of acute cellular rejection or antibody-mediated rejection. She has no history of gastrointestinal illness that might affect the absorption of tacrolimus. She has no known allergies to tacrolimus or other medications. She is able to comply with study procedures for the entire length of the study and her parent/legal guardian has signed an informed consent form. She meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the Envarsus XR® in Adolescent Renal Transplant Recipients clinical trial.

A 45-year-old male patient was admitted to the hospital with severe abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting. The diagnosis of acute pancreatitis was confirmed through serum amylase and lipase levels, and a characteristic CT-scan. The patient was diagnosed with severe acute pancreatitis as per the Balthazar's CT-scan severity index and APACHE-II score of 10. The C-reactive protein level was 175 mg/L. The patient was unable to initiate feeding and was predicted to have nil-by-mouth for more than 5 days. The patient's serum triglyceride levels were 2.5 mmol/L. The patient had no known allergies to fish, egg or soy proteins. The patient had no history of lipid etiology or severe hepatic impairment. The patient's renal function was within normal limits. The patient had no serious disturbances of blood clotting. The patient did not have acute shock or any general contraindications to infusion therapy. The patient did not have any acute or chronic inflammatory diseases. The patient was not immunosuppressed and was not receiving steroids. The patient agreed to participate in the trial and provided informed consent.

The patient is a 70-year-old man who has been diagnosed with chronic congestive heart failure for the past 5 years. He has been experiencing increased difficulty breathing at rest for the past 2 weeks and has been hospitalized for intravenous therapy. The patient's pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) is documented to be 20 mm Hg, Cl is 2.5 mL/min/m² and systolic blood pressure is 100 mm Hg. He has not had a myocardial infarction within the previous 48 hours or unstable angina, nor a stroke within the previous 3 months. The patient does not have significant valvular stenosis, hypertrophic or obstructive cardiomyopathy, constrictive pericarditis, primary pulmonary hypertension, or complex congenital heart disease. The patient is not receiving ongoing treatment with an intravenous vasoconstrictive agent for this episode of decompressed CHF that could not be discontinued for an appropriate washout period to permit the reassessment of baseline hemodynamic and clinical status prior to initiating drug study. The patient's clinical status is stable enough to tolerate placement of a Swan-Ganz catheter.

As this clinical trial involves parents or caregivers of youth or young adults (Y/YA) in first episode psychosis (FEP) services, the patient description will focus on the caregiver. The patient is a 45-year-old woman who is the primary caregiver for her 19-year-old son who has recently been diagnosed with FEP. Her son has been experiencing symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized thinking, which have led to difficulties in completing his studies and maintaining social relationships. The patient is concerned about her son's well-being and is struggling to navigate the mental health system. She has limited knowledge about FEP and its treatment options, and feels overwhelmed and isolated. She is interested in receiving support and guidance from someone who has gone through a similar experience and can provide her with practical information and emotional support. She is willing to participate in the study and receive weekly telephone-based support from a trained and supervised peer parent navigator for six to nine months. She hopes that this intervention will help her feel more empowered and connected to the mental health services available to her son, and improve his outcomes.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who was recently involved in a car accident resulting in multiple traumatic injuries including a traumatic brain injury. He was immediately taken to the ICU and placed on a ventilator. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are being managed with medications. His blood glucose levels have been fluctuating and have required insulin therapy. The attending ICU physician has predicted that the patient will require treatment in the ICU beyond the day following admission. An arterial line has been placed for routine clinical management, and the patient is expected to recover from their injuries. The patient or their legal surrogate is able to provide prior informed consent for participation in the NICE-SUGAR Study.

30-year-old female with a history of lower back pain after a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago. The patient has a history of occasional use of over-the-counter pain medication for her back pain. She is scheduled for an elective posterior lumbar interbody fusion for L4-L5 and L5-S1. The patient reports no known allergies to any medications. She has no pre-existing neuropsychiatric disorders and speaks English fluently. She has no history of substance abuse or alcohol use. The patient has no contraindications to peripheral nerve block and has no history of cerebrovascular disease, liver failure, or low blood pressure. She is currently on no medications.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with an AHI of 30 events/hour. He is overweight with a BMI of 32 kg/m² and has a history of hypertension, which is well controlled with medication. He reports excessive daytime sleepiness, snoring, and gasping for air during sleep. He is a non-smoker and does not use any illicit drugs. He has no history of craniofacial anomalies or central sleep apnoea. He is not allergic to sulphonamides or acetazolamide. He has no renal impairment, electrolyte imbalances, or adrenocortical insufficiency. He does not have any clinically significant metabolic, hepatic, or haematological disease. He does not have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or closed-angle glaucoma. He is not taking any drugs that substantially stimulate or depress respiration. He is willing to comply with the study procedures and has no active psychiatric disease. He is not pregnant.

The patient is an adult (18 years or older) who is HIV-positive and receives care at the HIV clinic of either Boston Medical Center or Grady Memorial Hospital. The patient has been on chronic opioid therapy for at least six months, with at least three opioid prescriptions written at least 21 days apart during that time. The patient is able to provide contact information for at least two individuals who can assist with follow-up, and has a home or mobile telephone. The patient speaks English and is willing and able to provide informed consent for participation in an observational study. The patient is not planning to move from the area within the next 12 months and is able to understand and participate in interviews with trained research staff.

The patient is a 25-year-old female who is in good health and has no history of chronic illnesses or respiratory problems. She is within the age range of 18-65 years and her body weight is over 50 kg with a body mass index within 19-29 kg/m2 inclusive. She is willing to comply with all study restrictions and procedures, including using the Dry Powder Inhaler correctly. Her spirometry readings (FEV1 and FVC) are ≥ 80% predicted value and FEV1/FVC ratio > 0.7 calculated using ECCS reference equations. Her vital sign assessments, including systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and heart rate (HR) are within normal ranges. She is not currently taking any prescription medications and agrees not to use any prescription or over-the-counter medications, including corticosteroids, decongestants, antihistamines, aspirin, and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), within 14 days before the first administration of study medication and throughout the duration of the study. She is not a smoker and has not smoked or used nicotine-containing products within the 6 months prior to screening. She is not allergic to any of the active or inactive ingredients in the study medication and has no other known contraindications for participation. The patient is willing to undergo multiple venepuncture procedures necessary for the study and is mentally and legally capable of giving written informed consent.

A 55-year-old man presented to the clinic with chest pain that started 2 days ago. He described the pain as a pressure-like sensation in the center of his chest that radiates to his left arm. The pain lasted for a few minutes and then subsided but occurred again with minimal exertion. He has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, for which he takes medication. He had a coronary stent implanted 3 months ago for an unstable angina episode. He is a non-smoker and denies any illicit drug use. He works as an accountant and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He has no family history of coronary artery disease. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to evaluate a new medication for the prevention of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, as well as reduce the incidence of bleeding during long-term treatment.

A 62-year old retired teacher was diagnosed with B-chronic lymphocytic leukemia (B-CLL) six months ago. She presented with fatigue, shortness of breath and easy bruising. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes. She lives alone and does some light housework. She has two adult children who live in a different state. The patient is on watch and wait protocol for her CLL. She doesn't have any major symptoms and her blood counts have been stable. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to help advance research for CLL treatment. She is willing to come to the hospital for the injections as needed. She doesn't smoke or use any illicit drugs. She currently takes medications for her hypertension and diabetes.

The patient is a 50-year-old male with a diagnosis of Type II Diabetes Mellitus. He has no history of diabetes retinopathy and is currently managing his diabetes with medication. He has no allergies or intolerances to medications and has not had any relevant ocular or ophthalmic pathology. He has not undergone any ocular surgeries in the past 6 months and has not used contact lenses. His HbA1c levels are stable at 7%. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the safety of topical Bosentan in Type II Diabetes patients.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a BMI of 25. He works as a software engineer and leads a sedentary lifestyle. He does not have any significant medical conditions, and his laboratory test results are within normal limits. He does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively. He is willing to avoid fish, shellfish, and crustaceans for the duration of the study and follow all study procedures, including fasting blood draws and compliance with study preparation. He is not currently taking any omega-3 or omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid supplements or medications and is willing to avoid them throughout the study period. He is willing to use an effective form of birth control if necessary. He has not donated blood in the past four weeks and is willing to cease being a blood donor during the study.

The patient is a 30-year-old woman diagnosed with ulcerative colitis for the past 6 months. Despite treatment with corticosteroids and immunomodulators, her condition remains moderately to severely active with a Mayo Score of 8 and endoscopic sub-score of 3. Her BMI is 23 kg/m2 and she weighs 55 kg. She has no significant medical history and all her laboratory tests are within normal limits. She has not received any live vaccines in the past month and has not had any infections requiring hospitalization or parenteral antibiotics in the past 4 weeks. She has not been on any biologic agents, psoralen and ultraviolet A (PUVA) therapy, or systemic medications such as methotrexate, cyclosporine A, acitretin, tofacitinib, or apremilast in the past 4 weeks. She is not using any topical anti-psoriasis medications except for emollients. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate APVO210 for the treatment of ulcerative colitis.

A 45-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with HER2 positive breast cancer. She has undergone three lines of HER2 targeting therapies but the tumor has progressed despite the treatment. She has been experiencing fatigue, loss of appetite and weight loss. Her ECOG performance status is 1. She has no history of major surgery, and her serum bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase, and alanine aminotransferase levels are within normal limits. She has a measurable lesion as defined per RECIST Version 1.1. She is willing and able to provide written informed consent for the trial and has no other serious underlying medical conditions or allergies to protein drugs or recombinant proteins. She is not pregnant and is willing to use reliable contraception methods throughout the treatment period and for at least seven months following the last dose of study drug.

The patient is a 34-year-old man who has been diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) for the past 2 years. He has been experiencing moderate symptoms of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. He has been on maintenance therapy with mesalamine for the past year, but has not seen significant improvement in his symptoms. He has never been on biological treatment for IBD. He is married with no children and works as an accountant. He exercises regularly and follows a healthy diet, but still struggles with maintaining a healthy weight. He does not smoke or use any illicit drugs. He is not currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both of which are well-controlled with medication. His current BMI is 27.3.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones. She presents to the hospital on the third postoperative day with severe abdominal pain, fever, and leukocytosis. The patient reports a history of intermittent epigastric pain, bloating, and nausea for the past three months. She has no previous history of gastrointestinal perforation or other abdominal surgeries. The patient's vital signs are stable, with a blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, a heart rate of 85 beats per minute, and a temperature of 38.5°C. The patient is able to provide informed consent for the study and is capable of maintaining an upright position for at least 10 minutes. The patient has no known allergies to any medications. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and is eligible for enrollment.

The patient is a 25-year-old woman who works in the healthcare industry. She has a history of seasonal allergies but is otherwise healthy and does not take any medications regularly. She has not received the flu vaccine in the past year but is interested in participating in this study to help contribute to research on flu vaccines. She is able to attend all study visits and is willing to comply with all study requirements. She has read and signed the study-specific informed consent.

The patient is an 8-year-old boy diagnosed with Wilms' tumor. He is scheduled for a major abdominal surgery with a midline incision. He has no known allergies to any drugs. He has no history of mental retardation or delayed development that may interfere with pain intensity assessment. His physical exam and lab studies are not remarkable for any other abnormalities. His renal function, liver enzymes, and cardiac function are within normal limits. He does not smoke or use illicit drugs. He is not sexually active, and his menses are not applicable.

The patient is a 45-year-old Brazilian woman who has had persistent asthma symptoms for the past several years. She experiences asthma symptoms on a daily basis, with night symptoms occurring at least once a week. Her forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) is between 40% and 80% of the predicted normal value. She has a medical history of severe asthma exacerbations that required hospitalization or emergency room visits in the past 12 months. She has a positive skin prick test for at least one perennial aeroallergen. She is currently taking more than 500 mcg/day of fluticasone or equivalent associated with a long-acting β2-agonist. Her inhaled corticosteroid and LABA doses have remained fixed for the past 12 weeks. She has not previously been treated with omalizumab. She is capable of reading and understanding asthma-related quality of life questionnaires. She does not have a history of psychiatric disorders or drug or alcohol abuse. She is not pregnant or nursing and is currently using an acceptable contraceptive method. She does not have a history of cancer or other uncontrolled diseases in the past 3 months. She is a non-smoker with no smoking history of > 10 pack-years.

The patient is a 28-year-old healthy male with a body weight of 70 kg. He has never smoked and does not consume alcohol excessively. He has no known medical conditions and has not taken any medications or herbal supplements within the past month. He is willing to abstain from alcohol during the trial. He has not participated in any other clinical trials within the past three months. He is physically fit and considered normal on physical examination, clinical laboratory tests, and electrocardiogram. He is willing to comply with the study protocol and abstain from any drugs during the trial.

The patient is a 28-year-old man who works a regular 9-5 office job. He has a BMI of 27 and has been recently diagnosed with impaired glucose tolerance. He has no history of shift work or any significant medical conditions. He engages in moderate physical activity but does not follow a specific diet. He is interested in participating in the study to learn more about how his diet may affect his energy metabolism and circadian rhythms. He is willing to comply with the dietary interventions and able to give informed consent.

62 year-old male smoker with a 30-pack year history presents with cough, shortness of breath and chest pain. A chest CT scan reveals a right upper lobe mass with ipsilateral hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy of the mass confirms the diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (adenocarcinoma). The patient is deemed unresectable due to the extent of the disease. Past Medical History: 1. Hypertension 2. Hyperlipidaemia 3. Diabetes mellitus type 2 4. Coronary artery disease 5. Depression. Medications: 1. Metformin 1000mg twice daily 2. Lisinopril 10mg daily 3. Atorvastatin 40mg daily 4. Nitroglycerin 0.4mg sublingual as needed 5. Sertraline 50mg daily. The patient has an ECOG performance status of 1.

A 58 year old man with a history of open-angle glaucoma presented to the clinic with complaints of decreased vision and increased intraocular pressure (IOP) in his left eye. The patient had been using timolol eye drops for the past 2 years to control his IOP, but had recently noticed a deterioration in his vision. His visual acuity was 20/20 in his right eye and 20/40 in his left eye. The patient's IOP was 25 mm Hg in his left eye and 18 mm Hg in his right eye. The patient has no history of any other ocular or systemic diseases. The patient has not been treated with latanoprost or other prostaglandin analogues in the past. The patient was interested in participating in a clinical trial to compare the effectiveness of Xalatan to usual care in controlling his IOP.

A 38 year old woman came to the clinic complaining of shortness of breath, chest tightness and coughing, especially during the night. She has been diagnosed with asthma for 10 years and has been taking daily inhalers as prescribed by her doctor. Despite her treatment, she has had several asthma attacks in the past year, resulting in emergency room visits and courses of oral steroids. She is a non-smoker, with no history of other lung diseases or allergies. Her lung function tests show an FEV1 of 75% predicted, and her chest X-ray is normal. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to investigate the effects of QVM149 on her asthma symptoms, and is willing to undergo lung function testing, imaging studies such as MRI and CT scan, as well as answer questionnaires about her symptoms. She is not pregnant or nursing, and is using highly effective contraception during the course of the study.

The patient is a 45-year-old male who has been admitted to the ICU with severe pneumonia and has required intubation for the past 72 hours. He is currently receiving mechanical ventilation and is scheduled for extubation tomorrow. The patient has a history of smoking and has a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He is currently receiving treatment with lisinopril and atorvastatin. His vital signs are stable with a temperature of 37.2°C, heart rate of 85 beats per minute, blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg, and oxygen saturation of 98% on a fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) of 0.4. His chest x-ray shows improvement in the pneumonia. The patient meets the weaning criteria for extubation and has a cuff leak volume (CLV) of 100 mL. He has not received any corticosteroids in the past 7 days. The patient is willing to participate in a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of high dose and low dose dexamethasone in preventing post-extubation airway obstruction.

This is a 52 year-old female diagnosed with stage II breast cancer. Following a lumpectomy, her oncologist recommends tamoxifen treatment. She has no prior history of breast cancer in her family, but is concerned about the potential side effects of tamoxifen. She speaks fluent Korean and has no difficulty reading or understanding written information. She is willing to participate in the study and provide written informed consent.

Patient is a 35-year-old woman who presents with chronic non-allergic and non-infectious rhinitis. She has been experiencing symptoms, including nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, disturbance of sense of smell, sneezing, and facial heaviness for the past 12 weeks. A negative phadiatop test confirms non-allergic rhinitis, and an inflammation score at anterior rhinoscopy or nasal endoscopy shows a score of 4 or higher. She has not undergone any endonasal surgery, and she does not have a history of drug addiction, known immunosuppression, lymphoma, cardiovascular, neurological or other medically significant illness, renal failure, or glaucoma. She is not currently on antibiotic therapy or corticosteroids administered in the two months prior to admission. She is interested in participating in the clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Nasacort in treating her chronic non-allergic and non-infectious rhinitis symptoms.

The patient is a 24-year-old male college student. He has a history of occasional recreational drug use, including marijuana and alcohol. He is in good health and does not have any chronic illnesses. He is not taking any prescription medication and has not used any illicit substances in the past month. He has a body mass index of 23 kg/m2. His vital signs are within normal limits, and his clinical laboratory test results are unremarkable. He does not have a history of asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, or any clinically significant pulmonary condition. His electrocardiogram shows a corrected QT interval of 420 msec. He has never donated blood or plasma in the past month. He is willing and able to provide voluntary, written informed consent. He is interested in participating in the study to help advance the understanding of opioid-induced respiratory depression and potential treatment options.

A 23-year-old female with cystic fibrosis presents to the clinic with acute pulmonary exacerbation. She reports coughing up green mucus and shortness of breath. She has a past medical history of mild hearing loss in her left ear but denies any tinnitus or vertigo. She is currently taking inhaled bronchodilators and hypertonic saline. She works as a freelance graphic designer and enjoys hiking and camping. She is not sexually active and is committed to using an acceptable birth control method if necessary. Her physical exam reveals decreased breath sounds and crackles in the right lower lung field. Spirometry shows a significant decrease in her forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1). Her audiometry indicates mild sensorineural hearing loss in her left ear. She is a non-smoker and denies any history of drug or alcohol abuse. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to prevent hearing loss caused by IV tobramycin treatment.

The patient is a 35-year-old woman who was diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer 2 years ago. She underwent mastectomy and received chemotherapy followed by radiation therapy. Despite the treatment, the cancer has spread to her lungs, liver, and bones. Her performance status is ECOG 1. She is married and has two children ages 7 and 9. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension which is well controlled with medications. Her family history is significant for breast cancer in her mother and maternal aunt. Her lab study results are as follows: Hemoglobin: 10.5 g/dL, WBC: 4,500/mm^3, Platelet count: 150,000/mm^3, Bilirubin: 1.2 mg/dL, SGOT/SGPT: 2 times normal, Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL. She has no active infections or allergies to eggs. She is not currently pregnant or nursing, but is interested in preserving her fertility.

The patient is a 75-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with severe mitral valve regurgitation. She has been experiencing increasing shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest discomfort over the past several months. She has multiple comorbidities, including hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Due to her age and medical history, she has been deemed too high-risk for open-heart surgery. She has been recommended for a transcatheter mitral valve repair procedure using the MitraClip® device. She has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in all follow-up visits associated with the clinical investigation.

A 9-year-old boy diagnosed with ADHD and currently taking medication for it is eligible for this clinical trial. He has no history of cardiac problems, relevant medical conditions, or positive drug screens. His teacher is willing to complete assessments during the school term. His parents have given informed consent for his participation in the study.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was recently admitted to the hospital due to acute decompensated heart failure. He has a history of hypertension and heart failure with an ejection fraction of 30%. He is currently classified as Stage C:Class III heart failure and has experienced shortness of breath, fatigue, and swelling in his legs. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial and has provided appropriate informed consent. He is able to comply with the requirements of the protocol, including follow-up evaluations and schedule. He is willing to use the Shape-HF Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing System. He is not pregnant, currently participating in another investigational device or drug trial, or a prisoner, minor or unable to adequately give informed consent due to mental or physical condition. He is not listed for transplant, and he does not have a clinical diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism or is dialysis dependent. His hypertension is well-controlled, and he has not been re-programmed for his cardiac resynchronization device. He does not have Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) that is oxygen or steroid dependent. His resting systolic blood pressure is 170 mmHg, and his Creatinine clearance rate (CrCL) is 60. He is not on IV Inotropic therapy and is not enrolling in hospice.

This is a 62 year-old male who has been diagnosed with hyperlipidemia. He has no significant past medical history and is not currently on any medication for this condition. His primary care physician has referred him to a nutrition and diet therapy clinic for further management. He has been advised to follow a low calorie diet for 4 weeks by a registered dietitian. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial that involves the use of rice bran oil as a supplement to his diet. He does not have any history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes. He is not pregnant or lactating.

As this is an observational study of healthcare workers, there is no specific patient description required for this clinical trial. However, potential participants would need to be active workers at Centro Medico Bournigal or Centro Medico Punta Cana and meet the inclusion criteria outlined in the study description.

A 28-year-old African American female with sickle cell anemia who is currently clinically stable with no acute episodes of pain would be a potential candidate for this clinical trial. She has not had any painful VOCs requiring medical intervention in the past year and has a baseline VAS pain score of less than 4 cm. She has not received a transfusion of packed red blood cells within the past four weeks and is not currently on iron chelation therapy. She has no history of sickle cell disease-attributed CNS disease, pulmonary hypertension, or priapism in the last year. She has no history of hypertension, myocardial infarction, myocardial ischemia, or angina, and her renal and hepatic functions are normal. She does not have any acute or chronic conditions that would limit her ability to complete the study and is not currently abusing drugs or alcohol. She has not received any other investigational drugs within the past 30 days.

The patient is a non-HIV positive female aged 21 years or older, who reports non-prescription injection drug use and engages in any of the following behaviors: syringe sharing, injecting drugs with a HIV-positive partner, recent opioid agonist treatment but still injecting drugs, sex exchange, inconsistent condom use, recent bacterial STI, and/or sex with a HIV-positive partner. The patient is not currently taking PrEP and is not pregnant, breastfeeding or trying to become pregnant. The patient is willing to participate in a research study that tests a novel approach for the delivery of PrEP care, which will pair PrEP with community-based syringe exchange program (SEP) services. The patient is willing to attend appointments and complete semi-structured and in-depth interviews based on the Behavioral Model for Vulnerable Populations. The patient is aware that drug-level monitoring for FTC/TDF adherence will be conducted. The patient has not been previously enrolled in this study.

25-year-old woman who has been taking low dose oral contraceptives for the past 2 years. She has not experienced any side effects and has been compliant with her medication. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the effects of St. John's Wort on the effectiveness of oral contraceptives. She has no contraindications to hormonal contraception and is willing to take the study medication for 5 months.

A 30-year-old woman who works as a teacher is interested in participating in the study. She has a keloid scar on her left shoulder that is 2 cm long and less than 1 cm at its widest point. She has never undergone any therapy for the keloid scar. She is generally healthy, with a BMI of 24, and has no history of acute or chronic disease. She is a non-smoker and has no allergies to local anesthesia. She has never had an anaphylactic shock or anaphylactoid reaction. She is not currently on any medication that would affect collagen synthesis or therapy with steroids. She has no ongoing dermatologic disorders. She has never participated in another study in the last 60 days and has not donated blood or plasma recently. She has no tattoos near the keloid scar and has not applied any lotion or cream on or near the keloid scar within the last 14 days. She has not used any scar improving product within the last year. She has no history of drug addiction or excessive use of alcohol.

The patient is a 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and angina pectoris. He reports chest pain or discomfort that occurs during physical activity or emotional stress and is relieved by rest. He has undergone an exercise-ECG and myocardial SPECT, both of which showed signs of ischemia. However, angiography revealed no significant stenosis. He is currently on a standard treatment regimen consisting of metoprolol, diltiazem, and isosorbide mononitrate but is still experiencing angina. He has no known allergies to any of the study medications and has not participated in any other clinical trial involving test medicine. His lab tests are normal, and he has no known valvular disease, secondary hypertension, or significant arrhythmias. He has not experienced a myocardial infarction in the last 30 days and has not had resting angina in the past week. He has no known endocrine disease, nephropathy, or hepatic disease, and is not currently undergoing treatment for COPD or using dipyridamole or phosphodiesterase-5-inhibitors. He has not undergone a heart transplant and has no magnetizable metallic implants.

The patient is a 25-year-old healthy male with a BMI of 23 kg/m2. He has no significant medical history and has not been diagnosed with any cardiovascular, pulmonary or renal disease. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol or any recreational drugs. He is willing to participate in a Phase 1 clinical trial to assess the absorption, metabolism, excretion and pharmacokinetics of [14C]-AKB-9778. He has no known allergies and is currently not taking any medication. He understands the risks and benefits of participating in the study and has given informed consent.

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a previous diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who has relapsed and has not responded to standard chemotherapy treatment with cytarabine and mitoxantrone. The patient presents with hypoplastic bone marrow and Grade 4 thrombocytopenia with platelet counts < 25 x 10^9/L due to chemotherapy. The patient must have discontinued any systemic treatment for AML, with the exception of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), at least 7 days prior to entry into the study. The patient should have documented hypoplasia from the bone marrow aspiration and biopsy 14 days +/- 2 days from the initiation of cytarabine treatment schedule, defined as < 5% blasts and < 20% cellularity. The patient should have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of =< 2 and be able to understand and comply with protocol requirements and instructions. The patient should have normal liver and kidney function, and a QTcF < 450 msec (QTcF < 480 msec for patients with Bundle Branch Block). The patient should not have a known immediate or delayed hypersensitivity reaction or idiosyncrasy to drugs chemically related to eltrombopag, or any pre-existing cardiovascular disease or arrhythmia known to increase the risk of thromboembolic events (e.g., atrial fibrillation). The patient should not be taking aspirin (ASA) or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS). The patient or legal representative must understand the investigational nature of this study and sign an Independent Ethics Committee/Institutional Review Board approved written informed consent form prior to receiving any study related procedure.

A 45-year-old male patient who has been on peritoneal dialysis for the past year is interested in participating in the clinical trial. He has a history of hepatitis B vaccination with one full primary course of licensed vaccine, but his anti-HBs antibody concentrations have decreased below 10 mIU/ml. He is seronegative for anti-HBc antibodies and for HBsAg at screening. He has no history of allergic disease or reactions and is not taking any immunosuppressive medications. He is currently on medication for hypertension and has no other underlying medical conditions. He is willing to comply with the requirements of the protocol and has provided written informed consent.

This clinical trial is specifically looking for individuals who have parents with type 2 diabetes and are not currently diabetic themselves. The study aims to better understand the development of prediabetes and whether race plays a role in its progression. The trial will last for 5 years, during which participants will undergo repeated testing to monitor their glucose levels and other relevant factors. Participants who develop prediabetes will receive intensive lifestyle intervention to see if it can reverse the condition and restore normal glucose regulation. To be eligible for the study, participants must be between 18 and 65 years old, ambulatory, and in good general health. They must not be taking medications that affect insulin sensitivity, secretion, or body weight, and they cannot have a history of liposuction, surgical weight reduction, or use of specific medications. Women who are pregnant or become pregnant during the study will have testing procedures delayed until 12 months after delivery.

The patient is a 28-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus. She is currently taking insulin injections as prescribed by her physician. She has no other significant medical history and is not currently taking any other medications. Her A1c level is 7.5%. She experiences occasional mild nausea but has not been vomiting. She has a normal EKG and serum potassium and magnesium levels. She is willing to consume eggs, wheat, and milk products. She is able to provide written informed consent, communicate adequately with the investigator, and comply with the requirements for the entire study. She is undergoing a clinically-indicated continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) study and is interested in participating in this study to improve her ability to control her blood sugars.

The patient is a 15 year-old Haitian adolescent who was diagnosed with HIV at the age of 12 after being screened at a local health clinic. She has been on ART for the past 3 years and has been regularly attending her monthly appointments at the adolescent HIV clinic in Port-au-Prince. She lives with her parents and two younger siblings in a small house in a low-income neighborhood. She attends school and enjoys playing soccer with her friends in her free time. She has experienced some side effects from her ART medication but has been able to manage them with the help of her healthcare providers. She is currently interested in participating in a clinical trial that will help improve access to HIV monitoring and care for adolescents like her in Haiti.

The patient is a 5-year-old boy with a clinical diagnosis of sleep-disordered breathing or obstructive sleep apnea. He has adenotonsillar hypertrophy and has never undergone an adenotonsillectomy before. He is otherwise healthy, with no history of bleeding disorders, craniofacial malformation, or developmental delay. He has not taken any nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in the two weeks prior to the surgery and has no allergies to medications used in the protocol. He has no planned hospital admission or other surgical procedures during the surgical period. His parents are interested in participating in a clinical trial that compares the traditional extracapsular electrocautery dissection method of tonsillectomy with the newly introduced Peak® Surgery System in children of his age group with a diagnosis of sleep-disordered breathing. They understand that the study aims to evaluate intra-operative and post-operative outcomes, including pain control, bleeding rates, time to resumption of normal diet and activity, analgesic use, and frequency of emergent visits over 14 days following surgery. They are willing to complete daily diaries for 14 days following surgery and to complete the Glasgow Children's Benefit Inventory 6 months after surgery.

The patient is a 50-year-old woman who was recently diagnosed with stage II invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast. She underwent breast-conserving surgery and is planned to receive adjuvant radiotherapy and chemotherapy as part of her routine clinical care. She has a good performance status with no significant medical history of coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, or atrial fibrillation. She has not received any thoracic or mediastinal radiation in the past. She is not pregnant or lactating. She is willing to participate in the study and has signed written informed consent. She has no contraindications for iodinated contrast injection. Her baseline echocardiogram and cMRI results are normal, with LVEF above 50% and no abnormal wall motion. She is between 40-70 years of age and is eligible for radiotherapy to the breast/chest wall with or without the lymph node areas. She is eligible for adjuvant systemic chemotherapy, which can be given before or after radiotherapy. She is not on neo-adjuvant chemotherapy or targeted HER2 therapy.

The patient is a 55-year-old man who was diagnosed with severe aortic stenosis and is scheduled for elective cardiovascular surgery. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He is currently taking metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin as prescribed by his primary care physician. He reports occasional shortness of breath and fatigue with physical activity. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use. He is 175 cm tall and weighs 77 kg. He has a BMI of 25.2. His preoperative fluid deficit is calculated to be 3080 mL. He has given informed consent to participate in the study.

Pt is a 50yo male with a history of good general health and adequate literacy of written Greek language. The patient does not have a history of dyslexia or attention-deficiency, and has not been diagnosed with any mental or psychiatric diseases. The patient has no reported history of any visual impairments or eye diseases. The patient is willing to participate in the study and understands the nature of the research.

The patient is a 56-year-old Caucasian male with a history of colon cancer. He underwent surgery and chemotherapy two years ago and has been disease-free since then. Recently, he started experiencing abdominal pain and underwent a CT scan that showed multiple metastatic lesions in his liver. He has no other significant medical history, and his physical examination is unremarkable. His ECOG performance status is 1. His blood work shows normal liver and kidney function. He is not on any medication currently. He has been offered chemotherapy, but he is concerned about the potential side effects. He is willing to participate in a clinical trial to explore alternative treatment options. His wife is supportive of his decision and is willing to accompany him to all study visits.

A 24-year old college student has a history of occasional headaches, which usually go away with over-the-counter pain relievers. She is in good health and doesn't have any chronic medical conditions. She is not currently taking any prescription medications or herbal supplements. She is scheduled to undergo surgical removal of two partial bony impactions. She has never undergone any surgery before and is a little anxious about the procedure. She doesn't smoke or drink alcohol. She is sexually active and uses oral contraceptives for birth control. She is willing to participate in the clinical trial and understands the risks and benefits of the study.

A 55-year-old Hispanic male went to the doctor's office for a routine check-up. During the examination, it was found that his blood pressure was high, with a reading of 150/95 mmHg. He has a family history of hypertension and his lifestyle includes a sedentary job and a diet high in sodium. He has not been on any medication for hypertension before. The doctor recommends an antihypertensive treatment with Telmisartan and explains the potential benefits and risks of the medication. The patient agrees to participate in the clinical trial and signs the informed consent form.

The patient is a 60-year-old man with a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in his left leg. He was treated with anticoagulants for six months and had no further episodes of DVT. However, he now presents with pain, redness, and swelling in his right leg, which was diagnosed as superficial venous thrombosis (SVT) of the small saphenous vein. He is otherwise healthy, with no significant medical history or ongoing medication use. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He works as a teacher and is physically active, walking and cycling regularly for exercise. He is interested in participating in the study to help determine the best treatment for SVT and prevent further complications. He is willing to follow the study protocol, including taking medication and wearing compression stockings.

70 year old female who has been experiencing chronic knee pain for the past year. She has tried various treatments including physical therapy and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but the pain persists. She has been scheduled for an elective knee replacement surgery. She lives alone and is fairly independent, but her mobility has been limited due to the knee pain. She does not have a history of psychiatric conditions or rheumatoid arthritis. She currently takes low dose aspirin for cardiovascular health. She speaks English fluently and is able to understand and complete questionnaires. She has not been on chronic opioids exceeding 90 MME/day.

A 55-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the outpatient clinic with a non-healing ulcer on his right foot. The ulcer is located on the plantar surface of the forefoot and has been present for the past 4 weeks. The patient reports that he has been experiencing pain and drainage from the ulcer. He denies any fever, chills, or other systemic symptoms. The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. Physical examination reveals a 1.5 cm x 2 cm ulcer with erythema and edema on the plantar surface of the right forefoot. The patient has intact sensation and is able to move all toes. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are palpable in the affected foot. The patient is a non-smoker and has not had any previous foot ulcers. The patient is willing and able to give consent to participate in the clinical trial.

A 42-year-old male who has been undergoing thrice-weekly hemodialysis for the past year presents for this study. He has been on a polysulfone membrane for the past six months and has a single-pool Kt/V of 1.3. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. He has no history of myocardial infarction or cerebrovascular event in the past 3 months. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His BMI is 30 mg/kg. He is currently taking aspirin 81 mg/d, atorvastatin 40 mg/d, metoprolol succinate 50 mg/d, and insulin glargine 60 units/d, insulin lispro 20 units before meals. He has no known allergies. He is interested in participating in the study and has provided written informed consent.

A 67-year-old female with a medical history of cataract surgery and implantation of the Liberty 677MY multifocal IOL in 2014 has been selected for participation in this clinical trial. The patient reports having a moderate decrease in visual acuity and difficulty with night vision in the past year. She has not been diagnosed with any ocular diseases, and her medical history is unremarkable for conditions affecting the eyes. She does not have any systemic diseases or take any medications that would interfere with the study. The patient is willing to comply with the study requirements and attend all scheduled follow-up appointments.

A 42-year-old office worker has been experiencing low back pain for the past 3 months. The pain is described as a dull ache and is located in the lower back. It is aggravated by prolonged sitting and standing. She has no history of trauma or recent heavy lifting. She has tried over-the-counter pain medications, but they provide only temporary relief. She is able to walk independently without any assistance. She has a history of occasional mild low back pain but has not sought treatment for it in the past. She is interested in participating in a study to compare different exercise approaches for low back pain.

A 32-year-old female presented with a history of recurrent joint pain, swelling, and stiffness for the past two years. She also reported having a butterfly-shaped rash on her cheeks and nose, and occasional fever. She was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) six months ago based on clinical criteria and positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) test. She has been treated with hydroxychloroquine and prednisone (10mg/day) for the past four months, but her symptoms have only partially improved. She has also experienced side effects from the prednisone, including weight gain and mood changes. Her laboratory tests showed positive anti-dsDNA antibody and a total SLEDAI-2K score of 8. She has no history of severe lupus nephritis or active CNS lupus. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to explore new treatment options for SLE.

The patient is a 35-year-old married man who has been experiencing difficulty achieving and maintaining an erection during sexual intercourse. He reports that this has been an ongoing issue for the past year and has caused significant distress in his personal life. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He has been diagnosed with chronic periodontitis and has been experiencing bleeding gums and bad breath for the past few months. He has not received any periodontal treatment in the last 6 months and has not taken any antibiotics during that time. He has no history of heart disease, diabetes mellitus, or hypertension. He has a full set of permanent teeth, excluding the third molars, and has a clinical attachment level and pocket depth of ≥4 mm in more than 30% of sites. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial that investigates the effects of non-surgical periodontal treatment on the severity of his erectile dysfunction.

The patient is a 40 year old male who works as a construction worker. He presents with complaints of chronic low back pain for the past 6 months, which has been affecting his work productivity and daily routine. He reports that the pain is non-specific and he has not been diagnosed with any specific problem. He has tried various pain medications including NSAIDs, but he did not get any significant relief. His past medical history is unremarkable, and he has not undergone any major surgeries. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He exercises regularly and maintains a healthy diet. He has no history of inflammatory diseases, coagulopathy, or anti-coagulation therapy. He denies taking fish oil supplements or fatty fish more than 2 times per week. He is willing to participate in the clinical trial to investigate the efficacy of fish oil on chronic nonspecific low back pain.

58 yo M with Durie-Salmon stage III multiple myeloma and a history of prior treatment with high-dose dexamethasone-containing therapy presented with increasing fatigue, bone pain, and worsening renal function. Recent lab results showed an elevated myeloma paraprotein level, creatinine of 2.6 mg/dL, and platelet count of 80,000/mm3. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 1. The patient has been off any prior anti-myeloma therapy for more than 28 days and has not received any experimental non-drug therapy within the past 56 days. The patient has not had any other malignancies in the past 3 years. The patient meets the inclusion criteria for the study and does not meet any of the exclusion criteria. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has provided informed consent.

A 55-year-old man with a history of stage IV lung cancer was referred to the psychiatric department for treatment of anxiety. He has a known history of depression and has been on antidepressants for the past year. He reports that his anxiety has been worsening over the past few weeks, and he has been having panic attacks. The patient is married with two adult children and works as an accountant. He reports feeling overwhelmed with the management of his cancer treatment and the impact it has had on his family.
