The patient has no history of substance abuse or major psychiatric disorders in his family. He is currently taking oxycodone for pain management and has no other significant medical history. The patient is interested in the use of novel treatments for his anxiety and is considering participating in a clinical trial involving the use of psilocybin. He is aware of the potential risks and benefits of the study and is willing to undergo two overnight hospital stays for treatment sessions. The patient is located in the Los Angeles area and meets the age criteria for the study. He has no history of CNS involvement or kidney disease, abnormal liver functions, epilepsy, or cardiovascular disease, including untreated hypertension. He is not taking insulin, oral hypoglycemic, anti-seizure or cardiovascular medications, except for anti-hypertensive drugs. He has not been taking Prozac for the last 5 weeks and is not consuming alcohol. He agrees to use effective birth control methods and is willing to undergo a pregnancy test.

A 45-year-old male presents to the neurosurgery clinic with complaints of headaches, decreased peripheral vision, and occasional double vision. He has a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes, both of which are well-controlled with medication. He reports no history of eye disease or surgery. On examination, the patient has decreased visual acuity in both eyes, with a visual field defect in the temporal field of the right eye and the nasal field of the left eye. The remainder of the ophthalmic examination is unremarkable. MRI imaging reveals a pituitary macroadenoma measuring 2.5 cm with suprasellar extension. The patient is scheduled for neurosurgical resection of the tumor. He agrees to participate in a clinical trial assessing the accuracy of OCT angiography as a prognostic marker for visual impairment in patients undergoing neurosurgery for compressive macroadenoma. Since he meets the inclusion criteria, he is enrolled in the study.

The patient is a 45 year old woman who completed treatment for stage II breast cancer (ER/PR positive, HER2 negative) two months ago. She has a BMI of 28 kg/m2 and is interested in losing weight to improve her overall health and reduce her risk of cancer recurrence. She is physically able to exercise and is willing to participate in a weight loss program. She has no history of mental illness and is mentally competent to provide informed consent for the study. She is available for baseline and 6-month clinic visits. She did not undergo a double mastectomy.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has undergone breast conserving surgery and has been diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma. The multidisciplinary team has recommended adjuvant whole breast and regional nodal irradiation. The patient has no history of previous radiation therapy to the thoracic, cervical or axillary region, and no distant metastasis has been detected. She has a life expectancy of over 2 years and has no pre-existing conditions or comorbidities that would make toxicity evaluation difficult. The patient has provided informed consent and is willing to participate in the trial to compare the effects of prone crawl treatment position and/or accelerated schedule on acute and late toxicities, quality of life and time management.

Sophie is a 29 year old woman who works as a graphic designer. She has been suffering from chronic neuropathic pain for the past year. She describes her pain as a burning sensation, which starts in her lower back and radiates down to her legs. She has been taking antidepressants and anti-epileptics for the past six months to manage her pain. She has no history of diabetes or central neuropathic pain. Sophie's BMI is within the range of 18-35. She has no history of surgical or medical conditions that would make her incompatible with the study. She is not currently receiving corticosteroid treatment or undergoing any inflammatory or evolutive pathology requiring long term treatment. She has not experienced any weight changes of more than 5% within the last 3 months. Sophie has agreed to participate in the study to help researchers better understand the relationship between the adrenocorticotropic axis and neuropathic pain.

A 55-year-old woman was diagnosed with stage II pancreatic cancer two months ago. She has undergone a distal pancreatectomy and is now scheduled to undergo chemotherapy with cytostatics. Her BMI is 27, and she has noticed a recent loss of appetite and weight loss. Her medical history is remarkable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, which are controlled with medications. She is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. She speaks Danish fluently and is able to read and understand Danish. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that may help improve the understanding of the relationship between fat-free mass and toxicity of cytostatics in cancer patients.

The patient is a 50-year-old male who has recently been diagnosed with advanced melanoma. He has a family history of skin cancer and has been sunburned several times in his life. A biopsy revealed that his cancer has a BRAF V600E genetic mutation. He has undergone previous treatment with chemotherapy and radiation therapy, but the cancer has progressed. He is currently experiencing fatigue, weight loss, and pain in his abdomen. His performance status is 1. He has normal organ and bone marrow function, with a platelet count of 150 K/uL, hemoglobin of 12 g/dL, and serum creatinine of 1.2 x institutional upper limit of normal. His left ventricular ejection fraction is 55%, and his QTc is 450 msec on the screening EKG. He has no history of long QT syndrome or HIV. He has no brain metastases, and his brain MRI is negative. He has no evidence of retinal pathology on ophthalmologic examination. He has not received prior BRAF or MEK inhibitor therapy. His archival tumor tissue is available for testing. He is willing to use adequate contraception during the study and sign a written informed consent document.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman who has suffered from recurrent urinary tract infections. She presents with symptoms of burning and urgency with urination. She has no fever or flank pain. Urine culture confirms the presence of a urinary tract infection. The patient is otherwise healthy and has no history of renal transplantation, spinal cord injury, or pelvic surgery within the last 6 months. She is not pregnant and has no history of bladder augmentation procedures using bowel. The patient is willing to comply with the study procedures and gives her written informed consent to participate.

The patient is a 34-year-old male diagnosed with schizophrenia more than a year ago. He has been on antipsychotic treatment for the past year, but he still experiences persistent symptoms, including delusions and hallucinations. He has been stable on the same conventional antipsychotic medication for the past 8 weeks. He is an outpatient and has never been hospitalized for his condition. He presents with a PANSS score of 55 at Visit 2. He complains of feeling tired and lethargic most of the time, which is affecting his ability to work and socialize. He has a history of substance abuse but has been clean for the past year. He has no other significant medical history. He is interested in exploring the possibility of switching to a different medication to alleviate his symptoms and improve his quality of life.

32-year-old female with a diagnosis of HIV-1 infection for 6 months was referred to the clinic for evaluation of potential new treatment options. The patient has been off antiretroviral therapy for two months and her plasma HIV RNA level was measured at 10,000 copies/mL during her most recent appointment. Her CD4 count at the same appointment was 354 cells/mm3 and CD4 fraction was 21%. The patient reports occasional fatigue, mild night sweats, and a recent episode of diarrhea that lasted for three days. She denies any fever, weight loss, or other symptoms. Her medical history is notable for a diagnosis of depression for which she is taking a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). She has no known drug allergies. The patient is a non-smoker and reports occasional alcohol use. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a naturally occurring substance known as Leukotriene B4 (LTB4) as a potential new treatment option for HIV-1 infection. Upon review of the eligibility criteria, the patient meets all of the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The patient is an 11 year old boy with a history of brain tumor. He was diagnosed with medulloblastoma last year and underwent surgery followed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy. However, the tumor has resumed growth despite the standard medical therapy. He is experiencing headaches, nausea, vomiting and dizziness. He is currently under treatment and is a student in the 5th grade. He likes playing video games and watching superhero movies. He has a younger sister and lives with his parents. His BMI is 18.5 with BP of 110/70. There is nothing remarkable in his physical exam. He has a Karnofsky Performance Score of 70%. His parents are concerned about the safety of the mebendazole drug as they have not heard of it before. They have consented to the trial after discussing the benefits and risks with the treating physician. The patient will chew the 500 mg orange flavored tablet three times a day with meals. The patient will have to come for regular blood draws to monitor the blood levels of the drug.

Patient A is a 70-year-old female with a diagnosis of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease and related dementia. She is currently living in a nursing home and has been experiencing sleep disturbances, depression, and agitation. She has a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) of 1 and a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 14. She does not have any major organ failure or illness, and has not had a history of head injury. She has normal blood pressure and blood glucose levels. She is not currently taking any psychotropic medications for sleep, and she does not have any obstructing cataracts, macular degeneration, or blindness. She is interested in participating in a clinical trial that will explore the effects of tailored light treatment on sleep efficiency, depression, and agitation in individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related dementia.

A 16-year-old adolescent with mild crowding of teeth and slight protrusion of upper incisors was referred to an orthodontist. The patient has no history of epilepsy, periodontal disease, infraocclusion, agenesis, or tooth impaction. The orthodontist suggested using a multibracket appliance with indirect bracket placement using 3D printed bonding trays. The patient has no other significant medical or dental history.

A 42-year-old male diagnosed with major depression for the past 6 months. He has been on venlafaxine for 4 weeks but has not experienced any significant improvement in his symptoms. He has a history of smoking and occasional alcohol use. He has no known allergies or medical conditions. The patient is interested in participating in the trial to potentially accelerate the response to his current medication. He is willing to comply with all study requirements and attend all study visits.

40-year-old male with a history of heart disease and a family history of sudden cardiac arrest. He wears a smart watch regularly and is interested in participating in research studies related to cardiac arrest. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and has no known allergies. He is physically active and exercises regularly. He has not experienced any cardiac events in the past but wants to help in the development of new methods for early recognition and treatment of cardiac arrest.

A 67-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes was admitted to the ICU due to respiratory distress and fever. The patient had a history of smoking 1 pack per day for the past 40 years. Upon admission, the patient's blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg, heart rate was 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate was 28 breaths per minute, and temperature was 38.5°C. The patient had an elevated white blood cell count and CRP levels. The arterial blood gas analysis revealed hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis. The patient was diagnosed with sepsis and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. The patient's SOFA score and serum TNF-a levels were monitored during their stay in the ICU. The patient received intravascular fluid replacement and was put on mechanical ventilation. The patient's hemoglobin level was maintained at 10g/dL and central venous pressure was maintained at 10 cmH2O. The patient remained in the ICU for 5 days and was eventually discharged with stable vital signs and improved respiratory status.

A 8-year-old female diagnosed with congenital heart disease and receiving diuretic medication for the last 2 months. The patient presents with mild fatigue and occasional shortness of breath during physical activity. The patient has no history of thiamin supplementation or receiving thiamin-containing vitamins. The patient does not have any history of hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis. The patient has no intestinal malabsorption, chronic lung disease, red blood cell abnormality, or G6PD deficiency. The patient is not receiving thiamin-producing probiotics or inotropic drugs. The patient's hemoglobin level is within normal range (Hb > 10 g/dL).

58 yo M diagnosed with exfoliative glaucoma with significant cataract formation in both eyes. Currently on two topical glaucoma medications with suboptimal IOP control averaging 22-24 mmHg in both eyes. Patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled on medication, and no other significant medical history. No prior ocular surgery or treatment for glaucoma. Patient is interested in participating in the study and willing to comply with the protocol. Best corrected visual acuity is 20/50 in the right eye and 20/40 in the left eye. Slit lamp examination reveals moderate nuclear sclerotic cataract in both eyes with no other significant ocular findings.

The patient is a 28-year-old male who sustained an acute injury to his wrist while playing basketball. He was diagnosed with a scaphoid fracture of type B2 by an orthopedic surgeon. He has no other concomitant fractures. The patient is right-handed and works as a computer programmer. He is otherwise healthy and has no known allergies. He has not undergone any previous surgeries or medical procedures. He is interested in participating in the clinical trial to potentially benefit from the personalised percutaneous external 3D guide for scaphoid fixation.

The patient is a 30-year-old male with a history of epilepsy and partial onset seizures with or without secondarily generalized seizures. He has been taking stable doses of monotherapy for 8 weeks prior to the study, but has been experiencing greater than or equal to 2 seizures within the last 8 weeks despite treatment. He is not currently on any antipsychotics or benzodiazepines, and has not used intermittent rescue benzodiazepines more than 2 times in an 8-week period prior to the study. He is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and has no history of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, nonmotor simple partial seizures only, or primary generalized epilepsies or seizures such as absences and/or myoclonic epilepsies. He has not had a history of status epilepticus within 12 weeks before the study and has not been diagnosed with a progressive central nervous system disease. He is not participating in any other intervention clinical trials.

A 55-year-old male came to the clinic with a cough and shortness of breath that had been getting worse over the past few weeks. He had a history of smoking for 30 years, but quit 5 years ago. He had never had lung cancer before. His chest X-ray and CT scan revealed a mass in his left lung. A biopsy confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) grade IIIb. He was otherwise healthy with no significant medical history. His performance status was good (ECOG-PS=1). He was interested in participating in a clinical trial to treat his cancer and was willing to undergo chemotherapy. He had no known allergies to medications and had never received paclitaxel, cisplatin, or carboplatin before. He had no other serious concomitant systemic disorders or medical conditions that would prevent him from completing the study.

A 12-year-old Chinese male with a confirmed diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is being considered for a clinical trial. The patient has undergone at least two prior drug treatments, but has experienced relapse and is now refractory to treatment. The patient has not received chemotherapy within the past two weeks and has normal cardiac, hepatic, and renal function. The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 1 and a life expectancy of more than 3 months. The patient has not received clofarabine before and is not allergic to fludarabine or cladribine. The patient does not have central nervous system involvement or uncontrolled infection and has recovered from any adverse effects of prior therapy. The patient may be eligible for a phase II clinical trial evaluating the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of clofarabine in Chinese pediatric patients with refractory or relapsed ALL.

The patient is a healthy 2-month-old infant who has not been vaccinated against poliovirus before. The infant has no known medical conditions or allergies, and their guardian is capable of understanding and signing the consent form for participation in the study. The infant's axillary temperature is within the normal range, and they have not received any subunit or inactivated vaccine in the past week, any live attenuated vaccine in the past two weeks, or any blood product in the past three months. The infant is eligible for the study and will receive three doses of the Sabin Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine (sIPV) with high D antigen content on the month 0, 1, 2 schedule. Serum samples will be collected before the first dose and 30 days after the third dose to assess the immunogenicity of the vaccine in the infant. Adverse events occurring within 30 days after each dose will also be collected to assess the safety of the vaccine.

A 45-year-old woman has been recently diagnosed with unilateral papillary thyroid carcinoma. She is in good health with no significant medical history. The tumor measures 1.5 cm and is confined to the right lobe of the thyroid gland. She has no symptoms related to the thyroid carcinoma and is otherwise asymptomatic. The patient is willing to participate in the study and has signed the informed consent. She meets the inclusion criteria of TNM staging T1N0M0 and does not have any exclusion criteria such as bilateral thyroid carcinoma or advanced TNM staging (T3 or T4). She will be randomized to either the experimental group or control group to compare the effectiveness of bilateral central lymph node dissection.

This clinical trial does not involve patients, but rather staff members within a designated UK Health Trust who have access to an android mobile phone. Therefore, a patient description is not applicable in this case.

The patient is a 65-year-old male with a history of osteoarthritis and avascular necrosis in the medial compartment of the knee. He has not responded to non-surgical treatments such as physical therapy, medication, and corticosteroid injections. The patient does not have a history of infection, rheumatoid arthritis, or inflammatory joint disease. He has no contraindications to the Oxford Partial Knee System according to the approved labeling. The patient is willing to undergo surgery and agrees to participate in the study. He understands the risks and benefits of the procedure and is capable of following directions.

As this is an expanded access program, no specific patient description can be generated without the context of the patient's individual medical history and current condition. The criteria for consideration of early access to experimental therapy are outlined in the summary, and the eligibility criteria for enrollment are not provided as this is not a traditional clinical trial. Patients who meet the criteria for unmet medical need and have exhausted all other treatment options may be considered for early access to experimental therapy, but the decision to grant access is solely at the discretion of CSL Behring. It is important to note that even if the patient meets the criteria, there is no guarantee that expanded access will be available for every experimental medicine, and access will cease if clinical trials or regulatory assessment determines the product does not demonstrate a positive risk benefit for patients.

The patient is a 58-year-old Caucasian woman who has been referred for colonoscopy due to a family history of colon cancer. She has no personal history of gastrointestinal disorders or surgeries and has not had a colonoscopy before. She has a BMI of 25 and is in good overall health. She reports no current symptoms related to her digestive system, such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, or constipation. Her bowel preparation for the colonoscopy is clear and adequate. She has no contraindications to position changes during the procedure and is willing to participate in the study. She understands the potential benefits of increased adenoma detection rates and is willing to undergo the colonoscopy with the possibility of position changes during the procedure.

The patient is a 45-year-old man with a history of type 1 diabetes diagnosed 20 years ago. He has been on insulin therapy for the past 10 years and is currently taking lispro and glargine. His blood glucose levels are well controlled, with an HbA1c of 7.2%. The patient also has a history of hypertension, which is currently being treated with amlodipine. He has been experiencing symptoms of kidney disease, such as frequent urination, fatigue and swelling of the feet. A previous urine test revealed elevated levels of albumin, indicating the presence of diabetic nephropathy. The patient is willing to participate in the study and is not of child-bearing potential. There is no history of non-diabetic kidney disease or malignancy.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who has been on hemodialysis for the past 6 months. He has been experiencing symptoms of depression, such as low mood, lack of energy, and loss of interest in activities that he used to enjoy. He also reports having trouble sleeping and feeling anxious about his health condition. His BDI-II score is 18, indicating moderate depression. He is currently taking medications for hypertension and anemia. The patient is interested in participating in a clinical trial investigating the effect of cognitive-behavioral group therapy on depression and quality of life in patients with ESRD. He is able to communicate well with the researchers and understands the informed consent process. He has not changed his anti-depressive agent or dose in the past 2 months.

A 52-year-old woman was diagnosed with non-palpable invasive breast cancer during a routine mammogram. The tumor is visible and enhances on prone MRI and is 1.5 cm in diameter. She desires breast conserving surgery and has provided informed consent to participate in the clinical trial. She has no history of pacemaker or neurostimulator, aneurysm clip, or metallic foreign body in or near her eyes. She is not severely claustrophobic and has no contraindication to the use of gadolinium-based intravenous contrast. She has no history of median sternotomy, and she is not pregnant. She has no other tumors in different quadrants of the breast.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who has been diagnosed with an aneurysm of the infrarenal abdominal aorta. He has been experiencing abdominal pain and discomfort for the past few months, which led him to seek medical attention. He has a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia, which have been treated with medication for the past 5 years. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol moderately. He exercises regularly, at least 3 times a week, for about 30 minutes each time. He has no history of surgeries or major illnesses. He has agreed to participate in the study and has provided informed consent. He is aware that he will need to undergo open surgery for his aneurysm and has been scheduled for the procedure in the near future.

The patient is a 55-year-old male who underwent kidney transplant surgery approximately 6 months ago. He has a history of hypertension and high cholesterol, which are managed with medication. He is a non-smoker and does not consume alcohol. He reports occasional forgetfulness and difficulty with focus and concentration. He is interested in participating in a clinical trial to assess the impact of Envarsus on cognitive function and cerebral blood flow. He is able to read, write, and speak English fluently and is able to arrange transportation to and from study sites. He has no history of claustrophobia or other contraindications for MRI. He is able to perform exercise on the Nustep machine and has no uncontrolled blood pressure issues.

Patient is a 60-year-old man who has been diagnosed with heart failure and is currently undergoing treatment with a cardiac resynchronization therapy device. The patient has been recommended to receive an Attain StarFix Model 4195 LV lead to improve the effectiveness of his current treatment. The patient is willing and able to provide written authorization and/or consent as required by the institution and geographical requirements. The patient is within the 30-day post-implant enrollment window and is not currently enrolled in or planning to enroll in any concurrent drug and/or device study that may confound the results of this study.

The patient is a 45-year-old woman who has been experiencing pain in her left shoulder for several months. She recently consulted with an orthopedic surgeon who diagnosed her with a rotator cuff tear and recommended surgery. She has a history of hypertension and is taking medication to control it. She has never had any adverse reactions to anesthesia or any other medications. She has not used any strong opioids in the past six months. She is interested in participating in the study to potentially reduce her postoperative pain and opioid use.
